On the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abd God, may God be pleased with him, say: “Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would deliver a sermon, he would lean against the trunk of a palm tree from among the pillars of the mosque. When the pulpit was made for him and he stood on it, that pillar shook and moaned like the moaning of a camel, so that the people of the mosque heard it, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came down and embraced it, and it calmed down.” Mujahid said: No stone descends from a high place to a low place except out of fear of God. What we have said is supported by the words of God Almighty: “If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God. And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought.” 21-Al-Hashr. The Almighty’s saying, And God is not unaware Basaha of what you do is a threat and a warning. It was said: He will not leave the punishment for what you do, but rather He will reward you for it. Ibn Kathir read ya’mal with a ya and the others with a ta.
2:75: 75. The Almighty’s saying, Do you then hope? Do you hope? He means: Muhammad and his companions that they will believe in you the Jews will believe you in what you tell them and a group of them used to hear the word of God meaning the Torah then they would distort it changing the rulings in it after they had understood it they knew it as they changed the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse of stoning while they knew that they were liars. This is the saying of Mujahid, Qatadah, Ikrimah, As-Suddi and a group. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: It was revealed about the seventy whom Moses chose for the appointment with his Lord, and that is because when they returned - after hearing the word of God - to their people, the people returned to their saying, and as for the truthful ones among them, they performed as they heard, and a group of them said: We heard God say at the end of His speech, if you are able to do so, then do so, and if you wish, then do not do so, so this is their distortion while they know that it is the truth.
2:76: 76. And when they meet those who believe Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Qatada said: meaning the hypocrites of the Jews who believed with their tongues when they meet the sincere believers "they say: We believe" as you believe and when they are alone they return to one another - Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf, Ka'b bin Asad, Wahb bin Yahudah and other leaders of the Jews - to their situation on that "they say: Do you tell them what God has revealed to you" what God has told you in your book: that Muhammad is the truth and his word is true. And Al-Fattah is the judge. Al-Kisa’i said: “With what God has made clear to you [of knowledge of the description and attributes of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace]. Al-Waqidi said: “With what God has revealed to you.” Similar to it is: We opened for them blessings from the heaven 44-Al-An’am, meaning We revealed. Abu Ubaidah said: With what God has bestowed upon you and given you, so that they may argue with you so that they may dispute with you, meaning the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, argue with your saying upon you, saying that you have acknowledged that he is a true prophet in your book, then you do not follow him!!” That is because they said to the people of Medina when he consulted them about following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Believe in him, for he is the truth. Then some of them said to one another: Are you telling them what God has revealed to you so that they may have an argument against you before your Lord in this world and the Hereafter? It was said that they informed the believers of the punishment with which God had punished them for their crimes, so some of them said to one another: Are you telling them what God has revealed to you of punishment so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord, so that they may see the honor for themselves over you before God? Mujahid said: It is the saying of the Jews of Banu Qurayzah. Some of them said to one another] when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: O brothers of apes and pigs, so they said: Who informed Muhammad of this? This came from none other than you. Do you not understand?
2:77: 77. God Almighty said: Or do they not know that God knows what they conceal they hide and what they declare they reveal, meaning the Jews.
2:78: 78. And the Almighty’s saying: And among them are illiterate people, meaning that among the Jews are illiterate people who do not know how to read and write. The plural of ummi is attributed to the mother, as if he remained as he was separated from the mother, not learning to write or read. [It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, “We are an illiterate nation. We do not write or calculate.”] It was said: It is attributed to the mother of villages, which is Mecca. They do not know the Book except in wishful thinking. Abu Ja`far read: Wishful thinking with a light ya’. All of the Qur’an has deleted one of the two ya’s for the sake of lightening, and the reading of the general public is with a shaddah. It is the plural of wishful thinking, which is recitation. God Almighty said: Except when he makes a wish, Satan casts into his wish 52-Al-Hajj, meaning in his recitation. Abu Ubaidah said: [Except its recitation and reading] from memory, they do not recite it from a book. It was said: They learn it by memory and reading, but they do not know its meaning. Ibn Abbas said: It means they do not know the meanings of the Book. Mujahid and Qatada said: Except for lies and falsehood. Al-Farra’ said: Wishes are fabricated hadiths. Uthman, may God be pleased with him, said: I have not wished since I converted to Islam (i.e. I have not lied). He meant by it the things that their scholars wrote from themselves and then added them to God Almighty, such as changing the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and other things. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is from wishing, and they are their false wishes that they wished for from God Almighty, such as their saying: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian 111-Al-Baqarah and their saying: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days 80-Al-Baqarah and their saying: We are the sons of God and His beloved 18-Al-Ma’idah. Based on this, except has the meaning of but, i.e. they do not know the Book, but they wish for things that will happen to them. And they and they only think and they only think, a thought and imagination, not certainty. Qatada and Al-Rabi’ said it. Mujahid said: They lie.
2:79: 79. The Almighty’s saying: Woe. Al-Zajjaj said: Woe is a word said by everyone who is in a state of ruin. It was said: It is the invocation of the unbelievers upon themselves with woe and destruction. Ibn Abbas said: Severe torment. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Woe is a valley in Hell. If the mountains of the world were to be driven through it, they would melt from the intensity of its heat. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah told us, Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Rashdin ibn Sa’d [on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, who narrated on the authority of Abu al-Samh on the authority of Abu al-Haitham] on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Woe is a valley in Hell into which the disbeliever falls for forty autumns before reaching its bottom, and as-Sajd is a mountain of fire into which he climbs for seventy autumns and then falls, and it is like that.” For those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, ‘This is from God,’ in order to exchange it for a small price. This is because the Jewish rabbis feared that their livelihood would be lost and their leadership would be removed when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, so they devised a plan to prevent the Jews from believing in him. They took his description in the Torah, which was: handsome face, handsome hair, black eyes, medium build. They changed it and wrote in its place: tall, blue-eyed. When their lower class asked them about his description, they would read what they had written and find it to be contrary to his description, so they would deny it and reject it. God Almighty said, So woe to them for what their hands have written, meaning what they wrote themselves, inventing to change the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And woe to them for what they earn, of food and it is said: of sins.
2:80: 80. And they said meaning the Jews The Fire will not touch us [The Fire will not touch us] except for a few days a predetermined amount, then the torment will be removed from us and will be followed by bliss. They differed regarding this verse. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: The Jews used to say: This world is seven thousand years, and we are only tormented for one day for every thousand years, then the torment will stop after seven days. Qatada and Ata' said: They meant the forty days in which their fathers worshipped the calf. Al-Hasan and Al-Aliyah said: The Jews said: Our Lord has rebuked us for something, so He swore to torment us for forty days, and the Fire will not touch us except for forty days, as a fulfillment of the oath. So God Almighty said, in refutation of them: Say O Muhammad, Have you taken a covenant with God an interrogative alif that entered into the alif of connection, with God "? He has confirmed that He will not punish you except for this period. God will not fail in His covenant and His promise. Ibn Masoud said: A covenant of monotheism, indicated by the Almighty’s saying: Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful 87-Maryam. Meaning: saying: There is no god but God. Or do you say about God that which you do not know? Then he said:
2:81: 81. Bala and bal and bala: two letters of correction, and their meaning is to negate the past report and confirm the future report. Whoever earns a bad deed means polytheism. And his sin has encompassed him The people of Medina read his sins in the plural, and encompassing means surrounding something from all sides. Ibn Abbas, Ata, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ar-Rabi' and a group said: It is polytheism that one dies upon. It was said: It is the major sin. And encompassing him means that he persists in it and dies without repenting. Ikrimah and Ar-Rabi' bin Khaitham said: Mujahid said: It is the sins that surround the heart. Whenever he commits a sin, it rises until it covers the heart, which is the rust. Al-Kalbi said: His sins destroyed him, the evidence for this is the Almighty's statement: Unless you are encompassed 66-Yusuf meaning you are destroyed. Then those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally.
2:82: 82. The Almighty said: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
2:83: 83. God the Almighty said: And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel in the Torah, and the covenant is the strong promise You shall not worship except God Ibn Kathir, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i readل عبادونwith a ya’, and Al-Kharun read with a ta’ because of God the Almighty’s saying And speak to people kindly meaning do not worship, so when it was deleted, the verb became raised, and Abi bin Ka’b read: Do not worship except God as a prohibition To parents, good treatment meaning and We enjoined upon them to be kind to their parents, being dutiful to them and compassionate towards them and submitting to their command, in what does not contradict the command of God the Almighty And to relatives meaning and to relatives, and kinship is a source like goodness And orphans plural of orphan, which is a child who has no father And the needy meaning the poor And speak to people kindly truthfully and truly regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so whoever asks you about him, tell him the truth and explain his description and do not conceal his matter, this is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil, and Sufyan Al-Thawri said: Command them to do good And forbid them from evil. It was said: It is gentleness in speech and dealing with people with good character. Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read: Hasanah with the opening of the Ha’ and the Seen, meaning good speech. And establish prayer and give zakat, then you turned away you turned away from the covenant and the pact except a few of you and that is because a people among them believed and you were turning away like your fathers turned away.
2:84: 84. The Almighty said: And when We took your covenant, ‘You shall not shed one another’s blood’ meaning, you shall not spill one another’s blood, meaning, you shall not shed one another’s blood. It was also said: Do not shed the blood of others lest your blood be shed, so it is as if you shed your own blood. And do not expel one another from your homes meaning, do not expel one another from their homes. It was also said: Do not mistreat those who live near you, for you will force them to leave because of your mistreat. Then you acknowledged this covenant as true and accepted it. And you bear witness today to that, O group of Jews, and you acknowledge acceptance.
2:85: 85. The Almighty’s saying, Then you are these, meaning: O these, and these is for emphasis, kill yourselves, meaning kill each other, and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting each other against them, with emphasis on the dhad, meaning you support each other. The ta’ was assimilated into the dhad, and Asim, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read with a light dhad, so they deleted the ta’ of interaction and kept the ta’ of address, like the Almighty’s saying, And do not cooperate, meaning both of them: you cooperate, and the supporter: the help in sin and aggression, disobedience and injustice, and if they come to you as captives, and Hamza read: captives, and they are the plural of captive, and their meaning is the same, you ransom them with money and you rescue them, and the people of Medina, Asim, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read you ransom them, meaning you exchange them, he meant: ransoming the captive for the captive, and it was said that the meaning of the two readings is the same. The meaning of the verse: Al-Suddi said: God Almighty took a command from the Children of Israel in the Torah that they would not kill each other, nor expel each other from their homes. Any male or female slave you find from the Children of Israel, buy him for the price and free him. So the Qurayzah were allies of the Aws, and the Nadir were allies of the Khazraj, and they used to fight in the Battle of Samir. So the Banu Qurayzah and their allies fought the Banu Nadir and their allies, and if they were victorious, they would destroy their homes and expel them from them. And if a man from either party was taken prisoner, they would gather around him until they ransom him, even if the prisoner was from their enemy. So the Arabs would taunt them and say: How do you fight them and ransom them? They would say: We were commanded to ransom them. So they would say: Why do you fight them? They said: We are ashamed that our allies should be humiliated. So God Almighty reproached them for that and said: Then you are these people who kill yourselves. The verse has an inversion and a delay and its organization and you expel a party of you from their homes, supporting each other against them in sin and aggression and it is forbidden for you to expel them. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them. So it is as if God Almighty took four covenants from them: to refrain from fighting, to refrain from expelling, to refrain from supporting each other against them with their enemies, and to ransom their captives. So they turned away from all of them except ransom. God the Almighty said: Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part? Mujahid said: He means that if you find it in someone else’s hand, you ransom him and kill him with your own hand. Then what is the reward of those who do that among you, O company of Jews, except disgrace, torment and humiliation, in the life of this world? So the disgrace of Qurayzah was killing and captivity, and the disgrace of Nadir was expulsion and banishment from their homes to Adhra’at and Jericho in Syria. And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment, which is the torment of the Fire. And God is not unaware of what you do. Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, and Abu Bakr read it with a ya, and the rest read it with a ta. God the Almighty said: Those are the ones who purchased.
2:86: 86 - Those who have exchanged the life of this world for the Hereafter, the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be aided. They will not be prevented from the punishment of God Almighty.
2:87: 87- The Almighty’s saying: “And We gave” We gave Moses the Book the Torah, all at once and We followed and followed after him with messengers messenger after messenger and We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs the clear indications, which are what God mentioned in Surat Al Imran and Al Ma’idah. It was said: He meant the Gospel. And We supported him strengthened him with the Holy Spirit Ibn Kathir read Al Quds with a sukoon on the dal and the others with a damma on it, and they are two languages like terror and terror, and they differed about the Holy Spirit. Al Rabi’ and others said: He meant by the Spirit the Spirit that He breathed into him, and the Holy is God, He added it to Himself as an honor and a specialization like the House of God, and the She-camel of God, as He said: So We breathed into him of Our Spirit 12- At-Tahrim and a Spirit from Him 171- An-Nisa. It was said: He meant by the Holy Purity, meaning the pure Spirit. He called His Spirit Holy because it was not contained in the loins of the males, and the wombs did not contain it. The menses, it was only an order from God the Most High, Qatada, Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak said: The Holy Spirit is Gabriel, peace be upon him. It was said: Gabriel was described as holy, meaning pure, because he did not commit a sin. Al-Hasan said: The Holy is God and His Spirit is Gabriel. God the Most High said: “Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth” 102- An-Nahl. And the support of Jesus by Gabriel, peace be upon them, is that he was ordered to walk with him wherever he walked until God ascended with him to heaven. It was said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, was called a spirit for his kindness and his position in the revelation that is the reason for the life of hearts. Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Jubair said: The Holy Spirit is the greatest name of God the Most High, by which He revived the dead and showed people wonders. It was said: It is the Gospel, for which a spirit was given to him just as (the Qur’an was made a spirit for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because it is the reason for the life of hearts). God the Most High said: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command 52- Ash-Shura. So when the Jews heard the mention of Jesus, peace be upon him, they said: O Muhammad, there is nothing like Jesus - as you claim - did, and not as you tell us about the prophets, so bring us what Jesus brought if you are truthful. God Almighty said: So whenever there came to you, O community of Jews, a messenger with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant. “You were arrogant and thought too proud to believe.” So you denied a group, such as Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you killed a group, such as Zechariah, John, Isaiah, and all the other prophets whom they killed, peace be upon them.
2:88: 88- And they said meaning the Jews Our hearts are covered the plural of aghlaf which is covered with a membrane, meaning that there is a covering over them so they do not comprehend or understand what they are saying, said Mujahid and Qatada, similar to the saying of God Almighty And they said, Our hearts are within coverings 5 - Fussilat Ibn Abbas read ghalaf with a damma on the lam and this is the reading of al-A'raj and it is the plural of ghalaf meaning our hearts are vessels for all knowledge so they do not need your knowledge, said Ibn Abbas and Ata' and al-Kalbi said: Its meaning is vessels for all knowledge so you do not hear a hadith without comprehending it except your hadith which you do not understand nor comprehend, even if there was good in it you would yearn for it and understand it. God the Almighty said: Rather, God has cursed them God has expelled them and kept them far from all good because of their disbelief, so few of them believe. Qatada said: Its meaning is that only a few of them will believe, because those who believed from the polytheists are more than those who believed from the Jews, meaning few of them believe. The accusative of little is in the state of the verb. Muammar said: They do not believe except a little of what is in their hands and they disbelieve in most of it, meaning few of them believe. The accusative of little is by removing the preposition, and what is a relative clause based on their statement. Al-Waqidi said: Its meaning is that they do not believe little or much, like a man saying to another: How little you do such-and-such, meaning you do not do it at all.
2:89: 89. And when there came to them a Book from God meaning the Qur'an confirming in agreement with what they had meaning the Torah and they meaning the Jews before" before the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, "would seek victory seek help against those who disbelieved" against the polytheists of the Arabs, because they used to say when a matter troubled them and an enemy attacked them: O God, grant us victory over them through the Prophet sent at the end of time, whose description we find in the Torah, so they were victorious, and they used to say to their enemies from the polytheists: The time has come when a Prophet will emerge confirming what we have said, so we will kill you with him as we killed Aad and Thamud and Iram." But when there came to them what they recognized" meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, other than the Children of Israel, and they recognized his description and attributes "they disbelieved in him" out of envy and spite. "So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.
2:90: 90. "How evil is that for which they have exchanged their souls. Ba'isa and Na'am" are two past tense verbs used for praise and blame. They do not act like verbs. Their meaning is: "How evil is that for which they have exchanged falsehood for truth." It was said: The purchase here means the sale and the meaning is evil what they sold their souls for, that is, when they chose disbelief and they gave themselves to the Fire that they disbelieve in what God has revealed meaning the Qur’an out of envy meaning envy. The root of baghy is corruption. It is said that the wound became corrupted when it became corrupt. Baghy is injustice, and its root is seeking. The aggressor is the one seeking injustice, and the envious oppresses the envied to the best of his ability, seeking to remove the blessing of God the Most High from him. That God may send down from His grace meaning the prophethood and the Book upon whomever He wills of His servants Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The people of Mecca and Basra read yanzil with a light except in Glory be to Him in two places And We send down from the Qur’an 93-Al-Isra’ and until He sends down 93-Al-Isra’. Ibn Kathir makes them both heavy. The Basrans made that He may send down a verse 37-Al-An’am heavy. Ya’qub added a heavy by what He sends down in An-Nahl and agreed with Hamza and Al-Kisa’i in making wazil light. 21 And We send it down only in due measure in Al-Hijr. And they returned with wrath means they returned with wrath upon wrath Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: The first wrath is due to their neglect of the Torah and their alteration, and the second is due to their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an. Qatada said: The first is due to their disbelief in Jesus and the Gospel, and the second is due to their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an. Al-Suddi said: The first is due to the worship of the calf and the second is due to disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And for the disbelievers: those who deny the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among all people is a humiliating punishment in which they will be humiliated.
2:91: 91. The Almighty said: And when it is said to them, ‘Believe in what God has revealed,’ meaning the Qur’an, they say, ‘We believe in what was revealed to us,’ meaning the Torah, that is sufficient for us, and they disbelieve in what is beyond it, meaning in other books, like the Almighty’s saying: But whoever seeks beyond that 7-Al-Mu’minun, meaning other than it. Abu Ubaidah said: [with what is beyond it] meaning in other books, and it is the truth, meaning the Qur’an, confirming is an accusative in the state of what they have of the Torah. Say, to them, O Muhammad, “so why did you kill,” meaning did you kill the prophets of God before? “And why”: its root is when, so the alif was deleted to differentiate between the accusative and the interrogative, like their saying in what and with what? “if you are believers” in the Torah, and you were forbidden in it from killing the prophets, peace be upon them.
2:92: 92. The Almighty said, And Moses had already come to you with clear proofs, with clear evidence and dazzling miracles, then you took the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers.
2:93: 93. And when We took your covenant and raised the Mount above you, [saying], 'Take what We have given you with determination and listen.' That is, respond and obey. Obedience and response are called hearing because of proximity, because it is a cause of obedience and response. "They said, 'We hear' your statement, 'and disobey' your command. It was said: We heard with the ears and disobeyed with the hearts. The people of meaning said: They did not say this with their tongues, but when they heard and received it with disobedience, it was attributed to the statement in an expanded manner. "And they made the calf drink into their hearts because of their disbelief." That is, the love of the calf. That is, its meaning is: The love of the calf entered their hearts and mixed with them, like the infusion of color due to the intensity of the association. It is said: So-and-so is infused with color if his whiteness is mixed with redness. In the al-Qasas 28:Moses ordered that the calf be cooled with a cooler, then thrown into the river, and he ordered them to drink from it. Whoever had any love of the calf left in his heart, the blackness of gold would appear on his drinker. God Almighty said: “Say: ‘How evil is that which your faith enjoins upon you,’ that you worship the calf instead of God. That is, how evil is the faith that enjoins upon you the worship of the calf, ‘if you are believers,’ according to your claim. That is because they said: ‘We believe in what was revealed to us,’ so God Almighty denied them.”
2:94: 94. The Almighty said: "Say: If the home of the Hereafter is with God for you" This is because the Jews made false claims such as their saying: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days 80-Al-Baqarah "And they said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian" 111-Al-Baqarah and their saying: We are the children of God and His beloved 18-Al-Ma'idah. So God the Almighty denied them and imposed the argument on them and said: Say to them, O Muhammad, If the home of the Hereafter is with God for you meaning Paradise with God purely meaning exclusively from among the people, then wish for death meaning desire it and ask for it because whoever knows that Paradise is his abode longs for it and there is no way to enter it except after death, so hasten it with your wish if you are truthful in your statement, and it was said: then wish for death meaning claim death for the false sect. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If they wished for death, every one of them would choke on his own saliva, and there would not remain a Jew on the face of the earth who did not die.
2:95: 95. God Almighty said: And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth because they know that they are lying in their claim. He meant because of what their hands have put forth meaning what they have put forth of deeds, and he attributed it to the hand [and not to the rest of the limbs] because most of the crimes of a person are committed by the hand, so his deeds are attributed to the hand even if the hand has no work in them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
2:96: 96. And you will find them The lam is the lam of the oath and the nun is an emphasis on the oath, meaning: By God, you will find them, O Muhammad, meaning the Jews, the most greedy of people for life and of those who associate others with God. It was said: It is connected to the first, and more greedy than those who associate others with God. It was said: Then the speech with his saying for life then he began of those who associate others with God and he meant by those who associate others with God the Magians. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Rabi' said that they were called polytheists because they spoke of light and darkness. He would like wants and wishes that one of them would live a thousand years meaning to live a thousand years, which is the greeting of the Magians among themselves, they say live a thousand years and every thousand is Newroz and a festival, God Almighty says: The Jews are more eager for life than the Magians who say that and it will not remove him distance him from the torment from the Fire that he should live a long life meaning his long life will not save him. [Zahzahu wa zahzah] from torment or zahzah: intransitive and transitive, and it is said zahzahtuhu fa zahzah and God is Seeing of what they do.
2:97: 97. The Almighty said: "Say: Who is an enemy to Gabriel?" Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: A rabbi from the rabbis of the Jews called Abdullah bin Suriya said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Which angel descended from the heaven? He said Gabriel. He said: That is our enemy from the angels, and if it were Michael, we would have believed in you. Gabriel descends with torment, fighting, and severity, and he has been hostile to us repeatedly, and one of the most difficult things for us was that God Almighty revealed to our Prophet that Jerusalem would be destroyed at the hands of a man called Bukhtanasr, and he informed us of the time at which it would be destroyed. When that time came, we sent a man from the strong men of the Children of Israel to seek him out and kill him. He set out until he met him in Babylon as a poor boy, and he seized him to kill him, but Gabriel pushed him away. Bukhtanasr grew strong and powerful, and he invaded us and destroyed Jerusalem. That is why we consider him an enemy. Then God Almighty revealed this verse. Muqatil said: The Jews said: Gabriel is our enemy because he was ordered to make the prophethood in us, but he made it in someone other than us. Qatada, Ikrimah and Al-Suddi said: Omar bin Al-Khattab had land at the top of Medina and its passageway was through the schools of the Jews. Whenever he came to his land, he would go to them and listen to them speech. They said to him: There is no companion of Muhammad more beloved to us than you. They pass by us and harm us, but you do not harm us, and we have hope in you. Omar said: By God, I do not come to you because I love you, nor do I ask you because I doubt my religion. I only come to you to increase my insight into the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to see its traces in your book [which you conceal]. They said: Who is the companion of Muhammad who comes to him from the angels? He said: Gabriel. They said: That is our enemy who informs Muhammad of our secrets, and he is the one who brings every torment, subsidence, famine and hardship. And when Michael comes, he brings fertility and spoils. Omar said to them: Do you recognize Gabriel and deny Muhammad? They said: Yes. He said: Then tell me about the status of Gabriel and Michael with God Almighty? They said: Gabriel is on His right and Michael is on His left. Omar said: Then I bear witness that whoever is an enemy of Gabriel is an enemy of Michael, and whoever is an enemy of Michael is of Gabriel, and whoever is an enemy of Gabriel is an enemy of him. Then Omar returned to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and found that Gabriel had preceded him in the revelation. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this verse and said: (Your Lord has agreed with you, O Omar.) Omar said: After that, I saw myself harder than a stone in the religion of God. God Almighty said: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - he has brought it down - meaning the Qur’an, referring to something not mentioned - upon your heart, O Muhammad, by God’s permission, by God’s command, confirming and agreeing with what was before it, with what came before it of the Scriptures, and as guidance and good tidings for the believers.”
2:98: 98. The Almighty’s saying: Whoever is an enemy to God and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael He singled them out for mention from among the angels even though they are included in His saying and His angels as a distinction and specification, like His Almighty’s saying: In them are fruits and date palms and pomegranates 68-Ar-Rahman. He singled out the date palms and pomegranates for mention even though they are included in the mention of fruits, and the waw in them means: or, meaning whoever is an enemy to one of these then he is an enemy to all, because the one who disbelieves in one is a disbeliever in all Then God is an enemy to the disbelievers Ikrimah said: Gabriel, Michael, and Israf are the servant in Syriac, and Wayl is God Almighty, and their meanings are the servant of God and the servant of the Most Merciful. Ibn Kathir read Gabriel with a fat-ha on the jim without a hamza, with the weight of Fa’il. Hassan said: Gabriel is the Messenger of God among us, and the Holy Spirit has no equal. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read it with a hamza and zalat al-ishba’ with the weight of Salsabil, and Abu Bakr read it with ikhtilas, and the others read it with a kasra on the jim without a hamza, and N and Mika’il, Abu Amr, Ya’qub and Hafs read Mika’il without a hamza. Jarir said: They worshipped the cross, lied about Muhammad, Gabriel, and Michael. Another said: And on the day of Badr, we met you, and Gabriel and Michael were our support for victory. Nafi’ read: with a hamza and abbreviation, with the weight of mifa’al, and the others read: with a hamza and saturation, with the weight of mika’il, and Ibn Suriya said: You did not bring us anything that we know, so God Almighty revealed:
2:99: 99. And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses clear and detailed about what is permissible and what is forbidden, the limits and the rulings and none disbelieve in them except the wicked those who go against the command of God Almighty.
2:100: 100. The Almighty’s saying, Or whenever the conjunction waw was preceded by the interrogative alif they made a covenant meaning the Jews made a covenant that if Muhammad came out, they would be faithful to him, but when he came out, they disbelieved in him. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reminded them of what God had taken from them of the covenant and enjoined upon them concerning Muhammad that they should believe in him, Malik bin Al-Saif said: By God, He did not enjoin upon us concerning Muhammad a covenant. So God Almighty revealed this verse, which is indicated by the reading of Abu Raja Al-Attardi: or whenever they were promised, so he made them the objects. Ata’ said: They are the covenants that were between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Jews, that they should not assist the polytheists in fighting him, but they broke them as Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir did. Its evidence is the statement of God Almighty: Those of them with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant 56-Al-Anfal. A group “groups” of them of the Jews “rejected it” and abandoned it. Rather, most of them do not believe.
2:101: 101. "And when there came to them a Messenger from God meaning Muhammad confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of God behind their backs" meaning the Torah, and it was said: the Torah, and it was said: the Qur'an "as if they did not know." Al-Sha'bi said: They used to read the Torah but did not know about it, and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: They wrapped it in silk and brocade and adorned it with gold and silver but did not act upon it, so that is their throwing it away.
2:102: 102. The Almighty said: And they followed meaning the Jews what the devils recited meaning: they did not recite. The Arabs put the future in place of the past, and the past in place of the future. It was said: what you were reciting, meaning reading. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: following and acting upon it. Ata’ said: speaking and speaking of it during the reign of Solomon meaning: his reign and his covenant. The story of the verse: The devils wrote magic and magic spells on the tongue of Asaf bin Barkhiya. This is what Asaf bin Barkhiya taught King Solomon. Then they buried it under his prayer mat until God took away the kingdom from him and Solomon did not notice. When he died, they extracted it and said to the al-Nas 114:Solomon made them king through it, so learn it. As for the scholars and righteous people of the Children of Israel, they said: God forbid that this be from God’s knowledge. As for the lowly ones, they said: This is Solomon’s knowledge. They turned to learning it and rejected the books of their prophets. Solomon was blamed for it. This was their state and their actions until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and revealed to him the innocence of Solomon. This is what Al-Kalbi said. Al-Suddi said: The devils would ascend to heaven and hear the words of the angels about what would happen on earth of death and other things. They would come to the priests and mix in what they heard seventy lies in every word and tell them about it. [So he wrote that down.] It spread among the Children of Israel that the jinn knew the unseen. So Solomon sent among the people and collected those books and put them in a box and buried it under his throne and said: I will not hear anyone say that the devil knows the unseen except that I will strike his neck. So when Solomon died and the scholars who knew about Solomon and his burying of the books had gone, and he left behind those who came after them, the devil appeared in the form of a human and came to a group of the Children of Israel and said: Shall I guide you to a treasure that you will never eat? They said: Yes. So he went with them and showed them the place under his throne. They dug and he stood in a corner and they said to him: Come closer. He said: I will not be present. If you do not find it, kill me. This is because none of the devils would come near the throne except that he would be burned. So they dug and took out those books. The devil, may God curse him, said: Solomon used to control the jinn, humans, devils and birds with this, then he flew away. The devil was away from them, and it became widespread among the people that Solomon was a magician, and they took those books and used them, so that is why magic is mostly found among the Jews. When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, God Almighty acquitted Solomon of that, and revealed in Solomon’s excuse: And Solomon did not disbelieve in magic. It was said: Solomon was not a disbeliever in magic and did not practice it. But the devils disbelieved. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, Al-Kisa’i, and Hamzah read, but with a light nun and and the devils in the nominative case. The others read but with a stressed nun and and the devils in the accusative case. Likewise, but God killed them 17-Al-Anfal but God threw 17-Al-Anfal. The meaning of but is to negate the past report and affirm the future. They teach people. It was said: The meaning of magic is knowledge and skill in something. God Almighty said: And they said, 'O magician, call upon your Lord for us' 49-Az-Zukhruf, meaning the scholar. The correct view is that magic is a form of deception and imagination. Magic is a reality according to the Sunnis, and most nations agree with it. However, acting upon it is disbelief. It was narrated from Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Magic makes people imagine, sickens, and may kill. He even made retaliation obligatory for those who kill with it. It is the work of Satan. The magician receives it from him by teaching it to him. When he receives it from him, he uses it for something else. It was said: It affects the heart of people, making a human being look like a donkey, or making a donkey look like a dog. The most correct view is that it is imagination. God Almighty said: It appears to him from their magic that they are moving fast. 66-Taha. However, it affects bodies with diseases, death, and madness. Speech has an effect on dispositions and souls. A person may hear something he dislikes, so he becomes angry and furious, and he may become feverish because of it. Some people have died because of speech they heard, so it is like accidents and illnesses that affect bodies. The Almighty said, And what was revealed to the two angels in Babylon, meaning, they act upon what was revealed to the two angels [i.e., inspiration and knowledge, so revelation means inspiration and teaching. It was said: And they followed what was revealed to the two angels]. Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan read the two angels with a kasra on the lam, and Ibn Abbas said: They are two magicians who were in Babylon, and Al-Hasan said: They are two strangers because the angels do not know magic. Babylon is Babylon of Iraq. It was named Babylon because the tongues were confused there when the tower of Nimrod fell, i.e. they were scattered. Ibn Masoud said: Babylon is the land of Kufa, and it was said Mount Damavand. The reading known to the two angels is with the fatha. If it is said: How is it permissible to teach magic from angels? It is said: It has two interpretations: One of them is that they do not intend to teach, but they describe magic and mention its invalidity and command its avoidance, and teaching means informing, so the wretched one abandons their advice and learns magic from their craft. The second interpretation: which is the most correct: that God Almighty tested people with the two angels at that time. Whoever is wretched learns magic from them [and takes it from them and practices it] and disbelieves in it, and whoever is fortunate leaves it and remains in faith, and the two teachers are increased in torment by teaching, so in it is a trial for the teacher [and the learner], and God can test His servants with whatever He wills, for He has the command and the judgment. The Almighty said, Harut and Marut are two Syriac names and they are in the accusative case according to the interpretation of the two angels, except that they were in the accusative case because of their foreignness and their being known. Their story, according to Ibn Abbas and the commentators, was that the angels saw what was ascending to the heavens of the evil deeds of the sons of Adam in the time of Idris, peace be upon him, so they rebuked them and said: These are the ones whom you made a successor on earth and chose them, so they disobey you. So God Almighty said: If I had sent you down to the earth and imposed on you what you imposed on them, you would have imposed what they imposed. So they said: Glory be to you, it was not appropriate for us to disobey you. God Almighty said to them: So choose two angels from among the best of you whom I will send down to the earth. So they chose Harut and Marut, and they were among the most righteous and devout of the angels. Al-Kalbi said: God Almighty said to them: Choose three, so they chose Uzza, who is Harut, and Uzzaya, who is Marut - he changed their names because they committed the sin - and Uzail. So God imposed lust in them and sent them down to the earth and commanded them to judge between people with justice and forbade them from Polytheism, unjust killing, adultery, and drinking alcohol. As for Uzail, when lust entered his heart, he faced his Lord and asked Him to raise him to the heavens. He raised him to the heavens, and He released him. He prostrated for forty years without raising his head, and after that he continued to lower his head out of shame before God Almighty. As for the other two: they remained steadfast in that and used to judge between the people during the day. When evening came, they would mention the greatest name of God and ascend to the heavens. Qatada said: Not even a month had passed before they were tempted. They all said that one day, Venus, who was one of the most beautiful women, argued with them. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: She was from Persia and was a queen in her country. When they saw her, she captured their hearts, so they tried to seduce her, but she refused and left. Then she returned the second day, and they did the same thing, but she refused and said: No, unless you worship what I worship, pray to this idol, kill a soul, and drink wine. They said: There is no way to do these things, for God Almighty has forbidden us from them. So she left, then she returned the third day, and with her was a cup of wine, and in their hearts was the inclination towards her, so they tried to seduce her, so she presented to them what she had said the day before, and they said: Praying to other than God is a great sin, and killing a soul is a great sin, and the lesser of the three is drinking wine. So they drank the wine, became intoxicated, and fell upon the woman, and committed adultery. When they finished, a man saw them, so they killed him. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: They prostrated to the idol, so God transformed Venus into a star. Some of them said: A woman, one of the most beautiful people, came to them, arguing with her husband, so one of them said to the other: Has something fallen into your heart? Like what fell into my soul from the love of this? He said: Yes. He said: Would you like to rule for her against her husband according to what you say? His companion said to him: Do you not know what punishment and torment is with God? His companion said to him: Do you not know what forgiveness and mercy is with God? They asked her herself, and she said: No, unless you kill him. One of them said: Do you not know what punishment and torment is with God? His companion said: Do you not know what forgiveness and mercy is with God? They killed him. Then they asked her herself, and she said: No, I have an idol that I worship. If you pray to it with me, I will. One of them said to his companion the same as the first saying, and his companion said the same, so they prayed with her to it, and she was transformed into a meteor. Ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and Al-Kalbi and Al-Suddi said: She said to them when they asked her about herself: You will not reach me until you tell me what you are ascending to heaven with. They said: In the name of God the Greatest. She said: You will not reach me until you teach me it. One of them said to his companion: Teach it. He said: I fear God, Lord of the worlds. The other said: Then where is the mercy of God Almighty? They taught her that, so she spoke, and she ascended to the sky, so God transformed her into a planet. Some of them believed that it was Venus itself, while others denied this and said: Venus is one of the seven planets that God swore by, saying, So I swear by the receding stars, the moving stars, the sweeping stars 15-At-Takwir. The one who tempted Harut and Marut was a woman who was called Venus for her beauty, but when she refused, God transformed her into a meteor. They said: When evening came, Harut and Marut intended to ascend to the sky, but their wings did not obey them, so they knew what had befallen them of wrath, so they went to Idris, the Prophet, peace be upon him, and informed him of their situation and asked him to intercede for them with God Almighty. They said to him: We have seen you ascend to worship as much as all the people of the earth ascend, so intercede for us with your Lord. Idris, peace be upon him, did that, so God gave them the choice between the torment of this world and the torment of the Hereafter, so they chose the torment of this world, since they knew that it would end, so they were being tormented in Babylon. They differed about the manner of their punishment. Abdullah bin Masoud said: They will be suspended by their hair until the Day of Resurrection. Ata bin Abi Rabah said: Their heads will be directed under their wings. Qatada said: Shackled from their feet to the roots of their thighs. Mujahid said: They will be placed in a well filled with fire. Omar bin Saad said: Upside down and beaten with iron whips. It was narrated that a man went to Harut and Marut to learn magic, but he found them hanging by their feet, their eyes blue, their skin black, and there were only four fingers between their tongues and the water, and they were being tortured with thirst. When he saw that, he was terrified by their location, so he said: There is no god but God. When they heard his words, they said to him: Who are you? He said: A man from the people. They said: Which nation are you from? He said: From the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: He is the Prophet of the Hour, and the end of our torment has drawn near. The Almighty said: And they do not teach anyone meaning anyone, and from is a connection to until they advise him first and say, ‘We are only a trial’ a test and trial so do not disbelieve meaning do not learn magic and practice it and thus disbelieve. The root of the word fitna is testing and examination, from their saying: I melted gold and silver if you melted them in fire, to distinguish the good from the bad. The word fitna is singular, and there are two of them, because fitna is a source, and sources are not dualized or pluralized. It was said that they say We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve seven times. Ata and Al-Suddi said: If he insists on learning, they say to him: Go to these ashes and approach them, and a bright light will emerge from them in the sky, and that is the light of knowledge, and something black like smoke will descend until it enters his ears, and that is the wrath of God Almighty. Mujahid said: No one can reach Harut and Marut, and a devil will differ between them on every issue, and they will learn from them that by which they will separate a man from his wife, which is that each one will be taken from his companion, and each one will be hated by his companion. God Almighty said: And they, it was said: the magicians, and it was said: the devils, can harm anyone with it, meaning with magic, except by God’s permission, meaning with His knowledge and creation, so the magician bewitches and God is. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Its meaning is except by His decree, power and will. And they learn what harms them means that magic harms them “and does not benefit them. And they have certainly known” meaning the Jews that whoever buys it meaning they choose magic has no share in the Hereafter meaning in Paradise and evil is that for which they have sold they sold their souls their share, since they chose magic and disbelief over religion and truth if they only knew. If it is said: Did He not say and they certainly knew for whoever buys it then what is the meaning of His Most High’s saying if they only knew after He informed us that they knew? It was said: By His saying and they certainly knew He meant the devils and His saying if they only knew He meant the Jews. It was said: Both of them refer to the Jews, meaning: But when they did not act upon what they knew, it was as if they did not know.
2:103: 103. And if they had believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an, and feared Judaism and magic, the reward from God would have been better for them, if they only knew.
2:104: 104. The Almighty said: "O you who have believed, do not say, 'Ra'ina' This is because the Muslims used to say, Ra'ina, O Messenger of God, from the word mara'a, meaning, give us your attention, meaning, devote your hearing to our words. It is said, ar'a'a ila al-shay', ra'ahu, and ra'ahu, meaning, listen to it and listen to it. This word shay'an was ugly in the language of the Jews, and it was said that its meaning to them was, listen, not hear." It was said: It is from rashness, if they wanted to make a person foolish, they would say to him: Ra’ina, meaning, you fool. So when the Jews heard this word from the Muslims, they said among themselves: We used to insult Muhammad secretly, but now we announce it. So they would come to him and say: Ra’ina, O Muhammad, and they would laugh among themselves. Sa’d ibn Mu’adh heard it and understood it, and he knew their language, so he said to the Jews: If I hear one of you say it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I will strike off his head. They said: Do you not say it? So God Almighty revealed: Do not say, ‘Ra’ina’ so that the Jews would not find a way to insult the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And say, ‘Unzurna’ meaning, look at us. It was also said: Wait for us and be patient with us. It is said: I looked at so-and-so and I waited for him. From this is the saying of God Almighty: Wait for us so that we may take from your light 13-Al-Hadid. Mujahid said: Its meaning is: We understood it. “And listen” to what you are commanded to do and obey. And for the disbelievers meaning the Jews is a painful punishment.
2:105: 105. The Almighty said: The disbelievers among the People of the Scripture do not wish This is because when the Muslims said to their Jewish allies: Believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said: What you are calling us to is not better than what we are in, and we would have liked it if it were better. So God revealed, as a refutation of them, The disbelievers among the People of the Scripture do not wish meaning what the disbelievers among the People of the Scripture, meaning the Jews, nor the polytheists love and wish, that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord meaning good and prophethood, and from is a connection between and God chooses for His mercy with His prophethood whoever He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty and bounty is initially kindness without a cause. It was said: What is meant by mercy is Islam and guidance. It was also said: The meaning of the verse is that God Almighty sent the prophets from the descendants of Isaac, but when He sent the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the descendants of Ishmael, this did not bring about the love and affection of the Jews, so the verse was revealed. As for the polytheists, their affection was not brought about because he came to mislead them and criticize their gods.
2:106: 106. The Almighty said, We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten. This is because the polytheists said: Muhammad does not command his companions to do something and then forbid them from it and command them to do something contrary to what he says except on his own initiative. He says [today a statement and returns from it tomorrow as God has informed. <<And when We substitute a verse for another - and God knows best] what He sends down, they say, You are only an inventor.>101- An-Nahl. And He sent down, We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten, so He explained the wisdom behind abrogation with this verse. Abrogation in the language has two meanings: One of them means conversion and transfer, and from it is the abrogation of the book, which is to transfer from one book to another. So in this way, the entire Qur’an is abrogated because it was copied from the Preserved Tablet. The second: It means lifting. It is said: The sun abrogated the shadow, meaning it took it away and nullified it. Based on this, some of the Qur’an is abrogating and some of it is abrogated, which is what is meant by the verse. This has several aspects, one of which is: that the line is confirmed and the ruling is abrogated, such as the verse of the will to relatives. The verse of the waiting period for death by one year, the verse of alleviation in fighting, the verse of the one who is tested, and the like. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said about the Almighty’s saying, We do not abrogate a verse, what we confirm its writing and change its ruling, such as the verse of stoning. Among them is that its recitation is lifted from the Qur’an and from the hearts, as narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah bin Sahl bin Hanif: that a group of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, stood up one night to recite a surah, but they did not mention from it anything except In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. So they went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, That is a surah whose recitation and rulings were lifted. It was said: Surat Al-Ahzab was like Surat Al-Baqarah, so most of it was lifted in recitation and ruling. Then, among the rulings that were abrogated, some were lifted and another was established in its place, just as the direction of prayer was abrogated from Jerusalem to the Kaaba, and the will for relatives was abrogated by inheritance, and the waiting period for death was abrogated from one year to four months and ten, and the patience of one for ten in fighting was abrogated by the patience of two, and among them is what is lifted and nothing else is established. His position is like the examination of women. Abrogation only applies to commands and prohibitions, not to report. As for the meaning of the verse, His saying, Whatever verse We abrogate, the general reading is with a fatha on the noon and a kasra on the seen from abrogation, meaning: We remove it. Ibn Amir read it with a damma on the noon and a kasra on the seen from abrogation, and it has two aspects: One of them: to make it like the abrogated. The second: that we make it a copy for him [it is said: I copied the book, meaning I wrote it, and someone else copied it if you made it a copy for him] or we forget it meaning we forget it in your heart. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: We leave it and do not abrogate it. God the Almighty said: They forgot God, so He forgot them 67- At-Tawbah, meaning they abandoned Him, so He abandoned them. It was also said: We forget it means: We order it to be abandoned. It is said: You forgot something if you ordered it to be abandoned. So the first abrogation is the lifting of the ruling and the establishment of something else in its place. Forgetting is an abrogator without establishing something else in its place. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read or we postpone it with a fat-ha on the first nun and a hamza on the seen, meaning we delay it and do not change it. It is said: We postponed God’s lifespan and God postponed his lifespan. There are two sayings that have the same meaning: One of them: We lift its recitation and delay its ruling, as He did in the verse of stoning. Based on this, the first abrogation means lifting the recitation and ruling. The second saying: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Ata’ said: As for what was abrogated from a verse, it is what was revealed from the Qur’an, we made it from the copy, or we postpone it, meaning we delay it and leave it in the Preserved Tablet and it does not come down. We have brought something better than it meaning something that is more beneficial for you, easier for you, and greater for your reward, not that one verse is better than another, because the speech of God is one and all of it is good. Or similar to it in benefit and reward. So whatever was abrogated to something easier is easier to do, and whatever was abrogated to something more difficult is greater in reward. Do you not know that God has power over all things? From abrogation and substitution, its wording is a question, but its meaning is a statement, meaning: you know.
2:107: 107. “Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have not, O group of disbelievers, besides God, any protector or helper, other than God...
2:108: 108. His statement: Or do you want to ask your Messenger? was revealed about the Jews when they said: O Muhammad, bring us a book from heaven in its entirety, just as Moses brought the Torah. So God Almighty said: Or do you want? meaning do you want? The mim is a connection. It was also said: Rather, you want to ask your Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as Moses was asked before. His people asked him: Show us God openly. It was also said: They asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: We will not believe you until you bring God and the angels face to face, just as Moses was asked by his people and they said: Show us God openly. In it is a prohibition on them from asking ugly questions after the evidence and proofs had appeared. And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief replaces faith with disbelief has certainly strayed from the right path he erred in the middle of the road. It was also said: He intended the right path.
2:109: 109. The Almighty said: Many of the People of the Scripture wish The verse was revealed about a group of Jews who said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and Ammar ibn Yasir after the Battle of UHud 11:If you were on the truth, you would not have been defeated. So return to our religion, for we are more guided than you. Ammar said to them: How can we break a covenant with you? They said: Severe. He said: Severe. He said: I have vowed not to disbelieve in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as long as I live. The Jews said: As for this one, he has converted to Islam. Hudhayfah said: As for me, I am satisfied with God as my Lord, Muhammad as my Prophet, Islam as my religion, the Qur’an as my Imam, the Kaaba as my Qiblah, and the believers as my brothers. Then they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have both achieved goodness and succeeded. Then God Almighty revealed: And many of the People of the Scripture wish meaning many of the People of the Scripture among the Jews wished and wanted that they could turn you back O company of believers to disbelievers after you have believed, out of envy accusative of the source, meaning they envy you out of envy from themselves meaning from their own volition and God did not command them to do that, after the truth has become clear to them in the Torah that the words of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were true and his religion was true. So pardon so leave and overlook and overlook. Pardon means erasure, and overlooking means turning away. This was before the verse of fighting until God brings about His command with His punishment: killing and capturing the children of Israel. Qurayzah, and the expulsion and banishment of Banu Nadir, as Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said. Qatada said: It is his command to fight them in his saying: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day until his saying: and they will be humbled 29-Tawbah. Ibn Kaysan said: With his knowledge and judgment on them, he judged some of them to Islam and some of them to be killed, taken captive and paid the jizyah. Indeed, God is over all things competent.
2:110: 110. And establish prayer and give zakah, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with God. It was said that what he meant by good is money, as in the Almighty's saying, If he leaves behind any good 180-Al-Baqarah, and what he meant by zakah and charity, you will find it with God, even the fruit and the morsel, like Uhud. Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do.
2:111: 111 - His statement, And they said, 'None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew,' meaning a Jew. Al-Farra' said: The extra ya' was deleted and the verb was returned to the Jewishness. Al-Akhfash said: Hood is the plural of ha'id, like a'id and ud, and ha'il and hawl, or Christians, because the Jews said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew and there is no religion except the religion of Judaism. The Christians said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Christian and there is no religion except the religion of Christianity. It was said: It was revealed about the delegation of Najran, who were Christians and gathered in the council of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the Jews, and some of them lied. God Almighty said: Those are their desires, meaning their false desires that they wished for from God without right. Say, O Muhammad, bring, its root is bring, “your proof,” your argument for what you claim, if you are truthful.
2:112: 112- Then he said in response to them, Yes, whoever submits his face meaning that the matter is not as they said, rather the ruling is for Islam, and only he who submits his face to God will enter Paradise, meaning that he sincerely devoted his religion to God. It was said: sincerely devoted his worship to God. It was said: humbled himself and was humble to God. The origin of Islam is submission and humility, and the face was singled out because if he is generous with his face in prostration, he will not be stingy with the rest of his limbs and he is a doer of good in his work. It was said: a believer. It was said: sincere. "Then he will have his reward with his Lord. And no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve."
2:113: 113- And His statement, And the Jews said, 'The Christians are not upon anything,' was revealed about the Jews of Medina and the Christians of Najran. That is because when the delegation of the people of Najran came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the rabbis of the Jews came to them: They debated until their voices rose. The Jews said to them, 'You are not upon anything of the religion,' and they disbelieved in Jesus and the Gospel. The Christians said to them, 'You are not upon anything of the religion,' and they disbelieved in Moses and the Torah. So God Almighty revealed, And the Christians said, 'The Jews are not upon anything,' and they recite the Scripture. Both groups recite the Scripture. It was said that its meaning is that there is no such difference in their books, so their recitation of the Scripture and their opposition to what is in it indicates that they are upon falsehood. Thus said those who do not know, meaning: their fathers who have passed away. Like their statement, Mujahid said: meaning: the common Christians. Muqatil said: meaning: the polytheists of the Arabs. Likewise they said about their Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions: that they are not upon anything of the religion. Ata’ said: There were nations before the Jews and Christians, such as the people of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shuaib, peace be upon them. They said to their prophet: He is not on anything. So God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection, He will decide between the truth and falsehood in what they used to differ of religion.
2:114: 114. His saying, And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being remembered? The verse was revealed about Titus bin Aspasbanus the Roman and his companions, because they invaded the Children of Israel and killed their children, burned the Torah, and destroyed the Holy House, throwing carcasses into it and slaughtering pigs in it, so it was in ruins until the Muslims rebuilt it during the days of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. Qatada and Al-Suddi said: It was Bukhtanasr and his companions who invaded the Jews and destroyed the Holy House, and they were aided in that by the Christians, Titus the Roman and his companions from the Romans. Al-Suddi said: Because they killed John the Baptist John the Baptist, and Qatada said: Some of the Jews urged them to aid Bukhtanasr the Babylonian the Zoroastrian, so God revealed: And who is more unjust meaning more ungrateful and more obstinate than he who prevents the mosques of God meaning the Holy House and its sanctuaries from being mentioned therein and strives worked in its destruction? It is not for them to enter it except in fear. This is because the Holy House is a place of pilgrimage for the Christians and a place of their visitation. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: No Roman entered it, meaning the Holy House after its construction, except in fear / if he had known about it, he would have been killed. Qatada and Muqatil said: No Christian should enter the Holy House except in disguise, if he had been able to do so, he would have been punished. Al-Suddi said: They were frightened by the jizya. It was said: This is a report with the meaning of an order, that is, abort them by jihad until none of them enters it except fearing killing and captivity, that is, what is appropriate. For them in this world is disgrace, torment and humiliation. Qatada said: It is killing for the combatant and the jizya for the dhimmi. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said that their three cities will be conquered: Constantinople, Rome, and Amorium. And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment, which is the Fire. Ata and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: It was revealed about the polytheists of Mecca, and what was meant by the mosques was the Sacred Mosque. They prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from performing Hajj and praying in it in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. If they were prevented from filling it with remembrance, then they sought to destroy it. For them it is not proper to enter it except in fear, meaning the people of Mecca. He said: I will open it for you so that you may enter it and you will be more deserving of it than them. So he opened it for them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered a crier to call out: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year. This was their fear, and it is established in the Shari’ah that no polytheist will be able to enter the Sacred Sanctuary. For them in this world is disgrace. Humiliation, disgrace, killing, captivity and exile.
2:115: 115. The Almighty said: To God belong the East and the West, so wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: A group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on a journey before the qiblah was changed to the Kaaba. Fog struck them and the time for prayer came, so they sought the qiblah and prayed. When the fog cleared, it became clear to them that they had not been right and that they had been mistaken in their seeking. When they returned, they asked the Messenger of God about that, and this verse was revealed. Abdullah bin Omar, may God be pleased with them both, said: It was revealed about the traveler who prays voluntary prayers wherever his mount takes him. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih al-Sarakhsi, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray on his mount while traveling, wherever it was facing.” Ikrimah said: It was revealed about changing the Qiblah. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: When the Qiblah was changed to the Kaaba, the Jews taunted the believers and said: They do not have a known Qiblah, so sometimes they face this way and sometimes that way. So God revealed this verse. Mujahid and Al-Hasan said: When it was revealed: And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you’ 60-Ghafir, they said: Where should we call upon Him? So God revealed: And to God belong the East and the West as a kingdom and a creation. So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God meaning wherever you turn your faces, there, meaning: there is the mercy of God. Al-Kalbi said: Then there is God, He knows and sees, and the face is a connection like the saying of God: Everything will perish except His Face 88-Al-Qasas, meaning except Him. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatada, and Muqatil ibn Hibban said: Then there is the Qiblah of God, and the face, the direction, and the direction are the Qiblah. It was said: the pleasure of God Almighty. God is Vast, meaning He is Rich and gives generously. Al-Farra’ said: The Vast is the Generous One whose giving encompasses everything. Al-Kalbi said: Vast in forgiveness and Knowing of their intentions wherever they pray and supplicate.
2:116: 116. The Almighty said: And they said, ‘God has taken a son.’ Ibn Amir read They said, ‘God has taken a son.’ Without the waw, and the others read it with the waw. [And they said, ‘God has taken a son.’] It was revealed about the Jews of Medina when they said, Ezra is the son of God, and about the Christians of Najran when they said, The Messiah is the son of God, and about the polytheists of Arabia when they said, The angels are the daughters of God. Glory be to Him. He is glorified and exalted. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abu Al-Yaman, that Shu`ayb narrated from Abdul Rahman bin Abi Hassan, from Nafi` bin Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty said: The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so, and he insulted Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, he claimed that I am not able to restore him as he was, and as for his insulting Me, it is his saying that I have a son. Glory be to Me that I should take a wife or a son.” God the Almighty said: Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth as servants and kings. All are obedient to Him. Mujahid, Ata’ and As-Suddi said: Obedient. Ikrimah and Muqatil said: Acknowledging their servitude to Him. Ibn Kaysan said: Standing in the testimony. The origin of Qunut is standing. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best prayer is prolonged Qunut. They differed regarding the ruling of the verse. A group held that the ruling of the verse is specific. Muqatil said: It refers to Ezra, the Messiah and the angels. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It refers to the people of His obedience, not to the rest of the people. A group held that the ruling of the verse is general for all creation because all requires encompassing the thing so that nothing is excluded from it. Then they took two paths regarding the infidels: Mujahid said: Their shadows prostrate to God against their will. God the Almighty said: And their shadows in the mornings and the evenings 13:15. As-Suddi said: This is the Day of Resurrection, and its proof is: And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. 111-Taha It was said obedient submissive and obedient to what they were created for.
2:117: 117. The Almighty’s saying: Originator of the heavens and the earth meaning He is their Creator and Originator without a previous example. And when He decrees a matter meaning He measures it, and it was said: He perfects it and measures it [and perfects it, and the root of the word qada is to finish, and from it it is said about someone who dies: it was decreed for him because he was finished with the world, and from it is the decree and decree of God] because He finished with it in terms of estimation and management. He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. Ibn ‘Amir read Be,’ and it is with the accusative of the letter “nun in all places except in Al-‘Imran: “Be,’ and it is. The truth is from your Lord.” And in Surat al-An’am 6:Be,’ and it is, His saying, the truth. He only put it in the accusative because the answer to the command with the letter fa is accusative. [Al-Kisa’i agreed with him in An-Nahl and Ya-Seen], and the others read it in the nominative with the meaning so it is. If it is said, how did he say so he only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is when the nonexistent is not addressed? Ibn Al-Anbari said: Its meaning is that he only says to it, i.e. for the sake of its creation. So based on this, the meaning of the address is lost. It was said: Even though it is nonexistent, since its existence was determined and it will inevitably be, it was like the existent, so the address is correct.
2:118: 118. The Almighty said: And those who do not know said Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Jews, and Mujahid said: The Christians, and Qatada said: The polytheists of the Arabs If only "why does God not speak to us" clearly that you are His Messenger. And everything in the Qur'an (if only) has the meaning of why, except one, which is His saying: "If only he was among those who glorify God 143-Saffat meaning if only there were or a sign comes to us" is an indication and sign of your truthfulness in your claim to prophethood. God Almighty said: Thus said those before them meaning the disbelievers of the past nations like their saying, their hearts are alike meaning they resemble one another in disbelief, cruelty, and seeking the impossible We have certainly made clear the verses for a people who are certain.
2:119: 119. Indeed, We have sent you with the truth meaning with the truth, as He said, And they ask you, is it true? 53-Yunus, meaning truthful. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Its proof is the Qur'an, Rather, they denied the truth when it came to them 5-Q. Ibn Kaysan said: Its proof is Islam and its laws, its proof is the Almighty's saying, And say, The truth has come 81-Al-Isra'. Muqatil said: Its meaning is that We did not send you in vain, but rather We sent you with the truth, as He said, And We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except with truth 85-Al-Hijr.
