The Almighty said, Bringing good tidings meaning, bringing good tidings to My friends and those who obey Me of the noble reward, and a warner meaning, warning and frightening My enemies and those who disobey Me of the painful punishment. Nafi’ and Ya’qub read and do not ask as a prohibition. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: That is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day: I wish I knew what my parents did, so this verse was revealed. It was said that it means, Do not ask about the evil of so-and-so, for it is beyond what you think, and it is not a prohibition. The others read and do not ask in the nominative case as a negation, meaning, You are not responsible for them, as God Almighty said, You are only responsible for conveying the message, and upon Us is the reckoning 20-Al Imran, about the companions of Hellfire, and Hellfire is the most part of the fire.
2:120: 120. God the Almighty said: “And never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you until you follow their religion. Say: ‘Indeed, the guidance of God is the [only] guidance.’” This is because they were asking the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a truce and hoping that if he gave them time, they would follow him. So God the Almighty revealed this verse, the meaning of which is that if you make a truce with them, they will not be pleased with it. They only ask for it as an excuse and will not be pleased with you unless you follow their religion. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: This is about the qiblah. The Jews of Medina and the Christians of Najran were hoping that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pray toward their qiblah. When God changed the qiblah toward the Kaaba, they despaired of him agreeing with them on their religion. So God the Almighty revealed: And never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you except with Judaism, nor will the Christians except with Christianity. The religion is the way, and if you follow their desires, it was said that the address was to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what was meant by it was the nation, like His saying: If you associate others with God, your work will surely become worthless Az-Zumar 65. After what has come to you of knowledge is the clarification that the religion of God is Islam. The Qiblah is the Qiblah of Abraham, peace be upon him, which is the Kaaba. You have against God neither protector nor helper.
2:121: 121. Those to whom We gave the Scripture. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It was revealed about the people of the ship who came with Ja’far ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and they were forty men, thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight from the monks of Ash-Sham, including Bahira. Ad-Dahhak said: They are those who believed from the Jews, Abdullah ibn Salam, Sa’iyya ibn Amr, Tamam ibn Yahudah, Asad and Asid ibn Ka’b, Ibn Yamin, and Abdullah ibn Suriya. Qatada and Ikrimah said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: They are the believers in general. They recite it with its true recitation. Al-Kalbi said: They describe it in their books with its true description for whoever asks them from the people, and the ha refers to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The others said: It refers to the Book. They differed about its meaning. Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, said: They recite it as it was revealed and do not distort it, and they make lawful what it makes lawful and forbid what it forbids. Al-Hasan said: They act according to its clear verses, believe in its ambiguous verses, and entrust the knowledge of what is unclear to them to its Knower. Mujahid said: They follow it with its true meaning. Follow him. He said, Those are the ones who believe in it, and those who disbelieve in it - it is those who are the losers.
2:122: 122. O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.
2:123: 123. And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be aided.
2:124: 124. The Almighty said: And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands, and he fulfilled them. Ibn Amir read Abraham with an alif in most places, and it is a foreign name, and therefore it is not in the genitive case. He is Ibrahim bin Tarakh bin Nakhur, and he was born in Susa in the land of Ahwaz, and it was said Babylon, and it was said: Kufi, and it was said: [Lashkar], and it was said Harran, and his father moved him to the land of Babylon, the land of Nimrod bin Canaan, and the meaning of the test is the test, examination, and command, and God tests the servants not to know their conditions with the test, because He knows them, but to know the servants' conditions so that they know each other. They differed about the words that God tested Abraham, peace be upon him, with. Ikrimah and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said: They are thirty words that He called the laws of Islam, and no one was tested with them and performed them all except Abraham, so he wrote for him the innocence. God Almighty said: And Abraham who fulfilled 37-An-Najm. Ten in the innocence those who repent and worship to the end, and ten in the confederates Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, and ten in Surat Al-Mu’minun in His statement: The believers have succeeded the verses, and His statement except those who pray in the questioner asked. Tawus said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: God tested him with ten things, which are: The fitrah is five for the head: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, inhaling water into the nose, using the siwak, and parting the hair, and five for the body: trimming the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, and cleaning oneself with water. And in the hadith: ((That Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to trim the moustache, the first to be circumcised, the first to clip the nails, and the first to see gray hair. When he saw it, he said: O Lord, what is this? He [Samah] said: Dignity. He said: O Lord, increase my dignity.)) Mujahid said: They are the verses that come after it in the words of God Almighty: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people 124-Al-Baqarah to the end of the story. Al-Rabi’ and Qatada said: The rituals of Hajj. Al-Hasan said: God tested him with seven things: with the planets, the moon, and the sun, so he looked well at them and knew that his Lord is eternal and will not disappear, and with the fire, so he was patient with it, and with the migration and with the sacrifice of his son and with circumcision, so he was patient with it. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the saying of Abraham and Ishmael when they were raising the Kaaba: Our Lord, accept from us 127-Al-Baqarah the verse, so they raised it with Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God [and God is Great]. Yaman bin Rabab said: They are the arguments of his people. God Almighty said: And an argument His people to the Almighty’s saying - And that was Our argument which We gave to Abraham 83-Al-An’am. It was said that it is His saying: He who created me and He guides me 78-Ash-Shu’ara’ to the end of the verses. He completed them. Qatada said: He performed them. Ad-Dahhak said: He performed them. And he said: [Nu’man] acted upon them. God the Almighty said: “He said: ‘I will make you a leader for mankind’ to be followed in goodness.” He said: Abraham “And from my descendants” meaning from my children also, so make from them leaders to be followed in goodness.” He said: God the Almighty “My covenant does not reach” does not affect the wrongdoers. Hamzah and Hafs read it with a sukoon on the ya’ and the rest read it with a fatha, meaning whoever among them is a wrongdoer, it does not affect him. Ata’ bin Abi Rabah said: My covenant is My mercy. Al-Suddi said: My prophethood. It was said: It is the imamate. Mujahid said: It is not permissible for an oppressor to be obeyed in his oppression. The meaning of the verse is: What I have entrusted to you of prophethood and imamate will not be attained by whoever among your children is a wrongdoer. It was said: By the covenant he meant security from the Fire, and by the wrongdoer is the polytheist, as God the Almighty said: Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing, those will have security. 82-Al-An’am.
2:125: 125. God Almighty said, And when We made the House meaning the Kaaba a place of assembly for mankind a place of reference for them. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said: They come to it from every side and perform Hajj. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said: A refuge and a shelter. Qatada and Ikrimah said: A gathering place. And a place of safety meaning a place of safety in which they are safe from the harm of the polytheists, for they did not attack the people of Mecca and say: They are the people of God and attack those around it, as God Almighty said: Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary while people are being snatched away all around them? 67-Al-Ankabut. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Ali bin Abdullah, I told Jarir, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: “This country was made sacred by God on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorns are not to be cut, its game is not to be frightened, its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who recognizes it, and its seclusion is not to be visited.” Al-Abbas said: O Messenger of God, except for the idhkhir, for it is for their culinary purposes and for their homes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Except for the idhkhir. The Almighty said: And they took Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a fatha on the kha’ as a statement, and the rest read it with a kasra on the kha’ as a command, from the station of Abraham a place of prayer. Ibn Yaman said: The entire mosque is the station of Abraham, and Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: The entire sanctuary is the station of Abraham, and it was said: He meant by the station of Abraham all the sites of Hajj, such as ‘Arafah, Muzdalifah, and all the other sites. The correct view is that the Station of Abraham is the stone in the mosque towards which the imams pray. It is the stone on which Abraham, peace be upon him, stood when building the House. It was said that the traces of his toes were visible on it, but they were erased from the frequent wiping with the hands. Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Suddi said: They were commanded to pray at the Station of Abraham, but they were not commanded to wipe it or kiss it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Musaddad, on the authority of Yahya bin Hamid, on the authority of Anas, who said: Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: ((I agreed with God in three things - or my Lord agreed with me in three things - I said, O Messenger of God, why don’t you take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer? So God Almighty revealed: And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. And I said, O Messenger of God, the righteous and the wicked enter upon you, so why don’t you order the mothers of the believers to wear the hijab? So God Almighty revealed the verse of the hijab. He said, and I was informed of the Prophet’s rebuke of some of his wives, so I went to them and said to them: If you stop, or God will replace him with better wives than you, so God Almighty revealed: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you (5- At-Tahrim). Muhammad bin Ismail also narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Auf, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: I agreed with my Lord in three things. I said, O Messenger of God, if only I had taken the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. Then the verse was revealed: And take, [O Muhammad], the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. As for the beginning of the story of the station, Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When Abraham, peace be upon him, brought Ishmael and Hagar and placed them in Mecca, and some time passed, and the Jurhumites settled there and Ishmael married a woman from them and Hagar died, Abraham asked Sarah’s permission to visit Hagar, and she gave him permission and stipulated that he not leave, so Abraham went to Mecca and Hagar had died, so he went to Ishmael’s house and said to his wife: Where is your companion? She said: He went hunting, and Ishmael, peace be upon him, used to go out of the sanctuary to hunt, so Abraham said to her: Do you have any hospitality? She said: I do not have any hospitality, and he asked her about their livelihood? She said: We are in hardship and difficulty, so she complained to him and he said to her: When your husband comes, greet him and tell him to change the threshold of his door, so Abraham went and Ishmael came and found the scent of his father, so he said [to his wife: Has anyone come to you? She said: An old man came to me with such and such description, as if she was making light of his matter. He said] What did he say to you? She said: He said: Give my greetings to your husband and tell him to change the threshold of his door. My father said that, and he has ordered me to leave you and go back to your family. So he divorced her and married another of them. Abraham stayed as long as God willed him to stay. Then he asked Sarah's permission to visit Ishmael, and she gave him permission but stipulated that he should not come down. Abraham, peace be upon him, came until he reached Ishmael's door and said to his wife: Where is your companion? She said: He went hunting and will come back now, God willing. Come down, may God have mercy on you. He said: Do you have any hospitality? She said: Yes. So she came with milk and meat. He asked her about their livelihood? She said: We are well and comfortable. So he invoked blessings upon them. If she had brought that day bread of wheat or barley and dates, it would have been the land of God with the most wheat, barley or dates. She said to him: Come down so I can wash your head. But he did not come down. So she brought him the station and placed it on his right side. He put his foot on it and washed the right side of his head. Then she moved to his left side and washed the left side of his head, and the traces of his feet remained on it. Then he said to her: When your husband comes, greet him and tell him that the threshold of your door has been straightened. When Ishmael came, he smelled the scent of his father and said to his wife: Has anyone come to you? She said: Yes, an old man with the most handsome face and the best scent. He said to me such and such and I said to him such and such. She washed his head and this is the place where his feet were. He said: That was Abraham, the prophet, my father, and you are the threshold. He ordered me to hold you. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair / on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Then he stayed away from them for as long as God willed, then he came after that and Ishmael was sharpening arrows under a palm tree near Zamzam. When he saw him, he went to him and they did as a father does to his son and a son does to his father. Then he said: O Ishmael, God Almighty has commanded me to do something that will help me with it? He said: I will help you. He said: God has commanded me to build a house here. At that point, they raised the foundations of the house, and Ishmael began to bring stones and Abraham built until the building was high. He brought this stone and placed it for him, and Abraham stood on the stone of the station while he was building and Ishmael was handing him the stones and they were saying: Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And in the hadith: (The Corner and the Station are two rubies from the rubies of Paradise, and had the hands of the polytheists not touched them, they would have illuminated what is between the east and the west.) God the Almighty said: And We enjoined upon Abraham and Ishmael meaning We commanded them and inspired them. It was said: He was named Ishmael because Abraham used to call upon God to grant him a son and he would say: Hear, O El, and El is God. So when he was granted a son, God named him with it. Purify My House meaning the Kaaba, He added it to him specifically and preferably, meaning build it on purity and monotheism. Saeed bin Jubayr and Ata’ said: Purify it from idols, doubts, and false speech. It was said: By its steam and its creation. The people of Medina and Hafs read My House with a fat-ha on the ya’ here and in Surat Al-Hajj. Hafs added in Surat Nuh: For those who circumambulate those who circle around it, and those who stay there those who reside nearby, and and those who bow the plural of bowing, and prostration the plural of prostrating, and they are the worshippers. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Those who circumambulate are the strangers, and those who stay there are the people of Mecca. Ata’, Mujahid, and Ikrimah said: Circumambulation is better for strangers, and prayer is better for the people of Mecca.
2:126: 126. God the Almighty said: “And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, make this’ meaning Mecca, and it was said: the Sacred Sanctuary ‘a secure city’ meaning one where its people are safe, ‘and provide its people with fruits’. He only prayed that because it was in a valley without crops. In the stories, it is mentioned that At-Ta’if was one of the cities of Ash-Sham in Jordan, so when Abraham, peace be upon him, prayed this prayer, God the Almighty ordered Gabriel, peace be upon him, to uproot it from its roots and circle it around the House seven times, then put it in the place where it is now, and from it most of the fruits of Mecca are. ‘Whoever among them believes in God and the Last Day’ is a prayer for the believers in particular. God the Almighty said: ‘And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little’ Ibn ‘Amir read ‘I will grant him enjoyment’ lightly with a damma on the hamza, and the rest read it with emphasis, and their meaning is the same, ‘a little’ meaning I will also provide the disbeliever for a little until the end of his life. This is because God the Almighty promised provision for all of creation, both believers and disbelievers. He only restricted it to little because the enjoyment of this world is little. ‘Then I will compel him’ meaning I will force him in the Hereafter ‘to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination’ meaning the return to which he will go. Mujahid said: He found At the station there is a book in which it says: God is the owner of Mecca, which He created on the day He created the sun and the moon, and He made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and He surrounded it with seven upright angels, whose sustenance comes to them from three paths, and they are blessed in meat and water.
2:127: 127. The Almighty said: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House. The narrators said: God Almighty created the location of the House two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam on the water, so the earth spread out from beneath it. When God sent Adam, peace be upon him, down to the earth, he felt lonely, so he complained to God Almighty, so God sent down the Frequented House from its rubies from the rubies of Paradise, with two doors of green emerald, an eastern door and a western door, and he placed it on the location of the House and said: O Adam, I am sending down to you a House that you may circumambulate as one circumambulates around My Throne, and you may pray at it as one prays at My Throne. And the Stone was sent down, and it was white, but it turned black from the touch of menstruation in the pre-Islamic period. So Adam headed from the land of India to Mecca on foot, and God appointed an angel to guide him to the House, so he performed the Hajj and performed the rituals. When he finished, the angels met him and said: Your Hajj is good, O Adam, for we performed the Hajj to this House two thousand years before you. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Adam performed the Hajj forty times from India to Mecca on foot, and it remained like that until the days of The Flood, so God Almighty raised him to the fourth heaven, and seventy thousand angels enter it every day, and they do not return to it. And He sent Gabriel, peace be upon him, until he hid the Black Stone in Mount Abu Qubais to protect it from drowning, so the location of the House was empty until the time of Abraham. Then God Almighty ordered Abraham, after Ishmael and Isaac were born to him, to build a House in which he would be remembered, so he asked God Almighty to show him its location, so God sent the Sakina to guide him to the location of the House, and it is a strong wind with two heads like a snake, so He ordered Abraham to build where the Sakina would settle, so Abraham followed it until they came to Mecca, and the Sakina moved over the location of the House like a scroll. This is what Ali and Al-Hasan said. Ibn Abbas said: God Almighty sent a cloud the size of the Kaaba, and it began to move and Abraham walked in its shade until it reached Mecca and stopped at the location of the House, and Abraham was called from it to build in its shade, neither increasing nor decreasing. It was said: God sent Gabriel to guide him to the location of the House, as God Almighty said: And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, so Abraham and Ishmael built the House, and Abraham was building it and Ishmael was handing him the stone. This is what God Almighty said: And when Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations of the House, meaning he founded it, and the singular is base. Al-Kisa’i said: The walls of the House. Ibn Abbas said: The House was built from five mountains: Mount Sinai, Mount Zeit, and Lebanon, which is a mountain in the Levant, and Al-Judi, which is a mountain in the Arabian Peninsula. They built its foundations from Hira, which is a mountain in Mecca. When Abraham reached the location of the Black Stone, he said to Ishmael: Bring me a beautiful stone that will be a sign for the people. So he brought him a stone and said: Bring me something better than this. So Ishmael went looking for it. Abu Qubays shouted: O Abraham, you have a trust with me, so take it. So he took the Black Stone and put it in its place. It was said: God Almighty built a house in the sky, which is the Frequented House, and it is called Ad-Dirah, and He ordered the angels to build the Kaaba on earth opposite it according to its size and likeness. It was said: The first to build the Kaaba was Adam, and he disappeared during the time of the Flood, then God revealed it to Abraham so that he could build it. His saying: Our Lord, accept from us contains an implication, meaning that they say: Our Lord, accept from us our construction. Indeed, You are the Hearer of our supplication, the Knower of our intentions.
2:128: 128. Our Lord, make us Muslims [in submission] to You monotheists, obedient, sincere, and submissive to You. And of our descendants meaning our children is a nation a group and the nation is the followers of the prophets submitting to you subject to you. And show us means we knew and recognized. Ibn Kathir read it with a sukoon on the ra', Abu Amr read it with a short vowel, and the rest read it with a kasra. Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr agreed with the sukoon in Ha Mim as-Sajdah. Its original form is ar'ina, but the hamza was deleted in order to make it lighter, and its vowel was transferred to the ra'. Whoever read it with a sukoon said: The hamza was gone, so its vowel was gone. Our rites means the laws of our religion and the rituals of our Hajj. It was said: The places of our pilgrimage. Mujahid said: Our slaughterhouses and the ritual is the sacrifice. It was said: Our places of worship. The origin of the ritual is worship, and the ascetic is the worshipper. So God Almighty answered their prayer and sent Gabriel and showed them the rituals on the Day of Arafah. When he reached Arafah, he said: Do you understand, O Ibrahim? He said: Yes. So he named the time Arafah and the place Arafah. And have mercy on us forgive us for You are the Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
2:129: 129. Our Lord, and send among them meaning among the Muslim nation from the descendants of Abraham and Ishmael, and it was said: from the people of Mecca a Messenger from among them meaning a Messenger, by which he meant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Sayyid Abu al-Qasim Ali bin Musa al-Musawi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abbas al-Balkhi told us, Imam Abu Sulayman Hamad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim al-Khattabi told us, Muhammad bin al-Makki told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, my nephew Ibn Wahb told us, my uncle told us, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Salih, on the authority of Saeed bin Suwayd, on the authority of Abdul-A’la bin Hilal al-Salami, on the authority of al-Arbadh bin Sariyah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “I am written with God as the Seal of the Prophets, and Adam was still kneaded in his clay, and I will inform you of the beginning of my affair. I am the supplication of Abraham, the good report of Jesus, and the vision of my mother which she saw when she gave birth to me, and a light came out of her that illuminated the palaces of Syria for her.” And he meant by this call of Abraham that he called for a messenger to be sent to the children of Ishmael from among them. Ibn Abbas said: All the prophets were from the children of Israel except ten: Noah, Hud, Salih, Shuaib, Lot, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all. He recites to them Your verses Your Book, meaning the Qur’an. A verse from the Qur’an is a continuous statement until it ends. It has been said that it is a group of letters. It is said that the people went out with their verse, meaning with their group. And He teaches them the Book meaning the Qur’an. And wisdom Mujahid said: Understanding the Qur’an. Muqatil said: The sermons of the Qur’an and what is in it of rulings. Ibn Qutaybiyyah said: It is knowledge and action, and a man is not wise until he combines them. It has been said: It is the Sunnah. It has been said: It is rulings and judgment. It has been said: Wisdom is jurisprudence. Abu Bakr bin Duraid said: Every word that admonishes you, calls you to do something noble, or forbids you from doing something ugly is wisdom. And purifies them means He cleanses them from polytheism and sins. It was said: He takes the zakat from their wealth. Ibn Kaysan said: He will testify for them on the Day of Resurrection with justice if they testify for the prophets that they conveyed the message of purification, which is the correction. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Ibn Abbas said: The Exalted is the One like whom there is no other. Al-Kalbi said: The Avenger is explained by the Almighty's saying: And God is Exalted in Might, the Possessor of Retribution 4-Al Imran. It was said: The Invincible One whom hands cannot reach and nothing can reach. It was said: The Strong, and might is power. God Almighty said: So We strengthened with a third 14-Yasin, meaning We strengthened. It was said: The Victorious. God Almighty said, informing us: And He strengthened me in the speech 23-Sad, meaning He defeated me. It is said in the proverb: Whoever is powerful, he will be robbed meaning whoever is powerful, he will be robbed.
2:130: 130. The Almighty said: And whoever turns away from the religion of Abraham This is because Abdullah bin Salam called his two nephews, Salamah and Muhajir, to Islam and said to them: You know that God Almighty said in the Torah: I am sending from the descendants of Ishmael a prophet whose name will be Ahmad. Whoever believes in him has been guided, and whoever does not believe is cursed. So Salamah converted to Islam and Muhajir refused to convert to Islam, so God Almighty revealed: Whoever turns away from the religion of Abraham meaning he abandons his religion and his law. It is said that he desires something if he wants it, and he turns away from it if he abandons it. His saying whoever is an interrogative word meaning rebuke and reproach, meaning: whoever turns away from the religion of Abraham “except he who makes a fool of himself.” Ibn Abbas said: whoever loses himself. Al-Kalbi said: whoever goes astray from himself. Abu Ubaidah said: whoever destroys himself. Ibn Kaysan and Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is ignorance of himself. Foolishness means ignorance and weakness of opinion. Every fool is ignorant, because whoever worships other than God has made himself ignorant, because he does not know that God created him. It was said: Whoever knows himself knows his Lord. In al-Naba 78:“God the Most High revealed to David, ‘Know yourself and know Me.’ He said: ‘O Lord, how do I know myself? And how do I know You?’ So God the Most High revealed, ‘Know yourself by weakness, helplessness and annihilation, and know Me by strength, power and permanence.’” Al-Akhfash said: Its meaning is that he was foolish in himself, and according to this statement, his soul is in the accusative case by removing the letter of description. Al-Farra’ said: It is in the accusative case for explanation, and the original was that he was foolish in himself, but when he added the verb to its owner, the explanatory soul came out to make the location of the foolishness known, just as it is said: I was fed up with him, meaning I was fed up with him. And We chose him in this world We chose him in this world and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous meaning with the prophets in Paradise. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: There is an advancement and delay in it, meaning We chose him in this world and the Hereafter, and indeed, he will be among the righteous.
2:131: 131. When his Lord said to him, ‘Submit,’ meaning, Stay steadfast in Islam and remain steadfast in it because he was a Muslim. Ibn Abbas said: He said to him when he left the group. Al-Kalbi said: Make your religion and worship sincere to God. Ata’ said: Submit to God Almighty and entrust your affairs to Him. He said, I have submitted to the Lord of the Worlds, meaning I have been entrusted. Ibn Abbas said: This was confirmed since he did not seek help from any of the angels when he was thrown into the fire.
2:132: 132. And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons and Jacob. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read: (And he enjoined it) with an alif, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an. The rest read: (And he enjoined it) with a shaddah, and they are two dialects like anzala and nazala, meaning Abraham enjoined it upon his sons and Jacob enjoined it upon his sons. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: He means by the word of sincerity there is no god but God. Abu Ubaidah said: If you wish, you can return the metaphor to the religion because he mentioned the religion of Abraham, and if you wish, you can return it to the will: that is, Abraham enjoined it upon his eight sons, Ishmael and his mother Hagar the Copt, Isaac and his mother Sarah, and six whose mother was Qantura bint Yaqtan the Canaanite, whom Abraham married after the death of Sarah and Jacob. He was called that because he and Esau were twins, so Esau came out first from his mother’s womb and Jacob came out after him, taking his heel. Ibn Abbas said: It was said: Jacob was called that because of the large number of his offspring, meaning: And Jacob also enjoined it upon his twelve sons, O my sons, meaning that O Sons, God has chosen has chosen for you the religion meaning the religion of Islam so do not die except as Muslims believing, and it was said: sincere, and it was said: delegated. The prohibition in the apparent speech was about death, but in reality they were prohibited from abandoning Islam. Persist in Islam so that death will not befall you except as Muslims. And on the authority of Al-Fudayl bin Iyad, may God have mercy on him, he said: Except as Muslims meaning having good thoughts about your Lord. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say three days before his death: Let none of you die except while he has good thoughts about God Almighty.
2:133: 133. Or were you witnesses? meaning, were you witnesses? He means that you were not witnesses in attendance. When death approached Jacob meaning when Jacob was close to death. It was said that it was revealed about the Jews when they said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Do you not know that when Jacob died, he advised his sons to follow Judaism? So according to this statement, the address is to the Jews. Al-Kalbi said: When Jacob entered Egypt, he saw them worshipping idols and fires, so he gathered his sons and feared for them, so God Almighty said, When he said to his sons, ‘What will you worship after me?’ Ata’ said that God Almighty did not take a prophet until he gave him the choice between life and death. So when Jacob was given the choice, he said, Give me time until I ask my sons and advise them. So God did that to him, so he gathered his sons and his grandson’s sons, and said to them, My time has come, so what will you worship after me? They said, We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac. Ishmael was their uncle, and the Arabs call an uncle a father just as an aunt is called a mother. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, A man’s paternal uncle is like his father. And he said about his uncle, Al-Abbas: Return. Ali Abi, for I fear that Quraysh will do to him what Thaqif did to Ura bin Masoud.” And that is because they killed him. One God is an object of the verb your God in the accusative case, and it has been said that we know Him as one God, and we are Muslims to Him.
2:134: 134. That is a nation a group that has passed away “that has passed away” that has what it earned of work and for you what you have earned, and you will not be asked about what they used to do meaning: each one will be asked about his work, not about the work of others.
2:135: 135. God the Almighty said: And they said, ‘Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided.’ Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about the leaders of the Jews of Medina, Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf, Malik ibn al-Sayyif, Wahb ibn Yahudah, and Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab, and about the Christians of Najran, al-Sayyid and al-Aqib and their companions. This is because they disputed with the Muslims about religion, each group claiming that it was more deserving of God’s religion. The Jews said: Our Prophet Moses is the best of the prophets, and our book the Torah is the best of the books, and our religion is the best of the religions, and they disbelieved in Jesus, peace be upon him, and the Gospel, and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an. The Christians said: Our Prophet is the best of the prophets, and our book the Gospel is the best of the books, and our religion is the best of the religions, and they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an. Each of the two groups said to the believers: Be on our religion, for there is no religion other than that. So God the Almighty said: Say, O Muhammad, Rather, the religion of Abraham, “Rather, we follow the religion of Abraham.” Al-Kisa’i said: It is an accusative of enticement, as if he is saying: Follow the religion of Abraham. It was said that its meaning is: Rather, we will be on The religion of Abraham, so he deleted upon and it became accusative hanifan in the accusative case according to the grammarians of Basra, and according to the grammarians of Kufa it was accusative in the cut-off case. He meant rather the religion of Abraham the Hanif, so when the alif and lam were dropped, it did not follow the definite indefinite noun and was cut off from it, so it was accusative. Mujahed said: Hanafiyyah is following Abraham in what he brought of the Sharia by which he became an imam for the people. Ibn Abbas said: Hanafi is the one who inclines completely towards the religion of Islam, and its origin is from Hanaf, which is a tilt and crookedness in the foot. Saeed bin Jubair said: Hanafi is the circumcised pilgrim. Ad-Dahhak said: If he is with a Muslim Hanif, then he is a pilgrim, and if he is not with a Muslim, then he is a Muslim. Qatada said: Hanifism is circumcision, prohibiting mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, and performing rituals. And he was not among the polytheists. Then He taught the believers the path of faith, and He, the Most High, said:
2:136: 136. "Say, 'We believe in God and what has been revealed to us' meaning the Qur'an, 'and what was revealed to Abraham' meaning ten scrolls, 'and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Tribes' meaning the sons of Jacob, who are twelve tribes, each of them a tribe, they were called that because a group was born to each one of them, and the tribe of a man is his grandson, and from this it was said that Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein, may God be pleased with them, were the two grandsons of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the tribes of the Children of Israel are like the tribes of the Arabs from the children of Ishmael and the peoples from the Persians, and there were prophets among the tribes, and for this reason He said: and what was revealed to them, and it was said that they are the sons of Jacob from his loins, they all became prophets, 'and what was given to Moses' meaning the Torah, 'and Jesus' meaning the Gospel, 'and what was given' was given to the prophets from their Lord, 'we make no distinction between any of them' meaning we believe in all of them, we do not make any distinction between any of them, so we believe in some and disbelieve in others as the Jews and Christians did, 'and we are Muslims to Him.'" Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Muhammad bin Bashar, I told Uthman bin Umar, I told Ali bin Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic for the people of Islam. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not believe the People of the Book and do not disbelieve them, and say, ‘We believe in God,’ verse.
2:137: 137- The Almighty’s saying: If they believe in the like of what you believe in, meaning in what you believe in, and this is how Ibn Abbas used to read it. The like is a connection like the Almighty’s saying: There is nothing like Him, meaning He is not like anything. It was said: Its meaning is if they believe in all that you believe in, meaning they come with faith like your faith and monotheism like your monotheism. It was said: Its meaning is if they believe in the like of what you believe in, and the ba’ is redundant like the Almighty’s saying: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, 25- Maryam. Abu Muadh the grammarian said: Its meaning is if they believe in your book as you believe in their book, “then they have been guided. But if they turn away, then they are only in dissension,” meaning in disagreement and dispute. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Ata’. It is said: Shaqq Mishaqan if he disagrees as if each one is taking a side other than the side of his companion. God Almighty said: Let not my dissension lead you astray 89- Hud, meaning My disagreement, and it was said: in enmity, its evidence: the Almighty’s saying: That is because they opposed God 13- Al-Anfal meaning they opposed God, so God will suffice you against them O Muhammad, meaning He will suffice you against the evil of the Jews and Christians, and it is sufficient to expel Banu Nadir, kill Banu Qurayzah, and impose the jizya on the Jews and Christians, and He is the Hearer of their words, the Knower of their conditions.
2:138: 138- The Almighty’s saying: The dye of God: Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Al-Kalbi, Qatada and Al-Hasan: The religion of God, and He called it a dye because the effect of religion appears on the religious person just as the effect of dye appears on the garment, and it was said because the religious person adheres to it and does not leave it, just as dye adheres to the garment, and Mujahid said: The nature of God, and it is close to the first, and it was said: The Sunnah of God, and it was said: He meant by it circumcision because it dyes its owner with blood, Ibn Abbas said: It is that when a child is born to one of the Christians and seven days pass, they immerse him in their yellow water called the baptismal water and dye him with it to purify him with that water in place of circumcision, and when they do that to him they say: Now he has become a true Christian, so God informed that his religion is Islam, not what the Christians do, and it is an accusative of enticement meaning adhere to the religion of God, Al-Akhfash said it is a substitute for His saying the religion of Abraham And who is better than God in dyeing in religion, and it was said: in purification, And we are His worshippers obedient.
2:139: 139- Say O Muhammad to the Jews and Christians Do you argue with us about God? meaning about the religion of God? Argumentation means disputing about God to show the proof, because they said that the prophets were from us and of our religion, and our religion is the most correct, so we are more deserving of God than you. So God Almighty said: Say, Do you argue with us about God? "And He is our Lord and your Lord" meaning we and you are equal in God, for He is our Lord and your Lord. "And for us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds meaning each one will receive the reward for his deeds, so how do you claim that you are more deserving of God? And we are sincere to Him" while you are polytheists. Saeed bin Jubair said: Sincerity is for the servant to sincerely dedicate his religion and his work to God, not associating partners with Him in his religion, and not showing off with his work. Al-Fudayl said: Abandoning work for the sake of people is showing off, and working for the sake of people is polytheism, and sincerity is for God to save you from both.
2:140: 140- The Almighty’s saying: Or do you say? meaning: Do you say, an interrogative phrase and its meaning is rebuke. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Hafs read with the letter ta’ because of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: Do you argue with us about God?” and after that He said: “Say: Are you more knowledgeable or is God?” and the others read with the letter ya’ meaning the Jews and Christians say: “Indeed, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the tribes were Jews or Christians. Say: “O Muhammad, are you more knowledgeable” about their religion or is God? and God the Almighty has informed us that Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but rather he was a monotheist, a Muslim. And who is more unjust than he who conceals conceals a testimony he has from God which is their knowledge that Abraham and his sons were Muslims and that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the truth and a messenger whom God testified to in their books. And God is not unaware of what you do.
2:141: 141. “That is a nation that has passed on. It shall have what it earned, and you shall have what you earn. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.” He repeated it for emphasis.
2:142: 142. The Almighty said: The fools will say the ignorant among the people, what has turned them turned them away from the qiblah which they used to face meaning Jerusalem. The qiblah is a verb from the verb to face and was revealed about the Jews and the polytheists of Mecca who criticized the change of the qiblah from Jerusalem to Mecca. They said to the polytheists of Mecca: Muhammad’s matter has been in doubt and he longs for his birthplace and has headed toward your country and is returning to your religion. Then God Almighty said: “Say: To God belong the east and the west” He owns and the creation is His slaves. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.
2:143: 143. And thus We have made you a just community was revealed about the leaders of the Jews. They said to Muadh ibn Jabal: Muhammad did not make you face our qiblah except out of envy, and our qiblah is the qiblah of the prophets. Muhammad knows that we are just among the people. Muadh said: We are on the truth and justice. So God Almighty revealed: And thus meaning and thus. It was said: The kaf is for comparison, meaning just as We chose Abraham and his descendants and selected them. And thus We have made you a just community is a response to His statement: And We had chosen him in this world 130-Al-Baqarah, meaning just and good. God Almighty said: The most just of them said 28-Al-Qalam, meaning the best and most just of them. The best of things are the middle ones. Al-Kalbi said: It means people of a religion that is moderate between extremism and negligence because they are both reprehensible in religion. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, I told Abu Ma`shar Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Warraq, I told Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Zakariya bin Yahya, I told Abu Al-Salt, I told Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood among us one day after the afternoon prayer and did not leave anything until the Day of Resurrection except that he mentioned it in that place of his, until when the sun was over the tops of the palm trees and the edges of the walls, he said: ‘As for what has passed of this world, nothing remains except what remains of this day of yours. Beware, this nation will die after seventy nations, which are the last of them, the best of them, and the most honorable of them to God Almighty.’” God the Almighty says: So that you may be witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection that the Messengers have conveyed the message to them. Ibn Jurayj said: I said to Ata’ what is the meaning of God the Almighty’s saying: So that you may be witnesses over the people? He said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are witnesses over whoever abandons the truth from among the people, all of them. And the Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be a witness over you justifying and purifying you. This is because God the Almighty will gather the first and the last on one plain, then He will say to the disbelievers of the past nations: Did there not come to you a warner? Al-Mulk 8 They will deny and say: No bearer of good tidings or warner has come to us. God the Almighty will ask the prophets, peace be upon them, about that and they will say: They lied, we conveyed it to them. So He will ask them for evidence - and He is more knowledgeable about them - to establish the argument. Then the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be brought and they will testify for them that they have conveyed the message. The past nations will say: How did they know? They only came after us? He will ask this nation and they will say, You sent to us a Messenger and revealed to him a Book in which you informed us of the message of the Messengers and you are truthful in what you have informed us. Then Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be brought and asked about the state of his nation and he will purify them and bear witness to their truthfulness. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Ishaq bin Mansour informed us, Abu Usamah informed us, Al-A’mash informed us, Abu Salih informed us, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Noah will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him, ‘Did you convey the message?’ He will say, ‘Yes, O Lord.’ He will ask his nation, ‘Did I convey the message to you?’ They will say, ‘No warner came to us.’ It will be said, ‘Who are your witnesses?’ He will say, ‘Muhammad and his nation.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, will say, ‘You will be brought and you will bear witness.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, will recite, ‘And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you.’” The Almighty said: And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing meaning changing it, meaning the Holy House in Jerusalem, so it is a case of deleting the complement, and it is possible that the second object of making is deleted, on the assumption that And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing was abrogated, and it was said that its meaning is the one you are facing, which is the Kaaba, like the Almighty’s saying: You are the best nation meaning you. Except that We may know who follows the Messenger. If it is said, what is the meaning of His statement: Except that We may know? He is All-Knowing of all things before it is related to what exists, its meaning is to know the knowledge that the one who works on it deserves reward and punishment. It is said: Except that We may know, meaning: to see and distinguish who follows the Messenger in the qiblah from who turns on his heels and apostatizes. In the hadith, when the qiblah was changed, a group of Muslims apostatized to Judaism, and they said: Muhammad has returned to the religion of his fathers. The people of meaning said: Its meaning is except that We may know who follows the Messenger from who turns on his heels, as if it had previously been known to him that changing the qiblah was a reason for the guidance of some people and the misguidance of others. The future tense may also come with the meaning of the past, as God Almighty said: Then why did you kill the prophets of God? 91-Al-Baqarah, meaning why did you kill them? And if it was meaning it had been, meaning the turning to the Kaaba. It is said: the metaphor refers back to the qiblah, and it is said: to the Kaaba. Al-Zajjaj said: And if the change was great, heavy and severe, Except for those whom God has guided, meaning God has guided them. Sibawayh said: And if it was )) An affirmation that resembles an oath, and that is why the letter lam was included in its answer, And God would not let your faith go to waste. This is because Huyayy ibn Akhtab and his Jewish companions said to the Muslims: Tell us about your prayers toward the Holy House in Jerusalem. If they are guidance, then you have turned away from them, and if they are misguidance, then you have drawn closer to God through them, and whoever among you dies upon them has died upon misguidance. So the Muslims said: Guidance is what God has commanded, and misguidance is what God has forbidden. They said: What is your testimony about those among you who died facing our Qiblah? Before the Qiblah was changed, As`ad ibn Zararah from Banu Najjar and Al-Bara` ibn Ma`rur from Banu Salamah had died. They were leaders and other men. Their clans went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, God has turned you to the Qiblah of Abraham, so what about our brothers who died while praying towards the Holy House? Then God Almighty revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste meaning your prayers towards the Holy House. Indeed, God is to mankind Kind and Merciful. The people of Hijaz, Ibn `Amir and Hafs read Ra`uf with a full vowel on the weight of Fa`ul because most of the names of God Almighty are on the weight of Fa`ul and Fa`il, and Ash-Shakur and Al-Raheem and Al-Kareem and others. Abu Ja`far softens the hamza, and the others read it with a short vowel on the weight of Fa`l. Jarir said: You see that Muslims have a right over you as an act of the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful. Compassion is the most severe mercy.
2:144: 144. The Almighty said: We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven. This verse, although it was later in recitation, is earlier in meaning, as it is the beginning of the story, and the matter of the qiblah was the first of the matters of the Sharia to be abrogated. That is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were in Mecca facing the Kaaba. When he migrated to Medina, God ordered him to pray toward the rock of the Holy House in order to be closer to the Jews’ belief in him if he prayed toward their qiblah, with what they found of his description in the Torah. So he prayed sixteen or seventeen months after the migration toward the Holy House. He loved to face the Kaaba because it was the qiblah of his father Abraham, peace be upon him. Mujahid said: He loved that for the sake of the Jews because they were saying that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, differs from us in our religion and follows our qiblah. So he said to Gabriel, peace be upon him: I wish that God would turn me toward the Kaaba because it is the qiblah of my father Abraham, peace be upon him. Gabriel said: I am only a servant like you and you are honored by your Lord, so ask your Lord, for you are in a high place with God Almighty. [So he returned] Gabriel, peace be upon him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept looking at the sky, hoping that Gabriel would send down what he liked regarding the matter of the qiblah, so God Almighty sent down We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased, that is, one you love and desire. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram, that is, toward it, and he meant the Kaaba and the sacred sanctuary. And wherever you are, on land or sea, east or west, turn your faces toward it, when praying. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ishaq bin Nasr told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, who said, I heard Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, say: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the House, he supplicated in all its corners and did not pray until he left it. When he left, he bowed two rak’ahs facing the Kaaba and said, This is the qiblah. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Amr bin Khalid told us, Zuhair told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, that the first time the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, he stayed with his grandfathers or he said his maternal uncles from the Ansar, and that he prayed facing Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, and he liked that his qiblah be facing the House, and that he prayed the first Asr prayer and some people prayed with him, and a man from those who prayed with him came out and passed by the people of the Quba Mosque while they were bowing, and he said: I bear witness by God that I prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, facing Mecca, so they turned as they were facing the House, and the Jews were amazed that he prayed facing Jerusalem because it was the qiblah of the People of the Book, but when he turned his face towards the House, they disapproved of that, and Al-Baraa’ said in this hadith of his: that he died facing the qiblah before some men changed and were killed, so we did not know what to say about them, so God Almighty revealed And God would never let your faith go to waste. The change of the Qiblah occurred in Rajab, two months after the sun had passed its zenith, before the Battle of Badr. Mujahid and others said: This verse was revealed while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the mosque of Banu Salamah, and he had prayed with his companions two rak’ahs of the noon prayer. He turned during the prayer and faced the gutter, and the men changed places for the women, and the women changed places for the men. So that mosque was called the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs. It was said: The change occurred outside the prayer, between the two prayers, and the report reached the people of Quba during the dawn prayer. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi al-Samari told us, Abu Mus’ab Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, that Abdullah ibn Umar said: While the people were in Quba performing the dawn prayer, someone came to them and said to them: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has had the Qur’an revealed to him tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Ka’bah, so face it. Their faces were towards Syria, so they turned towards the Ka’bah. When the Qiblah was changed, the Jews said: O Muhammad, is it something you invent of your own accord? Sometimes you pray towards Jerusalem and sometimes towards the Kaaba. If you had remained steadfast in our Qiblah, we would have hoped that you would be the companion we are waiting for? Then God revealed: And those who were given the Scripture know that it meaning the matter of the Kaaba is the truth from their Lord. Then He threatened them by saying: And God is not unaware of what you do. Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Amir and Al-Kisa’i read it with the letter ta’. Ibn `Abbas said: He means that you, O group of believers, seek My pleasure, and I am not unaware of your reward and recompense. The rest read it with the letter ya’, meaning I am not unaware of what the Jews do, so I will recompense them in this world and the Hereafter.
2:145: 145. The Almighty said: And if you brought to those who were given the Scripture meaning the Jews and Christians, they would say: Bring us a sign for what you say, so God Almighty said: And if you brought to those who were given the Scripture “every sign” a miracle they would not follow your qiblah meaning the Kaaba nor will you follow their qiblah, nor will some of them follow the qiblah of others because the Jews face Jerusalem, which is the West, and the Christians face the East, and the qiblah of the Muslims is the Kaaba. Abu Uthman bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Muhammad bin Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Al-Hasan bin Bakr Al-Marwazi told us, Al-Mualla bin Mansour told us, Abdullah bin Jaafar Al-Makhzami told us, on the authority of Uthman Al-Akhnasi, on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The qiblah is between the east and the west. He meant by it the right of the people of the East, and he meant by the East: the east of winter on the shortest day of the year, and by the West: the west of summer on the longest day of the year, so whoever puts the west of summer at this time on his right and the east of winter on his left, his face would be towards the qiblah. And if you were to follow their desires: what they meant was the address to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is the nation, after what has come to you of knowledge of the truth about the qiblah, then you would be among the wrongdoers.
2:146: 146. The Almighty said: Those to whom We have given the Scripture meaning the believers of the People of the Scripture, Abdullah bin Salam and his companions recognize him meaning they know Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as they know their own sons among the boys. Omar bin Al-Khattab said to Abdullah bin Salam that God has revealed to His Prophet Those to whom We have given the Scripture know him as they know their own sons. How is this knowledge? Abdullah said: O Omar, I recognized him when I saw him as I recognized my own son, and my recognition of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is stronger than my recognition of my own son. Omar said: How is that? He said: I bear witness that he is the Messenger of God, truly from God Almighty, and God has described him in our Book, and I do not know what women do. Omar said: May God guide you, O Ibn Salam, for you have spoken the truth. And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth meaning the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the matter of the Kaaba while they know. Then he said:
2:147: 147. The truth is from your Lord meaning this truth is the predicate of an implied subject. It was said that it was raised by implying a verb, meaning the truth has come to you from your Lord. So do not be among the doubters the doubters.
2:148: 148. The Almighty said: And for every direction meaning for the people of every religion there is a qiblah, and direction is the name of the one who is directed towards it. He is its master meaning he faces it and approaches it. It is said: I turned towards him and I turned away from him if you turned towards him, and I turned away from him if you turned away from him. Mujahid said: He is its master, and Al-Akhfash said: It is a metaphor for God Almighty, meaning God is the master of the nations towards their qiblah. Ibn Amir read: its master meaning: the one who faces is turned towards it. So race to do good deeds meaning to do good deeds, meaning: hasten to do acts of obedience, and what is meant is hastening to accept. Wherever you may be you and the People of the Book. God will bring you all together on the Day of Resurrection and reward you for your deeds. Indeed, God is over all things competent.
2:149: 149. The Almighty said: “And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And God is not unaware of what you do.” Abu Amir read it with a ya’ and the rest with a ta’.
2:150: 150. "And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it." It was repeated to emphasize the abrogation. "So that people will have no argument against you, except for those who do wrong. They differed in the interpretation of this verse and the meaning of His saying except." Some of them said: Its meaning is that the qiblah was turned toward the Kaaba. "So that people will have no argument against you, if you face something other than it, they will say, You have no qiblah, except for those who do wrong," and they are the Quraysh and the Jews. As for the Quraysh, they say that Muhammad returned to the Kaaba because he knew that it was the truth and that it was the qiblah of his fathers, so he will return to our religion. As for the Jews, they say that he did not turn away from the Holy House despite his knowledge that it was the truth, except that he acted according to his opinion. A group said, "So that people will have no argument against you," meaning the Jews. Their argument, by way of arguing with the believers in their prayers toward the Holy House, was that they used to say, "Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions did not know where their qiblah was until We guided them." And His saying, Except those who have wronged, and they are the polytheists of Mecca, and their argument is that they said - when their qiblah was turned to the Kaaba - that Muhammad has become confused about his religion and will return to our religion as he returned to our qiblah, and this is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid, Ata’, and Qatadah, and according to these two interpretations the exception is correct, and His saying, Except those who have wronged, means that no one has an argument against you except the polytheists of Quraysh, for they argue with you and dispute with you with falsehood and injustice, and arguing with falsehood is called a pilgrimage as God Almighty said, Their argument is invalid with their Lord 16-Ash-Shura. The position of those is in the accusative case as if he said except those who have wronged, as Al-Kisa’i said, and Al-Farra’ said it is in the accusative case due to the exception. The Almighty’s saying: From them means from the people. It was said that this is an exception separate from the first statement, meaning that those who have wronged argue with you in falsehood, as God Almighty said: They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption 157-An-Nisa’, meaning that they follow assumptions, so it is like a man saying: You have no right with me unless you wrong. Abu Waraq said, So that the people meaning the Jews will have no argument against you. This is because they knew that the Kaaba was the qiblah of Abraham and they found in the Torah that Muhammad would be turned towards it, so God Almighty turned him towards it so that they would have no argument and say: The prophet we find in our book will be turned towards it and you did not turn towards it. So when he turned towards it, their argument was gone, except for those who did wrong, meaning except that they would be unjust and conceal what they knew of the truth. Abu Ubaidah said: His saying, except for those who have wronged, is not an exception, but except is in the place of the conjunction and, meaning: And those who have wronged also have no argument, as the poet said: Every brother who leaves his brother, by your father's life, except Al-Farqadhan Its meaning is that the two stars also separate, so the meaning of the verse is, “So turn towards the Kaaba, ‘lest the people’ meaning the Jews ‘have an argument against you’ and say, ‘Why did you abandon the Kaaba, which was the qiblah of Abraham, while you were following his religion?’ Nor those who did wrong, who were the polytheists of Mecca, saying, ‘Why did Muhammad abandon the qiblah of his grandfather and turn from it to the qiblah of the Jews?’ ‘So do not fear them’ in turning towards the Kaaba and in their showing off to you in argument, for I am your guardian, I will make you prevail over them with argument and victory. ‘And fear Me, and that I may complete My favor upon you’ is in apposition to His statement, ‘lest the people have an argument against you’ and so that I may complete My favor upon you by guiding you to the qiblah of Abraham, so that the pure religion may be completed for you.’ Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said, ‘The completion of favor is death as a Muslim.’ Saeed bin Jubair said: No blessing is complete for a Muslim unless God admits him into Paradise. “And perhaps you will be guided.” So that you may be guided from misguidance. Perhaps and perhaps are obligatory from God.
2:151: 151. The Almighty’s saying: As We sent among you This kaf is for comparison and needs something to refer to. Some of them said: It refers to what came before it, meaning: And to complete My favor upon you, just as We sent a messenger. Muhammad bin Jarir said: Abraham, peace be upon him, made two supplications - one of them - he said: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You 128-Al-Baqarah. So God sent the messenger, who is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and promised to answer the second supplication by making from his descendants a Muslim nation, just as I answered his supplication by guiding you to His religion and making you Muslims and completing My favor upon you by explaining the laws of the pure religion. Mujahid, Ata’ and Al-Kalbi said: It is related to what comes after it, which is His saying: So remember Me, I will remember you. Its meaning is: Just as We sent among you a messenger from among you, so remember Me. This verse is addressed to the people of Mecca and the Arabs, meaning: Just as We sent among you, O Arabs. A Messenger from among you meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who recites to you Our verses meaning the Qur’an, and purifies you and teaches you the Book and wisdom it was said: wisdom is the Sunnah, and it was said: the sermons of the Qur’an, and teaches you that which you did not know of the rulings and laws of Islam.
2:152: 152. So remember Me, and I will remember you. Ibn Abbas said: Remember Me with My obedience, and I will remember you with My forgiveness. Saeed bin Jubair said: Remember Me in times of comfort and ease, and I will remember you in times of hardship and affliction. Its explanation is: Had he not been among those who glorify God, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day of Resurrection. 144-As-Saffat. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Umar bin Hafs told us, Al-A’mash told us, he said, I heard Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty says: “I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me to himself, I remember him to Myself. If he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than his. If he draws near to Me a handspan, I draw near to him an arm’s length. If he draws near to Me an arm’s length, I draw near to him a fathom’s length. And whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running.” Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, and Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah al-Kashmihani told us: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Siraj al-Tahhan told us, Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Quraysh ibn Sulayman told us, Abu Abd al-Malik al-Dimashqi told us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, Mundhir ibn Ziyad told us, on the authority of Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Anas, who said: I heard this hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as many as my fingers are ten, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty says: O son of Adam, if you remember Me in yourself, I will remember you in Myself, and if you remember Me in an assembly, I will remember you in an assembly better than them, and if you come one hand’s length from Me, I will come one cubit’s length from you, and if you come one cubit’s length from Me, I will come one fathom’s length from you, and if you walk to Me, I will run to you, and if you run to Me, I will hasten to you, and if you ask Me, I will give you, and if you do not ask Me, I will become angry with you.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Yahya bin Abdullah told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Ismail bin Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty says: I am with My servant as long as he remembers Me and his lips move with Me. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shureih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, Amr bin Qais Al-Sakuni told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Busr, who said: A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, which deeds are best? He said: That you depart from this world while your tongue is moist with the remembrance of God Almighty. God Almighty says: And be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful. This means, be grateful to Me through obedience and do not be ungrateful to Me through disobedience. For whoever obeys God has thanked Him, and whoever disobeys Him has been ungrateful to Him.
2:153: 153. God Almighty says: “O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, God is with the patient.” With help and victory.
2:154: 154. And do not say of those who are killed in the way of God, 'They are dead.' This was revealed about the Muslims killed at Badr, who were fourteen men, six from the Muhajireen and eight from the Ansar. People used to say of those who were killed in the way of God, So-and-so has died and the pleasures and delights of this world have gone away from him. So God, the Most High, revealed: And do not say of those who are killed in the way of God, 'They are dead.' "Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not." As He said about the martyrs of UHud 11:"And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision." 169-Al Imran. Al Hassan said that the martyrs are alive with God, the Most High. Their provisions are presented to their souls, and spirit and joy reach them, just as the fire is presented to the souls of the people of Pharaoh morning and evening, and pain reaches them.
2:155: 155. The Almighty’s saying: And We will surely test you meaning, and We will surely test you, O nation of Muhammad. The lam is for the answer to the oath, meaning, And God will test you. The test is from God to reveal the obedient from the disobedient, not to know something that he did not know. With something of fear. Ibn Abbas said, meaning fear of the enemy. And hunger means drought. And a decrease in wealth through loss and destruction. And lives means killing and death. It was said, And gray hair. “And fruits” means disasters in fruits. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i that he said, “Fear is the fear of God Almighty, and hunger is fasting Ramadan, and a decrease in wealth is paying zakat and charity, and lives are diseases, and fruits are the death of children because a man’s child is the fruit of his heart.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, who said: I buried my son Sinan, and Abu Talha Al-Khawlani was on the edge of the grave. When I wanted to go out, he took me by the hand and pulled me out and said: Shall I not give you good report? Ad-Dahhak bin Azrab told me, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the child of a servant dies, God the Almighty says to His angels: ‘Have you taken the soul of My servant’s child?’ They say: ‘Yes.’ He says: ‘Have you taken the fruit of his heart?’ They say: ‘Yes.’ So what did My servant say?’ They say: ‘He sought refuge in God and praised You.’ He says: ‘Build for him a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.’” And give good tidings to the patient in the face of calamities and misfortunes, then he described them and said:
2:156: 156. Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, ‘Indeed we belong to God, as servants and a king, and indeed to Him we will return.’ In the Hereafter. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Muhadhir bin Al-Mura’ told us, Sa’d bin Sa’id told us, on the authority of Umar bin Katheer bin Aflah, the freed slave of Umm Salamah told us, on the authority of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no calamity that befalls a servant and he says, ‘To God we belong and to Him we shall return. O God, reward me for my calamity and replace it with something better,’ except that God will reward him for his calamity and replace it with something better.” Umm Salamah said: When Abu Salamah died, God resolved to do so, so I said, ‘O God, reward me for my calamity and replace it with something better.’ So God replaced the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for me. Saeed bin Jubair said: No one has been given in a calamity what this nation has been given, meaning the request to seek God’s forgiveness. If anyone had been given it, it would have been given to Jacob, peace be upon him. Do you not hear the words of God Almighty in the story of Joseph, peace be upon him: Oh, my grief over Joseph 84-Yusuf?
2:157: 157. Those are the people of this description upon them are prayers from their Lord and mercy prayers, meaning mercy, for prayer from God is mercy, and mercy is mentioned by God as an emphasis, and all prayers, meaning: mercy after mercy and those are the ones who are guided to the return, and it was said to the truth and correctness, and it was said to Paradise and reward. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: What good justice and what good bonus, so the justice is prayer and mercy, and the bonus is guidance. There are reports about the reward of those who are afflicted and the reward of those who are patient, including what Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Muhammad ibn God ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa`sa`ah, that he said: I heard Abu al-Habbab Sa`id ibn Yasar say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever God intends good for, He afflicts him with it. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Malik bin Amr told us, Zuhair bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr bin Halhalah, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No fatigue, nor disease, nor anxiety, nor grief, nor harm, nor distress befalls a Muslim, even if it were the prick he receives from a thorn, but that God expiates some of his sins because of it.
