Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, Muhammad bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: A woman who had a blemish came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to heal me. He said: If you wish, I will pray to God to heal you, and if you wish, be patient and there will be no reckoning upon you. She said: Rather, I will be patient and there will be no reckoning upon me. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Saeed Khalaf ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Nizar told us, Abu Mansur al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Nadhri told us, Ahmad ibn Najdah told us, Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani told us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Asim, who is Ibn Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Mus`ab ibn Sa`d, on the authority of Sa`d, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the people who are most severely tested. He said: The prophets, and the most similar, then the most similar. God tests a man according to his religion, for the earth and his wealth are from sin.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Al-Layth told me, Yazid bin Abi Habib told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Sinan, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “The greatest reward with God is with the greatest trial. If God loves a people, He tests them. Whoever is satisfied will have satisfaction, and whoever is displeased will have displeasure.” Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hairi told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The believing man and woman will continue to be afflicted in their person, their wealth, and their children until they meet God with no sin upon them. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad Abdullah bin Bishran told us, Abu Ali Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The example of the believer is like that of a crop; the wind continues to blow it, and the believer continues to be afflicted with calamity. The example of the hypocrite is like that of a cedar tree; it does not shake until it is harvested.” Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Al-Hussein bin Bishran told us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Aizar bin Harith, on the authority of Omar bin Saad bin Abi Waqqas, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “It is amazing for the believer that if good befalls him, he praises God and is grateful, and if a calamity befalls him, he praises God and is patient. The believer is rewarded for everything he does, even for the morsel of food that he raises to his wife’s mouth.”
2:158: 158. The Almighty said: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. As-Safa is the plural of safa, which is hard, smooth rocks. It is said: safa and safa, like: pebble and pebbles and seed and seed, and Al-Marwah is the soft stone, and its plural is marwat, and the plural of many is marw, like date and dates and dates. Rather, God meant by them the two mountains known in Mecca at the ends of the Mas’a, and that is why He included the definite article in them. The symbols of God are the signs of His religion. Its origin is from the word ish’ar which means to inform, and its singular is sha’ir. Everything that is a sign for an offering by which one draws near to God, the Most High, such as prayer, supplication, and sacrifice, is a sha’ir. So, the circumambulation, the standing place, and the slaughtering are all symbols of God, and so are the sacred places. What is meant by the symbols here are the rituals that God made symbols of His obedience, and Safa and Marwah are among them, so that they are both circumambulated. Whoever performs Hajj to the House or performs ‘Umrah, Hajj in the language means the intention, and ‘Umrah means the visit. In the prescribed Hajj and ‘Umrah, there is intention and visitation. There is no blame upon him, meaning there is no sin upon him. Its origin is from janah, meaning he deviated from the intention. To circumambulate them, meaning to circle them. Its origin is yatatawuf, and the ta was assimilated into the ta. The reason for the revelation of this verse is that there were two idols on Safa and Marwa, Asaf and Na’ila, and Asaf was on Safa and Na’ila was on Marwa. The people of the Age of Ignorance used to walk between Safa and Marwa in reverence for the two idols and touch them. When Islam came and the idols were destroyed, the Muslims were reluctant to walk between Safa and Marwa because of the two idols, so God permitted it and informed them that it was one of the symbols of God. Scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse and the obligation of walking between Safa and Marwa during Hajj and Umrah. A group held that it is obligatory, which is the opinion of Ibn Amir, Jabir, and Aisha. This is what Al-Hasan said, and this is what Malik and Al-Shafi’i said. A group held that it is voluntary, which is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, and this is what Ibn Sirin and Mujahid said, and this is what Sufyan Ath-Thawri and the People of Opinion held. Ath-Thawri and the People of Opinion said that whoever leaves it must pay a blood sacrifice. Those who made it obligatory provided evidence for it with what Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Kisa’i Al-Khatib told us: Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us: Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ya’qub Al-Asamm told us: Al-Rabi’ told us: Sulayman told us: Al-Shafi’i told us: Abdullah bin Mu’ammal Al-A’idhi told us: Amr bin Abdul Rahman bin Muhaisin told us: Ata’ bin Abi Rabah told us: Safiyya bint Shaibah told me: Bint Abi Tajra’ah - her name was Habeeba, one of the women of Banu Abd Al-Dar - she said: I entered with some women from Quraysh into the house of the family of Abi Husayn, looking at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as he was walking between Al-Safa and Al-Marwah. I saw him walking, and his belt was spinning from the intensity of his walking, to the point that I thought I could see his knees. I heard him say: Walk, for God has prescribed walking for you. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Hishan ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, who said: I said to Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: What do you think of the statement of God Almighty: “Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs `Umrah, there is no blame upon him for walking between them.” I do not see anything wrong with anyone not walking between them. Aisha said: No, if it were as you say, it would be: There is no blame upon him for walking between them. This verse was revealed about the Ansar, who used to enter ihram for Manat, and Manat was next to Qudayd, so God Almighty revealed: Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. Asim said: I said to Anas bin Malik: Did you dislike walking between Safa and Marwa? He said: Yes, because it was one of the rituals of the pre-Islamic era until God Almighty revealed: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah, that he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he left the mosque and was heading towards al-Safa, say: We begin with that with which God began. So he began with al-Safa. He said: When he stood on al-Safa, he would say: There is no god but God alone, with no partner, His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. He would do that three times and supplicate, and he would do the same on al-Marwah. When he descended from al-Safa, he would walk until his feet reached the bottom of the valley, then he would run until he came out of it. Mujahed said: - may God have mercy on him - Moses, peace be upon him, performed Hajj on a red camel, wearing two Qatwani cloaks. He circumambulated the House, then ascended Safa and supplicated, then descended to perform the sa’i while reciting the Talbiyah, saying, Here I am, O God, here I am. God Almighty said, Here I am, My servant, and I am with you. So Moses, peace be upon him, fell down in prostration. God the Almighty said: And whoever volunteers good Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a ya’ and a shaddah on the ta’ and a jazm on the ‘ayn, and so did the second one. And whoever volunteers good - it is better for him, and that you fast 184-Al-Baqarah meaning volunteers. Ya’qub agreed with the first one, and the rest read it with a ta’ and a fathah on the ‘ayn in the past tense. Mujahid said: Its meaning is whoever volunteers to circumambulate Safa and Marwah. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: And whoever volunteers means increases the circumambulation after what is obligatory. It was said: whoever volunteers to perform Hajj and Umrah after performing the Hajj that is obligatory upon him. Al-Hasan and others said: He meant all the other deeds, meaning doing what is not obligatory upon him, such as zakat, prayer, circumambulation, and other types of acts of worship. Then God is Appreciative is a metaphor for His servant for his work, Knowing of his intention. And gratitude from God the Almighty is that He gives His servant more than he deserves. He thanks for the little and gives a lot.
2:159: 159. The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear to the people in the Scripture was revealed about the Jewish scholars who concealed the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the verse of stoning, and other rulings that were in the Torah. Those are cursed by God. The root of cursing is expulsion and distance. And cursed by those who curse means they ask God to curse them and say: O God, curse them. They differed about those who curse. Ibn Abbas said: All creatures except the jinn and humans. Qatada said: They are the angels. Ata’ said: The jinn and humans. Al-Hasan said: All servants of God. Ibn Mas’ud said: No two Muslims curse each other except that the curse returns to the Jews and Christians who concealed the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his description. Mujahid said: The cursers are the animals that curse the disobedient children of Adam when the rain is severe and the rain is withheld, and they say: This is from the evil of the sins of the children of Adam. Then he made an exception.
2:160: 160. He said: Except for those who repent from disbelief and reform “who submitted and reformed their deeds between themselves and their Lord” and made clear “what they concealed” for those I will turn to “I will overlook their faults and accept their repentance” and I am the Accepter of Repentance “the One who returns the hearts of My servants that have turned away from Me to Me” the Most Merciful to them after they have turned to Me.
2:161: 161. Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers - upon them is the curse of God and of the angels meaning the curse of the angels and of all mankind. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: This is on the Day of Resurrection. The disbeliever will be brought to a halt and God will curse him, then the angels will curse him, then the people will curse him. If it is said, then he said and all mankind, and the one who is cursed is one of the people, so how can he curse himself? It is said that he will curse himself on the Day of Resurrection. God the Most High said: And you will curse one another 25-Al-Ankabut. It is said that they will curse the wrongdoers and the disbelievers, and whoever curses the wrongdoers and the disbelievers while he is one of them has cursed himself.
2:162: 162. They will abide therein eternally residing in the curse and it was said in the Fire The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved they will not be given respite nor will they be reprieved. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They will not be given respite, so they will apologize, as God Almighty said: And they will not be permitted to make excuses 36-Al-Mursalat.
2:163: 163. The Almighty said: “And your God is one God. There is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” The reason for the revelation of this verse is that the infidels of Quraysh said, O Muhammad, describe to us your Lord and His lineage. So God Almighty revealed this verse and Surat Al-Ikhlas and the One who has no peer and no partner. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Bakr bin Ibrahim and Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Asma bint Yazid, that she said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “In these two verses is the greatest name of God: ‘Your God is one God; there is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful’ and ‘God; there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.’” Abu Al-Dhaha said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: Muhammad says that your God is one God, so let him bring us a sign if he is truthful.
2:164: 164. Then God Almighty revealed, Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, mentioning the heavens in the plural and the earth in the singular because each heaven is not of one type but of another type, and all the earths are of one type, which is the dust. So the sign in the heavens is their thickness and height without pillars or connection and what you see in them of the sun, moon, and stars, and the sign in the earth is its extension, spread, and vastness and what you see in it of trees, rivers, mountains, seas, gems, and plants. The Almighty said: And the alternation of the night and the day meaning their succession in coming and going, one succeeds the other. If one of them goes, the other comes after it, meaning after it. Similar to this is the Almighty’s saying: And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession Al-Furqan 62. Ata’ said: He meant their alternation in light and darkness, increase and decrease. Night is the plural of night, and nights is the plural of plural. Day is the plural of river, and night is mentioned before day because it is older than it. God Almighty said: “And a sign for them is the night. We strip thereof the day” 37-Yasin. And the ships that sail on the sea means ships, whether singular or plural. If it is intended by the plural, it is feminine, but in the singular, God Almighty said: Concerning the singular and masculine, When he fled to the laden ship 140-As-Saffat. And He said regarding the plural and feminine, Until, when you were in the ship and it sailed with them with a good wind 22-Yunus. And the ships that sail upon the sea The verse about ships is their being harnessed and their sailing on the surface of the water, and they are stable and do not settle under the water with that which benefits people meaning riding them and carrying loads on them in trade, earnings, and various types of demands and what God sends down from the sky of water meaning rain. It was said: He meant by the sky the clouds, God creates in the clouds and then descends from the clouds. It was also said that He meant by it the well-known sky, God Almighty creates water in the sky and then descends from the sky to the clouds and then from the clouds it descends to the earth and He revives thereby meaning the water the earth after its death meaning after its dryness and barrenness and He dispersed therein meaning He scattered therein of every living creature and the changing of the winds. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read Al-Rih without an Alif, and the rest read it with an Alif. Every Reeh in the Qur’an that does not have an Alif or a Lam differed in its plural and singular form, except in Al-Dhariyat “The barren wind” 41-Al-Dhariyat. They agreed to make it singular. And in the first letter of Surat Al-Rum The winds are good tidings 456-Al-Rum. They agreed to make it plural. Abu Ja’far read the rest of it in the plural form, and the reciters differed in it. Al-Rih is masculine and feminine, and its inflection is that it is used to refer to the south, the north, acceptance, the wasp, and the disasters. It was said: Its conjugation is that sometimes it is soft and sometimes it is stormy and sometimes it is hot and sometimes it is cold. Ibn Abbas said: The greatest soldiers of God are the wind and water. The wind is called wind because it relaxes the souls. Shureih the judge said: No wind blows except to heal a sick person who is healthy. The good report is in three winds: the east, the north, and the south. As for the wasp, it is the barren wind, in which there is no good report. It was said that there are eight winds: four for mercy and four for torment. As for the ones for mercy, they are the good tidings, the spreaders, the scatterers, and the sent ones. As for the ones for torment, they are the barren and the screaming on land and the stormy and the breaking ones at sea. And the subjugated clouds meaning the submissive clouds are called clouds because they withdraw, i.e. move quickly as if they are dragged, i.e. pulled, between the sky and the earth as signs for a people who understand so that they know that these things have a Creator and Maker. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Three from which it is not known where they come: thunder, lightning, and clouds.
2:165: 165. The Almighty said: And among mankind are those who take for themselves rivals to God meaning idols that they worship They love them as they love God meaning they love their gods as the believers love God. Al-Zajjaj said: They love the idols as they love God because they associate them with God, thus making God equal to their idols in love. And those who believe are stronger in love for God meaning they are more steadfast and more persistent in their love for Him because they do not choose anything other than Him over God. And when the polytheists take an idol and then see something better than it, they reject the first and choose the second. Qatada said: The disbeliever turns away from his deity at a time of calamity and turns to God Almighty as God Almighty informed us about them when He said: And when they embark on a ship, they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion 65-Al-Ankabut. And the believer does not turn away from God in prosperity and adversity, hardship and ease. Saeed bin Jubair said: On the Day of Resurrection, God the Almighty will command those who burned themselves in this world for seeing idols to enter Hell with their idols, but they will not enter because they know that the torment of Hell is eternal. Then He will say to the believers while they are in the hands of the infidels: If you are My beloved ones, then enter Hell. So they will rush into it, and a caller will call from beneath the Throne: And those who believe are stronger in love for God. It was said that He said: And those who believe are stronger in love for God because God the Almighty loved them first, then they loved Him. And whoever the worshipped one testifies to his love, his love will be more complete. God the Almighty said: He loves them and they love Him 54-Al-Ma’idah. God the Almighty says: And if those who do wrong could see Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir and Ya’qub read law tara with a ta’, while the others read it with a ya’. The answer to law here is omitted, and there are many similar examples in the Qur’an, such as God the Almighty’s saying: And if a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved or by which they could be split apart (al-Ra’d 13:31). Meaning: This would have been the Qur’an. So whoever reads it with a ta’ means: And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who wrong themselves, from the severity of the punishment, you would have seen a tremendous thing. It was said that its meaning is: Say, O Muhammad: O wrongdoer, if you could see those who wronged or associated partners with God in the severity of the punishment, you would have seen a terrible thing. And whoever reads it with a ya’ means: And if those who wronged could see themselves when they see the punishment, or if they saw the severity of God’s punishment and chastisement when they see the punishment, they would have known the harm of disbelief and that what they have taken of idols will not benefit them. The Almighty said: When they see Ibn Amir read it with a damma on the ya’ and the rest read it with a fatha on it the punishment that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment meaning that all power belongs to God. Its meaning is that they saw means they saw and were certain that all power belongs to God. Abu Ja`far and Ya`qub read Inna al-Quwwa and Inna God with a kasra on the alif as a new sentence, and the speech is complete when he says When they see the punishment with the answer implied.
2:166: 166. When those who followed disown those who followed them and they see the punishment This is on the Day of Resurrection when God will gather the leaders and followers and they will disown one another. This is the opinion of most of the commentators. Al-Suddi said: They are the devils disowning mankind. And the ties that were between them in this world, such as kinship and friendship, will be severed from them, and their friendship will turn into enmity. Ibn Jurayj said: The wombs, as God Almighty said: There will be no kinship between them that Day 101-Al-Mu'minun. Al-Suddi said: He means the deeds that they used to do in this world, as God Almighty said: And We will turn to whatever deeds they did and make them as dust scattered 23-Al-Furqan. The root of the cause is what leads to something, such as a means, kinship, or affection. From this, a rope is called a cause and a road is called a cause.
2:167: 167. And those who followed meaning the followers said, 'If only we had another chance' meaning a return to the world we could disown them meaning those who were followed as they disowned us today thus meaning as He showed them the punishment, thus God will show them and it was said as some of them disown each other, God will show them their deeds as regrets remorse upon them the plural of regret. It was said that God will show them what evil deeds they committed so they regret what they did, and it was said that He will show them what good deeds they left behind so they regretted wasting them. Ibn Kaysan said: They associated idols with God hoping that it would bring them closer to God, the Almighty and Majestic, but when they were punished for what they were hoping for as a reward, they regretted and repented. Al-Suddi said: Paradise will be raised up for them, and they will look at it and at their homes in it if they had obeyed God. It will be said to them, Those are your dwellings if you had obeyed God. Then it will be divided among the believers, and that is when they will regret and be sorry. And they will not come out of the Fire.
2:168: 168. The Almighty’s saying: O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth [that is] lawful and good. It was revealed about Thaqeef, Khuza’ah, Amir ibn Sa’sa’ah, and Banu Mudlij regarding what they forbade themselves of tillage, livestock, baheerah, sa’ibah, wasilah, and ham. The lawful is what the Shari’ah has made lawful and good. It was said: what is palatable and enjoyable. The Muslim finds the lawful good and rejects the unlawful. It was said: the good is the pure. And do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Abu Ja’far, Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa’i, Hafs, and Ya’qub read it with a damma on the ta’, and the rest read it with a sukoon. The footsteps of Satan are his traces and slips. It was said: they are the vows in sins. Abu Ubaidah said: they are the minor sins. Al-Zajjaj said: His methods Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy indicate enmity, and it was said: the manifestation of enmity. He showed his enmity by refusing to prostrate to Adam and his deception of him until he expelled him from Paradise.
2:169: 169. And it is clear that it is transitive and intransitive, then he mentioned his enmity and said: He only orders you to do evil meaning to sin. The root of evil is that which makes its doer sad, and it is the source of sa'a yusu'u su'u and ma'sa'ah, meaning it saddened him, and sawatuhu fasa'a means I saddened him, so he was sad. And indecency is the sins and what is ugly in speech and action, and it is a source like sira' and sira'. Bazan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Indecency is the sin for which a punishment is required, and evil is the sin for which there is no punishment. Al-Suddi said: It is adultery, and it was said that it is miserliness. That you say about God what you do not know of forbidding crops and livestock.
2:170: 170. "And when it is said to them, 'Follow what God has revealed,' It is said that this is a new story and that the ha and mim in them" are a metaphor for something not mentioned. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Jews to Islam, so Rafi' bin Kharijah and Malik bin Awf said: They said: Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing, meaning what we found our fathers doing, for they were better and more knowledgeable than us, so God revealed this verse. It was said that the verse is connected to what came before it and was revealed about the polytheists of the Arabs and the infidels of Quraysh, and the ha and mim refer to His statement: "And among mankind are those who take for themselves rivals besides God" 165-Al-Baqarah. "They said, 'Rather, we will follow what we found,' meaning what we found in our fathers of worshipping idols. It was said that its meaning is: And when it is said to them, 'Follow what God has revealed' in making permissible what they had forbidden themselves of crops, livestock, bahīrah, and sā'ibah. The ha and the meem refer to people in the Almighty’s saying: O people, eat. “They said: Rather, we will follow.” Al-Kisa’i read: Rather, we will follow by assimilating the lam into the nun. Likewise, the lam of hal and bal is assimilated into the ta, tha, zay, seen, sad, ta, and dha. Hamza agreed with the ta, tha, and seen. What we found “upon our fathers” of prohibition and permission. God Almighty said: Or if their fathers meaning how do they follow their fathers and their fathers did not understand anything and the waw in awlu is the waw of conjunction, and it is called the waw of astonishment, and the interrogative alif was added to it for rebuke, and the meaning is do they follow their fathers even though they were ignorant and did not understand anything, its wording is general but its meaning is specific. That is, they did not understand anything of the matters of religion because they understood the matters of this world and were not guided then God gave an example and said, may He be glorified:
2:171: 171. And the parable of those who disbelieve is that of one who cries to that which hears not. Crying and crowing are the voice of a shepherd to his sheep, meaning like you, O Muhammad. And the parable of the disbelievers in their preaching and calling to God Almighty is like the shepherd who cries to his sheep. It was said that the parable of the preacher and caller to the disbelievers with them is like the shepherd who cries to his sheep, and they hear nothing except a call a voice and a call. So he added the parable to those who disbelieved because the speech indicates it, as in the Almighty's saying, And ask the town 82-Yusuf, meaning that just as the animals hear the voice of the shepherd but do not understand or comprehend what is said to them, so too the disbeliever does not benefit from your preaching, he only hears your voice. It was said: Its meaning is: And the example of those who disbelieved in their lack of intelligence and understanding of God and His Messenger is like the example of the animals that are bleating, which do not understand the commands and prohibitions except the sound, so the meaning is for the one who is bleating and the speech is outside of the one who is bleating, and it is widespread in the speech of the Arabs. They do that and they turn the speech upside down to clarify the meaning for them. They say, So-and-so fears you as a lion fears, meaning as a lion fears him. And God the Almighty said, Verily, its keys would burden a band of men 76-Al-Qasas, and only a band of men would be burdened by the keys. And it was said that its meaning is like the example of those who disbelieved in calling upon idols that do not understand or reason, like the one who bleats to sheep, so he does not benefit from his bleating at all, except that he is in trouble from the call and the call. Likewise, the disbeliever does not get from calling upon the gods and worshipping them except trouble and affliction, as God the Almighty said, If you call upon them, they do not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you 14-Fatir. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: “And the parable of those who disbelieve in calling upon idols is like the parable of one who calls out in the depths of the mountains and hears a voice called ‘the echo’ from which he understands nothing.” So the meaning of the verse is like the parable of one who spends on something from which the caller hears nothing but a call and a cry. Deaf is what the Arabs say about someone who hears but does not understand: As if he is deaf. “Mute” about goodness, they do not say it. Blind about guidance, they do not see it. So they do not understand.
2:172: 172. The Almighty said: O you who have believed, eat from the good things from the lawful things that We have provided for you. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Jaad told us, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O people, God is good and does not accept anything but good. God commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, saying: ‘O messengers, eat from the good foods and work righteousness’ Al-Mu’minun 23:51, and He said: ‘O you who have believed, eat from the good things We have provided for you’ Al-Mu’minun 23:51. Then he mentioned a man who has traveled a long way, disheveled and covered in dust, stretching his hands to the sky, ‘O Lord, O Lord’, while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with unlawful things. So how can his supplication be answered?” And be grateful to God for His blessings if it is Him that you worship. Then He explained the prohibitions.
2:173: 173. He said: He has only forbidden you dead animals. Abu Ja`far read dead animals in the entire Qur’an with emphasis, while the rest stress some of them. Dead animals are everything that is not slaughtered properly, and and blood he meant by flowing blood, as indicated by the Almighty's saying: or blood poured forth 145-Al-An`am. The Shari`ah exempted fish and locusts from dead animals, and the liver and spleen from blood, so it permitted them. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al Khalal told us, Abu Al Abbas Al Asem told us, Al Rabi bin Sulaiman told us, Al Shafi’i told us, Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two dead animals and two types of blood have been made lawful for us: fish and locusts, and the two types of blood, I think he said: the liver and the spleen.” And the flesh of pigs he meant all its parts, so he referred to it as meat because it is most of it. And that which is dedicated to other than God meaning that which is slaughtered to idols and tyrants. The origin of ihlil is raising the voice. When they slaughtered to their gods, they would raise their voices in remembrance of them, and this became part of their practice until it was said to every slaughterer, even if he did not say the name of God out loud, Mahal. Al Rabi bin Anas and others said: And that which is dedicated to other than God he said that which the name of other than God is mentioned over it. Whoever is forced with a kasra on the noon and its sisters, Asim and Hamza read it, and Abu Amr agreed except for the lam and the waw like Say, call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious 110-Al-Isra and Yaqub except for the waw, and Ibn Amir agreed with the tanween, and the rest all with the dammah, so whoever is forced said: because the jazm moves to the kasra, and whoever is forced, then the dammah of the beginning of the verb moves its movement to what precedes it, and Abu Ja`far with a kasra on the taa and its meaning is whoever is forced to eat a dead animal, meaning he is in need and forced to do so. Ghair is accusative in the state, and it was said on the exception, and if you see ghair is suitable in its place la, then it is a state, and if illa is suitable in its place, then it is an exception. Bagh and no `Ad The origin of bugh is the intention of corruption, it is said that the wound bugh is a crime if it seeks corruption, and the origin of aggression is injustice and exceeding the limit, it is said that he oppressed him with injustice and oppression, and they differed in the meaning of his saying Ghair bagh and no `Ad, so some of them said Ghair bagh means: outside On the Sultan, nor Aad: A transgressor who has gone on a journey, such as going out to rob the road or to spread corruption on the earth. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Saeed bin Jubair. They said that it is not permissible for a transgressor who has gone on a journey to eat dead meat if he is forced to do so, nor for a traveler to take advantage of the concession until he repents. Ash-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him said the same: because allowing it is helping him in his corruption. A group of scholars said that transgression and aggression are related to eating, and they differed in its details. Al-Hasan and Qatada said, Non-transgressor does not eat it without being forced to. Non-transgressor means he does not transgress to his fill. It was said, Non-transgressor means he does not seek it while he finds something else. Non-transgressor means he does not transgress what is set for him, so he does not eat until he is full, but he eats from it a sufficient amount of food to sustain his life. Muqatil bin Hayyan said, Non-transgressor means he considers it permissible. Non-transgressor means he takes provisions from it. It was said, Not transgressing, meaning not exceeding the amount that was permitted to him, nor exceeding the limits, meaning not falling short in what was permitted to him and abandoning it. Masruq said: Whoever is forced to eat dead meat, blood, or pork and does not eat or drink until he dies will enter Hell. Scholars differed on the amount of dead meat that a person in need may eat. Some of them said that it should be enough to satisfy his hunger. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him and one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him. The other opinion is that it is permissible to eat until one is full, and this is what Malik may God have mercy on him said. Sahl ibn Abdullah said, Not a transgressor who separates from the community, nor a transgressor who innovates and opposes the Sunnah, and the innovator is not permitted to consume what is forbidden in a case of necessity, there is no sin upon him meaning there is no blame on him for eating it, Indeed, God is Forgiving to those who eat in a state of necessity, Merciful as He permitted His servants to do so.
2:174: 174. God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book ((It was revealed about the leaders of the Jews and their scholars who used to receive gifts and food from their lowest class, and they hoped that the Prophet sent would be from among them. But when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent from someone other than them, they feared that their food would be lost and their leadership would be removed, so they took the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and changed it, then brought it out to them. But when the low class looked at the changed description, they found it to be contrary to the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and exchange it meaning the concealed for a small price meaning a small exchange meaning the food they receive from their lowest class they eat nothing into their bellies except the Fire meaning except what leads them to the Fire, which is bribery, what is forbidden, and the price of debt. So when that led them to the Fire, it was as if they ate the Fire. It was said that its meaning is that it becomes a Fire in Their bellies. And God will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection. That is, He will not speak to them with mercy or what pleases them. Rather, He will speak to them with rebuke. It was said: He meant by this that He will be angry with them, as it is said: So-and-so does not speak to so-and-so if he is angry with him. And He will not purify them. That is, He will not cleanse them from the filth of sins. And for them is a painful punishment.
2:175: 175. "Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance and punishment in exchange for forgiveness. So how patient they are in the Fire!" Ata' and As-Suddi said: It is what: a question, the meaning of which is what made them patient in the Fire and what makes them patient in the Fire that they abandoned the truth and followed falsehood. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: By God, they have no patience for it, but how bold they are in doing the work that brings them closer to the Fire. Al-Kisa'i said: So how patient they are in doing the work of the people of the Fire, meaning how persistent they are in it.
2:176: 176. That is because God sent down the Book with the truth means that punishment is because God sent down the Book with the truth, but they denied it and disbelieved in it. Then that would be in the nominative case. Some of them said that its accusative case means that we did that to them because God, meaning because God sent down the Book with the truth, but they differed about it. It was said that its meaning is that, meaning their action that they do of disbelief, difference, and insolence towards God, because God sent down the Book with the truth, and that is the saying of God Almighty: "Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is all the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. God has set a seal upon their hearts" 7-Al-Baqarah. And indeed, those who differed about the Book - believing in some and disbelieving in others - are in extreme dissension - meaning in extreme disagreement and misguidance.
2:177: 177. The Almighty said: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west. Hamza and Hafs read... The rest read it: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the west. So whoever raised it made righteousness the subject of righteousness, and its predicate is His saying: That you turn away, meaning: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west. And whoever lowered it made that you turn away in the nominative case as the subject of that you turn away, meaning: That you turn your faces toward the west is not all righteousness, like His Almighty saying: Their argument was only that they said, 'Bring to us.' 25- Al-Jathiya. Righteousness is every good deed that leads its doer to Paradise. They differed as to who is addressed by this verse. Some people said: It means the Jews and Christians, because the Jews used to pray facing Jerusalem before sunset, and the Christians used to pray facing the east. Each group of them claimed that righteousness lies in that. So God the Most High informed us that righteousness is not their religion or their deeds, but rather what He explained in this verse. Qatada and Muqatil ibn Hayyan are of this opinion. Others said: It means the believers, because a man, at the beginning of Islam before the revelation of the obligatory duties, if he recited the two testimonies of faith and prayed facing the direction it was, then died in that state, Paradise was obligatory for him. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated and the obligatory duties were revealed and determined and the direction of prayer was changed to the Kaaba, God revealed this verse and said: Righteousness is not meaning that all of it is that you pray towards the east and the west and do not act otherwise. But righteousness is what is mentioned in this verse. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’ and Ad-Dahhak said this. But righteousness Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read but with a light nun and al-barr in the nominative case. The rest read it with a stressed nun and al-barr in the accusative case. The Almighty’s saying: Whoever believes in God made min a noun and it is a predicate for righteousness which is a verb and it is not said righteousness Zayd and they differed about its meaning. It was said that because min is in the place of the source, he made it a predicate for righteousness as if he said, But righteousness is faith in God. The Arabs make the noun a predicate for the verb and Al-Farra’ recited: By your life, it is not for young men to grow beards, but for young men to grow fresh skin. So he made the growth of the beard a predicate for the young man, and it was said that its meaning was implied, but righteousness is the righteousness of he who believes in God, so mentioning the first was sufficient for the second, like their saying, Al-Joud Hatim, meaning, Al-Joud Hatim, and it was said that its meaning is, but the righteous is he who believes in God, like the Most High’s saying, They are of degrees with God 163-Al Imran, meaning, of degrees, and it was said that its meaning is, but the righteous is he who believes in God, like the Most High’s saying, And the outcome is for righteousness 132-Taha, meaning for the righteous, and what is meant by righteousness here is faith and piety. And the Last Day and the angels all of them and the Book meaning the revealed books and the prophets all together and he gave the money he gave the money for his love they differed regarding this metaphor. Most of the people of interpretation said: it refers to the money, meaning he gave the money while he was healthy and loved the money. Ibn Masoud said: that you give it to him while you are healthy and stingy, hoping for wealth and fearing poverty. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Abdul Wahid told us, Ammarah bin Al-Qaqa’ told us, Abu Zur’ah told us, Abu Hurairah told us: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, which charity has the greatest reward? He said: “To give charity while you are healthy and miserly, fearing poverty and hoping for wealth, and not delaying until it reaches your throat and you say to so-and-so such-and-such and to so-and-so such-and-such, when so-and-so already had it.” It was said that it refers to God Almighty, meaning to the love of God Almighty. Relatives are relatives. Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Qutaybah told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Hafsa bint Sirin, on the authority of Al-Rubaab, on the authority of her uncle Salman bin Amir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Charity given to a poor person is charity, and charity given to a relative is two things: charity and maintaining ties of kinship.” The Almighty said: And orphans, and the needy, and the wayfarer. Mujahid said: It means the traveler who is cut off from his family and passes by you. The traveler is called the wayfarer because he stays on the road. It was also said: It is the guest who stays with the man. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his guest. “And those who ask” means those who seek. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Musab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Abu Bujayd al-Ansari, who are Abd al-Rahman ibn Bujayd, on the authority of his grandmother, who is Umm Bujayd, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Return the beggar even with a burnt hoof. And in another narration, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you cannot find anything except a burnt hoof, then give it to him. The Almighty’s statement, and for the slaves, means those who are freed from slavery. This was said by most of the commentators. It was said: freeing a slave and freeing a slave. It was said: ransoming captives. And establishes prayer and pays zakat, and gives zakat. And those who fulfill their covenant, between themselves and God, the Almighty, and between themselves and the people. When they make a covenant, meaning when they promise, they fulfill it. When they swear and vow, they fulfill it. When they make a covenant, they fulfill it. When they speak, they are truthful. When they are entrusted, they fulfill it. They differed in raising the statement, and those who fulfill it, it was said that it is an appositive to the report, meaning, But the righteous are the believers. And those who fulfill their covenant. It was said that its meaning is: And they are the ones who fulfill, as if he counted categories and then said: They are the ones who fulfill so-and-so. It was said that it was raised as the subject and the predicate, meaning they are the ones who fulfill, then he said, And the patient ones. There are four aspects to its accusative case: Abu Ubaidah said: It is in the accusative case because of the length of the speech. It is the custom of the Arabs to change the i’rab if the speech and the sequence are long. An example of this is in Surat An-Nisa’: And those who establish prayer (Surat al-Ma’idah 5:162) And the Sabians and the Christians. It was said that its meaning is I mean the patient ones. It was said that it is in the accusative case because of the saying of the relatives, meaning and I will give to the patient ones. Al-Khalil said: It is in the accusative case for praise, and the Arabs in the accusative case for praise and blame [as if they want to separate the praised and blamed, so they do not follow it with the beginning of the speech and in the accusative case, so the praise is like the Almighty’s saying: And those who establish prayer] 162-An-Nisa. And the blame is like the Almighty’s saying: Cursed wherever they are found 61-Al-Ahzab. God Almighty says: In poverty meaning hardship and poverty, and distress meaning sickness and time, and during battle meaning fighting and war. Al-Mutahhar bin Ali bin Abdullah Al-Farsi told us, Abu Dharr Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Salihani told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Habban told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Zuhair told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Haritha bin Mudrib, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the battle became fierce and the people met, we sought protection behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. No one was closer to the enemy than him, meaning when the war became intense. Those are the ones who were truthful in their faith, and those are the righteous.
2:178: 178. The Almighty said: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is retaliation. Al-Sha'bi, Al-Kalbi, and Qatada said: This verse was revealed about two tribes of Arabs who fought in the pre-Islamic period shortly before Islam, and there were deaths and injuries between them that none of them took from the other until Islam came. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: It was between Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir, and Saeed bin Jubayr said: It was between Aws and Khazraj, and they all said that one of the two tribes had more power and honor than the other, and they used to marry their women without dowries, so they swore: We will kill for the slave of us the free man of them, and for the woman of us the man of them, and for the man of us the two men of them, and they made their injuries double the injuries of those, so they brought their matter to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God Almighty revealed this verse and ordered equality, so they agreed and converted to Islam. His saying, Retaliation is prescribed for you, meaning that retribution is imposed on you for those killed. Retaliation is equality and similarity in injuries and blood money. Its origin is from qass al-tashir which means to follow the trace, so the one to whom it is done follows what was done to him and does the same. Then he explained the similarity and said: A free man for a free man, a slave for a slave, and a female for a female. The general ruling is that if the blood money is equal in the case of free Muslims or slaves among Muslims, or free people among those with whom a treaty has been signed or slaves among them, then the male is killed if he kills with the male and the female, and the female is killed if she kills with the female and the male. A believer is not killed for an unbeliever, nor a free man for a slave, nor a father for a child, nor a Muslim for a dhimmi. A dhimmi is killed for a Muslim, a slave for a free man, and a child for a parent. This is the opinion of most of the scholars from among the Companions and those who came after them. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi bin Sulaiman told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abu Juhayfah, who said: “I asked Ali, may God be pleased with him, ‘Do you have anything from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, other than the Qur’an? ’ He said, ‘No, by Him who created the seed and created the soul, unless God gives a servant understanding of the Qur’an and what is in this document. ’ I said, ‘What is in this document? ’ He said, ‘The mind, the release of the captive, and a believer should not be killed for the sake of an unbeliever. ’” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The prescribed punishments are not carried out in mosques, and a child is not to be killed for his father. Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i, and the people of opinion held that a Muslim is to be killed for a dhimmi, and that a free man is to be killed for a slave. The hadith is an argument for those who do not require retaliation for a Muslim for killing a dhimmi, and that a group is to be killed for one person. ((It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab that Omar bin Al-Khattab killed seven or five people because of a man they killed by treachery, and he said, If the people of Sana’a conspired against him, he would have killed them all.)) Retaliation applies to limbs as it applies to souls, except in one case, which is that a healthy, normal person is killed by a chronically ill person. As for limbs, if a paralyzed or missing hand is cut off with a finger, a healthy, complete hand is not cut off with it. The proponents of the opinion held that retribution for limbs only applies between two free men or women, and it does not apply between a male and a female, nor between slaves, nor between a free man and a slave. According to others, a limb in retribution is analogous to a soul. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Munir told us that he heard Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Sahmi tell us, Hamid told us, “On the authority of Anas bin Al-Nadr, that Al-Rabi’, his aunt, broke the front tooth of a slave girl, so they asked her for forgiveness, but they refused. So they offered compensation, but they refused. Then they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they refused except for retaliation. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered retaliation. Anas bin Al-Nadr said: O Messenger of God, will Al-Rabi’s front tooth be broken? No, by Him who sent you with the truth, her front tooth will not be broken. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Anas, the Book of God is retaliation. So the people were satisfied and forgave him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are among God’s servants those who, if they swear by God, He will fulfill their oath.” The Almighty said: But if his brother pardons him anything, meaning he leaves him and forgives him what is required of him, which is retaliation for premeditated murder, and is satisfied with the blood money. This is the opinion of most of the commentators. They said: Pardon is that the blood money is accepted for premeditated murder. His statement from his brother means from the blood of his brother, and by the brother he meant the one who was killed. The two metaphors in his statement to him and from his brother refer to who, which is the murderer. His statement something is evidence that if some of the guardians pardon, the retaliation is dropped because some of the blood money has been nullified. God the Almighty said: Then follow up with kindness meaning that the one seeking the blood money must follow up with kindness and not demand more than his right. And pay it to him with goodness meaning that the one who is required to pay the blood money must do so with kindness without delay. He ordered each of them to do good in what he has and what he owes. The view of most scholars from the Companions and Followers is that if the blood money guardian forgives retaliation for blood money, then he may take the blood money even if the killer does not agree to it. Some people said: He is not entitled to blood money except with the killer’s consent, and this is the view of Al-Hasan, Al-Nakha’i and the people of opinion. The evidence for the first view is what Abdul-Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us. Abdul-Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us. Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us. Al-Rabi’ told us. Al-Shafi’i told us. Muhammad bin Ismail bin Abi Fadeek told us on the authority of Abu Dhi’b on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Maqburi on the authority of Abu Shuraih Al-Ka’bi that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then you, O Khuza’ah, have killed this slain man from Hudhayl, and by God, I am his blood money. So whoever kills another man after him, his family has two choices: if they like, they may kill him, and if they like, they may take the blood money.” The Almighty says: That is a concession from your Lord and a mercy. That is, what you mentioned about pardoning retaliation and taking blood money is a concession and mercy from your Lord. This is because retaliation for a soul and wounds was obligatory in the Torah for the Jews, and they were not allowed to take blood money. In the law of the Christians, blood money was required, and they were not allowed to take retaliation. So God Almighty gave this nation the choice between retaliation and pardoning the blood money, as a concession and mercy from Him. But whoever transgresses after that and kills the offender after the pardon and acceptance of the blood money will have a painful punishment which is that he will be killed in retaliation. Ibn Jurayj said: He must be killed so that he will not accept the pardon. And in the verse there is evidence that the killer does not become an unbeliever by killing, because God Almighty addressed him after the killing with the address of faith and said: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is retaliation and He said at the end of the verse: But if any of his brother pardons him and he meant by that the brotherhood of faith, so He did not sever the brotherhood between them by killing.
2:179: 179. The Almighty said: And there is life for you in retaliation meaning survival, because if the one who intends to kill knows that he will be killed if he kills, he refrains from killing, so his survival and the survival of the one who intended to kill him will be. It was said in the proverb: (Killing reduces killing) and it was said in the proverb: (Killing prevents killing), and it was said that the meaning of life is his safety from retaliation in the Hereafter, because if retaliation is taken from him, he will live in the Hereafter, and if retaliation is not taken from him in this world, retaliation will be taken from him in the Hereafter. O you of understanding, that you may become righteous meaning that you may refrain from killing for fear of retaliation.
2:180: 180. The Almighty’s saying: It is prescribed for you meaning it is obligatory upon you when death approaches any of you meaning the causes of death and its effects of illnesses and diseases if he leaves wealth meaning money, similar to the Almighty’s saying: And whatever you spend of good 272-Al-Baqarah the bequest to parents and relatives The bequest was an obligation at the beginning of Islam for parents and relatives for whoever died and had wealth, then it was abrogated by the verse on inheritance. Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Hafs al-Tajir told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Waleed told us, al-Haytham ibn Jameel told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanma’, on the authority of Amr ibn Kharijah, who said: “I was holding the reins of the Prophet’s camel, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘God has given every person with a right his right, and there is no bequest for an heir.’” A group of people went to the view that its obligation was abrogated in the case of relatives who inherit, and its obligation remained in the case of those who do not inherit from among the parents and relatives, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas, Tawus, Qatada, and al-Hasan. Tawus said: Whoever makes a bequest to people whom he names as his relatives who are in need, it will be taken away from them and returned to his relatives. The majority went to the view that the obligation was abrogated in the case of all, and it is obligatory in the case of those who do not inherit. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Tahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of Ibn `Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not the right of a Muslim who has something to bequeath to spend two nights without his will being written down at his head. The Almighty’s saying: in a reasonable manner means that he should bequeath what is reasonable and not exceed one-third, and he should not bequeath to the rich and leave out the poor. Ibn Masoud said: The bequest is for the most needy, then the most needy. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Rahim al-Shaibani told us, Ahmad ibn Hazim ibn Abi Gharzah told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa and Abu Na`im told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of `Amir ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Sa`d ibn Malik, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to visit me, so I said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, should I bequeath all of my wealth? He said: No. I said: Half? He said: No. I said: A third? He said: A third, and a third is a lot. It is better for you to leave your heirs rich than to leave them poor, begging from people with their bare hands.” On the authority of Ibn Malikah, a man said to Aisha, may God be pleased with her: I want to make a will. She said: How much is your wealth? He said: Three thousand. She said: How many are your dependents? He said: Four. She said: God only said: If he leaves behind goods, and this is a small thing, so leave for your dependents. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: “I would rather bequeath a fifth than a quarter, and I would rather bequeath a quarter than a third. Whoever bequeaths a third, then he has not left anything behind.” Al-Hasan al-Basri, may God be pleased with him, said: He bequeaths a sixth, a fifth, or a quarter. Al-Sha’bi said: They only bequeathed a fifth or a quarter. The Almighty’s saying: Truly is in the accusative case as a source, and it was said that it is in the accusative case as a direct object, meaning that He made the will a right upon the righteous the believers.
2:181: 181. The Almighty’s statement: So whoever changes it meaning changes the will in the guardians or the guardians or the witnesses after he has heard it meaning after he has heard the statement of the testator, and for this reason the metaphor was mentioned even though the will is feminine, and it was said that the metaphor refers back to the will like the Almighty’s statement: But whoever receives an admonition from his Lord 275-Al-Baqarah referring the metaphor back to the admonition Then the sin is only upon those who change it and the dead person is innocent of it Indeed, God is Hearing of what the testator has bequeathed Knowing of the change that was changed, or Hearing of his will and Knowing of his intention.
2:182: 182. God the Almighty said: So whoever fears meaning knows, like His saying: But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits set by God (229-Al-Baqarah) meaning you know from a testator Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Abu Bakr and Ya’qub read with a fat-ha on the waw and a shaddah on the sad, like His saying: What He enjoined upon Noah 13-Ash-Shura And We enjoined upon man 8-Al-Ankabut and the others read with a sukun on the waw and a light sad, like His saying: God instructs you concerning your children 11-An-Nisa After a bequest he may have bequeathed or debt 12-An-Nisa Janf meaning injustice and deviation from the truth, and janf is inclination or sin meaning oppression, As-Suddi, Ikrimah and Ar-Rabi’ said: Jaanf is a mistake and sin is intentional So reconcile between them, there is no sin upon him and they differed in the meaning of the verse, Mujahid said: Its meaning is that if a man attends a sick person while he is making a testament and he sees him inclining either by negligence or extravagance, or by lying down The will is not in its proper place, so there is no blame on the one who is present to order him to be just and forbid him from injustice, so he should look at the testator and the heirs. Others said: What he meant by it is that if the deceased made a mistake in his will or was unjust intentionally, then there is no blame on his guardian or his trustee or the one in charge of the affairs of the Muslims to reconcile after his death between his heirs and those to whom the will was made, and to return the will to justice and truth, so there is no sin on him, meaning: there is no blame on him. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Tawus said: It is a kind of injustice, which is that he should bequeath to his grandsons, meaning his son, and to his daughter’s son, and to his daughter’s husband, meaning his daughter. Al-Kalbi said: The guardians and trustees would carry out the will of the deceased after the revelation of the words of God Almighty: But whoever changes it after he has heard it verse, even if all the money was used up and nothing remained. Then it was abrogated by the words of God Almighty: But if anyone fears from a testator deviation verse. Ibn Zayd said: So the testator was unable to bequeath to the parents and relatives as God Almighty commanded, and the testator was unable to reform, so God Almighty took that away from them and imposed the obligatory duties. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man or woman may work in obedience to God for sixty years, then death comes to them and they are harmed in their will, so Hell is obligatory for them. Then Abu Hurairah recited: after any bequest he may have made or debt to His saying without causing harm.
2:183: 183. The Almighty said: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting meaning it is obligatory and made obligatory. Fasting and fasting in the language means abstaining. It is said: he fasted the day when it was moderate and stood at noon, because when the sun reaches the middle of the sky it stops and stops moving for a while. From this, the Almighty said: Then say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast' 26-Maryam, meaning silence because it is abstaining from speech. In the Sharia, fasting is abstaining from eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse with the intention at a specific time as it was prescribed for those before you of the prophets and nations. They differed about this comparison. Saeed Ibn Jubayr said: The fasting of those before us was from dusk until the next night as it was at the beginning of Islam. A group of scholars said: He meant that fasting Ramadan was obligatory for Christians as it was imposed on us, and it might occur in extreme heat or extreme cold, and it was difficult for them on their travels and harmed their livelihoods, so their scholars and leaders agreed to make their fasting in a season of the year between winter and summer, so they made it in the spring and added ten days to it as expiation for what they had done, so it became forty, then their king complained of a mouth so he made a promise to God that if he recovered from his pain he would increase their fasting. A week, then he recovered, so he added a week to it, then that king died and another king took over and said: Complete it as fifty days. Mujahid said: They were afflicted with two deaths, so they said: Increase your fasting, so they added ten before and ten after. Al-Sha’bi said: If you fasted the entire year, you would break your fast on the day in doubt, so it is said from Sha’ban and it is said from Ramadan. This is because the month of Ramadan was imposed on the Christians, so they fasted the thirty days before and the day after, then the other century continued to follow the tradition of the century before it until they reached fifty days. This is what the Almighty said: As it was prescribed for those before you that you may become righteous. He meant by fasting, because fasting is a connection to righteousness because it involves subduing the self and breaking desires. It was said: That you may beware of desires from eating, drinking and sexual intercourse. For a fixed number of days. It was said: At the beginning of Islam, fasting three days of every month was obligatory, and fasting on the day of Ashura, so they fasted like that from spring to the month of Ramadan for seventeen months, then it was abrogated by fasting Ramadan. Ibn Abbas said: The first thing that was abrogated after the migration was the command The kiss and fasting. It is said: The fast of the month of Ramadan was revealed a month and a few days before Badr. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: The Battle of Badr took place on Friday, seventeen nights before the end of the month of Ramadan, at the beginning of eighteen months after the Hijra. Abu al-Hasan al-Shirazi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Musab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, that she said: “The day of Ashura was a day that the Quraysh used to fast during the pre-Islamic era. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, he fasted it and ordered the people to fast it. When Ramadan was made obligatory, it was the obligatory fast, and the day of Ashura was left. So whoever wishes may fast it, and whoever wishes may leave it.”
2:184: 184. It was said that what is meant by his saying a numbered number of days is the month of Ramadan, and it was not abrogated. The word days was put in the accusative case as a circumstance, meaning in a numbered number of days. It was also said: as an explanation. It was also said: on is the predicate of what its agent was not named. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey - then an equal number meaning he breaks his fast - then an equal number from other days meaning he must do an equal number, and the number and the number are one. from other days meaning other than the days of his illness and travel. Other is in the accusative case, but it is not declined, and that is why it was put in the accusative case. God the Almighty said: And for those who are able to fast. The scholars differed in the interpretation of this verse and its ruling. Most of them said that the verse was abrogated, which is the opinion of Ibn Umar, Salamah ibn al-Akwa’ and others. This is because at the beginning of Islam, they were given the choice between fasting and breaking the fast and making a ransom. God the Almighty gave them the choice so that it would not be difficult for them because they were not accustomed to fasting. Then the choice was abrogated and the obligation was revealed in the words of God the Almighty: So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. Qatada said: This is specific to the elderly man who is able to fast, but it is difficult for him. He was given permission to break the fast and make a ransom, then it was abrogated. Al-Hasan said: This is for the sick person who has what is called a sickness and he is able to fast. He has the choice between fasting and breaking the fast and making a ransom. Then it was abrogated by the words of God the Almighty: So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. And the license was established for those who are not able to fast, and a group of people went to the view that the verse is decisive and not abrogated, and its meaning is: And for those who were able to do it in their youth and were unable to do it after they grew old, then they must pay a ransom instead of fasting. Ibn Abbas read: And for those who are able to do it with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the ta’ and a light ta’ and a fatha on the waw and a shaddah, meaning they are required to fast, and its interpretation is for the elderly man and the elderly woman who are not able to fast, and the sick person whose illness is not expected to go away, so they are required to fast but are not able to do it, so they may break their fast and feed a poor person for each day, and this is the view of Saeed bin Jubair, and he made the verse decisive. The Almighty said: The ransom of feeding a poor person. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read it as an addition, and likewise in al-Ma’idah 5:The expiation of food. He added the ransom to the food, even though it was one due to the difference in the two words, like the Almighty’s saying: And the grain of the harvest 9-Qaf and their saying: the mosque of the congregation and Rabi’ al-Awwal. The others read: ransom and expiation with a definite article, food is raised and the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read it in the plural, and the others are on the singular, so whoever pluralized it put the noon in the accusative and whoever limited it lowered the noon and its noon, and the ransom: the reward, and it is obligatory to feed a poor person for each day a mudd of food according to the mudd of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is a pound and a third of the country’s main food, this is the saying of the jurists of Hijaz, and some jurists of Iraq said: He owes each poor person half a sa’ for each day he breaks his fast, and some of them said: Half a sa’ of wheat or a sa’ of something else, and some jurists said what the person who broke his fast ate on the day he broke his fast, and Ibn Abbas said: He gives each poor person his dinner and his suhoor. So whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. That is, he gives more than one poor person, so he feeds two poor people or more in place of each day. This was said by Mujahid, Ata’, and Tawus. It was also said: Whoever gives more than the amount required of him, and gives a sa’ and owes a mudd, it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you. So whoever went to the abrogation said that its meaning is that fasting is better for him than the ransom. It was said: This is for the elderly man if he takes on the task of fasting, even if it is difficult for him, he is informed that he should break his fast and ransom, if you only knew. And know that there is no permission for a responsible believer to break his fast in Ramadan except for three: One of them must make up for it and pay expiation, the second must make up for it but not pay expiation, and the third must pay expiation but not make up for it. As for the one who must make up for it and pay expiation, it is the pregnant woman and the breastfeeding woman if they fear for their children, then they break their fast and make it up, and they must pay expiation in addition to making it up. This is the opinion of Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid said this and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said this. Some people said that there is no ransom for them, and this is what Al-Hasan, Ata’, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Zuhri said, and Al-Awza’i, Al-Thawri, and the people of opinion said this. As for the one who must make up for it but not pay expiation, it is the sick person, the traveler, the menstruating woman, and the woman in childbirth. As for the one who must pay expiation without making up the fast, he is the elderly man and the sick person whose illness is not expected to go away. Then God Almighty explained the days of fasting.
2:185: 185. He said: The month of Ramadan is a patch on the meaning of it is the month of Ramadan. Al-Kisa'i said: The month of Ramadan was prescribed for you and the month was called a month because of its fame. As for Ramadan, Mujahid said: It is one of the names of God Almighty. It is said the month of Ramadan as it is said the month of God. The correct thing is that it is a name for the month and it was named after the hot stones, and they used to fast it in the intense heat, so the stones would be heated in the heat. The Almighty says: In which the Qur’an was revealed. The Qur’an was called the Qur’an because it includes surahs, verses, and letters, and includes stories, commands, prohibitions, promises, and threats. The root of the word qur’ is gathering and the hamza may be deleted from it, so it is said, Qarīt al-ma’ fi al-hawd if you gathered it. Ibn Kathir read: Qur’ān with the opening of the ra’ without a hamza, and this is how al-Shafi’i read it and said that it is not from qira’a but rather it is the name of this book like the Torah and the Gospel. It was narrated on the authority of Muqsim on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the words of God Almighty: The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’ān was revealed and His words: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree 1-al-Qadr, and His words: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night 3-ad-Dukhan, and it was revealed in all the months. God Almighty said: And a Qur’ān which We have divided 106-al-Isrā’, so he said that the Qur’ān was revealed all at once from the Preserved Tablet on the Night of Decree in the month of Ramadan to the House of Glory in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought it down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in stars over twenty-three years, so that is what God Almighty said: So I swear by the positions of the stars 75-al-Waqi’ah. Dawud ibn Abi Hind said: I said to al-Sha’bi: The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’ān was revealed was it not revealed? In the other months? He said: Yes, but Gabriel used to oppose Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Ramadan what was revealed to him, so God would rule as He wished, confirm what He wished, and cause him to forget what He wished. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The scrolls of Abraham, peace be upon him, were revealed on the last three nights of Ramadan, and it is narrated on the first night of Ramadan. The Torah of Moses, peace be upon him, was revealed on the last six nights of Ramadan. The Gospel was revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him, on the last thirteen nights of Ramadan. The Psalms of David were revealed on the eighteenth of Ramadan. The Criterion was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the twenty-fourth of Ramadan, six days after that.” The Almighty says: Guidance for mankind from misguidance. Guidance is in the accusative case because the Qur’an is definite and guidance is indefinite. And clear proofs of guidance meaning clear indications of what is permissible and what is forbidden, the limits and rulings. And the Criterion meaning the difference between truth and falsehood. God the Almighty said: So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. That is, whoever was residing in the city and the month came upon him. The scholars differed regarding whoever the month came upon while he was residing and then traveled. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: It is not permissible for him to break the fast. Ubaidah al-Salmani said the same, based on God the Almighty’s saying: So whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast it. That is, the entire month.
