Most of the Companions and jurists held that if someone sets out on a journey in the month of Ramadan, it is permissible for him to break the fast. The meaning of the verse is: So whoever among you witnesses the entire month, let him fast it, that is, the entire month. And whoever among you does not witness the entire month, let him fast what he witnesses of it. The evidence for this is what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhasi informed us. Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us. Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi informed us. Abu Mus’ab informed us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Ubaidullah ibn Utbah ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Mecca in the year of the conquest in Ramadan and fasted until he reached al-Kadeed, then he broke the fast and the people broke the fast with him. They used to take the most recent of the commands of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God the Almighty said: And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. He permitted breaking the fast due to the excuse of illness and travel, and He repeated this statement so that it is known that this ruling is established in the abrogating texts as it is established in the abrogated texts. They differed regarding the illness that permits breaking the fast. The people of the apparent meaning went to that what is called illness permits breaking the fast, and this is the saying of Ibn Sirin. Tarif bin Tamam Al-Attardi said: I entered upon Muhammad bin Sirin in Ramadan, and he was eating, and he said: This finger of mine hurts. Al-Hasan and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: It is an illness in which it is permissible to pray while sitting. The majority went to that it is an illness in which there is fear of an increase in fasting due to an unbearable cause. In short, if fasting exhausts him, he breaks the fast, but if it does not exhaust him, then he is like a healthy person. As for travelling, breaking the fast is permissible and fasting is permissible according to most scholars, except for what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said that fasting is not permissible while travelling, and whoever fasts must make up for it. They cited as evidence the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is not righteousness to fast while travelling. This is according to others regarding someone who is exhausted by fasting, so it is better for him to break the fast. The evidence for this is what Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malhi told us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu’aymi told us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail told us, Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ansari told us, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on a journey and saw a crowd and a man who had been shaded, so he said: What is this? They said: He is fasting. He said: It is not righteousness to fast while travelling.” The evidence for the permissibility of fasting is what Professor Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri told us. Abu Naim al-Isfarayini told us. Abu Awana told us. Abu Umayya told us. Abdullah al-Qawariri told us. Hammad ibn Zayd told us. Al-Jariri told us on the authority of Abu Nadrah on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: “We used to travel with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during Ramadan. Some of us were fasting and some of us were not fasting. The fasting person did not criticize the one who was not fasting, nor did the one who was not fasting criticize the one who was fasting.” They differed about which of the two matters is better. A group said: Breaking the fast while traveling is better than fasting. This was narrated from Ibn Umar, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Al-Sha’bi agreed with him. Some people said that fasting is better. This was narrated from Mu’adh bin Jabal and Anas, and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and Saeed bin Jubair said the same. A group said: The better of the two matters is the one that is easier for him, because God the Almighty says: God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship. This is the opinion of Mujahid, Qatadah, and Umar bin Abdul Aziz. Whoever fasts while staying in the morning and then travels during the day, it is not permissible for him to break his fast that day according to most scholars. A group said: He may break his fast, which is the opinion of Al-Sha’bi, and Ahmad said the same. As for the traveler, if he fasts while in the morning, it is permissible for him to break his fast by consensus. The evidence for this is what Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib reported: Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal reported to us. Abu Al-Habas Al-Asamm reported to us. Al-Rabi’ reported to us. Al-Shafi’i reported to us. Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad reported to us from Ja’far bin Muhammad from his father from Jabir, “That the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) went out to Mecca in the year of the conquest in…” Ramadan, so he fasted until he reached Kara’ al-Ghamim, and the people fasted with him. It was said to him, O Messenger of God, fasting has become difficult for the people, so he called for a cup of water after the afternoon prayer and drank while the people were watching, and some of them broke their fast. People fasted, and some of them were told that some people fasted, so he said, Those are the disobedient ones. They differed about the journey that permits breaking the fast. Some people said: It is a day’s journey. A group said: It is a two-day journey, which is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. A group said: It is a three-day journey, which is the opinion of Sufyan Al-Thawri and the People of Opinion. God the Almighty says: God intends for you ease by permitting breaking the fast when sick or traveling. And He does not intend for you hardship. Abu Ja`far read: hardship and easer and the like with a damma on the seen, while others read it with a sukoon. Al-Sha`bi said: No man is given the choice between two matters and chooses the easier of the two except that it is more beloved to God the Almighty. “And that you may complete the number” Abu Bakr read it with a shaddah on the meem, while others read it with a sukoon, which is the choice based on God the Almighty’s saying: This day I have perfected for you your religion 5:3. The waw in God the Almighty’s saying: And that you may complete the number is a waw of sequence, and the lam is a lam of ki, meaning: And He intends for you to complete the number, meaning that you may complete the number of days of the month by making up for what you broke during your sickness or travel. Ata’ said: And that you may complete the number means the number of days of the month. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The month is twenty-nine days, so do not fast until you see the crescent, and do not break your fast until you see it. If it is hidden from you, then complete the number as thirty.” Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Hiri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not anticipate the month by fasting a day or two, unless that coincides with a fast that one of you used to fast. Fast when you see it and break your fast when you see it. If it is obscured from you, then count thirty days and then break your fast.” And to glorify God and to magnify God for what He has guided you to He has guided you to what He has approved of, which is fasting the month of Ramadan, and He has singled you out for it, over all other people of religions. Ibn Abbas said: It is the takbirs of the night of Eid al-Fitr. It was narrated on the authority of al-Shafi’i, Ibn al-Musayyab, Urwah, and Abu Salamah that they used to say takbir aloud on the night of Eid al-Fitr, and he likened the night of sacrifice to it, except for those who were pilgrims, so he mentioned the talbiyah. And perhaps you will be grateful to God for His blessings. There are reports about the virtue of the month of Ramadan and the reward of those who fast. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Hasani Al-Marwazi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Siraj Al-Tahhan told us, Abu Ahmad bin Quraish bin Sulayman told us, Ali bin Abdul Aziz Al-Makki told us, Abu Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told me, on the authority of Abu Sahl Nafi bin Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When Ramadan comes, the devils are chained, the gates of Paradise are opened, and the gates of Hell are closed. Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad bin Al-Jarrah told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Muhammad bin Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Abu Kurayb Muhammad bin Al-Ala told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the first night of Ramadan comes, the devils and rebellious jinn are chained, and the gates of Hell are closed, and not one of its gates is opened. And the gates of Paradise are opened, and not one of its gates is closed. And a caller calls out: ‘O seeker of good, come forward, and O seeker of evil, hold back. And God has those who are freed from the Hellfire. And that is every night.’” Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Abi Nasr bin Ahmad Al-Kufani Al-Herawi told us, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Abdul-Rahman bin Umar bin Muhammad Al-Tujibi Al-Misri, known as Ibn Al-Nahhas, who was asked: Did Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ziyad Al-Anzi Al-Basri, known as Ibn Al-A’rabi, in Mecca, tell you? Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah Al-Za’farani told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and in the hope of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven. Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan out of faith and in the hope of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.” And in the hope of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven. And whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Decree out of faith and in the hope of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven.” Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us, Abu Sa`id Khalaf ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nizar informed us, al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Asad al-Saffar informed us, Abu Ja`far Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Ishaq al-`Anzi informed us, Ali ibn Hajar ibn Iyas al-Sa`di informed us, Yusuf ibn Ziyad informed us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud`an, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed us on the last day of Sha`ban and said: “O people, a great month has come upon you - and in another narration, it has come upon you with a ta` - it has come upon you: it has shone, a great month, a blessed month, a month in which there is a night better than a thousand months, a month in which God has made fasting obligatory, and standing in prayer during its nights voluntary. Whoever draws near during it with one of the good qualities is as if he had performed an obligatory act in any other month, and whoever performs an obligatory act in it is as if he had performed seventy obligatory acts in any other month. It is the month of patience.” The reward for patience is Paradise, and the month of consolation - that is, contribution - and a month in which provision is increased. Whoever fasts during both of its two days will have his sins forgiven and his neck freed from the Fire, and he will have a reward like his without anything being reduced from his reward. They said, O Messenger of God, not all of us can find what to break the fast with. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God gives this reward to whoever breaks the fast of a fasting person with a sip of milk or a date or a drink of water. Whoever satiates a fasting person, God, the Almighty, will give him a drink from my pool after which he will not thirst until he enters Paradise. Whoever makes things easy for his slave during it, God will forgive him and free him from the Fire until he enters Paradise. It is a month whose beginning is mercy, whose middle is forgiveness, and whose end is freedom from the Fire. So increase your four qualities in it, two qualities with which you will please your Lord, and two qualities with which you cannot do without. As for the two qualities with which you will please your Lord, they are testifying that there is no god but God and asking for His forgiveness. As for the two qualities with which you cannot do without, they are asking. God grants you Paradise, and you seek refuge in Him from the Fire.” Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Hafs al-Tajir told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Bakir al-Kufi told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every deed of the sons of Adam is multiplied for him, a good deed, ten times its like, up to seven hundred times. God Almighty said, except for fasting, for it is for Me and I will reward for it. The fasting person leaves his food, drink and desire for My sake. The fasting person has two joys, a joy when he breaks his fast and a joy when he meets his Lord. And the bad breath in his mouth is better to God than the scent of musk. Fasting is a shield, fasting is a shield.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Muhammad bin Mutraf told us, Abu Hazim told me, on the authority of Sahl bin Saad, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In Paradise there are eight gates, one of which is called Ar-Rayyan, and none will enter it except those who fast. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah told us, Abu Tahir ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Rashid ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Fasting and the Qur’an intercede for the servant. Fasting says: ‘O Lord, I prevented him from food, drink, and desires during the day, so intercede for him.’ And the Qur’an says: ‘O Lord, I prevented him from sleeping at night, so intercede for him.’ So they intercede.”
2:186: 186. The Almighty said: And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Jews of Medina said: O Muhammad, how can our Lord hear our supplication when you claim that between us and the heaven is a journey of five hundred years, even though each heaven is as thick as that? So this verse was revealed. Ad-Dahhak said: Some of the Companions asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: Is our Lord near so that we can confide in Him, or is He far so that we call upon Him? So God Almighty revealed: And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. And in it is an implication as if He said: So tell them that I am near to them with knowledge, nothing is hidden from Me, as He said: And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein 16-Q. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdul Wahid told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, invaded Khaybar, or he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, headed to Khaybar, the people looked out over a valley and raised their voices in glorification: God is Great, God is Great, there is no god but God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take it easy, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent, but rather you are calling upon one who hears and is near, and He is with you.” The Almighty said: I answer the call of the caller when he calls upon Me. The people of Medina, except for Qaloon and Abu Amr, read it with the ya’ in both of them in connection, and the rest deleted it in connection and pause. Likewise, the reciters differed in confirming the ya’s deleted from the script and deleting them in recitation. Ya’qub confirms all of them in connection and pause, and they agreed to confirm what is confirmed in the script in connection and pause. So let them respond to Me. It was said: responding means answering, meaning: so let them respond to Me with obedience. Answering in the language means obedience and giving what is asked for. Answering from God Almighty means giving, and from the servant is obedience. It was said: so let them respond to Me, meaning let them ask Me for an answer, and its true meaning is let them obey Me. And let them believe in Me that they may be guided. So that they may be guided. If it is said, then what is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: I answer the call of the caller and His saying: Call upon Me, I will respond to you, and he may be called upon a lot and not answer? We said: They differed regarding the meaning of the two verses. It was said that the meaning of supplication here is obedience, and the meaning of answer is reward. It was said that the meaning of the two verses is specific, even though their wording is general, their meaning being: I answer the supplication of the supplicant, if you wish, as He said: He will remove that to which you call, if He wills 41-Al-An’am, or I answer the supplicant’s supplication if it is in accordance with the decree, or: I answer him if answering is good for him, or I answer him if he does not ask for something impossible. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Mu’awiyah bin Saleh told me, that Rabi’ah bin Zaid told him, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God answers the supplication of one of you as long as he does not supplicate for a sin or the severing of family ties or is impatient. They said: What is impatience, O Messenger of God? He said: “He says, ‘I have called upon You, O Lord, I have called upon You, O Lord, I have called upon You, O Lord,’ but I do not see that You will answer me.’ Then he becomes frustrated and stops supplicating.” It was said that it is general, and the meaning of his saying I answer is I hear, and it was said that there is nothing in the verse more than answering the supplication, as for giving death, it is not mentioned in it, and the master may answer his slave, and the father his son, but he does not give him what he asked for, so the answer will inevitably happen when the supplication occurs, and it was said that the meaning of the verse is that his supplication will not be disappointed, so if what he asked for is decreed for him, he will give it, and if he does not decree it for him, he will save the reward for him in the Hereafter, or he will ward off evil from him because of it, and the evidence for that is what Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani informed us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani informed us, Hamid Zanjawayh informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, and he is Abdul Rahman bin Thabit bin Thauban informed us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, who told them that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no Muslim man on earth who supplicates to God Almighty with a supplication except that God grants it to him or wards off from him an equivalent amount of evil, as long as he does not supplicate for a sin or severing family ties.” It was said that God Almighty answers the supplication of the believer at the right time. He delays giving what he wants so that he may call upon Him and hear His voice, and he hastens to give to someone he does not like because he hates his voice. It was said: There are manners and conditions for supplication, and they are the reasons for the answer. Whoever completes them is among those who are answered, and whoever neglects them is among those who transgress in supplication and does not deserve the answer.
2:187: 187. God the Almighty said: Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives. Rafath is a metaphor for sexual intercourse. Ibn Abbas said: God the Almighty is modest and generous and uses the metaphor for everything mentioned in the Qur’an of direct contact, touching, penetration, penetration, and rafath. He meant sexual intercourse. Al-Zajjaj said: Rafath is a comprehensive word for everything that men want from women. The commentators said: In the beginning, if a man broke his fast, food, drink, and sexual intercourse were permissible for him until he prayed the last ‘Isha’ prayer or slept before it. If he prayed the ‘Isha’ prayer or slept before it, food and women were forbidden to him until the following night. Then ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, had intercourse with his wife after praying the ‘Isha’ prayer. When he washed himself, he began to cry and blame himself. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I apologize to God and to you for this sinful self. I returned to my family after praying the ‘Isha’ prayer and found a pleasant smell, so my soul tempted me to have intercourse with my wife. Do you find any permission for me? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was not worthy of that, O ‘Umar. Some men stood up and confessed something similar, so it was revealed in Omar and his companions. It is lawful for you meaning it is permitted for you on the night of fasting meaning on the night of fasting “to have sexual relations with your wives. They are clothing for you” meaning a dwelling place for you and you are clothing for them meaning a dwelling place for them. Its evidence is the statement of God the Almighty: And He made from her her mate that he might dwell in tranquility with her 189-Al-A’raf. It was said that nothing dwells like the dwelling of one spouse with the other. It was said: Each of the spouses was called a garment because they strip off when sleeping and come together in one garment until each of them becomes for the other like the garment that he wears. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: They are a bed for you and you are a blanket for them. Abu Ubaidah and others said: It is said of the woman that she is your clothing, your bed, and your garment. It was said: Clothing is the name for what covers something, so it is possible that each of them is a covering for the other from what is not permissible, as came in the hadith: Whoever marries has secured two-thirds of his religion. “God knows that you were betraying yourselves” meaning that you were betraying yourselves and wronging them by having intercourse after the evening meal. Al-Bara’ said: When the fast of Ramadan was revealed, they would not approach women during the entire month of Ramadan, and there were men who were betraying themselves, so God revealed: God knows that you were betraying yourselves “So He turned to you” He pardoned you “And He forgave you” And He erased your sins “So now have intercourse with them” have intercourse with them lawfully. Intercourse was called direct intercourse because the skin of each one of them touches the other, And seek what God has decreed for you meaning seek what God has decreed for you. It was said that what God has decreed for you in the Preserved Tablet means a child, as most of the commentators said. Mujahid said: Seek a child if this one does not give birth, then this one. Qatadah said: And seek the concession that God has decreed for you by permitting eating, drinking, and intercourse in the Preserved Tablet. Muadh ibn Jabal said: And seek what God has decreed for you, meaning the Night of Decree. His saying: And eat and drink until the white thread of the night becomes distinct to you. It was revealed about a man from the Ansar whose name was Abu Sirmah ibn Qays ibn Sirmah. Ikrimah said: Abu Qays ibn Sirmah. Al-Kalbi said: Abu Qays Sirmah ibn Anas ibn Abi Sirmah. That was because he spent the day working on his land while he was fasting. When evening came, he returned to his family with dates and said to his family: Offer the food. The woman wanted to feed him something hot, so she began to prepare something hot for him. At the beginning, he had prayed the ‘Isha’ prayer and slept, and food and drink were forbidden to him. When she finished eating, she saw him asleep and he was exhausted and had eaten, so she woke him up. He did not want to disobey God and His Messenger, so he refused to eat and became fasting and exhausted. It was not until midday that he fainted. When he regained consciousness, he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: O Abu Qays, what is wrong with you that you spent the evening in a state of idleness? He mentioned his wealth to him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was upset by that, so God revealed: Almighty God said, And eat and drink meaning during the nights of fasting until the white thread of light becomes distinct to you from the black thread meaning the whiteness of day from the blackness of night. They are called two threads because each one of them appears at first to be extended like a thread. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saeed bin Maryam told us, Abu Ghassan Muhammad bin Mutraf told us, Abu Hazim told us, on the authority of Sahl bin Saad, who said: And eat and drink until the white thread of night becomes distinct to you from the black thread was revealed, but the words of dawn were not revealed. So when men wanted to fast, one of them would tie a white thread and a black thread to his foot and would continue eating until he could clearly see them. Then God Almighty revealed after that of dawn, and they knew that what was meant by them was the night and the day. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, Hisham told us, Hisin bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, who said: When the verse until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread was revealed, I took a black rope and a white rope and put them under my pillow and I kept looking at them and at the night, but I could not see anything distinct from them. So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that, and he said, That is only the blackness of the night and the whiteness of the day. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim ibn `Abdullah ibn `Umar, on the authority of his father, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bilal calls out at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum calls out. He said: Ibn Umm Maktum was a blind man who would not call out until it was said to him, ‘It is morning, it is morning.’ Know that there are two types of dawn: false and true. The false dawn rises first, elongated like the tail of a stag, ascending to the sky. When it rises, the night does not end and food and drink are not forbidden to the fasting person. Then it sets, and after it the true dawn rises, spreading quickly across the horizon. When it rises, the day begins and food and drink are forbidden to the fasting person. Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Hannad and Yusuf bin Isa told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Sawada bin Hanzala, on the authority of Samra bin Jundub, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let not Bilal’s call to prayer or the prolonged dawn prevent you from your pre-dawn meal, but rather the dawn that spreads across the horizon. God Almighty says: Then complete the fast until the night. The fasting person is forbidden from eating and drinking at the break of true dawn and it extends until sunset. When the sun sets, the fast is broken. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Hisham bin Urwa told us, he said: I heard my father say: I heard Asim bin Omar bin Al-Khattab, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with them both, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the night comes from here and the day departs from here and the sun sets, then the fasting person has broken his fast. God Almighty says: And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques [and you intended to perform I’tikaf in the mosques, but what is meant is not having sexual relations with them in the mosques because that is forbidden outside of I’tikaf]. And I’tikaf is staying on something, and I’tikaf in the Sharia means staying in the mosque to worship God, and it is a Sunnah and is not permissible outside of the mosque, but it is permissible in all mosques. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Yusuf told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform I’tikaf during the last ten days of Ramadan until God Almighty took him, then his wives performed I’tikaf after him.” The verse was revealed regarding a group of the Prophet’s companions, may God bless him and grant him peace, who used to perform I’tikaf in the mosque. If a man among them needed to visit his wife, he would go out to her and have intercourse with her, then wash himself, and return to the mosque. They were forbidden from doing that during the day and night until they finished their I’tikaf. Intercourse is forbidden during I’tikaf and invalidates I’tikaf. As for other than intercourse, such as direct contact, such as kissing and touching with desire, it is disliked and does not invalidate I’tikaf according to most scholars, and it is the more apparent of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, just as it does not invalidate Hajj. A group said that it invalidates his I’tikaf, and this is the opinion of Malik. It was also said that If he ejaculates, his i'tikaf is invalidated, but if he does not ejaculate, then it is not like fasting. As for touching that is not intended for pleasure, it does not invalidate i'tikaf, as Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Umrah Bani Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed i'tikaf, he would bring his head and feet close to me, and he would not enter the house except for a human need.” The Almighty said: These are the limits set by God meaning those rulings that He mentioned regarding fasting and seclusion. The limits of God, that is, what God has forbidden. Al-Suddi said: the conditions of God. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: the obligations of God. The root of the word hadd in the language is to prevent, and from this the doorman is called a blacksmith, because he prevents people from entering. The limits of God are what God has forbidden from being violated. So do not approach them do not come to them. Thus “God makes clear His signs to the people that they may fear God” so that they may fear Him and be saved from the punishment.
2:188: 188. The Almighty said: And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly. It was said that this verse was revealed about Imru' al-Qais ibn Ayish al-Kindi, who claimed that Rabi'ah ibn Abdan al-Hadrami had taken over a piece of land from him before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he had taken it from him. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to al-Hadrami, Do you have evidence? He said: No. He said: Then you have his oath. So he went to swear. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If he swears to eat his money unjustly, he will meet God while He is turning away from him. So God revealed this verse: And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly. That is, do not eat one another’s wealth unjustly, that is, in a manner other than that which God has permitted. The root of falsehood is something that is lost, and eating unjustly has many types. It may be by way of usurpation and plunder, or by way of amusement, such as amusement, such as gambling, the fee of a singer, and the like. It may be by way of bribery and betrayal. And bring it down to the rulers. That is, bring the matters of that money between you and its owners to the rulers. The root of bringing down is to send the bucket and throw it into the well. It is said: He sent it down or he took it out. Ibn Abbas said: This is about a man who owes money and has no proof, so he denies the money and disputes over it to the ruler, and he knows that he is right and that he is sinful for withholding it. Mujahid said about this verse: Do not dispute while you are unjust. Al-Kalbi said:: It is to give false testimony. His saying: And bring it forward is in the place of the affirmative by repeating the letter of prohibition, meaning do not bring it forward to the judges. It was said that its meaning is: Do not eat falsely and attribute it to the judges. Qatada said: Do not bring your brother’s money forward to the judge while you know that you are unjust, for his judgment does not make permissible what is forbidden. Shuraih the judge used to say: I judge in your favor and I think that you are unjust, but I cannot do anything but judge based on the evidence, for my judgment does not make permissible what is forbidden for you. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Malik bin Anas told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Zainab bint Abi Salamah, on the authority of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am only a human being, and you bring your disputes to me, and perhaps some of you may be more eloquent in presenting his argument than others, so I judge in his favor based on what I hear from him. So whoever I judge in his favor with something that is the right of his brother, then let him not take it, for I am only cutting off for him a piece of the Fire.” God Almighty says: That you may consume a portion of people’s wealth in sin through injustice. Ibn Abbas said: With a false oath by which he seizes his brother’s wealth “and you know” that you are wrongdoers.
2:189: 189. The Almighty’s saying: They ask you about the new moons. It was revealed about Muadh bin Jabal and Tha’laba bin Ghanam, the Ansaris. They said: O Messenger of God, what is wrong with the crescent moon that appears thin and then increases until it is filled with light and then returns thin as it began and is not in the same state? So God the Almighty revealed: They ask you about the new moons. It is the plural of hilal like rada’ and rada’. It was called hilal because people raise their voices in remembrance when they see it, as they say, A baby cries out when he is born, and the people are going to Hajj when they raise their voices in Talbiyah. Say, ‘They are appointed times for mankind and for Hajj.’ It is the plural of miqat, meaning we did that. We did that so that people would know the times of Hajj, Umrah, fasting, breaking the fast, the due dates of debts, the number of wives, and other things. Therefore, He distinguished it from the sun, which is always in the same state. And righteousness does not consist in approaching houses from their backs. The commentators said: In the pre-Islamic period and at the beginning of Islam, if a man among them entered ihram for Hajj or Umrah, he would not enter a wall, house, or home through its door. If he was from the people of Madar, he would dig a hole in the back of his house to enter and exit from it, or he would take a ladder to climb from it. If he was from the people of Wabar, he would exit from behind the tent or pavilion and not leave or exit from the door until he was released from his ihram. They considered that righteousness, unless he was from the Hams, who were Quraysh and Kinanah [and Khuza’ah, Thaqif, Khatham, Banu Amir ibn Sa’sa’ah, and Banu Mudar ibn Mu’awiyah. They were called Hams because of their strictness in their religion. Hamasah means severity and firmness.] “One day, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the house of some of the Ansar, and a man from the Ansar called Rifa’ah ibn al-Tabut entered after him from the door while he was in ihram, so they disapproved of him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Why did you enter through the door while you were in ihram? He said: I saw you enter, so I entered after you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am Hams. The man said: If you are…” Aḥmasiyya, for I am an Aḥmasi, I am pleased with your guidance, your character and your religion. Then God Almighty revealed this verse: “Az-Zuhri said: When some of the Ansar entered ihram for Umrah, nothing would come between them and the sky. A man would go out slowly for Umrah, and a need would appear to him after he had left his house, so he would return and not enter through the door of the room because the roof of the house would come between him and the sky, so he would open the wall behind him. Then he would stand in his room and order what he needed until we were told that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered ihram for Umrah at the time of Hudaybiyyah, and he entered a room, and a man from the Ansar from Banu Salamah entered after him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Why did you do that? He said: Because I saw you enter. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am an Aḥmasi. The Ansari said: I am an Aḥmasi, meaning I am following your religion. Then God Almighty revealed: ‘And righteousness does not consist in entering houses from their backs. ’” Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr read: al-ghayub, al-juyub, al-‘uyun, and shuyukh with a kasra on the first letter because of the ya’. The rest read it with a damma on the original. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read juyubihinna with a kasra on the jim. Abu Bakr and Hamza read al-ghayub with a kasra on the ghayn. But righteousness is he who fears God. That is, righteousness is the righteousness of he who fears God. And enter houses through their doors while in a state of ihram and fear God that you may be successful.
2:190: 190. And fight in the way of God meaning in obedience to God those who fight you At the beginning of Islam, God the Most High commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to refrain from fighting the polytheists. Then when he migrated to Medina, He commanded him to fight whoever fought him from them with this verse. Al-Rabi' bin Anas said: This is the first verse revealed about fighting. Then He commanded him to fight all the polytheists, whether they fought or not, by His saying So kill the polytheists, so this verse was abrogated by it. It was said: It was abrogated by His saying So kill the polytheists, close to seventy verses. And His saying And do not transgress means do not initiate fighting with them. It was said: This verse is decisive and not abrogated. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to fight the fighters. The meaning of His saying: And do not transgress means do not kill women, children, the elderly, monks, or anyone who greets you. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid: Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Bakr ibn Sahl al-Qahstani, known as Abu Turab, told us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tarsusi told us, Yahya ibn Bakir told us, al-Layth ibn Saad, on the authority of Jarir ibn Hazim, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Yazid, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, who said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out an army, he would say: ‘Fight in the name of God and in the way of God. Fight those who disbelieve in God. Do not steal, and do not kill women, children, or old men.’” Al-Kalbi said, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that this verse was revealed regarding the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and that was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with his companions for the minor pilgrimage, and they were one thousand four hundred. They set out until they reached Hudaybiyyah, but the polytheists prevented them from entering the Sacred House, so he made peace with them on the condition that he would return that year, on the condition that they would leave Mecca for him the following year for three days, so that he could circumambulate the House. When the following year came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions prepared for the minor pilgrimage, and they feared that the Quraysh would not fulfill what they had said and would prevent them. About the Sacred House and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hated fighting them in the sacred month and in the sanctuary, so God Almighty revealed: And fight in the way of God meaning in the state of ihram those who fight you meaning Quraysh and do not transgress so that you begin fighting in the sanctuary while in the state of ihram for God does not like transgressors.
2:191: 191. The Almighty said: And kill them wherever you overtake them. The first verse was abrogated by this verse. The origin of culture is cleverness and insight into matters, and its meaning is kill them wherever you see them fighting and are able to kill them. And expel them from where they have expelled you. That is because they expelled the Muslims from Mecca, so He said: Expel them from their homes as they expelled you from your homes. “And persecution is worse than killing.” He means their associating partners with God Almighty is worse and greater than your killing them in the sanctuary and in the state of ihram. “And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them.” Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read: “And do not kill them until they kill you. But if they kill you,” without an alif in them from killing, meaning do not kill some of them. The Arabs say: We killed the sons of so-and-so, but they killed some of them. The rest read with an alif from fighting. This was at the beginning of Islam, as it was not permissible for them to start fighting in the sacred land. Then it was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: And fight them until there is no more persecution. This is the saying of Qatadah, and Muqatil said: Ibn Hayyan said: And kill them wherever you find them, meaning wherever you find them in the sacred precincts and in the sacred precincts. This verse was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque, meaning it was abrogated by the verse of the sword in Bara’ah, so it is abrogating and abrogated. Mujahed and a group said: This verse is decisive and it is not permissible to initiate fighting in the sanctuary. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.
2:192: 192. If they desist from fighting and disbelief, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning, He is Forgiving of what has passed and Merciful to His servants.
2:193: 193. And fight them meaning the polytheists until there is no more persecution meaning polytheism meaning fight them until they submit, so nothing is accepted from the polytheist except Islam. If he refuses, he is killed and the religion meaning obedience and worship is for God alone, so nothing is worshipped besides Him. Nafi` said: A man came to Ibn `Umar during the turmoil of Ibn al-Zubayr and said: What prevents you from going out? He said: What prevents me is that God has made my brother’s blood sacred. He said: Have you not heard what God the Almighty said: And if two parties among the believers should fight 9-Al-Hujurat. He said: O son of my brother, for me to be insulted by this verse and not fight is more beloved to me than to be insulted by the verse in which God the Almighty says: And whoever kills a believer intentionally 93-An-Nisa. He said: Did not God say: And fight them until there is no more Fitnah? He said: We did so during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when Islam was few and a man would be tempted in his religion, either by killing him or by torturing him, until Islam became widespread and there was no Fitnah and the religion was all for God. And you want to fight until there is Fitnah and the religion is for other than God. Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: A man said to Ibn `Umar: What do you think about fighting Fitnah? He said: Do you know what Fitnah is? Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, fought the polytheists, and entering upon them was a trial, not by fighting you for the kingdom. But if they desist from disbelief and submit, there is no aggression and there is no way except against the wrongdoers. Ibn Abbas said: This is indicated by the words of God Almighty: Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no aggression against me 28-Al-Qasas. The scholars of meaning said: Aggression is injustice, meaning if they submit, there is no plunder, capture, or killing except against the wrongdoers who remained upon polytheism. What is done to the polytheists of these things is not injustice. He called it aggression by way of retribution and retaliation, as He said: So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him and as God Almighty said: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it 40-Ash-Shura. The disbeliever was called an oppressor because he places worship in the wrong place.
2:194: 194. The Almighty’s saying: The sacred month for the sacred month was revealed regarding the Umrah of compensation, and that is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to perform the Umrah in Dhul-Qi’dah, and the polytheists prevented him from entering the House at Al-Hudaybiyyah, so he made peace with the people of Mecca on the condition that he would leave that year and return the following year and complete his Umrah. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left that year and returned the following year in Dhul-Qi’dah and completed his Umrah in the year seven of the Hijrah. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: The sacred month meaning Dhul-Qi’dah in which you entered Mecca and completed your Umrah in the year seven, for the sacred month meaning Dhul-Qi’dah in which you were prevented from entering the House in the year six, and the sacred things are retaliation the plural of sanctity, and he only made it plural because he meant the sanctity of the sacred month and the sacred city and the sanctity of ihram, and retaliation is equality and similarity, which is to do to the doer what he did, and it was said that this is in the matter of fighting, meaning: If they start fighting you in the sacred month, then fight them in it, because it is retaliation for what they did in it, and whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him and and fight them with the like of what He assaulted you. He named the recompense after the beginning, based on the duality of speech, as God Almighty said: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it 40-Ash-Shura And fear God and know that God is with the righteous.
2:195: 195. The Almighty’s saying: And spend in the cause of God He meant by it jihad and every good that is in the cause of God, but its generality is directed to jihad. And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction It was said: The ba’ in the Almighty’s saying with your own hands is redundant, meaning: And do not throw your hands, meaning yourselves into destruction He used the words of the self as the Almighty’s saying: For what your hands have earned 30-Ash-Shura meaning for what you have earned, and it was said that the ba’ is in its place, and there is an omission in it, meaning do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction, meaning ruin, and it was said: ruin is everything that ends in ruin, meaning do not take part in that, and it was said: ruin is what can be avoided, and ruin is what cannot be avoided, and the Arabs do not say to a person he threw his hand except in polytheism, and they differed in the interpretation of this verse, some of them said: This is about miserliness and not spending. He says, And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction, by not spending in the way of God. This is the opinion of Hudhayfah, Al-Hasan, Qatada, Ikrimah, and Ata. Ibn Abbas said: In this verse: Spend in the way of God even if you have nothing but an arrow or a small spear, and let not one of you say, I do not have anything. Al-Suddi said: Spend in the way of God even if it is a hobble. And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction, and do not say, I have nothing. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: When God commanded spending, a man said: We were commanded to spend in the way of God, and if we spent our money we would remain poor. So God revealed this verse. Mujahid said about it: Do not let fear of poverty prevent you from spending in the right way. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hairi told us, Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim al-Shaibani told us, Ahmad ibn Hazim ibn Abi Gharzah told us, Abu Ghassan told us, Khalid ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti told us, Wasil, the client of Abu Uyaynah, told us, on the authority of Bashar ibn Abi Saif, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of `Iyad ibn Ghadif, who said: We came to visit Abu Ubaidah, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever spends a surplus amount in the way of God, it will be rewarded seven hundred times over, and whoever spends a sum of money on his family, the good deed will be rewarded ten times over. Zaid bin Aslam said: There were men who went out on expeditions without money, and either they would be cut off, or if they were dependents, then God the Almighty commanded them to spend on themselves in the way of God. And whoever did not have anything to spend, he should not go out without money or sustenance, so he would throw himself into destruction. Destruction means to perish from hunger and thirst or by walking. It was said: The verse was revealed about abandoning jihad. Abu Ayyub al-Ansari said: It was revealed about us, the Ansar, because when God the Almighty made His religion victorious and supported His Messenger, we said among ourselves: We have abandoned our families and our wealth until Islam spread and God supported His Prophet, so if we return to our families and our wealth and stay in them and repair what was lost from them, then God the Almighty revealed: And spend in the way of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction. Destruction means staying with one’s family and wealth and abandoning jihad. Abu Ayyub continued to fight in the way of God until the last expedition he undertook. In Constantinople during the time of Muawiyah, he died there and was buried at the base of the wall of Constantinople, and they were praying to him for rain. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever dies without having fought or having thought of fighting dies in a state of hypocrisy. Muhammad bin Sirin and Ubaidah Al-Salmani said: Throwing oneself into destruction is despairing of the mercy of God Almighty. Abu Qilabah said: It is the man who commits a sin and says: I am ruined, I have no repentance, so he despairs of the mercy of God and indulges in sins. God Almighty forbade them from that. God Almighty said: Indeed, no one despairs of relief from God except the disbelieving people 87-Yusuf. God Almighty says: And do good [meaning, improve your actions and morals and be generous to the poor. Indeed, God loves the doers of good.]
2:196: 196. The Almighty said: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God. Alqamah and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i read: And establish Hajj and Umrah for God. They differed about completing it. Some of them said: It is to complete it with its rituals, limits, and Sunnahs. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Alqamah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Mujahid. The pillars of Hajj are five: Ihram, standing at Arafat, Tawaf Al-Ziyarah, Sa’i between Safa and Marwah, and shaving or trimming the head. There are two types of tahallul for Hajj, and the reasons for tahallul are three: throwing the pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqaba on the Day of Sacrifice, the Tawaf al-Ziyarah, and shaving. If two of these three things are found, the first tahallul is achieved, and the second tahallul is achieved with the three. After the first tahallul, all the prohibitions of ihram are permitted except for women, and after the second, all are permitted. The pillars of Umrah are four: ihram, tawaf around the House, walking between Safa and Marwah, and shaving. Saeed bin Jubair and Tawus said: The completion of Hajj and Umrah is that you enter ihram for them individually, starting from your family circle. The same was narrated by Ibn Masoud. Qatada said: The completion of Umrah is that you perform it outside the months of Hajj. If it is during the months of Hajj, then you stay until you perform Hajj, then it is a pleasure, and you must offer a sacrifice if you can find one, or fast if you cannot find one. The completion of Hajj is that you perform all of its rituals so that the one who performs it is not required to offer a blood sacrifice because of Qiran or pleasure. He said: Ad-Dahhak: Its completion means that the expenditure is lawful and that one refrains from what God has forbidden. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Its completion means that you go out from your family for their sake, and do not go out for trade or for a need. Omar bin Al-Khattab said: The delegation is large and the pilgrims are few, and the nation agreed on the obligation of Hajj for whoever is able to do it, and they differed on the obligation of Umrah, so most of the scholars went to its obligation and this is the opinion of Omar, Ali and Ibn Omar, and Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: By God, about Umrah, because of the context of Hajj in the Book of God, God Almighty said: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God and this is what Ata, Mujahid, Tawus, Qatadah and Saeed bin Jubayr said, and Al-Thawri and Al-Shafi’i went to him in the most correct of his two opinions, and a group went to it that it is a Sunnah and this is the opinion of Jabir and this is what Al-Shafi’i said and Malik and the people of Iraq went to him and they interpreted the words of God Almighty And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God to mean complete them if you enter into them, as for starting them, it is voluntary, and those who did not make them obligatory provided evidence with what was narrated from Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir from Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he was asked about Umrah, is it obligatory? He said: No, and to perform Umrah is better for you.” The first opinion is more correct. The meaning of His statement, And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God, is that you begin them. When you have entered into them, then complete them. This is an order to begin and complete them, i.e. establish them, like the statement of God Almighty, Then complete the fast until the night 187-Al-Baqarah, i.e. begin it and complete it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Amr bin Qais, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Follow up Hajj and Umrah, for they remove poverty and sins just as the bellows remove the impurities of iron, gold, and silver. There is no reward for an accepted Hajj except Paradise.” Ibn Umar said: There is no one among God’s creation who does not have to perform Hajj and Umrah, which are obligatory if he is able to do so, as God the Most High said: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God. So whoever does more after that, it is good and voluntary. The Ummah agreed that it is permissible to perform Hajj and Umrah in three ways: Ifrad, Tamattu’, and Qiran. The form of Ifrad is to perform Hajj alone, then after completing it, perform Umrah. The form of Tamattu’ is to perform Umrah during the months of Hajj, then after completing the rituals of Umrah, enter ihram for Hajj from Mecca and perform Hajj that year. The form of Qiran is to enter ihram for Hajj and Umrah together, or enter ihram for Umrah and then add Hajj to it. Before he begins the circumambulation, he becomes a Qarin, and they differed about what is best from these aspects: A group went to the fact that the individual is better, then the abstention, then the Qiran, and this is the opinion of Malik and Al-Shafi’i, when he informed us. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Aswad Muhammad ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal, on the authority of `Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of `Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, that she said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage. Some of us had entered into ihram for `Umrah, some of us had entered into ihram for Hajj and `Umrah, and some of us had entered into ihram for Hajj. As for those who had entered into ihram for `Umrah, they were released from ihram. As for those who had entered into ihram for Hajj or combined Hajj and `Umrah, they did not become released from ihram until the Day of Sacrifice. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Muslim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ja’far bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, while he was narrating about the Hajj of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: We went out with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, intending nothing but Hajj, and we did not know anything else, nor did we know Umrah. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj alone. Some people went to the view that the Qiran is better, and this is the view of Al-Thawri and the people of opinion, and they cited as evidence what Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad bin Musa Al-Sayrafi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ya’qub Al-Asamm told us, Muhammad bin Hisham bin Malas Al-Namari told us, Marwan bin Mu’awiyah Al-Fazari told us, Hamid told us, Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Here I am for Hajj and Umrah. Some people said that enjoyment is better, and this is the opinion of Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and they provided evidence for what Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malhi told us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail told us, Yahya ibn Bakir told us, al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah, that Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, enjoyed the Umrah until the Hajj during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and he offered a sacrifice, so he drove the sacrifice with him from Dhu al-Hulayfah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began and declared his intention to perform the Umrah, then declared his intention to perform the Hajj, so the people enjoyed the Umrah until the Hajj with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of the people offered a sacrifice and drove the sacrifice, and some of them did not offer a sacrifice. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Mecca, he said to the people, “Whoever among you has offered a sacrifice, he will not be released from anything he has forbidden until he completes his Hajj. Whoever among you has not offered a sacrifice, let him circumambulate the House, and walk between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and shorten his hair and let him become free, then declare his intention to perform the Hajj. Whoever does not find a sacrifice, let him fast three days during the Hajj and seven if he finds one.” He returned to his family, so he performed the circumambulation when he arrived in Mecca, and he touched the corner first, then he walked three times and walked four, then he bowed when he completed his circumambulation of the House at the station, performing two rak’ahs, then he said the greeting of peace and left, then he came to Safa and circumambulated Safa and Marwa seven times, then he did not become free from anything he had forbidden until he had completed his Hajj and slaughtered his sacrificial animal on the Day of Sacrifice and performed the ifadah and circumambulated the House, then he became free from everything he had forbidden, and he did as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did with those who sacrificed and brought sacrificial animals from among the people. On the authority of Urwa, that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, told him about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his enjoyment of the Umrah until the Hajj, so the people enjoyed with him the same thing that Salim told me on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Our Sheikh, the Imam, may God be pleased with him, said: The narrations differed regarding the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ihram, as we mentioned. Al-Shafi’i mentioned briefly in his book, Ikhtilaf al-Ahadith, that the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) included the mufrid, the qiran, and the mutamatti’, and each one took from him the matter of his rituals and issued from his teachings. So each one was attributed to him in the sense that he ordered it and permitted it. It is permissible in the Arabic language to add the thing to the one who ordered it, just as it is permissible to add it to the one who did it, as it is said that so-and-so built a house, meaning that he ordered its construction, and as it was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stoned Ma’iz, and he only ordered his stoning. Al-Shafi’i chose to add the singular to narrate the story of the Farewell Pilgrimage and its end, and because of the superiority of Aisha’s may God be pleased with her memorization, and the closeness of Ibn Umar to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Shafi’i leaned towards enjoyment in the differences in the hadiths, and he said: “Nothing of the differences is easier than this, even if the mistake in it is ugly in terms of it being permissible, because the Book, then the Sunnah, then what I do not know of any disagreement in, is that enjoyment of ‘umrah to Hajj and individual Hajj and Qiran, all of it is broad. He said: Whoever says that he individualized Hajj is like someone who is residing for Hajj except that he began his ihram with Hajj. Sheikh Al-Imam, may God have mercy on him, said: What indicates that he was enjoying is that the narration from Ibn ‘Umar and ‘Aishah contradicts it, and we have narrated from Ibn Shihab from Salim from Ibn ‘Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, enjoyed himself in [the Farewell Pilgrimage by performing ‘umrah to Hajj. Ibn Shihab said from ‘Urwah that ‘Aishah informed him from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace] in enjoying ‘umrah to Hajj, so the people enjoyed themselves with him in the same way that Salim informed me from Ibn ‘Umar. Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘This is an ‘umrah that we enjoyed.’” Saad bin Abi Waqqas said about temporary marriage: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did it and we did it with him. The Sheikh Al-Imam said: What was narrated from Jabir that he said: We went out intending nothing but Hajj - does not contradict Tamattu’ because their going out was for the purpose of Hajj, then some of them came forward to perform Umrah, and some of them were in the state of Hajj until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to make it Tamattu’. God Almighty said: But if you are prevented The scholars differed regarding the prevention that permits the pilgrim to break his state of ihram. A group went to the view that every obstacle that prevents him from reaching the Sacred House, and the meaning of his state of ihram is an enemy, illness, injury, loss of money, or a lost mount, permits him to break his state of ihram. Ibn Mas’ud said the same, and it is the view of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata’, Qatadah, and Urwah bin Al-Zubayr. Sufyan Al-Thawri and the people of Iraq went to it and said: Because prevention in the speech of the Arabs means confinement due to illness or disease. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaidah said: Whatever was due to illness or loss of money is said: he is confined, so he is confined, and whatever was due to the confinement of an enemy or prison is said: he is confined, and here the confinement of the enemy is considered confinement. By analogy with illness, since it is in its meaning, and they provided evidence for what was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Amr Al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever breaks or is lame has been released from his obligation and must perform Hajj the following year. Akrima said: I asked Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurairah and they said he was telling the truth. A group of people said that he is not permitted to become released except by being confined by the enemy, which is the opinion of Ibn Abbas. He said: There is no confinement except by the confinement of the enemy. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Omar and Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, which is the opinion of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Saeed bin Jubair, and Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Ishaq agreed with it. They said: Confinement and confinement have the same meaning. Tha’lab said: The Arabs say: If a man is prevented from his need, then he is prevented. And the enemy prevents him from moving, then he is prevented. They argued that this verse was revealed in the story of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and that was a confinement by the enemy, and this is indicated by the Almighty’s saying in the context of the verse: So when you are safe. And safety comes from fear. They weakened the hadith of Al-Hajjaj bin Amr, based on what was proven from Ibn Abbas that he said: There is no confinement except the confinement of the enemy. Some of them interpreted it as meaning that it is permissible to break or limp if that had been stipulated in the contract of ihram, as it was narrated that Duba’ah bint Al-Zubayr was in pain, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: “Perform Hajj and stipulate and say: O God, my place is where You have detained me.” Then the person who is prevented from performing Hajj becomes released from the state of ihram by slaughtering the sacrificial animal and shaving his head. The sacrificial animal is a sheep, which is what is meant by the Almighty’s saying, Then whatever sacrifice is easy to make. The place for slaughtering it is where he is prevented according to most scholars, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered the sacrificial animal there in the year of al-Hudaybiyah. Some people said that the person who is prevented from performing Hajj remains in his state of ihram and sends his sacrificial animal to the Sacred Sanctuary, and appoints someone to slaughter it there, then he becomes released from the state of ihram. This is the opinion of the people of Iraq. There is a difference of opinion regarding the person who is prevented from finding a sacrificial animal. Some say that he must do so, so he becomes free of the obligation and the sacrificial animal is his responsibility until he finds one. The second opinion is that he has a substitute. Based on this, there is a difference of opinion regarding him. In one opinion, he must fast tamattu’. In another opinion, a sheep is sufficient as a ransom for perfume and clothing. If the person in ihram needs to cover his head due to heat or cold, or to wear a shirt, or is sick and needs to be treated with a medicine that contains perfume, he does so and must pay the ransom. His ransom is in order and in order. He must slaughter a sheep. If he cannot find one, the sheep is sufficient for dirhams, and the dirhams are used to buy food and give it in charity. If he is unable to do so, he must fast for each mudd one day. Then, if the person who is prevented from entering ihram was for a purpose that he had settled on, then that purpose is his responsibility. If it was for a voluntary Hajj, does he have to make up for it? They differed regarding it. A group said that he does not have to make up for it, which is the opinion of Malik and al-Shafi’i. M said that he has to make up for it, which is the opinion of Mujahid, al-Sha’bi, al-Nakha’i and the people of opinion. The Almighty said: Then whatever is easy of the sacrifice [meaning, he should offer whatever is easy of the sacrifice] and its position is nominative. It was said: What is in the position of accusative, meaning, then offer whatever is easy. The sacrifice is the plural of gift, and it is the name for everything that is offered to the House of God to draw closer to Him. Whatever is easy of the sacrifice is a sheep, said Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn Abbas, because it is closer to ease. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: The highest is a camel, the middle is a cow, and the lowest is a sheep. God Almighty says: And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination. They differed about the place where the one who is prevented from slaughtering his sacrificial animal is permitted to reach it. Some of them said: It is slaughtering it in the place where he is prevented, whether it is outside the Haram or in the Sacred Sanctuary. The meaning of its place is where it is permissible to slaughter it and eat it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, Al-Zuhri told me, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me, on the authority of Al-Miswar bin Makhrama, in the story of Al-Hudaybiyyah, he said: When he finished the matter of the book, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: Get up and slaughter, then shave your heads. By God, not a single one of them got up until he said that three times. When none of them got up, he went to Umm Salamah and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah said: O Prophet of God, do you like that? Go out, then do not say a word to any of them until you slaughter your sacrificial animal and call your barber to shave you. So he went out and did not speak to any of them until he did that. He slaughtered his sacrificial animal and called his barber to shave him. When they saw that, they got up and slaughtered, and some of them shaved each other until some of them almost killed each other out of grief. Some of them said: The place of the sacrificial animal of the one who is prevented is the Sacred Sanctuary. If he is a pilgrim, then its place is the Day of Sacrifice. If he is a pilgrim, then its place is the day his sacrificial animal reaches the Sacred Sanctuary. The Almighty said: But if any of you is ill or has an ailment in his head meaning do not shave your heads while in a state of ihram unless you are forced to shave it due to illness or an ailment in the head from vermin or a headache. Then a ransom is implied in it, meaning: if he shaves, then he must pay a ransom. It was revealed about Ka’b ibn Ujrah. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hasan bin Khalaf told us, Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr and Raqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Abdul Rahman bin Abi Laila told me, on the authority of Ka’b bin Ujrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him and lice were falling on his face, so he said: Do your lice bother you? He said: Yes. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to shave his head while he was at Al-Hudaibiyah, and he did not tell them that they were going to leave it while they were hoping to enter Mecca. Then God revealed the ransom, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to feed six poor people a faraq, or to sacrifice a sheep, or to fast for three days. God the Almighty said: Then a ransom of fasting meaning three days or charity meaning three sa’s for six poor people, for each poor person half a sa’ or a sacrifice the singular of which is a sacrifice, the highest of which is a camel, the middle of which is a cow, and the lowest of which is a sheep, whichever sheep he slaughters. This ransom is based on choice and discretion, and he has the choice between slaughtering or fasting or giving charity, and each one wherever he wants. God the Almighty said: And when you are secure meaning from your fear and you have recovered from your illness and whoever enjoys the ‘umrah during the Hajj, then such an offering as can be obtained easily they differed regarding this enjoyment. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr thought that its meaning is: whoever is prevented until the Hajj passes him by and he does not become free of it and he comes to Mecca, he exits his state of ihram by performing an ‘umrah and enjoys his release by that ‘umrah until the next year, then he performs Hajj, so he enjoys that release until his second state of ihram in the following year. Some of them said that its meaning is and when you are secure and you have become free of your state of ihram after being prevented and have not performed an ‘umrah, and you have delayed the ‘umrah until the next year, so you perform the ‘umrah in The months of Hajj, then you are released and enjoy your release for Hajj, then you enter ihram for Hajj, so you must make what is easy of the sacrifice, and this is the opinion of Alqamah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Saeed bin Jubair. Ibn Abbas, Ata’, and a group said: It is the man who comes as a pilgrim from a horizon during the months of Hajj, and he completes his Umrah and stays in Makkah in a state of ihram until he begins Hajj from there, so he performs Hajj that year, so he is enjoying the release from Umrah until his ihram for Hajj, so the meaning of enjoyment is enjoying after leaving Umrah what was forbidden to him during ihram until his ihram for Hajj. There are four conditions for the obligation of the blood of Tamattu’: First, that he enters into ihram for Umrah during the months of Hajj. Second, that he performs Hajj after completing Umrah in this year. Third, that he enters into ihram for Hajj in Mecca and does not return to the miqat to enter into ihram. Fourth, that he is not one of those present at the Sacred Mosque. When these conditions are met, he must offer whatever sacrifice he can, which is the blood of a sheep that he slaughters on the Day of Sacrifice. If he slaughters it before that after entering into ihram for Hajj, it is permissible according to some scholars, like the blood of crimes. Some of them are of the view that it is not permissible before the Day of Sacrifice, like the blood of a sacrificial animal.
