The Almighty said: But whoever cannot find [the means], then a fast of three days during Hajj. That is, fast three days, fasting one day before Tarwiyah, the day of Tarwiyah, and the day of Arafah. If he fasts before it after entering ihram for Hajj, it is permissible. The day of sacrifice and the days of Tashreeq are not permissible according to most scholars. Some of them said that it is permissible to fast the three days of Tashreeq. This is narrated on the authority of Aisha, Ibn Omar, and Ibn Al-Zubayr, and it is the opinion of Malik, Al-Awza’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. The Almighty’s statement, seven when you return, meaning fast seven days when you return to your family and country. If one fasts the seven days before returning to his family, it is not permissible, and this is the opinion of most scholars. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas, and it was said that it is permissible to fast them after completing the Hajj rituals, and this is what is meant by the return mentioned in the verse. The Almighty said: These are ten complete days. He mentioned it for emphasis, and this is because the Arabs were not guided to the reckoning, so they needed the benefit of explanation and further clarification. It was said: There is an advance and a delay in it, meaning fasting ten days, three during the Hajj and seven when you return, so they are ten complete days. It was said: Complete in reward and recompense. It was said: Complete in what is meant by it of establishing the fast instead of the sacrifice. It was said: Complete with its conditions and limits. It was said that its wording is report and its meaning is an order, meaning complete it and do not reduce it. That meaning this ruling is for those whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque. They differed regarding those present at the Sacred Mosque. Some people went to the view that they are the people of Mecca, and this is the view of Malik. It was said: They are the people of the Sanctuary, and this is the view of Tawus from the followers. Ibn Jurayj said: The people of Arafat, Al-Raji’, Dajnan, and Nakhltan. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: Everyone whose homeland is less than the distance of shortening from Mecca is one of those present at the Sacred Mosque. Ikrimah said: They are those below the Miqat. It was said: They are the people of the Miqat and below it, and this is the view of the companions of the Prophet. Opinion, and the blood of the Qiran is like the blood of the Tamattu’ and the Makkan, if he combines or enjoys, then there is no sacrifice on him. Ikrimah said: Ibn Abbas was asked about the enjoyment of Hajj, so he said: The people of the Muhajirun and the Ansar and the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and we declared our ihram, and when we arrived in Mecca, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Make your ihram for Hajj an ‘Umrah, except for those who wear a sacrificial animal. So we circumambulated the House and Safa and Marwah, and we went to the women and put on our clothes, then he ordered us on the eve of Tarwiyah to declare our ihram for Hajj, so when we finished, our Hajj was complete and we were required to offer the sacrificial animal. So combine our two sacrifices in one year between Hajj and ‘Umrah, for God revealed it in His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet and permitted it for people other than the people of Mecca. God Almighty said: That is for those whose families are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. Whoever misses the Hajj, and missing it is due to missing standing at Arafat until dawn on the Day of Sacrifice, then he becomes free of the obligation of performing the Umrah, and he must make up for it the following year and pay the ransom, which is in order and estimation like the ransom for Tamattu’ and Qiran. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, that Hunad ibn al-Aswad came on the Day of Sacrifice while `Umar ibn al-Khattab was slaughtering his sacrificial animal, and he said: O Commander of the Faithful, we made a mistake in counting. We thought that this day was the Day of `Arafah. `Umar said to him: Go to Mecca and circumambulate the House, you and those with you, and walk between al-Safa and al-Marwah and slaughter a sacrificial animal if you have any, then shave or shorten your hair, then return. When the following year comes, perform Hajj and offer a sacrificial animal. Whoever cannot find any, then fast for three days during Hajj and seven when you return. And fear God in carrying out the commands and know that God is severe in punishment for committing the prohibitions.
2:197: 197. God the Almighty said: The Hajj is in well-known months meaning the time of Hajj is well-known months, which are: Shawwal, Dhul-Qi’dah, and nine of Dhul-Hijjah until dawn on the Day of Sacrifice. It is narrated from Ibn ‘Umar that Shawwal, Dhul-Qi’dah, and ten of Dhul-Hijjah, and each of the two expressions is correct and there is no difference. Whoever said ten expressed the nights with it, and whoever said nine expressed the days with it, because the last of its days is the Day of ‘Arafah, which is the ninth day. He only said months with the plural form, which is two months and some of the third, because it is a time, and the Arabs call the time complete by its short and long duration. So the Arabs say I came to you on Thursday, but he came to it in an hour of it. And he says I visited you this year, but he visited it in some of it. It was said that two and above them are a group, because the meaning of the plural is to join one thing to another. So if it is permissible to call two a group, it is permissible to call two and some of the third a group. God the Almighty mentioned two with the plural form, so He said, So your hearts have become inclined 4-At-Tahrim, meaning your two hearts. ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others said: He meant by the months Shawwal, Dhul-Qi’dah, and Dhul-Ziyyah in Mina, so they are like the Hajj. So whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them meaning whoever He made Hajj obligatory upon himself by entering into ihram and talbiyah, and in it is evidence that whoever enters into ihram for Hajj outside the months of Hajj, his ihram for Hajj is not valid. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas and Jabir, and this is what Ata, Tawus, and Mujahid said. Al-Awza’i and Al-Shafi’i agreed with him, and he said that his ihram for Umrah is valid because God Almighty has singled out these months for the purpose of Hajj in them, so if it were to be held outside of them, this specialization would not be of any benefit. He also linked the prayers to the appointed times, and whoever enters into ihram for the obligatory prayer before its time begins, his ihram for the obligatory prayer is not valid. A group of people said that his ihram for Hajj is valid, and this is the opinion of Malik, Al-Thawri, and Abu Hanifah, may God be pleased with them. As for Umrah, it is valid for all days of the year unless he is engaged in Hajj. It was narrated on the authority of Anas that he was in Mecca, and when he washed his head, he would go out and perform Umrah. God the Almighty said: No obscenity nor wickedness. Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read No obscenity nor wickedness with the nominative case and tanween in both of them. The others read it with the accusative case without tanween, like God the Almighty’s saying: No disputing during Hajj. Abu Ja`far read it all with the nominative case and tanween. They differed regarding rafath: Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn `Abbas, and Ibn `Umar said that it is sexual intercourse, and this is the saying of Al-Hasan, Mujahid, `Amr ibn Dinar, Qatadah, `Ikrimah, Al-Rabi`, and Ibrahim Al-Nakha`i. `Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: Rafath is intercourse with women, kissing, winking, and exposing her to obscene speech. Husayn ibn Qays said that Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with him, took hold of the tail of his camel and began to twist it while it was urging him on, saying: They walk with us whispering, if the bird is truthful, we will be with you, Lamisa. I said to him, Do you indulge in lewdness while you are in a state of ihram? He said, Rafth is what is said in front of women. Tawus said, Rafth is exposing oneself to women and mentioning it in front of them. Ata’ said, Rafth is what a man says to a woman while in a state of ihram, ‘When you have finished, I will have intercourse with you.’ It was also said, Rafth is obscenity and ugly speech. As for fusooq, Ibn Abbas said, It is all sins. This is the opinion of Tawus, al-Hasan, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Zuhri, al-Rabi’, and al-Qurazi. Ibn Umar said, It is what the pilgrim is forbidden from doing while in a state of ihram, such as killing game, clipping nails, removing hair, and the like. Ibrahim, Ata’, and Mujahid said, “It is insulting, based on the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘Insulting a Muslim is lewdness, and fighting him is disbelief.’” Ad-Dahhak said, “It is name-calling, based on the statement of God Almighty, ‘And do not insult one another by nicknames. Evil is the name of lewdness after faith.’” Al-Hujurat 11. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam told us, Sayyar Abu Al-Hakam told us, he said: I heard Abu Hazim say: I heard Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs Hajj for the sake of God and does not utter obscenities or commit sin returns as on the day his mother bore him. God the Almighty said: And there is no disputing during Hajj. Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas said: Disputing means arguing with one’s companion and quarreling with him until he angers him. This is the opinion of Amr ibn Dinar, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Ata’ and Qatadah. Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: It is when some of them say Hajj and some of them say Hajj tomorrow. Al-Qurazi said: When the Quraysh gathered in Mina, some would say: Our Hajj is more complete than your Hajj, and those would say: Our Hajj is more complete than your Hajj. Muqatil said: It is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them during the Farewell Pilgrimage when they had entered ihram for Hajj: Make your ihram for Hajj an ‘Umrah, except for those who wear sacrificial animals. They said: How can we make it an ‘Umrah when we have named Hajj? This is their argument. Ibn Zayd said: They used to stand in different positions, each claiming that his position was the position of Abraham, and they would argue about it. It was said: It is what the people of ignorance were like. Some of them would stand at Arafat and some at Muzdalifah, and some of them would perform Hajj in Dhul-Qa'dah and some of them would perform Hajj in Dhul-Hijjah, so everyone would say, What I did is correct. So the Most High said, And there is no argument in Hajj. That is, the matter of Hajj was settled on what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did, so there is no disagreement about it after that. This is the meaning of the Prophet's saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Behold, time has turned back to its state on the day God created the heavens and the earth. Mujahid said: Its meaning is, And there is no doubt in Hajj that it is in Dhul-Hijjah, so he abolished the postponement. The scholars of meaning said: The apparent meaning of the verse is negation, and its meaning is prohibition, that is, do not engage in obscenity, do not commit sin, and do not argue, like the Most High's saying, There is no doubt about it, that is, do not have doubts. And whatever good you do, God knows it, that is, it is not hidden from Him, so He will reward you for it. God the Almighty said: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. This was revealed about some people from Yemen who would go out to Hajj without provisions and would say: We are performing Hajj to the House of God and He does not feed us. So when they arrived in Mecca, they would ask people, and this might lead them to plunder and robbery. So God the Almighty said: And take provisions, meaning that which you will eat and with which you will cover your faces. The commentators said: cakes, raisins, gruel, dates, and the like. But indeed, the best provision is fear of God, from asking and plundering. And fear God, O you of understanding, O you of intellects.
2:198: 198. The Almighty said: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Ali bin Abdullah informed us, Sufyan informed us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhu Al-Majaz were markets in the pre-Islamic era. When Islam came, they felt guilty about trading in them, so God Almighty revealed: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the Hajj seasons. Ibn Abbas read it thus. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Taimi, who said: I said to Ibn Omar: We are a people who rent in this direction, meaning to Mecca, and they claim that we do not have Hajj. He said: Do you not enter ihram as they do, and circumambulate as they do, and throw stones as they do? I said, Yes. He said, You are a pilgrim. A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him about what you had asked me about, but he did not answer him with anything until Gabriel revealed this verse: There is no blame upon you meaning, if you seek bounty meaning, provision “from your Lord” meaning, by trading during the Hajj seasons. Then when you have poured out means, you have paid. Pouring out means paying in abundance, and its origin is from the Arab saying: A man poured out water meaning, from Arafat which is the plural of Arafat, a plural for what is around it, even if it is a single spot, like their saying, a garment of morals. They differed about the meaning for which the standing place and the day were called Arafat. Ata’ said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, used to show Abraham, peace be upon him, the rituals and say, Do you understand? He said: I knew, so that place was called Arafat, and today is Arafat. Ad-Dahhak said: When Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down to earth, he was in India and Eve in Jeddah, so each one of them sought out his companion, and they met in Arafat on the day of Arafat and got to know each other, so the day was called the day of Arafat and the place was Arafat. As-Suddi said: When Abraham announced the Hajj to the people and they responded to him with the Talbiyah and those who came to him came, God ordered him to go out to Arafat and described it to him, so he went out and when he reached the Jamrah near the Kaaba, Satan met him to turn him back, so he threw seven pebbles at him, saying Allahu Akbar with each pebble, so he flew and landed on the second Jamrah, so he threw it and said Allahu Akbar, so it flew, and when he looked at it, he did not recognize it, so it passed and was called Dhu al-Majaz. Then he set off until he stood in Arafat and recognized it by the description, so the time was called Arafat and the place was called Arafat, until when evening came, he approached the gathering, meaning he approached the gathering, so it was called Muzdalifah. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saleh on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that Abraham, peace be upon him, saw in his dream on the night of Tarwiyah that he was commanded to slaughter his son. When morning came, he thought about it all day, was this dream from God Almighty or from Satan? So the day was called the Day of Tarwiyah. Then he saw it on the night of Arafah a second time, and when morning came, he knew that it was from God Almighty, so the day was called the Day of Arafah. It was said that it was called that because people confess their sins on that day. It was also said that it was called that because of the fragrance, which means good. It was called Mina because blood is poured out in it, so there is dung and blood in it, and the place is not good. Arafat is pure from them, so it is good. The Almighty said: So remember God with supplication and Talbiyah at Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram which is the area between the two mountains of Muzdalifah from the two valleys of Arafat to Al-Muhsir. Neither Al-Muhsir nor Al-Muhsir are from Al-Mash’ar. It was called Al-Mash’ar from Al-Sha’ar, which is the sign, because it is one of the landmarks of Hajj. The origin of Al-Haram is from the prohibition, so it is forbidden to do in it what has not been called for. Al-Muzdalifah was called a gathering place because the two Isha prayers are combined in it. The departure from Arafat is after sunset, and whoever combines before sunrise is from the Day of Sacrifice. Tawus said: The people of the pre-Islamic era used to set out from Arafat before the sun set and from Muzdalifah after the sun rose, and they would say: Thabir has risen so that we may make a raid. But God delayed this and brought forward this. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Musa ibn `Uqbah, on the authority of Kurayb, the freed slave of `Abdullah ibn `Abbas, on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd, that he heard him say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out from `Arafat until he reached the ravine, dismounted and urinated, then performed ablution but did not perform it completely. So I said to him: ‘The prayer, O Messenger of God. ’ He said: ‘The prayer is ahead of you. ’ So he mounted, and when he came to Muzdalifah he dismounted and performed ablution and performed it completely. Then the call to prayer was made, so he prayed the sunset prayer, then each person made his camel kneel in his home. Then the call to prayer was made for the night prayer and he prayed it and did not pray anything between them.” Jabir said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out until he reached Muzdalifah, where he prayed the sunset and evening prayers with one call to prayer and two iqamas, and he did not glorify God at all between them. Then he lay down until dawn came, and he prayed the dawn prayer when the dawn became clear to him with one call to prayer and one iqama. Then he rode Al-Qaswa’ until he reached Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, and he faced the qiblah. He called upon it, glorified it, declared His oneness, and declared His oneness. He did not stop standing until it became very light, and he set out before the sun rose.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Zuhair bin Harb told us, Wahb bin Jarir told us, my father told us, on the authority of Yunus Al-Ayli, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that Usama bin Zaid rode behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Arafat to Muzdalifah, then Al-Fadl rode behind him from Muzdalifah to Mina. He said: Both of them said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to recite the Talbiyah until he threw the pebbles at Jamrat Al-Aqaba. The Almighty said: And remember Him as He has guided you. That is, remember Him with monotheism and glorification as He reminded you of guidance, so He guided you to His religion and the rituals of His pilgrimage. And if you were before that among those astray. That is, you were. It was also said: And before that you were nothing but astray. Like the Almighty’s saying: And we think you are among the liars. 186-Ash-Shu’ara’ That is, we think you are nothing but liars. The ha in His saying before that refers to guidance. It was also said: to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a metaphor for someone not mentioned.
2:199: 199. The Almighty’s saying: Then proceed from where the people proceed. The commentators said that the Quraysh and their allies and those who followed their religion were too proud to stand at Muzdalifah and say: We are the people of God and the inhabitants of His sanctuary, so we will not leave the sanctuary or leave it. They were too proud to stand with the rest of the Arabs at Arafat, and the rest of the people were standing at Arafat. So when the people proceeded from Arafat, the people proceeded from Muzdalifah, so God commanded them to stand at Arafat and proceed from it to Jam’ with the rest of the people, and He informed them that it was the Sunnah of Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them. Some of them said that He addressed all the Muslims with it. And the Almighty’s saying, From where the people proceed from Jam’a to Mina. They said that the proceeding from Arafat is before the proceeding from Jam’a, so how can it be permissible to say, So when you proceed from Arafat, remember God at the sacred monument, then proceed from Arafat? The first is the saying of most of the commentators. In the speech there is an estimation and a delay, the estimation of which is: And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein, there is no sexual relations nor disobedience nor disputing during Hajj. Then depart from where the people depart. And when you depart from Arafat, remember God at the sacred monument. It was said: Then it means and, meaning and pour out, like the Almighty’s saying: Then he was among those who believed 17-Al-Balad. As for the people, they are all Arabs except the Hams. Al-Kalbi said: They are the people of Yemen and Rabi’ah. Ad-Dahhak said: The people here are Abraham, peace be upon him, alone, as God Almighty said: Or do they envy people? An-Nisa’ 54. He meant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone. It is said that this is the one who is emulated and who is the tongue of his people. Az-Zuhri said: The people here are Adam, peace be upon him, alone. Its evidence is the reading of Saeed bin Jubayr, then they poured out from where the people poured out with the letter ya’. It is said: He is Adam who forgot God’s covenant when he ate from the tree. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Yusuf told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, who said: Usama was asked while I was sitting, how did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walk during the Farewell Pilgrimage when he set out? He said: He walked at a distance of his neck, and if he found a gap, he would cut it. Hisham said: And the cut is above the neck. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Ibrahim bin Suwaid told us, Amr bin Abi Amr, the freed slave of Al-Muttalib told me, Saeed bin Jubair, the freed slave of Walbah Al-Kufi told me, Ibn Abbas told me that he set out with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of Arafah, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard behind him a severe rebuke and the beating of camels, so he pointed to them and said: O people, be calm, for righteousness does not consist in neglecting, and seek forgiveness from God, for God is Forgiving and Merciful.
2:200: 200. The Almighty said: And when you have completed your rites meaning you have finished your Hajj and slaughtered your women, meaning your sacrifices. It is said: a man performs a ritual sacrifice if he slaughters his sacrifice, and that is after throwing the pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqaba and settling in Mina. Then remember God by glorifying, praising and thanking Him as you remember your fathers because the Arabs, when they finished the Hajj, would stand at the House and remember the glories of their fathers, so God the Almighty commanded them to remember Him and said: Then remember Me, for I am the one who did that to you and to your fathers and was good to you and to them. Ibn Abbas and Ata’ said: Its meaning is: So remember God as young children remember their fathers. This is because when a child first speaks, he mentions his father, not someone else, so he says: God, so remember God and nothing else, as a child mentions his father, or even more so. Ibn Abbas was asked about His statement: So remember God as you remember your fathers, and it was said: A day may come upon a man and he does not mention his father. Ibn Abbas said: It is not like that, but rather that you become angry for the sake of God if He is disobeyed, more so than you become angry for the sake of your parents if they curse them. And the statement of God the Almighty: Or more so in remembrance, means: and more so in remembrance, or more so, that is, more so in remembrance. “And among the people is he who says: Our Lord, give us in this world,” meaning the polytheists, who would not ask God the Almighty during the Hajj except for this world, saying: O God, give us sheep, camels, cows, and slaves. And a man would stand and say: O Lord, because my father had a large dome, a large bowl, and a lot of money, so give me the same as what You gave him. Qatada said: This is a slave whose intention is the world, for which he spent and for which he worked and struggled. And he will have no share in the Hereafter, of portion and share.
2:201: 201. "And among them is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'" Meaning the believers, and they differed regarding the meaning of the two good things. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: In this world that which is good is a righteous woman, and in the Hereafter that which is good is Paradise. Abu al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hanafi told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad bin Yaqub al-Tusi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Yusuf bin Khallad told us, al-Harith bin Abi Usama told us, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri told us, Haywah and Ibn Lahi’ah told us, they said, Shurahbil bin Sharik told us that he heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli narrating on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin al-Aas, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The whole world is provision, and the best provision of it is a righteous woman. Al-Hasan said: “In this world there is goodness: knowledge and worship, and in the Hereafter there is goodness: Paradise.” Al-Suddi and Ibn Hayyan said: In this world there is goodness: lawful provision and righteous deeds, and in the Hereafter there is goodness: forgiveness and reward. Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abi Tobah told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Al-Harith told us, Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Yaqub Al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah bin Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim bin Abdullah Al-Khalal told us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, Yahya bin Ayoub told us, Ubaidullah bin Zahr told me, Ali bin Yazid told us, Al-Qasim Abu Abd Al-Rahman told us, Abu Umamah told us, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The one I envy most among my friends is a believer who is easy-going, has a share of prayer, worships his Lord well, obeys Him in secret, is obscure among people, no one points to him, and his provision is sufficient, but he is patient with that. Then he whipped his hand said: ‘His death hastened, his mourners said little, his inheritance said little.’” Qatada said: In this world there is well-being and in the Hereafter there is well-being. Awf said about this verse: Whoever God gives Islam, the Qur’an, a family and wealth has been given good in this world and good in the Hereafter. Sheikh Abu al-Qasim Abdullah bin Ali al-Karkani al-Tusi told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Mahmash al-Ziyadi told us, Abu al-Fadl Abdus bin al-Husayn bin Mansur al-Sammar told us, Abu Hatim Muhammad bin Idris al-Hanthali al-Razi told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah al-Ansari told us, Hamid al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Banani, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man who had become like a chick, so he said: ‘Did you supplicate to God for something or ask Him for it? ’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, I used to say: O God, whatever You are going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world. ’ He said: ‘Glory be to God, then you cannot do it and you cannot bear it. Why did you not say: O God, our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and save us from the punishment of the Fire? ’” Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Ishaq al-Hajjaji told us, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Da’uli told us, Muhammad ibn Mishkan told us, Abu Dawud told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say often: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Kisa’i told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Saeed bin Salem Al-Qaddah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Yahya bin Ubayd, the client of Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib, that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, between the corner of Banu Jumah and the Black Corner: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
2:202: 202. The Almighty’s saying: For them is a share a portion of what they have earned of good and supplication for reward and recompense. And God is swift in account meaning if He takes account, His account is swift and does not require a contraction of the hand, nor awareness of the chest, nor contemplation or thought. Al-Hasan said: It is faster than the blink of an eye. It was also said: Its meaning is that the coming of the Resurrection is near, because what is bound to happen is near. God Almighty said: And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. 17-Ash-Shura.
2:203: 203. The Almighty's saying, And remember God means the takbirs after the prayer and at the Jamarat, one says takbir with every pebble and other times, during the appointed days. The appointed days are the days of Tashreeq, which are the days of Mina and stoning the Jamarat. They are called appointed because they are few, as in His saying, counted dirhams 20-Yusuf. The appointed days are the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, the last of which is the Day of Sacrifice. This is the saying of most scholars. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that the appointed days are: the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it. The appointed days are the Day of Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and the Days of Tashreeq. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: They are one thing, and they are the Days of Tashreeq. It was narrated from Nabisha al-Hudhali that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Days of Tashreeq are days of eating, drinking, and remembering God. Among the remembrances during the days of Tashreeq is the takbir. They differed about it. It was narrated on the authority of Omar and Abdullah bin Omar that they used to say takbir in Mina on those days after the prayer, in the gathering, on the bed and in the tent, and on the road. The people would say takbir with their takbir, and they would interpret this verse. And the Takbir after the prayer is prescribed in these days for the pilgrim and the non-pilgrim according to the majority of scholars, and they differed about its amount. Some people said that the Takbir begins after the Fajr prayer on the Day of Arafah and ends after the Asr prayer on the last day of Tashreeq. This is narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, and Makhul said the same, and Abu Yusuf, may God be pleased with him, said the same. Some people said that the Takbir begins after the Fajr prayer on the Day of Arafah and ends after the Asr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, and Abu Hanifa said the same. Some people said that it begins after the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice and ends after the Fajr prayer on the last day of Tashreeq. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Malik and Al-Shafi’i said the same. Al-Shafi’i said: Because people follow the pilgrim in it, and the pilgrim mentions the Talbiyah before this time, and they begin the Takbir on the Day of Sacrifice from the Dhuhr prayer. The wording of the Takbir: Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Al-Hasan used to say: God is Great, God is Great, God is Great three times in sequence - and this is the opinion of the people of Madinah, and Al-Shafi’i said the same. He said: Anything more than the remembrance of God is good. Among the people of Iraq, one says Allahu Akbar twice. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud. God the Almighty said: But whoever hastens to leave in two days, there is no sin upon him. He meant that whoever departs from the pilgrim on the second day of the days of Tashreeq, there is no sin upon him. That is because the pilgrim must spend the night in Mina on the first and second nights of the days of Tashreeq and throw twenty-one pebbles every day after noon, seven pebbles at each Jamrah. He permitted camel herders and those who provide water to the pilgrims to leave the overnight stay. Then whoever throws pebbles on the second day of the days of Tashreeq and wants to leave, he should leave the overnight stay on the third night and throw pebbles on that day. This is permissible for him, based on God the Almighty’s saying: But whoever hastens to leave in two days, there is no sin upon him. And whoever does not leave until the sun sets, he must spend the night until he throws pebbles on the third day, then leave. God the Almighty said: And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him. That means there is no sin upon whoever hastens and leaves on the second day for his haste, and whoever delays until he leaves on the third day, there is no sin upon him for his delay. It was said: Its meaning is So whoever hastens has taken a concession there is no sin upon him by taking a concession and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him by not taking a concession. It was said that its meaning is he returned forgiven, no sin upon him for rushing or delaying, as we narrated from He who performs Hajj and does not utter obscenities or commit sin returns as the day his mother bore him. This is the saying of Ali and Ibn Masoud. God the Almighty says: For whoever fears God meaning for whoever fears doing something during his Hajj that God has forbidden him to do, as He said: Whoever performs Hajj and does not utter obscenities or commit sin. Ibn Mas`ud said: Forgiveness of sins is only given to whoever fears God the Almighty during his Hajj. In Al-Kalbi’s narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the meaning of for whoever fears God is hunting. It is not permissible for him to kill game until the days of Tashreeq are over. Abu Al-`Aliyah said: His sin is gone if he fears God in what remains of his life. [And fear God and know that to Him you will be gathered you will be gathered in the Hereafter and He will reward you for your deeds].
2:204: 204. God the Almighty said: And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in the life of this world. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and Ata’ said: It was revealed about Al-Akhns bin Shuraiq Al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, whose name was Abu. He was called Al-Akhns because he prevented three hundred men of Banu Zuhrah from fighting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr. He was a man of sweet speech and sweet appearance. He used to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sit with him and show Islam, and say, I love you, and swear by God to that. He was a hypocrite, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to bring him close to his seat. Then God the Almighty said: And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in the life of this world, meaning you find him good and he finds it great in your heart. It is said in terms of approval, I like such-and-such, and in terms of dislike and denial, I am amazed by such-and-such. “And God is witness to what is in his heart,” meaning the hypocrite’s saying, By God, I believe in you and love you. He is the most quarrelsome, meaning the most fierce of opponents. It is said, You are stubborn, O man, and you are stubborn and stubborn. If you mean that he has overcome his opponent, you say, He gives birth to him, stubborn. It is said: a man is stubborn and a woman. A disease and a stubborn people, God Almighty said: And warn with it a stubborn people 97-Maryam. Al-Zajjaj said: Its derivation is from the two sides of the neck, and its interpretation is: that in the face he took from the right or left in the doors of the dispute, he prevailed, and the dispute is the source of his dispute with him, a dispute and a dispute, said Abu Ubaidah. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the plural of opponent, it is said: opponent, dispute, and opponents like sea, seas, and seas. Al-Hasan said: The stubborn dispute means lying in speech, Qatada said: Very harsh in disobedience, arguing with falsehood, speaking with wisdom and doing sin. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The most hated of men to God Almighty is the persistent quarrelsome one.
2:205: 205. And if he turns away meaning he turns away and turns away from you he strives in the land meaning he works in it, and it was said: he walked in it and walked to corrupt it Ibn Jurayj said: he severed the ties of kinship and shed the blood of Muslims and destroy the crops and the offspring This is because Al-Akhns had a dispute with Thaqeef, so he attacked them at night and burned their crops and destroyed their livestock. Muqatil said: He went to Taif to recover money from a creditor, so he burned a pile of money for him and hamstrung a female donkey for him. The offspring is the offspring of every animal, including people. Ad-Dahhak said: And when he takes over meaning he takes over the matter and becomes a governor. He strives throughout the land. Mujahid said: In the words of God Almighty: And when he takes over, he strives throughout the land he said: If he takes over and acts with aggression and injustice, God will withhold the rain and destroy the crops and the offspring. And God does not love corruption meaning He is not pleased with corruption. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Cutting off the dirham is a form of corruption on earth.
2:206: 206. His saying, And when it is said to him, ‘Fear God,’ meaning, fear God, “pride in sin takes hold of him,” meaning, pride and the zeal of ignorance drive him to commit sin, meaning, injustice. Pride means arrogance and invincibility. It was said that its meaning is, pride takes hold of him for the sin in his heart, so he used the ba’ in place of the lam. His saying, Hell is sufficient for him, meaning sufficient, and what an evil resting place, meaning a bed. Abdullah bin Masoud said: One of the greatest sins before God is for a servant to be told, Fear God, and he says, Take care of yourself. It was narrated that Omar bin Al-Khattab was told: Fear God, so he placed his cheek on the ground in humility to God Almighty.
2:207: 207. God the Almighty said: And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. That is, to seek the pleasure of God the Almighty. And God is Kind to His servants. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak that this verse was revealed regarding the expedition of Ar-Raji’. That is, the infidels of Quraysh sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Medina: We have become Muslims, so send to us a group of scholars from your companions to teach us your religion. This was a plot on their part, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khubayb ibn ‘Adi Al-Ansari, Murthad ibn Abi Murthad Al-Ghanawi, Khalid ibn Bakir, ‘Abdullah ibn Tariq ibn Shihab Al-Balawi, and Zaid ibn Ad-Dathna, and he put Asim ibn Thabit ibn Abi Al-Aflah Al-Ansari in charge of them. Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent ten spies and put Asim ibn Thabit Al-Ansari in charge of them. They set out and camped in the valley of Mecca and Medina, and with them were Ajwa dates, so they ate. An old woman passed by and saw the date pits, so she returned to her people in Mecca and said: The people of Yathrib from the companions of the Prophet have taken this road. Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode out seventy men, some of whom had spears, until they surrounded them. Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said: They mentioned a tribe of Hudhayl called Banu Lihyan, so they sent out nearly a hundred archers to them. They followed their tracks until they found their food, dates, in a place where they had stopped. They said: Dates of Yathrib. So they followed their tracks. When Asim and his companions sensed them, they took refuge in Fadfad. The people surrounded them and killed Murthad, Khalid, and Abdullah bin Tariq. Asim bin Thabit scattered his quiver, which contained seven arrows, and with each arrow he killed a prominent polytheist. Then he said: O God, I have protected Your religion at the beginning of the day, so cut my flesh at the end of the day. Then the polytheists surrounded him and killed him. When they killed him, they wanted to cut off his head to sell it to Salafah bint Sa`d bin Shahid. She had vowed when her son was killed on the Day of Uhud that if she could get hold of Asim’s head, she would pour wine into his skull. So God sent a man from the wasps, which are hornets, and it burned. Asim was not able to catch him, so he was called the fever of the anus. They said, Leave him until evening, so that he may go away, and we may seize him. Then a black cloud came and rained down rain like the rain of Uzali. Then God sent a stream into the valley, and Asim was carried away by it and went with him to Paradise, and fifty of the polytheists were carried to Hell. Asim had given God Almighty a covenant that no polytheist would touch him, and he would never touch another polytheist. Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to say when he heard that the wasp had prevented him, “It is amazing that God protects the believer. Asim had vowed that no polytheist would touch him and that no polytheist would ever touch him, so God protected him after his death, just as Asim had protected himself during his life.” The polytheists took Khubayb ibn Adi al-Ansari and Zurayd ibn al-Dathna prisoner and took them to Mecca. As for Khubayb, the sons of al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf bought him to kill him for their father. Khubayb was the one who killed al-Harith on the day of Badr. Khubayb remained with them as a prisoner until they decided to kill him. Then he borrowed a razor from al-Harith’s daughters to sharpen his teeth with, and she lent it to him. He went to her while she was unaware. The woman was not surprised when Khubayb sat the boy on his thigh with the razor in his hand. The woman cried out, and Khubayb said: Are you afraid that I will kill him? I would not have done that, for treachery is not our business. The woman then said: By God, I have never seen a prisoner better than Khubayb. By God, I found him one day eating a bunch of grapes in his hand, and he was bound with iron. There was no fruit in Mecca, but it was only provisions that God had provided for Khubayb. Then they went out of the sanctuary to kill him outside the sanctuary, and they wanted to crucify him. Khubayb said to them: Let me pray two rak’ahs. So they left him. Khubayb was the first to establish the prayer for every Muslim who was killed patiently. He prayed two rak’ahs, then he said: If it were not for their thinking that what I have is impatience, I would have increased. O God, count them in number and kill them one by one and do not leave a single one of them. Then he began to say: I do not care when I kill a Muslim, for whatever reason I die in the cause of God. This is in the essence of God, and if He wills, He will bless the limbs of a torn limb. They crucified him alive, and he said, O God, You know that there is no one around me who can convey my greetings to Your Messenger, so convey my greetings to him. Then Abu Suru’a Uqba ibn al-Harith rose up and killed him. It is said: There was a man from the polytheists called Salaman, Abu Maysarah, who had a spear with him and placed it between the breasts of Khubayb. Khubayb said to him, Fear God, but that only increased his rebellion. So he stabbed him and pierced him. This is what God Almighty said: And when it is said to him, ‘Fear God,’ pride in sin seizes him. He means Salaman. As for Zayd ibn al-Dathna, Safwan ibn Umayya bought him to kill him for his father, Umayya ibn Khalaf. So he sent him with a freedman of his called Nastas to al-Tan’im to kill him for his father. A group of Quraysh gathered, among them Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. When Abu Sufyan came to be killed, he said to him, I ask you by God, O Zayd, would you like Muhammad to be with us now in your place so that we could strike off his head and you could be with your family? He said, “By God, I would not like Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be in the place he is in now and be hurt by a thorn while I am sitting with my family.” Abu Sufyan said, I have never seen anyone among the people who loves anyone as much as the companions of Muhammad love Muhammad. Then Nastas killed him. When this report reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said to his companions, Which of you will bring Khubayb down from his wood and he will be granted Paradise? Az-Zubayr said, I will, O Messenger of God, and my companion Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad. So they went out, walking at night and lying in ambush during the day until they reached At-Tan’im at night. There were forty polytheists sleeping and drunk around the wood. They brought him down and he was moist and wet, and nothing had changed in him after forty days. His hand was over his wound and it was oozing with blood, the color of blood and the smell of musk. Az-Zubayr carried him on his horse and they set off. The infidels woke up and found that they had lost Khubayb, so they informed the Quraysh, and seventy of them rode on. When they caught up with them, Az-Zubayr threw Khubayb and the earth swallowed him, so he was called the Bali’ Al-Ard. Then Al-Zubayr said: What has made you so bold against us, O people of Quraysh? Then he lifted the turban from his head and said: I am Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam, and my mother is Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib, and my companion Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad is two lions lying down defending their cubs. If you wish, I will fight you, and if you wish, I will fight you, and if you wish, you can turn back. So, support them and go to Mecca. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Gabriel was with him. He said: O Muhammad, the angels are boasting about these two of your companions. Then the verse was revealed about Al-Zubayr and Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad: And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God when they sold themselves to bring Khubayb down from his cross. Most of the commentators said: It was revealed about Suhaib bin Sinan Al-Rumi when the polytheists took him with a group of believers and tortured them. Suhaib said to them: I am an old man and it does not harm you whether I am from your security or not. So would you like to take my money and leave me and my religion? So they did, and he stipulated that they should provide a mount and provide for me. He stayed in Mecca as God willed, then he went out to Medina and Abu Bakr and Umar met him with some men. Abu Bakr said to him: Your sale is profitable, O Abu Yahya. Suhaib said to him: And your sale, so do not be sad. Suhaib said: What is that? He said: God has revealed about you, and he recited this verse to him. Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab and `Ata` said: Suhaib came as an immigrant towards the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and a group of the polytheists of Quraysh followed him. He got down from his mount and threw away what was in his quiver, then said: O people of Quraysh, you know that I am one of the men who shoot at you. By God, I will not place an arrow from my quiver except in the heart of one of you. By God, you will not reach me until I have thrown away every arrow in my quiver, then I will strike with my sword what is left in my hand, then do what you wish. If you wish, I will show you my wealth in Mecca and you will let me go. They said: Yes. So he did that, and God revealed this verse. Al-Hasan said: Do you know about whom this verse was revealed? It was revealed about a Muslim who would meet an unbeliever and say to him, Say, ‘There is no god but God,’ but he would refuse to say it. So the Muslim said, By God, I will sacrifice myself for God. So he went forward and fought alone until he was killed. It was said that the verse was revealed about enjoining good and forbidding evil. Ibn Abbas said: I see someone who sells himself seeking the pleasure of God. He stands up and orders this person to fear God. If he does not accept and is overcome by pride in sin, he says: I sell myself for God. Fight him. The two men fought for this reason. When Ali would recite this verse, he would say: They fought, by the Lord of the Kaaba. Umar ibn al-Khattab heard a man reciting this: And among the people is he who sells himself seeking the pleasure of God. Umar said: To God we belong and to Him we shall return. A man stood up to enjoin good and forbid evil and was killed. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Shureih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Hammad bin Salamah told me, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, that a man said: O Messenger of God, which jihad is best? He said: The best jihad is to say a word of truth in the presence of an unjust ruler.
2:208: 208- The Almighty said: “O you who have believed, enter into peace completely.” The people of Hijaz and Al-Kisa’i read “peace” here with a fatha on the seen, and the rest read it with a kasra. In Surat Al-Anfal, “And if they incline to peace” with a kasra, and Abu Bakr and the rest read it with a fatha, and in Surat Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a kasra, Hamza and Abu Bakr. This verse was revealed about the believers among the People of the Book, Abdullah bin Salam Al-Nadhairi and his companions. They used to venerate the Sabbath and dislike camel meat and milk after they converted to Islam. They said: O Messenger of God, the Torah is the Book of God, so leave us and let us perform it in our night prayers. Then God Almighty revealed: “O you who have believed, enter into peace completely.” That is, into Islam. Mujahid said in the rulings of the people of Islam and their deeds: completely. That is, all of them. It was said: Enter Islam to the end of its laws, refraining from going beyond it to anything else. The origin of peace is submission and obedience, and that is why peace is called “peace.” Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman said about this verse: Islam is eight arrows, so count the prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, Umrah, jihad, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. He said: He who has no arrow has failed. And do not follow the footsteps of Satan, meaning his traces in what he has made attractive to you of prohibiting the Sabbath, camel meat, and other things. He is to you a clear enemy. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Tahhan told us, Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Quraysh told us, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Makki told us, Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam told us, Hisham told us, Mujalid told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abd God, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when Umar came to him and said, “We hear hadiths from the Jews and we are amazed. Do you think we should write some of them down?” He said, “Are you deluded as the Jews and Christians were deluded? I have come to you with them pure and white. If Moses were alive, he would have no choice but to follow me.”
2:209: 209. If you slip means you go astray, and it was said: you deviated, it is said that his foot slipped, slipping, if it was pushed aside, Ibn Abbas said: He means polytheism, Qatada said: God knows that people will slip, so He advanced in that and threatened in it so that He would have an argument against them, after the clear proofs have come to you meaning the clear evidence, then know that God is Exalted in Might in His punishment, Wise in His command, so the Exalted is the Victorious One who does not miss anything, and the Wise is the One who is correct in the matter.
2:210: 210. God the Almighty said: Do they wait? That is, do those who abandon entering into peace and follow the footsteps of Satan wait? It is said: I looked at him and waited for him with one meaning. So if the look is coupled with the remembrance of God or the remembrance of the face or to, it is only in the meaning of seeing. Unless God comes to them in shades is the plural of shade from the clouds which is the thin white cloud. It was called a cloud because it covers, that is, it conceals. Mujahid said: It is not a cloud, and it was only for the Children of Israel in their wandering. Muqatil said: Like the appearance of white fog. Al-Hasan said: In a veil of clouds so the people of the earth do not see [it]. And the angels Abu Ja`far read in the accusative case in apposition to the clouds, meaning: with the angels. The Arabs say: The prince came with the army, meaning with the camp. The rest read in the nominative case meaning: unless God and the angels come to them in shades of clouds. The first thing in this verse and what is similar to it is for a person to believe in its outward meaning and entrust its knowledge to God the Almighty, and to believe that God, the Exalted in His name, is free from the characteristics of an event. This is how it has been. Imams of the ships and scholars of the Sunnah. Al-Kalbi said: This is the hidden that is not explained. Makhul, Al-Zuhri, Al-Awza’i, Malik, Ibn Al-Mubarak, Sufyan Al-Thawri, Al-Layth Ibn Sa’d, Ahmad, and Ishaq used to say about it and similar things: Leave it as it came without asking how. Sufyan Ibn Uyaynah said: Everything that God described Himself with in His Book, its explanation is reading it and keeping silent about it. No one has the right to explain it except God Almighty and His Messenger. The Almighty said: And the matter has been decided. That is, the punishment has become obligatory, and the reckoning has been completed. This is God’s decision to judge with justice among creation on the Day of Resurrection. And to God all matters will return. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read it with a fatha on the ta’ and a kasra on the jim. The rest read it with a damma on the ta’ and a fatha on the jim.
2:211: 211. The Almighty said: Ask the Children of Israel meaning, O Muhammad, ask the Jews of Medina how many clear signs We gave them We gave their fathers and ancestors of a clear sign clear evidence of the prophethood of Moses, peace be upon him, such as the staff, the white hand, the splitting of the sea, and others. It was said: Its meaning is the evidence that was given to them in the Torah and the Gospel regarding the prophethood of Muhammad, peace be upon him. And whoever changes alters the favor of God the Book of God, and it was said: the covenant of God, and it was said: whoever denies the evidence of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after it has come to him, then indeed, God is severe in penalty.
2:212: 212. The life of this world has been made fair-seeming to those who disbelieve. Most of them agree that the one who makes it fair is God Almighty, and the making it fair-seeming from God Almighty is that He created beautiful things and wondrous sights, so the creation looked at them more than they deserved, so they were amazed by them and were tempted by them. Al-Zajjaj said: Satan made it fair-seeming to them. It was said that this verse was revealed about the polytheists of the Arabs, Abu Jahl and his companions, who were enjoying the wealth God had provided them in this world and denying the afterlife. And they mocked those who believed, meaning they mocked the poor believers. Ibn Abbas said: He meant by those who believed Abdullah bin Masoud, Ammar bin Yasir, Suhaib, Bilal, Khabab and their likes. Muqatil said: It was revealed about the hypocrites Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions. They enjoyed life in this world and mocked the weak believers and the poor immigrants and said: Look at these people whom Muhammad claims he can defeat. Ata’ said: It was revealed about the Jewish leaders of Banu Qurayzah, Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa’. They mocked the poor immigrants, so God promised them that He would give them the wealth of Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir without fighting. And they mock those who believed because of their poverty. And those who feared God meaning these poor people are above them on the Day of Resurrection because they are in the highest of highs while they are in the lowest of lows. Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzaz told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq Al-Dabry told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I stood at the gate of Paradise and saw that most of its people were the poor. I stood at the gate of Hell and saw that most of its people were women. The wealthy were detained, except for those among them who were from the people of Hell, and they were ordered to Hell.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Mulikhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sahl bin Saad Al-Saidi, that he said: “A man passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to a man sitting with him, ‘What do you think of this man?’ He said, ‘A man from the nobles of the people. By God, if he proposes marriage, he is deserving of being accepted, and if he intercedes, his intercession is accepted.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent. Then another man passed by and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘What do you think of this man?’ He said, ‘O Messenger of God, this man is from the poor Muslims. If he proposes marriage, he is deserving of not being accepted, and if he intercedes, his intercession is not accepted, and if he speaks, his words are not listened to.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘This man is better than the earth being filled with the likes of this man.’” And God provides for whom He wills without account. Ibn Abbas said: It means abundantly without measure, because everything that is subject to account is little. He sees: He gives abundantly to whom He wills and expands for whom He wills of His servants. Ad-Dahhak said: It means without any accountability. He provides for him in this world and does not hold him accountable in the Hereafter. It was said: This refers to God the Most High, meaning: He is stingy with whom He wills and expands for whom He wills. He does not give everyone according to his need, rather He gives abundantly to those who do not need it and does not give little to those who need it. So no one objects to Him, and He is not held accountable for what He provides, and it is not said: Why did You give this and deprive that? Why did You give this more than you gave that? It was said that it means that He does not fear that His treasuries will run out, so He does not need to account for what comes out of them, because accounting from the giver is only for those who fear that their treasuries will run out.
2:213: 213. The Almighty said: Mankind was one nation on one religion. Mujahid said: He meant Adam alone, he was one nation. He said: The one was called by the plural form because it is the origin of the lineage and the father of mankind. Then God created Eve and spread from her the people and they spread out and were Muslims until Cain killed Abel and they differed. Then God sent the prophets. Al-Hasan and Ata' said: The people from the time of Adam's death until the mission of Noah were one nation on the religion of disbelief like animals, so God sent Noah and other prophets. Qatada and Ikrimah said: The people were from the time of Adam until the mission of Noah and there were ten centuries between them, all of them on one law of truth and guidance, then they differed in the time of Noah so God sent Noah to them, so he was the first prophet sent, then after him He sent the prophets. Al-Kalbi said: They are the people of Noah’s Ark. They were believers, then they differed after Noah’s death. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: People at the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, were one nation, all of them infidels, then God sent Abraham and other prophets. It was said: The Arabs followed the religion of Abraham until Amr ibn Luhay changed it. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah on the authority of Abu Kaab who said: When people were presented to Adam, and were brought out from his back and acknowledged servitude, they were one nation, all Muslims, and they were never one nation except on that day, then they differed after Adam, as is mentioned in Surat Yunus 10:And mankind were but one nation, then they differed “So God sent the prophets” 19-Yunus and their total was one hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand and the messengers among them were three hundred and thirteen, and those mentioned in the Qur’an with the Book of Knowledge are twenty-eight prophets bringing good tidings of reward for those who believe and obey and warning warning of punishment for those who disbelieve and disobey and He sent down with them the Book meaning the Books, meaning and He sent down with each one of them the Book with the truth with justice and honesty to judge between people Abu Ja`far read to judge with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the kaf here and at the beginning of Al Imran and in An-Nur in two places because the Book does not judge in reality, but rather the judgment is by it, and the reading of the general public is with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the kaf, meaning for the Book to judge, its mention On the breadth of speech, as God Almighty says: This is Our Book that speaks to you with the truth (al-Jathiyah 45:29). It was said that its meaning is that each prophet should judge by his book in what they differed over. And there was no difference in it, meaning in the Book, except for those who were given it meaning they were given the Book after the clear proofs had come to them, meaning the rulings of the Torah and the Gospel. Al-Farra’ said: Their difference has two meanings: One of them is that some of them disbelieved in the Book of others. God Almighty said: And they say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others’ 150-An-Nisa’. The other is that they distorted the Book of God. God Almighty said: They distort words from their [proper] usages 46-An-Nisa’. It was said that the verse refers to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his Book. The People of the Book differed about it after clear proofs had come to them the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their books out of envy injustice and envy “among themselves. So God guided those who believed to that over which they differed” that is, what they differed about of the truth by His permission with His knowledge and will for them. Ibn Zayd said about this verse: They differed about the direction of prayer, some of them prayed toward the east, some of them prayed toward the west, and some of them prayed toward the Holy House, so God guided us to the Kaaba. They differed about fasting, so God guided us to the month of Ramadan. They differed about the days, so the Jews took the Sabbath and the Christians took Sunday, so God guided us to Friday. They differed about Abraham, peace be upon him, so the Jews said he was a Jew, and the Christians said he was a Christian, so God guided us to the truth about that. They differed about Jesus, so the Jews made him a slander and the Christians made him a god, so God guided us to the truth about him. And God guides whom He wills to a straight path.
2:214: 214. The Almighty’s saying: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise? Qatada and Al-Suddi said: This verse was revealed during the Battle of the Trench when the Muslims were afflicted with hardship, intense fear, cold, hardship, and various types of harm, as God Almighty said: And hearts will reach the throats 10-Al-Ahzab. It was also said that it was revealed during the Battle of Uhud. Ata’ said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions entered Medina, the hardship became severe for them, because they left without money and left their homes and wealth in the hands of the polytheists and preferred to please God and His Messenger. The Jews showed enmity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some people concealed their hypocrisy, so God Almighty revealed to soothe their hearts: Or did you think? meaning: Did you think? The mim is a connective, as Al-Farra’ said. Al-Zajjaj said: Rather, you thought. The meaning of the verse: Did you think, O believers, that you would enter Paradise? And there has not yet come to you “And what is the connective of” The likeness of those who passed away “Before you” Of the prophets and believers “Poverty” poverty, hardship and calamity “and distress” sickness and time “and they were shaken” meaning they were stirred by various kinds of calamities and misfortunes and were frightened “until the Messenger and those who believed with him said: When will God’s victory come?” The calamity continued to befall them until they were impatient for victory. God Almighty said: Indeed, the victory of God is near. Nafi’ read until the Messenger says in the nominative case, meaning until the Messenger said. If the verb that follows until has the meaning of the past and its wording is the wording of the future, then you have two options: nominative and accusative. The accusative is according to the apparent meaning of the statement, because until puts the future verb in the accusative case, and the nominative case is because its meaning is the past, and until does not work in the past. The Almighty’s saying: They ask you, what they should spend was revealed about Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who was a very old man with wealth. He said: O Messenger of God, what should we give in charity and to whom should we spend?
2:215: 215. The Almighty’s saying: They ask you, what they should spend. It was revealed about Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who was an old man with wealth. He said, O Messenger of God, what should we give in charity and to whom should we spend it? So God the Almighty revealed: They ask you, what should we spend? In His saying what there are two ways of parsing, one of them is that it is in the accusative case with His saying they spend, meaning what do they spend? The other is that it is in the nominative case with what, meaning what do they spend? Say, ‘Whatever you spend of good’ meaning of wealth “is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer. And whatever good you do, indeed, God is Knowing of it.” He will reward you for it. The commentators said: This was before the zakat was made obligatory, then it was abrogated by zakat.
2:216: 216. The Almighty’s saying: Fighting is prescribed for you means jihad is obligatory upon you. The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse. Ata’ said: Jihad is voluntary, and what is meant by the verse is the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one else. Al-Thawri agreed with this, and those who agreed with this supported the Almighty’s saying: “God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home, by a degree. And to all God has promised goodness” 95-An-Nisa. If the one who sits away had abandoned an obligation, there would be no goodness after it. Some of them followed the apparent meaning of the verse, and said: Jihad is obligatory upon all Muslims until the Day of Resurrection. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi Al-Khwarizmi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Amr Ahmad bin Abi Al-Furati told us, Abu Al-Haitham bin Kulayb told us, Ahmad bin Hazim bin Abi Gharzah told us, Saeed bin Othman Al-Saeedi told us, on the authority of Omar bin Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Sami, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever dies without having fought or having thought of fighting, dies in a state of hypocrisy. Some people said, and the majority agree: Jihad is a communal obligation. If some people perform it, then the rest are exempt from it, such as the funeral prayer and returning the greeting. Al-Zuhri and Al-Awza’i said: God has prescribed jihad for the people, whether they fight or stay behind. Whoever fights in it, he will be fine, and whoever stays behind, he is a provision. If he is called upon to help, he will help. If he is called upon to mobilize, he will go forth. If he is not in need of someone, he will stay behind. God the Almighty said: And it is hateful to you meaning, it is difficult for you. Some of the scholars of meaning said: This dislike is due to the nature’s aversion to it because of what is in it, of financial burden, hardship of the soul, and danger to the spirit, not that they disliked the command of God the Almighty. Ikrimah said: It was abrogated by God the Almighty’s saying: We hear and we obey meaning that they disliked it then loved it and said, We hear and we obey. God the Almighty said: And perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you because in war there is one of two good things: either victory and booty or martyrdom and Paradise. And perhaps you like a thing meaning sitting back from war and it is bad for you because of what is in it of missing out on booty and reward. And God knows while you do not know.
2:217: 217. God the Almighty said: They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein. The reason for the revelation of this verse is that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abdullah bin Jahsh, who was the cousin of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his father’s sister, in Jumada al-Akhira, two months before the Battle of Badr, seventeen months after his arrival in Medina. He sent with him eight men from the Muhajireen: Sa`d bin Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri, `Ukasha bin Mahmas al-Asadi, `Utbah bin Ghazwan al-Sulami, Abu Hudhayfah bin `Utbah bin Rabi`ah, Suhayl bin Bayda, `Amir bin Rabi`ah, Waqid bin Abdullah, and Khalid bin Bakir. He wrote a letter to their leader, Abdullah bin Jahsh, and said to him: “Go in the name of God and do not look into the letter until you have traveled for two days. When you arrive, open the letter and read it to your companions, then proceed as I have commanded you, and do not compel any of your companions to travel with you.” So Abdullah walked for two days, then he arrived and opened the letter, and in it was: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Now then: Go with the blessing of God with those of your companions who are with you until you arrive at Batn Nakhl and watch. He said: There is a caravan of Quraysh in it, perhaps you will bring us report from it. When he looked at the letter, he said: I hear and obey. Then he said that to his companions, and he said: He forbade me from forcing any of you, so whoever wants to bear witness, let him go and whoever does not want to, let him return. Then he went and his companions went with him, and none of them stayed behind until he was at a mine above the branch in a place in the Hijaz called Bahran. Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas and `Utbah ibn Ghazwan lost a camel of theirs to follow, so they stayed behind in pursuit of it, and he went with the rest of his companions until they camped at Batn Nakhal between Mecca and Taif. While they were like that, a caravan of Quraysh passed by carrying raisins, fat, merchandise, and Taif. Among them were Amr ibn al-Hadrami, al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, the freedman of Hisham ibn al-Mughira, Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, and his brother Nawfal ibn Abdullah al-Makhzumi. When they saw the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they feared them. Abdullah ibn Jahsh said: The people are terrified of you, so shave the head of one of you and let him attack them. So they shaved the head of Ukasha. Then he looked down on them and they said: The people of Ammar, there is no harm upon you. So give them security. That was on the last day of Jumada al-Akhira. They thought that it was Jumada, which is Rajab. The people consulted and said: If you leave them alone tonight, they will enter the sanctuary and protect themselves from you. So they decided to engage the people. Waqid ibn Abdullah al-Sahmi shot Amr ibn al-Hadrami with an arrow and killed him. He was the first of the polytheists to be killed. [He was the first to be killed in the migration. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, paid the blood money of Ibn al-Hadrami to his heirs from Quraish. Mujahid and others said that there was a covenant between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Quraish, and he claimed to the people of Mecca for years that he would not fight them and they would not fight him. Al-Hakam and Uthman were taken prisoner, and they were the first prisoners in Islam. Nawfal escaped and defeated them. The believers drove the caravan and the prisoners until they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina. The Quraysh said: Muhammad has made the sacred month permissible, so he shed blood and took captives. The people of Mecca were mocked for that, and those Muslims who were in it, and they said: O group of young men, you have made the sacred month permissible and fought in it! This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said to Ibn Jahsh and his companions: I did not command you to fight in the sacred month, and to stop the caravan and the two prisoners, and he refused to take anything of that, so this was difficult for the companions of the expedition, and they thought that they had perished and their hands had fallen, and they said: O Messenger of God, we killed Ibn al-Hadrami, then evening came and we looked at the crescent of Rajab, and we do not know whether we killed him in Rajab or in Jumada? And most of the people were like that, so God Almighty revealed this verse, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the caravan and separated a fifth from it, so it was the first fifth in Islam, and he divided the rest among the companions of the expedition, and it was the first spoils in Islam. He sent the people of Mecca to ransom their captives, so he said, Rather, we will stop them until Saad and Uqbah come, and if they do not come, we will kill them in exchange for them. So when they came, he ransomed them. As for Al-Hakam bin Kaysan, he converted to Islam and stayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, so he was killed as a martyr on the day of Bir Ma’unah. As for Uthman bin Abdullah, he returned to Mecca and died there as an unbeliever. As for Nawfal, he struck the belly of his horse on the day of the Confederates to enter the trench, so he fell into the trench with his horse and they were both crushed, so God killed him. The polytheists demanded his corpse as a price, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Take him, for he is a filthy corpse and a filthy blood money. This is the reason for the revelation of this verse. God Almighty says: They ask you about the sacred month, meaning Rajab, which was named thus because fighting is forbidden in it. Fighting in it means about fighting in it. Say “O Muhammad, Fighting in it is great great. The speech was completed here, then he began and said, And averted from the path of God meaning your averting the Muslims from Islam. And disbelieved in it meaning your disbelief in God. And the Sacred Mosque meaning the Sacred Mosque. It was said that your averting from the Sacred Mosque and expelling its people meaning expelling the people of the mosque from it is greater and greater in sin in the sight of God. And the trial” meaning the polytheism that you are upon is greater than killing meaning the killing of Ibn al-Hadrami in the sacred month. So when this verse was revealed, Abdullah bin Unays wrote to the believers in Mecca, “If the polytheists taunt you for fighting in the sacred month, then taunt them for disbelief and for expelling the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca and preventing the Muslims from the Sacred House.” Then he said, And they will not cease meaning the polytheists of Mecca, and it is a verb without a source like what may “fight you” O group of believers until they turn you back “turn you away” from your religion if they are able. And whoever among you turns back from his religion He died as a disbeliever, and those are the ones whose good deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally.” The companions of the expedition said, O Messenger of God, will we be rewarded for this journey of ours, and do we hope that this journey of ours will be a conquest?
2:218: 218.
