Then God Almighty revealed, Indeed, those who believed and those who emigrated left their clans and their homes and their wealth and fought against the polytheists in the cause of God in obedience to God, so He made it a jihad, those are the ones who hope for the mercy of God He informed that they are hoping for mercy and God is Forgiving and Merciful.
2:219: 219. The Almighty said: They ask you about wine and gambling the verse, was revealed about Omar bin Al-Khattab and Muadh bin Jabal, may God be pleased with them, and a group of the Ansar who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, give us a ruling on wine, give us a ruling on wine and gambling, for they are mind-boggling and waste of money? So God revealed this verse. The summary of what the commentators said about the prohibition of alcohol is that God Almighty revealed four verses about alcohol that were revealed in Mecca, which are: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision 67-An-Nahl. The Muslims used to drink it and it was permissible for them at that time. Then it was revealed regarding the question of Omar and Muadh bin Jabal: “They ask you about alcohol and gambling. Say, “In them is great sin.” When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has already forbidden alcohol. Some people left it because of His saying, Great sin, and some people drank it because of His saying, And for benefits for people. Until Abd al-Rahman bin Awf made a pilgrimage and invited some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and brought them alcohol. They drank and became drunk. The Maghrib prayer came, so they brought some of them forward to lead them in prayer. He recited, “Say, ‘O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship. ’” This is how it was until the end of the surah, deleting la. Then God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are “Drunken until you know what you are saying 43-An-Nisa So he forbade drunkenness during the times of prayer and they drank it at times other than the time of prayer, until a man would drink after the evening prayer and wake up and his drunkenness would go away, and he would drink after the dawn prayer and he would wake up when the time for noon came. Utbah ibn Malik made a ploy and invited some Muslim men, among them Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, who had roasted a camel’s head for them, so they ate from it and drank wine until it was taken from them. Then they boasted about that and claimed affiliation and recited poetry. Sa`d recited a poem in which he satirized the Ansar and boasted about his people, so a man from the Ansar took the camel’s jawbone and struck Sa`d’s head with it, wounding him in a clear wound. Sa`d went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and complained to him about the Ansari. Umar said: O God, explain to us Your opinion on wine in a clear statement. Then God Almighty revealed the prohibition of wine in Surat Al-Ma’idah until His saying: Will you then desist? This was a few days after the Battle of the Confederates, so Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: We have finished, O Lord. Anas said: Wine was forbidden, and at that time the Arabs had no life more wonderful than it, and nothing was forbidden to them more severe than wine. On the authority of Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, he said: When the verse was revealed in Surat Al-Ma’idah prohibiting alcohol, we went out with the jugs to the road and poured out what was in them. Some of us broke what we poured out and some of us washed it with water and mud. The alleys of the city were deserted for a while after that, and when it rained, the color of the alcohol became apparent in them and its smell spread. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Abdul Aziz bin Suhaib told us: Anas bin Malik said to me, We had no wine except to disgrace you. I was standing giving Abu Talha, so-and-so, and so-and-so a drink when a man came and said, Wine has been forbidden. They said, Pour out these jugs, Anas. They did not ask about them or return to them after the man’s story. On the authority of Anas: It was called wine because they used to leave it in the jars until it fermented and changed. On the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab: Because it was left until its essence became clear and its turbidity settled. The jurists differed about the nature of wine. Some people said: It is the juice of grapes or dates that has become strong and boiling without the action of fire on it. The imams agreed that this wine is impure and its drinker is punished and he is sinful and an infidel who permits it. Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa and a group held that the prohibition does not extend beyond this and that what is made from other than them is not prohibited, such as what is made from wheat, barley, corn, honey and vanilla, unless it causes intoxication, in which case it is prohibited. They said that if grape juice or dates is cooked until half of it is gone, it is permissible, but it is disliked. If it is cooked until two-thirds of it is gone, they said that it is permissible to drink it, except that intoxication from it is forbidden. They cite as evidence what was narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, wrote to some of his workers to provide the Muslims with the paint that two-thirds of it is gone and one-third remains. Abu Ubaidah and Muadh saw the paint being drunk on a third. Some people said: If the juice is cooked to the minimum level, it becomes permissible. This is the opinion of Ismail bin Aliyah. Most scholars have said that any drink that intoxicates in large quantities is alcohol, and a small amount of it is forbidden and its drinker must be punished. They cited as evidence what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Musab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the intoxicant, and he said: Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden. Abu Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Bakr bin Abi Al-Furat, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whatever intoxicates in large quantities, a small amount of it is forbidden. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad Al-Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Al-Rabi Al-Atki told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Ayoub bin Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every intoxicant is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks wine in this world and dies while addicted to it and does not repent will not drink it in the Hereafter.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmad bin Abi Raja’ told us, Yahya, on the authority of Abu Hayyan Al-Taimi, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: Umar delivered a sermon from the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: The prohibition of wine has been revealed, and it is made from five things: grapes, dates, wheat, barley, and honey. Wine is that which intoxicates the mind.” Al-Sha’bi narrated on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is wine from grapes, there is wine from dates, there is wine from honey, there is wine from wheat, and there is wine from barley. So it is proven that wine is not limited to what is made from grapes or dates. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Musab told us, Malik told us, Ibn Shihab told us, al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid told us that Umar ibn al-Khattab came out to them and said, I found the smell of alcohol on so-and-so, and he claimed that he drank lacquer. “I am asking about what he drank. If it intoxicates, I will flog him.” So Umar flogged him completely. What was narrated from Umar, Abu Ubaidah, and Muadh about lacquer is cooking until it is no longer intoxicating. Ibn Abbas was asked about the one who spits liquor, and he said, Muhammad preceded, so whatever intoxicates is forbidden. God the Almighty said: And gambling means betting. Ibn Abbas said: In the pre-Islamic era, a man would bet on his family and his money. Whichever of them gambled, the other would take his family and his money. So God the Almighty revealed this verse. Maysir is a verbal noun from their saying something was made easy for me if it was made easy, easy and easy. Then gambling was called Maysir and the gambler was called Yasir and Yasir. The origin of Maysir was in camels, and that was because the wealthy Arabs would buy camels, slaughter them, and divide them into ten parts. Then they would draw lots on them with ten arrows called Azlam and Al-Aqlam. Seven of them had shares: Al-Fadh, which had one share; Al-Tawam, which had two shares; Al-Raqeeb, which had three shares; Al-Halas, which had four shares; Al-Nafis, which had five; Al-Musabil, which had six shares; Al-Mu’alla, which had seven shares. Three of them had no shares, and they were Al-Munih, Al-Safeh, and Al-Waghd. Then they would put the lots in a map called Al-Rababa and place it in the hands of a just man among them called Al-Mujail and Al-Nafidh. Then he would draw lots and take out a goblet. From it in the name of one of them, so whoever’s share came out took his share according to what came out, and if one of the three who had no shares came out for him, he would take something and pay the entire price of the roots. Some of them said that he would not take anything and would not pay, and that the coin would be useless, then they would give that root to the poor and not eat anything from it. They would be proud of that and criticize whoever did not do that, and they would call it al-Barm, which is the origin of gambling that the Arabs used to do. What is meant by the verse is all types of gambling. Tawus, Ata’, and Mujahid said: Everything in which there is gambling is from gambling, even children playing with nuts and cubes. It was narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him, that dice and chess are from gambling. God the Almighty says: “Say: ‘There is a great sin in them’” A great burden of quarreling, insulting and saying obscene words. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read a great sin with a triple tha’, while the rest read it with a ba’. The sin in wine and gambling is what God mentioned in Surat al-Ma’idah 5:“Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through wine and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?” 91-Al-Ma’idah And benefits for people The benefit of wine is the pleasure of drinking it, joy, and the enjoyment of food and the profit they make from trading in it. The benefit of gambling is gaining money without toil or fatigue and the poor benefiting from it. The sin in it is that if a person’s money is lost without compensation, that upsets him so he becomes hostile to his friend and intends to harm him. And their sin is greater than their benefit. Ad-Dahhak and others said: Their sin after the prohibition is greater than their benefit before the prohibition. It was also said: Their sin is greater than their benefit before the prohibition, which is what results from enmity and hatred. God Almighty says: And they ask you, what they should spend. This is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged them to give charity, so they said, What should we spend? He said, Say, ‘Al-‘Afwa.’ Abu Amr read al-‘Afwa in the nominative case, meaning: what they spend is al-‘Afwa. The others read it in the accusative case, meaning, Say, ‘Spend al-‘Afwa.’ They differed on the meaning of pardon. Qatada, Ata’ and Al-Suddi said: It is what is in excess of need. The Companions used to earn money and keep to the amount needed for spending and give the excess in charity according to the ruling of this verse. Then it was abrogated by the verse of Zakat. Mujahid said: Its meaning is: Giving charity from one’s surplus wealth so that one does not remain a burden on the people. Imam Abu Ali Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Qadi narrated that Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi narrated that Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Omar bin Hafs Al-Tajir narrated that Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Omar Al-Kufi narrated that Wakee’ narrated that Al-A’mash narrated that Abu Salih narrated that Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best charity is that which is given from surplus wealth, and the upper hand is better than the lower hand, and start with those under your care. Amr bin Dinar said: The middle way, without extravagance or stinginess. God Almighty said: And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy 67-Al-Furqan. Tawus said: What is easy, and forgiveness: ease in everything and from it is the saying of God Almighty Take what is easy 199-Al-A’raf, meaning what is easy from people’s morals. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad al-Khalal told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told us, al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Sa’id bin Abi Sa’id, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have a dinar. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Spend it on yourself. He said: I have another. He said: Spend it on your children. He said: I have another. He said: Spend it on your family. He said: I have another. He said: Spend it on your servant. He said: I have another. He said: You know best.” The Almighty says: Thus does God make clear to you His signs. Al-Zajjaj said: He only said thus to one person while addressing a group, because the group means the tribe, as if he said: Thus, O tribe. It was said: It is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because his address includes addressing the nation, like the Almighty’s saying: O Prophet, when you divorce women 1-At-Talaq. God Almighty says: Perhaps you will reflect.
2:220: 220. The Almighty’s saying: In this world and the Hereafter. It was said: Its meaning is that God explains to you the signs regarding spending, so that you may reflect on this world and the Hereafter, so that you may keep from your wealth what will benefit you in this worldly life and spend the rest on what will benefit you in the Hereafter. Most of the commentators said: Its meaning is as follows: God explains to you the signs regarding this world and the Hereafter, so that you may reflect on the passing of this world and its transience, so that you may lose interest in it, and on the coming of the Hereafter and its permanence, so that you may desire it. God the Almighty said: And they ask you about orphans. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: When God the Almighty said: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best Al-An’am 152 and God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly An-Nisa’ 10 were revealed, the Muslims were extremely reluctant to deal with the property of orphans, to the point that they separated the property of orphans from their own property, to the point that food would be prepared for an orphan and some of it would be left over, so they would leave it and not eat it until it spoiled. This was difficult for them, so they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God the Almighty revealed this verse: “Say: ‘Reforming their property is best. ’” That is, reforming their property without payment or taking compensation is better for you and a greater reward, because of the reward for you in that, and better for them, because of the provision of their property for them. Mujahid said: He will provide them with his own food, but he will not provide them with the food of an orphan. And if you mix with them, this is the permissibility of mixing, that is, if you share their property with them and mix it with your property in your expenses and your dwellings. And your servants and your beasts, so you take from their money in exchange for your taking care of their affairs and you reward them for what you take from their money. Then your brothers means they are your brothers, and brothers help each other and take from each other’s money in a way that is good and pleasing. And God knows the corrupter of their money from the reformer of it, meaning the one who intends by mixing with them to betray and spoil the orphan’s money and eat it unjustly, from the one who intends to reform. And if God had willed, He would have made it difficult for you meaning He would have made it difficult for you and He would not have permitted you to mix with them. Ibn Abbas said: And if God had willed, He would have made what you take from the orphans’ money a disaster for you. The root of ‘anat is severity and hardship. Its meaning is: He charged you with everything that is difficult for you. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and the Exalted is the one who commands with might - making it easy for the servants or making it difficult for them. Wise in what He did of His management and leaving the hardship.
2:221: 221. The Almighty said: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. The reason for the revelation of this verse is that Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi was sent by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Mecca to secretly expel some Muslims from it. When he arrived, a polytheistic woman called Anaq, who had been his lover in the pre-Islamic era, heard about him. She came to him and said: O Abu Marthad, will you not be alone? He said to her: Woe to you, Anaq, Islam has prevented us from that. She said: Will you marry me? He said: Yes, but go back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask his advice. She said: Are you fed up with me? Then she cried out for help against him, so they beat him severely, then let him go. When he had finished his need in Mecca and returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he informed him of what had happened to him and to Anaq and what he had suffered because of her. He said: O Messenger of God, is it permissible for me to marry her? Then God, the Almighty, revealed: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. It was said: The verse was abrogated with regard to the People of the Book by the Almighty’s saying: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you 5-5. If it is said: How did you call someone who does not deny anything except the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, polytheists? Abu al-Hasan ibn Faris said: Because whoever says that the Qur’an is the speech of someone other than God has associated partners with God and others. Qatada and Saeed ibn Jubayr said: He meant by polytheistic women idolaters, for Uthman, may God be pleased with him, married Nailah bint Farafisa, who was a Christian and she converted to Islam under his rule, and Talhah ibn Ubaydullah married a Christian woman, and Hudhayfah married a Jewish woman. [So Umar, may God be pleased with him, wrote to him: Let her go. He wrote to him: Do you claim that it is forbidden? He said: I do not claim that it is forbidden, but I fear that you will deal with prostitutes among them.] God the Almighty said: And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even if she pleases you with her beauty and wealth. It was revealed about Khansa, a black slave girl who belonged to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. O Khansa, you have been mentioned in the highest loyalty, despite your blackness and ugliness. So he freed her and married her. Al-Suddi said: “It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Rawahah. He had a black slave girl. He became angry with her and slapped her. Then he became frightened and went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him about that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What is she, O Abdullah? He said: She testifies that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God, and she fasts Ramadan, performs ablution well, and prays. He said: This is a believer. Abdullah said: By the One Who sent you with the truth as a prophet, I will free her and marry her. So he did that. Some Muslims criticized him and said: Are you marrying a slave girl? They offered him a free polytheist. So God the Almighty revealed this verse.” God Almighty says: And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe. This is a consensus: It is not permissible for a Muslim woman to marry a polytheist. “And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he might please you. Those” meaning the polytheists invite to the Fire meaning to the deeds that lead to the Fire. And God invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission meaning by His decree and will. And He makes clear His signs to the people meaning His commands and prohibitions that they may remember that they may be admonished.
2:222: 222. God the Almighty said: And they ask you about menstruation. Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani told us, Abu Umar al-Qasim ibn Ja`far ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Hashemi told us, Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lulu’i told us, Abu Dawud Sulayman al-Ash`ath al-Sijistani told us, Musa ibn Isma`il told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Thabit al-Bunani told us, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that when a woman menstruated, the Jews would expel her from the house and would not eat or drink with her or have intercourse with her in the house. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about that, so God the Almighty revealed: “And they ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harmful thing, so keep away from women during menstruation.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Have intercourse with them in their houses and do everything except intercourse. The Jews said: This man does not want to leave anything of our affair without swearing an oath in it. So Asid ibn Hudayr and `Ibad ibn Bishr came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, the Jews say such and such, so should we not have intercourse with them during menstruation? The face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became so red that we thought he was angry with them. They went out and were met by a gift of milk for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He sent after them and gave them something to drink. We thought he was not angry with them. God Almighty says: And they ask you about menstruation. That is, about menstruation, which is the source of the verb to menstruate. The woman menstruates, menstruating, and menstruation, like walking and traveling. The origin of menstruation is eruption and flow. His statement, Say, ‘It is harmful.’ That is, dirty, and harmful is everything that is disliked of anything. So keep away from women during menstruation. By keeping away, he meant refraining from intercourse. And do not approach them. That is, do not have intercourse with them. As for touching and sleeping with them, that is permissible. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qubaysah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “I and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to bathe from one vessel, both of us in a state of ritual impurity. He used to order me to wear a waist wrapper, and he would have intercourse with me while I was menstruating. He used to stick his head out to me while he was in seclusion, so I would wash it while I was menstruating.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saad bin Hafs told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Zainab bint Abu Salamah, who told him, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: “I had my period while I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Al-Khamila. I slipped away and went out of it, took my menstrual clothes and put them on. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: ‘Have you menstruated?’ I said: ‘Yes.’ So he called me and brought me with him into Al-Khamila.” Abu al-Qasim ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi told us, Abu al-Harith Tahir ibn Muhammad al-Tahiri told us, Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim told us, Abu al-Muwajjah Muhammad ibn Amr told us, Sadaqah told us, Wakee told us, Misa’ar and Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Miqdam ibn Shuraih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “I used to drink while I was menstruating, so I would hand it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would put his mouth on the place where I had been drinking, and I would sweat, so he would take it and put his mouth on the place where I had been drinking.” Having intercourse with a menstruating woman is forbidden, and whoever does so disobeys God Almighty and the Imam will punish him if he is found to have done so. The scholars differed on whether he must make expiation, and most of them are of the view that he does not have to make expiation, so he should seek God’s forgiveness and repent to Him. Some people said that expiation is obligatory for him, including: Qatada, Al-Awza’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq, because Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malhi told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shuraih told us, Al-Qasim al-Baghawi told us, Ali ibn al-Ja’d told us, Abu Ja’far al-Razi told us, Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Mukhariq told us, Muqsim told us, Ibn Abbas told us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “A man had intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating. He said, ‘If the blood is thick, then let him give a dinar in charity, and if it is yellow, then half a dinar.’” This is narrated as a narration attributed to Ibn Abbas, and menstruation prevents the permissibility and obligation of prayer, and prevents the permissibility of fasting, but does not prevent its obligation, until she becomes pure, then she must make up the fast, but she does not have to make up the prayer, and the same applies to the woman who has given birth. Abu Uthman bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi, on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi, on the authority of Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Ali bin Hajar, on the authority of Ali bin Mashair, on the authority of Ubaidah bin Mu’tab Al-Dhabi, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “We used to menstruate in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then we would become pure, and he would order us to make up the fasts, but he would not order us to make up the prayers.” A menstruating woman is not permitted to circumambulate the House, or to seclude herself in the mosque, or to touch the Qur’an, or to read the Qur’an, and the husband is not permitted to have intercourse with her. Umar ibn Abdul Aziz told us, Al Qasim ibn Ja`far told us, Abu Ali Al Lulu`i told us, Abu Dawud told us, Musaddad told us, Abdul Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, Aflat ibn Khalifa told us: Jasra bint Dajajah told us: I heard Aisha say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and the faces of his companions’ houses faced the mosque, so he said: Turn these houses away from the mosque, for I do not permit the mosque for a menstruating woman or a person in a state of ritual impurity. God the Almighty said: Until they purify themselves. Asim read, according to the narration of Abu Bakr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i, with a shaddah on the ta’ and the ha’, meaning: until they wash themselves. The others read it with a sukoon on the ta’ and a damma on the ha’, so it was lightened. Its meaning is until they purify themselves from menstruation and their blood stops. So when they purify themselves means they wash themselves. Then have intercourse with them means have sexual intercourse with them from where God has commanded you meaning from where He has commanded you to keep away from them, which is the vagina. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ikrimah. Ibn Abbas said: Have intercourse with them in the vagina and do not go beyond it to anything else, meaning avoid the anuses. It was said that from means in, meaning where God the Almighty has commanded you, which is the vagina, like His Almighty’s saying: When the call is made for prayer on Friday 9-Al-Jumu’ah, meaning on Friday. It was said that Go to them from the direction that God has commanded you to go to them, which is purity. Ibn Al-Hanafiyyah said: From the direction that is permissible, not from immorality. It was said: Do not go to them while they are fasting or in seclusion. And there are no prohibitions: And come to them and have intercourse with them is lawful for you. And know that the prohibition of anything that menstruation prevents is not lifted by the cessation of the blood unless she performs ghusl or tayammum when there is no water, except the prohibition of fasting. If the menstruating woman’s blood stops at night and she intends to fast and her ghusl occurs during the day, her fast is valid. Divorce during menstruation is heretical, and if he divorces her after the cessation of the blood before ghusl, it is not heretical. And it is said: Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, said that if her bleeding stops for the most part of her period, which is ten days, then it is permissible for the husband to have intercourse with her before washing. Mujahid and Tawus said: If she washes her vagina, then it is permissible for the husband to have intercourse with her before washing. Most scholars say that it is forbidden unless she performs ghusl or tayammum when there is no water, because God Almighty has made the permissibility of intercourse with her conditional on two conditions: the cessation of bleeding and the ritual bath. He said, until they are pure, meaning from menstruation. Then when they are pure, meaning they have performed ghusl. Then come to them. Whoever reads they are pure, with emphasis, what is meant by that is the ritual bath, as God Almighty says, And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, then purify yourselves Al-Ma’idah 5:6, meaning perform ghusl. This indicates that intercourse is not permissible before the ritual bath. God the Almighty says: Indeed, God loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves. Ata’, Muqatil bin Sulayman and Al-Kalbi said: He loves those who repent from sins and loves those who purify themselves with water from impurities and impurities. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: He loves those who repent from sins and those who purify themselves from polytheism. Saeed bin Jubayr said: Those who repent from polytheism and those who purify themselves from sins. Mujahid said: Those who repent from sins do not return to them, and those who purify themselves from them have not committed them. The Repentant is the one who repents whenever he sins. Similar to the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, He is, to the repentant, Forgiving. 25-Al-Isra’.
2:223: 223. The Almighty said: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so come to your tilth however you wish. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha'labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid Al-Isfahani told us, Muhammad bin Ya'qub told us, Ibn Al-Munadi told us, Yunus told us, Ya'qub Al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Ja'far bin Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Umar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I am ruined. He said: What ruined you? He said: I moved my saddle last night. He did not answer him anything, so God revealed to him: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so come to your tilth however you wish. He said: Turn back and forth, and avoid the anus and menstruation. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Ahmad bin Al-Hussein Al-Hiri told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Abdul Rahim bin Munib told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Munkadir, that he heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: The Jews used to say about the one who has intercourse with his wife from behind in her vagina: The child will be cross-eyed, so the verse was revealed: Your women are as a tilth unto you, so go to your tilth however you wish. Mujahid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It was the custom of the People of the Book not to approach women except on the verge, and that is the most concealing way for a woman to be. This tribe of the Ansar had taken that from their actions, and this tribe of Quraysh used to enjoy themselves with them facing forward, from behind, and lying down. When the Muhajireen came to Medina, a man from them married a woman from the Ansar, and he went to do that with her, but she disapproved of him and said: We used to be approached on the verge, so if you wish, do that, otherwise avoid me. Until their affair spread, and that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: Your women are a place of cultivation for you meaning the place of the child. So come to your place of cultivation however you wish facing forward, from behind, and lying down. And however you wish is an interrogative particle that is a question about the state and place, meaning: how you wish and where you wish, after it is in one valve. Ikrimah said: However you wish refers to the vagina, and the same is reported by Al-Hasan. It was said: A place of cultivation for you meaning a place for you to cultivate and a place for the child to grow, like the earth. Which is planted, and it is evidence of the prohibition of the anus, because the place of cultivation and planting is the vagina, not the anus. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said this about coitus interruptus, meaning if you wish, then coitus interruptus, and if you wish, then do not. Ibn Abbas was asked about coitus interruptus, and he said: It is your field. If you wish, then thirst, and if you wish, then quench your thirst. It was narrated from him that he said: A free woman should be consulted about coitus interruptus, but a slave woman should not be consulted. Ahmad said the same. A group disliked coitus interruptus and said: It is the hidden infanticide. It was narrated from Malik from Nafi’ who said: I was holding up the pages for Ibn Umar, and he recited this verse: Your women are a field of cultivation for you. He said: Do you know why this verse was revealed? I said: No. He said: It was revealed about a man who had intercourse with his wife from behind, and that upset him, so this verse was revealed. It is narrated from Malik that he permitted this, but his companions denied it. It was narrated from Abdullah bin Al-Hasan that he met Salim bin Abdullah and said to him, O Abu Omar, what is the hadith that Nafi’ narrated from Abdullah that he did not see anything wrong with approaching women from behind? He said, “The slave lied and made a mistake. Rather, Abdullah said: They come in their vaginas from behind.” The evidence for the prohibition of the behinds is what Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad bin Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Omar Muhammad bin Ali bin Shafi’ told me, Abdullah bin Ali bin Al-Sa’ib told me, from Amr bin Ahyiha bin Al-Julah, from Khuzaymah bin Thabit, that a man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about approaching women from behind. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “In which of the two holes, or in which of the two beads, or in which of the two strands, from her behind in her vagina, then yes. Or from her behind in her behind, then no, for God is not ashamed of the truth. Do not approach women from behind.” Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Hafiz told us, Omar bin Ahmad bin Al-Qasim Al-Nahwandi told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Sulaiman Al-Hadrami told us, Abdullah bin Aban told us, Yahya bin Zakariya bin Abi Zaida told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Khalid, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cursed is he who comes to his wife from behind. God Almighty said: And prepare for yourselves Ata’ said: The naming is before intercourse. Mujahid said: And prepare for yourselves means if he comes to his wife, then let him pray. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Kurayb, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If one of you, when he wants to have intercourse with his wife, says: ‘In the name of God, O God, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You have provided us,’ then if a child is destined between them in that, Satan will never harm him.” It was said: Put it first for yourselves, meaning: seeking a child. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hassan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Abdul-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him.” It was said: It is marrying chaste women so that the child will be righteous. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Musaddad, I told Yahya, on the authority of Ubaid God, Saeed bin Abi Saeed told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A woman is married for four reasons: her wealth, her lineage, her beauty, and her religion. So marry the one who is religious, may your hands be covered with dust.” It was said that the meaning of the verse is to give precedence to excesses. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No Muslim will have three children die and the Fire will touch him, except for the sake of breaking an oath. Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi said: And put forward for yourselves meaning goodness and righteous deeds, as evidenced by the context of the verse: And fear God and know that you will meet Him, going to Him and He will reward you for your deeds, and give good tidings to the believers.
2:224: 224. The Almighty’s saying: And do not make God an object of your oaths. It was revealed about Abdullah bin Rawahah. There was something between him and his brother-in-law, Bashir bin Al-Nu’man Al-Ansari, regarding his sister. Abdullah swore that he would not enter upon him, nor speak to him, nor reconcile between him and his opponent. If he was asked about it, he would say: I swore by God that I would not do it, so it is not permissible for me unless my oath is fulfilled. So God revealed this verse. Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq when he swore that he would not spend on Mastih when he was involved in the slanderous hadith. The root of Al-Ardah is strength and power. From this, it was said of the beast that is used for travel that it is called Al-Ardah, because of its strength on it. Then it was said of everything that is suitable for something that is a subject for it, until they said of a woman that she is a subject for marriage if she is suitable for it. Al-Ardah is everything that obstructs and prevents something. The meaning of the verse is Do not make the oath by God a reason preventing you from righteousness and piety. One of you is called to maintain family ties or to be righteous, and he says, I swore by God that I would not do it, so he uses his oath to abandon righteousness. That you be righteous means that you do not be righteous, like the Almighty’s saying, God makes clear to you, lest you go astray 176- An-Nisa, meaning so that you do not go astray. “And fear God and make peace between people. And God is Hearing and Knowing.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him atone for his oath and do what is better.
2:225: 225. The Almighty says: God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths. Idle talk is any speech that is not taken into account. Scholars differed regarding idle talk in the oath mentioned in the verse. Some people said that it is what comes to the tongue in haste to connect the speech, without intention or intent, like someone saying: No, by God, Yes, by God, and No, by God. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Kisa’i told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that she said: The futility of an oath is when a person says, No, by God, and Yes, by God. Some of them traced it back to the Prophet, and this is what Al-Sha’bi and Ikrimah went to, and Al-Shafi’i said the same. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha: Idle oaths are those that are made in jest, argument, dispute, and talk that the heart does not accept. Some people said: It is to swear on something that he believes to be true, then it becomes clear to him that it is not. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Al-Zuhri, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Qatada, and Makhul. Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him said the same. They said that there is no expiation for it and no sin upon him. Ali said: It is an oath in anger. Tawus said the same. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is an oath in disobedience. God will not hold him accountable for breaking it, but he breaks it and expiates. Masruq said: There is no expiation upon him. Does he expiate for the steps of Satan? Al-Sha’bi said about a man who swears on a disobedience: Its expiation is that he repents from it. Every oath that it is not permissible for you to fulfill has no expiation, so if you ordered him to expiate, you would order him to fulfill it, according to his opinion. Zaid bin Aslam said: It is a man’s supplication against himself, saying to someone: May God blind my sight if I do not do such and such [May God take my money away from me if I do not come to you tomorrow], and he says: He is an unbeliever if he does such and such. All of this is futile and God will not hold him accountable for it. If He were to hold them accountable for it, He would hasten their punishment. And if God were to hasten evil for people as they hasten good, their term would have been ended for them. Yunus 11:11. He also said, And man invokes evil as he invokes good. Al-Isra 11:11. God the Almighty said: But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned, meaning you resolved and intended to swear, and the heart earned the contract and intention. And God is Forgiving and Merciful. Know that an oath is not binding except by God or by one of His names, or by one of His attributes. So an oath by God is to say: And by Him I worship, “To Him I pray,” In Whose Hand is my soul, and the like. An oath by His names is like saying: And by God and the Most Gracious, and the like. An oath by His attributes is like saying: By the glory of God and the greatness of God and the majesty of God and the power of God, and the like. So if he swears by one of these things regarding a matter in the future, then he has broken his oath, and expiation is required of him. And if he swears regarding a matter in the past that it was and it was not, or that it was not and it was, if he knew about it at the time he swore, then it is a false oath, and it is one of the major sins, and expiation is required for it according to some scholars, whether he knew it or was ignorant. Al-Shafi’i said this, but it is not required according to some of them, and this is the opinion of the people of opinion. They said that if he knew, then it is a major sin and there is no expiation for it, as in the case of all major sins, and if he was ignorant, then it is a false oath. They consider an oath to be vain, and whoever swears by other than God, such as saying: By the Kaaba, by the House of God, by the Prophet of God, or swearing by his two doors, and the like, then it is not an oath, so expiation is not required of him if he swears, and it is a disliked oath. Al-Shafi’i said: I fear that it is a sin. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, caught up with Umar ibn al-Khattab while he was walking with a group and he was swearing by his father. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God forbids you from swearing by your fathers, so whoever swears, let him swear by God or remain silent.”
2:226: 226. God the Almighty said: For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives, a waiting period of four months. They swear, and the oath is the oath. What is meant by the verse is the oath to refrain from having sexual relations with the woman. Qatada said: The oath was a divorce for the people of ignorance. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: This was one of the harmful things that the people of ignorance did. A man did not love his wife and did not want anyone else to marry her, so he swore that he would never approach her, so he would leave her neither divorced nor married. This was the case at the beginning of Islam, so God set a deadline for him in Islam. The scholars differed about it: Most of them went to the view that if he swore that he would never approach his wife or named a period of more than four months, he would be a wali, so he should not be interfered with before the passage of four months. After that, he should be stopped and ordered to return or to divorce after the woman demands it. Returning is to go back on what he said by having sexual relations, if he is able to do so. If he is not able to do so, then by saying something. If he does not return and does not divorce her, the ruler divorces her once. Umar, Uthman, Ali, Abu Al-Darda’, and Ibn Omar, Sulayman bin Yasar said: I met a dozen of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, all of whom said that the mawla should be stopped. Saeed bin Jubair, Sulayman bin Yasar, and Mujahid held this view, and Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq said the same. Some of the people of knowledge said: If four months have passed, a final divorce is valid for him, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas’ud, and Sufyan Al-Thawri and the people of opinion said the same. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Al-Zuhri said: A revocable divorce occurs. If he swears that he will not have intercourse with her for less than four months, he is not considered to have sworn an oath. If he has intercourse with her before that period has passed, he must pay expiation for the oath. If he swears that he will not have intercourse with her for four months, he is not considered to have sworn an oath according to those who say that it is suspended after the period has passed, because the continuation of the period is a condition for the suspension and the establishment of the demand for compensation or divorce, and the period has passed. According to those who do not say that it is suspended, he is considered to have sworn an oath, and the divorce occurs after the period has passed. The period of ila’: four months for both free men and slaves, according to Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, because it was coined for a meaning that goes back to nature, which is the woman’s lack of patience with her husband, so the free man and the slave are equal in it, like the period of impotence. According to Malik, may God have mercy on him, and Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, the period of impotence is divided into slavery, but according to Abu Hanifa it is characterized by the slavery of the woman, and according to Malik it is characterized by the slavery of the husband, as they said in divorce. God the Almighty said: Wait four months meaning wait for four months. Waiting means verifying and stopping. If they return they go back on the oath of intercourse. Then God is Forgiving and Merciful. If he has intercourse, he is no longer bound by the oath and must pay expiation for the oath according to most scholars. Al-Hasan, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i and Qatadah said: There is no expiation for him because God the Almighty promised forgiveness and said: Then God is Forgiving and Merciful. This is according to most scholars in dropping the punishment, not in expiation. If he says to his wife: If I bring you near, then my slave is free, or you are divorced, or God has freed a slave, or fasts, or prays, then he is a guardian because the guardian is the one who is obligated to command intercourse, and he is suspended after the expiry of the period. If he returns, the divorce or the manumission that is conditional upon it occurs. If he commits himself to the obligation, he must pay expiation for the oath according to one opinion. According to another opinion, he must pay what he committed himself to in his obligation of manumission, prayer, and fasting.
2:227: 227. And if they decide on divorce meaning they carry it out by pronouncing it, then indeed, God is Hearing of their words, Knowing of their intentions. This is evidence that she is not divorced after the expiration of the period unless her husband divorces her, because he stipulated the decision in it. And he said, then indeed, God is Hearing, Knowing so it indicates that it requires something that is heard, and the word is what is heard.
2:228: 228. The Almighty said: And divorced women meaning those who are freed from the bonds of their husbands shall wait “concerning themselves three menstrual periods” then they shall not marry. And menstrual periods is the plural of menstruation, and its small plural is aqra’u and its large plural is aqra’u. The scholars differed regarding menstrual periods, so a group of them went to the view that it is menstruation, and this is the view of Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, and Ibn Abbas, and this is what Al-Hasan and Mujahid said, and Al-Awza’i, Al-Thawri, and the people of opinion went to it, and they argued that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the woman with istihadah Leave the prayer during your menstrual periods, and she only leaves the prayer during her menstruation. A group of people said that it is the period of purity, and this is the opinion of Zaid bin Thabit, Abdullah bin Omar, and Aisha, and it is the opinion of the seven jurists and Al-Zuhri, and it is what Rabia, Malik, and Al-Shafi’i said. They argued that when Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with him, divorced his wife while she was menstruating, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Omar: “Tell him to take her back until she is pure, then if he wants he can keep her, and if he wants he can divorce her before he touches her, and this is the waiting period for which God has commanded women to be divorced.” He informed that the period of waiting is purity, and from the linguistic point of view, the poet said: Every year you are a brave warrior, and your determination to conquer is tightened to its furthest point. A wealth inheritor, and a place of honor in the neighborhood, because of the menstrual periods of your women that were lost therein. He meant that he would go out to fight and did not cheat on his wives, so their menstrual periods would be lost, but the time of purity is lost by travel, not the time of menstruation. The benefit of the disagreement is that if the woman in waiting begins her third menstruation, her waiting period ends according to the opinion of those who consider it to be purity, and the rest of the purity in which the divorce occurred is considered a menstrual period. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: If the divorced woman experiences blood from the third menstruation, then she is absolved of it and he is absolved of her. Whoever believes that the menstrual periods are the menstruation says that her waiting period does not decrease as long as she does not purify herself from the third menstruation. This disagreement is because the name of the menstrual period applies to purity and menstruation together. It is said that a woman menstruated, and she purified, so she is a reciter. They differed about its origin, so Abu Amr ibn al-Ala and Abu Ubaidah said: It is the time for the coming and going of something. It is said: So-and-so returned to his menstrual period and to his reciter, meaning the time in which he returns. This is the reciter of the winds, meaning the time of their blowing. Malik ibn al-Harith al-Hudhali said: I hated the barrenness of the Banu Shaleel when the winds blew for its reader Any time, and the menstrual cycle is suitable for both aspects, because menstruation comes at a time, and purity is like it, and it was said: It is from the qara’ which means to hold and collect, the Arabs say: The she-camel has never held a baby, meaning her womb has never held a child, and from this the water was qara’at in the cistern, meaning it gathered it, without the hamza, so the qara’ here is the retention and accumulation of blood, so based on this the preference is for purity because it holds the blood and collects it, and the menstruation releases it and releases it, and the general ruling on the number is that if the woman is pregnant, her waiting period is until she gives birth, whether the separation between her and the husband occurred by divorce or death, according to the Almighty’s saying: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth 4-Divorce. If she is not pregnant, consider: If the separation between them occurred by the death of the husband, then she must observe the waiting period of four months and ten days, whether the husband died before or after consummation, and whether the woman is one of those who menstruate or not, according to the Almighty’s saying: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days 4-Divorce. 234-Al-Baqarah And if separation occurs between them during life, then it is considered that if the divorce occurred before consummation of the marriage, then there is no waiting period for her, because God Almighty says: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period to count for them 49-Al-Ahzab. If it was after consummation, then consider: If the woman is one of those who have never menstruated or has reached the age of despair, then her waiting period is three months, based on the statement of God Almighty: And for those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you doubt, their waiting period is three months, and for those who have not menstruated 4-At-Talaq. If she is one of those who menstruate, her waiting period is three menstrual periods, based on the Almighty’s statement: Divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods. The statement shall wait, concerning themselves is a statement but its meaning is a command. The waiting period of a slave woman, if she is pregnant, is like that of a free woman. If she is not menstruating, her waiting period in the case of death is two months and five nights. In the case of divorce, if she is one of those who menstruate, her waiting period is two menstrual periods. If she is one of those who does not menstruate, her waiting period is a month and a half. It was said that it is two months like two menstrual periods for a woman who menstruates. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: A slave may marry two women and divorce them twice, and the waiting period of a slave woman is two menstrual periods. If she does not menstruate, then it is two months or a month and a half. And the Almighty said: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs. Ikrimah said: It means menstruation, which is when the man wants to take her back and she says: I have had my third menstruation. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: It means pregnancy. The meaning of the verse: It is not lawful for a woman to conceal what God has created in her womb of menstruation and pregnancy in order to nullify the husband’s right to take her back and have children. If they believe in God and the Last Day. Its meaning is that this is from the actions of believing women, even though believing women and disbelieving women are equal in this ruling, as you say: Give me my right if you are a believer. That is, giving rights is from the actions of believers. And their husbands means their husbands, plural of ba’l, like fuhulah is plural of fahl. The husband was called ba’l because he takes care of his wife’s affairs. The root of ba’l is master and owner. “He has more right to take them back” is more deserving of their return to them. In that meaning during the waiting period “if they want to make peace” meaning if they want to make peace and treat each other well, not to cause harm, as they used to do in the days of ignorance. A man would divorce his wife, then when her waiting period was about to end, he would take her back, then leave her for a while, then divorce her. Then when her waiting period was about to end, he would take her back, then after a while he would divorce her, intending by that to prolong her waiting period. And for them meaning women have rights over their husbands like those over them have over their husbands, according to what is reasonable. Ibn Abbas said about its meaning: I like to adorn myself for my wife as my wife likes her to adorn herself for me, because God Almighty said: And for them are rights similar to those over them, according to what is reasonable. Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi told us, Abu Sahl Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Tarfa al-Sajzi told us, Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi told us, Abu Bakr ibn Dasa told us, Abu Dawud al-Sijistani told us, Musa ibn Ismail told us, Hammad told us, Abu Qaza’ah Suwayd ibn Hujayr al-Bahili told us, on the authority of Hakim ibn Mu’awiyah al-Qushayri, on the authority of his father, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, what are the rights of one of our wives over him? He said: “That you feed her when you eat, and that you clothe her when you clothe yourself, and that you do not strike her in the face, and that you do not insult her, and that you do not desert her except in the house.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad Al-Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Hatim bin Ismail Al-Madani told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, that he said: We entered upon Jabir bin Abdullah, and I said: Tell me about the Hajj of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he narrated the story of the Farewell Hajj until he mentioned his sermon on the Day of Arafah. He said: “So fear God with regard to women, for they are captives with you. You have taken them as a trust from God, and you have made their private parts lawful for you by the word of God. You have the right over them that they should not let anyone you dislike share your bed. If they do that, then beat them, but not severely. They have the right over you to provide for them and clothe them in a reasonable manner. I have left among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray after it: the Book of God. You will be asked about me, so what will you say?” They said: We bear witness that you have conveyed the message, fulfilled your duty, and advised. So he pointed with his index fingers. He raises it to the sky and points it at the people, saying, O God, bear witness, O God, bear witness, three times. Ahmad Al-Salihi told us, Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hairi told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Muhammad bin Yahya told us, Ya’la bin Ubaid told us, Muhammad bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The most perfect of the believers in faith are the best of them in character, and the best of you are the best to your women. God Almighty says: And men have a degree over them. Ibn Abbas said: Because of what he gave her of the dowry and spent on her of money. Qatada said: By jihad. It was said: By reason. It was said: By testimony. It was said: By inheritance. It was said: By blood money. It was said: By divorce, because divorce is in the hands of men. It was said: By taking her back. Sufyan and Zaid bin Aslam said: By leadership. Al-Qutaibi said: And men have a degree over them, meaning: excellence in the truth. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Barti told us, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Thabyan, that Muadh ibn Jabal went out on a military expedition in which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent him, then he returned and saw some men prostrating to one another, so he mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, If I were to command anyone to prostrate to anyone, I would have commanded a woman to prostrate to her husband.
2:229: 229. The Almighty’s saying: Divorce is twice. It was narrated on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr who said: In the beginning, people used to divorce without limit or number. A man would divorce his wife, and when her waiting period was about to end, he would take her back, then he would divorce her again, then he would take her back, intending to harm her. Then this verse was revealed: Divorce is twice. It means that the divorce in which he has the right to take her back is twice. If he divorces her three times, she is not permissible for him except after marrying another husband. God Almighty says: Then keep her in an acceptable manner. It was said that by keeping her he meant taking her back after the second time. The correct view is that what is meant by it is keeping her back after taking her back. That is, if he takes her back after the second time, then he must keep her in an acceptable manner, everything that is known in the Sharia, from fulfilling the rights of marriage and good companionship. Or release her with kindness. This means that he leaves her after the divorce until her waiting period expires. It was also said that it means the third divorce. The Almighty said: Or release with kindness. The explicit wording by which divorce occurs without intention is three: divorce, separation, and release. According to Abu Hanifa, the explicit wording is only the word divorce. The general ruling on this is that if a free man divorces his wife with one or two divorces after consummating the marriage with her, he is permitted to take her back without her consent as long as she is in her waiting period. If he does not take her back until her waiting period has ended, or divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, or divorces her by khul’, she is not permissible for him except through a new marriage with her permission and the permission of her guardian. If he divorces her three times, she is not permissible for him unless she marries another husband. As for a slave, if there is a woman under him and he divorces her twice, she is not permissible for him except after marrying another husband. Scholars differed as to whether one of the spouses was a slave. Most of them held that the number of divorces should be based on the husband. A free man has three divorces over his slave wife, while a slave has only two divorces over his free wife. Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, said: Divorce is for men and the waiting period is for women. That is, the number of divorces is based on the man’s condition and the length of the waiting period is based on the woman’s condition. This is the opinion of `Uthman, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them. `Ata’ and Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab said the same, and Malik, al-Shafi`i, Ahmad, and Ishaq held the same opinion. Some people held the opinion that the woman should be considered in the number of divorces, so a slave man has three divorces over his free wife, while a free man has only two divorces over his slave wife. This is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri and the People of Opinion. God the Almighty said: And it is not lawful for you to take back from what you have given them you have given them any of dowries and other things. Then He made an exception for khul’ and said: Unless they both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits set by God. It was revealed about Jamilah bint Abdullah bin Abi Awfa. It is said: “Habiba bint Sahl was married to Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas and she hated him and he loved her, so there was a conversation between them. She went to her father and complained to him about her husband and said to him: He mistreats me and beats me. He said: Go back to your husband, for I hate for a woman to keep raising her hands complaining about her husband.” She said: So she went back to him a second time and she had marks of beatings on her. He said to her: Go back to your husband. When she saw that her father did not complain about her, she went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and complained to him about her husband and showed him marks of his beatings on her. She said: O Messenger of God, neither I nor he. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for Thabit and said: What do you have to do with your family? He said: By the One Who sent you as a prophet with the truth, there is no one on the face of the earth more beloved to me than you. He said to her: What are you saying? She hated to lie about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he asked her, she said: He is telling the truth, O Messenger of God, but I feared that he would destroy me, so take me out of him. She said: O Messenger of God, I would not tell you a story that God would reveal to you contrary to it. He is the most generous of people in his love for his wife, but I hate him, neither I nor he. Thabit said: I have given her a garden, so return it to me and I will set her free. He said to her: Will you return his garden to him and control your affairs? She said: Yes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Thabit, take from her what you gave her and set her free. So he did. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin God Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Zahir bin Jameel told us, Abdul Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, Khalid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the wife of Thabit bin Qais came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I do not blame Thabit for his character or religion, but I hate to disbelieve after becoming a Muslim. Will you return his garden to him? She said: Yes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Accept the garden and divorce her once. God the Almighty said: Except that they both fear meaning they know that they will not be able to maintain the limits set by God. Abu Ja`far, Hamza, and Ya`qub read except that they both fear with a damma on the ya’, meaning that they know that from both of them, meaning: the judge and the guardian know that from the spouses, based on the evidence of God the Almighty’s saying: If you fear, so He made fear for other than the spouses, and He did not say If they both fear. The others read they fear with a fatha on the ya’, meaning that the spouses know from themselves that they will not be able to maintain the limits set by God. The woman fears that she will disobey God in the matter of her husband, and the husband fears that if his wife does not obey him, he will assault her. So God forbade the man from taking from his wife anything that He has given her, unless the rebellion is from her, so she says: I will not obey any command from you, nor will I lie with you for long, and so on. God the Almighty said: But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of God, then there is no blame upon them for that by which she ransoms herself meaning, for that by which the woman ransoms herself from him. Al-Farra’ said: He meant by his saying on both of them the husband, not the woman, so he mentioned them both because they are linked together, like the Almighty’s saying: They forgot their fish Al-Kahf 61. The one who forgot was the young man of Moses, not Moses. It was said: He meant that there is no blame upon them both, there is no blame upon the woman for rebellion if she fears destruction and disobedience, nor for that by which she ransoms herself and gives of money, because she is forbidden from wasting money unjustly, nor for the husband for that by which he takes money from her if she gives it willingly. Most scholars are of the view that khul’ is permissible for more than what he gave her, and Al-Zuhri said: It is not permissible for more than what he gave her as a dowry. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: He does not take from her everything he gave her, but rather leaves some of it. Divorce is permissible in cases other than rebellion, except because it involves severing the connection without a reason. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi, on the authority of Abu Abdullah bin Fanjuwayh Al-Daynuri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Shaiba, on the authority of Ahmad bin Ja’far Al-Mustamli, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Yahya bin Ishaq bin Shakir bin Ahmad bin Khabab, on the authority of Isa bin Yunus, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Walid Al-Wasafi, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The most hated of permissible things to God is divorce. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjuwayh told us, Ibn Abi Asma Al-Rahbi told us, on the authority of Thawban, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Any woman who asks her husband for a divorce without a valid reason will be forbidden the scent of Paradise. Tawus said: Khul’ is usually limited to cases of fear of rebellion. If a man divorces his wife by uttering the word divorce in return for money and she accepts, then separation occurs and the number of divorces is reduced. The scholars differed regarding Khul’. Most of them held that it is an irrevocable divorce that reduces the number of divorces. This is the opinion of Umar, Uthman, Ali, and Ibn Mas’ud. This is also the opinion of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, Ata’, al-Hasan, al-Sha’bi, and al-Nakha’i. This is also the opinion of Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, and the people of opinion. This is the more apparent opinion of al-Shafi’i. Some people held that it is an annulment that does not reduce the number of divorces. This is the opinion of Abdullah ibn Umar and Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them. This is the opinion of Ikrimah and Tawus, and this is the opinion of Ahmad and Ishaq. They argued that God Almighty mentioned divorce twice, then mentioned Khul’ after that, then mentioned the third divorce, saying, But if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband. If Khul’ were a divorce, then the divorce would be four. Those who held the first opinion made the third al-Talaq 65:or a release with good treatment. God Almighty says: These are the limits set by God. That is, these are God’s commands and prohibitions. God’s limits are what the Sharia forbids one from exceeding. So do not transgress them. So do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits set by God - it is those who are the wrongdoers.
2:230: 230. The Almighty’s saying: And if he divorces her meaning the third divorce then she is not lawful to him afterward meaning after the third divorce until she marries another husband meaning: other than the one he divorced, and he has intercourse with them, and marriage includes intercourse and the contract together. It was revealed about Tamimah and it was said that Aisha bint Abd al-Rahman ibn Atik al-Qurazi was her cousin Rifa’ah ibn Wahb ibn Atik al-Qurazi, so he divorced her three times. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, that he heard her say: “The wife of Rifa’a Al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I was with Rifa’a, and he divorced me and made my divorce public. After him, I married Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Zubayr, and he only had what was like the hem of a garment. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled and said: Do you want to go back to Rifa’a? She said: Yes. He said: No, until he tastes your honey and you taste his honey.” It was narrated that she stayed as long as God willed, then she returned to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: My husband touched me. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to her: You lied in your first statement, so we will not believe you in the second. She stayed until the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed away. She went to Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him and he said: O successor of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), return my first husband, for my second husband touched me and divorced me. Abu Bakr said to her: I witnessed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when you came to him and he said to you what he said, so do not return to him. When Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him passed away, she went to Umar may God be pleased with him and said to him: The same. Umar may God be pleased with him said to her: She said to him: The same. Umar may God be pleased with him said to her: If you return to him, I will stone you. God the Almighty said: But if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them if they return to each other meaning if the second husband divorces her after he has had intercourse with her there is no blame upon them meaning upon the woman and the first husband if they return to each other meaning with a new marriage if they think meaning if they know, and it was said if they hope, because no one knows what will happen except God the Almighty that they will maintain the limits of God meaning that there will be reconciliation and good companionship between them. Mujahid said: Its meaning is if they know that their marriage was not based on deception, and by deception he meant tahlil, which is the view of Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, Malik, Ahmad and Ishaq. They said: If a woman who has been divorced three times marries another husband to make her permissible for the first husband, then the marriage is invalid. A group of people said that if he did not stipulate in the marriage with the second husband that he would separate from her, then the marriage is valid and tahlil is achieved and she is entitled to a dowry similar to hers, but it is disliked if she intends to do so. Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar ibn Ismail al-Tamimi told us, Abu al-Qasim Hamza ibn Yusuf al-Sahmi told us, Abu Ahmad Abdullah ibn Adi al-Hafiz told us, al-Hasan ibn al-Faraj told us, Amr ibn Khalid al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdul Karim, he is al-Jazari, on the authority of Abu Wasil, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he cursed the one who performs tahlil and the one for whom it is performed. Nafi’ said that a man came to Ibn Umar and said to him: A man divorced his wife three times, and his brother from another man went out to conspire and married her to make her permissible for the first man. He said: No, except a marriage of desire. We used to consider fornication as adultery during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
