The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has cursed the one who performs tahlil and the one for whom it is performed. “And these are the limits set by God which He makes clear to a people who know,” meaning they know what God Almighty has commanded them to do.
2:231: 231. The Almighty’s saying: And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term, the verse was revealed about a man from the Ansar called Thabit ibn Yasar who divorced his wife, and when her waiting period was about to end, he took her back, then he divorced her, intending to harm her. God the Almighty says: And they have reached their term, meaning they are on the verge of becoming divorced by the expiration of the waiting period. He does not mean the actual expiration of the waiting period, because if the waiting period expires, the husband does not have the right to keep her. Thus, puberty here means approaching puberty. And in God the Almighty’s saying after this, And they have reached their term, so do not prevent them, the actual expiration of the waiting period is included in both meanings. It is said: he reached the city if he came close to it and if he entered it. So keep them, meaning take them back with kindness. It was said that taking them back with kindness means that he witnesses her return and takes her back with words, not with intercourse. Or release them with kindness meaning, leave them until their waiting period is over, so that you will have more control over yourself. And do not keep them to cause harm in order to transgress meaning, do not intend to cause harm by prolonging the confinement. And whoever does that has wronged himself meaning, he has harmed himself by disobeying the command of God Almighty. And do not take the verses of God in jest. Al-Kalbi said, meaning the words of God Almighty: (Either keep them in kindness or release them with good treatment) and whoever disobeys the command of the Shari’ah is taking the verses of God in jest. Abu al-Darda’ said, It is when a man divorces his wife and then says, ‘I was joking,’ and frees her and says, ‘The same,’ and marries and says the same. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Amr Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Abu Habib bin Ardak, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Mahak, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “There are three things that are serious when done seriously, and serious when done in jest: divorce, marriage, and taking back a wife.” And remember the favor of God upon you through faith and what He has revealed to you of the Book meaning: the Qur’an and wisdom meaning: the Sunnah, and it was said: the admonitions of the Qur’an He admonishes you thereby, and fear God and know that God is Knowing of all things.
2:232: 232. And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term was revealed about Jamila bint Yasar, the sister of Muqal bin Yasar Al-Muzani. She was married to Abu Al-Badah Asim bin Adi bin Ajlan, and he divorced her. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmad bin Abi Amr told us, my father told me, Ibrahim told me, Yunus told me, Al-Hasan told me, Maqal bin Yasar told me, he said, I married my sister to a man, then he divorced her. When her waiting period was over, he came to propose to her, so I said to him: I married her to you, provided for you, and honored you, and you divorced her, then you came to propose to her? No, by God, she will never come back to you. He was a good man, and the woman wanted to go back to him, so God Almighty revealed: So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands 2:100. I said: Now I will do it, O Messenger of God. He said: So I married her to him. God Almighty says: And they have reached their term meaning their waiting period has expired so do not prevent them from marrying their husbands meaning do not prevent them from marriage. Preventing means preventing, and its origin is distress and hardship. It is said: A woman is prevented if her child is implanted in her womb and it is difficult for it to come out, and the incurable disease that is unbearable. The verse is evidence that the woman does not have the authority to conclude the marriage contract, because if she had the power to do so, there would be no preventing, and the guardian’s prohibition of preventing would have no meaning. It was said that the verse is addressed to the husbands to prevent them from causing harm because the beginning of the verse is addressed to them, and the first is more correct. If they agree among themselves in kindness with a lawful contract and a permissible dowry. That meaning that which was mentioned of the prohibition is admonished by whoever among you believes in God and the Last Day. He only said that in the singular form, and the address is to the guardians because the original in addressing the group is that, then it became so common that they thought that the kaf was from the same letter and was not a kaf of address, so they said that. So if they said this, the kaf would be in the singular form and in the accusative case in the dual and plural and feminine and masculine. It was said that it was addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Therefore, he made it singular, then he returned to addressing the believers and said, That is purer for you meaning better for you, and purer for your hearts from doubt, because if there was in the soul of each of them what they might be innocent of, then they would sin. And God knows while you do not know meaning He knows of the love of each of them for the other what you do not know.
2:233: 233. God the Almighty said: And mothers shall suckle their children meaning: divorced women who have children from their husbands who suckle, a report with the meaning of a command, and it is a command of recommendation, not a command of obligation, because it is not obligatory for them to suckle if there is someone to suckle the child, according to God the Almighty’s statement in Surat al-Talaq 65:And if they suckle for you, then give them their compensation 6-At-Talaq. If the mother desires to suckle, then she is more deserving than others. Two complete years meaning two years, and the mention of completion is for emphasis, as God the Almighty said: Those are ten complete years 196-Al-Baqarah. It was said that He said complete because the Arabs call some of the year a year and some of the month a month, as God the Almighty said: The Hajj is in well-known months 197-Al-Baqarah, but it is two months and some of the third, and He said: But whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him 203-Al-Baqarah, but he hastens in one day and some of a day, and it is said that someone stayed in such and such a place for two years, but he stayed there for one year and some of another, so God the Almighty explained that they are two complete years, twenty-four months. Scholars differed regarding this limit. Some of them said that it is a limit for some newborns. Ikrimah and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, narrated that if she gives birth after six months, she breastfeeds him for two full years. If she gives birth after seven months, she breastfeeds him for twenty-three months. If she gives birth after nine months, she breastfeeds him for twenty-one months. If she gives birth after ten months, she breastfeeds him for twenty months. All of that makes thirty months, because God Almighty says: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months 15-Al-Haqqaf. Some people said: It is a limit for every child born at any time, and his breastfeeding does not decrease from two years except with the agreement of the parents. So whoever wants to wean before the completion of the two years, he does not have that right unless they agree on it, according to the saying of God Almighty: But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation. This is the saying of Ibn Jurayj and al-Thawri and the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them. It was said: What is meant by the verse is to clarify that the breastfeeding by which the prohibition is established is that which occurs in the two years, so that which occurs after the two years does not prohibit. Qatada said: God imposed on mothers breastfeeding for two complete years, then He revealed the alleviation and said: For whoever desires to complete the breastfeeding. That is, this breastfeeding, and there is no specific limit for what is less than that, but rather it is according to the extent of the child’s righteousness and what he lives on. And upon the father of the child meaning the father is their provision their food and their clothing “according to what is easy” meaning according to what is easy. No soul is charged with a duty except [with that within] its capacity meaning its ability. No mother shall be harmed on account of her child. Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read with the ra’ raised, in accordance with His saying no duty. Its origin is tadharur, so the ra’ was assimilated into the ra’. Others read tadhar with the ra’ in the accusative case. They said: When the ra’ was assimilated into the ra’, it was moved to the lightest of the vowels, which is the accusative. The meaning of the verse is No mother shall be harmed by her child meaning that the child is taken from her to another woman after she has agreed to breastfeed him. Nor shall a child be born to him by his child meaning that the woman shall not throw him to his father after he has become accustomed to her, harming him by that. It was said that its meaning is No mother shall be harmed so that she is forced to breastfeed him if she dislikes breastfeeding him, and the child is accepted by another woman, because that is not obligatory upon her. Nor shall a child be born to him by his child so it is possible that the mother is given more than what is due to her if he is not breastfed by another woman. According to these two sayings, the root of the word is la tadhar with the first ra open for the passive verb, and the mother and the newborn are two objects, and it is possible that the verb belongs to them and tadhar means tadhar with the first ra closed for naming the agent and the meaning is la tudhar so that she refuses to breastfeed her child to make it difficult for his father nor a newborn for him meaning that the father does not harm the mother of the boy, so he takes him away from her and prevents her from breastfeeding him, and according to these sayings the harm is attributed to the parents, each one of them harms the other because of the child, and it is possible that the harm is attributed to the boy, meaning that neither of them harms the boy, so the mother does not breastfeed him until he dies or the father does not spend or takes him away from the mother until he harms the boy, so according to this the ba is redundant and its meaning is la tudhar a mother with her child and no father with his child, and all of these sayings are narrated from the commentators. God the Almighty said: And the heir shall have the same. They differed about this heir. Some people said: It is the heir of the boy, meaning: And the heir of the boy who, if the boy died and had money, would inherit it like what his father had in his lifetime. Then they differed about which heir is from his heirs. Some of them said: It is the boy’s male agnates, such as: the grandfather, brother, nephew, paternal uncle, and cousin. This is the saying of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. Ibrahim, al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Ata’ said the same, and it is the school of thought of Sufyan. They said: If the boy does not have money to spend on him, his agnates who inherit him are forced to breastfeed him. It was said: The boy’s heir is whoever they are, from men and women. This is the saying of Qatadah and Ibn Abi Layla and the school of thought of Ahmad and Ishaq. They said: Every heir is forced to spend on him according to the amount of his inheritance, whether they are agnates or not. Some of them said that it is the one who is a mahram to the heirs of the newborn, so the one who is not a mahram, such as a cousin or a freed slave, is not meant by the verse, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him. A group went to the view that what is meant by the heir is the boy himself, who is the heir of his deceased father, so the cost of his breastfeeding and his expenses are from his money, and if he does not have money, then it is on the mother, and no one is obligated to pay the expenses of the boy except the parents, and this is the opinion of Malik and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them, and it was said that it is the remainder of the parents of the newborn after the death of the other, so he has the same amount of money as the father had to pay for breastfeeding, expenses and clothing. It was said: It does not mean maintenance, but rather it means: And it is upon the heir to leave harm, and this is what Al-Sha’bi and Al-Zuhri said: If he wants meaning the parents weaning “weaning before two years” with their mutual consent meaning agreement of the parents and consultation meaning they consult the people of knowledge about it until they inform them that weaning at that time does not harm the child, and consultation is the extraction of an opinion there is no blame upon them meaning there is no blame upon them for weaning before two years and if you wish to have wet nurses for your children meaning for your children wet nurses other than their mothers if their mothers refuse to breastfeed them or it is impossible due to a disease in them, meaning: the cessation of milk or they want to marry there is no blame upon you if you hand over to their mothers what you have given what you have asked them of the wages for breastfeeding in proportion to what they breastfed, and it was said if you hand over the wages of the wet nurses to them in a reasonable manner, Ibn Kathir read what you have given and in Ar-Rum and what you have given of interest 39-Ar-Rum with a shortened alif Its meaning is what you did. It is said: You did something good if you did it. According to this reading, submission means obedience and submission, not in the sense of handing over the wage, meaning if you submit to his command and obey his judgment. It was said that if you submit to the breastfeeding with consent and agreement without causing harm, And fear God and know that God is Seeing of what you do.
2:234: 234. The Almighty’s saying: And those among you who die means they die and their appointed times are fulfilled. The word to die and to take have the same meaning, and the meaning of taking is to take something in full. And they leave wives they leave wives. They wait they wait for themselves four months and ten meaning they observe the waiting period by leaving off adornment, perfume, and clothing after being separated from their husbands for this period, unless they are pregnant, in which case their waiting period is until they give birth. The waiting period for death was initially a full year, according to the Almighty’s saying: And those among you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall bequeath to their wives a provision for a year, without removing them 240-Al-Baqarah. Then it was abrogated by four months and ten. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: This waiting period, meaning four months and ten days, was obligatory for her husband’s family, so God Almighty revealed: A provision for a year, and made the completion of the year seven months and twenty nights for her, and a will: if she wanted to live in her will, she could go out, and if she wanted to go out, she could go out. This is the saying of God Almighty: “but not expelling them. But if they go out, there is no blame upon you for what they do” 240-Al-Baqarah. So the waiting period is obligatory for her as it is. Ata said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: This verse abrogated her waiting period with his family and she remained in her will and if she wanted she could leave. Ata said: Then inheritance came and abrogated the residence so she could observe the waiting period wherever she wanted and she has no residence and she must observe the mourning period of death, which is to refrain from adornment and perfume. It is not permissible for her to anoint her head with any oil whether it contains perfume or not, and she may anoint her body with oil that does not contain perfume. If it contains perfume, it is not permissible. It is not permissible for her to apply kohl that contains perfume or adornment like black kohl. There is nothing wrong with Persian kohl that does not contain adornment. If she is forced to use kohl that contains adornment, many scholars have permitted it, including Salim ibn Abdullah, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Ata, and al-Nakha’i. Malik and the people of opinion said the same. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: She applies it to her at night and wipes it off during the day. Umm Salamah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came in when Abu Salamah died and I had put aloe vera on me. He said, It makes the face turn grey, so do not put it on except at night and remove it during the day. It is not permissible for her to dye her hair, wear brocade, silk, or jewelry. It is permissible for her to wear white clothes, wool, or fur. She should not wear clothes dyed for adornment, such as red, bright green, or yellow. It is permissible for clothes dyed for other than adornment, such as black and navy blue. Sufyan said: She should not wear dyed clothes under any circumstances. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Ishaq al-Hashimi told us, Abu Mus’ab told us, Malik told us, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr told us, Umar ibn Hazm told us, Humayd ibn Nafi’ told us, Zainab bint Abi Salamah told us, that she told him these three hadiths. Zainab said: I went to Umm Habibah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when her father, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, died. Umm Habibah asked for some perfume that had saffron in it, khaluq or something else, and she anointed a slave girl with it, then she touched her stomach and said: By God, I have no need for perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the pulpit: It is not permissible for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three nights, except for her husband, for four months and ten days. Zainab said: Then I went to Zainab bint Jahsh when her brother Abdullah died, so she asked for some perfume and applied it, then she said: By God, I have no need for perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the pulpit: It is not permissible for a woman to mourn for a dead person for more than three nights, except for her husband, for whom she mourns for four months and ten days. Zainab said: And I heard my mother, Umm Salamah, say: “A woman came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, my daughter’s husband died and she has a sore eye, should I apply kohl to it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No. Then he said: It is four months and ten days, and during the pre-Islamic era, one of you would throw dung at the beginning of a year.” Humayd said: So I said to Zainab: Why do you throw dung at the beginning of a year? Zainab said: When a woman’s husband died, she would enter a small house and wear her worst clothes, and she would not touch perfume or anything else until a year had passed. Then she would be brought an animal, a donkey, a sheep, or a bird, and she would wipe it, and she would rarely wipe anything without it dying. Then she would go out and give him dung and throw it away, and after that she would put on whatever perfume or other thing she wanted. Malik said: She would wipe her skin. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: The wisdom behind this period is that during it the soul is breathed into the child, and it is said that the child moves in the womb for half the period of pregnancy, four months and ten, close to half the period of pregnancy. He only said ten in the feminine form because he meant the nights, because if the Arabs make the number vague between the nights and the days, the nights prevail, so they say we fasted ten, and fasting can only be done during the day. Al-Mubarrad said: The feminine form of ten is because it is the period, meaning ten periods, each period is one day and one night. If the woman whose husband died was pregnant, then her waiting period is until she gives birth, according to most scholars from the Companions and those who came after them. It was narrated from Ali and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, that she waits for the last of the two periods of giving birth, or four months and ten. Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: The shorter Surah An-Nisa was revealed after the longer one, meaning by the shorter Surah al-Talaq 65:And for those who are pregnant, their period is until they give birth 4-At-Talaq. It was revealed after the Almighty’s saying: They shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten in Surah Al-Baqarah, so he interpreted it as abrogation. Most of the jurists specified the verse with the hadith of Subay’ah, which is what Abu Al-Hasan Al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir bin Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq Al-Hashemi informed us, Abu Musab informed us, Malik informed us, Hisham bin Urwah informed us, his father informed us, Al-Miswar bin Makhramah informed us that Subay’ah gave birth after the death of her husband by nights, so she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked his permission to marry, so he gave her permission. I got married. The Almighty said: And when they have fulfilled their term meaning their waiting period has expired there is no blame upon you addressing the guardians for what they do with themselves meaning of choosing husbands other than the contract, for the contract is up to the guardian, and it was said that what they did of adorning themselves for men is an adornment that the Shari’ah does not denounce in a just manner, and God is aware of what you do. And mourning is obligatory for the woman during the waiting period of death, as for the woman observing the waiting period after a divorce, it is considered that if it was a revocable divorce, then there is no mourning for her during the waiting period because she has the right to do what will make the husband’s heart yearn for her to take her back, and regarding the irrevocable divorce by khul’ and the three divorces, there are two opinions: One of them: She must mourn like the woman whose husband died, and this is the opinion of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Abu Hanifa said the same, and the second: She does not have mourning, and this is the opinion of Ata’, and Malik said the same.
2:235: 235. The Almighty said: And there is no blame upon you for that which you insinuate of marriage to women meaning women in their waiting period. The origin of insinuation is to hint at something, and insinuation in speech is that by which the listener understands what is meant without stating it explicitly. Insinuation of marriage is permissible during the waiting period, and it is for him to say: O Lord, there is someone who desires you, who can find someone like you, you are beautiful, you are righteous, you are generous to me, I desire you, and it is my goal to marry, and if God brings us together in a lawful manner, I will like you, and if I marry you, I will treat you well, and similar words without saying marry me, and the woman responds to him with the same if she desires it. Ibrahim said: There is nothing wrong with him giving her gifts and taking care of her during the waiting period if that is his concern. It was narrated that Sakina bint Hanzala was separated from her husband, so Abu Ja`far Muhammad bin `Ali al-Baqir entered upon her during her waiting period and said: O daughter of Hanzala, I am one of those whose kinship to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) is known, and the right of my grandfather over me and my precedence in Islam. Sakina said: Do you propose to me while I am in my waiting period and knowledge is taken from you? He said: I only told you about my kinship to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) entered upon Umm Salamah while she was in the waiting period of her husband Abu Salamah, and he mentioned to her his status with God the Almighty, and he was straining his hand until the mark of the mat was on his hand from the intensity of his straining on his hand. It is permissible to propose to her in the waiting period of death. As for the woman in waiting period due to separation from her husband, there is a view: If she is someone from whom it is not permissible to marry her, such as a woman who has been divorced three times or someone who has been separated by cursing or breastfeeding, then it is permissible to propose to her indirectly. If she is someone from whom it is permissible for the husband to marry, such as a woman who has been divorced by divorce or someone whose marriage has been annulled, then it is permissible to propose to her indirectly and explicitly. Is it permissible for others to propose to her? There are two opinions: One of them is that it is permissible, like a woman who has been divorced three times, and the second is that it is not permissible because repeating the marriage is established for the person who is in the waiting period, like a woman who has been divorced revocably, and it is not permissible for others to propose to her. And the Almighty’s saying: From the sermon of women The sermon is the request for marriage and it is the source of the man proposing to the woman, he propositions a sermon, and Al-Akhfash said: The sermon is the mention, and the sermon is the testimony, so its meaning is: in what you exposed to mentioning women in their presence, or you concealed you concealed in yourselves from marrying them, it is said: I concealed the thing and I concealed it, two languages, and Tha’lab said: I concealed the thing, meaning I hid it in my soul and I concealed it, and Al-Suddi said: It is that he enters and greets and guides if he wishes and does not speak about anything God knows that you will mention them in your hearts but do not make a secret promise to them They differed about the secret that is forbidden, so some people said: It is adultery, the man would enter upon the woman for the sake of adultery and he exposes marriage and says to her: Leave me, then when you fulfill your waiting period I will reveal your marriage, this is the saying of Al-Hasan, Qatada, Ibrahim, and Ata’ and the narration of Atiyyah from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, Zaid bin Aslam said: That is, he does not marry her secretly and keep her, so when It turned out that way. Mujahed said: It is the man saying: Do not deprive me of yourself, for I will marry you. Al-Sha’bi and Al-Suddi said: He does not take her covenant that she will not marry anyone else. Ikrimah said: He does not marry her or propose to her during her waiting period. Al-Shafi’i said: The secret is intercourse. Al-Kalbi said: That is, do not describe yourselves to them by having frequent intercourse, saying, I will bring you four or five and the like, and the secret is mentioned, meaning intercourse. Imru’ al-Qais said: Didn't you claim, with all your might, that I have grown old and that people like me do not keep secrets? Adultery and sexual intercourse are called secret because they take place in secret between a man and a woman. The Almighty’s saying: Unless you say a proper word is what we mentioned about the insinuation of the sermon. God Almighty says: And do not resolve to tie the marriage knot until the prescribed period has reached its term. That is, do not make the decision to tie the marriage knot during the waiting period until the prescribed period has reached its term, that is, until the waiting period has expired. God called it a prescribed because it is an obligation from God, as God Almighty says: It is prescribed for you, that is, it is imposed upon you. And know that God knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him, that is, fear God. And know that God is Forgiving and Forbearing, who does not hasten to punish.
2:236: 236. The Almighty’s saying: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them a dowry, meaning, and you have not touched them or specified for them a dowry, was revealed about a man from the Ansar who married a woman from Banu Hanifa and did not specify a dowry for her, then he divorced her before he had touched her, so this verse was revealed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Provide her with a gift, even if it is with your skullcap. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read ma lam tamasuhunna with an alif here and in Al-Ahzab on the basis of the mutual action because the body of each of them meets the body of the other as God Almighty said: before they touch each other 3-Al-Mujadilah. The rest read tamasuhunna without an alif because the intercourse is done by the man, as evidenced by the Almighty’s saying: and no man has touched me 47-Al Imran. The Almighty says: Or you impose on them a dowry. That is, you impose on them a dowry. If it is said, what is the reason for denying the blame on the divorced woman? It is said: Divorce cuts off the cause of the connection. It was mentioned in the hadith: The most hated of permissible things to God Almighty is divorce. And he denied the wing from it if separation is better than keeping it, and it was said that its meaning is that there is no way for women over you if you divorce them before touching and the obligation with a dowry or maintenance, and it was said: There is no blame upon you in divorcing them before touching at any time you wish, whether the woman is menstruating or pure because there is no Sunnah or innovation in divorcing them before consummation with her, unlike the one who has been consummated with, as it is not permissible to divorce her during her menstruation. And provide for them means give them from your wealth what they can enjoy, and the enjoyment and provision are what is provided for from provisions for the affluent meaning for the rich his ability and for the poor meaning for the poor his ability meaning his ability and capacity. Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Amir, Al-Kisa`i and Hafs read Qadar with the opening of the dal in both of them, and the others read with their sukoon, and they are two languages. It was said: Al-Qadar with the sukoon of the dal is the source and with the opening of the noun, Muta`an is the accusative of the source, meaning give them Muta`an in a fair manner meaning with what God has commanded you with without injustice a right upon the doers of good. And the explanation The ruling of the verse is that if a man marries a woman without specifying a dowry for her, then divorces her before intercourse, she is entitled to a temporary marriage, by consensus. But if he divorces her after specifying the dowry before intercourse, she is not entitled to a temporary marriage, according to the majority opinion, and she is entitled to half of the stipulated dowry. They differed regarding the woman who was divorced after consummation. A group held that she is not entitled to enjoyment because she is entitled to the dowry, which is the opinion of the people of opinion. A group held that she is entitled to enjoyment based on the Almighty’s saying, Divorced women shall have a provision according to what is acceptable. 241-Al-Baqarah. This is the opinion of Abdullah bin Omar, and this is what Ata, Mujahid, and Al-Qasim bin Muhammad said. Al-Shafi’i held this opinion because her entitlement to the dowry is in exchange for what was lost to her from the benefit of intercourse, so she is entitled to enjoyment despite the loneliness of separation. According to the first opinion, there is no enjoyment except for one, which is the divorced woman before the obligation and touching. According to the second opinion, every divorced woman is entitled to enjoyment except for one, which is the divorced woman after the obligation before touching. Abdullah bin Omar said: Every divorced woman is entitled to enjoyment except for the one for whom the obligation was imposed and her husband did not touch her, so half the dowry is sufficient for her. Al-Zuhri said: There are two types of pleasures, one of which the ruler decides upon, but the other is not, but rather it is binding on him between him and God Almighty. As for what the ruler decides, it is the divorce before the obligation and touching, which is the Almighty’s saying: It is a duty upon the righteous. And what is binding upon him between him and God Almighty and the ruler does not decide, it is the divorce after touching, which is the Almighty’s saying: It is a duty upon the righteous. Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubair said that every divorced woman has a right to enjoyment, whether it was before the obligation and touching or after the obligation before touching, based on the Almighty’s saying: Divorced women shall have a right to enjoyment according to what is acceptable 241-Al-Baqarah and the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Ahzab 33:Then give them a provision and release them with good manners 49-Al-Ahzab. They said: The meaning of the Almighty’s saying: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them an obligation is or you have not specified for them an obligation. Some of them said: Enjoyment is not obligatory, and the command to do so is a matter of recommendation and desirability. It was narrated that a man divorced his wife after having consummated the marriage with her, so she took him to Shuraih regarding the temporary marriage. Shuraih said: Do not refuse to be among the righteous, and do not refuse to be among the pious. But he did not force him to do that. They differed on the amount of pleasure. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The highest of it is a servant, and the middle of it is three garments, a shield, a blanket, and a loincloth, and below that is a protection or something made of paper. Al-Sha’bi and Al-Zuhri said the same. This is the doctrine of Al-Shafi’i. He said: The highest of it for the wealthy is a servant, and the middle of it is a garment, and the least of it is the least of what has a price, and good is thirty dirhams. Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf divorced his wife and gave her a black slave girl, meaning he gave her pleasure. Al-Hasan bin Ali, may God be pleased with him, gave his wife pleasure with ten thousand dirhams, and she said: A small pleasure from a separated beloved. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said: If the spouses disagree, the amount is half the dowry of her peers, not to exceed it. The verse indicates that the husband’s situation is taken into consideration in terms of hardship and ease. Among the rulings of the verse is that whoever marries an adult woman with her consent without a dowry, the marriage is valid, and the woman has the right to demand that he set a dowry for her. If he consummates the marriage with her before the set dowry, then she is entitled to a dowry of her peers. If he divorces her before the set dowry and consummation, then she is entitled to a compensation. If one of them dies before the set dowry and consummation, the scholars differed as to whether she is entitled to a dowry or not. A group of people said that she has no dowry, which is the opinion of Ali, Zaid bin Thabit, Abdullah bin Omar, and Abdullah bin Abbas, as if he divorced her before the obligation and consummation. A group of people said that she has the dowry, because death is like consummation in establishing the specified dowry, and also in requiring the dowry of her peers if there is no specified dowry in the contract, which is the opinion of Al-Thawri and the people of opinion. They provided evidence for what was narrated on the authority of Alqamah on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he was asked about a man who married a woman and did not specify a dowry for her and did not consummate the marriage with her until he died. Ibn Masoud said: She has the dowry of her women, neither less nor more, and she must observe the waiting period and she has the inheritance. Then Maqal bin Sinan Al-Ashja’i stood up and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled in the case of Baru’ bint Washaq, a woman from us, as you ruled. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, was happy. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: If the hadith of Baru’ bint Washiq is proven, then there is no proof in the statement of anyone other than the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If it is not proven, then she has no dowry and she has the inheritance. Ali used to say: In the hadith of Baru’ there is the statement of an Arab from Ashja’ on the Book of God and the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
2:237: 237. The Almighty said: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry, then half of what you specified. This is for the woman who is divorced after the dowry before touching, so she is entitled to half of the specified dowry. If one of them dies before touching, then she is entitled to the full specified dowry. What is meant by touching mentioned in the verse is intercourse. The scholars differed as to whether a man is alone with his wife and then divorces her before consummating the marriage with her. Some people said that she is only entitled to half of the dowry, and she does not have to observe a waiting period because God Almighty made half of the dowry obligatory with the divorce before touching, and did not make a waiting period obligatory. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and Ibn Masoud, and this is what Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said. Some people said: She is entitled to the full dowry, and she must observe the waiting period, based on what was narrated on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, that he said: If the curtains are lowered, then the dowry is due. The same was narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit. Some of them interpreted Umar’s statement as meaning that the dowry must be given to her if she surrenders herself, not as an estimate of the dowry. It was said that this verse abrogates the verse in Surat al-Ahzab 33:So you have no waiting period for them to count, so provide for them 49-al-Ahzab. The divorced woman before intercourse had a provision, but this verse abrogated it. The divorced woman who had a dowry before intercourse was entitled to half of the provision, and she has no provision. And the Almighty’s saying: And you have already prescribed for them a dowry, meaning you have named for them a dowry. Then half of what you have prescribed, meaning half of the named dowry, unless they relinquish it, meaning the women, meaning unless the woman gives up her share, in which case the entire dowry returns to the husband. God the Almighty said: Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives They differed about it: Some of them went to the one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the guardian, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said this, meaning: unless the woman forgives by leaving her share to the husband if she is a widow and is eligible for forgiveness, or her guardian forgives and leaves her share if the woman is a virgin or not eligible for the matter, then the forgiveness of her guardian is permissible, and this is the saying of Alqamah, Ata, Al-Hasan, Al-Zuhri, and Rabi’ah. Some of them went to the fact that the forgiveness of the guardian is only permissible if the woman is a virgin or a widow, then the forgiveness of her guardian is not permissible. Some of them said: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the husband, and this is the saying of Ali, and this is what Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Sha’bi, Shuraih, Mujahid, and Qatadah said, and they said: It is not permissible for her guardian to leave anything from the dowry, whether she is a virgin or a widow, just as it is not permissible for him to do so before the divorce by consensus, and just as it is not permissible for him to give away anything from her money, and they said: The meaning of the verse is unless the woman forgives by leaving her share, then all of the dowry returns to The husband or the husband forgives by leaving his share, so she gets the entire dowry. According to this interpretation, the meaning of the verse is: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the marriage of himself in every case before or after divorce. And to forgive is closer to righteousness. Its position is raised by the beginning, meaning forgiveness is closer to righteousness, meaning to righteousness, and the address is to both men and women because if the masculine and feminine come together, the masculine is more likely to prevail. Its meaning is: And your forgiveness of one another is closer to righteousness. And do not forget graciousness between you. That is, the graciousness of some of you to one another by giving the man the entire dowry or the woman leaving her share, urging them both to do good. Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do.
2:238: 238. God the Almighty said: Guard the prayers, and the middle prayer meaning, be constant and persistent in the prescribed prayers with their times and limits and complete their pillars. Then He singled out the middle prayer from among them by preserving it, indicating its virtue. The middle is the feminine of the middle, and the middle of something is its best and most just. The scholars from the Companions and those who came after them differed regarding the middle prayer. Some said: It is the dawn prayer, and this is the opinion of Umar, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Muadh, and Jabir. Ata, Ikrimah, and Mujahid said the same, and Malik and Al-Shafi’i tended towards it, because God the Almighty said: And stand before God, devoutly obedient and qunut is a long standing, and the dawn prayer is distinguished by a long standing and qunut because God the Almighty singled it out in another verse from among the prayers, as God the Almighty said: “And the recitation of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is witnessed” 78-Al-Isra, meaning that the angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it, so it is written in the register of the night and the register of the day, and because it is between two prayers of combining and it is not shortened or combined with others. Some people said that it is the noon prayer, which is the opinion of Zaid bin Thabit, Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, and Usama bin Zaid, because it is in the middle of the day and it is the middle prayer of the day in length. Umar ibn Abdul Aziz told us, Abu al-Qasim ibn Ja`far al-Hashemi told us, Abu Ali al-Lulu`i told us, Abu Dawud told us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, Amr ibn Abi Hakim told us: I heard al-Zubayr narrating on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer at noon, and he did not pray a prayer that was more difficult for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, than it. Then this verse was revealed: Guard strictly the prayers, and especially the middle prayer. Most of them said that it is the afternoon prayer. It was narrated by a group of people on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is the opinion of Ali, Abdullah bin Masoud, Abu Ayoub, Abu Hurairah, and Aisha, may God be pleased with them. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Qatada, and al-Hasan said the same. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of al-Qa`qa` ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Yunus, the freed slave of `Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: `Aisha ordered me to write a copy of the Qur’an for her and said: When you reach this verse, notify me: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer. So when I reached it, I notified her and she dictated to me: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer the `Asr prayer And stand before God, devoutly obedient. `Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from Hafsa something similar. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abu Na’im told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim bin Al-Najoud, on the authority of Zur bin Jahsh, who said: We said to Ubaidah, ask Ali about the middle prayer, so he asked him and he said: We used to think that it was the dawn prayer until I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the day of the Trench: “They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May God fill their bellies and graves with fire.” And because it is my prayer during the day and my prayer at night, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, singled it out for emphasis. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Al-Malhi, who said: We were with Buraydah in a raid on a cloudy day, so he said: Perform the afternoon prayer early, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever neglects the afternoon prayer, his deeds have been nullified. Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb said: It is the Maghrib prayer because it is in the middle, not the least or the most. It was not transmitted from any of the predecessors that it is the Isha prayer, but some of the later scholars mentioned it because it is between two prayers that cannot be shortened. Some of them said that it is one of the five prayers, not specifically. God Almighty made it ambiguous to encourage the servants to maintain the performance of all of them, just as He concealed the Night of Decree in the month of Ramadan and the hour of answering supplications on Friday, and He concealed the Greatest Name among the names so that they would maintain all of them. God Almighty says: And stand before God, devoutly obedient. That is, obedient. Al-Sha’bi, Ata’, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Tawus said: Qunut means obedience. God Almighty said: A nation devoutly obedient 120-An-Nahl, that is, obedient. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Every religious person has a prayer in which they perform it disobediently, so you stand for God in your prayer obediently. It was said that Qunut is silence about what is not permissible to speak about in prayer. Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi, on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi, on the authority of Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Ahmad bin Mani’, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Shabil, on the authority of Abu Amr Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, who said: We used to talk behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during prayer, and one of us would talk to the one next to him until the verse And stand before God, devoutly obedient was revealed, and we were commanded to be silent and forbidden from speaking. Mujahid said: Humble. He said: “From Qunut is prolonged bowing, lowering the gaze, squatting, and lowering the wing. When one of the scholars stood up to pray, he would fear the Most Merciful, not turning around, turning over pebbles, playing with something, or thinking about something worldly, except forgetfully.” It was said: What is meant by Qunut is prolonged standing. Abu Uthman al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi told us, Ibn Abi Umar told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked, ‘Which prayer is best? ’ He said, ‘Long supplication. ’ It was also said, ‘Qatainin,’ meaning supplicating.” His evidence is what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed qunut for a month in a row, calling down curses on the living, such as Sulaym, Ra’l, Dhakwan, and Asiyah. It was said that its meaning is praying, based on the Almighty’s saying: Is he who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night? 9-Az-Zumar, meaning praying.
2:239: 239. The Almighty said: But if you fear, then on foot on foot meaning on foot. It is said: a footman and men like a companion and companions and standing and standing and sleeping and sleeping or riding on their mounts, which is the plural of rider, meaning if you are not able to pray devoutly and fulfill the prayer due to fear, then pray on foot or riding on the backs of your mounts. This is in the case of fighting and fencing. He prays wherever his face is, on foot or riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it, and he nods in bowing and prostration and makes prostration lower than bowing. Likewise, if a wild animal intends to attack him or a flood overtakes him and he fears for his life, then running in front of him praying by nodding is permissible. Prayer in a state of fear is divided into sections. This is the prayer of intense fear, and the rest of the sections will be explained in Surat An-Nisa, God willing. The number of rak’ahs is not reduced by fear according to most scholars. Mujahid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: God enjoined prayer on the tongue of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when at home, four rak’ahs, when traveling, two rak’ahs, and when fearing, one rak’ah. This is the opinion of Ata’, Tawus, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatadah: that one should pray one rak’ah in a state of intense fear. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: If you are in combat and people are striking each other, then say: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest, and remember God, for that is your prayer. “And when you are secure, then remember God,” meaning pray the five daily prayers in full with their rights, as He has taught you what you did not know.
2:240: 240. God the Almighty said: And those of you who die “O assembly of men” and leave behind “wives” a bequest for their wives The people of Basra, Ibn Amir, Hamza and Hafs read wasiyyah in the accusative case, meaning let them make a bequest. The rest read it in the nominative case, meaning the bequest was prescribed for you. Provisions for a year “Provisions” is accusative as a source, meaning provide for them with provision. It was said: God made that for them provision, and provision is a year’s expenses for her food, clothing, housing and whatever she needs. Except for giving out is accusative as a state. It was said that a letter was removed as a description, meaning without giving out. This verse was revealed about a man from the people of Taif called Hakim bin Al-Harith who migrated to Madinah and had children, along with his parents and wife. Then he died, so God revealed this verse and gave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his parents and children from his inheritance, but did not give his wife anything. He ordered them to spend on her from her husband’s estate for a full year. The waiting period for death was at the beginning of Islam. A year, and it was forbidden for the heir to expel her from the house before the year was complete, and her expenses and housing were obligatory from her husband’s money for that year unless she left, and she was not entitled to inheritance. If she left her husband’s house, her expenses were dropped, and the man had to bequeath them, and this was the case until the verse of inheritance was revealed, and God Almighty abrogated the expenses of the year with a quarter and an eighth, and abrogated the waiting period of the year with four months and ten. God Almighty says: But if they go out meaning of their own accord before the year has passed without expelling the heirs, there is no blame upon you O guardians of the deceased, for what they do with themselves of honor meaning adorning themselves for marriage. And the lifting of blame from men has two aspects: One of them: There is no blame upon you in cutting off the maintenance if they go out before the year has passed. The other: There is no blame upon you for not preventing them from going out, because her staying in her husband’s house for a year is not obligatory upon her. God Almighty gave her the choice between staying for a year and receiving maintenance and housing, or going out and receiving neither maintenance nor housing, until He abrogated it by four months and ten days. And God is Almighty and Wise
2:241: 241. And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous. He only repeated the mention of enjoyment here to add meaning, because in other verses the ruling on the untouched is explained, and in this verse the ruling on all divorced women in enjoyment is explained. It was said that when the words of God Almighty were revealed: And give them provision according to the means of the wealthy and according to the means of the poor to His words A duty upon the doers of good 236-Al-Baqarah, a Muslim man said: If I did well, I did it, and if I did not intend that, I would not have done it. So God Almighty said: And for divorced women is a provision He made enjoyment for them with the letter of ownership, so He said: A duty upon the righteous meaning the believers who fear polytheism.
2:242: 242. Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may understand.
2:243: 243. The Almighty said: Have you not considered those who left their homes? Most of the commentators said: There was a village called Dawurdan before Wasit, where the plague broke out, so a group of them left and a group remained, so most of those who remained in the village perished, and those who left were saved. When the plague was lifted, they returned safe and sound. Those who remained said: Our companions were wiser than us. If we had done as they did, we would have survived. If the plague breaks out again, we will leave for a land where there is no epidemic. So the plague broke out the next year, so most of its people fled and left until they descended into a fertile valley. When they descended to the place where they sought safety, an angel called out to them from the bottom of the valley and another from the top: Die. So they all died. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi`ah, that `Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, went out to the Levant. When he arrived, he was hurried to hear that the plague had broken out in the Levant. `Abd al-Rahman ibn `Awf told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If you hear of it in a land, do not go there. But if it breaks out in a land where you are, do not leave fleeing from it.” So `Umar returned from Sargh. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and al-Dahhak said: They fled from jihad because a king of the kings of the Children of Israel ordered them to go out to fight their enemy. They camped, then they became cowardly and hated death, so they became ill and said to their king: The land that the plague comes to, we will not go to it until the plague stops there. So God sent death upon them, so they left their homes fleeing from death. When the king saw that, he said: O God, Lord of Jacob and God of Moses, You see the disobedience of Your servants, so show them a sign in themselves so that they know that they cannot flee. From you, so when they went out, God Almighty said to them: Die, as a punishment for them, so they all died and their animals died as one man died, and eight days passed until they swelled up and their bodies became soft, so the people went out to them and were unable to bury them, so they forbade them to a pen away from the wild beasts and left them in it. They differed about the amount of their number. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: They were three thousand. Wahb said: Four thousand. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: Eight thousand. Abu Ruq said: Ten thousand. Al-Suddi said: Thirty-some thousand. Ibn Jurayj said: Forty thousand. Ata’ ibn Rabah said: Seventy thousand. The first of the sayings is the saying of the one who said they were more than ten thousand, because God Almighty said: And they are thousands. Thousands is the plural of many and the plural of few is thousands. What is less than ten thousand is not called thousands. They said: So it came to that. So God revived them. It was said: Ezekiel called upon his Lord to revive them, and He revived them. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: They were the people of Ezekiel, whom God revived after eight days. When that happened to them, Ezekiel went out in search of them and found them dead, dead. He cried and said: O Lord, I was among a people who praised You, glorified You, sanctified You, magnified You, and extolled You, and I was left alone, with no people. Then God Almighty revealed to him: I have given their life to you. Ezekiel said: Revive them by God’s permission, and they lived. Mujahid said: When they were revived, they said: Glory be to You, O God, our Lord, and praise be to You. There is no god but You. So they returned to their people and lived a long time with the appearance of death on their faces. They did not wear a garment except that it became greasy like a shroud until they died at the appointed times that were written for them. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: And today that wind is found in that tribe of the Jews. Qatada said: God hated them for fleeing from death, so He killed them as a punishment for them, then they were resurrected to complete their appointed terms. [And if their appointed terms had come] they would not have been resurrected. That is what God Almighty said: Have you not seen? meaning, have you not known that I have informed you, and it is from seeing the heart. The scholars of meaning said: It is an expression of astonishment, saying: Have you seen the likes of them? Just as you say: Have you not seen what so-and-so does? And everything in the Qur’an, or have you seen it, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not witness it, this is its direction. To those who left their homes, and they were thousands. The plural of alif. It was said that mu’ta’tufquhu quluhu is the plural of alif like qa’id and qa’ud. The correct view is that what is meant by it is the number. Warn of death. That is, fear of death. So God said to them, ‘Die.’ is a command to change, like His saying: Be apes, despised. 65-Al-Baqarah. Then He brought them back to life. After their death. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind. It was said that it is general in the right of all in this world, and it was said that it is specific in the right of the believers. But most people do not give thanks. As for the disbelievers, they did not give thanks, and as for the believers, they did not reach the pinnacle of thanks.
2:244: 244. And fight in the way of God meaning in obedience to God against the enemies of God and know that God is Hearing and Knowing. Most of the commentators said: This is addressed to those who were brought back to life and were ordered to fight in the way of God, so they left their homes fleeing from jihad, so God caused them to die, then brought them back to life and ordered them to fight jihad. It was said: The address is to this nation, He ordered them to fight jihad.
2:245: 245. The Almighty’s saying: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? A loan is the name for everything that a person gives in order to be rewarded for it. So God the Almighty called the work of the believers for Him in the hope of the reward He promised them a loan, because they do it to seek His reward. Al-Kisa’i said: A loan is what you have advanced of good or bad deeds. The root of the word loan in the language is to cut off. It is the name given to the servants of God and the needy among His creation, as in the saying of God the Almighty: Indeed, those who harm God and His Messenger 57-Al-Ahzab, meaning they harm the servants of God, as came in the authentic hadith on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said that the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “God the Almighty will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:O son of Adam, I asked you for food and you did not feed Me. He said: O Lord, how could I feed You when You are the Lord of the worlds? He will say: My servant so-and-so asked you for food and you did not feed him. Did you not know that if you had fed him you would have found that with Me?” God the Almighty said: He lends to God meaning he spends in the obedience of God a good loan. Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Waqidi said: meaning he is rewarded, his soul is content with it. Ibn al-Mubarak said: from lawful money. It was also said that he does not show off or harm. He multiplies it for him. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Amir, and Ya`qub read He multiplies it for him with the shaddah. Abu `Amr agreed with him in Surat al-Ahzab. The others read He multiplies it with the alif and with a lightened s. They are two dialects. The evidence for the shaddah is his statement many times. Because the shaddah is for multiplication, Ibn `Amir, `Asim, and Ya`qub read with the accusative of the fa, and likewise in Surat al-Hadid in response to the question. It was also said that it was implied that. The others read with the nominative of the fa in accordance with his statement: He lends many times. Al-Suddi said that only God the Almighty knows this doubling. It was also said that it is seven hundred times. And God contracts and expands. The people of Basra and Jamzah read yabsut, here and in al-A`raf, basatah, with the sin. Like their counterparts, and others read them with a sad. It was said that it is seized by withholding sustenance and the soul and stinginess and is expanded by expansion. It was said that it is seized by accepting repentance and charity and is expanded by replacement and reward. It was said that it is life and death, so whoever He kills, He has seized him and whoever He extends his life, He has expanded it for him. It was said that this is in the hearts, when God Almighty commanded them to give charity, He informed that they cannot do that except with His guidance. He said: He seizes some hearts so they are not active in goodness and He expands some of them so they present goodness for themselves as came in the hadith, The hearts are between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, He turns them as He wills. The hadith. And to Him you will return, meaning you will return to God, and He will reward you for your deeds. Qatada said: The ha refers to the dust, as a metaphor for something not mentioned, meaning He created them from the dust and to Him they will return.
2:246: 246. God the Almighty said: Have you not seen the assembly of the Children of Israel? The assembly of people is their leaders and notables. The origin of the assembly is a group of people, and it has no singular form, like the people, the group, the tribe, the horses, and the jinn, and its plural is amlaa’. “After Moses” means after the death of Moses. When they said to a prophet of theirs. They differed about that prophet. Qatada said that he was Joshua bin Nun bin Ephraim bin Joseph, peace be upon him. Al-Suddi said: His name was Simeon, and he was named Simeon because a nation prayed to God to grant them a boy, and God answered their prayer and they gave birth to a boy, so they named him Simeon, saying God the Almighty heard my prayer, and the sin becomes a thing in Hebrew. He is Simeon bin Safiyyah bin Alqamah from the descendants of Levi bin Jacob. The rest of the commentators said: He is Ishmael, which in Hebrew is Ishmael bin Yal bin Alqamah. Muqatil said: He is from the descendants of Aaron. Mujahid said: He is Ishmael, which in Hebrew is Ishmael bin Yal bin Alqamah. Wahb, Ibn Ishaq, Al-Kalbi and others said: The reason for their questioning him was that when Moses, peace be upon him, died, he left behind him among the Children of Israel Joshua bin Nun, who established the Torah and the command of God Almighty among them until God Almighty took him. Then he left behind Caleb among them likewise until God Almighty took him. Then he left behind Ezekiel until God took him. Then the events among the Children of Israel became serious and they forgot God’s covenant until they worshipped idols. Then God sent Elijah to them as a prophet who called them to God Almighty. The prophets among the Children of Israel after Moses were sent to them to renew what they had forgotten of the Torah. Then after Elijah, Elisha was left behind and he was among them as God willed, then God took him and left behind successors and the sins became serious. Then an enemy appeared to them called the Belshatha, and they were the people of Goliath who lived on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea between Egypt and Palestine. They were the Amalekites. They defeated the Children of Israel and conquered much of their land and took many of their children captive and captured from the sons of their kings forty-four hundred young men, so they imposed the jizya on them. They took their Torah, and the Children of Israel suffered from them a calamity and hardship, and they had no prophet to manage their affairs. The tribe of prophecy had perished, and none remained of them except a pregnant woman, so they imprisoned her in a house for fear that she would give birth to a slave girl and exchange her for a boy, because they saw the desire of the Children of Israel for her child. The woman began to pray to God to grant her a boy, and she gave birth to a boy, and she named him Samuel, saying: God Almighty heard my prayer. The boy grew up, so she handed him over to learn the Torah in Jerusalem, and an old man from among their scholars took care of him and adopted him. When the boy reached puberty, Gabriel came to him while he was sleeping next to the old man, and no one could trust him, so Gabriel called him in the old man’s tone, O Samuel. The boy got up in a panic and went to the old man and said to him: Father, did you call me? The old man did not want to say No and startle the boy, so he said: My son, go back and sleep. The boy went back and slept, then he called him a second time, and the boy said: Father, did you call me? Then he said: Go back and sleep, for if I call you a third time, do not answer me. So the boy went back and slept. When it was the third time, Gabriel appeared to him and said: Go to your people and convey to them the message of your Lord, for God Almighty has sent you among them as a prophet. When he came to them, they denied him and said: You hastened to become a prophet and did not attain it. They said to him: If you are truthful, then send us a king so that we may fight in the way of God, as a sign of your prophethood. The basis of the matter of the Children of Israel was to unite around kings and for the kings to obey their prophets. So the king was the one who led the crowds, and the prophet would establish his affairs and advise him on the right path and bring him report from his Lord. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: God Almighty sent Samuel as a prophet, and they remained forty years in the best state. Then what happened to Goliath and the Amalekites happened, so they said to Samuel: Send us a king so that we may fight in the way of God. He was decisive in answering the command. So when they said that, he said: Will you? A question of doubt. Nafi’ read: ‘Asyatum with a kasra on the seen in the entire Qur’an, and the rest read it with a fatha, which is the eloquent language, as evidenced by the Almighty’s saying: Perhaps your Lord “if He has decreed” has imposed upon you fighting “with that king” that you do not fight “that you do not fulfill what you say with him” “They said: And what is the reason for the introduction of ‘an’ in this place, and the Arabs do not say ‘you are not worthy of doing’, but rather they say ‘you are not worthy of doing’”? It was said: The inclusion of an and its deletion are two correct languages. The affirmation is like the saying of the Most High: What is the matter with you that you are not with those who prostrate? 32-Al-Hijr and the deletion is like the saying of the Most High: What is the matter with you that you do not believe in God? 8-Al-Hadid. Al-Kisa’i said: Its meaning is: What is the matter with us that we do not fight? So he deleted fi. Al-Farra’ said: That is, what prevents us from not fighting in the way of God, like the saying of the Most High: What prevented you from prostrating? 12-Al-A’raf. Al-Akhfash said: An here is redundant and its meaning is: What is the matter with us that we do not fight in the way of God? And we have been expelled from our homes and our children meaning those who were defeated were expelled from their homes. The apparent meaning of the statement is generality and its hidden meaning is specificity, because those who said to their prophet: Send us a king so we can fight in the way of God were in their homes and homelands, and only those who were captured were expelled. The meaning of the verse is that they said in response to their prophet: We were only reluctant to fight because we were forbidden in our lands and our enemy would not prevail over us. As for If we reach this point, we will obey our Lord in jihad and protect our women and children. God Almighty said: But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, they turned away from jihad and neglected God’s command, except a few of them, and they are those who crossed the river with Talut and confined themselves to the room, as will come, God Almighty willing, and God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
2:247: 247. And their prophet said to them, ‘Indeed, God has sent you Saul as a king.’ That is because Samuel asked God to send them a king, so he brought a staff and a horn with holy oil in it. It was said to him, “Your master who will be king is as tall as this staff. Look at this horn with the oil in it. If a man enters upon you and the oil in the horn comes out, he is the king of the Children of Israel. So anoint his head with it and make him king over them.” Saul’s name in Hebrew was Saul bin Qais, from the sons of Benjamin bin Jacob. He was called Saul because of his height, and he was taller than anyone else in his head and shoulders. He was a tanner who worked on leather, as Wahb said. Al-Suddi said, He was a water-carrier who used to water his donkey from the Nile, which his donkey had left over, so he went out in search of him. It was said that he was a thief. Wahb said, “Rather, the donkeys of Taul’s father went astray, so he sent him and a slave of his to search for them. He passed by the house of Samuel, and the slave said to Taul, “If we went to this prophet and asked him about the matter of the donkeys, so he would guide us and pray for us.” So they went to him. While they were with him, mentioning to him the matter of the donkeys, the oil in the horn grew thick. Samuel, peace be upon him, stood up and measured Talut with a staff, and it was his height. He said to Talut, Bring your head near. So he brought it near and anointed it with the oil of holiness, then said to him, You are the king of the Children of Israel whom God Almighty has commanded me to make king over them. Talut said, Do you not know that my tribe is the lowest of the tribes of the Children of Israel and my house is the lowest of the houses of the Children of Israel? He said, Yes. He said, Then by what sign? He said, By the sign that you will return and your father has found a donkey. And it was so. Then he said to the Children of Israel: Indeed, God has sent you Saul as a king. They said: How can he have kingship over us? That is, how can he have kingship over us? And we are more deserving of kingship than he. They only said that because there were two tribes among the Children of Israel: a tribe of prophecy and a tribe of kingdom. The tribe of prophecy was the tribe of Levi, son of Jacob, from whom came Moses and Aaron, and the tribe of Benjamin, son of Jacob. They had committed a great sin; they used to have intercourse with women on the road during the day, so God, the Most High, became angry with them and took away the kingship and prophethood from them. They used to call him the tribe of sin. When their prophet told them that, they denounced him because he was not from the tribe of kingdom. Despite that, they said he was poor and had not been given an abundance of wealth. He said: God chose him over you and increased him abundantly in knowledge and body. This is because he was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel at his time. It was said that the revelation came to him when he was given kingship. Al-Kalbi said: And increased him abundantly in knowledge of war and in body in height, and it was said that body was in beauty. And Talut was the most handsome man among the Children of Israel and the most knowledgeable of them. And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing. It was said that the All-Encompassing is the One who has plenty, and that the All-Knowing is the Knowing, and it was said that the Knowing is the Knowing of what was and the Knowing of what will be. So they said to him: What is the sign of his kingdom? So their prophet said to them: The sign of his kingdom is that the Ark will come to you.
2:248: 248. This is what God Almighty said: And their prophet said to them, ‘The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you.’ The story of the Ark was that God Almighty sent down an Ark to Adam in which there was an image of the prophets, peace be upon them. It was made of aloes wood, about three cubits by two cubits. It was with Adam until he died, then after that with Seth, then the children of Adam inherited it until it reached Abraham, then it was with Ishmael because he was his eldest son, then with Jacob, then it was with the Children of Israel until it reached Moses. Moses would put the Torah and some of his belongings in it, so it was with him until Moses, peace be upon him, died. Then the prophets of the Children of Israel passed it on until the time of Samuel, and in it was mentioned God Almighty: Therein is tranquility from your Lord. They differed about what tranquility is. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: It is a violent, blowing wind with two heads and a face like a human face. Mujahid said: It is something resembling a cat with a head like a cat’s head and a tail like a cat’s tail and it has two wings. It was said that it had two eyes with rays and two wings of emerald and chrysolite. So when they heard its voice, they were certain of victory. And when they went out, they would put the Ark. In front of them, if he walks, they walk, and if he stops, they stop. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: It is a golden basin from Paradise in which the hearts of the prophets were washed. On the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, he said: It is a spirit from God that speaks when they disagree about something, informing them of what they want. Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: It is what they know of the signs and they find peace in it. Qatada and Al-Kalbi said: Sakinah is an active participle from sukoon, meaning peace from your Lord, so wherever the Ark was, they found peace in it and found peace. And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, meaning Moses and Aaron themselves. In it were two tablets of the Torah and fragments of the tablets that were broken. In it was Moses’ staff, his sandals, Aaron’s turban, his staff, and a bushel of manna that was sent down to the Children of Israel. So the Ark was with the Children of Israel, and if they disagreed about something, he would speak and judge between them, and if they attended to battle, they would present it before them so that they could gain victory over their enemy. But when they disobeyed and became corrupt, God sent the Amalekites against them, and they overcame them with the Ark. The reason for this was that Eli, the scholar who raised Samuel, peace be upon him, had two young sons. Eli was their priest and the one who handled their offerings. His two sons did something to the offering that was not in it. This was because Eli had two hooks attached to the offering that they tied to it. Whatever they took out was for the priest who tied it. So his two sons made hooks. The women prayed in the Holy House and held on to them. So God Almighty inspired them. So God Almighty inspired Samuel, peace be upon him, to go to Eli and say to him: The love of children prevented you from restraining your two sons from changing my offerings and my sanctuary and from disobeying me. So I will take away the priesthood from you and your children and I will destroy you and them. So Ishmael informed Eli of this and he was very frightened. An enemy from around them went to them, so he ordered his two sons to go out and fight that enemy. So they went out and brought out the ark with them. When they prepared to fight, Eli began to anticipate the report of what they had done. Then a man came to him while he was sitting on his chair. And he told him that the people had been defeated and that your two sons had been killed. He said, What happened to the Ark? He said, "The enemy took it, and he gasped and fell on his back from his chair and died. So the affair of the Children of Israel was confused and they dispersed until God sent Saul as king. They asked him for proof, and their prophet said to them, 'The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you.'" The story of the Ark was that those who had taken the Ark captive brought it to a village in Palestine called Azdud and placed it in the house of an idol of theirs, and placed it under the greatest idol. The next morning they saw the idol under it, so they took it and placed it on top of it and nailed the feet of the idol to the Ark. They saw that the hand and feet of the idol had been cut off and it was lying under the Ark and their idols were upside down.
