They took it out of the house of the idol and placed it in a part of their city. The people of that part suffered from pain in their necks until most of them died. Some of them said to each other: Did you not know that the God of the Children of Israel cannot be resisted by anything? They took it out to such-and-such a village. Then God sent a mouse to the people of that village. The mouse would spend the night with the man and he would wake up dead, having eaten what was in his stomach. They took him out to the desert and buried him in a dunghill of theirs. Everyone who came out there would suffer from hemorrhoids and colic, so they were perplexed. A woman who was with them from the captives of the Children of Israel from the sons of the prophets said to them: You will not cease to see what you hate as long as this is the case. The Ark is among you, so take it out from you. So they brought a cart at the sign of that woman and loaded the Ark on it, then hung it on two bulls and struck their sides. The two bulls came walking and God Almighty assigned four angels to drive them. They came until they stopped at the land of the Children of Israel. They broke their yoke and ropes and placed the Ark in a land where the harvest of the Children of Israel was and returned to their land. The Children of Israel were not frightened except by the Ark, so they glorified and praised God. This is what God Almighty said: The angels carry it, meaning they drive it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The angels came with the Ark, carrying it between heaven and earth while they were looking at it until they placed it with Talut. Al-Hasan said: The Ark was with the angels in heaven, then when Talut assumed the kingdom, the angels carried it and placed it among them. Qatada said: Rather, the Ark was in the wilderness behind Moses with Joshua bin Nun, so it remained there and the angels carried it until they placed it in the house of Talut, so they acknowledged his kingdom. Indeed in that is a sign. As a lesson for you, if you are believers, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Ark and Moses’ staff are in Lake Tiberias and they will come out before the Day of Resurrection.
2:249: 249. So when Talut set out with the soldiers meaning he went out with them. The root of separation is to cut off, meaning to cut off his place of residence and head to another. So Talut set out from Jerusalem with the soldiers, and they were that day seventy thousand fighters, and it was said: eighty thousand. No one stayed behind except an old man due to his old age, or a sick person due to his illness, or an excused person due to his excuse. This is because when they saw the Ark, they did not complain about the victory, so they hastened to jihad. So Talut said: I have no need for everything I see. No man who has built a building that he has not finished should go out with me, nor a businessman who works in it, nor a man who has married a woman and has not built with her, nor do I seek except the active, free youth. So eighty thousand of those he had appointed gathered for him, and it was in intense heat. They complained about the lack of water between them and their enemy, so they said: The water is scarce and cannot carry us, so pray to God to make a river flow for us. He said Talut God will test you your test to see your obedience - and He knows best - with a river Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi said: It is the river of Palestine, and Qatada said: A fresh river between the Jordan and Palestine So whoever drinks from it is not of me meaning he is not of the people of my religion and obedience And whoever does not taste it does not drink it then he is of me except for he who scoops a handful with his hand The people of Hijaz and Abu Amr read (ghurfa) with the fatha on the ghain and the others read it with the damma on the ghain and they are two dialects, Al-Kisa'i said: The ghurfa with the damma is what is obtained in the hand from water when scooped, and the ghurfa: with the fatha is scooping so the damma is a noun and the fatha is a source So they drank from it except a few of them accusative of exception and they differed about the few who did not drink, so Al-Suddi said: They were four thousand and others said: Three hundred and a few and this is correct. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abdullah bin Raja, I told Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: We, the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say that the number of the companions of Badr was the same as the number of the companions of Talut, who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except a few hundred and three hundred believers. It is narrated that three hundred and thirteen of them came and when they reached the river, thirst had overwhelmed them, and everyone drank from it except for this small number. Whoever took a handful as God commanded, his heart was strengthened, his faith was sound, and he crossed the river safely, and that one handful was enough for him to drink, carry, and mount. As for those who drank and disobeyed God’s command, their lips turned black and thirst overcame them, so they were not quenched. They remained on the bank of the river and avoided meeting the enemy, so they did not cross and did not witness the conquest. It was said that they all crossed it, but only those who did not drink attended the battle. So when he crossed it meaning the river, he meaning Talut and those who believed with him meaning the few said, meaning those who drank and disobeyed the command of God and were people of doubt and hypocrisy, We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Al-Suddi said, So they deviated and did not cross it. Those who thought were certain that they would meet God said, and they are those who remained steadfast with Talut. How many a company is a group, which is a plural that has no singular in its wording and plural, and groups and groups in the nominative and groups in the accusative and genitive few have overcome a large company by God’s permission by His judgment and will and God is with the patient with victory and assistance.
2:250: 250. And when they came forth meaning Talut and his soldiers, meaning the believers for Goliath and his soldiers the Muslims. The meaning of came forth is that they became in the open ground, which is what appeared and was level. They said, 'Our Lord, pour upon us' send down and pour down patience and plant firmly our feet strengthen our hearts and give us victory over the disbelieving people.
2:251: 251. So they defeated them by God’s permission meaning by God’s knowledge and David killed Goliath and the description of his killing: The commentators said: He crossed the river with Talut among those who crossed Isha Abu Dawud with his thirteen sons and he was the youngest of them and he used to throw arrows. So he said to his father one day, O my father, I do not throw anything with my arrows except that I defeat it. He said, Be happy, my son, for God has put your provision in your arrows. Then he came to him another time and said, O my father, I entered among the mountains and found a crouching lion, so I mounted it and took hold of its ears but it did not frighten me. So he said, Be happy, my son, for this is good that God wants for you. Then he came to him another day and said, O my father, I walk among the mountains and glorify God, and there is not a mountain that does not glorify God with me. So he said, Be happy, my son, for this is good that God has given you. So Goliath sent to Talut to come to me or bring to me someone who will fight me. If he kills me, then my kingdom is yours, and if I kill him, then your kingdom is mine.” That upset Talut so he called out in his army, Whoever killed Goliath, marry my daughter and share my kingdom with him. The people feared Goliath, but no one answered him. So Talut asked their prophet to call upon God Almighty, so he called upon God for that, and a horn containing holy oil and an iron oven was brought to him. It was said that your companion who will kill Goliath is the one who will be put on this horn, and the oil will boil until it will smear his head with it and not run down his face, and it will be on his head like a crown, and it will enter this oven and fill it and not shake in it. So Talut called the Children of Israel and tested them, but none of them agreed with him. So God revealed to their prophet that among the sons of Isha is one by whom God will kill Goliath. So Talut called Isha and said: Show me your sons. So he brought out for him twelve men like pillars. He began to show them to the horn, but he did not see anything. So he said: Do you have any sons left besides them? He said: No. So the prophet said: O Lord, he claimed that he had no sons besides them. So he said: He lied. So the prophet said: My Lord has lied to you. So he said: God has spoken the truth, O Prophet of God. I have a young son called David, and I was ashamed for people to see him because of his short stature and insignificance. So I left him in The sheep were tending them while he was in such and such a valley. David was a short, sickly man with a yellowish complexion, blue and hairy. So Talut called him. It is said that Talut went out to him and found that the valley had flowed between him and the pen where he used to rest. He found him carrying two sheep, crossing the flood with them and not wading with them in the water. When he saw him, he said: This is him, no doubt. He is merciful to animals, so he is more merciful to people. So he called him and put the horn on his head and it flowed. Talut said: Would you like to kill Goliath and I will marry you to my daughter and make your ring part of my kingdom? He said: Yes. He said: Do you perceive anything in yourself that will strengthen you to kill him? He said: Yes, I am a shepherd and a lion or a tiger or a wolf comes and takes a sheep, so I go to it and open its jaws and cut it to the back of its neck, and return it to his army. Then David, peace be upon him, passed by another stone on his way and said: Carry me, for I am the stone of Moses with which he killed such-and-such a king. So he carried it in his saddlebag. Then he passed by another stone and said: Carry me, for I am your stone with which you will kill Goliath. So he put it in his saddlebag. When they lined up for battle and Goliath came forward and asked to duel, David volunteered to fight him, so Saul gave him a horse, a shield and weapons. So he put on the weapons and rode the horse and walked a short distance, then he turned back to the king and said: Those around him have become cowardly. So he came and stood before the king and said: What is the matter with you? He said: If God does not grant me victory, this weapon will be of no avail to me, so let me fight as I wish. He said: Do as you wish. He said: Yes. So David took his saddlebags, put them on, took the sling and went towards Goliath. Goliath was one of the strongest and most powerful men, and he defeated armies single-handedly. He had an egg containing three hundred pounds of iron. When he looked at David, fear was cast into his heart. He said to him: Will you come out to me? He said: Yes. Goliath was riding a piebald horse, fully armed. He said: Bring me the sling and the stone as a dog is brought. He said: Yes, you are worse than a dog. He said: I will surely divide your flesh among the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky. David said: Or will God divide your flesh? David said: In the name of the God of Abraham. He took out a stone. Then he took out another and said: In the name of the God of Isaac, and put it in his sling. Then he took out a third and said: In the name of the God of Jacob, and put it in his sling. They all became one stone. David turned the sling and threw it, and God subjected the wind to him until the stone hit the nose of the egg, and it mixed with its brain and came out from the back of its neck, killing thirty men behind it. God defeated the army and Goliath fell dead. He took him and dragged him until he threw him in front of Saul. The Muslims were very happy and returned to Medina safe and sound, and the people remembered David. Then David came to Saul and said: Fulfill what you promised me. He said: Do you want the king's daughter without a dowry? Then David said: You did not stipulate a dowry for me, and I have nothing. He said: I will not burden you with more than you can bear. You are a brave man, and there are enemies around us who are uncircumcised. If you kill two hundred of them and bring me their uncircumcised ones, I will marry you to my daughter. So he went to them and every time he killed one of them, he would string his uncircumcised ones on a thread until he had stringed their uncircumcised ones. Then he brought them to Talut and threw them to him and said: Give me my wife. So he married him to his daughter and made his seal his kingdom. The people inclined to David and loved him and spoke much of him. Talut envied him and wanted to kill him, but a man called Dhu al-Aynayn informed the daughter of Talut of that. She said to David: You will be killed tonight. He said: Who will kill me? She said: My father. He said: Have I committed a crime? She said: One who does not lie told me. You do not have to be absent tonight until we see the truth of that. He said: If God has willed that, I cannot go out, but bring me a wineskin of wine. So she brought it and he put it on his bed and covered him and went under the bed. Then Talut went in at midnight and said to her: Where is your husband? She said: He was sleeping on the bed, so he struck him with the sword and the wine flowed. When he smelled the smell of the drink, he said: May God have mercy on David, how much he drank of wine. And he left. When morning came, he knew that he had done nothing, so he said: A man from whom I asked what I asked is worthy of not leaving me until he takes his revenge on me. So his veil and guards tightened and he closed his doors on him. Then David came to him one night while the eyes were still, so God, glory be to Him, blinded the veils and opened the doors for him. He entered upon him while he was sleeping on his bed, and placed an arrow at his head and an arrow at his feet, an arrow on his right and an arrow on his left, then he went out. When Talut woke up, he saw the arrows and recognized them, so he said: May God Almighty have mercy on David, he is better than me. I defeated him and intended to kill him, and he defeated me, so he refrained from me. If He had wanted, He would have placed this arrow in my throat, and I am not one who trusts him. When the next day came, he came to him a second time, and God blinded the veils, so he entered upon him while he was sleeping, and took the pitcher from which Talut performed ablution and the jug from which he drank, and cut hairs from his beard and some of the fringes of his clothes, then he went out and fled and hid. When morning came, Talut saw that, he set spies on David and pursued him most vehemently. Then one day Talut rode and found David walking in the wilderness and said: Today I will kill him. So he ran after him, and David became very strong, and when he was frightened he could not catch up. So he entered a cave, and God Almighty inspired the spider to weave a web over him. When Talut reached the cave and saw the spider’s construction, he said: If he had entered here, he would have torn the spider’s construction. So he left it and went on. So David set out and went to the mountain with the worshippers and worshipped there. The scholars and worshippers criticized Talut for the matter of David, so Talut would not let anyone stop him from killing David except that he killed him. He incited people to kill scholars, and he could not find a scholar among the Children of Israel who could kill him except that he killed him. Until a woman who knew the greatest name of God was brought to him, so he ordered his baker to kill her, and the baker took pity on her and said: We need a scholar. So he left her. Repentance fell into Talut’s heart and he regretted what he had done, and he began to cry until the people took pity on him. Every night he would go out to the graves and cry and call out: I call upon any servant of God who knows that I have repentance to tell me about it. When he repeated this to them, a caller from the graves called out to him: O Talut, are you not satisfied that you killed us until you harmed us while we were dead? He cried and became even more sad and sorrowful. The baker took pity on him and said: What is the matter with you, O king? He said: Do you know of a scholar on earth whom I can ask? Is there any repentance for me? The baker said: Your example is like that of a king who descended upon a village one evening and a rooster crowed and he took umbrage at that. He said: Do not leave a rooster in the village without slaughtering it. When he wanted to sleep, he said to his companions: When the rooster crows, wake us up so that we may set out early. They said to him: Did you leave a rooster so that we could hear his voice? But did you leave a scholar on earth? He became even sadder and wept. When the baker saw that, he said to him: Tell me, if I guide you to a scholar, perhaps you can kill him? He said: No. The baker trusted him and told him that the learned woman was with him. He said: Let me go to her and ask her: Is there any repentance for me? She was from a household that knew the Greatest Name, and when their men perished, their women would know. When Talut reached the door, the baker said, When she sees you, she is frightened. So he left him behind him and brought him in to her. He said to her, Am I not the greatest of people in showing favor to you? I saved you from being killed and gave you shelter. She said, “Yes, for I have a need of you. This is Talut asking if there is any repentance for me.” She fainted from fear. He said to her, He does not want to kill you, but he is asking if there is any repentance for him. She said, “No, by God, I do not know of any repentance for Talut. But do you know the location of the grave of a prophet?” So he went with them to the grave of Ishmael. She prayed and supplicated, then called out, O owner of the grave. Ishmael came out of the grave, shaking the dust off his head. When he looked at the three of them, he said, What is the matter with you that the Resurrection has come? She said, No, but Talut is asking if there is any repentance for him. Ishmael said, O Talut, what did you do after me? He said, I have not left any evil except that I did it, and I have come seeking repentance. He said, How many children do you have? He said: Ten men. He said: I do not know of any repentance for you except that you give up your kingdom and go out, you and your son, in the way of God, then lead your sons until they are killed before you, then you fight until the last of them. Then Ishmael returned to the grave and fell dead, and Talut returned, more sad than ever, fearing that his son would not follow him, and he cried until his eyelashes fell out and his body wasted away. Then his sons came to him and he said to them: Tell me, if I were thrown into the fire, would you ransom me? They said: Yes, we will ransom you with whatever we can. He said: It is Hell if you do not do what I tell you. They said: Present it to us. So he told them the story. They said: And you will be killed. He said: Yes. They said: There is no good for us in life after you. Our souls are content with what you asked. So he prepared his wealth and his children. His children came forward and they were ten and fought in front of him until they were killed. Then he advanced after them until he was killed. Then his killer came to David to give him the good report and said: I have killed your enemy. David said: I have killed your enemy. David said: You are not the one who will live after him. So he struck off his head. The kingdom of Saul continued until he was killed for forty years. The Children of Israel came to David and gave him the treasures of Saul and made him king over themselves. Al-Kalbi and Al-Dahhak said: David’s reign after killing Talut lasted seven years, and the Children of Israel did not agree on one king except for David. This is what God Almighty said: And God gave him the kingdom and wisdom, meaning: prophecy. God combined for David the kingdom and prophecy, which had not happened before. Rather, the kingdom was in one tribe, and wisdom is knowledge with action. The Almighty said: And He taught him from what He willed. Al-Kalbi and others said: It means: the making of armor, and he used to make it and sell it, and he would not eat except from the work of his hand. It was also said: the speech of birds and the speech of grasshoppers and ants, and beautiful speech. It was also said: it is the Psalms, and it was also said: it is the pleasant voice and melodies, so God did not give anyone of His creation a voice like his. When he recited the Psalms, the wild beasts would come near until he would take them by the necks, and the birds would shade him, listening to him, and the running water would stagnate and the wind would calm down. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that God Almighty gave him a chain connected to the galaxy and its head was at his monastery. Its strength was the strength of iron and its color was the color of fire. Its rings were round and detailed with jewels and studded with wet pearl bars. No event occurred in the air except that the chain would rattle. David knew of that event, and no one with a defect would touch it except that he would be cured. They used to resort to it for judgment after David, peace be upon him, until it was lifted. Whoever transgressed against his companion and denied him a right would come to the chain. Whoever was truthful would extend his hand to the chain and take it, and whoever was lying would not reach it. It remained like that until deceit and trickery appeared among them. It reached us that one of their kings entrusted a man with a precious jewel. When he got it back, he denied it, so they resorted to the chain for judgment. The one who had the jewel took a crutch, pricked it, and put the jewel in it and leaned on it until he brought the chain. The owner of the jewel said: Return the deposit to me. His companion said: I do not know of any deposit you have with me. If you are truthful, then take the chain. So he took it with his hand. It was said to the denier: Get up and take it. He said: To the owner of the jewel: Take this cane of mine and keep it until I reach the chain. So he took it to him. The denier stood up towards the chain and took it. The man said: O God, if you know that this deposit that he claims against me has reached him, then bring the chain near me. He extended his hand and took it. The people were amazed and doubted it. Then in the morning, God had lifted the chain. God the Almighty said: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, the people of Medina and Jacob read God’s defense with an alif here and in Surat Al-Hajj, while others read it without an alif because no one can overcome God the Almighty and He alone is the defender. Whoever reads it with an alif said: The defense may be from one person, like the Arabs’ saying: May God defend you well. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: And had God not repelled with the soldiers of the Muslims, the polytheists would have overcome the land, killed the believers, and destroyed the mosques and the countries. The rest of the commentators said: Had God not repelled with the believers and the righteous from the disbelievers and the wicked, the land and everyone in it would have perished. But God repels with the believer from the disbeliever, and with the righteous from the wicked. Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah bin Fanjuwayh told us, Abu Bakr bin Kharjah told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, Abu Hamid Al-Himsi told us, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Attar told us, Hafs bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Suqah, on the authority of Wabra bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty repels calamity from a hundred households of his neighbors through the righteous Muslim. Then he recited: And were it not that God checks some people by means of others, “The earth would have been corrupted, but God is full of bounty to the worlds.”
2:252: 252. These are the verses of God which We recite to you in truth, and indeed, you are among the messengers.
2:253: 253. "These are the messengers, some of them We preferred over others. Among them were those to whom God spoke" meaning the word of God Almighty, meaning Moses, peace be upon him. And He raised some of them in degrees meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Sheikh Al-Imam, may God have mercy on him, said: No prophet was given a sign except that our prophet was given the like of that sign and he was preferred over others with signs such as: the splitting of the moon, the yearning of the trunk upon leaving it, the greeting of stones and trees to him, the speech of animals and the testimony of his message, the springing of water from between his fingers, and other countless miracles and signs, the most evident of which is the Qur’an, which the people of heaven and earth were unable to produce anything like. Abu Bakr Yaqub bin Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ali al-Sayrafi told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad bin Ahmad al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu al-Abbas bin Muhammad bin Ishaq al-Thaqafi told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, al-Layth bin Saad told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no prophet among the prophets who was not given signs that would make people believe in the like of them. What I was given was only a revelation that God Almighty revealed to me, so I hope that I will have the most followers on the Day of Resurrection.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Muhammad bin Sinan, Hisham told us, I told Sayyar, I told Yazid Al-Faqir, I told Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given five things that were not given to anyone before me: I have been aided by terror from a distance of a month’s journey, the earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me, so whenever a man of my nation is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray, spoils of war have been made lawful for me, but they were not made lawful for anyone before me, and I have been given intercession. A prophet was sent to his people in particular, but I have been sent to all people.” Abu Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, I told Abu Al-Hassan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni, I told Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari, I told Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani, I told Ali bin Hajar, I told Ismail bin Jaafar, I told Al-Ala bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given six things over the prophets: I have been given comprehensive speech, I have been aided by terror, spoils of war have been made lawful for me, the earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me, I have been sent to all of creation, and the prophets have been sealed with me.” God Almighty says: “And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. And if God had willed, those after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them. But they differed. And among them were those who believed, and among them were those who disbelieved, because of His abandonment. And if God had willed, they would not have fought one another. He repeated it for emphasis. But God does what He intends. He guides whom He wills with grace, and He abandons whom He wills with justice.” A man asked Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and said: O Commander of the Faithful, tell me about destiny? He said: A dark path that you must not take. He repeated the question and said: A deep sea that you must not enter. He repeated the question and said: God’s secret on earth is hidden from you, so do not search for it.
2:254: 254. The Almighty said: O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided for you. Al-Suddi said: He meant by it the obligatory zakat. Another said: He meant by it voluntary charity and spending in good deeds. Before there comes a Day in which there is no trade. That is, no ransom. He called it a trade because ransom is the purchase of oneself. Nor friendship. "Nor intercession." Except with the permission of God. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', and the people of Basra read it all in the accusative case. Likewise in Surat Ibrahim verse 31: "There is no trade in it nor friendship." And in Surat At-Tur verse 23: "There is no idle talk in it nor sin." The others read it all in the nominative case and with the tanween. "And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers, because they put worship in the wrong place.
2:255: 255. The Almighty said: God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an informed us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani informed us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh informed us, Ibn Shaybah informed us, Abdul A’la informed us, on the authority of Al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu Al-Saleel, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rabah Al-Ansari, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Al-Mundhir, ‘Which verse of the Book of God is the greatest? ’ I said, ‘God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. ’ He said, ‘Then he struck my chest and said, ‘May knowledge be blessed for you. ’ Then he said, ‘By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, this verse has a tongue and two lips that sanctify the King at the foot of the Throne. ’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail, Uthman bin Al-Haitham Abu Amr said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entrusted me with guarding the zakat of Ramadan. Then someone came to me and began to scoop up some food, so I seized him and said: ‘I will take you to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ He said: ‘I am in need and have dependents and I am in dire need.’ So I let him go. In the morning, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O Abu Hurairah, what did your prisoner do last night?’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, he complained of dire need and dependents, so I took pity on him and let him go.’ He said: ‘He has lied to you and will return.’ I knew that he would return, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said that he would return. So I watched him and he came scooping up some food, so I seized him and said: ‘I will take you to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ He said: ‘Leave me, for I am in need and have dependents and I will not return.’ So I took pity on him.” So I released him. In the morning, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me: O Abu Hurairah, what happened to your prisoner? I said: O Messenger of God, he complained of severe need and children, so I took pity on him and released him. He said: He lied to you and will return. So I watched him for the third time. He came scooping up food, so I seized him and said: I will take you to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is the last of the three times. You claim that you will not return, then you do return. He said: Let me teach you some words by which God will benefit you. I said: What are they? He said: When you go to bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi: God - there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining until you finish the verse, for there will be a guardian from God over you and no devil will come near you until morning. So I released him. In the morning, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me: What did your prisoner do last night? I said: O Messenger of God, he claimed that he would teach me words by which God would benefit me. So I released him. He said: What are they? I said: He said to me, when you go to bed, recite the Throne Verse from the beginning until you finish the verse, God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. And he said: There will remain a guardian from God over you, and no devil will come near you until morning. And they were the most eager of people for good. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has told you the truth, although he is a liar. Do you know who you have been talking to for three nights, O Abu Hurairah? I said: No. He said, That was the devil. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abi Bakr, he is Al-Maliki, on the authority of Zurarah bin Mus’ab, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites the Throne Verse and two verses from the beginning of ‘Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing’ 40:2, will be protected that day until the evening. And whoever recites them in the evening will be protected that night until the morning.” God the Almighty said: God is raised by the subject and its predicate in There is no god but He, the Ever-Living is the Everlasting, the Eternal, and He is the One to Whom life belongs. Life is an attribute of God the Almighty. Al-Qayyum Umar and Ibn Masoud read Al-Qiyam and Alqamah read Al-Qayyim and all of them are languages with the same meaning. Mujahid said: Al-Qayyum is the one who is in charge of everything. Al-Kalbi said: The one who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned. It was also said: He is the one who is in charge of affairs. Abu Ubaidah said: He who does not go away He is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep. Slumber is drowsiness, which is light sleep, and drowsiness is between sleeping and waking. It is said from it: Washna yasna and wasna and sunna and sleep is the heavy one that removes strength and reason. Al-Mufaddal Al-Dabbi said: Slumber is in the head and sleep is in the heart. Slumber is the beginning of sleep, which is drowsiness. It was said: Slumber is in the head and drowsiness is in the eye and sleep is in the heart, so it is a heavy veil that falls on the heart and prevents knowledge of things. God the Almighty denied sleep from Himself because it is a plague and He is free from plagues and because He has changed and change is not permissible for Him. Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid told us, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Ali bin Harb told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us and said five words, and he said: “God does not sleep, nor is it befitting for Him to sleep, but He lowers the balance and raises to Him the deeds of the night before the deeds of the day and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night. His veil is light, were He to remove it, the radiance of His countenance would burn up everything that His sight reaches of His creation.” Al-Mas’udi narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, who said: His veil is the Fire. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth in dominion and creation. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? “By His command.” He knows what is before them and what is behind them. Mujahid, Ata’ and As-Suddi said: What is before them is of worldly affairs. And what is behind them is of the Hereafter. Al-Kalbi said: What is before them means the Hereafter because they are moving forward towards it. And what is behind them means the world because they are leaving it behind them. Ibn Jurayj said: What is before them is what has passed before them and what is behind them is what will come after them. Muqatil said: “What is before them is what was before the creation of the angels and what is behind them is what was after their creation. It was said: “What is before them” means what they have presented of good or evil and what is behind them is what they will do. And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge meaning of God’s knowledge except what He wills meaning He informs them of it. He means they do not encompass anything of the knowledge of the unseen except what He wills of what the messengers have informed them of, as God the Most High said: And He does not disclose His secret to anyone * Except to a messenger with whom He is pleased 36-Al-Jinn. His statement: God the Almighty said: His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth meaning it filled and encompassed them. They differed about the Throne. Al-Hasan said: It is the Throne itself. Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said: The Throne is placed in front of the Throne. The meaning of His statement: His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth is that its breadth is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth. In the hadiths, the heavens and the earth are next to the Throne like a ring in a desert, and the Throne is next to the Throne like a ring in a desert. It is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the seven heavens and the seven earths are in relation to the Throne like seven dirhams thrown into a shield. Ali and Muqatil said: Each leg of the Throne is as long as the seven heavens and the seven earths, and it is in front of the Throne. The Throne is carried by four angels, each angel has four faces, and their feet are in the rock under the seventh lowest earth, a distance of five hundred years. An angel in the image of the master of mankind, Adam, peace be upon him, and he asks for sustenance and rain for mankind from year to year. An angel in the image of the master of livestock, the bull, and he asks for sustenance for livestock from year to year, and his face is fresh since he worshipped the calf. An angel in the image of the master of beasts, the lion, and he asks for sustenance for beasts from year to year. [And an angel in the image of the master of birds, the eagle, and he asks for sustenance for birds from year to year.] In some reports, what is between the bearers of the Throne and the bearers of the Throne are seventy veils of darkness and seventy veils of light, the thickness of each veil is a distance of five hundred years. If it were not for that, the bearers of the Throne would have been burned by the light of the bearers of the Throne. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: He meant by the Throne His knowledge, and this is the saying of Mujahid. From this, the scroll of knowledge was called His book, and it was said: His Throne is His kingdom and His authority, and the Arabs call the ancient kingdom a throne. And it does not burden Him means it does not weigh Him down or make it difficult for Him. It is said: He brought me close meaning it weighed me down. His preservation means the preservation of the heavens and the earth. And He is the Most High is the exalted above His creation and the transcendent above things and rivals. It was said that the Most High is in the kingdom and authority. The Great is the great than whom nothing is greater.
2:256: 256. The Almighty said: There is no compulsion in religion. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: A woman from the Ansar would be a woman who did not have a living child. She would vow that if she had a living child, she would convert him to Judaism. If her child lived, she would make him a Jew. Then Islam came and they were among them. When Banu Nadir were brought, there were a number of the children of the Ansar among them. The Ansar wanted to take them back and said: They are our sons and brothers. Then this verse was revealed: There is no compulsion in religion. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Give your companions a choice. If they choose you, then they are from you. If they choose them, then send them away with them." Mujahed said: There were people who were being breastfed by the Jews from the Aws. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the expulsion of Banu Nadir, those who were being breastfed by them said: We will go with them and we will follow their religion. So their families were among them. Then the verse There is no compulsion in religion was revealed. Masruq said: A man from the Ansar from Banu Salim ibn Awf had two sons who converted to Christianity before the mission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then they came to Medina with a group of Christians carrying food. Their father stuck to them and said: I will not leave you until you become Muslims. They argued before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O Messenger of God, will some of me enter Hell while I am watching? Then God Almighty revealed: There is no compulsion in religion, and he released them. Qatada and Ata’ said: It was revealed about the People of the Book if they accepted the jizyah. This is because the Arabs were an illiterate nation who did not have a book, so nothing was accepted from them except Islam. When they converted willingly or unwillingly, God Almighty revealed: There is no compulsion in religion. So He ordered fighting the People of the Book until they converted or accepted the jizyah. Whoever among them paid the jizyah was not forced to convert to Islam. It was said that this was in the beginning before he was ordered to fight, so it was abrogated by the verse of the sword, which is the saying of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with them both. The right course has become distinct from the wrong. That is, faith from disbelief and truth from falsehood. So whoever disbelieves in Taghut means Satan. It was said: Everything that is worshipped other than God Almighty is a Taghut. It was said: Everything that makes a person transgress, so the ta’ was added to it instead of the lam of the verb, like their saying hanut and tabut, so the ta’ in it is replaced by the feminine ha’. And he believes in God has grasped the firmest handhold. That is, he has grasped. And hold fast to the firm and solid bond in religion. The most trustworthy is the feminine of the most trustworthy. It has been said that the most trustworthy handhold is the cause that leads to the pleasure of God Almighty: Its unbrokenness means it has no interruption. And God is All-Hearing means it was said: of your calling them to Islam. All-Knowing means your eagerness for their faith.
2:257: 257. God the Almighty says: God is the ally of those who believe. He is their helper and supporter. It has been said: He is the one who takes care of their affairs and does not leave them to anyone else. Al-Hasan said: He is the ally of their guidance. He brings them out from darkness into the light. That is, from disbelief to faith. Al-Waqidi said: Everything in the Qur’an about darkness and light means disbelief and faith, other than what is in Surat Al-An’am. And He made darkness and light. What is meant by it is night and day. Disbelief was called darkness because its path is ambiguous, and Islam was called light because its path is clear. And those who disbelieve, their allies are Taghut. Muqatil said: He means Ka’b ibn Al-Ashraf, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and all the leaders of misguidance. They bring them out from the light into darkness. They call them from the light into darkness. Taghut can be masculine and feminine, singular and plural. God the Almighty said about the masculine and singular: They want to refer judgment to Taghut, although they were commanded to disbelieve in him. 60-An-Nisa’ and He said about the feminine: And those who avoided… The tyrant that they worship it” 17-Az-Zumar and he said in the collection: They take them out of the light into the darkness. If it is said: He said: They take them out of the light while they are disbelievers who were never in the light? It is said: They are the Jews who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was sent because of what they found in their books of his description, so when he was sent they disbelieved in him. And it is said: It is general for all disbelievers. They said: Preventing them from entering into it is an exclusion as a man says to his father, You have expelled me from your property and it was not in it, as God Almighty said, informing about Joseph, peace be upon him: Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in God 37-Yusuf and he was never in their religion. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
2:258: 258. The Almighty’s saying: Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord? meaning, has the report of the one who argued with Abraham reached you, O Muhammad, that is, who disputed and argued, and he is Nimrod, who was the first to put the crown on his head, and acted tyrannically on earth and claimed divinity? That God gave him the kingdom meaning that God gave him the kingdom and he transgressed, that is, that argument was due to the king’s arrogance and tyranny. Mujahid said: The kings of the earth were four, two believers and two disbelievers. As for the two believers, they were Solomon and Dhul-Qarnayn, and as for the two disbelievers, they were Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar. They differed about the time of this debate. Muqatil said: When Ibrahim broke the idols, Nimrod imprisoned him and then took him out to burn him in the fire. He said to him: Who is your Lord to whom you are leading us? He said: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. Others said: This was after he was thrown into the fire. This was because people suffered from famine during the reign of Nimrod and people used to buy food from him. When a man came to him asking for food, he would ask him: Who is your Lord? If he said: You, he would sell him food. Ibrahim came to him among those who came to him and Nimrod said to him: Who is your Lord? He said: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. He was busy arguing and did not give him anything. Ibrahim returned and passed by a mound of dusty sand and took some of it to soothe the hearts of his family when he entered upon them. When he came to his family and put down his belongings, he slept. His wife went to his belongings and opened them and found that it was the best food anyone had ever seen. She took it and made some for him and brought it to him. He said: Where did this come from? She said, From the food that you brought me. So he knew that God had provided for him, so he thanked God. God Almighty said: When Abraham said, ‘My Lord is He who gives life and causes death.’ [This is the answer to an unmentioned question, which is: He said to him: Who is your Lord?] And Abraham said, My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. Hamza read My Lord is He who gives life and causes death with a sukoon on the ya’, and likewise My Lord has forbidden indecencies 33-Al-A’raf and About My signs those who are arrogant 146-Al-A’raf and Say to My servants who 31-Ibrahim and He gave me the Book 30-Maryam and Harm has touched me 83-Al-Anbiya’ and My righteous servants 105-Al-Anbiya’ and My grateful servants 13-Saba’ and The devil has touched me 41-Sallallahu Alaihi Wasallam and If God wills me 38-Az-Zumar and If God destroys me 28-Al-Mulk. Hamza made the ya’ sukoon on them, and Ibn Amir and Al-Kisa’i agreed with Ibn Amir in To My servants who believe and Ibn Amir in My signs who and the others opened it, Nimrod said, “I give life and cause death. The people of Medina read ana with the alif and the extension in the connection if it is followed by a fatha or a damma, and the rest deleted the alif, and they all stopped with the alif. Most of the commentators said: Nimrod called for two men, so he killed one of them and kept the other alive, so he made not killing him a revival for him, so Abraham moved on to another argument, not because of his inability, because his argument was necessary because he wanted to revive the dead by the revival, so he could have said: Then revive whoever you have killed, if you are truthful, so he moved on to another argument that is clearer than the first. Abraham said, 'God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.' So the disbeliever was dumbfounded. That is, he was perplexed and astonished and his argument was cut off. If it is said: How could he have been dumbfounded when he could have opposed Abraham and said to him: Ask your Lord until He brings it from the west? It is said: He did not say that because he feared that if he asked that, Abraham would call upon his Lord, which would have increased his disgrace and his being cut off. The correct view is that God diverted him from that opposition in order to show the argument against him or as a miracle for Abraham, peace be upon him. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
2:259: 259. The Almighty says: Or like the one who passed by a town. This verse is connected to the first verse, meaning Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham? and the one who passed by a town. It was said: Its meaning is, Have you seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord? and Have you seen the one who passed by a town? They differed about that which passed by. Qatada, Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: He is Aziz bin Sharkhiya. Wahb bin Munabbih said: He is Jeremiah bin Hilqiya, and he was the grandson of Aaron, and he is Al-Hadr. Mujahid said: He is an infidel who doubted the resurrection. They differed about that village. Wahb, Ikrimah and Qatada said: It is Jerusalem. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the Holy Land. Al-Kalbi said: It is the Monastery of Sabarabad. Al-Suddi said: Salma Badh. It was said: The Monastery of Heraclius. It was said: It is the land in which God destroyed those who left their homes, and they were thousands. It was said: It is the village of grapes, and it is two farsakhs from Jerusalem. And it is empty is fallen. It is said: The house was emptied with a kasra on the waw, it is khawa, shortened, if it fell. The house was emptied with a fatha, extended, if it was empty. On its thrones is its roofs, the singular of which is a throne. It was said: Every building is a throne, and its meaning is: The roofs fell and then the walls fell on them. He said, ‘How can God revive this after its death?’ The reason for that, according to what Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Munabbih narrated, was that God Almighty sent Jeremiah to Nashiyya ibn Amuz, the king of the Children of Israel, to guide him in that and bring him report from God Almighty. The events among the Children of Israel became great and they committed sins, so God Almighty inspired Jeremiah: Remind your people of My blessings and tell them about their events and call them to Me. Jeremiah said, I am weak if you do not strengthen me, helpless if you do not inform me, and forsaken if you do not support me. God Almighty said, I will inspire you. Jeremiah stood up among them and did not know what to say, so God inspired him at that time with a long, eloquent sermon in which he explained to them the reward of obedience and the punishment of disobedience. At the end of it, he said from God Almighty: “And I swear by My might that I will seize for them a trial in which the wise will be perplexed, and I will set over them a Persian tyrant whom I will clothe with awe and remove mercy from his chest, followed by a number like the blackness of the dark night.” Then God Almighty inspired Jeremiah: Jeremiah said: I will destroy the children of Israel through Japheth, and Bapheth was from the people of Babylon, and they were from the descendants of Bapheth, son of Noah, peace be upon him. When Jeremiah heard that, he cried out and wept, and tore his clothes and threw ashes on his head. When God heard his supplication and weeping, He called out to him: O Jeremiah, is what I have revealed to you difficult for you? He said: Yes, O Lord, destroy me before I see in the children of Israel something that I do not like. God Almighty said: By My might, I will not destroy the children of Israel until the matter is decided by You. Jeremiah was pleased with that and his soul was content, so he said: No, by the One Who sent Moses with the truth, I am not pleased with the destruction of the children of Israel. Then he came to the king and informed him of that, and he was a righteous king, so he was glad and joyful and said: If our Lord punishes us, it will be for many sins, and if He pardons us, it will be by His mercy. Then they remained after the revelation for three years, and they only increased in disobedience and persistence in evil. That was when their destruction drew near, and the revelation decreased. The king called them to repent, but they did not. So God empowered Nebuchadnezzar over them, and he went out with six hundred thousand banners, intending to go to the people of Jerusalem. When he had departed, the report came to the king, and he said to Jeremiah: Where is what you claimed that God revealed to you? Jeremiah said: God does not break His promise, and I trust in Him. When the time drew near, God sent to Jeremiah an angel who appeared to him as a man from the Children of Israel. Jeremiah said to him: Who are you? He said: I am a man from the Children of Israel. I have come to you to ask you about my relatives. I have maintained ties of kinship with them, and I have only treated them well, and my honoring them only increases my anger, so give me a fatwa about them. He said: Do well, maintain ties of kinship with them, and be glad for good. The king turned away and stayed for a few days, then he came to him in the form of that man and sat before him and said: I am the one who came to you about my family. Jeremiah said to him: Haven't their morals been purified for you yet? He said: O Prophet of God, by Him who sent you with the truth, I do not know of any honor that anyone has given to mercy except that I have presented it to them and done better. The Prophet Jeremiah, peace be upon him, said to him: Go back to them and ask God, who reforms His righteous servants, to reform them. The king stood up and stayed for a few days, and Nebuchadnezzar and his cavalry had descended around the Holy House with more locusts than the Children of Israel. Their king said to Jeremiah: O Prophet of God, where is what God promised you? He said: I trust in my Lord. Then the king came to Jeremiah while he was sitting on the wall of the Holy House, laughing and rejoicing in the victory of his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, which He promised him. He sat before him and said: I am the one who came to you about my family twice. The Prophet said: Is it not time for them to wake up from what they are in? The king said: O Prophet of God, I used to be patient with everything that happened to me from them before today, but today I saw them doing something that displeases God. The Prophet said: For what action did you see them? He said: For a great action that angered God, so God became angry and I came to you to inform you. I ask you by God who sent you as a prophet with the truth, except that you call upon God against them to destroy them. Jeremiah said: O Owner of the heavens and the earth, if they are doing what is right and correct, then spare them, and if they are doing something that does not please You, then destroy them. When the word came out of Jeremiah’s mouth, God sent a thunderbolt from the sky into the Holy House, and the place of sacrifice caught fire and seven of its gates caved in. When Jeremiah saw that, he cried out, tore his clothes, threw ashes on his head and said: O Owner of the heavens, where is the appointment that You promised me? Then it was announced that what happened to them did not happen except because of your fatwa and your supplication. The Prophet, peace be upon him, was certain that it was his fatwa and that the questioner was the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. Jeremiah flew until he mingled with the wild beasts. Then Nebuchadnezzar and his soldiers entered Jerusalem and trod the Levant and killed the Children of Israel until he annihilated them and destroyed Jerusalem. Then he ordered his soldiers to fill each man’s shield and throw it into Jerusalem, so they did until they filled it. Then he ordered them to gather whoever was in the countries of Jerusalem, so the young and old of the Children of Israel gathered around them. He chose seventy thousand boys from them and divided them among the kings who were with him. Each man got four boys, and among those boys were Daniel and Hananiah. He divided the remaining Children of Israel into three groups, one third he killed, one third he took captive, and one third he left in the Levant. This was the first incident that God brought down on the Children of Israel because of their oppression. When Nebuchadnezzar turned away from them, returning to Babylon with the captives of the Children of Israel, Jeremiah came on his donkey with grape juice in a jug and a basket of figs until he reached Elijah. When he stood over it and saw its devastation, he said: How can God revive this after its death? He who said that the one who passed by was Ezra said: When Nebuchadnezzar destroyed the Holy House and brought the Children of Israel to Babylon, Ezra was among them, along with Daniel and seven thousand of the people of the House of David. When Ezra escaped from Babylon, he traveled on his donkey until he reached the Monastery of Heraclius on the banks of the Tigris. He wandered around the village and did not see anyone there, although most of its trees were bearing fruit. He ate some of the fruit, squeezed some of the grapes and drank from it, and put the excess fruit in a basket and the excess juice in a wineskin. When he saw the destruction of the village and the destruction of its people, he said: How can God revive this after its death? He said it in amazement, not in doubt about the resurrection. We returned to the hadith of Wahb, who said: Then Jeremiah tied his donkey with a new rope, and God Almighty cast sleep upon him. When he slept, God took away his soul for a hundred years and caused his donkey to die, and his juice and figs were with him. God blinded the eyes of him so that no one saw him, and that was at noon. God prevented the wild beasts and birds from eating his meat. When seventy years had passed since his death, God sent an angel to a king of the Persian kings called Noushk and said: God commands you to go forth with your people and populate Jerusalem and Aelia until it returns to being more populated than it was. So the king delegated a thousand heromen with three hundred thousand workers for each heromen and they began to populate it. Then God destroyed Nebuchadnezzar with a mosquito that entered his brain, and God removed from the children of Israel those who remained, and he did not die in Babylon and returned them all to Jerusalem and its environs and they populated it for thirty years and they multiplied until they returned to the best they had been. When the hundred years had passed, God revived his eyes, and the rest of his body was dead. Then He revived his body while he was looking at it. Then he looked at his donkey and saw that its bones were scattered. Eggs, waving, then he heard a voice from the sky: O decayed bones, God commands you to gather together, so some of them gathered together, and some of them connected with each other, and it was called: God commands you to be clothed with flesh and skin, and it was like that, then it was called: God commands you to live, so he rose with God’s permission and brayed, and God gave Jeremiah a long life, so he is the one who sees in the deserts, so that is what God Almighty said: So God caused him to die for a hundred years, then He raised him up meaning He brought him back to life He said, ‘How long did you remain?’ meaning: How long did you stay? It is said: When God brought him back to life, He sent an angel to him and asked him, How long did you remain? “He said, ‘I have remained one day.’” That is because God Almighty caused him to die in the early morning and brought him back to life after a hundred years at the end of the day before the sun set. He said, I have remained one day, and he saw that the sun had set. Then he turned and saw the remainder of the sun, so he said, Or part of a day. Rather, part of a day. The king said to him, “Rather, you have remained one hundred years. So look at your food,” meaning the figs, and your drink, meaning the juice. It has not stale, meaning it has not changed. So the figs were as if they had been picked immediately, and the juice was as if it had been squeezed immediately. Al-Kisa’i said: It is as if the years had not passed him by. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and Ya’qub read lam yatasanna without deleting the ha’ in the connected word, and likewise fa bihdahum iqtidah 90-Al-An’am. The others read with the ha’ in both of them, connected and paused. Whoever dropped the ha’ in the connected word made the ha’ an extra connection and said: Its origin is yatasanna so he deleted the ya’ in the jussive mood and replaced it with a ha’ in the pause. Abu Amr said: They are from tasanna with two noons: which is the change like the Almighty’s saying: from black mud that has been altered 26-Al-Hajj, meaning it has changed, so a ya’ was replaced with one of the two noons like the Almighty’s saying: Then he went to his family, stretching himself 33-Al-Qiyamah, meaning he stretched himself out, and like His saying: And he who has hidden it has failed 10-Ash-Shams. Its origin is dasitahu dissimilative, and its diminutive is sanaiha and the verb is from sanah. He only said: lam yatasannahu and did not dualize it even though he informed about two things. He returned the change to the closest of the two words, which is the drink, and he was satisfied with mentioning one of the two mentioned. Because it has the meaning of the other: And look at your donkey. So he looked and saw that it was white bones. So God Almighty put the bones together, one on top of the other, and covered it with flesh and skin, and brought it back to life while it was looking. And that We may make you a sign for mankind. It was said that the waw is an extra, inserted letter. Al-Farra’ said: The waw was inserted in it to indicate that it is a condition for a verb after it, the meaning of which is: And that We may make you a sign, meaning: a lesson and an indication of the resurrection after death. This was said by most of the commentators. Al-Dahhak and others said: He returned to his village as a young man with his children and the children of old men and women, and his head and beard were black. The Almighty said: And look at the bones, how We resurrect them. The people of Hijaz and Basra read nanshiruha with a ra meaning We revive them. It is said: God resurrected the dead person, nanshira and nanshira and nanshira. God Almighty said: Then when He wills, He will resurrect him 22-Abasa. He said in the imperative: And to Him is the resurrection 15-Al-Mulk. The others read it with a zay meaning We raise them from the earth and return them to their place in the body and mount some of them on top of others. Inshiza of something means raising it and disturbing it. It is said: Anshazatuhu fanashaz meaning I raised it and it rose. They differed about the meaning of the verse. Most of them said: He meant the bones of his donkey. Al-Suddi said: God Almighty revived Ezra and then said to him: Look at your donkey, it has perished and its bones have decayed. God Almighty sent a wind that brought the bones of the donkey from every plain and mountain. The birds and beasts had taken them, and they gathered together and mounted one another while he was watching. So it became a donkey of bones with no flesh or blood. Then We covered them with flesh. Then He covered the bones with flesh and blood, so it became a donkey with no soul in it. Then an angel came walking until he took hold of the nostril of the winemaker and blew into it, so the donkey stood up and brayed with God’s permission. Some people said that he meant the bones of this man, because God Almighty did not cause his donkey to die, but rather caused him to die, so God revived his eyes and his head, and the rest of his body was dead. Then he said: Look at your donkey. So he looked and saw his donkey standing as it was the day he tied it up alive, it had not eaten or drunk for a hundred years, and he saw the ashes on its neck, new and unchanged. The meaning of the verse: And look at your donkey and look at your bones, how We will resurrect them. In the verse there is an inversion, and their meaning is: And look at your donkey, and look at the bones, how We will resurrect them, and that We may make you a sign for the people. Qatada said on the authority of Ka’b and Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: When God Almighty revived Ezra after He had caused him to die for a hundred years, he rode his donkey to his place of residence. The people did not recognize him and the people did not recognize his dwellings, so he set off among them until he reached his place of residence. There was a blind, crippled old woman who had been one hundred and twenty years old. She had recognized him and understood him. Ezra said to her: O woman, is this the place of Ezra? She said: Yes, this is the home of Ezra, and she cried and said: I have not seen anyone for so and so years mention Ezra. He said: I am Ezra. She said: Glory be to God, for we have lost Ezra for a hundred years, and we have not heard any mention of him. He said: I am Ezra. God caused me to die for a hundred years, then He resurrected me. She said: Ezra was a man whose prayers were answered, and he used to pray for the sick and the afflicted for recovery. So pray to God to restore my sight so that I may see you. If you are Ezra, I will recognize you. So he called upon his Lord and wiped his hand over her eyes, and they recovered. Then he took her hand and said: Get up, by the permission of God, the Most High. So God released her legs, and she stood up healthy. She looked at him and said: I bear witness that you are Ezra. So she went to the Children of Israel while they were in their clubs and gatherings, and Ezra’s son was an old man, one hundred and eighteen years old, and his grandsons were old men in the gathering. She called out: This is Ezra, he has come to you, but they denied her. She said: I am so-and-so, your mistress. He prayed to his Lord for me, and restored my sight and released my legs, and he claimed that God had caused him to die for a hundred years. Then he sent him, and the people rose and came to him. His son said: My father had a black mole like a crescent moon between his shoulders. So he uncovered his shoulders and behold, it was Uzair. Al-Suddi and Al-Kalbi said: When Ezra returned to his people, Nebuchadnezzar had burned the Torah and there was no covenant between the creation of God, so Ezra wept over the Torah, and an angel came to him with a vessel of water and gave him to drink from that water, and the Torah was represented in his chest, so he returned to the Children of Israel and God had taught him the Torah and sent him as a prophet, and he said: I am Ezra, but they did not believe him, so he said: I am Ezra, God has sent me to you to renew your Torah for you, they said: Dictate it to us, so he dictated it to them from his heart, and they said: God did not place the Torah in the chest of a man after it was gone except that he is his son, so they said: Ezra is the son of God, and the story will come in Surat Bara’ah, God willing. The Almighty said: So when that became clear to him, he said: I know. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read it in the subjunctive mood as a command, meaning God Almighty said: I know. The others read: I know, cutting off the alif and raising the meem as a report on the authority of Uzair, who said when he saw that: I know, “that God is over all things competent.”
2:260: 260. God the Almighty said: And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, show me how You revive the dead.’ Al-Hasan, Qatada, Ata’ al-Khurasani, and Ibn Jurayj said: The reason for this question from Abraham, peace be upon him, was that he passed by a dead animal. Ibn Jurayj said: It was the carcass of a donkey on the seashore. Ata’ said: In the Sea of Galilee. They said: He saw it and the animals of the sea and land had distributed it. When the sea rose, the whales and animals of the sea would come and eat from it, and whatever fell from it would go into the sea. When the sea ebbed and flowed, the beasts of prey would come and eat from it, and whatever fell from it would turn into dust. When the beasts of prey went away, the birds would come and eat from it, and whatever fell from it the wind would tear it apart in the air. When Abraham, peace be upon him, saw that, he was amazed by it and said: O Lord, You know that You will gather it from the bellies of beasts of prey, the crops of birds, and the stomachs of animals of the sea. Show me how You revive it so that I may see and increase in certainty. So God the Almighty rebuked him: He said, ‘Do you not believe?’ He said, ‘Yes, O Lord, I know and believe, but so that my heart may be at ease.’ That is, so that my heart may be at ease with seeing and observing. He wanted to have absolute certainty, because knowledge is not like seeing. It was said: The reason for this question from Abraham was that when he argued with Nimrod, saying, My Lord is He who gives life and causes death 258-Al-Baqarah, Nimrod said: I give life and cause death, so he killed one of the two men and released the other. Abraham said: God Almighty goes to a dead body and brings it back to life, so Nimrod said to him: You saw it, but he was not able to say yes, so he moved on to another argument, then he asked his Lord to show him the resurrection of the dead. He said, ‘Do you not believe?’ He said, ‘Yes, but so that my heart may be reassured’ by the strength of my argument. So if it is said, You saw it, I say, Yes, I saw it. Saeed bin Jubair said: When God chose Ibrahim as a friend, the Angel of Death asked his Lord to give him permission to give Ibrahim the good report of that, so He gave him permission. He came to Ibrahim, who was not in the house, so he entered his house, and Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was the most jealous of people. When he went out, he would close his door. When he came, he found a man in his house, so he got up to seize him and said to him: Who gave you permission to enter my house? He said: The Lord of this house gave me permission. Ibrahim said: You are right, and he knew that he was an angel. He said: Who are you? She said: I am the Angel of Death, I have come to give you the good report that God has chosen you as a friend. He praised God, the Almighty, the Majestic, and said: What is the sign of that? He said: That God will answer your prayer and bring the dead back to life through your question. Then Ibrahim said: My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said: Do you not believe? He said: Yes, but so that my heart may be reassured. That You have chosen me as a friend and that You answer me when I call upon You. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmad bin Saleh told us, I told Ibn Wahb, Yunus told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “We are more deserving of doubt than Abraham when he said, ‘My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.’ He said, ‘Do you not believe?’ He said, ‘Yes, but [so] that my heart may be reassured.’ May God have mercy on Lot, for he used to seek refuge in a strong support. If I had remained in prison as long as Joseph remained, I would have answered the caller.” Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj narrated this hadith on the authority of Harmalah bin Yahya on the authority of Wahb with this chain of transmission similar to it and he said: We are more deserving of doubt than Abraham when he said, ‘My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.’ It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Khuzaymah on the authority of Abu Ibrahim Ismail bin Yahya Al-Muzani that he said regarding this hadith, neither the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor Abraham doubted that God is able to revive the dead, but he doubted whether He would answer them to what they asked. Abu Sulayman Al-Khattabi said: In his saying, We are more deserving of doubt than Abraham, there is no admission of doubt on his part or on Abraham, but rather it negates doubt on their part. He says: If I do not doubt God Almighty’s ability to revive the dead, then Abraham is more deserving of not doubting. He said that out of humility and self-denial. Likewise, his saying, If I had remained in prison as long as Joseph remained, I would have answered the caller. It contains information that the question from Abraham, peace be upon him, was not presented out of doubt, but rather out of increased knowledge by sight, for sight provides knowledge and reassurance that which inference does not provide. It was said: When this verse was revealed, some people said: Abraham doubted, but not our Prophet. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This statement is out of humility on his part and giving precedence to Abraham over Same. His saying, Did you not believe? means that you believed, so why did you ask? He testified to his faith, as Gabriel said: Aren't you the best of those who ride mounts and the most generous of the worlds in terms of bellies? I mean you are too, but to reassure my heart with increased certainty. He said: Take four birds. Mujahid, Ata’, and Ibn Jurayj said: He took a peacock, a rooster, a dove, and a crow. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: And an eagle instead of a dove. Ata Al-Khurasani said: He was inspired to take a green duck, a black crow, a white pigeon, and a red rooster. And cut them to pieces. Abu Jaafar and Hamza read and cut them to pieces with a kasra on the sad, meaning cut them and tear them apart. It is said that sarā yasīr sīrān means he cut them, and anṣār means that something is cut off. Al-Farra’ said: It is inverted from saraita asri sariyan meaning to cut. The others read fasrahunna with a damma on the sad and its meaning is to incline them towards you and direct them. It is said: saratu al-shay’ asawruhu if you incline it, and a man is asawur if his neck is inclined. Ata’ said: Its meaning is to gather them and bring them together towards you. It is said: sar yasawur sawur if he gathers, and from this a group of bees is called sawur. Whoever interpreted it with inclination and damma said that its meaning is implied, sawurhunna ilayka then sawurunna so he deleted it, sufficing with his saying: then place on every mountain a part of them because it indicates it. Abu Ubaidah said: fasrahunna also means to cut them, and sawur means to cut. The Almighty said: Then place on every mountain a portion of them. Asim read, according to Abu Bakr’s narration, a portion with a mithqal and a hamza, and the others read it with a light pronunciation and a hamza, and Abu Ja`far read it with a shaddah on the zay without a hamza, and he meant by it some of the mountains. Some commentators said: God commanded Abraham to slaughter those birds, pluck their feathers, cut them up, and mix their feathers, blood, and meat together, so he did. Then He commanded him to place their parts on the mountains. They differed about the number of parts and mountains. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and Qatada said: He ordered that each bird be divided into four parts and that they be divided into four mountains, with a quarter of each bird on each mountain. It was said: a mountain on the eastern side, a mountain on the western side, a mountain on the northern side, and a mountain on the southern side. Ibn Jurayj and Al-Suddi said: He divided it into seven parts and placed it on seven mountains and held their heads then called them: Come with the permission of God the Most High, so every drop of blood of a bird flew to the other drop, and every feather flew to the other feather, and every bone went to the other bone, and every piece went to the other, and Ibrahim was watching, until every body met each other in the sky without a head. Then they came to their heads running, and whenever a bird came, it turned its head. If it had a head, it approached it, and if it had not, it stayed back, until every bird met its head. This is what God the Most High said: Then call them, and they will come to you running. It was said that what is meant by running is speeding and running, and it was said that what is meant by it is walking and not flying, as God the Most High said: Then hasten to the remembrance of God 9-Jumu’ah, meaning go on. The wisdom in walking and not flying is that it is further from doubt because if it flew, someone would think that it is not that bird and that its legs are not sound, and God knows best. It was said that running means flying, And know that God is Exalted in Might and Wise.
2:261: 261. The Almighty’s statement: The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God contains an implied meaning, like the charity of those who spend their wealth is like the parable of a planter of a grain, and by the way of God he meant jihad. It was said that all the doors of goodness brought forth “seven ears of corn” the plural of ear of corn “in each ear is a hundred grains.” If it is said, We have never seen an ear of corn containing a hundred grains, so how was the parable struck with it? It was said: This is conceivable, not impossible, and what is not impossible can be used as an example even if it does not exist.
