Its meaning is: In every ear of grain is a hundred grains, meaning God placed in it. It was said that it exists in millet. It was said that its meaning is that if it is sown, it produces a hundred grains, so whatever seed was in it was added to it. Ad-Dahhak interpreted it this way, saying: Every ear of grain produces a hundred grains. And God multiplies for whomever He wills, it was said that its meaning is that He multiplies this multiplication for whomever He wills. It was said that its meaning is that He multiplies on this and increases for whomever He wills between seven and seventy and seven hundred to whatever God wills of multiples that no one knows except God Almighty. And God is Vast, rich, He gives from His vastness. Knowing, of the intention of whoever spends His money.
2:262: 262. The Almighty said: Those who spend their wealth in the way of God. Al-Kalbi said: This verse was revealed about Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, may God be pleased with them both. "Abd al-Rahman brought four thousand dirhams as charity to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I had eight thousand, so I kept four thousand dirhams from it for myself and my family, and I lent four thousand to my Lord. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: May God bless what you kept for you and what you gave." As for Uthman, he equipped the Muslim army for the Battle of Tabuk with a thousand camels with their saddles and saddles, so this verse was revealed about them. Abdul Rahman bin Samura said: Uthman, may God be pleased with him, came with a thousand dinars in the army of hardship and poured it into the lap of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, put his hand in it and turn it over and say, What harm will it do to Ibn Affan after today? Then God, the Most High, revealed, Those who spend their wealth in the way of God in obedience to God, and do not follow up what they have spent with reminders meaning that God bestows His favor upon him by saying, I gave you such and such, and counts His favors upon him and then spoils them. Nor injury meaning that he taunts him by saying, How long do you ask for it and how much do you harm me? It was said that one of the types of injury is that someone mentions his spending on him in the presence of someone who does not like him to know about it. Sufyan said: As a favor and without harm is to say, I have given you and given, but you have not been grateful. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: My father used to say: If you give a man something and you see that your greeting is burdensome to him, then withhold your greeting from him. So God has forbidden His servants to show favors for a favor, and He has made it a characteristic of Himself, because among the servants there is reproach and distress, but from God there is favor and a reminder. For them is their reward, meaning their recompense, with their Lord, and there is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve.
2:263: 263. A good word means good words that are given to the questioner in a beautiful way, and it was said that it is a good number. Al-Kalbi said: A supplication for one's brother in his absence. Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed about reconciling people. And forgiveness means covering up his friendship and not tearing his veil. Al-Kalbi and Al-Dahhak said: He overlooks his oppressor, and it was said that he overlooks the poor person if he is rude to him when he rejects him. Better than charity that he gives to him. Followed by harm means reproaching the questioner or saying something that hurts him. And God is Rich means He is independent of the charity of His servants. Forbearing does not hasten to punish those who show off or hurt by charity.
2:264: 264. God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities meaning the rewards of your charities by showing off to the beggar. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: by showing off to God the Almighty and by causing harm to the one who gives it. Then he gave an example for that, saying: Like one who spends his wealth meaning like the one who spends his wealth to be seen by people meaning showing off and for reputation so that they see his spending and say that he is generous and bountiful and does not believe in God and the Last Day meaning that showing off invalidates the charity and spending with showing off is not an action of the believers. This is for the hypocrites because the disbeliever declares his disbelief without showing off. His example meaning the example of this hypocrite is like the example of a smooth rock which is a smooth stone, and it is singular and plural. So whoever makes it a plural makes its singular safwana and whoever makes it singular makes its plural safy upon it meaning on the smooth rock there was dust and a downpour which is heavy rain with great rain leaving it solid meaning smooth, and solid is a solid, smooth stone that has nothing on it. This is an example that God the Almighty gave for the spending of the hypocrite. The hypocrite and the believer who boasts about his charity and outwardly harms people, these people have deeds just as the dust is seen on this rock. When the Day of Resurrection comes, all of it will be void because it was not for God Almighty, just as the downpour removes the dust on the rock and leaves it solid. They will not be able to do anything about what they have earned, meaning the reward for anything they have earned and done in this world. And God does not guide the disbelieving people. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmini told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Amr bin Abi Amr, the client of Al-Muttalib told us, on the authority of Asim bin Omar, on the authority of Mahmoud bin Labid, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What I fear most for you is minor polytheism. They said: O Messenger of God, what is minor polytheism? He said: Hypocrisy. God will say to them on the Day when He will reward His servants for their deeds: Go to those for whom you were showing off in the world and see if you find any reward with them. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Harithi told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Haywah ibn Shuraih, al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid Abu Uthman al-Madaini told me that Uqbah ibn Muslim told him that Shafi’ al-Asbahi told him that he entered the city and saw a man around whom people had gathered, so he said, Who is this? He said: Abu Hurairah. So I approached him until I sat in front of him while he was talking to the people. When he was silent and alone, I said to him: I ask you by God, by the truth, why did you tell me a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “When God comes on the Day of Resurrection, He will descend to His servants to judge between them, and every nation will be kneeling. The first to be called will be a man who collected the Qur’an, a man who was killed in the way of God, and a man with great wealth. God will say to the reciter: Did I not teach you what I revealed to My Messenger? He will say: Yes, O Lord. He will say: What did you do with what you learned? He will say: I used to stand in prayer during the night and during the day. God will say to him: You lied. The angels will say: You lied. God Almighty will say: Rather, you wanted it to be said that so-and-so is a reciter, and that was said. The owner of the wealth will be brought and God will say to him: Did I not provide for you so generously that I did not leave you in need of anyone? He will say: Yes, O Lord. He will say: What did you do with what I gave you? He will say: I used to maintain family ties and give charity. God will say to him: You lied. The angels will say: He said: You lied. And God the Most High says: Rather, you wanted it to be said that so-and-so is generous, and that was said. And the one who was killed in the cause of God will be brought and He will say to him: For what were you killed? He will say: O Lord, I was commanded to fight in Your cause, so I fought until I was killed. And God the Most High says: You lied. And the angels will say: You lied. And God the Most High says: Rather, you wanted it to be said that so-and-so is brave, and that was said. Then the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) struck my knee and said: O Abu Hurairah, those three are the first of God’s creation to be set on fire by the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
2:265: 265. The Almighty’s saying: And the parable of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of God meaning seeking the pleasure of God Almighty and to strengthen themselves Qatada said: seeking reward. Al-Sha’bi and Al-Kalbi said: believing in themselves, meaning they give zakat willingly, certain of the reward and believing in God’s promise, knowing that what they give is better for them than what they left behind. It was said: certain of God’s failure to fulfill their promise. Ata and Mujahid said: They establish, meaning they deposit their money. Al-Hasan said: If a man intended to give charity, he established it. If it was for God, he would carry it out, but if he was sceptical, he would hold back. According to this statement, establishing means establishing, like the Almighty’s saying: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion Al-Muzzammil 8, meaning devotion. Like a garden meaning an orchard. Al-Mubarrad and Al-Farra’ said: If there are palm trees in the orchard, then it is a garden, and if there are vineyards in it, then it is a paradise. On a high place Ibn ‘Amir and ‘Asim read on a high place and to a high place in the water rises above it, but it does not rise above the water. He only made it a high place because the plants on it are better and purer. It was afflicted with a downpour heavy rain. So it produced its fruit its fruit. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, and Abu ‘Amr read it with a light emphasis. Nafi’ and Ibn Kathir added a light emphasis on its food and its eating. Abu ‘Amr lightened our messengers and your messengers and their messengers and our paths. “Twice” means it became weaker in terms of pregnancy. Ata’ said: It carried in one year more rain than another carries in two years. Ikrimah said: It carried twice in one year. And if no downpour hits it, then it rains means it rains lightly, which is the weak, light rain that is constant. Al-Suddi said: It is dew, and this is an example that God Almighty gave for the work of the sincere believer, saying: Just as this paradise is abundant in every situation and does not fail, whether the rain is little or much, so God weakens the charity of the sincere believer who does not deprive or harm, whether his expenses are little or much, and that is because if the dew continues, it is the work of a heavy downpour. God is Seeing of what you do.
2:266: 266. Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines with rivers flowing beneath it? This verse is connected to the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury. [His saying would means: Would any of you like to have a garden, i.e. an orchard of palm trees and grapevines with rivers flowing beneath it?] He will have therein all kinds of fruits, but he will be old and have weak offspring. “Then a hurricane struck it.” It is a violent wind that rises to the sky like a column, and its plural is hurricanes. “Therein is fire, and it was burned.” This is a parable that God has given for the work of the hypocrite and the show-off. He says: His work in its goodness is like the goodness of Paradise. He benefits from it as the owner of Paradise benefits from Paradise. Then, when he grows old or weak and has weak children, and a hurricane struck his garden with fire, and it was burned, he will need it more than ever, and he will be too weak to repair it because of his old age, and his children will be too weak to repair it because of their young age. He will not find anything to return to his children, nor will his children find anything to return to him, so they will all remain confused, helpless, with no means at their disposal. Thus, God will invalidate the work of this hypocrite and show-off when there is no one to help them, no repentance, and no forgiveness. Ubayd ibn Umair said: One day, Umar may God be pleased with him said to the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): About whom do you think this verse was revealed: Would any of you like to have a garden of date palms and grapevines? They said: God knows best. Umar may God be pleased with him became angry and said: Say, We know or We do not know. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: I have something in mind about it, O Commander of the Faithful. Umar may God be pleased with him said: My nephew, say it and do not belittle yourself. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: You have given an example of a deed. Umar may God be pleased with him said: What deed? Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: The deed of a hypocrite. Umar may God be pleased with him said about a rich man who did acts of obedience to God, and God sent Satan to him, so he committed sins until he drowned his deeds. Thus does God make clear to you the signs that you may give thought.
2:267: 267. O you who have believed, spend from the good things from the best. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, and Mujahid said: from the lawful things what you have earned from trade and industry. This indicates the permissibility of earning and that it is divided into good and bad. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ya’la bin Ubaid told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best thing a man eats is from his earnings, and his children are from his earnings. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Abu Mu’awiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Buhair bin Sa’d, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, on the authority of Al-Miqdam bin Ma’dikarib, that he told him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: No one has ever eaten food better than that which he eats from the work of his hands, and David would not eat except from the work of his hands. Abu Al-Qasim Yahya bin Ali bin Muhammad Al-Kashmihani told us, Najah bin Yazid Al-Maharibi told us in Kufa, Abu Ja`far Muhammad bin Ali bin Duhaim Al-Shaibani told us, Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Yahya bin Ubaid told us, Aban bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Sabah bin Muhammad, on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas`ud, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A servant does not acquire unlawful wealth and give it in charity, for God accepts it from him, nor spends from it, for God blesses him in it, nor leaves it behind him, except that it will be his provision for the Fire. God does not erase evil with evil, but He erases evil with good. Indeed, evil does not erase evil.” Zakat is obligatory on trade money according to most scholars. After a year, the stock is valued and a quarter of a tenth of its value is taken if its value is twenty dinars or two hundred dirhams. Samurah ibn Jundub said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to command us to give zakat on what we prepared for sale. On the authority of Abu Amr bin Hamas, that his father said: I passed by Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and I was carrying a leather garment on my neck. Omar said: Why don’t you pay your zakat, O Hamas? I said: I have nothing but this and I give it as a loan. He said: That is wealth, so put it down. So I put it down and he calculated it and took the zakat from it. The Almighty says: And from what We have produced for you from the earth. It was said that this refers to the tithe of fruits and grains. The scholars agreed that a tithe is obligatory on palm trees and vineyards and on grains that are eaten as sustenance if they are irrigated by rainwater or a river that flows to it without any effort. If they are irrigated by a waterwheel or by a mature crop, then half of the tithe is due. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Abdullah bin Wahb told us, Yunus bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: On what is watered by the sky and springs, or is of a natural origin, the tenth is due, and on what is watered by ripening, half of the tenth is due. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Abdullah bin Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Saleh Al-Tammar, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Atab bin Asid, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the zakat on grapes: It is estimated as the date palm is estimated, then its zakat is paid in raisins as the date palm zakat is paid in dates. Scholars differed on matters other than palm trees and vineyards, and on matters other than grains that are used for food. Some people said that there is no tithe on any of them, which is the opinion of Ibn Abi Laila and Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with them. Al-Zuhri, Al-Awza’i and Malik, may God be pleased with them, said: It is obligatory on olives. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, said: The tithe is obligatory on all legumes and vegetables, such as fruits, except grass and firewood. And every grain for which we have made the tithe obligatory, the time for its obligation is the hardening of the grain and the time of extraction after threshing and purification. The tithe is not obligatory on anything of it that reaches five wasqs according to most scholars. According to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, it is obligatory on everything, small or large. He provided evidence for the condition of the nisab with what Abu Al-Hasan Al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir bin Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus’ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Sa’sa’ah Al-Mazini, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no zakat on less than five wasqs of dates, and there is no zakat on less than five ounces of silver, and there is no zakat on less than five herds of camels. Yahya bin Ubadah narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no charity on grain or dates until it reaches five wasqs. Some people said: The verse is about voluntary charity. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Yahya bin Yahya told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no believer who plants a tree or sows a seed from which a human being, bird, or animal eats, except that it is considered a charity for him. The Almighty said: And do not spend at night. Ibn Kathir recited according to the narration of Al-Bazzi with a shaddah on the ta’ in the connection in it and its sisters, and it is thirty-one places in the Qur’an, because in the original there were two ta’s, one of which was dropped, so the single one is the dropped one and was assimilated. The others recited it with a shaddah, and its meaning is do not intend the bad one from it that you spend. It was narrated on the authority of Adi bin Thabit on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib who said: The Ansar used to take out, when the palm branches were cut, clusters of dates and unripe dates and hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that the poor immigrants would eat from them. A man among them would deliberately put in a cluster of husks, thinking that it was permissible for him to do so due to the large number of clusters that were placed. So the following was revealed about those who did that: And do not aim at the bad meaning the husks and the bad. Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: They used to give charity from the worst of their fruits and the worst of their money and set aside the good for themselves. So God, the Most High, revealed: And do not aim at the bad meaning the bad from it, spending “And you would not take it” meaning the bad unless you close your eyes to it closing your eyes is lowering your gaze. Here he meant to be easygoing and lenient, meaning if one of you had a right over a man and he came to him with this, he would not take it except while he thought that he had closed his eyes to his right and left him. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: If you found it being sold in the market, you would not have taken it at a good price. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’ who said: If that were given to you, you would not take it except out of shyness before its owner and anger. So how can you be satisfied with what you would not be satisfied with for yourselves? This is if all the money is good, then there is no harm in giving the bad, because the people of the shares are partners with him in what he has. But if all his money is bad, then there is no harm in giving the bad, And know that God is free from your charity, Praiseworthy in His actions.
2:268: 268- The devil threatens you with poverty meaning he frightens you with poverty. It is said, I promised him good and I promised him evil. God Almighty said about good, God has promised you many spoils 20- Al-Fath and He said about evil, The Fire which God has promised those who disbelieve 72- Al-Hajj. If good and evil are not mentioned, then you say about good: I promised him and about evil: I threatened him. Poverty is a bad situation and lack of money. Its origin is from the breaking of the vertebrae. The meaning of the verse is that the devil threatens you with poverty and says to the man, Keep your wealth with you, for if you give it in charity you will become poor. And he orders you to commit immorality meaning to be miserly and withhold zakat. Al-Kalbi said: All immorality in the Qur'an is adultery except for this. And God promises you forgiveness from Him meaning for your sins. Bounty meaning provision and replacement. And God is All-Encompassing meaning Rich and Knowing. Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Al-Ziyadi told us, Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, told us, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty says: Son of Adam, spend, and I will spend on you.” And he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The right hand of God is full, and no spending will diminish it. It is generous night and day. Have you seen what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? What is in His right hand has not decreased.” He said And His Throne is over the water, and in His other hand is justice, He raises and lowers. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ubaidullah bin Saeed told us, Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Hisham bin Urwah told us, on the authority of Fatima bint Al-Mundhir, on the authority of Asma’, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: “Spend and do not count, lest God count for you. Do not store away, lest God store away for you.”
2:269: 269. The Almighty said: He gives wisdom to whom He wills. Al-Suddi said: It is prophethood. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Qatada said: The knowledge of the Qur'an, its abrogating and abrogated verses, its decisive and ambiguous verses, its beginning and end, its lawful and unlawful verses, and the like. Ad-Dahhak said: The Qur'an and understanding in it. He said: In the Qur'an there are one hundred and nine abrogating and abrogated verses and one thousand lawful and unlawful verses. The believers cannot abandon them until they learn them. Do not be like the people of Nahrawan who interpreted verses of the Qur'an regarding the people of the Qiblah, when they were revealed regarding the People of the Book, who were ignorant of their knowledge, so they shed blood and looted wealth and testified against us for our misguidance. So stick to the knowledge of the Qur'an, for whoever knows what God revealed will not differ in any of it. Mujahed said: It is the Qur’an, knowledge, and jurisprudence. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on his authority: Correctness in speech and action. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: Knowing the meanings of things and understanding them. And whoever is given wisdom “whoever” is in the nominative case, as an agent for which no one has been named, and wisdom is its predicate. Ya’qub read whoever is given wisdom with a kasra on the ta’, meaning whoever God gives wisdom. The evidence for this is the reading of al-A’mash. And whoever God gives wisdom, it was narrated from al-Hasan. And whoever is given wisdom he said: piety in the religion of God “has certainly been given much good. And none remembers and is admonished “except those of understanding” those with intellects.
2:270: 270. The Almighty’s saying: And whatever you spend in what God has imposed upon you or vowed meaning: what you have made obligatory [you] upon yourselves in obedience to God and you have fulfilled it then God knows it He preserves it until He rewards you for it, and He only said: He knows it, and did not say: He knows it because He referred it back to the other of them like the Almighty’s saying: And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then throws it at an innocent person 112-An-Nisa, and if you wish, you can interpret it as (what) like His saying: And what has been revealed to you of the Book and wisdom by which He instructs you 231-Al-Baqarah, and He did not say with them And for the wrongdoers who place charity in the wrong place out of hypocrisy or give charity from what is forbidden there are no helpers from assistants who ward off the punishment of God from them, and it is the plural of helper, like: noble and noble.
2:271: 271. The Almighty said: If you disclose your charitable expenditures meaning you make them apparent they are excellent meaning: the quality is excellent, and (ma) is in the nominative case, (wahi) is in the accusative case, just as you say, Na'am al-rajul rajul, so if you know, you raise it and say, Na'am al-rajul Zayd, and its original form is Na'am ma, so you connect it. The people of Madinah, other than Warsh, Abu Amr, and Abu Bakr, read: Fananuma with a kasra on the noon and a sukoon on the 'ayn. Ibn 'Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read with a fatha on the noon and a kasra on the 'ayn. Ibn Kathir and Nafi', according to the narration of Warsh, read Ya'qub and Hafs with a kasra on both of them, and all of them are correct dialects. And likewise in Surat al-Nisa. And if you conceal it or give it to the poor that is, give it to the poor in secret it is better for you Better, and everything is acceptable if the intention is sincere, but secret charity is better, and in the hadith: Secret charity extinguishes the wrath of the Lord. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Habib ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Hafs ibn `Aasim, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, or on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are seven whom God will shade in His shade on the Day when there is no shade but His: a just leader, a young man who grew up in the worship of God Almighty, a man whose heart is attached to the mosque when he leaves it until he returns to it, two men who love each other for the sake of God, meet on that basis and part on that basis, a man who remembers God in private and his eyes overflow with tears, a man who is invited by a woman of position and beauty, but he says: I fear God, and a man who gives charity and conceals it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand is spending.” It was said: The verse is about his voluntary charity. As for the obligatory zakat, it is better to make it public so that people will follow his example, just as the obligatory prayer in congregation is better, and the voluntary prayer in the home is better. It was said: The verse is about the obligatory zakat. The relatives were good in it during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for our time, making it public is better so that people do not think badly of him. God the Almighty said: We will remove from you your misdeeds. Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra, and Abu Bakr read it with a nun and raised the ra meaning: And We remove. Ibn Amir and Hafs read it with a ya and raised the ra meaning: And God removes. The people of Medina, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read it with a nun and with the jazm in accordance with the fa in His statement: So it is better for you, because its position is the jazm of the recompense. His statement: From your misdeeds, it was said: From is a relative clause, meaning: We remove from you your misdeeds. It was said: It is for confirmation and partiality, meaning: the minor sins. And God is Aware of what you do.
2:272: 272. You are not responsible for their guidance. Al-Kalbi said that the reason for the revelation of this verse is that some Muslims had relatives and in-laws among the Jews and they used to spend on them before they converted to Islam. When they converted to Islam, they were reluctant to spend on them and wanted them to convert to Islam. Saeed bin Jubair said: They used to give charity to the poor of the People of the Covenant. When the poverty of the Muslims increased, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade giving charity to the polytheists so that need would lead them to enter Islam. So His statement, You are not responsible for their guidance, was revealed, preventing them from giving charity so that they would enter Islam because of their need for it. But God guides whom He wills, and he meant by it the guidance of success. As for the guidance of explanation and calling, it was up to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they gave it to them after the revelation of the verse. And whatever you spend of good meaning money is for yourselves meaning you do it for yourselves and you do not spend except seeking the face of God and whatever you spend of good is a condition like the first, and that is why the letter nun was deleted from them is repaid to you meaning its reward is provided for you, and its meaning is: it is paid to you, and that is why except was included in it and you are not wronged you are not deducted from the reward in any way, and this is in voluntary charity, God the Most High has permitted it to be given to the people of Islam and the people of the covenant, but as for the obligatory charity, it is not permissible to give it except to the Muslims, and they are the people of the two shares mentioned in Surat At-Tawbah.
2:273: 273. The Almighty’s saying: For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God. They differed about the position of this lam: It was said that it is a reference to the position of the lam in His saying (for yourselves) as if he said: And whatever you spend of good is for the poor, and you only spend for yourselves. And it was said: Its meaning is the charities that were mentioned previously. And it was said that its predicate is omitted, its estimate being: For the poor whose description is such and such, a right is obligatory. And they are the poor immigrants. They were about four hundred men. They did not have homes in Medina or clans. And they were in the mosque learning the Qur’an and crushing the date pits during the day. And they would go out in every expedition that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would send out. And they were the people of the suffah, so God, the Almighty, urged the people to do so, so there was a surplus from Him that He brought to them when evening came. Those who are restricted in the cause of God There are sayings about it. Qatada said - and this is the most appropriate - they thought that they were on the path of God. They are unable to travel the earth they are not free to trade and seek a livelihood and they are the people of the suffah whom we mentioned. It was said that they thought that they were on the path of God’s obedience. It was also said that its meaning is that poverty and lack are enough for them to travel the earth. Saeed bin Jubair said that they were people who were wounded with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the path of God, so they became confined, sickness and time prevented them from traveling the earth for jihad. Ibn Zayd said: Its meaning is that because of the great number of times they fought, the entire earth became a war against them and they are not able to travel the earth because of the great number of their enemies. He thinks them Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Asim and Hamza read: He thinks them, and its root is with the fat-ha on the seen, and the others read it with the kasra. The ignorant of their condition are rich from abstinence, that is, from asking and their contentment. Those who do not know their condition think that they are rich. Abstinence is the verb from chastity, which is to leave. It is said: he abstained from something if he took the trouble to abstain. You will recognize them by their mark. Marking, simā’, and ṣamā’: the mark by which something is recognized. They differed about its meaning here. Mujahid said that it is humility and modesty. As-Suddi said: the effect of effort from need and poverty. Ad-Dahhak said: the yellowness of their colors from hunger and distress. It was also said that their clothes were shabby. They do not ask people insistently. Ata’ said: if they have lunch, they do not ask for dinner. It was also said: they do not ask people insistently at all because he said: from self-restraint, and self-restraint is refraining from asking. And because he said: you will recognize them by their mark. If asking was their business, there would be no need to know them by mark. So the meaning of the verse is that they do not ask, in which case they would be insistent. And ‘al-ilḥāq’ means: insistence and obstinacy. Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Karim ibn Hawzan al-Qushayri told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Ismaili told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub told us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam told us, Anas ibn Ayyadh told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “It is better for one of you to take his rope and go and bring a bundle of firewood on his back, and God will suffice him thereby, than to ask people for their things, whether they give him or refuse him.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus’ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The poor person is not the one who goes around among the people, being turned away by a morsel or two, or a date or two. They said: Who is the poor person, O Messenger of God? He said: The one who does not find wealth to make him rich, nor is he noticed to give him charity, nor does he get up and ask people for something. It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever asks while he has an ounce or its equivalent has asked insistently. Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abu Sahl Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzaz told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya bin Addafar told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Ibad Al-Dabry told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Harun bin Riyab, on the authority of Kinanah Al-Adawi Qubaysah bin Mukhariq, who said: “I took on a burden among my people, so I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have taken on a burden among my people, and I have come to you to help me with it. He said: Rather, we will take it on your behalf, O Qubaysah, and give it to them from the charity. Then he said: O Qubaysah, begging is forbidden except in one of three cases: In the case of a man who is afflicted with a calamity that ravages his wealth, so he asks until he has a livelihood, then he stops. In the case of a man who is afflicted with a need, until three wise men from his people testify that begging has become permissible for him, so he asks until he has a livelihood, then he stops. In the case of a man who has taken on a burden, so he asks until he has a livelihood, then he stops. And in the case of a man who has taken on a burden, so he asks until he reaches maturity, then he stops. And in other cases.” Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Muhammad bin Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Qutaybah told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Hakim bin Jubayr, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul-Rahman bin Yazid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever asks people while he has enough to satisfy him, will come on the Day of Resurrection with scratches, scratches, or bruises on his face from his question. It was said: O Messenger of God, what will satisfy him? He said: Fifty dirhams or their value in gold.” God Almighty says: And whatever you spend of good of money then indeed, God is Knowing of it and there is a metaphor for it.
2:274: 274. Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: This verse was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. He had four dirhams and did not own anything else, so he gave away one dirham by night and one dirham by day, one dirham by secretly and one dirham by public. And on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: When the verse was revealed, For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God, Abdur-Rahman bin Awf sent many dinars to the people of the Suffa, and Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, sent a wasq of dates in the middle of the night, so God Almighty revealed about them, Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, the verse. By day, he meant the charity of Abdur-Rahman bin Awf, and by night, secretly, he meant the charity of Ali, may God be pleased with him. Abu Ad-Darda', Makhul, and Al-Awza'i said: It was revealed about those who tie up horses for jihad, for they are fed by night and by day, secretly and publicly. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Talha bin Abi Saeed told us, he said: Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Hafs told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Talha bin Abi Saeed told us, he said: I heard Saeed Al-Maqburi narrating that he heard Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever keeps a horse in the way of God, believing in God and believing in His promise, then its food, drink, dung and urine will be in his scale on the Day of Resurrection. God Almighty said: Then they will have their reward with their Lord. Al-Akhfash said: The report was made with the letter fa because alladhina means whoever and the answer to whoever with the letter fa is the reward, or the meaning of the verse: Whoever spends such-and-such will have his reward with his Lord. And there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
3:131: 275. The Almighty said: Those who consume interest meaning deal with it, and He only specified eating because it is the most intended part of money will not rise meaning on the Day of Resurrection from their graves except as one rises who is being trampled meaning who is being wrestled with by Satan. The root of khatab is striking and trampling, and it is striking without equality. It is said: a she-camel is khatub for one who tramples people and strikes the ground with her legs from touch meaning madness. It is said: a man is touched, so he is possessed if he is insane, and its meaning is: that the one who consumes interest will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection and he is like one who has been struck down. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Abdullah bin Yahya told us, Ya’qub bin Sufyan told us, Ismail bin Salim told us, Ibad bin Ibad told us, on the authority of Abu Harun Al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu Sughayd Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the story of the Night Journey, he said: “Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, took me to many men, each of them with a belly like a huge house, arranged on the path of the people of Pharaoh - and the people of Pharaoh are exposed to the Fire morning and evening - he said: They come like hungry camels, hitting the stones and trees, neither hearing nor understanding, and when the people of those bellies sense them, they stand up, and their bellies tilt them and they fall down, then one of them stands up and one of them tilts his belly and he falls down, and they are unable to move until the people of Pharaoh cover them and return them forward and backward, and that is their torment in the Barzakh between this world and the Hereafter.” He said And the people of Pharaoh will say: O God, never establish the Hour. He said And on the Day of Resurrection it will be said: Enter the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment 46-Ghafir. I said: O Gabriel, who are these? He said: These are the ones who consume interest. They will not rise except as one rises who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. God the Almighty said: That is because they said, ‘Trade is only like usury’ meaning that which befell them because of their saying this and considering it permissible. That is because the people of ignorance, when their money became due to their creditor and they demanded it from him, would pay it and the creditor would say to the one who had the right: ‘Give me more time so that I can give you more money’, and they would do that and say, ‘It is the same for us whether we increase it at the beginning of the sale with profit or at the end of the sale due to the delay’. So God the Almighty denied them and said: God has permitted trade and forbidden usury. Know that usury in the language means increase. God the Almighty said: And whatever you give in interest to increase in the wealth of people meaning to increase it does not increase with God 39-Ar-Rum. Asking for increase through trade is not forbidden in general. Rather, what is forbidden is an increase in a specific manner in a specific wealth, as the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) explained in what Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib informed us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm informed us, Al-Rabi’ informed us, Al-Shafi’i informed us, Abdul Wahhab informed us on the authority of Ayoub bin Abi Tamima on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar and another man narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not sell gold for gold, nor silver for silver, nor wheat for wheat, nor barley for barley, nor dates for dates, nor salt for salt, except equal for equal, eye for eye, hand to hand. But sell gold for silver, and silver for gold, and wheat for barley, and barley for wheat, and dates for salt, and salt for dates, hand to hand, however you wish - and one of them reduces the salt or the dates and one of them increases: whoever increases and increases has committed usury.” This hadith was narrated through the chains of transmission of Muhammad ibn Sirin on the authority of Muslim ibn Yasar and Abdullah ibn Atik on the authority of Ubadah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specified six things. The majority of scholars have held that the ruling on usury is established in these six things by the descriptions in them, and it extends to all money in which those descriptions are found. Then they differed regarding those descriptions. Some people held that the meaning in all of them is one, which is benefit, and they established usury in all money. The majority held that usury is established in dirhams and dinars by one description, and in food items by another description. They differed regarding that description. Some people said: It is established in dirhams and dinars by the description of cash, which is the opinion of Malik and al-Shafi’i. Some people said: It is established by the reason of weight, which is the opinion of the people of opinion, and they established usury in all weighed items such as iron, copper, cotton, and the like. As for the four things, some people said that usury is established in them due to the reason of the measure, which is the opinion of the people of opinion. They established usury in all measured things, whether they are food or not, such as plaster, lime, and the like. A group said that the reason in them is the taste with the measure and weight, so every food that is measured or weighed, usury is established in it, and it is not established in what is not measured or weighed, which is the opinion of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said the same in the old, and he said in the new: usury is established in them due to the description of the taste, and usury is established in all food things from fruits, vegetables, legumes, and medicines, whether they are measured or weighed, based on what was narrated on the authority of Muammar bin Abdullah, who said: I used to hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Food for food, like for like. The sum of usurious money according to Al-Shafi’i is what is a price or food, and usury is of two types: usury of excess and usury of women. If the usurious money is sold for its kind, for example, by selling one of the two currencies for its kind, or selling a food for its kind, such as wheat for wheat and the like, then both types of usury are established in it, so that it is not permissible except if they are equal according to the standard of the Shari’ah. If it is weighed, such as dirhams and dinars, then equality in weight is required. If it is measured, such as wheat for wheat and the like, and dinars, then equality in weight is required. If it is measured, such as wheat and barley, it is sold for its kind, then equality in weight is required, and the exchange is required in the meeting of the contract. If the usurious money is sold for something other than its kind, then consider: If he sold for something that does not agree with it in the description of usury, such as selling dirhams for dinars, or selling wheat for barley, or selling a food for another food of a different kind, then usury of excess is not established in it, so that it is permissible in excess or in bulk, and usury of women is established in it, so that it is stipulated. The exchange in the meeting, and the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Do not sell gold for gold - until he said - except equal for equal in it is the requirement of similarity and the prohibition of excess when the type is the same, and his saying (an eye for an eye) in it is the prohibition of women, and his saying hand to hand however you wish in it is the release of the difference when the type is different with the requirement of exchange in the meeting, this is in the usury of the sale. Whoever lends something on the condition that he will return something better, it is a loan that brings benefit, and every loan that brings benefit is usury. The Almighty said: But whoever receives an admonition from his Lord is a reminder and a warning, and the action was mentioned in response to the admonition and desists from consuming usury then he shall have what is past meaning what has passed of his sin before the prohibition is forgiven him and his affair is with God after the prohibition. If He wills, He will protect him until he persists in desisting, and if He wills, He will abandon him until he returns. It was said: His affair is with God in what He commands him and forbids him and what is permissible for him and what is forbidden for him, and he has no control over his own affairs and whoever returns after the prohibition to consuming usury, considering it permissible for him then those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Ghundar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Awn bin Abi Juhaifa, on the authority of his father, that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the price of blood, the price of a dog, and the earnings of a prostitute, and he cursed the one who consumes usury and the one who pays it, the tattooer and the one who gets tattooed, and the photographer. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad Al-Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Zuhair bin Harb told us, Hisham told us, Abu Al-Zubayr told us on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who consumes usury, the one who pays it, the one who writes it down, and the two who witness it, and he said: They are all the same.” Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Hamid bin Al-Sharqi told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Al-Nadr bin Muhammad told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Yahya - he is Ibn Abi Katheer - told us: Abu Salamah told me, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Usury has seventy forms, the least insignificant of which in the sight of God Almighty is like the one who has intercourse with his mother. 131- Then He frightened them and said: And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers.
2:276: 276. The Almighty said: God destroys interest meaning He diminishes it, destroys it, and takes away its blessing. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, God destroys interest meaning He does not accept any charity, jihad, pilgrimage, or kinship from him. And He increases the charities meaning He makes them fruitful and blesses them in this world, and multiplies the reward and recompense for them in the Hereafter. And God does not like any disbeliever in forbidding interest. Sinful is wicked in consuming it.
2:277: 277. "Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and established prayer and given zakah will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve."
2:278: 278. The Almighty said: O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of interest. Ata' and Ikrimah said: It was revealed about Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib and Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with them, who had advanced dates. When the harvest was due, the owner of the dates said to them: If you take your dues, I will not have enough to support my family. Would you like to take half and delay the other half, and I will double it for you? So they did, and when the time came, they asked for more. report of that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he forbade them, so God revealed this verse. They listened and obeyed and took their principal. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Al-Abbas and Khalid bin Al-Walid, who were partners in the pre-Islamic era, lending usury to Banu Amr bin Umair, people from Thaqeef. Islam came and they had huge amounts of money in usury, so God Almighty revealed this verse. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon on the Day of Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage: “Everything from the affairs of the pre-Islamic era is under my feet, and the bloods of the pre-Islamic era are abolished. The first blood that I abolish is the blood of Ibn Rabi’ah bin Al-Harith. He was breastfed by Banu Sa’d and was killed by Hudhayl. The usury of the pre-Islamic era is all abolished, and the first usury that I abolish is the usury of Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, and it is all abolished.” Muqatil said: It was revealed about four brothers from Thaqeef, Masoud, Abd Yalil, Habib and Rabi’ah, who were the sons of Amr ibn Umair ibn Awf al-Thaqafi. They used to lend money to the sons of al-Mugheerah ibn Abdullah ibn Umair ibn Makhzum, and they used to pay usury. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated Taif, these brothers converted to Islam and sought their usury from the sons of al-Mugheerah. The sons of al-Mugheerah said: By God, we do not pay usury in Islam, and God Almighty has removed it from the believers. So they took their dispute to Atab ibn Asid, who was the governor of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca. Atab ibn Asid wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the story of the two groups, and that was a great sum of money. So God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of usury. If you are believers
2:279: 279. If you do not do so meaning if you do not abandon what remains of the usury then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger Hamza and Asim read in the narration of Abu Bakr fa'adhanu with a long vowel on the weight of amanu, meaning then inform others that you are at war with God and His Messenger, and its origin is from the ear meaning to fall into the ears, and the others read fa'adhanu with a short vowel with a fatha on the dhal meaning then know and be certain of a war from God and His Messenger, and Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: It will be said to the usurer on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Take your weapon for war, the scholars of meanings said: The war of God is the fire and the war of the Messenger of God is the sword. And if you repent, if you abandon usury and turn away from it, “you shall have your capital. You shall not be wronged,” by demanding more, nor shall you be wronged, by decreasing the capital. So when the verse was revealed, Banu Amr al-Thaqafi and those who were dealing with usury among others said: Rather, we will repent to God, for we will not be held accountable for fighting God and His Messenger. So they were satisfied with the capital. Then Banu al-Mughirah complained of the hardship and said: Give us a reprieve until the crops ripen, but they refused to give a reprieve.
2:280: 280. So God the Most High revealed, And if he is in hardship, meaning, if the one who owes the debt is insolvent, the speech was raised by the name of was and did not provide a predicate for it, and that is permissible in the indefinite noun. You say, If he is a righteous man, then honor him. It was said, was means occurred, and in that case it does not need a predicate. Abu Ja`far read hardship with a damma on the seen, then a respite is an order in the form of a predicate, meaning, he has to respite, "to ease, Nafi` read easyness with a damma on the seen, and the others read it with a fatha, and the others read it with a fatha, and Mujahid read easyness with a damma on the seen, as an addition, and its meaning is ease and spaciousness, and that you give in charity, meaning that you leave your principal to the one in difficulty, is better for you if you only knew. Asim read sadaqqu" with a lightened sad, and the others read it with a shaddah. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu al-Tayyib Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman told us, Abu al-Abbas Ismail ibn Abdullah al-Mikali told us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Musa ibn Abdan al-Hafiz told us, Abu Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr ibn al-Sarh told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Hazim, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Qatada, on the authority of his father, that he was seeking a man for a right and he hid from him. He said: What made you do that? He said: Hardship. So he made him swear to that and he swore. Then he called for his document and gave it to him and said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever grants respite to one in difficulty or forgives his debt, God will save him from the distress of the Day of Resurrection. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ubayd God bin Musa told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rab’i, on the authority of Abu Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The angels met the soul of a man who was before you and said: ‘Did you ever do any good? ’ He said: ‘No. ’ They said: ‘Do you remember? ’ He said: ‘No, except that I was a man who used to lend people money, so I used to order my young men to look after the wealthy and forgive the poor. ’ God Almighty said: ‘Forgive him. ’” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah told us, Zaidah told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Rubai, on the authority of Abu Al-Yusr, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever grants respite to a debtor in difficulty or forgives him, God will shade him in His shade on the day when there is no shade but His. A chapter on religion, its proper settlement, and the severity of its command Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Walid told us, Shu’bah told us, Salamah bin Kuhail told us: I heard Abu Salamah in Mina narrating on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, “A man brought a lawsuit against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was harsh with him. His companions said: Leave him, for the one who has a right has a say. Buy him a camel and give it to him. They said: We cannot find anything better than his age. He said: Buy it and give it to him, for the best of you is the one who settles disputes best.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A`raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Delaying payment by a rich person is injustice, so if one of you is followed by a group of people, then let him follow him. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Ibrahim bin Saeed bin Ibrahim told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Umar bin Abi Salamah on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The soul of the believer is suspended by his debt until it is paid off. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi Sa`id al-Maqburi, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Qatada al-Ansari, on the authority of his father, that he said: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, tell me, if I am killed in the cause of God, patiently and seeking reward, advancing and not retreating, will God expiate my sins?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Yes.’ When he turned away, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him or ordered him to be called. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘How did you say that?’ He repeated what he had said to him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Yes, except for debt. Gabriel said the same.’”
2:281: 281. The Almighty said: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. The people of Basra read it with a fatha on the ta', meaning you will be patient with God. The others read it with a damma on the ta' and a fatha on the jim, meaning you will be returned to God Almighty. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: This is the last verse revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to him: Place it at the head of two hundred and eighty verses of Surat Al-Baqarah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived after it for twenty-one days. Ibn Jurayj said: Nine nights. Saeed bin Jubayr said: Seven nights. He died on Monday, two nights before the end of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, when the sun declined in the year eleven after the Hijrah. Al-Sha'bi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the last verse revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the verse on usury.
2:282: 282. The Almighty said: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: When God forbade usury, He permitted the Salam contract and said: I bear witness that the guaranteed advance payment for a specified term has been permitted by God Almighty in His Book and He permitted it in it. Then He said: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. His saying: If you deal with a debt means if you deal with him on credit. It is said: I dealt with him on credit if you dealt with him on credit. He only said on credit after his saying you dealt with him on credit because the debt may be in return or in exchange, so he mentioned it on credit so that the intended meaning of the word is known. It was said: He mentioned it for emphasis, like the saying of God Almighty: nor a bird that flies with its wings 38-Al-An’am. for a specified term means a known period of time, the beginning and the end. The term is required for the price in a sale and in a forward payment so that the owner of the right does not have a claim. It was said that it is its place. In a loan, the term is not required according to most scholars. Then write it down means write down what you dealt with, whether it was a sale, forward payment, or loan. They differed about this writing: Some of them said: It is obligatory, and the majority are of the opinion that it is a recommended matter, so if it is left, there is no problem, like the Almighty’s saying: And when the prayer is concluded, disperse within the land 10-Jumu’ah. Some of them said that writing the debt, giving witnessing, and pledge were obligatory, then all of them were abrogated by His saying: But if one of you trusts another, then let the one who is trusted discharge his trust which is the saying of Al-Sha’bi. Then He explained how to write, so He, the Most High, said: And let a scribe write between you meaning let the debt book be written between the claimant and the claimant in justice meaning with truth without addition or subtraction or advancing a deadline or delaying it. And let no scribe refuse meaning let no scribe refrain from writing. They differed about the obligation of writing on the scribe and the burden of witnessing on him. Some people went to its obligation if he is requested, which is the saying of Mujahid. Al-Hasan said it is obligatory if there is no scribe other than him. Some people said it is recommended and recommended. Ad-Dahhak said it was an obligatory duty on the scribe and the witness, then it was abrogated by His Almighty’s saying: And neither scribe nor witness shall be harmed “as God has taught him” meaning as God has prescribed and commanded him. So let him write and let him who has the right dictate. That is, the person who is required to dictate should acknowledge it with his tongue so that he knows what he owes. Dictation is two eloquent languages with one meaning, which the Qur’an has mentioned. Dictation here and dictation are the words of God Almighty: So it is dictated to him morning and evening 5-Al-Furqan. And let him fear God, his Lord meaning dictation. And let him not diminish anything from it meaning, and let him not diminish anything from the right that he owes. If the one who has the right is foolish meaning, ignorant of dictation, as Mujahid said. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said, a small child. Ash-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said, a fool is a spendthrift who corrupts his wealth or his religion. His saying, or a weak person, meaning an old man, and it was said that he is weak-minded due to dementia or insanity, or he is unable to dictate, due to muteness, disability, foreignness, imprisonment, or absence, which prevents him from attending the scribe, or ignorance of what he has and what he owes, then let his guardian dictate, meaning the value, with justice, meaning with truth and right. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and Muqatil said: He meant by the guardian the one with the right, meaning if the one with the right is unable to dictate, then let the guardian of the right and the owner of the debt dictate with justice because he is more knowledgeable about his right. And bring to witness, meaning and bring to witness, two witnesses, meaning two witnesses, from among your men, meaning the free Muslims, without slaves, children, and infidels. This is the saying of most scholars, and Shuraih and Ibn Sirin permitted the testimony of slaves. But if there are not two men, meaning the two witnesses are not men, then a man and two women, meaning let a man and two women testify. The jurists agreed that the testimony of women with men in matters of wealth is valid until proven by a man and two women. They differed in matters other than wealth. A group held that two testimonies with men are permissible in matters other than punishments, which is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion. A group held that matters other than wealth are not valid except by two just men. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, held that what women are usually aware of, such as childbirth, breastfeeding, marriage, virginity, and the like, is validated by the testimony of a man and two women, and by the testimony of four women. They agreed that the testimony of women is not valid in matters of punishment. The Almighty said: From among the witnesses whom you accept meaning from among those who are acceptable in their religion and trustworthiness. The conditions for [accepting] testimony are seven: Islam, freedom, reason, maturity, justice, chivalry, and the absence of suspicion. The testimony of an unbeliever is rejected because the testimony of those who are known to lie among people is not permissible. So the one who lies about God Almighty is more deserving of having his testimony rejected. The people of opinion permitted the testimony of the People of the Covenant against one another, but the testimony of slaves is not accepted. Shuraih and Ibn Sirin permitted it, and it is the opinion of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him. The insane person has no say until he has testimony, and the testimony of children is not permissible. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, was asked about that? He said: It is not permissible, because God Almighty says: From among the witnesses whom you accept. Justice is a condition, which is that the witness avoids major sins and does not persist in minor ones. Manliness is a condition, which is what is connected to the morals of the soul, which it is known that the one who abandons it has little shame, which is good appearance, conduct, company, and craftsmanship. If a man shows something of himself that his peers are usually ashamed to show, his lack of manliness is known and his testimony is rejected. The absence of suspicion is a condition so that the testimony of an enemy against an enemy is not accepted, even if his testimony against someone else is acceptable, because he is accused in the right of his enemy. The testimony of a man is not accepted for his son or father, even if his testimony against them is acceptable. The testimony of someone who brings benefit to himself with his testimony is not accepted, such as an heir who testifies against a man for killing his inheritor, or who repels harm from himself with his testimony, like the one testified against, like the one testified against who testifies to wound the one he testifies against, because suspicion is established in his testimony. Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi told us, Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Siraj al-Tahhan told us, Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Quraish ibn Sulayman told us, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Makki told us, Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam told us, Marwan al-Fazari told us, on the authority of a sheikh from the people of al-Hirah called Yazid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The testimony of a traitor, male or female, or one who has grudges against his brother, or one who is suspicious of loyalty or kinship, or one who is content with the people of the house is not permissible.” The Almighty said: That one of them should go astray. Hamza read that one of them should go astray with a kasra on the alif, that one should remember with a dhammah on the ra’, and its meaning is the reward and the beginning, and the position of that one of them should go astray is the jussive of the reward, except that it is not clear in the doubling. that one should remember is the nominative because what comes after the fa’ of the reward is the beginning, and the general reading is with a fatha on the alif and a nasb on the ra’ in connection with the first statement, and the position of that one of them should go astray is the accusative of that one of them should remember the other, and the meaning of that one of them should forget, meaning that if one of them forgets her testimony, the other reminds her and she says, Did we not attend such-and-such a gathering and hear such-and-such? Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read: Fa-tadhakkar with a light ta-dakka while the rest read it with a heavy ta-dakka and Dhikr and Idhkar have the same meaning. They are transitive from Dhikr which is the opposite of Nisyan. It was narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah that he said: It is from Dhikr meaning that one of them makes the other Dhikr meaning that their testimony becomes like the testimony of Dhikr. The first is more correct because it is conjoined with Nisyan. God the Almighty said: And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon. It was said that he meant by this when they are called upon to bear witness. He called them witnesses in the sense that they will be witnesses, which is an obligatory matter according to some of them. Some people said: It is obligatory to answer if there is nothing else, and if something else is found then he has a choice, which is the saying of Al-Hasan. Some people said: It is an exhortation and he has a choice in all cases. Some of them said, this is in establishing and performing the testimony, so the meaning of the verse And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon is to perform the testimony that they have borne, which is the saying of Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr. Al-Sha’bi said: The witness has a choice as long as he does not testify. Al-Hasan said: The verse is in both matters, in bearing witness and establishing it if he is free. And do not be weary that is, do not get tired of writing it down and the ha refers to the truth whether it is small the truth or big little or much until its term to the place of truth that that is, the writing is more just more fair with God because He commanded it, and following His command is more just than leaving it and more upright for testimony because writing reminds the witnesses and more suitable and closer to that you do not doubt doubt the testimony except that it is a present trade Asim read them in the accusative case as the predicate of was and implied the noun, its meaning: except that the trade is a present trade or the sale is a trade, and the rest read it in the nominative case and it has two aspects: One of them: to make the universe mean the occurrence of its meaning unless a trade occurs. The second: That you make the noun in the trade and the predicate in the verb, which is His saying, You circulate it among yourselves, meaning, unless it is a present trade that is circulating among you, and the meaning of the verse is unless it is a present trade, hand to hand, that you circulate among yourselves, in which there is no term, There is no blame upon you if you do not write it down, meaning the trade, and bring witnesses when you make a transaction. Ad-Dahhak said: It is a determination, and witnessing is obligatory in the small and large right, in cash or on credit. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, said: The matter in it is to the trust, according to the saying of God Almighty, But if some of you trust others, the verse, and the others said it is an exhortatory matter. The Almighty said: And let neither the scribe nor the witness be harmed. This is a prohibition for the absent, and its original form is yadharur, so one of the two ra’s was assimilated into the other and made the accusative due to the doubling due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, and they differed about it. Some of them said: Its original form is yadharur with a kasra on the first ra’, and the verb was made for the scribe and the witness, meaning the scribe is not harmed so he refuses to write, nor the witness so he refuses to testify, nor the scribe so he adds, subtracts, or distorts what was dictated to him, nor the witness so he testifies to what he was not testified to. This is the opinion of Tawus, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah. Some people said: Its original form is yadharur with a fatha on the ra’ for the passive verb, and they made the scribe and the witness the objects, and its meaning is that a man calls the scribe or the witness while they are busy with important work, and they say, We are busy with important work, so seek someone else. The caller says, God has commanded you to answer, and he insists on them, thus distracting them from their need, so he was forbidden from that and commanded to seek someone else. And if you do what I have forbidden you from of harm, then it is a transgression on you: meaning, a sin and a departure from The command: “And fear God, and God will teach you. And God is Knowing of all things.”
2:283: 283. And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a pledge taken in possession. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read farhan with a damma on the ha’ and the ra’. The rest read farhan, which is the plural of rahn, like baghal and baghal, and mountain and mountains. The plural of rahn is rahan, the plural of plural, as stated by Al-Farra’ and Al-Kisa’i. Abu Ubaid and others said: It is also the plural of rahn, like saqf and saqf. Abu Amr said: We only read farhan to differentiate between them and rahan al-kheel. Ikrimah read farhan with a damma on the ra’ and a sukoon on the ha’. The light and heavy pronunciation of rahn are two dialects, like katab and kutub and rusul and rusul. The meaning of the verse is: And if you are on a journey and cannot find writing instruments, then take a pledge from those to whom you owe, as a guarantee for your money. They agreed that the pledge is not complete except by taking possession. His saying a pledge taken in possession means take a pledge and take possession, even if he pledges and does not hand it over, the pledger is not forced to hand it over, but if he hands it over, it is binding on the pledger so that he is not permitted to take it back as long as some of the right remains. It is permissible in the city. Mortgage in the presence of a writer. Mujahid said: Mortgage is not permissible except during travel when there is no writer, according to the apparent meaning of the verse. According to others, the speech in the verse was based on the most common meaning, not on the condition.
