The evidence for this is what was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mortgaged his armor to Abu al-Shahm the Jew, and that was not while he was traveling nor when he did not have a scribe. If some of you trust others. In Abu’s wording, If he is entrusted, meaning if the one who owes the right is trustworthy with the one who owes the right, then he did not mortgage anything from him because of his good opinion of him. Let him who is entrusted discharge his trust meaning let him fulfill the trust and let him fear God, his Lord in fulfilling the right. Then He returned to addressing the witnesses and said: And do not conceal testimony if you are called upon to give it. He forbade concealing testimony and threatened against it, saying: And whoever conceals it, then his heart is sinful meaning his heart is wicked. It was said: God has not threatened against anything as He has threatened against concealing testimony. He said: Then his heart is sinful meaning that the heart is distorted. We seek refuge in God from that. And God is Knowing of what you do of giving testimony and concealing it.
2:284: 284. To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth as a kingdom [and its inhabitants are His slaves and He is their Owner] "And if you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills, and God is over all things competent." The scholars differed regarding this verse. Some people said: It is specific. Then they differed regarding the reason for [its specificity]. Some of them said: It is connected to the first verse. It was revealed regarding concealing testimony or concealing concealment. God will bring you to account for it, and this is the saying of Al-Sha'bi and Ikrimah. Some of them said: It was revealed regarding those who take the infidels as allies rather than the believers, meaning if you declare what is in yourselves regarding the allegiance of the infidels or keep it secret, God will bring you to account for it, and this is the saying of Muqatil as mentioned in Surat Al-Imran Let not the believers take the infidels as allies rather than the believers until He said: "Say: Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, God knows it" 29-Al-Imran. Most of them believed that the verse is general, then they differed about it. Some people said: It was abrogated by the verse that follows it. The evidence for this is what Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Al-Munhal Al-Dareer and Umayya bin Bastam Al-Aishi told us, and the wording is his, they said: Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Ruh, who is Ibn Al-Qasim, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “When God revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And if you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it’” the verse, he said: This was difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then they knelt down and said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, we have been charged with actions that we are able to bear: prayer, fasting, jihad, and charity, and this verse has been revealed to you and we are not able to bear it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you want to say as the People of the Book before you said: We hear and we disobey? Rather, say: We hear. And we obeyed Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination. When the people read it and their tongues were humbled by it, God revealed after it: “The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they said, “We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination.” When they did that, God abrogated it: “God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake.” He said, Yes. “Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us.” He said, Yes. “Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear.” He said, “And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.” He said, Yes. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, with the same meaning, and he said in all of that: I have done it, instead of saying yes, and this is the saying of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them, and Muhammad bin Sirin, Muhammad bin Kaab, Qatada, and Al-Kalbi agreed with it. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Yusuf al-Isfahani told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Faqih told us, Yaqub ibn Yusuf al-Qazwini told us, al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam al-Arni told us, Misa’ar ibn Kadam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of al-Nabasi, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God Almighty has forgiven my nation for what their souls whisper to them as long as they do not speak about it or act upon it. Some of them said that the verse is not abrogated because abrogation does not apply to report, but rather to commands and prohibitions, and His statement, God will hold you accountable for it is report that abrogation does not apply to. Then they differed in its interpretation. Some people said: God Almighty has established that the heart has earned, so He said, Because of what your hearts have earned 225-Al-Baqarah. So there is no servant of God who conceals an action or declares it from a movement of his limbs or a whisper in his heart except that God informs him of it and holds him accountable for it, then forgives whomever He wills and punishes as He wills. This is the meaning of Al-Hasan’s statement, which is indicated by His statement, Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those you will be questioned 36-Al-Isra’. Others said: The meaning of the verse is that God Almighty holds His creation accountable for all of their actions that they have shown or concealed and will punish them for it, except that He will punish them for what they have concealed and will punish them for it, except that He will punish them for what they have concealed of what they did not know about, such as what happens to them in this world of misfortunes, calamities and matters that they grieve over. This is the statement of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this. The verse, then he said: “O Aisha, this is God’s rebuke of the servant for what befalls him of fever and calamity, even a thorn or a piece of merchandise that he puts in his sleeve and loses it, and is terrified by it until he emerges from his sins as red gold emerges from the bellows.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Al-Layth told me, Yazid bin Abi Habib told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Sinan, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If God wants good for His servant, He hastens his punishment in this world, and if God wants evil for His servant, He withholds his sin from him until He meets him with it on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said, And if you disclose what is in your souls meaning what is in your hearts of what you have resolved to do, or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it. And do not disclose it while you are determined to do it, God will bring you to account for it. As for what your souls have thought of, which you have not resolved to do, then that is something that God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, and He will not hold you accountable for it. Its evidence is the statement of the Most High, God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned 225-Al-Baqarah. Abdullah bin Mubarak said: I said to Sufyan: Is the servant held accountable for his intention? He said: If it is a determination, then he will be held accountable for it. It was said that the meaning of accountability is informing and identifying, and the meaning of the verse: And if you disclose what is in your souls and act upon it or conceal it from what you concealed and intended, God will hold you accountable for it and reward you for it and make it known to you. Then He will forgive the believers, demonstrating His grace, and punish the disbelievers, demonstrating His justice. This is the meaning of what Ad-Dahhak said. It is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and it is indicated by his saying: God will hold you accountable for it, and he did not say He will hold you accountable for it. Accountability is not accountability, and the evidence for it is what Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Ali Az-Zarrad informed us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i informed us, Abu Saeed Al-Haytham bin Kulayb informed us, Isa bin Ahmad Al-Asqalani informed us, Yazid bin Harun informed us, Hammam bin Yahya informed us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Safwan bin Mahraz, who said: I was holding the hand of Abdullah bin Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with them both, and a man came to him and said: How did you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said about the secret conversation? He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “God, the Most High, will bring the believer close on the Day of Resurrection until He places His veil over him, concealing him from the people. He will say: ‘O My servant, do you recognize such and such a sin?’ He will say: ‘Yes, O Lord.’ Then He will say: ‘O My servant, do you recognize such and such a sin?’ He will say: ‘Yes, O Lord.’ Until when he has acknowledged his sins and sees in himself that he has perished, He will say: ‘I concealed them for you in this world, and I have forgiven you today.’ Then he will be given his book of good deeds. As for the disbeliever and the hypocrites, the witnesses will say: ‘These are the ones who lied about their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.’” Hud 18. The Almighty said: He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Amir, `Asim, and Ya`qub raised the ra’ and the ya’, and the others made them jazm. The raising is for the beginning and the jazm is for the arrangement. Tawus narrated on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, He forgives whom He wills for the great sin and punishes whom He wills for the small sin. “He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned.” And God is over all things competent. 230-Al-Anbiya’.
2:285: 285. The Almighty said: The Messenger believed meaning he believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and the believers - all of them believed in God meaning each one of them, and therefore he made the verb singular and His angels and His books and His messengers Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: His book, in the singular meaning the Qur’an, and it was said that its meaning is plural even if it was mentioned in the singular form like the Almighty’s saying: So God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners and sent down with them the Book 213-Al-Baqarah and others read and His books in the plural like the Almighty’s saying: And His angels and His books and His messengers 136-An-Nisa, We make no distinction between any of His messengers so we believe in some and disbelieve in others as the Jews and Christians did, and in it is an implied meaning they say we do not make a distinction, and Ya’qub read la yafareq with a ya’ so it is report about the Messenger, or its meaning is he does not make a distinction between all, and he only said (between one) and did not say between individuals because one is for the individual and the plural, God Almighty said: So what “From among you, from one of them, two barriers 47-Al-Haqqah And they said, ‘We hear’ your words and obey’ your command. It was narrated on the authority of Hakim on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with them both, that Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when this verse was revealed: God has praised you and your nation, so ask and you will be given. So he asked by God’s prompting, and He said: Your forgiveness, which is an accusative of the source, meaning forgive, Your forgiveness, or we ask You for Your forgiveness. “Our Lord, to You is the final destination. God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity.” The apparent meaning of the verse is to fulfill a need, and in it is an implied question, as if He said: And they said, Do not charge us except [with that within] our capacity, and He answered, meaning, God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, meaning its ability. Wisdom is a name for what is within a person’s capacity and does not make it difficult for him. They differed in its interpretation, so Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and Ata’ and most of the commentators went to the view that he meant by it the self-talk mentioned in God Almighty’s statement: And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, as we mentioned. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: They are the believers in particular. He made their religious affairs easy for them and did not charge them with anything in it except what they are able to do, as God Almighty said: God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship. “Hardship” 185-Al-Baqarah and God Almighty said: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty 78-Al-Hajj
2:286: 286. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah was asked about the Almighty’s saying, God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. He said: Except that He makes it easy and does not charge it beyond its capacity. This is a good statement because capacity is less than one’s ability. The Almighty said: For it is what it has earned meaning for the soul is what it has done of good, for it is its reward and recompense. And upon it is what it has acquired of evil and upon it is its burden. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us meaning do not punish us if we forget some of them made it from forgetfulness which is absent-mindedness. Al-Kalbi said that if the Children of Israel forgot something that they were commanded to do or made a mistake, the punishment was hastened for them, so something of food or drink was forbidden to them according to that sin, so God commanded the believers to ask Him to stop punishing them for that. It was said that it is from forgetfulness which is abandonment like the Almighty’s saying: They forgot God, so He forgot them 67-At-Tawbah. The Almighty’s saying: or we erred. It was said that its meaning is intention and deliberation. It is said: So-and-so erred if he did it deliberately. God Almighty said: Indeed, their killing was a great mistake. 31-Al-Isra’. Ata’ said: If we forgot or erred, meaning: if we were ignorant or intentional, and most of them made it from the mistake which is ignorance and forgetfulness, because what was intentional of the sin is not forgiven, rather it is in the will of God, and the mistake is forgiven. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The mistake, forgetfulness, and what they were forced to do are lifted from my nation. God the Almighty said: Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden meaning a heavy covenant that we cannot fulfill, so that you punish us for breaking it and abandoning it, as You placed it upon those before us meaning the Jews, so they did not fulfill it, so you punished them. This is the saying of Mujahid, Ata’, Qatadah, As-Suddi, Al-Kalbi and a group, which is indicated by God’s saying: And you took upon you My covenant 81-Al Imran, meaning My covenant. It was said: Its meaning is do not be strict or harsh upon us as You made it strict upon the Jews before us, and that is because God imposed fifty prayers upon them and ordered them to pay a quarter of their wealth in zakat, and whoever gets impurity on his garment, he cuts it off, and whoever commits a sin, his sin is written on his door, and similar burdens and shackles. This is what Uthman, Ata’, Malik ibn Anas, Abu Ubaidah and a group said, which is indicated by God the Almighty’s saying: And He will remove from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them 157-Al A’raf. It was said: A burden is a sin for which there is no repentance, meaning He protected us from something like it. The original meaning is: In reason and wisdom. The Almighty said: Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. That is, do not charge us with actions that we cannot bear. It was said that it is self-talk and whispering. It was narrated on the authority of Makhul that he said: It is the passion. It was said: The passion is the intensity of desire. And on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: It is love. And on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, he said: Passion. And Ibn Jurayj said: It is the transformation of monkeys and pigs. And it was said: It is the gloating of enemies. And it was said: It is division and severance. We seek refuge in God from it. The Almighty says: And pardon us meaning overlook and erase our sins. And forgive us means cover our sins and do not disgrace us. And have mercy on us for we do not attain the work except through Your obedience, and we do not abandon Your disobedience except through Your mercy. You are our Master means our supporter, protector, and guardian. So give us victory over the disbelieving people. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the words of God Almighty: Your forgiveness, our Lord, God Almighty said: I have forgiven you. And regarding His words: Do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake, he said: I will not impose blame upon you. “Our Lord, and do not place a burden upon us,” he said: I will not place a burden upon you, “And do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear,” he said: I will not place a burden upon you, “And pardon us,” to the end of which he said: I have pardoned you, and forgiven you, and have had mercy upon you and given you victory over the disbelieving people. And whenever Muadh bin Jabal finished reciting Surat Al-Baqarah, he would say: Aameen. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Abu Usama told me, Malik bin Mughul told me, on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Adi, on the authority of Talha bin Ali bin Masraf, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is in the sixth heaven. Whatever ascends from the earth ends at it and is taken from it, and whatever descends above it ends at it and is taken from it. He said: When that which covers the Lote Tree covers it (al-Najm 53:16). He said: A bed of gold. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given three things: the five daily prayers, and he was given the last verses of Surat Al-Baqarah, and he was forgiven for those of his nation who do not associate anything with God of the grave sins. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, on the authority of Abu Na’im Abd al-Malik ibn al-Husayn al-Isfarayini, on the authority of Abu Awana Ya’qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz, on the authority of Yunus and Ahmad ibn Shaiban, who said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abu Mas’ud, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The two verses from the end of Surat al-Baqarah, whoever recites them at night, they will suffice him. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Al-Ala’ bin Abdul-Jabbar told us, Jumad bin Salamah told us, Al-Ash’ath bin Abdul-Rahman Al-Jarmi told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Al-Ash’ath Al-San’ani, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty wrote a book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and He sent down two verses from it with which He concluded Surat Al-Baqarah. So do not recite them in a house for three nights, lest Satan come near it.”
3:1: 1- In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, the Almighty's saying "Alif, Lam, Meem. God" Al-Kalbi, Al-Rabi' bin Anas, and others said: These verses were revealed about the delegation of Najran, and they were sixty riders who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among them were fourteen men from their nobles, and among the fourteen were three men to whom their affairs would be referred: Al-Aqib: the leader of the people and their advisor, who they would not act except according to his opinion, and his name was Abd Al-Masih, and Al-Sayyid: their leader and the owner of their saddle, and his name was Al-Ayham, and Abu Haritha bin Alqamah, their bishop and their rabbi. They entered the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) when he prayed the afternoon prayer, wearing the clothes of the Habrat - cloaks and robes in the beauty of the men of Al-Harith bin Kaab. Those who saw them said: We have never seen a delegation like them. It was time for their prayer, so they stood up to pray in the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: Leave them. So they prayed facing the east. Then the master and the follower of the religion submitted. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to them: Become Muslims. They said: We became Muslims before you. He said: “You have both lied. What prevents you from Islam is your claim that God has a son, your worship of the cross, and your eating of pork.” They said: If Jesus is not the son of God, then who is his father? They all argued with him about Jesus. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to them: Do you not know that there is no son except that he resembles his father? They said: Yes. He said: Do you not know that our Lord is in charge of everything, He protects it and provides for it? They said: Yes. He said: Does Jesus have any control over that? They said: No. He said: Do you not know that nothing is hidden from God, whether on earth or in heaven? They said: Yes. He said: Does Jesus know anything about that except what he knows? They said: No. He said: For our Lord formed Jesus in the womb as He willed and our Lord has no form and no likeness and our Lord does not eat or drink. They said: Yes. He said: “Do you not know that his mother carried Jesus as a woman carries, then she gave birth to him as a woman gives birth to her child, then he was nourished as a child is nourished, then he would eat, drink and relieve himself?” They said: Yes. He said: How can this be as you claim? They remained silent, and God, the Most High, revealed the beginning of Surat Al Imran up to eighty-some verses. The Almighty said: Alif, Lam, Meem with an open mim and connected according to the general public. The opening of the mim is due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. It was moved to the lightest of the movements. Abu Yusuf and Yaqub bin Khalifah al-A’sha read on the authority of Abu Bakr: Alif, Lam, Meem with an interrupted mim with the intention of stopping, then he interrupted the hamza for the beginning and made it according to the language of those who interrupt the alif of connection.
3:2: 2- The Almighty’s saying God is the beginning and what follows is the predicate, and the Living, the Self-Sustaining is an attribute of Him.
3:3: 3- He sent down to you the Book meaning the Qur'an in truth with honesty confirming what was before it the books before it in monotheism, prophethood, report and some laws And He sent down the Torah and the Gospel * before and He only said: And He sent down the Torah and the Gospel, because the Torah and the Gospel were sent down all at once, and He said in the Qur'an was sent down because it was sent down in detail, and sending down is for multiplication, and the Torah, the Basrans said: Its origin is wariyah on the weight of faw'ala, like dawahlah and hawqala, so the first waw was changed to a ta' and the open ya' was made an alif so it became Torah, then it was written with a ya' according to the origin of the word, and the Kufians said: Its origin is taf'ala like tawthiyah and tawfiyah, so the ya' was changed to an alif according to the language of T They say for a slave girl, jara’a, and for a recommendation, tawsa’a. Its origin is from their saying: Warraa al-Zand when its fire comes out, and I lit it. God Almighty said: Have you seen the fire which you kindle? (al-Waqi’ah 56:71). So it was called the Torah because it is light and radiance. God Almighty said: And a radiance and a reminder for the righteous. (al-Anbiya 21:48). It was said that it is from the Torah, which is keeping a secret and alluding to it, and most of the Torah was alluding without being explicit. The Gospel: It is a verbal noun from the root najl, which means to go out, and from it the child was called najl because of his going out, so the Gospel was called by this name because God Almighty brought him out studying the truth and healthy. It is said: Nahu is from najl, which means spaciousness of the eye, and it was called by this name because He sent down spaciousness and light to them. It was said: The Torah in Hebrew is toor, and toor means the law, and the Gospel in Syriac is anqalion, and it means the crown.
3:4: 4- The Almighty’s saying: A guidance for mankind A guide for those who follow it, and He did not repeat it because it is a source, And He sent down the Criterion which distinguishes between truth and falsehood. Al-Suddi said: In the verse there is an advancement and delay, and its meaning is that He sent down the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion as guidance for mankind. God Almighty says: “Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God will have a severe punishment. And God is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.”
3:5: 5- Nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven.
3:6: 6- It is He who shapes you in the wombs however He wills male or female, white or black, beautiful or ugly, perfect or imperfect, There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise. This is in response to the Najran delegation of Christians, when they said: Jesus was born of God, so it is as if he is saying: How can God have a son when God Almighty formed him in the womb. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul Rahman bin Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Ansari told us, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Abu Khaithama Zuhair bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, he said: I heard Abdullah bin Masoud say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he is the truthful and believed one, told us: “The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty clean days, then he is a clot for a similar period, then he is a lump of flesh for a similar period, then God sends to him the angel” or he said: The angel sends to him with four words, and he writes down his provision, his deeds, his life span, and whether he will be wretched or happy. He said: “And one of you may do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only an arm’s length between him and it, then the Book overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of Hell and enters it. And one of you may do the deeds of the people of Hell until there is only an arm’s length between him and it, then the Book overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad Al-Farsi told us, Abu Ahmad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Abu Al-Tufayl, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Asid, who reported it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The angel enters upon the sperm after it has settled in the womb for forty or forty-five nights and says: ‘O Lord, will I be miserable or happy?’ And he writes that down, and he says: ‘O Lord, will I be male or female?’ And they write it down, and his deeds, his life span, and his provision are written down, then the scrolls are folded up and nothing is added to them or taken away from them.”
3:7: 7- The Almighty said: It is He who has sent down to you the Book, in it are verses that are precise clear and detailed, they are called precise from the rulings, as if He made them precise and prevented creation from tampering with them due to their clarity and the clarity of their meaning They are the mother of the Book meaning its origin that is worked upon in the rulings, and He only said: They are the mother of the Book and did not say the mothers of the Book that all the verses in their completeness and gathering are like one verse, and the speech of God is one and it was said: its meaning is each verse of them is the mother of the Book as He said: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign 50-Al-Mu'minun meaning each one of them is a sign and another the plural of another and He did not decline it because it is modified from the other, like: Amr and Zafar similar so if it is said how did He differentiate here between the precise and the ambiguous when He made the entire Qur'an precise in another place? He said: “Alif, Lam, Ra. This is a Book whose verses are perfected” Hud 1. And He made it all similar in another place, saying: God has sent down the best statement, a consistent Book Az-Zumar 23. It was said: When He made the whole perfect, He meant that the whole is true, with no frivolity or playfulness in it. And when He made the whole similar, He meant that some of it resembles some of it in truth, honesty, and goodness. And here He made some of it perfect and some of it similar. Scholars differed about it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The decisive verses are the three verses in the form of al-An’am 6:Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you’ 151, and its counterpart in the Children of Israel: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him 23-Al-Isra’ the verses. And it was narrated from him that he said: The ambiguous verses are the letters of spelling at the beginning of the surahs. Mujahideen Ikrimah said: The decisive verse is that which contains what is permissible and what is forbidden, and other than that it is ambiguous, some of it resembling some of it in truth and some of it confirming some of it, like the Almighty’s saying: And He misguides thereby only the wicked 26-Al-Baqarah And He places defilement upon those who do not use reason 100-Yunus. Qatada, Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: The definitive verses of the Qur’an are the abrogating verses that are acted upon, and the ambiguous verses are the abrogated verses that are believed in but not acted upon. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The definitive verses of the Qur’an are its abrogators, its lawful and unlawful verses, its limits and its obligations, and what is believed in and acted upon. The ambiguous verses are its abrogated verses, its beginning and end, its examples and its categories, and what is believed in but not acted upon. It was said: The definitive verses are what God has informed creation of their meaning, and the ambiguous verses are what God has kept to Himself knowledge, and no one has a way to know it, such as the report about the signs of the Hour, such as the emergence of the Antichrist, the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, the rising of the sun from the West, the establishment of the Hour, and the end of the world. Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Al-Zubayr said: You have glimpsed what cannot bear more than one interpretation, and the ambiguous is what bears more than one interpretation. It was said: The decisive is what its meaning is known and its arguments are clear and its evidence is evident and not ambiguous. The ambiguous is what its knowledge is attained by contemplation, and the common people do not know the details of the truth in it from the false. Some of them said: The decisive is what is independent in its meaning, and the ambiguous is what cannot stand alone in itself except by referring it to something else. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said in the narration of Bazan: The letters of the spelling at the beginning of the surahs are similar. This is because a group of Jews, including Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf and their peers, came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Huyayy said to him: We have heard that Alif, Lam, Meem was revealed to you. We ask you by God, was it revealed to you? He said: Yes. He said: If that is true, then I know the duration of your nation’s reign, which is seventy-one years. Was anything else revealed? He said: Yes Alif, Lam, Meem. He said: This is more, it is one hundred and sixty-one years. He said: Is anything else? He said: Yes Alif, Lam, Ra. He said: This is more, it is two hundred and seventy-one years. You have confused us, so we do not know whether we should take much of it or little of it. We are among those who do not believe in this. Then God the Almighty revealed: “It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific.” As for those in whose hearts is deviation meaning a deviation from the truth, and it was said doubt, they follow that of it which is ambiguous. They differed regarding the meaning of this verse. Al-Rabi’ said: They are the delegation of Najran who argued with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding Jesus, peace be upon him, and they said to him: Do you not claim that he is the Word of God and a spirit from Him? He said: Yes. They said: That is enough for us. Then God revealed this verse. Al-Kalbi said: They are the Jews who sought knowledge of the fate of this nation and extracted it by calculating the letters. Ibn Jurayj said: They are the hypocrites. Al-Hasan said: They are the Khawarij. When Qatada read this verse: As for those in whose hearts is deviation, he said: If they are not the Kharijites and the Sabians, then I do not know who they are. It was said: They are all the innovators. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Maslama told us, Yazid bin Ibrahim Al-Tastari told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with them both, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: “It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific” - up to His saying: Those of understanding. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So if you see those who follow that of it that is unspecific, then those are the ones whom God has named, so beware of them. The Almighty’s statement: Seeking discord means seeking polytheism. This was stated by Al-Rabi’ and Al-Suddi. Mujahid said: seeking doubts and confusion so that they may mislead their ignorant ones. And seeking its interpretation means its interpretation and its scholars. Its evidence is the Almighty’s statement: I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience 78-Al-Kahf. It was said: seeking its outcome, which is seeking the end of this nation from the calculation of the letters. Its evidence is the Almighty’s statement: That is better and more suitable for final outcome 350-Al-Isra’, meaning an outcome. God the Almighty says: And none knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge. The scholars differed in the structure of this verse. Some people said: The waw in His statement and those firmly rooted in knowledge is a conjunction waw, meaning that God knows the interpretation of the ambiguous and those firmly rooted in knowledge know it, and with their knowledge, they say, ‘We believe in it.’ This is the statement of Mujahid and Al-Rabi’. Based on this, His statement they say is a state, meaning: and those firmly rooted in knowledge say, We believe in it. This is like His statement, the Almighty: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God and to the Messenger and to near relatives. 7-Al-Hashr Then He said: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes. 8-Al-Hashr until He said: And those who were established in the home and in faith before them. 9-Al-Hashr Then He said: And those who came after them. This is a conjunction to what came before. Then He said: They say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us.’ 10-Al-Hashr meaning that despite their deserving the spoils, they say, Our Lord, forgive. For us, that is, saying in the present tense. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he used to say about this verse: I am among those who are firmly grounded in knowledge. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid: I am among those who know its interpretation. The majority of scholars have said that the waw in his statement and the firmly rooted is a waw of resumption, and the discussion ends with his statement: and none knows its interpretation except God, which is the statement of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Aisha, and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them, and the narration of Tawus on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, and al-Hasan and most of the followers said the same, and al-Kisa’i, al-Farra’, and al-Akhfash chose it. They said: None knows the interpretation of the ambiguous except God, and it is permissible for the Qur’an to have an interpretation that God has kept to Himself, and has not informed any of His creation of it, just as He has kept to Himself the knowledge of the Hour, the time of the sun rising from the West, the emergence of the Antichrist, the descent of Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him, and the like. Creation is committed to believing in the ambiguous, and believing in and acting upon the decisive. What confirms this is the reading of Abdullah: Its interpretation is with God, and the firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it.’ In the wording of Ubayy: And the firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it.’ Omar bin Abdul Aziz said: In this verse, the knowledge of those firmly grounded in knowledge of the interpretation of the Qur’an ended with them saying, We believe in it, all of it is from our Lord. This is the correct interpretation of the Arabic language and is more similar to the apparent meaning of the verse. God the Almighty says: And those firmly rooted in knowledge meaning those who have entered into knowledge, they are those who have mastered their knowledge to the point that no doubt enters into their knowledge. Its origin is from the firmness of something in something, which is its stability. It is said: Faith has become firmly rooted in the heart of so-and-so, firmly and firmly. It was said: Those firmly rooted in knowledge are the scholars and believers of the People of the Book, such as Abdullah bin Salam and his companions. The evidence for this is the Almighty’s statement: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them An-Nisa’ 162, meaning those who study the knowledge of the Torah. Malik bin Anas, may God be pleased with him, was asked about those firmly rooted in knowledge. He said: The scholar who acts according to what he knows and follows it. It was said: Those firmly rooted in knowledge are those who find four things in their knowledge: piety between themselves and God, humility between themselves and creation, asceticism between themselves and the world, and struggle between themselves and themselves. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: By their saying, We believe in it, God Almighty called them firmly rooted in knowledge. Their firmness in knowledge is their saying, We believe in it, meaning in the ambiguous. All is from our Lord, the decisive and the ambiguous, the abrogating and the abrogated, what we know and what we do not know. And none will remember, and none will take heed of what is in the Qur’an, except those of understanding, those with intellects.
3:8: 8- The Almighty said: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate meaning, the firm-minded say: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate meaning, do not let them turn away from the truth and guidance, as You have deviated the hearts of those in whose hearts is deviation, after You have guided us and guided us to Your religion and to belief in the clear and ambiguous verses of Your Book, and grant us from Yourself give us from Yourself mercy as success and confirmation of what we are upon of faith and guidance. Ad-Dahhak said: as a transgression and forgiveness, for You are the Giver. Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar ibn Ismail al-Tamimi told us, Abu al-Qasim Hamza ibn Yusuf al-Sahmi told us, Abu Ahmad ibn Adi al-Hafiz told us, Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim al-Qurashi, known as Ibn al-Rawas al-Kabir in Damascus told us, Abu Musahir Abd al-A’la ibn Musahir al-Ghasani told us, Sadaqah told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Jabir told us, Bishr ibn Ubayd God told us, he said: I heard Abu Idris al-Khawlani say: Al-Nawwas ibn Sam’an al-Kalabi told us, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no heart but that it is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills to make it straight, He makes it straight, and if He wills to deviate, He deviates it.” And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “O God, O Changer of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion, and the scale is in the hand of the Most Merciful. He raises some people and lowers others until the Day of Resurrection.” Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hairi told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Abdul Rahim bin Munib told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Saeed bin Iyas Al-Jariri told us, on the authority of Ghanim bin Qais, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of the heart is like a feather in a desert land, turned upside down by the winds.
3:9: 9- The Almighty said: Our Lord, You will surely gather the people for a Day, meaning to fulfill a Day. It was said: The lam means in, meaning on a Day about which there is no doubt, meaning there is no suspicion, and it is the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God does not fail in His promise, and it is a verbal noun from the word promise.
3:10: 10- The Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieve - neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God. Al-Kalbi said: From the punishment of God. Abu Ubaidah said: From means with, meaning with God. And those are the fuel of the Fire, like the way of the people of Pharaoh.
3:11: 11- Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, and Ikrimah and Mujahid said: Like the actions of the people of Pharaoh and their deeds in disbelief and denial. Ata', Al-Kisa'i and Abu Ubaidah said: Like the way of the people of Pharaoh. Al-Akhfash said: Like the way of the people of Pharaoh and their manners. Al-Nadr bin Shumayl said: Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh, meaning the habit of these disbelievers in denying the Messenger and rejecting the truth like the habit of the people of Pharaoh, and those before them the disbelievers of the past nations, like Aad, Thamud and others denied Our signs, so God seized them so God punished them for their sins. It was said that the structure of the verse is: Indeed, those who disbelieve - neither their wealth nor their children will avail them when the punishment and vengeance come, like the people of Pharaoh and the disbelievers of the past nations, We seized them, so their wealth and children will not avail them, and God is severe in penalty.
3:12: 12- The Almighty said: Say to those who disbelieve, 'You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell.' Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read them with a ya' in both, meaning that they will be overcome and gathered together. The others read them with a ta' in both, as a direct address, meaning: Say to them: You will be overcome and gathered together. Muqatil said: He meant the polytheists of Mecca, meaning: Say to the disbelievers of Mecca: You will be overcome on the day of Badr and gathered together to Hell in the Hereafter. So when this verse was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them on the day of Badr: Indeed, God will overcome you and gather you together to Hell. Some of them said: What is meant by this verse is the Jews. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: The Jews of Medina said when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated the polytheists on the day of Badr: This, by God, is the prophet whom Moses gave us glad tidings of. No banner will be returned to him. They wanted to follow him. Then some of them said to each other: Do not rush until you see another battle of his. Then when the day of Uhud came and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were afflicted, they doubted and were overcome by misery, so they did not submit. There was a covenant between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a period of time, but they broke that covenant. Ka`b ibn al-Ashraf set out with sixty riders to Mecca to provoke them, so they resolved to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God Almighty revealed this verse about them. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of his men, and Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated the Quraysh at Badr and returned to Medina, he gathered the Jews in the market of Banu Qaynuqa and said: O group of Jews, beware of God as happened to the Quraysh on the day of Badr and submit before He happens to you as happened to them, for you have known that I am a prophet sent by God. You will find that in your book. They said: O Muhammad, do not be deceived by the fact that you met a people who were ignorant of war, and you took advantage of them. By God, if we had fought you, you would have known that we are the people. Then God Almighty revealed: Say to those who disbelieve, ‘You will be overcome’ ‘defeated’ ‘and gathered’ ‘in the Hereafter to Hell’ ‘and evil is the resting place’ meaning evil is the bed, meaning the Fire.
3:13: 13- The Almighty said: There has certainly been a sign for you, and He did not say there has certainly been a sign for you, and sign is feminine because He referred it back to the explanation, meaning there has certainly been a statement for you, so He went to the meaning. Al-Farra’ said: It was mentioned because the adjective came between the verb and the feminine noun, so the verb was mentioned. Everything that came in this manner has its meaning. The meaning of the verse is: It has been a sign for you, i.e. a lesson and evidence of the truth of what I say, that you will be overcome. In two groups two groups, and its origin is the faya of war, because some of them return to each other. They met on the day of Badr. A group fighting in the way of God obeying God, and they were the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. They were three hundred and thirteen men, seventy-seven men from the Muhajireen, and two hundred and thirty-six from the Ansar. The standard-bearer of the Muhajireen was Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and the standard-bearer of the Ansar was Sa’d ibn Ubadah. There were seventy camels and horsemen among them, a horse for Al-Miqdad ibn Amr, and a horse for Marthad ibn Abi Marthad, and most of them were his men. They had six coats of mail and eight swords as weapons with them. God the Almighty said: And another disbelieving group meaning another entire group, and they are the polytheists of Mecca, and they were nine hundred and fifty men from the fighters, their leader was Utbah bin Rabi’ah bin Abd Shams, and among them were one hundred horses, and the Battle of Badr was the first battle witnessed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They see them twice as many The people of Medina and Ya’qub read it with the ta’, meaning you see, O group of Jews, the people of Mecca twice as many as the Muslims, and that is because a group of Jews were present at the Battle of Badr to see who the circle would be on, and they saw the polytheists twice as many as the Muslims, and they saw the victory with that for the Muslims, so that was a miracle and a sign. The others read it with the ya’ and differed about its meaning: Some of them made the flag for the Muslims, then it has two interpretations, one of them is that the Muslims see the polytheists twice as many as they are, so if it is said: How did he say twice as many when they were three times as many? It was said: This is like a man saying when he has a dirham, I need twice this dirham, meaning twice as much as it, so it would be three dirhams. The second interpretation - and it is more correct - is that the Muslims saw the polytheists as twice the number of themselves. God made them seem small in their eyes until they saw them as six hundred and twenty-six. Then God made them seem small in their eyes in another situation until they saw them as the number of themselves. Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him said: We looked at the Shamrak and saw that they were weaker than us, then we looked at them and did not see them exceed us by a single man. Then God made them seem small in their eyes again in another situation until they saw them as the number of themselves Ibn Mas’ud (may God be pleased with him said): Until he said to a man next to me: Do you see them as seventy? He said: I saw them as one hundred. Some of them said: The vision is a deterrent to the polytheists, meaning that the polytheists see the Muslims as twice their number. God made them few in number before the battle in the eyes of the polytheists so that the polytheists would be bold with them and not turn away. Then when they began to fight, God made them many in the eyes of the polytheists so that they would be cowardly, and made them few in the eyes of the believers so that they would be bold. That is what God Almighty said: And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes and made you as few in their eyes 44-Al-Anfal. The Almighty said: As seen by the eye meaning in the opinion of the eye, in the accusative case, by removing the letter of manufacture. “And God supports with His victory whomever He wills. Indeed in that” which I mentioned is a lesson for those of vision for those with reason. And it was said for those who saw both groups.
3:14: 14- The Almighty said: Beautified for people is the love of desires We pluralize desire, which is what the soul calls for, of women He began with them because they are the snares of Satan, and sons and qintars The plural of qintar, and they differed about it. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: A qintar is a lot of money, one on top of the other. Muadh bin Jabal, may God be pleased with him, said: A qintar is one thousand two hundred ounces. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said and Al-Dahhak: One thousand two hundred mithqals. And from them is another narration: Twelve thousand dirhams and a thousand dinars is the blood money of one of you. And from Al-Hasan: The qintar is the blood money of one of you. And Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah said: It is one hundred thousand and one hundred min, one hundred pounds, one hundred mithqals, and one hundred dirhams. And Islam came on the day it came and in Mecca there were one hundred men who had qintar. And Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Qatadah said: Eighty thousand. And Mujahid said: Seventy thousand. And from Al-Suddi he said: Four thousand mithqals. And Al-Hakam said: The qintar is the money between the sky and the earth. And Abu Nadrah said: It is the amount of a bull’s musk filled with gold or silver. It was called Qintar from the meaning of Ihkam. It is said: I Qintart something if you made it perfect, and from this the name Qantara was given. God the Almighty said: Al-Muqantara Ad-Dahhak said: The fortified and well-built. Qatada said: It is the many arranged one on top of the other. Yaman said: Al-Madfouna. As-Suddi said: The struck and engraved until it became dirhams and dinars. Al-Farra’ said: The doubled, so the qintars are three and the qintars are nine of gold and silver. It was said that gold was called gold because it goes and does not remain, and silver because it is shaken, meaning it is scattered. And the branded horses. Horses are a plural that does not have a singular from the word, and its singular is horse, like people and women and the like. Al-Musamma. Mujahid said: It is the well-marked and beautiful. Ikrimah said: Its branding is its beauty. Al-Saeed bin Jubayr said: It is the shepherdess. It is said: The horses are branded and branded. Al-Hasan and Abu Ubaidah said: It is the marked from the mark and the mark is the sign. Then some of them said: Its mark is the likeness and color, and this is the saying of Qatada. It was said: The branding. And livestock is the plural of blessings, which are camels, cows, and sheep. It is a plural that has no singular form. And tillage means crops. That which we mentioned is the enjoyment of worldly life indicates that it is a enjoyment that will perish. And God has with Him the best destination meaning the place of return. It contains a disinterest in this world and an encouragement for the hereafter.
3:15: 15- The Almighty said: “Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who fear God, there are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and purified spouses and approval from God.” The general public read it with a kasra on the ra’, and Abu Bakr narrated on the authority of Asim with a damma on the ra’, and they are two vowels like ‘adwan and ‘adwanah. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Sulaiman told us, Ibn Wahb told me, Malik told me, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Blessed and Exalted, says to the people of Paradise: O people of Paradise. They say: At your service, our Lord, and at your pleasure, and all good is in your hands. He says: Are you satisfied? They say: Why should we not be satisfied, O Lord, when you have given us what you have not given to any of your creation? He says: Shall I not give you something better than that? They say: O Lord, what is better than that? He says: I will bestow upon you My pleasure, and I will never be angry with you after that.”
3:16: 16- The Almighty said: And God is Seeing of the servants * Who say If you wish, you can make the place of those a genitive in response to His statement for those who feared God. And if you wish, you can make it a nominative in the beginning. It is possible that it is an accusative, meaning I mean those who say, Our Lord, we have believed “We have spoken the truth” So forgive us our sins “Conceal them for us and overlook them” And save us from the punishment of the Fire.
3:17: 17- The patient and the truthful If you wish, you can put it in the accusative case as a compliment, and if you wish, you can put it in the genitive case as a description, meaning the patient in carrying out the command and refraining from committing the prohibition, and in hardship and distress and at times of battle, and the truthful in their faith, Qatada said: They are people whose intentions are true and whose hearts and tongues are upright, so they are truthful in secret and in public, and the obedient the obedient praying and spending their money in obedience to God, and those who seek forgiveness in the hours of dawn Mujahid, Qatada and Al-Kalbi said: He means those who pray in the hours of dawn. And from Zaid bin Aslam, he said: They are those who pray the dawn prayer in congregation, and it was said the dawn because of its proximity to the dawn, and Al-Hasan said: They extended the prayer until the dawn, then they sought forgiveness, and Nafi' said: Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, used to stay up at night and then he would say: O Nafi', have we reached dawn? So I would say: No, so he would repeat the prayer, and if I said: Yes, yes, he would seek forgiveness from God and supplicate until morning. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Muhammad bin Al-Hasan bin Ahmad Al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Sarraj told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Yaqub bin Abdul Rahman told us, Suhayl bin Abi Saleh told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God descends to the lowest heaven every night when a third of the night remains and says: ‘I am the King, I am the King. Who is it that calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Who is it that asks of Me, that I may give him? Who is it that seeks My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?’” It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that Luqman said to his son: My son, do not be more helpless than this rooster that crows in the early hours of the morning while you are sleeping on your bed.
3:18: God the Almighty said: God bears witness that there is no god but He. It was said: This verse is about the Christians of Najran. Al-Kalbi said: "Two rabbis from the rabbis of Ash-Sham came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when they saw the city, one of them said to his companion: How similar is this city to the description of the city of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who will emerge at the end of time? When they entered upon him, they recognized him by the description, and said to him: Are you Muhammad? He said: Yes. They said to him: And you are Ahmad? He said: I am Muhammad and Ahmad. They said to him: We will ask you about something, and if you tell us about it, we will believe in you and trust you. He said: Ask. They said: Tell us about the greatest testimony in the Book of God the Almighty. So God the Almighty revealed this verse," and the two men converted to Islam. His saying, God has witnessed, meaning God has made clear, because testimony is made clear. Mujahid said: God’s judgment. (It was also said: God’s knowledge.) It was also said: God knows that there is no god but Him. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: God created souls four thousand years before bodies, and He created provisions four thousand years before souls. He testified to Himself for Himself before He created creation, when there was no sky, no earth, no land, and no sea, so He said: God testifies that there is no god but Him. His saying: and the angels means the angels bore witness. It was said: the meaning of God’s testimony is to inform and to inform, and the meaning of the testimony of the angels and the believers is to acknowledge. God Almighty’s saying: and those of knowledge means the prophets, peace be upon them. Ibn Kaysan said: It means: the Muhajireen and the Ansar. Muqatil said: The scholars of the believers of the People of the Book, Abdullah bin Salam and his companions. Al-Suddi and Al-Kalbi said: It means all the scholars of the believers. Upholding justice means with fairness. The structure of this verse is God bears witness upholding justice, accusative case of state, and it was said: accusative case of definiteness. The meaning of His statement Upholding justice is upholding the management of creation, as it is said: So-and-so is upholding the matter of so-and-so, meaning he is managing it and taking care of its causes, and upholding the right of so-and-so, meaning he rewards him. So God, the Majestic and Sublime, is the Manager, Provider, and Rewarder for deeds. There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise.
3:19: 19- Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam means the correct and acceptable religion, as God the Almighty said: And I have approved for you Islam as religion 3- Al-Ma'idah and He said: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him 85- Al-Imran. Al-Kisa'i opened the alif of that religion in response to the first that, meaning that God testifies that there is no god but Him, and testifies that those with God, Islam, is entering into peace, which is submission and obedience. It is said: He submitted, meaning he entered into peace and surrendered. Qatada said in His statement, Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam, he said: Testifying that there is no god but God and acknowledging what came from God the Almighty, which is the religion of God that He legislated for Himself and sent His messengers with and guided His saints to and He does not accept anything other than it and does not reward anything other than it. Abu Usayd al-Sharahi told us, I told Abu Ishaq al-Thalabi, I told Abu Amr al-Furati, I told Musa Imran bin Musa, I told al-Hasan bin Sufyan, I told Ammar bin Umar bin al-Mukhtar, my father told me on the authority of Ghalib al-Qattan, who said: I came to Kufa for trade and stopped near al-A’mash. I used to visit him. One night, I wanted to go down to Basra, and al-A’mash was standing at night praying the night prayer. He passed by this verse: “God bears witness that there is no god but Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - maintaining justice. There is no god but Him, the Almighty, the Wise.” Then al-A’mash said: And I bear witness to what God bears witness to, and I entrust this testimony to God, and it is a deposit for me with God. “Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam.” He said it repeatedly. I said that he had heard something about it, so I prayed with him and bid him farewell. Then I said: I heard you reciting a verse and repeating it, so what did you hear about it?” (He said to me: Haven’t you heard what is in it? I said: I have been with you for two years and you haven’t told me about it.) He said: By God, I will not tell you about it until a year has passed. So I wrote on his door that day and stayed there for a year. When the year had passed, I said: O Abu Muhammad, the year has passed. He said: Abu Wa’il told me on the authority of Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Its owner will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and God will say: This servant of Mine has a covenant with Me, and I am the most deserving of fulfilling the covenant. Admit My servant into Paradise.” God the Almighty said: And those who were given the Scripture did not differ Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about the Jews and Christians when they abandoned Islam, meaning those who were given the Scripture did not differ about the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, except after knowledge came to them, meaning the description of him in their books. Al-Rabi’ said: When death approached Moses, peace be upon him, he called seventy men from the rabbis of the Children of Israel and entrusted them with the Torah and appointed Joshua bin Nun as his successor. When the first, second and third centuries passed, division occurred among them, and they were those who were given the Scripture from the sons of those seventy until they shed blood among themselves, and evil and differences occurred, and that was after knowledge came to them, meaning the explanation of what was in the Torah, out of envy among themselves, meaning seeking kingship and leadership, so God empowered the tyrants over them. Muhammad bin Ja’far bin Al-Zubayr said: It was revealed about the Christians of Najran and its meaning is: And those who were given the Scripture did not differ meaning the Gospel about the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him, and they divided the statement about him except after knowledge came to them that God is One and that Jesus is His servant and Messenger, out of envy among themselves, meaning For hostility and opposition, And whoever disbelieves in the signs of God - then indeed, God is swift in account.
3:20: 20- The Almighty said: If they dispute with you meaning they argue with you, O Muhammad, about religion. This is because the Jews and Christians said, "We are not as you called us, O Muhammad. Judaism and Christianity are merely lineages. The religion is Islam, and we are upon it." So the Almighty said, Then say, 'I have submitted my face to God.' Meaning, I have submitted to God alone with my heart, my tongue, and all my limbs. The face was specifically mentioned because it is the most honorable of the limbs of a human being and contains his splendor. So if his face submits to something, all his limbs submit to it. Al-Farra' said: Its meaning is, I have devoted my work to God. And whoever follows me, meaning whoever follows me submits as I have submitted. Nafi' and Abu Amr confirmed the ya' in the Almighty's saying follow me according to the original, and the others deleted it according to the script because it is without a ya' in the Qur'an. And His statement: And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered ones, meaning the Arabs, Have you submitted? Its wording is a question but its meaning is a command, meaning submit as He said, Will you then desist? 91-Al-Ma’idah, meaning desist, For if they submit, then they are rightly guided. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse and the People of the Scripture said: We have submitted. So the Jews said: Do you bear witness that Jesus is the Word of God, His servant and His Messenger? They said: God forbid! And he said to the Christians: Do you bear witness that Jesus is the servant of God and His Messenger? They said: God forbid that Jesus should be a servant. So God Almighty said: But if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance, meaning conveying the message, and you are not responsible for guidance. And God is Seeing of His servants, Knowing who believes and who does not believe.
3:21: 21- The Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God deny the verses of God, meaning the Qur'an, and they are the Jews and Christians and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people Hamza read: and fight those who enjoin, Ibn Jurayj said: The revelation would come to the prophets of the Children of Israel, and no book would come to them, so they would remind their people and be killed, then men from among those who followed them and believed them would say and remind their people and be killed as well, so they are the ones who enjoin justice among the people. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Fanjuwayh Al-Daynouri told us, Abu Nasr Mansur bin Ja’far Al-Nahwandi told us, Ahmad bin Yahya bin Al-Jarud told us, Muhammad bin Amr bin Hayyan told us, Muhammad bin Himyar told us, Abu Al-Hasan Mawla of Banu Asad told us, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb Al-Khuza’i, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which people will be most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection? He said: A man who killed a prophet or a man who enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “And they kill the prophets unjustly and they kill those who enjoin justice among the people” until he reached His saying: And they will have no helpers. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Ubaidah, the Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets in one hour at the beginning of the day. Then one hundred and twelve men from the servants of the Children of Israel stood up and ordered those who killed them to do so in a just manner.” And he forbade them from evil, so they killed them all at the end of the day on that day. They are the ones whom God mentioned in His Book and revealed the verse about them: So give them tidings He informed them of a painful punishment. The fa was only inserted into the report of in and its meaning is those who disbelieve and kill, so give them tidings, because it is not said: Zayd is standing.
3:22: 22- Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers. The nullity of a deed in this world means that it will not be accepted, and in the Hereafter, that it will not be rewarded for it.
3:23: 23- The Almighty said: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture meaning the Jews calling to the Book of God they differed about this book, so Qatada said: They are the Jews who called to the ruling of the Qur’an but turned away from it. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding this verse: God Almighty made the Qur’an a judge between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Qur’an made the Jews and Christians believe that they were not on the right path, so they turned away from it. The others said: It is the Torah. Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the house of Al-Maras, upon a group of Jews, and called them to God Almighty. Na’im bin Amr and Al-Harith bin Zaid said to him: What religion do you follow, O Muhammad? He said: The religion of Abraham. They said: Abraham was a Jew. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Come to the Torah, for it is between us and you. But they refused, so God Almighty revealed this verse.” Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that a man and a woman from the people of Khaybar committed adultery and stoning was in their book, so they disliked stoning them because of their honor among them, so they brought their case to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they hoped that he would have a dispensation, so he ruled that they should be stoned. Al-Nu’man bin Awfa and Bahri bin Amr said to him: It has been carried out on them, O Muhammad, and stoning is not required of them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Between me and you is the Torah. They said: You have been fair to us. He said: Who among you is the most knowledgeable of the Torah? They said: A one-eyed man who lives in Fadak and is called Ibn Suriya. So they sent for him and he went to Medina. Gabriel had described him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Are you Ibn Suriya? He said: Yes. He said: Are you the most knowledgeable of the Jews? He said: That is what they claim. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for something from the Torah, in which stoning was written, and he said to him: Read. When he came to the verse of stoning, he placed his hand on it and read what came after it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdullah ibn Salam said, O Messenger of God, he has gone beyond it. So he stood up and lifted his hand from her, then he recited to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the Jews that if a married man and a married woman commit adultery and evidence is established against them, they are to be stoned. And if the woman is pregnant, she is to be waited until she gives birth to what is in her womb. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the two Jews to be stoned. The Jews became angry at that and left, so God Almighty revealed, Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They are invited to the Book of God.
3:24: 24- "To judge between them, then a party of them will turn away while they are averse. * That is because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. And they were deceived in their religion by what they were inventing. Deception is the desire for something that does not happen. Inventing lies.
3:25: 25- The Almighty said: How then will it be when We gather them meaning how will their condition be or how will they act when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt which is the Day of Resurrection and every soul will be fully compensated meaning the reward it earned of good or evil and they will not be wronged meaning their good deeds will not be diminished nor will their bad deeds be increased.
3:26: 26- The Almighty said: "Say: O God, Owner of the Kingdom." Qatada said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked his Lord to make the kingdom of Persia and Rome in his nation, so God Almighty revealed this verse. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca and promised his nation the kingdom of Persia and Rome, the hypocrites and the Jews said: Far from it, far from it, where will Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, have the kingdom of Persia and Rome? And they are more powerful and more secure than that. Was not Mecca and Medina enough for Muhammad until he coveted the kingdom of Persia and Rome? Then God revealed this verse: Say, O God. It was said that its meaning is O God. When the letter of address was deleted, the letter mim was added at the end of it. Some people said that the letter mim has a meaning in it, and its meaning is O God, we have secured goodness, meaning: come to us. The letter of address was deleted from it, like their saying: Come to us. Its original form was hal or ilina. Then it became widespread in speech, so the hamza was deleted to make it lighter. They may also make it lighter and say: lahum. His statement Malik al-Mulk meaning O Malik al-Mulk means the owner of the servants and what they own. It was said O Malik of the heavens and the earth. God the Most High said in some books: I am God, the King of kings, and the Owner of kings, and the hearts of kings and their forelocks are in My hand. If the servants obey Me, I will make them mercy upon them, and if they disobey Me, I will make them punishment upon them. So do not be preoccupied with the cause of kings, but repent to Me, and I will make them compassionate toward you. God the Almighty said: You give the kingdom to whomever You will. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said: It means the kingdom of prophethood. Al-Kalbi said: You give the kingdom to whomever You will: Muhammad and his companions. And you take the kingdom away from whomever You will. Abu Jahl and the leaders of Quraysh. It was also said: You give the kingdom to whomever You will: the Arabs. And you take the kingdom away from whomever You will: the Persians and the Romans. Al-Suddi said: You give the kingdom to whomever You will. God gave it to the prophets, peace be upon them, and commanded the servants to obey them. And you take the kingdom away from whomever You will. He took it away from the tyrants and commanded the servants to oppose them. It was also said: You give it to whomever You will: Adam and his children. And you send down the kingdom to whomever You will: Satan and his soldiers. And the Almighty said: And You honor whom You will and humiliate whom You will. Ata’ said: You honor whom You will: the Muhajireen and the Ansar, and You humiliate whom You will: the Persians and the Romans. It was also said: You honor whom You will: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions until they entered Mecca with ten thousand who were victorious over it, and You humiliate whom You will: Abu Jahl and his companions until their heads were cut off and they were thrown into the well. It was also said: You honor whom You will with faith and guidance, and You humiliate whom You will with disbelief and misguidance. It was also said: You honor whom You will with obedience and humiliate whom You will with disobedience. It was also said: You honor whom You will with victory and humiliate whom You will with subjugation. It was also said: You honor whom You will with wealth and humiliate whom You will with poverty. It was also said: You honor whom You will with contentment and satisfaction and humiliate whom You will with greed and covetousness. In Your Hand is good, meaning in Your Hand is good and evil, so He was satisfied with mentioning one of them. The Almighty said: Garments to protect you from the heat 81-An-Nahl, meaning the heat and the cold, so He was satisfied with mentioning one of them: Indeed, You are over all things. Powerful.
