3:27: 27- The Almighty said: "He causes the night to enter the day meaning He causes the night to enter the day until the day is fifteen hours and the night is nine hours And He causes the day to enter the night until the night is fifteen hours and the day is nine hours, so whatever is missing from one of them is added to the other And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living The people of Medina, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read the dead with a shaddah on the ya' here, and in Al-An'am, Yunus, and Ar-Rum in Al-A'raf to a dead land and in Fatir to a dead land Nafi' added or one who was dead and We gave him life 122-Al-An'am and the flesh of his brother is dead 12-Al-Hujurat and the dead land We have given life 33-Ya-Sin so he stressed it, and the others lighten it, and Ya'qub stressed He brings forth the living from the dead" and the flesh of his brother is dead, Ibn Mas'ud, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: The meaning of the verse is: He brings forth the animal from the sperm It is dead, and the sperm comes out of the animal Ikrimah and Al-Kalbi said: He brings forth the living from the dead, meaning the chick from the egg and the egg from the bird. Al-Hasan and Ata’ said: He brings forth the believer from the disbeliever and the disbeliever from the believer. So the believer has a living heart and the disbeliever has a dead heart. God the Most High said: Or was he dead and We gave him life? 122-An-Na’am. Al-Zajjaj said: He brings forth the fresh, tender plant from the dry seed, and He brings forth the dry seed from the living, growing plant. And You provide for whom You will without account without restriction nor stinginess. Abu al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hanafi told us, I told Abu Bakr Ahmad bin al-Hasan al-Hayri, I told Abu Ja`far Abdullah bin Ismail bin Ibrahim al-Hashemi, I told Muhammad bin Ali bin Zaid al-Sa`igh, I told Muhammad bin Abi al-Azhar, I told al-Harith bin `Umair, I told Ja`far bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, the Opening of the Book, the Throne Verse, and the two verses of Al-`Imran, “God bears witness - to His saying - Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam - and Say, O God, Owner of the Kingdom - to His saying - without account are suspended, between them and God Almighty is a veil. They said: O Lord, will you send us down to your land and to those who disobey you? God Almighty said: I swear by Me that no one of My servants will recite them after every prayer except that I will make Paradise his abode, regardless of what he has done, and I will make him dwell in the Holy Sanctuary, and I will look at him with My hidden eye seventy times every day, and I will fulfill for him seventy needs every day, the least of which is forgiveness.” And I will protect him from every enemy and envious person and support him against them.” Narrated by Al-Harith on the authority of Amr, and it is weak.
3:28: 28- The Almighty said: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Al-Hajjaj bin Amr bin Abi Al-Haqiq and Qais bin Zaid thought about a group of the Ansar to tempt them away from their religion, so Rafa’ah bin Al-Mundhir, Abdullah bin Jubair, and Sa’d bin Khaithama said to those al-Nas 114:Avoid these Jews lest they tempt you away from your religion, but those people refused except to befriend them, so God Almighty revealed this verse. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah and others, and they showed affection for the infidels of Mecca. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that it was revealed about the hypocrites, Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions, who used to be allies of the Jews and polytheists and bring them report, hoping that they would be victorious over the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God Almighty revealed this verse and forbade the believers from doing the same actions as they did. God the Almighty said: And whoever does that meaning befriends the infidels by conveying report to them and exposing them to the faults of the Muslims has nothing to do with God meaning he has nothing to do with the religion of God. Then He made an exception and said: Except that you fear them with a fear meaning: Except that you fear them with a fear. Mujahid and Ya’qub used taqiyah on the weight of baqiyah because they wrote it with a ya’ and did not write it with an alif, like pebble and seed. It is a verbal noun. It is said taqiyah / taqah and taqwa taqiyah and taqwa. So if you say itqayyat, the verbal noun is ittiqa. He said tatqawwa from ittiqa, then he said taqah and did not say ittiqa because if the meaning of the two words is one, it is permissible to make the verbal noun of one of them take the word of the other, like God the Almighty’s saying: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion 8- Al-Muzzammil. The meaning of the verse is that God Almighty forbade the believers from befriending the infidels, flattering them, and collaborating with them unless the infidels are dominant and apparent, or the believer is among a people of infidels whom he fears, so he appeases them with his tongue while his heart is at peace with faith, defending himself without making permissible any unlawful blood or money, or he shows the infidels to the Muslims’ private parts. Taqiyya is only done with fear of being killed and with sound intentions. God Almighty said: “Except for one who is forced and whose heart is at peace with faith” 106-An-Nahl. Then this is a concession, so if he is patient until he is killed, then he will have a great reward. Some people have rejected taqiyya today. Muadh ibn Jabal and Mujahid said: Taqiyya was in the Bedouin of Islam before the religion was established and the Muslims were strong. As for today, God has made Islam victorious, so the people of Islam should not be at peace with their enemy. Yahya al-Bakka said: I said to Saeed ibn Jubayr during the days of al-Hajjaj: Al-Hasan used to say to you taqiyya with your tongue while your heart is at peace with faith? Saeed said: There is no taqiyya in Islam. Taqiyya is only for those at war. And God warns you of Himself means God frightens you with His punishment for befriending the infidels, committing what is forbidden, and disobeying what is commanded. And to God is the final destination.
3:29: 29- "Say: Whether you conceal what is in your hearts" meaning your hearts of love for the disbelievers or reveal it of your loyalty to them in word and deed God knows it. Al-Kalbi said: Whether you conceal what is in your hearts to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of denial or reveal it, freely and by fighting him, God knows it and preserves it for you, until He rewards you for it. Then to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: And He knows raising it as a resumption what is in the heavens and what is on the earth meaning if nothing in the heavens or on the earth is hidden from Him, then how can your loyalty to the disbelievers and your inclination towards them in your heart be hidden from Him? And God is over all things competent.
3:30: 30- The Almighty’s saying, On the Day every soul will find is in the accusative case, by removing the letter of description, meaning on a day. It was said: by adding a verb, meaning: Remember and fear the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present nothing of it was omitted, as God Almighty said: And they will find what they did present 49-Al-Kahf. And what you have done of evil some of them made it a predicate in the accusative case, meaning you will find present what you have done of good and evil, so you will be pleased with what you have done of good. Some of them made it a resumed predicate. Evidence for this interpretation: the reading of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with them both, And what you have done of evil, you wish there was a long period between it and it. God Almighty says: You would wish that between it meaning between the soul and it meaning between evil there was a great distance. Al-Suddi said: A distant place. Muqatil said: Like the distance between the east and the west. The term is the deadline and the goal to which one ends. Al-Hasan said: One of them would be pleased never to throw away his work. It was said: He would wish that he had not done it. And God warns you of Himself, and God is Kind to His servants.
3:31: 31- The Almighty said: "Say: If you love God, then follow me, and God will love you." It was revealed about the Jews and Christians, when they said: We are the sons of God and His beloved. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood before the Quraysh, while they were in the Sacred Mosque, and they had set up their idols and hung ostrich eggs on them and put shanuf in their ears, and they were prostrating to them. He said: O Quraysh, by God, you have contradicted the religion of your father Abraham and Ishmael. The Quraysh said to him: We only worship them out of love for God, so that they may bring us closer to God. God the Almighty said: Say, O Muhammad, if you love God and worship idols so that they may bring you closer to Him, then follow me, and God will love you. I am His Messenger to you and His proof over you, meaning follow my law and my Sunnah, and God will love you. The believers’ love for God is their following His command, preferring His obedience, and seeking His pleasure. The believers’ love for God is His praise. Upon them, and His reward for them and His pardon for them, as is the saying of the Almighty: And He will forgive you your sins, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. It was said that when this verse was revealed, Abdullah bin Ubayy said to his companions that Muhammad makes obedience to him like obedience to God and orders us to love him as the Christians loved Jesus, son of Mary.
3:32: 32- Then the Almighty’s words were revealed: “Say, ‘Obey God and the Messenger.’ But if they turn away, then God does not love the disbelievers. He is not pleased with their actions and does not forgive them.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Isma’i, I told Muhammad bin Sinan, I told Falih, I told Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All of my nation will enter Paradise except for those who refuse. They said, And who refuses? He said, Whoever obeys me will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad Ismail, I told Muhammad bin Ubadah, I told Yazid, I told Salim bin Hayyan and he praised him, I told Saeed bin Mina’ who said: He told us or I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: “Angels came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was asleep. Some of them said: He is asleep, and some of them said: The eye is asleep and the heart is awake. They said: Your companion has a parable, so give him a parable. They said: His parable is like that of a man who built a house and held a banquet in it and sent an inviter. Whoever answered the inviter entered the house and ate from the banquet, and whoever did not answer the inviter did not enter the house and did not eat from the banquet. They said: Explain it to him so that he may understand it. They said: As for the house, it is Paradise and the inviter is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Whoever obeys Muhammad has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys Muhammad has disobeyed God, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, distinguished between people.”
3:33: 33- And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah the verse, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said: The Jews said, We are from the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and we are of their religion, so God, the Almighty, revealed this verse. Meaning: God chose these people with Islam and you are not of the religion of Islam. Chosen means chose, it is derived from the word safwa, which means pure from everything. Adam, the father of mankind, and Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran. It was said: He meant by the family of Abraham and the family of Imran Abraham, peace be upon him, and Imran themselves, like the Almighty’s saying: And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind 248-Al-Baqarah, meaning Moses and Aaron. Others said: The family of Abraham: Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes. Muhammad, peace be upon him, was from the family of Abraham, peace be upon him. As for the family of Imran, Muqatil said: He is Imran bin Yashar bin Fahat bin Levi bin Jacob, peace be upon them the father of Moses and Aaron. Al-Hasan and Wahb said: He is Imran bin Ashham bin Amun from the descendants of Solomon bin David, peace be upon them the father of Mary and Jesus. It was said: Imran bin Mathan. These were mentioned specifically because all the prophets and messengers are from their descendants a descendants upon the worlds.
3:34: 34- Dhariyah is derived from dhara' meaning to create, and it was said: from dhar because he extracted them from the loins of Adam/ like dhar, and the children and fathers are called dhariyah, so the children are dhariyah because he created them, and the fathers are dhariyah because he created the children from them, God Almighty said and a sign for them is that We carried their offspring 41-Ya Sin meaning their fathers Dhariyah is accusative in the meaning and chose offspring some of them from others meaning some of them from the children of others, and it was said some of them from others in support and it was said: some of them are on the religion of others and God is Hearing and Knowing.
3:35: 35- The Almighty said: When the wife of Imran said, and she is Hannah bint Qafudha, the mother of Mary 4. Imran is Imran bin Mathan, not Imran, the father of Moses, peace be upon him, and there were one thousand and eighty years between them. The sons of Mathan were the leaders of the Children of Israel, their rabbis and their kings. It was said: Imran bin Ashham. God Almighty says: My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated to Your service. That is, I have made what is in my womb dedicated, a vow from me to You. “So accept it from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” A vow is what a person obligates himself to do, devoted, that is, freed and devoted to God, devoted to His servants and to serving the church, not occupying him with anything in this world. Everything that is dedicated is freed. It is said: I freed the slave if I set him free and freed him from slavery. Al-Kalbi Muhammad bin Ishaq and others said: When a freed man was set free, he would be placed in the church, sweeping and serving it, and would not leave it until he reached puberty. Then he would be given the choice of whether he liked to stay, or if he liked to go wherever he wanted. If he wanted to leave after the choice, he would not be allowed to do so. There was no prophet or scholar among his descendants who was not set free for the Holy House. Only boys were set free, and a slave girl was not suitable for him because of the menstruation and harm that befell her. So Mary’s mother set free what was in her womb. The story in that was that Zachariah and Imran married two sisters. Isha’ bint Qafudha, the mother of Yahya, was with Zachariah, and Hannah bint Qafudha, the mother of Mary, was with Imran. He had withheld a child from Hannah until she grew old, and they were a family of God in a place. While she was in the shade of a tree, a bird was feeding a chick, and her soul was moved by that for the child, so she called upon God to grant her a child and said: O God, I promise you that if you grant me a child, I will give him in charity to the Holy House, so that he will be from… She was his custodian and servant, and she became pregnant with Maryam, so she released what was in her womb, but she did not know what it was. So her husband said to her: Woe to you, what have you done? Did you see that what is in your womb is a female, is she not fit for that? So they both fell into worry about that, so Imran died, and Hannah was pregnant with Maryam.
3:36: 36- When I delivered her meaning I gave birth to her, she was a girl, and the ha in his saying | delivered her refers to the warning to what was born, so it was made feminine. She said Hannah, and she was hoping that it would be a boy, My Lord, I have delivered a female as an apology to God Almighty. And God knows best what she delivered with the ta' in the subjunctive mood, informing about God Almighty, and this is the reading of the common people. Ibn Amir, Abu Bakr, and Yaqub read wada with the ta' in the nominative case, making it from the words of Mary's mother. And the male is not like the female in serving the church and the worshippers in it due to her nakedness and weakness and what befalls her from menstruation and childbirth. And I have named her Mary and Mary in their language means the worshipper and the servant, and Mary was the most beautiful of women at her time and the best of them. And I seek refuge for her I protect her and protect her with You and her offspring her children from Satan the accursed so Satan is the banished, cursed, and the one who is pelted with meteors. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abu Al-Yaman, I told Shuaib on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me, he said: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no child of Adam who is born except that Satan touches him when he is born, so the child cries out from Satan, except for Mary and her son. Then Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, says: And I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the accursed. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abu Al-Yaman, I told Shuaib Anabi Al-Zinad, on the authority of Al-Araj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The devil stabs every son of Adam in the side with his finger when he is born, except for Jesus, son of Mary. He went to stab him and stabbed the veil.”
3:37: 37- His saying, So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance, meaning that God accepted Mary from Hannah in place of the editor, and accepted means before and was pleased, and acceptance is a source of before which means accepted like passion and distribution, and nothing came except these three. It was said: The meaning of acceptance is to take care of her upbringing and to look after her. And He caused her to grow in a good manner means: And He caused her to grow in a good manner. It was said that this is a source other than the wording. Likewise, His saying: So her Lord accepted her with a good manner (and something similar is common, like your saying, She spoke a word. Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, So her Lord accepted her with a good manner) meaning He made her grow in a good manner, meaning He made her grow in a good manner, without any increase or decrease, so she would grow in a day what a newborn grows in a year. And Zachariah took her under his care. The people of the report said: Hannah took Mary when she gave birth to her, wrapped her in a rag, and carried her to the mosque, and placed her with the rabbis, the building of Aaron, and they were at that time in the direction of the Holy House, which was next to the veil of the Kaaba. She said to them: Here is this vow, so the rabbis competed over her because she was the daughter of their cloud and the owner of their sacrifice. Zachariah said to them: I am the most deserving of her among you, I have her maternal aunt. The rabbis said to him: We will not do that, for if it had been left to the most deserving of people, it would have been left to its mother who gave birth to it. We will cast lots for it and it will be with the one whose lot came out. So they set out, and they were twenty-nine men, to a flowing river. Al-Suddi said: It is the Jordan River. They threw their pens into the water on the condition that whoever’s pen stuck in the water and came up would have more right to it. It was said: Each pen had the name of one of them. It was said: They were writing the Torah, so they threw the pens that were in their hands into the water fartz and Zechariah’s pen rose above the water, and their pens descended and settled in the river. This was said by Muhammad bin Ishaq and a group. It was said: Zachariah's pen ran up to the top of the water, and their pens ran with the flow of the water. Al-Suddi and a group said: Rather, the pen of Zakariya was fixed and stood above the water as if it were in clay, and their pens ran with the running of the water and the water carried them away, so their arrow and their lot was Zakariya, and Zakariya was the head of the rabbis and their prophet, so that is what God Almighty said: And Zakariya was responsible for her. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and Asim read it with a shaddah on the fa’, so Zakariya is in the accusative case, meaning that God guaranteed her to Zakariya and included her in his care by lot. The others read it with a light shaddah, so Zakariya is in the nominative case, meaning that Zakariya included her in his care and took care of her, and he is Zakariya bin Adhan bin Muslim bin Sadooq, from the sons of Solomon bin David, peace be upon them. Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs on the authority of Asim read: Zakariya, shortened, and the others lengthen it. When Zakariya took Mary to himself, he built a house for her and nursed her. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He took her to her aunt Umm Yahya until, when she grew up and reached the age of women, he built a niche for her in the mosque and made a door in the middle of it, and no one could ascend to it except by ladder, like the door of the Kaaba, and no one could ascend to it except by it. He used to bring her food, drink and oil every day, Whenever Zakariya entered upon her the niche. By the niche he meant the room, and the niche is the most honorable and foremost of the gatherings, and it is also part of the mosque. The mosque is also called a mihrab. Al-Mubarrad said: The mihrab is not possible unless one ascends to it by a step. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: When Zakariya went out, he would lock seven doors on her, and when he entered her room, he found with her provision, meaning fruit out of season, summer fruit in the winter and winter fruit in the summer. He said, ‘O Mary, from where did you get this?’ Abu Ubaidah said: Its meaning is, From where did you get this? Some of them denied it and said: Its meaning is, from which direction did you get this? Because from where is for asking about direction and where? Asked about the place, she said, It is from God, meaning from the harvest of Paradise. Al-Hasan said: When Mary was born, she never breastfed. Her provision came to her from Paradise. Then Zachariah said to her, Where did you get this? She said, It is from God. She spoke while she was young, And God provides for whom He wills without account. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Then the Children of Israel were afflicted with a crisis and they were in that state until Zakariya was too weak to bear her, so he went out to the Children of Israel and said: O Children of Israel, you know by God that I have grown old and weak to bear Mary, the daughter of Imran, so which of you will take care of her after me? They said: By God, we have been exhausted and have been afflicted by the famine that you see. So they pushed her among themselves and found no alternative but to bear her, so they cast lots over her with pens and the arrow fell on a carpenter from the Children of Israel called: Joseph bin Yaqoub, who was the cousin of Mary, so he carried her. Mary saw in his face the severity of the burden that was on him, so she said to him: O Joseph, have good thoughts about God, for God will provide for us. So Joseph began to provide for her in her place with him, and he would bring her from his earnings every day what would be good for her, and when he brought it to her in the church, God would increase it. Then Zakariya would come in to her and see with her an abundance of provision, not as much as what Joseph brought her, so he said: O Mary, how did you get this? She said: It is from God. Indeed, God provides for whomever He wills without account. The historians said: When Zachariah saw that, he said: He who was able to bring Mary fruit at the wrong time without any reason is able to reform my wife and give me a child at the wrong time in my old age. So he desired a child, because his family had died out and Zachariah had grown old and despaired of having a child.
3:38: 38- God Almighty said: There meaning at that time Zachariah called upon his Lord so he entered the sanctuary and closed the door and communed with his Lord “He said: My Lord” meaning O Lord grant me give me from Yourself meaning from Yourself good offspring meaning a blessed, pious, righteous, and pleasing child. Offspring can be one or plural, male and female, and here it is one, as evidenced by the words of God Almighty So grant me from Yourself a heir 5-Maryam. He only said: good because the word offspring is feminine. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication meaning You hear it, and it was said that You answer it, like the words of God Almighty: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so hear me 25-Yasin meaning so answer me. 5 - And I feared the relatives, and the relatives: the paternal uncles. Mujahid said: the agnates. Abu Saleh said: the kalalah. Al-Kalbi said: the heirs. After me means: after my death. Ibn Kathir read: from behind me with the opening of the yaa, and the others with the closing of it. And my wife was barren, meaning she could not bear children, so grant me from Yourself, meaning give me from Yourself an heir, meaning a son.
3:39: 39- "The angels called him Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read Fanadah" with a ya', and the others with a ta'. Whoever reads with a ta', it is to feminize the word "angels" and for the plural, although if the males precede their verb and they are a group, then feminization is better for them, like the Almighty's saying: "The Bedouins said" 14-Al-Hujurat. And on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Abdullah bin Mas'ud, may God be pleased with them both, used to mention the angels in the Qur'an. Abu Ubaidah said: We only see that Abdullah chose that in opposition to the polytheists in their saying that the angels are the daughters of God Almighty. And Al-Sha'bi narrated that Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, said: If you differ about the ta' and the ya', then make them ya' and mention the Qur'an. And the angels here meant: Gabriel, peace be upon him, alone, as God Almighty said in Surat An-Nahl, The angels descend meaning Gabriel with the spirit with the revelation. And it is permissible in Arabic to report about one person in the plural form, as they say: I heard this report from people, but it was only heard from one person, similar to what God Almighty said: Those to whom the people said 173- Al Imran meaning Nu’aym ibn Mas’ud The people meaning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. And Al Fadl ibn Salamah said: If the killer is a leader, it is permissible to report about him in the plural form because his companions are gathered with him, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, was the leader of the angels, and it is rare for a person to be sent except with a group, so it was done according to that. God the Almighty said: And he was standing praying in the sanctuary meaning in the mosque. This is because Zachariah was the great rabbi who would offer the sacrifice, so the door of the altar would be opened and they would not enter until he gave them permission to enter. While he was standing praying in the sanctuary, meaning in the mosque away from the altar, he was praying, and the people were waiting for him to give them permission to enter, then he saw a young man wearing white clothes. He was startled by him and called out to him, and he was Gabriel, peace be upon him, O Zachariah, God gives you good tidings. Ibn Amir and Hamah read indeed God with a kasra on the alif, implying the statement, meaning: So the angels called him and said: God gives you good tidings. The others read it with a fatha, placing the call upon him, as if he said: So the angels called him that God gives you good tidings. Hamza read Yabashkar and its chapter with a light pronunciation of the entire Qur’an except for His statement: So what are you giving good tidings of? 54-Al-Hijr, for they agreed on its emphasis, and Al-Kisa’i agreed here in the two places and in Subhan, Al-Kahf, and As-Saqaf. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr agreed in "'Asq" and the rest with emphasis, whoever reads with emphasis then it is from basharah yabshar tabbishran, which is the most eloquent and articulate of languages. The evidence for emphasis is the Almighty's saying: "So give good tidings to my servants" (al-Zumar 39:17) "And We gave him good tidings of Isaac" (al-Saffat 37:112) They said: "We have given you good tidings in truth" (al-Hijr 15:55) and other verses. Whoever reads with emphasis then it is from basharah yabshar, which is the language of Tihamah, and Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, read it as "Yahya", it is a name that does not draw a genitive case because it is definite and because of the extra letter at the beginning like Yazid and Ya'mar, and its plural is yahyun like mawsoon and 'aysoon, and they differed as to why he was named Yahya? Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: Because God revived his mother’s barrenness through him. Qatada said: Because God revived his heart with faith. It was also said: Because God revived him with obedience until he did not disobey or intend to disobey. Believing is in the accusative case as a state. By a word from God means Jesus, peace be upon him. Jesus was called the Word of God because God said to him: Be without a father, and he was. The name Word was given to him because it was through him. It was also said: He was called the Word because he is guided by it, just as he is guided by the Word of God. The prophets informed the prophets by His Word in His books that He would create a prophet without a father, so He called him the Word because he had fulfilled that promise. John (peace be upon him) was the first to believe in Jesus (peace be upon him) and believed in him. John (peace be upon him) was six months older than Jesus, and they were cousins. Then John was killed before Jesus (peace be upon him) was taken up. Abu Ubaidah said: By a word from God meaning by a book from God and His verses. The Arabs say: Recite to me the word of so-and-so, meaning his poem. God the Almighty said: "And a master is an active participle from the verb sada" which means to rule and is the leader who is followed and ends with his saying. Al-Mufaddal said: He meant a master in religion. Al-Dahhak said: The master / of good character. Saeed bin Jubair said: The master is the one who obeys his Lord, the Almighty. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: The master is the knowledgeable jurist. Qatada said: A master in knowledge, worship and piety. It was also said: The forbearing one who is not angered by anything. Mujahid said: The generous one towards God the Almighty. Al-Dahhak said: The pious master. Sufyan Al-Thawri said: The one who is not envied. It was also said: The one who excels his people in all good qualities. It was also said: He is content with what God has allotted for him. It was also said: The generous one. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who is your master, O Banu Salamah? They said: Jadd bin Qais, on whom we are stingy. He said: What disease is worse than stinginess, but your master is Amr bin Al-Jamuh. God the Almighty said: And chaste and a prophet from among the righteous. The root of hasur is la hasr which means confinement. Hasur according to Ibn Masoud may God be pleased with him, Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, Qatadah may God be pleased with them, Ata’ and Al-Hasan means the one who does not come to women or approach them. According to this statement, it is a fa’ul with the meaning of fa’il, meaning that he restrains himself from desires. (It was said: He is the poor man who has no money), so hasur means the one who is confined, meaning the one who is forbidden from women. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: He had a garment like the hem of a garment, and he married in addition to that so that he would lower his gaze. There is another statement about it: that hasur is the one who abstains from intercourse despite being able to do so. Some people chose this statement for two reasons: One of them: because the speech was made in the form of praise, and this is closer to deserving of praise, and the second: that it is further from attributing a affliction to the prophets.
3:40: 40- The Almighty said: “He said, ‘My Lord,’ meaning, my Master, he said to Gabriel, peace be upon him. This is the saying of Al-Kalbi and a group. It was said: He said to God Almighty, “How can it be?” From where can it be? “I have a boy,” meaning a son. And old age has reached me. This is from the inverted, meaning, I have reached old age and grown old, as one says, I have reached exhaustion. It was said: Its meaning is, And old age has overtaken me and overtaken me and weakened me. Al-Kalbi said: When Zachariah was given the good report of a son, he was ninety-two years old. It was said: ninety-nine years old. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: He was one hundred and twenty years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. This is why God Almighty said: And my wife is barren, meaning sterile, she does not give birth. It is said: a barren man and a barren woman. Aqar with a damma on the qaf means barrenness and aqara. He said: And God does what He wills. If it is said: Why did Zakariya say after God Almighty promised him: How will I have a boy? Was he doubting God’s promise and His power? It is said: When Zakariya heard the call of the angels, Satan came to him and said: O Zakariya, the voice that you heard is not from God, but from Satan. If it was from God, He would have inspired it to you as He inspires you in all other matters. So he said that to prevent whisperings. This was said by Ikrimah and As-Suddi. Another answer is that he did not doubt God’s promise, but rather he doubted how it was, meaning how?
3:41: 41- The Almighty said: “He said: My Lord, make for me a sign” meaning a sign by which I will know when my wife is pregnant so that I may increase in worship in gratitude to You. “He said: Your sign is that you do not speak to people” refrain from speaking for three days and accept my worship completely, not that he restrained his tongue from speaking, but he was forbidden from speaking while he was correct and sound, as He said in Surah Maryam, verse 10: that you do not speak to people for three nights straight is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: And glorify God in the evening and the morning so He commanded him to remember and forbade him from speaking to people. Most commentators said: His tongue was restrained from speaking to people for three days. Qatada said: His tongue was restrained from speaking as a punishment for asking him for the sign after the angels spoke to him, so he was not able to speak for three days. His saying except by gesture means a sign, and a gesture may be with the tongue, the eye, or the hand. His gesture was with the index finger. Al-Farra’ said: A sign may be with the tongue without being made clear, and it is a low voice similar to a whisper. Ata’ said: He meant by it fasting for three days because when they fasted they did not speak except by gesture. And remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning. It was said that what is meant by glorification is prayer, and the evening is what is between the sun’s zenith and sunset, and from this the noon and afternoon prayers are called the evening prayers, and the morning is what is between the dawn prayer and the morning.
3:42: 42- The Almighty said: And when the angels said meaning Gabriel O Mary, God has chosen you He chose you and purified you It was said from the touch of men and it was said from menstruation and postpartum bleeding. Al-Suddi said: Mary did not menstruate, and it was said: from sins and chose you over the women of the worlds It was said: over the world of her time and it was said: over all the women of the worlds in that she was born without a father and that was not the case for any of the women, and it was said: by liberation in the mosque and no female was freed. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmad bin Raja told us, Al-Nadr told us on the authority of Hisham, my father told us: I heard Abdullah bin Jaafar, he said: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The best of its women is Mary, daughter of Imran, and the best of its women is Khadija, may God be pleased with them both. It was narrated by Wakee’ and Abu Muawiyah on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, and Wakee’ pointed to the sky and the earth. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, Amr bin Murrah told us, Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Many men have attained perfection, but none of the women have attained perfection except Mary, the daughter of Imran, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh. The superiority of Aisha over women is like the superiority of tharid over all other foods.” Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abdul Rahman bin Abdul Samad Al-Bazzar told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq Al-Dayri told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Omar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “It is sufficient for you from the women of the worlds that Mary, daughter of Imran, Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh.”
3:43: 43- The Almighty said: O Mary, be devout towards your Lord. The angels said to her, Obey your Lord. Mujahid said: Longen your standing in prayer for your Lord. And qunut is obedience. It was said: Qunut is long standing. Al-Awza'i said: When the angels said that to her, she stood up for prayer until her feet swelled and blood and pus flowed. And prostrate and bow. It was said: Prostration was mentioned before bowing because it was thus in their religion. It was said: Rather, bowing was before prostration in all religions. The waw is not for order but for gathering. It is permissible for a man to say: I saw Zayd and Amr, even if he had seen Amr before Zayd. With those bowing. He did not say: With those bowing to be more general and comprehensive, as it includes men and women. It was said: Its meaning is with those praying in congregation.
3:44: 44- The Almighty said: This is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you. He says to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, This which you mentioned from the hadith of Zachariah, John, Mary, and Jesus is from the report of the unseen meaning from the report of the unseen We reveal to you. He referred the metaphor to that, so that is why He mentioned it. And you were not with them, O Muhammad, when they cast their pens their arrows into the water to cast lots” as to which of them would be responsible for Mary, to embrace her and raise her. “Nor were you with them when they disputed” over her responsibility.
3:45: 45- The Almighty said: When the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary.' He only said: His name is a metaphor for Jesus, and they differed as to why he was not called Messiah. Some of them said: It is a fa'il in the sense of the passive participle, meaning that he was wiped from filth and purified from sins. It was said: Because he was wiped with blessing. It was said: Because he came out of his mother's womb wiped with oil. It was said: Gabriel wiped him with his wing so that Satan had no way to him. It was said: Because he was smooth-footed and had no sole. The Antichrist was called Messiah because one of his eyes was wiped. Some of them said: It is a fa'il in the sense of the active participle, like 'Alim and 'Aalim. Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: He was called Messiah because he did not touch anyone with a defect except that he was cured. It was said: He was called that because he used to wander the earth and not stay in one place. According to this statement, the 'mim' in it is redundant. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: The Messiah is the truthful one, and the Messiah means the one who destroys, and the Antichrist was named after him. The letter is one of the opposites: honorable, meaning noble, high, of status and esteem, in this world and the hereafter, and among those brought near to God.
3:46: 46- And he will speak to the people in the cradle as a child before the time of speech as mentioned in Surah Maryam. He said: "Indeed, I am a servant of God. He has given me the Scripture" verse 30. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Maryam said: When I and Jesus were alone, he would talk to me and I would talk to him. If someone distracted me from him, he would swim in my belly and I would hear him say and in maturity Muqatil said: He means when he meets before he is raised to the sky. Al-Husayn bin Al-Fadl said and in maturity after his descent from the sky. It was said: He informed us that he would remain until he reached maturity, and his speech after maturity is his report of miraculous things. It was said: and in maturity is a prophet who gave her good report of the prophethood of Jesus, peace be upon him, and his speech in the cradle is a miracle and in maturity is a call. Mujahid said: and in maturity means forbearing. The Arabs praise maturity and his speech in the cradle is a miracle and in maturity is a call. Mujahid said: and in maturity means forbearing. The Arabs praise middle age because it is the middle state in terms of advanced age, sound mind, and denial of opinion and experience. And among the righteous means: he is among the righteous servants.
3:47: 47- "She said: 'Lord', my Lord, she says it to Gabriel. It was said: She says to God Almighty, 'How can I have a son when no man has touched me' and no man has touched me?' She said that in astonishment, since it was not customary for a son to be born who has no father." He said, "Thus does God create what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is," as He wills.
3:48: 48- The Almighty’s saying: And teaches him the Book. The people of Medina, Asim, and Jacob read it with the letter ya because of the Almighty’s saying: Thus does God create what He wills. It was said: This is a response to His saying: Indeed, God gives you good tidings. “And teaches him.” The others read it with the letter noon for emphasis, like the Almighty’s saying: This is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you. His saying: The Book means writing and script, and wisdom means knowledge and understanding, and the Torah and the Gospel God taught him the Torah and the Gospel.
3:49: 49- And a messenger meaning, and We made him a messenger to the Children of Israel It was said: He was a messenger in his youth, and it was said: He was only a messenger after reaching puberty, and the first prophet of the Children of Israel was Joseph and the last of them was Jesus, peace be upon them, so when he was sent, he said: I Al-Kisa'i said: It was opened because he sent the message to him, and it was said: Its meaning is that I have come to you with a sign a sign from your Lord that confirms my words, and he only said: with a sign, and he came with signs because all of them indicated one thing, which is a truth in the message, so when Jesus, peace be upon him, said that to the Children of Israel, they said: What is it? He said: I Nafi' read with a kasra on the alif as a new beginning, and the rest read with a fatha on the meaning that I create meaning I form and measure for you from clay like the form of a bird Abu Ja'far read like the form of a bird here and in Al-Ma'idah, and the form is the prepared image from their saying: I prepared the thing that I measured and fixed it The majority read it in the plural because He created many birds. The people of Medina read and Jacob so it becomes a bird in the singular form here. In Surat Al-Ma’idah, they went to one type of bird because He did not create anything other than the bat. Rather, the bat was singled out because it is the most perfect bird in creation because it has a breast and teeth and it menstruates. Wahb said: It used to fly as long as people were looking at it, but when it disappeared from their sight, it fell dead, so that the act of creation would be distinguished from the act of the Creator, and so that it would be known that perfection belongs to God Almighty. And I heal the blind and the leper meaning I cure them and make them healthy. They differed about the blind. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: It is the one who was born blind. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: It is the blind. Ikrimah said: It is the one who was blind. Mujahed said: It is the one who sees during the day but does not see at night. And the leper is the one who has a clear vision. He only singled these two out because they are two incurable diseases. Medicine was prevalent at the time of Jesus, peace be upon him, so he showed them a miracle of that type. Wahb said: Perhaps fifty thousand sick people would gather at Jesus, peace be upon him, in one day. Whoever was able to reach him, he would reach him, and whoever was not, Jesus, peace be upon him, would walk to him and he would treat them with supplication on the condition of faith. God the Almighty said: And I revive the dead by God’s permission. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He revived four souls: Azar, the son of the old woman, the daughter of the tenth, and Sam, son of Noah. As for Azar, he was a friend of his, so his sister sent to Jesus, peace be upon him: Your brother Azar is dying, and there was a three-day journey between them. So he and his companions came to him and found that he had died three days ago. So he said to his sister: Let us go to his grave. So she went with them to his grave, and he called upon God the Almighty, and Azar rose and his blood was dripping. He came out of his grave and remained and had a son. As for the old woman’s son, he passed by Jesus, peace be upon him, dead on a bed being carried. So Jesus called upon God, sat on his bed, descended on the necks of the men, put on his clothes, carried the bed on his neck, and returned to his family. He remained and had a son. As for the daughter of the tenth, her father was a man who took tithes. His daughter died yesterday, so he called upon God, the Almighty, by His Greatest Name, and God, the Most High, revived her and she remained after that for a while and she had a child. As for Sam, son of Noah, peace be upon him, Jesus, peace be upon him, came to his grave and called upon God’s Greatest Name. He came out of his grave with half of his head gray for fear of the Hour, and they did not have gray hair at that time. He said: Has the Hour come? He said: No, but I called upon you by God’s Greatest Name. Then he said to him: Die. He said: On the condition that God protects me from the throes of death. So he called upon God and He did. God Almighty says: And I will inform you and tell you of what you eat that I did not see and what you store that you raise in your homes until you eat it. It was said: He was informing/the man of what he ate last night, what he is eating today, and what he has saved for dinner. Al-Suddi said: Jesus, peace be upon him, used to tell the boys in the book what their fathers were doing and he would say to the boy: Go, your family has eaten such and such and raised such and such for you. So the boy would go to his family and cry over them until they gave him that thing. Then they would say: Who told you this? He would say: Jesus. So they kept their boys away from him and said: Do not play with this magician. So they gathered them in a house. Then Jesus, peace be upon him, came looking for them, but they said: They are not here. So he said: What is in this house? They said: Pigs. Jesus said: That is how they will be. So they opened the gate for them and behold, they were pigs. This spread among the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel were concerned about him, but when his mother feared for him, she carried him on her donkeys, and a pit of them went out to the people of Egypt. Qatada said: This is only in the table, and it was a table that descended upon them wherever they were like manna and quails. They were commanded not to betray or hide for the next day, but they betrayed and hid. Jesus began to tell them what they had eaten from the table and what they had stored from it, so God transformed them into pigs. God Almighty says: Indeed in that which I mentioned is a sign for you, if you are believers.
3:50: 50- And confirming is an appositive to his saying and a messenger "of what came before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you" of meats and fats. Abu Ubaidah said: He meant by some all, meaning: all of what was forbidden to you. And some may be mentioned and meant by it all, like the saying of Labid. There are places where I don't like them, or some souls are attached to their doves. Meaning: all souls. The Almighty says: And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord. He means what was mentioned of the signs, and he only singled them out because they are all of one type in indicating his message. So fear God and obey me.
3:51: 51-"Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path."
3:52: 52- The Almighty said: And when Jesus perceived disbelief on their part meaning he found it. Al-Farra’ said, and Abu Ubaidah said: He knew, and Muqatil said: He saw disbelief on their part and they wanted to kill him, so he sought help against them and said: “He said: Who will be my helpers for God?” Al-Suddi said: The reason for that was that when God the Almighty sent Jesus, peace be upon him, to the Children of Israel and ordered him to call to Islam, the Children of Israel exiled him and expelled him, so he and his mother went out wandering in the land, and they stopped in a village with a man who hosted them and treated them well. That city had a tyrant who was aggressive, so that man came one day worried and sad, so he entered his house and Mary was with his wife, so Mary said to her: What is the matter with your husband that I see him sad? She said: Do not ask me. She said: Tell me, perhaps God will relieve his distress. She said: We have a king who appoints for each man of us a day to feed him and his soldiers and give them wine to drink, and if he does not do so, he will punish him, and today is our turn and we do not have the space for that. She said: So tell him not to worry, for I will command my son to pray for him, and that will suffice. Mary said to Jesus, peace be upon him, about that, and Jesus said: If you do that, evil will happen. She said: Do not worry, for he has been good to us and honored us. Jesus, peace be upon him, said: Then tell him, when that is near, fill your pots and jars with water, then inform me. So he did that, and Jesus, peace be upon him, called upon God Almighty, and the water in the pots turned into broth and meat, and the water in the jars into wine, the likes of which people had never seen before. When the king came, he ate, and when he drank the wine, he said: Where is this wine from? He said: From such and such a land. The king said: My wine is from that land, and it is not like this one. He said: It is from another land. When the confusion over the king became severe, he said: Then I will tell you, I have a young man who does not ask God for anything except that He gives it to him. He called upon God, and He turned the water into wine. The king had a son whom he wanted to make his successor, but he died a few days before that, and he was the most beloved of creation to him. So he said: A man called upon God until He turned the water into wine so that his prayer would be answered until My son will be revived. So he called Jesus, peace be upon him, and spoke to him about that. Jesus said: Do not do that, for if he lives, evil will happen. The king said: I do not care, do I not see him? Jesus said: If I revive him, you and my mother will be left to go wherever we want. He said: Yes. So he called upon God, and the boy lived. When the people of his kingdom saw that he had lived, they rushed to take up arms and said: We have eaten this until his death drew near, so he wants to appoint his son as his successor to it and eat as his father ate. So they fought. Jesus and his mother went and passed by the disciples while they were fishing. He said: What are you doing? They said: We are fishing. He said: Why don’t you walk so that we can catch people? They said: Who are you? He said: I am Jesus, son of Mary, the servant and messenger of God, one of the helpers to God. So believe and go with him. God the Almighty said: Of my helpers for God. Al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj said: “With God the Almighty, the Arabs say: ‘The flock to the flock are camels’ meaning with the flock, and as God the Almighty said: “And do not consume their wealth along with your wealth” An-Nisa’ 2, Ḍay with your wealth. Al-Hasan and Abu Ubaidah said: To means in, meaning from among my helpers in God, meaning in the essence of God and His path. It was said that to in its place means whoever adds his support to God’s support for me. They differed regarding the disciples. Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: They were fishermen who used to catch fish, and they were called disciples because of the whiteness of their clothes. It was also said: They were sailors. Al-Hasan said: They were whiteners, and they were called that because they used to whiten their clothes. Ata’ said: Mary entrusted Jesus, peace be upon him, with various tasks, the last of which was to the disciples, who were dyers and tanners, so she entrusted him to their chief to learn from him. They gathered at a place of clothing and a scroll was presented to him, so he said to Jesus: You have learned this craft and I am going on a journey and will not return for ten days. These are the clothes of the people of different colors, and I have marked each one of them with a thread of the color with which it is dyed, so it must be empty of them when I come. So he went out and Jesus cooked one pot of one color and put all the clothes in and said: Be, by God’s permission, as I want you to be. So he brought the disciples and all the clothes into the pit, and he said: What did you do? He said: I finished them. He said: Where are they? He said: In the well. He said: All of them. He said: He said: You have spoiled those garments. He said: Get up and look. So Jesus brought out a red garment, a yellow garment, and a green garment until he brought them out in the colors he wanted. The disciples were amazed, so he knew that this was from God. He said to the al-Nas 114:Come and look. So he and his companions believed in him, so they are the disciples. Ad-Dahhak said: They were called disciples because of the purity of their hearts. Ibn al-Mubarak said: They were called this because of the effect of worship and its light on them. The origin of the houris among the Arabs is intense whiteness. It is said: A man is squint-eyed and a woman is squint-eyed, meaning very white. Al-Kalbi and Ikrimah said: The disciples are the pure ones, and they were the pure ones of Jesus, peace be upon him, and they were twelve men. Ruh ibn al-Qasim said: I asked Qatada about the disciples. He said: They are the ones who are fit for the caliphate. And from him, he said: The disciples are the ministers. Al-Hasan said: The disciples are the supporters and the disciple is the supporter. The disciple in the speech of the Arabs is specifically the man who is sought for help / in what he is responsible for. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir told us: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon the people on the day of the Trench, and Al-Zubayr volunteered. Then he called upon them, and Al-Zubayr volunteered. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every prophet has a disciple, and my disciple is Al-Zubayr. Sufyan said: The helper disciple. Al-Muammar said: Qatada said: The disciples were all from Quraysh 106:Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Hamza, Jafar, Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, Uthman ibn Muzaffun, Abd al-Rahman, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, Talhah ibn Ubayd God, and al-Zubayr ibn al-`Awwam, may God be pleased with them all. The disciples said: We are the supporters of God, the helpers of God’s religion and His Messenger. We believe in God, and bear witness, O Jesus, that we are Muslims.
3:53: 53-Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed of Your Book and we have followed the Messenger Jesus so register us among the witnesses who testified to the truthfulness of Your prophets. Ata’ said: With the prophets because every prophet is a witness for his nation. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: With Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation, because they bear witness to the messengers’ message.
3:54: 54- The Almighty said: And they plotted meaning the infidels of the Children of Israel from whom Jesus sensed disbelief and they were wicked in killing Jesus, peace be upon him. This is because Jesus, peace be upon him, after his people expelled him and his mother, returned to them with the disciples and cried out to them with the call, so they intended to kill him and conspired to kill him. This is their plot. God Almighty said: And the plot of God, and God is the best of plotters. So the plot of the created beings is: malice, deception, and trickery. The plot of God is: luring the servant and taking him suddenly from where he does not know, as He said: We will lead them on gradually from where they do not know 182-Al-A'raf. Al-Zajjaj said: The plot of God Almighty is their recompense for their plot, so the recompense is called the beginning because it is in opposition to it, as God Almighty said: God mocks them 15-Al-Baqarah And He is the One who deceives them 142-An-Nisa. The plot of God Almighty is specifically for them in this verse, and it is His casting doubts. On their companion who wanted to kill Jesus, peace be upon him, until he was killed. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: Jesus met a group of Jews, and when they saw him they said: The sorcerer, the son of the sorcerer, has come, and the perpetrator is the son of the perpetrator, and they slandered him and his mother. When Jesus, peace be upon him, heard that, he invoked curses upon them and God transformed them into pigs. When Judah, the head of the Jews and their prince, saw that, he was alarmed and feared his call. The Jews united to kill Jesus, peace be upon him, and they rose up to kill him. God sent Gabriel to him, and he put him in a window with a window on the roof. God raised him to heaven from that window. Judah, the head of the Jews, ordered one of his companions, called Tatianus, to enter the window and kill him. When he entered, he did not see Jesus, so he delayed them, so they thought that he was fighting him there. God cast upon him the likeness of Jesus, peace be upon him. When he entered, he did not see Jesus, so he delayed them, so they thought that he was fighting him there. God cast upon him the likeness of Jesus, peace be upon him. When he came out, they thought that he was Jesus, peace be upon him, so they killed him and crucified him. Wahb said: They knocked on Jesus in the middle of the night, and set up a cross to crucify him. The earth became dark, so God sent the angels who stood between them and him. Jesus gathered the disciples that night and advised them, then he said: Let one of you disbelieve in me before the rooster crows and sell me for a few dirhams. So they brought out thirty dirhams for him, and they took them and he showed them to him. When he entered the house, God cast the likeness of Jesus upon him, so Jesus was raised and he took the one who showed them to him and said: I am the one who showed you to him, but they paid no attention to what he said and killed him and crucified him, thinking that he was Jesus. When the likeness of Jesus was crucified, Mary, the mother of Jesus, and a woman for whom Jesus had prayed and whom God had cured of madness came crying beside the crucified man, so Jesus, peace be upon him, came to them and said to them: Why are you crying? God the Almighty raised me up and nothing but good befell me, and this is something that seemed to them to be. Then, after seven days, God the Almighty said to Jesus, peace be upon him: Descend upon Mary Magdalene, the name of a place on her mountain, for no one has wept for you as she did, nor grieved as she did. Then let the disciples gather for you and spread them throughout the earth as callers to God the Almighty. So God sent him down upon her, and the mountain lit up with light when he descended. So he gathered for him and the disciples, and he spread them throughout the earth as callers to God the Almighty. Then God the Almighty raised him up to him, and that is the night in which the Christians entered. When the disciples awoke, each one of them spoke in the language of the one to whom Jesus had sent him, and that is what God the Almighty said: And they plotted, and God planned, and God is the best of planners. Al-Suddi said: The Jews imprisoned Jesus in a house with ten of the disciples, and a man from among them entered upon them, and God cast his resemblance upon him. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, Jesus, peace be upon him, said to his companions: Who among you will cast my resemblance upon him? He will be killed. A man from the people said: I will, O Prophet of God. So that man was killed, and God prevented Jesus, peace be upon him, and raised him to Him, and God clothed him with feathers and clothed him with light and cut off from him the pleasure of food and drink, and he flew with the angels, so he is with them around the world. He was a human, angelic, heavenly, earthly being. The historians said: Mary became pregnant with Jesus when she was thirteen years old, and she gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem in the land of Uri Shalam, sixty-five years after Alexander’s victory over the land of Babylon, so God revealed to him at the beginning of the thirtieth year, and God raised him from Jerusalem on the Night of Decree in the month of Ramadan, and he was thirty-three years old, so his prophethood was three years, and his mother Mary lived after his raising for six years.
3:55: 55- "When God said, O Jesus, I will take you and raise you up to Me." They differed about the meaning of taking you up here. Al-Hasan, Al-Kalbi, and Ibn Jurayj said: I will take you and raise you up from this world to Me without death. This is indicated by the Almighty's saying: "So when You took me up" 117-Al-Ma'idah, meaning You took me up to the heavens while I was alive, because his people only became victorious after he was taken up to the heavens, not after his death. So based on this, taking up has two interpretations. One of them is: I will raise you up to Me completely, without getting anything from you, from their saying I took up such-and-such and I took it up completely, and the other is: I take possession of you from their saying I took up such-and-such from him, meaning I received it. Al-Rabi' bin Anas said: What is meant by taking up is sleep and every one with an eye is asleep, and Jesus had slept, so God raised him up to the heavens sleeping, meaning: I am asleep and I will raise you up to Me, as God Almighty said: "And it is He who takes you up by night." 60-Al-An’am That is, He puts you to sleep. Some of them said: What is meant by death is death. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that its meaning is: I am causing you to die, as indicated by the words of God Almighty: “Say: The Angel of Death will take you” 11-Sajdah. Based on this, it has two interpretations: One of them is what Wahb said: God caused Jesus to die for three hours of the day, then God raised him up to Himself. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: The Christians claim that God Almighty caused him to die for seven hours of the day, then He revived him and raised him up. The other is what Adh-Dahhak and a group said: In this verse there is an advancement and a delay, the meaning of which is that I am raising you up to Me and purifying you from those who disbelieved, and I will cause you to die after sending you down from the sky. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi informed us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih informed us, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi informed us, Ali bin Al-Ja’d informed us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Abi Salamah Al-Majshun informed us on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is Muhammad’s soul, the son of Mary will soon descend among you as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the pig, abolish the jizya, and wealth will be so abundant that no one will accept it.” It is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, that he said: In his time, all religions will perish except Islam, and the Antichrist will perish and remain on earth for forty years, then he will die and the Muslims will pray over him. It was said to Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl: Do you find the descent of Jesus in the Qur’an? He said: Yes, and as an adult. He did not become an adult in this world, but rather it means as an adult after his descent from heaven. God the Almighty said: And He will purify you from those who disbelieve meaning He will bring you out from among them and save you from them. And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’, Ash-Sha’bi, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: They are the people of Islam who believed in him and followed his religion in monotheism from his nation Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They are superior to those who disbelieved, apparent and victorious with honor, strength, and strength. Ad-Dahhak said: He means the disciples, superior to those who disbelieved. It was also said: They are the Romans. It was also said: He meant the Christians by them, so they are superior to the Jews until the Day of Resurrection. The kingdom of the Jews has gone, but the kingdom of the Christians will remain until close to the Day of Resurrection. Based on this, following means claiming and loving, not following those who Then to Me is your return in the Hereafter. And I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ of the matter of religion and the matter of Jesus.
3:56: 56- As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world by killing, captivity, tribute, and humiliation and in the Hereafter meaning in the Hereafter with the Fire and they will have no helpers.
3:57: 57- And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their full rewards. Al-Hasan and Hafs read it with the letter ya, and the rest read it with the letter noon, meaning He will give them the full rewards for their deeds. And God does not love the wrongdoers, meaning He does not have mercy on the disbelievers, nor does He praise them with kindness.
3:58: 58- The Almighty said: That meaning this which I mentioned to you of the report about Jesus, Mary and the disciples We recite to you We inform you of it through Gabriel’s recitation to you of the verses and the wise remembrance meaning the Qur’an and the remembrance of wisdom. Muqatil said: The wise remembrance means the decisive one that is forbidden from falsehood. It was said: The wise remembrance is the Preserved Tablet, and it is hung in the sky from a white pearl. It was said: It is from the verses, meaning the signs indicating your prophethood because it is report that no one knows except the reader of a book or the one to whom it is revealed, and you are illiterate and do not read.
3:59: 59- The Almighty said: The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam. "The verse was revealed about the delegation of Najran, and that is because they said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why do you curse our companion? He said: What should I say? They said: You say that he is the servant of God. He said: Yes, he is the servant of God and His Messenger and His Word which He bestowed upon Mary the Virgin. They became angry and said: Have you ever seen a human being without a father? So God Almighty revealed: The likeness of Jesus before God "is that he was created without a father or mother." He created him from dust, then said to him (meaning Jesus, peace be upon him), "Be, and he was." That is, and he was. If it is said, what is the meaning of His saying He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be, and he was and no creation after creation? It is said that it means He created him, then He informed you that I said to him, Be," and he was, without any order in creation as there is in birth. It is like a man saying: I gave you a dirham today, then I gave you a dirham yesterday, meaning, then He informed you that I gave you a dirham yesterday. The above example is evidence of the permissibility of analogy, because analogy is the return of a branch to a root with a type of resemblance, and God Almighty returned the creation of Jesus to Adam, peace be upon them, with a type of resemblance.
3:60: 60- The Almighty said: The truth is from your Lord meaning it is the truth. It was also said that the truth came to you from your Lord. So do not be among the doubters the doubters. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation.
3:61: 61- The Almighty said: So whoever disputes with you about him meaning argues with you about Jesus or about the truth after what has come to you of knowledge that Jesus is the servant of God and His Messenger say, ‘Come’ and its root is come from the verb to rise but the damma on the ya’ was considered too heavy so it was deleted. Al-Farra’ said: It means come, as if he was saying: rise. His saying we call is in the jussive mood as a response to the command and the sign of the jussive mood is the falling of the wad our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves It was said: our sons meant Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain, and our women are Fatima. And our souls meant himself and Ali, may God be pleased with him, and the Arabs call the cousin of the man himself, as God Almighty said: And do not criticize one another 11- Al-Hujurat meaning your brothers, and it was said that it is in general the group of people of religion. Then let us supplicate. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: That is, we implore in supplication. Al-Kalbi said: We strive and exaggerate in supplication. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaidah said: We curse and supplication, cursing is said: Upon him be the curse of God, meaning his curse: So we place the curse of God upon the liars from us and from you in the matter of Jesus, so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, read this verse to the delegation of Najran and called them to the Mubahala, they said: Until we return and consider our matter, then we will come to you tomorrow, so some of them were alone with each other and said to the follower who had their opinion: O servant of the Messiah, what do you see? He said: By God, I have made you know, O Christians, that Muhammad is a prophet sent by God. By God, no people have ever had a prophet whose elders have lived and whose young have grown. If you do that, we will perish. If you refuse to do anything but remain as you say about your companion, then say farewell to the man and return to your country. So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had come in the morning embracing al-Husayn, taking al-Hasan by the hand, and Fatima was walking behind him and Ali was behind her, and he was saying to them: When I supplicate, then believe. So the Bishop of Najran said: O Christians, I see faces that if they asked God to move a mountain from its place, He would move it. So do not supplicate, lest you perish, and no Christian among you will remain on the face of the earth until the Day of Resurrection. So they said: O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you and to leave you in your religion and remain in our religion. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you refuse to curse, then submit and you will have what the Muslims have and you will have what they have. But they refused, so he said: Then I They said: We have no power to fight the Arabs, but we will make peace with you on the condition that you do not invade us, frighten us, or turn us away from our religion, on the condition that we give you two thousand garments every year, a thousand in Safar and a thousand in Rajab. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with them on that basis and said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the punishment has descended upon the people of Najran, and if they cursed each other, they would be transformed into monkeys and pigs, and the valley would be set ablaze with fire, and God would uproot Najran and its people, even the birds on the trees, and a year would not have passed over all the Christians until they perished.
3:62: 62- God Almighty said: “This is indeed the true story, the true report. There is no god but God.” And from the connection of its meaning, There is no god but God, “And indeed, God is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
3:63: 63- But if they turn away turn away from faith then indeed, God is Knowing of the corrupters who worship other than God and call people to worship other than God.
3:64: 64- The Almighty said: "Say, 'O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you.'" The commentators said: "The Najran delegation came to Medina and met with the Jews, and they argued about Abraham, peace be upon him. The Christians claimed that he was a Christian and they were of his religion and the people most worthy of him. The Jews said: Rather, he was a Jew and they were of his religion and the people most worthy of him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Both groups are innocent of Abraham and his religion. Rather, Abraham was a monotheist Muslim and I am of his religion, so follow his religion, the religion of Islam. The Jews said: O Muhammad, you only want us to take you as a lord as the Christians took Jesus as a lord. The Christians said: O Muhammad, you only want us to say about you what the Jews said about Ezra. So God Almighty revealed: Say, O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you. The Arabs call every story that has an explanation a word, and from this the poem was named the word equitable, meaning a level matter. It is said: So-and-so called for equality, meaning fairness. And the middle of everything is equal, and from it is the saying of the Most High: So he saw him in the middle of Hell 55-As-Saffat. It was only said for half equal because the most just and best of matters are their middle. And equal is an attribute of a word except that it is a source, and sources are not dualized, nor pluralized, nor feminine, so if you open the seen, it is extended, and if it is broken or closed, it is shortened like the saying of the Most High: A place equal 58-Taha. Then He explained the word and said: That we worship none but God. The place of that is raised on the omission of it, and Al-Zajjaj said: It is raised by the beginning, and it was said: Its place is accusative by removing the letter of the attribute, meaning that we worship none but God, and it was said: Its place is lowered instead of the word, meaning come to us to worship none but God and not associate anything with Him, and not take one another as lords besides God, as the Jews and Christians did, God the Most High said: They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God 31-At-Tawbah. And Ikrimah said: It is the prostration of some of them to each other, meaning do not prostrate to other than God. It was said: Its meaning is that we do not obey anyone in disobeying God. If they turn away, then say, ‘Bear witness.’ So say to them, Bear witness that we are Muslims, sincere in monotheism. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ told us, Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Ubaid God bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Masoud told us that Abdullah bin Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, told him that Abu Sufyan bin Harb told him that Heraclius sent to him with a group of Quraysh, and they were trading in the Levant during the period in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made a treaty with Abu Sufyan and the infidels of Quraysh.
