They came to him while he was in Ilia, so he called them to his council, and the leaders of the Romans were around him, and he called for the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which Dihya bin Khalifa Al-Kalbi had sent to the leader of Busra, so he gave it to Heraclius, and he saw it, and it was: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the servant of God and His Messenger, to Heraclius, the Great of the Romans. Peace be upon him who follows the guidance. Now then: I invite you to the call of Islam. Submit and you will be safe. Submit and God will give you your reward twice. But if you turn away, then upon you is only the sin of the Iryians. O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except God and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords besides God. But if they turn away, then say, Bear witness that we are Muslims [in submission].
3:65: 65- The Almighty said: O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? You claim that he was of your religion, but your religion is Judaism and Christianity. Judaism came after the Torah was revealed, and Christianity came after the Gospel was revealed. The Torah and the Gospel were revealed a long time after Abraham, and there were a thousand years between Abraham and Moses and a thousand years between Moses and Jesus. Do you not understand? The invalidity of your statement?
3:66: 66- The Almighty said: Here you are with a softening of the hamza where it was Madani, and Abu Amr and the rest with the hamza, and they differed about its origin, so some of them said: Its origin is: you and this is an alert, and Al-Akhfash said: Its origin is you, so the first hamza was changed to a ha, like their saying I poured out the water and I poured out. “These ones” its origin is ula with the alert ha’ entered into it and it is in the position of a call, meaning O these ones, you You argued you argued about that of which you have knowledge meaning about the matter of Moses and Jesus and you claimed that you are on their religion and the Torah and the Gospel were sent down to you So why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge and it is not in your book that he was Jewish or Christian, and it was said that you argued about that which he spoke about with knowledge meaning about the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they found his description in their book, so they argued about him with falsehood, so why do you argue about Abraham, and there is no N in your book and you have no knowledge about him? And God knows and you do not know. Then God Almighty acquitted Abraham of what they said, so He said:
3:67: 67- "Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim [submitting to God]. And he was not of the polytheists." The inclining toward truth is the one who deviates from all religions to the straight religion. It has also been said that the inclining toward truth is the one who believes in monotheism, performs Hajj, sacrifices, circumcises, and faces the Kaaba. It is the easiest of the two religions and the most beloved to God Almighty.
3:68: 68- The Almighty said: Indeed, the people who have the closest claim to Abraham are those who followed him meaning: those who followed him in his time, and this Prophet meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who believed with him, meaning from this nation, and God is the ally of the believers. Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated it on the authority of Ibn Shihab with his chain of transmission, the hadith of the migration to Abyssinia, when Ja’far ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Abyssinia and settled there, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, and what happened at Badr happened. The Quraysh gathered in the House of Assembly and said: We have a vendetta against those of the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who were killed at Badr among you. So collect money and present it to the Negus, so that he may give you some of your people who are with him, and two men of your opinion may volunteer for that. So they sent Amr ibn al-Aas and Ammarah ibn al-Walid with the gifts of leather and other things, and they boarded the sea and came to Abyssinia. When they entered upon the Negus, they prostrated to him and greeted him and said to him: Our people are sincere and grateful to you, and they love your righteousness, and they have sent us to you to warn you of these people who have come to you, because they are the people of a man. A liar came out among us, claiming that he is the Messenger of God, and none of us followed him except the foolish. We had made the matter difficult for them and forbidden them to a valley in our land where no one would enter upon them and no one would leave them. Hunger and thirst had killed them. When the matter became difficult for them, he sent his cousin to you to corrupt your religion, your kingdom, and your subjects. So, slay them and hand them over to us so that we may suffice you against them. They said: The sign of that is that when they enter upon you, they will not prostrate to you nor greet you with the greeting with which people greet you, out of aversion to your religion and your Sunnah. He said: So the Negus summoned them, and when they were present, Ja’far shouted at the door: The party of God is asking permission to enter upon you. The Negus said: Tell this shouter to repeat his words. Ja’far did so, and the Negus said: Yes, let them enter with the safety and protection of God. Amr ibn al-Aas looked at his companion and said: Do you not hear how they are ranting about the party of God and how the Negus answered them? That upset them both. Then they entered upon him and did not prostrate to him. Amr ibn al-Aas said: They say that they are too proud to prostrate to you, so the Negus said to them: What prevented you from prostrating to me and greeting me with the greeting with which those who come to me from the horizons greet me? They said: We prostrate to God who created you and made you king, and that greeting was only for us when we worshipped idols, so God sent among us a truthful prophet who commanded us to greet with the greeting that God was pleased with, which is peace, the greeting of the people of Paradise. The Negus knew that this was true and that it was in the Torah and the Gospel. He said: Which of you is calling: The party of God seeks permission to see you? Ja`far said: I will. He said: Speak. He said: You are a king from the kings of the people of the earth and from the people of the Book, and much talk or injustice is not appropriate for you, and I like to respond to my companions, so order these two men, one of them to speak and the other to listen so that you hear our conversation. Amr said to Ja`far: Speak. Ja`far said to the Negus: Are they slaves or free? Amr said: Rather, they are free and noble. The Negus said: If it is a qintar, then I will pay it. Amr said: No, not even a qirat. The Negus said: What do you want from them? Amr said: We and they were on one religion and one matter, the religion of our fathers, but they abandoned that and sought another, so we sent their people to you so that you might bring them to us. The Negus said: What is this religion that you were on and the religion that you followed? Tell me the truth. Ja’far said: As for the religion that we were on and abandoned, it is the religion of Satan. We disbelieved in God and worshipped stones. As for the religion to which we converted, it is the religion of God, Islam, which was brought to us by God as a Messenger and a Book like the Book of Jesus, son of Mary, in agreement with it. The Negus said: O Ja’far, you have spoken of a great matter, so take it easy. Then the Negus ordered the bell to be rang and every priest and monk gathered around him. When they had gathered around him, the Negus said: I ask you by God who sent down the Gospel to Jesus, do you find between Jesus and the Day of Resurrection a prophet sent? They said: Yes, by God, Jesus gave us glad tidings of him and said: Whoever believes in him has believed in me, and whoever disbelieves in him has disbelieved in me. The Negus said to Ja’far: What does this man say to you and what does he command you to do? He forbids you from it? He said: He recites to us the Book of God, and enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong, and enjoins good neighborliness, maintaining family ties, and being kind to orphans, and he orders us to worship God alone, with no partner or associate. He said: Recite to me what he recites to you. So he recited to them Surat Al-Ankaboot and Surat Al-Rum. The eyes of the Negus and his companions overflowed with tears and they said: O Jaafar, turn us away from this good talk. So he recited to them Surat Al-Kahf. Amr wanted to anger the Negus, but he said: They curse Jesus and his mother. The Negus said: What do you say about Jesus and his mother? So he recited to them Surat Maryam. When Jaafar mentioned Maryam and Jesus, peace be upon them, the Negus raised his siwak to the extent that it would make the eye bleed and said: By God, the Messiah did not do more than what you say. Then he turned to Jaafar and his companions and said: Go, for you are safe in my land (i.e. safe from anyone who insults or harms you). Then he said: Be of good cheer and do not fear, for there is no time today for the party of Abraham. Amr said: O Negus, and who is the party of Abraham? He said: These are the people and their companion who came from him and those who followed them. The polytheists denied that and claimed that they were not followers of the religion of Abraham. Then the Negus returned the money they had brought to Amr and his companion and said: Your gift to me was only a bribe, so take it, for God has given me control and has not taken a bribe from me. Jaafar said: So we departed and were in the best home and the most honorable neighborhood. That day God Almighty revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding their dispute over Abraham while he was in Medina, His Almighty saying: “Indeed, the people who have the closest claim to Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet and those who believe. And God is the ally of the believers.”
3:69: 69- The Almighty said: A group of the People of the Book wished It was revealed about Muadh bin Jabal, Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, and Ammar bin Yasir when the Jews called them to their religion. So the verse A group of the People of the Book wished was revealed wishing meaning the Jews that they could mislead you from your religion and return you to disbelief And they mislead only themselves, and they perceive [it] not.
3:70: 70- O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God? meaning the Qur’an and the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while you bear witness that his description is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel.
3:71: 71- O People of the Scripture, why do you mix truth with falsehood? You mix Islam with Judaism and Christianity that were revealed to Moses with the falsehood that you distorted and wrote with your own hands and conceal the truth while you know that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his religion are the truth.
3:72: 72- The Almighty said: And a group of the People of the Scripture said, ‘Believe.’ The verse: Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: Twelve rabbis from the Jews of Khaybar and the villages of Uyaynah conspired and said to each other: Enter the religion of Muhammad at the beginning of the day with the tongue without belief, then disbelieve at the end of the day and say: We looked in our books and consulted our scholars and found that Muhammad is not like that, and his lie became clear to us. If you do that, his companions will doubt their religion and accuse him and say: They are the People of the Scripture and they are more knowledgeable about it than us, so they will turn away from their religion. Mujahid, Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: This is about the direction of the qiblah when it was changed to the Kaaba, which was difficult for the Jews. So Ka’b ibn Al-Ashraf said to his companions: Believe in what was revealed to Muhammad about the matter of the Kaaba and pray towards it at the beginning of the day, then disbelieve and return to your qiblah at the end of the day, perhaps they will say, These are the People of the Book, and they know better, so they will return to our qiblah. So God Almighty informed His Messenger of their secret and revealed: And a party of the People of the Scripture said, ‘Believe in that which was revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day,’ the beginning of which was called a direction because it is the most beautiful part of it and the first thing that faces the observer and he sees it. And disbelieve at its end, perhaps they will return, so they will doubt and return from their religion.
3:73: 73- The Almighty's saying: "And do not believe except for him who follows your religion." This is connected to the first of the Jews' saying to each other: "And do not believe, meaning do not believe except for him who follows your religion who agrees with your religion, and the lam in for" is a connection, meaning do not believe except for one who follows your Jewish religion, like the Almighty's saying: "Say: Perhaps there will be a successor to you" 72-An-Nahl, meaning: your successor. "Say: Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God." This is report from God the Almighty that the statement is its statement, then they differed: Some of them said: It is an interrupting statement between two statements, and what follows it is connected to the first statement / report of the Jews' saying to each other, and its meaning is: And do not believe except for him who follows your religion, and do not believe that someone is given like what you have been given of knowledge, the Book, wisdom, and signs of manna, quails, and the splitting of the sea, and other miracles. And do not believe that they will argue with you before your Lord because you are more correct in religion than them. This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid. It was said: The Jews said to their lowest ones, And do not believe except in him who follows your religion, “that someone should be given the like of what you have been given,” knowledge, meaning: so that someone should not be given, and there is no implied meaning in it, like the Almighty’s saying, God makes clear to you, lest you go astray (An-Nisa’: 176), meaning: so that you do not go astray, he says: Do not believe them, lest they know the like of what you know, and you will have the advantage over them in knowledge, and lest they argue with you before your Lord and say: You have known that our religion is the truth, and this is the meaning of Ibn Jurayj’s saying. Al-Hasan and Al-A'mash readِرن ُتَسىwith a kasra on the alif, so the statement of the Jews is complete when he says: Except for those who follow your religion and what follows from the statement of God the Most High: Say, O Muhammad Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God, if he is given In means denial, meaning no one is given what you have been given, O nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, or they argue with you before your Lord meaning: unless the Jews argue with you falsely and say: We are better than you, so the statement of God the Most Highِرن ُتَسى(with your Lord) means with your Lord’s favor upon you, and this is the meaning of the statement of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Al-Kalbi and Muqatil. Al-Farra’ said: It is permissible forأتوسto mean حتىas it is said: It is attached to it or He gives you your right meaning until He gives you your right, and the meaning of the verse: No one has been given what you have been given, O nation of Muhammad, of religion and proof until they argue with you before your Lord. Ibn Kathir read that someone is given with a long vowel as a question, and then it is an abbreviation, the meaning of which is: that someone is given the like of what you, O group of Jews, have been given of the Book and wisdom, and you envy him and do not believe in him. This is the saying of Qatada and Al-Rabi’, and they said: This is from the saying of God Almighty, He says: Say to them, O Muhammad, Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God by sending down a book like your book and sending a prophet whom you envy and disbelieve in. “Say: ‘Indeed, the bounty is in the hand of God. He grants it to whom He wills. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.’” His statement, or they argue with you according to this reading, refers back to the error of the believers, and or is in the sense of if because they are conditional and consequential letters, one of which clarifies the position of the other. That is, if they argue with you, O company of believers, before your Lord, then say, O Muhammad: Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God, and we are upon it. It is possible that all of them are addressed to the believers, and the structure of the verse is: If someone is given the like of what you have been given, O company of believers, they envy you, then say, Indeed, the bounty is in the hand of God. And if they argue with you, then say, Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God. It is possible that the report about the Jews was completed when He said perhaps they will return, and the Almighty’s saying and do not believe is from the words of God, with which He strengthens the hearts of the believers so that they do not doubt when the Jews deceive and falsify their religion. He says, O group of believers, do not believe except those who follow your religion, and do not believe that anyone will be given the same as you have been given of religion and virtue, and do not believe that they will argue with you about your religion before your Lord and are able to do so, for guidance is the guidance of God, and (Indeed, virtue is in the hand of God. He gives it to whom He wills, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing), so the entire verse is God addressing the believers when the Jews deceive them so that they do not doubt.
3:74: 74- God Almighty says: He chooses for His mercy meaning His prophethood whoever He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.
3:75: 75- The Almighty said: And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will return it to you The verse was revealed about the Jews. God Almighty informed us that among them are trustworthiness and treachery. The qintar is a large amount of money, and the dinar is a small amount of money. He says: Among them are those who will return the trust even if it is large, and among them are those who will not return it even if it is small. Muqatil said: And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will return it to you They are the believers of the People of the Scripture, such as Abdullah bin Salam and his companions. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will not return it to you meaning: the infidel Jews, such as Ka`b bin Al-Ashraf and his companions. Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s saying: And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will return it to you meaning: Abdullah bin Salam. A man entrusted him with one thousand two hundred ounces of gold and he returned it to him. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will not return it to you meaning: Phinehas bin Azura, he entrusted him with A man from Quraysh gave him a dinar and betrayed him. His saying, He returns it to you. Abu Amr, Abu Bakr, and Hamza read yu’duhu and la yu’duhu and naslah and nu’tuhu and nawlah with the ha’ silent. Abu Ja’far, Qalun, and Ya’qub read it with the ikhtilas with a kasra, and the rest with the ishba’ with a kasra. Whoever sukun the ha’ said that it was placed in the place of the jazm, which is the missing ya’. Whoever ikhtilas was satisfied with the kasra instead of the ya’, and whoever ashba’ is based on the original, because the original in the ha’ is the ishba’. Except as long as you are standing over it. Ibn Abbas said, Malhan, meaning he stands over it and demands it insistently. Ad-Dahhak said, Mawaziban, meaning he is persistent in it by demanding it. It was said, he meant I deposited it and then I took it back while you were standing over it and did not leave it, so he returned it to you. If you left it and delayed it, he denied it and did not return it. That means that is the permissibility and betrayal. Because they said, ‘We have no right to the unlettered ones’ meaning: there is a sin in the money of the Arab. And it is difficult, as God Almighty said: There is no blame upon the righteous. This is because the Jews said: The money of the Arabs is permissible for us, because they do not follow our religion and there is no sanctity for them in our book, and they considered it permissible to oppress those who differed from them in their religion. Al-Kalbi said: The Jews said that all the money was ours, and whatever was in the hands of the Arabs was ours. They only wronged us and usurped it, so we had no way of taking it from them. Al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil said: The Jews pledged allegiance to some Muslim men during the pre-Islamic period. When they converted to Islam, they demanded the rest of their money from them. They said: You have no right over us, and we have no right to judge you. You have abandoned your religion and the covenant between us and you has been broken. They claimed that they found that in their books, but God Almighty called them liars. He, the Almighty, said: And they tell lies about God while they know. Then He said in response to them:
3:76: 76- Yes meaning: it is not as they said, but there is a way for them. Then he began and said: Who fulfilled meaning: but who or in "his covenant" meaning: the covenant of God that He entrusted to him in the Torah of belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur'an and fulfilling the trust. It was said: the "ha in his covenant refers back to the one who fulfilled and feared disbelief, betrayal, and breaking the covenant, for God loves the righteous." Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Qubaysah bin Uqbah, I told Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are four things in whomever they are found, he is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has one characteristic of hypocrisy until he gives it up: If he is entrusted, he betrays; if he speaks, he lies; if he makes a covenant, he breaks it; and if he quarrels, he behaves indecently.”
3:77: 77- The Almighty said: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price. Ikrimah said: It was revealed regarding the heads of the Jews who concealed what God had covenanted with them in the Torah regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they changed it and wrote with their own hands something else and swore that it was from God so that they would not miss out on the food and bribes that were theirs from their followers. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abu Awana, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath, and is patient, to seize the wealth of a Muslim, will meet God on the Day of Resurrection while He is angry with him. So God, the Most High, revealed, confirming that: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price to the end of the verse. Then Al-Ash’ath bin Qais entered and said: What is Abu Abd Al-Rahman telling you? They said: So-and-so. He said: It was revealed in the following: I had a well in the land of my cousin, so I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He said: Bring your evidence or his oath. I said: Then he will swear by it, O Messenger of God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath, and is patient, and is a sinner, to seize the wealth of a Muslim, will meet God on the Day of Resurrection while He is angry with him. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad Al Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al Hajjaj told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Abu Al Ahwas, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Alqamah bin Wa’il bin Hajar, on the authority of his father, who said: “A man from Hadhramaut and a man from Kinda came to the Prophet, and the Hadrami said: O Messenger of God, this man has taken over my land that belonged to my father. The Kindi said: It is land in my possession that I cultivate, and he has no right to it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Hadrami: Do you have proof? He said: No. He said: Then his oath is yours. He said: O Messenger of God, the man is immoral and does not care about what he swears to. He said: You have nothing from him except that. So he went to swear for him, and when he turned away, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If he swears to eat his money unjustly, he will meet God while He is averse to it.” And Abdul Malik bin Himyar narrated it on the authority of Alqamah, and he said that he was Imru’ Al Qais bin Abis Al Kindi and his opponent was Rabi’ah bin Abdan. It was narrated that when he was about to swear an oath, this verse was revealed, but Imru’ al-Qais refused to swear, and acknowledged his right to his opponent and handed it over to him. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Mus’ab informed us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Ka’b, on the authority of his brother Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever usurps the right of a Muslim by swearing an oath, God will forbid him Paradise and make Hell obligatory for him. They said: Even if it is something insignificant, O Messenger of God? He said: Even if it is a twig of arak. He said it three times. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Amr bin Muhammad told us, Hisham bin Muhammad told us, Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, Ibrahim bin Abdul Rahman told us, Abdullah bin Abi Awfa told us that a man displayed a commodity in the market and swore by God that he had been given something for it that he had not been given, so that he could make a Muslim fall for it. Then the verse was revealed, Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price. God the Almighty says: Indeed, those who exchange meaning they exchange the covenant of God and their false oaths for a small price” meaning: a small thing of the worldly debris they have no portion in the Hereafter” and its pleasures nor will God speak to them with words that will benefit them and please them. It was said that it means anger, as a man says: I will not speak to so-and-so if he is angry with him nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection meaning: He will not have mercy on them, nor will He treat them well, nor will He grant them goodness nor will He purify them meaning: He will not praise them with kindness nor purify them from sins and for them is a painful punishment. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad Al Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al Jaloudi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ali bin Mudrik, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Kharsha bin Al Har, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There are three whom God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it three times. Abu Dharr said: They have failed and lost. Who are they, O Messenger of God? He said: The one who lets his garment trail, the one who shows off, and the one who sells his goods with false oaths. In another narration: The one who lets his garment trail. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, I said, Asid Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Alawi, I said, Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Hamdawayh al-Marwazi, I said, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There are three whom God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it three times. Abu Dharr said: “They have failed and lost. Who are they, O Messenger of God?” He said: The one who lets his garment hang down, the one who shows off, and the one who sells his goods by swearing falsely. In another narration: The one who lets his garment hang down. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, I said, Asid Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Alawi, I said, Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Hamdawayh al-Marwazi, I said, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “There are three whom God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: a man who swears an oath regarding the property of a Muslim and seizes it, A man who swears a false oath after the afternoon prayer that he was given more for his goods than he was given, and he is lying. A man who withholds the surplus of his money, then God Almighty says: Today I withhold from you the surplus of what your hands have not earned.
3:78: 78- The Almighty said: And indeed, among them is a party meaning: from the People of the Book, a party, i.e. a group, and they are Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf, Malik bin Al-Saif, Huyayy bin Akhtab, Abu Yasir, and Shu'bah bin Umar the poet, distorting the Book with their tongues meaning: they bend their tongues by distorting and changing it - and that is what they changed from the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse of stoning and other than that, it is said: If his tongue was like this, i.e. he changed it you would think it meaning: you would think / what they distorted from the Book, which God Almighty revealed, and it is not from the Book, and they say, It is from God and it is not from God, and they say a lie about God intentionally, while they know, that they are liars, and Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The verse was revealed about the Jews and Christians together, and that is because they distorted the Torah and the Gospel and added to the Book of God what is not from it.
3:79: 79- The Almighty said: It is not for a human being that God should give him the Scripture the Gospel. Muqatil and Ad-Dahhak said: It is not for a human being, meaning Jesus, peace be upon him. This is because the Christians of Najran used to say that Jesus had ordered them to take him as a god, so the Almighty said: It is not for a human being, meaning Jesus, that God should give him the Scripture the Gospel. Ibn Abbas and Ata’ said: It is not for a human being meaning Muhammad that God should give him the Book meaning the Qur’an. This is because Abu Rafi’ al-Qurazi from the Jews and the chief from the Christians of Najran said: O Muhammad, do you want us to worship you and take you as a Lord? He said: God forbid that we should command anyone other than God to worship Him. God did not command me to do that, nor did He command me to do that. So God the Most High revealed this verse: It is not for a human being meaning it is not appropriate for a human being, like His statement: It is not for us to speak of this Surat An-Nur, verse 16, meaning it is not appropriate for us. Human beings are all of the children of Adam, there is no singular form for them, like the people and the army, and it is used in place of the singular and plural, that God should give him the Book and wisdom meaning understanding and knowledge, and it was said: the implementation of the wisdom from God the Almighty, and prophethood meaning the high status of the prophets / “Then he will say to the people, ‘Be servants to me instead of God. But be’ meaning: but he says, ‘Be,’ ‘of the Lord.’” They differed about it. Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Al-Hassan said: Be jurists and scholars. Qatada said: Wise and scholars. Saeed bin Jubair said: The scholar is the one who acts according to his knowledge. And on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Jurist teachers. It was said: The Rabbani is the one who educates people with the small things of knowledge before the big things. Ata’ said: Scholars are wise and sincere advisers to God in His creation. Abu Ubaidah said: I heard a knowledgeable man say: The Rabbani is the one who knows what is permissible and what is forbidden, what is good and what is forbidden, the one who knows the report of the nation, what was and what will be. It was said: The Rabbani are above the scholars, and the scholars are the scholars, and the Rabbani are those who combine knowledge with insight into the politics of people. Al-Mu'arraj said: Be rabbis who worship your Lord, from lordship. Originally it was my Lord, then the alif was added for emphasis, then the nun was added for the sukoon of the alif, as it was said: Sana'ani and Bahrani. Al-Mubarrad said: They are the masters of knowledge, and they were called this because they nurture knowledge, and they carry it out and nurture the learners in the small sciences before the big ones, and whoever undertakes to fix something and complete it has nurtured it, and one of them is: rabban (as they said: rabban), and thirsty, and satiated, and naked, then the relative ya was added to it, as they said: lahyani and raqbani. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: He is the one whose knowledge is increased by his actions. Muhammad bin al-Hanafiyyah said when Ibn Abbas died: Today the master of this nation died. By what you were meaning: by what you are, like the Almighty’s saying: Whoever was in the cradle a child Surat Maryam, verse 29, meaning: whoever is in the cradle You know the Book Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read ya’lamun with emphasis from teaching, and the others read ya’lamun with emphasis from knowledge, like His saying: By what you were studying meaning: you read.
3:80: 80-His saying: And He does not command you, Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza and Yaqub read with the accusative of the ra' in apposition to his saying: Then he says, so it is returned to the people, meaning: And He does not command that people, and it was said: Ali implied that, meaning: And that that people does not command you, and the rest read with the nominative as a resumption, meaning: And God does not command you, and Ibn Jurayj and a group said: And Muhammad does not command you, that you take the angels and the prophets as lords like the action of the Quraysh and the Sabians when they swore: The angels are the daughters of God, and the Jews and Christians when they said about the Messiah and Ezra what they said, Does He command you to disbelieve after you are Muslims? He said it in a way of astonishment and denial, meaning: He does not say this.
3:81: 81- The Almighty said: "And when God took a covenant from the prophets, 'What I have given you of the Book and wisdom.' Hamza read when" with the necessary kasra, and the others read it with the fatha. Whoever breaks the lam, it is the lam of addition that entered upon what, and its meaning is that which he wants for what I have given you, that is: He took the covenant from the prophets for what He gave them of the Book and wisdom, meaning that they are the people of the laws. Whoever opens the lam, its meaning is: for what I have given you, in the sense of report. It was said: in the sense of reward, that is: if I give you and whatever I give you. The answer to the reward is His statement: "You will believe." His saying: When I gave you Nafi’ and the people of Medina read we gave you as an expression of glorification, just as he said: And We gave David the Psalms (An-Nisa’: 163) And We gave him judgment when he was a boy (Surat Maryam 19:12). The others read with a ta’ to match the script, and because of his saying: And I am with you. They differed about the meaning of this verse: Some people went to the fact that God Almighty took a covenant from the prophets in particular that they would convey the Book of God and His messages to His servants, and that they would believe in each other, and He took a covenant from every prophet to believe in the prophets who would come after him, and to support him if he reached him, and if he did not reach him, to command his people to support him if they reached him, so He took the covenant from Moses to believe in Jesus, and from Jesus to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. (And others said: Because God took the covenant from them in the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace), and on this they differed: Some of them said: He only took the covenant from the People of the Book from whom the prophets were sent, and this is the saying of Mujahid and Al-Rabi’. Do you not see his saying: Then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to the People of the Book and not to the prophets, as indicated by the reading of Abdullah bin Mas’ud and Ubayy bin Ka’b: And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture, and as for the well-known reading: And when God took the covenant of the prophets, he meant: God took the covenant of the prophets that they take the covenant from their nations to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to believe in him and support him, if they catch up with him. Some of them said: He meant that God took a covenant from the prophets and all their nations in the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he was satisfied with mentioning the prophets because the covenant with the one being followed is a covenant with the followers, and this is the meaning of what Ibn Abbas said. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: God did not send a prophet, Adam and those after him, except that He took a covenant from him in the matter of Muhammad, and He took a covenant from his people to believe in him, and if he was sent while they were alive, they would support him. His saying: Then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that you may believe in him and support him, God Almighty says to the prophets when He extracted the offspring from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, and the prophets among them were like lamps and lamps, and He took a covenant from them regarding the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, He said: Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourselves My covenant, meaning: have you accepted upon yourselves My covenant, and the covenant is the heavy covenant, “They said: We have acknowledged,” God Almighty said: Then bear witness, meaning: bear witness you against yourselves and against your followers, and I am with you among the witnesses, over you and over them, and Ibn Abbas said: bear witness, meaning: know, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: God Almighty said to the angels: bear witness against them, as a metaphor for something not mentioned.
3:82: 82- But whoever turns away after that, the acknowledgment, then those are the wicked, that is, the disobedient ones who have left the faith.
3:83: 83- The Almighty said: Do they seek other than the religion of God? That is because "the People of the Book differed and each one claimed that he followed the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, and they disputed before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Both groups are innocent of the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, so they became angry and said: We are not satisfied with your judgment and we do not accept your religion, so God, the Almighty, revealed: "Do they seek other than the religion of God? Abu Ja`far, the people of Basra, and Hafs from Asim read Yabghun with the letter ya" because of the Almighty's saying: "And those are the wicked. The others read with the letter ta" because of the Almighty's saying: "When I gave you, and to Him submitted, whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly," so obedience means submission and following with ease, and unwillingness means what is difficult and with refusal from the soul. They differed regarding his statement, willingly or unwillingly. Al-Hasan said: The people of the heavens submitted willingly, and those on the earth submitted, some of them willingly and some of them unwillingly, for fear of the sword and captivity. Mujahid said: The believer willingly, and the disbeliever unwillingly, as evidenced by: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and so do their shadows in the mornings and the evenings. (al-Ra’d 13:15). It was said: This is the Day of the Covenant when He said to them: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. (al-A’raf 7:172). Some of them said: Willingly, and some of them: Unwillingly. Qatada said: The believer submitted willingly, so it benefited him, while the disbeliever submitted unwillingly at the time of battle, so it did not benefit him. God Almighty said: So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. (Ghafir 40:85). Al-Sha’bi said: It is their seeking refuge in Him when they were forced, as God Almighty said: And when they embark on a ship, they supplicate God, devoting their religion to Him alone. (al-Ankabut 29:172) -65). Al-Kalbi said: Willingly, he who was born into Islam, and unwillingly, he who was forced to convert to Islam, from among those who were taken captive and brought in chains, “and to Him they will return. Hafs read with a ya’ from Asim and Ya’qub, just as he read yabghūn with a ya’, and the rest read with a ta’ in both of them, except for Abu Amr, who read yabghūn with a ya’ and tarj’ūn with a ta’, and he said: Because the first is specific and the second is general, because the return of all creation is to God Almighty.
3:84: 84- The Almighty said: “Say, ‘We believe in God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.’” He mentioned the religions and sects and the confusion of people in them, then he ordered the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say, We believe in God, the verse.
3:85: 85- His saying: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him, was revealed about twelve men who apostatized from Islam and left Medina and came to Mecca as infidels, among them Al-Harith bin Suwaid Al-Nasari, so it was revealed about them: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.
3:86: 86-How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief? Its wording is a question and its meaning is denial, i.e. He does not guide everyone. The meaning before it is: How can God guide them in the Hereafter to Paradise and reward? "And they testified that the Messenger is true and clear proofs came to them. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people."
3:87: 87- Their recompense is that upon them is the curse of God and the angels and the people, all together.
3:88: 88- "They will abide therein eternally. The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved." This is because when Al-Harith bin Suwaid joined the infidels, he regretted it, so he sent to his al-Nas 114:Ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Is there any repentance for me? So they did that, and God Almighty revealed:
3:89: 89- Except for those who repent after that and reform, for indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, for what he had done, so a man from his people brought it to him and read it to him, so Al-Harith said: By God, I know that you are truthful, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more truthful than you, and God Almighty is the most truthful of the three, so Al-Harith returned to Medina and converted to Islam, and his conversion was good.
3:90: 90- The Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief. Qatada and Al-Hasan said: It was revealed about the Jews who disbelieved in Jesus, peace be upon him, and the Gospel after their belief in their prophets, then they increased in disbelief by their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It was revealed about the Jews and Christians who disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they saw him after they acknowledged that God was their Creator. Then they increased in disbelief, meaning: they persisted in their disbelief until they perished because of it. Al-Hasan said: They increased in disbelief every time a verse was revealed, they disbelieved in it, so they increased in disbelief. It was also said: They increased in disbelief by saying: We are waiting for Muhammad to be struck by a calamity. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about the eleven companions of Al-Harith bin Suwaid. When Al-Harith returned to Islam, they remained in disbelief in Mecca and said: We will remain in disbelief as long as we wish, and when we want to return, what was revealed about Al-Harith will be revealed about us. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca, whoever among them entered Islam, his repentance was accepted, and it was revealed about whoever among them died as disbelievers.
3:91: 91- Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers the verse. If it is said: God has promised to accept the repentance of whoever repents, then what is the meaning of His saying: Their repentance will never be accepted, and it is those who are astray? It is said: Their repentance will not be accepted if they return in the state of witnessing, as He said: And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, ‘Indeed, I have repented now’ Surah An-Nisa, verse 18. It was said: This is about the companions of Al-Harith bin Suwaid, when they refrained from Islam and said: We will wait for Muhammad, and if time helps him, we will return to his religion. But that will not be accepted from them because they are waiting and not certain, so those are the ones who are astray. The Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers - never will it be accepted from one of them an amount filling the earth, meaning: an amount that would fill the earth from east to west. Gold is in the accusative case as an explanation, like their saying: twenty dirhams. And if he ransomed himself with it, it was said that its meaning is if he ransomed himself with it, and the waw is an additional insertion. Those will have a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers. Abdul Wahid bin Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Ghundar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Imran, who said: I heard Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God will say to the one who will be least punished in Hell on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:If you had everything on earth, would you ransom yourself with it? He will say: Yes. He will say: I wanted something easier than that from you while you were in the loins of Adam, that you would not associate anything with Me, but you refused except to associate anything with Me.”
3:92: 92- The Almighty’s saying: You will never attain righteousness means: Paradise. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, and Mujahid. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Piety. It was said: Obedience. It was said: Goodness. Al-Hasan said: That you be righteous. Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, I told Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri, I told Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi, Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Be truthful, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to tell the truth and strives for truthfulness until he is recorded with God as truthful. Beware of lying, for lying leads to immorality, and immorality leads to Hellfire. A man continues to tell lies and strives for lies until he is recorded with God as a liar.” The Almighty says: Until you spend from what you love meaning: from the most beloved of your wealth to you. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: What is meant by this is paying zakat. Mujahid and Al-Kalbi said: This verse was abrogated by the verse on zakat. Al-Hasan said: Every expenditure by which a Muslim seeks the pleasure of God, even fruit, he attains this righteousness. Ata’ said: You will not attain righteousness, meaning: the honor of religion and piety, until you give charity while you are healthy and miserly. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, I told Zahir ibn Ahmad, I told Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, I told Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ishaq ibn `Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah al-Ansari was the wealthiest of the Ansar in Madinah, and the most beloved of his wealth to him was Bayra`, which was facing the mosque, and the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) used to enter it and drink from its pure water. Anas said: When this verse was revealed: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love, Abu Talhah went to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and said: “O Messenger of God, God the Most High says in His Book: ‘You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love,’ and the most beloved of my wealth to me is Bayra`, and it is a charity for God, and I hope for its reward and its storage with God. So spend it, O Messenger of God, wherever you wish.” The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: Good, good, that is profitable wealth. Or he said: That is profitable wealth, and I have heard what you said about it, and I think that you should give it to your relatives. Abu Talhah said: I will do it, O Messenger of God. So Abu Talhah divided it among…” His relatives and cousins. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash’ari to buy him a slave girl from the captives of Jalula on the day it was conquered. He called for her and she pleased him, so he said: God Almighty says: You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. So Umar freed her. On the authority of Hamza bin Abdullah bin Omar, he said: This verse came to the mind of Abdullah bin Omar: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. Ibn Omar said: So I remembered what God Almighty had given me, and nothing was more amazing to me than so-and-so, who is free for the sake of God Almighty. He said: If it were not for the fact that I would not go back on something that I had given to God, I would have married her. And whatever you spend, God is Knowing of it, meaning: He knows it and will reward for it.
3:93: 93- The Almighty said: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed. The reason for the revelation of this verse: "The Jews said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you claim that you are following the religion of Abraham? Abraham did not eat camel meat or milk, but you eat it, so you are not following his religion. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That was lawful to Abraham, peace be upon him. They said: Everything that we forbid today was forbidden to Noah and Abraham until it reached us. So God Almighty revealed this verse: 'All food was lawful to the Children of Israel.'" He meant: except for dead meat and blood, which were never lawful. Except what Israel had forbidden to himself - that is, Jacob, peace be upon him - before the Torah was revealed - meaning: The matter is not as they said about the prohibition of camel meat and milk for Abraham, rather everything was permissible for him and for the children of Israel, and Israel only forbade it to himself before the Torah was revealed - meaning: Its prohibition is not in the Torah. They differed about the food that Jacob forbade himself and its reason. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ata’, Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: The food was camel meat and milk. It was narrated that Jacob fell seriously ill and his illness lasted a long time, so he vowed that if God cured him of his illness, he would forbid himself the food and drink he loved most. The food he loved most was camel meat and the drink he loved most was camel milk, so he forbade them. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak said: They are the veins. The reason for this was that he complained of sciatica, which was the origin of his pain, as narrated by Juwaybir and Muqatil on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: Jacob had vowed that if God gave him twelve sons and he came to Jerusalem in good health, he would slaughter the last of them. An angel from the angels met him and said: O Jacob, you are a strong man, would you like to wrestle? So he wrestled with them, but neither of them defeated the other. The angel nudged him and caused him sciatica. Then he said to him: If I wanted to wrestle with you, I would have done so, but I nudged you this nudge because you had vowed that if you came to Jerusalem in good health, you would slaughter the last of your sons. So God made for you a way out of this by nudging him. When Jacob presented it, he wanted to slaughter his son and forgot what the angel had said. The angel came to him and said: I only nudged you to get out, and you have fulfilled your vow, so you have no way to your son. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Al-Suddi said: Jacob came from Harran intending to go to Jerusalem when he fled from his brother Esau. He was a strong, impetuous man. A king met him and Jacob thought he was a thief. He tried to defeat him, but the king poked Jacob’s thigh and then ascended to heaven while Jacob, peace be upon him, was looking at him. He suffered from sciatica and suffered from that and was severely afflicted. He could not sleep at night because of the pain and would spend the night with a sore throat. Jacob swore that if God healed him, he would not eat any sore throat or food containing sore throat, so he forbade himself from it. After that, his sons would follow the paths and extract them from the meat. Juwaybir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When Jacob was afflicted with sciatica, the doctors prescribed for him to avoid camel meat, so Jacob forbade it for himself. Al-Hasan achieved: Israel forbade himself from eating the meat of camels in worship of God Almighty. So he asked his Lord to permit him to do so, and God forbade it to his son. Then they differed about the status of this food that was forbidden to the Children of Israel after the revelation of the Torah. Al-Suddi said: God forbade them in the Torah what they had forbidden before its revelation. Atiyah said: It was only forbidden to them because of the prohibition of Israel, for he had said: If God spares me, no child of mine will eat it. It was not forbidden to them in the Torah. Al-Kalbi said: God did not forbid it to them in the Torah, but it was only forbidden to them after the Torah because of their injustice, as God Almighty said: But because of the injustice of those who were Jews, We prohibited to them [certain] good things which had been lawful to them Surat An-Nisa, verse 160. God Almighty said: And We forbade to those who were Jews all things having claws, until He said: That is how We recompensed them for their transgression, and indeed, We are truthful Surat An-Na’am, verse (146. When the Children of Israel committed a great sin, God forbade them good food or poured upon them a punishment, which is death. Ad-Dahhak said: None of that was forbidden to them, nor did God forbid it in the Torah. Rather, they forbade it to themselves in imitation of their father, then they attributed its prohibition to God, so God Almighty denied them, and said: Say, O Muhammad, Then bring the Torah and recite it, until it becomes clear that it is as you said, if you are truthful, but they did not bring it. So God Almighty said:
3:94: :94- But whoever invents a lie against God after that - it is those who are the wrongdoers.
3:95: 95- "Say, 'God has spoken the truth. So follow the religion of Abraham, the upright, and he was not of the polytheists.'" He only called them to follow the religion of Abraham because in following the religion of Abraham, following him, may God bless him and grant him peace..
3:96: God Almighty said: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed. The reason for the revelation of this verse is that the Jews said to the Muslims: Jerusalem is our qibla, and it is better than the Kaaba and older and it is the place of migration of the prophets. The Muslims said: Rather, the Kaaba is better, so God Almighty revealed: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed and a guidance for the worlds. “In it are clear signs, the standing place of Abraham. And whoever enters it shall be safe.” None of these virtues are for the Holy House. Scholars differed regarding the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah. Some of them said: It is the first House to appear on the surface of the water after the creation of the heavens and the earth. God created it two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam on the water, then the earth spread out from beneath it. This is the statement of Abdullah bin Omar, Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Suddi. Some of them said: It is the first house built on earth. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein: God Almighty placed a house under the display, which is the Frequented House, and He ordered the angels to circumambulate it. Then He ordered the angels who are the inhabitants of the earth to build a house on the earth in its likeness and capacity, so they built it and its name is Ad-Dharah. He ordered those on earth to circumambulate it as the people of heaven circumambulate the Frequented House. It was narrated that the angels built it two thousand years before the creation of the people, and they used to perform Hajj to it. When Adam performed Hajj, the angels said: “Your Hajj is good, O Adam. We performed Hajj to this House a thousand years before you.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: He meant that it was the first. On the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, Ad-Dahhak said: The first house in which blessings were placed. It was also said: The first house established for people to make Hajj to. It was also said: The first house made a Qiblah for people. Al-Hasan and Al-Kalbi said: Its meaning is: The first mosque and place of worship established for people to worship God in, as God Almighty said: In houses which God has permitted to be raised meaning the mosques. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, Musa bin Ismail told us, Abdul Wahid told us, Al-A’mash told us, Ibrahim bin Yazid Al-Taimi told us, on the authority of his father, he said, I heard Abu Dharr say: “I said, O Messenger of God, which mosque was established on earth first? He said: The Sacred Mosque. I said, Then which? He said: Al-Aqsa Mosque. I said: How much time was there between them? He said: Forty years, then wherever the prayer catches you after a separation, the virtue is in it.” The Almighty said: For the one at Bakkah. A group said: It is Mecca itself, and this is the saying of Ad-Dahhak. The Arabs alternate between the Ba and the Meem, so they say: Sabd Ra’shu and Samadhu, and Daraba Lazib and Lazim. The others said: Bakkah is the location of the House and Mecca is the name of the entire country. It was said: Bakkah is the location of the House and the sanctuary. It was called Bakkah because people weep in it, that is, they crowd together, weeping over one another, praying in front of one another, and passing in front of one another. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr said that it was called Mecca because it breaks the necks of tyrants, meaning it crushes them. No tyrant will attempt to build a wall against it except that God will break it. As for Mecca, it was named thus because of its scarcity of water, from the saying of the Arabs: The young camel sucks the udder of its mother and absorbs all the milk in it. It is called Umm Rahm because mercy descends upon it. Blessed is in the accusative case, meaning: blessed. And guidance for the worlds because it is the direction of prayer of the believers. In it are clear signs. Ibn Abbas read clear signs in the singular, and he meant the station of Abraham alone. The others read clear signs in the plural, and he mentioned among them the station of Abraham which is the stone on which Abraham stood, and the traces of his feet were in it but disappeared from the abundance of wiping with the hands. Among those signs are: the Black Stone, Al-Hateem, Zamzam and all the sacred sites. It was said: the station of Abraham is the entire sanctuary. Among the signs in the house is that birds fly but do not rise above it, and that if a bird of prey intends to hunt, when the hunted animal enters the sanctuary it refrains from it, and that it is a country to which the prophets, messengers, saints and righteous people came, and that obedience and charity in it are multiplied by a hundred thousand. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan bin Ahmad Al-Mukhaldi, I told Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Sarraj, I told Abu Musab Ahmad bin Abi Bakr Al-Zuhri, I told Malik bin Anas, on the authority of Zaid bin Rabah and Ubaid God bin Abi Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Aghar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque except the Sacred Mosque. God the Almighty said: And whoever enters it shall be safe from being argued about in it, and that is by the supplication of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he said: My Lord, make this a secure beginning. The Arabs in the pre-Islamic period used to kill each other and raid each other. Whoever enters the sanctuary is safe from being killed or raided, and this is what is meant by the verse according to Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and most of the commentators. God the Almighty said: Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary while people are snatched away all around them? Surat Al-Ankaboon, verse 67. It was said that what is meant by it is that whoever enters it in the year of the Umrah of Compensation with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is safe, as God the Almighty said: You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security. Surat Al-Fath, verse 27. It was said that it is a report with the meaning of a command, the meaning of which is: And whoever enters it, make him safe, as God the Almighty said: There shall be no obscenity, no wickedness, and no disputing during Hajj. Surat Al-Baqarah, 197, meaning: Do not engage in obscenity or commit wickedness, to the extent that some of the scholars have said that whoever is required to be killed as retaliation or a prescribed punishment and takes refuge in the sanctuary, then the punishment is not to be exacted from him there. But he does not feed nor does he buy and sell until he leaves it, so he is killed. Ibn Abbas said this, and Abu Hanifa said the same. Some people went to the view that the killing required by the Sharia is fulfilled in it, but if he commits the crime in the sanctuary, his punishment is fulfilled in it by spending. It was said: Its meaning is that whoever enters it, honoring it and drawing closer to God Almighty, will be safe from punishment on the Day of Resurrection. God Almighty said
3:97: 97- And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, for those who can afford the expenses. That is, Hajj to the House is an obligation that mankind owes to God. Abu Ja`far, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read Hajj to the House with a kasra on the ha’ in this letter in particular, while the others read it with a fatha on the ha’. This is the language of the people of the Hijaz, and they are two eloquent languages with the same meaning. Hajj is one of the pillars of Islam. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Musa told us, Hanzala bin Abi Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah bin Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Islam is built on five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establishing prayer, paying zakat, Hajj, and fasting Ramadan.” The scholars said: Hajj is obligatory according to five conditions: Islam, sanity, puberty, freedom, and ability. It is not obligatory for a non-believer or an insane person, and if they perform Hajj by themselves, it is not valid because the non-believer is not among the people of closeness and there is no ruling for the action of the insane person. It is not obligatory for a boy or a slave, and if a boy of sound mind or a slave whose circumcision is valid performs Hajj voluntarily, the obligation of Islam is not dropped from them. If a boy reaches puberty or a slave is freed after performing Hajj and the conditions of the obligation of Hajj are met for him, he must perform Hajj again, and it is not obligatory for someone who is not able, because of the Almighty’s saying: Whoever can afford it 2:177. However, if he takes the trouble to perform Hajj, the obligation of Islam is dropped from him. And the ability is of two types, one of them is that he is able by himself, and the other is that he is able with his own money. As for the ability by himself, it is that he is able by himself to go and finds provisions and a mount. Abdul Wahid bin Muhammad Al-Kisa’i Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Saeed bin Salim told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibad bin Ja’far, who said: So we returned to Abdullah bin Omar and I heard him say: “A man asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What is the Hajj? He said: The disheveled one who has spitted. Then another man stood up and said: O Messenger of God, which Hajj is best? He said: The one who is tired and has a cold sweat. Then another man stood up and said: O Messenger of God, what is the way? He said: Provisions and a mount.” The details are: that he finds a suitable mount for his situation and finds provisions for going and returning, in addition to the expenses of his family and those whose expenses and clothing he is obligated to pay for his going and returning, and a debt that he owes, and finds company to go out at a time when it is customary for the people of a town to go out at that time. If they go out before that or see the exit at a time when they do not pray unless they travel more than one stage each day, they are not obligated to go out at that time. It is stipulated that the road be safe. If there is fear of a Muslim or infidel enemy or a watchman seeking something, it is not obligatory for him. It is stipulated that the inhabited houses be inhabited and he can find provisions and water in them. If it is a time of drought and its people have dispersed or its waters have dried up, then it is not obligatory for him even if he does not find a mount but he is able to walk, or he does not find provisions but he can earn money on the road, then Hajj is not obligatory for him, and it is recommended if he does so, and Malik promised that it is obligatory for him. As for the ability to perform Hajj by someone else, it is: that the man is unable to do so himself, whether for a period of time or has an illness that is not expected to go away, but he has money that enables him to hire someone to perform Hajj on his behalf, he must hire someone, or he does not have money but his son or a stranger offers him obedience to perform Hajj on his behalf, he must order him if he trusts his truthfulness, because the obligation of Hajj is related to ability, and it is said in custom: So-and-so is able to build a house even if he does not do it himself, but rather he does it with his money or with his helpers. According to Abu Hanifa, Hajj is not obligatory if one performs an act of obedience, and according to Malik, it is not obligatory for someone who has been bitten by a piece of money. An argument for those who make it obligatory is what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Abbas, that he said: Al-Fadl ibn `Abbas was riding behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a woman from Khatham came to him to ask him for a fatwa. Al-Fadl kept looking at her and she kept looking at him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept turning Al-Fadl’s face the other way, and she said: O Messenger of God, God’s obligation upon His servants in Hajj has come upon my father, an old man who cannot stay on his mount. Should I perform Hajj on his behalf? He said: Yes. God Almighty says: And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is independent of the worlds. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Ata’ said: He denied the obligation of Hajj. Mujahid said: He who disbelieves in God and the Last Day. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It was revealed about the Jews when they said: Hajj to Mecca is not obligatory. Al-Suddi said: He who finds what he can perform Hajj with but does not perform Hajj until he dies, he has disbelieved in it. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Shuraihi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Kalamati told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Omar told us, Sahl bin Ammar told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Sabit, on the authority of Abu Umamah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is not prevented by an apparent need, or a deterrent illness, or an unjust ruler, and does not perform Hajj, then let him die as a Jew if he wishes, or as a Christian if he wishes.
3:98: 98- The Almighty said: Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while God is Witness over what you do?’
3:99: 99- Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of God those who believe, seeking it crookedly?’ That is, why do you turn away from the religion of God those who believe, seeking it crookedly. Abu Ubaidah said: Crookedness with a kasra is in religion, speech, and action, and crookedness with a fatha is in the wall, and every standing person, while you are witnesses, and God is not unaware of what you do. That it is written in the Torah is a description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that the religion of God that He does not accept other than it is Islam.
3:100: 100- O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, Zaid bin Aslam said: "Shas bin Qais the Jew - who was an old man of great disbelief and severe criticism of the Muslims - passed by a group of Aws and Khazraj in a gathering where they were talking, and he was angered by what he saw of their harmony and reconciliation between them in Islam after the enmity that had existed between them in the pre-Islamic era. He said: The leaders of Banu Qaylah have gathered in this country. By God, we have no place with them when they gather there. So he ordered a young man from the Jews who was with him and said: Go to them and sit with them. Then he reminded them of the day of Bu'ath and what had happened before it, and recited to them some of the poems they had recited about it. Bu'ath was a day when Aws fought with Khazraj, and the victory was for Aws over Khazraj. So he did so and spoke, and the people spoke at that time and disputed and boasted until two men from the two tribes jumped on the camel, Aws bin A Copt, one of Banu Haritha of the Aws, and Jabbar bin Sakhr, one of Banu Salamah of the Khazraj, argued with each other, then one of them said to the other: If you wish, by God, I will return her now as a young camel. Both groups became angry and said: We have already made the weapon, the weapon is your appointment is the apparent place, and she is free. So they went out to her, and the Aws and Khazraj joined together in their claim that they had in the pre-Islamic era. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he went out to them with the Muhajireen who were with him until he came to them. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O group of Muslims, is it the claim of the pre-Islamic era while I am among you after God has honored you with Islam, and cut off the matter of the pre-Islamic era from you and united you? Will you return to what you were upon as disbelievers? God, God. The people realized that it was an instigation from Satan and a plot from their enemy, so they threw down their weapons from their hands and cried and embraced each other, then they left with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, listening and obeying. Then God Almighty revealed this verse about them. They will turn you back into disbelievers after your belief. Jabir said: I have never seen a day uglier at the beginning and better at the end than that day. Then God Almighty said in amazement.
3:101: 101- And how can you disbelieve? meaning: Why do you disbelieve? And the verses of God are recited to you, the Qur'an, and among you is His Messenger, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Qatada said: In this verse there are two clear signs: the Book of God and the Prophet of God. As for the Prophet of God, he has passed away, but as for the Book of God, He has kept it among you as a mercy and blessing from God. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Abbas Al-Hamidi told us. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us. Abu Al-Fadl Al-Hasan bin Ya’qub bin Yusuf Al-Adl told us. Ahmad Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab Al-Abdi told us. Abu Ja’far bin Auf told us. Abu Hayyan Yahya bin Saeed bin Hayyan [on the authority of Yazid bin Hayyan] said: I heard Zaid bin Arqam say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us as a preacher. He praised God and thanked Him, then he said: “As for what follows, O people, I am only a human being. The Messenger of my Lord will soon come to me and I will respond to him. I am leaving among you two weighty things. The first of them is the Book of God, in which is guidance and light. So hold fast to the Book of God and adhere to it.” He urged it and encouraged it. Then he said: And my family, and my family, and I remind you of God in my family. The Almighty says: And whoever holds fast to God meaning: he abstains from God and adheres to His religion and obedience, has certainly been guided to a straight path, a clear path. Ibn Jurayj said: And whoever holds fast to God meaning: he believes in God. The root of protection is prevention, so everyone who prevents something is a protector of it.
3:102: 102- The Almighty said: "O you who have believed, fear God as He should be feared." Muqatil bin Hayyan said: There was enmity and fighting between the Aws and the Khazraj in the pre-Islamic period until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina. He reconciled between them, and after that two men from among them boasted: Tha'laba bin Ghanam from the Aws and As'ad bin Zararah from the Khazraj. The Aws said: Among us is Khuzaymah bin Thabit, the possessor of the two testimonies, and among us is Hanzala, who was washed by the angels, and among us is Asim bin Thabit bin Aflah, the one who was protected from the anus, and among us is Sa'd bin Mu'adh, whose death shook the throne of the Most Merciful and whose judgment on Banu Qurayza was pleased with God. Al-Khazraji said: Four of us mastered the Qur’an: Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Mu’adh ibn Jabal, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Abu Zayd. Among us was Sa’d ibn Ubadah, the orator and leader of the Ansar. A conversation took place between them, and they became angry and recited poetry and boasted.
