Then the Aws and the Khazraj came with weapons, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them, and God Almighty revealed this verse: O you who have believed, fear God as He should be feared. Abdullah bin Masoud and Ibn Abbas said: It is to be obeyed and not disobeyed. Mujahid said: That you strive in the way of God as He should be striven for and do not let the blame of a blamer deter you in God’s cause, and that you stand up for God with justice even if it is against yourselves, your fathers, and your children. Anas said: A servant does not fear God as He should be feared until he restrains his tongue. The commentators said: When this verse was revealed, it was difficult for them, so they said: O Messenger of God, who can do this? Then God Almighty revealed: So fear God as much as you are able At-Taghabun 16, and this verse was abrogated. Muqatil said: There is nothing in Al Imran that was abrogated except this. And do not die except as Muslims, meaning: believers. It was said: sincere, entrusting your affairs to God Almighty. Al-Fudayl said: having good thoughts about God. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Bakr Al-Abdusi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Hamdun bin Khalid bin Yazid told us, Sulayman bin Saif told us, Wahb bin Jarir told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O people, fear God as He should be feared. If a drop of Zaqqum were to fall on the earth, it would make the livelihood of the people of this world miserable. So how about one whose food is that and who has no other food?”
3:103: 103- The Almighty said: And hold fast, all together, to the rope of God. The rope is the cause by which one reaches the goal, and faith is called a rope because it is a cause by which one reaches the elimination of fear. They differed about its meaning here. Ibn Abbas said: Its meaning is to hold fast to the religion of God. Ibn Masoud said: It is the group. He said: Stick to the group, for it is the rope of God that God has commanded. What you dislike in the group and obedience is better than what you like in division. Mujahid and Ata’ said: By the covenant of God. Qatada and As-Suddi said: It is the Qur’an. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Indeed, this Qur’an is the rope of God, and it is the clear light, and the beneficial healing, and protection for whoever holds fast to it, and salvation for whoever follows it. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: By the rope of God means by the command of God and His obedience, and do not be divided as the Jews and Christians were divided. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus’ab, on the authority of Malik ibn Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, God the Most High is pleased with three things for you, and is displeased with three things for you. He is pleased with you that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, that you hold fast to the rope of God all together, and that you advise those who God has appointed over you. He is displeased with you: gossip, wasting money, and asking too many questions.” God the Almighty said: And remember the favor of God upon you, when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together. Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Ibn Yasar, and other historians said: The Aws and Khazraj were brothers from the same father and mother, and enmity arose between them because of a murder. That enmity and war between them lasted for one hundred and twenty years until God the Almighty extinguished that with Islam and brought them together through His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The reason for their coming together was that Suwaid ibn al-Samit, a brother of Banu Amr ibn Awf, was a nobleman whom his people called al-Kamil because of his bravery and lineage. He came to Mecca as a pilgrim or a performer of Umrah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been sent and ordered to call people to Islam. Suwaid responded to him when he heard about him and called him to God the Almighty and to Islam. So Suwaid said to him: Perhaps what you have is like what I have. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: [And what do you have with you? He said: The magazine of Luqman, meaning: his wisdom. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Show it to me. So he showed it to him, and he said: This is good speech. I have better than this. The Qur’an was sent down to him as light and guidance. He recited the Qur’an to him and called him to Islam, but he did not [distance] from him and said: This is indeed a good statement. Then he returned to Medina, and it was not long before the Khazraj killed him before the day of Bu’ath, for his people would say: He was killed while he was a Muslim. Then Abu Al-Haysir Anas bin Rafi came, and with him a group of Banu Al-Ashhal, among them Iyas bin Muadh, seeking an alliance from Quraysh against a group of Khazraj. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of them, he came to them and sat with them, and said: Do you want something better than what you came for? They said: What is that? He said: I am the Messenger of God, and he sent me to the servants to call them not to associate anything with God, and the Book was revealed to me. Then he mentioned Islam to them and recited the Quran to them. Iyas bin Muadh, who was a young boy, said: What people are these? By God, they are better than what you came for. Abu Al-Haysir took a handful of sand from the plain and struck Iyas with it in the face and said: Leave me alone, for by God we came for something other than this. Iyas was silent and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up from them, and they returned to Medina. The Battle of Buath took place between the Aws and the Khazraj, and Iyas bin Muadh did not stay long before he died. When God the Almighty wanted to manifest His religion and glorify His Prophet, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out during the season in which he met the group of Ansar to introduce himself to the tribes of the Arabs, as he did every season. At Al-Aqaba, he met a group of Khazraj whom God wanted good for. They were six men: As`ad ibn Zararah, `Awf ibn Al-Harith, who is the son of `Afra, Rafi` ibn Malik Al-`Ajlan, Qutbah ibn `Amir ibn Hadidah, `Uqbah ibn `Amir ibn Nabi, and Jabir ibn `Abdullah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Who are you? They said: A group of Khazraj. He said: Are you from the clients of the Jews? They said: Yes. He said: Will you not sit down so that I may speak to you? They said: Yes. So they sat with him, and he called them to God the Almighty and presented Islam to them and recited the Qur’an to them. They said: And among what God did for them in Islam was that the Jews were with them in their country, and they were people of the Book and knowledge, and they were people of idols and polytheism, and if something happened to them they would say: A prophet is now being sent and his time has come, we will follow him and kill you with him as the people of Aad and Iram were killed. So when the Messenger of God spoke to those people and called them to God Almighty, some of them said to each other: O people, you know by God that he is the prophet that the Jews promised you, so do not let him get ahead of you to him. So they answered him and believed him and submitted and said: We have left our people and there is no people between them as much enmity and evil as between them, and God may unite them with you and we will go to them and call them to your cause, and if God unites them against you, then there is no man more honorable than you. Then they turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returning to their country, having believed in him, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they arrived in Medina, they mentioned the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them and called them to Islam, until it spread among them and there was no house of the Ansar except that there was mention of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the next year, twelve men from the Ansar arrived at the season, and they were: As`ad ibn Zararah, Awf and Mu`adh, the sons of `Afra, Rafi` ibn Malik ibn al-`Ajlan, Dhakwan ibn `Abd al-Qays, `Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Yazid ibn Tha`labah, Abbas ibn `Ubadah, `Uqbah ibn `Amir, Qutbah ibn `Amir, and these were Khazrajites, and Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan and `Uwaimir ibn Sa`idah were from the Aws. They met him at al-`Aqabah, which is the first al-`Aqabah, and they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the basis of the pledge of women, on the condition that they would not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, to the end of the verse. If you fulfilled it, then Paradise is for you, but if you committed any of that and were punished for it in this world, then it is As an expiation for him, and if he concealed it from you, then your matter is up to God. If He wills, He will punish you, and if He wills, He will forgive you. He said: And that was before war was imposed on them. He said: When the people left, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent with them Mus`ab bin `Umair bin Hashim bin `Abd Manaf, and ordered him to recite the Qur’an to them, teach them Islam, and instruct them in the religion. Mus`ab was called the reciter in Medina, and his residence was with As`ad bin Zurarah. Then As`ad bin Zurarah went out with Mus`ab and entered with him into one of the walls of Banu Thafar. They sat in the wall and some men who had converted to Islam gathered around them. Sa`d bin Mu`adh said to Asid bin Hudhair: Go to these two men who have come to our house to fool our weak ones and rebuke them, for As`ad bin Zurarah is my maternal cousin, and were it not for that, I would have sufficed you. Sa`d bin Mu`adh and Asid bin Hudhair were the masters of their people from Banu `Abd al-Ashhal, and they were polytheists. So Asid bin Hudhair took his spear and went to Mus`ab and As`ad while they were sitting in the wall. When As`ad bin Zurarah saw him, he said to Mus`ab: This is the master of his people who has come to you, so give him charity while they were sitting in the wall. When As`ad bin Zararah saw him, he said to Mus`ab: This is the master of his people who has come to you, so be truthful with God in dealing with him. Mus`ab said: If he sits down, I will talk to him. He said: So he stood over them, cursing each other, and said: What brought you to us to belittle our weak ones? Stay away if you have a need for yourselves. Mus`ab said to him: Or will you sit down and listen? If you are satisfied with a matter, I will accept it, and if you dislike it, I will refrain from what you dislike. He said: You have been fair. Then he planted his spear and sat down with them. He spoke to Mus`ab about Islam and recited the Qur’an to him. They said: By God, we knew the face of Islam before he spoke about it, in its radiance and ease. Then he said: How beautiful and wonderful are these words. What will you do if you want to enter this religion? They said to him: Wash yourself and purify your garments, then bear witness to the truth. Then pray two rak’ahs. So he stood up, washed himself, purified his garments, and bore witness to the truth. Then he stood up and bowed two rak’ahs. Then he said to them: There is a man behind me who, if he follows you, no one from his people will stay behind. I will send him to you now. He is Sa’d ibn Mu’adh. Then he took his spear and went to Sa’d and his people, who were sitting in their gathering. When Sa’d ibn Mu’adh saw him coming, he said: I swear by God that Asid has come to you with a face different from the one he used when he left you. When he stood at the gathering, Sa’d said to him: What did you do? He said: I spoke to the two men, and by God, I saw no harm in them, and I forbade them. They said: Do as you like. I was told that Banu Haritha went out to As`ad ibn Zararah to kill him, and that is because they knew that he was your maternal cousin, so that they could despise you. Sa`d stood up angrily and rushed to what Banu Haritha had mentioned to him. He took the spear, then said: By God, I do not see that you have done anything. When he saw them at ease, he knew that Asid only wanted to hear from them, so he stood over them, cursing them. Then he said to As`ad ibn Zararah: Were it not for the kinship between me and you, I would not have thrown this from me, attacking us in our house with what we dislike. As`ad said to Mus`ab: By God, the master of his people has come to you. If he follows you, none of them will oppose you. Mus`ab said to him: Or you will sit and listen. If you are satisfied with a matter and desire it, accept it, and if you dislike it, we will remove from you what you dislike. Sa`d said: You are fair. Then he planted the spear and sat down. He presented Islam to him and recited the Qur’an to him: They said: “By God, we knew the face of Islam before he spoke about it in its radiance and ease, then bear witness to the testimony of truth and then pray two rak’ahs. So he stood up, washed himself, purified his clothes, bore witness to the testimony of truth and bowed two rak’ahs, then took his spear and headed towards the club of his people with Asid bin Khudair. When his people saw him coming, they said: We swear by God that Sa’d has returned to you with a face other than the one with which he left you. So when he stood before them, he said: O sons of Abd al-Ashhal, how do you know my affair among you?” They said: Our master, the best of us in opinion, and the most righteous of us in leadership. He said: The speech of your men and women is forbidden to me until you believe in God and His Messenger. He said: There was not a man or woman in the house of Banu Abd al-Ashhal who did not become a Muslim, man or woman. As`ad ibn Zararah and Mus`ab returned to the house of As`ad ibn Zararah and stayed with him calling the people to Islam until there was not a house of the Ansar that did not have Muslim men and women in it, except for the house of Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, Khatmah and Wa`il. This was because Abu Qais ibn al-Aslat, the poet, was among them, and they listened to him and obeyed him, so he stopped them from Islam until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, and Badr, Uhud and the Trench took place. They said: Then Mus`ab bin `Umair returned to Mecca and with him went out from the Ansar from the Muslims seventy men with the pilgrims of their people from the polytheists until they arrived in Mecca and made an appointment with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-`Aqabah in the middle of the days of Tashreeq, which is the second pledge of Al-`Aqabah. Ka`b ibn Malik - who had witnessed that - said: When we finished the Hajj, and it was the night on which we had made an appointment with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and with us was Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram or Jabir, we informed him, and we used to conceal our affair from those of the polytheists who were with us from our people, so we spoke to him and said to him: O Abu Jabir, you are a master among our masters and a noble among our nobles, and we prefer you over what you are in, lest you be firewood for the fire tomorrow. And we invited him to Islam, so he became a Muslim, and we informed him of the appointment with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he witnessed with us the Aqaba, and he was a leader. So we spent that night with our people in our tents, until when a third of the night had passed, we went out to meet the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sneaking away like a quail, until we gathered in the valley at the Aqaba, and we were seventy men and with us were two of our women, Nusaybah bint Ka`b, Umm `Amara, one of the women of Banu Najjar, and Asma bint `Amr ibn `Adi, Umm Mani`, one of the women of Banu Salamah. So we gathered in the valley awaiting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God's peace and blessings be upon him, until he came to us with his uncle Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, who was at that time following the religion of his people, except that he wanted to attend to the matter of his nephew, and to provide him with security. As soon as we sat down, the first to speak was Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, and he said: O people of Khazraj - and the Arabs used to call this tribe of the Ansar Al-Khazraj, their Khazraj and their Aws - Muhammad, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, is from us as you know, and we have protected him from our people from those who are of the same opinion as us, and he is in glory from his people and protected in his country, and he has refused except to be cut off from you and join you. So if you see that you will fulfill what you called him to and protect him from those who opposed him, then you are with what you have borne of that, and if you see that you will surrender him and abandon him after he came out to you, then from now on leave him, for he is in glory and protection. He said: We said, “We have heard what you said. Speak, O Messenger of God, and take for yourself and for your Lord whatever you wish.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke and recited the Qur’an and called to God Almighty and encouraged Islam, then he said: I pledge allegiance to you on the condition that you protect me from what you protect yourselves, your women, and your children. He said: Al-Bara’ bin Ma’rur took his hand and said: By Him who sent you as a prophet with the truth, we will protect you from what we protect our sons from, so pledge allegiance to us, O Messenger of God, for we are people of war and people of the circle, we inherited it from our forefathers. Abu Al-Haitham bin Al-Tayhan objected to the statement - while Al-Bara was speaking to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - and said: O Messenger of God, between us and the people are bonds, meaning covenants, and I will sever them. Is it possible that if we do that and then God gives you victory, will you return to your people and leave us? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled and then said: Blood for blood, destruction for destruction. You are from me and I am from you. I fight those with whom I fight and I am safe for those with whom I am safe. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bring out to me from among you twelve leaders who will be responsible for their people, including them, as the disciples were responsible for Jesus, son of Mary. So bring out twelve leaders, nine from the Khazraj and three from the Aws. Asim bin Amr bin Qatada said: When the people gathered to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Al-Abbas bin Ubadah bin Nadlah the Christian said: O people of Khazraj, do you know why you are pledging allegiance to this man? You are pledging allegiance to him to fight the reds and the blacks. If you think that if your wealth is decimated by a calamity and your nobles are killed, then surrender him, then from now on, for by God, if you do so, it will be a disgrace in this world and the next. And if you think that you will fulfill what you called him to despite the loss of wealth and the killing of nobles, then take him, for by God, he is the best in this world and the next. They said: We will take it even though we have lost our wealth and killed our nobles. What will we get from that, O Messenger of God, if we are faithful to it? He said: Paradise. He said: Extend your hand. So he extended his hand and they pledged allegiance to him. The first to strike his hand was Al-Bara’ bin Ma’rur. Then the people followed one another. When we pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the devil cried out from the top of the pass in the loudest voice I have ever heard: O people of Al-Jabajib, do you want to fight Mudhimmah and As-Sabaa? They have gathered to fight you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the enemy of God, this is the one who has crossed the pass. Listen, O enemy of God. By God, I will surely finish you off. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Return to your homes. Al-Abbas bin Ubadah bin Nadlah said: By Him who sent you with the truth, if you wish, we will attack the people of Mina tomorrow with our swords. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We were not commanded to do that, but return to your homes. He said: So we returned to our beds and slept on them until morning. When morning came, the great men of Quraysh came to us and came to our homes and said: O people of Khazraj, we have been informed that you have come to our companion to extract him from among us and pledge allegiance to him to fight us. By God, no one among the Arabs is more hateful to us that war should break out between us and them than you. He said: Then some of the polytheists of our people rose up from there and swore to them by God: Nothing of this happened and we knew it. And they were telling the truth. They did not know, and some of us were looking at each other, and the people stood up and among them was Al-Harith bin Hisham bin Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi and he was wearing two new sandals. He said, so I said to him a word as if I wanted to / make the people share in what they said, O Jabir, can you not take, while you are one of our masters, like the sandals of this young man from Quraysh? He said, Al-Harith heard it and took them off his feet and threw them to me and said: By God, you must wear them. Abu Jabir, may God be pleased with him, said: Stop, by God, you have protected the young man, so return his sandals to him. He said: I will not return them, by God, it is a good omen, by God, if the omen is true, I will take it away. He said: Then the Ansar returned to Medina, having strengthened their bonds. When they arrived there, they declared Islam there. This reached the Quraysh, so they harmed the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: God Almighty has made for you brothers and a home in which you are safe. So he ordered them to migrate to Medina and join their brothers from the Ansar. The first to migrate to Medina was Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi, then Amer ibn Rabi’ah, then Abdullah ibn Jahsh. Then the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed one after the other in sending them to Medina. God united the people of Medina, its Aws and Khazraj, in Islam, and His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, reconciled between them. God the Almighty said: “And remember the favor of God upon you, O company of Christians, when you were enemies before Islam, then He united your hearts through Islam, and you became, by His favor, by His mercy and by His religion, Islam, brothers in religion and allegiance among you. And you were, O company of Aws and Khazraj, on the brink of a pit of fire, meaning on the edge of a pit like the edge of a well. Its meaning is: You were on the edge of a pit of fire, with nothing standing between you and falling into it except that you die in your disbelief, then God saved you from it through faith. Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may be guided.”
3:104: 104- And let there be from you a nation meaning: be a nation, from is a conjunction that is not for partiality, like the Almighty's saying: So avoid the uncleanness of idols (al-Hajj 22:30). He did not mean avoiding some idols, but rather he meant avoid the idols, and the lam in His saying and let there be is the lam of command, calling to good to Islam, and enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and it is those who are the successful. Ismail Abdul Qahir told us, he said: Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, he said: Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Abi Shaybah told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, he said: Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with them both, said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand. If he is unable to do so, then with his tongue. If he is unable to do so, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.” Abu Abdullah bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, he said: Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, I heard Amr bin Abi Amr, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Ashhali, on the authority of Hudhayfah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or God will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, and then you will call upon Him and He will not answer you.” Imam Abu Ali Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Qadi told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Darawardi told us, Abu Al-Nu’man told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muslim Al-Qasmali told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, he said: I heard Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, say: O people, you recite this verse: “O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves. He who strays will not harm you if you are guided.” I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If people see something wrong and do not change it, God Almighty will soon punish them all. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Amr bin Hafs bin Ghayath told us, my father told us, Al-A’mash told me, Al-Sha’bi told me that he heard Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, may God be pleased with him, say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The example of one who flatters God’s limits and transgresses them is like a group of people who drew lots to board a ship. Some of them were in the lower part of it and some were in the upper part. Those in the lower part were passing the water over those in the upper part and were hurt by it. So he took an axe and began to poke at the bottom of the ship. They came to him and said: What is the matter with you? He said: You are hurt by me, and I need water. If they seize his hand, they will save him and save themselves, but if they leave him alone, they will destroy him and destroy themselves.”
3:105: 105- The Almighty said: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them. Most of the commentators said: They are the Jews and Christians, and some of them said: The innovators of this nation, and Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, said: They are the Kharijites in the Levant. Abdullah bin Shaddad said: Abu Umamah stood with me at the head of the Kharijites in Ash-Sham and said: They are the dogs of Hellfire. They were believers, then they disbelieved after their belief. Then he recited: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them until the Almighty’s saying: Did you disbelieve after your belief? Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Al-Hussein bin Bishran told us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, that Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is pleased with the spaciousness of Paradise, let him adhere to the group, for the devil is with the individual, and he is further away from two. God Almighty says: And those will have a great punishment.
3:106: 106- The day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black, Day is an accusative of circumstance, meaning: on a day, and the accusative of circumstance is a comparison to the object, meaning: the faces of the believers will turn white and the faces of the disbelievers will turn black. It was also said: the faces of the sincere will turn white and the faces of the hypocrites will turn black. On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he recited this verse and said: The faces of the people of the Sunnah will be white and the faces of the people of innovation will be black. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When the Day of Resurrection comes, what they used to worship will be lifted up for every people, and every people will strive to what they used to worship, and this is the saying of God Almighty: We will give him what he took (An-Nisaa’: 115). So when they reach it, they will be sad and their faces will turn black from sadness, and the people of the Qiblah, the Jews and the Christians will remain, not recognizing anything that was lifted up for them. Then God will come to them and those who used to prostrate to Him in this world will prostrate to Him, obedient and believing, and the People of the Book and the hypocrites will remain, unable to prostrate. Then permission will be given to them, and they will raise their heads, and the faces of the believers will be as white as snow. When the hypocrites and the People of the Book look at the faces of the believers, they will be extremely sad and their faces will turn black. They will say: Our Lord, why are our faces black? By God, we were not polytheists. Then God will say to the angels: Look how they lied to themselves. The people of meaning said: The whitening of faces: their radiance, good tidings, and happiness with their deeds and with the reward of God, and their blackening: their sadness, gloom, and eclipse with their deeds and with the punishment of God, indicated by the words of God the Most High: For those who do good is the best [reward] and even more, and neither darkness nor disgrace will cover their faces (Yunus 10:26). And God the Most High said: And those who have earned evil deeds - the recompense of evil will be like it, and disgrace will cover them (Yunus 10:27). And He said: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord, and some faces, that Day, will be dismal (al-Qiyamah 75:22-24). And He said: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, laughing and cheerful, and some faces, that Day, will be covered with dust (Abasa 80:37-40). As for those whose faces will be blackened, ‘Did you disbelieve after your belief?’ It means: It will be said to them: Did you disbelieve after your belief? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. If it is said: How did he say: Did you disbelieve after your belief, while they were not believers? It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab that he meant by it: the faith on the day of the covenant, when he said to them: Am I not your Lord? They said: He says: Did you disbelieve after your belief on the day of the covenant? Al-Hasan said: They are the hypocrites who spoke the faith with their tongues, but denied it in their hearts. On the authority of Ikrimah: They are the People of the Book. They believed in their prophets and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was sent, but when he was sent, they disbelieved in him. Some people said: They are from the people of our Qiblah. Abu Umamah said: They are the Khawarij. Qatada said: They are the people of innovation. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Nafi bin Umar told us, Ibn Abi Malekah told us, Asma bint Abi Bakr told us, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will precede you to the Cistern until I see who among you comes to me. Some people will be taken before me, and I will say: ‘O God, from me and from my nation.’ It will be said to me: ‘Did you notice what they did after you left?’ By God, they have not ceased to turn back on their heels.” Al-Harith Al-A’war said: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, on the pulpit saying: A man may leave his family and not return to them until he does an action that merits Paradise, and a man may leave his family and not return to them until he does an action that merits Hell. Then he recited, On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black, the verse, then he called out: They are the ones who disbelieved after believing - by the Lord of the Kaaba. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Al-Ala bin Abdul-Rahman told us, his father told us, Abu Hurairah told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hasten to do good deeds before there are trials like pieces of a dark night. A man will go to bed a believer and wake up an unbeliever, and he will go to bed a believer and wake up an unbeliever, selling his religion for worldly gain.”
3:107: 107- The Almighty said: And as for those whose faces will be white, these are the people of obedience, they will be in the mercy of God, the Paradise of God, therein they will abide eternally.
3:108: 108- "These are the verses of God which We recite to you in truth. And God does not intend injustice for the worlds."
3:109: 109- To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to God all matters will be returned.
3:110: 110- "You are the best nation produced for mankind." Ikrimah and Muqatil said: It was revealed about Ibn Masoud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Muadh ibn Jabal, and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with them. This was because Malik ibn al-Sayf and Wahb ibn Yahudah, the two Jews, said to them: We are better than you and our religion is better than what you are calling us to. So God Almighty revealed this verse. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, You are the best nation produced for mankind. They are those who migrated with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Medina. Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, especially the narrators and preachers whom God commanded the Muslims to obey. It was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab that he said: You are the best nation brought forth for mankind. It will be for the first of us and not for the last of us. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Muhammad Badr Al-Rahman bin Abi Shureih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah Anabi Hamza told us: I heard Zahdam bin Mudrib from Imran bin Husain, may God be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The best of you are my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them. Imran said: I do not know whether the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned his generation two or three times and said: After you there will be people who betray and are not trusted, who bear witness but are not asked to bear witness, who make vows but do not fulfill them, and obesity will appear among them. And with this chain of transmission on the authority of Ali bin Al-Ja`d, Shu`bah and Abu Mu`awiyah informed us on the authority of Al-A`mash on the authority of Dhakwan on the authority of Abu Sa`id on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Do not curse my companions, for by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend the equivalent of Mount Uhud in gold, it would not reach the level of one of them, nor even half of it.” Others said: They are all the believers of this nation. His saying, You were, meaning: you, is like the Most High’s saying: And remember when you were few (al-A’raf 7:86), and He said in another place: And remember when you were few (al-Anfal 8:26), and it was said: Its meaning is: you were the best nation with God in the Preserved Tablet. And some people said: His saying for the people is connected to His saying the best nation, meaning: you are the best people for the people. Abu Hurairah said: Its meaning is: You were the best of people. You brought them in chains and brought them into Islam. He said to the people, I brought out means: God did not bring out for the people a nation better than the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Ali Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Habish Al-Muqri told us, Ali bin Zanjawiya told us, Salamah bin Shabib told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Bahz bin Hakim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say regarding the words of God Almighty: You are the best nation produced for mankind, he said: You complete seventy nations, and you are the best of them and the most honored of them in the sight of God Almighty. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Ma’shar Ibrahim bin Muhammad Al-Firki told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Zakariya bin Yahya told us, Abu Al-Salt told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Ibn Zaid told us, Ali bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Beware, this nation will die seventy nations, the best of them and the most honorable of them to God Almighty. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, I am Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi, Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Muhammad told us, I am Al-Fadl bin Al-Fadl, Abu Khalifa Al-Fadl bin Al-Habbab told us, Abdul Rahman, meaning Ibn Al-Mubarak, told us, Hammad bin Yahya Al-Abbah told us, I am Thabit Al-Banani, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him. On his authority, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The example of my nation is like that of rain. It is not known whether its beginning or its end is better.” Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, I told Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi, I told Abu Muhammad Al-Mukhalladi, Abu Na’im told us, Abdul Malik bin Muhammad bin Adi, Ahmad bin Isa Al-Tanisi told us, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, Sadaqah bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Paradise was forbidden to all the prophets until I entered it, and it was forbidden to all the nations until my nation entered it. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us: Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us: Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Muhammad told us: Abu Al-Qasim Umar bin Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Hatim Al-Tirmidhi told us: My maternal grandfather Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Marzouq told us: Affan bin Muslim told us: Abdul Aziz bin Muslim told us: Abu Sinan, meaning Dhirar bin Murrah, told us on the authority of Muharib bin Dithar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Buraidah, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of them from this nation. God Almighty says: “You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in God. And if the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.” That is, the disbelievers.
3:111: 111- The Almighty said: "They will not harm you except with a slight harm." Muqatil said: The leaders of the Jews went to those among them who believed, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions, and harmed them. So God Almighty revealed: "They will not harm you except with a slight harm." That is, these Jews will not harm you, O believers, except with a slight harm by the tongue: a threat and a stab. It was said: a word of disbelief by which you will be harmed. "And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you, in defeat, and then they will not be aided, but you will have victory over them.
3:112: 112- "Humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found wherever they are found except by a rope from God" meaning: wherever they are found they are weakened, killed and taken captive, so they are not safe except by a rope from God: a covenant from God the Most High that they will submit, "and a rope from the people" from the believers by paying a tax or security, meaning: unless they hold fast to a rope and are safe. God Almighty says: And they incurred the wrath of God, they returned with it, “and poverty was imposed upon them. That was because they disbelieved in the signs of God and killed the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.”
3:113: 113- The Almighty said: “They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing.” Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Muqatil said: When Abdullah bin Salam and his companions converted to Islam, the Jewish rabbis said: None believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, except the worst of us, and had it not been for that, they would not have abandoned the religion of their fathers. Then God Almighty revealed this verse. They differed about its meaning. Some people said: It is an abbreviation, the meaning of which is: They are not equal among the People of the Book, one nation is established and the other is not established. So he left out the other, being satisfied with mentioning one of the two groups. The others said: The end of the speech is at His saying: They are not equal. This is a pause because the two groups of the People of the Book have already been mentioned in His Almighty saying: Among them are believers, but most of them are wicked. Then He said: They are not equal, meaning: the believers and the wicked. Then He described the wicked, saying: They will not harm you except with an injury. And He described the believers by saying: A standing nation. It was said: His saying from the People of the Book is the beginning of another statement, because the mention of the two groups had already occurred, then he said: These two groups are not the same, then he began and said: from the People of the Book. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: Its meaning is: The Jews and the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who uphold God’s command, are not equal, steadfast in the truth, and upright. And God Almighty’s statement, A nation that upholds, Ibn Abbas said: meaning, guided and upholding God’s command, they did not waste it or abandon it. Mujahed said: Just. Al-Suddi said: Obedient, adhering to the Book of God and His limits. It was also said: Standing in prayer. It was also said: The nation is the path. The meaning of the verse: that is, one who has a nation, that is, one who has a straight path. They recite the verses of God, they read the Book of God. Mujahid said: They follow the hours of the night, its hours. The singular is: ani, like nahi and anha, and ani and ana are like: ma’i and mi’a, and ani is like mana and amna. And they prostrate means: they pray, because recitation does not take place during prostration. They differed about its meaning. Some of them said: It is during the night prayer. Ibn Masoud said: It is the Isha prayer that they pray, but none of the People of the Book pray it. Ata’ said: “They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing together.” The verse means: Forty men from the people of Najran from the Arabs, thirty-two from Abyssinia, and eight from the Romans were on the religion of Jesus and believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. There were several Ansar among them before the coming of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, including As’ad ibn Zararah, Al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur, Muhammad ibn Maslamah, Mahmoud ibn Maslamah, and Abu Qais Sarmah ibn Anas. They were monotheists who would wash themselves after sexual impurity and perform the laws of the Hanafi school that they knew until God Almighty brought them the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they believed in him and supported him.
3:114: 114-The Almighty said: “They believe in God and the Last Day, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and hasten to good deeds. And those are among the righteous.”
3:115: 115- And whatever good they do, they will never be denied it. Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read with a ya' in both of them, describing the existing nation. The others read with a ta' in both of them, because of His statement, You were the best nation. Abu Amr sees both readings together, and the meaning of the verse is: And whatever good you do, you will never be deprived of its reward, rather you will be thanked and rewarded for it. And God is Knowing of the righteous, of the believers.
3:116: 116- Indeed, those who disbelieve - neither their wealth nor their children will avail them against God at all, meaning: their wealth will not be able to be ransomed, nor their children supported, at all, from God's punishment. He mentioned them both because a person sometimes defends himself by ransoming money and sometimes by seeking help from his children. And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally, and He made them among its companions because they are its people, they will not leave it nor depart from it, like a man's companion who will not leave him.
3:117: 117- Like what they spend in this worldly life, it was said: He meant the expenses of Abu Sufyan and his companions in Badr alone in enmity with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muqatil said: The spending of the Jews on their scholars. Mujahid said: He means all the expenses of the infidels in this world and their charity. It was said: He meant the spending of the hypocrite who does not seek the face of God Almighty, Like a wind in which there is a shriek (It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: that it is the hot poisons that kill. It was said: In it is a shriek, meaning: a sound. Most of the commentators said: In it is intense cold It struck the crops of a people the crops of a people who wronged themselves, by disbelief and disobedience and withholding the right of God Almighty, and destroyed it. The meaning of the verse is: The example of the expenses of the infidels in their going away at a time when they are needed is like the example of a crop that is struck by a cold wind and destroyed or a fire and burnt, so its owners do not benefit from it at all. And God has not wronged them in that, but they wrong themselves by disbelief and disobedience.
3:118: 118- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves The verse: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: There were men among the Muslims who maintained close relations with the Jews because of the kinship, friendship, alliance, neighbourhood and breastfeeding between them, so God Almighty revealed this verse forbidding them from keeping close relations with them for fear of temptation for them. Mujahid said: It was revealed about a group of believers who were befriending the hypocrites, but God Almighty forbade them from doing so, saying: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves, meaning: allies and close friends from outside your religion. A man’s intimates are his confidants, likening them to the lining of a garment that is next to his stomach, because they conceal his secrets and learn about him what others do not learn about. Then He explained the reason for the prohibition of harboring them, saying, They spare no effort in ruining you, meaning: they do not fall short or leave their efforts in what brings you evil and corruption. Khabal is evil and corruption. Khabalan is the second object because ya’lu is transitive with two objects. It was also said: by removing the preposition, meaning by khabal, as one says, I struck him painfully. “They wished for what you suffered,” meaning: they wished for what would be difficult for you, of harm, evil, and destruction. Hatred means hardship. Hatred has appeared, meaning: hatred, meaning that the sign of enmity has appeared, from their mouths, by cursing and slandering the Muslims. It was also said: by the polytheists knowing the secrets of the believers. And what their breasts conceal, of enmity and anger, is greater, “We have made clear to you the verses, if you would but use reason.”
3:119: 119- Here you are This is a warning, and you are a metaphor for the males being addressed. Those is the name of those referred to, meaning you, O believers. You love them meaning: you love these Jews whom I have forbidden you from keeping company with, due to the reasons between you of kinship, breastfeeding, and marriage. And they do not love you they, because of the opposition between you of religion. Muqatil said: They are the hypocrites whom the believers love because of the faith they have shown, and they do not know what is in their hearts. And you believe in the entire Book meaning: in all the books, and they do not believe in your Book. And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe,' and when they are alone, and some of them are with each other, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage meaning: the tips of the fingers, one of which is fingertip, with a damma or fatha on the meem, out of rage at what they see of the believers uniting and their word coming together. Biting the fingertips is an expression of intense rage, and this is from the metaphor of the example, even if there is no biting. "Say: Die in your rage i.e., remain in your rage until death, for God is Knowing of that within the breasts i.e., of what is in the hearts of good and evil.
3:120: 120-And the Almighty’s saying: If good befalls you meaning: it befalls you, O believers, by your victory over your enemy and the spoils you obtain from them, and people continue to enter your religion, and your livelihoods are abundant, it distresses them, makes them sad, but if evil befalls you, harm by the failure of your expedition or the injury of an enemy from among you, or a disagreement that occurs between you or a drought or a calamity that befalls you, “they rejoice at it. But if you are patient” in their harm and fear God and fear your Lord, their plot will not harm you meaning: it will not decrease you in the least, Ibn Kathir, Nafi’ and the people of Basra read “will not harm you with a light kasra on the ḍād. It is said: ḍarā yadhīr ḍīrān, and it is a jazm in response to the reward. The rest read it with a ḍād and a shaddah on the ra’ from ḍarra yadhīr ḍarrān, like radd yard raddan, and there are two views regarding its being raised: one of them. He wanted to make it definitive, and its original form is it harms you, so the ra was assimilated into the ra, and the damma of the first ra was transferred to the dad, and the damma of the second was added in imitation. The second: that la means not, and the fa is implied in it, and its meaning is: And if you are patient and fear God, then their plot will not harm you at all. “Indeed, God is encompassing of what they do.” He is All-Knowing.
3:121: 121- The Almighty said: And when you left your family in the morning, to place the believers at their stations for battle. Al-Hasan said: It is the day of Badr. Muqatil said: The day of the Confederates. The rest of the commentators said: It is the day of Uhud, because what follows it until close to the end of the surah is about the Battle of Uhud. Mujahid al-Kalbi and al-Waqidi said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left the house of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and walked on foot to Uhud. He began to line up his companions for battle as if he were raising an arrow. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and al-Suddi said on the authority of their men: The polytheists camped at Uhud on Wednesday. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of their camp, he consulted his companions and called Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, whom he had never called before. So he consulted him, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy and most of the Ansar said: O Messenger of God, stay in Medina and do not go out to them. By God, we have never gone out to an enemy without him killing us, nor has he entered upon us without us killing him. So how about when you are among us? So leave them, O Messenger of God. If they stay, they will stay in the worst place, and if they enter, the men will fight them in their faces and the women and children will throw stones at them from above them, and if they return, they will return disappointed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with this opinion. Some of his companions said: O Messenger of God, let us go out to these dogs, so that they will not see that we are cowards and weak towards them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw in my dream cows being slaughtered, so I interpreted it as good. I saw a notch in the fly of my sword, so I interpreted it as defeat. I saw that I put my hand into a strong shield, so I interpreted it as the city. So if you see fit to stay in the city.” He liked it when they entered the city and fought in the alleys. Some of the Muslims who had missed the day of Badr and whom God had honored with martyrdom on the day of Uhud said: Let us go out to our enemies. They kept on attacking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of their love for meeting the people, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered and put on his weapons for his nation. When they saw that he had put on his weapons, they regretted it and said: What we have done is bad. We advise the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while the revelation is coming to him. So they stood up and apologized to him and said: Do what you have seen. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not appropriate for a prophet to put on his weapons for his nation and then put them down until he fights. The polytheists had stayed in Uhud on Wednesday and Thursday, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left on Friday after leading his companions in the Friday prayer. On that day, a man from the Ansar died, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him, then he went out to them, and he became in the valley of Uhud on Saturday, the middle of Shawwal, in the year three of the Hijra. So what happened in the Uhud War was that, and that is what God Almighty said: And when you went forth from your family meaning: And remember when you went forth from your family placed the believers meaning: the believers descended at positions for the battle meaning: places and locations for the battle. It is said: You placed the people in positions if you settled them, and they settled if they settled together. God Almighty said: And We had already settled the Children of Israel in a position of truth (Yunus 10:93) and He said: That you two establish houses for your people in Egypt (Yunus 10:87). It was said that you establish a camp, And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
3:122: 122- When two parties from among you were about to lose heart meaning: to become cowardly, weak and fall behind. The two parties were Banu Salamah from the Khazraj and Banu Haritha from the Aws, and they were the two wings of the army. That is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Uhud with a thousand men, and it was said: with nine hundred and fifty men. When they reached the shore, Abdullah bin Ubayy fled with a third of the people and returned with three hundred, and said: Why should we kill ourselves and our children? Abu Jaber Al-Sulami followed them and said: I ask you by God regarding your Prophet and yourselves. Abdullah bin Ubayy said: If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you. Banu Salamah and Banu Haritha were about to turn back with Abdullah bin Ubayy, but God protected them and they did not turn back. Then God reminded them of His great blessings, and He, the Almighty, said: When two parties from among you were about to lose heart, and God is their Protector He is their Supporter and Preserver. And in God let the believers put their trust. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naeem told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: This verse was revealed about us, When two parties among you were about to lose heart, but God was their protector, Banu Salamah and Banu Haritha. I would not have liked it not to have been revealed, and God says: And God is their protector.
3:123: 123- The Almighty said: And God certainly gave you victory at Badr, and Badr is a place between Mecca and Medina and it is the name of a place, and most of them agree with that. It was also said: It is the name of a well there, and it was also said: Badr was a well for a man called Badr, as Al-Sha’bi said, and others denied it. God Almighty mentions in this verse His blessing of victory upon them on the day of Badr, and you were weak, plural: weak, and what He meant by this was that they were few in number, for they were three hundred and thirteen men, and God granted them victory despite their small number, So fear God that you may be grateful.
3:124: 124- When you said to the believers, 'Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you?' They differed regarding this verse. Qatada said: This was on the day of Badr, God Almighty reinforced them with a thousand angels as He said: So He responded to you, 'I will reinforce you with a thousand angels' (al-Anfal 8:9). Then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand as mentioned here, with three thousand angels sent down.
3:125: 125- Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marked marks. So they were patient on the day of Badr and feared God, so God reinforced them with five thousand as He promised. Al-Hasan said: And these five thousand will be the backbone of the believers until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: The angels did not fight in battle except on the day of Badr, and in other than that they witnessed the battle but did not fight, but rather they were a number and reinforcements. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When the battle of Uhud came, the people fled from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Sa`d bin Malik remained shooting, and a young man was collecting arrows for him. When the arrows ran out, he brought them to him and scattered them. He said, Shoot, Abu Ishaq, twice. When the battle ended, he was asked about that man, but he did not know. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah, I told Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah, I told Ibrahim bin Saad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Saad bin Abi Waqqas, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, and with him were two men fighting on his behalf, wearing white clothes, in the most intense fighting. I did not see them before or after. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, who said: Muhammad bin Bishr and Abu Usamah told us on the authority of Misa’ar on the authority of Sa’d bin Ibrahim on the authority of his father on the authority of Sa’d, meaning Ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: “I saw on the right and left of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud two men wearing white clothes. I had never seen them before or after,” meaning: Gabriel and Michael. Al-Sha’bi said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims were informed on the day of Badr that Kurz bin Jaber al-Muharibi wanted to reinforce the polytheists, and this was difficult for them. So God Almighty revealed: Will it not suffice for you that he reinforces you? until His saying marked. So Kurz was informed of the defeat, so he returned and did not come to them or reinforce them. So God did not reinforce them with the five thousand either, and they had been reinforced with a thousand. Others said: God Almighty promised the Muslims on the day of Badr, if they were patient in obeying Him and feared His prohibitions, that He would also support them in all their wars. They were not patient except on the day of the Confederates, so God supported them until they besieged Qurayzah and Nadir. Abdullah bin Abi Awfa said: We were besieging Qurayzah and Nadir as long as God willed, but He did not grant us victory. So we returned and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for a bath and he was washing his head when Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said: You have laid down your weapons but the angels have not laid down their burdens? So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for a rag and wrapped it around his head but did not wash it. Then he called to us and we stood up until we came to Qurayzah and Nadir. On that day, God Almighty supported us with three thousand angels, and granted us an easy victory. Ad-Dahhak and Ikrimah said: This was the day of Uhud, and God promised them reinforcements if they were patient, but they were not patient, so they were not reinforced. The Almighty said: That your Lord should reinforce you. And reinforcement means supporting an army with an army. It was said: That which is in the form of strength and support, it is said in it: reinforcement, and that which is in the form of increase, it is said: reinforcement, and from this is the Almighty’s saying: And the sea reinforces it (Luqman 31:27). It was said: reinforcement is in evil, and reinforcement is in good, as indicated by the Almighty’s saying: And He extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly (al-Baqarah 2:15) And We extend for him from the punishment an extension (Maryam 19:79). And He said in good: Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another (al-Isra’ 17:26). The Almighty said: With three thousand angels sent down. Ibn Amir read it with emphasis on the letter zay for emphasis, based on the Almighty’s saying: And if We had sent down to them the angels (Surat al-An’am 6:111). The others read it with emphasis, based on the Almighty’s saying: Why were angels not sent down to us? (al-Furqan 25:21) and His saying: And He sent down soldiers you did not see (al-Tawbah 9:26). Then he said: Yes, We will reinforce you if you are patient for your enemy and fear God that is, disobey your Prophet “and they come to you meaning the polytheists all at once. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Qatadah, Al-Hasan and most of the commentators said: From this aspect of theirs. Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: From this anger of theirs, because they only returned to war on the day of Uhud because of their anger on the day of Badr. Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels. He did not mean five thousand other than what was mentioned of three thousand, rather he meant with them. His saying marked means: marked. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Asim read it with a kasra on the waw, and the others read it with a fatha. Whoever broke the waw meant that they marked their horses, and whoever opened it meant themselves. Marking is the notification from the mark, which is the sign. They differed about that sign. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: The angels were on piebald horses wearing yellow turbans. Ali and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said: They were wearing white turbans that they had let down between their shoulders. (Hisham ibn Urwah and al-Kalbi said: Yellow turbans hanging down over their shoulders.) Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: They had been marked with wool on the forelocks and tails of the horses. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions on the day of Badr: Sell yourselves, for the angels have been marked with white wool on their skullcaps and helmets.
3:126: 126- The Almighty said: And God has not made it meaning this promise and support, except as good tidings for you meaning: good tidings for you to be happy with it and to reassure and to calm your hearts with it so do not be alarmed by the great number of your enemy and the small number of you, and victory is only from God, the Almighty, the Wise meaning: do not rely on the angels and soldiers for victory, for victory is from God Almighty, so seek His help and put your trust in Him, because glory and judgment belong to Him.
3:127: 127- The Almighty said: To cut off a part of those who disbelieved, meaning: God helped you at Badr to cut off a part, meaning: to destroy a group of those who disbelieved. Al-Suddi said: Its meaning is to destroy a pillar of polytheism by killing and taking captive, so seventy of their leaders and masters were killed on the day of Badr and seventy were taken captive. Whoever interprets the verse to mean the Battle of Uhud, sixteen of them were killed that day and the victory was for the Muslims until they disobeyed the command of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it turned against them. Or subdue them, Al-Kalbi said: He defeats them. Yaman said: He wrestles them down on their faces. Al-Suddi said: He curses them. Abu Ubaidah said: He destroys them. It was said: He grieves them. Al-Makboot is the sad one. It was said that its origin is: He inflicts grief and anger / on their livers. The ta and the dal alternate as it is said: He shaved his head and shaved it. It was said: He subdues them. With disappointment, they will return disappointed, they did not achieve anything of what they had hoped for from victory over you.
3:128: 128- The Almighty said: You have no part in the matter the verse, they differed about the reason for the revelation of this verse, some people said: It was revealed about the people of Bir Ma'unah, and they were seventy men of the Qur'an reciters, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them to Bir Ma'unah in Safar of the year four of the Hijrah, four months after Uhud, to teach the people the Qur'an and knowledge, their leader was Al-Mundhir bin Amr, so Amer bin At-Tufayl killed them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was deeply distressed by that, and he prayed for a month in all the prayers, calling for a curse and years against a group of those tribes, so the verse was revealed: You have no part in the matter. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Habban bin Musa told us, Abdullah, meaning Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Omar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Salim told me, on the authority of his father, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he raised his head from bowing in the last rak’ah of Fajr: O God, curse so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so, after he had said: God hears whoever praises Him, our Lord, to You is praise. Then God Almighty revealed: You have no part in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers. Some people said: It was revealed on the day of Uhud. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abdullah bin Muslimah bin Qanab told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with them both, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had his front tooth broken on the day of Uhud and his head was wounded. He kept wiping the blood off him and saying: How can a people succeed when they have wounded the head of their Prophet and broken his front tooth while he was calling them to God Almighty? Then God Almighty revealed: ‘You have no part in the matter.’” On the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, may God be pleased with them both, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of UHud 11:O God, curse Abu Sufyan, O God, curse Al-Harith bin Hisham, O God, curse Safwan bin Umayya. Then the verse was revealed: You have no part in the matter, unless God forgives them. So they became Muslim, and their Islam was good. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims saw on the day of Uhud what happened to their companions, such as the cutting off of their ears and noses and the cutting off of their genitals, they said: If God Almighty gives us victory over them, we will do to them what they did, and we will mutilate them in a way that no Arab has mutilated anyone before. So God Almighty revealed this verse. It was said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to call for their extermination, so this verse was revealed because he knew that many of them would convert to Islam. So the Almighty’s saying: You have no part in the matter means: it is not up to you, so the lam means to like His saying: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith (Surat Al Imran 3:193), meaning: to faith. The Almighty’s saying: Or He turns to them in mercy (some of them said: it means until He turns to them in mercy), or: until He turns to them in mercy, and it was said: it is a sequence of His saying: To cut off a part, and His saying: You have no part in the matter is an interruption between the order of the speech and the order of the verse: “To cut off a part of those who disbelieve or suppress them so they return disappointed. You have no part in the matter” rather the matter is a command in all of that.
3:129: 129-Then he said: “To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.”
3:130: 130- O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied, meaning what they used to do when the due date of the debt came, by increasing the money and delaying the request, and fear God in the matter of usury, so do not consume it, that you may be successful.
3:132: 132- And obey God and the Messenger that you may receive mercy, so that you may receive mercy.
3:133: 133- And hasten, the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read hastened without the waw, to forgiveness from your Lord, meaning hasten and race to the deeds that necessitate forgiveness. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: To Islam. It was narrated from him: To repentance. Ikrimah said the same. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: To performing the obligatory duties. Abu al-Aaliyah said: To migration. Ad-Dahhak said: To jihad. Muqatil said: To righteous deeds. It was narrated from Anas ibn Malik that it is the first takbir. And a garden meaning and to a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth meaning: its width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, as He said in Surat Al-Hadid And a garden as wide as the heaven and the earth Surat Al-Hadid - 21 meaning: its spaciousness, and the width was mentioned for emphasis because the length of everything is usually greater than its width. He says: This is a description of its width, so how is its length? Al-Zuhri said: Its width was only described, as for its length, only God knows it, and this is for example, not that it is like the heavens and the earth and nothing else, its meaning: like the width of the seven heavens and the seven earths according to your opinion, like the Almighty's saying: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure Surat Hud - 107 meaning: according to your opinion, like His saying: Otherwise, they will perish. It was narrated on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab that some Jews asked Omar bin Al-Khattab while his companions were with him, may God be pleased with them, and they said: Have you seen His saying: And a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth so where is the fire? Omar said: Have you seen when night comes, where is the day, and when day comes, where is the night? They said: It is like it in the Torah, and its meaning is that it is wherever God wills. If it is said: God the Almighty said: And in the heaven is your provision and that which you are promised (Surat al-Dhariyat 51:22), and what He meant by what He promised us is Paradise. So if Paradise is in the heaven, how wide is it as the heavens and the earth? It is said: The gate of Paradise is in the heaven and its width is as the heavens and the earth, as He has informed us. Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, was asked about Paradise: Is it in the heaven or on the earth? He said: Which earth and heaven can contain Paradise? It was said: Where is it? He said: Above the seven heavens under the Throne. Qatada said: They used to think that Paradise is above the seven heavens, and that Hell is under the seven earths prepared for the righteous.
3:134: 134- "Those who spend in prosperity and adversity", meaning: in ease and hardship, then what was mentioned of their morals that lead to Paradise is the mention of generosity, and it came in the hadith. Abu Saeed Al-Sharihi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha'labi told us, Abu Amr Al-Furati told us, Abu Al-Abbas Ahmad bin Ismail Al-Anbari told us, Abu Abdullah bin Hazim Al-Baghawi told us in Mecca, Abu Saleh bin Ayoub Al-Hashemi told us, Ibrahim bin Saad told us, Saeed bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Al-A'raj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The generous person is close to God, close to Paradise, close to the people, and far from the Fire. The miserly person is far from God, far from Paradise, far from the people, and close to the Fire. The ignorant generous person is more beloved to God than a miserly worshipper. And those who restrain anger" means: those who suppress anger when their souls are filled with it. Suppression is to hold something back when it is full. Suppressing anger means to fill one's heart with anger and to keep it inside one's chest and not express it. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: "When the hearts will be at the throats, suppressing" (Surat Ghafir 40:18). Abu Saeed Al-Shuraihi informed us. Abu Ishaq Al-Tha'labi informed us. Abu Amr Al-Furati informed us. Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Isfarayini informed us. Abu Abdullah bin Muhammad Zakariya Al-Alani informed us. Ruh bin Abdul-Mu'min informed us. Abu Abdul-Rahman Al-Muqri informed us. Saeed bin Abi Ayoub informed us. He said: Abu Marhum informed me on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas Al-Juhani on the authority of his father who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever suppresses his anger when he is able to vent it, God will call him on the Day of Resurrection in front of all creation and let him choose from any of the houris he wishes." And those who pardon people, Al-Kalbi said about the ill-mannered slaves, and Zaid bin Aslam and Muqatil said: about those who wronged them and treated them badly. And God loves the doers of good.
3:135: 135- The Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves the verse. Ibn Masoud said: The believers said: O Messenger of God, the Children of Israel were more honored by God than us. When one of them sinned, the expiation for his sin would be written on the threshold of his door: Cut off your nose and ear, do such and such. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent, and God Almighty revealed this verse. Ata’ said: It was revealed about Nabhan al-Tammar, whose nickname was Abu Ma’bad. A beautiful woman came to him to buy dates from him, so he said to her: These dates are not good, and there are better ones in the house. So he took her to his house, hugged her, and kissed her. She said to him: Fear God. So he left her and regretted that, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so this verse was revealed. Muqatil al-Kalbi said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, established a brotherhood between two men, one of them from the Ansar and the other from Thaqif. The Thaqafi went out on a raid and left the Ansari in charge of his family. One day, he bought meat for them. When the woman wanted to take some from him, he entered after her and kissed her hand. Then he regretted it and left, putting dirt on his head and wandered about. When the Thaqafi returned, the Ansari did not meet him, so he asked his wife about his condition. She said: May God not increase the number of brothers like him. She described the condition to him, and the Ansari was wandering in the mountains, repenting and seeking forgiveness. The Thaqafi searched for him until he found him, so he brought him to Abu Bakr, hoping to find comfort and relief with him. The Ansari said: I am ruined. He told him the story, and Abu Bakr said: Woe to you! Didn’t you know that God, the Most High, is more jealous for the raider than He is for the resident? Then they came to Umar, may God be pleased with him, and he said the same thing. Then they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to him the same thing as Muqatil.
