Then God, the Most High, revealed this verse: And those who, when they commit an immorality, meaning: Ugly, outside of what God Almighty has permitted him to do. The root of obscenity is ugliness and going beyond the limit. Jabir said: Obscenity is adultery. Or they wronged themselves is less than adultery, such as kissing, hugging, looking, and touching. Muqatil Al-Kalbi said: The immorality is less than adultery, such as kissing, touching, or looking at something that is not permissible, or they wronged themselves by committing a sin. It was said: They committed a major sin, or wronged themselves with minor sins. It was said: They committed an indecent act or wronged themselves by word. They remembered God means: they remembered God’s threat, and that God will ask them. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: They remembered God with their tongues when they committed sins. “So seek forgiveness for their sins. And who can forgive sins except God?” That is: Who can forgive sins except God? And they did not persist in what they did meaning: they did not persist or remain steadfast in it, but they repented, turned back, and sought forgiveness. The root of persistence is: persistence in something. Al-Hasan said: The servant commits a sin deliberately, persisting until he repents. Al-Suddi said: Insistence means keeping silent and not seeking forgiveness. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Yahya bin Yahya told us, Abdul Hamid bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Waqid Al-Amri, on the authority of Nasirah, who said: I met a freed slave of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and I said to him: Did you hear anything from Abu Bakr? He said: Yes, I heard him say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness is not persistent, even if he does so seventy times a day. “And they know.” Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: They know that it is a sin. It was also said: They know that persistence is harmful. Ad-Dahhak said: They know that God has the power to forgive sins. Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said: They know that they have a Lord who forgives sins. It was also said: They know that God is not too great to forgive sins, no matter how many they are. It was also said: They know that if they seek forgiveness, He will forgive them.
3:136: 136- "Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And excellent is the reward of the workers." The reward of the obedient. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Affan bin Muslim told us, Abu Awana told us, Uthman bin Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Ali bin Rabia Al-Asadi, on the authority of Asma bin Al-Hakam Al-Fazari, who said: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: I was a man who, if I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me from it as He willed, and if one of his companions told me, I would make him swear, and if he swore to me, I would believe him. Abu Bakr told me, and Abu Bakr was truthful, that he heard the Messenger of God say: There is no believing servant who commits a sin, then purifies himself well, then stands up and prays, then seeks God’s forgiveness, except that God will forgive him. Abu Isa narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Abu Awana, and he added, then he recited: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves Al-Ma’idah 1:17. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Hisham bin Abdul Malik told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Talha, who said: There was a judge in Madinah called Abdul Rahman bin Abi Umrah, and I heard him say: I heard Abu Hurairah say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “A slave committed a sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive me. His Lord, the Almighty, said: My slave knew that he had a Lord who forgives sins and takes them into account, so He forgave him. He remained as long as God willed, then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive me. His Lord, the Almighty, said: My slave knew that he had a Lord who forgives sins and takes them into account. I have forgiven My slave, so let him do as he wishes.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Al-Nu’man Al-Sadosi told us, Al-Mahdi bin Maimun told us, Ghailan bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ma’di Karib, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who narrated it on the authority of his Lord, the Blessed and Most High, who said: O son of Adam, if you call upon Me and put your hope in Me, I will forgive you for whatever is in you. Son of Adam, if you meet Me with sins nearly as great as the earth, I will meet you with forgiveness nearly as great as it, after you do not associate anything with Me. Son of Adam, if you sin until your sins reach the clouds of the sky, then you ask My forgiveness, I will forgive you.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Al-Hassan Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Hasani Al-Sharifi told us, Abu Al-Azhar Ahmad bin Al-Azhar told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Hakam bin Aban told us, my father told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty said: Whoever knows that I have the power to forgive sins, I will forgive him and I do not care, as long as he does not associate anything with Me.” Thabit Al-Bunani said: It has reached me that Satan cried when this verse was revealed: And those who, when they commit an immorality, to the end of it.
3:137: 137- The Almighty said: There have already been ways before you. Ata’ said: Laws. Al-Kalbi said: Every nation has a way and a path. If they follow them, may God be pleased with them. Mujahid said: There have already been ways before you, with the destruction of those who denied before you. It was said: ways, meaning: nations, and the Sunnah is the nation. The poet said: People have not witnessed any virtue like yours, nor have they seen anyone like you in the past traditions. It was said that its meaning is: People of the Sunnah, and the Sunnah is: the method followed in good and evil. It is said: So-and-so followed a good Sunnah, and a bad Sunnah if he did an action that was followed, whether good or evil. The meaning of the verse: I have sent forth and preceded from Me the ways of those who were before you from the past nations of disbelievers, by giving them respite and leading them on until the written term that I have set for their destruction and the dominance of My prophets over them is fulfilled. So travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied, meaning: the end of the matter of those who denied, and this was in the Battle of Uhud. God Almighty says: So I will give them respite and lead them on until the term that I have set for the victory of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his allies and the destruction of his enemies is fulfilled.
3:138: 138- This meaning: this Qur’an, is a statement for the people in general, and guidance from misguidance and an admonition for the righteous in particular.
3:139: 139- The Almighty’s saying: And do not weaken and do not grieve. This is an exhortation to the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to jihad, in addition to what they suffered of killing and wounding on the day of Uhud. God Almighty says: And do not weaken, meaning: do not become weak and do not be cowardly in jihad against your enemies because of what you have suffered of killing and wounding. Five of them were killed on that day: Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib and Mus`ab bin `Umair, and seventy men from the Ansar were killed. And do not grieve, for you will be the superior, meaning that you will have the final victory and triumph, if you are believers, meaning: since you are believers, meaning: because you are believers. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: When the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were defeated in the ravine, Khalid ibn al-Walid approached with the polytheists’ cavalry, wanting to climb the mountain over them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, do not let them prevail over us. O God, we have no power except through You.” A group of Muslim archers rose up and climbed the mountain and shot the polytheists’ cavalry until they defeated them. This is what God Almighty said: and you will be the superior. Al-Kalbi said: This verse was revealed after the Day of Uhud when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his companions to seek out the people because of the wounds they had suffered. This became difficult for the Muslims, so God Almighty revealed this verse, the evidence for which is God Almighty’s statement: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy (An-Nisa’: 104).
3:140: 140- If a wound should touch you Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read Qarah with a damma on the qaf wherever it appears, and the others read it with a fatha, and they are two languages that mean the same as effort and exertion. Al-Farra' said that Qarah with a fatha means a wound, and with a damma means the pain of a wound. This is addressed to the Muslims when they left Uhud with depression and sadness. God Almighty says: If a wound should touch you on the day of Uhud, then a wound similar to it has touched the people on the day of Badr, And those days We alternate among the people, a day for them and a day against them. The Muslims were victorious over the polytheists on the day of Badr until they killed seventy of them and captured seventy, and the polytheists were victorious over the Muslims on the day of Uhud until they wounded seventy of them and killed seventy-five. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Amr bin Khalid told us, Zuhair told us, Abu Ishaq told us: I heard Al-Bara bin Azib say: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed Abdullah bin Jubair over the infantry on the day of Uhud, and they were fifty men. He said: If you see the birds snatching us, do not move from this place until I send for you. And if you see us defeating the people and trampling them, do not move until I send for you. So they defeated them. He said: By God, we saw the women rushing forward, their anklets and legs showing, raising their clothes. The companions of Abdullah bin Jubair said: The spoils, O people of the spoils, your companions have appeared, so what are you waiting for? Abdullah bin Jubair said: Have you forgotten what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to you? They said: By God, we will go to the people and take a share of the spoils. So when they reached them, their faces were turned away and they came back defeated. That was when the Messenger called them from the rear, and no one remained with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. May God bless him and grant him peace, except for twelve men, and they killed seventy of us. On the day of Badr, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions had captured one hundred and forty men from the polytheists, seventy of them prisoners and seventy dead. Abu Sufyan said: Is Muhammad among the people? Three times. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade them from answering him. Then he said: Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? Three times. Then he said: Is Ibn Al-Khattab among the people? Three times. Then he returned to his companions and said: As for these, they have been killed. Umar could not control himself and said: You have lied, O enemy of God. Those whom you have counted are all alive, and there remains for you that which will upset you. He said: A day for a day at Badr, and war is a contest. You will find among the people the like of him. I did not command it and it did not upset me. Then he began to recite: Hubal is exalted, Hubal is exalted. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Will you not answer him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He said: Say: God is Most High and Most Majestic. He said: We have Al-Uzza and you have no Uzza. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Will you not answer him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He said: Say, “God is our Master, and you have no Master.” This meaning was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. In his hadith, Abu Sufyan said: A day for a day, and the days are cycles and war is a contest. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: “They are not the same. Our dead are in Paradise and your dead are in Hell.” Al-Zajjaj said: The state is for the Muslims over the infidels, because God Almighty said: And Our soldiers will be the victors. And on the day of Uhud, the infidels were over the Muslims because they disobeyed the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty says: And that God may know those who believe meaning: This discussion was only for God to know i.e., for God to see those who believe and distinguish the believer from the hypocrite, and to take from among you witnesses to honor people with martyrdom, and God does not love the wrongdoers.
3:141: 141- And that God may purify those who believe meaning: purify them from sins, and destroy the disbelievers meaning: annihilate and destroy them. Its meaning is: if they kill you, it is a purification for you, and if you kill them, it is their destruction and extermination.
3:142: 142- Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while God did not yet know those among you who struggled and He knows the steadfast.
3:143: 143- And you were wishing for death before you met it, that is, a group of Muslims wished for a day like the day of Badr so that they could fight and be martyred, but God showed them the day of Uhud. His saying, You were wishing for death, means: the cause of death, which is jihad, before you met it, and you have seen it, meaning: its causes. If it is said: What is the meaning of his saying, And you are looking, after his saying, You have seen him? It is said: He mentioned it for emphasis. It is said: Seeing may mean knowing, so he said, And you are looking, to show that what is meant by seeing is looking. It is said: And you are looking at Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
3:144: 144- The Almighty said: And Muhammad is no more than a Messenger; many Messengers have passed away before him. The companions of the battles said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until he descended to the ravine of Uhud with seven hundred men, and he appointed Abdullah bin Jubair, the brother of Khawat bin Jubair, in charge of the infantry, and they were fifty men, and he said: Stay at the foot of the mountain and spray us with arrows so that they do not come to us from behind, and whether it is for us or against us, do not move from your place until I send to you, for we will not cease to be victorious as long as you remain in your place. Then the Quraysh came, and on their right flank was Khalid bin Al-Walid, and on their left was Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl, and with them were women beating drums and reciting poetry, and they fought until the war became fierce. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a sword and said: Who will take this sword with its right and strike the enemy with it until it is in full force? Abu Dujana Samak bin Kharshah Al-Ansari took it, and when he took it, he put on a red turban and began to strut, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Peace be upon him: It is a gait that God Almighty hates except in this place. So he split the heads of the polytheists with it, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, and his companions charged at the polytheists and defeated them. We narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib who said: By God, I saw the women rushing forward, their anklets and legs showing, and their clothes raised. The companions of Abdullah bin Jubayr said: The spoils, by God, we will go to the people and take a share of the spoils. So when they came to them, their faces turned away. Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awam said: I saw Hind and her companions fleeing, climbing the mountain, showing their servants without taking anything. When the archers saw that the people had been exposed and saw their companions plundering the spoils, they came forward wanting to plunder. When Khalid bin Al-Walid saw the small number of archers and the Muslims’ preoccupation with the spoils, and saw their backs empty, he shouted to his cavalry about the polytheists, then he charged at the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from behind them, so they defeated them and killed them. Abdullah bin Qum’ah threw a stone at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, breaking his nose and front teeth and cutting his face, making him heavy and his companions disperse from him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rose to a rock on top of which he had been standing between two shields, but he could not, so Talhah sat under him and rose until he was on top of it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Talhah has made it obligatory. Hind and the women with her mutilated the dead companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cutting off their ears and noses until Hind made necklaces from that, and gave it to Wahshi and cut open the liver of Hamza and chewed it, but she could not swallow it, so she spat it out. Abdullah bin Qum’ah approached, intending to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but Mus’ab bin Umair, who was the bearer of the Messenger of God’s banner, defended the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Qum’ah killed him, and he thought that he had killed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He returned to the polytheists and said: I have killed Muhammad. A voice cried out: Muhammad has been killed. It is said that the voice was Satan. The people retreated, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the al-Nas 114:To the servants of God to the servants of God. Thirty men gathered around him and protected him until they drove the polytheists away from him. Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas shot until his bow broke. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him his quiver and said to him: Shoot, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you. Talhah was a very strong archer, and on that day he broke two or three bows. A man would pass by with a quiver of arrows and say: Scatter them for Abu Talhah. Whenever he shot, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would look at the place where his arrow had landed. Talhah ibn Ubaydullah’s hand was hit and it dried up when he protected the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Qatadah ibn al-Nu’man’s eye was hit that day until it fell on his cheek. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned it to its place, and it returned to its best condition. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left, Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi caught up with him, saying: I will not be saved if I am saved. The people said: O Messenger of God, will not one of us take pity on him? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Leave him alone until he comes close to him. Before that, my father used to meet the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and say: “I have a sheep which I feed every day with a grain of corn. I will kill you for it.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Rather, I will kill you, God willing. When he came close to him, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took the spear from al-Harith ibn al-Samma, then faced him and stabbed him in the neck, scratching him once and he fell off his horse, bellowing like a bull, and saying: Muhammad killed me. His companions seized him and said: There is nothing wrong with you. He said: “Yes, if this stab had been in Rabi’ah and Mudar, I would have killed them. Didn’t he say to me: ‘I will kill you?’” If he had spat on me after that statement, he would have killed me. He did not live more than a day until he died in a place called Sarf. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Amr bin Ali, I told Abu Asim, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: God’s wrath is intense against whoever kills a prophet, and God’s wrath is intense against whoever bleeds the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: It spread among the people that Muhammad had been killed, so some of the Muslims said: If only we had a messenger to Abdullah bin Ubayy so he could take a guarantee of safety for us from Abu Sufyan. Some of the Companions sat down and threw their hands up, and some of the hypocrites said: If Muhammad has been killed, then return to your former religion. Anas bin An-Nadr, the uncle of Anas bin Malik, said: O people, if Muhammad has been killed, then the Lord of Muhammad has not been killed, so what will you do with life after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? Fight for what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought for, and die for what he died for. Then he said: O God, I apologize to You for what these people say, meaning the Muslims, and I disavow before You what these people, meaning the hypocrites, have brought. Then he grabbed his sword and fought until he was killed. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to the rock while calling the people. The first to recognize the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Ka’b ibn Malik. He said, “I recognized his eyes shining under the helmet, so I called out at the top of my voice: ‘O Muslims, be glad! This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ He motioned for me to be silent. A group of his companions fled to him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, blamed them for fleeing. They said, ‘O Prophet of God, we would sacrifice our fathers and mothers for you. The report came to us that you have been killed, and our hearts were terrified, so we turned back and fled. Then God Almighty revealed this verse: ‘Muhammad is no more than a messenger; other messengers have passed away before him.’ And Muhammad is the one who is absorbed in all praise, because praise is only deserved by the perfect, and praise is above praise, so it is only deserved by the one who has complete control over the matter. And God honored His Prophet and Chosen One with two names derived from His name, may He be glorified and exalted Muhammad and Ahmad, and Hassan bin Thabit says about him: Have you not seen that God sent His servant with His proof? And God is Most High and Most Glorious. And he split his name from his own to glorify him, so he is the one with the honor, Mahmoud, and this is Muhammad. God Almighty says: “If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?” And whoever turns back on his heels “will never harm God at all” but he only harms himself “and God will reward the grateful.”
3:145: 145- And no soul can die, Al-Akhfash said: The lam in the soul is transferred, its meaning is: And no soul can die, except by the permission of God, by the decree and destiny of God, and it was said: by His knowledge, and it was said: by His command, a deferred book meaning: He wrote for every soul a term that no one can change or delay, and the book is in the accusative case as a source, meaning: He wrote a book, And whoever desires the reward of this world, We give him thereof meaning: whoever desires the world by his obedience and works for it, We give him thereof what is a reward for his work, he wants We give him from it what We will by what We have decreed for him, as He said: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend Surat Al-Isra - 18, it was revealed about those who left the center on the day of Uhud seeking the spoils, And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We give him thereof, meaning he wanted the Hereafter by his work, it was said: He meant those who stood firm with their leader Abdullah bin Jubayr until They were killed. And We will reward the grateful, meaning: the faithful and obedient. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Yahya Muhammad ibn Abd God ibn Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri told us, my father told us, al-Rabi’ ibn Subaih told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Ruqashi, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever’s intention is to seek the Hereafter, God will place his wealth in his heart, gather his affairs for him, and the world will come to him reluctantly. But whoever’s intention is to seek the world, God will place poverty before his eyes, scatter his affairs, and nothing will come to him from it except what is written for him.” Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Tawbah al-Zarrad told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Idris ibn Muhammad al-Jurjani and Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mu’allim al-Harawi told us, they said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Isa al-Malini told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Hasan ibn Sufyan al-Nasawi told us, Hayyan ibn Musa and Abdullah ibn Asma’, the nephew of Juwayriyah ibn Asma’ told us, he said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Actions are but by intentions, and each person will have but what he intended. So whoever migrates for the sake of God and His Messenger, then his migration is for the sake of God and His Messenger. Whoever migrates for the sake of worldly gain or a woman to marry, then his migration is for that for which he migrated.’”
3:146: 146- The Almighty said: And how many a prophet fought with him, many devout men. Ibn Kathir read and how many, with a long vowel and a hamza on the weight of fa'il, and Abu Ja'far softened the hamza, and the others read and how many with a hamza and a shaddah on the weight of ka'in, and its meaning is: and how much, and it is the kaf of comparison attached to the interrogative ay, and the tanween did not occur in the script except in this letter specifically, and some readers stop at and how many without a nun, and most stop at a nun, his saying killed Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and the people of Basra read with a damma on the qaf, and the others read killed, so whoever reads killed is because of his saying: they did not weaken and it is impossible to describe them as not weakening after they were killed, because Saeed bin Jubair said: We have not heard that a prophet was killed in battle, and because killed is more general. Abu Ubaid said: If God Almighty praises someone who fights, then the one who was killed is included in that, and if He praises someone who was killed, then no one else is included in that, so killer is more general. Whoever reads killed has three aspects: One of them: That the killing was attributed to the Prophet alone, then the statement would be complete when he said killed, and the verse would imply the meaning: and with him were many rabbis, just as it is said: So-and-so was killed and with him was a large army, meaning: and with him. The second aspect: That the killing affected the Prophet and the usurers who were with him, and what is meant is: some of those with him. The Arabs say we killed the sons of so-and-so, but they only killed some of them, and his saying they did not weaken refers back to the rest. The third aspect: that the killing should be for the usurers only. And his saying, Many rabbis, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: large groups. Ibn Masoud said: The rabbis are thousands. Al-Kalbi said: One rabbiyyah is ten thousand. Ad-Dahhak said: One rabbiyyah is a thousand. Al-Hasan said: Jurists are scholars. It was also said: They are the followers. The rabbiyyun are the governors, and the rabbiyyun are the subjects. It was also said: It is attributed to the Lord and they are those who worship the Lord. They did not weaken, meaning they did not become cowardly, for what afflicted them in the cause of God, nor did they weaken, from jihad because of the pain of the wounds they suffered and the killing of their companions. They did not humble themselves, Muqatil said: They did not surrender or submit to their enemy. As-Suddi said: They were not humiliated. / Ata’ said: They did not humble themselves. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They did not become cowardly, but they were patient in the command of their Lord and in obeying their Prophet and in jihad against their enemy. And God loves the patient.
3:147: 147- The Almighty’s saying: And their saying was not, is in the accusative case as the predicate of was, the noun in that they said, meaning: And their saying when their Prophet was killed was not, except that they said, ‘Our Lord, forgive us our sins’ meaning: the minor ones, and our transgression in our affair’ meaning: the major ones, and plant firmly our feet, so that they do not slip, and give us victory over the disbelieving people, meaning: Why did you not do and say the same about the companions of Muhammad?
3:148: 148-So God gave them the reward of this world, victory and spoils, and the good reward of the Hereafter, wages and Paradise, and God loves the doers of good.
3:149: 149- The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, meaning: the Jews and Christians, Ali, may God be pleased with him, said, meaning: the hypocrites in their saying to the believers when they were defeated: Return to your brothers and enter their religion. They will turn you back on your heels, they will return you to your original practice of associating partners with God, and you will become losers, deceived.
3:150: 150-Then he said: Rather, God is your protector, your helper and protector of your religion, and He is the best of helpers.
3:151: 151- We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve. That is because when Abu Sufyan and the polytheists set out on the day of Uhud, heading towards Mecca, they set out until they reached part of the road, then they regretted it and said: What a bad thing we have done! We killed them until none of them remained except the fugitives. We left them. Go back and eradicate them. So when they decided to do that, God cast terror into their hearts, until they turned back from what they had intended to do. We will cast, i.e., We will cast terror and fear into the hearts of those who disbelieve. Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Amir, Al-Kisa`i, and Ya`qub read terror with a damma on the `ayn, while the others read it with a sukoon. Because they associated with God that for which He had not sent down any authority, an argument and proof, and their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers, the abode of the disbelievers.
3:152: 152- The Almighty said: And God has fulfilled His promise to you. Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions returned to Medina from Uhud, and what had befallen them had befallen them, some of his companions said: Where did this come from? And God has promised us victory. So God Almighty revealed: And God has fulfilled His promise to you with victory and triumph, that is, victory and triumph were for the Muslims at the beginning, when you were attacking them by His permission that is, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed Uhud behind his back and faced Medina and placed Aynin, which is a mountain, on his left and stationed archers on it and put Abdullah bin Jubair in charge of them, and said to them: Protect our backs, and if you see us taking spoils, do not share with us, and if you see us being killed, do not help us, and the polytheists came and began fighting, and the archers began to shoot arrows at the horses of the polytheists, and the Muslims struck them with swords, until they turned and fled, so that is what God the Almighty said when you were attacking them by His permission meaning you killed them in a terrible killing by the decree of God. Abu Ubaidah said: The sense is the eradication by killing. Until you fail means: if you are cowardly. It was said that its meaning is: when you fail, and dispute over the matter and disobey. The waw is redundant in and dispute over, meaning: until if you fail, you dispute. It was said that there is an advancement and delay in it, its meaning: until if you dispute over the matter and disobey, you fail. The meaning of dispute is disagreement. Their disagreement was that the archers disagreed when the polytheists were defeated. Some of them said: The people have been defeated, so what is our position? And they turned to the spoils. Some of them said: Do not exceed the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdullah bin Jubair remained steadfast with a small group of less than ten. When Khalid bin Al-Walid and Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl saw that, they attacked the archers and killed Abdullah bin Jubair and his companions. They turned towards the Muslims and the wind changed and became a gale after it had been pouring. The ranks of the Muslims fell apart and they mixed together and began to kill without any sign, striking each other in shock. Satan cried out that Muhammad had been killed, and that was the reason for the defeat of the Muslims. God the Almighty said: And you disobeyed meaning: the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you disobeyed his command, after He had shown you God what you love O group of Muslims of victory and spoils, among you are those who desire this world meaning: those who left the position and turned to plunder, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter meaning: those who stood firm with Abdullah bin Jubair until they were killed. Abdullah bin Masoud said: I did not feel that any of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted this world until the day of Uhud, and this verse was revealed: Then He turned you away from them meaning: He turned you back from them with defeat, to test you to examine you, and it was said: to bring down the affliction upon you, and He has pardoned you meaning He did not eradicate you after the disobedience and disobedience, and God is full of bounty to the believers.
3:153: 153- When you ascend, meaning: And He has pardoned you when you ascended fleeing. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami, al-Hasan and Qatadah read you ascend with the ta' and 'ayn open, and the well-known reading is with the ta' closed and the 'ayn broken. Ascending: walking on level ground, and climbing: rising on mountains and roofs. Abu Hatim said: It is said that you ascended if you walked in front of you, and you ascended if you climbed a mountain or something else. Al-Mubarrad said: Ascend if you went far, and both readings are correct, for on that day there were among the defeated ascending and ascending. Al-Mufaddal said: Ascended, ascended, and ascended have the same meaning. And do not turn to anyone meaning: do not deviate from the path of anyone, and do not turn to one another, and the Messenger calls you at the rear of you meaning: at the rear of you and those behind you to me, servants of God, for I am the Messenger of God, whoever turns will have Paradise, and He rewarded you, so He recompensed you, He made reward mean punishment, and its origin is in good deeds because He put it in place of reward, like the saying of God Almighty: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment, He made the good report of the punishment, and its meaning is: He made the place of the reward that you were hoping for grief upon grief. It was said: The ba’ means upon, meaning: grief upon grief, and it was said: grief connected to grief, so the first grief: what they missed of victory and booty, and the second grief: what they suffered of killing and defeat. It was said: The first grief was when Khalid bin Al-Walid looked down on them with the polytheists’ cavalry, and the second grief was when Abu Sufyan looked down on them. That was because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out that day calling the people until he reached the people of the rock. When they saw him, a man put an arrow in his bow and wanted to shoot it, so he said, I am the Messenger of God. They were happy when they found the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was happy when he saw that among his companions there were those who would resist. They began to mention the conquest and what they had missed of it, and to mention their companions who had been killed. Abu Sufyan and his companions came until they stopped at the gate of the valley. When the Muslims looked at them, this worried them and they thought that they would attack them and kill them, but this made them forget what had happened to them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “They have no right to prevail over us. O God, if you kill this group, you will not be worshipped on earth.” Then he called upon his companions and they threw stones at them until they brought them down. It was said: They upset the Messenger by disobeying his command, so God rewarded them for that upset with the upset of killing and defeat. God Almighty says: So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, of conquest and spoils, nor over what has befallen you, meaning: nor over what has befallen you of killing and defeat. And God is Acquainted with what you do.
3:154: 154- Then He sent down upon you, O group of Muslims, after the distress, security, drowsiness. That is, security. Security and safety have the same meaning. It was said that security is when the cause of fear disappears, and safety is when the cause of fear remains. The cause of fear here was present, sleeping, instead of safety. It covers a group of you. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read covers with a ta' referring to safety, and the others read it with a ya' referring to drowsiness. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He will make them feel safe on that day, but they will be overcome by drowsiness. Only those who feel safe doze, and those who are afraid will not sleep. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Abdul Rahman told us, Hussein bin Muhammad told us, Shaiban told us, Qatada told us, Anas told us that Abu Talha said: We were overcome by drowsiness while we were in our ranks on the day of Uhud. He said: My sword kept falling from my hand, so I would grab it, and it would fall, and I would grab it. Thabit said on the authority of Anas on the authority of Abu Talha, who said: I raised my head on the day of Uhud and I did not see anyone among the people except that he was leaning under his covers from drowsiness. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awam said: I saw myself with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the war became intense against us. God sent sleep upon us. By God, I hear the words of Mu’tab bin Qushair, and drowsiness overwhelms me. I hear it only as if it were a dream. They say: If we had any control over the matter, we would not have been killed here. This is what God Almighty says: It overwhelms a party of you, meaning the believers, and a party whose souls are concerned, meaning the hypocrites. It was said: God intended by this to distinguish the hypocrites from the believers, so He caused drowsiness to fall upon the believers until they felt secure, but He did not cause sleep upon the hypocrites, so they remained in fear while their souls were concerned, meaning: It caused them to worry. It is said: An important matter. They think of God other than the truth meaning: He will not support Muhammad. It was said that they thought that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed. The thought of the Age of Ignorance meaning: like the thought of the people of ignorance and polytheism. “They say: Do we have anything?” meaning: What is ours? Its wording is a question and its meaning is: denial. Of the matter of something meaning: victory. “Say: The matter is entirely God’s.” The people of Basra read it with the lam raised as the subject and its predicate in God. The others read it with the accusative as a substitute and it was said: as an attribute. They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you. They say, If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here. This is because the hypocrites said to one another: If we had had sense, we would not have gone out with Muhammad to fight the people of Mecca, and our leaders would not have been killed. And it was said: If we were on the right path, we would not have been killed here. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: They think of God other than the truth, the pre-Islamic assumption, meaning: the denial of predestination, which is their saying: If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here, “Say: If you had been in your houses, those upon whom killing has been decreed would have come forth to their places of death,” their places of death, and that God may test, and God may examine, what is in your breasts and purify, bring out and reveal, “what is in your hearts. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts,” what is in the hearts of good and evil.
3:155: 155- Those of you who turned back meaning were defeated, of you, O group of Muslims, on the day the two armies met, the group of Muslims and the group of polytheists on the day of Uhud. Most of the Muslims had been defeated and there remained with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only thirteen men, six of whom were from the Muhajireen: Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Talhah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, may God be pleased with them. The Almighty said: It was only Satan who caused them to slip meaning: he sought their slip, as it is said: I hastened someone if you sought his haste. It was also said: he made them slip, which is the sin. It was also said: azla and istazala have the same meaning. Because of some of what they had earned meaning: because of the evil of their sins. Some of them said: because of their abandonment of the position. Al-Hasan said: What they had earned was their acceptance of what Satan whispered to them of defeat. “But God has pardoned them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Forbearing.”
3:156: 156- O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved, meaning: the hypocrites Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions, and said to their brothers, in hypocrisy and disbelief, and it was said: in lineage, when they traveled through the land meaning: traveled in it for trade or other, or were on a raid meaning: raiders, plural of raider, and killed, If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed, so that God might make that meaning: their saying and their assumption, regret "anguish" in their hearts. And God gives life and causes death, and God is Seeing of what you do." Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read they work with a ya', and the others read it with a ta'.
3:157: 157- And if you are killed in the way of God or die Nafi', Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read mutam with a kasra on the meem, and the others read it with a damma. Whoever reads it with a damma is from the one who died yamout, like you say: Whoever said yaqool qult, with a damma on the qaf, and whoever reads it with a kasra is from the one who died yamout, like you say: Whoever feared yakhuf: I feared, for forgiveness from God, in the end, and mercy is better than what they accumulate, of spoils, the reading of the general public is tajamu'u with a ta', because of his saying and if you are killed, and Hafs from Asim read yajamu'un with a ya', meaning: better than what people accumulate.
3:158: 158- And if you die or are killed, you will be gathered to God, in the end.
3:159: 159- The Almighty said: "Then by the mercy of God" meaning: by the mercy of God, and "what" is a conjunction, like His saying: "Then by the fact that He broke their covenant, You were gentle with them" meaning: you made your manners easy for them, and your patience was great, and you did not rush to them in what they did on the day of Uhud, "And if you had been rude" meaning: harsh, ill-mannered, and of little patience, "hard-hearted", Al-Kalbi said: rough in speech and hard-hearted in action, "they would have dispersed from around you" meaning: they would have fled and scattered from you, it is said: you dispersed them and they dispersed, meaning they separated them and they dispersed. "So pardon them, overlook what they did on the day of Uhud, and ask forgiveness for them until I intercede for them, and consult them in the matter" meaning: extract their opinions and know what they have, from the saying of the Arabs: I bought the animal and consulted it, if you extracted its gait, and I bought honey and consulted it if you took it from Its location, and extracted it. They differed about the meaning for which God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to consult, despite his perfect mind, sound opinion, and the revelation that came down to him, and the obligation of people to obey him in what they liked and disliked. Some of them said: It is specific in meaning, that is: And consult them in what you do not have a covenant with God Almighty about. Al-Kalbi said: It means, debate them in meeting the enemy and the war plots during the invasion. Muqatil and Qatada said: God Almighty commanded that they be consulted to please their hearts, for that would make them more affectionate towards Him and remove their grudges. For if the leaders of the Arabs did not consult them in a matter, that would be difficult for them. Al-Hassan said: God Almighty knew that he did not need to consult them, but he wanted those who came after him to follow his example. Abu Tahir bin Ali bin Abdullah Al-Farsi told us: Abu Dharr Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Ali Al-Salihani told us: Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Hayyan told us: Ali bin Al-Abbas Al-Muqana’i told us: Ahmad bin Mahan told us: My father told us: Talha bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: I have never seen a man who consulted men more than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty says: So when you have decided, then rely upon God, not upon consulting them. That is, carry out God’s command, trust in Him, and seek His help. Indeed, God loves those who rely [upon Him].
3:160: 160- If God helps you, God helps you and protects you from your enemy, then none can overcome you, like the day of Badr, and if He forsakes you, He leaves you without helping you as He did with Uhud, and forsake is to refrain from support and submission to destruction, then who is there who can help you after Him, that is, after His forsake, and in God let the believers put their trust, it was said: trust means that you do not disobey God for the sake of your provision, and it was said: that you do not seek for yourself a supporter other than God, nor for your provision a treasurer other than Him, nor for your work a witness other than Him. Abu Al-Qasim Abdul Karim bin Hawazin Al-Qushayri told us, Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Shuja Al-Bazzaz told us in Baghdad, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Jaafar Al-Haym Al-Anbari told us, Muhammad bin Abi Al-Awam told us, Wahb bin Jarir told us, Hisham bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran bin Husain, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account. It was said: O Messenger of God, who are they? He said: They are those who do not cauterize, nor seek omens, nor believe in omens, and who put their trust in their Lord. Then Ukasha bin Muhsin said: O Messenger of God, ask God to make me one of them. He said: You are one of them. Then another stood up and said: O Messenger of God, ask God to make me one of them. He said: Ukasha has preceded you in that. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, Hayat ibn Shuraih told us, Bakr ibn Amr told us, Abdullah ibn Hubayrah told us that he heard Abu Tamim al-Jaishani say: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “If you were to put your trust in God as He should be put into practice, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds, which go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening with full crops.”
3:161: 161- The Almighty said: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war the verse, and Ikrimah and Muqsim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: that this verse was revealed regarding a red velvet that was lost on the day of Badr, and some people said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed about the spoils of Uhud when the archers left the post to take the spoils and said: We fear that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will say, Whoever takes something, it belongs to him, and that the spoils will not be divided as they were not divided on the day of Badr. So they left the post and fell into the spoils. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: Did I not command you not to leave the post until my order came to you? They said: We left the rest of our brothers standing. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Rather, you thought that we would take spoils and would not divide them among you. So God the Most High revealed this verse. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that it was revealed about a group of his companions who had gone astray. It was said: The powerful insisted on him asking him about the spoils, so God Almighty revealed: It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war so that he would give to some people and withhold from others, but rather he must divide it equally among them. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said: This is about revelation. He says: It is not for a prophet to conceal anything from the revelation out of desire, fear, or flattery. God the Almighty said: And it is not for a prophet to cheat. Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra, and Asim read yaghlul with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the ghayn. Its meaning is: to betray, and what is meant by it is the nation. It was said that the lam in it is transferred, meaning: the prophet would not cheat. It was also said that its meaning is: that was not thought of him and it is not appropriate for him. The others read it with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the ghayn. This has two aspects: that it is also from ghuluul, meaning: it is not for a prophet to betray, meaning: that his nation betrays him. The other aspect is that it is from iqlal, meaning: it is not for a prophet to betray, meaning that he is accused of treachery. And whoever steals will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Kalbi said: That thing will be presented to him in the Fire, then it will be said to him: Put it down and take it. So he will put it down and carry it on his back. When it reaches its place, it will fall into the Fire. Then he will be ordered to go down to it and take it out, and that was done to him. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dailami, on the authority of Abu al-Ghaith, the freed slave of Ibn Mut`i`, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Khaybar, and we did not take any gold or silver as spoils of war, except for money, clothing, and goods. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, headed towards Wadi al-Qura, and Rafa`ah ibn Zayd had given the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a black slave called Mud`am. He said: So we went out until we were in Wadi al-Qura, and while Mud`am was unloading the Messenger of God’s saddlebags, a stray arrow came and struck him and killed him. The people said: ‘May he be granted Paradise.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the cloak that he took on the day of Khaybar from the spoils was not divided, and it is burning on him.’ When the people heard that, a man came with one or two straps to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A strap of fire or two straps of fire.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Musab told us, Malik told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hayyan told us, Abu Umrah al-Ansari told us, Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani told us, “A man died on the day of Khaybar, and they mentioned him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said, ‘Pray for your companion.’ The faces of the people changed because of that, and Zayd claimed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Your companion has committed treason in the cause of God.’ So we opened his belongings and found beads of the beads of the Jews, worth two dirhams.” Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad al-Khatib al-Marwazi told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad al-Khalal told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, al-Rabi bin Sulayman told us, al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah bin al-Zubayr, on the authority of Abu Hamid al-Sa’idi, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed a man from Azd called Ibn al-Lutbiyyah to collect the zakat. When he arrived, he said: ‘This is for you and this was given to me.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the pulpit and said: ‘What is the matter with the worker whom we send to do some of our work and he says: ‘This is for you and this was given to me.’ Why doesn’t he sit in his mother’s house or his father’s house and see whether he will be given a gift or not? By the One in Whose hand is my soul, no one will take anything from it except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his neck, whether it is a camel that roars or a cow that moos or a sheep that bleats.’ Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits, then he said: ‘O God, have I conveyed the message?’” Qais bin Abi Hazim narrated on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to Yemen and said: Do not take anything without my permission, for it is embezzlement, and whoever embezzles will bring what he has embezzled on the Day of Resurrection.” It was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If you find a man who has stolen, burn his belongings and beat him. It was narrated on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, may God be pleased with him: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, and Umar burned the property of the usurper and beat him.” God Almighty said: “And whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.”
3:162: 162- Is he who pursues the pleasure of God and abandons theft like he who incurs the wrath of God, he did, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.
3:163: 163- They have degrees with God, meaning: they have degrees with God. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It means whoever pursues the pleasure of God and whoever incurs the wrath of God will have different degrees with God. For whoever pursues the pleasure of God is the great reward, and for whoever incurs the wrath of God is the painful punishment. And God is Seeing of what they do.
3:164: 164- God has conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves. It was said that he meant the Arabs because there is no tribe among the Arabs who does not have a lineage among them except Banu Tha'laba. The evidence for this is the Almighty's statement: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves. Others said: He meant all the believers. The meaning of the Almighty's statement: from among themselves is: by faith and compassion, not by lineage. The evidence for this is the Almighty's statement: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, "reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they were, and they were, before, meaning before his sending, in manifest error.
3:165: 165- Or when i.e. when a calamity befell you, at Uhud, you had suffered twice as much, at Badr, and that was because the polytheists killed seventy Muslims on the day of Uhud and the Muslims killed seventy of them at Badr and took seventy captive, you said, 'How is this?' Where did we get this killing and defeat when we are Muslims and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is among us? Say, it is from yourselves. Ubaydah al-Salmani narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: God has disliked what your people did in taking ransom from the captives, and He has commanded you to give them the choice between coming forward and having their necks struck, or taking ransom on condition that a number of them be killed. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned that to the people, and they said: O Messenger of God, our tribes and brothers, rather we will take their ransom so that we will be able to fight our enemy and a number of us will be martyred [so seventy of them were killed on the day of Uhud]. The prisoners of Badr, this is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: “Say: It is from yourselves,” meaning: by your taking the ransom and choosing to be killed, Indeed, God is over all things competent.
3:166: 166-And whatever befell you on the day the two armies met, in the form of killing, wounding, and defeat, was by permission of God, that is, by His decree and destiny, and that He might make evident the believers, that is, to distinguish, and it was said, to see.
3:167: 167- And let those who are hypocrites and were told, 'Come, fight in the cause of God' meaning: for the sake of God's religion and obedience to Him, or defend, from your families and women, and Al-Suddi said: meaning, increase the number of Muslims and remain stationed. If you do not fight, that will be a repelling and suppression of the enemy, they said, 'If we had known of fighting, we would have followed you', and they are Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions who left Uhud and they were three hundred. God the Most High said: They are nearer to disbelief that Day meaning: closer to disbelief that Day than to faith (meaning: to faith), they say with their mouths meaning: the word of faith what is not in their hearts, and God knows best what they conceal.
3:168: 168- Those who said to their brothers, in lineage not in religion, and they were the martyrs of Uhud, and sat back meaning: these people who said about jihad sat back if they had obeyed us, and turned away from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and sat in their homes "they would not have been killed. Say", to them, O Muhammad, then avert, then repel, from yourselves death if you should be truthful, caution is no substitute for destiny.
3:169: 169- The Almighty said: And never think that those who were killed in the way of God are dead the verse. It was said: It was revealed about the martyrs of Badr, who were fourteen men, eight from the Ansar and six from the Muhajireen. Others said: It was revealed about the martyrs of Uhud, who were seventy men, four of whom were from the Muhajireen: Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, Mus`ab bin Umair, Uthman bin Shamas, and Abdullah bin Jahsh, and the rest of them were from the Ansar. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hairi told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Muhammad bin Hammad told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, who said: “We asked Abdullah he is Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with them both, about this verse: ‘And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision. ’ The verse. He said: As for me, we have already asked about that, and he said: Their souls are like green birds, and it is narrated: ‘In the belly of green birds with lanterns hanging from the Throne, they roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then they return to lanterns hanging from the Throne. While they are like that, your Lord looks at them and says: Ask Me whatever you wish. They said: O Lord, how can we ask You when we roam in Paradise wherever we wish? ’ So when they saw that they would not be left without asking anything, they said: We ask You to return our souls to our bodies so that we may be killed in Your way once again. So when He saw that they would not ask anything except this, they left it.” Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Shadhan told us, Naji’i told us, Salih bin Muhammad told us, Sulayman bin Amr told us, Ismail bin Umayya told us, Ata bin Abi Rabah told us, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When your brothers were killed on the day of Uhud, God Almighty placed their souls in the bodies of green birds that go to the rivers of Paradise, eat from its fruits, and roam in Paradise wherever they wish, and take refuge in golden lamps beneath the Throne. When they saw the goodness of their resting place, their food, and their drink, and saw what honor God had prepared for them, they said: ‘If only our people knew what bliss we are in and what God has done for us, so that they would desire jihad and not neglect it.’ God Almighty said: ‘I will inform you and convey the message to your brothers.’ They rejoiced at that and were filled with good cheer. Then God Almighty revealed: ‘And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead,’ until His saying: ‘The reward of the believers will not be lost.’” I heard Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi say: I heard Al-Hasan bin Ahmad Al-Qatibi say: I heard Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Yusuf say: I heard Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Bakri say: I heard Yahya bin Habib bin Arabi say: I heard Musa bin Ibrahim say: I heard Talha bin Kharash say: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met me and said to me: O Jabir, why do I see you so broken? I said: O Messenger of God, my father was martyred and left behind children and debt. He said: Shall I not give you good report of what God met your father with? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: God Almighty did not speak to anyone except from behind a veil, but He revived your father and spoke to him directly. He said: O My servant, ask of Me and I will give it to you. He said: O Lord, revive me so that I may be killed in Your cause a second time. The Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, said: It has already been decreed from Me that they will not return. So the verse was revealed about them: ‘And do not think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead.’” Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no servant who dies, and he has goodness with God, who would like to return to the world, even though he has the world and what is in it, except the martyr, because of what he sees of the virtue of martyrdom, for he would like to return to the world and be killed once again.” Some people said: This verse was revealed about the martyrs of Bir Ma'unah, and the reason for that was what Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of his father Ishaq ibn Yasar on the authority of Al-Mughira ibn Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Harith ibn Hisham and Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm and Hamid Al-Tawil on the authority of Anas ibn Malik and others from the people of knowledge who said: Abu Bara' Amir ibn Malik ibn Ja'far, the spear player, and he was the chief of Banu Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina and presented him with a gift, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused to accept it and said, "I do not accept the gift of a polytheist, so convert to Islam if you want me to accept your gift?" Then he offered him Islam and informed him of what he would gain from it and what God has prepared for the believers, and he recited the Qur'an to him but he did not convert to Islam, and he did not stay away and said: O Muhammad, what you are calling to is good and beautiful, so if you send some men from your companions to the people of Najd to invite them to your cause, I hope that they will respond to you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I fear for them the people of Najd. Abu Al-Baraa said: I am their protector, so send them to call people to your cause. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Mundhir bin Amr, the brother of Banu Sa'idah, with seventy men from the best of the Muslims, including Al-Harith bin Al-Summah, Haram bin Milhan, Urwah bin Asma bin Al-Salt Al-Sulami, Nafi' bin Yazid bin Warqa' Al-Khuza'i, and Amir bin Fuhaira, the freed slave of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. This was in Safar of the year 4 AH, four months before the end of Uhud. They set out until they reached Bir Ma'unah, which is a piece of land between the land of Banu Amir and the lava field of Banu Sulaym. When they reached it, some of them said to each other, "Which of you will deliver the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people of this water? Haram bin Milhan said, I will." So he went out with the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Amir bin At-Tufayl in the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Haram bin Milhan said, "O people of Bir Ma'unah, I am the Messenger of God to you. I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. So believe in God and His Messenger." A man came out to him from the ruins of the Ka'bah with a spear and struck his forehead with it until it came out from the other side. He said, "Allahu Akbar! I have won, by the Lord of the Ka'bah." Then Aamer bin Tufail called for help from Banu Aamer against the Muslims, but they refused to respond to his call and said: We will not betray Abu Bara’, who has made a pact and protection for them. Then he called for help from the tribes of Banu Salim - Asiya, Ra’l and Dhakwan - and they responded to him. They went out and surrounded the people in their tents. When they saw them, they took up their swords and fought them until they killed every last one of them, except for Ka’b bin Zaid, whom they left with a little breath left. He was left among the dead, and they preferred him over them. He lived until he was killed on the day of the Trench. Among the people’s troops were Amr bin Umayya Ad-Damri and a man from the Ansar, one of Banu Amr bin Awf. Nothing alerted them to the affliction of their companions except the birds circling over the camp! They said: By God, this bird has something to do with it. They came to look and found the people covered in blood and the horses that had killed them standing still. The Ansari said to Amr bin Umayya Ad-Damri: What do you see? He said: I think we should catch up with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and inform him. The Ansari said: God is Great, but I would not prefer myself to a place where Al-Mundhir bin Amr was killed. Then he fought the people until he was killed, and they took Amr bin Umayya Ad-Damri as a prisoner. When he told them that he was from Mudar, Amir bin At-Tufayl released him, cut his forelock, and freed him from a slave he claimed was on his mother. Amr bin Umayya came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him the report. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the work of Abu Bara’. I used to hate this and fear it. Abu Bara’ heard about this, and he was upset by Amir’s concealment of him, and by what happened to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of him and his protection. Among those who were killed was Amer bin Fuhaira. Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa on the authority of his father that Amer bin Tufail used to say: Who was the man among them who, when he was killed, I saw him raised between the sky and the earth until I saw the sky below him? They said: He is Amer bin Fuhaira. Then after that, Rabi’a bin Abi Bara’ attacked Amer bin Tufail and stabbed him on his horse, killing him. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abdul Ala bin Hammad, I told Yazid bin Zari’, I told Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “That Ra’l, Dhakwan, Asiya, and Banu Lihyan sought help from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, against an enemy of theirs, so he provided them with seventy of the Ansar, whom we used to call the reciters of the Qur’an in their time. They used to collect firewood during the day and pray at night, until they were at Bir Ma’unah, and they killed them and betrayed them. When the report reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he prayed in the morning for a month against some of the Arab tribes, against Ra’l, Dhakwan, Asiya, and Banu Lihyan.” Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: We recited the Qur’an to them, then it was lifted: Convey from us to our people that we have met our Lord, and He was pleased with us and pleased us. Then it was abrogated and lifted after we had recited it for a time, and God, the Most High, revealed: And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead the verse. It was said: When the guardians of the martyrs were blessed, they would grieve for the martyrs and say: We are in the blessing and our fathers, sons and brothers are in acceptance. So God, the Most High, revealed to relieve them and inform them about the state of their dead: And never think and do not suppose “those who are killed in the way of God” Ibn Amir read killed with emphasis, and the others with emphasis dead like the dead of those who were not killed in the way of God rather they are alive with their Lord It was said: alive in religion, and it was said: in remembrance, and it was said: because they are provided for and eat and enjoy themselves like the living, and it was said: because their souls bow and prostrate every night under the throne until the Day of Resurrection. It was said: Because the martyr does not decay in the grave, nor is the earth eaten away by him. Ubayd ibn Umair said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Uhud, he passed by Mus’ab ibn Umair who had been killed. He stopped over him and prayed for him. Then he recited: ‘Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to God.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I bear witness that these are witnesses before God on the Day of Resurrection. So go to them, visit them, and greet them. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one will greet them until the Day of Resurrection except that they will respond to him. ‘They will be provided with’ from the fruits and treasures of Paradise.”
3:170: 170- "Rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty His provision and reward, and they rejoice, and are happy, for those who have not yet joined them from behind them", of their brothers whom they left alive in this world on the paths of faith and jihad, knowing that if they are martyred and join them and attain the honor they attained, they are therefore rejoicing, "that there is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve.
3:171: 171- They rejoice in the grace and favor of God and that God meaning: and that God, and Al-Kisa'i read with a kasra on the alif as a new sentence. The reward of the believers will not be lost. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus’ab told us, Malik told us, Abu al-Zinad told us, al-A’raj told us, Abu Hurayrah told us, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has guaranteed to whoever strives in His cause, and nothing drives him out of his home except striving in His cause and believing in His word, that He will admit him into Paradise or return him to the home from which he left with whatever reward and spoils he has attained.” He said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one is wounded in the cause of God - and God knows best who is wounded in His cause - except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound gushing with blood, the color of blood and the smell of musk.” Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan told us, Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Darabajirdi told us, Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri told us, Saeed told us, Muhammad ibn Ajlan told us, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The martyr does not feel the pain of death except as one of you feels the pain of a pinch.
3:172: 172- The Almighty said: Those who responded to God and the Messenger the verse, and that is because when Abu Sufyan and his companions left Uhud and reached Ar-Rawha, they regretted their departure and blamed each other and said: You did not kill Muhammad nor did you follow the young women, you killed them until there was no one left except the fugitive and you left them? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about this and wanted to terrify the enemy and show them the strength of himself and his companions, so he called his companions to go out in search of Abu Sufyan. A group of them volunteered, despite the wounds they had suffered the day before. Then Jabir ibn Abdullah spoke and said: O Messenger of God, my father left me behind with seven sisters of mine, and he said to me, O my son, it is not appropriate for me or for you to leave these women without a man among them. I am not one who would prefer you over myself in jihad with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So stay behind with your sisters. So I stayed behind with them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him permission and he went out with him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to frighten the enemy and to inform them that he had gone out in pursuit of them, so that they would think he was strong and that what had happened to them had not weakened them, so they would turn back. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talha, Al-Zubayr, Sa`d, Sa`id, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, with seventy men, may God be pleased with them, until they reached Hamra` al-Asad, which is eight miles from Medina. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said to Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr: O son of my sister, by God, your father and grandfather - meaning Abu Bakr and Al-Zubayr - are among those about whom God Almighty said: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them. Then Ma’bad Al-Khuza’i passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Hamra’ Al-Asad. The Khuza’a - Muslims and unbelievers alike - were the backbone of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Tihamah. They made a deal with him and did not hide anything that was there from him. Ma’bad was a polytheist at that time, so he said: O Muhammad, by God, what has befallen you and your companions has been hard on us, and we wish that God Almighty had spared you from them. Then he left the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he met Abu Sufyan and those with him at Al-Rawha’.
