They had decided to return to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: We have killed most of his companions and their leaders, so we will attack the rest of them, so let us finish with them. When Abu Sufyan saw Ma’bad, he said: What is behind you, O Ma’bad? He said: Muhammad has gone out with his companions to seek you out in a gathering the likes of which I have never seen before. They are burning with desire for you. Those who stayed behind on your day have gathered with him and regretted what they did, and they have a hatred for you that I have never seen before. He said: Woe to you, what are you saying? He said: By God, I do not see you departing until you see the forelocks of the horses. He said: By God, we have decided to attack them to eradicate their remnants. He said: By God, I forbid you from that. By God, what I saw made me say some verses about him: My camel was almost knocked down by the sounds as the ground was covered with the locusts. He mentioned some verses, but Abu Sufyan and those with him rejected that. A group of Abd al-Qais passed by him, so he said: Where are you going? They said: We want to go to Medina. He said: Why? They said: We want provisions. He said: Will you deliver a message from Muhammad to me and shall I load your camels with raisins for you in Ukaz tomorrow when you meet us? They said: Yes. He said: When you reach him, tell him that we have decided to march against him and his companions to eradicate their remnants. Abu Sufyan returned to Mecca, and the group passed by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) who was a lion, and they told him what Abu Sufyan had said. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned to Medina after the third time. This is what most of the commentators say. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: This verse was revealed about the Battle of Badr Al-Sughra. On the day of Uhud, when Abu Sufyan wanted to leave, he said: O Muhammad, the appointment between us and you is the season of Badr Al-Sughra next year, if you wish. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is between us and you, God willing. So when the next year came, Abu Sufyan went out with the people of Mecca until they reached Majannah in the direction of Marr Al-Dhahran. Then God cast terror into his heart, so he decided to return. He met Nu’aym bin Mas’ud Al-Ashja’i who had arrived as a pilgrim. Abu Sufyan said to him: O Nu’aym, I have made an appointment with Muhammad and his companions that we would meet at the season of Badr Al-Sughra. This is a year of drought, and nothing will suit us except a year in which we graze trees and drink milk. It has come to my mind that I should not go out to it, and I hate for Muhammad to go out and I not to go out, as that would increase their boldness, and for the successor to be from them is more beloved to me than for it to be from me. So head to Medina, delay them, and inform them that I am in a large group that they cannot handle us. I have ten camels with me that I will set aside for you on Suhayl ibn Amr's hand and he guaranteed it, he said: So Suhayl came and Na'im said to him, O Abu Yazid: Will you guarantee me these she-camels so that I may go to Muhammad and deter him? He said: Yes, so Na'im went out until he reached Medina / and found the people preparing for the appointment with Abu Sufyan, so he said: Where are you going? They said: Abu Sufyan promised us at the Battle of Badr al-Sughra that we would fight for it, you have seen a bad opinion, they came to you in your homes and settlements and none of you escaped except the fugitive, and you want to go out while they have gathered for you at the season, and by God, none of you will escape, so the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked going out, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will go out even if I am alone, as for the coward he has returned, and as for the brave he has prepared to fight, and he said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with his companions until they reached Badr al-Sughra. They began to meet the polytheists and ask them about Quraysh, saying, They have gathered against you, intending to terrify the Muslims. The believers would say, God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Until they reached Badr, which was a market place for them in the pre-Islamic era, where they would gather every year for eight days. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed at Badr waiting for Abu Sufyan, and Abu Sufyan had returned from Majannah to Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions did not meet any of the polytheists. They happened upon the market, and they had merchandise and expenses with them, so they sold and obtained two dirhams for a dirham, and they returned to Medina safe and sound. This is what God, the Most High, said: Those who responded to God and the Messenger, meaning responded. The position of those is in the accusative case, describing the believers, meaning: God does not waste the reward of the believers who responded to God and the Messenger, after the wounds have afflicted them, meaning: the wounds have afflicted them. The speech ended here, then he began and said: For those who did well among them, by obeying the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and responding to his call to war, and avoiding disobeying him, there is a great reward.
3:173: 173- Those to whom the people said and the place of those is also a noun referring back to the first those and what is meant by the people is: Na'im ibn Mas'ud, according to the statement of Mujahid and Ikrimah, so it is from the general that is intended by the specific like the statement of the Most High: Or do they envy the people meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq and a group said: What is meant by the people is the caravan of Abd al-Qays, Indeed, the people have gathered against you meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions, So fear them, so fear them and beware of them, for you have no power over them, So it increased their faith belief, certainty and strength, "And they said: God is sufficient for us" meaning: God is sufficient for us, And He is the best Disposer of affairs meaning: the one to whom matters are entrusted, fa'il with the meaning of maf'ul. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmed bin Yunus told us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Ibrahim said it when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it when they said: The people have gathered against you, so fear them. But it only increased their faith, and they said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
3:174: 174- "So they returned, so they departed, by the grace of God with good health, they did not encounter an enemy, and bounty of trade and profit, which is what they obtained in the market, no harm touched them, no harm or misfortune befell them, and they followed the pleasure of God" in obeying God and obeying His Messenger, and that is because they said: Could this be a raid? So God gave them the reward of the raid and was pleased with them, "and God is possessor of great bounty.
3:175: 175- The Almighty said: That is only Satan, meaning: the one who said to you: The people have gathered against you, so fear them, from the action of Satan, he put it in their mouths to terrify them and make them cowardly towards them, frightens his allies, meaning he frightens you with his allies, and this is also the case in the reading of Abi bin Ka’b, meaning: he frightens the believers with the disbelievers. Al-Suddi said: he magnifies his allies in their hearts so that they fear them, this is indicated by the reading of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, frightens his allies, “so do not fear them but fear Me,” in abandoning My command, if you are believers, believing in My promise, for I guarantee you victory and triumph.
3:176: 176- The Almighty said: "And let it not grieve you, Nafi' read grieve you with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the zay, and so is the entire Qur'an except for His saying The greatest terror will not grieve them", Abu Ja'far said the opposite, and they are two languages: Hzn yhzn and ahzn yhzn, except that the predominant language is Hzn yhzn, "Those who hasten into disbelief", Ad-Dahhak said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh, and someone else said: They are the hypocrites who hasten into disbelief by supporting the disbelievers. "They will never harm God at all, by their haste into disbelief, God wants not to give them a share in the Hereafter, a portion in the reward of the Hereafter, so that is how He let them down until they hastened into disbelief, and for them is a great punishment.
3:177: 177- "Indeed, those who exchanged faith for disbelief will never harm God at all, but they will only harm themselves, and they will have a painful punishment.
3:178: 178- "And let not those who disbelieve think, Hamza read this and the one after it with a taa in both, and the others read with a yaa, so whoever reads with a yaa Fal-ladheen" is in the nominative case as an agent, meaning: And let not the disbelievers think that Our respite for them is good, and whoever reads with a taa means: And do not think, O Muhammad, those who disbelieve, but it is in the accusative case as a substitute for those, "that We only grant them respite is better for themselves", and respite is delay and postponement, it is said: I lived a long and praiseworthy life and I was granted respite for a while, and from this is the saying of the Most High: "And leave me alone for a long time" Maryam - 46 meaning: a long time, then He began and said: "We only grant them respite, We grant them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment". Muqatil said: It was revealed about the polytheists of Mecca. Ata’ said: About Qurayzah and Nadir. Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah Al-Qaffal told us, Abu Mansur Ahmad bin Al-Fadl Al-Burjunjirdi told us, Abu Ahmad Bakr bin Muhammad Hamdan Al-Sayrafi told us, Muhammad bin Yunus told us, Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abi Bakra, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked, ‘Which people are best?’ He said, ‘He who lives long and does good deeds.’ It was said, ‘Which people are worst?’ He said, ‘He who lives long but does bad deeds.’”
3:179: 179- The Almighty said: "God would not leave the believers in that state you are upon until He distinguishes the wicked from the good." They differed about it, and Al-Kalbi said: Quraysh said: O Muhammad, you claim that whoever opposes you is in the Fire and God is angry with him, and that whoever follows you in your religion is in Paradise and God is pleased with him, so inform us of who believes in you and who does not believe in you, so God the Almighty revealed this verse. Al-Suddi said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My nation was presented to me in their forms in clay as they were presented to Adam, and I was informed of who would believe in me and who would disbelieve in me. This reached the hypocrites, and they said in mockery: Muhammad claims that he knows who will believe in him and who will disbelieve among those who have not yet been created, and we are with him and he does not know us. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he stood on the pulpit and praised God and thanked Him, then he said: What is the matter with people who have questioned my knowledge? Do not ask me about anything between you and the Hour except that I will inform you of it. Abdullah bin Hudhafah as-Sahmi stood up and said: Who is my father, O Messenger of God? He said: Hudhafah. Then Umar stood up and said: O Messenger of God, we are pleased with God as our Lord, Islam as our religion, the Qur’an as our leader, and you as our Prophet, so forgive us, may God forgive you. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you then desist? Then he descended from the pulpit, and God, the Most High, revealed this verse. They differed regarding the ruling on the verse and its organization. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, Ad-Dahhak, Muqatil, Al-Kalbi and most of the commentators said: The address is to the infidels and hypocrites, meaning, God would not leave the believers in the state you are in, O group of infidels and hypocrites, of infidelity and hypocrisy, until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. Some people said: The address is to the believers whom he spoke about, meaning: God would not leave you, O group of believers, in the state you are in, of confusing the believer with the hypocrite, so he returned from the report to the address. "Until he distinguishes" Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ya' and with a shaddah, and so is the one in Al-Anfal. The rest read it with a light sukoon. It is said: mazā al-shay' yamīzūhu mizāzan and mayzāhu tamayzān if he separated it and distinguished it. It is only by itself. Abu Mu'adh said: If you separate between two things, you say: mazāt mizāt. If they are things, you say: mazātuhu tamayzān. Likewise, if you make one thing into two things, you say: farqāt with a light sukoon, and from this is parting of poetry. If you make it things, you say: farqātuhu tafrīq. The meaning of the verse is until the hypocrite is distinguished from the sincere. So God distinguished the believers from the hypocrites on the day of Uhud when they showed hypocrisy and stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Qatada said: Until the infidel is distinguished from the believer through migration and jihad. Ad-Dahhak said: God would not leave the believers as you are in the loins of men and the wombs of women, O group of hypocrites and polytheists, until He separates you from those in your loins and the wombs of your women of the believers. It was also said: until He distinguishes the wicked which is the sinner from the good which is the believer, until the sins are taken from the believer by what befalls him of calamity, trial and misfortune. And God would not inform you of the unseen because no one knows the unseen except Him. But God chooses from among His messengers whom He wills so He informs him of some of the knowledge of the unseen, similar to the words of God the Most High: Knower of the unseen, and He reveals not to anyone His secrets * Except to a messenger with whom He is pleased Surat Al-Jinn, verses 26-27. Al-Saddī said: Its meaning is that God would not have informed Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the unseen, but God chose him. So believe in God and His messengers, and if you believe and fear God, then for you is a great reward.
3:180: 180- "And let not those who withhold what God has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them," meaning: And let not the misers think that miserliness is good for them, "rather it is," meaning: miserliness, "evil for them. They will be encircled by what they withheld," meaning: They will be encircled by "what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection," meaning: He will make what he withheld of zakat a snake that will encircle his neck on the Day of Resurrection, biting him from head to toe. This is the saying of Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn `Abbas, Abu Wa'il, al-Sha`bi, and al-Suddi. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Ali bin Abdullah Al-Madini, I told Hashim bin Al-Qasim, Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Dinar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Saleh Al-Samman, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever God gives wealth to, and he does not pay its zakat, his wealth will be like a bald-headed serpent with two tufts of hair on the Day of Resurrection, which will encircle him on the Day of Resurrection, then seize him by his two jaws, and say: ‘I am your wealth, I am your treasure.’ Then he recited: ‘And let not those who withhold [from God] think…’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Amr bin Hafs bin Ghayath, I told my father, I told Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Ma’rur bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: I went to him, meaning: the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, or by the One besides Whom there is no god, or as he swore, there is no man who has camels, cows, or sheep and does not pay their dues except that they will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, the largest and fattest they can be, trampling him under their hooves and butting him with their horns. Whenever the last one passes, the first one returns to him until judgment is passed between the people.” Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: The meaning of the verse is that on the Day of Resurrection a collar of fire will be placed around their necks. Mujahid said: They will be required on the Day of Resurrection to bring what they were stingy with in this world of their wealth. Atiyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This verse was revealed about the Jewish rabbis who concealed the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prophethood. He meant by miserliness concealing knowledge, as He said in Surat An-Nisa’: Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness on people and conceal what God has given them of His bounty (An-Nisa’: 37). The meaning of his statement, They will be encircled by what they hoarded on the Day of Resurrection, is: they will bear its burden and sin, as God Almighty says, And they will bear their burdens on their backs (al-An’am 6:31). And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, meaning: He is the everlasting and everlasting after His creation perishes and their possessions disappear, and they die and He inherits them. Similar to the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it (Maryam 19:40) And God is Acquainted with what you do. The people of Basra and Mecca read ya’mal with the letter ya, and the others read it with the letter ta.
3:181: 181- The Almighty said: God has heard the statement of those who said, ‘God is poor, and we are rich.’ Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: When the verse, Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan, was revealed, the Jews said: God is poor, so he borrowed from us, and we are rich. Al-Hasan mentioned that the one who said this statement was Huyayy ibn Akhtab. Akrima, Al-Suddi, Muqatil and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote with Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, to the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa’, inviting them to Islam, to establish prayer, to pay zakat and to lend God a good loan. One day, Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, entered their schoolhouse and found many Jews gathered around a man from among them called Finhas ibn Azura, who was one of their scholars, and with him was another rabbi called Ashya’. Abu Bakr said to Finhas: Fear God and become Muslim, for by God you know that Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has brought you the truth from God, which you find written in your Torah. So believe and be truthful and lend God a good loan that will admit you into Paradise and multiply your reward.” Phinehas said: O Abu Bakr, do you claim that our Lord borrows our money, and only the poor borrow from the rich? If what you say is true, then God is poor and we are rich, and He forbids you from usury and gives to us. If He were rich, He would not have given us usury. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him became angry and struck Finhas hard in the face and said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, were it not for the covenant between us, I would have struck your neck, O enemy of God. Finhas went to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and said: O Muhammad, look at what your companion did to me. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said to Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him: What made you do what you did? He said: O Messenger of God, the enemy of God said a terrible thing, claiming that God is poor and they are rich. So I became angry for the sake of God and struck him in the face. Finhas denied that, so God revealed in response to Finhas and confirming what Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him: God has certainly heard the statement of those who say, ‘God is poor, and we are rich.’ “We will write down what they said,” of slander and falsehood against God and punish them for it, and Muqatil said: We will record it for them, and Al-Waqidi said: We will order the recorders to write it down, similar to the words of God Almighty: And indeed, We are its recorders, “And their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, ‘Taste the punishment of the burning fire,’” and Hamza read li-yakatub with a damma on the ya’, and wa-qatalahum with a fatha on the lam, and wa-yaqool with a ya’, and taste the punishment of the burning fire meaning: the fire, and it means the burner, just as it is said: For them is a painful punishment, meaning: painful.
3:182: 182- That is because of what your hands have put forth, and because God is not unjust to His servants, so he is punished without sin.
3:183: 183- The Almighty said: Those who said, 'God has made a covenant with us' the verse. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf, Malik bin Al-Saif, Wahb bin Yahudah, Zaid bin Al-Tabut, Phinehas bin Azura, and Huyayy bin Akhtab. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, you claim that God, the Almighty, sent you to us as a messenger and revealed the Book to you, and that God, the Almighty, has made a covenant with us in the Torah, that we will not believe in a messenger, who claims that he came from God, until he brings us an offering that is consumed by fire, so if you bring him to us, we will believe you. He said, so God, the Almighty, revealed: Those who said, meaning: God heard the words of those who said, and the place of those is lowered in response to the first those, "God has made a covenant with us," meaning: He commanded us and instructed us in His Books not to believe in a messenger, meaning: We do not believe a messenger who claims that he came from God until he brings us an offering that is consumed by fire, so it is evidence of his truthfulness. And the offering: is everything that The servant draws closer to God Almighty through his sacrifice, charity, and good deeds. Both are derived from the verb to draw closer. Sacrifices and spoils of war were not permissible for the Children of Israel. When they offered a sacrifice or took spoils of war, a white fire would come from the sky, without smoke, and with a roar and rustle, and it would consume them and burn that sacrifice and that spoil of war. This would be a sign of acceptance. If it was not accepted, it would remain as it was. Al-Suddi said: God Almighty commanded the Children of Israel: “Whoever comes to you claiming to be a Messenger of God, do not believe him until he brings you a sacrifice that will be consumed by fire, until the Messiah and Muhammad come to you. When they come to you, believe in them, for they will come without a sacrifice.” God Almighty said, establishing the argument against them: “Say, O Muhammad, ‘O company of Jews, there have come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you said,’ of the sacrifice. ‘So why did you kill them?’” Meaning: Zachariah, John, and all the other prophets who were killed. He meant by that their ancestors, so he addressed them with that because they were satisfied with the actions of their ancestors, if you are truthful. Its meaning is to deny them despite their knowledge of your truthfulness, like killing their fathers the prophets, despite bringing sacrifices and miracles. Then he said, consoling his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace:
3:184: 184- If they deny you, then messengers were denied before you who came with clear proofs and scriptures. Ibn Amir read and with scriptures, meaning: with the written books, the singular of which is Zabur like: Messenger and Messengers, and the enlightening book, the clear and luminous.
3:185: 185- The Almighty said: Every soul, breathed, shall taste death, and in the hadith: “When God Almighty created Adam, the earth complained to its Lord about what was taken from it, so He promised to return to it what was taken from it, so there is no one but that he will be buried in the soil from which he was created.” And you will only be given your wages, you will be given the reward for your deeds, on the Day of Resurrection, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. So whoever is removed, saved and removed, from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained success, he has attained salvation and escaped fear. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion, meaning benefit and enjoyment like an axe, a pot, and a bowl, then it disappears and does not remain. Al-Hassan said: It is like the greenness of plants and the toys of girls, it has no result. Qatada said: It is an abandoned commodity that is about to disappear with its owners, so take from this commodity what you can in obedience to God, and delusion is falsehood. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty says: ‘I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man.’ And recite, if you wish, ‘No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do.’” (al-Sajdah 32:17), and that in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider can travel for a hundred years without crossing it. And recite, if you wish, ‘and an extended shade.’ (al-Waqi’ah 56:30), and the space of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it. And recite, if you wish, ‘So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire]. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion.’”
3:186: 186- You will be tested in your wealth and your lives the verse, Akrima, Muqatil, Al-Kalbi and Ibn Jurayj said: The verse was revealed about Abu Bakr and Finhas bin Azura, and that is "that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr to Finhas bin Azura, the leader of Banu Qaynuqa, to ask for support, and he wrote him a letter and said to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, do not try anything against me until you return. So Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, came wearing a sword and gave him the letter. When he read it, he said: Your Lord needs us to help him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, thought of striking him with the sword, then he remembered the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not try anything against me until you return, so he refrained, and this verse was revealed." Al-Zuhri said: It was revealed about Ka`b ibn al-Ashraf, for he used to satirize the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and insult the Muslims, and incite the polytheists against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, in his poetry, and he used to flirt with the women of the Muslims. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who will find me Ibn al-Ashraf, for he has harmed God and His Messenger? Muhammad Maslama Al-Ansari said: I am yours, O Messenger of God. I will kill him. He said: Do so if you are able to do so. Muhammad ibn Maslama returned and remained for three days, neither eating nor drinking except what he wanted. He mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he called him and said to him: Why did you stop eating and drinking? He said: O Messenger of God, I said something and I do not know whether I will fulfill it or not. He said: You only have to make the effort. He said: O Messenger of God, we must say something. He said: Say whatever you wish, for whatever you wish, you are absolved from that. So Muhammad ibn Maslama, Salkan ibn Salam, Abu Na’ila, who was Ka’b’s foster brother, Ubad ibn Bishr, Al-Harith ibn Aws, and Abu ‘Isa ibn Jubayr all gathered to kill him. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked with them to Baqi’ al-Gharqad and then directed them. He said: Go in the name of God, O God, help them. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, and that was on a moonlit night. So they came until they reached his fortress, and they suddenly brought Abu Na’ila and talked with him for a while and recited poetry, and Abu Na’ila used to recite poetry, then he said: Woe to you, O son of Ashraf, I have come to you for a need that I want to mention to you, so keep it a secret from me. He said: I will. He said: The arrival of this man in our country was a calamity, the Arabs used to us and they shot at us from one bow, and the roads were cut off from us until the children were lost and our souls were exhausted. Ka’b said: I am the son of Ashraf, but by God I told you, O son of Salamah, that the matter would come to this. Abu Na’ila said: I have companions with me and we wanted you to sell us your food and we would pledge you and give you a pledge and treat you well in that. He said: Will you pledge your children to me? He said: We are ashamed that our children would be lent and it would be said: This one is a pledge of a camel’s weight, and this one is a pledge of two camels. He said: Will you pledge your women to me? They said: How can we pledge our women to you when you are the most beautiful of the Arabs and we do not trust you, and what woman would refrain from you because of your beauty? But we will mortgage you the ring, meaning: the weapon, and you know our need for the weapon. He said: Yes, and Abu Nailah wanted him not to deny the weapon if he saw it, so he promised him that he would bring it to him. So Abu Nailah returned to his companions and told them his story. So they came until they reached his fortress at night, and Abu Nailah, who had recently been married, called out to him and jumped up from his cloak. His wife said: I hear a voice dripping with blood, and you are a warrior, and a warrior does not come down at such an hour. So he spoke to them from the top of the fortress and said: He is my brother Muhammad ibn Maslamah and my foster son Abu Nailah, and if these people found me asleep they would not wake me, and if a noble person is called to a fight at night he answers. So he went down to them and talked with them for an hour, then they said: O son of Ashraf, would you like us to walk to the old woman’s ravine and talk there for the rest of our night? He said: If you wish? They went out walking, and Abu Na'ilah said to his companions: I am going to twist his hair and smell it, so if you see me get hold of his head, then go ahead and strike him. Then he smelled his hand in the blood of his head, then he smelled his hand, and said: I have never seen a bride's perfume like tonight. He said: It is the perfume of so-and-so's mother, meaning his wife. Then he walked for an hour, then returned for a similar time until he was calm. Then he walked for an hour, then returned for a similar time, then took hold of his blood of his head until he was secure. Then he said: Strike the enemy of God. Their swords clashed against him but were of no avail. Muhammad ibn Maslamah said: I remembered a thief in my sword, so I took him, and the enemy of God cried out a cry that left no fortress around us except that a fire was lit upon him. He said: I put him in his armpit, then I leaned on him until I reached his pubis, and the enemy of God fell. Al-Harith ibn Aws was wounded in the head by one of our swords, so we went out, and our companion Al-Harith was slow to reach us and bleeding, so we stopped for him for an hour, then he came to us following our tracks, so we carried him. We brought him to the Messenger of God at the end of the night while he was standing praying. We greeted him and he came out to us. We informed him of Ka`b’s murder and brought his head to him. He spat on our companion’s wound. So we returned to our people and the morning came and the Jews feared that we would fall to the enemy of God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever you capture from the Jews, kill him. Then Muhaysa bin Mas`ud attacked Sanayna, a Jewish merchant who used to deal with them and trade with them, and killed him. Huwaysa bin Mas`ud had not converted to Islam at that time and was older than Muhaysa. When he killed him, Huwaysa began to beat him and say: “O enemy of God, you killed him. By God, there is fat in your belly from his money.” Muhaisah said: By God, if the one who ordered me to kill him had ordered me to kill you, I would have struck your neck. He said: If Muhammad had ordered you to kill me, would you have killed me? He said: Yes. He said: By God, is it strange that a religion has brought you to this? So Huwaysa converted to Islam, and God Almighty revealed concerning Ka’b: You will surely be tested “You will surely be informed.” The lam is for emphasis, and it has the meaning of an oath, and the nun is for emphasis of the oath. In your wealth with disasters, disabilities, and loss. And in your souls with diseases. It was said: with the calamities of relatives and clans. Ata’ said: They are the emigrants whose wealth and homes were taken by the polytheists and they were tortured. Al-Hasan said: It is what was imposed on them in their wealth and souls of rights, such as prayer, fasting, Hajj, jihad, and zakat. And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you meaning: the Jews and Christians, and from those who associate others with God meaning: the polytheists of the Arabs, “much harm. But if you are patient” with their harm and fear God, “then indeed that is of the matters [worthy] of determination,” of the right and best of matters. Ata’ said: Of the reality of faith.
3:187: 187- And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, [saying], 'You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it.' Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra, and Abu Bakr read with the letter ya in both of them, based on the Almighty's statement: Then they threw it behind their backs. The others read with the letter ta in them, implying the statement, Then they threw it behind their backs, meaning: they threw it away, wasted it, and stopped acting upon it, and bought with it a small price, meaning: food and bribes, so evil is that which they buy. Qatada said: This is a covenant that God Almighty took from the people of knowledge, so whoever knows something, let him teach it, and beware of concealing knowledge, for it is destruction. Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said: If it were not for what God took from the People of the Book, I would not have told you anything. Then he recited this verse: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture verse. Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi told us, Abu Muadh al-Shah ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, Abu Bakr Umar ibn Sahl ibn Ismail al-Dinawari told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Barti told us, Abu Hudhayfah Musa ibn Mas`ud told us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is asked about knowledge that he knows and conceals it will be bridled on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire. Al-Hasan bin Ammarah said: I came to Al-Zuhri after he had abandoned hadith, and I found him at his door, so I said: What if you see that you narrate to me? He said: Didn’t you know that I have abandoned hadith? I said: Either narrate to me or I will narrate to you. He said: Narrate to me. I said: Al-Hakam bin Utaybah narrated to me on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, who said: I heard Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, say: God did not take a pledge from the ignorant to learn until He took a pledge from the people of knowledge to teach. He said: So he narrated to me forty hadith.
3:188: 188-His saying: Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done the verse, Asim, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read Do not think with a ta', meaning: Do not think, O Muhammad, that those who rejoice, and the others read with a ya', Do not think that those who rejoice in their joy will save them from the punishment, Do not think that they are, Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read: with a ya' and a damma on the ba' as report about those who rejoice, meaning do not think that they are, and the others read with a ta' and a fatha on the ba', meaning: Do not think that they are, O Muhammad, and he repeated his saying Do not think that they are for emphasis, and in the wording of Abdullah bin Mas'ud Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done, do not think that they are safe from the punishment without repetition. They differed about who this verse was revealed to. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Muhammad bin Jaafar told me, Zaid bin Aslam told me, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, “That some men from the hypocrites during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to fight, they stayed behind and rejoiced at their stay behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. But when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, they apologized to him and swore and wanted to be praised for what they had not done, so the verse was revealed: ‘Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done’… Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Ibrahim bin Musa, I told Hisham, that Ibn Jurayj told them: Ibn Abi Malekah told me that Alqamah bin Waqqas told him that Marwan said to his gatekeeper: Go, O Rafi, to Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and say to him: If every person who rejoices in what he has been given and loves to be praised for what he has not done will be punished, then we will all be punished. Ibn Abbas said: What is wrong with you? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Jews and asked them about something, but they concealed it from him, so they told him something else, showing him that they had sought praise from him for what they told him about what he asked them, and they rejoiced in what they had done by concealing it. Then Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, recited: “And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture” like this until His saying: They rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done. Ikrimah said: It was revealed about Phinehas, Ash’ya, and other rabbis who rejoiced in misleading people and in people’s attribution of knowledge to them, even though they were not people of knowledge. Mujahed said: They are the Jews who were happy with people’s admiration for their changing the Book and their praise of them for it. Saeed bin Jubair said: They are the Jews who rejoiced in what God gave to the family of Abraham, and they were innocent of that. Qatada and Muqatil said: The Jews of Khaybar came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We know you and believe you, and we are of your opinion and we will support you, but that was not in their hearts. So when they left, the Muslims said to them: What did you do? They said: We know him and believe him. So the Muslims said to them: You did well, so do it. So they praised them and prayed for them, and God Almighty revealed this verse and said: They rejoice in what they have done Al-Farra’ said: in what they did, as God Almighty said: You have certainly done a thing unprecedented Maryam 19:27, meaning: I did, and they love to be praised for what they have not done, so do not think that they are safe from the punishment, and for them is a painful punishment.
3:189: 189-To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, He disposes of them as He wills, and God is over all things competent.
3:190: 190- Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, on the authority of Abu Na'im Abd al-Malik ibn al-Husayn al-Isfarayni, on the authority of Abu 'Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, on the authority of Ibn Fadil, on the authority of Hisayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abd God ibn Abbas, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abd God ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he "slept with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and saw him wake up, so he used a miswak, then performed ablution, saying: 'Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth' until he finished the surah. Then he stood up and prayed two rak'ahs, in which he prolonged the standing, bowing, and prostration. Then he turned away and slept until he blew. Then he did that three times, six rak'ahs, each time using a miswak. Then he performed ablution, then recited these verses, then he prayed the witr with three rak'ahs. Then the muezzin came to him, so he went out to pray, saying: O God, place light in my sight, light in my hearing, and light in my My tongue is light, and make light behind me and light in front of me, and make light above me and light below me. O God, give me light.” Narrated by Krayb on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and he added: O God, place light in my heart, light in my sight, light in my hearing, light to my right, and light to my left. The Almighty said: Signs for those of understanding those with intellects. Then He described them and said:
3:191: 191- Those who remember God while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, Al-Nakha'i, and Qatadah said: This is in prayer. He prays standing, and if he is unable to do so, then sitting, and if he is unable to do so, then on his side. Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Muhammad bin Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Hannad told us, Wakee’ told us, Ibrahim bin Tahman told us, Hussain Al-Mu’allim told us, Abdullah bin Buraidah told us, Imran bin Husain said, I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the prayer of the sick person, and he said: Pray standing, and if you are unable to do so, then sitting, and if you are unable to do so, then on your side. Other commentators said that he meant by it the persistence in remembrance in all circumstances because man rarely omits one of these three states, similar to it in Surat An-Nisa’: So when you have completed the prayer, remember God while standing, sitting, or [lying] on your sides (An-Nisa’: 103), and they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, and what He has created in them, so that this may guide them to the power of God and they may know that it has a Creator, Able, Planner, and Wise. Ibn ‘Awn said: Reflection removes heedlessness and creates fear in the heart, just as water creates plants, and hearts are not cleansed by sorrows, nor are they enlightened by reflection. Our Lord, that is, and they say, Our Lord, “You did not create this,” referring it back to creation, so that is why He did not say this, “in vain,” that is, in vain and playful, but rather You created it for a great matter, and falsehood is in the accusative case by removing the preposition, that is, by falsehood, Glory be to You, so save us from the punishment of the Fire.
3:192: 192- Our Lord, whoever You admit to the Fire - You have disgraced him, meaning: You have humiliated him, and it was said: You have destroyed him, and it was said: You have disgraced him, because God Almighty said: And do not disgrace My guests (Hud 11:78). If it is said: God Almighty said: The Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him (al-Tahrim 66:8), and some of the people of faith will enter the Fire, and He said: Whoever You admit to the Fire - You have disgraced him, it was said: Anas and Qatadah said that its meaning is: Whoever remains eternally in the Fire - You have disgraced him. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said that this is specific to those who do not leave it, as Anas, may God be pleased with him, narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God will admit a people to the Fire, then they will leave it. "And the wrongdoers will have no helpers.
3:193: 193- Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller, meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, and most people said. Al-Qurazi said: It means the Qur’an, so not everyone meets the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, calling to faith, meaning to faith, "Believe in your Lord, so we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remit from us our misdeeds and take us with the righteous," meaning: among the righteous.
3:194: 194- Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers, that is, through the tongues of Your messengers, and do not disgrace us, do not punish us, do not destroy us, do not disgrace us, “on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in Your promise.” If it is said: What is the meaning of their saying: Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers, when they know that God does not break His promise? It is said: Its wording is a supplication but its meaning is report, i.e., to give us what You promised us through Your messengers, meaning: So forgive us our sins and cover our misdeeds from us “and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection” to give us what You promised us through Your messengers of grace and mercy. It is said: Its meaning is, Our Lord, make us among those who deserve Your reward and give them what You promised them through the tongues of Your messengers, because they were not certain that they deserved that honor, so they asked Him to make them worthy of it. It is said: They only asked Him to hasten what He promised them of victory over the enemies. They said: We know that You do not break Your promise, but we have no patience for Your patience, so hasten their disgrace and grant us victory over them.
3:195: 195- The Almighty said: “Their Lord responded to them, ‘I will not waste’, ‘I will not nullify’, ‘the work of any worker among you’, O believers, whether male or female.’ Mujahid said: Umm Salamah said, ‘O Messenger of God, I hear God mentioning men in migration but not women.’ So God Almighty revealed this verse, ‘Some of you are from others.’ Al-Kalbi said: In religion, support, and loyalty. It was said: All of you are from Adam and Eve. Ad-Dahhak said: Your men are like your women and your women are like your men in obedience, as He said: ‘And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another.’” (al-Tawbah 9:71) And those who emigrated and were expelled from their homes and were harmed in My cause, meaning: in My obedience and religion, and they are the emigrants whom the polytheists expelled from Mecca, and fought and were killed, Ibn ‘Amir and Ibn Kathir read they were killed, with emphasis. Al-Hasan said: It means that they were cut off in battle, and the others with emphasis. Most of the reciters read: and they fought and were killed, meaning that they fought the enemy and then were killed. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read and they fought and were killed, and it has two meanings. One of them means that whoever remained of them fought, and the meaning of his statement and they were killed is that some of them were killed. The Arabs say, We killed the sons of so-and-so, but they only killed some of them. The other meaning is and they were killed, and they fought. I will surely remove from them their misdeeds and admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, a reward from God, in the accusative case, Al-Kisa’i said. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a source, meaning: I will reward them with a reward, and God has with Him the best reward.
3:196: 196- The Almighty said: Let not the free movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you, it was revealed about the polytheists, because they were living in ease and comfort, trading and enjoying themselves, so some of the believers said: The enemies of God Almighty are in what we see of goodness, while we are in hardship? So God Almighty revealed this verse: Let not the free movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you, and their striking in the land and their disposition in the lands for trade and various types of earnings, so the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but it is intended for someone else.
3:197: 197- A little enjoyment, meaning: it is a little enjoyment, and in a fleeting language and a passing pleasure, Then their abode, their destiny, is Hell, and an evil resting place, the bed.
3:198: 198- But those who feared their Lord - for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally as a provision, as a reward and recompense, from God, in the accusative case for interpretation, and it was said: He made that a provision, and what is with God is better for the righteous, of the enjoyment of this world. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah, I told Sulayman bin Bilal, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Ubayd bin Hanin, that he heard Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, say: Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: “I came and saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a drinking place, and he was on a mat with nothing between him and it, and under his head was a pillow of leather stuffed with palm fibers, and at his feet were a dried palm frond, and at his head were hanging a camel. I saw the traces of the mat on his side, so I cried. He said: What makes you cry? I said: O Messenger of God, Khosrow and Caesar are in what they are in, and you are the Messenger of God? He said: Are you not satisfied that they have this world and we have the hereafter?”
3:199: 199- The Almighty said: "And indeed, among the People of the Scripture is he who believes in God" the verse. Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Anas, and Qatadah said: It was revealed about the Negus, the king of Abyssinia, whose name was Ashamah, which in Arabic is Atiyah. When he died, Gabriel, peace be upon him, announced his death to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day he died. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: Go out and pray for your brother who died in a land other than yours, the Negus. So he went to Al-Baqi' and was shown the land of Abyssinia. He saw the bed of the Negus and prayed over him and said four Takbirs and asked for forgiveness for him. The hypocrites said: Look at this man praying over an Abyssinian Christian foreigner whom he had never seen and who was not of his religion. So God, the Almighty, revealed this verse. Ata’ said: It was revealed about the people of Najran, forty men [from Banu Harith bin Ka’b], thirty-two from the land of Abyssinia and eight from the Romans, who were of the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him, so they believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Salam and his companions. Mujahid said: It was revealed about all the believers among the People of the Book: And indeed, among the People of the Book is he who believes in God, “and what has been revealed to you,” meaning the Qur’an, and what has been revealed to them, meaning the Torah and the Gospel, humble before God, submissive and humble before God, not exchanging the verses of God for a small price, meaning: they do not distort their books nor conceal the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the sake of leadership and food, as other Jewish leaders did, “those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, God is swift in account.”
3:200: 200- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, be patient and steadfast and remain steadfast. Al-Hasan said: Be patient with your religion and do not abandon it for hardship or ease. Qatada said: Be patient in obeying God. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil bin Sulayman said: According to the command of God. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: To perform the duties of God Almighty. Zaid bin Aslam said: To fight in jihad. Al-Kalbi said: On the affliction, and they were patient meaning: the infidels, and they were stationed meaning: the polytheists. Abu Ubaidah said: That is, they persisted and were steadfast. “Rabt” means tightening. The origin of ribat is that these people tie their horses, and those people their horses. Then it was said: That is for every resident in a border area who defends those behind him, even if he does not have a mount. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abdullah bin Munir, I heard Abu Al-Nadr, I told Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl bin Saad Al-Saidi, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A day’s guarding in the way of God is better than the world and everything in it, and the place of one of your whips in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it, and the soul that a servant takes in the way of God, or the morning, is better than the world and everything in it.” Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni told us, Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sharik al-Shafi’i told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jurabadhi told us, Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Shuraih told me, on the authority of Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Shurahbil ibn al-Samat, on the authority of Salman al-Khair, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever guards the land for a day and a night in the way of God will have the reward of fasting a month of residence. Whoever dies guarding the land will have the same reward, and he will be provided with provision, and he will be safe from the tribulations.” Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman said: There was no conquest in the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which one would be stationed, but rather it was waiting for the prayer after the prayer. The evidence for this interpretation is what Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Az-Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of al-`Ala` ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Shall I not tell you of that by which God erases sins and raises ranks? Performing ablution perfectly despite the difficulties, taking many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer. That is stationing, that is stationing.” And fear God that you may succeed. Some of the masters of the language said: Be patient in the face of blessings, be patient in the face of hardship and distress, and remain steadfast in the home of enemies, and fear the God of the earth and the heavens that you may succeed in the eternal home.
4:1: 1- The Almighty said: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul, meaning: Adam, peace be upon him, and created from it its mate, meaning: Eve, And He spread from them, spread and showed, many men and women, and fear God, through whom you ask one another, meaning: you ask one another, and the people of Kufa read with a light sin, deleting one of the two ta’s, like the Almighty’s saying: And do not cooperate, “and the wombs,” the reading of the general public with the accusative, meaning: and fear the wombs lest you sever them, and Hamza read with the genitive, meaning: through Him and the wombs, as it is said: I asked you by God and the wombs, and the first reading is more eloquent because the Arabs hardly coordinate an apparent with a hidden except by repeating the genitive and saying: I passed by him and Zayd, except that it is permissible with its scarcity, Indeed, God is ever, over you, a Watcher, meaning: a Preserver.
4:2: 2- The Almighty said: And give the orphans their property. Muqatil al-Kalbi said: "It was revealed about a man from Ghatafan who had a lot of money for his orphan nephew. When the orphan reached puberty, he asked for the money, but his uncle refused him. They brought their case to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed. When the uncle heard it, he said: We obey God and we obey the Messenger. We seek refuge in God from the great sin. So he gave him his money. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever protects himself from the greed of his soul and obeys his Lord in this way, then his home, meaning: his paradise, will be lawful for him. When the young man took his money, he spent it in the way of God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The reward is established, but the burden remains. They said: How does the burden remain? He said: The reward is established for the boy, but the burden remains for his father." His saying, And give is addressed to the guardians and trustees, and orphans: the plural of orphan, and orphan: the name of a young person who has no father or grandfather, and the money is only given to them after reaching puberty, and he called them orphans here in the sense that they were orphans. And do not exchange meaning: do not replace the bad with the good meaning: their money that is forbidden to you with the permissible money from yours. They differed about this exchange. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Nakha’i and Al-Suddi said: The guardians of the orphans used to take the good money from the orphan and replace it with the bad. Perhaps one of them would take a fat sheep from the orphan’s money and replace it with a thin one, and take a good dirham and replace it with a fake one, and say: A dirham for a dirham. So they were forbidden from doing that. It was said: The people of the Age of Ignorance did not inherit the elderly and children, and the eldest would take the inheritance, so his share of the inheritance was good, and what he took was bad. Mujahid said: Do not rush into unlawful sustenance before the lawful comes to you. And do not consume their wealth with your wealth, meaning: with your wealth, as God Almighty says: Who are my helpers for God? meaning: with God, Indeed, it was a great sin. meaning: a great transgression.
4:3: 3-And the Almighty’s saying: And if you fear that you will not be just toward the orphan girls, then marry those that please you of [other] women, two or three or four. The verse: They differed in their interpretation. Some of them said: Its meaning is that if you fear, O guardians of the orphans, that you will not be just toward them when you marry them, then marry others of the strangers, two or three or four. It was narrated to us by Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi, on the authority of Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail, on the authority of Abu Al-Yaman, on the authority of Shu`ayb, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: Urwah bin Al-Zubayr used to narrate that he asked Aisha, may God be pleased with her, And if you fear that you will not be able to deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry women of your choice. She said: She is an orphan who is in the care of her guardian, and he desires her beauty and wealth and wants to marry her at a rate lower than the norm of her wives, so they were forbidden from marrying them unless they were able to deal justly with them in completing the dowry, and they were ordered to marry women other than them. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: Then the people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a fatwa, so God, the Most High, revealed: “And they ask you concerning women. Say, ‘God gives you a fatwa concerning them. ’” until His saying, And you desire to marry them. So God, the Most High, explained in this verse that if the orphan girl was beautiful or wealthy, they would desire to marry her and they would not include her in her norm of completing the dowry, and if She was undesirable because of her lack of money and beauty, so they left her and sought other women. He said: Just as they leave her when they want her, they have no right to marry her if they want her unless they give her the fullest dowry and give her her rights. Al-Hasan said: There was a man from the people of Medina who had orphans among whom there was one whom he was permitted to marry, so he married her for her wealth, but she did not please him, out of dislike for a stranger to enter and share her wealth with him. Then he treated her badly and waited for her to die so that he could inherit her. God Almighty condemned that, and God revealed this verse. Ikrimah said: A man from Quraysh would marry ten women or more, and if he became destitute of the means to provide for his wives, he would turn to the orphan in his care and spend on him. So it was said to them: Do not exceed four, so that you will not need to take the money of the orphans. This is the narration of Tawus on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Some of them said: They were reluctant to deal with the orphans’ money and were lenient with women, so they would marry whomever they wanted, and sometimes they were just and sometimes they were not just. So when God the Most High revealed about the orphans’ money, And give the orphans their property, He revealed this verse, And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphans, meaning that just as you feared that you will not deal justly with the orphans, so too were they afraid that you will not deal justly with the women, so do not marry more than you can fulfill their rights, because women are like orphans in weakness. This is the saying of Saeed bin Jubayr, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi. Then He permitted marrying four women, saying: “Then marry such women as seem good to you, two or three or four. But if you fear that you will not be just” with them, then one. Mujahid said: Its meaning is that if you are reluctant to take care of the orphans and their money out of faith, then likewise were reluctant to commit adultery, so marry lawful women in a good marriage. Then He explained to them a number, and they would marry whomever they wanted without Number, the Almighty said: Then marry such women as seem good to you meaning: whoever seems good, as the Almighty said: And the heaven and He who constructed it Ash-Shams 5, meaning: And who constructed it? “Pharaoh said: And what is the Lord of the worlds?” Ash-Shu’ara 23. The Arabs place and what in place of each other, as the Almighty said: And among them is he who walks on his bellies, and among them is he who walks on two legs An-Nur 45. And good means: It is permissible for you to marry two, three, or four women, in derivation from two, three, or four, and therefore they are not declined. And the waw means or, for choice, as the Almighty said: That you stand before God in pairs and singly Saba 46: Those with wings, two, three, or four Ghafir 1. This is a consensus that no one from the nation is permitted to have more than four wives, and the increase was from the characteristics of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one from the nation shared it with him. It was narrated that “Qais bin Al-Harith had eight wives, so when this verse was revealed, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I divorced four and kept four. I said to the woman who had not given birth, ‘So-and-so, go away,’ and to the woman who had given birth, ‘So-and-so, come back.’” It was narrated that “Ghailan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi converted to Islam and he had ten wives, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Keep four and leave the rest.” If a free man marries four free women, it is permissible. As for a slave, it is not permissible for him to marry more than two women according to most scholars. Abdul Wahhab bin Ahmad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman, the freed slave of Abu Talhah, on the authority of Sulayman bin Yasar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he said: A slave may marry two women and divorce them twice, and a female slave must observe the waiting period of two menstrual cycles. If she does not menstruate, then two months or a month and a half. Rabi’ah said: It is permissible for a slave to marry four women, just like a free man. If you fear, or it was said: if you know, that you will not be just, between the four wives, then marry one, meaning: marry one. Abu Ja`far read one in the nominative case, or what your right hands possess, meaning concubines, who are not required to have the same rights as free women, nor are they entitled to a share, nor are their numbers restricted. The mention of oaths is an explanation, meaning: or what you possess. Some of the scholars of meaning said: or what your right hands possess, meaning: what your shares are enforced in, making it an oath of oath, not an oath of injury. That is closer, “that you do not deviate,” meaning: do not be unjust or inclined. It is said: a family scale, meaning: unjust and inclined. This is the saying of most of the commentators. Mujahid said: that you do not go astray. Al-Farra’ said: that you do not exceed what God has imposed upon you. The root of ‘awl is to exceed, and from it is the ‘awl of the obligatory duties. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: that your children do not become many, and no one said that it is only said from the multitude of children: ‘a’ala ya’il ‘iyala, if his children become many. Abu Hatim said: Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, was more knowledgeable. In the language of the Arabs, it is perhaps a language. It is said that it is the language of Himyar. Talha bin Masraf read that you do not be dependent, and it is an argument for the statement of Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him.
4:4: 4- And give the women their dowries as a free gift. Al-Kalbi and Mujahid said: This address is to the guardians, because if the woman's guardian married her off, if she was with them in the clan, he would not give her from her dowry, little or much. If her husband was a stranger, they would carry her to him on a camel and would not give her from her dowry other than that. So God forbade them from that and commanded them to give the right to its people. Al-Hadrami said: The guardians of women would give this man his sister on condition that the other would give him his sister, and there was no dowry between them. They forbade that and ordered that the dowry be named in the contract. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik ibn Nafi`, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade shighar. Al-Shighar: is when a man marries his daughter on the condition that another man marries his daughter, and there is no dowry between them. Others said: The address is to the husbands who were commanded to give their wives the dowry, and this is more correct because the address before was to the married couple, and the charities: the dowries, the singular of which is charities gift. Qatada said: an obligation, and Ibn Jurayj said: a named obligation, Abu Ubaidah said: and the gift can only be named and known, and Al-Kalbi said: a gift and a donation, and Abu Ubaidah said: willingly, and Al-Zajjaj said: as a gift. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Yusuf told us, Al-Layth told us, Yazid bin Abi Habib told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Khair, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The conditions that are most deserving of being fulfilled are those by which you make private parts lawful. “If they give up willingly to you anything of it,” meaning: If their souls are willing to give up anything of it, then they give it to you. So the action was transferred from the souls to their owners, so the soul was explained, and that is the definition of the soul, as God Almighty said: And he was straitened by them (Hud 11:77). Al-Ankabut -33 And be refreshed Maryam 026 It was said: Its wording is one and its meaning is plural, So eat it with pleasure and enjoyment, palatable and good. It is said that hana in food is yanha with the opening of the nun in the past tense and the breaking of it in the rest. It was said: hani is the good and palatable that lacks nothing, and mari’ is the praiseworthy outcome, complete digestion that does not harm. Abu Ja’far read hani’an mari’an with a shaddah on the ya in both of them without a hamza, and likewise bari, “bariyun,” bariyyun, and kahiyyah, and the others use a hamza on it.
4:5: 5- The Almighty said: And do not give the foolish your property which God has made a means of support for you. They differed about these foolish people. Some people said: They are women. Ad-Dahhak said: Women are among the most foolish of the foolish. Mujahid said: He forbade men from giving their money to women while they are foolish, whether they are wives, daughters or mothers. Others said: They are children. Az-Zuhri said: He says, do not give your foolish child your property which is your means of support after God the Almighty, lest he spoil him. Some of them said: They are women and children. Al-Hasan said: They are your foolish wife and your foolish son. Ibn Abbas said: Do not take your property which God has given you and made for you a livelihood and give it to your wife or children so that they are the ones who support you, then look at what is in their hands. Rather, keep your property and fix it and be the one who spends on them in their livelihood and provision. Al-Kalbi said: If a man knows that his wife is foolish and corrupt and His son is a fool and a corrupt person, so he should not give either of them power over his money and corrupt it. Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah said: It is the orphan’s money as it is with you, meaning do not give it to him and spend on him until he reaches adulthood. He only added to the guardians and said: your money because they are its support and its managers. The foolish person whose guardian is not allowed to give him his money is the one who deserves to be placed under guardianship, and that is if he is a spendthrift with his money or corrupts his religion. So the Most High said: And do not give to the foolish meaning: those who are ignorant of the right place, your money which God has made a means of support for you. Ibn Amir recited qayman without an alif, while others recited qiyman, which originally was qawwaman, but the waw was changed to a ya because of the kasra of what preceded it. It is the essence of the matter and that by which the matter is based. Here he meant the basis of your livelihood by which you live. Ad-Dahhak said: By it the Hajj, jihad, and righteous deeds are established, and by it the necks are freed from the Fire. And provide for them therein/meaning: feed them, and clothe them, for those whose care and maintenance you are obligated to provide for. He said therein and did not say: from it, because he meant: make provision for them therein, for provision from God is a gift without limit, and from the servants it is a temporary, limited procedure. And speak to them a kind word is a beautiful phrase. Ata’ said: If you win, I will give you, and if you gain, I will make a share for you. It was said: It is a supplication. Ibn Zayd said: If he is not one of those whose maintenance you are obligated to provide for, say to him: May God keep you and us healthy, may God bless you. It was said: A gentle word that will please their souls.
4:6: 6- The Almighty said: And test the orphans, the verse was revealed about Thabit bin Rifaa and his uncle, because Rifaa died and left his son Thabit who was young, so his uncle came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: My nephew is an orphan in my care, so what is permissible for me from his money and when should I give him his money? So God Almighty revealed this verse And test the orphans Test them in their minds, religion and their ability to keep their money, until they reach the age of marriage, meaning: the age of men and women, and if you perceive, you see, in them sound judgment, the commentators said that it means: intelligence, righteousness in religion, keeping money and knowledge of what is good for it. Saeed bin Jubair, Mujahid and Al-Sha'bi said: His money should not be given to him even if he is an old man until you perceive that he has reached sound judgment. The test varies according to their circumstances. If he is someone who deals in the market, the guardian should give him a small amount of money and look into his dealings. If he is someone who does not deal in the market, he should test him in his household expenses, spending on his slaves and his wages. The woman should be tested in the matter of her home, preserving her belongings, spinning and spinning. If he sees his good management and his dealings in matters repeatedly, his heart will be overcome by his wisdom, then the money should be given to him. Know that God Almighty has made the removal of guardianship from a minor and the permissibility of giving money to him conditional on two things: reaching puberty and maturity. Puberty occurs with one of four things, two of which are shared by men and women, and two of which are specific to women: What men and women share is one of them: age, and the second is wet dreams. As for age, if the newborn completes fifteen years, he is deemed to have reached puberty, whether he is a boy or a girl, because Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told me, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told me, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told me, Al-Rabi’ told me, Al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Uyaynah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I was presented to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Uhud, when I was fourteen years old, and he rejected me. Then I was presented to him in the year of the Trench, when I was fifteen years old, and he approved me. Nafi’ said: So I told this hadith to Omar bin Abdul Aziz, and he said: This is a difference between fighting and offspring, and he wrote that the fifteen-year-old should be assigned to fighting, and the one who had not reached that age should be assigned to offspring. This is the opinion of most scholars. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said: A girl reaches puberty when she reaches the age of seventeen, and a boy reaches puberty when he reaches the age of eighteen. As for wet dreams, the emission of semen, whether it was due to a wet dream, intercourse, or something else, benefited me. If I find that after completing nine years of age, whichever of the two, it is ruled that he has reached puberty, based on the Almighty’s saying: And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Muadh regarding the jizya when he sent him to Yemen: Take a dinar from every adult. As for pubic hair: which is the growth of coarse hair around the vulva: it is puberty in the children of polytheists, as it was narrated on the authority of Atiyah al-Qurazi, who said: I was among the captives of Qurayzah, and they would look and whoever had hair growing would be killed, and whoever had not grown hair would not be killed, so I was among those who had not grown hair. Is this considered puberty in the children of Muslims? There are two opinions on this, one of them: It is puberty like the children of infidels, and the second: It is not puberty because it is possible to trace the births of Muslims by referring to their fathers, but in the case of infidels, their births are not traced, and the word of their fathers is not accepted in this case because of their infidelity, so the sprouting, which is a sign of puberty, is considered puberty in their case. As for what is specific to women: menstruation and pregnancy. If a woman menstruates after completing nine years, she is deemed to have reached puberty. Likewise, if she gives birth, she is deemed to have reached puberty six months before giving birth, because that is the shortest period of pregnancy.
