That is, take Him as a disposer of affairs, and God is sufficient as a disposer of affairs and a supporter.
4:82: 82- The Almighty’s saying: Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an? meaning: Do they not think about the Qur’an? Contemplation is looking at the end of the matter, and contemplating everything is its end. Had it been from other than God, they would have found within it much discrepancy, meaning much disparity and contradiction, as Ibn Abbas said. It was said: They would have found within it, meaning: in the information about the unseen, what was and what will be, much discrepancy. Do they not think about it and know - by the absence of contradiction in it and the truth of what it informs - that it is the speech of God Almighty, because what is not from God is not free from contradiction and difference.
4:83: 83- The Almighty said: And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it, that is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to send out raiding parties, and when they were victorious or defeated, the hypocrites would rush to inquire about their situation, and they would spread it and talk about it before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did /thus weakening the hearts of the believers. So God Almighty revealed: And when there comes to them meaning: the hypocrites information about security meaning: conquest and spoils or fear killing and defeat they broadcast it they spread it and diffuse it, and if they had referred it back to the Messenger meaning: if they had not told it until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the one who told it and to those in authority among them meaning: those with opinion among the Companions such as Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali, may God be pleased with them, then those who extract it from them would have known about it meaning: they extract it and they are the scholars, meaning: they knew what should be concealed and what should be divulged. And deduction means extraction. It is said: To extract water means to extract it. Ikrimah said: They extract it, meaning: they are keen on it and ask about it. Ad-Dahhak said: They follow it, meaning those who heard that report from the believers and the hypocrites. If they had referred it back to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those with opinion and knowledge, those who extract it from them would have known it, meaning they would have loved to know it as it really is. And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, all of you, except a few. If it is said: How did He exclude the few, and had it not been for His grace, all would have followed Satan? It is said: It goes back to what came before it. It is said: Its meaning is that they spread it out except for a few who did not divulge it. By the few he meant the believers. This is the statement of Al-Kalbi and the choice of Al-Farra’. He said: Because if knowledge of the secret is revealed, its knowledge is derived and others, and divulging it may be in some and not others. It is said: Because those who deduce it from among them knew it except a few. Then His statement: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, is a complete statement. It was said: God’s grace is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur’an. He says, If it were not for that, you would have followed Satan, except for a few. They are people who were guided before the coming of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the revelation of the Qur’an, such as Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Waraqa ibn Nawfal, and a group other than them. The verse is evidence of the permissibility of analogy, as some knowledge is attained through recitation and narration, which is the text, and some knowledge is attained through deduction, which is analogy to the meanings contained in the texts.
4:84: 84- The Almighty said: So fight in the cause of God, you are not charged except with yourself, and that is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made an appointment with Abu Sufyan after the Battle of Uhud during the season of Badr Al-Sughra in Dhul-Qi'dah. When the appointed time came, he called the people to go out, but some of them disliked him, so God Almighty revealed: So fight in the cause of God, you are not charged except with yourself, meaning: Do not abandon jihad against the enemy and victory for the weak believers, even if you are alone, for God has promised you victory and has rebuked them for abandoning the fight. The fa' of the Almighty's saying: So fight is an answer to His saying: And whoever fights in the cause of God and is killed or is victorious, We will give him a great reward, so he fought, and urged the believers, to fight, meaning he urged them to jihad and encouraged them to receive the reward, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with seventy riders, and God spared them from fighting, so He, may He be glorified and exalted, said: Perhaps God, meaning: perhaps God, will restrain the violence of those who disbelieve, meaning: the fighting of those who disbelieved, the polytheists, and perhaps from God Obligatory, And God is more severe in punishment, meaning: more powerful and greater in power, and more severe in punishment, meaning: more severe in punishment.
4:85: 85- The Almighty said: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it, and whoever intercedes with an evil intercession will have a share of it, meaning: a share of it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Good intercession is reconciliation between people, and evil intercession is spreading gossip among people. It was said: Good intercession is saying good things about people, which brings reward and goodness, and bad intercession is backbiting and saying bad things about people, which brings evil. His saying, He is responsible for it means: for its burden. Mujahid said: It is the intercession of people for one another, and the intercessor is rewarded for his intercession even if he does not intercede. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Burdah, my grandfather Abu Burdah told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Musa, may God be pleased with him, who said: When a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking or seeking something, he would turn his face towards us and say: Intercede so that you may be rewarded, so that God may decree through the tongue of His Prophet what He wills. God Almighty says: And God is ever watchful over all things. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Metaphorically powerful. The poet said: And I held a grudge against him and was hateful of his wrongdoing. Mujahed said: A witness. Qatada said: A guardian. It was said: Its meaning is that it provides sustenance to every animal, meaning: it provides sustenance to it. It was mentioned in the hadith: It is enough of a sin for a person to neglect those whom he provides for and sustains.
4:86: 86- The Almighty said: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet in return with one better than it, or return it equally. Greeting: is a prayer for life, and what is meant by greeting here is peace. He says: If a Muslim greets you, respond with one better than it, or return it as he greeted you. So if he says: Peace be upon you, then say: And upon you be peace and the mercy of God. And if he says: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God, then say: And upon you be peace and the mercy of God and His blessings. So if he says: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings, then return the same. It was narrated that a man greeted Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings, then he added something, so Ibn Abbas said: Indeed, peace ends with blessing. It was narrated on the authority of Imran bin Husayn: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Peace be upon you.’ He responded to him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Ten.’ Then another came and said: ‘Peace be upon you and God’s mercy.’ He responded to him, and he sat down. He said: ‘Twenty.’ Then another came and said: ‘Peace be upon you and God’s mercy and blessings.’ He responded to him, and he said: ‘Thirty.’” Know that peace is a Sunnah and returning peace is an obligation. It is an obligation of sufficiency. Likewise, peace is a Sunnah of sufficiency. If one person from a group greets, it is sufficient in the Sunnah. If one person greets a group and one of them responds, the obligation is dropped from all of them. Imam Abu Ali Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Qadi told us, I told Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi, I told Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Omar bin Hafs Al-Tajir, I told Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Omar bin Bakir Al-Kufi, I told Wakee’, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not guide you to something that, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread peace among yourselves.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Ibn Ismail told us, Qutaybah told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Abi Al-Khair, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that a man asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Which Islam is best? He said: That you feed the poor and greet those you know and those you do not know. The meaning of his saying: Which Islam is best, he means which characteristics of Islam are best. It was said: Then greet them with something better than it, meaning if the one who surrendered was a Muslim, or return it with something similar if he was not a Muslim. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When one of the Jews greets you, he is only saying, ‘Death be upon you,’ so say, ‘Upon you.’ The Almighty says: Indeed, God is ever, over all things, a Reckoner. That is, over everything, whether returning a greeting in kind or better, a Reckoner, that is, a Rewarder. Mujahid said: a Guardian. Abu Ubaidah said: sufficient. It is said: Hasaba Hada meaning: it is sufficient for me.
4:87: 87- The Almighty said: "God, there is no god but He. He will surely gather you together." The lam is the lam of the oath, meaning: By God, He will surely gather you in death and in the graves, until the Day of Resurrection. The Resurrection was called the Resurrection because people rise from their graves. God the Almighty said: On the Day when they emerge from the graves quickly. Al-Ma'arij - 43. It was said: Because they rise to the reckoning. God the Almighty said: On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds. Al-Mutaffifin - 6. And who is more truthful than God in speech? That is, in word and promise. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read more truthful. And every silent sad after it is a dal with a nasalized zay.
4:88: 88- Why are you divided into two groups regarding the hypocrites? They differed about the reason for its revelation. Some people said: It was revealed about the hypocrites who stayed behind on the day of Uhud. When they returned, some of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Kill them, for they are hypocrites. Some of them said: Pardon them, for they spoke about Islam. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abu Al-Walid, I told Shu’bah, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, he said: I heard Abdullah bin Yazid narrating on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, he said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Uhud, some of those who went out with him returned, and the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were two groups, one group saying we will fight them and the other group saying we will not fight them, so this verse was revealed: ‘What is the matter with you that you are two groups concerning the hypocrites while God has made them fall back for what they have earned?’ He said: It is good and removes sins as fire removes impurities from silver.” Mujahid said: A group of people went to Medina and converted to Islam, then they apostatized and asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to go to Mecca to bring their goods to trade in. So they went out and stayed in Mecca. The Muslims differed about them. Some said: They are hypocrites, and others said: They are believers. Some of them said: It was revealed about some people from Quraysh who came to Medina and converted to Islam, then regretted that, so they left as if they were taking a walk until they were far from Medina. They wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: We are still on the same faith as we left you, but we have been to Medina and long for our land. Then they went out on their trade towards Ash-Sham, and this reached the Muslims, so some of them said: We will go out to them and kill them and take what they have because they have abandoned our religion. A group said: How can you kill people who are on your religion if they do not leave their homes? This was in the eyes of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was silent and did not forbid either group, so this verse was revealed. Some of them said: They are people who converted to Islam in Mecca but did not emigrate and they supported the polytheists, so the following was revealed: What is the matter with you, O group of believers, that you are divided into two parties regarding the hypocrites? That is, you have become two parties among them, that is, two groups. And God has turned them back That is, He has reversed them and returned them to disbelief for what they have earned “for their impure deeds.” Do you want to guide That is, to direct those whom God has led astray? It was said: With us, do you say that these are guided and God has led them astray? And he whom God leads astray That is, he whom God leads astray from guidance, you will not find for him a way That is, a path to the truth.
4:89: 89- The Almighty said: And they wish, they wished, meaning those who turned back from the religion wished that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be equal, in disbelief, and His saying so you would be did not mean the answer to the wish because the answer to the wish with the letter fa is accusative, rather He meant the sequence, meaning: They wish that you would disbelieve and they wish that you would be equal, like His saying: And they wish that you would compromise so they would compromise (al-Qalam 68:9) meaning: They wish that you would compromise and they wish that you would compromise. So do not take from them allies, He forbade befriending them, until they emigrate in the cause of God, with you. Ikrimah said: It is another migration, and migration has three aspects: The migration of the believers at the beginning of Islam, which is the Almighty’s saying: For the poor emigrants (al-Hashr 59:8) and His saying: And whoever emigrates from his home to God and His Messenger (al-Nisa 4:100), and similar verses. The migration of al-Munafiqun 63:which is going out in the way of God with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, patiently and seeking reward [as narrated here], he was prevented from befriending them until they emigrate in the way of God. The migration of the rest of the believers, which is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The emigrant is the one who emigrates from what God has forbidden. God Almighty says: But if they turn away, that is, turn away from monotheism and migration, then seize them, that is, take them as prisoners, and from this the prisoner is called akhidh, “and kill them wherever you find them,” in the sacred precincts and outside, and do not take from among them any protector or helper, then He excepted a group of them and said:
4:90: 90- Except those who reach a people This exception refers to killing, not to friendship, because friendship with the infidels and hypocrites is not permissible under any circumstances. The meaning of reach is: they are related to them, connected to them, and enter into their alliance and neighborhood. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: They mean and seek refuge with a people, between you and them is a covenant meaning: a pact, and they are the Aslamis. This is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a treaty with Hilal bin Uwaimir Al-Aslami before he left for Mecca on the condition that he would not help him or help anyone against him. Whoever reaches Hilal from his people or others and seeks refuge with him will have the same neighborliness as Hilal. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He meant by the people between you and them is a covenant, the Banu Bakr bin Zaid bin Manat, who were in a peace and truce. Muqatil said: They are Khuza'ah. And His statement: Or they come to you means: they connect with a people who have come to you, their chests are constricted meaning: their chests are narrow. Al-Hasan and Ya’qub read regret in the accusative case with the definite article, meaning: their chests are narrow, [meaning the people who came to you, who are Banu Mudlij, they had pledged not to fight the Muslims and pledged with Quraysh not to fight them, constricted: their chests are constricted], that they fight you meaning: from fighting you because of the covenant between you, or fight their people, meaning: whoever among them believes, and it is possible that its meaning is that they do not fight you with their people nor fight their people with you, meaning that Quraysh’s chests are constricted because of that. Some of them said: Or it has the meaning of the letter waw, as if he is saying: To a people between you and them there is a covenant or they came to you with their hearts restrained, meaning: their hearts restrained from fighting you and fighting with you, and they are the people of Hilal the Muslims and Banu Bakr. God Almighty forbade fighting these apostates if they connected with people of a covenant with the Muslims, because whoever joins a people with a covenant is subject to their rule regarding the preservation of blood. And the Almighty’s saying: And if God had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you, mentions His favor upon the Muslims by restraining the aggression of those with whom He had made a treaty. He says: Their hearts were narrowed from fighting you because of the terror He had cast into their hearts and restrained them from fighting you. And if God had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you with their people. But if they withdraw from you, meaning: they withdraw from killing you, and do not fight you, and whoever is connected to them, and it is said: on the day of the conquest of Mecca they fight you with their people, “and offer you peace,” meaning: peace, so they submit and surrender, then God has not made for you a way against them, meaning: a way through killing and fighting.
4:91: 91- The Almighty said: "You will find others." Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: They are Asad and Ghatafan who were present in Medina. They spoke about Islam hypocritically, although they were not Muslims. A man from among them would be asked by his people, "Why did you become Muslim? He would say, I believed in this monkey, this scorpion, and this beetle." And when they met the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would say, "We are of your religion," meaning by that security for both groups. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are the sons of Abd al-Dar who were of this description, wanting to be secure from you, so do not expose them, and to be secure from their people, so do not expose them, every time they return to the sedition, meaning: they call to polytheism, they fall into it, meaning: they return and return to polytheism, but if they do not withdraw from you, meaning: if they do not stop fighting you until you march to Mecca, “and offer you peace,” meaning: ransom and peace, and restrain their hands, and they do not restrain their hands from fighting you, then take them, as prisoners, and kill them wherever you find them, meaning: you find them, and those, meaning: the people of this description, We have given you a clear authority over them, meaning: [a clear and apparent argument through killing and fighting].
4:92: 92- The Almighty said: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer, the verse was revealed about Ayyash bin Abi Rabi'ah Al-Makhzumi, and that is because he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca before the migration and converted to Islam, then he feared that his conversion to Islam would be revealed to his family, so he fled to Medina, and fortified himself in one of its roofs, so Ummah was very upset about that and said to her two sons Al-Harith and Abu Jahl bin Hashim, who were his brothers on his mother's side: By God, no roof will shelter me nor will I taste food or drink until you bring him to me, so they went out in search of him, and Al-Harith bin Zaid bin Abi Anisa went out with them until they came to Medina, and they came to Ayyash while he was in the roof, and they said to him: Come down, for your mother has not been given a roof after you, and she has sworn that she will not eat food or drink until you return to her and you have a covenant from God upon us that we will not force you to do anything nor will we stand between you and your religion, When they mentioned to him his mother’s distress and they pledged to him by God, he came down to them and they took him out of the city, then they bound him with a chain, and each one of them flogged him a hundred lashes, then they brought him to his mother. When he came to her, she said: By God, I will not release you from your bonds until you disbelieve in what you believe in. Then they left him bound and thrown in the sun as God willed, so he gave them what they wanted. Then Al-Harith bin Zaid came to him and said: O Ayyash, is this what you were upon? By God, if it was guidance, then you have abandoned guidance, and if it was misguidance, then you were upon it. Ayyash became angry at his words and said: By God, I will never meet you alone without killing you. Then Ayyash converted to Islam after that and emigrated, then Al-Harith bin Zaid converted to Islam after him and emigrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ayyash was not present that day and did not know of his conversion to Islam. While Ayyash was walking on the back of Quba, he met Al-Harith and killed him. The people said: Woe to you, what did you do? He had converted to Islam, so Ayyash returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what happened to me and to Al-Harath is what you know, and I did not know that he had converted to Islam until I killed him. Then the verse was revealed: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. This is a prohibition against killing a believer, as God Almighty says: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God (al-Ahzab 33:53). Except by mistake is an isolated exception, meaning: But if it happened by mistake, And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave i.e., he must free a believing slave as expiation, and the blood money is paid in full, to his family i.e., to the family of the slain person who inherits him, unless they give in charity i.e., they give the blood money in charity, so they free a slave and leave the blood money, but if he is from a people at war with you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave", what is meant by this is if the man is a Muslim in the land of war alone with the infidels and someone who did not know of his Islam killed him, then there is no blood money for him, and he must pay expiation. It was said: What is meant by it is if the one killed was a Muslim in the land of Islam and he was from the lineage of a people of infidels, and his kinship in the land of war was at war with the Muslims, then there is expiation for him and no blood money for his family. Al-Harith ibn Zayd was from a people of infidels at war with the Muslims, and there was a freeing of a slave in it, but there was no blood money in it because there was no covenant between his people and the Muslims. God the Almighty said: And if he was from a people between whom and you there is a treaty, then a ransom is due to his family and the freeing of a believing slave. He meant by this if the one killed was an infidel, a dhimmi or a covenanted person, then blood money and expiation are required. The expiation is by freeing a believing slave, whether the one killed was a Muslim or a covenanted person, a man or a woman, a free man or a slave, and it is to be from the killer’s money. But whoever cannot find one, then a fast of two consecutive months. If the killer has a slave or is able to obtain one by having its price in excess of his expenses and the expenses of his dependents and his need for housing and the like, then he must free him, and it is not permissible for him to switch to fasting. If he is unable to obtain it, then he must fast two consecutive months. If he breaks his fast intentionally one day during the two months or forgets the intention and intends to fast another, then he must start the two months over. If he breaks his fast one day due to illness or travel, is the continuity interrupted? The scholars differed on this. Some of them said: It is interrupted and he must start the two months again. This is the opinion of Al-Nakha’i, and the more correct of the two opinions is that of Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him, because he broke his fast voluntarily. Some of them said: It is not interrupted and he must continue. This is the opinion of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Al-Hasan, and Al-Sha’bi. If a woman menstruates during the two months, she breaks her fast during the days of menstruation, and the sequence is not interrupted. If she becomes pure, she remains as she fasted, because it is a matter written on the sun and they cannot avoid it. If he is unable to fast, can he be compensated by feeding sixty poor people? There are two opinions on this. One of them is that he should be compensated as in the expiation for zihar. The second is that he should not be compensated because the Shariah did not mention an alternative for it, so it said: Then fasting for two consecutive months. “Repentance from God” means: God made this repentance for the unintentional killer. And God is Knowing of the one who killed unintentionally, Wise in what He judged you with. As for the discussion of the blood money, know that murder is of three types: purely intentional, quasi-intentional, and purely accidental. As for pure intent, that is, intending to kill a person in a way that is usually intended to kill, and killing him, then there is retaliation in it if there is equivalence, or a heavy blood money from the killer’s money at the time. Quasi-intentional: that he intends to hit him with something that usually does not kill him, such as hitting him with a light stick or a small stone once or twice, and he dies, then there is no retaliation in this case, but rather a heavy blood money must be paid by his family, deferred for three years. The expiation for the mistake is from his money in all types. According to Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him: premeditated murder does not require expiation, because it is a major sin like all major sins. The blood money for a free Muslim is one hundred camels. If there are no camels, their value in dirhams or dinars is due, according to one opinion. According to another opinion, a specific amount of money is due, which is one thousand dinars or twelve thousand dirhams, based on what was narrated on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him: The blood money for those who own gold is one thousand dinars, and for those who own silver it is twelve thousand dirhams. Some people said that the blood money is one hundred camels, or one thousand dinars, or ten thousand dirhams, which is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion. The blood money for a woman is half the blood money for a man, and the blood money for the People of the Covenant is one-third of the blood money for a Muslim, if he is a People of the Book, and if he is a Zoroastrian, then it is one-fifth of the blood money. It was narrated on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The blood money for a Jew or a Christian is four thousand dirhams, and the blood money for a Zoroastrian is eight hundred, which is the opinion of Saeed bin al-Musayyab and al-Hasan, and al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, agreed with it. Some people said that the blood money of a dhimmi or a protected person is the same as the blood money of a Muslim. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, and it is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion. Some people said: The blood money of a dhimmi is half the blood money of a Muslim. This is the opinion of Omar bin Abdul Aziz, and Malik and Ahmad, may God have mercy on them, said the same. The blood money for intentional and semi-intentional killing is increased by age, so it must be thirty one-year-old camels, thirty two-year-old camels, and forty three-year-old camels with their young in their bellies. This is the opinion of Umar ibn al-Khattab and Zayd ibn Thabit, may God be pleased with them both. It was also said by Ata’, and it was the opinion of al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, when Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib told us, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khalal, on the authority of Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm, on the authority of al-Rabi’, on the authority of al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud’an, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware, for intentional killing by mistake with a whip or a stick, one hundred three-year-old camels must be increased, including forty three-year-old camels with their young in their bellies. Some people said that the heavy blood money is quarters: twenty-five female camels that have given birth, twenty-five female camels that have two years of age, twenty-five female camels that have two years of age, twenty-five female camels that have two years of age, and twenty-five female camels that have two years of age. This is the opinion of Al-Zuhri and Rabi’ah, and it is what Malik, Ahmad, and the people of opinion said. As for the blood money for accidental killing, it is reduced, and it is agreed upon to be one-fifth, but they differed in dividing it. Some people said that it is twenty young camels, twenty two-year-old camels, twenty two-year-old camels, twenty three-year-old camels, and twenty two-year-old camels. This is the opinion of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Sulayman ibn Yasar, al-Zuhri, and Rabi’ah, and Malik and al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them, said the same. Some people replaced two-year-old camels with two-year-old camels. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, and Ahmad and the people of opinion said the same. The blood money of the parties according to this estimation, the blood money of the woman is half of the blood money of the man, and the blood money in the case of accidental or semi-intentional killing is on the agnates, who are the male relatives of the killer, and nothing is required of the perpetrator because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made it obligatory on the agnates.
4:93: 93- The Almighty said: And whoever kills a believer intentionally The verse: It was revealed about Muqays bin Subaba Al-Kinani, who had converted to Islam with his brother Hisham, and he found his brother Hisham killed in Banu Al-Najjar, so he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent with him a man from Banu Fihr to Banu Al-Najjar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, orders you, if you know the killer of Hisham bin Subaba, to hand him over to Muqays so that he may take revenge on him, and if you do not know, to pay him his blood money, so Al-Fihr informed them of that and they said: We hear and obey God and His Messenger, by God we do not know his killer but we will pay his blood money, so they gave him a hundred camels, then they turned back towards Madinah and Satan came to Muqays and whispered to him, so he said: Accept the blood money of your brother or you will be insulted, kill the one with you so that you will have a life in place of a life and the blood money will be extra, so Al-Fihr was distracted and threw him With a rock, he smashed it, then he rode a camel and drove the rest of it back to Mecca as a disbeliever, so the following verse was revealed about him: And whoever kills a believer intentionally “his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally,” because of his disbelief and apostasy. He is the one whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made an exception on the day of the conquest of Mecca, from the one who believed him and was killed while clinging to the curtains of the Kaaba. God Almighty says: And God became angry with him and cursed him meaning: He expelled him from mercy, and prepared for him a great punishment. They differed regarding the ruling on this verse. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that there is no repentance for the one who intentionally kills a believer. It was said to him: Has God said in Surat al-Furqan 25:And they shall not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right until He said: “And whoever should do that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in disgrace, except for those who repent” Al-Furqan 67-70. He said: This was in the pre-Islamic era, and that was when some people from the polytheists had killed and committed adultery, so they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What you are calling us to is good, if only you would tell us that there is expiation for what we have done. So the verse was revealed: And those who do not invoke with God another deity until His saying: Except for those who repent and believe. This is for those. As for the one in women, if a man knows Islam and its laws and then kills, his punishment is Hell. Zaid bin Thabit said: When the verse in Al-Furqan was revealed, And those who do not invoke with God another deity, we were amazed at its softness, so we waited for seven months, then the thick verse was revealed after the soft verse, so the soft verse was abrogated. By the thick verse he meant this verse, and by the soft verse he meant the verse of Al-Furqan. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: That is a Meccan verse and this is a Medinan verse that was revealed and nothing abrogated it. The majority of scholars, and the doctrine of the Sunnis, hold that the repentance of a Muslim who intentionally kills a Muslim is acceptable, based on the words of God Almighty: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, believes and does righteousness (Ta-Ha 20:82). He also said: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills (al-Nisa 4:48). What was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, is a strict and exaggerated warning against killing, as was narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah that he said: If he does not kill, it is said to him: You have no repentance, and if he kills and then comes back, it is said: You have repentance. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. The verse has nothing to do with those who say that one will remain in Hell forever for committing major sins, because the verse was revealed about a murderer who was an unbeliever, namely Muqays ibn Subaba. It was said that it is a warning to whoever kills a believer, considering his killing permissible because of his faith, and whoever considers the killing of people of faith permissible because of their faith is an unbeliever who will remain in Hell forever. It was said that the meaning of the Almighty’s statement: His recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally is: it is his recompense for what He has punished him for, but if He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him out of His generosity, for He has promised to forgive whomever He wills. It is said that Amr ibn Ubayd came to Abu Amr ibn al-Ala and said to him: Does God break His promise? He said: No. He said: Didn’t God the Most High say: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala said to him: You have come from a foreign language, O Abu Uthman. The Arabs do not consider breaking a threat to be a breach of trust and blame, but rather they consider breaking a promise to be a breach of trust and blame. He recited: Even if I promised him or made him a promise, I will break my promise and fulfill my promise. The evidence that anything other than polytheism does not necessitate eternal damnation in Hell is what we have narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever dies without associating anything with God will enter Paradise. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said, Abu Idris Aidh God bin Abdullah told me that Ubadah bin As-Samit, may God be pleased with him - who had witnessed Badr and was one of the leaders on the night of Aqaba - said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, while a group of his companions were around him: “Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill your children, nor bring forth slander that you have fabricated between your hands and feet, nor disobey in what is right. Whoever among you fulfills his promise, his reward is with God. Whoever commits any of that and is punished in this world, it is an expiation. Whoever commits any of that and God conceals it, it is up to God. If He wills, He will pardon him, and if He wills, He will punish him.” So we pledged allegiance to him on that. God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate the verse. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: “This verse was revealed about a man from Banu Murrah ibn Awf called Murdas ibn Nahik, who was from the people of Fadak and was a Muslim. No one from his people converted to Islam except him. They heard of a raiding party of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that was targeting them. A man called Ghalib ibn Fadala al-Laithi was in charge of the raiding party, so they fled and the man stayed because he was a Muslim. When he saw the horses, he feared that they were not from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he took his sheep to a mountaintop and climbed the mountain. When the horses caught up with each other, he heard them shouting “Allahu Akbar.” When he heard the shouting Allahu Akbar, he knew that they were from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He shouted Allahu Akbar and came down saying: “There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God, peace be upon you.” Usama ibn Zayd attacked him and killed him and drove away his sheep. Then they returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was deeply troubled by that.” He said: “Very strongly, and he had preceded them before that report, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did you kill him for what he had with him? Then he recited this verse to Usama bin Zaid, and he said: O Messenger of God, ask forgiveness for me, so he said: How about ‘There is no god but God’? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it three times, Usama said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept repeating it until I wished that I had not converted to Islam until that day, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked forgiveness for me after three times, and said: Free a slave.” Abu Dhabiyan narrated on the authority of Usama, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I said: O Messenger of God, he only said it out of fear of the weapon. He said: Why didn’t you split open his heart so that you could know whether he said it out of fear or not?” Akrima said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: A man from Banu Salim passed by a group of the Prophet’s companions, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had sheep with him, so he greeted them. They said: He only greeted you to seek refuge from you. So they rose up, killed him, and took his sheep and brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God Almighty revealed this verse:
4:94: 94-: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God. That is, if you travel for the sake of God, that is: jihad. Fatabayyunu Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read here in two places and in Surat Al-Hujurat with the letter ta' and the letter tha' from the word tabahit, meaning: stop until you know the believer from the disbeliever. The others read with the letter ya' and the letter nun from the word tabayyun, it is said: Tabayyun the matter if you pondered it. "And do not say to one who greets you with peace." This is the reading of the people of Medina, Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah, meaning: the meeting, which is the saying There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God. The others read As-Salam, which is the greeting of the Muslims because he had greeted them. It was said: As-Salam and As-Salam are one, meaning: do not say to one who greets you You are not a believer. "Seeking the goods of worldly life," meaning: seeking the spoils and booty, and "the goods of worldly life" are its benefits and enjoyment. "So with God are abundant spoils, meaning spoils, in abundance." It was said: abundant reward for one who avoids killing a believer. "Thus were you before," Sa'id bin Jubayr said: Thus were you concealing your faith from the polytheists. "So God bestowed His favor upon you," by showing Islam. He said: Qatada: You were astray from the beginning, but God bestowed upon you Islam and guidance. It was said that its meaning is: Thus, you were previously safe among your people, saying, There is no god but God, before the migration. So do not fear someone who says it, for God has bestowed His favor upon you by migration. So be careful lest you kill a believer. God is All-Knowing of what you do. I said: If the invaders see the symbol of Islam in a country or village, they should refrain from attacking them. For when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, attacked a people, if he heard the call to prayer, he would refrain from attacking them, and if he did not hear the call to prayer, he would attack them. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ Al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Nawfal bin Masahiq, on the authority of Ibn Issam, on the authority of his father, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whenever he sent out a military expedition, he would say: If you see a mosque or hear a muezzin, do not kill anyone.
4:95: 95- The Almighty said: Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home the verse, Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah told us, Ibrahim bin Abdullah told us, Ibrahim bin Saad Al-Zuhri told us, Saleh bin Kaysan told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sahl bin Saad Al-Saadi, may God be pleased with him, that he said: I saw Marwan bin Al-Hakam sitting in the mosque, so I came and sat next to him, and he told us that Zaid bin Thabit, may God be pleased with him, told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dictated to him: Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home, except for those who are disabled, and those who strive in the cause of God. He said: Then Ibn Umm Maktum came while he was dictating it to me, and he said: O Messenger of God, if I could strive, I would strive. He was a blind man, so God Almighty revealed to him, His thigh was on my thigh, and it was so heavy on me that I feared that my thigh would be crushed, then he was relieved and God revealed, except for those who are disabled. This verse is about jihad and the urging of it. He said: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal from jihad except those who are disabled. The people of Medina, Ibn Amir, and Al-Kisa’i read it with the nasb of the ra’, meaning: except those who are disabled. The others read it with the raf’ as a description of those who sit meaning: those who sit at home are not equal who are not disabled, meaning: except those who are weak in body and sight, and those who strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives, except those who are disabled, for they are equal to the striving ones, because the excuse made them sit. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hairi told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Abdul Rahim bin Munib told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hamid Al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from the Battle of Tabuk, he approached Medina and said: There are people in Medina who, whenever you travelled or crossed a valley, were with you in it. They said: O Messenger of God, are they in Medina? He said: Yes, and they are in Medina, and an excuse has kept them back. Al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who go out to Badr. God the Almighty said: God has favored those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home by a degree. That is, by virtue. It was said that by those who sit at home He meant those who are harmed. God favored the mujahidin over them by a degree because the mujahid engaged in jihad with the intention, while those who were harmed had the intention but did not engage in it, so they were lowered by a degree than them. And to both meaning the mujahid and the one who sits, God has promised the best meaning: Paradise for their faith. Muqatil said: He means the mujahid and the one who sits with an excuse. And God has favored the mujahidin over those who sit at home by a great reward, meaning/over those who sit without an excuse.
4:96: 96- "Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And God is Forgiving and Merciful." Ibn Muhayriz said about this verse: It is seventy degrees, and between every two degrees the gallop of a well-trained horse is seventy autumns. It was said: The degrees are Islam, Jihad, Hijrah, and martyrdom, which the Mujahideen achieved. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni told us, Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sharik al-Shafi’i told us, Abdullah ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jurabadhi told us, Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Abu Hani’ al-Khawlani told us, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Jabali, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Sa’id, whoever is satisfied with God as his Lord, with Islam as his religion, and with Muhammad as his Prophet, Paradise is guaranteed for him. Abu Sa’id was amazed by this and said: Repeat it to me, O Messenger of God. So he did. He said: And another by which God raises the servant one hundred degrees in Paradise, between every two degrees is like the distance between the heaven and the earth. He said: And what is it, O Messenger of God? He said: Jihad in the way of God, Jihad in the way of God. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu al-Qasim Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah told us, my father told us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Mutraz told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Shureih ibn al-Nu’man told us, Falih, on the authority of Hilal ibn Ali, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever believes in God and His Messenger, establishes prayer, and fasts Ramadan, it is incumbent upon God Almighty to admit him into Paradise, whether he fights in the cause of God or remains in the land in which he was born.” They said: Shall we not warn the people of that? He said: “In Paradise there are one hundred levels that God has prepared for those who fight in His cause, and between each two levels is like the distance between the heaven and the earth. So if you ask God for something, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it flow the rivers of Paradise.” Know that jihad is generally an obligation, but it is divided into an individual obligation and a communal obligation: The individual obligation is that the infidels enter the home of a group of believers. It is obligatory for every responsible man, who has no excuse, from the people of that town to go out to their enemy, whether he is free or slave, rich or poor, to defend himself and his neighbors. And it is a communal obligation for those Muslims who are far away from them. If the sufficiency of those who have settled with them is not fulfilled, then the Muslims who are far away from them must help them. If the sufficiency of those who have settled with them is fulfilled, then there is no obligation on those who are far away except by choice. Slaves and the poor are not included in this category. It is of this type that the infidels are settled in their country, so the imam must not miss a year without a raid that he may raid himself or with his troops so that the jihad is not neglected. The choice for the one who is able to wage jihad when the sufficiency of others is fulfilled is that he should not sit out the jihad, but it is not obligatory, because God Almighty promised the one who fights and the one who sits the reward in this verse, saying: And to each of them God has promised the best. If it were an obligation on everyone, the one who sits would not deserve punishment, not reward.
4:97: 97- The Almighty said: Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves the verse was revealed about people from the people of Mecca who spoke about Islam but did not emigrate, including: Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughira and Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and their likes. When the polytheists went out to Badr, they went out with them and were killed with the infidels, so God Almighty said: Indeed, those whom the angels take in death, meaning the Angel of Death and his helpers, or He meant the Angel of Death alone, as God Almighty said: Say, 'The Angel of Death who is set over you will take you in death' (al-Sajdah 32:11). The Arabs address one person in the plural form wronging themselves with polytheism, and it is an accusative of state, meaning: in a state of their wrongdoing. It was said: meaning by staying in the land of polytheism because God Almighty did not accept Islam after the Prophet's emigration, may God bless him and grant him peace, except with emigration, then that was abrogated after the conquest of Mecca, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no emigration after the conquest and these were killed on the day of Badr and the The angels turned their faces and their backs, and said to them: In what were you? That is the saying of the Most High: “They said: In what were you?” meaning: In what were you? Or in which of the two groups were you? Were you among the Muslims? Or among the polytheists? A question of rebuke and reproach, so they apologized for their weakness in resisting the polytheists, and “They said: We were oppressed,” helpless, in the land, meaning: to Medina and you left Mecca, from among the polytheists? Meaning the land of Mecca, They said, meaning: the angels, Was not the earth of God spacious enough for you to migrate therein, meaning: to Medina and you left Mecca, from among the polytheists? So God the Most High denied them and informed us of their lie, and said: Then their refuge, their home, is Hell, and evil it is as a destination, meaning: an evil destination to Hell.
4:98: 98- Then he made an exception for those who have an excuse, saying: Except for the weak among men, women and children who are unable to devise a plan they are unable to devise a plan, nor to provide for themselves, nor to have the strength to get out of it, nor are they guided to a way, meaning: they do not know a way to get out. Mujahid said they do not know the way to Medina.
16:110: 99- Then it is possible that God will pardon them, He will overlook them, and perhaps from God is obligatory, because it is for greed, and God, the Most High, if He makes a servant greedy, He will connect him to Him, and God is Pardoning and Forgiving. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: My mother and I were among those whom God excused, meaning among the weak, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate for these weak people in prayer. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muadh bin Fadala told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yahya, he is the son of Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God hears those who praise Him. Our Lord, to You is praise,’ in the last rak’ah of the ‘Isha’ prayer, he would supplicate, ‘O God, save Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah. O God, save Al-Walid. O God, save Salamah bin Hisham. O God, save the weak among the believers. O God, make your oppression severe upon Mudar. O God, make them years like the years of Joseph.” 110 - Then indeed, your Lord, to those who emigrated after they were persecuted, they were tortured and prevented from Islam, the polytheists tried them, and then strove and were patient, in faith, emigration, and jihad, indeed, your Lord, after that, after that trial and heedlessness, is Forgiving and Merciful. It was revealed about Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah, Abu Jahl’s foster brother, and about Abu Jandal bin Suhayl bin Amr, Al-Walid bin Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, Salamah bin Hisham and Abdullah bin Asid Al-Thaqafi. The polytheists tempted them, so they gave them some of what they wanted in order to be safe from their evil. Then they migrated after that and fought in jihad. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Saad bin Abi Sarh, who used to write for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Satan made him slip, so he joined the infidels. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that he be killed on the day of the conquest of Mecca. Uthman sought his protection, and he was his foster brother, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, granted him protection. Then he converted to Islam and his conversion was good, so God revealed this verse. Ibn Amir read fitnawa with the opening of the fa and the ta, and he attributed it to those polytheists who converted to Islam and tempted the Muslims.
4:100: 100- The Almighty said: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God will find on the earth many [alternative] locations and abundance. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: Alternative means: one who turns to him, and Mujahid said: one who moves away from what he dislikes. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Maraghim: it is said: I opposed my people and emigrated from them, and it is the one who is disturbed and driven away. It was narrated that when this verse was revealed, a very old and sick man from Banu Laith, whose name was Junda’ bin Damrah, heard it and said: “By God, I will not spend the night in Mecca. Take me out.” So they took him out and carried him on a bed until they reached At-Tan’im. Death overtook him, so he clapped his right hand over his left and said: “By God, this is for you and this is for your Messenger. I pledge allegiance to you on what your Messenger pledged allegiance to you on.” So he died and report of him reached the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: If he had reached Madinah, it would have been more complete and more rewarding. The polytheists laughed and said: How do you know what he asked for? So God revealed: And whoever emigrates from his home for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him meaning before he reaches his place of migration, his reward has fallen meaning: it is obligatory for him from God, by imposing it on himself as a favor from Him, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.
4:101: 101- The Almighty’s saying: And when you travel throughout the land, meaning: travel, there is no blame upon you, meaning: hardship and sin, for shortening the prayer, meaning from four rak’ahs to two rak’ahs, and that is in the noon, afternoon, and evening prayers, if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, meaning: assassinate you and kill you, in prayer. Similar to the Almighty’s saying: For fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs that he may tempt them Yunus - 83, meaning: kill them. The disbelievers have been to you a clear enemy meaning: apparent enmity. Know that shortening the prayer while traveling is permissible by consensus of the nation. They differed about the permissibility of completing it. Most of them held that shortening is obligatory, which is the opinion of Omar, Ali, Ibn Omar, Jabir, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them. Al-Hasan, Omar Ibn Abdul Aziz, and Qatadah said the same, and it is the opinion of Malik and the people of opinion, because it was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: The first prayer that was made obligatory was two rak’ahs, so I confirmed the prayer of travel and completed the prayer of residence. Some people have said that it is permissible to complete the prayer. This was narrated on the authority of Uthman and Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, may God be pleased with them. Al-Shafi`i, may God be pleased with him, said the same. If he wishes, he may complete the prayer or shorten it. Patience is better. Imam Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal, on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Shafi’i, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Riyah, on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did all of that, shortening the prayer and completing it. The apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates this, because it says: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer. The phrase there is no blame is only used for concessions, not for what is inevitable. The apparent meaning of the verse [requires that shortening] is not permissible except in cases of fear, but this is not the case. Rather, the verse was revealed regarding most of the Prophet’s travels, may God bless him and grant him peace, and most of them were not free from fear of the enemy. Shortening the prayer is permissible during travel when there is security according to most scholars. The evidence for this is what Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Muslim bin Khalid and Abdul Majeed bin Abdul Aziz bin Abi Rawad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Abi Ammar told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Babah, on the authority of Ya’la bin Umayyah, who said: “I said to Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: God Almighty only said, ‘shorten the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you,’ when the people were safe. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: I was amazed by what you were amazed by, so I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: It is a charity that God has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity.” Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Ayoub Al-Sakhtiyani, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God traveled between Mecca and Medina in safety, fearing none but God, and he prayed two rak’ahs. Some people said that the two rak’ahs of the traveler are not shortened, but rather shortening is praying one rak’ah in fear. This is narrated on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, and it is the opinion of Ata’, Tawus, Al-Hasan, and Mujahid. They made the condition of fear mentioned in the verse remain, and most scholars said that limiting oneself to one rak’ah is not permissible, whether one is afraid or safe. Scholars differed regarding the distance of shortening prayers. A group said: It is permissible to shorten prayers during long and short journeys. This was narrated on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him. Amr ibn Dinar said: Jabir ibn Zayd said to me: Shorten prayers at Arafat. As for the majority of jurists, they do not permit shortening prayers during short journeys. There is a difference of opinion about the limit of what is permissible to shorten the prayer. Al-Awza’i said: It is a day’s journey. Ibn ‘Umar and Ibn ‘Abbas, may God be pleased with them, used to shorten and break their fast in four cold days, which is sixteen farsakhs. Malik, Ahmad and Ishaq agreed with this view. The statement of Al-Hasan and Al-Zuhri is close to this. They said: It is a two-day journey. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, agreed with this view. He said: It is a two-night journey. He said in one place: Forty-six miles according to Al-Hashemi. Sufyan Al-Thawri and the people of opinion said: It is a three-day journey. It was said: His statement, If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, is connected to what follows it from the prayer of fear, separate from what precedes it. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari that he said: His statement, There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, was revealed to this extent. Then after a year, they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the prayer of fear, so it was revealed: “If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you. Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy.” And when you are among them, the verse. And there are many examples of this in the Qur’an, where the report comes in its entirety and then another report is coordinated with it, and it is apparently connected to it, but separate from it, like the statement of God, the Most High, “Now the truth has become evident. I did seek to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful.” (Yusuf 12:51) This is a narration about the wife of al-Aziz, and His statement, That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret. (Yusuf 12:52) is a report about Joseph, peace be upon him.
4:102: 102- The Almighty said: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer. Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Jabir, may God be pleased with them, that when the polytheists saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions standing up for the noon prayer in congregation, they regretted that they had attacked them. Some of them said to each other: Leave them, for after it they have a prayer that is dearer to them than their fathers and sons, meaning the afternoon prayer. So when they stand up for it, attack them and kill them. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down and said: O Muhammad, it is the prayer of fear, and God Almighty says: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, so he taught him the prayer of fear. And its sumMaryam 19:If the enemy is in their camp, not in the direction of the Qiblah, then the Imam divides the people into two groups, one group stands in front of the enemy to guard them, and the Imam begins the prayer with a group. When he has prayed one rak’ah with them, he stands and remains standing until they have completed their prayer. They go to his side, then the second group comes and he prays the second rak’ah with them, and remains sitting until they have completed their prayer for themselves. Then he gives them the salutation. This is the narration of Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did likewise at Dhat ar-Riqa’. Malik, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq agreed with this. I am Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi. Zahir ibn Ahmad told us. I am Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi. I am Abu Mus`ab. I am Malik. I am Yazid ibn Ruman. I am Salih ibn Khawat. I am one of those who prayed the fear prayer with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Dhat al-Riqa`. A group lined up with him and another group lined up facing the enemy. He prayed one rak`ah with the group that was with him, then he remained standing and they completed it for themselves. Then they turned away and lined up facing the enemy. The other group came and he prayed with them the remaining rak`ah, then he remained sitting and they completed it for themselves. Then he said the salutation with them. Malik said: That is the best thing I have heard about the fear prayer. And Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Musaddad, I told Yahya, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Salih bin Khawat, on the authority of Sahl bin Abi Hathmah, may God be pleased with them, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with this. Some people said that when the imam stands for the second rak’ah, the first group goes during the prayer to face the enemy, the second group comes and he prays the second rak’ah with him and he says the salutation, but they do not say the salutation, rather they go to face the enemy, and the first group returns and completes its prayer, then the second group returns and completes its prayer. This is the narration of Abdullah bin Omar, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed like this. This is the opinion of the people of opinion. Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, I told Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarhi, I told Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi, I told Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi, I told Muhammad bin Abdul-Malik bin Abi Al-Shawarib, I told Yazid bin Zari’, I told Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the fear prayer with one of the two groups, one rak’ah, and the other group facing the enemy. Then they turned away and stood in the place of those, and those came and he prayed with them another rak’ah, then he gave them the salutation, and those stood and prayed their rak’ah. Both narrations are correct. Some people said that this is permissible difference. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, said the hadith of Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah because it is more in agreement with the apparent meaning of the Qur’an and more cautious for the prayer and more effective in guarding the enemy. This is because God Almighty said: So when they prostrate, let them be behind you meaning: when they pray. Then He said: And let another group come who have not prayed. This indicates that the first group has prayed. He said: Let them pray with you. Its implication is that they should pray the entire prayer. Its apparent meaning indicates that each group leaves the imam after completing the prayer. It is a precaution for the matter of prayer, in that there is not much work and going and coming in it, and a precaution for the matter of war, in that if they were not in prayer, it would be possible for war and escape if they needed it. If the Imam prays four rak’ahs with each group praying two rak’ahs, it is permissible: I am Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, I am Abu Na’im Abd al-Malik ibn al-Husayn al-Isfarayini, I am Abu ‘Awanah Ya’qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz, he said: I am al-San’ani, I am ‘Affan ibn Muslim, he said: Aban al-‘Attar narrated to us from Yahya ibn Abi Katheer from Abu Salamah from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, he said: “We set out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until we were at Dhat al-Riqa’, and whenever we came upon a shady tree, we would leave it for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then a polytheist came and the sword of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was hanging on a tree, so he took the sword of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and drew it, and said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you fear me? He said: No. He said: Who will protect you from me? He said: God will protect me from you. He said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threatened him. He said: So he sheathed the sword and hung it up, and the call to prayer was made. He said: So he prayed two rak’ahs with one group, then they moved back, so he prayed with the other group.” Two rak’ahs. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had four rak’ahs, and the people had two rak’ahs.” Abdul Wahhab bin Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Al-Thiqa Ibn Ulayyah or someone else told me, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with them, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was leading the people in the noon prayer in fear in Batn Nakhl, so he prayed two rak’ahs with a group and then said the salutation, then another group came and he prayed two rak’ahs with them and then said the salutation. It was narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the fear prayer, that he prayed one rak’ah with these people and one rak’ah with those people, and they did not make it up. It was narrated by Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: The people had one rak’ah, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had two rak’ahs. Some people interpreted it as a prayer of intense fear, and they said: The obligation in this case is one rak’ah. Most scholars agree that fear does not reduce the number of rak'ahs, even if the enemy is on the side of the qiblah at a level. If they attack them, they will see them. The imam will pray with them all and they will guard themselves in prostration, as Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us. Abu Na'im al-Asfarayni informed us. Abu 'Awana al-Hafiz informed us. 'Ammar informed us. Yazid ibn Harun informed us. 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, on the authority of 'Ata', on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the fear prayer. We lined up behind him in two rows, and the enemy was between us and the qiblah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said Allahu Akbar and we all said Allahu Akbar. Then he bowed and we all bowed. Then he raised his head from bowing and we all raised our heads. Then he descended to prostrate and the row next to him. The last row stood up and slaughtered the enemy. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished prostrating and the row next to him stood up, the last row descended to prostrate. Then they stood up. Then the last row advanced and the first row retreated. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, bowed and we all bowed. Then he raised his head from bowing and we all raised our heads. Then he descended." In prostration and the row next to him that was last in the first rak’ah, and the last row stood up to slaughter the enemy, so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished prostrating and the row next to him, the last row descended in prostration and they prostrated, Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, greeted us all. Jabir, may God be pleased with him, said: Just as your guards do with their leaders. Know that the fear prayer is permissible after the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to most scholars. Some of them say that it is not permissible, but there is no basis for that. Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, said: Every hadith narrated in the chapters on the fear prayer is permissible to act upon. Six or seven aspects have been narrated in it. Mujahid said about the reason for the revelation of this verse, on the authority of Ibn Ayyash al-Zarqi, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Usfan, and Khalid ibn al-Walid was in charge of the polytheists, so we prayed the noon prayer. The polytheists said: We have been caught by surprise if we had attacked them while they were praying. So the verse was revealed between the noon and afternoon prayers. God the Almighty said: And if you are among them meaning: a witness with them and you lead them in prayer, then let a group of them stand with you meaning: let them stand, like God the Almighty’s saying: And when darkness falls upon them, they stand (al-Baqarah 2:20) meaning: stand, and take their weapons and they differed about those who take their weapons. Some of them said: He meant those who stood with the imam praying and took weapons in prayer, so based on this, he only takes it if it does not distract him from the prayer, and does not harm those beside him [so if its movement and weight distract him from the prayer, such as a quiver or a large shield, or if it harms those beside him] such as a spear, then he does not take it. It was said: And let them take their weapons, meaning: the rest who stood in the face of the enemy, And when they prostrate, meaning: pray, let them be behind you, meaning the place of those who are in front of the enemy, And let another group come who have not prayed, and they are those who were in the face of the enemy, and let them pray with you and let them take their precautions and their weapons, it was said: these are those who came, and it was said: they are those who prayed, And those who disbelieved wish, the disbelievers wish, that you would be heedless, meaning: if they found you heedless, of your weapons and your baggage so that they could attack you with a single attack, so they would target you and attack you with a single attack. And there is no blame upon you if you are harmed by rain or you are ill for laying down your weapons. He permitted laying down weapons in the case of rain or illness, because carrying weapons in these two cases is heavy. And take your precautions. That is, watch the enemy so that they do not catch you off guard. Precaution is that by which one protects oneself from the enemy. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: “It was revealed about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was when he raided Muharrib and Banu Anmar, and they camped and did not see anyone from the enemy, so the people laid down their weapons, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out for a need of his and laid down his weapon until he crossed the valley and the sky was drizzling, and the valley came between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat in the shade of a tree and saw Ghawrath ibn al-Harith al-Muharibi and said: May God kill me if I do not kill him, then he descended from the mountain with the sword, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not notice him until he was standing over his head and he had not drawn his sword from its sheath, so he said: O Muhammad, who will protect you from me now? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, then he said: O God, protect me from Ghawrath ibn al-Harith with whatever you wish, then he aimed the sword at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to strike him, but he fell on his face from a slip that he had slipped between his shoulders, and his sword fell, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up.” He handed it over to him and took it and said: O Ghawrath, who can protect you from me now?
