He said: No one. He said: Do you testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and I will give you your sword? He said: No, but I testify that I will never fight you or help an enemy against you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him his sword. Ghawrath said: By God, you are better than me. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, I am more deserving of that than you. Ghawrath returned to his companions and they said: Woe to you, what prevented you from him? He said: I reached out to him with the sword to strike him, but by God, I do not know who made me slip between my shoulders and I fell on my face. He mentioned his condition and said: The valley calmed down, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, crossed the valley to his companions and told them the report and recited to them this verse: {And there is no blame upon you, if you are troubled by rain or you are ill, for laying down your weapons and taking your precautions.} That is, from your enemy. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: Abd al-Rahman bin Awf was wounded. God has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment, in which they will be humiliated. / And the word jannah means sin. / From janaht: if you deviate from the intended path.
4:103: 103- "So when you have completed the prayer," meaning: the prayer of fear, i.e.: you have finished it, "then remember God," i.e. pray to God "standing, when healthy, sitting, when sick, and on your sides," when in difficulty and hardship. It was said: Remember God with glorification, praise, exaltation, and exaltation, in every situation. Amr bin Abdul Aziz Al-Kashani told us, Al-Qasim bin Jaafar Al-Hashemi told us, Abu Ali Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Lulu’i told us, Abu Dawud Al-Sijistani told us, Muhammad bin Al-Ala’ told us, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khalid bin Salamah, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to remember God at all times.” So when you are secure, that is, you are calm and safe, establish prayer, that is, complete it with four units with its pillars, Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times. It was said: It is an obligatory, prescribed, and determined duty, in the city it is four units and in travel it is two units. Mujahid said: That is, it is a temporary duty that God has set for them. The times of prayer were explained in the hadith. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hairi told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Hashim told us, Wakee told us, Sufyan, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ayyash bin Abi Rabia Al-Zarqi, on the authority of Hakim bin Hakim bin Abbad bin Hanif, on the authority of Nafi bin Jubair bin Mut’am, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Gabriel came to me at the House twice. He prayed Maghrib with me when the fasting person broke his fast, and prayed Isha with me when the twilight disappeared, and prayed Fajr with me when food and drink were forbidden to the fasting person, and prayed Dhuhr with me the next day when the shadow of everything was equal to it, and prayed Asr with me when the shadow of everything was twice its size, and prayed Maghrib with me when the fasting person broke his fast, and prayed Isha with me during the first third of the night, and prayed Fajr with me when light broke, then he turned to me and said: O Muhammad, this is the time of the prophets before you, the time is between these two times.” Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr bin Al-Hasan Al-Hairi told us, Wakee’ told us, Hajib bin Ahmad told us, Abdullah bin Hisham told us, Wakee’ told us, Badr bin Othman told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Musa Al-Ash’ari told us, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “A questioner came to him and asked him about the times of prayer. He did not answer him, then he ordered Bilal to call the adhan, then he ordered him to call the iqama when dawn broke, so he prayed. Then he ordered him to call the noon prayer, and the speaker says: The sun has passed its zenith or not, and he was more knowledgeable than them. Then he ordered him to call the afternoon prayer while the sun was high and white and pure. Then he ordered him to call the sunset prayer when the sun had set. Then he ordered him to call the night prayer when the twilight had fallen. He said: And he prayed the dawn prayer the next day, and the speaker says: The sun has risen or not risen. He prayed the noon prayer close to the time of the afternoon prayer yesterday, and he prayed the afternoon prayer, and the speaker says: The sun has turned red, and he prayed the sunset prayer before the red twilight had disappeared, and he prayed the night prayer in the first third of the night. Then he said: Where is the questioner about the time? The man said: I will, O Messenger of God. He said: Between These two times are time.
4:104: 104- The Almighty’s saying: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy the verse, the reason for its revelation is that when Abu Sufyan and his companions returned on the day of Uhud, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a group to follow them and they complained of the pain of their wounds, so God Almighty said: And do not weaken meaning: do not weaken in pursuing the enemy in pursuit of Abu Sufyan and his companions, If you are suffering suffering from the wounds, they are suffering meaning: they are suffering, meaning the infidels, as you are suffering and you hope from God what they do not hope for meaning: and you are still hoping for reward and recompense in the Hereafter and victory in this world what they do not hope for, and some of the commentators said: What is meant by hope is fear, because every hopeful person is afraid that he will not achieve what he hopes for. The meaning of the verse: And you hope from God, meaning: you fear God, meaning: you fear the punishment of God in a way that they do not fear. Al-Farra’ may God have mercy on him said: Hope does not mean fear except with denial, like the Almighty’s saying: Say to those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of God (Al-Ja’iyyah: 14), meaning: they do not fear. And the Almighty said: What is the matter with you that you do not expect for God a dignified life? (Nuh 71:13), meaning: you do not fear God’s greatness. It is not permissible to say I feared you in the sense of I feared you, or I feared you, and you mean I hoped for you. “And God is Knowing and Wise.”
4:105: 105- The Almighty said: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you. The verse, Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed about a man from the Ansar called Ta'mah ibn Ubayraq from Banu Thafar ibn Al-Harith who stole a shield from his neighbor called Qatadah ibn Al-Nu'man. The shield was in a bag containing flour, so the flour kept falling out of a hole in the bag until it reached the house, then he hid it with a Jewish man called Zaid ibn Al-Sameen. The shield was sought by Ta'mah, so he swore: By God, he did not take it and he had no knowledge of it. The owners of the shield said: We saw the trace of the flour until it entered his house. When he swore, they left him and followed the trace of the flour to the house of the Jew and took it from him. The Jew said: Give it to Ta'mah ibn Ubayraq. Banu Thafar, who are the people of Ta'mah, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him to argue on behalf of their companion, and they said: He said to him: If you do not do so, our companion will be disgraced. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to punish the Jew. It is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, in another narration that Ta'mah stole the shield in a bag containing bran, and tore the bag so that the bran was falling from it all the way. He brought it to the house of Zayd the Fatimin and left it at his door, and carried the shield to his house. When morning came, the owner of the shield came after the bran to the house of Zayd the Fatimin, took it and carried it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to cut off the hand of Zayd the Jew. Muqatil said: Zayd the Fatimin entrusted a shield to Ta'mah, but Ta'mah denied it, so God, the Most High, revealed this verse, saying: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth with commands, prohibitions and distinction, that you may judge between people by what God has shown you by what God has taught you and revealed to you, and be not an advocate for the treacherous [Ta'mah], a supporter and defender of him.
4:106: 106- And ask forgiveness of God, for what I intended to do to punish the Jew, and Muqatil said: And ask forgiveness of God for your argument about Ta'mah Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
4:107: 107- And do not argue do not quarrel, on behalf of those who betray themselves, that is, wrong themselves by betrayal and theft. Indeed, God does not like anyone who is a traitor and sinful meaning a traitor in the armor, a sinner in the Jew's arrow. It was said that it is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is someone else, like the Almighty's saying: If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, and seeking forgiveness for the prophets after prophethood is in one of three ways: either for a sin that preceded prophethood or for the sins of his nation and relatives, or for something permissible that the law came with a warning so he leaves it by seeking forgiveness, so seeking forgiveness means: hearing and obeying the ruling of the law.
4:108: 108- They hide from the people, that is: they conceal themselves and are ashamed of the people, meaning Bani Thafar bin Al-Harith, and they do not hide from God, that is: they do not conceal themselves and are not ashamed of God, and He is with them when they spend the night, they say and compose, and spending the night is planning an action at night, what is not pleasing of speech, and that is because the people of Ta'mah said among themselves: We will take the matter to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he will hear his words and oaths because he is a Muslim and will not hear from the Jew because he is an unbeliever, so God was not pleased with that from them, and God is encompassing of what they do, then he says to the people of Ta'mah:
4:109: 109- "Here you are", meaning: O these people, "you have argued", meaning: you have disputed, "about them" meaning: about Ta'mah, and in the reading of Abi bin Ka'b: about him "in the life of this world", and argument: the intensity of the dispute from the argument, and it is the intensity of the killing, so he wants to kill the opponent from his doctrine by the method of argumentation, and it was said: the argument is from the argumentation, and it is the earth, so it is as if each of the two opponents wants to subdue his companion and defeat him on the argument, "Then who will argue with God for them", meaning: about Ta'mah, "on the Day of Resurrection when God takes him with His punishment, or who will be a guardian over them", a guarantor, meaning: who will defend them and take care of their affairs on the Day of Resurrection? Then he resumed and said:
4:110: 110- And whoever does evil, meaning stealing, or wrongs himself, by accusing the innocent, and it was said: And whoever does evil, meaning: polytheism, or wrongs himself: meaning: a sin less than polytheism, and then seeks forgiveness of God, meaning: repents to Him and seeks His forgiveness, will find God Forgiving and Merciful, offering repentance to Ta'mah in this verse.
4:111: 111- And whoever earns a sin, meaning: swearing a false oath, meaning: what you stole was stolen by the Jew, he only earns it against himself, so he only harms himself with it, and God is All-Knowing of the shield thief, Wise, He ruled that the thief should be cut off.
4:112: 112- And whoever commits a sin i.e. stealing the shield, or a crime i.e. his false oath, and then throws it i.e. accuses what he has committed an innocent person i.e. attributing the theft to the Jew, has certainly borne the burden of slander slander is falsehood, and it is a lie whose enormity one is perplexed by, and a manifest sin i.e. a clear fault, and his saying and then throws it and he did not say them after mentioning the sin and the crime, is a reference to the sin, or he made the sin and the crime like one thing.
4:113: 113- The Almighty says: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, He says to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: A party of them would have surely decided, meaning: the people of Ta'mah, to mislead you, to make you err in judgment and confuse you until you defend Ta'mah, and they mislead none but themselves, meaning that its consequences will return to them, and they will not harm you at all, meaning that its harm will return to them, and God has sent down upon you the Book, meaning: the Qur'an, and wisdom, meaning: the judgment by revelation, and taught you what you did not know, of the rulings, and it was said: of the knowledge of the unseen, and the grace of God upon you has been great.
4:114: 114- The Almighty said: There is no good in much of their private conversations, meaning: the people of Ta'mah. Mujahid said: The verse is general for all people, and private conversation is secret planning. It was said: Private conversation is what a group of people plan alone, whether secretly or openly. So the meaning of the verse is: There is no good in much of what they plan among themselves, except for one who enjoins charity, meaning: except in the private conversation of one who enjoins charity. Private conversation is an action. It was said: This is an isolated exception, meaning: but for one who enjoins charity. It was said that private conversation here is: the men who are private conversations, as the Almighty said: And when they are in private conversation Al-Isra' 47 except for one who enjoins charity, meaning: urges it, or what is right, meaning: obedience to God and what the Shari'ah knows. All righteous deeds are known, because the minds know them. Or reconciliation between people. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Salim, who is the son of Abu al-Ja’d, on the authority of Umm al-Darda’, may God be pleased with her, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you of something better than the degree of fasting, charity, and prayer? He said: We said: Yes. He said: Reconciling people. And corruption of people is the razor. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Bishran told us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hamid bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of his mother, Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah, who was one of the first emigrants, she said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: He is not a liar who reconciles between people and says something good or conveys something good. God Almighty says: And whoever does that meaning: these things that He mentioned, seek[ing] the pleasure of God meaning: seeking His pleasure, We will give him in the Hereafter a great reward. Abu Amr and Hamza read yu’tihi with a ya’, meaning: God will give him, and the others read it with a noon.
4:115: 115- The Almighty’s saying: And whoever contradicts the Messenger, was revealed about Tu’mah ibn Ubayraq. When theft became apparent to him, he feared for his life that his hand would be cut off and he would be disgraced, so he fled to Mecca and renounced the religion. Then the Almighty said: And whoever contradicts the Messenger, meaning: opposes him, after guidance has become clear to him, of monotheism and the limits, and follows other than the way of the believers, meaning: other than the path of the believers, We will give him what he has taken, meaning: We will turn him over in the Hereafter] / to what he took in this world, and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination. It was narrated that Ta’mah ibn Ubayraq stayed with a man from Banu Salim from the people of Mecca called Al-Hajjaj ibn Alat. He dug into his house and a stone fell on him, so he could not enter or exit until morning. He was taken to be killed, but some of them said: Leave him alone, for he has sought refuge with you. So they left him and took him out of Mecca. He went out with merchants from Quda’ah towards Ash-Sham, and they stopped at a place where he stole some of their goods and fled. They sought him out, took him, and threw stones at him until they killed him, and those stones became his grave. It was also said that he boarded a ship to his grandfather and stole a bag containing dinars, which was taken and thrown into the sea. It was also said that he stayed in the Harrat of Banu Salim and worshipped an idol until he died, so God Almighty revealed about him.
4:116: 116- "Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates with God has certainly strayed far astray." That is, he has gone astray and has been deprived of all goodness. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: This verse is about an old man from the Bedouins who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, I am an old man who has committed sins, but I have not associated anything with God since I knew Him and believed in Him, and I have not taken a guardian other than Him, and I have not committed sins out of boldness towards God, and I have never imagined for the blink of an eye that I could escape from God. I am regretful, repentant, and seeking forgiveness. So what is my condition? Then God, the Most High, revealed this verse.
4:117: 117- The Almighty’s saying: They invoke besides Him only female deities, was revealed about the people of Mecca, meaning: what they worship, like the Almighty’s saying: And your Lord said, ‘Call upon Me’ (Ghafir 40:60), meaning: worship Me, as evidenced by the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me (Ghafir 40:60). His saying: Besides Him means: besides God, except female deities, he meant by female deities the idols because they used to call them by female names, so they would say: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat, and they used to say about the idol of each tribe: the female of Banu So-and-so, so in each one of them was a devil who would appear to the guardians and priests and speak to them, and for this reason He said: And they invoke none but a devil, this is the saying of most of the commentators. The correctness of this interpretation - that what is meant by females are idols - is indicated by the reading of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: They invoke besides Him only females, the plural of the idol, so the waw became a hamza. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Except females, meaning: dead, without a soul, because their idols were inanimate objects. He called them females because he is describing dead things, as he is describing females, and because females are lower than the two sexes, just as dead things are more despicable than animals. Ad-Dahhak said: He meant by females the angels, and some of them used to worship angels and say: the angels are females, as God Almighty said: And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females (al-Zukhruf 43:19). And they invoke only a rebellious devil, meaning: they worship only a rebellious devil, because if they worship idols, they have obeyed Satan. The rebellious is the rebellious, the stubborn, the one who goes against obedience, and he meant: Satan.
4:118: 118- May God curse him, meaning: May God distance him from His mercy, and he said, meaning: Satan said, I will take from among Your servants a prescribed portion, meaning: a known portion, so whatever Satan obeys in is prescribed, and in some interpretations: from every thousand one is for God Almighty and nine hundred and ninety-nine is for Satan, and the origin of the word fardh in the language is: cutting, and from it is the fardah in the river, which is the gap that is in it, and the fardh of the bow and the shrik is for the crack that is in the string and the thread with which the sling is tied.
4:119: 119- And I will mislead them means: from the truth, i.e. I will mislead them, Satan says it, and he meant by it embellishment, otherwise there is nothing to do with misguidance, as he said: I will make things attractive to them on the earth (al-Hijr 15:39) And I will arouse in them false hopes, it was said: I aroused in them the riding of whims, and it was said: I aroused in them that there is no Paradise, no Hell, and no resurrection, and it was said: I aroused in them the attainment of the Hereafter while riding sins, And I will command them to cut off the ears of cattle i.e. they will cut them off and split them, which is the Bahira And I will command them to change the creation of God, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Ad-Dahhak said: It means the religion of God, similar to the Almighty's saying: There is no changing the creation of God (Al-Rum: 30) i.e. the religion of God, meaning God's position in the religion by making permissible what is forbidden and forbidding what is permissible. Ikrimah and a group of commentators said: “So let them change the creation of God by castration, tattooing, and cutting off the ears, until some of them forbade castration and some of them permitted it for animals, because it has an apparent purpose. It was said: Changing the creation of God is that God Almighty created livestock for riding and eating, so they forbade them, and He created the sun, the moon, and the stones for the benefit of the servants, so they worshipped them instead of God. “And whoever takes Satan as a friend instead of God” meaning: a lord whom he obeys, has certainly suffered a clear loss.
4:120: 120- "He promises them and gives them false hope." His promise and hope are what he makes in a person's heart of long life and attaining the world. It may be by frightening him with poverty, preventing him from spending and maintaining family ties, as God Almighty said: "Satan threatens you with poverty" (al-Baqarah 2:268) and he gives them false hope that there will be no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Hell. "Satan promises them nothing but delusion, meaning falsehood.
4:121: 121- Their abode is Hell, and they will find no escape from it. That is, no escape or way out of it.
4:122: 122-God Almighty says: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is: from under the rooms and dwellings, “abiding therein forever. The promise of God is true. And who is more truthful than God in statement?”
4:123: 123- The Almighty said: It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book, the verse. Masruq, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak said: He meant it is not according to your desires, O Muslims, nor the desires of the People of the Book, meaning the Jews and Christians, and that is because they boasted, so the People of the Book said: Our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book came before your Book, so we are more deserving of God than you. And the Muslims said: Our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets and our Book rules over the Books, and we have believed in your Book and you have not believed in our Book, so we are more deserving. Mujahid said, It is not according to your desires, O polytheists of the People of the Book. This is because they said, There is no resurrection and no reckoning. The People of the Book said, The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. (al-Baqarah 2:80) None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian. (al-Baqarah 2:111) So God Almighty revealed, It is not according to your desires, meaning: The matter is not about desires, but rather the matter is about righteous deeds. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, and a group said: The verse is general and applies to every worker. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: “When this verse was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims and they said: O Messenger of God, who among us has not done evil except you, so what is the reward? He said: Some of it is in this world. Whoever does a good deed will have ten good deeds, and whoever is rewarded with a bad deed will have one of ten deducted, leaving him with nine good deeds. So woe to he whose ones outweigh his tenths. As for what is the reward in the Hereafter, his good deeds will be compared to his bad deeds, and in place of each bad deed he will be given a good deed, and the merit will be considered, and the reward will be given in Paradise, and every one with merit will be given his merit.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Abdusi, on the authority of Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Sulayman Al-Faqih in Baghdad, on the authority of Yahya bin Ja`far bin Al-Zubayr and Al-Harith bin Muhammad, who said: Ruh, who is Ibn `Ubadah, told us, on the authority of Musa bin `Ubaydah, who told me, Mawla bin Saba`, who said: I heard `Abdullah bin `Umar narrating on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, who said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when this verse was revealed to him: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me? He said: I said: Yes. He said: So recite it to me. He said: I do not know except that I felt a split in my back until I stretched out for it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr? I said: O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, and which of us has not done evil? We will be recompensed for every evil we have done?” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your companions. Believers will be rewarded for that in this world until they meet God with no sins. As for others, that will be collected for them until they are rewarded on the Day of Resurrection.”
4:124: 124- The Almighty said: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those will enter Paradise and not be wronged, [even] as much as a speck on a date seed. That is, the amount of a speck, which is the depression in the back of a date pit. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja`far, the people of Basra, and Abu Bakr read yadkhulun with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the kha’ here, it is in Surah Maryam and Ha Mim al-Mu’min. Abu `Amr added: yadkhulunha in Surah Fatir, and the others read it with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the kha’. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha on the authority of Masruq who said: When the verse was revealed, “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” the People of the Scripture said: We and you are the same. So this verse was revealed: And whoever does righteous deeds, the verse. And the following was also revealed:
4:125: 125- And who is better in religion, the most correct religion than one who submits his face to God, meaning: sincerely works for God, and it was said: entrusts his affair to God, and is a doer of good, meaning: monotheist, and follows the religion of Abraham, meaning: the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, in a pure monotheist, meaning: a sincere Muslim. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: And from the religion of Abraham is the prayer towards the Kaaba and circumambulating it and the rituals of Hajj, and Abraham was singled out because he was accepted by all nations, because he was sent with the religion of Abraham and some things were added to him. And God took Abraham as a close friend, a close friend, and closeness is the purity of affection. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: Abraham, peace be upon him, was the father of guests, and his house was on the middle of the road, and he hosted whoever passed by him from the people. Then the people were afflicted with a famine, so they crowded to the door of Abraham, peace be upon him, asking for food, and his provisions were provided to him every year from a friend of his in Egypt. So he sent his servants with the camels to the close friend who was in Egypt. His friend said to his servants: If Abraham, peace be upon him, only wanted it for himself, we would have endured it for him, for what has befallen the people has befallen us of hardship. So the messengers of Abraham, peace be upon him, returned, and they passed by a valley and said: [If] we carried from this valley so that the people would see that we have brought provisions, for we are ashamed to pass by them with our camels empty. So they filled those easy containers, then they came to Abraham and informed him, and Sarah was asleep. Abraham was concerned about the people’s place at his door, but his eyes overcame him and he slept, and Sarah woke up when the day had risen, and she said: Glory be to God, what has befallen The boys? They said: Yes. She said: So they did not bring anything? They said: Yes. So she went to the ghā’ir and opened it, and it was the finest flour of a young camel. She ordered the bakers to bake and feed the people. Abraham woke up and smelled the smell of food, so he said: O Sarah, where is this from? She said: From your Egyptian friend. He said: This is from your friend, God. He said: On that day, God took him as a friend. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of a friend is one in whose love there is no defect, and friendship is friendship, so he was called a friend because God loved him and chose him. It was said: It is from the word khalah, which means need. He was called a friend, meaning poor before God [because he did not make his poverty and need except for God, the Almighty]. The first is more correct because his saying, And God took Abraham as a friend requires friendship from both sides, and need from both sides cannot be imagined. Abu Al-Muzaffar bin Ahmad Al-Taimi narrated to us, Abu Muhammad Abd Al-Rahman bin Uthman bin Al-Qasim narrated to us, Khaithama bin Sulayman bin Haidah Al-Atrabulsi narrated to us, Abu Qilabah Al-Raqashi narrated to us, Bishr bin Umar narrated to us, Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If I were to take a close friend, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a close friend, but Abu Bakr is my brother and my companion, and God has taken your companion as a close friend.
4:126: 126- The Almighty said: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and God is ever encompassing of all things. That is, His knowledge encompasses all things.
4:127: 127- The Almighty said: “And they ask you about women. Say, ‘God gives you a ruling concerning them,’” the verse: Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: This verse was revealed about the daughters of Umm Kajah and their inheritance, and the story has already passed at the beginning of the surah. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: She is the orphan who is in the care of a man, and he is her guardian, so he desires to marry her if she is beautiful and wealthy for less than a year’s dowry, and if she is undesirable due to lack of wealth and beauty, he leaves her. In another narration: She is the orphan who is in the care of a man who has shared his wealth with him, so he desires to marry her because of her ugliness, and he hates for someone else to marry her, so he enters into his wealth and detains her until she dies and inherits her, so God forbade them from that. God the Almighty said: And they ask you for a legal opinion meaning: they inquire of you about women. “Say: God gives you a legal opinion about them and about what is recited to you in the Book.” It was said that its meaning is: And He gives you a legal opinion about what is recited to you. It was also said that its meaning is: And we give you a legal opinion about what is recited to you. He means: God gives you a legal opinion and His Book gives you a legal opinion about them. This is His Almighty saying: And give the orphans their property. His saying: in orphan women. This is an addition of the thing to itself because he meant by orphans the women, to whom you do not give, meaning: you do not give them, what has been prescribed for them, of their dowries, and you desire to marry them, meaning to marry them for their money and beauty for less than their dowries. Al-Hasan and a group said that he meant: you do not give them their right of inheritance, because they did not give women an inheritance, and you desire to marry them, meaning: not to marry them because of their ugliness. And the weak among children means: And he gives you a fatwa regarding the weak among children, who are the young, that you give them their rights, because the young were not given inheritance, meaning what is recited to you in the chapter on orphans from His statement: And give the orphans their property meaning by giving the rights of the young, And that you stand up for orphans with justice meaning: And he gives you a fatwa regarding the orphans with justice and fairness in their dowries and inheritances, And whatever good you do - indeed, God is ever Knowing of it, He will reward you for it.
4:128: 128- The Almighty said: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion The verse: It was revealed about Umrah, and it is said about Khawlah bint Muhammad bin Maslama, and about her husband Saad bin Al-Rabi' - and it is said Rafi bin Khadij - he married her when she was young, and when she grew old, he married a young woman, and preferred her over her, and he was rude to the daughter of Muhammad bin Maslama, so she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and complained to him, so this verse was revealed. Saeed bin Jubair said: There was a man who had an old wife and children from her, so he wanted to divorce her and marry another woman. She said: Do not divorce me and let me take care of my children and allocate to me from every two months if you wish, and if you wish do not allocate to me. He said: If that is appropriate, then it is more beloved to me. So he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him, so God the Most High revealed: And if a woman fears that is, knows from her husband that is, from her husband contempt that is, hatred. Al-Kalbi said: It means that he will not sleep with her or turn away from her and rarely sit with her. There is no blame upon them that is, upon the husband and the woman, that they reconcile, that is, they will come to terms. The people of Kufa read that they reconcile from reconcile, “between them an agreement” that is, in the division and maintenance, which is that the husband says to her: You have entered old age and I want to marry a beautiful young woman whom I prefer over you in the division of time night and day. If you are satisfied with this, then stay, and if you are reluctant, I will let you go. If she is satisfied, then she is the one who is doing good and is not forced to do that. If she is not satisfied without her right to the division, then the husband must fulfill her right to the division and maintenance or release her with kindness. If he keeps her and fulfills her right with I hate him, he is good. Sulayman bin Yasar said about this verse on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: If she reconciles with him regarding some of her right to the division and maintenance, then that is permissible as long as she is satisfied. If she denies it after the reconciliation, then that is her right and she has her right. Muqatil bin Hayyan said about this verse: It is that a man has an older woman and marries a younger woman. He says to the older woman: I have given you a share of my money on the condition that I divide more for this younger woman than I divide for you, and she is satisfied with what they have agreed upon. If she refuses to be satisfied, then he must be fair between them in the division. On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding this verse, he said: A woman is with a man and his eyes turn away from her because of her ugliness or old age, so she hates to leave him. If she gives him from her money, then it is permissible for him. If she gives him from her days, then it is permissible for him. And reconciliation is better. Meaning: keeping her after giving him a choice, and reconciliation on giving up some of her right to share and support is better than separation, as it is narrated that Sawdah, may God be pleased with her, was an old woman and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to leave her, so he said: Do not divorce me, for I am only responsible for sending among your wives. You have given my turn to Aisha, may God be pleased with her. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept her, and he used to divide her day for Aisha and Sawdah’s day, may God be pleased with her. The Almighty said: And the souls are inclined to greed, meaning: the greed of each of the spouses for his share from the other. Greed is the ugliest form of miserliness, and its true meaning is the eagerness to prevent good. But if you do good, meaning: you reform, and fear injustice. It was said: This is addressed to the spouses, meaning: if you do good by staying with her despite dislike and fear her injustice, then indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted, so He will reward you for your deeds.
4:129: 129- The Almighty said: "And you will never be able to be equal between wives," meaning: you will never be able to be equal between women in love and inclination of the heart, "even if you should strive to be equal, so do not incline," meaning: to the one you love, "totally" in division and spending, meaning: do not follow your desires with your actions, "leaving her as one in suspense," meaning: leaving the other as one who is tied up, neither single nor married. Qatada said: as if she is imprisoned, and in the reading of Abi bin Ka'b: as if she is imprisoned. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Qilabah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to divide his time among his wives, and he would be fair and say: O God, this is my division of what I own, so do not blame me for what You own and I do not. Some of them narrated it on the authority of Abu Qilabah on the authority of Abdullah bin Yazid on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, in a continuous chain of transmission. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever has two wives and leans towards one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side leaning. “But if you make amends and fear God,” and injustice, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
4:130: 130- And if they separate, meaning: the husband and the woman by divorce, God will enrich each from His abundance, from His provision, meaning: the woman with another husband and the husband with another woman, and God is all-Encompassing and Wise, all-Encompassing in grace and mercy, and wise in what He has commanded and forbidden. The ruling of the verse is: If a man has two or more wives, he must treat them equally in dividing his time. If he does not treat them equally in dividing his time, he has disobeyed God Almighty, and he must make up for the wronged woman. Equality is a condition for spending the night with her, but not for sexual intercourse, because it depends on the activity and that is not up to him. If he marries a free woman and a slave woman, he may spend two nights with the free woman and one night with the slave woman. If he marries a new woman in addition to his old wives, he should specify the new woman by spending seven nights with her in succession if she is a virgin. If she is previously married, then three nights, then he should make up for all of them equally after that. He does not have to make up for these nights for the old wives. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, on the authority of Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail, on the authority of Yusuf bin Rashid, on the authority of Abu Usamah Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Ayoub and Khalid, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: It is from the Sunnah that if a man marries a virgin while he has already been married, he should stay with her for seven days, then divide the time. And if he marries a previously married woman, he should stay with her for three days, then divide the time. Abu Qilabah said: If I wanted, I could say that Anas traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If a man wants to travel for a need, it is permissible for him to take some of his wives with him after he draws lots among them for it. Then he is not obligated to make up for the rest of the time of their travel, even if it is long, if his stay in his country does not exceed the time of the travelers. The evidence for this is what Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal, on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Shafi’i, on the authority of my uncle Muhammad bin Ali bin Shafi’, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to travel, he drew lots among his wives, and whichever one’s lot fell, he would go with her. But if he wanted to travel for a long time, he did not have the right to single out some of them, whether by drawing lots or otherwise.”
4:131: 131- The Almighty said: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth as servants and kings. And We have already enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you, meaning the people of the Torah and the Gospel and all the previous nations in their books, and upon you, the people of the Qur’an in your book, that you fear God, meaning: unify God and obey Him. And if you disbelieve, in what God has enjoined upon you, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, it was said: God has angels in the heavens and the earth who are more obedient to Him than you. And God is Self-sufficient, from all His creation, not in need of their obedience, Praiseworthy, praised for His blessings.
4:132: 132-And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs. Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means a witness that there are slaves in it, and it was said: a defender and protector. If it is said: What is the benefit in repeating the words of God Almighty: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? It is said: Each of them has a face. As for the first, its meaning is: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He commands you to fear Him, so accept His command. As for the second, He says: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and God is Self-sufficient, meaning: He is Self-sufficient and His is the kingdom, so ask Him for whatever you ask. As for the third, He says: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs, meaning: To Him belongs the kingdom, so take Him as a Disposer of affairs and do not rely on anyone other than Him.
4:133: 133- The Almighty’s saying: If He wills, He can do away with you, destroy you, O people, meaning: the infidels, and bring others, meaning others better than you and more obedient, and God is capable of that, capable.
4:134: 134- Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. Whoever desires worldly gain through his actions and does not desire God Almighty through them, God will give him worldly gain or repel from him what God desires, and he will have no reward in the Hereafter. Whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter through his actions, God will give him what he desires from this world and will reward him with Paradise in the Hereafter: And God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
4:135: 135- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for God, meaning: be persistently standing firm in testifying with justice, that is: with justice for God. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Be persistently standing firm in testifying against whomever it is, even if it is against yourselves or your parents and your relatives, in the womb, meaning: speak the truth even if it is against yourselves by admission or your parents and your relatives, then establish it against them for God, and do not favor a rich person because of his wealth, and do not have mercy on a poor person because of his poverty, for that is the Almighty's saying: If he is rich or poor, God is more worthy of them both, than you, meaning: establish it for the one against whom the testimony is given even if he is rich, and for the one for whom the testimony is given even if he is poor, then God is more worthy of them both than you, meaning entrust their matter to God. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is that God knows best about them. So do not follow your desires lest you be just, meaning, be unjust and incline toward falsehood instead of truth. It was said: Its meaning is, do not follow your desires in order to be just, meaning, to be just, as it is said: Do not follow your desires in order to please your Lord. And if you twist meaning: distort the testimony to invalidate the truth or turn away from it and conceal it and do not establish it. It is said: Twist meaning: push each other in establishing the testimony. It is said: I twisted his right if he pushed it, or I delayed it. It was said: This is addressed to the judges in their twisting of the jaws. He says: And if you twist, meaning: you lean toward one of the two opponents or turn away from him. Ibn Amir and Hamzah read tala with a damma on the lam. It was said: Its original form is talawa, so one of the two waws was deleted for ease. It was said: Its meaning is: And if you twist the performance of the testimony or turn away and leave it, then indeed, God is, with what you do, Knowing.
4:136: 136- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, believe in God and His Messenger the verse: Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This verse was revealed about Abdullah bin Salam, Asad and Asid, the sons of Kaab, and Tha'laba bin Qais and Salam, the nephew of Abdullah bin Salam, and Salamah, the son of his brother, and Yamin bin Yamin. These are the believers from the People of the Book who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We believe in you and your book and in Moses and the Torah and Ezra, and we disbelieve in all the books and messengers other than it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Rather, believe in God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur'an and in Moses and the Torah, and in every book before it." So God revealed this verse: O you who have believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur'an and in Moses, peace be upon him, and the Torah Believe in God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Book which He sent down to His Messenger meaning the Qur'an, and the Book which He sent down to His Messenger Before, from the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and all other books. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Abu Amr read nazal and anzal with a damma on the nun and the alif. The others read nazal and anzal with a fatha, meaning God sent down. And whoever disbelieves in God and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray. So when this verse was revealed, they said: “We believe in God and His Messenger and the Qur’an and every Messenger and Book that came before the Qur’an, and the angels and the Last Day. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims to Him.” Ad-Dahhak said: He meant the Jews and Christians by it, saying: O you who believe in Moses and Jesus, believe in Muhammad and the Qur’an. Mujahid said: He meant the hypocrites by it, saying: O you who believe with your tongue, believe with your heart. Abu Al-Aaliyah and a group said: This is addressed to the believers, saying: O you who believe, believe, meaning stand up and remain steadfast in faith, just as it is said to one who stands up: Stand up until I return to you, meaning stand firm. It was said: What is meant by it are the polytheists, meaning: O you who believe in Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, believe in God and His Messenger.
4:137: 137-And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief, Qatada said: They are the Jews who believed in Moses, then disbelieved afterward by worshipping the calf, then believed in the Torah, then disbelieved in Jesus, peace be upon him, then increased in disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: It is for all the People of the Book who believed in their Prophet and then disbelieved in him, and believed in the Book that was revealed to him and then disbelieved in it, and their disbelief in it: they abandoned it and then increased in their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: This is about a people who apostatized, who believed, then apostatized, then believed, then apostatized, then believed, then apostatized, then believed, then apostatized. And is the repentance of someone like this accepted? It was narrated from Ali may God be pleased with him: His repentance is not accepted, rather he is killed, because God the Almighty said: God would never forgive them, and most of the scholars agree that his repentance is acceptable. Mujahid said: Then they increased in disbelief, meaning they died in it. God would never forgive them, as long as they persisted in that, nor guide them to a way, meaning a path to the truth. If it is said: What is the meaning of his saying God would never forgive them, and it is known that he would not be forgiven if he remained a Muslim.
4:138: 138- Give good tidings to the hypocrites, tell them, O Muhammad, that they will have a painful punishment. The good report is any report that changes the complexion of the face, whether it is pleasant or unpleasant. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is to put the punishment in place of your good report for him, as the Arabs say: Your greeting is the blow and your rebuke is the sword, meaning: [instead of] the greeting. Then he described the hypocrites and said:
4:139: 139- Those who take the disbelievers as allies, meaning: they take the Jews as allies and supporters or confidants "instead of the believers. Do they seek honor with them?", meaning: assistance and support for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions? It was said: Do they seek strength and supremacy with them? For honor, meaning: supremacy, strength and power, is entirely for God.
4:140: 140- And it has already been revealed to you in the Book, Asim and Yaqub read nazal with the fatha on the noon and the zay: meaning: God has revealed, and the others read nazal with the damma on the noon and the kasra on the zay, meaning: upon you, O group of Muslims, that when you hear the verses of God meaning the Qur'an, being denied and ridiculed, then do not sit with them meaning: with those who ridicule, until they engage in a conversation other than that meaning: they engage in a conversation other than mocking Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur'an, and this is a reference to what God revealed in Surat Al-An'am And when you see those who engage in discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they engage in a conversation other than that Al-An'am-68. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: This verse includes every innovator in religion and every innovator until the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, you will be like them, meaning: If you sit with them while they are chattering and mocking and you are satisfied with it, then you are like them. If they chatter and mock, then there is nothing wrong with sitting with them, although it is disliked. Al-Hasan said: It is not permissible to sit with them even if they chatter and mock, because God Almighty says: But if Satan should cause you to forget, then do not remain after the remembrance with the wrongdoing people. The majority are of the first opinion. The verse of Al-An’am is Meccan, and this is Medinan, and the later one is more appropriate: Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together.
4:141: 141- Those who lie in wait for you, [wait for you to be afflicted], meaning: the hypocrites. But if you have a victory from God, meaning: triumph and spoils, they will say, to you, Were we not with you in your religion in jihad, we were with you so give us a share of the spoils, and if the disbelievers have a share, meaning a state and victory over the Muslims, they will say, meaning: the spenders for the disbelievers, Did we not gain control over you?, and gaining control means taking over and prevailing. God Almighty said: Satan gained control over them Al-Mujadilah-19, meaning: he took control and overcame, saying: Did we not inform you of the shame of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions and inform you of their secret. Al-Mubarrad said: The hypocrites say to the infidels, Did we not overcome you in your opinion and prevent you and turn you away from the believers? That is, from entering their group. It was said that its meaning is, Did we not gain control over you by supporting you and prevent you from the believers? That is, we repelled the attack of the believers by discouraging them from you and by corresponding with you about their report and affairs. The hypocrites intended by this statement to show favor to the infidels. God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, meaning: between the people of faith and the people of hypocrisy, and God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers, Ali said: in the Hereafter. Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them: any argument, and it was said: an appearance over the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
4:142: 142- "The hypocrites seek to deceive God, but He is the One who deceives them," meaning they treat Him as deceivers do, and He is the One who deceives them, meaning: He will reward them for their deception, and that is because they will be given light on the Day of Resurrection as the believers are, so the believers will proceed with their light on the path and the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished. "And when they stand up for prayer," meaning: the hypocrites, "they stand up lazily," meaning: sluggishly, not intending God by it. If someone sees them, they pray, otherwise they turn away and do not pray. "They show off to the people," meaning: they do that to show off to the people, not to follow God's command. "And they do not remember God except a little." Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Al-Hasan said: He only said that because they do it for show and to be heard, and if they intended by that little to please God, it would have been a lot. Qatada said: The mention of the hypocrites is only a little because God, the Most High, did not accept it, and everything that God accepts is a lot.
4:143: 143- "Wavering between that", meaning: hesitating and confused between disbelief and belief, "neither with these nor with those", meaning: they are not among the believers, so what is due to the believers is due to them, and they are not among the disbelievers, so what is taken from the disbelievers is taken from them, "And he whom God sends astray - you will not find for him a way", meaning: a path to guidance. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani told us, he said Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad Al-Farsi told us, I told Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul Wahhab - meaning Al-Thaqafi - told us, Abdullah bin Umar told us, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The example of the hypocrite is like that of a stray sheep between two flocks, it strays to this one at one time and to that one at another time.
4:144: 144- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. God forbade the believers from befriending the disbelievers. He said: Do you want to make for God a clear authority over you? That is, a clear argument for your punishment. Then He mentioned the ranks of the hypocrites, and He, the Most High, said:
4:145: 145- The hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire. The people of Kufa read in the depths with a silent ra and the rest read it with a fatha. They are two vowels like za'n and za'n and nahr and nahr. Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, said: in the lowest depths in iron coffins locked in the Fire. Abu Hurairah said: a locked house in which the Fire is blazing from above and below them. And you will not find for them a helper to prevent the punishment.
4:146: 146- Except for those who repent from hypocrisy and believe and reform their work and hold fast to God, trust in God and devote their religion to God, he meant sincerity in the heart, because hypocrisy is disbelief of the heart, so its removal is by sincerity of the heart, they will be with the believers Al-Farra' said: from the believers, and God will give the believers in the Hereafter a great reward, meaning: Paradise, and the ya was deleted in the script from the one who gives because it was dropped in the pronunciation, and it was dropped in the pronunciation because the lam in God was still.
4:147: 147- The Almighty’s saying: What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful? That is, if you are grateful for His blessings and believe in Him, there is an advancement and a delay in it, the meaning is: if you believe and are grateful, because gratitude is of no use with the absence of faith, and this is a question with the meaning of confirmation, meaning: He does not punish the believer who is not grateful, because His punishment of His servants does not increase His kingdom, and His leaving them punished for their actions does not decrease His authority, and gratitude is the opposite of disbelief, and disbelief is concealing the blessing, and gratitude is showing it, and God is ever Appreciative and Knowing, so gratitude from God the Almighty is contentment with a little of His worship and the weakening of the reward for it, and gratitude from the servant is obedience, and from God is the reward.
4:148: 148-His saying, God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. Meaning: God does not like the public mention of ugly words except by one who has been wronged. It is permissible for the wronged person to report the injustice of the oppressor and to supplicate against him. God the Most High said, But whoever retaliates after being wronged - against those there is no blame. (al-Shura 42:41). Al-Hasan said: His supplication against him is to say, "O God, help me against him. O God, extract my right from them." It is said: If you wish, it is permissible for him to say something similar, but not more. Abu Abdullah Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Al-Ala bin Abdul-Rahman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The two who insult each other, whatever they say, is at fault, so long as the one who was wronged has not retaliated. Mujahid said this about a guest who stays with a people and they do not welcome him or treat him well, then he has the right to complain and mention what was done to him. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Al-Layth told us, Yazid bin Abi Habib told us, Abu Al-Khair told us, Uqbah bin Amir said: We said, O Messenger of God, you send us and we stay with a people and they do not welcome us, so what do you think? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: “If you stay with a people and they command you what is appropriate for a guest, then accept it. If they do not do so, then take from them the right of a guest that is appropriate for them.” Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim and Zaid bin Aslam read: Except for he who wrongs with the opening of the Dhad and the Lam, meaning: but the wrongdoer was spoken to aloud with evil. It was said that its meaning is: God does not like the loud recitation of the Surahs, but he who wrongs speaks aloud. The first reading is the well-known one, and God is All-Hearing to the supplication of the wronged, All-Knowing of the punishment of the wrongdoer.
4:149: 149- The Almighty said: If you disclose a good deed, meaning: a good deed and do it, ten will be written for him, and if they do it but he does not do it, one good deed will be written for him, which is His saying: or you conceal it, and it was said that what is meant by good is money, meaning: if you disclose a charity that you give openly or conceal it and give it secretly, or you pardon an offense, meaning: an injustice, then indeed, God is ever Pardoning and Powerful, so He is more deserving of pardoning you on the Day of Resurrection.
4:150: 150- The Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His messengers the verse was revealed about the Jews, because they believed in Moses, peace be upon him, the Torah and Aziz, and disbelieved in Jesus, the Gospel, Muhammad and the Qur’an, and they want to make distinction between God and His messengers and say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ and they want to adopt a way in between, meaning: a religion between Judaism and Islam and a school of thought to which they adhere.
4:151: 151-Those are the disbelievers, truly. He verified their disbelief to know that disbelief in some of them is like disbelief in all of them. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
4:152: 152- And those who believed in God and His messengers, all of them, and made no distinction between any of them, meaning: between the messengers, who are the believers, they say: We do not differentiate between any of His messengers, those - He will give them their rewards, for their belief in God, His books, and His messengers. Hafs read from Asim, He will give them with a ya, meaning: God will give them and the rest with a noon/ and God is Forgiving and Merciful.
4:153: 153- The Almighty said: The People of the Scripture ask you the verse, and that is because Ka’b bin Al-Ashraf and Phinehas bin Azura from the Jews said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you are a prophet, then bring us a complete book from the heaven, as Moses, peace be upon him, brought it, so God revealed to him: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. This question from them was a question of control and suggestion, not a question of submission, and God Almighty does not send down verses based on the suggestion of His servants. His statement, And they asked Moses something greater than that means: greater than that, meaning: the seventy people with whom Moses, peace be upon him, went out to the mountain, and they said, ‘Show us God openly’ meaning: clearly. Abu Ubaidah said: its meaning is that they said openly, Show us God. “Then the thunderbolt seized them because of their wrongdoing, then they took the calf” meaning as a god, after the clear proofs had come to them, so We pardoned that, and We did not eradicate them. It was said: This is a call to repentance, meaning: Those who committed crimes repented, so We pardoned them, so you repent so that We may pardon you, And We gave Moses a clear authority meaning: a clear proof from the miracles, which are the nine verses.
4:154: 154- The Almighty said: And We raised the Mount above them with their covenant and said to them, ‘Enter the gate, bowing down.’ And We said to them, ‘Do not transgress on the Sabbath.’ The people of Medina read it with a shaddah on the dal and a fathah on the ‘ayn. Nafi’ with the narration of Warsh, and the others make it jazm. Its meaning is: Do not transgress and do not wrong by hunting whales in it. And We took from them a firm covenant.
4:155: 155- The Almighty’s saying: Because they broke their covenant, meaning: because they broke it, and what is related like the Almighty’s saying: Then because of mercy from God (Al Imran 3:159), and similar to it, “And their disbelief in the signs of God and their killing of the prophets without right and their saying, ‘Our hearts are covered.’ Rather, God has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief,” meaning: He has sealed them, So they will not believe except a few, meaning: of those who denied the messengers, not of those whose hearts were sealed, because of those whose hearts God has sealed, they will never believe, and by a few he meant Abdullah bin Salam and his companions, and it was said: its meaning is that they will not believe a little or a lot.
4:156: 156-And because of their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander, when they accused her of adultery.
4:157: 157- "And their saying, 'We have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the Messenger of God.' But they killed him not, nor crucified him, but it appeared to them so." That is because God Almighty cast the likeness of Jesus, peace be upon him, on the one who led the Jews to him. It was said that they imprisoned Jesus, peace be upon him, in a house and put a guard over him, so God Almighty cast the likeness of Jesus, peace be upon him, on the guard, so they killed him. And other things were said, as we mentioned in Surat Al Imran. God the Almighty said: And those who differed concerning him, concerning his killing, are in doubt about it, meaning, concerning his killing. Al-Kalbi said: Their difference of opinion about it is that the Jews said, We killed him, and a group of the Christians said, We killed him, and a group of them said, Neither these nor those killed him, but rather God raised him up to the heavens while we were looking at him. It was said: God the Almighty cast a resemblance of the face of Jesus, peace be upon him, onto the face of Satyafus, but He did not cast it onto his body, so they differed about it. Some of them said, We killed Jesus, because the face is the face of Jesus, peace be upon him. Some of them said, We did not kill him, because his body is not the body of Jesus, peace be upon him. So they differed. Al-Suddi said: Their difference of opinion is because they said, If this is Jesus, then where is our companion? And if this is our companion, then where is Jesus? God the Almighty said, They have no knowledge of it, of the truth of whether he was killed or not, except the following of conjecture, but they follow conjecture in killing him. God the Almighty said, And they did not kill him for certain, meaning, They did not kill Jesus for certain.
4:158: 158-Rather, God raised him up to Himself. It was said that his saying certainly refers to what comes after it, and his saying and they did not kill him is a complete statement, the meaning of which is: Rather, God raised him to Himself for sure. The ha in they did not kill him is a metaphor for Jesus, peace be upon him. Al-Farra’, may God have mercy on him, said: Its meaning is: And they did not kill the one they thought was Jesus for sure. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that its meaning is: They did not kill what they thought for sure. And God is Exalted in Might is impregnable by taking revenge on the Jews, Wise is He ruled with the curse and wrath upon them, so He sent against them Daytus bin Aspsianus the Roman, who killed a great number of them.
4:159: 159- The Almighty said: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, meaning: There is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus, peace be upon him. This is the opinion of most of the commentators and scholars. As for His statement before his death, they differed regarding this metaphor. Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said: It is a metaphor for the People of the Book, and its meaning is: There is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus, peace be upon him, before his death, if he falls into hardship when his faith will not benefit him, whether he is burned, drowned, thrown into a well, a wall falls on him, a wild animal eats him, or dies suddenly. This is a narration on the authority of Abu Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, who said: It was said to Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: What do you think if he falls from the top of a house? He said: He speaks it in the air. He said: It was said: What do you think if one of them is beheaded? He said: His tongue stutters. Some people said that the letter ha in his death is a metaphor for Jesus, peace be upon him, meaning: “And who among the People of the Book will not believe in Jesus before the death of Jesus, peace be upon him, when he descends from heaven at the end of time, and no one will remain who will not believe in him until the religion is one, the religion of Islam.” We narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The son of Mary will soon descend among you as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the pig, abolish the jizya, and wealth will be so abundant that no one will accept it. All religions will perish in his time except Islam. He will kill the Antichrist and will remain on earth for forty years, then he will die and the Muslims will pray over him.” Abu Hurairah said: Read, if you wish, ‘And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death,’ before the death of Jesus, son of Mary. Then Abu Hurairah repeated it three times. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah: The letter ha in his saying that they will believe in him is a metaphor for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said that no book will die until it believes in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: It refers back to God Almighty. He says: There is none from the People of the Scripture but that he believes in God Almighty, before his death when he is witnessed, when his faith will not benefit him. God Almighty says: And on the Day of Resurrection he will be, meaning Jesus, peace be upon him, a witness over them, that he delivered the message of his Lord to them, and acknowledged servitude to himself [as God Almighty said, reporting on him: And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them (al-Ma’idah 5:117), and every prophet is a witness over his nation]. God Almighty says: How then will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], over these as a witness? (An-Nisa’: 41).
4:160: 160- The Almighty said: Then because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, which is what was mentioned previously about their breaking the covenant, their disbelief in the signs of God, their slander against Mary, and their saying: We killed the Messiah, “We forbade them good things which had been lawful to them,” which is what was mentioned in Surat Al-An’am, where He said: And We forbade those who were Jews every animal having claws Al-An’am-146. The structure of the verse: Because of the wrongdoing of those who are Jews, which is what we mentioned, and because of their turning away and because they turned themselves and others away from the way of God a lot, meaning: from the religion of God a lot.
4:161: 161- And their taking of usury, although they were forbidden from it, in the Torah, and their consuming of people's wealth unjustly, from bribery in ruling, and the food they obtain from their common people, We punished them by forbidding them good things, so whenever they committed a major sin, something of the good things that were permissible for them was forbidden to them, God Almighty said, That is how We recompensed them for their transgression, and indeed, We are truthful. Al-An'am-146 And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
4:162: 162- But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them, meaning: not all the People of the Book have this characteristic, but those firmly rooted in knowledge who have insight among them, and he meant by it those Jewish scholars who converted to Islam such as Abdullah bin Salam and his companions, and the believers, meaning: the Muhajireen and the Ansar, believe in what has been revealed to you, meaning: the Qur'an, and what was revealed before you, meaning: all the revealed books, and those who establish prayer, they differed about the reason for its being in the accusative case, so it was narrated from Aisha / may God be pleased with her and Aban bin Othman: that it is a mistake from the scribe that it should be written and those who establish prayer and likewise his saying in Surat Al-Ma'idah Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians Al-Ma'idah - 62, and his saying Indeed, these two are magicians Taha - 63, they said: that is a mistake from the scribe. Uthman said: There is a mistake in the Qur’an that the Arabs will correct with their tongues. It was said to him: Why don’t you change it? He said: Leave it, for it does not make permissible what is forbidden nor forbid what is permissible. The majority of the companions and scholars agree that it is correct, but they differed about it. It was said: It is an accusative of praise. It was said: It is an accusative with an implied verb, the meaning of which is: I mean those who establish prayer and they are the ones who give zakat. It was said: Its position is in the genitive case. They differed about its meaning. Some of them said: Its meaning is: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them and those who establish prayer. It was said that its meaning is: They believe in what was revealed to you and to those who establish prayer. Then His saying: And those who give zakat is a return to the first sequence, And the believers in God and the Last Day - those - We will give them a great reward. Hamza read siyu’tihum with a ya’ and the rest with a noon.
4:163: 163- The Almighty said: "Indeed, We have revealed to you" This is based on what came before from His saying: "The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven" An-Nisaa' 153, so when God mentioned their faults and sins, they became angry and denied everything that God Almighty revealed, and they said: God did not send down anything to any human being, so He revealed: "And they did not estimate God with His true estimate when they said: God has not sent down anything to any human being" Al-An'am 91 and He revealed: "Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him" So He mentioned a number of the messengers to whom He revealed, and He began by mentioning Noah, peace be upon him, because he was a human being like Adam, peace be upon him, God Almighty said: "And We made his descendants the survivors" As-Saffat 77 and because he was the first prophet of the prophets of the Sharia, and the first warner of polytheism, and the first whose nation was punished for rejecting his call, and he destroyed the people of the earth with his call, and he was the longest The prophets lived a long life and their miracle was in themselves, because they lived a thousand years and not a tooth of theirs fell out, not a hair of theirs grew, and not a single one of their strengths diminished. No prophet endured the harm of his people as he endured throughout his long life. God the Almighty said: And We inspired Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, who are the sons of Jacob, and Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms, Al-A’mash and Hamzah read Psalms, and the Psalms with a damma on the zay wherever it was, meaning: the plural of Zabur, meaning We gave David books and pages that were written, meaning: written. The others read with a fatha on the zay, which is the name of the book that God the Almighty revealed to David, peace be upon him, and in it was praise, glorification, and thanks to God the Almighty.
