David would go out into the wilderness, stand up, and recite the Psalms, and the scholars of the Children of Israel would stand with him, so they would stand behind him and the people would stand behind the scholars, and the jinn would stand behind the people, the greatest and the greatest, and the devils would stand behind the jinn, and the beasts that were in the mountains would come and stand before him in amazement at what they heard from him, and the birds would flutter over their heads. But when he committed the sin, he did not see that, so it was said to him: That is the comfort of obedience, and this is the loneliness of disobedience. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Bakr Al-Jawzaqi told us, Abu Al-Abbas told us, Yahya bin Zakariya told us, Al-Hasan bin Hammad told us, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Umawi told us, Talha bin Yahya, on the authority of Abi bin Abi Musa, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you had seen me last night while I was listening to your recitation, you would have been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David. He said: By God, O Messenger of God, if I had known that you were listening to its recitation, I would have recite it. Whenever Umar, may God be pleased with him, saw him, he would say: Remember us, O Abu Musa, and he would recite in his presence.
4:164: 164- The Almighty said: "And messengers We have mentioned to you before," meaning: And as We revealed to Noah and to the messengers, "messengers" is in the accusative case by removing the letter of description, and it was said: Its meaning is and We have mentioned to you messengers, and in Abu's reading "And messengers We have mentioned to you before, And messengers We have not mentioned to you, and God spoke to Moses directly," Al-Farra' said: The Arabs call what is conveyed to a person speech by any way it is conveyed, but they do not confirm it with the infinitive, so if it is confirmed with the infinitive, and it is only the reality of the speech - like the will - it is said: So-and-so wanted a will, meaning the reality of the will, and it is said: He wanted the wall, and it is not said that the wall wanted a will because it is a metaphor and not a reality.
4:165: 165- The Almighty said: "Messengers as bearers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers," and they will say: You did not send to us a messenger and you did not send down to us a book, and in it is evidence that God Almighty does not punish creation before sending the Messenger, God Almighty said: "And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger Al-Israa-15, And God is Exalted in Might and Wise." Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Musa bin Ismail, I told Abu Awanah, I told Abdul Malik, from Warad, the scribe of Al-Mughira, from Al-Mughira, he said: "Saad bin Ubadah, may God be pleased with him, said: If I saw a man with my wife, I would strike him with the sword without hesitation, so that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Are you amazed at Saad's jealousy? By God, I am more jealous than him, and God is more jealous than me, and because of God's jealousy God has forbidden indecencies, whether apparent or hidden, and No one loves an apology more than God, and for that reason He sent the warners and the bringers of good tidings. No one loves praise more than God, and for that reason God promised Paradise.”
4:166: 166- The Almighty said: But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: "The leaders of Mecca came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, we asked the Jews about you and about your description in their book, and they claimed that they did not know you. A group of Jews entered upon him, and he said to them: By God, I know that you know that I am the Messenger of God. They said: We do not know that. So God Almighty revealed: "But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you" if they deny you and call you a liar. He revealed it with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness, and sufficient is God as a witness."
4:167: 167-Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted from the way of God, by concealing the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, have certainly gone far astray.
4:168: 168-Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged It was said: He only said wronged - even though their wrongdoing was due to their disbelief - as an emphasis. It was also said: Its meaning is that they disbelieved in God and wronged Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by concealing his description. God would not forgive them nor guide them to a path, meaning: the religion of Islam.
4:169: 169-Except the path to Hell, meaning Judaism, abiding therein forever, and that is easy for God. This is regarding those who He previously ruled that they would not believe.
4:170: 170- O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. Its meaning is: So believe, and faith will be better for you. But if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and God is ever Knowing and Wise.
4:171: 171-O People of the Scripture, do not go to extremes in your religion, was revealed about the Christians, who are of different types: the Jacobites, the Melkites, the Nestorians, and the Marcists. The Jacobites said: Jesus is God, and so did the Melkites. The Nestorians said: Jesus is the son of God, and the Marcists said: He is the third of three. They were taught by a Jewish man called Paul, who will come in Surat At-Tawbah, God willing. Al-Hasan said: It is possible that it was revealed about the Jews and Christians, because they both went to extremes regarding the matter of Jesus, the Jews by falling short, and the Christians by exceeding the limit, and the root of extremism is exceeding the limit, and it is forbidden in religion. God Almighty said: Do not go to extremes in your religion, do not be strict in your religion so that you slander God, and do not say about God except the truth, do not say that He has a partner or a son, The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was only the Messenger of God and His Word, which is His saying, Be, and he was a human being without a father, [and it was said otherwise], He cast it into Mary, meaning He informed her and told her about it, as one says, I cast a good word to you, “and a spirit from Him,” it is a spirit like all other spirits except that God Almighty added it to Himself [as an honor]. It was said: The spirit is the breath that Gabriel, peace be upon him, breathed into Mary’s armour, so she became pregnant with the permission of God Almighty. The breath was called a spirit because it is a wind/that comes out of the spirit and is added to itself because it was by his command. It was said: A spirit from Him, meaning a mercy. So Jesus, peace be upon him, was a mercy for those who followed him and believed in him. It was said: The spirit: the revelation. He revealed to Mary the good report, and to Gabriel, peace be upon him, the blowing, and to Jesus, Be, and it was, as God Almighty said: He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command (al-Nahl 16:2), meaning: by revelation. It was said: He meant Gabriel, peace be upon him, by the spirit, meaning: and His word that He cast into Mary, and He also cast it to her as a spirit from Him by His command, and he is Gabriel, peace be upon him, as He said: The angels and the Spirit descend (al-Qadr 97:4), meaning: Gabriel is in her, and He said: Then We sent to her Our Spirit (Maryam 19:17), meaning: Gabriel. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Sadaqah bin Al-Fadl told us, Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’, Amr bin Hani told us, Junada bin Umayya told us, on the authority of Ubadah, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever bears witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner for Him, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that Jesus is the servant and Messenger of God and His Word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise and Hell are true, God will admit him to Paradise regardless of his deeds.” So believe in God and His messengers and do not say, ‘Three,’ meaning: do not say, They are three, as the Christians used to say: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Stop, it will be better for you. The meaning is: Stop, it will be better for you to stop. “God is only one God. Glory be to Him. He is far above having a son.” And know that adoption is not permissible for God Almighty, because adoption is only permissible for someone who can imagine having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs.
4:172: 172- The Almighty said: The Messiah would not disdain to be a servant of God, and that is "that the delegation of Najran said: O Muhammad, you are criticizing our companion and saying: He is a servant of God. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not a disgrace for Jesus, peace be upon him, to be a servant of God. So He revealed: "The Messiah would not disdain He would not be arrogant or haughty, and disdain is arrogance with haughtiness, nor the angels brought near," and they are the bearers of honor, they do not disdain to be servants of God. This verse is used as evidence by those who say that the angels are superior to humans, because God, the Almighty, ascended from Jesus to the angels, and no one ascends except to the highest. It is not said: So-and-so is not disdainful of this or his servant, rather it is said: So-and-so is not disdainful of this or his master, and they have no argument in it because He did not say that to raise their status above the status of humans, but rather in response to those who say that the angels are gods, just as He responded to the Christians for saying that the Messiah is the son of God, and he said in response to the Christians, according to their claim, that they say that the angels are superior. God Almighty said: And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them all to Himself. It was said: Disdain is arrogance with haughtiness, and haughtiness is loftiness and magnification without haughtiness.
4:173: 173- As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty of multiplying what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant of His worship, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper.
4:174: 174- The Almighty said: O mankind, there has come to you a proof from your Lord, meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the saying of most commentators. It was said: It is the Qur’an, and proof is the argument. And We have sent down to you a clear light, clear means the Qur’an.
4:175: 175- But as for those who believed in God and held fast to Him, they refrained from the deviance of Satan, He will admit them to mercy from Him and bounty, meaning Paradise, and guide them to Himself on a straight path. God Almighty said: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not related to relatives who are not related to others.” “It was revealed about Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited me while I was sick and out of my mind. He performed ablution and poured some of his ablution water over me, and I regained my senses. I said: O Messenger of God, to whom does the inheritance belong? Only those who are not related to others inherit from me? Then, “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not related to others.” We have already mentioned the meaning of those who are not related to others and the ruling of the verse at the beginning of the surah. This verse explains the ruling on the inheritance of brothers from the father and mother or the father.
4:176: 176- His statement, They ask you means: They inquire of you and ask you, "Say: God gives you a fatwa concerning those who are not related to others." If a man dies and has no children and has a sister, she shall have half of what he leaves behind and he shall inherit from her, meaning if the sister dies, then all of her inheritance goes to the brother, If she has no children, if she has a son, then the brother has nothing, and if her child is a female, then the brother gets what is left over from the daughters' share, If there are two of them, they shall have two-thirds of what he leaves behind, he meant two or more, which is that whoever dies and has sisters, they get two-thirds, And if they are brothers, both men and women, then the male shall have the equivalent of the share of two females, "God makes clear to you, lest you go astray," Al-Farra' may God have mercy on him said, Abu Ubaidah: Its meaning is that you should not go astray, and it was said that its meaning is: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, "And God is Knowing of all things." Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abdullah bin Raja, I told Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, may God be pleased with them, who said: The last Surah to be revealed in full was Baraa’ah, and the last verse to be revealed was the conclusion of Surah An-Nisa’: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning the deceased who has no children.’” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that the last verse to be revealed was the verse on usury, and the last surah to be revealed was When the help of God and the conquest come. It was narrated on his authority that the last verse to be revealed was the Almighty’s saying: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God Al-Baqarah 281. It was narrated that after Surat An-Nasr was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived for a year. After that, Surat Bara’ah was revealed, which was the last surah to be revealed in full. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived for six months after that. Then it was revealed on the way to the Farewell Pilgrimage: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: ‘God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not related to you.’” So it was called the verse of summer. Then it was revealed while he was standing in Arafat: This day I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you. (al-Ma’idah 5:3). He lived for eighty-one days after that. Then the verses about usury were revealed. Then it was revealed: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. So he lived for twenty-one days after that.
5:1: One hundred and twenty verses, revealed in all of Medina except for His saying: This day I have perfected your religion for you, the verse, which was revealed in Arafat. In the name of God, the most gracious, the most merciful It was narrated on the authority of Abu Maysarah that he said: God Almighty revealed in this Surah eighteen rulings that He did not reveal in any other Surah. His saying: “And the strangled, and the beaten, and the fallen, and the gored, and what a wild animal has eaten, except what you slaughter, and what is slaughtered on stone altars, and that you seek lots with arrows,” And what you have trained of birds of prey, training them, “And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them, and chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you,” and the completion of purification in His saying: When you rise to prayer, “And the male thief, male thief,” Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram, “God has not ordained any bahīrah, nor Ṣa’ibah, nor wasīlah, nor Ḥām,” and His saying: As a testimony between you when death approaches one of you. 1- The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, fulfill your contracts, meaning your covenants. Al-Zajjaj said: They are the most binding of covenants. It is said: I made a contract with so-and-so and I made a contract with him, meaning: I bound him to that with certainty. Its origin is from tying something with jealousy and connecting it to it as a rope is tied to a rope [if it is connected]. They differed regarding these contracts. Ibn Jurayj said: This is addressed to the People of the Book, meaning: O you who believe in the previous books, fulfill the covenants that I have entrusted to you regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is His statement: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, ‘You shall make it clear to the people.’ Surat Al Imran, 187 Others said: It is general. Qatada said: He meant by it the oaths that they contracted in the pre-Islamic era. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: They are the covenants of the fathers and the Qur’an, they are the contracts that people contract among themselves. Lawful to you are the animals of cattle. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: They are all livestock, namely camels, cows, and sheep. He meant to make lawful what the people of ignorance had forbidden themselves of livestock. Abu Dhabiyan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The livestock are the fetuses. And the same was narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: They are the fetuses that are found dead in the wombs of their mothers if they are slaughtered or slaughtered. Most scholars hold that it is permissible. [The Sheikh Al-Imam said]: I read to Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi and I said: It was read to Abu Sahl Muhammad bin Umar bin Tarfa and you were present, so it was said to him: Abu Sulayman Al-Khattabi told you, I told you, Abu Bakr bin Dasa, I told you, Abu Dawud Al-Sijistani, I told you, Musaddad, I told you, Hisham, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Abu Al-Wadak, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with them, he said: We said: O Messenger of God, we slaughter a camel, a cow, and a sheep and we find a fetus in its belly, should we throw it away or eat it? He said: Eat it if you wish, for its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother. Abu Al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The slaughter of a fetus is the slaughter of a nation. Some of them stipulated notification. Ibn Omar said: The slaughter of what is in its mouth is in its slaughter if its creation is complete and its hair has grown. The same was said by Al-Saeed bin Al-Musayyab. According to Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, it is not permissible to eat a fetus if it comes out dead after the mother has been slaughtered. Al-Kalbi said: The beast of livestock: its wild animals, which are gazelles and wild cows. It was called a beast because it was unable to distinguish between words, and it was said: because it does not speak. Except what is recited to you meaning: what was mentioned in His statement: Forbidden to you are dead animals until His statement: And that which is slaughtered on altars. “Except for the game hunted” is an accusative in the state, meaning: not for the game hunted. The meaning of the verse: All livestock are made lawful for you except for what is wild among them, for it is game that is not lawful for you while in a state of ihram. This is the statement of God Almighty: “And you are in a state of ihram. Indeed, God decrees what He wills.”
5:2: 2. The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not violate the symbols of God, was revealed about Al-Hatim, whose name was Shureih bin Dabi’ah Al-Bakri. He came to Madinah, and left his horses outside Madinah, and entered alone upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: To what do you call the people? He said: To testify that there is no god but God, [and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God], and to establish prayer and pay zakat. He said: [Good], except that I have leaders without whom I will not decide a matter, and perhaps I will convert to Islam and bring them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said to his companions: A man from Rabi’ah will enter upon you who speaks [with the tongue of] Satan. Then Shuraih left him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has entered with the face of an infidel and exited with the back of a traitor, and the man is not a Muslim. He passed by the wild animals of Medina and drove him away, and they followed him but did not catch up with him. When the following year came, he went out as a pilgrim with the pilgrims of Bakr bin Wa’il from Yamamah, and with him was a great deal of merchandise, and he had put on the sacrificial animal. The Muslims said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: This thief has gone out as a pilgrim, so leave us alone with him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has put on the sacrificial animal. They said: O Messenger of God, this is something we used to do in the days of ignorance. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused, so God, the Almighty, revealed: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: They are the rituals of Hajj. The polytheists used to perform Hajj and offer sacrifices, but the Muslims wanted to attack them, but God forbade them from doing so. Abu Ubaidah said: The symbols of God are the gifts that are marked, and marking is from the symbol, which is the mark, and marking them: informing them of what is known as a gift, and marking here: is to stab the side of the camel’s hump with a sharp object until blood flows, and that is a sign that it is a gift, and it is a Sunnah for gifts if they are camels, because Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abu Naim, I told Aflah, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: “I twisted the necklaces of the Prophet’s body, may God bless him and grant him peace, with my own hands, then he put them on and marked them and gave them as a gift, so whatever was forbidden to him was permissible for him.” Al-Shafi’i compared cows to camels in terms of feeling. As for sheep, they do not feel a wound, as they cannot bear a wound due to their weakness. According to Abu Hanifa, the sacrificial animal does not feel a wound. Atiyah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: Do not violate the rites of God, which means hunting while you are in a state of ihram, based on the words of God Almighty: And when you are in a state of ihram, then hunt. Al-Suddi said: He meant the sanctuary of God, and it was said: What is meant by it is the prohibition of killing in the sanctuary. Ataa said: The rites of God are the sanctities of God, avoiding His wrath, and following His obedience. His saying: nor the sacred month meaning fighting during it. Ibn Zayd said: It is the intercalation, because in the Age of Ignorance they used to make it permissible one year and forbid it the next. nor the sacrificial animals which is everything that is offered to the House of God from a camel, cow or sheep. nor the necklaces meaning the gifts that are adorned, meaning those with necklaces. Ata’ said: He meant the owners of the necklaces, because in the Age of Ignorance if they wanted to leave the sanctuary they would adorn themselves and their camels with something from the bark of the trees of the sanctuary so that they would not be exposed, so the Shari’ah forbade making anything of it permissible. Mutraf ibn Ash-Shakheer said: It is the necklaces themselves, because the polytheists used to take some of the bark of the trees of Mecca and adorn themselves with it, so they were forbidden to remove its trees. God the Almighty says: nor those who are at the Sacred House, meaning: those who intend to go to the Sacred House, meaning the Kaaba, so do not interfere with them, seeking they ask for bounty from their Lord, meaning provision through trade, and approval, meaning: according to their claim, because the disbelievers have no share in approval. Qatada said: It is that their livelihood in this world be improved and punishment not be hastened for them in it. It was said: seeking bounty for the believers and the polytheists in general, and seeking approval for the believers in particular, because the Muslims and the polytheists used to perform Hajj. This verse up to here is abrogated by His saying: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them Surat At-Tawbah, 5 and His saying: So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs Surat At-Tawbah, 28. It is not permissible for a polytheist to perform Hajj nor for a disbeliever to be safe with the offerings and necklaces. The Almighty’s saying: And when you have completed your state of ihram, then hunt, is a command of permission, permitting those who are in a state of ihram to hunt, like the Almighty’s saying: So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse throughout the land Al-Jumu’ah, 10. And do not let them incite you, Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: Do not let them burden you, it is said: So-and-so incited me to do such-and-such, meaning he made me bear it. Al-Farra' said: Do not let them gain you, it is said: He committed a crime, meaning he earned it, and so-and-so is the crime of his family, meaning he earned them, and it was said: Do not let them leave you, "The hatred of a people, meaning their hatred and enmity, and it is the source of shan'ita, Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read shan'an qawm with a sukoon on the first nun, and the others read it with a fatha, and they are two dialects, and the fatha is better, because the sources are mostly fa'lan, with a fatha on the ayn, like darabaan, saylan, naslaan, and the like, that they prevented you from the Sacred Mosque, Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a kasra on the alif as a new sentence, and the others read it with a fatha on the alif," meaning: because they prevented you, and the meaning of the verse: "And do not let the enmity of a people incite you to aggression because they prevented you." Muhammad bin Jarir said: Because the Surah was revealed after the Hudaybiyyah incident, and the punishment had already occurred, that you transgress against them by killing and taking their money, and cooperate meaning: that some of you help others, in righteousness and piety. It was said that righteousness is following the command, and piety is avoiding the prohibition. It was also said that righteousness is Islam, and piety is the Sunnah. And do not cooperate in sin and aggression. It was said that sin is disbelief, and aggression is injustice. It was also said that sin is disobedience, and aggression is innovation.
5:3: Abu Al-Qasim Abdul Karim bin Hawazin Al-Qushayri told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Tahir Al-Daqqaq told us in Baghdad, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad bin Al-Zubayr Al-Qurashi told us, Al-Hasan bin Ali bin Affan told us, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Salih, Abdul Rahman bin Jubayr bin Nafeer bin Malik Al-Hadrami told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an Al-Ansari, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about righteousness and sin. He said: Righteousness is good character, and sin is that which troubles your soul and you would hate for people to find out about it.” And fear God, for God is severe in penalty. 3- The Almighty’s saying: Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God, meaning: what was slaughtered with a name other than God, and the strangled, which is the one that is strangled and dies. Ibn Abbas said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to strangle the sheep until it died, and the beaten sheep, which is the one that is killed with wood. Qatada said: They used to beat it with a stick, and when it died, they ate it. The fallen sheep, which is the one that falls from a high place or into a well and dies. The gored sheep, which is the one that is gored by another and dies. The feminine ha is used in the active participle if it is in the sense of the active participle. If it is in the sense of the passive participle, the masculine and feminine are equal in it, such as ‘ayn kuhayl and kuff khadayb. If the noun is deleted and the adjective is singular, they insert the ha and say: ra’ina kuhayla and khadayba. Here the ha is inserted because the noun did not precede it, so if the ha was dropped, it would not be known whether it is a feminine or masculine adjective. The same applies to the slaughtered animal and the slaughtered animal. And the eater of the beast, and what the beast ate, meaning what remained of what the beast ate, which the people of the Age of Ignorance used to eat, except what you slaughtered, meaning: except what you managed to slaughter of these things. The root of slaughter is completion. It is said: I slaughtered the fire if I completed lighting it. What is meant here is: completing the rupture of the jugular veins and the flow of blood. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whatever causes the blood to flow and the name of God is mentioned over it, then all of it is permissible, except for the tooth and the nail. The minimum slaughtering method for an animal is one that can be cut through the esophagus and the throat, and it is also permissible to cut the two veins with them. It is permissible to use any sharp tool that can be cut from iron, reed, glass, or stone, except for the tooth and the nail, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade slaughtering with them. What is permissible is what you slaughter after a wild animal has wounded it or eaten something from it, if it has caught up with it and life is stable in it, so you slaughter it. As for what has become a state of slaughter due to the wound of a wild animal, it is considered a dead animal, so it is not permissible even if you slaughter it. The same applies to what has fallen or been gored, if you catch it alive before it has become a state of slaughter, so you slaughter it, it is permissible. If you shoot at a game in the air and hit it, and it falls to the ground and dies, it is permissible because falling to the ground is a necessity. If it falls on a mountain, tree, or roof, then falls from it and dies, it is not permissible, and it is from what has fallen, unless the arrow hits its slaughtering place in the air, in which case it is permissible no matter how it falls, because the slaughtering has occurred when the arrow hits the slaughtering place. And what was slaughtered on altars, it was said: al-nasb is the plural of nasaab, which is one and its plural is ansaab like ‘aq and ‘anaq, and it is the thing that is erected. They differed about it. Mujahid and Qatada said: There were three hundred and sixty stones erected around the House. The people of the Age of Ignorance used to worship them, venerate them, and slaughter for them. They were not idols. Rather, idols are the pictures and engravings. The others said: They are the erected idols. Its meaning is: And what was slaughtered in the name of the idol. Ibn Zayd said: And what was slaughtered on the idol and what was dedicated to other than God with it: they are one. Qatrib said: On means the lam, meaning: and what was slaughtered for the sake of the idol. And that you seek division by arrows, meaning: it is forbidden for you to seek division by arrows. Divination is asking for a share and a judgment from arrows. Arrows are: lots that have no feathers or blades. The singular is: zalam, zalam with the opening of the zay and the closing of the zay. Their arrows were seven equal lots made of shawhat, which would be with the custodian of the Kaaba. Written on one was: yes, and on one was: no, and on one of you, and on one was: from someone other than you, and on one was: attached, and on one was: the intellect, and one was absent and had nothing on it. So when they wanted something from travel or marriage or circumcision or something else, or they disputed about lineage or differed about bearing the intellect, they would go to Hubal, which was the greatest idol of the Quraysh in Mecca, and they would come with one hundred dirhams and give them to the owner of the arrows so that he could roll the arrows, and they would say: O our God, we wanted such and such. If it came out yes, they would do it, and if it came out no, they would not do that for a year, then they would return to the arrows again. So when they rolled the arrows by lineage, If one of you leaves, he will be among them, and if someone other than you leaves, he will be an ally, and if he leaves attached, he will remain in his position, with no lineage or alliance. If they differ over reason, then whoever is opposed to reason will be held accountable. If the ignorant one leaves, they will argue again until the one who is written down leaves. So God Almighty forbade that and prohibited it, saying: That is wickedness. Saeed bin Jubair said: Azlam are white pebbles that they used to play with. Mujahid said: They are the Persian and Roman dice that they gamble with. Al-Sha’bi and others said: Azlam are for the Arabs, and ka’ab are for the non-Arabs. Sufyan ibn Wakee’ said: They are chess. We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Divination, fortune-telling, and augury are from the jibt. What is meant by fortune-telling is playing with pebbles. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjuwayh told us, Ibn Al-Fadl Al-Kindi told us, Al-Hasan Ibn Dawud Al-Khashab told us, Suwaid Ibn Saeed told us, [Abu Al-Mukhtar] told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik Ibn Umair, on the authority of Raja Ibn Haywah, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever practices divination, or casts lots, or has an omen that will prevent him from traveling, will not see the highest levels of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection. The Almighty said, Today those who disbelieved have despaired of [defeating] your religion, meaning that you would return to your religion as disbelievers. This is because the disbelievers were hoping that the Muslims would return to their religion, but when Islam became strong, they despaired. Despair and hopelessness have the same meaning. “So do not fear them, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as religion.” This verse was revealed on Friday, the Day of Arafah, after the afternoon prayer during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing in Arafat on his she-camel, Al-Adhbaa, and the she-camel’s hump almost broke from its weight, so it knelt down. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hasan bin Al-Sabah told us, Jaafar bin Awn told us, Abu Al-Umais told us, Qais bin Muslim told us, Tariq bin Shihab told us, Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said that a Jewish man said to him: “O Commander of the Faithful, there is a verse in your book that you recite. If it had been revealed to us Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival.” He said: Which verse? He said: This day I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as your religion. Umar said: “We know that day and the place in which it was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing in Arafat on Friday.” Umar indicated that that day was a festival for us.” Ibn Abbas said: There were five holidays on that day: Friday, Arafah, the holiday of the Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians. The holidays of the people of the religions did not come together on a day before or after it. Harun bin Antara narrated on the authority of his father, who said: “When this verse was revealed, Omar, may God be pleased with him, cried. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘What makes you cry, Omar?’ He said: ‘What makes me cry is that we used to have an increase in our religion, but when it is complete, nothing is ever complete without being diminished.’ He said: ‘You have spoken the truth.’” This verse was the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he lived eighty-one days after it. He died on Monday, after the sun had declined two nights before the end of the month of Rabi’ al-Awwal [in the year eleven of the Hijra. It was said that he died on the twelfth of the month of Rabi’ al-Awwal]. His migration was on the twelfth. The Almighty said: This day I have perfected your religion for you meaning: On the day this verse was revealed, I have perfected your religion for you, meaning the obligatory duties, the Sunnahs, the prescribed punishments, jihad, the rulings, the lawful and the unlawful. So after this verse nothing was revealed that was lawful or unlawful, nor anything from the obligatory duties. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and it was narrated from him that the verse on usury was revealed after it. Saeed bin Jubair and Qatada said: I have perfected your religion for you, so no polytheist has performed Hajj with you. And it was said: I have made your religion manifest and secured you from the enemy. The Almighty said: And I have completed My favor upon you, meaning: And I have fulfilled My promise in His statement: And to complete My favor upon you Surat Al-Baqarah, 150. So it was from the completion of His favor that they entered Mecca in safety and were victorious over it, and they performed Hajj reassured and no polytheists had mixed with them, And I have approved for you Islam as a religion. I heard Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi say: I heard Abu Muhammad bin Abi Hatim say: I heard Abu Bakr Al-Naysaburi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hasan bin Al-Musayyab Al-Marwazi say: I heard Abu Hatim Muhammad bin Idris Al-Hanthali say: I heard Abdul Malik bin Maslama Abu Marwan Al-Masri say: I heard Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr bin Al-Munkadir, may God be pleased with him, I heard my uncle Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir say: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with him say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: God Almighty said: This is a religion that I have approved for Myself and nothing will reform it except generosity and good character, so honor it with them as long as you accompany it.” The Almighty said: But whoever is forced by necessity in a state of famine, meaning: he strives hard in a state of famine, and famine is the stomach being empty of food. It is said that a man has a satiated stomach if he is full and empty. Not inclined to sin, meaning: inclined to sin, which is eating more than he is full. Qatada said: not exposing himself to disobedience in his intention, then God is Forgiving and Merciful, and there is an implication in it, meaning: so eat it, then God is Forgiving and Merciful. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Hassan Al-Mazuri told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Siraj Al-Tahhan, on the authority of Abu Ahmad Muhammad bin Quraish bin Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdul Aziz Al-Makki, on the authority of Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam, on the authority of Muhammad bin Katheer, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Hassan bin Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laithi, “A man said: O Messenger of God, we are in the land and famine strikes us, so when will dead meat be permissible for us? He said: As long as you do not take it with you, or have a late meal, or eat green vegetables, then do as you please.”
5:4: 4- The Almighty said, They ask you, what is lawful for them verse. Saeed bin Jubair said, this verse was revealed about Adi bin Hatim and Zaid bin Al-Muhalhil Al-Ta’i, who is Zaid Al-Khayl, whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Zaid Al-Khair. They said, O Messenger of God, we are a people who hunt with dogs and falcons, so what is lawful for us from them? So this verse was revealed. It was said: The reason for its revelation is that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the killing of dogs, they said: O Messenger of God, what is permissible for us from this nation that you ordered to kill? So this verse was revealed. When it was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted the keeping of dogs that are beneficial, and forbade keeping those that are of no benefit. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Al-Hussein Ali bin Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Bishran told us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever keeps a dog, except a dog for herding, hunting, or farming, a qirat will be deducted from his reward every day. The first is more correct in the revelation of the verse. “Say: Lawful to you are all good things,” meaning slaughtered in the name of God Almighty. It was said that it is everything that the Arabs enjoy and find enjoyable without there being a text in the Book or Sunnah prohibiting it. And what you have trained of birds of prey, meaning: Lawful to you is the hunting of what you have trained of birds of prey. They differed about these birds of prey. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: They are dogs and nothing else. What is hunted by a dog other than a dog is not permissible unless it is able to slaughter it. This is not acted upon. Rather, most scholars agree that what is meant by birds of prey are the wild beasts such as the cheetah, tiger, and dog, and the birds of prey such as the hawk, eagle, and falcon, and the like that can be trained. Hunting all of them is permissible. They are called birds of prey because they provide their owners with their livelihood from hunting, i.e., they earn it. It is said: So-and-so is the hunter of his family, i.e., their earner, mukalibeen. The one who trains them is also called kalab. The accusative of mukalibeen is for every animal, i.e., in the case of training these birds of prey, i.e., you incite them to hunt. Dogs are mentioned because they are more numerous and more general. What is meant are all hunting birds of prey. You teach them, you train them in the etiquette of taking prey, from what God has taught you, i.e., from the knowledge that He has taught you. As-Suddi said: i.e., as God has taught you. From means the letter kaf. “So eat of what they catch for you.” He meant that if a trained animal of prey goes out at the dispatch of its owner and takes and kills the prey, it is permissible. Training is that three things are present in it: if it is pulled out, it is pulled out; if it is driven away, it is driven away; and if it takes the prey, it holds on and does not eat. If this is done repeatedly, or at least three times, then it is trained, and it is permissible to kill it by sending its owner. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Thabit bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If you send your trained dog and say the name of God, and it catches and kills, then eat, but if it eats, then do not eat, for it caught for its own sake. If it mixes with dogs over which the name of God was not mentioned, and they catch and kill, then do not eat, for you do not know which one it killed. If you shoot game and find it after a day or two with nothing on it but the mark of your arrow, then eat, but if it falls into the water, then do not eat.” They differed as to whether you caught the game and ate some of it. Most of the scholars held that it is forbidden, and this was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is the opinion of Ata’, Tawus, and Al-Sha’bi. Al-Thawri, Ibn Al-Mubarak, and the People of Opinion said the same, and it is the most correct opinion of Al-Shafi’i, because he said: And if he ate, then do not eat, for he only caught it for himself. Some of them permitted eating it. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar, Salman al-Farsi, and Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas. Malik said the same: When it was narrated on the authority of Abu Tha`labah al-Khushani, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you send your dog and mention the name of God Almighty, then eat it even if it eats from it. As for the untrained bird of prey, if it takes prey, or the trained bird, if it goes out without being sent out and takes and kills, it is not permissible unless its owner finds it alive and slaughters it, in which case it is permissible. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Haywah told us, Rabia bin Yazid Al-Dimashqi told us, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Abu Tha’laba Al-Khushani, who said: I said: “O Prophet of God, we are in a land of the People of the Book. Can we eat from their utensils? And in a land of game, I hunt with my bow and my trained dog. What is permissible for me?” He said: “As for what you mentioned about the utensils of the People of the Book, if you find anything else, then do not eat from them. If you do not find anything else, then wash them and eat from them. Whatever you hunt with your bow and mention the name of God over it, then eat. And whatever you hunt with your dog that is not trained and you realize that it was slaughtered correctly, then eat.” The Almighty said: “And mention the name of God over it. And fear God. Indeed, God is swift in account.” This explains that mentioning the name of God Almighty over the slaughtered animal is a condition when it is slaughtered, and in hunting when a bird or arrow is shot. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi told us, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Hasan ibn Alawiya al-Jawhari, who said: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Athram al-Muqri in Basra told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Shaiba, on the authority of Abu Uday, on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two horned, white rams, which he slaughtered with his own hand, and he said Bismillah and Allahu Akbar. He said: I saw him placing his foot on their sides and slaughtering them with his own hand and saying In the name of God and God is Great.”
5:5: 5- The Almighty said: Today all good things are lawful for you, meaning: slaughtering in the name of God Almighty, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, meaning the slaughtering of the Jews and Christians and those who entered their religion from all nations before the mission of the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is lawful for you. As for those who entered their religion after the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, their slaughtering is not lawful. If a Jew or Christian slaughters in the name of someone other than God, such as a Christian slaughtering in the name of Christ, then disobey him. Omar said: It is not lawful, and this is the opinion of Rabi'ah. Most scholars said that it is lawful, and this is the opinion of Al-Sha'bi, Ata', Al-Zuhri, and Makhul. Al-Sha'bi and Makhul were asked about a Christian slaughtering in the name of Christ. They said: It is lawful, because God Almighty has made their slaughtering lawful, and He knows what they say. Al-Hasan said: If a Jew or Christian slaughters and mentions a name other than God while you are listening, then do not eat it, but if he is absent from you, eat it, because God has made it lawful for you. The Almighty said: And your food is lawful for them. So if it is said: How is it permissible for them to eat our food when they are infidels and not from the people of the law? Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that it is permissible for you to feed them, so the address of permissibility is with the Muslims. And it was said: Because he mentioned the ruling on women after it, and did not mention the permissibility of Muslim women for them, so it is as if he said it is permissible for you to feed them, but forbidden for you to marry them. The Almighty said: And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you. This refers back to the first and is separate from His saying: And your food is lawful for them. They differed on the meaning of chaste women: Most scholars held that what was meant by them were free women, and they permitted marriage to any free woman, whether she was a believer or a Christian, whether she was wicked or chaste, and this is the opinion of Mujahid. These people said: It is not permissible for a Muslim to marry a Christian slave woman, because God Almighty said: Then from among those whom your right hands possess of believing girls Surat An-Nisa’, 25. He permitted marriage to a slave woman on the condition that she be a believer, and most of them permitted marriage to a Christian slave woman who was at war. Ibn Abbas said: It is not permissible, and he recited: Fight those who do not believe in God until His saying: Until they pay the jizyah willingly and are humbled Surat At-Tawbah, 29. So whoever pays the jizyah, his women are permissible for us, and whoever does not pay it, his women are not permissible for us. Some people said that what is meant by chaste women in the verse are the chaste women from both groups, whether they are free women or slave women. He permitted marriage to a female slave from the People of the Book, and they forbade prostitutes from among the believers and the People of the Book. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan. Al-Sha’bi said: The chastity of a woman from the People of the Book is that she should be chaste and wash herself from major ritual impurity. If you give them their dowries, while being chaste, not fornicators, not openly committing fornication, nor taking lovers, meaning: secretly committing fornication. Al-Zajjaj said: God forbade sexual intercourse for the purpose of fornication and taking lovers, and permitted it for the purpose of chastity, which is marriage. And whoever disbelieves in faith, his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He says that the protection of Muslims from disbelief does not suffice them at all, and it applies to all al-Nas 114:And whoever disbelieves in faith, his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said about the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And whoever disbelieves in faith meaning: in God in whom faith is obligatory. Al-Kalbi said: By faith, meaning: by the word of monotheism, which is the testimony that there is no god but God. Muqatil said: “With what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is the Qur’an.” It was said: Whoever disbelieves in faith, that is, he considers what is forbidden permissible and forbids what is permissible, his work has been in vain, and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas said: He has lost the reward.
5:6: 6- The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, meaning: when you want to rise to prayer, like the Almighty’s saying: So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge in God, Surat An-Nahl, 98, meaning: when you want to recite. The apparent meaning of the verse requires ablution every time one wants to stand up for prayer. You should inform us, through the explanation of the Sunnah and the actions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that what is meant by the verse is: If you stand up for prayer while you are not pure. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God does not accept the prayer of any one of you if he has broken his ablution until he performs ablution. On the day of the Trench, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, combined four prayers with one ablution. Abu al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Abu al-Harith Tahir bin Muhammad al-Tahiri, on the authority of Abu Muhammad al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Halim, on the authority of Abu al-Muwajjah Muhammad bin Amr bin al-Muwajjah, on the authority of Abdun, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraidah, on the authority of his father, that on the day of the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the five prayers with one ablution, and wiped over his socks. Zaid bin Aslam said: The meaning of the verse is: When you rise to pray from sleep. Some of them said: It is an order in the way of recommendation, recommendation for the one who stands up for prayer to renew his ablution even if he is in a state of purity. Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, narrated that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Whoever performs ablution in a state of purity, God will write for him ten good deeds. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Hanzala bin Aamer that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded ablution for every prayer, whether one was pure or not. When that was difficult for him, he commanded the use of the siwak for every prayer. Some of them said: This is an announcement from God Almighty to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he does not have to perform ablution unless he stands up for prayer and not for other actions. So He gave him permission to do after the impurity what he has of actions other than prayer. Abu al-Qasim al-Hanafi informed us, I told Abu al-Harith al-Tahiri, I told al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Haleem, I told Abu al-Muwajjah, I told Sadaqah, I told Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, I heard Saeed ibn al-Huwayrith, I heard Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, say: ((We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he returned from the toilet and food was brought to him. It was said to him: Why don’t you perform ablution? He said: Why? Should I pray and then perform ablution?)) The Almighty said: Wash your faces. The face is defined as the area from the hairline to the end of the chin in length and between the ears in width. All of it must be washed in ablution. It is also necessary to reach the area under the eyebrows, the eyelashes, the moustache, the pubic hair, or the pubic hair, even if it is thick. As for the sideburns and beard, if they are thick and the skin cannot be seen from underneath them, it is not necessary to wash their insides in ablution, but rather it is necessary to wash their outsides. Is it necessary to pass water over the outer part of the beard that extends beyond the chin? There are two opinions on this: One of them: It is not obligatory, and Abu Hanifa said the same, because hair that falls below the edge of the head is not subject to the same ruling as the head in terms of the permissibility of wiping over it, and likewise hair that falls below the edge of the face in terms of the obligation to wash it. The second opinion: It is necessary to pass water over its surface, because God Almighty commanded washing the face, and the face is what is in front of this organ, and it is said in the language that someone’s face became pale and his face grew: if his beard grew. The Almighty said: And your hands to the elbows, meaning: with the elbows, as God Almighty said: And do not consume their wealth along with your wealth Surat An-Nisa, 2, meaning: with your wealth, and He said: Who are my helpers for the sake of God? Surat Al Imran, 52 and Surat As-Saff, 14, meaning: with God. Most scholars agree that it is obligatory to wash the elbows, and in the case of the foot, it is obligatory to wash the heels. Al-Sha’bi and Muhammad ibn Jarir said: It is not obligatory to wash the elbows and heels in the case of the hand and foot, because the letter to indicates the limit and the boundary, so it is not included in the boundary. We said: This is not a limit, but rather it has the meaning of with, as we mentioned. It was said: If something is limited to its kind, the end is included in it, and if it is limited to something other than its kind, it is not included, like the Almighty’s saying: Then complete the fast until the night Surat Al-Baqarah, 187. The night is not included in it because it is not of the same kind as the day. The Almighty said: And wipe over your heads. The scholars differed regarding the amount of wiping of the head that is obligatory. Malik said: It is obligatory to wipe the entire head, just as it is obligatory to wipe the entire face in tayammum. Abu Hanifa said: It is obligatory to wipe a quarter of the head. According to Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, it is obligatory to wipe the amount that is called wiping. Those who permitted wiping part of the head cited as evidence what Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khalal told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, al-Shafi’i told us, Yahya ibn Hassan told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd and Ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of Ayoub al-Sakhtiyani, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Amr ibn Wahb al-Thaqafi, on the authority of al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah, “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution and wiped his forelock, his turban, and his shoes.” Some scholars permitted wiping the turban with this hadith, and al-Awza’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq said the same. Most scholars did not permit wiping over the turban instead of wiping the head. They said: In the hadith of Al-Mughira, the obligation of wiping was dropped from him by wiping the forelock, and in it is evidence that wiping the entire head is not obligatory. The Almighty said: And your feet to the ankles. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, Al-Kisa’i, Ya’qub, and Hafs read and your feet with the nasb of the lam, while the others read and your feet with the genitive case. Whoever reads and your feet with the genitive case, it is in apposition to His statement: So wash your faces and your hands, meaning: wash your feet. Whoever reads with the genitive case, a few of the people of knowledge have said that one wipes over the feet. It was narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas that he said: Ablution is two washings and two wipings. This was narrated from ‘Ikrimah and Qatadah. Al-Sha’bi said: Gabriel came down with the wiping and said: Do you not see the one who performs tayammum wiping what was a washing and nullifying what was a wiping? Muhammad bin Jarir al-Tabari said: The person performing ablution has the choice between wiping over the socks and washing the feet. The majority of scholars from the Companions, the Followers, and others held that washing the feet is obligatory. They said: The lowering of the lam in the word al-arj is due to the proximity of the word, not to the agreement of the ruling, as God Almighty said: The punishment of a painful Day. So painful is an attribute of the punishment, but it takes the i’rab of day for proximity, and like their saying: The hole of a lizard is ruined. So ruined is an attribute of the stone and takes the i’rab of lizard for proximity. The evidence for the obligation of washing the feet: Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Abbas Al-Hamidi Al-Khatib told us, Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ya’qub told us, Yahya bin Muhammad bin Yahya told us, Al-Hajabi and Musaddad told us: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mahak, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed behind on a journey that we were on, and he caught up with us and the afternoon prayer had exhausted us, and we were performing ablution, so we began to wipe over our feet, and he called out to us at the top of his voice: Woe to the heels from the Fire.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdun told us, Muammar told us, Al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Ata bin Yazid, on the authority of Hamran, the freed slave of Uthman, who said: “I saw Uthman, may God be pleased with him, perform ablution, pour water over his hands three times, then rinse his mouth, nose up his nose, and blow his nose, then wash his face three times, then wash his right hand up to the elbow three times, then wash his left hand up to the elbow three times, then wipe his head, then wash his right foot three times, then his left foot three times, then he said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution similar to my ablution, then he said: Whoever performs ablution like my ablution, then prays two rak’ahs, not thinking about anything in them, God will forgive his previous sins.” Some of them said: What he meant by his saying and your feet is wiping over the socks, as it was narrated that “when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) bowed, he would place his hands on his knees.” It does not mean that there was no barrier between them. It is said: So-and-so kissed the head and hand of the emir, even if the turban was on his head and his hand was in his sleeve. Ahmad ibn ‘Abdullah al-Nu’aymi told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yusuf, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma’il, on the authority of Abu Nu’aym, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of ‘Urwah ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of his father may God be pleased with them both, who said: “I was with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) one night on a journey, and he said: ‘Do you have water with you?’ I said: ‘Yes.’ So he got down from his mount and walked until he was hidden from me in the darkness of the night. Then he came, and I poured water from the waterskin over him, and he washed his face and hands. He was wearing a woollen cloak, but he could not take his arms out of it until he took them out from under the cloak and washed his arms. Then he wiped his head. Then I bent down to take off his socks, but he said: ‘Leave them, for I put them on while they were pure.’ So he wiped over them.” The Almighty says: to the ankles. The ankles are the two protruding bones on the sides of the feet, and they are the joint of the leg and foot. They must be washed with the feet, as we mentioned with the elbows. The obligatory parts of ablution are: washing the three limbs as God Almighty mentioned, and wiping the head. The scholars differed regarding the obligation of intention. Most of them held that it is obligatory because ablution is an act of worship and requires intention like all other acts of worship. Some of them held that it is not obligatory, which is the opinion of al-Thawri and the people of opinion. They differed about the obligation of order, which is to wash his limbs in order of loyalty as God Almighty mentioned. A group went to its obligation, and it is the saying of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq, may God have mercy on them, and it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him. Al-Shafi’i provided evidence with the words of God Almighty: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God Surat Al-Baqarah, 158. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began with As-Safa and said: We begin with what God began with. Likewise here God Almighty began by mentioning washing the face, so we must begin in action with what God Almighty began by mentioning. A group of people said that the order is a Sunnah, and they said that the waw mentioned in the verse is for the collection and not for the order, as God Almighty said: Zakat is only for the poor and the needy Surat At-Tawbah, 60. They agreed that it is not necessary to observe the order in distributing the zakat to the people of the two shares. Whoever obligated the order responded that it was not transmitted from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he observed the order between the people of the two shares. In ablution, it was not transmitted that he performed ablution except in order, as God Almighty mentioned. The explanation of the Book is taken from the Sunnah, as God Almighty said: O you who believe, bow and prostrate Surat Al-Hajj, 77, because He mentioned bowing before prostration, and it was not transmitted from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he did anything but that, so observing the order in it was obligatory, and likewise the order here. The Almighty said: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, then purify yourselves. That is, wash yourself. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, Malik told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, his father told us, Aisha told us, may God be pleased with her, “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, washed himself after major ritual impurity, he would begin by washing his hands, then he would perform ablution as he would for prayer, then he would put his fingers in the water and run them through the roots of his hair, then he would pour three handfuls of water over his head with his hands, then he would pour water over all of his skin.” God the Almighty says: And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the relieving himself or you have contacted women and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. This is evidence that it is obligatory to wipe the face and hands with earth, God does not intend to place upon you by what He has enjoined upon you of ablution, ritual bathing and dry ablution, any difficulty, “but He intends to purify you” from ritual impurity, major ritual impurity and sins, and to complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: The completion of the favor is the expiation of sins through ablution, as God the Almighty said: That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come Surat al-Fath, 2, so He made the completion of His favor the forgiveness of sins. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Kisa’i told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khalal told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, al-Rabi’ told us, al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hamran: “Uthman performed ablution with the seats three times, three times, then he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution as I do, his sins will leave his face, hands, and feet.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, Malik told us, Hisham ibn `Urwah told us, his father told us, Hamran, the freed slave of `Uthman, said: `Uthman ibn `Affan, may God be pleased with him, was sitting on the benches one day when the afternoon prayer came, so he called for water and performed ablution, then he said: By God, I will tell you a hadith. Were it not for a verse in the Book of God, I would not have told you about it. Then he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no man [Muslim] who performs ablution and does it well, then prays the prayer, except that what is between it and the next prayer will be forgiven for him until he prays it. Malik said: I think he meant this verse: Establish prayer for My remembrance. Ibn Shihab narrated it, and `Urwah said: The verse: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs Surat al-Baqarah, 159. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Yahya bin Bakir, I told Al-Layth, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Naim Al-Mujmir, who said: I climbed with Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, to the roof of the mosque, and he performed ablution. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “My nation will be called on the Day of Resurrection with radiant limbs and bright faces from the traces of ablution. So whoever among you can lengthen his radiance, let him do so.”
5:7: 7- The Almighty’s saying: And remember the favor of God upon you, meaning: all the favors, and His covenant with which He bound you, His covenant with which He made a covenant with you, O believers, when you said, ‘We hear and we obey,’ that was when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hear and obey in what they liked and disliked. This is the saying of most of the commentators. Mujahid and Muqatil said: It means the covenant that was taken from them when He brought them out from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, “and fear God. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts,” what is in the hearts of good and evil.
5:8: 8- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for God, witnesses in justice, meaning: be persistently standing firm in justice [speaking] the truth. He commanded them to be just and truthful in their actions and words, and let not the hatred of a people, the enmity of a people, incite you not to be just, meaning: to abandon justice towards them because of their enmity. Then He said: Be just, meaning towards your friends and enemies, that is nearer to righteousness, meaning: to righteousness, "and fear God. Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do."
5:9: 9- God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward. This is in the accusative case, because the verb of the promise is based on forgiveness, and its nominative case is based on the estimation of: And He said to them forgiveness and a great reward.
5:10: 10- And those who disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of Hellfire.
5:11: 11- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you, by defending you, when a people were about to stretch out their hands against you by killing. Qatada said: This verse was revealed while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Batn Nakhl. The Banu Tha’laba and the Banu Muharrib wanted to kill him and his companions when they were busy praying. God Almighty informed His Prophet of that, and God revealed the prayer of fear. Al-Hasan said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was besieging Ghatafan in Nakhl. A polytheist man said: Would you like me to kill Muhammad? They said: How will you kill him? He said: We wish you had done that. So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wearing his sword. He said: O Muhammad, show me your sword. So he gave it to him. The man kept shaking the sword and looking at the sword and at the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Who can protect you from me, O Muhammad? He said: God. So the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threatened him, but he shook the sword and went away. Then God Almighty revealed this verse. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Kalbi and Ibn Yasar said on the authority of his men: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Mundhir bin Amr Al-Sa’idi, who was one of the leaders, on the night of Al-Aqaba, with thirty riders from the Muhajireen and Ansar to Banu Amir bin Sa’sa’ah. They went out and met Amir bin At-Tufayl at the well of Ma’unah, which is one of the places of Banu Amir. They threw themselves down, and Al-Mundhir bin Amr and his companions were killed, except for three men who were searching for something they had lost, one of them Amr bin Umayyah Ad-Damri. They were not alarmed by anything except the birds circling in the sky, and blood clots were falling from between their trunks. One of the men said: He killed our companions. Then he turned and ran until he met a man. They exchanged two blows. When the blow was combined, he raised his head to the sky and opened his eyes and said: God is the Greatest, Paradise and Lord of the Worlds. His two companions returned and met two men from Banu Salim. There was a truce between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their people. They claimed to be Banu Amir, so they killed them and their people came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They asked for blood money, so he went out with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talha and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, may God be pleased with them, until they entered upon Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf and Banu al-Nadir to ask them for help in their blood money. They had pledged to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to stop fighting and to help him with the blood money. They said: Yes, O Abu al-Qasim, it is time for you to come to us and ask for something. Sit down so that we may feed you and give you what you asked for. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions sat down, and some of them spoke to each other privately and said: You will not find Muhammad closer than him now, so who will appear at this house and throw a rock on it and relieve us of him? Omar bin Jahash said: I will. So he came to a huge millstone to throw it at him, but God Almighty held back his hand and Gabriel came and informed him. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, returning to Medina. Then he called Ali and said: Do not leave your place. If any of my companions comes out to you and asks you about me, say: Go to Medina. So Ali, may God be pleased with him, did that until they reached him, then they followed him. Then God Almighty revealed this verse and said: “So restrain their hands from you and fear God. And in God let the believers put their trust.”
5:12: 12- The Almighty said: And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We appointed from among them twelve leaders. That is because God Almighty promised Moses, peace be upon him, that He would give him and his people the Holy Land, which is the Levant, and the Canaanites, the mighty, inhabited it. So when the Children of Israel settled in Egypt, God Almighty ordered them to go to Jericho from the land of the Levant, which is the Holy Land, and it had a thousand villages in a thousand gardens, and He said: O Moses, I have written it for you as a home and a settlement, so go out to it and fight the enemy in it, for I will support you against them, and take from your people twelve leaders from each tribe, a leader who will be a guarantor for his people to fulfill what they were commanded to do. So Moses chose the leaders and Moses walked with the Children of Israel until they approached Jericho, so he sent these leaders to spy on him the report and learn its science, and they met a man from the giants called Awj bin Anq, and his height was three thousand three hundred and three Thirty cubits and a third of a cubit, and he was held back by the clouds and drank from them and took the fish from the bottom of the sea and roasted it in the eye of the sun and raised it to it and then ate it. It is narrated that the water covered the mountains on the earth and what went beyond the knees of Og and he lived for three thousand years until God destroyed him at the hands of Moses, peace be upon him, and that was because he came [and pulled out] a rock from the mountain the size of the army of Moses, peace be upon him, and it was a parasang by a parasang, and he carried it to cover it with it, so God sent the hoopoe and it cracked the rock with its beak and it fell on his neck and crushed it, so Moses, peace be upon him, came while he was stunned and killed him, and his mother [Og] was one of the daughters of Adam and her seat was [a grove] of the earth, so when Og met the leaders and on his head was a bundle of firewood, he took the twelve and put them in his bag and went with them to his wife, and said: Look at these who claim that they want to fight us, and he threw them in front of her and said: Shall I not crush them with my feet? His wife said: No, leave them alone until they tell their people what they saw. So he did that. It was narrated that he put them in his sleeve and brought them to the king, who threw them before him. The king said: Go back and tell them what you saw. He would not carry a bunch of their grapes except for five of them on a piece of wood, and he would put five people in half of a pomegranate if he removed its seeds. So the leaders returned and began to find out their conditions, and some of them said to each other: O people, if you tell the Children of Israel the report of the people, they will turn away from the Prophet of God, but keep it secret. They told Moses and Aaron, and they saw their opinion and took a covenant from each other about that. Then they broke the covenant and each one of them began to forbid his tribe from fighting them and to tell them what he saw: except for two men. That is what God Almighty said: And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders. “And God said, ‘Indeed, I am with you,’” meaning, He will help you against your enemy. Then He began speaking and said, If you establish prayer,’ O company of Children of Israel, and give zakat and believe in My messengers and support them,’ meaning, you will help them. It was also said: and you will respect and honor them, ‘and lend God a goodly loan,’ it was said: it is paying zakat, and it was also said: it is spending on one’s family, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds,’ I will wipe out your misdeeds, “and I will surely admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the right path,’” meaning: he has strayed from the right path, meaning the path [of truth]. The right path of everything is its middle.
