5:13: 13- So because they broke it meaning: because they broke it, and what is a connection, their covenant, Qatada said: They broke it for several reasons because they denied the messengers who came after Moses and killed the prophets of God and rejected His book and neglected His obligations, We cursed them, [Ata'] said: We distanced them from Our mercy, Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: We punished them by transforming them, And made their hearts hard, Hamza Al-Kisa'i read it as qasiyyah with a shaddah on the ba' without an alif, and they are two dialects like dhakiyah and dhakiyah, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: qasiyyah means dry, and it was said: thick and unyielding, and it was said that its meaning is: their hearts are not pure faith, rather their faith is tainted with disbelief and hypocrisy, and from it is the dirhams qasiyyah which are the bad and adulterated. They distort words from their proper places. It was said that it is their changing the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said that it is their distortion through misinterpretation. And they have forgotten a portion of that by which they were reminded. That is, they left their share of what they were commanded to do of belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and explaining his description. And you will not cease, [O Muhammad], to discover treachery among them. That is, treachery. The active participle is in the sense of the source, like the liar and the vain. It was also said that it is in the sense of the active participle, and the ha’ is for emphasis, like [narration], genealogy, sign, and account. It was also said that it is on a treacherous group. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: on treachery, that is, on disobedience. Their treachery was their breaking of the covenant and their support of the polytheists in waging war on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their intention to kill him and poison him, and similar acts of treachery that appeared, except a few of them. They did not betray or break the covenant, and they are those who converted from the People of the Book. So pardon them and overlook. “That is, turn away from them and do not interfere with them. Indeed, God loves the doers of good. This was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
5:14: 14- The Almighty said: "And of those who said, 'We are Christians,' We took their covenant." It was said: He meant by them the Jews and the Christians, so He was satisfied with mentioning one of them. The correct view is that the verse is specifically about the Christians because the Jews were mentioned before. Al-Hasan said: It is evidence that they are Christians by their name, not by the name of God Almighty. We took their covenant in monotheism and prophethood. "But they forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded, so We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection." With different desires and arguments in religion, Mujahid and Qatadah said: He means between the Jews and the Christians. Some people said: They are the Christians alone, and they became sects, including the Jacobites, Nestorians, and Melkites, and each sect disbelieves in the other. "And God will inform them of what they used to do in the Hereafter.
5:15: 15- The Almighty said: O People of the Book, meaning the two books, There has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Book, meaning: from the Torah and the Gospel, such as the deal of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the verse of stoning, and other things, and pardons much, meaning: He ignores much of what you concealed, so He does not expose it or hold you accountable for it, There has come to you from God a light, meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said: Islam, and a clear Book, meaning: clear, and it was said: clear, and it is the Qur’an.
5:16: 16- With it God guides those who pursue His pleasure, His pleasure, "the paths of peace", it was said that peace is God the Almighty, and His path is His religion that He legislated for His servants, and with which He sent His messengers, and it was said: peace is safety, like pleasure and enjoyment have the same meaning, and what is meant by it are the paths of safety, and He brings them out from darknesses into the light, that is: from the darkness of disbelief to the light of faith, by His permission, with His success and guidance, and guides them to a straight path, / which is Islam.
5:17: 17- The Almighty said: They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the Messiah, the son of Mary,’ and they are the Jacobites among the Christians who say that the Messiah is God Almighty. Say, ‘Then who has control over anything from God?’ That is, who is able to prevent anything from God’s command if He decrees it? “If He wills to destroy the Messiah, the son of Mary, and his mother, and everyone on the earth, all together. And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and God is over all things competent.”
5:18: 18- The Almighty said: And the Jews and the Christians said, ‘We are the sons of God and His beloved ones.’ It was said: They meant that God Almighty is like a father to us in tenderness and affection, and we are like sons to Him in closeness and status. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: The Jews found in the Torah, O sons of my rabbis, so they changed it to O sons of my firstborn, and from that they said: We are the sons of God. It was said: Its meaning is we are the sons of the messengers of God. God Almighty says: “Say: ‘Then why does He punish you for your sins?’” He means if the matter is as you claim, that you are His sons and beloved, then a father does not punish his son, and a beloved does not punish his beloved, and you acknowledge that He will punish you? It was said: Then why does He punish you? That is: Why did He punish those before you for their sins, transforming them into apes and pigs? Rather, you are human beings from among those He created, like all the children of Adam, rewarded for evil and good. He forgives whom He wills as a favor, and punishes whom He wills as justice. And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the final destination.
5:19: 19- The Almighty said: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, making clear to you the signs of guidance and the laws of religion, after a hiatus from the messengers, meaning a break from the messengers. They differed about the length of the period between Jesus, peace be upon him, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Uthman al-Nahdi said: Six hundred years. Qatada said: Five hundred and sixty years. Muammar and al-Kalbi said: Five hundred and forty years. It was called a period because the messengers followed one after the other after Moses, peace be upon him, without interruption until the time of Jesus, peace be upon him. And after Jesus, peace be upon him, there was no one but our Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. So that you may not say, lest you say, “There has come to us no bearer of good tidings or a warner. But there has come to you a bearer of good tidings and a warner. And God is over all things competent.”
5:20: 20- The Almighty said: And when Moses said to his people, ‘O my people, remember the favor of God upon you when He made prophets among you’ [i.e., among you prophets] ‘and made you kings’, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He means owners of servants and retinues. Qatada said: They were the first to have servants, and those before them did not have servants. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, a woman, and an animal, he would be recorded as a king. Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Habli said: I heard Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, and a man asked him and said: Are we not among the poor immigrants? Abdullah said to him: Do you have a wife to whom you can take refuge? He said: Yes. He said: Do you have a house to live in? He said: By my uncle. He said: Then you are among the rich. He said: Then I have a servant. He said: Then you are among the kings. Al-Suddi said: And He made you free kings who control your own affairs after you had been in the hands of the Copts who enslaved you. Al-Dahhak said: Their homes were spacious and had running water, so whoever had a spacious home with running water was a king. And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds, meaning the scholars of your time. Mujahid said: He meant manna, quails, stones, and the shade of clouds.
5:21: 21- The power of God Almighty: O my people, enter the Holy Land which God has assigned to you. They differed about the Holy Land. Mujahid said: It is Mount Tur and what is around it. Ad-Dahhak said: Ilya and Jerusalem. Ikrimah and As-Suddi said: It is Jericho. Al-Kalbi said: It is Damascus, Palestine and some of Jordan. Qatada said: It is all of Ash-Sham. Ka'b said: I found in the revealed Book of God that Ash-Sham is God's treasure on His earth and that most of His servants are in it. The Almighty said, God has decreed for you meaning: He wrote in the Preserved Tablet that they are dwellings for you. Ibn Ishaq said: God has given them to you. It was also said: He made them for you. Al-Suddi said: God has commanded you to enter them. [Qatada said]: They were commanded to do so as they were commanded to pray, meaning: it was made obligatory upon you. And do not turn back on your heels, or you will become losers. Al-Kalbi said: Abraham, peace be upon him, ascended
5:22: 22- They said, 'O Moses, indeed therein are a people of mighty men.' This is because the leaders who went out to spy on the report, when they returned to Moses and told him what they had witnessed, Moses said to them: Keep their affair secret and do not tell it to anyone in the army, lest they fail. So each man of them told his relative and cousin except for two men who were faithful to what Moses had told them. One of them was Joshua bin Nun bin Ephraim bin Joseph, peace be upon them, the young man of Moses, and the other was Caleb bin Yoqna, the son-in-law of Moses, peace be upon him, to his sister Mary, daughter of Imran. He was from the tribe of Judah, and they were among the leaders. A group of the Children of Israel learned of this and raised their voices in weeping and said, "Oh, would that we were in the land of Egypt! Would that we would die in this [wilderness] and that God would not let us enter their land so that our women, children, and burdens would be spoils for them." The man kept saying to his companion: Come, let us appoint a leader over us and return to Egypt. This is what God Almighty said, informing about them: They said, 'O Moses, indeed therein are a people of mighty men.' A mighty people, and we will never enter it until they leave it. If they leave it, then we will enter.” The root of the word mighty is: the one who is mighty and invincible to subjugation. It is said: a tall palm tree is mighty if it is inaccessible to hands. Those people were called mighty because of their height and the strength of their bodies. They were from the giants and the remnants of the people of Ad. When the Children of Israel said what they said and were about to return to Egypt, Moses and Aaron fell down in prostration, and Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes. They are the ones God Almighty spoke about in His saying:
5:23: 23- Two men from among those who feared said, meaning: they feared God Almighty. Saeed bin Jubair read they fear with a damma on the ya', and he said: The two men were from the tyrants, so they submitted and followed Moses. God bestowed His favor upon them with success and protection. They said: Enter upon them through the gate, meaning the village of the tyrants. And when you have entered it, you will be victorious, because God Almighty fulfills His promise. And we saw them, and their bodies were great but their hearts were weak, so do not fear them. And upon God rely, if you are believers, so the Children of Israel wanted to stone them with stones, but they disobeyed them.
5:24: 24- "They said, 'O Moses, we will never enter it as long as they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. We will remain right here.'" Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Abu Naim, I told Israel, on the authority of Mukhariq, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, he said: I heard Ibn Masoud say: I witnessed a scene from Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad, and I would have preferred to be his companion than to be treated justly. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was calling down curses on the polytheists, and he said: We will not say as the people of Moses, peace be upon him, said: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, but we will fight on your right and on your left, in front of you and behind you. I saw the face of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, shine and he was pleased with what he said. So when the Children of Israel did what they did, disobeying the command of their Lord and their concern for Joshua and Caleb, Moses, peace be upon him, became angry and called down curses on them:
5:25: 25- He said, ‘My Lord, I have no control over anyone except myself and my brother.’ [It was said: Its meaning is my brother/ he does not have control over anyone except himself, and it was said: Its meaning is he does not give me anyone except myself and my brother.] So separate, separate, between us, it was said: judge between us, and between the wicked people, the disobedient ones.
5:26: 26- "He said, God Almighty, it is forbidden to them," it was said: Here the speech is complete, its meaning is that the city is forbidden to them forever, it did not mean a prohibition of worship, but rather it meant a prohibition of prevention, so God Almighty revealed to Moses: [By Me I have sworn] that I will forbid them from entering the Holy Land except for My servants Joshua and Caleb, and I will bring them into this wilderness "forty years," [wandering] in place of every day in which you are detained for a year, and I will throw their corpses into these wastelands, and as for their children who did not know evil, they will enter it, so that is what God Almighty said: "It is forbidden to them for forty years, wandering, bewildered, in the land, so do not grieve over the wicked people," meaning do not grieve over such people, so they stayed for forty years in six leagues and they were six hundred thousand fighters, and they were walking every day seriously, and when evening came they were in the place from which they departed. It was said: Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, were not among them, and the most correct is that they were among them and there was no punishment for them, rather the punishment was for those people, and everyone who entered it who was over twenty years old died in the wilderness except Joshua and Caleb, and no one entered Jericho who said we will never enter it, so when they perished and the forty years passed, and the young ones from their descendants grew up, they went to war with the giants. They differed about who led that war and by whose hand the conquest took place. Some people said: Moses conquered Jericho and Joshua was at the forefront of his army. Moses, peace be upon him, marched towards them with those who remained of the Children of Israel. Joshua entered it and fought the giants. Then Moses, peace be upon him, entered it and stayed there as long as God Almighty willed. Then God Almighty took him to Himself, and no one knows his grave. This is the most correct of the statements, as the scholars agree that Awj bin Anq was killed by Moses, peace be upon him. Others said: The tyrants were fought by Joshua, and he did not go to them after the death of Moses, peace be upon him. (They said: Moses died) and Aaron were both in the wilderness. The story of Aaron's death Al-Suddi said: God Almighty revealed to Moses that I will kill Aaron, so bring him to such-and-such a mountain. Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, set out towards that mountain and behold, they saw a tree the likes of which had never been seen before, and behold, a house built and in it a bed with a mattress on it and a pleasant scent in it. When Aaron saw that, he was pleased and said: O Moses, I would like to sleep on this bed. He said: Sleep on it. He said: I fear that the Lord of this house will come and become angry with me. Moses said to him: Do not be afraid, I will suffice you in the matter of the Lord of this house, so sleep. Moses said: Sleep with me, for if the Lord of the house comes, He will become angry with me and with you both. When they slept, death overtook Aaron. When he found his end, he said: O Moses, you have deceived me. When he died, the house was raised and that tree was gone and the bed was raised with him to the sky. When Moses returned to the Children of Israel and Aaron was not with him, they said: Moses killed Aaron and was jealous of him because of the Children of Israel’s love for him. Moses, peace be upon him, said: Woe to you, he was my brother, so how could I kill him? When they complained a lot about him, he stood up and prayed two rak’ahs, then he supplicated to God Almighty and descended the bed until… They looked at him between heaven and earth and believed him. On the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, he said: Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, ascended the mountain, and Aaron died [and Moses remained]. The Children of Israel said to Moses, peace be upon him, You killed him, so they harmed him. Then God commanded the angels to carry him until they passed by. They told the Children of Israel about him, and the angels spoke of his death until the Children of Israel knew that he had died. Then God, the Most High, cleared him of what they had said. Then the angels carried him and buried him, and no one saw the location of his grave except the marble, so God made him deaf and mute. Amr bin Maimon said: Aaron died before Moses, peace be upon him, died in the wilderness. They had gone out to some caves. Aaron died and Moses buried him and returned to the Children of Israel. They said: He killed him because we love him, and he was beloved by the Children of Israel. Moses, peace be upon him, supplicated to his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and God revealed to him: Go with them to his grave, for I will resurrect him. So he went with them to his grave. Moses called out to him and he came out of his grave shaking his head. He said: Did I kill you? He said: No, but I died. He said: Then return to your bed, and they left. As for the death of Moses, peace be upon him, Ibn Ishaq said: Moses, peace be upon him, hated death and held it in high esteem, so God wanted to make death beloved to him. So, Joshua bin Nun was informed, and he would come to him in the morning and evening. He said: Moses, peace be upon him, would say to him, O son of God, what did God tell you? [So Joshua would say to him, “O Prophet of God, did I not accompany you for such and such years? Did I ask you about something that God told you] so that you would be the one to start with it and mention it? And he would not mention anything to him. So when Moses saw that, he hated life and loved death. Abu Ali Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Angel of Death came to Moses bin Imran and said to him: Answer your Lord. Moses, peace be upon him, slapped the Angel of Death in the eye and gouged it out. The Angel of Death returned to God Almighty and said: You sent me to a servant of yours who does not want death, and I gouged out my eye. God restored his eye to him and said: Go back to my servant and say to him: Do you want life? If you want life, then place your hand on the back of an ox and whatever hair your hand hides, you will live by it for a year. He said: Then what? He said: Then you will die. He said: Now, my Lord, bring me close to the Holy Land, a stone’s throw away. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, if I were there, I would show you his grave next to the road near the red sand dune.” Wahb said: Moses went out to do some errand of his and passed by a group of angels digging a grave. He had never seen anything more beautiful than it, nor like what was in it of greenery, freshness and joy. He said to them: O angels of God, why are you digging this grave? They said: For a servant who is honored by his Lord. He said: This servant of God is in a position like the one I have never seen lying down before. The angels said: O chosen one of God, would you like it to be yours? He said: I would like it. They said: Then go down and lie down in it and turn to your Lord. He said: So he lay down in it and turned to his Lord, then he breathed with an easier breath, and God, Blessed and Exalted be He, took his soul, then the angels settled over him. It was said: The Angel of Death brought him an apple from Paradise, so he smelled it and took his soul. Moses was one hundred and twenty years old. When Moses, peace be upon him, died and the forty years had passed, God sent Joshua as a prophet. He informed them that God had commanded him to fight the giants. They believed him and followed him. He headed with the Children of Israel to Jericho, and with him was the Ark of the Covenant. He surrounded the city of Jericho for six months. When the seventh month came, they blew the trumpet and the people made a great uproar, so the city wall fell. They entered and fought the giants and defeated them and attacked them, killing them. The group of the Children of Israel would gather around the neck of a man, striking it until they cut it off. The fighting took place on Friday, and a remnant of them remained. The sun was about to set and enter the night of Saturday. He said: O God, return the sun to me. He said to al-Shams 91:You are in the obedience of God Almighty and I am in His obedience. He asked the sun to stop and the two moons to remain so that he could take revenge on the enemies of God Almighty before the Sabbath. The sun was returned to him and an hour was added to the day until he killed them all. He pursued the kings of the Levant and took thirty-one of them until he defeated them. All the land of Ash-Sham, and all of Ash-Sham became for the children of Israel, and he distributed his workers in its regions/ and collected the spoils, so the fire did not descend, so God revealed to Joshua that there was embezzlement in it, so he ordered them to pledge allegiance, so they pledged allegiance to him, and the hand of one of them stuck to his hand, so he said: Bring what you have, so he brought him a bull’s head of gold crowned with rubies and jewels that he had embezzled, so he put it in the offering and put the man with him, so the fire came and consumed the man and the offering, then Joshua died and was buried in Mount Ephraim, and it was He was one hundred and twenty-six years old, and he managed the affairs of the Children of Israel after Moses, peace be upon him, for twenty-seven years.
5:27: 27- The Almighty said: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, and they are Abel and Cain, and he is called Qabin, when they offered a sacrifice, and the reason for their sacrifice, according to what the people of knowledge have mentioned, was that Eve used to give birth to Adam, peace be upon him, in every pregnancy, a boy and a girl, and all that she gave birth to were forty children in twenty pregnancy, the first of them was Cain and his twin, Aqlima, and the last of them was Abd al-Mughith and his twin, Umma al-Mughith, then God Almighty blessed the offspring of Adam, peace be upon him. Ibn Abbas said: Adam did not die until his children and his children’s children reached forty thousand. They differed about the birth of Cain and Abel. Some of them said: Adam had intercourse with Eve one hundred years after their descent to Earth, and she gave birth to Cain and his twin, Aqlima, in one womb. Then she gave birth to Abel and his twin, Buddah, in another womb. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of some scholars of the first book: Adam used to have intercourse with Eve in Paradise before he committed the sin, so she became pregnant with Cain and his twin sister Aqlima, and she did not find any fever, or pain, or labor pains on them until she gave birth to them, and she did not see any blood with them. When he descended to the earth, he had intercourse with her, and she became pregnant with Abel and his twin sister, and she found fever, pain, labor pains, and blood on them. When Adam’s children grew up, he would marry the boy of this womb to the girl of another womb, so the man among them would marry any of his sisters he wanted except his twin sister who was born with him, because there were no women at that time except their sisters. When Cain and his twin sister Aqlima were born, then Abel and his twin sister Lubad, and there were two years between them according to al-Kalbi, and they reached maturity, God Almighty commanded Adam, peace be upon him, to marry Cain to Lubad, the sister of Abel, and to marry Abel to Lubad, the sister of Cain. Cain’s sister was more beautiful than Abel’s sister, so Adam mentioned that to his son and Abel was pleased. And Cain became angry and said: She is my sister, I have more right to her, and we are from [the birth of] Paradise and they are from [the birth of] Earth, so his father said to him: She is not lawful for you, but he refused to accept that, and said: God did not command him to do this, but it is his opinion, so Adam, peace be upon him, said to them: So offer a sacrifice, and whichever of you accepts his sacrifice is more entitled to it, and if the sacrifices were accepted, a white fire would descend from the sky and consume it, and if they were not accepted, the fire would not descend and the birds and beasts would consume it, so they went out to offer [a sacrifice]. Cain was a farmer, so he offered a heap of food to whoever he wanted to plant, and he thought in his heart: I do not care whether it is accepted from me or not, he will never marry my sister, and Abel was a sheep owner, so he took the best ram from his flock and offered it, and he thought in his heart the pleasure of God Almighty, so they placed their sacrifice on top of the mountain, then Adam, peace be upon him, called, and a fire came down from the sky and consumed Abel’s sacrifice but did not consume Cain’s sacrifice, so that is what God Almighty said: It was accepted from one of them, [meaning Abel], but it was not accepted from the other, meaning Cain. So they came down from the mountain and Cain was angry because his sacrifice was rejected. He harbored envy until Adam came to Mecca to visit the House. When Adam disappeared, Cain came to Abel while he was with his sheep. He said, ‘I will kill you.’ He said, Why?’ He said, “Because God accepted your sacrifice and rejected my sacrifice. You will marry my beautiful sister and I will marry your ugly sister, and people will say that you are better than me and your son will boast over my son.” Abel said, What is my fault? God only accepts from those who fear Him.
5:28: 28- "If you were to stretch out your hand towards me to kill me, I would not stretch out my hand towards you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the Worlds." Abdullah bin Omar said: By God, the one who was to be killed was the stronger of the two men, but hardship prevented him from stretching out his hand towards his brother. This is permissible in the law of Adam for the one who was to be killed to submit and surrender in search of reward, as Uthman, may God be pleased with him, did. Mujahid said: It was written for them at that time that if a man wanted to kill another, he should not refrain and be patient.
5:29: 29- I want you to bear, return, and it was said: bear, with my sin and your sin, meaning: with the sin of killing me to your sin, meaning the sin of your hardships that you knew before, this is the saying of most of the commentators. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Its meaning is that I want my sin that I committed to be upon you if you kill me and your sin, so you bear my sin and my blood together, and it was said: Its meaning is that you return with the sin of killing me and the sin of your disobedience for which your sacrifice was not accepted, or the sin of your envy. If it is said: How did he say, I want you to bear my sin and your sin, when the will to kill and disobey is not permissible? It is said that this is not a true will, but rather when he knew that he would inevitably kill him, he prepared himself to surrender in search of reward, so it is as if he wanted to kill him metaphorically, even if he did not want it in reality. It is said that its meaning is that I want you to bear the punishment of killing me, so it is a correct will, because it is in accordance with the ruling of God Almighty, so this is not a will to kill, but rather because of the reason for killing, which is sin and punishment, and you will be among the companions of the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
5:30: 30- The Almighty said: So his soul made it easy for him, meaning: it obeyed him, supported him and helped him, killing his brother, meaning in killing his brother, [Mujahid said: So he encouraged him, and Qatada said: So his soul made it seem good to him, and Yaman said: His soul made it easy for him, meaning it made it easy] Its meaning: His soul made it appear to him that killing his brother was easy for him, meaning it was easy for him, so he killed him. When Cain intended to kill Abel, he did not know how to kill him. Ibn Jurayj said: Satan appeared to him and took a bird and placed its head on a rock, then smashed its head with another rock while Cain was looking at it, so he taught it how to kill, so Cain smashed Abel's head between two rocks, and he was killed while he was surrendering. It was said: He assassinated him while he was asleep, so he smashed his head and killed him. This is the Almighty's saying: So he killed him, and he became among the losers, and Abel was twenty years old when he was killed. They differed about the place where he was killed. [It was said: In Basra, in the place of the Great Mosque. The body of the killer turned black, and Adam, peace be upon him, asked him about his brother. He said: I was not his guardian. He said: Rather, she said it, and that is why your body turned black. Adam remained for a hundred years without laughing once since he killed him.] Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: On Mount [Thawr] and it was said at the Aqaba of Hira. When he killed him, he left him in the open and did not know what to do with him because he was the first of the sons of Adam to die on the face of the earth. The wild beasts sought him out, so he carried him in a bag on his back for forty days, and Ibn Abbas said a year, until I returned. The birds and wild beasts swarmed around him, waiting for him to throw him away so they could eat him. Then God sent two ravens and they fought. One of them killed the other, then dug a hole for him with its beak and foot until it was secure for him, then threw him into the hole and buried him, and Cain looked at him. This is what God Almighty said:
5:31: 31- So God sent a raven scratching the ground to show him how to hide his brother's private parts. When Cain saw that, he said, Woe to me! A word of regret. It was said that when he saw the burial from the raven, he was more knowledgeable than him and that what he did was ignorance, so he regretted and regretted. He said, 'Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and hide my brother's private parts?' That is, his corpse. It was also said: his private parts because he had stolen his clothes. So he became one of the regretful, for carrying him on his shoulders, not for killing him. It was also said: for parting from his brother. It was also said: he regretted the lack of benefit in killing him, as he angered his parents, and he did not benefit from killing him at all. His regret was not for killing and riding the wolf. Abdul Muttalib bin Abdullah bin Hantab said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, the earth and everything on it shook for seven days, then the earth drank his blood as one drinks water. Then God called out to him, Where is your brother Abel? He said, I do not know, as I was not watching him. Then God Almighty said, Your brother’s blood calls out to Me from the earth, so why did you kill your brother? He said, Then where is his blood if I killed him? So God Almighty forbade the earth that day from ever drinking blood after him. Muqatil bin Sulayman said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: When Cain killed Abel and Adam, peace be upon him, in Mecca, the trees became intertwined, the foods changed, the fruits became sour, the water became bitter, and the earth became dusty. Adam, peace be upon him, said: Something has happened on earth. So he went to India and found Cain had killed Abel. So he began to say, and he was the first to write poetry: The country and its people have changed, and the face of the earth is dusty and ugly. Everything changed in color and taste, and the cheerful face became less It was narrated: The handsome. It was narrated on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Whoever says that Adam, peace be upon him, said poetry has lied. Muhammad, peace be upon him, and all the prophets, peace be upon them, are equal in forbidding poetry. However, when Cain killed Abel, Adam, who was a Syriac, eulogized him. When Adam recited his elegy, he said to Seth: O my son, you are a trustee, memorize these words so that they may be inherited and people may be moved by them. It continued to be transmitted until it reached Ya`rub bin Qahtan, who spoke Arabic and Syriac and was the first to write in Arabic. He used to write poetry, so he looked at the elegy and returned the first to the last and the last to the first, so he weighed it into poetry and added verses to it, including: Why should I not shed tears for Abel, who is buried in the grave? I see my whole life in sorrow, so am I at peace with my life? When Adam, peace be upon him, lived one hundred and thirty years, five years after killing Abel, Eve gave birth to Seth, meaning: God’s gift, meaning that he was left behind by Abel, whom God Almighty taught the hours of the night and day, and taught him how to worship creation at every hour of them, and sent down fifty pages to him, so he became Adam’s guardian and heir apparent. As for Cain, he was told to go, fugitive, homeless, terrified, and fearful, not feeling safe from anyone he saw. So he took his sister Iqlimah by the hand and fled with her to Aden in the land of Yemen. Then Satan came to him and said to him: Fire consumed Abel’s sacrifice because he worshipped fire, so you set up a fire also for yourself and your descendants. So he built a house of fire, and he was the first to worship fire. No one would pass by it without throwing stones at it. Then his blind son came with his son, and his son said: This is your father Cain. So the blind man threw stones at his father and killed him. The son of the blind man said: Did you kill your father? So he raised his hand and slapped his son, and he died. The blind man said: Woe is me! I killed my father with my shot and killed my son with my slap. Mujahed said: One of Cain’s legs was hung to her thigh, her leg, and she was hung from that day until the Day of Resurrection, with her face toward the sun as it turned around her, in the summer a fence of fire and in the winter a fence of snow. He said: The children made musical instruments of the pen, drums, flutes, lutes and tambourines, and they were immersed in amusement, drinking alcohol, worshipping fire, committing adultery and committing indecencies until God destroyed them with the flood in the days of Noah, peace be upon him, and the descendants of Seth remained. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Omar bin Hafs bin Ghayath told us, my father told us, Al-A’sha told us, Abdullah bin Marra told me, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam will bear a share of its blood, because he was the first to institute killing.
5:32: 32- The Almighty said: Because of that, Abu Ja`far read because of with a broken nun connected, and the general reading is with a jazm nun, meaning: as a result of that killer and his crime, it is said: ajal ya`jul ajlan if he committed a crime, like akhada yakhudhu, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul, he killed it and retaliation is taken from him, or corruption in the land meaning without a soul and without corruption in the land from disbelief or adultery or highway robbery, or something like that it is as if he had killed all of mankind, they differed regarding Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, in the narration of Ikrimah: Whoever kills a prophet or a just imam is as if he had killed all of mankind, and whoever attacks a group of Bani or a just imam is as if he had saved all of mankind. Mujahed said: Whoever kills a soul forbidden to be killed will burn in Hellfire for killing it, just as he would burn in Hellfire if he killed all of humanity. Whoever saves a soul from being killed will be saved from killing all of humanity. Qatada said: May God make her reward great and her burden great. Its meaning is that whoever considers it permissible to kill a Muslim unjustly, it is as if he had killed all of mankind in sin because they are not safe from him. And whoever saves a life, and refrains from killing it, it is as if he had saved all of mankind [in reward because they are safe from him. Al-Hasan said: It is as if he had killed all of mankind. Meaning: He is required to pay retaliation for killing her, just as he would have been required to pay if he had killed all of mankind. And whoever saves a life: that is, he pardons the one for whom retaliation is required and does not kill him, it is as if he had saved all of mankind. Sulayman ibn Ali said: I said to Al-Hasan: O Abu Saeed, is it for us as it was for the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, by the One besides Whom there is no god, the blood of the Children of Israel was not more precious to God than our blood. And indeed Our messengers came to them with clear proofs; then indeed, many of them, after that, were transgressors upon the earth.
5:33: 33- The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption in the land, the verse. Ad-Dahhak said: It was revealed about a group of people from the People of the Book who had a treaty with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they broke the treaty, cut off the way, and spread corruption on the land. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about the people of Hilal bin Uwaimir. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a pact with Hilal bin Uwaimir, who is Abu Burdah Al-Aslami, on the condition that he would not help him or help anyone against him. Whoever passes by Hilal bin Uwaimir to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is safe and will not be attacked. Then a group of Banu Kinanah who wanted to convert to Islam passed by some of the people of Hilal bin Uwaimir who had converted to Islam, and Hilal was not a witness. So they attacked them and killed them and took their money. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down with the judgment concerning them. Saeed bin Jubair said: It was revealed about some people from Uraynah and Ukl who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and pledged allegiance to him on Islam, but they were liars. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them to the camels of charity, but they apostatized and killed the shepherd and drove away the camels. [Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Abu Qilabah Al-Jarmi told me] on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: A group of people from Ukl came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they converted to Islam and settled in Madinah. So he [the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace] ordered them to go to the camels of charity and drink from their urine and milk. So they did and they recovered, then they apostatized and killed their shepherds and drove away the camels. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent after them, and he brought them and cut off their hands and feet and gouged out their eyes, and he did not cauterize them until they died. It was narrated by Ayoub on the authority of Qilabah on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: He cut off their hands and feet, then ordered nails to be used to apply kohl to their eyes, and threw them into the lava field to pray for rain, but they were not given rain until they died. Abu Qilabah said: They killed, stole, fought against God and His Messenger, and spread corruption on earth [which is what is meant by God Almighty’s saying: and they spread corruption on earth]. They differed regarding the ruling on these Arabs. Some of them said: It is abrogated because mutilation is not permissible. Some of them said: Its ruling is fixed except for the smelting [and mutilation]. Qatada narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin that this was before [the punishment was revealed]. Abu al-Zinad said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that to them, God revealed the punishments and forbade him from mutilation, so he did not return. On the authority of Qatada, he said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after that urged charity and forbade mutilation. Sulayman al-Taymi said on the authority of Anas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, blinded those people because they had spared the eyes of the shepherds. Al-Layth ibn Sa`d said: This verse was revealed as a rebuke to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and as a teaching of his punishment for them. He said: This is their punishment, not mutilation. Therefore, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not stand up to preach except that he forbade mutilation. They differed about the warriors who deserve this punishment. Some people said: They are those who block the road and carry weapons, and the stubborn ones in the cities. This is the opinion of Al-Awza’i, Malik, Al-Layth bin Sa’d, and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them. Some people said: The stubborn ones in the cities do not have the same ruling as the combatants in deserving these punishments. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him. The punishment for those who fight is what God Almighty mentioned: That they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. Some people went to the view that the imam has the choice in the matter of those who fight between killing, cutting off, crucifixion, [and exile] as is apparent in the verse, and this is the view of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Hasan, Al-Nakha’i, and Mujahid. Most of them went to that these punishments are based on the order of the crimes and not on the choice, [because Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, I told Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal, I told Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm, I told Al-Rabi’, I told Al-Shafi’i, I told Ibrahim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Salih, the client of Al-Tawa’mah] on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding highway robbers, if they kill and take money, they are killed and crucified, and if they kill and do not take money, they are killed and not crucified, and if they take money and do not kill, their hands and feet are cut off on opposite sides, and if they frighten people on the road and do not take money, they are banished from the land. This is the opinion of Qatada, Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i, and the people of opinion, may God Almighty have mercy on them. [And if a highwayman is killed, he must be killed] inevitably, so that he is not forgiven by the blood money’s pardon. And if he takes a minimum amount of money, which is a quarter of a dinar, his right hand and left foot are cut off. And if he kills and takes the money, he is killed and crucified. They differed on how it should be done: The apparent view of Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, is that he should be killed and then crucified. It was also said that he should be crucified alive and then stabbed until he dies crucified, which is the view of Al-Layth bin Sa’d. It was also said that he should be crucified alive for three days and then taken down and killed. If he terrifies others on the road, he should be banished. They differed about banishment: Some people said that the imam should seek him out, so he should be banished from every town where he is found. This is the opinion of Saeed bin Jubair and Omar bin Abdul Aziz. It was also said that he should be sought out so that the prescribed punishments could be carried out on him. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas and Al-Layth bin Saad, and Al-Shafi’i said the same. The people of Kufa said that banishment means imprisonment, and it is banishment from the land. Muhammad bin Jarir said: He should be banished from his country to another and imprisoned in prison [in the country to which he was banished until his repentance is evident. Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was the first to be imprisoned in prisons]. He said: I will imprison him until I know that he has repented, and I will not banish him to a country where he will harm them. That, which I mentioned of the prescribed punishment, for them is disgrace torment, humiliation and scandal, in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
5:34: 34- "Except for those who repent before you have power over them. Know that God is Forgiving and Merciful." Whoever believes that the verse was revealed about the infidels, said that its meaning is: Except for those who repented from their polytheism and submitted before you have power over them, then there is no way for them to be punished for any of the prescribed punishments, nor is there any responsibility for what they took in their state of disbelief of blood or money. As for the Muslim combatants, whoever [repents] among them before you have power over them, and before the imam seizes him, then every punishment that is due as a right of God is dropped from him, and he is not dropped from him by repentance before he is able to overpower him, and the killing is required, and the retaliation remains for the guardian of the murdered person, so if he wishes he may pardon him, and if he wishes he may exact it, and if he has taken the money, then [amputation] is dropped from him, and if he has combined both, then the killing and crucifixion are dropped from him, and the money must be guaranteed, and this is the opinion of Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him. Some of them said: If he comes repentant before he is able to do so, no one will be held accountable for his blood or money unless he has specific money with him to its owner. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that Haritha bin Yazid went out to fight, shed blood, and took money. Then he came back repentant before he was overpowered. Ali, may God be pleased with him, did not make him responsible [for blood or money, unless he had money with him, in which case he would return it to its owner]. As for the one who repented after he was overpowered, nothing of it is dropped from him. It was said: Every punishment that is due to God Almighty, such as highway robbery, theft, adultery, and drinking, is dropped by repentance in all cases, and most are of the opinion that it is not dropped.
5:35: 35- O you who have believed, fear God and seek seek the means of approach to Him meaning: closeness, the active participle of the verb to seek to approach someone with such-and-such, meaning: to draw near to him, and its plural is wasail, and strive in His cause that you may succeed [SumMaryam 19:Obey God’s command and you will be saved].
5:36: 36- "Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and as much more with it to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them." He informed us that if the disbeliever owned the entire world and as much with it and then ransomed himself thereby from the punishment, that ransom would not be accepted from him, and they will have a painful punishment.
5:37: 37- They want to get out of the Fire, but they will never get out of it. There are two aspects to this. One of them is that they intend and seek a way out of it, as God Almighty said: Every time they want to get out of it (al-Hajj 22:22). The second is that they wish for that in their hearts, as God Almighty said, informing us about them: Our Lord, get us out of it (Al-Mu'minun: 107). And for them is a lasting punishment.
5:38: 38- And the male thief, male thief, cut off their hands, meaning their right hands, and this is also the case in the Mushaf of Abd ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him. The ruling is that whoever steals a [minimum] amount of money from a safe place without any doubt, his right hand will be cut off from the wrist. Amputation is not required for stealing less than the minimum amount according to most scholars. It was reported that Ibn al-Zubayr used to have his hand amputated for a small amount, but most scholars disagree with him. They differed about the amount for which the hand should be cut off: Most of them held that the hand should not be cut off for less than a quarter of a dinar. If he steals a quarter of a dinar or something the amount of which is a quarter of a dinar, the hand should be cut off. This is the opinion of Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali, may God be pleased with them. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Awza’i, and al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them, said the same, because Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Kisa’i informed us, I told Abd al-Aziz Ahmad al-Khalal, I told Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm, I told al-Rabi’, I told al-Shafi’i, I told Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cutting off for a quarter of a dinar or more. Abu al-Hasan al-Shirzi told us, Zahir bin Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, Malik told us, Nafi` told us, Abdullah told us, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off the hand of a thief for stealing a shield worth three dirhams. It was narrated on the authority of Uthman that he cut off the hand of a thief for a citron valued at three dirhams, as he had exchanged twelve dirhams for one dinar. This is the opinion of Malik, may God have mercy on him, that he cut off the hand for three dirhams. Some people said that the hand should not be cut off for less than a dinar or ten dirhams. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, and Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion agreed with it. Some people said that the hand is not cut off except for five dirhams. This was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, and Ibn Abi Laila said the same. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Umar bin Hafs bin Ghayath told me, my father told me, Al-A’mash said: I heard Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: May God curse the thief who steals an egg and has his hand cut off, and who steals a rope and has his hand cut off. Al-A’mash said: They used to think that it was iron eggs and ropes. They thought that some of them were worth dirhams. This hadith is used as evidence by those who believe that cutting off the hand for a small thing is permissible, and according to most scholars it is based on what Al-A’sha said, / because of the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: “And if he steals something that is not protected, such as fruit in a wall that has no guard, or an animal in the wilderness that has no guard, or goods in a house that is separate from other houses, then he is not to be cut off.” It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “There is no cutting off for hanging fruit or for a mountain guard. But if a stable or a granary shelters it, then cutting off is for what amounts to the price of a shield.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is no amputation of the hand of a traitor, a plunderer, or a thief. If he steals money that is suspicious, such as a slave stealing from his master’s money, or a son stealing from his father’s money, or a father stealing from his son’s money, or one of the partners stealing something from the joint money, there is no amputation for him. If a thief steals for the first time, his right hand is cut off from the elbow, and if he steals for the second time, his left leg is cut off from the ankle joint. They differed as to whether he steals a third time: most of them are of the opinion that his left hand is cut off, then if he steals a fourth time, his right foot is cut off, then if he steals after that, he is punished and imprisoned until his repentance is evident. This is what was narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and it is the opinion of Qatadah. Malik and al-Shafi’i said the same, because it was narrated from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Regarding the thief who steals, if he steals, cut off his foot, then if he steals again, cut off his hand, then if he steals again, cut off his foot. Some people said that if he steals a third time after his right hand and left foot have been cut off, his hand is not to be cut off, but rather he is to be imprisoned. This was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: I would be ashamed not to leave him a hand with which to clean himself or a foot with which to walk. This is the opinion of Al-Sha’bi and Al-Nakha’i, and it was also said by Al-Awza’i, Ahmad, and the people of opinion. The Almighty’s statement: As a recompense for what they have earned, is in the accusative case as a state and as cutting off, and similar to it is: A punishment, meaning a punishment, from God, and God is Exalted in Might and Wise.
5:39: 39- But whoever repents after his wrongdoing, i.e. his theft, and reforms his work, "then God will accept his repentance. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful", this is between him and God Almighty. As for cutting off his hand, it is not dropped by repentance according to the majority. Mujahid said: The thief's repentance is cut off, so if he cuts off his hand, his repentance is achieved. The correct view is that cutting off is a punishment for the crime, as He said: A punishment for what they earned, so repentance is necessary afterwards, and his repentance is regret for what has passed and the determination to leave it in the future. If the thief's hand is cut off, he must pay the compensation for the money he stole according to the majority of scholars. Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion said: He is not required to pay compensation, and by consensus, if the stolen item is still with him, he can take it back and his hand is cut off, because cutting off is the right of God Almighty and the compensation is the right of the servant, so one does not prevent the other, like taking back the object.
5:40: 40- The Almighty’s saying, Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is everyone. It was said that its meaning is, Do you not know, O human being? So it is addressed to every person among the people. He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills. Al-Suddi and Al-Kalbi said: He punishes whom He wills: whoever dies in his disbelief, and forgives whom He wills: [the major sin], whoever repents from his disbelief. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: He punishes whom He wills for the minor sin, and forgives whom He wills for the major sin. And God is over all things competent.
5:41: 41- The Almighty said: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you, meaning: into befriending the disbelievers, for they will not defeat God, of those who say, ‘We believe,’ with their mouths, but their hearts do not believe, and they are the hypocrites, and of those who are Jews, meaning: the Jews, listeners, meaning: a people who listen, for lies, like the saying of the one praying: God hears whoever praises Him, meaning: God accepts, and it was said: listeners for the sake of lies, meaning they listen to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, then they go out and say: We heard from him such and such, but they did not hear that from him, listeners for another people who did not come to you, meaning: they are spies, meaning: Banu Qurayzah for another people, and they are the people of Khaybar. “A man and a woman from the nobles of Khaybar committed adultery and they were married, and the punishment for them was stoning in the Torah. The Jews were reluctant to stone them because of their honor, so they said: This man in Yathrib does not have stoning in his book, but it is flogging. So send to your brothers from Banu Qurayzah, for they are his neighbors and he has agreed to it, so let them ask him about that. So they sent a group of them secretly and said to them: Ask Muhammad about adulterers if we are married, what is their punishment? If he orders you to flog, then accept it, and if he orders you to stone, then beware of it and do not accept it from him. So they sent the adulterers with them, so the group came until they camped among Banu Qurayzah and Nadir, and they said to them: You are neighbors of this man and he is in his own country.” It happened that so-and-so and so-and-so committed adultery with our chaste women, so we would like you to ask Muhammad for our sake about his judgment on it. So Qurayza and Nadir said to them: Then God will command you to do what you hate. Then a group of people, including Ka`b ibn al-Ashraf, Ka`b ibn Asad, Sa`iyah ibn `Amr, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Kinanah ibn Abi al-Haqiq, and others, went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, tell us about the adulterer and adulteress if we are married. What is their punishment in your book? Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you satisfied with my judgment? They said: Yes. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down with the stoning and informed them of that, but they refused to accept it. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to him: Place Ibn Suriya between you and them, and he described him to him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Do you know a young man with no beard and no one eye who lives in Fadak and is called Ibn Suriya? They said: Yes. He said: What kind of man is he among you? They said: He is the most knowledgeable Jew remaining on the face of the earth about what God Almighty revealed to Moses, peace be upon him, in the Torah. He said: So they sent for him, and they did so, and he came to them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Are you the son of Suriya? He said: Yes. He said: And are you the most knowledgeable of the Jews? He said: That is what they claim. He said: Do you make it between me and you? They said: Yes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: I ask you by God, there is no god but Him, who sent down the Torah to Moses, peace be upon him, and brought you out of Egypt, and split the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh, and who shaded you with clouds and sent down to you manna and quails, and sent down to you His Book in which is what is lawful and what is unlawful, do you find in your Book stoning for the married? Ibn Suriya said: Yes, and by what you mentioned to me, were it not for the fear that the Torah would burn me if I lied or changed it, I would not have confessed to you. But how is it in your book, O Muhammad? He said: If four just men testify that he has put it in it as a kohl stick is put in a kohl container, then he must be stoned. Ibn Suriya said: By Him who sent down the Torah to Moses, thus did God the Almighty send down the Torah to Moses, peace be upon him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What was the first thing you permitted, the command of God? He said: If we captured a noble person, we would leave him alone, but if we captured a weak person, we would carry out the prescribed punishment on him. Fornication became widespread among our nobles, until the cousin of our king committed fornication, and we did not stone him. Then another man committed fornication, and the king wanted to stone him, but his people stood up to protect him. They said: By God, you will not stone him until so-and-so is stoned - the cousin of the king. So we said: Come, let us meet and establish something other than stoning that would be for the lowly and the noble. So we established flogging and blackening, which is to flog forty lashes with a rope coated with tar, then blacken their faces, then carry them on two donkeys with their faces facing the donkey’s backside and parade them around. So they made this the place of stoning. The Jews said [to Ibn Suriya]: How quickly you informed him of this, and you were not worthy of our praise of you, but you were absent, so we hated to backbite you. So he said to them: He recited to me the Torah, and if it were not for the fear that the Torah would destroy me, I would not have informed him. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to be stoned at the door of his mosque, and he said: O God, I am the first to revive your command when they killed it. Then God Almighty revealed, O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Umar, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned to him that a man and a woman among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: What do you find in the Torah regarding stoning? They said: We will disgrace them and flog them. `Abdullah ibn Salam said: “You have lied. It contains the verse of stoning.” So they brought the Torah and spread it out, and one of them placed his hand on the verse of stoning and read what came before it and what came after it. `Abdullah said to him: Raise your hand. So he raised his hand and saw in it the verse of stoning. They said: “He spoke the truth, O Muhammad. It contains the verse of stoning.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to be stoned. `Abdullah ibn `Umar said: I saw the man bending over the woman to protect her from the stones. It was said: The reason for the revelation of this verse was retaliation, and that is “that Banu Nadir had a superiority over Banu Qurayzah, so Banu Qurayzah said: O Muhammad, our brothers are Banu Nadir, and our father is one, our religion is one, and our prophet is one. If they kill one of us, they will not shackle us and will give us his blood money of seventy wasqs of dates. If we kill one of them, they will kill the killer and take double from us, one hundred and forty wasqs of dates. If the one killed is a woman, they will kill a man from us for her, and a man from them will kill two men from us, and a free slave from us, and our wounds will be doubled from their wounds, so judge between us and them. So God Almighty revealed this verse.” The first is more correct because the verse is about stoning. His saying: And among those who are Jews are those who listen to falsehood. It was said that the lam means to. It was said that it is the lam of ki, meaning: they listen in order to lie to you. The lam in his saying: for a people means: for a people others who did not come to you, and they are the people of Khaybar. They distort the words, [plural of the word], from after their places, meaning: after placing them in their places. He mentioned the metaphor in response to the wording of the words, “They say: If you are given this, then take it,” meaning: [If] Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, issues a fatwa to you regarding flogging and blackening, then accept it. “And if you are not given it, then beware. And he whose trial God intends,” meaning his disbelief and misguidance, Ad-Dahhak said: his destruction. Qatadah said: his punishment. You will not possess for him anything from God, meaning you will not be able to repel God’s command regarding him. Those are the ones whose hearts God did not intend to purify, and in it is a response to those who deny predestination. For them in this world is disgrace, meaning: for the hypocrites and the Jews, so disgrace The hypocrites will be disgraced and their cover will be torn off by revealing their hypocrisy, and the Jews will be disgraced by the jizya, killing, captivity, and exile, and they will see from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions what they dislike, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment, eternity in Hell.
5:42: 42- The Almighty said: They listen to falsehood and devour what is unlawful. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja`far, the people of Basra, and Al-Kisa’i read “li-... Al-Hasan said: If someone brought a bribe to a ruler, he would put it in his sleeve and show it to him and speak about his need, so he would listen to him and not look at his opponent, so he would hear the lie and eat the bribe. And also on his authority he said: That is only in the case of a judge if you bribe him to justify a falsehood for you or to nullify a right for you. As for a man giving to the ruler fearing his injustice in order to ward it off from himself, then there is no problem. So, the bribe in the judgement is the bribe according to the saying of Al-Hasan, Muqatil, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Mas`ud said: It is the bribe in everything. Ibn Mas`ud said: Whoever intercedes to restore a right or repel [an injustice], and it is given to him and he accepts, then it is bribe. So it was said to him: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, we did not see that except as taking it in order to judge. So he said: Taking it in order to judge is disbelief. God Almighty said: “And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.” Surat Al-Ma’idah, 44 Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shureih, on the authority of Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Jaad, on the authority of Ibn Abi Tha’lab, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God curses the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes a bribe. Illegal earnings are any earnings that are not permissible. God Almighty said: “If they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all.” God Almighty gave His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, the choice to judge between them. If he wanted to judge, he could, or if he wanted to leave them alone. They differed on the ruling of the verse today: Does the ruler have the option to rule between the People of the Book if they bring their case to us? Most scholars said: It is a fixed ruling, and there is nothing abrogated in Surat Al-Ma’idah. The rulers of the Muslims have the option to rule between the People of the Book. If they wish, they may rule, and if they wish, they may not. If they rule, they may rule according to the ruling of Islam. This is the opinion of Al-Nakha’i, Al-Sha’bi, Ata’, and Qatadah. Some people said: The ruler of the Muslims must judge between them, and the verse was abrogated by the words of God Almighty: And judge between them by what God has revealed Surat Al-Ma’idah, 49, which is the opinion of Mujahid and Ikrimah. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Only two verses of Al-Ma’idah were abrogated: the words of God Almighty: Do not violate the symbols of God were abrogated by the words of God Almighty: Kill the polytheists and the words: But if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them were abrogated by the words of God Almighty: And judge between them by what God has revealed As for if a Muslim and a non-Muslim come to us for judgment, it is obligatory for us to judge between them, and there is no difference of opinion about it, because it is not permissible for a Muslim to submit to the judgment of the non-Muslims. His words: And if you judge, judge between them with justice means: with fairness, Indeed, God loves those who are just meaning those who are just. We narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The just will be with God on pulpits of light.
5:43: 43- The Almighty said: "And how do they make you a judge between them while they have the Torah?" This is an astonishment to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in brief, that is: How do they make you a judge between them and they are satisfied with your judgment while they have the Torah? "In it is the judgment of God, which is stoning, and then they turn away after that, and those are not believers, that is, they will not believe you.
5:44: 44- The Almighty said: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it,” meaning: they submitted and obeyed [the command of] God Almighty, as He informed about Abraham, peace be upon him: When his Lord said to him, ‘Submit,’ he said, ‘I submit to the Lord of the worlds.’ Surat Al-Baqarah, 131, and as He said: And to Him submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth. Surat Al-Imran, 83, and He meant by them the prophets who were sent after Moses, peace be upon him, to judge by what was in the Torah, and they submitted to the ruling of the Torah and ruled by it, for among the prophets were those who were not commanded to rule by the Torah, including Jesus, peace be upon him. God Almighty said, To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Surat Al-Ma’idah, 48. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: He meant by it that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the Jews should be stoned. He mentioned it in the plural form, as he said: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God Surat An-Nahl, 120. And the Almighty’s saying: For those who are Jews, there is an inversion, meaning: In it is guidance and light for those who are Jews. Then He said: The prophets who submitted to Islam and the rabbis will judge by it. It was said: It is in its place, and its meaning is: The prophets who submitted to Islam will judge by it over those who are Jews, as He said: And if you do evil, then for it Surat Al-Isra’, meaning: upon it. And He said: For those is the curse Surat Ar-Ra’d, 25, meaning: upon them. It was said: There is an omission in it, as if He said: for those who are Jews and upon those who are Jews, so He omitted one of them for the sake of brevity. The rabbis and the scholars, meaning the scholars, the singular of which is habbar, with the haa open or closed, the kasra is more eloquent, and he is the scholar who has mastered something. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Ubaid said: It is in the hadith A man will emerge from the Fire whose habbar and sabrah have gone, meaning his beauty and appearance, and from it is the word tahbeer which means improvement, so the scholar was called habbar because of the beauty of knowledge and its splendor, and it was said: the rabbis here are from the Christians, and the rabbis are from the Jews, and it was said that both of them are from the Jews. The Almighty said: Because of what they were entrusted with of the Book of God meaning, what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, and they were witnesses thereto, that is, it is like that. “So do not fear the people, but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then those are the disbelievers.” Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: These three verses were revealed about the Jews, not those who committed evil from this nation. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may God be pleased with him, regarding His statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then those are the disbelievers. The wrongdoers and the wicked are all in reference to the disbelievers. It was said: It applies to all people. Ibn ‘Abbas and Tawus said: It is not disbelief that removes one from the religion, but if he does it [a disbeliever], he is not like someone who disbelieves in God and the Last Day. Ata’ said: It is less disbelief than disbelief, less oppression than oppression, and less immorality than immorality. Ikrimah Manah said: Whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, denying it, has committed an act of disbelief, and whoever acknowledges it but does not rule by it is an unjust and immoral person. Abdul Aziz bin Yahya Al-Kinani was asked about these verses, and he said: They apply to all that God has revealed, not just some of it. So whoever does not rule by all that God has revealed is a disbeliever, oppressor, and sinner. As for whoever rules by what God has revealed of monotheism and abandons polytheism, and then does not rule by all of what God has revealed of the laws, he does not deserve the ruling of these verses. The scholars said: This is if he intentionally rejects the text of God’s ruling clearly, but as for whoever is unaware of it or makes a mistake in interpretation, then no.
5:45: 45- The Almighty’s saying: And We ordained for them therein, meaning: We made it obligatory for the Children of Israel in the Torah, that a life for a life, meaning: the life of the killer for the life of the one killed, in fulfillment of his obligation, and an eye for an eye, gouged out with it, and a nose for a nose, cut off with it, and an ear for an ear, cut off with it. Ibn Abbas said: God Almighty informed of His ruling in the Torah, which is: a life for a life, and so on. So why are they afraid, so they kill for a precious life, and gouge out two eyes for an eye? Nafi’ lightened the ear in all the other Qur’ans, and a tooth for a tooth, plucked out with it, and all the limbs are analogous to it in retaliation, and wounds are retaliation, so this is a generalization after a specification, because He mentioned the eye, nose, ear, and tooth, then He said: and wounds are retaliation, meaning in what can be retaliated for, such as the hand, foot, tongue, and the like. As for what cannot be retaliated for, such as a broken bone or a wound, such as a wound or the like, then there is no It is a retaliation in it, because it is not possible to stop at its end, and Al-Kisa’i read and the eye and what comes after it in the nominative case, and Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Ja’far, and Abu Amr read and the wounds in the nominative case only, and the others read it all in the accusative case like the soul. The Almighty said: But whoever gives it in charity, meaning retaliation, it is an expiation for him. It was said: The ha in for him is a metaphor for the wounded person and the guardian of the murdered person, meaning: an expiation for the one who gives in charity. This is the saying of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, Al-Hasan, Al-Sha’bi, and Qatada. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Daynouri told us, Umar bin Al-Khattab told us, Abdullah bin Al-Fadl told us, Abu Khaithama told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever gives charity from his body, God will expiate for him a proportion of his sins. A group said: It is a metaphor for the one who injures and the killer, meaning: If the offender forgives the offender, then his forgiveness is an expiation for the offender’s sin, for which he will not be held accountable in the Hereafter, just as retaliation is an expiation for it. As for the reward of the one who forgives, it is upon God Almighty. God Almighty said: But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is upon God (al-Shura 42:40). This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and it is the saying of Ibrahim, Mujahid, and Zaid bin Aslam, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
5:46: 46- The Almighty said, And We followed in their footsteps, meaning: in the footsteps of the prophets who submitted, “with Jesus, the son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah. And We gave him the Gospel in it,” meaning: in the Gospel, guidance and light and confirming, meaning the Gospel, what was before him of the Torah and guidance and instruction for the righteous.
