5:47: 47- And let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein, Al-A'mash and Hamza read and let him judge with a kasra on the lam and a fatha on the meem, meaning: so that he may judge, and the others read with a sukoon on the lam and a jazm on the meem as a command, Muqatil bin Hayyan said: God commanded the rabbis and the scholars to judge by what is in the Torah, and He commanded the priests and monks to judge by what is in the Gospel, so they disbelieved and said that Ezra is the son of God and the Messiah is the son of God, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wicked, those who have gone outside the command of God Almighty:
5:48: 48- The Almighty’s saying: And We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Book, the Qur’an, in truth, confirming what was before it of the Book, that is, of the books sent down before, and as a guardian over it, Al-Walibi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: that is, as a witness over it, and this is the saying of Mujahid, Qatada, Al-Suddi, and Al-Kisa’i. Hassan said: The book is the authority for our Prophet, and the truth is known by those with understanding. He wants: a witness and a certifier. And Akrima said: with a dal. And Saeed bin Jubair and Abu Ubaidah said: A trustworthy one. And Al-Hasan said: Ameen. And it was said: its origin is Mu’aymin, Mafa’il from Ameen, just as they said: Mubaytar from Al-Baytar, so the hamza accepted a ha’, just as they said: I poured out the water and poured it out, and Ayhat and Hayhat and the like. And the meaning of the trustworthiness of the Qur’an is what Ibn Jurayj said: The Qur’an is trustworthy over what came before it of the books, so whatever the People of the Book reported about [their book], if it is in the Qur’an then they are truthful, otherwise they are liars. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Ad-Dahhak said: Judge, and Al-Khalil said: Watcher and Preserver, and the meanings are close, and the meaning of all is: that a book whose truthfulness is attested to by the Qur’an is the Book of God Almighty, and that which is not is not. So judge, O Muhammad, between them, between the People of the Book when they litigate before you, by what God has revealed, by the Qur’an, and do not follow their inclinations away from the truth that has come to you, meaning do not turn away from the truth that has come to you and do not follow their inclinations, For each of you We prescribed a law and a method, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Mujahid said: meaning a way and a tradition, so the law and the method are the clear path, and everything that is legislated is a law and a law, and from this are the laws of Islam because its people embarked on them, and by this he meant that the laws are different, and each people of a religion has a law. Qatada said: The address is to the three nations: the nation of Moses, the nation of Jesus, and the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and upon them all. The Torah has a law, the Gospel has a law, and the Criterion has a law, and the religion is one, which is monotheism. And if God had willed, He would have made you one nation, that is, one religion, but that He may test you, to examine you, in what He has given you, of the books and the laws He has made clear to you, so that He may distinguish the obedient from the disobedient, the one who agrees from the one who disagrees, so hasten to do good, so hasten to do righteous deeds, to God is your return, all of you, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
5:49: 49- The Almighty said, And judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what God has revealed to you, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said: Ka'b bin [Asad], Abdullah bin [Suriyya], and Shas bin Qais, from the leaders of the Jews, said to each other: Let us go to Muhammad so that we may give him a fatwa about his religion. So they went to him and said, O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis and nobles of the Jews, and if we follow you, the Jews will not oppose us. And there are disputes between us and the people, so we bring them to your judgment, so judge for us against them. We will believe in you, and others will follow us. Their intention was not to believe, but rather their intention was to deceive and invite him to lean in judgment, so God, the Almighty, revealed the verse. But if they turn away, meaning they turn away from faith and ruling by the Qur’an, then know that God only wants to afflict them for some of their sins, meaning: know that their turning away is because God wants to punish them in this world for some of their sins, and indeed many of the people, meaning the Jews, are wicked.
5:50: 50- Do they seek the judgment of the time of ignorance? Ibn Amir read you seek with a taa' and the others read it with a yaa', meaning: they seek, And who is better than God in judgment for a people who are certain?
5:51: 51- O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They differed about the revelation of this verse, even though its ruling is general for all believers. Some people said: It was revealed about Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Abdullah ibn Abi Salul, and that is because they had a dispute. Ubadah said: I have Jewish allies who are numerous and powerful, and I declare before God and His Messenger that I am innocent of their guardianship and the guardianship of the Jews, and I have no guardian except God and His Messenger. Abdullah said: But I do not declare myself innocent of the guardianship of the Jews, because I fear calamities, and I must have them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu al-Habbab, whatever you desire from the guardianship of the Jews over Ubadah ibn al-Samit is yours and not his. He said: When he comes, then God Almighty revealed this verse. Al-Suddi said: When the Battle of Uhud was severe for a group of people and they feared that the infidels would prevail over them, a Muslim man said: I will join so-and-so the Jew and take a guarantee of safety from him, for I fear that the Jews will prevail over us. Another man said: As for me, I will join so-and-so the Christian from the people of Ash-Sham and take a guarantee of safety from him. So God Almighty revealed this verse forbidding them both. Ikrimah said: It was revealed about [Abu Lubabah] bin Abdul Mundhir. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Banu Qurayzah [when he besieged them]. They consulted him about disembarking, and they said: What will be done to us when we disembark? So he put his finger to his throat, meaning: He will kill you. So this verse was revealed. Some of them are allies of others, in support and victory, and they are united against the Muslims. And whoever among you takes them as allies, [and agrees with them and supports them], “then indeed he is one of them. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.”
5:52: 52- The Almighty said: Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease, meaning: hypocrisy, meaning Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions from the hypocrites who are loyal to the Jews, rushing towards them, in helping them and befriending them, saying, 'We fear that a misfortune will strike us', a state, meaning: that time will turn a state and we will need their support for us, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Its meaning is that we fear that the matter of Muhammad will not be completed and the matter will turn against us, and it was said that we fear that time will turn against us with a calamity of drought and famine and they will not give us provisions and loans, Then perhaps God will bring about victory, Qatada and Muqatil said: By the decisive decree of victory for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, over those who opposed him, and Al-Kalbi and Al-Suddi said: The conquest of Mecca, and Ad-Dahhak said: The conquest of the villages of the Jews such as Khaybar and Fadak, or a command from Him, it was said: By the completion of the matter of Muhammad May God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: It is a punishment for them. It was said: The expulsion of Banu Nadir. So they will become, meaning these hypocrites, regretful of what they kept secret in their souls, of their allegiance to the Jews and their spreading of report to them.
5:53: 53- And then, those who believe will say [The people of Kufa read: and say, with the waw and the nominative] and the people of Basra read with the waw and the lam in the accusative case in apposition to that he may come meaning: and perhaps those who believe will say, and the others read by deleting the waw and raising the lam, and this is how it is in the copies of the people of [Al-Aliyah], dispensing with the conjunction letter due to the connection of this verse with what preceded it, meaning those who believe will say at the time when God Almighty reveals the hypocrisy of the hypocrites, Are these the ones who swore by God, they swore by God, their strongest oaths, meaning: they swore with the strongest oaths, that they are with you, meaning: they are believers, he means: that the believers at that time will be amazed at their lies and their false oaths. God Almighty said, Their deeds have become worthless, meaning that all the good they did has become void, and they have become losers, meaning that they have lost this world through their disgrace, and the Hereafter through punishment and loss of reward.
5:54: 54- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth [in place of him] a people He will love and who will love Him. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read reverts as indicating weakness from his religion so he returns to disbelief. Al-Hassan said: God Almighty knew that a people would turn away from Islam after the death of their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so He informed us that He would bring a people whom God loves and who love Him. They differed about who those people were. Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, Al-Hasan and Qatada said: They are Abu Bakr and his companions who fought the apostates and those who refused to pay zakat. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) died, most of the Arabs apostatized except the people of Mecca, Medina and Bahrain from Abd al-Qays, and some of them refused to pay zakat. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him was the reason behind fighting them. The companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) thought about that. Umar may God be pleased with him said: How can we fight people when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I have been commanded to fight people until they say ‘There is no god but God.’ Whoever says it has protected his wealth and his life from me, except for his right, and his reckoning is with God Almighty?” Abu Bakr said: “By God, I will fight whoever separates prayer from zakat, the right of wealth. By God, if they refused me [a young goat] that they used to pay to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), I would fight them for withholding it.” Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, said: The Companions hated fighting those who refused to pay zakat, and they said: The people of the Qiblah. So Abu Bakr put on his sword and went out alone, and they had no choice but to go out after him. Ibn Masoud said: We disliked that at the beginning, but we praised him for it at the end. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash said: I heard Abu Hasin say: No one was born after the prophets better than Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. He took the place of one of the prophets in fighting the apostates. During the life of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, three groups apostatized: Among them were [Banu Madhhij] and their chief was Dhu al-Khimar, Ubahla ibn Ka’b, al-Ansi, who was nicknamed al-Aswad. He was a soothsayer and magician who prophesied in Yemen and took control of its lands. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to Muadh ibn Jabal and those Muslims with him and ordered them to urge the people to adhere to their religion and to rise up to fight al-Aswad. Fayruz al-Daylami killed him in his bed. Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, said that the report came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the sky that night, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Al-Aswad was killed last night by a blessed man. It was said: Who is he? He said: Fayruz, [Fayruz won]. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave his companions the good report of al-Aswad’s death. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, died the next day. [The report] of al-Ansi’s killing reached Medina at the end of the month of Rabi’ al-Awwal after Usama had left, and that was the first conquest that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, had achieved. The second group: Banu Hanifa in Yamamah, and their leader is Musaylimah the Liar, [his name is Thamama bin Qais], who had prophesied during the lifetime of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the last year of the tenth year, and he claimed that he had associated partners with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in prophecy, and “wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Musaylimah the Messenger of God to Muhammad the Messenger of God, and after that, half of the land is yours, and he sent [that] to him with two men from his companions, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: [Do you bear witness that Musaylimah is the Messenger of God? They said: Yes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said] If it were not for the fact that messengers are not killed, I would have struck off your necks, then he replied: From Muhammad the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Musaylimah the Liar, and after that, the land belongs to God, and He gives it as an inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants, and the good end is for the righteous, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became ill and died, so Abu Bakr sent Khalid bin Al-Walid to Musaylimah the Liar with a large army until God destroyed him at the hands of Wahshi, the servant of Mut’am bin Adi, who killed Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, after a fierce war, and Wahshi used to say: I killed the best people in the pre-Islamic era and the worst people in Islam. The third group: Banu Asad, and their leader is Tulaiha bin Khuwaylid bin Al-Walid. Tulaiha was the last to apostatize and claim prophethood during the life of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the first of the apostates to be fought after the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr sent Khalid bin Al-Walid to him, and Khalid defeated them after a fierce battle. Tulaiha escaped and fled towards the Levant, then he converted to Islam after that and his conversion was good. After the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, [during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him], many people apostatized, until God spared the Muslims the trouble of supporting His religion at the hands of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. Aisha said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, the Arabs turned back, hypocrisy spread, and something happened to Abu Bakr that would have shaken the steadfast mountains if it had happened to them. Some people said: What is meant by his saying: “Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him” are the Ash’aris. It was narrated on the authority of Ayyadh ibn Ghanim al-Ash’ari who said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him’, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are this people, and he pointed to Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, and they were from Yemen.” Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin [Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin] Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Muhammad bin Amr bin Alqamah told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people of Yemen have come to you, and they are the weakest of hearts and the most tender of souls. Faith is Yemeni and wisdom is Yemeni.” Al-Kalbi said: They are living people from Yemen, two thousand from the Nakha’ tribe, five thousand from Kinda and Bajila, and three thousand from the spoils of war. They fought in the way of God on the day of Al-Qadisiyah during the days of Omar, may God be pleased with him. The Almighty’s statement, Humble toward the believers, means: merciful slaves, like His statement, And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and He did not mean humiliation, but rather He meant that their side was gentle toward the believers. It was said that it is from humiliation, from their saying, a docile animal, that they are humble, as God the Almighty said, And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily, “Mighty against the disbelievers,” meaning: severe and harsh toward the disbelievers, they are hostile to them and overcome them, from their saying, mighty means he overcame them. Ata’ said, Humble toward the believers is like a child toward his father and like a slave toward his master, Mighty against the disbelievers is like a wild animal toward its prey, similar to His statement, the Almighty, Harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. “They strive in the cause of God and do not fear the blame of any blamer,” meaning: they do not fear the blame of people for God’s sake. This is because the hypocrites were watching the infidels and fearing their blame. We narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hear and obey and to stand up or speak the truth wherever we are, not fearing the blame of any blamer for God’s sake. That is the grace of God which He bestows upon whom He wills, meaning their love for God, their gentleness towards the Muslims, and their severity towards the disbelievers, are from God’s grace upon them, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
5:55: 55- Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe, [It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, that it was revealed about Ubadah bin As-Samit and Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul when Ubadah disavowed the Jews and said: I take God and His Messenger and those who believe as allies, so it was revealed about them from His saying: O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, to His saying: Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe], meaning Ubadah bin As-Samit, the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Jabir bin Abdullah said: Abdullah bin Salam came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, our people, Qurayzah and An-Nadir, have deserted us and separated from us and have sworn not to sit with us, so this verse was revealed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it to him, and he said: O Messenger of God, we are pleased with God and His Messenger and the believers as allies. According to this interpretation, what he meant by his saying: and they are bowing is the voluntary prayer at night and during the day, as Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said. Al-Suddi said: His statement: And those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakat, while they bow in prayer, he meant Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. A beggar passed by him while he was bowing in the mosque, so he gave him his ring. Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement: Your guardian is only God and His Messenger and those who believe, he said: They are the believers, some of them are guardians of others. Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali Al-Baqir said: Your guardian is only God and His Messenger and those who believe, it was revealed about the believers, so it was said to him that some people say that it was revealed about `Ali, may God be pleased with him, so he said: He is one of the believers.
5:56: 56- "And whoever takes God and His Messenger and those who believe as allies", meaning: takes on the responsibility of obeying God and supporting His Messenger and the believer, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: He means the immigrants and the helpers, "then the party of God", meaning: the helpers of the religion of God, "they are the victorious.
5:57: 57- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not take as your friends those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement. Ibn Abbas said: Rafa'ah bin Zaid bin al-Tabut and Suwaid bin al-Harith had outwardly declared Islam, then they became hypocrites, and they were men from among the Muslims who were friendly to them. Then God the Almighty revealed this verse: O you who have believed, do not take as your friends those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement, by showing that with their tongues in words while they were inwardly disbelievers, of those who were given the Scripture before you, meaning: the Jews, and the disbelievers, the people of Basra and al-Kisa'i read the disbelievers with the dammah on the ra', (meaning: and of the disbelievers), and the others read it with the accusative, meaning: do not take the disbelievers as your allies and fear God if you are believers.
5:58: 58- The Almighty said: “And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not reason.” Al-Kalbi said: When the caller of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for it, the Jews would say: They have stood up, they have stood up, and prayed, in a mocking way, and they laughed, so God Almighty revealed this verse. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about a Christian man in Medina who, when he heard the muezzin say: I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, would say: Burn the liar. One night his servant entered with a fire [while he and his family were asleep] and a spark flew from it, and the house burned down, and he and his family burned down. Others said: When the infidels heard the call to prayer, they envied the Muslims, so they entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, you have innovated something that we have not heard of among the nations before you. If you claim prophethood, then you have contradicted the prophets before you in what you have innovated. If there was any good in it, the prophets would have been the most deserving of it. So where did you get a cry like that of a goat? What a hideous sound and what a loathsome matter! So God Almighty revealed this verse, and revealed: And who is better in speech than one who invites to God?
5:59: 59- The Almighty said: Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, do you blame us?’ The verse. Al-Kisa’i read: Do you blame? by assimilating the lam into the ta’, and he also assimilates the lam of hal into the ta’, tha’, and nun. Hamza agreed with him on the ta’ and tha’, and Abu Amr agreed with him on hal tara in two places. Ibn Abbas said: “A group of Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab, Rafi’ ibn Abi Rafi’ and others, and they asked him about the messengers who believed in him. He said: ‘I believe in God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael’ until His saying: ‘And we are Muslims to Him.’ But when he mentioned Jesus, peace be upon him, they denied his prophethood and said: ‘By God, we do not know of people of a religion who have less share in this world and the next than you, nor a religion worse than your religion.’ So God Almighty revealed this verse: ‘Say, O People of the Scripture, do you blame us for anything but our belief in God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are wicked?’ That is, do you hate anything from us except our belief and your wickedness? You only hated our belief even though you knew that we were right, because you were wicked by remaining in your religion out of love of leadership and love of money.”
5:60: 60- Then he said: Say, O Muhammad, Shall I inform you, I tell you, of something worse than that, which you mentioned, meaning their saying, We have not seen people of a religion less fortunate in this world and the hereafter than you, nor a religion worse than your religion, so he mentioned the answer with the wording of the beginning, even if the beginning was not evil, like the Almighty’s saying: Shall I inform you of something worse than that, the Fire? Al-Hajj, 72, reward is a reward and recompense, accusative for interpretation, with God he whom God has cursed, meaning: he whom God has cursed, and with whom He has become angry, meaning: the Jews, and made of them apes and pigs, so the apes are the people of the Sabbath, and the pigs are the disbelievers of the table of Jesus, peace be upon him. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: That the two transformed ones were both from the people of the Sabbath, so their young men were transformed into monkeys and their old men were transformed into pigs. And worshipped the Taghut, meaning: He made some of them worship the Taghut, meaning: He obeyed Satan in what he suggested to them. And the confirmation of this is the reading of Ibn Masoud: And those who worshipped the Taghut, and Hamza read and worshipped with a damma on the ba’, the Taghut with a genitive on the ta’, meaning the servant, and they are two languages: Abd with the jazm of the ba’ and Abd with the damma of the ba’, like seven and seven, and it was said that it is the plural of servants, and Al-Hasan read and worshipped the Taghut, in the singular form, Those are in worse position and further astray from the right path, meaning: from the path of truth.
5:61: 61- And when they come to you, they say, meaning: these hypocrites, and it was said: they are the ones who said: Believe in what was revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end, they entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We believe in you and we believe you in what you said, while they were concealing disbelief, and they entered with disbelief and they left with it, meaning: they entered as disbelievers and left as disbelievers, and God knows best what they were concealing.
5:62: 62- And you will see many of them, meaning: of the Jews hastening into sin and aggression, it was said: sin is disobedience and aggression is injustice, and it was said: sin is what they concealed from the Torah, and aggression is what they added to it, and their consuming of what is unlawful, bribes, how evil is what they used to do.
5:63: 63- If only, why not, the rabbis and scholars forbade them, meaning: the scholars. It was said: the rabbis are the scholars of the Christians and the scholars are the scholars of the Jews, "from their sinful speech and their consumption of ill-gotten gains. Evil is what they have been doing."
5:64: 64- The Almighty said, And the Jews said, ‘The hand of God is chained.’ Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, and Qatada said: God Almighty had given the Jews so much wealth that they were the wealthiest and most fertile of people. But when they disobeyed God in the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denied him, God withheld from them the abundance that He had given them. At that time, Phinehas bin Azura said: The hand of God is chained, meaning: it is confined and restrained from sustenance. They attributed it to miserliness. God is exalted above that. It was said: Phinehas said this statement, and when the others did not stop and were satisfied with his words, God made them a partner in it. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is that God’s hand is restrained from punishing us, and He will not punish us except for what He has decreed, as much as our fathers worshipped the calf. The first is more appropriate, because of His saying: He spends as He wills. Their hands are chained, meaning: their hands are held back from doing good deeds. Al-Zajjaj said: God Almighty answered them and said: I am the generous one and they are the misers, and their hands are the ones that are chained and withholding. It was said: It is from the chaining in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, as God Almighty said: When the shackles are on their necks and the chains (Ghafir 40:71). And they are cursed, means they are tormented, for what they said, so those who cursed them are those who were transformed into apes and pigs and humiliation and poverty were imposed upon them in the Hereafter by the Fire, Rather, His hands are spread out, and the hand of God is an attribute of [His] attributes like hearing, sight and face. God Almighty said: When I created with My hands (Sad: 75), and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Both of His hands are right, and God knows best about His attributes, so the servants must believe and submit in them. The Imams of the Salaf from the people of Sunnah said about these attributes: They should be given as they came without asking how. He spends, He provides, “how He wills. And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief,” meaning: whenever a verse is revealed, they disbelieve in it and increase in transgression and disbelief, [whenever a verse is revealed] and We cast between them enmity and hatred, meaning: between the Jews and the Christians, as Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: And it was said that between the sects of the Jews, God made them differ in their religion and hate each other “until the Day of Resurrection. Whenever they kindled a fire for war, God extinguished it,” meaning: the Jews corrupted and disobeyed the ruling of the Torah, so God sent Nebuchadnezzar against them, then they corrupted, so God sent Titus the Roman, then they corrupted, so God empowered the Magians against them, then they corrupted, so God sent the Muslims against them. It was said: Whenever they gathered their affair to corrupt the affair of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ignited the fire of war, God extinguished it, and repelled them and defeated them and gave victory to His Prophet and His religion. This is the meaning of what Al-Hasan said. Qatada said: This is general in every war that the Jews sought, so you will not find the Jews in a country except that you will find them among the most humiliated of people, And they strive to cause corruption in the land, and God does not love corrupters.
5:65: 65- And if the People of the Scripture had believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and feared disbelief, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to gardens of pleasure.
5:66: 66- And if they had established the Torah and the Gospel, meaning: they had established their rulings and limits and acted upon what was in them, and what was revealed to them from their Lord, meaning: the Qur’an, and it was said: the books of the prophets of the Children of Israel, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet, it was said: above them is the rain, and beneath their feet is the vegetation of the earth. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: I would have sent down rain upon them and brought forth for them plants from the earth. Al-Farra’ said: He meant by it the expansion of livelihood, as it is said that someone is in goodness from head to toe. Similar to this is the saying of God Almighty: And if only the people of the cities had believed and feared God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth Al-A’raf, 96. Among them is a moderate nation, meaning: the believers of the People of the Book, Abdullah bin Salam and his companions. Moderate means just, not extravagant, nor short and harsh. The meaning of moderation in the language is: moderation in work, neither exaggeration nor shortcoming. And many of them, Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, evil is what they do, evil is what they do. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: They did ugly things while denying the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
5:67: 67- The Almighty said: O Messenger, announce what has been revealed to you from your Lord the verse, it was narrated on the authority of Masruq who said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: Whoever tells you that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealed something of what God revealed to him has lied, and he says: O Messenger, announce what has been revealed to you from your Lord the verse. Al-Hasan narrated: When God Almighty sent His Messenger, he was fed up and knew that some people would deny him, so this verse was revealed. It was said: It was revealed regarding the fault of the Jews, and that is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to Islam, and they said, We converted before you, and they began to mock him, saying to him: Do you want us to treat you with kindness as the Christians treated Jesus, son of Mary, with kindness? When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw that, he remained silent, and this verse was revealed, and he ordered him to say to them: O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything, the verse. It was said: Convey what was revealed to you about stoning and retaliation, it was revealed in the story of the Jews. It was said: It was revealed regarding the matter of Zainab bint Jahsh and her marriage. It was said: In jihad, because the hypocrites hated it, as God Almighty said: But when a decisive surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with the look of one fainting from death (Muhammad 47:20). And some of the believers hated it, as God Almighty said: Have you not seen those to whom it was said, ‘Restrain your hands?’ (An-Nisa’: 70). So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sometimes refrained from urging jihad because he knew that some of them hated it, so God revealed this verse. God Almighty says: And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. The people of Medina read His messages in the plural, while the rest read His message in the monotheistic. The meaning of the verse is: If you do not convey to everyone and leave out some of it, then you have not conveyed anything, meaning: Your sin in leaving out conveying some of it is like your sin in leaving out conveying all of it, like His statement: “And they say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ and they wish to adopt a way in between. Those are the disbelievers, truly.” An-Nisa’, 150-151 He informed us that their disbelief in some of it nullifies belief in some of it. It was said: Convey what was revealed to you meaning: Proclaim its conveyance, like His saying: So proclaim what you are commanded Al-Hijr, 94. And if you do not do so: if you do not proclaim its conveyance, then you have not conveyed His message. He commanded him to convey what was revealed to him openly, expecting reward, patiently, and not afraid. If you concealed something from Him out of fear that would overtake you, then you have not conveyed His message. And God will protect you from the people, He will preserve you and protect you from the people. If it is said: Wasn’t his head wounded, his front teeth broken, and he harmed in various ways? It was said: Its meaning is that it protects you from being killed, so they will not be able to kill you. It was said: This verse was revealed after his head was cut off, because Surat Al-Ma’idah was one of the last parts of the Qur’an to be revealed. It was said: God singles you out for infallibility among people, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is infallible. God does not guide the disbelieving people. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Sinan bin Abi Sinan Al-Dawli and Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, that Jabir bin Abdullah told him, “He went on a military expedition with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before Najd. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, he returned with him and they were overtaken by noon in a valley with many jujube trees. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dismounted and the people dispersed to seek shade under the trees. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dismounted under a tree and hung his sword on it. We slept, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called us and there was a Bedouin with him. He said, ‘This man drew my sword while I was asleep. I woke up and it was in his hand, drawn.’ He said, ‘Who can protect you from me?’ I said, ‘God’ three times. He did not punish him and sat down.” Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, “The Bedouin drew his sword and said: Who can protect you from me, O Muhammad? He said: God. The Bedouin’s hand trembled and the sword fell from his hand. He began to hit the tree with his head until his brain was scattered. Then God Almighty revealed this verse.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ismail bin Khalil told us, Ali bin Masaher told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Abdullah bin Aamer bin Rabia said: I heard Aisha, may God be pleased with her, say: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed up all night, and when he arrived in Medina he said: ‘If only a righteous man from among my companions would guard me tonight. ’ Then we heard the sound of weapons, and he said: ‘Who is this? ’ He said: ‘I am Saad bin Abi Waqqas, I have come to guard you. ’ Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to sleep.” Abdullah bin Shaqiq said on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was guarding until this verse was revealed: ‘And God will protect you from the people.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stuck his head out of the dome and said to them: ‘O people, go away, for God Almighty has protected me.’”
5:68: 68- The Almighty said: Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord,’ meaning: uphold their rulings and what is required of you in them, “and what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not despair, do not grieve, “over the disbelieving people.”
5:69: 69- Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians and the Christians, and its correct form was and the Sabians, and we have mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah the reason for its elevation. Sibawayh said: There is an advancement and delay in it, its meaning is: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Christians are those who believed in God until the end of the verse, and the Sabians are likewise, and His saying: Indeed, those who believed means: with the tongue, and His saying: Whoever believed in God means: with the heart, and it was said: Those who believed in the true faith Whoever believed in God, meaning: remained steadfast in faith, and the Last Day and did righteousness - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
5:70: 70- The Almighty said: We took a covenant from the Children of Israel in monotheism and prophethood, “and We sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group denied him,” Jesus and Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them, and a group killed, John and Zechariah.
5:71: 71- And they thought, they assumed that there would be no trial, meaning: torment and killing, and it was said: a trial and a test, meaning: they thought that they would not be afflicted and that God would not torment them. The people of Basra, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read be with the noon raised to mean that it would not be, and the others put it in the accusative as if there was no before it no, so they were blind, from the truth so they did not see it, and deaf, from it so they did not hear it, meaning they were blind and deaf after Moses, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, then God turned to them, by sending Jesus, peace be upon him, then many of them were blind and deaf, by disbelieving in Muhammad, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, and God is Seeing of what they do.
5:72: 72- The Almighty said: They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the Messiah, the son of Mary,’ and they are the Melkites and Jacobites among them. “And the Messiah said, ‘O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates others with God - God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.’”
5:73: 73- They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'God is the third of three,' meaning: the Marcosians, and it contains an implied meaning: the third of three gods, because they say that divinity is shared between God, the Most High, Mary, and Jesus, and each one of these is a god, so they are three gods. This is shown by the words of God the Almighty to the Messiah: Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as gods besides God?' Al-Ma'idah 116. Whoever says that God is the third of three, without meaning divinity, does not disbelieve, because God says: There is no secret conversation between three but that He is the fourth of them Al-Mujadilah, 7. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him: What do you think of two, of whom God is the third? Then he said in response to them: "And there is no god except the One God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, they will surely afflict", [will surely afflict], those who disbelieve among them a painful punishment. He specifically mentioned those who disbelieved because He knew that some of them would believe.
5:74: 74- Will they not repent to God and seek His forgiveness? Al-Farra' said: This is a command in the form of a question, like the Almighty's saying: Will you then desist? Al-Ma'idah, 91, meaning: desist, and the meaning is: God [orders you] to repent and seek forgiveness for this great sin, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.
5:75: 75- The Almighty said: The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; messengers have passed away before him, [have passed away], before him were messengers, meaning: he is not a god, but rather he is like the messengers who have passed away, they were not a tool, and his mother was truthful, meaning: very truthful. It was said: She was called a friend because she believed in the signs of God, as God Almighty said in describing her: And she believed in the words of her Lord At-Tahrim, 12, They ate food, meaning they lived on food and nourishment like all other humans, so how can someone who is not established except by eating food be a god? It was said: This is a metaphor for the event, because whoever eats and drinks must urinate and defecate, and how can someone with this description be a god? Then he said: See how We make clear to them the signs, then see how they are turned away, meaning how they are turned away from the truth.
5:76: 76- "Say: Do you worship besides God that which has no power to harm or benefit you? And God is the Hearing, the Knowing."
5:77: 77- "Say, O People of the Scripture, do not go to extremes in your religion beyond the truth," meaning: do not exceed the limit, and extremism and shortcoming are both reprehensible in religion, and His saying: "other than the truth," meaning: in your religion that contradicts the truth, and that is because they contradicted the truth in their religion, then they went to extremes in it by insisting on it, "and do not follow the inclinations of a people, and inclinations are the plural of inclination, which is what the desire of the soul calls for, who have gone astray before," meaning: the leaders of misguidance in the two groups of the Jews and Christians, and the address is to those who were in the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who were forbidden from following their predecessors in what they innovated according to their inclinations, "and have led many astray," meaning: those who followed them according to their inclinations, "and have gone astray from the straight path," from the intended path, meaning: by misguidance, so the first misguidance is from misguidance, and the second is by misguiding those who followed them.
5:78: 78- The Almighty said: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David, meaning: the people of Ayla when they transgressed on the Sabbath, and David, peace be upon him, said: O God, curse them and make them a sign, so they were transformed into apes, and Jesus, the son of Mary, meaning: by the tongue of Jesus, peace be upon him, meaning: the disbelievers of the people of the table, when they did not believe, Jesus said: O God, curse them and make them a sign, so they were transformed into pigs, that is because they disobeyed and were transgressing.
5:79: 79- They did not forbid one another from the evil they were doing, (i.e. they did not forbid one another) How evil was what they were doing. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili told us, Wahb bin Baqiyah told us, Khalid - meaning Ibn Abdullah Al-Wusti - on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab on the authority of Amr bin Murrah on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among those who came before you from the Children of Israel, if a worker among them committed a sin, the one who forbade him would forbid him as an excuse. But the next day, he would sit with him, eat with him, and drink with him as if he had not seen him committing a sin the day before. When God, the Blessed and Exalted, saw that from them, He struck the hearts of some of them against others, and made of them apes and pigs, and cursed them on the tongues of David and Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon them, because they disobeyed and transgressed. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you must take the hand of the foolish and force him to follow the truth, or God will strike the hearts of some of you against others and curse you as He cursed them.”
5:80: 80- The Almighty’s saying, You will see many of them, it was said: from the Jews, Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, taking as allies those who disbelieve, the polytheists of Mecca when they went out to them to attack the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Hasan said: from them, meaning from the hypocrites, taking as allies the Jews, How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them, how evil is that which they have put forward of deeds for their return in the Hereafter, that God is angry with them, God is angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.
5:81: 81- The Almighty said, If they had believed in God and the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what was revealed to him meaning the Qur’an, they would not have taken them meaning the infidels, as allies, but many of them are wicked meaning they are outside the command of God Almighty.
5:82: 82- The Almighty’s saying: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God, meaning: the polytheists of the Arabs, And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, ‘We are Christians,’ does not mean all Christians because in their hostility toward the Muslims they are like the Jews in killing and taking Muslims captive, destroying their lands, demolishing their mosques, and burning their copies of the Qur’an, with no loyalty or respect for them. Rather, the verse is about those among them who converted to Islam, such as the Negus and his companions. (It was said: It was revealed about all Jews and all Christians, because the Jews are harder-hearted and the Christians are softer-hearted than them, and they were less supportive of the polytheists than the Jews.) The commentators said: The Quraysh plotted to tempt the believers away from their religion, so each tribe attacked the Muslims in it, harming and torturing them. Whoever was tempted was tempted, and God protected whomever He wished from them. God, the Most High, protected His Messenger through his uncle Abu Talib. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw what was happening to his companions and was unable to prevent them, and he had not yet been ordered to wage jihad, he ordered them to go out to the land of Abyssinia. He said: There is a righteous king there who does not oppress or oppress anyone, so go out to him until God makes a way out for the Muslims. He meant the Negus, and hear Ashamah, who is in Abyssinia, as a gift. The Negus is the name of the king, like their saying Caesar and Kisra. So eleven men and four women went out to it secretly, and they were Uthman ibn Affan and his wife Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Az-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam, Abdullah, Abdullah ibn Masoud, and Abd Al-Rahman ibn Awf, Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah and his wife Suhayl ibn Suhayl. Amr, Mus`ab ibn `Umair, Abu Salamah ibn `Abd al-Asad and his wife Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah, `Uthman ibn Maz`un, `Amir ibn Rabi`ah and his wife Layla bint Abi Hathmah, Hatib ibn `Amr and Sahl ibn Bayda`, may God be pleased with them, went out to sea and took a ship to the land of Abyssinia for half a dinar. This was in Rajab in the fifth year of the mission of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was the first migration. Then Ja`far ibn Abi Talib went out, and the Muslims followed one another to it. All of the Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia were eighty-two men, in addition to the women and children. When the Quraysh learned of this, they sent Amr ibn al-Aas and his companion with gifts to the Negus and his patriarchs to return them to them, but God protected them. The story is mentioned in Surat Al Imran. When they returned disappointed, the Muslims stayed there in the best home and the best neighborhood until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated and his affair rose, and that was in the year six of the Hijra. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to the Negus through Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri to marry him to Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan - who had migrated to him with her husband and then her husband died - and to send to him those Muslims who were with him. The Negus sent to Umm Habibah a slave girl called Abraha to inform her of the Messenger of God’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, engagement to her. She gave her gifts out of joy for that, and she gave permission to Khalid ibn Sa`id ibn al-`As to marry her for a dowry of four hundred dinars. The suitor for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Negus, may God have mercy on him. The Negus sent her four hundred dinars through Abraha. When she brought them to her, she gave her fifty dinars, but she returned them and said: The king ordered me not to take anything from you. She said: I am the owner of the king’s oil and clothes, and I have believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I have believed in him. My need from you is for you to greet him from me. She said: Yes. The king ordered his women to send you whatever they had of aloes and ambergris, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would see it on her and with her and not object. Umm Habibah said: So we went out to Medina, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Khaybar. So those who went out to him went out, and I stayed in Medina until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived. So I entered upon him, and he was asking me about the Negus, so I read to him the greetings of Abraha, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned the greetings to them both. And God Almighty revealed: Perhaps God will establish between you and those of them with whom you have been at enmity, affection. Meaning: Abu Sufyan, affection, meaning: by marrying Umm Habibah. And when Abu Sufyan came to marry Umm Habibah, he said: That stallion will not have his nose knocked. After Jaafar’s arrival, the Negus sent his son Azha bin Ashama bin Abjar to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with sixty men from Abyssinia. He wrote to him: O Messenger of God, I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God, truthful and trustworthy, and I have pledged allegiance to you and your cousin, and I have submitted to God, Lord of the Worlds. I have sent to you my son Azha. If you wish, I will come to you myself. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. So they boarded a ship following Jaafar and his companions until they were in the middle of the sea, and they drowned. Jaafar and his companions met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with seventy men wearing woolen garments, sixty-two of them from Abyssinia and eight from the people of Ash-Sham. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to them Surat Yasin to the end. They cried when they heard the Qur’an and believed. He said: Believe. They said: How similar this is to what was revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him. Then God, the Most High, the Most Great, revealed this verse: And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, ‘We are Christians.’ "It means: the delegation of the Negus who came with Jaafar, and they were the seventy, and they were the owners of the monasteries. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said that they were forty men, thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight Romans from the people of Ash-Sham. (Ata’ said: They were eighty men, forty from Najran from Banu Al-Harith bin Ka’b, thirty-two from Abyssinia, and eight Romans from the people of Ash-Sham.) Qatada said: It was revealed about some people of the Book who were following a true religion that Jesus, peace be upon him, brought. When God sent Muhammad, peace be upon him, they believed in him and believed in him, so God Almighty praised them for that. That is because among them are priests, meaning scholars. Qatrib said: A priest and a priest are scholars in the language of the Romans. And monks, meaning monks who are worshippers and monasteries. The singular of them is a monk, like a knight and knights, and a rider and riders. It may be singular and its plural is monks, like farban and qarabin. And that they are not arrogant, they do not think it too great to believe and submit to the truth.
5:83: 83- "And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger," Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, "you see their eyes overflowing, flowing, with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth," Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said in the narration of Ata': He means the Negus and his companions, Ja'far recited to them in Abyssinia, Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad, and they continued to cry until Ja'far finished reciting. "They say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses,'" meaning the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the evidence for this is the Almighty's saying, "That you may be witnesses over the people" Al-Baqarah 143. And why should we not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth? That is because the Jews taunted them and said to them: Why do you believe? They answered them with this, And we hope that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people, that is: with the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, explaining that My righteous servants will inherit the earth Al-Anbiya’ 105.
5:84: 85- "So God rewarded them, God gave them, for what they said, gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally," and their words were successful and the reward was linked to the words because they were coupled with sincerity, as evidenced by His statement: "And that is the reward of the doers of good," meaning: the monotheistic believers, and His statement before: "You will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth, indicates that the mute and knowledge in the heart with the words are faith.
5:85: 86- And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire.
5:86: 87 - The Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful for you, the verse. The commentators said: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the people one day and described the Resurrection, and the people were moved by him and wept. Ten of his companions gathered in the house of Uthman ibn Maz'un al-Jumahi, and they were Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and Abdullah ibn Umar, and Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and Salman al-Farsi, and Muqal ibn Muqrin, may God be pleased with them. They consulted and agreed to become monks, wear hair-sackcloth, shave their penises, fast all the time, stand in prayer at night, and not sleep on mattresses, and not eat meat or fat, and not approach women or perfume, and to travel the earth. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he went to the house of Uthman ibn Maz'un but did not find him, so he said to his wife Umm Hakim bint Abi Umayyah And her name was Al-Khawla’, and she was a perfumer: Is what I have heard about your husband and his companions true? She hated to lie to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and hated to reveal it to her husband, so she said: O Messenger of God, if Uthman has told you something, then he has told you the truth. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left, and when Uthman entered, she told him about it. So he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he and his companions, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Did I not hear that you agreed on such and such? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, and we only wanted good. So he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I was not commanded to do that. Then he said: Your souls have rights over you, so fast and break your fast, stand and sleep, for I stand and sleep, fast and break my fast, eat meat and fat, and come to women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me. Then he gathered the people and addressed them, saying: What is the matter with people who forbid women, food, perfume, sleep, and the desires of women? I do not command you to be priests and monks, for it is not in my religion to abandon meat and women, nor to take monasteries. The tourism of my nation is fasting, and their monasticism is jihad. Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, and perform Hajj and Umrah, and establish prayer, and give zakat, and fast Ramadan, and be upright and you will be upright. Those who came before you were destroyed only by severity. They were severe upon themselves, so God was severe upon them. Those are their remnants in the homes and monasteries.” Then God Almighty revealed this verse. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah Al-Kashmihani told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Harith told us, Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yaqub Al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah Al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Rashdin ibn Sa’d, Ibn An’am told me, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Mas’ud, that Uthman ibn Maz’un, may God be pleased with him, came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Give us permission to castrate ourselves. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “He is not one of us who is castrated or has his private parts castrated. The castration of my nation is fasting.” He said: O Messenger of God, give us permission to travel. He said: The travel of my nation is jihad in the way of God. He said: O Messenger of God, give us permission to become monastic. He said: The monasticism of my nation is sitting in the mosques and waiting for the prayer. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that a man said: O Messenger of God, I ate some meat and it made me sick and I felt a desire, so I forbade myself from meat. Then God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you, meaning: the pleasures that the souls desire, from what God has made lawful for you of good foods and delicious drinks, and do not transgress, meaning: do not go beyond what is lawful to what is unlawful. It was said: it is the genitals, Indeed, God does not like transgressors.
5:89: 88- And eat of what God has provided for you [that is] lawful and good. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak said: “The lawful is what you take directly, and the good is what nourishes and grows. As for solids such as clay and dirt and what does not nourish, then it is disliked except for the purpose of medical treatment.” And fear God, in whom you are believers. Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juwzjani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, Abu Saeed Al-Haytham bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa told us, Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Darooqi, Salamah bin Shabib, and Mahmoud bin Ghailan told us. They said: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved sweets and honey.” 90- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, and idols are but meaning: gambling, and altars meaning: the idols, they were called that because they used to set them up, the singular of which is nab with a fatha on the noon and a sukoon on the sad, and nab with a damma on the noon, light and heavy, and arrows meaning: the lots with which they used to draw lots, the singular of which is zalam, filth, filthy and disgusting, from the work of Satan, from his adornment, so avoid it, referring the metaphor back to filth, that you may be successful.
5:88: 89- The Almighty said: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: When the verse: Do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful for you was revealed, they said: O Messenger of God, what should we do with the oaths that we have sworn? They had sworn to what they had agreed upon, so God revealed: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths “but He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths.” Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and Abu Bakr read aqdtum with a light aqadtum, and Ibn ‘Amir read aqdtum with an alif, and the others read aqdtum with a shaddah, meaning: you intended, and what is meant by the verse is that you intended and deliberated. Then its expiation, meaning: the expiation for what you have deliberated in your oaths if you break them, is feeding ten poor people. They differed about its amount. Some people went to the view that he should feed each poor person a mudd of food according to the mudd of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is a pound and a third of the country’s staple food, and likewise in all expiations. This is the view of Zayd ibn Thabit and Ibn ‘Umar, and this is what Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Al-Qasim, Sulayman ibn Yasar, ‘Ata’, and Al-Hasan said. The people of Iraq said: He owes one mudd for every poor person, which is half a sa’. This is narrated on the authority of Omar and Ali, may God be pleased with them. Abu Hanifa said: If he fed from wheat, then half a sa`, and if he fed from something else, then a sa`. This is the opinion of Al-Sha`bi, Al-Nakha`i, Sa`id bin Jubayr, Mujahid, and Al-Hakam. Even if he gave them lunch and dinner, it is not permissible. Abu Khanifa permitted it, and this is narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him. Dirhams, dinars, bread, or flour are not permissible. Rather, grain must be given to them. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, permitted all of that. If all of it is given to one poor person it is not permissible, Abu Hanifa permitted giving the food of ten to one poor person in ten days, and it is not permissible to give it except to a free Muslim in need, as it is not permissible to give it to a dhimmi, a slave, or a rich person. Abu Hanifa permitted giving it to the People of the Covenant. They agreed that giving zakat to the People of the Covenant is not permissible. And the Almighty said: From the best of what you feed your families, meaning from the best of your family’s food. Ubaidah Al-Salmani said: The best is bread and vinegar, the best is bread and meat, and the best is pure bread, and all are sufficient. The Almighty says: Or their clothing. Whoever is required to pay expiation for an oath has a choice: if he wants, he can feed ten poor people, or if he wants, he can clothe them, or if he wants, he can free a slave. If he chooses clothing, then they differed regarding its amount: Some people said that each poor person should be clothed with one garment that is called clothing, such as a loincloth, a cloak, a shirt, trousers, a turban, a cloak, or something similar. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata’, and Tawus, and Al-Shafi’i, may God Almighty have mercy on him, also agreed with it. Malik said: Every person must wear what is permissible for his prayer, so he should wear one garment, and women should wear two garments, a shirt and a veil. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: For every poor person, two garments. God the Almighty said: or the freeing of a slave. If he chooses to free a slave, he must free a believing slave. Likewise, all expiations, such as the expiation for murder, zihar, and sexual intercourse during the day in Ramadan, must free a disbelieving slave in all of them except for the expiation for murder, because God the Almighty restricted the slave in them to faith. We said: The absolute is interpreted according to the restricted {just as God the Almighty restricted the testimony to justice in one place, saying: And bring to witness two just men among you and divorce, 2, and He made it absolute in another place, saying: And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men Al-Baqarah, 282. Then justice is a condition in all of them, interpreting the absolute according to the restricted}, and likewise here, and it is not permissible to free an apostate by consensus from the expiation. It is required that the slave be free of any defect that would clearly harm the work, so that it is not permissible for a person to be freed from a contract of manumission, a slave who is a slave of God, or a slave whom he bought on the condition of manumission, or bought his relative who is to be freed with the intention of expiation. He is freed, but it is not permissible for expiation. The people of opinion are freeing a person who is freed from a contract of manumission if he has not performed any of the rites, and freeing a relative for expiation. It is required that the slave be free of any defect that would clearly harm the work, so that it is not permissible for a person with one hand or one foot cut off, nor for a blind person, nor for a person who is mentally ill, nor for a completely insane person. It is permissible for a one-eyed person, a deaf person, or a person with one of the ears or nose cut off, because these defects do not clearly harm the work. According to Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, every defect that deprives a type of benefit in perfection prevents permissibility, even if he allowed a person with one hand cut off, but he did not allow a person with both ears cut off. The Almighty said: But whoever cannot find [a means of it], then a fast of three days. If the one who is obligated to pay expiation for an oath is unable to feed, clothe, or free a slave, he must fast for three days. Inability means that he does not have enough money to feed or free a slave beyond his sustenance and the sustenance of his dependents and his need, so he must fast for three days. Some of them said: If he has enough to feed, even if it is not more than enough, then he is not allowed to fast. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubair. They differed about the necessity of fasting consecutively in this case: A group of people said that it is not necessary to fast consecutively, but rather if he wishes he may continue and if he wishes he may separate, and consecutive fasting is better and is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. A group of people said that it is necessary to fast consecutively by analogy with the expiation for murder and zihar, and this is the opinion of Al-Thawri and Abu Hanifa, and it is indicated by the reading of Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, so fasting three consecutive days. That, meaning: that which you mentioned, is expiation for your oaths when you swear, and you break your oath, because expiation is not necessary except after breaking the oath. They differed about offering expiation before breaking the oath. Some people held that it is permissible, based on what we have narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees that something else is better than it, let him offer expiation for his oath and do what is better. This is the opinion of ‘Umar {and Ibn ‘Umar}, Ibn ‘Abbas and ‘Aa’ishah, and al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin said the same. Malik, al-Awza’i and al-Shafi’i held the same opinion, except that al-Shafi’i said: If he offers expiation by fasting before breaking the oath, it is not permissible because it is physical. Rather, it is permissible by feeding, clothing or freeing a slave, just as it is permissible to offer zakaah before a year, and it is not permissible to hasten the fast of Ramadan before its time. Some people held the opinion that it is not permissible to offer expiation before breaking the oath, and Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him said the same. God the Almighty said: And guard your oaths. It was said that what he meant by this is not swearing, i.e., do not swear. It was also said that this is the most correct, that he meant by it: If you swear, do not break your oath. What is meant by it is guarding the oath from breaking it. This is if his oath was not to leave something recommended or do something disliked. If he swore to do something disliked or leave something recommended, then it is better for him to break his oath and make atonement. This is because Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Mullaji informed us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, I told Muhammad bin Ismail, I told Hajjaj bin Munhal, I told Jarir bin Hazim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Samurah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Abdul Rahman bin Samurah, do not ask for leadership, for if you are given it because you asked for it, you will be left to it, and if you are given it without asking for it, you will be helped to do it. And if you swear an oath and you see something better than it, then make atonement for your oath and do what is better.” God Almighty says: Thus does God make clear to you His signs that you may be grateful.
5:90: 91 - Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through wine and gambling. As for the animosity over wine, the drinkers become drunk, riotous and quarrel, as did the Ansari who wounded Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas with the jawbone of a camel. As for the animosity over gambling, Qatada said: A man would gamble for his family and wealth, then he would remain sad, deprived of his family and wealth, and angry at his {customers}. And avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer, that is because whoever is busy drinking wine or gambling, it distracts him from the remembrance of God, and disrupts his prayer, as it did with the guests of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. A man came forward to lead them in the Maghrib prayer after they had drunk, so he recited, Say, 'O you disbelievers,' meaning, Shall I worship that which you worship?, omitting the word la. "Will you then desist?" That is: stop. It is a question and its meaning is a command, like the Almighty’s saying: So will you be grateful? Surat Al-Anbiya’ - 80.
5:91: 92- And obey God and obey the Messenger and beware, the prohibitions and prohibitions, But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification. In the warning to the one who drinks alcohol, Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Furani told us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abdullah al-Taysifuni told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmoud al-Mahmoudi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Masarjisi told us in Nishapur, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanthali told us, Salih ibn Qudamah told us, my brother Abd al-Malik ibn Qudamah told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Every intoxicant is forbidden. It is an inevitability upon God that no servant drinks it in this world except that God Almighty will give him to drink on the Day of Resurrection from the mud of Khabal. Do you know what the mud of Khabal is?” He said: The sweat of the people of Hell. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever drinks alcohol in this world and does not repent from it will be forbidden from it in the Hereafter. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ahmad bin Abi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Sagani told us, Abu Naim Abdul Aziz bin Omar bin Abdul Aziz told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah Al-Ghafiqi from the people of Egypt, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, that he said: I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God has cursed wine, its drinker, its server, its buyer, its presser, its presser, its carrier, and the one who consumes its price.
5:92: 93- The Almighty said: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten. The reason for the revelation of this verse is that the Companions, may God be pleased with them, said when the prohibition of alcohol was revealed: O Messenger of God, what about our brothers who died while they were drinking alcohol and {eating} from the money of gambling? Then God Almighty revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten, and drank wine and ate from the wealth of gambling, if they fear polytheism, and believe, and were truthful, and do righteous deeds and then fear wine and gambling after they were forbidden, and believe and then fear what God forbade them to eat and drink, and do good, and God loves the doers of good. It was said: The meaning of the first is if they fear polytheism, and believe and were truthful and then fear, meaning: they persisted in that piety, and believed increased in faith, then feared all sins and did good. It was said: meaning: fear by doing good, and every doer of good is pious, and God loves the doers of good.
7:32: 94- The Almighty said: O you who believe, God will surely test you with something of the game, the verse was given in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah and they were in a state of ihram. God tested them with hunting, and the wild beasts were covering their camps because of their large numbers, so they thought of seizing them, so the verse was revealed: O you who believe, God will surely test you, so that God would test them. The benefit of the test is to show the obedient from the disobedient, otherwise He would not need to test with something of the game, but rather some, so He said with something because He tested them with the game of the land in particular that your hands may reach, meaning: chicks and eggs and what cannot escape from the small game, and your spears, meaning: the large game, so that God may know, so that God may see, because He has taught him, who fears Him unseen, meaning: who fears God but has not seen Him, like the Almighty's saying: who fear their Lord unseen Al-Anbiya 49, meaning: who fears Him and does not hunt. In the state of ihram, But whoever transgresses after that, meaning: hunts after his ihram, will have a painful punishment. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: He will be flogged on his back and his clothes will be taken away. 32- The Almighty said: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants?” meaning wearing clothes during the circumambulation, and the good things of provision, meaning meat and fat during the days of Hajj. On the authority of Ibn Abbas and Qatada: The good things of sustenance are what the people of ignorance forbade, such as the lakes and the sa’ib. “Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world, and exclusively for them on the Day of Resurrection.” There is an omission in it, the meaning of which is: It is for those who believe and for the polytheists in the life of this world, for the polytheists share with the believers in the good things of this world, and in the Hereafter it is exclusively for the believers, and the polytheists have no share in it. It was said: It is pure on the Day of Resurrection from the distress and sorrow for the believers, for it is for them in this world with the distress and sorrow.
