Its meaning is: We did not say that they [completed what they had assigned to the idols from what they had assigned to God, nor] completed what they had assigned to God from what they had assigned to the idols. Qatada said that when a famine struck them, they would seek help from what they had assigned to God and eat from it, and they would save what they had assigned to their partners and not eat [anything] from it. Evil is what they judge, meaning: Evil is what [they do]. 137- And thus it was made attractive to many of the polytheists, meaning: just as the prohibition of cultivation and livestock was made attractive to them, so it was made attractive to many of the polytheists, the killing of their children by their partners, Mujahid said, their partners, meaning: their devils made the burying of girls attractive and made it seem good to them for fear of poverty. The devils were called partners because they obeyed them in disobeying God, and the partners were attributed to them because they adopted them. Al-Kalbi said: Their partners were the guardians of their gods who used to adorn the killing of children for the infidels. A man among them would swear that if such-and-such a boy was born to him, he would slaughter one of them, just as Abdul Muttalib swore to his father Abdullah. Ibn Amir read: Zain with a damma on the zay and a kasra on the ya’, Qalt in the nominative case, Awladhim in the accusative case, Shirakaim in the genitive case as an introduction, as if he said: It was made attractive to many of the polytheists that their partners killed their children. He separated the verb from its subject with the direct object, and they are the children, as the poet said: So I pushed him away, as I pushed the camel Abu Mazada away. That is: Abu Mazada threw the camel into the water, so the action, which is killing, was attributed to the partners, even though they did not undertake that because they are the ones who decorated it and called for it, so it is as if they did it. The Almighty’s statement, to turn them back, means to destroy them, and to confuse them, means to mix up their religion, Ibn Abbas said: to make them doubt their religion, and they were on the religion of Ishmael, so they turned away from it due to the confusion of the devils. And if God had willed, they would not have done it, that is, if God had willed, He would have protected them until they did that of forbidding cultivation and livestock and killing children, so leave them, O Muhammad, and what they invent, inventing lies, for God is watching them. 138- And they said meaning: the polytheists, These are livestock and crops that are forbidden, meaning: forbidden, meaning: what they made for God and their gods of crops and livestock as mentioned above. Mujahid said: What he meant by livestock are: the bahīrah, the sā'ibah, the wasīlah, and the Ḥām. None shall eat of them except whom We will, according to their claim meaning men, not women. And livestock whose backs are forbidden meaning: the hawāmi, they did not ride them, And livestock over which they do not mention the name of God meaning: they slaughter them in the name of idols, not in the name of God. Abu Wa'il said: Its meaning is that they do not perform Hajj on them nor ride them to do good. Inventing falsehood against Him meaning: that they do that and claim that God commanded them to do it, inventing falsehood against Him. He will recompense them for what they invent.
6:139: 139- And they said, 'What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives,' meaning, our women. Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Al-Sha'bi said: He meant the fetuses of the Baha'ir and the Sawa'ib, so whatever is born alive from them is exclusively for the men without the women, and whatever is born dead is eaten by both men and women. The letter ha' was inserted in khalasa for emphasis, like the specific and general, like their saying: nasaba and alamah. Al-Farra' said: The letter ha' was inserted to feminize the livestock because what is in their bellies is like them, so it was made feminine by its feminization. Al-Kisa'i said: Khalas and Khalasa are one and the same, like wa'z and mu'azah. “And if it is dead,” Ibn ‘Amir [and Abu Ja’far] read: it is with a ta’ dead in the nominative case, the verb is mentioned with the feminine marker, because dead is feminine in wording. Abu Bakr read from ‘Asim: it is with a ta’ dead in the accusative case, meaning: And if the fetuses are dead. Ibn Kathir read: and if it is with a ya’ dead in the nominative case, because what is meant by dead is the dead, meaning: And if what is in the wombs is dead. The others read: and if it is with a ya’ dead in the accusative case, referring it back to what, meaning: And if what is in the wombs is dead, [this is indicated by the fact that he said]: Then they are partners in it, and he did not say in it, and he meant that men and women are partners in it. He will recompense them for their description, meaning: for their description, or for their description of lying about God Almighty. He is Wise and Knowing.
6:140: 140- Those who killed their children have certainly lost out, Ibn Amir and Ibn Kathir read killed with emphasis on the ta' for emphasis, while the others read it without emphasis. Foolishly, ignorantly. Without knowledge, it was revealed about Rabi'ah and Mudar and some other Arabs. They used to bury their daughters alive for fear of captivity and poverty, but Banu Kinanah did not do that. And they forbade what God had provided for them, meaning: the Bahira, the Sa’ibah, the Wasila, and the Ham, as a slander against God, as they said: God had commanded them to do it. They have gone astray and were not guided.
6:141: 141- The Almighty said: And it is He who created, originated. Gardens, orchards, trellised and untrellised, meaning: elevated, raised and untrellised. Ibn Abbas said: Trellised: what is spread out on the surface of the earth and spreads out from what is trellised, such as: grapevines, gourds, watermelons and others, and untrellised: what stands on a trunk and is covered, such as palm trees, crops and other trees. Al-Dahhak said: Both, especially the vineyard, some of which are trellised and some of which are not. And the palm trees and the crops, meaning: He created the palm trees and the crops, of different kinds of food, its fruit and its taste, including sweet and sour, good and bad, and the olives and the pomegranates, similar, in appearance, but not similar, in taste, like two pomegranates that are the same color but different in taste, eat of its fruit when it bears fruit, this is a command of permission. And give its due on the day of its harvest. The people of Basra, Ibn Amir, and Asim read Harvest with a fat-ha on the ha’, while the others read it with a kasra on it, and their meanings are the same, like Saram and Saram and Jazzaz and Jazzaz. They differed on this right: Ibn Abbas, Tawus, Al-Hasan, Jabir bin Zaid, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It is the obligatory zakat of one-tenth and half-tenth. Ali Ibn Al-Hussein, Ata, Mujahid, Hammad, and Al-Hakam said: It is a right in money other than zakat. He ordered that it be given, because the verse is Meccan and zakat was imposed in Medina. Ibrahim said: It is the bunch. Al-Rabi’ said: It is the one who picks up the ears of corn. Mujahed said: They used to hang the bunch of dates at the harvest time so that those who passed by would eat from it. Yazid bin Al-Asamm said: When the people of Medina harvested the dates, they would bring a bunch of dates and hang them on the side of the mosque. A poor man would come and hit it with his stick, and it would fall, so he would pick it up. Saeed bin Jubair said: This was a right that was commanded to be done at the beginning of Islam, but it was abrogated by the obligation of the tenth. Muqsim said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Zakat abrogated every expenditure in the Qur’an. “And do not be extravagant. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess.” It was said that by extravagance he meant giving everything. Ibn Abbas said in Al-Kalbi’s narration: Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas cut five hundred palm trees and divided them in one day and left nothing for his family, so God Almighty revealed this verse. Al-Suddi said: Do not be extravagant, meaning do not give your money so that you remain poor. Al-Zajjaj said: According to this, if a person gives all his money and does not give anything to his family, then he has been extravagant, because it was stated in the hadith: Start with those you support. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Its meaning is do not withhold charity. So the interpretation of the verse according to this is: Do not exceed the limit in miserliness and withholding, so that you withhold the obligatory charity. Muqatil said: Do not associate idols with you in farming and livestock. Al-Zuhri said: Do not spend in disobedience. Mujahid said: Extravagance is that by which you fall short of the right of God, the Almighty. He said: If Abu Qubays was gold for a man and he spent it in obedience to God, he would not be extravagant. But if he spent a dirham or a mudd in disobedience to God, he would be extravagant. Iyas bin Muawiyah said: Whatever you do with exceeds the command of God is extravagance and wastefulness. Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Abu Zaid, who said: The address is to the sultans, saying: Do not take more than your right.
6:142: 142- The Almighty said: And from the livestock, meaning: He created from the livestock loads, which are everything that is carried on from the camels, and bedding, which are the young camels that do not carry. Eat of what God has provided for you and do not follow the footsteps of Satan, do not follow his path and traces in forbidding cultivation and livestock. He is to you a clear enemy.
6:144: 144- "And of the camels, two, and of the cows, two. Say, 'Is it the two males that He has forbidden, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?'" This is because they used to say: These are livestock and cultivation of Hajar, and they said: What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives, and they forbade the Bahirah, the Sa'ibah, the Wasilah, and the Ham, and they used to forbid some of them to men and women, and some of them to women but not to men. When Islam came and the rulings were established, they argued with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their orator was Malik ibn Awf Abu al-Ahwas al-Jashmi, and he said: "O Muhammad, [it has reached us] that you forbid things that our fathers used to do." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have forbidden types of sheep without a basis, and God created these eight pairs for eating and benefiting from them, so where did this prohibition come from? From the male or from the female? So Malik ibn Awf was silent and confused and did not speak. If he had said that the prohibition came because of the males, it would have been necessary to All males are forbidden, and if he said because of femininity, then all females must be forbidden, and if it is because the womb contains him, then all should be forbidden, because the womb only contains a male or a female. As for specifying the prohibition to the fifth child or the seventh or some, where does that come from? It is narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Malik: O Malik, why don’t you speak? Malik said to him: Rather, speak and I will listen to you. “Or were you witnesses,” present, when God enjoined this upon you? Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God to lead people astray without knowledge? It was said that he meant by this: Amr ibn Luhay and those who came after him on his path, Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
6:145: 145- Then he explained that prohibition and permission are by revelation and sending down, so he said: Say, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden.’ It was narrated that they said: So what is forbidden then? So it was revealed: Say, O Muhammad, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden,’ meaning: anything forbidden, for one who eats it, meaning: one who eats it, unless it be a dead animal. Ibn ‘Amir and Abu Ja’far read takun with a ta’, dead in the nominative case, meaning: unless it be a dead animal. Ibn Kathir and Hamzah read takun with a ta’, dead in the accusative case, assuming a feminine noun, meaning: unless the soul or the body is dead. The rest read yakun with a ya’ dead in the accusative case, meaning: unless [the food] is dead, or blood poured out, meaning: spilled and flowing. Ibn ‘Abbas said: He means what comes out of the animal while they are alive, and what comes out of the souls and what comes out of the jugular veins at slaughter, and it does not include the liver and spleen, because they are solid, and the Shari’ah has come to permit them, nor what is mixed with the meat from blood, because it is not flowing. Imran bin Hudayr said: I asked Abu Majlaz about blood that mixes with meat, and about the pot in which red blood is seen? He said: There is nothing wrong with it, he only forbade spilled blood. Ibrahim said: There is nothing wrong with blood in a vein or brain, except for blood that is spilled intentionally. Ikrimah said: If it were not for this verse, Muslims would have followed the same veins as the Jews. Or the flesh of swine, for it is impure is forbidden, or an abomination dedicated to other than God which is what is slaughtered in a name other than that of God Almighty. Some scholars have said that the prohibition is limited to these things. This is narrated on the authority of Aisha and Ibn Abbas, who said: “And included in the dead are: strangled animals, those beaten to death, and what is mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Ma’idah.” Most scholars agree that the prohibition is not limited to these things, and what is prohibited by the text of the Book is what is mentioned here. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden.’ The Sunnah has prohibited things that must be said. Among them: What Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Ubaidullah bin Muadh Al-Anbari told us, my father told us, Shu’bah told us, Al-Hakam told us, Maymun bin Mihran told us, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade every beast of prey with fangs, and every bird with talons.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Musab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Hakim, on the authority of Ubaydah ibn Abi Sufyan al-Hadrami, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Eating every fanged beast of prey is forbidden. The basic principle according to Al-Shafi’i is that if there is no text stating that it is forbidden or permissible, then if it is something that the Shari’ah has ordered to be killed - as it says: Five evils are to be killed in the sacred precincts and outside of it, or it has forbidden to kill it, as it was narrated that it has forbidden to kill the bee and the ant - then it is forbidden. As for anything other than that, the reference is to the majority of them, so it is forbidden, because God Almighty addressed them with His saying: “Say: Lawful to you are all good things,” so it is proven that whatever they find permissible is permissible. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limits] - then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. He permitted eating these forbidden things when forced, but not as an act of aggression.
6:146: 146- The Almighty said: And to those who were Jews, meaning the Jews, We have forbidden every animal with claws, which is the animal and bird that does not have split toes, such as the camel, the ostrich, the goose, and the duck. Al-Qatibi said: It is every bird with claws and every animal with hoofs, and he narrated it from some of the commentators, and he said: The hoof was called a claw as a metaphor. And of the cattle and the sheep We have forbidden them their fat, meaning the fat of the stomach, which is the omentum, and the fat of the kidneys, except what adheres to their backs, meaning: except what adheres to the urethra and the side from inside their bellies, or the entrails, which are the camels, the singular of which is: hausiya or hausiya, meaning: what the entrails carry of fat. Or what is mixed with a bone, meaning: the fat of the buttocks. All of this is included in the exception, and the prohibition is specific to the omentum and the fat of the kidney. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah told us, Al-Layth told us, Yazid bin Abi Habib told us, Ata bin Abi Rabah told us, Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say in the year of the conquest while he was in Mecca: God and His Messenger have forbidden the sale of wine, dead animals, pigs, and idols. It was said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of the fat of dead animals, for it is used to coat ships, grease hides, and people use it for lighting lamps? He said: No, it is forbidden. Then the Messenger of God said at that time: May God curse the Jews, for when God Almighty forbade their fat, they melted it down, sold it, and ate its price. “That is how We recompensed them,” meaning: that prohibition was a punishment for them, for their transgression, meaning: for their injustice in killing the prophets, preventing people from the path of God, taking usury, and making people’s money lawful unjustly. And indeed, We are truthful, in informing them of what We prohibited them from and of their transgression.
6:147: 147- But if they deny you, then say, ‘Your Lord is full of vast mercy,’ by delaying the punishment from you, but His punishment is not averted from the criminal people, when its time comes.
6:148: 148- Those who associate others with God will say, when the proof is binding on them and they are certain of the invalidity of what they were doing of associating others with God and forbidding what God did not forbid [they said] If God had willed, we would not have associated others with God, nor would our fathers, before, nor would we have forbidden anything, of the lakes and the sa'iba and others. They wanted to make His statement, If God had willed, we would not have associated others with God, an argument for them to maintain their association with God. They said that God, the Most High, is able to prevent us from what we are doing so that we do not do it. If He were not pleased with what we are doing and wanted it from us and commanded us to do it, He would have prevented us from doing it. So God, the Most High, said, denying them: Thus did those before them deny, of the disbelievers of the past nations, until they tasted Our punishment, of Our torment. The people of predestination use this verse as evidence. They say that when they said: If God had willed, we would not have associated partners with Him, God denied them and responded to them, saying: Thus did those before them deny. We said: The denial is not in their saying, If God had willed, we would not have associated partners with Him, rather that saying is true, but in their saying, God Almighty commanded us to do it and was pleased with what we are doing, as He informed us about them in Surat Al-A’raf (verse 28): And when they commit an immorality, they say, ‘We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to do it.’ So the response to them in this is as God Almighty said: Say, ‘God does not command immorality.’ The evidence that the denial was mentioned in what we said, not in their saying: If God had willed, we would not have associated others with Him, is His statement: Thus did those before them deny, with emphasis. If that were report from God Almighty about their lie in their saying: If God had willed, we would not have associated others with Him, He would have said, Those before them denied, with emphasis, and thus He would have attributed to them the lie, not the denial. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: If they had mentioned this statement out of respect and reverence for God Almighty, and out of their knowledge of Him, He would not have criticized them for that, because God Almighty said: And if God had willed, they would not have associated others with Him, and He said: They would not have believed unless God willed, Al-An’am, 111. The believers say that, but they said it as a denial, guesswork, and argument without knowledge of God and what they are saying. Similar to His statement, Almighty and Majestic is He: And they said, ‘If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them.’ Az-Zukhruf, 20. God Almighty said: “They have no knowledge of that. They are only guessing.” Al-An’am, 116. It was said about the meaning of the verse that they were saying the truth with this word, except that they were considering it an excuse for themselves and making it an argument for themselves in abandoning faith. They were refuted in this because God’s command is separate from His will and desire, for He is the Willer of all beings, but He does not command everything He wants. The servant must follow His command and he does not have to depend on His will, for His will is not an excuse for anyone. “Say: ‘Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? ’” meaning: a book and proof from God, that you can produce for us, so that what you claim against God Almighty of polytheism or the prohibition of what you have prohibited will be made clear. You follow, what you follow in what you are upon, nothing but conjecture, without knowledge and certainty, and you are only guessing, lying.
6:149: 149- “Say: ‘Then God has the conclusive argument’, the complete argument against His creation through the Book [and the Messenger] and the explanation, ‘and if He had willed, He could have guided you all’,” so this indicates that He did not will the faith of the disbeliever, and if He had willed, He would have guided him.
6:150: 150- “Say: Bring,” it is said to one, two, or plural, your witnesses who testify, meaning: Bring your witnesses who testify, that God has forbidden this, this goes back to what came before of their forbidding things to themselves and their claim that God commanded them to do it, if they testify, lying, then do not testify, you, with them and do not follow the inclinations of those who deny Our signs and those who do not believe in the Hereafter and who equate others with their Lord, meaning: they associate others with Him.
6:151: 151- The Almighty said: Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him.’ This is because they asked and said: What is it that God Almighty has prohibited? So the Almighty said: Say, ‘Come, I will recite.’ Recite what your Lord has prohibited to you truly and certainly, not as a conjecture or a lie as you claim. If it is said: What is the meaning of his saying, Your Lord has forbidden you to associate anything with Him, and what is forbidden is polytheism, not abandoning polytheism? It was said that the position of that is in the nominative case, meaning that you should not associate partners with Him. It was also said that its location is in the accusative case, and they differed about the reason for its accusative case. It was said that its meaning is that it is forbidden for you to associate partners with Him, and la is a relative clause like the Almighty’s saying, What prevented you from prostrating? (al-A’raf 7:12), meaning: what prevented you from prostrating. It was also said that the speech ended when He said, Your Lord has forbidden, then He said: You should not associate anything with Him, as an enticement. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for this to be carried on the meaning, meaning: I recite to you the prohibition of polytheism. It is permissible for it to be on the meaning: I advise you not to associate anything with Him. And to parents, do good, and do not kill your children out of poverty, poverty. We provide for you and for them, meaning: do not bury your daughters alive for fear of poverty, for I provide for you and for them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed, [what is apparent means: what is public, and what is concealed] means secret. The people of ignorance considered adultery in public to be ugly, but they did not see anything wrong with it in secret. So God Almighty forbade adultery in public and in secret. Ad-Dahhak said: What is apparent is wine, and what is hidden is adultery. And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. God Almighty has forbidden the killing of a believer or a person with whom a covenant has been made, except by right, except for what makes killing permissible, such as apostasy, retaliation, or adultery that requires stoning. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Al-Hussein Al-Hiri told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Muhammad bin Hammad told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The blood of a Muslim man who bears witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God is not permissible to be shed except in one of three cases: a married man who commits adultery, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community.” That that I mentioned He has enjoined upon you, He has commanded you with it, that you may understand.
6:152: 152- And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, meaning: in a way that is good for him and makes him grow. Mujahid said: It is trading in it. Ad-Dahhak said: It is to seek it for him and not take anything from its profit, until he reaches maturity, Ash-Sha'bi and Malik said: maturity is forbearance, until good deeds are recorded for him [and bad deeds are recorded against him]. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Until he becomes sensible and his strength is gathered. Al-Kalbi said: maturity is between eighteen and thirty years. It was said: Up to forty years. It was said: Up to sixty years. Ad-Dahhak said: Twenty years. As-Suddi said: Thirty years. Mujahid said: maturity is thirty-three years. Ashd is the plural of shadd, like qad and aqad, and it is the strengthening of the strength of his youth and age, and from it comes the shadd of the day which is its height. It was said that reaching the peak of ashd is that his maturity is felt after puberty. The meaning of the verse: Do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, forever, until he reaches maturity. Then give him his property if he is of sound mind. And give full measure and weight in justice, with justice. We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, meaning: its ability to give full measure and weight. That is, the giver is not charged more than what is required of him, and the one with the right is not charged with being satisfied with less than his right, so that his soul does not feel constrained by it. Rather, each of them is commanded to do what is within his capacity, without any blame upon him for it. And when you speak, be just, so be truthful in your judgment and testimony, even if it is a relative, that is, even if the one being judged and the one being testified against are relatives, “and fulfill the covenant of God. This is what He has enjoined upon you that you may remember,” that is, be admonished. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read you remember with a light dhal, the entire Qur’an, and the others with a shaddah on it. Ibn Abbas said: These verses are decisive in all books, nothing has abrogated them, and they are forbidden to all of the children of Adam. They are the mother of the book. Whoever acts upon them will enter Paradise, and whoever abandons them will enter Hell.
6:153: 153- "And that this", meaning: this which I have commanded you in these two verses, "is My path, My way and My religion, straight, level, upright, so follow it, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read and" with a kasra on the alif as a new sentence, and the others read: with a fatha on the alif, Al-Farra' said: The meaning is, I recite to you that this is My path, straight. Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read: with a sukoon on the noon. "And do not follow the paths", meaning: the different paths other than this path, such as Judaism, Christianity, and other religions, and it was said: whims and innovations, "for you will be divided, so you will be inclined, and scattered, from His path, from His way and religion which He was pleased with, and with which He commanded, that, which I mentioned, He has commanded you with it that you may become righteous". Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd al-Samad al-Turabi, known as Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Haytham, told us, al-Hakim Abu al-Fadl Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Haddadi told us, Abu Yazid Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Khalid told us, Abu Yaqub Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanthali told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line for us and then said: This is the path of God. Then he drew lines to its right and to its left, and said: These are paths, on each path of which is a devil calling to it. Then he recited: ‘And this is My path, which is straight, so follow it’” the verse.
6:154: 154- Then We gave Moses the Scripture. If it is said: Why did He say: Then We gave and the letter then is for following up and giving Moses the Scripture was before the coming of the Qur'an? It is said: Its meaning is then I inform you that We gave Moses the Scripture, so then was included to delay the report, not to delay the revelation. Completely upon him who did good. They differed about it. It was said: Completely upon the good-doers of his people. So who means whom, that is, upon those who did good among his people. There were good-doers and bad-doers among them. This is indicated by the reading of Ibn Mas’ud: upon those who did good. Abu Ubaidah said: Its meaning is upon everyone who did good. That is, We completed the virtue of Moses with the Book upon the good-doers. That is, We showed his virtue to them. The good-doers are the prophets and the believers. It was said: who did good is Moses, and who means what, that is, upon what Moses did good. Its meaning is: We gave him the Book, meaning the Torah, as completion of the blessing upon him, for his goodness in obedience and worship, and conveying the message and carrying out the command. It was said that Ihsan means knowledge, and Ahsan means knowledge, and its meaning is: Complete with what Moses had done well in knowledge and wisdom, meaning we gave him the Book in addition to that. It was said that its meaning is: Completely from me for my kindness to Moses. “And in detail,” explaining everything, that he needs from the laws of religion, and guidance and mercy, this is in the description of the Torah, that they may believe in the meeting with their Lord, Ibn Abbas said: so that they may believe in the resurrection and believe in reward and punishment.
6:155: 155- And this, meaning: the Qur’an, is a blessed Book which We have revealed, so follow it, and act according to what is in it, and fear God, and obey, that you may receive mercy.
6:156: 156- That you say, meaning lest you say, as in the Almighty's saying: God makes clear to you lest you go astray, An-Nisa, 176, meaning: lest you go astray. It was said: Its meaning is that we revealed it out of dislike that you say, Al-Kisa'i said: Its meaning is beware of saying, O people of Mecca, The Book was only revealed to two groups before us, meaning: the Jews and the Christians, and if we were, and we were, from their study, their reading, negligent, we do not know what it is, its meaning is that we revealed the Qur'an to you lest you say that the Book was revealed to those before us in their language and their tongue and we did not know what was in it and we were negligent in studying it, so you make it an excuse for yourselves.
6:157: 157- "Or you say, 'If only the Scripture had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they are.'" A group of the infidels said that if only what was sent down to the Jews and Christians had been sent down to us, we would have been better than them. God Almighty said: "There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord, a clear argument in a language you know, and guidance, an explanation, and mercy," and a blessing for those who follow it. "So who is more unjust than he who denies the signs of God and turns away, turns away, from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our signs with a terrible punishment, a severe punishment, for what they used to turn away, [turn away].
6:158: 158- The Almighty’s saying: Do they wait, meaning: Do they wait after their denial of the messengers and their rejection of the Qur’an, except that the angels come to them, to seize their souls, and it was said: with the punishment. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read comes to them with the letter ya here and in An-Nahl, and the rest with the letter ta, “or your Lord comes,” without how, to separate the judgment between His creation on the Day of Resurrection, or some of the signs of your Lord come, meaning the rising of the sun from the West, most of the commentators agreed with it, and Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, On the Day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before, meaning: faith will not benefit them when the sign appears that compels them to believe, or earned good through its faith, meaning: the faith of a disbeliever will not be accepted, nor the repentance of a sinner. “Say, ‘Wait,’ O people of Mecca, ‘We are waiting,’ with you for the punishment. Abu Ali Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, on the authority of Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi, on the authority of Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan, on the authority of Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami, on the authority of Abdul Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the West. When it rises and the people see it, they will all believe. That is when no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith.” Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hairi told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Muhammad bin Hammad told us, Abu Muawiyah Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Umar bin Marra, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The hands of God are extended for the sinner of the night to repent during the day, and for the sinner of the day to repent at night, until the sun rises from the west. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, on the authority of Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an, on the authority of Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani, on the authority of Hamid bin Zanjawayh, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Shumayl, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever repents before the sun rises from the West, God will accept his repentance. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud told us, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, who said: I came to Safwan bin Assal Al-Muradi and he mentioned on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: God Almighty has made a door in the West, the width of which is a journey of seventy years, for repentance, which will not be closed until the sun rises from it. This is the saying of God Almighty: On the Day that some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before. Abu Hazim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three things that, if they appear, will not benefit a soul from its faith if it did not believe before or earn any good through its faith: the Antichrist, the Beast, and the rising of the sun from the west.”
6:159: 159- The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who divided their religion, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: faraqu, with an alif here and in Surat Al-Rum, meaning: they left their religion and abandoned it. The others read: faraqu, with a shaddah, meaning: they made the religion of God, which is one - the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, the Hanafi religion - into different religions, so one people became Jewish and another people became Christian. This is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: and they became sects, meaning: they became different groups, and they are the Jews and Christians, according to the saying of Mujahid, Qatada, and Al-Suddi. It was said: They are the people of innovations and doubts of this nation. It was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Aisha: O Aisha, those who left their religion and became sects are the people of innovations and doubts of this nation. Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Hanafi narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Aqil ibn al-Azhari ibn Aqil al-Faqih al-Balkhi, on the authority of al-Ramadi Ahmad ibn Mansur, on the authority of al-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad, on the authority of Thawr ibn Yazid, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr al-Salami, on the authority of al-Arbadh ibn Sariyah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the dawn prayer and gave us an eloquent sermon that brought tears to our eyes and made our hearts fearful. Someone said: ‘O Messenger of God, it is as if this is a farewell sermon, so advise us.’ He said: ‘I advise you to fear God and to listen and obey, even if you are an Abyssinian slave, for whoever among you lives will see much difference. So adhere to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly-guided caliphs, cling to it firmly and beware of newly invented matters, for every innovation is misguidance.’” It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Children of Israel split into seventy-two sects, and my nation split into seventy-three sects, all of them in Hell except one. They said: Which one is it, O Messenger of God? He said: What I and my companions are upon. Abdullah bin Masoud said: “The best speech is the Book of God, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the worst of matters are their innovations.” Jabir narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Almighty said: You are not of them in anything. It was said: I am not of fighting them in anything, the verse of fighting abrogated it. This is according to the opinion of those who say: What is meant in the verse is the Jews and Christians. And whoever says: What is meant by the verse is the people of desires, said: What is meant by His saying: You are not of them in anything is that you are innocent of them and they are innocent of you. The Arabs say: If you do such and such, then you are not of me and I am not of you, meaning: each one of us is innocent of his companion. Their affair is only with God, meaning: in recompense and rewards. Then He will inform them of what they used to do, when they come to the Day of Resurrection.
6:160: 160- The Almighty said: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, meaning: he will have ten good deeds the like thereof. Jacob read ten with a tanween, the like thereof with the nominative case. And whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof, and they will not be wronged. Hassan told us, on the authority of Saeed Al-Munai’i, on the authority of Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash Al-Ziyadi, on the authority of Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Qattan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yusuf Al-Qattan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yusuf Al-Sulaimi, on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If one of you improves his Islam, then every good deed he does will be recorded as ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, and every bad deed he does will be recorded as its like, until he meets God Almighty.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani told us, on the authority of Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad Al-Farsi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan, on the authority of Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Ma’rur bin Suwayd, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty says: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof and more. Whoever brings an evil deed will have the recompense of an evil deed like it or I will forgive him. Whoever draws near to Me a handspan, I will draw near to him an arm’s length. Whoever draws near to Me an arm’s length, I will draw near to him a fathom’s length. Whoever comes to Me walking, I will come to him running. Whoever meets Me with an earth’s worth of sins, not associating anything with Me, I will meet him with the like thereof of forgiveness.” Ibn Omar said: The verse is about good deeds other than charity. Charity is multiplied seven hundred times.
6:161: 161- The Almighty said: “Say: My Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion.” The people of Kufa and Ash-Sham read qayyiman with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ya’, lightly, while the others read it with a fatha on the qaf and a kasra on the ya’, stressed, and their meaning is the same, which is the straight and upright. Its accusative is in the sense of He has guided me to a right religion, the religion of Abraham, a monotheist, and he was not of the polytheists.
6:162: 162- "Say: Verily, my prayer and my sacrifice", it was said that he meant by the sacrifice the sacrifice in Hajj and Umrah, and Muqatil said: My sacrifice is my Hajj, and it was said: My religion, and my life and my death, meaning: my life and my death, are for God, Lord of the Worlds, meaning: He gives me life and causes me to die, and it was said: My life is with righteous deeds and my death if I die in faith is for God, Lord of the Worlds, and it was said: My obedience in my life is for God and my reward after my death is from God, Lord of the Worlds. The people of Medina read: and my life with a sukoon on the ya' and my death with a fatha on it, and the general reading is my life with a fatha on the ya' so that two sukoon letters do not come together.
6:163: 163- The Almighty said: He has no partner, and this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims. Qatada said: And I am the first of the Muslims of this nation.
6:164: 164- "Say: Shall I seek other than God as a lord?" Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them said: A master and a god while He is the Lord of all things. This is because the infidels used to say to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Return to our religion. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira used to say: Follow my path and I will bear your burdens. God the Almighty said: And no soul earns except against itself, no soul earns except what the sinner bears of it, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, meaning no soul will bear the burden of another, meaning: no one will be held accountable for the sin of another, Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
6:165: 165- And it is He who has made you successors on the earth, meaning: He destroyed the people of the past generations and made you inherit the earth, O nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after them, so He made you successors from among them in it, succeeding them in it and populating it after them. Successors is the plural of successor, just as female servants is the plural of female servant, and everyone who comes after someone who has passed away is a successor because he succeeds him. And He has raised some of you above others in degrees, meaning: He has differentiated your conditions, making some of you above others in creation, provision, livelihood, strength, and virtue, that He may test you in what He has given you, to test you in what He has provided you, meaning: He tests the rich and the poor, the noble and the lowly, the free and the slave, to show what reward and punishment will be upon you, Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, because what is coming is swift and near. It was said: it is destruction in this world, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful, Ata' said: He is swift in punishment for His enemies, Forgiving for His friends, and Merciful towards them.
7:1: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All of it is Meccan except for five verses, the first of which is: And ask them about the city that was. 1- The sucker
7:2: 2- A Book, meaning: this is a book, revealed to you, which is the Qur'an, so let there not be in your breast any distress therefrom, Mujahid said: doubt, so the address is to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is the nation. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: distress means tightness, meaning do not let your breast feel tight with conveying and carrying out what you were sent with, to warn with it, meaning: a book revealed to you so that you may warn with it, and a reminder to the believers, an admonition to them, and it is a nominative, returned to the Book.
7:3: 3- Follow, meaning: and tell them to follow: what has been revealed to you from your Lord and do not follow other guardians besides Him, meaning: do not take other than Him as guardians whom you obey in disobeying God Almighty, little do you remember, you learn a lesson, and Ibn Amir read: they remember, with a ya and a ta.
7:4: 4- "And how many a town have We destroyed, with punishment, and how many is for multiplication and Lord is for diminution, So Our punishment came to them, Our punishment, at night, or while they were taking a nap", from the siesta, its meaning is: So Our punishment came to them at night while they were sleeping, or during the day while they were taking a nap, meaning sleeping at noon, and the siesta is resting in the middle of the day, even if there is no sleep with it. The meaning of the verse is: Our punishment came to them while they were not expecting it, either at night or during the day. Al-Zajjaj said: And or is for the inflection of the punishment, once at night and once during the day. It was said: Its meaning is from the people of the towns those whom We destroyed at night, and from them those whom We destroyed during the day. If it is said: What is the meaning of We destroyed it, so Our punishment came to it? How can punishment come after destruction? It is said: The meaning of His statement, We destroyed it is: We decreed its destruction, so Our punishment came to it. It is also said: So Our punishment came to it is an explanation of His statement, We destroyed it, like the statement of the speaker, You gave to me, so you were kind to me. There is no difference between it and his statement, You were kind to me, so give to me. So one of them is a substitute for the other.
7:5: 5- "So what was their claim", meaning: their statement, their supplication, and their entreaty. The claim can mean both a claim and a prayer. Sibawayh said: The Arabs say, "O God, let us share in the good claim of the Muslims, meaning in their supplication, when Our punishment came to them, Our torment, except that they said, Indeed, we were wrongdoers, meaning that they were not able to repel the punishment, and the result of their matter was to admit the crime when admission was of no use.
7:6: 6- Then We will surely question those to whom it was sent, meaning: the nations, about their response to the messengers. This is a question of rebuke, not a question of inquiry. That is: We will ask them about what they did with what the messengers conveyed to them, and We will surely question the messengers, about the conveyance.
7:7: 7- So We will narrate to them with knowledge meaning: We will inform them with knowledge. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Their book of deeds will speak against them, as God the Almighty says: This is Our book that speaks against you with the truth. Al-Jathiya, 29, And We were not absent, from the messengers in what they conveyed, and from the nations in what they responded to.
7:8: 8- The Almighty said: And the weighing on that Day will be the truth, meaning: the Day of Questioning. Mujahid said: Its meaning is: And the judgment on that Day will be just. The majority said: He meant by it the weighing of deeds on the scale, and that is because God Almighty will set up a scale with a tongue and two pans, each pan being the length of the distance between the east and the west. They differed about the method of weighing. Some of them said: The scrolls of deeds are weighed. We narrated: (A man will have ninety-nine scrolls spread out before him, each scroll as far as the eye can see. Then a card will be taken out for him in which is the testimony that there is no god but God and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. The scrolls will be placed on one side of the scale and the card on the other side. The scrolls will fly away and the card will be heavy.) It was said: People are weighed. We narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: A great, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection and he will not weigh as much as a mosquito’s wing in God’s sight. It was said that deeds are weighed. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Good deeds are brought in a good form and bad deeds in an ugly form, and they are placed on the scale. The wisdom in weighing deeds is for God to test His servants with faith in this world and to establish proof against them in the Hereafter. But those whose scales are heavy, Mujahid said: his good deeds, they are the successful ones.
7:9: 9- And those whose scales are light - they are the ones who have lost themselves because they were unjust to Our verses," denying. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, said when death approached him in his will to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: The scales of those whose scales are heavy on the Day of Resurrection are only because they followed the truth in this world, and it was heavy for them. And it is right for a scale in which the truth is placed tomorrow to be heavy. And the scales of those whose scales are light on the Day of Resurrection are only because they followed falsehood in this world, and it was light for them. And it is right for a scale in which falsehood is placed tomorrow to be light. If it is said: He said: whose scales are heavy was mentioned in the plural form, and the scale is one? It is said: It is possible that its wording is plural and its meaning is one, like his saying: O messengers, and it is said: For every servant there is a scale, and it is said: The origin is one great scale, and for every servant there is a scale attached to it, and it is said that it is plural because the scale includes the two pans, the two witnesses, and the tongue, and the weighing is not complete except by their coming together.
7:10: 10- The Almighty’s saying: And We have established you in the land, meaning: We have established you, and what is meant by establishment is ownership and ability, And We have made for you therein means of livelihood, meaning: causes by which you live during the days of your life, from trade, earnings, food, drink, and livelihoods, the plural of livelihood, you are little grateful, for what I have done for you.
7:11: 11- The Almighty said: "And We created you, then We shaped you." Ibn Abbas said: We created you, meaning: your origins and your fathers, then We shaped you in the wombs of your mothers. Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said: As for We created you, it is Adam, and as for We shaped you, it is his offspring. Mujahid said in We created you: Adam, then We shaped you in the back of Adam, then We shaped you on the Day of the Covenant when He brought you forth like ants. Ikrimah said: We created you in the loins of men, then We shaped you in the wombs of women. Yaman said: He created man in the womb, then He shaped him and split his hearing, sight, and fingers. It was said: He created and shaped all of Adam, and then means the conjunction "and." Then We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam.’ If it is said: The command to prostrate the angels was said to have been made for the creation of the children of Adam, so what is the point of his saying then We said and then for order and delay? It is said: According to the opinion of those who attribute creation and formation to Adam alone, this statement is correct. As for the opinion of those who attribute it to the offspring: there are answers to it: One of them is then in the sense of and, meaning: And we said to the angels, so it is not for order and follow-up. It was said that he meant then to tell you that we said to the angels, prostrate. It was said that it was presented and delayed, and its meaning is: We created you, meaning: Adam, then we said to the angels, prostrate to Adam, then we formed you. God Almighty said, So they prostrated, meaning the angels, except Iblis, he was not among those who prostrated, to Adam.
7:12: 12- He said, God Almighty, O Iblis: What prevented you from not prostrating when I commanded you? That is: What prevented you from prostrating? And not is redundant, as God Almighty says: And it is forbidden for a city which We have destroyed that they will not return. Al-Anbiya, 95. He said, Iblis responding, I am better than him, because You created me from fire and created him from clay, and fire is better and I am better than clay. Ibn Abbas said: The first person to make an analogy was Satan, but he made a mistake in making the analogy. So whoever makes an analogy with religion based on his own opinion, God will associate him with Satan. Ibn Sirin said: The sun was not worshipped except by analogy. Muhammad bin Jarir said: The wicked one thought that fire was better than clay, and he did not know that virtue is for the one to whom God has given virtue. God has given clay preference over fire in several ways, including: that the essence of clay is sobriety, dignity, forbearance, and patience, which is what prompted Adam, after the happiness that preceded him, to repent, be humble, and supplicate, so He gave him selection, repentance, and guidance. And the essence of fire is lightness, rashness, sharpness, and haughtiness, which is what prompted Satan, after the misery that preceded him, to be arrogant and persistent, so He gave him curse and misery. And because clay is the cause of gathering things and fire is the cause of their separation, and because soil is the cause of life, the life of trees and plants is through it, and fire is the cause of destruction.
7:13: 13- The Almighty said: He said, ‘Then descend from it,’ meaning: from Paradise. It was said: from the sky to the earth. He had the kingdom of the earth, so he brought him out of it to the islands of the sea and his throne was in the green sea. He does not enter the earth except in fear, in the form of a thief, like an old man with cloaks on him, who is terrified until he comes out of it. God Almighty says: It is not for you to be arrogant, by disobeying the command, in it, meaning: in Paradise. So it is not appropriate for an arrogant person who disobeys God Almighty’s command to reside in Paradise or Heaven: Then get out, for you are among the debased, among the humiliated. Debased means humiliation and disgrace.
7:14: 14- He said, Satan at that time, Give me respite, give me time and delay me so that I do not die, until the Day they are resurrected, from their graves, which is the final blast at the Hour of Resurrection. The wicked one wanted him not to taste death.
7:15: 15- He said, God Almighty, Indeed, you are among those granted respite, those who are delayed, and He explained the period of respite and the reprieve in another place, saying: Until the Day of the Appointed Time, Al-Hijr, 38, which is the first blast when all of the descendants will die.
7:16: 16- "He said, 'So because you led me astray', they differed about what it was said: It is a question meaning, so with what did you lead me astray? Then he began and said: "I will surely sit in wait for them" and it was said: what is the recompense, meaning: because you led me astray, I will surely bear a grudge against them. And it was said: It is what the source of the oath, its meaning is: because you led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them, like his saying, "because my Lord has forgiven me" Yasin, 27, meaning: because of the forgiveness of my Lord. The meaning is: By Your power over me and the penetration of Your authority over me. Ibn al-Anbari said: That is, in what You caused in my heart of error which was the reason for my fall from heaven. You led me astray: You led me astray from guidance. It was also said: You destroyed me. It was also said: You disappointed me. I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path, that is: I will sit for the children of Adam on Your straight path, which is Islam.
7:17: 17- Then I will come to them from before them, Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: From before them, meaning from the direction of the Hereafter, so I will make them doubt it, and from behind them, making them desire their worldly life, and from their right, making their religious affairs unclear to them, and from their left, making sins desirable to them. Atiyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: From before them, from the direction of their worldly life, meaning I will make it seem beautiful in their hearts, and from behind them, from the direction of the Hereafter, so I will say: There is no resurrection, no revival, no Paradise, no Hell, and from their right, from their good deeds, and from their left, from their bad deeds. Al-Hakam said: From before them means from the world, making it attractive to them. From behind them: from the Hereafter, discouraging them from it. From their right: from the truth, turning them away from it. From their left: from falsehood, making it attractive to them. Qatada said: He came to them from before them and informed them that there is no resurrection, nor Paradise, nor Hell. From behind them: from the matters of this world, making it attractive to them and calling them to it. From their right: from their good deeds, making them slow to reach it. From their left: making evil deeds and transgressions attractive to them and calling them to them. He came to you, O son of Adam, from every direction, except that He did not come to you from above you. He was not able to come between you and the mercy of God. Mujahid said: From before them and from their right from where they see, and from behind them and from their left where they do not see. Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning of His statement where they do not see means that they do not make mistakes, and where they do not see means that they do not know that they are making mistakes. And you will not find most of them grateful, believing. If it is said: How did the wicked one know that? It is said: He said it as a guess and he was right. God Almighty said: And Satan proved true about them his guess Saba’, 20.
7:18: 18- He said, God the Most High to Satan, Get out of it, disgraced and banished, meaning: shameful. The most severe disgrace is the one who is blamed and censured, so he is blameworthy and the one who blames him, he is blameworthy, like he walked walking. The one who is banished is the one who is banished and expelled. It is said: he drove him away, he drives him away, if he distanced him and expelled him. Ibn Abbas said: Disgraced means hated. Qatada said: Disgraced and banished means: cursed and banished. Al-Kalbi said: Disgraced: blameworthy, banished: excluded from Paradise and from all good. For those of them who follow you, from the children of Adam, I will surely fill Hell, the lam is the lam of the oath with you all, meaning: from you and your descendants and all the disbelievers of the descendants of Adam.
7:19: 19- And O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.
7:20: 20- "Then Satan whispered to them, that is, to them, and whispering is a talk that Satan casts into the heart of a person to make apparent to them that which was hidden from them of their private parts", that is, to show them what was covered and concealed from them of their private parts. It was said: The lam in it is the lam of consequence, and that is because Satan did not whisper this, but the consequence of their matter was that, which was the exposure of their private parts, as God Almighty said: "So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, so that he might become for them an enemy and a grief" Al-Qasas, 8. Then He explained the whispering, saying: "And he said", meaning: Satan to Adam and Eve, "Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree except that you should become angels", meaning: lest you should be, out of hatred that you should be angels from the angels who know good and evil, "or become of the immortals", of the remaining ones who do not die, as He said in another place: "Shall I guide you to the tree of immortality and a kingdom that will not decay?" Taha, 120.
7:21: 21- And he swore to them, 'Indeed, I am to you one of the sincere advisers,' meaning: he swore and took an oath to them. This is from the reciprocal verb that is specific to one person. Qatada said: He swore to them by God until he deceived them. A believer may be deceived by God, so he said: I was created before you and I am more knowledgeable than you, so follow me and I will guide you. Iblis was the first to swear falsely by God, so when he swore, Adam thought that no one would swear falsely by God, so he was deceived by him.
7:22: 22- He deceived them, meaning: he tricked them. It is said: So-and-so continued to deceive so-and-so, meaning: he continued to deceive him and speak to him with false, vain words. It was said that he lowered them from the position of obedience to the state of disobedience, and dangling does not occur except from a high place to a low place. Dangling means sending the bucket into the well. It is said: He dangled himself and he lowered others. Al-Azhari said: Its origin is the dangling of a thirsty person into the well to quench his thirst from the water and he does not find water, so he is dangling with deception, and deception means showing advice while concealing deception. So when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, Al-Kalbi said: When they ate from it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Before they swallowed, the punishment seized them. The punishment is that their private parts became apparent to them, and their clothing fell off them until each of them saw what was hidden from him of the private parts of the other, and they did not see that. Wahb said: Their clothing was of light. Qatada said: It was a nail that God dressed them with from the nail as a garment. So when they fell into sin, their private parts became apparent to them, so they felt ashamed. And they began, they came and began to mend, patch, glue, and join, over themselves from the leaves of Paradise, which are fig leaves, until it became like a garment. Al-Zajjaj said: They put one sheet of paper upon another to cover their private parts. It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Adam was a tall man, like a palm tree with much hair on his head. When he committed the sin, his private parts became apparent to him, but he could not see them. So he set out fleeing into Paradise. Then a tree from the trees of Paradise appeared to him and held him back by his hair. He said to it: ‘Let me go.’ It said: ‘I will not let you go.’ Then his Lord called out to him: ‘O Adam, do you want to flee from me?’ He said: ‘No, my Lord, but I felt shy before you.’” And their Lord called to them, ‘Did I not forbid you from that tree?’ meaning, eating from it, and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy. Muhammad ibn Qays said: His Lord called to him, O Adam, did you eat from it when I forbade you? He said, My Lord, Eve fed me. He said to Eve, Why did you feed it? She said, The serpent commanded me. He said to the serpent, Why did you command it? She said, Satan commanded me. So God Almighty said, “As for you, Eve, just as I caused the tree to bleed, you will bleed every month. As for you, O serpent, I will cut off your legs so that you will walk on your belly and face, and your head will be smashed to pieces by whoever meets you. As for you, O Satan, you are cursed and banished.”
7:23: 23- They said, 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.'
7:24: 24- He said, 'Go down, some of you as enemies to others, and you will have upon the earth a place of settlement and provision for a time.'
7:25: 25- "He said, 'Therein you will be revived', meaning you will live on earth, 'and therein you will die and from there you will be brought forth', meaning: from the earth you will be brought forth from your graves for the resurrection. Ibn 'Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read: "You will be brought forth", with the ta' open here and in Az-Zukhruf. Ya'qub agreed here, and Hamza and Al-Kisa'i added: And thus you will be brought forth at the beginning of Ar-Rum, and the rest read it with the ta' closed and the ra' open in them.
7:26: 26- O children of Adam, We have sent down upon you, meaning: We created for you clothing. It was said: He said: We sent down because clothing is only made from the plants of the earth, and plants are made from what comes down from the sky, so the meaning of His saying: We sent down, is: We sent down its causes. It was said: All the blessings of the earth are attributed to the blessings of the sky, as God Almighty said: And We sent down iron Surat Al-Hadid, 25, and iron is only extracted from the earth. The reason for the revelation of this verse is that during the pre-Islamic era, they used to circumambulate the House naked, and they used to say: We will not circumambulate in clothes in which we disobeyed God. So the men used to circumambulate naked during the day and the women at night. Qatada said: A woman would circumambulate and place her hand on her private parts and say: Today some or all of it appears, and whatever appears of it I do not permit. God Almighty commanded us to cover up, saying: We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts, covering your private parts. The singular form is saw’ah, which was named thus because its exposure would displease its wearer, so do not go around naked. And feathers, meaning wealth, according to Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi. It is said that a man is tarish if he is disheveled. It is also said that feathers are beauty, meaning that which they adorn themselves with of clothing. It is also said that it is clothing. And the clothing of righteousness, that is best. The people of Medina, Ibn Amir, and Al-Kisa’i read and clothing with the sin in the accusative case, in apposition to his statement clothing. The others read it with the nominative case, as a subject and its predicate is good. They made that a connection in the speech, and for this reason Ibn Mas’ud and Ubayy ibn Ka’b read and the clothing of righteousness, that is best. They differed about the garment of piety. Qatada and Al-Suddi said: The garment of piety is faith. Al-Hasan said: It is modesty because it encourages piety. Atiyah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is righteous work. And on the authority of Uthman bin Affan, he said: Good conduct. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: The clothing of piety is the fear of God. Al-Kalbi said: It is chastity. The meaning is: The clothing of piety is better for its owner if he wears it than the clothing created for him for adornment. Ibn Al-Anbari said: The clothing of piety is the first clothing, and he repeated it to inform us that covering the private parts is better than being naked during the circumambulation. Zaid bin Ali said: The clothing of piety is the tools with which one protects oneself in war, such as armor, helmet, forearm, and legs. It was said: The clothing of piety is wool and coarse clothes that the pious wear. This is from the signs of God that perhaps they will remember.
7:27: 27- "O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you, let not Satan lead you astray, as he expelled your parents, that is, as he tempted your parents Adam and Eve, expelling them, from Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts," so that each one could see the private parts of the other. "Indeed, he sees you, that is, Satan sees you, O children of Adam, he and his tribe," his soldiers. Ibn Abbas said: he and his children. Qatada said: his tribe: the jinn and the devils, "from where you do not see them," Malik bin Dinar said: An enemy who sees you and you do not see him is fierce in his dispute and his trouble, except for those whom God protects, "Indeed, We have made the devils allies, companions and helpers, for those who do not believe," and Al-Zajjaj said: Their authority over them increases their error as He said: "Indeed, We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, to incite them with [extreme] incitement." (Maryam 19:83)
7:28: 28- "And if they commit an immorality" Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: It is their circumambulation of the House naked. Ata' said: Polytheism and immorality are the names for every ugly act that reaches the peak of ugliness. "They said, 'We found our fathers doing it'", and it contains an implied meaning: And if they commit an immorality and are forbidden from it, they say, 'We found our fathers doing it'. It was said: And where did your fathers take it from? They said, "And God has commanded us to do it. Say, 'Indeed, God does not command immorality. Do you say about God that which you do not know?'"
7:29: 29- "Say: My Lord has commanded justice." Ibn Abbas said: There is no god but God. Ad-Dahhak said: With monotheism. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: With justice. And direct your faces at every masjid. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: It means direct your faces wherever you are in prayer, towards the Kaaba. Ad-Dahhak said: If the time for prayer comes and you are at a masjid, pray in it and none of you should say, I am praying in my masjid. It was said: Its meaning is make your prostration to God sincerely. And call upon Him and worship Him, devote your religion to Him, obedience and worship, as He began you, you will return. Ibn Abbas said: God Almighty began the creation of the children of Adam as believers and disbelievers, as He said: It is He who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer At-Taghabun, 2. Then He will return them on the Day of Resurrection as He created them, believers and disbelievers. Mujahid said: They will be resurrected as they died. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad bin Musa Al-Sayrafi told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Isa Al-Barti told us, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every servant will be resurrected in the state in which he died, the believer in his faith and the disbeliever in his disbelief. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They returned to his work with them. Saeed bin Jubair said: As it was written for you, so shall you be. Muhammad bin Kaab said: Whoever God began his creation with misery will end up in it even if he does the deeds of the people of happiness, just as Iblis used to do the deeds of the people of happiness and then ended up in misery. Whoever God began his creation with happiness will end up in it even if he does the deeds of the people of misery, just as the magicians used to do the deeds of the people of misery and then ended up in happiness. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Abu Ghassan told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, who said: I heard Sahl bin Saad say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A servant may do, in what people see, the deeds of the people of Paradise, even though he is one of the people of Hellfire. And he may do, in what people see, the deeds of the people of Hellfire, even though he is one of the people of Paradise. Actions are judged by their endings.” Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: Just as He began you and created you in this world when you were nothing, so you will return alive on the Day of Resurrection, as God Almighty said: As We began the first creation, We will repeat it Al-Anbiya’, 104. Qatada said: He began them from dust and to dust they will return, similar to what God Almighty said: From it We created you, and into it We will return you Taha, 55.
7:30: 30- The Almighty’s saying: A group He has guided, meaning God has guided you, and a group is right, “it is obligatory for them to go astray,” meaning: by prior will, they have taken the devils as allies instead of God and they think that they are guided, in it is evidence that the disbeliever who thinks that he is on the right path in his religion and the denier and the stubborn are the same.
7:31: 31- The Almighty said: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid, the commentators said: Banu Amir used to circumambulate the House naked, so God Almighty revealed: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid, meaning clothing. Mujahid said: What covers your private parts, even an cloak. Al-Kalbi said: Adornment is what covers the private parts at every mosque for circumambulation or prayer. And eat and drink, Al-Kalbi said: Banu Amir did not eat food during their pilgrimage except what was sufficient and did not eat fatty food, thus glorifying their pilgrimage. The Muslims said: We are more deserving of that, O Messenger of God. So God, the Almighty, revealed: And eat meaning meat and fat and drink milk but be not excessive, prohibiting what God has made lawful for you of meat and fat, Indeed, He does not like those who are excessive, who do that. Ibn Abbas said: Eat whatever you want and wear whatever you want as long as you do not miss two things: extravagance and conceit. Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Waqid said: God has gathered all of medicine in half a verse and said: Eat and drink but be not excessive.
7:33: 33- Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - such of them as are apparent and such as are concealed.' Meaning: circumambulating naked, what is apparent is the circumambulation of men during the day, and what is concealed is the circumambulation of women at night. It was said: It is adultery, secretly and publicly. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: I said: Did you hear this from Abdullah? He said: Yes, so he traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “No one is more jealous than God, and that is why He has forbidden indecencies, both apparent and hidden. No one loves praise more than God, and that is why He has praised Himself.” The Almighty said: And sin, meaning: guilt and disobedience. Ad-Dahhak said: The sin for which there is no punishment. Al-Hasan said: Sin: Alcohol. The poet said: I drank sin until my mind went astray, so sin takes away the mind And oppression, injustice and arrogance, without right, and that you associate with God that for which He has not sent down authority, as an argument and proof, and that you say about God that which you do not know, in the prohibition of cultivation and livestock, according to the statement of Muqatil. And others said, it is general in the prohibition of speaking about religion without certainty.
7:34: 34- And for every nation there is a term, a period, and food and drink. Ibn Abbas, Ata' and Al-Hasan said: It means a time for the punishment to descend upon them. So when their term comes, and their eating is cut off, they will not remain behind an hour nor will they precede it, meaning: nor will they advance. That was when they asked for the punishment, so this verse was revealed.
7:35: 35- The Almighty said: O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you, meaning: come to you. It was said: He meant all the messengers. Muqatil said: He meant by his saying: O children of Adam the polytheists of the Arabs and by the messengers Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone, reciting to you My verses, Ibn Abbas said: My obligations and My rulings, But whoever fears God and amends, meaning: fears polytheism and amends his actions.
