It was said: He purifies what is between him and his Lord, there will be no fear upon them, if people fear, nor will they grieve, meaning: if they grieve.
7:36: 36- And those who denied Our verses and were arrogant toward them, they were arrogant about believing in them, and arrogance was mentioned because every denier and disbeliever is arrogant. God Almighty said, Indeed, when it was said to them, ‘There is no god but God,’ they were arrogant As-Saffat, 35, Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
7:37: 37- So who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God assigns to Him a partner, or denies His signs, the Qur'an those will receive their share of the Book, meaning: their portion of what was written for them in the Preserved Tablet. They differed about it. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: What was written for them of punishment and decreed for them of black faces and blue eyes. Atiyah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was written for those who invent a lie against God that their face will be black. God the Most High said: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God - their faces will be blackened Az-Zumar, 60 Saeed bin Jubair and Mujahid said: What preceded them of misery and happiness. Ibn Abbas, Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: It means the deeds they did and for which good and evil were written, for which they will be rewarded. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: What was written for them of provisions, terms, ages, and deeds, when they were finished, Our messengers came to them, taking their souls, meaning the Angel of Death and his helpers, They said, meaning the messengers say to the disbeliever, Where were those you used to call upon, worship, other than God, a question of rebuke and reprimand, They said, ‘They have gone astray from us,’ they have become useless and departed from us, and they testified against themselves, they admitted when they witnessed death, that they were disbelievers.
7:38: 38- "He said, 'Enter among nations,' meaning: God will say to them on the Day of Resurrection, 'Enter among nations,' meaning: with groups, 'that have passed away,' that have passed away, 'before you of the jinn and mankind in the Fire,' meaning the disbelievers of the past nations, 'Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister,' meaning its sister in religion, not in lineage, so the Jews curse the Jews and the Christians curse the Christians, and every group curses its sister and the followers curse the leaders, and He did not say its brother because He meant the nation and the group, 'until when they overtake it,' meaning: they overtake and catch up and gather in the Fire, 'all together, the last of them will say,' Muqatil said: meaning the last of them to enter the Fire, and they are the followers, 'for their first,' meaning: for their first. Al-Suddi said: The people of the end of time will be those who associated partners with God. This is their religion. Our Lord, these are those who led us astray, meaning the leaders. So give them a double punishment in the Fire, meaning: double the punishment upon them. He said, God Almighty, for every double, meaning for the leaders and followers, double the punishment. But you do not know what punishment awaits each group of you. The majority read: but you do not know, and Abu Bakr read they do not know with the letter ya, meaning: the followers do not know what the leaders have, nor do the leaders know what the followers have.
7:39: 39- And the first of them said, meaning the leaders, to the last of them, meaning the followers, You had no superiority over us, because you disbelieved as we disbelieved, so we and you are equal in disbelief and equal in punishment, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn.
7:40: 40- Indeed, those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them, the gates of heaven will not be opened for them with a taa, Abu Amr lightened it, and with a yaa, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i lightened it, and the rest with a shaddah with a taa, for their supplications or their deeds. Ibn Abbas said: for their souls because they are evil and do not ascend, but rather fall with them to Sijjin. The gates of heaven are only opened for the souls of the believers, their supplications and their deeds, and they will not enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle, meaning: until a camel passes through the eye of a needle, and the tailor and the needle are the needle, and what is meant by it is: that they will never enter Paradise because if something is attached to something that is impossible, this indicates an emphasis on prevention, as it is said: I will not do such and such until a crow turns gray or tar turns white. He means I will never do it. And thus do We recompense the criminals.
7:41: 41- For them is a bed of Hellfire, meaning a mattress, and above them is a covering, meaning a blanket. It is the plural of ghashiyah, meaning what covered them and covered them. He means that the fire will surround them from every side, as God said, For them are canopies of Fire above them and canopies beneath them Az-Zumar, 16, And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
7:42: 42- And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We charge no soul except [with that within] its capacity, meaning: its ability and that which it is not burdened with or restricted by, Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
7:43: 43- And We will remove and bring out whatever is in their hearts of resentment, of deceit and enmity that was between them in this world, so We made them brothers on thrones facing each other, not envying each other for anything that God has given to one another, with rivers flowing beneath them. Al-Hasan narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: By God, it was revealed about us, the people of Badr: And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment, brothers on thrones facing each other. Ali, may God be pleased with him, also said: I hope that I, Uthman, Talha, and Al-Zubayr will be among those to whom God Almighty said, And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Salt bin Muhammad told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Al-Mutawakkil Al-Naji, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The believers will be saved from the Fire, and they will be detained on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and some of them will take revenge on others for the wrongs that were committed between them in this world, until when they are refined and purified, they will be permitted to enter Paradise. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of them will be guided to his home in Paradise more than he was to his home in this world.” Al-Suddi said about this verse: When the people of Paradise are led to Paradise, they will find a tree at its gate, at the base of its trunk are two springs. They will drink from one of them, and whatever rancor is in their hearts will be removed, and it is the pure drink. They will wash themselves from the other, and the freshness of bliss will flow upon them, and they will never be disheveled or disheveled after that, ever. That is, to this, meaning the path to Paradise. Sufyan al-Thawri said that its meaning is that He guided us to an action for which this is the reward. And we would not have been guided, Ibn Amir read were not guided without the waw, “had God not guided us. The messengers of our Lord have certainly brought the truth.” This is what the people of Paradise will say when they see what the messengers promised them with their own eyes. And it will be announced to them, ‘This is Paradise, which you have inherited because of what you used to do.’ It was said that this is the announcement when they see Paradise from afar. They will be announced, This is Paradise. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah al-Khatib told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Agharr, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, and on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: A caller will call out: You will be healthy and never fall ill, you will live and never die, you will live and never die, you will be young and never grow old, you will enjoy yourself and never be miserable. This is what he said: It will be announced to you, ‘This is Paradise, you have inherited it because of what you used to do.’ This is an authentic hadith narrated by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj on the authority of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Abd al-Rahman ibn Hamid on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri with this chain of transmission, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no one but that he has a place in Paradise and a place in Hell. As for the unbeliever, he inherits the believer’s place in Hell, and the believer inherits the unbeliever’s place in Paradise.”
7:44: 44- The Almighty said: And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, ‘We have found what our Lord promised us to be true,’ of reward, meaning truthfully, Have you found what your Lord promised to be true? of punishment, to be true? They will say, Yes. Al-Kisa’i read it with a kasra on the ‘ayn wherever it was, and the rest read it with a fatha, and they are two dialects. Then a crier will announce between them, meaning a crier will call out, so that both parties can hear, that the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers. The people of Medina, Basra, and Asim read: that lightly, curse, nominative, and the others read it with emphasis, the curse of God accusative on the wrongdoers, meaning: the disbelievers.
7:45: 45- Those who turn people away, that is, divert people, from the path of God, obedience to God, and seek to make it crooked, that is, they seek to make it crooked and deviant, that is, they nullify the path of God, deviating from the straight path. Ibn Abbas said: They pray to other than God, and they glorify what God has not glorified. And crookedness with a kasra on the ‘ayn in religion, command, land, and everything that is not upright, and with a fatha in everything that is upright, such as a wall, a spear, and the like. And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter.
7:46: 46- And between them is a veil, meaning: between Paradise and Hell. It was said: between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell is a veil, which is the wall that God Almighty mentioned in His statement: So He will set up between them a wall with a door Al-Hadid, 13. God Almighty says: And on the heights are men. Al-A’raf is the wall between Heaven and Hell. It is the plural of ‘arf, which is the name for a high place. From this comes the word ‘arf’ the rooster’s ‘arf’ because it is higher than the rest of its body. Al-Suddi said: This wall was called ‘A’raf because its people know people. They differed about the men whom God spoke about on the heights. Hudhayfah and Ibn Abbas said: They are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, so their bad deeds prevented them from entering Paradise, and their good deeds prevented them from entering Hell. They will stand there until God decides what He wills regarding them, then they will enter Paradise by the grace of His mercy, and they will be the last to enter Paradise. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, who said: Saeed ibn Jubayr said, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: People will be brought to account on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever’s good deeds outweigh his bad deeds by one will enter Paradise, and whoever’s bad deeds outweigh his good deeds by one will enter Hell. Then he recited the words of God the Most High: “But whose scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful. But whose scales are light - it is they who have lost themselves.” Al-A’raf 8-9. Then he said: The scale will be lightened by the weight of a grain or it will tip the scales. He said: And whoever’s good deeds and bad deeds are equal, he will be among the people of A’raf. They will stand on the Bridge, then they will recognize the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. When they look at the people of Paradise, they will call out, “Peace be upon you.” And when they turn their eyes to the people of Hell, they will say, Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people. As for the people of good deeds, they will be given a light with which they will walk before them and on their right, and every servant on that day will be given a light. When they come to the Bridge, God will take away the light of every hypocrite, male and female. So when the people of Paradise see what the hypocrites have encountered, they will say, Our Lord, perfect for us our light. As for the people of A'raf, the light was not taken away from before them, and their evil deeds prevented them from continuing, so greed remained in their hearts because the light was not taken away from before them. Then God says: They did not enter it while they were greedy, and greed was the light before them, then they entered Paradise, and they were the last of the people of Paradise to enter. Shurahbil bin Saad said: The people of Al-A'raf are people who went out to fight without their fathers' permission. Muqatil narrated it in his interpretation, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: They are men who fought in the cause of God [disobeying their fathers and were killed, so they were freed from the Fire by being killed in the cause of God], and they were prevented from Paradise because of their fathers' disobedience, so they are the last to enter Paradise. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid: They are people who were pleased with one of their parents but not the other. They will be detained on Al-A’raf until God judges between the creation, then they will enter Paradise. Abdul Aziz bin Yahya Al-Kinani said: They are those who died during the period and did not change their religion. It was also said: They are the children of the polytheists. Al-Hasan said: They are the people of virtue among the believers who ascended to the heights and look at the people of Paradise and the people of Hell together, and they see the conditions of the two groups. God the Almighty says: They will recognize each by their mark, meaning they will recognize the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces and the people of Hell by the blackness of their faces. “And they will call out to the companions of Paradise, ‘Peace be upon you,’” meaning, when they see the people of Paradise, they will say, “Peace be upon you.” They will not enter it, meaning, the companions of Al-A’raf will not enter Paradise, while they are yearning, to enter it. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: God did not make that yearning in them except as an honor [meaning] for them. Al-Hasan said that He who made yearning in their hearts will lead them to what they yearn for.
7:47: 47- And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they seek refuge in God, they say, 'Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people,' meaning: the disbelievers in the Fire.
7:48: 48- And the companions of the A'raf will call out to men who were great in this world from the people of Hell, whom they will recognize by their mark. They will say, What avail you is your multitude, in this world of wealth and children, and what you were arrogant, about faith. Al-Kalbi said: They will call out while they are on the wall: O Walid bin Al-Mughira, O Abu Jahl bin Hisham, O so-and-so, then they will look at Paradise and see in it the poor and weak whom they used to mock, such as Salman, Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal and their likes. Then the companions of the A'raf will say to those disbelievers:
7:49: 49- Are these the ones you swore you swore that God will not grant them mercy meaning: you swore that they will not enter Paradise. Then it will be said to the people of A'raf: Enter Paradise, no fear shall there be concerning you, nor shall you grieve. And there is another saying: When the people of A'raf say to the people of Hell what they say, the people of Hell will say to them: Those people have entered Paradise and you have not. So they taunt them for that, and swear that they will enter Hell. Then the angels who detained the people of A'raf will say: O people of Hell, you swore that God would not grant them mercy. Then the angels will say to the people of A'raf: Enter Paradise, no fear shall there be concerning you, nor shall you grieve. So they enter Paradise.
7:50: 50- The Almighty said: And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, ‘Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you,’ meaning, pour out on us some of the food God has provided you from Paradise. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When the people of Al-A’raf reached Paradise, the people of Hell desired relief and said: O Lord, we have relatives among the people of Paradise, so give us permission so that we may see them and speak to them. So they will look at their relatives in Paradise and the bliss they are in and will recognize them, but the people of Paradise will not recognize them because of the blackness of their faces. Then the people of Hell will call out to the people of Paradise by their names and inform them of their relatives: Pour upon us some water or from what God has provided you. They will say: Indeed, God has forbidden them to the disbelievers. Meaning: water and food.
7:51: 51- Those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion which is what Satan has made attractive to them of prohibiting the Bahira and its sisters, and the wailing and clapping around the House, and all the other reprehensible traits that they used to do in the days of ignorance. It was said: their religion, meaning their festival, and the worldly life has deceived them, so today We will forget them, We will leave them in the fire, as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs meaning as they left work for the meeting of this Day of theirs, and they used to deny Our verses.
7:52: 52- And We have certainly brought them a Book, meaning the Qur’an, which We have detailed, “which We have explained,” with knowledge, from Us, of what is good for them, as guidance and mercy, meaning We made the Qur’an a guide and a mercy, for a people who believe.
7:53: 53- Do they await meaning: Do they wait, for anything but its interpretation? Mujahid said: Its reward. Al-Suddi said: Its consequence. Its meaning: Do they await anything but what their affair will come to, in torment and their destination in the Fire. On the Day its interpretation comes meaning its reward and what their affair will come to, those who forgot it before will say, 'The messengers of our Lord have come with the truth,' they acknowledged it when acknowledgment would not benefit them, Do we have any intercessors today to intercede for us or shall we be returned to the world, and do other than what we used to do? They have lost themselves, they destroyed themselves with torment, and what they used to invent has gone astray [and become void], from them.
7:54: 54- The Almighty’s saying, Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, meaning in the amount of six days because a day is from sunrise to sunset, and on that day there was no day, no sun, and no sky. It was said: Six days are like the days of the Hereafter, and each day is like a thousand years. It was also said: Like the days of this world. Saeed bin Jubair said: God, the Almighty, was able to create the heavens and the earth in a moment and an instant, so He created them in six days [to teach] His creation to be certain and take their time in matters. It was stated in the hadith: Patience is from God, and haste is from Satan. “Then He rose over the Throne.” Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: He settled down. Abu Ubaidah said: He ascended. The Mu’tazilah interpreted istiwa’ to mean domination. As for the Sunnis, they say: istiwa’ on the Throne is an attribute of God, the Most High, without how. A man must believe in it, and knowledge of it is left to God, the Almighty and Majestic. A man asked Malik ibn Anas about his statement: The Most Gracious established Himself firmly on the Throne (Ta-Ha 20:5), how did He rise? He lowered his head for a long time, and his eyes were watery, then he said: istiwa’ is not unknown, and how is not rational, and belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation, and I do not think you are anything but astray. Then he ordered him to be taken out. It was narrated on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, al-Layth ibn Sa’d, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, and other Sunni scholars regarding these verses that came in the ambiguous attributes: Leave them as they came without asking how. The throne in the language: is the bed. It was said: it is what is high and provides shade, and from it is the throne of the vineyards. It was said: the throne is the king. The night overtakes the day. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr, and Ya'qub read: Yaghshi with emphasis here and in Surat Ar-Ra'd, and the rest with emphasis, meaning: the night comes over the day and covers it, and there is an omission in it, meaning: and the day overtakes the night, and he did not mention it because the speech indicates it, and he mentioned in another verse, saying: He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night (al-Zumar 39:5), pursuing it hastily, meaning: quickly, and that is because if one of them follows the other and succeeds it, it is as if he is pursuing it. And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected, Ibn 'Amir read them all with the nominative case as the subject and predicate, and the rest with the accusative case, and likewise in Surat An-Nahl in apposition to His statement: He created the heavens and the earth, meaning: He created these things subjected, meaning: submissive, "by His command. Is not His the creation and the command?" His is the creation because [He created them], and His is the command, He commands in His creation what He wills. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: God distinguished between creation and command, so whoever combines them has committed disbelief. Blessed be God, meaning: God is exalted and glorified. It was also said: He is exalted. And blessed is the elevated. It was also said: Blessed is derived from barakah, which means growth and increase, meaning: blessing is acquired and attained by remembering Him. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He came with every blessing. Al-Hasan said: The blessing comes from Him. It was also said: Blessed is sanctified. And sanctification is purity. It was also said: Blessed be God, meaning: In His name everything is blessed. The scholars said: The meaning of this [attribute] is established and lasting as long as it has not ceased and will not cease. The origin of blessing is establishment. It is said: Blessed be God, but it is not said: Blessed or blessed, because it was not intended to be confirmed. Lord of the Worlds.
7:55: 55- Call upon your Lord humbly, in humility and submission, and in secret, meaning secretly. Al-Hasan said that there is a seventy-fold difference between a secret supplication and a public supplication. The Muslims used to strive hard in supplication, but no voice was heard from them, except for a whisper between them and their Lord. This is because God, the Exalted, says, Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret. And God mentioned a righteous servant and was pleased with his action, saying, When he called upon his Lord a secret call [Surat Maryam]. Indeed, He does not like transgressors. It was said: Transgressors in supplication. Abu Majlaz said: They are the ones who ask about the homes of the prophets, peace be upon them. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani told us, al-Qasim ibn Ja`far al-Hashemi told us, Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Lulu`i told us, Abu Dawud al-Sijistani told us, Musa ibn Ismail told us, Hammad, meaning ibn Salamah, told us, al-Jariri told us, on the authority of Abu Na`amah, “that Abdullah ibn Mughaffal heard his son say: O God, I ask You for the white palace on the right of Paradise when I enter it. He said: O my son, ask God for Paradise and seek refuge from the Fire, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There will be people in this nation who will go to extremes in purification and supplication.” It was said: He meant by it aggression by loudly shouting [and screaming]. Ibn Jurayj said: Among aggression is raising the voice and calling out with supplication and screaming. We narrated on the authority of Abu Musa who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, invaded Khaybar, the people overlooked a valley and raised their voices in glorification. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. Rather, you are calling upon One who hears and is near.” Atiyah said: They are those who call down curses upon the believers in matters that are not permissible, and they say: O God, disgrace them, O God, curse them.
7:56: 56- And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation, meaning do not cause corruption on it through sins and calling to other than obedience to God after God has reformed it by sending the messengers and explaining the Sharia, and calling to obedience to God. This is the meaning of the statement of Al-Hasan, Al-Suddi, Al-Dahhak, and Al-Kalbi. Atiyah said: Do not disobey on earth, lest God withhold the rain and destroy the crops because of your disobedience. So this is the meaning of his statement: after its reformation, meaning after God’s reformation of it with rain and fertility. And call upon Him in fear and hope meaning fear of what He has of forgiveness and reward. Ibn Jurayj said: Fear of justice and hope of bounty. Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good and he did not say near. Saeed bin Jubair said: Mercy here means reward, so the description refers to the meaning and not the wording, like His statement: And when relatives, orphans, and the needy are present at the division, provide for them from it (An-Nisa’: 8) and he did not say from it because he meant inheritance and money. Al-Khalil bin Ahmed said: “Qarib and Ba’id in the language are: masculine and feminine, singular and plural.” Abu Omar bin Al-Ala said: “Qarib in the language can mean closeness and distance. Arabs say: This woman is close to you if it means kinship, and ‘Qarib to you’ if it means distance.”
7:57: 57- The Almighty’s saying: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings. He read it with the letter ba’ and with a damma and a sukoon on the sheen here and in Al-Furqan, Surat Al-Furqan, and Surat An-Naml, and it means: that they herald rain, as evidenced by the Almighty’s saying: The winds are good tidings. (al-Rum 30:46) [And Hamza Al-Kasani read (Nashra) and the letter noon and with a fatha, and it is the good, soft wind. God Almighty said] And the spreaders spread out. (al-Mursalat 77:3) Ibn Amir read with a damma on the letter noon and a sukoon on the sheen, and the others read with a damma on the letter noon and the sheen, the plural of nashur, like sabur, rasool, and rusul, meaning scattered, and they are the winds that blow from every direction. In front of His mercy, meaning: before the rain. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Thiqa told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Thabit Qais, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: A strong wind overtook the people on the road to Mecca while Umar was on Hajj, and it became intense. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said to those around him: What has reached you regarding the wind? They did not respond to him with anything. Then I was informed of what [Umar had asked about regarding the wind], so I urged my mount until I caught up with Umar, may God be pleased with him, and I was in the back of the people. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, I was informed that you asked about the wind, and I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The wind is from the spirit of God, it brings mercy and torment, so do not curse it, and ask God for its good, and seek refuge in Him from its evil. And it was narrated by Al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Al-Zuhri with his chain of transmission. Until when it carries the winds, heavy clouds with rain, We drive it and the metaphor is returned to the clouds, to a dead land meaning: to a dead land in need of water. It was said: its meaning is to revive a dead land with no vegetation in it, So We sent down with it meaning: with the clouds. It was said: to that dead land water meaning: rain, “And We brought forth with it all kinds of fruits. Thus do We bring forth the dead,” and evidence for reviving the earth after its death was given by reviving the dead, that you may remember. Abu Hurairah and Ibn Abbas said: When all the people die at the first blast, God will send upon them rain like the semen of men from water under the throne called the water of life, so they will grow in their graves like the plants of crops until their bodies are fully formed, He will breathe the spirit into them, then He will cast sleep upon them and they will sleep in their graves, then they will be gathered at the second blast while they find the taste of sleep in their heads and eyes, so at that time they will say: Woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleep? (Ya-Sin 36:52).
7:58: 58- The Almighty said: And the good land - its vegetation comes forth by permission of its Lord. This is a parable that God Almighty has given for the believer and the disbeliever. The example of the believer is like that of the good land, rain falls on it and its vegetation comes forth by permission. And that which is bad, meaning the salty land, whose vegetation does not come forth except with difficulty. Abu Ja`far read it with the fatha on the kaf, and the others read it with the kasra, meaning: with a little difficulty, with effort and hardship. The first is like the believer who, when he hears, calls upon it, understands it, and benefits from it. The second is like the disbeliever who hears the Qur’an but it does not affect him, like a filthy land in which the effect of rain is not apparent. Thus do We explain the signs We make them clear, for a people who are grateful. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Al-Ala told us, Hammad bin Usamah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Abu Musa, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The example of what God has sent me with of guidance and knowledge is like abundant rain falling on a land. Some of it was accepted by the water and produced abundant grass and herbs. Some of it was barren and held the water, so God benefited the people with it, so they drank, gave water to drink, and planted crops. And some of it was reached by land that was nothing but flat plains that neither held water nor produced grass. This is the example of one who understands the religion of God and what God has sent me with benefits him, so he learns and teaches, and the example of one who does not raise his head with that and does not accept the guidance of God with which I was sent.”
7:59: 59- The Almighty said: Indeed, We sent Noah to his people. He is Noah, son of Lamech, son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, who is Idris, and he is the first prophet sent after Idris. He was a carpenter whom God sent to his people when he was fifty years old. Ibn Abbas said: Forty years old. It was said: He was sent when he was two hundred and fifty years old. Muqatil said: One hundred years old. Ibn Abbas said: He was called Noah because of how much he mourned for himself. They differed about the reason for his wailing. Some of them said: Because he called for the destruction of his people. It was said: Because he consulted his Lord about his son Canaan. It was said: Because he passed by a leprous dog and said: Go away, you ugly one. So God Almighty revealed to him: Did you find fault with me or did you find fault with the dog? So he said, to his people, O my people, worship God; you have no god other than Him. Abu Ja`far and Al-Kisa’i read of a god other than Him, with a kasra on the ra’ wherever it was, describing the god, and Hamza agreed with him in Surat Fatir 35:Is there a creator other than God? Fatir 3. The others read with a raised ra’ as an introduction, meaning: You have no god other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you, if you do not believe, the punishment of a tremendous Day.
7:60: 60- The leaders of his people said, ‘Indeed, we see that you are in clear error’ error and deviation from the truth, clear clear.
7:61: 61- Noah said, ‘O my people, there is no error in me.’ He did not say there is no error, because the meaning of error or the presentation of the verb is but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.
7:62: 62- I informed you Abu Amr read: I informed you with the lightening as it was from innovation. For His saying: I have informed you [Al-A'raf-93] the messages of my Lord, [so that he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord and the others read with the emphasis from the conveying for His saying the Most High: Convey what has been revealed to you [Al-Ma'idah-67], the messages of my Lord] and I advise you, it is said I advised him and I advised him. And advice is to want for others the good that he wants for himself, and I know from God what you do not know, that His punishment is not averted from the criminal people.
7:63: 63- Or are you surprised an interrogative alif that entered the conjunction waw, that there came to you a reminder from your Lord Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: It was said: a statement. It was said: a message. To a man from among you to warn you of the punishment of God if you do not believe and that you may fear God, that is, so that you may fear God, and that you may receive mercy so that you may receive mercy.
7:64: 64- So they denied him meaning: they denied Noah, so We saved him from the flood, and those with him in the ark, in the ship, "and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people" meaning: disbelievers. Ibn Abbas said: Abbas: Their hearts were blinded to knowing God. It was said: Blindness and the blind are like green and green. Muqatil said: They were protected from the punishment descending upon them, which is drowning.
7:65: 65- The Almighty said: And to Aad [We sent] their brother Hud, meaning: And We sent to Aad - who is Aad bin Aws bin Aram bin Sam bin Noah, peace be upon him - and they are the first Aad, their brother in lineage, not in religion, Hud, who is Hud bin Abdullah bin Rabah bin Al-Jaloud bin Aad bin Aws. Ibn Ishaq said: Hud bin Shalih bin Arphaxad bin Sam bin Noah “He said, ‘O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. Will you not then fear Him?’” Do you not fear His vengeance?
7:66: 65 - "The leaders of his people who disbelieved said, 'Indeed, we see you, O Hud, in foolishness, in stupidity and ignorance.' Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: You call us to a religion that we do not know, 'and indeed, we think you are among the liars,' that you are the Messenger of God to us.
7:67: 67- He said, Hud, O my people, there is no foolishness in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.
7:68: 68 - I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am to you a trustworthy adviser. An adviser who calls you to repentance, trustworthy in conveying the message. Al-Kalbi said: I was trustworthy among you before today.
7:69: Or do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you, meaning himself, "to warn you. And remember when He made you successors", meaning on the earth, after the people of Noah, meaning: after their destruction, and increased you in stature, meaning: height and strength. Al-Kalbi and Al-Suddi said: The height of the tall among them was one hundred cubits, and the height of the short among them was sixty cubits. Abu Hamza Al-Thamali said: Seventy cubits. Wahb said: The head of one of them was like a great dome, and the man's eye was where hyenas hatched, as were their nostrils. So remember the favors of God, the blessings of God, the singular of which is to like ma'i and am'a, qaf and aqfa, and its equivalent is ana'a al-layl, the singular of which is ana and ana'a, that you may be successful.
7:70: 70 - They said, ‘Have you come to us to make us worship God alone and abandon what our fathers used to worship? ’ of idols, Then bring us what you promise us, of punishment, if you should be of the truthful.
7:71: 71 - He said, Hud, There has come down upon you from your Lord an abomination, meaning: a punishment, and the sin is replaced by the zay, and anger, meaning: wrath, Do you argue with me about names you have named, that you have created, you and your fathers, the commentators said: They had idols that they worshipped and they named them with different names, for which God has sent down no authority, argument and proof, so wait, the descent of the punishment, I am with you among those who wait.
7:72: 72- So We saved him, meaning Hud when the punishment was coming down, and those with him by mercy from Us, and We eliminated the last of those who denied Our signs, meaning: We uprooted them and destroyed them all, and they were not believers. The story of Ad, as mentioned by Ibn Ishaq and others, was that they were a people who settled in Yemen and their dwellings were in Al-Ahqaf, which is a sandy area between Oman and Hadhramaut. They had spread throughout the land and conquered its people by virtue of the strength that God Almighty had given them. They were the owners of idols that they worshipped, an idol called Sada, an idol called Samud, and an idol called Al-Haba. So God sent to them Hud as a prophet, and he was from the most noble of them in lineage and the best of them in rank. He commanded them to believe in the oneness of God and to refrain from oppressing people, and he did not command them to do anything else. They denied him and said, Who is stronger than us? So they built factories and attacked with the attack of tyrants. When they did that, God withheld the rain from them for three years until it exhausted them. At that time, when a calamity befell the people and they sought relief, their request was to God Almighty at His Sacred House in Mecca, both Muslims and polytheists. Many different people would gather in Mecca, with different religions, and all of them respected Mecca. The people of Mecca at that time were the Amalekites, and they were called Amalek because their father was Amalek bin Ladha bin Sam bin Noah. The leader of the Amalekites at that time in Mecca was a man called Muawiyah bin Bakr, and Muawiyah’s mother was Kalhada bint Al-Khaibari, a man from Aad. When the rain dried up in Aad and they were struggling, they said, Prepare a delegation from among you to Mecca so that they may bring rain for you. So they sent Qayl bin Anz, Luqaym bin Hazal from Hazil, Uqayl bin Sandayn bin Aad Al-Akbar, Murthad bin Saad bin Ufair, who was a Muslim who concealed his Islam, and Jalhamah bin Al-Khaibari, the maternal uncle of Muawiyah bin Bakr. Then they sent Luqman bin Aad Al-Asghar bin Sandayn bin Aad Al-Akbar, and each of these men set out with a group of his people until the number of their delegation reached seventy men. When they arrived in Mecca, they went to Muawiyah bin Bakr, who was outside Mecca, outside the sanctuary. He accommodated them and honored them. They were his maternal uncles and in-laws. They stayed with him for a month, drinking wine and being sung to by two locusts, two slave girls belonging to Muawiyah bin Bakr. Their journey was a month and their stay was a month. When Muawiyah bin Bakr saw how long they had stayed, and that their people had sent them to seek help from the calamity that had befallen them, he was upset by that and said, “My maternal uncles and in-laws have perished and these people are staying with me and they are my guests. By God, I do not know what to do with them. I am ashamed to order them to go out to do what they were sent to do, so that they may think that they were his two slave girls.” They said, “Recite poetry so that we may sing to them, without knowing who said it. Perhaps that will move them.” Muawiyah bin Bakr said: Oh Qayl, woe to you! Get up and sleep, perhaps God will give us rain. And he watered the land of Aad, for Aad have become unable to make clear their speech. From extreme thirst, we do not expect it from the old man or the young man. Their women were fine, their women became my days And if the beasts come to them openly, do not fear the arrows of the enemy. And you are here, whatever you desire, day and night, to the fullest. Your delegation is worse than the delegation of a people who did not receive greetings and peace. When the two locusts sang to them, some of them said to one another: O people, your people have sent you to seek help from you because of the calamity that has befallen them, and you have delayed them, so enter this sanctuary and ask for rain for your people. Then Marthad bin Sa`d bin `Ufair, who had secretly believed in Hud, said: By God, you will not be given rain by your prayers, but if you obey your Prophet and turn to your Lord, you will be given rain. So he declared his Islam at that time and said: Aad disobeyed their messenger, so they spent the night thirsty and the sky did not provide them with water. They have an idol called Samoud, which is opposed by Sada and Al-Haba. The Messenger showed us the path of righteousness, so we saw the guidance and the blindness was dispelled. And the God of Hood is my God. In God we rely and hope. They said to Muawiyah ibn Bakr: Detain Murthad ibn Sa`d from us and do not let him come with us to Mecca, for he has followed the religion of Hud and abandoned our religion. Then they went out to Mecca to pray for rain for `Ad. When they returned to Mecca, Murthad ibn Sa`d left Mu`awiyah’s house until he reached them before they could pray to God for anything they had gone out for. When he reached them, he stood up to pray to God, and there was a delegation of `Ad praying. He said: O God, give me what I ask for alone and do not involve me in anything that the delegation of `Ad is asking You for. Qayl ibn `Anz was the head of the delegation of `Ad. The delegation of `Ad said: O God, give Qayl what he asked for and make our request his request. And Luqman bin Aad, who was the master of Aad, had stayed behind from the delegation of Aad when they called, until when they finished their call, he stood up and said: O God, I have come to You alone in my need, so grant me my request, and he asked God for a long life, so he lived seven years. And Qil bin Anaz said when he called: O our God, if Hud was truthful, then give us rain, for we have perished, so God created three clouds, white, red and black, then a caller from the clouds called to him O Qil, choose for yourself and your people from the clouds whatever you wish, so Qil said: I have chosen the black cloud, for it is the cloud that produces the most water, so a caller called to him: You have chosen ashes and ash that will not leave a single one of the people of Aad, and God, the Most High, drove the black cloud that Qil had chosen with what was in it of vengeance to Aad until it emerged upon them from a valley of theirs called Al-Mughith, so when they saw it, they were happy and said: This is a cloud that will give us rain, God the Most High says: Rather, it is that which you hastened. There is a wind in it, a painful punishment. It destroys everything by the command of its Lord. Al-Ahqaf 24-25 That is, everything it passes by. The first to see what was in it and know that it was a deadly wind was a woman from Ad called Muhaddad. When she realized what was in it, she cried out and then fainted. When she did not recover, they asked her, What did you see? She said, "I saw the wind in it like meteors of fire, in front of which were men leading it. So God subjected it to them for seven nights and eight days in succession, and it did not leave anyone from Ad except that they perished. Hud and the believers with him secluded themselves in a pen, and nothing of the wind affected him or those with him except what softened the skin and pleased the souls. It would pass by some of Ad with their camels, carrying them between the sky and the earth and crushing them with stones. The delegation of Ad left Mecca until they passed by Muawiyah ibn Bakr and alighted upon him. While they were with him, a man came on a she-camel on a moonlit night, the third evening of the calamity of Ad, and told them the report. They asked him, "Where did you leave Hud and his companions? He said, I left them on the seashore." It seemed that they doubted what he had told them. Hazilah bint Bakr said, "By the Lord of the Kaaba, he is telling the truth." They mentioned that when Marthad bin Saad, Luqman bin Aad, and Qayla bin Anz were called in Mecca, it was said to them: I have given you your desires, so choose for yourselves, except that there is no way to immortality, and death is inevitable. So Marthad said: O God, give me truthfulness and righteousness, and he was given that, and Luqman said: O Lord, give me a lifespan. So he was told: Choose. So Umar chose seven eagles. He would take the chick when it hatched from its eggs and take the male from it for its sustenance, until it died, he would take another one. He continued to do that until he reached the seventh. Each eagle lived eighty years, and the last of them was Labd. So when Labd died, Luqman died with him. As for what was said, he said: I choose to be afflicted with what afflicted my people, so it was said to him: It is destruction, so he said: I do not care, I have no need to remain after them, so he was afflicted with what afflicted the ‘Aad of punishment, so he perished. Al-Suddi said: God sent the barren wind to the people of Aad. When it approached them, they looked at the camels and the men, and the wind was blowing them between the sky and the earth. When they saw it, they rushed to their homes, entered them, and closed their doors. Then the wind came and tore off their doors, entered upon them, and destroyed them in them. Then it drove them out of their homes. When God destroyed them, He sent black birds upon them, and they carried them to the sea and threw them into it. It was narrated that God Almighty commanded the wind to throw sand upon them, and they were under the sand for seven nights and eight days, groaning under the sand. Then He commanded the wind to remove the sand from them, and it carried them and threw them into the sea. No wind ever came out except with a measure, except on that day, when it rebelled against the keepers and overcame them, and they did not know how much its measure was. In the hadith: It came out to them about the size of a tear in a ring, and it was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: The grave of Hud, peace be upon him, is in Hadhramaut on a red sand dune. Abdul Rahman bin Sabit said: Between the corner, the station, and Zamzam are the graves of ninety-nine prophets, and the graves of Hud, Shuaib, Salih, and Ishmael, peace be upon them, are in that spot. It is narrated that when a prophet’s people perished, he and the righteous with him would come to Mecca to worship God there until they died. A
7:73: 73- The Almighty said: And to Thamud We sent their brother Salih, and he is Thamud bin Aaber bin Aram bin Salem bin Noah, and here he meant the tribe. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: Thamud was named so because of its scarcity of water, and thamud means little water. Their dwellings were in the rocks between the Hijaz and the Levant to Wadi al-Qura. Their brother Salih means: We sent to Thamud their brother in lineage, not in religion, Salih, and he is Salih ibn Ubayd ibn Asif ibn Mashih ibn Ubayd ibn Khadir ibn Thamud. “He said, ‘O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord,’ an argument from your Lord that I am truthful. ‘This is the she-camel of God,’ he added it to him as a preference and specification, as one says the House of God. ‘For you is a sign,’ an accusative in the state of state. ‘So leave her to graze,’ the grass, ‘in the land of God and do not touch her with harm,’ do not harm her by hamstringing her, ‘or a painful punishment will seize you.’”
7:74: 74- And remember when He made you successors after 'Aad and settled you, He settled you and settled you, in the land, taking for yourself palaces from its plains and carving out homes in the mountains, they used to dig homes in the mountains, so in the summer they would live in mud houses, and in the winter in mountain houses. It was said: They used to carve homes in the mountains because mud houses did not last for their entire lives due to their long lives, So remember the favors of God and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption, and corruption is the most severe form of corruption.
7:75: 75- The chiefs said, Ibn Amir read: And the chiefs said with the letter waw those who were arrogant among his people, meaning the nobles and leaders and those who were too proud to believe in Salih, to those who were oppressed, meaning the followers, to those among them who believed, meaning: the disbelievers said to the believers, Do you know that Salih is a messenger from his Lord, to you, They said, Indeed, we are believers in that with which he has been sent."
7:76: 76- Those who were arrogant said, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in that in which you have believed.’ They are deniers.
7:77: 77- So they hamstrung the she-camel. Al-Azhari said: Hamstringing is cutting the camel's heel, then slaughtering was made hamstringing because the one who slaughters the camel hamstrings it and then slaughters it. And they were insolent toward the command of their Lord. Insolence is exaggeration in falsehood. It is said: Ata ya'tawa 'atwan if they were arrogant. The meaning is that they disobeyed God and abandoned His command regarding the she-camel and denied their prophet. And they said, 'O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, meaning: of punishment, if you should be of the messengers.
7:78: 78- So the earthquake seized them, which is the earthquake and movement of the earth, and they were destroyed by the shout and the earthquake, and they became in their homes, it was said: He meant the homes, and it was said: He meant in their land and their town, and that is why he used the singular form of home, prostrate, motionless and dead. It was said: They fell on their faces, dead to the last one.
7:79: 79 - So he turned away, Salih turned away, from them and said, ‘O my people, I have indeed conveyed to you the message of my Lord and given you sincere advice, but you do not like sincere advisers.’ If it is said: How did he address them by saying, I have indeed conveyed to you the message of my Lord and given you sincere advice, after they had perished in the earthquake? It was said: As the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed the infidels killed at Jarr when he threw them into the well, and he began to call them by their names and the names of their fathers: “Is it easy for you that you obeyed God and His Messenger? We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?” Umar said: O Messenger of God, what speaks of bodies that have no souls in them? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are not more attentive to what I say than they are, but they do not respond.” It was said: He addressed them to be a lesson to those who came after them. It was said: There is an inversion in the verse, and its interpretation is: So he turned away from them and said, O my people, I have conveyed to you the message of my Lord. Then the earthquake seized them. The story of Thamud, as mentioned by Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Wahb and others, was that ‘Aad perished and their rule came to an end. Thamud was inhabited after them, and they were made successors on the earth. They entered it and multiplied and inhabited it, until one of them would build a dwelling from mud and it would collapse while the man was still alive. When they saw that, they took houses from the mountains. They were in a comfortable life, so they rebelled and spread corruption on the earth and worshipped other than God. So God sent him to them as a young boy, and he called them to God until he became old and dishonored, and only a few of them followed him, who were weak. When Salih insisted on calling upon them and conveying the message and warned them a lot and frightened them, they asked him to show them a sign that would confirm what he was saying. So he said to them: What sign do you want? They said: Come out with us tomorrow to our festival. They had a festival in which they would go out with their idols on a specific day of the year, and you would call upon your god and we would call upon our gods. If you are answered, we will follow you, and if we are answered, you will follow us. Salih said to them: Yes. So they went out with their idols to their festival, and Salih went out with them. They called upon their idols and asked them that Salih would not be answered in anything he called upon. Then Junda’ bin Amr bin Hawas, who was at that time the master of Thamud, said: O Salih, bring us out of this rock - a separate rock in a corner of the stone called Al-Kathbah - a she-camel with a hollow, bare, and young camel - and a she-camel is like a yacht among camels - and if you do, we will believe you and have faith in you. Salih took their covenant from them: If you do, you will believe in me and have faith in me. They said: Yes. So Salih prayed two rak’ahs and called upon his Lord, and the rock gave birth as a pregnant woman gives birth to her young. Then the plateau moved and split open, revealing a she-camel with a hollow, bare, and young camel, as they described. None knows what was between its sides except God, and they were looking. Then it produced a drink like it in size, so Junda’ bin Amr and a group of his people believed in him. The nobles of Thamud wanted to believe in him and confirm him, but Dhu’ab bin Amr bin Labid, the owner of their idols, and Rbab bin Samghar, who was their soothsayer, forbade them. They were from the nobles of Thamud. When the she-camel came out, Salih said to them: This is the she-camel of God, she has a drink and you have a drink on a specific day. So the she-camel stayed with her water in the land of Thamud, grazing on trees and drinking water. She would come to the water at night, and when it was her day, she would put her head in a well in the rock called the Well of the She-camel. She would not move her head until she had drunk all the water in it, not leaving a drop. Then she would raise her head and it would puff up until it had emptied for them, and they would milk whatever they wanted of milk. They would drink and store it until they had filled all their vessels. Then she would leave from a different path from which she had come. She would not be able to leave from where she had come, and it would be too narrow for her. Then, when it was their day, they would drink whatever they wanted of water and store whatever they wanted for the day of the she-camel. They were thus in comfort and peace. The she-camel would spend the summer when it was hot in the back of the valley, and the livestock would flee from her, their sheep, cows, and camels, and they would descend to the bottom of the valley in its heat and drought. She would spend the winter in the bottom of the valley when it was winter, and their livestock would flee. To the valley in the cold and drought, and that harmed their livestock due to the trial and test, so that was too much for them, so they rebelled against the command of their Lord and that led them to hamstring the she-camel, so they agreed to hamstring her. There were two women from Thamud, one of them was called Unayzah bint Ghanim bin Majlaz, who was nicknamed Umm Ghanim. She was the wife of Dhu’ab bin Amr and was an old woman, and had beautiful daughters and wealth in camels, cows and sheep. Another woman was called Saduf bint Al-Muhaya, who was beautiful and rich and had many livestock. They loved to hamstring the she-camel because it harmed them in their livestock, so they tricked her into hamstringing the she-camel. Saduf called a man from Thamud called Al-Hubab to hamstring the she-camel, and offered herself to him if he did so, but he refused. So she called a cousin of hers called Musadd’ bin Muharij bin Al-Muhaya, and offered herself to him on condition that he hamstring the she-camel. She was one of the most handsome and wealthy people, and he agreed to do so. Unayzah bint Ghanim called Qadar bin Salif, who was a short, red-haired man. They claimed that he had been the daughter of a fornicator, but Salif had not, but he was born on Salif’s bed. She said: I will give you any of my daughters you wish on condition that you hamstring the she-camel. Qadar was a powerful and respected man among his people. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us that Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us that Muhammad bin Yusuf told us that Muhammad bin Ismail told us that Musa bin Ismail told us that Wahib told us that Hisham told us on the authority of his father that Abdullah bin Zama’ah told him that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon and he mentioned the she-camel and the one who hamstrung her. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the most wretched of them arose Ash-Shams 12, a mighty, powerful man, powerful among his people, arose for her like Abu Zama’ah. We returned to the story, they said: So Qudar bin Salif and Musda’ bin Muharij set out and seduced the seducers of Thamud, and seven men followed them, so they were nine men, so Qudar and Musda’ and their companions set out and watched the she-camel when it came to the water, and Qudar had ambushed it at the base of a rock on its way, and Musda’ ambushed it on another way, so it passed by Musda’, so he shot it with an arrow and it lodged in the muscle of its leg, and the daughter of Ghanim of Unayzah came out, and ordered her daughter, and she was one of the most beautiful people, so she revealed herself to Qudar and then she restrained him, so he attacked the she-camel with the sword and exposed her hock, so she fell and roared once, warning of her stench, then he stabbed her in the heart and slaughtered her, and the people of the town came out and divided up its meat and cooked it, and when he saw its stench, he set out until he came to a high mountain called Sanu, and it was said that its name was Qara, and he came to Salih and it was said to him: Catch up with the she-camel, for she has been hamstrung, so he came and they came out to meet him and apologize to him: Oh The Prophet of God said: It was so-and-so who hamstrung it, and it is not our fault. So Salih said: Look, will you catch its young? If you catch it, perhaps the punishment will be lifted from you. So they went out looking for it, and when they saw it on a mountain, they went to take it. Then God Almighty inspired the mountain, and it rose high in the sky until the birds could not reach it. Salih came, and when the foal saw him, he cried until his tears flowed. Then he foamed three times, and the rock burst open, and he entered it. Salih said, “For every foam there is a term of one day, so enjoy yourselves in your home for three days. That is a promise that will not be denied.” Ibn Ishaq said: Four of the nine men who had hamstrung the she-camel followed Al-Saqb, among them Musad’ ibn Mihraj and his brother Thabb ibn Mihraj. Musad’ shot him with an arrow that pierced his heart, then dragged him by his foot and made him fall down. They threw his flesh as bitter as his mother’s flesh. Salih said to them: You have violated the sanctity of God, so be glad of God’s punishment and vengeance. They said, mocking him: When will that be, Salih? And what is the sign of that? They used to name the days among them: Sunday is the first, Monday is the easiest, Tuesday is the last, Wednesday is the tyrant, Thursday is the pessimistic, Friday is the merciful, and Saturday is the merciful. They hamstrung the she-camel on Wednesday, so Salih said to them when they said that: You will wake up on the morning of Mu’nis with your faces yellow, then you will wake up on the morning of the day of the merciful and your faces red, then you will wake up on the day of the merciful and your faces black, then the punishment will come to you on the first day. When Salih said that to them, the nine who had hamstrung the she-camel said: Come, let us kill Salih. If he is truthful, we will hasten him before us, and if he is lying, we will catch up with his she-camel. So they came to him at night to spend the night with his family, but the angels struck them with stones. When they were slow to reach their companions, they came to Salih’s house and found them crushed with stones. They said to Salih: You killed them. Then they intended to attack him, but his clan stood up to protect him and put on their weapons. They said to them: By God, you will never kill him, for he promised you that the punishment would descend upon you after three days. If he is truthful, you will only increase your Lord’s anger against you, and if he is lying, then you will be behind what you want. So they turned away from them that night, and on Thursday morning their faces were yellow as if they had been smeared with saffron, young and old, male and female. They were certain of the punishment and knew that Salih had told them the truth, so they sought him out to kill him. Salih fled from them until he took refuge in a tribe of Thamud called Banu Ghanim, and he descended upon their master, a man called Nufayl, who was known as Abu Hudab, and he was a polytheist, and he hid him, and they were unable to find him, so they went to the companions of Salih to torture them to lead them to him, and a man from the companions of Salih called Mubdi’ bin Harm said: O Prophet of God, they torture us to lead them to you, so should we lead them to him? He said: Yes, so he led them to him, and they went to Abu Hudab and spoke to him about that, and he said: Yes, I have Salih with me and he is your guardian, and you have a way against him, so they turned away from him and left him, and the torment that God had sent down upon them distracted them from it, so some of them began to tell others what they saw in their faces, and by the evening they all cried out: Behold, two days of the appointed time have passed and the torment has come upon you, and by the morning of the third day their faces were black as if they had been covered with tar, so they all cried out: Behold, the torment has come upon you. When Sunday night came, Salih and those who had converted to Islam with him left their midst and went to Ash-Sham. He settled in Ramla Palestine. When morning came, the people shrouded themselves and embalmed themselves and threw themselves to the ground, turning their eyes to the sky at one time and to the earth at another, not knowing from where the torment would come to them. When the sun rose on Sunday, a cry came to them from the sky, in which was the sound of every thunderbolt and the sound of everything that has a sound on earth. It tore their hearts apart in their chests, and none of them, young or old, remained but perished, as God Almighty said: So they became kneeling in their homes, except for a crippled girl called Dhari’ah bint Salif. She was a disbeliever who was very strong in her disbelief and enmity towards Salih. God released her legs after she had witnessed the torment, so she went out faster than anything had ever been seen until she reached Qazhah, which is Wadi al-Qura. She informed them of what she had witnessed of the torment and what had befallen Thamud. Then she drew some water and was given to drink, but when she drank, she died. Al-Suddi mentioned another aspect of the hamstringing of the camel. He said: God Almighty revealed to Salih, peace be upon him: He said to them, Your people will hamstring your she-camel. They said, We would not do that. Salih said, In this month of yours, a boy will be born who will hamstring your she-camel, and your destruction will be at his hands. They said, No child will be born to us in this month except that we will kill him. Nine of them had a child in that month, so they slaughtered their sons. Then a son was born to the tenth, but he refused to slaughter his son, and he had not had a son before that. This made the nine angry with Salih because he was the reason for the killing of their sons. They swore by God that we would spend the night with him and his family. They said, We will go out so that the people will see that we have set out on a journey, so we will go to the cave and be in it. When night fell and Salih went out to his mosque, we went to him and killed him. Then we returned to the cave and were in it. Then we returned to our homes and said, We did not witness the destruction of his family, and we are telling the truth. So they believed us, thinking that we had set out on a journey. Salih did not sleep with them in the village, and he would spend the night in a mosque called the Mosque of Salih. When morning came, he would come to them and preach to them and remind them, and when evening came, he would go out to the mosque and spend the night there. They set out and entered the cave, and the cave fell on them and killed them. Some men who had seen what had happened among them set out and found that they had been crushed, so they returned shouting in the village: O servants of God, Salih was not satisfied with ordering them to kill their children until he killed them. So the people of the village gathered to hamstring the she-camel. Ibn Ishaq said: The nine divided the camel over Salih’s stay after they hamstrung the camel, as we mentioned. Al-Suddi and others said: When the tenth son was born, meaning Qadar, he grew up in a day as a youth other than him on Friday, and grew up in a month as a youth other than him in a year. When he grew up, he sat and passed by some people drinking, so they wanted water to mix their drink with. That day was the day the she-camel was drinking, but they found that the she-camel had drunk the water. This was difficult for them and they said: What should we do with the milk? If we were to take this water that the she-camel drinks and give it to our livestock and crops to drink, it would be better for us. The tenth son said: Would you like me to hamstring her for you? They said: Yes. So they hamstrung her. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Maskeen told us, Yahya bin Hassan bin Hayyan Abu Zakariya told us, Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended to Al-Hijr during the Battle of Tabuk, he ordered them not to drink from its well or draw water from it. They said: We have kneaded from it and drawn water. So he ordered them to throw away that dough and pour out that water.” Ibn Nafi’ said on the authority of Ibn Umar: “So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to pour out what they drew from its wells and to feed the dough to the camels, and he ordered them to draw water from the well that the she-camel used to drink from.” Abu al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by al-Hijr during the Battle of Tabuk, he said to his companions: Let none of you enter the village, nor drink from their water, nor enter upon these tormented people unless you are weeping lest the same thing happen to you as happened to them. Then he said: “As for what follows, do not ask your Messenger for signs. These are the people of Salih who asked their Messenger, so God sent the she-camel, and she used to come back from this pass and come back from that pass and drink their water on the day she came. He showed them the ascent of the young camel from the continent, but they rebelled against the command of their Lord and hamstrung it. So God destroyed from under the sky all of them in the east and west of the earth except one man called Abu Righal, and he was Abu Thaqif, who was in the sanctuary of God, and the sanctuary of God protected him from the punishment of God. When he came out, what happened to his people happened to him, so he was buried, and with him was buried a branch of gold. 7:130: 130 - The Almighty said: And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years, meaning with drought and famine. The Arabs say: A year afflicted them, meaning drought and severe year. Qatada said: As for the years, they are for the people of the deserts, and as for the decrease in fruits, they are for the people of the cities, that they may remember, meaning: take heed. This is because hardship softens the hearts and makes them desire what is with God, the Almighty.
7:131: 131 - So when good comes to them, meaning: fertility, abundance, and well-being, they say, ‘This is for us,’ meaning, we are its people and deserve it according to the custom that has come to us in the abundance of our provisions, and they do not see it as a favor from God Almighty for which they should be grateful. But if evil befalls them, meaning drought and calamity, and they see what they dislike, they take an omen, they have a bad omen, about Moses and those with him, and they say, No calamity has befallen us until we have seen them. This is from the bad luck of Moses and his people. Saeed bin Jubair and Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir said: Pharaoh's reign was four hundred years. He lived six hundred and twenty years without seeing any harm. If he had been hungry for a day, or fever for a night, or pain for an hour during that period, he would never have claimed divinity. God the Almighty said: Unquestionably, their omen is only with God. That is, their share of fertility and drought, good and evil, is all from God. Ibn Abbas said: Their omen is what God has decreed and destined for them. In another narration from him: Their bad luck is with God and from God. That is, their bad luck only came to them because of their disbelief in God. It was said that its meaning is the great bad luck that they will have from God in the form of the torment of the Fire. But most of them do not know, that what has befallen them is from God.
7:132: 132 - And they said, meaning: the Copts to Moses, Whatever sign you bring us, whenever a word is used for condition and consequence, to bewitch us with it, to change us from the religion we are on, we will not believe you, believing.
7:133: 133 - So We sent upon them the flood. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, Qatadah, and Muhammad bin Ishaq said - their words were mixed with each other -: When the magicians believed, and Pharaoh returned defeated, he and his people refused to do anything except remain in disbelief and persist in evil, so God continued to send them signs and took them with years and a decrease in fruits. When he dealt with them with the four signs: the staff, the hand, the years, and the decrease in fruits, they refused to believe, so he invoked against them, saying: O Lord, your servant Pharaoh has exalted himself in the land, has transgressed and rebelled, and his people have broken your covenant. O Lord, seize them with a punishment that will be a punishment for them and a lesson for my people and a sign and a warning for those after them. So God sent upon them the flood, which is water. God sent upon them the water while the houses of the Children of Israel and the houses of the Copts were intertwined and mixed, so the houses of the Copts were filled until they stood in the water up to their collarbones, and whoever among them sat was drowned, and did not enter. The houses of the Children of Israel were flooded with water, and the water stagnated on their land. They were unable to plow or do anything. This continued for them for seven days, from Sabbath to Sabbath. Mujahed and Ata’ said: The flood is death. Wahb said: The flood is the plague in the language of Yemen. Abu Qilabah said: The flood is smallpox, and they were the first to be punished with it, so it remained on earth. Muqatil said: The flood was the water that overflowed their crops. Ibn Dhibyan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The flood was a command from God that swept over them. Then he recited: And a company from your Lord swept over them while they were asleep (al-Qalam 68:19). Kufa grammarians said: The flood is a noun that is not pluralized, like the preponderance and the deficiency. The people of Basra said: It is a plural, the singular of which is Tufanah. So he said to Moses: Call upon your Lord to remove the rain from us, so we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you. So he called upon his Lord, so He lifted the flood from them. So God caused to grow for them in that year something that He had not caused to grow for them before, of grass, crops, and fruits, and their land became fertile. They said: This water was nothing but a blessing and fertility for us. So they did not believe and stayed in good health for a month. Then God sent locusts upon them, and they ate most of their crops, fruits, and leaves of the trees until they ate the doors, roofs of the houses, wood, clothes, luggage, and iron nails of the doors until their houses fell down. The locusts were afflicted with hunger, so they were never satisfied, and the Children of Israel did not suffer from any of that, so they roared and made a noise, and they said: O Moses, call upon your Lord for us, if you remove the calamity from us, we will believe in you. And they gave him the covenant and pledge of God. So Moses, peace be upon him, called upon God, so God removed the locusts from them after they had stayed upon them for seven days from Saturday to Saturday. In al-Naba 78:(It is written on the chest of every locust: God’s greatest soldier). It is said that Moses went out into the open air and pointed with his staff towards the east and the west, so the locusts returned from where they came, and there was still some of their crops and produce, so they said: We have enough left for us, so we will not abandon our religion, so they did not fulfill what they had promised, and they returned to their evil deeds, so they stayed for a month in good health, then God sent lice upon them. And they differed about lice Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Lice are the weevils that come out of wheat. Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Qatada and Al-Kalbi said: Lice are the crawling insects, locusts and the flying insects that have wings, and the small insects that do not have wings. Ikrimah said: They are the daughters of the locust. Abu Ubaidah said: They are the humnan, which is a type of tick. Ata Al-Khurasani said: They are lice. Abu Al-Hasan read it like this lice with the qaf open and the meem silent. They said: God commanded Moses to walk to a sandy dune in a village in Egypt called Ain Shams. Moses walked to that sandy dune and struck it with his staff, and lice flocked to them. They followed what remained of their crops, trees, and plants and ate it, and licked the entire ground. They would enter between the clothing of one of them and his skin and bite it, and one of them would eat food and become filled with lice. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Lice are the weevils that come out of grains. A man would take ten bags to the mill and not return even three of them. They were not afflicted with a calamity that was more severe to them than lice. It took their hair, skin, eyelashes, and eyebrows and stuck to their skin as if it were smallpox and prevented them from sleeping and resting. They cried out and cried out to Moses, We repent, so pray to your Lord for us to remove the calamity from us. So Moses, peace be upon him, prayed to God and God removed the lice from them after they had stayed with them for seven days from Saturday to Saturday. Then they broke their oath and returned to their worst deeds. They said: We were never more certain that he was a magician than we are today who turns sand into beasts. So Moses prayed after they had lived a month in peace, and God sent frogs upon them, and their houses, courtyards, food, and vessels were filled with them. No one would uncover a vessel or food without finding frogs in it. A man would sit with frogs on his chin, and when he wanted to speak, a frog would jump into his mouth. They would jump into their pots, spoiling their food and extinguishing their fires. One of them would lie down and the frogs would climb on him and pile him up so high that he could not go to the apartment of another, and he would open his mouth to eat, but the frog would beat his food to his mouth. He would not knead dough without it cracking in it, and he would not open a pot without it filling it with frogs, and they suffered severe harm from them. Narrated Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The frogs were wild, and when God sent them to the people of Pharaoh, they heard and obeyed, so they began to throw themselves into the boiling pots and into the ovens while they were bubbling, so God rewarded them for their good obedience by sending them cold water. When they saw that, they wept and complained about it to Moses, and they said, This time we will repent and not return. So he took their covenants and agreements, then he called upon his Lord, and He removed the frogs from them after he had stayed seven days from Sabbath to Sabbath. They stayed a month in good health, then they broke the covenant and returned to their disbelief. So Moses called upon God, and God sent blood upon them, so the Nile flowed upon them with blood and their waters became blood, and they did not draw water from the wells and rivers except that they found it to be thick, red blood. So they complained to Pharaoh and said, We have no drink. He said, He has bewitched you. They said, From where did he bewitch us when we do not find any water in our vessels except thick blood?
