Pharaoh would gather the Copt and the Israelite in one vessel, so that what was near the Israelite would be water and what was near the Copt would be blood and they would go to the jar in which there was water, and water would come out for the Israelite and blood for the Copt, until a woman from the family of Pharaoh would come to a woman from the children of Israel when they were overcome by thirst and say, Give me some of your water to drink, so she would pour for her from her waterskin and the vessel would become blood, until she would say, Put it in your mouth and then pour it into my mouth, so she would take water in her mouth and when she vomited it in her mouth it would become blood. Pharaoh was so thirsty that he would be forced to chew on fresh trees, and when he chewed them their water would turn into salty, bitter water in his mouth, so they were left in that state for seven days, drinking nothing but blood. Zayd ibn Aslam said: The blood that was imposed on them was nosebleeds. So they came to Moses and said: O Moses, call upon your Lord to remove this blood from us, so that we may believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you. So he called upon his Lord, the Almighty, and He removed it from them, but they did not believe. This is what God Almighty said: So We sent upon them the flood and the locusts and the lice and the frogs and the blood as distinct signs, one following the other. The details are that each punishment lasted a week, and between every two punishments was a month. But they were arrogant and were a criminal people.
7:134: 134 - And when the punishment fell upon them, meaning: the torment descended upon them, which is what God Almighty mentioned of the flood and other things.. Saeed bin Jubair said: The punishment is the plague, and it is the sixth torment after the five verses, until seventy thousand of them died in one day, and they spent the night without burying each other. They said to Moses, O Moses, call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you, meaning: according to what He has commanded you. Ata’ said: What has informed you? It was said: “What we have promised you regarding the answer to your supplication: ‘If you remove the affliction from us’, meaning the plague, ‘we will believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you.’” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, on the authority of Zahir ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi, on the authority of Abu Mus`ab, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Abu al-Nadr, the freed slave of `Umar ibn `Ubayd God, on the authority of `Amir ibn Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, on the authority of his father, that he heard him ask Usamah ibn Zayd: Did you hear from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the plague? Usamah ibn Zayd said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The plague is a punishment sent upon the Children of Israel or upon those who came before you. So if you hear about it in a land, do not go there, and if it breaks out in a land while you are in it, do not leave fleeing from it.”
7:135: 135 - The Almighty said: So when We removed the punishment from them until a term they were to reach meaning: until drowning in the sea at once they broke their covenant they broke the covenant.
7:136: 136 - So We took retribution from them and drowned them in the sea meaning: the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them meaning: heedless of the punishment before it came. It was said: its meaning is turning away from Our signs.
7:137: 137 - And We gave as an inheritance to the people who were oppressed, subjugated and humiliated by slaughtering sons and using women and enslaving them, and they are the children of Israel, the easts of the earth and the wests meaning Egypt and the Levant which We blessed with water, trees, fruits, fertility and abundance and the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel meaning: the word of God was fulfilled, which is His promise to them of victory and empowerment on the earth, and that is His Almighty saying: And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land Al-Qasas - 5 for their patience in their religion and in the punishment of Pharaoh and We destroyed "We annihilated what Pharaoh and his people were making, in the land of Egypt of buildings, and what they were building Mujahid said they were building houses and palaces. Al-Hasan said: they were building trees, fruits and grapes. Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read ya’arshūn with a damma on the ra’ here and in An-Nahl, and others read it with a kasra.
7:138: 138 - The Almighty said: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea. Al-Kalbi said: Moses crossed the sea with them on the day of Ashura after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, so he fasted in gratitude to God Almighty. So they came and passed by a people who were devoting themselves to worshipping God. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read devoting themselves to worshipping God with a kasra on the kaf, and the others read it with a damma on it, and they are two dialects, on idols “idols” for them, which they worship instead of God. Ibn Jurayj said: They were statues of cows, and that was the first thing that happened with the calf. Qatada said: Those people were from Lakhm and they had settled in Ar-Raqqah, so the Children of Israel said when they saw that: They said, ‘O Moses, make for us a god’ meaning: an example that we can worship as they have gods. This was not a doubt on the part of the Children of Israel about the Oneness of God, but rather its meaning was: Make for us something that we can glorify and draw closer to God Almighty by glorifying it. They thought that this would not harm the religion, and that was due to their extreme ignorance. Moses said, ‘Indeed, you are a people ignorant’ of the greatness of God.
7:139: 139 - Indeed, these people are doomed to destruction, and in vain is what they were doing.
7:140: 140 - He said meaning Moses Shall I seek for you other than God meaning I seek for you and ask, a god while He has favored you over the worlds meaning: over the worlds of your time. Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abu Sahl Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzar told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Dayri told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sinan bin Abi Sinan Al-Dayli, on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laithi, who said: “We went out with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, before Hunayn, and we passed by Sidrat Al-Anwat, so we said: O Messenger of God, make for us Dhat Anwat as the infidels had Dhat Anwat, and the infidels used to hang their weapons on Sidrat Al-Anwat and worship around it, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is Great, this is like what the Children of Israel said to Moses, ‘Make for us a god as they had gods. You are following the ways of those before you.’”
7:141: 141 - The Almighty said: And when We saved you, Ibn Amir read Anjakum and this is how it is in the copies of the Qur’an of the people of Ash-Sham, from the people of Pharaoh who subject you to the worst torment, killing your sons, Nafi’ read Yaqtulu lightly, from killing, and the others read it with emphasis to emphasize the great killing, and they spare your women, and in that is a great trial from your Lord.
7:142: 142- And We appointed for Moses thirty nights, of Dhul-Qa'dah, and completed them with ten, of Dhul-Hijjah, “so the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And Moses said,” when he set out to the mountain to commune, to his brother Aaron, ‘Take my place,’ be my successor, among my people and reform, meaning reform them by urging them to obey God. Ibn Abbas said: He means to be kind to them and do good to them. And do not follow the way of the corrupters, meaning: Do not obey those who disobey God and do not agree with his command. This is because Moses, peace be upon him, promised the Children of Israel while they were in Egypt: that if God destroyed their enemy, He would bring them a book in which there is a statement of what they should do and what they should leave! So when God did that to them, Moses asked his Lord for the book, and God Almighty commanded him to fast for thirty days. When thirty days were completed, he found the bad smell in his mouth, so he brushed his teeth with a carob stick. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: He ate from the bark of a tree, and the angels said to him: We smelled the scent of musk from your mouth, but you spoiled it with the siwak. So God Almighty commanded him to fast ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, and he said: Did you not know that the bad breath of a fasting person is better to me than the scent of musk? So their trial was in the ten days that he added.
7:143: 143 - The Almighty said: And when Moses came to Our appointed time, meaning: for the time that We set for him to speak to him. The commentators said: Moses, peace be upon him, purified himself and made his clothes pure for the appointment with his Lord when he came to Mount Sinai. And in the story: God, the Almighty, sent down darkness over seven parasangs and drove away from him Satan and drove away from him the vermin of the earth and removed from him the two angels and scraped the sky for him and he saw the angels standing in the air and saw the throne prominent and the word of God and he spoke to Him so that he could hear, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, was with him but he did not hear what his Lord said and brought him close until he heard the scratching of the pen, so Moses, peace be upon him, found the speech of his Lord sweet and longed to see Him. "He said: My Lord, show me so that I may look at You," Al-Zajjaj said: It is an abbreviation, meaning: Show me yourself so that I may look at You. Ibn Abbas said: Give me so that I may look at You. If it is said: How did he ask to see You when he knew that God, the Almighty, cannot be seen in this world? Al-Hasan said: He was overcome with longing so he asked to see You. It was said: He asked to see, thinking that it was permissible for him to see in this world. God Almighty said: You will not see Me. And no human being can bear to look (at Me in this world. Whoever looks at Me) in this world will die, so he said: My God, I heard Your words and I longed to look at You, and for me to look at You and then die is more beloved to me than for me to live and not see You. So God Almighty said: But look at the mountain, and it is the greatest mountain of Madyan, called Zubayr. Al-Suddi said: When God spoke to Moses, the evil Iblis sank into the earth until he emerged between Moses’ feet, and whispered to him: A devil is speaking to you. Then Moses asked to see Him, and God, the Almighty, said: You will not see Me. Those who deny seeing Him clung to the apparent meaning of this verse, and said: God, the Almighty, said: You will not see Me. And will not is for support, and they have no argument in it. The meaning of the verse is: You will not see Me in this world or in the present, because he was asking to see Him in the present, and will not is not for support, like the Almighty’s saying: And they will never wish for it Al-Baqarah 2:95, informing about the Jews. Then He informed about them that they wish for death in the Hereafter, saying: O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us Az-Zukhruf 77, and Oh, would that it were the final judgment Al-Haqqah 27. The evidence for this is that he did not attribute it to ignorance of asking to see Him, and he did not say that I do not see Him, so that they would have an argument, but rather he linked seeing Him to the stability of the mountain, and the stability of the mountain on the manifestation is not impossible if God, the Almighty, gave it that power. That which is suspended on something that is not impossible is not impossible. God the Almighty said: But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me. Wahb and Ibn Ishaq said that when Moses asked his Lord to see him, God sent fog, thunderbolts, darkness, thunder and lightning, and the mountain on which Moses was standing was surrounded by four leagues on every side. God ordered the angels of the heavens to intercept Moses, and the angels of the lowest heaven passed by him, many cows, their mouths glorifying and sanctifying Him in great voices like the sound of loud thunder. Then God ordered the angels of the second heaven to descend upon Moses, and they intercepted him. So they descended upon him like lions, their faces glorifying and sanctifying Him. The weak servant Ibn Imran was terrified by what he saw and heard, and every hair on his head and body shuddered. Then he said: I regret my question, so will anything save me from the place I am in? The best and most important of the angels said to him: O Moses, be patient for what you asked, for it is little of the much that you saw. Then God ordered the angels of the third heaven to descend upon Moses, so they intercepted him. They descended like eagles, their voices were violently shaking and their mouths were glorifying and sanctifying like the voices of a great army. Their colors were like the flames of fire. Moses was terrified and his soul was intense and he despaired of life. Then the best of the angels said to him: Stay where you are, O son of Imran, until you see what you cannot be patient with. Then God the Most High ordered the angels of the fourth heaven to descend and intercept Moses, son of Imran. They descended upon him, and nothing of those who passed by him before them resembled them. Their colors were like the flames of fire, and the rest of their creation was like white snow. Their voices were loud with sanctification and glorification, and nothing of the voices of those who passed by him before them could compare to them. His knees clashed, his heart trembled and his crying became intense. Then the best of the angels and their head said to him: O son of Imran, be patient with what you asked for, for you have seen little of much. Then God Almighty commanded the angels of the fifth heaven to descend, so they intercepted Moses and descended upon him with seven colors, but Moses could not follow them with his sight. He had never seen anything like them nor heard anything like their voices, so his heart was filled with fear, his sadness intensified, and his crying increased. Then the best of the angels and their leader said to him: O son of Imran, stay where you are until you see something that you cannot bear. Then God commanded the angels of the sixth heaven to descend upon My servant who asked to see Me. So they descended upon him. In the hand of each angel was something like a tall palm tree, a fire brighter than the sun, and their clothing was like the flames of fire. When they glorified and sanctified, the angels of the heavens who were before them responded to them, all of them saying in loud voices: Glory be to the Holy One, the Lord of Majesty, who never dies. On the head of each angel were four faces. When Moses saw them, he raised his voice glorifying with them when they glorified and he was crying and saying: My Lord, remember me and do not forget Your servant. I do not know whether I will escape from what I am in or not. If I go out, I will be burned, and if I stay, I will die. Then the chief of the angels and their head said to him: O son of Imran, your fear is about to intensify and your heart will be torn out, so be patient for what you have asked. Then God the Almighty ordered that His Throne be carried by the angels of the seventh heaven. When the light of the Throne appeared, the mountain split from the majesty of the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, and the angels of the heavens raised their voices all together, saying: Glory be to the Holy One, the Lord of Majesty, who never dies, with the intensity of their voices. The mountain shook and every tree in it crumbled, and the weak servant Moses fell unconscious on his face, not having his soul with him. God sent the spirit in His mercy, and it covered him, and turned the stone that Moses was on over him and made it like a dome so that Moses would not be burned. The spirit raised him like a lam, and Moses stood up, glorifying God the Almighty and saying: I believe in You, my Lord, and I believe that no one sees You and lives. Whoever looks at Your angels, his heart is torn apart. How great You are and how great are Your angels. You are the Lord of lords, the God of gods, and the King of kings. Nothing is equal to You and nothing can stand before You. My Lord, I repent to You. Praise be to You, You have no partner. How great You are and how majestic You are, Lord of the worlds. This is what God the Almighty said: So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He rendered it level. Ibn Abbas said: The light of his Lord appeared to the mountain, a mountain. Az-Zubayr. Ad-Dahhak said: God revealed from the light of the veils like the nostril of a bull. Abdullah bin Salam and Kaab Al-Ahbar said: God’s greatness was not revealed to the mountain except like the eye of a needle until it became ground. As-Suddi said: He was not revealed except the size of the little finger. This is indicated by what Thabit narrated on the authority of Anas, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse and said: Like this, and he placed the thumb on the upper joint of the little finger, and the mountain crumbled.” It was narrated on the authority of Sahl bin Sa`d Al-Sa`idi that God Almighty revealed from seventy thousand veils a light the size of a dirham, and He made the mountain level, that is, level with the ground. Hamza and Al-Kisa`i read daka` with an elongated vowel without a tanween here and in Surat Al-Kahf and and Asim agreed with him in Al-Kahf, and others read daka with a shortened vowel and a tanween, so whoever shortened it, its meaning is that He made it pounded: daka and daq are one and the same, and it was said that its meaning is that God pounded it, that is, He crushed it, as He said: No, when the earth is pounded, pounded (al-Fajr 89:21), and whoever reads with an elongated vowel means: He made it level with the ground, pounded. It was said: Its meaning is to make it like a camel without a hump. Ibn Abbas said: He made it dust. Sufyan said: The mountain sank into the earth until it fell into the sea and is sinking into it. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: It became enormous sand. Al-Kalbi said: He made it dust, meaning he broke it into small mountains. It was mentioned in some interpretations: Because of his greatness, there were six mountains, three of which were located in Medina: Uhud, Warqan, and Radwi, and three of which were located in Mecca: Thawr, Thabir, and Hira. The Almighty said: And Moses fell unconscious. Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said: He was unconscious. Qatada said: He was dead. Al-Kalbi said: Moses fell unconscious on Thursday, the Day of Arafah, and he was given the Torah on Friday, the Day of Sacrifice. Al-Waqidi said: When Moses fell unconscious, the angels of the heavens said: What has Ibn Imran to do with asking to see God? In some books it is stated that the angels of the heavens came to Moses while he was unconscious and began to kick him with their feet and said: O son of menstruating women, did you hope to see the Lord of Glory? So when he recovered Moses from his unconsciousness and his mind came back to him, he realized that he had asked for something that was not appropriate for him. “He said: Glory be to You, I repent to You” for asking to see God and I am the first of the believers that you are not seen in this world. Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: And I am the first of the Children of Israel to believe in you
7:144: 144 - He said, O Moses, indeed I have chosen you over the people. I chose you over the people. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read inni with the opening of the ya’ and likewise my brother * strengthen Taha - 31, with my messages, the people of Hijaz read with my messages with the Tahwid, and the others with the plural, and with my words, so take what I have given you I gave you and be among the grateful to God for His blessings. If it is said: What is the meaning of his saying, I have chosen you over the people with My messages, when someone else was given the message? It was said: Since the message was not general for all people, his saying, I have chosen you over the people, is correct, even if someone else shares it with him, just as he says to a man, I have singled you out for my advice, and if he consults someone else, if the advice is not general, it is correct. In part of the story: After his Lord spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, no one could look at him because his face was covered with light, and a veil remained over his face until he died. His wife said to him: I have been widowed from you since your Lord spoke to you. So he uncovered his face to her and it took her like a ray of sunshine. She put her hand on her face and prostrated to God, and said: Ask God to make me your wife in Paradise. He said: That is if you do not marry after me, because a woman is for the last of her husbands. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ali Al-Muzaki told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Sarraj told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Rashid bin Asaad bin Abdul-Rahman Al-Maghfiri told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ka’b Al-Ahbar: Moses looked at the Torah and said: “I find a nation that is the best of nations brought forth for mankind. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and believe in God and in the first Book and in the last Book, and they fight the people of misguidance until they fight the one-eyed Antichrist. O Lord, make them my nation.” He said: They are the nation of Muhammad, O Moses. He said: “O Lord, I find a nation that is the praiseworthy, the shepherds of the sun, the judges. When they want something, they say, ‘We will do it, God willing.’ So make them my nation.” He said: They are the nation of Muhammad. He said: “O Lord, I find a nation that consumes its expiations and its charities, and the former people used to burn their charities in the fire. They are the ones who respond and are responded to, the intercessors for whom intercession is made, so make them my nation.” He said: They are the nation of Muhammad. He said: “O Lord, I find a nation that is the ones who praise and are the ones who are answered, the intercessors for whom intercession is made. So make them my nation.” He said: They are the nation of Muhammad. He said: “O Lord, I find a nation that is the ones who praise and are the ones who... I find a nation that, if one of them rises to a high place, glorifies God, and if he descends into a valley, praises God. The ground is a place of purification for them and the earth is a place of prostration for them wherever they are. They purify themselves from major ritual impurity with the ground as they purify themselves with water when they cannot find water. They are radiant and their faces are white from the traces of ablution. So make them my nation. He said: They are the nation of Ahmad. He said: My Lord, I find a nation that, if one of them intends to do a good deed but does not do it, a good deed like it is written for him, and if he does it, it is written for him ten times its like, up to seven hundred times. And if he intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, it is not written for him, but if he does it, a bad deed like it is written for him, so make them my nation. He said: They are the nation of Ahmad. He said: My Lord, I find a nation that is merciful, weak, inheriting the Book from those We have chosen of Our servants. Among them are those who wrong themselves, and among them are those who are moderate, and among them are those who are foremost in good deeds. I do not find anyone among them except that they receive mercy. So make them my nation. He said: They are the nation of Muhammad. He said: My Lord, I find a nation whose copies of the Qur’an are in their chests, wearing the colors of the clothes of the people of Paradise, and they line up in their prayers the rows of angels, their voices In their mosques, like the buzzing of bees, none of them will ever enter the Fire except those who see the reckoning as a stone is seen from behind a tree. So make them my nation. He said: They are the nation of Ahmad. So Moses was not amazed at the goodness that God gave to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation. He said: I wish I were one of the companions of Muhammad or his nation. So God revealed to him three verses with which He would please him: “O Moses, indeed I have chosen you over mankind with My messages and with My speech” until His saying: I will show you the home of the wicked “And among the people of Moses is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby.” So Moses was completely pleased.
7:145: 145 - The Almighty said: And We wrote for him, meaning Moses, on the tablets. Ibn Abbas said: He means the tablets of the Torah. In the hadith: They were from the lote trees of Paradise, the length of the tablet was twelve cubits. And in the hadiths about God creating Adam with His hand it says: And He wrote the Torah with His hand and planted the Tuba tree with His hand. Al-Hasan said: The tablets were made of wood. Al-Kalbi said: They were made of green chrysolite. Saeed bin Jubair said: They were made of red ruby. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: The tablets were made of hail. Ibn Jurayj said: They were made of emerald. God commanded Gabriel to bring them from Aden, and he wrote them with the pen with which he wrote the remembrance and drew from the River of Light. Wahb said: God commanded him to cut the tablets from a solid rock, which God softened for him, so he cut them with his hand and split them with his finger, and Moses heard the scratching of the pen with the ten words. That was on the first day of Dhul-Qi’dah, and the tablets were ten cubits, the length of Moses. Muqatil and Wahb said: And We wrote for him on the tablets, like the engraving on a ring. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: The Torah was revealed and it was seventy camel loads long, and a part of it was read in a year. Only four men read it: Moses, Joshua, Ezra, and Jesus. Al-Hasan said: This verse in the Torah is a thousand verses, meaning And We wrote for him on the tablets of everything, of what they were commanded to do and forbidden from, an admonition, forbidding ignorance, and the true meaning of admonition is a reminder and warning of what one fears the consequences of, and a detailed explanation of everything, meaning: an explanation of everything from the commands and prohibitions, the lawful and the unlawful, the limits and rulings. Take it with strength, meaning: with seriousness and diligence. It was said: with strength of heart and soundness of resolve, because if he takes it with weakness of intention, it will lead to weakness, and command your people to take the best of it, Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: They make lawful what is lawful in it, and forbid what is unlawful in it, and they ponder its likes, and act upon its clear verses, and stop at its ambiguous verses. And Moses, peace be upon him, was more devout than his people, so he commanded what they were not commanded to do. Qatrib said: With the best of them, meaning with their beauty, and all of them are good. It was said: The best of them are the obligatory and voluntary acts, which are what one deserves a reward for, and what is less than that is permissible, because one does not deserve a reward for it. It was said: With the best of them, with the best of the two matters in everything, such as forgiveness is better than retaliation, and patience is better than victory. “I will show you the abode of the wicked,” Mujahid said: Its destination in the Hereafter. Al-Hasan and Ata’ said: It means Hell, warning you not to be like them. Qatada and others said: I will take you to Ash-Sham and show you the dwellings of the past generations who disobeyed the command of God so that you may take heed from them. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: He meant the abode of Pharaoh and his people, which is Egypt, as indicated by the reading of Qasama bin Zuhair: I will inherit for you the abode of the wicked, and Al-Suddi said: The abode of the wicked is the place of the end of the infidels. Al-Kalbi said: What they passed by when they traveled of the dwellings of ‘Aad and Thamud and the generations that were destroyed.
7:146: 146 - The Almighty’s saying: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right. Ibn Abbas said: He means those who are arrogant towards My servants and fight My friends until they do not believe in Me, meaning: I will turn them away from accepting My signs and believing in them. They will be punished by being deprived of guidance for their stubbornness towards the truth, like His saying: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: I will prevent them from understanding the Qur’an. Ibn Jurayj said: He means from the creation of the heavens and the earth and everything in them, i.e. I will divert them from contemplating them and taking lessons from them. It was said: The ruling of the verse is for the people of Egypt in particular, and what is meant by the verses is the nine verses that God gave to Moses, peace be upon him. Most of them are of the view that the verse is general: And if they see (meaning: these arrogant ones) every sign, they will not believe in it, and if they see the path of right guidance, Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read Al-Rashd with a fat-ha on the ra’ and the shin, and the others read it with a damma on the ra’ and a sukun on the shin. They are two dialects like sickness and sickness, miserliness and miserliness, and grief and grief. Abu Amr differentiated between them, saying: Rushd with the dammah means correctness in the matter, and with the fathah it means uprightness in religion. The meaning of the verse: That they see the path of guidance and righteousness and do not take it for themselves as a path, “and if they see the path of error” meaning the path of misguidance “they take it as a path. That is because they denied Our verses and were heedless of them” from thinking about them and learning from them, heedless and forgetful.
7:147: 147 - And those who deny Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, meaning: and the meeting of the Hereafter, which is the time of reward and punishment, their deeds have become worthless, they have become void and become as if they had never existed. Will they be recompensed in the Hereafter except for what they used to do, meaning except for the recompense for what they used to do, in this world.
7:148: 148 - The Almighty said: And the people of Moses took after him, meaning: after his departure to the mountain from their ornaments which they borrowed from the people of Pharaoh. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read from their ornaments with a kasra on the ha' and Ya'qub read with a fatha on the ha' and a sukoon on the lam, and the Samaritan took from it a calf and threw into its mouth some of the dust from the traces of Gabriel's horse, peace be upon him, and it turned into a calf, a body, alive with flesh and blood with a mooing, which is the sound of cows, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and a group of the people of interpretation. It was said: It was a body made of gold with no soul in it, and a voice could be heard from it. It was said: He heard the sound of the rustling wind entering his stomach and exiting, but the first is more correct. It was said: He only mooed once. It was also said: He mooed a lot, whenever he mooed they prostrated to him, and if he was silent they raised their heads. Wahb said: He could be heard mooing while he was not moving. Al-Suddi said: It was mooing and walking. Have they not seen meaning: those who worshipped the calf that it does not speak to them nor guide them to a way? God said: Almighty God said: They took him as a god and were unjust. That is, they took him as a god and were unbelievers.
7:149: 149 - And when it fell into their hands, meaning they regretted worshipping the calf. The Arabs say to anyone who regrets something: it has fallen into their hands, and they saw that they had gone astray, they said, If our Lord does not have mercy on us, our Lord repents to us, and forgives us overlooks us, we will surely be among the losers." Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read: Have mercy on us and forgive us with the ta' in both of them our Lord with the ba' in the accusative. This regret and seeking forgiveness from them was after Moses returned to them.
7:150: 150 - The Almighty said: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. Abu Darda' said: Grief means intense anger. Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi said: Grief means sad. Grief is more severe than sadness. He said, 'How evil is that which you have done after me.' That is: How evil is that which you have done after my departure. It is said: He left him with good or evil if he treated his family well or badly after his departure from them. Did you hasten? "Had you preceded the command of your Lord?" Al-Hasan said: The promise of your Lord that He promised you during the forty nights." Al-Kalbi said: Did you hasten to worship the calf before the command of your Lord came to you. "And he threw down the tablets," which contained the Torah and he was carrying it, so he threw it on the ground out of intense anger. The narrators said: The Torah was seven-sevenths, and when he threw down the tablets, they were broken and six-sevenths were lifted and seven remained. What was of the report of the unseen was lifted, and what remained was what contained admonition, rulings, what was permissible and what was forbidden. And he took hold of his brother’s head, by his locks and beard, dragging him towards him. Aaron was three years older than Moses and was more beloved to the Children of Israel than Moses, because he was soft-tempered. He said, Aaron at that time, son of a mother. The people of Kufa and Ash-Sham read here and in Taha with a kasra on the meem, meaning, O son of my mother. So the ya’ of addition was deleted and the kasra was left to indicate addition, like his saying, O servants. The people of Hijaz, Basra, and Hafs read with a fatha on the meem, meaning, O son of his mother. It was said: He made it one name and built it on the opening, like their saying: Hadhramaut, and fifteen, and the like. He only said Ibn Umm, and Harun was his brother from his father and mother, to soften him and gain his sympathy. It was said: He was his brother on his mother’s side, not his father’s. The people considered me weak, meaning the worshippers of the calf, and they almost killed me, they intended and came close to killing me. So do not let the enemies rejoice over me and do not place me in your accountability for me with the wrongdoing people, meaning the worshippers of the calf.
7:151: 151 - Moses said when his brother's excuse became clear to him, My Lord, forgive me, for what I did to my brother, and my brother, if he was negligent in denouncing the worshippers of the calf, and admit us all into Your mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.
7:152: 152 - The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who took the calf meaning: they took it as a god they will be afflicted with wrath from their Lord in the Hereafter and humiliation in the life of this world. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is what they were commanded to do of killing themselves. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: Indeed, those who took the calf he meant the Jews who were in the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he taunted them for the actions of their fathers and attributed it to them they will be afflicted with wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world he meant what Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir were afflicted with of killing and exile. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It is the jizya. And thus do We recompense the slanderers, the liars. Abu Qilabah said: By God, it is the recompense of every slanderer until the Day of Resurrection that God will humiliate him. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: This is for every innovator until the Day of Resurrection.
7:153: 153 - The Almighty said: And those who have committed evil deeds and then repented after that and believed - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful.
7:154: 154 - The words of God Almighty: And when Moses’ anger subsided, meaning: it subsided, he took up the tablets, which he had thrown down, and six-sevenths of them had gone, and in their copy, they differed about it. It was said that he meant the tablets, because they were copied from the Preserved Tablet. It was said: When Moses threw the tablets, they were broken, so he made another copy of them, and this is what is meant by his saying: and in its copy. It was said: He meant: and in what was abrogated from it. Ata’ said: In what remained from it. Ibn Abbas and Amr ibn Dinar said: When Moses threw the tablets and they broke, he fasted forty days and they were returned to him in two tablets, and in them was guidance and mercy, meaning: guidance from misguidance and mercy from punishment, for those who fear their Lord, meaning: for those who fear their Lord. The lam in for their Lord is an additional emphasis, like His saying: He has sent you back (al-Naml 27:72). Al-Kisa’i said: When it comes before the verb, it is good, like His saying: You interpret the vision (Yusuf 12:43). Qatrib said: He meant they fear their Lord. It was also said: He meant devout. It was also said: He meant devout for their Lord.
7:155: 155 - The Almighty’s statement, And Moses chose from his people, meaning from his people, so the word was in the accusative case because the letter of description was removed, seventy men for Our appointed time, is evidence that not all of them worshipped the calf. Al-Suddi said: God Almighty commanded Moses to come to Him with some of the Children of Israel to apologize to Him for worshipping the calf, so Moses chose from his people seventy men, and when they came to that place, they said: We will not believe you until we see God clearly, so the thunderbolt struck them and they died. Ibn Ishaq said: He chose them to repent to Him for what they had done and to ask for repentance for those of their people they had left behind. This indicates that they all worshipped the calf. Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: The earthquake seized them because they did not leave their people when they worshipped the calf, and they did not command them to do good or forbid them from evil. Ibn Abbas said: The seventy who said: We will not believe in you until we see God with our own eyes, and the thunderbolt overtook you (al-Baqarah 2:55) were before the seventy who were overtaken by the earthquake. Rather, God Almighty commanded Moses, peace be upon him, to choose seventy men from his people, so he chose them and led them forth. So that they might call upon their Lord, and among what they called upon was that they said: O God, give us what You have not given to anyone before us, and will not give to anyone after us. So God disliked that in their call, and the tremor seized them. Wahb said: The tremor was not a sound, but when the people saw that awe, they were seized with trembling and became anxious and trembling, until their joints were almost revealed. When Moses saw that, he had mercy on them and feared death for them, and their loss was severe for him. They were his ministers for good, listening and obedient. Then he called out and cried and implored his Lord, and God removed that tremor from them, so they were reassured and listened to the words of their Lord. That is what the Almighty said: He said, meaning Moses, My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, meaning for worshipping the calf, and me, for killing the Copt. Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done? meaning the worshippers of the calf. Moses thought that they were punished for taking the calf, and he said this in the way of a question, asking: Will You destroy us for the actions of the fools? Al-Mubarrad said: His saying Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done is a question of compassion, meaning: Do not destroy us, and Moses, peace be upon him, knew that God Almighty is more just than to punish someone other than Him for the sin of the wrongdoer. The Almighty said: It is only your trial, meaning: the one into which the fools fell. It was nothing but your test and trial. You led a people astray with it and they were tempted, and You guided a people and protected them until they remained steadfast in Your religion. This is the meaning of His saying: “You misguide with it whomever You will and guide whomever You will. You are our Protector,” our Helper and our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, for You are the best of forgivers.
7:156: 156 - And decree for us make obligatory for us in this world that which is good, grace and well-being and in the Hereafter that is: and in the Hereafter that which is good, forgiveness and Paradise, indeed we have turned to You, that is: we have repented to You, "God the Most High said: "My punishment - I afflict with it whomever I will, of My creation, and My mercy encompasses all things", encompasses all things, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: His mercy encompasses in this world the righteous and the wicked, and on the Day of Resurrection it is specifically for the righteous. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: It encompasses all things, but it is only obligatory for those who are righteous, and that is because the disbeliever is provided for, and it is repelled from him by the believers due to the vastness of God's mercy for the believers, so he lives in it, and when he reaches the Hereafter it is obligatory for the believers specifically, like the one who is illuminated by the fire of another when the owner of the lamp goes with his lamp. Ibn Abbas - may God be pleased with them - Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj said: When the verse: And My mercy encompasses all things was revealed, Satan said: I am one of that things. Then God Almighty said: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God and give zakat and those who believe in Our verses. The Jews and Christians wished for it and said: We fear God and believe and give zakat. So God made it for this nation and said:
7:157: 157 - Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet the verse. Nawf Al-Bakali Al-Himyari said: When Moses chose seventy men from his people, God Almighty said to Moses: Make the earth a place of prostration and purification for you, you pray wherever the prayer overtakes you except near a toilet or a bathroom or a grave, and I will put tranquility in your hearts, and I will make you read the Torah from the memory of your hearts, read by the man and the woman, the free and the slave, the young and the old, so Moses said that to his people, and they said: We do not want to pray except in churches, and we cannot carry tranquility in our hearts, and we cannot read the Torah from the memory of our hearts, and we do not want to read it except by looking, so God Almighty said: Then I will write it down for those who fear God and give zakah until His saying: Those are the successful ones, so God made it for this nation. Moses, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, make me their prophet, so He said: Their prophet is from among them. He said: O Lord, make me one of them. He said: You will not reach them. Moses, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, I came to you with a delegation from the Children of Israel, but you made our delegation for someone else. Then God Almighty revealed: And among the people of Moses was a community guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby (al-A’raf 7:159). Moses was satisfied. God the Almighty said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He is your Prophet, who was illiterate; he could neither read nor write nor calculate. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are an unlettered nation; we neither write nor calculate. It is attributed to the mother, meaning he is as his mother bore him. It was also said that it is attributed to his nation, its original form is my nation, so the ta was dropped in the attribution as it was dropped in the Meccan and Medinan words. It was also said that it is attributed to the mother of villages, which is Mecca. Which they find meaning: they find his description, attributes, and prophethood written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, I told Muhammad bin Yusuf, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Sinan told us, Falih told us, Hilal told us, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, he said: I met Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, and I said: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah. He said: Yes, by God, he is described in the Torah with some of his description in the Qur’an: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and a protection for the unlettered. You are My servant and My Messenger. I have named you Al-Mutawakkil. He is not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets. He does not repel evil with evil, but pardons and forgives. And God will not take him until He establishes through him the crooked religion, so that they say: There is no god but God. And He opens through him blind eyes, deaf ears, and sealed hearts. Narrated by Abdul Aziz bin Salamah, on the authority of Hilal, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Salam, Imam Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Qadi told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Harun Al-Taysifuni, on the authority of Abu Al-Hassan Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Turabi, on the authority of Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Bastam, on the authority of Abu Al-Hassan bin Sayyar Al-Qurashi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Abi Hamza, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Saleh, on the authority of Abdullah bin Damrah bin Ka’b - may God be pleased with him - who said: I find written in the Torah: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, neither rude nor harsh nor loud in the markets, nor does he repay evil with evil, but pardons and forgives. His nation is the praisers, they praise God in every position and glorify Him in every Najd, they wrap their waists around their waists and perform ablution at their extremities, their rows in prayer and their rows in battle are the same, their caller calls in the sky, they have the buzzing of bees in the depths of the night, his birthplace is in Mecca, his migration is in Kaaba, and his kingdom is in Ash-Sham. God the Almighty says: He enjoins upon them what is right meaning: faith, and forbids them from what is wrong meaning: polytheism. It was said: what is right is the Shari’ah and Sunnah, and what is wrong is that which is not known in the Shari’ah or Sunnah. Ata’ said: He enjoins upon them what is right: by abandoning rivals, having good morals, and maintaining family ties, and He forbids them from what is wrong: by worshipping idols and severing family ties. And makes lawful for them the good things meaning: what they used to forbid in the pre-Islamic era, such as bahīrah, sa’ibah, wasīlah, and Ḥām. And forbids them the bad things meaning: dead animals, blood, pork, adultery, and other forbidden things. And removes from them their burden Ibn ‘Amir read ‘āsarhum in the plural. And burden is everything that burdens a person, whether in word or deed. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi, and Mujahid said: It means the heavy covenant that was taken from the Children of Israel to act according to what was in the Torah. Qatada said: It means the severity that was upon them in religion, and the shackles means the burdens that were upon them, such as: killing people in repentance, cutting off sinful limbs, cutting filth from clothing with scissors, specifying retaliation for murder and prohibiting taking blood money, leaving work on the Sabbath, and that their prayers are not permissible except in churches and other such hardships. It was likened to the shackles that bind the hand to the neck. So those who believed in him meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and supported him and honored him, and aided him against the enemies and followed the light that was sent down with him meaning the Qur’an they are the successful ones.
7:158: 158 - The Almighty said: “Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death. So believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet who believes in God and His words,’” meaning: His verses, which is the Qur’an. Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: He means Jesus, son of Mary, and it is read His word, and follow him that you may be guided.
7:159: 159 - The Almighty said: And among the people of Moses meaning the Children of Israel is a nation meaning a group guiding with the truth meaning: they direct and call to the truth. It was said: its meaning is they are guided and upright upon it, and by it they act justly meaning: they rule with the truth and act justly. Al-Kalbi, Al-Dahhak, and Al-Rabi’ said: They are a people behind China, in the far east on a river {that runs with sand} called the Udaf River. None of them has any wealth except his companion. They receive rain at night and are awake during the day, and they farm so that none of us can reach them, and they are on the right path. He mentioned: Gabriel, peace be upon him, took the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of his Isra’, and spoke to them. {Gabriel said to them: Do you know whom you are speaking to? They said: No. He said to them: This is Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, so believe in him.} They said: O Messenger of God, Moses, peace be upon him, commanded us that whoever among you meets Ahmad should greet him from us. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, responded to Moses and them, then he recited to them ten Surahs of the Qur’an that were revealed in Mecca, and he commanded them to pray and give zakat, and he commanded them to stay where they were. They used to observe the Sabbath, so he commanded them to gather and abandon the Sabbath. It was said: They are the Jews who converted to Islam during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The first is more correct.
7:160: 160 - The Almighty said: And We divided them, meaning: We divided them, meaning the Children of Israel, into twelve tribes, nations. Al-Farra’ said: He said: twelve, and sabt is masculine because he said: nations, so the feminine form refers back to nations. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: We divided them into twelve nations, and he said: tribes, nations. In the plural, and anything above ten cannot be interpreted in the plural, so it is not said: Twelve men came to me, because asbat in reality is an adjective for the omitted explanation, which is the group, meaning: And We divided them into twelve groups, nations. It was said: There is an advancement and delay in it, and its meaning is: And We divided them into twelve tribes, and the tribes are the tribes, the singular of which is a tribe. God Almighty said: And We inspired Moses when his people asked him for water in the wilderness, Strike the rock with your staff. Then water gushed forth. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: It sweated which is gushing forth, then it gushed forth. From it were twelve springs, for each tribe a spring. Every people knew, “every tribe” their drinking place, and each tribe had one branch. God Almighty says: And We shaded them with clouds in the wilderness to protect them from the heat of the sun, And We sent down upon them manna and quails, [saying], ‘Eat from the good things We have provided for you.’ And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.
7:161: 161 - And when it was said to them, Dwell in this city and eat from it wherever you wish and say, 'Forgiveness,' and enter the gate in prostration. We will forgive you," the people of Medina, Ibn Amir, and Yaqub read:تّدنرwith the ta' and a damma and a fatha on the fa'. The others read it with the nun and a fatha and a kasra on the fa', "your sins," Ibn Amir readخطياتكم in the singular and raising the ta', {Abu Amr read: خطياتكم, and the people of Medina and Yaqub read: خطياتكمin the plural and raising the ta'. The others read it in the plural and a kasra on the ta', "We will increase the doers of good."
7:162: 162 - But those who did wrong among them substituted other words than those spoken to them, so We sent upon them a punishment from the sky because they were wronging.
7:163: 163- The Almighty said: And ask them about the city that was by the sea It was said: It is Madyan, {that is: O Muhammad, ask these Jews who are your neighbors a question of rebuke and reprimand about the city that was by the sea} that is: near it. Ibn Abbas said: It is a village called Ilah between Madyan and Al-Tur on the seashore. Al-Zuhri said: It is Tiberias, Syria. When they transgressed on the Sabbath That is: They were unjust on it and transgressed the command of God Almighty to catch fish, When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day, in plain sight That is: Appearing on the water in large numbers, plural of street. Ad-Dahhak said: Consecutive. In the story: She used to come to them on Saturday like fat, white rams. And on a day when they do not observe the Sabbath, it will not come to them like their coming on the Sabbath. Al-Hasan read: they do not observe the Sabbath with a damma on the ya’, meaning: they do not enter the Sabbath. The well-known reading is with a nasb on the ya’, and its meaning is: they do not honor the Sabbath. Thus do We test them, we test them, by what they used to commit, so Satan whispered to them and said: God did not forbid you from hunting, but He forbade you from eating, so they hunted. Or it was said: He whispered to them that you were only forbidden from taking, so they built ponds on the shore of the sea, driving whales to them on the Sabbath, then taking them on Sunday. They did that for a while, then they dared to take the Sabbath, and they said: We do not see the Sabbath except that it has been made lawful for us, so they took and ate and sold, so the people of the village were divided into thirds, and they were about seventy thousand, a third forbade it, and a third did not forbid it and kept quiet and said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? A third were the people of sin. When they did not stop, the forbidding ones said: We will not live with you in one village. So they divided the village with a wall, one door for the Muslims and one door for the aggressors. David, peace be upon him, cursed them. Then one day, the forbidding ones came out and none of the aggressors came out. They said: They have a matter, perhaps the wine overcame them, so they did it on the wall. Then they were monkeys. The monkeys recognized their lineage from humans, but humans did not recognize their lineage from monkeys. So the monkeys would come to their human relatives and smell his clothes and cry. He would say: Did we not forbid you? They would say with their heads: Yes. Only the religion they forbade was saved, and the rest of them perished.
7:164: 164 - The Almighty said: And when a group of them said, 'Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy?' They differed about who said this. It was said: They were from the doomed group, because they were not told to stop this bad deed before the punishment descends upon you, and we know that God will send down His punishment upon you if you do not desist. They responded and said: Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy? or You know that He will punish them with a severe punishment? They said: That is, those who forbade said: As an excuse, that is, our preaching is an excuse to your Lord. Hafs read: As an excuse in the accusative, meaning we do that as an excuse to your Lord. The most correct view is that it is from the saying of the silent group. They said, Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy? They said, As an excuse to your Lord. Its meaning is that enjoining what is right is obligatory upon us, so we must preach to these people as an excuse to God. And perhaps they will fear God, meaning: they will fear God and abandon sin. If the address was to the aggressors, He would have said, Perhaps you will fear God.
7:165: 165 - So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, meaning: they abandoned what they had been admonished with, We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong, meaning the rebellious group, with a terrible punishment, meaning: severe and painful, from bas, which is severity. The reciters differed on it. The people of Medina and Ibn Amir recited ba’is with a kasra on the ba’, in the form fa’il, except that Ibn Amir pronounces it with a hamza. Abu Ja’far and Nafi’ do not pronounce it with a hamza. Asim recited in Abu Bakr’s narration with a fatha, with a sukun on the ya’, and with a fatha on the hamza, in the form fa’il, like sa’iqal. The others recited it with the form fa’il, like ba’ir and saghir. Because they were wicked, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: I hear God say: We saved those who forbade evil, and We seized those who did wrong with a terrible punishment, so I do not know what He did with the silent group? Ikrimah said: I said to him: May God make me your ransom, do you not see that they have denied and hated what they were doing, and said: Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy? And if God did not say, You saved us, then He did not say, You destroyed them. So he liked my statement, so he was pleased and ordered for me two cloaks and clothed me in them. Yaman bin Rabab said: The two groups were saved: those who said, Why do you preach to a people? and those who said, An excuse before your Lord. And God destroyed those who took the whales. This is what Al-Hasan said. Ibn Zayd said: The one who forbade was saved, and the two groups perished. This is the most severe verse in abandoning the prohibition of evil.
7:166: 166 - The Almighty said: But when they transgressed that which they were forbidden, Ibn Abbas said: They refused to return from the sin, We said to them, ‘Be apes, despised,’ banished, so they remained for three days while people looked at them, then they perished.
7:167: 167 - When your Lord proclaimed, meaning: your Lord proclaimed and informed. It is said: he proclaimed and he proclaimed, like he threatened and he threatened. Ibn Abbas said: your Lord proclaimed, your Lord said. Mujahid said: the command of your Lord. Ata' said: the judgment of your Lord. He will surely send upon them until the Day of Resurrection, meaning: upon the Jews, those who will afflict them with the worst of torment, God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation to fight them until they submit or pay the jizyah. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
7:168: 168 - And We divided them, and dispersed them into nations on the earth, groups that God dispersed, so their affair was scattered until they could come together as a word. Among them are the righteous, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: He means those who met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believed in him. And among them are those who are less than that, meaning those who remained in disbelief. Al-Kalbi said: Among them are the righteous who are beyond the Udaf River, beyond China, and among them are those who are below that, meaning: those here from the Jews, And We tested them with good things, with fertility and well-being, and bad things, with drought and hardship, that perhaps they would return, so that they would return to the obedience of their Lord and repent.
7:169: 169 - The Almighty said: Then there came after them those who came after them, meaning: after those whom we described came a successor, and the successor is the generation that comes after the generation. Abu Hatim said: The successor with a sukoon on the lam is the children, singular and plural alike, and the successor with a fatha on the lam is the substitute, whether it is a child or a stranger. Ibn Al-A'rabi said: Al-Khalaf with the fat-ha: the good, and with the jazm: the bad. Al-Nadr bin Shumayl said: The word al-Khalaf with a sukoon or a vowel on the lam in the word bad century is one, but in the word good century it is with a sukoon on the lam and nothing else. Muhammad bin Jarir said: Most of what came in praise is with the opening of the lam, and in blame with it being sukun. It may be moved in blame and sukun in praise. They inherited the Book, meaning: the Book passed to them from their fathers, which is the Torah. They take the goods of this lower world, so goods are the enjoyment of this world, and goods, with the sukun of the ra, are all the money other than dirhams and dinars. And the lower world meant the world, which is this transient abode, so it is a reminder of the world, and these Jews inherited the Torah, so they read it and neglected to act according to what was in it, and disobeyed its rulings, taking bribes in the ruling of God and changing His words, and they say, ‘He will forgive us,’ meaning our sins, wishing falsehoods from God. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah told us, Abu Tahir told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Harith told us, Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yaqub Al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah Al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam Al-Ghassani, on the authority of Damrah ibn Habib, on the authority of Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The intelligent person is he who judges himself and works for the afterlife, and the weak person is he who follows his desires and hopes for God. “And if something similar to it comes to them, they take it.” This is a statement about their eagerness for the world and their insistence on sins. He says that if something similar to it comes to them, they take it, whether it is lawful or unlawful, and they hope for forgiveness from God, and if they find something similar the next day, they take it. Al-Suddi said: The Children of Israel would not appoint a judge except that he would take a bribe in his judgment. It would be said to him: Why do you take a bribe? He would say: I will be forgiven, and the others would criticize him. Then, if he died or was removed and a man from those who criticized him was put in his place, he would also take a bribe. He says: And if something similar to it comes to the others, they would take it. Has not the covenant of the Book been taken from them that they will not say about God except the truth? That is, the covenant was taken from them in the Torah that they will not say falsehood about God, which is wishing for forgiveness with persistence, and there is no promise of forgiveness in the Torah that persists, and they studied what is in it, they read what is in it, so they remember that, and if they had understood it, they would have worked for the Hereafter. Studying the Book means reading it and contemplating it time after time, “and the Hereafter is better for those who fear God. So will you not reason?”
7:170: 170- And those who hold fast to the Book, Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim: hold fast with a light pronunciation, and the general reading is with a heavy pronunciation, because it is said: I held fast to something, and it is not said I held fast to something, rather it is said: I held fast to it, and Abi bin Kaab read: And those who hold fast to the Book, in the past tense, and it is good for the Almighty's saying: And establish prayer since it is rare for a past to be connected to a future except in meaning, {And He intended} those who act according to what is in the Book, Mujahid said: They are the believers from the People of the Book, Abdullah bin Salam and his companions, they held fast to the Book that Moses brought, they did not distort it, they did not conceal it, and they did not take it as food. And Ata' said: They are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. "And establish prayer. Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers."
7:171: 171 - The Almighty said: And when We lifted the mountain above them, meaning: We split the mountain, and it was said: We raised it as if it were a canopy, Ata' said: A roof. Canopy: everything that covers you, and they thought, they knew "that it would fall upon them. Take," meaning: We said to them, take, what We have given you with strength, with seriousness and effort, and remember what is in it, and act upon it, that you may become righteous, and that was when they refused to accept the rulings of the Torah, so God raised a mountain over their heads. Al-Hasan said: When they looked at the mountain, each one of them fell down prostrating on his left eyebrow, looking with his right eye at the mountain for fear that it would fall on him, and for this reason you will not find a Jew except that his prostration is on his left eyebrow.
7:172: 172 - The Almighty said: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants the verse. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Abi Anisa, on the authority of Abdul Hamid ibn Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Zayd ibn al-Khattab, who told him, on the authority of Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was asked about this verse: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants (al-Baqarah 2:17). Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, being asked about it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, created Adam, then wiped his back with His right hand and extracted from him offspring. He said: ‘I created these for Paradise and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise.’ Then He wiped his back and extracted from him offspring. He said: ‘I created these for Hell and they will do the deeds of the people of Hell.’ A man said: ‘Then what is the purpose of the deeds, O Messenger of God?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When God, the Almighty, creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and He enters him into Paradise because of it. And when He creates a servant for Hell, He employs him in the deeds of the people of Hell until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Hell, and He enters him into Hell because of it.’” Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a good hadith. Muslim ibn Yasar did not hear from ‘Umar, and some of them mentioned a man in this chain of transmission between Muslim ibn Yasar and ‘Umar. Muqatil and other commentators said: God wiped the right side of Adam’s back and brought out from it white offspring like moving particles. Then He wiped the left side of his back and brought out from it black offspring like moving particles. He said: O Adam, these are your offspring. Then He said to them: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. He said to the white ones: These are in Paradise with My mercy and I do not care. They are the companions of the right. He said to the black ones: These are in Hell and I do not care. They are the companions of the left. Then He returned them all to his loins. So the people of the graves are imprisoned until all the people of the covenant come out from the loins of men and the wombs of women. God the Most High said about those who broke the first covenant: And We did not find for most of them any covenant. (al-A’raf 7:102) Some of the commentators said: The people of happiness acknowledged it willingly and said: Yes, and the people of misery said it out of fear and unwillingness, and that is the meaning of His statement: And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly (Al Imran 3:83). They differed about the location of the covenant. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: In Batn Nu'man - a valley next to Arafat - and it was also narrated from him: It is in Dahna in the land of India, and it is the place where Adam (peace be upon him) descended. Al-Kalbi said: Between Mecca and Taif. Al-Suddi said: God brought Adam (peace be upon him) out of Paradise so he did not descend from the sky, then He wiped his back and brought out his offspring. It was narrated: God brought them all out and formed them and gave them minds with which they could work and tongues with which they could speak, then He spoke to them directly - meaning clearly - and said: Am I not your Lord? Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that God the Most High gave the likes of ants an understanding with which they could understand, as God the Most High said: An ant said, ‘O ants, enter your dwellings.’ (al-Naml 27:18) It was narrated that God the Almighty said to them all: Know that there is no god but Me, and I am your Lord. You have no lord but Me, so do not associate anything with Me, for I will take revenge on whoever associates anything with Me and does not believe in Me. I will send to you messengers who will remind you of My covenant and pledge, and I will send down to you books. So they all spoke and said: We bear witness that You are our Lord and our God. We have no lord but You. So He took their covenants with that, then He wrote down their terms, their provisions, and their calamities. Then Adam looked at them and saw among them the rich and the poor, the handsome and the less than that, so he said: O Lord, why did You not make them equal? He said: I would like to thank you. So when he confirmed their belief in His Oneness and made them testify against each other, He returned them to His loins. The Hour will not come until everyone from whom He took a covenant is born. This is what God Almighty said: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their loins. That is, from the loins of the children of Adam, their offspring. The people of Medina, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read: their offspring in the plural and with a kasra on the ta’. Others read: their offspring in the singular and with a fatha on the ta’. If it is said: What is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying, And when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their loins, and He only brought them out from the loins of Adam? It is said: God brought forth the descendants of Adam, some from the loins of others, in the same way that people are born from their fathers in order, so He dispensed with mentioning the loins of Adam when He knew that they were all his sons and brought forth from his loins. God Almighty says: And make them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They say, ‘Yes.’ That is, they make some of them testify of others: We testify that you say. Abu Amr read: that they say and they say with the letter ya in both of them, and the others read it with the letter ta in both of them. They differed concerning His statement: We bear witness. Al-Suddi said: It is report from God about Himself and His angels that they bore witness to the admission of the children of Adam. Some of them said: It is report about the statement of the children of Adam when God called some of them to witness against each other, and they said: Yes, we bear witness. Al-Kalbi said: That is from the statement of the angels, and there is an omission in it, the meaning of which is: When the offspring said: Yes, God said to the angels: Bear witness, they said: We bear witness. His statement: that they should say means: And He called them to witness against themselves that they should say, i.e. lest they should say or out of hatred for them to say. And whoever reads with the letter ta’, then the meaning of the statement is: I address you: Am I not your Lord, lest you say, On the Day of Resurrection, indeed, we were unaware of this, i.e., about this covenant and admission. If it is said: How can the argument be binding on someone who does not remember the covenant? It was said: God has made clear the evidence of His Oneness and the truthfulness of His Messengers in what they have informed us. Whoever denies it is obstinate and breaks the covenant, and the argument is binding on him. And because they forget and do not memorize, the argument does not fall away after the truthful informant, the owner of the miracle, informs.
7:173: 173 - The Almighty’s saying: Or you say, ‘Our fathers were polytheists before, and we were descendants after them.’ He says: The covenant was taken from you so that you would not say, O polytheists: Our fathers were polytheists before, and we broke the covenant, and we were descendants after them, meaning we were followers of them and we followed their example, so you would make this an excuse for yourselves and say, Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers have done? Will You punish us for the crime of our falsifying fathers? They cannot argue with such speech after God Almighty reminds us of the covenant taken on monotheism.
7:174: 174 - And thus do We explain the verses meaning: We explain the verses so that the servants may contemplate them, and perhaps they will return from disbelief to monotheism.
7:175: 175 - The Almighty said: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them the verse. They differed about him. Ibn Abbas said: He is Balaam bin Ba'oura. Mujahid said: Balaam bin Ba'er. Atiyah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He was from the Children of Israel. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, may God be pleased with him, that he was from the Canaanites from the city of the Jabbarin. Muqatil said: He is from the city of Balqa. And his story - as mentioned by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Ishaq, Al-Suddi and others - was that when Moses intended to fight the giants and settled in the land of the Canaanites in the land of Ash-Sham, the people of Balaam came to Balaam - and he had the greatest name of God - and they said: Moses is a man of iron and with him is a large army, and he came to expel us from our country and kill us and destroy the Children of Israel, and you are a man whose supplications are answered, so go out and supplicate to God to turn them away from us, so he said: Woe to you, the Prophet of God and with him are the angels and the believers, how can I supplicate against them while I know from God what I know, and if I do this, my world and my afterlife will be lost, so they went back to him and insisted, so he said: Until I command my Lord, and he did not supplicate until he saw what he was commanded to do in a dream, so he commanded to supplicate against them, so he was told in a dream do not supplicate against them, so he said to his people. I have commanded my Lord and I have forbidden. So they presented him with a gift and he accepted it. Then they went back to him and he said: Until I am commanded, so I command. But nothing was permissible to him. He said: I have commanded, but nothing was permissible to me. They said: If your Lord disliked that you should invoke curses upon them, He would have forbidden you as He forbade you the first time. So they continued to implore him until they tempted him, and he was tempted. So he rode his donkey towards a mountain that overlooked the camp of the Children of Israel, called Hisban. After he had walked on it for a short time, it lay down with him. So he got off it and beat it until it became soft, then he mounted it. It did not walk with him for long until it lay down. So he did the same to it and it stood up. So he mounted it and it did not walk with him for long until it lay down. So he struck it until it became soft. God permitted it to speak, so it spoke to him as an argument against him. She said: Woe to you, Balaam, where are you taking me? Do you not see the angels in front of me, preventing me from this path of mine? Are you taking me to the Prophet of God and the believers to invoke curses upon them? But he did not stop, so God set her free and she set off until she brought him to Mount Hisban. He began to invoke curses upon them, but he did not invoke anything upon them except that God turned his tongue to his people, and he did not invoke anything good upon his people except that God turned his tongue to the Children of Israel. His people said to him: O Balaam, do you know what you are doing? You are only invoking curses upon us?! He said: This is not what I own, this is something that God has overcome, so his tongue fell on his chest, and he said to them: Now the world and the hereafter have gone from me, and nothing remains but deceit and trickery, so I will deceive and scheme for you, beautify the women and adorn them and give them goods, then send them to the camp to sell them there, and order them that no woman should withhold herself from a man who wants her, for if one man of them commits adultery, you will be spared them, so they did. When the women entered the camp, a Canaanite woman named Kasti, daughter of Tsur, passed by a man from the nobles of the Children of Israel called Zimri, son of Shallum, head of the tribe of Simeon, son of Jacob, so he went to her and took her by the hand when he was pleased with her beauty, then he came with her until he stood with her in front of Moses, and he said: I think you will say this is forbidden to you? He said: Yes, it is forbidden to you, do not come near it. He said: By God, I will not obey you in this. Then he entered his tent with her and fell upon her. Then God sent the plague upon the Children of Israel at that time. Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, was the one in charge of Moses. He was a man who had been given great stature and strength in striking. He was absent when Zimri, son of Shallum, did what he did. Then he came while the plague was ravaging the Children of Israel. He reported the report, so he took his spear, which was all iron, and entered the tent upon them while they were lying down. He strung them together with his spear, then he went out with them, raising them to the sky. He held the spear in his arm and leaned his elbow on his waist. He leaned the spear against his beard. He was the firstborn of Eleazar. He kept saying: O God, this is what we do with those who disobey you. And the plague was lifted, and he calculated how many of the children of Israel had perished in the plague between the time Zimri afflicted the woman and the time Phinehas killed him, and they found that seventy thousand of them had perished in an hour of the day.
