So from there the children of Israel gave Phinehas’ son from every sacrifice they had slaughtered the hilt, the arm, and the beard, because he leaned the spear on his waist, took it with his arm, and supported it on his beard, and the firstborn from all their wealth and their lives, because he was the firstborn of Eleazar. And concerning Balaam God Almighty revealed, And recite to them the report of him to whom We gave Our signs 1:13. Muqatil said: The king of Balqa said to Balaam: Pray to God against Moses. He said: He is of my religion, I will not pray against him. So he carved a piece of wood to crucify him. When he saw that, he went out on his donkey to pray against him. When he saw their army, the donkey stood up and stopped, so he struck her. She said: Why did you strike me? I am ordered, and there is a fire in front of me that has prevented me from walking. So he returned and informed the king. He said: Either you pray against him or I will crucify you. So he prayed against Moses by the Greatest Name: that he not enter the city. His prayer was answered, and Moses and the Children of Israel fell into the wilderness because of his prayer. Moses said: O Lord, for what sin did we fall into the wilderness? He said: Because of the prayer of Balaam. He said: Just as you heard his prayer against me, hear my prayer against him. {So Moses, peace be upon him, prayed} that the Greatest Name and faith be taken away from him. So God took away knowledge from him and stripped him of it, so it came out of his chest like a white dove. That is what He said: And he stripped himself of it. Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Zaid bin Aslam said: This verse was revealed about Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt Al-Thaqafi. His story was: He had read the books and knew that God would send a messenger, so he hoped that he would be that messenger. When Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent, he envied him and disbelieved in him. He was a man of wisdom and good preaching. He used to visit some kings. When he returned, he passed by the dead of Badr and asked about them. It was said: Muhammad killed them. He said: If he was a prophet, he would not have killed his relatives. When Umayyah died, his sister Far’ah came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked her about the death of her brother. She said: While he was sleeping, two men came to him and uncovered the roof of the house. They came down and one of them sat at his feet and the other at his head. The one at his feet said to the one at his head: Did you remember? He said: Did you remember? He said: Is he pure? He said: My father. She said: So I asked him about that and he said: Good is intended for me. So he turned away from me and he fainted, and he did not regain consciousness. He said: Every life, no matter how long it lasts, will become bitter until it passes away. I wish I had been, before what happened to me, in the mountains of the tyrant, tending the ibex. The Day of Judgment is a great day, in which the young will grow old on a difficult day. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Recite to me some of your brother’s poetry. So she recited to him some of his poems, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: His poetry believed but his heart disbelieved. Then God Almighty revealed: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them. In a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about Basus, a man from the Children of Israel who had been given three answered prayers, and he had a wife who had a child from her. She said: Make me a prayer from her. He said: You have one of them, so what do you want? She said: Ask God to make me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. So he prayed for her and she was made the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. But when she knew that there was no one like her among them, she turned away from him. The husband became angry and prayed against her and she became a barking dog. So two prayers were lost for her. Then her sons came and said: We cannot stay like this. Our mother has become a barking dog, and people are taunting us because of her. Ask God to return her to the state she was in. So he prayed to God and she returned to the way she was, and all the prayers were lost for her. The first two opinions are more apparent. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: It was revealed about the hypocrites among the People of the Book who knew the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as they knew their own sons. Qatada said: This is a parable that God the Almighty gave for someone who was offered guidance but refused to accept it. This is what He said: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs. Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi said: The greatest name of God. Ibn Zayd said: He did not ask for anything except that He gave it to him. Ibn Abbas said in another narration: He was given a book from the books of God, but it was peeled off, meaning: He came out of it as a snake sheds its skin. Then Satan pursued him, meaning: He caught up with him and overtook him, and he was among the deviators.
7:176: 176 - And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby, meaning: We could have elevated his status and position by those verses. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: We elevated him by his knowledge of them. Mujahid and Ata' said: We removed disbelief from him and protected him by the verses. But he clung to the earth, meaning: He settled in the world and inclined towards it. Al-Zajjaj said: Khalada and Akhlad are one and the same. Its origin is from khulud which means permanence and residence. It is said: So-and-so clung to a place if he resided in it. The earth here refers to the world, because all the deserts and wildernesses in it are earth, and all its goods are extracted from the earth. And he followed his desire, he submitted to what his desires called him to. Ibn Zayd said: His desires were with the people. Ata' said: He wanted the world and obeyed his Satan. This is the most severe sign for scholars, for God informed us that He gave him a sign from His greatest name, answered prayers, knowledge and wisdom. Thus, by being content with the world and following desires, he deserved to change the blessing upon him and to be stripped of it. Who is safe from these two characteristics except for the one whom God has protected? Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mahmoud, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Zakariya ibn Abi Za’idah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa’d ibn Zararah, on the authority of Ka’b ibn Malik al-Ansari, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Two hungry wolves sent among sheep are not more destructive to them than a man’s greed for wealth and honor is to his religion. God Almighty said: “His example is that of a dog: if you chase him, he pants, or if you leave him alone, he pants.” It is said: The dog pants, panting, if he sticks out his tongue. Mujahid said: He is like the one who reads the Book but does not act upon it. Meaning: If you reprimand this infidel, he will not desist, and if you leave him alone, he will not be guided. The two states are the same to him, like the states of a dog: if he is chased and attacked, he will pant, and if he is left alone and satisfied, he will pant. Al-Qatibi said: Everything that pants only pants from exhaustion or thirst, except the dog, which pants when tired, at rest, and thirsty. So God made it an example for those who deny His signs, saying: If you admonish it, it is lost, and if you leave it, it is lost, like a dog. If you chase it, it pants, and if you leave it as it is, it pants. Similar to this is the saying of God Almighty: “And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or are silent” (al-A’raf 7:193). Then He made this example general for all those who deny the signs of God, saying: “That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the story that perhaps they will give thought.” It was said: This is an example for the infidels of Mecca, because they wished for a guide to guide them and call them to obey God, but when a prophet came to them whose truthfulness they had no doubt, they denied him, so they were not guided, whether they left him or left him.
7:177: 177 - Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs, meaning: Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs. The meaning is: Evil is the example of the people, so like was deleted and the people was put in its place, so it was raised, and they were wronging themselves.
7:178: 178 - He whom God guides is the guided one, and he whom He sends astray - it is those who are the losers.
7:179: 179 - And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. God Almighty informed us that He created many of the jinn and mankind for the Fire, and they are the ones upon whom the eternal word of misery has come true, and whoever God created for Hell has no way of escaping from it. Abu Bakr Yaqub bin Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ali al-Sayrafi told us, Abu Muhammad al-Hasan bin Ahmad al-Mukhalladi told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Abi Hamza al-Balkhi told us, Musa bin Muhammad bin al-Hakam al-Shatawi told us, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Talha bin Yahya, on the authority of Aisha bint Talha, on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, witnessed the funeral of a boy from the boys of the Ansar, and Aisha said: ‘Blessed is he, a bird from the birds of Paradise.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And how do you know? God created Paradise and created its people while they were in the loins of their fathers, and He created Hell and created its people while they were in the loins of their fathers.’” It was said: The lam in His statement, for Hell is the lam of consequence, meaning: We created them, and the consequence of their affair is Hell, like the statement of the Most High: So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might be to them an enemy and a grief (al-Qasas 28:8). Then He described them and said: They have hearts with which they do not understand, meaning they do not know goodness and guidance. And they have eyes with which they do not see, the path of truth and the way of right guidance. And they have ears with which they do not hear, the admonitions of the Qur’an, so they reflect on them and take heed from them. Then He gave them an example of ignorance and limiting themselves to eating and drinking, saying: Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray, meaning: like livestock in that their concern is eating, drinking, and enjoying desires, rather, they are more astray because livestock distinguish between harm and benefit, so they do not go ahead with harm, while these go ahead with the Fire in defiance, knowledge of destruction has passed. Those are the heedless.
7:180: 180 - The Almighty said: And to God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. Muqatil said: That is because a man called upon God in his prayer and called upon the Most Gracious, so some of the polytheists of Mecca said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions claim that they worship one Lord, so why does this man call upon two? So God, the Almighty, revealed: And to God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. The best is the feminine of the best, like the greater and the lesser, so invoke Him by them. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Al-Hussein bin Ali bin Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Bishran told us, Abu Ali Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Abdul-Razzaq told us, Muammar bin Hammam bin Munabbih told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever counts them will enter Paradise. He is odd and loves odd numbers.” And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names, Hamza read: Yalhadun - with the opening of the ya’ and the ha’ wherever it was - Al-Kisa’i agreed with him in An-Nahl, and the rest with the damma of the ya’ and the kasra of the ha’. The meaning of blasphemy is: to deviate from {the goal}. It is said: allahad yalhad lahudan: if he deviated. Ya’qub ibn Al-Sikkit said: blasphemy is to deviate from the truth and introduce into it what is not from it. It is said: allahad fi al-din, and lahadd, and Hamza read it with this. And leave those who deviate concerning His names: They are the polytheists who changed the names of God Almighty from what they are, so they named their idols with them, adding and subtracting, so they derived Al-Lat from God, Al-Uzza from Al-Aziz, and Manat from Al-Mannan. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. It was said: It is their calling idols gods. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They blaspheme in His names, meaning they lie. The scholars of meaning said: Blasphemy in the names of God: calling Him by what He was not called by, and was not mentioned in the Book of God or the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In sumMaryam 19:The names of God the Most High are based on revelation, for He is called Generous but not Generous, even if it has the same meaning as Generous. He is called Merciful but not Compassionate. He is called All-Knowing but not Wise. God the Most High said: They seek to deceive God, but He deceives them (An-Nisa’: 142). The Almighty said: And they plotted, and God plotted (AAl Imran 3:54). In supplication, one should not say: O Deceiver, O Deceiver. Rather, one should be called by His names that were revealed based on His love for glorification, so one should say: O God, O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful, O Almighty, O Generous, and so on. They will be recompensed for what they used to do in the Hereafter.
7:181: 181 - The Almighty said: And among those We created is a nation, meaning a group, who guide with the truth and do justice thereby. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are the emigrants and those who follow them in righteousness. Qatada said: It has reached us that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse, he would say: “This is for you, and the people before you have been given something similar. And among the people of Moses is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Al-Walid told us, Ibn Jaber told me, and he is Abdul Rahman bin Yazid bin Jaber, Umair bin Hani told me that he heard Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There will always be a group of my nation that upholds the command of God, and they will not be harmed by those who fail them or oppose them until the command of God comes and they are still like that.” Al-Kalbi said: They are from all of creation.
7:182: 182- And those who deny Our signs - We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know. Ata' said: We will plot against them from where they do not know. It was said: We will come to them from their place of safety, as in: Then God came to them from where they did not expect. (al-Hashr 59:2). Al-Kalbi said: He will make their deeds seem good to them and destroy them. Ad-Dahhak said: Whenever they commit a sin, We will renew a blessing for them. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: We bestow blessings upon them and make them forget to thank Him. The scholars of meanings said: Graduation means to gradually do something secretly, little by little, without being surprised or openly. From this comes the word daraj the child walks slowly, and from this comes the word daraj the book if he folds it little by little.
7:183: 183 - And I will give them respite, meaning: I will give them time and extend their lifespan so that they will persist in sins. Indeed, My plan is firm, meaning: My punishment is strong and severe. Ibn Abbas said: My plot is severe. It was said: It was revealed about the mockers, so God killed them in one night.
7:184: 184 - The Almighty said: Have they not considered what is in their companion? Qatada said: "It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on Safa at night and began calling out to the Quraysh, clan by clan: O sons of so-and-so, warning them of God's wrath and its events. Then one of them said: Your companion is mad, he kept shouting until morning. Then God Almighty revealed: "Have they not considered what is in their companion?" Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: "of madness" madness. "He is, what he is, only a clear warner", then he urged them to look to the path that leads to knowledge, saying:
7:185: 185 - Have they not considered the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what God has created in them of anything, meaning: and do they not consider what God has created of things to prove His Oneness. And that perhaps their time has drawn near, meaning: perhaps their time has drawn near and they die before they believe and are sent to the punishment, Then in what statement after it will they believe?, meaning: after the Qur'an will they believe? He says: in what book other than what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought will they believe, and there is no prophet or book after him, then he mentioned the reason for their turning away from belief and said:
7:186: 186 - He whom God sends astray, there is no guide for him, and He abandons them. The people of Basra and Asim read it with the letter ya and raising the letter ra. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with the letter ya and making the letter ra in the subjunctive mood, because the mention of God had come before it, and making the letter ra in the subjunctive mood is a response to misleads. Others read it with the letter noon and raising the letter ra as if it were a new statement. In their transgression they wander blindly, they hesitate and are perplexed.
7:187: 187 - The Almighty said: "They ask you about the Hour: when will it come to pass?" Qatada said: Quraysh said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is kinship between us and you, so tell us, when will the Hour come?" So God, the Almighty, revealed: "They ask you about the Hour," meaning: the Resurrection. "When will it come to pass?" Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: its end. Qatada said: its establishment, and its root is steadfastness, meaning: when will it be established? "Say, O Muhammad, its knowledge is only with my Lord," He has kept its knowledge to Himself and no one knows it except Him. "He will not reveal it," He will not uncover it or make it apparent. Mujahid said: No one will bring it about, "its time except Him. It is heavy in the heavens and the earth," meaning: its knowledge is heavy and its matter is hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth, and everything hidden is heavy. Al-Hasan said: He says that when it comes, it will be heavy and overwhelming for the people of the heavens and the earth, It will not come to you except suddenly, suddenly, without warning. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, Abu Al-Zinad told us on the authority of Abdul Rahman Al-Araj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will come while two men have spread their garments between them, but they will neither buy nor fold them. The Hour will come while a man has brought milk from his she-camel, but he will not eat it. The Hour will come while he is cleaning his trough, but he will not water his camel from it. The Hour will come while a man has raised his food to his mouth, but he will not eat it.” They ask you as if you were knowledgeable about it, meaning: you are knowledgeable about it, from their saying you exaggerated in the question, meaning: you went to extremes in asking about it until you knew it. “Say: Its knowledge is only with God, but most people do not know,” that its knowledge is with God until they asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it.
7:188: 188 - "Say: I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm except what God wills." Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The people of Mecca said: O Muhammad, does not your Lord inform you of the cheap price before it increases so that you can buy it and profit from it when it increases? And of the land that He wants to become barren so that you can travel to a land that has become fertile? So God, the Most High, revealed: "Say: I do not possess for myself any benefit," meaning: I do not have the power to bring benefit for myself, i.e. to gain benefit by making a profit, nor to cause harm, i.e. to repel harm by moving from a land that is about to become barren, except what God wills that I possess. And if I had known the unseen, I would have increased in good, and no harm would have touched me, meaning: if I had known fertility and drought, I would have increased in good, meaning: money, during the year of famine, and no harm would have touched me, meaning: harm, poverty, and hunger. Ibn Jurayj said: “Say: I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm,” meaning: guidance or misguidance. And if I had known the unseen, meaning: when death would be, I would have increased in goodness, meaning: righteous deeds, and no harm would have touched me. Ibn Zayd said: I avoided evil and guarded against it. It was said: Its meaning is, And if I knew the unseen, when the Hour will be, I would have informed you so that you would believe, and no harm would have touched me because of your denial. It was said: No harm would have touched me is the beginning, meaning: No madness would have touched me because they attributed it to madness. I am only a warner to those who do not believe in what I have brought, and a bringer of good tidings of Paradise, for a people who believe who believe.
7:189: 189 - The Almighty said: It is He who created you from one soul, meaning Adam, and made, and created from it its mate, meaning Eve, that he might dwell in tranquility with her, so that he might find comfort in her and take refuge with her. Then when he covered her, meaning he had intercourse with her and had sexual intercourse with her, she bore a light burden, which is the first thing a woman bears from the sperm that is light for her. She passed through it, meaning she continued with it, stood and sat with it, it did not burden her. Then when it became heavy, meaning the child grew in her womb and she became heavy with her pregnancy and her birth was near, they called upon God, their Lord, meaning Adam and Eve, If You should give us, O our Lord, a good one, meaning a normal human being like us, we will surely be among the grateful. The commentators said: When Eve became pregnant, Satan came to her in the form of a man and said to her: What is in your womb? She said: I do not know. He said: I fear that it may be an animal, a dog, or a pig. How do you know where it will come out from? From your anus and kill you, or from your front and rip your belly open? Eve was afraid of that and mentioned that to Adam, peace be upon him, and they were both worried about that. Then he came back to her and said: I am in a position with God, so if you ask God to make him a well-mannered person like you and make his exit easy for you, you will name him Abd al-Harith? Iblis’s name among the angels was al-Harith. She mentioned that to Adam, and he said to her: Perhaps he is our friend whom you know. Iblis came back to her and kept on at them until he deceived them. When she gave birth, they named him Abd al-Harith. Al-Kalbi said: Satan said to her: If I call upon God and give birth to a human being, will you name him after me? She said: Yes. So when she gave birth, he said: Name him after me. She said: What is your name? Al-Harith said: If he had named himself for her, she would have known him, so she named him Abd al-Harith. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: Eve would give birth to Adam’s children and he would name them Abdullah, Ubaidullah, and Abd al-Rahman. Then death would overtake them. Then Satan came to them and said: If you wish for a child to live, name him Abd al-Harith. So she gave birth and they named him Abd al-Harith, and he lived. It was stated in the hadith: Satan deceived them twice, once in Paradise and once on Earth. Ibn Zayd said: A son was born to Adam, and he named him Abdullah. Then Satan came to them and said: What did you name your son? They said: Abdullah. A son had been born to them before that, and they named him Abdullah, but he died. Satan said: Do you think that God will leave His servant with you? No, by God, He will take him away as He took the other, but I will show you a name that will remain with you as long as you live. So they named him Abd Shams, and the first is more correct. That is what He said:
7:190: 190 - So when He gave them both a righteous man, a well-proportioned human being, they made partners for Him in what He had given them, the people of Medina and Abu Bakr read: partnership with a kasra on the sheen and the tanween, meaning: partnership. Abu Ubaidah said: meaning a portion and share, and others read: partners with a damma on the sheen and extended on the plural of partner, meaning: Iblis, he informed about the singular in the plural form. That is: they made a partner for Him when they named him Abd al-Harith, and this was not a partnership in worship nor that al-Harith was their Lord, for Adam was a prophet who was protected from polytheism, but what was meant was that al-Harith was the reason for the child's salvation and the safety of his mother, and the name slave may be given to someone who is not meant to be owned, just as the name Lord is given to someone who is not meant to be worshipped, like a man who, when a guest visits him, calls himself Abd al-Daif, out of submission, not because the guest is his Lord, and he says to others: I am your slave. Joseph said to the Aziz of Egypt: He is my Lord, but he did not mean that he was his god. This is the same. And his saying: So God is exalted above what they associate with Him, it was said: This is the beginning of a statement and he meant by it the association of the people of Mecca, and if he meant by it what precedes, then it is correct in that it would have been better for them not to have done what they did of associating partners with God in the name. There is another saying about the verse: It refers to all the polytheists from the descendants of Adam, and this is the saying of Al-Hasan and Ikrimah, and its meaning is: He made their children partners, so He omitted the children and put them in their place, just as He added the actions of the fathers to the children in reproaching them for the actions of the fathers, so He said: Then you took the calf, “And when you killed a soul,” He addressed the Jews who were in the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that action was from their fathers. It was said: They are the Jews and Christians, God gave them children who became Jews and Christians. Ibn Kaysan said: They are the infidels who named their children Abd Al-Uzza, Abd Al-Lat, Abd Manat, and the like. And Ikrimah said: He addressed each one of creation by saying, He created you, meaning He created each one from his father and made from her his mate, meaning He made from her her mate. This is a good statement, were it not for the statement of the predecessors, such as Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Mujahid and Saeed ibn al-Musayyab and a group of commentators, that it was about Adam and Eve. God Almighty said: So God is exalted above what they associate with Him.
7:191: 191 - The Almighty’s saying: Do they associate with Him that which does not create anything? meaning: Satan and the idols, and they themselves are created, meaning: they are created.
7:192: 192 - And they cannot help them meaning: the idols cannot help those who obey them. Nor can they help themselves, Al-Hasan said: They cannot protect themselves from harm from those who intend to harm them with a kasra or something similar. Then he addressed the believers and said:
7:193: 193 - And if you invite them to guidance, and if you invite the polytheists to Islam, they will not follow you, Nafi' read it with a light emphasis, and so did: The deviators follow them (Ash-Shu'ara': 244). Others read it with a heavy emphasis in both of them, and they are two dialects. It is said: He followed him and He followed him, and He followed him, It is the same for you whether you invite them, to the religion, or whether you are silent, about their invitation, they will not believe, as He said: It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them, they will not believe (al-Baqarah 2:6). It was said: And if you invite them to guidance, meaning: the idols, they will not follow you because they are not rational.
7:194: 194 - Indeed, those you invoke besides God, meaning the idols, are servants like you, meaning that they are owned by people like you. It was said: Your likes are in subjection, meaning: they are subjected and humiliated for what is wanted from them. Muqatil said: His statement Servants like you meant the angels, and the address was to a people who used to worship the angels. The first is more correct. So call upon them and let them respond to you if you should be truthful, that they are gods. Ibn Abbas said: So worship them, will they reward you or recompense you if you are truthful that you have benefit from them? Then he explained their inability and said:
7:195: 195 - Do they have feet with which they walk, or do they have hands with which they strike? Abu Ja`far read with a damma on the ta' here and in Al-Qasas and Ad-Dukhan, and others read with a kasra on the ta', Or do they have eyes with which they see, or do they have ears with which they hear? He meant that the power of the created beings is through these limbs and tools, and the idols do not have these tools, so you are superior to them with the walking feet, the striking hands, the seeing eyes, and the hearing ears, so how do you worship those who are better and more powerful than you? "Say, 'Call upon your partners,' O group of polytheists, 'Then plot,' you and they, 'and do not wait,' meaning: Do not give me respite, and hasten in my plot.
7:196: 196 - Indeed, my ally is God, who revealed the Book, meaning the Qur’an, meaning that He takes me under His protection and supports me as He supported me by revealing the Book, and He takes care of the righteous, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: He means those who do not equate anything with God, so God takes care of them with His support, and the enmity of those who are hostile to them does not harm them.
7:197: 197 - And those whom you call upon besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.
7:198: 198 - "And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear, meaning the idols, and you see them, O Muhammad, looking at you, meaning the idols, while they do not see." Looking does not mean actually looking, but rather facing. The Arabs say: My house looks at your house, meaning: it faces it. It was said: And you see them looking at you, meaning: as if they are looking at you, like the Almighty's saying: "And you see the people drunk" (al-Hajj 22:2), meaning: as if they are drunk. This is the saying of {most} of the commentators. Al-Hasan said: "And if you call them to guidance," meaning: the polytheists, they do not hear nor do they do that with their hearts, and you see them looking at you with their eyes while they do not see with their hearts.
7:199: 199 - The Almighty said: Take what is easy, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr said: God commanded his prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to take what is easy from people's morals. Mujahid said: Take what is easy means taking what is easy from people's morals and actions without spying, such as accepting an apology, pardoning, being lenient, not searching for things, and the like. It was narrated that when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: What is this? He said: I do not know until I ask him. Then he returned and said: Your Lord commands you to connect with those who have severed ties with you, give to those who have deprived you, and forgive those who have wronged you. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, As-Suddi, Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi said: It means take what you have been forgiven of wealth, which is what is left over from your family. This is the meaning of His statement: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say: ‘The excess.’” (al-Baqarah 2:219). Then this was abrogated by the obligatory charity. God the Almighty said: And enjoin what is right. This means what is right, which is everything that is recognized by the Shari’ah. Ata’ said: And enjoin what is right, ‘There is no god but God.’ (Al-Bukhari: 107). And turn away from the ignorant, Abu Jahl and his companions. This was abrogated by the verse of the sword. It was said: If an ignorant person treats you foolishly, do not respond to him foolishly. This is like His statement: “And when the ignorant address them, they say, ‘Peace.’” (al-Furqan 25:63). This is the greeting of abandonment. Ja’far As-Sadiq said: God commanded His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to have good morals, and there is no verse in the Quran that is more comprehensive of good morals than this verse. Abdullah bin Abdul Samad {Al-Jurjani} told us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, Al-Haitham bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Jadali, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was neither obscene nor vulgar nor loud in the markets, and he did not repay evil with evil, but he pardoned and forgave.” Abu al-Fadl Ziyad bin Muhammad al-Hanafi narrated to us, Abu Saeed Abdul Malik bin Abi Uthman al-Wa’iz narrated to us, Imad bin Muhammad al-Baghdadi narrated to us, Ahmad bin Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed al-Hafiz, Muhammad bin Ismail narrated to us, Umar bin Ibrahim, meaning al-Kufi, narrated to us, Yusuf bin Muhammad bin al-Munkadir narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God sent me to perfect noble morals and perfect good deeds.
7:200: 200 - The Almighty said: "And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan," meaning: if an evil suggestion comes to you, befalls you, or comes to you from Satan. The evil suggestion from Satan is a whisper. Al-Zajjaj said: The evil suggestion is the slightest movement from a human being, and from Satan the slightest whisper. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: "When this verse was revealed: 'Show forgiveness,' the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How, O Lord, and anger? Then the verse was revealed: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God, meaning: seek refuge in God. For He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
7:201: 201 - Indeed, those who fear God, meaning the believers, when an impulse from Satan touches them, Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra, and Al-Kisa'i read: Tayf, and the others read Ta'if with a long vowel and a hamza, and they are two languages like Al-Mayt and Al-Mayt and their meanings are: something that touches you. Some people differentiated between them, so Ibn Amr said: Al-Ta'if is what surrounds something, and Al-Tayf is the gathering and whispering. It was said: Al-Ta'if is what surrounds it from the whisperings of Satan, and Al-Tayf is the gathering and the touch. Remember, they knew. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the man who becomes angry and remembers God and suppresses his anger. Mujahid said: It is the man who is about to commit a sin and remembers God and abandons it. Then they will see, meaning they will see the locations of their sins through remembrance and contemplation. Al-Suddi said: If they slip, they will repent. Muqatil said: If the pious person is tempted by a temptation from Satan, he will remember and know that it is a sin, so he will see and refrain from disobeying God.
7:202: 202 - His statement: And their brothers support them, meaning the brothers of the devils from the polytheists support them, meaning: the devil supports them. Al-Kalbi said: Every disbeliever has a brother from the devils. In error, meaning: they seek to mislead them so that they continue in it. It was said: they increase them in misguidance. The people of Madinah read: They support them with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the meem, from the word imdad, and the others read: with a fatha on the ya and a damma on the meem, and they are two dialects with the same meaning. Then they do not stop, meaning: they do not stop. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: Neither do mankind stop from the evil deeds they do, nor do the devils refrain from them, so based on this his statement: Then they do not stop is from the actions of the polytheists and devils together. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: It means that the polytheists do not refrain from misguidance nor do they see it, unlike what He said about the believers: They remembered, and at once they saw.
7:203: 203 - And if you do not bring them a sign, meaning: if you do not bring the polytheists a sign, "they will say: Why did you not choose it?" Why did you not invent it and create it of your own free will? The Arabs say: I invented the speech if you fabricated it. Al-Kalbi said: The people of Mecca used to ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for signs out of stubbornness, and if he was late, they would accuse him and say: Why did you not choose it? That is: Why did you not invent it and create it of your own free will? Say to them, O Muhammad, I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord, then he said: This, meaning: the Qur'an, is insight, arguments, clarification, and proof from your Lord, the singular of which is insight, and its origin is the appearance of something and its solidity until a person sees it and is guided by it. He says: These are signs that lead you to the truth. And guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
7:204: 204 - The Almighty said: And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy. They differed about the reason for the revelation of this verse. A group said that it was about recitation during prayer. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that they used to talk during prayer about their needs, so they were ordered to be silent and listen to the recitation of the Qur'an. Some people said: It was revealed about not reciting aloud behind the imam. It was narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: This verse was revealed regarding raising one’s voice while praying behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Kalbi said: They would raise their voices in prayer when they heard mention of Heaven and Hell. On the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, that he heard some people reading while the imam was reciting. When he finished, he said: Is it not time for you to understand? When the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent as God has commanded you. This is the statement of Al-Hasan, Al-Zuhri, and Al-Nakha’i: that the verse is about reading during prayer. Saeed bin Jubair, Ata’ and Mujahid said: The verse is about the sermon. They were ordered to listen to the sermon of the imam on Friday. Saeed bin Jubair said: This is about listening to the day of Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr and Friday, and to what the imam recites out loud. Omar bin Abdul Aziz said: It is necessary to listen to the words of every preacher. The first is more appropriate, which is that it is in the recitation during prayer because the verse is Meccan and Friday prayers were obligatory in Medina. They agreed that one is commanded to listen while the imam is giving the sermon. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal, on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Shafi’i, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you say to your companion, ‘Be quiet,’ while the imam is delivering the sermon on Friday, then you have engaged in idle talk. Scholars differed regarding reciting behind the imam during prayer. A group held that it is obligatory, whether the imam recites aloud or silently. This was narrated on the authority of Umar, Uthman, Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Muadh, and it is the opinion of Al-Awza’i and Al-Shafi’i. Some people said that he should recite in what the imam recites quietly, but he should not recite when he recites aloud. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, and it is the opinion of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad. Al-Zuhri, Malik, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq said the same. Some people said that he should not recite, whether the imam recites silently or aloud. This was narrated on the authority of Jabir, and this is what al-Thawri and the people of opinion said. Those who do not see recitation behind the imam adhere to the apparent meaning of this verse, and those who made it obligatory said that the verse is not in the Fatiha, and if he recites the Fatiha, he follows the imam’s pauses and does not dispute the imam in the recitation. The evidence for this is what Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi, on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mahboubi, on the authority of Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Hannad, on the authority of Abdah bin Sulayman, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Mahmoud bin Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer and the recitation became difficult for him, so when he finished he said: ‘I see you reciting behind your imam?’ We said: ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Do not do that except with the Mother of the Book, for there is no prayer for the one who does not recite it.’”
7:205: 205 - The Almighty said: And remember your Lord within yourself, Ibn Abbas said: He means by remembrance: reading in prayer, meaning reading secretly to himself, in humility and in secret, fear, meaning: you supplicate to Me and fear Me. This is in the secret prayer. And His saying: and without raising your voice loudly, he meant in the loud prayer, very loudly, rather in a low voice and quiet, so that those behind you can hear. Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: He commanded that they remember Him in their hearts by supplicate to Him in supplication and humility without raising the voice and shouting the supplication in the mornings and the evenings and do not be among the heedless, meaning: in the early mornings and the evenings, the singular of asal is asil like yameen and yameen, and it is between the afternoon and sunset.
7:206: 206 - Indeed, those who are with your Lord, meaning: the angels who are brought near with grace and honor, are not too proud, are not too proud, to worship Him, and they glorify Him, and declare Him pure and remember Him, saying: Glory be to God. And to Him they prostrate. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hairi told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Abd Al-Rahim bin Munib told us, Ya’la bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the son of Adam recites a verse of prostration and prostrates, Satan withdraws, weeping, and says: ‘Woe to him! This one was commanded to prostrate, and he prostrated, so Paradise is his. I was commanded to prostrate, but I disobeyed, so Hell is mine.’” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, on the authority of Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an, on the authority of Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani, on the authority of Hamid bin Zanjawayh, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Hisham, on the authority of Ma’dan, who said: I asked Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: Tell me a hadith that God will benefit me with. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no servant who prostrates to God once but that God raises him a degree thereby and removes a sin from him thereby.
8:1: Madinan, and it consists of seventy-five verses. It was said: Except for seven verses from His saying, And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to the last seven verses, which were revealed in Mecca. The most correct view is that they were revealed in Medina, even though the event took place in Mecca. 1 - They ask you about the spoils of war the verse. The commentators said: The reason for the revelation of this verse is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Badr: Whoever comes to such and such a place will have such and such of the spoils of war, and whoever kills someone will have such and such, and whoever takes a prisoner prisoner will have such and such. When they met, the young men rushed to him, and the elders and prominent people stayed by the banners. When God granted victory to the Muslims, they came seeking what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had given them. The elders said: We were a support for you, and if you had been defeated, you would have joined us, so do not take the spoils without us. Abu Al-Yusr bin Amr Al-Ansari, the brother of Banu Salamah, stood up and said: O Messenger of God, you promised that whoever killed someone would get such-and-such, and whoever took a prisoner would get such-and-such. We have killed seventy of them and taken seventy of them prisoner. Sa`d bin Mu`adh may God be pleased with him stood up and said: By God, O Messenger of God, what prevented us from seeking what these people sought was neither a lack of reward nor cowardice in the face of the enemy, but we hated to expose your ranks, lest the horses of the polytheists turn against you and strike you. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned away from them. Sa`id said: O Messenger of God, the people are many and the spoils are less than that, so if you give to those whom you mentioned, nothing much will remain for your companions. So this verse was revealed: They ask you about the spoils. Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that what was in the army be collected, and the Muslims differed about it. Those who collected it said: It is ours, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given each man what he had acquired as a gift. Those who were fighting the enemy said: If it were not for us, you would not have acquired it. Those who were guarding the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We saw fit to kill the enemy and take the goods, but we feared for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the enemy might attack us, and we stood up to protect him, for you are not more deserving of it than we are. Makhul narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili, who said: I asked Ubadah ibn al-Samit about the spoils of war. He said: It was revealed about us, the companions of Badr, when we disagreed about the voluntary spoils of war and our morals deteriorated. So God took it out of our hands and gave it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among us equally. In that was piety to God, obedience to His Messenger, and reconciliation between us. Saad bin Abi Waqqas, may God be pleased with him, said: “On the day of Badr, my brother Umair was killed, and I killed Saeed bin Al-Aas bin Umayya, and I took his sword, which was called Dhu Al-Katheetha, and I liked it so I brought it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, God has healed my chest from the polytheists, so grant me this sword. He said: This is not for me or for you, go and throw it in the handcuffs. So I threw it and returned, and I had what only God knows about the killing of my brother and the taking of my weapon, and I said: Perhaps this sword will be given to someone who has not suffered as I have. I had only gone a little while before the Messenger came to me, and God Almighty had revealed: “They ask you about the spoils of war,” the verse. I feared that something had been revealed about it, so when I reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: O Saad, you asked me for the sword and it was not mine, and now it is mine, so go and take it, it is yours.” Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The spoils of war were exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one else had a share in them. Whatever the Muslim armies captured of anything, they brought it to him. Whoever withholds a needle or a wire from it, it is considered theft. His saying: They ask you about the spoils of war means: about the ruling on the spoils of war and knowledge of them. It is a question of inquiry, not a question of request. It was said: it is a question of request. This was said by Ad-Dahhak and Ikrimah. His saying: About the spoils of war means: from the spoils of war, about means from. It was said: about is a connection, meaning: they ask you about the spoils of war, and this is the reading of Ibn Masoud without about. The spoils of war are the spoils of war, the singular of which is nafal, and its root is increase. It is said: I gave you and I gave you meaning: I increased you. The spoils of war were called anfal because they are an increase from God Almighty for this nation in particular. Most commentators agree that the verse is about the spoils of Badr. Ata’ said: It is what the polytheists took over from the Muslims without fighting, whether male or female slaves or property, so it is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do with it as he wishes. The Almighty said: “Say: ‘The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.’” {He divides them as He wills.} They differed concerning it. Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Al-Suddi said: This verse was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils - a fifth of it belongs to God and to the Messenger. The spoils at that time belonged to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God Almighty abrogated it with a fifth. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: It is established and not abrogated. The meaning of the verse is: Say: The spoils of war belong to God, this world and the Hereafter, and to the Messenger. He places them where God Almighty commands him. That is, the judgment in them belongs to God and His Messenger. God has explained their uses in His Almighty saying: And know that whatever you obtain of anything - a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger Al-Anfal 2:17. So fear God and amend your affairs, meaning: fear God by obeying Him and amend your affairs by abandoning disputes and disagreements, and submitting the matter of the spoils to God and the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And obey God and His Messenger, if you are believers.
8:2: 2 - The believers are only, he says, not the believer who disobeys God and His Messenger, but the believers are sincere in their faith, who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, their hearts become afraid and trembling. It was said: When they are frightened by God, they submit out of fear of His punishment. And when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith, belief and certainty. Umair bin Habib, who was a companion of the Prophet, said: Faith has an increase and a decrease. It was said: What is its increase? He said: If we remember God the Almighty and praise Him, that is its increase, and if we forget and neglect, that is its decrease. Umar bin Abdul Aziz wrote to Adi bin Adi: Faith has obligations, conditions, laws, limits, and Sunnahs, so whoever completes them has completed faith, and whoever does not complete them has not completed faith. And upon their Lord they rely, meaning: they entrust their affairs to Him, trust in Him, and do not hope in anyone other than Him, nor do they fear anyone other than Him.
8:3: 3- Those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them.
8:4: 4 - Those are the true believers, meaning certainly. Ibn Abbas said: They were innocent of disbelief. Muqatil said: Truly, there is no doubt about their faith. And in it is evidence that not everyone can describe himself as a true believer because God Almighty only described a specific people with specific descriptions, and not everyone has those descriptions. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: A man asked Al-Hasan, saying: Are you a believer? He said: If you are asking me about belief in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, Paradise, Hell, resurrection, and accountability, then I believe in them. But if you are asking me about His statement: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful (al-Baqarah 2:14), then I do not know whether I am one of them or not. Alqamah said: We were on a journey and we met some people. We said: Who are these people? They said: We are the true believers. We did not know how to answer them until we met Abdullah ibn Masoud and told him what they had said. He said: What did you say to them? We said: We did not say anything to them. He said: Why didn’t you say: Are you from the people of Paradise? The believers are the people of Paradise. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Whoever claims that he is truly a believer or that he is with God, but does not testify that he is in Paradise, has believed in half of the verse, but not the other half. They will have degrees with their Lord. Ata’ said: He means the degrees of Paradise which they ascend through their deeds. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: Seventy degrees, between every two degrees the distance between which a well-trained horse would travel for seventy years. And forgiveness, for their sins, and generous provision, good, meaning what is prepared for them in Paradise.
8:5: 5 - The Almighty’s saying: As your Lord brought you out from your home with truth, they differed about the reason for this kaf in His saying As your Lord brought you out, Al-Mubarrad said: Its meaning is that the spoils are for God and the Messenger, even if they disliked it, just as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth, even if they disliked it. And it was said: Its meaning is: Go ahead with God’s command regarding the spoils, even if they disliked it, just as you went ahead with God’s command in leaving the home to seek the caravan, even though they were reluctant. Ikrimah said: Its meaning is, fear God and reconcile your differences, for that is better for you, just as expelling Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his home by right is better for you, even if a group of you hate it. Mujahed said: Its meaning is that just as your Lord brought you out of your home with the truth, despite the reluctance of a group of them, so they hate fighting and argue about it. It was said: It refers to his saying: They will have degrees with their Lord, meaning: God promised them degrees, a right that God Almighty will fulfill, just as He brought you out. From your home with truth, fulfill the promise of victory and triumph. It was said: The Kaf means upon, meaning: Continue on what your Lord brought you out of. Abu Ubaidah said: It means an oath metaphorically, and the one who brought you out, because what is in the place of who, and its answer is they argue with you, and the oath falls on this, its meaning is: they argue with you, and God is the one who brought you out of your home with the truth. It was said: The Kaf means when, and its meaning is: And remember when your Lord brought you out. It was said: What is meant by this expulsion is his expulsion from Mecca to Medina. Most of them are of the opinion that what is meant by it is his expulsion from Medina to Badr, meaning: Just as your Lord commanded you to leave your home to Medina with the truth, it was said: By revelation to seek out the polytheists, And indeed, a party of the believers, from them, are averse.
8:6: 6 - They argue with you about the truth, that is, about fighting, after it has become clear, and that is because when the believers were certain of fighting, they hated it, and said: Why did you not know that we would meet the enemy and prepare to fight them, but we went out for the caravan? This is their argument after it became clear to them that you would not do anything except what you were commanded to do, and your truthfulness in your promise became clear, as if they were being driven to death due to their intense hatred of fighting, while they were watching, there is an inversion, its meaning is: And indeed, a group of the believers are averse, as if they were being driven to death while they were watching, arguing with you about the truth after it has become clear. Ibn Zayd said: These polytheists argued with him about the truth as if they were being driven to death when they were called to Islam due to their hatred of it while they were watching.
8:7: 7 - The Almighty said: And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours, Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Muhammad Ibn Ishaq, and al-Suddi said: Abu Sufyan came from the Levant with a caravan of Quraysh with forty riders from the infidels of Quraysh, among them: Amr Ibn al-Aas, and Mukhramah Ibn Nawfal al-Zuhri, and in it was a lot of trade, which is al-Latimah, until they were close to Badr, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of that, so he called his companions to him and informed them of the abundance of money and the small number, and he said: This is the caravan of Quraysh in which is your money, so go out to it, perhaps God Almighty will give it to you, so the people volunteered, some of them lightly and some of them heavy, and that was because they did not think that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would encounter war. When Abu Sufyan heard about the Prophet’s march, may God bless him and grant him peace, he hired Damdam bin Amr al-Ghifari and sent him to Mecca. He ordered him to go to the Quraysh and mobilize them and inform them that Muhammad had attacked their caravan with his companions. Damdam quickly set out for Mecca. Three nights before Damdam came to Mecca, Atika bint Abdul Muttalib saw a vision that frightened her. She sent to her brother Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib and said to him: O my brother, by God, I saw a vision last night that frightened me and I feared that evil and calamity would befall your people because of it, so keep what I am telling you a secret. He said to her: What did you see? She said: I saw a rider coming on his camel until he stopped in Al-Abtah, then he shouted at the top of his voice: O people of treachery, go forth to your deaths in three days. I saw the people gathered around him. Then he entered the mosque and the people were following him. While they were around him, he made his camel stand on the roof of the Kaaba and shouted in the same voice in the same voice: O people of treachery, go forth to your deaths in three days. Then he made his camel stand on the top of Abu Qubays and he shouted in the same voice. Then he took a rock and anchored it and it began to fall until it reached the bottom of the mountain. It collapsed and there was not a house in Mecca or a house in its dwellings that it did not enter, terrified. Al-Abbas said: By God, this is a dream I saw! Keep it a secret and do not mention it to anyone. Then Al-Abbas went out and met Al-Walid bin Utbah bin Rabi’ah bin Abd Shams, who was a friend of his. He mentioned it to him and asked him to keep it a secret. Al-Walid mentioned it to his father Utbah, and the story spread until the Quraysh talked about it. Al-Abbas said: So I went out to circumambulate the House, and Abu Jahl bin Hisham was sitting with a group of Quraysh talking about Atika’s vision. When Abu Jahl saw me, he said: O Abu al-Fadl, when you have finished your circumambulation, come to us. He said: So when I had finished, I came and sat with them, and Abu Jahl said to me: O sons of Abdul Muttalib, when did this prophetess speak among you? I said: What is that? He said: The dream that Aatika saw? I said: What did she see? He said: O sons of Abdul Muttalib, are you not satisfied that your men should prophesy until your women prophesy? Aatika claimed in her dream that he said, Go forth in three days. If what she said is true, then it will happen. But if the three days pass and nothing of that happens, then we will write a document against you that you are the most lying people in the Arab household. Al-Abbas said: By God, I did not do anything to him except that I denied it and denied that she had seen anything. Then we parted, and by evening there was not a woman from Banu Abd al-Muttalib who did not come to me and say: Did you allow this wicked, immoral man to have intercourse with your men, then he has taken advantage of the women and you are listening, and then there was no jealousy in you for anything that I heard? He said: I said, By God, I have done what I did to him a lot, and by God I will confront him, and if he returns, I will suffice you. He said: So I went out on the third day of Aatika’s vision, and I was very angry and felt that I had missed something from him that I wanted to catch up with. He said: So I entered the mosque and saw him, and by God, I was walking towards him, trying to get him to return to some of what he had said, so I would fall upon him. He was a light-hearted man, with a sharp face, a sharp tongue, and a sharp look, when he went out towards the door of the mosque, intense. He said: I said to myself: What is wrong with him, may God curse him? Is this all out of fear of me that I curse him? He said: Then he heard what I did not hear, the voice of Damdam bin Amr, crying out in the valley, standing on his camel, and he had cut off his camel, turned his saddle, and torn his shirt, and he was saying: O people of Quraysh, your wealth is with Abu Sufyan, and Muhammad and his companions have attacked it. I do not think that you will reach it. Help, help. He said: But what had happened distracted me from him and distracted him from me, so the people prepared quickly and none of the nobles of Quraysh remained behind except Abu Lahab who remained behind and sent in his place Al-Aas bin Hisham bin Al-Mughirah. When the Quraysh gathered to march, they mentioned what had happened between them and Banu Bakr ibn Abd Manaf ibn Kinanah ibn al-Harith. They said: We fear that they will come to us from behind. This almost deterred them, but Satan appeared to them in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ja`sham, who was one of the nobles of Banu Bakr. He said: I will protect you from Kinanah coming to you from behind with something you dislike. So they went out quickly, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with his companions, during the past nights of the month of Ramadan, until he reached a valley called Dhafran, and the report came to him about the march of the Quraysh to prevent their caravan, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until he was in Ar-Rawha’, and he took a spring for swimming and informed him about them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, also sent a spy from Juhayna, an ally of the Ansar, called Abdullah bin Urayqit, who brought him report of the people. The caravan had outpaced the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Gabriel came down and said: God has promised you one of two groups, either the caravan or the Quraysh. The other was more beloved to them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted his companions about seeking the caravan and the Nafir war. Abu Bakr stood up and said it well. Then Umar stood up and said it well. Then Al-Miqdad bin Amr stood up and said: O Messenger of God, go as God has shown you, for we are with you. By God, we do not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting here. Rather, we say: Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are with you, fighting. By the One Who sent you with the truth, if you march with us to Bark al-Ghamad, meaning the city of Abyssinia, we will fight with you until you reach it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said good things to him and prayed for goodness for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Advise me, O people. He only means the Ansar, because they are the number of people, and when they pledged allegiance to him at Al-Aqabah, they said: O Messenger of God, we are free from your protection until you reach our home. When you reach us, then you are under our protection, and we will protect you as we protect our sons and women. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, feared that the Ansar would not see it as their duty to support him except against those of his enemy who attacked him in Medina, and that it was not their duty to send them to an enemy from their country. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that, Sa`d ibn Mu`adh said to him: By God, it seems as if you want us, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: We have believed in you and confirmed you and we testify that what you have brought us is the truth and you have given us for that {covenants and pacts} to hear and obey. So go, O Messenger of God, to what you wish. By Him Who sent you with the truth, if you were to parade us across this sea and cross it, we would cross it with you and not a single man of us would stay behind. We do not dislike that you should meet our enemy tomorrow. We are patient in war and true in meeting. Perhaps God Almighty will show you from us something that will please your eyes. So go with us with God’s blessing. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with what Sa`d said and was encouraged by that. Then he said: Go with God’s blessing and be glad, for God has promised me one of the two groups. By God, it is as if I am now seeing the place where the people will fall. Thabit said on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the place where so-and-so will fall, and this is the place where so-and-so will fall. He said: And he put his hand on the ground here and there. He said: No one moved from the place where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had his hand. That is what God Almighty said: And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours. That is, the two parties, one of them was Abu Sufyan who passed by the caravan, and the other was Abu Jahl with the mobilization. And you wish, that is, you want that the one without the power be yours, meaning the caravans that do not fight. Power: strength and force. It is also said the weapon. And God wants to establish the truth that is, to make it manifest and exalt it, with His words by His command to you to fight. It was also said, with His punishment that preceded the manifestation and glorification of the religion, and to cut off the root of the disbelievers that is, to uproot them until not one of them remains, meaning: the disbelieving Arabs.
8:8: 8 - So that the truth may be established, so that Islam may be established, and falsehood may be nullified, meaning: disbelief may be destroyed, even though the criminals hate it, the polytheists. The Battle of Badr took place on Friday morning, seventeen nights into the month of Ramadan.
8:9: 9 - The Almighty said: When you called upon your Lord, seeking refuge in Him from your enemy and asking Him for help and victory. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at the polytheists, who were one thousand, and his companions were three hundred and a few men. He and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, entered the hut, and faced the Qiblah and stretched out his hands and began to call upon his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic: "O God, fulfill for me what You promised me. O God, if You destroy this group of Muslims, You will not be worshipped on earth." He continued to call upon his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, stretching out his hands until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr took his cloak and threw it over his shoulders, then embraced him from behind and said: O Prophet of God, your calling upon your Lord is sufficient for you, for He will fulfill for you what He promised you. Then God Almighty revealed: When you called upon your Lord “And He answered you, ‘I will reinforce you’” sending you reinforcements and protection with a thousand angels following one another. The people of Medina and Jacob read mardfin with an open dal, meaning: God sent the Muslims behind him and brought them reinforcements. The others read it with a kasra on the dal, meaning: one after the other. It is said: I followed him, meaning I followed him. It is narrated that Gabriel descended with five hundred and Michael with five hundred in the form of men on piebald horses, wearing white clothes and white turbans on their heads, the ends of which they had let down between their shoulders. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and Abu Bakr said: God will fulfill for you what He promised you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shuddered while he was in the hut, then he woke up and said: O Abu Bakr, God’s victory has come to you. This is Gabriel holding the reins of a horse, leading it on its two teeth, with dust on its back. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, on the authority of Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Musa, on the authority of Abdul Wahhab, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Badr: This is Gabriel holding the head of his horse, wearing the tools of war. Abdullah bin Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: The angels’ appearance on the day of Badr was white turbans, and on the day of Hunayn they were green turbans. The angels did not fight on any day other than the day of Badr, and on other days they were numerous and supported. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Asid bin Malik bin Rabi’ah, who had witnessed Badr, that he said after he lost his sight: If I had been with you today at Badr and had my sight, I would have shown you the valley from which the angels came out.
8:10: 10 - The Almighty said: And God has not made it, meaning: the support of angels, except as good tidings, meaning: good report, “and that your hearts may be reassured thereby. And victory comes only from God. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise.”
8:11: 11 - When drowsiness overtakes you, Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read: yaghshakum with the opening of the ya', al-na'as is raised on the basis that the action is for him, like the Almighty's saying in Surat Al-Imran A security, a drowsiness that overwhelms a group of you Al-Imran - 154, and the people of Medina read: yaghshikum with the damma of the ya' and the kasra of the sheen, lightened, al-na'as is accusative, like the Almighty's saying: As if their faces were covered and others read with the damma of the ya' and the kasra of the sheed, stressed, al-na'as is accusative, on the basis that the action is for God the Almighty, like the Almighty's saying: So that which overcame it covered it An-Najm - 54, and drowsiness is a light sleep. Amanat security is from him, the source of Amanat I felt security and Amanat and Amanat safety and Amanan safety and Amanan safety Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: Drowsiness in battle is a security from God, and in prayer it is a whisper from Satan. And He sends down upon you from the sky water to purify you thereby. That is because the Muslims camped on the day of Badr on a dusty sand dune, where the feet and hooves of animals would sink. The polytheists had preceded them to the water of Badr, and some of the Muslims became ritually impure and some of them were ritually unclean. They became thirsty, and Satan whispered to them, saying: You claim that you are on the truth and that among you is the Prophet of God and that you are the friends of God, and the polytheists have defeated you in reaching the water, and you are praying in a state of ritual impurity and ritual impurity. How do you hope to prevail over them? So God, the Almighty, sent down rain upon them, from which the valley flowed, and the believers drank, washed themselves, performed ablution, gave water to their camels, filled their water skins, and extinguished the dust, and covered the ground until the feet could rest on it. The whisperings of Satan were removed from them, and their souls were at ease. That is what God, the Almighty, said: And He sends down upon you from the sky water to purify you thereby from ritual impurity and ritual impurity. And He removes from you the evil of Satan and his whisperings, and strengthens your hearts with certainty and patience, and makes your feet firm thereby so that they do not sink into the sand by making the earth rough. It was said: He makes your feet firm thereby with patience and strength of heart.
8:12: 12 - When your Lord inspired to the angels, whom He provided for the believers, I am with you, with help and victory, so strengthen those who believe, meaning: strengthen their hearts. It was said: that strengthening was their presence with them in the fighting and their assistance, meaning: strengthen them by fighting with them against the polytheists. Muqatil said: That is, give them good tidings of victory. The angel would walk in front of the row in the form of a man and say: Be glad, for God is your supporter. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve. Ata’ said: He means fear of My friends. So strike above the necks. It was said: This is an address to the believers. It was also said: This is an address to the angels, and it is connected to His statement: So strengthen those who believe. And His statement: Above the necks. Ikrimah said: He means the heads because they are above the necks. Ad-Dahhak said: Its meaning is, strike the necks. Above is a connection, as God the Almighty said: So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike the necks. Muhammad 4 It was also said: Its meaning is, strike the necks. Above means: on. And strike off from them every fingertip, Atiyah said: meaning every joint. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jurayj, and Ad-Dahhak said: meaning the extremities. Banan is the plural of Bananah, which are the tips of the fingers of the hands and feet. Ibn Al-Anbari said: The angels did not know how to kill humans, so God Almighty taught them. Ismail bin Abdul Qadir Al-Jurjani told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad Al-Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Hajjaj told us, Zuhair bin Harb told us, Amr bin Yunus Al-Hanafi told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Abu Zamil - he is Samak Al-Hanafi - told us, Abdullah bin Abbas said: “While a Muslim man was on that day pursuing a polytheist man in front of him, he heard the whip strike above him, and the voice of the horseman saying: ‘Go forward, Haizum!’ He looked at the polytheist in front of him and fell down, and he looked at him and saw that his nose had been smashed and his face split like a whip strike, and it all turned green. Then the Ansari came and told that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘You have spoken the truth. That was from the reinforcements of the third heaven.’ So they killed seventy that day and took seventy captive.” It was narrated on the authority of Abu Dawood Al-Mazini, who had witnessed Badr, that he said: I was following a polytheist to strike him when his head fell before my sword reached it, and I knew that someone other than me had killed him. Abu Umamah bin Sahl bin Hanif narrated on the authority of his father, who said: By God, I saw us on the day of Badr, and one of us would point his sword at a polytheist, and his head would fall off his body before the sword reached him.
