And Ikrimah said, Abu Rafi, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was a slave of Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, may God be pleased with him, and Islam had entered us, the people of the house, and Umm Al-Fadl had converted to Islam and I had converted to Islam, and Al-Abbas feared his people and hated to contradict them, and he concealed his conversion to Islam, and he had a lot of money that was scattered among his people, and Abu Lahab, the enemy of God, had stayed behind from Badr and sent in his place Al-Aas bin Hisham bin Al-Mughirah, and when the report came to him about the disaster of the companions of Badr, God subdued him and disgraced him, and we found strength and honor in ourselves, and I was a weak man and I was working on the arrows and carving them in the chamber of Zamzam, and by God I was sitting carving the arrows, and Umm Al-Fadl was sitting with me, when the wicked Abu Lahab came dragging his feet until he sat on the rope of the chamber, and his back was to my back, and while he was sitting, the people said, This is Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib who has arrived, so Abu Lahab said: My nephew is here, for you have the report, so he sat with him and the people were standing. He said: O my nephew, tell me how was the situation of the people? He said: Nothing, by God. It was only that we met them and turned our shoulders to them, killing us and taking us captive as they wished. By God, that happened as long as I blamed the people. We met white men on piebald horses between the sky and the earth. No, by God, they are not worthy of anything and nothing can stand up to them. Abu Rafi said: So I lifted the rope of the room with my hand and said: By God, those are the angels. Abu Lahab raised his hand and struck my face hard. I rebelled against him, but he picked me up and threw me to the ground, then he knelt on me and struck me. I was a weak man. Umm al-Fadl went to one of the pillars of the room, took it and struck him with it a terrible blow that split his head. She said: Do you consider him weak because his master is away from him? So he stood up, humiliated and by God, he did not live more than seven nights until God struck him with a lentil and killed him. Muqsim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The one who captured Al-Abbas was Abu Al-Yusr, Ka’b bin Amr, the brother of Banu Salamah. Abu Al-Yusr was a strong man, and Al-Abbas was a large man. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Al-Yusr, ‘How did you capture Al-Abbas?’ He said, ‘O Messenger of God, a man helped me against him whom I had never seen before or after that. His appearance was such and such.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘A noble king helped you against him.’”
8:13: 13 - That is because they opposed God, they disobeyed God, “and His Messenger. And whoever opposes God and His Messenger - then indeed, God is severe in penalty.”
8:14: 14 - That, meaning: this punishment and beating that I hastened for you, O disbelievers, at Badr, so taste it, immediately, and that for the disbelievers, meaning: know and be certain that for the disbelievers there is a term in the afterlife, the punishment of the Fire. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he had finished with Badr: ‘You should go with the caravan, there is nothing less than it.’ Al-Abbas called out to him while he was a prisoner in his chains: ‘It is not suitable.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Why?’ He said: ‘Because God Almighty promised you one of the two groups and He has given you what He promised you.’”
8:15: 15 - The Almighty said: O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing, meaning gathered together, crowding one another. Advancing means drawing close in battle. Advancing is a verbal noun, therefore it is not pluralized, like their saying, a people of justice and contentment. Al-Layth said: Advancing is a group advancing against their enemy at once, so they are advancing, and the plural is advancing. Do not turn your backs to them, meaning do not flee, because the one who is defeated turns his back.
8:16: 16 - And whoever turns his back to them that Day, his back, except turning aside for the sake of battle, meaning: turning aside, seeing himself as defeated, and intending to seek surprise while he wants to return, or withdrawing to a company, meaning: joining and becoming a group of believers, wanting to return to the battle. The meaning of the verse is: the prohibition of fleeing from the infidels and turning away from them, except with the intention of turning away to fight and joining a group of Muslims to seek their help and return to fight. Whoever turns his back without this intention will be threatened, as God Almighty said: He has certainly drawn upon himself the wrath of God, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination. The scholars differed regarding this verse. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said: This is specifically for the people of Badr. It was not permissible for them to flee because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with them, and they did not have a group to which they could turn, except for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He turned to a group, so his flight would not be a major sin. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak. Yazid bin Abi Habib said: God made Hell obligatory for those who fled on the day of Badr. Then, when the day of Uhud came after that, He said: The devil only made them slip because of some of what they had earned, but God has already pardoned them (Al Imran 3:155). Then, after that, the day of Hunayn came, and He said: Then you turned back, fleeing (al-Tawbah 9:25). Then God will turn in forgiveness after that to whom He wills (al-Tawbah 9:27). Abdullah bin Omar said: “We were in an army that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent us. The people were surrounded and fled, so we said: O Messenger of God, are we the ones who flee? He said: Rather, you are the ones who attack. I am the group of Muslims.” Muhammad bin Sirin said: When Abu Ubaidah was killed, the report reached Omar, so he said: If he had joined me, we would have been his group, so I am the group of every Muslim. Some of them said: The ruling of the verse is general and applies to everyone who turns back in defeat. It was stated in the hadith: One of the major sins is fleeing from battle. Ata bin Abi Rabah said: This verse was abrogated by the words of God Almighty: Now God has lightened your burden (al-Anfal 8:66). It is not for a people to flee from the likes of them, so that was abrogated except in this number. And on this, most of the scholars say that if the Muslims are half of their enemy, it is not permissible for them to flee or turn their backs and withdraw from them. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever flees from three does not flee, but from two has fled.
8:17: 17 - The Almighty said: So you did not kill them, but it was God who killed them. Mujahid said: The reason for this verse is that when they turned away from fighting, a man would say: I killed so-and-so, and another would say the same, so the verse was revealed. Its meaning is: So you did not kill them with your strength, but God killed them {by His victory} over you and His strengthening of you. It was said: But God killed them with the help of angels. And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw, the people of interpretation and battles said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon the people, so they set out until they reached Badr, and the Quraysh’s messengers came to them, and among them was Aslam, a black slave of Banu al-Hajjaj, and Abu Yasar, a slave of Banu al-‘As ibn Sa’id. They brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to them: Where are the Quraysh? They said: They are behind this dune that you see on the far side - and the dune is al-‘Aqanqal - so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: How many are the people? They said: Many. He said: What is their number? They said: We do not know. He said: How many do they slaughter every day? They said: Ten one day and nine the next. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people are between nine hundred and a thousand. Then he said to them: Who are among them the nobles of Quraysh? They said: Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, Shaibah ibn Rabi’ah, Abu al-Bukhtari ibn Hisham, Hakim ibn Hizam, and al-Harith ibn Amir, Tu'aymah ibn 'Adi, Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Nabih and Munabbih, the sons of Al-Hajjaj, and Suhayl ibn 'Amr. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is Mecca, and the most precious parts of its liver have been thrown to you. When the Quraysh approached and the Messenger of God saw them descending from Al-'Aqanqal, which is the sand dune from which they came to the valley, he said to them: This is the Quraysh, and they have come with their arrogant and proud people, {challenging you} and denying your Messenger. O God, grant me the victory that you promised me. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said to him: Take a handful of dirt and throw it at them. When the two armies met, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a handful of pebbles covered with dirt and threw it in the faces of the people, and said: May your faces be disfigured. There was not a single polytheist among them who did not have some of it enter his eyes, mouth, and nostrils. They fled, and the believers followed them, killing them and taking them captive. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: “It was mentioned to us that on the day of Badr the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took three pebbles and threw one pebble at the right flank of the people, one pebble at the left flank of the people, and one pebble in their midst, and said: ‘May your faces be disfigured,’ and they were defeated.” This is what God Almighty said: And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw, because it is not within the power of any human being to throw a handful of pebbles at the faces of an army and not leave an eye among them without some of it hitting it. It was said: The meaning of the verse is: You did not reach it when you threw, but God reached it. It was said: I did not throw terror into their hearts when I threw pebbles, but God threw terror into their hearts until they were defeated, ‘and that He might test the believers with a good test,’ meaning: and that He might bestow upon the believers a great blessing of victory and spoils. Indeed, God is Hearing of your supplications, Knowing of your intentions.
8:18: 18 - "That which you mentioned of killing, shooting and good affliction, and that God", it was said: there is an implication in it, meaning: {and know} that God "weakens, weakens, the plot of the disbelievers". Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and the people of Basra read: Mohen with emphasis and tanween, Kaed is accusative, and the others read Mohen with emphasis and tanween except Hafs, for he adds it and does not add tanween and lowers Kaed.
8:19: 19 - The Almighty said: If you ask for victory, victory has already come to you. This is because Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr when the people met: God has severed our ties of kinship and brought us something we did not know, so we will destroy him this morning. So he was the one who asked for victory for himself. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Ibrahim bin Saad told us on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather who said: Abdul Rahman bin Auf said: I was in the ranks on the day of Badr when I turned and saw to my right and left two young men, young in age. I did not feel secure in their position, then one of them said to me secretly from his companion: O uncle, show me Abu Jahl. I said: O son of my brother, what will you do with him? He said: I have vowed to God Almighty that if I see him, I will kill him or die trying. The other said to me secretly from his companion the same thing, and it did not please me to be between two men in their position, so I pointed him out to them, and they attacked him like two falcons until they struck him, and they were the sons of Afra. And Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, on the authority of Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna, on the authority of Ibn Abi Uday, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day: Who will look for us at what Abu Jahl has done? He said: So Ibn Masoud went and found that Ibn Afra had beaten him until he was cold. He said: So he took hold of his beard and said: Are you Abu Jahl? He said: Is there anyone above a man who was killed by his people or you killed him?” Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Abdullah bin Abi Bakr told me: Muadh bin Amr bin Al-Jamuh said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his campaign, he ordered Abu Jahl bin Hisham to be sought among the dead. He said: O God, do not let anything escape You. He said: When I heard that, I made him my concern, so I went towards him and struck him with a blow that cut off his foot and half of his leg. He said: His son Ikrimah struck me on my shoulder, so he threw my hand away and it clung to the skin of my side, and the fighting made me fail. I fought most of my day, dragging it behind me. When it hurt me, I put my foot on it, then I stretched out with it until I threw it. Then he passed by Abu Jahl, who was the son of Muadh bin Afra, and he struck him until he fell down, then he left him with a breath of fresh air. Then Abdullah bin Masoud passed by {Abu Jahl}. Abdullah bin Masoud said: I found him with his last breath, so I recognized him, so I put my foot on his neck, then I said: Has God disgraced you, O Enemy of God? He said: How did they disgrace me? I killed a man whom you killed. Tell me, to whom does the circle belong? I said: To God and His Messenger. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he said: “Abu Jahl said to me: ‘O shepherd, you have climbed a difficult ascent, then I cut off his head and brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, this is the head of Abu Jahl.’ He said: ‘Is it God, other than whom there is no god?’ I said: ‘Yes, by other than whom there is no god.’ Then I threw it in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he praised God Almighty.” Al-Sayyidi and Al-Kalbi said: When the polytheists came out to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca, they took hold of the curtains of the Kaaba and said: O God, support the superior of the two armies, the most guided of the two groups, the most honorable of the two parties, and the best of the two religions. So regarding this, the verse was revealed: If you seek victory, victory has already come to you. That is, if you seek victory, victory has come to you. Ikrimah said: The polytheists said, By God, we do not know what Muhammad has brought, so judge between us and him with the truth. So God Almighty revealed: If you ask for victory, victory has come to you. That is, if you ask for justice, judgment has come to you. Abi bin Kaab said: This is an address to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty said to the Muslims: If you seek victory, victory has already come to you. That is, if you seek help, victory and triumph have come to you. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hairi told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad told us, Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib told us, Ismail ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Khabbab, may God be pleased with him, who said: We complained to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was leaning on his cloak in the shade of the Kaaba, and we had suffered great hardship from the polytheists. We said: Will you not call upon God for us? Will you not seek victory for us? He sat down, his colour or face red, and said to us: “There were those before you who would seize a man and dig a hole for him in the ground, then a saw would be brought and placed over his head, then he would be divided into two parts, but that would not divert him from his religion. And iron combs would comb through his flesh, bones and nerves, but that would not divert him from his religion. By God, this matter will be completed until a rider among you can travel from Sana’a to Hadramawt, fearing none but God, but you are hasty.” His saying: And if you desist, meaning he is saying to the disbelievers: If you desist from disbelieving in God and fighting His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “it is better for you. But if you return,” to fighting and fighting him, We will promise something similar to the incident that happened to you on the day of Badr. It was said: And if you return to supplication and opening supplication, We will promise victory for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. “And your company will not avail you at all, even if it were many. And indeed, God is with the believers.” The people of Medina, Ibn Amir, and Hafs read and God with a fat-ha on the hamza, meaning: And because God is with the believers, likewise and your company will not avail you at all. It was said: It is an apocopation of his saying: That is you, and indeed, God weakens the plot of the disbelievers. Others read: and indeed, God with a kasra on the alif as an introductory word.
8:20: 20 - The Almighty’s saying, O you who have believed, obey God and His Messenger and do not turn away from him, meaning: do not turn away from him, while you listen, the Qur’an and its sermons.
8:21: 21- And do not be like those who say, 'We hear,' while they do not hear, meaning: they say with their tongues, We hear,' with their ears, while they do not hear, meaning they do not learn a lesson or benefit from what they hear, so it is as if they did not hear.
8:22: 22- The Almighty said: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God, meaning: the worst of those who crawl on the face of the earth {of God's creation} are the deaf and dumb, about the truth so they do not hear it or say it, who do not reason the command of God the Almighty, He called them living creatures because of their little benefit from their minds, as God the Almighty said: Those are like livestock, rather, they are more astray Al-A'raf - 179. Ibn Abbas said: They are a group of Banu Abd al-Dar Banu Qusayy, they used to say: We are deaf, dumb and blind to what Muhammad brought, so they were all killed at Uhud, and they were the bearers of the banner, and only two men from them were saved: Mus'ab bin Umair and Suwaybit bin Harmalah.
8:23: 23 - And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear, meaning: He would have made them hear the hearing of understanding and acceptance. And if He had made them hear, after He knew that there was no good in them, they would not have benefited from that, they would have turned away while they were averse, due to their stubbornness and denial of the truth after it had appeared. It was said: They used to say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Bring Qusayy back to life for us, for he was a blessed old man, so that he may testify to your prophethood, and we will believe in you. So God, the Almighty, said: And if He had made them hear, Qusayy's speech, they would have turned away while they were averse.
8:24: 24 - The Almighty said: O you who have believed, respond to God and the Messenger, meaning respond to them with obedience, when he calls you, meaning the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to that which gives you life, meaning: to that which gives you life. Al-Suddi said: It is faith, because the disbeliever is dead and comes to life through faith. Qatada said: It is the Qur’an, in which is life, salvation and protection in both worlds. Mujahed said: It is the truth. Ibn Ishaq said: It is jihad, with which God has honored you after humiliation. Al-Qatibi said: Rather, martyrdom. God Almighty said about the martyrs: Rather, they are alive with their Lord, and they are provided for. (Al Imran 3:169) We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Ubayy ibn Ka`b, may God be pleased with him, while he was praying, and called him. Ubayy hurried in his prayer, then he came and the Messenger of God said: What prevented you from answering me when I called you? He said: I was praying. He said: Doesn’t God Almighty say: O you who have believed, respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life? {He said: No doubt, O Messenger of God, do not call upon Me except that I respond, even if you are praying.} God Almighty says: And know that God intervenes between a man and his heart. Saeed bin Jubair and Ata’ said: He intervenes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith. Ad-Dahhak said: He stands between the unbeliever and obedience, and between the believer and disobedience. Mujahed said: It comes between a person and his heart, so he does not understand or know what he is doing. Al-Suddi said: It comes between a person and his heart, so he cannot believe or disbelieve except with His permission. It was said: When the people were called to fight in a state of weakness, their suspicions worsened and their hearts were troubled, so it was said to them: Fight in the way of God and know that God comes between a person and his heart, replacing fear with security and cowardice with boldness. And to Him you will be gathered, so He will reward you for your deeds. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hairi told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Muhammad bin Hammad told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God used to say often: O Changer of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. They said: O Messenger of God, we believe in you and in what you have brought, so do you fear for us? He said: The hearts are within me, two fingers of God’s fingers, and He turns them.
8:25: 25 - And fear a trial, a test and a calamity that you will not be afflicted with, His saying: that you will not be afflicted with is not a pure recompense, and if it were a recompense, the letter nun would not have entered into it, but it is {a negation}, and in it is a part of the recompense like the saying of the Most High: O ants, enter your dwellings lest Solomon and his soldiers crush you An-Naml - 18, and its meaning is and fear a trial that if you do not fear it will befall you, so it is like the saying of the one who says: Get down from the beast, lest it throw you down, so this is the answer to the command with the wording of the prohibition, meaning if you get down, it will not throw you down. The commentators said: This verse was revealed about the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its meaning is: Beware of a trial that will befall the oppressor and the non-oppressor. Al-Hasan said: It was revealed about Ali, Ammar, Talha, and Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them. Al-Zubayr said: We read this verse and I do not think we are among its people, but we are the ones meant by it, meaning what happened on the Day of the Camel. Al-Suddi, Muqatil, Al-Dahhak, and Qatada said: This is about a specific group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who were afflicted with the tribulation on the Day of the Camel. Ibn Abbas said: God Almighty commanded the believers not to accept evil among them, lest God afflict them with a punishment that befalls the oppressor and the non-oppressor. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah told us, Abu Tahir al-Harithi told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Saif ibn Abi Sulayman, who said: I heard Adi ibn Adi al-Kindi say: A client of ours told me that he heard my grandfather say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God does not punish the common people for the actions of the elite until they see evil among themselves and they are able to denounce it but they do not denounce it. If they do that, God will punish the common people and the elite.” Ibn Zayd said: What he meant by fitnah is division of speech and opposition of some to others. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman told me, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There will be tribulations in which the one who is sitting is better than the one who is standing, and the one who is standing is better than the one who is walking, and the one who is walking is better than the one who is running. Whoever looks out for them will be looked out for, so whoever finds a refuge or a place of safety, let him seek refuge in it.” His saying, Do not afflict those among you who have wronged exclusively, means: the punishment, and know that God is severe in penalty.
8:26: 26 - The Almighty said: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, meaning: And remember, O group of emigrants, when you were few in number, oppressed in the land of Mecca, at the beginning of Islam, fearing that people would snatch you away, meaning: the infidels of Mecca. Ikrimah said: the infidels of the Arabs. Wahb said: the Persians and the Romans. So He gave you shelter, to Medina, and supported you with His victory, meaning: He strengthened you on the day of Badr with the Ansar. Al-Kalbi said: He strengthened you on the day of Badr with the angels, and provided you with good things, meaning: the spoils, He made them lawful for you and did not make them lawful for anyone before you, that you might be grateful.
8:27: 27 - O you who have believed, do not betray God and the Messenger, Al-Suddi said: They would hear something from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spread it, until it reached the polytheists. Al-Zuhri and Al-Kalbi said: The verse was revealed about Abu Lubabah, Harun bin Abdul-Mundhir Al-Ansari, from Banu Awf bin Malik, and that is because “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged the Jews of Banu Qurayzah for twenty-one nights, and they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a peace treaty on the basis of what their brothers from Banu Nadir had made peace on, on the condition that they would march to their brothers in Adhraat and Ariha in the land of Ash-Sham, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused to give them that unless they submit to the judgment of Sa`d bin Mu`adh, so they refused and said: Send to us Abu Lubabah bin Abdul-Mundhir, and he was a sincere advisor to them, because his wealth, children and dependents were with them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him, and he came to them, and they said to him: O Abu Lubabah, what do you think if we submit to the judgment of Sa`d bin Mu`adh? Abu Lubabah pointed with his hand to the ring of slaughter, so do not do it, Abu Lubabah said: By God, my feet did not move in their place until I knew that I had betrayed God and His Messenger.” Then he set off on his way and did not come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and tied himself to one of the pillars of the mosque and said: By God, I will not taste food or drink until I die or God accepts my repentance. When the report of him reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: If he had come to me, I would have asked forgiveness for him, but since he did what he did, I will not release him until God accepts his repentance. So he remained for seven days, not tasting food or drink until he fell unconscious. Then God accepted his repentance, and it was said to him: O Abu Lubabah, you have accepted your repentance. He said: No, by God, I will not release myself until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the one who releases me. So he came to him and released him with his hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: O Messenger of God, part of my complete repentance is that I leave the home of my people in which I committed the sin and give up all my wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A third will not suffice you, so give it in charity. So the verse was revealed concerning it: Do not betray God and the Messenger. “And betray your trusts,” meaning: [and do not betray your trusts], while you know, that it is a trust. It was said: And you know that what you did, by pointing to the throat, is a betrayal. Al-Suddi said: If they betrayed God and the Messenger, they have betrayed their trust. Ibn Abbas said: Do not betray God by abandoning His obligations, nor the Messenger by abandoning his Sunnah, nor betray your trust. Ibn Abbas said: It is what is hidden from people’s eyes of God’s obligations and the deeds that God has entrusted to them. Qatada said: Know that the religion of God is a trust, so fulfill to God Almighty what He has entrusted you with of obligations and limits, and whoever has a trust upon him should fulfill it to the one who entrusted him with it.
8:28: 28 - And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial. It was said: This is also about Abu Lubaba, and that his wealth and children were with Banu Qurayza, so he said what he said out of fear for them. It was said: This applies to all people. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Malhi told us - by dictation - and Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Tusi told us, they said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Muhammad Al-Isfarayini told us, Muhammad bin Muhammad bin [Razmuyah] told us, Yahya bin Muhammad bin Ghalib told us, Yahya bin Yahya told us, Abdullah bin Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought a young boy, so he kissed him and said: Indeed, they are miserly and cowardly, and indeed, they are among the basil of God Almighty.” And that God has a great reward with Him, for whoever advises God and His Messenger and fulfills his trust.
8:29: 29 - The Almighty said: O you who have believed, if you fear God, by obeying Him and avoiding disobeying Him, He will grant you a criterion, Mujahid said: a way out in this world and the hereafter. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: A way out of doubts in religion. Akrima said: Salvation means that it separates you from what you fear. Ad-Dahhak said: A clarification. Ibn Ishaq said: A distinction between truth and falsehood, through which God reveals your truth and extinguishes the falsehood of those who oppose you. Al-Furqan is a verbal noun like preponderance and deficiency. “And He will remove from you your misdeeds,” that is, He will erase from you your past sins, and forgive you, and God is the possessor of great bounty.
8:30: 30 - The Almighty’s saying: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, this verse is connected [to His saying]: And remember when you were few, and remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you, and when they said, O God, because this surah is Madani and this plot and this saying only happened in Mecca, but God mentioned them in Medina as in His Almighty’s saying: If you do not aid him, God has already aided him At-Tawbah - 40, and this plot was, according to what Ibn Abbas and other commentators mentioned: When the Ansar converted to Islam, the Quraysh feared that the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would worsen. So a group of their elders gathered in the House of Assembly to consult about the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Their leaders were: Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabiah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Abu Sufyan, Tu’aymah bin ‘Adi, Shaibah bin Rabiah, Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, Abu Al-Bukhtari bin Hisham, Zama’ah bin Al-Aswad, Hakim bin Hizam, Nabih and Munabbih, the sons of Al-Hajjaj, and Umayyah bin Khalaf. Satan intercepted them in the form of an old man. When they saw him, they said: Who are you? He said: An old man from Najd. I heard about your meeting, so I wanted you to take Muhammad and imprison him in a house, tie him up tightly, and close the door of the house except for a window so that you can serve him food and drink, and wait for him to be struck by the vicissitudes of fate until he perishes in it, as the poets who came before him perished. He said: The enemy of God, the Najdi sheikh, cried out and said: What a bad opinion you have seen. By God, if you imprison him in a house and his matter goes out from behind the door that you have closed to his companions, they will soon attack you and fight you and take him from your hands. They said: The sheikh has spoken the truth. Hisham bin Amr from Banu Amir bin Luay said: As for me, I think that you should carry him on a camel and take him out from among you. What he does will not harm you or where he falls. If he is absent from you and you are relieved of him, then Satan said: This is not an opinion that you can rely on. You go to a man who has corrupted your dreams and you take him out to someone else so that he corrupts them. Have you not seen the sweetness of his speech and the sweetness of his tongue and how he takes hearts by what you hear of his talk? By God, if you do that, he will go and win the hearts of people, then he will march with them to you and expel you from your country. They said: The old man has spoken the truth. Abu Jahl said: By God, I will advise you with an opinion that I see no other than it. I see that you should take from every clan of Quraysh a young man of good lineage, middle-aged, and young, then give each young man of them a sharp sword, then strike him with one blow. If they kill him, his blood will be distributed among all the tribes. I do not think that this tribe of Banu Hashim will be able to fight all of Quraysh, and if they see that, they will accept the blood money and Quraysh will pay his blood money. Iblis said: This young man has spoken the truth, and he is the best of you in opinion. The opinion is what he said, and I see no other opinion. So they dispersed according to the opinion of Abu Jahl, and they agreed on it. Then Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of that and ordered him not to spend the night in the bed in which he used to spend the night. Then God gave him permission to go out to Medina. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Ali ibn Abi Talib to sleep in his bed and said to him: Walk with this cloak of mine, for nothing you dislike will come to you from them. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and took a handful of dirt, and God took away their sight from him. He began to sprinkle dirt on their heads while he was reciting: Indeed, We have placed shackles on their necks until His saying: So they do not see. Surat Yasin - 8/9. He and Abu Bakr went to the cave of Thawr, and left Ali behind in Mecca until he returned the deposits that he had accepted. The deposits were deposited with him, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of his truthfulness and trustworthiness. The polytheists spent the night guarding Ali in the bed of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, thinking that he was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When morning came, they rushed to him and saw Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: Where is your companion? He said: I do not know. So they followed his tracks and sent for him. When they reached the cave, they saw a spider’s web over its door. They said: If he had entered it, the spider’s web would not have been over its door. So he stayed in it for three days, then he came to Medina. That is what God Almighty said: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you. “To imprison you, to chain you up, to imprison you, to tie you up, “or to kill you or to expel you. And they plan, and God plans.” Ad-Dahhak said: They make and God makes. And planning and devising, which is from God, means planning with truth. It was said: He will reward them with the reward of devising. And God is the best of planners.
8:31: 31 - And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, meaning Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say something like this," because he used to go as a merchant to Persia and Al-Hirah and hear the report of Rustam and Isfandiyar, and the stories of the Persians, and he would pass by the Jews and Christians and see them reading the Torah and the Gospel and bowing and prostrating. So he came to Mecca and found the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying and reciting the Qur'an, so Al-Nadr said: We have heard. If we wished, we could say something like this. This is nothing but legends of the ancients, report of past nations and their names and what the ancients wrote in their books. Legends: the plural of legend, which means written, from their saying I wrote meaning I wrote.
8:32: 32 - The Almighty said: And when they said, ‘O God, if this is the truth from You,’ the verse was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith from Banu Abd Al-Dar. Ibn Abbas said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated the story of the past generations, Al-Nadr said: If you wished, you could say something like this: This is nothing but legends of the ancients - meaning: This is nothing but what the ancients wrote in their books - then Uthman ibn Maz’un, may God be pleased with him, said to him: Fear God, for Muhammad speaks the truth. He said: So I speak the truth. Uthman said: Muhammad says: There is no god but God. He said: And I say: There is no god but God, but these are the daughters of God, meaning the idols. Then he said: O God, if what Muhammad says is the truth from You - and the truth is the subject of the verb was and it is a pillar and a link - then rain down upon us stones from the sky, as You rained them down upon the people of Lot, or bring us a painful punishment, meaning some of what You punished the nations with, and in this was revealed: A questioner asked about a punishment to come to pass. (al-Ma’arij 70:1) Ata’ said: A dozen verses were revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and he was afflicted with the punishment he asked for on the day of Badr. Saeed bin Jubair said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed three men from Quraysh on the day of Badr: Tu’aymah bin Adi, Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt, and Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith. Anas, may God be pleased with him, narrated that what Abu Jahl said. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Al-Nadr told us, Ubaidullah bin Muadh told us, my father told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid, the companion of Al-Ziyadi, he heard Anas bin Malik say: Abu Jahl said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. So this was revealed:
8:33: 33 - "And God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness. And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them?" God the Almighty said: And God would not punish them while you are among them. They differed about the meaning of this verse. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: This is a narration from the polytheists that they said it and it is connected to the first verse, and that is because they used to say that God would not punish us while we seek His forgiveness, and He would not punish a nation while its prophet is with it. So God the Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioning their ignorance, their deception, and their opening up to themselves: And when they said, ‘O God, if this is the truth from You,’ the verse, and they said, And God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness. Then He said in response to them, And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them? Even if you are among them and they seek forgiveness, and they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque. Others said: This is a new statement in which God Almighty says, informing about Himself: And God would not punish them. They differed in its interpretation. Ad-Dahhak and a group said: Its interpretation is: And God would not punish them while you are among them, residing among them. They said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was residing in Mecca. Then he left them and a remnant of the Muslims remained there seeking forgiveness. So God Almighty revealed: And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. Then those people left them and were punished, and God permitted the conquest of Mecca, so it is the punishment that He promised them. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: God did not punish a village until the Prophet and those who believed left it and he joined what he was commanded to do. Then he said: And God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness, meaning the Muslims. So when they left, God Almighty said: And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them? So God punished them on the day of Badr. Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari said: There were two types of security among you: And God would not punish them while you were among them, and And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. As for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he has passed away, and seeking forgiveness will remain among you until the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said: This seeking of forgiveness is for the polytheists, because they used to say after the circumambulation: Your forgiveness, your forgiveness. Yazid bin Ruman said: Quraysh said: If this is the truth from you, then rain down stones on us from the sky. When evening came, they regretted what they said, and said: I seek your forgiveness, O God. So God Almighty said: And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. Qatada and Al-Suddi said: Its meaning is: And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness, meaning: If they had sought forgiveness, but they were not seeking forgiveness, and if they had acknowledged the sin and sought forgiveness, they would have been believers. It was said: This is a call to Islam and seeking forgiveness with this word, like a man saying to another, I will not punish you as long as you obey me, meaning, obey me so that I will not punish you. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: And they seek forgiveness means they submit. He said: If they had submitted, they would not have been punished. Al-Walibi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “And among them are those who were destined by God to submit, believe, and seek forgiveness, such as: Abu Sufyan, Sufyan ibn Umayyah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Suhayl ibn Amr, Hakim ibn Hizam, and others.” Abdul Wahhab narrated on the authority of Mujahid: And they seek forgiveness means that in their loins are those who seek forgiveness.
8:34: 34 - The Almighty’s saying: And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them? That is: What prevents them from being punished, meaning after you have left them, while they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque? That is: They prevent the believers from circumambulating the House. It was said: By the first punishment he meant the punishment of extermination, and by his saying And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them he meant: with the sword. It was said: By the first he meant the torment of this world, and by this verse he meant the torment of the Hereafter. Al-Hasan said: The first verse, which is His statement, And God would not punish them, was abrogated by the statement of God Almighty, And why should they not be punished by God? “And they were not its guardians,” Al-Hasan said: The polytheists used to say, We are the guardians of the Sacred Mosque, so God responded to them by saying: And they were not its guardians, meaning: the guardians of the House. Its guardians, meaning: the guardians of the House, are only the righteous, meaning: the believers who fear polytheism, but most of them do not know.
8:35: 35 - The Almighty said: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping. Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said: Whistling means whistling, and in the language it is the name of a white bird that is found in the Hijaz and has a whistling sound, as if he said: Except the sound of whistling, and clapping means clapping. Ibn Abbas said: The Quraysh used to circumambulate the House naked, whistling and clapping. Mujahid said: A group of Banu Abd al-Dar used to oppose the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the circumambulation, mock him, put their fingers in their mouths, and whistle. Mucking means putting the fingers in the cheeks. Whistling is called tasddiyya, and from it comes the echo that a person hears on a mountain. Jaafar bin Rabia said: I asked Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman about the words of God Almighty: Except for whistling and clapping. So he brought his hands together and blew into them a whistle. Muqatil said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed in the mosque, two men would stand on his right and whistle, and two men would stand on his left and clap, in order to confuse the Prophet’s prayer, may God bless him and grant him peace. They were from Banu Abd al-Dar. Saeed bin Jubair said: Tasdiyya is their preventing the believers from the Sacred Mosque, from religion, and from prayer. According to this interpretation, it is: Tasdiyya with two dals, one of the dals was changed to a ya’, just as it is said tathannayt from dhan, and taqdi al-bazi if the falcon breaks, meaning the falcon breaks. Ibn al-Anbari said: He called it prayer because they were commanded to pray in the mosque, so they made that their prayer. So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.
8:36: 36 - The Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God, meaning: to turn away from the religion of God. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed about the obedient ones on the day of Badr, and they were twelve men: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah ibn Abd Shams, Nabih and Munabbih, the sons of Al-Hajjaj, Abu Al-Bukhtari ibn Hisham, Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, Hakim ibn Hizam, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Zam’ah ibn Al-Aswad, Al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal, and Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, and all of them were from Quraysh. He used to feed each one of them ten carrots every day. Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah said: It was revealed about Abu Sufyan who spent forty ounces on the polytheists on the day of Uhud. God Almighty said: They will spend it, then it will be a cause of regret for them. He means: What they spent in this world will be a cause of regret for them in the Hereafter. Then they will be overcome, they will not be victorious. And those who disbelieved, among them, will be gathered to Hell. He specified the disbelievers because some of them had converted to Islam. 36. Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God. This verse was revealed about those who were fed on the day of Badr, who were twelve men from Quraysh, each of whom was fed ten camels every day. Or about Abu Sufyan, who hired two thousand Arabs on the day of Uhud, in addition to those Arabs who sought help, and spent forty ounces on them. Or about the owners of the caravan, for when Quraysh were defeated at Badr, it was said to them, Help us with this wealth to fight Muhammad, so that we may take revenge on him. So they did. What is meant by the way of God is His religion and following His Messenger. They will spend it in its entirety. Perhaps the first is a statement about their spending at that time, which is the spending of Badr, and the second is a statement about their spending in the future, which is a limit. It is possible that both are intended to mean one thing, with the context of the first explaining the purpose of spending and the context of the second explaining its consequence, even though it has not yet occurred. Then it will be a cause of regret for them regret and sorrow for missing it without intending to make its essence become a cause of regret, which is the consequence of spending it, an exaggeration. Then they will be overcome in the end, even though the war between them was ongoing before that. And those who disbelieved meaning those who persisted in disbelief among them if some of them converted to Islam. To Hell they will be gathered will be driven.
8:37: 37 - So that God may distinguish the wicked [in the way of Satan] from the good, meaning: the disbeliever from the believer, so that the believer will be sent to Paradise and the disbeliever to Hell.God Al-Kalbi said: Evil deeds are like good deeds, so good deeds are rewarded with Paradise, and evil deeds are rewarded with Hell. It was said: It means: Evil spending in the way of Satan is better than good spending in the way of God. And He places some of the wicked upon others, meaning: on top of each other, and piles them all up, meaning: He gathers them. And from this comes the word heaped clouds, which are dense and gathered together. He places them in Hell. Those are the losers, referring back to His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth. “Those are the losers” whose trade has lost because they bought with their money the torment of the Hereafter. 37. That God may distinguish the wicked from the good, the disbeliever from the believer, or corruption from righteousness. The lam is related to they will be gathered together or they will be defeated, or what the polytheists spent in their enmity against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from what the Muslims spent in supporting him. The lam is related to His statement, Then there will be regret upon them. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read li-yameez from the word tameez, which is more eloquent than mayz. "And He will place the wicked, some of it upon some, and heap it all together," so He will gather it and join some of it to others until they overlap due to their extreme crowding, or He will add to the disbeliever what he spent to increase his punishment, as is the perfection of those who hoard. "And He will put it in Hell," all of it. "Those" refers to the wicked because it is estimated as the wicked group, or to the spenders. "They are the losers," the complete losers because they lost themselves and their wealth.
8:38: 38 - Say to those who have disbelieved that if they desist, from polytheism, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them, meaning: what has passed of their sins before Islam, but if they return [to faith], then the precedent of the former peoples has already taken place, in God’s victory for His prophets and the destruction of His enemies. Yahya ibn Mu’adh al-Razi said: Monotheism was not unable to destroy the disbelief that came before it, and I hope that it will not be unable to destroy the sin that comes after it.God
8:39: 39 - And fight them until there is no more persecution meaning: polytheism. Al-Rabi’ said: until no believer is tempted away from his religion and the religion is all for God meaning: and the religion is purely for God with no polytheism in it, but if they desist from disbelief, then indeed, God is Seeing of what they do. Ya’qub read ya’malun with a ta’, and the others read it with a ya’. 39. And fight them until there is no more persecution “and religion is all for God” and false religions are extinguished from them. But if they desist from disbelief. Then indeed, God is Seeing of what they do so He will reward them for desisting from it and becoming Muslim. And from Ya’qub with the letter ta meaning that indeed, God is Seeing of what you do of jihad and calling to Islam and bringing people out of the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith, so He will reward you. And His linking it to their desisting indicates that just as He calls for rewarding them for directly engaging in the action, He also calls for rewarding those who fight them for causing it.
8:40: 40 - And if they turn away, from the faith and return to fighting its people, then know that God is your Protector, your Supporter and Helper. What an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper.
8:41: 41 - The Almighty said: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, then indeed, God has a fifth of it (al-Bayhaqi 41:41). Spoils and booty: are two names for money that Muslims obtain from the money of the infidels. A group of people said that they are one, and a group said that they are different: Spoils are what the Muslims obtain from them by force through fighting, and booty is what was obtained through a peace treaty without fighting. So God the Almighty mentioned in this verse the ruling on spoils, saying: Then indeed, God has a fifth of it, and the Messenger has a share. Most of the commentators and jurists have said that his saying: For God is an opening statement by way of blessing and adding this money to himself for his honor, and it does not mean that a share of the spoils is for God alone, for the whole of this world and the hereafter are for God, the Almighty. This is the saying of Al-Hasan, Qatada, Ata’, Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi, who said: The share of God and the share of the Messenger are one. And the spoils are divided into five fifths, four fifths for those who fought for it, and one fifth for five categories as God, the Almighty, mentioned: And for the Messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer. Some of them said: The fifth is divided into six shares, which is the opinion of Abu Al-Aaliyah, a share for God: it is spent on the Kaaba. The first is more correct, that the fifth of the spoils is divided into five shares, a share that belonged to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his life, and today it is for the interests of the Muslims and what strengthens Islam, which is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, used to put the Prophet’s share, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the forelegs and weapons. Qatada said: It is for the caliph after him. Some of them said: The share of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is returned in the fifth, and the fifth is for four categories. His saying: And for the near of kin means that a share of the fifth is for the near of kin, who are the relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They differed about them. Some people said: All of Quraysh. Others said: They are those for whom charity is not permissible. Mujahed and Ali bin Al-Hussein said: They are the sons of Hashim. Al-Shafi’i said: They are Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, and Banu Abd Shams and Banu Nawfal have nothing from it, even though they are brothers. The evidence for this is as follows: Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Mutraf bin Mazen told us, on the authority of Muammar bin Rashid, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Muhammad bin Jubair bin Mut’im told me, on the authority of his father, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the share of the relatives between Banu Hashim and Banu Al-Muttalib, I and Uthman bin Affan came to him and said: O Messenger of God, these are our brothers from Banu Hashim, we do not deny their virtue because of the position that God has placed you among them. Have you seen our brothers from Banu Al-Muttalib, have you given to them and left us or withheld from us? Our kinship and their kinship are one. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Banu Hashim and Banu Al-Muttalib are one thing, like this and he interlaced his fingers.” Scholars differed on the share of relatives: is it fixed today? Most of them said that it is proven, and this is the opinion of Malik and Al-Shafi’i. The proponents of the opinion said that it is not proven, and they said: The share of the Messenger of God and the share of the relatives are returned in the fifth, and the fifth of the spoils is for three categories: orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer. Some of them said: It is given to the poor among them, not the rich. The Book and the Sunnah indicate that it is proven, and the caliphs after the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to give it, and the poor were not given preference over the rich, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the caliphs after him used to give al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib a share of his wealth. Al-Shafi’i included him in the inheritance that is due on the basis of kinship, except that it is given to the near and the distant. He said: The male is given preference over the female, so the male is given two shares and the female one share. His saying: And the orphans is the plural of orphan, and the orphan who has a share in the fifth is the young Muslim who has no father, if he is poor, and the needy are the people of need and want among the Muslims, and the wayfarer is the traveler who is far from his money, so this is the expenditure of the fifth of the spoils and four-fifths of the spoils are divided among the conquerors who witnessed the battle, for the horseman among them three shares, and for the foot soldier one share, because: Abu Salih Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Mu’adhin told us, Abdullah ibn Yusuf told us, Abu Saeed ibn al-A’rabi told us, Sa’dan ibn Nasr told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Umar, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave three shares to a man and his horse: one share for him and two shares for his horse. This is the opinion of most scholars, and it was adopted by al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, Malik, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, said: The horseman gets two shares, and the foot soldier gets one share. And it is submitted to the slaves, women and children if they attend the fighting, and the property seized by the Muslims is divided like movable property. According to Abu Hanifa: The imam has a choice regarding the property: between dividing it among them, or making it according to interests. The apparent meaning of the verse does not differentiate between real estate and movable property. Whoever kills a polytheist in combat deserves to take his spoils from the spoils of war, based on what was narrated on the authority of Abu Qatada that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the month of Hunayn: Whoever kills a person and has evidence against him, his spoils are his. And the spoils are: everything that belongs to the person killed, such as clothing, weapons, and the horse he is riding. The Imam may give some of the army a share of the spoils, due to the additional hardship and suffering they will suffer in war. He may single them out from among the rest of the army and make them equal to the group in the two shares of the spoils: Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqil, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would give some of those he sent out from the raids as voluntary gifts to themselves specifically, except for a section of the general army. It was narrated on the authority of Habib bin Muslimah Al-Fahri, who said: I witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a quarter of the voluntary charity at the beginning and a third at the return. They differed about the source of the voluntary charity. Some people said: From the fifth of the fifth, the share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the opinion of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Al-Shafi’i said the same. This is the meaning of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have nothing from what God has bestowed upon you except the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you. Some people said: It is one of the four fifths after separating the fifth like the arrows of the warriors, and this is the saying of Ahmad and Isaac. Some of them went to the view that the voluntary portion of the spoils of war before the fifth is like the spoils of war for the killer. As for the spoils of war: it is what the Muslims took from the money of the infidels without sending horses or camels, by making peace with them on money that they pay, and the money of the jizya, and what is taken from their money if they enter the land of Islam for trade, or one of them dies in the land of Islam and has no heir, then all of this is spoils of war. The spoils of war were exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his lifetime. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: God has singled out the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this spoils of war with something that He has not given to anyone else. Then he recited: And what God has bestowed upon His Messenger from them until His saying: Able (al-Hashr 59:6). This was exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He would spend on his family and children their annual expenses from this money, then he would take what remained and make it the property of God Almighty. Scholars differed about the distribution of the spoils of war after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some people said: It is for the imams after him. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions about it: One of them is for the fighters whose names are recorded in the register of jihad, because they are the ones who take the place of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in terrorizing the enemy. The second opinion is that it is for the interests of the Muslims, and it begins with the fighters, so they are given from it what they need, then the most important interests, and so on. Scholars differed on the fifth of the spoils of war. Al-Shafi’i said that one-fifth of it is given to the people of the spoils, divided into five shares. Four-fifths of it is given to the fighters and the opposing forces. Most of them said: The spoils of war are not divided into fifths, but rather all of them are spent in one place, and all Muslims have a right to them: Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzaz told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq Al-Dabry told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Malik bin Aws bin Al-Hadathan: that he heard Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: There is no Muslim on the face of the earth who does not have a right to this booty, except for what your right hands possess. Abu Saeed Al-Tahiri told us that my grandfather Abd Al-Samad bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Bazzaz told us that Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us that Abu Ishaq Al-Dabry told us that Abd Al-Razzaq told us that Muammar told us on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Ikrimah bin Khalid on the authority of Malik bin Aws bin Al-Hadathan who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, recited: Zakat is only for the poor and the needy until he reached Knowing and Wise (al-Tawbah 9:60). He said: This is for these people. Then he recited: And know that whatever you obtain of anything, a fifth of it is for God until he reached and for the wayfarer. Then he said: This is for these people. Then he recited: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns until he reached for the poor emigrants who were expelled (al-Hashr 59:7-9). Then he said: This includes all Muslims. If I live, the shepherd will come to him while he is in the gardens of Himyar and his share of it will not break on his forehead. God Almighty says: If you have believed in God, it was said that he meant, Know that whatever you gain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger, He commands in it what He wants, so accept it if you have believed in God. And what We have sent down to Our servant, meaning: if you have believed in God and in what We have sent down to Our servant, meaning: His saying, They ask you about the spoils of war, “The Day of Discrimination,” meaning the Day of Badr, when God distinguished between truth and falsehood, which was the day the two armies met, the party of God and the party of Satan, and it was a Friday, seventeen days before the end of Ramadan. And God is over all things competent, to grant you victory despite your fewness and your greatness.
8:42: 42 - When you, meaning: when you are descending, O group of Muslims, on the lower side of the valley, meaning: on the edge of the valley closest to Medina, and the lower side. The feminine of the lower, and they, meaning your enemy from the polytheists, on the farthest side, on the edge of the valley furthest from Medina, and the farthest is the feminine of the farthest. Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read with the enemy with a kasra on the ‘ayn in both, and the rest read it with a damma on both. They are two dialects like clothing and clothing and bribery and bribery. And the caravan, meaning: the caravan, meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions, is below you, meaning: in a place below you to the seashore, three miles from Badr. And if you had made an appointment, you would have differed in the appointment, because the Muslims went out to seize the caravan and the infidels went out to prevent it, so they met without an appointment. God Almighty said: And if you had made an appointment, you would have differed in the appointment, because of your small number and the great number of your enemy. But God gathered you without an appointment, that God might accomplish a matter that was to be done, of the victory of His allies, the glory of His religion, and the destruction of His enemies, that he who perishes may perish with clear evidence, meaning that he who dies may die with clear evidence that he saw and a lesson that he witnessed and an argument that was established for him, and he who lives may live with clear evidence, and he who lives may live with clear evidence of His promise: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger (al-Isra’ 17:15). Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Its meaning is that whoever disbelieves after an argument has been established against him may disbelieve, and whoever believes in the same way may believe. So destruction is disbelief, and life is faith. Qatada said: So that he who goes astray may go astray with clear evidence, and he who is guided with clear evidence may be guided. The people of Hijaz, Abu Bakr and Yaqub read: Hayyi with two ya’s, like Khashi. The others read: with one doubled ya’, because it is written with one ya’. And indeed, God is Hearing of your supplications, Knowing of your intentions.
8:43: 43 - The Almighty said: When God showed them to you He showed you, O Muhammad, the polytheists, in your dream meaning: your sleep. Al-Hasan said: In your dream meaning in your eye, because the eye is the place of sleep, little, but if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart meaning you would have become cowardly and you would have disputed meaning: you would have differed in the matter meaning: in hesitation and courage, but God saved meaning He saved you from disobedience and failure, Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts. Ibn Abbas said: He knows what is in your breasts of love for God the Almighty:
8:44: 44 - And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, Muqatil said: This is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw in a dream that the enemy was few before meeting the enemy, and he told his companions what he saw. Then, when they met at Badr, God made the polytheists few in the eyes of the believers. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: They seemed so small to us that I said to a man next to me: Do you think they are seventy? He said: I think they are a hundred. Then we captured a man and said: How many were you? He said: A thousand. And He will make you, O believers, in their eyes, As-Suddi said: Some of the polytheists said: The caravan has departed, so go back. Abu Jahl said: Now that Muhammad and his companions have come out to you, do not go back until you have exterminated them. Muhammad and his companions are nothing but cannibals, so do not kill them, and tie them up with ropes - he says this from the power that is in his soul - Al-Kalbi said: Some of them were proud of each other so that they would dare to fight, so He made the polytheists insignificant in the eyes of the believers so that they would not be loved, and He made the believers insignificant in the eyes of the polytheists so that they would not flee, so that God may accomplish a matter of exalting Islam and honoring its people and humiliating polytheism and its people. Was done is happening, and to God all matters return.
8:45: 45 - The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, when you meet a company meaning: a disbelieving group, then stand firm to fight them, and remember God much meaning: call upon God for victory and triumph over them, that you may succeed meaning: be hopeful of success.
8:46: 46 - The Almighty said: And obey God and His Messenger and do not dispute, do not differ, lest you lose heart, that is, become cowardly and weak, and your strength departs, Mujahid said: your victory. Al-Suddi said: your courage and your seriousness. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: your sharpness. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: your strength. Al-Akhfash said: your state. The wind here is a metaphor for the execution of the matter and its running as intended. The Arabs say: the wind of so-and-so blew if his matter went as he wanted. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: it is the wind of victory. There has never been victory except by a wind sent by God Almighty to strike the faces of the enemy. And from it is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And I was aided by the north wind, and the ‘Ad were destroyed by the south wind. On the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Muqrin, he said: I was present with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If he did not fight at the beginning of the day, he would wait until the sun had set, the wind had blown, and victory had descended. God the Almighty said: “And be patient. Indeed, God is with the patient.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Muawiyah bin Amr told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of Salim Abu Al-Nadr, the freed slave of Omar bin Ubaidullah, who was his scribe, who said: Abdullah bin Abi Awfa wrote to him and I read it to him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on one of the days in which he encountered the enemy, waited until the sun declined, then he stood among the people and said: “O people, do not wish to encounter the enemy and ask God for well-being. When you encounter them, be patient and know that Paradise is under the shadows of swords. Then he said: O God, Revealer of the Book, Mover of the clouds, and Defeater of the parties, defeat them and grant us victory over them.”
8:47: 47 - The Almighty said: And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently, boasting and evil, and to be seen by people, Al-Zajjaj said: Insolence is tyranny in blessings and not being grateful for them, and hypocrisy is showing off the good so that it is seen and concealing the bad, and they hinder [people] from the way of God, and God encompasses what they do, it was revealed about the polytheists when they came to Badr and they were insolent and proud, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, this is Quraysh who has come with its arrogance and pride, arguing with You and denying Your Messenger, God, grant me the victory that You promised me, they said: When Abu Sufyan saw that he had secured his caravan, he sent to Quraysh that you only came forth to protect your caravan, but God has saved it, so go back, so Abu Jahl said: By God, we will not go back until we return to Badr, and Badr was a season of the seasons of the Arabs where they would gather for a market every year, so we would stay there for three days, slaughter camels, feed the food, and water the water. Wine was sung to us, and the female singers played for us, and the Arabs heard about us and they would never cease to fear us. So they met them and poured out cups of death instead of wine, and the female mourners wailed for them instead of the female singers. So God forbade His believing servants from being like them and commanded them to be sincere in their intentions and to seek reward, so that His religion would be victorious and His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be supported.
8:48: 48 - The Almighty said: And when Satan made their deeds fair-seeming to them, and his making it fair-seeming was that when the Quraysh gathered to march, they remembered the war that had taken place between them and Banu Bakr, so that almost dissuaded them, so Satan came with an army of devils with his banner, and he appeared to them in the form of Suraqah bin Malik bin Ja'sham, and said, to them, No one from among mankind can overcome you today, and I am your protector, meaning: I will protect you from Kinanah, So when the two armies came into sight, meaning the two groups met, Satan saw the angels descending from the sky, and he knew that he would not be able to defeat them, he turned back on his heels, Ad-Dahhak said: He turned away, fleeing. An-Nadr bin Shumayl said: He turned back on his back, fleeing. Al-Kalbi said: When they met, Satan was in the ranks of the polytheists in the form of Suraqah bin Malik, taking the hand of Al-Harith bin Hisham, so he turned back on his heels, so Al-Harith said to him: Fleeing without fighting? So he held him, pushed him in the chest, and set off, and the people fled. When they arrived in Mecca, they said, The people defeated Suraqa. When Suraqa heard of that, he said, I have heard that you say, ‘I defeated the people.’ By God, I did not know about your march until I heard of your defeat! They said, Did you not come to us on such-and-such a day? So he swore to them. When they converted to Islam, they knew that it was the devil. Al-Hasan said regarding his statement: “And he said, ‘Indeed, I am innocent of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see.’” He said: Iblis saw Gabriel wrapped in a cloak walking in front of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in his hand was the bridle leading the horse, which he did not ride. Qatada said: Iblis used to say: I see what you do not see, and he spoke the truth. He said: I fear God, and he lied. By God, he does not fear God, but he knew that he had no strength or protection, so he brought them to him and surrendered them. This is the habit of the enemy of God for those who obey him. When truth and falsehood meet, he surrenders them and disavows them. Ata' said: I fear that God will destroy me among those who perish. Al-Kalbi said: He was afraid that Gabriel, peace be upon him, would take him and know his condition, so they would not obey him. It was said: Its meaning is that I fear God, meaning I know the truth of His promise to His friends because he was confident in His command. And God is severe in penalty. It was said: Its meaning is that I fear God for you, and God is severe in penalty. It was also said: The speech stopped at his saying I fear God, then God says: And God is severe in penalty. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ali, on the authority of Talhah ibn `Ubayd God ibn Kurayz, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Satan has never been seen on a day when he is smaller, more defeated, more humiliated, or more angry than on the Day of `Arafah. This is only because he sees the descent of mercy and the forgiveness of great sins by God, the Most High, except for what happened on the Day of Badr.” It was said: What did he see on the Day of Badr? He said: “He saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, and he was commanding the angels.” This is a mursal hadith.
8:49: 49 - The Almighty said: When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said, doubt and hypocrisy, These people were deceived by their religion, meaning: The believers were deceived by their religion. These were people who were weak in Mecca and had converted to Islam, and their relatives had detained them from migrating. When the Quraysh went out to Badr, they were forced to leave. When they saw the small number of Muslims, they became suspicious and turned back, and said: These people were deceived by their religion. So they were all killed, including: Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abu Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, al-Harith ibn Zama’ah ibn al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, Ali ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, and al-‘As ibn Munabbih ibn al-Hajjaj. God Almighty said: And whoever relies upon God, meaning: and whoever submits his affair to God and trusts in Him, then indeed, God is Exalted in Might, strong, He does with His enemies as He wills, Wise.
8:50: 50 - And if you could but see, O Muhammad, when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, meaning: they take their souls. They differed about it. It was said: This is at death, the angels strike the faces and backs of the disbelievers with whips of fire.
