It was said: He meant those polytheists who were killed at Badr, the angels would strike their faces and their backs. Saeed bin Jubair and Mujahid said: He meant their buttocks, but God is modest and uses euphemisms. Ibn Abbas said: When the polytheists turned their faces toward the Muslims, the angels would strike their faces with swords, and when they turned away, the angels would catch up with them and strike their backs. Ibn Jurayj said: He means what is before them and what is behind them, meaning: They will strike their entire bodies, and what is meant by death is killing. And taste the punishment of the burning fire, meaning: The angels will say: Taste the punishment of the burning fire. It was said: The angels had iron clubs with which they would strike the disbelievers, so the fire would burn in their wounds, and that is what the Almighty said: And taste the punishment of the burning fire. Al-Hasan said: This is on the Day of Resurrection when the keepers of Hell will say to them: Taste the punishment of the burning fire. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: They will say that to them after death.
8:51: 51 - That, meaning: that strike that befell you, is because of what your hands have put forth, meaning: because of what your hands have earned, and that God is not unjust to His servants.
8:52: 52 - Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh, like the actions, deeds and customs of the people of Pharaoh, meaning: the habit of these people in their disbelief is like the habit of the people of Pharaoh. Ibn Abbas said: It is that the people of Pharaoh were certain that Moses was a prophet from God, but they denied him. Likewise, these people, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, came to them with the truth, but they denied him, so God sent down a punishment upon them as He sent down upon the people of Pharaoh. And those before them, meaning: "disbelieved in the signs of God, so God seized them for their sins. Indeed, God is Powerful and Severe in penalty."
8:53: 53 - That is because God would not change a favor which He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is within themselves. He meant: God Almighty does not change what He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is within themselves, by being ungrateful and abandoning gratitude. So if they do that, God will change what is within them, and will take away the favor from them. Al-Suddi said: God’s blessing is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God bestowed his blessing upon the Quraysh and the people of Mecca, but they denied him and disbelieved in him, so God transferred him to the Ansar, and God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
8:54: 54 - Like the way of Pharaoh’s people, like the way Pharaoh’s people did, and those before them, of the disbelieving nations, they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, We destroyed some of them with an earthquake, some with a sinking, some with a transformation, some with a wind, and some with drowning. Thus, We destroyed the disbelievers of Badr with the sword, when they denied the signs of their Lord, and We drowned Pharaoh’s people, and all of them were wrongdoers, meaning: the first and the last.
8:55: 55- Indeed, the worst of beasts in the sight of God are those who disbelieve - so they will not believe. Al-Kalbi and Qatil said: He means the Jews of Banu Qurayzah, including Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions.
8:56: 56 - Those of whom you made a treaty, meaning you made a treaty with them. It was said: meaning: you made a treaty with them. It was said that of was included because its meaning is: you took a treaty from them, then they break their treaty every time, and they are Banu Qurayzah, they broke the treaty that was between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they aided the polytheists with weapons to fight the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, then they said: we forgot and made a mistake, so he made a treaty with them a second time, so they broke the treaty and sided with the infidels against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of the Trench, and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf rode to Mecca, and he agreed with them in opposing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they do not fear God, they do not fear God Almighty in breaking the treaty.
8:57: 57 - If you find them in war, Muqatil said: If you catch up with them in war and take them prisoner, then scatter with them those behind them, Ibn Abbas said: Then torment them from behind them. Saeed bin Jubair said: Warn those behind them about them. The root of scattering is to disperse and scatter. Its meaning is to disperse with them the gathering of every breaker, i.e.: Do with those who broke your covenant and came to fight you in the act of killing and tormenting, so that those behind them from the people of Mecca and Yemen will fear you and be afraid of you, perhaps they will remember, remember and take heed and not break the covenant.
8:58: 58 - And if you fear that is, you know, O Muhammad, from a people with whom you have a treaty, treachery - a breach of a treaty, due to the signs of treachery that appear to you from them, as appeared from Qurayzah and Nadir, then throw back to them - throw their treaty to them, on an equal footing - he says, inform them before you wage war against them that you have broken the treaty between you and them, so that you and they will be equal in knowledge of the breach of the treaty, and they will not [accuse] that you broke the treaty by waging war against them, Indeed, God does not love the treacherous. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi told us, Abu Sahl Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Tarfa al-Sajzi told us, Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Razzaq ibn Dasa al-Tammar told us, Abu Dawud Sulayma ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani told us, Hafs ibn Umar al-Namri told us, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Fayd, on the authority of [Salim] ibn Amir, on the authority of a man from Himyar, who said: There was a treaty between Mu'awiyah and the Romans, and he was moving towards their country, until when the treaty expired he attacked them. Then a man came on a horse saying: God is Great, God is Great, loyalty, no treachery. He looked and saw that he was Amr ibn Abasa. So Mu'awiyah sent for him and asked him, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever has a treaty between him and a people, he should not tighten a knot or loosen it until its term expires or he denounces it to them equally. So Mu'awiyah, may God be pleased with him, returned.
8:59: 59 - The Almighty said: And let not those who disbelieve think that they will outstrip, Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Amir, Hamza and Hafs read yaḥṣbun with a ya’, and others read it with a ta’, sabaqū meaning: they missed, it was revealed about those polytheists who were defeated on the day of Badr. So whoever reads it with a ya’ says let not those who disbelieve think that they will outstrip or escape Our punishment, and whoever reads it with a ta’ then it is addressing, Ibn `Amir read: Indeed they are not helpless with a fathah on the alif, meaning: because they are not helpless, and they do not escape Me. And the others read it with a kasrah on the alif as an initial.
8:60: 60 - The Almighty said: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power. Preparation: taking something for a time of need. Of power, meaning: of the tools that will give you power over them, such as horses and weapons. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj, Harun bin Maruf told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Abu Ali, Thamamah bin Shafi, that he heard Uqbah bin Amir say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, while he was on the pulpit: “Prepare for them whatever you are able of power. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery.” With this chain of transmission, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The Romans will be conquered for you, and God Almighty will suffice you. So none of you should be unable to play with his arrows.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Naim told us, Abdul Rahman bin Al-Ghasil told us, on the authority of Hamza bin Abi Asid, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Badr when we lined up for the Quraysh and they lined up for us: If they attack you, then use arrows. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abdul Samad bin Abdul Warith told us, Hisham Al-Dastawai told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d, on the authority of Ma’dan bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abu Najih Al-Salami, who said: We besieged At-Ta’if with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever shoots an arrow in the cause of God will have a degree in Paradise. He said: So I shot sixteen arrows that day. And I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever shoots an arrow in the cause of God will have the equivalent of a freed slave. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Al-Hussein Ali bin Muhammad bin Bishran told us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Katheer, on the authority of Zaid bin Salam, on the authority of Abdullah bin Zaid Al-Azraq, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir Al-Juhani, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God admits three people to Paradise with a single aral-Saff 61:its maker, the one who extends it, and the one who shoots it in the way of God.” It was narrated on the authority of Khalid bin Zaid, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God will admit three people into Paradise because of a single aral-Saff 61:the one who makes it and expects good from his making, the one who shoots it, and the one who shoots it. Shoot and ride, and shooting is more beloved to me than riding. Everything that a man does for fun is futile except shooting with his bow, training his horse, and playing with his wife, for they are from the truth. Whoever abandons archery after learning it out of a desire for it, then it is a blessing that he has abandoned, or he said, he has been ungrateful for.” His saying: And among the tethering of horses, meaning: tying them up and keeping them for war. Ikrimah said: Strength is fortresses, and among the tethering of horses are females. It was narrated on the authority of Khalid ibn al-Walid that he would not ride in battle except females because of their little neighing. And on the authority of Abu Muhayriz, he said: The Companions, may God be pleased with them, preferred male horses to the ranks and female horses to the night raids. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Naim told us, Zakariya told us on the authority of Amer, Urwa Al-Barqi told us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Horses have good tied to their forelocks until the Day of Resurrection, reward and spoils. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Hafs told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Talha bin Abi Saeed told us: I heard Saeed Al-Maqburi narrating that he heard Abu Hurairah say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever keeps a horse in the way of God out of faith in God and belief in His promise, then its food, its drink, its dung, and its urine will be on his scale on the Day of Resurrection. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Horses are of three types: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a cover, and for a man they are a burden. As for the one for which he is a reward, it is a man who ties them up in the way of God and lets them ride long distances in a meadow or garden, and whatever they hit in their length from that meadow or garden, they are good deeds for him. If they cut their lengths and reach a peak or two, their traces and inheritance are good deeds for him. If they pass by a river and drink from it, and he does not want to give them water, that is good deeds for him, so they are a reward for that man. As for the one for which he is a cover, it is a man who ties them up out of pride and chastity, and does not forget the right of God in their backs or necks, in that is a cover for him. As for the one for which he is a burden, it is a man who ties them up out of pride, showing off, and aversion.” For the people of Islam, it is a sin for that. “And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about donkeys, so he said: Nothing was revealed to me about them except this comprehensive and unique verse: “So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.” You terrorize with it, you frighten the enemy of God, your enemy, and others, meaning: and you terrorize others, besides them, you do not know them, God knows them. Mujahid, Muqatil, and Qatadah said: They are Banu Qurayzah. Al-Suddi said: They are the people of Persia. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: They are the hypocrites, you do not know them, because they are with you saying: There is no god but God. And it was said: They are the disbelieving jinn. Whatever you spend in the way of God will be fully repaid to you, He will fully repay you for it, and you will not be wronged, your reward will not be diminished.
8:61: 61 - The Almighty’s saying: “And if they incline to peace,” meaning: they incline toward reconciliation, then incline toward it, meaning: lean toward it and make peace with them. It was narrated on the authority of Qatada and Al-Hasan: That this verse was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (Al-Bara’: 5) And put your trust in God! Trust in God, For He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
8:62: 62 - And if they intend to deceive you, they betray you. Mujahid said: He means Banu Qurayzah. Then sufficient for you is God, God is sufficient for you. It is He who supported you with His victory and with the believers, meaning: with the Ansar.
8:63: 63 - And He brought their hearts together, that is, between the Aws and the Khazraj. There was grudge and blood feud between them in the pre-Islamic era, so God made them brothers after they had been enemies. "If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together. But God brought their hearts together. Indeed, He is Exalted in Might and Wise."
8:64: 64 - The Almighty said: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers. Saeed bin Jubair said: Thirty-three men and six women converted to Islam with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Umar bin Al-Khattab converted to Islam, and with him the number was forty, and this verse was revealed. They differed about the position of min. Most of the commentators said that it is in the accusative case, in apposition to the kaf in His statement: God is sufficient for you and and He is sufficient for those who follow you. Some of them said: It is in the nominative case, in apposition to the name of God, meaning: God is sufficient for you and those who follow you from among the believers.
8:65: 65 - The Almighty said: "O Prophet, urge the believers to fight," meaning: urge them to fight. "If there are twenty of you, men, patient, seeking reward, they will overcome two hundred," of their enemy, they will subdue them. "And if there are a hundred of you, patient and seeking reward, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, that is because they are a people who do not understand," meaning: the polytheists fight without expecting reward or seeking reward, and they do not stand firm if you support them in fighting, for fear that they will be killed. This is a report with the meaning of a command, and this was on the day of Badr when God imposed on one man from the believers to fight ten of the disbelievers, so it was too heavy for the believers, so God made it easier for them, so He revealed:
8:66: 66 - Now God has lightened your burden and knows that there is weakness in you, meaning: weakness in one person compared to fighting ten and in one hundred compared to fighting a thousand. Abu Ja`far read: weak with the opening of the `ayn and the extension for the plural, and the others read with the sukoon of the `ayn, So if there are a hundred of you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, of the infidels, And if there are a thousand of you, they will overcome two thousand by permission of God, and God is with the patient, so he returned from ten to two, so if the Muslims are half of their enemy, it is not permissible for them to flee. Sufyan said: Ibn Shabrama said: I see enjoining good and forbidding evil as something like this. The people of Kufa read: And if there are a hundred of you with a ya’ in both of them, and agreed with the people of Basra in the first, and the rest with a ta’ in both of them. Asim and Hamza read da’fan with a fatha on the dhad here and in Surat Ar-Rum, and the rest read it with a damma.
8:67: 67 - And the Almighty’s saying: It is not for a prophet to have captives, Abu Ja`far and the people of Basra read: takun with a ta’ and the rest with a ya’, and Abu Ja`far read: asara, and the others asra. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Murrah on the authority of Abu Ubaid on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: “When the day of Badr came and the prisoners were brought, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you say about these people? Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, they are your people and your family, so spare them and wait for them, perhaps God will accept their repentance, and take a ransom from them, so that we may have strength against the infidels. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, they lied to you and expelled you, so bring them forward so that we may strike their necks. Give Ali power over Uqayl so that he may strike his neck, and give me power over so-and-so - a relative of Umar - so that I may strike his neck, for these are the leaders of infidelity. Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: O Messenger of God, look for a valley with plenty of firewood and bring them into it, then light a fire over them. Al-Abbas said to him: You have severed your ties of kinship. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent and did not answer them, then he entered. Some people said: He will accept the words of Abu Bakr, and some said: He will accept the words of Umar, and some said: He will accept the words of Ibn Rawahah. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out.” And he said: Verily, God, the Most High, softens the hearts of men until they are softer than milk, and hardens the hearts of men until they are harder than stones. And your example, O Abu Bakr, is like that of Abraham, who said: So whoever follows me - indeed, he is of me, and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are Forgiving and Merciful (Ibrahim 14:36). And your example, O Abu Bakr, is like that of Jesus, who said: If You should punish them - indeed, they are Your servants; but if You forgive them - indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise (al-Ma’idah 5:118). And your example, O Umar, is like that of Noah, who said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers (Nuh 71:26), and like that of Moses, who said: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts (Yunus 10:88). Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Today you are dependents, and none of them will escape except by ransom or by beheading.” Abdullah bin Mas’ud said: Except for Suhayl bin Bayda, for I heard him mention Islam, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent. I have never seen myself more afraid of stones falling from the sky than that day. Until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Except for Suhayl ibn Bayda. Ibn Abbas said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was moved by what Abu Bakr said, but he was not moved by what I said. When the next day came, I came and found the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr sitting [crying]. I said: O Messenger of God, tell me about what you and your companion are crying about. If I find the means to cry, I will cry, and if I do not find the means to cry, I will pretend to cry because of your crying? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am crying because of what your companions offered me regarding taking ransom. Their punishment was offered to me closer than this tree, a tree close to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And God, the Most High, revealed: It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a great slaughter on the land until His saying: So eat of what you have taken as spoils of war, lawful and good Al-Anfal 8:67-69. So God made the spoils lawful for them. By His saying: He has captives is the plural of captive like slain is the plural of qatila. His statement: until he makes great slaughter in the land, meaning: he exaggerates in fighting the polytheists and taking them captive. You desire, O believers, the worldly goods by taking ransom, and God desires the Hereafter, He desires for you the reward of the Hereafter by defeating the polytheists and supporting the religion of God Almighty, and God is Exalted in Might and Wise. The ransom for each prisoner was forty ounces, and an ounce was forty dirhams. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: This was the day of Badr, and the Muslims at that time were few. When they became numerous and their power grew stronger, God revealed about the prisoners: Then either by favor afterwards or by ransom (Muhammad 47:4). God Almighty gave His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers the choice in the matter of the prisoners: if they wanted to kill them, they could enslave them, if they wanted to ransom them, they could free them.
8:68: 68 - The Almighty said: Had it not been for a previous decree from God, Ibn Abbas said: Spoils of war were forbidden to the prophets and nations, so whenever they acquired some spoils of war, they would make it an offering, and fire would descend from the sky and consume it. Then, on the day of Badr, the believers rushed to the spoils and took the ransom, so God, the Almighty, revealed: Had it not been for a previous decree from God, meaning had it not been for a previous decree from God in the Preserved Tablet that spoils of war would be permissible for you. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Saeed bin Jubair said: If it were not for a previous book from God that no one who witnessed Badr with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be punished. Ibn Jurayj said: If it were not for a previous book from God that He will not lead a people astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid, and that He will not take people who did things out of ignorance, that would have touched you, would have reached you and afflicted you, for what you took of ransom before you were commanded to do so, a great punishment. Ibn Ishaq said: None of the believers who were present were more interested in the spoils of war than Umar ibn al-Khattab, who advised the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill the prisoners. Sa`d ibn Mu`adh said: O Messenger of God, killing in great numbers was more beloved to me than sparing the men. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a punishment were to descend from the sky, none would be saved from it except Umar ibn al-Khattab and Sa`d ibn Mu`adh.
8:69: 69 - Then God Almighty said: "So eat of what you have taken as lawful and good spoils, and fear God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful." It was narrated that when the first verse was revealed, the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, withheld their hands from what they had taken as ransom, so the verse: "So eat of what you have taken as spoils" was revealed. We narrated on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Spoils of war were made lawful for me, but they were not made lawful for anyone before me." Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Al-Ziyadi told us, Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God said: Spoils of war were not permissible for anyone before us, because God saw our weakness and inability and made them permissible for us.
8:70: 70 - The Almighty’s saying: O Prophet, say to those of the captives in your hands, Abu Amr and Abu Jaafar read: of the captives with an alif, and the rest without an alif. It was revealed about Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib may God be pleased with him, who was taken prisoner on the day of Badr. He was one of the ten who guaranteed the food of the people of Badr. The day of Badr was his turn, and he had gone out with twenty ounces of gold to feed the people. He wanted to feed them that day, but they fought and the twenty ounces remained with him, so they were taken from him in the war. So he spoke to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to count the twenty ounces as part of his ransom, but he refused and said: As for what you went out with to help us, I will not leave it for you. And he was charged with ransoming his nephews, Uqayl ibn Abi Talib and Nawfal ibn Al-Harith. Al-Abbas said: O Muhammad, you left me begging from the Quraysh as long as I live? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Where is the gold that you gave to Umm Al-Fadl when you left Mecca and you said to her: I do not know what will happen to me on this face of mine, so if something happens to me, it is for you, for Abdullah, for Ubaidullah, for Al-Fadl and for Qutham, meaning his Prophet. Al-Abbas said to him: How do you know? He said: My Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, informed me of it. Al-Abbas said: I bear witness that you are truthful! And that there is no god but God and that you are His servant and Messenger, and no one has seen it except God, the Almighty, the Majestic. This is what God, the Almighty, said: O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives, from whom you have taken ransom, If God knows good in your hearts, meaning faith, He will give you better than what was taken from you, of ransom, and forgive you, your sins, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. [Al-Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said] So God replaced it for me with twenty slaves, all of them merchants who traded with a lot of money, and the least of them traded with twenty thousand dirhams instead of twenty ounces, and He gave me Zamzam, and I would not like to have all the money of the people of Mecca in exchange for it, and I await forgiveness from my Lord, the Almighty, the Majestic.
8:71: 71 - The Almighty’s saying, And if they intend to betray you, meaning the captives, they betrayed God before, and He gave them power over you, at Badr, and God is Knowing and Wise. Ibn Jurayj said: What he meant by betrayal is disbelief, meaning: If they disbelieve in you, they disbelieved in God before, and He gave them power over you at Badr until they killed them and took them captive. This is a threat to them if they return to fighting the believers and opposing them.
8:72: 72 - The Almighty said: Indeed, those who believed and emigrated, meaning: left their people and their homes, meaning the emigrants. And strived with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God and those who gave shelter the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the emigrants with him, meaning: settled them in their homes, and aided meaning: and supported them against their enemies, who are the Ansar, may God be pleased with them, they are allies of one another, not their relatives among the disbelievers. It was said: in aid and support. Ibn Abbas said: In inheritance, they used to inherit by migration, so the Muhajireen and Ansar used to inherit from each other without their relatives, and whoever believed but did not migrate did not inherit from his relative who migrated until the conquest of Mecca and migration was cut off, and they used to inherit from each other by their relatives wherever they were, and that was abrogated by the words of God Almighty: And those of kinship are nearer to each other in the ordinance of God (al-Ahzab 33:6), And those who believed but did not emigrate - you have no right to their guardianship at all meaning inheritance, until they emigrate Hamza read: their guardianship with a kasra on the waw, and the rest with a fatha, and they are one like indication and indication. And if they seek your aid in religion meaning: the believers who did not migrate seek your aid, then you must aid them except against a people between you and whom there is a treaty a covenant, so do not aid them against them, and God is Seeing of what you do.
8:73: 73 - And those who disbelieve are allies of one another," in aid and victory. Ibn Abbas said: In inheritance, meaning: the polytheists inherit from one another, "If you do not do so, there will be turmoil on earth," Ibn Abbas said: If you do not take in inheritance what I have commanded you to do. Ibn Jurayj said: Unless they cooperate and support each other. Ibn Ishaq said: God made the Muhajireen and Ansar people of guardianship in religion, to the exclusion of all others, and He made the infidels guardians of one another. Then He said: If you do not do it, which is that the believer takes the infidel as his guardian rather than the believer, there will be tribulation on earth and great corruption, so the tribulation on earth is the strength of disbelief, and the great corruption is the weakness of Islam.
8:74: 74 - And those who believed and emigrated and fought in the cause of God and those who gave shelter and aided - those are the believers, truly. There is no doubt or suspicion in their faith. It was said: They confirmed their faith by emigrating, fighting, and spending money in the cause of religion. For them is forgiveness and noble provision in Paradise. If it is said: What is the meaning of repeating this verse? It was said: The emigrants were divided into classes: Some of them were the people of the first emigration, and they were the ones who emigrated before Hudaybiyyah, and some of them were the people of the second emigration, and they were the ones who emigrated after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah before the conquest of Mecca, and some of them had two emigrations, the emigration to Abyssinia and the emigration to Medina, so what is meant by the first verse is the first emigration, and what is meant by the second is the second emigration.
8:75: 75 - His statement: And those who believed afterward and emigrated and fought with you - those are of you. That is, with you, meaning: you are from them and they are from you, and those of kinship are more worthy of one another. This is the abrogation of inheritance by emigration and the return of inheritance to those of kinship. His saying, In the Book of God, meaning: in the judgment of God Almighty. It was said: What he meant by the Book of God is the Qur’an, meaning: the division that He explained in Surat An-Nisa’, Indeed, God is Knowing of all things.
9:1: Muqatil said: This surah is Madani except for two verses at the end of the surah. Saeed bin Jubair said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Surat At-Tawbah? He said: It is the scandalous one that kept being revealed: And from them, and from them until they thought that it had not left anyone of them except that he was mentioned in it. He said: I said: Surat Al-Anfal? He said: That is Surat Badr. I said: Surat Al-Hashr? He said: Say Surat Banu An-Nadir. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad bin Muhammad Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Jurjani told us, Abu Ahmad Abdullah bin Adi Al-Hafiz told us, Ahmad bin Ali bin Al-Muthanna told us, Ubaidullah Al-Qawariri told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Awf bin Abi Jamila Al-A’rabi told us, Yazid Al-Farsi told me, Ibn Abbas told me, may God be pleased with them both, he said: I said to Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him: What made you go to Al-Anfal, which is from Al-Mathani, and to Bara’ah, which is from Al-Mi’in, and you combined them and did not write between them In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and put them in the seven long ones? Uthman said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one of those who would come upon him in time, and the surahs of many numbers would be revealed to him. When something was revealed to him, he would call one of his scribes and say: Place this verse in the surah in which such and such is mentioned. Al-Anfal was among those revealed in Medina, and Bara’ah was among the last to be revealed, and its story was similar to its story. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away without explaining to us that it was part of it. Therefore, I combined them and did not write between them a line saying In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and I placed it among the seven long ones. 1- The Almighty said: A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger, meaning: This is a declaration of immunity from God. It is a source like nash’at and na’ana’ah. The commentators said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Tabuk, the hypocrites were spreading rumors and the polytheists were breaking the covenants that were between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God, the Almighty, commanded that their covenants be broken, and that is what God, the Almighty, said: And if you fear treachery from a people (al-Anfal 8:58). Al-Zajjaj said: Innocence means: God Almighty and His Messenger have declared themselves innocent of giving them covenants and fulfilling them if they broke them. To those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty. The address is to the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the one who made a treaty with them and concluded a contract with them, because he made a treaty with them and his companions were satisfied with that, so it is as if they made a treaty and concluded a covenant.
9:2: 2- So travel freely in the land, he returned from the report to the address, meaning: Tell them: Travel freely, meaning walk in the land, coming and going, safe and not afraid of any of the Muslims. Four months, and know that you will not cause failure to God, meaning: you will not escape or outpace, and that God will disgrace the disbelievers, meaning: He will humiliate them by killing them in this world and punishing them in the Hereafter. Scholars differed regarding this postponement and regarding those to whom God and His Messenger declared their innocence from the covenants that were between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: A group of people said: This is a reprieve from God Almighty for the polytheists. Whoever’s covenant period is less than four months, He raises it to four months. Whoever’s covenant period is more than four months, He reduces it to four months. Whoever’s covenant period is without a specific term, He limits it to four months. Then after that, he is at war with God and His Messenger, and he is killed wherever he is found and taken prisoner unless he repents. The beginning of this period is the day of the greater Hajj, and its end is until the tenth of the month of Rabi’ al-Akhir. As for the one who does not have a covenant, his term is until the sacred months have passed, which is fifty days. He said: Al-Zuhri: The four months are Shawwal, Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, because this verse was revealed in Shawwal, and the first is more correct and is the view of the majority. Al-Kalbi said: The four months were for those who had a treaty of less than four months, so he completed four months for them. As for those who had a treaty of more than four months, this is an order to complete their treaty by the words of God Almighty: Then fulfill their treaty with them until their term. Al-Hasan said: God Almighty commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight whoever fought him from the polytheists, so He said: Fight in the way of God those who fight you, so he would not fight except those who fought him, then He commanded him to fight the polytheists, and to disavow them, and He gave them a period of four months, so none of them had a period of more than four months, neither the one who had a treaty before the disavowal nor the one who did not have a treaty, so the period for all of them was four months, and the blood of all of them, the people of the treaty and others, was made permissible after the expiration of the period. It was said: This was revealed before Tabuk. Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Mujahid and others said: It was revealed about the people of Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a covenant with the Quraysh in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah that they would stop fighting for ten years during which people would be safe. Khuza’ah entered into the covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Banu Bakr entered into the covenant of the Quraysh. Then Banu Bakr attacked Khuza’ah and took advantage of it, and the Quraysh aided them with weapons. When Banu Bakr and the Quraysh joined forces against Khuza’ah and broke their covenant, Amr ibn Salim Al-Khuza’i came out until he stood before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: No, I am asking Muhammad to swear by our father and his father Al-Atlada So support, may God guide you, and call upon the servants of God to come as support. White as the sun, he rises, but if he is seen, his face becomes pale and cloudy. They attacked us in the middle of the night and killed us while we were kneeling and prostrating. You were our father and we were our children. Then we surrendered and did not withdraw our hands. Among them is the Messenger of God, who has been stripped of his clothes in a group like a foaming sea. The Quraysh broke their promise to you and violated your firm covenant. They claimed that you cannot save anyone, and they are more humiliated and fewer in number. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will not be victorious if I do not support you. He prepared for Mecca in the eighth year of the Hijra. When it was the ninth year, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to perform Hajj, then he said: The polytheists will be present and will circumambulate naked, so he sent Abu Bakr that year as the commander of the season to lead the Hajj for the people, and he sent with him forty verses from the beginning of Bara’ah to read them to the people of the season, then after him he sent Ali, may God honor his face, on his she-camel Al-Adhba’ to read to the people the beginning of Bara’ah, and he ordered him to announce in Mecca, Mina, and Arafat: The covenant of God and the covenant of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been absolved from every polytheist, and no one should circumambulate the House naked. Abu Bakr returned and said: O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, has something been revealed about me? He said: No, but no one should convey this except a man from my family. Are you not satisfied, O Abu Bakr, that you were with me in the cave and that you will be my companion at the Cistern? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, set out as the leader of the Hajj, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, went to announce the declaration of innocence. The day before the Day of Repentance, Abu Bakr addressed the people and told them about their rituals, and he established the Hajj for the people. The Arabs in that year were at their stations in the pre-Islamic period of Hajj, until the Day of Sacrifice came, and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God honor his face, stood up and announced to the people what he had been commanded to do, and he recited to them Surat al-Bara’ah. Zayd ibn Yathi' said: We asked Ali: Why were you sent on that pilgrimage? He said: I was sent with four things: No one shall circumambulate the House naked, and whoever has a treaty with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his term shall be four months, and none shall enter Paradise except a believing soul, and the polytheists and Muslims shall not meet after this year. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the Farewell Pilgrimage in the year ten. If someone says: How did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, send Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, then dismiss him and send Ali, may God be pleased with him? We said: The scholars mentioned that the Messenger of God did not dismiss Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and he was the emir, but rather he sent Ali, may God be pleased with him, to proclaim these verses, and the reason for that was: The Arabs had agreed among themselves in making and breaking covenants, so that no one would undertake that except their master, or a man from his clan, so he sent Ali, may God be pleased with him, to remove the reason, so that they would not say: This is contrary to what we know and is contrary to breaking the covenant. The evidence that Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him was the leader: Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ishaq told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, my nephew Ibn Shihab told us, on the authority of his uncle, Humaid bin Abdul Rahman told me that Abu Hurairah said: Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him sent me on that pilgrimage with two muezzins on the Day of Sacrifice to announce in Mina: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked. Humaid bin Abdul Rahman said: Then the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) sent Ali behind him and ordered him to announce the declaration of innocence. Abu Hurairah said: Ali announced with us to the people of Mina on the Day of Sacrifice: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.
9:3: 3- The Almighty’s saying: And an announcement is in apposition to His saying: innocence meaning: informing. And from this is the call to prayer. It is said: I announced it to him so he announced it, meaning: I informed him. Its origin is from the call to prayer, meaning: I put it in his ear. From God and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage. They differed on the day of the greater pilgrimage: Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is the day of Arafah. This was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn al-Zubayr. This is the opinion of Ata’, Tawus, Mujahid, and Saeed ibn al-Musayyab. A group said: It is the Day of Sacrifice. It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, went out on the Day of Sacrifice on a white mule, heading to the cemetery. A man came to him and took hold of the reins of his mount and asked him about the greatest day of Hajj. He said: This is your day, let it go. This is narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa and Al-Mughirah bin Shuba. It is the opinion of Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i and Sa’id bin Jubayr. And the Sadi. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Mujahid: The greatest day of Hajj is the days of Mina, and Sufyan al-Thawri used to say: The greatest day of Hajj is the days of Mina, such as the day of Siffin, the day of the Camel, and the day of Bu’ath. What is meant by it is the time and place, because these wars lasted for many days. Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal said: The greatest day of Hajj is the day on which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj. This is what Ibn Sirin said, because the Hajj of the Muslims and the Eid of the Jews, Christians and polytheists came together on it, and they did not come together before or after it. They differed about the greater Hajj. Mujahid said: The greater Hajj is the Qiran, and the lesser Hajj is the Hajj ifrad. Al-Zuhri, Al-Sha’bi and Ata’ said: The greater Hajj is the Hajj, and the lesser Hajj is the Umrah. It is called the lesser because of the deficiency in its actions. God Almighty says: God is free from the polytheists and so is His Messenger, meaning: His Messenger is also free from the polytheists. And Jacob read and His Messenger with the accusative of the lam, meaning: that God and His Messenger are innocent. If you repent means: if you return from your disbelief and sincerely believe in monotheism, “then it is better for you. But if you turn away” means: if you turn away from faith, “then know that you cannot cause failure to God. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.”
9:4: 4- Except for those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty, this is an exception to His statement: A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty except for the treaty of those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty, and they are Banu Damrah, a tribe of Kinanah. God the Most High and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded that their treaty be completed until its term, and there were nine months left of their term, and the reason for that was that they did not break the treaty, and this is the meaning of God the Most High's statement: Then they did not fail you in anything of their treaty that you made with them, nor did they aid, nor did they help, against you anyone, of your enemy. Ata' bin Yasar read: They did not fail you with the voiced Ḍād from breaking the treaty, so complete their treaty with them, so fulfill their treaty with them, until their term, until the term that you made with them, Indeed, God loves the righteous.
9:5: 5- The Almighty’s saying, So when the sacred months have passed, has ended and gone, it has been said: they are the four months: Rajab, Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram. Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq said: They are the months of the covenant. Whoever has a covenant, his covenant is four months. Whoever does not have a covenant, his term is until the end of Muharram, fifty days. It was called sacred because God Almighty forbade the believers from shedding the blood of the polytheists and exposing them to harm. If it is said: This amount is some of the sacred months, and God Almighty says: So when the sacred months have passed? It was said: Since this amount was connected to what had passed, it was called the collection, and its meaning is: The specified period has passed with which the sacred months are to end. And the Almighty’s saying: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, in the sacred precincts and outside, and capture them, take them prisoner, and besiege them, meaning: imprison them. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He means that if they fortify themselves, then besiege them, meaning: prevent them from leaving. It was said: Prevent them from entering Mecca and from acting in the lands of Islam. And lie in wait for them at every place of ambush, meaning: on every road. The place of ambush is the place where the enemy is watched. From the root word raṣadat to watch something, meaning: to watch for it. He means: be an ambush for them so that you can catch them from whatever direction they go. It was said: Sit in wait for them on the road to Mecca, so that they do not enter it. If they repent, from polytheism, and establish prayer and give zakat, then let them go on their way, meaning: leave them alone so that they may do their work in their cities and enter Mecca, for God is Forgiving, to those who repent, Merciful to them. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: This verse abrogated every verse in the Qur’an that mentioned turning away and being patient with the harm of enemies.
9:6: 6- The Almighty said: "And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection," meaning: If he seeks your protection from the polytheists whom you have ordered to fight and kill, meaning: He seeks your protection after the sacred months have passed so that he may hear the words of God. "Then grant him protection, so protect him and grant him security, so that he may hear the words of God, regarding what is due to him and against him of reward and punishment, Then escort him to his place of safety," meaning: If he does not submit, escort him to his place of safety, meaning: the place where he is safe is the home of his people, and if he fights you after that and you are able to defeat him, then kill him, "That is because they are a people who do not know," meaning: They do not know the religion of God Almighty and His Oneness, so they are in need of hearing the words of God. Al-Hasan said: This verse is decisive until the Day of Resurrection.
9:7: 7- The Almighty said: How can the polytheists have a treaty with God and with His Messenger? This is in the form of astonishment, and its meaning is denial, meaning: they will not have a treaty with God or with His Messenger, while they betray and break the treaty. Then He made an exception and said, the Almighty and Majestic: Except those with whom you made a treaty at the Sacred Mosque. Ibn Abbas said: They are Quraysh. Qatada said: They are the people of Mecca with whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a covenant on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah. God Almighty said: So as long as they are upright with you, meaning, with the covenant, then be upright with them. But they were not upright, and they broke the covenant, and helped Banu Bakr against Khuza’ah. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set four months for them after the conquest to choose from their affair: either to submit to Islam, or to go to any country they wanted. So they submitted to Islam before the four months. Al-Suddi, Al-Kalbi and Ibn Ishaq said: They are from the tribes of Bakr: Banu Khuzaymah, Banu Mudlij, Banu Damrah and Banu Al-Dayl, and they are the ones who entered into the covenant of Quraysh on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and no one broke the covenant except Quraysh and Banu Al-Dayl from Banu Bakr, so he ordered the covenant to be completed for those who did not break it, and they are Banu Damrah. This statement is closer to being correct, because these verses were revealed after the Quraysh broke the covenant and after the conquest of Mecca. How could he say about something that had already happened: So if they are upright with you, be upright with them? Rather, they are the ones about whom God Almighty said: Except for those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty and then they did not fail you in the least, as the Quraysh failed you, and they did not support anyone against you as the Quraysh supported Banu Bakr against Khuza’ah, the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Indeed, God loves the righteous.
9:8: 8- The Almighty said: How, even if they gain the upper hand over you? This is a response to the first verse, its meaning is: How can they have a covenant with God? How, even if they gain the upper hand over you! They do not observe concerning you any pact of kinship or covenant. Al-Akhfash said: How do you not kill them, even though if they gain the upper hand over you, that is, if they defeat you, they do not observe: they do not respect? Ad-Dahhak said: They do not wait. Qatrib said: They do not observe concerning you any pact. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: Kinship. Yaman said: Womb. Qatada said: The oath is the pledge. Al-Suddi said: It is the covenant. The same applies to the pledge, except that it was repeated because of the difference in the two words. Abu Majlaz and Mujahid said: Al-Il means God Almighty. Ubayd ibn Umair used to read: Jabr Il with emphasis, meaning: Abdullah. In the report, some people from the people of Musaylimah the Liar came to Abu Bakr, so Abu Bakr asked them to read Musaylimah’s letter and they read it. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: This speech did not come from Al-Il, meaning: from God. The evidence for this interpretation is Ikrimah’s reading of they do not observe in a believer except with the letter ya, meaning: God Almighty. Like Gabriel and Michael. And no covenant, that is, no promise. They please you with their mouths, that is, they give you with their tongues something other than what is in their hearts, but their hearts refuse, faith, and most of them are wicked. If it is said: This is about the polytheists, and all of them are immoral, so how did he say: And most of them are immoral? It was said: What he meant by immorality is breaking the covenant. There were some polytheists who fulfilled their covenant, but most of them broke it. That is why he said: And most of them are immoral.
9:9: 9- They sold the verses of God for a small price, that is, they broke the covenant between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by feeding them a meal that Abu Sufyan gave them. Mujahid said: Abu Sufyan fed his allies, so they hindered from his path, preventing people from entering the religion of God. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: That is because the people of Taif provided them with money to strengthen them in fighting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Indeed, evil is what they were doing.
9:10: 10- They do not observe any covenant or pact with regard to a believer, meaning: Do not spare them, O believers, as they would not spare you if they appeared, and those are the transgressors, by breaking the covenant.
9:11: 11- But if they repent from polytheism, and establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers i.e. they are your brothers in religion, they have what you have and are subject to what you are subject to, and We detail the verses and make clear the verses for a people who know, Ibn Abbas said: This verse forbade the blood of the people of the Qiblah. Ibn Masoud said: I ordered them to pray and give zakah, so whoever does not give zakah has no prayer. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ told us, Shuaib bin Abi Hamza told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Masoud told us that Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, succeeded him, and some of the Arabs disbelieved, Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said to Abu Bakr: How can you fight people when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ Whoever says, ‘There is no god but God,’ his wealth and his life are protected from me, except for what is due, and his reckoning is with God?” Abu Bakr said: By God, I will fight whoever differentiates between prayer and zakat, for zakat is a right due from wealth. By God, if they withheld from me a young camel that they used to pay to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I would fight them for withholding it. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: By God, it was only after Abu Bakr’s heart was opened to fighting that I knew it was the truth. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Amr bin Abbas told us, Ibn Al-Mahdi told us, Mansour bin Saad told us, on the authority of Maimun bin Siyah, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever prays as we pray, faces our qiblah, and eats our slaughtered animal, he is a Muslim who has the protection of God and the protection of His Messenger.
9:12: 12- The Almighty said: And if they break their oaths, they break their covenants, after their covenant, their contract, meaning: the polytheists of Quraysh, and attack, they cast aspersions at your religion they criticize it. This is evidence that if a dhimmi attacks the religion of Islam outwardly, his covenant will not remain valid, Then fight the leaders of disbelief, the people of Kufa and Ash-Sham read: leaders with two hamzas wherever it was, and the rest read it with a softening of the second hamza. And the leaders of disbelief: the heads of the polytheists and their leaders from the people of Mecca. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and all the leaders of Quraysh at that time who broke the covenant, and they were the ones who intended to expel the Messenger. Mujahid said: They are the people of Persia and Rome. Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said: The people of this verse were not fought and its people did not come after they have no oaths, meaning: they have no covenants: plural of oath: Qatrib said: they do not fulfill the covenant. Ibn Amir read: they have no oaths with a kasra on the alif, meaning: they have no belief and no religion. It was said: it is from security, meaning: do not trust them and kill them wherever you find them, perhaps they will desist, meaning: so that they will desist from attacking your religion and supporting you. It was said: from disbelief, then he urged the Muslims to fight.
9:13: 13-Then He, the Most High, said: Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths? They broke their covenants, and they are the ones who broke the peace treaty at Hudaybiyyah and helped Banu Bakr fight Khuza’ah. And they intended to expel the Messenger from Mecca when they gathered in Dar al-Nadwa, and they initiated the fighting against you “the first time,” meaning: on the day of Badr, and that is because they said when the caravan surrendered: We will not leave until we eradicate Muhammad and his companions. A group of commentators said: He meant that they began fighting Khuza’ah, the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace. Do you fear them? Do you fear them so that you stop fighting them? But God has more right that you should fear Him, in stopping fighting them, if you are believers.
9:14: 14- Fight them; God will punish them by your hands, God will kill them by your hands, and will disgrace them, and humiliate them by captivity and subjugation, and give you victory over them and heal the hearts of a people, and will heal the disease in the hearts of a people, believing, from the harm they had suffered from them. Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: He meant the hearts of Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Quraysh helped Banu Bakr against them, until they caused them pain, so God healed their hearts from Banu Bakr through the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers.
9:15: 15- And He removes the anger of their hearts, their distress and their finding with the help of the Quraysh early on against them, then he said, resuming: And God accepts the repentance of whomever He wills, so He guides him to Islam as He did with Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Suhayl ibn Amr, and God is Knowing and Wise. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: Raise the sword except for Khuza'ah from Banu Bakr until the afternoon.
9:16: 16- The Almighty said: Or did you think, did you think that you would be left alone, it was said: This is addressed to the hypocrites. And it was said: To the believers for whom fighting is difficult. So He said: Or did you think that you would be left alone and not commanded to fight, nor tested, to make clear the truthful from the liar, and God has not yet known, and God has not seen those of you who strive and have not taken besides God or His Messenger or the believers an intimate friend, confidants and allies who support them and divulge their secrets to them. Qatada said: A confidant is treachery. Ad-Dahhak said: Deception. Ata' said: Friends. Abu Ubaidah said: Everything that you introduce into something that is not part of it is a confidant, and a man is among the people but is not one of them. A man's confidant is someone who is exclusive to his innermost affairs without the people. It is said: He is my confidant, and they are my confidant, for the singular and the plural. And God is Acquainted with what you do.
9:17: 17- The Almighty said: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God the verse. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: When Al-Abbas was taken prisoner on the day of Badr, the Muslims taunted him with disbelief and severing family ties, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, spoke harshly to him. Al-Abbas said: Why do you mention our faults and not our good qualities? Ali, may God be pleased with him, said to him: Do you have any good qualities? He said: Yes, we maintain the Sacred Mosque, we cover the Kaaba, and we provide water for the pilgrims. Then God Almighty revealed in response to Abbas: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God, meaning: It is not appropriate for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God. It is obligatory for Muslims to prevent them from doing so, because mosques are only built for the worshippers of God alone, so whoever is a disbeliever in God is not supposed to build them. A group of people said that what is meant by it is: the well-known building of mosques/ and its repair when they are in ruins, so the disbeliever is prevented from it, even if he recommends it, it is not complied with. Some of them interpreted the building here as entering the mosque and sitting in it. Al-Hasan said: It was not appropriate for the polytheists to be left alone and become the people of the Sacred Mosque. Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read: Mosques of God in the singular form, and he meant the Sacred Mosque, because God the Almighty said: And the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque, and because God the Almighty said: So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque. The others read: Mosques of God in the plural form, and he also meant the Sacred Mosque. Al-Hasan said: He only said Mosques because it is the qiblah of all mosques. Al-Farra’ said: Perhaps the Arabs used the singular to mean the plural and the plural to mean the singular. Don’t you see that a man rides a mule and says: I have taken up riding mules? And it is said: So-and-so has many dirhams and dinars, meaning dirhams and dinars? God Almighty says: Bearing witness against themselves of disbelief. He meant: And they are witnesses. So when and they was omitted, it was made accusative. Al-Hasan said: They did not say we are disbelievers, but their speech of disbelief bears witness against them of disbelief. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Their testimony against themselves of disbelief was their prostration to idols. This was because the infidels of Quraysh had set up their idols outside the Sacred House at the bases, and they would circumambulate the House naked. Every time they circumambulated a circuit, they would prostrate to their idols, and they only increased their distance from God Almighty by doing so. Al-Suddi said: Their testimony against themselves of disbelief is that the Christian is asked, Who are you? and he says, I am a Christian. The Jew says, I am a Jew. The polytheist is asked, What is your religion? and he says, Polytheist. God Almighty said: Their deeds have become worthless, because they are not for God Almighty, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Its meaning is that they bear witness against their Messenger’s disbelief, because there is no woman in the womb who did not give birth to him.
9:18: 18-Then the Almighty said: The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day and establish prayer and give zakah and do not fear except God and did not fear anyone other than God in religion, and did not abandon God’s command out of fear of anyone other than Him, It is possible that those will be among the [rightly] guided, and It is possible from God is obligatory, meaning: Those are the ones who are guided, and the guided are those who adhere to the obedience of God the Almighty, which leads to Paradise. Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Nasawi told us, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Hayri told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub told us, Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Hijazi told us, Baqiyah told us, Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mahdi told us, on the authority of Amr ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If you see a man visiting a mosque, then bear witness to his faith, for God Almighty said: ‘The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day.’” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Muhammad bin Mutraf told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning or evening, God will prepare for him a place in Paradise every time he goes in the morning or evening. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Ja’far, my father told me, on the authority of Mahmoud bin Labid, that Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, wanted to build a mosque, but the people disliked that and wanted him to leave it. So Uthman said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever builds a mosque for God, God will build for him a similar structure in Paradise. And Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn bin Muhammad al-Qadi told us, I told Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi, Muhammad bin al-Husayn al-Qattan told us, Ali bin al-Husayn al-Darbajirdi told us, Abu Asim told us with this chain of transmission, and he said: God built him a house in Paradise.
9:19: 19- The Almighty said: Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims the verse. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid bin Muhammad Al-Wazzan told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Ubaidullah Al-Ma’afari told us, Abu Dawud Sulayman bin Al-Ash’ath Al-Sijistani told us, Abu Tawbah Al-Rabi’ bin Nafi’ Al-Halabi told us, Mu’awiyah bin Salam told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Salam, on the authority of Abu Salam, Al-Nu’man bin Bashir told us: I was at the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a man said: I do not care if I do not do any work after I provide water for the pilgrims. The other said: I do not care if I do not do any work after I renovate the Sacred Mosque. The other said: Jihad in the way of God is better than what you have said. So Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, rebuked them and said: Do not raise your voices at the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as it is Friday. But when you have prayed, go in and ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about what you disagreed about. So he did so, and God, the Almighty, revealed: Have you made the provision of water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque? until His saying: And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Al-Abbas said when he was taken prisoner on the day of Badr: If you had preceded us in Islam, migration, and jihad, we would have been building the Sacred Mosque and providing water to the pilgrims. Then God Almighty revealed this verse, and informed us that their building the Sacred Mosque and their providing water would not benefit them if they were associating partners with God, and that faith in God and jihad with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were better than what they were doing. Al-Hasan, Al-Sha’bi, and Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi said: It was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib, Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, and Talha bin Shaiba. They boasted, so Talha said: I am the owner of the House, and I have the key to it. Al-Abbas said: I am the owner of the water-giving and the one who takes care of it. Ali said: I do not know what you are saying. I prayed towards the Qiblah for six months before the people, and I am the owner of jihad. Then God Almighty revealed this verse: Have you made the watering of the pilgrims? Watering: a source like care and protection. His saying: And the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque is like the one who believes in God and the Last Day, is an abbreviation, meaning: Do you consider providing water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque to be like the faith of the one who believes in God and the jihad of the one who strives in the way of God? It was said: The watering and the maintenance mean the one who provides water and the one who maintains it. Its meaning is: Have you considered the one who provides water to the pilgrims and the one who maintains the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the cause of God? This is like the Almighty’s saying: And the [best] outcome is for righteousness, meaning: for the righteous. This is indicated by the reading of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr and Ubayy bin Ka’b: Have you considered the one who provides water to the pilgrims and the one who maintains the Sacred Mosque on the plural of the one who provides water to the pilgrims and the one who maintains it. “Like one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the cause of God, they are not equal in the sight of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Abu Usamah told us, Yahya bin Muhallab told us, on the authority of Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the watering place and asked for water. Al-Abbas said: O Fadl, go to your mother and bring the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a drink from her. He said: Give me a drink. He said: O Messenger of God, they are putting their hands in it. He said: Give me a drink. So he drank from it. Then he came to Zamzam while they were watering and working in it. He said: Work, for you are doing righteous work. Then he said: Were it not that you would be overcome, I would have come down until I put the rope on this,” and he pointed to his shoulder. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj, Muhammad bin Munhal Al-Dareer told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Hamid Al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah Al-Muzani, who said: “I was sitting with Ibn Abbas near the Kaaba when a Bedouin came to him and said: Why do I not see your cousins giving you honey and milk while you give you wine? Is it because you have a need or because you are stingy? Ibn Abbas said: Praise be to God, we have no need or stinginess. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came on his mount and Usama was behind him. He asked for water, so we brought him a vessel of wine and he drank and gave Usama the rest to drink, and he said: You have done well and made it beautiful, so do so, for we do not want to change what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has commanded.”
9:20: 20- The Almighty said: Those who believed and emigrated and fought in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives are greater in degree in virtue, with God, than those who boasted about providing water to the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque. And those are the successful, the ones saved from the Fire.
9:21: 21- Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and approval and gardens for them wherein is lasting pleasure.
9:22: 22- "They will abide therein forever. Indeed, God has with Him a great reward."
9:23: 23- O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies. Mujahid said: This verse is connected to the one before it. It was revealed in the story of Al-Abbas and Talha and their refusal to emigrate. Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by the migration to Medina, some of them had their families and children clinging to him, saying: We implore you by God not to neglect us. So he took pity on them and stayed with them and abandoned the migration, so God Almighty revealed this verse. Muqatil said: It was revealed about the nine who apostatized from Islam and went to Mecca, so God forbade them from being allies, so God revealed: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies, confidants and friends, so that you divulge your secrets to them and prefer staying with them over emigration, if they prefer, they choose “disbelief over faith. And whoever among you takes them as allies,” so that he exposes to them the weaknesses of the Muslims and prefers staying with them over emigration and jihad, then those are the wrongdoers. At that time, no one would take a break from faith except a emigrant, so this is the meaning of His statement: then those are the wrongdoers.
9:24: 24- Then the Almighty said: Say O Muhammad to those who stayed behind in emigrating: If your fathers, that is because when the first verse was revealed, those who converted to Islam but did not emigrate said: If we emigrate, our wealth will be lost, our trade will be gone, our homes will be destroyed, and our kinship ties will be severed. So the following was revealed: "Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your kindred", Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim: your kindred with the alif for the plural, and the others without the alif for the singular, because the plural of the kindred is kindred: and wealth you have acquired you have earned it and commerce in which you fear decline and dwellings that please you, that is: you find pleasant, meaning palaces and homes, are dearer to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His cause, so wait, so wait, until God brings about His command, Ata' said: His judgment. Mujahid and Muqatil said: By the conquest of Mecca, this is a threatening matter. And God does not guide, does not grant success or direct the wicked people, those who disobey.
9:25: 25- The Almighty said: God has certainly given you victory in many battlefields, meaning scenes, and on the day of Hunayn, and Hunayn is a valley between Mecca and Taif. And Urwah said: next to Dhu al-Majaz. The story of Hunayn, as reported by the narrators, was that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca and there were still days left of the month of Ramadan. Then he went out to Hunayn to fight Hawazin and Thaqif with twelve thousand, ten thousand of the emigrants and two thousand of the freed slaves. Ata’ said that they were sixteen thousand. Al-Kalbi said: They were ten thousand, and they were the largest they had ever been on that day, and the polytheists were four thousand from Hawazin and Thaqif, and Malik ibn Auf al-Nasri was in charge of Hawazin, and Kinanah ibn Abd Yalil al-Thaqafi was in charge of Thaqif. When the two armies met, a man from the Ansar called Salamah ibn Salamah ibn Waqash said: We will not be defeated today despite our small number. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was displeased with his words, and they left the man’s word to him. In another narration: God was not pleased with his words, and left them to themselves, so they fought a fierce battle, and the polytheists were defeated and left their children behind. Then they called out: O protectors of the black land, mention the scandals. So they retreated and the Muslims were exposed. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the freed slaves fled with the people that day, and when the people fled, they fled. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Aziz told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Yahya bin Yahya told us, Abu Khathima told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq who said: A man said to Al-Bara bin Azib: O Abu Ammarah, did you flee on the day of Hunayn?
