He said: No, by God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not turn away, but the young men of his companions and their secret ones went out, and they were bareheaded and had no weapons, or many weapons, and they met a people of archers who hardly missed an arrow, a group of Hawazin and Banu Nasr, and they shot them with shots that hardly missed, so they came there to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his white mule, and Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib was leading him, so he got down and sought help and said: I am the Prophet, no lie, I am the son of Abdul Muttalib, then he lined them up. It was narrated by Muhammad bin Ismail on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Musa on the authority of Israel on the authority of Abu Ishaq. He added: No one was seen among the people on that day more severe than him. Zakariya narrated it on the authority of Abu Ishaq. Al-Bara’ added: When the battle became fierce, we would protect ourselves with it, and the bravest of us was the one who would stand alongside it - meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Shu`bah narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq who said: Al-Bara’ said: Hawazin were a people of archers, and when we met them we attacked them, but they were defeated. The Muslims turned to the spoils and met us with arrows, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not flee. Al-Kalbi said: There were three hundred Muslims around the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the rest of the people fled. Others said: No one remained with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that day except: Al-Abbas bin Al-Muttalib, Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith, and Ayman bin Umm Ayman, and he was killed that day in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us/ Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, he said: Abu Tahir, Ahmad bin Amr bin Sarh told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus told us on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: Kathir bin Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib told me, he said: Abbas said: “I witnessed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn, and Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith and I stuck with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we did not leave him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on a white mule of his that Furwah bin Nafatha Al-Judhami had given him as a gift, and when the Muslims and the infidels met, the Muslims turned and fled, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to gallop his mule ahead of the infidels, and I was holding the reins of the Messenger of God’s mule, holding it back, wanting it not to go fast, and Abu Sufyan was holding his stirrup, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, O Abbas: Call the companions of the samura, so Abbas said - and he was a man I said at the top of my voice: Where are the people of the samura? He said: By God, when they heard my voice, their turning was like the turning of a cow to its young. They said: At your service, at your service. He said: So they fought, and the infidels, and the call was among the Ansar, saying: O group of Ansar, O group of Ansar. Then the call was limited to Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked while he was on his mule, as if he was reaching out to them, at their fight, and he said: This is when the battle is fierce. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took pebbles and threw them in the faces of the infidels, then he said: They are defeated, by the Lord of Muhammad. I went to look, and the fighting was as I had seen it. He said: By God, he had only thrown his pebbles at them, and I could still see their edge weakened and their matter in retreat. Salamah ibn al-Akwa’ said: “We fought with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Hunayn. He said: When they attacked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he got off the mule, then took a handful of dirt from the ground, then faced them in the face and said: ‘May your faces be disfigured! God did not create a single human being among them without filling his eyes with dirt with that handful.’ So they turned and fled, and God Almighty defeated them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided their spoils among the Muslims.” Saeed bin Jubair said: God Almighty supported his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with five thousand marked angels. In al-Naba 78:A man from the tribe of Nadr, called Shajarah, said to the believers after the battle: Where are the piebald horses and the men wearing white clothes? We did not see you among them except as a mole, and we were killed only by their hands. So they informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, and he said: Those are the angels. Al-Zuhri said: It was reported to me that Shaibah bin Uthman bin Talhah said: I turned my back on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn, and I wanted to kill him with Talhah bin Uthman and Uthman bin Talhah, who had been killed on the day of Uhud. Then God informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what was in my soul, so he turned to me and struck my chest and said: I seek refuge in God for you, O Shaibah. My limbs trembled, and I looked at him, and he was dearer to me than my hearing and sight, so I said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God, and that God has informed you of what is in my soul. When God defeated the polytheists and they turned back, they set out until they reached Awtas, where their families and wealth were. The Messenger of God sent a man from the Ash'ariyyin called Abu Amir and put him in charge of the Muslim army to Awtas. He marched towards them and they fought. Durayd ibn al-Summah was killed, the polytheists were defeated and the Muslims took their families as captives. Their leader, Malik ibn Auf al-Nasri, fled and came to Taif, fortified himself there and took his wealth and family among those he took. The leader of the Muslims, Abu Amir, was killed. Al-Zuhri said: Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab informed me that they captured six thousand captives that day. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Taif and besieged them for the rest of that month. When Dhu al-Qi`dah entered, which was a sacred month, he turned away from them and went to al-Jirana, where he entered ihram for Umrah and divided the spoils of Hunayn and Awtas there. He brought together some people, including Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, and al-Aqra` ibn Habis, and gave them some. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, Al-Zuhri told us, Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, told me that some of the Ansar said to the Messenger of God - when he gave his Messenger some of the wealth of Hawazin, and he began to give men from Quraysh a hundred camels - they said: May God forgive the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for giving to Quraysh and leaving us while our swords are dripping with their blood? Anas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed of what they said, so he sent for the Ansar, gathered them in a leather tent and did not leave anyone with them except them. When they had gathered, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them and said: What was the talk that I heard about you? Their jurists said to him: As for those of good opinion, O Messenger of God, they did not say anything, but as for some of us who are young in age, they said: May God forgive the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for giving to Quraysh and leaving the Ansar. And our swords were dripping with their blood. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I give to men who have recently converted from disbelief. Are you not satisfied that people take their wealth and you return to your homes with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? By God, what you are returning with is better than what they are returning with. They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, we are satisfied. He said to them: You will see great preference after me, so be patient until you meet God and His Messenger at the Cistern. Yunus said on the authority of Ibn Shihab: I give to men who have recently converted to disbelief, so that I may win them over. He said: So be patient until you meet God and His Messenger, for I am at the Pool. They said: We will be patient. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Wahib told us, Amr bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Tamim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Zaid, on the authority of Asim, who said: “When God bestowed spoils of war on His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hunayn, he divided them among the people among those whose hearts were to be reconciled, and did not give the Ansar anything. It was as if they had found that what the people had suffered had not befallen them. So he addressed them and said: O group of Ansar, did I not find you astray and God guided you through me? And you were divided and God united you through me. And you were poor and God enriched you through me? Whenever he said something, they said: God and His Messenger are believers. He said: What prevents you from responding to the Messenger of God? Whenever he said something, they said: God and His Messenger are believers? He said: If you wished, you could say such and such. Would you be pleased for the people to go with the sheep and the camel, and you go with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to your homes? Had it not been for the migration, I would have been a man from the Ansar. If the people took a valley or a gorge, I would take a valley.” The Ansar and their people, the Ansar, a slogan and the people a cover, you will encounter discrimination after me, so be patient until you meet me at the pond. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin / Abi Omar Al-Makki told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Omar bin Saeed bin Masruq on the authority of his father on the authority of Ubayya bin Rafa’a on the authority of Rafi bin Khadij, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave Abu Sufyan bin Harb, Sufyan bin Umayya, Uyaynah bin Hisn, and Al-Aqra’ bin Habis, each of them one hundred camels, and he gave Abbas bin Mirdas less than that. Abbas bin Mirdas said: There was no fortress or prison that surpassed Mardas in the complex. Do you make my loot and the loot of the players crawl like a bald-headed camel? I was not lower than either of them, and whoever is lowered today will not be raised. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, completed one hundred for him. In the hadith, some people from Hawazin converted to Islam after that, and said: O Messenger of God, you are the best of people and the most pious of people, and you have taken our children, women, and money. Abdul Wahid bin Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saeed bin Ufair told us, Al-Layth told me, Aqeel told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr: that Marwan and Al-Miswar bin Makhrama told him that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up when the delegation of Hawazin came to him as Muslims, and they asked him to return their money and captives to them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I have with me those you see, and the most beloved speech to me is the most truthful. So they chose one of the two groups: either the captives or the money. They said: We will choose our captives. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and praised God Almighty as He deserves, then he said: As for what follows, your brothers have come repentant, and I have decided to return their captives to them. Whoever among you would like to make that permissible for them, let him do so, and whoever would like to have a share until we give it to him from the first of what God bestows upon us, let him do so. The people said: We have made that permissible, O Messenger of God.” God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We do not know who among you has given permission for this and who has not, so go back until your leaders report your matter to us. So the people went back, and their leaders spoke to them, then they went back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him that they had given their consent and given permission. So God, the Most High, revealed in the story of Hunayn: God has already given you victory in many battles, and on the day of Hunayn, when your great numbers pleased you, until you said: We will not be defeated today because of our small numbers, “but it did not avail you at all,” meaning that victory does not come from numbers, and the earth became strait for you, despite its vastness, meaning despite its vastness and breadth, then you turned back in flight, defeated.
9:26: 26- Then God sent down after the defeat, His tranquility, meaning: security and reassurance, which is an active participle from tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and He sent down soldiers you did not see, meaning: the angels. It was said: not for fighting, but to support the disbelievers and encourage the Muslims, because it is narrated: that the angels did not fight except on the day of Badr, and He punished those who disbelieved, by killing, capturing, taking their families captive, and stealing their money, and that is the reward of the disbelievers.
9:27: 27- Then after that God wills to forgive whomever He wills, and guides him to Islam, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.
35:10: 28- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, indeed, the polytheists are unclean the verse, Ad-Dahhak and Abu Ubaidah said: Najis: dirty. It was also said: filthy. It is a source that is the same for males and females, duals and plurals. As for Najis: with a kasra on the noon and a sukoon on the jim, it is not said in the singular, rather it is said: Rajis Najis, so if it is singular it is said: Najis, with a fatha on the noon and a kasra on the jim, and what is meant by it is: impurity of the ruling, not impurity of the substance. They were called Najis as a form of blame. Qatada said: He called them Najis because they are ritually impure and do not bathe, and they have a wet dream and do not perform ablution. God Almighty said: So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque. He meant to prevent them from entering the Sanctuary because if they entered the Sanctuary they would have approached the Sacred Mosque. He meant the Sanctuary, and this is like what God Almighty said: Glory be to Him who took His Servant by night from the Sacred Mosque (al-Isra’ 17:1). He meant the Sanctuary because he took him by night from the house of Umm Hani’. The great Sheikh Imam said: The totality of the lands of Islam with regard to the infidels is divided into three categories: One of them: The Sacred Sanctuary. It is not permissible for an infidel to enter it under any circumstances, whether he is a dhimmi or a person granted protection, due to the apparent meaning of this verse. If a messenger from the land of the infidels comes to the Imam while the Imam is in the Sacred Sanctuary, he is not permitted to enter the Sacred Sanctuary. Rather, he sends someone to hear his message outside the Sacred Sanctuary. The people of Kufa permitted those with a covenant to enter the Sacred Sanctuary. The second part of the Levant: Al-Hijaz, it is permissible for the infidel to enter it with permission, but he may not stay there for more than the duration of a journey, which is three days, based on what was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If I live, God willing, I will expel the Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula until I will not leave anyone in it except Muslims. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went and made a will, saying: Expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, did not have time for that, and Omar, may God be pleased with him, expelled them during his caliphate, and he gave a three-day grace period to anyone who came from them as a trader. The Arabian Peninsula extends from the furthest part of Aden Abyan to the countryside of Iraq in length, and as for width, it extends from Jeddah and its surroundings from the sea coast to the outskirts of the Levant. The third section: All other Islamic countries, in which it is permissible for an infidel to reside with protection and security, but they may not enter mosques except with the permission of a Muslim. His saying: After this year of theirs, meaning: the year in which Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, performed Hajj with the people, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, proclaimed the declaration of innocence, which was the year nine of the Hijra. His saying: And if you fear poverty, that is because the people of Mecca made their living from trade and the polytheists used to come to Mecca with food and trade, so when they were prevented from entering the Sacred Sanctuary they feared poverty and hardship, and they mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: And if you fear poverty, so he read it as poverty. It is said: Aal means to be supported. “Then God will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed, God is Knowing and Wise.” Ikrimah said: So God enriched them by sending down abundant rain upon them, so their wealth increased. Muqatil said: The people of Jeddah, Sana’a, and Jarish from Yemen converted to Islam and brought abundant provisions to Mecca, so God spared them what they feared. Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: God compensated them for it with the jizya and enriched them with it. God Almighty said: 10- Whoever desires honor, then to God belongs all honor. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of the verse is: Whoever desires to know to whom belongs honor, then to God belongs all honor. Qatada said: Whoever wants honor, let him seek honor through obedience to God. This means calling for obedience to the One who has honor, that is, let him seek honor from God through obedience to Him, just as it is said: Whoever wants money, then the money belongs to so-and-so, that is, let him seek it from him. This is because the disbelievers worshipped idols and sought honor through them, as God said: “And they have taken other gods besides God that they might be for them a source of honor. No!” Maryam 19:81. He also said: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers - do they seek honor with them? But indeed, honor belongs entirely to God. An-Nisa 139. To Him, that is, to God, ascends the good word, which is his saying, There is no god but God. It was also said that it is the man’s saying, Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Al-Hajjaj bin Nasr told us, Al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mahariq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: If I narrate to you a hadith, I will inform you of its verification from the Book of God, the Almighty and Majestic: There is no Muslim slave who says five words: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is Great, and blessed be God, except that an angel takes them and places them under his wing, then ascends with them, and they do not pass by a group of angels except that they ask forgiveness for the one who says them until the face of the Lord of the Worlds is revived by them. Its verification from the Book of God, the Almighty and Majestic, is His statement: To Him ascends the good words, Ibn Mas’ud mentioned it. It was said: The good word is the remembrance of God. And on the authority of Qatada: To Him ascend the good word, meaning: God accepts the good word. The Almighty said: And righteous deeds raise it up, meaning: righteous deeds raise up good words. The ha in His statement raises it up refers back to good words, and this is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and most of the commentators. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: Good speech is the remembrance of God and righteous action is the performance of His obligations. So whoever remembers God but does not perform His obligations, his speech will be rejected based on his actions. Faith is not by wishful thinking or by adornment, but rather by what is established in the heart and confirmed by actions. So whoever says something good but does something bad, God will reject his words. And whoever says something good and does something good, God will raise him up with his actions, because God says: To Him ascends good speech, and righteous action raises it up. And it is stated in the hadith: God does not accept a word without action, and no word or action without intention. Some people said: The ha’ in his statement raises it refers to the righteous deed, meaning: the good word raises the righteous deed, so no deed is accepted unless it is issued from monotheism, and this is the meaning of the statement of Al-Kalbi and Muqatil. It was said: Elevation is an attribute of God Almighty/ its meaning is: God Almighty elevates the righteous deed. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Righteous action is that which is pure, meaning that sincerity is the reason for acceptance of good deeds and words. His evidence is the saying of God the Almighty: So let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone. (al-Kahf 18:110). He made the opposite of righteousness polytheism and hypocrisy. And those who plot evil deeds, Al-Kalbi said: meaning those who do evil deeds. Muqatil said: meaning polytheism. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: meaning those who plotted against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the house of prophethood, as God the Almighty said: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you (al-Anfal 8:30). Mujahid said: Shahr bin Hawshab, they are the people of hypocrisy. They will have a severe punishment, and their plotting will be ruined. It will be nullified and destroyed in the Hereafter.
9:29: 29-And that is: the Almighty’s saying: Fight those who do not believe in God. Mujahid said: This verse was revealed when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the fighting of the Romans, so he went on a campaign after its revelation in the Battle of Tabuk. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about the Qurayza and Nadir Jews, so he made peace with them. It was the first jizya imposed on the people of Islam, and the first humiliation that befell the People of the Book at the hands of the Muslims. God the Almighty said: Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day. If it is said: Do the People of the Scripture believe in God and the Last Day? It is said: They do not believe as the believers do, for if they say Aziz is the son of God and the Messiah is the son of God, that is not belief in God. And they do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, nor do they adopt the religion of truth, meaning: they do not adopt the religion of truth, adding the name to the description. Qatada said: The truth is God, meaning: they do not adopt the religion of God, and His religion is Islam. Abu Ubaidah said: Its meaning is that they do not obey God the Almighty as the people of truth do. Of those who were given the Scripture, meaning: the Jews and Christians. Until they pay the jizyah, which is the tax imposed on their necks, by hand, by force and humiliation. Abu Ubaidah said: It is said of anyone who gives something unwillingly and against his will: he gave it by hand. Ibn Abbas said: They give it by hand and do not send it by the hand of anyone else. It was said: by hand, meaning: in cash, not on credit. It was said: It is an acknowledgement of the Muslims’ favor upon them by accepting the jizya from them, while they are humbled, humiliated and subjugated. Ikrimah said: They pay the jizya while standing, and the one who receives it is sitting. And Ibn Abbas said: It is taken from him and his neck is trampled on. Al-Kalbi said: If he gives, he is slapped on the back of the neck. It was said: He is taken by his beard and hit on his two sides. It was said: He is pulled and dragged violently to the place of giving. It was said: Giving it to him is the young ones. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: Children are the ones who are subject to the rulings of Islam. The nation agreed on the permissibility of taking the jizya from the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians, if they are not Arabs. They differed regarding the Arab People of the Book and the non-People of the Book from the non-Arab infidels. Al-Shafi’i held that the jizya is based on religions, not lineages. It is taken from the People of the Book, whether they are Arabs or non-Arabs, and it is not taken from the people of idols under any circumstances. He argued that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from Ukaydir Dumah, a man from the Arabs who is said to be from Ghassan, and he took it from the People of the Covenant of Yemen, most of whom are Arabs. Malik and Al-Awza’i said: It is taken from all infidels except the apostate. Abu Hanifa said: It is taken from the People of the Book in general, and it is taken from the non-Arab polytheists, but it is not taken from the Arab polytheists. Abu Yusuf said: It is not taken from the Arab, whether he is a People of the Book or a polytheist, but it is taken from the non-Arab, whether he is a People of the Book or a polytheist. As for the Magians: the Companions, may God be pleased with them, agreed to take the jizya from them. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad al-Khalal told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, al-Rabi’ told us, al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar who heard Bajalah say: Umar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, did not take the jizya from the Magians until Abd al-Rahman bin Awf witnessed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from the Magians of Hajar. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Musab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, “that `Umar ibn al-Khattab mentioned the Magians and said: I do not know what to do with them. `Abd al-Rahman ibn `Awf said: I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Treat them as you treat the People of the Book.” In the refusal of Omar, may God be pleased with him, to take the jizya from the Magians until Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf witnessed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from the Magians of Hajar, this is evidence that the opinion of the Companions was that it should not be taken from every polytheist, but rather it should be taken from the People of the Book. They differed as to whether the Magi were among the People of the Book or not. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: They had a book that they were studying, and in the morning they saw their book being carried on a night journey, and it was taken from among them. They agreed to prohibit the sacrifices of the Magi and their marriage, unlike the People of the Book. As for those who entered the religion of the Jews and Christians from among the polytheists, the following is considered: If they entered it before the abrogation and change, they acknowledge the jizyah, and their marriages and sacrifices are permissible. If they entered their religion after the abrogation with the coming of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they do not acknowledge the jizyah, and their marriages and sacrifices are not permissible. And those about whom we doubt that they entered it after the abrogation or before it: they acknowledge the jizyah, to protect the blood, and their marriages and sacrifices are not permissible, to protect the prohibition. Among them are the Christians of the Arabs from Tanukh and Hira Banu Taghlib. Umar, may God be pleased with him, acknowledged them to pay the jizyah, and said: Their sacrifices are not permissible for us. As for the amount of the jizyah: its minimum is a dinar, and it is not permissible to reduce it. The dinar is accepted from the poor, the rich, and the middle class, as Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi informed us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi informed us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi informed us, Mahmoud bin Ghailan informed us, Abdul-Razzaq informed us, Sufyan informed us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to Yemen and ordered him to take from every adult a dinar or its equivalent in Ma’afir. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to take from every adult, that is, an adult, a dinar or he did not differentiate between the rich, the poor, and the middle class. This is evidence that it is not obligatory on children, and likewise it is not obligatory on women. Rather, it is taken from free, sane, adult men. Some people said that every wealthy person should pay four dinars, every middle-class person should pay two dinars, and every poor person should pay one dinar, which is the opinion of the people of opinion.
9:30: 30- The Almighty said: The Jews say, ‘Ezra is the son of God,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Messiah is the son of God.’ Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Salam bin Mishkam, Al-Nu’man bin Awfa, Shas bin Qais, and Malik bin Al-Saif. They said: How can we follow you when you have abandoned our Qiblah and you do not claim that Ezra is the son of God? Then God Almighty revealed: The Jews say, ‘Ezra is the son of God.’ Asim, Al-Kisa’i and Ya’qub read Uzair with tanween, and the others without tanween, because it is a foreign name and resembles a diminutive noun. As for the nun, he said: Because it is a light name, so its direction is to decline it, even if it is foreign like Noah, Hud and Lot. Abu Ubaidah chose the tanween and said: Because this is not attributed to his father, but rather it is like saying Zaid the son of the prince and Zaid the son of our sister, so Aziz is the subject and what comes after it is the predicate for it. Ubaid bin Umair said: This statement was said by one Jewish man named Phinehas bin Azura, and he is the one who said: God is poor and we are rich Al Imran - 181. Atiyyah Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Jews said that Ezra was the son of God because Ezra was among them, and they had the Torah and the Ark, but they forgot the Torah and acted unjustly. So God lifted the Ark from them, made them forget the Torah, and abrogated it from their hearts. So Ezra called upon God and implored Him to return to him what had been abrogated from their hearts. While he was praying, imploring God Almighty, a light descended from the sky and entered his body, and the Torah was returned to him. He called out to his people and said: O my people, God has given me the Torah and returned it to me! So the people clung to him and taught them. They remained as long as God Almighty willed. Then the Ark descended after it had gone from them. When they saw the Ark, they showed what was in it to the one who taught them Ezra, and they found it to be the same. They said: This Ezra was not given except that he is the son of God. The Christians said: The Messiah is the son of God. The reason for that was that they were Muslims for eighty-one years after Jesus, peace be upon him, was raised up. They prayed towards the Qiblah and fasted Ramadan, until a war broke out between them and the Jews. There was a brave man among the Jews called Paul who killed a group of the companions of Jesus, peace be upon him. Then he said to the Jews: If the truth is with Jesus, then we have disbelieved in him and Hell is our destination. We are deceived. If they enter Paradise, we will enter Hell. I will scheme and lead them astray until they enter Hell. He had a horse called Al-Aqab on which he fought. He hamstrung his horse and showed remorse, and put dirt on its head. The Christians said to him: Who are you? He said: Paul is your enemy. Then I was called from heaven: You have no repentance unless you are victorious, and that was proven. They brought him into the church, and he entered a house for a year, not leaving it day or night until he learned the Gospel. Then he came out and said: I was called that God has accepted your repentance, so they believed him and loved him. Then he went to Jerusalem, and made Nestorius swear an oath to them and taught him that Jesus, Mary, and God were three. Then he went to the Romans and taught them divinity and humanity, and said: Jesus was neither human nor body, but the son of God. He taught that to a man called Jacob. Then he called a man called Malka, and said: God has always existed and Jesus will never cease. When he had gained control of them, he called these three one by one, and said to each one of them: You are my salvation, and I saw Jesus in a dream and He was pleased with me. And he said to each one of them: Tomorrow I will sacrifice myself, so call the people to your sect. Then he entered the altar and slaughtered himself and said: I am only doing this to please Jesus. When the third day came, each one of them called the people to his sect, and each one of them followed a group of people, and they differed and fought, so God Almighty said: And the Christians say, ‘The Messiah is the son of God.’ “That is their statement with their mouths,” meaning they say it with their tongues without knowledge. The scholars of meaning said: God Almighty did not mention a statement accompanied by mouths and tongues except that it was false. They imitate, Asim read it with a kasra on the ha' with a hamza, and the others read it with a damma on the ha' without a hamza. They are two dialects. It is said: dahaita and daha'atahu, and their meaning is the same. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: they imitate. Imitation means resemblance. Mujahid said: They agree. Al-Hasan said: They agree, The statement of those who disbelieved before, Qatada and Al-Suddi said: The Christians imitated the statement of the Jews before, so they said: The Messiah is the son of God, just as the Jews said: Ezra is the son of God. Mujahid said: They imitate the statement of the polytheists before, who used to say: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat are the daughters of God. Al-Hasan said: He likened their disbelief to the disbelief of the disbelieving nations that came before, just as He said about the polytheists of the Arabs: “Thus said those before them like their statement. Their hearts are alike.” Al-Baqarah 2:188. Al-Qutaibi said: He means that those Jews and Christians who were in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said what the first of them said, May God fight them, Ibn Abbas said: May God curse them. Ibn Jurayj said: That is, may God kill them. It was said: It is not in the real sense of fighting, but rather in the sense of astonishment, How are they turned away from the truth? That is, they are turned away from the truth after the evidence for it has been established.
9:31: 31- They took their rabbis and monks as lords, meaning: their scholars and reciters. The rabbis are the scholars, and one of them is rabbi, and habbar with kasra or fatha on the har, and the monks from the Christians are the owners of monasteries. If it is said: Did they not worship the rabbis and monks? We say: Its meaning is that they obeyed them in disobeying God and made permissible what they made permissible and forbade what they forbade, so they took them as lords. It was narrated on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I had a cross of gold around my neck. He said to me, ‘O Adi, throw this idol off your neck.’ So I threw it off and then I came to him while he was reciting: ‘They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God,’ until he finished. I said to him: ‘We do not worship them.’ He said: ‘Do they not forbid what God has permitted, so you forbid it, and permit what God has forbidden, so you permit it?’ I said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘That is their worship.’” Abdullah bin Mubarak said: And has religion been changed except by kings, evil rabbis and monks? And the Messiah, the son of Mary, meaning: they took him as a god, “and they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no god but Him. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him.”
9:32: 32- They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, meaning: to invalidate the religion of God with their tongues and their denial of it. Al-Kalbi said: The light is the Qur'an, meaning: they want to reject the Qur'an with their tongues by denying it, but God refuses except to perfect His light, meaning: to exalt His religion, make His word manifest, and complete the truth with which He sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though the disbelievers dislike it.
9:33: 33- It is He who has sent His Messenger, meaning: the one who insists on completing His religion. He is the one who sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with guidance, it was said: with the Qur'an. It was also said: with an explanation of the duties, and the religion of truth, which is Islam, to make it manifest, to make it supreme and support it over all religion, to all other religions, even though the polytheists hate it. They differed about the meaning of this verse. Ibn Abbas said: The letter ha refers back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning: to teach him all the laws of the religion and make them clear to him so that nothing of them is hidden from him. Others said: The letter ha refers to the religion of truth, and its appearance over religions is that God Almighty is not to be worshipped except through it. Abu Hurairah and Ad-Dahhak said: When Jesus, son of Mary, descends, there will not remain any people of a religion except that they will enter Islam. We narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, he said: And in his time all religions will perish except Islam. Al-Miqdad narrated that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There will not remain on the face of the earth a house of mud or hair except that God will enter it with the word of Islam, either by the glory of the glorious or the humiliation of the humiliated. Either God will honor them and make them among His people, and He will be glorified by them, or He will humiliate them and they will submit to Him. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Habib told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad Sulayman bin Mansur told us, Abu Muslim bin Ibrahim bin Abdullah Al-Kaji told us, Abu Asim Al-Nabil told us, Abdul Hamid told us - he is Ibn Ja’far - on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Al-Ala’, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Night and day will not pass until Al-Lat and Al-Uzza are worshipped. She said: I said, “O Messenger of God, I did not think that would happen after God Almighty revealed to you: ‘It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, even though they who associate others with God dislike it. ’” Then he said: “That will happen as long as God wills, then God Almighty will send a good wind that will take away whoever had an atom’s weight of good in his heart, then whoever has no good in him will remain, and the people will return to the religion of their fathers.” Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: The meaning of the verse is to make it prevail over all religions with clear arguments. It was said: To make him prevail over the religions around the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and defeat them. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: God made His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, prevail over all religions by making clear to everyone who heard him that he was the truth, and that any religion that contradicted him was false. He said: And He made him prevail by the fact that the sum of polytheism is two religions: the religion of the People of the Book and the religion of the illiterate. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, subdued the illiterate until they converted to Islam willingly or unwillingly. He killed the People of the Book and took them captive until some of them converted to Islam, and some of them paid the jizya in humiliation, and his rule was applied to them. This is his victory over all religion, and God knows best.
9:34: 34- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and monks, meaning: the scholars and reciters of the People of the Book, devour the wealth of people unjustly, (meaning: take) bribes in their rulings, and distort the Book of God, and write with their own hands books saying: This is from God, and they take a small price for it from their lowest ones, which is the food that they obtain from them in order to change the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They fear that if they were to believe them, those food would go away from them, and they turn away, and divert people, from the way of God, the religion of God Almighty. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God - give them tidings of a painful punishment. Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: All wealth on which zakat is paid is not a treasure, even if it is buried. And all wealth on which zakat is not paid is a treasure, even if it is not buried. And the same was reported from Ibn Abbas. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Suwaid bin Saeed told us, Hafs bin Maysarah told us on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam that Abu Salih Dhakwan told him that he heard Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay its due from it except that on the Day of Resurrection, plates of fire will be beaten out for him and heated in the fire of Hell and his forehead and back will be branded with them. Whenever they cool, they will be returned to him in a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the servants, and he will see his path either to Paradise or to Hell. And there is no owner of camels who does not pay their due from it, and their due from it is milking them on the day they come back, except that on the Day of Resurrection, a vast plain will be spread out for them, the most abundant of them, and not a single young foal will be missing, trampling it with their hooves and biting it with their mouths. Whenever the first of them passes by, it will be returned.” “Then he will be given the last of it, on a day the length of which will be fifty thousand years, until God judges between the servants, and he will see his path, either to Paradise or to Hell. And no owner of cows or sheep will not pay their dues, except that on the Day of Resurrection, a flat, swollen plain will be spread out for him, and he will not miss a thing of it, in which there will be no hornless, bald, or rough-footed sheep. They will butt him with their horns and trample him with their hooves. Whenever the first of them passes by him, the last of them will return to him, on a day the length of which will be fifty thousand years, until God judges between the servants, and he will see his path, either to Paradise or to Hell.” We narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever God gives wealth and does not pay its zakat, his wealth will be presented to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald-headed serpent with two tufts of hair. It will encircle him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will seize his two jaws and say: ‘I am your wealth, I am your treasure.’ Then he recited: ‘And let not those who withhold what God has given them think…’” 10:10. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: All wealth that exceeds four thousand dirhams is a treasure, whether zakat is paid from it or not, and anything less than that is expenses. It was said: What is left over from what is needed is a treasure. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Wakee told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Ma’rur bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the shade of the Kaaba. When he saw me, he said: They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Kaaba. He said: So I came and sat down, and I was not able to stand up, so I said: O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, who are they? He said: They are the ones with the most wealth, except for those who said: This way, this way, and this way, in front of him, behind him, to his right, and to his left, and they are few.” It was narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, that he used to say: Whoever leaves white or red, will be cauterized with it on the Day of Resurrection. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that he said: “A man from the people of the Suffa died, and a dinar was found in his loincloth, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Caution.’ Then another man died, and two dinars were found in his loincloth, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Two cauteries.’” The first statement is more correct, because the verse prohibits zakat, not the accumulation of lawful money. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Good money is good for a righteous man. Mujahid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When this verse was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims and they said, None of us can leave anything for his children. So Omar mentioned that to the Messenger of God, and he said, God Almighty did not impose zakat except to purify what remains of your wealth. Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with him, was asked about this verse. He said: That was before zakat was revealed, but when it was revealed, God made it a purification for wealth. Ibn Omar said: I would not care if I had gold equal to Mount Uhud, and I knew its number, so I could pay zakat on it and act in obedience to God. God the Almighty said: And do not spend it in the way of God, and He did not say: And do not spend them both. He mentioned both gold and silver. It was said: He meant treasures and gold and silver objects. It was also said: He referred the metaphor to silver because it is more general, as God the Almighty said: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult. (al-Baqarah 2:45), referring the metaphor to prayer because it is more general, and as God the Almighty said: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it. (al-Jumuah 62:11), referring the metaphor to trade because it is more general, Then give them tidings of a painful punishment. That is, warn them.
9:35: 35- On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell, meaning: it will enter the fire and be lit on it, meaning on the treasures, and it will be branded with it, burning with it, their foreheads, meaning: the foreheads of its treasurers, and their flanks and their backs, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud who said: A dinar will not be placed on a dinar nor a dirham on a dirham, but its skin will be expanded until each dinar and dirham is placed in a separate place. Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked: Why did he specifically cauterize the foreheads, sides, and backs? He said: Because when the rich man who owns the treasure sees the face of the poor man, he will turn away from him the space between his eyes, turn his back to him, and turn away from him with his flank. The Almighty said: This is what you have hoarded, meaning: It will be said to them: This is what you have hoarded, for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard, meaning: you withheld the rights of God Almighty in your wealth. Some of the Companions said: This verse is about the People of the Book. The majority said: It is general and applies to the People of the Book and Muslims, and Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, said the same.
9:36: 36- The Almighty said: The number of months, meaning: the number of months, with God is twelve months in the Book of God, and they are Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, the month of Rabi' al-Thani, Jumada al-Awwal, Jumada al-Akhira, Rajab, Sha'ban, the month of Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah. His saying: in the Book of God means: in the judgment of God. It was said: in the Preserved Tablet. Abu Ja'far read: twelve, nineteen, and eleven, with a silent shin, and the general public read it with a fatha, the day He created the heavens and the earth, and what is meant by it: the lunar months, which are the months that Muslims count in their fasting, pilgrimage, festivals, and all their affairs, and with the solar months the year is three hundred and sixty-five days and a quarter, and the lunar months are less than three hundred and sixty days due to the lack of eligibility. It is most likely to be three hundred and fifty-four days, of which four are sacred. Four of the months are sacred: Rajab, Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, one in succession and three in succession. That is the upright religion, meaning: the straight reckoning. So do not wrong yourselves therein. It was said that His statement therein refers to all the months of the year, meaning: Do not wrong yourselves therein by committing sins and abandoning obedience. It was also said: therein means: in the sacred months. Qatada said: Good deeds are of greater reward in the sacred months, and injustice therein is greater than injustice in other months, even though injustice is great in any case. Ibn Abbas said: So do not wrong yourselves therein, meaning making permissible what is forbidden and raiding therein. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: Do not make what is permissible therein forbidden, nor what is forbidden therein permissible, like the action of the polytheists, which is the intercalation. And fight the polytheists all together, all in general, “as they fight you all together. And know that God is with the righteous.” The scholars differed about the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months. Some people said: It was a major sin, then it was abrogated by His statement: And fight the polytheists all together, as if he was saying in them and other than them. This is the statement of Qatadah, Ata’ al-Khurasani, al-Zuhri and Sufyan al-Thawri. They said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, raided Hawazin at Hunayn, and Thaqif at Taif, and besieged them in Shawwal and some of Dhu al-Qi’dah. Others said: It is not abrogated. Ibn Jurayj said: Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah swore by God: It is not permissible for people to raid in the sanctuary, nor in the sacred months, unless they fight in them, and it was not abrogated.
9:37: 37- The Almighty said: The postponement is only an increase in disbelief. It was said: It is a source like the blazing fire and the burning fire. It was said: It is a passive participle like the wounded and the killed, and it is from delay. And from it is the postponement in the sale, it is said: God postponed for him, meaning he delayed, and it is extended and hamzated according to most of the readers, and Warsh read from Nafi' via Al-Bukhari: with a shaddah on the yaa without a hamzah, and it was said: Its origin is the hamzah, so it was lightened. It was said: It is from the word Nasyan meaning forgotten, meaning abandoned. The meaning of Nasii is to delay the prohibition of one month to another month. This is because the Arabs believed in the veneration of the sacred months, as if that was something they adhered to from the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him. Their main livelihood was hunting and raiding, so it was difficult for them to refrain from that for three consecutive months. Sometimes a war would break out in one of the sacred months and they would hate to delay their war, so they postponed, meaning they delayed the prohibition of that month to another month. They would delay the prohibition of Muharram until Safar, so they would prohibit Safar and permit Muharram. If they needed to delay the prohibition of Safar, they would delay it until Rabi’, and so on, month after month, until the prohibition covered the entire year. Islam came about and Muharram returned to the place that God Almighty had placed it in, and that was after a long time. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave a sermon during his Hajj. Also: Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf Al-Farbari told us, Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Bukhari told us, Muhammad bin Salam told us, Abdul Wahid told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Ayoub told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Abu Bakrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Time has come back to its original state on the day the heavens and the earth were created. The year is twelve months, four of which are sacred, three of which are consecutive: Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, and Rajab Mudar, which is between Jumada and Sha’ban.” He said: What month is this? We said: God and His Messenger know best. He remained silent until we thought that he would call it by another name. He said: Is it not Dhul-Hijjah? We said: Yes. He said: What city is this? We said: God and His Messenger know best. He remained silent until we thought that he would call it by another name. He said: Is it not the Sacred City? We said: Yes. He said: What day is this? We said: God and His Messenger know best. He remained silent until we thought that he would call it by another name. He said: Is it not the Day of Sacrifice? We said: Yes. He said: Then your bloods and your wealth are sacred to you. Muhammad said: “I think he said: “And your honor is sacred to you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this city of yours, in this month of yours. You will meet your Lord, and He will ask you about your deeds. Do not return after me to misguidance, striking the necks of one another. Let the witness convey to the absent, for perhaps some of those he conveys it to may be more aware of it than some of those who hear it. Have I conveyed the message? Have I conveyed the message?” They said: The postponement continued with them, so they would sometimes perform Hajj in one month in some years and perform Hajj the following year in another month. Mujahid said: They used to perform Hajj every month for two years. They performed Hajj in the month of Dhul-Hijjah for two years, then they performed Hajj in Muharram for two years, then they performed Hajj in Safar for two years, and so on with the months. Abu Bakr’s Hajj, may God be pleased with him, coincided with the Hajj of the month of Hajj, which was Dhul-Hijjah. So he stood at Arafat on the ninth day, and he delivered a sermon on the tenth day in Mina, and he informed them that the months of intercalation had been replaced by the passage of time, and the matter had returned to what God had set the months’ calculations upon when He created the heavens and the earth, and he commanded them to preserve it so that it would not change in the coming days. They differed about the first person to postpone the Nasi’: Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Qatada and Mujahid said: The first person to postpone the Nasi’ was Banu Malik ibn Kinanah, and they were three: Abu Thamama Junad ibn Auf ibn Umayya Al-Kinani. Al-Kalbi said: The first person to do that was a man from Banu Kinanah called Nu’aym ibn Tha’labah, and he was the leader of the people during the season. When the people were about to head to the front, he stood up and addressed the people and said: There is no turning back on what you have decreed. I am the one who is not criticized nor answered. The polytheists would say to him: At your service. Then they would ask him to postpone a month so that they could make changes in it. He would say: Indeed, Safar of the year is forbidden. When he said that, they would loosen the strings, remove the spears and the ropes. If he said it was permissible, they would tie the strings, tighten the ropes, and make a raid. After Naim bin Tha’laba, there was a man called Junada bin Awf, who was the one whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, met. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: He is a man from Banu Kinanah called Al-Qalmas. Their poet said: And among us is the one who forgets the month Al-Qalmas. And they did not do that except in Dhu al-Hijjah when the Arabs gathered for the season. Jubair said on the authority of Al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: The first person to establish the postponement was Amr bin Luhay bin Qama’ah bin Khandaf. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Zuhair bin Harb told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Amr bin Luhay bin Qama’ah bin Khandaf, the father of Banu Ka’b, dragging his intestines in the fire. This is what we mentioned, which is the intercalation that God the Most High mentioned, saying: The intercalation is only an increase in disbelief, meaning an increase in disbelief upon their disbelief, with which He misguides those who disbelieve, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read: He misguides with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the dad, like God the Most High said: He made their evil deeds seem good to them, and Ya’qub read with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the dad, which is the reading of Al-Hasan and Mujahid, meaning He misguides those who disbelieved with it, and the others read with a fatha on the ya’ and a kasra on the dad, because they are the ones who are astray, according to His statement: They make it lawful, meaning the intercalation, a year and forbid it a year in order to agree, meaning: to agree, and agreement is agreement, the number of what God has forbidden, meaning that they did not make lawful a month of the forbidden, so that the forbidden would not be more than four months, as God has forbidden, so that it would be in agreement with the number, and they make lawful what God has forbidden, their evil deeds seem good to them, Ibn Abbas said: Satan makes them seem good, and God does not guide the disbelieving people.
9:38: 38- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told to go forth in the cause of God you cling heavily to the earth? The verse was revealed to encourage the Battle of Tabuk. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Taif, he ordered jihad to conquer the Romans. This was at a time when people were in difficulty and the heat was intense, when the fruits and shade were good. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not want to undertake a battle except that he would cover it with another one until that battle happened. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, undertook it in intense heat, faced a long journey, and faced vast deserts. They were many in number. He explained their matter to the Muslims so that they would prepare themselves as their enemy would. It was difficult for them to go forth and they were clumsy. So God, the Almighty, revealed: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told meaning: the Messenger of God said to you: Go forth go forth in the cause of God you cling heavily to the earth meaning: you stuck to your land and your homes. Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? That is, with the lowliness and insignificance of this world in comparison to the pleasures of the Hereafter. But the enjoyment of the life of this world is but little compared to the Hereafter.
9:39: 39-Then He threatened them for abandoning jihad, and the Almighty said: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment, in the Hereafter. It was said: It is the withholding of rain from them in this world. Najdah ibn Nafi' asked Ibn Abbas about this verse, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon a tribe of the Arabs to mobilize, but they were reluctant to him, so he withheld the rain from them, and that was their punishment. And He will replace you with another people better than you and more obedient. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: They are the sons of Persia. It was said: They are the people of Yemen. And you will not harm Him at all by not mobilizing. And God is over all things competent.
9:40: 40- The Almighty said: "If you do not aid him, God has already aided him." This is a notification from God, the Almighty, that He is the One who is responsible for the aid of His Messenger and the glory of His religion, whether they aided him or not, and that He aided him when the guardians were few and the enemies were many, so how is it today when he is in great numbers and numbers? "When those who disbelieved drove him out, from Mecca when they plotted against him and wanted to kill him by night, the second of two," meaning he is one of the two, and the two: one of them is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the other is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, "When they were in the cave, which is a tunnel in Mount Thawr in Mecca, When he said to his companion, 'Do not grieve; indeed God is with us.'" Al-Sha'bi said: God, the Almighty, rebuked all the people of the earth in this verse except for Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. Abu al-Muzaffar Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tamimi told us, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman told us, Khaithamah ibn Sulayman told us, Ahmad ibn Abd God al-Dawraqi told us, Sa`id ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Hashim, on the authority of Kathir al-Nawa, on the authority of Jami` ibn Umair, who said: I came to Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, and I heard him say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him: You are my companion in the cave and my companion at the Cistern. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Whoever says that Abu Bakr was not a companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is an infidel because he denies the text of the Qur’an. As for the rest of the companions, if he denies it, he is an innovator, not an infidel. And the Almighty’s saying: Do not grieve, indeed God is with us. Abu Bakr’s grief was not out of cowardice, but rather out of compassion for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: If I am killed, then I am one man, and if I am killed, the entire nation will perish. It was narrated that when he set out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the cave, he walked for a while in front of him and for a while behind him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What is the matter with you, Abu Bakr? He said: I remember the pursuit, so I walk behind you, then I remember the ambush, so I walk in front of you. When they arrived at the cave, he said: Stay where you are, O Messenger of God, until I clear the cave. So he entered and cleared it, then he said: Come down, O Messenger of God. So he came down. Umar said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, that night was better than the family of Umar. Abu Al-Muzaffar Al-Tamimi told us, Muhammad bin Abdul-Rahman bin Othman, known as Ibn Abi Al-Nadhar, told us, Khaithamah bin Sulayman told us, Abu Qilabah Al-Raqashi told us, Hayyan bin Hilal told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us, Thabit Al-Banani told us, Anas bin Malik told us that Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, told them, he said: I looked at the feet of the polytheists above our heads while we were in the cave, so I said: O Messenger of God, if one of them looked under his feet he would see us, so he said: O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when God is their third? Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqil, Ibn Shihab said: Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I never knew my parents except that they were practicing the religion, and not a day passed without the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, coming to us at the ends of the day, in the morning and in the evening. When the Muslims were tested, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Muslims: I was shown the land of your migration, with palm trees, between two lava plains, which are the two Harrats. So those who migrated before Medina migrated, and most of those who had migrated in the land of Abyssinia returned to Medina. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, prepared himself before Medina, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Take it easy, for I hope that permission will be given to me. Abu Bakr said: Do you hope that, may my father be sacrificed for you? He said: Yes. So Abu Bakr kept himself with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to accompany him, and he fed He had two camels - he had samr leaves, which are the tamarisk leaves - for four months. Ibn Shihab said. Urwah said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: “While we were sitting one day in Abu Bakr’s house at noon, someone said to Abu Bakr: This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wearing a veil at an hour when he does not usually come to us. Abu Bakr said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for him, by God he did not come at this hour except for a command. She said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and asked permission, and he gave him permission, so he entered. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr: Go out from you. Abu Bakr said: They are your family, may my father be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God. He said: Then I have been given permission to go out. Abu Bakr said: Are you the companions, may my father be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes. Abu Bakr said: Then take one of these two mounts of mine, O Messenger of God. The Messenger of God said: For the price. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: So we prepared them with the utmost rigor, and we prepared for them a meal in a bag. Asma’ bint Abu Bakr cut a piece of her belt and tied it to the mouth of the bag, and that is why she was called Dhat The two belts, she said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr went to a cave in Mount Thawr, and they stayed there for three nights, and Abdullah bin Abu Bakr, a young, educated boy, would spend the night with them, and he would leave them at dawn and would be with the Quraysh in Mecca in the morning, as if he had spent the night there, and he would not hear anything that they were about to do except that he would remember it until he came to them with report of it when darkness fell, and Aamer bin Fuhayrah, the freed slave of Abu Bakr, would graze a gift of sheep for them, and he would let them rest for them when the hour of the evening had passed, and they would spend the night in a rusul, which was the milk of their gift and their food, until Aamer bin Fuhayrah would call to them at dawn, and he would do that every night of those three nights, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dayl, and he was from Banu Abd bin Adi, a skilled guide, and the kharit is the skilled guide, he had immersed an alliance with the family of al-Aas bin Wa’il al-Sahmi, and he was of the religion of the infidels of Quraysh, so they trusted him, so they gave him their two camels and made an appointment with him in a cave. After three nights, Thor left with their two camels on the morning of the third, and Amer bin Fuhaira and the guide set out with them, and he took them on the coastal road. Ibn Shihab said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Malik al-Mudliji informed me, and he is the nephew of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ja’sham: His father informed him that he heard Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ja’sham say: Messengers of the infidels of Quraysh came to us, offering blood money for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, for each one of them, for whoever killed or captured him. While I was sitting in a gathering of my people, Banu Mudlij, a man from them came and stood over us while we were sitting, and said: O Suraqa, I have just seen black people on the coast, I think they are Muhammad and his companions. Suraqa said: So I knew that they were them, so I said to him: They are not them, but you saw so-and-so and so-and-so go before our eyes. Then I remained in the gathering for an hour, then I got up and entered the house, and I ordered my maid to go out with my horse, which was behind a hill, and to hold it back for me. I took my spear and went out with it from the back of the house, and I drew a line through the ground with its tip, and I lowered its top until I came to my horse, and I mounted it and pushed it to bring me closer until I was near them. My horse stumbled, so I fell off it. I stood up, reached into my quiver, took out arrows and cast lots with them as to whether they would harm me or not. Then the one I was forced to do came out. I mounted my horse and disobeyed the arrows. They drew near to me until I heard the recitation of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), and he was not turning around, while Abu Bakr was turning around a lot. My horse’s hands sank into the ground until they reached my knees. I fell off it, then urged it on and it got up, but it could hardly take its hands out. When it had straightened up, there was a shining dust in the sky like smoke. I cast lots with the arrows and the one I was forced to do came out. I called out to them for safety, and they stopped. I mounted my horse until I came to them, and it occurred to me when I encountered what I encountered. From the detention of them, the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will appear. So I said to him: Your people have set a blood money for you, and I have informed them of what the people want from them, and I have offered them provisions and goods, but they did not give me anything and did not ask me for anything except that they said: Hide from us. So I asked him to write me a letter of security, so he ordered Amer bin Fuhayrah to write on a piece of leather, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, departed. Ibn Shihab said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met al-Zubayr in a group of Muslims who were merchants returning from Syria. Al-Zubayr clothed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr in white clothes. The Muslims in Medina heard about the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca, so they would go out every morning to the lava field and wait for him until the heat of noon would bring them back. One day, they turned back after waiting for a long time. When they had returned to their homes, a Jewish man arrived on one of their rooftops to see something. He saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, white as a mirage. The Jew could not help but say at the top of his voice: O people of the Arabs, this is your grandfather whom you are waiting for. The Muslims rose up to greet him and met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the back of the lava field. He turned with them to the right until he descended with them to Banu Amr ibn Awf. That was on Monday of the month of Rabi` al-Awwal. Abu Bakr stood up for the people, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat silently. Those of the Ansar who had come from among those who had come began to The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not see Abu Bakr greet him until the sun had set on the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Bakr came and shaded him with his cloak, and the people recognized the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) at that time. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stayed with Bani Amr ibn Awf for about ten nights, and founded the mosque that was founded on piety. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed in it, then he mounted his mount and walked with the people until it knelt near the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in Medina. On that day, some Muslim men were praying in it. It was a date shed for Suhayl and Sahl, two orphan boys in the care of As`ad ibn Zurarah. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said when his mount knelt: This, God willing, is the home. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called the two boys and bargained with them for the shed so that he could make it a mosque. They said: Rather, we will plunder it for you, O Messenger of God. Then he built it as a mosque, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) began to carry bricks with them in its construction, saying while carrying the bricks: This porter is not the porter of Khaybar. He is the most pious and pure of our Lord. He says: O God, the reward is the reward of the Hereafter, so have mercy on the Ansar and the Muhajireen. It was represented by the house of a Muslim man who was not named to me. Ibn Shihab said: We have not been informed in the hadiths that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited a complete verse of poetry other than these verses. Al-Zuhri said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr entered the cave, God Almighty sent a pair of pigeons until they laid eggs at the bottom of the tunnel, and a spider until it wove a house. In the story, a dove grew at the mouth of the cave, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, blind their eyes from us. So the seekers began to strike right and left around the cave, saying: If they entered this cave, the pigeons’ eggs would break and the spider’s house would disintegrate. The Almighty said: “Then God sent down His tranquility upon him.” It was said: upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas said: upon Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had tranquility before. And supported him with soldiers you did not see, and they were the angels who descended to turn the faces and eyes of the disbelievers away from seeing him. It was said: They cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers until they returned. Mujahid and Al-Kalbi said: He aided him with the angels on the day of Badr. He informed us that He turned away the plot of the enemies from him in the cave, then He revealed his victory with the angels on the day of Badr. And He has made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, and their word is polytheism, and it is the lowest until the Day of Resurrection, and the word of God is the highest, until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abbas said: It is the statement, There is no god but God. It was said that the word of those who disbelieved is what they plotted against him to kill him, and the word of God is the promise of God that He will support him. And Yaqub read: and the word of God with the ta’ in the accusative case as a conjunction, and God is Exalted in Might and Wise.
9:41: 41- The Almighty said: Go forth, whether light or heavy. Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ikrimah said: Young men and old men. And from Ibn Abbas: Active and not active. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: Riders and pedestrians. Abu Saleh said: Light of wealth, meaning poor, and heavy means rich. Ibn Zaid said: The heavy one is the one who has an estate, so he is heavy and hates to leave his estate, and the light one has no estate. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Light are those who travel with wealth, and heavy are those who are in difficulty. And it was said: Light of weapons, meaning: little of it, and heavy means: much of it. Al-Hakam bin Utaybah said: Busy and not busy. And Marra Al-Hamadhani said: Healthy and sick.
