Yaman bin Rabab said: Single and married. It was said: Light from your entourage and followers, and heavy, having many of them. It was said: Light, hurrying out at the moment of hearing the trumpet, and heavy after taking it easy and preparing for it. “And strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of God. That is best for you, if you only knew.” Al-Zuhri said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab went out to fight and one of his eyes had gone, so it was said to him: You are ill and suffering from a disease. He said: God has called forth the light and the heavy, and if I am not able to fight, then the blacks will increase and the provisions will be preserved. Ata Al-Khurasani said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This verse was abrogated by His statement: And it is not for the believers to go forth all together. Al-Suddi said: When this verse was revealed, its importance became severe for the people, so God abrogated it and revealed: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the ill verse.
9:42: 42-Then it was revealed about the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk: If it had been an imminent offer, and the noun was is implied, meaning: if what you are calling them to were an imminent offer, meaning: an easy-to-reach booty, and a short journey, meaning: easy and near, they would have followed you, they would have gone out with you, but the distance was too great for them, meaning: the distance, and the distance is the long journey, because it is difficult for a person. It was said: the distance is the goal they are aiming for, and they will swear by God, ‘If we were able, we would have gone out with you,’ destroying themselves, meaning with a false oath, and God knows that they are liars, in their oaths and faith, because they were able.
9:43: 43- May God forgive you. Amr bin Maymun said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did two things that he was not commanded to do: his permission for the hypocrites, and his taking ransom from the prisoners of Badr, so God rebuked him as you hear. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Look at this kindness. He began with forgiveness before he reproached him for the sin. It was said: God Almighty honored him and raised his status by opening the speech with supplication for him, as a man says to someone he is addressing if he is generous to him: May God forgive you for what you did to me? And may God be pleased with you, why didn’t you visit me? It was said that its meaning is: May God continue to forgive you. Why did you give them permission? That is, to stay behind you, until it became clear to you who were truthful, in their excuses, and you knew who were lying, in it, that is, you knew who had no excuse. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know the hypocrites on that day.
9:44: 44- Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your permission to fight with their wealth and their lives, meaning: they do not ask your permission to stay behind, and God is Knowing of the righteous.
9:45: 45- Only those ask your permission who do not believe in God and the Last Day and whose hearts are in doubt, that is, doubted and hypocritical, so in their doubt they waver, confused.
9:46: 46- "And if they had intended to go out to the conquest, they would have prepared for it, that is, they would have prepared for it a set of equipment", equipment and strength from peace and arms, "but God disliked their going out, their going out, so He held them back, He prevented them and detained them from going out, and it was said, 'Sit', in your homes, with those who sit", meaning: with the sick and the chronically ill. It was also said: with the women and children. The Almighty's statement: "And it was said", that is, some of them said to one another: Sit. It was also said: He inspired in their hearts and inspired them with the reasons for their failure.
9:47: 47- If they had come out with you, that is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to fight in the Battle of Tabuk, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, camped his army at Thaniyat al-Wada', and Abdullah bin Ubay camped at Dhi Jidda, below Thaniyat al-Wada', and he was not the smallest of the two armies, so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out, Abdullah bin Ubay stayed behind with those who stayed behind from the hypocrites and the people of doubt, so God, the Most High, revealed consoling His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If they had come out meaning the hypocrites with you meaning with you, they would not have increased you except in confusion meaning: corruption and evil. The meaning of corruption is: causing cowardice and failure among the believers by exaggerating the matter, and they would have hastened, in your midst, among you by causing enmity and hatred among you by gossiping and spreading gossip from one to another. It was said: they would have hastened in what would harm you.. They seek to tempt you" means: they ask you for something to tempt us. They say: such and such has been gathered against you, and you will be defeated and your enemy will prevail over you, and so on. Al-Kalbi said: They seek to tempt you, meaning: shame and evil. Ad-Dahhak said: Fitnah is polytheism. It is said: I sought evil and good for him, I seek it for him, meaning I seek it for him. And among you are those who listen to them. Mujahid said: Its meaning is that among you are those who love them and deliver to them what they hear from you, and they are the spies. Qatada said: Its meaning is that among you are those who obey them, meaning: they listen to their words and obey them. And God is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers.
9:48: 48- They had sought discord before, meaning: they sought to turn your companions away from the religion and return them to disbelief, and to discourage people from you before this day, as Abdullah bin Ubay did on the day of Uhud when he turned away from you with his companions. And they turned things upside down for you, and they stirred up opinions about you and invalidating your religion, by discouraging you and scattering your affairs, until the truth came, victory and triumph, and the command of God appeared, the religion of God, while they were averse.
9:49: 49- The Almighty said: And among them is he who says, 'Give me permission and do not put me to trial', this was revealed about Jadd bin Qays the hypocrite. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prepared for the Battle of Tabuk, he said: O Abu Wahb, would you like to fight the yellow people? Meaning the Romans, and take concubines and slave girls from them. Jadd said: O Messenger of God, my people know that I am a man who is fond of women, and I fear that if I see the daughters of the yellow people I will not be able to keep away from them. Give me permission to stay and do not put me to trial with them, and I will help you with what I have. Ibn Abbas said: Jadd bin Qays became ill and his only excuse was spending, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him and said: I give you permission. Then God Almighty revealed: And among them meaning the hypocrites is he who says, 'Give me permission' to stay behind and do not put me to trial with the daughters of the yellow people. Qatada said: Do not blame me: Indeed, they have fallen into temptation, meaning: they fell into polytheism and sin because of their hypocrisy and their opposition to the command of God and the command of His Messenger, and indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers, encompassing them and gathering them in it.
9:50: 50- If good befalls you, victory and spoils, it distresses them, saddens them, meaning: the hypocrites, but if a disaster befalls you, killing and defeat, “they say, ‘We have taken our decision,’ we warned, meaning: we took firm action in sitting back from the invasion, “before,” meaning: before this disaster, and they turn away, and retreat, while they are rejoicing, happy with the disaster that has befallen you.
9:51: 51- Say to them, O Muhammad, Nothing will ever happen to us except what God has decreed for us, that is, against us in the Preserved Tablet. He is our Master, our Supporter and Preserver. Al-Kalbi said: He is more deserving of us than we are of ourselves in death and life. And in God let the believers put their trust.
9:52: 52- "Say: Do you await for us, O hypocrites, anything but one of the two best things?" Either victory and spoils or martyrdom and forgiveness. We narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: "God has guaranteed to whoever strives in His cause, and nothing drives him out of his home except striving in His cause and believing in His word: that He will admit him to Paradise, or return him to the home from which he left with whatever reward or spoils he has attained." The Almighty’s statement, And We are waiting for you, is one of two evils: either: that God will afflict you with a punishment from Himself, so He destroys you as He destroyed the previous nations, or by our hands, meaning: by the hands of the believers if you reveal what is in your hearts, so wait, for we are waiting with you. Al-Hasan said: So wait for the promises of Satan, for we are waiting for the promises of God to make His religion manifest and to eradicate those who oppose it.
9:53: 53- "Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly," a command with the meaning of condition and reward, meaning: if you spend willingly or unwillingly. It was revealed about the grandfather of Qais when he asked permission to stay, he said: I will help you with my money, he said: if you spend willingly or unwillingly it will not be accepted from you, for you, meaning: because you, were a people of immorality.
9:54: 54- And what prevented them from being accepted from them? Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read: accept with a ya' because the verb came before it, and the rest read it with a ta' because the verb is attributed to a feminine plural which is expenditures, so you are the verb to know that the subject is feminine, their expenditures, their charity, except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger, meaning: what prevented their expenditures from being accepted is their disbelief, and they do not come to prayer except while they are lazy, sluggish because they do not hope for a reward for performing it, and they do not fear punishment for abandoning it. If it is said: How is laziness in prayer condemned when they do not pray at all? It is said: The condemnation is directed at the disbelief that leads to laziness, because disbelief causes laziness, and faith is energizing, and they do not spend except while they are reluctant, because they consider it a loss and its prevention a gain.
9:55: 55- So do not let their wealth or their children impress you. Impressiveness is being pleased with what one is amazed by. He says: Do not be pleased with what We have bestowed upon them of wealth and children, because if the servant is tempted by God, God will increase his wealth and children. God only intends to punish them with them in the life of this world. If it is said: What punishment in wealth and children when they enjoy them in the life of this world? It was said: Mujahid and Qatada said: There is an inversion in the verse, meaning: Do not let their wealth or their children impress you in this worldly life. God only wants to punish them with them in the Hereafter. It was said: Torture through calamities that befall money and children. Al-Hasan said: He torments them with it in this world by taking zakat from it and spending in the way of God. It was also said: He torments them with the fatigue of collecting it, the fear of preserving it, the hatred of spending it, and the regret of leaving it with someone who does not praise him. Then he is presented to a king who does not excuse him. And their souls will perish, meaning: they will go out, while they are disbelievers, meaning: they will die in disbelief.
9:56: 56- And they swear by God that they are of you, meaning: of your religion, but they are not of you, but they are a people who are afraid, who fear to reveal what they are upon.
9:57: 57- If they find a refuge, a fortress, a stronghold, and a stronghold. Ata' said: An escape. It was also said: A people who feel safe in them. Or caves, a cavern in the mountains, the plural of cave, which is the place where one sinks, i.e. hides. Ata' said: catacombs. Or an entrance, a place to enter into, and its origin is: madtakhil mufta'il, from adkhala yakhul. Mujahid said: Mahrazan. Qatada said: Sarban. Al-Kalbi said: A tunnel in the ground like the tunnel of a jerboa. Al-Hasan said: A face they enter in opposition to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was read: madkhal with a fatha on the m and a light dal, and Ya'qub read it likewise, they turned back to it, they turned back to it fleeing from you, while they rush, they hasten in refusal and aversion, nothing turning their faces away. The meaning of the verse is: If they find a way out from you and an escape, they would leave you.
9:58: 58- The Almighty’s saying, And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities, the verse is about Dhu al-Khuwaysira al-Tamimi, whose name is Hawqus bin Zuhair, the origin of the Khawarij. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman told me that Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, said: “While we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was distributing a portion among us, Dhu Al-Khuwaisira, a man from Banu Tamim, came to him and said: O Messenger of God, be just. He said: Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just? I have failed and lost if I am not just. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to strike off his head. He said to him: Leave him, for he has companions who would make your prayer insignificant compared to their prayer and your fasting insignificant compared to their fasting. They recite the Qur’an, but it does not go beyond their collarbones. They pass through the religion as an arrow passes through the target. He looks at its point but finds nothing in it, then he looks at its hilt but finds nothing in it, then he looks at its point, which is its fulcrum, but finds nothing in it, then he looks at its fulcrum, which is its spear, but finds nothing in it, then he looks at its fulcrum.” There is nothing in it. The dung and blood preceded their sign: a black man, one of his arms like a woman’s breast, or like a piece of cloth that flows. They will emerge at a time when the people are divided.” Abu Saeed said: I bear witness that I heard this hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I bear witness that Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, fought them and I was with him. So he ordered that man to be sought, and he was found, and he was brought until I looked at him with the description that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given him. Al-Kalbi said: A man / from the hypocrites called Abu Al-Jawaz said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: You did not divide equally, so God revealed: And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities meaning: they find fault with you in your order and distribution of them and criticize you for them. It is said: Lamazah and Hamza, meaning: they criticize him, meaning that the hypocrites used to say that Muhammad only gives to those he loves. And Yaqub read Yalmazak where it was: Yalamzak, meaning: Yaruzak, meaning: he tests you. If they are given from it, they are pleased; but if they are not given from it, at once they are angry, it was said that if they are given a lot, they are happy, and if they are given a little, they are angry.
9:59: 59- And if they had been satisfied with what God and His Messenger gave them, meaning: they had been content with what God and His Messenger had apportioned for them, and had said, 'God is sufficient for us,' meaning: God is sufficient for us, God will give us from His bounty, and so will His Messenger, what we need, Indeed, we are desirous toward God, that He would expand upon us from His bounty, so that we would not need charity or other people's money. The answer to if is omitted, meaning: it would have been better for them and more beneficial to them.
9:60: 60- The Almighty said: Zakat is only for the poor and the needy the verse, God Almighty explained in this verse the people who have a share in the charity and divided it into eight categories. It was narrated on the authority of Ziyad bin Al-Harith Al-Sada'i who said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and pledged allegiance to him, then a man came to him and said: Give me some of the charity, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: God was not satisfied with the ruling of a prophet or anyone else regarding charity until he ruled on it and divided it into eight parts, so if you are one of those parts, I will give you your right. God Almighty says: For the poor and the needy. So he took the types of charity: the poor, and the second: the needy. Scholars differed regarding the description of the poor and needy. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ikrimah, and Al-Zuhri said: The poor is the one who does not ask, and the needy is the one who asks. Ibn Omar said: He is not poor who collects dirham after dirham and date after date, but he who purifies himself and his clothes and is not able to do anything, the ignorant thinks them rich because of their abstinence. Qatada said: The poor person is the needy person, and the destitute person is the healthy person in need. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: The poor are from the Muslims, and the needy are from the People of the Book. Al-Shafi’i said: The poor person is the one who has neither wealth nor a profession that would be of any use to him, whether for a period of time or otherwise. The needy person is the one who has wealth or a profession that does not make him rich, whether he is a beggar or not. The needy person is in a better state than the poor person, because God Almighty said: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people (al-Kahf 18:79), confirming that they own it along with the name of being poor. And according to the opinion of the al-Nas 114:the poor person is better off than the needy person. Al-Qatibi said: The poor person is the one who has the means to live, and the needy person is the one who has nothing. It was said: The poor person is the one who has a home and a servant, and the needy person is the one who has no property. They said: Everyone who is in need of something is in need of it even if he is rich and does not need anyone else. God Almighty said: You are those in need of God (Ghafir 40:15). The needy person is the one who is in need of everything. Do you not see how He urged us to feed him and made the food of expiation for him? There is no need greater than the need to satisfy hunger. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: The poor are the immigrants, and the needy are those Muslims who did not immigrate. In short: poverty and destitution are two expressions of need and weakness of condition. The poor person is the needy person whose back has been broken by need, and the destitute person is the one whose soul has become weak and still, unable to move in search of sustenance. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisham, meaning Ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Adi bin Al-Khayar: that two men told him that they came to the Messenger of God and asked him about charity, so he went up to them and pointed, and said: If you wish, I will give it to you, and there is no share in it for the rich or the one who has the strength to earn. They differed on the limit of wealth that prevents taking charity. The majority said: Its limit is that he has enough to suffice him and his family for a year, and this is the opinion of Malik and Al-Shafi’i. The proponents of opinion said: Its limit is that he owns two hundred dirhams. Some people said: Whoever has fifty dirhams, it is not permissible for him to give charity, based on what we narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever asks people while he has enough to satisfy him, he will come on the Day of Resurrection with scratches, wounds, or marks on his face from his begging. It was said: O Messenger of God, what will satisfy him? He said: Fifty dirhams or their value in gold.” This is the opinion of Al-Thawri, Ibn Al-Mubarak, Ahmad, and Ishaq. They said: It is not permissible for a man to be given more than fifty dirhams from zakat. It was said: Forty dirhams, based on what was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever asks while he has an ounce or its equivalent, has asked persistently. God Almighty says: And those who work on it. They are the messengers who are responsible for collecting the alms from those who are entitled to them and putting them in their proper place. They are given from the alms money, whether they are poor or rich, and they are given a reward similar to their work. Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid said: They are entitled to one-eighth of the charity. And those whose hearts are to be reconciled. The fourth category of those who are entitled to charity are those whose hearts are to be reconciled. They are divided into two categories: Muslims and infidels. As for the Muslims, they are divided into two categories: those who entered Islam but had weak intentions, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would give to them to win their hearts over, as he gave to Uyaynah ibn Badr, Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis, and Al-Abbas ibn Mirdas. Or they converted to Islam but had strong intentions, and they were noble people like Adi ibn Hatim and Al-Zubayr ibn Badr. So he would give to them to win their people over and to encourage others like them to convert to Islam. It is permissible for the Imam to give them from the fifth of the spoils of war, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would give them from that and not from the charity. The second category of those who reconcile Muslims: is when a group of Muslims are facing a group of infidels in a remote location, and the Muslim armies cannot reach them except with great expense, and they are not fighting jihad, either because of the weakness of their intention or the weakness of their condition. So it is permissible for the Imam to give them from the share of the fighters from the charity money. And it was said: from the share of those who reconcile. And among them are a group of people facing a group of those who refuse to pay zakat, and they take zakat from them and carry it to the Imam, so the Imam gives them from the share of those who reconcile from the charity money. And it was said: from the share of the path of God. It was narrated that Adi bin Hatim came to Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq with three hundred camels from the alms of his people, and Abu Bakr gave him thirty camels from them. As for the infidels among those to be reconciled: they are those whose evil is feared, or whose Islam is hoped for, so the Imam wants to give this one as a precaution against his evil, or to give that one to encourage him to Islam. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to give them from the fifth of the fifth, as he gave to Safwan ibn Umayya when he saw his inclination towards Islam. As for today, God has honored Islam, praise be to Him, and has made it independent of men being reconciled to it, so no polytheist is given as a means of reconciling them under any circumstances. Many of the people of knowledge have said this, that those to be reconciled are cut off and their share is invalid. This was narrated from Ikrimah, and it is the opinion of al-Sha’bi, and it is also said by Malik, al-Thawri, the People of Opinion, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. Some people said: Their share is fixed. This is narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, and it is the saying of Al-Zuhri, Abu Jaafar Muhammad bin Ali, and Abu Thawr. Ahmad said: They are given if the Muslims need it. God the Almighty said: And for the freeing of slaves. The fifth category: They are the slaves, and they are those who have been freed from the contract of manumission. They have a share of the zakat. This is the opinion of most of the jurists, and it was stated by Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Zuhri, Al-Layth bin Sa’d, and Al-Shafi’i. A group said: Slaves are bought with the share of the slaves and then freed. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan, and it was stated by Malik, Ahmad, and Ishaq. The Almighty says: And those in debt. The sixth category is: those in debt, and they are divided into two categories: a category that has indebted themselves for something other than disobedience to God, so they are given from the charity if they do not have enough money to pay off their debts, but if they have enough money to pay off their debts, then they are not given anything. A category that has indebted for something good and to reconcile people, so they are given from the charity money what they can use to pay off their debts, even if they are rich. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of `Ata’ ibn Yasar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Charity is not permissible for a rich person except for five: for a fighter in the cause of God, or for a debtor, or for a man who bought it with his money, or for a man who has a poor neighbor and gives charity to the poor and the poor person gives a gift to the rich person, or for a worker who collects it.” It was narrated by Muammar on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam on the authority of Ata bin Yasar on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a connected meaning. As for the one whose debt is based on disobedience, it will not be paid to him. And the Almighty’s saying: And in the way of God, he meant by it: the warriors, so they have a share of the charity, which they are given if they want to go out to the battle, and whatever they need to help them with the matter of the battle from: expenses, clothing, weapons, and provisions, even if they are rich, and nothing of it is given to them during the Hajj according to most scholars. Some people said: It is permissible to spend a share in the way of God on Hajj. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Ahmad, and Ishaq. God Almighty says: And the wayfarer. The eighth category: They are the wayfarers. So whoever wants to travel in a permissible way and does not have what it takes to cover the distance, he is given from the charity in proportion to what he needs to cover that distance, whether he has money in the country to which he is traveling or not. Qatada said: The wayfarer is the guest. The jurists of the fortune teller said: The wayfarer is the stranded pilgrim. The Almighty says: An obligation meaning: obligatory from God. It is an accusative of separation, and it was said: as a source, meaning: God imposed these things as an obligation. And God is Knowing and Wise. Jurists differed on how to divide charity, and on the permissibility of spending it on certain categories: A group of people said that it is not permissible to spend it all on some of them while there are other categories, and this is the opinion of Ikrimah, and Al-Shafi’i said the same. He said: The zakat of each category of his money must be divided among the six categories present, whose shares are fixed equally, because the share of the one who reconciles is dropped, and the share of the worker if he divides it by himself, then the share of each category of them is not permissible to spend it on less than three of them if there are three or more of them, so if there is a difference between those three, it is permissible, and if there is only one of some categories, the share of that category is spent on him as long as it does not exceed the limit of entitlement, and if his need ends and there is something left, he returns it to the rest. A group of people said that if all of it is given to one of these categories, or to one person, it is permissible. God Almighty named these eight categories to inform them that charity does not go beyond these categories, not to require it to be divided among them all. This is the opinion of Omar and Ibn Abbas, and Saeed bin Jubair and Ata’ said the same. Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion agreed with it, and Ahmad said the same. He said: It is permissible to give it to one category, but dividing it is better. Ibrahim said: If the money is a lot and can be divided, divide it among the categories. If it is a little, it is permissible to put it in one category. Malik said: He should investigate the place of need among them and give priority to the first and foremost of those with a good relationship and need. If he sees that the good relationship is more among the poor in one year, he should give priority to them. If he sees it in another category in one year, he should transfer it to them. And whoever is given something from the charity, it does not exceed the amount of his entitlement, so the poor does not exceed the amount of his wealth, and if he attains the lowest level of wealth, he is not given anything after that, and if he is a professional but does not find the tools of his trade: he is given the amount with which he obtains the tools of his trade, and the worker is not given more than the wage of his knowledge, and the slave is given the amount with which he is freed. And for the debtor according to the amount of his debt, and for the warrior according to the amount of his expenses for going and returning and staying in his battle and what he needs of horse and weapons, and for the wayfarer according to the amount of his arrival at his destination or his money. They differed about transferring the charity from the country of the money to another place, while there are those who deserve it there: Most of the scholars disliked it, because Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi informed us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi informed us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi informed us, Abu Kurayb informed us, Waki’ informed us, Zakariya bin Ishaq Al-Makki informed us, Yahya bin Abdullah bin Al-Sayfi informed us on the authority of Abu Ma’bad on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Muadh to Yemen and said: “You are going to a people of the Book, so call them to testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. If they obey you in that, then inform them that God has imposed on them five prayers during the day and night. If they obey in that, then inform them that God has imposed on them charity to be taken from their rich and given to their poor. If they obey in that, then beware of the best of their wealth, and beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no veil between it and God.” This indicates that it is a charity from the rich of each people that is given to the poor of that people. They agreed that if he was transferred from one country to another, he should pay it with dislike, and the obligation is dropped from his responsibility, except for what was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Abdul Aziz, may God be pleased with him, that he returned a charity that was carried from Khorasan to the Levant to its place in Khorasan.
9:61: 61- And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, 'He is an ear.' This verse was revealed about a group of hypocrites who were harming the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and saying what was not appropriate. Some of them said: Do not do that, for we fear that what you are saying will reach him and he will harm us. Al-Jalas bin Suwaid said: Rather, we will say whatever we want, then we will go to him and deny what we said, and swear, and he will believe us in what we say. Muhammad is an ear, meaning: the ear of his listener. It is said: So-and-so is an ear and an ear, on the weight of his action, if he hears everything that is said to him and accepts it. Its origin is from the word adhan which means: he listened. It was said: he is an ear, meaning: he has a listening ear. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: It was revealed about a hypocrite called Nabtal ibn al-Harith. He was a man with disheveled hair, red eyes, dark cheeks, and a deformed appearance. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wants to look at the devil, let him look at Nabtal ibn al-Harith. He used to tell the hypocrites about the Prophet’s speech, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said to him: Do not do that. He said: Muhammad is only an ear, so whoever tells him something, he believes it. So we say whatever we want, then we go to him and swear by God and he believes us. Then God Almighty revealed this verse. God the Almighty said: “Say: A good ear for you.” The general public read it with the addition, meaning: a good and righteous listener for you, not a bad and corrupt listener. Al-A’mash and Al-Barjami read on the authority of Abu Bakr: A good ear for you, with both nominative and tanween, meaning: that he hears from you and believes you is better for you than that he lies to you and does not accept your words. Then he denied them and said: He believes in God, meaning: no, rather he believes in God, and believes the believers, meaning: he believes the believers and accepts them, not the hypocrites. It is said: I trusted him and I trusted him, meaning I believed him. And mercy, Hamza read: and mercy in the accusative case, meaning a good ear for you, and a mercy ear. The others read: and mercy in the nominative case, meaning: it is a good ear, and it is mercy for those among you who believe, because it was the reason for the believers’ belief: And those who harm the Messenger of God will have a painful punishment.
9:62: 62- They swear to you by God to please you. Qatada and Al-Suddi said: A group of hypocrites gathered, among them Al-Jalas bin Suwaid and Wadi'ah bin Thabit, and they attacked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: If what Muhammad says is true, then we are worse than donkeys. They had a young boy from the Ansar called Amir bin Qais, so they belittled him and said this statement. The young boy became angry and said: By God, what Muhammad says is true and you are worse than donkeys. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. He called them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them, and they swore that Amir was a liar. Amir swore that they were liars, so the Prophet, may God bless them and grant them peace, believed them. Amir began to supplicate and say: O God, make the truthful one true and the liar a liar. Then God, the Most High, revealed this verse. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about a group of hypocrites who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, they came to him to apologize and swear, so God Almighty revealed this verse: They swear to you by God to please you, but God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers.
9:63: 63- Do they not know that whoever opposes God and His Messenger? opposes God and His Messenger, that they are on the same side as God and His Messenger, "for him is the fire of Hell, wherein he will abide eternally. That is the great disgrace." That is, the great scandal.
9:64: 64- The hypocrites are afraid, that is, the hypocrites fear, that a Surah will be sent down upon them, that is, sent down upon the believers, that will inform them of what is in their hearts, that is, of what is in the hearts of the hypocrites of envy and enmity toward the believers, which they used to say among themselves and keep secret and fear the disgrace of the revelation of the Qur'an concerning them. Qatada said: This surah is called Al-Fadihah, Al-Mubtatherah, and Al-Muthirah. It exposes their shame and faults. Abdullah bin Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: God Almighty revealed the mention of seventy hypocrites by their names and the names of their fathers, then He abrogated the mention of the names as a mercy to the believers, so that they would not reproach one another, because their children were believers. Say, Mock, but God will bring out what you fear. Ibn Kaysan said: “This verse was revealed about twelve hypocrites who stood in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-Aqaba when he returned from the Battle of Tabuk, in order to kill him when he ascended it. They had with them a Muslim man whose affair they concealed from them, and they disguised themselves from him on a dark night. Gabriel informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what they had planned, and ordered him to send to them someone who would strike the faces of their camels, with Ammar ibn Yasir leading the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Hudhayfah driving him. He said to Hudhayfah: Who do you recognize from the people? He said: I do not recognize any of them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are so-and-so and so-and-so, until he counted them all. Hudhayfah said: Why don’t you send to them and kill them? He said: I hate for the Arabs to say that when he defeated his companions he came to kill them. Rather, God will suffice us against them with Al-Dabilah.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Isa told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Qais bin Ubadah, who said: We said to Ammar, “Have you seen your fighting? Have you seen it? For an opinion may be right or wrong, or is it a covenant that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made to you?” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not make a covenant with us that he did not make with all people. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In my nation - Shu’bah said, and I think he said: Hudhayfah told me, he said: In my nation - there are twelve hypocrites who will not enter Paradise, nor will they smell its fragrance, until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. Eight of them will be sufficient for them, a lamp of fire will appear on their shoulders until it emerges from their chests.”
9:65: 65- The Almighty said: And if you ask them, they will surely say, ‘We were only conversing and joking’ the verse. The reason for the revelation of this verse, according to what Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and Qatada said, is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was traveling on the Tabuk expedition, and before him were three hypocrites, two of whom were mocking the Qur’an and the Messenger, and the third was laughing. It was said: They used to say: Muhammad claims that he will defeat the Romans and conquer their cities. How far he is from that! It was said that they were saying: Muhammad claims that a Qur’an was revealed to our companions residing in Medina, but it is only his words and speech. So God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, and he said: Detain the caravan for me. So he called them and said to them: You said such and such. They said: We were only chatting and playing, meaning we were talking and chatting as caravans do to cut off the road by talking and playing. Omar said: I saw Abdullah bin Ubayy running in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and stones were hitting him, and he was saying: We were only joking and playing, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saying: By God, His verses, and His Messenger, you were mocking. He did not pay any attention to him and did not say anything more. God Almighty says: Say, meaning: Say, O Muhammad, Was it at God and His verses, His Book, and His Messenger that you were mocking?
9:66: 66- "Do not apologize. You have disbelieved after your belief." If it is said: How did he say: You have disbelieved after your belief, and they were not believers? It was said: Its meaning is: You showed disbelief after you showed faith. If We pardon a party of you, meaning: We forgive a party of you, and by party he meant one person, We punish with a noon and a kasra on the dhal, a party is in the accusative case. Others read: Ya’fe with a ya’ and a damma on the fa’, Ta’tha’be with a ta’ and a fatha on the dal, a party is in the nominative case without naming the subject. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: The one who was pardoned was one man, and he is Makhshi bin Himyar Al-Ashja’i. It is said that he repented from his hypocrisy and said: O God, I keep hearing a verse being recited to me that makes my skin shiver and my heart tremble. O God, make my death a killing in Your path, so that no one will say, I was washed, I was shrouded, I was buried. Then he was killed on the day of Yamamah, and there was no one among the Muslims who did not know his death except him.
9:67: 67- The Almighty said: The hypocrites, men and women, are of one another, meaning: they are of one religion. It was said: their command is one by uniting in hypocrisy, they enjoin what is wrong, polytheism and disobedience, and forbid what is right, meaning faith and obedience, and they withhold their hands, meaning: they hold them back from charity and spending in the way of God and do not extend them to do good, they forgot God, so He forgot them, they abandoned obeying God, so God forgave them from His success and guidance in this world, and from His mercy in the Hereafter, and He left them in His punishment, Indeed, the hypocrites are the wicked.
9:68: 68- "God has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. It is sufficient for them," sufficient as a punishment for their disbelief, and God has cursed them, distanced them from His mercy, and for them is a lasting punishment, eternal.
9:69: 69- Like those before you, meaning: you did as those before you did by deviating from the command of God, so you were cursed as they were cursed. They were stronger than you in power, in strength and strength, "and had more wealth and children. So they enjoyed their lot", so they enjoyed and benefited from their share of this world by following their desires and were satisfied with it instead of the Hereafter. So you enjoyed your lot, O disbelievers and hypocrites, just as those before you enjoyed their lot, and you followed their path, and you plunged into falsehood and lying about God Almighty, and denying His messengers, and mocking the believers, like those who plunged, meaning: just as they plunged. It was said: Like those who have waded, and that is because who is an incomplete noun, like what and whom that expresses one and all, similar to the Almighty’s saying: Like the one who kindled a fire, then He said: God has taken away their light Al-Baqarah 2:17. Their deeds have been in vain in this world and the Hereafter, and it is they who are the losers. That is, just as their deeds have been in vain and they have lost, so too will your deeds be in vain and you will lose. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz told us, Abu Omar Al-Sanaani from Yemen told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You will follow the ways of those before you, inch by inch and cubit by cubit, to the point that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would follow them. We said: O Messenger of God, the Jews and Christians? He said: Who else? And in the narration of Abu Hurairah: Are there any people other than them? And Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: “You are the most similar of the nations to the Children of Israel in appearance and guidance. You follow their actions step by step, except that I do not know whether you worship the calf or not.”
9:70: 70- The Almighty said: Did there not come to them, meaning the hypocrites, report, “of those before them,” when they disobeyed Our messengers and disobeyed Our command, how We punished them and destroyed them. Then He mentioned them, saying: The people of Noah, who were destroyed by the flood, and Aad, who were destroyed by the wind, and Thamud, by the earthquake, and the people of Abraham, by the loss of the blessing and the destruction of Nimrod, and the companions of Madyan, meaning the people of Shuaib, who were destroyed by the punishment of the Day of Shadow, and the overturned cities, the overturned cities that We turned upside down, and they were the people of Lot, their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they denied them and disobeyed them as you did, O group of disbelievers, so beware of hastening the punishment, and it was not God who would wrong them, but they wronged themselves.
9:71: 71- The Almighty said: And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another in religion, agreement of word, aid and support. They enjoin what is right in faith, obedience and goodness, and forbid what is wrong in polytheism and disobedience and what is not known in the Sharia, and establish prayer the obligatory prayer, “and give zakat and obey God and His Messenger. Those - God will have mercy upon them. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise.”
9:72: 72- God has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and good dwellings, good homes, in gardens of perpetual residence, meaning: gardens of perpetual residence and abode. It is said: he abode in a place if he resided in it. Ibn Masoud said: It is the middle of Paradise. Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas said: There is a palace in Paradise called Aden surrounded by towers and meadows. It has five thousand doors and none shall enter it except a prophet, a friend, or a martyr. Al-Hassan said: A palace of gold that no one can enter except a prophet, a friend, a martyr, or a just judge. Ata bin Al-Saib said: Aden is a river in Paradise, its gardens are on both its banks. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: Aden is the highest level in Paradise, and in it is the Spring of Tasnim, and the gardens are around it, surrounding it, and it has been covered from the time God Almighty created it until its people descend upon it: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, the righteous, and whoever God wills. In it are palaces of pearls, rubies, and gold, and a pleasant wind blows from beneath the Throne, and dunes of the most fragrant white musk enter upon them. And the pleasure of God is greater. That is, God’s pleasure with them is greater than that. That is the great attainment. We narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri may God be pleased with him that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “God the Almighty will say to the people of Paradise: ‘O people of Paradise, are you satisfied?’ They will say: ‘Our Lord, why should we not be satisfied when You have given us what You have not given to any of Your creation?’ He will say: ‘Shall I not give you something better than that?’ They will say: ‘Our Lord, what is better than that?’ He will say: ‘I will bestow My pleasure upon you, and I will never be angry with you after that.’”
9:73: 73- The Almighty said: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers: with the sword and killing, and the hypocrites, and they differed about the description of striving against the hypocrites, Ibn Masoud said: with his hand, and if he is unable to do so, then with his tongue, and if he is unable to do so, then with his heart, and he said: Do not meet the hypocrites except with a frowning face. Ibn Abbas said: with the tongue and abandoning kindness. Ad-Dahhak said: by harsh speech. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: by implementing the prescribed punishments on them. And be harsh upon them, and their refuge in the Hereafter, is Hell, and wretched is the destination. Ata' said: This verse abrogated everything about forgiveness and pardon.
9:74: 74- The Almighty said: They swear by God that they did not say it. Ibn Abbas said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the shade of a room and said: A man will come to you and look at you with the eyes of a devil. When he comes, do not speak to him. They did not wait long before a blue-eyed man appeared. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and said: Why are you cursing me, you and your companions? So the man went and came with his companions, and they swore by God that they did not say it. Then God Almighty revealed this verse." Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about Al-Jalas bin Suwaid. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon one day in Tabuk, in which he mentioned the hypocrites, called them filthy and criticized them. Al-Jalas said: If Muhammad is truthful, then we are worse than donkeys. Amir bin Qais heard him: Yes, Muhammad is truthful and you are worse than donkeys. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to Medina, Amir bin Qais came to him and told him what Al-Jalas had said. Al-Jalas said: He lied about me, O Messenger of God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to swear at the pulpit. Al-Jalas stood at the pulpit after the afternoon prayer and swore by God, there is no god but Him, that he had not said it, and Amir had lied about me. Then Amir stood and swore by God, there is no god but Him, that he had said it and I had not lied about him. Then he raised his hands to the sky and said: O God, send down upon Your Prophet confirmation of the truthful one among us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers said: Amen. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down before they parted with this verse, until he reached: If they repent, it will be better for them. Then Al-Jalas stood up and said: O Messenger of God, I hear that God Almighty has offered me repentance. Amer bin Qais was truthful in what he said. I said it and I seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him. So the Messenger of God accepted that from him and his repentance was good. God the Almighty said: And they have certainly said the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam, meaning: they showed disbelief after showing faith and Islam. It was said: It is cursing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: The word of disbelief is the saying of Al-Jalas: If Muhammad is truthful, then we are worse than donkeys. It was also said: The word of disbelief is their saying: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble, (al-Munafiqun 63:8). This story will come in its place in Surat Al-Munafiqun, And they intended that which they did not attain, Mujahid said: The hypocrites intended to kill the Muslim who heard them say: We are worse than donkeys, so that he would not spread it. It was said: They were twelve hypocrites who stood at the pass on the road to Tabuk to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came and ordered him to send someone to strike the faces of their camels, so he sent Hudhayfah for that purpose. Al-Saddī said: They said that when we arrived in Medina, we would place a crown on the head of Abdullah ibn Ubayy, so that they could reach it. And they did not resent them, and they did not hate or disapprove of them, except that God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. That is because the freed slave of Al-Jalas was killed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his blood money of twelve thousand dirhams, and he became independent. Al-Kalbi said: Before the arrival of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they were living in difficult circumstances, but when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them, they became independent with the spoils. If they repent from their hypocrisy and disbelief, “it will be better for them. But if they turn away,” turn away from faith, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world, with disgrace, and in the Hereafter, that is, in the Hereafter with the Fire, and they will have no protector or helper on earth.
9:75: 75-The Almighty said: And among them are those who made a covenant with God, ‘If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely give in charity’ verse. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah bin Hamid Al-Isfahani told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Samarqandi told us, Muhammad bin Nasr told us, Abu Al-Azhar Ahmad bin Al-Azhar told us, Marwan bin Muhammad bin Shu’aib told us, Ma’an bin Rafa’ah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili, who said: “Thalaba bin Hattab Al-Ansari came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to grant me wealth. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to you, Tha’laba, a little for which you can express your gratitude is better than a lot that you cannot bear. Then he came to him after that and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to grant me wealth. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you not see in the Messenger of God a good example? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if I wanted the mountains to move with me in gold and silver, they would move. Then he came to him after that and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to grant me wealth, for by the One Who sent you with the truth, if God grants me wealth, Money, so that I may give every person his due right. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, grant Tha’laba money.” He said: So he took sheep and they grew like worms, and the city became too small for him so he moved away from it and went down to one of its valleys and they grew like worms, and he used to pray with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the noon and afternoon prayers, and he used to pray with his sheep the rest of the prayers, then they multiplied and grew until he was far from the city, so he would only attend the Friday prayer, then they multiplied and grew and he also distanced himself until he would not attend the Friday prayer or the congregational prayer. So when it was Friday he would go out to meet the people and ask them about the report, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned him one day and said: What has happened to Tha`laba? They said: O Messenger of God, Tha`laba took sheep that no valley could hold, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to Tha`laba, woe to Tha`laba, woe to Tha`laba. Then God revealed the verse of charity, so the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) sent a man from Banu Sulaym and a man from Juhayna and wrote down for them the ages of charity, how they were to take it, and he said to them: Go to Tha'laba bin Hatib and so-and-so, a man from Banu Sulaym, and take their charity. So they went out until they came to Tha'laba and asked him for the charity and he read him the letter of the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him). He said: This is nothing but a tribute, this is nothing but a sister of the tribute. Go until you are done and then return to me. So they went and As-Salami heard them and looked at the best ages of his camel and set them aside for charity, then he faced them with it. When they saw it, they said: This is not upon you. He said: Take it, for my soul is content with that. So they went to the people and took the charity, then they returned to Tha'laba. He said: Show me your letter. So he read it and said: This is nothing but a sister of the tribute. Go until I see what I think. He said: So they came and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw them before they spoke to him. He said: Woe to Tha’laba, woe to Tha’laba. Then he prayed for good for Al-Salami, and they told him what Tha’laba had done. Then God Almighty revealed about him: And among them are those who made a covenant with God, ‘If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely give alms’ 10:13, until His saying: And because they used to lie. And with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a man from among Tha’laba’s relatives. He heard that, so he went out until he came to him and said, Woe to you, Tha'laba! God has revealed such and such about you. So Tha'laba went out until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him to accept his charity. He said, God the Almighty has prevented me from accepting your charity. So he began to throw dirt on his head. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, This is your work, and I ordered you but you did not obey me. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused to accept his charity, he returned to his home. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died. Then he came to Abu Bakr and said, Accept my charity. Abu Bakr said, "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not accept it from you, so how can I accept it?" Abu Bakr died and did not accept it. When 'Umar took over, he came to him and said, Accept my charity. He said, "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not accept it from you, so how can I accept it from you?" But he did not accept it. When 'Uthman took over, he came to him but he did not accept it from him, and Tha'laba died during the caliphate of 'Uthman. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, and Qatada said: He came to a gathering of the Ansar and made them testify that if God gives me from His bounty, I will give every person with a right his right, give charity from it, maintain family ties, and treat relatives well. Then his cousin died and left him money, but he did not fulfill what he said, so God Almighty revealed this verse. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: It was revealed about Tha’laba bin Hattab and Mu’tab bin Qushair, who were from Banu Amr bin Awf. They went out to a group of people and said: By God, if God gives us wealth, we will give in charity. But when God Almighty gave it to them, they were stingy with it. So God Almighty’s statement: And among them means the hypocrites, are those who made a covenant with God, ‘If He gives us from His bounty, we will give in charity’ and to fulfill God’s right from it. And we will be among the righteous, they do the work of the righteous in it, such as maintaining kinship ties and spending on charitable purposes.
9:76: 76- But when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it and turned away, averse.
9:77: 77- "He punished them, so He made them suffer, hypocrisy in their hearts", meaning: He was patient with the consequences of their hypocrisy. It is said: He punished someone with regret if he was patient with the consequences of that matter. It is also said: He punished them with the hypocrisy of their hearts. It is said: He punished him and He made him suffer have the same meaning. "Until the Day they meet Him, meaning He deprived them of repentance until the Day of Resurrection, because they broke their promise to God and because they used to lie". Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Abu Suhayl Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies, when he makes a promise, he breaks it, and when he is entrusted, he betrays.”
9:78: 78- The Almighty said: Do they not know that God knows their secrets and their private conversations? Meaning: what they conceal in their hearts and what they whisper among themselves, and that God is Knower of the unseen.
9:79: 79- The Almighty said: Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity the verse. The commentators said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged people to give charity. “Abdur-Rahman bin Awf came with four thousand dirhams and said: O Messenger of God, I have eight thousand. I have come to you with four thousand, so spend them in the way of God, and I have kept four thousand for my family. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God bless what you have given and what you have kept.” So God blessed his wealth to the point that he left behind two wives when he died, and the value of his wealth for them amounted to sixty thousand dirhams. On that day, Asim bin Adi Al-Ajlani gave charity with one hundred wasqs of dates. Abu Aqil Al-Ansari, whose name was Al-Habbab, came with a sa’ of dates and said: O Messenger of God, I spent the night carrying water in a jug until I got two sa’s of dates. I kept one of them for my family and brought you the other. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to scatter it in charity. The hypocrites criticized them and said: Abdur-Rahman and Asim gave only to show off, and God and His Messenger are independent of Abu Aqil’s sa’. But he wanted to be remembered for himself so that he could be given from charity. So God, the Almighty, revealed: Those who slander that is, criticize the volunteers “among the believers in giving charity” that is: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Asim. And those who find nothing but their effort that is: their energy, that is: Abu Aqil. Effort means energy, with the dammah in the language of Quraysh and the people of Hijaz. Al-A’raj read it with the fathah. Al-Qutaybi said: Effort with the dammah means energy and with the fathah means hardship. They mock them they ridicule them. God mocked them that is: God rewarded them for their mockery, and for them is a painful punishment.
9:80: 80- Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, its wording is a command, but its meaning is a statement, meaning: whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, God will not forgive them. If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them, and the number seventy is mentioned to exaggerate the despair of hoping for forgiveness. Ad-Dahhak said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has given me permission, so I will add to the seventy, perhaps God will forgive them. So God revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is the same to them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them - God will never forgive them. This is because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger, and God does not guide the wicked people.
9:81: 81- Those who stayed behind rejoiced about the Battle of Tabuk. The one who was left behind is the one who was left behind in their seat meaning in their sitting in opposition to the Messenger of God, Abu Ubaidah said: meaning after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: in opposition to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they set out and stayed, and they disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God and they said, Do not go forth in the heat, and the Battle of Tabuk was in intense heat, Say, 'The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood'", they know and this is how it is in the copy of Abdullah bin Masoud.
9:82: 82- So let them laugh a little in this world, and weep much in the Hereafter. Its meaning is: So let them laugh a little, then they will weep much, as recompense for what they used to earn. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Sayyid Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Alawi told us: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Husayn al-Sharqi told us, Abdullah ibn Hashim told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Anas, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much. Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Abi Tobah told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Harith told us, Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Yaqub Al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah bin Mahmoud told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Abdullah Al-Khalal told us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Imran bin Zaid Al-Tha’labi, Yazid Al-Raqashi told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “O people, cry, and if you cannot, then pretend to cry, for the people of Hell will cry in Hell until their tears run down their faces like streams, then the tears will stop, and blood will flow and the eyes will become sore, that if ships were to sail through them, they would sail.”
9:83: 83- The Almighty said: But if God returns you i.e., returns you, O Muhammad, from the Battle of Tabuk, to a party of them, meaning: of those who stayed behind. And He said: a party of them because not everyone who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk was a hypocrite, and they ask your permission to go out, with you on another battle, say, to them, You will never go out with me, on a journey, “nor will you fight with me an enemy. Indeed, you were satisfied to sit back the first time,” in the Battle of Tabuk, so sit with those who stayed behind, i.e., with the women and children, and it was said with the elderly and the sick. Ibn Abbas said: With those who stayed behind without an excuse. It was said: With the dissenters. Al-Farra’ said: It is said: a companion of dissent if he is a dissenter.
9:84: 84-"And never pray over any of them who dies" the verse. The commentators said: Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul was sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sick. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon him, he said to him: Has love for the Jews destroyed you? He said: O Messenger of God, I did not send you to rebuke me, I only sent you to ask forgiveness for me. He asked him to shroud him in his shirt and pray over him. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdul bin Abbas, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he said: “When Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul died, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was called to pray over him. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and went to him, I said: O Messenger of God, will you pray over Ibn Ubayy bin Salul when he said on such and such a day: such and such? I will count his words. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled and said: Leave me alone, Umar. When I repeated them, he said: I was given a choice and I chose. If I knew that if I increased the seventy, he would be forgiven, I would have increased them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him and then left. He did not stay long until the two verses of Bara’ah were revealed: “And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave,” up to His saying: And they are wicked. He said: I was amazed. After my audacity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that day, and God and His Messenger know best. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, Amr said: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: He put some of his saliva in his mouth and put his shirt on him. And God knows best. He had given Abbas a shirt. Sufyan said: Harun said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wearing two shirts, so Ibn Abdullah said: O Messenger of God, dress my father in the shirt that is closest to your skin. It was narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: When the day of Badr came, Al-Abbas was brought and he did not have a garment on him, so they found the shirt of Abdullah bin Ubayy that he could afford, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave it to him. For this reason, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took off the shirt that Abdullah had given him. Ibn Uyaynah said: He had done the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a favor and he wanted to reward him. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about what had been done to Abdullah bin Ubayy, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “My shirt and my prayers will not avail him at all. By God, I had hoped that a thousand of his people would become Muslim because of him.” It was narrated that a thousand of his people became Muslim because of him when they saw him seeking blessings from the shirt of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. His saying: And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave, nor stand over him, nor take charge of his burial, from their saying: So-and-so took charge of so-and-so’s affair: if he took care of his affair. They disbelieved in God and His Messenger and died while they were wicked, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pray over a hypocrite after that, nor did he stand at his grave until he died.
9:85: 85-The Almighty said: “And do not let their wealth and children impress you. God only intends to punish them through them in this world and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.”
9:86: 86- And when a surah is revealed, [saying], 'Believe in God and strive with His Messenger,' those of means among them ask your permission to remain, and they say, 'Leave us to be with those who remain,'" in their homes.
9:87: 87- They were content to be with the lowly and base people, meaning women. It was also said: with the lowest and most insignificant of people. It is said: So-and-so is the lowly person of his people if he is below them. And their hearts are sealed, so they do not understand.
9:88: 88- "But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their lives. And those will have all the good things," meaning: the good things. It was also said: the beautiful female slaves in Paradise. God Almighty said: In them are good and beautiful things, the plural of good. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The meaning of good is only known to God, as He, the Most High, said: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes (al-Sajdah 32:17). And those are the successful ones.
9:89: 89- "God has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. That is the great attainment."
9:90: 90- The Almighty said: And the excuse-makers came from among the desert Arabs so that permission might be given to them the verse, Yaqub and Mujahid read: the excuse-makers with a light pronunciation, and they are those who exaggerate in their excuse, it is said in the proverb: He who warned has been excused, meaning: He who gave the warning exaggerated in his excuse, and the others read the excuse-makers with a heavy pronunciation, meaning: those who are negligent, it is said: he excused, meaning: he fell short, and Al-Farra' said: The excuse-makers are the ones who apologize, the ta' was assimilated into the dhal and the movement of the ta' was transferred to the 'ayn. Ad-Dahhak said: “The people who are excused are the people of Amer bin At-Tufayl who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in defense of themselves and said: O Prophet of God, if we go out to war with you, the Bedouins of Tayy will attack our wives, children, and livestock. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: God has informed me of your report and God will suffice you.” Ibn Abbas said: They are those who stayed behind with an excuse, with the permission of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And those who denied God and His Messenger sat down, meaning: the hypocrites. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: Both groups were wrongdoers: some made up an excuse falsely, and they are the ones God Almighty meant in His saying: And the excuse-makers came, and some stayed behind without making an excuse, so they sat down out of audacity towards God Almighty, and they are the hypocrites, so God threatened them with His saying: A painful punishment will befall those of them who disbelieved, then He mentioned the people of excuse, and He, the Most High, said:
9:91: 91- "There is no blame upon the weak," Ibn Abbas said: meaning the elderly, the old, and the disabled. It was said: they are the children, and it was said: women, "nor upon the sick or upon those who do not find anything to spend, meaning the poor, no hardship," no sin. It was said: tightness in sitting back from fighting, "if they are sincere to God and His Messenger," in their absence and sincerely believe and work for God and pledge allegiance to the Messenger. "There is no way against the doers of good," meaning: by way of punishment, "and God is Forgiving and Merciful." Qatada said: It was revealed about Aaidh bin Amr and his companions. Ad-Dahhak said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Umm Maktum, who was blind.
9:92: 92- The Almighty’s saying: And there is no way for those who, when they come to you, that you may carry them, means: There is no way for the first ones or for those who came to you, and they are seven people called the weepers: Ma’qil ibn Yasar, Sakhr ibn Khansa’, Abdullah ibn Ka’b al-Ansari, Alba ibn Zayd al-Ansari, Salim ibn Umair, Tha’laba ibn Ghanima, and Abdullah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, God has urged us to go out with you, so carry us. They differed regarding his saying: to carry them. Ibn Abbas said: They asked him to carry them on the animals. It was said that they asked him to carry them on patched slippers and sewn sandals, so that they could go on a raid with him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not find anything to carry you on. They turned away, crying, and that is what God Almighty said: They turned away, their eyes overflowing with tears, grieved that they could not find anything to spend.
9:93: 93-The only way, by punishment, is against those who ask your permission, to stay behind, while they are rich and are content to be with those who stay behind, with the women and children, and God has set a seal upon their hearts so they do not know.
9:94: 94- They will apologize to you when you return to them. It is narrated that the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk were eighty-some people. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, they came to apologize falsely. God the Almighty said: "Say, 'Do not apologize. We will never believe you.'" We will not believe you. God has already informed us of your report, in what preceded, And God will see your work and so will His Messenger. In the new sentence, will you repent from your hypocrisy or will you persist in it? Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do.
9:95: 95- They will swear to you by God when you return to them, when you return to them from your invasion, to turn away from them, to overlook them and not reproach them, so turn away from them, so leave them and what they have chosen for themselves of hypocrisy, indeed they are unclean, impure, meaning: their work is ugly, and their refuge, in the Hereafter, is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Jadd bin Qais, Mu’tab bin Qushair, and their companions, who were eighty hypocrites. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Medina, he said: Do not sit with them or speak to them.
9:96: 96-And Muqatil said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubayy who swore to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by God, there is no god but Him, and he would not fail to do so after that, and he asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be pleased with him, so God Almighty revealed this verse, and revealed: “They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, then indeed, God is not pleased with the wicked people.”
9:97: 97-The Bedouins, meaning the Bedouins, are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy than the urbanites, and more deserving, more appropriate and more appropriate, not to know the limits of what God has revealed to His Messenger, due to their distance from hearing the Qur’an and knowing the Sunnahs, and God is Knowing, of what is in the hearts of His creation, Wise in what He has imposed of His obligations.
9:98: 98- And among the bedouins is he who regards what he spends as a loss. Ata' said: He does not expect a reward for giving it, nor does he fear punishment for withholding it, but rather he spends out of fear or hypocrisy. The loss is committing to what is not obligatory, and he waits, and waits for you the circles meaning: the vicissitudes of time, which sometimes bring good and sometimes bring evil. Yaman bin Rabab said: It means that time will turn against you, the Messenger will die and the polytheists will appear, upon them is the circle of evil "upon them" calamity and sorrow will revolve, and they will see in Muhammad and his religion only what will upset them.
