Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read: the circle of evil here and in Surat Al-Fath, with a damma on the seen, meaning: harm, affliction and misfortune. The others read with a fatha on the seen as a source. It was said: with a fatha it means apostasy and corruption, and with a damma it means harm and misfortune. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. It was revealed about the Bedouins of Asad, Ghatafan, and Tamim. Then He made an exception and said:
9:99: 99- And among the bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day. Mujahid said: They are Banu Muqrin from Muzaynah. Al-Kalbi said: Aslam, Ghifar, and Juhaynah. Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzar told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Dabry told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Aslam, Ghifar, and some of Juhayna and Muzaynah are better in the sight of God on the Day of Resurrection than Tamim, Asad bin Khuzaymah, Hawazin, and Ghatafan. “And he takes what he spends as means of drawing closer to God.” Qurrabaat is the plural of qurbah, meaning he seeks closeness to God Almighty. And the prayers of the Messenger, meaning his supplication and seeking forgiveness from him. Ata’ said: They desire the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Indeed, it is a means of drawing closer to them. Nafi’ read it with the narration of Warsh, qurbah with a damma on the ra’, and the rest read it with a sukoon. God will admit them into His mercy, into His Paradise. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
9:100: 100-"And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar" the verse. Jacob read it in the nominative case in apposition to his statement: "And the first forerunners". They differed about the first two predecessors. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Qatad, Ibn Sirin and a group said: They are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs. Ata bin Abi Rabah said: They are the people of Badr. Al-Sha’bi said: They are those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan, and the Pledge of Ridwan was at Al-Hudaybiyah. They differed about who was the first to believe in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after his wife Khadija, although they agreed that she was the first to believe in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them said: The first to believe and pray was Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and this is the opinion of Jabir. Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq said: He converted to Islam when he was ten years old. Some of them said: The first to believe after Khadija was Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Al-Sha’bi. Some of them said: The first to convert to Islam was Zaid bin Haritha, which is the opinion of Al-Zuhri and Urwah bin Al-Zubayr. Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Hanthali combined these sayings and said: The first man to convert to Islam was Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and the first woman to convert to Islam was Khadija, and the first boy to convert to Islam was Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and the first slave to convert to Islam was Zaid bin Haritha. Ibn Ishaq said: When Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, converted to Islam, he declared his conversion to God and His Messenger. He was a beloved, easy-going man, the most well-mannered of the Quraysh and the most knowledgeable about what was in it. He was a merchant of good character and well-known. The men of his people used to come to him and befriend him for more than one matter, because of his knowledge and good company. So he began to call to Islam whoever he trusted from his people, and they converted at his hands - in what is known. It was reported to me: Uthman ibn Affan, Az-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam, Abd Al-Rahman ibn Awf, Saad ibn Abi Waqqas, and Talhah ibn Ubaidullah. He brought them to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) when they responded to him, so they became Muslims and prayed. These eight were the first to embrace Islam. Then people followed one another in embracing Islam. As for the first Ansar, they were those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) on the night of Aqaba. They were six in the first Aqaba and seventy in the second. They were those who believed when Mus`ab ibn `Umair came to them to teach them the Qur’an. Many people became Muslims with him, as well as a group of women and children. The Almighty said: And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen who migrated from their people and clan and left their homelands. And the Ansar meaning: and among the Ansar, who are those who supported the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, against his enemies from the people of Medina and sheltered his companions, and those who followed them with good conduct. It was said: They are the rest of the Muhajireen and the Ansar, apart from/ the first forerunners. It was said: They are those who followed their path in faith, migration, or support until the Day of Resurrection. Ata said: They are the ones who remember the Muhajireen and Ansar with mercy and supplication. Abu Sakhr Hamid bin Ziyad said: I came to Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi and said to him: What do you say about the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: All the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are in Paradise, the good and the bad. I said: How do you say this? He said: O man, read the words of God the Most High: And the first forerunners [in Islam] among the Muhajireen and the Ansar until he said: God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. And He said: And those who followed them with good, a condition for the followers, which is that they follow them in their good deeds and not their bad ones. Abu Sakhr said: It is as if I have never read this verse. We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not curse my companions, for by the One in Whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend the equivalent of Mount Uhud in gold, it would not equal one of their handfuls or even half of it. Then God Almighty gathered them together in the reward and said: God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow. Ibn Kathir read: underneath which rivers flow. And it is also in the Qur’ans of the people of Mecca: “They will abide therein forever. That is the great attainment.”
9:101: God the Almighty said: And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites, and they are from Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ashja', Aslam and Ghifar, whose homes were around Medina. He says: Among these bedouins are hypocrites, And among the people of Medina, meaning: Among the people of Medina from Aws and Khazraj are hypocrites, They are accustomed to hypocrisy, meaning: They are accustomed to hypocrisy. It is said: So-and-so rebelled against his Lord, meaning: He rebelled and persisted in disobeying Him. That is, he was accustomed to it, persisted in it and became accustomed to it. And from this: the one who desires and the one who rebels. Ibn Ishaq said: They persisted in it and refused to do anything else. Ibn Zayd said: They stayed with him and did not repent. You do not teach them, you, Muhammad, “We teach them. We will punish them twice.” They differed about these two punishments. Al-Kalbi and Al-Suddi said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up as a preacher on Friday and said: ‘Go out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite. Go out, so-and-so.’ He expelled people from the mosque and disgraced them. This is the first punishment. The second is the punishment of the grave.” Mujahed said: The first: killing and captivity, and the second: the torment of the grave. And from him another narration: They were tormented with hunger twice. Qatada said: The torment in this world and the punishment of the grave. Ibn Zayd said: The first is the calamities in wealth and children in this world, and the other is the torment of the afterlife. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: The first is to impose punishments on them, and the other is the torment of the grave. Ibn Ishaq said: It is the anger of Islam that befalls them and their entering into it without any regard for it, then the torment of the grave. It was said: One of them is the angels striking their faces and backs when they take their souls, and the other is the torment of the grave. It was said that the first was to burn their mosque, the mosque of harm, and the other was to burn them in the fire of Hell. Then they will be returned to a great punishment, meaning: to the punishment of Hell, where they will remain forever.
9:102: 102- The Almighty said: And others, meaning: and from the people of Medina, or: from the Bedouins others, and this does not refer to the hypocrites, confessed, acknowledged, their sins, they mixed a righteous deed, which is their acknowledgment of their sins and their repentance, and another evil, meaning: with another evil deed, the waw was placed in place of the ba, as it is said: I mixed water and milk, meaning: with milk. The bad deed: is their failure to follow the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the good deed: is their remorse and tying themselves to the masts. It was said: their battles with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. “Perhaps God will accept their repentance. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” This verse was revealed about a group of people who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. Then they regretted that and said: We will be in the shade with the women, while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions are in jihad and warfare! When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, approached Medina, they said: By God, we will tie ourselves to the pillars and not release them until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the one who releases them and excuses us. So they tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, he passed by them and saw them and said: Who are these? They said: These are the ones who stayed behind from you, so they pledged to God, the Almighty, that they would not release themselves until you release them and are pleased with them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I swear by God that I will not release them nor excuse them until I am ordered to release them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the battle with the Muslims! So God revealed this verse and sent to them the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who released them and excused them. When they were released, they said: O The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is our money that we have left behind, so give it in charity, purify us, and ask forgiveness for us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was not commanded to take anything from your money. Then God Almighty revealed: Take alms from their money verse. They differed regarding the number of those who repented. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: They were ten, including Abu Lubabah. Atiyah narrated on his authority: They were five, one of whom was Abu Lubabah. Saeed bin Jubair and Zaid bin Aslam said: They were eight. Ad-Dahhak and Qatada said: They were seven. They all said: One of them was Abu Lubabah. Some people said: It was revealed about Abu Lubaba specifically. They differed about his sin. Mujahid said: It was revealed about Abu Lubaba when he said to Qurayza: If you accept his ruling, then it is slaughter, and he pointed to his throat. Al-Zuhri said: It was revealed about his failure to participate in the Battle of Tabuk, so he tied himself to a pole and said: By God, I will not absolve myself nor taste food or drink until I die or God accepts my repentance! So he remained for seven days without tasting food or drink until he fell unconscious. Then God Almighty revealed this verse, and it was said to him: You have accepted your repentance! He said: By God, I will not absolve myself until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the one who absolves me. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and absolved him with his hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: O Messenger of God, part of my repentance is that I leave the home of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I give up all of my wealth as charity to God and His Messenger. He said: A third will suffice you, O Abu Lubabah. They all said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a third of their money and left two-thirds, because God Almighty said: Take from their money, and did not say: Take their money. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: These are in addition to the three who were left behind.
9:103: 103- The Almighty said: Take from their wealth a charity in order to purify them, from their sins, and sanctify them thereby, meaning: raise them from the ranks of the hypocrites to the ranks of the sincere. It was said: increase their wealth and pray for them, meaning: pray for them and ask forgiveness for them. It was said: it is the saying of the one who seeks [the charity] when he takes charity from him: May God reward you for what you have given and bless you in what you have left. Prayer in the language: supplication. Indeed, your prayer Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read: / your prayer on the singular and the accusative of the ta' here, and in Surah Hud your prayers and in Surah Al-Mu'minun on their prayer [all on the singular], Hafs agreed with them here and in Surah Hud. The others read it in the plural and break the ta' here. “Peace be upon them,” meaning: your supplication is a mercy for them. This was said by Ibn Abbas. It was also said: reassurance and tranquility for them, that God Almighty has accepted from them. Abu Ubaidah said: steadfastness for their hearts. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. They differed about the obligation of supplication for the imam when taking alms: Some of them said: It is obligatory. Some of them said: It is recommended. Some of them said: It is obligatory in obligatory alms and recommended in voluntary alms. It was said: It is obligatory for the imam and recommended for the poor to supplicate for the giver. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam bin Abi Iyas told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Abi Awfa - who was one of the people of the tree - say: “Whenever his people came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with charity, he would say: O God, bless them. My father came to him with his charity and he said: O God, bless the family of Abi Awfa.” Ibn Kaysan said: This is not about the obligatory charity, but rather it is about the charity of expiation for an oath. Ikrimah said: It is the obligatory charity. When the repentance of these people was revealed, those who did not repent from those who stayed behind said: These people were with us yesterday, they did not [speak] or sit with us, so what is wrong with them? Then God Almighty said: Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities?
9:104: 104- Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities? That is, He accepts them, and that God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Yaqub Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi bin Sulaiman told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard Abu Al-Qasim, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, say: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no servant gives charity from lawful earnings – and God does not accept anything but what is lawful, and nothing ascends to the heaven but what is lawful – except that he is placing it in the hand of the Most Merciful, the Almighty, who raises it for him as one of you raises his foal, until the morsel of food will come on the Day of Resurrection and it will be like a huge mountain. Then he recited: ‘Indeed, it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities.’”
9:105: 105- The Almighty said: “And say, ‘Work, and God will see your work, and [so will] His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.’” Mujahid said: This is a threat to them. It was said: Seeing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is by God Almighty informing him, and seeing the believers is by instilling love in their hearts for the righteous and hatred for the corrupt.
9:106: 106- The Almighty said: "And others are deferred for the command of God, whether He will punish them or forgive them. And God is Knowing and Wise." The people of Medina and Kufa, except for Abu Bakr, read marjūn without a hamza, and the others: with a hamza, and postponement means delay, marjūn: postponed. For the command of God: for the judgment of God the Almighty regarding them, and they are the three whose story will come later: Ka'b bin Malik, Hilal bin Umayya, and Murarah bin Ar-Rabi', they did not exaggerate in repentance and apology as Abu Lubabah did, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped them for fifty nights and forbade people from speaking to them and mixing with them, until anxiety split them and the earth became narrow for them despite its vastness, and they were from the people of Badr, so some people began to say: They are lost, and others said: Perhaps God will forgive them, so they became deferring for the command of God [not knowing] whether He will punish them or have mercy on them, until their repentance was revealed after fifty nights.
9:107: 107- The Almighty said: And those who took, the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read those without the waw, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an, and the others read: and those with the waw. A mosque of harm. This verse was revealed about a group of hypocrites who built a mosque to harm the mosque of Quba. They were twelve hypocrites: Wadi’ah ibn Thabit, Judham ibn Khalid, from whose house this mosque was removed, Tha’laba ibn Hatib, Jariyah ibn Amir, his two sons Mujammi’ and Zayd, Mu’tab ibn Qushayr, ‘Abbad ibn Hanif, the brother of Sahl ibn Hanif, Abu Habeeba ibn al-Az’ar, Nabtal ibn al-Harith, Bajad ibn ‘Uthman, and a man called Bahzaj. They built this mosque to harm, meaning to harm the believers, and disbelief in God and His Messenger, and to cause division among the believers, because they all prayed in the mosque of Quba. So they built the mosque of harm so that some of them could pray in it, which would lead to disagreement and division of opinion. Mujammi’ ibn Jariyah was leading them in prayer. When they had finished building it, they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was preparing to go to Tabuk. They said: O Messenger, we have built a mosque for those who are sick and in need, and for the rainy night and the winter night, and we would like you to come to us and pray with us in it and ask God to bless us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I am on a journey, and if we come back, God willing, we will come to you and pray for you in it. “And as a watch for those who fought God and His Messenger before,” meaning: waiting and preparing for those who fought God and His Messenger. It is said: I prepared for him: if I prepared for him. He is Abu Amir the monk, and this Abu Amir was a man from them, and he is Abu Hanzala, the one washed by the angels, and he had become a monk in the pre-Islamic era and converted to Christianity and wore hair-sackcloth, “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, Abu Amir said to him: What is this that you have brought? He said: I have brought the Hanafi religion, the religion of Abraham. Abu Amir said: We are upon it, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are not upon it, he said: Yes, but you have introduced into the Hanafi religion what is not from it, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I did not do it, but I brought it white and pure, so Abu Amir said: May God kill the liar among us, banished, alone and a stranger, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Amen. And he called him Abu Amir the immoral.” When the day of Uhud came, Abu Amir said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will not find a people who will fight you except that I will fight you with them. He continued to fight him until the day of Hunayn. When Hawazin was defeated, he despaired and fled to the Levant. He sent word to the hypocrites that they should prepare whatever force and weapons they could, and build me a mosque, for I am going to Caesar, the king of the Romans, and bring an army of the Romans. So he sent Muhammad and his companions out, and they built the Mosque of Harm next to the Mosque of Quba. This is what God Almighty said: And as an ambush for him who wages war against God and His Messenger, and he was Abu Amir the wicked, so that he would pray in it when he returned from the Levant. His saying: before refers to Abu Amir, meaning he fought God and His Messenger before, that is, before the construction of the Mosque of Harm. And let them swear, ‘If We intended’, what We intended by building it, except good, except the good deed, which is kindness to the Muslims and generosity towards the weak and unable to travel to the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. "And God bears witness that they are liars," in their saying and oaths. It was narrated that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Tabuk and settled in Dhi Awan, a place near Medina, they came to him and asked him to come to their mosque. He called for his shirt to wear and come to them. Then the Qur’an was revealed to him and God, the Most High, informed him of the story of the Mosque of Harm and what they intended to do. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Malik ibn Ad-Dakhshum, Ma’n ibn Adi, Amir ibn As-Sakn, and Wahshi, the killer of Hamza, and said to them: Go to this mosque whose people are oppressors, demolish it and burn it. So they quickly went out until they reached Banu Salim ibn Awf, who were the people of Malik ibn Ad-Dakhshum. Malik said: Wait for me until I bring you fire from my people. So his people went in and he took a palm frond and set it on fire. Then they went out quickly until they entered the mosque and its people were in it. They burned it and demolished it, and its people dispersed from it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that it be used as a rubbish bin to throw in it the carcasses, stench, and garbage. Abu Amer the monk died in the Levant, alone, unique and strange. It was narrated that the Banu Amr ibn Awf, who built the Quba Mosque, came to Umar ibn al-Khattab during his caliphate to ask for permission for Mujammi ibn Haritha to lead them in their mosque. He said: No, nor even the blessing of the eye. Is he not the imam of the Mosque of Harm? Mujammi said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, do not rush me, for by God I prayed in it without knowing what they were hiding behind it. If I had known, I would not have prayed with them in it. I was a young boy who read the Qur’an, and they were old men who did not read the Qur’an. I prayed, thinking only that they were seeking to draw closer to God Almighty, and I did not know what was in their hearts. Umar excused him, believed him, and ordered him to pray in the Quba Mosque. Ata’ said: When Omar conquered the cities, he ordered the Muslims to build mosques, and he ordered them not to build two mosques in their city, one of which would harm the other.
9:108: 108- The Almighty said: Never stand therein, Ibn Abbas said: Do not pray therein. God the Almighty forbade His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from praying in the Mosque of Harm. For a mosque founded on righteousness, the lam is the lam of initiation. It was said: the lam of the oath, meaning: By God, a mosque founded, meaning: its foundation was built on righteousness, from the first day, meaning: from the first day it was built and its foundation was laid, is more worthy for you to stand therein, praying. They quarreled in the mosque that was founded on piety. Ibn Omar, Zaid bin Thabit, and Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said: It is the mosque of Medina, the mosque of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. The evidence for that is: Ismail bin Abdul Qahir informed us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad informed us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi informed us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan informed us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj informed us, Muhammad bin Hatim informed us, Yahya bin Saeed informed us, on the authority of Hamid Al-Kharrat, who said: I heard Abu Salamah Abdul Rahman say: Abdul Rahman bin Abi Saeed passed by me, so I said to him: How did you hear your father mention the mosque that was founded on piety? He said: My father said: “I entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the house of one of his wives and I said: O Messenger of God, which of the two mosques was founded on piety? He said: So he took a handful of pebbles and threw them on the ground, then he said: It is this mosque of yours, the mosque of Madinah. I said: I bear witness that I heard your father mention it thus.” Abu al-Hasan al-Shirazi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi informed us, Abu Musab informed us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Khabib ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Hafs ibn Asim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is over my pond. Some people said that it is the Quba Mosque, and this is the narration of Atiyah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is the saying of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Saeed ibn Jubayr, and Qatadah: Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to come to the Quba Mosque every Saturday, walking and riding, and Abdullah bin Omar used to do the same. Nafi’ added on the authority of Ibn Omar on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he should pray two rak’ahs in it. God Almighty says: In it are men who love to purify themselves, from ritual impurity, major ritual impurity, and copper. Ata’ said: They used to clean themselves with water and not sleep at night in a state of ritual impurity. Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani told us, Abu Umar al-Qasim ibn Ja`far ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Hashemi told us, Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Amr al-Lu’lu’i told us, Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash`ath al-Sijistani told us, Muhammad ibn al-`Alaa told us, Mu`awiyah ibn Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Maymunah, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “This verse was revealed about the people of Quba’: ‘In it are men who love to purify themselves. ’ He said: ‘They used to clean themselves with water, so this verse was revealed about them. ’And God loves those who purify themselves. ’ That is, those who purify themselves.”
9:109: 109- Is he who founded his building? Nafi' and Ibn Amir read asas with a damma on the hamza and a kasra on the seen, bianayahu in both of them is raised without naming the subject. The others read asas with a fatha on the hamza and the seen, bianayahu: with a nasb on the noon, naming the subject. On piety from God and the pleasure of God is better, meaning: on seeking piety and the pleasure of God Almighty is better Or he who founded his building on the brink: on the brink, a cliff? Abu Amr, Hamza and Abu Bakr read jarf with a sukoon on the ra', and the rest read with a damma on the ra' and they are two dialects, and it is a well that has not been covered. Abu Ubaidah said: It is the abyss and what the flood sweeps away from the valleys and is swept away by the water and remains weak, har, meaning: ha'ir and it is the falling one. It is said: ha'ir yahur so he is ha'ir, then it is reversed and it is said: ha'ir like shak and sha'ik and 'aq and 'aaq. It was said: It is from the word yahar which means to collapse, and its meaning is: the fallen thing that collapses one after the other, as sand and soft things collapse. It collapsed with it, meaning: it fell with the builder into the fire of Hell, meaning that building this harmful mosque is like building on the edge of Hell, so it collapses with its people in it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He means that hypocrisy led them to the Fire. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. Qatada said: By God, he did not stop until he fell into the fire. He told us that a spot was dug in it, and smoke was seen coming out of it. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: I saw smoke coming out of the Mosque of Harm.
9:110: 110- Their structure which they built will remain a source of doubt, meaning: suspicion and hypocrisy, in their hearts, they think that they were doing good in building it, just as the people of Moses loved the calf. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said. Al-Kalbi said: Regret and remorse because they regretted building it. Al-Suddi said: The demolition of their structure will remain a source of doubt, resentment and anger in their hearts. Unless their hearts are cut off, meaning: their hearts are cracked and they die. Ibn ‘Amir, Abu Ja’far, Hamza, and Hafs read: taqta’ with a fatha on the ta’, meaning: it is cut off. The others read it with a damma. Ya’qub alone read: (to an) light, extremely, taqta’ with a damma on the ta’, light, from cutting, as indicated by the interpretation of Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah: They will not cease to be in doubt about it until they die and then become certain. And God is Knowing and Wise.
9:111: 111- The Almighty said: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties the verse. Muhammad bin Ka'b Al-Qurazi said: "When the Ansar pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of Al-Aqabah/ in Mecca, and they were seventy people, Abdullah bin Rawahah said: O Messenger of God, stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish. He said: I stipulate for my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and I stipulate for myself, that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your properties from. They said: If we do that, what will we have? He said: Paradise. They said: The profit of the sale, we do not take it off nor do we resign. So the verse was revealed: "Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise." Al-A'mash read: "in Paradise." They fight in the cause of God, killing and being killed. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read they are killed by placing the object before the subject, meaning that some of them kill each other, and the rest are killed. The others read it by placing the subject before the object. A true promise meaning: the reward of Paradise is a promise and a truth for them in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an. That is, God the Almighty promised them this promise and explained it in these books. It was said that it is evidence that all people of religions were commanded to fight for the reward of Paradise. Then He congratulated them and said: And who is more faithful to his covenant than God? So rejoice, so be happy in your transaction which you have contracted, and that is what is the great attainment. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: God the Almighty has pledged allegiance to you and made both transactions yours. Qatada said: God Almighty is the eighth of them, so He made it more expensive for them. Al-Hasan said: Listen to the profitable pledge that God has made to every believer. And it was narrated that he said: God has given you the world, so buy Paradise with some of it.
9:112: 112- Then he described them and said: The repentant ones. Al-Farra' said: It was resumed in the nominative case because the verse was complete and the speech had stopped. Al-Zajjaj said: The repentant ones are in the nominative case because of the beginning and its predicate is implied. The meaning is: The repentant ones - until the end of the verse - will also have Paradise. That is: whoever did not fight in jihad, neither stubbornly nor intending to abandon jihad, because some Muslims suffice for others in jihad, [so whoever has this description] will also have Paradise. This is better, as if he promised Paradise to all believers, as he said: And to each of them God has promised good (An-Nisa': 95). So whoever made it subordinate to the first, the promise of Paradise was specific to the mujahideen described with this description. The Almighty says: Those who repent meaning: those who repented from polytheism and absolved themselves from hypocrisy, those who worship meaning: those who are obedient and sincere in their worship of God Almighty, those who praise meaning: those who praise God in every situation, in good times and bad. We narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The first to be called to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection are those who praise God in prosperity and adversity. “The travelers,” Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: They are the fasting ones. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: The fasting person is called a traveler because he abstains from all pleasures, including food, drink, and sexual intercourse. Ata’ said: The travelers are the warriors who fight in the way of God. It was narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Maz’un, may God be pleased with him, that he said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to travel. He said: The travel of my nation is jihad in the way of God. “Those who bow and prostrate,” meaning: those who pray, those who enjoin what is right, through faith, and forbid what is wrong, through polytheism. It was said: what is right is the Sunnah and what is wrong is innovation. And those who preserve the limits set by God, those who carry out the commands of God. Al-Hasan said: those who are loyal to their pledge to God. And give good tidings to the believers.
9:113: 113- It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists. They differed about the reason for the revelation of this verse. Some people said: The reason for its revelation: What Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me, on the authority of his father, he said: When the death of Abu Talib was approaching, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and found Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Abi Umayya bin Al-Mughirah with him. He said: O uncle, say: There is no god but God, a word with which I will argue for you before God. Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Umayya said: Do you reject the religion of Abdul Muttalib? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept presenting it to him and they kept repeating that statement until Abu Talib said the last thing he said to them: On the religion of Abdul Muttalib, and he refused to say: There is no god but God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, I will seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so. Then God revealed: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire. And He revealed about Abu Talib: You do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Hatim bin Maimun told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Yazid bin Kaysan told us, Abu Hazim Al-Ashja’i told me, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God said to his uncle: “Say: ‘There is no god but God,’ and I will bear witness to it for you on the Day of Resurrection.” He said: “Were it not that the Quraysh would taunt me and say: ‘He was only driven to do that out of impatience,’ I would have made you happy with it.” Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but God guides whom He wills. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us [Abdullah bin Yusuf told us] Al-Layth told me, Yazid bin Al-Haad told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Khabab, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention his uncle in his presence and say: Perhaps my intercession will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be placed in a shallow part of the Fire that reaches his ankles, and his brain will boil from it. Abu Hurairah and Buraidah said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Mecca, he came to the grave of his mother Amina and stood over it until the sun became hot, hoping that he would be given permission to seek forgiveness for her. Then the verse was revealed: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists 1:13. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Yazid Kaysan, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited his mother’s grave and he wept and made those around him weep. He said: ‘I asked permission from my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, to seek forgiveness for her, but He did not give me permission. I asked permission to visit her grave, and He gave me permission. So visit graves, for they remind you of death.’” Qatada said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will seek forgiveness for my father, just as Abraham sought forgiveness for his father. Then God Almighty revealed this verse: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: When God Almighty revealed the report about Abraham, peace be upon him, he said to his father: “Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord.” I heard a man asking forgiveness for his parents, even though they were polytheists, so I said to him: You ask forgiveness for them, even though they were polytheists? He said: Did Abraham not ask forgiveness for his father? So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so God Almighty revealed: Indeed, in Abraham you have an excellent example to follow, until His saying: Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, ‘I will surely ask forgiveness for you’ Al-Mumtahanah 4.
19:47: 114- The Almighty said: And Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. Some of them said: The ha in him refers back to Abraham, peace be upon him. And the promise was from his father, because his father had promised him that he would convert to Islam, so Abraham said to him, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, meaning if you convert to Islam. Some of them said that the letter ha’ refers to the father, because Abraham promised his father that he would ask forgiveness for him in the hope that he would convert to Islam. This is his saying: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. This is indicated by the reading of al-Hasan: He promised her his father, with the unified ba’. The evidence that the promise was from Abraham, and that the repentance was in the case of the father’s polytheism, is the Almighty’s saying: There has certainly been for you a good example in Abraham, until He said: Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, ‘I will surely ask forgiveness for you’ Al-Mumtahanah 4. So He made it clear that Abraham was not a model in this repentance, but rather he asked forgiveness for him while he was a polytheist because of the promise, hoping that he would become Muslim. So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, because he died in disbelief, he disavowed him. It was said: So when it became clear to him in the Hereafter that he was an enemy of God, he disavowed him, meaning: he disavowed him, and that is what: Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ismail bin Abdullah told us, my brother Abdul Hamid told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Tha’lab, on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Abraham will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and on Azar’s face will be dark and dusty. Abraham will say to him: Did I not tell you not to disobey me? His father will say to him: Today I will not disobey you. Abraham, peace be upon him, will say: O my Lord, you promised me that you would not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection, so what disgrace is greater than my father’s being further away? God Almighty will say: I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers. Then it will be said: O Abraham, what is beneath your feet? He will look and see a slaughtered animal covered in blood. He will be seized by its legs and thrown into the Fire.” In another narration: He will disown him on that day. God Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing. They differed regarding the meaning of most compassionate. It was stated in the hadith: Indeed, most compassionate is the humble and supplicant. Abdullah bin Masoud said: The supplication is the piety. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He is the repentant believer. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: The most compassionate is the most merciful to the servants of God. Mujahed said: The one who is steadfast is the one who is certain. Akrima said: It is the certainty in the language of Abyssinia. Kaab Al-Ahbar said: He is the one who groans a lot. Abraham, peace be upon him, used to say a lot: Ah from the fire, before ah was of no use. It was said: He is the one who groans from sins. Uqba bin Aamer said: The one who is afflicted with remembrance of God Almighty a lot. On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: Al-Wah is the one who praises. It was narrated on his authority: Al-Wah is the one who teaches good. Al-Nakha’i said: He is the jurist. Ata' said: He is the one who turns away from everything that God hates. He also said: He is the one who fears Hell. Abu Ubaidah said: He is the one who groans with compassion and fear, and who beseeches with certainty. He means that his beseeching should be certain and necessary for obedience. Al-Zajjaj said: Abu Ubaidah’s statement contains most of what has been said about the groaner. Its origin: from groaning, which is when the chest hears the sound of someone breathing heavily, and the verb from it is oh and groan, and the forbearing is forgiving of whoever insults him or harms him, as he said to his father, when he threatened him, and his saying: If you do not desist, I will stone you, so leave me for a long time. He said, “Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord.” Maryam - 46 On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, he said: The forbearing is the master. 47 - He said Ibrahim "Peace be upon you", meaning: You are safe from me, I will not afflict you with harm, and that is because he was not commanded to fight him because of his disbelief. It was said: This is a greeting of abandonment and separation. It was also said: A greeting of kindness and gentleness, and it is the response of the forbearing person to the foolish. God Almighty said: “And when the ignorant address them, they say, ‘Peace.’” (al-Furqan 25:63) The Almighty said: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. It was said that when he was exhausted by his matter and his promise to turn to God about it, he asked Him to grant him monotheism and forgive him. Its meaning is: I will ask God Almighty for you to repent so that you may attain forgiveness. He was ever kind to me, kind and gentle. Al-Kalbi said: A scholar who would answer me when I called upon him. Mujahid said: He accustomed me to answering my prayers.
9:115: 115- The Almighty said: And God would not misguide a people after He had guided them the verse. Its meaning is: God would not have judged you to be misguided by abandoning the commands to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, until He makes clear to them what they should avoid, meaning until He presents to you the prohibition, so if it becomes clear and you do not follow it, then at that point you deserve to be misguided. Mujahid said: God’s statement to the believers regarding not seeking forgiveness for the polytheists in particular, and His statement to them regarding His disobedience and obedience in general, so do it or leave it. Ad-Dahhak said: God would not punish a people until He made clear to them what they do and what they leave behind. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: This is about the abrogated verses, and that is because some people came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they converted to Islam, and alcohol was not forbidden, and the qiblah was not turned towards the Kaaba, so they returned to their people and they were in that state, then alcohol was forbidden and the qiblah was turned, and they had no knowledge of that, then after that they came to Madinah and found that alcohol had been forbidden and the qiblah had been turned, so they said: O Messenger of God, you were of one religion and we are of another, so we are astray? So God Almighty revealed: And God would not lead a people astray after He has guided them, meaning: God would not invalidate the work of a people who knew of the abrogated verse until the abrogating verse was made clear to them. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things, then He glorified Himself and said:
9:116: 116-Indeed, to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He rules as He wills. He gives life and causes death, and you have not besides God any protector or helper.
9:117: 117- The Almighty said: God has indeed accepted the repentance of the Prophet the verse, God accepted repentance means: He overlooked and pardoned. The meaning of His repentance of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is His permission for the hypocrites to stay behind him. It was said: He opened the speech with it because it was the reason for their repentance, so He mentioned it with them, like the Almighty's saying: Then a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger Al-Anfal - 41, and similar to it. And the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship, meaning: in the time of hardship, and He did not mention a specific hour, and the Battle of Tabuk was called the Battle of Hardship, and the army was called the Army of Hardship. Hardship means severity, and it was a battle of hardship for them in terms of their noon, provisions, and water. Al-Hasan said: The ten of them would go out on one camel, following one another. A man would ride for a while, then get off and his companion would ride likewise. Their provisions were rotten dates and spoiled barley. The group of them would go out with nothing but dates between them. If one of them felt hungry, he would take a date and chew it until he could taste it, then give it to his companion, who would suck it and drink a sip of water with it, and so on until the last of them had passed, and nothing remained of the date except the seed. So they went with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Tabuk, with their truthfulness and certainty. Omar ibn al-Khattab said: “We went out with the Prophet (peace be upon him) to Tabuk in intense heat. We stopped at a place where we were so thirsty that we thought our necks would break. A man would slaughter his camel, squeeze its dung and drink it, putting what was left on his liver. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: ‘O Messenger of God, God has accustomed you to good in supplication, so supplicate to God for us. ’ He said: ‘Do you like that? ’ Say: ‘Yes. ’ So he raised his hands and did not bring them back until the sky said: ‘It shaded, then it poured out, and they filled what they had with them. Then we went and did not find it had passed the army. ’ ‘After it almost deviated. ’ Hamza and Hafs read: ‘Yazigh’ with a ‘ya’ because of the word ‘almost’ and did not say: ‘almost’. The others read it with a ‘ta’. Deviation means inclination, i.e. after it almost deviated. ‘The hearts of a group of them’ means the hearts of some of them. He did not mean inclination away from the religion, but rather inclination towards falling behind and turning away due to the hardship that was upon them. Al-Kalbi said: They are people who were backward and then caught up with him. “Then He accepted their repentance.” If it is said: How did He repeat the mention of repentance when He said at the beginning of the verse: God has accepted the repentance of the Prophet? It was said: Repentance was mentioned at the beginning of the verse before mentioning the sin, and it is pure grace from God Almighty. Then when he mentioned the sin, he repeated repentance, and what is meant by that is its acceptance. He is Most Kind and Most Merciful to them. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever God accepts his repentance, He will never punish him. The Almighty said: And concerning the three who were left behind, meaning they were left behind from the Battle of Tabuk. It was said: they were left behind, meaning their matter was postponed, due to the repentance of Abu Lubaba and his companions. These three are: Ka’b ibn Malik the poet, Murarah ibn al-Rabi’, and Hilal ibn Umayya, all of them from the Ansar. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik, that Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik - who was the leader of Kaab from his sons when he went blind - said: “I heard Kaab bin Malik narrating when he stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk. Kaab said: I never stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in any battle he fought except the Battle of Tabuk, except for the Battle of Badr, and he did not reproach anyone who stayed behind from it. Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out seeking the caravan of Quraysh until God gathered them and their enemy without an appointment. I witnessed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the night of Al-Aqabah when we pledged to Islam, and I would not have liked to have the battle of Badr in it, even though Badr was more famous among the people than it. And from my experience, I was never stronger or more comfortable when I stayed behind from him in that battle.” The raiders, by God, I never had two camels together before that, until I gathered them in that raid, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not want to raid except that he followed it with another, until that raid, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raided it in intense heat and faced a long journey and a great victory and many enemies, so he explained their matter to the Muslims so that they would prepare for their raid, so he informed them of the direction he wanted, and the Muslims with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were many, and they were not gathered by a memorizing book - meaning the diwan - Kaab said: There is no man who wanted to be absent except that he thought that it would be hidden from him unless a revelation was sent down from God, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raided that raid when the fruits and shade were good, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prepared himself and the Muslims with him, so I began to go out in order to prepare with them, and I would return and I had not completed anything, and I would say to myself: I am able to do it if I wish, so the matter continued with me until the people became serious, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims with him, and I had finished some of my preparations, so I said: I will get ready after a day or two and then catch up with them. So I went out after they had departed to get ready, but I returned without having finished anything. Then I went out and returned without having finished anything, and he kept on dragging me until they hurried, and the raid was delayed. I intended to set out and catch up with them, and I wish I had done so, but that was not destined for me. So whenever I went out among the people after the departure of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and walked among them, it saddened me that I did not see a role model for myself except a man who was accused of hypocrisy or a man from among the weak whom God had excused. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk. He said while he was sitting among the people in Tabuk: What happened to Ka`b? A man from Banu Salamah said: O Messenger of God, his cloak and his gaze on his shoulders held him back. Mu`adh ibn Jabal said: What you said is bad. By God, O Messenger of God, we know nothing but good about him. So the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) was silent. Kaab bin Malik said: When I heard that he was returning, my concern came to me, so I began to remember the lie and say: How can I escape his wrath tomorrow? And I sought help in that from every wise man among my family. When it was said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is about to arrive, falsehood was removed from me, and I knew that I would never leave it with anything that contained a lie. So I decided to give charity, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was arriving. When he returned from a journey, he would start at the mosque, and bow in it two rak’ahs, then sit for the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him and began to apologize to him and swear to him. They were eighty-odd men. The Messenger of God accepted their outward expressions, pledged allegiance to them, asked forgiveness for them, and entrusted their secrets to God. So I came to him, and when I greeted him, he smiled the smile of someone angry, then he said: Come. So I came walking until I sat in front of him. He said to me: What kept you away? Didn’t you buy your back? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. By God, if I had sat with anyone other than you from the people of this world, I would have seen that I would escape his wrath with an excuse. I have been given an argument, but by God, I know that if I told you a hadith today, A lie that you are pleased with about me, for God will soon make you angry with me. And if I tell you a true story, you will find fault with me for it. I hope for God’s forgiveness. No, by God, I have no excuse. By God, I have never been stronger or more comfortable than when I stayed behind from you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for this He told the truth, so get up and let God decide on you. So I got up and some men from Banu Salamah rose up and followed me and said to me: By God, we did not know that you had committed a sin before this, and you were unable not to apologize to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as those who stayed behind apologized to him. It would have been sufficient for you to seek forgiveness from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. By God, they continued to rebuke me until I wanted to go back and lie to myself. Then I said to them: Has anyone else experienced this with me? They said: Yes, two men who said the same as you said. They were told the same as you had been told. I said: Who are they? They said: Murarah ibn al-Rabi’ al-Amri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqfi. Then they mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr and in whom there is an example, so I went when they mentioned them to me. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the Muslims from speaking to us, O three, among those who stayed behind from him. So the people avoided us and changed towards us until the land became strange to me, and it was not the land that I knew. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they submitted and sat in their homes crying. As for me, I was the youngest and most courageous of the people. I would go out and attend the prayer with the Muslims, and I would wander around the markets, and no one would speak to me. I would come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greet him while he was sitting in his place after the prayer. I would say to myself: Did he move his lips in return to my greeting or not? Then I would pray close to him and steal glances at him. When I turned to my prayer, he would turn to my prayer, and when I turned towards him, he would turn away from me. When this coldness of people had become too long for me, I walked until I climbed over the wall of Abu Qatada, who was my cousin and the dearest person to me. I greeted him, but by God, he did not return my greeting. So I said to him, ‘O Abu Qatada, I ask you by God, do you know that I love God and His Messenger?’ He was silent. So I went back to him and asked him, but he was silent. So I went back and asked him, and he said, ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ My eyes welled up with tears, and I turned away until I climbed over the wall. He said: While I was walking in the market of the city, a Nabataean from the Nabataeans of Syria, who had come with food to sell in the city, said: Who will guide me to Ka`b ibn Malik? So the people began to point him towards me, until he came to me and gave me a letter from the King of Ghassan. I read it and it said: As for what follows: It has reached me that your companion has treated you harshly, and God has not placed you in a house of humiliation or loss, so come to us and we will console you. So I said when I read it: This is also a calamity, so I took it to the oven and lit it. Then, when forty nights of the fifty had passed, a messenger from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commands you to separate from your wife. I said: Should I divorce her, or what should I do? He said: No, rather separate from her and do not approach her. And he sent to my companion the same thing, so I said to my wife: Go back to your family and stay with them until God decides on this matter. Ka'b said: The wife of Hilal ibn Umayya came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, Hilal ibn Umayya is an old man who is lost and has no servant. Would you mind if I serve him? He said: No, but he should not come near you. She said: By God, he has no desire for anything, and by God, he has not stopped crying since what happened to him happened until this day. Ka'b said: One of my family members said to me: Why don't you ask permission from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) about your wife as he gave permission to the wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah to serve him? I said: By God, I will not ask permission from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and how do I know what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) will say to me if I ask permission from him about her, and I am a young man. After that, I stayed for ten nights until fifty nights had been completed since the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) forbade us from speaking to him. When I prayed the dawn prayer, it was the fiftieth night, and I was on the roof of one of our houses. While I was sitting in the state that God mentioned, my soul was constricted and the earth, despite its vastness, was constricting me, I heard the voice of a louder voice on Mount Sala', saying at the top of his voice: O Ka'b ibn Malik, be of good cheer. So I fell down prostrating before God and knew that relief had come, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, announced God’s repentance for us when he prayed the dawn prayer. The people went to give us good report, and my companion went before me, giving good report. A man ran towards me on a horse and ran like a man from Aslam, and he completed his journey on the mountain, and the sound was faster than the horse. When the one whose voice I heard came to give me good report, I took off my garment and dressed him in it because of his good report. By God, I did not own anything else that day. I borrowed two garments and put them on and went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The people met me in groups, congratulating me on my repentance and saying: May God’s repentance be blessed for you. Ka`b said: Until I entered the mosque and saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sitting with people around him. Talha bin Ubaid God ran to me and shook my hand and congratulated me. By God, no man from the Muhajireen stood up to me except him, and I will never forget that for Talha. Ka'b said: When I greeted the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, while his face was shining with joy: Rejoice in the best day that has passed you since your mother gave birth to you! I said: Is it from you, O Messenger of God, or from God? He said: No, rather it is from God. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was happy, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon, and we used to know that from him. When I sat in front of him, I said: O Messenger of God, part of my repentance is that I give up my wealth as charity to God and His Messenger. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you. I said: Then I will keep my share in Khaybar. I said: O Messenger of God, God has saved me only because of my truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I will only speak the truth as long as I live. By God, I do not know of anyone among the Muslims whom God has blessed with truthfulness since I mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, better than He has blessed me. I have not deliberately told a lie since I mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until this day, and I hope that God will protect me as long as I live. And God revealed to His Messenger: God has accepted the repentance of the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar, until His saying: And be with the truthful. And Ishaq bin Rashid narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri with this chain of transmission on the authority of Ka’b, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade me from speaking to him and to my companion, so I remained like that until the matter became long for me, and nothing was more important to me than that I die and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pray for me, or that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and I would be among the people in that position, and none of them would speak to me or pray for me! And God revealed our repentance to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the last third of the night remained, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with Umm Salamah, and Umm Salamah was kind to me and helped me in my matter, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Umm Salamah, accept Ka’b’s repentance. She said: Shall I not send to him and give him good report? He said: Then the people will crush you and prevent you from sleeping the rest of the night, until when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer, he announced God’s repentance for us.”
9:118: 118- The Almighty said: And concerning the three who were left behind, until the earth, vast as it is, became strait for them, it expanded, and their souls became strait for them, with grief and worry, and they assumed, that is, they were certain, that there is no refuge from God, no place of panic from God, “except to Him. Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent,” that is, so that they might be steadfast in repentance, for their repentance had already come. Indeed, it is God who is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.
9:119: 119-O you who have believed, fear God and be with those who are truthful. Nafi' said: With Muhammad and his companions. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: With Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them. Ibn Jurayj said: With the emigrants, because God the Almighty said: For the poor emigrants until His saying: Those are the truthful Al-Hashr - 8. Ibn Abbas, may God the Almighty be pleased with them, said: With those whose intentions were sincere and whose hearts and deeds were upright and who went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Tabuk with sincerity of intention. It was said: With those who were honest in admitting their guilt and did not make false excuses. Ibn Masoud used to recite: And be with the truthful. Ibn Masoud said: Lying is not appropriate in seriousness or in jest, nor is it appropriate for one of you to promise his child something and then not fulfill it for him. Recite if you wish, and he recited this verse.
9:120: 120- The Almighty’s saying: It was not for the people of Madinah appears to be a statement, but its meaning is a prohibition, like the Almighty’s saying: And it was not for you to harm the Messenger of God (al-Ahzab 33:53) and those around them of the bedouins, the inhabitants of the deserts: Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ashja’, Aslam, and Ghifar. to stay behind the Messenger of God, if he went on a raid. nor to desire, that is: nor to desire, their own selves over his own, in accompanying him, helping him, and fighting alongside him. Al-Hasan said: They should not desire for themselves that hardships should befall them, so they should choose ease and comfort, while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the hardship of travel and enduring fatigue. That is because they are not afflicted, in their journey, with thirst, nor fatigue, nor hunger, “in the cause of God, nor do they tread any path of land, which enrages the disbelievers, their treading it, nor do they attain any attainment against the enemy, that is, they do not inflict upon their enemy killing, captivity, booty, or defeat, “except that a righteous deed is recorded for them because of it. Indeed, God does not allow the reward of the righteous to be lost.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Yazid bin Abi Maryam told us, Ubayya bin Rafa’a told us: Abu Abs caught up with me while I was going to Friday prayer and said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever’s feet become dusty in the way of God, God will forbid them from the Fire. They differed regarding the ruling of this verse. Qatada said: This is specific to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If he went out to fight himself, no one had the right to stay behind him except for an excuse. As for other imams and governors, whoever among the Muslims wanted to stay behind him, if the Muslims did not have a need for him. Al-Walid bin Muslim said: I heard Al-Awza’i, Ibn Al-Mubarak, Ibn Jabir, and Omar bin Abdul Aziz say about this verse: It is for the first and last of this nation. Ibn Zayd said: This was when the people of Islam were few, but when they became numerous, God Almighty abrogated it and permitted whoever He wished to stay behind, saying: And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once.
9:121: 121- The Almighty said: And they do not spend any expenditure, meaning: in the way of God, small or large, even if it is the string of a whip, nor do they cross a valley, they do not pass a valley on their way, coming or going. But it is recorded for them, meaning: their tracks and steps, that God may reward them with the best of what they used to do. It was narrated on the authority of Khuraim ibn Fatik that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever spends an expenditure in the way of God, it is recorded for him seven hundred times. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Hanthali told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Amr Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Abu Masoud Al-Ansari, who said: “A man came with a bridled camel and said: This is for the sake of God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You will have seven hundred bridled camels for it on the Day of Resurrection.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Muammar told us, Abdul Warith told us, Al-Hussein told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told me, Abu Salamah told me, Basr bin Saeed told me, Zaid bin Khalid, may God be pleased with him, told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever equips a fighter in the cause of God has fought, and whoever leaves behind a fighter in the cause of God with report has fought.
9:122: 122- The Almighty said: And it is not for the believers to go forth all together the verse: Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Al-Kalbi: When God the Almighty revealed the faults of the hypocrites in the Battle of Tabuk, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sending out raiding parties, and the Muslims would go forth all together to the battle and leave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone, so God the Almighty revealed this verse. This is a negation in the sense of a prohibition. God Almighty says: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth to fight? That is, why should not a group from every tribe go out to fight, and a group remain with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they may gain understanding in religion, meaning the group who remain behind, learning the Qur’an, the Sunnah, the obligations, and the rulings, and when the troops return, they inform them of what was revealed after them, so the troops remain learning what was revealed after them, and other troops are sent out. That is what He says: And that they may warn their people, and teach them the Qur’an and frighten them with it, when they return to them that they may beware, so that they do not know otherwise. Al-Hasan said: This understanding and warning refers to the revolting group, and its meaning is: Why don’t a group go forth to understand, that is, to see what God shows them of victory over the polytheists and support for the religion, and to warn their people from the infidels when they return to them from jihad, so that they inform them of God’s victory for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers, so that they may beware of opposing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what happened to their companions from the infidels will happen to them. Al-Kalbi said: It has another aspect, which is that some tribes of Banu Asad from Khuzaymah were afflicted by a severe famine, so they came with their children until they settled in Medina, where they spoiled its roads with excavations and raised its prices, so the following verse was revealed: “And it is not for the believers to go forth all at once. So why should not a party from every division of them go forth?” That is, it was not for them to go forth all at once, but rather a party from every tribe to gain understanding of the religion. Mujahid said: It was revealed about people who went out into the desert seeking report from its people, and they found some good from them, and they called whomever they found of the people to guidance. The people said to them: We do not see you except that you have left your companion and come to us. They found in themselves annoyance about that, and they all came from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God revealed this verse, meaning: Why should not a group from every division go forth to gain understanding of the religion and listen to what was revealed after them and warn their people? Meaning: All the people when they return to them and call them to God, perhaps they will beware of God’s wrath and punishment. And a group stayed behind seeking good. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Abdullah bin Abi Saeed bin Abi Hind told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever God wants good for, He gives him understanding of the religion. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You will find people like mines of gold and silver. The best of them in the pre-Islamic era are the best of them in Islam if they understand.” Jurisprudence: is the knowledge of the rulings of religion. It is divided into an individual obligation and a collective obligation. An individual obligation, such as knowledge of purification, prayer, and fasting, is upon every accountable person to know. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. Likewise, every act of worship that the Shariah has made obligatory upon every person, he must know its knowledge, such as knowledge of zakat if he has money, and knowledge of Hajj if it is obligatory upon him. As for the communal obligation, it is: to learn until he reaches the level of ijtihad and the rank of issuing fatwas. If the people of a country refrain from learning it, they have all disobeyed. If one person from every country rises up and learns it, the obligation is dropped from the others, and they must imitate him in whatever incidents befall them. Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over the lowest of you. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: One jurist is more difficult for Satan than a thousand worshippers. Al-Shafi’i said: Seeking knowledge is better than voluntary prayer.
9:123: 123- The Almighty said: O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are near you the verse. They were ordered to fight the closest to them in house and lineage. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: such as Banu Qurayzah, Banu Nadir, Khaybar, and the like. It was said: He meant the Romans because they were the inhabitants of the Levant, and the Levant was closer to Medina than Iraq, and that they may find in you harshness, severity and zeal. Al-Hasan said: Be patient in their struggle, and know that God is with the righteous, with help and victory.
9:124: 124- The Almighty said: And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ Certainty. The hypocrites used to say this in mockery. God Almighty said: But as for those who believed, it increased them in faith, certainty and belief, and they rejoice, rejoicing at the revelation of the Qur’an.
9:125: 125-And as for those in whose hearts is disease, doubt and hypocrisy, it will increase their filth upon their filth, meaning: disbelief upon their disbelief. So when every surah is revealed that they deny, their disbelief in it increases. Mujahed said: This verse is a reference to faith: it increases and decreases. Omar used to take the hand of one or two of his companions and say: Come, so that we may increase in faith. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Faith appears as a white spot in the heart, and the greater the faith, the more that whiteness increases until the entire heart becomes white. Hypocrisy appears as a black spot in the heart, and the greater the hypocrisy, the more blackness increases until the entire heart becomes black.
