By God, if you were to split open the heart of a believer, you would find it white, and if you were to split open the heart of a hypocrite, you would find it black. He said: And they died as disbelievers.
9:126: 126-His statement: Or do they not see? Hamza and Yaqub read:َقَقْلنمwith the ta' addressing the believers, and the others read it with the ya', reporting the hypocrites mentioned. That they are tested are afflicted once or twice every year with diseases and hardships. Mujahid said: with famine and hardship. Qatadah said: with invasion and jihad. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: They are disgraced by showing their hypocrisy. Ikrimah said: They are hypocrites then believe then are hypocrites. Yaman said: They break their covenant once or twice a year. Then they do not repent from breaking the covenant and they do not return to God from hypocrisy, nor do they remember, meaning: they do not learn from what they see of the fulfillment of God's promise of victory and triumph for the Muslims.
9:127: 127- And when a surah is revealed, in which the hypocrites are criticized and rebuked, they look at one another, wanting to flee, some of them say to each other, Does anyone see you, meaning: any of the believers, if you stand up, and if no one sees them, they leave the mosque, and if they know that someone sees them, they stay and remain, then turn away, from believing in it. It was said: they turned away from their places where they hear, God turned their hearts away, from believing. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: God led them astray as a punishment for their action, because they are a people who do not understand, from God's religion. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Do not say when you pray, 'We have turned away from the prayer', for some people turned away and God turned their hearts away, but say, 'We have completed the prayer.'
9:128: 128- The Almighty said: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. You know his lineage and ancestry. Al-Suddi said: From the Arabs, from the children of Ishmael. Ibn Abbas said: There is no tribe among the Arabs that did not give birth to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they have a lineage among them. Jaafar bin Muhammad al-Sadiq said: He was not affected by anything from the children of the pre-Islamic era since the time of Adam, peace be upon him. Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid told us, Hamid bin Muhammad told us, Ali bin Abdul Aziz told us, Muhammad bin Abi Na’im told us, Hisham told us, Al-Madani told me - meaning: Abu Ma’shar - on the authority of Abu Al-Huwayrith on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was not born from the fornication of the people of ignorance. I was born only through marriage like the marriage of Islam.” Ibn Abbas, Al-Zuhri, and Ibn Muhaisin read from yourselves with the opening of the fa, meaning: from the most noble and best of you. Dear to him, severe for him, what you have suffered, it was said that what is a conjunction, meaning: has suffered you, and it is the hardship and harm that has come upon you. Al-Qatibi said: what has suffered you and harmed you. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: what has led you astray. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi said: You have not completed it. He is anxious over you, meaning, over your faith and righteousness. Qatada said: He is anxious over you, meaning, over your lost one, that God guides him. To the believers, Most Kind, Most Merciful, it was said: Most Kind to the obedient, Most Merciful to the sinners.
9:129: 129- If they turn away, if they turn away from faith and wage war against you, "then say, 'Sufficient for me is God. There is no god but He. In Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.'" It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab who said: The last verses to be revealed from the Qur’an were these two verses: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves until the end of the surah. He said: They are the most recent verses from God.
10:1: Surat Yunus, peace and blessings be upon him, is Meccan except for three verses from the words: If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you to the end. In the name of God, the most gracious, the most merciful 1- “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.” Alif, Lam, Ra and Alif, Lam, Ra are read by the people of Hijaz, Ash-Sham, and Hafs with a fat-ha on the ra in both. The others read it with imala. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: Alif, Lam, Ra, I am God, I see, and Alif, Lam, Ra, I am God, I know and I see. Saeed bin Jubair said: Alif Lam Ra, “Ha Meem,” and Nun are the letters of the name Ar-Rahman. We have already discussed the letters of spelling. These are the verses of the Wise Book, meaning: these. By the Wise Book he meant the Qur’an, and it was said that he meant the verses that He revealed before that, and for that reason he said: those, and those are a reference to an absent feminine, and the Wise: the One who establishes what is permissible and what is forbidden, and the limits and rulings, fa’il with the meaning of maf’il, as evidenced by his saying: A Book whose verses are perfect (Hud 11:1). It was said: It means the ruler, fa’il means fa’il, and its evidence is the Almighty’s saying: And He sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between the people Al-Baqarah 213. It was said: It means the one being ruled, fa’il means the one being ruled. Al-Hasan said: He ruled in it with justice, kindness, and giving to relatives, and with forbidding indecency, evil, and transgression, and He ruled in it with Paradise for whoever obeyed Him and with Hell for whoever disobeyed Him.
10:2: 2- The Almighty said: Was it a wonder to the people? Wonder: a state that befalls a person when he sees something that is contrary to what is usual. The reason for the revelation of the verse is that when God the Almighty sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a Messenger, the polytheists said: God is too great for His Messenger to be a human being. So God the Almighty said: Is it a wonder to mankind meaning: the people of Mecca, the alif in it is for rebuke, that We have inspired a man from among them meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to warn mankind meaning: inform them while frightening them, and give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing with their Lord. They differed about it: Ibn Abbas said: A good reward for the deeds they have done. Ad-Dahhak said: A reward of truth. Al-Hasan said: A good deed they have done in the past that they will do. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It is happiness in the first mention. Zaid ibn Aslam said: It is the intercession of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ata’ said: A station of truth that will not disappear, nor will there be misery in it. It was said: A high status. The word qadm is added to truth and it is its description, like their saying masjid al-jami’ the mosque of the congregation and harvest grain. Abu Ubaidah said: Everyone who is foremost in good or evil is considered a “qadm among the Arabs. It is said: So-and-so has a foot in Islam, and he has a foot of truth with me and a foot of evil. It is made feminine and it is said: a good foot and a righteous foot. “The disbelievers said: ‘Indeed, this is an obvious magician.’” Nafi’ and the people of Basra and Ash-Sham read: la-sahir without an alif, meaning the Qur’an. Ibn Kathir and the people of Kufa read: la-sahir with an alif, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
10:3: 3- The Almighty said: “Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself on the Throne. He directs the affair,” He alone decides it, There is no intercessor except after His permission, meaning: that the intercessors do not intercede except with His permission, and this is a response to Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, for he used to say: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Al-Lat and Al-Uzza will intercede for me. The Almighty says: That is God, your Lord, meaning: The One who did these things is your Lord, you have no Lord other than Him. “So worship Him. Will you not remember?” Will you not be admonished?
10:4: 4- "To Him is your return, all of you. The promise of God is true," true, without breaking it. It is in the accusative case as a source, meaning: He promised you a true promise. Indeed, He begins creation and then repeats it, meaning: He revives them from the beginning, then causes them to die, then revives them. The general reading is: Indeed with a kasra on the alif as a resumption. Abu Ja`far read it with a fatha, meaning that He rewards those who believe and do righteous deeds with justice, with fairness. And those who disbelieve will have a drink of scalding water, hot water that has reached its boiling point, and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.
10:5: 5- It is He who made the sun a radiance during the day, and the moon a light at night. It was said: He made the sun a source of radiance, and the moon a source of light, and determined for it phases meaning: He determined for it phases, meaning He prepared for it phases that it cannot exceed or fall short of, and He did not say: He determined them both. It was said: The estimation of the houses refers to them both, but he was satisfied with mentioning one of them, as he said: And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should please Him (al-Tawbah 9:62). It was said: It refers to the moon specifically because the moon is used to determine the passing of months and years, not the sun. The lunar mansions are twenty-eight, and their names are: Ash-Shartayn, Al-Batina, Ash-Tharyaa, Ash-Dabaran, Ash-Haq’ah, Ash-Hana’ah, Ash-Dhira’, An-Nasr, Ash-Tawf, Ash-Jabha, Az-Zubrah, Ash-Sarfa, Ash-Awa’, Ash-Samak, Ash-Ghafr, Ash-Zubani, Ash-Iklil, Ash-Qalb, Ash-Shula, Ash-Na’ayim, Ash-Baldah, Sa’d Adh-Dhabih, Sa’d Bal’a, Sa’d As-Su’ud, Sa’d Al-Akhbiya, Far’ Ad-Dulu Al-Muqaddam, Far’ Ad-Dulu Al-Muqaddam, and Batn Al-Hut. These houses are divided into twelve zodiac signs: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. Each sign has two houses and a third of a house. The moon descends into one of these houses every night, and is hidden for two nights if the month is thirty, and for one night if it is twenty-nine. Thus, those houses are formed, and the sun’s position in each house is thirteen days, so the end of the year occurs with its end. The Almighty said: That you may know the number of years, meaning: the number of mansions. That you may know the number of years, their beginning and end, and the reckoning, meaning: the reckoning of months, days, and hours. God did not create that, referring it back to creation and estimation. If He had referred it back to the mentioned entities, He would have said: those. Except with truth, meaning: He did not create it in vain, but rather to show His creation and indicate His power. He details the signs for a people who know, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hafs, and Ya’qub read: He details with a ya, because of His saying: He did not create. The rest read: He details with a noon for emphasis.
10:6: 6- Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day and in what God has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear God.
10:7: 7- Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us, meaning: do not fear Our punishment nor do they expect Our reward. Hope can mean fear and greed, and are satisfied with the life of this world, so they chose it and worked for it, and are content with it: they are content with it. And those who are heedless of Our signs, meaning: heedless of Our evidence and do not take heed. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: They are heedless and turn away from Our signs about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur'an.
10:8: 8- Their abode is the Fire because of what they used to earn, of disbelief and denial.
10:9: 9- The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them because of their faith, contains an implied meaning: Their Lord will guide them because of their faith to a paradise, underneath which rivers flow. Mujahid said: He will guide them on the path to paradise, He will make for them a light by which they will walk. It was said: He guides them means He rewards and recompenses them. It was said: Its meaning is that their Lord guides them to His religion, i.e., by their belief in His guidance. Rivers flow beneath them means: in front of them, like the Almighty’s saying: Your Lord has provided a stream beneath you (Maryam 19:24). He did not mean that it was beneath her while she was sitting on it, but rather he meant in front of her. It was said: It flows beneath them, meaning: by their command, in the gardens of bliss.
10:10: 10- Their supplication, meaning: their saying and speech. It was said: their supplication. In it is Glory be to You, O God, which is a word of glorification, declaring God free from all evil. We narrated: The people of Paradise are inspired with praise and glorification, just as they are inspired with the soul. The commentators said: This word is a sign between the people of Paradise and the servants in the food. When they want food, they say: Glory be to You, O God. Then they are brought to them at the right time what they desire on tables, each table a mile by a mile, on each table seventy thousand plates, and on each plate a type of food that does not resemble one another. Then when they finish eating, they praise God. This is what God Almighty says: “And their final call will be: ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’” God Almighty says: “And their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’” That is, they will greet one another with peace. It was also said: The angels’ greeting to them will be peace. It was said: The angels come to them from their Lord with peace. And their final supplication will be, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’ He means: They begin their speech with glorification and end it with praise.
10:11: 11- The Almighty said: And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they hasten for good, Ibn Abbas said: This is about a man saying when angry to his family and children: May God curse you, and may God not bless you. Qatada said: It is a man's supplication against himself, his family and his wealth for something he hates to be answered. Its meaning is: If God were to hasten for people the answer to their supplications for evil and dislike as they hasten for good, that is: as they love to hasten for good, their term would have been fulfilled for them, Ibn Amir and Yaqub read: would have been fulfilled with the opening of the qaf and the dad, their term is accusative, meaning: He would have destroyed the one against whom He supplicated and caused his death. The others said: would have been fulfilled with the qaf and the dad closed, their term is nominative, meaning: He would have finished destroying them and they would all have died. It was said: It was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith when he said: “O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky” (al-Anfal 8:32). This is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: So We will leave those who do not expect to meet Us, who do not fear the Resurrection and the Reckoning, in their transgression they wander blindly. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bishran told us, Abu Ali Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ziyadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam ibn Munabbih, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, I have made a covenant with You that You will not break. I am only a human being, and what humans do comes from me. So if any of the believers I have harmed, or cursed, or flogged, or cursed, make it for him a prayer, a charity, and an act of devotion, by which You will bring him closer to You on the Day of Resurrection.”
10:12: 12- The Almighty’s saying: And when harm touches man, effort and hardship, he calls upon Us to lie on his side, meaning: on his side, lying down, or sitting or standing, meaning in all of his states, because man does not go beyond one of these states. So when We removed his harm from him, he passed on as if he had never called upon Us to do harm that had befallen him, meaning he continued on his previous path before the harm befell him, and forgot what he had been through of effort and affliction, as if he had never called upon Us to do harm that had befallen him, meaning: he had not asked Us to remove harm that had befallen him. Thus was made attractive to the transgressors those who exceeded the limit in disbelief and disobedience, what they were doing, of disobedience. Ibn Jurayj said: Thus was made attractive to the transgressors what they were doing of supplication at the time of affliction and abandoning gratitude at the time of ease. It was said that its meaning is just as your deeds were made attractive to you, so were the deeds of the transgressors who were before you made attractive.
10:13: 13- The Almighty said: And We had destroyed generations before you when they committed injustice they associated partners with God, “and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe. Thus,” meaning: just as We destroyed them for their disbelief, We will recompense we will punish and destroy the criminal people, the disbelievers for their denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He is frightening the disbelievers of Mecca with the punishment of the previous nations who denied.
10:14: 14- Then We made you successors, meaning: successors, on the earth after them, meaning: after the generations that We destroyed, to see how you will act, and He knows best about them. We narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Behold, this world is sweet and green, and God has made you successors in it, so He will see how you will act.
10:15: 15- The Almighty said: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, Qatada said: He means the polytheists of Mecca. Muqatil said: They are five men: Abdullah bin Umayya Al-Makhzumi, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, Mukraz bin Hafs, Amr bin Abdullah bin Abi Qais Al-Amiri, and Al-Aas bin Aamer bin Hashim. Those who do not expect to meet Us - those mentioned above - said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you want to believe in you, bring a Qur’an other than this, which does not contain abandonment of the worship of Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat, and does not contain any defects in them. If God did not reveal it, then say it yourself, or change it, so replace a verse of punishment with a verse of mercy, or replace a forbidden verse with a lawful verse, or replace a lawful verse with a forbidden verse. Say, to them, O Muhammad, It is not for me to change it of my own accord, from my own self. I only follow what is revealed to me, meaning: I only follow what is revealed to me in what I command you to do and what I forbid you from doing. Indeed, if I disobey my Lord, I fear the punishment of a tremendous Day.
10:16: 16- "Say: If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you," meaning: If God had willed, He would not have revealed the Qur'an to me. Nor would I have made you aware of it, meaning: Nor would God have taught you. Al-Bazzi read on the authority of Ibn Kathir: Nor would I have made you aware of it, restricting it to the affirmative, meaning: Nor would you have known of it without my reading it to you. Ibn Abbas read: To warn you with it, from warning. I have remained among you a lifetime, a period of time, which is forty years, before it, before the revelation of the Qur'an, and I did not bring you anything. Do you not understand? That it is not from before me. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained among them for forty years before the revelation, then God revealed to him, so he stayed in Mecca after the revelation thirteen years, then he migrated and stayed in Medina for ten years and died at the age of sixty-three. Anas narrated: He stayed in Mecca for ten years after the revelation and in Medina for ten years, and he died at the age of sixty. The first is more famous and more evident.
10:17: 17- The Almighty said: Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God, claiming that He has a partner or a son, or denies His signs, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an, Indeed, the criminals will not succeed, the polytheists will not be saved.
10:18: 18- And they worship besides God that which neither harms them, if they disobey Him and abandon His worship, nor benefits them, if they worship Him, meaning: the idols, and they say, These are our intercessors with God. Say, Do you inform God, do you inform God, of that which He does not know?", God is the Truthful. The meaning of the verse: Do you inform God that He has a partner, or that He has an intercessor without His permission, and God does not know of a partner for Himself? "In the heavens and on the earth. Glory be to Him and He is Exalted above what they associate with Him." Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read: tashirkuna with the ta', here and in Surat An-Nahl in two places, and in Surat Ar-Rum, and the others read it all with the ya'.
10:19: 19- The Almighty said: And mankind were but one community, meaning: in Islam. We have mentioned the difference in this in Surat Al-Baqarah. Then they differed, and were divided into believers and disbelievers, and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, in that He set a term for each nation. Al-Kalbi said: It is a respite for this nation and that He will not destroy them with punishment in this world, it would have been judged between them, by sending down the punishment and hastening the punishment for the deniers, and that was a separation between them, in that over which they differ. Al-Hasan said: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, which went on in His judgment that: He will not judge between them in that over which they differed with reward and punishment before the Day of Resurrection, it would have been judged between them in this world and the believer would enter Paradise and the disbeliever the Fire, but the term preceded from God and He made their meeting place the Day of Resurrection.
10:20: 20- And they say, meaning: the people of Mecca, Why was not a sign sent down to him, meaning: the work of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his Lord, as you suggest, Then say, 'The unseen belongs only to God,' meaning: Say, you have only asked me about the unseen, and the unseen belongs only to God, no one knows why He did not do that and no one knows it except Him. It was said: The unseen is the revelation of the verse, no one knows when it will be revealed except Him, So wait for its revelation, I am with you among those who wait, and it was said: So wait for God's judgment between us with truth by showing the one who is right over the one who is wrong.
10:21: 21- The Almighty said: And when We let the people taste, meaning: the disbelievers, mercy after hardship, meaning: comfort and ease after hardship and affliction, and it was said: rain after drought, touched them, meaning: struck them, then they have a plan concerning Our signs, Mujahid said: denial and mockery. And Muqatil bin Hayyan said: They do not say: This is God’s provision, rather they say: We were given water by such-and-such a star, and this is His saying: And you make your provision that you deny Al-Waqi’ah-82. “Say: God is swifter in plotting,” quicker in punishment, more severe in taking, and more capable of retribution. He wants His punishment to destroy you to be quicker to you than what comes from you in repelling the truth. Our messengers, our guardians, write down what you plot, and Jacob read: plot with a ya.
10:22: 22- The Almighty said: It is He who makes you travel, makes you run and carries you. Abu Ja`far and Ibn `Amir read: He spreads you with the letter nun and the letter shin from evil, which is spreading and spreading, on land, on the backs of beasts, and in the sea, on the ark, until when you were in the ark, meaning: in the ships, it can be singular and plural, and they sailed with them, meaning: the ships sailed with the people, he returned from the address to the report, with a pleasant wind, gentle, and they rejoiced in it, meaning: with the wind, a wind came to it, meaning: the ark came with a wind, a storm, strong blowing, and he did not say a stormy wind, because the wind is specific to the storm. It was said: the wind is masculine and feminine. And there came to them, meaning: the passengers of the ship, the waves, which is the movement and mixing of the water, from every side, and they thought, were certain, that they were surrounded, that they were close to destruction, meaning: destruction surrounded them, so they called upon God, sincere to Him in religion, meaning: they were sincere in their supplication to God and did not call upon anyone but God. And they said, If You should save us, O our Lord, from this, the violent wind, we will surely be among the grateful, with faith and obedience to You.
10:23: 23- But when He delivered them, at once they rebelled in the land, they oppressed and transgressed against the command of God Almighty on the earth, without right, that is, with corruption. O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves, because its consequences will come back to them, then He began by saying: The enjoyment of worldly life, that is, this is the enjoyment of worldly life, the report of an implied beginning, like His saying: They did not remain except for an hour of a day of notification Al-Ahqaf-35, that is, this is a notification. It was said: it is a connected statement, and transgression is the beginning, and enjoyment is its report. Its meaning is: Your desire is only for the enjoyment of worldly life, and it is not suitable as provision for the Hereafter, because you are thereby incurring the wrath of God. Hafs read: Enjoyment in the accusative case, meaning you will enjoy the enjoyment of worldly life, Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.
10:24: 24- The Almighty said: The example of the life of this world, in its passing and disappearance, is only like water which We send down from the sky, and it mixes with it, that is, with the rain, the vegetation of the earth, Ibn Abbas said: it grows with the water of every color, of that which people eat, of grains and fruits, and livestock, of grass, until the earth takes on its adornment, its beauty and splendor and the flowers appear green, red, yellow, and white, and is beautified. That is, it is decorated, and this is how it is in Ibn Masoud’s reading: adorned. And its people thought that they had power over it, to cut it, pick it, and harvest it, referring the metaphor back to the earth. Meaning: The plant, since it was understood. It was said: He returned it to the crop. It was said: To the decoration. Our command came to it, Our decree, to destroy it, by night or by day, and We made it a harvest, meaning: harvested and cut off, as if it had not flourished yesterday, as if it had not existed yesterday. Its origin is from ghani in a place if one resided in it. Qatada said: Its meaning is that the one who clings to the world will be visited by the command of God and His punishment, the most heedless of all. Thus do We detail the verses for a people who reflect.
10:25: 25- The Almighty says: "And God invites to the abode of peace." Qatada said: Peace is God, and His abode is Paradise. It was said: Peace means safety. Paradise was called the abode of peace because whoever enters it is safe from harm. It was said that what is meant by peace is greeting. Paradise was called the abode of peace because its people greet each other with peace and the angels greet them. God the Almighty said: "And the angels will enter upon them from every gate. Peace be upon you." (Ar-Ra'd: 23). We narrated on the authority of Jabir who said: “Angels came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sleeping. Some of them said: He is asleep, and some of them said: The eye is asleep but the heart is awake. They said: This companion of yours has a parable. He said: Give him a parable. Some of them said: His parable is like that of a man who built a house, held a banquet in it, and sent out an inviter. Whoever answered the inviter entered the house and ate from the banquet, and whoever did not answer the inviter did not enter the house and did not eat from the banquet. They said: Interpret it for him so that he may understand it. Some of them said: He is asleep, and some of them said: The eye is asleep but the heart is awake. They said: The house is Paradise and the inviter is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Whoever obeys Muhammad has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys Muhammad has disobeyed God, and Muhammad has divided people.” And He guides whom He wills to a straight path. The straight path is Islam, which is comprehensive in its call to show the proof, and specific in its guidance, independent of creation.
10:26: 26- The Almighty’s saying: For those who do good is the best and more, meaning: for those who do good deeds in this world is the best, which is Paradise, and more: which is looking at the face of God. This is the saying of a group of the Companions, including Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, Hudhayfah, Abu Musa, and Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with them. It is the saying of al-Husayn, Ikrimah, Ata’, Muqatil, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Abbas Al-Hamidi informed us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Yaqoub informed us by dictation, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Sagani informed us, Al-Aswad bin Aamer informed us, Hammad bin Salamah informed us, on the authority of Thabit - meaning Al-Banani - on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Suhaib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: For those who do good is the best and more. He said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, a caller will call out: O people of Paradise, you have an appointment with God that He wants to fulfill for you. They will say: What is this promise? Has He not made our scales heavy, made our faces white, admitted us to Paradise, and saved us from Hell?” He said: Then the veil will be lifted and they will look upon the face of God Almighty. He said: They have not been given anything more beloved to them than looking at Him.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The good deed is: a good deed is rewarded with its like, and the increase is multiplying it tenfold to seven hundred times. Mujahid said: The good deed is: a good deed like a good deed, and the increase is forgiveness and approval. And their faces will not be covered with dust, dust, plural of qatra. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: blackness of the face, nor humiliation, disgrace. Qatadah said: gloom. Ibn Abi Laila said: This is after they have seen their Lord. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
10:27: 27- And those who have earned evil deeds will be recompensed with the like thereof, meaning: they will have the like thereof, as He said: And whoever brings evil will not be recompensed except the like thereof (Al-An'am: 160). "And humiliation will overwhelm them. They will have no protector from God", and of is a relative clause, meaning: they will have no protector from God. As if their faces were covered, were covered, with pieces, plural of piece, of the night in darkness, is in the accusative case as a state and not as an adjective, and therefore He did not say: darkened, its meaning is: pieces of the night in a state of its darkness, or pieces of the dark night. Ibn Kathir, Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read: pieces with a silent ta', meaning some, like His saying: with pieces of the night (Hud 11:81). Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
10:28: 28- The Almighty said: And the Day We shall gather them all together, then We shall say to those who associated, ‘Stay where you are,’ meaning: You and your partners, meaning: the idols. Its meaning is: Then We shall say to those who associated, ‘Stay where you are, you and your partners,’ meaning: the idols. So We removed We distinguished and separated between them, that is, between the polytheists and their partners, and We severed the connection that existed between them in this world, and that is when every worshipped thing other than God disowns the one who worshipped it, and their partners said, that is, the idols, You did not worship us, at Our request, and they said: Yes, we used to worship you, and the idols said:
10:29: 29- "God is sufficient as a witness between us and you, if we were unaware of your worship of Him." That is, we were only unaware of your worship of Him. We did not hear, see, or understand.
10:30: 30-God the Almighty said: "There you will be tested", meaning: you will be tested. It was said: its meaning is: you will learn and stand on it. Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read: "It will be recited" with two ta's, meaning: it will read, "every soul", its record. It was said: its meaning is that every soul will follow "what it has put forward", what it has presented of good or evil. It was said: its meaning is that it will see, "and they will be returned to God, to His judgment, so He is the only one who judges them, their true Master", who takes charge of and owns their affairs. If it is said: Did He not say: "And that the disbelievers will have no Master" Muhammad 11? It was said: Master there means the helper, and here it means: the owner, "and lost from them, was removed from them and invalidated, what they used to invent", in this world of denial.
10:31: 31- The Almighty said: “Say: Who provides for you from the sky and the earth?” That is, from the sky with rain, and from the earth with plants? Or who has control over hearing and sight? That is, who gives you hearing and sight? And who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living? He brings forth the living from the sperm and the sperm from the living. And who manages the affair? That is, He decides the affair. “They will say: God.” He is the One who does these things. “So say: Will you not fear Him?” Do you not fear His punishment for your polytheism? It was said: Will you not fear polytheism despite this admission?
28:88: 32- That is God, your Lord, the one who does these things is your Lord, "the truth. So what is there after the truth except error? So how are you turned away?" That is: So where are you turned away from worshipping Him while you acknowledge Him? 88- “And do not invoke with God another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face.” That is, except Him. It was said: except His kingdom. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: except what is intended for His Face. His is the judgment. That is, the decisive judgment. And to Him you will be returned. You will be returned in the Hereafter, and He will reward you for your deeds.
10:33: 33- Likewise. Al-Kalbi said: Thus, has come to pass, it is obligatory, the word of your Lord, His previous judgment, upon those who are wicked, they disbelieved, that they will not believe, Abu Ja`far, Nafi`, and Ibn `Amir read the words of your Lord in the plural here in two places, and in Al-Mu`min, and the others in the singular.
10:34: 34- "Say: Is there among your partners", your idols one who initiates creation, who creates creation without an origin or example, then repeats it, then revives it after death in its original form, if they answer you, otherwise say you: God initiates creation then repeats it, so how are you deluded? That is: are you diverted from the intended path.
10:35: 35- “Say: Is there among your partners any who guides to the truth?” If they say: No - and they must do so - “Say: God guides to the truth.” That is, to the truth. Is he who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed than he who does not guide? Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read: with a silent Ha' and a light Dal, and the others read: with a stressed Dal, then Abu Ja'far and Qalun read: with a silent Ha', and Abu Amr with a rum of the Ha' between the Fatha and the Sukun, and Hafs read: with a Fatha of the Ya' and a Kasra of the Ha', and Abu Bakr with a Kasra of both, and the rest with a Fatha of both, and its meaning is: is guided - in all of them - so whoever lightens the Dal, he said: it is said: I guided him, so he was guided, and whoever stressed the Dal assimilated the Ta' into the Dal, then Abu Amr wanted according to his doctrine in preferring to lighten, and whoever sukun the Ha' left it as it was as he did in 'I'tadawwa and Yakhsamoon, and whoever opened the Ha' moved the Fatha of the assimilated Ta' to the Ha', and whoever broke the Ha' because of the meeting of two Sukoons, the Jazm speaker moves it to the Kasra, and whoever breaks the Ya' with the Ha' follows the Kasra with the Kasra. God Almighty says: Unless he is guided. The meaning of the verse: Is God, who guides to the truth, more deserving of being followed, or an idol that is not guided unless it is guided? If it is said: How did he say: Unless he is guided, when it is inconceivable that an idol can be guided or be guided? It was said: The meaning of guidance for idols is movement, meaning that they do not move from one place to another unless they are carried and transported, which shows the inability of idols. Another answer is: The mention of guidance is metaphorical, because when the polytheists took idols as gods and placed them in the position of someone who hears and understands, they expressed them in the same way as someone who knows and understands, and they were described with the attribute of someone who understands. What is the matter with you? How do you judge? How do you judge when you claim that God has a partner?
10:36: 36- The Almighty said: And most of them follow nothing but conjecture, some of them say that the idols are gods, and that they will intercede for them in the Hereafter, based on their conjecture, which was not mentioned in any book or messenger. By most, He meant all those who say that, Indeed, conjecture does not avail against the truth at all, meaning: it does not ward off any of God's punishment from them. It was said: it does not take the place of knowledge, Indeed, God is Knowing of what they do.
10:37: 37- The Almighty said: And this Qur’an could not have been invented by anyone other than God. Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is: And it is not appropriate for such a Qur’an to have been invented by anyone other than God, like the Almighty’s saying: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war (Al Imran 3:161). It was said: An means lam, meaning: This Qur’an could not have been invented by anyone other than God. His saying: But the confirmation of what was before it, meaning: what was before the Qur’an from the Torah and the Gospel. It was said: It is a confirmation of what is before the Qur’an of the Resurrection and the Resurrection, and the details of the Book, clarifying what is in the Book of what is permissible and forbidden, the obligations and rulings, there is no doubt about it from the Lord of the worlds.
10:38: 38- Or do they say, Abu Ubaidah said: Or means and, meaning: and they say, He invented it, Muhammad invented the Qur'an on his own, "Say: Then bring a surah like it," the Qur'an is likened to And call upon whomever you can, of those you worship, besides God, to help you in that, if you should be truthful, that Muhammad invented it. Then he said:
10:39: 39- Rather, they denied that of which they had no knowledge, meaning: the Qur'an. They denied it without having knowledge of it, and its interpretation had not yet come to them, meaning: the consequence of what God promised in the Qur'an, that their affair would end in punishment. He means: that they did not know what the consequence of their affair would end in. Thus did those before them deny, meaning: just as these disbelievers denied the Qur'an, so did those before them from the disbelievers of the past nations deny. Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers, the final matter of the polytheists was destruction.
10:40: 40- And among them are those who believe in it, meaning: among your people are those who believe in the Qur’an, and among them are those who do not believe in it, due to God’s prior knowledge of them, and your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters, those who do not believe.
10:41: 41- And if they deny you O Muhammad, then say, 'To me is my work' and its reward, and to you is your work and its reward, You are innocent of what I do and I am innocent of what you do, this is like the Almighty's saying: To us are our works and to you are your works Al-Qasas-55, To you is your religion and to me is mine Al-Kafirun-6. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: This verse was abrogated by the verse on jihad. Then he said that success lies in believing in Him and not in anyone else:
10:42: 42-He said: And among them are those who listen to you with their external hearing, but it does not benefit them. Can you make the deaf hear? He means: the hearing of the heart, even though they do not understand.
10:43: 43- "And among them are those who look at you, with their apparent sight, can you guide the blind, meaning the blindness of the heart, even if they do not see?" This is a consolation from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says: You are not able to make hear one whose hearing you have taken away, nor to guide one whose sight you have taken away, nor to grant success to faith one whom you have judged not to believe.
10:44: 44- God does not wrong people at all, because He is generous and just in all His actions, but people wrong themselves, through disbelief and disobedience.
10:45: 45- The Almighty said: And the Day He will gather them together, Hafs read it with a ya', and the others with a noon, as if they had not remained except for an hour of the day, Ad-Dahhak said: As if they had not remained in this world except for an hour of the day. Ibn Abbas said: As if they had not remained in their graves except for the amount of an hour of the day, They will recognize one another, they will recognize one another when they are raised from the graves as they knew each other in this world, then the recognition will be cut off when they witness the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. In some of the narrations: That a person will recognize on the Day of Resurrection who is beside him and will not speak to him out of awe and fear. Those who deny the meeting with God and are not guided have certainly lost. What is meant by loss is the loss of the soul, and there is nothing greater than that.
10:46: 46- The Almighty said: And if We show you, O Muhammad, some of what We promise them, during your lifetime of torment, or cause you to die, it was said, their torment, then to Us is their return, in the Hereafter, then God is Witness over what they do, so He will reward them for it. Then means and, meaning: And God is Witness. Mujahid said: So the part that I showed them was their demise at Badr, and all other types of torment after their death.
10:47: 47- The Almighty said: “And for every nation is a messenger. So when their messenger comes,” and they deny him, it will be judged between them with justice, meaning they will be tormented in this world and destroyed with torment, meaning: before the Messenger comes, there will be no reward or punishment. Mujahid and Muqatil said: So when their Messenger who was sent to them comes on the Day of Resurrection, it will be judged between him and them with justice, and they will not be wronged, they will not be tormented without sin, nor will they be held accountable without proof, nor will their good deeds be diminished nor will their bad deeds be increased.
10:48: 48- And they say, meaning: the polytheists say: When will this promise that you promise us, O Muhammad, of torment come to pass. And it was said: the Day of Resurrection, if you are truthful, you, O Muhammad, and your followers.
10:49: 49- Say, 'I do not possess for myself,' I do not have the power to do anything for myself, neither harm nor benefit, meaning: to repel harm nor bring benefit, except what God wills, that I possess, for every nation there is a term, a set period, when their term comes, the time of the end of their lives, they will not remain behind an hour nor will they precede it, meaning: they will not remain behind nor advance.
10:50: 50- The Almighty said: "Say: Have you considered: if His punishment should come upon you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals are hastening for?" That is, what is it that the polytheists are hastening for from God? It was said: What is it that the criminals are hastening for of the punishment, and they have fallen into it. The true meaning is that they were hastening for the punishment, saying: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. (al-Anfal 8:32). So God the Almighty says: What is it that they are hastening for? That is, what do the criminals know about what they are hastening for and asking for, like a man who says to another after he has done something ugly: What have you done to yourself?
10:51: 51- Then when it occurs, it was said: its meaning is there? And then, and it is not a conjunction, when it occurs the punishment descends, you believed in it, meaning in God at the time of despair. And it was said: you believed in it, meaning you believed in the punishment at the time of its descent, now, there is an implication in it, meaning: it is said to you: now do you believe when the punishment occurs? and you were hastening it, denying and mocking.
10:52: 52- Then it will be said to those who did wrong, who associated partners with God, "Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn," in this world.
10:53: 53- And they ask you, meaning: they inquire of you, O Muhammad, is it true, meaning what you promise us of torment and the coming of the Hour, "say: Yes, by my Lord," meaning: yes, by my Lord, it is the truth, there is no doubt about it, and you will not escape, meaning: you will not escape the torment, because whoever is unable to do something has missed it.
10:54: 54- And if every soul that has wronged, that is, associated others with God, had all that is on the earth, it would offer it for ransom, on the Day of Resurrection. Ransom here means offering what will save one from the punishment. And they concealed their regret, Abu Ubaidah said: Its meaning is: They showed their regret, because that is not a day for patience and doing good. It was said: Its meaning is they concealed, that is, the leaders concealed their regret from the weak, for fear of their blame and their expression, when they saw the punishment and it was judged between them with justice, their punishment was finished, and they were not wronged.
10:55: 55- "Indeed, to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, the promise of God is true, but most of them do not know."
10:56: 56-It is He who gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.
10:57: 57- The Almighty said: O mankind, there has come to you instruction, a reminder, from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts, meaning: a cure for ignorance, for what is in the breasts. Meaning: a healing for the blindness of the hearts, and the chest is the place of the heart, and it is the most precious place in a person because it is close to the heart, and guidance, from misguidance, and mercy for the believers, and mercy is a blessing upon the needy, because if a king gave something to a king it would not be said that he showed him mercy, even though it was a blessing because he did not put it in the hands of the needy.
10:58: 58- The Almighty said: “Say: By the grace of God and His mercy.” Mujahid and Qatada said: The grace of God is faith, and His mercy is the Qur’an. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said: God’s grace and mercy is that He made us among its people. Ibn Omar said: God’s grace is Islam, and His mercy is His adornment in the heart. Khalid bin Maadan said: God’s grace is Islam, and His mercy is the Sunnah. It was said: God’s grace is faith, and His mercy is Paradise. So let them rejoice in that, meaning: let the believers rejoice that God has made them among His people. It is better than what they accumulate, meaning: what the disbelievers accumulate of money. It was said: both are reports about the disbelievers. Abu Ja`far and Ibn `Amir read: Falihrihu with a ya’, and Tajammuun with a ta’, and Ya`qub read both of them with a ta’, different from it, addressing the believers.
10:59: 59- Say O Muhammad to the infidels of Mecca, Have you seen what God has sent down to you of provision? He expressed creation by sending down, because what is on earth is good, and what was sent down from the sky of provision, of crops and udders, and you made of it unlawful and lawful, is what they made unlawful of crops and livestock such as the bahīrah, the sa'ibah, the wasīlah, and the Ḥam. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the saying of God the Most High: And they have assigned to God a share of what He created of crops and livestock Al-An'am 6:136. "Say: Has God permitted you," in this prohibition and permission, or rather, do you invent a lie against God, which is their saying: And God has commanded us to do it.
10:60: 60- And what will those who invent lies against God think on the Day of Resurrection? Do they think that God will not hold them accountable for it or punish them for it? Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, but most of them are not grateful."
10:61: 61- The Almighty said: And you are not. O Muhammad, in a matter, a deed, and the plural is affairs, and what you recite from it, from God, of the Qur’an, revealed, and it was said: from it, meaning from the matter of the Qur’an, revealed about it, then He addressed him and his nation and said: And you do not do any deed except that We are witnesses over you when you are involved in it, meaning: you enter and engage in it, the ha’ refers to the deed, and the addition: entering into the deed. Ibn al-Anbari said: you rush into it. It was said: you multiply in it. Addition: Pay a lot. "And nothing is hidden from your Lord", is absent from your Lord. Al-Kisa'i read "ya'zib" with a kasra on the zay, and the others read it with a damma, and these are two dialects. "From the weight of a dart", meaning: the weight of an atom, and "from" is a relative clause, and the dart is: the small red ant. "On the earth nor in the heaven nor smaller than that", meaning: from the dart, "nor greater" Hamza and Ya'qub read: with the ra' raised in both of them, in apposition to the position of the dart before the entry of "from", and the others read: with the nasb, intending the kasra, in apposition to the dart in the kasra. "Except in a clear book", which is the Preserved Tablet.
10:62: 62- The Almighty said: Indeed, the allies of God have nothing to fear, nor shall they grieve. They differed as to who deserves this name. Some of them said: They are those whom God the Almighty mentioned when He said:
10:63: 63- Those who believed and were fearing God. Some people said: They are those who love one another for the sake of God Almighty. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Husayn, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, may God be pleased with him, who said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “God has servants who are neither prophets nor martyrs, whom the prophets and martyrs envy for their closeness and their seat with God on the Day of Resurrection. He said: And in a corner of the people was a Bedouin, so he knelt on his knees and threw his hands up and said: Tell us, O Messenger of God, about them, who are they?” He said: I saw joy on the face of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: They are servants of God’s servants from different countries and tribes, there is no kinship between them to maintain ties, nor worldly wealth to exchange, they love one another for the sake of God’s spirit, God will make their faces light, and will make for them pulpits of pearls in front of the Most Merciful, people will be terrified but they will not be terrified, and people will be afraid but they will not be afraid.” It was narrated by Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Bahram, who said: Shahr bin Hawshab told us, Abdul Rahman bin Ghanem told me on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ash’ari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “He was asked: Who are the friends of God? He said: Those who, when they are seen, remind God.” It is narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God Almighty said: ‘My friends are among My servants who remember Me and I remember them.’”
10:64: 64- They will have good tidings in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. They differed about this good tidings: It was narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: "I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the Almighty's saying: 'They will have good tidings in this worldly life.' He said: It is a righteous vision that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him." Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me, that Abu Hurairah said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Nothing remains of prophecy except the good tidings. They said: What are the good tidings? He said: The good dream. It was said: Good report of this world is: good praise, and in the hereafter: Paradise. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abdul Razzaq bin Abi Shurayj told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni who said: I heard Abdullah bin Al-Samit say: Abu Dharr said: O Messenger of God, what if a man works for himself and people love him? He said: That is the immediate good report for the believer. Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj narrated this hadith on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid on the authority of Abu Imran, and he said: And people praise him for it. Al-Zuhri and Qatada said: It is the descent of angels with good report from God Almighty at the time of death. God Almighty said: The angels descend upon them, [saying], ‘Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised.’ (Fussilat 41:30). Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The good report of this world means: at death the angels come to them with the good report, and in the hereafter when the soul of the believer departs, it ascends to God, and he is given the good report of God’s pleasure. Al-Hasan said: It is what God gave the believers in His Book of His Paradise and His generous reward, such as His saying: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds (al-Baqarah 2:25), And give good tidings to the believers (al-Ahzab 33:47), And receive good tidings of Paradise (Fussilat 41:30). It was said: He gave them good report of this world through the Book and the Messenger that they are the friends of God, and he gave them good report of the graves and in their books of deeds of Paradise. There is no changing the words of God, no altering His words, no breaking His promise. That is the great attainment.
10:65: 65- "And let not their statement grieve you," meaning: the statement of the polytheists. The speech was completed here, then he began, saying: "Indeed, honor belongs to God, meaning victory and power belong to God all together," He is your supporter, the supporter of your religion, and the one who will take revenge on them. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: All glory belongs to God, meaning: God gives glory to whomever He wills, as He said in another verse: And to God belongs glory, and to His Messenger, and to the believers (al-Munafiqun 63:8), and the glory of the Messenger and the believers in God is all for God. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
10:66: 66- "Indeed, to God belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. And what follows those whom they invoke besides God as partners?" This is a question that means: And what follows those whom they invoke besides God as partners? It was said: They do not follow the truth, because they repeat it on the assumption that they are partners and intercede for us, and it is not as they assume. They follow nothing but conjecture, they think it will bring them closer to God Almighty, and they do nothing but guess, they lie.
10:67: 67- "It is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day to see," shining and seeing in it, as they say: a sleeping night and a pleasant life. Qatrib said: The Arabs say: the night became dark and the day became bright and seeing, meaning: it became full of darkness, light and sight. "Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen," hearing the consideration that it is something that only a knowledgeable and capable person can do.
10:68: 68- They said, meaning: the polytheists, God has taken a son, which is their saying that the angels are the daughters of God, Glory be to Him! He is the Self-sufficient, from His creation, To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, servants and kings, Indeed, you have, what you have, of authority, argument and proof, and of is a connection, Do you say about God what you do not know?
10:69: 69- "Say: Those who invent lies against God will not succeed." They will not be saved, and it was said: They will not remain in this world, but:
10:70: 70- Enjoyment, a little that they enjoy and a provision that they benefit from until the end of their terms, and Enjoyment is raised with an implied word, meaning: it is enjoyment, in this world, then to Us is their return, then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.
10:71: 71- The Almighty said: And recite to them the story of Noah, meaning: Read, O Muhammad, to the people of Mecca the story of Noah when he said to his people, and they are the sons of Cain, O my people, if my stay among you has become too much for you, too great and heavy for you, and my reminding you, and my admonition to you with the signs of God, with His proofs and evidence, and you have resolved to kill me and expel me, “then in God I have relied. So decide your plan,” meaning: decide your plan and resolve upon it, and your partners, meaning: and call upon your partners, meaning: your gods, and seek help from them so that they may unite with you. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: So decide your matter with your partners, so when with was left, it was in the accusative case. And Yaqub read: and your partners in the nominative case, meaning: So decide your matter, you and their partners. Then let not your affair be a burden to you, meaning: hidden and unclear, as they say: The crescent moon was a burden to the people, meaning: it was unclear to them, Then carry it out to me, meaning: carry out what is in your hearts and finish it. It is said: So-and-so carried it out if he died and passed away, and he carried out his debt if he finished it. It was said: It means: They came to me with killing and harm. It was said: Then do what you are going to do. This is like the magicians’ saying to Pharaoh: Then do what you are going to do (Ta-Ha 20:72), meaning: Do what you are going to do. And do not wait, and do not delay, and this is by way of making it impossible. God informed about Noah that he was confident in God Almighty’s victory and was not afraid of the plot of his people, knowing that they and their gods could neither benefit nor harm them except if God willed.
10:72: 72- But if you turn away i.e. you turn away from my words and accept my advice, then I have not asked of you for conveying the message and the call, any reward, making and compensation, my reward, what I do and my recompense, is only from God, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims, i.e. among the believers. It was said: among those who submit to God's command.
10:73: 73- But they denied him, meaning Noah, so We saved him and those with him in the ark and made them successors, meaning: We made those with him in the ark, the inhabitants of the earth, successors to those who perished. "And We drowned those who denied Our signs. So see what was the end of those who were warned," meaning: the final fate of those whom the messengers warned but did not believe.
10:74: 74- Then We sent after him messengers, that is, after a type of messengers. to their people, and they came to them with clear proofs, with clear evidence, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before, that is, in what the people of Noah had denied before, thus do We set a seal, that is, we seal, on the hearts of the aggressors.
10:75: 75- Then after them We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs, meaning: the nobles of his people, with Our signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people.
10:76: 76- So when there came to them, meaning: Pharaoh and his people came, the truth from Us, they said, 'This is clearly magic.'
10:77: 77- Moses said, 'Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' The meaning of the statement is, Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' So the first magic was omitted, as the statement was sufficient to indicate it. And magicians will not succeed.
10:78: 78- They said, meaning: Pharaoh and his people to Moses, Have you come to us to turn us away, to divert us. Qatada said to divert us, from what we found our fathers doing and you two will have pride, the kingdom and authority, in the land, the land of Egypt. Abu Bakr read: and it will be with the letter ya, and we are not believers in you, believing.
10:79: 79- And Pharaoh said, 'Bring me every learned magician.'
10:80: 80- So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, 'Cast down what you are going to cast down.'
10:81: 81- So when they threw, Moses said, 'What you have brought is magic.' Abu Amr and Abu Jaafar read: Al-Sihr with a long vowel for interrogation, and the others read it without a long vowel, as indicated by the reading of Ibn Masoud: What you have brought is magic without the alif and lam. "God will surely nullify it. God does not uphold the work of corrupters."
10:82: 82-And God will establish the truth with His words, with His verses, even though the criminals hate it.
10:83: 83- None believed in Moses, Moses did not believe in the signs he brought them, except a seed of his people, they differed about the ha in his people, it was said: it refers back to Moses, and he meant by them the believers from the Children of Israel who were in Egypt and left with him. Mujahid said: they were the children of those to whom Moses was sent from the Children of Israel, the fathers perished and the children remained. Others said: The letter ha refers to Pharaoh. Atiyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: They were a small number of Pharaoh’s people who believed, among them was Pharaoh’s wife, a believer from Pharaoh’s family, Pharaoh’s treasurer, his treasurer’s wife, and his hairdresser. Another narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were seventy thousand Coptic households from Pharaoh’s family, and their mothers were from the Children of Israel, so a man would follow his mother and maternal uncles. It was said: They are a people who escaped the killing of Pharaoh, and that is because when Pharaoh ordered the killing of the children of the Children of Israel, if a woman from the Children of Israel gave birth to a son, she would give him to a Copt for fear of being killed, so they grew up with the Copts, and converted to Islam on the day the magicians were defeated. Al-Farra’ said: They were called descendants because their fathers were Copts and their mothers were from the Children of Israel, just as the children of the Persians who fell to Yemen are called sons, because their mothers were not from the same race as their fathers. For fear of Pharaoh and his chiefs, it was said that by Pharaoh he meant the people of Pharaoh, i.e. for fear of the people of Pharaoh and their chiefs, as He said: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82), i.e. the people of the town. It was also said that he said: and their chiefs and Pharaoh are one because when the king is mentioned, it is understood from him he and his companions, as it is said that the caliph is mentioned first, meaning he and those with him. It was also said that he meant the chiefs of the offspring, because their chiefs were from the people of Pharaoh. To tempt them, i.e. to turn them away from their religion, and he did not say tempt them because he was speaking about Pharaoh and his people were like Pharaoh, And indeed, Pharaoh was haughty, arrogant, in the land, and indeed he was among the transgressors, those who exceeded the limit, because he was a slave and claimed divinity.
10:84: 84- "And Moses said, to the believers of his people, O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely upon Him, if you should be Muslims."
10:85: 85- "They said, 'In God we trust,' we relied, then they prayed and said, Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people," meaning: Do not make them prevail over us and do not destroy us by their hands, lest they think that we were not on the right path and thus increase in their transgression. Mujahid said: Do not punish us with a punishment from You, lest the people of Pharaoh say: If they were on the right path they would not have been punished and they think that they are better than us and thus become tempted.
10:86: 86-"And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people."
10:87: 87- The Almighty said: And We inspired Moses and his brother, Aaron, to establish houses for your people in Egypt. It is said: So-and-so established a house and a bed for himself if he took it, and I established it for him if I took it for him, and make your houses places of prayer. Most of the commentators said: The Children of Israel did not pray except in their churches and synagogues, and it was apparent, so when Moses was sent, Pharaoh ordered their destruction and prevented them from praying, so they were ordered to establish mosques in their homes and pray in them out of fear of Pharaoh. This is the saying of Ibrahim and Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Mujahed said: Moses and those with him feared that Pharaoh would pray in the congregational churches, so they were ordered to make mosques in their homes facing the Kaaba, and to pray in them secretly. Its meaning is: And make your homes facing the qiblah. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Kaaba was the qibla of Moses and those with him. And establish prayer and give good tidings to the believers, O Muhammad.
10:88: 88- The Almighty said: And Moses said, ‘Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment’, of worldly pleasures, and wealth in the life of this world, our Lord, that they may go astray from Your way. They differed about this lam. It was said: It is the lam of ki, meaning: I gave them so that You might tempt them so that they might go astray and be led astray, like His saying: We would have given them abundant water to test them thereby (al-Jinn 72:16). It was said: It is the lam of consequence, meaning: they go astray and the consequence of their matter is misguidance, like His saying: So Pharaoh’s family picked him up, to become for them an enemy and a grief (al-Qasas 28:8). His saying: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth. Mujahid said: Destroy it. Obliteration means annihilation. Most of the commentators said: He transformed it and changed its form. Qatada said: Their money, crops, crops, and jewels turned into stones. Muhammad bin Kaab said: He turned their sugar into stones. The man was with his wife in his bed, so they became two stones. The woman was standing baking bread, so she became a stone. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It has reached us that dirhams and dinars have become engraved stones in their original form, in wholes, halves, and thirds. Omar bin Abdul Aziz called for a map containing things from the remains of the Pharaoh’s family, and he took out from it a cracked egg and a cracked nut, and it was a stone. Al-Suddi said: God transformed their wealth into stones, palm trees, fruits, flour, and foods, and it was one of the nine signs. And harden their hearts, meaning: make them hard and seal them so that they do not soften or accept faith, so that they will not believe. It was said: It is an accusative in response to the supplication with the letter fa. It was also said: It is in apposition to His statement that they may go astray, meaning: that they may go astray so that they will not believe. Al-Farra’ said: It is a supplication in the subjunctive mood, as if he said: O God, so that they will not believe, until they see the painful punishment, which is drowning. Al-Suddi said: It means that their nation is in disbelief.
10:89: 89- God said to Moses and Aaron, Your prayer has been answered, it was attributed to them and the prayer was from Moses because it was narrated that Moses was praying and Aaron was saying Amen, and saying Amen is a prayer. In some al-Qasas 28:There were forty years between Moses' prayer and its answer. So stand firm, in the message and the call, and carry out My command until the punishment comes to them. And do not follow, a prohibition with the heavy nun, and its place is in the jussive mood. It is said in the singular Do not follow with the opening of the nun because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and with the breaking of the nun in the dual for this reason. Ibn Amir read with the lightening of the nun because the nun of emphasis is heavy and light, the path of those who do not know, meaning: And do not follow the path of those who are ignorant of the truth of My promise, for My promise is not broken, and My threat is descending upon Pharaoh and his people.
10:90: 90- And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, We crossed with them, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them, caught up with them and overtook them, Pharaoh and his soldiers, it is said: he pursued him and followed him if he caught up with him and overtook him, and he followed him with emphasis if he walked behind him and followed his example. It was said: they are one. In oppression and enmity, meaning: injustice and aggression. It was said: In oppression in speech and enmity in action. The sea had split for Moses and his people, and when Pharaoh and his soldiers reached the sea, they were afraid to enter it, so Gabriel preceded them on a thin horse and waded into the sea, and the horses rushed behind him, and when the last of them entered and they were the first to come out, the water closed over them. And the Almighty said: Until, when drowning overtook him, meaning: the water submerged him and his death was near, he said, 'I believe that,' Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the alif, meaning: I believe and said that he. Others read that with the fat-ha, meaning that she believed in it, There is no god but the one in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am among the Muslims. So Gabriel, peace be upon him, put some of the sea mud in his mouth.
10:91: 91-And he said: Now, and you have disobeyed before and were among the corrupters. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When God drowned Pharaoh, he said: I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: O Muhammad, if you had seen me when I take from the sea and put it in his mouth for fear that mercy would reach him." So when Moses informed his people of the destruction of Pharaoh and his people, the Children of Israel said: Pharaoh has not died. So God commanded the sea to throw Pharaoh on the shore, red and short, like a bull. The Children of Israel saw him, and from that time on, the water does not accept a dead person. That is what His saying:
10:92: 92- So today We will save you, meaning We will cast you onto a high place on the earth, which is: a high place. Jacob read We will save you with a light pronunciation, with your body, with your body with no soul in it. It was said: with your body: with your armor, and he had a famous armor studded with jewels, so they saw him in his armor and believed him. That you may be a sign to those who come after you, a lesson and a sermon, And indeed, many of the people, of Our signs, are heedless.
10:93: 93- And We certainly settled the Children of Israel We settled the Children of Israel after the destruction of Pharaoh, in a true abode, a true home, meaning: Egypt. It was said Jordan and Palestine, which is the Holy Land that God wrote as an inheritance for Abraham and his descendants. Ad-Dahhak said: It is Egypt and Ash-Sham, And We provided for them of the good things, the lawful things, and they did not differ meaning the Jews who were in the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in believing in him and that he was a prophet, until knowledge came to them meaning: the Qur'an and the statement that he is the Messenger of God, the truth and his religion is the truth. It was said: Until their known one came to them, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they knew him before his emergence. So knowledge means the known, just as it is said of a created being: creation. God Almighty said: This is the creation of God (Luqman 31:11), and it is said: This dirham was struck by the prince, meaning: struck by him. Your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ, of religion.
10:94: 94- The Almighty said: If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, meaning: the Qur’an, then ask those who read the Scripture before you, and they will tell you that it is written in their Torah. It was said: This is addressed to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is someone else, according to the custom of the Arabs, as they address a man and respond to someone else, like the Almighty’s saying: O Prophet, fear God (al-Ahzab 33:1). He addressed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it are the believers, as evidenced by the fact that he said: Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Aware and did not say: with what you do. And he said: O Prophet, when you divorce women (al-Talaq 65:1). It was said: People during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were divided between those who believed, those who disbelieved, and those who doubted. This address is to the people of doubt, and its meaning is: If you, O human being, are in doubt about what We have revealed to you of guidance through the tongue of Our Messenger Muhammad, then ask those who read the Book before you. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: He means those who believed from the People of the Book, Abdullah bin Salam and his companions, so they testify to the truthfulness of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and inform you of his prophethood. Al-Farra’ said: God Almighty knew that His Messenger was not in doubt, but He mentioned it according to the custom of the Arabs, one of them would say to his slave: If you are my slave, then obey me, and he would say to his son: Do such and such if you are my son, and this would not be in the form of doubt. The truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
10:95: 95- "And do not be among those who deny the signs of God, lest you be among the losers." All of this is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is someone else.
10:96: 96- The Almighty said: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect, “is incumbent upon them,” “it has been said: His curse.” Qatada said: God’s wrath. It has been said: The word is His saying: These are in the Fire, and I do not care. They do not believe.
10:97: 97- "And if every sign came to them, indicating, until they see the painful punishment", Al-Akhfash said: He feminized the verb "every" because it is added to the feminine, which is his saying: "sign, and the word every" is the same for the masculine and feminine.
10:98: 98- The Almighty said: Why was there not meaning: why was there not, a village, and its meaning is: there was not a village because in the question there is a kind of denial, meaning: the people of a village, believed, when witnessing the punishment, so their faith benefited them, in the state of hardship, except the people of Jonah, for his faith benefited them at that time. And people is the accusative of the discontinuous exception, meaning: but the people of Jonah, when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and gave them enjoyment for a time, which is the time when their appointed times would come to an end. They differed as to whether they saw the punishment with their own eyes or not. Some of them said: Did they see evidence of the punishment? The majority are of the opinion that they saw the punishment with their own eyes, as evidenced by His statement: We removed from them the punishment of disgrace. The discovery is after the occurrence or if it is close. The story of the verse - as mentioned by Abdullah bin Masoud, Saeed bin Jubair, Wahb and others - is that the people of Yunus were in Nineveh, in the land of Mosul. God sent Yunus to them calling him to faith. He called them but they refused. It was said to him: Tell them that the punishment will come to them in the morning in three days. So he told them that, and they said: We have not found him to lie, so look. If he spends the night among you, then he is nothing, and if he does not spend the night, then know that the punishment will come to you in the morning. So in the middle of that night, Yunus came out from among them, and when they woke up, the punishment covered them and was above their heads the length of a mile.
