Wahb said: The sky was covered with a huge black cloud, smoking a lot of smoke, and it descended until it covered them in their city and their roofs turned black. When they saw that, they were certain of destruction, so they sought their prophet Yunus but did not find him. God cast repentance into their hearts, so they went out to the plain with themselves, their women, their children and their animals, and they put on sackcloth and showed faith and repentance, and they were sincere in their intentions and separated every mother and her child from the people and the livestock, so some of them yearned for one another, and their voices rose, and their voices mingled with their voices, and they cried out and beseeched God Almighty, and they said, We believe in what Yunus brought. So his Lord had mercy on them, so He answered their prayer and removed the punishment from them after He had led them astray. That was on the day of Ashura. Yunus had gone out and remained waiting for the punishment and destruction of his people but he did not see anything, and whoever lied and had no evidence was killed. Yunus said: How can I return to my people when I have lied to them? So he set out, blaming his Lord and angry with his people. He came to the sea and found people riding a ship. They recognized him and carried him without pay. When he entered it and it was in the middle of them and it began to move, the ship stopped, neither returning nor advancing. The people of the ship said, There is something wrong with our ship. Yunus said, "I know its matter. A man of great sin has boarded it." They said, Who is he? He said, "I am. Throw me into the sea." They said, We would not throw you away from us until we have an excuse for your affair. They drew lots three times and his lot was lost. The fish was at the foot of the ship, its mouth open, awaiting the command of its Lord concerning it. Yunus said, By God, you will all perish, or you will throw me into it. So they threw him into it and departed, and the fish took him. It was narrated that God Almighty inspired a great whale to head towards the ship. When the people of the ship saw it, it was like a great mountain, with its mouth open and looking at those on the ship as if it was seeking something. They were afraid of it. When Jonah saw it, he threw himself into the water. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: He went out angry with his people and came to the Roman Sea and there was a laden ship, so he boarded it and when the ship became rough, it tipped over until they were about to drown. The sailors said: Here is a disobedient man or a runaway slave, and this is the rule of a ship if there is a runaway on it it does not sail. It is our rule to draw lots in such a case, and whoever the lot falls on we throw him into the sea, and it is better for one person to drown than for the ship to sink with everything on it. So they drew lots three times, and the lot fell on Yunus every time. Yunus said: I am the disobedient man and the runaway slave, so he threw himself into the water and a whale swallowed him. Then another whale came bigger than him and swallowed this whale, and God revealed to the whale: Do not harm a hair of it, for I have made your belly its prison and have not made it food for you. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The whale was called: We did not make Jonah a food for you, but we made your belly a protection and a place of prostration for it. It was narrated that he stood up before the drawing of lots and said: I am the disobedient and runaway slave. They said: Who are you? He said: I am Yunus bin Matta. They recognized him and said: We will not meet you, O Messenger of God, but we will cast lots. So the lot fell on him, and he threw himself into the water. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: The whale swallowed him and threw him to the bottom of the seventh earth. He was in its belly for forty nights. He heard the pebbles glorifying God, so he called out in the darkness: There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I have been among the wrongdoers. God answered him and commanded the whale, so it threw him on the shore of the sea, and he was like a starving chick. God caused a gourd tree to grow over him, so he began to take shelter under it and assigned a squash tree to drink from its milk. The tree dried up, so he wept over it, so God revealed to him: You weep over a tree that has dried up, but you do not weep over a hundred thousand or more whom I wanted to destroy. So Jonah went out and saw a young boy grazing. He said: Who are you, young boy? He said: From the people of Yunus. He said: When you return to them, tell them that I met Yunus. The boy said: You know that if I do not have proof, I will be killed. Yunus, peace be upon him, said: This spot and this tree will testify for you. The boy said to him: Order them. Yunus said: When this boy comes to you, testify for him. They said: Yes. So the boy returned and said to the king: I met Yunus, and the king ordered him to be killed. He said: I have proof, so send with me. So he came to the spot and the tree and said: I ask you by God, do you have Yunus as a witness? They said: Yes. So the people returned terrified and said to the king: The tree and the land have testified for him. So the king took the boy by the hand and seated him in his seat and said: You have more right to this place than I. So that boy established their rule for them for forty years.
10:99: 99- The Almighty’s saying: And if your Lord had willed, O Muhammad, “those on earth would have believed, all of them together. So would you compel the people in order that they become believers?” This is a consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he was keen for all people to believe, so God informed him of the solution to his remembrance: that no one believes except he for whom God has predestined happiness, and no one goes astray except he for whom misery has predestined.
10:100: 100- "And it is not for a soul", and it is not appropriate for a soul. It was said: It is not for a soul, "to believe except by God's permission", Ibn Abbas said: By God's command. Ata' said: By God's will. It was said: By God's knowledge. "And He places the impurity", Abu Bakr read: "And We place it" with a noon, and the rest with a ya', meaning: And God places the impurity, meaning: the punishment, which is the punishment, "upon those who do not reason", from God's command and prohibition.
10:101: 101- "Say: Look," meaning: Say to the polytheists who ask you for signs: Look, What is in the heavens and the earth? of signs, evidence, and lessons. In the heavens are the sun, the moon, the stars, and others, and on the earth are the mountains, seas, rivers, trees, and others. And signs and warnings do not avail, the messengers, for a people who do not believe, and this is about a people whom God knows will not believe.
10:102: 102- Do they then await, meaning: the polytheists of Mecca, except the like of the days of those who have passed on, who passed away, before them, of the deniers of the nations? Qatada said: He means the events of God with the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud. The Arabs call torment days, and bliss days, like His statement: And remind them of the days of God Ibrahim-5, and everything that has passed you of good and evil are days, "Say: Then wait, indeed, I am with you among those who wait."
10:103: 103- Then We will save Our messengers, Yaqub read Nanji with a light pronunciation that is different from it, and those who believed, with them when the punishment descends, meaning: We saved, future meaning past, likewise, as We saved them, truly, obligatory, upon Us We will save the believers, Al-Kisa'i, Hafs, and Yaqub read Nanji with a light pronunciation and the others with a heavy pronunciation, and Naja and Anja have the same meaning.
10:104: 104-The Almighty said: Say, ‘O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion,’ which I call you to. If it is said: How did he say: If you are in doubt, and they believed that what he brought was false? It was said: There were doubters among them, so they are the ones meant by the verse, or that when they saw the verses they were disturbed and doubted their situation and the situation of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Almighty said: I do not worship those you worship besides God, of idols, but I worship God, who takes your souls, who causes you to die and takes your souls, and I have been commanded to be among the believers.
10:105: 105-His statement: And that you direct your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth. Ibn Abbas said: Your actions. It was also said: Be steadfast in the religion, inclining toward truth. And do not be of those who associate others with God.
10:106: 106- And do not invoke, nor worship, besides God that which neither benefits you, if you obey it, nor harms you, if you disobey it, for if you do, and worship other than God, then you would be among the wrongdoers, who harm themselves and place worship in the wrong place.
10:107: 107- And if God should touch you with harm, that is, if He should afflict you with hardship and affliction, there is none who can remove it, that is, none who can repel it, "except Him. And if He intends for you good," prosperity, blessing, and abundance, there is none who can repel His favor, that is, none who can prevent His provision. He afflicts with it, with each one of the harm and good, "whoever He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
10:108: 108- "Say, 'O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord,' meaning: the Qur'an and Islam. 'So whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment,' meaning: to his own detriment, and I am not a guardian over you,' a guarantor, who will preserve your deeds. Ibn Abbas said: The verse on fighting abrogated it.
10:109: 109-And follow what is revealed to you and be patient until God decides, by giving you victory, subduing your enemy, and making His religion prevail, and He is the best of judges, so He decided to fight the polytheists and to impose the jizya on the People of the Book, who pay it willingly and are humbled.
11:1: Meccan, except for the words: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day, which are one hundred and twenty-three verses. 1- “Alif, Lam, Ra. The Book,” meaning: This is a Book. Its verses are perfected, Ibn Abbas said: It was not abrogated by a book as the books and laws were abrogated by it. Then it is explained in detail, it is explained with rulings and what is permissible and what is forbidden. Al-Hasan said: It is perfected with commands and prohibitions, then it is explained in detail with promises and threats. Qatada said: It is perfected, God has perfected it, so there is no difference or contradiction in it. Mujahid said: It is explained in detail. It was said: It is explained in detail, meaning: It was revealed little by little, from One Who is Wise and Acquainted.
11:2: 2- That you worship none but God", meaning: In that book: that you worship none but God, and the position of "that" is nominative. It was said: Its position is genitive, its meaning: that you worship none but God, "I am to you from Him" meaning: from God "a warner, to the disobedient, and a bearer of good tidings", to the obedient.
11:3: 3- And that, in apposition to the first, seek forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him, meaning: return to Him in obedience. Al-Farra' said: Then here means and, meaning: and repent to Him, because seeking forgiveness is repentance and repentance is seeking forgiveness. It was said: Ask forgiveness from your Lord for your sins, then repent to Him in the new chapter. He will grant you good provision, He will grant you a good life in ease, tranquility, security and spaciousness. Some of them said: A good life is contentment with what is easy and patience with what is destined. Until a specified term, until death, and every possessor of virtue will be given his virtue, meaning: and every possessor of good deeds in this world will be given his reward and recompense in the Hereafter. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Whoever increases his obedience in this world, his degrees will increase in the Hereafter in Paradise, because degrees are based on deeds. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever’s good deeds outweigh his bad deeds will enter Paradise, and whoever’s bad deeds outweigh his good deeds will enter Hell, and whoever’s good deeds and bad deeds are equal will be among the people of A’raf, then he will enter Paradise after that. It was said: Everyone who has virtue will be given his virtue, meaning: whoever works for God Almighty, God will guide him in the future in obedience to Him. And if you turn away, that is, turn away, then I fear for you the punishment of a great Day, which is the Day of Resurrection.
11:4: 4-To God is your return, and He is over all things competent.
11:5: 5- The Almighty said: Indeed, they turn away their breasts. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Al-Akhns bin Shuraik, who was a man of sweet speech and sweet appearance. He would meet the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with what he liked, but he concealed in his heart what he disliked. His saying: They hide their hearts means: They hide the rancor and enmity in their hearts. Abdullah bin Shaddad said: It was revealed about some hypocrites who, when they passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would bend their chests and backs, lower their heads, and cover their faces so that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not see them. Qatada said: They used to bow their chests so that they would not hear the Book of God Almighty or mention Him. It was said: A man from the infidels would enter his house, lower his curtain, bend his back, and cover himself with his garment, and say: Does God know what is in my heart? Al-Suddi said: They turn away means: they turn away with their hearts, from their saying: I turned away my reins. It was also said: They turn away, and from this comes the word turn away the garment. Ibn Abbas read: yathnawuni with the weight of yahluli making the verb a source, and its meaning is exaggeration in the praising. To hide from Him, meaning: from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mujahid said: To hide from God if they can, Except when they cover themselves with their garments, covering their heads with their garments, “He knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.” Al-Azhari said: The meaning of the verse from beginning to end is: The state of those who harbor enmity against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is not hidden from us. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Sabah told us, Hajjaj told us: Ibn Jurayj said, Muhammad bin Abbad bin Ja`far told me that he heard Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, recite: Indeed, they turn their breasts away, so he said: I asked him about it. He said: There were people who liked to relieve themselves and then go to heaven, and to have intercourse with their wives and then go to heaven, so that was revealed about them.
11:6: 6- The Almighty said: And there is no creature on the earth, meaning: there is no creature, of is a relative clause, and the creature is every animal that crawls on the face of the earth. His saying: Except that it is upon God to provide for her, meaning: He is the one who is responsible for that as a favor, and it is up to His will. If He wills, He provides for her, and if He wills, He does not provide for her. It was said: On means: From, that is: from God’s provision. Mujahed said: Whatever provision she received was from God Almighty, and perhaps He did not provide for her until she died of hunger. And He knows its resting place and its place of deposit. Ibn Muqsim said: This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Its resting place is the place where it takes refuge and settles in it day and night, and its place of deposit is the place where it is buried if it dies. Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: The place of rest is the wombs of mothers and the place of repository is the place where you die. Ata’ said: The place of rest is the wombs of mothers and the place of repository is the loins of fathers. It was narrated by Saeed bin Jubair, Ali bin Abi Talha, and Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: The place of settlement is Paradise and Hell, and the place of deposit is the grave, based on the Almighty’s saying in describing Paradise and Hell: A good place to settle and to stay (al-Furqan 25:76). All is in a clear book, meaning: all is recorded in the Preserved Tablet before He created it.
11:7: 7- The Almighty said: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was over the water, before He created the heavens and the earth, and that water was on the wind. Kaab said: God Almighty created a green ruby, then looked at it with awe and it became trembling water. Then He created the wind, and put the water on its back, then He placed the throne on the water. Damrah said: God Almighty’s throne was over the water, then He created the heavens and the earth, and created the pen and wrote with it what He created and what was to come of His creation, then that book praised and glorified God for a thousand years before He created anything of His creation. To test you, to examine you, and He knows best, which of you is best in deed, who obeys God and is most pious in avoiding what God Almighty has forbidden. And if you say, O Muhammad, Indeed, you will be resurrected, that is, after death, those who disbelieve will surely say, ‘This is not but obvious magic,’ meaning the Qur’an. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: a magician, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
11:8: 8- And if We delay the punishment from them for a limited term, for a limited period, and the root of the word nation is: a group, so it is as if he said: until the loan of one nation and the coming of another nation they will say, 'What is holding it back?' What is holding it back? They say it to hasten the punishment and to mock it, meaning: that it is nothing. God Almighty said: Behold, the Day will come upon them, meaning: the torment, not averted from them, it will not be averted from them, and that which they used to ridicule will befall them, befall them, that which they used to ridicule, meaning: the consequences of their ridicule.
11:9: 9- The Almighty’s saying: And if We let man taste mercy from Us, a blessing and abundance, and then take it away from him, meaning: We take it away from him, he is indeed despairing, despondent in hardship, ungrateful for the blessing.
11:10: 10- And if We let him taste a blessing after a hardship had befallen him, after a calamity had befallen him, he will surely say, 'The bad things have departed from me,' the hardships have been removed from me, Indeed, he is joyful and boastful, the most insolent, and joy is: pleasure in the heart in attaining what is desired, and pride is: arrogance towards people by enumerating virtues, and that is forbidden.
11:11: 11- Except for those who are patient, Al-Farra' said: This is an isolated exception, meaning: But those who are patient and do righteous deeds, for if hardship befalls them they are patient, and if they attain a blessing they are grateful, for them is forgiveness, for their sins, and a great reward, which is Paradise.
11:12: 12- Perhaps you, O Muhammad, will abandon some of what is revealed to you, so do not convey it to them. This is because when the infidels of Mecca said: Bring a Qur'an other than this (Yunus 10:15) that does not contain insults to our gods, they wanted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to abandon their gods openly, so God Almighty revealed: Perhaps you would abandon some of what is revealed to you, meaning: cursing the gods, and your breast would be constricted by it, meaning: perhaps your breast would be constricted that they would say, meaning: that they would say, Why was a treasure not sent down to him, that he would spend, or an angel came with him, to confirm him, said Abdullah bin Abi Umayya Al-Makhroomi. God Almighty said: You are only a warner, you are only responsible for conveying the message, and God is, over all things, Disposer of affairs, Guardian.
11:13: 13- "Or do they say, 'He invented it,' rather, they say, He fabricated it. Say, Then bring ten fabricated surahs like it." If it is said: He said in Surat Yunus 10:Then bring a surah like it, and they were unable to do so, so how did he say: Then bring ten surahs, so it is like a man saying to another: Give me a dirham, and he is unable to do so, so he says: Give me ten? Answer: Surah Hud was revealed first. Al-Mubarrad denied this and said: Rather, Surah Yunus was revealed first. He said: The meaning of his statement in Surah Yunus 10:Then bring a surah like it, is: like it in the report of the unseen, the rulings, the promise and the threat. But they were unable to do so, so he said to them in Surah Hud 11:If you are unable to bring a surah like it in the report, the rulings, the promise and the threat, then bring ten surahs like it without report, promise or threat. Rather, it is merely eloquence. And call upon whomever you can, and seek help from whomever you can, other than God, if you should be truthful.
11:14: 14- If they do not respond to you, O companions of Muhammad: It was said: Its wording is plural and what is meant by it is the messengers, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone. Know, it was said: This is addressed to the believers. It was also said: To the polytheists, that it was sent down with the knowledge of God, meaning: the Qur’an. It was also said: He sent it down and in it was His knowledge, that there is no god but Him, meaning: Know that there is no god but Him. Are you Muslims? Its wording is a question but its meaning is a command, meaning: Submit.
11:15: 15- The Almighty’s saying: Whoever desires the life of this world, meaning: whoever desires the life of this world, and its adornment, was revealed regarding everyone who does a deed with the intention of other than God Almighty. We will fully repay them for their deeds therein, meaning: We will fully repay them for their deeds in this world by providing them with abundant provision, avoiding hardships, and the like. And therein they will not be deprived, meaning: in this world their portion will not be diminished.
11:16: 16- Those are the ones who will have nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire, and what they did therein will be in vain meaning: in this world, and in vain, what they used to do. They differed about the meaning of this verse. Mujahid said: They are the people of hypocrisy. We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What I fear most for you is minor polytheism. They said: O Messenger of God, what is minor polytheism? He said: Hypocrisy.” It was said: This is about the infidels. As for the believer: he wants this world and the hereafter, and his desire for the hereafter is predominant, so he is rewarded for his good deeds in this world, and is recompensed for them in the hereafter. We narrated on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty does not wrong the believer in a good deed. He is rewarded for it with provision in this world and recompense for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed with his good deeds in this world until when he reaches the Hereafter, he has no good deed for which he can be given anything good.”
11:17: 17- The Almighty’s saying: Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord? It is said that there is an omission in the verse, and its meaning is: Is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord like he who desires the life of this world and its adornments, or is he who is on clear evidence from his Lord like he who is in misguidance and ignorance? What is meant by the one who is on clear evidence from his Lord is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And a witness from Him follows him, meaning: someone follows him who testifies to his truthfulness. They differed regarding this witness: Ibn Abbas, Alqamah, Ibrahim, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, and most of the commentators said: It is Gabriel, peace be upon him. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: It is the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He is an angel who protects him and guides him. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: It is the Qur’an, its organization and its miracle. It was said: He is Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Ali said: There is no man from Quraysh about whom a verse of the Qur’an was not revealed. A man said to him: And what was revealed about you? He said: And a witness from him recites it. It was said: A witness to it is the Gospel. And before it, meaning: before the coming of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: before the revelation of the Qur’an. The Book of Moses, meaning: the Book of Moses was an Imam and a mercy, for those who followed it, meaning: the Torah, which confirms the Qur’an and is a witness for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Those believe in it, meaning: the Companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: He meant those who converted to Islam from the People of the Book. And whoever disbelieves in it, meaning: in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: in the Qur’an, of the parties, of the disbelievers from among the people of all religions, the Fire is his promised destination. Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Al-Ziyadi told us, Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one from this nation hears of me, neither Jew nor Christian, and then dies without believing in that with which I was sent, except that he will be among the people of the Fire.” God Almighty says: So be not in doubt about it, meaning: in doubt about it, It is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.
11:18: 18- "And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God," claiming that He has a son or a partner, meaning: no one is more unjust than him. "Those," meaning: the liars and those who deny, "will be presented before their Lord," and He will ask them about their deeds. And the witnesses say, meaning: the angels who were recording their deeds, said Mujahid. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. They are the prophets and messengers, peace and blessings be upon them, and this is what Ad-Dahhak said. Qatada said: All creatures. We narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God brings the believer close, places His cloak over him, and conceals him, and says: Do you recognize such-and-such sin? Do you recognize such-and-such sin? He says: Yes, O Lord. Then, when He has made him acknowledge his sins and he sees in himself that he has perished, He says: I concealed them for you in this world, and I forgive them for you today. So he is given his book of good deeds.” As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, He calls out to them in front of all creation, “These are the ones who lied about their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.”
11:19: 19- Those who hinder [people] from the way of God, prevent people from the religion of God, and seek to make it crooked, and they are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers.
11:20: 20- Those were not able to escape, Ibn Abbas said: forerunners. Qatada said: fleeing. Muqatil said: passing. On the earth and they had no protectors besides God, meaning supporters and helpers who would protect them from Our punishment, the punishment will be doubled for them, meaning: their punishment will be increased. It was said: the punishment will be doubled for them because they led others astray and the followers followed their example. They could not hear, nor could they see. Qatada said: They were deaf to hearing the truth, so they did not hear it, and they could not see the guidance. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: God, the Almighty, informed us that He stood between the polytheists and their obedience to Him in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, He said: They could not hear, which is His obedience, and as for the Hereafter, He said: So they could not, with their eyes lowered.
11:21: 21- Those are the ones who have lost their souls, they have deceived themselves, and what they used to invent has gone astray from them, they claim about the intercession of angels and idols.
11:22: 22- No crime, meaning: truly. It was also said: Yes. Al-Farra' said: Inevitably, that in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers, meaning: more than others, even if everyone is in loss.
11:23: 23- Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds and humbled themselves, Ibn Abbas said: feared. Qatada said: repented. Mujahid said: were reassured. It was also said: were humble. And His statement: to their Lord, meaning: to their Lord. Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
11:24: 24- The parable of the two groups, the believer and the disbeliever, "is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison?" Al-Farra' said: He did not say are they equal, because the blind and the deaf are in a position as if they are one, because they are from the description of the disbeliever, and the seeing and the hearing are in a position as if they are one, because they are from the description of the believer. So will you not remember? That is: will you not be admonished.
11:25: 25- The Almighty said: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], ‘Indeed, I am to you a clear warner.’ Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read ani with the opening of the hamza, meaning: that I am. The rest read it with the breaking of the hamza, meaning: “so he said, ‘I am,’ because in sending there is the meaning of saying: I am to you a clear warner.
11:26: 26- "That you worship none but God. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day," meaning: painful. Ibn Abbas said: Noah, peace be upon him, was sent after forty years, and he continued calling his people for nine hundred and fifty years, and he lived sixty years after the flood, and his age was one thousand and fifty years. Muqatil said: He was sent when he was one hundred years old. It was said: He was sent when he was fifty years old. It was said: He was sent when he was two hundred and fifty years old, and he continued calling his people for nine hundred and fifty years, and he lived after the flood for two hundred and fifty years, so his age was one thousand four hundred and fifty years. God Almighty said: And he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years (al-Ankabut 29:14), meaning: He remained among them calling.
11:27: 27- Then the chiefs of his people who disbelieved said: The chiefs are the nobles and leaders. We do not see you, Noah, except as a human being, a human being, "like us. And we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us", our lowest, and the lowest is the lowest of everything and the plural is: arzal, then it is pluralized as arazal, like: dog and dogs and akalib, and he said in Surat Ash-Shu'ara: And the lowest of us followed you meaning: the lowest. And Ikrimah said: the weavers and the shoemakers, in the beginning of the opinion, Abu Amr read badi with a hamza, meaning: the beginning of the opinion, they mean that they followed you in the beginning of the opinion without deliberation and thinking, and if they had thought they would not have followed you. The others read without a hamza, meaning the apparent opinion from their saying: bada'a something: if it appeared, its meaning: they followed you outwardly without contemplating and thinking inwardly. Mujahed said: It is seen with the eyes, “We do not see that you have any advantage over us. Rather, we think you are liars.”
11:28: 28- He said, Noah, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord," meaning: a statement from my Lord, and He has given me mercy, meaning: guidance and knowledge, from Himself, then it has become hidden from you, meaning: hidden and confused for you. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read: and it has become hidden from you, with a damma on the 'ayn and a shaddah on the 'mim, meaning: it has become doubtful and confusing for you. Shall We impose it upon you, meaning: Shall We impose upon you the clear evidence and mercy, while you are averse to it, not wanting it. Qatada said: If the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, were able to force their people to believe, they would have forced them to believe, but they were not able to.
11:29: 29- His saying: And O my people, I do not ask of you any wealth for it, meaning: for the revelation and conveying the message, a metaphor for something not mentioned, My reward, what is my recompense, is only from God, and I will not drive away those who believe, this is evidence that they asked him to drive away the believers, They will meet their Lord, meaning: they will go to their Lord in the afterlife, and He will reward those who drove them away, but I see that you are a people behaving ignorantly.
11:30: 30- O my people, who will protect me from God? Who will protect me from God's punishment? If I expel them, will you not remember? Will you not be admonished?
11:31: 31- And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of God, so that I can bring from them what you ask for, nor do I know the unseen, so that I can tell you what you want. It was said that when they said to Nuh 71:Those who believed in you only followed you in what you see of them, Noah said in response to them: And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of the unseen of God, from which He knows what people conceal, nor do I know the unseen, so that I know what they conceal in their souls, so my way is to accept what is apparent of their faith, nor do I say that I am an angel, this is the answer to their saying: We see you only as a human being like us. "And I do not say to those whom your eyes despise," meaning: those whom your eyes despise and belittle, meaning: the believers, because they said: They are the lowest of us, "God will never give them any good," meaning: success, faith, and reward, "God knows best what is in their souls, of good and evil than me, then I would be among the wrongdoers," if I said this.
11:32: 32-“They said, ‘O Noah, you have argued with us,’ you have disputed with us, ‘and prolonged your argument with us. So bring us what you threaten us with,’ of punishment, ‘if you should be of the truthful.’”
11:33: 33- He said, 'Only God will bring it upon you if He wills,' meaning: the punishment, and you will not escape by two things.
11:34: 34- And my advice will not benefit you, meaning my advice, if I wanted to advise you, if God wants to mislead you, to lead you astray, He is your Lord, to Him belongs the judgment and the command, and to Him you will be returned, so He will reward you for your deeds.
11:35: 35- Or do they say, 'He invented it'? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He meant Noah, peace be upon him. Muqatil said: He meant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Say, 'If I invented it, then upon me is my crime,' meaning: my sin and the consequences of my crime. Crime is: earning a sin. And I am innocent of what you commit, I will not be held accountable for your sins.
11:36: 36- The Almighty said: And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The people of Noah, peace be upon him, used to beat Noah until he fell, then they would throw him in a felt blanket, and they would throw him into the bottom of a house, and they would think that he had died, but he would come out the next day and call them to God Almighty. It was narrated that an old man among them came leaning on a stick, and his son was with him, and he said: O my son, do not be deceived by this crazy old man. He said to him: O my father, give me the stick. So he took the stick from his father and struck Noah until he wounded him with a terrible wound. Then God Almighty revealed to him: None of your people will believe except those who have already believed. “So do not be sad” meaning: do not be grieved, over what they used to do, for I will destroy them and save you from them. Then Noah prayed against them and said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers Noah 26. Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair al-Laythi that he had heard that they used to beat him and strangle him until he fainted. When he regained consciousness, he would say: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know. Then, when they persisted in their sin and the affliction became severe upon them, and generation after generation would wait, and no generation would come but that it would be more evil than the one before it, until the last of them would say: This one was with our fathers and grandfathers, like this madman, and they would not accept anything from him. So he complained to God Almighty and said: My Lord, I have called upon my people night and day, until he said: My Lord, do not leave on the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers. Then God Almighty revealed to him:
11:37: 37- "And construct the ark under Our eyes, Ibn Abbas said, with our sight. Muqatil said, with our knowledge. It was also said, with our protection." And We revealed, with Our command. “And do not speak to Me concerning those who have wronged. Indeed, they are to be drowned,” with the flood. It was said that its meaning is do not speak to Me concerning giving the unbelievers respite, for I have decreed that they be drowned. And it was said: Do not speak to Me concerning your son Canaan and your wife Wa’ilah, for they are to perish with the people. In the story, Gabriel came to Noah, peace be upon him, and said: Your Lord, the Almighty, commands you to build the ark. He said: How can I do it when I am not a carpenter? He said: Your Lord says, do it, for you are under My eye. So he took the axe and began to do it without making a mistake. It was said: God inspired him to make it like the trunk of a bird.
11:38: 38- The Almighty said: "And build the ark." So when God the Almighty commanded him to build the ark, Noah, peace be upon him, began to build the ark on behalf of his people. He began to cut wood, strike iron, and prepare the equipment for the ark from tar and other things. His people would pass by him while he was working and mock him, saying: O Noah, have you become a carpenter after the prophecy? And God made the wombs of their women barren, so that no children were born to them. The people of the Torah claimed that God commanded him to build the ark from teak wood, to make it azure, to coat it with pitch inside and out, to make its length eighty cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height in the sky thirty cubits, and the cubit reaches the shoulder, and to make it three layers, a lower, a middle, and an upper, and to make windows in it, so Noah did as God Almighty commanded him. Ibn Abbas said: Noah built the ship in two years. The ship was three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high in the sky. It was made of teak wood. He made three bellies for it. In the lower bellie he carried wild beasts, predators, and vermin, and in the middle bellie he carried the animals and livestock. He and those with him rode in the upper bellie with whatever provisions he needed. Qatada said: Its door was in its width. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan: Its length was one thousand two hundred cubits and its width was six hundred cubits. The first known thing is that its length was three hundred cubits. On the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, he said: Noah, peace be upon him, spent a hundred years planting and cutting trees, and a hundred years building the ark. It was said: He planted the tree for forty years and dried it for forty years. On the authority of Kaab al-Ahbar, Noah built the ship in thirty years, and it was narrated that it took three years. Layers, the lower layer for animals and beasts, the middle layer for humans, and the upper layer for birds. When the dung of the animals increased, God inspired Noah to poke the elephant’s tail, so he poke it and a male and female pig fell from it, and they headed towards the dung. When the tar fell into the belly of the ship, it began to gnaw at it and its ropes, so God Almighty inspired him to strike between the eyes of the lion, so he struck and a male and female cat came out of its nostril, and they headed towards the mouse. God the Almighty said: And every time a group of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him. They would say: This one who claims to be a prophet has become a carpenter. It was narrated that they would say to him: O Noah, what are you doing? He would say: I will build a house that walks on water. They would laugh at him. “He said: If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you,” if you witness God’s punishment, as you ridicule. So if it is said: How is it permissible to ridicule a prophet? It is said: This is based on a double meaning, meaning: If you treat me ignorantly, then I will treat you ignorantly when the punishment descends upon you. It is also said: Its meaning is: If you ridicule us, then you will see the consequences of your ridicule.
11:39: 39- "Then you will know who will be afflicted with a punishment that will disgrace him, that will humiliate him, and upon whom will be inflicted, that will befall him, an everlasting punishment," that is, permanent.
11:40: 40- Until when Our command comes Our punishment, and the oven overflows, they differed about the oven: Ikrimah and Al-Zuhri said: It is the surface of the earth, and that is because it was said to Nuh 71:If you see water overflowing on the surface of the earth, then board the ship. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The oven has risen, meaning: the dawn and the light of morning have risen. Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Al-Sha’bi said: It is the oven in which bread is baked, and this is the opinion of most commentators. And the narration of Atiyah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan said: It was an oven made of stones, Eve was talking in it, then it went to Noah, peace be upon him, and it was said to Nuh 71:If you see water bubbling from the oven, then you and your companions get on board. They differed about its location. Mujahid and Al-Sha'bi said: It was in the direction of Kufa. Al-Sha'bi used to swear: The oven did not boil except from the direction of Kufa. He said: Noah built the ark in the interior of the Kufa mosque. The oven was to the right of the person entering, next to the Kinda Gate, and the boiling water from it was a sign for Noah, peace be upon him. Muqatil said: That was Adam’s oven, and it was in the Levant in a place called Ain Warda. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He was in India. Boiling: boiling. God Almighty says: We said, ‘Load in it’, meaning in the ship, of every pair. Pairs: every two who cannot do without each other. Each one of them is called a pair. It is said: a pair of sandals and a pair of sandals. What is meant by pairs here is the male and the female. Hafs read here and in Surat al-Mu’minun 23:of every with tanween, meaning: of every type, two pairs. He mentioned it for emphasis. In the story: Noah, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, how can I carry two of each kind? So God gathered the beasts and birds to him, and he began to strike with his hands at each kind, and the male would fall into his right hand and the female into his left hand, and he would carry her in the ship. And your family, meaning: carry and your family, meaning: your children and your children, except for those against whom the word has already been decreed, of destruction, meaning: his wife Wa’ilah and his son Canaan, and whoever believes, meaning: carry whoever believes in you, as God Almighty said: And none believed with him except a few, and they differed regarding their number. Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: There were only eight people on the ship: Noah, his wife, and his three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives. Al-A'mash said: They were seven: Noah, his three sons, and his three daughters-in-law. Ibn Ishaq said: They were ten, in addition to their wives: Noah, his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and six people who believed in him and all of their wives. Muqatil said: They were seventy-two men, women, his three sons and their wives, so their total number was seventy-eight, half of them men and half of them women. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: There were eighty men on Noah’s ship, one of whom was Jarhum. Muqatil said: Noah carried Adam’s body with him and placed it between the men and women. Noah intended to carry all the animals and birds. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: The first thing Noah carried was the whip and the last thing he carried was the donkey. When he entered the donkey and entered its chest, Satan clung to its tail, so its legs would not move. Noah kept saying: Woe to you, enter. It would get up but could not, until Noah said: Woe to you, enter, and Satan is with you. A word slipped from his tongue. When Noah said it, Satan let him go, so he entered, and Satan entered. Noah said to him: What brought you in to me, O enemy of God? He said: Didn’t you say, enter, even if Satan is with you? He said: Get out of my sight, O enemy of God. He said: You have no choice but to carry me with you. So he was, as they claim, on the deck of the ark. It was narrated on the authority of some of them: The snake and the scorpion came to Noah and said: Carry us. He said: You are the cause of harm and affliction, so I will not carry you. They said to him: Carry us and we guarantee that we will not harm anyone who mentions you. So whoever recites when he fears their harm, “Peace be upon Noah in the worlds,” they will not harm him. Al-Hassan said: Noah did not carry anything on the ship except what gives birth and lays eggs. As for the insects that are born from the clay of the earth, such as bugs and mosquitoes, he did not carry anything of them.
11:41: 41- And he said, 'Embark therein,' meaning: Noah said to them, Embark therein,' meaning in the ship, In the name of God, its course and its anchorage." Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read: "Majriha with a fatha on the meem, meaning its course, and its anchorage" with a damma on it. Muhammad bin Muhaisin read: "Majriha and its anchorage with a fatha on the meem from jarat and rasat," meaning: In the name of God, its course and its anchorage, and they are two verbal nouns. The others read: "Majriha and its anchorage with a damma on the meem from ajrita and arsata," meaning: In the name of God, its course and its anchorage, and they are also two verbal nouns, like His saying: "Leave me at a blessed home" (Al-Mu'minun: 29) and "Enter me in a truthful entrance and exit me in a truthful exit" (Al-Isra': 80). What is meant here is: landing, entering, and exiting. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. Ad-Dahhak said: When Noah wanted the ship to sail, he would say: In the name of God, and it would sail. And when he wanted it to dock, he would say: In the name of God, and it would anchor.
11:42: 42- And it sailed with them in waves like mountains, and waves are what rise from the water when the wind is strong on it, he likened it to mountains in its size and height above the water. And Noah called to his son, Canaan, and Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Sam, and he was a disbeliever, and he was apart, from him and did not board the ship: O my son, embark with us, Ibn Amir, Hamza, Asim, and Yaqub read it with the baa pronounced, and the others assimilate it into the meem, and be not with the disbelievers, lest you perish.
11:43: 43- "He said to him, I will seek refuge, I will become and take refuge, on a mountain that will protect me from the water", that will prevent me from drowning. "No one can protect today from the command of God, from the punishment of God, except for him whom God has mercy", it was said: protected except for the one whom God has mercy upon, like His saying: "in a life of contentment" Al-Haqqah-21 meaning: pleasing, "and the waves came between them and he, so he became, among the drowned". It was narrated that the water rose to the tops of the mountains by forty cubits. It was also said: fifteen cubits. It was narrated that when the water increased in the alleys, the mother of a boy feared for him, and she loved him very much, so she went out to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she rose until she reached two-thirds of it. When it reached her, she went until she stood on the mountain. When the water reached her neck, she lifted the boy with her hands until the water carried her away. If God had mercy on any of them, He would have had mercy on the mother of the boy.
11:44: 44- And it was said, meaning after the flood had ended: O earth, swallow, drink, your water, and O sky, withhold, hold back, and the water subsided, decreased and dried up, it is said: the water subsided, if it decreased, and God made it subsided, meaning He reduced it, and the matter was accomplished, the matter was completed, which was the destruction of the people, and it came to rest, meaning the ship came to rest, on al-Judi, which is a mountain in al-Jazirah near Mosul, and it was said, 'Away,' destruction, for the wrongdoing people." It was narrated that Noah, peace be upon him, sent a raven to bring him report of the land, but it landed on a carcass and did not return. So he sent a dove, which brought olive leaves in its beak and smeared its feet with mud. Noah knew that the water had dried up, so it was said that he cursed the raven with fear, so that it would not be familiar with houses. He put the green dove around its neck and prayed for its safety, so that it would be safe and familiar with houses. It was narrated that Noah, peace be upon him, boarded the ship ten days before the end of Rajab, and the ship sailed with them for six months. It passed by the Kaaba and circled around it seven times, and God raised it from drowning, but its place remained. They disembarked on the day of Ashura, and Noah fasted, and ordered all those with him to fast in gratitude to God Almighty. It was said: None of the infidels was saved from drowning except Awj bin Anq, as the water reached his hull. The reason for his salvation was that Noah needed teak wood for the ship and could not transport it, so Awj carried it to him from Syria, and God Almighty saved him from drowning for that reason.
11:45: 45- The Almighty said: And Noah called upon his Lord and said, ‘My Lord, indeed my son is of my family,’ and You promised me that You would save me and my family? And Your promise is true, there is no breaking it, and You are the most just of judges, You ruled that some people would be saved and others would perish.
11:46: 46- He said God Almighty "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family. Indeed, he has done something other than righteousness." Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read: work with a kasra on the meem and a fatha on the lam, not with a nasb on the ra' on the verb: meaning: he did polytheism and denial. The others read with a fatha on the meem and a dhammah on the lam and a tanween on it, not with a dhammah on the ra', meaning: your asking Me to save him is an action other than righteousness. So do not ask, O Noah, what you have no knowledge of. The people of Hijaz and Ash-Sham read fa-la-tas’alan with a fat-ha on the lam and a shaddah on the nun, and they break the nun except for Ibn Kathir, who opens it. The others read it with a jazm on the lam and a kasrah on the light nun. Abu Ja`far, Abu `Amr, Warsh, and Ya`qub confirm the ya’ in Mosul. I advise you not to be among the ignorant. They differed about this son. Mujahid and Al-Hasan said: He was a son of a perjured woman from someone other than Noah, and Noah did not know about that, and that is why he said: That of which you have no knowledge. Al-Hasan read: So they betrayed them At-Tahrim 10. Abu Jaafar Al-Baqir said: He was his wife’s son and Noah taught him, and that is why he said of my family and did not say of me. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair, Ad-Dahhak and most of them said: Noah, peace be upon him, was from his lineage. Ibn Abbas said: No prophet’s wife ever rebelled against him. His statement, He is not of your family, means: of the people of religion, because he was different from him in religion. His statement, So they betrayed them, means: in religion and righteous deeds, not in bed. His saying: I advise you not to be among the ignorant, means: that you call for the destruction of the infidels and then ask for the salvation of an infidel.
11:47: 47- "Noah said, 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You for that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers.'"
11:48: 48- It was said, 'O Noah, disembark' get off the ship, "in peace from Us", meaning with security and safety from Us, and blessings upon you, blessing is: the establishment of goodness, and from it: the camel kneeling. It was said: the blessing here is: that God Almighty made his offspring the ones who remain until the Day of Resurrection, and upon nations from among those with you, meaning: upon the offspring of nations from among those who were with you in the ship, meaning upon generations that will come after you, from the offspring of those with you, from your children and they are the believers, Muhammad bin Ka'b Al-Qurazi said: It includes every believer until the Day of Resurrection, and nations whom We will enjoy, this is the beginning, meaning: nations whom We will enjoy in this world, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us, and they are the disbelievers and the people of misery.
11:49: 49- "This is from the report of the unseen, the report of the unseen, We reveal it to you. You did not know it, nor did your people, before this, before the revelation of the Qur’an, so be patient, in carrying out God’s command and conveying the message and what you encounter of harm from the infidels, just as Noah was patient, Indeed, the outcome, in the end, is happiness and victory, is for the righteous."
11:50: 50- The Almighty’s saying: And to ‘Ad meaning: And We sent to ‘Ad, their brother Hud, in lineage but not in religion, He said, ‘O my people, worship God,’ worship God alone, “You have no deity other than Him. You are not but inventers,” you are not in your polytheism except liars.
11:51: 51- O my people, I do not ask of you for it, that is, for conveying the message, any reward, “my reward,” what is my recompense, is only from Him who created me, created me, so will you not reason?
11:52: 52- And O my people, seek forgiveness of your Lord, that is, believe in Him, and seeking forgiveness here means belief, then repent to Him, from worshipping other than Him and from your previous sins, He will send the sky upon you in showers, that is, He will send rain upon you in succession, time after time in times of need, and will add strength to your strength, that is, strength to your strength. That is because God Almighty withheld rain from them for three years, and made the wombs of their women barren so that they did not give birth, so Hud, peace be upon him, said to them: If you believe, God will send rain upon you, so that you will increase in wealth, and He will restore the wombs of mothers to what they were, so that they will give birth and you will increase in strength with wealth and children. It was said that you will increase in strength in religion to the strength of the body. And do not turn away as criminals, that is, do not turn away as polytheists.
11:53: 53- They said, 'O Hud, you have not brought us any clear evidence,' meaning, with clear proof and evidence for what you say, nor will we abandon our gods because of your word, meaning, because of your word, nor will we believe you, believing you.
11:54: 54- We say nothing but that some of our gods have afflicted you meaning: have afflicted you with evil meaning: you do not engage in what we engage in of disobeying us and cursing our gods except that some of our gods have afflicted you, meaning: have afflicted you with evil through madness and insanity, and that is because you cursed our gods and they took revenge on you by deceiving you. We do not hold your matter to be anything other than this, He said to them, Indeed, I call God to witness, regarding myself, and bear witness, O my people that I am innocent of what you associate.
11:55: 55-Besides Him, meaning: the idols, then plot against me all together, so plot against me and your idols, then do not wait, do not delay or give me respite.
11:56: 56- I have put my trust meaning: I have relied "on God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock." Ad-Dahhak said: He gives it life and causes it to die. Al-Farra’ said: Its owner and the one who is able to do it. Al-Qatibi said: He subdues it, because whoever you take by the forelock, you subdued him. It was said: The forelock was mentioned specifically because the Arabs use this when describing a person as being humiliated, so they say: So-and-so’s forelock is in the hand of so-and-so. And if they captured a person and wanted to release him and show him favor, they would cut off his forelock in order to boast about it, so God addressed them with what they knew. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path, meaning: Even though my Lord has power over them, He does not wrong them and He does not act except with goodness and justice, so He rewards the doer of good for his goodness and the doer of evil for his disobedience. It was said that its meaning is that the religion of my Lord is on a straight path. It was said: It contains an implication, meaning: My Lord urges you and carries you on a straight path.
11:57: 57- "But if you turn away", that is, turn away, meaning: turn away from what I have called you to, "I have conveyed to you that with which I was sent to you, and my Lord will replace you with another people, that is, if you turn away, God the Almighty will destroy you and replace you with another people who are more obedient than you, who will worship Him alone and worship Him, and you will not harm Him at all", by your turning away and turning away, you will only harm yourselves. It was said: You will not decrease Him at all if He destroys you because your existence and nonexistence are equal, "Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things", that is, He is the Guardian of all things, He protects me from you harming me.
11:58: 58- The Almighty said: And when Our command came, Our punishment, We saved Hud and those who believed with him, and they were four thousand. By mercy by grace from Us, and We saved them from a severe punishment, which is the wind with which He destroyed the ‘Aad. It was said: The severe punishment is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, meaning: Just as We saved them from punishment in this world, so We will save them in the Hereafter.
11:59: 59- "And those were 'Aad, he returned it to the tribe, they denied the signs of their Lord and disobeyed His messengers, meaning Hud alone, he mentioned it in the plural form because whoever denies a messenger is as if he denied all the messengers, and they followed the command of every stubborn tyrant" meaning: and the base and the lowly followed the people of arrogance and stubbornness, and the tyrant is the arrogant, and the stubborn is the one who does not accept the truth, it is said: when a man is stubborn, he refuses to accept something even if he knows it. Abu Ubaidah said: The stubborn, the obstinate, the obstinate, and the obstinate: the one who opposes you with disagreement.
11:60: 60- "And they were pursued in this world by a curse," meaning: they were followed by a curse that would follow them and go with them. The curse is: estrangement and expulsion from mercy, "and on the Day of Resurrection," meaning: on the Day of Resurrection also they will be cursed as they were cursed in this world and the Hereafter, "Behold, the 'Aad disbelieved in their Lord," meaning: in their Lord. It is said: I disbelieved in him and I disbelieved in him, just as it is said: I thanked him and thanked him and advised him and advised him. "Behold, away with 'Aad, the people of Hud," it was said: away from the mercy of God. It was also said: destruction. Distance has two meanings: one is the opposite of closeness, it is said: after, he is far away, after, and the other means destruction, it is said: after, he is far away, after, and after.
11:61: 61- The Almighty said: And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih, meaning: We sent to Thamud their brother Salih in lineage, not in religion. He said, ‘O my people, worship God.’ They believed in the oneness of God Almighty. “You have no god other than Him. He produced you from the earth,” He began your creation, from the earth, and that is because they are from Adam, peace be upon him, and Adam was created from the earth. And settled you therein, meaning: He made you its inhabitants and its residents. Ad-Dahhak said: He prolonged your life therein until one of them lived from three hundred to a thousand years, and the same was true of the people of ‘Aad. Mujahid said: I will make you live for my life, meaning: I will make it for you as long as you live. Qatada said: I will make you live in it. “So seek His forgiveness and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near,” to the believers, answering their prayers.
11:62: 62- "They said, meaning Thamud, O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this", the statement, meaning: we were hoping that you would be a master among us. It was said: we were hoping that you would return to our religion, because they were hoping that he would return to the religion of his tribe, but when he showed their call to God Almighty and abandoned the idols, they claimed that their hope in him was cut off, so they said: "Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped before, of the gods, and indeed, we are in disturbing doubt about that to which you invite us", a place of suspicion and accusation, it is said: I showed him suspicion if I did to him an action that causes him to be suspicious.
11:63: 63- "He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself,' prophecy and wisdom, then who will protect me from God? That is, who will prevent me from God's punishment, if I disobey Him, then you will not increase me except in loss." Ibn Abbas said: Its meaning is that you are not aware of your loss. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: Salih, peace be upon him, was not in a loss until he said: You do not increase me except in loss. The meaning is: You do not increase me with what you say except in attributing to me loss to you. In the language, Tafsiq and Tafsir are: the relation to immorality and debauchery, and likewise Takhsir is: the relation to loss.
11:64: 64- "And O my people, this is the she-camel of God for you as a sign," the accusative case of state and separation, and that is because his people asked him to bring forth a she-camel of ten years from this rock, and they pointed to a rock, so Salih, peace be upon him, called and a she-camel came forth from it and immediately gave birth to a child like her, so this is the meaning of his saying: "This is the she-camel of God for you as a sign, so leave her to eat in the land of God, of grass and plants, so you will not be burdened by her, and do not touch her with harm": and do not harm her by hamstringing her, "lest a near punishment seize you, if you kill her, for a punishment will come upon you."
11:65: 65- “So they hamstrung her, and Salih said to them, ‘Enjoy yourselves’, live ‘in your homes’, that is, in your homes, ‘for three days’, then you will perish, ‘that is a promise not to be denied’, that is, not a lie. It was narrated that he said to them: The punishment will come to you after three days. On the first day, your faces will be yellow, on the second day, red, and on the third day, black. And it was as he said, and the punishment came to them on the fourth day.
11:66: 66- The Almighty said: “So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him by mercy from Us,” by a blessing from Us, and from the disgrace of that Day, meaning: from his punishment and humiliation. Abu Ja`far, Nafi`, and Al-Kisa’i read: Disgrace of that Day and Punishment of that Day with the fat-ha on the meem. The rest read it with the kasra. Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, the Exalted in Might.
11:67: 67- And those who did wrong, who disbelieved, were seized by the shriek, that is, Gabriel, peace be upon him, shouted at them a single shout and they all perished. It was said: A shout came to them from the sky in which was the sound of every thunderbolt and the sound of everything on earth, and their hearts were torn apart in their chests. And he said: And the shriek seized is feminine, because the shriek means shouting. So they became in their homes, prostrated, dead and dying.
11:68: 68- As if they had never dwelt therein, they reside and are there Behold, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord, so away with Thamud, Hamza, Hafs, and Yaqub read: Thamud without a tanween, and likewise in Surat Al-Furqan, Al-Ankabut, and An-Najm. Abu Bakr agreed with An-Najm, and the rest read with a tanween, and Al-Kisa'i read: for Thamud with a dhal in the genitive and the tanween, and the rest with a dhal in the accusative, so whoever made it a genitive, it is because it is a masculine noun, and whoever did not make it a genitive made it a name for the tribe.
11:69: 69- The Almighty said: And Our messengers came to Abraham with good tidings, meaning the messengers were the angels. They differed about their number, so Ibn Abbas and Ata’ said: They were three: Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil. Al-Dahhak said: There were nine of them. Muqatil said: There were twelve kings. Muhammad bin Kaab said: Gabriel was with seven others. Al-Saddī said: They were ten kings in the form of young boys with bright faces. "With the good report" with the good report of Isaac and Jacob. And it was said: with the destruction of the people of Lot. "They said, 'Peace,' meaning, Give us peace. Ibrahim said, 'Peace,' meaning, Upon you be peace." It was said that it is a nominative case, as in the narration of the Almighty: "And say, 'Forgive us.'" Al-Baqarah 2:85; Al-A'raf 161. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read "Salam" here and in Surat Adh-Dhariyat with a kasra on the seen without an alif. It was said that it means peace, just as it is said: "Hal and Halal, and Haram and Haram." It was said that it means peace, meaning, "We are at peace," meaning peace with you, not war. And he did not delay in bringing a roasted calf. Haneeth and Mahnuth are roasted on stones in a pit of the ground and were fat and dripping with fat, as he said in another place: And he brought a fattened calf (al-Dhariyat 51:26). Qatada said: His year was Ibrahim’s cattle.
11:70: 70- "When he saw that their hands did not reach it," meaning: the calf, "he disliked them, he rejected them, and he had a feeling of fear, he concealed of them," fear. Muqatil said: It entered his heart, and the root of "wujus" is to enter, fear entered his heart. Qatada said: That is because when a guest came to them and did not eat from their food, they thought that he had not come with good but had come with evil. "They said, 'Fear not,' O Abraham, we are messengers of your Lord." Meaning: "We, the angels of God, were sent to the people of Lot."
11:71: 71- "And his wife" Sarah bint Haran bin Ahwar, who is Abraham's cousin. "Standing" from behind the curtain, hearing their words. It was said: She was standing, serving the messengers, and Abraham was sitting with them. "She laughed", Mujahid and Ikrimah said: She laughed, meaning: She menstruated at the time. The Arabs say: The rabbit laughed, meaning: She menstruated, and most of them are of the opinion that what is meant by it is the well-known laughter. They differed about the reason for her laughter. It was said: She laughed because the fear was removed from her and from Abraham when they said, Do not be afraid. Al-Suddi said: When Abraham brought the food to them and they did not eat, Abraham was afraid and thought they were thieves, so he said to them: Will you not eat? They said: We do not eat food except for a price. Abraham said: Then it has a price. They said: What is its price? He said: You mention the name of God at the beginning of it and praise Him at the end. Gabriel looked at Michael and said: It is right for this one that his Lord should take him as a friend. When Abraham and Sarah saw that their hands did not reach him, Sarah laughed and said: How strange are our guests! We serve them ourselves out of honor for them, and they do not eat our food. Qatada said: I laughed at the heedlessness of Lot’s people and the approaching punishment from them. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: I laughed at Ibrahim’s fear of three people in his house while he was among his servants and entourage. It was said: She laughed with joy at the good report. Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: She laughed in amazement that she could have a child at her advanced age and the age of her husband. According to this statement, the verse is in the order of precedence and delay, and its meaning is: And his wife was standing, so We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob. So she laughed and said: Woe is me! Shall I bear a child while I am an old woman? God the Almighty said: So We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob. That is, after Isaac, Jacob. He meant the father of the child, so she was given good tidings that she would live until she saw her child’s child. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Hafs, and Jacob read it with the accusative of the ba’, that is, after Isaac, Jacob. It was said: with the implication of a verb, that is, and We bestowed upon him after Jacob. The rest read it with the nominative, deleting the letter of description. It was said: and after Isaac, Jacob would come, so when she was given the good tidings of the child, she laughed and struck her face, that is, she struck her face in amazement.
11:72: 72- "She said, 'Woe to me!'", a lamentation and a word that a person says when he sees something that amazes him, meaning: Oh, how amazing. The original is "Oh, how amazing. Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman?", and she was ninety years old according to Ibn Ishaq. Mujahid said: ninety-nine years old. "And this is my husband, my husband, he was called that because he took care of her, old man," accusative as a state, and Ibrahim's age was one hundred and twenty years according to Ibn Ishaq. Mujahid said: one hundred years, and there was a year between the good report and the birth, "This is indeed an amazing thing."
11:73: 73- They said, meaning the angels, Do you wonder at the command of God?" Meaning: Do not wonder at the command of God, for when God Almighty wills something, it will happen. "The mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, O people of the House", meaning: the House of Abraham, peace be upon him. It was said: This is in the sense of a supplication from the angels, and it was said: It means goodness, mercy, and grace. And blessings is the plural of blessing, which is the establishment of goodness. And in it is evidence that the spouses are from the people of the House. He is Praiseworthy, Glorious. Praiseworthy means praiseworthy in His actions, and Glorious means generous. The root of glory is elevation.
11:74: 74- So when the fear had departed from Abraham, the fear, and the good report had come to him, of Isaac and Jacob, "He argues with us about the people of Lot," there is an implication in it, meaning: he began and continued to argue with us. It was said: Its meaning is that he speaks to us because Abraham, peace be upon him, does not argue with his Lord, the Almighty, but rather asks Him and requests from Him. Most of the commentators said: Its meaning is that he argues with Our messengers. His argument was that he said to the angels: Tell me, if there were fifty believers in the cities of Lot, would you destroy them? They said: No. He said: Or forty? They said: No. He said: Or thirty? They said: No. Until he reached five. They said: No. He said: Tell me, if there was one Muslim man in it, would you destroy it? They said: No. At that point, Abraham, peace be upon him, said: Lot is in it. They said: We know best who is in it. We will save him and his family, except for his wife, who was among those who remained behind.
11:75: 75- Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, compassionate, and frequently turning back to God. Ibn Jurayj said: There were four thousand thousand people in the villages of Lot’s people, so the messengers said to Abraham at that time.
11:76: 76- O Abraham, turn away from this, meaning: turn away from this statement and leave the argument, indeed, the command of your Lord has come, meaning, the punishment of your Lord and the judgment of your Lord, and indeed, there will come upon them, descending upon them, a punishment that cannot be averted, meaning: it will not be averted from them.
11:77: 77- The Almighty said: And when Our messengers came, meaning: these angels, to Lot, in the form of handsome, beardless young men, he was distressed by them, meaning: Lot was saddened by their arrival. It is said: I made him sad, so he was sad, just as it is said: I pleased him, so he was pleased. And he was distressed by them, meaning: in heart. And it is said: So-and-so was distressed by such-and-such: if he fell into a calamity from which he could not escape. That is because when Lot, peace be upon him, saw the beauty of their faces and the pleasantness of their scents, he feared that his people would intend to commit an immoral act against them, and he knew that he would need to defend them. "And he said, 'This is a difficult day,'" meaning: severe, as if evil and affliction had befallen him, meaning: intense. Qatada and Al-Suddi said: The angels left Abraham, peace be upon him, towards the village of Lot. They came to Lot at noon, while he was working his land. It was said: He was collecting firewood. And God Almighty said to them: Do not destroy them until Lot testifies against them four times. So they invited him as a guest and he set off with them. After walking for an hour, he said to them: What has reached you about the people of this village? They said: What is their matter? He said: I bear witness by God that it is the worst village on earth in terms of deeds. He said that four times, and they entered his house with him. It was narrated that the angels came to Lot’s house and found him in his home, and no one knew about it except the people of Lot’s house. His wife went out and informed her people, and said: There are men in Lot’s house whose faces I have never seen before.
11:78: "And his people came running to him," Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: They rushed to him. Mujahid said: They ran. Al-Hasan said: He walked between two walks. Shammar bin Atiyah said: Between running and jogging. And before, that is, before they came to Lot, they were doing evil deeds, they were coming to men from behind. He said, to them when they went to his guests and thought they were young boys, O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you, that is, by marriage, and in his guests with his daughters, and at that time, the marriage of a Muslim woman to a disbeliever was permissible, just as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, married his daughter to Utbah ibn Lahab and Abu al-‘As ibn al-Rabi’ before the revelation, and they were disbelievers. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: He offered his daughters to them on the condition of Islam. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said: His saying: These are my daughters, he meant: their women, and he added to himself because every prophet or his nation. And in the reading of Abi bin Kaab: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers (al-Ahzab 33:6) and he is a father to them. It was said: This was mentioned as a way of defending, not as a confirmation, and they were not satisfied with this. So fear God and do not disgrace me in front of my guest, meaning: Fear God and do not disgrace me in front of my guest, meaning: Do not insult me or disgrace me in front of my guests. Is there not among you a righteous man? Ikrimah said: A man who says there is no god but God. Ibn Ishaq said: A man who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong.
11:79: 79- “They said, ‘You have certainly known, O Lot, that we have no right to your daughters,’ meaning: they are not our wives, so we do not deserve them through marriage. It was said that its meaning is that we have no need or desire for them. ‘And indeed, you know what we want,’ of coming to men.
11:80: 80- He said, to them at that time: If only I had power over you, meaning physical power, or power through followers, or could take refuge in a strong support, meaning: join a fortifying clan. The answer to if is implied, meaning we would have fought you and come between you and them. Abu Hurairah said: God did not send a prophet after him except in the protection of his clan. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib bin Abi Hamza told us, Abu Al-Zinad told us, on the authority of Al-Araj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God forgives Lot if he takes refuge in a strong corner. Ibn Abbas and the commentators said: Lot closed his door and the angels were with him in the house, and he was debating with them and imploring them from behind the door, while they were trying to climb over the wall. When the angels saw what Lot was suffering because of them:
11:81: 81- "They said, 'O Lot, your support is strong. We are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you.' So open the door and leave us and them. So he opened the door and they entered. Gabriel asked permission from his Lord, the Almighty, to punish them, and He gave him permission. So he stood in the form in which he would be, and spread his wing, and upon him was a scarf of strung pearls. He had shining front teeth, a clear forehead, and his head was a veil like coral, as white as snow, and his feet were green.
