So he struck their faces with his wing, and blinded their eyes and blinded them, so they could not know the way nor find their way to their homes. So they turned away saying, 'Escape, escape! For in the house of Lot there are the most magicians of the people on earth who have bewitched us.' They kept saying, 'O Lot, stay where you are until morning, and you will see what you will receive from us tomorrow.'" They promised him, so Lot said to the angels: When is the time for their destruction? They said: The morning. He said: I want something faster than that, so if you destroy them now, they said: Is not the morning near? Then they said: So hurry, O Lot, with your family. The people of Hijaz read Fasir and An Asr by connecting the alif wherever it occurs in the Qur’an from Sara Yasri. The rest read it by cutting the alif from Asra Yasri. Their meaning is the same, which is traveling at night. In parts of the night. Ibn Abbas said: In a part of the night. Ad-Dahhak said: In the remainder. Qatada said: After the beginning of it has passed. It was said: It is the first part of the night. And let none of you turn back except your wife, Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read: your wife with the ta’ raised as an exception from turning back, meaning: let none of you turn back except your wife, for if she turns back she will perish. Lot had taken her out with him, and he forbade those who followed him from among those he took as a night journey to turn back, except for his wife, for when she heard this torment she turned back and said: O my people, so a stone caught up with her and killed her. And the others read: with the accusative of the ta’ as an exception to the Isra’, meaning: So travel with your family except for your wife, so do not travel with her and leave her behind with her people, for her desire is towards them, and the confirmation of the reading of Ibn Mas’ud: So travel with your family during a part of the night and let none of you look back except your wife. “It is what has befallen them that has befallen them,” of torment. Their appointed time is the morning, meaning: the appointed time for their destruction is at the time of dawn. Lot said: I want something faster than that, so they said: Is not the morning near?
11:82: 82- His saying, So when Our command came Our punishment, We turned it upside down, that is, Gabriel, peace be upon him, entered his wing under the destroyed villages of the people of Lot, which were five cities, and in them were four hundred thousand. It was said: four thousand thousand, so he raised all the cities until the people of heaven heard the crowing of roosters and the barking of dogs, so no vessel was turned over for them and no sleeper woke up, then he turned it upside down and turned it upside down. And We rained upon it, meaning upon its scum and travelers. It was said: After turning it upside down, He rained upon it stones of baked clay, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Saeed bin Jubayr said: Snak and Kul is Persian, Arabized. Qatada and Ikrimah said: Sijjil is clay. Its evidence is the Almighty’s saying: We will send upon them stones of clay (al-Dhariyat 51:33). Mujahid said: Its beginning is stone and its end is clay. Al-Hassan said: The origin of the stones was clay, so they were made stronger. Al-Dahhak said: It means bricks. It was said: As-Sijil is the name of the lowest heaven. It was said: They are mountains in the sky. God Almighty said: And He sends down from the sky mountains in which is hail (al-Nur 24:43). God Almighty says: In order. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: successive, one after the other, the passive participle of nadd, which is placing one thing on top of another.
11:83: 83- Marked, from the description of stones, and it is an accusative in the state, and its meaning is marked: Ibn Jurayj said: It has a mark on it that does not resemble the stones of the earth. Qatada and Ikrimah said: Perhaps it has red lines in the shape of a trunk. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: It was sealed with something like rings. It was said: Written on each stone is the name of the person who threw it. With your Lord, and they are not far from the wrongdoers, meaning those stones, from the polytheists of Mecca. Qatada and Ikrimah said: He means the wrongdoers of this nation. By God, God has not protected a wrongdoer from them yet. In some of the hadiths: There is no oppressor except that he is exposed to a stone falling on him from hour to hour. It was narrated that the stone followed their squatters and travelers wherever they were in the country, and one of them entered the sanctuary and the stone remained suspended in the sky for forty days until it came out and struck him and killed him.
11:84: 84- The Almighty said: And to Madyan, meaning: And We sent to the sons of Madyan, “their brother Shu`ayb. He said, ‘O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. And do not reduce the measure and the weight,’ meaning: Do not reduce, and they were going against their polytheism, “Indeed, I see you in prosperity,” Ibn Abbas said: Well-off and in blessings. Mujahid said: In abundance and plenty, so He warned them of the loss of blessings, the high prices, and the coming of punishment, if they did not repent. So He said: And indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing Day, that will encompass you and destroy you.
11:85: 85- O my people, give full measure and weight, complete them, with justice, with fairness. It was said: by straightening the tongue of the scale, and do not withhold, do not reduce, people’s things and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
11:86: 86- What remains from God is better for you if you are believers. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: It means that what God has left for you of what is lawful after giving full measure and weight is better than what you take by cheating. Mujahid said: What remains from God, meaning obedience to God, is better for you if you are believers that what you have is from God's provision and giving. And I am not a guardian over you, a trustee. It was said: He only said that because he was not commanded to fight them.
11:87: 87- They said, 'O Shu'aib, does your prayer command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped?' of idols. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Shu'aib, peace be upon him, used to pray a lot. That is why they said this. Al-A'mash said: It means: your recitation. Or that we should do with our wealth as we wish, of increasing or decreasing. It was said: Shuaib, peace be upon him, forbade them from cutting off dinars and dirhams and claimed that it was forbidden to them, so they said: Or that we do with our money what we want of cutting it off. You are indeed the forbearing, the wise. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: They meant: the ship that goes astray. The Arabs describe a thing by its opposite, saying: the one who has been bitten is safe, and the desert is a wilderness. It was also said: They said it in mockery. It was said: It means the forbearing and wise, according to you. It was said: It is correct, meaning that you, Shuaib, are among us, forbearing and wise. It is not appropriate for you to break the stick of your people and oppose their religion, as the people of Salih, peace be upon him, said: You were among us a source of hope before this (Hud 11:62).
11:88: 88- "He said, 'O my people, have you considered, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me from Him a good provision, lawful.' It was also said: abundant. Shu'aib, peace be upon him, had a lot of money. It was also said: good provision means knowledge and understanding. "And I do not intend to go against you in what I forbid you from," meaning: I do not intend to forbid you from something and then commit it. "I only intend, what I intend in what I command you to do and forbid you from, except reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but from God," and success means facilitating the path of goodness and obedience. "Upon Him I have put my trust, I have relied, and to Him I turn," I return in the misfortunes that befall me. It was said: In the afterlife.
11:89: 89- And O my people, let not my dissensions, my disagreements, cause you to be afflicted with what befell the people of Noah, from drowning, or the people of Hud, from the wind, or the people of Salih, from the shout, and the people of Lot are not far from you, because they had recently experienced the destruction of the people of Lot. It was said that its meaning is that the people of Lot were not far from you, and that is because they were neighbors of the people of Lot.
11:90: 90- "And seek forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving." Loving has two meanings: One of them is that He loves the believers. It was said that it means the beloved, that is, the beloved of the believers. It was reported that Shu'aib, peace be upon him, was the orator of the prophets, peace be upon them.
11:91: 91- "They said, 'O Shu'aib, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed we see you as weak among us,'" meaning that he was blind, meaning weak eyesight. "And had it not been for your people, meaning your clan, who were protecting him from his people, we would have stoned you," we would have killed you. Stoning is the ugliest form of killing. "And you are not dear to us."
11:92: 92- He said, 'O my people, is my family more honorable to you than God?' That is, the position of my family is more feared by you than God. That is, if you refrain from killing me because of my family, then it is better for you to protect me for the sake of God. And you have taken it behind your backs. That is, you have cast God's command behind your backs and abandoned it. Indeed, my Lord encompasses what you do.
11:93: 93- "And O my people, work according to your position," meaning: according to your ease and ability. It is said: So-and-so works according to his position if he works slowly and easily. "I am working, according to my ability, You will know," which of us is the one who wronged himself, and who is at fault in his action, so that is His statement: "He upon whom a punishment will come that will disgrace him, humiliates him, and he who is a liar," it was said: "He who" is in the accusative case, meaning: you will know the liar. It was said: Its place is in the nominative case, its meaning: And he who is a liar knows his lie and tastes the consequences of his action. "And watch, and await the punishment, I am with you, watching," waiting.
11:94: 94- And when Our command came, We saved Shu'aib and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the shriek seized those who did wrong. It was said that Gabriel, peace be upon him, shouted at them and their souls left them. It was also said that a shriek came to them from the sky and destroyed them. And they became in their homes prostrate, dead.
11:95: 95- As if they had never slept meaning: as if they had never resided or been in it, except far away, destruction, for Madyan as far away, Thamud perished.
11:96: 96- The Almighty said: And We sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority, a clear argument.
11:97: 97- “To Pharaoh and his chiefs. So they followed the command of Pharaoh, but Pharaoh’s command was not right.”
11:98: 98- He will lead his people, he will precede them, on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them, he will make them enter the Fire, and what an evil place to be led, meaning: what an evil entrance to be entered.
11:99: 99- And they will be pursued in this, meaning: in this world, with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection, how wretched is the provision, meaning: the aid that is given. It was said: the gift that is given, and that is because the two curses followed one another, a curse in this world and a curse in the Hereafter.
11:100: 100- “This is from the report of the towns which We relate to you. Some of them are standing,” inhabited, and harvested, ruined. It was said: Some of them are standing, the walls remain and the roofs have fallen, and harvested means: its trace has been erased. Muqatil said: Standing is where traces can be seen, and harvest is where traces cannot be seen, and harvest means harvested.
11:101: 101- And We did not wrong them, with punishment and destruction, but they wronged themselves, with disbelief and disobedience. So their gods which they invoked besides God did not avail them at all when the command of your Lord came, the punishment of your Lord, and they only increased them in destruction, meaning: other than loss, and it was said: destruction.
11:102: 102- And thus, and so on, "is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are unjust. Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe." Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Sadaqah bin Al-Fadl informed us, Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, Yazid bin Abi Burdah informed us, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, God gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. He said: Then he recited, And thus is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are unjust, the verse.
11:103: 103- The Almighty said: Indeed in that is a sign, for a lesson, “for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day when the people will be gathered together,” meaning the Day of Resurrection, and that is a witnessed Day, meaning: the people of heaven and earth will witness it. 3- A witness and what is witnessed. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah bin Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed day is the Day of Arafah, and the witness is Friday. The sun does not rise or set on a day better than Friday. In it is an hour in which no believing servant will find it and call upon God for good but that God will answer him, or seek refuge in Him from evil but that He will protect him from it.” This is the statement of Ibn Abbas. Most of them say: The witness is on Friday and the witnessed is on the Day of Sacrifice. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar: The witness is Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Sacrifice. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: The witness is the Day of Tarwiyah, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Yusuf bin Mahran narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The witness is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? An-Nisa’ 41, and he said: That is a day on which people will be gathered, and that is a witnessed day. Abdul Aziz bin Yahya said: The witness is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the witnessed is God Almighty. Its explanation is his saying, And We have brought you as a witness over these. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The witness is Adam, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Akrima said: The witness is the human being and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. It was also narrated from him: The witness is the angel who testifies against the son of Adam, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. He recited: And every soul will come with a driver and a witness (Qaf: 21), and And that will be a witnessed Day (Hud 11:103). It was also said: The witness is the guardian angels and the witnessed is the sons of Adam. Ata’ ibn Yasar said: The witness is Adam and his offspring, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Al-Walabi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The witness is God Almighty and the one who is witnessed on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The witness is this nation and the witness is all other nations. Its explanation is: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people (al-Baqarah 2:143). Salim bin Abdullah said: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about his statement: And a witness and what is witnessed. He said: The witness is God and what is witnessed is us. Its explanation is: And sufficient is God as a witness (An-Nisa’: 79). It was also said: The witness is the limbs of the children of Adam, and what is witnessed is the son of Adam. Its explanation is: On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them (al-Nur 24:24). It was also said: The witness is the prophets and what is witnessed is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Its explanation is: His statement: And when God took a covenant from the prophets until His statement: So bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses (Al Imran 3:81).
11:104: 104- And We do not delay it, meaning: And We do not delay that day, so We do not establish the Resurrection upon you. And Yaqub read, and He does not delay it with the letter ya, “except for a specified term,” known to God.
11:105: 105- The Day He comes was read with the letter ya confirmed and deleted, no soul speaks, meaning: no soul speaks “except by His permission. Among them are the wretched and the happy,” meaning: among them are those who have been destined for misery and among them are those who have been destined for happiness. Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abu Sahl Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzar told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Ibad Al-Dabry told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Saeed bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Salami, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: “We went out to a funeral procession, and while we were in Al-Baqi’, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us with a belt in his hand. He came and sat down, then he scratched the ground with it for a while, then he said: There is no soul that has not been breathed but its place in Paradise or Hell has been written, and it has not been written as miserable or happy. A man said: Should we not rely on our book, O Messenger of God, and abandon work? He said: No, but work, for everyone is facilitated for what he was created for. As for the people of misery, they are facilitated for the work of the people of misery, and as for the people of happiness, they are facilitated for the work of the people of happiness. He said: Then he recited: ‘But as for he who gives and fears God * And is truthful With goodness, We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need, And denies the best, We will ease him toward difficulty. Al-Layl
11:106: 106- His statement: But as for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire for them therein sighing and sobbing. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Sighing is a loud sound, and sobbing is a weak sound. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: Sighing is the first braying of donkeys, and sobbing is its last when it repeats it in its stomach. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Sighing is in the throat and sobbing is in the chest.
11:107: 107- They will abide therein eternally, remaining and residing therein, as long as the heavens and the earth endure. Ad-Dahhak said: As long as the heavens and the earth of Paradise and Hell endure, and everything above you and shading you is a sky, and everything your foot rests on is an earth. The scholars of meaning said: This is an expression of support according to the custom of the Arabs. They say, I will not come to you as long as the heavens and the earth remain, and it will not be like this as long as night and day alternate. They mean: never. God Almighty says: Except what your Lord wills. They differed regarding these two exceptions. Some of them said: The exception regarding the people of misery refers to a group of believers whom God will put into Hell for sins they committed, then He will take them out of it. So that would be an exception of a different kind, because those who were taken out of Hell happy were excepted by God from the group of the miserable. This is as follows: Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Hafs bin Omar told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Some people will be afflicted with the scorch of Hellfire for sins they committed, as punishment, then God will admit them to Paradise by virtue of His mercy, and they will be called the people of Hell.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Na’imi told us. Muhammad bin Yusuf told us. Muhammad bin Ismail told us. Musaddad told us. Yahya told us on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Dhakwan. Abu Raja’ told us. Imran bin Husayn, may God be pleased with him, told me on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A group of people will emerge from the Fire through the intercession of Muhammad and will enter Paradise. They will be called the people of Hell.” As for the exception of the people of happiness, it refers to the period of their stay in Hell before entering Paradise. It was said: Except for what your Lord wills of the two groups of their long life in this world and their detention in the intermediate realm between death and resurrection, before their destination to Paradise or Hell. Meaning: They will remain eternal in Paradise or Hell except for this amount. It was said: No, as your Lord wills: except as your Lord wills, meaning they will remain in it as long as the heavens and the earth remain, except as your Lord wills of the increase in the amount of time the heavens and the earth remain, and that is eternity in it, just as you say: So-and-so owes me a thousand except for the two thousand, meaning: except for the two thousand that came before. It was said: Except in the sense of the letter waw, meaning: And your Lord willed that these people remain in Hell and these people in Paradise, like His saying: So that mankind will have no argument against you, except those who have wronged (al-Baqarah 2:150), meaning: nor those who have wronged. It was said: Its meaning is that if your Lord had willed, He would have taken them out of it, but He did not will that He decreed that they would remain eternally. Al-Farra’ said: This exception is from God and He does not do it, like your saying: By God, I will hit you unless I see otherwise and you are determined to hit him. Your Lord is able to do whatever He wills.
11:108: 108- And as for those who are blessed, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read Sa'daw with a damma on the seen and a kasra on the 'ayn, meaning: they were granted happiness. Sa'd and As'ad have the same meaning. The others read with a fatha on the seen, based on the analogy of Shaqaw. They will abide in Paradise as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except for what your Lord wills, Ad-Dahhak said: Except for what they remain in the Fire until they enter Paradise. Qatada said: God knows best what is in its two pronouns. A gift that is not cut off, meaning not cut off. Ibn Zayd said: God the Most High informed us of what He wills for the people of Paradise, so He said: A gift that is not cut off, and He did not inform us of what He wills. And on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him, he said: A time will come upon Hell in which there will be no one, and that will be after they have remained in it for ages. On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, the same. According to the Sunnis, if it is proven, its meaning is that no one of the people of faith will remain in it. As for the places of the infidels, they will be filled forever.
11:109: 109- So be not in doubt, in doubt, about what these people worship that they are astray, they worship nothing but as their fathers before them were worshipped, there is an implication in it, meaning: as their fathers were worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their share" their portion of the reward. "Undiminished."
11:110: 110- And We gave Moses the Scripture, the Torah, and they differed concerning it, as some believed in it and some denied it, as your people did with the Qur’an, consoling his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, in delaying the punishment for them, it would have been judged between them, that is, they would have been punished immediately and their punishment and destruction would have been completed, and indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it, a place of suspicion and accusation.
11:111: 111- And if both, Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu Bakr read: And if both, with a silent nun on the lightening of the heavy in, and the rest with it with emphasis, when he stressed it here and in Ya Seen and Al-Tariq: Ibn Amir, Asim and Hamza, Abu Ja'far agreed here, and in Al-Tariq and in Al-Zukhruf, with emphasis Asim and Hamza and the rest with it with emphasis, so whoever stressed said the original in it: And if both for whom, then from was connected to the preposition with, then the nun was changed to a mim for assimilation, so three mims came together and one of them was deleted, so what remained was when with emphasis, and what here means: whom, it is the name of a group of people, as God Almighty said: Marry those that are good for you An-Nisaa' 3, meaning: those that are good for you, and the meaning is that both are for a group that will fulfill them. And whoever reads with a light pronunciation said: What is the connection that was added between the two lams to separate them due to the undesirability of their coming together? The meaning is: And indeed, both of them will be fulfilled. It was said: Ma means whom, meaning: for those who will pay them back, and the lam in filma is the lam of emphasis that comes before the predicate of in, and in liyuwaifinhum is the lam of the oath, and the oath is implied and its meaning is by God, for your Lord will pay them back their deeds, meaning: the reward for their deeds, for He is All-Knowing of what they do.
11:112: 112- The Almighty said: So stand firm as you have been commanded, meaning: stand firm in the religion of your Lord, acting upon it, and calling to it as you have been commanded, and whoever repents with you, meaning: and whoever believes with you, let them stand firm. Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: Steadfastness means standing firm in what is commanded and what is forbidden, and not evading the evasion of a fox. Imam Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Qadi told us, Abu Al-Tayyib Sahl bin Muhammad bin Sulayman told us, my father told us by dictation, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, Muhammad bin Al-Ala bin Kurayb told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sufyan bin Abdullah Al-Thaqafi, who said: “I said, O Messenger of God, tell me something about Islam that I will not ask anyone about after you. He said, ‘Say, I believe in God, then be steadfast.’” And do not transgress. Do not exceed My command and do not disobey Me. It was said that its meaning is do not go to extremes and exceed what I have commanded and forbidden. He is Seeing of what you do. Nothing of your deeds is hidden from Him. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: No verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that was more difficult for him than this verse. That is why he said: Hud and its sisters made my hair turn gray. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdul Salam bin Mutahhar told us, Umar bin Ali told us, on the authority of Ma’n bin Muhammad Al-Ghafari, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The religion is easy, and no one will overburden himself with religion except that it will overcome him. So strive straight and be close to God, and be glad and seek help by praying in the morning and in the afternoon and some of the night.”
11:113: 113- The Almighty said: And do not incline toward those who do wrong. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said: Do not incline. Inclination is love and inclination in the heart. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Do not be pleased with their deeds. Al-Suddi said: Do not flatter the oppressors. And on the authority of Ikrimah: Do not obey them. And it was said: Do not be at ease with those who do wrong. The Fire will touch you will befall you, and you will have no protectors besides God, meaning: helpers who will prevent you from His punishment, and then you will not be helped.
11:114: 114- The Almighty said: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day, meaning: the morning and the evening: meaning: the dawn and sunset prayers. Mujahid said: The two ends of the day are the dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers. And at the approach of the night, meaning the sunset and night prayers. Muqatil said: The dawn and noon prayers are at one end, and the afternoon and sunset prayers are at the other end, and at the approach of the night, meaning the evening prayer. Al-Hasan said: The two ends of the day: Fajr and Asr, and the last part of al-Layl 92:Maghrib and Isha. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The two ends of the day: Morning and Evening, meaning the Fajr and Maghrib prayers. His saying: And the approach of the night meaning: its hours, the singular of which is zalfa. Abu Ja`far read zalfan with a dammah on the lam. “Good deeds eliminate bad deeds,” meaning: the five daily prayers eliminate sins. It was narrated that it was revealed about Abu Al-Yusr, who said: “A woman came to me to buy dates, so I told her that there were dates in the house that were better than these. She entered the house with me, so I went to her and kissed her. I went to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and mentioned that to him. He said: ‘Cover yourself and repent.’ So I went to Umar, may God be pleased with him, and mentioned that to him. He said: ‘Cover yourself and repent.’ I could not be patient, so I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him. He said: ‘Did you leave behind a fighter in the cause of God with his family in such a way that he thought he was one of the people of Hell?’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lowered his head until God revealed to him: ‘And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night,’ the verse. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Is it for this in particular or for all people?’ He said: ‘Rather, for all people.’” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, “A man had intercourse with a woman before him, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him, so God Almighty revealed: ‘And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds.’ The man said: O Messenger of God, is this for me? He said: For all of my nation, all of them.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir informed us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad informed us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi informed us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan informed us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj informed us, Abu Tahir and Harun bin Saeed Al-Ayli informed me: They said: Ibn Wahb informed us, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, that Umar bin Ishaq, the freed slave of Zaidah, informed him on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: The five daily prayers and Friday to Friday and Ramadan to Ramadan are expiations for what is between them if major sins are avoided. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Muhammad Al-Hussein bin Ahmad Al-Mukhaldi told us, Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Sarraj told us, Qutaybah told us, Al-Layth and Bakr bin Mudar told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Hadi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Tell me, if there was a river at the door of one of you and he bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain on him? They said: No. He said: So it is like the five daily prayers, God wipes away sins with them. The Almighty said: That, meaning: that which we mentioned. It was said: it is a reference to the Qur’an, a reminder a sermon for those who remember, meaning: for those who remember it.
11:115: 115- And be patient O Muhammad, with the harm you encounter. It was said: with prayer, and similar to it is And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant therein (Ta-Ha 20:132) For indeed, God does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good, in their deeds. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He means those who pray.
11:116: 116- The Almighty said: Why was there not among the generations whom We destroyed before you, and the verse is for rebuke those who have a remainder, meaning: those who have discernment. It was also said: those who have obedience. It was also said: those who have goodness. It is said: so-and-so has a remainder if he has goodness. Its meaning is: why was there not among the generations before you someone who has goodness who would forbid corruption on earth? It was also said: its meaning is those who have a remainder of goodness. It is said: so-and-so has a remainder of goodness if he has a praiseworthy trait. They forbid corruption on earth, meaning they forbid corruption, and its meaning is denial, meaning: there were no survivors among them. Except a few, this is an isolated exception meaning: but a few, of those We saved from among them, and they are the followers of the prophets who forbade corruption on earth. And those who did wrong pursued that in which they were luxurious, they enjoyed, and the luxurious is the one who is pampered. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: They were given permission. Al-Farra’ said: They were accustomed to comfort and pleasures and preferring the world, meaning: And those who did wrong followed what they were accustomed to of comfort and pleasures and preferring the world over the hereafter. And they were criminals, disbelievers.
11:117: 117- And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly, meaning: He would not destroy them for their polytheism, while their people were righteous, dealing with one another fairly and not wronging one another. He would only destroy them if they were unjust to one another. It was said: He would not destroy them unjustly while they were righteous in their actions, but He would destroy them for their disbelief and committing evil deeds.
11:118: 118- The Almighty said: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind, all of them. one nation, with one religion. But they will not cease to differ, with various religions, including Jews, Christians, Zoroastrians, and polytheists.
11:119: 119- "Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy", meaning: But those upon whom your Lord has mercy, He guides them to the truth, so they do not differ, "and for that He created them", Al-Hasan and Ata' said: And for that He created them. Ashhab said: I asked Malik about this verse, and he said: He created them so that a group would be in Paradise and a group in the Blaze. Abu Ubaidah said: What I prefer is the statement of those who said: He created a group for His mercy and a group for His punishment. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak said: And for mercy He created them, meaning those whom He had mercy on. Al-Farra’ said: The people of mercy were created for mercy, and the people of difference were created for difference. The gist of the verse is that the people of falsehood differ, and the people of truth agree. So God created the people of truth to agree, and the people of falsehood to differ. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled, and the decree of your Lord has been fulfilled, I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.
11:120: 120- And We relate to you from the report of the messengers what strengthens your heart thereby, meaning: And whatever you need from the report of the messengers, that is, from their report and the report of their nations, We relate to you to strengthen your heart thereby, to increase your certainty and strengthen your heart, and that is because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard it, it strengthened his heart to be patient with the harm of his people. And the truth has come to you in this world, Al-Hasan and Qatada said: in this world. Others said: In this Surah. This is the opinion of the majority. He singled out this Surah for honor, even though the truth had come to him in all the Surahs. And an admonition, meaning: an admonition came to you, and a reminder for the believers.
11:121: 121- And say to those who do not believe, ‘Work according to your position,’ a threatening and warning order, We are working.
11:122: 122- And wait, for what will befall us of God’s mercy, for we are waiting, for what will befall you of God’s wrath.
11:123: 123- And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, meaning: He knows what is hidden from the servants in them, and to Him will return the entire matter, in the afterlife. Nafi’ and Hafs read: Yarju’ with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the jim, meaning: He returns. The others read it with a fatha on the ya’ and a kasra on the jim, meaning: the whole matter returns to Him so that the creation has no control. So worship Him and put your trust in Him, trust in Him, and your Lord is not unaware of what you do, the people of Medina, Ash-Sham, Hafs, and Ya’qub read you do with a ta’ here and at the end of Surat An-Naml. The others read it with a ya’ in both. Kaab said: The end of the Torah is the end of Surat Hud. Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juwzjani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, Abu Saeed Al-Haitham bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Abu Kurayb Muhammad bin Al-Ala told us, Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, I have grown old. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hud, Al-Waqi’ah, Al-Mursalat, ‘Amma Yatas’alun, and Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat have made my old age. It is narrated: Hud and her sisters made me grow old.
12:1: (Surat Yusuf, peace be upon him, is Meccan) 1- “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book,” meaning: its lawful and unlawful, its limits and rulings. Qatada said: By God, His blessing, guidance and right direction are made clear. This comes from the word banā which means appeared. Al-Zajjaj said: He clarifies the truth from falsehood and the lawful from the unlawful. This is from abaan, meaning to make apparent.
12:2: (Surat Yusuf, peace be upon him, is Meccan) 2- Indeed, We have sent it down meaning: the Book, as an Arabic Qur’an that you may understand, meaning: We sent it down in your language, so that you may learn its meanings and understand what is in it.
12:3: 3- "We relate to you", meaning: We recite to you "the best stories", and the narrator is the one who follows the traces and brings the report as it appears. Meaning: It shows you the report of past nations and centuries in the best possible way. It was said: What is meant by it is the story of Joseph, peace be upon him, in particular. He called it the best of stories because of the lessons, wisdom, jokes, and benefits it contains that are suitable for religion and the world, from the lives of kings and slaves, scholars, the cunning of women, patience in the face of the harm of enemies, and the goodness of overlooking them after meeting, and other benefits. Khalid bin Ma’dan said: Surah Yusuf and Surah Maryam are the two surahs that the people of Paradise will enjoy in Paradise. Ibn Ata’ said: No one who listens to Surah Yusuf will find comfort in it. The Almighty said: With what We have revealed to you What is the source, meaning: with Our revelation to you, This Qur’an, even though you were, and you were, before it, meaning: before Our revelation, among the unaware, among those who are heedless of this story and do not know it. Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Qur’an was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited it to them for a period of time. They said: O Messenger of God, if you would tell us, then God Almighty revealed: God has sent down the best statement (al-Zumar 39:23). They said: O Messenger of God, if you would tell us a story. Then God Almighty revealed: We narrate to you the best of stories. They said: O Messenger of God, if you would remind us. Then God Almighty revealed: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? Iron-16.
12:4: 4- The Almighty said: When Joseph said to his father, meaning: And remember when Joseph said to his father, and Joseph is a Hebrew name, and therefore it is not subject to inflection, and it was said that it is Arabic. Abu Al-Hassan Al-Aqta’ was asked about Joseph. He said: “Asf in the language means sadness, and Aseef means a slave. They came together in Joseph, peace be upon him, so he was named after him.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad said, Abdul Samad told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The generous one is the son of the generous one, the son of the generous one, the son of the generous one, Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham. “O my father,” Abu Jaafar and Ibn Amir read O my father with the opening of the ta’ in the entire Qur’an, assuming: O my father. Others read: O my father with a kasra on the ta’ because its original form is: O my father, and the jussive is moved to the kasra. I saw eleven stars, meaning stars from the sky. The word stars is used in the accusative case for interpretation. And the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating to me. He did not say, I saw them prostrating to me. The ha, the mim, the ya, and the nun are euphemisms for rational beings, because when he informed about them with the action of rational beings, he expressed them with the euphemism of rational beings, like the Almighty’s saying: O ants, enter your dwellings (al-Naml 27:18). The stars in the interpretation were his sisters, and they were eleven men, and he was illuminated by them as he was illuminated by the stars, and the sun was his father, and the moon was his mother. Qatada said this. Al-Saddī said: The moon is his maternal aunt, because his mother, Rachel, had died. Ibn Jurayj said: The moon is his father and the sun is his mother, because the sun is feminine and the moon is masculine. Joseph, peace be upon him, was twelve years old when he saw this vision. It was said: He saw it on Friday night, the night of the moon, and when he told his father about it,
12:5: 5- He said, 'O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers,' because the vision of the prophets, peace be upon them, is a revelation, so Jacob knew that if his brothers heard it, they would envy him, so he ordered him to keep it secret, so they may plot against you a plot, so they may scheme to destroy you because they know its interpretation and envy you. The lam in his saying for you is a connective, like the Almighty's saying: They fear their Lord (al-A’raf 7:154). It was said: It is like their saying I advised you and I advised you, and I thanked you and I thanked you. Indeed, Satan is a clear enemy to man, meaning: Satan makes things seem attractive to them and makes them suffer, due to his ancient enmity. Abdul Wahid bin Al-Malhi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abd Rabbih bin Saeed, who said: I heard Abu Salamah say: I used to see a dream that would worry me until I heard Abu Qatada say: I used to see a dream that would make me sick, until I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The good dream is from God Almighty, and the bad dream is from Satan. So if one of you sees something he likes, he should not tell it to anyone except someone he loves, and if he sees something he dislikes, he should seek refuge in God from its evil and from the evil of Satan, and spit three times, and should not tell it to anyone, for it will not harm.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shureih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ya’la bin Ata’, on the authority of Wakee’ bin Adas, on the authority of Abu Razeen Al-Uqaili, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A dream is a part of forty or forty-six parts of prophecy, and it is on a flying man. So if he tells it, it will come true. I think he said: Do not tell it except to a beloved or intelligent person.”
12:6: The Almighty said: And thus will your Lord choose you, your Lord chooses you, Jacob says to Joseph, meaning: Just as He raised your status with this vision, so will your Lord choose you, and teach you the interpretation of dreams, meaning the interpretation of the vision. It is called interpretation because it leads to what he saw in his dream, and interpretation is what leads to the outcome of the matter, and completes His favor upon you, meaning: with prophethood, and upon the family of Jacob, meaning: upon his children, for all of his children were prophets, as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac, so He made them prophets, Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise. It was said: What is meant by the completion of the blessing upon Abraham is the friendship. It was said: His salvation from the fire, and Isaac’s salvation from slaughter. It was said: By bringing out Jacob and the tribes from his loins. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: There were forty years between this vision of Joseph and its fulfillment with the arrival of his parents and brothers to him, and this is the opinion of most of the commentators. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: There were eighty years between them. When this vision reached Joseph’s brothers, they envied him and said: He was not satisfied for his brothers to prostrate to him until his parents prostrated to him, so they rebelled against him.
12:7: 7-God Almighty says: Indeed, it was in Joseph and his brothers, meaning: in his story and the story of his brothers. Their names are: Reuben, who was the eldest of them, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Zebulun, and it was said: Zebulun, and Asher, and their mother is Leah, the daughter of Lian, and she is the cousin of Jacob, peace be upon him, and he had four sons from two of his concubines, one of whom was named Zilpah and the other Ilhamah: Dan, Naphtali, and it was said: Naphtoli, Gad, and Asher. Then Leah died, and Jacob, peace be upon him, married her sister Rachel, and she bore him Joseph and Benjamin. It was said: and the son of Jamin, so the sons of Jacob, peace be upon him, were twelve men. Signs. Ibn Kathir read verse as a monotheism, meaning: a sermon and a lesson, and it was said: a wonder. Others read: verses in the plural. For those who ask, that is, the Jews asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the story of Joseph, peace be upon him. It was said: They asked him about the reason for the migration of Jacob's son from Canaan to Egypt. He told them the story of Joseph, and they found it in agreement with what was in the Torah, so they were amazed by it. This is the meaning of his saying: Signs for those who ask, meaning: evidence of the prophethood of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: Signs for those who ask and for those who do not ask, like his saying: It is the same for those who ask (Fussilat 41:10). It was said: Its meaning is a lesson for those who take heed, for it includes the envy of Joseph’s brothers, and what happened to them due to envy, and it includes his vision, and what God fulfilled from it, and it includes Joseph’s patience, peace be upon him, in not satisfying his desire, and in slavery and in prison, and what happened to him regarding the kingdom, and it includes Jacob’s sadness and patience and what happened to him regarding reaching his goal and other verses.
12:8: 8- When they said to Joseph, the lam in it is the answer to the oath, meaning: By God, Joseph, and his brother, Benjamin, are dearer to our father than we, Joseph and his brother Benjamin were from the same mother, and Jacob, peace be upon him, had a strong love for Joseph, peace be upon him, and his brothers saw in him an inclination towards him that they did not see in themselves, so they said this statement, and we are a group, a group and they were ten. Al-Farra’ said: The ‘asaba is ten or more. It was said: The clan is between one and ten. It was said: between three and ten. Mujahed said: Between ten and fifteen. It was said: between ten and forty. It was said: A group that is fanatical about one another, and has no singular form, such as a group or a tribe. Indeed, our father is in manifest error, meaning he made a clear mistake in preferring Joseph and his brother over us. What is meant by this is not straying from the religion, and if they had wanted that, they would have disbelieved in him. Rather, what is meant by it is: error in managing worldly affairs. They say: We are more beneficial to him in worldly affairs, in improving his livelihood and tending his livestock, so we are more deserving of love than he is. So he is mistaken in directing his love to him.
12:9: 9- Kill Joseph. They differed about who said this. Wahb said: It was said by Shimon. Kaab said: It was said by Dan. Or throw him to the ground, meaning: to a ground far from his father. It was also said: to a ground where wild beasts will eat him. He will be pure for you, he will purify you and describe to you. The face of your father, from his preoccupation with Joseph, and you will be after him, after the killing of Joseph, a righteous people, repentant, meaning: repent after you have done this and God will forgive you. Muqatil said: Your situation will be resolved between you and your father.
12:10: 10- One of them said, 'Do not kill Joseph.' He was Judah. Qatada said, "Rubil, who was Joseph's maternal cousin. He was the oldest of them and had the best opinion of him. The first is more correct, that it was Judah. He forbade them from killing him and said, 'Killing is a great sin.'" And throw him into the bottom of the well. Abu Ja`far and Nafi` read: Ghayabat al-Jab with the plural in the two letters. The rest read Ghayabat al-Jab with the singular: meaning: in the bottom of the well and its darkness. Ghayaba is every place that conceals something from you and hides it. Al-Jab is the unlined well because it is a hole, meaning: it was cut off and not covered. He picks it up: he takes it. Picking up means taking something from a place you do not expect. Some of the car means some of the travelers, so he takes it to another place, so you can rest from him. If you are going to do it means if you are determined to do it. They were adults at that time, and they were not prophets yet. It was said: They were not adults, and this is not correct, as evidenced by their saying: And you will be a righteous people after him. They said, O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins. The young boy had no sin. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Their actions included crimes such as: severing family ties, disobeying parents, showing little mercy to innocent children, betraying trust, breaking promises, and lying to their father. God pardoned them for all of that so that no one would despair of God’s mercy. Some scholars said: They decided to kill him, but God protected them out of mercy for them. If they had done so, they would have all perished. All of this happened before God Almighty informed them. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala was asked: How did they say he grazes and plays when they were prophets? He said: That was before God Almighty informed them, and when they decided to separate him from his father by means of some trick.
12:11: 11- They said to Jacob, O our father, what is the matter with you that you do not trust us with Joseph? Abu Ja`far read: Ta`mana without ishmām, and this is a narration from Nafi`, and the rest read: Ta`mana with a ḍammah on the first assimilated noon, and this is an indication of the ḍammah, without a ḍammah, to show that its original form is: La ta`mana with two noons on taf`alana, so the first noon was assimilated into the second, they began by denouncing him for not sending him with them as if they said: You are not sending him with us, do you fear for us regarding him? And indeed, we are to him sincere advisers. Muqatil said: There is an inversion in the speech, and that is because they said to their father: Send him with us. Their father said: Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him. Then they said: Why do you not trust us with Joseph, while we are to him sincere advisers? Here, sincerity means: taking care of the interest, and it was said: righteousness and compassion, meaning: We are compassionate towards him, taking care of his interest, and we will protect him until we return him to you.
12:12: 12- Send him with us tomorrow, to the desert, to graze and play, Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read with the letter nun in both and the letter ayn in the accusative case from narta'a, and the people of Kufa read with the letter ya in both and the letter ayn in the accusative case from yart'a meaning Joseph, and Jacob read: narta'a with the letter nun and ya'lab with the letter ya. And grazing is the expansion of pleasure. It is said: So-and-so grazes his money if he spends it on his desires, meaning we enjoy ourselves, eat, drink, have fun, and be active. The people of Hijaz read: yatra’a with a kasra on the ‘ayn, and it is derived from ra’i’. Then Ibn Kathir read with a noon in both of them, meaning: We guard and protect each other. Abu Jaafar and Nafi’ read it with a ya’, describing Joseph, meaning: He tends the livestock as we tend. And indeed, We will be its guardian.
12:13: 13- Jacob said to them, Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away, meaning: it grieves me that you should take him away, and the grief here is: the pain of the heart at parting with the beloved, and I fear that a wolf may eat him while you are unaware of him, and that is because Jacob had seen in a dream that a wolf attacked Joseph, and he was afraid of that, so he said this statement.
12:14: 14- They said, 'If the wolf eats him while we are a group,' ten, 'then we will surely be losers,' weak and helpless.
12:15: 15- So when they went with him and agreed, that is, they resolved, to put him, to throw him, in the bottom of the well, and We inspired him, this waw is redundant, its meaning is: We inspired him, like the Almighty's saying: So when they both submitted and he laid him down on his forehead, * And We called to him As-Saffat-103, that is, We called to him, You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they perceive not, meaning: We inspired Joseph, peace be upon him, to confirm your vision and to inform your brothers of this action of theirs while they perceive not God's inspiration and His informing him of that, said Mujahid. It was said: Its meaning is: And they will not feel it on the day you tell them that you are Joseph, and that was when they entered upon him and he recognized them while they did not recognize him. Wahb and others mentioned: They took Joseph, peace be upon him, with the utmost honor and began to carry him. When they went out into the wilderness, they threw him down and began to beat him. When one of them beat him, he would call for help from another, so the other beat him. He did not see any mercy from them. They beat him until they almost killed him, and he cried out, Oh my father, if only you knew what the sons of slave girls are doing to your son. When they were about to kill him, Judah said to them, Did you not give me a pledge not to kill him? So they took him to the well to throw him in. He was twelve years old - and it was said: eighteen years old - and they brought him to a well off the road, wide at the bottom and narrow at the top. Muqatil said: Three farsakhs from the home of Jacob, peace be upon him. Ka’b said: Between Midian and Egypt. Wahb said: In the land of Jordan. Qatada said: It is the well of Jerusalem. They began to lower him into the well and he clung to the edge of the well. They tied his hands and took off his shirt. He said: O my brothers, return the shirt to me so that I may hide in it in the well. They said: Let the sun, the moon, and the stars hide you. He said: I did not see anything. So they threw him into it. It was said: They put him in a bucket and sent him into it until he reached half of it, wanting him to die. There was water in the well, so he fell into it, then he took refuge in a rock in it and stood on it. When they threw him into it, he began to cry, so they called out to him. He thought that mercy had reached them, so he answered them. They wanted to crush him with a rock and kill him, but Judah prevented them. Judah used to bring him food, and he remained in it for three nights. “And We inspired him: ‘You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs.’” Most of them are of the opinion that God Almighty inspired him with this and sent Gabriel, peace be upon him, to comfort him and give him good report of the coming out, and to inform him that he would inform them of what they had done and would punish them for it, even though they were unaware. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Then they slaughtered a young goat and put its blood on Joseph’s shirt, peace be upon him.
12:16: 16- And they came to their father at nightfall, weeping. The scholars of meaning said: They came in the darkness of the evening to be bolder in apologizing with lies. It was narrated that Jacob, peace be upon him, heard their screaming and wailing, so he went out and said: What is the matter with you, my sons? Has anything happened to your sheep? They said: No. So what happened to you, and where is Joseph?
12:17: 17- "They said, 'O our father, indeed we went racing each other,' meaning: to throw ourselves into the air and get lost. Al-Suddi said: to struggle on our feet. And we left Joseph with our belongings, meaning: with our clothes and our cloaks. "And the wolf ate him. And you will not believe us." By believing us, even if we were, even if we were, truthful. If it is said: How did they say to Jacob, You do not believe the truthful one? It was said: It means that you accuse us in this matter because you feared us in the beginning and accused us of it. It was said: Its meaning is do not believe us even if we are truthful before God.
12:18: 18- And they brought his shirt with false blood, meaning: with blood that was false, because it was not Joseph's blood. It was said: with blood that was falsely attributed to him, so the source was placed in place of the noun. In the story: They stained the shirt with blood and did not tear it, so Jacob, peace be upon him, said: How did the wolf eat him and not tear his shirt? So he accused them. He said: Rather, your souls have suggested to you a matter, so patience is most fitting. Meaning: My matter is most fitting, or my action is most fitting, patience. It was said: So, patience is beautiful, I chose it. And beautiful patience in which there is no complaint or impatience. And God is the One sought for help against what you describe, meaning: I seek God’s help to be patient against what you deny. And in the story: They brought a wolf and said, This is the one who ate him. So Jacob said to him, O wolf, you ate my son and the fruit of my heart? So God Almighty made him speak, and he said, By God, I have never seen your son’s face. He said: How did you end up in the land of Canaan? He said: I came because of a kinship relationship, and these people hunted me down. So Joseph stayed in the well for three days. God Almighty said: 11- Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you the verses, the reason for the revelation of this verse is what Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah told us, Ibrahim bin Saad told us, on the authority of Salih, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Alqama bin Waqqas, and Ubaid God bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Masoud, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the people of the slander said to her what they said, and all of them told me a group of her hadith, and some of them were more knowledgeable of her hadith than others and more reliable in telling it, and I have learned from each man of them the hadith that he told me on the authority of Aisha, and some of their hadith confirms some. They said: Aisha said: Whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wanted to travel, he would cast lots among his wives, and whichever of them won the lot, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would go with him. Aisha said: So he cast lots among us during a military campaign he participated in, and my lot won. So I went out with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after the veil was revealed. I was carried in a litter and I was lowered into it. We traveled until, when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had finished that military campaign and returned, and we were approaching Madinah, he gave the call to depart one night. So I got up when the call to depart was given, and I walked until I passed the army. When I had finished my business, I went back to my saddlebag and touched my chest. I saw that a necklace of Dhofar agate had broken, so I went back and looked for my necklace, but the pursuit of it held me back. She said: The group who were traveling with me came and carried my litter and loaded it onto the camel I was riding on, thinking that I was in it. At that time, women were light, not weak, nor were they covered with meat, but only ate a little food. So the people did not find the lightness of the litter strange when they lifted it and carried it. I was a young girl, so they sent the camel and set out. I found my necklace after the army had continued, so I came to their homes and there was no one among them calling or answering, so I headed towards the house I was in and I thought that they would miss me and return to me. While I was sitting in my house, my eyes overcame me and I fell asleep. Safwan ibn al-Mu’attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, was behind the army. He came to my house in the morning and saw the blackness of a sleeping person, so he recognized me when he saw me. He had seen me before the veil, so I woke up with his retaliation when he recognized me. I covered my face with my cloak, and by God, we did not speak a word nor did I hear a word from him except his retaliation. He went down until he made his camel kneel and stepped on her hand, so I got up. So I got on it, and he set off leading me on the camel until we reached the army, which was about to leave at noon. She said: So whoever perished perished, and the one who carried out the slander was Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul. Urwa said: I was told that it was spread and talked about in his presence, and he approved of it, listened to it, and was impressed by it. Urwa also said: He did not name among the people of the slander except Hassan bin Thabit, Mastah bin Athatah, and Hamna bint Jahsh, among other people whom I have no knowledge of, other than that they are a group, as God Almighty said: And he who bore its burden. He said: Abdullah bin Abi Salul. Urwa said: Aisha hated for Hassan to be cursed in her presence, and she would say: He is the one who said: My father, my mother, and my honor are a protection for the honor of Muhammad from you. Aisha said: “So we went to Madinah, and when I arrived I was ill for a month, and the people were spreading slander, but I did not feel any of that. What made me suspicious in my illness was that I did not experience from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the kindness that I used to see from him when I was ill. Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would come to me, greet me, and say, ‘How are you?’ Then he would leave. That made me suspicious, and I did not feel any evil until I went out when I had recovered. I went out with Umm Mastih before the watering places, which was our place of defecation. We would not go out except at night until nightfall, and that was before we took the toilets near our homes, and we were commanded by the first Arabs to defecate before defecating, and we were bothered by the toilets/to take them near our homes.” She said: So I set out, with Umm Masrah - the daughter of Abu Ruhm ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn Amir, the aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and her son was Masrah ibn Athatah ibn Ibad ibn al-Muttalib. Umm Masrah and I turned towards my house when we had finished our business. Umm Masrah stumbled in her cloak and said: May Masrah be cursed! I said to her: What a bad thing you have said! Are you cursing a man who witnessed Badr? She said: Oh, you whore! Didn’t you hear what he said? I said: What did he say? Then she told me what the slanderers had said. She said: My illness increased upon my illness, and when I returned to my house, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came in to me and said: How are you? I said to him: Do you give me permission to go to my parents? She said: I wanted to ascertain the report from them. She said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave me permission, so I said to my mother: O my mother, what are the people saying? She said: O my daughter, take it easy, for by God, there has rarely been a woman who was content with a man who loved her and had co-wives, except that they increased her anger against her. I said: Glory be to God, do people really talk about this? She said: So I cried that night until morning, and my tears could not stop and I could not sleep, and then I woke up crying again. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, summoned Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usama ibn Zaid when the revelation was delayed, asking them and consulting them about separating from his wife. Usama advised the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on what he knew of his wife’s innocence and on what he knew about his own well-being. Usama said: Your wife, and we know nothing but good about her. Ali said: O Messenger of God, God has not made things difficult for you, and there are many women besides her. Ask the slave girl and she will tell you the truth. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, summoned Barira and said: O Barira, have you seen anything that made you suspicious? Barira said: By Him who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything about her that I overlooked more than that she was a young girl, who would sleep while her family’s dough was being made, and then the goats would come and eat it. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up that day and apologized to Abdullah bin Ubayy while he was on the pulpit, and he said: O group of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man who has harmed my family, and by God I have only known good about my family, and they have mentioned a man about whom I have only known good, and he does not enter my family except with me. She said: Saad bin Muadh, the brother of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, stood up and said: I, O Messenger of God, excuse you, for if he is from the Aws, I will strike his neck, and if he is from our brothers from the Khazraj, order us and we will do what you order. She said: A man from the Khazraj stood up, and Umm Hassan was his cousin from his thigh, and he was Saad bin Ubadah, and he was the chief of the Khazraj. She said: Before that, he was a righteous man, but his zeal carried him, so he said to Saad: You have lied, by God, you will not kill him and you will not be able to kill him, and if he was from your people, you would not have liked him to be killed. So Asid bin Hudayr, who was Saad’s cousin, stood up and said to Saad bin Ubadah: You have lied, by God, so we will kill him, for you are a hypocrite who argues on behalf of The hypocrites. She said: The two tribes, Aws and Khazraj, rose up until they were about to fight while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing on the pulpit. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept calming them down until they were silent and he was silent. She said: So I cried all that day, my tears not stopping, nor could I sleep. She said: “And my parents came to me in the morning, and I cried for two nights and a day, not sleeping, nor could I stop crying, until I thought that crying would split my liver. While my parents were sitting with me, and I was crying, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to enter, so I gave her permission, and she sat and cried with me.” She said: While we were in that state, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon us, greeted us, and then sat down. She said: He has not sat down with me since what was said before that was said, and he remained for a month without receiving any revelation concerning me. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, bore witness when he sat down, then said: As for what follows, O Aisha, such and such has reached me about you. If you are innocent, God will acquit you, and if you have committed a sin, then seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him, for if a servant confesses and then repents, God will accept his repentance. She said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished speaking, my tears flowed until I did not feel a single drop of them. I said to my father: Answer the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding what he said. My father said: By God, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I said to my mother: Answer the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding what he said. My mother said: By God, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I said, as I was a young girl who did not read much of the Qur’an: By God, I know that you have heard this hadith until it settled in your souls and you believed in it. If I tell you that I am innocent, you will not believe me, and if I confess to you something of which God knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By God, I do not find an example for me and you except the words of my father Yusuf when he said: So be patient, and God is the sought for help against that which you describe (Yusuf 12:18). Then I turned and lay down on my bed, knowing, and God knows, that I was innocent at that time, and that God would acquit me because of my innocence. But by God, I did not think that God would send down a revelation concerning me that would be recited. My status in my own eyes was too insignificant for God to speak about me, but I hoped that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would see in a dream a vision by which God would acquit me. By God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not seek his seat nor did any of the people of the house leave until the revelation was sent down to him, and he was seized by what he used to be seized by the open space, until sweat dripped from him like pearls, even on a cold day, from the weight of the words that were sent down to him. She said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was relieved while he was laughing, and the first word he spoke was: O Aisha, by God, God has acquitted you. She said: Then my mother said to me: Go to him, but I said: By God, I will not go to him, for I praise none but God. She said: Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you 10 verses. When God revealed my innocence, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who used to spend on Mistah ibn Athatha because of his kinship to him and his poverty, said: By God, I will never spend anything on Mistah after what he said to Aisha. Then God revealed: And let not those of virtue among you swear And the capacity until his saying Forgiving, Most Merciful. Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said: Yes, by God, I would love for God to forgive me. So he returned to Mistah the money he had been spending on him and said: By God, I will never take it away from him. Aisha said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) asked Zainab bint Jahsh about my situation. He said to Zainab: What did you know or see? She said: O Messenger of God, I protect my hearing and my sight. By God, I only know good. Aisha, who was the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) who was my equal, God protected her with piety. She said: Her sister Hamna began to fight for her, and she was killed among those who were killed. Ibn Shihab said: This is what I heard from the hadith of these people. Aisha said: By God, the man who was told what was said to him said: Glory be to God, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I have never uncovered the bosom of a woman. She said: Then he was killed after that in the cause of God. It was narrated by Muhammad bin Ismail on the authority of Yahya bin Bakir. Al-Layth told us on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Ibn Shihab with a similar chain of transmission. He said: If you have committed a sin, then seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him, for if a servant confesses his sin and God accepts his repentance, until His saying: Then you perished among those who perished from the companions of slander. Abu Usamah narrated on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to my house and asked about my maid. She said: No, by God, I did not know of any fault in her except that she would lie down until a sheep would come in and eat its yeast or dough. Some of his companions rebuked her and said: Tell the truth to the Messenger of God until they made it up to her. She said: Glory be to God, by God, I did not know of anything about her except what a jeweler knows about a piece of red gold. In it she said: And revelation was sent down to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and it was lifted from him and I could see the joy on his face as he wiped his forehead and said: Be of good cheer, Aisha, for God has revealed your innocence. My parents said to me: Get up and go to him. I said: No, by God, I will not get up and go to him, nor will I praise Him or anyone, but I praise God who has cleared me. You heard it and did not deny it or change it. As for the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, those who brought forth the slander with lies, and slander is the worst lie, it was called slander because it was diverted from the truth, from their saying: to slander something if to turn it off its face, and that is because Aisha deserved praise for her immunity and honor, so whoever accused her of evil turned the matter off its face, a group among you meaning: a group of them Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, Mastah bin Athatah, Hassan bin Thabit, Hamna bint Jahsh, the wife of Talha bin Ubayd God, and others, do not think it is bad for you, O Aisha and O Safwan, and it was said: it is addressed to Aisha, her parents, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Safwan, meaning: do not think the slander is bad for you, rather it is good for you because God will reward you for that and reveal your innocence. For every man among them, meaning from the false clan, is what he has earned of sin, meaning: the recompense for the sin he committed, according to how much he indulged in it, and he who took upon himself its greater burden, meaning: he bore most of it and initiated it. Ya’qub read it with a damma on the kaf, while the common folk read it with a kasra. Al-Kisa’i said: They are two dialects. Ad-Dahhak said: He took it upon himself to spread the hadith, and he is Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Urwah bin Aisha, And the one who bore the brunt of it among them, she said: Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and the painful torment is the Fire in the Hereafter. Ibn Abi Malekah narrated on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha in the hadith of the slander, she said: Then I mounted and Safwan took the reins. We passed by a group of hypocrites, and it was their custom to dismount, separating themselves from the people. Abdullah bin Ubayy, their leader, said: Who is this? They said: Aisha. He said: By God, she did not escape from him and he did not escape from her. He said: The wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man until morning, then he came leading her. Hassan, Mastah, and Hamna also began to do that, and they were the ones who bore the brunt of it. Some people said: He is Hassan bin Thabit.
