Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Bishr bin Khalid told us, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah bin Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I entered upon Aisha, and Hassan bin Thabit was with her, reciting poetry in which he praised some of his verses, and he said: Razan's horse is not worth a doubt and becomes hungry from the meat of the ignorant Aisha said to him: But you are not like that. Masruq said: I said to her: Why did you allow him to enter upon you when God Almighty said: And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof will have a great punishment? She said: What punishment is more severe than blindness? She said: He was defending or satirizing on behalf of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that those who had accused Aisha be flogged eighty times.
12:19: 19- And a car came, and they are the traveling people, they were called a car because they travel on the earth, it was a group from Madyan who were going to Egypt, so they took the wrong path and got down near the well, and it was in a desert far from the civilization of the shepherds and passers-by, and its water was salty and sweet when Joseph, peace be upon him, was thrown into it, so when they got down they sent a man from the people of Madyan called Malik bin Dhi'r, to ask for water, so that is what the Almighty said: So they sent their water-drawer and the water-drawer is the one who precedes the group to the water and prepares the ropes and buckets. He lowered his bucket, meaning he sent it into the well. It is said: I lowered the bucket if you sent it into the well, and I lowered it if you took it out. Joseph held on to the rope, and when he came out, he saw a boy who was the most handsome he could be. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Joseph was given half of his beauty. It is said that he inherited this beauty from his grandmother Sarah, who was given one-sixth of beauty. Ibn Ishaq said: Joseph and his mother took two-thirds of the beauty. When Malik ibn Dhi'r saw him, he said, O good report. Most people read it like this, with the alif and the fat-ha on the ya'. The water-drawer gave his companions good report, saying, Rejoice. The people of Kufa read, O good report, without an addition, meaning that the water-drawer called out to a man from among his companions named Bushra. This is a boy. Ibn Mujahid narrated on the authority of his father: that the walls of the well were crying over Joseph when he was taken out of it. And they took him captive, they hid him, as merchandise. Mujahid said: Malik ibn Dhi'r and his companions from the merchants who were with them took him captive and said, He is merchandise that some of the people of the water had taken to Egypt for purchase, fearing that they would ask them to share in it. It was said: He meant that Joseph’s brothers were concerned about Joseph’s affair and said, This is our slave who has run away. God Almighty said: And God is Knowing of what they do. So Judah brought food to Joseph, but he did not find it in the well. So he told his brothers about it, and they searched for him and found Malik and his companions coming down. So they came to them and found Joseph, and they said, This is a runaway slave from us. It is said: They threatened Joseph until his condition was not known. He said the same as they said, then they sold him. This is what God Almighty said:
12:20: 20- And they sold him, that is, they sold him, for a cheap price. Ad-Dahhak, Muqatil, and As-Suddi said: It is forbidden because the price of a free man is forbidden, and it is called forbidden because it is deprived of its blessing. On the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud: Bakhs means falsehood. Akrima and Al-Sha’bi said: For a small price. Dirhams instead of price, counted, mentioning the number is an expression for its smallness. It was said: He said counted because at that time they did not weigh anything that was less than forty dirhams, but rather they counted it, and if it reached an ounce, they weighed it. They differed on the number of those dirhams: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, and Qatadah said: Twenty dirhams, so they divided them two dirhams each. Mujahed said: Twenty-two dirhams. Akrima said: Forty dirhams. And they were, meaning: Joseph’s brothers, among the ascetics, meaning: Joseph, in him, because they did not know his status with God. It was said: They were among the ascetics in the price, because their intention was not to obtain the price, but rather their intention was to distance Joseph from his father. Then Malik bin Dhi’r and his companions set off with Yusuf, and his brothers followed them saying: Make sure he does not run away. He said: So they went with him until they reached Egypt, and Malik offered him for sale, and Qutayfair bought him, as Ibn Abbas said. It was said: Izfir was the king’s commander, and he was in charge of the treasuries of Egypt and was called Al-Aziz. The king at that time in Egypt and its environs was Al-Rayyan bin Al-Walid bin Sharwan from the Amalekites. It was said: This king did not die until he believed and followed Joseph in his religion, then he died while Joseph was alive. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: When they entered, Qutayf met Malik bin Dhi’r and offered him twenty dinars, a pair of sandals, and two white garments. Wahb ibn Munayyah said: The car brought Yusuf to Egypt and they entered the market with him to offer him for sale. People haggled over his price until his price reached his weight in gold, his weight in silver, his weight in musk and silk. His weight was four hundred pounds, and he was thirteen years old. So Qutayfir bought him from Malik ibn Dhi’r for this price. This is what God Almighty said:
12:21: 21- And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife, whose name was Rachel, and it was said: Zulaikha, Honor his abode, meaning: his home and residence, and abode is the place of residence. It was said: Honor him in food, clothing and accommodation. Qatada and Ibn Jurayj said: His status. Perhaps it will benefit us. That is, we will sell it for a profit if we want to sell, or it will suffice us if it reaches some of our needs. Or we adopt him as a son. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: The most perceptive of people are three: Al-Aziz regarding Joseph, when he said to his wife: Make his stay generous, perhaps he will benefit us, and the daughter of Shu’aib, peace be upon him, when she said to her father regarding Moses, peace be upon him: O my father, hire him, and Abu Bakr regarding Umar, may God be pleased with them both, when he appointed him as his successor. And thus We established Joseph in the land, meaning: in the land of Egypt. That is, just as We saved Joseph from being killed and brought him out of the well, thus We established him in the land and made him overseer of its treasuries. And that We might teach him the interpretation of dreams, meaning: We established him on earth so that We might teach him the interpretation of dreams, which refers to visions. And God is predominant over His affair. It was said that the ha in his affair is a metaphor for God Almighty. He says: God is predominant over His affair, He does what He wills. Nothing can overcome Him, and no one can reverse His judgment. It was said: It refers to Joseph, peace be upon him, meaning: God is in control of Joseph’s affair with management and protection, and does not entrust him to anyone until he reaches the end of his knowledge of it. But most people do not know what God will do.
12:22: 22- And when he reached his prime, the peak of his youth, strength and power. Mujahid said: thirty-three years. Al-Saddī said: Thirty years. Al-Dahhak said: Twenty years. Al-Kalbi said: The most severe period is between eighteen and thirty years. Malik, may God have mercy on him, was asked about the most severe. He said: It is patience. We gave him wisdom and knowledge. Wisdom means prophethood, and knowledge means understanding of religion. It was said: A ruling means: correctness in speech, and knowledge: in the interpretation of dreams. It was said: The difference between the wise and the knowledgeable is that the knowledgeable is the one who knows things, and the wise is the one who acts according to what knowledge requires. And thus do We reward the doers of good. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The believers. And also from him: The guided ones. Ad-Dahhak said: Those who are patient in adversity, as Joseph, peace be upon him, was patient.
12:23: 23- And she in whose house he was sought to seduce him, meaning: the wife of Al-Aziz. Seduce is to ask for an action, and what is meant here is that she invited him to herself to have intercourse with her, and she closed the doors, meaning: she locked them, and there were seven of them, and she said, 'Come to me,' meaning: come and approach. The people of Kufa and Basra read it as Hayt Lak with the ha and ta open. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read: Hayt with a kasra on the ha’ and a fatha on the ta’. Ibn Kathir read: Hait with the ha’ open and the ta’ closed. Al-Salami and Qatada read: Ha’ita laka with a kasra on the ha’ and a damma on the ta’ with a hamza, meaning: I prepared myself for you. Abu Amr and Al-Kisa’i rejected this and said that this was not narrated from the Arabs. The first is known to the Arabs. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught me: Heet laka. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Kisa’i used to say: It is a language of the people of Hauran that was brought to the Hijaz, and its meaning is come to me. Akram said: It is also in Hawrani dialect. Mujahed and others said: It is an Arabic word and it is a word of urging and eagerness to do something. Abu Ubaidah said: The Arabs do not dualize Heet, nor do they make it plural or feminine, and it is the same in every case. "Joseph said to her at that time: 'God forbid', meaning: I seek refuge in God and hold fast to God from what you have called me to. 'He is my Lord' meaning that your husband is Qutfir, my master. 'He has made my abode good', meaning: He has made my home honorable. This is what most commentators say. It was said: The letter ha refers back to God Almighty, meaning: God Almighty is my Lord, He made my abode good, meaning: He sheltered me, and saved me from the affliction of the well. The wrongdoers will not succeed, meaning: If I did this and betrayed him in his family after he had honored my abode, then I am a wrongdoer, and the wrongdoers will not succeed. It was said: The wrongdoers will not succeed: meaning the adulterers will not be happy.
12:24: 24- And she certainly desired him and he desired her. Desire is: approaching the action without entering into it. Her understanding: her intention to commit a sin and fornicate. As for his concern: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: He loosened the purse and sat in it like a traitor. On the authority of Mujahid, he said: He untied his trousers and began to fix his clothes. This is the opinion of most of the predecessors, such as Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Hasan. Al-Dahhak said: The devil ran between them, so he struck Joseph’s neck with one hand and the woman’s neck with the other hand until he brought them together. Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam said: Some people denied this statement, and the statement is what the predecessors of this nation said, and they were more knowledgeable about God than to say about the prophets, peace be upon them, without knowledge. Al-Suddi and Ibn Ishaq said: When the wife of Al-Aziz wanted to seduce Joseph, peace be upon him, she began to mention his good qualities and his desire for her, so she said: O Joseph, how beautiful your hair is! He said: It is the first thing to be scattered from my body. She said: How beautiful your eyes are! He said: It is the first thing that will flow on my face in my grave. She said: What a beautiful face you have! He said: It is for the dust to eat. It was said that she said: The silk bed is spread out, so get up and fulfill my need. He said: Then my share of Paradise will be gone. She kept tempting him and inviting him to pleasure, while he was a young man who felt the same lust as a man does, and she was a beautiful, pretty woman, until he softened towards her because of what he saw of her desires, and he desired her. Then God Almighty helped His servant and prophet with the proof that he mentioned. Some of the later scholars claimed that this is not appropriate for the state of the prophets, peace be upon them. He said: The speech ended when he said: And she certainly intended to do it, then he began the story about Joseph, peace be upon him, and said: And he intended to do it had he not seen the proof of his Lord, in the order of precedence and delay, meaning: Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have intended to do it, but he saw the proof and did not intend to do it. Grammarians rejected it and said: The Arabs do not delay lawla after the verb, so you do not say: I stood up if it weren’t for Zayd, meaning if it weren’t for Zayd I would have stood up. It was said: She wanted Joseph to deceive her, and Joseph wanted her, meaning: he wished that she would be his wife. This interpretation and others like it are not satisfactory because they contradict the sayings of the ancient scholars from whom religion and knowledge are taken. Some of them said: The amount that Joseph, peace be upon him, did was a minor sin, and minor sins are permissible for the prophets, peace be upon them. It was narrated that when Joseph, peace be upon him, entered upon the king after he was released from prison and the woman confessed, Joseph said: That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret. Gabriel said to him: Did you think of her, O Joseph? Then Joseph said: And I do not acquit myself verse. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: God Almighty did not mention the sins of the prophets, peace be upon them, in the Qur’an to reproach them, but rather He mentioned them to clarify the place of His grace upon them, and so that no one would despair of His mercy. It was said: He tested them with sins so that He would be unique in purity and honor, and all creation would meet Him on the Day of Resurrection with the brokenness of sin. It was said: To make them leaders for the people of sins in hope and abandoning despair of forgiveness and pardon. Some of the people of truth said: Worry is of two types: a fixed worry, which is when there is determination, resolve, and contentment with it, such as the worry of the wife of the Aziz, and the slave is taken by it, and a passing worry, which is the thought, and the talk of the soul without choice or determination, such as the worry of Joseph, peace be upon him, and the slave is not taken by it as long as he does not speak or act. Abu Ali Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty said: If My servant thinks about doing a good deed, I write it down for him as a good deed so long as he does not do it. If he does it, I write it down for him as ten times its like. If he thinks about doing a bad deed, I forgive him for it so long as he does not do it. If he does it, I write it down for him as one like it.” The Almighty said: Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, they differed about that proof: Qatada and most of the commentators said: He saw the image of Jacob, and he was saying to him: O Joseph, you are doing the work of fools, and you are written among the prophets! Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them: Jacob, peace be upon him, appeared to him and struck his chest with his hand, and his desire came out of his fingers. Al-Suddi said: “It was called, ‘O Joseph, have intercourse with her!’ Your situation as long as you do not have intercourse with her is like that of a bird in the sky that cannot be tamed. Your situation if you have intercourse with her is like that of a bird that dies and falls to the ground, unable to defend itself. Your situation as long as you do not have intercourse with her is like that of a stubborn bull that cannot be tamed. Your situation if you have intercourse with her is like that of a bull that dies and ants enter the base of its horns, unable to defend itself.” On the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding his statement: And he intended to do it, he said: He untied his trousers and sat down from her as a man sits with his wife, and there appeared a hand between them without a wrist or an upper arm, on which was written: And over you are guardians, * Noble and recording, * They know what you do (al-Infitar 82:11). So he got up and ran away and she got up, and when the fear left them, it returned and she got up, and when the fear left them, it returned and he got up, and he saw that hand written on it: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God (al-Baqarah 2:281). So he ran away and she got up, and when the fear had gone away from them, she came back and he came back. Then God Almighty said to Gabriel, peace be upon him: Save my servant before he commits a sin. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down and bit his finger, saying: O Joseph, you are doing the work of fools and you are written with God among the prophets. It was narrated that he wiped it with his wing and his desire came out of his fingers. Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi said: Joseph raised his head to the ceiling of the house when he was about to marry her, and he saw writing on the wall of the house: “Do not come near adultery. Indeed, it is an immorality and an evil way.” Atiyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In Al-Burhan, he saw the image of the king. Jaafar bin Muhammad Al-Sadiq, may God be pleased with them both, said: The proof is the prophecy that God placed in his chest, which stood between him and what angers God Almighty. On the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein, he said: There was an idol in the house, so the woman stood up and covered it with a garment. Then Yusuf said to her: Why did you do this? She said: I was ashamed of him seeing me committing a sin. Then Joseph said: Are you ashamed of something that does not hear, see, or understand? I have more right to be ashamed of my Lord, and he fled. The Almighty said: Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, the answer to had he not seen is omitted, and its meaning is: Had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have committed the sin. Thus, to turn away from him evil and immorality. Evil means sin. It was also said that it means ugly evil. Immorality means adultery. He is one of Our sincere servants. The people of Medina and Kufa read the sincere with a fatha on the lam, as long as there was no mention of religion after it. The Kufians added sinful in Surat Maryam, so they opened it. The meaning of the sincere ones chosen for prophethood is evidenced by: We have purified them with sincerity Sad ~ -146. Others read it with a kasra on the lam, meaning: those who are sincere in obedience and worship to God.
12:25: 25- And they raced to the door, and that is because when Joseph saw the proof, he ran to the door of the house, and the woman followed him to hold the door so that Joseph would not go out, and the woman caught up with him, so she clung to his shirt from behind, and pulled him towards her so that he would not go out. And she tore his shirt meaning: she tore it from the back meaning: from behind, and when they went out they met Al-Aziz, and this is what he said: And they found her master at the door meaning: they found the husband of the woman Qutfir at the door sitting with a cousin of Rachel, so when she saw him she feared him and said before saying to her husband What is the recompense of one who intended evil for your family meaning: adultery, then she feared that he would kill him so she said: Except that he be imprisoned meaning: imprisoned, or a painful punishment meaning: whipping, so when Joseph heard her words.
12:26: 26- He said, 'She sought to seduce me,' meaning: She asked me to commit an immoral act, but I refused and fled. It was said: What did Joseph want to mention? When the woman said: What is the punishment for someone who intended evil for your family? He mentioned it. He said: She tried to seduce me. A witness testified, and a judge ruled, from among her people. They differed about that witness: Saeed bin Jubair and Ad-Dahhak said: He was a baby in the cradle, and God Almighty made him speak. This is the narration of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Four spoke while they were young: the son of Mashta, the daughter of Pharaoh, the witness of Joseph, the companion of Jurayj, and Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him.” It was said: That boy was the woman's cousin. Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and Mujahid said: He was not a boy, but a wise man with an opinion.
12:27: 27- Al-Suddi said: He is the cousin of Ra’il, so he ruled and said: If his shirt is torn from the front, meaning: from the front, then you have told the truth and he is one of the liars. And if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied and he is among the truthful.
12:28: 28- When he saw, Qutfir, his shirt torn from the back, he knew the betrayal of his wife and the innocence of Joseph, peace be upon him. He said to her It is, meaning: this action, "of your plot. Indeed, your plot is great." It was said: this is from the statement of the witness. Then Qutfir turned to Joseph and said:
12:29: 29- Yusuf, meaning: O Yusuf, turn away from this meaning: from this hadith, so do not mention it to anyone so that it does not spread. It was said: Its meaning is do not care about him, for he has proven your excuse and innocence. Then he said to his wife: And seek forgiveness for your sin, meaning: repent to God, for you were among the sinners. It was said: This is from the witness’s statement to Joseph and Rachel. And what he meant by his saying: And ask forgiveness for your sin, that is, ask your husband not to punish you and forgive you, for you were among the sinners, among the sinners, until you tried to seduce a young man and betrayed your husband, and when he refused, you lied to him. And he only said: of the sinners, and did not say: of the sinful women, because he did not mean by it to inform about women, but rather he meant by it to inform about those who do that, meaning: of the sinful people, like the Almighty’s saying: And she was among the obedient (al-Tahrim 66:12), its explanation is the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people (al-Naml 27:43).
12:30: 30- The Almighty said: And women in the city said the verse. He says: The report of Joseph and the woman spread throughout the city, the city of Egypt. It was also said that it was the city of Ain Shams. The women talked about it and said - and they were five women: the wife of the king’s chamberlain, the wife of the owner of the animals, the wife of the baker, the wife of the cupbearer, and the wife of the prison keeper, said Muqatil. It was said: They are women from the nobles of Egypt. The wife of Al-Aziz seeks to seduce her young man, that is, her Canaanite slave, for himself, that is, she asks her slave to commit an immoral act. He has made her passionately in love, that is, he has made her passionately in love. Al-Kalbi said: His love covered her heart so that she would do nothing but him. It was said: She loved him until his love entered her heart, meaning: inside her heart. Al-Suddi said: The pericardium is a thin skin on the heart. He said: Love entered the skin until it affected the heart. Al-Sha’bi and Al-A’raj read: Shaghafaha with the unvoiced ‘ayn, meaning: love took her in every direction. And from it is the peaks of mountains, which are their tops. Indeed, we see you in clear error, meaning: apparent error. And it was said: its meaning is that she abandoned what her peers are like in terms of chastity and concealment.
12:31: 31- When she heard, Rachel, of their deceit, of their words and their talk, as Qatada and Al-Suddi said. Ibn Ishaq said that they only said that as a trick to show them Joseph, and his beauty and handsomeness were described to them. It was said: She revealed her secret to them and kept it a secret from them, so they revealed it, and that is why he called it a plot. She sent to them, Wahb said. She held a banquet and invited forty women, including those who had insulted her. “And I prepared for them a place to lean on,” meaning something to lean on. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Mujahid said: Mutaka’ means food. He called it Mutaka’ because when people eat, they lean on cushions. So the food was called Mutaka’ as a metaphor. It is said: We leaned on someone’s side, meaning we ate. It is also said: Mutaka’ is what you lean on to drink, talk or eat. In the anomalies, it is read Mutaka’ with a sukoon on the ta’. They differed about its meaning. Ibn Abbas said: It is the citron. The same is narrated from Mujahid. It was said that it is the citron in Abyssinia. Al-Dahhak said: It is the rabaward. Akrima said: It is everything that is cut with a knife. Abu Zaid Al-Ansari said: Everything that is cut with a knife is, among the Arabs, mattak, and mattak and battak with the letter m and the letter b means cutting. So the banquet was decorated with various fruits and foods, pillows were placed, and the women were invited. And she gave: she gave, each one of them a knife, so they would eat the meat, cutting it with the knife. And she said, to Joseph, Go out to them, meaning that she had seated him in another place, so Joseph went out to them. Ikrimah said: Joseph’s superiority over the people in beauty was like the superiority of the moon on the night of the full moon over all the other stars. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the night I was taken up to heaven, I saw Joseph like the moon on a full moon night. Ishaq bin Abi Farwa said: When Joseph walked through the alleys of Egypt, his face would be seen shining on the walls. When they saw him, they exalted him. They magnified him. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They were terrified by his matter and were astonished. It was also said: They exalted him, meaning: they embraced him because of his beauty. This is not correct. And they cut, that is, they cut with the knives they had, their hands, thinking that they were cutting citrons, but they did not feel the pain because their hearts were occupied with Joseph. Mujahed said: / They only felt blood. Qatada said: Their hands were tied until they were thrown away. The most correct would be to say absolutely without explanation. Wahb said: A group of them died. And they said, ‘God forbid, this is not a human being,’ meaning: God forbid that this is a human being. Abu Amr read: God forbid, with the ya’ in the connection, as is the original. The others read it without the ya’ because it is often used on the tongues, and in accordance with the Book. His saying: This is not a human being is in the accusative case by removing the letter of description, meaning: this is not a human being. This, meaning: what is this, is nothing but an angel, from the angels, honorable, to God Almighty.
12:32: 32- She said, meaning: Rachel, This is what you blamed me for, meaning: in my love for him. Then she stated what she had done, saying: And I did indeed try to seduce him, but he refused, meaning: he refused. She only stated it because she knew that they were not to blame her, and that what happened to her from seeing him had happened to them, so they said to him: Obey your mistress. Rachel said: And if he does not do what I command him, and if he does not obey me in what I have called him to do, he will be imprisoned, meaning: he will be punished by imprisonment, and he will be among the humiliated, among the humiliated. The nun of emphasis is heavy and light, and the pause on his saying: lyasjanna is with the nun because it is stressed, and on his saying wal-yakuuna is with the alif because it is light, and it is similar to the nun of i’rab in nouns, like the Almighty’s saying: I saw a man, and if you pause, you say: I saw two men with the alif, and similar to it: We will seize by the forelock * forelock (al-Alaq 96:15, 16). So Joseph, peace be upon him, chose prison over disobedience when the woman threatened him.
12:33: 33- He said, 'My Lord,' meaning: O Lord, prison is more beloved to me than what they invite me to. It was said: The supplication was specifically from them, but he added them to them to move from explicitness to insinuation. It was said: They all invited him to themselves. Yaqub alone read: al-sijn with a fatha on the seen. The general public read it with a kasra on it. It was said: If he had not said: Prison is more beloved to me, he would not have been afflicted with prison. It is better for a person to ask God for well-being. The Almighty says: And unless You turn away their plot from me, I will incline toward them. I incline toward them and follow them. It is said: So-and-so inclined toward such-and-such, he inclines toward it, he inclined, he inclined, and he was inclined, if he leaned toward it and longed for it. And I am among the ignorant, is evidence that if a believer commits a sin, he commits it out of ignorance.
12:34: 34- So He responded to him. He responded to him. "His Lord averted from him their plot. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing." To his supplication, the Knower of their plot.
12:35: 35- Then it appeared to them, that is, to Al-Aziz and his companions in the opinion, and that is that they wanted to limit the matter of Joseph to the command to turn away. Then it appeared to them to imprison him. After they had seen the signs, indicating Joseph's innocence from the length of the shirt, the speech of the child, and the women cutting off their hands and losing their minds, to imprison him for a time, for a period in which they would see their opinion. Ata' said: Until people's talk stops. Akrima said: Seven years. Al-Kalbi said: Five years. Al-Suddi said: That is because the woman said to her husband: This Hebrew slave has disgraced me in front of the people, telling them that I tried to seduce him, so either you give me permission to go out and apologize to the people, or you imprison him. So he imprisoned him, and he mentioned that God Almighty made that imprisonment a purification for Joseph, peace be upon him, from his desire for the woman. Ibn Abbas said: Joseph stumbled three times when he was about to do it, so he was imprisoned. When he said, Mention me to your Lord, he remained in prison for several years. When he said to his brothers, You are indeed thieves, they said, If he steals, a brother of his stole before.
12:36: 36- The Almighty said: And two young men entered the prison with him, and they were two young men who belonged to Rayyan bin Al-Walid bin Sharwan Al-Amaleq, the great king of Egypt. One of them was his baker and the one who provided him with food, and the other was his cupbearer and the one who provided him with drink. The king got angry with them and imprisoned them. The reason for this was that a group of the people of Egypt wanted to plot against him and assassinate him, so they guaranteed these two money to poison the king in his food and drink, so they agreed to them. Then the cupbearer refused, and the baker accepted the bribe and poisoned the food. When the food and drink were brought... The cupbearer said: Do not eat, O king, for the food is poisoned. The baker said: Do not drink, for the drink is poisoned. The king said to the cupbearer: Drink, so he drank it and it did not harm him. He said to the baker: Eat from your food, but he refused. He tried that food on an animal and it ate it and died. So the king ordered them to be imprisoned. When Joseph entered prison, he began to spread his knowledge and say, I can interpret dreams. One of the two young men said to his companion, Come, let us test this Hebrew slave. They appeared to him and asked him questions without having seen anything. Ibn Masoud said, They did not see anything, but rather they dreamed to test Joseph. Some people said: Rather, they were a true vision. Joseph saw them and they were worried, so he asked them about their situation. They mentioned that they were the king’s companions who had imprisoned them, and that they had seen a vision that had saddened them. Joseph said: Tell me what you saw. So they told him. One of them said, the one who was the one who was drinking, I saw myself squeezing wine, meaning grapes. Grapes are called wine because of what they are made of, just as one says: So-and-so is cooking bricks, meaning he is cooking milk for bricks. It was also said that wine is grapes in the language of Oman, because he said: I saw myself in a dream as if I was in an orchard, and there was a root of a rope on which were three clusters of grapes, so I picked them, and the king’s cup was in my hand, so I squeezed them into it and gave the king a drink, and he drank it. And the other said, the baker, I saw myself carrying bread on my head from which birds were eating. That is, he said: I saw as if there were three baskets above my head containing bread and various types of food, and wild birds were nibbling at it. Tell us its interpretation, he told us its explanation and interpretation and what this vision leads to. We see that you are among the doers of good, meaning: the knowledgeable, according to the dream’s expression, and goodness means knowledge. It was narrated that Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim was asked about his saying: Indeed, we see you among the doers of good, and what was his goodness? He said: If someone was sick in prison, he would visit him and take care of him. If a gathering was too small for him, he would make room for him. If he needed something, he would collect something for him. In addition to this, he would strive hard in worship and would stand up all night to pray. It was said: When he entered the prison, he found people who had been severely afflicted, had lost hope, and had been long in grief. So he began to console them and say: Be of good cheer and be patient, and you will be rewarded. They said: May God bless you, young man. How beautiful your face, character, and speech are. We have been blessed in your company. Who are you, young man? He said: I am Yusuf, son of the chosen one of God, Yaqub, son of the sacrifice of God, Isaac, son of the friend of God, Abraham. The prison guard said to him: Young man, by God, if I could, I would set you free, but I will treat you well, so you can remain in any prison cell you wish. It is narrated that when the two young men saw Joseph, they said to him: We loved you when we saw you. Joseph said to them: I ask you by God not to love me, for by God, no one has ever loved me without a calamity befalling me because of his love. My aunt loved me, so a calamity befell me. Then my father loved me, so I was thrown into the well. The wife of Al-Aziz loved me, so I was imprisoned. When they told him the dream, Joseph was reluctant to interpret for them what they had asked him, because he knew that it would be unpleasant for one of them. So he ignored their question and took up other matters in showing the miracle and calling to monotheism.
12:37: 37- He said, 'No food will come to you that you are provided with,' It was said: He meant by that in a dream, he said, No food will come to you that you are provided with in your sleep, 'except that I will inform you of its interpretation,' in wakefulness. It was said: He meant by it while awake, saying: No food comes to you from your homes that you are provided with, that you feed and eat, except that I will inform you of its interpretation, its quantity, its colour, and the time at which it will reach you. Before it comes to you, before it reaches you, and what food you ate, how much you ate and when you ate, this is like the miracle of Jesus, peace be upon him, when he said: And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses (Al Imran 3:49). They said: This is the work of soothsayers and priests, so where did you get this knowledge? He said: I am not a soothsayer, but that, the knowledge, “is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in God and who are disbelievers in the Hereafter,” and the repetition of they is for emphasis.
12:38: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, he showed that he was from the descendants of the prophets. It was not for us, it is not appropriate for us, to associate anything with God, meaning: God has protected us from polytheism. That, monotheism and knowledge, is from the grace of God upon us and upon mankind, what He showed them of guidance, but most people are not grateful, then he called them to Islam and said:
12:39: 39- O my two companions of the prison, He made them the companions of the prison because they are in it, just as the inhabitants of Paradise are called: the companions of Paradise, and the inhabitants of Hell are called: the companions of Hell, Are separate lords, meaning: various gods, this one of gold, this one of silver, this one of iron, this one higher, this one middle, and this one lower, different and neither harmful nor beneficial, better or God, the One, the Prevailing, who has no second. The Prevailing: the one who is victorious over all. Then He explained the impotence of the idols, saying:
12:40: 40- "What you worship besides Him", that is, besides God, and it was mentioned in the plural form and the error began for the two because he meant all the people of the prison, and everyone who is in the same state as them from the people of polytheism, "except names you have named, gods and lords devoid of meaning and those names have no reality, you and your fathers - God has sent down no authority for them, argument and proof, The judgment, what is the judgment and command and prohibition, is only for God. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That is the correct religion, the straight one, but most people do not know", then he interpreted their vision and said:
12:41: 41- O my two companions of the prison, as for one of you, meaning the one who drinks, "his lord will drink wine and the three clusters for three days. He will remain in prison, then the king will call him back after three days and restore him to the position he was in. "As for the other," meaning the one who feeds, the king will call him back after three days and the three baskets for three days. He will remain in prison, then he will be released, "and he will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head." Ibn Masoud said: When they heard what Joseph said, they said: We did not see anything, we were only playing. Joseph said: The matter about which you are asking has been decided, meaning: The matter about which you are asking has been completed, and God’s judgment upon you, which I told you about, has become binding, whether you saw it or not.
12:42: 42- And he said, meaning: Joseph at that time, to the one he thought, he knew that he would be saved from them, which was the cupbearer, mention me to your Lord, meaning: your master the king, and say to him: There is a boy in prison who has been unjustly imprisoned for a long time, but Satan made him forget the mention of his Lord, it was said: Satan made the cupbearer forget to mention Joseph to the king, meaning: Satan made him forget to mention him to his Lord. Ibn Abbas said, and most of the scholars agree: Satan made Joseph forget to mention his Lord when he sought relief from someone other than Him and sought help from a creature. That was a distraction that occurred to Joseph from Satan. He stayed, so he remained, in prison for a few years, and they differed about the meaning of a few, so Mujahid said: between three and seven. Qatada said: Between three and nine. Ibn Abbas said: Less than ten. Most commentators agree that the term bad’a in this verse means seven years, and he had stayed five years before that, so his total was twelve years. Wahb said: Job was afflicted with affliction for seven years, Joseph was left in prison for seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was tortured and turned into beasts for seven years. Malik bin Dinar said: When Joseph said to the cupbearer, Mention me to your Lord, he was told, O Joseph, you have taken a representative besides me, so I will prolong your imprisonment. So Joseph cried and said, O Lord, make my heart forget the great affliction, so I said a word and I will not return. Al-Hasan said: Gabriel entered upon Joseph in prison, and when Joseph saw him, he recognized him and said to him: O brother of the warned, why do I see you among the sinners? Gabriel said to him: O pure of the pure, the Lord of the worlds sends you peace and says to you: Were you not ashamed before Me to seek intercession through humans? By My glory, I would have kept you in prison for a number of years. Joseph said: Is He pleased with me in that? He said: Yes. He said: Then I do not care. Kaab said: Gabriel said to Joseph, “God the Almighty says: Who created you?” He said: God. He said: Who made you beloved to your father? He said: God. He said: Who saved you from the distress of the well? He said: God. He said: Who taught you the interpretation of dreams? He said: God. He said: Who turned away evil and indecency from you? He said: God. He said: How then did you seek intercession through a human being like you?”
12:43: 43- When seven years had passed - Al-Kalbi said: This seven is in addition to the five that came before that - and the relief of Joseph was near, the great king of Egypt saw a strange vision that terrified him, and that was that he saw seven fat cows, and they came out of the sea, then seven lean cows came out after them, extremely emaciated, and the lean ones swallowed the fat ones and they entered their bellies, and nothing of them was seen nor was anything distinct from the lean ones. Then he saw seven green ears of corn whose grains had formed, and seven others that were dry that had been harvested, and the dry ones had overwhelmed the green ones until they overwhelmed them and nothing of their greenness remained, so he gathered the magicians and the priests and the fortune tellers and the interpreters and told them his vision, and that is what God Almighty said: And the king said, ‘Indeed, I saw seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones, and seven green ears of corn and others that were dry.’ So he said to them, “O eminent ones! Advise me about my vision, if you can interpret visions.
12:44: 44- They said, 'Confused dreams', mixed up confused dreams, horrors, the singular of which is 'daghth', and its origin is a bundle of hashish, and dreams is the plural of 'dhalm', which is a vision, and the verb from it is 'halamt', 'ahlam', with the 'lam' open in the past tense and the 'lam' closed in the past tense, 'halam' and 'halman', heavy and light. And we are not scholars of the interpretation of dreams.
12:45: 45- And he who had escaped from being killed, from both of them, from the two young men, and he was the cupbearer, said, and remember, that is, he remembered Joseph's saying, Remember me to your Lord, after a time, after a while, which was seven years. I will inform you of its interpretation, that is, the young man knelt before the king, and said: There is a man in the prison who interprets dreams, so send, and in it is an abbreviation, meaning: So send me to him, O king, so he sent him and he came to the prison/ Ibn Abbas said: And the prison was not in the city.
12:46: 46-He said: Joseph, meaning: O Joseph, O truthful one, and the truthful one is the one who is very truthful, Give us your opinion about seven fat cows which seven lean ones are eating, and seven green ears of corn and others that are dry, for the king saw this vision, perhaps I may return to the people, the people of Egypt, perhaps they may know, the interpretation of the vision. And it was said: perhaps they may know your position in knowledge. Then Joseph said to them, explaining and teaching: As for the fat cows and the green ears of corn, they are seven years of famine. And as for the lean cows and the dry ears of corn, they are years of drought. This is what God Almighty said, informing about Joseph:
12:47: 47- He said, 'You shall cultivate for seven years as you please.' This is a statement in the sense of an order, meaning: cultivate for seven years according to your custom of cultivation. Perseverance: habit. It was also said: with diligence and effort. Asim read with Hafs’ narration: Daban with the opening of the hamza. They are two dialects. It is said: I persevered in the matter if you worked hard at it. So whatever you harvest, leave it in its spike, he ordered them to leave the wheat in the spike so that it would last longer and not spoil, except a little of what you eat, meaning: what you thresh a little for eating. He ordered them to save most and eat as much as needed.
12:48: 48- Then after that will come seven difficult years. He called the fruitful years difficult because of their severity on people. They will eat up, that is, they will destroy and perish, what you have prepared for them, that is, whatever food you have prepared for them will be eaten. He added eating to the years by way of expansion, except a little of what you store up, which you store up and save for sowing.
12:49: 49- Then there will come after that a year in which people will be given relief, meaning: they will be given rain, from ghayth: which is rain. It was said: they will be saved from the Arabs' saying: I sought help from so-and-so and he helped me, and in it they will press, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: they will press, with a ta' because the entire speech is addressed, and the others read it with a ya' referring to the people, and its meaning is: they will press grapes for wine, olives for oil, and sesame for fat. He meant by it an abundance of comfort and goodness. Abu Ubaidah said: they will press, meaning they will be saved from distress and drought, and pressing and pressing: salvation and refuge.
12:50: 50- "And the king said, 'Bring him to me.'" That is because when the cupbearer returned to the king and informed him of what Joseph had told him about the interpretation of his dream, and the king knew that what he had said would happen, he said, "Bring him to me." When the messenger came to him, and said to him: Answer the king, he refused to go out with the messenger until his innocence was proven. Then, he said, to the messenger: Return to your Lord, meaning: your master the king, and ask him what happened to the women who cut their hands, and he did not explicitly mention the wife of Al-Aziz out of politeness and respect. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If I had remained in prison as long as Joseph remained, I would have answered the caller. “My Lord is All-Knowing of their plot,” meaning: God is All-Knowing of their actions. Joseph only wanted to mention them after a long period of time so that the king would not look at him with suspicion, and so that he would come to him after the doubt about his affair had been removed. So the messenger returned to the king from Joseph with his message, and the king summoned the women and the wife of the Aziz.
12:51: 51- He said to them, What is the matter with you? What is your affair and your matter, when you sought to seduce Joseph from himself? He addressed them, and what was meant was the wife of Al-Aziz. It was said that the wife of Al-Aziz sought to seduce him from himself, and the rest of the women ordered him to obey her, so that is why he addressed them. They said, God forbid. God forbid. We know nothing bad about him. Treason. The wife of Al-Aziz said, Now the truth has become clear. It has become clear and evident. It was said that the women went to the wife of Al-Aziz and confessed to her, and she confessed. It was also said that she was afraid that they would testify against her, so she confessed. I sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful, in his statement: She sought to seduce me. When Joseph heard that, he said:
12:52: 52- That, meaning: that which I did by returning the king's messenger to him, so that he may know, the Aziz, that I did not betray him, with his wife, in absentia, meaning: in his absence, and that God does not guide the plot of traitors, his saying that so that he may know from Joseph's words is connected to the words of the Aziz's wife: I sought to seduce him, without distinguishing, for the listeners to know. It was said: There is an advancement and delay in it: its meaning is: Return to your Lord and ask Him what happened to the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is Knowing of their plot. That is so that He may know that I did not betray Him in secret. It was said: When Joseph said this statement, Gabriel said to him: Not even when you intended to do it? Then Joseph said: I do not acquit myself. Al-Suddi said: The wife of Al-Aziz said to him: Not even when you took off your trousers, O Joseph? So Joseph said:
12:53: 53- And I do not acquit myself, from error and slipping, so I purify it, Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, to disobedience, except for those upon whom my Lord has mercy, meaning: except for those upon whom my Lord has mercy and whom He has protected, what means from - like the Almighty's saying: Then marry those that are lawful for you An-Nisaa' 3, meaning: those that are lawful for you - and they are the angels, God Almighty protected them and did not let lust in them. It was said: Except for those whom my Lord has mercy upon, referring to the state of infallibility upon seeing the proof. My Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. When the king realized Joseph’s excuse, peace be upon him, and recognized his trustworthiness and knowledge:
12:54: 54- And the king said, 'Bring him to me, that I may take him exclusively for myself.' That is, I will make him exclusively for myself. So when he spoke to him, in this abbreviation, it is estimated: So the messenger Joseph came and said to him: Answer the king now. It was narrated that he stood up and prayed for the people of the prison, saying: O God, make the hearts of the good people kind to them, and do not make the report general to them, for they are the most knowledgeable people about the report of every country. So when he left the prison, he wrote on the prison door: This is the grave of the living, the house of sorrows, the experience of friends, and the gloating of enemies. Then he washed himself and cleansed himself of the filth of prison, put on fine clothes, and headed to the king. Wahb said: When he stood at the king's door, he said: My Lord is sufficient for me from my worldly life, and my Lord is sufficient for me from His creation. His neighbor is mighty, and His praise is great, and there is none other than Him. Then he entered the house, and when he entered upon the king, he said: O God, I ask You for Your good from his good, and I seek refuge in You from his evil and the evil of others. When the king looked at him, Joseph greeted him in Arabic. The king said: What is this language? He said: The language of my uncle Ishmael. Then he prayed for him in Hebrew. The king said: What is this language? He said: This is the language of my fathers, and the king did not know these two languages. Wahb said: The king spoke seventy languages, and whenever he spoke in one language, Joseph would answer him in that language and add to it Arabic and Hebrew. The king was amazed at what he saw from him despite his young age, and Joseph was thirty years old at that time. So he seated him and said, Indeed, today you are with us of high status, meaning in prestige, trustworthy, meaning truthful. It was narrated that the king said to him, I would like to hear my vision from you orally. Then Joseph said: Yes, O King, I saw seven fat, white, beautiful cows. The Nile revealed them to you, and they appeared to you from its bank, their offspring gushing milk. While you were looking at them and marveling at their beauty, the Nile dried up, its water subsided and began to dry up. Then came out of its mud seven thin, disheveled, dusty cows with shrunken bellies, without udders or offspring. They had fangs, molars, and paws like the paws of dogs, and trunks like the trunks of wild beasts. They devoured the fat ones like wild beasts, ate their flesh, tore their skins, crushed their bones, and chewed out their marrow. While you were looking and marveling, there were seven green ears of grain and seven others black, in one place, their roots in the soil and water. While you were saying to yourself, ‘Who am I?’ Green and fruitful, and these are black and dry, and the source is one and the same, and their roots are in the water, then a wind blew and scattered the leaves of the dry black ones onto the green and fruitful ones, and the fire caught fire in them, and they were burned and became black, and this is what you saw, then you woke up from your sleep terrified. The king said: By God, this vision - even if it is strange - is not more strange than what I heard from you. So what do you think of my vision, my friend? Then Joseph, peace be upon him, said: I see that you should gather food and plant a lot of crops in these fertile years, and put the food in the storehouses with its reeds and ears so that the reeds and ears will be fodder for the animals, and you order the people to raise one-fifth of their food, so that the food that you have gathered for the people of Egypt and those around it will suffice you, and the people will come to you from the regions for provisions, and you will gather treasures that no one before you had gathered. The king said: Who will get this for me, who will collect it, sell it, and spare me the trouble of dealing with it?
12:55: 55- So he said, Joseph, Put me in charge of the storehouses of the land. Storehouses: the plural of treasury, and he meant the storehouses of food and money, and the land: the land of Egypt, meaning: the storehouses of your land. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: On the tax and income of Egypt. I am a Guardian, All-Knowing, meaning: Guardian of the treasuries, All-Knowing of their interests. It was also said: Guardian, All-Knowing: a writer and accountant. It was said: He is the Guardian of what you entrust to me, and the Knower of what you entrust to me. It was said: He is the guardian of the account, knowledgeable of languages, and knows the language of everyone who comes to me. Al-Kalbi said: He is the Guardian of His estimation in the fertile years in the barren land, and He is aware of the time of famine when it occurs. So the king said to him: Who is more deserving of it than you?! So he appointed him that and said to him: Today you are with us, of high status and position, and are trustworthy over the treasuries. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Fanjawi told me, Mukhallad bin Ja’far Al-Baqraji told us, Al-Hasan bin Alawiya told us, Ismail bin Isa told us, Ishaq bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on my brother Joseph. If he had not said, ‘Put me in charge of the treasures of the land,’ He would have appointed him immediately. But He delayed that for a year, so he stayed in his house with the king for a year.” And on his authority on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: When the year had passed from the day on which he asked for the emirate, the king summoned him, so he went and adorned him with his sword and placed for him a bed of gold crowned with pearls and rubies, and he put on it a robe of brocade, and the length of the bed was thirty cubits, and its width was ten cubits, and on it were thirty mattresses and sixty cushions, then he ordered him to come out, so he came out crowned, and his color was like snow, and his face was like the moon, and the observer could see his face in the clarity of the color of his face, so he went until he sat on the bed, and the kings submitted to him, and the king entered his house and entrusted him with the matter of Egypt, and he removed Qutfir from what he had been in charge and appointed Joseph in his place. Ibn Ishaq said: Ibn Zayd said: The king of Egypt had many treasures, so he surrendered all his authority to him and made his command and judgment enforceable. They said: Then Qutfir died during those nights, so King Joseph married Rachel, Qutfir’s wife. When he entered upon her, he said: Is this not better than what you wanted? She said: O friend, do not blame me, for I was a beautiful, soft woman, as you see, in a kingdom and a world, and my companion did not have intercourse with women, and I was as God made you in your beauty and appearance, but my soul overcame me, and Joseph found her a virgin, so he had intercourse with her, and she bore him two sons: Ephraim, son of Joseph, and Misha, son of Joseph.
12:56: 56-And the kingdom of Egypt was secured for Joseph, meaning: he gathered them together, and established justice among them, and men and women loved him. This is what God Almighty said: And thus We established Joseph in the land, meaning: the land of Egypt We gave him, to settle therein, meaning: to settle wherever he wished and to do in it whatever he wished. Ibn Kathir read: Nasha’ with a nun in response to his saying: Makna and the others read it with a ya in response to his saying: Yatabo’u. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will, meaning: Our blessings, and We do not waste the reward of the righteous, Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: meaning the patient. Mujahed and others said: Joseph, peace be upon him, continued to call the king to Islam and to be gentle with him until the king and many people converted to Islam. This was in this world.
12:57: 57-And the reward of the Hereafter, the reward of the Hereafter, is better for those who believe and are righteous. When Joseph was reassured in his kingdom, he managed to collect food in the best way possible. He built fortresses and many houses, and collected food in them for the lean years. He spent generously until the fertile years passed and the lean years entered with a horror that people had never known before. It was narrated that he had arranged for the king and his entourage to eat once every day, at noon. When the year of famine began, the first to be overcome by hunger was the king, at midnight, so he cried out, O Joseph, hunger, hunger! Joseph said: This is the time of famine. In the first year of the drought, everything they had prepared in the fertile years perished. So the people of Egypt began to buy food from Joseph. He sold them the first year for money until there was not a dinar or a dirham left in Egypt except a handful. He sold them the second year for jewelry and gems until there was nothing left in people’s hands. He sold them the third year for livestock and beasts until he had all of them. He sold them the fourth year for male and female slaves until there was not a single male or female slave left in anyone’s hand. He sold them the fifth year for estates, real estate, and houses until he had all of them. He sold them the sixth year for their children until he enslaved them. He sold them the seventh year for their necks until he enslaved them. There was not a free man or woman left in Egypt except that he became his slave. The people said: We have never seen a king more magnificent or greater than this. Then Joseph said to the king: How did you see my Lord’s action in what He granted me? What do you think of that? The king said to him: The decision is yours and we will follow you. He said: I call God to witness and I call you to witness that I freed the people of Egypt, every last one, and returned their property to them. It was narrated that Joseph was never satisfied with food in those days, so he was asked: Are you hungry while you have the treasures of the earth in your hand? He said: I fear that if I am full I will forget the hungry. Joseph, peace be upon him, ordered the king’s cooks to make his lunch at noon. He wanted the king to taste hunger and not forget the hungry. Hence, the kings made their lunch at noon. He said: And the people went to Egypt from every direction to buy food, but Joseph made it impossible for any of them - even if he was great - to have more than one camel load, in order to divide the food equally among the people, and the people crowded around him, and the land of Canaan and the lands of the Levant were afflicted with what afflicted the people in all the lands of famine and hardship, and what afflicted the people befell Jacob, so he sent his sons to Egypt for provisions, and he held on to Benjamin, Joseph’s brother on his mother’s side, and that is what the Almighty said:
12:58: 58- And the brothers of Joseph came and they were ten, and their home was in Al-Arnat in the land of Palestine, in the Ghor of Ash-Sham, and they were people of the desert and camels and sheep, so Jacob, peace be upon him, called them and said: O my sons, it has reached me that there is a righteous king in Egypt who sells food, so prepare to buy food from him, so he sent them and they came to Egypt, and they entered upon him, upon Joseph, and he recognized them, Joseph, peace be upon him. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: He recognized them by the first time he saw them. Al-Hassan said: He did not know them until they knew him. And they did not recognize him, meaning: they did not recognize him. Ibn Abbas said: There were forty years between when they threw him into the well and when they entered upon him, and that is why they did not recognize him. Ata' said: They did not recognize him because he was on the king's bed and the king's crown was on his head. It was said: Because he was dressed like the kings of Egypt, wearing silk clothes and a gold necklace around his neck. When Joseph looked at them and they spoke to him in Hebrew, he said to them: Tell me who you are and what is your matter, for I have been ignorant of your affair. They said: We are shepherds from the land of Ash-Sham, and hardship has befallen it, so we have come to quarrel. He said: Perhaps you came to see the shame of my country. They said: No, by God, we are not spies. We are brothers, sons of one father, an old man called Jacob, a prophet of God. He said: How many are you? They said: We were twelve, and one of our brothers went with us into the desert and died there, and he was the most beloved of us to our father. He said: How many are you here? They said: Ten. He said: Where is the afterlife? They said: With our father, because he is the brother of the one who died on his mother’s side, so our father finds comfort in him. He said: Who knows that what you say is true? They said: O King, we are in a country where none of the people know us. Then Joseph said: Bring me your brother from your father, if you are truthful, and I am satisfied with that. They said: Our father is sad about his separation, and we will try to seduce his father. He said: Leave some of you with me as a hostage until you bring me your brother. So they cast lots among themselves, and the lot fell on Simeon, who had the best opinion of Joseph. So they left him with him. This is what God Almighty said:
12:59: 59- And when he had furnished them with their provisions, meaning: he had loaded each one with a camel for their provisions, "he said: Bring me a brother of yours from your father," meaning Benjamin, Do you not see that I give full measure? meaning: I complete it and do not deprive people of anything, so I give you an extra camel load for the sake of your brother, and I honor your status and treat you well, and I am the best of hosts, Mujahid said: meaning the best of hosts. And he had treated them well.
12:60: 60- If you do not bring it to me, then you will have no measure with me, meaning: you will have no food with me for me to eat, nor will you come near, meaning: do not come near my house and my country after that, and it is a definite prohibition.
12:61: 61- They said, 'We will seek him out from his father,' meaning: We will seek him out and ask him to send him with us, and we will do, what you have commanded us to do.
12:62: 62- "And he said to his young men," Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read: "to his young men" with an alif and a nun, and the rest read: "to his young men with a ta' without an alif, meaning to his young men, and they are two dialects like children and boys, make their merchandise" the price of their food, and it was dirhams. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were sandals and leather. It was said: It was eight jars of gruel from the parched barley. The first is more correct. In their saddlebags, their vessels, the plural of saddle, so that they may recognize it when they turn back, they depart, to their families so that they may return. They differed about the reason for which Joseph did this. It was said: He wanted to show them his generosity in returning the merchandise and providing a guarantee of righteousness and kindness, so that it would be more likely for them to return, so that they might recognize it, that is, their honor towards us. It was said: He saw it as meanness to take the price of food from his father and brothers, even though they needed it, so he returned it to them without them knowing, out of generosity. Al-Kalbi said: He feared that his father would not have enough paper to bring back again. It was said: He did that because he knew that their religion would compel them to return the merchandise to deny the mistake and they would not consider it permissible to keep it.
12:63: 63- "So when they returned to their father, they said, 'O our father,' we have come to the best man. He has given us a place and honored us with an honor that if he had been a man from the sons of Jacob, we would not have honored him with the honor he gave us. So Jacob said to them, 'When you come to the king of Egypt, greet him from me, and say to him, 'Our father prays for you and supplicates for you because of what you have given us.' Then he said, 'Where is Simeon?' They said, 'The king of Egypt has taken him hostage.' They told him the story, and he said to them, 'Why did you tell him?' They said, 'He took us and said, 'You are spies,' - since we spoke to him in Hebrew - and they told him the story, and they said, 'O our father:' He denied us the measure, Al-Hasan said: It means he denied us the measure if you do not carry our brother with us. It was said: Its meaning is that he gave a lamb in the name of each one and withheld the measure from us for Benjamin, and what is meant by the measure is food, because it is measured. So send with us our brother, Benjamin. We measure. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: He measures for himself as we measure. The others read: We measure with a nun, meaning: We measure and he is the food. It was said: We measure for him, “and indeed, We are its guardians.”
12:64: 64- He said, 'Shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother', Joseph "before', meaning: How can I trust you with him when you did to Joseph what you did? "Then God is the best guardian." Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read: "Hafizan" with an alif for the explanation, as one says he is the best man, and the others read: "Hafizan" without an alif for the source, meaning: the best of you in guardianship, he says: His guardianship is better than your guardianship. "And He is the Most Merciful of the merciful."
12:65: 65- And when they opened their baggage, which they had brought from Egypt, they found their merchandise, the price of the food, "returned to them. They said, 'O our father, what do we seek?'" That is, what do we seek and what do we ask for? That is because they mentioned to Jacob, peace be upon him, the king's kindness to them and urged him to send Benjamin with them. So when they opened the baggage and found the merchandise, This is our merchandise returned to us, that is, what do we ask for in words? This is the clear manifestation of kindness and honor. He gave us full measure and returned the price to us. They wanted to please their father, and provide for our people, that is, we buy them food and carry it to them. It is said: mar ahluh yamīr mira: if he carries food to them from one country to another. And similarly: amtaar yamtaar imtiyār. And we protect our brother, Benjamin, that is, from what you fear for him. And we will be given an increase in our loads, a camel’s load, meaning: a camel’s load that is measured for us because he was given a camel’s load in the name of each man, that is an easy measure, meaning: what we carried was little and would not suffice us and our families. It was said: its meaning is: we will be given an increase in a camel’s load, that is an easy measure with no burden or hardship in it. Mujahed said: The camel here is the donkey. A camel’s load means a donkey’s load, and it is a language. A donkey is called a camel. They were the owners of donkeys, and the first is more correct, which is the well-known camel.
12:66: 66- "Jacob said to them, I will not send him with you until you give me a pledge, give me a covenant, a pact and a promise, from God", and the pledged covenant: is confirmed by an oath. It was said: it is confirmed by calling God to witness against Himself "to bring him to me, and the lam was inserted in it because the meaning of the speech is an oath, unless you are surrounded", Mujahid said: unless you all perish. Qatada said: Unless you are overcome to the point that you cannot bear it. In the story: The brothers were in dire straits and struggled to the utmost, so Jacob had no choice but to send Benjamin with them. So when they gave him their pledge, / they gave him their covenants, he said, meaning Jacob, God is a witness over what we say, a witness. It was said: a guardian. Ka’b said: When Jacob said, God is the best guardian, God Almighty said: By My glory, I will surely return to you both after you have put your trust in Me.
12:67: 67- And he said, to them, Jacob, when they wanted to leave him, O my sons, do not enter from one gate, but enter from separate gates, and that was because he feared for them the evil eye, because they had been given beauty, strength, and a long stature, and they were the sons of one man, so he ordered them to separate when they entered so that they would not be struck by the evil eye, because the evil eye is real, and it was reported in the hadith: The evil eye puts a man in the grave and a camel in the cooking pot. On the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i: He said that because he hoped that they would see Joseph in the dispersion. The first is more correct. Then he said: And I cannot avail you at all against God, meaning: If God has decreed a decree concerning you, it will befall you whether you are together or separated, for what is destined will happen and caution is of no use against destiny. The judgment, what is the judgment, is only for God, this is Jacob’s entrusting of his affairs to God. In Him I have relied, I depended, and in Him let the reliant rely.
12:68: 68- And when they entered from where their father had commanded them meaning: from the separate gates. It was said: the city was the city of Al-Farmaa and it had four gates, so they entered it from its gates, it did not avail, to ward off from them anything from God, God Almighty spoke the truth about Jacob in what he said, except for a need, meaning, in Jacob's soul which he fulfilled, he pitied them as fathers pitied their sons and the matter went according to him, and indeed, meaning: Jacob, peace be upon him, was a man of knowledge, meaning: he did what he did out of knowledge, not out of ignorance, because We taught him, meaning: because We taught him. It was said: he was a worker according to what he knew. Sufyan said: He who does not act upon what he knows is not a scholar. It was also said: He is a guardian of what we have taught him. But most people do not know, what Jacob knows because they did not follow the path of attaining knowledge. Ibn Abbas said: The polytheists do not know what God inspired His saints.
12:69: 69- The Almighty said: And when they entered upon Joseph, they said, "This is our brother whom you ordered us to bring to you. We have brought him to you." He said, You have done well and you have hit the mark, and you will find the reward for that with me. Then he settled them down and honored them, then he hosted them and seated each two of them at a table. Benjamin was left alone, so he cried and said, If my brother Joseph were alive, he would have seated me with him. Joseph said, This brother of yours has been left alone. So he sat him down with him at his table, and he began to eat with him. When night came, he ordered them to do the same and said, Let each two of your brothers sleep in the same way. Benjamin was left alone, so Joseph said, This one will sleep with me on my bed. So he slept with him, and Joseph kept hugging him and smelling his scent until morning, and Reuben kept saying, We have never seen anything like this. When morning came, he said to them, I see that this man has no other with him, so I will hug him to myself so that his home will be with me. Then he settled them down in a place and provided them with food, and he placed his brother down. For his mother with him, so that is what God Almighty said: He took his brother to him, that is, he took his brother to him. When he was alone with him, he said: What is your name? He said: Benjamin. He said: What is Benjamin? He said: The son of the problematic one, because when he was born his mother died. He said: What is your mother's name? He said: Rachel, daughter of Levi. He said: Do you have any children? He said: Yes, ten sons. He said: Do you have a brother from your mother? He said: I had a brother who died. Joseph said: Would you like me to be your brother instead of your brother who died? Benjamin said: Who can find a brother like you, O king? But neither Jacob nor Rachel gave birth to you. Then Joseph wept and went to him and embraced him, and said to him: "He said: I am your brother, so do not be sad," that is, do not be sad, for what they used to do, for what they did to us in the past, for God Almighty has been good to us, and do not let them know anything of what I have told you. Then Joseph gave full measure to his brothers, and loaded a camel for them, and a camel for Benjamin in his name. Then he ordered the king's watering place to be placed in Benjamin's saddlebag. Al-Suddi said: The water container was placed in his brother’s saddlebag, and the brother did not notice. Ka'b said: When Joseph said to him, I am your brother, Benjamin said, I will not leave you. Joseph said to him, "I know how distressed my father is because of me, and if I imprison you, his distress will increase, and I will not be able to do this until I make you known for a terrible matter and attribute to you something that is not praiseworthy." He said, I do not care, so do whatever you want, for I will not leave you. He said, I will hide my measure in your saddlebag and then call out against you for theft, so that I may prepare for your return after you are released. He said, Then do it. That is what God Almighty said:
12:70: 70- When he had prepared their provisions, he put the water-trough in his brother's saddlebag, which is the drinking-trough from which the king drank. Ibn Abbas said: It was made of emerald. Ibn Ishaq said: It was made of silver. It was also said: It was made of gold. Ikrimah said: It was a silver bowl studded with jewels. Joseph made it a measure so that nothing else could be used to measure, and he used to drink from it. The water-trough and the measure were one and the same, and it was placed in Benjamin’s food container. Then they departed and Joseph gave them time until they left and went home. It was said: Until they left the building, then he sent someone after them to stop them and detain them. Then a crier called out, O caravan, which was the caravan carrying loads. Mujahid said: The caravan was made of donkeys. Al-Farra’ said: They were camel owners. You are thieves, stop. Before: They said it without Joseph’s order. It was said: They said it on his orders, and it was a slip of the tongue from him. It was also said: They said it on the basis that they stole Joseph from his father. When the messenger reached them, he said to them: Did we not honor your hospitality, treat you well, give you your full measure, and do to you what we did not do to others? They said: Yes, but what is that? They said: We lost the king’s water supply, and we do not accuse anyone but you of it.
12:71: 71-That is what the Almighty said: They said and turned towards them, referring to the muezzin and his companions, What do you miss? What has been lost from you? Loss is the opposite of ecstasy.
12:72: 72- They said, 'We have lost the king's cup, and whoever brings it shall have a camel-load' of food, and I am responsible for it,' the muezzin says.
12:73: 73- They said, meaning: Joseph's brothers, By God meaning: By God, and this word was made special by replacing the waw in it with the taa in the oath, unlike the rest of the names of God Almighty. You have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, to steal in the land of Egypt. If it is said: How did they say you knew? And from where did they know that? It was said: They said: You know that we did not come to cause corruption on earth. Since we traveled this road, we have not harmed anyone with anything. So ask about us whoever we pass by, and whether we have harmed anyone. It was said: Because they returned the merchandise that was placed in their bags. They said: If we had been thieves, we would not have returned it. It was said: They said that because they were known for not taking what was not theirs, and when they entered Egypt, they would muzzle the mouths of their animals so that they would not take anything from the people’s crops. And we were not thieves.
12:74: 74- They said, meaning: the caller and his companions, Then what is his punishment, meaning: the punishment of the thief, if you are lying, in your saying and we were not thieves.
12:75: 75- They said, meaning: Joseph's brothers, His punishment is that whoever is found in his baggage, that is his punishment, meaning: The punishment of the thief is that the thief should hand over his theft to the one from whom it was stolen, so he can steal it for a year.
