This was the custom of the family of Jacob in the ruling on the thief, and the ruling of the king of Egypt was to strike the thief/and fine him twice the value of the stolen item. Joseph wanted to imprison his brother with him, so he returned the ruling to them so that he could imprison him with him according to their ruling. And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers, those who do what they should not have done, such as stealing the property of others. Then the Messenger said: Your luggage must be searched. So he began to search them. It was narrated that he returned them to Joseph, who ordered their vessels to be searched before him.
12:76: 76- So he began with their vessels, to remove the accusation, before his brother's vessel, so he would search their vessels one by one. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that he would not open a baggage or look into a vessel except that he would seek forgiveness from God out of guilt for what he had accused them of, until nothing remained except Benjamin's saddlebag. He said: I do not think he took this, so his brothers said: By God, we will not leave until you look into his saddlebag, for it is better for you and for us. So when they opened his baggage, they took him out of it. This is what God Almighty said: Then he extracted it from his brother’s vessel. The metaphor is feminine in his statement, Then he extracted it, and the measure is masculine, as evidenced by his statement, And whoever brings it shall have a camel’s load, because he returned the metaphor here to the watering place. It was said: The measure is masculine and feminine. When he took the measure out of Benjamin's saddlebag, his brothers hung their heads for shame and came to Benjamin and said, What have you done to disgrace us and blacken our faces, O sons of Rachel? Will you still cause us harm? Since when did you take this measure? Benjamin said, "No, the sons of Rachel will still cause us harm. You took my brother and destroyed him in the wilderness, and this measure was placed in my saddlebag, in which you put the merchandise in your saddlebags." So they took Benjamin as a slave. It was said: That man took him by the neck and returned him to Joseph as thieves are returned. Thus did We plan against Joseph, and the plot here is the recompense of plotting, meaning: as they did in the beginning with Joseph of plotting, We did to them. And Jacob, peace be upon him, said to Joseph: So they will plot against you a plot, so We planned against Joseph in their matter. And the trick of creation: the deceit, and from God Almighty: the management with truth. It was said: We were inspired. It was said: We planned. It was said: We wanted. Meaning: We made for Joseph until he embraced his brother and separated him from his brothers. He would not have taken his brother and taken him into his own hands, under the king’s law, meaning: under his rule. Qatada said this. Ibn Abbas said: under his authority. Unless God willed, meaning: Joseph would not have been able to imprison his brother under the king’s rule had it not been for our plotting against him with our kindness until he found a way to do so, which is what the brothers said that the punishment for a thief is slavery, so Joseph’s desire was fulfilled by the will of God Almighty. We raise by degrees whom We will, with knowledge, just as We raised the degree of Joseph over his brothers. And Jacob read: Yarfa’ and Yashaa’ with the letter ya in both of them and adding degrees to min in this surah. The correct view is that the action in both of them is attributed to God Almighty, and this was mentioned previously in His statement: Except if God wills, meaning: God raises the degrees of whomever He wills. The rest read with the letter nun in both of them, except that the Kufians read: degrees with the tanween, and others with the addition, meaning: We raise it, and the one who raises is also God Almighty. And above every possessor of knowledge is another All-Knowing. Ibn Abbas said: Above every possessor of knowledge is another All-Knowing until knowledge ends with God Almighty. So God Almighty is above every All-Knowing.
12:77: 77- They said, 'If he steals, a brother of his stole before,' meaning his brother from his mother, meaning: Joseph. They differed about the theft that they described as Joseph, peace be upon him. Saeed bin Jubair and Qatada said: His grandfather, his mother’s father, had an idol that he worshipped, so he took it secretly, or broke it and threw it in the road so that it would not be worshipped. Mujahed said: One day, a beggar came to Joseph, so he took an egg from the house and gave it to the beggar. Sufyan bin Uyaynah said: He took a chicken from the birds that were in Jacob’s house and gave it to a beggar. Wahb said: He used to hide food from the table for the poor. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Joseph was with his aunt, Isaac's daughter, after the death of Rachel. His aunt embraced him and loved him intensely. When he grew up, Jacob fell in love with him, so he came to her and said: O my sister, hand Joseph over to me, for by God I cannot bear for him to be absent from me for an hour. She said: No, by God. He said: By God, I will not leave him. She said: Leave him with me for a few days so I can look at him, perhaps that will console me. So he did that. Then she took a belt of Isaac's that they inherited as adults, and she had it because she was Isaac's eldest son. She tied the belt around Joseph under his clothes when he was young. Then she said: Isaac's belt has been lost. Search the household. So they searched and found it with Joseph. She said: By God, he is safe for me. Jacob said: If he did that, he is safe for you. So she kept him until she died. That is what Joseph's brothers said: If he steals, a brother of his stole before. So Joseph kept it secret, he concealed it, in himself and did not reveal it to them. The metaphor came because he meant the word by it, which is his saying: He said, ‘You are in the worst position,’ he mentioned it secretly to himself and did not state it explicitly. He means that you are in the worst position, that is, in status with God, than those whom you accused of stealing in your actions with Joseph, because there was no real theft from Joseph, and your betrayal was real, and God knows best what you describe, you say.
12:78: 78- They said, 'O noble one, he has an old father.' And in the story, they became very angry at this situation, and when the sons of Jacob became angry, they could not be tolerated. And when Reuben became angry, nothing could stand up to his anger, and when he cried out, every pregnant woman who heard his voice would miscarry her child. And because of this, if one of the sons of Jacob touched him, his anger would subside. It was said: This was the description of Simon, one of the sons of Jacob. It was narrated that he said to his brothers: How many markets are there in Egypt? They said: Ten. He said: You take care of the markets for me and I will take care of the kingdom for you, or you take care of the kingdom for me and I will take care of the markets for you. So they went to Joseph and Reuben said: You must return our brother to us or I will cry a cry that will not leave a pregnant woman in Egypt except that she will miscarry her child. And every hair on Reuben's body stood up and came out of his clothes. Joseph said to his young son: Go to Reuben and touch him. And it was narrated: Take his hand and bring him to me. So the boy went and touched him and his anger subsided. Reuben said: Here is seed of Jacob's seed. Joseph said: Who is Jacob? It was narrated that he became angry a second time, so Joseph stood up to him, kicked him, and grabbed him by the collar. He fell to the ground and said: You Hebrews think that no one is stronger than you? When their situation reached this point and they saw that they had no way to free him, they submitted and were humbled, and said: O Aziz, he has an old, elderly father who loves him, so take one of us in his place, instead of him, for we see that you are among the doers of good, in your actions. It was said: He is one of those who do good to us by fulfilling the measure, being a good host, and returning the merchandise. It was also said: They mean that if you do that, you will be one of those who do good.
12:79: 79- He said, Joseph, God forbid, I seek refuge in God, that we should take except from him with whom we found our property, and he did not say except from the one who stole, to avoid lying, Indeed, then we would be wrongdoers," if we took an innocent person for a criminal.
12:80: 80- So when they despaired of him, meaning: they despaired of Joseph answering them to what they asked of him. Abu Ubaidah said: They despaired and were certain that the brother would not return to them. They conferred privately, meaning: they were alone with each other, whispering and consulting, and no one else mixed with them. The word Naji is suitable for a group, as he said here, and it is suitable for a single person, as he said: And We brought him near for a private conversation (Maryam 19:52). It is only permissible for a single person and a group because it is a source that is made an adjective, like justice and falsehood. Likewise, Najwa can be a noun and a source. God Almighty said: And when they were in a private conversation (al-Isra’ 17:47), meaning: they were in private conversation. He also said: There is no private conversation between three (Al-Mujadilah: 7), and he said in the source: The private conversation is only from Satan (Al-Mujadilah: 10). Their elder said, meaning: in intelligence and knowledge, not in age. Ibn Abbas and Al-Kalbi said: He is Judah, and he is the wisest of them. Mujahed said: He is Shimon, and he had leadership over his brothers. Qatada, Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak said: He is Rubil, and he was the oldest of them in age, and he is the one who forbade the brothers from killing Joseph. Did you not know that your father took a covenant from you from God and before that you neglected fell short in Joseph? They differed about the location of what. It was said: It is accusative by placing the knowledge on it, meaning: Did you not know before that you were negligent regarding Joseph? It was said: It is in the nominative case as a subject, and the speech was completed when he said: From God, then he said: And before. This is your negligence regarding Joseph. It was said: What is a connection. That is: And before this, you neglected Joseph. I will not leave the land, which I am in, which is the land of Egypt, until my father gives me permission, to leave it and calls me, or God decides for me, to return my brother to me, or for me to leave and leave my brother. It was said: Or God will rule in my favor with the sword, so I can fight them and get my brother back. And He is the best of judges, the most just of those who judge between people.
12:81: 81- Return to your father, the brother imprisoned in Egypt says to his brothers. Return to your father, and say, 'Our father, your son, Benjamin, has stolen.' Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak read it as sarqa with a damma on the seen and a kasra on the ra and a shaddah on it, meaning: he attributed to theft, just as one says khawantuhu for attributing him to treason. We only testified to what we knew. That is, we only said this based on what we knew, for we saw the sa` being taken out of his baggage. It was said: Its meaning is: And we did not bear witness, meaning: There was no testimony from us during our lifetime about anything except what we knew, and this is not testimony from us, but rather it is report about what your son did, according to their claim. It was said: Jacob, peace be upon him, said to them: This man does not know that a thief will be caught stealing except by your word. They said: We did not testify before Joseph that a thief will be caught stealing except by what we knew. And that was the ruling with the prophets, Jacob and his sons. And we were not guardians of the unseen. Mujahid and Qatadah said: We did not know that your son would steal and that our situation would turn out to be this way. If we had known that, we would not have gone to him. Rather, we said, We will protect our brother as much as we have the means to protect him. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: We were not guardians of its night and day, its coming and going. Akrima said: We were not guardians of the unseen, so perhaps it was slipped into his bag at night.
12:82: 82- "And ask the town in which we were," meaning: the people of the village, which is Egypt. Ibn Abbas said: It is a village in Egypt from which they had traveled to Egypt. "And the caravan in which we came," meaning: the caravan in which we were. They were accompanied by people from Canaan, neighbors of Jacob. Ibn Ishaq said: The brother who was detained in Egypt knew that his brothers were people of suspicion before their father because of what they had done regarding Joseph, so he ordered them to tell this to their father. "And we are truthful." If it is said: How did Joseph allow himself to do this to his father without telling him where he was, and imprison his brother while he knew how intense his father was with him, and in this is the meaning of disobedience, severing family ties, and lack of compassion? It was said: People talked a lot about it, but the truth is that he did that by the command of God Almighty, who commanded him to do that, to increase Jacob’s affliction and multiply his reward and make him join his ancestors in rank. It was said: He did not reveal himself to his brothers because he was not sure that they would plot against him and hide it from his father. The first is more correct.
12:83: 83- "He said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something,'" and it is an abbreviation of its meaning: So they returned to their father and mentioned to their father what their elder had said, and Jacob said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something," meaning: He took your brother to Egypt to seek immediate benefit. So have patience, and perhaps God will bring them all to me, meaning: Joseph, Benjamin, and their brother who was residing in Egypt. He is the All-Knowing, of my grief and sorrow over their loss, the All-Wise, in managing His creation.
12:84: 84- The Almighty said: And he turned away from them, that is because when Jacob, peace be upon him, heard the report of Benjamin, his grief was complete and reached its peak, and his grief over Joseph was stirred up so he turned away from them, and he said, Oh my grief, oh my grief, over Joseph, and grief is the most intense grief, and his eyes turned white from grief", his sight went blind. Muqatil said: He did not see with them for six years, "so he was suppressing", meaning: suppressed, filled with grief, holding it in and not expressing it. Qatada said: He kept his grief in his heart and said nothing but good. Al-Hasan said: There were eighty years between Joseph leaving his father's lap until the day he met him, and Jacob's eyes did not dry, and there was no one on the face of the earth on that day more honorable to God than Jacob.
12:85: 85- They said, meaning: the sons of Jacob, By God, you will not cease to remember Joseph, meaning: you will not cease to remember Joseph, you will not cease to love him, and no is omitted from his saying you will not cease, it is said: he did not cease to do such and such, meaning: he did not cease, like the saying of Imru' al-Qais: I said, By God, I will stand still even if they cut off my head and my limbs. That is: I will not leave. Until it is buried, Ibn Abbas said: We were buried. Mujahed said: Haradh is what is below death, meaning: close to death. Ibn Ishaq said: Corrupt, you have no mind. Al-Hardh: the one whose body and mind are corrupted. It was also said: melting from worry. The meaning of the verse: until the body is weak and the mind is insane. The root of Haradh is corruption of the body and mind from sadness, old age, or love. It is said: a Haradh man and a Haradh woman, two Haradh men and two Haradh women, men and women as well. It is the same for one and two, for a group, for a male and a female, because it is a source that is placed in place of a noun. Or you will be among the perishing, meaning: among the dead.
12:86: 86- He said Jacob, peace be upon him, when he saw their harshness, I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God. And suffering is the most intense grief, and it was called that because its owner cannot be patient with it until he proves it, that is, shows it. Al-Hasan said: My suffering means: my need. It is narrated that a neighbor of his came to Jacob and said: O Jacob, why do I see you so broken and wasted, and you have not reached the age your father did? He said: What God has afflicted me with of the worries of Joseph has broken me and wasted me. So God revealed to him: O Jacob, do you complain about me to My creation? He said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive me for it. He said: I have forgiven you for it. After that, whenever he was asked, he would say: I only complain about my sorrow and grief to God. It was narrated that he was asked: O Jacob, what has made you lose your sight and your back bow? He said: My weeping over Joseph has made me lose my sight, and my back has been bent over by my grief over his brother? Then God revealed to him: Do you complain about Me? By My glory and majesty, I will not reveal what is wrong with you until you call upon Me. Then he said: I only complain of my distress and grief to God. God revealed to him: By My glory and majesty, if they were dead, I would have brought them out for you. I only found fault with you because you slaughtered a sheep, and a poor man stood at your door and you did not stab him with anything from it. The most beloved of My creation to Me are the prophets, then the poor. So prepare food and invite the poor to it. He made food and then said: Whoever is fasting should break his fast tonight at the house of Jacob. It was narrated that after that, whenever he had lunch, he would order someone to call out: Whoever wants lunch, let Jacob come. And whenever he had breakfast, he would order someone to call out: Whoever wants to break his fast, let Jacob come. So he would eat lunch and dinner with the poor. On the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, he said: God Almighty revealed to Jacob: Do you know why I punished you and kept Joseph away from you for eighty years? He said: No, my God. He said: Because you roasted a young goat and were stingy with your neighbor, and ate without feeding him. It was narrated that the reason for Jacob’s trial was that he slaughtered a calf in front of his mother while she was mooing. Wahb, Al-Suddi and others said: Gabriel came to Joseph, peace be upon him, in prison and said: Do you know me, O friend? He said: I see a pure image and a pleasant smell. He said: I am the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds and I am the Trustworthy Spirit. He said: What brought you into the sinners’ house, when you are the best of the best, the head of those brought near, and the trustee of the Lord of the Worlds? He said: Did you not know, O Joseph, that God Almighty purifies houses through the purity of the prophets, and that the land they enter is the purest of lands, and that God Almighty has purified the prison and what is around it through you, O pure of the pure and son of the righteous and sincere? He said: How can I be called one of the righteous and count as one of the sincere and pure, when I have been admitted as one of the sinners and called one of the wicked? Gabriel said: Because your heart was not tempted and you did not obey your mistress in disobeying your Lord, therefore God named you among the truthful, counted you among the sincere, and included you with your righteous fathers. Joseph said to me: Do you know about Jacob, O faithful spirit? He said: Yes, God gave him beautiful patience and tested him with grief over you, so he is suppressing it. He said: How much sadness? He said: The grief of seventy bereaved women. He said: What is his reward, Gabriel? He said: The reward of a hundred martyrs. He said: Do you think I will meet him? He said: Yes. Joseph was pleased, and he said: I do not care what I encounter if I see him. God Almighty says: And I know from God what you do not know, meaning: I know from Joseph’s life what you do not know. It was narrated that the Angel of Death visited Jacob and said to him: O king with a pleasant scent and a handsome appearance, have you taken the soul of my son among the souls? He said: No. Jacob calmed down and hoped to see him, and said: I know that Joseph’s vision is true and that you and I will prostrate to him. Al-Saddī said: When his son told him about the king’s conduct, Jacob felt anxious and became hopeful, and said, Perhaps it is Joseph. So he said, O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Yazid bin Abi Farwa: that Jacob, peace be upon him, wrote a letter to Joseph, peace be upon him, when Benjamin was imprisoned: From Jacob, Israel of God, the son of Isaac, the sacrifice of God, the son of Abraham, the friend of God, to the king of Egypt. As for what follows: We are a family upon whom calamity has befallen us. As for my grandfather Abraham, his hands and feet were bound and he was thrown into the fire, so God made it cool and safe for him. As for my father, his hands and feet were bound and a knife was placed on the back of his neck, so God ransomed him. As for me, I had a son who was the most beloved of my sons to me, so his brothers took him to the wilderness and brought me his shirt stained with blood. They said: The wolf has eaten him. My eyes went out from crying over him. Then I had a son who was his brother on his mother’s side, and I used to amuse myself with him. You imprisoned him and claimed that he had stolen, and we are a family who do not steal or give birth to a thief. If you return him to me, otherwise I will invoke a curse upon you that will reach the seventh of your children. When Joseph read the letter, he could not control his crying and his patience was exhausted, so he revealed himself as we will mention, God willing. Come here.
12:87: 87- The Almighty said: O my sons, go and inquire, inform and seek good, from Joseph and his brother, and inquiring with the letter ha and the letter jim are not far from each other, except that inquiring with the letter ha is for good and with the letter jim for evil, and inquiring is seeking something with the senses. Ibn Abbas said: Its meaning is seek and do not despair, and do not lose hope of the mercy of God, meaning: of the mercy of God, and it was said: of the relief of God. Indeed, no one despairs of the mercy of God except the disbelieving people.
12:88: 88- When they entered upon him, and it contains an implied meaning: So they went out returning to Egypt until they reached it and entered upon Joseph, peace be upon him. They said, O noble one, hardship has touched us and our family, meaning: hardship and hunger, and we have brought poor merchandise, meaning: little, poor, and unsold, and it is not spent on the price of food except by permission from the seller for it, and the origin of izja' is the market and payment. It was said: the merchandise is poor because it is not spent, and it is only permissible by payment from the one who takes it. They differed about it. Ibn Abbas said: They were bad, counterfeit dirhams. It was said: It was created by instincts and ropes. It was said: It was a Bedouin commodity made of wool and cotton. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was the green seed. It was said: It was made from the gruel of the pastry. It was said: It was leather and sandals. Give us full measure, meaning: Give us what you used to give us before at a good, full price. And be charitable to us, meaning: favor us with something between the good and bad prices and do not reduce it for us. This is what most commentators say. Ibn Jurayj and Al-Dahhak said: He did us a favor by returning our brother to us. God rewards, “rewards,” those who give charity. Ad-Dahhak said: They did not say, May God reward you, because they did not know that he was a believer. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah was asked: Was charity forbidden to any of the prophets other than our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him? Sufyan said: Have you not heard the words of God Almighty: “And give us charity. Indeed, God rewards the charitable.” He means that charity was permissible for them. It was narrated that Al-Hasan heard a man saying: O God, give me charity. He said: God does not give charity, but rather he who seeks reward gives charity. Say: O God, give me or be generous to me.
12:89: 89- He said, 'Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother while you were ignorant?' They differed about the reason that led Joseph to say this. Ibn Ishaq said: It was mentioned to me that when they spoke to him with this speech, he was overcome by tenderness and his tears streamed down, so he revealed what he had been concealing from them. Al-Kalbi said: He said that when he told his brothers that Malik bin Dhi’r said: I found a boy in a well in such and such a condition, so I bought him for so many dirhams. They said: O king, we sold that boy. Joseph was enraged by that and ordered them to be killed. They went with them to kill them, but Judah turned away saying: Jacob was sad and wept over the loss of one of us until he lost his sight, so how would it be if he came to kill all his sons? Then they said to him: If you do that, send our belongings to our father, for he is in such and such a place. That was when he felt sorry for them and wept, and said those words. It was said: He said it when he read his father’s letter to him and could not hold back his tears. He said: Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you separated them and did what you did while you were ignorant of what would happen to Joseph? It was also said: They were sinners and disobedient. Al-Hasan said: When you were young and had the ignorance of youth. If it is said: How did he say what you did to Joseph and his brother, and what they did to his brother, and they did not seek to imprison him? It is said: They said to him about the Saa’, it will continue to be a trial for us. And it is said: We have not seen any good from you, O sons of Rachel. And it is said: Since he was from one mother, they used to harm him after the loss of Joseph.
12:90: 90- "They said, 'Are you indeed Joseph?'" Ibn Kathir and Abu Ja`far read: "Indeed you" as a statement, and the others read it as a question. Ibn Ishaq said: Joseph was speaking from behind a curtain. When Joseph said: Do you know what you have done? He removed the curtain from them and lifted the veil, and they recognized him. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When he said this, Joseph smiled, and they saw his teeth like strung pearls, so they likened him to Joseph, and they asked, Are you really Joseph? Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Joseph’s brothers did not recognize him until he took the crown off his head, and he had a mark on his horn, and Jacob had a similar one, and Isaac had a similar one, and Sarah had a similar one, like a mole. So they recognized him and said: Are you really Joseph? It was said: They said it based on imagination until, He said, I am Joseph, and this is my brother, Benjamin, God has bestowed favor upon us, He has bestowed favor upon us by bringing us together. He who fears God by performing the obligatory duties and avoiding sins, and is patient about what God Almighty has forbidden him. Ibn Abbas said: He fears adultery and is patient about celibacy. Mujahid said: He fears sin and is patient about imprisonment, then indeed, God does not allow to be lost the reward of the righteous.
12:91: 91-They said, apologizing, By God, God has favored you over us, meaning: God chose you and favored you over us, even though we were sinners, meaning: We were not in all our actions except mistaken and guilty. It is said: he made a mistake if he intended it, and he made a mistake if it was unintentional.
12:92: 92- "He said, Joseph, who was forbearing, There is no blame upon you today, no reproach upon you today, and I will not mention your sin to you after today, God will forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful."
12:93: 93-When Joseph made himself known to them, he asked them about his father, saying: What did my father do after I left? They said: His eyes have gone. So he gave them his shirt and said: Go with this shirt of mine and throw it over my father’s face, and he will come back with his sight, meaning: he will be able to see. It was also said: He will come to me with his sight because he had invited him. Al-Hasan said: He did not know that he would regain his sight until God Almighty informed him. Al-Dahhak said: That shirt was woven from Paradise. On the authority of Mujahid, he said: Gabriel ordered him to send him his shirt, and that shirt was the shirt of Abraham, peace be upon him, because he was stripped of his clothes and thrown into the fire naked, so Gabriel came to him with a shirt of silk from Paradise, and dressed him in it, and that shirt remained with Abraham, peace be upon him, and when he died, Isaac inherited it, and when he died, Jacob inherited it, and when Joseph grew up, Jacob put that shirt in a reed, and covered its top, and hung it around his neck, because he feared the evil eye for him, so it would not leave him. When he was thrown into the well naked, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him with that talisman on Joseph, so he took out the shirt from it and dressed him in it, and at that time Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to Joseph, peace be upon him, and said: Send that shirt, for in it is the scent of Paradise, and it does not fall on a sick or afflicted person except that he recovers, so Joseph gave that shirt to his brothers and said: Throw it on my father’s face and he will regain his sight, and And bring me your family, all together.
12:94: 94- And when the caravan departed, that is, it left the hut of Egypt heading to Canaan, their father said, that is, Jacob said to his grandson, I smell the scent of Joseph. It was narrated that the morning wind asked permission from its Lord to bring Jacob the scent of Joseph before the bearer of good report came to him. Mujahed said: Jacob smelled the scent of Joseph from a distance of three days. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: from a distance of eight nights. Al-Hasan said: There were eighty farsakhs between them. It was said: A wind blew and slapped the shirt, and the scent of the shirt carried it to Jacob, who found the scent of Paradise. He knew that there was no scent of Paradise on earth except what was from that shirt, so he said: I find the scent of Joseph. If only you would refute me, you would make me foolish. Ibn Abbas said: you would ignore me. Ad-Dahhak said: you would grow old and say old. An old man who has lost his mind. It was said: You are making me weak. Abu Ubaidah said: You are misleading me. The root of fand is corruption.
12:95: 95- They said, meaning: his grandchildren's grandchildren, By God, you are indeed in your old error, meaning: your old mistake in mentioning Joseph, do not forget it, and error is going astray from the right path, for they believe that Joseph has died and they see that Jacob has been busy mentioning him.
12:96: 96- So when the bearer of good tidings came, meaning the bearer of good tidings on behalf of Joseph, Ibn Masoud said: The bearer of good tidings came before the caravan. Ibn Abbas said: He is Judah. Al-Suddi said: Judah said: I went to Jacob with the shirt stained with blood and told him that Joseph was eaten by a wolf. So I will go to him today with the shirt and tell him that his son is alive and make him happy as I made him sad. Ibn Abbas said: Judah carried him and went out barefoot and bareheaded, running with seven loaves of bread, which he did not finish eating until he reached his father. The distance was eighty farsakhs. It was said: Al-Basheer is Malik bin Dha’ar. He threw it on his face, meaning: the bearer of good report threw Joseph’s shirt on Jacob’s face, and he regained his sight. So he regained his sight after he had been blind, and his strength returned to him after weakness, his youth after old age, and his joy after sadness. He said, Did I not tell you that I know from God that which you do not know? From the life of Joseph and that God will bring us together. It was narrated that he said to the bearer of good tidings: How did you leave Joseph? He said: He is the king of Egypt. Jacob said: What should I do with the king? In what religion did you leave him? He said: In the religion of Islam. He said: Now the blessing is complete.
12:97: 97- "They said, 'O our father, ask forgiveness for us for our sins. Indeed, we were sinners.'"
12:98: 98- He said, 'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord.' Most commentators said: He delayed the supplication until dawn, which is the time when God Almighty says: Is there anyone who supplicates so that I may answer him? When Jacob reached the appointed time, he stood up to pray at dawn. When he finished, he raised his hands to God Almighty and said: O God, forgive me for my grief over Joseph and my lack of patience with him, and forgive my children for what they did to their brother Joseph. Then God Almighty revealed to him that I have forgiven you and them all. On the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, meaning on Friday night. Wahb said: He used to ask forgiveness for them every Friday night for more than twenty years. Tawus said: He delayed the supplication until the sun sets on Friday night, so it coincided with the night of Ashura. On the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. He said: I will ask Joseph, if He forgives you, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. It is narrated that Joseph had sent two hundred camels and much equipment with the herald to Jacob to bring Jacob, his family and his children. Jacob prepared to go out to Egypt, and they went out, seventy-two men and women. Masruq said: They were ninety-three. When he approached Egypt, Joseph spoke to the king who was above him, so Joseph and the king went out with four thousand soldiers, and the people of Egypt rode with them to meet Jacob. Jacob was walking, leaning on Judah, and he looked at the horses and the people and said: O Judah, this is the Pharaoh of Egypt. He said: No, this is your son. When each one approached his companion, Joseph went to begin greeting him, but Gabriel said: Not until Jacob begins greeting him. Jacob said: Peace be upon you, O remover of sorrows. It was narrated that they got off and embraced each other. Al-Thawri said: When Jacob and Joseph, peace be upon them, met, each of them embraced the other and cried. Joseph said: O my father, you cried until you lost your sight. Didn’t you know that the Day of Resurrection would bring us together? He said: Yes, my son, but I was afraid that your religion would be taken away and a separation would occur between me and you.
12:99: 99-Therefore, the Almighty’s saying: So when they entered upon Joseph, he took to him means: he took to him his parents. Most of the commentators said: He was his father and his aunt Leah, and his mother Rachel had died during Benjamin’s childbirth. Al-Hassan said: He is his father and mother, and she was alive. In some interpretations, God Almighty revived his mother until she came with Jacob to Egypt. And he said, ‘Enter Egypt, if God wills, in safety.’ If it is said: He said, When they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents into his care. So how did he say, Enter Egypt, if God wills, in safety, after he had informed us that they had entered it? What is the point of this exception when the entry had taken place? It was said: Joseph said this to them when he met them before they entered Egypt. There is an inversion in the verse, and the exception is due to seeking forgiveness, which is from what Jacob said to his sons: I will seek forgiveness for you from my Lord, God willing. It was said: The exception goes back to security from the passport because they did not enter Egypt before that except with a passport from their kings. He says: Security from the passport, God Almighty willing, as He said: You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, in safety (al-Fath 48:27). It was said: If here means when, meaning: if God wills, as God Almighty says: And you will be superior if you are believers (Al Imran 3:139). That is: if you are believers.
12:100: 100- And he raised his parents to the throne, meaning: on the bed, he made them sit. Raising means moving to the heights. And they fell down before him in prostration, meaning: Jacob, his aunt, and his brothers. The greeting of the people on that day was prostration, and prostration did not mean placing the foreheads on the ground, but rather bowing and humility. It was said: They placed their foreheads on the ground, and that was as a way of greeting and reverence, not as a way of worship. That was permissible among previous nations, but it was abrogated in this Sharia. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Its meaning is: They fell down prostrating before God Almighty in front of Joseph. The first is more correct. And he said, Joseph at that time: “O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it come true,” which is his saying: Indeed, I saw eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me. “And He has been kind to me,” my Lord, meaning: He has bestowed His blessings upon me, when He brought me out of prison, and He did not say from the well, even though it was a more severe trial than prison, using generosity, so that his brothers would not be ashamed after he said to them: There is no blame upon you today, and because God’s blessing upon him in bringing him out of prison is greater, because after leaving the well he became a slave and a servant, and after leaving prison he became a king, and because his falling into the well was due to the envy of his brothers, and in prison he was a reward from God Almighty for a mistake he made. And he brought you from the Bedouins, and the Bedouins are a simple land inhabited by livestock people with their livestock, and they were people of the desert and livestock. It is said that he went to the desert. After the devil had incited corrupted, between me and my brothers, with envy. My Lord is Kind, meaning: He is kind, to whomever He wills, and it was said that it means to whomever He wills. The truth of Al-Lateef is: He who conveys kindness to others through gentleness. He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. Historians said: Jacob stayed in Egypt with Joseph for twenty-four years in the most blessed state and the most comfortable life, then he died in Egypt. When death approached him, he ordered his son Joseph to carry his body until he buried it with his father Isaac, so Joseph did that, and went with it until he buried it in the Levant, then he returned to Egypt. Saeed bin Jubair said: Jacob, peace be upon him, was transported in a teak coffin to Jerusalem, and that coincided with the day on which Esau died, so they were buried in one grave. They were born in one womb, and their age was one hundred and forty-seven years.
12:101: 101-When God gathered Joseph together, he knew that the pleasures of this world would not last. He asked God for a good end, and said: My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom, meaning: the kingdom of Egypt. The kingdom is the vastness of destiny for the one who has politics and management. And You have taught me of the interpretation of dreams, meaning: the interpretation of dreams. Creator, meaning: O Creator, of the heavens and the earth, meaning: their Creator. You are my protector, meaning: my helper and the one who takes care of my affairs. In this world and in the Hereafter, cause me to die a Muslim, meaning: take me to You as a Muslim, and join me with the righteous, meaning my prophet fathers. Qatada said: No prophet asked for death except Joseph. In the story: When God reunited him and brought his parents and family to him, he longed for his Lord, the Almighty, and said this statement. Al-Hasan said: He lived for many years after this. Another said: When he said this, less than a week passed before he died. They differed about the duration of Joseph’s absence from his father. Al-Kalbi said: Twenty-two years. It was said: forty years. Al-Hasan said: Joseph was thrown into the well when he was seventeen years old, and he was absent from his father for eighty years. He lived twenty-three years after meeting Jacob, and he died when he was one hundred and twenty years old. In the Torah, he died at the age of one hundred and ten years, and Joseph had three sons from the wife of Al-Aziz: Ephraim, Mesha, and Rahmah, the wife of the afflicted Job, peace be upon him. It was said: Joseph lived sixty years after his father. It was said: more. And the sayings about him differed. He died at the age of one hundred and twenty years, and they buried him in the Nile in a marble box. When he died, people argued over him, and the people of each neighborhood asked that he be buried in their neighborhood, hoping for his blessing. They even wanted to fight, so they decided to bury him in the Nile, where the waters of Egypt disperse, so that the water would flow over him and his blessing would reach all of them. Akrima said: He was buried on the right side of the Nile, so that side became fertile and the other side became barren. He was then moved to the left side, so that side became fertile and the other side became barren. They buried him in the middle of it, and they estimated that with a chain, so both sides became fertile until Moses took him out and buried him near his fathers in the Levant.
12:102: 102-That, which you mentioned, is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them, meaning: you, O Muhammad, were not with the sons of Jacob, when they decided on their plan, meaning: they resolved to throw Joseph into the well, and they were plotting, against Joseph.
12:103: 103- And most people are not believers, O Muhammad, even if you were eager to do so, because of their belief. It was narrated that the Jews and Quraysh asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the story of Joseph. When he told them in accordance with the Torah, they did not submit. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saddened, and it was said to him: They will not believe, even if you are keen for them to believe.
12:104: 104- And you do not ask them for it, meaning: for conveying the message and calling to God Almighty, of reward, making and recompense, it is, meaning the Qur'an, except a reminder, a sermon and a reminder, for the worlds.
12:105: 105- And how many, and how many, of a sign, a lesson and an indication, in the heavens and the earth which they pass over while they are turning away from them, they do not think about them nor take heed of them.
12:106: 106- "And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him." So their faith was that when they were asked: Who created the heavens and the earth? They said: God. And when they were asked: Who sends down the rain? They said: God. Then despite that, they worship idols and associate others with Him. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: It was revealed regarding the Talbiyah of the polytheists among the Arabs. They used to say in their Talbiyah: “Here I am, O God, here I am, here I am. You have no partner except a partner who is Yours. You own him and what he owns.” Ata’ said: This is about supplication, because the disbelievers forgot their Lord in times of ease, but when calamity befell them, they were sincere in supplication, as God Almighty said: And they thought that they were surrounded, so they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion (Yunus 10:22). And God Almighty said: “So when they embark on a ship, they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to land, at once they associate others with Him” (al-Ankabut 29:65), and other verses.
12:107: 107- Do they then feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from God? That is, a severe punishment. Mujahid said: A punishment that will overwhelm them, similar to the Almighty's statement: The Day the punishment will overwhelm them from above them (al-Ankabut 29:55). Qatada said: A calamity. Ad-Dahhak said: He means thunderbolts and calamities. Or that the Hour will come upon them suddenly, suddenly, while they perceive not, of its occurrence. Ibn Abbas said: The shout will stir up people while they are in their markets.
12:108: 108- Say, O Muhammad, This, the call to which I call and the method I follow, my way, my tradition and my approach. Muqatil said: My religion, similar to His statement: Invite to the way of your Lord (al-Nahl 16:125), meaning: to His religion. I call to God with insight, with certainty. Insight is the knowledge that distinguishes between right and wrong. I and those who follow me, meaning, whoever believes in me and trusts me also calls to God. This is what Al-Kalbi and Ibn Zayd said. They said: It is the right of those who follow him to call to what he called to, and to remind them of the Qur’an. It was said: The speech was completed when he said: I call to God, then he resumed: With insight, I and whoever follows me, meaning: I have insight from my Lord and everyone who follows me. Ibn Abbas said: He means that the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were on the best path and the most direct guidance, the source of knowledge, the treasure of faith, and the soldiers of the Most Merciful. Abdullah bin Masoud said: Whoever wants to follow our example, let him follow the example of those who have died, for the living are not safe from temptation. Those are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They were the best of this nation, the most pious of heart, the most profound in knowledge, and the least pretentious. They were a people whom God chose to be companions of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to establish His religion. So recognize their virtue, follow their footsteps, and hold fast to whatever you can of their morals and conduct, for they were on the straight path. God Almighty says: And glory be to God, meaning: Say glory be to God, sanctifying Him from what they associate with Him. And I am not of the polytheists.
12:109: 109-And We did not send before you, O Muhammad, except men, not angels, to whom We revealed, Hafs read: We revealed with a noon and a kasra on the ha’, and the others read it with a ya’ and a fatha on the ha’. From the people of the villages, meaning: from the people of the cities rather than the deserts, because the people of the cities are more intelligent, better, more knowledgeable, and more patient. Al-Hassan said: God did not send a prophet from the Bedouins, nor from the jinn, nor from women. It was said: He was not sent from the desert because of their roughness and harshness. Have they not traveled through the land, meaning: these polytheistic deniers, and observed what was the end, the last command, of those before them, meaning: the nations who deniers, so that they might take heed. And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God, says the Most High: This is for the people of our guardianship and obedience, that we will save them when the punishment descends, and what is in the home of the Hereafter is better for them, so we left what we mentioned out of sufficiency, because the speech indicates it. God Almighty says: And for the home of the Hereafter. It was said that its meaning is for the home of the present and the Hereafter. It was said: It is adding something to itself, like His saying: Indeed, this is the absolute truth (al-Waqi’ah 56:959) and like their saying: Thursday, and Rabi’ al-Akhir. Do you not understand? So you believe.
12:110: 110- Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our victory came to them. The reciters differed regarding his saying: they had been denied: The people of Kufa and Abu Jaafar read: They lied with a light pronunciation, and Aisha rejected this reading. Others read it with emphasis. Whoever is severe said: Its meaning is until the messengers despaired of the faith of their people. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he read: And they denied, with the kaf open and the dhal lightened, and it has two interpretations: One of them means: that the polytheistic people thought that the messengers had lied. The second means: that the messengers thought - that is, knew - that their people had fabricated a lie against God by their disbelief in their people’s faith. They thought: that is, they were certain - meaning the messengers - that the nations had denied them with a denial that could not be hoped for after their belief. Suspicion means certainty: This is the meaning of Qatada’s statement. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Until the messengers despaired of those among their people who denied them believing them, and they thought that those among their people who believed in them had denied them and turned away from their religion, due to the severity of the trial and affliction upon them and the slowness of victory. And whoever reads it with the light vowel said: Its meaning is: Until the messengers despaired of the belief of their people and thought, i.e. their people thought that the messengers had denied them in the threat of punishment. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Its meaning is the weakness of the hearts of the messengers, meaning: The messengers thought that they had been lied to regarding the victory they were promised. They were human beings, so they became weak and despaired and thought that they had failed to fulfill their promise. Then he recited: Until the Messenger and those who believed with him say, ‘When is the victory of God?’ (al-Baqarah 2:214), meaning: The messengers came to grant us victory. And We save whom We will. The common people read it with two noons, meaning: We save whom We will. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Asim, and Ya'qub read it with one noon with a dammah, a shaddah on the jim, and a fathah on the ya' for what the agent is not named, because it is written in the Qur'an with one noon, so the position of whom is nominative, according to this reading. According to the first reading, it is accusative, so We save whom We will from the descent of the punishment, and they are the obedient believers. Our punishment cannot be averted from the criminal people, meaning the polytheists.
12:111: 111- There was in their stories, that is, in the story of Joseph and his brothers, a lesson, a sermon, "for those of understanding. It was not", that is, the Qur'an, a fabricated story, that is, invented, but a confirmation of that, that is, but it was a confirmation of that which was before it, of the Torah and the Gospel, and a detailed account of everything, of what the servants need of what is permissible and forbidden, commands and prohibitions, and guidance and mercy, clarification and blessing, for a people who believe.
13:1: 1- Meccan, except for His saying: And those who disbelieve will not cease, and His saying: And those who disbelieve will say, ‘You are not a messenger,’ and it is forty-three verses. Al-Mar Ibn Abbas said: Its meaning is: I am God, I know and I see. These are the verses of the Book, meaning: those are the report that the verses of the Torah, the Gospel, and the previous books have told you. And that which has been revealed to you, meaning: and this Qur’an that has been revealed to you, from your Lord is the truth, meaning: it is the truth, so hold fast to it. The position of who is raised as a subject, and the truth is its predicate. It was said: Its place is in the accusative case, meaning: Those are the verses of the Book and the verses of what was revealed to you, then he began: the truth, meaning: that is the truth. Ibn Abbas said: He meant by the Book the Qur’an, and its meaning is: These are the verses of the Book, meaning the Qur’an. Then he said: And this Qur’an that was revealed to you from your Lord is the truth. But most people do not believe. Muqatil said: It was revealed about the polytheists of Mecca when they said: Muhammad says it on his own. He rejected their statement and then explained the evidence of his Lordship. The Almighty said:
13:2: 2- God is He who raised the heavens without any pillars that you can see, meaning: the masts, the singular of which is column, like: adim and adam, and pillars are also its plural, like: rasool and rusul. Its meaning is the denial of intent altogether, which is the most correct, meaning: there is no support below it to support it, nor a relationship above it to hold it together. Iyas bin Muawiyah said: The sky is vaulted over the earth like a dome. It was said: You see it refers back to the pillars, meaning: it has pillars but you do not see it. He claimed that its pillars are Mount Qaf, which surrounds the world, and the sky is above it like a dome. Then He established Himself on the Throne, He rose above it, and subjected the sun and the moon, He made them subservient to the benefit of His creation, so they are subjugated. Each runs, that is, they run as God Almighty wills, for a specified term, that is, until a known time, which is the passing of the world. Ibn Abbas said: By the specified term, He meant its degrees and stations, which they will reach and not exceed. He directs the affair, He decrees it alone. He details the signs, He clarifies the evidence. That you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord, so that you may be certain of His promise and believe in Him.
13:3: 3- And it is He who spread out the earth, He expanded it, and placed therein firm mountains, fixed mountains, the singular of which is: rasayyah. Ibn Abbas said: Abu Qubays was the first mountain placed on the earth, and rivers, and He placed rivers therein. And of all the fruits He has made therein two mates, meaning: two types, red and yellow, sweet and sour. He covers the night with the day, meaning: He covers the day with the darkness of the night, and covers the night with the light of the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought, meaning they draw conclusions. And contemplation is the heart’s turning to seeking the meanings of things.
13:4: 4- And on the earth are neighboring tracts, close together, some close to each other, and they are different: this one is good and produces vegetation, and this one is salt marsh and does not produce vegetation, this one has little yield, and this one has much yield, and gardens: orchards, of grapes and crops and palm trees in pairs, all of which were raised by Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hafs, and Ya’qub, in apposition to the gardens, and the others made them genitive in sequence with the grapes. Sunwan: plural of sunu, which is palm trees that have one root. And other than two, is the palm tree that is unique in its origin. The commentators said: Sanawan means together, and ghayr sawan means separate. Its equivalent in speech is: Qanawan is the plural of Qanu. Including the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Al-Abbas: A man’s paternal uncle is like his father. There is no difference in the dual and plural forms of sanwan and qanwan except in the case of inflection, as the nun in the dual form is broken and not tanween, while in the plural it is tanween. It is watered with one water. Ibn Amir, Asim, and Yaqub read it is watered with a ya meaning that all of that is watered with one water. The others read it with a ta because of the Almighty’s saying: and gardens and because the Almighty said after that some of them upon others, and He did not say some of it. Water is a delicate, fluid body with which every living thing lives. And We prefer some of them over others in eating, in fruit and taste. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read and we prefer with a ya, based on the Almighty’s saying: He directs the affair and details the verses (al-Ra’d 13:2). Others read it with the letter nun meaning: We prefer some of them over others in eating. It was mentioned in the hadith in his saying: And we prefer some of them over others in eating. He said: Persian, date, sweet, and sour. Mujahed said: Like the children of Adam, the good and the bad, and their father is one. Al-Hasan said: This is a parable that God Almighty gave for the hearts of the children of Adam. He says: The earth was a single clay in the hand of the Most Gracious, the Almighty, so He spread it out, and it became adjacent pieces. Then rain descends upon it from the sky, and this one produces its flowers, trees, fruits, and plants, and this one produces its salt marsh, salt, and filth, and everything is watered by one water. Thus, people were created from Adam, peace be upon him, so a reminder descends from the sky, so hearts are softened and become humble, and hearts harden and become distracted. Al-Hasan said: By God, no one has sat with the Qur’an without getting up with an addition or subtraction. God Almighty said: And We send down of the Qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy to the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss (al-Isra’ 17:82). Indeed in that that you mentioned are signs for a people who understand.
13:5: 5- "And if you are amazed, then their statement is amazed." Amazement is the change in the soul when seeing what is usually unlikely, and the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its meaning is: If you are amazed at their denial of the afterlife while they acknowledge that creation began with God Almighty, then their matter is amazed. Some of the polytheists denied the resurrection, while acknowledging that God Almighty began creation. It was established in their hearts that the return is easier than the beginning, and this is a source of wonder. It was said: Its meaning is: And if you are amazed at the polytheists’ denial and their taking as gods that neither harm nor benefit, and they have seen from the power of God Almighty what He has given them examples of, then you are amazed at their statement, that is: you are also amazed at their statement: When we are dust, after death, shall we indeed be in a new creation, that is: we will be recreated anew as we were before death. Nafi`, Al-Kisa`i and Ya`qub read A`idha as a question, Inna without it, as a statement, the opposite of which is: Abu Ja`far and Ibn `Amir. And likewise in Subhan in two places, and Al-Mu`minun, and Al-Sajdah, and the rest read it as a question in both of them and in / As-Saffat in two places like this except that Abu Ja`far agrees with Nafi` in the beginning of As-Saffat, so he brings forward the question and Ya`qub does not ask a question in the second When we die and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be recompensed? (al-Saffat 37:53). God Almighty said: Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, and those are the ones whose necks will be shackled, on the Day of Resurrection, and those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally.
13:6: 6- The Almighty said: "And they urge you to hasten the evil before the good." Hastening means asking to hasten a matter before its time comes. The evil here is punishment, and the good is well-being. This is because the polytheists of Mecca were asking for punishment instead of well-being in mockery of them, saying: "O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment." (al-Anfal 8:32). And before them there have been examples, meaning: there have been punishments before them among the nations that disobeyed their Lord and denied His messengers. Examples is the plural of example, with the first letter m open and the second letter tha closed, like charity and charity. And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.
13:7: 7- And those who disbelieve say, ‘Why was not a sign sent down to him’, meaning: to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his Lord? meaning: a sign and proof of his prophethood. God Almighty said: You are only a warner, frightening, and for every people is a guide, meaning for every people there is a prophet who calls them to God Almighty. Al-Kalbi said: A caller who calls them to the truth or to misguidance. Ikrimah said: The guide is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says: You are only a warner and a guide for every people, meaning: a caller. Saeed bin Jubair said: The guide is God Almighty.
13:8: 8- The Almighty says: God knows what every female carries, whether male or female, whether normal or imperfect, one, two or more. And what the wombs absorb, meaning what they decrease, and what they increase. The commentators said: The decrease in the wombs means menstruation during pregnancy. If the pregnant woman menstruates, there will be a decrease in the child, because the menstrual blood is the nourishment of the child in the womb. If the blood is shed, the nourishment decreases and the child is decreased. If she does not menstruate, the child increases and is complete. So the decrease is the decrease in the creation of the child by the exit of the blood, and the increase is the completion of his creation by the retention of the blood. It was said: If she menstruates, the food is reduced and the duration of pregnancy increases until it completes nine months apparently. If she sees blood for five days, she gives birth after nine months and five days, so the deficiency is in the food and the increase is in the duration. Al-Hasan said: Its decrease is its decrease from nine months, and its increase is its increase over nine months. It was said that deficiency is the miscarriage, and increase is the completion of creation. The minimum gestation period is six months. A baby may be born during this period and survive. They differed about the maximum: Some people said: The maximum is two years, which is the statement of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said the same. A group of people said that the maximum is four years, and this is what Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said. Hammad bin Salamah said: Haram bin Hayyan was called Haram because he remained in his mother’s womb for four years. And everything with Him has a measure, meaning: with a fixed limit that He does not exceed or fall short of.
13:9: 9- The Great Knower of the Unseen and the Seen, to whom everything is inferior, the Most High, who is above everything by His power.
13:10: 10- The Almighty’s saying: It is the same among you whether you conceal your speech or declare it aloud, meaning: the one who speaks aloud is equal in God’s knowledge, and he who hides by night, meaning: concealed by the darkness of the night, and wanders by day, meaning: going about his business openly. As-Sirb with the first letter seen open and the second letter ra silent: the road. Al-Qatibi said: He is out and about during the day means he is taking care of his needs. Ibn Abbas said about this verse: He is a suspicious person, who takes things lightly at night, but when he goes out during the day, people see that he is innocent of sin. It was said: concealed at night, meaning: apparent, from their saying: hid the thing, if you showed it, and hid it: if you concealed it. And sarib by day: meaning hidden and entering into a flock.
13:11: 11- He has angels who follow one another, meaning: God Almighty has angels who follow you by night and by day. When the angels of the night ascend, the angels of the day follow them, and when the angels of the day ascend, the angels of the night follow them. And the follow-up: is the return after the beginning, and it was mentioned in the feminine form because its singular is mu’aqab, and its plural is mu’aqabat, then the plural is mu’aqabat, as it was said: the sons of Sa’d and the men of Bakr. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A`raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “They take turns among you, angels at night and angels during the day, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer, then those who spent the night among you ascend, and their Lord asks them - and He knows best about them - ‘How did you leave My servants? ’ They say: ‘We left them while they were praying and we came to them while they were praying. ’” The Almighty says: From before him and from behind him, meaning: from in front of this one who hides at night and travels during the day, and from behind him: from behind his back, they protect him by the command of God, meaning: by the command of God, that is: they protect him by the permission of God Almighty until what is destined comes, and when what is destined comes, they leave him alone. It was said: They protect it from the command of God: meaning from what God commanded to be protected from it. Mujahid said: There is no servant but that he has an angel assigned to him, who protects him in his sleep and wakefulness from the jinn, humans, and vermin. Nothing of them comes to him wanting him but he says, Behind you! except something that God permits and it befalls him. Kaab al-Ahbar said: If God Almighty had not assigned angels to protect you in your food, drink, and private parts, the jinn would have snatched you away. Ikrimah said: The verse is about the princes and their guards who protect him from in front of them and from behind them. It was said: The verse is about the two angels sitting on the right and on the left, writing down the good and bad deeds, as God Almighty said: When the two receivers receive, one sitting on the right and one on the left (Qaf: 17). Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning of they preserve him is: they preserve his deeds from the command of God, meaning: good and bad deeds. It was said: The letter ha in his saying to him refers back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Juwaybir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: He has guardians, meaning that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, has guardians from the Most Merciful, before him and behind him, who protect him from the command of God, meaning: from the evil of the jinn and the calamities of the night and day. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid said: These verses were revealed about Amer bin Al-Tufayl and Arbad bin Rabi’ah, and their story was as Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Saleh on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Amer bin Al-Tufayl and Arbad bin Rabi’ah, both of them from the tribe of Amer, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with a group of his companions. They entered the mosque and the people were amazed at the beauty of Amer, who was one-eyed and was one of the most noble of people. A man said: O Messenger of God, this is Amer bin Al-Tufayl coming towards you. He said: Leave him, for if God wants good for him, He will guide him. He came and stood over him and said: O Muhammad, what will happen to me if I become a Muslim? He said: You have what the Muslims have and you are responsible for what the Muslims are responsible for. He said: You will make me in charge after you. He said: It is not up to me, it is up to God Almighty, He makes it where He wills. He said: So you put me on the hair and you on the mud? He said: No. He said: Why do you make it for me? He said: I will give you the reins of the horses to fight on. He said: Isn’t that until today? Come with me so I can talk to you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, got up with him. Aamer had advised Arbad bin Rabi’ah, If you see me talking to him, go behind him and strike him with the sword. So he began to argue with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to argue with him, so Arbad went behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to strike him, but he drew a span of his sword, then God Almighty held him back from him, so he was not able to draw it, and Aamer kept gesturing to him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned and saw Arbad and what he had done with his sword, so he said, O God, suffice me against them however You wish. Then God sent lightning upon Arbad on a clear, scorching day, and it burned it down. Amer fled and said: O Muhammad, you called upon your Lord to kill Arbad. By God, I will fill it against you with bare horses and beardless youths. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty will prevent you from that, and the sons of Qaylah, meaning: the Aws and the Khazraj. So Aamer went down to the house of a woman from Saluliya, and when morning came, he put his weapon on him, and its color had changed, and he started running in the desert, and saying: Come out, O Angel of Death, and he recited poetry, and he said: By Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, if I see Muhammad and his companion, meaning the Angel of Death, I will pierce them with my spear. So God sent an angel to him, and he slapped him with his wing and he fell into the dust, and a great wound came out on his knees at that time, so he returned to the house of the Saluliya, and he said: A wound like the wound of a camel, and death in the house of the Saluliya. Then he called for his horse, and he mounted it, and he made it run until he died on its back, and God answered the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and killed Aamer bin Tufail by stabbing and Arbad by lightning, and God, the Almighty, revealed about this story His saying: “It is the same among you, he who conceals his speech and he who declares it, and he who hides it by night and goes forth by day. He has guardians before him.” Meaning, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had guardians who guard him from before him and behind him by the command of God. That is, those consequences are from God’s command, and there is an advancement and a delay in it. He said to these two: God will not change the condition of a people, of well-being and blessings, until they change what is in themselves, of the beautiful state, and disobey their Lord. And when God intends evil for a people, meaning: punishment and destruction, there is no repelling it, meaning: there is no one to repel it, and they have no protector besides Him, meaning: a refuge to which they can turn. It was said: A protector is someone who takes care of their affairs and prevents punishment from reaching them.
13:12: 12- The Almighty said: It is He who shows you lightning, causing fear and hope. It was said: fear of the thunderbolt, hope for the benefit of the rain. It was said: Fear is for the traveler, he fears harm and hardship from him, and greed is for the resident, he hopes for blessing and benefit from him. It was said: Fear of rain in the wrong place and time, and greed when it is in the right place and time. There are countries that if they have rain they become dry and if they do not have rain they become fertile. And He creates the heavy clouds, with rain. It is said: God created the cloud, so it became established, meaning: He made it appear, and clouds are a plural, the singular of which is cloud. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: The cloud is a sieve of water.
13:13: 13- And the thunder glorifies Him with praise. Most commentators agree that thunder is the name of an angel who drives the clouds, and the sound heard from it is His glorification. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever hears the sound of thunder and says: Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels out of fear of Him, and He is over all things competent, then if a thunderbolt strikes him, then I am responsible for his blood money. On the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr: When he heard the sound of thunder, it was very intense for the people of the earth. In some hadiths, God Almighty says: If My servants had obeyed Me, I would have given them rain at night, and made the sun rise upon them during the day, and would not have made them hear the sound of thunder. Jarir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Thunder is an angel assigned to the clouds, directing them to where he is commanded, and that the seas of water are in the depression of his thumb, and that he glorifies God Almighty, and when he glorifies, there remains no angel in the heavens except that he raises his voice in glorification, and then the rain falls. And the angels out of fear of Him, meaning: the angels glorify Him out of fear of God Almighty and awe of Him. It was said that by these angels he meant the helpers of thunder. God Almighty made helpers for him, so they are fearful, submissive, and obedient. God Almighty says: And He sends down thunderbolts, the plural of thunderbolt, which is: deadly punishment, lightning descends and burns whoever it strikes, and He strikes with it whomever He wills, as He struck Arbad bin Rabi’ah. Muhammad bin Ali Al-Baqir said: Thunderbolt strikes Muslims and non-Muslims, but it does not strike those who remember God. And they are arguing, quarreling, about God, was revealed concerning Arbad bin Rabi’ah, when he said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Who is your Lord, from pearls or rubies or gold? Then a thunderbolt came down from the sky and burned him. Al-Hassan was asked about the Almighty’s saying: And He sends down thunderbolts, the verse. He said: There was a man from the tyrants of the Arabs to whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a group of people to call him to God and to His Messenger. He said to them: Tell me about the Lord of Muhammad to whom you call me. What is he? Is he gold, silver, iron, or copper? The people were shocked by his words, so they turned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we have never seen a man more ungrateful in heart or more rebellious towards God than him! They turned away and said: O Messenger of God, he did not add to his first statement and is more evil. He said: Go back to him. So they went back. While they were with him, arguing with him and calling him, and he was saying this, a cloud rose and was above their heads. It thundered and flashed and threw a thunderbolt, and the unbeliever was burned while they were sitting. So they came running to inform the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, met them and said to them: Your companion was burned. They said: How did you know? They said: God revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills while they dispute about God. “He is very severe in punishment,” Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: He is very severe in taking. Ibn Abbas said: He is very strong-willed. Al-Hassan said: Very spiteful. Mujahed said: Very strong. Abu Ubaidah said: Severe punishment. It was said: very cunning. Al-Mahal and Al-Muhamala: deceit and overcoming.
13:14: 14- His is the call of truth, meaning: God has the call of truth. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: The call to truth is monotheism. Ibn Abbas said: Testifying that there is no god but God. It was said: Supplication with sincerity, and sincere supplication is only for God Almighty. And those they invoke besides Him, meaning: they worship idols instead of God Almighty. They do not respond to them at all, meaning: they do not answer them with anything they want of benefit or warding off harm, except like one who extends his hands toward water to reach his mouth but it will not reach it, meaning: except like one who extends his hands to grasp water and the one who grasps water has nothing in his hand and none of it reaches his mouth. Likewise, the one who invokes idols, which neither harm nor benefit, has nothing in his hand. It was said: Its meaning is like a thirsty man who sees water from afar, so he points with his hand to the water, and calls for it with his tongue, but it never comes to him. This is the meaning of what Mujahid said. And similarly, on the authority of Ali and Ata’: Like a thirsty person sitting on the edge of a well, he extends his hand into the well but does not reach the bottom of the well to the water, nor does the water rise to him, so extending his hand to the water and his supplication to it does not benefit him, nor does it reach his mouth. Likewise, those who call upon idols, their supplication does not benefit them, and they are not able to do anything. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: Like a thirsty person who spreads his hands in water, it will not benefit him unless he scoops up water with them, and the water will not reach his mouth as long as he spreads his hands. This is a metaphor for the disappointment of the infidels. And the invocation of the disbelievers, their idols, is nothing but error, which leads them astray when they need it, as He said: And what they used to invent has gone astray from them Al-An’am 6:24 and others. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The infidels’ supplication to their Lord is nothing but misguidance, because their voices are veiled from God Almighty.
13:15: 15- The Almighty said: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly, meaning: the angels and the believers, and unwillingly, meaning: the hypocrites and the disbelievers who were forced to prostrate by the sword. And their shadows, meaning: the shadows of those who prostrate willingly and obediently, and the shadow of the disbeliever who prostrates willingly and unwillingly. In the morning and the evening, meaning that if he prostrates in the morning or evening, his shadow prostrates with him. Al-Asal: plural of Asl, and Asl is the plural of Asl, which is the period between the afternoon and sunset. It was said: Their shadows, meaning: their persons in the morning and evening: in the early morning and evening. It was said: The shadow’s prostration is its submission to what is wanted for it.
13:16: 16- The Almighty said: “Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?” That is, their Creator and Manager. They will say: God, because they acknowledge that God is their Creator and the Creator of the heavens and the earth. So if they answer you, then you too, O Muhammad, say: God. It was narrated that when he said this to the polytheists, they turned to him and said: You answer. So God Almighty commanded him and said: Say God.
