Then God said to them, to make the argument binding: “Say: Have you taken guardians besides Him?” Meaning: Although you acknowledge that God is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, you have taken guardians besides Him and worshipped them instead of God, meaning: idols, and they do not possess for themselves benefit or harm, so how can they possess for you? Then he gave them an example and said: “Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?” Likewise, the disbeliever and the believer are not equal. Or are they equal? Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr read istawwa with a ya’, and the others read it with a ta’ because there is no barrier between the noun and the feminine verb. Darkness and light, meaning: Just as darkness and light are not equal, disbelief and faith are not equal. Or have they made for God partners who created like His creation so that the creation became indistinguishable to them? That is, what they created became confused with what God Almighty created, so they do not know what God created and what their gods created. Say, God is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing. Then God Almighty gave two examples of truth and falsehood, saying:
13:17: 17- "He sent down" meaning: God Almighty, "water from the sky meaning rain, and valleys flowed from that water, according to their capacity" meaning: in smallness and largeness, "and the torrent that came from that water, carried a rising foam", foam: the impurity that appears on the surface of the water, and also on the surface of the pot, "rising" meaning high and raised above the water, so the pure, remaining water is the truth, and the vanishing, disappearing water that clings to the trees and sides of the valleys is falsehood. It was said: His statement, He sends down water from the sky, is a metaphor for the Qur’an, and the valleys are a metaphor for the hearts. He means: The Qur’an descends, and the hearts bear from it according to the degree of certainty, reason, doubt, and ignorance. So this is one of the two metaphors. Another example: God Almighty said: And from that which they kindle in the Fire. Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read yuqdunu with a ya because of the Almighty’s saying: that which benefits people, and there is no addressing here. Others read with a taa’: And from what you kindle, meaning: And from what you kindle in the fire. Ignition: putting fire under something to melt it. Seeking adornment, that is, to seek decoration, and he meant gold and silver, because adornment is sought from them, or goods, that is, seeking goods, which is what is beneficial, such as iron, copper, lead, and brass, which are melted and used to make utensils and other things that are beneficial, scum like it. “Thus does God compare truth and falsehood,” meaning: if it is dissolved, it also has an addition like the foam of water. The remaining pure substance of these gems is like the truth, and the foam that is not useful is like falsehood. As for the foam, which rises above the stream and the metal, it goes away as scum, meaning: wasted and in vain. Scum is what the valley throws of foam and the pot to its sides. It is said: The valley became dry and frothy, meaning it threw away its scum. The pot boiled and frothy, meaning it boiled and threw away its foam, and when it stopped, nothing remained in it. Meaning: Even if falsehood is high for a time, it will fade away. It was said: Jafa’an means: scattered. It is said: The wind scattered the clouds if it dispersed them and took them away. As for what benefits people, meaning: water and metals such as gold, silver, brass, and copper, it remains in the earth, meaning: it remains and does not go away. Thus does God set forth parables. God Almighty made this an example of truth and falsehood, meaning that falsehood is like foam that disappears and is lost, while truth is like water and metal that remains in the hearts. It was said: This is a consolation for the believers, meaning: The matter of the polytheists is like foam that appears in the image as something but has no reality, and the matter of the believers is like water that is settled in its place and has permanence and stability.
13:18: 18- The Almighty said: For those who responded to their Lord, responded, to their Lord, and obeyed Him, is the best, Paradise, and those who did not respond to Him, if they had all that is in the earth and as much more with it, they would offer it as ransom, meaning: they would give that on the Day of Resurrection as ransom from the Fire, for them is an evil reckoning. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: An evil reckoning is that a man is held accountable for all of his sins and nothing is forgiven for him. / And their abode in the Hereafter is Hell, and an evil resting place, the bed, meaning: an evil bed is prepared for them.
13:19: 19- The Almighty said: Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and believes in it and acts according to what is in it, like one who is blind, from it, who does not know it or act according to it. It was said: It was revealed about Hamza and Abu Jahl. It was said: In Ammar and Abu Jahl. The first is Hamza or Ammar and the second is Abu Jahl, who is the blind man. Meaning: Those who see the truth and follow it are not the same as those who do not see it and do not follow it. Only those with understanding will remember and be admonished.
13:20: 20- Those who fulfill the covenant of God, with what God Almighty has commanded them to do and imposed upon them, so they do not disobey it, and do not break the covenant, and it was said: He meant the covenant that He took from the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him, when He brought them out from his loins.
13:21: 21- And those who join what God has commanded to be joined, it was said: He meant by this belief in all the books and messengers and they do not differentiate between them. Most of them say that he meant maintaining kinship ties. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Al-Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid ibn Zanjawayh told us, Ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah that Abd Al-Rahman ibn Awf visited Abu Al-Darda’ and he said - meaning Abd Al-Rahman - I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “In what he narrates from his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime: I am God, and I am the Most Gracious, and it is the womb. I derived a name for it from My name. So whoever maintains it, I will maintain it, and whoever severs it, I will sever it.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid Ibn Zabjuwayh told us, Ibn Abi Uways told us, he said: Sulayman Ibn Bilal told me, on the authority of Mu’awiyah Ibn Abi Mazrad, on the authority of Sa’id Ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God created the creation, and when He finished, the womb rose and took hold of the waist of the Most Merciful, and He said: ‘Easy!’ It said: ‘This is the place of one who seeks refuge in You from being cut off.’ He said: ‘Are you not pleased that I connect with those who connect with you and sever those who sever you?’ She said: ‘Yes, O Lord!’ He said: ‘Then that is for you.’ Then Abu Hurayrah said: Read, if you wish, ‘Then would you perhaps, if you were given authority, cause corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship?’ (Muhammad 47:22).” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid Ibn Zanjawayh told us, Muslim Ibn Ibrahim told us, Katheer Ibn Abdullah Al-Yashkari told us, Al-Hasan Ibn Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Awf told us on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There are three under the Throne on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:the Qur’an, which will argue with its servants, it has a back and a back, trustworthiness, and kinship, which will call out: ‘Whoever maintains ties with me, God will maintain ties with him, and whoever severs ties with me, God will sever ties with him.’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid Ibn Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah Ibn Salih told us, Al-Layth Ibn Saad told me, Aqil told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Anas Ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever loves for his provision to be expanded and his life to be extended, let him maintain the ties of kinship. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Uyaynah bin Abdul Rahman, who said: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is no sin more likely to have God hasten the punishment for its perpetrator in this world, along with what He has stored up for him in the Hereafter, than oppression and severing family ties. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Al-Hussein bin Bishran told us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ziyadi told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Muhammad bin Jubayr bin Mut’im, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: A person who severs ties of kinship will not enter Paradise. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi told us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Saydalani told us, Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Nasr told us, Abu Na’im al-Fadl ibn Dukayn told us, Amr ibn Uthman told us. I heard Musa ibn Talhah mention on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, may God be pleased with him, “A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during one of his journeys and said: Tell me what brings me closer to Paradise and distances me from Hellfire. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Worship God, do not associate anything with Him, establish prayer, pay zakat, and maintain family ties.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid Ibn Zanjawayh told us, Abu Ya’la and Abu Na’im told us: Qatar told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who maintains ties of kinship is not the one who reciprocates, but the one who maintains ties of kinship is the one who, when his ties of kinship are severed, maintains them. Narrated by Muhammad Ibn Ismail, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Kathir, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qatar, who said: If ties of kinship are severed, he maintains them. God Almighty says: And they fear their Lord and dread the evil of the reckoning.
13:22: 22- And those who are patient, in obeying God. Ibn Abbas said: in the command of God Almighty. Ata' said: in calamities and misfortunes. It was said: from desires. It was said: from sins. Seeking the countenance of their Lord, seeking to glorify Him by disobeying Him. And they establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, meaning they pay zakat. And they repel evil with good. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: They repel evil with good deeds, and this is the meaning of His statement: Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds (Hud 11:114). It was reported in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you do a bad deed, then do a good deed alongside it to erase it, secret for secret and public for public. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, Yazid ibn Abi Habib told us, Abu al-Khair told us that he heard Uqbah ibn Amir, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The example of one who does evil deeds and then does good deeds is like a man who was wearing a tight suit of armor that was choking him, then he did a good deed and a link came loose from it, then he did another and another link came loose, until he came out to the ground.” Ibn Kaysan said: The meaning of the verse is: They repel sin through repentance. It was said: They do not repay evil with evil, but rather repel evil with good. Al-Qatibi said: Its meaning is: If they are foolish, they will be patient. Foolishness is bad, and patience is good. Qatada said: Respond to them kindly, similar to the Almighty’s saying: “And when the ignorant address them, they say, ‘Peace.’” (al-Furqan 25:63). Al-Hasan said: If they are deprived, they give, if they are wronged, they forgive, and if they are cut off, they connect. Abdullah bin Mubarak said: These are eight characteristics indicating the eight gates of Paradise. For them is the final home, meaning Paradise, meaning: their final home is the home of reward. Then he explained that and said:
13:23: 23-Gardens of Eden, orchards of residence which they will enter, as will those who were righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants, and the angels will enter upon them from every gate. It was said: from the gates of Paradise. It was also said: from the gates of the palaces.
13:24: 24- "Peace be upon you", meaning: they say peace be upon you. Muqatil said: May God save you from the calamities you feared. Muqatil said: They will enter upon them in the amount of one day and one night of the three days of this world, with gifts and presents from God Almighty, saying, “Peace be upon you, for what you patiently endured. Excellent is the final home.” Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Baqiyah ibn al-Walid, Artah ibn al-Mundhir told me: I heard a man from the elders of the army called Abu al-Hajjaj say: I sat with Abu Umamah and he said: The believer will be reclining on his couch when he enters Paradise, and with him are two rows of servants, and at the edge of the rows is a door with a door. Then an angel from among the angels of God comes and asks permission. The furthest of the servants goes to the door, and there he is, the angel asking permission. He says to the one next to him: An angel is asking permission. The one next to him says to the one next to him: An angel is asking permission, likewise, until he reaches the believer. He says: Give him permission. The one closest to the believer says: Give him permission. The one next to him says to the one next to him: Give him permission, likewise, until he reaches the furthest of them who is at the door. It is opened for him, and he enters, greets, and then departs.
13:25: 25- And those who break the covenant of God after ratifying it, this is about the disbelievers. And sever that which God has ordered to be joined, meaning: they believe in some prophets and disbelieve in others. It was also said: they sever kinship ties, and spread corruption on the earth, meaning: they commit sins, for those is the curse and for them is the evil home, meaning: the Fire, and it was also said: the evil of the place of return because the place of return of people is their homes.
13:26: 26- The Almighty said: God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it, meaning: He expands it for whom He wills and restricts it for whom He wills. And they rejoiced in the life of this world, meaning: the polytheists of Mecca were arrogant and haughty. Joy is a pleasure in the heart in attaining what one desires, and it is evidence that joy in this world is forbidden. And the life of this world compared to the Hereafter is nothing but enjoyment meaning: a little and fleeting. Al-Kalbi said: Like a sugar bowl, a bowl, a cup, and a pot; you benefit from them and then they go away.
13:27: 27- "And those who disbelieve from the people of Mecca say, Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord? Say, Indeed, God misguides whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]." That is, He guides to Himself whomever He wills by turning back. It was said: He guides to His religion whoever turns back to Him with his heart.
13:28: 28- Those who believe, in the accusative case, instead of his saying: whoever turns back, “and their hearts are reassured,” are calmed, by the remembrance of God, Muqatil said: by the Qur’an, and calmness is by certainty, and disturbance is by doubt, Unquestionably, by the remembrance of God hearts are reassured, the hearts of the believers are calmed and certainty is established in them. Ibn Abbas said: This is about the oath. He says: If a Muslim swears by God about something, the hearts of the believers will be at peace with it. If it is said: Did not God Almighty say: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful (al-Anfal 8:2), so how can there be tranquility and fear in one state? It was said: Fear is when the threat and punishment are mentioned, and reassurance is when the promise and reward are mentioned. So the hearts are fearful when the justice of God and the severity of His reckoning are mentioned, and they are reassured when the grace, reward, and generosity of God are mentioned.
13:29: 29- Those who believe and do righteous deeds, beginning, Blessed are they is its predicate. They differed in the interpretation of Tooba. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: Joy and comfort to their eyes. Akrima said: Yes, they do not have money. Qatada said: It is good for them. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada: This is an Arabic word, in which a man says to another man: Blessed are you, meaning you have found good. Ibrahim said: It is better for them and more honorable. Al-Farra’ said: Its origin is from the word tayyib, and the waw in it is due to the damma of the ta. There are two dialects for it. The Arabs say: Tubaak and Tuba lak, meaning good for them. And a good end means: a good destination. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Tuba is the name of Paradise in Ethiopian. Al-Rabi' said: It is the garden in the Indian language. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, Abu Hurairah and Abu al-Darda’ that they said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise that shades all of Paradise. Ubayd ibn Umair said: It is a tree in the Garden of Eden. Its root is in the house of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. In every house and room there is a branch of it. God did not create a color or flower without having some of it in it except black. God did not create a fruit or berry without having some of it in it. From its root flow two springs: camphor and salsabil. Muqatil said: You will have a leaf from it that will protect a nation over which there will be a king who will glorify God Almighty with various types of glorification. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, “A man asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what is Tuba? He said: A tree in Paradise, a distance of one hundred years, from whose sleeves the clothes of the people of Paradise come out.” On the authority of Muawiyah bin Qurra, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet: “Tuba is a tree that God Almighty planted with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. It produces ornaments and finery, and its branches can be seen from behind the wall of Paradise.” Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Ziyad, the freed slave of Banu Makhzum, that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, say: There is a tree in Paradise in whose shade a rider can travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Read if you wish: And an extended shade (al-Waqi’ah 56:30). That reached Ka’b, so he said: He has spoken the truth, by the One Who sent down the Torah to Moses, peace be upon him, and the Qur’an to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If a man were to ride a tree or a stump, then go around the base of that tree, he would not reach it until he fell down old. God Almighty planted it with His hand and breathed into it from His spirit, and its branches are beyond the wall of Paradise. There is no river in Paradise except that it flows from the base of that tree. And with this chain of transmission on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Ash’ath bin Abdullah, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: In Paradise there is a tree called Tuba. God Almighty says to it: Open for My servant whatever he wishes, so it opens for him a horse with its saddle and bridle and its appearance as he wishes. It opens for him a mount with its saddle and reins and its appearance as he wishes, and clothes.
13:30: 30- The Almighty said, Thus have We sent you to a nation: Just as We sent the prophets to the nations, We sent you to this nation, that has passed away, passed away, before it were nations that you might recite, to read, upon them that which We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Qatada, Muqatil, and Ibn Jurayj said: The verse is Madani and was revealed in connection with the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. When Suhayl ibn Amr came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they agreed to write the treaty, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali, may God be pleased with him: Write, In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. They said: We do not know the Most Gracious except the companion of Yamamah - meaning Musaylimah the Liar - write as you used to write: In Your name, O God. This is the meaning of his statement: And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious. It is known that the verse is Meccan, and the reason for its revelation was that Abu Jahl heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the sanctuary calling out, O God, O Most Merciful. So he returned to the polytheists and said: “Muhammad calls upon two gods. He calls upon God, and he calls upon another god called the Most Merciful. We do not know the Most Merciful except the Most Merciful of Yamamah.” So this verse was revealed, and the words of God Almighty were revealed: “Say, ‘Call upon God or call upon the Most Merciful. Whichever [name] you call upon, He has the best names.’” (al-Isra’ 17:110) Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: It was revealed about the infidels of Quraysh when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Prostrate to the Most Gracious. They said: Who is the Most Gracious? God Almighty said: Say, to them, O Muhammad, that the Most Gracious, whose knowledge you denied, “is my Lord. There is no god but He. In Him I have relied,” I have relied, and to Him is my return, meaning: my repentance and my return.
13:31: 31- The Almighty said: And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, the verse. It was revealed about a group of polytheists of Mecca, including Abu Jahl bin Hisham and Abdullah bin Abi Umayya. They sat behind the Kaaba and sent for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He came to them and Abdullah bin Abi Umayya said to him: If you want us to follow you, then send the Qur’an to the mountains of Mecca and remove it from us until it becomes spacious, for it is a narrow land for our farms. And make for us springs and rivers in it, so that we may plant trees and farm and make orchards. For you are not, as you claim, more insignificant to your Lord than David, peace be upon him, when He subjected the mountains to him to glorify God with him, or subjected the wind to us so that we could ride it to Syria for our provisions and needs and return in the same day. For the wind was subjected to Solomon, as you claim, and you are not more insignificant to your Lord than Solomon. And revive for us your grandfather Qusayy or whomever you wish from our fathers and our dead so that we may ask him about your affair. Is what you say true or false? Jesus used to bring the dead back to life, and I am not more insignificant to God than he is. So God Almighty revealed: And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, so they were removed from the face of the earth, or the earth could be split open, meaning: it could be split open and rivers and springs made, or the dead could be spoken to, and they differed in the answer to if. Some people said: His answer is omitted, and it was sufficient for the listeners to know his meaning and estimate: This Qur’an would have been like the poet’s saying: I swear that if anything came to us from his messenger other than you, we would not have found a defense against you. He meant: We would have returned it, and this is the meaning of Qatada’s saying: If He had done this to a Qur’an before your Qur’an, He would have done it to your Qur’an. Others said: The answer to if is presented. The meaning of the statement is: And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious, And if there were a Qur’an by which the mountains were moved, as if he said: If the mountains were moved by it, or the earth were split asunder by it, or the dead were made to speak by it, they would have disbelieved in the Most Gracious and not believed, because of what we have previously known about them, as He said: And if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered together before them all things before, they would not have believed. (al-An’am 6:111) Then He said: Rather, the matter belongs to God entirely, meaning: in these things, if He wills, He does it, and if He wills, He does not do it. Have not those who have believed despaired? Most commentators said: Its meaning is: Have they not known? Al-Kalbi said: It is the language of the Nakha’. It was said: The language of Hawazin, as indicated by the reading of Ibn Abbas: Have not those who believe become clear? Al-Farra denied that it meant knowledge, and claimed that he had not heard any Arab say: yastan meaning: I knew, but the meaning of knowledge is implied in it. This is because when the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard this from the polytheists, they hoped that God would do what they asked for so that they would believe, so the verse was revealed: Have not those who have believed despaired? meaning: the companions, may God be pleased with them all, of the belief of these people, meaning they did not despair of knowledge, and everyone who knows something despairs of its opposite. He says: Has knowledge not made them despair: that if God had willed, He could have guided all mankind. “And those who disbelieve will continue to be afflicted by what they have done,” their disbelief and their evil deeds, with a calamity, meaning: a calamity and a disaster that befalls them with various types of affliction, sometimes with drought, sometimes with looting, and sometimes with killing and captivity. Ibn Abbas said: He meant by al-Qari’ah the raids that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to send to them. Or it descends, meaning: the secret and the devastating, near their home, and it was said: Or it descends: meaning you, O Muhammad, descend by yourself near their home, until the promise of God comes, it was said: the Day of Resurrection. And it was said: the conquest and victory and the appearance of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his religion. Indeed, God does not fail in His promise, and the infidels were asking for these things in mockery, so God revealed as consolation to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace:
13:32: 32- And messengers before you were mocked, just as they mocked you, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved, I gave them respite and extended their time, and from this comes the two colors, which are: night and day, then I seized them, I punished them in this world with killing and in the Hereafter with fire, so how was My punishment, meaning: My punishment of them.
13:33: 33- Is He then who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? That is, He who preserves it, provides for it, knows it, and rewards it for what it has done. The answer to this is omitted, and its meaning is: like one who is not in charge, but is incapable of taking care of himself. And they have attributed to God partners. Say, Name them. It was said: Describe them and then see if they are worthy of being worshipped? Or do you inform Him meaning: do you inform God Almighty: of what He does not know on earth, for He has not known of a partner for Himself nor a god on earth other than Him, or on an outward appearance meaning: or do you cling to an outward appearance, of speech, heard, which is in reality false and has no basis. It was said: with falsehood, the poet said: The slanderers blamed me for loving her, and that is a complaint whose shame is apparent in you. Meaning: fleeting. Rather, their plot has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, their treachery. Mujahid said: their polytheism and their lying about God. And they were prevented from the path, meaning: they were turned away from the religion. The people of Kufa and Yaqub read wasdawwa and in Ha Mim al-Mu’min wasd with a damma on the sad in both of them, and the others read it with a fatha based on the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God (al-Hajj 22:25), and His saying: Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God (Al-Nahl: 88 and others). And he whom God sends astray, by letting him down, will have no guide.
13:34: 34- For them is a punishment in the life of this world, by killing and captivity, but the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, more severe, and they will have no protector from God, no protector to prevent them from the punishment.
13:35: 35- The Almighty’s saying: The description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised meaning: the description of Paradise, like the Almighty’s saying: And to God belongs the highest description (al-Nahl 16:60) meaning: the highest description, Underneath which rivers flow, meaning: the description of Paradise which the righteous have been promised that rivers flow beneath it. It was said: Like a metaphorical connection, Paradise, which the righteous are promised, beneath which rivers flow. “Its food is eternal,” meaning: its fruit and pleasures are never-ending, and its shade, meaning: its shade is shady and never disappears. This is a response to the Jahmites who said that the pleasures of Paradise will perish. That is the consequence meaning: the outcome for those who fear God meaning: Paradise, and the consequence for the disbelievers is the Fire.
13:36: 36- The Almighty said: And those to whom We gave the Scripture meaning: the Qur’an, and they are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, rejoice in what has been revealed to you of the Qur’an, and of the parties meaning: the infidels who formed parties against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are the Jews and Christians, whoever denies some of it, this is the saying of Mujahid and Qatadah. Others said: The mention of the Most Gracious was little in the Qur’an at the beginning, but when Abdullah bin Salam and his companions converted to Islam, they were upset by the little mention of Him in the Qur’an despite the many mentions of Him in the Torah. When God repeated His mention in the Qur’an, they rejoiced at it, so God, the Most High, revealed: And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], but among the parties are those who deny some of it. That is, the polytheists of Mecca when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote in the treaty: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, they said: We do not know the Most Gracious except the Most Gracious of Yamamah, meaning Musaylimah the Liar. So God, the Most High, revealed: And they, at the mention of the Most Gracious, are disbelievers. (Al-Anbiya’: 36) And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious. (al-Ra’d 13:30). Some of them said it because they did not deny the mention of God and denied the mention of the Most Merciful. Say, O Muhammad, “I have only been commanded to worship God and not to associate anything with Him. To Him I call, and to Him is my return.” That is, my return.
13:37: 37- And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment, meaning: Just as We sent down the Book to you, O Muhammad, and the parties denied it, so We sent down the judgment and religion in Arabic. It was attributed to the Arabs because it came down suddenly to them and the parties denied it. It was said: The structure of the verse is: Just as the books were sent down to the messengers in their languages, so We have sent down to you the Book as Arabic wisdom. And if you were to follow their desires, in religion. And it was said: in the direction of prayer, after what has come to you of knowledge, you will have against God neither protector nor protector, meaning: no helper nor protector.
13:38: 38- The Almighty said: And We have certainly sent messengers before you. It was narrated that the Jews - and it was said: the polytheists - said: This man has no interest except in women, so God Almighty revealed: And We have certainly sent messengers before you and made for them wives and offspring. We did not make them angels who do not eat, drink, or marry. And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God, this is the answer of Abdullah bin Abi Umayya. Then he said: For every term is a book, meaning for every matter that God has decreed there is a book that He has written for it and a time in which it will occur. It was said: For every appointed time, God has a book in which He has recorded it. It was said that it is presented in advance and delay, meaning: that is, each book has a term and a duration, that is: the revealed books each have a time in which they are revealed.
13:39: 39- God erases what He wills and confirms. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Asim, and Yaqub read and confirms with a light pronunciation, while the others read it with a heavy pronunciation. They differed on the meaning of the verse: Saeed bin Jubair and Qatada said: God erases whatever He wills of the laws and obligations, abrogates it and changes it, and confirms whatever He wills of them and does not abrogate it. Ibn Abbas said: God erases whatever He wills and confirms except for sustenance, life span, happiness, and misery. We narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The angel enters upon the sperm after it has settled in the womb for forty or forty-five nights, and says: ‘O Lord, will I be miserable or happy?’ So they write it down. He says: ‘O Lord, will I be male or female?’ So they write it down, and his deeds, his impact, his life span, and his provision are written down. Then the scrolls are folded up and nothing is added to them or taken away from them.” On the authority of Omar and Ibn Masoud - may God be pleased with them - that they said: He erases happiness and misery as well, and erases sustenance and life span, and establishes whatever He wills. It was narrated on the authority of Omar, may God be pleased with him, that he used to circumambulate the House while crying and saying: O God, if You have written me among the people of happiness, then keep me among them. And if You have written for me misery, then erase my misery and keep me among the people of happiness and forgiveness. For You erase whatever You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud. In some of the narrations: A man may have thirty years left of his life, so he cuts off his kinship ties, and they are restored in three days. A man may have three days left of his life, so he maintains his kinship ties, and they are extended to thirty years. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid Ibn Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah Ibn Salih told us, Al-Layth Ibn Sa’d told me, Ziyadah Ibn Muhammad Al-Ansari told me, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala Ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty descends in the last three hours of the night, and in the first hour of them He looks in the Mother of the Book which no one looks at but Him, and He erases what He wills and confirms. It was said: The meaning of the verse is that the guardians write down all the deeds and sayings of the children of Adam, so God erases from the register of the guardians what does not contain reward or punishment, such as his saying: I ate, I drank, I entered, I left, and similar words in which he is truthful, and He confirms what contains reward and punishment. This is the saying of Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi. Al-Kalbi said: The entire statement is written down, until Thursday comes and everything that does not contain reward or punishment is removed from it. Attia said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is the man who works in obedience to God Almighty, then returns to disobeying God and dies in misguidance, so he is the one who is erased, and the one who is established: the man works in obedience to God, then dies in obedience to God Almighty, so he is the one who is established. Al-Hasan said: God erases whatever He wills, meaning that whoever’s time has come, He takes away and whoever’s time has not yet come, He keeps until his time comes. On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: God erases whatever He wills of the sins of the servants and forgives them, and confirms whatever He wills and does not forgive them. Ikrimah said: God erases whatever He wills of sins through repentance, and establishes good deeds in place of sins, as God Almighty said: Then God will replace their evil deeds with good ones (al-Furqan 25:70). Al-Suddi said: God erases whatever He wills meaning the moon, and establishes meaning the sun, as explained by God Almighty’s statement: So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible (al-Isra’ 17:12). Al-Rabi’ said: This is about the souls that God Almighty takes when we sleep. If He wants someone to die, He erases them and keeps them. If He wants someone to remain, He confirms them and returns them to their owner. This is explained by the Almighty’s statement: God takes the souls at the time of their death (al-Zumar 39:42), And with Him is the Mother of the Book, meaning: the origin of the Book, which is the Preserved Tablet that cannot be changed or altered. Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: They are two books: a book other than the Mother of the Book, from which He erases whatever He wills and confirms, and the Mother of the Book, from which nothing is changed. On the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God Almighty has a Preserved Tablet, the length of a journey of five hundred years, made of white pearl with two covers of ruby. God has three hundred and sixty moments in it every day. God erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. Ibn Abbas asked Kaab about the Mother of the Book. He said: The knowledge of God, what He created, and what He created, they do.
13:40: 40- And if We show you some of what We promise them, of the torment before your death, or We cause you to die, before that, then upon you is only the notification, there is nothing upon you except that, and upon Us is the reckoning, the recompense on the Day of Resurrection.
13:41: 41- The Almighty’s saying: Have they not seen meaning: the people of Mecca, who asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the verses, that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders, most of the commentators agree that what is meant by it is the conquest of the lands of polytheism, for whatever is added to the lands of Islam has been reduced from the lands of polytheism. He says: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders, so We conquer it for Muhammad, land after land, around their land, so will they not interpret? This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and a group. Some people said: It is the destruction of the earth, meaning: Did they not see that we come to the earth and destroy it and destroy its people, so do they not fear that we will do that to them? Mujahed said: It is the destruction of the earth and the capture of its people. On the authority of Ikrimah, he said: The people died. And on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, the same. Ata and a group said: Its decrease is the death of scholars and the departure of jurists. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ismail bin Abi Uwais told us, Malik told me, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God does not take away knowledge by snatching it from the servants, but He takes away knowledge by taking away the scholars, until when no scholar remains, the people will take ignorant leaders, and when they are asked, they will issue fatwas without knowledge, so they go astray and lead others astray.” Al-Hasan said: Abdullah bin Masoud said: The death of a scholar is a gap in Islam that nothing can fill as long as night and day alternate. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: You must acquire knowledge before its people are taken away. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: The example of jurists is like that of hands. If one hand is cut off, it cannot be restored. Sulayman said: People will continue to be good as long as the first one remains until the last one learns. If the first one perishes before the last one learns, people will perish. It was said to Saeed bin Jubair: What is the sign of the destruction of people? He said: The destruction of their scholars. And God judges, and there is no objector to His judgment. There is no one who can reverse His judgment, nor can His ruling be overturned. And He is swift in reckoning.
13:42: 42- And those before them plotted, meaning: before the polytheists of Mecca, and plotting: bringing harm to a person without him realizing it. To God belongs all the plotting, meaning: with God is the reward for their plotting. It was said: God is the Creator of all their plotting, in His hand is good and evil, and to Him belongs benefit and harm, so no one’s plotting harms anyone except with His permission. He knows what every soul earns, and He will know the disbelievers. The people of Hijaz and Abu Amr read the disbeliever in the singular, while the others read the disbelievers in the plural. For whom is the final home? meaning: the final home of the Hereafter when they enter Hell, and the believers enter Paradise.
13:43: 43- And those who disbelieve say, ‘You are not a messenger.’ Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.’ He means: The believers among the People of the Book also bear witness to that. Qatada said: He is Abdullah bin Salam. Al-Sha’bi denied this and said: The surah is Meccan, and Abdullah bin Salam converted to Islam in Medina. Abu Bishr said: I said to Saeed bin Jubair, And who has knowledge of the Book? Is he Abdullah bin Salam? He said: How can he be Abdullah bin Salam when this surah is Meccan? Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: And with Him is the knowledge of the Book is God Almighty, as indicated by the reading of Abdullah bin Abbas, And with Him with a sukoon on the meem and the dal, meaning: from God Almighty, and Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Jubair read And with Him with a kasra on the meem and the dal the knowledge of the Book as a passive verb, as indicated by the saying of God Almighty: And We taught him knowledge from Us (al-Kahf 18:65) and His saying: The Most Gracious * taught the Qur’an (Al-Rahman: 1,2).
14:1: Meccan and it has fifty-one verses except for two verses from the words of God Almighty: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? to His words: Then your destination is the Fire. “Alif, Lam, Ra. This is a Book,” meaning: this is a Book which We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, meaning: the Qur’an, that you may bring mankind out of darkness into the light, meaning: to call them from the darkness of misguidance to the light of faith, by the permission of their Lord, by the command of their Lord. It was said: With the knowledge of their Lord. To the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy meaning: to His religion. The Almighty is the victorious one, and the Praiseworthy is the one deserving of praise.
14:2: God who Abu Jaafar and Ibn Amir read: God in the nominative case as a new sentence, and its predicate is what follows it. Others read it with the accusative case as a description of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. And when Jacob arrived, he lowered his head. Abu Amr said: The genitive case is for advancement and delay, and its meaning is: to the path of God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, “To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment.”
14:3: Those who prefer, choose, the life of this world over the Hereafter and avert [people] from the path of God, that is, they prevent people from accepting the religion of God, and seek to make it crooked, that is, they seek to make it crooked and deviant, meaning: they seek the path of God, deviating from the straight path. It was said: The letter ha refers to the world, meaning: they seek the world by deviating from the truth, i.e. towards what is forbidden. Those are far astray.
14:4: God Almighty says: And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people to state clearly to them, in their language so that they would understand him. If it is said: How can this be, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to all of creation? It was said: He was sent from the Arabs in their language, and the people followed them. Then he sent messengers to the regions, calling them to God Almighty and translating for them in their languages. “God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
14:5: And We sent Moses with Our signs, saying, ‘Bring your people out of darkness into the light’ meaning: from disbelief to faith in the call, and remind them of the days of God. Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: of God’s blessings. Muqatil said: By the events of God with the previous nations. It is said: So-and-so is knowledgeable about the days of the Arabs, meaning: their events. But he meant what was in the days of God of blessings and tribulations, so he sufficed by mentioning the days instead of them because they were known to them. Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful person. “Patient” means very patient, and grateful means very grateful. He meant: for every believer, because patience and gratitude are among the characteristics of believers.
14:6: And when Moses said to his people, 'Remember the favor of God upon you when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh who were subjecting you to terrible torment and slaughtering your sons,' Al-Farra' said: The reason for this waw is that God the Most High informed them that the people of Pharaoh were tormenting them with types of torment other than slaughtering, and with slaughtering, and when he put the waw in slaughtering and killing he wanted to explain the torment that they were subjecting them to, and keeping your women alive, leaving them alive and in that is a great trial from your Lord.
14:7: And when your Lord declared, meaning: He informed. It is said: he declared and he declared have the same meaning, like he threatened and he threatened, If you are grateful, meaning if you believe and obey, I will surely increase you in blessings. It was said: Gratitude is the bond of what is present and the catch of what is lost. It was said: If you thank me by obeying, I will increase your reward. And if you disbelieve, My blessings and deny them and do not thank me for them, then indeed, My punishment is severe.
14:8: And Moses said, 'If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy.' That is, He is Free of need of His creation, Praiseworthy and praised in His actions, because He is generous and just in them.
14:9: "Has there not come to you the report of those, the report of those, before you - the people of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud - and those after them - none knows them except God", meaning: those who came after the people of Noah, 'Aad/and Thamud. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, that he read this verse and then said: The genealogists lied. On the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: There were thirty centuries between Abraham and Adnan, and none knows them except God Almighty. Malik bin Anas hated for a person to attribute himself as a father to Adam, and the same applies to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because no one knows those fathers except God Almighty. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, with clear evidence, but they put their hands over their mouths, Ibn Masoud said: They bit their hands in rage, just as He said, They bit their fingertips in rage (Al Imran 3:119). Ibn Abbas said: When they heard the Book of God, they were amazed and put their hands to their mouths. Mujahid and Qatada said: They denied the messengers and rejected what they brought. It is said: I rejected so-and-so’s words in his mouth, meaning I denied him. Al-Kalbi said: It means that the nations put their hands over their mouths, meaning: they put their hands over their mouths as a sign to the messengers to be silent. Muqatil said: They put their hands over the mouths of the messengers to silence them. It was said: Hands mean blessings. Its meaning is: They returned what, if they had accepted, would have been hands and blessings in their mouths, meaning: with their mouths, meaning with their tongues. And they said, meaning the nations to the messengers, Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed, we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us, causing doubt and causing accusation.
14:10: Their messengers said, 'Is there any doubt about God?' This is a question that means denying what they believed, Creator of the heavens and the earth, their Creator, He calls you to forgive you some of your sins, meaning: your sins, and some is a relative clause, and to delay you for a specified term, until the time your terms are fulfilled, so He does not hasten you with punishment. They said to the messengers: You are only human beings like us, in appearance, and you are not angels. Rather, you want, with your words, “to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship. So bring us a clear authority,” a clear proof of the truth of your claim.
14:11: Their messengers said to them, 'We are only human beings like you, but God bestows favor upon whom He wills of His servants,' with prophecy and wisdom, "and it was not for us to bring you any authority except by God's permission. And upon God let the believers put their trust."
14:12: And why should we not put our trust in God when we know that we cannot attain anything except through His decree and destiny, and He has guided us to our ways, showed us the right path, and showed us the path of salvation. And we will surely be patient, the lam is the lam of the oath, metaphorically: By God, we will surely be patient, for what you have harmed us with, and upon God let the trustful put their trust.
14:13: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, ‘We will surely expel you from our land, or you must return to our religion.’ They mean: unless you return, or until you return to our religion.
14:14: Then their Lord inspired them, 'We will surely destroy the wrongdoers, and We will surely inhabit you in the land after them.' That is, after their destruction. That is for him who fears standing before Me meaning: standing before Me, as He said: And for him who fears standing before his Lord are two gardens (al-Rahman 55:46). So He attributed the servant’s standing to himself, just as you say: I regret hitting you, meaning my hitting you, and feared My threat meaning My punishment.
14:15: The Almighty said: And they sought victory meaning: they sought help. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: He means the nations, and that is because they said: O God, if these messengers are truthful, then punish us. Similar to the Almighty’s saying: “And when they said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky” (al-Anfal 8:42). Mujahid and Qatadah said: And they sought help meaning the messengers. This is because when they despaired of the faith of their people, they sought help from God and called for punishment for their people, as Noah, peace be upon him, said: My Lord, leave not upon the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers (Nuh 71:26). And Moses, peace be upon him, said: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, (Yunus 10:88). And he failed, he lost: and it was said: he perished, every tyrant is stubborn. The tyrant is the one who does not see anyone above him. And determinism is seeking superiority with no goal beyond it, and this description is only for God Almighty. It was said: Al-Jabbar is the one who compels creation to do what he wants, and Al-Aneed is the one who opposes the truth and deviates from it. This was said by Mujahid, and on the authority of Ibn Abbas - may God be pleased with them both -: He is the one who turns away from the truth. Muqatil said: He is the arrogant one. Qatada said: The stubborn one is the one who refuses to say there is no god but God.
14:16: Behind him is Hell meaning: in front of him, as God Almighty says: And behind them was an angel (al-Kahf 18:76), meaning: in front of them. Abu Ubaidah said: It is one of the opposites. Al-Akhfash said: It is like saying, This matter is behind you, meaning that it will come to you, and I am behind so-and-so, meaning I will reach him. Muqatil said: Behind him is Hell, meaning: after him. And he will be given to drink from a water of pus, meaning: from a water that is pus, which is what flows from the bodies of the infidels of pus and blood. Muhammad bin Kaab said: What flows from the vaginas of adulterers, the infidel will drink it.
14:17: "He sips it": that is, he drinks it, not all at once, but sips by sips, due to its bitterness and heat, "and he can hardly swallow it, and can hardly swallow" is a relative clause, meaning he can hardly swallow it, like the Almighty's saying: "He could hardly see it" (al-Nur 24:40), meaning he could not see it. Ibn Abbas - may God be pleased with him - said: He does not permit it. It was said: Its meaning is that he can hardly swallow it, and if he swallows it, it boils in his stomach. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Safwan ibn Amr, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Busr, on the authority of Abu Umamah - may God be pleased with him - “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: “And he will be given to drink of a purulent water, gulping it down,” he said: It is brought close to his mouth and he dislikes it, but when he brings it close to him, it burns his face and the scalp falls off, and when he drinks it, it tears up his intestines until it comes out of his anus. God Almighty says: And they will be given to drink scalding water, so it will tear up their intestines (Muhammad 47:15) and He says: And if they call for help, they will be helped with water like molten brass, which will burn their faces (al-Kahf 18:29). And the Almighty’s saying, And death will come to him from every side, means: He will feel the anxiety and pain of death from every part of his body. Ibrahim Al-Taimi said: Even from under every hair on his body. It was said: Death comes to him from in front of him, from behind him, from above him, from below him, from his right and from his left. And he is not dead, so he rests. Ibn Jurayj said: His soul is attached to his throat, so it does not exit his mouth and he dies, nor does it return to its place in his body and life comes to him. Similar to it is: Then he neither dies therein nor lives (al-A’la 87:13). And behind him, in front of him, is a severe punishment, severe. It was said: The severe punishment is eternity in the Fire.
14:18: The likeness of those who disbelieved in their Lord is their deeds meaning: the deeds of those who disbelieved in their Lord - like the Almighty's saying: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces will be blackened (al-Zumar 39:60) - meaning: you will see the faces of those who lied about God blackened, like ashes which the wind blows violently on a stormy day, describing the day as stormy, and stormy is a description of the wind because the wind is in it, just as it is said: a hot day and a cold day, because the heat and cold are in it. It was said: Its meaning is: On a windy day, so the wind was omitted because it was mentioned before. This is a parable that God gave for the deeds of the infidels, meaning: They do not benefit from the deeds that they did in this world because they associated others with God in it, like the ashes that the wind scatters, which are of no benefit. This is what God Almighty said: They will not be able, meaning: the infidels, to do anything in the Hereafter, from what they have earned, in this world. That is the farthest error.
14:19: "Have you not seen that God created the heavens and the earth? Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read He created the heavens and the earth in Surat An-Nur He created every living creature" with an addition. Others read “created” in the past tense and earth in the accusative case. In truth means: He did not create them in vain, but rather He created them for a great reason. If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation, someone other than you is more obedient to God than you.
14:20: "And that is not difficult for God", very strong, meaning that things are easy in His power, nothing is difficult for God Almighty, no matter how great and mighty it is.
14:21: The Almighty said: And they will all appear before God, meaning: they will come out from their graves to God and will all appear. Then the weak ones will say, meaning: the followers, to those who were arrogant, meaning: they were arrogant towards the people, and they are the leaders and chiefs: Indeed, we were your followers, the plural of follower, like guard and guards, So will you be able to protect us from any of the punishment of God? They said, meaning the leaders who were followed: If God had guided us, we would have guided you, meaning: If God had guided us, we would have called you to guidance, but when He led us astray, we called you to misguidance. “It is the same to us whether we are impatient or patient. There is no escape for us,” no escape or escape. Muqatil said: They will say in the Fire: Come, let us be impatient, and they will be impatient for five hundred years, but their impatientness will not benefit them. Then they will say: Come, let us be patient, and they will be patient for five hundred years, but it will not benefit them. Then they will say: “It is the same to us whether we are impatient or patient. We have no escape.” Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi said: I was informed that the people of Hell called for help from the guards. God the Almighty said: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, ‘Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment’ (Ghafir 40:49). The keepers replied: Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs? They said, Yes. The keepers replied: Call upon Him, but the call of the disbelievers is only in error. (Ghafir 40:50). When they despaired of what the keepers had, they cried out, O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us. (al-Zukhruf 43:77). They asked for death, but it did not answer them for eighty years. A year is three hundred and sixty days, and a day is like a thousand years of what you count. Then He said to them after the eighty, You will remain. When they despaired of what came before it, some of them said to each other, Indeed, what you see has befallen you of the affliction, so come, let us be patient, perhaps patience will benefit us as the people of this world were patient in obeying God, and it benefited them. So they agreed to be patient, and their patience lasted a long time, then they became impatient and cried out, “It is the same to us whether we are impatient or patient. We have no help.” Muhais means: from a place of refuge. He said: Then Satan stood up and addressed them, saying: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, the verse. When they heard his words, they hated themselves, so they were called: The hatred of God is greater than your hatred of yourselves when you were called to faith but you disbelieved. (Ghafir 40:10). He said: So they called a second time: “Then send us back; we will do righteousness. Indeed, we are certain.” He replied to them: And if We willed, We could have given every soul its guidance. (al-Sajdah 32:12, 13). They called a third time: Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers. (Ibrahim 14:44). He replied to them: Did you not swear before that you would not perish? (Ibrahim 14:44). Then they called a fourth time: Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness other than what we used to do? He replied to them: Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember, and a warner came to you? (Fatir 35:37). He said: So he remained with them as long as God willed, then He called them: Were not My verses recited to you, and you used to deny them? When they heard that, they said, Now He will have mercy on us. Then they said, “Our Lord, our misery overcame us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it. If we return, then we will be wrongdoers.” Then He said, Be gone into it, disgraced, and do not speak to me. Al-Mu’minun 105-108 Then hope and supplication were cut off from them, and they turned to one another, barking in one another’s faces, and the Fire closed in on them.
14:22: God Almighty said: And Satan said, meaning: Iblis, when the matter was decided, meaning: he finished it and brought the people of Paradise and the people of Hell into Hell. Muqatil said: A pulpit will be placed for him in Hell, and he will ascend it and the infidels will gather around him to blame him, but he will say to them: God promised you the promise of truth, and He fulfilled it for you. And I promised you and broke my promise, and it was said: He will say to them: I told you there would be no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Hell. And I had no authority over you, authority. And it was said: I did not come to you with an argument for what I called you to, except that I called you, this is an isolated exception, the meaning of which is: But I called you and you responded to me, so do not blame me, but blame yourselves, for responding to me and following me without authority or proof. I am not your helper, your savior, and you are not my savior, my helper. Al-A'mash and Hamza read bi-masrakhy with a kasra on the ya', and the others read it with a nasb for the sake of doubling. Whoever read it with a kasra, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, it was moved to a kasra, because the ya' is the sister of the kasra. The grammarians did not accept it, and it was said that it is the language of Banu Yarbu'. The original is bi-masrakhyni, but the nun was dropped for the sake of the addition, and the ya' of the group was assimilated into the ya' of the addition. I have disbelieved in what you associated with Him before, meaning: I have disbelieved in your making me a partner in His worship, and I disavow that. The wrongdoers, the unbelievers, will have a painful punishment. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Rashdin ibn Sa’d, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad told me, on the authority of Dukhayn al-Hijri, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir - may God be pleased with him - on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith of intercession. He mentioned the hadith and then said: “Jesus, peace be upon him, says: That is the unlettered prophet. They will come to me and God will permit me to stand, and from my seat will rise the most fragrant scent anyone has ever smelled, until I come to my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, and He will intercede for me and make for me a light from the hair of my head to the nails of my feet. Then the disbelievers will say: The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so who will intercede for us? They will say: It is none other than Iblis, he is the one who led us astray. So they will come to him and say to him: The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so stand up and intercede for us, for you are the one who led us astray. So he will stand, and from his seat will rise the most foul odor.” Someone smelled it, then Hell became great, and he said at that time: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, the verse.
14:23: God Almighty says: “And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally by permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’” They greet one another, and the angels greet them. It was said: The One who revives with peace is God Almighty.
14:24: And the Almighty said: Have you not seen how God presents a parable? Have you not learned? The parable is a common saying to liken one thing to another. A good word is the saying: There is no god but God, like a good tree is the palm tree, meaning like a tree with good fruit. Dhibyan said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is a tree in Paradise. Its root is firm, in the earth, and its branch, its highest point, is in the sky. Likewise, the root of this word is firmly rooted in the heart of the believer through knowledge and belief. So when he speaks it, it ascends, not being hidden until it reaches God Almighty. God Almighty said: To Him ascends good words, and righteous deeds raise it up. (Fatir 35:10)
14:25: "It bears fruit, it gives its fruit, at all times by the permission of its Lord/ and time" in the language means the time. They differed about its meaning here. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: Now here means a full year, because the palm tree bears fruit every year. Saeed bin Jubair, Qatada and Al-Hasan said: Six months from the time it is seen until it is harvested. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. It was said: Four months from the time of its appearance until its maturity. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Two months from the time it is eaten until the time of harvest. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: Every time means every morning and evening, because the fruit of the palm tree is always eaten day and night, summer and winter, whether it is dates, fresh dates, or unripe dates. Likewise, the deeds of the believer ascend at the beginning and end of the day, and the blessing of his faith never ceases, rather it reaches him at all times. The wisdom in representing faith with a tree is that a tree is not a tree except with three things: a firm root, an upright base, and a high branch. Likewise, faith is not complete except with three things: belief in the heart, words on the tongue, and actions with the body. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Abdullah bin Dinar told us that he heard Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the trees is a tree whose leaves do not fall, and it is like a Muslim. So tell me what it is.” Abdullah said: “The people mentioned the trees of the desert, and it occurred to me that it was the palm tree, but I was embarrassed. Then they said: Tell us what it is, O Messenger of God? He said: It is the palm tree.” Abdullah said: “So I mentioned that to Omar, and he said: If you had said it was the palm tree, it would have been more beloved to me than such and such.” It was said that the wisdom behind its being likened to a palm tree among all other trees is that the palm tree is likened to a human being in that if its top is cut off, it dries up, while all other trees branch out from their sides after their tops are cut off. And because it is like a human being in that it does not bear fruit except through pollination, and because it was created from the excess clay of Adam, peace be upon him, and for this reason the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Honor your paternal aunt. It was said: And who is our paternal aunt? He said: The palm tree. “And God presents examples for the people that perhaps they will remember.”
14:26: And the example of a bad word, which is polytheism, is like a bad tree, which is colocynth. It was said: Garlic neighborhood. It was said: It is the Kashout, which is the Ashqa. Uprooted means it was uprooted, from above the earth, it has no stability, stability. Meaning: It has no fixed root in the earth, nor a branch ascending to the sky. Likewise, there is no good in the unbeliever, and no good word or righteous deed ascends to him.
14:27: God Almighty says: God confirms those who believe with the firm word, the word of monotheism, which is the saying: There is no god but God, in the life of this world, meaning before death, and in the Hereafter, meaning in the grave. This is the saying of most of the commentators. It was said: In this worldly life: when questioned in the grave, and in the Hereafter: when resurrected. The first is more correct. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Walid told us, Shu’bah told us, Alqamah bin Marthad told me: I heard Sa’d bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a Muslim is asked in the grave, he testifies that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. This is what God Almighty said: ‘God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter.’” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir informed us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad informed us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi informed us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan informed us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj informed us, Muhammad bin Bashar informed us, Muhammad bin Jaafar informed us, Shu’bah informed us with this chain of transmission on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God will confirm those who believe with the firm word. He said: It was revealed regarding the torment of the grave. It will be said to him: Who is your Lord? He will say: My Lord is God, and my Prophet is Muhammad. This is what God Almighty said: God will confirm those who believe with the firm word. And Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Ayyash bin Al-Waleed informed us, Abdul A’la informed us, Saeed informed us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, that he told them that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a servant is placed in his grave, and his companions turn away from him, he hears the sound of their sandals. Two angels come to him and make him sit, and they say: What did you say about this man, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? As for the believer, he says: I bear witness that he is the servant of God and His Messenger. It is said to him: Look at your seat in Hell, God has replaced it for you with a seat in Paradise, and he sees them both.” Qatada said: And it was mentioned to us that his grave will be made spacious for him, then he returned to the hadith of Anas, who said: As for the hypocrite and the disbeliever, it will be said to him: What did you say about this man? He will say: I do not know, I used to say what the people say. It will be said to him: You neither knew nor followed, and he will be struck with iron hammers, and he will cry out a cry that will be heard by those near him except for the two heavy burdens. Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar bin Ismail al-Tamimi told us, Abu al-Qasim Hamza bin Yusuf al-Sahmi told us, Abu Ahmad Abdullah bin Adi al-Hafiz told us, Abdullah bin Saeed told us, Asad bin Musa told us, Anbasa bin Saeed bin Katheer told us, my grandfather told me on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The dead person hears the sound of sandals when people turn their backs on him, then he sits up and his shroud is placed around his neck, then he is asked. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a dead person is buried, two black and blue angels come to him, one of them is called Al-Munkar and the other Al-Nakeer. They say: What did you say about this man? He says: He is the servant of God and His Messenger. I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the servant of God and His Messenger. They say to him: We knew that you would say this. Then his grave is made spacious for him, seventy cubits by seventy cubits, then it is illuminated for him. Then it is said: Sleep like the sleep of a bridegroom who is not awakened except by the most beloved of his family, until God Almighty resurrects him. Even if he was a hypocrite or a disbeliever, he says: I heard the people saying something and I said the same, I do not know. They say: We knew that you would say that. Then the earth is told to close around him, and it closes around him, and his ribs interlock, and he remains tormented in it until God resurrects him from that resting place.” It was narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the taking of the soul of the believer and said: “His soul is returned to his body and two angels come to him and make him sit in his grave and say to him: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet? He says: My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my prophet is Muhammad. They rebuke him and say to him a second time: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet? This is the last trial that will be presented to the believer, and God Almighty will make him steadfast. He says: My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my prophet is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then a voice from the heaven calls out: My servant has spoken the truth. He said: This is what God Almighty said: ‘God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.’” Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu al-Abbas Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Taysifuni told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Turabi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Bastam told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Sayyar al-Qurashi told us, Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Qurra Abu Ishaq told us, Hisham ibn Yusuf told us, Abdullah ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of Hani’, the freed slave of Uthman, who said: “Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished burying a man, he would stand over him and say: Ask forgiveness for your brother and ask God to make him steadfast, for he is being questioned now.” Omar bin Al-Aas said in the context of death while crying: So when I die, do not let any mourners or fire accompany me. When you bury me, sprinkle the dirt over me, then stand around my grave for the amount of time it takes to slaughter a camel and divide its meat, so that I may get used to you and see what I will say to the messengers of my Lord. God Almighty says: And God misguides the wrongdoers, meaning: He does not guide the polytheists to the correct answer in the grave. And God does what He wills, of success, failure, confirmation, and failure to confirm.
14:28: God Almighty says: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? The verse. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the Almighty’s statement, Those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief, he said: By God, they are the disbelievers of Quraysh. Amr said: They are Quraysh, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is God’s blessing. And they caused their people to dwell in the abode of ruin, he said: The ruin was on the day of Badr. His statement, They changed the favor of God means: They changed the favor of God upon them in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when God Almighty sent him from among them = disbelief, they disbelieved in him, so they caused, that is: they caused their people, who followed them in their disbelief, to dwell in the abode of ruin and destruction. Then he explained the ruin and said:
