14:29: "Hell, they will enter it, and wretched is the resting place, the permanent abode. On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: Those who exchanged God’s blessing for disbelief: they are the infidels of Quraysh who were slaughtered on the day of Badr. Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: They are the two most wicked of the Quraysh 106:Banu Al-Mughira and Banu Umayya. As for Banu Al-Mughira, you spared them on the day of Badr, and as for Banu Umayya, enjoy them for a while.
14:30: "And they have made rivals to God, examples, and God Almighty has no rival, to lead astray," Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read with the opening of the ya', and likewise in Al-Hajj, Surat Luqman, and Surat al-Zumar 39:"to lead astray, and the others read with the closing of the ya' meaning to lead astray people, from His path. Say, enjoy, live in this world, for your destiny is the Fire."
14:31: Say to My servants who have believed to establish prayer, Al-Farra' said: It is a jussive mood for recompense, and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, before there comes a Day in which there will be no trade or friendship, friendship and closeness. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amr, and Ya'qub read: There will be no trade or friendship in it in the accusative case in both of them as a general negation. The rest read: There will be no trade or friendship in it in the nominative case and with tanween.
14:32: “God is He who created the heavens and the earth and sent down water from the sky and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you and made the ships subject to you to sail through the sea by His command,” and made the rivers subject to you, He made them subservient to you, so that you may sail them wherever you wish.
14:33: And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, constantly pursuing their courses, they run in what benefits the servants and do not stop. Ibn Abbas said that they are constantly pursuing their courses in obedience to God Almighty. And He has subjected to you the night and the day, alternating between light and darkness, and increase and decrease.
14:34: And He gave you of everything you asked of Him, meaning: And He gave you of everything you asked of Him, so the second thing was omitted, as the speech was sufficient to indicate the partiality. It was said: It is for multiplication, like your saying: So-and-so knows everything, and all people were given to him, and you mean some of them, similar to the Almighty’s saying: We opened to them the gates of every [good] thing (al-An’am 6:44). Al-Hasan read from every with the tanween what in the negative, meaning from everything that you did not ask for, meaning: He gave you things that you did not ask for or request. And if you should count the favors of God, meaning: the favors of God, you could not enumerate them, meaning: you would not be able to count them or give thanks for them. Indeed, man is unjust and ungrateful, meaning: he is unjust to himself by committing sins, and ungrateful to his Lord, the Almighty, for His blessings. It was said: The oppressor is the one who thanks someone other than the one who bestowed a blessing upon him, and the ungrateful is the one who denies the one who bestowed a blessing upon him.
14:35: God Almighty said: And when Abraham said, ‘My Lord, make this city secure,’ meaning the sanctuary, ‘and keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols,’ meaning the sanctuary, and keep me away from it,’ it is said: I kept something away from him, “I kept it away,” I kept it away, and I kept it away have the same meaning. If it is said: Abraham, peace be upon him, was infallible from worshipping idols, so how can the question be valid? And many of his sons worshipped idols, so where is the answer? It was said: The supplication for Abraham, peace be upon him, was to increase infallibility and steadfastness. As for his supplication for his sons: he meant his sons from his loins, and none of them worshipped an idol. It was said: His supplication was for those of his children who were believers.
14:36: My Lord, indeed they have led many people astray, meaning: Many people have been led astray by them from the path of guidance until they worshipped them. This is an inverted version of what God Almighty said: That is only Satan who frightens his allies (Al Imran 3:175), meaning: he frightens them with his allies. It was said: Misguidance was attributed to idols because they are the cause of it, just as someone says: The world tempted me. The temptation was attributed to the world because it is the cause of the temptation. Whoever follows me, then he is of me, meaning: of my religion, and whoever disobeys me, then You are Forgiving and Merciful, Al-Suddi said: Its meaning is: and whoever disobeys me and then repents. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: And whoever disobeys me in anything less than polytheism. It was said: He said that before God taught him that He does not forgive polytheism.
14:37: The Almighty said: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants, “some” was inserted for partiality, and the metaphor of the verse is: I have settled some of my descendants, in an uncultivated valley, which is Mecca, because Mecca is a valley between two mountains, near Your sacred House, He called it sacred because what is forbidden near it is not forbidden near anything else. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub Al-Sakhtiyani and Kathir bin Abi Kathir bin Al-Muttalib bin Abi Wada’a - adding one of them to the other - on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The first time women used lanyards was before the mother of Ismail. She used lanyards to cover her traces on Sarah. Then Ibrahim, peace be upon him, brought her and her son Ismail while she was breastfeeding him, until he placed them near the House, near a tree above Zamzam at the top of the mosque. There was no one in Mecca at that time and there was no water in it. He placed them there, and placed near her a bag of dates and a water skin with water. Then Ibrahim returned and went away. Ismail’s mother followed him and said: O Ibrahim, where are you going and leaving us in this valley where there are no people or anything? She said that to him repeatedly, but he did not pay attention to her. She said to him: Did God command you to do this? He said: Yes. She said: Then He will not let us down. Then she returned, and Abraham set out until he was at the pass where they could not see him. He faced the House, then he called out with these supplications and raised his hands and said: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without cultivation, until he reached They thank. And the mother of Ismail kept suckling Ismail and drinking from that water until what was in the water skin was used up, she became thirsty and her son became thirsty, and she kept looking at him squirming or she said writhing, and she set off, hating to look at him, and she found Safa to be the nearest mountain on earth to her, so she stood on it and then faced the valley to see if she could see anyone, but she did not see anyone, so she descended from Safa until she reached the valley, she raised the edge of her armor, then she ran as a person struggles until she passed the valley, then she came to Marwa and stood on it and looked to see if she could see anyone, but she did not see anyone, so she did that seven times. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is why people strive between them. When she reached Al-Marwah, she heard a voice and said: Shhh - meaning herself - then she listened and heard again and said: I have heard if you have help. Then she saw the king at the place of Zamzam, so he searched with his heel - or he said with his wing - until the water appeared, so she began to wade through it and say with her hand like this, and she began to scoop up water from her water skin and it was bubbling after she scooped up. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on the mother of Ismail if she had left Zamzam alone. Or he said: If she had not scooped up the water, Zamzam would have been a flowing spring. He said: So she drank and breastfed her son, and the king said to her: Do not fear loss, for here is the House of God, which this boy and his father will build, and God does not forsake His people. The site of the House was elevated above the ground like a hill, and the floods would come to it from its right and its left, and it remained like that until a group of people from Jurhum - or a family from Jurhum - passed by them coming from the road of Kada’, and they camped at the bottom of Mecca. They saw a flying bird, and they said: This bird circles around water, and we know this valley and what water it has. So they sent a runner or two, and they found water, so they returned and told them about the water. They came and found the mother of Ismail at the water, and they said: Do you give us permission to camp with you? She said: Yes, but you have no right to the water. They said: Yes. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Ishmael’s mother said that, and she loved company. So they came down and sent for their family, who came down with them until there were some households there, and the boy grew up and learned Arabic from them, and they liked him and were pleased with him when he grew up. So when he reached puberty, they married him to a woman from among them. And Ishmael’s mother died, and Abraham came after Ishmael had married to look at his estate… We mentioned that story in Surat Al-Baqarah.” God Almighty says: “Our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people yearn for them,” hearts: the plural of fu’ad, long for them, yearn and long for them. Al-Suddi said: Its meaning is that their hearts are inclined towards this place. Your Mujahid said: If he had said the hearts of the people, we would have had mercy on you, the Persians, the Romans, the Turks, and the Indians. Saeed bin Jubair said: The Jews, Christians, and Magians argued, but he said: the hearts of the people, which are the Muslims. And provide them with fruits, what You provided the inhabitants of the villages with water, that they may be grateful.
14:38: Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we declare, of our affairs. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: From the longing for Ishmael and his mother when He settled them in a barren valley. And nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven, it was said: This is a connection to the words of Abraham. Most of them said: God Almighty says: And nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven.
14:39: Praise be to God who has given me in my old age, gave me, "Ishmael and Isaac. My Lord is indeed the Hearer of supplication", Ibn Abbas said: Ishmael was born to Abraham when he was ninety-nine years old, and Isaac was born when he was one hundred and twelve years old. Saeed bin Jubair said: Abraham was given the good report of Isaac when he was one hundred and seventeen years old.
14:40: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, meaning: one who establishes prayer with its pillars and maintains it, and from my descendants, meaning: make from my descendants those who establish prayer. Our Lord, accept my supplication, meaning: my work and my worship. He called worship supplication, and it was stated in the hadith: Supplication is the core of worship. It was said: Its meaning is: Answer my prayer.
14:41: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents. If it is said: How can he ask forgiveness for his parents when they are not believers? It is said that it has been said that his mother converted to Islam. It was said: He meant: If they converted to Islam and repented. It was said: He said that before his father’s matter became clear to him, and God Almighty explained the excuse of His friend, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his seeking forgiveness for his father in Surat At-Tawbah. And for the believers, meaning: forgive all the believers, on the Day when the reckoning takes place, meaning: it will appear and become apparent. It was said: He meant the Day when people will say, for the reckoning, so mentioning the reckoning was sufficient because it is understood.
14:42: God Almighty says: And never think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. Heedlessness is a meaning that prevents a person from understanding the truth of things, and the verse is to console the wronged and threaten the wrongdoer. He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare in horror, meaning: they will not close their eyes from the horror of what they will see on that Day. It was also said: they will rise and move from their places.
14:43: Rushing, Qatada said: Hastening. Saeed bin Jubair said: The two descendants are like the enemy of the wolf. Mujahed said: Long-sighted. The meaning of Ihta’a is that they do not turn right or left, and they do not know where their feet are. Holding their heads high, meaning: holding their heads high. Al-Qatibi said: Al-Muqni` is the one who raises his head and looks at what is in front of him. Al-Hassan said: People’s faces on the Day of Resurrection will be towards the sky, and no one will look at anyone else. Their glances will not return to them meaning: their eyes will not return to them from the intensity of their gaze, and they will be staring, preoccupied with what is in front of them. And their hearts are empty, meaning: empty. Qatada said: Their hearts have left their chests and are in their throats, neither leaving their mouths nor returning to their places. So the hearts are air with nothing in them, and from this the space between the sky and the earth is called air because of its emptiness. It was said: Empty, not aware of anything and not sensible due to fear. Al-Akhfash said: Hollow, without minds. The Arabs call everything hollow air. Saeed bin Jubair said: And their hearts are empty meaning: they are hesitant, they are seething in their chests, and they have no place to settle. The true meaning is that hearts will be removed from their places, and eyes will be staring at the horror of that day.
14:44: And warn the people, frighten them, of a Day, that is, of a day, when the punishment will come to them, which is the Day of Resurrection, Then those who did wrong will say, they associated partners with God, Our Lord, give us respite, give us respite, for a short term, this is their request to be returned to the world, that is, return us to it, We will answer Your call and follow the messengers, so they will be answered: Did you not swear before, you swore in the worldly abode, that you would not be removed, from it, that is, you would not be resurrected. And this is the saying of God Almighty: And they swear by God their most solemn oaths that God will not resurrect anyone who dies (al-Nahl 16:38).
14:45: And you dwelt, in this world, in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, by disbelief and disobedience, the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and others. And it became clear to you how We dealt with them, that is, you knew Our punishment of them, and We presented to you examples, that is, We made clear that your example is like their example.
14:46: And they plotted their plot, and with God is their plot, meaning: the reward for their plot, and if their plot was, Ali and Ibn Masoud read: and if their plot was with the letter dal, and the general public read it with the letter nun. That the mountains may pass away from it. The common people read lanzul with a kasra on the first lām and a fathah on the second. Meaning: Their plot was not true. Al-Hassan said: Their plot is so weak that mountains can move. It was said: Its meaning is that their plot will not remove Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who is as firm as the mountains. Ibn Jurayj and Al-Kisa’i read: to be removed with the first lam open and the second lam raised, meaning: their plot, even if it is so great that it reaches a place that moves mountains, they will not be able to remove the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Qatada said: Its meaning is that their polytheism was due to the mountains descending from it, as God Almighty said: And the mountains collapse in devastation, because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son (Maryam 19:19). It is narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, regarding the meaning of the verse: It was revealed about the tyrant Nimrod who argued with Abraham about his Lord, and that he said: If what Abraham says is true, I will not stop until I ascend to the sky and know what is in it. So he took four young eagles and raised them until they grew up and made a coffin, and made a door for it at the top and a door at the bottom. Nimrod sat with a man in the coffin, and set up planks at the edges of the coffin, and put meat on their heads and tied the coffin to the legs of the eagles. They broke out and ascended in greed for the meat, until a day passed and they were far away in the air. Nimrod said to his companion: Open the upper door and look at the sky. Have we brought it near? So he opened the door and looked and said: The sky is as it was. Then he said: Open the lower door and look at the earth. How do you see it? So he did, and he said: I see the earth like a sea and the mountains like smoke. Then the eagles flew another day, and rose until the wind prevented them from flying. Then he said to his companion: Open the two doors. So he opened the upper one and saw the sky as it was, and he opened the lower one and saw the earth black and dark. Then he was called: O tyrant, where are you going? Akrima said: There was with him in the coffin a young man who had carried a bow and arrows with him. He shot an arrow and the arrow returned to him stained with the blood of a fish that had thrown itself into the air from the sea - and it was said: a bird that had been hit by the arrow - so he said: I have been spared the burden of the sky. He said: Then Nimrod ordered his companion to straighten the planks and cut off the meat, so he did, and the vultures descended with the Ark, and the mountains heard the rustling of the Ark and the vultures, so they were frightened and thought that something had happened from the sky, and that the Hour had come, so they almost fell from their places, and that is what God Almighty said: And their plot was to move the mountains.
14:47: Do not think that God will fail to fulfill His promise to His messengers, with victory for His friends and the destruction of His enemies. There is an inversion of this, meaning: Do not think that God will fail to fulfill His promise to His messengers, Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Possessor of Retribution.
14:48: God Almighty said: On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Khalid bin Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ja`far bin Abi Katheer, Abu Hazim bin Dinar told me, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa`d Al-Sa`idi, may God be pleased with him - he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a white, pure land like a loaf of bread, on which no one will have knowledge. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Khalid - he is Ibn Yazid - on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the Day of Resurrection, the earth will be a single loaf of bread, which the Almighty will turn over in His hand as one of you turns over his loaf of bread while traveling, as provision for the people of Paradise.” On the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, regarding this verse, he said: The earth will be replaced with a land like pure white silver, in which no blood has been shed and upon which no sin has been committed. Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: The earth will be replaced with silver and the sky with gold. Muhammad bin Kaab and Saeed bin Jubair said: The earth will be replaced with white bread that the believer will eat from beneath his feet. It was said: The meaning of the change is making the heavens gardens and making the earth fires. It was said: Changing the earth means changing it from one form to another, and it is moving its mountains, filling up its rivers, leveling its valleys, cutting down its trees, and making it a flat desert. Changing the heavens means changing their state by folding up its sun, eclipsing its moon, scattering its stars, and making it bitter like oil, and bitter like molten metal. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Ali bin Masahr told us, on the authority of Dawud - who is the son of Abi Hind - on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the words of God Almighty: ‘The Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well]’. So where will the people be on that Day, O Messenger of God? He said: ‘On the Bridge.’” Thawban narrated: “A Jewish rabbi asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Where will the people be on the day when the earth is changed to another earth? He said: They will be in the darkness beyond the bridge.” God Almighty says: And they will emerge, they will emerge from their graves, for God, the One, the Prevailing, who does what He wills and rules as He wills.
14:49: And you will see the criminals that Day bound together, bound together, in shackles, in chains and fetters, the singular of which is safad, and whoever you bind tightly, you have shackled. Abu Ubaidah said: I handcuffed the man, so he is masfud, and I handcuffed him with emphasis, so he is musafd. It was said: Every disbeliever is linked with his devil in a chain, as explained by the Almighty’s saying: Gather together those who did wrong and their companions (al-Saffat 37:22), meaning: their companions from the devils. It was said: Its meaning is that their hands and feet are tied to their necks with shackles and chains, and from this the rope is called: Qarn.
14:50: Their shirts, meaning their shirts, singular is sirbal. From tar is what camels enjoy. Ikrimah and Yaqub read from qatran with two words with a tanween. Qatran means molten copper and brass, and now means that which has reached its boiling point. God Almighty said: They will circulate between it and scalding water (al-Rahman 55:44). And the Fire will cover their faces, meaning: it will rise.
14:51: That God may reward every soul for what it has earned, of good and evil, for God is swift in account.
14:52: This, meaning: this Qur’an, is a message, meaning: a message and an admonition, for mankind, and that they may warn, and frighten, thereby and that they may know that He is but One God, meaning: so that they may use these verses to prove the oneness of God Almighty: and that those of understanding may remember, meaning: so that those of intellects may take heed.
15:2: 2- Perhaps Abu Jaafar, Nafi' and Asim read it with a light ba' and the rest read it with a heavy ba'. These are two dialects. Rabb is for diminution and kam is for multiplication. Rabb is used with a noun and perhaps with a verb. It is said: Rabb rajul ja'ani, and perhaps rajul ja'ani, and what is here is used for the verb after it. Yudhu, yatashu, those who disbelieve wish that they were Muslims. They differed about the situation in which the infidel wishes to convert to Islam. Ad-Dahhak said: The state of observation. It was said: The Day of Resurrection. It is well known that when God brings the believers out of the fire. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the people of Hell are gathered together in Hell, and with them are whomever God wills of the people of the Qiblah, the disbelievers will say to those in Hell from the people of the Qiblah: Are you not Muslims? They will say: Yes. They will say: What benefit did your Islam provide for you while you are with us in Hell? They will say: We had sins and we were seized for them. Then God Almighty will become angry with them [by His grace], and He will command everyone who was from the people of the Qiblah in Hell to be taken out of it. At that time, the disbelievers will wish that they were Muslims." If it is said: How did he say perhaps when it is for belittling, and this wish is common among the infidels? We said: It may have been mentioned for emphasis, or he meant that their preoccupation with the torment does not free them up for regret, but that only crosses their minds sometimes.
15:3: 3- Leave them, O Muhammad, meaning: those who disbelieved, to eat in this world, and enjoy, from their pleasures, and distract them, “hope,” distracts them, from taking their share of faith and obedience, for they will know, when they come to the Resurrection and taste the consequences of what they did, and this is a threat and a warning. Some scholars said: Leave them is a threat, and His statement: They will soon know is another threat. So when can life be comfortable between two threats? The verse was abrogated by the verse on fighting.
15:4: 4- And We did not destroy a city, meaning: of the people of a city, but it had a known decree, meaning: a set term that cannot be advanced, and the punishment will not come to them until they reach it, nor will it be delayed from them.
15:5: 5- No nation can precede its appointed time from a connection, nor can they delay it, meaning: death is neither advanced nor delayed, and it was said: the punishment that is inflicted.
15:6: 6- And they said," meaning: the polytheists of Mecca, "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down," meaning: the Qur'an, and they meant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, "Indeed, you are mad," and they mentioned the sending down of the Reminder as a way of mockery.
15:7: 7- "If you do not, why don't bring us the angels, to witness for you the truth of what you say, if you are of the truthful", you are a prophet.
15:8: 8- "We do not send down the angels, the people of Kufa except Abu Bakr read with two noons the angels in the accusative case, and Abu Bakr read with the taa and a damma and a fatha on the zay the angels in the nominative case, and the rest read with the taa and a fatha and a fatha on the zay the angels" in the nominative case. Except with the truth meaning: with the punishment. If the angels had descended, they would have hastened the punishment. And they would not then have been given respite meaning: delayed. The disbelievers were asking for the angels to be sent down visibly, so God Almighty answered them with this. Its meaning is: If they had descended visibly, the respite would have been removed from the disbelievers and they would have been punished immediately.
15:9: 9- "Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, meaning the Qur'an, and indeed, We will be its guardian," meaning: the Qur'an is protected from the devils, lest they add to it, subtract from it, or change it. God Almighty said: "Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it" Fussilat 42. Falsehood is Satan, he is not able to add to it what is not from it, nor subtract from it what is from it. It was said that the letter ha in lahu refers back to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning: We will protect Muhammad from those who wish him harm, as God Almighty said: And God will protect you from the people (al-Ma’idah 5:67).
15:10: 10- The Almighty says: And We sent before you, meaning: messengers, among the sects of the ancients, meaning: among the nations and past centuries. Shiites: They are the gathered people whose word is agreed upon.
15:11: 11- And there came not to them a messenger but they mocked him, as they did to you. He mentioned it as a consolation to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
15:12: 12- Thus do We cause it to enter, meaning: just as We caused disbelief, denial, and mockery of the Messengers to enter the hearts of the sects of the first people, thus do We cause it to enter: We cause it to enter, into the hearts of the criminals, meaning: the polytheists of Mecca, your people. And in it is a refutation of the Qadarites.
15:13: 13- They do not believe in it, meaning: they do not believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in the Qur’an, and the way of the ancients has passed, has gone, the precedent of the ancients, meaning: God Almighty's events of destruction among those who denied the messengers from the past nations frightened the people of Mecca.
15:14: 14- And if We opened to them, meaning: to those who say, Why don't you bring us the angels, "a gate from heaven and they continued to ascend therein," meaning: the angels continued to ascend therein, while they saw it clearly. This is the opinion of the majority. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is that these infidels continued to ascend in it, meaning: they climbed. The first is more correct.
15:15: 15- They said, 'Our eyes have only been covered,' Ibn Abbas said. Al-Hassan said: I was bewitched. Qatada said: I took it. Al-Kalbi said: I went blind. Ibn Kathir read sakrat with a light pronunciation, meaning: I blocked and prevented looking, just as a river is blocked due to the blocking of water. Rather, we are a people bewitched, meaning: magic was done to us, and Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - bewitched us.
15:16: 16- The Almighty said: And We have certainly placed in the heaven constellations, and the constellations are the large stars, taken from the word to appear. It is said: A woman appeared, meaning: she appeared. He meant by it: the houses in which the sun, moon, and planets descend, and they are twelve signs: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. Attia said: They are palaces in the sky, guarded by guards. And We adorned it, meaning the sky with the sun, the moon, and the stars, for the observers.
15:17: 17- And We have preserved it from every accursed devil, cursed. It was also said: accursed. Ibn Abbas said: The devils were not prevented from the heavens, and they would enter them and bring report of them and present it to the priests. When Jesus, peace be upon him, was born, they were prevented from three heavens. When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was born, they were prevented from all the heavens. None of them wanted to eavesdrop except that he was shot with a meteor. When they were prevented from those places, they mentioned that to Satan, and he said: Something has happened on earth. He said: So he sent them and they found the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting the Qur’an, and they said: This, by God, has not happened.
15:18: 18- Except for he who eavesdrops, for you are the ones who eavesdrop, and a clear flame pursues him, and flame is a flame of fire. This is because the devils ride each other to the lowest heaven, and they eavesdrop on the angels, so they throw stars and they never miss. Some of them they kill, some of them they burn their faces, sides, hands, or wherever God wills, and some of them they confuse and become ghouls who lead people astray in the desert. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr told us, he said: I heard Ikrimah say: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, as if it were a chain on a rock. Then when fear is banished from their hearts, they say: What did your Lord say? They say to the one who said it: The truth, and He is the Most High, the Great. Then the eavesdroppers hear it, and the eavesdroppers are like this, one above the other - and Sufyan described his hand, turning it and spreading it between his fingers - so one of them hears the word and throws it to the one below him, then the other throws it to the one below him, until he throws it on the tongue of the magician or the soothsayer, and perhaps the meteor catches up with him before he utters it, and perhaps he utters it before it catches up with him, and he tells a hundred lies with it, and he says: Did He not tell us on such and such a day such and such will happen? So he believes in that word that was heard from heaven.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Abi Maryam told us, Al-Layth told us, Ibn Jaafar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The angels descend in the clouds, and they mention the matter that was decreed in the heavens, and the devils eavesdrop and hear it, and they inspire it to the soothsayers, and they tell a hundred lies from themselves along with it.” Yaqub bin Utbah bin Al-Mughira bin Al-Akhns bin Shuraiq said: The first to be alarmed by the shooting of stars was this tribe of Thaqeef. They came to a man from them called Amr bin Umayya, one of the Banu Alaj, who was the most guided of the Arabs. They said to him: Haven’t you seen what has happened in the sky of shooting stars? He said: Yes, so look. If the landmarks of the stars by which people are guided on land and sea and by which the seasons of summer and winter are known for what is good for people in their livelihoods are the ones that are shot at, then they are the folding of the world and the destruction of the creation in it. If they are stars other than God’s, which are fixed in their state, then this is what God Almighty intended for this creation. Muammar said: I said to Al-Zuhri: Were stars used to be shot in the pre-Islamic era? He said: Yes. I said: What do you think of the words of God Almighty: And we used to sit therein in stations to listen (al-Jinn 72:6)? He said: It became more severe and intensified when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent. Ibn Qutaybah said: Stoning was practiced before his mission - may God bless him and grant him peace - but it was not as severe as it was after his mission. It was said: The star falls and throws the devils, then returns to its place. And God knows best.
15:19: 19- The Almighty said: And the earth We have spread out, We spread it out over the surface of the water. It is said that it is a journey of five hundred years, in the same amount it was spread out from under the Kaaba. And We cast therein firm mountains, fixed mountains. The earth used to shake until God anchored it with mountains. And We caused to grow therein, that is, in the earth, of every well-balanced thing, measured and known. It was said: It means in the mountains, and they are jewels of gold, silver, iron, copper, and others, even arsenic and kohl, all of which are weighed. Ibn Zayd said: They are things that are weighed.
15:20: 20- And We have made for you therein means of livelihood, the plural of livelihood, it was said that he meant by it foods, drinks and clothing, which are what a human being lives on in this world, and those for whom you are not providers, meaning: We made therein those for whom you are not providers from the beasts and livestock, meaning: We made them for you and provided you with their sustenance, and of in the verse means what, like the Almighty's saying: And among them is he who walks on his bellies and among them is he who walks on two legs An-Nur-45. It was said: Min is in its place, because he meant the slaves with the animals. It was said: Min is in the accusative case, in apposition to the kaf and the mim in lakum.
15:21: 21- And there is nothing, meaning: there is nothing, but that with Us are its treasuries, meaning the keys to its treasuries. It was said: I want rain with it. And We do not send it down except in a known measure. Every land has a set limit, and it is said: Not a drop falls from the sky except with an angel who directs it where God Almighty wants and desires. On the authority of Jaafar bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said: In the Throne is an example of everything that God created on land and sea, and this is the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories.
15:22: 22- And We sent the winds that were fertile meaning: pregnant, because they carry water to the clouds, and it is the plural of laqahah, it is said: a pregnant camel if it carries a child. Ibn Masoud said: God sends the wind, which brings water, and the clouds pass over it, and it flows like a she-camel flows, then it rains. Abu Ubaidah said: He meant by pollinators the pollinators, the singular of which is pollinator, because it pollinates trees. Ubaid bin Umair said: God sends the good report wind, which makes the earth stand upright. Then God sends the wind that stirs up the clouds. Then God sends the wind that brings the clouds together and makes them into a heap. Then He sends the pollinators, which pollinate the trees. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash said: Not a drop falls from the clouds except after the four winds work on it: the north wind stirs it up, the south wind gathers it, and the south wind scatters it. In al-Naba 78:The south winds blow. In some of the hadiths: The south wind does not blow without sending forth abundant rain. As for the barren wind: it brings torment but does not fertilize. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, someone whose hadith I do not accuse of being false told us, Al-Ala’ bin Rashid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There never was a wind except that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knelt on his knees and said: O God, make it a mercy and do not make it a torment. O God, make it a wind and do not make it a wind. Ibn Abbas said: In the Book of God Almighty: Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind (al-Qamar 54:19) When We sent upon them the barren wind (al-Dhariyat 51:41), and He said: And We sent the winds as fertilizing agents (al-Hijr 15:22), and He said: That He sends the winds as good tidings (al-Rum 30:46). His statement: Then We sent down water from the sky and gave it to you to drink, meaning: We made the rain a drink for you. It is said: So-and-so gave so-and-so to drink if it is what he gave him to drink, and gave him to drink if it is what he gave him to drink. The Arabs say: I gave the man water and milk to drink if it was for his to drink, and if they gave him water for his land and animals to drink, they say: I gave him to drink. “And you are not its keepers,” meaning the rain is in our treasuries, not in your treasuries. Sufyan said: We are not its preventers.
15:23: 23- And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors, that is, We cause all creatures to die, so that no living being remains except Us. The inheritor is one of the attributes of God Almighty. It was said: The one who remains after the annihilation of creation. It was said: Its meaning is that the destiny of creation is to Him.
15:24: 24- And We have certainly known those among you who went before, and We have certainly known those who came after. Ibn Abbas said: He meant by those who went before the dead, and by those who came after the living. Al-Shaabi said: The first and the last. Ikrimah said: The forerunners are those who created God, and the latter are those who did not create God. Mujahed said: The early generations are the predecessors, and the late generations are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hassan said: Those who are ahead in obedience and goodness, and those who are behind and slow in it. It was said: Those who are in the front rows in prayer and those who are behind them. This is because women used to go out to congregational prayer and stand behind the men. Perhaps there was one man who had doubts in his heart and would go back to the last row of men, and perhaps there was one woman who had doubts in her heart and would go forward to the first row of women to be closer to the men. So this verse was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best rows for men are the first and the worst are the last, and the best rows for women are the last and the worst are the first. Al-Awza’i said: He meant those who pray at the beginning of the time and those who pray at the end of it. Muqatil said: He meant those who advanced and those who were behind in the battle line. Ibn Uyaynah said: He meant those who convert to Islam and those who do not convert to Islam.
15:25: 25- "And your Lord will surely gather them. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing," according to what He knows about them. It was said: He will kill everyone, then gather them, the first and the last. Abu Salih Ahmad bin Abdul Malik Al-Mu’adhin told us, Abu Saeed Al-Sayrafi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever dies upon something, God will resurrect him upon it.
15:26: 26- The Almighty said: And We have certainly created man, meaning: Adam, peace be upon him. He was called a human being because of his appearance and the sight’s perception of him. It was said: from forgetfulness because he was entrusted with something and he forgot. From clay, which is dry clay that if you tap it you hear a clanging sound, i.e. a sound. Ibn Abbas said: It is the free clay, from which the water has drained and cracked, and when stirred it rattles. Mujahed said: It is stinking mud. Al-Kisa’i chose this and said: It is from the root word sal to make meat stink and asl to make it stink. From black mud, black mud is called mud, “changed,” meaning: altered. Mujahid and Qatada said: It is the stinking, changed one. Abu Ubaidah said: It is what is poured. The Arabs say: I poured the water, meaning I poured it. Ibn Abbas said: It is wet, stinking soil that is made into clay like pottery. In some of the hadiths: God Almighty mixed Adam’s clay and left it until it became changed and black, then He created Adam, peace be upon him, from it.
15:27: 27- And the jinn We created before, Ibn Abbas said: He is the father of the jinn just as Adam is the father of mankind. Qatada said: He is Iblis, who was created before Adam. It is said: the jinn or the jinn, and Iblis is the father of devils. Among the jinn are Muslims and infidels, and they live and die. As for the devils, none of them are Muslims, and they die when Iblis dies. Wahb said: Some of the jinn are born and eat and drink like humans, and some of the jinn are like the wind and do not eat, drink, or reproduce. From the fire of poisons, and poisons are hot winds that enter a person's pores and kill him. It is said: poisons during the day and heat at night. On the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih: The poisons are a fire that has no smoke, and lightning bolts are heaped up from it, and it is a fire between the sky and the veil. So when God creates a matter, it tears the veil and falls to what it was commanded to do, so the thunder that you hear is in the tearing of that veil. It was said: The fire of poison is the flame of fire. It was said: From the fire of poison, meaning: from the fire of Hell. On the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Iblis was from the tribe of angels called the jinn. They were created from the scorching fire, and the jinn were created in the same way as they were mentioned in the Qur’an from a smokeless flame of fire. As for the angels, they were created from light.
15:28: 28- The Almighty said: And when your Lord said to the angels, ‘Indeed, I am going to create a human being,’ meaning: I will create a human being, from clay from altered black mud.
15:29: 29- Then when I have proportioned him, I have adjusted his form and completed his creation, and breathed into him of My [created] soul, so he became a living human being, and the soul is a subtle body by which a person lives, and He added it to Himself as an honor, then fall down to him in prostration, a prostration of greeting, not a prostration of worship.
15:30: 30- Then the angels prostrated, those who were commanded to prostrate, all of them together. If it is said: Why did he say all of them together when the intended meaning was achieved by his saying the angels prostrated? We said: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh claimed that he mentioned this as confirmation. Al-Mubarrad said: His saying, Then the angels prostrated, it was possible that some of them prostrated, so he mentioned all of them to remove this confusion. Then it was possible that they prostrated at different times, so this confusion was removed by his saying, all of them. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: God Almighty said to a group of angels: Prostrate to Adam, but they did not do so, so God sent fire upon them and burned them. Then He said to another group: Prostrate to Adam, and they prostrated.
15:31: 31- Except Satan, he refused to be with those who prostrated.
15:32: 32- He said, O Iblis, what is the matter with you that you are not with those who prostrate?
15:33: 33- He said, 'I would not prostrate to a human being whom You created from clay from altered black mud.' He meant: I am better than him because he is clay, and I am fire, and fire eats clay.
15:34: 34- He said, 'Then get out of it, for you are expelled, banished.' That is, from Paradise.
15:35: 35- And upon you is the curse until the Day of Judgment. It was said: The people of the heavens curse Satan just as the people of the earth curse him, so he is cursed in the heavens and the earth.
15:36: 36- He said, 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.' The wicked one wanted not to die.
15:37: 37- He said, 'Then you are among those granted respite.'
15:38: 38- He said, 'Then you are among those reprieved * Until the Day of the Appointed Time,' meaning: the time when all creatures will die, which is the first trumpet blast. It is said that the period of Satan’s death is forty years, which is the period between the two blasts. It is said: God Almighty’s response to him in granting him respite was not an honor to him, but rather an increase in his affliction and misery.
15:39: 39- He said, 'My Lord, because You have put me in error,' you have led me astray. It was also said: you have disappointed me in Your mercy, I will surely make attractive to them on the earth, the love of the world and Your disobedience, and I will mislead them, meaning: I will lead them astray, all together.
15:40: 40- Except for Your servants among them who are sincere, the believers who sincerely obeyed and worshipped You, and whoever opens the lam, meaning: whoever You sincerely worshipped in Your worship and chose.
15:41: 41- He said, God Almighty, This is a straight path to me, Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is a straight path to me. Mujahed said: The truth returns to God Almighty, and His path is upon Him, and nothing is crooked for Him. Al-Akhfash said: It means: I am the guide to the straight path. Al-Kisa’i said: This is a threat and warning, as when a man says to someone who is arguing with him: Your path is upon me, meaning: Do not escape from me, as God Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful (al-Fajr 89:14). It was said: Its meaning is on the right path with clarification, proof, success and guidance. Ibn Sirin, Qatada, and Yaqub read: Ali, from the word al-‘ulu meaning: high. Some of them expressed it as: high to attain, straight to deviate.
15:42: 42- Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them, meaning: power. The people of meaning said: It means on their hearts. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah was asked about this verse and he said: Its meaning is that you have no authority over them to commit a sin that is too narrow for forgiveness. These are the chosen ones of God whom He has guided and chosen. Except for those who follow you of the deviators.
15:43: 43- And Hell is the promised place for them all, meaning the promised place for Satan and those who follow him.
15:44: 44-It has seven doors, plates. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Do you know how the gates of Hell are? Like this, and Shu’bah placed one of his hands on the other, meaning: seven gates, one above the other, and God placed the heavens on the horizon and placed the fires, one above the other. Ibn Jurayj said: Hell has seven levels: the first is Hell, then Laza, then Al-Hutama, then Al-Sa’ir, then Saqar, then Al-Jahen, then Al-Haweya. For each door there is a portion allocated to them, meaning: for each level there are people who live in it. Ad-Dahhak said: In the first level are the people of monotheism who were brought into the Fire. They are punished according to the extent of their sins, then they are brought out. In the second are the Christians, in the third are the Jews, in the fourth are the Sabians, in the fifth are the Magians, in the sixth are the polytheists, and in the seventh are the hypocrites. This is what God Almighty says: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire An-Nisa’ 145. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Hell has seven gates, one of which is for those who draw their swords against my nation, or he said, against the nation of Muhammad.
15:45: 45- The Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs, meaning: in orchards and rivers.
15:46: 46- Enter it meaning: it will be said to them, enter Paradise, "in peace", meaning: in safety, secure, from death, expulsion, and calamities.
15:47: 47- And We removed, We extracted, whatever was in their hearts of rancor, which is the hatred, enmity, malice, and envy, brothers, accusative in the state, on couches, plural of a couch, facing each other, facing each other, neither of them looking at the back of the other. In some report: If a believer in Paradise wishes to meet his believing brother, each one’s bed will move to the other’s, and they will meet and talk.
15:48: 48- No fatigue will touch them therein, meaning: exhaustion, nor will they be expelled from it, this is the most explicit verse in the Qur’an on eternity.
15:49: 49- The Almighty said: Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful. Ibn Abbas said: It means to those of them who repent. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “went out one day to a group of his companions who were laughing, and he said: ‘Are you laughing while there is Hellfire before you?’ Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down with this verse and said: ‘Your Lord says to you, O Muhammad, why have you made My servants despair of My mercy?’”
15:50: 50- And that My punishment is the most painful punishment. Qatada said: It has reached us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the servant knew the extent of God's forgiveness, he would not refrain from doing what is forbidden, and if he knew the extent of His punishment, he would despise himself. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Yaqub bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God created mercy on the day He created it as one hundred mercies, then He kept ninety-nine mercies with Him, and sent one mercy to all of His creation. If the disbeliever knew all the mercy that is with God, he would not despair of Paradise, and if the believer knew all the torment that is with God, he would not feel safe from the Fire.”
15:51: 51- "And tell them about the guests of Abraham" meaning: about his guests. Guest: a noun that applies to one, two, plural, masculine and feminine, and they are the angels whom God Almighty sent to give Abraham, peace be upon him, the good report of a son, and to destroy the people of Lot.
15:52: 52- "When they entered upon him and said, 'Peace,' he said," Ibrahim: "Indeed, we are afraid of you," afraid because they did not eat his food.
15:53: 53- "They said, 'Do not be afraid. We give you good tidings of a learned boy.'" That is, a boy in his youth, learned in his adulthood, meaning: Isaac. So Abraham, peace be upon him, was amazed at his old age and the old age of his wife.
15:54: 54- "He said, 'You have given me good report,' meaning: of a child, 'even though old age has touched me,' meaning: in a state of old age. He said it in a way of astonishment. 'So with what do you give me good report?' Nafi' read it with a kasra on the noon and a light sukoon, meaning: you give me good report. Ibn Kathir read it with a shaddah on the noon, meaning: you give me good report. The noon of the plural was assimilated into the noon of the addition. The others read it with a fatha on the noon and a light sukoon.
15:55: 55- "They said, 'We give you good tidings of truth, so do not be among the despairing.'"
15:56: 56- "He said, 'And whoever despairs,'" Abu Amr, Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read it with a kasra on the noon, and the others read it with a fatha on it, and they are two dialects: qanat yaqnatu, and qanat yaqnatu, meaning: whoever despairs, "from the mercy of his Lord except those who have gone astray," meaning: the losers, and despairing of the mercy of God is a great sin, like feeling secure from His deceit.
15:57: 57-Abraham said to them: What is the matter with you, what is your affair, O messengers?
15:58: 58- "They said, 'We have been sent to a people of criminals,' polytheists."
15:59: 59- Except the family of Lot, his followers and people of his religion, We will surely save them all, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i softened the jim, and the rest stressed it.
15:60: 60- Except his wife, meaning: Lot's wife, We have decreed, We have decided, that she is among those who remain behind, those who remain in the punishment, and the exception from the negation is affirmation, and from the affirmation is negation, so He excepted Lot's wife from those who were saved, so she was included with those who perished. Abu Bakr read Qadarna here and in Surat An-Naml with a light dal, while the rest read it with a heavy dal.
15:61: 61-So when the messengers came to the family of Lot.
15:62: 62- He said, Lot to them, You are a people who do not know you, meaning: I do not know you.
15:63: 63- They said, 'Rather, we have brought you that about which they were in doubt.' That is, they doubted that it would befall them, which was the punishment, because he had threatened them with punishment and they did not believe him.
15:64: 64-And We have brought you the truth, with certainty. It was said: with torment, and indeed, We are truthful.
15:65: 65- "So set out with your family during a part of the night and follow their backs" meaning: go behind them, "and let none of you look back", so that they will not be terrified by the punishment if it descends upon their people. It was said that God made this a sign for those who would be saved from the family of Lot. And go where you are commanded. Ibn Abbas said: meaning Ash-Sham. Muqatil said: meaning Zughar. It was also said: Jordan.
15:66: 66- And We decreed that matter for him, meaning: We completed that matter for the people of Lot, meaning: We perfected the matter that We commanded regarding the people of Lot, and We informed him: That the root of these people, is indicated by Abdullah's reading: And We told him that the root of these people, meaning: their origin, is cut off, uprooted, in the morning, if they enter the morning.
15:67: 67- And the people of the city came, meaning Sodom, rejoicing, at Lot’s guests, meaning: they gave each other good report, hoping to commit the immorality with them.
15:68: 68- He said, Lot to his people, Indeed, these are my guests, and it is the right of a man to honor his guest, so do not disgrace them.
15:69: 69- And fear God and do not be disgraced, and do not be shy.
15:70: 70- "They said, 'Did we not forbid you from hosting anyone from the worlds?'" That is, did we not forbid you from hosting anyone from the worlds? It was said: Did we not forbid you from letting strangers enter the city, for we commit immorality from them?
15:71: 71- "He said, 'These are my daughters.' I will marry them to you if you become Muslims. So do what is lawful and leave what is unlawful, 'if you are going to do.'" What I command you to do. It was said: He meant by daughters the women of his people because the Prophet is like a father to his nation.
15:72: 72- God Almighty said: By your life, O Muhammad, that is, by your life, they are in their intoxication, their confusion and misguidance, wandering blindly, hesitating. Qatada said: They play. It was narrated on the authority of Abu al-Juza’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: God did not create a soul more honorable to Him than Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God Almighty did not swear by anyone’s life except by his life.
15:73: 73- Then the blast overtook them at sunrise, meaning: when the sun shone, so the punishment began when they woke up, and its completion was when they rose.
15:74: 74- So We turned it upside down and rained down upon them stones of baked clay.
15:75: 75- Indeed in that are signs for those who take signs. Ibn Abbas said: For those who observe. Mujahed said: For those who are scrutinizing. Qatada said: For those who consider. Muqatil said: For the thinkers.
15:76: 76- And it means: the villages of Lot's people, is on a clear path, meaning: on a clear road. Mujahed said: A marked path that is not hidden or disappearing.
15:77: 77- Indeed in that is a sign for the believers.
15:78: 78- "And if, and the companions of the thicket, the thicket, were wrongdoers", disbelievers, and the lam is for emphasis, and they were the people of Shu`ayb, peace be upon him, they were the companions of thickets and intertwined trees, and most of their trees were the dom tree, which is the tamarisk.
15:79: 79- So We took vengeance on them with punishment, because God imposed heat on them for seven days, then God sent a cloud and they took refuge in it seeking relief, so God sent fire from it upon them and burned them, so that is what God Almighty said: So the punishment of the Day of Shadow seized them Ash-Shu'ara' 189. And indeed meaning the cities of the people of Lot and the people of the thicket are on a clear path, in a clear and evident way.
15:80: 80- The Almighty said: And the companions of Al-Hijr denied the messengers, which is the city of Thamud, the people of Salih, and it is between Medina and Ash-Sham, the messengers, meaning Salih alone.
15:81: 81- And We gave them Our signs, meaning: the she-camel, her young, and the well. So the signs in the she-camel are her emergence from the rock, her growth, the nearness of her birth, and the abundance of her milk, but they were turning away from it.
15:82: 82- And they used to carve out houses from the mountains, secure, from destruction and the mountain falling on them.
15:83: 83- Then the blast seized them, meaning: the blast of torment, in the morning, meaning: entering the time of dawn.
15:84: 84- What they used to earn did not avail them, of polytheism and evil deeds. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, Salim ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when he passed by al-Hijr, he said: Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves unless you are weeping, lest what befell them befall you. He said: And he covered himself with his cloak while he was on the saddle. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar: Then he covered his head and hastened his pace until he crossed the valley.
15:85: 85- The Almighty said: “And We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except in truth. And indeed, the Hour” meaning: the Resurrection is coming. He will reward the doer of good for his good and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. So pardon with gracious pardon, so turn away from them and pardon with gracious pardon. The verse on fighting abrogated it.
15:86: 86-Indeed, your Lord is the Creator, the Knower [of His creation].
15:87: 87- The Almighty said: And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses, Omar and Ali said: They are the opening of the Book. And this is the view of Qatada, Ata, Al-Hasan, and Saeed bin Jubair. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam told us, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, Saeed Al-Maqburi told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Mother of the Qur’an is the seven oft-repeated verses and the Great Qur’an. On the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said about the seven Mathani: It is the opening of the Book, and the Great Qur’an: It is the rest of the Qur’an. They differed as to why Al-Fatihah was called Mathani? Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Qatada said: Because it is repeated in prayer and is recited in every rak’ah. It was said: Because it is divided between God and the servant into two halves, one half is praise and the other half is supplication, as narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, who said: God Almighty says: I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant into two halves. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: It was called Mathani because it was revealed twice: once in Mecca and once in Medina, and each time seventy thousand angels were with it. Mujahed said: It was called Mathani because God Almighty excluded it and saved it for this nation and did not give it to anyone else. Abu Zaid Al-Balkhi said: It was called Mathani because it prevents evil people from committing immorality, like the Arabs say: I prevented my reins. It was said: Because the beginning is praise. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The seven Mathani are the seven long ones, the first of which is Surat Al-Baqarah, and the last of which is Al-Anfal with At-Tawbah. Some of them said: Surat Yunus instead of Al-Anfal. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan bin Ahmad Al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Hamdun bin Khalid and Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Muslim told us: Hilal bin Al-Ala’ told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Utbah, on the authority of Yahya bin Katheer, on the authority of Shaddad bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Asma Al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty gave me the seven long ones in place of the Torah, and gave me the hundred ones in place of the Gospel, and gave me the paired ones in place of the Psalms, and my Lord favored me with the Mufassal.” On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given the seven long ones, and Moses was given six. When he threw down the tablets, he raised two and four remained. Ibn Abbas said: The seven long verses were called Mathani because the obligatory duties, limits, proverbs, report, and lessons were mentioned in them. Tawus said: The entire Qur’an is repeated. God Almighty said: “God has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book, repeated in pairs” (al-Zumar 39:234). The Qur’an was called repeated because the prophets and stories are repeated in it. According to this statement: What is meant by the seven is seven sevenths of the Qur’an, so its meaning is: and they are the great Qur’an. It was said: the waw is inserted, meaning: And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an.
15:88: 88- The Almighty said: Do not extend your eyes, O Muhammad, to that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] spouses, of various kinds, of them, meaning: of the infidels, wishing for it. God Almighty forbade His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from desiring the world and competing with its people for it. And do not grieve over them, meaning: do not grieve over what you missed of sharing with them in this world. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Abu Jaafar Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Anzi told us, Isa bin Nasr told us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, Jahm bin Aws told us, he said: I heard Abdullah bin Maryam - Abdullah bin Rustum passed by him in his procession, and he said to Ibn Abi Maryam 19:I desire to sit with you and talk to you, and when he had passed, Ibn Maryam said - I heard Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Do not envy a sinner for his blessings, for you do not know what he will encounter after his death. He has a killer with God who will not die." This reached Wahb bin Munabbih, so Wahb sent Abu Dawud Al-Awar to him, and he said: O Abu So-and-so, what is a killer who will not die? Ibn Abi Maryam said: Hellfire. Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Muzaffari al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Saeed Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Faqih told us, Abu al-Hasan ibn Ishaq told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Absi told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him - he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Look at those who are below you and do not look at those who are above you, for that is more likely to prevent you from despising God’s blessing upon you. It was said: This verse is connected to what preceded it, because when God Almighty blessed him with the Qur’an, He forbade him from desiring worldly things. It was narrated that Sufyan ibn Uyaynah - may God have mercy on him - interpreted the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He is not one of us who does not chant the Qur’an, meaning: he does not find contentment with the Qur’an. So he interpreted this verse. God Almighty says: And lower your wing, be gentle with them, to the believers, and be kind to them. The two wings are the sides of the son of Adam.
15:89: 89-And say, 'Indeed, I am the clear warner.'
15:90: 90- As We sent down upon those who divided Al-Farra' said: Its meaning is: I warned you of a punishment like the punishment of those who divided. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas - may God be pleased with them both - that he said: They are the Jews and Christians.
15:91: 91- Those who divided the Qur'an into parts, they divided it and made it into parts, believing in some of it and disbelieving in some of it. Mujahid said: They are the Jews and Christians who divided their book, divided it, and changed it. It was said: The dividers are people who divided the Qur’an. Some of them said: It is magic. Some of them said: It is poetry. Some of them said: It is a lie. Some of them said: It is legends of the ancients. It was said: The division is that they divided the statement about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: He is a magician, a soothsayer, and a poet. Muqatil said: They were sixteen men sent by Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah during the season. They divided up the roads and paths of Mecca and sat at its passes saying to those who came from Al-Hajjaj: Do not be deceived by this outcast man who claims prophethood from among us. A group of them said: He is crazy, a group said: He is a soothsayer, and a group said: He is a poet. Al-Walid sat at the door of the mosque and they appointed him as a judge. When he was asked about him, he said: Those, meaning those who divided up, told the truth. His saying: organs It was said: It is the plural of organ taken from their saying I divided the thing if you separated it. Its meaning is: They made the Qur’an into organs, so some of them said: Magic. Some of them said: Divination. Some of them said: Legends of the ancients. It was said: It is the plural of ‘Udhah. It is said: ‘Udhah and ‘Udhayn, like Barra and Barin, ‘Azzah and ‘Uzayn. Its origin is ‘Udhah, the original ‘ha’ has been lost, just as they omitted ‘Shafa’ah’ from ‘Shafaha’, as evidenced by the fact that you say ‘Shafiha’ in the diminutive form. What is meant by ‘Udhah’ is lying and slander. It was said: What is meant by the two bites is the bite, which is magic. He means: They called the Qur’an magic.
15:92: 92-By your Lord, We will surely question them all, on the Day of Resurrection.
15:93: 93- "About what they used to do" in this world. Muhammad bin Ismail said that several scholars said: About his saying, "There is no god but God." If it is said: How can we reconcile this verse with the Almighty’s saying: On that Day no human being or jinn will be asked about his sin (al-Rahman 55:39). Ibn Abbas said: He does not ask them, Did you do this? because He knows them better than they do. Rather, He says, Did you do such and such? Qatrub relied on this and said: There are two types of questions: a question of inquiry and a question of rebuke. So the Almighty’s statement, On that Day no man or jinn will be asked about his sin (al-Rahman 55:39), means an inquiry. And His statement, We will surely question them all means a rebuke and a reprimand. Akrima said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the two verses: The Day of Resurrection is a long day in which there will be situations in which they will be questioned in some situations, and not questioned in others. Similar to this is the saying of God Almighty: This is a Day when they will not speak (al-Mursalat 77:35), and He said in another verse: Then on the Day of Resurrection you will surely dispute before your Lord (al-Zumar 39:31).
15:94: 94- The Almighty said: So proclaim what you are commanded. Ibn Abbas said: Make it apparent. It is narrated from him: Implement it. Al-Dahhak said: I know. Al-Akhfash said: Separate, meaning: differentiate between truth and falsehood with the Qur’an. Sibawayh said: Decide as you are commanded. The root of sadaq is separation. “Farq” is the command of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this verse to declare the call. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaidah that he was hiding until this verse was revealed, so he and his companions went out. And turn away from the polytheists, was abrogated by the verse on fighting.
15:95: 95- Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers, God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: So proclaim the command of God, and do not fear anyone other than God Almighty, for God will suffice you against your enemies just as He sufficed you against the mockers, and they are five men from the leaders of Quraish: Al-Walid bin Al-Makhzumi - who was their leader - and Al-Aas bin Wael Al-Sahmi, and Al-Aswad bin Abdul Muttalib bin Al-Harith bin Asad bin Abdul Uzza bin Zam'ah, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had prayed against him, saying: O God, blind his sight and bereave him of his children, and Al-Aswad bin Abdul Yaghuth bin Wahb bin Abdul Manaf bin Zuhrah, and Al-Harith bin Qais bin At-Talalatah. Gabriel came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the mockers were circling the House, so Gabriel stood up and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood beside him, and Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah passed by him and said: Gabriel, O Muhammad, how do you find this? He said: What a bad servant of God! He said: He had sufficed him, and he pointed to Al-Walid’s leg. Then he passed by a man from Khuza’ah who was feathering his arrows, and he was wearing a Yemeni cloak, and he was dragging his garment. A splinter of an arrow got stuck in his garment, but his pride prevented him from lowering his head and removing it. It began to strike his leg, scratching him, and he became ill from it and died. Al-Aas bin Wa'il passed by him and Gabriel said: How do you find this, O Muhammad? He said: What a bad servant of God. Gabriel pointed to the soles of his feet and said: I have taken care of him. He went out on his mount with his two sons to take a walk. He stopped in one of those valleys and stepped on a thorn from it. A thorn entered the sole of his foot. He said: It was bitten, it was bitten. They searched but found nothing, and his foot swelled until it became like a camel's neck, and he died on the spot. Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib passed by him and said: Gabriel, how do you find this? He said: A bad slave. So he pointed with his hand to his eyes and said: I have spared him and he has become blind. Ibn Abbas said: Gabriel threw a green leaf at him, so he lost his sight and his eyes hurt, so he started hitting his head against the wall until he died. In Al-Kalbi’s narration: Gabriel came to him while he was sitting at the base of a tree with a rope, and he began to butt his head against the tree and hit his face with thorns. He called for help from his servant, and his servant said: I do not see anyone doing anything to you except yourself, until he died, saying: The Lord of Muhammad killed me. Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth passed by him, and Gabriel said: How do you find this, O Muhammad? He said: What a bad servant of God, even though he is my maternal uncle. He said: I have taken care of him, and he pointed to his stomach. His stomach became watery and he died for a while. In a narration by Al-Kalbi, he left his family and was poisoned, turning black until he returned to being an Abyssinian. He came to his family, but they did not recognize him, and they closed the door on him until he died, saying: The Lord of Muhammad killed me. Al-Harith bin Qais passed by him and Gabriel said: How do you find this, O Muhammad? He said: An evil slave. He pointed to his head and said: I have taken care of him. Then he blew out pus and killed him.
15:96: 96- Ibn Abbas said: He ate a salted fish and became thirsty, so he kept drinking water until his stomach was full and he died. This is what God Almighty said: Indeed, We will suffice you against those who mock, against you and the Qur’an, “who set up with God another god. They are going to know.”
15:97: 97-It was said: Their mockery and division: is that when God Almighty revealed in the Qur’an Surat Al-Baqarah, Surat An-Nahl, Surat An-Naml, and Surat Al-Ankabut, they would gather and say mockingly: This is in Surat Al-Baqarah, and he says this in Surat An-Nahl, and he says this in Surat Al-Ankabut, so God Almighty revealed: And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say.
15:98: 98- So glorify the praises of your Lord, Ibn Abbas said: So pray by the command of your Lord, and be among those who prostrate, among the humble worshippers. Ad-Dahhak said: So glorify the praises of your Lord: Say, Glory be to God and His praise “and be among those who prostrate”: those who pray. It was narrated that when something saddened the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would resort to prayer.
15:99: 99-And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty, meaning the certain death, and this is the meaning of what was mentioned in Surat Maryam 19:And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I remain alive. Al-Mutahhar bin Ali Al-Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Salihi told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Jaafar Abu Al-Sheikh Al-Hafiz told us, Umayyah bin Muhammad Al-Sawaaf Al-Basri told us, Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Azdi told us, my father and Al-Haitham bin Kharijah told us: Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Shurahbil bin Muslim, on the authority of Abu Muslim Al-Khawlani, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “It was not revealed to me to accumulate wealth and be among the merchants, but it was revealed to me to glorify the praises of your Lord and be among those who prostrate, and worship your Lord until the certainty comes to you.” It was narrated on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at Mus`ab ibn `Umair approaching, wearing a ram’s hide that he could already wrap around his waist. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Look at this man whose heart God has enlightened. I saw him among his parents, nourished with the best food and drink. I saw him wearing a garment that he bought, or that was bought for him, for two hundred dirhams. Then the love of God and His Messenger called him to what you see.” And God knows best.
16:1: Meccan, [one hundred and twenty-eight verses] except for the Almighty’s saying: And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were punished, to the end of the surah. 1- It came means: it came, drew near, and was close. The command of God Ibn Arafa said: The Arabs say: The command came to you while it was still expected, meaning: God’s command came as a promise, so do not rush it to happen. God’s command. Al-Kalbi and others said: What is meant by it is the Resurrection. Ibn Abbas said: When the words of God Almighty, The Hour has drawn near (al-Qamar 54:1) were revealed, the infidels said to one another: This man claims that the Day of Resurrection has drawn near, so refrain from some of what you were doing until you see what will happen.
