When nothing was revealed, they said: We do not see anything. Then the words, The reckoning of the people has drawn near (al-Anbiya 21:1) were revealed, and they were afraid. When the days passed, they said: O Muhammad, we do not see anything of what you are frightening us with. Then God Almighty revealed: The command of God has come. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, jumped up and the people raised their heads and thought that it had truly come. Then the words, So do not hasten it were revealed, and they were reassured. Urgency: asking for something before its time. When this verse was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I and the Hour were sent like these two, and he pointed with his two fingers, and it almost preceded me. Ibn Abbas said: The mission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one of the signs of the Hour. When Gabriel, peace be upon him, passed by the people of the heavens as a messenger to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said: God is Great, the Hour has come. Some people said: What is meant by the command here is the punishment of the deniers and the torment by the sword. This is because Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky. So he hastened the torment, and this verse was revealed. Al-Nadr was killed on the day of Badr with patience. Glory be to Him, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him. This means that He is exalted in praiseworthy descriptions above what the polytheists describe Him with.
16:2: 2- He sends down the angels, the general public read it with a damma on the ya and a kasra on the zay, and the angels is accusative. Yaqub read it with a taa and a fatha on it and a fatha on the zay, and the angels is nominative, He sends down the angels with the spirit with the revelation, He called it a spirit because He revives the hearts and the truth with it. Ata' said: By prophecy. Qatada said: With mercy. Abu Ubaidah said, With the spirit means with the spirit, which is Gabriel. “From His command over whomever He wills of His servants: ‘Warn,’ know that there is no god but Me, so fear Me.” It was said that its meaning is to command them to say, There is no god but God, warning and frightening them with the Qur’an if they do not say it. His saying, So fear means: So be afraid.
16:3: 3. “He created the heavens and the earth in truth. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him.” That is, He is exalted above what they associate with Him.
16:4: 4. He created man from a sperm-drop, and at once he is an adversary, arguing falsely, clear. It was revealed about Abi bin Khalaf Al-Jumahi, who denied the resurrection. He came with a rotten bone and said: Do you say that God Almighty will revive this after it has rotted? As He, the Most High, said: And he has set forth for Us an example and has forgotten his own creation (Ya-Sin 36:77). It was also revealed about him. The correct view is that the verse is general, and it explains the power and exposes the ugliness of what they did, of denying God’s blessings even though they were evident to them.
16:5: 5. The Almighty’s saying, And the grazing livestock He has created, meaning camels, cows, and sheep, for you in them is warmth, meaning: from their fur, hair, and wool, clothing and blankets to warm you, and benefits, through offspring, milk, riding, carrying, and other things, and from them you eat, meaning their meat.
16:6: 6. And there is beauty for you in them, an adornment, when you bring them back in the evening, that is, when you return them in the evening from their pastures to their resting places where they take refuge, and when you send them out to pasture, that is, when you take them out in the morning from their stages to their pastures. He mentioned the returns first because the benefits are taken from them after the return, and their owner is more pleased with them when they are at rest.
16:7: 7. And carry your burdens, your loads to a country, other than your country. Ikrimah said: The country is Mecca. You could not reach it except with great difficulty, meaning: with hardship and effort. The half is also the half, meaning: you could not reach it except with a decrease in the lack of the soul and the loss of half of it. Abu Jaafar read bishq with the opening of the sheen, and they are two dialects, like ratl and ratl. “Your Lord is Most Kind and Most Merciful” to His creation, as He gave them these benefits.
16:8: 8. And the horses, meaning: And He created the horses, which is a generic noun that has no singular form, like camels and women, and mules and donkeys for you to ride and as an adornment, meaning: And He made them an adornment for you along with the benefits that they contain. And he used this verse as evidence for those who forbade horse meat, which is the saying of Ibn Abbas, and he recited this verse and said: This is for riding [and the opinion of] Al-Hakam, Malik, and Abu Hanifa. A group of people permitted horse meat, which is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Shuraih, Ata’, and Saeed bin Jubayr. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq also said the same. And whoever permitted it said: The purpose of the verse is not to explain what is permissible and what is forbidden, but rather what is meant by it is for God to inform His servants of His blessings and alert them to the perfection of His power and wisdom. They provided evidence for this by: Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Amr - he is Ibn Dinar - on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the meat of donkeys on the day of Khaybar, but permitted the meat of horses.” Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar bin Ismail al-Tamimi told us, Abu al-Qasim Hamza bin Yusuf al-Sahmi told us, Abu Ahmad Abdullah bin Adi al-Hafiz told us, al-Hasan bin al-Faraj told us, Amr bin Khalid told us, Abdullah bin Abdul Karim told us, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Jabir, that they used to eat horse meat during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he forbade eating the meat of mules and donkeys. It was narrated on the authority of al-Miqdam bin Ma’di Karib on the authority of Khalid bin al-Walid that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade eating the meat of horses, mules and donkeys, and its chain of transmission is weak. And He creates what you do not know. It was said: It means what God has prepared in Paradise for its people, and in Hell for its people, of what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Qatada said: It means: weevils in plants and worms in fruits.
16:9: 9. The Almighty’s saying: And upon God is the direction of the way means: explaining the path of guidance from misguidance. And it was said: explaining the truth with verses and proofs, and the direction is the straight path. And among them is some that are crooked means: And among the paths is some that are crooked and deviate from the straight path. The intended meaning of the path is the religion of Islam, and among them is some that are crooked: Judaism, Christianity, and all other religions of disbelief. Jabir bin Abdullah said: The intention of the path: explaining the laws and obligations. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak and Sahl bin Abdullah said: He intended the path is the Sunnah, and from it is the unjust desires and innovations, its evidence is the saying of God Almighty: And that this is My path, which is straight, so follow it and do not follow other paths (al-An’am 6:153). And if He had willed, He could have guided you all, similar to the Almighty’s saying: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance (al-Sajdah 32:13)
16:10: 10. The Almighty’s saying: It is He who sent down water from the sky for you, from which you drink, you drink it, and from it grow trees, meaning: from that water is the drink of your trees and the life of your plants, and in it, meaning: in the trees, you graze, you graze your livestock.
16:11: 11. "He causes to grow for you with it" meaning: God causes to grow for you with it, with the water that He sent down. Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim "It causes to grow" with a noon. "The crops, the olives, the palm trees, the grapes, and from all the fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought."
16:12: 12. And He has subjected to you, [subdued to you], the night and the day and the sun and the moon and the stars are subjected, subdued, by His command, meaning: by His permission. Hafs read and the stars are subjected in the nominative case as the beginning. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
16:13: 13. And He created for you, for your sake, meaning: He subjected what He created for you, on the earth, of animals, trees, fruits, and other things, different, in the accusative case as a state, of its colors. “Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember.”
16:14: 14. And it is He who has subjected the sea that you may eat from it tender meat meaning: fish, and extract from it ornaments which you wear meaning: pearls and coral, and you see the ships sailing through it maidens. Qatada said: Coming and going, which means that you see two ships, one coming and the other going, sailing with the same wind. Al-Hassan said: Mawakhir means full. Al-Farra and Al-Akhfash said: Shawwaq splits the water with its wings. Mujahed said: The winds move the ships. The root of al-makhr is to lift and split. In the hadith, If one of you wants to urinate, let him look at where the wind is coming from and blow, and let him turn his back on it so that the urine does not get cold on him. Abu Ubaidah said: Sawaikh and Makhr are the sound of the wind blowing when it is strong. And that you may seek of His bounty, meaning: trade, and perhaps you will be grateful, if you see God’s work in what He has subjected to you.
16:15: 15. And He has cast into the earth firm mountains, lest it should shift with you. That is, [so that it should not shift with you], that is, move and tilt. Al-Maid: is the disturbance and equilibrium, and from it the dizziness that afflicts a seafarer is called: Meid. Wahb said: When God created the earth, it began to sway, so the angels said: This does not allow anyone to rest on its back. Then it became anchored to the mountains, and the angels did not know what the mountains were created from. And rivers and paths meaning: He made rivers and different paths in it, that you may be guided to what you want and not go astray.
16:16: 16. "And signs", meaning: road landmarks. Some of them said: Here the speech ended, then he began, "And by the star they are guided." Muhammad bin Kaab and Al-Kalbi said: He meant by the signs the mountains, so the mountains are signs of the day, and the stars are signs of the night. Mujahed said: He meant by all the stars, some of which are signs and some of which are used to guide people. Al-Suddi said: By the star he meant the Pleiades, the daughters of the bier, the two stars of the sky, and Capricorn, by which one is guided to the roads and the qiblah. Qatada said: God created the stars for three reasons: to be an adornment for the sky, landmarks for roads, and missiles for the devils. Whoever says otherwise has assumed something of which he has no knowledge.
16:17: 17. Is He who creates like He who does not create? meaning: the idols. So will you not remember?
16:18: 18. "And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful for your failure to be grateful for His favors, Merciful" to you as He has given you abundant favors and has not cut them off from you due to your shortcomings and sins.
16:19: 19. And God knows what you conceal and what you declare.
16:20: 20. Those you call upon besides God means: idols. Asim and Yaqub read they call upon with the letter ya. “They do not create anything, and they are created.”
16:21: Dead meaning: the idols not alive and they do not feel meaning: the idols when will they be resurrected, and the Qur'an indicates that the idols will be resurrected and life will be put into them and they will disavow their worshippers. It was said: The infidel idol worshippers do not know when they will be resurrected.
16:22: 22- The Almighty’s saying: “Your God is one God. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial,” denying, and they are arrogant, haughty.
16:23: 23- There is no doubt, truly "that God knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He does not like the arrogant." Abu Saeed Bakr bin Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmi al-Bastami told us, Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman bin Ibrahim bin Sakhtawayh told us, Abu al-Fadl Sufyan bin Muhammad al-Jawhari told us, Ali bin al-Hasan bin Abi Isa al-Hilali told us, Yahya bin Hammad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abaan bin Taghlib, on the authority of Fadil al-Faqimi, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, on the authority of Alqamah bin Qais, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: He who has in his heart an atom’s weight of arrogance will not enter Paradise, and he who has in his heart an atom’s weight of faith will not enter Hell. A man said: O Messenger of God, what if a man likes his clothes to be nice? He said: God is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.”
16:24: 24- And when it is said to them, meaning: to those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and they are the polytheists of Mecca who divided up its punishment, if the pilgrim asks: What has your Lord revealed? they say: Legends of the ancients, their hadiths and falsehoods.
16:25: 25- That they may bear their burdens, the sins of their souls, completely, and perfection was mentioned because the calamities that befall them in this world and the good deeds they do will not atone for them anything on the Day of Resurrection and from the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge, without an argument, so they turn them away from faith, How evil is that which they bear, they bear. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi informed us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni informed us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari informed us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani informed us, Ali bin Hajar informed us, Ismail bin Jaafar informed us, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Abdul-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. And whoever calls to misguidance will have a sin like the sins of those who follow him, without that detracting from their sins in the slightest.” 61. And God will save those who fear Him by means of their attainment. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr read by means of their attainment with an alif for the plural, meaning: by the paths that lead them to victory and salvation. The others read by means of their attainment in the singular because attainment means winning, meaning: He will save them from the Fire by means of their winning through their good deeds. Al-Mubarrad said: The attainment is a verbal noun from the verb to win, and the plural is hasan like happiness and happiness. No harm will touch them, meaning no harm will befall them, nor will they grieve.
16:26: 26- The Almighty said: Those before them plotted, and he is Nimrod bin Canaan, who built the tower in Babylon to ascend to the heavens. Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: The height of the tower in the sky was five thousand cubits. Ka'b Muqatil said: Its length was two leagues, then a wind blew and threw its head into the sea, and the rest of it fell on them while they were under it. When the tower fell, people were confused from fear that day, and they spoke in seventy-three languages, and that is why it was called Babel. The language of the people before that was Syriac, and that is what God Almighty said: So God attacked their building from the foundations meaning: He intended to destroy their building / from its foundations, so the roof fell upon them meaning the top of the houses from above them, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive from their place of safety.
16:27: 27- Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them, humiliate them with torment, and say, ‘Where are My partners about whom you used to quarrel,’ you used to oppose the believers about them, why do they not come and ward off the torment from you? Nafi’ broke the nun of tashaqoon with the addition, and the others opened it. Those who were given knowledge said, [meaning the believers], Indeed, disgrace [meaning humiliation] today and evil [meaning torment] are upon the disbelievers.
16:28: 28- Those whom the angels take in death, their souls are taken by the Angel of Death and his helpers. Hamza read takes in death with a ya' and what came after it was wronging with themselves, by disbelief, and it was accusative as a state, meaning: in a state of their disbelief. "So they threw down their peace" meaning: they surrendered and submitted and said: We were not doing any evil, polytheism, so the angels said to them: Yes, indeed God is Knowing of what you were doing. Ikrimah said: He meant by that those of the disbelievers who were killed at Badr.
16:29: 29- So enter meaning: He said to them, "enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein eternally. How evil is the abode of the arrogant," about faith.
16:30: 30- And it was said to those who feared" This is because the Arab tribes used to send during the season someone to bring them report of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he came, he would ask those who sat on the roads about him, and they would say: A magician, a soothsayer, a poet, a liar, a madman. Why did you not meet him? It is better for you. The questioner would say: I am the worst visitor. If I return to my people without entering Mecca, I will meet him. So he would enter Mecca and see the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they would tell him that he was truthful and that he was a prophet sent. This is what He said: "And it was said to those who feared, 'What has your Lord sent down?' They would say, 'Good.'" Meaning: He sent down good. Then he began by saying: For those who do good in this world is good, an honor from God. Ibn Abbas said: It is doubling the reward to one tenth. Al-Dahhak said: It is victory and conquest. Mujahed said: It is good sustenance. And the home of the Hereafter, meaning the home of the Hereafter, is better and an excellent home for the righteous. Al-Hasan said: It is this world, because the righteous provision themselves for the Hereafter in it. Most of the commentators said: It is Paradise.
16:31: 31-Then he explained it and said: “Gardens of Eden, which they will enter, with rivers flowing beneath them. They will have therein whatever they wish. Thus does God reward the righteous.”
16:32: 32- Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, believing and pure from polytheism. Mujahed said: Their actions and words are pure. It was said: Its meaning is: Their death will be good and easy. They say meaning: the angels to them, “Peace be upon you.” It was said: They convey to them the peace of God, Enter Paradise for what you used to do.
16:33: 33- The Almighty’s saying: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them to seize their souls, or that the command of your Lord should come meaning: the Day of Resurrection, and it was said: the punishment. Thus did those before them meaning: they disbelieved, and God did not wrong them by punishing them, but they were wronging themselves.
16:34: 34- So the evil consequences of what they did befell them, the punishments for their disbelief and their evil deeds, and what they used to ridicule befell them, [came upon them], and befell them.
16:35: 35- And those who associate others with God said, 'If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything besides Him.' Meaning: Al-Bahira, Al-Sa'ibah, Al-Wasilah, and Al-Ham. Had God not been pleased with them for something else and guided us to something else, "Thus did those before them. Is there upon the messengers except the clear notification?" Meaning: They are not to guide, rather they are to convey.
16:36: 36- And We have certainly sent to every nation a messenger meaning: just as We sent to you, Worship God and avoid Taghut meaning everything that is worshipped besides God, And among them were those whom God guided meaning: God guided them to His religion, And among them were those upon whom error was due meaning: it was due by previous decree until they died in their disbelief, So travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied meaning: the outcome of their affair, which is the destruction of their homes through punishment and destruction.
16:37: 37 If you are keen on their guidance, O Muhammad, then God does not guide whomever He leads astray. The people of Kufa read guides with a fat-ha on the ya’ and a kasra on the dal, meaning: God does not guide whomever He leads astray. It was said: Its meaning is that whomever God leads astray is not guided. Others read it with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the dal, meaning whoever God leads astray has no guide, as He said: Whoever God leads astray has no guide (al-A’raf 7:86). And they will have no helpers meaning no one to prevent them from being punished.
16:38: 38- The Almighty said: And they swear by God with their most solemn oaths that God will not resurrect whoever dies, and they deny the resurrection. God Almighty said in response to them: Yes, it is a true promise binding upon Him, but most people do not know.
16:39: 39- To make clear to them that over which they differ. That is, to make clear to them the truth in that over which they differ. And that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars.
16:40: 40- Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. God Almighty says: If We intend to resurrect the dead, then there is no difficulty for Us in bringing them back to life, nor in anything that happens. We only say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, Abu Hurairah told us, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God said: My servant lied to Me, and he had no right to do so, and My servant insulted Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his lying to Me, it is that he says: He will not restore us as We began, and as for his insulting Me, it is that he says: Has God taken a son, while I am the Self-Sufficient, I have not begotten, and there is none comparable to Me.”
16:41: 41- The Almighty’s saying, And those who emigrated for the cause of God after they had been wronged, they were tortured and harmed for the cause of God. It was revealed about Bilal, Suhaib, Khabbab, Ammar, Abis, Jabr, and Abu Jandal bin Suhayl. The polytheists captured them in Mecca and tortured them. Qatada said: They are the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The people of Mecca wronged them and expelled them from their homes until a group of them fled to Abyssinia. Then God settled them in Medina after that, making it a place of migration for them, and He gave them supporters from among the believers. We will surely give them a good place in this world, meaning that He will settle them in Medina. It was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab that when he gave a man [of the immigrants] a gift, he would say: May God bless you in it. This is what God promised you in this world, and what He has stored for you in the Hereafter is better. Then he recited this verse. It was said: Its meaning is that we will treat them well in this world. It was said: The good in this world is success and guidance. And the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew. His statement, if they only knew, refers to the polytheists because the believers knew it.
16:42: 42- Those who are patient, in God’s face for what befell them, and upon their Lord rely.
16:43: 43- And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed, was revealed about the polytheists of Mecca when they denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: God is greater than for His Messenger to be a human being, so why did He not send us an angel? So ask the People of the Reminder, meaning the believers among the People of the Book, if you do not know.
16:44: 44- With clear proofs and scriptures. They differed about the one who brought the preposition with in his statement, with clear proofs. It was said: It refers back to his statement, And We did not send, otherwise it means other than, metaphorically: And We did not send before you with clear proofs/and scriptures other than men to whom revelation was sent, and We did not send angels. It was said: Its interpretation is: We did not send before you except men to whom revelation was sent. We sent them with clear proofs and scriptures. And We have sent down to you the message that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them. By the message He meant revelation, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a clarifier of the revelation, and the clarification of the Book is sought from the Sunnah. And that they may give thought.
16:45: 45- Do those who plotted who committed evil deeds before, meaning: Nimrod bin Canaan and others of the infidels, feel secure that God will not cause the earth to swallow them up or that the punishment will come to them from where they do not perceive?
16:46: 46- Or He seizes them, with punishment, in their changing, their behavior during travels. Ibn Abbas said: in their differences. Ibn Jurayj said: In their advance and retreat, they will not escape, they will outpace God.
16:47: 47- Or He takes them in fear, and fear means diminishing, meaning: He diminishes from their extremities and sides little by little until they all perish. It is said: Time made him fearful and betrayed him: if it diminished him and took his money and his servants. It is said that this is the language of Banu Hudhayl. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi said: From fear, meaning: He punishes a group, and the others fear that what happened to them will happen to them. Indeed, your Lord is Most Kind and Most Merciful, when He did not hasten the punishment.
16:48: 48- The Almighty’s saying: Have they not seen what God has created of things - Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read with a ta’ as a direct address, and likewise in Surat Al-Ankabut, and the others with a ya’, reporting on those who plotted evil deeds - to what God has created of things of an upright body, with a shadow, that provides shade, Abu Amr and Ya’qub read with a ta’ and the others with a ya’. Its shadows, meaning: they tilt and rotate from side to side, so they are in one state at the beginning of the day, then they shrink and then return at the end of the day to another state, prostrating to God, so their tilting and rotation: their prostration to God Almighty. The shade in the evening is called fay’ because it returns from the west to the east, so fay means returning. Prostration means leaning. It is said: The palm tree prostrated when it leaned. The Almighty said: On the right and the left, prostrating to God. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: As for the right, it is the beginning of the day, and the left, it is the end of the day. The shadows prostrate to God. Al-Kalbi said: The shadow before sunrise is to your right, to your left, in front of you, and behind you, and likewise when it sets. When the sun rises, it is in front of you, and when it rises, it is to your right. Those after it are behind you. When it is before the sun sets, it is to your left. This is its shade, its turning, and it is its prostration. Mujahed said: When the sun sets, everything prostrates to God. It was said: What is meant by shadows is the prostration of people. If it is said, why did he unify the right and gather the left? It was said: It is the custom of the Arabs to suffice with one when two signs are combined, as in the Almighty’s saying: God has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing Al-Baqarah 2:7, and His saying: He brings them out from darkness into the light Al-Baqarah 2:257. It was said: The right hand refers to the saying: What God created. The word what is one, and the left hand refers to the meaning. And they are humbled, subdued.
16:49: 49- And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, He only informed of what is due to the predominance of what is not rational over what is rational in number, and the ruling is for the majority like the predominance of the masculine over the feminine, of moving creatures, He meant of every moving creature. It is said: Prostration means obedience, and all things are obedient to God Almighty, from animals to inanimate objects. God Almighty said: They said, ‘We have come in obedience’ (Fussilat 41:11). It was said: The prostration of things is to humble them and make them subservient to what they were intended for and made subservient to. It was said: The prostration of inanimate objects and inanimate objects: the appearance of the effect of creation in it, meaning that it calls the heedless to prostrate when contemplating and pondering it. God Almighty said: We will show them Our signs in the horizons (Fussilat 41:53). And the angels, He specifically mentioned the angels, even though they are among what is in the heavens and the earth, as an honor and elevation of their status. It was said that they came out of the description of creeping, as they have wings with which they fly. It was said that he meant: To God prostrates whatever is in the heavens of angels and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels prostrate. And they are not arrogant.
16:50: 50 - They fear their Lord above them, as He says: And He is the Prevailing over His servants Al-An’am - 18 And they do what they are commanded. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Bakr bin Ibrahim Al-Sha’ranbi told us, Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Dhahali told us, Ubaidullah bin Musa Al-Absi told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Muwarriq, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I see what you do not see, and I hear what you do not hear. The heaven groaned, and it has every right to groan. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, there is no place in it the length of four fingers except that there is an angel in it glorifying God. If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much, and you would not take pleasure in women on your beds, and you would ascend to high places to trade.” Abu Dharr said: I wish I were a tree being cut down. Narrated by Abu Isa on the authority of Ahmad bin Mani’, on the authority of Abu Ahmad Al-Zubairi, on the authority of Israel, who said: Except that there is an angel prostrating to God.
16:51: 51 - The Almighty said: “And God said, ‘Do not take two gods. He is only one God, so fear Me.’”
16:52: 52 - And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him belongs the religion, obedience and sincerity, constantly, always fixed. Meaning: There is no one who is obeyed or obeyed except that this is cut off from him by disappearance or death, except God Almighty, for obedience to Him is continuous and does not end. Do you fear other than God? That is, do you fear? This is a question of denial.
16:53: 53 - The Almighty’s saying: And whatever blessing you have is from God, meaning: Whatever blessing you have is from God. Then when harm befalls you, drought and disease, to Him you cry out, making a commotion and crying out in supplication and seeking help.
16:54: 54 - Then when the hardship is removed from you, at once a party of you associate others with their Lord.
16:55: 55 - So that they may disbelieve, so that they may deny, [and this lam is called the la of the consequence, meaning: the result of their affair is their disbelief] with what We have given them We gave them of blessings and the removal of hardship and calamity, so enjoy yourselves, meaning: live in this world for the period of time that I have specified for you, and you will soon know the outcome of your affair. This is a warning to them.
16:56: 56 - And they assign to that which they have no knowledge, that is, the idols, a share of what We have provided for them, of wealth, which is what they assigned to the idols from their crops and livestock, so they said: This is for God, according to their claim, and this is for our partners. Then he returned from the report to the speech and said: By God, you will be asked, on the Day of Resurrection, about what you used to invent, in this world.
16:57: 57 - And they attribute to God daughters, and they are Khuza'ah and Kinanah. They said: The angels are the daughters of God Almighty: Glory be to Him! And for them is what they desire, meaning: And they attribute to themselves the sons they desire, so ma is in the accusative case, and it is permissible for it to be in the beginning, so ma is in the nominative case.
16:58: 58 - And when one of them is given the report of a female, his face darkens, changing from grief and hatred, and he is filled with grief and anger, and he is filled with sadness and anger, so he suppresses it, meaning: he holds it in and does not show it.
16:59: 59 - He hides i.e. he disappears, from the people because of the bad report he has been given, of sadness and shame, then he thinks: Should he keep it? He mentioned the metaphor in response to what with humiliation i.e. humiliation, or bury it in the dirt i.e. he hides it from him, burying it alive. This is because Mudar, Khuza'ah and Tamim used to bury their daughters alive, fearing poverty for them and the greed of those who were not equal to them. When an Arab man had a daughter and wanted to keep her alive, he would dress her in a wool or hair cloak and leave her to tend his camels and sheep in the desert. If he wanted to kill her, he would leave her until she was six years old. He would say to her mother: Adorn her so that I may take her to her in-laws. He would dig a well for her in the desert. When he reached the well, he would say to her: Look at this well. He would push her from behind into the well, then he would heap dirt on her head until the well was level with the ground. This is what God Almighty said: Will he keep her in humiliation or bury her in the dust? Whenever Sa’sa’a, Al-Farazdaq’s uncle, felt something like that, he would send camels to the girl’s father to revive her with that, so Al-Farazdaq said, boasting about it. My uncle who prevented the birth of the dead, so he revived the dead, so no one was buried alive. How evil is what they judge. How evil is what they judge: daughters are for God and sons for themselves. Similar to this is: Do you have the male and He has the female? That is indeed an unfair division. (al-Najm 53:22). It was also said: How evil is their judgment: burying girls alive.
16:60: 60 - For those who do not believe in the Hereafter, meaning: for those who describe daughters for God and sons for themselves, an evil example, the evil characteristic of needing a child, hating females, and killing them for fear of poverty, and to God is the highest example, the highest characteristic, which is monotheism and that there is no god but Him. It was said: All the attributes of majesty and perfection, such as knowledge, power, permanence, and other attributes. Ibn Abbas said: The worst example: the fire, and the highest example: the testimony that there is no god but God. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
16:61: 61 - And if God were to punish people for their wrongdoing, and to hasten to punish them for their disbelief and disobedience, He would not leave upon it, meaning: upon the earth, a metaphor for something not mentioned, any living creature. Qatada said about the verse: God did that in the time of Noah, so He destroyed everyone on the earth, except for those who were in Noah’s ship, peace be upon him. It was narrated that Abu Hurairah heard a man say: The oppressor harms no one but himself. He said: What a bad thing you have said! The houbara dies in its nest because of the oppression of the oppressor. Ibn Masoud said: The dung beetle is tormented in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam. It was said: The meaning of the verse is: If God were to punish the fathers of the oppressors for their oppression, the lineage would be cut off, and there would be no children, and no one would remain on the earth. But He gives them respite for a specified term, He gives them respite with His patience for a specified term, until the end of their terms and the end of their lives. And when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it.
16:62: 62 - The Almighty’s saying: And they attribute to God that which they hate, for themselves, meaning daughters, and their tongues describe, meaning: they say, the lie that they will have the best, meaning sons. The location of in is accusative in place of the lie. Yaman said: What he means by al-Hasna is Paradise in the afterlife, if Muhammad is truthful about the resurrection. No doubt indeed. Ibn Abbas said: Yes, they will have the Fire in the Hereafter, and they are transgressors. Nafi’ read it with a kasra on the ra’, meaning: extravagant. Abu Jaafar read it with emphasis on the letter Ra and with a kasra, meaning: they neglect God’s command. Others read it with the opening of the letter ra and the lightening of it, meaning: forgotten in the fire, as Ibn Abbas said. Saeed bin Jubair said: They are banished. Muqatil said: They are abandoned. Qatada said: They will be hastened to the fire. Al-Farra’ said: They will be brought to the Fire. This is based on the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will precede you at the Cistern, meaning: I will be ahead of you.
16:63: 63 - By God, We sent to nations before you, just as We sent to this nation, but Satan made their evil deeds seem good to them, “so he is their protector,” their helper, today, and their companion. He called him their protector, for their obedience to him, and for them is a painful punishment, in the Hereafter.
16:64: 64 - And We have not sent down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that in which they differed, of religion and rulings, and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe, meaning: We have not sent down to you the Book except as clarification, guidance, and mercy. So guidance and mercy are connected to His statement that you may make clear.
16:65: 65 - And God sends down water from the sky, meaning: rain, and revives the earth thereby, with plants, after its death, its dryness. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen, the listening of the hearts, not the listening of the ears.
16:66: 66 - And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you, an admonition, We give you drink, with the nun open here and in al-Mu'minun, Ibn Nafi', Ibn Amir, Abu Bakr, Ya'qub, and the rest read it with the damma and they are two dialects. From what is in their bellies, al-Farra' said: The metaphor is returned to the livestock, and the livestock is one. The word na’am is masculine. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: Na’am is masculine and feminine. If it is feminine, then it has the meaning of the plural, and if it is masculine, then it has the same wording.” Al-Kisa’i said: He referred it back to what he meant in the bellies of what we mentioned. The historian said: The metaphor refers to some and part, as if he said: We give you to drink from what is in it, which is milk, since not all of it has milk, and the milk in it is implied. From excrement, which is the weight in the rumen, so if it comes out of it it is not called excrement, and pure milk blood, from blood and excrement that does not have the color of blood nor the smell of prostitution. Pleasing to the drinkers, delicious and flows easily through the throat. It was said: No one has ever choked on milk. Ibn Abbas said: If the animal eats fodder and it settles in its stomach and grinds it, then the bottom of it is excrement, the middle of it is milk, and the top of it is blood, and the liver is in control of it, dividing it by the decree of God Almighty, so the blood flows in the veins, the milk in the udder, and the excrement remains as it is.
16:67: 67 - And from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapevines, meaning: And for you also is a lesson in what We give you to drink and provide for you from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapevines, you take from it, and the metaphor in from it refers back to the omitted what, meaning: what you take from it, intoxicant and good provision. Some people said: Sugar means wine, and good provision means vinegar, raisins, dates, and syrup. They said: This was before wine was forbidden. This is what Ibn Masoud, Ibn Omar, Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan, and Mujahid agreed with. Al-Shaabi said: Sugar is what you drink, and good provision is what you eat. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Sugar is vinegar, in the language of Abyssinia. Some of them said: Sugar is intoxicating wine, which is the infusion of dates and raisins when it becomes strong, and cooked juice, which is the saying of Al-Dahhak and Al-Nakha’i. Those who permit drinking wine and those who forbid it say: The meaning of the verse is information, not permissibility. The first of the sayings is that his statement: You take from it intoxicant is abrogated. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Intoxicant is what is forbidden from its fruit, and good provision is what is permissible. Abu Ubaidah said: Sugar: taste. It is said: This is sugar for you, meaning: taste. There is certainly in that a sign for a people who understand.
16:68: 68 - “And your Lord inspired the bee,” meaning: He inspired it and cast it into their souls, so they understood it. The bees are honey bees, the singular of which is a bee. That you may build houses in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they erect. They build. It is customary for its people to build places for it, so that it may take refuge in them. Ibn Zayd said: They are the vineyards.
16:69: 69 - Then eat of all the fruits. The meaning of all does not mean generality, and it is like the Almighty’s saying: And you have been given of all things (al-Naml 27:23). So follow the ways of your Lord submissively. It was said: It is an attribute of the paths, meaning: They are submissive to bees and easy to walk on. Mujahed said: No place is difficult for her to walk. Others said: Docile is an attribute of the bee, meaning: obedient and led by subjugation. It is said that its owners move it from one place to another and it has a beekeeper who, if it stops, stops and if it walks, it walks. There comes forth from their bellies a drink, meaning honey. Its colors vary, white, red, and yellow. In it is healing for people, meaning in honey. Mujahid said: meaning in the Qur’an, but the first is more appropriate. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir informed us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad informed us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi informed us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan informed us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj informed us, Muhammad bin Muthanna informed us, Muhammad bin Ja`far informed us, Shu`bah informed us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Al-Mutawakkil, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My brother has abdominal pain. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give him honey to drink. So he gave him honey to drink. Then he came and said: I gave him honey to drink, but it only made his abdominal pain worse. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said this to him three times. Then he came a fourth time and said: Give him honey to drink. He said: I gave him honey to drink, but it only made his abdominal pain worse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has spoken the truth and your brother’s stomach has lied. So he gave him honey to drink and he was cured.” Ibn Masoud said: Honey is a cure for every disease, and the Qur’an is a cure for what is in the chests. It was narrated that he said: You should use two cures: the Qur’an and honey. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
16:70: 70 - And God created you, then He takes you as children, young men, or adults, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age, the worst of it. Muqatil said: meaning old age. Qatada said: The most decrepit age is ninety years. It was narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: The most decrepit age is seventy-five years. It was also said: eighty years. So that he may not know anything after his knowledge, so that he may not understand anything after his first understanding, Indeed, God is Knowing and Competent. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Ismail informed us, [Musa bin Ismail informed us], Harun bin Musa informed us, Abdullah Al-Awar informed us, on the authority of Shu’aib, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate: I seek refuge in You from miserliness, laziness, the worst part of life, the torment of the grave, the trial of the Antichrist, and the trial of life and death.
16:71: 71 - And God has favored some of you over others in provision. He has made things easy for one and difficult for another, and has made things less and more. So those who prefer My provision over those whom their right hands possess, of slaves, are equal therein, meaning: until they and their slaves are equal in that. God Almighty says: They are not pleased that they and their slaves should be equal in what I have provided for them, and they have made My slaves partners in My dominion and authority. This requires proof against the polytheists. Qatada said: This is an example given by God Almighty. Is there anyone among you who shares his wife, bed, and wealth with his slave? Do you consider God’s creation and His servants equal? Do they then deny the favor of God? by associating others with Him. Abu Bakr read it with a ta’ because of his statement, And God has favored some of you over others in provision, and the others read it with a ya’ because of his statement, So they are equal therein.
16:72: 72 - The Almighty said: And God has made for you mates from among yourselves, meaning: women. He created from Adam his wife Eve. It was said: from among yourselves meaning: from your kind, mates. And He has given you from your wives sons and grandchildren. Ibn Masoud and Al-Nakha’i said: The grandchildren are a man’s two sisters over his daughters. And on the authority of Ibn Masoud also: They are the in-laws, so the meaning of the verse according to this statement is: And He made for you from your wives sons and daughters, whom you marry and because of them you have sisters and in-laws. Akrima, Al-Hasan, and Al-Dahhak said: They are the servants. Mujahed said: They are the helpers. Whoever helps you has protected you. Ata' said: They are the man's grandchildren, who help him and serve him. Qatada said: A profession in which they practice and serve you from among your children. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: The sons are the young ones, and the grandchildren are the older children who help him in his work. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are the children’s children. Al-Awfi narrated on his authority: They are the sons of a man’s wife, not his. And He has provided you with good things of blessings and lawful things. So is it in falsehood meaning idols, that they believe and in the favor of God they disbelieve? Meaning monotheism and Islam. It was said: Falsehood: Satan, he ordered them to prohibit the Bahira and the Sa’iba, and by the grace of God meaning: by what God has made permissible for them they disbelieve: they deny its permissibility.
16:73: 73 - And they worship besides God that which possesses no provision for them from the heavens, meaning the rain, or the earth, meaning the plants, anything. Al-Akhfash said: It is a substitute for provision, meaning: that they possess no provision at all, little or much. Al-Farra’ said: “He put ‘something’ in the accusative case because of the provision being bestowed upon him, meaning: he is not provided with anything, ‘nor are they able’, and they are not able to do anything, mentioning the inability of idols to provide benefit or ward off harm.”
16:74: 74 - So do not make comparisons for God, meaning: similarities. So you liken Him to His creation, and make a partner for Him, for He is One and has no equal. Indeed, God knows and you do not know, the error of what you make of comparisons. Then He made a comparison [for the disbelievers and the believers], and He, the Most High, said:
16:75: 75 - "God sets forth a parable: a slave owned by someone who has no power over anything." This is the parable of the disbeliever. God has given him wealth, but he does not do any good with it. And whoever We have provided with good provision from Us, he spends from it secretly and publicly. This is the parable of the believer. God has given him wealth, so he works with it in obedience to God, and spends it in pleasing God, secretly and publicly, so God rewards him for it with Paradise. Are they equal? He did not say equal because of the word from and they are a noun that is suitable for one, two, and plural. Likewise, His saying they are not able in the plural because of what. Meaning: Is this miserly poor person the same as the generous rich person? Likewise, the disobedient infidel is not the same as the obedient believer. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ata’ regarding his statement: A slave owned, meaning Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, And he whom We have provided from Us with a good provision, meaning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. Then he said: Praise be to God, but most of them do not know. He says, “It is not as you say. The idols have no hand in it, nor any favor for which they should be praised. Rather, complete praise is to God Almighty, because He is the Benefactor, the Creator, and the Provider. But most of the disbelievers do not know.” Then he gave an example of the idols, saying:
16:76: 76 - "And God presents an example: two men, one of them mute, unable to do anything, and he is a burden on his master." Each: a burden and a burden on his master his cousin, and those under his authority. Wherever he directs him he sends him he brings no good, because he does not understand what is said to him, nor is it understood from him. This is like idols, they do not hear, nor speak, nor understand. And he is a burden on his master his worshipper, he needs to be carried, placed, and served. Is he equal to one who commands justice? meaning: God Almighty is able, speaking, commanding monotheism, and he is on a straight path. [Al-Kalbi said: meaning he guides you to a straight path. It was said: He is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who commands justice and is on the straight path. It was said: Both examples are for the believer and the unbeliever. It was narrated by Atiyah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ata’ said: The mute one: Abi bin Khalaf, and the one who commands justice: Hamza, Othman bin Affan, and Othman bin Maz’un. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Hashim bin Amr bin Al-Harith bin Rabi’ah Al-Qurashi, who was not very good and was hostile to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: It was revealed about Uthman bin Affan and his freedman. Uthman used to spend on him, and his freedman hated Islam. 43- The Day they emerge from the graves, from the tombs, in haste, to answer the caller, as if they were to a target, Ibn Amir, Ibn Abbas, and Hafs read: target with a damma on the noon and the sad, and the others read it with a fatha on the noon and a sukoon on the sad, meaning to something set up, it is said: So-and-so is a target for my eyes. Al-Kalbi said: to a flag and a banner. And whoever reads it with a damma, Muqatil and Al-Kisa’i said: meaning to their idols that they used to worship besides God, like His statement: And that which was sacrificed on stone altars (al-Ma’idah 5:3). Al-Hasan said: They hasten to it, whichever of them will take it first, they hasten, they hasten.
16:77: 77 - “And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And the matter of the Hour is not but as the twinkling of an eye,” when He says to it Be and it is, or it is nearer, rather it is nearer, Indeed, God is over all things competent, it was revealed about the disbelievers who hasten the Resurrection in mockery.
16:78: 78 - The Almighty said: And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, Al-Kisa’i read the wombs of your mothers with a kasra on the hamza, and Hamza read it with a kasra on the meem and the hamza, and the rest read it with a damma on the hamza and a fatha on the meem, You do not know anything, the speech was completed, then He began and said, the Almighty: And He gave you hearing, sight, and hearts, because God Almighty made these things for them before they emerged from the wombs of their mothers, and He only gave them knowledge after they emerged, that you may be grateful, the blessing of God.
16:79: 79 - Have they not seen? Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Yaqub read it with a ta', and the rest read it with a ya', because of his saying: And they worship. To the birds are subjected, tamed, in the atmosphere of the sky, which is the air between the sky and the earth. On the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar, that the birds rise twelve miles, and nothing rises above this, and above the atmosphere is the sky, and above the sky is the sky. What holds them up in the air “except God. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.”
16:80: 80 - And God has made for you from your houses [which are made of stone and mud] a dwelling place meaning: a dwelling in which you live, and He has made for you from the hides of cattle, houses meaning tents, domes, tents, and pavilions made of carpets and leather, which you find light meaning: their load is light for you, on the day of your departure your journey on your journey, Ibn Amir and the people of Kufa read it with a sukoon on the ‘ayn, and the others read it with a fatha, which is the more eloquent of the two languages, and on the day of your residence in your country, it is not burdensome for you in either case. And from their wool, fur, and hair, meaning: the wool of sheep, the fur of camels, and the hair of goats, and the metaphors refer to livestock, furniture, Ibn Abbas said: money, Mujahid said: goods. Al-Qatibi said: Furnishings: all money, including camels, sheep, slaves, and goods. Another said: It is the household furnishings, such as furniture and blankets. And for enjoyment, as provision from which they benefit, for a time, meaning death. It was also said: until it wears out.
16:81: 81 - And God has made for you, from what He has created, shades that you can take shelter under from the intense heat, and they are the shades of buildings and trees, and has made for you shelters in the mountains, meaning: the flocks, and the two ghīrs, the singular of which is kan, and has made for you garments shirts of linen, silk, and wool, to protect you, to prevent you from the heat. The scholars of meaning said: He meant the heat and the cold, so He was satisfied with mentioning one of them because the speech indicates it. "And garments: to protect you from your violence", meaning: the armor, and the battle: war, meaning: the weapons protect you from your violence from striking you. Thus does He complete His favor upon you that you may submit, that is, be sincere in your obedience to Him. Ata Al-Khurasani said: The Qur’an was revealed according to their knowledge. He said: And He has made for you shelters in the mountains. He did not make for them more and greater plains, but they were people of mountains, as He said: And of their wool and their fur and their hair, because they were people of fur and hair. And as He said: And He sends down from the sky, from mountains, hail. (al-Nur 24:43) What was sent down of snow was more, but they did not know snow. He said: To protect you from the heat, and what protects from the cold was more, but they were people of heat.
16:82: 82 - If they turn away, if they turn away, then there is no blame or any sign of negligence on you for that, for upon you is only the clear notification.
16:83: 83 - They know the blessing of God, Al-Suddi said, meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then they deny it, they lie about him. Some people said: It is Islam. Jahid and Qatada said: It means that what is counted for them of blessings in this surah, they acknowledge that it is from God, then if it is said to them: Give charity and comply with God’s command in it, they deny it and say: We inherited it from our fathers. Al-Kalbi said: When he mentioned these blessings to them, they said: Yes, all of these are from God, but they are through the intercession of our gods. Awf bin Abdullah said: It is a man saying, If it weren’t for so-and-so, such-and-such would have happened, and if it weren’t for so-and-so, such-and-such would not have happened. “And most of them are disbelievers,” the deniers.
16:84: 84 - The Almighty said: And the Day We raise up from every nation a witness, meaning a messenger, then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved, in apology, and it was said: in the speech at all, nor will they be asked to repent, seeking to please, meaning: they will not be charged to please their Lord, because the afterlife is not a place of accountability, and they will not return to this world to repent. The true meaning of seeking to please is: it is the exposure to seeking to please, and this door is closed in the afterlife to the disbelievers.
16:85: 85 - And when those who did wrong see the punishment, meaning Hell, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
16:86: 86 - And when those who associated others with God will see their partners on the Day of Resurrection, they will say, ‘Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You,’ meaning the idols, so they will throw the word to them, meaning the idols, indeed, you are liars, in calling us gods whom we did not call you to worship.
16:87: 87 - And they will cast, meaning the polytheists, “to God on that Day peace,” they will surrender and submit to His judgment over them, and their gods will not avail them at all, and what they used to invent will be lost, and removed, from them, that she would intercede for them.
16:88: 88 - Those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God, prevented people from the path of truth, We will increase for them punishment upon punishment, Abdullah said: Scorpions with fangs like tall palm trees. Saeed bin Jubair said: Snakes like camels, and scorpions like mules, one of which stings so hard that its owner feels its protection for forty autumns. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: It means five rivers of molten brass like fire flowing from beneath the Throne, in which they will be tormented, three for the length of the night and two for the length of the day. It was said: They come out from the heat of the fire to the cold of the freezing cold, and they rush to the fire from the severity of the freezing cold, seeking help from it. It was said: Their punishment will be doubled because they were corrupting in this world through disbelief and turning people away from faith.
16:89: 89 - And the Day We will raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, meaning their prophet from among themselves, because prophets were sent to nations from among themselves. And We have brought you, O Muhammad, as a witness over these, to whom you were sent. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification, clarification, for everything, needed of commands and prohibitions, lawful and unlawful, limits and rulings, and as guidance, from misguidance, and as mercy and good tidings, good report, for the Muslims.
16:90: 90 - The Almighty said: God commands justice, fairness, and doing good, to people. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: Justice means monotheism, and goodness means performing the obligatory duties. On his authority: Ihsan: Sincerity in monotheism, and this is the meaning of the Prophet’s saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ihsan is to worship God as if you see Him. Muqatil said: Justice means monotheism, and benevolence means forgiving people. And giving to relatives means maintaining family ties. And he forbids indecency means ugly speech and action. Ibn Abbas said: adultery, and wrongdoing means what is not known in the Sharia or Sunnah, and oppression means arrogance and injustice. Ibn Uyaynah said: Justice is the equality of secret and public, goodness is that his secret is better than his public, and immorality and evil is that his public is better than his secret. He admonishes you that you may remember. Ibn Masoud said: The most comprehensive verse in the Qur’an is this verse. Ayyub said on the authority of Ikrimah: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to Al-Walid: ‘God commands justice’ to the end of the verse, and he said to him: ‘O son of my brother, repeat it.’ So he repeated it to him, and he said: ‘By God, it has sweetness and freshness, its top is fruitful and its bottom is abundant, and it is not the speech of humans.’”
16:91: 91 - The Almighty said: And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant, and the covenant here is: the oath. Al-Sha’bi said: A covenant is an oath, and its expiation is the expiation of an oath. And do not break oaths after confirming them, meaning emphasizing them, so that you break them, and you have made God a guarantor over you, meaning a witness to fulfillment. God knows what you do. They differed about who this verse was revealed to, even if its ruling is general. It was said: It was revealed about those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God commanded them to fulfill it. Mujahid and Qatada said: It was revealed about the oath of the people of ignorance. Then God gave an example of breaking a covenant, saying:
16:92: 92 - And do not be like the one who undoes her spinning after it has been strong, meaning: after spinning it and making it firm. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: She was a clumsy, foolish woman from Quraysh, called Raytah bint Amr ibn Sa`d ibn Ka`b ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim, and she was nicknamed Ja`r. She had a bad temper, and she had a spindle the size of an arm, a hook the size of a finger, and a large spindle, the same size, and she used to spin yarn from wool, hair, and fur, and she would order her slave girls to do so, so they would spin from morning until noon, and when noon came, she would order them to undo everything they had spun, and this was her habit. Meaning: It did not stop working, nor did it stop breaking it when it worked. Likewise, if you break a covenant, you will not stop working, nor will you fulfill it when you make a covenant. Ankathan means ruins, the singular of which is nakth, which is what was unraveled after spinning, whether it was yarn or rope. You take your oaths as a means of deception among you, meaning: deception, treachery, and trickery. Deception is what enters into something for the purpose of corruption. It was said: Income and deception: to show loyalty and conceal breach. That there be means: that there be a nation that is more numerous meaning: more and higher, than a nation. Mujahid said: This is because they used to make alliances with allies, and if they found a people who were more numerous and more powerful than them, they would break their alliance with them and make an alliance with the more powerful. So its meaning is: You sought power by breaking the covenant, such that one nation was more numerous than another nation. So God forbade them from that. God is only testing you with it, God chooses you by commanding you to fulfill the covenant, and He will make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ in this world.
16:93: 93 - And if God had willed, He could have made you one nation, on one religion, which is Islam, but He sends astray whom He wills, by letting them down, out of His justice, and guides whom He wills, by granting them success, out of His grace, and you will surely be asked about what you used to do, on the Day of Resurrection.
16:94: 94 - And do not take your oaths as a means of deception and corruption among yourselves, deceiving and corrupting people with them, so that they are content with your oaths and feel secure, then you break them, so that your foot slips after it was firmly established, so that you perish after you were secure. The Arabs say to every afflicted person after being well, or someone who falls into trouble after being safe: his foot slipped, and taste the evil because you have averted from the path of God, it was said: its meaning is: you made the path of breaking the covenant easy for people by breaking the covenant, and for you is a great punishment.
16:95: 95 - And do not exchange the covenant of God for a small price, meaning do not break your covenants, seeking a small worldly gain by breaking them, but fulfill them. Indeed, with God is, of the reward for you for fulfilling them, best for you, if you only knew [the difference between the two exchanges, then he explained that]. So he said:
16:96: 96 - What you have will perish meaning: the world and what is in it will perish, but what is with God is everlasting. “And We will surely reward those who were patient,” [Abu Ja`far, Ibn Kathir, and `Asim read with a nun, and the rest with a ya’] with the best of what they used to do. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Amr bin Abi Amr, the client of Al-Muttalib, told us, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever loves his worldly life will harm his afterlife, and whoever loves his afterlife will harm his worldly life, so prefer what remains over what perishes.
16:97: 97 - The Almighty said: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life. Saeed bin Jubair and Ata’ said: It is lawful sustenance. Al-Hassan said: It is contentment. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: It means living in obedience. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: It is the sweetness of obedience. Mujahid and Qatada said: It is Paradise. Aouf narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan. He said: Life is not pleasant for anyone except in Paradise. And We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.
16:98: 98 - The Almighty’s saying: So when you recite the Qur’an, meaning: you want to recite the Qur’an, then seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed, like the Almighty’s saying: When you rise to prayer, wash (al-Ma’idah 5:6) Seeking refuge is a Sunnah when reading the Qur’an. Most scholars agree that seeking refuge in God comes before reading. Abu Hurairah said: After that. Its wording is to say: I seek refuge in God from Satan the accursed. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Shu’bah bin Amr bin Marra told us, I heard Asim from Ibn Jubayr bin Mut’im, from his father, that he “saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying. He said: So he said: God is most great, most great, three times, [and praise be to God abundantly, three times, and glory be to God in the morning and evening, three times.] O God, I seek refuge in You from the accursed Satan, from his insinuations, his puffing, and his spitting.” Amr said: Nafakh: arrogance, Nafth: poetry, Hamza: death, death is madness, and seeking refuge in God is holding fast to Him.
16:99: 99 - He has no authority, argument and authority, over those who believe and put their trust in their Lord, Sufyan said: He has no authority to force them to commit a sin and not forgive.
16:100: 100 - His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian, who obey him and enter under his authority, and those who associate others with Him, meaning: they associate others with God. It was said: The metaphor refers to Satan, and its metaphor is those who, because of him, associate others with God.
16:101: 101 - "And if We substitute a verse for another verse, meaning if We abrogate the ruling of a verse and substitute another ruling in its place, and God knows best what He sends down, He knows best what is best for His creation in what He changes and alters of His rulings, they say, 'You are only a fabricator,' O Muhammad, who fabricates," that is because the polytheists said: Muhammad mocks his companions, he commands them today to do something and forbids them from it tomorrow, he is nothing but a fabricator, by saying it on his own. God Almighty said: But most of them do not know. The truth of the Qur’an, and the clarification of the abrogating and the abrogated.
16:102: 102 - “Say: It was sent down from your Lord in truth,” meaning the Qur’an, by the Holy Spirit, Gabriel, to strengthen those who believe, meaning: to strengthen the hearts of the believers so that they may increase in faith and certainty, and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims.
16:103: 103- And We certainly know that they say, 'It is only a human being who teaches him,' a human being, and it is not from God. They differed about this human being: Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught a blacksmith in Mecca whose name was Balaam, and he was a Christian, with a foreign tongue. The polytheists would see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entering and leaving him, and they would say, It is only Balaam who teaches him. Ikrimah said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to teach a boy of Banu al-Mughira called Ya’ish, and he used to read the books. So the Quraysh said: Only Ya’ish teaches him. Al-Farra’ said: The polytheists said that he only learned from Ayesh, a slave of Huwaytib bin Abdul-Uzza, who had converted to Islam and had converted to Islam well, but was a mute. Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as I have been told, often used to sit at Al-Marwah with a Roman Christian slave, a slave of some of the Banu Al-Hadrami. We had two slaves from the people of Ain Al-Tamr, one of whom was called Yasar, and was nicknamed Abu Fakiha, and the other was called Jabr. They used to make swords in Mecca, and they used to recite the Torah and the Gospel. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would often pass by them while they were reciting, and he would stop and listen. Ad-Dahhak said: When the infidels harmed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would sit with them and find comfort in their conversation. The polytheists said: Muhammad only learns from them, so this verse was revealed. God Almighty said, in refutation of them: The tongue of the one they incline towards, that is, they incline towards it and point to it, is foreign. Ajami is the one who does not speak clearly, even if he lives in the desert. Ajami is attributed to the non-Arabs, even if he is eloquent. A Bedouin is a Bedouin, and an Arab is attributed to the Arabs, even if he is not eloquent. And this is a clear Arabic tongue, eloquent. He meant by the tongue the Qur’an, and the Arabs say: language is a tongue. It was narrated that the man they were pointing to converted to Islam and his conversion to Islam was good.
16:104: 104 - Indeed, those who do not believe in the verses of God - God will not guide them, God will not direct them, and they will have a painful punishment, then God Almighty informed us that the disbelievers are the slanderers.
16:105: 105 - He said: Only those who do not believe in the verses of God invent lies, and it is those who are the liars. No, O Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If it is said: He said: Only those who do not believe in God invent lies, then what is the meaning of his saying and it is those who are the liars? It was said: He only fabricates lies: reporting their actions, and they are the liars is an attribute that is necessary for them, like a man saying to another: You lied and you are a liar, meaning: You lied in this statement, and it is your habit to lie. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Hafs Umar bin Ahmad Al-Jawhari told us, my grandfather Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Umar bin Hafs told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Faraj Al-Azraq told us, Saeed bin Abdul Hamid bin Ja’far told us, Ya’la bin Al-Ashdaq told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Jarad, who said: “I said: O Messenger of God, does a believer commit adultery? He said: It could happen. He said: Does a believer steal? He said: It could happen. I said: Does a believer lie? He said: No. God said: ‘Only those who do not believe in the verses of God invent falsehood.’”
16:106: 106 - Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief, except for one who is forced. Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed about Ammar, because the polytheists took him, his father Yasir, his mother Sumayyah, Suhayb, Bilal, Khabbab, and Salim, and tortured them. As for Sumayyah, she tied two camels together and a spear was brought before her and she was killed, and her husband Yasir was killed, and they were the first two people killed in Islam. As for Ammar, he gave them what they wanted with his tongue, under duress. Qatada said: “The Banu al-Mughira took Ammar and threw him into the well of Maymun and said to him: Disbelieve in Muhammad. He followed them in that, but his heart was averse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed that Ammar had disbelieved, so he said: No, Ammar is full of faith from his head to his feet, and faith has mixed with his flesh and blood. Ammar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, crying, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is wrong with you? He said: Evil, O Messenger of God, I spoke ill of you and mentioned your gods. He said: How did you find your heart? He said: Reassured by faith. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped his eyes and said: If they return to you, then return to them what you said.” So this verse was revealed. Mujahid said: It was revealed about some people from Mecca who believed, so some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them to emigrate, for we do not see you as one of us until you emigrate to us. So they left, intending to go to Medina, but the Quraysh caught up with them on the way, so they disbelieved reluctantly. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Jabr, the freed slave of Amir ibn al-Hadrami. His master forced him to disbelieve, so he disbelieved under duress. And his heart is at rest with faith. Then Jabr’s freed slave converted to Islam, and his conversion was good, and Jabr migrated with his master. But whoever opens his breast to disbelief meaning, opens his breast to disbelief by accepting it and chooses it, upon them is wrath from God, and for them is a great punishment. Scholars agreed that if someone is forced to say a word of disbelief, it is permissible for him to say it with his tongue. If he says it with his tongue without believing it, it is not disbelief. If he refuses to say it until he is killed, that is better. Scholars differed regarding the divorce of a person under duress. Most of them said that it does not take place.
16:107: 107 - That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter, and because God does not guide the disbelieving people, He does not guide them.
16:108: 108 - “Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing and sight God has sealed. And it is those who are the heedless,” of what is intended for them.
16:109: 109 - There is no doubt that in the Hereafter they will be the losers, meaning the ones who are deceived.
16:111: 111 - On the Day every soul will come disputing, arguing and protesting, for itself, for what it did of good and evil, preoccupied with it and not devoting itself to anything else, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and they will not be wronged. It was narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab said to Ka`b al-Ahbar: We feared you. He said: “O Commander of the Faithful, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you were to meet on the Day of Resurrection with the deeds of seventy prophets, hours would pass and you would not be concerned with anything but yourself. Hell will have a sigh that will cause no close angel or chosen prophet to remain but that he will fall on his knees, even Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, who will say: ‘O Lord, I ask You for nothing but myself.’” The confirmation of that is what God revealed to you: The Day every soul will come pleading for itself. Narrated Akrima from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said: The disputes between people will continue on the Day of Resurrection until the soul disputes with the body. The soul will say: O Lord, I had no hand with which to hold, no foot with which to walk, and no eye with which to see. The body will say: You created me like wood, with no hand with which to hold, no foot with which to walk, and no eye with which to see. So this came like a ray of light, and through it my tongue spoke, my eyes saw, and my feet walked. So God gives them an example: A blind man and a crippled man entered a garden in which there were fruits. The blind man could not see the fruit, and the crippled man could not reach it. So the blind man carried the crippled man and they ate some of the fruit, so the punishment will be upon them.
16:112: 112 - The Almighty said: “And God presents an example: a city that was secure,” meaning: Mecca, it was secure, its people were not attacked or raided, “at peace,” stable with its people, they did not need to move to seek refuge as the rest of the Arabs needed, its provision comes to it in abundance from every place, it is brought to it from land and sea, similar to: the fruits of all things are brought to it Al-Qasas - 57.
