So it denied the favors of God, the plural of favor, and it was said: the plural of blessings like badly and worst, “so God made it taste the garment of hunger,” God afflicted them with hunger for seven years, and the Arabs cut off their provisions by the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they were exhausted and ate burnt bones, carcasses, dead dogs, and wool, which is hair treated with blood, until one of them would look at the sky and see something like smoke from hunger. Then the leaders of Mecca spoke to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: This You have become hostile to men, so what about women and children? So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave permission to the people to carry food to them while they were still polytheists. He mentioned clothing because what had befallen them of emaciation and pallor and the change in their appearance from what they had been like before was like clothing to them, and fear, meaning: the expeditions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his raiding parties that would surround them. Because of what they were doing.
16:113: 113 - And there had certainly come to them a Messenger from among themselves, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.
16:114: 114 - So eat of what God has provided for you [that is] lawful and good, and be grateful for the favor of God, if it is Him that you worship.
16:115: 115 - “He has only forbidden you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limits] - then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.”
16:116: 116 - The Almighty said: And do not say about what your tongues describe as falsehood, meaning: do not say, as a description of your tongues, or because of your description of falsehood, meaning: that you permit and prohibit for the sake of falsehood and not for anything else, This is lawful and this is forbidden, meaning the bahīrah and the sā’ibah, to invent a lie against God, so that you say that God has commanded us to do this, Indeed, those who invent a lie against God will not succeed, they will not escape the punishment of God.
16:117: 117 - A little enjoyment, meaning: they have little enjoyment, or they have little enjoyment in this world. And for them is a painful punishment, in the Hereafter.
16:118: 118 - And We have forbidden to those who are Jews what We have related to you before, meaning in Surat Al-An’am, which is the Almighty’s saying: And We have forbidden to those who are Jews all animals having claws Al-An’am - 146 the verse. And We did not wrong them by forbidding it to them, but they were wronging themselves so We forbade it to them because of their transgression.
16:119: 119 - Then indeed, your Lord, to those who did evil in ignorance and then repented after that and reformed, the meaning of reform: steadfastness in repentance, indeed, your Lord, after that, meaning: after ignorance, is Forgiving and Merciful.
16:120: 120 - The Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was a nation. Ibn Masoud said: The nation is a teacher of goodness, meaning: he was a teacher of goodness, and the people of the world followed his example. He combined in him the praiseworthy qualities that are combined in a nation. Mujahed said: He was the only believer, and all the people were infidels. Qatada said: There is no religion among the people who do not follow it and are pleased with it. Obeying God, obedient to Him. It was also said: carrying out the commands of God Almighty. Hanif, a Muslim, upright in the religion of Islam. It was also said: sincere. And he was not of the polytheists.
16:121: 121 - Grateful for His blessings, He chose him, “and guided him to a straight path,” meaning: to the religion of truth.
16:122: 122 - And We gave him good in this world, meaning the message and friendship. It was also said: the tongue of truth and good praise. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: It means the prayers in the saying of this nation: O God, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham. It was said: righteous children in old age. It was said: General acceptance in all nations. And indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous, with his righteous fathers in Paradise. There is an inversion in the verse, meaning: And We gave him good in this world and the Hereafter, and indeed, he is among the righteous.
16:123: 123 - Then We revealed to you, O Muhammad, that you follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, a pilgrim who is a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists. The scholars of the principles of jurisprudence said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to follow the law of Abraham, except for what was abrogated in his law, and what was not abrogated became his law.
16:124: 124 - The Almighty’s saying: The Sabbath was only made for those who differed about it. It was said: Its meaning is that the Sabbath was only made a curse for those who differed about it, meaning: they opposed it. It was said: Its meaning is that God did not impose on them the glorification and prohibition of the Sabbath except on those who differed about it, meaning: they disagreed about it. Some people said: It is the greatest of days, because God Almighty finished creating things on Friday, then He made the Sabbath the Sabbath. Some people said: Rather, the greatest day is Sunday, because God Almighty began the creation of things on it, so they chose to glorify something other than what God imposed on them, and God imposed on them the glorification of Friday. Al-Kalbi said: Moses, peace be upon him, ordered them to observe Friday, and he said: Dedicate one day to God every seven days, so worship Him on Friday, and do not work on it for your craft, and six days for your craft. But they refused and said: We only want the day on which God was free from creation, Saturday. So he made that day for them and made it difficult for them. Then Jesus, peace be upon him, came to them with Friday, and they said: We do not want their holiday to be after our holiday - meaning the Jews - so they adopted Sunday. So God gave Friday to this nation, and they accepted it and were blessed in it. Abu Ali Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah told us, on the authority of Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection. However, they were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them. This is their day which was imposed upon them and they differed over it, so God guided us to it, so they follow us on it. So the Jews will be tomorrow and the Christians the day after tomorrow.” God Almighty said: The Sabbath was only made obligatory for those who differed about it. [Qatada said: Those who differed about it were] the Jews. Some of them considered it permissible and some of them forbade it. And your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
16:125: 125 - Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom, with the Qur’an, and good instruction, meaning the sermons of the Qur’an. It was said: Good advice is a call to God with encouragement and intimidation. It was said: It is soft and gentle speech without harshness or harshness. And argue with them in a way that is best, and argue with them and debate with them in the best way, meaning: ignore their harm, and do not fall short in conveying the message and calling to the truth. This was abrogated by the verse on fighting. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided.
16:126: 126 - And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. These verses were revealed in Medina regarding the martyrs of Uhud. When the Muslims saw what the polytheists did to their dead on the day of Uhud, by slitting open their bellies and mutilating them badly - until none of the dead Muslims remained who were not mutilated except Hanzalah ibn al-Rahib, for his father Abu Amir al-Rahib was with Abu Sufyan, so they left Hanzalah for that reason - the Muslims said when they saw that: If God gives us victory over them, we will increase their actions and mutilate them in a way that no Arab has ever done to anyone. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood over his uncle Hamza ibn Abdul Muttalib, and they had cut off his nose and ear, cut off his testicles, and slit open his stomach. Hind bint Utbah took a piece of his liver, chewed it, and moistened it to eat it. It did not remain in her stomach until she threw it away. This reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said: If she had eaten it, she would never have entered the Fire. Hamza is too honorable in the sight of God Almighty to have anything of his body enter the Fire. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at his uncle Hamza, and looked at something that he had never looked at before, it was more painful to his heart than it. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on you, for you know that you were nothing but a doer of good deeds and a maintainer of kinship. Were it not for the grief that came after you for me, I would have been happy to leave you. Until you are gathered from different groups. By God, if God gives me victory over them, I will mutilate seventy of them in your place. Then God Almighty revealed: And if you punish, then punish verse. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient verse. That is: And if you pardon, it is better for those who pardon. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, we will be patient, and he refrained from what he wanted and atoned for his oath. Ibn Abbas and Al-Dahhak said: This was before the revelation of Bara’ah, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered fighting those who fought him and forbade initiating fighting. Then, when God strengthened Islam and its people, Bara’ah was revealed, and they were ordered to wage jihad, and this verse was abrogated. Al-Nakha’i, Al-Thawri, Mujahid, and Ibn Sirin said: The verse is decisive and was revealed regarding the one who is wronged by injustice. It is not permissible for him to take from his oppressor more than the oppressor took from him. It commands retribution and forgiveness, and forbids aggression. Then He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace:
16:127: 127 - And be patient, and your patience is not but through God, meaning: with the help and guidance of God, and do not grieve over them, in their turning away from you, and do not be in distress over what they are plotting, meaning: over what they have done of actions. Ibn Kathir read here and in An-Naml narrow with a kasra on the letter dhad, while others read it with a fatha on the letter dhad. The people of Kufa said: They are two dialects, like ratl and ratl. Abu Amr said: Al-Daiq with the fat-ha: sorrow, and with the kasra: severity. Abu Ubaidah said: Distress with a kasra is in the scarcity of livelihood and housing, but as for what is in the heart and chest, it is with a fatha. Ibn Qutaybah said: Distress is a softening of the word, like easy and easy, and soft and soft. So, based on this, it is an adjective, as if he said: Do not be in a difficult situation because of their deceit.
16:128: 128 - Indeed, God is with those who fear Him, the prohibitions, and those who do good, with help and support.
17:1: 1- Meccan and has one hundred and eleven verses. Glory be to Him who took His servant by night. Glory be to God: God Almighty is free from all evil, and He is described as innocent of all deficiency by way of exaggeration. Glory be can mean astonishment. He took His servant by night means: He made him travel, and likewise He made him travel, and the servant is: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. From the Sacred Mosque. It was said that the Night Journey was from the Mosque of Mecca. Qatada narrated on the authority of Anas on the authority of Malik Ibn Sa’sa’ah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: While I was in the Sacred Mosque in the sanctuary between sleeping and awake, Gabriel came to me with Al-Buraq. Then he mentioned the hadith of the Ascension. Some people said: He ascended from the house of Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib, and the meaning of his saying: from the Sacred Mosque is: from the sanctuary. Muqatil said: The Night of Isra was one year before the migration. It is also said: It was in Rajab. It is also said: It was in the month of Ramadan. To the Al-Aqsa Mosque, meaning: Jerusalem. It was called Al-Aqsa because it is the farthest of the mosques visited. It was also said: because of its distance from the Sacred Mosque. Which We have blessed around it, with rivers, trees, and fruits. Mujahid said: He called it blessed because it is the abode of the prophets, the place where the angels and revelation descend, and from it people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection. To show him some of Our signs, some of the wonders of Our power. There he saw the prophets and the great signs. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. He mentioned the All-Hearing to indicate that He is the One who answers his supplication, and he mentioned the All-Seeing to indicate that He is the One who protects him in the darkness of the night. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she used to say: The body of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not lost, but God took his soul on a night journey. Most people say that he was in his body while awake, and authentic reports have been transmitted on this matter. Abu Omar Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Abu Hamid Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Bukhari told us, Hudbah bin Khalid told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us, Qatada told us H. Al-Bukhari said: Khalifa Al-Asfari told me: Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed and Hisham told us. He said: Qatada narrated to us H on the authority of Malik bin Sa’sa’ah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them about the night he was taken on the Night Journey. H Al-Bukhari said: Yahya bin Bakir narrated to us, Al-Layth narrated to us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Anas, who said: Abu Dharr used to narrate that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: H, and Abu Sa’id Ismail bin Abdul Qahir informed us, Abu Al-Hasan Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad [Al-Farsi informed us, Abu Al-Hussein Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Muhammad] bin Sufyan informed us, Abu Al-Hussein Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj informed us, Shaiban bin Farukh informed us, Hammad bin Salamah informed us, Thabit Al-Banani informed us on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said - [Some of them hadiths were mixed in with others - Abu Dharr said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:] The ceiling of my house was opened up for me while I was in Mecca, and Gabriel came down and opened up my chest, then he washed it with Zamzam water, then he came… A golden basin filled with wisdom and faith, I pour it into my chest, then close it. Malik bin Sa`sa`ah said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them about the night he was taken on the Night Journey. He said: “While I was in al-Hatim, or he may have said in al-Hijr, between sleeping and waking, and he mentioned between two men, I was brought a golden basin filled with wisdom and faith. It was cut open from the throat to the navel of the belly, and my heart was taken out, washed, stuffed, and then returned.” Saeed and Hisham said: Then he washed his stomach with Zamzam water and was filled with faith and wisdom. Then he was given Al-Buraq, which is a tall white animal, bigger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, placing its hoof at the end of its eye. I rode it and set off with Gabriel until I came to Jerusalem. He said: Then I tied it to the ring that the prophets are tied to. He said: Then I entered the mosque and prayed two rak’ahs in it and then I went out. Gabriel came to me with a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, and I chose the milk. Gabriel said: You have chosen the fitrah. Gabriel took me until he came to the lowest heaven and asked to be admitted. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him. What a good coming he has come. It was opened. When I reached it, there was Adam in it. He said to me: This is your father Adam, so greet him. I greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son. In the hadith of Abu Dharr: We ascended to the lowest heaven, and there was a man sitting with black people on his right and black people on his left. If he looked to his right, he laughed, and if he looked to his left, he wept. He said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and the righteous son. I said to Gabriel: Who is this? He said: This is Adam, and these black people on his right and left are the souls of his sons. The people on the right among them are the people of Paradise, and the black people on his left are the people of Hell. If he looked to his right, he laughed, and if he looked to his left, he wept. Then he ascended until he came to the second heaven and asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, what a good arrival he has come. So it was opened. When I finished, there were Yahya and Isa, peace be upon them, and they are cousins. He said: This is Yahya and Isa, so greet them. I greeted them back and they said: Welcome to the righteous brother and righteous prophet. Then he ascended with me to the third heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. He said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, what a good arrival he has come. So it was opened. When I finished, there was Joseph, and he had been given half of his beauty. He said: This is Joseph, so greet him. So I greeted him and he greeted me back. Then he said: Welcome to the righteous brother and righteous prophet. Then he ascended with me until he came to the fourth heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, what a good arrival he has come. So it was opened. When I reached it, there was Idris. He said: This is Idris, so greet him. So I greeted him, and he responded and then said: Welcome to the righteous brother, the Prophet, and the righteous man. Then he ascended with me until he came to the fifth heaven and asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, what a good arrival he has come. When I finished, there was Aaron. He said: This is Aaron, so greet him. I greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said: Welcome to the righteous brother and righteous prophet. Then he ascended with me until he came to the sixth heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, what a wonderful arrival he has come. When I reached the end, there was Moses. He said: This is Moses, so greet him. So I greeted him back and he responded. Then he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous brother. When I passed, he cried. It was said to him: What makes you cry? He said: I cry because a young man was sent after me and more of his nation will enter Paradise than will enter it from my nation. Then he ascended with me to the seventh heaven, and Gabriel asked to be let in. It was said: Who is this? Gabriel said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. It was said: Welcome to him, what a wonderful arrival he has come. When I finished, there was Abraham. He said: This is your father Abraham, so greet him. So I greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son. Then the Frequented House was raised for me, and I asked Gabriel. He said: This is the Frequented House, in which seventy thousand angels pray every day. When they leave it, they do not return to it, as it is the last thing they are required to do. Thabit said on the authority of Anas: Then I saw Abraham leaning his back against the Frequented House, and behold, seventy thousand angels enter it every day and do not return to it. Then he took me to the Lote Tree of the Limit, and behold, its fruit was like the jars of Hajar, and behold, its leaves were like the ears of elephants. He said: Then, when what happened to it from the command of God happened, it changed, and no one among God’s creation can describe its beauty. At its base are four rivers: two hidden rivers and two apparent rivers. So I said: What are these, O Gabriel? He said: As for the hidden ones, they are two rivers in Paradise, and as for the apparent ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates. And He revealed to me what He revealed, and He imposed on me fifty prayers every day and night. So I went down to Moses, and he said: What has your Lord imposed on your nation? I said: Fifty prayers. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to make it lighter, for your nation cannot bear that, for I have tested the Children of Israel and experienced them. He said: So I went back to my Lord and said: O Lord, make it lighter for my nation. So He removed five from me. So I went back to Moses and said: Remove five from me. He said: Your nation cannot bear that, so go back to your Lord and ask Him to make it lighter. He said: I kept going back and forth between my Lord and Moses until He said: O Muhammad, there are five prayers every day and night, for each prayer ten, they are five and they are fifty, the word with Me does not change, and whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is written for him, and if he knows it, ten are written for him, and whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, nothing is written for him, but if he does it, one bad deed is written for him. He said: So I went down until I reached Moses and informed him. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to make things easier for your nation. I said: I asked my Lord until I felt ashamed, but I am satisfied and submit. He said: When I passed, a caller called out: I have fulfilled my duty and made it easy for my servants. Then I was brought into Paradise and there were pearls in it, and its soil was musk. Ibn Shihab said: Ibn Hazm informed me that Ibn Abbas and Abu Habbah Al-Ansari used to say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then he ascended with me until I appeared at a level where the pens were scratching. Ibn Hazm and Anas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God imposed fifty prayers on my nation. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Al-Buraq was brought on the night of the Isra’, bridled and saddled, and it was difficult for him. Gabriel said: ‘Is it Muhammad who would do this? No one has ridden you who is more honorable to God than him, so be patient.” Ibn Buraidah said on the authority of his father: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When we reached the Holy House, Gabriel pointed with his finger, pierced the stone with it, and fastened Al-Buraq with it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Mahmoud informed us, Abdul Razzaq informed us, Muammar informed us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab informed me on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the night of my Isra, I met Moses. He said: I described him, and he was a man - I thought he said: twitchy - with a man’s head as if he were from the men of Shanu’ah. He said: And I met Jesus, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described him and said: Medium-sized, red, as if he had come out of Dimas, meaning: the bath. And I saw Abraham, and I resembled his son to him. He said: And I was brought two vessels: one of them had milk, and the other had wine. It was said to him: Take whichever one you want. So I took the milk and drank it. It was said to me: You have been guided to the natural disposition [or you have attained the natural disposition]. But if you had taken the wine, your nation would have gone astray.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, he said: It is a vision that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was shown on the night he was taken on the Night Journey to Jerusalem. He said: And the cursed tree in the Qur’an? He said: It is the tree of Zaqqum. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah told us, Sulayman told me, on the authority of Sharik bin Abdullah, who said: I heard Anas bin Malik say: On the night of the Night Journey of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Kaaba Mosque, three men came to him, before revelation came to him, while he was sleeping in the Sacred Mosque. The first of them said: Which one is he? He said: The one in the middle is the best of them. The last of them said: Take the best of them. That night happened, and he did not see them until they came to him another night, as his heart sees, and his eye sleeps, but his heart does not sleep. This is how the prophets sleep, but their hearts do not sleep. They did not speak to him until they carried him and placed him near the Well of Zamzam. Gabriel split open his throat and his loins until he was finished with his chest and his belly, and he washed him with the water of Zamzam with his hand. And he narrated the hadith of the Ascension with its story. He said: Then he was in the lowest heaven, with two rivers flowing. He said: This is the Nile and the Euphrates, their origin is one. Then he went with him to the second heaven, and he saw another river with a palace of pearls and emeralds on it. He struck his hand and it was the most fragrant musk. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is the Kauthar that your Lord has hidden for you. And he narrated the hadith, and said: Then he ascended with me to the seventh heaven, and said: Moses said: O Lord, I did not think that You would raise anyone above me, then He ascended with him above that with what none knows except God until he came to the Lote Tree of the Limit, and the Almighty, the Lord of Majesty, approached and came close until he was two bow lengths away from him or nearer, and He revealed to him, among what God reveals to him, fifty prayers every day and night, and he said: Moses kept returning him to his Lord until it became five prayers, then Moses stopped him at the fifth, and said: O Muhammad, by God, the Children of Israel tried to seduce my people with something less than this, but they were weak in it and abandoned it, so your nation is weaker in hearts, bodies, bodies, sights, and hearing, so go back so that your Lord may lighten your burden, all of this while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to Gabriel to advise him, and Gabriel did not dislike that, so He raised him at the fifth, and he said: O Lord, my nation is weak in bodies, hearts, hearing, and bodies, so lighten our burden, so the Almighty said: O Muhammad, He said: At your service and at your pleasure, He said: Indeed, The word with Me does not change, as I have enjoined upon you in the Mother of the Book. So every good deed is rewarded tenfold, so they are fifty in the Mother of the Book, and five upon you. So Moses said: Go back to your Lord, so that He may lighten your burden as well. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, I felt shy before my Lord because of what I went to. He said: Then go down in the name of God. So he woke up and found himself in the Sacred Mosque. Muslim narrated this hadith in an abbreviated form on the authority of Harun bin Saeed Al-Aili, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Sulayman bin Bilal. Our Sheikh, the Imam, may God be pleased with him, said: Some of the people of hadith have said that we did not find anything from Muhammad ibn Ismail and Muslim in their books that could not be interpreted except this, and he referred the matter to Sharik ibn Abdullah, because he mentioned in it that this was before revelation came to him, and the people of knowledge agreed that the Night Journey was after revelation by about twelve years, one year before the Hijrah. It also says: The Almighty approached and descended. Aisha mentioned that the one who approached and descended was Gabriel, peace be upon him. Our Sheikh, the Imam, may God be pleased with him, said: This objection is not valid in my opinion, because this was a vision in a dream, God Almighty showed him before the revelation, as evidenced by the last part of the hadith: He said, so he woke up while he was in the Sacred Mosque, then he ascended while awake after the revelation a year before the migration, fulfilling his previous vision, just as he saw the conquest of Mecca in a dream in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah in the year six of the migration, then it was fulfilled in the year eight and the words of God Almighty were revealed: God has certainly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger in truth (al-Fath 48:27). It was narrated that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned on the night of his Isra’ and was in Dhu Tuwa, he said: O Gabriel, my people do not believe me. He said: Abu Bakr, and he is the truthful one, believes you. Ibn Abbas and Aisha, may God be pleased with them, said on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the night of my Night Journey came and I woke up in Mecca, I was distressed by my situation and knew that people would deny me. It was narrated that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat isolated and sad. Abu Jahl passed by him and sat next to him and said to him mockingly: Did you benefit from anything? He said: Yes, I was taken on a Night Journey last night. He said: Where to? He said: To Jerusalem. He said: Then you woke up among us. He said: Yes. Abu Jahl did not think he would deny it, fearing that he would deny the hadith. He said: Are you telling your people what you told me? He said: Yes. Abu Jahl said: O people of Banu Ka'b bin Lu'ay, come. He said: So the gatherings dispersed to him and they came and sat with them. He said: Then tell your people what you told me? He said: Yes, I was taken on a Night Journey last night. They said: Where to? He said: To Jerusalem. They said: Then you woke up among us? He said: Yes. He said: Some clapped, and some put their hands on their heads in amazement. Some of those who had believed in him and believed him turned back. A polytheist went to Abu Bakr and said: What do you think of your companion who claims that he was taken on a night journey to Jerusalem? He said: Did he really say that? He said: Yes. He said: If he said that, then he has told the truth. They said: Do you believe him that he went to Jerusalem in one night and came back before morning? He said: Yes, I believe him in what is even more distant than that. I believe him in report from heaven in the morning or the evening. That is why Abu Bakr was called the Truthful. He said: Among the people were those who had come to the Al-Aqsa Mosque, and they said: Can you describe the mosque to us? He said: Yes. He said: I went describing and describing, and I kept describing until I became confused [with some of the descriptions]. He said: The mosque was brought to me while I was looking at it until it was placed near the house of Aqil, and he described the mosque while I was looking at it. The people said: As for the description, by God, you have hit the mark. Then they said: O Muhammad, tell us about our caravan, it is more important to us. Did you find anything from it? He said: Yes, I passed by the caravan of Banu So-and-so, and it was in Ar-Rawha’, and they had lost a camel of theirs while they were searching for it, and in their saddlebags there was a cup of water. It became thirsty, so I took it and drank it, then I put it back as it was. Ask them: Did they find water in the cup when they returned to it? They said: This is a sign. He said: I passed by the camel of Banu So-and-so, and So-and-so and So-and-so were riding and sitting for them at Dhu Tuwa. Their camel ran away from me and threw at So-and-so, and his hand was broken. Ask them about that. They said: This is a sign. They said: Then tell us about our caravan? He said: I passed by it at At-Tan'im. They said: What was its number, its loads, its condition, and who was on it? He said: Yes, its condition was such-and-such, and so-and-so and so-and-so were on it. A grey camel with two sewn bags on it preceded it. It appears to you at sunrise. They said: This is a sign. Then they went out, hastening towards the pass, saying: By God, Muhammad has narrated something and explained it, until they came to a hill, and sat on it and waited for the sun to rise so that they could deny him. Then one of them said: By God, the sun has risen, and another said: By God, the camels have risen, led by a white camel, and among them is so-and-so and so-and-so, as he had told them. But they did not believe, and they said: This is nothing but obvious magic. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir informed us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad informed us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi informed us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan informed us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj informed us, Zuhair bin Harb informed us, Hajar bin Al-Muthanna informed us, Abdul Aziz - who is the son of Abi Salamah - informed us - on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Fadl, on the authority of Abi Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abi Hurairah, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw myself in Al-Hijr, and the Quraysh were asking me about my Night Journey, so they asked me about things from the Holy House that I did not confirm, so I was distressed in a way I had never been distressed before. He said: God raised him up for me to look at him, and they did not ask me about anything except that I informed them about it. I saw myself in a group of prophets, and Moses was standing praying, and a man with curly hair as if he were from the men of Shanu’ah, and Jesus was standing praying, the person closest to him in resemblance was Urwah bin Mas’ud Al-Thaqafi, and Abraham was standing praying, the person most similar to him was your companion - meaning himself - then the prayer came and I led them in prayer. When I finished praying, someone said to me: O Muhammad, this is Malik, the companion of Hellfire, so greet him. So I turned to him and he greeted me first.
17:2: 2 - The Almighty said: And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guide for the Children of Israel, that you not, that you not, take besides Me a guardian, a lord and a guarantor. Abu Amr said: Do not take with the letter ya because it is a report about them, and the others: with the letter ta, meaning: We told them: Do not take.
17:3: 3 - The offspring of those whom We carried, Mujahid said: This is a call, meaning: O offspring of those whom We carried, with Noah, in the ship, so We saved them from the flood, Indeed, he was a grateful servant, Noah, peace be upon him, when he ate food, drank a drink, or put on a garment, he would say: Praise be to God, so he was called a grateful servant, meaning: very grateful.
17:4: 4 - The Almighty said: And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture the verses. Sufyan bin Saeed Al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Mansur bin Al-Mu'tamir on the authority of Rib'i bin Harash on the authority of Hudhayfah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the Children of Israel transgressed and killed the prophets, God sent against them the king of Persia Bukhtanasr, and God's reign lasted for seven hundred years. He marched against them until he entered Jerusalem, besieged it and conquered it, and killed seventy thousand people over the blood of John the son of Zakariya, peace be upon him. Then he took its people [and children] captive, and plundered the ornaments of Jerusalem, and extracted from it seventy thousand and one hundred thousand carts of ornaments. I said: O Messenger of God, was Jerusalem great? He said: Yes, Solomon, son of David, built it from gold, silver, rubies, and emeralds, and its pillars were made of gold. God gave him that, and subjected the devils to him, so they would bring him these things in the blink of an eye. So Bukhtanasr marched with them until he reached Babylon, and the Children of Israel remained in his hands for a hundred years, enslaved by the Magians and the sons of the Magians, among them the prophets. Then God had mercy on them and revealed to a king of the kings of Persia called Cyrus, and he was a believer, that he would march to them to rescue the remnants of the Children of Israel, so Cyrus marched to the Children of Israel and took the jewelry of the House of Jerusalem until he returned it to him, so the Children of Israel stayed there obedient to God Almighty for a hundred years, then they returned to sins so God empowered over them a king called Antianus so he invaded the Children of Israel until he reached Jerusalem, so he took its people captive and burned Jerusalem, and he said to them: O Children of Israel, if you return to sins we will return to you a second time [with captivity], so they returned, so God empowered over them a Roman king called Faqis bin Astianus, so he invaded them by land and sea and took them captive and took the jewelry of the House of Jerusalem and burned Jerusalem, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is from the description of the jewelry of the House of Jerusalem, and the Mahdi will return it to Jerusalem, and it is one thousand seven hundred ships that he will throw at Jaffa until it is transported to Jerusalem, and with it God will gather the first and the last. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: The Children of Israel had sins and transgressions, and God was forgiving of them and kind to them. The first thing that befell them because of their sins, as He informed us on the tongue of Moses, peace be upon him, was that a king among them was called Siddiqah. Whenever God Almighty appointed a king over them, He sent with him a prophet to guide and direct him. He did not send down books to them, but they were commanded to follow the Torah and the rulings contained in it. When that king took power, God sent with him Isaiah bin Asfiya. This was before the mission of Zachariah, John, and Jesus, peace be upon them. Isaiah was the one who gave good report about Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, and he said: Rejoice, Jerusalem, now the rider of the donkey will come to you, and after him the owner of the camel. That king ruled the Children of Israel and Jerusalem for a period of time, and when his reign came to an end, the events among them were great, and Isaiah was with him. God sent against them Sanjarib, the king of Babylon, with six hundred thousand banners. He came walking until he camped around Jerusalem, and the king was sick, with an ulcer in his leg. The prophet Isaiah came and said to him: O King of the Children of Israel, Sanjarib, the king of Babylon, has come to you with his soldiers with six hundred thousand banners, and the people have feared them and have been dispersed. This was a great burden on the king, and he said: O Prophet of God, has there come to you a revelation from God about what has happened, so that you can tell us what God will do with us, with Sanjarib, and his soldiers? He said: No revelation came to me. While they were like that, God revealed to the Prophet Isaiah to go to the king of the Children of Israel and order him to make his will and appoint whoever he wishes from his family to rule over his kingdom. So Isaiah went to the king of the Children of Israel Zadiqa and said to him: Your Lord has revealed to me to order you to make your will and appoint whoever you wish from your family to rule over your kingdom, for you are going to die. When Isaiah said that to Zadiqa, he turned toward the qiblah and prayed and supplicated and wept. He said while weeping and supplicating to God with a sincere heart: O God, Lord of lords and God of gods, O Holy, Holy One, O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate, O Most Kind, Whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes, remember me of my work and my actions and my good judgment on the Children of Israel, for all of that was from You and You know it better than I do. My secret and my public are Yours and You are the Most Merciful. So He responded to him, and he was a righteous servant. So God Almighty inspired Isaiah to tell his friend that his Lord had responded to him and had mercy on him, and had delayed his life for fifteen years, and had saved him from his enemy Sennacherib. So Isaiah came to him and told him that, and when he said that to him, the pain went away from him and the sadness ceased from him, and he fell down in prostration and said: O my God and the God of my fathers, I have prostrated to You and glorified and magnified and magnified You are the One who gives the kingdom to whomever You will, and You take the kingdom away from whomever You will, and You honor whomever You will and humiliate whomever You will, You are the Knower of the unseen and the seen, You are the First and the Last, the Evident and the Hidden, and You are merciful and You answer the call of the needy, and You are the One who answered my call and had mercy on my supplication. When he raised his head, God inspired Isaiah to tell his friend the king to order one of his servants to bring him dragon water and put it on his ulcer and he would be healed. In the morning he would be healed. So he did and he was healed. The king said to Isaiah: Ask your Lord to give us knowledge of what He will do to our enemy. God said to Isaiah: Tell him: I have saved you from your enemy and delivered you from them, and they will all die in the morning except for Sinjar and five men from his scribes. When morning came, a crier came and cried out at the gate of the city, “O King of the Children of Israel, God has saved you from your enemy. Go out, for Sennacherib and those with him have perished.” When the king went out, he sought Sennacherib but could not be found among the dead. The king sent for him and the search caught up with him in a cave with five of his scribes, one of whom was Bukhtanasr. They put them in the mosques and brought them to the king of the Children of Israel. When he saw them, he fell down in prostration from the time the sun rose until the afternoon. Then he said to Sennacherib, What do you think our Lord did to you? Did He not kill you with His power and strength while we were unaware? Sanjarib said to him: The report of your Lord and His victory for you and His mercy with which He has shown you came to me before I left my country, but I did not obey a guide, and nothing brought me misery except [humiliation in this world and torment in the hereafter]. If I had listened or understood, I would not have attacked you. His friend said: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, who has spared us from you as He willed. Our Lord did not keep you and those with you alive because of your honor with your Lord, but He only kept you and those with you alive so that you would increase in misery in this world and torment in the Hereafter, and so that you would inform those behind you of what you saw of our Lord’s action towards you, so that you would warn those who come after you. Were it not for that, He would have killed you, and your blood and the blood of those with you is easier for God than the blood of a tick, if it were killed. Then the king of the children of Israel ordered the commander of his guard to throw the mosques around their necks, and he paraded them around Jerusalem and Elijah for seventy days, and he gave them two loaves of barley every day for each man of them. Then Sennacherib said to the king of the children of Israel: Killing is better than what you are doing to us. So the king ordered them to the prison of killing. Then God revealed to Isaiah, peace be upon him: Tell the king of the children of Israel to send Sennacherib and those with him to warn those behind them, and to honor them and carry them until they reach their country. So Isaiah informed the king of that, and [the king, his friend] did as he was ordered. So Sennacherib and those with him set out until they reached Babylon. When they arrived, he gathered the people and told them what God had done to his soldiers. His priests and magicians said to him: O King of Babylon, we used to relate to you the report of their Lord and the report of their prophet and the revelation of God to their prophet, but you did not obey us. They are a nation that no one can defeat with their Lord. Sennacherib’s affair was to frighten them, but God sufficed them as a reminder and a lesson. Then Sennacherib remained after that for seven years, then he died and Bukhtanasr, his grandson, succeeded him, as his grandfather had done, so he remained for seventeen years, then God took the king of the Children of Israel, his friend, so the matter of the Children of Israel was confused and they competed for the kingship until they killed each other, and their prophet Isaiah was with them and they did not accept from him, so when they did that God said to Isaiah, Stand up among your people and I will reveal on your tongue, so when the prophet Isaiah stood up God made his tongue speak with revelation, so he said: “O sky, listen and O earth, be silent, for God wants to tell the story of the Children of Israel whom He raised with His grace, and made for Himself, and singled them out with His honor, and preferred them over His servants, and they are like lost sheep that have no shepherd, so He sheltered their strays, and gathered their lost ones, and mended their broken ones, and treated their sick, and fattened their thin ones, and preserved their fat ones, so when He did that they became arrogant and their rams butted each other, and some of them killed others, until there was not a single healthy bone left for another broken one to mend, Woe to this sinful nation who do not know whence good has come to them, that the camel remembers its homeland and is tempted by it, that the donkey remembers the meadow where it has been full and returns to it, that the bull remembers the meadow in which it has been fattened and is tempted by it, and that these people do not remember whence good has come to them, and they are people of understanding and intellect, they are neither cows nor donkeys. I will give them an example, so let them listen to it. Say to them: How do you see a land that was once empty, desolate, dead, without any civilization, and had a wise Lord, who surrounded it with a wall, built palaces in it, caused a river to flow, and planted olives, pomegranates, palm trees, grapes, and all kinds of fruits in it, and appointed a wise and ambitious guardian over it, strong and trustworthy, but when it rose, its ripening came out ruined? They said, "This is an evil land! We think that its wall and palace should be demolished, its river should be buried, its values should be seized, and its crops should be burned until it becomes, as it was the first time, a dead ruin with no life in it. God said, He said to them, 'The wall is My religion, the palace is My law, the river is My book, the values are My prophet, and the crops are themselves, and the carob tree that brought forth the crops is their evil deeds. I have decreed upon them their decree upon themselves, and this is an example of what I have set for them. They seek to draw near to Me by slaughtering cows and sheep, but the meat does not reach Me nor do I eat it. They claim to draw near to Me through piety and refraining from slaughtering the souls that I have forbidden, but their hands are stained with it and their clothes are covered with its blood. They build houses as mosques for Me, and purify their interiors, but defile and pollute their hearts and bodies. They decorate and adorn the mosques for Me, and they ruin and corrupt their minds and dreams. So what need do I have to build houses when I do not live in them?'" What need do I have to decorate the mosques when I do not enter them? I was only ordered to raise them so that I may remember and glorify God in them. They say: We fasted, but our fasting was not lifted, we prayed, but our prayer was not illuminated, we gave charity, but our charity was not purified, we called out like the cooing of doves, and we cried like the howling of wolves. In all of that, our prayers were not answered. God said: Ask them, what prevents Me from answering them? Am I not the Hearer of the hearers, the Seeer of the seers, the Nearest of the responders, and the Most Merciful of the merciful? How can I lift their fasting while they clothe it with false speech and strengthen it with unlawful food? Or how can I enlighten their prayers while their hearts are attentive to those who fight Me, oppose Me, and violate My prohibitions? Or how can their charities be purified by Me while they give charity with the money of others? I only reward those who have been usurped for it? Or how can I answer their supplication while it is only a word on their tongues, and action is far from that? I only answer the gentle supplicant, and I only hear the words of the chaste and poor, and one of the signs of My pleasure is the pleasure of the poor. They say, when they heard my words and my message reached them: These are transmitted sayings, inherited hadiths, and a composition of the kind that magicians and soothsayers compose. They claim that if they wanted to produce a hadith like it, they could do so, and if they wanted to know the unseen through what the devils suggest to them, they could know. And I have decreed on the day I created the heavens and the earth a decree that I have confirmed and imposed upon Myself, and I have set a deferred term before it that must come to pass. So if they are truthful in what they claim of knowledge of the unseen, then let them tell you: When will I carry it out? Or at what time will it be? And if they are able to do what they wish, then let them do with the same power with which I have decreed, for I will make it manifest over all religions, even if the polytheists hate it. And if they are able to say what they wish, then let them say the same wisdom with which I have directed the matter of that decree, if they are truthful. And I have decreed on the day I created the heaven and the earth that I would make prophethood among the hired, and that I would make kingship among the shepherds, and honor among the humble, and strength among the weak, and wealth among the poor, and knowledge among the ignorant, and wisdom among the unlettered. So ask them when this will be and who will carry it out, and who are the helpers and supporters of this matter, if they know. For I will send for that an unlettered, trustworthy prophet who is neither rude nor harsh, nor a clamorer in the markets, nor adorned with obscenities, nor a speaker of slander. I will guide him to every good thing, and bestow upon him every noble characteristic. I will make tranquility his garment, righteousness his slogan, piety his conscience, wisdom his reason, truthfulness and loyalty his nature, and forgiveness and goodness his character. And justice is his way of life, [and truth is his law] and guidance [and the Qur’an] is his leader, and Islam is his religion and Ahmad is his name. With it I guide after misguidance, and with it I teach after ignorance, and with it I raise after indolence, and with it I make famous after denial, and with it I increase after fewness, and with it I enrich after poverty, and with it I gather after division, and with it I unite different hearts, scattered desires and dispersed nations, and I make his nation the best nation brought forth for mankind, they enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, in monotheism for Me, faith and sincerity for Me. They pray standing, sitting, bowing and prostrating, and they fight in My cause in ranks and groups, and they go out from their homes and their wealth seeking My pleasure. I inspire them to glorify and unify, to praise and extol, and to extol and extol in their marches, their gatherings, their beds, their virtues and their resting place. They glorify and praise and sanctify over the heads of the nobles, and they purify their faces and limbs for Me. They tie their garments in half for Me. Their sacrifice is their blood, and their Bibles are in their chests. They are monks by night and lions by day. That is My bounty, which I bestow upon whom I will, and I am the possessor of great bounty. When Isaiah finished speaking, they attacked him to kill him, but he fled from them. A tree met him and split open for him, so he entered it. Satan caught up with him, took hold of a fringe of his garment and showed it to them. They put a saw in the middle of it and sawed it until they cut it down, and cut him in the middle. After that, God appointed a man from among them as a successor over the Children of Israel, whose name was Nashiah ibn Amoz, and sent to them Jeremiah ibn Hilkiah as a prophet, and he was from the tribe of Aaron ibn Imran. Ibn Ishaq mentioned that he was Al-Khidr, whose name was Jeremiah. He was called Al-Khidr because he sat on a white fur and then got up from it while it was shaking green. Then God sent Jeremiah to that king to guide him and direct him. Then the events among the Children of Israel became great and they committed sins and made the forbidden permissible. So God inspired Jeremiah to go to your people from the Children of Israel and tell them what I command you to do and remind them of My blessings and make them aware of their events. Jeremiah said: O Lord, I am weak if you do not strengthen me, helpless if you do not convey to me, and forsaken if you do not support me. God Almighty said: Did you not know that all matters proceed from My will, and that hearts and tongues are in My hand, I turn them as I wish? I am with you and nothing will reach you with Me. Jeremiah stood up among them and did not know what to say, so God Almighty inspired him at the time to deliver an eloquent sermon in which he explained the reward of obedience and the punishment of disobedience. At the end of it he said about God Almighty: And I swear by My might that I will raise up for them a trial in which the forbearing will be perplexed, and I will set over them a cruel tyrant whom I will clothe with awe, and I will remove mercy from his chest, and he will be followed by a number like the blackness of the dark night. Then God revealed to Jeremiah: I will destroy the children of Israel with Japheth, and Japheth is from the people of Babylon - as we mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah - so God empowered Nebuchadnezzar over them, so he went out with six hundred thousand banners, and entered Jerusalem with his soldiers and trampled on the Levant, and killed the children of Israel until he annihilated them, and destroyed Jerusalem, and ordered his soldiers to fill each man’s shield with dirt and then throw it into Jerusalem, so they did that until they filled it, then he ordered them to gather all the people in the cities of Jerusalem, so every young and old of the children of Israel gathered around him, so he chose seventy thousand boys from them, and when the spoils of his army came out, and he wanted to divide them among them, the kings who were with him said to him: O king, all our spoils are yours, and divide among us these boys whom you chose from the children of Israel, so he divided them among the kings who were with him, so each important man got four boys, and he divided the rest of the children of Israel into three groups, so a third remained in the Levant, a third was taken captive, and a third was killed and went away. With the youth of Jerusalem and the seventy thousand boys until he brought them to Babylon, this was the first battle that God brought down upon the Children of Israel because of their injustice. This is what God Almighty said: “So when the first of the two promises came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might,” meaning: Bukhtanasr and his companions. Then Nebuchadnezzar remained in his kingdom as long as God willed, then he saw a vision that pleased him, for he saw something that happened to him, and God made him forget what he had seen. So he called Daniel, Hananiah, Azaziah, and Michael, who were descendants of the prophets, and asked them about it. They said, Tell us about it and we will tell you its interpretation. He said, I do not remember it, and if you do not tell me about it and its interpretation, I will tear off your shoulders. So they left him and called upon God and beseeched Him, and He informed them of what he had asked them about. So they came to him and said, I saw a statue whose feet and legs were of pottery, whose knees and thighs were of copper, whose belly was of silver, whose chest was of gold, and whose head and neck were of iron. He said, You have spoken the truth. They said, While you were looking at it and you were amazed, God Almighty sent a rock from the sky that crushed it, and it is what made you forget it. He said, You have spoken the truth. He said, What is its interpretation? They said, "Its interpretation is that you saw the King of Kings. Some of them had the gentlest kingship, some had the best kingship, and some had the most severe kingship. Clay is the weakest of them, then above it is copper, which is more severe than it. Then above copper is silver, which is better than that and more excellent. Gold is better than silver, which is more excellent. Then your kingship is iron, which is more severe and more powerful than what was before it. And the rock that you saw, God sent from the sky and crushed it. A prophet will be sent by God from the sky and he will crush all of it and the matter will be returned to him." Then the people of Babylon said to Nebuchadnezzar: Have you seen these young men from the Children of Israel whom we asked you to give us and you did? We have disowned our women since they were with us. We have seen our women turn their faces away from us to them. So expel them from among us or kill them. He said: It is your business with them. Whoever among you wants to kill whoever is in his hand, let him do so. When they brought them close to being killed, they cried out to God Almighty and said: O Lord, we have been afflicted by the sins of others. So God promised to answer them, and they were killed except for those Nebuchadnezzar left behind, including Daniel, Hananiah, Azaziah, and Michael. Then when God wanted to destroy Nebuchadnezzar, he arose and said to those of the Children of Israel who were under his control: Have you seen this house that I have destroyed and the people whom I have killed? What is this house? They said: This is the House of God, and these are its people. They were descendants of the prophets, but they were unjust and transgressed, so I was given power over them because of their sins. And their Lord, the Lord of the heavens and the earth and the Lord of all creation, honored and glorified them. But when they did what they did, God destroyed them and gave power over them to others. He was arrogant and thought that his power had done that to the Children of Israel. He said: Tell me, how can I ascend to the highest heaven and kill those in it and take it as my kingdom, for I have finished with the earth? They said: No one among creation has the power to do so. He said: You must do it, or I will kill you all. They cried and supplicated to God Almighty, so God sent a mosquito upon him by His power, which entered his nostril until it bit his brain. He would not rest or calm down until his head was struck on his brain. When he died, they split his head open and found the mosquito biting his brain so that God would show His servants His power. God saved those of the Children of Israel who remained in His hands, so they returned them to the Levant, where they built and multiplied until they were in the best condition they had ever been. They claim that God Almighty revived those who were killed and they joined them. Then, when they entered Ash-Sham, they entered it without a covenant from God Almighty, and the Torah had been burned. Ezra was one of the captives who were in Babylon, so he returned to Ash-Sham, crying over it day and night. He had left the people, and he was like that when a man came to him and said, O Ezra, what makes you cry? He said, I cry over the Book of God and His covenant that was among us, the only thing that will fix our worldly life and our afterlife. He said, Would you like it to be returned to you? Then he went back, fasted, purified himself, and purified his clothes, then he went to the place he had promised and sat in it. That man came to him with a vessel of water, and he was a king whom God had sent to him, so he gave him to drink from that vessel, and the Torah was represented in his chest, so he went back to the Children of Israel and laid down the Torah for them, so they loved him until they had never loved anything like him before. Then God took him, and after that the Children of Israel began to invent events, and God returned to them and sent messengers to them, so a group of them lied and a group killed, until the last of their prophets whom God sent to them were Zachariah, John, and Jesus, and they were from the house of David. Then Zachariah died, and it was said that Zachariah was killed. When God raised Jesus from among them, and they killed John, God sent upon them a king from the kings of Babylon called Khardush, so he marched against them with the people of Babylon until he entered upon them in the Levant, and when he prevailed over them, he ordered a chief of his soldiers called Bayurzadhan, the one who killed. He said: I have sworn by my God that if I am victorious over the people of Jerusalem, I will kill them until their blood flows in the midst of my army, but I cannot find anyone to kill. So he ordered him to kill them until that reached them in Bayrzadhan. He entered Jerusalem and stood in the spot where they were offering their sacrifices. He found blood boiling, so he asked them, saying: O Children of Israel, what is the matter with this blood boiling? They told me his story. They said: This is the blood of our sacrifice which we offered but it was not accepted from us, so that is why it boils. We have offered sacrifices for eight hundred years and they were not accepted from us except this. He said: You did not believe me. They said: If it were like the beginning of our time, it would have been accepted from us, but the kingdom, prophethood and revelation have been cut off from us, so that is why it was not accepted from us. So Bayurzadhan slaughtered seven hundred and seventy pairs of their heads over that blood, but it did not calm down. So he ordered that seven hundred of their young men be brought and he slaughtered them over the blood, but it did not calm down. So he ordered seven thousand of their old men and their wives to be brought and he slaughtered them over the blood, but it did not cool down. When Bayurzadhan saw the blood not calming down, he said to them: O Children of Israel, woe to you! Believe me and be patient with the command of your Lord, for you have ruled the earth for a long time, doing whatever you want before I do not leave among you a fire-blower, female or male, except that I kill him. When they saw the effort and severity of the killing, they believed his story, and they said: This blood is the blood of a prophet who used to forbid us from certain matters. Many of them incurred the wrath of God. If we had obeyed him in them, he would have been more guiding to us. He used to tell us about your affair, but we did not believe him, so we killed him. This is his blood. Then Bayorzadhan said to them: What was his name? They said: Yahya bin Zakariya. He said: Now you have believed me. For such a thing your Lord has taken revenge on you. When Bayorzadhan saw that they believed him, he fell down in prostration and said to those around him: Close the gates of the city, and bring out those who were here from the army of Khardush, and leave the Children of Israel alone. Then he said: O Yahya, son of Zakariya, my Lord and your Lord knows what has befallen your people because of you and what has been killed from them, so calm down by the permission of your Lord before I do not leave a single one of your people. So the blood calmed down by the permission of God, and Bayorzadhan lifted the killing from them, and said: I believe in what the Children of Israel believe in and I am certain that there is no Lord other than Him. He said to the Children of Israel: Khardush has ordered me to kill from you until your blood flows in the midst of his army, and I am not able [to disobey him]. They said to him: Do as you are ordered. So he ordered them to dig a trench, and he ordered their wealth of horses, mules, donkeys, camels, cows and sheep to be slaughtered until the blood flowed in the army, and he ordered the dead who were killed before that to be thrown on the livestock that he had killed, so Khardush thought nothing but That what was in the trench was from the children of Israel, and when the blood reached his army, he sent to Bayorzadhan to lift the killing from them. Then he returned to Babylon, and he had destroyed the children of Israel or almost [to destroy them], and it was the last battle that God sent down on the children of Israel, and that is His saying: "You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice", so the first battle was with Bukhtanasr and his soldiers, [and the other was with Khurdush and his soldiers], and it was the greater of the two battles, so they did not raise a banner after that, and the kingdom in the Levant and its environs passed to the Greek Romans, except that the remnants of the children of Israel increased, and they had the leadership in Jerusalem and its environs in a way other than the king's, and they were in comfort until they changed and caused events, so God empowered over them Tatius bin Asbianus the Roman, so he destroyed their country and expelled them from it and God took away the kingdom and leadership from them and humiliation was imposed on them so that they were not in a nation except for humiliation and tribute, and Jerusalem remained in ruins until the days of Omar bin Al-Khattab, so the Muslims rebuilt it by his order. Qatada said: God sent Goliath against them in the first place, so he took captives, killed and destroyed. Then We gave you back the upper hand over them, meaning in the time of David. Then, when the promise of the Hereafter came, God sent Nebuchadnezzar against them, so he took captives and destroyed. Then he said: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you. So God returned mercy to them, then the people returned with the worst of what was in their presence, so God sent upon them whatever He willed of His vengeance and punishment. Then God sent upon them the Arabs, as He said: And when your Lord proclaimed that He would surely send upon them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst of torment. So they are in torment until the Day of Resurrection. Al-Suddi mentioned with his chain of transmission: A man from the Children of Israel saw in a dream that the destruction of the Holy House was at the hands of an orphan boy, the son of a widow from the people of Babylon, called Bukhtanasr. They believed him, so their vision came true. He came to ask about him until he came down to his mother while he was collecting firewood. He came with a bundle of firewood on his head, so he threw it down and sat down. He spoke to him and then gave him three dirhams and said: Buy food and drink with these. So he bought meat for one dirham, bread for one dirham, and wine for one dirham. They ate and drank. He did the same on the second day and the same on the third day. Then he said: I would like you to write me a guarantee of safety if you ever rule. He said: Are you mocking me? He said: I am not mocking you, but you do not have to take her as a hand with me. So he wrote him a letter of security and said: What do you think if I come and the people around you have prevented me from you? He said: Raise your document on a reed so that I may recognize you. So he wrote to him and gave it to him. Then the king of the Children of Israel honored John the son of Zakariya and brought him close to his seat. He loved his wife’s daughter, and Ibn Abbas said: His sister’s daughter. So he asked John the son of Zakariya about marrying her, so he forbade him from marrying her. Her mother heard about that and she hated John the son of Zakariya. When the king sat down to drink, she dressed her in thin red clothes, perfumed her, and dressed her in jewelry. She sent her to the king and ordered her to give him a drink. If he wanted her for himself, she would refuse him until he gave her what she asked for. When he gave her, she asked for the head of John the son of Zakariya to be brought in a basin, so she did. When he wanted her, she said: I will not do it until you give me what I ask you. He said: What do you ask me for? She said: The head of Yahya ibn Zakariya is in this basin. He said: Woe to you, ask me for something other than this. She said: I want nothing but this. When morning came, his blood was boiling. He ordered that dirt be thrown on him, and the blood rose up, meaning the blood rose boiling, and dirt was thrown on him until it reached the wall of the city while it was boiling. So Sakhban, the king of Babylon, sent an army to them and put Bukhtanasr in charge of them. Bukhtanasr and his companions marched until they reached that place and fortified themselves against him in their cities. When the situation became difficult for them, he wanted to return, but an old woman from the old women of the Children of Israel came out to him and said: Do you want to return before the city is conquered? He said: Yes, my stay has been long and my companions are hungry. She said: What do you think if I conquer the city, will you give me what I ask of you and kill whomever I command you to kill and refrain from doing so when I command you to refrain? He said: Yes. She said: When morning comes, divide your army into four quarters, then place a quarter at each corner, then raise your hands to the sky and call: We ask you to open, O God, with the blood of John the son of Zachariah, for it will fall. So they did, and the city fell and they entered from its sides. She said: Withhold your hand, and she went with him to the blood of John the son of Zachariah and said: Kill for this blood until it subsides. So he killed seventy thousand for it until it subsided. When it subsided, she said: Withhold your hand, for God is not pleased when a prophet is killed until he kills the one who killed him and the one who was pleased with his killing. The owner of the document came to him with his document, so he refrained from him and from his family, so he destroyed the Holy House and threw the corpses into it, and the Romans helped him in its destruction because the Children of Israel killed John the son of Zachariah. He went with him with the leaders of the Children of Israel and he went with Daniel and some of the children of the prophets and he went with him with the head of Goliath. When he arrived in Babylon, he found that Sakhabin had died, so he ruled in his place. The most honorable people in his eyes were Daniel and his companions. The Magi envied them and slandered him and said: Daniel and his companions do not worship your God and do not eat your sacrifice. So he asked them and they said: Yes, we have a Lord whom we worship, and we do not eat of your sacrifice. So the king ordered a thigh for them and they threw them in it, and they were six, and he threw with them seven harmful beasts to eat them. So they went and then they returned and found them sitting and the beast spread out its arms with them and did not scratch any of them. Then they found a seventh man with them, so he said: Who is this seventh? There were only six of them. So the seventh came out and he was a king and he slapped him and he became among the wild beasts, and God transformed him for seven years. Wahb said: God transformed Nebuchadnezzar into an eagle among birds, then into a bull among beasts, then into a lion among wild beasts. His transformation lasted seven years, and his heart was the heart of a human being. Then God restored his kingdom to him and he believed. Wahb was asked, Was he a believer? He said: “I found the People of the Book differing about him. Some of them said he died a believer, and some of them said he burned the Temple Mount and its books and killed the prophets. So God became angry with him and did not accept his repentance.” Al-Suddi said: Then when Bukhtassar returned to his form after the transformation and God restored his kingdom to him, Daniel and his companions were the most honorable people to him, so the Magians envied them and said to Bukhtassar: When Daniel drinks wine, he cannot control himself from urinating, and that is a disgrace to them. So he made food and drink for them, so they ate and drank, and he said to the doorman: Look for the first one who comes out to urinate and hit him with the tabarzin. If he says I am Bukhtassar, then say: You lie, Bukhtassar ordered me. So the first one to stand up to urinate was Bukhtassar. When the doorman saw him, he attacked him and said: Woe to you, I am Bukhtassar. He said: You lie, Bukhtassar ordered me. So he hit him and killed him. This is what he mentioned in Al-Mubtada, except that the narration of the one who narrated that Bukhtassar invaded the Children of Israel when they killed John the Baptist, son of Zechariah, is a mistake according to the people of the biography. Rather, they are unanimous that Bukhtassar only invaded the Children of Israel when they killed Isaiah during the reign of Jeremiah, and from the time of Jeremiah and Bukhtassar’s destruction of the Temple. The Holy City to the birth of John the son of Zakariya was four hundred and sixty-one years. This is because they used to count from the time of Nebuchadnezzar’s destruction of the Holy City to the time of its reconstruction during the reign of Cyrus the son of Ahshurash the son of Asihid in Babylon by Bahman the son of Isfandiyar [seventy years, then from after his reconstruction to the appearance of Alexander in the Holy City eighty-eight years, then from after his kingdom] to the birth of John the son of Zakariya three hundred and sixty years. The correct version of this is what Muhammad bin Ishaq mentioned. The Almighty said: And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture. That is, We informed them and told them in what We gave them of the Scriptures that they would corrupt. And the judgment has aspects: it is a command, like His saying: And your Lord has decreed (al-Isra’ 17:23) And it is a judgment, as in His saying: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them Yunus - 93, and An-Nahl - 78 And it is a creation, as in His saying: Then He completed them as seven heavens (Fussilat 41:2) Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: It means that we decreed upon them, and to means upon, and what is meant by the book is the Preserved Tablet. You will surely cause corruption, the oath lam, its meaning is: By God, you will surely cause corruption, on the earth twice, with sins, and what is meant by the earth is the land of Ash-Sham and Jerusalem, and you will surely declare, and you will surely be arrogant, and you will surely oppress people, with great haughtiness.
17:5: 5 - So when the first of the two times comes, meaning: the first of the two times. Qatada said: Their corruption the first time was that they violated the rulings of the Torah and committed forbidden acts. Ibn Ishaq said that their corruption the first time was the killing of Isaiah between the tree and their committing of sins. We sent against you Our servants, Qatada said, meaning Goliath the Khazar and his soldiers, whom David killed. Saeed bin Jubair said: He means Sanjarib from the people of Nineveh. Ibn Ishaq said: Bukhtanasr the Babylonian and his companions. This is more apparent. Oli Bas, possessing strength, severe, in war, Fajasawa, meaning: they roamed and went around, throughout the houses, in the middle of them seeking you and killing you, and Jaws means seeking something thoroughly. Al-Farra’ said: Fajasawa killed you between your houses. And it was a promise to be fulfilled, a decree that would come into being and not be broken.
17:6: 6 - Then We gave you back the upper hand, meaning: the return and the state, over them and reinforced you with wealth and children and made you more numerous, in number, meaning: those who would go out with them and the country returned better than it was.
17:7: 7 - If you do good, you do good for yourselves, meaning: it will be rewarded for it, but if you do evil, it will be for it, meaning: upon it, as God Almighty says: “So peace be upon you” (al-Waqi’ah 56:91), meaning: upon you. It was said: it will be rewarded and punished for it.
