So when the promise of the Hereafter comes meaning: the last time of your corruption, and that is their intention to kill Jesus, peace be upon him, when he was raised, and their killing of John, son of Zakariya, peace be upon them, so God sent the Persians and the Romans, Khordoush and Titus, against them until they killed them and took them captive and banished them from their homes, so that is what God Almighty said: to disfigure your faces, meaning: your faces will be sad, and disfigurement of the face means introducing sorrow and grief. Al-Kisa’i [and Ya’qub] read bi-saw’ with a noon and a fatha over the hamza for emphasis, like his saying: And We decreed and We sent. Ibn ‘Amir and Hamza read with a ya’ and a fatha over the hamza for emphasis, meaning: May God disfigure your faces. It was also said: May the promise disfigure your faces. The rest read it with the letter ya and the letter hamza with a damma on the hamza for the plural, meaning that your faces will be disgraced for the servants of great strength. And let them enter the mosque, meaning: the Holy House and its environs, as they entered it the first time, and destroy, meaning: what they have conquered of your lands, “with complete destruction.”
17:8: 8 - Perhaps your Lord, O Children of Israel, will have mercy upon you, after taking revenge on you, and restore the state to you, but if you return, We will return, meaning: if you return to disobedience, We will return to punishment. Qatada said: So they returned, so God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, and they pay the jizyah willingly, and they are humiliated. And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers, a prison and confinement from the word confinement, which means confinement. Al-Hasan said: A mat means a mattress. He also referred to the mat that is spread out and laid out.
17:9: 9 - Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright, meaning: to the most correct path. It was said: the word that is most just, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, and gives good tidings, meaning: the Qur'an, to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have, that they will have, a great reward, which is Paradise.
17:10: 10 - And those who do not believe in the Hereafter - We have prepared for them a painful punishment, which is the Fire.
17:11: 11 - And the Almighty’s saying: And man calls forth, the waw was omitted in wording to receive the silent lam, like His saying: We will call the guards (al-Alaq 96:18), and it was also omitted in writing, but it is not omitted in meaning. Its meaning is: And man calls forth evil upon his wealth, his children, and himself, so he says when angry: O God, curse him and destroy him, and the like. His supplication for good, that is, like his supplication to his Lord [for good] that He bestow upon him blessings and well-being. If God answered his supplication for himself, he would be destroyed, but God does not answer with His grace. And man is ever hasty in supplicating for that which he does not like to be answered for. A group of the people of interpretation said this, and Ibn Abbas said: Impatience, he has no patience for prosperity or adversity. God 11. And man invokes evil And he invokes God Almighty when He is angry for evil upon himself, his family, and his wealth, or he invokes Him for what he thinks is good when it is evil. His invocation of good is like his invocation of good. And man is ever hasty He rushes to whatever comes to his mind without considering its consequences. It was said that what is meant is Adam, peace be upon him, for when the spirit reached his navel, he went to get up but fell. "It was narrated that he, peace be upon him, handed a prisoner to Sawda bint Zam'a, and she took pity on him because of his groaning, so she let his shoulders fall, so he fled and supplicated against her to have his hand cut off, then he regretted it and said, peace be upon him: O God, I am only a human being, so whoever supplicates against me, make my supplication a mercy for him. So it was revealed. "It is possible that what is meant by man is the disbeliever and by supplication is his hastening of punishment in mockery, like the saying of Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith: O God, support the best of the two wars, O God, if this is the truth from You verse. So he was answered and his neck was struck off patiently on the day of Badr.
17:12: 12 - The Almighty said: And We made the night and the day two signs, meaning: two signs indicating Our existence, Our oneness, and Our power. So We erased the sign of the night. Ibn Abbas said: God made the light of the sun seventy parts, and the light of the moon likewise, so He erased sixty-nine parts of the light of the moon and made them with the light of the sun. God It was narrated that God Almighty commanded Gabriel to move his wing over the face of the moon three times, so the light was extinguished and the light remained in it. Ibn Al-Kawwa asked Ali about the blackness on the moon. He said: It is a trace of erasure. And We have made the sign of the day visible, illuminating and illuminating, meaning that one can see by it. Al-Kisa’i said: The Arabs say absara’ an-nahar when it is bright enough to be seen by it, that you may seek bounty from your Lord and know the number of years and the account, meaning: If God had left the sun and moon as He created them, night would not be distinguished from day, the fasting person would not know when to break his fast, the time for Hajj, the time for the appointed time, or the time for rest and relaxation. And We have explained everything in detail. 12. And We made the night and the day two signs indicating the All-Powerful, the All-Wise, by their succession in one order with the possibility of others. So We erased the sign of the night meaning the sign which is the night, by supervising and adding to them for clarification like adding a number to the counted. And We made the sign of the day visible shining or visible to people from its sight so he sees, or visible to his family like his saying: a cowardly man if his family is cowardly. And it was said that the two signs are the moon and the sun, and the meaning of the statement is and We made the two lights of the night and the day two signs, or We made the night and the day with two signs and erasing the sign of the night which is the moon made it dark in itself and its light extinguished, or its light decreased little by little until the new moon, and making the sign of the day which is the sun visible means making it have rays that see things with its light. That you may seek bounty from your Lord To seek in the broad daylight the means of your livelihood and to attain thereby the clarification of your deeds. And that you may know By their differences or their movements. The number of years and the account And the type of account. And everything You need a god in the matter of religion and the world. We have explained it in detail We have clarified it in a clear and unambiguous manner.
17:13: 13 - The Almighty said: And We have fastened every person’s fate to his neck. Ibn Abbas said: His actions and what he was able to do will be with him wherever he is. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: His good and evil are with him and will not leave him until he is held accountable for them. Al-Hassan said: His good fortune and his bad fortune. On the authority of Mujahid: There is no newborn child but that there is a piece of paper around his neck on which is written whether he will be wretched or happy. The scholars of meaning said: By the bird he meant what God had decreed for it to do and what it would become of happiness or misery. It was called a bird according to the custom of the Arabs regarding what they used to consider as good omens and bad omens from the occurrences of birds and their departures. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Qatibi said: He meant by the bird its share of good and evil, from their saying: So-and-so’s arrow flew with such-and-such, and he singled out the neck from among the other limbs because it is the place of necklaces and collars and other things that adorn or disfigure, so it followed the speech of the Arabs in likening necessary things to necks. And We will bring out for him, God Almighty says: And We will bring out for him, on the Day of Resurrection, a book. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Ya’qub read: And We will bring out for him, with the opening of the ya and the closing of the ra, meaning: And the bird will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a book. Abu Jaafar read yakhruj with a dammah on the ya’ and a fathah on the ra’. He will find it. Ibn Amir and Abu Ja`far read it with a damma on the ya`, a fatha on the lam, and a shaddah on the qaf, meaning: the person will find that book, i.e., he will be given it. The rest read it with a fatha on the ya`, which is light, meaning he will not see it unfolded. In the narrations: God the Most High commands the angel to fold the scroll when the servant's life is complete, so it will not be unfolded until the Day of Resurrection. 13. And We have bound every man to his bird His knowledge and what was decreed for him as if it had flown to him from a nest of the unseen and the nest of destiny, because they used to take good omens and pessimism from the appearance of the bird and its spirit, it was used metaphorically for what is the cause of good and evil from the destiny of God the Most High and the deeds of the servant. Around his neck means the collar is attached to his neck. And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book It is the record of his knowledge or his soul engraved with the traces of his deeds, because voluntary deeds cause states in the soul and therefore their repetition indicates that they have faculties, and its accusative as a direct object or a state of a deleted direct object, which is the pronoun of the bird, and this is supported by the reading of Yaqub, and he emerges from he emerged and he emerges and it was read, meaning God the Almighty, he finds it spread out to remove the cover, and they are two descriptions of the book, or he finds it is a description and spread out is a state of the direct object. Ibn Amir read it in the passive form from the verb I met him like this.
17:14: 14 - Read your book, meaning: He will be told: Read your book. God Almighty says: Sufficient for you this Day is yourself as a reckoner, an accountant. Al-Hasan said: He who made you your own accountant has been just towards you. Qatada said: On that day, he who was not a reader in this world will read. God
17:15: 15 - Whoever is guided is guided only for the benefit of himself, for his reward is due, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment, for his punishment is due to him. And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, meaning: no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another of sins, meaning: no one shall be punished for the sin of another, and We never punish until We have sent a messenger, establishing the proof and cutting off the excuse, and in it is evidence that what is obligatory is obligatory by hearing, not by reason.
17:16: 16 - And when We desire to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, Mujahid read: We commanded with emphasis, meaning: We gave power to its wicked ones, but they disobeyed. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ya’qub read We commanded with an extension, meaning: We increased its numbers. The rest read it with a shortened and lightened vowel, meaning: We ordered them to obey, but they disobeyed. It is possible that it means we made them leaders, and it is possible that it means we made them many. It is said: God ordered them, meaning God made them many. In the hadith: The best wealth is a mare that is ordered, meaning one with many offspring. It is also said: From it, the people ordered an affair if they increased in number, and it is not from the word order in the sense of action, for God does not order immorality. Abu Ubaidah chose the reading of the common people and said: Because the three meanings come together in it, meaning command, emirate, and abundance. Its affluent people are its pampered and wealthy people. But they committed wickedness therein, so the word came into effect upon it, meaning the punishment was due upon it. So We destroyed it with complete destruction, meaning: We ruined it and destroyed everyone in it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Bakr told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, that Zainab bint Abi Salamah told him, on the authority of Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, on the authority of Zainab bint Jahsh, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon her in a state of fear and said: “There is no god but God, woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a hole has been opened in the dam of Gog and Magog like this,” and he made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it. Zainab said: “I said: O Messenger of God, will we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us?” He said: Yes, if evil increases.
17:17: 17 - His saying: And how many generations have We destroyed meaning: the ones who denied, after Noah, frightening the infidels of Mecca, And sufficient is your Lord as Knower and Seeer of the sins of His servants, Abdullah bin Abi Awfa said: A century is one hundred and twenty years, so God sent the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the first century, and at the end of it was Yazid bin Muawiyah. It was said: One hundred years. It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Qasim on the authority of Abdullah bin Busr Al-Mazini, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed his hand on his head and said: This boy will live for a century.” Muhammad bin Al-Qasim said: We continued to count for him until he was one hundred years old, then he died. Al-Kalbi said: Eighty years. It was also said: Forty years.
17:18: 18 - Whoever desires the immediate, meaning this world, that is, the immediate home, We hasten for him therein whatever We will, of expansion and restriction, for whomever We intend, to do that to him or destroy him, Then We have made for him, in the Hereafter, Hell, which he will burn, entering its fire, censured and expelled, banished and banished.
17:19: 19 - And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort, does its work, while he is a believer - for those, their effort is ever appreciated, accepted.
17:20: 20 - Both of these and those We provide, meaning: We provide for both groups, those who want this world and those who want the Hereafter, from the gift of your Lord, meaning: He provides for both of them, then their situation differs in the end, and the gift of your Lord, the provision of your Lord, is not forbidden, prohibited from His servants. What is meant by gift is gift in this world, otherwise the disbelievers have no share in the Hereafter.
17:21: 21 - Look, O Muhammad, how We have favored some of them over others, in provision and [righteous] work, meaning: the seeker of the immediate and the seeker of the Hereafter, and the Hereafter has greater degrees and greater preference.
17:22: 22 - And do not make with God another god, the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is someone other than him. It was said: Its meaning is, O human being, do not make [another god with God], so that you will sit blamed and forsaken, blamed without praise, forsaken without victory.
17:23: 23 - The Almighty said: And your Lord has decreed, and your Lord has commanded, as Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Al-Hasan said. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: And your Lord has made it obligatory. Mujahid said: And your Lord recommended. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim that he read it as And your Lord commanded. He said: They attached the waw to the sad so it became a qaf. “That you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment,” meaning: He commanded that you be good to your parents, being dutiful to them and compassionate towards them. Either they reach old age with you, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read it with an alif for the dual form. Based on this, his saying, one of them or both of them, is a new statement, like the Almighty’s saying, Then many of them became blind and deaf (al-Ma’idah 5:71) and His saying, And those who did wrong conferred secretly, and His saying, those who did wrong, is the beginning. The rest read, they will reach old age for the singular form. Do not say to them, 'uff', there are three versions of it. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Yaqub read it with the fat-ha on the fa', and Abu Ja`far, Nafi`, and Hafs read it with the kasra on the fa' and with tanween, and the rest read it with the kasra on the fa' without tanween, and its meaning is one and the same, which is the word of hatred. Abu Ubaidah said: The origin of taff and alaf is dirt on the fingers when you twist them. It was said: Af is what is in the groin area of dirt, and taff is what is in the fingers. It was said: Uff is the dirt of the ear and Taff is the dirt of the nails. It was said: Uff is the dirt of the nail, and Taff is what you lift from the ground with your hand of something insignificant. Do not scold them, and do not rebuke them. And speak to them a generous word, that is, good, beautiful, and gentle. Ibn Al-Musayyab said: Like the words of a sinful slave to a rude master. Mujahed said: Do not name them, nor use their nicknames, but say: O my father [O my mother]. Mujahed said: In this verse also: If they reach such an age in your life that they urinate, do not feel disgusted by them, and do not say to them ugh when you remove the toilet and urine from them, as they used to remove it from you when you were young.
17:24: 24 - And lower to them the wing of humility, meaning be gentle with them and submit. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said, Be gentle with them so that you do not withhold anything they love. "Out of mercy, out of compassion, and say, 'My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small," meaning: if they were Muslims. Ibn Abbas said: This is abrogated by the statement, "It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists" (al-Tawbah 9:13). Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, I told Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman - meaning Al-Salami - on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The parent is the middle gate of Paradise, so protect him if you wish or neglect him. Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zarrad told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Idris al-Jurjani told us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Malini told us, Hasan ibn Sufyan told us, Yahya ibn Habib ibn Adi told us, Khalid ibn al-Harith told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Ata’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The pleasure of God is in the pleasure of the parent, and the wrath of God is in the wrath of the parent. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad bin Musa Al-Sayrafi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Saffar told us, Abu Jaafar Muhammad bin Ghalib bin Tamam Al-Dhabi told us, Abdullah bin Muslima told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one who shows off, no one who disobeys his parents, and no one who is addicted to alcohol will enter Paradise. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Bamwayh al-Isfahani told us, Abu Saeed Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Basri told us, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabah told us, Rabi’ ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Saeed al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May the nose of a man in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me be rubbed in the dust. May the nose of a man in whose presence the month of Ramadan comes and he is not forgiven be rubbed in the dust. May the nose of a man in whose parents reach old age and they do not admit him into Paradise be rubbed in the dust.”
17:25: 25 - Your Lord knows best what is in your souls, of being dutiful to your parents and disobedient to them, if you are righteous, dutiful and obedient after falling short as you were in fulfilling what was required of you regarding the rights of your parents and other things, then He is, to those who turn back [to Him], after disobedience, Forgiving. Saeed bin Jubair said about this verse: He is the man who hastens to his parents, intending nothing but good by doing so, and he will not be held accountable for it. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: The one who repents is the one who sins and then repents, then sins and then repents. Saeed bin Jubair said: Returning to goodness. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: It is returning to God in what He decrees and what befalls Him. On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are the ones who glorify God. His evidence is his saying: O mountains, echo with him (Saba’: 10). Qatada said: They are the worshippers. Awf bin Aqil said: They are those who pray the Duha prayer. Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn al-Husayn al-Ruqi al-Tusi told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ya`qub told us, Abu al-Nadr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, al-Hasan ibn Sufyan told us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Waki` told us, on the authority of Hisham, the companion of al-Dastawai, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Awf, on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the people of Quba while they were praying the Duha prayer, and he said: The prayer of the repentant is when the young camels have eaten their fill of the forenoon. Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir said: Al-Awab is the one who prays Maghrib and Isha prayers with me. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Angels surround those who pray between sunset and night prayers, and it is the prayer of the repentant.
17:26: 26 - The Almighty’s saying: And give the relative his right, meaning maintaining kinship ties, and what he meant by it is: human kinship, and most people agree with this. On the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein: He meant the kinship of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the poor and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully, meaning: do not spend your money on sin. Mujahed said: If a person spent all his money on what is right, it would not be extravagance, but if he spent a mudd on what is wrong, it would be extravagance. Ibn Masoud was asked about extravagance and he said: Spending money in a way that is not right. Shu`bah said: I was walking with Abu Ishaq on the road to Kufa, and he came to the door of a house made of plaster and brick, and he said: This is extravagance. In Abdullah’s words: Spending money unjustly.
17:27: 27 - Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, meaning: their allies. The Arabs say that anyone who adheres to the Sunnah of a people is their brother. And Satan was ever ungrateful to his Lord, ungrateful for a blessing.
17:28: 28 - And if you turn away from them, was revealed about Mahja', Bilal, Suhaib, Salim, and Khabbab, who would sometimes ask the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for what they needed, but he would not find anything, so he would turn away from them out of shyness from them and refrain from speaking, so And if you turn away from them was revealed, and if you turn away from these whom He commanded you to give, seek mercy from your Lord which you hope for, waiting for provision from God which you hope will come to you, then speak to them a gentle word gentle, which is the promise, meaning: promise them a beautiful promise. It was said: The gentle word is to say: May God provide for us and you.
17:29: 29 - And do not make your hand chained to your neck, Jabir said: A boy came and said: O Messenger of God, my mother is asking you for a coat of mail, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had nothing but his shirt, so he said to the boy: From one hour to another it will appear, so he returned another time, and he returned to his mother and she said: Tell him: My mother is asking you for the coat of mail you are wearing, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered his house and took off his shirt and gave it to him, and sat naked, so Bilal called the call to prayer, and they waited for him but he did not come out, so he occupied the hearts of his companions, so some of them entered upon him and saw him naked, so God Almighty revealed: And do not make your hand chained to your neck, meaning: And do not withhold your hand from spending in what is right like one whose hand is chained and is unable to extend it. And do not extend it, by giving, to the full extent, so that you give everything you have, so that you sit blamed, with [your questioners] blaming you for withholding if you do not give them. And the blamed one is the one who has done something that he blames himself for, or that someone else blames him for, deprived, cut off from you, with nothing to spend. It is said: I made him regret asking if you insist on him, and a beast of burdens if it is exhausted and weak. Qatada said: regretful regretting what you have missed.
17:30: 30 - Indeed, your Lord expands - expands the provision for whom He wills and restricts - that is, He restricts and restricts - Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Knowing and Seeing.
17:31: 31 - The Almighty said: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, poverty, We provide for them and for you, and that is because the people of ignorance used to bury their daughters alive for fear of poverty, so they were forbidden from doing so, and they were informed that their sustenance and the sustenance of their children was from God Almighty, Indeed, killing them was a great sin, Ibn Amir and Abu Jaafar read a sin with a fatha on the kha and a shortened ta. Ibn Kathir read with a kasra on the kha and an extended ta, and the others read with a kasra on the kha and a jazm on the ta, and the meaning of all is the same, i.e. a great sin.
17:33: 33 - And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right, and its right is what we narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The blood of a Muslim man is not permissible except in one of three cases: a man who disbelieved after his belief, or committed adultery after being married, or killed a soul without a soul in which case he is killed." And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, meaning: power and authority over the killer by killing him, Mujahid said. Al-Dahhak said: His authority is that he has the choice. If he wants, he can take revenge from him, if he wants, he can take blood money, and if he wants, he can forgive. Do not be excessive in killing. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: Do not be excessive with a ta’, addressing the guardian of the murdered person. The others read: with a ya’ for the absent person, meaning: The guardian should not be excessive in killing. They differed about this extravagance that was forbidden. Ibn Abbas and most of the commentators said: Its meaning is that no one should be killed except the killer. This is because in the pre-Islamic era, if one of them was killed, they would not be satisfied with killing his killer until they killed someone more honorable than him. Saeed bin Jubair said: If the killer is one person, then a group of people should not be killed instead of one person. And the people of the Age of Ignorance, if the one killed was a nobleman, would not be satisfied with killing the killer [alone] until they killed a group of his relatives with him. Qatada said: It means that the killer should not be mutilated. He was victorious, so the ha refers back to the one killed in his statement: And whoever is killed unjustly, meaning: The one killed is victorious in this world by requiring retaliation for his killer, and in the hereafter by expiating his sins and requiring Hell for his killer. This is the statement of Mujahid. Qatada said: The letter ha refers to the guardian of the murdered person, meaning that he is victorious over the murderer by obtaining compensation from him or the blood money. It was said in his saying: So he should not exceed the limits in killing, that he meant the aggressive killer, saying: He should not exceed the limits in killing without right, because if he did that, then the guardian of the murdered person would be victorious on my behalf by fulfilling the retribution from him.
17:34: 34 - "And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, until he reaches maturity. And fulfill your covenant," by doing what God has commanded and refraining from what God has forbidden. It was said: He meant by the covenant what a person commits himself to. The covenant was questioned, Al-Suddi said: It was required. It was said: The covenant is asked about the one who made the covenant, so it is said: Why did you break it, like the buried girl who is asked: Why was she killed?
17:35: 35 - And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with an even balance. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read with an even balance with a kasra on the qaf, while the rest read it with a damma. They are two languages, and it is the scale, whether small or large, meaning: with the scales of justice. Al-Hasan said: It is the qiban. Mujahid said: It is Roman. Another said: It is Arabic, taken from qist, which means justice, meaning: weigh with justice. The straight path - that is better and more suitable in outcome, meaning: in consequence.
17:36: 36 - And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Qatada said: Do not say: I saw, but you did not see it, I heard, but you did not hear it, I knew, but you did not know it. Mujahed said: Do not accuse anyone of something you do not know. Al-Qatibi said: Do not follow it with intuition and guesswork. In the language, it means following the trace. It is said: I followed someone, I followed him, and I followed him, and I followed his traces, and the rhyme was named after it, because they follow the traces. Al-Qatibi said: It is taken from the nape of the neck, as if he follows things, he follows them and gets to know them. The true meaning is: Do not speak [O human] based on guesswork and conjecture. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart - about all those one will be questioned. It was said that its meaning is that a person will be questioned about his hearing, sight, and heart. It was said: Hearing, sight, and heart will be asked about what a person has done. His saying: All of those means: all of these limbs and organs. According to the first opinion, those refers back to their owners. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Tahir Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Abu Ali Hamid bin Muhammad Al-Rafa’ told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdul Aziz told us, Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, Saad bin Aws Al-Absi told us, Bilal bin Yahya Al-Absi told me that Shatir bin Shakl told him on the authority of his father Shakl bin Hamid who said: “I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, teach me an incantation with which I may seek refuge. So he took my hand and said: Say: O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, the evil of my sight, the evil of my tongue, the evil of my heart, and the evil of my semen.” So I memorized it. Saad said: Semen is its fluid. 8- Then you will be asked on that Day about the pleasures, Muqatil said: meaning the infidels of Mecca, who were in goodness and pleasures in this world, so they will be asked on the Day of Resurrection about their gratitude for what they had, and they did not thank the Lord of the pleasures because they worshipped other than Him, then they will be punished for not being grateful, this is what Al-Hasan said. On the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: You will be asked on that Day about pleasure. He said: Security and health. Qatada said: God will ask every person who has been blessed about what He has bestowed upon him. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Al-Haitham Al-Turabi told us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamuyeh Al-Sarakhsi told us, Ibrahim ibn Khazim Al-Shashi told us, Abd ibn Hamid told us, Shababah told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Al-Ala’, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak ibn Arzam Al-Ash’ari, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The first thing that the servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection regarding blessings will be: Did We not give you good health and provide you with cold water to drink?’” Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juzajani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, Abu Saeed Al-Haytham bin Kulayb Al-Shashi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam bin Abi Iyas told us, Shaiban Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Abdul Malik bin Umair told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out at a time when no one went out or met him. Abu Bakr came to him and said: ‘What brought you, O Abu Bakr?’ He said: ‘I went out to meet the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to look at his face and to greet him.’ It was not long before Umar came and said: ‘What brought you, O Umar?’ He said: ‘Hunger, O Messenger of God.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And I have found some of that.’ So they went to the house of Abu Al-Haytham bin Al-Tayhan Al-Ansari, who was a man with many date palms and sheep, but he had no servants. They did not find him, so they said to his wife: ‘Where is your companion?’ She said: ‘Go get us fresh water,’ but he did not find him.” They were not long before Abu Al-Haytham came with a waterskin to draw water from and put it down. Then he came to embrace the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and sacrificed his father and mother for him. Then he went with them to his garden and spread out a rug for them. Then he went to a palm tree and brought a straw and put it down. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Why don’t you pick some of its fresh dates and unripe dates for us? He said: O Messenger of God, I wanted you to choose from its fresh dates and unripe dates. So they ate and drank from that water. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “This, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, is among the blessings that you will be asked about on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:cool shade, good fresh dates, and cool water.” Abu Al-Haytham went to prepare food for them, but the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do not slaughter a lactating woman. So he slaughtered a young goat or a young kid for them and brought it to them, and they ate. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do you have a servant? He said: No. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: So when captives come to us, come to us. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was brought two heads and there was no third with them. Abu Al-Haytham came to him and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Choose from them. He said: O Prophet of God, choose for me. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The one who is consulted is trustworthy. Take this one, for I saw him praying, and treat him well. Abu Al-Haytham took him to his wife and told her what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had said. His wife said: You will not achieve what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said unless you free him. He said: Then he is freed. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, did not send a prophet or a caliph except that he had two entourage: an entourage that enjoined him to do good and forbade him from evil, and an entourage that never failed to corrupt him. And whoever is protected from a bad entourage is protected. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Bliss is the health of the body, hearing, and sight. God asks His servants how they used them, and He knows that better than they do. This is His statement: Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart - about all those one will be questioned. (al-Isra’ 17:36) Akrima said: About health and leisure. Saeed bin Jubair said: About health, leisure and money. Imam Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan told us in Mecca, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, they said: Abdullah ibn Saeed ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There are two blessings in which many people are deceived: health and free time.’” Muhammad ibn Kaab said: He means about what He bestowed upon you through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: About Islam and the Sunnah. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: Making the laws easier and the Quran simpler.
17:37: 37 - And do not walk upon the earth exultantly, meaning with arrogance, haughtiness, and conceit, which is the interpretation of walking, so he took it out in the source, Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, meaning: you will not traverse it with your arrogance until you reach its end, and you will never reach the mountains in height, meaning: you will not be able to reach the mountains and be equal to them with your arrogance. Its meaning is: that a person does not attain anything with his arrogance and haughtiness, like someone who wants to tear the earth apart and reach the mountains but does not attain anything. It was said: This was mentioned because someone who walks with arrogance walks sometimes on his heels and sometimes on the balls of his feet, so it was said to him: You will not dig through the earth if you walk on your heels, and you will not reach the height of the mountains if you walk on the balls of your feet. Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juwzjani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, Al-Haitham bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Uthman bin Muslim bin Hormuz, on the authority of Nafi’ bin Jubayr bin Mut’am, on the authority of Ali, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked, he would walk with a swaying motion, as if he were descending from a steep slope.” Abu Muhammad al-Jurjani told us, Abu al-Qasim al-Khuza’i told us, al-Haytham ibn Kulayb told us, Abu ‘Isa al-Tirmidhi told us, Qutaybah ibn Sa’d told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu Yunus, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I have never seen anything more beautiful than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was as if the sun was running in his face, and I have never seen anyone walk faster than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was as if the earth was being folded up for him. We would exert ourselves, but he did not care.”
17:38: 38 - "All of that was evil and hateful to your Lord," Ibn Amir and the people of Kufa read: raising the hamza and adding the ha', as an addition, and its meaning is: All of what we mentioned from His statement: "And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him was evil" meaning: What we counted for you was evil and hateful to your Lord, because He has counted good things like His statement: "And give the relative his right And lower to them the wing of humility" and other than that. Others read: bad in the accusative case with a tanween, meaning: everything we mentioned from His saying: And do not kill your children to this point is bad, with no good in it, since it all refers back to what is prohibited and nothing else, and he did not say disliked because it includes an advancement and a delay, and its meaning is: all of that was disliked, bad: [And his saying disliked is for repetition, not for description, its metaphor is: all of that was bad and it was disliked], or it refers back to the meaning and not the word, because bad is the sin and it is masculine.
17:39: 39 - That which we mentioned, is from what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom. And everything that God has commanded or forbidden is His wisdom. And do not make with God another god, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed these verses, and what is meant by that is the nation, or you will be thrown into Hell, blamed and expelled, banished and removed from all good.
17:40: 40 - The Almighty’s saying: Has your Lord chosen you? meaning: He chose you and made for you the chosen ones and for Himself what is not chosen, meaning: He chose you, with sons and took for Himself daughters from among the angels, because they used to say that the angels were the daughters of God, Indeed, you are saying a terrible word, addressing the polytheists of Mecca.
17:41: 41 - The Almighty said: And We have certainly explained in this Qur’an, meaning: [what was mentioned of] lessons, wisdom, examples, rulings, arguments, and information, and the emphasis is for emphasis and repetition, that they may remember, meaning: that they may remember and be admonished. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read with a sukoon on the dhal and a damma on the kaf, and likewise in Al-Furqan. And it does not increase them, our explanation and our remembrance, except in aversion, going away and distancing from the truth.
17:42: 42 - Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists, If there were with Him gods as they say, Hafs and Ibn Kathir read they say with a ya’ and the others read it with a ta’, then they would have sought, meaning the gods, a way to the Lord of the Throne, with exaggeration and force to remove His kingdom, as the kings of the world do to each other. It was said: Its meaning is that they sought a way to the Lord of the Throne by drawing closer to Him. Qatada said: So that they may know God and His grace and seek what brings them closer to Him. The first is more correct. Then He exonerated Himself, and the Almighty said:
17:43: 43 - Glory be to Him, and He is far above what they say. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read you say with a ta’ and the others with a ya’, a great exaltation.
17:44: 44 - The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Hafs, and Ya’qub read glorify with a ta’, and the others read it with a ya’ because of the barrier between the verb and the feminine. There is nothing but glorifies Him with praise. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: There is nothing living but glorifies Him with praise. Qatada said: It means animals and plants. Akrima said: The tree glorifies God, but the column does not. On the authority of Al-Muqaddam bin Ma’dikarib, he said: The dust glorifies God as long as it does not get wet, but if it gets wet it stops glorifying God. The bead glorifies God as long as it is not lifted from its place, but if it is lifted it stops glorifying God. The leaf glorifies God as long as it is on the tree, but if it falls it stops glorifying God. The garment glorifies God as long as it is new, but if it gets dirty it stops glorifying God. The water glorifies God as long as it is running, but if it is still it stops glorifying God. The wild beasts and birds glorify God when they cry out, but if they are still they stop glorifying God. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: There is not a single inanimate or living thing that does not glorify Him with praise, even the creaking of a door and the cracking of a ceiling. Mujahed said: All things glorify God, whether they are alive, dead, or inanimate, and their glorification is: Glory be to God and praise be to Him. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayr told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “We used to consider the verses as a blessing, but you consider them as a warning. We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey and water became scarce, so he said: ‘Seek some leftover water.’ So they brought a vessel with a little water in it, so he put his hand in the vessel and said: ‘Come to the blessed purification, and the blessing is from God.’ I saw the water springing forth from between the fingers of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we used to hear the food glorifying God while it was being eaten.” Some of the scholars of meaning said: The heavens, the earth, inanimate objects, and all other animals, except rational beings, glorify God as long as they indicate, through their subtle composition and wondrous appearance, their Creator. This becomes like glorification from them. The first is what was transmitted from the predecessors. Know that God Almighty has knowledge of inanimate objects that no one else can comprehend, so His knowledge should be entrusted to Him. But you do not understand their glorification, meaning you do not know the glorification of anyone except those who glorify Him in your languages and tongues. He is Forbearing and Forgiving.
17:45: 45 - The Almighty said: And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible veil, which prevents their hearts from understanding it and benefiting from it. Qatada said: It is the covering, and the concealed means the covering, like His saying: Indeed, His promise was to be fulfilled (Maryam 19:61). The object means the subject. It was said: It is hidden from people’s eyes, so they do not see it. Some of them interpreted it as a veil from the visible eyes, as narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that “when the verse: ‘Perish the hands of Abu Lahab’ was revealed, Abu Lahab’s wife came with a stone, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with Abu Bakr, but she did not see him. She said to Abu Bakr: Where is your companion? I have heard that he has satirized me. He said: By God, he does not speak poetry, nor does he say it. She returned saying: I had brought this stone to crush his head. Abu Bakr said: She did not see you, O Messenger of God. He said: No, there has always been an angel between me and her, covering me.”
17:46: 46 - "And We have placed over their hearts coverings, covers, lest they understand it", hatred that they understand it. It was said: lest they understand it, "and in their ears deafness", heaviness lest they hear it. "And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an", meaning if you say: There is no god but God in the Qur'an and you are reciting it, "they turn back in aversion", plural of nafir, like: qa'id, qa'ud, jalis, and julus, meaning aversion.
17:47: 47 - We know best what they listen to, it was said: to it is a connection, meaning: they seek to hear it, when they listen to you, while you are reciting the Qur'an, and when they are whispering, whispering about your matter. It was said: whispering, some of them say: this is crazy, and some of them say: a soothsayer, and some of them say: a magician, and some of them say: a poet. When the wrongdoers say, meaning: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and his companions, You follow none but a man bewitched, bewitched. [Mujahid said]: deceived. It was said: diverted from the truth. It is said: What bewitched you from such-and-such, meaning what diverted you? Abu Ubaidah said: That is, a man who has magic, and magic is the lung, that is, he is a human being like you, addicted to food and drink, he eats and drinks. The poet said: We see two places where the unseen is inevitable and we are enchanted by food and drink. That is: we feed and we entertain.
17:48: 48 - Look, O Muhammad, how they have given you examples, likenesses. They said: a poet, a magician, a soothsayer, and a madman. They have gone astray, so they are confused and have deviated, so they cannot find a way, meaning: to reach the path of truth.
17:49: 49 - "And they said, 'When we are bones' after death, 'and fragments'?" Mujahid said: dust. It was also said: debris. And fragments is everything that is broken and decayed of everything, like crumbs and debris. "Will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?"
17:50: 50 - Say to them, O Muhammad: Be stones or iron, in severity and strength. This is not an obligatory command, but rather an incapacitating command, meaning: Feel in your hearts that you are stones or iron in strength.
17:51: 51 - "Or a creation of what is great in your hearts," it was said: the sky, the earth [and the mountains]. Mujahid, Ikrimah, and most of the commentators said: It is death, for there is nothing greater in the soul of the son of Adam than death. That is, if you were death itself, I would kill you and resurrect you. “And they will say: Who will restore us?” Who will resurrect us after death? “Say: He who created you” – created you – the first time – and He who is able to create is able to restore. And they will shake their heads at you – that is, they will move them when you say that to them, mocking you, “and say: When is it?” – that is, the resurrection and the Day of Judgment. “Say: Perhaps it will be near” – that is, it is near, because perhaps from God is obligatory, similar to the statement of God Almighty: And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near (al-Ahzab 33:63).
17:52: 52 - "The Day He calls you from your graves to the place of resurrection, and you will respond with His praise", Ibn Abbas said: By His command. Qatada said: By obeying Him. It was said: Acknowledging that He is their Creator and Resurrector and they praise Him when praise will not benefit them. It was said: This is addressed to the believers, for they will be resurrected praising. "And you think that you have remained, in this world and in the graves, but a little", because if a person remained for thousands of years in this world and in the grave, that would be considered a little in comparison to the duration of the Day of Resurrection and eternity. Qatada said: They despise the duration of this world in comparison to the Resurrection.
17:53: 53 - The Almighty said: And tell My servants to say that which is best, Al-Kalbi said: The polytheists were harming the Muslims, so they complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God Almighty revealed: And tell My servants the believers to say to the disbelievers that which is best and not to reward them with their foolishness. Al-Hasan said: He says to him: May God guide you. And this was before the permission for jihad and fighting. It was said: It was revealed about Omar bin Al-Khattab, who was insulted by some infidels, so God commanded him to forgive. It was said: God commanded the believers to say and do what is best, meaning: the best trait. It was said: The best is the word of sincerity, There is no god but God. “Indeed, Satan sows discord among them,” meaning: he corrupts and sows enmity among them. Indeed, Satan is ever to mankind a clear enemy, meaning apparent enmity.
17:54: 54 - “Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you,” that is, He will grant you success so that you will believe, or if He wills, He will punish you, that is, He will cause you to die in polytheism so that you will be punished. This was said by Ibn Jurayj. Al-Kalbi said: If He wills, He will have mercy on you and save you from the people of Mecca, and if He wills, He will punish you and give them power over you. And We have not sent you over them as a guardian as a guardian and guarantor. It was said: The verse on fighting abrogated it.
17:55: 55 - And your Lord is most knowing of those in the heavens and the earth, meaning: Your Lord is the One who knows those in the heavens and the earth, so He made them different in their forms, morals, conditions, and religions. And We have certainly preferred some prophets over others. It was said that He made the people of the heavens and the earth different, just as He preferred some prophets over others. Qatada said about this verse: God took Abraham as a friend, and spoke to Moses directly, and said to Jesus: Be, and he was, and gave Solomon a kingdom that no one after him would have, and gave David the Psalms as He said: And We gave David the Psalms, and the Psalms is a book that God taught David, and it includes one hundred and fifty surahs, all of which are supplications, glorification, and praise of God Almighty, and in it there is nothing forbidden or permissible, nor obligations, nor limits. Meaning: You did not deny the superiority of the prophets, so how do you deny the superiority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his giving of the Qur’an? This is addressed to those who acknowledge the superiority of the prophets, peace be upon them, from among the People of the Book and others.
17:56: 56 - The Almighty said: “Say: Call upon those you claim besides Him,” that is, the polytheists were afflicted with a severe drought to the point that they ate dogs and carrion, so they sought help from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray for them. God Almighty said: Say to the polytheists Call upon those you claim besides Him that they are gods for they do not possess the power to remove harm drought and hunger from you nor to transfer to someone else, or to change the situation from hardship to ease.
17:57: 57 - Those whom they call upon seek a means of approach to their Lord, meaning those whom the polytheists call upon as gods whom they worship. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: They are Jesus, his mother, Ezra, the angels, the sun, the moon, and the stars. They seek that is, they ask their Lord for the means, that is, closeness. It was said: The means is the highest degree, that is, they supplicate to God in seeking the highest degree. It was said: The means is everything that brings one closer to God Almighty. His saying: Which of them is nearest? means: They look to see which of them is nearest to God and seek His intercession. Al-Zajjaj said: Which of them is nearest seeks a means to God Almighty and draws near to Him through righteous deeds, and they hope for His mercy, His Paradise, “and they fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to be feared,” meaning they seek to beware of Him. Abdullah bin Masoud said: The verse was revealed about a group of Arabs who worshipped a group of jinn. The jinn converted to Islam, but the humans who worshipped them did not know about their conversion to Islam, so they held on to their worship, so God reproached them and revealed this verse. Ibn Masoud read those who call with a taa.
17:58: 58 - And there is no town - and there is no town - but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection - meaning: destroying it and killing its people, or punishing it with a severe punishment - with various types of punishment if they disbelieve and disobey. Muqatil and others said: Its destroyer, with regard to the believers, is by causing death, and its punisher, with regard to the disbelievers, is by various types of punishment. Abdullah bin Masoud said: If adultery and usury appear in a village, God will permit its destruction. "It was in the Book, in the Preserved Tablet, inscribed," written. Ubadah bin al-Samit said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing God created was the pen. He said, ‘Write.’ It said, ‘What should I write?’ He said, ‘Destiny.’ And whatever was and whatever will be is eternal.”
17:59: 59 - The Almighty said: And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. Ibn Abbas said: “The people of Mecca asked [the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace] to turn Safa into gold for them and to move the mountains away from them so that they could farm. So God Almighty revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you wish to be patient with them, I will do so. And if you wish to give them what they asked for, I will do so. But if they do not believe, I will destroy them as I destroyed those who were before them [of the nations]. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, rather be patient with them.” So God Almighty revealed: And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs which the disbelievers of your people asked for except that the former peoples denied them so We destroyed them. If your people do not believe after the signs are sent, We will destroy them, because it is Our way with nations that if they ask for signs, then they do not believe after they are sent, that We destroy them and do not give them respite. And We have decreed that this nation be given respite in the punishment, so the Most High said: Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and more bitter (al-Qamar 54:46). Then He said: And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, illuminating and clear, but they wronged her, meaning: they denied that she was from God, as He said: Because they were wronging Our signs (al-A’raf 7:9), meaning: they denied. It was said: they wronged themselves by denying it, meaning: so We hastened the punishment upon them. We do not send the signs meaning: the lessons and evidence, except as a warning to the servants so that they may believe. Qatada said: God Almighty frightens people with whatever signs He wishes, so that they may return.
17:60: 60 - The Almighty said: And when We said to you, ‘Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people,’ meaning: they are in His grasp, they are not able to escape His will, so He is your protector and protector from them, so do not fear them and continue with what He has commanded you to do of conveying the message, as He said: And God will protect you from the people Al-Ma’idah - 67. And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, so most of them agree that what is meant by it is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw on the Night of Ascension of wonders and signs. Ibn Abbas said: It is a vision that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw with his own eyes. This is the opinion of Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan, Masruq, Qatada, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibn Jurayj and most of them. The Arabs say: I saw with my own eyes a vision or a vision. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned it to the people, some of them denied it and lied, so it was a trial for the people. Some people said: His soul was taken on a night journey, but not his body. Some of them said: He had two ascensions: an ascension of vision with the eye, and an ascension of vision with the heart. Some people said: By this vision he meant what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, that he and his companions entered Mecca, and he set out to travel to Mecca before the appointed time, but the polytheists stopped him, so he returned to Medina. His return in that year was after he had been informed that he would enter it as a trial for some of them, until he entered it the following year, so God Almighty revealed: God has certainly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger in truth (al-Fath 48:27). And the accursed tree in the Qur'an means the tree of Zaqqum. Its metaphor is: The accursed tree mentioned in the Qur'an. The Arabs say for every disgusting food: accursed food. It was said: [Its meaning is that it is accursed] to eat it. The tree was placed in the accusative case in apposition to the vision, meaning: And We did not make the vision that We showed you and the accursed tree except as a trial for the people, so the trial in the vision was what we mentioned. The temptation in the cursed tree is from two aspects, one of them is that Abu Jahl said: Ibn Abi Kabshah promises you a fire that burns stones, then he claims that a tree will grow in it, and you know that fire burns trees. The second is that Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri said: Muhammad frightens us with Zaqqum, and we do not know Zaqqum except as butter and dates. Abu Jahl said: O girl, come and give us Zaqqum. So she brought dates and butter, and he said: O people, [make us zaqqum], for this is what Muhammad frightens you with. So God Almighty described it in As-Saffat. It was said: The cursed tree is: the one that twists around the tree and dries it up, meaning the kashooth. And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression, meaning: great rebellion and insolence.
17:61: 61 - "And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He said, 'Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?'" That is, I created him from clay and brought him. This is what was narrated on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that God Almighty sent Iblis until he took a handful of the earth's soil, from its sweet and salty soil, and created Adam from it. So whoever He created from sweet soil is happy, even if he is the son of disbelievers, and whoever He created from salt is miserable, even if he is the son of prophets.
17:62: 62 - He said, meaning Satan: Have you seen, meaning he told me, and the kaf is to emphasize the address, this one whom You have honored over me, meaning: preferred over me: If You delay give me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely devour his offspring, meaning: I will eradicate them by misguidance. It is said that the locusts devour the crops if they eat them all. It was said: it is from the saying of the Arabs, nak al-daba yanhankahu: if he tied a rope to its lower jaw to lead it, meaning: I will lead them however I wish. It was said: I will take control of them by seduction, except a few, meaning the infallible ones whom God Almighty excepted in His saying: Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority (al-Hijr 15:42).
17:63: 63 - He said God: Go, and whoever follows you among them, Hell will be your recompense meaning: your recompense and the recompense of your followers, an abundant recompense, plentiful and complete. It is said: I made it plentiful, I made it plentiful.
17:64: 64 - And his saying: And provoke, and belittle and exhaust whoever you can of them, meaning: of the descendants of Adam, with your voice, Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: By calling to disobey God. And every caller to disobey God [is from the army of Satan. Al-Azhari said: Its meaning is: Call them with a call that will provoke them to your side, i.e., make them look down on you. Mujahed said: With singing and flutes. And attack them with your cavalry and infantry. It was said: Gather your plots and your cavalry against them. It is also said: Ajlba and Jalba if they shouted. He said: Shout with your cavalry and infantry and urge them against him by seduction. Muqatil said: Seek help against them from your soldiers’ riders and infantry. The cavalry is the riders, and the foot is the infantry. The commentators said: Every rider and walker who commits sins against God is one of Satan’s soldiers. Mujahid and Qatada said: He has horses and men from the jinn and humans, and he is everyone who fights in disobedience, and the man, the men and the women are one, it is said: a man and a man, like: merchant and trader, and rider and rider, and Hafs read and your man with a kasra on the jim and they are two languages. And share with them in wealth and children. Sharing in wealth means everything that is acquired from something forbidden, or spent on something forbidden. This is the opinion of Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Saeed bin Jubair. Ata’ said: It is usury. Qatada said: It is what the polytheists used to forbid from livestock, such as the bahīrah, the sa’ibah, the wasīlah, and the ham. Ad-Dahhak said: It is what they used to slaughter for their gods. As for the partnership in children: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is the buried girl. Mujahed and Al-Dahhak said: They are the children of fornication. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: It is that they made their children Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians. Another narration from Ibn Abbas: It is their naming of their children Abd al-Harith, Abd Shams, Abd al-Uzza, Abd al-Dar, and the like. It was narrated on the authority of Jaafar bin Muhammad that the devil sits on a man’s penis, and if he does not say: In the name of God, he has intercourse with his wife and ejaculates into her vagina as a man ejaculates. It was narrated in some report: There are among you two who are lost. It was said: Who are the lost? He said: Those who are joined by the jinn. It was narrated that a man said to Ibn Abbas: My wife woke up and there was a flame of fire in her vagina. He said: That is from the intercourse of the jinn. In the hadiths: When Satan was brought out to earth, he said: O Lord, You brought me out of Paradise for the sake of Adam, so give me power over him and his offspring. He said: You are the one who gives power. He said: I cannot do it except through You, so give me more. He said: Incite whomever you can of them with Your voice, the verse. So Adam said: O Lord, You have given Satan power over me and my offspring, and I cannot do it except through You. He said: No child will be born to You except that You will assign someone to protect him. He said: Give me more. He said: A good deed is rewarded tenfold, and a bad deed is rewarded likewise. He said: Give me more. He said: Repentance is offered as long as the soul is in the body, so He said: Give me more. He said: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves (al-Zumar 39:53). In the hadith: That Satan said: O Lord, You sent prophets and revealed books, so what is my recitation? He said: Poetry. He said: What is my book? He said: Tattooing. He said: Who are my messengers? He said: The priests. He said: Where is my dwelling? He said: Baths. He said: Where is my seat? He said: The markets. He said: What is my food? He said: That which my name is not mentioned over. He said: What is my drink? He said: All intoxicants. He said: What is my rope? He said: Women. He said: What harms me? He said: Psalms. The Almighty said: He promised them, meaning: from them the good in their obedience to You. And it was said: Tell them: There is no Paradise, no Hell, and no resurrection. And Satan promises them nothing but delusion, and delusion is embellishing falsehood with what is thought to be true. If it is said: How did God mention these things when He says: God does not command immorality (al-A’raf 7:28)? It was said: This is by way of threat, like the Almighty’s saying: Do whatever you will (Fussilat 41:40), and like the saying of the speaker: Do whatever you will and you will see.
17:65: 65 - His saying: “Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs,” meaning a guardian over whom the matter is entrusted.
17:66: 66 - The Almighty said: Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you meaning: He drives and sails the ship for you, in the sea that you may seek of His bounty meaning that you may ask for His provision, Indeed, He is to you Merciful.
17:67: 67- And when distress touches you, severity and fear of drowning, into the sea, you go astray, that is, vanish and fall, whom do you call upon, of the gods, except Him, except God, so you find no helper other than Him or anyone else, but when He delivered you, answered your call and saved you from the terror of the sea and brought you out, to the land, you turned away, from faith, sincerity and obedience, in ingratitude for His blessings, and man is ever ungrateful.
17:68: 68 - Do you then feel secure that He will not cause you to be swallowed up by the land side meaning that He will not send upon you a storm of stones from the sky, as He rained upon the people of Lot. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Qutaybi said: A storm of stones is the wind that throws pebbles, which are small stones, and then you will not find for yourselves a protector Qatada said: a protector.
17:69: 69 - Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it, meaning into the sea, another time, “and send upon you a violent wind,” Ibn Abbas said: meaning a storm, which is a strong wind. Abu Ubaidah said: It is the wind that crushes everything, that is, it crushes and destroys it. Al-Qatibi said: It is the one that cuts the trees, i.e. breaks them. He will drown you because of your disbelief, then you will not find for yourself against Us any supporter or avenger, and submit means follower, i.e. a follower demanding revenge. It was said: Who follows us in denial? Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read that we swallow up, and send, and return you, and send, and fana’idrakum with a noon in them, because of the saying upon us. The others read it with a ya’ because of the saying: except for Him. Abu Ja’far and Ya’qub read and he will drown you with a ta’, meaning the wind.
17:70: 70 - The Almighty said: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It means that they eat with their hands, unlike the human being who eats from the ground with his mouth. It was narrated on his authority that he said: With the mind. Ad-Dahhak said: With speech. Ata’ said: With straightening and extending the stature, and the animals leaning on their faces. It was also said: With a beautiful image. It was also said: Men have beards, and women have forelocks. It was also said: By making all other things subservient to them. It was also said: Because among them is the best nation brought forth for mankind. “And We carried them on land and sea,” meaning: We carried them on land on beasts and at sea on ships. And We provided them with good things, meaning: delicious foods and drinks. Muqatil said: ghee, butter, dates, and sweets. And He made the provision of others that which is not hidden. And We preferred them over many of those We created, with a marked preference. The apparent meaning of the verse is that He preferred them over many of those He created, not over all of them. Some people said: They are superior to all creation except the angels. Al-Kalbi said: They are superior to all creatures except for a group of angels: Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, the Angel of Death, and their likes. There is a difference of opinion about the preference of angels over humans. Some people said: They are preferred over all creation and over all angels. The majority may be used in place of all, as God Almighty said: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? until His saying: And most of them are liars Ash-Shu’ara’ 221/222. That is, all of them. In the hadith on the authority of Jabir, he said: “When God created Adam and his descendants, the angels said: O Lord, You created them to eat, drink, and marry, so make this world for them and the Hereafter for us. God Almighty said: I will not make one whom I created with My hands and breathed into from My spirit like one to whom I said: Be, and he was.” It is better to say: The common believers are better than the common angels, and the elite believers are better than the elite angels. God Almighty said: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - those are the best of creation (al-Bayyinah 98:7). It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The believer is more honorable to God than the angels who are with Him.
17:71: 71 - The Almighty said: On the Day We will call every people with their leader, Mujahid and Qatada said: with their prophet. Abu Salih and Ad-Dahhak said: with their book that was revealed to them. Al-Hassan and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: By their deeds. Qatada also said: In their book in which are their deeds, as evidenced by the context of the verse. So whoever is given his record in his right hand, and the record is called an imam, as God Almighty said: And We have recorded all things in a clear register (Ya-Sin 36:12). On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: By the Imam of their time who called them in this world to misguidance or guidance. God Almighty said: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command (Al-Anbiya’: 73), and He said: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire (al-Qasas 28:41). It was said: With their deity. And on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: Every people gather with their leader in good and evil. Muhammad bin Kaab said: By their Imam. It was said: I mean by their mothers. There are three aspects of wisdom in this: one for the sake of Jesus, peace be upon him, the second for the honor of Hassan and Hussein, and the third so that the children of fornication will not be disgraced. So whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their record, and they will not be wronged a thread. That is, their right will not be diminished by the amount of a thread.
17:72: 72 - "And whoever is blind in this," they differed about this reference, so some people said: It refers to the blessings that God Almighty has enumerated, so in these verses from His saying: "Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you, to His saying as a preference," He says: And whoever among you is blind in these blessings that he has seen, "he is in, in the matter, of the Hereafter, which he has not seen or witnessed, blind and further astray from the path," this is narrated from Ibn Abbas. Others said: It refers to the world. He says: Whoever in this world is blind of heart to seeing God’s power and His signs and seeing the truth, he will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray, meaning: he will have lost his way. It was said: He who is blind to consideration in this world will be blind to apology in the hereafter. Al-Hassan said: Whoever is a misguided disbeliever in this world, will be blind and more astray in the Hereafter, because his repentance is accepted in this world, but his repentance is not accepted in the Hereafter. Some readers pronounce these two letters with a fatha, while others pronounce them with a kasra. Abu Omar pronounces the first with a kasra and the second with a fatha, so he is more blind in the Hereafter, because of his saying: and more astray from the path.
17:73: 73 - The Almighty said: And they almost tempted you away from what We revealed to you the verse. They differed about the reason for its revelation: Saeed bin Jubair said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to touch the Black Stone, but the Quraysh prevented him, and said: [Do not touch] until you touch our gods and touch them. So he said to himself: I have no problem doing that, and God Almighty knows that I am reluctant to do it, after He calls me to touch the Black Stone. It was said: They asked him to touch their gods so that they would submit and follow him, so he thought about that, so God revealed this verse. Ibn Abbas said: “A delegation from Thaqeef came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We pledge allegiance to you on the condition that you give us three things. He said: What are they? They said: That we do not bow down - that is, in prayer - nor break our idols with our hands, and that you allow us to enjoy Al-Lat for a year without worshipping it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no good in a religion in which there is no bowing or prostration. As for you breaking your idols with your hands, that is for you, but as for the tyrant - meaning Al-Lat and Al-Uzza - I will not allow you to enjoy them. They said: O Messenger of God, we would like the Arabs to hear that you have given us what you have not given to others. If you fear that the Arabs will say, ‘You have given them what you have not given us,’ then say, ‘God has commanded me to do that.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent. The people hoped that his silence would lead him to give them that, so God Almighty revealed this verse: ‘And they almost tempted you’ to turn you away ‘from that which We have revealed to you’ ‘to invent’, to fabricate. “We have no choice but to do otherwise.” If you had done what they called you to do, they would have taken you as a friend. That is, they would have been your friend and your confidant.
17:74: 74 - And had We not strengthened you, on the truth with Our protection, you would have almost inclined, that is, leaned, to them a little, that is, close to doing so. If it is said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was infallible, so how is it permissible for him to approach what they asked for, and what they asked for is disbelief? It was said: That was a thought of the heart, and it was not a decision, and God Almighty has forgiven the talk of the soul. Qatada said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say after that: O God, do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye. The correct answer is: God Almighty said: And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them a little. And God made him steadfast, but he did not incline. This is like the Almighty’s saying: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few. (An-Nisa’: 83), [and He was gracious, but they did not follow.]
17:75: 75 - Then We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death, meaning: If you had done that, We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death, meaning: We would have doubled the punishment for you in this world and the hereafter. It was said: Weakness is torment. It was called weakness because the pain in it is doubled. Then you will not find for yourself a helper against Us, meaning: a helper who will prevent you from Our punishment.
17:76: 76 - The Almighty said: And indeed they almost tempted you from the land to expel you from it, they differed in the meaning of the verse, some of them said: This verse is Medinan.
