Al-Kalbi said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, the Jews hated his stay in Medina out of envy, so they came to him and said: O Abu Al-Qasim, you know that this is not the land of the prophets, for the land of the prophets is Ash-Sham [which is the holy land, and Abraham and the prophets, peace be upon them, were in it, so if you are a prophet like them, then go to Ash-Sham], and what prevents you from going out to it is your fear of the Romans, and God will protect you from the Romans if you are His messenger, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, camped three miles from Medina. In another narration: to Dhu Al-Hulayfah until his companions gather to him and he leaves, so God revealed this verse and the land here refers to Medina. Mujahid and Qatada said: The land is the land of Mecca. The verse is Meccan. The polytheists wanted to expel him from it, but God restrained them from him until He ordered him to emigrate, so he left by himself. This is more appropriate for the verse because what precedes it is report about the people of Mecca and the surah is Meccan. It was said: They are all the infidels. They wanted to provoke him from the land of the Arabs by gathering and mobilizing against him, but God Almighty prevented His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they did not achieve what they hoped for from him. Provocation means to disturb quickly. And then they will not remain after you meaning: after you. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, Hafs, and Ya'qub read after you based on the words of God Almighty: Those who stayed behind rejoiced in their sitting behind the Messenger of God (al-Tawbah 9:81). Their meaning is the same. Except for a little meaning: they will not remain after you except for a little until they perish. According to this first opinion: the duration of their lives. According to the second: the period between the Prophet's departure, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Madinah until they were killed at Badr.
17:77: 77- The Almighty’s saying: The way of those We sent before you of Our messengers means: like our way, so it was in the accusative case by deleting the kaf. And the way of God with the messengers is that if the nations deny them, He does not punish them as long as their prophet is among them, but if their prophet leaves their midst, He punishes them. And you will not find any change in Our way, meaning any alteration.
17:78: 78 - His saying: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun. They differed regarding the decline of al-Shams 91:It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud that he said: The decline of the sun is sunset. This is the saying of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, and Jabir said: It is the setting of the sun, and this is the saying of Ata’, Qatada, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and most of the followers. The meaning of the word combines them because the root of the word daluk is tilt, and the sun tilts when it declines and when it sets. And the interpretation of it as noon is the more correct of the two opinions, due to the large number of those who say it, and because if we interpret it as such, the verse would include all the prayer times. The decline of the sun includes the noon and afternoon prayers, and until the darkness of the night includes the sunset and evening prayers, and the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is the morning prayer. The Almighty said: Until the darkness of the night, meaning: the appearance of its darkness. Ibn Abbas said: the beginning of the night. Qatada said: the time of the sunset prayer. Mujahid said: the setting of the sun. And the Qur’an of dawn, meaning: the dawn prayer. The dawn prayer was called the Qur’an because it is not permissible except with the Qur’an. The Qur’an is in the accusative case for two reasons, one of which is that it is in apposition to the prayer, meaning: And establish the Qur’an of dawn, as Al-Farra’ said. The people of Basra said: on the basis of enticement, meaning: And upon you is the Qur’an of dawn. The Qur’an of dawn is witnessed, meaning: it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman told me that Abu Hurairah said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The prayer of a group is better than the prayer of one of you alone by twenty-five parts, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer. Then Abu Hurairah said: Recite if you wish: Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed.
17:79: 79 - The Almighty said: And during part of the night, pray therein. That is, get up after sleeping, and praying at night only happens after sleeping. It is said: he prayed at night if he got up after sleeping, and he slept if he slept. The meaning of the verse: standing at night for prayer. The night prayer was an obligation upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the beginning, and upon the nation, as God Almighty said: O you who are wrapped up in clothing, stand up in the night, except for a little (al-Muzzammil 73:1). Then the alleviation was revealed, so the obligation was abrogated for the nation by the five daily prayers, and the recommendation remained: God Almighty said: So recite what is easy of it (al-Muzzammil 73:20), and the obligation remained for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Three things are obligatory for me, and they are Sunnah for you: Witr, the siwak, and the night prayer.” The Almighty’s saying: As a voluntary act for you means: an addition for you. He means: an additional virtue, over all the other obligatory acts, that God has imposed upon you. Some people said that the obligation was abrogated in his case as in the case of the female slave, so it became a voluntary act. This is the opinion of Mujahid and Qatada, because God Almighty said: A voluntary act for you and did not say upon you. If it is said: What is the meaning of specialization, which is an increase in the right of all Muslims as in his right, may God bless him and grant him peace? It was said: The specification is because the voluntary prayers of the servants are an expiation for their sins, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was forgiven for his past and future sins, so his voluntary prayers do not work to expiate sins, so he still has an increase in his status. Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juwzjani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, Abu Saeed Al-Haitham bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Qutaybah and Bishr bin Muadh told us: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Ziyadah bin Alaqah, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood until his feet swelled. It was said to him: ‘Do you do this while your past and future sins have been forgiven?’ He said: ‘Should I not be a grateful servant?’” Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab ibn Malik told us, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Abi Bakra, on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Qays ibn Makhrama, that he told him, on the authority of Yazid ibn Khalid al-Juhani, that he said: I will watch the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, tonight, so I will rest on his threshold or his tent, and he will stand and pray two short rak`ahs, then he will pray two long rak`ahs, then he will pray two rak`ahs less than the two before them, [then he will pray two rak`ahs less than the two before them, then he will pray two rak`ahs less than the two before them], then he will pray the witr, so there are thirteen rak`ahs for that. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi Sa`id al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn `Abd al-Rahman, that he told him that he asked `Aisha, may God be pleased with her: How was the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Ramadan? She said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not increase in Ramadan or at any other time to more than eleven rak`ahs. He would pray four, and do not ask about their beauty and length, then he would pray four, and do not ask about their beauty and length, then he would pray three. `Aisha said: I said: O Messenger of God, do you sleep before you pray witr? He said: O `Aisha, my eyes sleep but my heart does not sleep.” Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Na’im Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Isfarayni told us, Abu ‘Awana Ya’qub ibn Ishaq told us, Yunus ibn Harun ibn ‘Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus, Ibn Abi Dhi’b, and ‘Umar ibn al-Harith told me that Ibn Shihab told them on the authority of ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr on the authority of ‘A’ishah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray eleven rak’ahs between the time he finished the ‘Isha’ prayer and the dawn prayer, saying the tasleem after every two rak’ahs, then he would pray the witr with one rak’ah, and he would prostrate for the amount of time it takes for one of you to recite fifty verses before raising his head. When the muezzin stopped the dawn call to prayer and dawn became clear to him, he would stand up and perform two short rak’ahs, then he would lie down on his right side until the muezzin came to him to call the iqamah and he would go out.” Some of them added to others. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Munib told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Hamid al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: We never wanted to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying except that we saw him, and we never wanted to see him sleeping except that we saw him. He said: He used to fast during the month until we would say he would not break his fast at all, and he would break his fast until we would say he would not fast at all. The Almighty said: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise. “Perhaps” is obligatory from God Almighty, because He does not fail to give His servants or do to them what He has made them desire. The praised station is: the station of intercession for his nation, because the first and the last will praise him in it: Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyan told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah bin Yazid Al-Maqri told us, Hayat told us, on the authority of Ka’b, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Jubayr, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you hear the muezzin, say what he says: Then pray for me, for whoever prays for me, God will pray for him ten times. Then ask God to grant me Al-Wasilah, for it is a station in Paradise that should not be given to anyone but one of God’s servants, and I hope that I am he. Whoever asks for Al-Wasilah for me, intercession will be granted to him.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abbas told us, Saeed bin Abi Hamza told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says when he hears the call: O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad the means and the excellence, and raise him to the praised station which You promised him, my intercession will be permissible for him on the Day of Resurrection.” Abu Hamid bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hiri told us, Hajib bin Ahmad Al-Tusi told us, Abdul Rahim bin Munib told us, Ya’la told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every prophet has a supplication that is answered, and I have saved my supplication as intercession for my nation, and it will be granted to you - God willing - whoever dies without associating anything with God.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Hajjaj bin Munhal said, Hammam bin Yahya told us, Qatada told us on the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The believers will be detained on the Day of Resurrection until they are concerned about that, and they will say: If only we could intercede with our Lord to relieve us from our place, then they will come to Adam and say: You are Adam, the father of mankind, God created you with His hand, and settled you in His Paradise, and His angels prostrated to you, and He taught you the names of everything, intercede for us with your Lord so that He may relieve us from this place of ours, then He will say: I am not here, and He will mention his sin that he committed and his eating from the tree, which he had forbidden, but go to Noah, the first prophet whom God sent to the people of the earth.” They will come to Noah, and he will say: I am not here with you. He will mention his sin that he committed, asking his Lord without knowledge. But go to Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful. They will come to Abraham, and he will say: I am not here with you. He will mention three lies that he told. But go to Moses, a servant to whom God gave the Torah, spoke to him, and brought him close in private. He said: They will come to Moses, and he will say: I am not here with you, and he will mention his sin that he committed by killing a soul, but go to Jesus, the servant of God and His Messenger, the Spirit of God and His Word. They come to Jesus, and he says: I am not there with you, but go to Muhammad, a servant whom God has forgiven his past and future sins. He said: They come to me, and I ask permission to see my Lord in His house, and He gives me permission to see him. When I see Him, I fall down in prostration, and He leaves me as long as God wills me to leave him. Then He says: Raise your head, O Muhammad, and say, and you will be heard. Intercede, and your intercession will be accepted. Ask, and you will be given. He said: So I raise my head, and I praise my Lord with praise and glorification that He teaches me, then I intercede, and He sets a limit for me, and I go out, and He admits them to Paradise. Qatada said: I also heard him say: “Then I go out and take them out of the Fire and admit them into Paradise. Then I return and ask permission to see my Lord in His house, and He gives me permission to see him. When I see Him, I fall down prostrating before Him, and He leaves me as long as God wills that He leaves me. Then He says: Raise your head, O Muhammad, and say, ‘You hear,’ and intercede, and your intercession will be granted. Ask, and you will be given.’ He said: So I raise my head and praise my Lord with praise and glorification that He teaches me. Then I intercede, and He sets a limit for me, so I go out and admit them into Paradise. [Then I return a third time and ask permission to see my Lord in His house, and He gives me permission to see him. When I see Him, I fall down prostrating, and He leaves me as long as God wills that He leaves me. Then He says: Raise your head, O Muhammad, and say, ‘You hear,’ and intercede, and your intercession will be granted. Ask, and you will be given.’ He said: So I raise my head and praise my Lord with praise and glorification that He teaches me. Then I intercede, and He sets a limit for me, so I go out and admit them into Paradise.” Qatada said: I also heard him say: Then he brought them out and brought them out of the Fire and admitted them into Paradise until none remained in the Fire except those whom the Qur’an had imprisoned - meaning, for whom eternity was obligatory. He said: Then he recited this verse: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station [He said: This is the praised station] that your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, promised.] And with this chain of transmission he said: [Muhammad bin Ismail narrated to us] Sulayman bin Harb narrated to us, Hammad bin Zaid narrated to us, Ma’bad bin Hilal al-Ghazi narrated to us: We went to Anas bin Malik and he mentioned the hadith of intercession, with its meaning, he said: So I ask permission to see my Lord and He gives me permission, and He inspires me with praises that I praise Him with which I do not have now, so I praise Him with those praises and prostrate before Him, and it is said: O Muhammad, raise your head and speak and you will hear [and ask and you will be given] and intercede and your intercession will be accepted, so I say: O Lord, my nation, my nation, and He says: Go and bring out from it whoever has in his heart the weight of a barley seed of faith, so I go and do so, then I return and praise Him with those praises and prostrate before Him and mention the same, and it is said: Go and bring out whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom or a mustard seed of faith. So I went and did that, then I returned and praised Him with those praises, then I prostrated before him and mentioned the same, then it is said: Go and bring out whoever has in his heart the slightest, slightest, smallest faith, so I went and did that. When we left Anas, we passed by Al-Hasan and greeted him and narrated to him the hadith up to this point, so he said: Hey! We said: He did not say anything more than that, so he said: He narrated to me while he was [at that time] twenty years ago as he narrated to you. Then he said: Then I return a fourth time and praise Him with those praises, then I prostrated before him and it is said: O Muhammad, raise your head and say and you will be heard, ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. So I say: O my Lord, do You permit me regarding the one who said, There is no god but God? He says: By My might, majesty, pride and greatness, I will surely bring out from it whoever said, There is no god but God. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that he said: The sun will come near on the Day of Resurrection until the sweat reaches half of the ear. While they are like that, they will call for help from Adam, then from Moses, then from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He will intercede to judge between creation, and he will walk until he takes hold of the ring of the door. On that day, God will raise him to a praiseworthy station, and all the people of the assembly will praise him. And Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Mamuyyah informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us, Muhammad ibn Hamuyyah informed us, Saeed ibn Sulayman informed us, Mansur ibn Abi al-Aswad informed us, al-Layth informed us, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the first of them to go out [when they are sent], and I am their leader when they come, and I am their orator when they listen, and I am their intercessor when they are detained [and I am their bearer of good tidings when they despair] of honor, and the keys on that day will be in my hand, and the banner of praise on that day will be in my hand, and I am the most honored of the children of Adam in the sight of my Lord, and a thousand servants will circulate around me as if they were hidden eggs or scattered pearls.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Al-Hakam bin Musa told us, Maqal bin Ziyad told us on the authority of Al-Awza’i, Abu Ammar told me, Abdullah bin Farukh told me, Abu Hurairah told me, he said, may God be pleased with him: I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and the first for whom the grave will split open, and the first intercessor, and the first for whom intercession will be accepted. There are many hadiths about intercession, and the first to deny it was Amr ibn Ubayd, who is an innovator according to the consensus of the Sunnis. It was narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Suhaib al-Faqir who said: I was fascinated by the opinion of the Khawarij, and I was a young man, so we went out intending to perform Hajj. We passed by Madinah, and there was Jabir bin Abdullah telling people about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned the people of Hell. I said to him: O companion of the Messenger of God, what is this that they are telling, while God, the Almighty, says: Indeed, whoever you admit to the Fire - I have disgraced him (Al Imran 3:192) and Every time they want to get out of it, they will be returned to it (Sajdah: 20). He said: O young man, do you recite the Qur’an? I said: Yes. He said: Have you heard of the station of Muhammad al-Mahmoud to which God will send him? I said: Yes. He said: It is the station of Muhammad al-Mahmoud through which God will bring out those who will be brought out of the Fire. [Then he described the placement of the bridge and the people passing over it], and that some people will come out of the Fire after they have been in it. He said: So we returned and said: Do you think this old man is lying about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? It was narrated on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty took Abraham as a friend, and your companion is the beloved of God and the most honorable of creation to God. Then he recited: ‘Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a position of praise.’” [He said: He will sit on the throne.] [On the authority of Mujahid, regarding the Almighty’s saying: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a position of praise, he said: He will seat him on the throne.] On the authority of Abdullah bin Salam, he said: He makes him sit on the chair.
17:80: 80 - The Almighty said: And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and let me exit a truthful exit.’ What is meant by the entrance and exit is the entry and exit, and the people of interpretation differed about it: Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He let me in with a truthful entrance: Medina. And he brought me out with a truthful exit: Mecca. It was revealed when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to emigrate. Ad-Dahhak said: And He brought me out with a true exit: from Mecca, safe from the polytheists, And He brought me in with a true entrance: Mecca, appearing over it with the opening. Mujahed said: “Enter me into the matter with which you sent me of prophecy with a true entrance into Paradise, and take me out of this world, and I have fulfilled what is required of me of its right, with a true exit.” On the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: He let me enter with a truthful entrance: Paradise, and He let me exit with a truthful exit: from Mecca. It was said: Enter me into Your obedience, and take me out of the prohibitions. It was said: Its meaning is: Enter me where You have entered me with truthfulness, and take me out with truthfulness. That is: Do not make me one of those who enter with one face and exit with another, for the one with two faces will not be safe or respected with God. He described the entry and exit as truthful, because the exit and entry lead to victory, honor, and the state of religion. He also described the foot as truthful, saying: They will have a sure footing with their Lord (Yunus 10:2). And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority. Mujahid said: A clear argument. Al-Hasan said: A strong kingdom with which You will grant me victory over those who oppose me, and apparent honor with which I will establish Your religion. So God promised him that He would take away the kingdom of Persia, Rome, and others and give it to him. Qatada said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that he would not be able to do this without a supporting authority, so he asked for a supporting authority: the Book of God, His limits, and the establishment of His religion.
17:81: 81 - The Almighty said: “And say, ‘The truth has come,’ meaning the Qur’an, ‘and falsehood has perished,’ meaning, the devil has gone. Qatada said, and Al-Suddi said: The truth is Islam, and falsehood is polytheism. It was said: The truth is the worship of God, and falsehood is the worship of idols. Verily, falsehood is bound to perish. It is said: his soul perished, meaning it left. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Sadaqah bin Al-Fadl told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar bin Abdullah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Mecca on the day of the conquest, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols. He began to poke them with a stick [in his hand] and say: ‘The truth has come and falsehood has perished.’ ‘The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor repeats.’”
17:82: 82 - The Almighty said: And We send down from the Qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers. It was said: From is not for partiality, and its meaning is: And We send down from the Qur’an that which is all healing, that is: clarification from misguidance and ignorance, by which what is different is made clear, what is problematic is made clear, and one is cured from doubt, and one is guided from confusion, so it is a healing for the hearts by removing ignorance from them as a mercy for the believers. And it only increases the wrongdoers in loss, because the wrongdoer does not benefit from it, while the believer benefits from it and it is a mercy for him. It was said: The loss increases for the oppressor, as every verse that is revealed brings renewed denial from them and increases their loss. Qatada said: No one has sat with this Qur’an without leaving it with an addition or a subtraction. God has decreed what He has decreed, as healing and mercy for the believers, and He does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.
17:83: 83 - The Almighty said: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away, from remembering and supplicating to Us, and distances himself, meaning he distances himself from Us, meaning he abandons drawing close to God through supplication. Ata' said: He became arrogant and proud, and Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i break the nun and the hamzah, and Abu Bakr opens the nun and breaks the hamzah, and Ibn Amir and Abu Ja'far read and he was far away like he came. It was said: it means he was far away, and it was said: he was far from the rising, which is getting up and standing. And when evil touches him, that is, hardship and harm, he is despairing, that is, hopeless and despondent. It was said: Its meaning is that he beseeches and supplicates when he is in harm and hardship, and if the answer is delayed, he despairs. And the believer should not despair of the answer, and if it is delayed, he should stop supplicating.
17:84: 84 - The Almighty said: “Say: Each one acts according to his own nature.” Ibn Abbas said: According to his own way. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: According to his intention. Muqatil said: On his creation Al-Farra said in his own way. Al-Qatibi said: According to his nature and disposition. It was said: On the path he chose for himself, and it is from the form. It is said: I am not of my form nor my likeness, and they are all close together. The Arabs say: A path with many branches if the paths branch off from it. The metaphor of the verse: Everyone works according to what resembles him, as it is said in the proverb: Every person is similar in his actions. Your Lord knows best who is best guided to the path.
17:85: 85 - The Almighty said: “And they ask you about the soul. Say, ‘The soul is from the command of my Lord.’” The verse. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qais bin Hafs told us, Abdul Wahid - meaning Ibn Ziyad - told us, Al-A'mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: While I was walking with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the fields of Medina, and he was leaning on a palm branch that he had with him, he passed by a group of Jews. Some of them said to each other: Ask him about the spirit. Some of them said: Do not ask him, he will not come up with anything about it that you dislike. Some of them said: Let us ask him. A man from among them stood up and said: O Abu Al-Qasim, what is the spirit? He remained silent. I said: Revelation is being sent to him. I stood up, and when the revelation was revealed to him, he said: “And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.” Al-A'mash said: This is how it is in our reading. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The Quraysh gathered and said: Muhammad was raised among us with trustworthiness and honesty, and we do not accuse him of lying. He claimed what he claimed, so send a group of people to the Jews in Medina and ask them about him, for they are people of the Book. So they sent a group to them, and the Jews said: Ask him about three things. If he answers all of them or does not answer any of them, then he is not a prophet. If he answers two and does not answer one, then he is a prophet. So ask him about the young men who were lost in the early days, what happened to them? For they had an amazing story. And about a man who reached the east and the west of the earth, what is his story? And about the soul? So they asked him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will tell you what you asked tomorrow, and he did not say, God willing. So the revelation continued - Mujahid said: twelve nights, and it was said: fifteen days, and Ikrimah said: forty days - and the people of Mecca were saying: Muhammad promised us tomorrow and we have woken up without him telling us anything, until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saddened by the delay of the revelation and he was distressed by what the people of Mecca were saying, then Gabriel came down with his saying: And never say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow’, except if God wills, and the story of the youths was revealed: Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs a wonder? And it was revealed about those who reached the East and the West: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn, and it was revealed about the soul: “And they ask you about the soul. Say, ‘The soul is from the command of my Lord.’” They differed about the spirit that was asked about. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is Gabriel, and this is the saying of Al-Hasan and Qatada. It was narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: He is an angel with seventy thousand faces, each face has seventy thousand tongues, with all of which he glorifies God Almighty. Mujahed said: He was created in the form of human beings, with hands, feet, and heads, and they are not angels, nor are they people, and they eat food. Saeed bin Jubair said: God Almighty did not create a creation greater than the spirit other than the throne. If He wanted to swallow the seven heavens and the seven earths and whoever is in them with one bite, He would have done so. The image of His creation is like the image of the angels, and the image of His face is like the image of humans. He will stand on the right of the throne on the Day of Resurrection, and he is the closest of creation to God Almighty today at the seventy veils, and he will be closest to God on the Day of Resurrection, and he is one of those who intercede for the people of monotheism. If there were not a veil of light between Him and the angels, the people of the heavens would have been burned by his light. It was said: The spirit is the Qur’an. It was said: What is meant by it is Jesus, peace be upon him, for he is the spirit of God and His word, and its meaning is: He is not as the Jews say nor as the Christians say. Some people said: It is the spirit composed of creation by which man lives, and this is the most correct. Some people spoke about it, and some of them said: It is blood. Don’t you see that when an animal dies, nothing is lost except the blood? Some people said: It is the animal’s soul, as evidenced by the fact that it dies due to the retention of breath. Some people said: It is an offer. Some people said: It is a delicate body. Some of them said: The soul is a meaning in which light, goodness, elevation, and permanence are combined. Do you not see that if it exists, the human being is described with all of these qualities, but if it leaves, everything is gone? The first of the sayings is that his knowledge is entrusted to God Almighty, and this is the saying of the people of the Sunnah. Abdullah bin Buraidah said that God did not give a close angel or a sent prophet knowledge of the soul. And the Almighty said: “Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord.” It was said: From the knowledge of my Lord. And of knowledge you have been given only a little meaning: compared to the knowledge of God. It was said: This is addressed to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: It is addressed to the Jews because they used to say, We were given the Torah, which contains much knowledge. It was said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew the meaning of the soul, but he did not tell anyone about it because his failure to tell anyone about it was evidence of his prophethood. The first is more correct, because God Almighty has kept His knowledge to Himself.
17:86: 86 - The Almighty said: And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you, meaning the Qur’an. Its meaning is: Just as We have prevented you and others from having knowledge of the spirit, if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you, meaning the Qur’an, and then you would not find for yourself concerning it a protector against Us.
17:87: 87 - Except by mercy from your Lord. This is an isolated exception, the meaning of which is: But We do not will that, as a mercy from your Lord. His favor upon you was great. If it is said: How can the Qur’an be lost, when it is the word of God Almighty? It was said: What is meant by it is: erasing it from the Qur’ans and removing what is in the hearts. Abdullah bin Masoud said: Read the Qur’an before it is taken away, for the Hour will not come until it is taken away. It was said: These copies of the Qur’an will be taken away, so what about what is in people’s hearts? He said: It will pass over it at night and what is in their hearts will be taken away, and they will wake up not having memorized anything and not finding anything in the copies of the Qur’an, then they will delve into poetry. On the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, he said: The Hour will not come until the Qur’an returns from where it was revealed, making a sound around the Throne like the buzzing of bees. The Lord will say: What is wrong with you, while He is more knowledgeable? He will say: O Lord, I recite but no one acts upon me.
17:88: 88 - The Almighty said: Say, ‘If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur’an, they could not produce the like of it.’ They would not be able to do that, even if they were to each other assistants. It was revealed when the infidels said: If we wanted, we could say the same thing, but God Almighty denied them. The Qur’an is miraculous in its organization, composition, and reporting of the unseen. It is speech at the highest levels of eloquence, unlike the speech of creation, because it is not created. If it were created, they would have produced something similar to it.
17:89: 89 - The Almighty said: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an from every [kind of] example, from every aspect of lessons, rulings, promises, threats, and other things. But most of the people refused except to be disbelievers, in denial.
17:90: 90 - The Almighty’s saying: And they said, ‘We will not believe you,’ until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth. The people of Kufa and Ya’qub read gush forth with a fat-ha on the ta’ and a damma on the jim, with a light pronunciation, because the spring is one. The rest read it with a shaddah from tafjir, and they agreed on the shaddah of His saying: Then the rivers will gush forth within it abundantly, because rivers are plural, and the shaddah indicates abundance, and because of His saying gushing forth after. It was narrated by Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, Abu Al-Bukhtari ibn Hisham, Al-Aswad ibn Abdul Muttalib, Zama’ah ibn Al-Aswad, Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Al-As ibn Wa’il, and Nabih and Munabbih, the sons of Al-Hajjaj, gathered with those who had gathered with them after sunset at the back of the Ka’bah. Some of them said to each other: Send to Muhammad and speak to him and argue with him until they find an excuse for him. So they sent to him that the nobles of your people have gathered to speak to you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them quickly, thinking that he had changed his mind about his affair, and he was keen on them, loving their guidance until he sat with them. They said: O Muhammad, we have sent to you to excuse you, and by God we do not know a man from the Arabs who has brought upon his people what you have brought upon your people. You have cursed the fathers, criticized the religion, and belittled dreams. And you have cursed the gods, and divided the community, and there is no ugly matter that you have not done between you and us. If you have come with this talk seeking money, we will give you from our money until you are the wealthiest of us. If you seek honor, we will make you our leader. If you want kingship, we will make you our king. If this matter that you are in is seen to have overcome you, You cannot return it. We spent our money on seeking medicine so that we could cure you of it, or excuse you. They used to call the follower of the jinn: the leader. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not have what you say. I did not come to you with what I came to you with to seek your money, nor to gain honor over you, nor to rule over you. Rather, God sent me to you as a messenger, and revealed to me a book, and commanded me to be a bearer of good tidings and a warner to you. So I conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you. If you accept me, then that is your portion in the world to come, and if you reject me, I will be patient with God’s command until God judges between me and you. They said: O Muhammad, if you do not accept what we have offered you, then you know that there is no one whose land is narrower than ours or whose life is more difficult than ours. So ask your Lord who sent you to remove these mountains from us, for they have become narrow for us, and to expand our land for us and cause rivers to gush forth in it like the rivers of Syria and Iraq, and to send to us those of our fathers who have passed away, and let among them be Qusayy ibn Kilab, for he was a truthful old man, so that we may ask them about what you say: is it true or false? If they believe you, then we will believe you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was not sent for this. I have conveyed to you what I was sent with. If you accept it from me, then it is your portion in this world and the hereafter, and if you reject it, I will be patient with God’s command. They said: If you do not do this, then ask your Lord to send us a king who will believe you, and ask Him to give you gardens, palaces, and treasures of gold and silver that will make you independent of what we see you doing, for you will go to the markets and seek a living just as we seek it. He said: I was not sent with this, but God sent me as a bearer of good tidings and a warner. They said: Then make the sky fall as you claimed. If your Lord had willed, He would have done so. He said: That is up to God. If He wills, He will do that to you. One of them said: We will not believe you until you bring God and the angels face to face. When they said that, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up, and with him stood Abdullah bin Abi Umayya, who was the son of his paternal aunt Atika bint Abdul Muttalib, and he said: O Muhammad, your people offered you what they offered you and you did not accept it from them. Then they asked you for themselves things by which they would know your status with God Almighty and you did not do it. Then they asked you to hasten what you are threatening them with of punishment, and you did not do it. By God, I will never believe you until you take a ladder to the sky and ascend it, and I will watch until you reach it and bring with you a published copy and a group of angels who will testify to what you say. By God, if you did that, I would think that I would not believe you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went back to his family, saddened by what he saw of their estrangement, and God Almighty revealed: And they said, ‘We will never believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth’ meaning the land of Mecca “”meaning springs.”
17:91: 91 - Or you have a garden, an orchard of palm trees and grapes, and rivers gush forth within it abundantly, a splitting.
17:92: 92 - Or the sky falls upon us in fragments as you have claimed. Nafi', Ibn Amir, and Asim read it with the fatha on the seen, meaning: in pieces, and it is the plural of kasfa, which is: a piece and a side, like: kasra and kasra. The others read it with the sukoon on the seen for the sake of singularity, and its plural is aksaaf and kusuf, meaning: it falls in a single layer, and it was said: he meant its side upon us. It was said: its meaning also is cutting, and it is the plural of breaking like sidrat and sidr in Ash-Shu'ara' and Saba' kasfan with the fatha, Hafs, and in Ar-Rum it is sukoon Abu Ja'far and Ibn Amir. Or you bring God and the angels as a tribe, Ibn Abbas said: As a guarantor, meaning: They guarantee what you say. Ad-Dahhak said: As a guarantor. Mujahid said: It is the plural of tribe, meaning: with the types of angels, tribe by tribe. [Qatadah said: Opinionally, meaning: the midwife sees them], meaning: directly. [Al-Farra’ said: “It is from the Arabs’ saying: I met so-and-so as a tribe, and directly,” meaning: directly.]
17:93: 93 - Or you have a house of gold meaning: of gold, and its origin is adornment, or you ascend, ascend, into the sky, this is the saying of Abdullah bin Abi Umayya, And we will not believe in your ascension, in your ascent, until you bring down to us a book that we can read, in which we are commanded to follow you, "Say: Glory be to my Lord", and Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read said meaning Muhammad, and others read it as a command, meaning: Say, O Muhammad, Were you anything but a human messenger, he commanded him to glorify and exalt Him, meaning that if He had wanted to send down what they asked for, He would have done so, but God does not send down verses based on what humans suggest, and I am only a human being and what you asked for is not within the power of humans. Know that God Almighty gave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, signs and miracles that suffice for all of this, such as: the Qur’an, the splitting of the moon, the gushing of springs from between the fingers, and the like. The people, in general, were stubborn and did not intend to seek evidence to believe, so God answered their question.
17:94: 94 - The Almighty said: And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, out of ignorance, Has God sent a human being as a messenger? He meant: The infidels were saying, We will not believe you because you are a human being, and why did God not send us an angel? So God Almighty answered them:
17:95: 95 - “Say, ‘If there were angels walking about in peace and security on the earth,’ settled and residing, ‘We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger,’ of their kind, because the heart is more inclined toward the kind than toward something other than the kind.’”
17:96: 96 - Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you.’ That I am the Messenger of God to you. He is ever, of His servants, Knowing and Seeing.
17:97: 97 - The Almighty said: And he whom God guides is the one who is guided, and he whom He sends astray - you will find for them no protectors besides Him, guiding them, and We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Al-Hasan bin Shuja’ Al-Sufi, known as Ibn Al-Mawsili, told us, Abu Bakr bin Al-Haitham told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad Al-Sayegh told us, Hussain bin Muhammad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, “A man said: O Messenger of God, how will the unbeliever be resurrected on his face on the Day of Resurrection? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The One who made him walk on his two feet is able to make him walk on his face.” It was mentioned in the hadith: They protect their faces from every hump and thorn. “Blind, mute, and deaf.” If it is said: How did He describe them as blind, dumb and deaf? He said: And the criminals will see the Fire (al-Kahf 18:53), and He said: There they will be left for destruction (al-Furqan 25:13), and He said: They will hear its wrath and its roaring (al-Furqan 25:12), did He prove seeing, speaking and hearing? It was said: They will be gathered as God described them, then these things will be returned to them. Another answer: Ibn Abbas said: Blind, they do not see what pleases them, mute, they do not speak with an argument, deaf, they do not hear anything that pleases them. Al-Hassan said: This is when they are led to the place of standing until they enter the Fire. Muqatil said: This is when it will be said to them: Be gone into it and do not speak Al-Mu’minun 33:108, and they will all become blind, dumb and deaf, they will not see, speak or hear. “Their refuge is Hell. Every time it subsides,” Ibn Abbas said: Every time its flames subside. Mujahid said: It was extinguished. Qatadah said: It weakened. It was said: It is calm without any decrease in the pain of the disbelievers, because God the Most High said: It will not cease from them Az-Zukhruf 43:75. It was said: Every time it subsides, meaning: it wants to subside, We will increase their blazing fire, meaning: fuel. It was said: What is meant by his saying: Whenever it fades away is: their skins are cooked and burned, they are returned to what they were in, and the fire was increased in intensity to burn them.
17:98: 98 - That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, ‘When we are bones and dust, will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?’ So God Almighty answered them and said:
17:99: 99 - Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth, in their greatness and intensity, is able to create the likes of them, in their smallness and weakness. Similar to the Almighty’s saying: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind Ghafir - 57 And He has appointed for them a term meaning: a time for their punishment, there is no doubt about it that it will come to them. It was said: it is death, and it was said: it is the Day of Resurrection. But the wrongdoers refused except to be ungrateful meaning: in denial and stubbornness.
17:100: 100 - Say, ‘If you possessed the treasures of my Lord’s mercy,’ meaning: the blessings of my Lord. It was also said: the provisions of my Lord, then you would withhold, meaning you would be stingy and withhold, for fear of spending, meaning: for fear of poverty, as Qatada said. It was said: Fear of running out. It is said: The man spent, meaning he became destitute and his money was gone. The thing was spent, meaning it was gone. It was said: You would have refrained from spending for fear of poverty. And man is ever stingy, meaning: miserly and withholding from spending.
17:101: 101 - The Almighty said: And We gave Moses nine clear signs, meaning: clear indications, so they are the nine signs. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: It is the stick, the white hand, the knot that was on his tongue and he untied it, the splitting of the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood. Ikrimah, Qatada, Mujahid, and Ata’ said: They are the flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, a stick, a hand, years, and a decrease in fruits. Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi mentioned: obliteration, the sea instead of years, and a decrease in fruits. He said: So the man among them was with his family in his bed and they had become two stones, and the woman among them was standing and baking bread and she had become a stone. Some of them said: They are verses of the Book. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Thaqafi told us, Harun bin Muhammad bin Harun Al-Attar told us, Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Mahan told us, Al-Walid Al-Tayalisi told us, Shu’bah bin Amr bin Murrah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muslimah, on the authority of Safwan bin Assal Al-Muradi, “A Jew said to his companion: Come so that we may ask this prophet. The other said: Do not say prophet, for if he heard, he would have four eyes. So they came to him and asked him about this verse: ‘And We gave Moses nine clear signs. ’ He said: Do not associate anything with God, and do not kill the soul which God has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery, and do not consume usury, and do not practice magic, and do not walk with an innocent person to the ruler to kill him, and do not be extravagant, and do not accuse a chaste woman, and do not flee from battle, and you in particular the Jews must not transgress on the Sabbath. So they kissed his hand and said: We bear witness that you A prophet. He said: What prevents you from following me? They said: David prayed to his Lord that there would always be a prophet among his descendants, and we fear that if we follow you the Jews will kill us. “So ask,” O Muhammad, of the Children of Israel when Moses came to them. It is possible that the address was to him and someone else was meant, and it is possible that the one who addressed him, peace be upon him, and ordered him to ask in order to reveal their lie with their people. Then Pharaoh said to him, ‘Indeed, I think, O Moses, that you are bewitched,’ meaning: they bewitched you, as Al-Kalbi said. Ibn Abbas said: Deceived. It was said: diverted from the truth. Al-Farra and Abu Ubaidah said: A magician, so he put the object in place of the subject. Muhammad bin Jarir said: He is given the knowledge of magic, so these are the wonders that you do from your magic.
17:102: 102- He said, Moses, I have known, the general public read it with the opening of the ta', addressing Pharaoh, and Al-Kisa'i read it with the closing of the ta', and he narrates that from Ali, and he said: The wicked one did not know that Moses was on the truth, and if he had known he would have believed, but Moses was the one who knew, Ibn Abbas said: Pharaoh knew it but he was stubborn, God Almighty said: And they denied it, while their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance An-Naml - 14. This reading, which is the accusative of the ta’, is more correct in meaning, and most of the reciters agree with it, because Musa cannot be relied upon for his own knowledge, and the raising of the ta’ cannot be proven from Ali, because it was narrated from a man from Murad from Ali, and that is because the man is unknown, and none of the reciters adhered to it except al-Kisa’i. None sent down these, these nine verses, except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as insights, the plural of insight, meaning that He sees with it. And indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed. Ibn Abbas said: cursed. Mujahid said: perished. Qatada said: destroyed. Al-Farra’ said: that is, diverted and prevented from good. It is said: What prevented you from this matter? That is, what prevented you and diverted you from it.
17:103: 103 - So he wanted to provoke them, meaning: Pharaoh wanted to provoke Moses and the Children of Israel, meaning: to expel them, from the land, meaning the land of Egypt, so We drowned him and all those with him, and We saved Moses and his people.
17:104: 104 - And We said after him, meaning after the destruction of Pharaoh, “to the Children of Israel: Dwell in the land,” meaning the land of Egypt and Syria, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, meaning the Day of Resurrection, We will bring you in droves, meaning all together to the place of Resurrection. A drove is a large group: if they are mixed together of every kind, it is said: the armies are mixed together, and the group of the Resurrection is the same, among them are the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked. Al-Kalbi said: So when the promise of the Hereafter comes meaning the coming of Jesus from heaven We will bring you in droves meaning: the conflict from every people, from here and there, they will all be gathered together.
17:105: 105 - The Almighty said: And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it has come down, meaning the Qur’an, And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings to the obedient, and a warner to the disobedient.
17:106: 106 - And a Qur'an which We have divided into parts. It was said that its meaning is: We revealed it in stages, and it was not revealed all at once, as evidenced by the reading of Ibn Abbas: And a Qur'an which We have divided into parts, with emphasis, and the reading of the general public with emphasis, meaning: We separated it. It was also said: We explained it. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is: We distinguished between truth and falsehood, so that you may recite it to the people at intervals, meaning: slowly and carefully, and in a continuous manner, over twenty-three years, And We revealed it gradually.
17:107: 107 - “Say: Believe in it or do not believe,” this is in the way of threat and intimidation, Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, it was said: They are the believers among the People of the Book, and they were those who sought the religion before the mission of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then they converted to Islam after his mission, such as: Zaid bin Omar bin Nufayl, Salman al-Farsi, Abu Dharr, and others. When it is recited to them, meaning: the Qur’an, they fall upon their chins, meaning: they fall on their chins. Ibn Abbas said: He meant by this their faces, prostrating.
17:108: 108 - And they say, 'Glory be to our Lord! The promise of our Lord is sure to be fulfilled.' That is, it will be fulfilled.
17:109: 109 - And they fall upon their chins weeping, meaning: they fall on their faces weeping. Weeping is recommended when reciting the Qur'an. And it increases them, the revelation of the Qur'an, in humility, in submission to their Lord. Similar to the Almighty's saying: When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping. Maryam - 58. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Amr bin Bakr Muhammad Al-Muzani told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Junayd told us, Al-Hasan bin Al-Fadl Al-Bajali told us, Asim told us, on the authority of Ali bin Asim, Al-Masoudi told us, he is Abdul-Rahman bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman, the freed slave of Abu Talha, on the authority of Isa bin Talha, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “He who weeps out of fear of God will not enter the Fire until the milk returns to the udder, and the dust of the cause of God and the smoke of Hell will never come together in the nostrils of a Muslim.” Abu al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri told us, Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Khaliq ibn Ali ibn Abd al-Khaliq al-Mu’adhin told us, Ahmad ibn Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdan told us, Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Kadimi told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Bahili told us, Abu Habib al-Ghanawi told us, Bahz ibn Hakim told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The Fire is forbidden to three eYa-Sin 36:an eye that wept out of fear of God, an eye that stayed awake in the way of God, and an eye that lowered its gaze from what God has forbidden.”
17:110: 110 - The Almighty said: “Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious.” Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated in Mecca one night and began to cry and say in his al-Sajdah 32:O God, O Most Gracious. Abu Jahl said: Muhammad forbids us from our gods and he calls upon two gods! So God, the Most High, revealed this verse. Its meaning is: They are two names for one. Whatever you call upon, “what” is a relative clause, meaning: whatever you call upon from these two names and from all of His names, He has the best names. “And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice,” Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu’aimi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Ismail informed us, Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim informed us, Hisham informed us, Abu Bishr informed us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, he said: It was revealed while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was hiding in Mecca. When he prayed with his companions, he would raise his voice with the Qur’an, and when the polytheists heard him, they would revile the Qur’an, the One who revealed it, and the One who brought it. So God the Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not recite your prayer aloud, meaning, your recitation, lest the polytheists hear and revile the Qur’an. And do not recite it in a low voice from your companions, lest they hear, and seek a way between that. And with this chain of transmission on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail, he said: Musaddad told us on the authority of Hisham on the authority of Abu Bishr with his chain of transmission similarly, and he added: And seek a way between that. Let them hear, and do not recite aloud until they learn the Qur’an from you. Some people said: The verse is about supplication, and it is the saying of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and Al-Nakha’i, Mujahid, and Makhul: Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Talq bin Ghannam told us, Zaidah told us on the authority of Hisham on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, regarding his statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, she said: This was revealed regarding supplication. Abdullah bin Shaddad said: Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, greeted them, some Bedouins from Banu Tamim would say: O God, grant us wealth and children, and they would say that out loud. Then God revealed this verse: And do not recite your prayer aloud, meaning: Do not raise your voice in your recitation or supplication, and do not recite it in a low voice. Mukhāfatah: lowering the voice and being silent. And seek a way between that, meaning: between speaking loudly and speaking quietly. Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Khuza’i told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Mahmoud bin Ghailan told us, Yahya bin Ishaq told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Rabah Al-Ansari, on the authority of Abu Qatada that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr: “I passed by you while you were reading and you were lowering your voice, so he said: I heard the one with whom you were whispering, so he said: Raise your voice a little, and he said to Umar: I passed by you while you were reading and you were raising your voice, so he said: I wake up the sleepy and drive away the devil, so he said: Lower your voice a little.”
17:111: 111 - “And say: Praise be to God, who has not taken a son.” God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to praise Him for His oneness, and the meaning of praising God is: praising Him as He deserves. Al-Hussein bin Fadl said: It means: Praise be to God who made me know that He did not take a son. And he had no partner in the kingdom, nor did he have a protector from humiliation. Mujahid said, He was not humiliated, so he would not need a protector to strengthen him. “And magnify Him greatly,” meaning: He magnified Him so that He would not have a partner or guardian. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Imam Abu al-Tayyib Sahl [ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sagani told us, Nadr ibn Hammad Abu al-Harith al-Warraq told us, Shu’bah told us] on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: I heard Saeed ibn Jubayr narrating on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first to be called to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection are those who praise God in prosperity and adversity. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Al-Hasan bin Bishran told us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar told us, Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, that Abdullah bin Amr said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Praise be to God, the pinnacle of gratitude. No servant thanks God without praising Him.” Abu al-Fadl ibn Ziyad ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi told us, Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad al-Ansari told us, Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa`id told us, Yahya ibn Khalid ibn Ayyub al-Makhzumi told us, Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir ibn Bishr al-Khuzami al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Talha ibn Kharash, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best supplication is ‘Praise be to God,’ and the best remembrance is ‘There is no god but God.’ Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Zuhair told us, Mansour told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Bashar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Umaila, on the authority of Samra bint Jundub, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The most beloved words to God Almighty are four: There is no god but God, God is Greatest, Glory be to God, and Praise be to God. It does not matter which of them you start with.”
18:1: 1 - One hundred and ten verses - and it is Meccan. Praise be to God who has sent down to His servant the Book. God praised Himself for His blessings upon His creation, and He mentioned the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically, because the revelation of the Qur’an to him was a blessing to him in particular, and to all people in general. And He has not made therein any crookedness.
18:2: 2 - Qayman", there is an inversion, its meaning is: He sent down to His servant the Book as a straight one, and did not make it crooked, Qayman means: straight. Ibn Abbas said: just. Al-Farraa said: Qayman over all the books, meaning: confirming them and abrogating their laws. Qatada said: It is not about advancing and delaying, but rather its meaning is: He sent down the Book to His servant and did not make it crooked, but made it straight and it was not different, as God Almighty said: And if it had been from other than God, they would have found within it much contradiction (An-Nisa’: 82). It was said: Its meaning is that He did not make it created. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: An Arabic Qur’an without any crookedness (al-Zumar 39:28), meaning: not created. To warn of a severe punishment, meaning: to warn of a severe punishment, from Him, meaning: from Him, and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward, meaning Paradise.
18:3: 3 - Staying there forever meaning: residing therein
18:4: 4 - And to warn those who say, 'God has taken a son.'
18:5: 5 - They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers, meaning: they said it out of ignorance, not knowledge. Kabbarat, meaning: it became great. Kalam, is in the accusative case as a specification. It is said that it is understood as: the word became great as a word. It was also said: from a word, so min was deleted and became in the accusative case. It comes out of their mouths, meaning: it appears from their mouths. If they say, what they say, is nothing but a lie.
18:6: 6 - Perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over them after them, if they do not believe in this message meaning the Qur’an, out of sorrow meaning sadness, and it was said anger.
18:7: 7 - Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it. If it is said: What is the adornment in snakes, scorpions, and devils? It was said: It contains an adornment in the sense that it indicates the oneness of God Almighty. Mujahid said: He meant men in particular, and they are the adornment of the earth. It was also said: He meant by them the scholars and the righteous. It was also said: The adornment is plants, trees and rivers, as He said: Until, when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified (Yunus 10:24). To test them, to examine them, which of them is best in deed, meaning: the most righteous in deed. And it was said: which of them will leave the world alone?
18:8: 8 - And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren plain. So, the plain is the surface of the earth. It was said: It is the dirt, barren dry and smooth, and does not grow anything. It is said: The earth is barren if its plants are eaten.
18:9: 9 - The Almighty’s saying: Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder? Meaning, did you think, O Muhammad, that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder? That is, they are a wonder among Our signs. It was said: Its meaning is that they are not more amazing than Our signs, for what I created of the heavens and the earth and what is in them of wonders is more amazing than them. al-Kahf 18:is the cavern in the mountain. They differed about the Inscription: Saeed bin Jubair said: It is a tablet on which the names of the People of the Cave and their stories were written - and this is the most apparent of the sayings - then they placed it on the door of the cave. The tablet was made of lead, and it was said: of stone. Based on this, the Inscription means inscribed, meaning: written, and the inscription is the writing. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it is the name of the valley in which the People of the Cave were, and based on this it is from the valley’s raqmah, which is its side. Kaab Al-Ahbar said: It is the name of the village from which the People of the Cave came out. It was said: It is the name of the mountain in which the cave is located. Then God mentioned the story of the People of the Cave, saying:
18:10: 10 - When the young men took refuge in the cave, meaning they went to it, and they differed about the reason for their going to the cave: Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said: The people of the Gospel were confused, and sins became great among them, and the kings became arrogant among them until they worshipped idols and sacrificed to tyrants, and among them were remnants of the religion of Christ, adhering to the worship of God and His Oneness. Among those who did that from their kings was a king from the Romans called Decayanos who worshipped idols and sacrificed to tyrants, and killed whoever opposed him. He would go to the villages of the Romans, and he would not leave anyone in a village he settled in without causing strife until he worshipped idols and sacrificed to tyrants or killed him, until he settled in the city of the People of the Cave, which is Ephesus. When he settled in it, he became arrogant to the people of faith, so they concealed him and fled in every direction. When Decayanos arrived there, he ordered that the people of faith be followed and gathered for him, and he took a police force from the infidels from its people, who would follow the people of faith in their places and bring them out to Decayanos so he would give them the choice between killing and worshipping idols and sacrificing to tyrants. Some of them desired life, and some of them were… He refused to worship other than God, so he was killed. When the people of severity in faith in God saw that, they began to surrender themselves to torment and killing. They were killed and cut up, and the pieces of their bodies were tied to the city wall on its sides and at every gate of its gates until the tribulation became great. When the young men saw that, they were extremely sad. They stood up and occupied themselves with prayer, fasting, charity, glorification, and supplication. They were from the nobles of the Romans, and they were eight men. They cried and supplicated to God and began to say: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will not call upon any god besides Him. We have indeed said an outrage if we worship other than Him. Remove this tribulation from Your believing servants, and lift this calamity from them so that they may declare Your worship. While they were in such a state, and they had entered their prayer place, the police caught up with them and found them prostrating on their faces, crying and supplicating to God. They said to them: What kept you from the king’s command? They set out to him, then they went out and brought their case to Decius, saying: People are gathering to sacrifice to your gods, and these young men from your household are mocking you and disobeying your command! When he heard that, he sent for them, and they were brought with their eyes overflowing with tears and their faces covered in dust. He said to them: What prevented you from witnessing the sacrifice to our gods who are worshipped on earth and making yourselves an example for the leaders of your city? Choose: Either sacrifice to our gods, or I will kill you. Then Maksalmina, the eldest of them, said: We have a God who fills the heavens and the earth with His majesty. We will never call upon any god other than Him. To Him is due praise, glorification, and exaltation from our souls, purely and forever. Him we worship and Him we ask for salvation and goodness. As for the tyrants, we will never worship them. Do with us as you wish. Maksalmina’s companions said to Decius what Maksalmina had said. When they said that, he ordered that a garment that was worn by their leaders be removed from them. Then he said: I will be free to do this to you and carry out for you the punishment that I have threatened you with. What prevents me from hastening that for you is that I see you as young men, young in age. I do not wish to destroy you until I have appointed for you a term in which you will remember and review your minds. Then he ordered that the ornaments that were on them of gold and silver be removed from them. Then he ordered that they be taken out of his presence. And Decius set out for a city other than their own, near them, for some business of his. When the young men saw his departure, they hastened his arrival, and they feared that if he came to their city he would remind them [and torment them]. So they conspired among themselves that each man of them should take a provision from his father’s house and give it in charity, and provision themselves with what remained, then go to a cave near the city in a mountain called Bakhlus, and stay there and worship God until Decius came, they would come to him and stand before him, and he would do with them as he wished. When some of them said that to one another, each young man of them went to his father’s house, took a provision and gave it in charity, then they set out with what remained with them, and a dog that they had followed them until they came to that cave, and they stayed in it. Kaab al-Ahbar said: They passed by a dog that followed them, but they chased it away. He did that repeatedly, and the dog said to them: O people, what do you want from me? Do not fear my side. I am the most beloved of God’s beloveds, so sleep so that I may guard you. Ibn Abbas said: They fled at night from Decius, and they were seven. Then a shepherd passed by with a dog, and he followed them in their religion, and his dog followed him, so they left the city to the cave, which was close to the city. Ibn Ishaq said: They remained in it, doing nothing but praying, fasting, glorifying, praising and praising God, seeking the face of God. They assigned their expenses to a young man among them called Yamlikha, who would buy their provisions for them from the city secretly. He was one of the most patient and courageous of them. When he entered the city, he would put on the fine clothes he was wearing and take clothes like the clothes of the poor who were eating there. Then he would take a piece of paper and go to the city and buy them food and drink, and spy on them to see if he and his companions had been mentioned in any way. Then he would return to his companions. They remained in that state for as long as they remained. Then Decius came to the city and ordered the nobles of its people to slaughter for the tyrants. The people of faith were terrified by that. Yamlikha was in the city buying food for his companions, so he returned to his companions crying with a little food, and he informed them that the tyrant had entered the city, and that they had been mentioned and sought with the nobles of the city. They were terrified and fell in prostration, calling upon God and beseeching Him and seeking refuge from Him. The trial, then Yamlikha said to them: O my brothers, raise your heads and feed and trust in your Lord, so they raised their heads and their eyes overflowed with tears, so they fed, and that was sunset, then they sat talking and studying and reminding each other, and while they were like that God struck their ears with sleep in the cave, and their dog stretched out his arms at the door of the cave, so what happened to him happened to them, and they were believers and certain and their expenses were at their heads. The next day, Decius missed them and looked for them, but he did not find them. He said to some of them: “I am upset about the situation of these young men who have gone. They thought that I was angry with them because of their ignorance of what they did not know about me. I would not have attacked them if they had repented and worshipped my gods.” The city’s leaders said: “You are not worthy of having mercy on a people who are wicked, rebellious, and disobedient. I have set a term for them, and if they had wanted, they could have returned at that time, but they did not repent.” When they said that, he became very angry. Then he sent for their fathers and brought them and asked them about them. He said: Tell me about your rebellious sons who disobeyed me, [and he threatened to kill them]. They said to him: “As for us, we did not disobey you. Why did you kill us because of a rebellious people who took our money and destroyed it in the markets of the city, then they went and climbed a mountain called Bakhlus?” When they said that to him, he let them go, and he did not know what to do with the young men. Then God inspired him to order the cave to be closed on them. God wanted to honor them and make them a sign for a nation that would succeed them, and to show them that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that God will resurrect those in the graves. So Decius ordered the cave to be closed on them, and he said: Leave them as they are in the cave, dying of hunger and thirst, and their cave that they chose will be their grave. He thought that they were awake and knew what would happen to them, but God had taken their souls in a sleep, and their dog was stretching out his arms at the door of the cave, and what had covered them had covered them, they were turning to the right and to the left. Then two believing men in the house of King Decius, who concealed their faith, one of them was named Yindros and the other Ronas, decided to write the story of the young men, their lineages, their names and their report on a lead tablet and put them in a copper coffin, and put the coffin in the building. They said: Perhaps God will make these young men a believing people before the Day of Resurrection, so that whoever opens up about them will know when he reads this book [their report]. So they did and built on it, and Decius remained as long as he remained, then he and his people died, and many centuries after him, and kings succeeded kings. Ubayd ibn Umair said: The People of the Cave were young men with collars and forelocks, and they had their hunting dog with them. They went out on a great festival of theirs in great garb and procession, and they brought out with them their gods that they worshipped. God cast faith into the hearts of the young men, and one of them was the king’s minister, so they believed and each one of them hid his faith.
