They said to themselves: We will leave these people, and no punishment will befall us for their crime. A young man from among them went out until he reached the shade of a tree, and sat in it. Then another came out and saw him sitting alone, hoping that he would be like him without revealing it. Then the other came out and they gathered in a place, and some of them said to each other: What brought you together? Each one concealed his faith from his companion for fear for himself. Then they said: Let each young man go out and be alone with his companion, then each one of them disclose his secret to his companion. So they did, and behold, they were all in faith. Then there was a cave in the mountain near them, so some of them said to one another: Then take refuge in the cave, and your Lord will spread out His mercy for you. So they entered the cave with their hunting dog, and they slept for three hundred years, adding nine. Their people lost them and sought them out, but God blinded them to their traces and their cave. So they wrote their names and lineages on a tablet: So-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so, sons of our kings. We lost them in such-and-such a month in such-and-such a year in the kingdom of so-and-so, son of so-and-so. And they put the tablet in the king’s treasury, and they said: This will have a place. And that king died, and century after century came. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: The disciple of Jesus, peace be upon him, came to the city of the People of the Cave and wanted to enter it, but he was told: There is an idol at its gate, and no one enters it without prostrating to it. He thought about entering it, so he went to a bathhouse near the city, and he used to hire himself out to the bath-keepers and work in it. The owner of the bathhouse saw the blessing in his bathhouse, and some young men from the people of the city hung up on him, so he began to tell them report of the heavens and the earth and report of the afterlife until they believed and believed him. The condition of the owner of the bathhouse was that the night was mine, and no one would come between me and him or between the prayer. He remained like that until the son of the king brought a woman and entered the bathhouse with her. The disciple taunted him and said: You are the son of the king and you enter with this woman? He felt ashamed and went away, then he returned again, and the disciple said the same thing to him, so he cursed and rebuked him, but he did not pay attention to that until they entered and died in the bathhouse. The king was brought and it was said to him: The owner of the bathhouse killed your son, so he searched but could not find him and fled. The king said: Who was his companion? So they named the young men and sought them out, and they left the city and passed by a companion of theirs who had the same faith as them. He went with them and had a dog with him until night fell to them at the cave. They entered it and said, We will stay here until the night, then we will wake up, God willing, and you will see what you think. But God struck their ears, and the king went out with his companions seeking them until they found them. They entered the cave, and when one of them wanted to enter it, he was terrified and no one could bear to enter it. One of them said, If you had power over them, would you not have killed them? He said, Yes. He said, Then build a door to the cave over them and leave them in it to die of hunger and thirst. So he did. Wahb said: Then time passed after time after time after the door of the cave was closed on them, then a shepherd was caught by the rain at the cave and he said if I opened this cave and put my sheep in it from the rain it would be good, so he kept treating it until it was opened and God restored their souls to them the next day when they woke up. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Then the people of that country were ruled by a righteous man called Bedros. When he ruled, he remained in his rule for sixty-eight years, so the people formed parties in his rule, some of whom believed in God and knew that the Hour was true, and some of whom denied it. This was a great burden on the righteous king, so he cried and supplicated to God and was deeply saddened when he saw the people of falsehood increasing and prevailing over the people of truth, and saying that there is no life except the life of this world, and that only the souls are resurrected and not the bodies. So Bedros began to send to those whom he thought well of and that they were leaders among creation, so they began to deny the Hour until they almost turned the people away from the truth and the religion of the disciples. When the righteous king saw this, he entered his house and locked it, and put on a sackcloth and put ashes under it and sat on it. He spent his night and day for a period supplicating to God Almighty and crying, and saying: O Lord, You see the differences of these people, so send them a sign that will show them [the falsehood of what they are upon]. Then the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, who… He hated the destruction of the servants. He wanted to show the young men of the cave and show the people their situation and make them a sign and proof against them so that they would know that the Hour is coming without a doubt, and to respond to his righteous servant Bedros and complete his favor upon him, and to gather those who had been scattered from the believers. So God cast into the soul of a man from the people of that country in which the cave was located, and that man’s name was Ulyas, to demolish that structure that was at the mouth of the cave and build a pen for his sheep. So he hired two young men who began to remove those stones and build that pen, until they removed what was at the mouth of the cave and opened the door of the cave. God concealed them from the people with terror. So when they opened the door of the cave, God, the Possessor of power and authority, the Resurrector of the dead, permitted the young men to sit in the middle of the cave. So they sat happy, their faces bright, their souls good, and they greeted one another. It was as if they had awakened at the hour in which they used to awaken when they woke up at night. Then they got up to pray and prayed as they used to do. Nothing that they would find strange was seen in their faces or colors, like their appearance when they slept, and they saw Decius. In their search, when they had finished their prayer, they said to Yamlikha, their provider: Tell us what the people said about us last night in the presence of this tyrant? They thought that they had slept as much as they used to, but it seemed to them that they had slept longer than they used to, so that they asked each other: How long have you been asleep? They said: We have slept a day or part of a day. Then they said: Your Lord knows best how long you have slept, and all that is in their minds is easy. Yamlikha said to them: You have sought in the city but have not been found, and he wants to bring you today so that you may be slaughtered for the tyrants or he may kill you. Whatever God wills after that, He does. Then Maksalmina said to them: O my brothers, know that you will meet God, so do not disbelieve after your belief if the enemy of God calls you. Then they said to Yamlikha: Go to the city and hear what is said about us there, and what is mentioned in the presence of Decianus, and be gentle and do not let anyone know about you, and seek us some food and bring it to us, and give us more than the food we brought, for we have become hungry. So Yamlikha did as he used to do and put away his clothes and took the clothes in which he disguised himself and took some paper [from their expenses that were with them and which were stamped with the seal of Decianus, so they were like the size of a quarter of a shoe, so Yamlikha set out]. When he passed by the door of the cave, he saw the stones removed from the door of the cave and was amazed by them, then he passed by and did not pay attention to them until he reached the door of the city secretly, so he turned away from the road for fear that one of its people would see him and recognize him and not realize that Decianus and his people had perished three hundred years before that. So when Yamlikha reached the door of the city, he raised his eyes and saw above the back of the door a sign that is for the people of faith if faith is apparent in it, so when he saw it, he was amazed and began to look at it secretly and began to look to the right. And to the north, then he left that door and turned to another of its doors and saw the same thing, so it seemed to him that the city was not as he knew it, and he saw many people talking whom he had not seen before, so he began to walk and wonder and it seemed to him that he was confused, then he returned to the door he had come from and began to wonder to himself and say: I wonder what this is? As for yesterday evening, the Muslims were hiding this sign and making light of it, but today it is apparent, perhaps I am asleep? Then he saw that he was not asleep, so he took his cloak and put it on his head, then he entered the city and began to walk in the middle of its market and heard people swearing by the name of Jesus, son of Mary, which increased his fear and he saw that he was confused, so he stood up leaning his back against one of the walls of the city, saying to himself: By God, I do not know what this is. As for yesterday evening, there is not a person on the face of the earth who mentions Jesus, son of Mary, except that he will be killed, and as for tomorrow, I hear them and every person mentions the name of Jesus and does not fear anyone. Then he said to himself: Perhaps this is not the city that I know, and by God I do not know a city near our city. So he stood up confused and then he met a young man and said to him: What is the name of this city, young man? He said: Its name is Ephesus. He said to himself: Perhaps I am possessed or something that has taken my mind away, and by God it is right for me to hasten to leave it before I am disgraced in it or evil befalls me and I perish. Then he came to and said: By God, if I had hastened to leave the city before it was discovered, it would have been easier for me. So he approached those who sell food and took out the papers that were with him and gave them to one of them and said: Sell me food with these papers. The man took them and looked at the type of paper and its engraving and was amazed by it. Then he threw them to one of his companions who looked at them. Then they began to throw them among themselves from man to man, amazed by them. Then they began to consult each other and say to each other: This man has found a treasure hidden in the earth for a long time. When Yamlikha saw them consulting about him, he was very afraid, and he began to tremble and think that they had become aware of him and recognized him, and that they only wanted to take him to their king Decius. Other people began to come to him and recognize him [but they did not recognize him], so he said to them while he was very afraid of them:: Be kind to me, you have taken my paper, so keep it, but as for your food, I have no need of it. They said to him: “Who are you, young man, and what is your business? By God, you have brought a treasure from the treasures of the ancients, and you want to hide it from us. Go with us, show us, and share in it with us. We fear for you what you have found, for if you do not, we will bring you to the sultan and hand you over to him, and he will kill you.” When he heard what they said, he said to himself: You have fallen into everything I was wary of. They said: O young man, by God, you cannot hide what you have found. So Yamlikh began not knowing what to say to them or what to return to them, and he was afraid until he did not find anything to tell them. When they saw that he did not speak, they took his cloak and threw it around his neck, then they began to lead him through the streets of the city [their young and old] until everyone in it heard about him. They asked him: What is the report? ], and it was said: This is a man who has a treasure. So the people of the city, young and old, gathered around him and began to look at him, and said: By God, this young man is not from this city, and we have never seen him in it and we never know him. So Yamlikha did not know what to say to them. When the people of the city gathered around him, he was afraid and remained silent and did not speak. He was certain that his father and brothers were in the city, and that his lineage and ancestry were from the people of the city, from its great people, and that they would come to him if they heard about him. While he was standing there, confused, waiting for some of his people to come to him and rescue him from their hands, they kidnapped him and took him to the heads of the city and its administrators who were running its affairs. They were two righteous men, one of whom was named Arius and the other was named Tantius. When he took him to them, Yamlikha thought that he was taking him to Decius the Giant, so he began to look right and left, and the people began to mock him as they mock a madman. Yamlikha began to cry, then he raised his head to the sky and said: In his soul: O God, God of heaven and God of earth, pour patience upon me today and infuse with me a spirit from You to support me with it against this tyrant. And he began to cry and say to himself: Separate me from my brothers. I wish they knew what I have suffered. If only they knew, they would come to me and we would all stand before this tyrant. For we had pledged to be together, not disbelieving in God or associating anything with Him. Separate me from them, so that they will not see me and I will not see them ever. We had pledged never to be separated in life or death. Yamlikha spoke to himself, as he told his companions when he returned to them, until he reached the two righteous men Arius and Tantius. When Yamlikha saw that he would not go with him to Decius, he came to and his crying stopped. Arius [and Tantius] took the paper and looked at it and were amazed by it. Then one of them said to him: Where is the treasure that you found, young man? Then Yamlikha said: I did not find a treasure, but this is the paper of my fathers and the inscriptions and coins of this city. But by God, I do not know what my business is or what I should say to you. Then one of them said: Who are you? Then Yamlikha said: As for me, I thought that I was from the people of this city. They said: Who is your father and who knows you in it? So he told them the name of his father, but they did not find anyone who knew him or his father. Then one of them said to him: You are a lying man, do not tell us the truth. Yamlikha did not know what to say to them, but he lowered his head [and lowered his gaze] to the ground. Some of those around him said: This is a madman. Some of them said: He is not mad, but he is deliberately fooling himself in order to escape from you. Then one of them said to him and looked at him with a sharp look: Do you think that we will send you and believe you that this is your father’s money and this paper was engraved and minted for more than three hundred years, and you are only a young boy. Do you think that you can slander us and mock us while we are unkempt as you see, and around you are the leaders of the people of the city and its rulers, and the treasuries of this town are in our hands, and we do not have any of this minting, a dirham or a dinar. I think that I will order you to be severely tortured, then I will tie you up until you confess to this treasure that you have found. When he said that, Yamlikha said to them: Tell me something I will ask you about, and if you do, I will tell you the truth about what I have. They said: Ask, and we will not hide anything from you. He said to them: What did King Decius do? They said: We do not know today on the face of the earth a king called Decius, and there was only a king who perished a long time ago and many centuries after him perished. So Yamlikha said: I am then perplexed and no one among the people believes me in what I say. We were young men [on one religion, which is Islam] and the king forced us to worship idols and sacrifice to tyrants, so we fled from him yesterday evening and slept. When we woke up, I went out to buy them food and spy on the report, and I was as you see. So go with me to the cave in Mount Panglaos, and I will show you my companions. When Arius heard what Yamlikha was saying, he said: O people, perhaps this is a sign from the signs of God that God has made for you through the hands of this young man. So go with us with him to show us his companions. So Arius and Astius went with him and the people of the city, the great and the small, went with them towards the people of the cave to see them. When the young men of the cave saw Yamlikha withholding their food and drink from the amount that he used to bring, they thought that he had been taken and taken to their king. Decianus, while they were thinking and fearing that, they heard voices and the horses’ cries ascending towards them, so they thought that they were messengers of the tyrant Decianus sent to them to bring them, so they stood up to pray and greeted each other, and advised each other, and said: Let us go to our brother Yamlikha, for he is now in the hands of the tyrant, waiting for us to come to him, while they were saying that and sitting in the back of the cave, they saw none but Arius and his companions standing at the door of the cave. And Yamlikha preceded them and entered upon them while he was weeping. When they saw him weeping, they wept with him. Then they asked him about his condition, and he informed them and narrated to them the whole story. Then they knew that they had been asleep by God’s command all that time by God’s command, and that they had been awakened to be a sign to the people and a confirmation of the resurrection, and to know that the Hour was coming without a doubt. Then Arius entered after Yamlikha and saw a coffin of copper sealed with a silver ring. He stood at the door of the cave and called one of the city’s nobles. He opened the coffin with them, and they found in it two lead tablets written on them: That Maksalmina, Makshalmina, Yamlikha, Martonus, Kashtonus, Yabronus, Demus, Battius, and Halush were young men who fled from their destroyer Decius the Giant, fearing that he would turn them away from their religion. So they entered this cave. When he was informed of their location, he ordered the cave to be blocked up with stones. We have written down their condition and their story. So that those who came after them would know if they found them, then when they read it and were amazed, and praised God who showed them the sign of resurrection in them, then they raised their voices in praise of God and glorification of Him, then they entered upon the youths into the cave and found them sitting among them, their faces shining and their clothes not worn out, so Arius and his companions fell down in prostration, and praised God who showed them a sign of His signs, then they spoke to each other and the youths informed them of what they had suffered from their king Decius [of forcing them to worship idols and sacrifice to tyrants and concealing their faith from him and their fleeing to the cave], then Arius and his companions sent a messenger to their righteous king Pedros saying: Hurry to us so that you may see a sign of the signs of God that God has made in your kingdom, and made it a sign for the worlds so that it may be for them a light and radiance and confirmation of the resurrection, so hurry to the youths whom God Almighty has resurrected, and their deaths had been more than three hundred years ago, so when the report reached the king, his mind returned to him and his concern went away, so he said: I praise you, O God, Lord of the heavens and the earth, and I worship you and glorify you. You have been generous to me and have had mercy on me, and you have not extinguished the light that you had given to my fathers for the righteous servant, King Constantine. When the people of the city heard about him, they rode to him and went with him until they came to the city of Ephesus. The people of the city met them and went with him until they climbed towards the cave. When the youths saw Pedros, they rejoiced at him and fell prostrate on their faces. Pedros stood up, embraced them and wept, while they were sitting before him on the ground, glorifying and praising God. Then the youths said to Pedros: We entrust you to God [your faith and the results of your deeds] and peace be upon you and the mercy of God. May God protect you and your kingdom, and we seek refuge in God from the evil of mankind and jinn. While the king was standing, they returned to their beds and slept, and God Almighty took their souls. The king rose to them and put their clothes on them and ordered that each man of them be placed in a coffin of gold. When evening came and he slept, they came to him in a dream and said to him: We were not created from gold or from… Silver, but we were created from dust and to dust we shall return, so leave us as we were in the cave on the dust until God raises us from it. Then the king ordered a teak coffin to be made and they were placed in it, and God concealed them when they left them with terror, so no one was able to enter upon them. Then the king ordered a mosque to be made at the door of the cave in which to pray, and he made for them a great festival and ordered that it be visited every year. It was said: When Yamlikha was carried to King Al-Salih, the king said to him: Who are you? He said: I am a man from this city, and he mentioned that he went out yesterday or a few days ago, and he mentioned his home and people whom no one knew, and the king had heard that young men had gone missing in the early days and that their names were written on the tablet in the treasury, so he called for the tablet and looked at their names and he was one of those people, and he mentioned the names of the others and Yamlikha said they are my companions, so when the king heard that he rode with the people who were with him, and when they came to the door of the cave, Yamlikha said: Leave me so that I may enter upon my companions and give them good report, for if they see you with me you will terrify them, so he entered and gave them good report, but God took their souls and blinded their traces so they could not find their way to them, and that is what God Almighty said: When the young men took refuge in the cave means: they went to the cave. It is said: So-and-so took refuge in such-and-such a place, meaning: he made it his home in the cave, which is a cave in Mount Banglus and the name of the cave is: Khayram. They said, ‘Our Lord, grant us mercy from You.’ The meaning of mercy is guidance in religion. It was also said that it means provision. And prepare for us means make easy for us right guidance in our affair, meaning that which seeks Your pleasure and that which guides us. Ibn Abbas said: Right guidance means a way out of the cave in safety.
18:11: 11 - So We put them to sleep and cast sleep upon them. It was said that its meaning was that We prevented sounds from reaching their ears, because when a sleeper hears a sound, he wakes up. In the cave for a number of years, meaning that We put them to sleep for a number of years, and the number was mentioned for emphasis. It was said that mentioning it indicates abundance, because a small amount is not usually counted.
18:12: 12 - Then We raised them up, meaning from their sleep, to know, meaning: the knowledge of observation, which of the two parties, meaning the two groups, how long they remained. That is because the village disputed about how long they remained in the cave. And they differed in His statement how long they remained, how long they remained, how long, meaning: an end. And Mujahid said: a number, and he put it in the accusative case as an explanation.
18:13: 13 - We relate to you [We recite to you] their story, the story of the People of the Cave. In truth, in honesty. They were youths, young men, who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance, in faith and insight.
18:14: 14 - And We bound, We strengthened, their hearts, with patience and steadfastness, and We strengthened them with the light of faith until they were patient in abandoning the home of their people, and leaving the honor and affluent life they were in, and fled with their religion to the cave, when they stood up, before Decius when he rebuked them for abandoning the worship of idols, "and said, 'Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. Never will we call upon any god besides Him'", they said that because their people were worshipping idols, then we would have said an outrage, meaning: If we called upon other than God, then we would have said an outrage. Ibn Abbas said: injustice. Qatada said: a lie. The root of excess and excess is a metaphor for fate and excess.
18:15: 15 - These are our people, meaning: the people of his country, who have taken besides Him, meaning: besides God, gods, meaning: idols that they worship, if only they had not come upon them, meaning: upon their worship, with a clear authority, with a clear argument [that shows and clarifies that idols do not deserve to be worshipped besides God], so who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God, and claims that He has a partner and a son.
18:16: 16 - Then some of them said to each other: And when you withdrew from them, meaning their people, and what they worship except God, Ibn Mas'ud read and what you worship other than God and as for the well-known reading, its meaning is: that they were worshipping God and worshipping idols with Him, they say: And when you withdrew from them and all that they worship except God, then you did not withhold your worship so take refuge in the cave, so take refuge in it, He will spread out for you, will expand for you, your Lord from His mercy and will prepare for you, will make easy for you, from your affair a comfort meaning: what returns to Him is your ease and your comfort. Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read marfqan with a fatha on the meem and a kasra on the fa', and the others read it with a kasra on the meem and a fatha on the fa', and their meaning is the same, which is what a person is comforted by.
18:17: 17 - The Almighty said: And you see the sun when it rises, declining, Ibn Amir and Yaqub read: tazur with a sukoon on the zay and a shaddah on the raa, on the weight of tahmar, and the people of Kufa read: with a fatha on the zay and a light alif after it, and the others read with a shaddah on the zay, and all of them have the same meaning, that is: it inclines and turns away, from their cave on the right meaning: the right side, and when it sets, it leaves them meaning: it leaves them and turns away from them, on the left, the origin of qard is cutting, and they are in a hollow of it meaning: a wide area of the cave and its plural is gaps, Ibn Qutaybah said: Their cave was facing the daughters of the bier, the sun does not fall into it at sunrise or at sunset or in between. He said: God chose for them a place to sleep in a canal where the sun does not enter upon them and harm them with its heat and change their colors, and they are in a wide area where the cold wind and its breeze reach them, and the distress and sorrows of the cave are removed from them. Some of them said: This is a false statement, which is that the cave was facing the daughters of the bier, so the sun did not fall on them, but God turned the sun away from them with His power and prevented it from reaching them. Do you not see that he said: This is from the signs of God, from the wonders of God’s creation and the evidence of His power that is considered, He whom God guides is the guided one, and he whom He leaves astray, meaning: he whom God leaves astray and does not guide, you will not find for him a protector, a helper, a guide.
18:18: 18 - The Almighty’s saying: And you think them awake, meaning: alert, the plural of yaqīz, and yaqūd, while they are asleep, sleeping, the plural of raqīd like qā’id and qūd, and their condition was confused because their eyes were open, breathing, but not speaking. And We turned them to the right and to the left, once to the right side and once to the left side. Ibn Abbas said: They would turn them once a year from one side to the other so that the earth would not consume their flesh. It was said that the day of Ashura was the day of their turning. Abu Hurairah said: They would turn them twice every year. And their dog stretched out his forelegs at the entrance. Most of the commentators agree that it was of the same type as dogs. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: He was a lion and the lion was called a dog. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed against Utbah ibn Abi Lahab and said, O God, send upon him one of your dogs. So a lion devoured him. The first is more correct. Ibn Abbas said: It was a white-haired dog. It is narrated about him: Above the Qalti and below the Kurdish, (Qalti: a Chinese dog). Muqatil said: It was yellow. Al-Qurazi said: Its intense yellowness was almost red. Al-Kalbi said: Its color was like heather. It was also said: The color of a stone. Ibn Abbas said: His name was Qatmir. Ali said: His name was Rayyan. Al-Awza’i said: Batur. Al-Suddi said: Tur. Ka’b said: Sahilah. Khalid bin Ma'dan said: There is no animal in Paradise except the dog of the People of the Cave and the donkey of Balaam. His saying, at the entrance. Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: The entrance is the courtyard of the cave. Ata’ said: The entrance is the door. As-Suddi said: The entrance is the door, and this is the narration of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. If it is said: The cave had no door or threshold? It was said: It means the place of the door and the threshold. The dog had spread his arms and turned his face towards them. Al-Suddi said: When the People of the Cave turned over, the dog turned over with them. When they turned to the right, the dog broke his right ear and lay on it. When they turned to the left, he broke his left ear and lay on it. If you had looked at them, O Muhammad, you would have turned away from them in flight, because God has clothed them with such awe that no one can reach them until the Book reaches its term and God Almighty awakens them from their sleep. And you would have been filled with terror from them, fear. The people of Hijaz read it with a shaddah on the lam, while the others read it without it. They differed as to why there was terror: It was said that it was due to the loneliness of the place. Al-Kalbi said: Because their eyes were open, like someone who is awake and wants to speak, while he is asleep. It was said: Because of their abundant hair, long nails, and their turning without feeling or noticing. It was said: God Almighty prevented them with terror so that no one would see them. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: We went on a military expedition with Muawiyah towards the Romans, and we passed by the cave in which the People of the Cave were. Muawiyah said: If only these people were revealed to us so we could look at them. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said: One better than you prevented that. He said: If you had looked at them, you would have turned away from them in flight. So Muawiyah sent some people and said: Go and look. When they entered the cave, God sent a wind upon them that drove them out.
18:19: 19 - The Almighty’s saying: And thus We raised them up, meaning: just as We put them to sleep in the cave and preserved their bodies from decay over time, so also We raised them up from the sleep that resembles death, that they might question one another, that is, that some of them might question others, and the lam in it is the lam of consequence, because they were not raised up to be questioned. One of them said: He was their leader, Maksalmina, How long have you been asleep? That is because they were surprised by how long they had slept. It is said that they were alarmed by what they had missed of the prayer, so they said that. They said, We have stayed a day, meaning that they entered the cave in the morning and said, “When they woke up in the evening, they said, ‘We have stayed a day.’ Then they looked and saw that there was still some sun left, so they said, ‘Or part of a day.’ When they looked at the length of their hair and nails, they knew that they had stayed for more than a day. They said, “Your Lord knows best how long you have stayed.” It was said that when their leader, Maksalmina, heard the disagreement among them, he said, Leave the disagreement, your Lord knows best how long you have stayed. “Then send one of you with this money of yours,” meaning Yamlikha. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Abu Bakr read: with your paper with a silent ra and the rest read it with a kasra on both of them, and their meaning is the same, which is silver, whether minted or not. To the city, it was said: it is Tarsus, and its name in pre-Islamic times was Ephesus, so they called it Tarsus in Islam. So let him see which food is purest. That is, the most permissible food, so that it is not from usurpation or a forbidden cause. It was also said: They ordered him to seek the slaughter of a believer and not from the slaughter of someone who slaughters for other than God, and among them were believers who concealed their faith. Ad-Dahhak said: The best food. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The best food. Ikrimah said: More, and the root of zakat is increase. It was also said: The cheapest food. So let him bring you provision from Him, meaning: sustenance and food for you to eat, and let him be gentle, and let him be gentle on the road and in the city, and let them be concealed and secretive, and let no one know, of the people, about you.
18:20: 20 - If they gain control over you, meaning: if they know where you are, they will stone you. Ibn Jurayj said: they will curse you and hurt you verbally. It was also said: they will kill you. It was also said: it was their custom to kill with stones, which is the worst kind of killing. It was also said: they will beat you, or return you to their religion, meaning: to disbelief. And you will never succeed then, if you return to it.
18:21: 21 - The Almighty said: And thus We made known to them, meaning: We informed them, that they may know that the promise of God is true, meaning the people of Baydrus who denied the resurrection, and that there is no doubt about the Hour when they dispute among themselves about their affair, Ibn Abbas said: They dispute about the building, so the Muslims said: We will build a mosque for them in which people pray because they are of our religion, and the polytheists said: We will build a building for them because they are of our lineage. Ikrimah said: They disputed about the resurrection. The Muslims said: The resurrection is for the bodies and souls together. Some people said: It is for the souls without the bodies. So God Almighty resurrected them and showed them that the resurrection is for the bodies and souls. It was said: They disputed about the duration of their stay. It was also said: About their number. They said, “Build over them a structure. Their Lord knows best about them.” Those who prevailed in their affair said, We will surely build over them a mosque.
18:22: 22 - They will say, 'Three, their dog being the fourth'. It was narrated that Sayyid, Al-Aqib and their companions from the Christians of Najran were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the mention of the People of the Cave came up. Sayyid - who was a Jacobite - said: They were three, their dog being the fourth. Al-Aqib - who was a Nestorian - said: They were five, their dog being the sixth. The Muslims said: They were seven, their dog being the eighth. So God confirmed the Muslims' statement after He had narrated the Christians' statement, and He said: "They will say, 'Three, their dog being the fourth'. And they will say, 'Five, their dog being the sixth' - guessing at the unseen," meaning: conjecture and guesswork without certainty. He did not say this about the seven, so He said: And they say, meaning the Muslims, seven, their dog being the eighth. They differed about the waw in his saying: And the eighth of them. It was said: Leaving it out or mentioning it is the same. It was said: It is the waw of judgment and investigation, as if he narrated their differences, and the speech was completed when he said: And they say seven, then he confirmed this statement by saying: And their eighth is their dog, and the eighth does not come except after the seventh. It was said: This is the waw of eight, and that is because the Arabs count and say one, two, three, four, five, six, seven and eight, because the contract was seven for them as it is ten for us today, similar to the saying of God Almighty: Those who repent, those who worship, those who praise to His saying: And those who forbid evil (al-Tawbah 9:112), and He said about the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you - Muslims, believers, obedient, repentant, worshipping, fasting, previously married and virgins (al-Tahrim 66:5). “Say, ‘My Lord knows best their number. None knows them except a few.’” Ibn Abbas said: “I am one of the few. They were seven.” Muhammad bin Ishaq said: They were eight. He read: And the eighth of them was their dog, meaning: their guardian. The correct version is the first. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: They are Maksalmina, Yamlikha, Martunus, Binunus, Sarinunus, Dhu Nuwanus, and Kashfitanunus, which is the shepherd, and the dog Qatmir. So do not dispute about them, that is, do not argue or speak about their number and status, except with an outward argument, except with the outward meaning of what We have told you. He says: What I have told you is enough for you, so do not add to it. He paused at that. And do not consult anyone about them, from the People of the Book, without them, that is, do not return to what they say after We have informed you.
18:23: 23 - And never say of anything, 'I will do that tomorrow,' meaning: If you decide to do something tomorrow, do not say, I will do it tomorrow, but rather say, God willing. This is because the people of Mecca asked him about the spirit, the People of the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn, and he said, I will tell you tomorrow, and he did not say, God willing. So the revelation continued for days, and then this verse was revealed.
18:24: 24 - Except that God wills. And remember your Lord when you forget, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is if you forget the exception and then remember, then make an exception. Ibn Abbas permitted an interrupted exception, even if it was for a year. Al-Hasan permitted it as long as he was in the gathering, and some of them permitted it if the time was close, but if it was far then it is not valid. And it was not permitted to except a group until it was connected to the speech. Ikrimah said: He means the verse: And remember your Lord when you become angry. Wahb said: It is written in the Bible: Son of Adam, remember Me when you are angry, and I will remember you when I am angry. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: This is in prayer. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Al-Hasan bin Ahmad Al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Sarraj told us, Qutaybah told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever forgets the prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it. “And say, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to a path closer to right conduct than this.’” That is, He will make me steadfast on a path that is closer to Him and more right. It was said: God commanded His Prophet to remind him if he forgot something, and to ask him to guide him to what is better for him than remembering what he forgot. It is said: When the people asked him about the story of the People of the Cave out of stubbornness, God Almighty commanded him to inform them that God would give him evidence of the truth of his prophethood that was more convincing to them than the story of the People of the Cave, and he did so, as He gave him knowledge of the unseen that was clearer to them in the argument and closer to guidance than the story of the People of the Cave. Some of them said: This is something that he was commanded to say along with his saying God willing if he mentioned the exception after forgetting. And if a person forgets God willing, then his repentance from that is to say: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something closer to right conduct than this.
18:25: 25 - The Almighty said: And they remained in their cave, meaning: the People of the Cave. Some of them said: This is report about the People of the Book that they said that. If it was report from God the Almighty about the amount of their stay, then there would be no point in saying "Say: God knows best how long they stayed", and this is the saying of Qatada. And it is indicated by the reading of Ibn Masoud And they remained in their cave, then God the Almighty responded to them and said: "Say: God knows best how long they stayed". Others said: This is a statement from God Almighty about the length of their stay in the cave, and this is the most correct. [As for his saying: “Say: God knows best how long they stayed,” its meaning is: that the matter is about the length of their stay] as we mentioned. If they dispute with you about it, then answer them and say: God knows best how long they stayed, meaning: He knows better than you, and He has informed us of the length of their stay. It was said: The People of the Book said: This period from the time they entered the cave until this day is three hundred and nine years, so God responded to them and said: “Say: God knows best how long they remained,” meaning: after the taking of their souls until this day, no one knows it except God. The Almighty said: Three hundred years. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read three hundred without tanween, and the others read it with tanween. If it is said: Why did he say three hundred years [and not one year]? It was said: His statement, And they remained in their cave for three hundred years, was revealed. They said: Days, months, or years? So years was revealed. Al-Farra’ said: Some Arabs put sennain in place of sana. It was said: Its meaning is that they remained in their cave for three hundred years. And they increased by nine, Al-Kalbi said: The Christians of Najran said: As for three hundred, we know, but as for nine, we have no knowledge of it, so it was revealed.
18:26: 26 - "Say: God knows best how long they stayed." It was narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: According to the People of the Book, they stayed for three hundred solar years, and God Almighty mentioned three hundred lunar years, and the difference between the solar and lunar years in every hundred years is three years, so in three hundred there are nine years, so that is why He said: And they increased by nine. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. The unseen is that which is hidden from perception, and nothing is hidden from God Almighty’s perception. I see and hear means: God sees everything that exists and hears everything that is heard! That is, nothing is hidden from His hearing and sight. They have no protector meaning: what do the people of the heavens and the earth have, besides Him meaning: besides God, a protector “a helper,” nor does He share in His rule with anyone, Ibn ‘Amir and Ya’qub read nor does He share with the ta’ of addressing and prohibiting, and the others read with the ya’, meaning: God does not share in His rule with anyone. It was said: The rule here is the knowledge of the unseen, meaning: He does not share in His knowledge of the unseen with anyone.
18:27: 27 - The Almighty said: And recite meaning: and read, O Muhammad, what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord, meaning the Qur’an, and follow what is in it. There is no changing His words, Al-Kalbi said: There is no changing the Qur’an. It was also said: There is no changing what He promised with His words to the people of His disobedience. And you will not find, you, besides Him, if you do not follow the Qur’an, a refuge, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: a protection. Al-Hasan said: an entrance. Mujahid said: a refuge. It was also said: a justification. It was also said: an escape. Its origin is from inclination.
18:28: 28 - The Almighty said: "And be patient with yourself" the verse, was revealed about Uyaynah bin Hisn Al-Fazari who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he converted to Islam, and with him were a group of poor people, among them Salman, who was wearing a cloak that had been sweated through, and in his hand was a palm branch that he was splitting and weaving. Uyaynah said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Doesn't the smell of these people bother you? We are the leaders and nobles of Mudar. If we convert to Islam, the people will convert to Islam, and nothing prevents us from following you except these people, so keep them away from you until we follow you, or make a place for us and a place for them. Then God Almighty revealed: "And be patient with yourself", meaning: O Muhammad, keep yourself "with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, the two ends of the day, seeking His countenance", meaning: they want God, not seeking any worldly gain. Qatada said: It was revealed about the People of the Suffa, who were seven hundred poor men in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They did not return to trade, farming, or herding. They would pray one prayer and wait for another. When this verse was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Praise be to God who has placed among my nation those with whom I have been commanded to be patient. “And do not turn your eyes away from them,” that is, do not divert or exceed, seek the adornments of worldly life, that is, seek to sit with the rich and noble and keep company with worldly people. And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, meaning: We have made his heart heedless of Our remembrance, meaning: Uyaynah ibn Hisn. It was also said: Umayyah ibn Khalaf. And follows his desire, meaning his desire in seeking desires, and whose affair is [in] excess, Qatada and Mujahid said: Wasted. It was also said: Its meaning is he wasted his life and neglected his days. It was also said: Regret. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Extravagance. Al-Farra’ said: Abandoned. It was also said: Falsely. It was also said: Contrary to the truth. Al-Akhfash said: Transgressing the limit. It was said: The meaning of transgressing the limit is the statement of Uyaynah: If we submit, all people will submit, and this is a great excess.
18:29: 29 - And say, 'The truth is from your Lord,' meaning: what was mentioned of faith and the Qur'an, meaning: Say, O Muhammad, to those whose hearts We have made heedless of Our remembrance: O people, [the truth has come to you from your Lord] and to Him is success and failure, and in His hand is guidance and misguidance, and I have no say in that. So whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve. This is in the way of threat and warning, like His saying: Do whatever you will Fussilat 40. It was said that the meaning of the verse is: And say, “The truth is from your Lord, and I do not drive away the believers for your own desires. So if you wish, then believe, and if you wish, then disbelieve. If you disbelieve, then your Lord has prepared for you a Fire whose walls will surround you. But if you believe, then for you is what God Almighty has described for the people of His obedience.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the meaning of the verse: Whoever God wills to have faith, he believes, and whoever He wills to disbelieve, he disbelieves. This is His statement: And you do not will except that God wills (al-Insan 76:30). Indeed, We have prepared: We have prepared, and made ready, from preparation, which is the equipment, for the wrongdoers for the disbelievers, a fire whose pavilion will surround them the pavilion: the room that surrounds the tents. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Rashdin ibn Sa’d, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Diraj ibn Abi al-Samh, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The canopy of Hell will be four walls, each wall as thick as a forty-year journey. Ibn Abbas said: It is a wall of fire. Al-Kalbi said: It is a neck that emerges from the fire and surrounds the infidels like a fence. It was said: It is smoke surrounding the infidels, and it is what God Almighty mentioned: Go to a shade of three branches (al-Mursalat 77:30). And if they cry out for help, due to severe thirst, they will be helped with water like molten metal. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Rashdin ibn Sa’d, Amr ibn al-Harith told us, on the authority of Diraj ibn Abi al-Samh, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: With water like molten metal. He said, like cloudy oil, and when it is brought near to him, the scalp of his face falls into it. Ibn Abbas said: It is thick water like the dregs of oil. Mujahed said: It is pus and blood. Ibn Masoud was asked about: al-Mahl, so he called for gold and silver and lit a fire over them until they melted, then he said: This is most similar to al-Mahl. He grills faces He cooks faces from his heat. What a bad drink and what a bad place to rest. Ibn Abbas said: A home. Mujahid said: A gathering place. Ata’ said: A residence. Al-Qatibi said: A sitting place. The root of al-murtafiq is a reclining place.
18:30: 30 - The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - never will We allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds. If it is said: Where is the answer to His saying: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds? It was said: His answer is his saying: For them are gardens of Eden with rivers flowing. As for his saying: Indeed, We will not be lost, it is an interjection. It was said: It contains an implication, meaning: Those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will not waste their reward, but will reward them. Then He mentioned the reward and said:
18:31: 31 - "For them are Gardens of Eden", meaning: residence. It is said: So-and-so resided in a place if he resided there. It was called Eden because of the eternity of the believers therein. "Underneath them rivers flow, and they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold." Saeed bin Jubair said: Each one of them will be adorned with three bracelets, one of gold, one of silver, and one of pearls and rubies. "And they will wear green garments of fine silk, which is the finest of brocade, and heavy brocade", which is the thickest of it. The meaning of thickness in the garments of Paradise is its perfection. Abu Imran al-Jawni said: The silk is the brocade woven with gold. "Reclining therein, in the gardens, on couches", which are the beds in the chambers, the singular of which is couch. "An excellent reward, meaning an excellent recompense, and a beautiful, the gardens, a resting place", meaning a seat and a place to stay.
18:32: 32 - And give them an example of two men the verse, it was said: It was revealed about two brothers from the people of Mecca from Banu Makhzum, one of them was a believer, and he is Abu Salamah Abdullah bin Abdul Asad bin Abdul Yalil [and he was the husband of Umm Salamah before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the other was an unbeliever, and he is Al-Aswad bin Abdul Asad bin Yalil]. It was said: This is a parable of Uyaynah ibn Hisn and his companions with Salman and his companions, he likened them to two men from the Children of Israel, two brothers, one of them was a believer and his name was Judah according to Ibn Abbas, and Muqatil said: Yamlikha, and the other was a disbeliever and his name was Qatrus, and Wahb said: Qatfir, and they are the ones whom God the Most High described in Surat Al-Saffat, and their story was, according to what Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak narrated on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani, who said: There were two men who were partners and they had eight thousand dinars, and it was said: They were two brothers who inherited eight thousand dinars from their father and divided them, so one of them bought land for a thousand dinars, so his companion said: O God, so-and-so has bought land for a thousand dinars, so I will buy land from You in Paradise for a thousand dinars, so he gave a thousand dinars in charity, then his companion built a house for a thousand dinars, so this one said: O God, so-and-so built a house for a thousand dinars, so I will buy a house from You in Paradise for a thousand dinars, so he gave that in charity, then his companion married a woman and spent a thousand dinars on her Then this believer said: O God, I propose to You a woman from the women of Paradise for a thousand dinars, so give them in charity. Then his companion bought servants and goods for a thousand dinars, and this man said: O God, I buy from You goods and servants in Paradise for a thousand dinars, so give them in charity. Then he was afflicted with great need, so he said: If I go to my companion, perhaps he will do me a favor. So he sat on his way until he passed by him with his entourage, so he stood up and the other looked at him and recognized him, so he said: So-and-so? He said: Yes. He said: What is the matter with you? He said: I was afflicted with need after you left, so I came to you so that you might bring me good. He said: What happened to Malik, since we divided the same wealth and you took half of it? So he told him his story, and he said: Are you among those who believe in this? Go, and I will not give you anything. So he sent him away and decreed that they should die, and the following was revealed concerning them: “Then some of them turned to others, questioning one another. One of them said: Indeed, I had a companion.” As-Saffat 37:50-51 It was narrated that when he came to him, he took him by the hand and began to walk around him and show him his own wealth, so he got down to them. “And give them an example: two men. We made for one of them two gardens of grapevines and surrounded them with palm trees.” That is, We surrounded them on both sides with palm trees. Haffaf is the side, and its plural is ahfa. It is said: The people surrounded it, that is, they went around its sides. And placed crops between them. That is, We placed palm trees around the grapevines and crops in the middle of the grapevines. It was said between them meaning between the two gardens there was crops, meaning: there was no place of ruin between the two gardens.
18:33: 33 - Both gardens yielded, meaning each one of the two gardens gave, its fruit, its fruit in full, and it was not wronged, it was not diminished, in anything of it, and We caused a river to gush forth, the general public read it with emphasis, Yaqub read it with a light jim, through them a river, meaning: We split and brought forth a river in the middle of them.
18:34: 34 - And he had, for the owner of the garden, fruits. Asim, Abu Ja`far, and Ya`qub read: fruits with the opening of the tha` and the meem, and likewise: with his fruit. Abu `Amr read: with the damma of the tha` and the sukoon of the meem, and the others read them with the damma of both. Whoever reads it with the fat-ha, it is the plural of fruit, which is the edible fruit that the tree produces. Whoever reads it with the dammah, it means abundant, fruitful wealth of every kind, plural of fruits. Mujahid said: gold and silver. It was said: all fruits. Al-Azhari said: The fruit is pluralized as fruit, fruit is pluralized as fruits, then fruits is pluralized as fruit. He said, meaning the owner of the garden, to his companion, the believer, while he was conversing with him, addressing him and answering him: I have more wealth than you and more men, meaning: clan and relatives. Qatada said: servants and retinue. Muqatil said: children, confirming the words of God Almighty: If you see that I am less than you in wealth and children (al-Kahf 18:39).
18:35: 35 - And he entered his garden, meaning the disbeliever, he took his Muslim brother by the hand and led him around it and showed him its fruits, while he was unjust to himself, with his disbelief, he said, 'I do not think that this will ever perish,' the people of meaning said: Its beauty fascinated him and its flowers deceived him, so he imagined that it would never perish, and he denied the resurrection.
18:36: 36 - He said: And I do not think the Hour will come, And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a return, the people of Hijaz and Ash-Sham read it like this in the dual form, meaning from the two gardens, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an, and the others read from it meaning: from the garden that he entered, returning meaning: returning. If it is said: How did he say: And if I am returned to my Lord while he is denying the resurrection? It was said: Its meaning is: And if I am returned to my Lord - as you claim - He will give me something better than it there, for He did not give me this Paradise in this world except to give me something better than it in the Hereafter.
18:37: 37 - His companion the Muslim said to him, while he was conversing with him, 'Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust?' meaning He created you from dust, then created you from a sperm-drop, then proportioned you as a man.' meaning He made you a perfect human being, a male.
18:38: 38 - But He is God, my Lord. Ibn Amir and Yaqub read: but we with an alif in the connection, and the rest read without an alif, and they agreed to prove the alif in the pause, and its original is: but I, so the hamza was deleted to make it easier, due to its frequent use, then one of the two noons was assimilated into the other, Al-Kisa'i said: It is an advancement and a delay, its meaning: but God is my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord.
18:39: 39 - And why did you not, when you entered your garden, meaning: Why did you not, when you entered your garden, “say: ‘Whatever God wills,’” meaning: The matter is whatever God wills. It was said: Its answer is implied, meaning: Whatever God wills, it was. And His saying: There is no power except with God, meaning: I am not able to preserve my money or repel anything from it except [with God’s permission]. It was narrated on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa on the authority of his father that whenever he saw something of his money that he liked or entered one of his gardens, he would say: What God wills, there is no power except with God. Then he said: If you see that I have less wealth and children than you, and I is a pillar, and therefore less is in the accusative case, meaning: If you see that I have less wealth and children than you, then you become arrogant and haughty towards me.
18:40: 40 - Perhaps my Lord will give me, perhaps my Lord, something better than your Paradise and send upon it, meaning upon your Paradise, a punishment, Qatada said: a torment. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: a fire. Al-Qutaybi said: targets. From the sky, and it is like a thunderbolt or something that destroys it, the singular of which is: Hisbanah, and it becomes a slippery plain, meaning a barren, smooth land with no plants in it. It was said: feet slip on it. Mujahid said: enormous sand.
18:41: 41 - Or its water becomes sunken, meaning: sunken, cut off, and gone, not reached by hands or buckets. Sunken is a source that is used in place of a noun, such as: falsehood and justice. Then you will not be able to seek it out, meaning: if you seek it, you will not find it.
18:42: 42 - And its fruit was encompassed, meaning: the punishment encompassed the fruit of his garden, because God Almighty sent fire upon it and destroyed it and its water sank. Then he became, its disbelieving owner, turning his hands over, meaning: clapping one hand over the other, and turning his hands back to back, in regret and longing, for what he had spent on it while it was desolate, meaning fallen, on its trellises, its roofs, and saying, 'Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord.'
18:43: 43 - God Almighty said: And he had no company a group to aid him other than God to prevent him from God’s punishment, nor was he victorious a steadfast avenger, meaning: he was not able to defend himself. It was said that he was not able to restore what he had lost.
18:44: 44 - There is the guardianship of God the Truth, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read the guardianship with a kasra on the waw, meaning authority, and the others read it with a fatha on the waw, from: allegiance and victory, like the Almighty's saying: God is the protector of those who believe Al-Baqarah - 257. Al-Qatibi said: He means that they will be his protectors on that day and disavow what they used to worship. It was said: With the fat-ha: Lordship, and with the kasra: Emirate. Al-Haqq with the qaf raised: Abu Amr and Al-Kisa’i as a description of guardianship, and Abu’s reading confirms it: There is guardianship for God the Truth, and the others read it with the genitive as a description of God, like the Almighty’s saying: Then they will be returned to God, their true Master (al-An’am 6:62). He is the best in reward, the best reward for those who obey Him if it were someone else who would reward, and the best in consequence, meaning: the consequence of His obedience is better than the consequence of the obedience of someone else, so He is the best in reward, and consequence: obedience. Hamza and Asim read consequence with a sukoon on the qaf, and the others read it with a damma.
18:45: 45 - The Almighty said: And present to them, O Muhammad, meaning: to your people, the similitude of the life of this world is like water which We send down from the sky, meaning: rain, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, from which emerges every color and flower, and it becomes, soon, stubble, dry. Ibn Abbas said: Ad-Dahhak said: broken. And stubble is what dries up and crumbles from the plant and becomes stubble, scattered by the winds, Ibn Abbas said: the winds stir it up. Abu Ubaidah said: they scatter it. Al-Qatibi said: And God is over all things competent, capable.
64:14: 46 - Money and children, which Utbah and his rich companions boasted about, are the adornment of the life of this world, not provisions for the Hereafter. Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: Wealth and children are the cultivation of this world, and good deeds are the cultivation of the Hereafter, and God may gather them for some people. And the lasting good deeds, they differed about them. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Mujahid said: It is saying Glory be to God, “Praise be to God,” There is no god but God, and God is Greatest. We have narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best speech is four words: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest.” Abu al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hanafi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Abu Ja`far Abdullah bin Ismail al-Hashemi told us, Ahmad bin Abdul-Jabbar al-`Attardi told us, Abu Mu`awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A`mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: For me to say, ‘Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest,’ is more beloved to me than anything the sun rises upon. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Uthman told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Increase the lasting good deeds. It was said: What are they, O Messenger of God? He said: The religion. It was said: What are they, O Messenger of God? He said: Allahu Akbar, “La ilaha illa God,” Tasbih, “Al-Hamdulillah,” and There is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty. Saeed bin Jubair, Masruq and Ibrahim said: The lasting good deeds are: the five daily prayers. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Another narration from him: that they are good deeds, and this is the saying of Qatada. The Almighty says: Better in the sight of your Lord as reward, meaning recompense. What is meant is and better in hope, meaning what a person hopes for. God Almighty said: 14- O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. Ibn Abbas said: These were men from the people of Mecca who had converted to Islam and wanted to migrate to Medina, but their wives and children prevented them and said: We have been patient with your Islam, so we will not be patient with being separated from you. So they obeyed them and abandoned the migration, so God Almighty said: So beware of them, that you obey them and abandon the migration. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. This is for someone who stayed with his family and children and did not emigrate. When he emigrated, he saw that those who had emigrated before him had understood the religion. They were to punish his wife and children who had been discouraged from emigrating. If they joined him in the land of emigration, he would not spend on them or bestow any good upon them. So God, the Most High, commanded that he pardon and forgive them. Ata bin Yasar said: It was revealed about Awf bin Malik Al-Ashja’i. He had a family and children, and whenever he wanted to go out for a military expedition, they would cry to him and show compassion for him, and say: To whom are you leaving us? He would take compassion for them and stay. Then God revealed: Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you by making you abandon obedience, so beware of accepting them from them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then do not punish them for their opposition to you, for God is Forgiving and Merciful.
18:47: 47 - The Almighty’s saying: And the Day We set the mountains in motion. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read: set in motion with a ta’ and a fat-ha on the ya’. The mountains is in the nominative case. Its evidence is the Almighty’s saying: And when the mountains are set in motion At-Takwir - 3. Others read it with a noon and a kasra on the yaa, the mountains is accusative, and moving the mountains means moving them from one place to another. And you will see the earth exposed, meaning: visible, with no trees, mountains, or plants on it, as He said: “He will leave it as a level plain. You will not see therein any crookedness or unevenness” (Ta-Ha: 107). Ata’ said: It is the emergence of what is inside it of the dead and others, so you see the interior of the earth appearing. And We gathered them together, all of them, to the place of standing and reckoning, and We did not leave out of them, that is, We did not leave out of them, a single one.
18:48: 48 - And they will be presented before your Lord in rows, meaning row by row, group by group, not that they are one row. It was said: standing, then it will be said to them, meaning the disbelievers: You have come to Us as We created you the first time, meaning alive, and it was said: individually as mentioned in Surat Al-An'am. And it was said: uncircumcised. But you claimed that We would not make an appointment for you, on the Day of Resurrection, he says to those who deny the Resurrection. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ma’la bin Asad told us, Wahb told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, who said: “People will be gathered in three ways: those who desire and those who fear, two on a camel, three on a camel, four on a camel, and ten on a camel. The rest of them will be gathered in the Fire, which will rest with them where they rested, spend the night with them where they spent the night, rise with them in the morning where they rose, and spend the evening with them where they spent the evening.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Katheer told us, Sufyan bin Al-Mughirah bin Al-Nu’man told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised. Then he recited, “As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [It is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.” (Al-Anbiya’: 104). The first to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Abraham. Some of my companions will be taken to the left, and I will say, My companions, my companions. He will say, They have not ceased turning back on their heels since I left them. I will say as the righteous servant said, And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them, up to His saying, The Exalted in Might, the Wise. (al-Ma’idah 5:117/118). Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, [Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi told us] Abu al-Qasim Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughlis told us, in Baghdad, Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamadani told us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Hatim ibn Abi Saghir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “I said, O Messenger of God, how will people be gathered on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Naked and barefoot. She said: I said, And the women? He said: And the women. She said: I said, O Messenger of God, we are shy. He said: O Aisha, the matter is more serious than that, that they are concerned about looking at each other.”
18:49: 49 - The Almighty said: And the Book is placed, meaning: the books [of the servants' deeds] are placed in the hands of the people, on their right and left, and it was said: its meaning is that they are placed in the hands of God the Almighty. Then you will see the criminals fearful, afraid, of what is in it, of evil deeds, and they will say, when they see it, Oh woe to us, Oh our destruction, and woe and woe means destruction, and everyone who falls into destruction calls out for woe, and the meaning of the call is to alert those being addressed, What is this Book that does not leave out anything small or great, of our sins. Ibn Abbas said: The small is a smile, and the big is a loud laugh. Saeed bin Jubair said: The small is the touch, the touch, and the kiss, and the big is adultery. Except that he counted it, he counted it. Al-Suddi said: he wrote it down and recorded it. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: he memorized it. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu al-Abbas Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Taysifuni told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Turabi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Bastam told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yasar al-Qurashi told us, Yusuf ibn Adi al-Masri told us, Abu Damrah Anas ibn Ayyad told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, who said: I do not know it except on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Beware of minor sins, for the example of minor sins is like that of a people who camped in a valley, and one of them brought a stick, and another brought a stick, and they cooked their bread, and minor sins are destructive.” God Almighty says: And they will find what they did present, written and recorded in their book, and your Lord does not wrong anyone, meaning that the reward of anyone who does good will not be diminished. Ad-Dahhak said: No one will be held accountable for a crime he did not commit. Abdullah bin Qais said: People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the two presentations: they will be arguments and excuses. As for the third presentation: at that time, the pages will fly into the hands, so I will take him with my right hand and I will take him with my left. Some of them attributed it to Abu Musa.
18:50: 50 - The Almighty said: And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ meaning: And remember, O Muhammad, when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ “and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was from the jinn,” Ibn Abbas said: He was from a group of angels called the jinn, who were created from the scorching fire. Al-Hasan said: He was from the jinn and not from the angels, so he is the origin of the jinn just as Adam is the origin of mankind. So he disobeyed, meaning he went out, from the command of his Lord, from obeying his Lord. Then will you take him, meaning O children of Adam, and his descendants as allies instead of Me, while they are enemies to you, meaning enemies. Mujalid narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi who said: “I was sitting one day when a man came and said: ‘Tell me, does Satan have a wife?’ I said: ‘I did not witness that wedding.’ Then I remembered the words of God Almighty: ‘Then would you take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me?’ I knew that offspring can only be from a wife, so I said: ‘Yes.’” Qatada said: They reproduce as the children of Adam reproduce. It was said: He inserts his tail into his anus and lays an egg, and the egg hatches to reveal a group of devils. Mujahid said: Among the descendants of Iblis are Laqis and Walhan, and they are the companions of purity and prayer, and Al-Hafaf and Marra and he is his nickname, and Zalnbur who is the owner of [the markets, he beautifies idle talk and false oaths and praising goods, and Thabr who is the owner of calamities] he beautifies scratching faces and slapping cheeks and tearing pockets, and Al-Awar who is the owner of adultery who blows into the urethra of a man and the buttocks of a woman, and Matous who is the owner of false report and throws it in the mouths of people, they do not find any basis for it, and Dasim who is the one who if a man enters his house and does not greet or mention the name of God, his sight is of the goods that are not raised or kept in their place, and if he eats and does not mention the name of God, he eats with it. Al-A’mash said: I might enter the house without mentioning the name of God or converting to Islam, and I would see a woman who was washing herself and say, Take this away, and I would argue with them. Then I would mention the name of God and say, Dasm, Dasm. It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “There is a devil for ablution called Al-Walhan. So beware of the whisperings of water.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Yahya bin Khalaf Al-Bahili told us, Abdul A’la told us, on the authority of Saeed Al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu Al-Ala, that Uthman bin Abi Al-Aas “came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, Satan has come between me and my prayer and my recitation, confusing it for me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is a Satan called Khanzab, so if you sense him, seek refuge in God from him, and spit to your left three times. He said: So I did that and God removed him from me.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir informed us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad informed us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi informed us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan informed us, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Satan places his throne on the water, then he sends out his troops, and the one closest to him in status is the one who causes the greatest temptation. One of them comes and says: I did such and such, and he says: You did nothing. He said: Then one of them comes and says: I did not leave him until I separated him from his wife. He said: So he brings him close to him and says: Yes, you are.” Al-A’mash said: I think he said: So he embraces him. God Almighty says: What an evil exchange for the wrongdoers. Qatada said: What an evil exchange they have made for the obedience of Satan and his offspring in exchange for the worship of their Lord.
18:51: 51 - I did not make them witness, I did not bring them, and Abu Ja`far read I did not make them witness with the letter nun and the letter alif for emphasis, meaning: We brought them, meaning Iblis and his offspring. It was said: the disbelievers. Al-Kalbi said: He means the angels, He created the heavens and the earth, nor did He create themselves, he says: I did not make them witness to a creation so that I could seek their help in creating it and consult them in it, and I would not have taken the misguiders as supporters, meaning: the devils who mislead people as supporters, meaning: supporters and helpers.
18:52: 52 - The Almighty said: And the Day He will say Hamzah read with a nun and the others with a ya, meaning: God will say to them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Call upon My partners meaning the idols whom you claimed that they were My partners so call upon them so they sought help from them but they did not respond to them meaning they did not answer them and did not support them and We placed between them meaning between the idols and their worshippers. It was said: between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance, a place of destruction that destroys, said Ata’ and Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Abbas said: It is a valley in the Fire. Mujahid said: A valley in Hell. Akrima said: It is a river in the fire, flowing with fire, and on its banks are snakes like black mules. Ibn Al-A'rabi said: Any barrier between two things is destructive, and its root is destruction. It is said: Awbaquhu, meaning: He destroyed him.
