Al-Farra’ said: And We made their communication in this world a destruction for them in the Hereafter. According to this statement, communication is evident, as in the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, ties between you have been severed (al-An’am 6:94). According to the reading of those who read with the nominative case.
18:53: 53 - And the criminals will see the Fire, meaning the polytheists, and they will think, they will be certain, that they will fall into it, they will enter it and fall into it, and they will find no way out from it, because it has surrounded them from every side.
18:54: 54 - The Almighty said: And We have certainly presented, explained, in this Qur’an for the people from every [kind of] example, meaning so that they may remember and take heed, but man is most disputatious of anything, arguing about falsehood. Ibn Abbas said: He meant Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith and his argument about the Qur’an. Al-Kalbi said: He meant Abi bin Khalaf Al-Jumahi. It was said: What is meant by the verse are the infidels, because God Almighty said: And those who disbelieve argue with falsehood (al-Kahf 18:56). It was said: It is general, and this is more correct. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, that Al-Hussein bin Ali told him: Ali told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night and said: Will you not pray? So I said: O Messenger of God, our souls are in the hand of God, so if He wills to resurrect us, He will resurrect us. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away when I said that to him and did not respond to me with anything, then I heard him turning away and striking his thigh and saying: And man is most disputatious of anything.
18:55: 55 - The Almighty said: And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them? The Qur’an, Islam, and the explanation from God Almighty, and it was said: It is the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And they ask forgiveness of their Lord, unless there comes to them the precedent of the former peoples, meaning: Our precedent in destroying them if they do not believe. It was said: Except that he asked for the same way of the ancients to come to them, of witnessing the punishment, as they said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment (al-Anfal 8:32). Or the punishment comes to them before them, Ibn Abbas said: meaning: clearly from the encounter. Mujahid said: suddenly. Abu Jaafar and the people of Kufa read: before with a damma on the qaf and the ya’, the plural of qabil, meaning: types of punishment, one type after another.
18:56: 56 - "And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. And those who disbelieve argue with falsehood," and their argument is their saying: "Has God sent a human being as a messenger?" (Al-Isra': 94). "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?" (al-Zukhruf 43:31), and the like, "to refute, to invalidate, thereby the truth, and the root of refutation is slippery, meaning to remove the truth by it, and they took My verses and that with which they were warned in ridicule," in it is an implied meaning that what they were warned with, which is the Qur'an, in ridicule, meaning mockery.
18:57: 57 - And who is more unjust than he who is reminded, admonished, of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them, turns away from them and abandons them and does not believe in them, and forgets what his hands have put forth, that is, what he did of sins before, Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, covers, lest they understand it, that is, comprehend it, meaning lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness, that is, deafness and heaviness, and if you call them, O Muhammad, to guidance, to the religion, they will never be guided then, and this is about people whom God knows will not believe.
18:58: 58 - And your Lord is the Forgiving, the Possessor of Mercy, the Possessor of Grace. If He were to impose blame upon them, punish the disbelievers, for what they have earned, of sins, He would have hastened the punishment for them, in this world. Rather, for them is an appointed time, meaning the resurrection and the reckoning. They will not find besides Him a refuge, a shelter.
18:59: 59 - And those towns We destroyed, meaning: the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, the people of Lot, and others, when they wronged, they disbelieved, and We appointed for their destruction an appointed time, meaning: a time limit. Abu Bakr read for their destruction with the opening of the meem and the lam, [and Hafs read with the opening of the meem and the kasra of the lam, and likewise in An-Namm a destruction, meaning for the time of their destruction], and the others read with the closing of the meem and the opening of the lam, meaning: for their destruction.
18:60: 60 - The Almighty said: And when Moses said to his boy, ‘I will not cease until I reach the junction of the two seas.’ Most scholars said: He is Moses bin Imran. Some of them said: He is Moses bin Misha, one of the sons of Joseph, and the first is more correct. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmed Al-Malhi told us, Ahmed bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Amr bin Dinar told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf Al-Bakali claims that Moses, the companion of Al-Khidr, is not the Moses of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of God has lied. Abi bin Kaab told us that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Moses stood up as a preacher among the Children of Israel, and was asked who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. God rebuked him, because he did not refer the knowledge to Him. Then God revealed to him that I have a servant at the confluence of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Moses said: O Lord, how can I get him? He said: Take a fish with you and put it in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, it is there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket and set off, and his servant Joshua bin Nun set off with him, until they reached the rock, they put their heads down and slept, and the fish stirred in the basket and came out of it and fell into The sea, so it took its path in the sea as a shoal, and God Almighty held back the flow of water from the whale, so it became like a ceiling over it. When he woke up, his companion forgot to tell him about the whale, so they set out for the rest of their day and night until the next day, Moses said to his boy: Bring us our lunch, we have certainly encountered fatigue in this journey of ours. He said: Moses did not find fatigue until he passed the place he was ordered to, and his boy said to him: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the whale, and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan, and it took its path in the sea as a wonder. He said: So the whale had a shoal, and for Moses and his boy it was a wonder. Moses said: That is what we were seeking. He said: They returned, following their tracks until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment, so Moses greeted him, and Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, said: How can I be in your land? He said: I am Moses. He said: Moses, the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: You will not be able to have patience with me, O Moses. I have knowledge of the knowledge of God which He has taught me that you do not know, and you have knowledge of the knowledge of God which God has taught you, which I do not know. Moses said: You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. Al-Khidr said to him: If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you. So they set out walking along the shore of the sea, and a ship passed by, so they spoke to them to carry them. They recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried them without a rope. When they boarded the ship, Al-Khidr had already torn off one of the ship’s planks with an axe. Moses said to him: They carried us without a rope. Did you go to their ship and rip it open to drown its people? Indeed, He said: Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me? He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot and do not burden me with my affair. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first of Moses was forgetfulness [and the middle was a condition and the third was deliberate]. He said: A bird came and landed on the edge of the ship and pecked at the sea. Al-Khidr said to him: My knowledge and your knowledge have not diminished from the knowledge of God except as this bird has diminished from this sea. Then they got out of the ship. While they were walking on the shore, Al-Khidr saw a boy playing with the boys. Al-Khidr took hold of his head and tore it off with his hand and killed him. Moses said to him: Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done something horrible. He said: Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me? He said: This is more severe than the first. He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me. You have received an excuse from me. So they set out until they came to the people of a town. They asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. They found a wall there that was about to collapse, so he fixed it. He said: It was leaning. Al-Khidr raised his hand and fixed it. Moses said: People we came to, but they did not feed us or host us. If you wished, you could have taken payment for it. He said: This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not bear patiently. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he said: We wish that Moses had been patient so that he could tell us about their story. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: And before them was a king who seized every good ship by force, and he used to recite: And as for the boy, he was a disbeliever, while his parents were believers. On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair in another narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Moses, the Messenger of God, stood up one day and mentioned the people until the eyes overflowed and the hearts softened. He turned away and a man caught up with him and said: O Messenger of God, is there anyone on earth who is more knowledgeable than you? He said: No. So God rebuked him, because he did not refer knowledge to God. It was said: Yes, [our servant Al-Khidr]. He said: O Lord, and where? He said: At the confluence of the two seas. [He said: O Lord, grant me knowledge that is more knowledgeable about you than you.] He said: Take a dead whale where the soul is breathed into it. In another narration, it was said to him: Take provisions of a salty whale, for that is where the whale is lost. So he took a whale and put it in a basket.” We return to the interpretation, the Almighty’s saying: And when Moses said to his servant, Joshua bin Nun, I will not cease, meaning I will not cease walking until I reach the junction of the two seas, Qatada said: The Persian Gulf and the Roman Sea, which are towards the east. Muhammad bin Ka’b said: Tangiers. Abi bin Ka’b said: Africa. Or I spend ages, even if it is ages, meaning a long time and period, and its plural is ages, and ages is the plural of ages. Abdullah bin Omar said: Age is eighty years, so they carried bread and a salted fish until they reached the rock at the confluence of the two seas at night, and near it was a spring called the Water of Life, and nothing touches that water except living, so when the spirit of the water and its cold touched the fish, it stirred in the basket and came to life and entered the sea.
18:61: 61 - This is what God Almighty said: So when they reached, meaning Moses and his servant, the place where they met, meaning between the two seas, they forgot, they left, their fish, and the fish was with Joshua, and he is the one who forgot it, and he attributed the forgetfulness to them because they both had provisions for their journey, just as it is said: The people went out to such and such a place, and they carried such and such provisions, and only one of them carried it. So he took - that is, the whale - his path in the sea, a swarm - that is, a path. [It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: The water separated from the path of the whale and became a hole that did not close, so Moses entered the hole following the whale’s trail and behold, he was Al-Khidr.” Ibn Abbas said: The whale did not touch anything in the sea without drying up until it became a rock. Al-Kalbi said: Joshua bin Nun performed ablution from the spring of life, and the salty fish in the bucket of that water was sprinkled on it, and it came to life. Then it jumped into that water and began to strike with its tail, and it did not strike anything of the water with its tail while it was going except that it dried up. We have narrated that when they reached the rock, they put their heads down and slept, and the whale became agitated, so it came out and fell into the sea, and it took its way in the sea as a swarm, so God stopped the flow of water from the whale, so it became like a ceiling over it. When Moses woke up, his companion forgot to tell him, so they set off until the next day.
18:62: 62 - The Almighty’s saying: So when they had passed, meaning that place, which is the meeting place of the two seas, he said, Moses, to his boy, ‘Bring us our lunch,’ meaning our food. Lunch is what is prepared for eating in the morning, and dinner is what is prepared for eating in the evening. We have certainly encountered fatigue on this journey of ours, meaning: exhaustion and hardship, and that is because hunger was cast upon Moses after passing the rock, so that he would remember the fish and return to his goal.
18:63: 63 - He said to him, and he remembered, Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? It was a rock that was in the promised place. Maqal bin Ziyad said: It is the rock that is below the River of Oil, I forgot the fish, meaning I left it and lost it. That is because when Joshua saw that from the fish, he got up to catch up with Moses and tell him, but he forgot to tell him, so they stayed that day until they prayed the noon prayer the next day. It was said that there is an omission in the verse, meaning: I forgot to mention to you the matter of the whale. Then he said: And none made me forget to mention it to you except Satan, meaning: And none made me forget to mention to you the matter of the whale except Satan. Hafs read: He made me forget it, and in al-Fath 48:upon him be God with a damma on the ha. It was said that it means he made me forget him so that I would not remember him. And he took his way in the sea, a wondrous thing. It was said: This is from the words of Joshua, who said: The whale leapt into the sea and took a path in it, so I was amazed by that. We narrated in al-Naba 78:The whale had a school, and Moses and his servant had a wonder. It was said: This is from what Moses said when Joshua told him and took his way in the sea. Moses said to him: Amazing, as if he said: Amazingly amazing. Ibn Zayd said: What is more amazing than a whale that is eaten openly, then becomes alive after some of it has been eaten?
18:64: 64 - He said, Moses, That is what we were seeking, meaning we were seeking, so they returned, following their footsteps," meaning: they returned, following the traces from which he had come, meaning: they followed it, and they found a servant of Ours. It was said: he was a king from the angels. The correct version that came in the histories, and was confirmed from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is that he was Al-Khidr, and his name was Balya bin Malkan. It was said: he was from the descendants of the Children of Israel. It was said: he was from the sons of kings who renounced the world. Al-Khidr is a title for him, and he was called that because: Abu Ali Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said, Abu Hurairah told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He was called Al-Khidr because he sat on a white fur and it swayed green beneath him. Mujahed said: He was called Al-Khidr because when he prayed, everything around him turned green. We narrated: Moses saw Al-Khidr covered with a garment, so he greeted him. Al-Khidr said: How can I bring peace to your land? He said: I am Moses, I have come to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. In another narration, he found him covered with a garment, lying on his back, part of the garment under his head and part under his feet. In another narration, he found him while he was praying. It is narrated that he found him on a green carpet on the seabed. This is what God Almighty said:
18:65: 65 - And they found one of Our servants to whom We had given mercy, meaning a blessing, from Us and had taught him knowledge from Us, meaning knowledge of the unseen by inspiration. Al-Khidr was not a prophet according to most scholars.
18:66: 66 - So when Moses said to him, 'Shall I follow you?' He said: I came to you to follow you and accompany you, on condition that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. Abu Amr and Yaqub read: Sound judgment with a fat-ha on the ra' and the shin, and the others read: with a damma on the ra' and a sukoon on the shin, meaning correctness. And it was said: Knowledge with which you guide me. In some reports, when Moses said this to him, Al-Khidr said to him: The Torah is enough knowledge and the Children of Israel are enough occupation. Moses said to him: God commanded me to do this at that time.
18:67: 67 - He said, al-Khidr, You will not be able to have patience with me. He only said that because he knew that he would see reprehensible things, and it is not permissible for prophets to have patience with reprehensible things. Then he explained his excuse for not being patient, saying:
18:68: 68 - And how can you be patient with something you do not have knowledge of?
18:69: 69 - He said, Moses, You will find me, God willing, patient, he only made an exception because he did not trust himself to be patient, nor will I disobey you in any matter, meaning: I will not disobey you in what you command.
18:70: 70 - "He said: If you follow me," meaning if you accompany me, and he did not say: follow me, but rather left the choice up to him, except that he imposed a condition on him, saying: "Do not ask me, Abu Ja`far, Nafi`, and Ibn `Amir read it with the opening of the lam and the emphasis on the noon, and the others with the sukoon of the lam and the softening of the noon, about something that I do of what you disapprove of and do not object to, until I mention it to you," until I begin to mention it to you and explain its matter to you.
18:71: 71 - So they set out, walking along the coast looking for a ship to board. They found a ship to board. They found a ship and boarded it. The people on the ship said: These are thieves, and they ordered them to leave. The owner of the ship said: They are not thieves, but I see the faces of the prophets. We narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “A ship passed by them and they spoke to them to carry them. They recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried them without a ship. When they reached the sea, Al-Khidr took an axe and tore a plank from the ship.” “Until, when they embarked on the ship, he made a hole in it. Moses said to him, ‘Did you make a hole in it to drown its people?’” Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: li-yaghraq with a ya’ and a fatha on the ra’, its people in the nominative case as a requirement. The others read: with a ta’ and a ya’ and a kasra on the ra’, its people in the accusative case as belonging to Al-Khidr. You have done something bitter meaning: something reprehensible. In the speech of the Arabs, Imr means cunning. Its origin is: everything severe and plentiful. It is said: The people became numerous if they became numerous and their matter became severe. Al-Qatibi said: Imran means: amazing. It was narrated that when Al-Khidr made a hole in the ship, the water did not enter it. It was narrated that when Moses saw that, he took his garment and stuffed the hole with it. It was narrated that Al-Khidr took a glass cup and patched the hole in the ship with it.
18:72: 72 - He said, the scholar, who was Al-Khidr, Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?
18:73: 73 - He said, Moses, Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, Ibn Abbas said: He did not forget, but it is an implied speech, as if he forgot something else. It was said: Its meaning is what you left out of your covenant, and forgetting is abandonment. Abi bin Kaab said on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The first of Moses was forgetfulness, the middle was a condition, and the third was deliberate. Do not burden me and do not deceive me, with my affair being difficult. It was said: Do not impose hardship on me. It is said: I burdened him with hardship, meaning: I made that difficult for him. He says: Do not make my affair difficult for me, and treat me with ease, and do not treat me with difficulty.
18:74: 74 - So they set out until they met a boy and killed him. In the story, they came out of the sea walking, and they passed by two boys playing, so Al-Khidr took a charming boy with a bright face, laid him down, and then slaughtered him with a knife. Al-Suddi said: He had the most handsome face. His face was glowing with beauty. We narrated that he took hold of his head and pulled it out with his hand. Abd al-Razzaq narrated this story, and he pointed with his three fingers, the thumb, index finger and middle finger, and pulled out his head. It was narrated that he hit his head with stones. It was said: He hit his head against the wall and killed him. Ibn Abbas said: He was a boy who had not yet reached puberty, and this is the opinion of the majority. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet of God did not say: You killed a pure soul except when he was a boy who had not yet reached puberty. Al-Hasan said: He was a man. Shuaib al-Jubba’i said: His name was Haisur. Al-Kalbi said: He was a young man who would cut off the land, take possessions, and seek refuge with his parents. Al-Dahhak said: He was a young boy who was corrupt and his parents were harmed by him. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abdullah bin Muslimah bin Mu’tab told us, Muammar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ruqayyah bin Musaqala, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The boy whom Al-Khidr killed was born a disbeliever, and if he had lived, he would have exhausted his parents with his transgression and disbelief. He said, Moses, did you kill a pure soul? Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, Abu Ja’far, and Abu Amr read: pure with an alif, and the others read: pure. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said: Their meaning is the same, like the harsh and the harsh. Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala’ said: pure is the one who never sinned, and pure is the one who sinned and then repented. Without a soul, meaning: she did not kill a soul [with something] that required killing. You have done something reprehensible, meaning something reprehensible. Qatada said: Reprehensible is greater than something commanded, because it is the reality of destruction, and in the breach of the ship there was fear of destruction. It was said: The matter is greater, because it involved drowning a large number of people. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, Ya’qub, and Abu Bakr read here: Nakar and in Surat At-Talaq with a dammah on the kaf, and the others with a sukoon on it.
18:75: 75 - He said meaning Al-Khidr: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? In Surat At-Talaq, with the kaf in the damma, and the others with it in the sukoon.
18:76: 76 - He said, Moses, If I ask you about anything after this, after this time, do not accompany me, and leave me. Jacob read: do not accompany me, without the alif of companionship. I have given you an excuse from Me. Abu Ja`far, Nafi`, and Abu Bakr read from Me with a light nun, while the others read it with a heavy nun. Ibn Abbas said: That is, I have given you an excuse for what is between Me and you. It was said: You warned me that I could not be patient with you. It was also said: The excuse for leaving me became clear to you. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafir bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Qaisi told us, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ruqayyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on us and on Moses. Whenever he mentioned one of the prophets, he would start with himself. Had he not been hasty, he would have seen wonder. But he was held back by his companion. He said: "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep company with me. You have received an excuse from me." If he had been patient, he would have seen wonder.
18:77: 77 - The Almighty said: So they set out, until they came to the people of a town, Ibn Abbas said: He means: Antioch. Ibn Sirin said: It is Al-Ubla, which is the land furthest from the sky. It was also said: Barqa. And on the authority of Abu Hurairah: The town of Andalusia They asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. Abi bin Kaab said on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Until when they came to the people of a village, they were mean and went around the gatherings and asked the people for food, but they refused to host them. It was narrated that they went around the village and asked them for food, but they did not feed them, and they asked them for hospitality, but they did not host them. Qatada said: The worst villages are those that do not host guests. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: A Berber woman fed them after they had asked the men for food but they did not feed them. So he prayed for their women and cursed their men. The Almighty says: And they found therein a wall about to collapse, meaning to fall. This is a metaphor for the speech of the Arabs, because the wall has no will, but rather its meaning is: it is close and about to fall, just as the Arabs say: My house looks at so-and-so’s house if it is opposite it. So he straightened it, that is, he leveled it. It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, So Al-Khidr raised his hand and straightened it. Saeed bin Jubair said: He wiped the wall with his hand and it became straight. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He demolished it and then sat down to build it. Al-Suddi said: Rather, he made it with clay and began to build the wall. He said, Moses, If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ya`qub read: I would have taken a wage for it, with a light ta’ and a kasra on the kha’. The others read: I would have taken a wage for it, with a heavy ta’ and a fatha on the kha’. These are two dialects: like I followed and I followed. “For it” means for repairing the wall. Ajran means a fee. Its meaning is: You know that we are hungry and that the people of the village have not fed us, so if you had taken a wage for your work.
18:78: 78 - He said, Al-Khidr: This is a parting between me and you, meaning this is a time of parting between me and you. It was said: This denial of abandoning the reward is the parting between us. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is this is a parting between us, meaning the parting of our connection, and he repeated between for emphasis. I will inform you, meaning I will tell you the interpretation of that which you could not bear patiently. In some interpretations, Moses took hold of his garment and said: Tell me the meaning of what you did before you left me. He said:
18:79: 79 - As for the ship, it belonged to poor people who worked at sea. Ka’b said: It belonged to ten brothers, five of whom were in the sea and five of whom worked at sea. This is evidence that even if a poor person owns something, the name poor does not cease to apply to him if what he owns does not suffice him. They work at sea means: they are hired and earn from it. So I wanted to make it defective, make it defective. And behind them means in front of them, was a king, as in His saying: Behind him was Hell (Ibrahim 14:16). It was said: behind them behind them, and their return was on their way to him, and the first is more correct, indicated by the reading of Ibn Abbas and there was a king before him. He takes every ship by force, meaning: every good ship by force. Ibn Abbas used to recite it like this, so Al-Khidr tore it apart and damaged it so that the usurping king would not take it. His name was Al-Julanda and he was an unbeliever. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: His name is Mutawala bin Julanda Al-Azdi. Shuaib al-Juba’i said: His name is Haddad bin Badad. It was narrated that Al-Khidr apologized to the people and told them about the usurping king, and they did not know about him. He said: I wanted him to leave her when she passed by him because of her defect, and when he passed by them they would fix her and benefit from her. It was said: They sealed her with a bottle. It was also said: With tar.
18:80: 80 - The Almighty said: And as for the boy, his parents were believers, so we feared, meaning we knew, [and in the reading of Ibn Abbas: And as for the boy, his parents were believers, so we feared, meaning: we knew], that he would overburden them, that he would overwhelm them, and Al-Kalbi said: that he would burden them, through transgression and disbelief, Saeed bin Jubair said: So we feared that his love would lead them to follow him in his religion.
18:81: 81 - So We wanted to replace them both, Abu Jaafar, Nafi' and Abu Amr read: with emphasis here and in Surat At-Tahrim and Al-Qalam, and the others read it with emphasis, and they are two dialects, and some of them differentiated and said: Al-Tabdil is changing something, or changing its state and the same thing is still there, and Al-Ibdal is raising something and putting something else in its place, Their Lord is better than him in purity, meaning righteousness and piety, and nearer to kinship, Ibn Amir, Abu Jaafar, and Ya'qub read: with a damma on the ha', and the rest read it with a jazm, meaning: in connection with mercy. It was said: It is from the womb and kinship, Qatada said: meaning he is more connected to the womb and is dutiful to his parents. Al-Kalbi said: God replaced them with a slave girl, and a prophet married her, and she bore him a prophet, and God guided his mother from the nations through him. On the authority of Jaafar bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father: God replaced them with a girl who gave birth to seventy prophets. Ibn Jurayj said: Replace them with a Muslim boy. Mutraf said: His parents were happy when he was born and sad when he was killed. If he had lived, it would have been their destruction. So let a person be satisfied with the decree of God Almighty, for God’s decree for the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree in what he likes.
18:82: 82 - The Almighty said: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and their names were Asram and Sareem, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, they differed about that treasure, they differed about that treasure: It was narrated on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: It was gold and silver. Akrima said: It was money. On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: The treasure was pages containing knowledge. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said: It was a golden tablet on which was written: (It is strange that one who is certain of death, how he rejoices! It is strange that one who is certain of the reckoning, how he is heedless! It is strange that one who is certain of provision, how he tires himself! It is strange that one who is certain of destiny, how he is exhausted! It is strange that one who is certain of the transience of the world and its vicissitudes with its people, how he feels reassured by it! There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God). And on the other side it was written: (I am God, there is no god but Me, alone, without partner. I created good and evil, so blessed is he whom I created for good and through whose hands I made it happen, and woe to he whom I created for evil and through whose hands I made it happen). This is the saying of most of the commentators. It was also narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Al-Zajjaj said: When the word treasure is used in general, it refers to a treasure of money. However, when it is restricted, it is permissible to say that he has a treasure of knowledge, and this tablet was a collection of both. And their father was righteous. It was said that his name was Kaseh and that he was one of the pious. Ibn Abbas said: They were preserved by the righteousness of their parents. It was said: There were seven fathers between them and the righteous father. Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir said: God protects, through the righteousness of the servant, his children [and his children’s children], his family, his clan, and the people of the villages around him. They will remain in God’s protection as long as he is among them. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: I am praying and then I remember my son, so I prolong my prayer. The Almighty said: And your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity, meaning: that they should reach maturity and understand. It was said: that they should reach their maturity and strength. It was also said: eighteen years. "And they will extract then their treasure, a mercy, a blessing, from your Lord." And I did not do it of my own accord, meaning by my choice and opinion, but rather I did it by the command and inspiration of God. That is the interpretation of that which you could not bear patiently, meaning you could not bear it patiently. Was able and was able have the same meaning. It was narrated that when Moses wanted to leave him, he said to him: Give me advice. He said: Do not seek knowledge to speak about it, but seek it to act upon it. They differed as to whether Al-Khidr was alive or dead. It was said that Al-Khidr and Elias were alive and met every year at the season. The reason for his life, as it is narrated, was that he drank from the spring of life. This was because Dhul-Qarnayn entered the darkness to seek the spring of life. Al-Khidr was at the forefront of his army, so Al-Khidr came upon the spring, so he descended, washed, performed ablution, drank, and prayed in thanks to God Almighty. Dhul-Qarnayn lost his way and returned. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said after praying the Isha prayer one night: What do you think of this night of yours? After a hundred years, not one of those who is alive today on the face of the earth will remain. If Al-Khidr were alive, he would not have lived after him.
18:83: 83 - The Almighty said: “And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, ‘I will recite to you a report about him.’” As report, and they differed about his prophethood: Some of them said: He was a prophet. Abu al-Tayyib said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asked about Dhul-Qarnayn: Was he a prophet or a king? He said: He was neither a prophet nor a king, but he was a servant who loved God and God loved him. He advised God and God advised him. It was narrated that Omar, may God be pleased with him, heard a man say to another: O Dhul-Qarnayn. He said: You named yourself after the names of the prophets, but you were not satisfied until you named yourself after the names of the angels. Most people agree that he was a just and righteous king. They differed about the reason for calling him Dhul-Qarnayn. Al-Zuhri said: Because he reached the two horns of the sun, its rising and setting. It was said: Because he was the king of Rome and Persia. It was said: Because he entered the light and darkness. It was said that he saw in a dream that he was seized by the horns of the sun. It was said: Because he had two beautiful locks of hair. It was said: Because he had two horns that were hidden by the turban. Abu al-Tayyib narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: He was called Dhul-Qarnayn because he ordered his people to fear God, so they struck him on his right horn and he died, then God resurrected him. Then he ordered them to fear God, so they struck him on his left horn and he died, then God revived him. They differed about his name. It was said that his name was Marzban bin Marzaba the Greek from the descendants of Yunan bin Japheth bin Noah. It was also said that his name was Alexander bin Philophus bin Yamalos the Roman.
18:84: 84 - The Almighty said: Indeed, We established him upon the earth, meaning We paved the way. Enabling means preparing the means. Ali said: He subjected the clouds to him, so they carried him upon them, and extended the means for him, and spread out the light for him, so that night and day were the same for him. This is the meaning of establishing him upon the earth, which is that He made it easy for him to travel upon it and made its paths easy for him. And We gave him of all things meaning: We gave him of everything that creation needs. It was said: It is one of the things that kings use to conquer cities and fight enemies. A cause, meaning: knowledge that causes everything he wants, and by which he travels throughout the regions of the earth. The cause is: that which brings something about. Al-Hasan said: To reach where he wanted. It was also said: We brought the ends of the earth close to him.
18:85: 85 - So he followed a path, meaning: he took a path and walked. The people of Hijaz and Basra read: So he followed and Then he followed connected and stressed. The others read it by cutting off the alif and making the ta' jazm. It was said that their meaning is the same. The correct answer is: The difference between them is that whoever cuts off the alif and makes the ta’ jazm, and it was said: Their meaning is the same. The correct answer is: The difference between them. Whoever cuts off the alif, its meaning is: he attained the truth. Whoever reads it with emphasis, its meaning is: he walked. It is said: I continued to follow him until I followed him, meaning: I continued to walk behind him until I caught up with him. His saying: a cause means: a path. Ibn Abbas said: a home.
18:86: 86 - Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a hot spring. Abu Ja`far, Abu `Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa`i, and Abu Bakr read: Hamiyyah with an unhamzated alif, meaning: hot. The others read: Hamiyyah with a unhamzated alif, meaning: having hot mud, which is black clay. Muawiyah asked Kaab: How do you find in the Torah that the sun sets? He said: We find in the Torah that it sets in water and mud. Al-Qatibi said: It is possible that the meaning of his saying in a hot spring is: there is a hot spring there, or in the opinion of the eye. And he found there a people, meaning: near the spring, a nation. Ibn Jurayj said: A city with twelve thousand gates. If it were not for the noise of its people, you would have heard the sound of the sun setting. We said, ‘O Dhul-Qarnayn!’ This is used as evidence by those who claim that he was a prophet, because God Almighty addressed him, and the most correct view is that he was not a prophet, and what is meant by it is inspiration. Either you punish, meaning: either you kill them if they do not enter Islam, or you treat them kindly, meaning: you pardon and forgive. It was also said: you take them captive and teach them guidance. God gave him the choice between the two options.
18:87: 87 - “He said, ‘As for he who has wronged,’ meaning, disbelieved, ‘We will punish him,’ meaning, we will kill him, ‘then he will be returned to his Lord,’ in the Hereafter, ‘and He will punish him with a terrible punishment,’ meaning, with fire, and fire is more terrible than killing.”
18:88: 88 - "But as for he who believes and does righteousness, he will have the best reward." Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, Hafs, and Ya'qub read: "jaza'an" in the accusative case with a tanween, meaning: he will have the best. "jaza'an" in the accusative case as a source [which is a source that takes the place of a state, meaning: he will have the best reward with it]. Others read: with the nominative case as an addition, so al-husna is Paradise, and he added the reward to it, as he said: And the home of the Hereafter is better Yusuf - 9, and the home is the Hereafter. It was said that what is meant by al-Hasna according to this reading is: righteous deeds. That is, he will have the reward for righteous deeds. And We will speak to him of Our command with ease, meaning: We will speak to him gently, and treat him with ease in Our command. Mujahid said: Easy means: well-known.
18:89: 89 - Then he followed a path, meaning: he took paths and houses.
18:90: 90 - Until, when he reached the place of sunrise, meaning the place of its rising, he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made any shield against it. Qatada and Al-Hasan said: There was no shield between them and the sun, and that was because they were in a place where no building could be built, so they would be in groups of their own, until when the sun had passed their zenith, they would go out to their livelihoods and their fields. Al-Hassan said: When the sun rose, they would enter the water, and when it rose above them, they would come out, grazing like animals. Al-Kalbi said: They are naked people, one of them spreads out one of his ears and covers himself with the other.
18:91: 91 - The Almighty’s saying: Likewise, it was said: its meaning is just as he reached the setting of the sun, so he reached its rising. The correct view is that its meaning is: just as he ruled on the people who are at the setting of the sun, so he ruled on those who are at the rising of the sun. And We have encompassed what he has with Him, meaning: what he has and what he has with him of soldiers, equipment, and tools with knowledge, meaning: knowledge.
18:93: 93 - Until he reached between the two barriers, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Hafs read: the two barriers and a barrier here with the fatha on the seen, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i agreed with a barrier, [the rest read: with the damma on the seen, and in Yasin a barrier with the fatha Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs] and the rest read with the damma, some of them said: they are two languages, their meaning is one. And Ikrimah said: whatever was made by the sons of Adam is the barrier with the fatha, and whatever was made by God is the barrier with the damma, and Abu Amr said the same. And it was said: the barrier: with the fatha is a source, and with the damma is a noun, and here they are: two mountains, Dhul-Qarnayn blocked what was between them, a barrier between Gog and Magog and those behind them. And he found a people beyond them meaning: in front of the two barriers. They hardly understand a word. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: they understand with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the qaf, meaning they do not understand the words of others. The others read: with a fatha on the ya’ and the qaf, meaning they do not understand the words of others. Ibn Abbas said: They do not understand the words of anyone, and people do not understand their words.
18:94: 94 - “They said, ‘O Dhul-Qarnayn!’” If it is said: How did they say that when they did not understand? It was said: A translated verse was spoken about them. Its evidence is: Ibn Masoud’s reading: They can hardly understand a word. Those below them said, O Dhul-Qarnayn. “Indeed, Gog and Magog,” Asim read them with two hamzas [and also in Al-Anbiya’, Gog and Magog have been conquered], and the others without a hamza [in the two surahs]. They are two languages, their origin is from the flames of fire, which is its light and sparks, and they were likened to it because of their large number and intensity. It was said: with the hamza from the intensity of the blazing fire, and without the hamza two foreign names, such as: Harut and Marut, and they are from the sons of Japheth, son of Noah. Ad-Dahhak said: They are a generation of the Turks. As-Suddi said: The Turks are a group of Gog and Magog who went out and Dhul-Qarnayn struck the dam, [and remained outside it, so all the Turks are from them. And on the authority of Qatada: They are twenty-two tribes, Dhul-Qarnayn built the dam] on twenty-one tribes, and one remained, so they are the Turks. They were called the Turks because they were left outside. Historians said: Noah’s sons were three: Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Shem was the father of the Arabs, Persians, and Romans. Ham was the father of the Abyssinians, Zanj, and Nubia. Japheth was the father of the Turks, Khazars, and Slavs, and Gog and Magog. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Ata’: They are ten parts, and the children of Adam are all one part. It was narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, that he said: “Yajuj is a nation, and Majuj is a nation, each nation is four hundred thousand nations. A man of them will not die until he sees a thousand males from his loins, all of whom have taken up arms and are from the children of Adam, marching to destroy the world. It was said: They are three types. One type of them is like the cedars, the trees of the Levant, its height is one hundred and twenty cubits in the sky. Another type of them is the same in width and length, one hundred and twenty cubits, and no mountain or iron can withstand them. Another type of them spreads out one of their ears and covers himself with the other. They do not pass an elephant, wild animal, or pig without eating it, and whoever of them dies, they eat it. Their vanguard is in the Levant and their rear guard is in Khurasan. They drink the rivers of the East and Lake Tiberias.” On the authority of Ali, he said: Some of them are a handspan tall, and some of them are extremely tall. Kaab said: They are rare among the children of Adam. Adam had a wet dream one day and his sperm mixed with the dust, so God created from that water Gog and Magog. They are connected to us from the father’s side, not the mother’s. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Dhul-Qarnayn was a Roman man, the son of an old woman. When he reached puberty, he was a righteous slave. God said to him: I am sending you to nations with different languages. Among them are two nations between which is the length of the earth: one of them is at the setting of the sun, called Nasik, and the other is at its rising, called Mansak. There are also two nations between which is the width of the earth: one of them is in the right hemisphere, called Hawil, and the other is in the left hemisphere, called Ta'wil. There are nations in the middle of the earth, including the jinn, mankind, Gog and Magog. Dhul-Qarnayn said: By what power can I overcome them? By what group can I outnumber them? And by what language can I speak to them? God the Almighty said: I will make you stand upright, and I will make your tongue easy for you, and I will strengthen your arm so that nothing will frighten you, and I will clothe you with awe so that nothing will terrify you, and I will subject to you the light and the darkness and make them your soldiers, the light will guide you from before you and the darkness will surround you from behind you, so he set out, until he came to the setting of the sun and found a crowd and a number that only God can count, so he confronted them with darkness until he gathered them in one place, and called them to God and His worship, and some of them believed, and some of them turned away from Him, so he went to those who turned away from Him and brought darkness upon them so that it entered their hearts and their homes and they entered into his call, so he recruited a great army from the people of the west and set out leading them and the darkness was driving them until he came to Hawil and did among them as he did with a hermit, then he went until he reached a hermit at the rising of the sun, and he worked in it and recruited from it soldiers as he did with the two nations, then he took the left side of the earth and came to Tawil and did in it as he had known it before, then he went to the nations that In the middle of the earth, when he approached the eastern end of the Turks, a righteous nation of mankind said to him: O Dhul-Qarnayn, between these two mountains there are creatures resembling beasts who prey on animals and wild beasts, [they have fangs and molars] like wild beasts, they eat snakes and scorpions, and every living thing, they were created on the earth and no creation increases as they increase, and there is no doubt that they will fill the earth and prevail over it and spread corruption in it, so shall we give you a tribute on condition that you make a barrier between us and them? He said: What my Lord has given me is better. He said: Return to the rocks and iron and copper so that I may learn their knowledge. So he set out until he reached the middle of their land and found them to be of the same size, the height of one of them being half of a square man among us, they have claws like fingernails in our hands and fangs and molars like wild beasts, and they have fringes of hair on their bodies to cover them and protect them from the heat and the cold, and each one of them has two large ears, one of which he spreads out and the other covers himself with, he spends the summer in one and the winter in the other, they copulate. The animals copulated where they met. When Dhul-Qarnayn saw that, he went to the area between the two mountain-sides, measured the distance between them, and dug a foundation until he reached the water. He filled it with rock and made its clay copper, which was melted and poured over it, so it became like a vein from a mountain under the ground. God Almighty said: They said, ‘O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land.’ Al-Kalbi said: Their corruption was that they would go out during the spring to their land and leave nothing green in it without eating it, and nothing dry without carrying it, and they would bring it into their land, and they would encounter severe harm and killing from them. It was said: Their corruption was that they used to eat people. It was said: It means that they will cause corruption on earth when they come out. Shall we then make for you a tax? Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read kharaj with an alif, and the others read kharaj without an alif. These are two languages with the same meaning, meaning a fee and wage from our money. Abu Amr said: Al-Kharj: What you donate, and Al-Kharaj: What you are obligated to pay. It was also said: Al-Kharaj: On the land, and Al-Kharaj: On the necks. It is said: Pay the tax on your head and the tax on your city. On the condition that you place a barrier between us and them, that is, a barrier, so that they cannot reach us.
18:95: 95 - He said, to them Dhul-Qarnayn: What has empowered me in it? Ibn Kathir read empowered me with two apparent noons, and the others read with one doubled noon with assimilation, meaning: What has empowered me in it, My Lord is better, than He made you, so help me with strength, meaning: I do not want money, rather help me with your bodies and strength, I will place between you and them a barrier, meaning: a dam, they said: What is that strength? He said: Workers and craftsmen who are good at building and work, and the machine. They said: What is that machine? He said:
18:96: 96 - Atooni: give me, and Abu Bakr read: Bring me meaning bring me, Zabr Al-Hadid meaning pieces of iron, the singular of which is Zabra, so they brought it to him and the firewood, and he placed some of it on top of the other, and he kept placing the iron on the firewood and the firewood on the iron, until he leveled between the two mountain sides, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read: with a damma on the sad and the dal, and Abu Bakr made the dal jazm, and the others read it with a fatha, and they are the two mountains, he leveled: meaning he leveled between the two ends of the mountains. He said, Blow. In the story, he put the coal and firewood in the iron sheets, then he said, Blow, meaning, into the fire. Until when He made it a fire, meaning the iron became fire, He said, ‘Bring me,’ Hamza and Abu Bakr read it connected, while the others read it with the alif cut off. He poured over it molten copper, meaning: Bring me molten copper so that I may pour over it. “Ifr” means pouring, and the drop means molten copper. So the fire began to consume the wood, and the copper became” in place of the wood until the iron adhered to the copper. Qatada said: It is like an inky cloak, with a black pattern and a red pattern. In the story: Its width was fifty cubits, its height was two hundred cubits, and its length was one farsakh.
18:97: 97 - They were not able to ascend it, to climb over it from above due to its length and smoothness, nor were they able to pierce it, from below it, due to its strength and hardness. Hamza read: They were not able with a shaddah on the ta', assimilating the ta' of ifti'al into the ta'.
18:98: 98 - He said, meaning Dhul-Qarnayn, This, meaning the dam, is a mercy, meaning a blessing, “from my Lord. So when the promise of my Lord comes,” it was said: the Resurrection. And it was said: the time of their emergence. He made it level. The people of Kufa read level with a long vowel and a hamza, meaning: smooth ground. The others read it without a long vowel, meaning: He made it level and flat with the surface of the earth. And the promise of my Lord is true. Qatada narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi’ on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “That Gog and Magog will dig it every day until they almost see the rays of the sun. The one over them will say: Go back and you will dig it tomorrow. Then God will restore it to how it was. Then, when their time has come, they will dig it until they almost see the rays of the sun. The one over them will say: Go back and you will dig it tomorrow, God willing. He made an exception, so they will return to it and it will be as it was when they left it. They will dig it and come out to the people, following the waters and the people will take refuge in their fortresses against them. They will shoot their arrows into the sky, and they will return in it like blood. They will say: We have conquered the people of the earth and have overcome the people of the sky. Then God will send upon them a scum in their backs and they will perish. And indeed, the beasts of the earth will grow fat.” And you thank them for their meat. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghafr bin Muhammad Al Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Mihran Al Razi told us, Al Waleed bin Muslim told us, Abdul Rahman bin Yazid bin Jaber told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Jaber Al Ta’i, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Jubair bin Nufayr, on the authority of his father Jubair bin Nufayr, on the authority of Al Nawwas bin Sam’an, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the Antichrist one morning, and he spoke in a low and high tone until we thought he was among a group of palm trees. When we went to him, he recognized that in us, and he said: What is the matter with you? We said: O Messenger of God, you mentioned the Antichrist one morning, and he spoke in a low and high tone, until we thought he was among a group of palm trees. He said: Is it someone other than the Antichrist that I fear for you? If he emerges while I am among you, then I will be his opponent on your behalf. But if he emerges while I am not among you, then every man is his own opponent, and God is my successor over every Muslim. He is a young man with a white spot in his right eye. I liken him to Abd al-Uzza ibn Qatan, so whoever among you meets him, let him recite to him the opening verses of Surat al-Kahf. He will emerge from a gap between Syria and Iraq, wreaking havoc right and left. O servants of God! Be steadfast. We said: O Messenger of God, how long will he remain on the earth? He said: Forty days, a day like a year, a day like a month, a day like a week, and the rest of his days are like your days. We said: O Messenger of God, is that day which is like a year sufficient for us to pray one day? He said: No, estimate its time. We said: O Messenger of God, how quickly will he walk on the earth? He said: Like rain that the wind has driven back, so he comes to the people and calls them and they believe in him and respond to him, so he orders the sky to rain on the earth, so it grows and their livestock return to them with the longest peaks, the most abundant udders and the most extended flanks, then he comes to the people and calls them and they respond to his words, he said: So he turns away from them, and they become destitute and have nothing of their wealth in their hands, and he passes by the ruins and says to it: Come forth like your light, and its treasures follow him like swarms of bees, then he calls a man full of youth and strikes him with the sword and cuts him into two pieces, straight to the target, then he calls him and he accepts and his face lights up and he laughs, and while he is like that, God sends the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and he descends at the white minaret east of the gate of Damascus, between two marshes, placing his hands on the wings of two angels, If he lowers his head, it rains, and if he raises it, it rains like pearls. It is not permissible for an unbeliever to find the scent of his breath except that he dies, and his breath ends where his glance ends, so he pursues him until he reaches him at the gate of Ludd and kills him. Then Jesus will come to a people whom God has protected from him, so he wipes their faces and tells them of their degrees in Paradise. While he is like that, God reveals to Jesus: I have brought forth servants of mine whom no one can fight, so protect my servants to the mountain. God will send Gog and Magog, and they will swarm from every side. The first of them will pass by Lake Tiberias and drink what is in it, and the last of them will pass by and say: This was once the case. The Prophet of God and his companions will be besieged, until the head of a bull for one of them is better than a hundred dinars for one of you today. The Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will desire it, so God will send upon them the gnats in their necks, so they will become like the death of a single soul. Then the Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will descend to the earth and they will not find a place on the earth the size of a hand span except that it will be covered with dust. Their stench and stench will fill it, so the Prophet of God, Jesus, and his companions will ask God, so God will send birds with the necks of camels, which will carry them and throw them wherever He wills. Then God will send rain that will not be missed by a house of mud or hair, and it will wash the earth until it leaves it like a stump. Then it will be said to the earth: Grow your fruit and restore your blessings. On that day, a group will eat from the pomegranate and seek shade under its shell. The Messengers will be blessed until a she-camel will suffice a group of people, a she-camel will suffice a tribe of people, and a she-camel will suffice a thigh of people. While they are like this, God will send a pleasant wind that will take them under their armpits and seize the soul of every believer and every Muslim. The worst of people will remain, fighting like donkeys, and the Hour will come upon them. And with this chain of transmission, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Ali bin Hajar Al-Saadi told us, Abdullah bin Abdul-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jaber and Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jaber, with this chain of transmission, similar to what we mentioned, and he added after his saying: - There was once water here -: “Then they will march until they reach Jabal Al-Khamar, which is the mountain of Jerusalem, and they will say: We have killed those on earth, so come, let us kill those in the sky. So they will shoot their arrows into the sky, and God will return their arrows to them stained with blood.” Wahb said: They used to come to the sea, drink its water, eat its animals, then eat wood and trees, and whoever they captured from the people, and they were not able to come to Mecca, Medina, or Jerusalem. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmad told us, my father told us, Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Utbah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: They will perform Hajj to the House and Umrah after the emergence of Gog and Magog. In the story: Dhul-Qarnayn entered the darkness, and when he returned, he died in the month of Zur. Some of them mentioned that he was over thirty years old.
18:99: 99 - The Almighty said: And We will leave some of them that Day surging against others. It was said: This is at the dam. He says: We will leave Gog and Magog, meaning: they will enter into each other like waves of water, and they will mix with each other because of their great number. It was said: This will be when the Hour comes, when people will enter into each other, and their humans will mix with their jinn, confused. And the Trumpet will be blown, because the emergence of Gog and Magog is one of the signs of the approaching Hour. Then We will gather them together, in one place.
18:100: 100 - And We will present, We will make clear, Hell that Day to the disbelievers, presented, so that they may see it with their own eyes.
18:101: 101 - “Those whose eyes were covered,” meaning: a membrane, and covering is what covers something and conceals it, from My remembrance, meaning: from faith and the Qur’an, and from guidance and clarification, and it was said: from seeing the evidence. And they were unable to hear, meaning: to hear acceptance and faith, because of the overwhelming misery that overwhelmed them. It was said: They do not understand. It was also said: They were unable to, meaning: They were unable to hear from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what he recited to them due to the intensity of their enmity towards him, like a man saying: I cannot hear anything from so-and-so, due to his enmity.
18:102: 102 - The Almighty’s saying: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as allies besides Me? Lords, meaning by servants: Jesus and the angels. No, rather they are enemies to them and disavow them. Ibn Abbas said: He means the devils who obeyed them instead of God. Muqatil said: The idols were called servants, as He said: Indeed, those you invoke besides God are servants like you (al-A’raf 7:194). The answer to this question is omitted. Ibn Abbas said: He means that I get angry for myself. He says: Do those who disbelieve think that they can take other than Me as allies, while I do not get angry for myself and I do not punish them? It was said: Do they think that it would benefit them to take My servants as allies other than Me? Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a lodging, meaning: a home. Ibn Abbas said: It is their abode. It was said: A lodging is what is prepared for a guest, meaning: It is prepared for them with Us as a lodging is for a guest.
18:103: 103 - The Almighty said: “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?” Meaning: those who exhausted themselves in work in which they hoped to gain merit and reward, but attained destruction and ruin, like someone who buys a commodity in which he hopes to make a profit, but loses and his efforts fail. They differed about them: Ibn Abbas and Saad bin Abi Waqqas said: They are the Jews and Christians. It was said: They are the monks.
18:104: 104 - Those who confined themselves to monasteries. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: They are the people of Harura. Their efforts are in vain, their work and effort are in vain, in the life of this world while they think that they are doing well in work, that is, in action.
18:105: 105 - “Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in the meeting with Him. So their deeds have become worthless,” i.e., nullified, so We will not assign to them any weight on the Day of Resurrection, i.e., We will not give them any importance or value. The Arabs say: So-and-so has no weight with me, i.e., value, I have debased him. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Ahmad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail, Muhammad bin Abdullah told us, Saeed bin Maryam told us, Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, on the authority of Al-Araj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: A great, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection and he will not weigh as much as a mosquito’s wing in God’s sight. He said: Read, if you wish, So We will not assign to them any weight on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said: People will come on the Day of Resurrection with deeds that are as great to them as the mountains of Tihamah, but when they are weighed they will weigh nothing. This is what God Almighty says: And We will not assign to them any weight on the Day of Resurrection.
18:106: 106 - That which I mentioned of the failure of their deeds and the lowliness of their status, then he began and said: Their recompense is Hell because they disbelieved and took My signs, meaning the Qur'an, and My messengers in ridicule, meaning mockery and derision.
18:107: 107 - The Almighty said: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise. We narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If you ask God, ask Him for Paradise, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it flow the rivers of Paradise. Kaab said: There is no paradise in Paradise higher than the Paradise of Firdaws, in which there are those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. Qatada said: Al-Firdaws: The highest, middle, best and most elevated part of Paradise. Kaab said: Al-Firdaws is the garden in which there are grapes. Mujahed said: It is the garden in Roman. Akrima said: It is Paradise in the Ethiopian language. Al-Zajjaj said: It is in Roman, transferred to the Arabic wording. Al-Dahhak said: It is the paradise with intertwined trees. It was said: It is the beautiful garden. It was said: It is the one that grows various types of plants, and its plural is farādis. “A place of rest.” It was said that it means a home. It was also said that it is what is prepared for the one who is staying, meaning that the fruits of the Gardens of Paradise and its delights were for them as a place of rest. The meaning of were for them is: in God’s knowledge before they were created.
18:108: 108 - They will abide therein, not desiring, not seeking, any change from it, meaning a shift to another. Ibn Abbas said: They do not want to move from it, just as a man moves from one house to another if it does not suit him.
18:109: 109 - The Almighty said: “Say: ‘If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord,’” Ibn Abbas said: The Jews said, “O Muhammad, you claim that we have been given wisdom, and in your book, ‘And whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good.’ Then you say: ‘And you have been given only a little knowledge?’ So God revealed this verse.” It was said: When the verse was revealed: And you have been given only a little knowledge, the Jews said: We have been given the Torah, which contains knowledge of everything. So God Almighty revealed: “Say: If the sea were ink,” ink was called to provide the writer, and its origin is from increase and the coming of one thing after another. Mujahid said: If the sea were ink for the pen and the pen were writing, the sea would be exhausted meaning its water before it is exhausted. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read yanfad with a ya’ because the verb came before it, and the rest read it with a ta’ the words of my Lord, meaning His knowledge and wisdom. And if We brought the like of it as a supplement, meaning: If the creation wrote and the sea supplied them, the sea would be exhausted and the words of my Lord would not be exhausted, even if We brought the like of the water of the sea in its abundance as a supplement or more. [And supply is in the accusative case as a specification] similar to the statement of God Almighty: And if all the trees on the earth were pens and the sea were replenished thereafter by seven more seas, the Words of God would not be exhausted (Luqman 31:27).
18:110: 110 - The Almighty said: "Say, 'I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is one God.'" Ibn Abbas said: God taught His Messenger humility so that he would not be arrogant towards His creation, so He commanded him to acknowledge and say: I am a human being like you, except that I was singled out for revelation and God honored me with it. It has been revealed to me that your God is one God, with no partner. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, meaning fears the fate of Him. It was said: He hopes to see his Lord, so hope can mean both fear and hope. The poet said: Not everything you hope for of good will come true, nor everything you hope for of evil will come true. He combined the two meanings. So let him do righteous work and not associate anyone with the worship of his Lord, meaning: let him not show off with his work. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Naim told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Salamah, he is Ibn Kuhail, he said: I heard Jundub say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever listens, God will listen to him, and whoever shows off, God will show off with him. We narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: What I fear most for you is minor polytheism. They said: O Messenger of God, what is minor polytheism? He said: Hypocrisy. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad bin Musa Al-Sayrafi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ya’qub Al-Asamm told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam told us, my father told us, Shu’aib told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haad, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: I am the most independent of partners from association. Whoever does an action in which he associates someone else with Me, then I am innocent of it. It belongs to the one who did it.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Hafs bin Omar told us, Hammam told us on the authority of Qatada, Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d Al-Ghatafani told us, on the authority of Ma’dan bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, who narrated it on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Antichrist. And Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani informed us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani informed us, Hamid Ibn Zanjawayh informed us, Abu Al-Aswad informed us, Ibn Lahi’ah informed us, on the authority of Ziyad, on the authority of Sahl - he is Ibn Mu’adh - on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever recites the beginning and end of Surat Al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his feet to his head, and whoever recites it all, it will be a light for him from the earth to the heavens.
19:1: 1 - Meccan, and it has ninety-eight verses. The Almighty said: Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad. Abu Amr read it with a kasra on the ha’ and a fatha on the ya’, and the opposite is Ibn Amir and Hamza, and with both of them kasra: Al-Kisa’i and Abu Bakr, and the rest with both of them fatha. The letter dal appears with the letter dhal in sad dhikr by Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, Asim [and Ya’qub], and the rest with assimilation. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It is one of the names of God Almighty. Qatada said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an. It was said: It is the name of the Surah. It was also said: It is an oath by which God swore. It is narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement Kaaf, Ha, Ain, Sad that he said: The kaf is from Kareem and Kabeer, the ha is from Had, the ya is from Raheem, the ain is from Aleem and Azim, and the sad is from Sadiq. Al-Kalbi said: Its meaning is: Sufficient for His creation, a guide for His servants, His hand is above their hands, Knowing of His creation, Truthful in His promise.
19:2: 2- Remembrance, raising the pronoun, meaning: What we recite to you is a remembrance of the mercy of your Lord, [and there is an advancement and delay in it] meaning: He mentioned to you, His servant Zachariah, with His mercy.
19:3: 3 - When he called, he called, his Lord, in his prayer niche, a secret call, he called secretly from his people in the dead of night.
19:4: 4 - He said, 'My Lord, indeed I am feeble', weak and thin, my bones have become feeble", from old age. Qatada said: He complained of falling out molars, "and my head was ablaze", meaning: the hair of his head had turned white, "grey, disheveled, and I have never been, in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy", he says: You have accustomed me to answering in the past and You have not disappointed me. It was said: Its meaning is that when you called me to faith, I believed and I did not suffer from abandoning faith.
19:6: 6 - He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read: with the tha' in both of them in the accusative case, as an answer to the supplication, and the others read it in the nominative case as a state and description, meaning: a guardian and an inheritor. They differed about this inheritance. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is that he will inherit my money and inherit from the family of Jacob the prophecy and happiness. It was said: He meant the inheritance of prophecy and knowledge. It was said: He meant the inheritance of the rabbis, because Zachariah was at the head of the rabbis. Al-Zajjaj said: It is better to carry it on an inheritance other than money because it is unlikely that Zachariah, who was a prophet, would fear that his cousins would inherit his money. Meaning: He feared that his cousins would neglect the religion of God and change its rulings based on what he had witnessed from the Children of Israel in changing the religion and killing the prophets. So he asked his Lord for a righteous guardian who would trust him with his nation and inherit his prophethood and knowledge so that the religion would not be lost. This is the meaning of what Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. And make him, O Lord, pleasing, meaning righteous, pious, and pleasing.
19:7: 7 - The Almighty’s saying: O Zachariah, indeed We give you good tidings, and it is abbreviated, meaning: So God answered his prayer, and said: O Zachariah, indeed We give you good tidings, of a boy, a male child, “whose name is John. We have not given him a namesake before,” Qatada and Al-Kalbi said: No one before him was named John. Saeed bin Jubair and Ata’ said: We did not make a likeness or example for Him, as God Almighty said: Do you know of any similar to Him? meaning an example. Meaning: He had no equal, because he never disobeyed or intended to disobey. It was said: He had no equal in the matter of women, because he was a master and chaste. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: That is, barren women have not given birth to a child like him. It was said: God did not intend for Yahya to have all the virtues combined, but rather He intended some of them, because Al-Khalil and Al-Kalim were before him, and they were better than him.
19:8: 8 - He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a boy while my wife is barren?' That is, my wife is barren. And I have reached extreme old age, that is, dryness. Qatada said: He means emaciation of bones. It is said: an old man becomes old, ya'tu 'aytu 'aytu and 'asyan: if he reaches the end of his age and grows old, and an old man becomes 'aytu 'as: if he reaches a state of dryness and dehydration. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: ‘Atiya, Bakiya, Saliya, and Jathiya with the first letters broken, and the rest with the first letters raised, and they are two dialects.
19:9: 9 - He said, ‘Thus said your Lord, it is easy for Me.’ “And I created you.” Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read We created you with a nun and an alif for emphasis, before, meaning before Yahya, and you were nothing.
19:10: 10 - He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign,’ indicating my wife’s pregnancy.
