He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, sound and sound, without any illness or muteness.’ Mujahed said: That is, do not let illness prevent you from speaking. It was said: Three consecutive nights, and the first is more correct. In the story: He was not able to speak to people, but when he wanted to mention God Almighty, his tongue would loosen.
19:11: 11 - The Almighty said: So he came out to his people from the sanctuary, and the people were waiting behind the sanctuary for him to open the door for them so they could enter and pray, when Zachariah came out to them with a changed color, so they denied him and said: What is the matter with you, O Zachariah? So he inspired them, so he gestured to them. Mujahid said: He wrote for them on the earth, to glorify, meaning: pray to God, morning, in the morning, and evening, and its meaning is that he would come out to his people in the morning and evening and command them to pray, and when it was time for his wife to become pregnant, he was prevented from speaking until he came out to them and commanded them to pray by gesture.
19:12: 12 - The Almighty’s saying: O Yahya, it was said: There is an omission in it, the meaning of which is: And We gave him Yahya and said to him: O Yahya, Take the Book, meaning the Torah, with strength, seriously, and We gave him wisdom, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Prophethood, as a boy, and he was three years old. It was said: He meant by wisdom understanding the book, so he read the Torah when he was young. On the authority of some of the predecessors: Whoever recites the Qur’an before reaching puberty is among those who were given wisdom as a child.
19:13: 13 - "And compassion from Us", mercy from Us. Al-Hutay'ah said to Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: Have mercy on that king, for every situation has its own words. That is: have mercy. And zakat, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Zakat means obedience and sincerity. Qatada, may God be pleased with him, said: It is righteous work, and this is what Al-Dahhak said. The meaning of the verse: And We gave him mercy from Us and compassion for the servants, so that he would call them to obey their Lord and do righteous work in sincerity. Al-Kalbi said: It means charity that God gave to his parents. He was pious, a Muslim, sincere and obedient. His piety was such that he did not commit any sin or even think about it.
19:14: 14 - And dutiful to his parents, meaning dutiful, kind to them, and good to them. And he was not a tyrant or disobedient, and the tyrant is the arrogant, and it was said: the tyrant is the one who strikes and kills in anger, and the disobedient is the rebellious.
19:15: 15 - "And peace be upon him", meaning: safety for him, the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: The most lonely thing a person can be in these situations: the day he is born, when he emerges from what he was in, the day he dies, when he sees people he has never seen, and the day he is raised, when he sees himself in a gathering place the likes of which he has never seen. So Yahya was singled out for safety in these situations.
19:16: 16 - The Almighty said: And mention in the Book, in the Qur’an, Mary, when she withdrew, she moved away and secluded herself, from her family, from her people, to a place in the east, meaning: a place in the house facing the east, and it was a very cold winter day, so she sat in the east, combing her hair. It was said: She had become pure from menstruation, so she went to wash herself. Al-Hassan said: Hence, the Christians took the East as their qiblah.
19:17: 17 - So I took, so I struck, a veil from them, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: a screen. It was said: I sat behind the wall. Muqatil said: Behind the mountain. And Ikrimah said: Maryam used to be in the mosque, and when she menstruated, she would go to her aunt’s house, until she became pure and returned to the mosque. While she was washing herself from menstruation and had stripped herself, Gabriel appeared to her in the form of a young man with no beard, a radiant face, curly hair, and a well-proportioned build. This is what he said: Then We sent to her Our Spirit, meaning Gabriel, peace be upon him, and he appeared to her as a well-proportioned man. It was said that what was meant by the spirit was Jesus, peace be upon him, who came in the form of a man and she became pregnant with him. The first is more correct. When Mary saw Gabriel heading toward her, she called out to him from afar, so
19:18: 18 - She said, 'Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you should be fearing God, believing and obedient.' If it is said: Refuge is only sought from the wicked, so how did she say: I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are pious? It was said: This is like the saying of someone: If you are a believer, then do not wrong me. That is: Your faith should prevent injustice, and so it is here. Meaning: Your piety should be a deterrent against immorality.
19:19: 19- "He said", to her Gabriel: "I am only a messenger from your Lord to give you", Nafi and the people of Basra read: "to give you with the letter ya", meaning: so that your Lord may give you, and the others read: "to give you, the action is attributed to the Messenger, even though the gift was from God Almighty, because He sent him. A pure boy, a righteous son, pure from sins.
19:20: 20 - She said, Maryam 19:How, from where, can I have a boy while no man has touched me, no husband has come near me, nor am I unchaste, wicked? She means that the child would be from marriage or fornication, and there was neither of those here.
19:21: 21 - He said, Gabriel: Likewise, it was said: its meaning is as you said, O Mary, but, your Lord said, and it was said: thus said your Lord, it is easy for Me, meaning: creating a child without a father, and that We may make him a sign, a mark, for mankind, and an indication of Our power, and a mercy from Us, and a blessing for those who follow him in His religion, and it was, "a matter decreed, ruled and decided upon, not to be rejected or changed.
19:22: 22 - The Almighty said: So she carried him. It was said: Gabriel lifted her armor and blew into its pocket, so she carried him when she put it on. It was said: He reached into the pocket of her armor with his finger and then blew into the pocket. It was said: He blew into the sleeve of her shirt. It was also said: Into her mouth. It was said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, blew from afar, and the wind reached her, and she became pregnant with Jesus immediately. She withdrew with him, that is, she moved away with the pregnancy and went into seclusion, in a remote place, far from her people. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The farthest part of the valley, which is the valley of Bethlehem, was to escape from her people who would taunt her for giving birth without a husband. They differed about the duration of her pregnancy and the time of her delivery. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The pregnancy and birth occurred at one hour. It was said: Her pregnancy lasted nine months, like that of all other women. It was said: The duration of her dream was eight months, and that was another sign because no child born for eight months lives, and Jesus was born for this period and lived. It was said: She gave birth after six months. Muqatil bin Sulayman said: Mary carried him in an hour, and Sur in an hour, and she gave birth to him in an hour when the sun had passed its zenith on that day, and she was ten years old, and she had menstruated twice before she became pregnant with Jesus.
19:23: 23 - He brought her to labor, meaning he forced her and brought her, to the trunk of the palm tree, which is the pain of childbirth, to the trunk of the palm tree. It was a dry palm tree in the desert, in the harsh winter, and it had no fronds. It was said: She took refuge in it to lean on it and cling to it during the pain of childbirth, She said, ‘Oh, I wish I had died before this,’ she wished for death out of shame before people and fear of scandal, and I was forgotten, Hamza and Hafs read forgotten with the nun open, [and the rest with the nun closed, and they are two languages, like: al-watar and al-watar, and al-jisr and al-jisr, which is the forgotten thing, and forgotten in the language: everything that was thrown away and forgotten and not mentioned due to its insignificance. Forgotten, meaning: abandoned. Qatada said: something that is not known or remembered. Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, and Mujahid said: a discarded corpse. It was also said: it means I was not created.
19:24: 24 - He called to her from beneath her, Abu Ja`far, Nafi`, Hamza, Al-Kisa`i, and Hafs read: from beneath her with a kasra on the meem and the ta`, meaning Gabriel, peace be upon him, and Mary was on a hill, and Gabriel was behind the hill beneath her, so he called to her. Others read it with the opening of the meem and the taa, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, also meant that he called her from the foot of the mountain. It was said: It is Jesus, when he came out of his mother’s womb, he called to her: Do not be sad, and this is the saying of Mujahid and Al-Hasan. The first is the statement of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Al-Suddi, Qatada, Al-Dahhak, and a group: that the caller was Gabriel, when he heard her words and knew her grief, he called to her, Do not be sad. Your Lord has placed a stream beneath you. A stream is a small river. It was said: Under you, meaning God made it under your command. If you command it to run, it runs, and if you command it to stop, it stops. He said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Gabriel, peace be upon him - and it is said: Jesus, peace be upon him - struck the ground with his foot, and a spring of fresh water appeared and flowed. It was said: There was a dry river in which God Almighty made water flow, and the dry palm tree was revived, so it grew leaves, bore fruit, and was moist. Al-Hasan said: Underneath you is a secret meaning: Jesus, and by God he was a secret servant, meaning: high.
19:25: 25 - "And shake towards you", meaning it was said to Maryam 19:Move "the trunk of the palm tree", the Arabs say: shake it and shake it, just as one says: cut his head and cut his head, and extend the rope and extend it, "it falls upon you", the well-known reading with the opening of the ta and the qaf and the emphasis on the seen, meaning: it falls, so one of the two ta's was assimilated into the seen, meaning: the palm tree falls upon you with dates, and Hamza lightened the seen and deleted the ta' that others had assimilated. Hafs read it with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the qaf, light on the weight of tafa’ala. And tasaqata means dropped, and the feminization is for the sake of the palm tree. And Jacob read: Yasaqat with a shaddah on the Ya’, referring back to the trunk. Fresh dates, harvested. It was said: The harvest is that which has reached its peak and the time for harvesting has come. Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim said: I do not think there is anything better for a woman in childbirth than fresh dates, nor anything better for a sick person than honey.
19:26: 26 - The Almighty said: So eat and drink, meaning: O Mary, eat from the dates and drink from the river water, and be content, meaning: be at peace. It was also said: May your eyes be content with your son Jesus. It is said: May God make your eyes content, meaning: May your heart encounter what pleases you, so may your eyes be content from looking at anyone other than Him. It was also said: May God make his eyes content, meaning may He make them sleep. It is said: Qarra yaqrur if he is still. It was said: If the eye cries out of joy, the tears are cold, and if it cries out of sadness, the tears are hot. From this it was said: May God cool his eye and warm his eye. If you see anyone among mankind, meaning: you see. The letter nun of emphasis was added to it from sadness, so the tears are hot. From this it was said: May God cool his eyes and may God warm his eyes. If you see anyone among mankind, meaning: you see. The letter nun of emphasis was added to it, so the letter ya was broken because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Meaning: If you see anyone among mankind asking you about your child, Say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful to fast,’ meaning: silence. This is how Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, used to recite it. Fasting in the language means abstaining from food, drink and speech. Al-Suddi said: There was among the Children of Israel someone who wanted to strive hard, so he would fast from speaking, just as he would fast from food, and he would not speak until evening. It was said: God Almighty commanded her to say this as a sign. It was said: He ordered her to say this much orally, then refrain from speaking after that. I will not speak to any human today, it is said: She used to speak to the angels, but not to humans.
19:27: 27 - So she brought him to her people, carrying him. It was said that she gave birth, then immediately carried him to her people. Al-Kalbi said: Joseph the carpenter carried Mary and her son Jesus [peace be upon them] to a cave, and she remained there for forty days until she was purified from her childbirth, then Mary, peace be upon her, carried him to her people. Jesus, peace be upon him, spoke to her on the way and said: O mother, be of good tidings, for I am the servant of God and His Messiah. When she entered upon her family with the boy, they wept and were sad, and they were a righteous household. “They said: O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented,” something great and strange. Abu Ubaidah said: Every extraordinary matter, whether a wonder or a deed, is unprecedented. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about Omar: I have never seen a genius who does his work. That is, does his work. Y
19:28: 28 - O sister of Aaron, meaning O one who resembles Aaron. Qatada and others said: Aaron was a righteous and devout man among the Children of Israel. It was narrated that forty thousand people from the Children of Israel followed his funeral procession on the day he died, all of them named Aaron apart from the rest of the people. [They likened her to him] in the sense that we thought you were like him in righteousness. It does not mean that they were brothers in lineage, as God Almighty said: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils (al-Isra’ 17:27), meaning: their likenesses. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Alqamah bin Wa’il, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah, who said: “When I came to Najran, they asked me and said: ‘You recite “O sister of Aaron,” and Moses came before Jesus by such and such!’ So when I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I asked him about that and he said: ‘They used to name their prophets and the righteous people before them.’” Al-Kalbi said: Aaron was Mary’s brother from her father, and he was the most virtuous man among the Children of Israel. Al-Suddi said: They meant Aaron, the brother of Moses, because she was from his lineage, just as a Tamimi is called: O brother of Tamim. It was said: Aaron was a very corrupt man among the Children of Israel, so they likened her to him. Your father, Imran, was not a bad man, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: an adulterer, “nor was your mother,” Hannah, a prostitute, meaning an adulteress. So where did you get this child from?
19:29: 29 - Then Mary pointed to him, meaning to Jesus, peace be upon him, to speak to him. Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: Since she had no argument, she pointed to him so that his words would be an argument for her. In the story: When she pointed to him, the people became angry and said: With what you did, are you mocking us? They said, How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? That is, the one who is in the cradle, is her lap. It was said: It is the cradle itself and kana means: He. Abu Ubaidah said kana is a conjunction, meaning: How do we speak to a baby in the cradle? kana may also come as a filler in speech that has no meaning, like His saying: Was I anything but a human messenger? (al-Isra’ 17:93), meaning: Am I? Al-Suddi said: When Jesus heard their words, he stopped breastfeeding and turned to them. It was said: When she pointed to him, he left his chest and leaned on his left, and turned to them and began to point with his right:
19:30: 30 - He said, 'I am the servant of God.' Wahb said: Zachariah came to her when she was debating with the Jews, and he said to Jesus: Speak with your proof if you were commanded to do so. Then Jesus, peace be upon him, said, while he was forty days old - and Muqatil said: Rather, it was the day he was born. He acknowledged his servitude to God Almighty the first time he spoke, lest he be taken as a god. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet. It was said that its meaning is that He will give me the Book and make me a prophet. It was said: This is a report of what was written for him in the Preserved Tablet, just as it was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When were you a prophet? He said: I was a prophet while Adam was between the spirit and the body. Most people said that he was given the Gospel when he was a young child, and he had the intelligence of a man. On the authority of Al-Hassan: He said: He was inspired with the Torah while he was in his mother’s womb.
19:31: 31 - And made me blessed wherever I may be, meaning beneficial wherever I go. Mujahid said: A teacher of goodness. Ata' said: I call to God and to His Oneness and worship. It was said: Blessed to whoever follows me. And He enjoined upon me prayer and zakat, meaning: He ordered me to do them. If it is said: Jesus did not have money, so how could he be commanded to pay zakat? It was said: It means by zakat if I had money. It was also said: By increasing good deeds. As long as I live.
19:32: 32 - And dutiful to my mother meaning, He made me dutiful to my mother, and did not make me a wretched tyrant meaning, disobedient to his Lord. It was said: the wretched is the one who sins and does not repent.
19:33: 33 - "And peace be upon me the day I was born", meaning: safety at birth from the stabs of Satan. And the day I die, meaning upon death from polytheism, and the day I am raised alive, from the terrors. And when Jesus spoke to them with this, they acted as if Mary was innocent, then Jesus, peace be upon him, was silent, and did not speak after that until he reached the period in which children speak.
19:34: 34 - That is Jesus, son of Mary, [Al-Zajjaj said: That is, the one who said, I am the servant of God, Jesus, son of Mary,] The word of truth, Ibn Amir, Asim, and Yaqub read: The word of truth with the accusative of the lam, which is an accusative of the source, meaning: he said the word of truth, about which they are in doubt, meaning: they differ, so one says: He is the son of God, and another says: He is God, and another says: He is a lying magician. Others read it with the lam raised, meaning: it is the saying of the truth, that is, this speech is the saying of the truth. He added the saying to the truth, as he said: the truth of certainty and the promise of truth. It was said: It is an attribute of Jesus, son of Mary, meaning that Jesus, son of Mary, is the Word of God and the truth is God, about whom they are in doubt, they doubt, differ, and say other than the truth. Then he denied having a son, saying:
19:35: 35 - It is not for God to take a son, meaning it is not part of His nature to take a son. It was said: The lam is transferred, meaning it is not for God to take a son. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a matter, if He wants to bring about a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.
19:36: 36 - And God is my Lord and your Lord, the people of Hijaz and Abu Amr read: That God with the opening of the alif, referring back to his saying: And He enjoined upon me prayer and zakat and that God is my Lord and your Lord, and the people of Ash-Sham and Kufa and Jacob read with the breaking of the alif as a new beginning So worship Him, this is a straight path.
19:37: 37 - "Then the parties differed among themselves," meaning: the Christians. They were called parties because they formed three groups regarding the matter of Jesus: the Nestorians, the Melkites, and the Jacobites. "So woe to those who disbelieved from the scene of a tremendous Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection.
19:38: 38 - I hear and see them, meaning how much I hear and see them on the Day of Resurrection when hearing and sight will be of no use to them! He informed us that they will hear and see in the Hereafter what they did not hear and see in this world. Al-Kalbi said: No one on the Day of Resurrection will hear or see more than them when God Almighty says to Jesus: Did you say to the people? Maryam 116. On the Day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in manifest error. That is, in clear error.
19:39: 39 - The Almighty said: And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter is decided. The reckoning is completed and the people of Paradise are admitted to Paradise, and the people of Hell are admitted to Hell, and death is slaughtered. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Amr bin Hafs bin Ghayath told us, my father told us, Al-A’mash told us, Abu Salih told us, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Death will be brought in the form of a white ram, and a caller will call out: ‘O people of Paradise!’ They will look out and look, and he will say: ‘Do you recognize this?’ They will say: ‘Yes, this is death,’ and all of them have seen it. Then he will call out: ‘O people of Hell!’ They will look out and look, and he will say: ‘Do you recognize this?’ They will say: ‘Yes, this is death,’ and all of them have seen it. Then he will slaughter it, and he will say: ‘O people of Paradise, eternity and no death, and O people of Hell, eternity and no death.’ Then he recited: ‘And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter is decided, while they are in heedlessness, and they will not believe.’” Abu Isa narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Mani’, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Ismail, on the authority of Al-A’mash with this chain of transmission, and he added: “If God Almighty had not decreed life and permanence for the people of Paradise, they would have died of joy, and if God Almighty had not decreed life and permanence for the people of Hell, they would have died of grief.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muadh bin Asad told us, Abdullah told us, Omar bin Muhammad bin Zaid told us on the authority of his father that he told him on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the people of Paradise go to Paradise and the people of Hell go to Hell, death will be brought and placed between Paradise and Hell. Then it will be slaughtered and a caller will call out: O people of Paradise, no death, and O people of Hell, no death. So the people of Paradise will increase in joy to their joy, and the people of Hell will increase in sorrow to their sorrow.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, Abu Al-Zinad told us, on the authority of Al-Araj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “No one will enter Paradise except that he will be shown his place in Hell if he had done wrong, so that his gratitude will increase. And no one will enter Hell except that he will be shown his place in Paradise if he had done good, so that it will be a cause of regret for him.” Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi told us, Abu al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Yahya ibn Ubayd God told us: I heard my father say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one dies except that he regrets it. They said: What is his regret, O Messenger of God? He said: If he was a good person, he regrets that he did not do more, and if he was a bad person, he regrets that he did not stop. The Almighty said: And they are in heedlessness, meaning: of what will happen to them in the Hereafter, and they do not believe, they do not believe.
19:40: 40 - The Almighty said: Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it. That is, We will kill the inhabitants of the earth and destroy them all, and the Lord alone will remain to inherit them. And to Us they will return. So We will reward them for their deeds.
19:41: 41 - The Almighty said: "And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet." The truthful: the one who is very truthful and upholds it. It was said: whoever is truthful to God in His Oneness, and believes in His prophets and messengers, and believes in the resurrection, and carries out the commands and acts upon them, then he is the truthful. And the prophet: the one who is high in rank by being sent by God Almighty.
19:42: 42 - When he said, Ibrahim, to his father, Azar, while he was worshipping idols, O my father, why do you worship that which hears not, a sound, nor sees, anything, nor avails you, that is, it is not sufficient for you, at all.
19:43: 43 - O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge - of God and knowledge - that which has not come to you, so follow me - in my religion - and I will guide you to a straight path - a straight path.
19:44: 44 - O my father, do not worship Satan, do not obey him in what he makes attractive to you of disbelief and polytheism. Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful, disobedient. was means the state, meaning: he is like that.
19:45: 45 - O my father, indeed I fear, that is, I know, that a punishment from the Most Merciful will afflict you, that is, if you persist in disbelief, and you will be a friend of Satan, a companion in the Fire.
19:46: 46 - He said, his father answered him: Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? If you do not stop, if you do not keep quiet and stop insulting our gods and cursing them, I will stone you, Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and Ad-Dahhak said: I will insult you and distance you from me with ugly words. Ibn Abbas said: I will hit you. Ikrimah said: I will kill you with stones. And leave me alone for a long time. Al-Kalbi said: Avoid me for a long time. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: For a while. Saeed bin Jubair said: A long time. The root of hain is staying, and from it is said: I stayed for a while. “Al-Mulwan” means night and day. Qatada and Ata’ said: Safe. Ibn Abbas said: Stay away from me safe and sound so that no reproach will befall you from me. It is said: So-and-so is satisfied with such-and-such a matter: if he is sufficient.
19:48: 48 - And I will withdraw from you and from what you call upon besides God, meaning: I will withdraw from what you worship besides God. Muqatil said: His withdrawal from them was that he left them from Kutha and migrated from there to the Holy Land, And I will call upon my Lord, meaning: I will worship my Lord, Perhaps I will not be wretched in calling upon my Lord, meaning: I will not be wretched in calling upon Him and worshipping Him, as you are wretched in worshipping idols. It was said: May he answer me when I call upon him and not disappoint me.
19:49: 49 - So when he had left them and what they worshipped besides God, and he went as an emigrant, We gave him after the emigration Isaac and Jacob. We relieved his loneliness [from being separated from them], and We comforted his eyes, with children who were honored by God Almighty, and each of them We made a prophet, meaning: Isaac and Jacob.
19:50: 50 - And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy. Al-Kalbi said: Money and children, and this is the opinion of the majority. They said: What was spread out for them in this world of abundant provision. It was also said: The Book and prophethood. And We made for them a high reputation for truth, meaning good and lofty praise among all people of religions, so they all support them and praise them.
19:51: 51 - The Almighty said: “And mention in the Book Moses. Indeed, he was sincere,” without doubting, he sincerely worshipped and obeyed God Almighty. The people of Kufa read selected with a fat-ha on the lam, meaning: chosen, chosen by God Almighty. It was said: God purified him from filth. And he was a messenger and a prophet.
19:52: 52 - And We called to him from the right side of the Mount, meaning: the right of Moses, and Mount is a mountain between Egypt and Madyan. It is said that his name was Al-Zubayr and that was when he came from Madyan and saw the fire, he was called, O Moses, indeed I am God, Lord of the worlds (al-Qasas 28:30). And We brought him near in private, meaning, in private conversation. So, the one who is private is the one who is confided in, just as one says: a companion and a friend. Ibn Abbas said: Its meaning is: He brought him close and spoke to him. The meaning of bringing him close is making him hear his speech. It was said: He raised it above the curtains until he heard the creaking of the pen.
19:53: 53 - And We bestowed upon him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, a prophet, when Moses called out and said: And appoint for me a helper from my family, Aaron, my brother (Ta-Ha 20:29/30), so God answered his call and sent Aaron, and that is why He named him a gift to Him.
19:54: 54 - The Almighty said: And mention in the Book Ishmael, and he is Ishmael, son of Abraham, the grandfather of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Indeed, he was true to his promise, Mujahid said: He did not promise anything without fulfilling it. Muqatil said: He promised a man that he would stay in his place until the man returned to him, so Ismail stayed in his place for three days until the man returned to him. Al-Kalbi said: He waited for him until a year had passed. And he was a messenger, to the people of Jurhum, a prophet, informing on behalf of God Almighty.
19:55: 55 - And he used to enjoin his family meaning: his people. It was also said: his family and all of his nation, to perform the prayer and give the zakat, Ibn Abbas said: He means what God Almighty made obligatory upon them, which is the true faith that was made obligatory upon us, and he was pleasing to his Lord, fulfilling His obedience. It was said: God Almighty was pleased with him for his prophethood and message.
19:56: 56 - The Almighty said: And mention in the Book, Idris, who was the grandfather of Noah's father, and his name was Enoch. He was called Idris because of his frequent study of books. He was a tailor and the first to write with a pen, and the first to sew clothes, and wear sewn clothing, and before him they wore skins, and the first to take up arms, and fight the infidels, and the first to study astrology and mathematics, Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
19:57: 57 - And We raised him to a high station. It was said: It means Paradise. And it was said: It is the elevation by the high rank in this world. It was said: He was raised to the fourth heaven. Anas bin Malik narrated on the authority of Malik bin Sa’sa’ah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he saw Idris in the fourth heaven on the night of the Ascension. The reason for Idris being raised [to heaven], according to what Kaab and others said, was that he walked one day on an errand and was struck by the sun’s glare. He said: O Lord, I walked one day, so what about someone who carries it for a journey of five hundred years in one day? O God, lighten its weight and heat for him. When the king woke up in the morning, he found the lightness and heat of the sun to be something he did not know. He said: O Lord, what have you decreed for him? He said: My servant Idris asked me to lighten his burden and his heat, so I answered him. He said: My Lord, make a friend between me and him. So He gave him permission until he came to Idris. Idris used to ask him, so he said to him: I have been informed that you are the most honorable of the angels and the most powerful with the Angel of Death, so intercede with him to delay my death, so that I may increase in gratitude and worship. The angel said: God does not delay a soul when its time has come, and I am speaking to it. So he raised him to the sky and placed him at the rising of the sun. Then he came to the Angel of Death and said: I have a need from you, a friend of mine from the sons of Adam intercedes with you to delay his death. He said: That is not up to me, but if you like, I will inform him of his death, so that he may advance it for himself. He said: Yes. So he looked in his register and said: You spoke to me about a man whom I do not see dying ever. He said: How? He said: I do not find him dying except at the rising of the sun. He said: Then I came to you and left him there. He said: Go, and I do not see you finding him except that he has died. By God, nothing remains of Idris’ life. The angel returned and found him dead. They differed as to whether he is alive in heaven or dead. Some people said: He is dead. Others said: He is alive. They said: Four of the prophets are alive, two on earth: Al-Khidr and Elias, and two in heaven: Idris and Jesus. Wahb said: Every day, Idris was offered as much worship as was offered to all the people of the earth at his time. The angels were amazed by him and the Angel of Death longed for him. He asked permission from his Lord to visit him, and He gave him permission. He came to him in the form of a human being. Idris used to fast all year long. When it was time to break his fast, he invited him to his food, but he refused to eat with him. He did that for three nights, but Idris denied him. On the third night, he said to him: I want to know who you are. He said: I am the Angel of Death. I asked permission from my Lord to accompany you. He said: I have a need of you. He said: What is it? He said: Take my soul. So God inspired him to take his soul. He took his soul and God returned it to him after an hour. The Angel of Death said to him: What is in your request of taking the soul? He said: So that I may taste the anguish and grief of death, so that I may be more prepared for it. Then Idris said to him: I have another need of you. He said: What is it? He said: Raise me to the sky so that I may look at it and at Paradise and Hell. So God permitted him to be raised. When he came close to Hell, he asked me for another need. He said: What do you want? He said: Ask Malik to open its gates for me so that I may enter it. So he did. Then he said: As long as you do not show me Hell, show me Paradise. So he went with him to Paradise and asked to be opened, so its gates were opened and he entered Paradise. Then the Angel of Death said: Come out so that you may return to your place. So he clung to a tree and said: I will not come out of it. So God sent a wise angel between them. The angel said to him: Why do you not come out? He said: “Because God the Most High said: ‘Every soul will taste death’ 3:185, and I have tasted it. He also said: “There is none of you but will pass over it” Maryam 19:71, and I have passed over it. He also said: And they will not be removed from it Al-Hijr 15:48, so I will not come out.” So God revealed to the Angel of Death: By my permission he entered Paradise and by my command he will not come out, for he is alive there. That is what God the Most High said: And We raised him to a high station.
19:58: 58 - Those upon whom God bestowed favor from among the prophets, from the descendants of Adam, meaning: Idris and Noah, and from those We carried with Noah, meaning from the descendants of those We carried with Noah in the ship, meaning Abraham, because he was born from Sam, son of Noah, and from the descendants of Abraham, meaning Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob. His saying: And Israel, meaning from the descendants of Israel, who are Moses, Aaron, Zechariah, John, and Jesus. His saying: And among those whom We have guided and chosen, these were among those whom We guided and chose, when the verses of the Most Gracious were recited to them, they fell down in prostration and weeping, prostrating is the plural of prostrating, and weeping is the plural of weeping. God informed us that when the prophets heard the verses of God, they prostrated and wept.
19:59: 59 - The Almighty said: Then there came after them a generation, meaning: after the aforementioned prophets came a generation, and they were bad people. The generation - with the fat-ha - is the good, and with the jazm the bad. Al-Suddi said: He meant the Jews and those who followed them. Mujahid and Qatada said: They are in this nation. They missed the prayer, they left the obligatory prayer. Ibn Masoud and Ibrahim said: They delayed it from its time. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It is not to pray the noon prayer until the afternoon prayer comes, nor the afternoon prayer until the sun sets. And they followed their desires, meaning: sins and drinking alcohol, meaning they preferred their own desires over obeying God. Mujahid said: These are people who will appear at the end of time, flirting with each other in the markets and alleys. They will surely encounter Ghayy, Wahb said: Ghayy is a river in Hell, with a deep bottom and a foul taste. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Ghay is a valley in Hell, and the valleys of Hell seek refuge from its heat. It is prepared for the persistent adulterer, the addicted drinker of alcohol, the usurer who does not give up interest, the disobedient, and the false witness. Ata’ said: Al-Ghay is a valley in Hell that flows with pus and blood. Kaab said: It is a valley in Hell, the deepest and hottest, in a well called Al-Haym. Whenever Hell subsides, God opens that well and Hell is set ablaze in it. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Harithi told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, and Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, the Almighty, Hisham ibn Bashir told us, Zakariya ibn Abi Maryam al-Khuza’i told us, he said: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: The distance between the edge of Hell and its bottom is a journey of seventy autumns of falling stone, or he said a falling rock, its bone is like ten tens of fat bones. A client of Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn al-Walid said to him: Is there anything under that, O Abu Umamah? He said: Yes, it is error and sins. Ad-Dahhak said: Despair and loss. It was also said: Destruction. It was also said: Torment. His saying: Then they will encounter error does not mean that they will only see, but rather it means that they will meet and be in contact with the vision.
19:60: 60 - "Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous deeds. For them, they will enter Paradise and not be wronged at all."
19:61: 61 - The Gardens of Eden which the Most Gracious has promised to His servants in the unseen, and they have not seen them. Indeed, His promise was to come true, meaning: coming, the passive participle has the meaning of the active participle. It was said: He did not say coming because everything that came to you, you have brought it, and the Arabs do not differentiate between the saying of the speaker: Fifty years have come upon me and his saying: I have come upon fifty years, and he says: Goodness has come to me and I have come to goodness. Ibn Jarir said: His promise means: His appointment, which is Paradise, coming His friends [the people of Paradise] and the people of His obedience will come to him.
19:62: 62 - They will not hear therein, in Paradise, any idle talk, falsehood, obscenity, or superfluous speech. Muqatil said: It is a false oath. “Except peace,” an exception of a different kind, meaning: Rather, they will hear therein peace. That is, a word from which they will be safe. (And peace) is a comprehensive name for goodness, because it includes safety. Meaning: The people of Paradise do not hear what makes them sin, but rather they hear what keeps them safe. It was said: It is the greeting of some of them to others, and the greeting of the angels to them. It was said: It is God’s peace upon them. And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening. The commentators said: There is no night in Paradise by which morning and evening are known, rather they are in light forever, but they bring their provisions according to the amount of the two ends of the day. It was said: They know the time of day by lifting the veils, and the time of night by lowering the veils. It was said: What is meant by it is a comfortable life and ample provision without any restriction. Al-Hasan Al-Basri used to say: The Arabs did not know of anything better in life than provision in the morning and evening, so God Almighty described His Paradise with that. 46. And that is the saying of God Almighty: The Fire, is a nominative case in place of evil, they are exposed to it morning and evening, morning and evening. Ibn Masoud said: The souls of Pharaoh’s family are in the bellies of black birds that are exposed to the Fire twice a day, going to the Fire in the morning and back, and it is said: O family of Pharaoh, these are your dwellings until the Hour comes. Qatada, Muqatil, Al-Suddi, and Al-Kalbi said: The soul of every unbeliever will be exposed to the Fire morning and evening as long as the world exists. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him in the morning and the evening. If he is among the people of Paradise, then he is among the people of Paradise, and if he is among the people of Hell, then he is among the people of Hell. And it is said to him: This is your seat until God resurrects you to it on the Day of Resurrection.” Then God the Almighty informed about their final resting place on the Day of Resurrection, saying: And on the Day the Hour comes, enter. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Amr, and Abu Bakr read: the Hour, “enter,” without the alif and the connecting letter, and with a damma on the initial letter, and with a damma on the kha from enter, meaning: it will be said to them: Enter, O family of Pharaoh, into the most severe torment. The others read: enter, without the alif and the kasra on the kha from enter, meaning: it will be said to the angels: Enter the family of Pharaoh into the most severe torment. Ibn Abbas said: He means the various types of torment with which they were tormented since they were drowned.
19:63: 63 - That is the Paradise which We give as an inheritance to some of Our servants. That is, We give and provide. It was said: He gives as an inheritance to His believing servants the dwellings that would have been for the people of Hell if they had believed, whoever was righteous. That is, the righteous among His servants.
19:64: 64 - The Almighty said: And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord, Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Khallad bin Yahya informed us, Umar bin Dhir informed us, he said: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Gabriel, what prevents you from visiting us? So the verse was revealed: "And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us," the verse. He said: This was the answer to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Qatada, Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: “Gabriel was delayed from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when his people asked him about the People of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn and the Spirit. He said: ‘I will tell you tomorrow,’ and he did not say: ‘God willing,’ until it was difficult for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he came down after a few days, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘You delayed me until my opinion was bad and I longed for you.’ Gabriel said to him: ‘I was longing, but I am a commanded servant. When I am sent, I descend, and when I am detained, I remain detained.’ Then God revealed: ‘And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. ’ And He revealed: ‘By the forenoon, and by the night when it is still. Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you. ’” He has what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that, meaning: He has knowledge of what is before us. They differed about it. Saeed bin Jubair, Qatadah and Muqatil said: What is before us means the matter of the Hereafter, reward and punishment. And what We created means what has passed of this world. And what is between that means what will be from this time until the Day of Resurrection. It was said, What is before us means what remains of this world, what is behind us means what has passed of it, and what is between that means what is between the two blasts, and between them is forty years. It was said: What is before us is what remains of this world, what is behind us is what has passed of it, and what is between that is the duration of our lives. It was said: What is before us: after we die, what is behind us: before we are created, and what is between that: the duration of life. It was said: What is before us: the earth if we want to descend to it, and what is behind us: the sky if we descend from it, and what is between that: the air, meaning: that all of that belongs to God Almighty, so we are not able to do anything except by His command. And your Lord is not forgetful, meaning: forgetful. He says: Your Lord has not forgotten you, meaning: He has not abandoned you. The forgetful is the one who abandons.
19:65: 65 - Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be patient in His worship, meaning: be patient in His commands and prohibitions. Do you know of anyone with a similar name? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: For example. Al-Kalbi said: Do you know anyone called God other than him?
19:66: 66 - The Almighty said: And man says, meaning: Abi bin Khalaf Al-Jumahi, who denied the resurrection. He said: When I die, will I then be brought back alive? He said this in mockery and denial of the resurrection.
19:67: 67 - God Almighty said: Or does he not remember, meaning: he remembers and thinks. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, ‘Asim, and Ya’qub read remember lightly, the human being, meaning: Abi bin Khalaf. We created him before, and he was nothing, meaning: this denier does not think about the beginning of his creation and use it as evidence for the return. Then he swore by himself, saying:
19:68: 68 - By your Lord, We will surely gather them We will gather them in the Resurrection, meaning: the polytheists who deny the Resurrection, and the devils with the devils, and that is because every disbeliever will be gathered with a devil in a chain, Then We will bring them around Hell, it was said in Hell, on their knees, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Groups, plural of on their knees. Al-Hasan and Al-Dahhak said: The plural of jath is: kneeling on the knees. Al-Saddī said: Standing on their knees due to the narrowness of the place.
19:69: 69 - Then We will extract, we will extract, from every sect, meaning: from every nation and people of religion from the infidels. Which of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful, rebellious. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: meaning boldness. Mujahid said: immoral, meaning: the most rebellious, then the most rebellious. Al-Kalbi said: Their leader and chief in evil wants to bring in someone who is greater in crime and more disbelieving. In some of the narrations: They will all be gathered around Hell, chained and shackled, then the most disbelieving will be brought forward, then the most disbelieving. And the word Ayhum was raised to mean: the one who is asked: Which of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful? It was said: On the resumption, then we will extract [it works in the place of from every sect].
19:70: 70 - Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of it, burning, meaning: most deserving of entering the Fire. It is said: he prayed, he prays, burning, like: he met, he finds, he meets, and he prayed, he prays, burning, like he went, he passes, he passes, if he entered the Fire and endured its heat.
19:71: 71 - The Almighty said: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, and there is not one of you but will pass over it. It was said: The oath is implied in it, meaning: By God, there is not one of you but will pass over it, and passing over is arriving at the place. They differed about the meaning of coming here, and what the metaphor refers to in His statement: coming into it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, said, and this is the opinion of the majority, that the meaning of coming into here is entering, and the metaphor refers to the Fire. They said: The Fire is entered by the righteous and the wicked, then God saves the righteous and brings them out of it. The evidence that entering is entering is the statement of God Almighty, narrating about Pharaoh: He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire (Hud 11:98). Ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar that Nafi` ibn al-Azraq consulted Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him about the entrance. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: It is entering. Nafi` said: The entrance is not the entrance. Abdullah ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him recited the words of God the Almighty: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. You will be brought to it.” (Al-Anbiya’: 98). Will these people enter it or not? Then he said: O Nafi`, by God, you and I will enter it, and I hope that God will get me out, but I do not think that God the Almighty will get you out of it because of your denial. Some people said: What is meant by entering is not entering. They said: No believer will ever enter the Fire, because God Almighty said: “Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. They will not hear its hissing sound.” (Al-Anbiya’: 101-102). They said: Everyone who enters it will not leave it. What is meant by His statement: There is not one of you but will pass over it, is presence and seeing, not entering, as God Almighty said: And when he came to the water of Madyan (al-Qasas 28:23). He meant presence. Ikrimah said: The verse is about the infidels, for they enter it but do not leave it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, that he said, There is not one of you but will pass over it, meaning the Day of Resurrection, and the metaphor refers back to it. The first is more correct. And the Sunnis agree that they will all enter Hell, then God Almighty will remove from it the people of faith, based on the evidence of His Almighty saying: Then We will save those who feared God, meaning those who feared polytheism, and they are the believers. And salvation is only from that which you entered into. Al-Kisa’i and Ya’qub read nanji with a light pronunciation, while the others read it with a heavy pronunciation. The evidence for this is: what Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If three of a Muslim’s children die, he will not enter Hellfire, except for the sake of breaking the oath. By the oath he meant his saying: There is not one of you but will pass over it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “He who says, ‘There is no god but God’ and in his heart is the weight of a barley grain of goodness will be brought out of the Fire. He who says, ‘There is no god but God’ and in his heart is the weight of a grain of barley of goodness will be brought out of the Fire. He who says, ‘There is no god but God’ and in his heart is the weight of an atom of goodness will be brought out of the Fire.” Abaan said on the authority of Qatada: of faith instead of goodness. Abu Al-Muzaffar Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ali Al-Shuja’i told us, Abu Nasr Al-Nu’man bin Muhammad bin Mahmoud Al-Jurjani told us, Abu Uthman Amr bin Abdullah Al-Basri told us, Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab told us, Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Abu Al-Nu’man told us, Salam bin Maskeen told us, Abu Al-Dhilal told us on the authority of Anas bin Malik on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “A man in Hell will call out for a thousand years, ‘O Most Gracious, O Most Generous.’ God, the Almighty, will say to Gabriel, ‘Go and bring Me this servant of Mine.’ Gabriel went and found the people of Hell crying and weeping. He returned and informed his Lord, the Almighty, who said, ‘Go, for he is in such and such a place.’ He brought him. He said, ‘O My servant, how did you find your place and your resting place?’ He said, ‘O Lord, the worst place and the worst resting place.’ He said, ‘Return My servant.’ He said, ‘I did not expect that You would return me to it when You took me out of it.’ God, the Almighty, will say to His angels, ‘Leave My servant.’” As for the Almighty’s saying: They will not hear its hissing sound (al-Anbiya 21:102), it was said: God Almighty informed us about the time when they will be in Paradise that they will not hear its hissing sound, so it is possible that they heard that before they entered Paradise, because He did not say: They will not hear its hissing sound. And it is possible that they will not hear its hissing sound when they enter it, because God Almighty will make it cool and peaceful for them. Khalid bin Ma'dan said: The people of Paradise will say: Did not our Lord promise us that we would return to the Fire? It will be said: Yes, but you passed by it while it was extinguished. In the hadith: The fire says to the believer: Go away, believer, for your light has extinguished my flame. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the words of God Almighty: There is not one of you but will pass over it, he said: Whoever among the Muslims has passed over it. In the hadith: Fever is a bellows of Hell, and it is the believer’s portion of Hell. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Hisham, my father told me, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Fever is from the heat of Hell, so cool it with water. “It was an inevitability decreed upon your Lord,” meaning: your entering Hell was an inevitable and necessary thing. Decided: God decreed it upon you.
19:72: 72 - Then We will save those who feared God, meaning those who feared polytheism. Al-Kisa’i read We will save with a light pronunciation, and the rest read it with a heavy pronunciation. And We will leave the wrongdoers therein kneeling, all of them. It was said: kneeling on their knees. This is evidence that they all entered it, then God removed the righteous from it and left the wrongdoers therein, who are the polytheists. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Ata bin Yazid Al-Laithi told me that Abu Hurairah told them that the people said: O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Do you find it difficult to see the moon on a full moon night with no clouds in front of it? They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: Do you find it difficult to see the sun with no clouds in front of it? They said: No. He said: “Then you will see it like that. The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: ‘Whoever worships something, let him follow it.’ Some of them will follow the sun, some of them will follow the moon, and some of them will follow the tyrants. This nation will remain with its hypocrites. Then God, the Almighty, will come to them and say: ‘I am your Lord.’ They will say: ‘This is our place until our Lord comes to us.’ When our Lord comes, we will recognize Him. Then God will come to them and say: ‘I am your Lord.’ They will say: ‘You are our Lord.’ He will call them, and the bridge will be set up in the midst of Hell, and I will be the first of the messengers to cross with my nation. On that day, none will speak except the messengers, and the speech of the messengers on that day will be: ‘O God, save, save.’ In Hell are hooks like the thorns of the Sa’dan tree. Have you seen the thorns of the Sa’dan tree? They said: “Yes.” He said: ‘They are like the thorns of the Sa’dan tree, except that the extent of their strength is not known.” The greatest of them is God. It snatches people by their deeds. Some of them are destroyed by their knowledge, and some of them are thrown away and then escaped. When God wants to have mercy on whomever He wants from the people of Hell, God commands the angels to bring out whoever used to worship God. They bring them out and recognize them by the marks of prostration. God has forbidden the Fire to consume the marks of prostration. So they come out of the Fire. The Fire consumes every son of Adam except the marks of prostration. So they come out of the Fire having been scorched. The water of life is poured over them and they grow as a seed grows in the silt of a torrent. Then God finishes judging between the servants, and a man remains between Paradise and Hell, and he is the last of the people of Hell to enter Paradise. He faces the Fire and says: O Lord, turn my face away from the Fire. Its odor has stung me and its heat has burned me. He says: If I do that to you, will you ask for something else? He says: No, by Your glory. Then God gives him whatever covenant and pledge He wills, and God turns his face away from the Fire. When he is brought to Paradise and sees its splendor, he is silent as long as God wills him to be silent, then he says: O Lord, bring me forward to the gate of Paradise. God the Blessed and Exalted says: Were you not given the covenant and pledge that you would not ask for anything other than what you asked for? He says: O Lord, I will not be the most miserable of Your creation. He says: What would it be if You were given that, that You would ask for anything other than it? He says: No, by Your glory, I will not ask You for anything other than that. Then his Lord gives him whatever covenant and pledge He wills, and He brings him forward to the gate of Paradise. When he reaches its gate and sees its flowers and what is in it of freshness and joy, he is silent as long as God wills him to be silent, and he says: O Lord, admit me to Paradise. God the Almighty says: Woe to you, O son of Adam, how treacherous you are! Were you not given the covenant and pledge that you would not ask for anything other than what You were given? He says: O Lord, do not make me the most miserable of your creation. God laughs at him, then He allows him to enter Paradise. He says: Wish. He wishes until his wish is cut off. God the Most High says: Wish for such and such. His Lord reminds him, until when his wishes are finished, God the Most High says: For you and the like thereof with it. Abu Sa`id said to Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God said: That is for you and ten times the like thereof. Abu Hurairah said: I did not remember from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except his saying: For you and the like thereof with it. Abu Sa`id said: I heard him say: That is for you and ten times the like thereof.” Muhammad ibn Ismail narrated it on the authority of Mahmud ibn Ghailan, who told us on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, who told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ata ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with the same meaning. He said: “Then God Almighty will come to them in a form other than that which they recognize and say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in God from you. This is our place until our Lord comes to us. When our Lord comes to us, we will recognize Him. Then God will come to them in the form which they recognize and say: I am your Lord. They will say: You are our Lord, and they will follow Him.” Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Hiri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Some people of monotheism will be tormented in the Fire until they become charcoal, then mercy will reach them. He said: They will fall down and be thrown at the gates of Paradise. He said: The people of Paradise will sprinkle water on them and they will grow like gourds growing in the water of a torrent, then they will enter Paradise.” Abu Muhammad ibn Abd al-Samad al-Juwzjani told us, Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn Ahmad al-Khuza’i told us, Abu Saeed al-Haytham ibn Kulayb told us, Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi told us, Hanad ibn al-Sarri told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ubaydah al-Salmani, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I know the last of the people of Hell to emerge from Hell. He will be a man who will crawl out of it and it will be said to him: ‘Go and enter Paradise.’ He will go to enter Paradise and will find that the people have taken their places. He will return and say: ‘O Lord, the people have taken their places.’ It will be said: ‘Do you remember the time when you were?’ He will say: ‘Yes.’ It will be said to him: ‘Make a wish.’ He will make a wish and it will be said to him: ‘Then you will have what you wished for and ten times the world.’ He will say: ‘Are you mocking me and you are the king?’ He said: ‘I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughing until his molars were visible.’” Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Umm Mubashar, on the authority of Hafsah, that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I hope that, God willing, no one who witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire. I said: “O Messenger of God, has God not said: ‘There is not one of you but will pass over it. This is an inevitability decreed by your Lord.’” He said: “Have you not heard Him say: ‘Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.’”
19:73: 73 - The Almighty said: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear proofs, “those who disbelieve say,” meaning: Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith and his relatives from Quraysh, to those who believe, meaning the poor companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among them were roughness, and in their lives was roughness, and in their clothes was shabby, and the polytheists used to comb their hair, oil their heads, and wear silk clothes, so they said to the believers: Which of the two parties is better in position, in home and dwelling, [which is the place of residence. Ibn Kathir read: Maqam with a dammah on the mim, meaning a residence. And the best gathering, meaning a council, and the same applies to a club. So God Almighty answered them and said:
19:74: 74 - And how many generations before them have We destroyed who were better in furnishings, meaning in possessions and wealth. Muqatil said: clothing and garments, vision, most of the reciters read with a hamza, meaning: a view, from vision, and Ibn Amir, Abu Ja`far, and Nafi` except Warsh read: and riyaa with a shaddah without a hamza, and it has two interpretations: one of them is the first, by dropping the hamza, and the second: from irrigation: which is the opposite of thirst, and its meaning: quenching one's thirst from a blessing, for the one who is in luxury shows in him the quenching of a blessing, and the poor one shows the traces of poverty.
19:75: 75 - "Say: Whoever is in error - let the Most Merciful extend to him a term." This is a command in the sense of a statement, meaning: He will leave him in his transgression and give him respite in his disbelief, until, when they see what they are promised - either the punishment, which is captivity and killing in this world, or the Hour, meaning: the Resurrection, when they will enter the Fire, then they will know, at that time, who is worse in position, in dwelling, and weaker in soldiers, with fewer supporters, are they or the believers? Because they will be in the Fire, and the believers will be in Paradise. This is a response to them in His statement: Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company?
19:76: 76 - The Almighty says: And God increases those who are guided in guidance, meaning faith and certainty upon their certainty, and the lasting good deeds, meaning the remembrances and righteous deeds that remain for their doer, are better in the sight of your Lord as reward and better as return, meaning a consequence and a return.
19:77: 77 - The Almighty said: "Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'?" Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Amr bin Hafs informed us, my father informed us, Al-A'mash bin Muslim informed us, on the authority of Masruq, Khabbab told us: I was a blacksmith, and I worked for Al-'As bin Wa'il, and my wealth accumulated with him, so we came to him to collect it, and he said: No, by God, I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad. I said: By God, not until you die and are resurrected. He said: And will I die and then be resurrected? I said: Yes. He said: Then I will have wealth and children, so I will pay you. Then God Almighty revealed: "Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'?
19:78: 78 - The Almighty said: He knows the unseen. Ibn Abbas said: Do I look in the Preserved Tablet? And Mujahid said: Do I know the knowledge of the unseen so that He knows whether he is in Paradise or not? Or has he made a covenant with the Most Merciful? That is, he said, There is no god but God. Qatada said: It means a good deed that he had done. Al-Kalbi said: Did he make a covenant with him that he would enter Paradise?
19:79: 79 - No, he replied, meaning, he did not do that, We will write down, we will record for him, what he says, [and we will reward him for it in the Hereafter. It was said: We will command the angels to write down what he says.] And we will extend for him from the punishment an extension, meaning: We will increase his punishment upon the punishment. It was said: We will prolong the duration of his punishment.
19:80: 80 - And We shall inherit from him what he says, meaning what he has of money and children by our destroying him and invalidating his kingdom and his saying what he says, because he claimed that he has money and children in the Hereafter, meaning: We will not give it to him and we will give it to someone else, so the inheritance will return to what is under the statement, not to the statement itself. It was said: The meaning of his saying: And we inherit from him what he says is: We preserve what he says until we reward him for it. And he will come to us alone on the Day of Resurrection, without money or children.
19:81: 81 - The Almighty said: And they took besides God gods meaning: the polytheists of Quraysh took idols as gods that they worshipped, so that they might be a source of honor for them, meaning a source of protection, so that they might be intercessors for them who would prevent them from being punished.
19:82: 82 - No, meaning it is not as they claimed, they will disbelieve in their worship, meaning they will deny the idols and gods that they used to worship as the polytheists worship them and will disavow them, as God Almighty said, We disavow to You what they used to worship (al-Qasas 28:63). And they will be their opponents, meaning their enemies, and they were their allies in this world. It was said: They are their helpers, who lie to them and curse them.
19:83: 83 - The Almighty said: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers? That is, We have given them power over them, and that was when He said to Satan, And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, the verse (al-Isra’ 17:64), incite them with incitement, incite them with incitement from obedience to disobedience, and incitement (and shaking) means moving, that is, you move them and urge them to commit sins.
19:84: 84 - So do not be hasty in seeking punishment for them, meaning do not be hasty in seeking their punishment. We are only counting for them a [definite] number, Al-Kalbi said: meaning the night, the days, the months, and the years. It was said: The breaths they take in this world until the appointed time for their punishment.
19:85: 85 - The Almighty’s saying: The Day when We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation. That is: Remind them, O Muhammad, of the day on which those who feared God in this world through their obedience will be gathered to the Most Merciful, to His Paradise as a delegation, that is: groups, the plural of delegate, like: rider and riders, and companion is companions. Ibn Abbas said: On camels. Abu Hurairah said: On camels. Ali bin Abi Talib said: By God, they will not be resurrected on their feet, but on camels with gold saddles and saddles of rubies. If they intend to ride them, they will walk, and if they intend to ride them, they will fly.
19:86: 86- And We will drive the criminals, the disbelievers, to Hell in droves, meaning on foot. It was said: Thirsty, their necks cut off from thirst. The droves are a group who go to water, and no one goes to water except after being thirsty.
19:87: 87 - They do not possess intercession except for he who has made a covenant with the Most Merciful, meaning there is no god but God. It was said: Its meaning is that the intercessors do not intercede except for those who have made a covenant with the Most Merciful, meaning: the believers, like His saying: They do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased (al-Anbiya 21:28). It was said: No one can intercede except he who testifies that there is no god but God, meaning no one can intercede except the believer.
19:88: 88 - And they said, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son,’ meaning the Jews and Christians, and those who claim that the angels are daughters of God. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: childan with a damma on the waw and a sukoon on the lam, here and in Az-Zukhruf and Surat Nuh. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ya’qub agreed in Surat Nuh, and the rest read it with a fatha on the waw and the lam. They are two languages like: Al-Arab and Al-Arab, and Al-Ajam and Al-Ajam.
19:89: 89 - You have certainly done something terrible, Ibn Abbas said, denying it. Qatada and Mujahid said: Great. Muqatil said: You have said something terrible. And in the speech of the Arabs: the greatest of calamities.
19:90: 90 - The heavens are almost, Nafi' read Yakad with a ya' here and in Ha Mim * Ain Sin Qaf because the verb came before it, and the rest read it with a ta' because the heavens are feminine, They burst from it, here and in Ha Mim * Ain Sin Qaf with a noon from the bursting, Abu Amr, Abu Bakr, and Ya'qub agreed with Ibn Amir and Hamza here because of the Almighty's saying: When the sky is split (al-Infitar 82:1) and The sky is split (al-Muzzammil 73:18), and the rest read it with a ta' from the bursting and their meaning is the same, it is said: the thing burst and burst, meaning it cracked. And the earth will split open and the mountains will collapse in ruins, meaning: they will be broken. It was said: The earth will split open meaning: it will swallow them up, and the splitting open in the sky means that it will fall on them, and the mountains will collapse in ruins meaning that they will collapse on them.
19:91: 91 - "That they invoked, meaning that they made a son for the Most Gracious", Ibn Abbas and Ka'b said: The heavens, the earth, the mountains, and all of creation were terrified except for the two heavy ones, and they almost collapsed, and the angels became angry, and Hell was raging when they said: God has taken a son. Then God denied having a son, saying:
19:92: 92 - It is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son, meaning that it is not befitting for Him to take a son, and He is not described as such.
19:93: 93 - There is none in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful, meaning that he will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, as a slave, humbled and submissive. This means that all of creation is His slave.
19:94: 94 - He has counted them and counted them with a precise count, meaning: He has counted their breaths, their days, and their traces, so nothing is hidden from Him.
19:95: 95 - And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone, alone, with nothing of this world with him.
19:96: 96 - The Almighty said: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection. That is, love. Mujahid said: God loves them and makes them beloved to His believing servants. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt told us, Abu Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “When God loves a servant, He says to Gabriel: I love so-and-so, so love him. Gabriel loves him, then he calls out to the people of heaven: God Almighty loves so-and-so, so love him. The people of heaven love him, then acceptance is placed for him on earth. And if He hates a servant…” Malik said: I do not think he would have said something similar about hatred. Haram bin Hayyan said: No servant turns his heart to God Almighty except that God turns the hearts of the people of faith to him until He grants him their love.
19:97: 97 - The Almighty said: We have only made it easy for your tongue, meaning We have made the Qur’an easy for your tongue, O Muhammad, so that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous, meaning the believers, and warn thereby a people who are obstinate, severe in their dispute, plural of al-ald. Al-Hassan said: Deaf to the truth. Mujahed said: Al-Ald: The unjust one who does not behave properly. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Ald is the one who does not accept the truth and claims falsehood.
19:98: 98 - And how many generations before them have We destroyed who were better. Do you see, and it was said, do you find, anyone of them, or do you hear from them a rumbling, meaning a sound? And rumbling: a low sound. Al-Hasan said: They all perished, and not a single eye or trace of them remained.
20:1: 1 - Meccan. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ibn Abi Uwais told us, my father told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Halali, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given the surah in which the cow was mentioned from the first mention, and I was given Ta Ha and the Ta-Sin from the tablets of Moses, and I was given the openings of the Qur’an and the endings of the surah in which the cow was mentioned from beneath the throne, and I was given the Mufassal as a voluntary act.” Ta-Ha, Abu Amr reads with a fatha on the ta’ and a kasra on the ha’. Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr read them with a kasra, and the rest read them with a fatha. It was said: It is an oath. It was also said: It is one of the names of God Almighty. Mujahed, Al-Hasan, Ata’, and Ad-Dahhak said: Its meaning is, O man. Qatada said: It is, man, in Syriac. Al-Kalbi said: It is, O man, in the language of Ak. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Its meaning is to step on the ground with your feet, meaning: during the night prayer. Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi said: God Almighty swore by his length and guidance. Saeed bin Jubair said: The letter ta is the opening letter of his name Al-Tahir, and the letter ha is the opening letter of his name Haad. Al-Kalbi said: When the revelation came down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca, he strove hard in worship until he would alternate between his feet in prayer due to the length of his standing, and he would pray all night long. Then God revealed this verse, and commanded him to make it easy on himself, so he said:
20:2: 2 - We did not send down the Qur'an to you to make you miserable. It was said: When the polytheists saw his diligence in worship, they said, The Qur’an was not revealed to you, O Muhammad, except for your misery. So the verse We have not revealed the Qur’an to you to make you miserable was revealed, meaning that you would suffer and tire yourself out. The root of misery in the language is hardship.
20:3: 3 - Except as a reminder for those who fear [i.e., but We sent it down as a lesson for those who fear. It was said: Its meaning is We did not send down the Qur'an to you to make you miserable. We sent it down only as a reminder for those who fear].
