20:4: 4 - A revelation, instead of saying a reminder, “from those who created the earth,” meaning: from God who created the earth, and the high heavens, meaning: the high and lofty, and it is the plural of high, like his saying: great and great, and small and smaller.
20:5: 5 - The Most Gracious is firmly established on the Throne.
20:6: 6 - To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them, meaning the air, and whatever is beneath the soil, and soil is: moist dirt. Ad-Dahhak said: meaning whatever is beyond the soil. Ibn Abbas said: The earths are on the back of the Noon, and the Noon is on a sea, and its head and tail meet under the Throne, and the sea is on a green rock, the greenness of the sky is from it, and it is the rock that God mentioned in the story of Luqman, and it will be in a rock, and the rock is on the horn of a bull, and the bull is on the soil, and what is under the soil is known only to God Almighty, and that bull has its mouth open, so when God Almighty makes the seas one sea, they will flow into the belly of that bull, and when they fall into its belly, they will dry up.
20:7: 7 - And if you speak aloud, [i.e., you declare it], then He knows the secret and what is more hidden. Al-Hasan said: The secret is what a man confides in others, and what is more hidden than that is what he keeps secret in himself. On the authority of Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Jubair: The secret is what you keep secret in your soul and what is more hidden than the secret: what God Almighty places in your heart later, and you do not know that you will tell yourself about it, because you know what you keep secret today and you do not know what you will keep secret tomorrow, and God knows what you keep secret today and what you will keep secret tomorrow. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The secret is what the son of Adam keeps secret in his soul, and concealed is what is hidden from him of what he will do before he knows it. Mujahed said: The secret is the action that you conceal from people, and more hidden is the whispering. It was said: The secret: is the determination [And hidden: what comes to mind but is not determined upon. Zaid bin Aslam said: He knows the secret and what is more hidden: meaning He knows the secrets of the servants, and He has hidden His secret from His servants, so no one knows it. Then he united himself and said:
20:8: 8 - "God, there is no god but He. To Him belong the best names."
20:9: 9 - The Almighty’s saying: And has the story of Moses come to you? meaning: has it come to you, a question with the meaning of confirmation.
20:10: 10 - When he saw a fire, that is because Moses asked permission from Shu'aib to return from Madyan to Egypt to visit his mother and sister, so he gave him permission, so he left with his family and his money, and it was the days of winter, and he took the wrong road for fear of the kings of Syria, and his wife was sick, not knowing whether it was night or day. So he walked in the wilderness not knowing its paths, so the journey forced him to the western right side of the mountain on a dark, snowy, very cold night, and his wife was in labor, so he struck his flint but it did not light. It was said: Moses was a jealous man, so he would accompany his companions at night and leave them during the day, so that his wife would not see. Once, he made a mistake on the road on a dark, wintry night, when God Almighty wanted to honor him, so he started striking the flint but it did not light, so he saw a fire from afar to the left of the road from the side of the mountain. So he said to his family, ‘Stay here.’ Hamza read it with a damma on the ha’ here and in Al-Qasas. I have seen, meaning: I have seen, a fire, perhaps I can bring you a torch from it, a flame of fire, and a torch is a piece of fire that you take from the end of a column of fire, or find guidance on the fire, meaning: I can find someone near the fire who can guide me to the way.
20:11: 11 - "So when he came to it," he saw a green tree from its bottom [to its top, surrounded by a white fire burning as bright as could be, so the light of the fire did not change] the greenness of the tree, nor did the greenness of the tree change the light of the fire. Ibn Masoud said: It was a green samra tree. Qatada, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: It was made of the Awsaj tree. Wahb said: It was from the blackberry. It was said: It was the jujube tree. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. The commentators said: What Moses saw was not fire, but rather light. It was mentioned with the word fire because Moses thought it was fire. Most of the commentators said: It is the light of the Almighty Lord, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and others. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the fire itself, and it is one of the veils of God Almighty. Evidence for this is what we narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The veil of the fire, if He were to remove it, the radiance of His face would burn everything that His sight reaches of His creation. In the story, Moses took some dry grass and headed towards the tree. Whenever he got close, the fire would come closer to him, and whenever he got farther away, it would come closer. He stood there, perplexed, and heard the angels glorifying God, and tranquility was bestowed upon him. He was called, O Moses, Wahb said, “He was called from the tree, and it was said, ‘O Moses!’ He responded quickly, not knowing who had called him, and said, ‘I hear your voice but I do not see your place, so where are you?’ He said, ‘I am above you and with you, in front of you and behind you, and closer to you than your own self.’ So he knew that this was only due to God, and he was certain of it.”
20:12: 12 - “I am your Lord.” Abu Ja`far, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read ani with the alif open, meaning: it was called out that I am. Others read it with a kasra on the alif, meaning: He was called and it was said: I am your Lord. The Almighty said: Then take off your shoes. The reason for that was what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, regarding his statement: Then take off your shoes. He said: They were made of the hide of a dead donkey. It is also narrated that they were not tanned. Akrima and Mujahid said: He was ordered to take off his shoes so that he could touch the soil of the Holy Land with his feet, and thus attain its blessing because it was sanctified twice. So Moses took them off and threw them from behind the valley. You are in the sacred valley, meaning the purified one, Tawa, and Tawa is the name of the valley. The people of Kufa and Ash-Sham read: Tawa with the tanween here and in Surat An-Nazi'at, and the others read it without the tanween because it was modified from Taw, so when it was modified from its face, it was diverted from its i'rab, like Omar and Zafar. Ad-Dahhak said: Tawa is a deep, round valley like Al-Tawi in its roundness.
20:13: 13 - And I have chosen you, I have selected you with My messages, Hamza read: And I with a shaddah on the nun, We have chosen you for emphasis. So listen to what is revealed, to you:
20:14: 14 - Indeed, I am God, there is no god but Me, so worship Me, and do not worship anyone other than Me, and establish prayer for My remembrance, Mujahid said: Establish prayer to remember Me in it, and Mujahid said: If you leave prayer and then remember it, then establish it. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihin told us, Abu Amr Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Muzani told us, Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hafid told us, al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Bajali told us, Affan told us, Qatada told us on the authority of Anas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever forgets a prayer, let him pray it when he remembers it, for there is no expiation for it except that. Then he said: I heard him say after that: And establish prayer for My remembrance.
20:15: 15 - The Hour is coming, I almost hide it. It was said that it means that the Hour is coming, I almost hide it. Almost is a relative clause. Most of the commentators said that it means: I almost hide it from myself. Likewise in the Mushaf of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: I almost hide it, so how could a creature know it? In some readings: How can I reveal it to you? This was mentioned according to the custom of the Arabs when they exaggerate in concealing something. They say: I concealed your secret in my soul, meaning: I hid it to the utmost concealment. And nothing is hidden from God, the Almighty. Al-Akhfash said: Akad means I want. The meaning of the verse is: The Hour is coming, but I want to hide it. The meaning of concealing it is to exaggerate and intimidate, because if they did not know when the Hour would come, they would be on guard against it at all times. Al-Hasan read it with the opening of the alif, meaning he revealed it. It is said: I revealed something if you revealed it, and I concealed it if you covered it. God Almighty says: That every soul may be rewarded for what it strives for, meaning for what it does of good and evil.
20:16: 16 - So let not he who does not believe in it and follows his own desires turn you away from it, meaning he disobeyed God’s command, so you will perish, meaning you will be destroyed.
20:17: 17 - The Almighty's saying: "And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?" This is a question of confirmation, and the wisdom in this question is to alert him and make him aware that it is a staff, so that when he turns it into a snake, he will know that it is a great miracle. This is according to the custom of the Arabs, a man would say to another: Do you know this? And he has no doubt that he knows it, and he wants his acknowledgement with his tongue to be added to his knowledge of it in his heart.
20:18: 18 - He said, 'It is my staff.' It was said that it had two branches, and at the bottom of it was a point, and it had a stick. Muqatil said: Its name was Naba'a. I lean on it: I depend on it when I walk, when I get tired, and when I jump. And I beat down leaves with it for my sheep: I hit the dry tree with it so that its leaves fall and the sheep graze on them. Ikrimah read and Ahash with the unvoiced seen, meaning: he drove the sheep with it, and has means driving the sheep. And I have other purposes in it, other needs and benefits. The plural of ma’ribah is with the ra open or closed. He did not say other because of the beginnings of the verses. What he meant by ma’rib is what the stick is used for in travel, and he used it to carry provisions and tie the rope with it to draw water from the well, and kill snakes with it, and fight wild beasts with it, and seek shade with it if he tied it, and other things. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Moses used to carry his provisions and water-skin on it, and it would walk with him and talk to him. He would strike the ground with it and bring out what he would eat that day, and he would put it in a deep place and water would come out. When he lifted it up, the water would go away. When he desired a fruit, he would put it in a deep place and it would branch out like a tree, produce leaves and bear fruit. When he wanted to draw water from the well, he would lower it and it would grow the length of the well and its two branches would become like a bucket until he drew water. It would light up at night like a lamp, and when an enemy appeared to him, it would fight and defend him.
20:19: 19. He said, God Almighty: Throw it down, O Moses, throw it away. Wahb said: Moses thought he was saying reject it.
20:20: 20. "So he threw it down/ with a face of rejection, then he looked, and behold, it was a snake, yellow, the largest of snakes, scurrying", walking quickly on its belly. And he said in another place: "As if it were a jinn" (al-Naml 27:10), which is a small, light-bodied snake. And he said in another place: (a snake), which is the largest of snakes. As for the snake: it includes the young and the old, the male and the female. It was said: (The jinn) refers to the beginning of its state, as it was a snake the size of a stick, then it would swell and become puffy until it became a serpent, (The serpent) refers to the end of its state. It was said that it was as big as a snake and as fast as a jinn. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Moses looked and saw that the staff was a snake, the largest of snakes. Its two branches had become its jaws, and its spear had become its neck and crest. It was shaking like meteors, and its eyes were blazing like fire. It passed over a huge rock like the backs of camels, and it was breaking the huge tree with its fangs, and a great grinding sound could be heard from its teeth. When Moses saw that, he turned and fled, then he remembered his Lord and stood out of shame before Him. Then he was called: O Moses, come back and go back to where you were. So he returned, very afraid.
20:21: 21. "He said, 'Take it,' in your right hand, 'and do not fear. We will restore it to its former state,' its first form, that is, We will return it to being a stick as it was. Moses was wearing a coat of wool that he had woven with sticks. When God Almighty said, 'Take it,' he wrapped the end of the coat of wool around his hand, and God Almighty commanded him to uncover his hand, so he uncovered it. Some of them mentioned: When he wrapped the sleeve of the armor around his hand, an angel said to him: Tell me, if God permitted what you feared, would the armor be of any use to you? He said: No, but I am weak, and from weakness I was created. So he uncovered his hand and put it in the mouth of the snake, and behold, it was a stick as it was, and his hand was in its fork in the place where he used to put it when he leaned. The commentators said: God Almighty wanted to show Moses the sign that He had given him, which no creature could do, so that he would not be frightened by it if he presented it to Pharaoh. His saying: Her first life is in the accusative case with the deletion of to, meaning: to her first life.
20:22: 22. The Almighty said: And put your hand into your side, meaning: your armpit. Mujahid said: Under your upper arm, and the side of a person is his upper arm to the base of his armpit. It will come out white, bright and radiant, without disease, without defect, and disease here means leprosy. Ibn Abbas said: His hand had a bright light that illuminated the night and day like the light of the sun and the moon, another sign, meaning: another proof of your truthfulness other than the staff.
20:23: 23. To show you some of Our greatest signs, and He did not say greatness for the heads of the verses. It was said: There is an implication in it, meaning: To show you some of Our greatest signs, the evidence for which is the statement of Ibn Abbas: The hand of Moses was the greatest of His signs.
20:24: 24. God Almighty said: Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed, meaning: he has exceeded the limit in disobedience and rebellion, so call him to worship Me.
20:25: 25. He said, Moses: My Lord, expand my chest for me, expand it for the truth. Ibn Abbas said: He means so that I do not fear anyone but You, and that is because Moses feared Pharaoh with intense fear due to the severity of his power and the large number of his soldiers, and he was distressed by what he was tasked with in resisting Pharaoh alone, so he asked God to expand his heart for the truth so that he would know that no one is able to harm him except by God's permission, and if he knew that, he would not fear Pharaoh and the severity of his power and the large number of his soldiers.
20:26: 26. And make my task easy for me, meaning: Make easy for me what you commanded me to do, which is to deliver the message to Pharaoh.
20:27: 27. And loosen the knot from my tongue, because Moses was in Pharaoh's lap one day when he was young, and Pharaoh slapped him and grabbed his beard, so he said to his wife Asiya: This is my enemy and he wanted to kill him, but Asiya said: He is a boy who does not understand or discern. In another narration, when Moses' mother weaned him, she sent him back, and he grew up in the care of Pharaoh and his wife Asiya, who raised him and took him as a son. One day, while he was playing in front of Pharaoh, and in his hand was a stick, he raised the stick and struck Pharaoh's head with it. Pharaoh became angry and thought ill of his striking him, so he wanted to kill him. Asiya said: O king, he is young and does not understand, so test him if you wish. She brought two bowls: in one was hot coals and in the other was jewels. She placed them in front of Moses, and he wanted to take the jewels, but Gabriel took Moses' hand and placed it on the fire. He took a hot coal and put it in his mouth, and his tongue was burned and a knot formed on it.
20:28: 28. They understand my words, he says: Untie the knot so they understand my words.
20:29: 29. And appoint for me a minister, a helper and supporter, from my family. The minister is the one who supports you, helps you, and bears some of the burden of your work. Then he explained who he is, saying:
20:30: 30. Aaron, my brother. Aaron was four years older than Moses, and he was more eloquent, more handsome, and white in complexion, while Moses was dark-skinned and had curly hair.
20:32: 32. And let him share in my affair, meaning: in prophecy and conveying the message. Ibn Amir read more strongly with the alif open, and and let him share with the alif closed as an answer, narrating from Moses, meaning: I will do that. The others read it as a supplication. The question, in apposition to what came before from his saying: My Lord, expand my chest for me * and make my affair easy for me.
20:33: 33. So that we may glorify You much, Al-Kalbi said: We pray to You much.
20:34: 34. And we remember You often, we praise You and thank You for the blessings You have bestowed upon us.
20:35: 35. Indeed, You have been watching over us, All-Knowing, All-Aware.
20:36: 36. He said, God Almighty: You have been given, I have been given, your request, everything you asked for, O Moses.
20:37: 37. And We have bestowed upon you, We have bestowed upon you, another time, meaning before this time, which is:
20:38: 38. When We inspired your mother, inspiration, what is inspired, what inspires them. Then He explained that inspiration and enumerated His blessings upon him:
20:39: 39. Throw him into the chest: meaning: We inspired her to put him in the chest, throw him into the sea, meaning the Nile River, and let the sea cast him onto the shore, meaning the river bank. Its wording is a command but its meaning is a statement, its metaphor is: until the sea casts him onto the shore: an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his will take him, meaning Pharaoh. So she took a coffin and put in it ginned cotton and put Moses in it, and she cut off his head and his slits - meaning his cracks - then she threw him into the Nile, and a large river flowed from it in the house of Pharaoh. While Pharaoh was sitting at the head of the pool with his wife Asiya, suddenly a coffin was brought with water, so he ordered the young men and women to bring it out. They brought it out and opened its head, and there was a boy with the most beautiful face of the people. When Pharaoh saw him, he loved him so much that he could not control himself. This is what God the Almighty said: {And I have bestowed upon you love from Me}. Ibn Abbas said: He loved him and made him beloved to His creation. Ikrimah said: No one saw him but loved him. Qatada said: There was beauty in the eyes of Moses; no one saw him but fell in love with him. And let her be made before my eyes, meaning that she be raised in my sight and view. Abu Ja`far read and let her be made in the jussive mood.
20:40: 40. When your sister walked, whose name was Mary, learning about him, "and she said: Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?" That is, to a woman who would breastfeed him and hold him close to her. This is because he did not accept the breast of a woman. So when his sister told them that, they said: Yes. So she brought the mother and he kissed her breast. This is what God Almighty said: So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be cooled, by meeting you, and she should not grieve, that is, so that her grief would go away. And you killed a person, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: He killed an infidel Copt. Kaab al-Ahbar said: He was twelve years old at that time. So We saved you from the grief, meaning from the grief and distress of being killed. And We tested you with trials, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: We tested you with a test. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: We tried you with a trial. Mujahid said: We purified you with purity. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, in the narration of Saeed bin Jubair: That the trials are his falling into one trial after another from which God delivered him, the first of which was that his mother carried him in the year in which Pharaoh was slaughtering children, then he was thrown into the sea in the chest, then he was prevented from breastfeeding except from his mother’s breast, then he was seized by Pharaoh’s beard until he wanted to kill him, then he took a live coal instead of a whip, then the Copt killed him, and he went out to Madyan in fear. So Ibn Abbas used to tell the story to Saeed bin Jubair, so according to this the meaning of We have tested you is We have delivered you from those trials, just as gold is tested by fire and is purified from all impurity in it. And trials is a verbal noun. So she stayed, meaning she left Egypt and stayed, for years among the people of Madyan, meaning she tended the sheep for ten years. Madyan is the town of Shu’ayb, peace be upon him, eight stages from Egypt, to which Moses fled. Wahb said: He stayed with Shu`ayb, peace be upon him, for twenty-eight years, ten of which were the dowry of his daughter Safira, daughter of Shu`ayb, and eighteen years he stayed with him until he had a child. Then you came according to the measure, O Moses, Muqatil said: According to an appointment. This appointment was not with Moses, but rather it was an appointment in God’s decree. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: You came according to the measure that I had estimated that you would come. Abdul Rahman bin Kaysan said: At the beginning of forty years, which is the amount of time in which revelation is sent to the prophets, and this is the meaning of what most commentators say, that is, at the time that God promised him and decreed that He would send him the message, which is forty years.
20:41: 41. The Almighty’s saying: And I have chosen you for Myself, meaning I have chosen you and selected you for My revelation and message, meaning that you would be directed to My will and love, and that is because his carrying out the message [is directed to] the will and love of God. Al-Zajjaj said: I chose you for my affair and made you the one who establishes my proof and the one who addresses me and my creation, as if I am the one who established the proof through you against them and addressed them.
20:42: 42. Go, you and your brother, with My signs, with My evidence. Ibn Abbas said: He means the nine signs with which Moses was sent. And do not slacken, do not be harsh. Al-Suddi said: Do not slacken. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: Do not fall short, in My remembrance.
20:43: 43. Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. Abu Amr and the people of Hijaz read: For myself, go, "My remembrance, go, and Indeed, my people have taken" (al-Furqan 25:30), "After me, his name" (al-Saff 61:6) with the opening of the yaa in them, and Abu Bakr agreed with them: "After me, his name, and the rest read it with the sukoon.
20:44: 44. So speak to him with gentle speech, meaning: Be gentle with him and be kind to him. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Do not be harsh in your speech. Al-Suddi and Ikrimah said: Give him a kunya, so say: O Abu Al-Abbas, and it was said: O Abu Al-Walid. Muqatil said: It means gentle speech: Would you like to be purified? And I will guide you to your Lord so that you may fear Him? (al-Nazi’at 79:18-19). It was said: He ordered kindness in speech because of the right of education. Al-Suddi said: The gentle saying is that Moses came to him and promised him, if he accepted the faith, a youth that would not grow old, and a kingdom that would not be taken away from him except by death, and that he would enjoy the pleasure of food, drink, and sex until his death, and if he died he would enter Paradise. This pleased him and he would not decide on a matter without Haman, who was absent. When he returned, he told him what Moses had called him to, and said, I wanted to accept it from him. Haman said to him, “I thought that you had a mind and an opinion. You are a lord, do you want to be worshipped? And you worship, do you want to be worshipped?” So he changed his mind. At that time, Aaron was in Egypt, so God commanded Moses to go to Aaron and revealed to Aaron while he was in Egypt to meet Moses, so he met him a stage away and told him what was revealed to him. Perhaps he will remember or fear, meaning: he will be admonished and fear and thus be safe. If it is said: How did he say: Perhaps he will remember, when he knew beforehand that he would not remember and would not submit? It was said: It means go with hope and desire, and God’s decree is behind your matter. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: It refers to someone other than Pharaoh. Its meaning is: Perhaps someone who remembers will remember, and someone who fears will fear when he sees the kindness and goodness of the one whom You created and bestowed blessings upon, then he claims divinity. Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Omar Al-Warraq said: Perhaps from God is obligatory, and Pharaoh remembered and feared when remembrance and fear did not benefit him, and that was when he was drowning. He said: I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am one of the Muslims. A man read this verse to Yahya bin Muadh: So speak to him with gentle speech. Yahya wept and said: My God, this is Your gentleness with the one who says, I am God, so how is Your gentleness with the one who says, You are God?!
20:45: 45. They said, meaning Moses and Aaron: Our Lord, indeed we fear that he will hasten upon us, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: He will hasten upon us killing and punishment. It is said: So-and-so hastened upon him if he hastened to do something bad, and he hastened upon something, meaning he did it quickly and outdid it, or that he will transgress, meaning he will exceed the limit in harming us.
20:46: 46. He said, 'Do not fear, for I am with you, hearing and seeing.' Ibn Abbas said: I hear your supplication and answer it, and I see what is intended for you and prevent it. I am not unaware of you, so do not worry.
20:47: 47. So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord,' meaning, we have been sent to you, so send with us the Children of Israel, meaning, leave them alone and release them from your work, and do not torment them, meaning, do not tire them out with work. Pharaoh used to employ them in hard work, We have come to you with a sign from your Lord, Pharaoh said: What is it? So he held out his hand, which had rays like the rays of the sun, "and peace be upon those who follow the guidance," meaning, it does not mean greeting, but rather it means, whoever submits is safe from the punishment of God.
20:48: 48. Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away. God only punishes those who deny what We have brought and turn away from it.
20:49: 49. He said, 'Who is your Lord, O Moses?' Who is your God who sent you?
20:50: 50. He said, ‘Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided it.’ Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He gave each thing its goodness and guided it to what is good for it. Mujahed said: He gave everything its image. He did not make the creation of man like the creation of animals, nor the creation of animals like the creation of man. Then He guided him to his benefits of food, drink, and sexual intercourse. Ad-Dahhak said: “He gave each thing its creation: meaning the hand for grip, the foot for walking, the tongue for speech, the eye for sight, and the ear for hearing. Saeed bin Jubair said: “He gave each thing its creation”: meaning a pair, for man the woman, for camels the she-camel, for donkeys the female donkey, and for horses the male ram. Then He guided: meaning He inspired him with how the male approaches the female.
20:51: 51. "Pharaoh said: 'What about the previous generations?' The meaning of the state" is: the condition, meaning: What is the condition of the past generations and the bygone nations, such as the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud, in what you are calling me to, for they used to worship idols and deny the resurrection?
20:52: 52. He said, Moses: The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, meaning: Their deeds are preserved with God and He will reward them. It was said: Moses attributed the knowledge of that to God because he did not know that, as the Torah was revealed after the destruction of Pharaoh and his people. In a Book, meaning: in the Preserved Tablet. My Lord does not err, meaning: He does not make mistakes. It was also said: Nothing goes astray from Him nor is He absent from anything. Nor does He forget, [meaning: He does not make mistakes] what happened to them until He rewards them for their deeds. It was also said: He does not forget, meaning: He does not leave, so He takes revenge on the disbeliever and rewards the believer.
20:53: 53. "Who made the earth a cradle for you." The people of Kufa read: "a cradle" here, and in Az-Zukhruf, so it is a source, meaning: a bed. The others read: "a cradle," like the Almighty's saying: "Have We not made the earth a cradle?" An-Naba' 16, meaning: a bed, and it is the name of what is spread out, like a carpet: the name of what is spread out. And He made paths easy for you therein [Path means to insert something into something, and the meaning is: He inserted paths into the earth for you to follow]. Ibn Abbas said: He made paths easy for you therein for you to follow. And He sends down water from the sky, meaning: rain. Moses was told about, then God told about Himself by saying: Then We brought forth with it, with that water, pairs, kinds, of diverse plants, of different colors, tastes, and benefits, including white, red, green, and yellow. So each kind of it is a pair, some for people and some for animals.
20:54: 54. Eat and graze [i.e., graze] your livestock. The Arabs say: I grazed the sheep and let them graze, i.e., let your livestock graze. Indeed in that, which I mentioned, are signs for those of understanding, for those with reason. Its singular is prohibition. It is called prohibition because it forbids its owner from evil deeds and sins. Ad-Dahhak said: For those of understanding: those who refrain from what is forbidden to them. Qatada said: For the pious.
20:55: 55. From it meaning from the earth, We created you, meaning your father Adam. Ata Al-Khurasani said: The angel sets out and takes some of the soil from the place where he will be buried and sprinkles it on the sperm, and God creates from the soil and the sperm. This is what God Almighty says: From it We created you, and into it We will return you, meaning: at death and burial, and from it We will extract you another time, on the Day of Resurrection.
20:56: 56. The Almighty said: And We showed him, meaning Pharaoh, all of Our signs, meaning the nine signs that God gave Moses, but he denied them, and claimed that they were magic, and refused, to submit.
20:57: 57. He said, meaning Pharaoh, Have you come to us to expel us from our land, meaning Egypt, with your magic, O Moses, meaning: You want to conquer our lands so that you will have the kingdom and expel us from it.
20:58: 58. So we will bring you magic like it, so make an appointment between us and you, meaning: set a term and a time between us, we will not fail it, [Abu Ja`far read we will not fail it in the subjunctive mood, we will not exceed it], We and you are in a place apart, Ibn `Amir, `Asim, Hamza and Ya`qub read: sawaw with a damma on the seen, and the others read it with a kasra, and they are two dialects like `Ada and `Ada and Tuwa and Tuwa. Muqatil and Qatada said: A just place between us and you. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: Half, and its meaning is: the distance between the two groups is equal to it. Mujahed said: Fair. Al-Kalbi said: He means other than this place.
20:59: 59. He said, 'Your appointment is on the Day of Adornment.' Mujahid, Qatada, Muqatil, and Al-Suddi said: It was a day of celebration for them, on which they would adorn themselves and gather every year. It was also said: It was the Day of Nowruz. Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Jubair said: The day of Ashura. And that the people will be gathered at noon, meaning: at noon, during the day, in broad daylight, so that it will be further from suspicion.
20:60: 60. So Pharaoh turned and gathered his plot, his cunning, his tricks, and his magic, then he came, the appointed time.
20:61: 61. Moses said to them, meaning: to the magicians whom Pharaoh had gathered, and they were seventy-two magicians, each one of whom had a rope and a staff. It was said: They were four hundred. Kaab said: They were twelve thousand. It was said more than that. Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against God, lest He destroy you with a punishment. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read fisahtakum with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the ha’. The rest read it with a fatha on the ya’ and the ha’, and these are two dialects. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: He will destroy you. Qatada said: He will uproot you. “And he who invents lies has failed.”
20:62: 62. So they disputed their affair among themselves, meaning: they debated and consulted, meaning the magicians, about the matter of Moses secretly from Pharaoh. Al-Kalbi said: They said secretly: If we defeat Moses, we will follow him. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When Moses said to them: Do not fabricate lies against God, some of them said to each other: This is not the words of a magician. And they whispered secretly, meaning the intimate conversation, can be a source and a noun.
20:63: 63. Then they said, whispering to one another: These two are magicians, meaning Moses and Aaron. Ibn Kathir and Hafs read: Indeed with a light nun, “these two” meaning these two are nothing but magicians, like His statement: Indeed, we think you are among the liars (Ash-Shu’ara’: 186), meaning we think you are nothing but among the liars. Ibn Kathir stresses the nun in these two. Abu Amr read in with emphasis on the nun and thana with a ya according to the original. Others read: in with emphasis on the nun, “hadhan” with an alif, and they differed about it. Hisham bin Urwah narrated, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha: that it was a mistake by the writer. Some people said: This is the language of Al-Harith bin Ka’b, Khatham, and Kinanah, as they make the dual nouns in the nominative, accusative, and genitive with an alif. They say: The two Zayds came to me [and I saw the two Zayds] and I passed by the two Zayds. [They do not leave] the alif of the dual in any of it. Likewise, they make every silent ya’ that has a fatha before it an alif, as in the dual. They say: I broke his hands and rode him, meaning his hands and him. And their poet said: He was provided with a blow between his ears that made him wander the dust barren. He wants between his ears. Another said: Her father and her father's father have reached the peak of glory. It was said: The meaning of the verse is: These two, so the letter ha was deleted. A group of people said that the letter an here means yes, i.e. yes, these two. It was narrated that a Bedouin asked Ibn al-Zubayr for something and he forbade it, so he said: May God curse the she-camel that carried me to you. Ibn al-Zubayr said: In and its owner, i.e. yes. The poet said: Early in the morning, my critics came to me and I blamed them They say, "Grey hair has covered you, and you have grown old. I said, It is..." I mean: Yes.. They want to expel you from your land, Egypt, with their magic and do away with your best way, Ibn Abbas said: He means the leaders and nobles of your people. It is said: These are the way of their people, meaning their nobles. The best is the feminine of the best, which is the best. Al-Sha’bi narrated on the authority of Ali, who said: They turn people’s faces towards them. Qatada said: Their best way is their best way. On that day, the Children of Israel were the most numerous and wealthy of the people. So the enemy of God said: They want to take them for themselves. It was said: In your best way: meaning, according to your Sunnah and religion that you follow, and best is an adjective for the way. The Arabs say: So-and-so is on the best way, meaning: on the straight path.
20:64: 64. So assemble your plot, Abu Amr read: So assemble by connecting the alif and opening the meem, from the word gather, meaning do not leave anything of your plot without bringing it about, as evidenced by his statement: (So assemble his plot), and the others read it by cutting the alif and breaking the meem. It has been said: its meaning is also to gather, the Arabs say: I gathered the thing and I gathered it, meaning one thing. The correct meaning is determination and firmness, i.e., all of you resolve to plot against him together, and do not differ, lest your matter be disrupted. Then come in a row, meaning all together, said Muqatil and Al-Kalbi. Some people said: meaning lined up and gathered together so that your awe will be greater. Abu Ubaidah said: The gathered row, and the place of prayer is called a row. Its meaning: Then come to the promised place. And today he who prevails will succeed, meaning: he who prevails will win.
20:65: 65. They said, meaning the magicians, O Moses, either you throw down, your staff, or we will be the first to throw down, our staff.
20:66: 66. "He said," Moses: "Rather, throw, you first, and behold, their ropes, and there is an implication in it, meaning, so throw, and behold, their ropes and their staffs, the plural of staff, appear to him, Ibn Amir and Yaqub read (imagined) with a ta' referring to the ropes and staffs, and the others read with a ya' referring it to the trick and magic, from their magic that it moves." In the story, when they threw the ropes and sticks, they took the people’s eyes. Moses and the people saw as if the earth was filled with snakes, and they had taken a mile on every side, and they saw that they were moving.
20:67: 67. "So Moses felt fear within himself," meaning he found, and it was said: he concealed fear within himself, and they differed regarding his fear: it was said: the fear of human nature, and that is because he thought that she was intending to target him. Muqatil said: He feared that the people would be confused about the matter and would doubt his command and not follow him.
20:68: 68. We said, to Moses: Do not fear, for you are the superior, meaning the victorious, meaning: you will have the upper hand and victory.
20:69: 69. "And throw down what is in your right hand, meaning the stick, and swallow - it grabs and swallows, what they made, Ibn Amir read (talqaf) with the raising of the fa here, and the others read it with the jazm as a response to the command, inma sana'u, that which they made, kayd sahir", meaning a magic trick, this is how Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it: with the kasra of the seen without an alif, and the others read: (sahir) because adding the trick to the subject is more appropriate than adding it to the verb, even though that is not forbidden in Arabic, "nor will the magician succeed wherever he comes", from the earth, Ibn Abbas said: he will not be happy wherever he is. It was said: its meaning is wherever he tricked.
20:70: 70. "So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, 'We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.'
20:71: 71. "He said, 'You have believed in him before I give you permission. Indeed, he is your chief,' that is, your leader and teacher, who taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment, me for believing in him, or the Lord of Moses for abandoning belief in him? "And more lasting, that is, more permanent.
20:72: 72. They said, meaning the magicians: We will not prefer you, meaning we will not choose you, over what has come to us of clear proofs, meaning the evidence. Muqatil said: meaning the white hand and the staff. It was said: Their argument was that if this was magic, then where were our ropes and sticks? It was said: From the clear proofs meaning from clarification and knowledge. Abu al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza narrated that he said: When they prostrated, they did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise and Hell, and saw the reward of its people, and saw their homes in Paradise. Then they said: We will not prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us. By Him Who created us, meaning: We will not prefer you over God Who created us. It was said: It is an oath. Then decide what you will decide, meaning: Do what you will do. You only decide this worldly life, meaning: Your affair and authority are in this world and will soon be gone.
20:73: 73. Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you forced us to do of magic. It was said: How did they say this, when they came willingly, swearing by the might of Pharaoh that they would be victorious? It was said: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hassan that he said: Pharaoh used to force some people to learn magic so that its origin would not be lost, and he was the most forbidding of them to begin with. Muqatil said: There were seventy-two magicians, two from the Copts and seventy from the Children of Israel. Pharaoh forced those from the Children of Israel to learn magic, so that is what they said: And you did not force us to do magic. Abdul Aziz bin Aban said: The magicians said to Pharaoh: Show us Moses when he sleeps. So he showed them Moses sleeping with his staff guarding him. They said to Pharaoh: This is not a magician. When a magician sleeps, his magic is nullified. But he refused to let them know. This is what God Almighty said: And you did not compel us to do magic. “And God is better and more lasting,” Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Better than you in reward, and more lasting in punishment. Muhammad bin Kaab said: He is better than you in reward if he obeys, and more lasting in punishment if he disobeys. This is an answer to his saying: And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting.
20:74: 74. Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, it was said: This is the beginning of a statement from God Almighty. It was said: It is part of the magicians' statement a criminal, meaning: a polytheist, meaning: he died as a polytheist, for him is Hell, where he will not die, so he will rest, nor will he live, a life from which he will benefit.
20:75: 75. And whoever comes to Him, Abu Amr reads the ha' with a sukoon, and Abu Ja'far, Qalun, and Ya'qub steal it, and the others read it with a sukoon, a believer, he died in faith, has done righteous deeds, so those will have the highest degrees, the lofty ones, the highest, plural, and (the highest) is the feminine of the highest.
20:76: 76. “Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. That is the reward of he who purifies himself.” That is, he is purified from sins. Al-Kalbi said: He gave zakat on his soul and said, There is no god but God. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Ubayd al-Sammar told us, Abu Ahmad Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Abbas al-Dahqan told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Attardi told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Atiyya, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of the highest ranks will be seen by those beneath them as you see a shining star in one of the horizons of the sky, and Abu Bakr and Umar are among them and they are blessed.
20:77: 77. The Almighty said: And We had already inspired Moses, ‘Travel with My servants by night’, meaning: Travel with them by night from the land of Egypt, and strike for them a path through the sea, meaning make a path for them through the sea by striking with a stick, dry, dry, with no water or mud in it, because God made the path dry for them through the sea, do not fear being overtaken, Hamza read (do not fear) with the jussive mood as a prohibition, and the rest read it with the alif and the nominative mood as a negation, because the Almighty said: and do not fear, it was said: do not fear that Pharaoh will overtake you from behind, and do not fear that the sea will drown you in front of you.
20:78: 78. "So he followed them, so he caught up with them, Pharaoh with his soldiers", and it was said: its meaning is that Pharaoh ordered his soldiers to follow Moses and his people, and the "ba in it is redundant and he was among them, so he covered them, he afflicted them, from the sea that which covered them", which is drowning. [And it was said: he covered them means that some of the sea's water covered them and concealed them, not all of it]. It was said: They were overwhelmed by the same sea that overwhelmed the people of Moses, so they drowned, but Moses and his people were saved.
20:79: 79. And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them, meaning: he did not guide them, and this is a denial of Pharaoh’s treatment of his people. And I do not guide you except to the path of right conduct Ghafir-29.
20:80: 80. The Almighty said: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, Pharaoh, and We made an appointment with you on the right side of the Mount and sent down to you manna and quails.
20:81: 81. "Eat from the good things that We have provided for you." Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read: (Anjitkum), (Wa'adtkum), and (Razaktkum) with the ta' for the sake of singularity, and the others read it with the nun and the alif for the sake of glorification, and they did not differ about Wa-Nazlna because it is written with the alif. And do not transgress therein. Ibn Abbas said: Do not be unjust. Al-Kalbi said: Do not be ungrateful for the blessing, lest you become transgressors. It was said: Do not spend in disobedience to Me. It was said: Do not hoard, then hoard and it will worm, it will be destroyed, Al-A’mash and Al-Kisa’i read: (it will be destroyed) with a damma on the ha’, (and whoever descends) with a damma on the lam, meaning: he descends, and the others read it with a kasra, meaning: it is necessary, upon you is My wrath, and whoever descends upon Him is My wrath has fallen, he has perished and fallen into the fire.
20:82: 82. And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, Ibn Abbas said: repents from polytheism, and believes, and believes in the Oneness of God and confirms Him, and does righteousness, performs the obligatory duties, and then is guided, Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He knows that this is a success from God. Qatada and Sufyan al-Thawri said: It means he adhered to Islam until he died upon it. Al-Sha’bi, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: He knew that there was a reward for that. Zaid bin Aslam said: Learn knowledge to be guided by it in how to act. Ad-Dahhak said: He remained steadfast. Saeed bin Jubair said: He adhered to the Sunnah and the community.
20:83: 83. And what made you hasten, meaning: what made you hasten, from your people, that is, Moses chose seventy men from his people to go with him to the mountain, to take the Torah, so he went with them and then he was hastened to Moses from among them out of longing for his Lord, the Almighty, the Majestic, and he left the seventy, and ordered them to follow him to the mountain, so God Almighty said to him: And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?
20:84: 84. He said, answering his Lord Almighty: They are on my heels, meaning: they are close to me and will come after me, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You might be pleased, that is, to increase Your pleasure.
20:85: 85. He said, 'We have indeed tried your people after you,' meaning: We tested those whom you left behind with Aaron, and they were six hundred thousand, and they were tempted by the calf, except for twelve thousand, after you, meaning: after you went to the mountain, and the Samaritan led them astray, meaning: He called them and turned them towards worshipping the calf and attributed it to the Samaritan because they went astray because of him.
20:86: 86. "So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved," sad. "He said, 'O my people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise,' meaning that He would truly give you the Torah, was the covenant prolonged for you, meaning the period of my separation from you, or did you desire that the wrath of your Lord should descend upon you,'" meaning: did you desire to do an act that would necessitate the wrath of your Lord upon you, "but you broke your promise to me?
20:87: 87. "They said, 'We did not fail to meet you by our own power.'" Nafi', Abu Ja'far, and Asim read: "by our own power with the mim open, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with the damma, and the others read it with the kasra", meaning: We control our own affairs. It was said: By our choice, and whoever read it with the "damma" then its meaning is by our power and authority, and that is because when a person falls into a calamity and a trial he does not control himself. But we carried, Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Abu Bakr, and Ya’qub read: (hamalna) with the ha’ open and the mim soft. The others read it with the ha’ closed and the mim doubled, meaning: they made us carry it and charged us with carrying it, burdens of the people’s adornments, from the jewelry of Pharaoh’s people. He called them burdens because they took them as a loan and did not return them. This is because the Children of Israel had borrowed jewelry from the Copts, and that was with them when they left Egypt. It was said: When God Almighty drowned Pharaoh, the sea threw up their jewelry and they took it, and it was spoils, and spoils were not permissible for them at that time, so He called them burdens for that reason. "So we threw it, it was said that the Samaritan said to them, Dig a hole and throw it into it until Moses returns." Al-Suddi said: Aaron said to them: This is spoils of war that are not permissible, so dig a hole and throw them into it until Moses returns and decides what he thinks about it. So they did. His statement: So we threw it means: we threw it into the hole. Likewise the Samaritan threw meaning what he had of jewelry into it. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: Aaron lit a fire and said: Throw into it what you have, so they threw it into it. Then the Samaritan threw what he had of dirt from the hoof of Gabriel’s horse that he had with him. Qatada said: He had taken a handful of that dirt in his turban.
20:88: 88. So he brought out for them a calf with a body that mooed, and they said, 'This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot.' That is, Moses left it here and went looking for it. It was also said that he lost his way and went astray.
20:89: 89. God Almighty said: Do they not see that it does not return to them a word? That is, they do not see that the calf does not speak to them or answer them if they call upon it, nor does it possess for them any harm or benefit. It was said that Aaron passed by the Samaritan while he was making the calf and said to him: What is this? He said: I make what benefits and does not harm, so pray for me. Aaron said: O God, give him what he asked for based on what is in his soul. So he threw dirt into the calf's mouth and said: Be a calf that bellows like that at the prayer of Aaron. The truth is that this was a trial with which God afflicted the Children of Israel.
20:90: 90. And Aaron had said to them before, before Moses returned, O my people, you are only being tested by it, you were tested by the calf, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me, in my religion in worshipping God, and obey my command, in abandoning the worship of the calf.
20:91: 91. They said, 'We will not cease,' meaning, we will not stop, 'dedicating ourselves to it,' in worshipping it, 'remaining,' 'until Moses returns to us.' So Aaron withdrew from them with twelve thousand of those who did not worship the calf. When Moses returned and heard the shouting and the commotion and they were dancing around the calf, he said to the seventy who were with him, 'This is the sound of the tribulation.' When Aaron saw it, he took hold of the hair of his head with his right hand and his beard with his left.
20:92: 92. "He said, 'O Aaron, what prevented you when you saw them going astray?'" They associated partners with God.
20:93: 93. That you do not follow, meaning: that you follow me, and do not is a conjunction, meaning that you follow my command and my will, meaning: Why did you not fight them, knowing that if I were among them, I would fight them for their disbelief. It was said: That you do not follow me, meaning: What prevented you from joining me and informing me of their misguidance, so that your separation from them would be a deterrent to them from what they did? Did you disobey my command? meaning did you go against my command.
20:94: 94. "He said, 'O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head,' meaning by the hair of my head and he had taken its forelocks, 'I feared', if I denied them they would become two parties killing each other, 'that you would say, You have divided the Children of Israel, meaning I feared that if I left them and followed you they would become parties fighting each other, and you would say, You have divided the Children of Israel, and you did not observe my word, and you did not keep my command when I said to you, Take my place among my people, and reform, meaning be gentle with them. Then Moses turned to the Samaritan.
20:95: 95. He said, 'What is the matter with you?' What is your affair and your condition? What made you do what you did? 'O Samaritan.'
20:96: 96. He said, 'I saw what they did not see.' I saw what they did not see, I knew what they did not see, and I knew what they did not know. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: By what they did not see with the letter ta’ as an address, while the others read it with the letter ya’ as a report. So I took a handful from the trace of the Messenger, meaning from the dust of Gabriel’s trace, and threw it, meaning I threw it into the calf’s mouth. Some of them said: He only appeared because the dust was taken from under the hoof of Gabriel’s horse. If it is said: How did he recognize him and see Gabriel among all the other people? It was said: Because when his mother gave birth to him in the year in which the sons were killed, she placed him in the cave to protect him, so God sent Gabriel to raise him because of the strife he caused at his hands. And so it has made my soul beautiful, that is, it has adorned it, for me.
20:97: 97. "He said, 'Then go, for you have in life' - that is, as long as you are alive - 'to say, 'Do not touch' - that is, do not mix with anyone, and no one will mix with you.' And Moses, son of Israel, was commanded not to mix with him, nor to come near him. Ibn Abbas said: You and your father are not to be touched. Masas comes from mamasa, meaning: we do not touch each other. So the Samaritan wandered in the wilderness with the wild animals and beasts, neither touching any of us nor being touched by anyone. God punished him with that, and whenever he met someone he would say lammasas, meaning do not come near me and do not touch me. It was said: If he touched someone or someone touched him, they would all get a fever, to the point that even their remnants today say that. And if someone other than them touched one of them, they would all get a fever at the same time. And indeed, you have, O Samaritan, an appointment for your punishment, which you will not fail to fulfill. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read: which you will not fail to fulfill with a kasra on the lam, meaning you will not be absent from him, nor will you be able to leave him, but you will meet him on the Day of Resurrection. The others read with a fatha on the lam, meaning you will not lie to him and God will not fail you. Its meaning is that God Almighty will reward you for your action and you will not miss it. And look at your god, you claim, to whom you have remained devoted, meaning you have remained devoted to Him, worshipping Him. The Arabs say: I continued to do such-and-such, meaning I remained, and I touched means I touched. We will burn it, with fire. Abu Ja`far read it with a lightened burning. Then we will blow it away, to scatter it, into the sea, in the sea, blown away. It was narrated that Moses took the calf and slaughtered it, and blood flowed from it, because it had become flesh and blood. Then he burned it with fire, and from this the burnt threshing floor was called al-Muharr. Al-Suddi said: Moses took the calf, then burned it with the threshing floor, then scattered it in the sea.
20:98: 98. “Your God is only God, other than whom there is no god. His knowledge encompasses all things.” His knowledge encompasses all things.
20:99: 99. Thus do We relate to you some of the report of what has already occurred, of matters, and We have given you from Ourselves a reminder, meaning the Qur’an.
20:100: 100. Whoever turns away from it, meaning: from the Qur’an, and does not believe in it or act upon what is in it, will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection, a heavy load of sin.
20:101: 101. They will abide therein eternally, residing in the torment of sin, and evil will be their burden on the Day of Resurrection, meaning evil is the sin they have taken upon themselves out of disbelief in the Qur’an.
20:102: 102. "On the Day the Trumpet is Blown, Abu Amr read Blows" with a noon and a fatha and a damma on the fa', because of the statement: "And We will gather them, and the others read it with a ya' and a damma on the fa' without naming the subject, And We will gather the criminals, the polytheists, On that Day blue", and blueness is the greenness: in the blackness of the eye, so they will be gathered blue-eyed and black-faced. It was said: "blue" means blind. It was said: thirsty.
20:103: 103. "They whisper among themselves, meaning they consult among themselves and speak secretly, If you remain, meaning how long you remain in this world, except ten," meaning ten nights. And it was said: in the graves. And it was said: in the two blasts, which is forty years, because the punishment is lifted from them between the two blasts. They considered the length of their stay short because of the horror of what they witnessed.
20:104: 104. God Almighty said: We know best what they say, meaning what they discuss among themselves, when the best of them in conduct says, the most perfect of them in mind and the most just of them in speech, You have only remained a day, shortening that in their eyes compared to the horrors that await them on the Day of Resurrection. It was said: They forgot the length of time they had remained because of the severity of what had befallen them.
20:105: 105. The Almighty said: “And they ask you about the mountains. Say, ‘My Lord will blow them away with a blast.’” Ibn Abbas said: A man from Thaqeef asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: How will the mountains be on the Day of Resurrection? Then God revealed this verse. Blasting is uprooting, meaning he uproots it from its roots and turns it into scattered dust.
20:106: 106. He will leave it, meaning he will leave the places of the mountains on the earth, a flat, level plain, meaning a smooth, level land with no vegetation. The flat plain means the flat part of the earth, and the smooth plain means the smooth.
20:107: 107. You will not see therein any crookedness or unevenness. Mujahid said: lowness or highness. Al-Hasan said: Al-Awj is the low part of the land, and Al-Amat is the elevated part of the hills, meaning: you do not see a valley or a hill. Qatada said: You will not see any crack or hill in it.
20:108: 108. On that Day they will follow the Caller, meaning the voice of the Caller who calls them to the place of Resurrection, and he is Israfil, and he places the trumpets in his mouth and says: O decayed bones, torn skins, and scattered flesh, come to the presence of the Most Merciful. There is no crookedness in it, meaning: in his supplication, and it is from the inverted, meaning: there is no crookedness for them in the supplication of the supplicant, they do not deviate from it to the right or to the left, nor are they able to do it, but rather they follow it quickly. And the voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, meaning: they will be still, humbled, and submissive. He described the voices as being hushed, meaning their people, so you will hear nothing but a whisper, meaning the sound of feet trampling on the Day of Resurrection. Whispering is a low sound like the sound of camels’ hooves when walking. Mujahid said: It is the softening of speech and lowering of the voice. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Moving the lips without speaking.
20:109: 109. On that Day, no intercession will benefit, meaning: no intercession will benefit anyone among the people, except for him whom the Most Merciful has given permission, meaning: except for him whom He has given permission to intercede, and whose word He is pleased with, meaning: and whose word He is pleased with. Ibn Abbas said: meaning: he said, There is no god but God, and this indicates that no one will intercede except the believer.
20:110: 110. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, the metaphor refers to those who follow the caller, meaning God knows what is before them, what they have put forward, and what is behind them, what they have left behind of worldly matters. It was said: What is before them of the Hereafter and what is behind them of deeds. And they do not encompass Him in knowledge. It was said: The metaphor refers to what, meaning: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not know Him. It was also said: The metaphor refers to God because His servants do not encompass Him in knowledge.
20:111: 111. And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, they will be submissive and humbled, and from this the prisoner is called: ‘Aan. Talq bin Habib said: It is prostrating on the forehead before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. And he has failed who bears injustice, Ibn Abbas said: He has lost who associates partners with God, and injustice is polytheism.
20:112: 112. And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, he will not fear, Ibn Kathir read he will not fear in the subjunctive mood as a response to the Almighty's statement: And whoever does, and the others read he will not fear in the nominative case as a predicate, of injustice or oppression, Ibn Abbas said: He will not fear that his bad deeds will be increased, nor will his good deeds be decreased. Al-Hassan said: His good deeds will not be diminished, nor will he be held accountable for the sin of a wrongdoer. Ad-Dahhak said: He will not be held accountable for a sin he did not commit, nor will a good deed he did be invalidated. The root of digestion is: decrease and breakage, and from it comes the digestion of food.
20:113: 113. And likewise, that is, as we explained in this surah, We have sent it down, that is, We sent down this book, as an Arabic Qur’an, that is, in the language of the Arabs, and We have diversified therein the warning, that is, We diversified therein the mention of the warning, that they may fear God, that is, avoid polytheism, or cause them to be reminded, that is, the Qur’an may renew for them a lesson and admonition so that they may consider and be admonished by mentioning God’s punishment of the past nations.
20:114: 114. So exalted is God, the True King, God is far above the heresy of the heretics and what the polytheists say, And do not hasten with the Qur'an, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when Gabriel came down to him with the Qur'an, he would rush to recite with him, before Gabriel finished what he wanted to recite, and for fear of slipping away and forgetting, so God forbade him from that, and said: And do not hasten with the Qur'an meaning do not hasten to recite it before its revelation is completed to you, meaning before Gabriel finishes conveying it, similar to the saying of God the Almighty: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it Surat Al-Qiyamah-16 and Ya'qub read: Yaqdi with the letter noon and its fatha and the letter dad with the kasra, and the letter ya with the fatha: His revelation, in the accusative. Mujahid and Qatada said: Its meaning is do not recite it to your companions, and do not dictate it to them until its meanings become clear to you. “And say, ‘My Lord, increase me in knowledge,’ meaning the Qur’an and its meanings. It was also said: knowledge in addition to what you have learned. When Ibn Masoud read this verse, he would say: O God, Lord, increase my knowledge, faith, and certainty.
20:115: 115. The Almighty’s saying: And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, meaning: We commanded him and inspired him not to eat from the tree before those who broke Your covenant and abandoned belief in Me, and they are the ones mentioned by God in His saying: Perhaps they will become righteous, “but he forgot” so he abandoned the command, and the meaning is that they broke the covenant, for Adam also had a covenant with Us and he forgot, and We found on his part no firm resolve, Al-Hasan said: We found on his part no patience for what he was forbidden from. And Atiyah Al-Awfi said: To preserve what he was commanded to do. Ibn Qutaybah said: A determined opinion, as he obeyed his enemy, Satan, who envied him and refused to prostrate to him. In the language, determination means: making oneself determined to do something. Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: If Adam’s dream was weighed against the dreams of all his children, his dream would be heavier, and God said: And We found on his part no firm resolve. If it is said: Do you say that Adam forgot God’s command when he ate from the tree? It was said: It is possible that he forgot about it, and forgetfulness at that time was not lifted from a person, rather he was held accountable for it, but it was lifted from us. It was said: He forgot God’s punishment and thought that it was a prohibition as a sign of purity.
20:116: 116. The Almighty said: And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ they prostrated, except for Iblis, who refused, to prostrate.
20:117: 117. "So We said, 'O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife' - Eve, so do not let him expel you both from Paradise and you become miserable - meaning: you become tired and exhausted, and your livelihood is from the toil of your right hand by the sweat of your brow. Al-Suddi said: It means plowing, planting, harvesting, grinding, and baking. On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: He said: A red bull descended to Adam, and he used to plow on it and wipe the sweat from its forehead, and that was his misery. He did not say: They were both exhausted in order to return him to Adan, because his effort was greater, as the man is the one who seeks his wife. It was said: for the heads of the verses.
20:118: 118. You will not go hungry therein, meaning in Paradise, nor will you be naked.
20:119: 119. And that you, Nafi' and Abu Bakr read with a kasra on the alif as a new beginning, and the others read with a fatha in agreement with his saying: that you will not be hungry therein, and that you will not be thirsty, nor will you be exposed to the sun, meaning: do not go out into the sun so that its heat will harm you. And Ikrimah said: The sun and its harm will not affect you, because there is no sun in Paradise, and its people are in extended shade.
20:120: 120. Then Satan whispered to him, saying, ‘O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of immortality?’ meaning a tree from which if you eat from it you will remain immortal, and a kingdom that will not decay, that will not perish or end.
20:121: 121. So they ate, meaning Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, “from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord,” by eating from the tree, and went astray, meaning he did what he was not supposed to do. It was said: he lost his way to Paradise and went astray when he sought immortality by eating what he was forbidden to eat, but he was disappointed and did not achieve his goal. Ibn Al-A'rabi said: That is, his life was ruined, and he went from glory to humiliation, and from comfort to fatigue. Ibn Qutaybah said: It is permissible to say Adam disobeyed, but it is not permissible to say Adam is a disobedient person, because it is only said disobedient for someone who is accustomed to doing sins, like a man who sews his clothes, it is said he sewed his clothes, but it is not said he is a tailor until he does that again and gets used to it. Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi told us, Abu Muadh al-Shah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Muzani told us, Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Naysaburi told us in Baghdad, Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la al-Sadfi told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Tawus, who heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Adam and Moses argued. Moses said: ‘O Adam, you are our father who let us down and expelled us from Paradise.’ Adam said: ‘O Moses, God chose you to speak to him and wrote the Torah for you with His hand. Do you blame me for something that God decreed for me forty years before He created me?’ So Adam argued with Moses.” And Abd al-Rahman al-A’raj narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and he added: “Adam said, ‘O Moses, how long did you find that God wrote the Torah before I was created?’ Moses said, ‘Forty years.’ Adam said, ‘Did you find in it: And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Do you blame me for doing a deed that God wrote for me to do forty years before He created me?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘So Adam argued with Moses.’”
20:122: 122. Then his Lord chose him, he chose him and selected him, and turned to him in forgiveness, with pardon, and guided him, he guided him to repentance when they said: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves.
20:123: 123. "He said, 'Descend from it, all of you, as enemies to one another. And if there comes to you guidance from Me - whoever follows My guidance - will neither go astray nor suffer.'" Saeed bin Jabr narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Whoever recites the Qur'an and follows what is in it, God will guide him from misguidance in this world, and God will protect him on the Day of Resurrection from a bad reckoning, because God says: "So whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer." Al-Sha’bi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: God Almighty protected the follower of the Qur’an from going astray in this world and being miserable in the hereafter, and he recited this verse.
20:124: 124. And whoever turns away from My remembrance, meaning: the Qur’an, and does not believe in it or follow it, then indeed, he will have a depressed life, narrow, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Abu Hurairah, and Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that they said: It is the torment of the grave. Abu Saeed said: It is squeezed until his ribs overlap. In some Musnads, it is narrated on the authority of the Prophet: The grave will close around him until his ribs interlock, and he will continue to be tormented until he is resurrected. Al-Hasan said: It is Zaqqum, Dharee’ and Ghaslain in the Fire. Ikrimah said: It is the forbidden. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the filthy earnings. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Misery. It was narrated on his authority that he said: All wealth that a servant is given, whether little or much, and he does not fear God with it, there is no good in it, and it is hardship in living. And there are people who turned away from the truth and they were people of plenty in this world, so their living was hard, and that is because they saw that God would not replace it for them, so their living became difficult for them because of their bad opinion of God. Saeed bin Jubair said: It deprives him of contentment until he is never satisfied. And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. Ibn Abbas said: Blind of sight. Mujahid said: Blind of the argument.
20:125: 125. He said, ‘My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was seeing?’ With the eye or seeing with the argument.
20:126: 126. "He said, 'Likewise,' meaning just as 'Our signs came to you and you forgot them,' so you abandoned them and turned away from them, 'likewise today you will be forgotten.' You will be left in the Fire. Qatada said: They forgot the good but they did not forget the punishment.
20:127: 127. And thus, that is, just as We rewarded those who turned away from the Qur’an, so do We reward those who transgressed, who associated others with God, “and did not believe in the signs of their Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe,” that is, what He will punish them with in this world and in the grave, and more lasting, and more lasting.
20:128: 128. Have they not been guided, the Qur'an explains to them, meaning: the infidels of Mecca, how many generations before them We destroyed who walked in their dwellings, their homes and houses when they traveled. The address is to the Quraysh who used to travel to the Levant and see the homes of the destroyed people of Al-Hijr, Thamud, and the villages of Lot. Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding, for those of reason.
20:129: 129. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable and a term appointed, in it there is an advancement and a delay, the meaning is: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, but it would have been inevitable and a term appointed, and the word is the ruling to delay the punishment from them, meaning and had it not been for a ruling that preceded to delay the punishment from them and a term appointed, which is the resurrection, it would have been inevitable, meaning the punishment would not have been inevitable for them as it was inevitable for the past generations of disbelievers.
20:130: 130. So be patient over what they say, abrogated by the verse on fighting, and glorify the praises of your Lord, meaning pray to God and grant him peace by the command of your Lord. It was said: pray to God with praise and thanks to Him, before the rising of the sun, meaning the dawn prayer, and before its setting, meaning the afternoon prayer, and during the hours of the night, its hours, the singular of which is inni, "so glorify," meaning the sunset and evening prayers. Ibn Abbas said: He means the beginning of the night, "and the ends of the day," meaning the noon prayer, and the time of noon was called the ends of the day because its time is at noon, and it is the end of the first half and the beginning of the end of the other half. It was said: What is meant by the hours of the night is the Isha prayer, and what is meant by the ends of the day is the Dhuhr and Maghrib prayers, because Dhuhr is at the end of the first end of the day, and at the beginning of the other end, so it is at two ends of it and the third end is sunset, and at that time the Maghrib prayer is performed. "Perhaps you will be satisfied", meaning that you will be satisfied with his reward in the Hereafter. Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim (tar-dhi) with a damma on the ta', meaning that you will be given his reward. It was said: "tar-dhi" means that God the Most High will be satisfied with you, as He said: "And he was pleasing to his Lord" (Maryam 19:55). It was also said: The meaning of the verse is perhaps that you will be satisfied with the intercession, as He said: "And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied" (al-Duha 93:5). Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Abbas Al-Khatib Al-Hamidi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yaqoub Al-Shaibani told us by dictation, Ibrahim bin Abdullah Al-Saadi told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of Jarir bin Abdullah, who said: “We were sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: You will see your Lord as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in prayer before sunrise and before sunset, then do so.” Then he recited: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting.
20:131: 131. God the Almighty said: And do not extend your eyes. Abu Rafi’ said: “A guest came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he sent me to a Jew and said to me: ‘Tell him that the Messenger of God says to you: Sell me such and such flour and lend me until the crescent of Rajab.’ So I went to him and said that to him, and he said: ‘By God, I will not sell it or lend it to him except with a pledge.’ So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him, and he said: ‘By God, if he sells it to me and lends me, I will repay him, and I am trustworthy in heaven and trustworthy on earth. Go to him with my iron armor.’ So this verse was revealed: ‘And do not extend your eyes,’ do not look, ‘at what We have given for enjoyment,’ ‘in pairs,’ ‘of them is the flower of the life of this world,’ meaning its adornment and delight. Ya’qub read ‘flower’ with the opening of the ha’, while the general public read it with the jazm, ‘to test them therein,’ meaning to make that a trial for them by increasing their blessings so that they will increase in disbelief and transgression, ‘and the provision of your Lord,’ in the afterlife, meaning Paradise, ‘is better and more lasting.’ Abu Ibn Kaab: He who does not seek comfort in the glory of God will be torn apart with regrets. He who follows his sight to what is in the hands of people will lose his sadness. He who thinks that God’s blessing is in his food, drink, and clothing will have little knowledge and his punishment will be imminent.
20:132: 132. And enjoin prayer upon your family, meaning your people. It was also said: whoever follows your religion, as God Almighty said: And he used to enjoin prayer upon his family (Maryam 19:55), And be steadfast therein, meaning be steadfast in prayer, for it forbids immorality and wrongdoing.
