We do not ask you for provision, that is, We do not charge you to provide for any of Our creation, nor to provide for yourself. Rather, We charge you with work. We provide for you, and the final outcome, that is, the beautiful, praiseworthy conclusion, is for the righteous, that is, for the people of righteousness. Ibn Abbas said: Those who believed in you, followed you, and feared Me. In some Musnads, it is mentioned that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was afflicted with harm, he would pray and recite this verse.
20:133: 133. The Almighty said: And they said, meaning the polytheists, Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord? meaning the proposed sign, for he had already brought them many signs. Did there not come to them a clear proof? The people of Medina, Basra, and Hafs from Asim read: came to them to feminize the proof, and the others read it with the letter ya because the verb came first, and because the proof is the explanation, it was returned to the meaning, a proof of what is in the former scriptures, meaning an explanation of what is in it, and it is the Qur’an, the strongest in meaning and the clearest sign. It was said: Did not the explanation of what was in the first scriptures come to them: the Torah, the Gospel, and other report of the nations that they proposed the signs, and when they came to them they did not believe in them, how We hastened for them the punishment and destruction, so what assures them that if the sign comes to them their condition will be like the condition of those?
20:134: 134. And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, before sending the Messenger and revealing the Qur’an, they would have said, ‘Our Lord, why did You not send to us a Messenger?’ calling us, meaning: they would have said on the Day of Resurrection, so that we would have followed Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced, with punishment, humiliation, disgrace, shame, and disgrace.
20:135: 135. "Say, 'Every one is waiting,' waiting for the circles of time. This is because the polytheists said, 'We are waiting for Muhammad to be affected by the events of time, and if he dies we will be saved.' God Almighty said, 'Then wait,' so wait, 'and you will know,' when God's command comes and the Day of Resurrection comes, 'who are the companions of the straight path,' 'and who are guided,' who are we or you astray?'
21:1: 1. The reckoning of the people has drawn near, it was said that alan means from, meaning that the time of God’s reckoning of them for their deeds has drawn near, meaning the Day of Resurrection. It was revealed about those who deny the resurrection, while they are in heedlessness turning away, from preparing for it.
21:2: 2. Whatever reminder comes to them from their Lord is new, meaning whatever God sends down from the Qur’an to remind them and admonish them with. Muqatil said: God brings about a matter [after a matter]. It was said: The newly-introduced remembrance is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said and explained of the Sunnahs and sermons, other than what is in the Qur’an, and he attributed it to the Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, because he said by the command of the Lord, except that they listen to it while they are playing, meaning that they listen to it as players who do not consider or learn a lesson.
21:3: 3. Lahiyan, sahiyaan ghaawy, their hearts, turning away from the remembrance of God, and His saying Lahiyan, is an adjective that precedes the noun, and it is the right of the adjective to follow the noun in parsing, and if the adjective precedes the noun then it has two states: separation and connection, in separation it is the accusative like the saying of God the Almighty: their eyes humbled (al-Qamar 54:7), and their shadows are low over them (al-Insan 76:11), and Lahiyan qulubhum, and in connection it is the state of what precedes it in parsing like His saying, We brought out from this city whose people were wrongdoers (An-Nisa': 75), and those who wronged whispered secretly, meaning they associated partners with God, His saying: and whispered is a verb that preceded the plural and its right was wasra, Al-Kisa'i said: there is an advancement and a delay in it, he meant: and those who wronged whispered secretly. It was said: It was raised as a substitute for the pronoun in asrawa. Al-Mubarrad said: This is like your saying that those in the house set out, the sons of Abdullah, as a substitute for what is in asrawa. Then he explained their secret that they whispered to each other, saying: Is this anything but a human being like you? They denied the sending of humans and asked for the sending of angels. Do you then practice magic? meaning, do you bring magic and accept it, while you see? meaning, do you know that it is magic?
21:4: 4. Say, to them, O Muhammad, My Lord knows what is said in the heaven and the earth, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read: (My Lord said), on the authority of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, He knows what is said in the heaven and the earth, meaning nothing is hidden from Him, and He is the All-Hearing, of their words, the All-Knowing, of their actions.
21:5: 5. Rather, they said, 'Confused dreams', its falsehoods [and sayings] and its horrors that he saw in a dream, Rather, he invented it, he fabricated it, Rather, he is a poet", meaning that the polytheists divided the saying about him and what he says, some of them said: Confused dreams, and some of them said: Rather, it is a lie, and some of them said: Rather, Muhammad is a poet, and what he brought to you is poetry. "So let Muhammad bring us a sign, if he is truthful, as the former messengers were sent, with signs.
21:6: 6. God Almighty said in response to them: No town believed before them, before the polytheists of Mecca, from a town, meaning from the people of a town to which the signs came. We destroyed it, we destroyed them by denying it. Will they believe? if a sign came to them. Its meaning is: Those people did not believe in the signs when they came to them. Will these people believe?
21:7: 7. The Almighty said: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed, this is an answer to their saying: Is this anything but a human being like you? meaning: We did not send angels to the first peoples, rather We sent men to whom We revealed, So ask the people of the message, meaning: the people of the Torah and the Gospel, meaning the scholars of the People of the Book, for they do not deny that the messengers were human beings, even if they denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He ordered the polytheists to ask them because they were closer to believing those who did not believe in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, than they were to believing those who believed in him. Ibn Zayd said: By the message He meant the Qur'an, meaning: So ask the believing scholars from the people of the Qur'an, if you do not know.
21:8: 8. And We did not make them, meaning the messengers, bodies, and He did not say bodies because it is a generic name, that they do not eat food, this is a response to their saying What is the matter with this messenger that he eats food? (al-Furqan 25:7), He says We did not make the messengers angels, but rather We made them human beings who eat food, and they were not immortal, in this world.
21:9: 9. Then We fulfilled the promise to them, which We promised them to destroy their enemies, and We saved them and whomever We willed, meaning We saved the believers who believed them, and We destroyed the transgressors, meaning the polytheists who denied, and every polytheist is transgressing against himself.
21:10: 10. We have sent down to you a Book, O people of Quraysh, in which is your remembrance, that is, your honor, as He said: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people (al-Zukhruf 43:44), and it is an honor for whoever believes in it. Mujahed said: It contains your hadith. Al-Hasan said: It contains your mention, meaning what you need regarding your religious affairs, Do you not understand?
21:11: 11. And how many a city have We destroyed, that is, destroyed, and al-Qasm means breaking, and brought forth after it, that is, after the destruction of its people, another people.
21:12: 12. So when they sensed Our punishment, that is, [saw] Our punishment with the sense of sight, at once they were running from it, that is, they hastened to flee.
21:13: 13. "Do not run, meaning they were told do not run, do not flee, and return to what you have been enjoying, meaning what you have enjoyed, and your homes so that you may be asked", Ibn Abbas said: About the killing of your prophet. Qatada said: Something from your worldly life. This verse was revealed about the people of Hasura, a village in Yemen whose people were Arabs. So God sent a prophet to them calling them to God, but they denied him and killed him. So God empowered Nebuchadnezzar over them, until he killed them and took them captive. When the killing continued, they regretted it, fled, and were defeated. So the angels said to them in mockery: Do not run, and return to your homes and your wealth so that you may be asked. Qatada said: Perhaps you ask for something from your worldly life, so you give to whomever you wish and withhold from whomever you wish, for you are people of wealth and blessings. They say that in mockery of them, so Bukhtanasr pursued them and the swords took them, and a caller called from the sky: O revenge of the prophets. When they saw that, they acknowledged their sins when it did not benefit them.
21:14: 14. They said, 'Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers.'
21:15: 15. "And that has not ceased to be their call, meaning that word, which is their saying, Woe to us, is their call that they call with and repeat. Until We made them a harvest, with swords as crops are harvested, dormant, dead.
21:16: 16. The Almighty said: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play, meaning in vain and in vain.
21:17: 17. If We had intended to take a diversion, they differed about diversion. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Ata': Diversion is the woman, which is the opinion of Al-Hasan and Qatadah. He said in the narration of Al-Kalbi: Diversion is the child, which is the opinion of Al-Suddi, and it is more apparent in the case of the woman because intercourse is called diversion in the language, and the woman is the place of intercourse. We would have taken it from Ourselves, meaning from Our houris, not from you from the people of the earth. It was said: Its meaning is that if that was permissible in its description, He would not have taken it in a way that would be apparent to them and concealed so that they would not find out about it. The interpretation of the verse is that when the Christians said what they said about the Messiah and his mother, God responded to them with this and said: We would have taken him from Our presence because you know that a man’s son and wife are with him, not with anyone else, if We were to do it. Qatada, Muqatil, and Ibn Jurayj said: If is for negation, meaning: We were not to do it. It was said: If We were to do it is for the condition, meaning if we were among those who would do that, We would have taken him from Our presence, but We did not do it because it is not befitting of the Lordship.
21:18: 18. Rather, that is, leave what they said, for it is a lie and falsehood, We slander, we throw and give power, with the truth, with faith, over falsehood, over disbelief. It was said: The truth is the word of God, that He has no son, and falsehood is their saying that God has taken a son. So He destroys him, destroys him. The root of striking is to cut the head until it reaches the brain. Then he is gone, going away. The meaning is: We nullify their lie with what we explain of the truth until it evaporates and disappears. Then He threatened them for their lie, saying: And for you is woe, O group of disbelievers, for what you describe, God with what is not befitting of Him of a companion and a son. Mujahid said: For what you lie about.
21:19: 19. And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth, as servants and kings, and whoever is with Him, meaning the angels, they are not too proud to worship Him, they are not averse to worshipping Him, nor do they learn from it, nor do they grow weary, they do not become exhausted. It is said: he grew weary and weary if he became tired and exhausted. Al-Suddi said: they do not learn from worship.
21:20: 20. They glorify God night and day, never slackening, they do not weaken or get tired. Ka’b al-Ahbar said: Glorification for them is like the soul for the children of Adam.
21:21: 21. Or have they taken gods from the earth? is an interrogative meaning denial, i.e. they have not taken, that resurrect, meaning idols made of wood and stone, which are from the earth, that resurrect, that is, they revive the dead, and divinity is only deserved by the one who is able to revive and create from nothingness and bestow the most eloquent forms of blessings.
21:22: 22. If there were within them, meaning in the heavens and the earth, gods besides God, meaning other than God, they would have been ruined, they would have been destroyed and those in them would have perished due to the existence of the gods’ opposition because every matter issued by two or more does not proceed in accordance with the system. Then He exalted Himself and said: So glory be to God, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe, meaning from what the polytheists describe Him with, such as a partner or a son.
21:23: 23. He is not questioned about what He does, and He judges His creation because He is the Lord. And they will be questioned, meaning the creation will be questioned, about their actions and deeds because they are slaves.
21:24: 24. "Or have they taken other gods besides Him?" An interrogative of denial and rebuke. "Say, 'Bring forth your proof.'" That is, your argument for that. Then he said, resuming, "This," meaning the Qur'an. "A mention of those with me," in which is report of those with me in my religion and those who follow me until the Day of Resurrection, with what they will receive of reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience. "And a mention, is report, of those before me," of the previous nations, what was done to them in this world and what will be done to them in the Hereafter. And from Ibn Abbas in the narration of Ata': The mention of those with me is the Qur'an, and the mention of those before me is the Torah and the Gospel, meaning: Review the Qur'an, the Torah, the Gospel, and all the other books. Will you find in them that God has taken a son? "But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.
21:25: 25. "And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs on the authority of Asim read We revealed to him with a noon and a kasra on the ha' for emphasis, because of his saying And We did not send, and the others read with a ya' and a fatha on the ha' for the passive verb, that there is no god but Me, so worship Me, and they are unique.
21:26: 26. The Almighty’s saying: And they say, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son,’ was revealed about Khuza’ah when they said: The angels are daughters of God. Glory be to Him, He exalted Himself above what they said. Rather, they are servants, meaning they are servants, meaning the angels, honored.
21:27: 27. They do not precede Him in speech, they do not precede Him in speech and they do not speak except what He commands them to do, and they act by His command, meaning that they do not disobey Him in word or deed.
21:28: 28. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, meaning what they did and what they will do. It was said: what was before their creation and what will be after their creation. And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased, Ibn Abbas said: meaning for the one who said there is no god but God. Mujahid said: meaning for the one with whom He is pleased. And they are fearful of His fear, fearful and not secure from His deceit.
21:29: 29. And whoever among them says, ‘I am a god besides Him,’ Qatada said: He meant Satan when he called for the worship of himself and commanded obedience to himself, for none of the angels said, I am a god besides God, “that is it We will recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers,” those who place divinity and worship in the wrong place.
21:30: 30. "Have not those who disbelieved seen? Ibn Kathir read Have they not seen" [without the waw], and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an. Its meaning is: Have not those who disbelieved known that the heavens and the earth were joined together? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, and Ata' and Qatadah said: They were one thing stuck together. "Then We split them apart," We separated them with air. In the language, "ratq means a dam, and fattah" means a slit. Kaab said: God created the heavens and the earth, one on top of the other, then He created the wind and placed it in the middle and opened it with it. Mujahed and Al-Suddi said: The heavens were connected in one layer, then He split them and made them seven heavens. Likewise, the earth was connected in one layer, then He made it seven earths. Ikrimah and Atiyah said: The sky was sealed and did not rain, and the earth was sealed and did not produce vegetation. Then He split the sky with rain and the earth with vegetation. He only said sealed for the sake of monotheism, and it is one of the descriptions of the heavens and the earth because it is a source that is placed in place of a noun, like falsehood and fasting and the like. And We made, [and created] from water every living thing, meaning: We gave life with the water that descends from the sky to every living thing, meaning from the animals, including plants and trees, meaning that it is the cause of the life of everything. The commentators say: [meaning] that every living thing is created from water. Like the Almighty’s saying: And God created every creature from water (al-Nur 24:45). Abu Al-Aaliyah said: He means the sperm. If it is said: Has God created some of what is living from other than water? It is said: This is by way of exaggeration, meaning that most of the living things on earth were created from water or remained in water, Will they not then believe?
21:31: 31. And We placed on the earth firm mountains, fixed mountains, lest it should move with them, [meaning so that it would not move with them], and We placed therein, in the firm mountains, passes, roads and paths. A pass is the wide road between two mountains, meaning We placed paths between the mountains so that they may be guided to their destinations, paths, an explanation of the passes, that they may be guided.
21:32: 32. And We have made the sky a protected ceiling, from falling, as evidenced by the Almighty's statement: And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission (al-Hajj 22:65), and it was said: protected from the devils by meteors, as evidenced by the Almighty's statement: And We have protected it from every devil expelled (al-Hijr 15:17), and they, meaning the disbelievers, are turning away from its signs, what God created in it of the sun, moon, stars and other things, not thinking about it or considering it.
21:33: 33. And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon, each in an orbit swimming, running and moving quickly like a swimmer in water. Rather, He said: swimming, and did not say swimming as is said for something that is not rational, because He mentioned the action of rational beings of running and swimming, so He mentioned it as being rational. The orbit of the stars that includes them. In Arabic, the orbit is everything that is round. Its plural is aflak, and from it comes the word falak the spindle’s orbit. Al-Hasan said: The universe is a mill like the spindle’s orbit. He means that the place in which the stars move is round like the roundness of a mill. Some of them said: The sky in which that is, in which that planet is, so every planet runs in the sky in which it is determined, and this is the meaning of what Qatada said. Al-Kalbi said: The sky is the roundness of the sky. Others said: The sky is a wave that is blocked below the sky, in which the sun, moon, and stars move.
21:34: 34. The Almighty said: And We have not granted to any human being before you immortality, meaning perpetual existence in this world, So if I die, will they be immortal? That is, will they be immortal if I die? This verse was revealed when they said, We are waiting for Muhammad to be struck by a calamity of death.
21:35: 35. Every soul will taste death, and We test you, We test you with evil and good, with hardship and prosperity, health and sickness, wealth and poverty, and it was said: with what you love and what you hate, as a trial, a test to see how grateful you are for what you love, and how patient you are for what you hate, and to Us you will be returned.
21:36: 36. And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you only in ridicule. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl, whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by and laughed and said: This is the prophet of Banu Abd Manaf. Is this the one who mentions your gods? That is, they say to each other: Is this the one who mentions your gods? That is, they find fault with them. It is said: So-and-so mentions so-and-so, meaning he finds fault with him, and so-and-so mentions God, meaning he glorifies and venerates Him. And they are disbelievers in the mention of the Most Merciful. That is because they used to say: We do not know the Most Merciful except Musaylimah. The second and is a connection.
21:37: 37. The Almighty’s statement: He created man from haste. They differed about it. Some people said: Its meaning is that his structure and creation are from haste and are inherent in it, as He said: And man is ever hasty. (al-Isra’ 17:11). Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Suddi said: When the spirit entered Adam’s head and eyes, he looked at the fruits of Paradise. When it entered his stomach, he desired food, so he jumped up before the spirit reached his feet in haste to the fruits of Paradise. He fell, and it was said: Man was created from haste. What is meant by man is Adam, and he bequeathed haste to his children. The Arabs say about someone who does a lot of something: I was created from it, just as the Arabs say: I was created in play, and I was created in anger. This is intended to exaggerate in describing him in that way. This is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: And man is ever hasty. Some people said: Its meaning is the creation of man, meaning Adam, from God’s haste in creating him, because his creation was after the creation of everything else at the end of the day on Friday, so He hastened in creating him before sunset. Mujahed said: When the spirit revived his head, he said: O Lord, hasten my creation before sunset. It was said: quickly and hastily, unlike the order in which all other human beings are created, from the sperm, the clot, the lump of flesh, and others. Some people said: Min ijal, meaning: from clay. The poet said: The spring grows in the solid rock, and the palm trees grow between the water and the calf. I will show you My signs, so do not be impatient. [This was revealed about the polytheists] who were hastening the punishment and saying: Rain stones on us from the sky. It was said: It was revealed about Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, so God Almighty said: I will show you My signs, meaning My promises, so do not be impatient, meaning do not seek the punishment before its time. So He showed them on the Day of Badr. It was said: They were hastening the Resurrection.
21:38: 38. "And they say, 'When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?'"
21:39: 39. So God Almighty said: If only those who disbelieve knew when they will not be restrained, they will not be repelled from their faces the Fire nor from their backs, it was said: nor from their backs the whips, nor will they be aided, they will be prevented from the punishment. The answer to if only in His statement: If only those who is omitted, meaning: If only they knew, they would not have persisted in their disbelief, nor would they have hastened, nor would they have said: When will this promise come?
21:40: 40. Rather, it will come to them meaning the Hour suddenly, suddenly, and it will confuse them, meaning it will bewilder them. It is said: So-and-so is confounded, meaning he is perplexed, and they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be given respite, meaning they will be given time.
21:41: 41. And messengers before you were mocked, but that which they used to mock befell those who mocked them, it was revealed, the punishment for their mockery.
21:42: 42. “Say: Who guards you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?” if He sends down His punishment upon you? Ibn Abbas said: Who can protect you from the punishment of the Most Merciful? Rather, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord, from the Qur’an and God’s admonitions.
21:43: 43. "Or do they have, or is a relative clause in it, and in similar cases, gods to protect them from Us", there is an inversion in it, its meaning is: Or do they have gods other than Us to protect them, then He described the gods as weak, so the Most High said: "They cannot help themselves, they protect themselves, so how can they help their worshippers, nor do they have any companions from Us", Ibn Abbas said: they protect. And Atiyyah said: They are protected from him, the Arabs say: I am your protector and companion from so-and-so, meaning I am protected from him. And Mujahid said: they are supported. And Qatada said: And they are not accompanied by any good from God.
21:44: 44. Rather, We gave these, the disbelievers, and their fathers enjoyment in this world, meaning We gave them respite. It was also said: We gave them the blessing, until their life was prolonged, meaning time was extended for them and they were deceived. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? Meaning, We do not reduce the borders of the polytheists and increase the borders of the believers. He means the appearance of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his conquest of the lands of polytheism, land by land. Are they the victors? Or are we?
21:45: 45. Say, ‘I only warn you by revelation,’ meaning I frighten you with the Qur’an, and the deaf do not hear the call, Ibn ‘Amir read it with the ta’ and a damma on it and a kasra on the meem, the deaf is in the accusative case, making the address to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the others read it with the ya’ and a fatha on it and a fatha on the meem, the deaf is in the nominative case, when they warn, they frighten.
21:46: 46. And if a whiff of it touches them, that is, it afflicts them, a touch, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said, a touch. It was also said, a little. Ibn Jurayj said, a share, from their saying, So-and-so gave so-and-so a share of his money, meaning, he gave him a portion of it. It was also said, a blow, from their saying, the beast struck with its foot, meaning, from the punishment of your Lord, they will surely say, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers,' meaning, by our destruction, we were polytheists. They called for woe upon themselves after they acknowledged polytheism.
21:47: 47. And We will set up the just scales, meaning those with justness, and justness means fairness, on the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul will be wronged at all, neither will the reward for his good deeds be diminished nor will his bad deeds be increased. In the hadiths: The scale has a tongue and two pans. It was narrated that David, peace be upon him, asked his Lord to show him the balance, so He showed him each pan measuring between the east and the west. He fainted, then came to and said: O my God, who is able to fill his pan with good deeds? He said: O David, if I am pleased with my servant, I fill it with a date. And if it is the weight of a mustard seed, the people of Medina read mithqal with the lam raised here and in Surat Luqman, meaning if it is the weight of a grain, and the others put it in the accusative case meaning: And if that thing is the weight of a grain, meaning the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it, we will bring it to reward with it. And sufficient are We as reckoners. Al-Suddi said: Reckoners. The meaning of counting is counting. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Knowing and preserving, because whoever calculates something knows it and preserves it.
21:48: 48. The Almighty said: And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion, meaning the Book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood, which is the Torah. Ibn Zayd said: The Criterion is victory over enemies, as God Almighty said: And We did not send down to Our Servant on the Day of Criterion (al-Anfal 8:41), meaning the Day of Badr, because He said and a light, and He inserted the waw into it, meaning We gave Moses victory and light, which is the Torah. And whoever said: What is meant by Al-Furqan is the Torah, said: The waw in His statement: and a light, is an extra, inserted letter, meaning: We gave him the Torah as a light. And it was said: It is another description of the Torah, and a reminder, a reminder, for the righteous.
21:49: 49. Those who fear their Lord unseen, meaning they fear Him even though they have not seen Him, and are fearful of the Hour, fearful.
21:50: 50. And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down, meaning the Qur’an, and it is a reminder for those who remember it, blessed, seeking blessings from it and seeking good from it. So will you, O people of Mecca, deny it? This is a question of rebuke and reproach.
21:51: 51. The Almighty said: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgment, Al-Qurazi said: meaning righteousness, before, meaning before Moses and Aaron. The commentators said: His sound judgment, meaning He guided him before, meaning before puberty, which was when he left the flock while he was young, meaning We guided him when he was young, as the Almighty said to John, peace be upon him: And We gave him judgment while he was a boy (Maryam 19:12), And We were well-versed in him, that he was worthy of guidance and prophethood.
21:52: 52. “When he said to his father and his people, ‘What are these statues’, meaning the images, meaning the idols, ‘to which you are devoted’, meaning you are committed to worshipping them.
21:53: 53. They said, ‘We found our fathers worshipping it,’ so we followed their example.
21:54: 54. He said, Abraham, You and your fathers were in manifest error, a clear error in your worship of it.
21:55: 55. They said, ‘Have you brought us the truth, or are you one of the players?’ They meant, Are you right in what you say, or [are you one of the players?]
21:56: 56. He said, ‘Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who created them,’ meaning, He created them, and I am of that among the witnesses, meaning, that He is the God who is the only one worthy of worship. It was said: Among the witnesses that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth.
21:57: 57. And by God, I will surely destroy your idols, I will plot against them, after you have turned your backs, meaning after you have turned your backs and set out for your festival. Mujahid and Qatada said: Ibrahim only said this in secret from his people, and only one man heard it, so he disclosed it to him and said: We heard a young man mentioning them, whose name is Ibrahim. Al-Suddi said: They had a festival gathering every year, and when they returned from their festival, they would enter upon the idols and prostrate themselves before them, then they would return to their homes. When that festival came, Ibrahim’s father said to him: O Ibrahim, if you go with us to our festival, you will like our religion. So Ibrahim went out with them, and when he was on the way, he threw himself down and said, I am sick, saying, I have a sore leg. When they had gone, he called out to the last of them, and the weakest of the people remained, By God, I will surely destroy your idols. They heard him say that. Then Ibrahim returned to the house of the gods, and they were in a great hall facing the door of the hall, with a great idol next to it, smaller than it, and the idols next to each other, each idol smaller than it, to the door of the hall. They had prepared food and placed it in front of the gods, and they said: When we return and the gods have blessed our food, we will eat. When Ibrahim looked at them and at the food in front of them, he said to them in mockery: Why don’t you eat? When they did not answer him, he said: What is the matter with you that you do not speak? He struck them with his right hand and began to break them in his hand until nothing remained but the largest idol. He hung the axe around its neck and then left. This is what God Almighty said.
21:58: 58. So He made them into fragments, Al-Kisa'i read Jathathan with a kasra on the jim, meaning breaking and cutting, the plural of Jadhdh, which is dry straw like Khafif and Khafaf, and others read it with a damma, like wreckage and remains, except for a great one of theirs, for he did not break it and put the axe on its neck, and it was said that he tied it with his hand, and there were seventy-two idols, some of them of gold and some of silver and some of iron and lead and copper and wood and stone, and the great idol was of gold crowned with jewels and in its eyes were two glowing rubies. The Almighty said: Perhaps they will return to Him, it was said: Its meaning is perhaps they will return to His religion and to what He calls them to if they know the weakness and inability of the gods, and it was said: perhaps they will return to Him and ask Him, so when the people returned from their festival to the house of their gods and saw their idols in fragments.
21:59: 59. They said, ‘Who has done this to our gods? He is indeed one of the wrongdoers,’ meaning one of the criminals.
21:60: 60. They said, meaning those who heard Abraham's words: By God, I will surely destroy your idols, "We heard a young man mentioning them, criticizing and insulting them, his name is Abraham, he is the one we think did this, and this reached Nimrod the tyrant and the nobles of his people.
21:61: 61. They said, ‘Bring him before the eyes of the people,’ Nimrod said: He said, “Bring him openly in the sight of the people, ‘perhaps they will bear witness,’ that he is the one who did it. They hated to take him without evidence. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Al-Suddi said, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, “perhaps they will bear witness,” meaning they will be present at his punishment and what will be done to him. So when they brought him,
21:62: 62. They said, to him, Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?
21:63: 63. He said, Ibrahim, Rather, their eldest did it, he was angry that they worshipped these little ones with him while he was older than them, so he broke them. Ibrahim wanted to establish an argument against them by doing so, and that is what he said: Then ask them, if they should speak, so that they would inform those who did that to them. Al-Qatibi said: Its meaning is that their leader did it if they could speak, as a condition. So he made speaking a condition for the action, meaning that if they were able to speak, they would be able to do it. So he showed them their inability to speak, and within it I did it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Kisa’i that he would stop at his saying Rather, he did it and say: Its meaning is [he did it] from his action. The first is more correct because it was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Ibrahim did not lie except three lies, two of which were for the sake of God: his saying: ‘Indeed, I am ill’ 37:89, and his saying: ‘Rather, their chief did it’, and his saying to Sarah: ‘This is my sister.’” It was said about his saying: Indeed, I am ill that is, I will become ill. It was also said: The illness of the heart means, grieved by your misguidance. His saying to Sarah: This is my sister, meaning in religion. These interpretations are to deny lying from Abraham, and the first is the first to talk about it. It is possible that God Almighty permitted him to do that for the purpose of reform and to rebuke them and argue with them, just as He permitted Joseph until he ordered his crier to say to his brothers: O caravan, indeed, you are thieves 37:70. And they had not stolen.
21:64: 64. So they returned to themselves, meaning they thought with their hearts and returned to their minds, and said, we see nothing but as He said: Indeed, you are the wrongdoers, meaning by your worship of someone who does not speak. And it was said: You are the wrongdoers of this man in your asking him, and these are your gods present, so ask them.
21:65: 65. Then they turned their heads back, the commentators said: God made the truth flow from their tongues in the first statement, then misery overtook them, so this is the meaning of His statement: Then they turned their heads back, meaning they returned to disbelief after they admitted to wrongdoing against themselves. It is said that the sick person turned back if he returned to his original state, and they said, You have certainly known that these do not speak, so how do we ask them? So when the argument was directed to Abraham, peace be upon him,
21:66: 66. "He said, to them, Do you worship besides God that which neither benefits you at all, if you worship it, nor harms you," if you abandon its worship?
21:67: 67. Fie upon you, meaning damnation and filth upon you, “and what you worship besides God. Do you not understand?” meaning do you not have a mind to know this? So when the argument became necessary for them and they were unable to answer.
21:68: 68. They said, 'Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to do so.' That is, if you are going to support them. Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: The one who said this was a Kurd. It was said that his name was Hayzan, so God caused the earth to swallow him up and he will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection. It was said: Nimrod said it, so when Nimrod and his people decided to burn Abraham, peace be upon him, they imprisoned him in a house and built a structure for him like a pen. It was said: They built a furnace in a village called Kutha, then they collected for it hard wood from various types of wood for a period of time until the man would fall ill and say, If God cures me, I will collect firewood for Abraham. The woman would vow in some of what she sought that if she got it, she would be buried in Abraham’s fire. The man would recommend buying firewood and throwing it in it, and the woman would spin and buy firewood with her spinning, then throw it in it as a reward for her religion. Ibn Ishaq said: They used to collect firewood for a month, and when they had collected as much firewood as they wanted in each area, the fire ignited and became so intense that birds would fly by it and be burned by the intensity of its blazing heat. So they lit it for seven days. It was narrated that they did not know how to throw him into it, so Satan came and taught them how to make a catapult, so they did. Then they went to Abraham, raised him to the top of the building, tied him up, and put him in the catapult, bound and shackled. Then the heavens, the earth, and all the angels in it, and all of creation except the two heavy ones, cried out in one cry, Our Lord, Abraham, Your friend, is being thrown into the fire, and there is no one on Your earth who worships You except him, so give us permission to support him. Then God Almighty said, “He is My friend, I have no friend other than him, and I am his god, and he has no god other than Me. If he seeks help from any of you or calls upon Him, then let him support him, for I have given him permission to do so. But if he does not call upon anyone other than Me, then I know him best and I am his guardian, so leave Me alone with him.” When they wanted to throw him into the fire, the keeper of the waters came to him and said, If you wish, I will put out the fire. And the keeper of the winds came to him and said, If you wish, I will fly the fire into the air. Abraham said, “I have no need of you. God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.” It was narrated on the authority of Abu Kaab that when they tied him up to throw him into the fire, Abraham said: There is no god but You, glory be to You, Lord of the worlds. To You is praise and to You is dominion. You have no partner. Then they threw him into the fire in the catapult, and Gabriel met him and said: O Abraham, do you have a need? He said: No, to you. Gabriel said: Then ask your Lord. Abraham said: It is sufficient for me to ask, for His knowledge of my condition is sufficient for me. Kaab al-Ahbar said: He made everything extinguish the fire for him except the gecko, which was blowing on the fire. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ubaidullah bin Musa and Ibn Salam told us on his authority, Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Jubayr on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab on the authority of Umm Sharik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “ordered the killing of the gecko, and said: It was blowing fire on Abraham.”
21:69: 69. God Almighty said: “We said, ‘O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham.’” Ibn Abbas said: If he had not said “peace,” Abraham would have died from its coldness. It is well-known in the hadiths that on that day, no fire remained on the earth except that it was extinguished, so no fire in the world would have benefited from that day. If he had not said “and peace upon Abraham,” it would have remained cool forever. Al-Suddi said: The angels took hold of Abraham’s shoulders and made him sit on the ground. There was a spring of fresh water, red roses, and narcissus. Kaab said: The fire did not burn Abraham except his bonds. They said: Abraham was in that place for seven days. Al-Munhal bin Amr said: Ibrahim said: I have never been more blessed than the days I was in Hell. Ibn Yasar said: God Almighty sent the Angel of Shadow in the form of Abraham, and he sat beside Abraham to comfort him. They said: God sent Gabriel with a shirt of silk from Paradise and a carpet, so he dressed him in the shirt and made him sit on the carpet and sat with him talking to him. Gabriel said: O Abraham, your Lord says: Did you not know that the fire does not harm my beloved ones? Then Nimrod looked and looked down on Abraham from his palace and saw him sitting in a garden with the angel sitting beside him and around him a fire burning wood. He called out to him: O Abraham, your God is great, whose power has reached such a level that it has come between you and what I see. O Abraham, can you get out of it? He said: Yes. He said: Do you fear that if you stay in it it will harm you? He said: No. He said: Get up and get out of it. So Abraham got up and walked in it until he got out of it. When he got out to him, he said to him: O Abraham, who is the man whom you saw with you in your form sitting beside you? He said: That is the Angel of the Shadow, my Lord sent him to me to keep me company in it. Nimrod said: O Abraham, I am offering to your God as a sacrifice for what I saw of His power and might in what He did to you when you refused to do anything but worship Him and make Him One. I am slaughtering four thousand cows for Him. Abraham said to him: Then God will not accept from you what you were upon in your religion until you leave it for my religion. He said: I cannot leave my kingdom. But I will slaughter it for him. So Nimrod slaughtered it for him, then he stopped Abraham, and God prevented him from it. Shuaib al-Jubba’i said: Abraham was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old.
21:70: 70. The Almighty said: And they intended to plot against him, but We made them the greatest losers. It was said: Its meaning is that they lost the effort and the expense and did not achieve their goal. It was said: Its meaning is that God Almighty sent mosquitoes upon Nimrod and his people, which ate their flesh and drank their blood, and one of them entered his brain and killed him.
21:71: 71. The Almighty said: And We saved him and Lot Surah Al-Anbiya from Nimrod and his people in the land of Iraq, to the land which We have blessed for the worlds, meaning the Levant, which God blessed with fertility, an abundance of trees, fruits, and rivers, and from it He sent most of the prophets. Abi bin Kaab said: He called it blessed because there is no fresh water except that its source springs from under the rock that is in Jerusalem. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, that Umar ibn al-Khattab said to Ka’b: Why don’t you move to Medina, in which is the migration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his grave? Ka’b said: Rich, I have found in the revealed Book of God, O Commander of the Faithful, that Ash-Sham is God’s treasure from His land, and in it is His treasure from His servants. Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, Surat Al-Anbiya, my grandfather Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzaz told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq Al-Dayri told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There will be migration after migration, and the best of people will be those who migrate to Abraham. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: The men of his people responded to Abraham when they saw what God had done to him, making the fire cool and safe for him, out of fear of Nimrod and his people. Lot believed in him, and he was his nephew, Lot bin Haran bin Tarah, and Haran was Abraham’s brother. They had a third brother called Nakhor bin Tarah, and Sarah, his cousin, Sarah bint Haran the elder, Abraham’s uncle, also believed in him. He left Kutha in the land of Iraq, emigrating to his Lord, and with him were Lot and Sarah, as God Almighty said: So Lot believed in him and said, ‘Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord.’ (al-Ankabut 29:26). He left seeking to escape with his religion and safety in worshipping his Lord, until he settled in Harran, where he stayed as long as God willed. Then he left it as an emigrant until he arrived in Egypt. Then he left Egypt for the Levant, and he settled in the Seven Lands of Palestine, which is the desert of the Levant. Lot settled in Al-Mu’tafikah, which is one of the Seven Lands, a day and a night’s journey away, and closer. So God sent him as a prophet, and that is what He said. God Almighty said: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for the worlds.
21:72: 72. And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift. Mujahid and Ata' said: The meaning of an additional gift is a gift, and both of them are from God's gift. An additional gift means a gift. Al-Hasan and Ad-Dahhak said: A favor. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Zayd, and Qatadah, may God be pleased with them: The additional gift is Jacob, because God Almighty gave him Isaac because of his supplication when he said: Grant me from among the righteous (al-Saffat 37:100), and Jacob added [the son of the son], and the additional gift is the addition, And each of them We made righteous, meaning: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
21:73: 73. And We made them leaders, to be followed in goodness, guiding by Our command, calling people to Our religion, and We inspired in them the doing of good deeds, acting according to the laws, establishing prayer, meaning: preserving it, and giving zakat, giving it, and they were worshippers of Us, monotheists.
21:74: 74. And to Lot We gave, meaning: And We gave Lot, and it was said: And remember Lot, We gave him, judgment, meaning: deciding between opponents with truth, and knowledge, “And We saved him from the city that was doing evil,” meaning: Sodom, whose people were having intercourse with men in their backsides and defecating in their clubs, along with other things. They were doing evil deeds, Indeed, they were a people of evil, wicked.
21:75: 75. "And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was among the righteous."
21:76: 76. And Noah, when he called out, he called out, before, that is, before Abraham and Lot, so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress, Ibn Abbas said: from drowning and the denial of his people. It was said: because he was the longest-lived of the prophets and the most severely afflicted, and distress is the most severe grief.
21:77: 77. And We aided him, that is, We prevented him, from the people who denied Our signs, from harming him. Abu Ubaidah said: That is, against the people, Indeed, they were an evil people, so We drowned them all.
21:78: 78. The Almighty said: And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, they differed about the field. Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, and most of the commentators said: The field was a vineyard with its clusters hanging down. Qatada said: It was a crop, When the sheep of the people pastured therein, meaning they grazed it at night and spoiled it. Pasturing at night means grazing and neglecting during the day, and they are grazing without a shepherd. And We were witnesses to their judgment, meaning: That was with Our knowledge and sight, and its knowledge was not hidden from Us. Al-Farra' said: He pluralized two, so he said their judgment, meaning David and Solomon, because two is a plural, and it is like His statement: But if he had brothers, then for his mother is a sixth (An-Nisa': 11), and He meant two brothers. Ibn Abbas, Qatada and Al-Zuhri said: “Two men entered upon David, one of them a farmer and the other a sheep farmer. The farmer said: ‘This man’s sheep got loose at night and fell into my field and ruined it, so nothing remained of it.’ So David gave him the necks of the sheep for the field. They went out and passed by Solomon, who said: ‘How did he judge between you?’ So they told him. Solomon said: ‘If I had been in charge of their affairs, I would have judged differently.’” It was narrated that he said something other than this is easier for both parties. So David was informed of that, so he called him and said: How do you judge? It was narrated that he said: By the right of prophethood and fatherhood, tell me what is easier for both parties. He said: Give the sheep to the owner of the farm so that he may benefit from its milk, offspring, wool and benefits, and the owner of the sheep should sow for the owner of the farm the same as his farm. When the farm is as it was on the day it was eaten, it should be given to its people, and the owner of the sheep should take his sheep. So David said: The judgment is what you have judged, and he ruled accordingly. It was said: When Solomon ruled, he was eleven years old. As for the ruling of Islam [on this issue], what the livestock sent out during the day spoils of someone else’s property, its owner is not liable, and what it spoils at night, its owner is liable, because it is common knowledge that the owners of the crops protect it during the day, and the livestock are released during the day and returned at night to the pasture. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Haram ibn Sa`d ibn Muhaysa, “A she-camel belonging to al-Bara` ibn `Azib entered a garden and caused damage. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the people of the gardens were responsible for guarding it during the day, and that whatever the livestock caused damage at night was the responsibility of its people.” The people of opinion held that if the owner was not with it, then he was not responsible for what his livestock caused damage, whether at night or during the day.
21:79: 79. The Almighty said: And We made Solomon understand it, meaning We taught him the issue and inspired it to Solomon, and to each, meaning David and Solomon, We gave judgment and knowledge. Al-Hasan said: If it were not for this verse, you would have seen the rulers perish, but God was praised for his correctness and commended this one for his diligence. The scholars differed as to whether David’s judgment was based on diligence or text, and the same was true of Solomon’s judgment. Some of them said: It is done through ijtihad. They said that it is permissible for the prophets to make ijtihad so that they may attain the reward of those who make ijtihad, except that David made a mistake and Solomon was right. They said: It is permissible for the prophets to make a mistake, except that they are not to be approved of. As for the scholars, they have the right to make ijtihad in incidents if they do not find a text in the Book or the Sunnah, and if they make a mistake, there is no sin upon them, [because it is dropped from them], because Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib informed us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm informed us, Al-Rabi bin Sulaiman informed us, Al-Shafi’i informed us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad informed us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah bin Al-Hadi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Taimi, on the authority of Bishr bin Saeed, on the authority of Abu Qais, the client of Amr bin Al-Aas, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Aas that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If the judge makes a ruling and makes an effort and gets it right, then he has two rewards, and if he makes a ruling and makes an effort and gets it wrong, then he has one reward. Some people said: David and Solomon ruled by revelation, and Solomon’s ruling abrogates David’s ruling. This speaker says: It is not permissible for the prophets to rule by ijtihad because they do not need ijtihad by revelation. They said: It is not permissible for the prophets to make a mistake. Those who held that every mujtahid is correct argued with the apparent meaning of the verse and the hadith where the reward was promised to the mujtahid for the mistake, and this is the saying of the people of opinion. A group held that not every mujtahid is correct, but rather if the ijtihad of two mujtahids differed in an incident, the truth would be with one, not with him specifically. If each one was correct, the division would have no meaning. His saying, peace be upon him: If he makes an effort and makes a mistake, he will have a reward, did not mean that he will be rewarded for the mistake, but rather he will be rewarded for his effort in seeking the truth because his effort is an act of worship, and the sin in making a mistake is removed from him if he does not spare any effort. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Abu Al-Zinad told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman Al-A’raj that he heard Abu Hurairah that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There were two women with their two sons, and a wolf came and took the son of one of them. Her companion said: He only took your son, and the other said: He only took your son. So they brought their case to David, and he ruled in favor of the elder. They went out to Solomon and told him, so he said: Bring me a knife so I can cut him between them. The younger said: Do not do that, may God have mercy on you, he is her son. So he ruled in favor of the younger.” God the Almighty said: And We subjected with David the mountains, to glorify God, and the birds, meaning, We subjected the mountains and the birds to glorify God with David when he glorified God. Ibn Abbas said: He understood the glorification of the stones and trees. Wahb said: The mountains would respond to him with glorification, and so would the birds. Qatada said: They would glorify, meaning they would pray with him when he prayed. It was said: When David became weary, God would let him hear the glorification of the mountains and the birds, so that he would be energized in glorifying God and long for Him. And We were to do, meaning: what was mentioned of making them understand, giving judgment, and subjecting them.
21:80: 80. And We taught him the craft of armour for you, and what is meant by armour here is shields because they are worn, and in the language it is a name for everything that is worn and used in all weapons, and it means what is worn like sitting and riding, Qatada said: The first to make armour, thread it and shape it was David, and before it was plates, and the armour combines lightness and strength, to fortify you, to protect you and prevent you, from your violence, meaning the war of your enemy, Al-Suddi said: from the weapon falling upon you, Abu Jaafar, Ibn Amir, Hafs from Asim and Yaqub read: to fortify you with a ta', meaning the craft, and Abu Bakr from Asim read with a noon because of his saying: And We taught him, and the others read with a ya', making the verb for the garment, and it was said: for God Almighty to fortify you, So are you grateful? He says to David and his family. And it was said: He says to the people of Mecca, so are you grateful for My blessings in obeying the Messenger.
21:81: 81. The Almighty said: And to Solomon We subjected the wind, blowing violently, meaning, We subjected the wind to Solomon, which is a moving air, and it is a delicate body that is prevented by its gentleness from being seized, and its movement is apparent to the senses. The wind is both masculine and feminine, a violent, violent blowing wind. If it is said: He said in another place, It flows gently by His command, and gentleness is gentleness? It is said: The wind was under his command, if he wanted it to be strong, it would be strong, and if he wanted it to be gentle, it would be gentle. It flows by His command to the land which We have blessed, meaning the Levant, and that is because it would flow for Solomon and his companions wherever Solomon wanted, then it would return to his home in the Levant. And We are of all things, We taught him, Knowing, of the correctness of the management in it. We knew that what Solomon was given of the subjection of the wind and other things called him to submit to his Lord, the Almighty. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Whenever Solomon, peace be upon him, went out to his council, the birds would flock to him and the jinn and humans would stand up for him until he sat on his throne. He was a man of war who rarely sat down from war, and he would not hear of a king in any part of the earth except that he would come to him and humiliate him. It is claimed that when he wanted to wage war, he would order his camp to be set up and a piece of wood would be pitched on the ground, then people, animals, and war machines would be loaded onto it. When he carried what he wanted, he would order a storm of wind to enter under that wood and carry it until it was able to carry it, and the wind would pass by him for a month in his evening and a month in his morning to wherever he wanted. The gentle wind would pass by his camp and the farm, but it would not move it, stir up dust, or harm a bird. Wahb said: It was mentioned to me that there was a house on the Tigris side, in which was written [written] by some of Solomon’s companions, either from the jinn or from mankind: We have settled in it, and we did not build it, and we found it built. We went out from Istakhr and said, and we are returning from it, God willing, so we will spend the night in Syria. Muqatil said: The devils wove for Solomon a carpet, a farsakh by a farsakh, of gold and silk. A pulpit of gold was placed for him in the middle of the carpet, and he would sit on it. Around it were three thousand chairs of gold and silver. The prophets would sit on the golden chairs, and the scholars on the silver chairs, and around them were the people, and around the people were the jinn and devils. The birds would shade him with their wings so that the sun would not fall on him, and the morning breeze would lift the carpet a month’s journey from morning to evening and from evening to morning. On the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: Six hundred thousand chairs were placed for Solomon, and the humans would sit on the one next to him, then the jinn would sit next to them, then the birds would shade them, then the wind would carry them. Al-Hassan said: When the horses occupied the Prophet of God, Solomon, peace be upon him, until he missed the afternoon prayer, he became angry for the sake of God Almighty and hamstrung the horses. God replaced them with better ones, and made the wind blow at his command as he wished. He would go out in the morning from Ilia and rest in Istakhr, then return from it and its rest would be in Kabul. Ibn Zayd said: He had a wooden ship that had a thousand corners, and in each corner were a thousand houses, and the jinn and humans rode with him in it. Under each corner were a thousand devils who raised that ship, and when it rose, a gentle wind would come and carry it and them. He would take a nap with a people who were a month away from him, and he would spend the evening with a people who were a month away from him. The people would not know until the armies had shaded them with him. It was narrated that Sulayman set out from the land of Iraq in the morning and prayed in the city of Marv, and prayed the afternoon prayer in the city of Balkh, the wind carrying him and his soldiers, and the birds shading them, then he set out from the city of Balkh, passing through the lands of the Turks, then he came to them to the land of China, going a month’s journey in the morning and returning in the same amount of time, then he turned right from the sunrise on the coast of the sea until he came to the land of Qandahar, and he went out from it to the land of Makran and Kerman, then he passed it until he came to the land of Persia, so he settled there for a few days and went out from there and said in Kaskar, then he went to the Levant, and his settlement was in the city of Tadmur, and the matter of the devils, before his departure from the Levant to Iraq, was that they built it for him with slabs and columns and white and yellow marble, and in that Al-Nabigha says: O Solomon, when the king said to him, Go into the wilderness and determine its location from the hotel. And the army of the jinn, I have given them permission to build Palmyra with stones and columns.
21:82: 82. The Almighty said: And of the devils, meaning, We subjected to him from the devils, some who dive for him, meaning, they go under the water and bring out for him from the bottom of the sea gems, and do work other than that, meaning other than diving, which is what God the Almighty mentioned: They make for him whatever he wills of shrines and statues (Saba’: 13) the verse. And We were their guardians, so that they would not go against His command. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that We protected them from corrupting what they had done. In the story, when Solomon sent a devil with a person to do a job for him, he would say to him: When he finishes his work before nightfall, occupy him with another job so that he does not corrupt what he has done. It was the habit of the devils that if they finished a job and did not occupy themselves with another job, they would ruin and corrupt what they had done.
21:83: 83. The Almighty said: And Job, when he called upon his Lord, meaning he called upon his Lord. Wahb bin Munabbih said: Job, peace be upon him, was a Roman man, and he was Job bin Amos bin Razeh bin Rum bin Isa bin Isaac bin Ibrahim. His mother was from the children of Lot bin Haran. God had chosen him, given him knowledge, and spread the world out for him. He had Al-Bathniyah in the land of Ash-Sham, all of it plain and mountainous. He had all kinds of wealth in it, from cows, camels, sheep, horses, and donkeys, such that no man would have had more than him in number and abundance. He had five hundred acres, followed by five hundred slaves, each slave had a wife, a child, and wealth. He carried a donkey for each acre, and each donkey gave birth to two, thirty, four, and five, and above that. God Almighty had given him a family and children, men and women. He was pious, God-fearing, and merciful to the poor. He fed the poor and took care of widows and orphans. He honored the guest and guided the wayfarer. He was grateful for God’s blessings and fulfilled God’s right. The enemy of God, Iblis, was prevented from afflicting him with what afflicts the rich people of delusion, heedlessness, and preoccupation with the worldly affairs of God. He was with three men who believed in him and confirmed him: a man from Yemen called Al-Yaqin, and two men from a town called Yaldad and Safir, and they were old men. Iblis was not prevented from anything in the heavens, and he would stand in them wherever he wanted until God raised Jesus, so he was prevented from four heavens. Then when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, he was prevented from the remaining three. Iblis heard the angels responding with prayers for Job, and that was when God mentioned him and praised him, so he was overcome by oppression and envy, so he quickly ascended until he stood in the heaven where he used to stand, and he said, “O God, I looked into the matter of Your servant Job and found him to be a servant upon whom You bestowed favors and he thanked You, and I healed him and he praised You. If You had tested him by taking away what You had given him, he would have changed from his state of thanking You and worshipping You, and he would have left Your obedience.” God, the Most High, said, Go, for I have given you power over his wealth. So the enemy of God, Iblis, attacked. Until he fell to the ground, then he gathered the jinn and the rebellious devils, and said to them: What power do you have? Then the enemy of God, Iblis, came in an ugly form, sitting on a camel, and found him standing praying. He said, O Job, a fire has come and covered your camels, burning them and everyone in them except me. Job said, “Praise be to God who gave it and took it. I have long since intended to destroy my wealth and myself.” Iblis said, “Your Lord sent fire from the sky upon it, and it burned, leaving people astounded and amazed by it. Some of them said, ‘Job did not worship anything, and he was only in delusion. ’ Some of them said, ‘If only he had been…’” Job's God is able to do something to prevent [his guardian], and some say: Rather, he did it so that his enemy would gloat and his friend would be sad. Job said: Praise be to God when He gave to me and when He took from me. Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, naked I shall return to the dust, and naked I shall be gathered to God. You should not rejoice when He lends you and grieve when He takes away what He has loaned from you. God is more deserving of you and of what He has given you. If God had known good in you, O servant, He would have transferred your soul with those souls and you would have become a martyr. But He knew evil in you and so He delayed you. So Iblis returned to his companions [disappointed], humiliated and disgraced, and said to them: What strength do you have? Then Iblis came to Job while he was praying, and said to him the same as the first time. Job responded to him the same as the first time. Then Iblis returned to his companions and said: What power do you have? I did not speak to Job’s heart. Then Iblis said: I have such power that if I wish, I can turn into a violent wind that blows away everything it comes upon. He said: Go to the fields and the crops. He went and they did not notice until a violent wind blew and blew away everything as if it had never been. Then Iblis came to Job while he was praying, and said to him the same as the first time. Job responded to him the same as the first time. Whenever he saw the loss of any of his wealth, he praised God and extolled Him. He was satisfied with his fate and prepared himself to be patient in the face of the affliction, until he had no money left. When Iblis saw that he had spent his wealth, he ascended [to heaven] and said, “O my God, Job sees that you did not give him enjoyment of his son, and you are giving him wealth. Will you give me power over his son?” This is a calamity that men’s hearts cannot withstand. God Almighty said, Go, for I have given you power over his son. So the enemy of God pounced until he came to the sons of Job while they were in their palace. He continued to shake them until it collapsed from its foundations. Then he began to clash its walls against each other and to throw wood and stones at them, until when he had mutilated them in every way, he lifted the palace and turned it over so that they were upside down. Then he went to Job, posing as the teacher who taught them wisdom, who was wounded and scratched in the face, his blood and brains flowing. He told him and said, “If you had seen how your sons were tortured and turned over so that they were upside down on their heads, their blood and brains flowing, and if you had seen how their bellies were ripped open and their intestines scattered, you would have cut them apart.” Your heart, and he kept saying this and similar things until Job felt pity and cried and took a handful of dirt and put it on his head and said: I wish my mother had not given birth to me. Satan took advantage of that and quickly ascended with what was from Job’s grief, happy with it. Then Job did not stay long before he regained his sight and sought forgiveness, and his companions from the angels ascended with his repentance, so his repentance preceded to God and He knows best. Satan stood humiliated and said: O my God, what made money and children easy for Job is that he sees from You that You did not give him pleasure in himself, so You return the money and children to him. Will You give me power over his body? Then God the Almighty said: Go, for I have given you authority over his body, but you have no authority over his tongue or his heart. God the Almighty knew him better and did not give him authority over him except out of mercy for him, to increase his reward and make him a lesson for the patient, and a reminder for the worshippers in every calamity that befalls them, so that they may follow his example in patience and hope for reward. So the enemy of God pounced quickly and found Job prostrating, so he hurried before he raised his head and came to him from the front and blew into his nostril a blast from which his entire body was set ablaze. From his horn to his feet came out warts like the humps of sheep, in which there was an itch. He scratched with his nails until they all fell off, then he scratched them with coarse sackcloth until he cut them off, then he scratched them with pottery and coarse stones. He continued scratching them until his flesh became raw, cut up, changed and putrid. The people of the village took him out and put him on a dustbin, and they made a hut for him, but all of God’s creation rejected him except his wife, who was Rahmah, daughter of Ephraim, son of Joseph, son of Jacob. She used to visit him with When the three of his companions, namely Yaqan, Yaldad and Safir, saw what God had afflicted him with, they accused him and rejected him without abandoning his religion. When the affliction became prolonged, they went to him, wept and blamed him, and said to him: Repent to God for the sin for which you were punished. He said: A young man was present with them who had believed in him and confirmed him, so he said to them: You have spoken, you old men, and you were more deserving of speaking than I because of your age, but you have left behind better words than what you said, and more correct opinions than what you saw, and more beautiful matters than what you have done. And Job had a better right and conscience over you than what you have described. Do you know, you old men, the right of whom you have diminished, and the sanctity of whom you have violated, and who is the man you have criticized and accused? Did you not know that Job was the prophet of God and the best of His creation and the elite of the people of the earth until this day of yours? Then you did not know, and God did not inform you of his affair, that He was displeased with him in any of his affair since God gave him what He gave him until this day of yours, nor that He took away from him any of the honor with which He honored him, nor that Job said about God other than the truth in the length of time you have accompanied him until this day of yours. If it was the affliction that disgraced him in your eyes and placed him in your souls, then you have known that God tests the believers, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous, and His affliction of those is not evidence of His displeasure with them or of His humiliation of them, but it is an honor and goodness for them. And if Job was not of this status with God except that he was a brother whom you loved for the sake of companionship, then it would not be appropriate for the forbearing person to reproach his brother when he was afflicted, nor to reproach him for the calamity, nor to criticize him for what he does not know while he is distressed and sad, but rather he has mercy on him and weeps with him, and seeks forgiveness for him, and is sad for his sadness, and guides him. On the guidance of his command, and he is not wise or wise from ignorance of this, so beware of God, O old men, and in the greatness and majesty of God, and the mention of death is what cuts your tongues and breaks your hearts, did you not know that God has servants who are silenced by fear of Him without defect or dumbness, and that they are the eloquent, the articulate, the noble, the intelligent, the knowledgeable of God, but when they mention the greatness of God, their tongues are cut off, their skins shudder, their hearts are broken, and their minds are lost in reverence and veneration for God Almighty, so when they wake up from that, they race to God Almighty with good deeds, counting themselves with the oppressors and sinners, and they are righteous and innocent, and with the negligent and the negligent, and they are wise and strong, so Job said: God Almighty plants wisdom with mercy in the heart of the young and the old, so when it grows in the heart, God reveals it on the tongue, and wisdom does not come from age and gray hair nor from long experience, and if God makes the servant wise in youth His status did not fall among the wise men, as they saw the light of honor bestowed upon him by God Almighty. Then Job turned away from them and turned to his Lord, seeking help and beseeching Him, and said, “My Lord, for what reason did You create me? If only You had known the sin that I committed and the work that I did, so that You would have turned Your noble face away from me. If only You had caused me to die and joined me with my noble fathers, death would have been more beautiful for me. Was I not a home for the stranger, a place of rest for the poor, a guardian for the orphan, and a guardian for the widow? My God, I am Your servant. If I do good, then Your grace is due to me, and if I do evil, then in Your hand is my punishment. You have made me an object of display and a burden for temptation. A calamity has befallen me, and if You had imposed it on a mountain that would be too weak to bear it, how could my weakness bear it? It is Your decree that has humiliated me, and it is Your authority that has made me sick and made my body thin. If my Lord had removed the awe that is in my chest and set my tongue free so that I could speak with a full mouth about what a servant should argue for himself, I would have hoped that He would cure me of what I am suffering from, but He said, He met me and was exalted above me, for He sees me and I do not see Him, and hears me and I do not hear Him. He did not look at me and have mercy on me, nor did He come near me or bring me near so that I may present my excuse and speak of my innocence and plead for myself. When Job and his companions said that, a cloud overshadowed him until his companions thought it was a painful torment. Then it was called, “O Job, God the Almighty says: Here I am, I have come near to you and have not ceased to be close to you. Arise and present your excuse, speak of your innocence, plead for yourself, strengthen your belt, and stand in the place of a tyrant who pleads with a tyrant if you are able, for no one should plead with Me except a tyrant like me. Your soul, O Job, has granted you a matter that you cannot achieve with the like of your strength. Where were you in relation to Me on the day I created the earth and placed it on its foundation? Were you with me, extending its edges? Did you know to what extent its power is or on what you placed its edges? Was it your obedience that the water carried the earth, or was it through your wisdom that the earth was a cover for the water? Where were you from me on the day when I raised the sky as a ceiling in the air, not suspended by the cause of those above it, nor supported by those below it? Will your wisdom be such that its light flows, or its stars move, or will its night and day differ by your command? Where are you from me on the day when We send forth the rivers and the seas are drowned? Did your authority hold back the waves of the seas at their limits? Or did your power open the wombs when they reached their term? Where were you from me on the day when I poured water on the soil and erected the lofty mountains? Do you know from what I anchored them? And with what weight I weighed them? Or do you have an arm that can carry them? Or do you know from where the water that You sent down from the sky comes from? Or do you know from what the clouds were created? Or do you know where the storehouses of snow are? Or where are the mountains of hail? Where is the storehouse of night with day [and the storehouse of day with night]? And where is the storehouse of the wind? And in what language do the trees speak? And who placed the minds in the hearts of men? And who split the ears and the eyes? And to whose kingdom the angels were humbled and who subdued the tyrants with his might? And who divided the provisions with his wisdom? In many words, He mentioned the effects of His power to Job, so Job said: My status is small and my tongue and mind are all behind me, and my strength has weakened from this matter that has befallen me, O my God. You know that everything that I have mentioned is the work of Your hands and the planning of Your wisdom, and greater and more amazing than that, if You willed, You could have done.
