Nothing is beyond You, and nothing is hidden from You. When the affliction befell me, O my God, I spoke and did not control my tongue, and it was the affliction that made me speak. I wish the earth had split open for me so that I could go into it and not say anything that would anger my Lord. I wish that I had died in my grief in my most severe affliction before that. I spoke when I spoke so that You would excuse me, and I was silent when I was silent so that You would have mercy on me. A word slipped from me, so I will not return. I have placed my hand over my mouth and bit my tongue, and stuck my cheek to the dust. I seek refuge in You today from You and I seek Your protection from the severity of the affliction, so protect me. I seek Your aid from Your punishment, so help me. I seek Your assistance in my matter, so help me. I rely on You, so suffice me, and I hold fast to You. So protect me, and I seek Your forgiveness, so forgive me, for I will not return to anything that You hate from me. God the Almighty said: O Job, My knowledge has been carried out regarding you, and My mercy has preceded My wrath. So I have forgiven you, and I have restored to you your family and your wealth and the like of them with them, so that you may be a sign for those who come after you, and a lesson for the afflicted and a consolation for the patient. So strike with your foot, this is a cool bath and a drink in which is your healing, and offer an offering to your companions, and ask forgiveness for them, for they have disobeyed Me regarding you. So he struck with his foot, and a spring gushed forth for him, so he entered it, and God removed from him all the affliction that had befallen him. Then he went out and sat down, and his wife came looking for him in his bed, but she did not find him, so she stood up like a bewildered woman, then she said: O servant of God, do you know about the afflicted man who was here? He said to her: Would you recognize him if you saw him? She said: Yes, and why should I not know him? So he smiled and said: I am he, and she recognized him by his laughter, so she embraced him. Ibn Abbas said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Abdullah, he did not leave his embrace until all their wealth and children had passed by them. This is what God Almighty said: “And Job, when he cried to his Lord, ‘Indeed, adversity has touched me.’” They differed about the time of his call and the reason for which he said, Indeed, adversity has touched me, and about the duration of his affliction. Ibn Shihab narrated on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, that Job remained in his affliction for eighteen years. Wahb said: Job remained in affliction for three years, not a day longer. Kaab said: Job was in his affliction for seven years, seven months and seven days. Al-Hasan said: Job remained lying on a rubbish dump in the garbage dump of the Children of Israel for seven years and months, with animals swarming around him, and no one would approach him except for mercy, which was patient with him sincerely, bringing him food and praising God with him when he praised Him. Job, despite that, did not stop remembering God and being patient with his affliction. Then Satan cried out a cry in which he gathered his soldiers from all corners of the earth. When they gathered around him, they said: What is your sorrow? He said: This slave, for whom I left neither wealth nor children, has exhausted me, but he only increased his patience. Then I took control of his body and left him as an ulcer lying on a rubbish dump, and no one would approach him except his wife. I sought your help to help me against him, and they said to him: Where is your plot by which you destroyed those who came before? He said: All of that has become useless in Job, so advise me. They said: We advise you, where did you come from Adam when you expelled him from Paradise? He said: From his wife. They said: What about Job from his wife? He cannot disobey her and no one else has the right to approach him. He said: You are right. So he set off until he came to his wife while she was giving charity. He appeared to her in the form of a man and said: Where is your husband, O servant of God? She said: He is scratching his sores and the insects are circling his body. When he heard it, he hoped that it was a word of impatience, so he whispered to her and reminded her of the blessings and wealth she had, and he reminded her of Job’s beauty and youth and the hardship he was in and that this would never end for them. Al-Hasan said: So she cried out, and when she cried out, he knew that she had become impatient, so he brought her a goat and said: Let Job slaughter this for me and be healed. She came crying: O Job, how long will your Lord torment you? Where is the wealth, where are the children, where is the friend, where is your beautiful color, where is your beautiful body? Slaughter this goat and rest. Job said: The enemy of God has come to you and breathed into you, woe to you! Have you seen what you are crying over of wealth, children and health? Who gave it to me? She said: God. He said: How long have we been given enjoyment of it? She said: Eighty years. He said: Since when have we been tested? She said: Seven years and a few months ago. He said: Woe to you! You have not been fair. Have you not been patient in affliction for eighty years, just as we were in prosperity for eighty years? By God, if God heals me, I will flog you a hundred lashes. You have ordered me to slaughter for other than God. Your food and drink that you have brought me is forbidden to me [or is forbidden to me] to taste anything of what you bring me after you have said this to me. So go away from me, so that I may not see you. So he drove her away and she went away. When Job saw that he had no food, drink, or friend, he fell down in prostration and said: O Lord, Verily, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. So it was said to him: Raise your head, for your request has been answered. Strike with your foot. So he struck with his foot, and a spring gushed forth, so he washed himself from it. Nothing of his illness remained apparent except that it fell off, and his youth and beauty returned to him better than before. Then he struck with his foot, and another spring gushed forth, so he drank from it. There remained no illness in his body except that it came out. So he stood up healthy and dressed in a robe. He said: So he began to look around and did not see anything of his family and wealth except that it had God weakened him until, by God, He mentioned to us that the water in which he washed himself, golden locusts flew onto his chest, so he began to hold them in his hand. God revealed to him, O Job, have I not enriched you? He said, Yes, but it is your blessing, so who can be satisfied with it? He said, “So he went out and sat on a prominent place. Then his wife said, “What do you think, if he expelled me to someone who ate him? Should I leave him to die of hunger and be lost and eaten by wild beasts? I will return to him, and no sweeping place will be seen, nor will there be that state that was before.” And if things had changed, she began to go around where the sweeping place was and weep, and that was in Job’s eyes, and the owner of the estate was afraid to come to him and ask him about him. So Job called her and said, What do you want, O servant of God? She wept and said, “I wanted that afflicted one who was rejected on the sweeping place. I do not know whether he was lost or what he did.” Job said, What happened? She wept and said, My husband. He said, Would you recognize him if you saw him? She said, Would he be hidden from anyone who saw him? Then she looked at him in awe of him, then she said: He is the most similar of God’s creation to you, since he is healthy. He said: I am Job, whom you ordered to sacrifice to Satan, and I obeyed God, disobeyed Satan, and called upon God, the Exalted, and He responded to what you see. Wahb said: Job remained in the affliction for three years. When Job defeated Satan and could not do anything to him, he came to his wife in a form that was not like the form of the sons of Adam in size, body and beauty, on a mount that was not like the mounts of people, but had greatness, splendor and perfection. He said to her: Are you the companion of this afflicted man, Job? She said: Yes. He said: Do you know me? She said: No. He said: I am the god of the earth, and I am the one who did to your companion what I did because he was a servant of the god of the heavens and left me, so he angered me. If he prostrated to me once, I would return to him and to you all that you had of wealth and children, for they are with me. Then he showed them to her in the valley where he had met her. Wahb said: I heard that he only said to her: If your companion had not mentioned the name of God over him, he would have been cured of the affliction that he had. And God knows best. In some books: Satan said to her: Prostrate to me once so that I may return your money and children to you and heal your husband. So she returned to Ayoub and told him what he had said to her [and I do not think she did]. He said: The enemy of God has come to you to tempt you away from your religion. Then he swore [that if God healed him] that he would strike her a hundred lashes. Then he said: Harm has befallen me because of Satan’s desire for my wife to prostrate to him and his calling her and me to disbelief. Then God Almighty had mercy on Ayoub’s wife because of her patience with him in the face of the affliction, and made things easy for her and wanted to fulfill Ayoub’s oath, so He ordered him to take a bunch of sticks containing a hundred small sticks and strike her with it once, as God Almighty said: And take in your hand a bunch and strike with it and do not break your oath (Sad: 44). It was narrated that Satan took a coffin and put medicines in it and sat on his wife’s path treating people. Ayoub’s wife passed by him and he said [O old man], I have a sick person, should I redeem him? He said, "Yes, by God, and I do not want anything except for him to say, If you heal him, you will heal me. So I mentioned that to Ayoub, and he said, It is Satan who has deceived you," and he swore that if God healed him, he would strike her with a hundred lashes. Wahb and others said: Job’s wife used to work for the people and bring him his food. When the affliction became prolonged and the people grew tired of her and no one employed her, one day she looked for something to feed him but found nothing, so she cut a horn from her head and sold it for a loaf of bread and brought it to him. He said to her: Where is your horn? So she told him, and then he said: Harm has befallen me. Some people said: He only said that when the worms intended to attack his heart and tongue, and he feared that he would stop remembering and thinking. Habib bin Abi Thabit said: He did not ask God to reveal it until three things became apparent to him. The first: Two friends came to him when they heard about him. They came to him and he had nothing left but his eyes. They saw a great matter and said: If you had a status with God, this would not have happened to you. The second: His wife asked for food but could not find anything to eat, so she sold her forelock and brought him food. The third: Satan said: I will heal him, so that he would say: You healed me. It was said: Satan whispered to him that his wife had committed adultery, so he cut off her forelock. At that moment, his patience ran out, so he prayed and swore to flog her a hundred lashes. It was also said: Its meaning is that harm has befallen me from the gloating of enemies. It was even narrated that it was said to him [after he recovered], what was most difficult for you in your affliction? He said: The gloating of enemies. It was also said: He said that when a worm fell from his thigh, so he put it back in its place. And Klee said: God has made me your food, so I bit him with a bite that was more painful than all the bites of worms he had suffered. If it is said: God called him patient, and he showed complaint and distress, by saying: Verily, distress has touched me, and Satan has touched me with hardship (Surah Sad: 41), it is said: This is not a complaint, but rather a supplication, as evidenced by the saying of God the Almighty: So We responded to him, and that distress is only in complaining to creation, but as for complaining to God the Almighty, it is not distress nor abandoning patience, as Jacob said: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God (Surah Yusuf 12:86). Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Likewise, whoever shows complaint to people while being satisfied with God’s decree, that is not distress, as it was narrated that “Gabriel entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his illness and said: How do you find yourself? He said: I find myself sad and I find myself distressed.” He said to Aisha when she said, Oh my head, but rather, Oh my head.
21:84: 84. The Almighty said: So We responded to him and removed the affliction that was upon him, and that is because he said, Strike with your foot, so he struck with his foot and a spring [of water] gushed forth. So He ordered him to wash from it, so he did, and every illness that was on his outside went away. Then he walked forty steps, and He ordered him to strike the ground with his foot again, so he did, and a spring of cold water gushed forth. So He ordered him to drink from it, and every affliction that was on his inside went away, as healthy as can be, so a spring of cold water gushed forth. So He ordered him to drink from it, and every illness that was on his inside went away, and he became as healthy as can be among men and as handsome as can be. And We gave him his family and the like of them with them. They differed on that. Ibn Masoud, Qatada, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and most of the commentators said: God Almighty returned his family and children to him in their entirety. God revived them for him and gave him the like of them with them, and this is the apparent meaning of the Qur’an. Al-Hasan said: God gave him the equivalent of the offspring of his wealth that God restored [to him and his family]. This is indicated by what Al-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas narrated that God Almighty restored the woman’s youth and she bore him twenty-six sons. Wahb said he had seven daughters and three sons. Ibn Yasar said: He had seven sons and seven daughters. It was narrated on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, that he had two troughs, one for wheat and one for barley. Then God Almighty sent two clouds, one of which poured gold on the trough of wheat and the other poured paper on the trough of barley until it overflowed. It was narrated that God Almighty sent an angel to him and said: Your Lord sends you peace for your patience, so go out to your destination. So he went out to him and God sent golden locusts upon him. One flew away, so he sold it and returned it to his destination. The angel said to him: Is what is in your destination not enough for you? He said: This is a blessing from my Lord, and I will never be satisfied with His blessings. Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “While Job was bathing naked, golden locusts fell upon him. Job began to gather them in his garment, and his Lord called out to him, ‘O Job, was I not independent of what you see?’ He said, ‘Yes, my Lord, by Your glory, but I cannot do without Your blessing.’” Some people said: God gave Job in this world the same as his family who perished, but as for those who perished, they did not return to him in this world. Ikrimah said: It was said to Job: Your family is yours in the Hereafter, so if you wish, We will hasten them for you in this world, and if you wish, they will be yours in the Hereafter. And We have given you the like of them in this world. He said: They will be for me in the Hereafter, and he was given the like of them in this world. So based on this, the meaning of the verse is: And We have given him his family in the Hereafter and the like of them with them in this world. And by family he meant children, a mercy from Us, meaning a blessing from Us, and a reminder for the worshippers, meaning: a lesson and a warning for them.
21:85: 85. The Almighty said: And Ishmael, meaning the son of Abraham, and Idris, who is Enoch, and Dhul-Kifl, all were among the patient, in the command of God, and they differed about Dhul-Kifl. Ata’ said: God revealed to a prophet of the Children of Israel: I want to take your soul, so offer your kingdom to the Children of Israel. Whoever guarantees that he will pray at night without slackening, fast during the day without breaking his fast, and judge between people without getting angry, then give your kingdom to him. So he did that. Then a young man stood up and said: I will guarantee this for you. So he guaranteed it and fulfilled it. So God thanked him and informed him, and he was named Dhul-Kifl. Mujahid said: When Al-Yasa’ grew old, he said: [If] I were to appoint a man as my successor over the people, who would work for them during my lifetime, so that I could see how he would work. He said: So he gathered the people and said: Whoever accepts three things from me, I will appoint him as my successor: he fasts during the day, stands in prayer at night, and does not get angry. Then a man whom the eye despises stood up and said: I will. So he turned him back that day, and said the same thing the next day, and the people were silent. Then that man stood up and said: I will. So he appointed him as his successor, and Satan came to him in the form of a weak old man when he went to bed for the afternoon nap, and he did not sleep at night [or during the day] except for that sleep, so he knocked on the door and said: Who is this? He said: An old, oppressed man. So he got up and opened the door and said: There is a dispute between me and my people, and they have wronged me, and this and that. So he kept on prolonging it until the afternoon came and the midday meal was over. Then he said: When you go, come to me, for I will take your right. So he went and went. He was in his council, waiting to see if he could see the old man, but he did not see him. So he got up looking for him, and the next day he sat down to judge between the people and waited for him, but he did not see him. When he returned to the afternoon meal and went to bed, he came to him and knocked on the door. He said: Who is this? He said: The oppressed old man. So he opened [the door for him] and he said: Didn’t I tell you that when you sit down, come to me? He said: They are the most wicked people. If they know that you are sitting, they say, We will give you your right, and if you stand up, they deny me. He said: Then go, and when you go, come to me. So he missed the siesta and went and looked but did not see him, and drowsiness overcame him, so he said to one of his family: Do not let anyone come near this door until I sleep, for sleep has become difficult for me. At that time, he came but the man did not give him permission. When he was exhausted, he looked and saw a window in the house, so he climbed through it, and behold, he was in the house knocking on the door from inside. He woke up and said: O so-and-so, did I not command you? He said: As for those before me, you were not given permission, so look from where you came. He went to the door and behold, it was locked as he had locked it, and the man was with him in the house. He said: Do you sleep while the opponents are at your door? So he recognized him and said: Are they the enemies of God? He said: Yes, you exhausted me, so I did what you see to anger you, but God protected you. So he was called Dhul-Kifl because he undertook a matter and fulfilled it. It was said that Satan came to him and said: I have a debtor who is delaying payment, so I would like you to stand with me and collect my right from him. So he went with him, and when he was in the market, he left him and went away. It was narrated that he apologized to him and said: My friend ran away. It was said: Dhul-Kifl was a man who promised to pray one hundred rak’ahs every night until God took him, and he fulfilled his promise. They differed as to whether he was a prophet. Some of them said: He was a prophet. It was said: He was Elias. It was said: Zachariah. Abu Musa said: He was not a prophet, but a righteous servant.
21:86: 86. And We admitted them into Our mercy, meaning what God bestowed upon them of prophethood and the reward He granted them in Paradise, for they are among the righteous.
21:87: 87. The Almighty’s saying: And Dhul-Nun, meaning: Remember the companion of the whale, who was Jonah, son of Matta, when he went away in anger, they differed about its meaning: Ad-Dahhak said: In anger with his people. This is the narration of Al-Awfi and others on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He said: Jonah and his people were living in Palestine, and a king invaded them and took nine and a half tribes captive, leaving one and a half tribes. So God inspired the prophet Isaiah to go to King Hezekiah and tell him to send a strong prophet, for I will cast terror into the hearts of those people until they send the Children of Israel with him. The king said to him: Who do you think he is? There were five prophets in his kingdom. Jonah said: He is strong and trustworthy. So the king called Jonah and ordered him to go out. Jonah said to him: Did God order you to send me out? He said: No. He said: Did He name me to you? He said: No. He said: There are other strong prophets here besides me. They insisted on him, so he went out from among them, in anger with the prophet, the king, and his people. He came to the Roman Sea and rode it. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa`id ibn Jubayr and a group said: He left his people in anger at his Lord, because He had removed the punishment from his people after He had threatened them. He hated to be among people who had experienced him breaking his promise to them, and he was ashamed of them. He did not know the reason for the lifting of the punishment. His anger was out of disdain for the appearance of breaking his promise, and that he would be called a liar, not out of hatred for the judgment of God Almighty. In some reports, it was the custom of his people to kill anyone they found lying to, so he feared that they would kill him when the punishment had not come to them as promised, so he became angry. Here, anger is like the reciprocal verb that comes from one, like travel and punishment, so the meaning of his saying angry is angry. Al-Hasan said: He was angry with his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, because He had ordered him to go to his people to warn them of His wrath and call them to Him. So he asked his Lord to give him time to prepare to go to them, but he was told that the matter would be faster than that, so he asked to be given time to get a sandal to wear, but he was not given time, and he was in a tight disposition [so he went away angry]. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, Gabriel came to Yunus and said: Go to the people of Nineveh and warn them. He said: Look for a beast. He said: The matter is more urgent than that. So he became angry and went to the ship. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Yunus ibn Matta was a righteous servant, but his character was narrow. When the burdens of prophethood were placed upon him, he collapsed under them as a quarter collapses under a heavy load, so he threw it from his hand and fled from it. Therefore, God removed him from the most determined of the messengers, saying to His Prophet [Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace]: So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will (al-Ahqaf 46:35), and He said: And be not like the companion of the fish (al-Qalam 68:48). God the Almighty said: So he thought that We would not decree punishment for him, meaning that We would not pass judgment on him. This was stated by Mujahid, Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, and Al-Kalbi. It is the narration of Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. It is said: God has decreed something with a decree and He has decreed with a decree meaning one thing. This is the case with His statement: We have decreed death among you (al-Waqi’ah 56:60) in the reading of those who read it with a light vowel. Evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Umar ibn Abdul Aziz and Az-Zuhri: So he thought that We would not decree punishment for him, with a heavy vowel. Ata’ and many scholars said: Its meaning is that he thought that We would not restrict his imprisonment, from God the Almighty’s statement: God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it (Ar-Ra’d: 26), meaning restricts it. Ibn Zayd said: It is an interrogative meaning: Did he think that his Lord would be unable to do anything to him, so He would not be able to do anything to him? And Ya’qub read Yaqdur with a damma on the ya’ in the passive voice, light. On the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: It has reached me that when Yunus committed the sin, he set out in anger with his Lord, and Satan made him slip until he thought that We would not have power over him. He had a predecessor and worshipped God, but God refused to leave him to Satan, so He cast him into the belly of the whale, and he remained in it for forty days and nights. Ata’ said: Seven days (and it was said: Three days). It was said: The whale took him a journey of six thousand years. It was said: He reached the borders of the seventh earth, so he repented to his Lord, the Most High, in the belly of the whale, and reviewed himself and said: There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers, when I disobeyed You and did nothing, so I will not worship other than You. So God brought him out of the belly of the whale by His mercy. The previous interpretations are more appropriate for the state of the prophets, that he set out in anger with his people or with the king, So he called out in the darkness, meaning the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the whale, There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God inspired the whale to take him and do not scratch his flesh or break his bones. So he took him and then threw him down to his home in the sea. When he reached the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound and said to himself, What is this? Then God inspired him: This is the glorification of sea creatures. He said: So he glorified God while he was in the belly of the whale. The angels heard his glorification and said: Our Lord, we hear a weak voice in a strange land, and in another narration, a known voice from an unknown place. He said: “That is My servant Yunus. He disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the whale.” They said: Is that the righteous servant who used to ascend to You from Him every day and night a righteous deed? He said: Yes. So they interceded for him. Then He ordered the whale to throw him up on the shore, as God Almighty said: So We cast him out upon the open shore while he was sick. 37:145
21:88: 88. This is what God Almighty said: So We responded to him, meaning: We answered him, and saved him from the distress, from that darkness, and thus do We save the believers, from every distress when they call upon Us and seek help. Ibn Amir and Asim read, according to the narration of Abu Bakr: Naji with one nun and a shaddah on the jim and a sukoon on the ya because it is written in the Qur’an with one nun. The grammarians differed regarding this reading, and most of them went to the view that it is a mistake because if it was on what its agent was not named, the ya would not be sukoon and the believers would be raised, and some of them corrected it, and Al-Farra’ mentioned that it has another meaning, which is the omission of the source, meaning the salvation saved the believers, and the believers are in the accusative case like you say: The darb struck Zaydan, then you say Zaydan struck with the accusative case on the omission of the source, and the ya is sukoon in Naji as they are in Baqa and the like. Al-Qatibi said: Whoever reads with one nun and a shaddah, then he only meant Naji from tanjiyyah, except that he assimilated and deleted a nun in order to make it lighter, and the grammarians did not accept that. Because the point of articulation of the letter nun is far from the letter jim, and assimilation occurs when the point of articulation is close, and the common people read nanji with two nuns from injaa, and it was written with one nun because the second nun was silent and the silent letter was not apparent on the tongue, so it was deleted as they did in illa, so they deleted the nun from inna because of its concealment. And they differed about when the message of Yunus was? Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was after God brought him out of the belly of the whale, as evidenced by the fact that God the Almighty mentioned it in Surat Al-Saffat, So We cast him out upon the open shore (al-Saffat 37:145), then He mentioned after it: And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more (al-Saffat 37:147), and the others said: It was before, as evidenced by the Almighty’s saying: And indeed, Yunus was among the messengers * When he fled to the laden ship (al-Saffat 37:139-140).
21:89: 89. The Almighty said: And Zachariah, when he called upon his Lord, he called upon his Lord, My Lord, leave me not alone, alone with no children, and provide me with an heir, and You are the best of inheritors, praising God that He is the One who remains after the destruction of creation and that He is the best of those who remain alive.
21:90: 90. So We responded to him and gave him John, a son, and made his wife good for him, meaning We made her fertile after she had been barren, most of the commentators said, and some of them said: She was ill-tempered, so He made her good for him by granting her good character. They, meaning the prophets whom He named in this surah, used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope, hope, and fear, fear, desire for the mercy of God, and fear of the punishment of God, and they were humble before Us, meaning humble, Qatada said: submissive to the command of God. Mujahid said: Humility is the fear that is necessary in the heart.
21:91: 91. And she who guarded her chastity, protected herself from what is forbidden, and he meant Mary, daughter of Imran, So We breathed into her of Our spirit, that is, We commanded Gabriel until he breathed into the pocket of her garment, and with that breath We caused Christ to breathe into her womb, and He added the spirit to it as an honor for Jesus, peace be upon him, And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds, that is, an indication of the perfection of Our ability to create a child without a father, and He did not say two signs when they are two signs because the meaning of the speech is And We made their affair and matter a sign and because the sign was one in them, which is that she brought him forth without a male.
21:92: 92. The Almighty’s saying, Indeed, this is your nation, meaning your religion and your faith, one nation, meaning one religion, which is Islam. He invalidated all religions other than Islam, and the origin of the nation is the group that has one goal, so the Shari’ah made it one nation because its people gathered for one goal, and the accusative of nation is to definite. And I am your Lord, so worship Me.
21:93: 93. And they divided their affair among themselves, meaning they differed in religion and became sects and parties. Al-Kalbi said: [They divided their religion among themselves] cursing each other and disowning each other. And here division means severance. "All will return to Us, so We will reward them according to their deeds.
21:94: 94. So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - no denial will there be for his effort, he will not be denied nor will his effort be invalidated, rather he will be thanked and rewarded for it, and indeed, We are its recorders, preserving his work. It was said: The meaning of thanks from God is reward.
21:95: 95. "And it is forbidden for a village," Haza, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr read: "And it is forbidden, breaking the ha' without an alif, and the rest read it with an alif haram," and they are two dialects like halal and halal. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning of the verse is It is forbidden for a village, that is, the people of a village, “We destroyed it, to return after destruction. So based on this, la is a conjunction. Others said: The forbidden means the obligatory. So based on this, la is fixed, meaning it is obligatory for the people of a village, We destroyed it, “that they not return,” to the world. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that it is forbidden for the people of a village that We destroyed, that is, We decreed their destruction, that their deeds be accepted because they do not return, that is, they do not repent. The evidence for this meaning is that He said in the verse before it: So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there is no denial for his effort, that is, his work is accepted. Then he mentioned this verse after it and explained that the work of the disbeliever is not accepted.
21:96: 96. The Almighty said: Until when it is opened, Ibn Amir, Abu Ja`far and Ya`qub read: opened with emphasis to indicate abundance, and the others read it with emphasis, Gog and Magog, meaning the opening of the barrier for Gog and Magog, and they from every mound, meaning a high place and hill, and a mound is a high place, they rush down, they quickly descend from the hills and mountains like the rush of a wolf, which is the speed of its gait, and they differed about this metaphor, so some people said: He meant by them Gog and Magog based on what we narrated on the authority of Al-Nawwas bin Sam`an on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: And God will send forth Gog and Magog and they rush down from every mound, and some people said: He meant all of creation, meaning that they will emerge from their graves, and this is indicated by the reading of Mujahid, and they from every grave with a jim and a tha’ as he said: Then from the graves they rush to their Lord (Yunus 10:51). Ismail bin Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad Al-Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Hajjaj told us, Abu Khaithama Zuhair bin Harb told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Furat Al-Qazzaz, on the authority of Abu Al-Tufayl, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Asid Al-Ghifari, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at us while we were talking and said: What are you talking about? They said: We are talking about the Hour. He said: It will not come until you see ten signs before it. So he mentioned the smoke, the Antichrist, the beast, the rising of the sun from the west, the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, Gog and Magog, and three landslides: one in Al-Maghraf, one in the east, and one in the Arabian Peninsula. The last of these will be a fire that will emerge from Yemen and drive people to their place of assembly.”
21:97: 97. The Almighty’s statement: And the true promise has drawn near, meaning the Resurrection. Al-Farra’ and a group said: The waw in his statement and has drawn near is an insertion, so its meaning is until Gog and Magog are conquered, the true promise has drawn near, as God Almighty said: So when they had both submitted and he laid him down on his forehead, * And We called to him (al-Saffat 37:103), meaning We called to him. The evidence for this is what was narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: If a man acquired a foal after the emergence of Gog and Magog, he would not ride it until the Hour comes. Some people said: It is not permissible to omit the waw, and they made it the answer to until when you open it in his saying O woe to us, so it is a metaphor for the verse. Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose and the true promise draws near, they will say, Woe to us! We were indeed heedless of this. His saying: Then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring. There are three aspects to His saying it will be. The first is that it is a metaphor for sight. Then He made sight clear, meaning, Then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring. The second: that it is a pillar, as in His saying: For indeed, eyes are not blind (al-Hajj 22:46). The third: That the end of the speech is at His saying: (it), with the meaning of then it is prominent, meaning from its proximity as if it is present, then He began: The eyes of those who disbelieve are staring, by presenting the report before the beginning, its metaphor is the eyes of those who disbelieve are staring. Al-Kalbi said: The eyes of the disbelievers were staring and could hardly blink from the intensity and horror of that day, they said, Woe to us! We were heedless of this, the day, but we were wrongdoers, by placing worship in the wrong place.
21:98: 98. You, O polytheists, and what you worship besides God, meaning the idols, are the firewood of Hell, meaning its fuel. Mujahid and Qatadah said: its firewood, and firewood in the language of the people of Yemen means firewood. Ikrimah said: it is firewood in the language of Abyssinia. Ad-Dahhak said: meaning they throw them into the fire as pebbles are thrown. The origin of hasb is throwing. God the Almighty said: We sent upon them a wind of stones (al-Qamar 54:34), meaning a wind that throws stones at them. Ali ibn Abi Talib read: firewood of Hell, you will enter it, meaning you will enter it.
21:99: 99. If these, meaning the idols, were gods in reality, they would not have entered it, meaning their worshippers would not have entered the Fire, and all are therein eternally, meaning the worshipper and the worshipped.
21:100: 100. Therein they will have a sigh, and they will not hear therein. Ibn Mas`ud said: In this verse, if there remain in the Fire those who will remain therein eternally in coffins of fire, then those coffins will be placed in other coffins [then those coffins in other coffins] with nails of fire on them, they will not hear anything and none of them will see that there is anyone in the Fire who is being tortured other than him. Then he made an exception and said:
21:101: 101. Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us, some scholars said: Indeed here means: except for those for whom good has preceded from Us, meaning happiness and the beautiful provision in Paradise, those will be removed from it, it was said: the verse is general and applies to all for whom happiness has preceded from God. Most of the commentators said: He meant by that everyone who worshipped other than God and was obedient to God and hated the worship of the one he worshipped. That is because “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the mosque and the leaders of Quraysh were in Al-Hatim and around the Kaaba there were three hundred and sixty idols. Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith appeared to him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to him until he silenced him. Then he recited to him: “Indeed, you and what you worship other than God are fuel for Hell,” the three verses. Then he stood up and Abdullah Al-Zubayri Al-Sahmi approached him and Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah told him what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said to them. Abdullah said: By God, if I had found him, I would have argued with him. So they called the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ibn Al-Zubayri said to him: Did you say: Indeed, you and what you worship other than God are fuel for Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Do not the Jews worship Ezra and the Christians worship Christ, and the Banu Malih worship the angels? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, they worship the devils. Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us. Meaning Ezra, the Messiah, and the angels, those are far removed from it. And it was revealed about Ibn al-Zubayri: “They did not present it to you except to argue. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.” (al-Zukhruf 43:58). A group claimed that what is meant by the verse is the idols, because God Almighty said: And what you worship besides God. And if He had meant by it the angels and people, He would have said, And those you worship besides God.
21:102: 102. They will not hear its hissing sound, meaning its sound and the movement of its flames when they descend to their homes in Paradise. The sense and the hissing sound are the hidden sound: And they will abide in that which their souls desire, residing as He said: And therein is whatever the souls desire and delights the eyes (al-Zukhruf 43:71).
21:103: 103. The greatest terror will not grieve them. Ibn Abbas said: The greatest terror is the last blast, as evidenced by the words of God the Almighty: And the Day the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will be terrified. (al-Naml 27:87). Al-Hasan said: Until the servant is ordered to the Fire. Ibn Jurayj said: When death is slaughtered and it is called out, O people of Paradise, eternal life and no death! And O people of Hell, eternal life and no death! Saeed bin Jubair and Ad-Dahhak said: It is when Hell closes in on them, after God brings out from it whomever He wants to bring out. And the angels will meet them, meaning the angels will meet them at the gates of Paradise, congratulating them and saying, This is your Day which you were promised.
21:104: 104. The Day We fold the heaven, Abu Ja`far read: yatwa with a ta’ and a damma and a fatha on the waw, and the heaven, raised in the passive voice, and the general public read with a nun and a fatha and a kasra on the waw, and the heaven, accusative, like folding the scroll for the books, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Hafs from Asim read for the books in the plural, and the others read for the book in the singular, and they differed about the scroll, so Al-Suddi said: The scroll is an angel who writes down the deeds of the servants, and the lam is redundant, meaning like folding the scroll of the books like His saying He has followed you (al-Naml 27:72), the lam in it is redundant, and Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and the majority said: The scroll is the newspaper for the books, meaning for what was written, meaning like folding the newspaper on its written one, and the scroll is a noun derived from the writing, which is correspondence, and folding is the stairs which is the opposite of spreading, as We began the first creation, We will repeat it, meaning as We began them in the wombs of their mothers, barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, thus We will return them on the Day of Resurrection, similar to the saying of God Almighty: And you have certainly come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time. (Al-An`am: 94), and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You will be gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. Then he recited: As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. “A promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.” He meant the return and resurrection.
21:105: 105. The Almighty said: And We had already written in the Psalms, after the Reminder, Saeed bin Jubair and Mujahid said: The Psalms are all the revealed books, and the Reminder is the mother of the book that is with Him, and the meaning is after what was written is His remembrance in the Preserved Tablet. Ibn Abbas and Al-Dahhak said: The Psalms are the Torah and the Reminder are the books revealed after the Torah. Al-Sha'bi said: The Psalms are the Book of David, [and the Remembrance is the Torah. It was said: The Psalms are the Psalms of David] and the Remembrance is the Qur'an, and after means before, like the Almighty's saying: And behind them was a king (al-Kahf 18:79): meaning in front of them, And after that He spread out the earth (An-Nazi'at: 30) before it, that the earth, meaning the land of Paradise, My righteous servants will inherit it, Mujahid said: He means the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as evidenced by the Almighty's saying: And they said, 'Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth' (al-Zumar 39:74), and Ibn Abbas said: He meant that the lands of the infidels would be conquered by the Muslims, and this is a ruling from God to make the religion prevail and the Muslims be honored. It was said: He meant by the land the Holy Land.
21:106: 106. Indeed in this, meaning in the Qur'an, is a message, reaching the goal, meaning whoever follows the Qur'an and acts upon it will reach the reward he hopes for. It was said: a message, meaning sufficiency. It is said about this thing a message and a message, meaning sufficiency, and the Qur'an is the provision of Paradise like the message of the traveler, for a people who worship, meaning the believers who worship God, and Ibn Abbas said: knowledgeable. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: They are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the people of the five daily prayers and the month of Ramadan.
21:107: 107. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds. Ibn Zayd said: He means a mercy for the believers specifically, so he is a mercy for them. [And Ibn Abbas said: It is general for those who believe and those who do not believe. So whoever believes, he is a mercy for him] in this world and the hereafter, and whoever does not believe, he is a mercy for him in this world by delaying the punishment for them and removing the transformation, the sinking, and the extermination from them. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am only a mercy sent.
21:108: 108. "Say, 'It is only revealed to me that your God is one God. So will you submit?'" That is, submit.
21:109: 109. "But if they turn away, then say, 'I have warned you,' meaning, I have informed you of the war and that there will be no peace between us, 'on an equal footing,' meaning, a warning between those who are equal in their knowledge, not seeking permission for it without you, so that you may prepare for what is intended for you, meaning, I have warned you in a way that we and you are equal in knowledge of it. It was said: so that you may be equal in faith, 'and I do not know,' meaning, and I do not know, 'is near or far what you are promised,' meaning the Resurrection.
21:110: 110. He knows what you say aloud and knows what you conceal.
21:111: 111. And I do not know that perhaps it is, meaning perhaps the delay of the punishment from you is a metaphor for something not mentioned, a trial, a test, for you, so that He may see how you will act, and He knows best, and provision for a time, meaning that you will enjoy yourself until your appointed times come to an end.
21:112: 112. He said, 'My Lord, judge with truth', Hafs read from Asim: He said, 'My Lord, judge', and the others: He said, 'My Lord, judge' judge between me and he who denied me with the truth, so if it is said, how did he say, 'Ahem, with truth' when God does not judge except with truth? It is said: The truth here means punishment as if he hastened the punishment for his people so they were punished on the day of Badr, similar to the saying of God Almighty: Our Lord, judge between us and our people with truth (al-A’raf 7:89), and the people of meaning said: its meaning is, My Lord, judge with Your true judgment so the judgment was omitted and the truth was put in its place, and God Almighty judges with truth whether requested or not, and the meaning of the request is the appearance of the desire of the seeker in His true judgment, And our Lord, the Most Gracious, is sought for help against that which you describe, of lies and falsehood.
22:1: 1. Meccan except for some verses from the words of God Almighty: These two are opponents to His words: And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy. “O mankind, fear your Lord,” meaning: beware of His punishment by obeying Him. Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing. An earthquake and a tremor are intense movement in a tremendous state. They differed regarding this earthquake: Alqamah and Al-Sha’bi said: It is one of the signs of the Hour. [It was also said: The Day of Resurrection.] Al-Hassan and Al-Suddi said: This earthquake will occur on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abbas said: The earthquake of the Hour will occur and will be with it.
22:2: 2. On the Day you see it, meaning the Hour, and it was said: the earthquake, will be distracted Ibn Abbas said: will be preoccupied, and it was said: will be forgotten, it is said: I was distracted from such-and-such, meaning I left it and was preoccupied with something else. Every nursing mother from what she was nursing, meaning: every woman with a child she is nursing, it is said: a nursing woman, without the ha', if it is intended as a description, like menstruating and pregnant, but if they intended the action, they insert the ha'. And every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, meaning: she will miscarry her child from the terror of that day. Al-Hasan said: The nursing mother will forget her child without weaning him, and the pregnant woman will give birth to what is in her womb without completing it. This indicates that this earthquake will be in this world, because after the resurrection there will be no pregnancy. Whoever said: It will be on the Day of Resurrection, said this in order to magnify the matter, not in its true sense, like their saying: Something happened to us that would make a newborn turn gray, meaning its severity. And you see people drunk, but they are not drunk. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: sakra wa ma hum bisakra without an alif. These are two dialects for the plural of sakran, like kasala and kasali. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is: You see people drunk from fear, but they are not drunk from drink. It was said: Its meaning is: And you see people as if they are drunk, but the punishment of God is severe. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Hafs al-Tajir told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Bakir al-Kazfi al-Absi told us, Wakee’ told us on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:‘O Adam, arise and send forth the people of Hell. ’ He will say: ‘At Your service and Your pleasure, and all good is in Your hands, O Lord, and what is the people of Hell? ’ He will say: ‘From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. ’ He said: ‘Then the newborn will turn gray, and every pregnant woman will give birth to her child, and you will see [the people] drunk, but they are not drunk, but the punishment of God is severe. ’ He said: ‘They will say: And who is that one? ’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Nine hundred and ninety-nine from Gog and Magog and one from you. ’ The people said: ‘God is the greatest. ’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘By God, I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise. ’ By God, I hope that You will be one-third of the people of Paradise. By God, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. The people were very proud, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On that day, you will be among the people like a white hair on a black bull, or a black hair on a white bull.” It was narrated on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, and others: These two verses were revealed during the Battle of Banu Al-Mustaliq at night, and a herald called out to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), so they urged the mounts until they were around the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). He recited it to them, and he had never seen more people weeping than that night. When morning came, they had not taken the saddles off the mounts, nor pitched their tents, nor cooked a pot, and the people were either weeping or sitting sadly and contemplating. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: Do you know what day that is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “That is the day when God the Almighty will say to Adam, ‘Arise and send forth from your descendants those who will be sent to Hellfire.’ Adam will say: ‘From each of you?’ God the Almighty will say: ‘From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine will go to Hellfire and one will go to Paradise.’” That was a great burden on the Muslims, and they wept and said: So who will be saved, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: Be of good cheer, strive to be steadfast, and come close, for with you are two creatures that were never before in the Fire. A people except that they multiply: Gog and Magog. Then he said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. So they glorified and praised God. Then he said: I hope that you will be two-thirds of the people of Paradise. The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are my nation. The Muslims are not to the infidels except like a mole on the side of a camel or like a mark on the arm of an animal. Rather, Like a black hair on a white bull or like a white hair on a black bull. Then he said: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account. Umar said: Seventy thousand? He said: Yes, and with each one there will be seventy thousand. Then Ukasha bin Muhsin stood up and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to make me one of them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are one of them. Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said: Pray to God to make me one of them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ukasha has preceded you in that.
22:3: 3. The Almighty’s saying: And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge, was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, who was very argumentative, and used to say: The angels are daughters of God, and the Qur’an is legends of the ancients, and he denied the resurrection and revival of those who have become dust. God Almighty says: And he follows meaning: he follows in his argument about God without knowledge, every rebellious devil. The rebellious one is the one who persists in evil.
22:4: 4. It was decreed for him, it was decreed for Satan, that whoever takes him as a friend, follows him, he, meaning Satan, will mislead him, meaning: he will mislead whoever takes him as a friend, and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze, then he made the argument binding on those who deny the resurrection, saying:
22:5: 5. O mankind, if you are in doubt, in doubt, about the resurrection, then We created you, meaning: your father Adam, who is the origin of the lineage, from dust, then from a sperm-drop, meaning: his offspring, and sperm-drop is semen, and its origin is a small amount of water, and its plural is sperms, then from a clot, which is thick, congealed blood, and its plural is alaq, because the sperm-drop becomes thick blood then it becomes flesh, then from a lump of flesh, which is a small amount of flesh, the size of what is chewed, formed and unformed. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: Mukhallaqa means perfectly created, and un-Mukhallaqa means imperfectly created. Mujahed said: Imaginary and non-imaginary, meaning the miscarriage. It was said: The created is the child that the woman gives birth to at the right time, and the uncreated is the miscarriage. It was narrated on the authority of Alqamah on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud who said: When the sperm settles in the womb, an angel takes it in his hand and says: O Lord, is it formed or unformed? If he says: Unformed, the womb expels it as blood and there is no soul. If he says: Formed, the angel says: O Lord, is it male or female, miserable or happy? What is the life span, what is the work, what is the provision, and in what land will it die? Then it is said to him: Go to the Mother of the Book, for you will find all of that in it. So he goes and finds it in the Mother of the Book and copies it, and it remains with him until he comes to its last description. To show you, the perfection of Our power and wisdom in managing the stages of your creation, and so that you may infer from His power in the beginning of creation His power to restore. It was said: To show you what you do, what you leave, and what you need in worship. And We place in the wombs whom We will, so they do not abort it or cause it to miscarry, for a specified term, the time when it emerges from the womb fully formed and mature. Then We bring you out from the wombs of your mothers as a child, meaning: a child, and He did not say: children, because the Arabs mention the plural with the singular noun. It was said: as a likening to the verbal noun like justice and falsehood. Then that you may reach your full strength, meaning: perfection and strength. And among you is he who dies, before reaching old age, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age, meaning: old age and senility, so that he does not know anything after having known, meaning: he reaches an age at which his mind changes and he does not understand anything. Then he mentioned another proof of the resurrection, saying: And you see the earth lifeless, meaning: dry, with no vegetation in it. But when We send down upon it water, meaning rain, it quivers, moving with vegetation, because the earth rises with vegetation, and that is how it moves. And it swells, meaning: it rises and increases. It was said: there is an inversion of the meaning: it swelled and quivered and its vegetation swelled, so the complement was deleted, and the quivering in vegetation is more apparent. It is said: the plant quivered, meaning: it grew tall, and it is feminine because the earth is mentioned. Abu Jaafar read wa-rabat with a hamza, and the same is true of Ha-Mim as-Sajdah, meaning: it rose and ascended. And it produces from every beautiful pair, meaning: a beautiful variety that pleases whoever sees it, meaning: it pleases. This is another proof of the resurrection.
22:6: 6. That is because God is the Truth, meaning: so that you may know that God is the Truth, and that He gives life to the dead and that He is over all things competent.
22:7: 7. And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that God will resurrect those in the graves.
22:8: 8. And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge, meaning Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, nor guidance, explaining nor an enlightening book.
22:9: 9. The second of his affection, meaning: swaggering out of his arrogance. Mujahid and Qatada said: twisting his neck. Atiyah and Ibn Zayd said: turning away from what he is called to out of arrogance. Ibn Jurayj said: turning away from the truth out of arrogance. Atf: side, and the man's atf: his two sides to the right and left, and it is the place where a person turns, meaning he twists and inclines when turning away from something, similar to the saying of God the Almighty: And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly (Luqman 31:7), and God the Almighty said: And when it is said to them, Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you, they turn their heads away (al-Munafiqun 63:5). To lead astray from the way of God, from the religion of God, for him in this world is disgrace, torment and humiliation, which is killing at Badr, so Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith and Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ayt were killed on the day of Badr with patience. And We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning Fire.
22:10: 10. And it will be said to him: That is because of what your hands have put forth, and that God is not unjust to His servants, so He punishes them without sin, and He, glory be to Him, disposes of His servant in whatever way He wills, for His judgment is just and He is not unjust.
22:11: 11. The Almighty said: And among mankind is he who worships God on the edge, the verse was revealed about the Bedouins who used to come to Madinah as immigrants from their desert. When one of them came to Madinah and his body was healthy there and his mare gave birth to a beautiful foal and his wife gave birth to a boy and his wealth increased, he would say: This is a good religion and I have attained goodness in it and he would be reassured by it. But if he was afflicted with illness and his wife gave birth to a girl and his arrows miscarried and his wealth decreased, he would say: I have not attained anything since I entered this religion except evil, so he would turn away from his religion, and that is the trial. So the Almighty revealed: And among the people is he who worships God on the verge, most of the commentators said: on doubt, and its origin is from the edge of something, which is its edge, like the edge of a mountain or a wall that is like a stand on it that is not stable, so it was said to the one who doubts in religion that he worships God on the edge of the mountain, unstable and exposed to falling on one side of the edge due to the weakness of its standing, and if they worshipped God in gratitude for ease and patience in hardship, they would not be on the verge, Al-Hasan said: He is the hypocrite who worships Him with his tongue without his heart, If good befalls him, health in his body and ease in his livelihood, he is reassured by it, meaning: he is satisfied with it and is at peace with it, But if a trial befalls him, affliction in his body and difficulty in his livelihood, he turns back on his face, he apostatizes and returns on his heels to the face he was on of disbelief, he has lost this world, meaning this doubter has lost this world by missing out on what he had hoped for, and the Hereafter, by the loss of religion and eternity in the Fire. Yaqub read loser with an alif, and the Hereafter in the accusative case. That is the manifest loss, it seems.
22:12: 12. He calls upon besides God that which does not harm him, if he disobeys Him and does not worship Him, and that which does not benefit him, if he obeys Him and worships Him. That is the farthest error, from the truth and guidance.
22:13: 13. He calls upon him whose harm is nearer than his benefit. This verse is one of the problems in the Qur'an and there are questions about it: First, they said: God said in the first verse, He calls upon that which does not harm him besides God, and He said here, whom his harm is nearer. So how can we reconcile between them? It was said that his statement in the first verse, He calls upon other than God that which does not harm him, means: his abandonment of his worship does not harm him, and his statement, To whom his harm is nearer, means: the harm of his worship. If it is said: He said, His harm is closer than his benefit, and there is no benefit in worshipping an idol at all? It was said: This is according to the custom of the Arabs, for they say about something that does not exist at all: far, like the Almighty’s saying: That is a distant return (Qaf: 3), meaning: there is no return at all. So since the benefit of the idol is far, meaning: there is no benefit in it at all, it was said: its harm is closer, because it exists. The third question: His statement, He whose harm is nearer, what is the meaning of this lam? They differed about it. Some of them said: It is a conjunction, its metaphor is: He calls upon the one whose harm is nearer. Ibn Masoud read it in this way. It was said: (To the one whose harm is nearer) meaning to the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit. It was said: (He calls upon) means to say. The predicate is omitted, meaning he says: To the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit, He is God. It was said: Its meaning is that he calls upon someone whose harm is closer than his benefit, so he deleted the latter, making use of the former. If you said: It is used for someone whose good is greater than his evil, it is used, then the latter is deleted, it is permissible. It was said: for emphasis, meaning: he calls upon God for the one who harms him more than he benefits him. It was said: He calls from is a connection to his statement: That is the distant misguidance. He says: That is the distant misguidance he calls, then he resumes and says: To him whose harm is nearer than his benefit. So from is in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is: What an evil protector, meaning the helper. It was said: the worshipped. And what an evil companion, meaning the friend and companion, meaning: the idol, and the Arabs call a husband a companion because of the mixing.
22:14: 14. The Almighty said: “Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, God does what He wills.”
22:15: 15. Whoever thinks that God will not support him meaning his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch out a rope to the sky, meaning the roof of the house according to the majority, meaning: let him tie a rope to the roof of his house and strangle himself with it until he dies, then let him cut the rope after strangulation. It was said: Then let him cut meaning let him stretch the rope until it breaks and he dies strangling, then let him see whether his plot, his deed and his trickery, will vanish what enrages him (ma) means a source, meaning: will his plot and his trickery vanish his anger, meaning: let him choke with anger until he dies. This is not by way of certainty, meaning: that he should do it because he cannot cut and look after strangulation and death, but it is as is said to the envious person: If you are not satisfied with this, then choke and die of anger. Ibn Zayd said: What is meant by the sky is the well-known sky. The meaning of the verse: Whoever thinks that God will not support His Prophet and plots against him in order to cut him off from him, let him cut him off from his roots, for his roots are in the sky. So let him extend a chain to the sky and then cut off the revelation that comes to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and let him see if he is able to relieve his anger with this action. It was narrated that this verse was revealed about a people from Asad and Ghatafan, whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called to Islam, and there was an alliance between them and the Jews. They said: We cannot follow this path because we fear that Muhammad will not be victorious and his matter will not be made manifest, and the alliance between us and the Jews will be severed, and they will not provide us with leadership or shelter. So this verse was revealed. Mujahed said: Victory means provision and the letter ha’ refers back to “whoever and its meaning is: whoever thinks that God will not provide for him in this world and the hereafter. It was revealed about whoever has bad thoughts about God the Almighty and fears that God will not provide for him, Then let him extend a rope to the sky, meaning to the sky of the House, and let him see if his actions will remove what enrages him, and he is afraid that he will not be provided for. Victory may also mean sustenance. The Arabs say: Whoever supports me, God will support him. That is, whoever gives me, God will give him. Abu Ubaidah said: The Arabs say: A victorious land, meaning: rain-soaked. Abu Amr, Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and Ya’qub read: Then let them sever their vows and Then let them sever their vows with a kasra on the lam, and the rest read them both with a jazm because all of them are lams of command. Ibn ‘Amir added: And let them fulfill their vows and let them circumambulate (al-Hajj 22:29) with a kasra on the lam in both of them. Whoever reads with a kasra in Then let them sever their vows and Then let them sever their vows made a distinction because Then is separated from the statement, and the waw is as if it is from the word itself like the fa’ in His statement: So let them look.
22:16: 16. And likewise, meaning: like that, what preceded from the verses of the Qur’an, We have sent down, meaning: the Qur’an, clear verses, and that God guides whom He wills.
22:17: 17. Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans or Magians or polytheists, meaning idol worshippers, “God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God is, over all things, Witness.”
22:18: 18. Have you not seen?, Have you not learned? It was said: Have you not seen [read] in your heart that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the beasts. Mujahid said: Their prostration is the transformation of their shadows. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: There is no star, sun or moon in the sky except that it prostrates when it sets and then does not rise until permission is given to it, so it takes the right until it returns to its place of rising. It was said: Their prostration means obedience, for there is no inanimate object except that it is obedient to God, humbled before Him and glorifying Him, as God the Most High informed us about the heavens and the earth, They said, 'We have come in obedience.' (Fussilat 41:11), and He said in describing the stones, And indeed, among them are those that fall down for fear of God. (al-Baqarah 2:74), and God the Most High said: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification. (Al-Isra': 44), and this is a good doctrine that agrees with the statement of the people of the Sunnah. His statement: And many of the people, meaning: of all of these things glorify God Almighty. And many of the people, meaning the Muslims. And many upon whom the punishment is justified, and they are the disbelievers because of their disbelief and their failure to prostrate, and despite their disbelief their shadows prostrate to God Almighty. The and in His statement: And many upon whom the punishment is justified, is a and of resumption. And he whom God humiliates, meaning: God humiliates him, there is none to honor him, meaning: he whom God humiliates, no one will subdue him, Indeed, God does what He wills, meaning: He honors and humiliates, so happiness and misery are by His will and desire.
22:19: 19. The Almighty’s saying: These two opponents have disputed about their Lord, meaning: they argued about His religion and His command. The opponent is a noun similar to the source, so He said: they disputed in the plural form, like His saying: And has there come to you the report of the opponents when they climbed over the wall of the private chamber? (Sad: 21), and they differed about these two opponents: Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us, Abu Hashim told us, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Qais bin Ibad, who said: I heard Abu Dharr swear that this verse: These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord, was revealed about those who came out on the day of Badr: Hamza and Ali, Ubaidah bin Al-Harith, Utbah, and Shaiba, the sons of Abu Rabi’ah, and Al-Walid bin Utbah. And Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulaiman told us, he said: I heard my father say: Abu Majlaz told us, on the authority of Qais bin Ibad, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, he said: I am the first to kneel before the Most Merciful to argue on the Day of Resurrection. Qais said: And about them was revealed: These two opponents who disputed about their Lord. He said: They are those who fought on the day of Badr: Ali and Hamza, Ubaidah, Shaiba bin Rabi’ah, Utbah bin Rabi’ah, and Al-Walid bin Utbah. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: On the day of Badr, Utbah ibn Rabi’ah went out between his brother Shaibah ibn Rabi’ah and his son Al-Walid ibn Utbah and called for a duel. Three young men from the Ansar went out to him: Uwadh and Mu’awwidh, sons of Al-Harith, and their mother is ‘Afra’, and ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah. They said: Who are you? They said: A group of the Ansar. When they named themselves, they said: Noble and equal. Then their crier called: O Muhammad, bring out to us our equals from our people. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Stand up, O Ubaidah ibn Al-Harith, O Hamza ibn ‘Abd Al-Muttalib, and O ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib. When they approached, they said: Who are you? They mentioned and said: Yes, they are equal and noble. So Ubaidah fought, and the oldest of the people was Utbah. Hamza fought Shaibah, and Ali fought al-Walid ibn Utbah. As for Hamza, he did not wait long before he killed Shaibah and Ali al-Walid. Ubaidah and Utbah differed between them, and each of them [defeated] the other. Hamza and Ali thought of striking Utbah with their swords, so they threw him down and carried Ubaidah to his companions, and his leg had been cut off and its marrow was flowing. When they brought Ubaidah to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Are you not a martyr, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes. Ubaidah said: If Abu Talib were alive, he would have known that I am more deserving of what he said than he is, when he says: We surrender to him until we fall around him and forget about our children and wives Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: The verse was revealed about the Muslims and the People of the Book. The People of the Book said: We are more deserving of God and have an earlier Book than you, and our Prophet was before your Prophet. The believers said: We are more deserving of God. We believed in our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and your Prophet and in what God revealed of the Book, and you know our Prophet and our Book and you disbelieved in it out of envy. This is their dispute over their Lord. Mujahid, Ata bin Abi Rabah, and Al-Kalbi said: They are the believers and the unbelievers, all of them, regardless of their religion. Some of them said: He made the religions six in the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews (al-Ma’idah 5:69), the verse, so He made five for Hell and one for Paradise, so the Almighty’s saying: These two are opponents who dispute about their Lord refers to them, so the believers are opponents and the rest of the five are opponents. And Ikrimah said: Paradise and Hell argued, as Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i informed us, Abu Tahir Al-Ziyadi informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad Hussain Al-Qattan informed us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami informed us, Abdul Razzaq informed us, Muammar informed us, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah informed us: He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Paradise and Hell argued, and Hell said: I am favored by the arrogant and the tyrannical. And Paradise said: Why is it that only the weak, the worthless, and the deceived enter me? God the Almighty said to Paradise: You are only My mercy, with you I have mercy on whomever I wish of My servants. And He said to Hell: You are only My punishment, with you I punish whomever I wish of My servants. And each of you will have its fill. As for Hell, it will not be filled until God places His foot in it, and it will say: Enough, enough. Then it will be filled and some parts will be drawn towards others, and God will not wrong any of His creation. As for Paradise, God the Almighty will create a creation for it.” Then God Almighty explained what the two opponents have, saying: As for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them. Saeed bin Jubair said: Garments of molten copper, and there is no vessel that is hotter than it when heated. It was called garments because it surrounds them like clothing. Some of them said: The people of Hell will wear pieces of fire, Boiling water will be poured over their heads. Boiling water is hot water that has reached its peak temperature.
22:20: 20. It will melt with it meaning: it will melt with the boiling water, what is in their bellies, it is said: I melted the buttocks and the fat with fire if I melted them, I melted them, meaning it will melt with the boiling water that is poured over their heads until what is in their bellies of fat and entrails falls off, and the skins meaning: its heat will roast their skins so that they fall off. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Zayd, on the authority of Abu al-Samh, on the authority of Abu Hujaira, whose name is Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The boiling water is poured over their heads and penetrates their skulls until it reaches their stomachs, and it melts what is in their stomachs until it comes out of their feet, and it is melting, then it is returned to how it was.”
22:21: 21. The Almighty said: And for them are maces of iron, iron whips, the singular of which is: muqama. Al-Layth said: The muqama is like a whip made of iron, from their saying: I struck his head, if I struck him violently. And in the hadith: If an iron mace were placed in the ground and then the two heavy things gathered on it, they would not lift it from the ground.
22:22: 22. Whenever they want to get out of it from distress, meaning: whenever they try to get out of the fire because of the distress and anguish that befalls them, they are returned to it, meaning: they are returned to it with whips. And in the interpretation: Hell will swarm with them and throw them to its top, and they want to get out of it, but the guards strike them with whips of iron and they fall into it for seventy autumns. And taste the punishment of the burning, meaning: the burning, like the painful and the hurtful. Al-Zajjaj said: These are one of the two opponents. He said about the other, and they are the believers:
22:23: 23.
