"Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will be adorned with bracelets of gold, the plural of bracelet, and pearls," the people of Medina and Asim read (and pearls) here and in Surat Al-Mala'ikah in the accusative case, and Ya'qub agreed here on the meaning of and they will be adorned with pearls, and because it is written in the copies of the Qur'an with an alif, and the others read it in the genitive case in apposition to His statement: (of gold), and Abu Ja'far and Abu Bakr leave out the first hamza in the entire Qur'an, and they differed about the reason for proving the alif in it, so Abu Amr said: They proved it as they proved it in: they said and they were, and Al-Kisa'i said: They proved it for the hamza, because the hamza is a letter from the letters, "and their clothing therein is silk," meaning: they will wear in Paradise the garments of silk, which is what men were forbidden to wear in this world. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Ja’d told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Dawud Al-Sarraj, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever wears silk in this world, God will not make him wear it in the Hereafter. If he enters Paradise, the people of Paradise will wear it, but he will not wear it.”
22:24: 24. The Almighty said: And they are guided to the good of speech, Ibn Abbas said: It is the testimony that there is no god but God. Ibn Zayd said: There is no god but God, and God is the greatest, and praise be to God [and glory be to God]. Al-Suddi said: It means the Qur’an. It was said: It is the saying of the people of Paradise: Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us (al-Zumar 39:74) And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy, to the religion of God, which is Islam, (and the Praiseworthy) is God, who is praised for His actions.
22:25: 25. The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God, is a continuation of the future tense with the past tense, because the future tense is intended to mean the past tense, as the Almighty said in another place: Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God (An-Nisa’: 167), meaning: Those who disbelieved in what came before, and avert [people] from the way of God in the present, i.e., they avert. And the Sacred Mosque, i.e., they avert [people] from the Sacred Mosque. Which We have made for mankind, a qiblah for their prayers, a place of ritual and worship, as He said: It was appointed for mankind (Al Imran 3:96). Equally, Hafs read on the authority of Asim and Ya’qub: (equally) in the accusative case by placing the preposition on it because the preposition takes two objects. It was said: Its meaning is that it is level in it, the one who resides in it and the one who comes to it. The others read it with the nominative case as the subject and what follows it is the predicate, and the completion of the speech is when he said for the people. He meant by the one who resides in it: the one who resides in it, and the one who comes to it from elsewhere: the one who comes to it and returns to it. They differed on the meaning of the verse. Some people said: It is the same for the one staying there and the one who comes back, meaning: in respect of venerating its sanctity and performing the rituals there. Mujahid, Al-Hasan and a group agreed with this, and they said: What is meant by it is the Sacred Mosque itself. The meaning of equality is equality in venerating the Kaaba in the virtue of praying in the Sacred Mosque and circumambulating the House. Others said: What is meant by it is all of the sanctuary, and the meaning of equality is that the resident and the nomad are equal in residing in it, neither of them has more right to the house in which he is than the other, except that no one should be disturbed in it if he has been to a house before, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, Qatada and Ibn Zayd. They said: They are equal in [houses] and dwellings. Abdul Rahman bin Sabit said: When the pilgrims came to Mecca, no one from the people of Mecca was more deserving of their status than them. Umar bin Al-Khattab used to forbid people from closing their doors during the season. According to this opinion, it is not permissible to sell or rent the houses of Mecca. According to the first opinion - which is closer to the truth - it is permissible, because God the Almighty said: Those who were expelled from their homes (al-Hajj 22:40), and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, so the house was attributed to him as a king. Umar bought a prison house in Mecca for four thousand dirhams, which indicates that it is permissible to sell it. This is the opinion of Tawus and Amr bin Dinar, and Al-Shafi’i said the same. The Almighty said: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice meaning: in the Sacred Mosque, committing an act of injustice, which is the inclination towards injustice. The ba in His statement in an act of injustice is redundant, like His statement: produces oil (al-Mu’minun 23:20). Its meaning is whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice. Al-A’sha said: Our spears have guaranteed the provision of our children, meaning: the provision of our children. Al-Mubarrad denied that the ba is redundant and said: The meaning of the verse is whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice. They differed about this atheism. Mujahid and Qatada said: It is polytheism and the worship of other than God. Some people said: It is everything that was forbidden in word or deed, even insulting the servant. Ata’ said: It is entering the sanctuary without being in a state of ihram, or committing any of the prohibitions of the sanctuary, such as killing game or cutting down trees. Ibn Abbas said: It is that you kill someone who does not kill you, or you wrong someone who does not wrong you. This is the meaning of what Ad-Dahhak said. On the authority of Mujahid, he said: Bad deeds are multiplied in Mecca just as good deeds are multiplied. Habib bin Abi Thabit said: It is the hoarding of food in Mecca. Abdullah bin Masoud said about his statement: And whoever intends therein to commit an injustice or wrongdoing - We will make him taste a painful punishment, he said: If a man intends to commit a sin, it will not be recorded against him, as long as he does not commit it. And if a man intends to kill a man in Mecca while he is in Aden Abyan, or in another country, God will make him taste a painful punishment. Al-Suddi said: Unless he repents. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that he had two tents, one outside the sanctuary and the other in the sanctuary. When he wanted to reproach his family, he would reproach them in the other tent. He was asked about that and he said: We used to say that it was considered blasphemy for a man to say, No, by God, and Yes, by God.
22:26: 26. The Almighty said: And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, meaning: We set foot on it. Ibn Abbas said: We made. It was also said: While Al-Zajjaj said: We made the site of the House [a site for Abraham. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: We prepared it. We only mentioned the location of the House because the Kaaba was raised to the sky at the time of the flood. Then when God Almighty commanded Abraham to build the House, he did not know where to build it, so God sent a violent wind that swept away for him what was around the House on the foundation. Al-Kalbi said: God sent a cloud the size of the House, and it stood in front of the House, and in it was a head that spoke, O Ibrahim, build according to my size, so build on it. God Almighty said: That you do not associate anything with Me, meaning: We made a covenant with Ibrahim and said to him: Do not associate anything with Me, and purify My House for those who perform Tawaf, meaning: those who perform Tawaf around the House, and those who stand, meaning: those who stay, and those who bow and prostrate, meaning: those who pray.
22:27: 27. And proclaim to the people meaning: inform and call to the people, the Hajj, so Ibrahim said: How can my voice reach? He said: You are responsible for the call to prayer and I am responsible for the delivery, so Ibrahim stood on the station and the station rose until it became like the tallest mountains, so he put his fingers in his ears, and turned his face right and left and east and west and said: O people, your Lord has built a House and has prescribed for you the Hajj to the House, so respond to your Lord, so everyone who used to perform Hajj from the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers responded to him: Here I am, O God, here I am. Ibn Abbas said: The first to respond to him were the people of Yemen, and they are the people who performed Hajj the most. It was narrated that Ibrahim ascended Abu Qubais and called out. Ibn Abbas said that what is meant by the people in this verse are the people of the Qiblah. Al-Hasan claimed that his statement, And proclaim to the people the Hajj is a new statement and that the one commanded to make this call was Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was commanded to do so during the Farewell Pilgrimage. Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, Hajj has been made obligatory upon you, so perform Hajj. The Almighty says: They will come to you on foot, on foot, the plural of rajil, like qayim and qiyam, and sai’im and sai’m, “and on every lean camel,” meaning: riding on every lean camel, and the lean camel is the emaciated camel. They will come from every distant ravine, meaning: from every distant road. The plural of ya’tina is because of the place of every and the meaning of the female camels.
22:28: 28. "That they may witness, that they may attend, benefits for them", Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Muhammad bin Ali Al-Baqir said: Pardon and forgiveness. Saeed bin Jubair said: Trade, and it is the narration of Ibn Zayd from Ibn Abbas, who said: Markets. Mujahid said: Trade and what pleases God of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. "And mention the name of God on appointed days", meaning the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah according to most of the commentators. It was called (in appointed) because of the eagerness to know its calculation for the time of Hajj at the end of it. It is narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him: that it is the Day of Sacrifice and three days after it, and in the narration of Ata' from Ibn Abbas that it is the Day of Arafah and the Sacrifice and the Days of Tashreeq. Muqatil said: The appointed days are the Days of Tashreeq. "On what He has provided for them of livestock", meaning: the gifts and sacrifices, which are from the blessings, which are camels, cows and sheep. Al-Zajjaj chose the known days: the Day of Sacrifice and the Days of Tashreeq, because the mention of the name of the livestock indicates the naming of it before slaughtering it, and the slaughtering of gifts is on these days. So eat from it is an order of permission and not an obligation. He only said that because the people of the Jahiliyyah did not eat any of the meat of their gifts, and the scholars agreed that if the gift was voluntary, it is permissible for the one giving the gift to eat from it, and likewise the voluntary sacrifice because: Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashhimani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said in the story of the Farewell Pilgrimage: Ali came with a camel from Yemen and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drove one hundred camels, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered sixty-three camels with his own hand and Ali slaughtered what remained, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that a piece of each camel be taken and put in a pot, so they ate from its meat and drank from its broth. They differed regarding the sacrificial offering required by Islamic law. Is it permissible for the person making the sacrifice to eat any of it? Such as the blood of enjoyment and qiran, the blood required for spoiling or missing the Hajj, and the penalty for hunting? Some people said that it is not permissible for him to eat anything from it, and this is what Al-Shafi’i said, and likewise what he made obligatory upon himself by vow. Ibn Umar said: He does not eat from the reward for hunting and vows, and he eats from other than that, and this is what Ahmad and Ishaq said. Malik said: He eats from the sacrificial animal of enjoyment and from every sacrificial animal that is obligatory upon him except for the ransom for harm and the reward for hunting and the vowed animal. According to the people of opinion, he eats from the blood of enjoyment and the qiran and he does not eat from what is obligatory other than them. The Almighty said: And feed the wretched and needy, meaning: the poor person who has nothing and the wretched person who is extremely miserable, and misery is extreme poverty.
22:29: 29. Then let them complete their untidiness, untidiness means dirt and filth from long hair and nails and dishevelment. The Arabs say to someone they find disgusting: How dirty you are! The pilgrim is disheveled and dusty, he has not shaved his hair or trimmed his nails, so completing untidiness means removing these things so that they complete their untidiness, meaning: to remove their filth. What is meant by this is exiting the state of ihram by shaving, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, trimming the nails, and wearing clothes. Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas said: (Completing untidiness) means all the rituals of Hajj. Mujahid said: It is the rituals of Hajj, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, and trimming the nails. It was said that untidiness here means throwing the pebbles. Al-Zajjaj said: We do not know untidiness and its meaning except from the Qur’an. God the Almighty said: And let them fulfill their vows. Mujahid said: He meant the vow of Hajj and the offering and whatever a person vows to do during Hajj, i.e. to complete it by performing it. It was said: What is meant by it is fulfilling what he vowed according to its apparent meaning. It was said: He meant by it to go out from what he vowed or did not vow. The Arabs say to everyone who went out from what he was obligated to do and fulfilled his vow. Asim read, according to Abu Bakr’s narration, Wa Liyyufawu with the accusative of the waw and the shaddah on the fa. And let them circumambulate the Ancient House, meaning the obligatory circumambulation, which is the circumambulation of farewell on the Day of Sacrifice after stoning and shaving. There are three types of circumambulation: the circumambulation of arrival, which is when someone arrives in Mecca circumambulates the House seven times, jogging three times from the Black Stone until he reaches it, and walking four times. This circumambulation is a Sunnah, and there is nothing wrong with whoever leaves it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmad - he is Abu Isa - told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman bin Nawfal Al-Qurashi that he asked Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, and he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj, and Aisha told me that the first thing he did when he arrived was to perform ablution, then circumambulate the House, and then it was not an Umrah. Then Abu Bakr performed Hajj, and the first thing he did was circumambulate the House, and then it was not an Umrah. Then Umar did the same, then Uthman performed Hajj, and I saw that the first thing he did was circumambulate the House. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Kisa’i told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Anas bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when he performed the circumambulation during Hajj or Umrah, the first thing he would do when he arrived was to walk three times and walk four times, then he would pray two prostrations, then he would circumambulate between Safa and Marwah seven times.” The second Tawaf: is the Tawaf of Ifadah on the Day of Sacrifice after stoning and shaving. It is obligatory and one cannot be released from the state of Ihram unless one performs it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Umar bin Hafs told us, my father told us, Al-A’mash told us, Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, she said: “Safiya menstruated on the night of the departure, and she said: ‘I see nothing but that I am detaining you.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘My hair is barren. Did you circumambulate on the Day of Sacrifice?’ It was said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then depart.’” Thus it is proven that whoever does not circumambulate on the Day of Sacrifice the Tawaf Al-Ifadah is not permitted to depart. The third circumambulation: is the farewell circumambulation. There is no permission for someone who wants to leave Mecca to the distance of shortening the prayers to leave it until he has circumambulated the House seven times. Whoever leaves it must offer a sacrifice, except for a menstruating woman who is permitted to leave the farewell circumambulation. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The people were commanded that the last thing they should do should be to circumambulate the House, except that a concession was granted to the menstruating woman. Sand is used specifically for the arrival circumambulation, but there is no sand in the farewell and farewell circumambulations. His saying: By the ancient house They differed about the meaning of the ancient: Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid and Qatadah said: It was called the ancient because God freed it from the hands of tyrants who would not destroy it, so no tyrant ever prevailed over it. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: It was called the ancient because it was never ruled. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: It was called this because it is ancient and it was the first house established for people. It is said: An ancient dinar, meaning old. It was also said: It was called the ancient because God freed it from drowning, so it was raised during the days of the flood.
22:30: 30. That means: the matter is that, meaning what was mentioned of the acts of Hajj, and whoever honors the sacred things of God, meaning the sins of God and what He has forbidden, and honoring them means abandoning their association. Al-Layth said: The sacred things of God are those that it is not permissible to violate. Al-Zajjaj said: The sacred thing is that which must be performed and it is forbidden to neglect it. Some people said that the meaning of the sacred things here is: the rituals, as indicated by the verses that are connected to them. Ibn Zayd said: The sacred things here are: the Sacred House, the Sacred City, the Sacred Month, the Sacred Mosque, and the state of ihram. That is better for him with his Lord, meaning: honoring the sacred things is better for him with God in the Hereafter. God the Almighty said: And lawful to you are the livestock, that you eat them if you slaughter them, and they are camels, cows, and sheep, except what is recited to you, its prohibition, which is His statement in Surat al-Ma’idah 5:Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood (al-Ma’idah 5:3), the verse, So avoid the uncleanness of idols, meaning: worshipping them. He says: Be on the side of them, for they are unclean, meaning: the cause of uncleanness, which is punishment, and uncleanness means uncleanness. Al-Zajjaj said: from here is for paronomasia, meaning: avoid the idols that are unclean, and avoid false statement, meaning: lying and slander. Ibn Mas’ud said: false testimony, and it was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up as a preacher and said: O people, false testimony is equal to associating partners with God, then he recited this verse. It was said: it is the saying of the polytheists in their Talbiyah: Here I am, you have no partner, here I am, except for a partner who is yours, whom you own and what he owns.
22:31: 31. Hanifs for God, sincere to Him, not associating anything with Him. Qatada said: They were performing Hajj while they were polytheists, and they prohibited their daughters, mothers, and sisters, and they were called Hanifs, so the verse was revealed: Hanifs for God, not associating anything with Him, meaning: Hajj pilgrims to God, Muslims, monotheists, meaning: whoever associates anything with God is not Hanif. And whoever associates others with God, it is as if he had fallen from the sky to the earth, and the birds snatched him away, meaning the birds took him and carried him away. Snatching and abduction are the act of grabbing something quickly. The people of Madinah read: Fatakhatafuhu with a fatha on the kha and a shaddah on the ta, meaning: the wind snatches him away, or the wind blows him down, meaning: it tilts and carries him away, in a remote place, meaning: far away. Its meaning is: the one who associates others with God is as far from the truth as the one who fell from the sky and the birds took him away, or the wind blew him down, so he cannot reach him at all. It was said: The state of the polytheist falling from the sky is likened to him not having a plan for himself until he falls to the point where the wind knocks him down, so he is doomed inevitably, either by the birds snatching his flesh or by his falling down to a remote place. Al-Hasan said: The actions of the disbelievers are likened to this state in that they are gone and nullified, so they are unable to do anything about them.
22:32: 32. That, meaning: what I mentioned about avoiding uncleanliness and false speech, and whoever honors the symbols of God - indeed, it is from the piety of the hearts, Ibn Abbas said: (The symbols of God) are the body and the offering, and its origin is from the word ishaar, which is to announce it so that it is known that it is an offering, and honoring it means to consider it fat and to approve of it. It was said: (The symbols of God) are the signs of His religion, for indeed, it is from the piety of the hearts, meaning: honoring it is from the piety of the hearts.
22:33: 33. There are benefits for you in it meaning: in the body before it is designated for sacrifice, in its milk, offspring, wool, fur, and riding on its backs, “for a specified term, which is that he designates it and makes it a sacrifice, and if he does that, he will have nothing of its benefits. This is the statement of Mujahid, and the statement of Qatada and Ad-Dahhak, and it was narrated by Muqsim on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: Its meaning is that you have benefits in gifts after they are required and called gifts, such that you ride them and drink their milk when needed (for a specified period), meaning: until you slaughter them, and this is the saying of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah. Scholars differed about riding the sacrificial animal: Some people said: It is permissible for him to ride it and carry loads on it without harming it. This is the opinion of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq, because Abu Al-Hasan Al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Ali Zahir bin Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq Al-Hashemi informed us, Mus’ab informed us on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man leading a sacrificial animal and said to him: Ride it. He said: O Messenger of God, it is a sacrificial animal. He said: Ride it, woe to you, on the second or third.” And he also said to him: Drink its milk after it is left over from watering its young. The people of opinion said: He should not ride it. Some people said: He should not ride it unless he is forced to. Some of them said: What he meant by the rituals is the rites and sights of Mecca. Therein you have benefits in trade and markets for a specified term which is leaving Mecca. It was said: (You will have benefits in it) in the form of reward and recompense for performing the rituals. Until a specified term, meaning: until the end of the days of Hajj. Then its place meaning: its place of slaughter, is at the Ancient House meaning: its place of slaughter is at the Ancient House, meaning the entire land of the Sacred Sanctuary, as He said: So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque (al-Tawbah 9:28), meaning: the entire Sacred Sanctuary. It was narrated on the authority of Jabir in the story of the Farewell Pilgrimage that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I slaughtered here, and all of Mina is a place of slaughter, so slaughter in your homes. And whoever said: The rituals are the rites, said: The meaning of his saying Then its place is at the Ancient House is: the place of the people from their ihram to the Ancient House, that is: that they circumambulate it with the circumambulation of visitation on the Day of Sacrifice.
22:34: 34. God Almighty said: And for every nation, meaning: a group of believers who came before you, We have appointed rituals, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read with a kasra on the seen here and at the end of the surah, meaning a noun like council and dawning, meaning: an altar, which is the place of sacrifice. The others read with a fatha on the seen as a source, like entrance and exit, meaning: shedding blood and slaughtering sacrifices, that they may mention the name of God over what He has provided for them of grazing livestock, [when slaughtering and slaughtering them, and He called them grazing livestock] because they do not speak. He said: grazing livestock, and He restricted it to livestock, because some animals are not grazing livestock, such as horses, mules, and donkeys, and it is not permissible to include them in the sacrifices. Your God is one God, meaning: name the sacrifices with the name of God alone, for your God is one God. So submit to Him, submit and obey. And give good tidings to the humble, Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: the humble. Mujahid said: those who are at peace with God Almighty, and the humble is the peaceful place on earth. Al-Akhfash said: the humble. Al-Nakha’i said: the sincere. Al-Kalbi said: they are those whose hearts are tender. Amr ibn Aws said: they are those who do not wrong and when they are wronged they do not take revenge.
22:35: 35. Those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful and those who are patient over what befalls them, of affliction and calamity, and establish prayer, meaning: those who establish prayer at its appointed times, and spend out of what We have provided them, giving charity.
22:36: 36. The Almighty said: And the body, the plural of badana, which is called badana because of its size and bulk. He means: the large, healthy camels. It is said that a man’s body is badan and badana if he is large, but if he becomes old and sagging, it is said that he has become badan tabadeenan. Ata and Al-Suddi said: The animals are camels and cows. As for sheep, they are not called a camel. We have made them for you among the symbols of God, one of the signs of His religion. They are called symbols because they are marked, which is when you stab them with a sharp object in their hump so that it is known that they are sacrificial animals. There is good for you in them, benefit in this world and reward in the Hereafter. So mention the name of God over them, when slaughtering them. Standing in rows, meaning standing on three legs with their legs and one of their hands in line, and their left hand is tied, so they slaughter them in the same way. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muslimah told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ziyad bin Jubair, who said: I saw Ibn Umar come upon a man who had made a sacrificial animal kneel down to slaughter it. He said: Send it out standing, tied up, according to the Sunnah of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mujahed said: The Sawaf is when its left leg is tied and it stands on three legs. Ibn Masoud read: Sawafin which means that one hand is tied from it and it is slaughtered in three, and it is like Sawaf. Abi, Al-Hasan and Mujahid read: Sawafi with a ya meaning: pure and sincere for God, with no partner for Him in it. And when its sides have fallen, meaning: it has fallen after the slaughter, so its sides have fallen to the ground. The root of falling is falling. It is said: The sun has fallen when it sets. Then eat from it, an order of permission. And feed the contented and the needy, they differed in its meaning. Ikrimah, Ibrahim, and Qatadah said: The contented is the one who sits in his house, chaste, content with what he is given and does not ask, and the needy is the one who asks. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The contented one is the one who does not expose himself or ask questions, and the one who shows himself to you and exposes himself to you without asking questions. So according to these two interpretations, the contented one is from contentment. It is said: he was content if he was satisfied with what was allotted to him. Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan and Al-Kalbi said: Al-Qani’ is the one who asks, and Al-Mu’tar is the one who offers his attention and does not ask. Thus, Al-Qani’ comes from Qana’a to be content, meaning to ask. Al-Hasan read: and the one who asks for something which is like the one who asks for something. It is said: he asked for something and he asked for it and he asked for it and he asked for it and he asked for it if he came to him asking for something, either as a question or as an offer. Ibn Zayd said: Al-Qani’ means the poor person, and Al-Mu’tar means the one who is not poor and does not have a sacrifice to offer, so he comes to the people and attacks them for the sake of their meat. Likewise, that is, just as we described of slaughtering it while standing, We have subjected it to you, as a blessing from us so that you may be able to slaughter it, that you may be grateful, so that you may be grateful for God’s blessing upon you.
22:37: 37. Neither their meat nor their blood will reach God, because when the people of ignorance slaughtered sacrificial animals, they would smear the Kaaba with their blood as an act of worship to God, so God revealed this verse: Neither their meat nor their blood will reach God Yaqub read (tanal and tanaleh) with a taa in both, and the general public read it with a yaa. Muqatil said: Their meat nor their blood will not be raised to God, but what reaches Him from you is piety, but what reaches Him from you are righteous deeds, piety, and sincerity that is intended for the sake of God, Thus He has subjected them to you, meaning: the sacrificial animals, that you may glorify God for having guided you, He guided you to the signs of His religion and the rituals of His Hajj, which is to say: God is greater for having guided us, and praise be to God for having tested us and our children, and give good tidings to the doers of good, Ibn Abbas said: the monotheists.
22:38: 38. The Almighty said: Indeed, God defends those who believe, Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read: (Yadfa') and the others read: (Yadfa') with an alif, meaning: He repels the evil of the polytheists from the believers and prevents them from the believers. Indeed, God does not like any treacherous ingrate, meaning: a treacherous person in the trust of God, ungrateful for His blessings. Ibn Abbas said: They betrayed God and made a partner with Him and were ungrateful for His blessings. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever approaches idols with his sacrifice and mentions a name other than God over it, then he is a treacherous ingrate.
22:39: 39. The Almighty said: Permission is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged. The people of Medina, Basra, and Asim read: (permission) with a damma on the alif, and the rest read it with a fatha, meaning: God has given permission, (to those who are being fought), the people of Medina, Ibn Amir, and Hafs read (they fight) with a fatha on the ta, meaning the believers who are being fought by the polytheists, and the others read it with a kasra on the ta, meaning those who are given permission to wage jihad (fight) the polytheists. The commentators said: The polytheists of Mecca used to harm the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they would continue to be sad, among them beaten and wounded, and they would complain about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would say to them: Be patient, for I was not commanded to fight until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated. Then God Almighty revealed this verse, and it is the first verse in which God permitted fighting, so this verse was revealed in Medina. Mujahid said: This verse was revealed about a specific group of people who emigrated from Mecca to Medina, and they were prevented, so God gave them permission to fight the infidels who were preventing them from emigrating, because they were wronged, meaning: because of what they were wronged and the harm they were subjected to, and indeed, God is able to give them victory. 14. Tell those who have believed to forgive those who do not expect the days of God, meaning they do not fear the events of God nor do they care about His vengeance. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: It was revealed about Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, because a man from Banu Ghifar insulted him in Mecca, so Umar, may God be pleased with him, wanted to strike him, so God revealed this verse and commanded him to forgive him. Al-Qurazi and Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about some of the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from the people of Mecca who were suffering severe harm from the polytheists before they were ordered to fight. They complained about that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so God revealed this verse, which was then abrogated by the verse on fighting. That He may reward a people. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read linjazi with a noon, while the others read it with a ya’, meaning that God may reward. Abu Ja’far read lijazi with a damma on the first ya’, a sukoon on the second, and a fatha on the zay. Abu Amr said: This is a mistake. Al-Kisa’i said: Its meaning is that He may reward a people for what they used to earn.
22:40: 40. Those who were expelled from their homes without right, instead of the first (about those) except that they say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ meaning: they were not expelled from their homes except because they said, Our Lord is God alone. “And had God not repelled some people by means of others,” through jihad and the establishment of legal punishments, it would have been demolished, the people of Hijaz read it with a light dal, while others read it with a shaddah indicating abundance, so the light dal is for little and much, and the shaddah is specific to much, monasteries, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: meaning the monasteries of the monks. Fatada said: the monasteries of the Sabians, and churches, the churches of the Christians, the plural of (bay’ah) which is the church of the Christians, and prayers, meaning the churches of the Jews, which they call in Hebrew saluta, and mosques in which the name of God is much mentioned, meaning the mosques of the Muslims from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning of the verse: Had God not repelled some people by means of others, the place of their prayer would have been destroyed in the law of every prophet. In the time of Moses, the churches would have been destroyed, in the time of Jesus, the synagogues and monasteries, and in the time of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the mosques. Ibn Zayd said: He meant by prayers the prayers of the people of Islam, for they are cut off if the enemy enters upon them. And God will surely support those who support Him, meaning: support His religion and His Prophet. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
22:41: 41. "Those who, if We establish them in the land, will establish prayer and give zakah, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong." Al-Zajjaj said: This is from the description of those who support Him. The meaning of "We establish them in the land" is: We will support them against their enemy until they are able to control the land. Qatada said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hasan said: They are this nation. "And to God belongs the outcome of all matters," meaning: the final matters of creation and their destination to Him. He means: Every kingdom other than His kingdom will be nullified, so matters will revert to Him without any dispute or claim.
22:42: 42. The Almighty’s saying: And if they deny you, is consoling His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the people of Noah, ‘Aad, and Thamud denied before them.
22:43: 43. And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot.
22:44: 44. "And the companions of Madyan denied Moses, so I granted respite to the disbelievers," meaning: I gave them respite and delayed their punishment, "then I seized them, [punished them], so how was My denial," meaning: My denial, meaning: how I denounced them for what they did of denying the punishment and destruction, frightening those who oppose the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and deny him.
22:45: 45. So how many, how many "of a town We have destroyed", with the letter ta', this is how the people of Basra and Ya'qub read it, and the others read: (we destroyed it) with the letter nun and the alif for emphasis, "and it is wrongful", meaning: and its people are wrongdoers, "so it is empty, fallen on its thrones, on its roofs, and a well that is not in use": [meaning: and how many wells are not in use] abandoned and devoid of its people "and a lofty palace", Qatada, Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: tall and high, from their saying "shadd bina'u" if he raised it. Sa'id bin Jubayr, Mujahid and Ata' said: plastered, from shed, which is plaster. It was said: The abandoned well and the built palace are in Yemen. As for the palace, it is on the top of a mountain, and the well is at its foot. Each of them has people who were in a state of prosperity, then they disbelieved, so God destroyed them, and the well and the palace remained empty. Abu Ruq narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: This well was in Hadhramaut in a town called Hadhura. Four thousand people who believed in Salih were saved from the punishment. They came to Hadhramaut with Salih. When they were present, Salih died, so it was called Hadhramaut because when Salih was present, he died. They built Hadhura and sat on this well and appointed a man over them. They stayed there for a long time and multiplied until they became numerous. Then they worshipped idols and disbelieved, so God sent to them a prophet called Hanzala bin Safwan. He was a porter among them, so they killed him in the market, so God destroyed them, and their well was disused and their palaces were destroyed.
22:46: 46. Have they not traveled through the land, meaning: the infidels of Mecca, and seen the fates of the disbelievers from the past nations, and have they hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear, meaning: what is mentioned to them of the report of the past centuries so that they may consider it, for it, the ha' is a pillar, is not blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts, mentioning (which are within the breasts) is an emphasis like His saying: It flies with its two wings (Al-An'am: 38) meaning that the harmful blindness is the blindness of the heart, as for the blindness of the sight, it is not harmful in the matter of religion. Qatada said: The apparent sight: in language and enjoyment, and the sight of the heart: is the beneficial sight.
22:47: 47. "And they urge you to hasten the punishment", was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith when he said: If this is the truth from you, then rain down stones on us from the sky. "And God will never fail in His promise", and He fulfilled that on the day of Badr. "And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count", Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read: (َنُدوَن) with the ya' here because of the saying: "َنُدوَنك", and the rest read: with the ta' because it is more general, because it is addressed to those who are impatient and the believers, and they agreed that the revelation of (ال سَنُة) is with the ta'. Ibn Abbas said: It means one of the six days in which God created the heavens and the earth. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: One of the days of the Hereafter. The evidence for this is what was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Rejoice, O group of the vagabonds of the emigrants, with the perfect light on the Day of Resurrection. You will enter Paradise half a day before the rich people, and that is the equivalent of five hundred years.” Ibn Zayd said: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. These are the days of the Hereafter. And His statement: Its measure is fifty thousand years of those which you count. This refers to the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of this is that they are hastening the punishment, and indeed, a day of their punishment in the Hereafter is a thousand years. It was said: Its meaning is that one day of the days of torment that they hastened in terms of heaviness, length, and severity is like a thousand years of what you count, so how can you hasten it? This is like what is said: The days of worries are long, and the days of joy are short. It was said: Its meaning is that a day with Him is the same as a thousand years in terms of respite, because He is able to take them whenever He wills, and nothing escapes Him through delay. So the occurrence of what they are hastening of punishment and its delay are equal in His ability. This is the meaning of what Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Ata’.
22:48: 48. And how many a town did I grant respite to while it was unjust, then I seized it and to Me is the final destination.
22:49: 49. "Say, 'O mankind, I am only to you a clear warner.'"
22:50: 50. So those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and noble provision, the noble provision that never ends. It was said: It is Paradise.
22:51: 51. "And those who strive against Our signs, that is, they worked to invalidate Our signs, are unable to do so." Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read: (extremists) with emphasis here and in Surah Saba', meaning: discouraging people from believing. The others read: (extremists) with an alif, meaning: obstinate and difficult. Qatada said: Its meaning is thinking and estimating that they are unable to do so with their claim that there is no resurrection, no revival, no Paradise, and no Hell. The meaning of they are unable to do so is: they escape us, so we are not able to do so. This is like the statement of God the Almighty: {Or do those who do evil think that they can outrun Us?} (al-Ankabut 29:4), "Those are the companions of Hellfire." It was said: (extremists) are overpowering, each one wants to show the inability of the other.
22:52: 52. The Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan threw into his speech, the verse. Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi and other commentators said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw his people turning away from him and he was distressed by what he saw of their distancing themselves from what he had brought them from God, he wished in his heart that God would bring him something that would bring him closer to his people because of his keenness on their faith. One day, he was in the council of the Quraysh and God Almighty revealed Surah An-Najm. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it until he reached the words: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? Satan put into his tongue what he had been thinking and wishing for: Those are the exalted cranes, and indeed, their intercession is to be hoped for. When the Quraysh heard that, they rejoiced at it and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued his recitation. He recited the entire surah and prostrated at the end of the surah, so the Muslims prostrated with his prostration, and all the polytheists in the mosque prostrated. There remained in the mosque no believer or disbeliever except Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah and Abu Uhayha Sa’id ibn Al-’As, so they took handfuls of sand from the plain and raised them to their foreheads. They prostrated on it, because they were two very old men and could not prostrate. The Quraysh dispersed and were pleased with what they heard of the mention of their gods and they said: Muhammad has mentioned our gods in the best way, and they said: We know that God gives life and causes death, creates and provides, but these gods of ours intercede for us with Him, so if He grants them a share, then we are with Him. When evening came, Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, what have you done? You have recited to the people what I have not brought to you from God, the Almighty! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was very sad and feared God greatly, so God revealed this verse to console him, and He was merciful to him. Those of the Prophet’s companions who were in Abyssinia heard about it and were informed of the prostration of the Quraysh. It was said: Quraysh and the people of Mecca converted to Islam, so most of them returned to their tribes and said: They are dearer to us. When they approached Mecca, they heard that what they had been saying about the people of Mecca converting to Islam was false, so no one entered except under protection or in secret. When this verse was revealed, Quraysh said: Muhammad regretted what he had mentioned about the status of our gods with God, so he changed that. The two letters that Satan had put on the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had fallen into the mouth of every polytheist, so they increased in evil to what they were in, and in severity towards those who converted to Islam. God Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messenger, meaning the one to whom Gabriel brings revelation directly, nor prophet, meaning the one whose prophethood is inspired or in a dream. Every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger, except when he wished, some of them said: meaning he loved something and desired it and thought about it unless he was commanded to do it. Satan cast into his wish, meaning his desire. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Whenever he speaks, Satan casts something into his speech and finds a way to it. There is no prophet who does not wish that his people would believe in him, and no prophet wishes that except that Satan casts something upon him that would please his people, so God abrogates what Satan casts. Most of the commentators said: The meaning of his saying: He wished is: He recited and read the Book of God Almighty. The devil cast into his wish meaning: into his recitation. The poet said about Uthman when he was killed: Wishing for the Book of God the first night and the last one will meet the dove of destiny They differed as to whether he used to recite during prayer or outside of prayer. Some people said: He used to recite during prayer. Others said: He used to recite outside of prayer. If it is said: How is it permissible for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to make a mistake in recitation when he was infallible in the fundamentals of religion, and the Almighty said in the Qur’an: Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it (Fussilat 41:42), meaning Satan? It was said: People differed in their answer to it. Some of them said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not recite it, but Satan mentioned that between his recitation, so the polytheists thought that the Messenger had recited it. Qatada said: The Prophet fell asleep and it came out of his mouth as a result of Satan’s suggestion, but he had no knowledge of it. Most of them said: This happened on his tongue due to Satan’s suggestion, as a result of forgetfulness and negligence, and God soon alerted him to it. It was said: A devil called Abyad did this act, and it was a trial and a test from God Almighty, who tests His servants as He wishes. Then God abrogates what Satan casts, meaning, He invalidates it and removes it. Then God establishes His verses, meaning He confirms them. And God is Knowing and Wise.
22:53: 53. That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is disease meaning: a trial and affliction, doubt and hypocrisy, and hard meaning harsh, their hearts, from accepting the truth, and they are the polytheists, and that is because they were tempted when they heard that, then it was abrogated and removed, so they became more insolent, and they thought that Muhammad was saying it of his own accord and then regretting it and it was invalidated, and indeed the wrongdoers, the polytheists, are in extreme dissension, in severe disagreement.
22:54: 54. And that those who have been given knowledge may know, monotheism and the Qur'an. Al-Suddi said: Belief in the abrogation of God Almighty, that, means: that which God has made firm from the verses of the Qur'an is the truth from your Lord, so they will believe in it, that is: they will believe that it is from God, so their hearts will submit to it, that is: their hearts will be at peace with it, and indeed, God is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path, that is: the straight path, which is Islam.
22:55: 55. And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it, meaning: in doubt about what Satan put on the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They say: Why did he mention it with goodness and then turn away from it? Ibn Jurayj said: (of it) meaning of the Qur’an. It was also said: of the religion, which is the straight path. until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, meaning: the Resurrection. It was also said: death, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren Day, Ad-Dahhak and Ikrimah said: the punishment of a Day that has no night, which is the Day of Resurrection. Most of them agree that the barren day is the Day of Badr, because the Hour was mentioned before, and it is the Day of Resurrection. The Day of Badr was called barren because there was no good for the infidels on that day, like the barren wind that brings no good, neither clouds nor rain. [Barrenness in the language means prevention, it is said: a barren man if he is prevented from having children]. It was said: Because there is no equal to it in the enormity of its matter for the angels to fight on it. Ibn Jurayj said: Because they did not look at it until night until they were killed before the evening.
22:56: 56. The kingdom on that Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection, is for God, alone, without dispute. He will judge between them, then He explained the judgment, saying, So those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in gardens of pleasure.
22:57: 57. And those who disbelieve and deny Our verses - for those is a humiliating punishment.
22:58: 58. And those who emigrated for the cause of God, they left their homelands and clans in obedience to God and seeking His pleasure, and then were killed or died, and they are like that, Ibn Amir read (killed) with emphasis, that God will provide them with a good provision, and the good provision that never ends is the provision of Paradise, and indeed, God is the best of providers, it was said: it is His saying: Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision (Al Imran 3:169).
22:59: 59. He will surely admit them to an entrance that will please them, because there they will have what their souls desire and their eyes delight in. And indeed, God is Knowing, of their intentions, Forbearing, of them.
22:60: 60. "That", meaning: the matter that we have told you about, "and whoever punishes with the like of that with which he was punished", the wrongdoer will be recompensed with the like of the wrong he did to him. Al-Hasan said: It means he fought the polytheists as they fought him, "and then was wronged", meaning: he was wronged by being expelled from his home, meaning: the polytheists did to him of wrongdoing against the Muslims until they were forced to leave their homelands. It was revealed about a group of polytheists who came to a group of Muslims on the last two nights of Muharram, but the Muslims disliked fighting them and asked them to stop fighting for the sake of the sacred month, but the polytheists refused and fought them, and that was their wrongdoing against them, and the Muslims stood firm against them and were victorious over them. God the Most High said: "God will surely aid him, and the first punishment means recompense, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Forgiving, He forgave the faults of the believers and pardoned their sins.
22:61: 61. That meaning: that victory is because God, who is able to do whatever He wills, and part of His ability is that: He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and that God is Hearing and Seeing.
22:62: 62. That is because God is the Truth and that which they invoke, the people of Basra, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read with a ya’, while the others read with a ta’, meaning the polytheists, besides Him is falsehood and that God is the Most High, the High over everything, the Great, the Great to whom everything is beneath.
22:63: 63. Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green, with plants, God is Kind, with the provisions of His servants and the extraction of plants from the earth, Aware, with what is in the hearts of His servants and the extraction of plants from the earth, if the rain is delayed for them.
22:64: 64. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, as servants and kings, and indeed, God is the Free of need, of His servants, the Praiseworthy, in His actions.
22:65: 65. Have you not seen that God has subjected to you whatever is on the earth and the ships, meaning: He has subjected to you the ships, that run through the sea by His command, and it was said: (what is on the earth): the animals are ridden on land, and (the ships) are ridden in the sea, and He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, meaning: so that it does not fall to the ground, “except by His permission. Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful.”
22:66: 66. And it is He who gave you life, that is, He created you when you were nothing, then He will cause you to die, when your appointed times come to an end, then He will bring you to life, on the Day of Resurrection for reward and punishment, Indeed, mankind is ungrateful, for God’s blessings.
22:67: 67. The Almighty said: For every nation We have appointed a ritual which they must follow. Ibn Abbas said: He means a law which they must follow. It was narrated from him that he said: A festival. Qatada and Mujahid said: A place of sacrifice where they slaughter. It was also said: A place of worship. It was also said: A familiar place where they are familiar. In Arabic, the ritual is the usual place for doing good or evil. From this comes the word Hajj rituals for people’s frequent visits to the places of Hajj. So let them not dispute with you in the matter, meaning in the matter of slaughtering. It was revealed about Badil bin Warqa’, Bishr bin Sufyan, and Suzayd bin Khunais. They said to the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why do you eat what you kill with your own hands and not eat what God has killed? Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of his saying, Do not dispute with them is: Do not dispute with them, just as it is said: So-and-so does not dispute with you, meaning: Do not dispute with him. This is permissible in what is between two people, but it is not permissible to say: So-and-so does not hit you, when you mean: Do not hit him. This is because dispute and quarrel are not complete except with two people, so if one of them is left out, then there is no quarrel there. And invite to your Lord, to faith in your Lord, for you are on a straight path.
22:68: 68. And if they argue with you, say, 'God knows best what you do.'
22:69: 69. God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ. Then you will know the truth from falsehood. Difference is when each of the two opponents goes in a direction other than that which the other went in.
22:70: 70. Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that - all of it - is in a book - meaning the Preserved Tablet. Indeed, that - meaning: His knowledge of all of that - is easy for God.
22:71: 71. And they worship besides God that for which He has not sent down any authority, an argument, and of which they have no knowledge, meaning that they did what they did out of ignorance, not knowledge, and for the wrongdoers, the polytheists, no helper, a protector who can prevent them from God’s punishment.
22:72: 72. And when Our clear verses are recited to them, meaning: the Qur'an, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve the disapproval, meaning the denial, it is evident in their faces from hatred and frowning, they are almost assaulting, meaning: they fall and stretch out their hands to them with evil. It was said: they strike, with those who recite to them Our verses, meaning: with Muhammad and his companions from the intensity of anger. It is said: he attacked him with it, if he attacked him with force and violence, and the root of attack is: coercion. Say, O Muhammad, Shall I inform you of something worse than that? That is, something worse for you and more hateful to you than this Qur’an that you are listening to, the Fire, that is, it is the Fire, which God has promised to those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination.
22:73: 73. O people, a parable is struck, the meaning of strike is to make, like their saying: the sultan struck the mission on the people, and imposed the jizya on the people of the covenant, meaning he made that upon them. The meaning of the verse: he made a likeness for me, and likened the idols to me, meaning: the polytheists made the idols my partners and worshipped them. The meaning of so listen to him is: so listen to their condition and description. Then he explained that and said: Indeed, those you call upon besides God, meaning: the idols, Yaqub read it with a ya and the rest read it with a ta will not create a fly, one in its smallness and fewness because it is not able to do anything to it. The fly: singular, its plural is ḍiba, and the plural is ḍiba, like ghurab, aghrabah, and ghuraban. And if they gathered together for it, meaning, for His creation, and if the fly should steal something from them, they could not recover it from it. Ibn Abbas said: They used to coat the idols with saffron, and when it dried, the fly would come and steal from it. Al-Saddī said: They would place food in front of the idols, and they would fall, and flies would land on it and eat from it. Ibn Zayd said: They used to adorn the idols with rubies, pearls and various types of jewels, and perfume them with various types of perfumes. Perhaps one of them would fall and be taken by a bird or fly, and the gods would not be able to recover it. This is what His statement, And if a fly should steal something from them, means: If a fly should steal something from the idols, they would not be able to rescue it from it. The seeker and the sought are weak. Ibn Abbas said: The seeker is the fly seeking what it can steal of perfume from the idol, and the sought is the idol from which the fly seeks to steal.” It was said: The opposite: The seeker is the idol and the sought is the fly. Ad-Dahhak said: The seeker is the worshipper and the sought is the worshipped.
22:74: 74. They have not appreciated God with His true appreciation, they have not glorified Him with His true greatness, nor have they known Him with His true knowledge, nor have they described Him with His true description, if they associate with Him that which cannot be protected from a fly or evaded. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
22:75: 75. God chooses, meaning He selects from the angels messengers, who are Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, Azrael, and others, and from the people, meaning: He chooses from the people messengers such as Abraham, Moses, Jesus, Muhammad, peace be upon him, and other prophets, peace be upon them. It was revealed when the polytheists said: Has the message been sent down to him from among us? So He informed us that the choice is up to Him, and He chooses whomever He wills from among His creation. God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, meaning: He hears what they say and sees whom He chooses for His message.
22:76: 76. He knows what is before them, Ibn Abbas said: what they sent forth, and what is behind them, what they left behind. Al-Hasan said: What is before them: what they did, and what is behind them: what they will do afterward. It was said: “What is before them: His angels, His books, and His messengers before He created them, “and what is behind them”: meaning: He knows what will happen after their demise. And to God all matters will return.
40:60: 77. O you who have believed, bow and prostrate, meaning: pray, because prayer is not complete without bowing and prostrating, and worship your Lord, singling Him out, and do good, Ibn Abbas said: maintaining kinship ties and good morals, that you may succeed, so that you may be happy and win Paradise. The scholars differed regarding the prostration of recitation when reciting this verse: Some people said that he prostrates at it, and this is the opinion of Umar, Ali, Ibn Umar, Ibn Masoud, and Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Al-Mubarak, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq said the same. They provided evidence for this with what Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Qutaybah told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Mishrah bin Ha’an, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, is Surah Al-Hajj superior in that it contains two prostrations? He said: Yes, and whoever does not prostrate in them should not recite them. Some people said that he does not prostrate here, which is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion. The number of prostrations in the Qur’an is fourteen according to most scholars, three of which are in the Mufassal. Some people said that there is no prostration in the joints. This was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab and Ibn Abbas, and Malik said the same. It was authentically reported on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: We prostrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Iqra and When the sky is split. Abu Hurairah was one of the later converts to Islam. They differed about the prostration of Sad. Al-Shafi’i said that it is a prostration of gratitude and is not among the obligatory prostrations. This is narrated from Ibn Abbas. Some people said that one prostrates in it. This was narrated from Umar. Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, the People of Opinion, Ahmad, and Ishaq said the same. According to Ibn al-Mubarak, Ishaq, Ahmad, and a group, the prostration of the Qur’an is fifteen prostrations. They counted the two prostrations of Hajj and the prostration of Sad. It was narrated from Amr ibn al-Aas that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited fifteen prostrations in the Qur’an.” 78. The Almighty said: And strive in the cause of God with the striving due to Him. It was said: Struggle in the cause of God against the enemies of God (with the striving due to Him) is to exhaust one’s energy in it. Ibn Abbas said: And it was also narrated from him that he said: Do not fear the blame of a critic in the cause of God, for it is the right striving, as the Almighty said: They strive in the cause of God and do not fear the blame of a critic (al-Ma’idah 5:54). Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: Work for God as He should be worked for and worship Him as He should be worshipped. Muqatil bin Sulayman said: It was abrogated by His statement: So fear God as much as you are able (al-Taghabun 64:16). Most of the commentators said: The right of jihad is that one’s intention be purely for the sake of God Almighty. Al-Suddi said: It is that one be obeyed and not disobeyed. Abdullah bin Mubarak said: It is the struggle against the self and desires, and it is the greater jihad, and it is the true jihad. It was narrated that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from the Battle of Tabuk, he said: We have returned from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad, and by the lesser jihad he meant jihad against the infidels, and by the greater jihad he meant jihad against the self. He has chosen you meaning: He has selected you for His religion, and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty meaning: that the believer is not afflicted with any of the sins except that God makes a way out for him from it, some of them through repentance, some of them through the redress of wrongs and retribution, and some of them through various types of expiation. So there is no sin in the religion of Islam for which the servant cannot find a way to escape punishment for it. It was said: If the times of your obligations are tight, such as the crescent of Ramadan, the Eid al-Fitr, and the time of Hajj, if that is unclear to you, then He will make it easy for you until you are certain. Muqatil said: It means concessions in cases of necessity, such as shortening the prayer while traveling, performing tayammum, eating carrion when necessary, breaking the fast while traveling or sick, and praying while sitting when unable to do so. This is the opinion of Al-Kalbi. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The hardship was what was upon the Children of Israel from the burdens that were upon them, and God removed it from this nation. The religion of your father Abraham, meaning the word your father, is in the accusative case, with the letter of description removed. It was also said that it is in the accusative case for enticement, meaning follow the religion of your father Abraham, [and we were only commanded to follow the religion of Abraham] because it is included in the religion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If it is said: What is the point of his saying: The religion of your father when not all Muslims trace their lineage back to Abraham? It was said: He addressed the Arabs with it, and they were descendants of Abraham. It was also said: He addressed all Muslims with it, and Abraham is their father, meaning that it is obligatory to respect him and preserve his right as it is obligatory to respect a father, and it is like the Almighty’s saying: And his wives are their mothers (al-Ahzab 33:6), and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am to you like a father [to his son]. He named you means that God the Most High named you Muslims before, meaning before the revelation of the Qur'an in the previous books. In this meaning: in this book, this is the saying of most of the commentators. Ibn Zayd said: (He) goes back to Abraham, meaning that Abraham named you Muslims in his days, before this time, and at this time, and it is His saying: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You (al-Baqarah 2:127), that the Messenger may be a witness over you, on the Day of Resurrection that he has conveyed to you, and that you may be, you, witnesses over the people, that their messengers have conveyed to them, so establish prayer and give zakah and hold fast to God meaning: trust in God and rely on Him. Al-Hasan said: Hold fast to the religion of God. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Ask your Lord to protect you from everything that He dislikes. It was said: Its meaning is call upon Him to make you steadfast in His religion. It was also said: Holding fast to God is adhering to the Book and the Sunnah, He is your Master, [your Guardian], your Supporter and your Preserver, What an excellent Master and what an excellent Helper, the Helper for you. 60. And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you.’ That is, worship Me alone and I will respond to you, reward you, and forgive you. So when He expressed worship as supplication, He made repentance a response. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Dhir, on the authority of Yas’i’ Al-Kindi, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the pulpit: Verily, supplication is worship. Then he recited: ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.’” Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Dawraqi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qurashi told us in Baghdad, Muhammad ibn Ubayd ibn al-Ala’ told us, Ahmad ibn Badil told us, Waki’ told us, Abu al-Malih told us: I heard Abu Salih mentioning on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does not supplicate to God, God will be angry with him. It was said: Supplication is remembrance and question, Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell, humiliated. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja`far, and Abu Bakr read: (they will enter) with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the kha’. The others read with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the kha’, (humiliated), humiliated and disgraced.
23:1: Makkiyy, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Hayri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Yunus ibn Sulayman told us, Yunus, the companion of Ayla, dictated to me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: “When revelation came down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a sound like the buzzing of bees would be heard near his face, and we stayed for an hour - and in another narration: It came down to him one day and we stayed for an hour - then he faced the qiblah and raised his hands and said: O God, increase us and do not decrease us, and honor us and do not humiliate us, and give to us and do not deprive us, and give us preference and do not give others preference over us, and be pleased with us, then he said: Ten verses have been revealed to me, whoever recites them will enter Paradise, then he recited: ‘The believers have succeeded’ to ten verses.” It was narrated by Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ali ibn al-Madini, and a group on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, and they said: Give to us and do not deprive us, satisfy us and be satisfied with us. 1. The Almighty says: Indeed, the believers have succeeded. “Qad” is a letter of emphasis. The scholars said: Qad brings the past closer to the present, indicating that they have achieved success and that they are in it now. This is more eloquent than simply mentioning the action. And success means salvation and survival. Ibn Abbas said: Those who believe in monotheism have been blessed and will remain in Paradise.
23:2: 2. Those who are humble in their prayers. They differed on the meaning of humility. Ibn Abbas said: Submissive and humble. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: Fearful. Muqatil said: Humble. Mujahid said: It is lowering the gaze and lowering the voice. Humility is similar to submission, except that submission is in the body, and humility is in the heart, body, sight, and voice. God Almighty said: And voices are hushed before the Most Merciful (Ta-Ha 20:108). On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: It is that he does not look right or left. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is that he does not know who is on his right or who is on his left, and he does not look back out of humility to God Almighty. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musaddad told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, Ash’ath bin Salim told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about turning around in prayer, and he said: It is a theft that Satan steals from the prayer of the servant.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu al-Hasan al-Qasim ibn Bakr al-Tayalisi told us in Baghdad, Abu Umayyah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tarsusi told us, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Ubayd God told us, Salih ibn Abi al-Akhdar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abu Dharr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God continues to turn towards the servant as long as he is in his prayer, as long as he does not turn away. If he turns away, He turns away from him.” Amr bin Dinar said: It is stillness and good appearance. Ibn Sirin and others said: It is that you do not raise your gaze from the place of your prostration. Abu Hurairah said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to raise their eyes to the sky during prayer. When the verse, Those who are humble in their prayer, was revealed, they lowered their eyes to the places of prostration. Abdul Wahid Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Ibn Abi Aruba told us, Qatada told us that Anas bin Malik told them that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is the matter with people who raise their eyes to the sky during their prayer? His words were so harsh about that that he said: They should stop doing that or their eyes will be snatched away. Ata’ said: It is that you do not play with any part of your body during prayer. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “saw a man playing with his beard during prayer and said: If this man’s heart were humble, his limbs would be humble.” Abu Uthman al-Dhabi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abu Dharr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When one of you stands up to pray, he should not wipe the pebbles, for mercy faces him. It was said: Humility in prayer is to gather one’s attention, turn away from everything else, and contemplate what comes to one’s tongue in terms of recitation and remembrance.
23:3: 3. The Almighty said: And those who turn away from ill speech. Ata' said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: From polytheism. Al-Hasan said: From sins. Al-Zajjaj said: From every falsehood and amusement and what is not permissible of speech and action. It was said: It is opposing the infidels with cursing and insults. God the Almighty said: And when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity. (al-Furqan 25:72), meaning: When they hear ugly speech, they honor themselves by not engaging in it.
23:4: 4. And those who are active in paying zakat, meaning: those who are active in paying the obligatory zakat, so the action was expressed by the verb because it is an action. It was said: zakat here is righteous work, meaning: and those who are active in doing righteous work.
23:5: 5. And those who guard their private parts, the private parts: a noun that includes the private parts of a man and a woman, and guarding the private parts: abstaining from what is forbidden.
23:6: 6. Except from their wives, meaning: from their wives, and (on) means (from). Or what their right hands possess, what is in the accusative case, meaning or from what their right hands possess, and the verse is specifically about men, as evidenced by His statement: Or what their right hands possess and a woman is not permitted to enjoy the vagina of her slave. For they will not be blamed, meaning he guards his vagina except from his wife or female slave, then he will not be blamed for that, and he will not be blamed for them if it is in a manner permitted by the Shariah, but not in a state other than that which is permissible, and in the case of menstruation and postpartum bleeding, then it is forbidden and he will be blamed for his action.
23:7: 7. But whoever seeks beyond that, that is, seeks and requests other than wives and owned female slaves. Then those are the transgressors, the wrongdoers who transgress from the permissible to the forbidden. This is evidence that masturbation is forbidden, and this is the opinion of most scholars. Ibn Jurayj said: I asked Ata' about it and he said: It is disliked. I heard that a people will be gathered and their hands will be pregnant, so I think that they are these people. And on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, he said: God punished a nation who played with their private parts.
23:8: 8.
