27:11: And His statement: 11- "Except for he who has wronged and then substituted evil for good, for indeed, I am Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful." There is a difference of opinion regarding this exception. It was said: This is an indication that when Moses killed the Copt, he feared that, then he repented and said: "My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me," and He forgave him. Ibn Jurayj said: God, the Most High, said to Moses: "I only frightened you because you killed a soul." He said: The meaning of the verse is: God does not frighten the prophets except because of a sin that one of them commits. If it befalls him, He frightens him until he repents. According to this interpretation, the exception is correct, and the report about the messengers ends with His statement: "Except for he who has wronged," then the report begins about the state of all people who have wronged. In the verse, there is something omitted that is not necessary to mention because of the evidence of the discussion, its meaning: But whoever has wronged and then substituted evil for good, for indeed, I am Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. Some scholars said: This is not an exception from the messengers because injustice is not permissible for them, rather it is an exception from what is omitted in the speech, meaning: There is no fear in the presence of the messengers, but fear is for others from the oppressors, except for he who has wronged and then repented. This is from the discontinuous exception, meaning: But whoever wrongs from among the rest of the people, then he will fear, but if he repents and replaces evil with good, then God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning God will forgive him and remove the fear from him. Some grammarians said: Except here means nor, meaning: Neither the messengers nor the wrongdoers fear me. Then he changed bad to good, saying: Neither the messengers nor the repentant sinners fear me, like the Almighty’s saying: So that mankind will have no argument against you, except for those of them who have wronged Al-Baqarah 2:150, meaning: nor those who have wronged.
27:12: Then God showed him another sign and said: 12- And put your hand into your bosom, and the bosom is where the pocket of the shirt is, i.e., cut. The commentators said: He was wearing a coat of wool that had no sleeves or buttons, so he put his hand into his bosom and took it out, and behold, it was flashing like lightning. That is what He said: It will come out white without disease, without leprosy, in nine signs, meaning this is a sign from the nine signs that you are sent with, “to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they were a people of evildoers.”
27:13: 13- So when Our clear signs came to them, clear evidence with which one can see, they said, ‘This is obvious magic,’ apparent.
27:14: 14- And they denied them, meaning: they rejected the signs and did not acknowledge that they were from God, and their souls were convinced of them, meaning: they knew that they were from God. His statement: injustice and arrogance, meaning: polytheism and arrogance to believe in what Moses brought, Then see how was the end of the corrupters.
27:15: God Almighty says: 15- And We certainly gave David and Solomon knowledge, meaning: the knowledge of judgment, the language of birds and beasts, the subjugation of devils, and the glorification of mountains. And they said, ‘Praise be to God, who has favored us,’ with prophethood, the Book, and the subjugation of devils, jinn, and mankind, over many of His believing servants.
27:16: 16- And Solomon inherited David’s prophecy, knowledge, and kingdom, without the rest of his sons. David had nineteen sons, and Solomon was given the same kingdom as David, and he was given the ability to control the wind and the demons. Muqatil said: Solomon was a greater king than David and more just than him. David was more pious than Solomon, and Solomon was grateful for the blessings of God Almighty. And he said, ‘O people, teach us the language of birds.’ He called the sound of birds language because one can understand it, just as one can understand the speech of people. It was narrated on the authority of Ka'b that he said: Warshaan cried out in the presence of Solomon, peace be upon him, and he said: Do you know what he is saying? They said: No. He said: He says: Give birth to death and build for destruction. A quail cried out, and he said: Do you know what he is saying? They said: No. He said: He says: I wish these people had never been created. A peacock cried out, and he said: Do you know what he is saying? They said: No. He said: He says: As you judge, you will be judged. A hoopoe cried out, and he said: Do you know what this is saying? They said: No. He said: He says: He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy. A shrike cried out, and he said: Do you know what he is saying? They said: No. He said: He says: Seek forgiveness from God, you sinners. A toot cried out, and he said: Do you know what he is saying? They said: No. He said: He says: Every living thing will die and every iron will be wasted. A swallow cried out, and he said: Do you know what he is saying? They said: No. He said: He says: Go forward with goodness and you will find it. A dove cooed, and he said: Do you know what it is saying? They said: No. He said: It says: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, filling the heavens and the earth. And my dove crowed. He said: Do you know what it says? They said: No. He said: It says: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. He said: And the crow curses the ten-year-old, and the kite says: Everything will perish except God, and the sandgrouse says: He who is silent is safe, and the parrot says: Woe to he whose concern is the world, and the frog says: Glory be to my Holy Lord, and the hawk says: Glory be to my Lord and with His praise, and the frog says: Glory be to Him who is remembered in every tongue. On the authority of Makhul, he said: Diraj shouted in the presence of Sulayman and said: Do you know what he is saying? They said: No. He said: He says: The Most Gracious is firmly established on the Throne. On the authority of Farqad Al-Sabkhi, he said: Solomon passed by a nightingale perched on a tree, waving its head and swaying its tail. He said to his companions: Do you know what this nightingale is saying? They said: God and His Prophet know best. He said: It is saying: I ate half a date, so the world is fine. It was narrated that a group of Jews said to Ibn Abbas, "We will ask you about seven things. If you tell us, we will believe and be truthful." He said, Ask for the sake of understanding and do not ask for the sake of stubbornness. They said, "Tell us what the hoopoe says when it whistles, and the rooster when it crows, and the frog when it croaks, and the donkey when it brays, and the horse when it neighs, and what do the starling and the partridge say?" He said, "Yes. The hoopoe says, 'O God, curse those who hate Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.' The rooster says, 'Remember God, you heedless ones.' The frog says, 'Glory be to the One worshipped in the depths of the seas.' The donkey says, 'O God, curse the tax collector.' The horse says, 'When the two ranks meet, Glory be to the Holy One, Lord of the angels and the spirit.' The starling says, 'O God, I ask You for sustenance for every day, O Provider.' The partridge says, 'The Most Gracious is firmly established on the Throne.'" So the Jews embraced Islam, and their Islam was excellent. It was narrated on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Ali, who said: When the eagle crows, it says: O son of Adam, live as long as you wish, for the end of it is death. When the hawk crows, it says: There is comfort in being far from people. When the lark crows, it says: O my God, curse those who hate the family of Muhammad. When the swallow crows, it recites: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and it prolongs the astray as the reciter prolongs. God the Almighty says: And We have been given of all things. Prophets and kings are given. Ibn Abbas said: Of the affairs of this world and the hereafter. Muqatil said: He means prophethood, kingship, and the subjugation of the jinn, devils, and winds. Indeed, this is the manifest bounty, the apparent increase over what others have been given. It was narrated that Solomon, peace be upon him, was given the kingdom of the East and West of the earth, and he ruled for seven hundred years and six months, ruling over all the people of the world, from the jinn, humans, animals, birds, and wild beasts. He was given the ability to speak all things, and in his time, wondrous creations were made.
27:17: God Almighty said: 17- And there were gathered before Solomon his soldiers of jinn, mankind, and birds in his march, and they were sent in ranks, so they were kept back. Qatada said: There was a group for each class of his soldiers, the first of which would return to the last of them so that they would not advance in the march, and the deterrent is the restrainer, and he is the captain. Muqatil said: They were sent in ranks, they were driven. Al-Suddi said: They stop. It was also said: They gather. The origin of waze’ is to restrain and prevent. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Solomon's camp was one hundred farsakhs, twenty-five of which were for humans, twenty-five for jinn, twenty-five for beasts, and twenty-five for birds. He had one thousand houses made of glass on wood, in which were three hundred clear winds and seven hundred secret ones. He would command the violent winds to lift him up, and command the soft winds to carry him. God revealed to him while he was traveling between heaven and earth: I have increased your kingdom so that no one among creation speaks of anything except that the wind brings it, and it will inform you.
27:18: God Almighty said: 18- "Until, when they came upon the Valley of the Ants," it was narrated on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih on the authority of Ka'b who said: When Solomon rode, he would carry his family, servants and retinue. He had made kitchens and bakeries in which he carried iron ovens and large pots, each pot holding ten islands. He had made paddocks for the animals in front of him, so the cooks would cook and the bakers would pass, and the animals would run before him between the sky and the earth, and the wind would blow them. So he traveled from Istakhr to Yemen and took the path of the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Solomon said: This is the abode of the migration of a prophet at the end of time. Blessed is he who believes in him and blessed is he who follows him. And he saw around the House idols that were worshipped besides God. So when Solomon passed the House, the House wept, / So God revealed to the House what makes you weep? He said: O Lord, what makes me cry is that this is one of your prophets and a people of your friends who passed by me and did not descend or pray near me, and idols are worshipped around me instead of you. So God revealed to him: Do not cry, for I will fill you with faces prostrating, and I will send down a new Quran about you, and I will send from you a prophet at the end of time who will be the most beloved of My prophets to me, and I will place in you inhabitants from My creation who will worship Me, and I will impose on My servants an obligation that they will flock to you like eagles flock to their nests, and they will yearn for you like a camel yearns for her young and a dove for her egg, and I will purify you from idols and devil worshippers. Then Solomon went on until he passed by Wadi As-Sudair, a valley in Taif, and he came to Wadi An-Naml. This is what Ka’b said: It is a valley in Taif. Qatada and Muqatil said: It is a land in the Levant. It was also said: It was a valley inhabited by the jinn, and those ants were their mounts. Nawf Al-Himyari said: The ants of that valley were like flies. It was also said: Like the Bukhati. What is well known is: It is the small ant. Al-Sha’bi said: That ant had two wings. It was also said: It was a lame ant, so it called out: “An ant said, ‘O ants, enter your dwellings.’ She did not say, ‘Enter,’ because when He gave them speech like humans, they were addressed as humans would. ‘Do not let Solomon and his soldiers crush you,’ ‘Do not crush you,’ while they perceive not.” So Solomon heard her words, and no creature spoke except that the wind carried that and threw it into Solomon’s ears. Muqatil said: Solomon heard her words from three miles away. Ad-Dahhak said: The name of that ant was Tahiyah. Muqatil said: Her name was Jarma. If it is said: How can the destruction of Solomon and his soldiers be imagined, when the wind carried Solomon and his soldiers on a carpet between the sky and the earth? It was said: His soldiers were mounted, and among them were foot soldiers who were folded on the ground for them. It was said: It is possible that this was before God subjected the wind to Solomon. The commentators said: The ants knew that Solomon was a prophet who was not tyrannical or unjust. The meaning of the verse is: If you did not enter your dwellings, they would trample you and would not notice you. It is narrated that when Solomon reached the Valley of the Ants, he held back his soldiers until the ants entered their homes.
27:19: God Almighty said: 19- So he smiled, laughing at her words. Al-Zajjaj said: Most of the prophets’ laughter was a smile. And his saying laughing means smiling. It was said: It began with a smile and ended with laughter. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Sulayman told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr told us, he is Ibn Al-Harith, Al-Nadr told us, he told him on the authority of Sulayman bin Yasar, on the authority of Aisha, she said: “I never saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughing so much that I could see his uvula. He would only smile.” Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juzajani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Khuza’i told us, Al-Haytham bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mughira on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Juz’ who said: “I have never seen anyone smile more than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Muqatil said: Solomon laughed at the ant’s words out of astonishment, because when a person sees something he is not used to, he is astonished and laughs, then Solomon thanked his Lord for what He had bestowed upon him. “And he said, ‘My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me, by Your mercy, into [the company of] Your righteous servants.’” That is, admit me into their company, establish my name with their names, and gather me with them. Ibn Abbas said: He means with Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the prophets who came after them. It was also said: admit me into Paradise, by Your mercy, with Your righteous servants.
27:20: God Almighty said: 20- And he inspected the birds, meaning: he sought them and looked for them. Inspection is seeking what he had lost, and the meaning of the verse is: he sought what he had lost of the birds. And he said, ‘Why do I not see the hoopoe?’ Meaning: Why do I not see the hoopoe? The Arabs say: Why do I see you so sad? Meaning: What is the matter with you? The hoopoe is a well-known bird. The reason for his inspecting the hoopoe and asking about it was said to be his failure to pronounce the letter nun. This is because whenever Solomon would descend to a house, he and his army of birds would shade him from the sun, and the sun would hit him from the place where the hoopoe had been, so he looked and saw it empty. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the hoopoe was Solomon’s guide to water. He knew where the water was and could see it underground, just as he could see it in a bottle. He knew its nearness and its distance, so he would peck the ground, and then the devils would come and skin it and extract the water. Saeed bin Jubair said: When Ibn Abbas mentioned this, Nafi’ bin Al-Azraq said to him: “O Wassaf, watch what you say. A boy among us sets a trap and throws dirt on it, and a hoopoe comes and does not see the trap until it falls around his neck.” Ibn Abbas said to him: Woe to you, when fate comes, it obstructs sight. In another narration: When fate and destiny descend, reason is lost and sight is blinded. So Solomon stopped at a place and needed water. They searched for it but did not find any. He looked for the hoopoe to guide him to water, and said: Why do I not see the hoopoe? assuming that he was with his soldiers, but he did not see him. Then doubt overcame him about his absence, so he said: Or was he among the absent ones? Meaning, was he among the absent ones? The mim is a connective, and it was said that am means rather.
27:21: Then he threatened him for his absence, saying: 21- I will surely punish him with a severe punishment. They differed about the punishment with which He threatened him. The most correct of the sayings is that his feathers and tail will be plucked out and he will be thrown out into the sun, drying out, unable to protect himself from ants or any of the vermin of the earth. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: I will cover him with tar and expose him to the sun. It was also said: I will put him in a cage. It was also said: I will separate him from his companion. It was also said: I will imprison him with his enemy. “Or I will slaughter him,” I will cut his throat, or he brings me clear authority, with a clear argument for his absence and a clear excuse. Ibn Kathir read: to bring me with two nuns, the first with a shaddah, while the others read it with one shaddah nun. The reason for the hoopoe's occultation, according to what the scholars have mentioned, is that when Solomon finished building the Temple in Jerusalem, he decided to go to the Sacred Sanctuary. So he prepared to set out, and took with him jinn, humans, devils, birds and wild animals, so that his camp reached a distance of one hundred farsakhs, but the wind carried them away. When he reached the Sacred Sanctuary, he stayed there as long as God willed him to stay. Every day, in his residence in Mecca, he would slaughter five thousand camels, five thousand bulls and twenty thousand sheep. He said to the nobles of his people who were present: "This is a place from which will emerge an Arab prophet with such-and-such characteristics. He will be granted victory over all who oppose him, and his awe will extend a distance of a month's journey. Near and far are equal in his view of the truth. For the sake of God, he is not afraid of the blame of any blamer." They said: What religion will he follow, O Prophet of God? He said: "He follows the religion of the true monotheism. So blessed is he who meets him and believes in him." They said: How long is it until his emergence, O Prophet of God? He said: The length of a thousand years, so let the witness among you inform the absent, for he is the master of the prophets and the seal of the messengers. He said: So he stayed in Mecca until he completed his rituals, then he left Mecca in the morning, and walked towards Yemen and reached Sana'a at noon, which is a month's journey. He saw a beautiful land adorned with greenery, so he wanted to alight there to pray and have lunch. When he alighted, the hoopoe said: Solomon is busy with his descent, so ascend towards the sky and look at the length and breadth of the world. So he did that, and looked right and left and saw a garden of Bilqis. He turned towards the greenery and fell into it and there he was, a hoopoe, so he alighted upon it. The name of Solomon's hoopoe was Ya'fur, and the name of the hoopoe of Yemen was Anfeer. The Anfeer of Yemen said to Solomon, Where have you come from and where are you going? He said: I have come from Syria with my companion Solomon, son of David. He said: And who is Solomon? He said: "The king of the jinn, mankind, devils, birds, beasts, and winds. So where are you from?" He said: I am from this country. He said: And who is its king? He said: A woman called Bilqis, and your master has a great kingdom, but Bilqis's kingdom is not inferior to his, for she is the queen of all Yemen, and under her hand are twelve thousand commanders, each commander having a hundred thousand fighters. Will you go with me so that you may see her kingdom? He said: I fear that Solomon might visit me during the time of prayer if he needs water. The Yemeni hoopoe said: Your master would be pleased if you could bring him report of this queen, so he went with him and saw Bilqis and her kingdom, and he did not return to Solomon until the afternoon. He said: When Solomon dismounted and the time for prayer came, and he had dismounted by no water, he asked the humans, jinn and devils about water but they did not know. He looked for the birds and lost the hoopoe, so he called the chief of the birds - the eagle - and asked him about the hoopoe. The eagle said: May God set the kingdom right, I do not know where it is, and I did not send it anywhere. At that, Solomon became angry and said: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment the verse. Then he called the eagle, the master of birds, and said, Upon the hoopoe, just now. The eagle raised himself up above the sky until he clung to the air. He looked at the world like a bowl in the hands of one of you. Then he looked right and left and saw the hoopoe coming from the direction of Yemen. The eagle swooped down on him, wanting to catch him. When the hoopoe saw that, he knew that the eagle meant him harm, so he implored him, saying, By God, who gave you strength and power over me, have mercy on me and do not harm me. The eagle turned away from him and said, "Woe to you, may your mother be bereaved of you. The Prophet of God has sworn that he will torture or slaughter you." Then they flew off towards Solomon. When they arrived at the camp, the eagle and the birds met him and said, Woe to you, where have you been today? The Prophet of God has threatened you. They told him what he had said. The hoopoe said, Did the Messenger of God not make an exception? Then the eagle and the hoopoe flew until they reached Solomon, who was sitting on his throne. The eagle said, I have brought him to you, O Prophet of God. When the hoopoe came near, he raised his head and lowered his tail and wings, dragging them on the ground in humility to Solomon. When he came near, he took him by the head and stretched him out and said, Where have you been? I will surely punish you with a severe punishment. The hoopoe said, O Prophet of God, remember your standing before God Almighty. When Solomon heard that, he trembled and forgave him. Then he asked him, What delayed you from coming to me?
27:22: Then the hoopoe said what God told us about in His saying: 22- So he stayed not far away. Asim and Ya’qub read: So he stayed with the kaf open, and the others read it with the kaf closed, and they are two dialects, not far away, meaning: not long. “So he said: I have encompassed that which you have not encompassed.” Encompassment is knowledge of something from all sides. He says: I learned what you did not know, and I reached what you and your soldiers did not reach. And I came to you from Sheba. Abu Amr, Al-Bazzi, on the authority of Ibn Kathir, read from Sheba and for Sheba in Surat Saba’ with the hamza open. Al-Qawwas, on the authority of Ibn Kathir, read it with a sukoon without a hamza. The others read it with the accusative case. Whoever did not accusative it made it the name of the country, and whoever did make it accusative made it the name of a man. It was mentioned in the hadith: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about Sheba, and he said: He was a man who had ten sons, six of whom were auspicious and four were unlucky.” With good report, “certain.”
27:23: So Suleiman said: What is that? He said: 23- I found a woman to rule them. Her name was Bilqis bint Sharaheel, from the lineage of Ya’rub bin Qahtan. Her father was a king of great importance, and forty kings were born to him, and he was the last of them. He ruled the entire land of Yemen. He used to say to the kings of the outskirts: None of you is equal to me. He refused to marry among them, so they married him to a woman from the jinn called Rayhana bint al-Sakn, and she bore him Bilqis. He had no other children besides her. It was mentioned in the hadith: One of Bilqis’s parents was a jinn. When Abu Bilqis died, she coveted the kingdom, so she asked her people to pledge allegiance to her. Some obeyed her, while others disobeyed. They made a man king over them, and they split into two groups, each group taking over a part of the land of Yemen. Then the man they made king behaved badly toward the people of his kingdom, to the point that he would extend his hand to the women of his subjects and commit adultery with them. His people wanted to depose him, but they could not. When Bilqis saw that, jealousy overcame her, so she sent to him offering herself to him. The king responded to her and said: Nothing prevented me from initiating the marriage proposal to you except despair of you. She said: “I do not desire you. You are a worthy and generous man. Gather the men of my people and propose to them for her hand.” So he gathered them and proposed to them for her hand. They said: We do not see her doing this. He said to them: She initiated the marriage proposal, so I would like you to hear her words. So they came to her and mentioned it to her, and she said: Yes, I love the child. So they married her to him. When she was brought to him, she went out with many of her servants. When she came to him, she gave him wine to drink until he became drunk. Then she cut off his head and went back to her house at night. When morning came, the people saw the king dead and his head hung at the door of her house. They knew that this marriage was a trick and deception on her part. They gathered around her and said: You have more right to this kingship than anyone else. So they made her their queen. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Uthman bin Al-Haitham told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Bakra, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard that the people of Persia had made the daughter of Kisra their king, he said: A people who appoint a woman as their ruler will never prosper. God Almighty says: And she has been given of all things, which kings need in terms of tools and equipment, and she has a mighty throne, a huge bed that was made of gold and crowned with pearls, rubies, and emeralds, and its legs were made of rubies and emeralds, and over it were seven doors, each with a closed door. Ibn Abbas said: The throne of Bilqis was thirty cubits by thirty cubits, and its height in the sky was thirty cubits. Muqatil said: Its length was eighty cubits and its height in the sky was eighty cubits. It was said: Its length was eighty cubits, its width was forty cubits, and its height was thirty cubits.
27:24: 24- “I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God. Satan has made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided.”
27:25: 25- That they should not prostrate themselves, Abu Ja`far and Al-Kisa`i read: that they should not prostrate themselves with a light pronunciation, and if they stop they stop. Ala ya: Ala ya`thim then they begin: Prostrate yourself with the meaning: Ala ya ya`thim and they made it a renewed command from God, and they deleted these as they were satisfied with the indication of ya on it, and some of them mentioned hearing from the Arabs: Ala ya irhamuna, meaning Ala ya qawm, and Al-Akhtal said: Oh, Aslami, oh Hind, oh Hind of Bani Bakr, even if Hayyan is a enemy until the end of time He means: O Aslami, O Hind. Based on this, his saying O is an interjection from outside the story, either from the hoopoe or from Solomon. Abu Ubaidah said: This is a renewed command from God, meaning: O people, prostrate. Others read: that they should not prostrate with emphasis, meaning: Satan made their deeds seem good to them so that they would not prostrate, to God who brings forth what is hidden, meaning: the hidden, concealed, in the heavens and the earth, meaning: what is hidden. Most commentators said: Khaba’ al-Sama’ means rain, and Khaba’ al-Ard means plants. In Abdullah’s reading: He brings forth the hidden from the heavens and the earth, and from and in alternate. The Arabs say: I will extract knowledge from you, meaning: from you. It was said: The meaning of Al-Khaba’ is the unseen, meaning: He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And He knows what you conceal and what you declare. Al-Kisa’i and Hafs, on the authority of Asim, read it with a ta’ in both of them, because the beginning of the verse is an address according to Al-Kisa’i’s reading with a light ala, and the others read it with a ya’.
27:26: 26- God, there is no god but He, Lord of the Mighty Throne, meaning: He is the One who deserves to be worshipped and prostrated to, and no one else. The throne of the Queen of Sheba, although great, is small and insignificant compared to His throne, the Almighty and Majestic. Here the hoopoe’s words are complete.
27:27: When the hoopoe finished speaking. 27- He said, Solomon said to the hoopoe: We will see whether you have spoken the truth, or whether you are among the liars? So the hoopoe guided them to the water, so they dug the wells, and watered the people and animals. Then Solomon wrote a letter: From the servant of God, Solomon, son of David, to Bilqis, Queen of Sheba: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Peace be upon him who follows the guidance. As for what follows: Do not exalt yourselves over me, but come to me in submission.” Ibn Jurayj said: Solomon did not add anything to what God related in his book. Qatada said: And so the prophets used to write in sentences, neither lengthening nor multiplying. So when he wrote the letter, he sealed it with musk and sealed it with his ring.
27:28: Then he said to the hoopoe: 28- Go with this letter of mine and throw it to them. Abu Amr, Asim, and Hamzah read it with a sukoon on the ha’, but Abu Ja’far, Ya’qub, and Qalun pronounce it with a kasra, while the others pronounce it with a sukoon, then turn away from them, move away from them and be close to them, and see what they return, what they respond with. Ibn Zayd said: The verse has an inversion of the original meaning: Go with this letter of mine and throw it to them and see what they return, then turn away from them, meaning: come back to me. So the hoopoe took the letter and brought it to Bilqis, who was in a land called Ma’rib, three days away from Sana’a. He came to her in her palace and the doors were locked. Whenever she slept, she locked the doors and took the keys and placed them under her head. Then the hoopoe came to her while she was sleeping, lying on her back, and threw the letter on her throat. This is the statement of Qatada. Muqatil said: The hoopoe carried the book in its beak until it landed on the woman’s head, surrounded by leaders and soldiers. It fluttered for a while while people watched it, until the woman raised her head and the hoopoe threw the book into her lap. Ibn Munabbih and Ibn Zayd said: She had a window facing the sun, and the sun would set in it when it rose. When it was slow to approach her, she would prostrate to it. Then the hoopoe came to the window and blocked it with his wings, so the sun rose without her noticing. When the sun was slow to approach, she stood up to look. Then the hoopoe threw the scroll to her, and Bilqis took the scroll, and she could read. When she saw the seal, she trembled and submitted because the kingdom of Solomon was in his seal, and she knew that the one who had sent the letter to her was a greater king than her. So she read the letter, and the hoopoe stayed a short time. She came and sat on the throne of her kingdom and gathered the leaders of her people, who were twelve thousand leaders, with each leader one hundred thousand fighters. Ibn Abbas said: With Bilqis were one hundred thousand leaders, with each leader one hundred thousand, and the king is less than the greatest king. Qatada and Muqatil said: Her advisors were three hundred and thirteen men, each man with ten thousand. He said: So they came and took their seats.
27:29: 29- She said, Bilqis to them: O assembly, and they were the nobles and leaders of the people, Indeed, a noble letter has been delivered to me. Ata’ and Ad-Dahhak said: She called it noble because it was sealed. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: The nobleness of the letter is its seal. Qatada and Muqatil said: A noble letter means: good, and this is the choice of Az-Zajjaj, who said: What is in it is good. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Noble, meaning: noble because of the nobility of its owner. It was said: She called it noble because it was initiated by In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
27:30: Then she explained who wrote the book and said: 30- It is from Solomon, and she explained what was written and said: And it is in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
27:31: 31- Do not be arrogant to me, Ibn Abbas said: meaning: Do not be haughty towards me. It was also said: Do not act arrogantly or haughtily towards me. Its meaning is: Do not refuse to answer, because not answering is a form of arrogance and magnification. And come to me in submission, believing and obedient. It was said: It is from Islam, and it was also said: It is from submission.
27:32: 32- “She said, ‘O assembly, advise me in my affair,’ advise me in what has been presented to me, and answer me in what I consult you about, ‘I am not going to decide,’ judge and decide, ‘a matter until you witness,’ meaning: be present.
27:33: 33- They said, in response to her: We are men of strength, in fighting, and men of great courage, in war. Muqatil said: By strength they meant large numbers, and by great courage bravery, and this is an exposure from them to fighting if she orders them to do so. Then they said: And the matter is up to you, O queen, in fighting and leaving it, so see, from the opinion, what you command, and you will find us obedient to your command.
27:34: 34- She said, Bilqis, responding to their threat to fight: When kings enter a town, by force, they corrupt it, they ruin it, and make the most honorable of its people humiliated, that is, they humiliate its nobles and leaders, so that things will be right for them. She warns them of Solomon’s march toward them and his entry into their country, and the report of it spread here, so God confirmed her words and said: And thus they do, that is, as she said, they do.
27:35: Then she said: 35- And I am sending to them a gift. A gift is a present given as a gesture of kindness. Bilqis was a clever woman who governed and managed, so she said to the leaders of her al-Nas 114:I am sending to them, meaning: to Solomon and his people, a gift to make him accept my kingdom and test him with it, is he a king or a prophet? If he is a king, he will accept the gift and leave, and if he is a prophet, he will not accept the gift and will not be satisfied with us unless we follow his religion. This is what God Almighty said: Then We will examine with what the messengers will return. So she presented him with female slaves, both male and female. Ibn Abbas said: She dressed them in one garment so that no male would be distinguished from female. Mujahid said: They dressed the boys in the clothing of female slaves and dressed the female slaves in the clothing of male slaves. They differed about their number. Ibn Abbas said: One hundred male servants and one hundred female servants. Mujahid and Muqatil said: Two hundred male servants and two hundred female servants. Qatada and Saeed bin Jubair said: I sent him a brick of gold in silk and brocade. Thabit Al-Banani said: She presented him with gold plates in brocade vessels. It was also said that they were four bricks of gold. Wahb and others said: Bilqis took five hundred young boys and five hundred young girls. She dressed the young boys in the clothing of young girls, and placed bracelets of gold on their arms, and necklaces of gold on their necks, and earrings and bracelets studded with various jewels in their ears. She dressed the young girls in the clothing of young boys, with cloaks and belts. She carried the young girls on five hundred camels, and the young boys on five hundred mules. On each horse was a bridle of gold studded with jewels, and their ornaments were of colored brocade. She sent him five hundred bricks of gold and five hundred bricks of silver, and a crown crowned with pearls and high rubies. She sent him musk, ambergris, and aloes wood. She took a bag and placed in it a precious pearl without a hole and a perforated agate bead with a crooked hole. She called a man from the nobles of her people called Al-Mundhir ibn Amr, and she brought to him men from her people who were men of opinion. And she became wise, and wrote with him a book in the copy of the gift, and said in it: If you are a prophet, then distinguish between the female and male servants, and tell what is in the bag before you open it, and pierce the pearl with a straight hole, and insert a thread into the pierced bead without treatment from man or jinn. Bilqis ordered the boys, saying: When Solomon speaks to you, speak to him in feminine and effeminate language, similar to the language of women. She ordered the slave girls to speak to him in harsh language, similar to the language of men. Then she said to the Messenger: Look at the man when you enter upon him. If he looks at you with an angry look, then know that he is a king and do not be frightened by his appearance, for I am more honorable than him. If you see the man cheerful and gentle, then know that he is a prophet sent by God. Understand his words and return the answer. So the messenger set off with the gifts, and the hoopoe came quickly to Solomon and told him the whole story. So Solomon ordered the jinn to strike bricks of gold and bricks of silver, and they did. Then he ordered them to spread out from the place where he was, to a distance of nine farsakhs, a single field of bricks of gold and silver, and to make a wall around the field, the tops of which would be of gold and silver. Then he said: What animals are more beautiful than what you have seen on land and sea? They said: O Prophet of God, we saw such and such animals in the sea, spotted with different colors, with wings, crests, and forelocks. He said: Bring them to me immediately. So they brought them. He said: Tie them to the right and left of the battlefield on bricks of gold and silver, and throw their fodder into them. Then he said to the jinn: Bring your children. A large number of people gathered, and he made them stand on the right and left of the battlefield. Then Solomon sat in his seat on his throne, and placed for him four thousand chairs on his right and the same on his left. Then Solomon sat in his seat on his throne, and placed for him four thousand chairs on his right and the same on his left. He ordered the devils to stand in rows of leagues, and he ordered the humans to stand in rows of leagues, and he ordered the wild beasts, predators, insects, and birds to stand in rows of leagues on his right and left. When the people approached the field and looked at Solomon's kingdom and saw animals the likes of which their eyes had never seen frothing on the bricks of gold and silver, their spirits shortened and they threw away the gifts they had with them. In some accounts, when Solomon ordered the field to be paved with bricks of gold and silver, he ordered them to leave a place on their way the size of the bricks they had with them. When the messengers saw the place of the bricks empty and the whole ground paved, they feared that they would be accused of that, so they threw away what they had with them in that place. When they saw the devils, they saw a strange sight and were startled. The devils said to them: Pass on, there is no harm to you. They passed by groups after groups of jinn, humans, birds, vermin, beasts and wild animals, until they stopped before Solomon. Solomon looked at them with a pleasant face and said: What is behind you? The chief of the people told him what they had come for and was given the queen's letter. He looked at it and then said: Where is the truth? So he brought it and moved it, and Gabriel came and told him what was in the bag. He said: In it is a precious pearl without a hole, and a perforated agate with a crooked hole. The Messenger said: You have spoken the truth. So he pierced the pearl and put the thread through the bead. Solomon said: Who will pierce it for me? So Solomon asked the humans and then the jinn, but they had no knowledge of that. Then he asked the devils, and they said: We will send for the termite. So the termite came and took a hair in its mouth and entered it until it came out the other side. Solomon said to it: What do you need? It said: My provision will be in the tree. So he said that to you. It was narrated that a worm that lived in the willow came and said: I will put the thread through the hole so that my livelihood will be in the willow. So that was done for it. It took the thread in its mouth and entered the hole and came out the other side. Then he said: Who will have this bead and thread it through the thread? A white worm said: I will do it, O Messenger of God. So the worm took the thread in its mouth and entered the hole until it came out the other side. Solomon said: What do you need? It said: I will make my provision in fruits. He said: That is for you. Then he distinguished between the slave girls and the boys by ordering them to wash their faces and hands. The slave girl would take water from the vessel with one hand, then put it on the other hand and then strike her face with it, and the boy would take water from the vessel and strike his face with it. The slave girl would pour water on the inside of her forearm, and the boy on the back of his forearm. The slave girl would pour water, and the boy would pour water over his hands, so he distinguished between them with that.
27:36: Then Solomon returned the gift, as God Almighty said: 36- And when Solomon came, he said, ‘Do you provide me with wealth?’ Hamza and Ya’qub read: Do you provide me with wealth? with one doubled nun and the addition of the yaa. The others read: with two light nuns. The people of Hijaz and Basra confirm the yaa, while the others delete it. But what God has given me, God gave me of prophethood, religion, wisdom, and kingship, is better than what He has given you. Rather, you rejoice in your gift, because you are people who boast about the world and compete with it. You rejoice in giving gifts to one another. As for me, I do not rejoice in it, and the world is not among my needs, because God Almighty has empowered me in it and given me from it what He has not given to anyone else. Despite that, He has honored me with religion and prophethood.
27:37: Then he said to Al-Mundhir bin Amr, the leader of the delegation: 37- Return to them, with the gift, for We will come to them with soldiers they cannot resist, they cannot bear, and We will expel them from it, that is, from their land and country, which is Sheba, humiliated and they will be subdued, humiliated if they do not come to Me as Muslims. Wahb and others of the People of the Book said: When the messengers of Bilqis returned to her from Solomon, she said: I know - by God - that this is not a kingdom and we are not able to do it. So she sent to Solomon: I am coming to you with the kings of my people so that I may see what you command and what you call for in your religion. Then she ordered her throne to be placed in the last of seven houses, one inside the other, in the last of her seven palaces. Then she closed the doors to it and appointed guards to guard it. Then she said to those she left in charge of her sultanate: Keep what is before you and my royal throne, so that no one may reach it or see it until I come to you. Then she ordered a crier to call out to the people of her kingdom, informing them of the departure. She went to Solomon with twelve thousand Qayl of the kings of Yemen, under the command of each Qayl were many thousands. Ibn Abbas said: “Solomon was an awe-inspiring man who would never initiate anything until he was the one asked about it. One day, he went out and sat on his royal throne. He saw a noise close to him, so he said, ‘What is this?’ They said, ‘Bilqis has come to this place from us.’ It was a farsakh away from Solomon.” Ibn Abbas said: There was a distance of a farsakh between Kufa and Al-Hirah, so Solomon then turned to his soldiers.
27:38: 38- He said, ‘O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?’ That is, as believers. Ibn Abbas said, obediently. They differed about the reason why Solomon ordered her throne to be brought. Most of them said: Because Solomon knew that if she converted to Islam, her money would be forbidden to him, so he wanted to take her bed before it was forbidden to him to take it because of her conversion to Islam. It was said: To show her the power of God Almighty and the greatness of His authority in a miracle that He will perform on her throne. Qatada said: Because he liked his description of the hoopoe, so he wanted to see him. Ibn Zayd said: He wanted to order it to be made indefinite and changed to test her intelligence.
27:39: 39- An ‘Ifrit from among the jinn said, meaning the strong ogre. Wahb said: His name is Kudhi, and it was said: Dhakwan. Ibn Abbas said: The ‘Ifrit is the cunning one. Ad-Dahhak said: He is the wicked one. Ar-Rabi’ said: He is the thick one. Al-Farra’ said: He is the strong and powerful one. It was said: He is the rock of the jinn, and it was like a mountain where he places his foot at the end of its horizon. I will bring it to you before you rise from your seat, meaning: from the seat in which you decide. Ibn Abbas said: And he had a seat every morning in which he would decide until the end of the day. And I am for it, meaning: for carrying it, strong and trustworthy, despite the jewels in it. Solomon said: I want something faster than this.
27:40: F40- He who had knowledge from the Book said, and they differed about it. Some of them said: He is Gabriel. It was said: He is an angel from the angels with whom God supported His Prophet Solomon, peace be upon him. Most commentators said: He is Asif bin Barkhiya, and he was a truthful person who knew the greatest name of God, which if he is called by it, he answers, and if he is asked by it, he gives. Juwaybir and Muqatil narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Asif said to Solomon when he was praying: Extend your eyes until you can see the end of your vision. So Solomon extended his eyes and looked to the right, and called upon Asif. Then God sent the angels who carried the bed from under the ground, taking it one by one until the ground was torn open with the bed in front of Solomon. Al-Kalbi said: Asaf fell down in prostration and called upon the Greatest Name of God, and her throne disappeared beneath the earth until it sprang up near Solomon’s throne. It was also said that the distance was the length of two months. They differed regarding the supplication that Asif made. Mujahid and Muqatil said: O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Al-Kalbi said: O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining. This was narrated on the authority of Aisha. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: The supplication of the one who has knowledge from the Book: “O our God and the God of all things, One God, there is no god but You. Bring me her throne.” Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: It was Solomon. A scholar from the Children of Israel, to whom God had given knowledge and understanding, said to him: I will bring it to you before you blink. Solomon said: Bring it. He said: “You are the Prophet, the son of the Prophet, and no one is more respected by God than you. If you call upon God and ask of Him, He will be with you.” He said: You have spoken the truth. So he did that, and the throne was brought at that time. God the Almighty says: {Before your glance returns to you} Saeed bin Jubair said: It means: Before the furthest thing you see returns to you, which is that someone from you within the reach of your sight reaches you. Qatadah said: Before a person comes to you from the reach of the sight. Mujahid said: It means continuing to look until your glance returns defeated. Wahb said: You stretch your eyes, but your glance does not reach its limit, until I present it before you. {And when he saw it} meaning: Solomon saw the throne, {placed near him}, carried to him from Ma'rib to Syria in the amount of time a glance returns, {He said, This is from the bounty of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful for His blessing, {or ungrateful" for it. {And whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself} meaning: the benefit of his gratitude returns to him, which is that he deserves the completion and continuity of the blessing, because gratitude is the condition of an existing blessing and the catch of a lost blessing. {And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need}, without gratitude, {Generous}, in bestowing favors upon those who are ungrateful for His blessings.
27:41: God Almighty says: 41- He said, ‘Disguise her throne for her.’ He says: Change her bed to a state that she would not recognize when she saw it. Qatada and Muqatil said: It means adding to it and subtracting from it. It was narrated that he made its bottom its top and its top its bottom, and made the place of the red jewel green and the green red. We will see whether she will be guided, to her throne so that she recognizes it, or whether she will be among the ignorant, those who are not guided, to it. And what prompted Solomon to do that, as mentioned by Wahb, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, and others, is that the devils feared that Solomon would marry her and thus divulge to him the secrets of the jinn, and that was because her mother was a jinn, and if she bore him a son, they would not cease from subjecting Solomon and his descendants after him, so they spoke ill of her to make him lose interest in her, and they said: There is something wrong with her mind and her foot is like a donkey’s hoof and her legs are hairy. So Solomon wanted to test her mind by disguising her throne and looking at her feet by building a tower.
27:42: 42- So when she came, it was said, ‘Is this your throne?’ She said, ‘It is as if it is the same.’ Muqatil said: She recognized it, but she mistook it for them, just as they mistook it for her. Ikrimah said: She was wise and did not say, ‘Yes,’ for fear of being lied to, nor did she say, ‘No,’ for fear of being disbelieved. She said, ‘It is as if it is the same.’ So Solomon recognized the perfection of her intelligence, since she neither acknowledged nor denied it. It was said that she was confused about the throne because she had left it in a house behind seven closed doors and she had the keys with her. She was told: It is your throne, so closing the doors did not help you. So he said: And we were given knowledge, of the truth of Solomon’s prophethood through the previous verses about the gift and the messengers, before it, before the verse about the throne, and we were Muslims, obedient and submissive to Solomon’s command. It was said that his saying: And we were given knowledge before her was said by Sulayman, meaning: And we were given knowledge of God and His ability to do whatever He wills before this woman, and we were Muslims. This is the saying of Mujahid. It was said: Its meaning is that we were given knowledge of her Islam and her coming willingly before her coming, and we were Muslims, obedient to God Almighty.
27:43: God Almighty said: 43- And what she used to worship besides God prevented her, meaning: what she used to worship besides God, which was the sun, prevented her from worshipping God, meaning: the worship of the sun prevented her from monotheism and the worship of God. So according to this interpretation, what is in the nominative case. It was said: Its meaning is that it prevented her from worshipping God, not that her mind was defective, as the jinn said: There was something wrong with her mind, but she was worshipping other than God. It was said: Its meaning is that Solomon prevented her from what she used to worship other than God, meaning: He prevented her from that and stood between her and him, so the place of what is in the accusative case. She was from a disbelieving people. This is a resumption. God Almighty informed us that she was from a people who worshipped the sun, and she grew up among them and knew nothing but sun worship.
27:44: God Almighty says: 44- It was said to her, ‘Enter the palace’ [the verse]. This is because Solomon wanted to look at her feet and legs without asking her to uncover them, when the devils said: Her feet are like a donkey’s hooves, and they are hairy legs. He ordered the devils to build him a palace, meaning a palace of glass. It was also said that it was a house of glass, white as water. It was also said that the palace was the courtyard of the house, and he made water flow beneath it and threw into it all kinds of sea creatures, fish, frogs, and others. Then he placed his bed on its front and sat on it, and the birds, jinn, and humans clung to it. It was also said that he made a plate of glass and placed statues of whales and frogs beneath it, so that when someone saw it, he would think it was water. It was said: He built the palace to test her understanding, as she did with the male and female servants. When he sat on the bed, he called Bilqis, and when she came, she was told to enter the palace. And when she saw it, she thought it was a sea, meaning most of the water, and she uncovered her shins, to wade into it to Solomon. Solomon looked and saw that she was the most beautiful of people in feet and legs, except that her legs were hairy. When Solomon saw that, he turned his gaze away from her and called to her, He said, ‘Indeed, it is a smooth, level palace,’ smooth and level, of glass, and not water. Then Solomon called her to Islam, and she had seen the state of the throne and the palace, so she responded, and said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself,’ by disbelief. Muqatil said: When she saw the throne and the palace, she knew that Solomon’s kingdom was from God, so she said, My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself by worshipping other than You, “and I submit with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds, meaning: she devoted herself to monotheism for Him. It was said: When she reached the tower and thought it was a sea, she said to herself: Solomon wants to drown me, and killing me would be easier for me than this. So her saying: I have wronged myself means that thought. They differed about her affair after her conversion to Islam. Awn ibn Abdullah said: A man asked Abdullah ibn Utbah: Did Solomon marry her? He said: Her affair ended with her saying: I have submitted with Solomon to God, Lord of the Worlds, meaning: We have no knowledge beyond that. Some of them said: He married her, and when he wanted to marry her, he hated what he saw of the hair on her legs, so he asked the al-Nas 114:What removes this? They said: The razor. The woman said: No iron has ever touched me. So Solomon hated the razor and said: It cuts her legs. He asked the jinn and they said: We do not know. Then he asked the devils and they said: We will find a trick for you so that you will be like white silver. So they made lime and baths, and the lime and baths remained from that day on. When Solomon married her, he loved her intensely and confirmed her in her kingdom. He ordered the jinn to build for her in the land of Yemen three fortresses that people had never seen the likes of in height and beauty, and they are: Salhin, Baynun, and Umdan. Then Solomon used to visit her once every month after he had returned her to her kingdom and would stay with her for three days, travelling from Syria to Yemen, and from Yemen to Syria. She gave birth to a child for him, as mentioned. It was narrated on the authority of Wahb, who said: They claimed that when Bilqis converted to Islam, Solomon said to her: Choose a man from your people so that I may marry you to him. She said: And someone like me, O Prophet of God, marries men while I had the kingdom and authority among my people? He said: Yes, there is nothing else in Islam except that, and you should not forbid what God has made lawful for you. She said: If that is not possible, marry me to Dhu Tubba, king of Hamadan. So he married her to him, then he returned her to Yemen, and he gave her husband Dhu Tubba’ power over Yemen, and called for Zuba’ah, the prince of the jinn of Yemen, and said: Do for Dhu Tubba what he has appointed you to do. So he remained its king, doing for him whatever he wanted there until Solomon died. When a year had passed and the jinn realized Solomon’s death, a man from among them came and went through Tihamah until he was in the heart of Yemen. He cried out at the top of his voice: O company of jinn, King Solomon has died, so raise your hands. So they raised their hands and dispersed, and the kingdom of Dhu Tubba’ came to an end, and the kingdom of Bilqis with the kingdom of Solomon. It was said that the kingdom reached Solomon when he was thirteen years old and he died when he was fifty-three years old.
27:45: God Almighty says: 45- And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, saying, that is, worship God, alone, and at once they were two parties, believers and disbelievers, disputing, about religion. Muqatil said: Their dispute is what was mentioned in Surat al-A’raf 7:The eminent among his people who were arrogant said to those who had been oppressed among them, to those who believed, until His saying: O Salih, bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the messengers Al-A’raf 75-77.
27:46: F46- He said, to them, Salih, O my people, why do you hasten the evil, the affliction and punishment, before the good, the well-being and mercy, why do you not seek forgiveness from God, by repenting from your disbelief, that you may receive mercy.
27:47: 47- “They said, ‘We have bad omens,’ meaning: we have a bad omen. The root is ‘we have bad omens,’ ‘for you and for those with you.’ It was said that they said that to split their word. It was also said that the rain was withheld from them at that time and they suffered a drought, so they said: This hardship and distress has befallen us because of your bad luck and the bad luck of your companions. He said, ‘Your bad omen is with God.’” Meaning: Whatever good or evil befalls you is with God by His command, and it is written for you. It was called a bad omen because of the speed with which it descends upon a person, for nothing is faster than an inevitable fate. Ibn Abbas said: The bad omen came to you from God because of your disbelief. It was said: Your bird, meaning: your work with God. It was called a bird because of the speed of its ascent to the sky. Rather, you are a people who are tested. Ibn Abbas said: You are tested with good and evil, similar to the Almighty’s saying: And We test you with evil and good as trial (Al-Anbiya’: 35). Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi said: You are tormented.
27:48: God Almighty said: 48- And there were in the city meaning: the city of Thamud, which is Al-Hijr, nine men, from among their nobles, who spread corruption in the land and did not reform, and they were the ones who agreed to hamstring the she-camel, and they were the seducers of the people of Salih, and their leader was Qadar bin Salif, and he was the one who took charge of hamstringing it, and they were committing sins.
27:49: They said: 49- They swore by God, they made an alliance, some of them said to each other: meaning: swear by God, O people. The position of the word they swore is in the jussive mood, and some people said: its location is in the accusative case as a past tense verb, meaning: that they made an alliance and pledged, its meaning is: they said, swearing by God, that we will kill him by night, meaning: we will kill him by night, and his family, meaning: and his people who converted to Islam with him. Al-A'mash, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read that you will kill him by night and that you will say with a ta' in both of them and a damma on the lam of the verb as a direct address, and the others read it with a nun in both of them and a fatha on the lam of the verb, then we will say to his heir, meaning: the heir of his blood, we did not witness, we did not attend, the destruction of his family, meaning: their destruction, and we do not know who killed him, and whoever opens the meem means the destruction of his family, and we are truthful, in our saying that we did not witness that.
27:50: 50- And they planned a plan, they committed a treachery when they intended to attack Salih by night and kill him, and We planned a plan, We rewarded them for their plan by hastening their punishment, while they did not perceive.
27:51: 51- Then see how was the consequence of their plotting, I. The people of Kufa read I with a fat-ha on the alif in response to the consequence, meaning: the consequence was that we destroyed them. The others read: We with a kasra as a resumption, We destroyed them, meaning: We destroyed the nine of them. They differed about the manner of their destruction. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: God sent angels that night to the house of Salih to guard him. The nine came to the house of Salih brandishing their swords. The angels pelted them with stones from where they could see the stones but not the angels, killing them. Muqatil said: They camped on the slope of a mountain, looking out for one another to reach the house of Salih, but the mountain collapsed on them and destroyed them. And their people, all of them, God destroyed them with the shout.
27:52: 52- “Then those are their houses, empty,” accusative of state, meaning: empty, because of what they did wrong, meaning: because of their wrongdoing and disbelief. Indeed in that is a sign, for a lesson, for a people who know, our power.
27:53: 53- And We saved those who believed and were righteous. It is said that the survivors among them were four thousand.
27:54: God Almighty said: 54- And Lot, when he said to his people, ‘Do you commit immorality while you see?’ meaning, you know that it is immoral. It was also said that its meaning is that you see one another, but they do not conceal it out of their transgression.
27:55: 55- Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? Rather, you are a people behaving ignorantly.
27:56: 56- “And the only answer of his people was that they said, ‘Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who purify themselves.’”
27:57: 57- “So We saved him and his family, except for his wife. We decreed her to be among those who remained behind,” meaning: those who remained in the punishment.
27:58: 58- And We rained down upon them a rain, which is stones, so wretched, so wretched, the rain of those who were warned.
27:59: God Almighty says: 59- Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ This is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanding him to praise God for the destruction of the disbelievers of past nations. It was also said: for all of His blessings. “And peace be upon His chosen servants.” Muqatil said: They are the prophets and messengers. The evidence for this is God Almighty’s saying: “And peace be upon the messengers.” Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Abu Malik: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Kalbi said: They are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: They are all believers, past and present. Is God better than what they associate? The people of Basra and Asim read associating with a ya', while the others read it with a ta'. He is addressing the people of Mecca, and it imposes the argument on the polytheists after the destruction of the unbelievers. He says: Is God better for those who worship Him, or are idols better for those who worship them? The meaning is: God saves those who worship Him from destruction, and idols are of no avail to their worshippers when the punishment descends.
27:60: 60- "Is He who created the heavens and the earth? meaning, are your gods better, or He who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down for you water from the sky, meaning rain, and caused to grow thereby gardens"? Orchards is the plural of garden. Al-Farra' said: A garden is a surrounded orchard, so if there is no wall around it, then it is not a garden. "Of delight," meaning, a beautiful view, and delight is the beauty that delights those who see it. "It was not for you to cause its trees to grow," meaning, it is not appropriate for you, because you are not able to do it. "Is there a god with God?" is a question of denial, meaning: Is there a god with Him other than Him who helped Him create it? Rather, there is no god with Him. "Rather, they are a people, meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, who are equal, who associate others with Him.
27:61: 61- Is He who made the earth a resting place, that does not shake with its people, and placed within it, in the middle of it, rivers, that carry water, and placed for it firm mountains, fixed mountains, and placed between the two seas, the fresh and the salty, a barrier, preventing one from mixing with the other, Is there a god with God? But most of them do not know, the oneness of his Lord and His authority.
27:62: 62- Is there one who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him and removes the evil and makes you successors on the earth? Its inhabitants He destroys one generation and creates another. It was also said: He makes your children your successors. It was also said: He made you successors of the jinn on the earth. Is there a deity with God? Little do you remember. Abu Amr read it with a ya’ and the others with a ta’.
27:63: 63- Who guides you in the darknesses of the land and sea, if you travel, and who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, meaning: before the rain, Is there a god with God? Exalted is God above what they associate with Him.
27:64: 64- Is He who begins creation and then repeats it, after death, and who provides for you from the sky and the earth, meaning: from the sky rain and from the earth vegetation. Is there a god with God? Say, Produce your proof, your argument for your claim that there is another god with God, if you should be truthful.
27:65: 65- Say, ‘None in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen except God.’ This verse was revealed about the polytheists when they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the time of the Hour, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.
27:66: 66- Rather, their knowledge has overtaken them. Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Umar read: adrak with the pattern af'al meaning: it reached and caught up, just as one says: My knowledge overtook him if it caught up with him and reached him. He means: what they were ignorant of in this world and the knowledge of which was lost to them, they will know in the Hereafter. Mujahid said: Their knowledge will overtake them in the Hereafter, and they will know it when they witness it when their knowledge will not benefit them. Muqatil said: Rather, they will know in the Hereafter when they witness it what they doubted and were blind to in this world, which is His statement: Rather, they are in doubt about it, meaning: they are today in doubt about the Hour. The others read: Rather, adarak connected and doubled with an alif after the doubled dal, meaning: their knowledge will be overtaken and continued in the Hereafter and will catch up. It was said: Its meaning is that they have gathered their knowledge that the Hereafter will occur, and they are in doubt about their time, so it has the same meaning as the first. It was said: It is in the form of a question, meaning: Will their knowledge of that be made up for and continued in the Hereafter? That is: It was not continuous and their knowledge of it was lost and was absent, so they did not reach it or comprehend it, because the question contains a type of denial that indicates it. Ibn Abbas read bala with the addition of the yaa and idrak with the opening of the alif for interrogation, meaning: he did not realize. In the letter abi “am” they realized their knowledge, and the Arabs put bal in place of am and am in place of bal. In short: God has informed us that when they are resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, their knowledge of the Hereafter and what they are promised in it of reward and punishment will be equal, even if their knowledge in this world is different. Ali bin Issa mentioned that the meaning of bal here is: If and its meaning is: If they had attained in this world what they will attain in the Hereafter, they would not have been satisfied. The Almighty said: Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, today they are in doubt about the Hour. Rather, they are blind to it. The plural of Amm is blind of heart. Al-Kalbi said: He means they are ignorant of it.
27:67: 67- And those who disbelieved said, meaning the polytheists of Mecca, When we have become dust and our fathers, will we indeed be brought forth? from our graves alive. The people of Medina read: When we are not questioning, “When we are” with the question. Ibn Amir and Al-Kisa’i read: When we are with two hamzas, When we are with two nuns. The others read it with the question.
27:68: 68- This has been promised to us, meaning: this resurrection, us and our fathers before, meaning: before Muhammad, and that is nothing. This, what is this, is nothing but legends of the ancients, their hadiths and lies that they wrote.
27:69: 69- Say, ‘Travel through the land and observe what was the end of the criminals.’
27:70: 70- And do not grieve over them, for their denial of you and their turning away from you, and do not be in distress over what they are plotting, revealed about the mockers who divided up the punishment of Mecca.
27:71: 71- And they say, ‘When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?’
27:72: 72- “Say: Perhaps it will be a follower of you,” meaning: it will come near and draw near, to you. It was also said: it will follow you, and the meaning is: it will follow you. The lam was inserted as it was inserted in His statement: They fear their Lord (al-A’raf 7:154). Al-Farra’ said: The lam is an additional conjunction, as you say: I saved him a hundred, and I saved for him some of what you are hastening, from the punishment, so that happened to them on the day of Badr.
27:73: 73- And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty to mankind, Muqatil said, to the people of Mecca, as He did not hasten the punishment upon them, “but most of them are not grateful, that is.
27:74: 74- And indeed, your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare.
27:75: 75- And there is nothing absent, meaning: nothing absent from a hidden secret, a concealed matter, or something absent, in the heavens or the earth except that it is in a clear book, meaning: in the Preserved Tablet.
27:76: 76- Indeed, this Qur’an relates to the Children of Israel, that is, it explains to them, most of that over which they differ, of matters of religion. Al-Kalbi said: The People of the Book differed among themselves and became parties attacking one another, so the Qur’an was revealed to explain what they differed over.
27:77: 77- And it, meaning the Qur’an, is a guidance and a mercy for the believers.
27:78: 78- Indeed, your Lord will judge, separate, between them, that is, between those who differ in religion on the Day of Resurrection, by His judgment, the truth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Invincible, so no command can be rejected. The Knowing, of their conditions, so nothing is hidden from Him.
27:79: 79- So put your trust in God, for you are upon the clear truth. Al-Bayn.
27:80: 80- Indeed, you do not make the dead hear, meaning the unbelievers, nor do you make the deaf hear the call. Ibn Kathir read: does not hear with a ya’ and a fatha on the meem, the deaf are nominative, and likewise in Surat Ar-Rum. The rest read it with a ta’ and a damma on the meem, the deaf are accusative. When they turn their backs, turning away. If it is said, what is the meaning of his saying: And they turned their backs, if they were deaf and could not hear, whether they turned their backs or not? It was said: He mentioned it for emphasis and exaggeration. It was said: If a deaf person is present, he may hear by raising his voice and understand by gestures, but if he turns away, he neither hears nor understands. Qatada said: If a deaf person turns away and you call him, he does not hear. Similarly, the unbeliever does not hear what he is called to of faith. The meaning of the verse is that, due to their extreme aversion to what they are called to, they are like a dead person who cannot be made to hear, or a deaf person who cannot hear.
27:81: 81- And you are not a guide to the blind. Al-A’mash and Hamzah read: tahdi with a ta’ and a fatha on the verb blind with a nasb on the ya’ here and in Ar-Rum. The others read bahadi with a ba’ on the noun, blind with a kasra on the ya’, from their misguidance, meaning: you are not a guide to those whom God has blinded from guidance and whose hearts have been blinded from faith. You do not hear, what you do not hear, except those who believe in Our verses, except those who believe in the Qur’an that it is from God, they are Muslims, sincere.
27:82: God Almighty said: 82- And when the word comes to pass against them, then the punishment is obligatory upon them. Qatada said: When God becomes angry with them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them, and they differed about its speech. Al-Suddi said: It will speak to them about the invalidity of religions other than the religion of Islam. Some of them said: Her speech is that she says to one person: This is a believer, and she says to another: This is an unbeliever. It was said that her words were like what God Almighty said: That people were not certain of Our signs. Muqatil said: Speak to them in Arabic and say: The people were not certain of Our signs. Tell the people that the people of Mecca did not believe in the Qur’an and the Resurrection. The people of Kufa read: that people with a fat-ha on the alif, meaning: that people, and the rest read it with a kasra as a new beginning, meaning: that people were not certain of Our signs before they came out. Ibn Omar said: This is when he does not command what is good and forbid what is evil. Saeed bin Jubair, Asim Al-Jahdari, and Abu Raja Al-Attardi read: talakalamhum with a fatha on the ta’ and a soft lam from the word kalam which means wound. Abu al-Juza' said: I asked Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, about this verse: Do you speak to them or do you speak to them? He said: "You do both. You speak to the believer and you speak to the unbeliever." Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Al-Ala bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hasten to do good deeds before six things happen: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the Antichrist, the beast of the earth, the fate of one of you, and the affairs of the general public.” Ismail bin Abdullah told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad Al Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Muhammad bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first of the signs to appear will be the rising of the sun from the west, and the emergence of the beast among the people at noon. Whichever of them comes first, the other will follow soon after it.” Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi informed us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi informed us, Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Ahmad bin Fanjuwayh informed us, Abu Bakr bin Kharjah informed us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Sulaiman Al-Hadrami informed us, Hisham bin Hammad informed us, Amr bin Muhammad Al-Abqari informed us, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umair Al-Laithi, on the authority of Abu Sariha Al-Ansari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The beast will have three outings in a lifetime. It will go out once in the farthest reaches of Yemen, and its fame will spread in the desert, but its fame will not enter the village, meaning Mecca. Then it will remain for a long time, then it will go out again near Mecca, and its fame will spread in the desert, but its fame will enter the village - meaning Mecca - and while the people were one day in the most sacred of mosques to God and the most honored by God Almighty - meaning the Sacred Mosque - they were not startled except by it being in a corner of the mosque, approaching and approaching. This is what Ibn Umar said. And between the Black Corner and the door of Banu Makhzum on the right of the one who goes out, in the middle of that, so the people turned away from it. A group of them stood before her and they knew that they could not defeat God. She came out upon them, shaking the dust from her head. She passed by them and disappeared from their faces until she left them like the shining stars. Then she turned on the earth, and no pursuer could catch her nor could any fugitive defeat her. So much so that a man would stand up and seek refuge from her by praying, but she would come to him from behind and say: So-and-so, are you praying now? He would turn his face to her and she would brand him on his face. People would pass by her in their homes, and they would accompany each other on their journeys and share wealth. The disbeliever would be known from the believer. The believer would be told: O believer, and the disbeliever would be told: O disbeliever.
