Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told me, Abu Bakr bin Malik Al-Qat’i told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Bahz told us, Hammad told us - he is Ibn Abi Salamah - Ali bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Aws bin Khalid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Beast will emerge with the staff of Moses and the ring of Solomon, and it will polish the face of the believer with the staff and smash the nose of the disbeliever with the ring, until the people of the table will gather and one of them will say, ‘O believer,’ and another will say, ‘O disbeliever.’” It was narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: It is not a beast with a tail, but without a beard, as if he was indicating that it is a man, but most of them are of the opinion that it is a beast. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr that he described the beast and said: Its head is the head of a bull, its eye the eye of a pig, its ear the ear of an elephant, its horn the horn of a deer, its chest the chest of a lion, its color the color of a leopard, its flank the flank of a cat, its tail the tail of a ram, its legs the legs of a camel, and between every two joints are twelve cubits. With it is the staff of Moses and the ring of Solomon. Not a believer will remain but that it will prick his face in his mosque with the staff of Moses, a white prick, and his face will shine. Not a disbeliever will remain but that it will prick his face with the ring of Solomon, and his face will blacken, to the point that people will trade in the marketplace: How much, O believer? How much, O disbeliever? Then the beast will say to him: O so-and-so, you are from the people of Paradise, and O so-and-so, you are from the people of Hell. This is what God Almighty said: And when the word comes to pass against them, We will bring out for them a creature from the earth (al-Baqarah 2:17). Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Aqil bin Muhammad Al-Jurjani the jurist told me, Abu Al-Faraj Al-Ma’afa bin Zakariya Al-Baghdadi told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Jarir Al-Tabari told us, Abu Kurayb told us, Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzuq, on the authority of Atiyya, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Beast will emerge from a crack in Al-Safa like a horse galloping for three days, and a third of it will not emerge. And on his authority, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, he said: Issam ibn Dawud ibn al-Jarrah told me, my father told us, Sufyan ibn Saeed told us, Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of Rib'i ibn Harash, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the Beast. I said: O Messenger of God, from where will it emerge? He said: From the most sacred mosques before God, while Jesus is circumambulating the Ka'bah with the Muslims with him, the earth beneath them will strike, and the Safa will split from the direction of al-Mash'ar, and the Beast will emerge from the Safa, its head first appearing, polished, with fur and feathers. No seeker will catch up with it, and no fugitive will escape it. It will name people ‘believer’ and ‘disbeliever’. As for the believer, it will leave his face like a shining star, and it will write between his eyes ‘believer’. As for the disbeliever, it will make a black dot between his eyes, and it will write between his eyes ‘disbeliever’.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he struck Al-Safa with his staff while he was in a state of ihram, and said: The beast can hear the striking of my staff. On the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: The beast will emerge from a ravine, its head touching the clouds, and its feet on the ground as long as they are not out. It will pass by a person praying and will say: What is prayer for you? So it will snatch his head from the ground. On the authority of Ibn Omar, he said: The beast will come out on the night of Jumu’ah, while the people are walking to Mina. On the authority of Suhayl ibn Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The worst valley is the valley of Ajyad, two or three times. It was said: Why is that, O Messenger of God? He said: A beast will emerge from it and scream three times that will be heard from both sides of the world. Wahb said: Her face is the face of a man, and her creation is like that of a bird. She tells whoever sees her that the people of Mecca were not certain of Muhammad and the Qur’an.
27:83: God Almighty says: 83- And the Day We shall gather from every nation a company, meaning: from every century a group, of those who deny Our signs, and the from here is not for partiality, because all of the deniers will be gathered, and they will be distributed, the first of them will be detained over the last of them until they are gathered together, then they will be driven to the Fire.
27:84: 84- Until, when they come, on the Day of Resurrection, God will say, to them: Did you deny My signs while you did not encompass them in knowledge, and did not truly know them, What were you doing? when you did not think about them? The meaning of the verse is: Did you deny My signs without knowing them, and did not think about their authenticity, but rather you denied them out of ignorance?
27:85: 85- And the word has come to pass, the punishment has become obligatory, upon them for what they did wrong, for what they associated with God, so they will not speak. Qatada said: How can they speak when they have no argument? Similar to the words of God Almighty: This is a Day when they will not speak * Nor will they be permitted to make excuses. It was said: They will not speak because their mouths are sealed.
27:86: God Almighty says: 85- Have they not seen that We have made the night for them to rest in and the day to see? “Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.” They believe and take heed.
27:87: God Almighty says: 87- And the Day the Trumpet is blown, then whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified. The Trumpet is a horn that Israfil will blow into. Al-Hasan said: The Trumpet is the horn. Some of them initially said that the souls are gathered into the horn, then it is blown into, and the souls go to the bodies, and the bodies come to life. And His statement: Then whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, means: they will be struck dead, as He said in another verse: Then whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be struck dead (al-Zumar 39:68), meaning: they will die, and the meaning is that fear will be cast upon them until they die. It was said: Israfil will blow the trumpet three times: the blast of terror, the blast of unconsciousness, and the blast of rising before the Lord of the Worlds. His saying, Except whom God wills. They differed regarding this exception. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel about his saying, ‘Except whom God wills.’ He said, ‘They are the martyrs, wearing their swords around the Throne.’” Saeed bin Jubair and Ata’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are the martyrs because they are alive with their Lord and fear cannot reach them. In some narrations: The martyrs are the chosen ones of God Almighty, meaning: those whom God Almighty has excluded. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: He means Gabriel, Michael, then the spirit of Israfil, then the spirit of the Angel of Death, then the spirit of Gabriel, and the last of them to die will be Gabriel, peace be upon him. It is narrated that God the Almighty says to the Angel of Death: Take the soul of Israfil. Then he says: Who remains, O Angel of Death? He says: Glory be to You, my Lord, blessed and exalted are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor. Gabriel, Michael, and the Angel of Death remain. He says: Take the soul of Michael. He takes his breath and falls down like a great mountain. He says: Die, O Angel of Death. He dies and Gabriel says: Who remains? He says: Blessed and exalted are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor. Your face is everlasting and eternal, and Gabriel is the dead, mortal. He says: Gabriel, you must die. He falls down in prostration, flapping his wings. It is narrated that the superiority of His creation over the superiority of Michael is like a great mountain over a mountain of birds. It is narrated that he remains with these four bearers of the Throne, and he takes the souls of Gabriel and Michael, then the souls of the bearers of the Throne, then the soul of Israfil, then the soul of the Angel of Death. Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharqi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abdullah al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah ibn Ali al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kashmihani told us, Ali ibn Hajar told us, Ismail ibn Ja`far told us, Muhammad ibn `Amr ibn `Alqamah told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Trumpet will be blown and everyone in the heavens and the earth will be stunned except whom God wills. Then it will be blown again and I will be the first to raise his head. Then I will see Moses taking hold of one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he was among those whom God, the Almighty, excepted or whether he raised his head before me? And whoever says I am better than Jonah, son of Matta, has lied.” Ad-Dahhak said: They are satisfied, and the Houris, and Malik, and the Zabaniya. And it was said: The scorpions of Hell and its snakes. The Almighty said: And all, meaning: those who were brought back to life after death, came to Him. A’mash, Hamza, and Hafs read: came to Him, shortened by opening the ta’ on the verb, meaning: they came to Him. The others read it with a long vowel and a damma on the ta’, like the Almighty’s saying: And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone Maryam 19:95, humiliated, subdued.
27:88: The Almighty said 88- And you will see the mountains, you think them rigid, standing, while they will pass as the clouds pass, meaning: they will move as the clouds move until they fall to the ground, and they will be level with it. This is because everything great and every large gathering is beyond the sight due to its great number and the distance between its edges, so it is considered by the observer to be standing while it is moving. Likewise, the movement of the mountains will not be seen on the Day of Resurrection due to its greatness, just as the movement of the clouds will not be seen due to its greatness while it is moving. The creation of God is in the accusative case as a source, Who perfected all things, meaning: He is most wise. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do. Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read it with the letter ya, and the rest read it with the letter ta.
27:89: 89- Whoever brings a good deed, with the word of sincerity, which is the testimony that there is no god but God. Abu Ma’shar said: Ibrahim used to swear and did not make an exception: that the good deed is there is no god but God. Qatada said: with sincerity. And it was said: it is every act of obedience, he will have better than it, Ibn Abbas said: from it good will reach him, meaning: from that good deed he will have better than the Day of Resurrection, which is the reward and safety from punishment. As for him having anything better than faith, no, because there is nothing better than his saying there is no god but God. It was said: He will have better than that, meaning: the pleasure of God. God the Almighty said: And the pleasure of God is greater (al-Tawbah 9:72). Muhammad bin Ka’b and Abd al-Rahman bin Zayd said: He will have better than that, meaning: multiples. God the Almighty gave him ten or more for one. This is good because multiples have characteristics, including: that the servant will be asked about his work and will not be asked about multiples, and that Satan has a way to his work and has no way to multiples, and the opponents have no hope of multiples, and because the good deed is according to the servant’s merit and the multiplication is as befits the generosity of the Lord, the Blessed and Exalted. And they will be safe from the terror of that Day. The people of Kufa read: from the terror of that Day with the tanween yawmidhi and the fatha on the mim. The others read it with the addition because it is more general, as it implies safety from all the terrors of that Day. With the tanween, it is as if it is a terror without a terror. The people of Medina open the mim from yu’idh.
27:90: 90- And whoever brings evil, meaning polytheism, their faces will be thrown into the Fire, meaning they will be thrown on their faces. It is said: I threw a man on his face, meaning you threw him on his face, so he fell down and prostrated. And the guards of Hell will say to them: Are you recompensed except for what you used to do? in this world of polytheism.
27:91: God Almighty says 91- I have only been commanded, God says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say, I have only been commanded, “to worship the Lord of this city, meaning Mecca, who has made it sacred, God made it a safe sanctuary, in which no blood shall be shed, no one shall be wronged, its game shall not be hunted, and its solitude shall not be violated, and to Him belongs all things, creation and dominion, and I have been commanded to be of the Muslims, to God.
27:92: 92- And that I recite the Qur’an, meaning: I was commanded to recite the Qur’an, and whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself, meaning: the benefit of his guidance will return to him, and whoever goes astray, from faith and strays from the path of guidance, say, ‘I am only of the warners,’ of those who are frightened, so I have no duty except to convey [the message]. This was abrogated by the verse on fighting.
27:93: 93- “And say, ‘Praise be to God,’ for His blessings. ‘He will show you His signs,’ meaning the day of Badr, of killing, captivity, and the angels striking their faces and backs. Similar to what God Almighty said: ‘I will show you My signs, so do not be impatient.’” (Al-Anbiya’: 37). Mujahid said: He will show you His signs in the heavens and the earth and in yourselves, just as He said: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves. (Fussilat 41:53). So you will recognize them, meaning the signs and evidence. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do, and He promised them reward for their deeds.
28:1: Meccan, except for the words of God Almighty: Those to whom We gave the Scripture, to His words: We do not seek the ignorant, and in it is a verse that was revealed between Mecca and Medina, which is the words of God Almighty: Indeed, He who imposed the Qur’an upon you will return you to a place of return. Ta-Mim.
28:2: 2- These are the verses of the clear Book.
28:3: 3- We recite to you, [O Muhammad], from the report of Moses and Pharaoh in truth, in truth, for a people who believe, who believe in the Qur’an.
28:4: 4- Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself, he was arrogant, haughty, and haughty, in the land, the land of Egypt, and made its people into factions, groups and classes in service and subjugation, oppressing a party of them, meaning by party: the Children of Israel. Then He explained the oppression by saying: slaughtering their sons and keeping their women alive. He called this oppression because they were unable and weak to repel him from themselves, indeed, he was of the corrupters.
28:5: 5- And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land, meaning: the Children of Israel, and make them leaders, leaders in goodness to be emulated. Qatada said: governors and kings, his evidence is the Almighty’s statement: and made you kings, Mujahid said: callers to goodness. and make them heirs, meaning: the possessions of Pharaoh and his people, who would succeed them in their dwellings.
28:6: 6- And We will establish them in the land, We will settle them in the land of Egypt and Syria, and We will make it a place for them to settle in, And We will show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers, Al-A'mash, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read: and He will see with the letter ya and its fathah, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers, in the nominative cases, as the verb is for them. The others read it with the letter noon and its damma, and the letter ra with the kasrah, and the letter ya after it is the accusative case, as the verb falls upon it, from them that which they were wary of, and wariness is avoiding harm, and that is because they were informed that their destruction would be at the hands of a man from the Children of Israel, so they were afraid of him, so God showed them that which they were wary of.
28:7: 7- And We inspired the mother of Moses. This is an inspirational revelation, not a prophetic revelation. Qatada said: We cast into her heart, and the mother of Moses was Johabddint Levi, son of Jacob, to nurse him. They differed regarding the duration of breastfeeding. Some say it was eight months, and some say it was four months. It was said: For three months she was breastfeeding him in her lap, and he was crying and not moving. Then when you fear for him, meaning: of being slaughtered, cast him into the river, and the river is the sea, and here he meant the Nile, and do not fear, it was said: do not fear for him from drowning, and it was said: from a hyena, and do not grieve, over his separation, Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers, Ata’ narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When the Children of Israel increased in number in Egypt, they oppressed the people, committed sins, did not enjoin what is right and did not forbid what is wrong, so God empowered the Copts over them, and they weakened them until God saved them through the hands of His Prophet. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: When the time for Moses' mother to give birth approached, she was one of the midwives whom Pharaoh had appointed to treat the children of Israel's pregnancies, and she was close to Moses' mother. When the labor pains struck, she sent for her and said, What has befallen me has befallen me, so let your love for me today benefit me. So she treated her midwife, and when Moses fell to the ground, a light between his eyes astounded her, and every joint in her trembled, and the love of Moses entered her heart. Then she said to her, "O man, I did not come to you when you called me except to heal the killing of your newborn, but I have found for your son a love like no other love, so protect your son, for I see that he is our enemy." When the midwife left her, some spies saw her, so they came to her door to enter upon Moses' mother. His sister said, O mother, there are guards at the door. So she wrapped Moses in a rag and placed him in the oven while it was burning. Her mind was lost, and she did not understand what she was doing. He said: So they entered and found the oven lit, and they saw that Moses' mother had not changed color and no milk had appeared from her. They said to her: What brought the midwife to you? She said: She is a guest for me. So she came to visit me. Then they left her and her mind came back to her, and she said to Moses' sister: Where is the baby? She said: I do not know. Then she heard the baby crying from the oven, so she went to him, and God, the Most High, had made the fire cool and safe for him, so she carried him. He said: Then when Moses’ mother saw Pharaoh’s insistence on having children, she feared for her son, so God cast into her soul the idea that she would make him an ark and then throw the ark into the sea, which is the Nile. She went to a carpenter from Pharaoh’s people and bought a small ark from him. The carpenter said to her: What are you doing with this ark? She said: Build me a son so I can hide it in the ark, and she hated lying. He said: She did not say: I fear Pharaoh’s plot against it. So when she bought the ark and carried it and went with it, the carpenter went to the slaughterers to tell them about Moses’ mother. When he wanted to speak, God held his tongue so he could not speak, and he began to gesture with his hand so the trustees did not know what to say. When their leader was exhausted, he said: Beat him, so they beat him and took him out. When the carpenter reached his place, God restored his tongue so he spoke. He also went to the trustees and came to them to tell them, but God took his tongue and his sight so he could not speak and could not see anything, so they beat him. And they took him out, and he fell into a valley, falling into it, bewildered. So he swore to God that if He restored his tongue and sight, he would not inform on him and that he would be with him, protecting him wherever he was. So God knew that he was truthful and restored his tongue and sight, so he fell down prostrating to God and said: O Lord, guide me to this righteous servant. So God guided him to him, and he came out of the valley and believed in him and confirmed him, and he knew that this was from God Almighty. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: When Moses’ mother became pregnant with Moses, she concealed her matter from all the people, so no one from God’s creation knew about her pregnancy. This was something that God concealed when He wanted to bestow it upon the Children of Israel. So when the year in which he was to be born came, Pharaoh sent the midwives and went to them, and they searched the women in a way they had never done before. Moses’ mother became pregnant with Moses, and her belly did not protrude, her color did not change, and her milk did not appear. The midwives did not interfere with her. So when the night in which he was to be born came, she gave birth to him without a guardian or a midwife, and no one knew about her except his sister Mary. Then God revealed to her: “Breastfeed him, and if you fear for him, then his mother concealed him for three months, breastfeeding him in her lap, and he did not cry or move. Then when she feared for him, she made a closed coffin for him and then threw him into the sea at night. Ibn Abbas and others said: Pharaoh had a daughter at that time, and he had no other children. She was one of the most honorable people to him. Every day she had three needs that she would raise to Pharaoh. She had severe leprosy, and Pharaoh had gathered the doctors and magicians of Egypt for her. They looked into her case and said to him: O king, she will not be cured except by the sea. There is a resemblance to a human being in it, and some of his saliva is taken and her leprosy is smeared with it, and she will be cured of that. This will be on such and such a day and at such and such an hour when the sun rises. So when it was Monday, Pharaoh went to a gathering that was on the bank of the Nile with his wife, Asiya bint Muzahim. Pharaoh’s daughter came with her maids until she sat on the bank of the Nile with her maids, playing with them and sprinkling water on their faces. Then the Nile came with the Ark, battered by the waves. Pharaoh said: This is something in the sea that has caught on to the tree. Bring it to me. So they rushed to it with ships from every side until they placed it in front of him. They tried to open the door, but they could not, and they tried to break it, but they could not. Asiya approached. She saw in the chest a light that no one else had seen, so she addressed it and opened the door. There was a small boy in his cradle, and there was a light between his eyes. God had placed his provision in his thumb, sucking milk from it. God put love for Moses in Asiya’s heart, and Pharaoh loved him and was kind to him. Pharaoh’s daughter came. When they took the boy out of the chest, Pharaoh’s daughter took what was dripping from his saliva and smeared her leprosy with it, and she was healed. She kissed him and hugged him to her chest. The seducers from Pharaoh’s people said, “O king, we think that the newborn you are warning the Children of Israel about is this one. He was thrown into the sea out of fear of you, so kill him.” Pharaoh wanted to kill him, but Asiya said, “A comfort to me and to you. Do not kill him. Perhaps he will be of benefit to us, or we will adopt him as a son.” She could not bear children. She asked Pharaoh for Moses, and he gave him to her. Pharaoh said, As for me, I have no need of him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, If Pharaoh had said that day, ‘He is…’ May God guide him as He guided her.” So Asiya accepted his name and said: “I named him Musa because we found him in the water and the trees. So Musa is the water and Si is the tree.”
28:8: This is what the Almighty said: 8- So Pharaoh’s family picked him up, and picking up is the presence of something without asking for it, so that he would be to them an enemy and a grief, and this lam is called the lam of consequence and the lam of becoming, because they did not pick him up so that he would be to them an enemy and a grief, but rather the outcome of their matter became that. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read: grief with a damma on the ha’ and a sukoon on the zay, and the others read it with a fatha on the ha’ and the zay, and they are two dialects, Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were sinners, disobedient and sinful.
28:9: God Almighty said: 9- And Pharaoh’s wife said, ‘A comfort of the eye for me and for you.’ Wahb said: When the chest was placed in Pharaoh’s hands, they opened it and found Moses in it. When he looked at him, he said, A Hebrew from the enemies. This angered him and he said, How did this boy miss the slaughter? Pharaoh had married a woman from the Children of Israel called Asiya bint Muzahim. She was one of the best women and one of the daughters of the prophets. She was a mother to the poor, showing mercy to them, giving them charity, and giving to them. She said to Pharaoh while she was sitting on his side: “This child is older than a year old. I have only ordered that the boys be slaughtered for this year, so leave him so that he may be a comfort to my eyes.” Do not kill him. It was narrated that she said to him: “He came to us from another land and is not from the Children of Israel. Perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son while they do not perceive,” that their destruction was at his hands. Pharaoh spared him, and God bestowed His love upon him. He said to his wife: Perhaps he may benefit you, but as for me, I do not want to benefit him. Wahb said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said about Moses as Asiya said: Perhaps he may benefit us, God would have benefited him, but he refused, because of the misery that God had decreed for him.
28:10: And the Almighty said: 10- And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty, meaning: empty of everything except the remembrance of Moses and his thoughts, and this is the opinion of most of the commentators. Al-Hasan said: Empty, meaning: forgetting the revelation that God revealed to her when He ordered her to throw him into the sea and not to fear or grieve, and the covenant that He promised that He would return him to her and make him one of the messengers. Then Satan came to her and said: I hated for Pharaoh to kill your son so that his reward and recompense would be for you, and you took it upon yourself to kill him, so you threw him into the sea and drowned him. When the report came to her that Pharaoh had killed him in the Nile, she said: He fell into the hands of his enemy from whom you fled. So the great affliction made her forget what had been God’s covenant with her. Abu Ubaidah said: Empty means: empty of sadness, because she knew the truth of God’s promise. Al-Qatibi denied this and said: How can this be when God Almighty says: She would have almost disclosed it had We not strengthened her heart? The first is more correct. God the Almighty said: "She almost revealed him, the letter ha' before the word bihi" refers to Moses, meaning: She almost revealed that he was her son due to the intensity of her grief. Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: She almost said: "Oh, my son!" Muqatil said: When she saw the ark being lifted by a wave and lowered by another, she feared that it would drown and almost cried out in compassion. Al-Kalbi said: She almost revealed that he was her son, and that was when she heard people saying to Moses after he had grown up: "Moses is the son of Pharaoh!" It was difficult for her and she almost said: "Rather, he is my son." Some of them said: The ha' refers to the revelation, meaning: She almost revealed the revelation that God revealed to her to return him to her. Had We not strengthened her heart, with protection, patience, and steadfastness, that she would be among the believers, those who believed in God’s promise when He said to her: Indeed, We will return him to you.
28:11: 11- And she said to his sister, that is, to Mary, the sister of Moses: Follow him, follow his traces until you learn report of him, and she saw him from afar, that is, from afar, and in the story she was walking to the side and looking stealthily so that she thought she was not seeing him, and they did not perceive, that she was his sister and that she was watching him.
28:12: Ibn Abbas said: Pharaoh's wife's main concern in this world was to find a wet nurse, but whenever they brought a wet nurse, he would not take her breast. This is what God Almighty said: 12- And We forbade him wet nurses. What is meant by prohibition is prevention. Wet nurses is the plural of wet nurse. before means before the arrival of Moses’ mother. When Moses’ sister, whom his mother had sent to look for him, saw that, she said to them: Shall I guide you? And in the story, Moses remained for eight nights without accepting a breast, and he would wake up in the morning looking for a wet nurse for him. She said, meaning Moses’ sister, Shall I direct you to a household that will take care of him, that is, guarantee him for you, and nurse him? She was a woman whose child had been killed, and the most beloved thing to her was to find a young child to nurse, and who are sincere to him. Sincerity is the opposite of deception, and it is purifying the work from the impurities of corruption. They said: Yes, so we brought her. Ibn Jurayj and Al-Suddi said: When Moses' sister said, "And they are his sincere advisers, they seized her and said, You know this boy, so guide us to his family. She said, I do not know him, and I said, They are his sincere advisers." It was said that she said: I only said this out of a desire to please the king and connect with him. It was said that when she said: Shall I direct you to a household? they asked her: Who? She said: My mother. They said: Does your mother have a son? She said: Yes, Aaron. Aaron was born in a year in which no one was to be killed. They said: You have spoken the truth. So they brought her to us. She went to her mother and told her about her son’s condition, and she came with her to them. When the boy smelled his mother’s scent, he kissed her breast and began to suck it until his sides were filled with wetness. Al-Suddi said: They used to give her a dinar every day.
28:13: This is what God Almighty said: 13- So We restored him to his mother so that her eyes might be refreshed, by returning Moses to her, and she would not grieve, that is, so that she would not grieve, and that she might know that the promise of God is true, by returning him to her, but most of them do not know, that God promised her by returning him to her.
28:14: 14- And when he reached his prime, Al-Kalbi said: The prime is between eighteen and thirty years old. Mujahid and others said: Thirty-three years old. And he reached maturity, meaning: he reached forty years old. It was narrated by Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: he reached maturity and his youth had ended. We gave him wisdom and knowledge, meaning: understanding, reason, and knowledge of the religion. So Moses learned and judged before he was sent as a prophet. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
28:15: God Almighty says: "And he entered the city," meaning: Moses entered the city. Al-Suddi said: It is the city of Memphis in the land of Egypt. Muqatil said: The village of Hayin was two farsakhs from Egypt. It was also said: The city of Ain al-Shams, "while its people were unaware," which was the time of the midday nap when people were busy taking a siesta. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: He entered it between sunset and night prayers. They differed about the reason for which he entered the city at this time. Al-Suddi said: That is because Moses, peace be upon him, was called the son of Pharaoh, so he used to ride Pharaoh’s ships and wear clothes like his. One day, Pharaoh rode while Moses was not with him. When Moses came, he was told: Pharaoh has ridden, so he rode after him and the one approaching caught up with him in the land of Memphis, so he entered it during the day, and there was no one at its edge. That is what God Almighty said: And he entered the city at a time when its people were unaware. Ibn Ishaq said: Moses had a group of followers from the Children of Israel who listened to him and followed his example. When he realized what he was doing, he saw the truth and saw the separation from Pharaoh and his people. He differed from them in his religion until he was remembered and they feared him and he feared them. He would not enter a village except in fear and in secret. One day he entered it while its people were unaware. Ibn Zayd said: When Moses, in his youth, attacked Pharaoh with the staff, Pharaoh wanted to kill him. His wife said: He is too young. So he left him alone and ordered him to be taken out of his city. He did not enter upon them until he had grown up and reached his prime. He entered the city while its people were unaware, meaning: of the mention of Moses, that is: after they had forgotten about him and his command due to the length of time they had known him. It was narrated on the authority of Ali regarding his saying: When they were heedless, that it was a holiday for them and they were busy with their amusement and games. He found therein two men fighting, arguing and disputing. This one was from his party, from the Children of Israel, and this one was from his enemy, from the Copts. It was said that the one from his party was the Samaritan, and the one from his enemy was from the Copts. It was said that he was Pharaoh’s cook named Philiston. It was also said: “This one was from his party. This one was from his enemy,” meaning: this one was a believer and this one was an unbeliever. The Copt would make the Israelite carry firewood to the kitchen. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When Moses reached his prime, no one from the family of Pharaoh could get to any of the children of Israel unjustly until they completely resisted. The children of Israel were proud of Moses’ position, because they knew that he was one of them. Moses found two men fighting, one from the children of Israel and the other from the family of Pharaoh. The one from his party sought help from him against the one from his enemy. The Israelite sought help from him against the Pharaoh. Seeking help means asking for help. Moses became angry and became very angry because he took him while he knew Moses’ position among the children of Israel and his protection of them, and the people only knew that he was breastfed by Moses’ mother. So he said to the Pharaoh: Let him go. He said: I only took him to carry firewood to your father’s kitchen. So he disputed with him, and the Pharaoh said: I was about to make him attack you. Moses had been given a broad nature and great strength and power. So Moses struck him. Ibn Masoud read: Moses struck him. Their meaning is the same, which is striking with the palm of the hand. It was said: Al-Wakkaz is a strike in the chest and a shove in the back. Al-Farraa said: Their meaning is one, which is pushing. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Wakkaz is pushing with the fingertips. In some interpretations: Moses counted eighty-three times and struck him in the chest, then he finished with him, meaning: he killed him and finished with his matter, and everything that you finished with, you have finished with it and decided upon him. Moses, peace be upon him, regretted it, and he did not intend to kill him, so he buried him in the sand. “He said, ‘This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy,’” meaning: he made misguidance clear.
28:16: 16- “He said, ‘My Lord, I have wronged myself,’ by killing the Copt without command, ‘so forgive me,’ so He forgave him. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.”
28:17: 17- He said, ‘My Lord, because You have bestowed Your favor upon me,’ with forgiveness, ‘I will never be a supporter,’ ‘helper,’ ‘of the criminals.’ Ibn Abbas said: of the disbelievers. This indicates that the Israelite whom Moses helped was a disbeliever, and this is the opinion of Muqatil. Qatada said: I will never repeat a sin after that. Ibn Abbas said: He did not make an exception, so he was tested with it on the second day.
28:18: 18- So he entered the city, that is, in the city where the Copt was killed, fearful, of his killing the Copt, watching, waiting for something bad to happen. Watching is waiting for something bad. Al-Kalbi said: He waits for when he will be taken, and then he who had sought his help the day before cried out to him: seeking his help and crying out to him later. Ibn Abbas said: Pharaoh was approached and told: The Children of Israel killed a man from among us, so take our right for us. He said: Find for me his killer and someone to testify against him, for it is not right to judge without evidence. While they were wandering around and could not find any evidence, Moses passed by the next day and saw that Israelite fighting a Pharaoh, so he sought his help against the Pharaoh and came across Moses, who had regretted what he had done the day before in killing the Copt. Moses said to him, to the Israelite: You are clearly a heretic, clearly a heretic. Yesterday I fought a man and killed him because of you, and today you are fighting another and you are asking me for help against him? It was said: Moses said to the Pharaoh: You are a blatant heretic, and your injustice is clear. The first is more correct, and most of the scholars agree that he said that to the Israelite.
28:19: 19- So when he intended to seize him who was an enemy to them both, that is, Moses was overcome by compassion for the Israelite, so he stretched out his hand to seize the Pharaoh. The Israelite thought that he intended to seize him because he saw his anger and heard him say: Indeed, you are clearly a transgressor. He said: O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only desire what you desire to be a tyrant in the land, by killing unjustly, and you do not intend to be among the reformers. When the Copt heard what the Israelite said, he knew that Moses was the one who killed the Pharaoh, so he went to Pharaoh and informed him of that, and Pharaoh ordered Moses to be killed. Ibn Abbas said: When Pharaoh sent the slaughterers to kill Moses, they took the greatest path.
28:20: 20- And a man came, from the party of Moses, from the farthest part of the city, meaning: from its end. Most of the people of interpretation said: His name was Hizbil, a believer from the family of Pharaoh. It was also said: His name was Shimon, and it was also said: Shaman. He ran, meaning: He walked quickly. He took a short path until he reached Moses first, so he informed him and warned him until he took another path. “He said: O Moses, indeed the chiefs are conspiring against you,” meaning: the nobles of Pharaoh’s people are consulting about you, to kill you, Al-Zajjaj said: They are ordering each other to kill you, so leave, from the city, I am to you among the sincere advisors, in ordering you to leave.
28:21: 21- So he went out from it, Moses, fearing and watching, that is, waiting for the request, he said, ‘My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people,’ the disbelievers. And in the story: Pharaoh sent for him when he was informed of his escape, so he said, Take the winding path, for he does not know which way to go.
28:22: 22- And when he turned towards Madyan, meaning: he intended to go towards it, continuing towards it. It is said: his house is opposite the house of so-and-so, if it is adjacent to it, and its origin is from the meeting. Al-Zajjaj said: It means he took the road that is opposite Madyan in it, and Madyan is Madyan bin Ibrahim, the town was named after him, and Moses had left in fear without a backpack, shoes or provisions, and Madyan was an eight-day journey from Egypt. “He said: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way,” meaning: he intended to go on the road to Madyan, he said that because he did not know the road to it before, so when he called, an angel came to him with a goat in his hand and took him to Madyan. The commentators said: Moses left Egypt and had no food except tree leaves and greens, until he could see the greenness in his stomach, and he did not reach Madyan until his feet fell off. Ibn Abbas said: It was the first trial from God Almighty to Moses, peace be upon him.
28:23: 23- And when he came to the water of Madyan, which was a well from which they used to water their livestock, he found there a group of people watering their livestock, and he found besides them, meaning: apart from the group, two women holding back, meaning: they were holding back and preventing their sheep from the water until the people had finished and the well was clear for them. Al-Hasan said: They were keeping the sheep from mixing with the sheep of the people. Qatada said: They were keeping the people away from their sheep. It was said: They were preventing their sheep from straying and going astray. The first statement is more correct, because of what follows it, which is his statement: He said, meaning: Moses to the two women, What is the matter with you? What is the matter with you that you do not water your livestock with the people? They said, We will not water our sheep until the shepherds depart. Abu Ja`far, Abu `Amr, and Ibn `Amir read: desired with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the dal, indicating necessity, meaning: until the shepherds return from the water. The others read it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the dal, meaning: until they turn their livestock away from the water. Shepherds is the plural of shepherd, like merchant and merchants. The meaning of the verse is: We will not water our livestock until the shepherds depart, because we are two women who cannot bear to water, nor can we compete with the men. So when they depart, we will water our livestock as much as their livestock has left in the cistern. Our father is very old, he cannot water his livestock, so we needed to water the sheep. They differed about the name of their father. Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi and Al-Hasan said: He is the Prophet Shuaib, peace be upon him. Wahb ibn Munabbih and Saeed ibn Jubayr said: He is Jethro, the nephew of Shuaib. Shuaib had died before that after he lost his sight, so he was buried between the Maqam and Zamzam. It was said: A man who believed in Shuaib. They said: When Moses heard their words, he took pity on them and pulled out a rock from the top of another well that was near them, and only a group of people could lift it. Ibn Ishaq said: Moses pushed the people away from the head of the well, and watered the two women’s sheep. It is narrated that when the people returned with their sheep, they covered the top of the well with a stone that could only be lifted by ten men. Then Moses came and lifted the stone alone, and watered the two women’s sheep. It is said that he removed one sin and prayed for blessings in it, so he watered all the sheep from it.
28:24: That is what he said: 24- So he watered for them both, then he turned to the shade, the shade of a tree, so he sat in its shade because of the intense heat, and he was hungry. And he said, ‘My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need.’ Food, is in need. Linguists say that the lam means to. It is said: He is in need of it, and in need of it. He says: Indeed, I am, for whatever good You send down to me, meaning food. Poor, needy. He was asking for food because of his hunger. Ibn Abbas said: He asked God Almighty for a piece of bread to sustain him. Al-Baqir said: He said it even though he was in need of a half a date. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Moses said: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need, and he was the most honorable of His creation to Him, and he was in need of a half a date. Mujahid said: He did not ask Him for anything but bread. They said: When they returned to their father, they quickly returned before the people and their sheep were full. He said to them: What made you hurry? They said: We found a righteous man who was merciful to us and watered our sheep for us. He said to one of them: Go and call him for me.
28:25: God the Almighty said: 25- Then one of them came to him walking shyly. Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: She was not a swarm of women coming from the sky, but she came concealed, having put the sleeve of her armor over her face out of shyness. “She said: ‘My father invites you to reward you for having watered our flocks.’” Abu Hazim Salamah bin Dinar said: When Moses heard that, he did not want to go, but he was hungry and had no choice but to go. The woman walked and Moses walked behind her, and the wind was blowing her garment and distorting her buttocks. Moses did not want to see that from her, so he said to her: Walk behind me and show me the way if I make a mistake. So she did that. When he entered upon Shu’ayb, he saw dinner being prepared, so he said: Sit down, young man, and have your dinner. Moses said: I seek refuge in God. Shu’ayb said: Why is that? Aren’t you hungry? He said: Yes, but I fear that this is a substitute for what I have given them to drink, and we are from a family that does not seek a substitute for a worldly act for the deeds of the Hereafter. Shu`ayb said to him: No, by God, young man, but this is my custom and the custom of my fathers, to welcome the guest and provide food. So Moses sat and ate. So when he came to him and related to him the story, meaning: his entire affair, of the Copt’s killing and Pharaoh’s intention to kill him, “he said, ‘Do not fear. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people,’” meaning: Pharaoh and his people. He only said this because Pharaoh had no authority over Midian.
28:26: 26- One of them said, O my father, hire him, take him as a worker to tend our sheep, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy, meaning: the best one you can employ is the one who is strong to work and fulfills the trust, so her father said to her: How do you know of his strength and trustworthiness? She said: As for his strength, he lifted a stone from the top of a well that only ten men could lift. And it was said: except forty men. As for his trustworthiness, he said to me, Walk behind me so that the wind does not blow your body away.
28:27: 27- He said, Shu’ayb then: I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, and their names were Safura and Liya according to Shu’ayb al-Jubba’i. Ibn Ishaq said: Safura and Sharqa. Others said: The elder is Safra’ and the younger is Safira’. It was also said that he married the elder. Most of them said that he married the younger of the two, whose name was Safura, and she was the one who went to seek Moses, on condition that you hire me for eight years, meaning: that you be my hired hand for eight years. Al-Farra’ said: It means: make my reward for marrying her that she tend my sheep for eight years. The Arabs say: May God reward you with your reward, meaning: He rewarded you. The years are the singular of which is Hajj. But if you complete ten, it is from you, meaning: if you complete ten years, then that is a favor and a donation from you, it is not obligatory upon you. And I do not want to make it difficult for you, meaning: oblige you to complete the ten unless you volunteer. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous. Umar said: It means: in good company and fulfilling what you said.
28:28: 28- He said, Moses, That is between me and you, meaning: This condition is between me and you. Whatever you stipulated for me is yours, and whatever you stipulated regarding marrying one of them is mine, and the matter is between us. The conversation was completed. Then he said: Whichever of the two terms you complete, meaning: which of the two terms, and what is the connection between completed: I completed and finished with it, the eight or the ten, there is no aggression against me, there is no injustice against me by demanding more than them, and God is Witness over what we say, Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: Witness between me and you. And it was said: Guardian. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, Marwan bin Shuja’ told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: A Jew from the people of Al-Hirah asked me: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? I said: I will not know until I go to the best of the Arabs and ask him. So I went and asked Ibn Abbas, who said: He fulfilled the most important and best of the two terms. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, says something, he does it. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “If you are asked which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? Say: The better and more righteous of the two. And if you are asked: Which of the two women did he marry? Say: The younger of the two, who came and said: O my father, hire him. So he married the younger of the two and fulfilled the contract more fully.” Wahb said: He married him to the eldest. It was narrated on the authority of Shaddad ibn Aws, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Shuaib, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wept out of love for God Almighty until he went blind, and God restored his sight. Then he wept until he went blind, and God restored his sight. Then he wept until he went blind, and God restored his sight. Then God said: What is this weeping? Is it from longing for Paradise or fear of Hellfire? He said: No, O Lord, but from longing to meet You. Then God revealed to him: If that is the case, then congratulations to you on meeting Me, O Shuaib. That is why Moses, the one who spoke to Me, served you.” When they made this contract between them, Shu`ayb ordered his daughter to give Moses a stick with which to repel the wild beasts from his sheep. They disagreed about that stick. Ikrimah said: Adam left Paradise with it, and Gabriel took it after Adam’s death, and it remained with him until he met Moses with it at night and gave it to him. Others said: It was from the myrtle of Paradise. Adam carried it from Paradise and the prophets inherited it. No one took it except a prophet who ate it. It passed from Adam to Noah, then to Abraham until it reached Shuaib. It was the staff of the prophets with him and he gave it to Moses. Al-Suddi said: That staff was entrusted to him by a king in the form of a man. He ordered his daughter to bring him a staff. She entered, took the staff, and brought it to him. When Shu`ayb saw it, he said to her, Return this staff and bring me another. She threw it down and wanted to take another, but none would get her hands on it except herself. She did that three times, and then he gave it to Moses. Moses took it out with him. Then the old man regretted it and said, It was entrusted to him. He went after it and asked to return the staff, but Moses refused. He said, It is my staff. They agreed to place the first man they met between them. Then an angel in the form of a man met them and ruled that the staff should be thrown down, and whoever carried it could take it. Moses threw down the staff, and the old man tried to take it, but he could not. Moses took it in his hand and raised it, and the old man left it for him. Then when the term was completed, and Shu'aib handed over his daughter to Moses, Moses said to the woman: Ask your father to give us some of the sheep. So she asked her father, and Shu'aib said: You both have everything that she gave birth to this year, apart from her own kind. It was said: Shuaib wanted to reward Moses for his good care, to honor him and to keep in touch with his daughter, so he said to him: I have given you from the kids that my sheep give birth to this year, all of them are piebald and spotted. Then God revealed to Moses in a dream: Strike with your staff the water in the sheep trough. Moses struck the water with his staff and then watered the sheep from it, and not one of them missed the opportunity without giving birth between piebald and spotted. So Shuaib knew that this was a provision that God Almighty had brought to Moses and his wife, so he fulfilled his condition and handed the sheep over to him.
28:29: God Almighty said: 29- So when Moses had fulfilled the term, meaning he had completed it and finished it, and traveled with his family, Mujahid said: When Moses had fulfilled the term, he stayed with his son-in-law for another ten years, and then he stayed with him for twenty years. Then he asked his permission to return to Egypt, and he gave him permission. So he went out with his family to the side of Egypt. He perceived, meaning he saw, a fire from the side of the mountain. He was in the wilderness on a dark, very cold night, and his wife was in labor. He said to his family, ‘Stay here; I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you information from it,’ about the road, or a burning ember from the fire, meaning a piece or a flame from the fire. It has three languages. Asim read it as jadhwa with a fatha on the jim, Hamza read it with a damma, and the others read it with a kasra. Qatada and Muqatil said: It is a stick that has been partially burned, and its plural is jadh. Perhaps you may warm yourself, meaning you may warm yourself.
28:30: 30- And when he came to it, he was called from the right bank of the valley, from the side of the valley to the right of Moses, in the blessed spot, for Moses, made it blessed because God spoke to Moses there and sent him as a prophet. Ata’ said: He means the holy one, from the tree, from the direction of the tree. Ibn Mas’ud said: It was a green, shining tamarisk tree. Qatada, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: It was a bramble tree. Wahb said: It is from the blackberry, and on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: It is the jujube, O Moses, I am God, Lord of the worlds.
28:31: 31- And throw down your staff. But when he saw it writhing, moving, as if it were a jinn, meaning a small snake due to the speed of its movement, he turned back, fleeing from it, and did not look back, did not return. Then it was called: "O Moses, come forward and do not fear. Indeed, you are among those who are safe."
28:32: 32- Walk, put your hand in your pocket and it will come out white without disease, leprosy, so it came out and it had a ray like the light of the sun, and draw your wing towards you from fear, the people of Kufa and Ash-Sham read: with a damma on the ra' and a sukoon on the ha', and with a fatha on the ra' Hafs, and the others read it with a fatha on both of them, and all of them are languages meaning fear. The meaning of the verse: If your hand is destroyed and you do not see any of its rays, then put it in your pocket and it will return to its original state. Al-Janah: The entire hand. It was also said that it is the upper arm. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them: God commanded him to put his hand to his chest, so that the fear he had experienced upon seeing the snake would go away. He also said: There is no one who fears after Moses except that when he places his hand on his chest, his fear goes away. Mujahed said: Whoever is frightened and folds his wings towards him, the fear will go away from him. It was said: What is meant by closing the wing is tranquility, that is: calm your fear and lower your side, because it is the nature of the fearful that his heart is disturbed and his body trembles. Similar to that is His statement: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy (al-Isra’ 17:24), meaning gentleness, and His statement: And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers (Ash-Shu’ara’: 215), that is: be gentle with them and be kind to them. Al-Farra’ said: He meant by the wing the stick, meaning: Bring your stick to you. It was said: The word ‘rahb’ means ‘sleeve’ in the language of Himyar. Al-Asma’i said: I heard some Bedouins say: Give me what is in your ‘rahb’, meaning: in your sleeve. Its meaning is: Put your hand towards you and take it out of the sleeve, because he took the stick and his hand was in his sleeve. These two, meaning the staff and the white hand, are two proofs, two signs, “from your Lord to Pharaoh and his establishment. Indeed, they were a wicked people.”
28:33: 33- He said, ‘My Lord, I have killed one of them, and I fear that they will kill me.’
28:34: 34- And my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I in speech, and he only said that because of the knot in his tongue from the ember being placed in it, so send him with me as a support, a helper. It is said, I supported him, meaning: I helped him. Nafi’ read support with a fat-ha on the dal without a hamza, seeking lightness. The rest read it with a sukoon on the dal with a hamza, to believe me, Asim and Hamza read it with a dhammah on the qaf, meaning: a supporting support that confirms. The others read it with the jazm as an answer to the supplication and to believe Aaron in the statement of all. Muqatil said: So that Pharaoh would believe me, Indeed, I fear that they will lie, meaning Pharaoh and his people.
28:35: 35- He said, ‘We will strengthen you with your brother,’ meaning: We will strengthen you with your brother, and Aaron was in Egypt at that time, and We will give you both authority, an argument and proof, so they will not reach you with Our signs, meaning: they will not reach you with killing or harm because of Our signs. It was said: There is an inversion of this, and its meaning is: And We will give you both authority with Our signs through what We give you of miracles so they will not reach you, you and those who follow you will be the victors, meaning: you and your followers will have the victory over Pharaoh and his people.
28:36: 36- So when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, clear ones, they said, ‘This is nothing but invented magic,’ fabricated, and we had not heard of this, of what you are calling us to, among our forefathers of old.
28:37: 37- And Moses said, the people of Mecca read it without the waw, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an, My Lord knows best who brings guidance from Him, who is right and who is wrong, and who will have the final home, the praiseworthy outcome in the Hereafter, indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed, meaning: the disbelievers.
28:38: 38- “And Pharaoh said, ‘O eminent ones, I know of no god for you other than me. So kindle for me, O Haman, a fire over the clay. ’ So cook for me bricks. It was said that he was the first to make bricks and build with them. ‘And make for me a tower,’ a high palace. It was said that it was a minaret. The commentators said: When Pharaoh ordered his minister Haman to build the tower, Haman gathered the workers and laborers until fifty thousand builders had gathered, in addition to the followers and hired workers, and those who cooked the bricks and plaster, carved the wood, and hammered the nails. They raised it and built it until it rose to a height that no building of any of creation had reached. God Almighty wanted to tempt them with it, so when they finished it, Pharaoh climbed over it and ordered an arrow to be thrown towards the sky, and it returned to him stained with blood. He said, ‘I have killed the god of Moses. ’ Pharaoh was riding mules, so God sent Gabriel at sunset, and he struck him with his wing, cutting him into three pieces, and one of them fell on Pharaoh’s army. So I killed a million of them, and some of them fell into the sea and some into the west, and no one who did anything with it remained but perished. This is what God Almighty said: “Then kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay, and make for me a tower that I may look up to the God of Moses,” to look at him and understand his condition, and indeed I think he, meaning Moses, is among the liars, in his claim that the earth and creation have a god other than me, and that he is His Messenger.
28:39: 39- And he and his soldiers were arrogant upon the earth without right and thought that they would not be returned to Us. Nafi’, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Ya’qub read: they will return with a fatha on the ya’ and a kasra on the jim, and the rest read it with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the jim.
28:40: 40- “So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. Then see what was the end of the wrongdoers.”
28:41: 41- And We made them leaders, leaders and chiefs, inviting to the Fire, but on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped, they will not be prevented from the punishment.
28:42: 42- And We pursued them in this world with a curse, disgrace and torment, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised, among the banished and cursed. Abu Ubaidah said: Among the doomed. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: Among those disfigured with black faces and blue eyes. It is said: God made him ugly, and made him ugly: if He made him ugly, and it is said: He made him ugly with ugliness, and ugliness, if He distanced him from all good.
28:43: God Almighty says: 43- And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the former generations, meaning: the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and others who were before Moses, as insights for the people, meaning: so that they would see through that Scripture and be guided by it, and guidance, from misguidance for whoever acts upon it, and mercy, for whoever believes in it, that they might be reminded, with what is in it of admonitions and insights.
28:44: 44- And you were not, O Muhammad, on the western side, meaning: on the western side of the mountain, as stated by Qatada and As-Suddi. Al-Kalbi said: on the western side of the valley. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He means where Moses spoke to his Lord, when We decreed to Moses the matter, meaning We enjoined upon him and established the matter with him with the message to Pharaoh and his people, nor were you among the witnesses, those present at that time, so he remembered it of his own accord.
28:45: 45- But We created generations, We created nations after Moses, peace be upon him, and life was prolonged for them, meaning: the period was prolonged for them, so they forgot God’s covenant and abandoned His command. This is because God Almighty had made a covenant with Moses and his people, the Jews, regarding Muhammad, peace be upon him, and belief in him. But when life was prolonged for them and generations after generations succeeded each other, they forgot those covenants and abandoned fulfilling them. And you were not residing among the people of Madyan, as Moses and Shuaib were among them, reciting to them Our verses, reminding them of the promise and the threat. Muqatil said: He means you did not witness the people of Madyan and recite their report to the people of Mecca, but We were messengers, meaning: We sent you as a messenger and revealed to you a book containing this report, so you recited it to them, and were it not for that you would not have known it and not informed them of it.
28:46: 46- And you were not by the mountain, on the side of the mountain on which God spoke to Moses, when We called, it was said: when We called to Moses: Take the Book with strength. Wahb said: Moses said: O Lord, show me Muhammad. He said: You will not reach that, and if you wish, I will call his nation and let you hear their voice. He said: Yes, O Lord. God Almighty said: O nation of Muhammad. They answered him from the loins of their fathers. Abu Zur’ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir said: He called out, O nation of Muhammad, I have answered you before you called upon Me and I have given you before you asked Me. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him - and some of them attributed it to the Prophet - that God said: O nation of Muhammad, and they responded to Him from the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers: Here I am, O God, here I am. Indeed, all praise and blessings are Yours, and the kingdom. You have no partner. God Almighty said: O nation of Muhammad, indeed My mercy precedes My wrath and My forgiveness precedes My punishment. I gave to you before you asked Me and I answered you before you called upon Me. I forgave you before you disobeyed Me. Whoever comes to Me on the Day of Resurrection with the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is My servant and Messenger will enter Paradise, even if his sins are more numerous than the foam of the sea. God Almighty says: But as a mercy from your Lord, meaning: But He has shown you mercy by sending you and revealing to you the revelation and informing you of the report that is hidden from you, that you may warn a people to whom no warner came before you, meaning: the people of Mecca, that they may remember.
28:47: 47- And had it not been that a disaster would strike them, punishment and retribution, for what their hands have put forth, of disbelief and disobedience, so they would say, ‘Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could follow Your signs and be among the believers?’ The answer to would it not have been is omitted, meaning: We would have hastened the punishment upon them, meaning: had it not been that they argue that We did not send a messenger to them, We would have hastened the punishment upon them for their disbelief. It was said that its meaning is that We would not have sent you to them as a messenger, but We sent you so that the people would not have an argument against God after the messengers.
28:48: 48- So when the truth came to them from Us, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said, meaning the infidels of Mecca, Why was Muhammad not given the like of what Moses was given? of the signs such as the white hand and the staff. It was also said: the like of what Moses was given as a book all at once. God the Almighty said: Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? That is, they disbelieved in the signs of Moses as they disbelieved in the signs of Muhammad. They said, ‘Two magics that backed up each other.’ The people of Kufa read: two magics, meaning the Torah and the Qur’an. Backing up means: each magic strengthens the other. Backing up was attributed to the two magics broadly. Al-Kalbi said: Their statement was when they sent to the leaders of the Jews in Medina and asked them about Muhammad. They told them that his description was in their book, the Torah. They returned and told them what the Jews had said, and they said: Two magics that backed up each other. Others read: Two magicians, meaning Muhammad and Moses, peace be upon them, because the meaning of pretending to be people and their actions is more similar to books, and they said, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in all of them.’
28:49: 49- Say, to them, O Muhammad, Bring a book from God that is better guidance than both of them, meaning: than the Torah and the Qur’an, that I may follow it, if you should be truthful.
28:50: 50- If they do not respond to you, meaning: they do not come with what you asked for, “then know that they only follow their own desires. And who is more astray than he who follows his own desires without guidance from God? Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.”
28:51: 51- And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: We explained. Al-Farra’ said: We sent down the verses of the Qur’an one after the other. Qatadah said: The Word was conveyed to them in this Qur’an, meaning how it was done to those who came before. Muqatil said: We explained to the disbelievers of Mecca what is in the Qur’an of the report of the past nations and how they were punished for their denial. Ibn Zayd said: We conveyed to them the good of this world with the good of the Hereafter until it was as if they had witnessed the Hereafter in this world, that they might remember.
28:52: 52- Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, before Muhammad, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace. It was also said: before the Qur’an, they believe in it, was revealed about the believers among the People of the Book, Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions. Muqatil said: Rather, they are the people of the Gospel who came from Abyssinia and believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Saeed bin Jubair said: They were forty men who came with Jaafar from Abyssinia to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they saw the privation of the Muslims, they said: O Prophet of God, we have wealth, so if you give us permission, we will return and bring our wealth and help the Muslims with it. So he gave them permission, and they returned and brought their wealth and helped the Muslims with it. Then this verse was revealed about them: Those to whom We gave the Scripture, until His Most High’s saying: And they spend from what We have provided them. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: It was revealed about eighty of the People of the Book, forty from Najran, thirty-two from Abyssinia, and eight from the Levant.
28:53: Then God described them and said: 53- And when it is recited to them, meaning the Qur’an, “they say, ‘We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord.’” This is because the mention of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was written for them in the Torah and the Gospel. Indeed, we were, before it, Muslims, meaning: before the Qur’an, Muslims who were sincere to God in monotheism and believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was a true prophet.
28:54: 54- Those will be given their reward twice, for their belief in the first book and the other book, because they were patient, in their religion. Mujahid said: It was revealed about a group of the People of the Book who converted to Islam and were harmed. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarkhasi told us, Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Hafs al-Juwayni told us, Ahmad ibn Sa`id al-Darimi told us, Uthman told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Salih, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash`ari that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three who will be given their reward twice: a man who had a female slave and disciplined her well, then freed her and married her; a man from among the People of the Book who believed in His Book and believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace; and a servant who worshipped God well and advised his master well.” God Almighty says: And they repel evil with good. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: They repel polytheism with the testimony that there is no god but God. Muqatil said: They repel the harm and insults they hear from the polytheists with forgiveness and pardon. And from what We have provided them they spend, in obedience.
28:55: 55- If they hear ill speech, i.e., ugly speech, they turn away from it. This is because the polytheists used to curse the believers among the People of the Book and say, Perdition be upon you! You have abandoned your religion. They would turn away from them and not respond to them. And they say, ‘To us our deeds and to you your deeds.’ To us our religion and to you yours. “Peace be upon you.” This does not mean the greeting of peace, but rather the peace of abandonment, meaning, You have been safe from us, we will not oppose you with cursing and ugly speech. “We do not seek the ignorant,” i.e., the religion of the ignorant, meaning, We do not like the religion that you follow. It was also said, We do not want to be among the people of ignorance and foolishness. This was before the Muslims were ordered to fight.
28:56: God Almighty said: 56- Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, meaning: I loved his guidance. It was said: I loved him because of his kinship, but God guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided. Mujahid and Muqatil said: for whomever He has destined to be guided. It was revealed about Abu Talib. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Say, There is no god but God, and I will bear witness to it for you on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Were it not that the Quraysh would reproach me, saying, He was only driven to do that by impatience, I would have made it a comfort to your eyes. Then God Almighty revealed this verse.
28:57: 57- And they said, ‘If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land.’ Mecca, this verse was revealed about Al-Harith bin Uthman bin Nawfal bin Abd Manaf. He said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: We know that what you say is true, but if we follow your religion, we fear that the Arabs will expel us from our land, Mecca. This is the meaning of his statement: We will be snatched away from our land. Snatching means to be taken away quickly. God the Almighty said: Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary? This is because the Arabs in the pre-Islamic period would raid one another and kill one another, and the people of Mecca were safe wherever they were, due to the sanctity of the sanctuary. It is well known that gazelles were safe from wolves and pigeons were safe from hawks there. Collects: The people of Medina and Jacob read it with a ta’ for the fruits, and the others with a ya’ for the barrier between the feminine noun and the verb, meaning: it brings and collects. To it: it is said: I collected the water in the basin, meaning: I gathered it. Muqatil said: it is carried to the sanctuary. The fruits of all things, provision from Us, but most of them do not know, that what he says is true.
28:58: God Almighty says: 58- And how many a city have We destroyed, meaning of the people of a city, which was insolent in its livelihood, meaning: in its livelihood, meaning: it acted arrogantly and became tyrannical. Ata’ said: They lived in arrogance, consuming God’s provisions and worshipping idols. Those were their dwellings, which were not inhabited after them except for a little, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Only travelers and passers-by inhabited them for a day or an hour. Its meaning is: It was not inhabited after them except for a little. It was also said: Its meaning is: Only a small part of it was inhabited, and most of it was ruined. And We were the inheritors, like His statement: Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it Maryam 19:40.
28:59: 59- And your Lord would not destroy the cities, meaning: the unbelieving cities and their people, until He had sent to its mother city a messenger, meaning: to its largest and greatest city a messenger to warn them. He specified the greatest city for sending the messenger to, because the messenger is sent to the nobles, and the nobles inhabit the cities and the places that are the mother of what is around them, reciting to them Our verses, Muqatil said: The Messenger informs them that the punishment will descend upon them if they do not believe, And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers, polytheists, meaning: I destroyed them because of their wrongdoing.
28:60: 60- And whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment, you enjoy it for the days of your life, then it will perish and end, “and what is with God is better and more lasting. So will you not reason?” That what is lasting is better than what is perishable. Most readers read: ta'qaloon with a ta', while Abu Amr reads: ta'qaloon with a ta' and a ya'.
28:61: 61- Is he to whom We have promised a good promise, meaning Paradise, and he will attain it, will be afflicted with it, attain it, and will go to it, like he to whom We have given enjoyment of worldly life, which will soon be gone, then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth, the Fire? Qatadah said: meaning the believer and the disbeliever. Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Jahl. Muhammad bin Kaab said: It was revealed about Hamza, Ali, and Abu Jahl. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Ammar and Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira.
28:62: 62- And the Day He will call to them and say, ‘Where are My partners whom you used to claim?’
28:63: 63- Those upon whom the word has come into effect will say, upon whom the punishment was due and they are the leaders of misguidance, Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray, that is, we called them to misguidance, and they are the followers, We led them astray as we were led astray, we led them astray as we were led astray, we disavow them to You, “they did not worship us,” and some of them disavowed each other and became enemies, as God Almighty said: Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another Az-Zukhruf 67.
28:64: 64- And it was said to the infidels: Call upon your partners, meaning the idols, to save you from the punishment. So they called upon them, but they did not respond to them, they did not answer them, and they saw the punishment, if only they had been guided. The answer to if is omitted, based on the estimation: If only they had been guided in this world, they would not have seen the punishment.
28:65: 65- And the Day He will call them, meaning: God will ask the disbelievers, and say, ‘What did you answer the messengers?’
28:66: 66- So the report will be hidden from them, meaning: the report and excuses. Mujahid said: the arguments. On that Day, so they will have no excuse or argument. So they will not ask one another: they will not answer. Qatada said: they will not argue. It was said: they will be silent and will not ask one another.
28:67: 67- But as for he who repents, believes, and does righteousness, he may be among the successful, among the happy and successful.
28:68: God Almighty says: 68- And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses. This verse was revealed in response to the polytheists when they said: Why was this Qur’an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?
