Meaning: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, or Urwah bin Masoud Al-Thaqafi. God Almighty informed us that He does not send messengers based on their choice. God the Almighty said: It is not for them to choose. It was said: It is for affirmation, meaning: And God chooses what is best for them, meaning: He chooses what is best and most suitable. It was also said: It is for negation, meaning: The choice is not up to them, and they do not have the right to choose against God, as God the Almighty said: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice. (al-Ahzab 33:36). Choice is a noun from choice that replaces a verbal noun, and it is also a name for the chosen one, as it is said: Muhammad is the best of God’s creation. Then He exalted Himself and said: Glory be to God and He is above what they associate with Him.
28:69: 69- And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare.
28:70: 70- “And He is God, there is no deity except Him. To Him is praise in the first and the last.” His followers praise Him in this world, and they will praise Him in the Hereafter in Paradise. And His is the judgment. He decides judgment among creation. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He has judged that those who obey Him will be forgiven and that those who disobey Him will be miserable. And to Him you will be returned.
28:71: God Almighty said: 71- “Say, ‘Have you considered?’ Tell me, O people of Mecca, ‘if God made the night continuous for you,’ forever, ‘until the Day of Resurrection,’ with no day with it, ‘what god other than God could bring you light,’ a day in which you seek sustenance, ‘will you not hear?’ Hearing, understanding, and accepting.
28:72: 72- “Say, ‘Have you considered: if God made the day continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection,’” with no night in it, what god other than God could bring you a night in which to rest? Then will you not see? What error you are in.
28:73: 73- And of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein, that is, during the night, and that you may seek of His bounty during the day, and that you may be grateful, for the blessings of God Almighty.
28:74: 74- And the Day He will call to them and say, ‘Where are My partners whom you used to claim?’ He repeated the mention of the call to the polytheists to increase the rebuke and reprimand.
28:75: 75- And We will extract, We will bring forth, from every nation a witness, meaning: their Messenger who was sent to them, as He said: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness? (An-Nisa’: 41), Then We will say, ‘Bring forth your proof,’ your argument that I have a partner. So they will know that the truth, monotheism, is with God, and lost from them is that which they used to invent, in this world.
28:76: God Almighty said: 76- Indeed, Korah was from the people of Moses, he was his cousin, because Korah was the son of Yashar, the son of Qahath, the son of Levi, the son of Jacob, peace be upon him, and Moses was the son of Imran, the son of Qahath. Ibn Ishaq said: Korah was the uncle of Moses, he was the brother of Imran, and they were the sons of Yashar. There was no one among the Children of Israel who had read the Torah more than Korah, but he was a hypocrite just as the Samaritan was a hypocrite, and he transgressed against them, it was said: he was an agent for Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, so he transgressed against them and oppressed them. Qatada said: he transgressed against them with his abundance of money. Ad-Dahhak said: He wanted to commit polytheism against them. Shahr bin Hawshab said: He increased the length of his clothes by a handspan. We narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will not look on the Day of Resurrection at the one who drags his clothes out of arrogance. It was said: He was arrogant and haughty towards them. And We gave him of the treasures whose keys is the plural of miftaah which is that which opens a door. This is the saying of Qatada, Mujahid and a group. It was also said: His keys are his treasuries, as He said: And with Him are the keys of the unseen (al-An’am 6:59), meaning: His treasuries, that would be too much for a company of strong men, meaning: to burden them, and to make them sway if they carried it due to its weight. Abu Ubaidah said: This is from the inverted form, its meaning: that a company of strong men would be too much for it. It is said: So-and-so carried such-and-such if he carried it heavily. They differed regarding the number of the agnates. Mujahid said: Between ten and fifteen. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: Between three and ten. Qatada said: Between ten and forty. It was also said: Forty men. It was also said: Seventy. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: Its keys were carried by forty of the strongest men. Jarir said on the authority of Mansour on the authority of Khaithamah, he said: I found in the Bible that the keys to the treasures of Qarun and Qar were sixty mules, and there was no more than one key on a finger, and each key contained a treasure. It is said: Wherever Qarun went, he carried with him the keys to his treasures. They were made of iron, but when they became too heavy for him, he made them of wood. They became too heavy, so he made them of cowhide the length of his fingers, and they were carried with him when he rode on forty mules. When his people said to him, said to Qarun, his people from the Children of Israel: Do not rejoice, do not be arrogant, do not show off, and do not be merry, for God does not like the exultant, the wicked and arrogant who do not thank God for what He has given them.
28:77: 77- And seek, through that which God has given you, the home of the Hereafter. Seek what God has given you of wealth, blessings, and Paradise, which means thanking God for what He has bestowed upon you and spending it in the pleasure of God, and do not forget your portion of this world. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: Do not neglect working in this world for the hereafter so that you are saved from the punishment, because the true portion of a person in this world is to work for the hereafter. Al-Suddi said: By giving charity and maintaining kinship ties. Ali said: Do not forget your health, strength, youth and wealth to seek the hereafter with them. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Shadhan told us, Abu Yazid Hatim bin Mahbub Al-Shami told us, Hussain Al-Marwazi told us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, Jaafar bin Burqan told us, on the authority of Ziyad bin Al-Jarrah, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun Al-Awdi, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a man while advising him: Take advantage of five things before five others: your youth before your old age, your health before your illness, your wealth before your poverty, your free time before you become busy, and your life before your death.” The hadith is mursal. Al-Hasan said: He was ordered to give priority to what is best and to hold back what would make him rich. Mansour bin Zadan said regarding his statement: And do not forget your share of this world, he said: Your sustenance and the sustenance of your family. And do good as God has done good to you, meaning: do good by obeying God as God has done good to you by His grace. It was said: Be good to people as God has been good to you, and do not seek corruption on earth. Whoever disobeys God has sought corruption on earth, God does not love corrupters.
28:78: 78- He said, meaning Qarun, It was only given to me because of knowledge I have, meaning: because of grace and goodness, and God’s knowledge of it is with me, so He saw that I was worthy of it, so He favored me with this wealth over you as He favored me with other things. It was said: It is the knowledge of alchemy. Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab said: Moses knew alchemy, so he taught Joshua ibn Nun a third of that knowledge, and he taught Caleb ibn Yuqana a third of it, and he taught Qarun a third of it, so Qarun deceived them until he added their knowledge to his own, and that was the reason for his wealth. It was said: I have knowledge of dealing with trade, agriculture, and various types of earnings. God the Almighty says: Does he not know that God destroyed before him generations who were mightier than him in strength and greater in accumulation of wealth? And the criminals will not be asked about their sins. Qatada said: They will enter Hell without being held to account or questioned. Mujahid said: This means that the angels will not be asked about them, because they know them by their appearance. Al-Hasan said: They will not be asked to inquire, but rather to rebuke and reprimand.
28:79: 79- So he came out to his people in his finery. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: He and his people came out in red and yellow clothes. Ibn Zayd said: With seventy thousand wearing saffron. Mujahid said: On white mules with purple saddles. Muqatil said: He came out on a gray mule with a golden saddle with purple, and with him were four thousand horsemen wearing purple, and with them were three hundred slave girls wearing white jewelry and red clothes, and they were on gray mules. “Those who desired the life of this world said, ‘Oh, would that we had like that which Qarun has been given. Indeed, he is one of great fortune,’” of wealth.
28:80: 80- And those who were given knowledge said, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: meaning the rabbis from the Children of Israel. Muqatil said: those who were given knowledge of what God promised in the Hereafter said to those who wished for what Qarun was given in this world: Woe to you! The reward of God is better, meaning what God has of reward and recompense is better for those who believe, who believe in the Oneness of God, and do righteous deeds, than what Qarun was given in this world. And none will receive it except the steadfast, Muqatil said: they will not be given it, meaning righteous deeds. Al-Kalbi said: they will not be given it in the Hereafter. It was said: none will receive this statement, which is His saying: Woe to you! The reward of God is better, except those who are steadfast in obeying God and avoiding the adornments of this world.
28:81: The Almighty said: 81- So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. The people of knowledge of the report said: Qarun was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel after Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, and the most knowledgeable of them of the Torah, and the most handsome and rich of them. He had a beautiful voice, but he rebelled and transgressed. The beginning of his transgression and disobedience was that God revealed to Moses to command his people to hang four threads on their cloaks, with a blue thread at each end, the color of the sky, so that they would be reminded by it when they looked at it, and know that I reveal My words from it. Moses said: O Lord, will you not command them to make all their cloaks green? For the Children of Israel despise these threads. His Lord said to him: O Moses, the small part of My command is not small, so if they do not obey Me in the small matter, they will not obey Me in the great matter. Moses, peace be upon him, called them and said: God commands you to hang green threads on your cloaks, the color of the sky, so that you will remember your Lord when they look at it. You have seen it, so the Children of Israel did what Moses commanded them to do, and Korah was arrogant and did not obey him, and said: The masters only do this to their servants so that they may be distinguished from others, and this was the beginning of his disobedience and transgression. When Moses crossed the sea with the Children of Israel, the hymn was made for Aaron, which was the leadership of the altar. The Children of Israel would bring their offerings to Aaron, and he would place them on the altar, and fire would come down from heaven and consume them. Korah felt bad about that and came to Moses and said: O Moses, you have the message and Aaron the hymn, and I have nothing to do with that, and I am reading the Torah, I cannot bear this. Moses said to him: I did not make it for Aaron, but God made it for him. Then Korah said, By God, I will not believe you until you show me proof. So Moses gathered together the chiefs of the Children of Israel and said, Bring your staffs. So he tied them together and threw them into his tent in which he used to worship God. They guarded their staffs until morning, and Aaron's staff was shaking with green leaves, and it was made of almond wood. Moses said, O Korah, do you see this? Korah said, By God, this is not more amazing than what magic does. Korah withdrew from Moses with his belongings, and Moses tried to flatter him because of the kinship between them, but he harmed him all the time and only increased in his arrogance, haughtiness, and hostility towards Moses. Until he built a house, made its door of gold, and plated its walls with gold sheets. The notables of the Children of Israel would come to him morning and evening, and he would feed them food, talk to him, and make them laugh. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: When the zakat was revealed to Moses, Korah came to him and made a deal with him: for every thousand dinars, for one dinar, for every thousand dirhams, for one dirham, for every thousand sheep, for one sheep, and for every thousand things, for something else. Then he returned to his house and locked him up. He found it too much, but his soul did not allow it. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said to them: O Children of Israel, Moses commanded you to do everything, and you obeyed him. Now he wants to take your money. They said: You are our leader, so order us to do whatever you wish. He said: I order you to bring so-and-so, the prostitute, and we will give her a reward until she accuses Moses of adultery. When she does that, the Children of Israel will rebel against him and reject him. So they left her. Korah gave her a thousand dirhams, and it was said a thousand dinars, and it was said a golden basin. It was said: I will give you money and mix you with my women on the condition that you accuse Moses of adultery tomorrow when the Children of Israel are present. So the next day, Korah gathered the Children of Israel and came to Moses and said: The Children of Israel are waiting for you to come out and you will command them and forbid them. Then Moses came out to them while they were in a wide open area. He stood up and said, "O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we will cut off his hand. Whoever slanders, we will flog him eighty times. Whoever commits adultery without having a wife, we will flog him one hundred times. Whoever commits adultery while having a wife, we will stone him to death." Korah said to him, Even if it was you? He said, Even if it was me. He said, The Children of Israel claim that you committed adultery with so-and-so. He said, Call her, and if she says so, then it is as she says. When she came, Moses said to her, O so-and-so, did I do to you what these people say? And he was greatly distressed by her, and asked her by the One Who split the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah, unless she told the truth. So God Almighty granted her success, and she said to herself: “Today I will make a repentance that is better than harming the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” She said: No, they lied, but Korah made me promise to throw myself at you. So Moses fell down in prostration, weeping, and saying: O God, if I am your Messenger, then be angry for me. Then God Almighty revealed to him: I have commanded the earth to obey you, so command it as you wish. Moses said: O Children of Israel, God has sent me to Korah, so whoever is with him should remain in his place, and whoever is with me should withdraw. So they withdraw, and only two men remained with Korah. Then Moses said: O Earth, seize them. So the Earth seized them by the feet of their feet. In another narration: He was on his bed and mattress, so I took him until his bed was hidden. Then he said: O earth, take them. So it took them up to his knees. Then he said: O earth, take them. So it took them up to their middles. Then he said: O earth, take them. So it took them up to their necks. Korah and his companions were supplicating to Moses all the time, and Korah was pleading with him by God and the womb. It was narrated that he pleaded with him seventy times, but Moses, peace be upon him, did not pay attention to him due to the intensity of his anger. Then he said: O earth, take them. So the earth closed over them. God revealed to Moses, What is wrong with your heart? He sought your help seventy times, but you did not help him. By My glory and majesty, if he had sought my help once, I would have helped him. In some of the narrations: I will not make the earth obedient to anyone after you. Qatada said: He was swallowed up and he continues to sink into the earth every day to the height of a man, never reaching its bottom until the Day of Resurrection. He said: The Children of Israel began to whisper among themselves that Moses had only called down a curse on Qarun so that he could take his house, treasures, and wealth. So God Almighty called down a curse on Moses until the earth swallowed up his house, treasures, and wealth. This is what God Almighty said: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his house. “And he had no company” to aid him other than God, to protect him from God, nor was he among those who could defend themselves from the swallowing up that befell him.
28:82: 82- And those who wished to be in his place yesterday became regretful. Those who wished for the wealth and adornment that God had provided them with became regretful of that wish. The Arabs express becoming with before, “became,” and became. They say: So-and-so became a scholar, became destitute, and became sad. “They say, ‘Woe to God!’” They differed in the meaning of this word. Mujahid said: Did you not know? Qatadah said: Did you not see? Al-Farra’ said: “It is a statement of confirmation, like a man saying: “Do you not see what God has done and His goodness?” He mentioned that he was told by someone who heard a Bedouin woman say to her husband: Where is your son? He said: Woe to him, meaning: Do you not see him behind the house? Al-Hasan said: “It is a word of introduction, meaning: God expands provision.” It was said: It is a warning like ‘ala,’ and Qatrib said: Woe to you means woe to you, from which the lam was deleted, as Antara said: The saying of the knights, Woe to Antar, has healed my soul and cured its illness. Meaning: Woe to you, and that is in the accusative case because of the omission of know that God. Al-Khalil said: Woe is separated from ka-ana and its meaning is astonishment, as you say: Woe, why did you do that! This is because the people regretted it and said: Woe! regretting what they had done in the past. As if its meaning is I think that and I estimate it, as you say: Relief has come to you, meaning I think that and I estimate it. He expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it, meaning He expands and restricts. Had it not been that God had bestowed favor upon us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us up. Hafs and Ya’qub read it with a fat-ha on the kha’ and the seen. The majority read it with a damma on the kha’ and a kasra on the seen. And it is as if the disbelievers will not succeed.
28:84: 84- Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, but whoever brings an evil deed - those who do evil will not be recompensed except for what they used to do.
28:85: God the Almighty says: 85- Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur'an, meaning: He sent down the Qur'an to you according to the majority of commentators. Ata' said: He has made it obligatory for you to act in accordance with the Qur'an, will bring you back to a place of return, to Mecca. This is the narration of Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and it is also the opinion of Mujahid. Al-Qatibi said: A man's place of return is his country, because he turns and then returns to his country. This is because when the Prophet, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, left the cave as a migrant to Medina, he traveled a route other than the one to Mecca and yearned for it. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said: Do you yearn for your country and place of birth? He said: Yes. He said: God the Almighty says: Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur'an will bring you back to a place of return, and this verse was revealed in Al-Juhfah and is neither Meccan nor Medinan. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: He will return you to a place of return means death. Az-Zuhri and Ikrimah said: To the Resurrection. It was also said: To Paradise. Say, ‘My Lord knows best who has brought guidance,’ meaning: He knows who has brought guidance. This was an answer to the infidels of Mecca when they said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You are indeed in error. God Almighty said: Say to them, My Lord knows best who has brought guidance, meaning himself, and who is in manifest error, meaning the polytheists. Its meaning is: He knows best about both groups.
28:86: God Almighty said: 86- And you did not expect that the Scripture would be revealed to you, meaning: the Qur’an would be revealed to you, except as a mercy from your Lord. Al-Farra’ said: This is an isolated exception, meaning: But your Lord had mercy on you and gave you the Qur’an. So never be a supporter of the disbelievers, meaning: a helper to them in their religion. Muqatil said: That was when he was called to the religion of his forefathers, so God mentioned His blessings and forbade him from supporting them in what they were following.
28:87: 87- And let not them turn you away from the verses of God, meaning the Qur’an, “after they have been revealed to you. And invite to your Lord,” to knowing Him and His Oneness, and do not be among those who associate others with God. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The address appears to be to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but what is meant by it are the people of his religion, meaning: Do not support the disbelievers and do not agree with them.
29:2: 2- “Alif, Lam, Meem. * Do people think that they will be left alone, without being tested or tried, that they will say, ‘We believe’ and they will not be tested?” No! We will surely test them to distinguish the sincere from the hypocrites, the truthful from the liar. They differed about the reason for the revelation of this verse. Al-Sha’bi said: It was revealed about some people in Mecca who had acknowledged Islam. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them: No acknowledgment of Islam will be accepted from you until you emigrate. So they set out intending to go to Medina, but the polytheists pursued them and fought them. Some of them were killed and some escaped. Then God revealed these two verses. It is as if Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He meant by the people who believed in Mecca: Salamah ibn Hisham, Ayyash ibn Rabi’ah, Al-Walid ibn Al-Walid, Ammar ibn Yasir, and others. Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir, who was being tortured for the sake of God Almighty. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Mahja’ bin Abdullah, the freed slave of Umar. He was the first Muslim to be killed on the day of Badr. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The master of martyrs is Mahja’, and he is the first of this nation to be called to the gates of Paradise. His parents and wife were distressed, so God revealed this verse about them. It was said: And they are not tempted by the commands and prohibitions, because God Almighty commanded them to begin with mere faith, then He imposed upon them prayer, zakat, and all the other laws, which was difficult for some of them, so God revealed this verse.
29:3: Then he consoled them, saying: 3- And We certainly tried those before them, meaning the prophets and believers. Some of them were sawed and some were killed. The Children of Israel were tested by Pharaoh, who subjected them to terrible torment. So God will surely make evident those who are truthful, in their saying, We believe, “and He will surely make evident the liars,” and God knows best about them before the choice. The meaning of the verse is: So God will make evident the truthful from the liars until His knowledge is known. Muqatil said: So they will see God. It was said: So God will distinguish, as He said: So that God will distinguish the wicked from the good (al-Anfal 8:38).
29:4: 4- Or do those who do evil deeds think, meaning polytheism, that they can outsmart Us, that is, defeat Us and escape Us, so that We will not be able to take revenge on them? Evil is what they judge, evil is what they judged when they thought that.
29:5: 5- Whoever hopes to meet God, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said, and Muqatil said: Whoever fears the Resurrection and the Judgment. Hope means fear. Saeed bin Jubair may God be pleased with him said: Whoever hopes for God’s reward, then God’s appointed time will surely come, meaning: what God has promised of reward and punishment. Muqatil said: meaning: the Day of Resurrection will certainly happen. The meaning of the verse is: Whoever fears God or has hope in Him should prepare for Him and work for that day, as He said: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work Al-Kahf 110, And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
29:6: 6- And whoever strives, strives only for himself, for which he will be rewarded. Struggle is patience in the face of hardship, and this can be in war, or it can be against one’s own self. Indeed, God is free from need of the worlds, from their deeds and worship.
29:7: 7- And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds, We will nullify them, meaning: until they become like what they did not do, and removal is replacing the misdeed with the good, and We will reward them with the best of what they used to do, meaning: with their best deeds, which is obedience. It was said: We will give them more than what they did and better, as He said: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof Al-An`am - 160.
29:8: God Almighty says: 8- And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, good treatment, meaning: to be dutiful to them and kind to them. Its meaning is: And We have enjoined upon man to treat his parents with what is good. This verse, which is in Surah Luqman verse 15 and Al-Ahqaf verse 15, was revealed about Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas may God be pleased with him - who is Sa`d ibn Malik Abu Ishaq Al-Zuhri, and his mother is Hamna bint Abi Sufyan ibn Umayya ibn Abd Shams - when he converted to Islam. He was one of the first to embrace Islam and was dutiful to his mother. His mother said to him: What is this religion that you have introduced? By God, I will not eat or drink until you return to what you were following, or I die and you are reproached for that forever, and it is said: O killer of his mother. Then she remained for a day and a night without eating or drinking and without seeking shade. Then she became exhausted. Then she remained for another day and a night without eating or drinking. Then Sa`d came to her and said: O mother, even if there were a hundred souls and they left one by one, I would not abandon my religion, so eat, but if you wish, do not eat. When she despaired of him, she ate and drank. Then God the Most High revealed this verse, and commanded him to be dutiful to his parents and to be kind to them and not to obey them in associating partners with God. This is what God the Most High said: But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. It was stated in the hadith: There is no obedience to any creature in disobedience to God. Then He promised that you would return to Him, saying: To Me you will return, and I will inform you of what you used to do. I will inform you of your good and bad deeds, and I will reward you for them.
29:9: 9- And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them among the righteous, among the group of the righteous, who are the prophets and saints, and it was said: among the entrance of the righteous, which is Paradise.
29:10: God Almighty said: 10- And among the people is he who says, ‘We believe in God,’ but when he is harmed for the sake of God, a calamity befalls him from the people, he is tempted, he considers the trial of the people to be like the punishment of God, meaning: he considers the harm and punishment of the people to be like the punishment of God in the Hereafter, meaning: he is impatient with the punishment of the people and does not have patience with it, so he obeys the people as one who fears His punishment obeys God. This is the saying of Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd, they said: He is the hypocrite who, when he is harmed for the sake of God, turns away from the religion and disbelieves. And if victory comes from your Lord, meaning, a conquest and a state for the believers, they will surely say, meaning, these hypocrites to the believers: Indeed, we were with you, against your enemy, and we were Muslims, and we were Muslims, but we were forced until we said what we said. So God denied them and said: Is not God more knowing of what is in the hearts of the worlds? of faith and hypocrisy.
29:11: 11- And God will surely make known those who believe, who are truthful and remain steadfast in Islam when afflicted, and He will surely make known the hypocrites, who abandon Islam when afflicted. They differed about the revelation of this verse. Mujahid said: It was revealed about people who believed with their tongues, but when they were afflicted with a calamity from people or a misfortune in themselves, they were tempted. Akrima said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: It was revealed about those who were expelled by the polytheists to Badr, and they are the ones about whom the following verse was revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves An-Nisa’ 97. Al-Sha’bi said: These ten verses from the beginning of the Surah to here are Medinan, and the rest of the Surah is Meccan.
29:12: 12- And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, ‘Follow our way.’ Mujahid said: This is from what the disbelievers of Mecca said to those who believed among them. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Abu Sufyan said it to those who believed among Quraysh, ‘Follow our way: our religion and the way of our fathers, and we are responsible for every consequence from God that befalls you.’ This is what His statement, ‘And We will bear your sins,’ means your burdens. Al-Farra’ said: Its wording is a command, but its meaning is a recompense. Its metaphor is: If you follow our way, We will bear your sins, like His statement, ‘Then let the sea throw him up onto the shore.’ (Ta-Ha: 39). It was said: It is a subjunctive mood based on a command, as if they ordered themselves to do that, but God, the Almighty, denied them and said, ‘And they will not bear any of their sins. Indeed, they are liars,’ regarding what they said about bearing their sins.
29:13: 13- And they will bear their own burdens, meaning the burdens of their own deeds, and burdens besides their own burdens, meaning the burdens of those they led astray and obstructed from the path of God, along with their own burdens. Similar to this is the Almighty’s statement: That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection and also some of the burdens of those whom they led astray without knowledge (Al-Hall: 25). And that they may be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent, a question of rebuke and rebuke.
29:14: God Almighty said: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, and then the flood seized them, so they drowned, while they were wrongdoers. Ibn Abbas said: polytheists.
29:15: 15- So We saved him and the companions of the ship, meaning from drowning, and made it, meaning the ship, a sign, meaning a lesson, for the worlds, for it remained on Mount Judi for a long time. It was also said: We made their punishment for drowning a lesson. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Noah was sent for forty years, and he remained among his people calling them for a thousand years less fifty, and he lived sixty years after the flood until people increased and became widespread, and his age was one thousand and fifty years.
29:16: God Almighty says: 16- And Abraham, meaning: We sent Abraham, when he said to his people, ‘Worship God and fear Him,’ obey God and fear Him, that is better for you, if you only knew.
29:17: 17- You only worship idols besides God, statues, and you invent falsehood, you tell lies. Mujahid said: You make idols with your own hands and call them gods. Indeed, those you worship besides God do not possess for you any provision, they are not able to provide for you, so seek, so ask, “with God is provision, and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.”
29:18: 18- And if you deny, then nations before you denied, such as Aad, Thamud, and others, and they were destroyed, and the Messenger’s duty is only to convey clearly.
29:19: 19- Have they not seen how God begins creation? How He creates them initially as a drop of semen, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then He returns him in the Hereafter at the resurrection. Indeed, that is easy for God.
29:20: 20 - Say, ‘Travel through the land and observe how He began creation.’ So look at their dwellings and their traces, how He began their creation. Then God will produce the final creation. That is, then God, who created it, will produce it a second creation after death. Just as it was not impossible for Him to produce it at first, it is not impossible for Him to produce it again. Ibn Kathir and Abu Omar read: Al-Nash’ah with a fat-ha on the shin and extended wherever it occurs. The others read it with a sukoon on the shin and shortened, similar to Al-Raafa and Al-Ra’fah. God is capable of everything.
29:21: 22- He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.
29:22: 22- And you will not cause failure on earth or in heaven. If it is said: What is the point of his saying: nor in heaven and the address to humans, and they are not in heaven? Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is that there is no miracle in the heavens, like the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit: So whoever among you satirizes the Messenger of God, praises him, and supports him, it is the same. He meant: Who praises Him and who supports Him? So he implied who, meaning: The people of the earth cannot defeat Him on earth, nor the people of the heavens in the heavens. Qatrib said: Its meaning is: You cannot defeat Him on earth or in the heavens, even if you were there, like a man saying: So-and-so cannot escape me here or in Basra, meaning: nor in Basra, even if he were there. And you have besides God no protector or helper, meaning: no protector to protect you from Me, nor helper to defend you from My punishment.
29:23: 23- And those who disbelieve in the signs of God and the meeting with Him, in the Qur’an and in the Resurrection, those have despaired of My mercy, in My Paradise, and those will have a painful punishment. These verses are a reminder and warning to the people of Mecca, and they are interjected in the story of Abraham.
29:24: Then He, the Most High, said: 24- And the only answer of his people was that they said, ‘Kill him or burn him.’ But God saved him from the Fire, and made it cool and safe for him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe, who believe.
29:25: 25- And he said, meaning Abraham to his al-Nas 114:You have only taken idols besides God out of affection between you. Ibn Kathir, Al-Kisa’i, Abu Amr, and Ya’qub read: affection in the nominative case without a tanween, between you in the genitive case with the addition of the meaning: Those whom you have taken idols besides God are affection between you, in the life of this world, then it ends and is of no benefit in the hereafter. Hamza and Hafs put the word mawaddah in the accusative case without a tanween, as an addition to the word itkhidāt being used on it. Others read it as mawaddah with the accusative ending baynakum meaning: You only took these idols as a form of affection between you in this worldly life, coming together to worship them and continuing to worship them in this world. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and curse others. The idols will disown their worshippers, the leaders will disown their followers, and the followers will curse the leaders. And your refuge, all of you worshippers and those worshipped, will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.
29:26: 25- So Lot believed him, meaning: he believed him, and he was the first to believe Abraham, who was his nephew, and he said, meaning Abraham, Indeed, I will emigrate to my Lord, so he emigrated from Kufa, which was from the black lands of Kufa, to Harran, then to Ash-Sham, and with him were Lot and his wife Sarah, and he was the first to emigrate. Muqatil said: Abraham, peace be upon him, emigrated when he was seventy-five years old, Indeed, it is He who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
29:27: 27- And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob, and placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book. It is said that God did not send a prophet after Abraham except from his descendants. And We gave him his reward in this world. This is the good praise that all people of religions support. Al-Suddi said: It is the righteous son. It was also said that he saw his place in Paradise. And indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. This means: in the company of the righteous. Ibn Abbas said: Like Adam and Noah.
29:28: God Almighty said: 28- “And Lot, when he said to his people, ‘Indeed you’ - Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr read: ‘Indeed you’ with the interrogative, and the rest read it without the interrogative, and they agreed on the interrogative of the second, ‘to commit an immorality’ - which is committing men, ‘which no one in the world has preceded you with.’”
29:29: 29- Do you indeed approach men and block the way? This is because they were committing indecency with the travelers who passed by them, so the people did not allow them to pass by. It was also said: You block the way of offspring by preferring men over women, and you commit evil in your assemblies, the club, the assembly, and the forum: the assembly of the people and their speaker. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Al-Abbas bin Sahl bin Muhammad Al-Marwazi told us, my maternal grandfather Abu Al-Hasan Al-Mahmoudi told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Khuzaymah told us, that Bishr bin Muadh told them, Yazid bin Zurai’ told us, Hatim bin Abi Saghira told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Abu Salih, the freed slave of Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib, on the authority of Umm Hani’, she said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his statement: And you commit evil in your assemblies. I said: What evil did they commit? He said: They would throw pebbles at the people of the streets and mock them. It is narrated that they would sit in their gatherings, and every man would have a bowl of pebbles with him. If a passerby passed by them, they would throw them at him, and whoever of them got it had the most right to it. It was said that he would take what he had with him and marry him, and fine him three dirhams, and they had a judge for that. Al-Qasim bin Muhammad said: They used to fart in their gatherings. Mujahid said: They used to have intercourse with each other in their gatherings. On the authority of Abdullah bin Salam, he said: Some of them would spit on each other. On the authority of Makhul, he said: Among the behaviors of the people of Lot were chewing gum, applying henna to their fingers, untying their lower garments, whistling, slandering, and sodomy. The response of his people, when Lot denounced the shameful deeds they were doing, was only that they said, mockingly: Bring us the punishment of God, if you should be of the truthful, that the punishment was about to descend upon us. So at that point.
29:30: 30- He said, Lot: My Lord, help me against the corrupt people, by fulfilling my words about the punishment.
29:31: 31- And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, from God, of Isaac and Jacob, they said, ‘Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city,’ meaning the people of Lot, and the city was Sodom, indeed, its people were wrongdoers.
29:32: 32- He said, Abraham said to the messengers: “Indeed, Lot is in it. They said,” meaning: The angels said: “We know best who is in it. We will surely save him.” Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read: We will surely save him with a light pronunciation, and the rest read it with a heavy pronunciation, and his family, except his wife, who was among those who remained behind, meaning: those who remained in the punishment.
29:33: 33- And when Our messengers came to Lot, he thought they were human, he was distressed by them and was distressed by them, by their coming, and they said, ‘Do not fear,’ from your people against Us, “and do not grieve,’ by Our destruction of them, Indeed, We will save you and your family, except your wife; she will be among those who remain behind. Ibn Kathir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Abu Bakr, and Ya’qub read: saving you with a light pronunciation, and the others read it with a heavy pronunciation.
29:34: 34- Indeed, We will send down, Ibn Amir read it with emphasis, and the others read it with emphasis, upon the people of this town a punishment, a torment, from the sky, Muqatil said: subsidence and stones, because they were defiant.
29:35: 35- And We have certainly left among them, of the cities of Lot, a clear sign, a clear lesson, for a people who understand, who ponder the signs as people of understanding do. Ibn Abbas said: The clear sign is the traces of their ruined homes. Qatada said: They are the stones with which they were destroyed, which God left until the first of this nation saw them. Mujahid said: They are the appearance of black water on the surface of the earth.
29:36: 36- And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu`ayb, meaning: And We sent to Madyan their brother Shu`ayb, and he said, ‘O my people, worship God and hope for the Last Day,’ meaning: and fear, and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
29:37: 37- But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became within their homes, fallen down.
29:38: 38- And ‘Aad and Thamud, meaning: We destroyed ‘Aad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you, O people of Mecca, from their dwellings, their homes in Al-Hijr and Yemen, and Satan made their deeds pleasing to them and averted them from the path, from the path of truth, while they were seeing clearly. Muqatil, Al-Kalbi, and Qatadah said: They were conceited about their religion and their misguidance, thinking that they were on the right path, while they were on falsehood. The meaning is that they were seeing clearly in their own eyes. Al-Farra’ said: They were wise and insightful.
29:39: 39- And Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman, meaning: We destroyed these people, and Moses had already come to them with clear proofs, with evidence, but they were arrogant in the land and were not forerunners, meaning: they were not able to escape Our punishment.
29:40: 40- “So We seized each one for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones,” meaning the people of Lot. Haasib is the wind that carries pebbles, which are small pebbles. And among them were those whom the blast seized, meaning Thamud. And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, meaning Qarun and his companions. And among them were those whom We drowned, meaning the people of Noah, Pharaoh and his people. And God would not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.
29:41: 41- The parable of those who take protectors other than God, meaning idols, hoping for their support and benefit, is like that of the spider who takes a home, for herself to take refuge in. Its home is extremely weak and frail, and does not protect it from heat or cold. Likewise, idols do not possess the power to benefit or harm their worshippers. And indeed, the flimsiest of houses is the spider’s home, if they only knew.
29:42: 42- Indeed, God knows whatever they call upon besides Him, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. The people of Basra and Asim read: they call upon with the letter ya to mention the nations before it, and the others read it with the letter ta.
29:43: 43- And these are examples, similarities, and example: a common statement that includes comparing the other to the first, meaning: the examples of the Qur’an with which He likened the conditions of the infidels of this nation to the conditions of the infidels of the previous nations, We present them, we explain them, to the people, Muqatil said: to the infidels of Mecca, and none understands them except those of knowledge, meaning: none understands the examples except the scholars who understand from God. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told us, Ibn Barzah told us, Al-Harith Ibn Abi Usamah told us, Dawud Ibn Al-Muhber told us, Ibad Ibn Kathir told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ and Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘And these examples We present to the people, but none grasps them except those of knowledge.’ He said: The knowledgeable one is he who understands what God says, acts in obedience to Him, and avoids His wrath.”
29:44: God Almighty says: 44- God created the heavens and the earth in truth, meaning: for the truth and to demonstrate the truth. Indeed in that, in their creation, is a sign, indicating for the believers, of His power and His Oneness.
29:45: 45- Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, meaning the Qur’an, “and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing.” Immorality is what is ugly among deeds, and wrongdoing is what is not known in the Sharia. Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas said: In prayer there is a limit and a deterrent from the sins of God. So whoever’s prayer does not command him to do good and forbid him from evil, his prayer will only increase his distance from God. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: Whoever’s prayer does not prevent him from indecency and wrongdoing, his prayer will be a burden on him. It was narrated on the authority of Anas that he said: “There was a young man from the Ansar who used to pray the five daily prayers with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would not leave any indecency without committing it. He described his condition to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘His prayer will stop him one day.’ But it was not long before he repented and his condition improved.” Ibn Awn said: The meaning of the verse is that prayer prevents its performer from indecency and wrongdoing as long as he is performing it. It was said: By prayer he meant the Qur’an, as God Almighty said: And do not recite aloud your prayer Al-Isra’ 110, meaning: in your recitation, and he meant that he recites the Qur’an in prayer, so the Qur’an forbids him from indecency and wrongdoing. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shureih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Ja’d told us, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “A man said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: A man recites the Qur’an all night, and when morning comes he steals. He said: His recitation will stop him.” In another narration, it was said: O Messenger of God, so-and-so prays during the day and steals at night. He said: His prayer deters him. The Almighty says: And the remembrance of God is greater, meaning: the remembrance of God is the best act of obedience. Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri informed us, Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bishran informed us in Baghdad, Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Safwan al-Barda’i informed us, Abu Bakr Abd God ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya informed us, Harun ibn Ma’ruf Abu Ali al-Dharir informed us, Anas ibn Ayyad informed us, Abd God ibn Sa’id ibn Abi Hind informed us, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, the client of Abd God ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Abu Tajriya, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Lord, the highest of them in your degrees, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike your necks? ’ They said: ‘What is that, O Messenger of God? ’ He said: ‘Remembrance of God. ’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abu Al-Aswad told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Darraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Samh, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was asked, ‘Which of the servants will have the highest degree with God on the Day of Resurrection?’ He said, ‘Those who remember God often.’ They said, ‘O Messenger of God, and who fights in the cause of God?’ He said, ‘Even if he were to strike the infidels and polytheists with his sword until it breaks or is covered in blood, the one who remembers God often would be higher in degree than him.’” We narrated that an Arab said: O Messenger of God, which deeds are best? He said: To leave this world while your tongue is moist with the remembrance of God. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad Al-Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj Al-Qushayri told us, Umayya bin Bastam Al-Aishi told us, Yazid told us, meaning bin Zurai’, Rawh bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was traveling on the road to Mecca and passed by a mountain called Jamdan. He said: ‘Go on, this is Jamdan. The solitary men have gone ahead.’ They said: ‘And who are the solitary men, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘The men and women who remember God often.’” Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Khallad ibn Aslam told us, al-Nadr told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I bear witness that Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa’id bore witness that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No people sit remembering God except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and God mentions them to those who are with Him. Some people said: The meaning of His statement, And the remembrance of God is greater is: God’s remembrance of you is better than your remembrance of Him. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is the opinion of Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr. It is also narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ata’ said in his statement: Prayer prohibits indecency and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of God is greater, he said: The remembrance of God is greater than to remain with sin. “And God knows what you do,” Ata’ said: He means that nothing is hidden from Him.
29:46: God the Almighty said: 46- And do not argue with the People of the Scripture, do not quarrel with them, except in a way that is best, that is, by the Qur’an and calling to God with His verses and pointing out His proofs. And by those who pay the jizyah, He meant except those who commit injustice among them, that is, those who refuse to pay the jizyah and wage war, so argue with them with the sword until they submit or pay the jizyah. The metaphor of the verse is: except those who wrong you, because all of them are unjust by disbelief. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: They are the people of war and those with whom there is no treaty. Qatadah and Muqatil said: It was abrogated by His statement: Fight those who do not believe in God (al-Tawbah 9:29). And say, ‘We believe in that which was revealed to us and revealed to you.’ He means that if one of them tells you before the jizyah something from what is in their books, do not argue with him about it, and do not believe them or disbelieve them, and say, We believe in that which was revealed to us and revealed to you. “Our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims in submission to Him.” Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Muhammad ibn Abd God al-Nu’aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Ismail informed us, Muhammad ibn Bashar informed us, Uthman ibn Umar informed us, Ali ibn al-Mubarak informed us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic for the people of Islam. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not believe the People of the Book and do not disbelieve them, and say: We believe in God and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to you.” Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmad At-Tahiri told us, Abd Al-Samad bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Bazzaz told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Dabry told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar bin Al-Zuhri told us, Ibn Abi Namlah Al-Ansari told us that his father Abu Namlah Al-Ansari told him: “While he was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a Jewish man came to him and a funeral procession passed by and said: ‘O Muhammad, does this funeral procession speak?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God knows best.’ The Jew said: ‘It speaks.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whatever the People of the Book tell you, do not believe them or disbelieve them. Say: ‘We believe in God, His Books, and His Messengers.’ If it is false, you will not believe it, but if it is true, you will not disbelieve it.”
29:47: God Almighty says: 47- And thus, meaning: just as We sent down the Book to them, “We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. So those to whom We gave the Book believe in it,” meaning: the believers among the People of the Book, Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions, and among these, meaning: the people of Mecca, are those who believe in it, and they are the believers among the people of Mecca, and none reject Our signs except the disbelievers. This is because the Jews knew that Muhammad was a prophet and that the Qur’an was true, so they rejected. Qatada said: Denial only occurs after knowledge.
29:48: 48- And you did not recite, O Muhammad, before it any Scripture, before We sent down the Scripture to you, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand, nor write it, meaning: you did not read or write before the revelation, then the falsifiers would have had doubts, meaning if you had been writing or reading the scriptures before the revelation, the falsifiers, the polytheists of Mecca, would have had doubts and said: He reads it from the scriptures of the ancients and copies it from them, said Qatada. Muqatil said: The falsifiers are the Jews, and its meaning is: if they would have doubted you and accused you, and said that the one we find described in the Torah as illiterate, he does not read or write, but this is not the case.
29:49: 49- Rather, they are clear signs, Al-Hasan said: meaning the Qur’an is clear signs, in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge, meaning the believers who have carried the Qur’an. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, and Qatada said: Rather, he - meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace - has clear signs in the hearts of those among the People of the Book who were given knowledge, because they find him with his description and attributes in their books, And none reject Our signs except the wrongdoers.
29:50: 50- And they said, ‘Why were not signs sent down to him from his Lord?’ as were sent down to the prophets before. Ibn Kathir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr read: A sign of monotheism. The others read: Signs from his Lord, based on the Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘The signs are only with God,’ and He is able to send them if He wills, and I am only a clear warner. I warn the people of disobedience of the Fire, and the sending down of signs is not in my hands.
29:51: 51- Was it not sufficient for them, this is the answer to his saying: Why were not verses sent down to him from his Lord? He said: Was it not sufficient for them that We sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Meaning: Was it not sufficient for them from the verses of the Qur’an which is recited to them? Indeed in that, in the sending down of the Qur’an, is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe, meaning: a reminder and an admonition for those who believe and act upon it.
29:52: 52- Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you.’ I am His Messenger and this Qur’an is His book. “He knows what is in the heavens and the earth. And those who believe in falsehood” Ibn Abbas said: in other than God. Muqatil said: in the worship of Satan, and disbelieve in God - those are the losers.
29:53: 53- And they urge you to hasten the punishment. This verse was revealed about Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith when he said: Then rain down upon us stones from the sky. “And were it not for a specified term,” Ibn Abbas said: “I did not promise you that I would not punish your people or eradicate them and delay their punishment until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: “Rather, the Hour is their appointed time.” (al-Qamar 54:46). Ad-Dahhak said: The duration of their lives, because when they die they will be punished. It was said: On the day of Badr, The punishment would have come upon them and it will come upon them, meaning: the punishment, and it was said: the term, suddenly while they are not aware, of its coming.
29:54: 54- They urge you to hasten the punishment, he repeated it to emphasize, and Hell will surely encompass the disbelievers, gathering them together so that not one of them will remain without entering it.
29:55: 55- The Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, meaning: When the punishment covers them, Hell will surround them, as He said: For them is a bed of Hell and above them are coverings (al-A’raf 7:41), And He will say, ‘Taste,’ Nafi’ and the people of Kufa read: And He will say, ‘Taste,’ meaning: And the one in charge of their punishment will say to them: Taste, and the others read it with a nun, because since it was by His command, it was attributed to Him, for what you used to do, meaning: the reward for what you used to do.
29:56: 56- O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship Me. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed regarding the weak Muslims of Mecca. He said: If you are in difficulty in Mecca showing faith, then leave it for the land of Medina, for My earth - meaning Medina - is spacious and safe. Mujahed said: The land of Medina is vast, so they migrated and fought there. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: If someone commits sins in a land, then leave it, for My land is vast. Ata' said: If you are ordered to commit sins, then flee, for My land is vast. Likewise, anyone who is in a land where sins are committed and is unable to change that must migrate to a place where he can worship. It was said: It was revealed about a people who had not emigrated to Mecca, and they said: We fear, if we emigrate, hunger and hardship of living, so God revealed this verse and did not excuse them for not leaving. Mutraf bin Abdullah said: My land is vast, meaning: My provision is vast for you, so go out.
29:57: 57- Every soul will taste death, fearing death to make migration easier for them, meaning: everyone will die wherever they are, so do not stay in the land of polytheism for fear of death, Then to Us you will be returned, so We will reward you for your deeds, and Abu Bakr read: they will return with the letter ya.
29:58: 58- And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely assign to them lofty chambers in Paradise, Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a silent tha’ without a hamza. It is said: a man stayed if he stayed, and athwaytuhu if you put him in a house where he will stay. The others read it with a ba’ and a fatha and a shaddah on the waw and a hamza after it, meaning: We will surely assign them lofty chambers in Paradise, “beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Excellent is the reward of the workers.”
29:59: 59- Those who are patient, in the face of hardships and do not abandon their religion because of the severity that befell them, and upon their Lord rely, they depend.
29:60: 60- And how many a creature carries not its own provision," that is, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the believers who were in Mecca and who had been harmed by the polytheists: Migrate to Medina. They said: How can we go to Medina while we have neither a home nor money there? Who will feed us and give us drink there? So God revealed: "And how many a creature that needs food, carries not its own provision," that is, it does not take its provision with it nor does it store anything for tomorrow like livestock and birds. "God provides for it and for you," wherever you are. "And He is the Hearing, the Knowing," the Hearer of your words: We do not find anything to spend in Medina, the Knower of what is in your hearts. Sufyan said on the authority of Ali bin Al-Aqmar: And how many an animal does not carry its sustenance? He said: It does not save anything for tomorrow. Sufyan said: Nothing of God’s creation is hidden except man, mouse, and ant. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shuraihi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi told us, Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq told us, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz told us, Ismail ibn Zararah al-Raqi told us, Abu al-Atuf al-Jarrah ibn Munhal told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Riyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I entered with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, into one of the gardens of the Ansar, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to pick up dates with his hand and eat, and he said: Eat, O Ibn Umar, I said: I do not desire it, O Messenger of God, he said: But I desire it, and this is the fourth morning since I have not eaten food and I have not found it, so I said: We belong to God, God is the one sought for help, he said: O Ibn Umar, if I asked my Lord, He would give me the likes of the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar, many times over, but I go hungry one day and satiated the next, so what will you do, O Ibn Umar, if you live long and remain among the dregs of people who hide a year’s provision and certainty is weak, so the verse was revealed: And how many an animal carries nothing "Rizqha" the verse. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Hussein bin Ahmad Al-Mukhalidi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Sarraj told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Jaafar bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Thabit, “on the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not save anything for tomorrow.” We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you were to trust in God as He should be trusted, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds that go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening with full crops. Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Muzaffari told us, Abu Saeed Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Faqih told us, Abu Nasr ibn Hamduyah al-Mutawwa’i told us, Abu al-Muwajjah Muhammad ibn Urwah told us, Abdun told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ismail, he is the son of Abu Khalid, on the authority of two men, one of them Zubayd al-Yami, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “O people, there is nothing that brings you closer to Paradise and distances you from the Fire except that I have commanded you to do it, and there is nothing that brings you closer to the Fire and distances you from Paradise except that I have forbidden you from it. The Trustworthy Spirit has whispered in my heart that no soul dies until it has received its provision, so fear God and be fair in seeking it, and do not let the slowness of provision lead you to seek it by disobeying God, because what is with God can only be attained by obeying Him.” Hisham said, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud.
29:61: God Almighty says: And if you ask them, meaning the infidels of Mecca, who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they will surely say, ‘God,’ so how are they deluded?
29:62: 62- “God expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for whom He wills. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things.”
29:63: 63- And if you ask them, ‘Who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ This is because the doer of these things is God. But most of them do not reason. It was said: Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ This is because they acknowledge that the argument is binding upon them. But most of them do not reason. They deny monotheism while acknowledging that He is the Creator of these things.
29:64: God Almighty says: 64- And this worldly life is not but diversion and amusement. Diversion is: enjoying the pleasures of this world, and amusement is: fooling around. It was called this because it is fleeting. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the life, meaning: the everlasting, everlasting life. And life means life, meaning: in it is the everlasting life, if they only knew, the passing of this world and the permanence of the Hereafter.
29:65: God Almighty says: 65- So when they embark on a ship, and fear drowning, they supplicate God, devoting their religion to Him alone, and abandon the idols, but when He delivers them to land, at once they associate others with Him, this is a statement of their stubbornness and that when faced with hardships they acknowledge that only God Almighty is able to remove them, but when the hardships are over they return to their disbelief. Ikrimah said: When the people of ignorance embarked on a sea journey, they would carry idols with them, and when the winds became strong, they would throw them into the sea and say, O Lord, O Lord.
29:66: 66- So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them. This is the lam of command, and its meaning is threat and warning, like His saying: Do whatever you will Fussilat 40, so that they may deny the blessing of God in saving them, and that they may enjoy themselves. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a sukoon on the lam, and the rest read it with a kasra, in accordance with His saying: So that they may disbelieve. “So they will know.” It was said that whoever breaks the lam makes it a lam of ki, and likewise in So that they may disbelieve. The meaning is that there is no benefit for them in associating partners with God except disbelief and enjoying what they enjoy in this world without a share in the Hereafter.
29:67: 67- Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched away all around them, meaning the Arabs, taking each other captive, while the people of Mecca are safe, is it then in falsehood, meaning idols and Satan, that they believe and in the favor of God, meaning Muhammad and Islam, that they disbelieve?
29:68: 68- And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God, claiming that God has a partner and that He has commanded immoral acts, or denies the truth, about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an, “when it has come to him. Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?” An interrogative with the meaning of confirmation, meaning: Is there not a home for this disbelieving denier in Hell?
29:69: 69- And those who strive for Us, those who strive against the polytheists to support our religion, We will surely guide them to Our ways, we will surely make them steadfast in what they fought for. It was said: We will increase their guidance, as He said: And God increases those who are guided in guidance Maryam 19:76. It was also said: We will guide them to the straight path, and the straight path is the one that leads to the pleasure of God Almighty. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: If people differ, then look at what the people of the borders are doing, for God said: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways. It was said: Jihad is patience in performing acts of obedience. Al-Hasan said: The best form of jihad is opposing one’s desires. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: And those who strive in seeking knowledge, We will surely guide them to the ways of acting upon it. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: And those who strive in establishing the Sunnah, We will surely guide them to the ways of Paradise. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And those who strive in Our obedience, We will surely guide them to the ways of Our reward. “And indeed, God is with the doers of good,” with victory and assistance in this world and with reward and forgiveness in the Hereafter.
30:3: 3- “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land.” The reason for the revelation of this verse, as mentioned by the commentators, is that there was fighting between Persia and the Romans, and the polytheists wanted Persia to defeat the Romans, because the Persians were illiterate Zoroastrians, and the Muslims wanted the Romans to defeat the Persians, because they were People of the Book. So Khosrow sent an army to the Romans and appointed over them a man called Shahrazad, and Caesar sent an army to Persia and appointed over them a man called Yahfs. They met in Adhra’at and Busra, which is the closest part of the Levant to the land of the Arabs and Persians, and Persia defeated the Romans. This reached the Muslims in Mecca, and it was difficult for them, and the infidels of Mecca rejoiced at it, and they said to the Muslims: You are People of the Book, and the Christians are People of the Book, and we are illiterate, and our brothers from the Persians have defeated your brothers from the Romans, and if you fight us, we will defeat you. So God Almighty revealed these verses, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq went out to the infidels and said: You rejoiced By the victory of your brothers, do not rejoice, for by God, they will prevail over Persia, as our Prophet has informed us. Then Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi stood up and said, You have lied. He replied, You are a more lying enemy of God. The Prophet said, “Set a time limit between us, and I will wager on ten camels from me and ten camels from you. If the Romans prevail over Persia, you will lose, and if the Persians prevail, you will lose.” They did so, and set the time limit at three years. Abu Bakr came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him of that, and that was before gambling was forbidden. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “That is not what you have stated. The term ‘munahaba’ is between three and nine years.” So he increased the risk and he extended the time limit. Abu Bakr went out and met Ubayy and said, Perhaps you have regretted it? He said, “No. Come, I will increase the risk and extend the time limit. Make it one hundred camels and one hundred camels, up to nine years, and some say seven years.” He said, I have done it. When Ubayy ibn Khalaf feared that Abu Bakr would leave Mecca, he came to him and stuck to him. He said, I fear that you will leave Mecca, so appoint a guarantor for me. So his son, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, made him a guarantor. When Ubayy ibn Khalaf wanted to leave for Uhud, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr came to him and stuck to him. He said, No, by God, I will not leave you until you give me a guarantor. So he gave him a guarantor. Then he left for Uhud and returned to Ubayy ibn Khalaf, where he died from the wounds inflicted upon him by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when he fought him. The Romans defeated the Persians on the day of Hudaybiyyah, which was at the beginning of seven years of their battle. It was also said that it was on the day of Badr. Al-Sha’bi said: The period of mourning that took place between the people of Mecca, and in it was their gambler Abi bin Khalaf, and the Muslims and their gambler Abu Bakr, and that was before gambling was forbidden, had not passed until the Romans defeated Persia and tied up their horses in Madain and Banu Rum. So Abu Bakr gambled with Abi and took the money of the risk from his heirs, and brought it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Give it in charity. The reason for the Romans’ victory over Persia - according to what Ikrimah and others said - was that after Shahrazad defeated the Romans, he continued to trample them and destroy their cities until he reached the Gulf. One day, while his brother Farrakhan was sitting overlooking the city, he said to his companions: I saw as if I was sitting on the throne of Khosrau. His word reached Khosrau, so he wrote to Shahrazad: When my letter reaches you, send me Farrakhan’s head. So Khosrau wrote to him: “O King, you will not find anyone like Farrakhan. He has a fierce temper and a voice against the enemy, so do not do that.” So Khosrau wrote to him: There are men from Persia who are behind him. So he hurried to bring him his head. Khosrau returned to him, but he became angry and did not answer him. He sent a messenger to the people of Persia saying: I have removed Shahrazad from you and appointed Farrakhan the king over you. Then he gave the messenger a small paper in which he ordered him to kill Shahrazad, and said: If Farrakhan takes over the kingship and his brother submits to him, then give him. So when Shahrazad read the letter, he said: I hear and obey. He got down from his throne, and Farrakhan sat down. He handed him the scroll and said, Bring me Shahrazad. So he brought him forward to behead him. Shahrazad said, Do not hurry me until I write my will. He said, Yes. So he called for the basket and gave him three scrolls and said, I have consulted Khosrau about you for all this time, and you want to kill me with one letter? So he restored the kingdom to his brother. Shahrazad wrote to Caesar, King of the Romans, "I have a need of you that cannot be carried by hail or conveyed by scrolls. Meet me, but do not meet me except with fifty Romans, for I will meet you with fifty Persians." Then Caesar came with 500,000 Romans, and began placing spies before him on the roads. He was afraid that he had been deceived, until his spies informed him that he had only 50 men with him. Then he spread out a tent for them and they met in a brocade tent that had been pitched for them, and each of them had a knife. They called for an interpreter between them. Shahrazad said, "Those who destroyed your cities were my brother and I, with our cunning and bravery. Khosrow envied us and wanted me to kill my brother, but I refused. Then he ordered my brother to kill me, so we have both deposed him, so we will fight him with you." He said, You have both done right. Then one of them gestured to the other that a secret is between two people, and if it passes beyond two people, it is revealed. So they killed the interpreter together with their knives. At that point, the Romans gained victory over the Persians, so they pursued them, killing them. Khosrow died and the report reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and he and those with him rejoiced. This is what God, the Almighty, said: "Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land," meaning: the land of Ash-Sham closest to the land of the Persians. Ikrimah said: It is Adhraat and Kaskar. Mujahid said: The land of Al-Jazira. Muqatil said: Jordan and Palestine. And they, after their defeat, meaning: the Romans from Abd, after the Persians defeated them. Ghalb and ghalba are two words, they will be defeated, Persians.
30:4: 4- In a few years, and a few is between three and seven, and it was said: between three and nine, and it was said: less than ten. Abdullah ibn Umar, Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, Al-Hasan, and Isa ibn Umar read: Ghalaba with a fatha on the ghain and the lam, Sayghalaba with a damma on the yaa and a fatha on the lam. They said: It was revealed when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us of the Romans’ victory over the Persians. The meaning of the verse is: Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans defeated the Persians in the land nearest to you. And after their defeat, they will be victorious. The Muslims will defeat them within a few years. And at the end of this period, the Muslims embarked on a jihad against the Romans. The first is more correct. It is the opinion of most commentators. To God belongs the command before and after, meaning: before the Roman Empire over Persia and after it. So whichever of the two parties is victorious, it is by God’s command, judgment, and decree. And on that Day the believers will rejoice.
30:5: 5- By the victory of God, the Romans over the Persians. Al-Suddi said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers rejoiced at their victory over the polytheists on the day of Badr, and the victory of the People of the Book over the polytheists. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Victorious, the Merciful, to the believers.
30:6: 6- God’s promise, in the accusative case as a source, meaning: God promised a promise that the Romans would prevail over Persia, God does not break His promise, but most people do not know.
