30:7: 7- They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, meaning: the matter of their livelihood, how they earn and trade, when they plant, sow and harvest, and how they build and live. Al-Hasan said: One of them may peck a dirham with the tip of his fingernail and remember its weight without making a mistake, but he does not pray well. And they are heedless of the Hereafter, heedless of it, ignorant of it, they do not think about it and do not work for it.
30:8: 8- Have they not reflected within themselves? God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth, meaning: for the truth, and it was said: to establish the truth, and for a specified term, meaning: for a known time when it ends and is the Day of Resurrection, and indeed, many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers.
30:9: 9- Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? Or have they not traveled through the land and observed the fates of the nations before them and taken heed? They were stronger than them in strength and tilled the land, they plowed it and turned it over for cultivation, and cultivated it more than they cultivated it, meaning: more than the people of Mecca cultivated. It was said that he said that because the people of Mecca did not have plowing, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they did not believe, so God destroyed them. It was not God who wronged them, by diminishing their rights, but they were wronging themselves, by diminishing their rights.
30:10: 10- Then the end of those who did evil, meaning: did evil deeds, was the worst, meaning: the trait that would make them evil, which is the Fire. It was said: the worst is a name for Hell, just as goodness is a name for Paradise, because they lied, meaning: because they lied. It was said that the interpretation of the worst is what follows it, which is His statement: that they denied, meaning: Then the consequence of the wrongdoers was denial, as those evil deeds led them to deny, the signs of God and they used to mock at them. The people of Hijaz and Basra read: consequence in the nominative case, meaning: then the end of their affair was evil. The others read it in the accusative case as the predicate of was, meaning: then the evil was the end of those who did evil.
30:11: 11- God begins creation and then repeats it, meaning: He creates them in the beginning then brings them back to life after death. He did not say: He brings them back, but rather He returned them to creation. Then to Him you will be returned, so He rewards them for their deeds. Abu Amr and Abu Bakr read: they return with a ya, and the others read it with a ta.
30:12: 12- And on the Day the Hour appears, the criminals will be in despair. Qatada and Al-Kalbi said: The polytheists will despair of all good. Al-Farra’ said: Their speech and argument will be cut off. Mujahid said: They will be disgraced.
30:13: 13- And they had no intercessors among their partners, and they were disbelievers in their partners. Denying and disavowing, they disavow it and it disavows them.
30:14: 14- And on the Day the Hour appears, that Day they will be separated, meaning: the people of Paradise will be distinguished from the people of Hell. Muqatil said: They will be separated after the reckoning into Paradise and Hell and will never meet again.
30:15: 15- But as for those who have believed and done righteous deeds, they will be in a garden, meaning a lush garden, rejoicing. Ibn Abbas said: They will be honored. Mujahid and Qatadah said: They will be blessed. Abu Ubaidah said: They will be pleased. And happiness means joy. It was said that happiness in the language means: every good blessing, and improvement means improvement. Al-Awza'i said on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer: You will be delighted by listening to God in Paradise. Al-Awza'i said: When he begins to listen to God, there will not remain a tree in Paradise that will not be visited. He also said: There is no one among God's creation with a better voice than Israfil. When he begins to listen to God, he will interrupt the prayers and glorifications of the inhabitants of the seven heavens.
30:16: 16- And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, meaning: the resurrection on the Day of Resurrection, they will be brought to the punishment.
30:17: God Almighty says: 17- So glory be to God, meaning: glorify God, and its meaning is: pray to God, when you reach the evening, meaning: you enter the evening, which is the sunset and night prayers, and when you rise, meaning: you enter the morning, which is the dawn prayer.
30:18: 18- And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth. Ibn Abbas said: The people of the heavens and the earth praise Him and pray to Him. And in the evening, meaning: Pray to God in the evening, meaning the afternoon prayer. And when you appear, you enter the noon prayer, which is the noon prayer. Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to Ibn Abbas: Do you find the five daily prayers in the Qur'an? He said: Yes. He recited these two verses and said: This verse mentions the five daily prayers and their times. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Sami, the freed slave of Abu Bakr ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Salih al-Samman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says: ‘Glory be to God and His praise’ one hundred times every day, his sins will be forgiven, even if they are like the foam of the sea.” Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Hafs al-Tajir told us, al-Sari ibn Khuzaymah al-Abiwardi told us, al-Mu’alla ibn Sa’d told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of Sami, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says in the morning and in the evening: ‘Glory be to God and His praise,’ one hundred times, no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better than what he has come with, except someone who says the same as he said or more.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, Amara bin Al-Qaqa’ told us, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two phrases are light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to God and His praise, glory be to God the Almighty.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ali bin Al-Madini told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman, the client of the family of Talhah, who said: I heard Kurayb Abu Rashdin narrating on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Juwayriyah bint Al-Harith bin Abi Dharar, “That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out one morning from her house, and her name was Barra, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, changed it and named her Juwayriyah, and he disliked it being said that he went out from Barra, so he went out while she was in the mosque, and returned after the day had risen, and he said: Have you not remained in this place since you left? She said: Yes. He said: After you left, I said four words three times, which, if they were weighed against your words, they would outweigh them: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, the number of His creation, and the pleasure of His soul, and the weight of His throne, and the ink of His words.”
30:19: God Almighty said: 19- “He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. And thus you will be brought out.” Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read: You will be brought out with a fatha on the ta’ and a damma on the ra’. The rest read it with a damma on the ta’ and a fatha on the ra’.
30:20: 20- And among His signs is that He created you from dust, meaning He created your origin, meaning Adam, from dust, then suddenly you were human beings spreading out, spreading out on the earth.
30:21: 21- And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves, it was said: from your kind from among the children of Adam. And it was said: He created Eve from Adam’s rib, that you may dwell in tranquility with them, and He placed between you affection and mercy, He placed affection and mercy between the spouses, so they love and are merciful to one another, and nothing is more beloved to one of them than the other without kinship between them, Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought, in the greatness and power of God.
30:22: 22- And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages, meaning: the diversity of languages, such as Arabic, Persian, and others, and your colors, white, black, and red, and you are the offspring of one man and one woman. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge, Hafs read: for those of knowledge with a kasra on the lam.
30:23: 23- And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day and your seeking of His bounty, meaning: your sleep by night and your seeking of His bounty by day, meaning: your going about seeking a livelihood, Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen, listening with contemplation and consideration.
30:24: 24- And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, causing fear, for the traveler from thunderbolts, and hope, for the resident for rain. And He sends down water from the sky and revives thereby, meaning with rain, the earth after its lifelessness, that is, after its dryness and barrenness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
30:25: 25- And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Ibn Mas`ud said: They stand unsupported by His command. It was also said: They will continue to stand by His command. Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth. Ibn Abbas said: From the graves, at once you will emerge, from it. Most scholars agree that the meaning of the verse is: Then when He calls you with a single call, at once you will emerge from the earth.
30:26: 26- “And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.” Obedient. Al-Kalbi said: This is specific to whoever among them is obedient. Ibn Abbas reported: All are obedient to Him in life, eternity, death, and resurrection, even if they disobey in worship.
30:27: 27- And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, He creates them first then returns them after death for resurrection, and that is easier for Him, said Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khathim, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Al-Kalbi: meaning: It is easy for Him and nothing is difficult for Him, and this is the narration of Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. And Af’al sometimes comes in the sense of the doer, as in the saying of Al-Farazdaq. He who made the sky high built for us a house whose pillars are stronger and taller Meaning: tall and dear. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: It is easier for him: meaning: easier. The reason for this is that it is a way of giving an example, meaning: it is easier for him according to what occurs in your minds, because what occurs in people’s minds is that repetition is easier than creation, meaning: beginning. It was said: It is easier for him than you. It was said: It is easier for Him, meaning: for creation, they will rise with one shout, so it is easier for them than being sperm, then a clot, then a lump of flesh until they become men and women. This is the meaning of the narration of Ibn Hibban on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas. To Him belongs the highest description, meaning the highest attribute, in the heavens and the earth. Ibn Abbas said: It means that there is nothing like Him. Qatada said: It means that there is no god but Him, and He is the Exalted in Might, in His kingdom, the Wise, in His creation.
30:28: 28- He has given you an example from yourselves, that is, He has shown you a similarity to your own condition, and that example is from yourselves. Then He explained the example and said: Do you have from those whom your right hands possess, that is, your male and female slaves, partners in what We have provided for you, of wealth, so that you and they are equal in it, that is, do your slaves share with you in your wealth that We have given you, fearing them as you fear yourselves, that is, you fear that they will share with you in your wealth and divide it with you, just as a free man fears his free partner in wealth, so that he may be alone in it in a matter that is not his, and just as a man fears his partner in inheritance, even though he wants to be alone in it. Ibn Abbas said: You fear that they will inherit you as you inherit one another. If you do not fear this from your slaves and are not satisfied with that for yourselves, then how can you be satisfied that the gods you worship are my partners and they are my slaves? The meaning of his saying: yourselves, meaning: your equals among the free people, as in his saying: The believing men and believing women think well of themselves (al-Nur 24:12), meaning: of their equals. Thus do We detail the verses for a people who understand, who look at these proofs with their minds.
30:29: 29- Rather, those who do wrong follow their own desires, who associate others with God, without knowledge, out of ignorance of what is required of them. So who can guide one whom God has led astray? That is, whom God has led astray. And they will have no helpers, who will protect them from the punishment of God Almighty.
30:30: God the Almighty said: 30- So set your face toward the religion, meaning: make your religion sincere for God, as Saeed bin Jubair said. Setting the face means establishing the religion. Another said: make your actions righteous. The face is that toward which a person turns, and his religion and actions are among those toward which he turns to straighten them, upright, inclined and upright toward it, the fitrah of God, the religion of God, and it is the accusative of enticement, meaning: adhere to the fitrah of God, upon which He created mankind, meaning: He created mankind upon it. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas and a group of commentators that what is meant by fitrah is the religion, which is Islam. Some people said that the verse is specific to believers, who are those whom God created as Muslims: Abu Ali Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah told us, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Everyone is born in a state of fitrah natural disposition, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as you breed an animal. Do you find among them any whose mutilated parts are such that you yourselves mutilate them?” They said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of one who dies while he is young? He said: God knows best what they would have done. Al-Zuhri narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, without mentioning the one who dies while he is young. He added: Then Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish: The nature of God upon which He has created mankind. His statement, Whoever is born is born upon the fitrah, meaning upon the covenant that God took from them when He said, Am I not your Lord? They will say, Yes. (al-A’raf 7:172). Every newborn in the world has this affirmation, which is the Hanafi school of thought upon which creation occurred, even if someone other than Him is worshipped. God the Almighty said, And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ (al-Zukhruf 43:87), and they will say, We only worship them that they may bring us closer to God. (al-Zumar 39:3). However, innate faith is of no consequence in worldly rulings. Rather, what is considered is the religious faith that is commanded and acquired through will and action. Don’t you see that he says, Then his parents made him a Jew? So, even though he has innate faith, he is ruled by the ruling of his disbelieving parents. This is the meaning of the Prophet’s statement, peace and blessings be upon him, God the Almighty says, ‘Indeed, I created My servants as Hanifs, but the devils led them astray from their religion.’ This meaning is also narrated from Al-Awza’i and Hammad ibn Salamah. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak that he said: The meaning of the hadith is that every newborn is born in his fitrah, that is, in the way he was created in the knowledge of God Almighty, whether for happiness or misery. So each of them will eventually become what he was created with, and will behave in this world with actions that are inconsistent with it. So among the signs of misery for a child is that he is born to a Jew or a Christian, and they will make him - because of his misery - believe in their religion. It was said: Its meaning is that every newborn is born at the beginning of creation in a state of fitrah, that is, with a sound nature and disposition prepared to accept religion. If he were left in this state, he would continue to adhere to it, because this religion is present and its beauty is in the minds. Only those who turn away from it and turn to something else turn away from it due to a defect of the defects of upbringing and imitation. If he were saved from those defects, he would not believe in anything else... Then we take as an example the children of the Jews and Christians and their following of their fathers and inclination towards their religions, and thus they stray from the sound nature and the straight path. Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi mentioned these meanings in his book. His statement: There is no changing the creation of God. Whoever interprets the fitrah as referring to religion says: It means there is no changing the religion of God. It is a statement with the meaning of a prohibition, i.e., do not change the religion of God. Mujahid and Ibrahim said: The meaning of the verse is: Adhere to the fitrah of God, i.e., the religion of God, and follow it and do not exchange monotheism for polytheism. That is the right religion, i.e., the straight one, but most people do not know. It was said: There is no change in God’s creation, meaning: what man was created with of happiness and misery does not change, so the happy person does not become miserable and the miserable person does not become happy. Ikrimah and Mujahid said: It means the prohibition of castrating animals.
30:31: 31- turning to Him meaning: So turn your face, you and your nation, turning to Him, because addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, includes the nation with him, as He said: O Prophet, when you divorce women At-Talaq 1, turning to Him meaning: returning to Him in repentance and approaching Him in obedience, and fear Him and establish prayer and do not be among those who associate others with God.
30:32: 32- Of those who divided their religion and became sects, meaning: they became different sects, and they are the Jews and Christians. It was said: they are the people of innovations from this nation, Every faction rejoices in what it has, meaning: satisfied with what it has.
30:33: God Almighty says: 33- And when harm touches people, drought and hardship, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him, turning to Him in supplication, then when He gives them a taste of mercy from Him, fertility and blessings, at once a party of them associate others with their Lord.
30:34: 34- So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them. Then He addressed those who did this with a threatening tone, saying: Then enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know, your condition in the Hereafter.
30:35: 35- Or have We sent down to them authority? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: An argument and an excuse. Qatada said: A book, so it speaks, utters, about what they used to associate, meaning: it takes action against their association and commands them to do it.
30:36: 36- And when We let people taste mercy, meaning fertility and abundant rain, they rejoice therein, meaning the joy of arrogance, but if evil befalls them, meaning drought and little rain, and it is said: fear and calamity, because of what their hands have put forth, of evil deeds, at once they despair, they lose hope in the mercy of God. This is contrary to the description of the believer, for he thanks God when he is blessed, and hopes in his Lord when he is in difficulty.
30:37: 37- Have they not seen that God extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
30:38: God Almighty says: 38- So give the relative his right, of kindness and kinship, and the needy, whose right is that charity be given to him, and the wayfarer, meaning the traveler, and it was said that he is the weak one. That is best for those who desire the countenance of God, seeking God’s reward for what they do, and those are the successful.
30:39: God the Almighty said: 39- And whatever you give in interest, Ibn Kathir read: You give in a shortened form, while others read it with a long vowel, meaning: You gave. Whoever shortens it means: What you give in interest, and their giving it is in the form of giving, just as you say: I gave something wrong, and I gave something right. So it leads in meaning to the saying of whoever lengthens it. So that it may increase in the wealth of the people, the people of Medina and Ya’qub read: So that it may increase in the wealth of the people, with the ta’ and a damma and a sukoon on the waw for addressing, meaning: So that you may increase and be patient with an increase in the wealth of the people. The others read it with the ya’ and a fatha, and they put the waw in the accusative case and made the verb for interest because of His saying: So that it does not increase with God, in the wealth of the people, meaning: in snatching the wealth of the people and attracting it. They differed on the meaning of the verse. Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Tawus, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and most of the commentators said: It is a man who gives a gift to another in order to receive more in return. This is permissible and lawful, but he will not be rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s statement: It will not increase with God. This was forbidden to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in particular, because God, the Almighty, said: And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return (al-Muddaththir 74:6). That is, do not give and then ask for more than you were given. Al-Nakha’i said: It is a man who gives to his friend or relative to increase his wealth, without seeking the pleasure of God. Al-Sha’bi said: It is a man who sticks to another man, serves him, and travels with him, so he makes his money’s profit seeking his support, not for the sake of God, so it does not increase with God because he did not do it for the sake of God Almighty. And whatever you give in zakat, you give in charity, seek[ing] the countenance of God - it is those who will receive a multiplication, the reward will be multiplied for them, so they will be given ten times the like of a good deed. So the multiplied is the one who has many good deeds. The Arabs say: The people are lean and fat: if their camels become lean or fat.
30:40: 40- “God is He who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you to life. Is there among your associates any who do any of that? Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.”
30:41: God the Almighty said: 41- Corruption has appeared on land and sea, meaning: drought and scarcity of vegetation. By land He meant the deserts and open spaces, and by sea He meant the cities and villages that are on running water. Ikrimah said: The Arabs call a land a sea, saying: the land has become barren and the supply of the sea has been cut off, because of what the hands of people have earned, meaning: because of the evil of their sins. Atiyah and others said: The land is the surface of the earth from cities and others, and the sea is the well-known sea, and the scarcity of rain affects the land as it affects the sea, so the insides of shells become empty because when the rain comes, the shell rises to the surface of the sea and opens its mouth, and whatever rain falls into its mouth turns into pearls. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Mujahid said: Corruption on land means one of the sons of Adam killing his brother, and at sea means the usurpation of a ship by an unjust king. Ad-Dahhak said: The earth was green and luxuriant, and no son of Adam would come to a tree without finding fruit on it. The seawater was fresh, and lions would not attack cows or sheep. But when Cain killed Abel, the earth trembled, the trees quaked, the seawater became salty and bitter, and the animals attacked each other. Qatada said: This was before the mission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The earth was filled with injustice and misguidance. Then, when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, some people returned with the sins that their hands had committed, meaning the infidels of Mecca. That He may let them taste some of what they have done, that is, the punishment of some of the sins they have committed, that they may return, from disbelief and their evil deeds.
30:42: 42- Say, ‘Travel through the land and observe what was the end of those before,’ so that you may see their homes and dwellings empty, ‘most of them were polytheists,’ meaning: they were polytheists, but they were destroyed because of their disbelief.
30:43: 43- So direct your face toward the right religion, the straight religion, which is the religion of Islam, before there comes a Day from God that cannot be repelled, meaning: the Day of Resurrection, when no one will be able to repel it from God. On that Day they will be divided, meaning: they will be separated, a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze.
30:44: 44- Whoever disbelieves, his disbelief will be upon him, meaning: the consequences of his disbelief, and whoever does righteousness, it is for themselves that they prepare, they prepare the beds and level them in the graves.
30:45: 45- That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds out of His bounty. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: So that God may reward them more than the reward for their deeds, For He does not love the disbelievers.
30:46: God Almighty says: 46- And among His signs is that He sends the winds as good tidings, giving good tidings of rain, and that He may let you taste of His mercy, a blessing, the rain, which is fertility, the ships that you may sail through the sea, with these winds, by His command and that you may seek of His bounty, to seek His provision by trading at sea, and perhaps you will be grateful, the Lord of these blessings.
30:47: God Almighty says: 47- And We had certainly sent before you messengers to their people, and they came to them with clear proofs, with clear evidence of their truthfulness, and We took retribution from those who committed crimes, We punished those who denied them, and it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers, and save them from the punishment. In this there is good tidings for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of victory in the end and triumph over the enemies. Al-Hasan said: He saved them with the messengers from the punishment of the nations. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abd Al-Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Ahmad bin Zanjawayh told us, Abu Al-Sheikh Al-Harrani told us, Abu Musa bin A’yan told us, on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Al-Darda’, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no Muslim who defends the honor of his brother except that it is a right upon God to defend him from the fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited this verse: And it is incumbent upon Us to support the believers.
30:48: 48- It is God who sends the winds, and they stir up the clouds, that is, spreads them out, and spreads them out in the sky as He wills, a journey of a day or two or more for whomever He wills, and makes them into fragments, scattered pieces, and you see the rain, the rain, emerging from within it, its middle, and when He causes it to fall upon whomever He wills, that is, with the rain, of His servants, at once they rejoice, they rejoice at the rain.
30:49: 49- And if they were, and they were, before it was sent down to them before it, in despair, meaning hopeless. And it was said: And if they were, meaning: and they were nothing but despairing. And he repeated his statement: before it, for emphasis. It was said: The first refers to the sending down of rain, and the second to the creation of clouds. In the letter of Abdullah bin Masoud: And they were, before it was revealed to them, in a state of confusion, not repeated.
30:50: 50- So look at the traces of God’s mercy, this is how the people of Hijaz, Basra, and Abu Bakr read it. Others read it: at the traces of God’s mercy, in the plural. By God’s mercy, he meant the rain, meaning: look at its good effect on the earth. Muqatil said: The trace of God’s mercy means: His blessing, which is the vegetation. “How He revives the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed, that is the One who revives the dead.” Meaning: The One who revives the earth is the One who revives the dead. And He is over all things competent.
30:51: 51- And if We send a wind, a cold, harmful one that spoils the crops, and they see it yellow, that is, they see the plants and crops yellow after being green, they would remain, they would become, after it, that is, after the crops turn yellow, ungrateful, denying the previous blessings, meaning that they rejoice when they are fertile, and if I send a punishment upon their crops, they would deny My previous blessings.
30:52: 52- For you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs and depart.
30:53: 53- "And you cannot guide the blind from their misguidance. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses, and they are Muslims."
30:54: 54- God is He Who created you from weakness, it is read with a damma or fatha on the sad, as damma is the language of Quraysh, and fatha is the language of Tamim. The meaning of from weakness is: from a sperm, meaning from weak, meaning: from weak water, as God the Almighty said: Did We not create you from a despised water? (al-Mursalat 77:20), Then after weakness He made strength, after the weakness of childhood, youth, which is the time of strength, Then after strength He made weakness, old age, “and gray hair. He creates what He wills,” from weakness, strength, youth, and gray hair, and He is the Knowing, of managing His creation, the Powerful, over what He wills.
30:55: 55- And on the Day the Hour appears, the criminals will swear, the polytheists will swear, that they had not remained in this world more than an hour, except for an hour. They considered the appointed time of this world insignificant when they saw the Hereafter. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: They had not remained in their graves more than an hour, as He said: On the Day they see that which they are promised, it will be as if they had not remained [in the world] except for an hour of a day (al-Ahqaf 46:35). Likewise, they were lying, they were distracted from the truth in this world. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: They lied in their statement for more than an hour, just as they lied in this world that there would be no resurrection. The meaning is that God wanted to expose them, so they swore an oath about something that became clear to the people of the gathering that they were lying about. This was by God’s decree and predestination, as evidenced by His statement: They are turned away from the truth, meaning: they are diverted from the truth.
30:56: Then he mentioned the believers’ denial of their lies, saying: 56- And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, ‘You have indeed remained in the Book of God,’ meaning, in what God had already decreed for you in His previous knowledge of remaining in the graves. It was also said: In the Book of God, meaning, in the judgment of God. Qatada and Muqatil said: There is an inversion of the meaning of this, and those who were given knowledge and faith will say, You have indeed remained until the Day of Resurrection, meaning those who know the Book of God. They recited the words of God the Most High: And behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected (al-Mu’minun 23:100), meaning, they said to the deniers: “You have indeed remained until the Day of Resurrection. This is the Day of Resurrection,” which you denied in this world, but you did not know, that it would occur in this world.
30:57: Knowing it now will not benefit you, as evidenced by the Almighty’s saying: 57- On that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong, meaning their excuse, nor will they be asked to repent, meaning they will not be asked to repent and return in the Hereafter. The people of Kufa read: will not benefit with a ya’ here and in Ha Mim al-Mu’min, and Nafi’ agreed with him in Ha Mim al-Mu’min, and the rest read it with a ta’ in both of them.
30:58: 58- “And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an from every [kind of] example. And if you bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, ‘You are not but falsifiers.’” You are nothing but falsehood.
30:59: 59- Thus does God set a seal on the hearts of those who do not know the Oneness of God.
30:60: 60- "So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth," in granting you victory and victory over your enemy. And do not let those who are not certain fool you. "Do not let those who are not certain fool you" means: "Do not let those who are not certain" lead you to ignorance and follow them in error. It was also said: "Do not let those who are not certain of the Resurrection and the Judgment fool your opinion and patience.
31:2: 2- These are the verses of the Wise Book.
31:3: 3- Guidance and mercy. Hamza read: mercy in the nominative case as a subject, meaning: it is guidance and mercy. The others read it in the accusative case as a state for the doers of good.
31:4: 4- Those who establish prayer and give zakat and, of the Hereafter, are certain.
31:5: 5- Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful.
31:6: 6- And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech, the verse. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith bin Kalda, who used to trade and would come to Al-Hirah and buy report of the Persians and tell them to the Quraysh, saying: Muhammad tells you the story of Aad and Thamud, and I tell you the story of Rustam and Isfandiyar and the report of the Chosroes. They would find his speech amusing and stop listening to the Quran, so God revealed this verse. Mujahid said: It means buying female singers and musicians. The explanation for this interpretation is: someone who buys something that is entertaining or something that is entertaining. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Al-Fadl bin Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Muzaki told us, my grandfather Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Khuzaymah told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Mish’al bin Milhan Al-Ta’i told us, on the authority of Mutrah bin Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Zajar, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abdul Aziz, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “It is not permissible to teach female singers or sell them, and their prices are forbidden. This is the reason for the revelation of this verse: ‘And among mankind is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [people] from the way of God.’ And there is no man who raises his voice in singing except that God sends two devils against him: one on this shoulder, and the other on this shoulder, and they do not cease to strike him with their feet until he is the one who is silenced.” Abdul Rahman bin Ahmad Al-Qaffal told us, Abu Mansur Ahmad bin Al-Fadl Al-Burujirdi told us, Abu Ahmad Bakr bin Muhammad bin Hamdan Al-Sayrafi told us, Muhammad bin Ghalib bin Tamam told us, Khalid bin Abi Yazid told us, on the authority of Hisham - he is Ibn Hassan - on the authority of Muhammad - he is Ibn Sirin - on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the price of a dog and the earnings of a flute player.” Makhool said: Whoever buys a female slave who is a singer to keep her for her singing and continues to beat her until she dies, I will not pray for him, because God says: And among the people is he who buys the amusement of speech Al-Masdar Online, 20:10. On the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and Saeed bin Jubair, they said: Idle talk is singing, and the verse was revealed about it. The meaning of his saying: He buys the amusement of speech, is: He replaces and chooses singing, flutes, and musical instruments over the Qur’an. Abu al-Saba’ al-Bakri said: I asked Ibn Mas’ud about this verse, and he said: It is singing, and God is the One besides Whom there is no god, repeating it three times. Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i said: "Singing causes hypocrisy to grow in the heart. Our companions used to take hold of the mouths of alleys and play tambourines." It was also said: Singing is an incantation for adultery. Ibn Jurayj said: It is the drum. Ad-Dahhak said: It is polytheism. Qatada said: It is all forms of amusement and play. To lead astray from the path of God without knowledge, meaning: he does it out of ignorance. Qatada said: It is enough misguidance for a person to choose false speech over true speech. God the Almighty says: And he takes it in ridicule, meaning: he takes the verses of God in ridicule. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Hafs, and Ya’qub read: And he takes it with the dāl in the accusative case, in apposition to His statement: To mislead. The others read it with the dāl in the nominative case, in conjunction with His statement: To buy. Those will have a humiliating punishment.
31:7: 7- “And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as if he had not heard them, as if there was deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.”
31:8: 8- Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have gardens of pleasure.
31:9: 9- “They will abide therein eternally. This is the promise of God, in truth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
31:10: 10- “He created the heavens without pillars that you can see, and He placed firm mountains on the earth, lest it should move with you, and He dispersed therein all kinds of creatures, and We sent down water from the sky and caused to grow therein every noble kind.” Hasan.
31:11: 11- This, meaning what you mentioned of what you see, “is what God created. So show me what those other than Him have created,” of your gods that you worship. Rather, the wrongdoers are in clear error.
31:12: God Almighty said: 12- And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom, meaning: reason, knowledge, acting upon it, and being correct in matters. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: He is Luqman ibn Na’ur ibn Nahor ibn Tarah, who is Azar. Wahb said: He was Job’s nephew. Muqatil said: It was mentioned that he was Job’s maternal uncle’s son. Al-Waqidi said: He was a judge among the Children of Israel. Scholars agreed that he was a wise man, but not a prophet, except for Ikrimah, who said: Luqman was a prophet. He was the only one to say this. Some of them said: Luqman was given the choice between prophecy and wisdom, so he chose wisdom. It was narrated that while he was sleeping during the middle of the day, a voice was called, O Luqman, would you like God to make you a successor on earth to judge between people with justice? The voice answered and said, “If my Lord gives me the choice, I will accept well-being and not accept affliction. If He decides upon me, then I hear and obey, for I know that if He does that for me, He will support and protect me.” The angels said in a voice they could not see, Why, Luqman? He said, “Because the ruler is in the toughest and most turbulent of positions, where injustice surrounds him from every side. If he acts justly, he is more likely to be saved, and if he errs, he misses the path to Paradise. To be humiliated in this world is better than to be noble. Whoever chooses this world over the Hereafter will be tempted by this world and never attain the Hereafter.” The angels were amazed at his eloquent speech. He slept and was given wisdom. He awoke while speaking it. Then David was called after him and he accepted it without making any condition as Luqman had stipulated. He fell into sin more than once, but God pardoned him all the time, and Luqman supported him with his wisdom. On the authority of Khalid Al-Rubai’i, he said: Luqman was an Ethiopian slave who was a carpenter. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: He was a tailor. It was also said: He was a shepherd. It was narrated that a man met him while he was speaking wisdom and said: Are you not so-and-so the shepherd? How did you reach what you reached? He said: By speaking truthfully, fulfilling trusts, and leaving what does not concern me. Mujahid said: He was a black slave with large lips and cracked feet. God Almighty says: “That I should be grateful to God. And whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy.”
31:13: 13- And when Luqman said to his son, whose name was An’am, and it is said: Mishkam, “while he was admonishing him: O my son, do not associate anything with God. Indeed, association is a great wrong.” Ibn Kathir read: O my son, do not associate anything with God with a sukoon on the ya’, and Hafs with a fatha, and the rest with a kasra. O my son, establish prayer, with a fatha on the ya’, according to Ibn Kathir and Hafs, and Al-Qawwas with a sukoon on it, and the rest with a kasra.
31:14: 14- And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, his mother carried him, with weakness upon weakness. Ibn Abbas said: Hardship after hardship. Ad-Dahhak said: Weakness upon weakness. Mujahid said: Hardship upon hardship. Az-Zajjaj said: When a woman becomes pregnant, weakness and hardship follow one another. It is said: Pregnancy is weakness, labor pains are weakness, and childbirth is weakness. And his weaning, meaning: his weaning, “is in two years. [And] be grateful to Me and to your parents. To Me is the final destination.” Reference: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said about this verse: Whoever prays the five daily prayers has thanked God, and whoever supplicates for the parents after the five daily prayers has thanked the parents.
31:15: 15- But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in this world with appropriate kindness. That is, with appropriate kindness, which is righteousness, kinship, and good companionship. And follow the way of those who turn back to Me. That is, the religion of those who turn to My obedience, which is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. Ata' said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means Abu Bakr. When he converted to Islam, Uthman, Talhah, Az-Zubayr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf came to him and said to him: Have you believed this man and have faith in him? He said: Yes, he is truthful. So they believed in him. Then he took them to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until they converted to Islam. These people had precedence in Islam; they converted to Islam under the guidance of Abu Bakr. God Almighty said: And follow the way of him who turns back to Me, meaning Abu Bakr, Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do. It was said: These two verses were revealed about Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas and his mother, and the story has already been mentioned. It was said: The verse is general and applies to all people.
31:16: 16- O my son, if it be the weight of a mustard seed, the metaphor in his statement: it refers to the sin, as Luqman’s son said to his father: O my father, if I commit a sin where no one can see me, how will God know about it? He said: O my son, if it be the weight of a mustard seed, let it be in a rock, Qatada said: it be in a mountain. Ibn Abbas said: in a rock beneath the seven earths, and it is in it that the deeds of the wicked are recorded, and the greenery of the sky is from it. Al-Suddi said: God created the earth on a whale - which is the letter Nun that God Almighty mentioned in the Qur’an, Nun and the Pen. The whale is in the water, the water is on the back of a rock, the rock is on the back of an angel, the angel is on a rock, which is the rock that Luqman mentioned, neither in the sky nor on the earth, and the rock is on the wind. “Or in the heavens or on the earth, God will bring it forth. Indeed, God is Subtle,” in extracting it, Aware, knowing its location. Al-Hasan said: The meaning of the verse is the encompassing of things, small and large. In some books, this word was the last word spoken by Luqman, and his gall bladder burst from its awe, so he died.
31:17: 17- O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you, meaning harm, Indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of resolve, meaning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and being patient over the harm in them, are among the obligatory matters that God has commanded, or among the matters that one resolves to do because they are obligatory.
31:18: 18- And do not turn your cheek away from people. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Asim, Abu Ja`far, and Ya`qub read: Do not turn away with emphasis on the `ayn without an alif. The others read: Tasa`ar with an alif. It is said: He turned away his face and Sa`ar: if he leaned and turned away out of arrogance. A man who is `as`ar means: one with a slanted neck. Ibn Abbas said: He says: Do not be arrogant, so as not to belittle people and turn your face away from them when they speak to you. Mujahed said: He is the man with whom you have a grudge, and you meet him and he turns his face away from you. Akrima said: He is the one who, when greeted, turns his neck out of arrogance. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas and Qatada said: Do not look down on the poor. Let the poor and the rich be equal in your eyes. And do not walk on the earth exultantly, out of arrogance. Indeed, God does not like anyone who is arrogant, in his walk, boasting, towards people.
31:19: 19- And be moderate in your walk, meaning: let your walk be moderate, not imaginative or hasty. Ata’ said: Walk with dignity and serenity, like His statement: They walk upon the earth easily (al-Furqan 25:63). And lower your voice, lower your voice. Muqatil said: Lower your voice, Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds, the ugliest of sounds, is the voice of donkeys, which begins with a sigh and ends with an inhalation, and they are the voices of the people of Hell. Musa bin A’yan said: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri say about His statement: The most disagreeable of sounds is the braying of donkeys. He said: The braying of everything is glorification of God except the donkey. And the saying of Jaafar Al-Sadiq in his saying: The most reprehensible of sounds is the sound of donkeys, he said: It is the ugly, reprehensible sneeze. Wahb said: Luqman spoke with twelve thousand chapters of wisdom, which people incorporated into their speech, their judgments, and his rulings. Khalid Al-Rab’i said: Luqman was an Abyssinian slave, and his master gave him a sheep and said: Slaughter it and bring me the two best parts of it. So he brought him the tongue and the heart. Then he gave him another sheep and said: Slaughter it and bring me the two worst parts of it. So he brought him the tongue and the heart. His master asked him, and he said: There is nothing better than these two when they are good, and nothing worse than these two when they are bad.
31:20: God Almighty said: 20- Have you not seen that God has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and has bestowed upon you His blessings, He completed and perfected, His favors. The people of Medina, Abu Amr, and Hafs read His favors with a fat-ha on the ‘ayn and a damma on the ha’ for the plural, and the others read it with a tanween for the singular, and its meaning is also plural like His saying: And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them (Ibrahim 14:14), apparent and hidden, Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The apparent favor is Islam and the Qur’an, and the hidden is what He concealed from you of sins and did not hasten to punish you. Ad-Dahhak said: The apparent is the beauty of the image and the proportionality of the limbs, and the hidden is knowledge. Muqatil said: The apparent is the proportionality of character, livelihood, and Islam. The hidden is what is concealed of sins. Al-Rabi’ said: The apparent is with the limbs, and the hidden is with the heart. It was said: The apparent is the acknowledgment: with the tongue, and the hidden is the belief: in the heart. It was said: The apparent meaning is the complete provision, and the hidden meaning is good character. Ata’ said: The apparent meaning is the alleviation of the laws, and the hidden meaning is intercession. Mujahid said: The apparent meaning is the emergence of Islam and victory over the enemies, and the hidden meaning is the support of angels. It was also said: The apparent meaning is the support of angels, and the hidden meaning is the instilling of terror in the hearts of the infidels. Sahl bin Abdullah said: The apparent meaning is following the Messenger, and the hidden meaning is loving him. And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge. This verse was revealed about Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and others like them. They used to dispute with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about God and His attributes without knowledge, nor guidance nor an enlightening Book.
31:21: 21- And when it is said to them, ‘Follow what God has revealed,’ they say, ‘Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.’ God Almighty said: Or even if Satan were inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze. The answer to if is omitted, and its meaning is: he invites them and they follow him, meaning: they follow Satan even though Satan is inviting them to the punishment of the Blaze.
31:22: 22- And whoever submits his face to God, meaning: to God, that is: he dedicates his religion to God, and entrusts his affair to God, and is a doer of good, in his actions, has grasped the most trustworthy handhold, that is: he has held fast to the most trustworthy covenant that he does not fear will be broken, and to God is the outcome of all matters.
31:23: 23- "And whoever disbelieves - let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts."
31:24: 24- We give them enjoyment for a little while, meaning: We give them time to enjoy the pleasures of this world for a little while until their appointed time comes to an end, then We force them, then We compel them and return them in the Hereafter, to a severe punishment, which is the punishment of the Fire.
31:25: 25- And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ But most of them do not know.
31:26: 26- “To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.”
31:27: God Almighty says: 27- "And if all the trees on earth were pens," the verse. The commentators said: It was revealed in Mecca. God Almighty says: "And they ask you about the soul," to His saying: "And of knowledge you have been given only a little." (Al-Isra': 85). When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, the Jewish rabbis came to him and said: O Muhammad, we have heard that you say: "And of knowledge you have been given only a little." Do you mean us or your people? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, I do mean it. They said: Do you not recite among what came to you: "We were given the Torah, and in it is knowledge of all things?" The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is little compared to the knowledge of God, and God has given you that which, if you acted upon, would benefit you. They said: O Muhammad, how can you claim this when you say: "And whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good." (al-Baqarah 2:269). How can this be combined with little knowledge and much good? Then God revealed this verse. Qatada said: The polytheists said: The Qur’an and what Muhammad brings will soon be exhausted and come to an end. So the verse was revealed: And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, meaning: were sharpened into pens, and the sea were to replenish it. Abu Amr and Ya’qub read: And the sea in the accusative case in apposition to what. The rest read it in the nominative case as a new sentence. He adds to it, meaning: He increases it, and after it is in the accusative case, from His creation. Seven seas, “the Words of God would not be exhausted.” In the verse there is an abbreviation, the meaning of which is: And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea were to replenish it after it, with which to write the Words of God, the Words of God would not be exhausted. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise. According to Ata’ ibn Yasar, this verse is Medinan, while according to others, it is Meccan. They said: The Jews ordered the Quraysh delegation to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say this to him while he was still in Mecca. And God knows best.
31:28: 28- He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul, meaning that the creation and resurrection of a single soul is like the creation of a single soul, nothing is impossible for Him. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing.
31:29: 29- “Have you not seen that God merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term? And that God, with what you do, is Acquainted.”
31:30: 30- That is because God is the Truth, meaning: that which I mentioned so that you may know that God is the Truth, and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood and that God is the Most High, the Grand.
31:31: 31- Have you not seen that the ships sail through the sea by the grace of God? He means that this is from God’s grace upon you, to show you some of His signs, His wonders, Indeed in that are signs for everyone who is patient, upon God’s command/ grateful, for His blessings.
31:32: 32- And when waves cover them like shadows, Muqatil said: Like mountains. Al-Kalbi said: Like clouds. Shadow is the plural of shadow, which is likened to the wave in its abundance and height. He made the wave, which is singular, like the shadow, which is plural, because the wave comes from it one thing after another. “They supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivered them to the land, some of them were moderate,” meaning: just, fulfilling on land what they had pledged to God in the sea of monotheism for Him, meaning: steadfast in their faith. It was revealed about Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl. He fled to the sea in the year of the conquest, and a strong wind came upon them. Ikrimah said: If God saves me from this, I will return to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I will place my hand in his. The wind calmed down, and Ikrimah returned to Mecca, converted to Islam, and his conversion was good. Mujahid said: Among them are those who are moderate in speech but conceal disbelief. Al-Kalbi said: Moderate in speech means: among the disbelievers, because some of them were more vehement in speech and more extreme in their slander than others. None denies Our verses except every deceitful ungrateful person, and deceit is the worst kind of treachery.
31:33: 33- O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day that will not recompense, will not decide or avail, A father will not recompense his son, nor will a son avail his father at all, Ibn Abbas said: Every person is concerned with himself, Indeed, the promise of God is truth, so let not the worldly life delude you and let not the Deceiver delude you about God, meaning Satan. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is to commit a sin and hope for forgiveness.
31:34: 34- Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. This verse was revealed about Al-Warith bin Amr bin Haritha bin Muharib bin Hafsah, one of the Bedouins. He came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him about the Hour and its time. He said: Our land is barren, so when will the rain fall? I have left my wife pregnant, so when will she give birth? I know where I was born, so in which land will I die? So God revealed this verse: "Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. No soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul perceives in what land it will die." Abi bin Kaab read: with the verse of the land, and the well-known reading is: with any land, because the land does not contain any signs of femininity. It was said: He meant by the land the place: Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah told us, Ibrahim bin Sa’idah told us on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The keys of the unseen are five: God has knowledge of the Hour, He sends down the rain, He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die.” God is All-Knowing and All-Aware.
32:1: Meccan. Ata’ said: Except for three verses from His saying: Is he who is a believer? to the last three verses. 1- Alif-Lam-Mim.
32:2: 2- The revelation of the Book, there is no doubt about it, is from the Lord of the Worlds. Muqatil said: There is no doubt about it that it is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds.
32:3: 3- Or do they say, rather they say, He invented it. It was said that the mim is a connective, meaning: Do they say He invented it? A question of rebuke. It was said that am has the meaning of and, meaning: And they say He invented it. It was said that there is an implied meaning in it, its metaphor is: Do they believe, or do they say He invented it? Then he said: Rather, it, meaning the Qur’an, is the truth from your Lord that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come meaning: No warner has come before you. Qatadah said: They were an illiterate nation to whom no warner came before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: That was during the period that was between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless them both, that they may be guided.
32:4: 4- “God is He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days and then established Himself on the Throne. You have not besides Him any protector or intercessor. Then will you not remember?”
32:5: 5- He directs the affair, that is, He decides the affair and sends down judgment and decree, from heaven to earth. It was said that the revelation descends with Gabriel from heaven to earth, then it ascends, ascends, to Him, Gabriel with the command, in a Day the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count, that is, in one day of the days of this world and the extent of a thousand years’ journey, five hundred years’ descent and five hundred years’ ascent, because the distance between heaven and earth is five hundred years. He says: If one of the sons of Adam walked in it, he would not cover it except in a thousand years, and the angels cover it in one day. This is in describing the angel’s ascension from earth to heaven. As for His statement: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years Al-Ma’arij 4, He meant the length of the distance between the earth and the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is the station of Gabriel. Gabriel, the angels, and those with him from the people of his station travel a distance of fifty thousand years in one day of the days of this world. This is all the meaning of what Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said. His saying, To Him, means, To God. It was said: According to this interpretation, it means, To the place of the angel to whom God Almighty commanded him to ascend. Some of them said: A thousand years and fifty thousand years, all of them on the Day of Resurrection, some of them longer and some of them shorter. Its meaning is: He manages the affair from the heaven to the earth for the duration of the days of this world, then it ascends, meaning: The affair and management will return to Him after the world has passed away, and the affair of the princes and the rule of the rulers has ceased on a day the length of which is a thousand years, which is the Day of Resurrection. As for His saying: Fifty thousand years, he meant that for the disbeliever, God will make that day for him the length of fifty thousand years, and for the believer less than that, so it came in the hadith: It will be for the believer the length of an obligatory prayer that he prayed in this world. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: The believer is only responsible for what is between noon and afternoon prayers. This may be a description of its severity, horror, and hardship. Ibn Abi Malekah said: “Abdullah ibn Fayruz, the client of Uthman ibn Affan, and I went to Ibn Abbas. Ibn Fayruz asked him about this verse and about His statement, ‘Fifty thousand years.’ Ibn Abbas said, ‘Days that God has named, I do not know what they are, and I hate to say about God’s Book what I do not know.’”
32:6: 6- He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, meaning: He is the One who created the heavens and the earth that He mentioned/He knows what is hidden from creation and what is present, the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
32:7: 7- He who created everything which He perfected. Nafi’ and the people of Kufa read: He created it with a fat-ha on the lam of the verb, while the others read it with a sukoon on it, meaning: He created everything perfectly. Ibn Abbas said: He perfected and perfected it. Qatada said: He made it good. Muqatil said: He knew how to create everything, from your saying: So-and-so does such-and-such well if he knows it. It was said: He created every animal in its image, He did not create some in the image of others, so every animal is perfect in its creation and good, and every part of its organs is destined to be suitable for its livelihood. And He began the creation of man from clay, meaning Adam.
32:8: 8- Then He made his offspring, meaning his descendants, from a lineage, a sperm, called a lineage because it comes from a human being from a despised water, meaning: weak, which is the sperm of a man.
32:9: 9- Then He proportioned him, then proportioned His creation, and breathed into him of His spirit, then He returned to his offspring, and said: And made for you, after you were sperm, “hearing and sight and hearts. Little do you give thanks,” meaning: You do not give thanks to the Lord of these blessings and worship Him alone.
32:10: 10- And they said, meaning those who denied the resurrection, If we are lost, meaning perish, in the earth, and become dust, and its origin is from their saying: the water is lost in the milk when it disappears, Will we then be in a new creation? This is a question of denial. God Almighty said: Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord, meaning: in the resurrection after death.
32:11: 11- “Say: ‘The Angel of Death who is assigned to you will take your souls’,” that is, he will take your souls, “and he who takes your souls will take your souls, and he is Azrael. Taking is the completion of the number, meaning that he will take their souls until no one remains from the number for whom death was decreed. It was narrated that the Angel of Death has had the world made like the palm of the hand, from which its owner can take what he likes without difficulty. He takes the souls of creation in the east and west of the earth, and he has helpers from the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment. Ibn Abbas said: The Angel of Death's steps are between the east and the west. Mujahed said: The earth was made for him like a basin from which he could take whatever he wanted. In some reports: The Angel of Death is on an ascension between heaven and earth, and his helpers extract the soul of a person. When he reaches his mouth, he slaughters him, and the Angel of Death seizes him. Khalid bin Ma'dan narrated on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, who said: The Angel of Death has a spear that reaches between the east and the west, and he scans people's faces. There is no household but that the Angel of Death scans them twice a day. If he sees a person whose time has come, he strikes his head with that spear and says: Now the army of the dead will visit you. His saying: “Then to your Lord you will return,” meaning: you will come to Him alive, and He will reward you for your deeds.
32:12: 12- And if you could but see when the criminals, the polytheists, hang their heads, bowing their heads, before their Lord, in shame and remorse, Our Lord, meaning: they say, Our Lord, we have seen, that we were not denying it, and we have heard, from You confirming what Your messengers brought us. And it was said: We have seen our sins and heard what was said about us, so return us, so return us to the world, “that we may do righteousness. Indeed, we are certain [in faith].” The answer to if is implied in its metaphor, and you would see the wonder.
32:13: 13- And if We willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, its right path and its success in faith, but the truth, it is necessary, “is the word from Me: ‘I will fill Hell with jinn and people all together,’” which is His saying to Satan: I will fill Hell with you and those who follow you among them, all together Sad-85.
32:14: Then it will be said to the people of Hell - and Muqatil said: When they enter Hell, the guards will say to them: 14- So taste for having forgotten the meeting of this Day of yours, meaning: you abandoned belief in it in this world. Indeed, We have forgotten you, We abandoned you, and taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do, of disbelief and denial.
32:15: God Almighty says: 15- Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded by them, are admonished by them, fall down in prostration, fall on their faces in prostration, and exalt [God] with praise of their Lord, it was said: they prayed at the command of their Lord. It was also said: they said: Glory be to God and praise be to Him, and they are not arrogant, about believing in and prostrating to Him.
32:16: 16- "They turn away, they rise and turn away, their sides from the beds, the plural of bed", which is the place on which one lies, meaning the mattress, and they are the ones who stay up at night to pray. They differed about the meaning of this verse. Anas said: It was revealed about us, the Ansar. We used to pray the Maghrib prayer and not return to our homes until we prayed the Isha prayer with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. On the authority of Anas also, he said: It was revealed about some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who used to pray the Maghrib prayer until the Isha prayer. This is the opinion of Abu Hazim and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, and they said: It is the prayer of the repentant. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The angels surround those who pray between sunset and night prayers, and it is the prayer of the repentant. Ata' said: They are those who do not sleep until they pray the last evening prayer. On the authority of Abu Darda, Abu Dharr, and Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with them: They are those who pray the last evening prayer and the dawn prayer in congregation. We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever prays the Isha prayer in congregation, it is as if he spent half a night in prayer, and whoever prays the Fajr prayer in congregation, it is as if he spent a whole night in prayer. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Sumay, the freed slave of Abu Bakr ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Salih al-Samman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If people knew the reward for the call to prayer and the first row, and could find no other way to do so than to draw lots, they would draw lots. If they knew the reward for arriving early in the morning, they would race to it. If they knew the reward for the `Isha and Fajr prayers, they would come to them even if they had to crawl.” The most famous saying is that it means the night prayer, which is the saying of Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Malik, Al-Awza’i and a group. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bishran told us, Abu Ali Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Jabal, who said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on our journey. One day I was close to him while he was walking, so I said: O Messenger of God, tell me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise and keep me away from the Fire. He said: You have asked about a great matter, and it is easy for whomever God makes it easy for: Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, establish prayer, pay zakat, fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj to the House. Then he said: Shall I not guide you to the gates of goodness: Fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and a man’s prayer in the depths of the night? Then he recited: Their sides forsake their beds until he reached a reward for what they used to do. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of the head of the matter, its pillar, and the pinnacle of its hump? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: The head of the matter Islam, its pillar is prayer, and its pinnacle is jihad. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of the essence of all of that? I said: Yes, O Prophet of God. He said: Then he took hold of my tongue and said: Refrain from this. I said: O Prophet of God, will we be held accountable for what we say? He said: May your mother lose you, O Muadh! Are people tossed on their faces – or he said on their noses – into Hellfire except for the harvest of their tongues? Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Hanafi narrated to us, Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad al-Mukhalladi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani narrated to us, Hamad ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, Abu Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, Muawiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, Rabi’ah ibn Yazid narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You should perform the night prayer, for it was the practice of the righteous who came before you, and it brings you closer to your Lord, and it expiates bad deeds, and it deters from sin. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ruh bin Aslam told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Our Lord is amazed by two men: a man who rises from his comforter and blanket, from among his beloved and his family, to his prayer. God says to His angels: Look at My servant, he has risen from his bed and comforter, from among his beloved and his family, to his prayer, desiring what is with Me and fearing what is with Me. And a man who fights in the cause of God and his companions are defeated with him, so he knows what is upon him in defeat and what is for him in returning, so he returns and fights until his blood is shed. God says to His angels: Look at My servant, he has returned desiring what is with Me and fearing what is with Me until his blood is shed.’” Abu Uthman al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi told us, Qutaybah ibn Sa`id told us, Abu `Awanah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Humayd ibn `Abd al-Rahman al-Himyari, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The best fasting after the month of Ramadan is the month of God, Muharram, and the best prayer after the obligatory prayer is the night prayer.’” Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ibn Mu’anaq, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘In Paradise there are rooms whose outside can be seen from their inside and whose inside can be seen from their outside. God has prepared them for those who speak gently, feed the poor, fast regularly, and pray at night while people are asleep.’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Isbagh told us, Abdullah bin Wahb told me, Yunus told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Al-Haytham bin Abi Sinan told us, he told me that he heard Abu Hurairah in his stories mentioning on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to say: A brother of yours does not speak obscene language, meaning Abdullah bin Rawahah. He said: And among us is the Messenger of God reciting his book when the dawn breaks brightly. He showed us guidance after blindness, so our hearts are convinced that what He said will come true. He spends the night turning away from his bed when the beds become burdensome for him with the disbelievers. The Almighty says: They call upon their Lord in fear and hope. Ibn Abbas said: “Out of fear of the Fire and hope for Paradise. “And from what We have provided them, they spend.” It was said that this refers to obligatory charity. It was also said that it is general in meaning, including both obligatory and voluntary charity.
32:17: 17- No soul knows what has been hidden for them. Hamza and Ya'qub read: I have hidden for them, with a silent ya, meaning: I have hidden for them. Among his proofs is Ibn Mas'ud's reading of I have hidden with a nun. The others read it with a fatha. From the comfort of their eyes, from what their eyes will be comforted with, as reward for what they used to do. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ishaq bin Nasr told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, Abu Saleh told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: ‘I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, a storehouse of which you have only seen.’ Then he recited: ‘No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do.’” Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: This is something that has no explanation. Another one said: They concealed their deeds, so God concealed their reward.
32:18: God the Almighty said: 18- Is he who is a believer like he who is a sinner? They are not equal. This verse was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib and Al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt, the maternal brother of Uthman. There was a dispute and discussion between them about something, so Al-Walid ibn Uqba said to Ali, Be quiet, for you are a child, and by God I am more eloquent than you, sharper of a spear than you, braver of a spirit than you, and fill the army with more men. Ali said to him, Be quiet, for you are a sinner. Then God the Almighty revealed: Is he who is a believer like he who is a sinner? They are not equal. He did not say, They are not equal, because He did not mean one believer and one sinner, but rather He meant all believers and all sinners.
32:19: 19- As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge, to which the believers will take refuge, as a reward for what they used to do.
32:20: 20- “As for those who disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned to it and it will be said to them, ‘Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.’”
32:21: 21- And We will make them taste of the lesser punishment short of the greater punishment, meaning: other than the greater punishment, that perhaps they will return. Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, and Ibrahim said: The lesser punishment is the calamities and illnesses of this world, and this is the narration of Al-Walibi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Ikrimah said on his authority: The prescribed punishments. Muqatil said: Seven years of famine in Mecca until they ate carcasses, bones, and dogs. Ibn Mas’ud said: It is being killed by the sword on the day of Badr, and this is the saying of Qatadah and As-Suddi. Below the greater punishment, meaning: the punishment of the Hereafter, that perhaps they will return, to faith, meaning: whoever remained of them after Badr and after the famine.
