32:22: 22- And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them? Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals, meaning: the polytheists.
32:23: 23- And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, so be not in doubt about meeting him, meaning: Do not be in doubt about meeting Moses on the night of the Ascension, as Ibn Abbas and others said. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Ghundar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatada, may God have mercy on him, who said: Hudhayfah told me, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, who said: The cousin of your Prophet - meaning Ibn Abbas - told us, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “On the night of my Night Journey, I saw Moses, a tall, dark-skinned, curly-haired man, as if he were from the men of Shanu’ah. I saw Jesus, a square-faced man, with a reddish-white complexion, and a smooth head. I saw Malik, the keeper of Hell, and the Antichrist, with signs that God showed him, so do not be in doubt about meeting him.” Abu Saleh Ahmad bin Abdul Malik Al-Mu’adhdhin informed us, Abdullah Al-Muhammadi informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ibrahim Al-Bazzaz informed us, Muhammad bin Yunus informed us, Omar bin Habib Al-Qadi informed us, Sulayman Al-Taymi informed us, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When I was taken up to heaven on the Night Journey, I saw Moses praying in his grave. We narrated in the Ascension that he saw him in the sixth heaven and consulted him about the matter of prayer. Al-Suddi said: Do not be in doubt about meeting him, meaning: about Moses receiving the Book of God with satisfaction and acceptance.
32:24: 24- And We made it, meaning: the Book, which is the Torah. Qatada said: Moses. And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, meaning: from the Children of Israel. Leaders, leaders in goodness to be followed, meaning: the prophets who were among them. Qatada said: the followers of the prophets. They guide, they call, by Our command when they were patient. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read it with a kasra on the lam and a soft mim, meaning: for their patience. The rest read it with a fatha on the lam and a shaddah on the mim, meaning: when they were patient in their religion and in the affliction from their enemy in Egypt. And they were certain of Our signs.
32:25: 25- Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
32:26: 26- Have they not been guided, has it not become clear, “how many generations We destroyed before them who used to walk about in their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs. Will they not then listen?” God’s signs and sermons, so that they may learn from them.
32:27: 27- Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land, meaning: the dry, rough land in which there is no vegetation. Ibn Abbas said: It is a land in Yemen. Mujahid said: It is the land of Babin, And We bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock eat, of grass and straw, and themselves, of grains and sustenance. Do they not see?
32:28: 28- And they say, ‘When will this conquest be, if you should be truthful?’ It was said that by the Day of Conquest he meant the Day of Resurrection on which judgment will be made between the servants. Qatada said: The companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the disbelievers: We have a day on which we will enjoy ourselves and rest, and judgment will be made between us and you. They said mockingly: When will this conquest be? Meaning: judgment and ruling. Al-Kalbi said: It meant the conquest of Mecca. Al-Suddi said: The Day of Badr, because the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say to them: God has supported us and made us victorious over you. They would say: When will this conquest be?
32:29: 29- Say, on the Day of Conquest, on the Day of Resurrection, their faith will not benefit those who disbelieve, and whoever interprets the conquest as the conquest of Mecca or the killing on the Day of Badr said: Its meaning is that the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them if the punishment comes to them and they are killed, nor will they be reprieved, they will not be given time to repent and apologize.
32:30: 30- So turn away from them, Ibn Abbas said: It was abrogated by the verse of the sword, and wait, for they are waiting, it was said: Wait for My appointment for you with victory, for they are waiting for the events of time through you. And it was said: Wait for Our punishment upon them, for they are waiting for that. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Naim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Saad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Harmaz, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite in the dawn prayer on Friday, ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. A revelation’ and ‘Has there come upon man a period of time?’” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abu Na’im told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not sleep until he had recited: ‘Blessed’ and ‘Alif, Lam, Meem. A revelation.’”
33:1: 1- O Prophet, fear God. This verse was revealed about Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Abu al-A'war Amr ibn Sufyan as-Sulami. They came to Madinah and camped with Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the leader of the hypocrites, after the Battle of Uhud. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given them security on the condition that they would speak to him. Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh and Tu'mah ibn Ubayraq stood with them and said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him: Refuse to mention our gods, al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat, and say: They have intercession for those who worship them, and we will leave you to your Lord. Their words were difficult for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so Umar said: O Messenger of God, give us permission to kill them. He said: I have already given them security. Umar said: Go out under the curse and wrath of God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Umar to expel them from Madinah, and God Almighty revealed: O Prophet, fear God, meaning: persist in piety, like a man who says to another while he is standing: Stand here, meaning: remain standing. It was said that the address was to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what was meant by it was the illiterate person. Ad-Dahhak said: It means, fear God and do not break the covenant between you and them. And do not obey the disbelievers from the people of Mecca, meaning: Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah, and Abu Al-Awar, and the hypocrites from the people of Medina, Abdullah bin Ubayy, Abdullah bin Saad, and Ta’mah. Indeed, God is Knowing of His creation, before He created them, Wise in what He planned for them.
33:2: 2- “And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.” Abu Amr read: They do knowledgeable and they do seer with the ya in both of them, and others read it with the ta.
33:3: 3- And put your trust in God Trust in God, and God is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs, protecting you, and it was said: guarantor of your provision.
33:4: God Almighty said: 4- God has not made for any man two hearts within him. This verse was revealed about Abu Muammar, Jamil ibn Muammar al-Fihri, who was an intelligent man who memorized what he heard. The Quraysh said: Abu Muammar would not have memorized these things unless he had two hearts. He used to say: I have two hearts, and I understand each one of them better than the mind of Muhammad. When God defeated the polytheists, and on the day of Badr, Abu Muammar was defeated by them. Abu Sufyan met him, and he had one of his sandals in his hand and the other on his foot. He said to him: O Abu Muammar, what is the condition of the people? He said: They were defeated. He said: Why is one of your sandals in your hand and the other on your foot? Abu Muammar said: I only felt that they were on my foot. So they knew on that day that if he had two hearts, he would not have forgotten his sandal in his hand. Al-Zuhri and Muqatil said: This is an example that God Almighty gave for the one who pronounces zihar from his wife and Al-Mutanabbi has a son other than him. He says: Just as a man cannot have two hearts, so too the wife of the one who pronounces zihar cannot be his mother until she is a trust, and he cannot have one son who is the son of two men. And He has not made your wives whom you declare to be your mothers. The people of Ash-Sham and Kufa read: those here and in Surat At-Talaq with a ya' after the hamza. Qaloon read on the authority of Nafi' and Ya'qub without a ya' after the hamza. The others read it with a soft hamza, and all of these are well-known dialects. Tazaharoon, Asim read it with an alif and a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the ha', lightened. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the ta' and the ha', lightened. Ibn 'Amir read it with a fatha and a shaddah on the dha', and the others read it with a fatha and a shaddah on the dha' and the ha' without an alif between them. The example of Zihar is when a man says to his wife, You are to me like the back of my mother. God the Almighty says, He has not made your women, to whom you say this, like your mothers in terms of prohibition. Rather, it is an abomination and a falsehood, and there is expiation for it, which we will mention, God willing, in Surat Al-Mujadilah. And He has not made your adopted sons meaning: those you have adopted your sons. This abrogates adoption, as in the pre-Islamic era a man would adopt another man and make him like his own son, calling him his name and inheriting his inheritance. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had freed Zayd ibn Haritha ibn Shurahil al-Kalbi and adopted him before the revelation, and made him a brother to Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was married to Zayd ibn Haritha, the hypocrites said that Muhammad married his son’s wife and he forbade that. So God revealed this verse and abrogated adoption. That is your statement from your mouths, meaning their saying Zayd ibn Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their claiming lineage that has no truth. And God speaks the truth, meaning: His statement is the truth. And He guides to the way, meaning: He guides to the path of truth.
33:5: 5- Call them by the names of their fathers, who gave birth to them, that is more just, more equitable, in the sight of God. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Ma’la bin Asad informed us, Abdul Aziz Al-Mukhtar informed us, Musa bin Uqba informed us, Salim informed me, “on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar that Zaid bin Haritha, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We did not call him anything but Zaid bin Muhammad until the Qur’an was revealed.” Call them by the names of their fathers; it is more just in the sight of God. “But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients,” if they are freedmen and not your sons. That is, call them by the names of your brothers in religion. It was also said: your clients, meaning your guardians in religion. And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred, before the prohibition, in attributing them to someone other than their father, but [only] for what your hearts deliberately intended, of calling them by other than their fathers after the Prophet. Qatada said: Among the things you have erred in is that you attribute him to someone other than his father, while he thought that was the case. The position of what in the Almighty’s statement: what you did intentionally is in the accusative case in response to the what in His statement: in what you have erred in, meaning: but in what your hearts intended. “And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd God al-Nu’aimi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Ismail informed us, Muhammad ibn Bashar informed us, Ghundar informed us, Shu’bah informed us on the authority of Asim, who said: I heard Abu Uthman say: I heard Sa’d, who was the first to shoot an arrow in the way of God, and Abu Bakra, who had climbed the scales of the fortress of Ta’if with some people, and they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: We heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever claims to have a father other than his own, knowingly, Paradise is forbidden to him.
33:6: God the Almighty said: 6- The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves, meaning that they are closer to each other in the implementation of his rule over them and the obligation of obeying him. Ibn Abbas and Ata’ said: It means that if the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) calls them and their own selves call them to something, then obeying the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is more important to them than their own obedience to themselves. Ibn Zayd said: The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves in what he has decreed concerning them, just as you are closer to your servant in what you have decreed against him. It was said: He is more important to them in carrying out jihad and sacrificing one’s life for him. It was said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would go out to fight and some people would say: We will go and ask permission from our fathers and mothers, so the verse was revealed. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Abu Amir told us, Falih told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no believer but that I am closer to him in this world and the Hereafter. Read if you wish: ‘The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves.’ So any believer who dies and leaves behind wealth, let his blood relatives inherit it. And whoever leaves behind a debt or a loss, let him come to me, for I am his protector.” The Almighty said: And his wives are their mothers. In the word Abi it says: And his wives and their mothers, and he is a father to them. They are the mothers of the believers in honoring their right and prohibiting their marriage in support, not in looking at them and being alone with them, for it is forbidden in their right as in the right of strangers. God Almighty said: And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition. (al-Ahzab 33:53). It is not said of their daughters that they are the sisters of the believers, nor of their brothers and sisters that they are the maternal uncles and aunts of the believers. Al-Shafi’i said: Al-Zubayr married Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, who was the sister of the Mother of the Believers, but he did not say she was the aunt of the Believers. They differed as to whether they were the mothers of all believing women. It was said: They were the mothers of all believing men and women. It was said that they were the mothers of the believers, not the women. Al-Sha’bi narrated on the authority of Masruq that a woman said to Aisha, may God be pleased with her: O mother! She said: I am not your mother, I am only the mother of your men. This shows that the meaning of this motherhood is the prohibition of marrying them. God the Almighty said: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the ordinance of God, meaning in inheritance. Qatada said: Muslims used to inherit from one another through emigration. Al-Kalbi said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) established brotherhood among the people. He would establish brotherhood between two men, and if one of them died, the other would inherit from him without his agnates, until this verse was revealed: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the ordinance of God, in the ruling of God, than the believers, whom the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) established brotherhood between, and the emigrants, meaning those related by blood. Some of them are nearer to inherit from others than to inherit through faith and emigration. So this verse abrogated inheritance through brotherhood and emigration and replaced it with one of kinship. His saying: Unless you do a good deed to your guardians, he meant by good a will for those who are responsible for him from among the contracting parties. This is because when God abrogated inheritance by oath and migration, He permitted a man to bequeath to his guardian whatever he liked from his third. Mujahid said: By good, he meant support and preservation of the sanctity of the right of faith and migration. It was said: What he meant by the verse is to prove inheritance through faith and migration, meaning: And those of kinship among the believers and the emigrants are more worthy of one another, meaning: There is no inheritance between a Muslim and a disbeliever, nor between an emigrant and a non-emigrant, unless you do something good to your relatives, meaning: unless you bequeath something to your relatives even if they are not people of faith or migration, and this is the saying of Qatada, Ata’, and Ikrimah. That was written in the Book, meaning: what you mentioned about relatives being closer to one another was written in the Preserved Tablet. Al-Qurazi said: in the Torah.
33:7: God Almighty said: 7- And when We took a covenant from the prophets, to fulfill what they were entrusted with, to believe one another, and to give good tidings to one another. Muqatil said: He took their covenant to worship God, to call others to the worship of God, to believe one another, and to give sincere advice to their people, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary. These five were specifically mentioned from among the prophets because they were the people of the books and laws and the messengers of resolve. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was mentioned first because: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha’labi told us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadith told me, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya’qub al-Muqri’ told us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Sa’idi told us, Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn Bilal told us, my father told us, Sa’id told us - meaning Ibn Bashir - on the authority of Qatada on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was the first of the prophets in creation and the last of them in mission. Qatada said: This is the statement of God Almighty: And when We took a covenant from the prophets, and from you and from Noah, so He, may God bless him and grant him peace, began with him before them. And We took from them a solemn covenant, a firm pledge to fulfill what they had undertaken.
33:8: 8- To question the truthful about their truthfulness, meaning the prophets about their conveyance of the message. The wisdom in asking them, even though He knows they are truthful, is to rebuke those to whom they were sent. It was said: To ask the truthful about their deeds for the sake of God Almighty. And it was said: To ask the truthful with their mouths about the truthfulness in their hearts. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.
33:9: God Almighty said: 9- O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you, and that was when the Muslims were besieged with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the days of the Trench, when there came to you armies, meaning the confederates, who were Quraysh, Ghatafan, the Jews of Qurayzah, and Nadir, so We sent upon them a wind, which was the north wind. Ikrimah said: The south side said to the north side on the night of the confederates, “Go, let us aid the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace,” and the north side said, The lava does not blow at night, and the wind that was sent upon them was the north wind. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I was aided by the north wind, and the ‘Ad were destroyed by the south wind. God the Almighty said: And soldiers you did not see, meaning the angels. The angels did not fight that day, so God sent upon them a cold wind that uprooted the stakes, cut the tent ropes, extinguished the fires, overturned the pots, and caused the horses to clash with one another. The angels’ glorification of God increased in the corners of their army until the chief of each tribe would say: O sons of so-and-so, come to me. When they gathered around him, he would say: Escape, escape, because God sent terror upon them and they were defeated without fighting. And God is Seeing of what you do. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ruman, a client of the Al-Zubayr family, told me, on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, and someone I do not accuse, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik, and on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Bakra ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, and on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi, and on the authority of others from our scholars, some of their hadiths were included in each other: That a group of Jews, including Salam ibn Abi Al-Haqiq, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Kinanah ibn Al-Rabi’ ibn Abi Al-Haqiq, Hudah ibn Qays, and Abu Ammar Al-Wa’ili, with a group of Banu Al-Nadir and a group of Banu Wa’il, and they are the ones who formed the Confederates against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until they came to the Quraysh in Mecca and called them to war against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We will be with you against him until we eradicate him. The Quraysh said to them: O group of Jews, you are the people of the first Book and the knowledge of what we have come to differ about, we and Muhammad, so our religion is better. Or his religion? They said: Rather, your religion is better than his religion, and you are more deserving of the truth than they are. He said: They are the ones about whom God revealed: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in jibt and taghut, until His saying: And sufficient is Hell as a Blaze An-Nisa’ 51-55. When they said that to the Quraysh, they were pleased with what they had said and were encouraged to fight the Messenger of God. They gathered for that purpose, and then those Jews went out until they came to Ghatafan from Qais Ghailan. They invited them to that and informed them that they would be with them in it, and that the Quraysh had pledged allegiance to them on that, so they responded to them. So the Quraysh went out, led by Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and the Ghatafan went out, led by Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfah ibn Badr, with Fazara, and Al-Harith ibn Awf ibn Abi Haritha Al-Mari with Banu Murrah, and Mas`ud ibn Rakhila ibn Nuwayrah ibn Tarif with those of his people who followed him from Ashja`. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about them and what they had gathered for him, he dug a trench around the city. The one who suggested the trench to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Salman al-Farsi. It was the first scene Salman witnessed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was still free. He said: O Messenger of God, when we were besieged in Persia, we would dig a trench around them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, worked on it until they completed it. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid Al-Isfahani told us, Muhammad bin Ja’far Al-Tabari told us, Hammad bin Al-Hasan told us, Muhammad bin Khalid bin Uthma told us, Katheer bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Auf, my father told me, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew the line of the Trench in the Year of the Confederates, then he cut off forty cubits for every ten. The Muhajireen and Ansar argued over Salman Al-Farsi, who was a strong man. The Muhajireen said: Salman is from us, and the Ansar said: Salman is from us. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Salman is from us, the people of the House.” Amr ibn Auf said: I, Salman, Hudhayfah, An-Nu’man ibn Muqrin Al-Mazini, and six of the Ansar were forty cubits apart. We dug until we reached Dhi Naab. God brought out a white rock in the middle of the trench that broke our iron and made it difficult for us. We said: O Salman, go up to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and tell him about this rock. Either he turns away from it, for turning away is near, or he orders us to do what he says about it, for we do not like to go beyond his line. Salman went up to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was pitching a Turkish dome over it. He said: O Messenger of God, a white rock of white rock came out from the middle of the trench, broke our iron and made it difficult for us, so that neither little nor much could weave through it. So order us to do what you say about it, for we do not like to go beyond your line. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) descended the trench with Salman and the nine of them on the cleft of the trench. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took the pickaxe from Salman and struck it with a blow that split it, and lightning from it lit up what was between its two lava plains. -meaning the city- until it was as if there was a lamp in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the Takbir of Victory and the Muslims said the Takbir. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) struck it a second time and lightning flashed from it that lit up what was between its two lava plates until it was as if there was a lamp in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the Takbir of Victory and the Muslims said the Takbir. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) struck it and broke it, and lightning flashed from it that lit up what was between its lava plates until it was as if there was a lamp in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the Takbir of Victory and the Muslims said the Takbir. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) struck it and broke it, and lightning flashed from it that lit up what was between its lava plates until it was as if there was a lamp in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the Takbir of Victory and the Muslims said the Takbir. Then he took Salman’s hand and climbed it. Salman said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God, I have seen something the like of which I have never seen before. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned to the people and said: Have you seen what Salman is saying? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: I struck my first strike, and the lightning flashed, which you saw, and the palaces of Al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra lit up for me as if they were the fangs of dogs. Gabriel informed me that my nation will be victorious over them, so be of good cheer. The Muslims were filled with joy and said: Praise be to God, a true promise. He promised us victory after the siege. The hypocrites said: Do you not marvel at Muhammad making false promises to you and telling you that he can see the palaces of Al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra from Yathrib, and that they will be conquered for you, while you are only digging the trench out of fear and cannot emerge? Then the Quran was revealed: And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, ‘God and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion.’ And God revealed concerning this story: Say, ‘O God, Owner of the Kingdom.’ (Al Imran 3:26) Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Muawiyah bin Amr told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Humaid, who said: I heard Anas say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the Trench and saw the Muhajireen and Ansar digging on a cold morning. They did not have slaves to do that for them. When he saw the fatigue and hunger they were enduring, he said: O God, life is the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajireen.” They said in response to him: We are the ones who pledged allegiance to Muhammad to wage jihad as long as we live. And Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd God al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Ismail informed us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Shu`bah informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara’, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was carrying dirt on the day of the Trench until his stomach was covered in dust - or covered in dirt - and he was saying: By God, if it weren't for God, we would not have been guided, given charity, or prayed. So send down tranquility upon us and plant firmly our feet if we meet [the enemy]. Those who have transgressed against us, if they want to cause discord, we will refuse. And he raises his voice: Our father, our father. We return to the hadith of Ibn Ishaq, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished the trench, the Quraysh advanced and encamped at the place where the streams of Ruma met, from al-Jurf and al-Ghaba, with ten thousand of their Abyssinians and those who followed them from Banu Kinanah and the people of Tihamah. The Ghatafan advanced and those who followed them from Najd, and encamped at Dhanab Nuqma on the side of Uhud. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims set out and turned their backs to Sala’ with three thousand of the Muslims. He pitched his camp there, with the trench between him and the people. He ordered the women and children to be raised up onto the roofs. And the enemy of God, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, went out from Banu Nadir until he came to Ka’b ibn Asad al-Qurazi, the one who had made a treaty with Banu Qurayzah and their covenant. He had made a treaty with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his people and had pledged to him on that. When Ka’b heard of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he closed his fortress behind him. He asked permission to enter but he refused to open it for him. Huyayy called out to him: O Ka’b, open it for me. He said: “Woe to you, Huyayy! You are an ill-omened man. I have pledged to Muhammad, so I will not break what is between me and him. I have seen nothing from him but loyalty and truthfulness.” He said: Woe to you, open for me so I may speak to you. He said: I will not do it. He said: By God, if you close the door on me except for your coarseness, I will eat from it with you, so guard the man. So he opened it for him and he said: Woe to you, Ka'b, I have come to you with the glory of the age and a raging sea. I have come to you with the Quraysh with their leaders and nobles until I have brought them down at the meeting place of the torrents of Rome, and with Ghatafan with their leaders and nobles until I have brought them down with a sin of vengeance at the side of Uhud. They have pledged and agreed with me that they will not leave until they have exterminated Muhammad and those with him. Ka'b ibn Asad said to him: By God, you have come to me with the humiliation of the age and in a place whose water has been spilled by thunder and lightning, and in which there is nothing. So leave me and Muhammad and what I am doing, for I have seen nothing from Muhammad but truthfulness and loyalty. So Huyayy ibn Akhtab kept on torturing Ka'b from top to bottom until he gave him permission, on the condition that he gave him a covenant and a pact from God. If Quraysh and Ghatafan return and do not harm Muhammad, I will enter your fortress with you until what happened to you happens to me. So Ka’b ibn Asad broke his covenant and disavowed what had happened between him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the report reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims, he sent Sa`d ibn Mu`adh, one of the Banu `Abd al-Ashhal, who was at that time the chief of the Aws, and Sa`d ibn `Ubadah, one of the Banu Sa`idah, who was at that time the chief of the Khazraj, and with them `Abdullah ibn Rawahah, the brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Khawwat ibn Jubayr, the brother of the Banu `Amr ibn `Awf. He said: Go and see whether what we have heard about these people is true or not. So if it is true, then make me understand a tune that I know, and do not weaken the people. But if they are faithful to what is between us and them, then announce it openly to the people. So they went out until they reached them and found them in the worst condition they had ever heard from them. They spoke ill of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: There is no contract between us and Muhammad and no covenant. Saad bin Ubadah insulted them and they insulted him, and he was a man of harshness. Saad bin Muadh said to him: Stop insulting them, for what is between us and them is worse than insulting. Then Saad and Saad and those with them came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and greeted him and said: Adal and al-Qara, for the treachery of Adal and al-Qara against the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the companions of al-Raji’: Khubayb bin Adi and his companions. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God is Great. Be of good cheer, O group of Muslims. Then the calamity became great and the fear became intense. Their enemy approached them from above and from below them until the believers had every suspicion. Hypocrisy emerged from some of the hypocrites until Mu'tab bin Qushair, the brother of Banu Amr bin Awf, said: Muhammad promised us that we would eat the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar, yet one of us would not be able to go to the toilet. God and His Messenger promised us nothing but deception. And until Aws bin Qayzi, one of Banu Haritha bin Qayzi, said: O Messenger of God, our houses are vulnerable to the enemy, and that was in front of a group of men from his people, so give us permission to return to our homes, for they are outside the city. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed there, and the polytheists stayed there for twenty-some nights, nearly a month, and there was no war between the people except for the shooting of arrows and pebbles. When the affliction on the people became severe, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to Uyaynah ibn Hisn and to Al-Harith ibn Umar, the leaders of Ghatafan, and gave them a third of the fruits of Madinah on the condition that they return with those with them from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. A peace treaty took place between him and them, until they wrote the document but the testimony was not given. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned that to Sa`d ibn Mu`adh and Sa`d ibn `Ubadah, and consulted them about it. They said: O Messenger of God, is it something that God has commanded you to do that we must do, or something that you love and do, or something that you will do for us? He said: No, rather it is something I am making for you. By God, I am not doing that except because I saw that the Arabs had shot you with a single bow and surrounded you from every side, so I wanted to break their power over you. Saad bin Muadh said to him: O Messenger of God, we and these people were on polytheism and idol worship. We did not worship God nor did we know Him, and they did not eat a single fruit from it except as a gift or by sale. So when God honored us with Islam and strengthened us through you, we give them our money! We have no need of that. By God, we will not give them anything but the sword, until God judges between us and them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You can do that. Saad took the scroll, erased what was written on it, and then said: Let them strive against us. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims remained, and their enemy was besieging them, and there was no fighting between them, except that the horsemen of Quraysh, among them Amr ibn Abd Wudd, the brother of Banu Amir ibn Luay, and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Hubayrah ibn Abi Wahb al-Makhzumi, and Nawfal ibn Abdullah, and Dirar ibn al-Khattab, and Mirdas, the brother of Banu Muharrib ibn Fihr, had dressed for battle and went out on their horses and passed by Banu Kinanah and said: Prepare for war, O Banu Kinanah, for today you will know who the horsemen are. Then they approached the trench until they stopped at the trench, and when they saw it they said: By God, this is a trick that the Arabs had never plotted. Then they headed for a narrow place in the trench and struck their horses, so they broke through it, and they went around with them in the salt marsh between the trench and Sala’. Ali ibn Abi Talib went out with a group of Muslims until they took the gap from which they had driven their horses, and the horsemen came rushing towards them. Amr ibn Abd Wudd had fought on the day of Badr until he was wounded, but he did not witness anyone. When it was the day of the trench, he went out as a teacher to see his place. When he and his horse stood, Ali said to him: O Amr, you promised God that no man from Quraysh would invite you to one of two options except that you would take one of them from him. He said: Yes. Ali ibn Abi Talib said to him: I invite you to God, to His Messenger, and to Islam. He said: I have no need of that. He said: Then I should invite you to a duel. He said: Why, my nephew? By God, I do not want to kill you. Ali said: But by God, I want to kill you. Amr became enraged at that, so he rushed on his horse, hamstrung it, and struck… Then he turned to Ali, and they fought and fought, and Ali killed him, and his cavalry came out defeated until they stormed the trench, fleeing, and two men were killed with Amr: Munabbih bin Uthman bin Ubayd bin al-Sabbaq bin Abd al-Dar, who was hit by an arrow and died from it in Mecca, and Nawfal bin Abdullah bin al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, who had stormed the trench and got entangled in it, so they threw stones at him, and he said, O people of the Arabs, killing him is better than this, so he went down to him to kill him, and the Muslims were overwhelmed by his body, so he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to sell them his body, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We have no need for his body and its price, so he has made you suffer with him, so he left them alone with him. Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, said: “On the day of the Battle of the Trench, we were in the fortress of Banu Haritha, which was one of the most secure fortresses of Medina. Umm Sa`d ibn Mu`adh was with us in the fortress, and that was before the veil was imposed on us. Sa`d ibn Mu`adh passed by, wearing a torn shield from which his entire arm was protruding, and in his hand was a spear, and it was said: Stay a little while and you will realize the battle. There is no harm in death if the time comes. His mother said to him: “Truth be to you, my son, for by God you have permitted it.” Aisha said: “I said to her: O mother of Saad, by God I wish that Saad’s armor was longer than it is.” She said: And I feared for him where the arrow had hit him. She said: “On that day, Saad was shot by an arrow, and the kohl part of it was cut off. It was shot by Khabbab bin Qais bin Al-Arqa, one of the Banu Amir bin Lu’ayy. When it hit him, he said: ‘Take it, for I am the son of Al-Arqa.’ Saad said: ‘May God make your face sweat in the Fire.’ Then Saad said: ‘O God, if you have left anything of the war against the Quraysh, then leave me for it, for there is no people I would rather fight than a people who harmed your Messenger, denied him, and expelled him. If you have put an end to the war between us and them, then make it a martyrdom for me and do not let me die until my eyes are comforted by the Banu Qurayza, and they were his allies and clients in the pre-Islamic period.” Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Yahya bin Ibad bin Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr on the authority of his father Ibad who said: Safiyya bint Abdul Muttalib was in Fare’, the fortress of Hassan bin Thabit. She said: Hassan was there with his wife and children. Safiyya said: A Jewish man passed by us and began to circle the fortress, and the Banu Qurayzah and the children were fighting. Safiyya said: A Jewish man passed by us and began to circle the fortress, and the Banu Qurayzah had fought and severed what was between us and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and there was no one between us and them to defend us, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims were in the throats of their enemy, unable to turn away from them, when someone came to us. She said: I said: O Hassan, this Jew, as you see, is circling the fortress, and by God, I do not trust that he will reveal our faults to the Jews behind us, and he has distracted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from us, so go down to him and kill him. He said: May God forgive you, O daughter of Abdul Muttalib, by God I know that I am not the one who will do this. She said: When he said that to me and I did not see anything with him, I covered myself, then took a pole, then went down from the fortress to him, and struck him with the pole until I killed him. When I finished with him, I returned to the fortress and said: O Hassan, go down to him and loot him, for nothing prevented me from looting him except that he is a man. He said: I have no need for his loot, O daughter of Abdul Muttalib. They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were in a state of fear and severity described by God Almighty due to the presence of their enemy and their approach to them from above and from below them. Then Nu`aym ibn Mas`ud ibn `Amir from Ghatafan came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: “O Messenger of God, I have become Muslim, but my people do not know of my Islam. So order me to do whatever you wish.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: You are only one man among us, so help us if you can, for war is deception. Nu`aym ibn Mas`ud went out until he came to Banu Qurayzah, and he had been their companion in the pre-Islamic period. He said to them: O Banu Qurayzah, you know my love for you and the special relationship between me and you. They said: You have spoken the truth; you are not accused by us. He said to them: “The Quraysh and Ghatafan came to fight Muhammad, and you supported them against him. The Quraysh and Ghatafan are not the same. The country is your country, in it are your wealth, children, and women. You are not able to move from it to another. The Quraysh and Ghatafan, their wealth, children, and women, are far away. If they see a chance or booty, they will seize it, but if it is something else, they will seize it.” They went back to their country and left the man alone. You cannot defeat the man in your country if he leaves you alone. Do not fight with the people until you take a hostage from among their nobles, who will be a trustworthy partner for you and will fight Muhammad with you until you defeat him. They said: You have given advice and sound counsel. Then he went out until he reached the Quraysh and said to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and the men of Quraysh who were with him, "O people of Quraysh, you know my love for you and my separation from Muhammad. A matter has reached me and I feel it is my right to convey to you sincere advice, so keep it a secret." They said, We will. He said, "You know that the Jews have regretted what they did between themselves and Muhammad, and they sent word to him, 'We regret what we have done. Would it please you if we took from the two tribes, from Quraysh and Ghatafan, some of their noblemen and gave them to you so that you could strike off their heads, and then we would be with you in dealing with whoever remains of them?" So he sent word to them, "Yes. But if the Jews send to you seeking hostages from among your men, do not hand over a single man to them." Then he went out until he came to Ghatafan and said: O people of Ghatafan, you are my origin and my clan and the people dearest to me, and I do not see you accusing me. They said: You have spoken the truth. He said: Then conceal it from me. They said: We will do. Then he said to them the same as he had said to Quraysh and warned them what he had warned them. When it was the night of Saturday in the fifth year of Shawwal, and among what he had done to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Sufyan and the leaders of Ghatafan sent to Banu Qurayzah Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl with a group of Quraysh and Ghatafan. They said to them: We are not in a place of residence. The hooves and the hoof have perished, so go out to fight until we fight Muhammad and settle what is between us and him. Banu Qurayzah said to them: Today is Saturday, and it is a day on which we do not do anything. Some of us have committed an act that was not hidden from you. However, we are not those who will fight with you until you give us a hostage from among your men, who will be in our hands as a trust for us until we fight Muhammad. So we We fear that if the war becomes severe and the fighting intensifies, you will go to your country and leave us, and the man is in our country, and we are not able to do that with Muhammad. So when the messengers returned to them with what Banu Qurayzah had said, Quraysh and Ghatafan said: We know, by God, that what Nuaym ibn Mas`ud told you is true. So they sent to Banu Qurayzah: By God, we will not hand over to you a single man from our men. If you want to fight, then go out and fight. Banu Qurayzah said when the messengers reached them with this: What Nuaym ibn Mas`ud told you is true. The people only want to fight. If they find an opportunity, they will seize it, and if not, they will retreat to their country and leave you and the man alone in your country. So they sent to Quraysh and Ghatafan: By God, we will not fight with you until you give us a hostage. But they refused, and God failed them, and God sent a wind against them on very cold winter nights, and it began to overturn their pots and throw them away. Their vessels. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about their disagreement, he called Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and sent him to them to see what the people had done that night. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, and others narrated on the authority of Ibrahim al-Tamimi, on the authority of his father, who said: A young man from the people of Kufa said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: O Abu Abdullah, did you see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and accompany him? He said: Yes, O my nephew. He said: How did you act? He said: By God, we were struggling. The young man said: By God, if we had lived to see him, we would not have left him walking on the earth, and we would have carried him on our shoulders and served him, and we did this and that. Hudhayfah said: O my nephew, by God, I saw myself on the Night of the Confederates with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: Who will get up and go to these people and bring us report of them, so that God may admit him to Paradise? Not a single man among us got up. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then turned to us and said the same, and the people were silent. Not a single man among us got up. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed a part of the night, then turned to us and said: Who will stand and see what the people have done, so that he may be my companion in Paradise? Not a single man got up because of the intensity of the fear, the intensity of the hunger, and the intensity of the cold. When no one got up, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called me and said: O Hudhayfah! I had no choice but to get up when he called me. I said: At your service, O Messenger of God! I got up to go to him, and my sides were shaking. He wiped my head and face, then said: Go to these people until you bring me report of them, and do not say anything until you return to me. Then he said: O God, protect him from in front of him and behind him and from his right and from his left, and from above him and from below him. So I took my arrow, and strapped on my weapon, then I set off walking toward them as if I were walking in a bathhouse. I went and entered among the people, and he had sent a wind upon them. And the soldiers of God are doing to them what they are doing, leaving them no cooking pot, no fire, and no building. Abu Sufyan was sitting warming himself, so I took an arrow and put it in the bow of my bow, and I wanted to shoot him. If I had shot it, I would have hit him, but I remembered the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Do not do anything until you return to me. So I put my arrow back in my quiver. When Abu Sufyan saw what the wind and the soldiers of God were doing to them, leaving them no cooking pot, no fire, and no building, he stood up and said: O people of Quraysh, let each man among you take the hand of the one sitting with him and see who he is. So I took the hand of the one sitting with me and said: Who are you? He said: Glory be to God! Don’t you know that I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so? And behold, he was a man from Hawazin. Abu Sufyan said: O people of Quraysh, by God, you have not become in a permanent place. The mounts and hoofs have been destroyed, the Banu Qurayzah have betrayed us, and we have experienced from them what we disliked, and we have encountered from this wind what you see, so depart, for I am departing. Then he went to his camel which was tied up and sat on it, then he struck it and it leapt with it on three occasions, and he did not release its halter until it was standing. Ghatafan heard what the Quraysh had done, so they fled back to their country. He said: So I returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as if I were walking in a bathhouse. I came to him while he was standing praying. When he finished, I told him the report, and he laughed until his fangs were visible in the blackness of the night. He said: So when I told him and finished, I was calm and the warmth left me. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought me closer to him, and made me lie down at his feet, and threw the edge of his garment over me, and pressed my chest to the bottom of his feet. I did not stop sleeping until morning. When morning came, he said: Get up, O Noman.
33:10: The Almighty said: 10- When they came upon you from above you, meaning: from the parts of the valley from the east, and they were Asad and Ghatafan, and over them were Malik bin Auf Al-Nasri and Uyaynah bin Hisn Al-Fazari with a thousand from Ghatafan, and with them were Tulaiha bin Khuwaylid Al-Asadi in Banu Asad and Huyayy bin Akhtab in the Jews of Banu Qurayzah, and from below you, meaning: from the bottom of the valley, from the west, and they were Quraysh and Kinanah, over them was Abu Sufyan bin Harb in Quraysh and those who followed him, and Abu Al-Awar Amr bin Sufyan Al-Sulami from the direction of the Trench. It is said that the Battle of the Trench was caused by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelling Banu Nadir from their homes. And when the eyes turned away, they turned and stared / from terror, and it was said: they turned away from everything and did not look except at their enemy, and the hearts reached the throats, so they moved from their places until they reached the throats from fear, and the throat is the hollow of the windpipe, and this is a metaphor, he expressed it to express the intensity of fear, Al-Farra’ said: its meaning is that they were avoided, and the path of the coward when his fear is intense is that his lungs swell, and when the lungs swell, they raise the heart to the throat, and for this reason it is said of the coward: his magic swelled. And you have different thoughts about God, meaning: your thoughts differed. The hypocrites thought that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, may God be pleased with them, would be exterminated, while the believers thought that victory and triumph would be theirs. The people of Medina, Ash-Sham, and Abu Bakr read al-Zununa, al-Rasula, and al-Sabila with the alif in both connected and paused sentences, because it is written in the copies of the Qur’an. The people of Basra and Hamza read without the alif in both cases, according to the original principle. The others read with the alif in the pause, not in the connected sentences, to match the beginnings of the verses.
33:11: 11- There he was tested, meaning: at that time the believers were tested, by confinement and fighting, to distinguish the sincere from the hypocrites, and they were shaken with a violent shaking, they were moved violently.
33:12: 12- And when the hypocrites said, Mu’tab bin Qushair, and it was said: Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions, and those in whose hearts is disease, doubt and weak belief: God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion, which is what the hypocrites say: Muhammad promises us the conquest of the palaces of Syria and Persia, and one of us cannot go beyond his tent. This, by God, is delusion.
33:13: 13- And when a group of them said, meaning: of the hypocrites, who were Aws Bani Qayzi and his companions, O people of Yathrib, meaning Medina. Abu Ubaidah said: Yathrib is the name of a land, and the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is in a part of it. In some reports, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade calling Medina Yathrib, and said: It is Tabah, as if he disliked this word. You have no place to stay. The general public read it with a fat-ha on the meem, meaning: you have no place to stay and reside in. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and Hafs read it with a damma on the meem, meaning: you have no place to stay. So return, to your homes from following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: from fighting to your dwellings. And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, and they were Banu Khartha and Banu Salamah, saying, ‘Our houses are exposed,’ meaning: empty and lost, and located near the enemy and where thieves are feared. Abu Raja’ al-Attardi read ‘awrah with a kasra on the waw, meaning: short-walled, easy for thieves to enter. So God denied them, saying, And it is not exposed; they only want to flee, meaning: they only want to flee.
33:14: 14- And if you had entered upon them, meaning: if you had entered upon the city, meaning these armies that they want to fight, and they are the parties, from its regions, its sides and its regions, the plural of country, then asked for the fitnah, meaning: polytheism, they would have come to it, they would have given it. The people of Hijaz read they would have come to it in a shortened form, meaning: they would have resorted to it and done it and turned back from Islam. And they would not have remained there, meaning: they would not have considered the fitnah, except for a little, and they would have hastened to respond to polytheism, content with it. This is the opinion of most of the commentators. Al-Hasan and Al-Farra’ said: They did not stay in Medina after the disbelief was given to them except for a short time until they perished.
33:15: 15- And they had already made a covenant with God before, that is, before the Battle of the Trench, that they would not turn their backs, from their enemy, that is, that they would not be defeated. Yazid bin Ruman said: They are Banu Haritha. They intended on the day of Uhud to fail with Banu Salamah, but when what happened about them happened, they made a covenant with God that they would not return to something like it. Qatada said: They were people who had been absent from the Battle of Badr and had seen the honor and virtue that God had given the people of Badr. They said: If God lets us witness a fight, we will fight. So God brought that to them. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: They were seventy men who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the night of Al-Aqabah, and they said: Set whatever conditions you wish for your Lord and for yourself. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I set a condition for my Lord that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and I set a condition for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves, your wives and your children from.” They said: If we do that, what will we have, O Messenger of God? He said: You will have victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. They said: We have done that. And that was their covenant. This statement is not satisfactory to me, because those who pledged allegiance on the night of Aqaba were seventy people, and there was no one among them who doubted or said such a statement. Rather, the verse is about a people who pledged to God that they would fight and not flee, but they broke the pledge. And the covenant of God was responsible for it.
33:16: 16- Say, to them, Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, which was decreed for you because whoever has his appointed time will die or be killed, and then you will not enjoy [yourselves] except for a little, meaning: you will not enjoy yourself after fleeing except for the duration of your appointed time, which is short.
33:17: 17- Say, ‘Who is it that can protect you from God?’ That is, prevent you from His punishment, if He intends to do you harm, defeat, or intends to show you mercy, victory, and they will not find for themselves besides God a protector, That is, a relative who benefits them, nor a helper, That is, a helper who protects them.
33:18: 18- God knows those among you who hold back, meaning those who discourage people from following the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who say to their brothers, ‘Come to us,’ meaning, return to us and leave Muhammad alone, and do not witness the war with him, for we fear your destruction. Qatada said: These were hypocrites who discouraged the supporters of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to their brothers: Muhammad and his companions are nothing but a morsel of food. If they were meat, Abu Sufyan and his companions would have swallowed them. Leave the man alone, for he is doomed. Muqatil said: It was revealed about the hypocrites. The Jews sent word to the hypocrites and said: What makes you kill yourselves at the hands of Abu Sufyan and those with him? If they gain power over you this time, they will not spare any of you. We feel sorry for you. You are our brothers and neighbors. Come to us. Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions turned to the believers, hindering them and frightening them with Abu Sufyan and those with him. They said: If they gain power over you, they will not spare any of you. What do you hope for from Muhammad? He has no good in him; he will only kill us here. Let us go to our brothers, meaning the Jews. The believers only increased in faith and hope for reward because of what the hypocrites said. The Almighty said: And they do not come to battle/war, except a little, for show and to be heard without expecting anything. And if that little was for God, it would be a lot.
33:19: 19- Stingy with you, miserly with spending in the way of God and support. Qatada said: miserly with the spoils. God described them as miserly and cowardly, saying: But when fear comes, you will see them looking at you, their eyes rolling, in their heads from fear and cowardice, like one who has fainted from death, meaning: like the rolling of one who has fainted from death, because the one who is close to death and is overcome by its causes loses his mind and his sight is fixed, so he does not blink. But when the fear has gone, they will smite you, they will hurt you and throw you in a state of security, with sharp tongues, “sharp tongues,” plural of hard hadid. An eloquent orator with a sharp tongue is called maslaq, “musallaq,” sallaq, and sallaq. Ibn Abbas said: salaqoqum means: they will attack you and attack you with disparagement and backbiting. Qatada said: They stretched out their tongues against you when dividing the spoils, saying: Give us, for we witnessed the battle with you, so you are not more deserving of the spoils than us. They are the most miserly people when it comes to spoils, and the most cowardly people when it comes to battle. Miserious with good means: when it comes to spoils, they quarrel with the believers. Those did not believe, so God rendered their deeds worthless. Muqatil said: God rendered their jihad null and void. And that is easy for God.
33:20: 20- They think, meaning: these hypocrites, the parties, meaning: Quraysh, Ghatafan and the Jews, that they have not gone, they did not turn away from fighting them out of cowardice and fear, and they have turned away, and if the parties come, meaning: they return to them to fight after going, they would wish that they were in the desert among the bedouins, meaning: they wish that they were in the desert of the bedouins out of fear and cowardice. It is said: bada badawan, if he went out to the desert, they ask about your report, your report and what happened to your situation. Ya'qub read: yasaa'aloon with a shaddah and a long vowel, meaning: they ask each other, and if they were, meaning: these hypocrites, among you, they would not have fought except a little, as an excuse, meaning: they fight a little to establish their excuse, and they say, We fought. Al-Kalbi said: except a little, meaning: pelting with stones. Muqatil said: Except for hypocrisy and reputation without any expectation.
33:21: God Almighty said: 21- There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern to follow. Asim read: an example where he was, with a damma on the hamza, and the rest read it with a kasra. These are two dialects, meaning: a good example. It is a verb from to imitate, like example from to follow, a noun in place of a verbal noun, meaning: follow him in a good way if you support the religion of God and support the Messenger and do not stay behind him, and be patient with what befalls you as he did when his front tooth was broken and his face was wounded, and his uncle was killed and he was harmed with various kinds of harm, so he consoled you with that himself, so do likewise and follow his Sunnah. for him whose hope is in God, instead of his saying: for you, and it is a specification after generalization for the believers, meaning: the example is in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for him whose hope is in God. Ibn Abbas said: He hopes for the reward of God. Muqatil said: He fears God and the Last Day, meaning he fears the Day of Resurrection on which deeds will be rewarded, and he remembers God often, in all situations, in good times and bad.
33:22: Then he described the state of the believers when they met the parties, saying: 22- And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, in submission to God’s command and belief in His promise: This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth. God promised them what was mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? until His saying: Unquestionably, the victory of God is near. Al-Baqarah 2:214. The verse implies that the believers will be afflicted with such a calamity. So when they saw the confederates and the hardship that befell them, they said: This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger spoke the truth. “And it only increased them in faith and submission,” meaning: belief in God and submission to God’s command.
33:23: God Almighty says: 23- Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God, meaning: they fulfilled what they pledged to God and kept it. And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, meaning: he completed his vow and fulfilled his pledge, so he was patient in jihad until he was martyred. Naḥb is a vow, and naḥb also means death. Muqatil said: He fulfilled his vow meaning: his appointed time, so he was killed fulfilling it, meaning Hamza and his companions. It was said: He fulfilled his vow meaning: he did his best in fulfilling the pledge, from the Arabs’ saying: We love so-and-so in his travels all day and night, if he extended his time and did not stop. And among them is he who awaits, martyrdom. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Among them are those who met their fate, those who were martyred on the day of Badr and Uhud, and among them are those who are waiting, meaning: those who remain after these believers are waiting for one of two things, either martyrdom or victory, and they have not changed their covenant at all. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Saeed Al-Khuza’i told us, Abdul A’la told us, on the authority of Humayd, who said: I asked Anas, and Amr bin Zararah told me, Ziyad told us, Humayd Al-Tawil told me, on the authority of Anas, who said: My uncle Anas bin Al-Nadr was absent from the battle of Badr, and he said: O Messenger of God, I was absent from the first battle in which you fought the polytheists. If God lets me witness the battle against the polytheists, God will see what I do. Then, when the day of Uhud came and the Muslims were defeated, he said: O God, I apologize to You for what these people did - meaning his companions - and I disavow before You what these people did - meaning the polytheists. Then he advanced and Sa’d bin Mu’adh met him, and he said: O Sa’d bin Mu’adh, Paradise, by the Lord of Al-Nadr, I smell its fragrance from before Uhud. Sa’d said: So, O Messenger of God, I could not find what he did. Anas said: So we found on him eighty-odd sword wounds, spear thrusts, or arrow wounds. With an arrow, and we found him killed and the polytheists had mutilated him, and no one recognized him except his sister by his finger. Anas said: We thought or saw that this verse was revealed about him and his likes: Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God, to the end of the verse. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Khabbab ibn al-Arat, who said: “We migrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the way of God, seeking the face of God, so our reward is obligatory upon God. Some of us passed away without eating anything from their reward, including Mus’ab ibn Umair, who was killed on the Day of Uhud. Nothing was found for him to be shrouded in except a cloak. When we placed it on his head, his feet would come out, and when we placed it on his feet, his head would come out. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Place it near his head and put some idhkhir on his feet.’ He said: ‘Whoever has its fruit ripe, he will be guided by it.’” Abu al-Muzaffar Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tamimi told us, Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman, known as Ibn Abi Nasr, told us, Khaythama ibn Sulayman ibn Haydara al-Atrabulsi told us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Jawhari told us in Antioch, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, al-Salt ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Abu Nasrah, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at Talha ibn Ubayd God and said: ‘Whoever would like to look at a man walking on the face of the earth who has fulfilled his vow, let him look at this man.’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Abi Shaybah told us, Wakee bin Ismail told us, “On the authority of Qais, he said: I saw Talha’s hand paralyzed, with which he protected the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud.”
33:24: God Almighty says: 24- That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness, meaning: the reward for their truthfulness, and their truthfulness is the fulfillment of the covenant, and punish the hypocrites if He wills or accept their repentance, so He guides them to faith, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
33:25: 25- And God repelled those who disbelieved, from Quraysh and Ghatafan, in their fury, their hearts were not satisfied by obtaining what they wanted, they did not obtain any good, victory, and God spared the believers the fighting, with the angels and the wind, and God is Powerful and Exalted in Might, powerful in His kingdom and Exalted in His vengeance.
33:26: 26- And He sent down those who supported them from among the People of the Scripture, meaning: those who aided the confederates from Quraysh and Ghatafan against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims, and they are Banu Qurayzah, from their fortresses, their strongholds and strongholds, the singular of which is saysiyah, and from it the horn, the fork of a rooster, and the thorn are called saysiyah. This is because when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke up on the night in which the confederates had returned to their country, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers had returned from the Trench to Medina, and they laid down their weapons, then at noon Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wearing a turban of brocade, on a saddlebag with a saddle on it and a velvet of brocade on it, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with Zaynab bint Jahsh while she was washing his head and had washed his side, so he said: Have you laid down your weapons, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes. Gabriel said: May God forgive you. The angels have not laid down their weapons for forty nights, and you have only just returned from pursuing the people. It was narrated that dust was on the face of Gabriel, peace be upon him, and his horse, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, began wiping the dust off his face and horse, and said: God commands you to march to Banu Qurayzah, so rush to them, for I have cut their strings, opened their gates, and left them in an earthquake and confusion. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered a crier to announce: Whoever is listening and obedient should not pray the Asr prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, sent Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, with his banner to them, and the people rushed to it. Ali, may God be pleased with him, marched until he approached the fortresses, and he heard them making ugly remarks to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. He turned back and met the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, on the road, and said: O Messenger of God, it does not matter if you approach these wicked people. He said: Why? I think you heard them insulting me. He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: If they had seen me, they would not have said anything like that. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, approached their fortresses, he said: O brothers of monkeys and pigs, has God disgraced you and brought down His vengeance upon you? They said: O Abu al-Qasim, you were not ignorant. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by his companions at the two mountains before reaching Banu Qurayzah. He said, Did anyone pass by you? They said, “Yes, O Messenger of God. Dihya bin Khalifah Al-Kalbi passed by us on a white mule with a saddlebag on it, covered with a brocade velvet.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, That was Gabriel, sent to Banu Qurayzah to shake their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Banu Qurayzah, he dismounted at one of their wells in a corner of their property. People followed him, and some men came to him after the last evening prayer, and they had not prayed the afternoon prayer, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said: No one should pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. So they prayed the afternoon prayer there after the last evening prayer, and God did not criticize them for that, nor did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rebuke them for it. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them for twenty-five nights until the siege was exhausting them, and God cast terror into their hearts. Huyayy ibn Akhtab entered the fortress of Banu Qurayzah when the Quraysh and Ghatafan had withdrawn from them, fulfilling the covenant he had made with Ka’b ibn Asad. When they were certain that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would not leave them until he fought them, Ka'b ibn Asad said, O group of Jews, what you see has happened to you, and I present to you three options, so take whichever you wish. They said, What are they? He said, "We will follow this man and believe him, for by God it has become clear to you that he is a prophet sent by God and that he is the one you find in your Book. Then you will be safe regarding your homes, your wealth, your children, and your women." They said, We will never depart from the rulings of the Torah, nor will we replace them with anything else. He said, "If you refuse this, then let us kill our sons and women, then go out to Muhammad as men brandishing swords, leaving behind us nothing that would worry us until God judges between us and Muhammad. If we perish, we perish, and we have left behind us nothing to fear for, and if we are victorious, by my life, we will take the women and children." They said, We will kill these poor people, for what good is there in living after them? He said: If you refuse this, then tonight is the eve of the Sabbath, and perhaps Muhammad and his companions have felt secure on that day, so come down so that we may take Muhammad and his companions by surprise. They said: Shall we spoil our Sabbath and do on it what those before us did not do? As for those whom you have done, they have been transformed into what you are not unaware of? He said: Not a man among you has ever spent a single night in this lifetime being resolute. He said: Then they sent to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saying: Send to us Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir, the brother of Banu Amr ibn Awf, who were allies of the Aws, so that we may consult him about our affair. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent him to them, and when they saw him, the men stood up to him, and the women and children were delighted with him, weeping in his face out of compassion for them. They said: O Abu Lubabah, do you think we should submit to the judgment of Muhammad? He said: Yes. They said: What will be done to us when we come down? Then he pointed with his hand to the ring of slaughter. Abu Lubabah said: By God, my feet did not move until I knew that I had betrayed God and His Messenger. Then Abu Lubabah went on his way and did not come to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until he was tied to one of its pillars in the mosque. He said: I will not leave this place until God accepts my repentance for what I have done. I swear to God that I will never tread on Banu Qurayzah again, and that God will never see me in a land where I betrayed God and His Messenger. When the report reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he was slow to come, he said: If he had come to me, I would have asked forgiveness for him. But if he has done what he has done, I will not let him leave his place until God accepts his repentance. Then God revealed the repentance of Abu Lubabah to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was in the house of Umm Salamah. Umm Salamah said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughing, so I said: Why are you laughing, O Messenger of God? May God make your teeth laugh. He said: He accepted Abu Lubabah’s repentance. I said: Shall I not give him the good report of that, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes, if you wish. So she stood at the door of her room, and that was before the veil was imposed on them, and she said: O Abu Lubabah, be of good cheer, for God has accepted your repentance.
