He said: The people rushed towards him to release him, but he said: No, by God, until the Messenger of God is the one who releases me with his own hand. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by him outside until morning, he released him, then he said: Tha’laba bin Shu’ba, Asid bin Shu’ba, and Asid bin Ubaid, who are a group of Banu Hudhayl, are not from Qurayza or Nadir, their lineage is more than that, they are the paternal cousins of the people. They converted to Islam that night in which Banu Qurayza submitted to the judgment of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And on that night Amr bin Sa’di Al-Qurazi went out and passed by the guards of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Muhammad bin Maslama Al-Ansari was in charge that night. When he saw him, he said: Who is this? He said: Amr ibn Sa'di. Amr had refused to join Banu Qurayzah in their treachery against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he said: I will never betray Muhammad. Muhammad ibn Maslama said when he recognized him: O God, do not deprive me of the mistakes of the noble. Then he set him free. He went out on his way until he spent the night in the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in Medina that night. Then he went, not knowing where he was going on God's earth. His situation was mentioned to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he said: That is a man whom God has saved through his loyalty. Some people claim that he had entrusted Rumah with those whom he entrusted from Banu Qurayzah when they submitted to the judgment of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so his arrow was lying there, not knowing where it went. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the same thing about him, and God knows best. When morning came, they submitted to the judgment of the Messenger of God. The Aws jumped up and said: O Messenger of God, they are our clients, not the Khazraj. I did to the clients of the Khazraj yesterday what you know. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had besieged the Banu Qaynuqa’ before Banu Qurayzah, and they were allies of the Khazraj. They submitted to his judgment, and Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul asked them about it, so he gave them to him. When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you not satisfied, O people of the Aws, that a man from among you should rule over them? They said: Yes. He said: That is up to Sa`d ibn Mu`adh. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had placed Sa`d ibn Mu`adh in the tent of a Muslim woman called Rufaydah in his mosque. She used to treat the wounded and consider herself a servant of those Muslims who had a loss. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had said to his people when he was struck by an arrow in the trench: Place him in Rufaydah’s tent until I visit him soon. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had given him judgment over Banu Qurayzah, his people came to him and carried him on a donkey for which they had made a leather cushion. He was a large man. Then they came with him to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and they said: O Abu `Amr, be kind to your clients, for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only appointed you to do that so that you would be kind to them. When they increased his anger, he said: It is time for Sa`d not to be deterred by the blame of any blamer for the sake of God. Some of his people who were with him returned to the house of Banu al-Ashhal and the men of Banu Qurayzah informed them of the report of the death of the Prophet before Sa`d ibn Mu`adh reached them. He taught him what he had heard from him. When Sa`d reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Rise up to your master and bring him down. So they rose up to him and said: “O Abu `Amr, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has appointed you over your clients to judge them.” Sa`d said: You have God’s covenant and pledge that the judgment in it is what you judge. They said: Yes. He said: And on those who are here in the area where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is, and he turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of respect for him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes. Saad said: Then I rule concerning them that the men be killed, the wealth divided, and the children and women be taken captive. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Saad: You have ruled concerning them with the judgment of God from above seven heavens. Then they were brought down, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, imprisoned them in the house of Bint Al-Harith, a woman from Banu Al-Najjar. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the market of Medina, which is its market today, and he dug a trench in it, then he sent to them and their necks were struck in those trenches. He took them out to him in groups, and among them was the enemy of God, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Ka’b ibn Asad, the chief of the people, and they were six hundred or seven hundred, and the one who reported them said they were between eight hundred and nine hundred. They said to Ka’b ibn Asad while he was taking them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in groups: O Ka’b, what do you see of what will be done to us? Ka’b said: In every place? You do not understand. Do you not see that the caller does not desist, and that whoever among you takes him does not return? By God, it is killing. This was the way of life until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished with them. Then Huyayy ibn Akhtab, the enemy of God, came, wearing an apple-sized garment that he had torn on himself from every side, like the place of a fingertip, fingertip by fingertip, so that he would not be taken away by his hands, tied to his neck with a rope. When he looked at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said, By God, I do not blame myself for my enmity towards you, but he who abandons God will be abandoned. Then he turned to the people and said, O people, there is nothing wrong with the command of God, a Book, a decree, and an epic battle that was written for the Children of Israel. Then he sat down and struck off his head. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that she said: “No women of Banu Qurayzah were killed except one woman. She said: ‘By God, she was sitting next to me, talking to me and laughing inside and out.’ While the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was killing their men with swords, a voice called out her name: ‘Where is so-and-so?’ She said: ‘I am, by God.’ I said: ‘Woe to you, what is wrong with you?’ She said: ‘Should I be killed?’ I said: ‘Why?’ She said: ‘Something I have told you.’ He then took her and struck off her head. Aisha used to say: ‘I will never forget how amazed I was at her good nature and how much she laughed, even though I knew she was going to be killed.’” Al-Waqidi said: “The name of that woman was Shababah, the wife of al-Hakam al-Qurazi. She had killed Khallad ibn Suwayd. She threw a millstone at him, so the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) called for her and struck off her head with Khallad ibn Suwayd. He said: ‘Ali and al-Zubayr were striking the heads of Banu Qurayzah, and the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was sitting there.” Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri that Az-Zubayr ibn Bata Al-Qurazi, who was called Abu Abd Al-Rahman, had shown favor to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas during the pre-Islamic period on the day of Bu’ath. He seized him, cut his forelock, and then set him free. On the day of Qurayzah, he came to him as an old man and said: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, do you know me? He said: Is someone like you who is ignorant of someone like me? He said: I wanted to reward you for your favor with me. He said: The generous rewards the generous. Then Thabit came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, Az-Zubayr has shown favor with me and has shown favor to me, and I want to reward him for it, so pardon me for his blood. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: It is yours. So he came to him and said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has pardoned me for your blood.” He said: He is an old man with no family or children, so what can he do with his life? Thabit came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, his family and his wealth? He said: They are yours. So he came to him and said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave me your wife and your children, so they are yours. He said: The people of the house of Hijaz have no wealth, so how can they remain like that? Thabit came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: What is it, O Messenger of God? He said: It is yours. So he came to him and said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has given me your wealth, so it is yours. He said: O Thabit, what did God do with the one whose face was a Chinese mirror in which the virgins of the tribe could be seen? Ka'b ibn Asad? He said: He was killed. He said: What did the master of the towns and the desert, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, do? He said: He was killed. He said: What did our leader do when we attacked and our protector when we attacked, Azal ibn Shamwil? He said: He was killed. He said: What did the two councils do? Meaning Banu Ka'b ibn Qurayzah and Banu Amr ibn Qurayzah? He said: They went and were killed. He said: Then I ask you with my hand in your possession, Thabit, except that you join me with the people, for by God there is no good in life after these people. I will not be patient for God’s sake for a period of time until I meet my beloved ones. Thabit brought him forward and struck his neck. When Abu Bakr al-Siddiq heard his saying that he would meet his beloved ones, he said: By God, he will meet them in the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever. They said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had ordered the killing of those of them who had ramified their property, then he divided the wealth of Banu Qurayzah, their women and children among the Muslims. On that day, he announced two shares for horses and two shares for men, and he took out one-fifth of it, so the rider got three shares, the horse got two shares, his rider got one share, and the foot soldier who did not have a horse got one share. The number of horses was thirty-six, and this was the first spoils to be taken, then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Sa`d ibn Zayd al-Ansari, brother of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, with captives from Banu Qurayzah to Najd, and he bought horses and weapons for them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had chosen for himself from among their women Rayhana bint `Amr ibn Khananah, one of the women of Banu `Amr ibn Qurayzah, and she remained with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until he died while she was in his possession. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was keen to marry her and impose a veil on her, so she said: O Messenger of God, rather leave me in your possession, for it is easier for me and for you. When she was taken captive, she hated Islam and refused to accept anything but Judaism. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, removed her and was displeased with her situation. While he was with his companions, he heard the sound of sandals behind him and said, This belongs to Tha’laba ibn Shu’ba, giving me good report of Rayhana’s conversion to Islam. So he came to him and said, O Messenger of God, Rayhana has converted to Islam. This pleased him. When the affair of Banu Qurayzah was over, Sa`d ibn Mu`adh’s wound burst open. This was because he had made supplication after he had judged Banu Qurayzah as he had judged, saying: “O God, You know that there are no people I would rather fight than a people who denied Your Messenger. O God, if You have left anything of the war of Quraysh against Your Messenger, then keep me for it, and if You have ended the war between him and them, then take me to You.” His words burst open, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned him to his tent that had been pitched over him in the mosque. Aisha said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, and `Umar were present. By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, I could tell `Umar’s crying from Abu Bakr’s crying, and I was in my room.” She said: “And they were as God, the Most High, said: ‘Compassionate among themselves’” (al-Fath 48:29). The conquest of Banu Qurayzah took place at the end of Dhul-Qi`dah in the fifth year of the Hijrah. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, Israel told us, I heard Abu Ishaq say, I heard Sulayman bin Sard say, “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say when the confederates were expelled from him: Now we will attack them and they will not attack us. We will march towards them.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “There is no god but God alone. He honored His soldiers, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone. There is nothing after Him.” God Almighty said in the story of Qurayza: “And He brought down those who supported them among the People of the Scripture from their strongholds and cast terror into their hearts. A party you killed,” meaning the men. It is said that they were six hundred, and you took captive a party, meaning the women and children. It is said that they were seven hundred and fifty, and it is said that they were nine hundred.
33:27: 27- And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, their wealth, and a land which you had not yet trodden, yet, Ibn Zayd and Muqatil said: He meant Khaybar. Qatada said: We were told that it was Mecca. Al-Hasan said: Persia and Rome. Ikrimah said: Every land that will be conquered until the Day of Resurrection. And God is over all things competent.
33:28: God Almighty said: 28- “O Prophet, tell your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you,” the provision of divorce, and release you with gracious release.
33:29: 29- And if you desire God and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, then indeed, God has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward. The reason for the revelation of this verse is that the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked him for something of worldly goods, and asked him to increase their spending, and they hurt him with the jealousy of some of them towards others. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) abandoned them and swore that he would not approach them for a month and did not go out to his companions. They said: What is the matter with him? They used to say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced his wives. Umar said: I will tell you about his matter. He said: So I entered upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, have you divorced them? He said: No. I said: O Messenger of God, I entered the mosque and the Muslims were saying: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced his wives. Should I go down and tell them that you did not divorce them? He said: Yes, if you wish. So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, should not divorce his wives.” Then this verse was revealed: “And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it. But if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those charged with authority among them, then those who can investigate it would have known about it among them.” An-Nisa’ 4:83. So I was the one who investigated that information, and God revealed the verse of choice. On that day, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had nine women under him: five from Quraysh 106:Aisha bint Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Hafsa bint Umar, Umm Habiba bint Abu Sufyan, Umm Salama bint Abi Umayya, and Sawda bint Zam’a. And non-Quraysh women: Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyya, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyya, Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Khaybariyya, and Juwayriyya bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiya, may God be pleased with them. When the verse of choice was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began with Aisha, and she was the most beloved of them to him. He gave her a choice and recited the Qur’an to her, and she chose God, His Messenger, and the house of God. The Hereafter, and she saw joy on the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she followed her in that. Qatada said: When they chose God and His Messenger, God thanked them for that and restricted it to them, saying: It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Zuhair bin Harb told us, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Zaki bin Ishaq told us, Abu Al-Zubayr told us on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: Abu Bakr entered seeking permission to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he found the people sitting at his door, and he had not given permission to any of them. He said: So he gave permission to Abu Bakr and he entered, then Umar came and sought permission and he gave him permission, and he found the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sitting surrounded by his wives, silent and sullen. He said: I will say something that will make the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, laugh. He said: O Messenger of God, if you had seen the daughter of Kharijah asking me for support, I would have gone to her and slapped her on the neck. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed and said: They are around me as you see, asking me for support. Abu Bakr went to Aisha and slapped her on the neck, and Umar went to Hafsa and slapped her on the neck, both of them saying: Do not ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he handed over something that he never had, then he kept away from them for a month or twenty-nine, then this verse was revealed: O Prophet, tell your wives, until he reached: For the good among you is a great reward, he said: So he started with Aisha and said: O Aisha, I want to present to you a matter that I would like you not to rush into until you consult your parents. She said: What is it, O Messenger of God? So he recited the verse to her. She said: O Messenger of God, should I consult my parents? Rather, I choose God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter. And I ask you not to tell any of your wives what I have said. He said: No woman of them will ask me except that I will tell her. Indeed, God did not send me to be difficult or to be difficult, but He sent me as a teacher and makes things easy. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore that he would not enter upon his wives for a month.” Al-Zuhri said, “Urwah ibn al-Zubayr told me on the authority of Aisha that she said: ‘When twenty-nine days had passed, which I had counted, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon me.’ She said, ‘He began with me, and I said, ‘O Messenger of God, you swore that you would not enter upon us for a month, and you have entered upon twenty-nine days, which I had counted?’ He said, ‘The month is twenty-nine.’” Scholars differed regarding this option: Was it a delegation of divorce to them until the choice was made by himself or not? Al-Hasan, Qatada, and most of the scholars held the view that it was not a delegation of divorce, but rather he gave them the choice that if they chose this world, he would divorce them, based on the statement of God the Almighty: Then come, I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release. The evidence for this is that their response was not immediate, as he said to Aisha, Do not hasten until you consult your parents. In the case of delegation of divorce, the response should be immediate. Some people said that it was a delegation of divorce if they chose themselves, it was a divorce. Scholars differed on the ruling on giving his wife a choice. Umar, Ibn Mas`ud, and Ibn Abbas said: If a man gives his wife a choice and she chooses her husband, nothing happens. If she chooses herself, then one divorce occurs. This is the opinion of Umar ibn `Abd al-`Aziz, Ibn Abi Layla, Sufyan, al-Shafi`i, and the People of Opinion, except that according to the People of Opinion, it is an irrevocable divorce if she chooses herself. According to the others, it is revocable. Zayd ibn Thabit said: If she chooses the husband, then one divorce occurs, and if she chooses herself, then three. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan, and Malik said the same. It was also narrated on the authority of Ali that if she chooses her husband, then one divorce occurs, and if she chooses herself, then it is an irrevocable divorce. Most scholars agree that if she chooses her husband, nothing happens. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Umar bin Hafs told us, my father told us, Al-A’mash told us, Muslim told us, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us a choice, so we chose God and His Messenger, and that did not count against us.
33:30: God Almighty said: 30- O wives of the Prophet! Whoever of you commits a manifest immorality, with obvious disobedience, it was said: It is like His Almighty saying: If you should associate [anything] with God, your work will surely become worthless (al-Zumar 39:65), not that some of them committed an immorality. Ibn Abbas said: What is meant by immorality is rebellion and bad character. The punishment will be doubled for her, twofold. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read: nullify with a noon and a kasra and shaddah on the 'ayn, the punishment is accusative. The others read it with a ya and a fathah on the 'ayn, the punishment is nominative, and Abu Ja'far and the people of Basra stress it, and Abu Amr stressed this one alone because of his saying: double. The others read: nullify with an alif and a fathah on the 'ayn, the punishment is nominative, and they are two dialects like ba'd and ba'id. Abu Amr and Abu Ubaidah said: you weakened something if you made it twice as much, and you multiply it if you made it similar to it. And that was easy for God. Muqatil said: Her punishment was easy for God, and the doubling of their punishment for disobedience is due to their honor, just as the doubling of the punishment of a free woman is due to the doubling of a slave woman’s punishment, and their reward is doubly due to the elevation of their status. This indicates that they are the most honorable women in the world.
33:31: 31- And whoever among you is obedient to God and His Messenger, Ya’qub read: whoever among you obeys, and obeys with the ta’ in both of them, and the general public read it with the ya’ because whoever is a tool that takes the place of a noun and expresses the singular and plural, the masculine and the feminine, and does righteousness, We will give her her reward twice over, meaning: twice the reward of others. Muqatil said: In place of each good deed, twenty good deeds. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read: works and yuttuha with a ya in both of them, in agreement with his saying: and whoever comes and is devout. The others read it with a ta, “and We have prepared for her a noble provision,” good, meaning Paradise.
33:32: 32- O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. Ibn Abbas said: He means that your status with me is not like the status of other righteous women. You are more honorable to me, and your reward is greater with me. He did not say: like one, because one is a general term that applies to one, two, plural, male, and female. God Almighty said: We make no distinction between any of His messengers Al-Baqarah 2:285, and He said: And there is not one of you who can prevent Him from Him Al-Haqqah 47. If you fear God, God and obey Him, then do not speak softly, do not speak softly to men and do not speak softly, lest he in whose heart is a disease should covet, that is, lust and desire, and it was said that it means hypocrisy. The meaning is: do not say anything that a hypocrite or a wicked person might find a way to covet you. A woman is encouraged to be harsh in her speech when addressing strangers, in order to cut off their desires. And speak a good word for the sake of religion and Islam, clearly and explicitly, without submission.
33:33: 33- And abide in your houses. The people of Medina and Asim read: Wa qarran with the qaf open, and the others read it with the qaf closed. So whoever opens the qaf means, I abide meaning: the time in your houses, from their saying: I resided in the place, I resided, it is said: I resided, I resided, I resided, and they are two languages. So the first ra’, which is the root of the verb, was deleted due to the heaviness of the doubling, and its vowel was transferred to the qaf like their saying: in I shaded it, it shaded. God Almighty said: So you remained amused (al-Waqi’ah 56:65), She remained devoted to it (Ta-Ha 20:97). And from the breaking of the qaf, it has been said: It is from qararat iqra, meaning they acknowledged - with a broken ra’ - so the first was deleted and its vowel moved to the qaf as we mentioned, and it was said - and this is the most correct - that it is an order from dignity, like their saying from the promise: ‘Adan’, and from the connection: ‘Salna’, meaning: Be people of dignity and tranquility, from their saying waqara fulan yaqara waquran if he was calm and reassured. And do not display yourselves. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Tabarruj means to be coquettish and flirtatious. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: It is to strut. It was also said: It is to display adornment and show off one’s charms to men. The display of the first Jahiliyyah. They differed regarding the first Jahiliyyah. Al-Sha’bi said: It was between Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: During the time of David and Solomon, peace be upon them, a woman would wear a shirt made of pearls, not stitched on the sides, so her figure could be seen in it. Al-Kalbi said: This was during the time of the mighty Nimrod. Women would wear pearl armor and walk in the middle of the street with nothing else on, offering themselves to men. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The first ignorance was between Noah and Idris, and it lasted a thousand years. There were two clans of the children of Adam, one of them lived in the plain and the other in the mountain. The men of the mountain were beautiful and the women were ugly, and the women of the plain were beautiful and the men were ugly. Iblis came to a man from the plain and hired himself out to him, so he served him and made something like the one that shepherds play with, so he came with a voice that people had never heard the like of. This reached those around them, so they came to listen to it, and they made a festival to which they would gather throughout the year. The women would uncover themselves for the men, and the men would adorn themselves for them. A man from the mountain attacked them on their festival and saw the women and their beauty, so he came to his companions and informed them of this, so they turned to them and descended with them, and indecency became apparent among them. This is what God Almighty said: And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the first ignorance. Qatada said: It is before Islam. It was said: The first ignorance: what we mentioned, and the other ignorance: people who do the same as they will do at the end of time. It was said: The first may be mentioned even if there is no other, like the Almighty’s saying: And that He destroyed the first ‘Ad (al-Najm 53:50), and there is no other. God the Almighty said: “And establish prayer and give zakah and obey God and His Messenger. God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the House.” By uncleanness, He meant the sin that God forbade women from, as stated by Muqatil. Ibn Abbas said: It means the work of Satan and that which God is not pleased with. Qatada said: It means evil. Mujahid said: Impurity is doubt. What he meant by the people of the house are the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they are in his house. This is the narration of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He recited his statement: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God, which is the statement of Ikrimah and Muqatil. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri and a group of the followers, including Mujahid, Qatada, and others, said that they were Ali, Fatima, Al-Hassan, and Al-Hussein. Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi narrated to us, Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Ansari narrated to us, Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa’idi narrated to us, Abu Hammam al-Walid ibn Shuja’ narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariya ibn Za’idah narrated to us, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Mus’ab ibn Shaybah, on the authority of Safiyyah bint Shaybah al-Hajibiyah, on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out one morning wearing a black hair cloak. He sat down, and Fatimah came and he put her in it. Then Ali came and he put him in it. Then Hasan came and he put him in it. Then Husayn came and he put him in it. Then he said: ‘God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.’” Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Muhammad al-Hamidi told us, Abdullah al-Hafiz told us, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ya’qub told us, al-Hasan bin Mukram told us, Uthman bin Umar told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Sharik bin Abi Namir, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yasar, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: “In my house was revealed the verse: ‘God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House.’” She said: “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for Fatimah, Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn, and said: ‘These are my people of the House.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, am I not one of the people of the House?’ He said: ‘Yes, God willing.’” Zayd ibn Arqam said: The people of his household are those to whom charity is forbidden after him: the family of Ali, the family of Aqil, the family of Jaafar, and the family of Abbas.
33:34: God Almighty says: 34- And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God, meaning: the Qur’an, and wisdom, Qatadah said: meaning the Sunnah. Muqatil said: the rulings and admonitions of the Qur’an. Indeed, God is Kind and Aware, meaning: Kind to His friends and Aware of all His creation.
33:35: God Almighty said: 35- Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the verse. This is because the wives of the Prophet said: O Messenger of God, God mentioned men in the Qur’an but did not mention women in a good way, so there is no good in us to be mentioned with. We fear that our obedience will not be accepted. So God revealed this verse. Muqatil said: Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah and Naisa bint Ka'b Al-Ansariyyah said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Why does our Lord mention men but not women in anything in His Book? We fear that there is no good in them. So this verse was revealed. It was narrated that Asma bint Umays returned from Abyssinia with her husband Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and entered upon the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Has anything been revealed in the Qur'an about us? They said: No. So she came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, women are in a state of disappointment and loss. He said: Why is that? She said: Because they are not mentioned in a good way as men are. So God revealed this verse: “Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the obedient men and obedient women, the truthful men and the patient women, in what pleases them and what pleases them, the truthful women and the patient men and the humble women, in what God has commanded, the humble women and the humble men and the humbly men and the charitable women, from what God has provided them, the charitable men and the fasting women, the charitable men and the fasting women, the guarding their private parts, from what is not permissible, the guarding women and the men who remember God often and the women who remember.” Mujahid said: A servant is not one of those who remember God often until he remembers God standing, sitting, and lying down. We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The solitary ones have preceded. They said: And who are the solitary ones, O Messenger of God? He said: The men and women who remember God often. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said: “Whoever entrusts his affair to God, the Almighty, is included in His statement: ‘The Muslim men and Muslim women.’ And whoever acknowledges that God is his Lord and Muhammad is His Messenger, and his heart does not contradict his tongue, is included in His statement: ‘And the believing men and believing women.’ And whoever obeys God in the obligatory duties and the Messenger in the Sunnah, is included in His statement: ‘And the obedient men and obedient women.’ And whoever protects his speech from lying, is included in His statement: ‘And the truthful men and truthful women.’ And whoever is patient in obedience, and in avoiding disobedience, and in the face of calamity, is included in His statement: ‘And the patient men and patient women.’ And whoever prays and does not know who is on his right and on his left, is included in His statement: ‘And the humble men and humble women.’ And whoever gives in charity a dirham every week, is included in His statement: ‘And the charitable men and charitable women.’ And whoever fasts every month the white days: the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth, is included in His statement: ‘And the fasting men and fasting women.’ And whoever guards his private parts from what is not permissible, is included in His statement: ‘And the guardians.’” Their private parts and the women who protect themselves. Whoever performs the five daily prayers with their due rights is included in His statement: And the men who remember God often, and the women who remember. God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.
33:36: God Almighty says: 36- It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision. The verse was revealed about Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah and her brother Abdullah ibn Jahsh and her mother Umayyah bint Abdul Muttalib, the aunt of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to his freed slave Zayd ibn Haritha. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had bought Zayd in the pre-Islamic period of Ya’kaz, freed him, and adopted him. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to Zaynab, she agreed and thought that he was proposing to her for himself. But when she learned that he was proposing to Zayd, she refused and said: I am your cousin, O Messenger of God, and I do not accept him for myself. She was white, beautiful, and had a sharp edge. Her brother disliked that as well. So God Almighty revealed: And it is not for a believing man meaning Abdullah ibn Jahsh, or a believing woman meaning his sister Zaynab, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter meaning when God and His Messenger want a matter, which is the marriage of Zaynab to Zayd, that they should have any option in their decision. The people of Kufa read: that it should be with a ya as a barrier between the feminine and the verb. The others read it with a ta to feminize the choice from Their order, and the choice: the choice. Meaning: To want something other than what God wants or to abstain from what God and His Messenger have commanded. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error. He made a clear mistake. When they heard that, they accepted it and submitted. She put her affair in the hands of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and so did her brother. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her to Zaid, and he consummated the marriage with her. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave her ten dinars, sixty dirhams, a veil, a coat of mail, a loincloth, a blanket, fifty mudds of food, and thirty sa’s of dates.
33:37: God Almighty said: 37- And when you said to him whom God has bestowed favor upon and whom you have bestowed favor, ‘Keep your wife to yourself,’ The verse was revealed about Zaynab. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married Zaynab to Zayd, she stayed with him for a while. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Zayd one day for some need, and saw Zaynab standing in a coat of mail and a veil. She was white, beautiful, and had the most perfect figure among the women of Quraysh. He liked her and was impressed by her beauty, so he said: Glory be to God, the Changer of hearts, and he left. When Zayd came, I mentioned that to him, and Zayd realized it. He instilled in Zayd’s heart aversion to her at the time, so he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I want to leave my companion. He said: Why do you dislike her? He said: No, by God, O Messenger of God, I have seen nothing but good from her, but she acts arrogantly towards me because of her honor and hurts me with her tongue. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Keep your wife, meaning Zaynab bint Jahsh, and fear God in her matter. Then Zayd divorced her, and this is what God Almighty said: And when you said to him whom God had bestowed favor upon, with Islam, and whom you had bestowed favor upon, with emancipation, namely Zayd ibn Haritha: Keep your wife to yourself and fear God in her and do not separate from her, while concealing within yourself that which God is about to reveal, meaning: you concealed within yourself that which God is about to reveal, meaning: it was in his heart if he separated from her and married her. Ibn Abbas said: He loved her. Qatada said: He wished he had divorced her. "And you fear people." Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said: You feel shy of them. It was said: He feared that people would say: He ordered a man to divorce his wife and then he married her. And God is more deserving of being feared, said Omar, Ibn Masoud, and Aisha. No verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that was more difficult for him than this verse. It was narrated on the authority of Masruq that he said: Aisha said: If the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had concealed anything of what was revealed to him, he would have concealed this verse: And you conceal within yourself that which God is to reveal. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud’an who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin asked me what al-Hasan says about the verse: And you conceal within yourself that which God is to reveal, and you fear the people, while God has more right that you should fear Him? I said: He says that when Zayd came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Prophet of God, I want to divorce Zaynab, that pleased him and he said: Keep your wife and fear God. Ali ibn al-Husayn said: That is not so. God had informed him that she would be one of his wives and that Zayd would divorce her. When Zayd came and said: I want to divorce her, he said to him: Keep your wife. God admonished him and said: Why did you say: Keep your wife, when I had informed you that she would be one of your wives? This is the first and most appropriate for the state of the prophets, and it is in accordance with the recitation, because God knew that He would reveal and display what He concealed, and He did not display anything other than her marriage to him, so He said: We have married her to you. If what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealed was his love for her or his desire to divorce her, then he would have shown that, because it is not permissible for him to inform that he would show it and then conceal it and not show it. This indicates that he was only rebuked for concealing what God had informed him of, that she would be his wife, and he only concealed it out of shyness to say to Zaid: The one who is under you and in your marriage will be my wife. This is a good and acceptable statement, even though the other statement, which is that he concealed his love for her or his marriage to her if he divorced her, does not detract from the state of the prophets, because the servant is not to be blamed for what occurs in his heart in such matters, as long as he does not intend sin by it, because love and the inclination of the soul are of the nature of evil. His saying: Keep your wife and fear God is an order to do good, and it is fear, not sin. God Almighty’s statement: And God is more deserving of being feared, does not mean that he did not fear God in the past, for he, peace be upon him, said: I am the one among you who fears God and is most pious to Him, but when he mentioned fear of people, he mentioned that God Almighty is more deserving of being feared in all circumstances and in all things. The Almighty said: And when Zaid had satisfied his need for her, meaning: his need to marry her, We married her to you. He mentioned satisfying his need to know that the wife of an adopted man is permissible after consummating the marriage with her. Anas said: Zainab used to boast to the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: Your families married you, but God married me from above the seven heavens. Al-Sha’bi said: Zainab used to say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have three things to say about you that no other woman can say about you: My grandfather and your grandfather are one, God married me to you in heaven, and the ambassador is Gabriel, peace be upon him. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Hatim bin Maimun told us, Bahz told us, Sulayman bin Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: When Zaynab’s waiting period had ended, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Zayd: Mention her to me. Zayd went until he came to her while she was kneading her dough. He said: “When I saw her, she became so great in my chest that I could not look at her because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had mentioned her. So I turned my back on her and retreated on my heels, and I said: ‘O Zaynab, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has sent someone to mention you.’” She said: I will not do anything until I command my Lord. So she went to her mosque, and the Qur’an was revealed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered upon her without permission. He said: I saw that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fed us bread and meat, until the day extended, then the people went out and some men remained talking in the house after eating. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out and I followed him and he kept following the rooms of his wives, greeting them and saying: O Messenger of God, how did you find your family? He said: I do not know whether I told him that the people had gone out or he told me. He said: He went until he entered the house, so I went to enter with him, but he threw the curtain between me and him, and the veil came down. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not hold a wedding feast for any of his wives as he did for Zaynab. He held a wedding feast for a sheep.” Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, Muhammad ibn Hisham ibn Malas al-Namri told us, Marwan al-Fazari told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, held a wedding feast when he married Zaynab bint Jahsh, and he fed the Muslims a feast with bread and meat.” The Almighty said: So that there will be no blame upon the believers - sin - in respect of the wives of their adopted sons when they have satisfied their desire with them. And adopted sons is the plural of adopted son, which means adopted son. He says: We married you to Zaynab, and she is the wife of Zayd whom you adopted, so that it is known that the wife of an adopted son is lawful for the adopted son, even if the adopted son has consummated the marriage with her, unlike the wife of a loin son, who is not lawful for the father. And the command of God was to be carried out, meaning: God’s decree was to be carried out and His rule was to be implemented, and He decreed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would marry Zaynab.
33:38: God Almighty says: 38- There is no blame upon the Prophet for what God has enjoined upon him, meaning: in what God has made lawful for him, the way of God, meaning: like the way of God/, accusative by removing the preposition, and it was said: accusative for enticement, meaning: adhere to the way of God, among those who passed on before, meaning: in the past prophets, that He not hold them accountable for what He made lawful for them. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: When David combined himself with the woman he loved, he meant that he combined Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with Zaynab. It was said: He referred to marriage by the Sunnah, as it is one of the Sunnahs of the Prophets, peace be upon them. It was said: to the large number of wives, such as David and Solomon, peace be upon them. And the command of God was a predestined decree, a decree that was decreed, that was going to happen and that will happen in the future.
33:39: 39- Those who convey the messages of God, meaning God’s way with the prophets who convey God’s messages, and fear Him and do not fear anyone except God, they do not fear what people say or blame them for what God has made permissible for them and imposed upon them, and sufficient is God as Accountant, the Guardian of the deeds of His creation and their Accountant.
33:40: Then when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married Zaynab, the people said: Muhammad married his son’s wife. Then God Almighty revealed: 40- Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, meaning: Zayd ibn Haritha, meaning: he is not the father of any of your men whom he did not give birth to, so it is forbidden for him to marry his wife after separating from her. If it is said: Did he not have sons: Al-Qasim, Al-Tayeb, Al-Tahir, and Ibrahim, as well as: Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Hassan: This son of mine is a master? It was said: These were young, not men. What we said is correct: He meant the father of one of your men. But the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets, God sealed prophethood with him. Asim read: seal with a fatha on the ta’ of the noun, meaning: the last of them. The others read it with a kasra on the ta’ of the agent, because he sealed the prophets with him, so he is their seal. Ibn Abbas said: He means that if I had not sealed the prophets with him, I would have made him a son who would be a prophet after him. It was narrated on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When God Almighty decreed that there would be no prophet after him, He did not give him a male child who would become a man, And God is Knowing of all things. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni told us, Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad al-Khudashahi told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, Abkar al-Jurabadhi told us, Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus ibn Zayd told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: Abu Hurayrah used to say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My example and that of the prophets is like that of a palace, the construction of which was well-built, but a space of one brick was left. Then the watchmen went around it, marveling at the beauty of its construction except for the space of that brick, and they did not find fault with anything else. So it was I who filled the space of that brick. The construction was sealed with me, and the messengers were sealed with me.” Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juzajani told us, Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, Al-Haytham bin Kulayb Al-Shashi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Saeed bin Abdul Rahman Al-Makhzumi told us, and more than one said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Muhammad bin Jubayr bin Mut’im, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am Al-Mahi, through me God will erase disbelief, I am Al-Hashir, at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am Al-Aqib, and Al-Aqib is the one after whom there will be no prophet.”
33:41: God the Almighty said: 41- O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance. Ibn Abbas said: God the Almighty did not impose an obligation on His servants without setting a known limit for it. Then He excused those who have an excuse other than remembrance, for He did not set a limit for it, and He did not excuse anyone for abandoning it except those who were overcome by their mind. He commanded them to do so in all circumstances, as He said: So remember God while standing, sitting, and [lying] on your sides. An-Nisa’ 103. And He said: Remember God with much remembrance, meaning: by night and by day, on land and at sea, in health and sickness, in secret and in public. Mujahid said: Frequent remembrance means that you never forget Him.
33:42: 42- And glorify Him, meaning: pray to Him, in the morning, meaning: the dawn prayer, and in the evening, meaning: the afternoon prayer. Al-Kalbi said: And in the evening are the noon, afternoon, and evening prayers. Mujahed said: It means: Say: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest, and there is no power or strength except with God. So he used the term glorification to refer to its sisters. It was said: What is meant by his saying: remembrance frequently is that these words are said by the pure, the ritually impure, and the one in a state of minor ritual impurity.
33:43: 43- It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels do. So, the blessings from God are mercy, and from the angels are seeking forgiveness for the believers. Al-Suddi said: The Children of Israel said to Moses: Does our Lord pray? This statement was difficult for Moses, so God revealed to him: Tell them: I pray, and My prayer is My mercy, and My mercy encompasses all things. It was said: God's prayer for a servant is spreading good remembrance of him among His servants. It was also said: Praising him. Anas said: When the verse, Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet was revealed, Abu Bakr said: God has not singled you out with an honor, O Messenger of God, without making us share in it. So God revealed this verse. His statement: To bring you out from darkness into the light, meaning: from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith. This means that through His mercy, guidance, and the angels’ supplications for you, He brought you out from the darkness of disbelief into the light. And He is ever Merciful to the believers.
33:44: 44- Their greeting, meaning: the greeting of the believers, on the Day they meet Him, meaning: they see God, “is ‘Peace,’” meaning: God will greet them and keep them safe from all harm. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib who said: Their greeting on the day they meet Him, meaning: when they meet the Angel of Death, he will not take the soul of a believer without greeting him with peace. On the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: When the Angel of Death comes to take the soul of a believer, he says: Your Lord sends you peace. It was said: The angels greet them and give them good report when they emerge from their graves, And He has prepared for them a noble reward, meaning: Paradise.
33:45: God Almighty says: 45- O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner, meaning: a witness to the messengers regarding the message, and a bringer of good tidings for those who believe in Paradise, and a warner of Hell for those who deny Our signs.
33:46: 46- And calling to God, to His Oneness and obedience, by His permission, by His command, and an illuminating lamp, He called it a lamp because it is used to guide people, like a lamp that illuminates the darkness.
33:47: And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from God great bounty."
33:48: 48- And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. We mentioned its interpretation at the beginning of the surah. And ignore their harm. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: Be patient with their harm. Al-Zajjaj said: Do not punish them for it. This was abrogated by the verse on fighting. And put your trust in God, and sufficient is God as a guardian.
33:49: 49- O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them, this is evidence that divorce before marriage does not take place, because God Almighty made divorce conditional on marriage. Even if he said to a foreign woman: If I marry you, then you are divorced, and said: Every woman I marry is divorced, and he married, the divorce does not take place. This is the opinion of Ali, Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Muadh, and Aisha. It was also said by Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, Urwah, Shuraih, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, al-Qasim, Tawus, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata’, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Mujahid, al-Sha’bi, Qatadah, and most of the scholars may God be pleased with them. Al-Shafi’i also said this. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud: That divorce takes place, and this is the opinion of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i and the people of opinion. Rabia, Malik, and Al-Awza’i said: If a woman’s eye is affected, it is valid, but if it is blind, it is not valid. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: They lied about Ibn Masoud. If he said it, it was a slip of the tongue of a scholar who said: If you marry so-and-so, she is divorced. God Almighty says: If you marry believing women and then divorce them, and He did not say: If you divorce them and then marry them. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Daymuri told us, Umar bin Ahmad bin Al-Qasim Al-Nahwandi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir Al-Naysaburi told us in Mecca, Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told us, Ayoub bin Suwayd told us, Ibn Abi Dhi’b told us on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no divorce before marriage. God the Almighty said: before you touch them, i.e., have intercourse with them, then you have no waiting period to count for them, i.e., count it by menstrual periods and months, so provide for them, i.e., give them what they can enjoy. Ibn Abbas said: This is if he did not specify a dowry for her, then she is entitled to a provision. But if he specified a dowry for her, then she is entitled to half the dowry and no provision. Qatada said: This verse was abrogated by His statement: Then give half of what you imposed Al-Baqarah 237. It was said: This is a recommended matter, so the pleasure is recommended for her with half the dowry. Some of them said that she deserves enjoyment in all cases, based on the apparent meaning of the verse. And release them with goodness, release them on their way with kindness, without causing harm.
33:50: God Almighty says: 50- O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their dowries, meaning their bridal-money, and those your right hand possesses from what God has bestowed upon you, returning to you from the infidels so that you may take them as captives and own them, such as Safiyyah and Juwayriyah, and Mariyah was among those whom his right hand possessed and bore him Ibrahim, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, meaning the women of Quraysh, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts, meaning the women of Banu Zuhrah, who emigrated with you, to Medina. So whoever among them did not emigrate with him, it is not permissible for him to marry her. Abu Saleh narrated on the authority of Umm Hani’ that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca, he proposed to me, and God revealed this verse. I was not permissible for him, because I was not among the emigrants and I was among those who had been freed. Then the condition of emigration was abrogated for the purpose of permissibility. And a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet if the Prophet wishes to marry her, exclusively for you, not including the believers. That is, We have made lawful for you a believing woman who offers herself to you without a dowry. As for a non-believer, she is not lawful for him if she offers herself to him. They differed as to whether it was permissible for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to marry a Jewish or Christian woman in exchange for a dowry? A group of people said that it was not permissible for him to do that, because of his saying: and a believing woman. Some of them interpreted migration in his saying: those who migrated with you to mean Islam, meaning: they converted to Islam with you. This indicates that it was not permissible for him to marry a non-Muslim woman. Marriage was concluded in his case in the sense of a gift without a guardian, witnesses, or a dowry. This was one of his special characteristics in marriage, because God Almighty said: Purely for you, not for the believers, like more than four. The obligation to give women a choice was one of his special characteristics, and no one shared it with him. Scholars differed as to whether a marriage contract is valid with the use of the word gift in the case of a female slave. Most of them held the view that it is not valid unless the word marriage or marriageable is used. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Zuhri, Mujahid, and Ata'. It was also the view of Rabi'ah, Malik, and al-Shafi'i. Some people said that it is concluded by using the wording of gift and ownership, which is the opinion of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i and the people of Kufa. Those who said that it is not valid except with the word of marriage or marriage differed regarding the marriage of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some people said that it was valid with the word of gift, based on the Almighty’s saying: Purely for you, not for the believers. Others went to the view that it is not concluded except by the word of marriage or wedlock, as in the case of a female slave, based on the Almighty’s saying: If the Prophet wants to marry her, and his specialisation, may God bless him and grant him peace, was to leave the dowry, not to use the word of marriage. They differed about the woman who offered herself to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and whether he had any of them as wives. Abdullah bin Abbas and Mujahid said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not have a woman who gave herself to him, and he did not have a woman except through a marriage contract or through the right of possession. His saying: If she gave herself is in the manner of a condition and a reward. Others said: Rather, he had a gift, and they differed about her. Al-Sha’bi said: She is Zaynab bint Khuzaymah al-Hilaliyah, who is called: the mother of the poor. Qatada said: She is Maymunah bint Al-Harith. Ali bin Al-Hussein, Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: She is Umm Sharik bint Jabir from Banu Asad. Urwa bin Al-Zubayr said: She is Khawla bint Hakim from Banu Salim. The Almighty said: We have already known what We have enjoined upon them, meaning: We have made obligatory upon the believers, regarding their wives, of the rulings that they may not marry more than four and may not marry except with a guardian, witnesses, and a dowry, and those their right hands possess, meaning: what We have made obligatory of the rulings regarding those their right hands possess, so that there will be no difficulty for you, and this goes back to the beginning of the verse, meaning: We have made lawful for you your wives and those your right hands possess and those given to you as gifts so that there will be no difficulty or distress for you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.
33:51: 51- You may postpone, meaning: you may defer, whoever you wish of them and take in, meaning: you may take in, to you whomever you wish. The commentators differed about the meaning of the verse. The most famous of the sayings is that it refers to dividing his time between them, because it was obligatory for him to divide his time equally between them, but when this verse was revealed, it was dropped from him and the choice regarding them became his. Abu Razin and Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed when some of the Mothers of the Believers became jealous of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and some of them asked for more maintenance. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ignored them for a month until the verse of choice was revealed. God the Almighty commanded him to give them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and to release those who chose this world and to keep those who chose God, His Messenger and the Hereafter, on the condition that they were the Mothers of the Believers and that they would never marry, and that he would take with him whomever he wished from them and give hope to whomever he wished, and they would be satisfied with him dividing his wealth among them or not dividing it, or dividing it for some of them and not for others, or giving some of them preference in maintenance and division. So the matter would be up to him and he would do as he wished. This was one of his special characteristics, so they were satisfied with that and chose him on this condition. They differed as to whether he excluded any of them from the division of time. Some of them said: He did not exclude anyone. Rather, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) - despite what God had given him of that - treated them equally in the division of time, except for Sawda, who agreed to give up her right to the division and assigned her day to Aisha. It was said: He took some of them out. Jarir narrated on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Abu Razin who said: When the option was revealed, they feared that he would divorce them, so they said: O Prophet of God, give us whatever you wish of your wealth and yourself and leave us as we are. So this verse was revealed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, postponed some of them and sheltered others. Among those he sheltered were Aisha, Hafsa, Zainab, and Umm Salamah, so he would divide his time equally among them. He postponed five of them: Umm Habiba, Maymunah, Sawda, Safiyya, and Juwayriyya, so he would divide among them whatever he wished. Mujahid said: You may postpone any of them you wish, meaning: You may dismiss any of them you wish without divorce, and she may return to you any of them you wish after dismissing them without renewing the contract. Ibn Abbas said: You may divorce whomever you wish of them and keep whomever you wish. Al-Hasan said: You may leave marrying whomever you want and marry whomever you want from the women of your nation. He said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to a woman, no one else had the right to propose to her until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left her. It was said: Accept whomever you wish of the believing women who give themselves to you, and you may take them in, and leave whomever you wish and do not accept them. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Salam told us, Ibn Fadil told us, Hisham told us on the authority of his father who said: Khawlah bint Hakim was among those who offered themselves to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Aisha said: Isn’t a woman ashamed to offer herself to a man? When the verse: You may defer to any of them you wish was revealed, I said: O Messenger of God, I do not see your Lord except that He hastens to fulfill your desires. God the Almighty said: And if you desire from among those you have set aside, meaning: you seek and want to take with you a woman from among those you have set aside from the portion of time, there is no blame upon you, there is no sin upon you. So God has permitted him to leave the portion of time with them, so that he may delay whomever he wishes from among them during her turn and have intercourse with whomever he wishes from among them outside her turn, and he may return to his bed the one whom you have set aside, as a preference for him over all other men. That is more likely that their eyes will be comforted and they will not grieve, meaning: the choice that you have given him in their company is closer to their satisfaction and better for their souls and less to their grief if they know that this is from God the Almighty, and they will be satisfied with what you have given them, you have given them, all of them, of confirmation, postponement, isolation and shelter, and God knows what is in your hearts, regarding the matter of women and the inclination towards some of them, and God is Knowing and Forbearing.
33:52: God Almighty said: 52- It is not lawful for you to take other women after that, nor to exchange them for other wives. Abu Amr and Ya`qub read: It is not lawful with a ta’, and the others read it with a ya’. After means after these nine whom you gave them a choice and they chose you. This is because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them a choice and they chose God and His Messenger, God thanked them and forbade him women other than them and forbade him from divorcing them or replacing them with other wives. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. They differed as to whether he was permitted to have women after that? Aisha said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until he was permitted to have other women. Anas said: He died while forbidding it. Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: The meaning of the verse is that women are not lawful for you except those whom We have made lawful for you, and this is His statement: Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives the verse, then He said: Women are not lawful for you after that except those whom We have made lawful for you in the manner mentioned above. It was said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: If the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had died, would it have been permissible for him to marry again? He said: What prevents him from doing so? It was said: The Almighty's saying: "It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that," He said: God only made lawful for him a certain type of women. He said: "O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives," then He said: "It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that." Abu Salih said: He was ordered not to marry a Bedouin woman, whether male or female, and he was to marry from the women of his people, from the daughters of his paternal uncles, aunts and maternal aunts, if he wished, three hundred. Mujahid said: Its meaning is that it is not permissible for you to have Jewish or Christian women after the Muslim women, nor to exchange them for them, meaning: Nor to exchange the Muslim women for other Jews and Christians, meaning: The mother of the believers is not to be Jewish or Christian, except for what your right hand possesses. It is permissible for him to have concubines with what his right hand possesses of the People of the Book. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: meaning, do not exchange them for them, nor exchange your wives who are under your care for other wives by divorcing them and marrying others. So, it was forbidden for him to divorce the women who were with him, since he made them the mothers of the believers, and he forbade them to anyone else when they chose him. As for marrying others, it was not forbidden. Ibn Zayd said about his statement: nor that you exchange them for other wives, the Arabs in the pre-Islamic era used to exchange their wives. A man would say to another man: Exchange me for your wife, and I will exchange you for my wife. You give me your wife, and I will give you my wife. So God revealed: nor that you exchange them for other wives, meaning do not exchange your wives for someone else by giving him your husband and taking his wife, except for what your right hand possesses. There is no problem with you exchanging your slave girl for whatever you wish, but as for free women, no. It was narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “Uyaynah ibn Hisn entered upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) without permission, and Aisha was with him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: ‘Uyaynah, where is the permission to enter?’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, I have not asked permission to enter upon a man from Mudar since I became an adult.’ Then he said: ‘Who is this red-skinned woman next to you?’ He said: ‘This is Aisha, the Mother of the Believers.’ Uyaynah said: ‘Shall I not grant you permission to leave the house of the best of creation?’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘God has forbidden that.’ When he left, Aisha said: ‘Who is this, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘This is an obedient fool, and as you can see, he is the master of his people.’” The Almighty says: Even if their beauty pleases you, meaning: You are not allowed to divorce any of your wives and marry another in her place, even if you are pleased with her beauty. Ibn Abbas said: He means Asma bint Umays Al-Khathamiyyah, the wife of Ja’far ibn Abi Talib. When Ja’far was martyred, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to propose to her, but he was forbidden from doing so. Except what your right hand possesses. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: After these, Maria became king. And God is ever a Watcher over all things, a Preserver. This verse provides evidence that it is permissible to look at a woman whom one wants to marry. It was narrated on the authority of Jabir may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: If one of you proposes to a woman, if he is able to look at what will encourage him to marry her, then let him do so. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni told us, Abu Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Sharik al-Shafi’i told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, Abu Bakr al-Jurbudhi told us, he said: Ahmad ibn Harb told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Asim - he is Ibn Sulayman - on the authority of Bakr ibn Abdullah, on the authority of al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah, who said: I proposed marriage to a woman, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Have you looked at her? I said: No. He said: Then look at her, for that is more likely to create harmony between you. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid told us, Hamid bin Muhammad told us, Bishr bin Musa told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Yazid bin Kaysan told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “That a man wanted to marry a woman from the Ansar, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Look at her, for there is something in the eyes of the women of the Ansar.” Al-Hamidi said: He meant smallness.
33:53: God Almighty said: 53- O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are permitted, the verse. Most commentators said: This verse was revealed regarding the wedding feast of Zaynab bint Jahsh when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, consummated the marriage with her. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Anas bin Malik told me that he was ten years old when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina. He said: Umm Hani used to make me serve the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I served him for ten years. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died when I was twenty years old. So I was the most knowledgeable of people about the veil when it was revealed. The first thing that was revealed was in the house of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with Zaynab bint Jahsh. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became her bride. He called the people and they ate some food and then left. A group of them remained with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they stayed for a long time. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up for God’s sake and went out, and I went out with him so that they would go out. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked and I walked until he came to Aisha’s room. Then he thought that they had gone out, so he returned and I went back with him. When he entered upon Zaynab, they were sitting and had not gone out. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, and I returned with him until he reached the threshold of Aisha’s room. He thought that they had left, so he returned and I returned with him. They had left, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a curtain between me and him, and lowered the veil. Abu Uthman - whose name was Al-Ja`d - said on the authority of Anas, who said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the house and lowered the curtain while I was in the room, and he was saying: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission until his saying: And God is not ashamed of the truth. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was revealed about some Muslims who used to wait for the food of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they would enter upon him before the food was ready, then they would eat and not leave. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was bothered by them, so the following was revealed: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when permission is given to you He says: unless you are invited, to food, so he gives you permission and you eat it, not awaiting its preparation, not waiting for it to be ready or cooked. It is said: ana al-hamim if its heat is over, and ana anhu if he does that: if it is time, ana with a kasra on the hamza shortened, and if you open it you extend it and say ana’an, and there are two pronunciations for it: ana ya’na and ana ya’in, like: han yahin. “But when you are invited, then enter. And when you have eaten,” have eaten the food, then disperse, disperse and leave his house, not seeking the company of conversation, nor seeking the company of conversation. They used to sit after eating and talk for a long time, so they were forbidden from doing that. That used to bother the Prophet, so he would be shy of you, but God is not shy of the truth, meaning: He does not abandon disciplining you and explaining the truth out of shyness. And if you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition, meaning: from behind a curtain. After the verse on the hijab, no one was to look at any of the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, whether she was veiled or not. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts from suspicion. It has been authenticated regarding the reason for the revelation of the verse of hijab, as told to us by Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi, Muhammad bin Yusuf, Muhammad bin Ismail, Yahya bin Bakir, Al-Layth, Aqil, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah, that the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to go out at night when they defecated to the open plain, and Umar used to say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Veiling your women, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not do so.
