So one night, Sawdah bint Zam’ah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out at night at night, and she was a tall woman, so Umar called out to her: Do we not recognize you, O Sawdah? - out of eagerness for the hijab to be revealed - so God Almighty revealed the verse of hijab. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: “Umar said: My Lord agreed with me on three matters. I said: O Messenger of God, why don’t you take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer? So God revealed: ‘And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer.’ I said: O Messenger of God, both the righteous and the wicked enter upon you, so why don’t you order the Mothers of the Believers to wear the hijab? So God revealed the verse on the hijab. He said: I was informed of some of the things that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did to his wives. He said: So I entered upon them and asked them to come to him one by one. I said: By God, you must stop or God will replace him with wives better than you, until I came to Zainab, and she said: O Umar, there was nothing in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to admonish his wives until you admonish them. He said: So I went out, and God Almighty revealed: ‘Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you.’” At-Tahrim 5, to the end of the verse. The Almighty said: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God, you are not to harm him in any way, nor to marry his wives after him ever, it was revealed about a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were to die, I would marry Aisha. Muqatil bin Sulayman said: He is Talha bin Ubayd God. God Almighty informed us that this was forbidden, and said: Indeed, that was in the sight of God a great sin, meaning: a great sin. Muammar narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri that Al-Aliyah bint Dhibyan, whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divorced, married a man and gave birth to a child for him, and that was before the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were forbidden to people.
33:54: 54- Whether you disclose a thing or conceal it, then indeed, God is ever, of all things, Knowing. This verse was revealed about those who intended to marry Aisha after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: A man from the companions said: Why are we prevented from entering upon our cousins? Then this verse was revealed.
33:55: When the verse of the veil was revealed, fathers, sons and relatives said: And we also speak to them from behind the veil? So God revealed: 55- There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, nor their sons, nor their brothers, nor their brothers’ sons, nor their sisters’ sons, meaning: there is no sin upon them for not covering themselves from these people, nor their women, it was said that he meant by this Muslim women, so that it is not permissible for the People of the Book to enter upon them, and it was said that it is general for Muslim women and the People of the Book, and he only said: nor their women because they are from their kind, nor those whom their right hands possess. They differed as to whether a woman's slave is a mahram to her or not? Some people said that it is forbidden, based on the Almighty’s saying: nor those whom their right hands possess. Some people said: He is like foreigners, and what is meant by the verse is female slaves, not male slaves. And fear God lest you be seen by others, for God is ever, over all things, a Witness.
33:56: God Almighty says: 56- Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. Ibn Abbas said: He meant that God has mercy on the Prophet, and the angels pray for him. Ibn Abbas also said: They send blessings to seek blessings. It was said: Prayer from God is mercy, and from the angels is forgiveness. O you who have believed, pray upon him, ask for mercy for him, “and greet him with peace,” meaning: greet him with the greeting of Islam. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: God’s prayer is His praise of him before the angels, and the angels’ prayer is supplication. Abu Saeed Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Abbas al-Hamidi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hafiz told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Faqih in Baghdad told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Zuhair ibn Harb told us, Musa ibn Ismail told us, Abu Salamah told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, Abu Farwah told us, Abdullah ibn Isa ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla told me that he heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla say: “Ka’b ibn Ujrah met me and said: ‘Shall I not give you a gift that I heard from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)?’ I said: ‘Yes, give it to me.’ He said: ‘We asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and we said: O Messenger of God, how should we send blessings upon you, the people of the House?’ He said: ‘Say: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham, for You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. O God, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham, for You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.’” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn `Amr ibn Hazm, on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Amr ibn Sulayman al-Zarqi, who said: Abu Hamid al-Sa`i told me that they said: O Messenger of God, how should we send blessings upon you? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Say: ‘O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and his wives and his offspring as You sent blessings upon Abraham, and bless Muhammad and his wives and his offspring as You blessed the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious.’” Abu Amr and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Nasawi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub told us, al-Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri told us, Khalid ibn Mukhallad al-Qatwani told us, Musa ibn Yaqub al-Zamai told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Kaysan, Abdullah ibn Shaddad told me, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The people closest to me on the Day of Resurrection will be those who send the most prayers upon me.’” Abu Abdullah bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, Al-Ala bin Abdul-Rahman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever sends blessings upon me once, God will send blessings upon him ten times. Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Al-Harith told us, Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Yaqub Al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah bin Mahmoud told us, Ibrahim bin Abdullah Al-Khalal told us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit Al-Banani, on the authority of Sulayman, the client of Al-Hasan bin Ali, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of his father, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he came one day with glad tidings on his face, and he said: Gabriel came to me and said: Your Lord says, ‘Is it not pleasing to you, O Muhammad, that no one from your nation prays for you except that I pray for him ten times, and no one from your nation greets you except that I greet him ten times?’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shureih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali Al-Ja’d told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Asim - he is Ibn Ubayd God - he said: I heard Abdullah bin Amir bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of his father, that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever sends blessings upon me, the angels will send blessings upon him as long as they send blessings upon me. So let the servant say little of that or do a lot.” Abu al-Qasim Yahya ibn Ali al-Kashmihani told us, Janah ibn Yazid al-Maharibi told us in Kufa, Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim al-Shaibani told us, Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, `Abdullah ibn Musa and Abu Na`im told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of `Ubaydullah ibn al-Sa`ib, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has angels who travel around the earth and convey to me the greetings of my nation.”
33:57: God Almighty said: 57- Indeed, those who abuse God and His Messenger - God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment. Ibn Abbas said: They are the Jews, Christians, and polytheists. As for the Jews, they said: Ezra is the son of God, and God’s hand is chained. They said: God is poor. As for the Christians, they said: The Messiah is the son of God, and the third of three. As for the polytheists, they said: The angels are the daughters of God, and the idols are His partners. We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty says: My servant has insulted Me, saying: God has taken a son, while I am the One, the Self-Sufficient, who neither begets nor was begotten, and there is none comparable to Me.” We narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty said: ‘The son of Adam harms Me by cursing time, and I am time. In My hand is the matter. I alternate night and day.’” It was said: The meaning of they harm God is that they blaspheme His names and attributes. Akrima said: They are the owners of the pictures. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Al-Ala told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, who heard Abu Hurairah say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God Almighty said: ‘And who is more unjust than he who takes up a creation like My creation? Let them create an atom or let them create a grain or a barley husk.’” Some of them said: They harm God, meaning: They harm God’s friends, like the Almighty’s saying: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82), meaning: the people of the town. We narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty said: Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I declare war on him. And He said: Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine has declared war on Me.” The meaning of harm: is disobeying the command of God Almighty and committing His sins. He mentioned it according to what people know among themselves, and God Almighty is far above being harmed by anyone. Harming the Messenger, Ibn Abbas said: It is when his face is cut and his front tooth is broken. It was also said: a poet, a magician, a teacher, or a madman.
33:58: 58- And those who harm believing men and believing women for no reason, without doing anything that warranted their harm. Mujahid said: They attack them and accuse them without any crime, have certainly borne the burden of slander and a manifest sin. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib, because some hypocrites were harming and insulting him. It was said: It was revealed about Aisha. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about the fornicators who used to walk in the streets of Madinah, following women when they came out at night to relieve themselves. They would wink at the woman, and if she kept quiet, they would follow her, and if she rebuked them, they would stop. They only sought out female slaves, but they did not know the free woman from the female slave because the attire of all was the same. They would go out in a coat of mail and a veil, the free woman and the female slave. They complained about that to their husbands, and they mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so this verse was revealed: And those who harm believing men and believing women Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
33:59: Then He forbade free women from imitating slave women, saying, Glory be to Him: 59- O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. The plural of jilbab is jilbab, which is the sheet that a woman covers herself with over her shirt and veil. Ibn Abbas and Abu Ubaidah said: He ordered the believing women to cover their heads and faces with jilbabs except for one eye, so that it would be known that they were free women. That is more likely that they will be known, that they are free, so that they will not be harmed, so that they will not be exposed, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. Anas said: A veiled slave girl passed by Omar ibn al-Khattab, so he hit her with a whip and said, O you coquettish woman, are you imitating free women? Take off your veil.
33:60: God Almighty said: 60- If the hypocrites do not desist, from their hypocrisy, and those in whose hearts is disease, immorality, meaning the fornicators, and the spreaders of false rumors in the city, with lies. This is because some of them, when the armies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out, would falsely accuse the people of having been killed and defeated, and they would say: The enemy has come to you, and so on. Al-Kalbi said: They loved for immorality to spread among the believers and for the report to be divulged. We will tempt you against them, we will incite you against them and give you authority over them, then they will not live with you therein, they will not live with you in the city except for a little while, until they leave it. And it was said: We will give you authority over them until you kill them and empty the city of them.
33:61: 61- Cursed, banished, accusative case of state, wherever they are found, found and perceived, they will be seized and killed in a massacre, meaning: this is the ruling on them as ordered.
33:62: 62- The way of God, meaning: like the way of God, with those who passed on before, of the hypocrites and those who did as these did, and you will not find any change in the way of God.
33:63: God Almighty says: 63- “People ask you about the Hour. Say, ‘Its knowledge is only with God.’ And what would make you know?” That is, what would make you know about the Hour and when it will occur? That is, you do not know it. Perhaps the Hour is near.
33:64: 64- Indeed, God has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Blaze.
33:65: 65- They will abide therein forever, finding neither protector nor helper.
33:66: 66- On the Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire, back to back when they are dragged upon it, they will say, ‘Oh, if only we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger,’ in this world.
33:67: 67- And they said, ‘Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters.’ Ibn Amir and Yaqub read: our masters with a kasra on the ta’ and an alif before it, in the plural of the plural. The others read it with a fatha on the ta’ without an alif before it, and our great ones, so they led us astray from the path.
33:68: 68- Our Lord, give them double the punishment, meaning: double the punishment of others, and curse them with a great curse, Asim read: great with the letter b. Al-Kalbi said: meaning: a great punishment. The others read it with the letter th, based on the Almighty’s saying: On them is the curse of God and of the angels and of mankind, all together Al-Baqarah 2:161. This testifies to the abundance, meaning: time after time.
33:69: God Almighty said: 69- O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but God cleared him of what they said. So God purified him of what they said: And he was in the sight of God of high esteem, generous and of high standing. It is said: A man’s face is of high standing, so he is of high standing, if he has prestige and esteem. Ibn Abbas said: He was very fortunate with God. He never asked for anything without giving it to him. Al-Hassan said: His prayers were answered. It was said: He was responsive and acceptable. They differed about what Moses was harmed with: So Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd God al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Ismail informed us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us, Ruh ibn Ubadah informed us, Awf informed us, on the authority of al-Hasan, Muhammad, and Khulas, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Moses was a modest, discreet man. Nothing of his skin was visible out of modesty. He was harmed by those among the Children of Israel who harmed him. They said: He only conceals himself this way because of a defect in his skin, either leprosy, or a disease. God wanted to clear him of what they said. So he was alone one day and placed his clothes on the stone, then washed himself. When he finished, he went to his clothes to take them, but the stone ran away with his clothes. Moses took his staff and asked the stone, and he kept saying: My clothes are a stone, my clothes are a stone, until he reached a group of the Children of Israel. They saw him naked, the most beautiful of what God had created, and he cleared him of what they said. The stone stood up, took his clothes, put them on, and began to wash the stone. He hit him with his stick. By God, there were scars on the stone from the effect of his hitting him three, four or five times. This is what God Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but God cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of God. Some people said: The reason they harmed him was that when Aaron died in the wilderness, they claimed that Moses had killed him. So God commanded the angels to pass by him among the Children of Israel and they knew that he had not killed him, so God cleared him of what they had said. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is that Qarun hired a prostitute to throw herself at Moses in front of the crowd, but God protected her and absolved Moses of that, and Qarun was destroyed. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Walid told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: I heard Abu Wa’il say: I heard Abdullah say: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a division, and a man said: This division is not for the sake of God. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him, and he became angry until I saw the anger on his face, then he said: May God have mercy on Moses, he was harmed more than this and he was patient.”
33:70: God Almighty said: 70- O you who have believed, fear God and speak words of appropriate justice. Ibn Abbas said: Correct. Qatada said: Just. Al-Hasan said: Truthful. It was also said: Upright. Ikrimah said: It is to say, There is no god but God.
33:71: 71- He will rectify your deeds for you. Ibn Abbas said: He will accept your good deeds. Muqatil said: He will purify your deeds, “and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great victory.” That is, he has attained all good.
33:72: God Almighty said: 72- Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to do so… (al-Baqarah 2:196). What He meant by the Trust was the obedience and duties that God imposed on His servants. He offered it to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains on the condition that if they fulfilled it, He would reward them, and if they neglected it, He would punish them. This is the statement of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Masoud said: Trustworthiness includes performing prayers, paying zakat, fasting Ramadan, performing Hajj, speaking the truth, paying debts, being just in measuring and weighing, and more difficult than all of these are deposits. Mujahid said: Trust: the duties and limits of religion. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: What they were commanded to do and what they were forbidden to do. Zaid bin Aslam said: It is fasting, ritual ablution after sexual impurity, and what is hidden from the religious laws. Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas said: The first thing God created of man was his private parts. He said: This is a trust I have entrusted to you. So the private parts are a trust, the eye is a trust, the hand is a trust, the foot is a trust, and there is no faith for one who has no trust. Some of them said: They are people’s trusts and keeping promises. So it is the right of every believer not to cheat a believer or a covenant holder in anything, little or much. This is the narration of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas. So God presented this trust to the beings of the heavens, the earth and the mountains. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas and a group of the Followers and most of the Salaf. So He said to them: Will you bear this trust and what is in it? They said: What is in it? He said: If you do good, you will be rewarded, and if you disobey, you will be punished. They said: No, O Lord, we are subject to Your command. We do not want reward or punishment. They said that out of fear, awe, and reverence for the religion of God, so that they would not carry it out, neither in disobedience nor in opposition. The offer was given to them as a choice, not as an obligation. If He had obliged them, they would not have refused to carry it. All inanimate objects are subject to God, the Almighty, the Majestic, obedient, and prostrate to Him, as He, the Most High, said to the heavens and the earth: “Come willingly or by compulsion. They said, ‘We come willingly.’” (Fussilat 41:11). He said to the stones: And indeed, among them are those that fall down for fear of God. (al-Baqarah 2:74). God, the Most High, said: Do you not see that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and the moving creatures? (al-Hajj 22:18). Some scholars said: God Almighty instilled in them reason and understanding when He presented the trust to them, so that they understood the message and responded as they responded. Some of them said: What is meant by the presentation to the heavens and the earth is the presentation to the people of the heavens and the earth, its presentation to the angels in it. It was said: on all of its people, not its individuals, as God Almighty said: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82), meaning: the people of the town. The first is more correct, and it is the opinion of scholars. But they refused to bear it and feared it, meaning: they feared that the trust would not be fulfilled and that punishment would be due to them. And man bore it, meaning: Adam, peace be upon him. So God said to Adam: “I offered the trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, and you did not release them. Will you accept it with what is in it?” He said: O Lord, what is in it? He said: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. So Adam bore it and said: Between my ears and my shoulders. God Almighty said: “But if you bear it, I will help you. I will place a veil over your sight, so if you fear that you will look at what is not lawful for you, then lower its veil over it. I will place a lock over your tongue for a time, so if you commit adultery, then lock it. I will place a garment over your private parts, so do not uncover it over what is forbidden to you.” Mujahid said: There was only a period of time between the time he carried her and the time he left Paradise. Al-Naqqash narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he said: The Trust was represented as a thrown rock, and the heavens, the earth, and the mountains were called to it, but they did not come near it, and they said: We are not able to carry it. Adam came without being called, and moved the rock, and said: If I were ordered to carry it, I would carry it. They said to him: Carry it. So he carried it to his knees, then he put it down, and said: By God, if I wanted more, I would. They said to him: Carry it. So he carried it to his waist, then he put it down, and said: By God, if I wanted more, I would. They said to him: Carry it. So he carried it until he put it on his shoulder, and when he wanted to put it down, God said: Stay where you are, for it is on your neck and the necks of your descendants until the Day of Resurrection. He was unjust and ignorant. Ibn Abbas said: He was unjust to himself and ignorant of God’s command and the trust he had been entrusted with. Al-Kalbi said: He was unjust when he disobeyed his Lord, ignorant and did not know what the punishment was for abandoning a trust. Muqatil said: He was unjust to himself and ignorant of the consequences of what he bore. Al-Zajjaj and other scholars of meanings said: There are two opinions regarding His statement, And man has borne it. They said: God entrusted Adam and his children with something, and He entrusted the heavens, the earth, and the mountains with something. So, the trustworthiness with regard to the children of Adam is what we mentioned in obedience and fulfilling the obligations. The trustworthiness with regard to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains is submission and obedience to the One for whom He created them. It was said: His statement, But they refused to bear it, means: They fulfilled the trust. It is said: So-and-so did not bear the trust, meaning: he did not betray it. And man has borne it, meaning: he betrayed it. It is said: So-and-so bore the trust, meaning: he sinned by betraying it. God Almighty said: And let them bear their burdens (al-Ankabut 29:13). Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan on this interpretation: He said, “And the human being bore it, meaning the infidel and the hypocrite, bore the trust, meaning: they betrayed it.” The predecessors said what we mentioned.
33:73: God Almighty said: 73- That God may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women. Muqatil said: To punish them for betraying the trust and breaking the covenant, “and that God may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” He guides them and has mercy on them for what they have fulfilled of the trust. Ibn Qutaybah said: That is, we presented the trust so that the hypocrisy of the hypocrite and the polytheism of the polytheist would be exposed, so that God would punish them, and the faith of the believer would be exposed, so that God would accept his repentance, that is, He would return to him with mercy and forgiveness if he fell short in some acts of obedience.
34:1: 1- Praise be to God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, in terms of kingdom and creation, and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter, as it is to Him in this world, because all blessings in both worlds are from Him. It was said: Praise be to God in the Hereafter is the praise of the people of Paradise, as God Almighty said: And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow’ (Fatir 35:34), Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us (al-Zumar 39:74), and And He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
34:2: 2- He knows what goes into the earth, that is, what enters it of water and the dead, and what comes out of it, of plants and the dead when they are gathered, and what comes down from the sky, of rain, and what ascends, “in it,” of angels and the deeds of the servants, and He is the Most Merciful, the Forgiving.
34:3: 3- And those who disbelieve say, ‘The Hour will not come to us.’ Say, ‘Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.’ The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read: Knower of the unseen in the nominative case, while others read it in the genitive case as an attribute of the Lord, meaning: And my Lord is Knower of the unseen. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read: Allaam in the form of Fa’al, and the mim in the genitive case. Not even the weight of an atom is hidden from Him the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller than that, meaning: of an atom, nor anything greater except that it is in a clear Book.
34:4: 4- “That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds. Those,” meaning: those who believe, will have forgiveness and noble provision, good, meaning: in Paradise.
34:5: 5- And those who strive against Our verses to frustrate them, they think that they can escape Us, for them is a punishment of painful torment. Ibn Kathir, Hafs, and Ya’qub read: painful in the nominative case here and in Al-Jathiya as a description of the torment. The others read it in the accusative case as a description of the torment. Qatada said: The torment is the worst of torment.
34:6: 6- And those who have been given knowledge will see, meaning: the believers among the People of the Book: Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions. Qatada said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, meaning: the Qur’an, is the truth, meaning: it is from God, and guides, meaning: the Qur’an, to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, which is Islam.
34:7: 7- And those who disbelieved said, denying the resurrection and astonished by it: Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when you are torn apart, cut into pieces and dispersed and become dust, then you will be in a new creation, he says to you: You will be in a new creation.
34:8: 8- He fabricated, an interrogative alif that came before the alif of connection, and therefore it was placed in the accusative case. A lie against God, or is he mad? They say: Do you claim a lie, or is he mad? God Almighty said in response to them: Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in torment and far astray, from the truth in this world.
34:9: 9- “Have they not seen what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth,” so that they know that wherever they are, My earth and heavens encompass them and they cannot leave its regions, and I am able to do anything to them, If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them up, Al-Kisa’i read: We can swallow them up with the assimilation of the fa’ into the ba’, or cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon them, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: If He wills, He can swallow them up or He can fall down, with the ya’ in them for the mention of God before, and the others read with the nun in them, Indeed in that, meaning: in what you see of the heaven and the earth, is a sign, indicating Our ability to resurrect, for every servant who turns back, repentant and returns to God with his heart.
34:10: God the Almighty said: 10 - And We had certainly given David bounty from Us, meaning the gift and the Book, and it was said: the kingdom. And it was said: everything he was given of a beautiful voice, softening iron, and other things that he was specifically given, O mountains, meaning: And We said, O mountains, Repeat, meaning: glorify, with him, if he glorifies, and it was said: it is a verb from to return, which means to return, meaning: return with him. Al-Qatibi said: its origin is from to return in traveling, which is to travel all day and descend at night, as if he said: I repeat all day by glorifying with him. And Wahb said: We inspire with him. "And the birds" is in apposition to the mountains, because every vocative is in the accusative case. It was said that its meaning is: And We subjected and commanded the birds to glorify Him. Jacob read "and the birds" in the nominative case in response to the mountains, meaning: Repeat, you and the birds. And when David called out in a direction, the mountains would answer him with their echo, and the birds would flock to him from above him, so the echo of the mountains that people hear today is from that. It was said: When David passed through the mountains and glorified God, the mountains would respond to him with glorification in the same manner as he glorified God. It was said: When David, peace be upon him, felt tired, God would make him hear the mountains glorify God to encourage him. And We made iron soft for him, until the iron in his hand was like wax and dough, from which he could make whatever he wanted without fire or hammer. The reason for this, as narrated in the hadiths, is that when David, peace be upon him, ruled the Children of Israel, it was his habit to go out to the people in disguise. If he saw a man he did not know, he would go up to him and ask him about David, saying, What do you say about David, while he is among you? What kind of man is he? They would praise him and speak well of him. So God appointed for him an angel in the form of a human. When David saw him, he went up to him as was his habit and asked him. The angel said, He is a good man, except for one trait. David was startled by that and said, What is it, O servant of God? He said, He eats and feeds his family from the public treasury. He was alerted by that and asked God to provide him with a means by which he would be independent of the public treasury, so that he could live from it and feed his family. So God, the Most High, softened iron for him and taught him how to make armor, and he was the first to make it. It is said that he used to sell each shield for four thousand dirhams, and he would eat from it and feed his family and give it in charity to the poor and needy. It is said that he used to make a shield every day and sell it for six thousand dirhams, spending two thousand of it on himself and his family, and giving four thousand in charity to the poor of the Children of Israel. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “David, peace be upon him, would not eat except from the work of his own hands.”
34:11: 11- Make long, wide, and complete coats of mail that are dragged on the ground, and measure the chains of mail, and the chain of mail is the weaving of the coat of mail. Its maker is called al-Sirad and al-Ziraad. He says: Measure the nails in the ring of the coat of mail, meaning: do not make the nails thin so that they slip out, nor thick so that they break the ring. It is also said: the chain of mail is the nail in the ring. It is said: a chained coat of mail, meaning: the ring is nailed. And measure the chain of mail, make it according to the intended purpose and according to the need. And work righteousness, meaning: David and his family, Indeed, I, of what you do, am Seeing.
34:12: 12- And to Solomon the wind, meaning: And We subjected the wind to Solomon. Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim: The wind in the nominative case, meaning: He subjected the wind. Its morning journey is a month and its evening journey is a month, meaning: The morning journey of that wind subjected to him was a month’s journey, and its evening journey was a month’s journey, and it would travel with him in one day a two-month journey. Al-Hasan said: He would go out from Damascus and take a nap in Istakhr, which is a month’s journey away from there. Then he would go back from Istakhr and spend the night in Kabul, which is a month’s journey away from there for a fast rider. It was said that he ate his food in the river and had dinner in Samarkand. And We made a spring of molten copper flow for him, meaning: We melted a spring of copper for him. Qatar means copper. The commentators said: The copper spring flowed for him for three days and nights like running water, and it was in the land of Yemen. Today people only benefit from what God brought forth for Solomon. And among the jinn were those who worked before him by permission of their Lord, by the command of their Lord. Ibn Abbas said: God subjected the jinn to Solomon and commanded them to obey him in what he commanded them. And whoever among them deviates, that is, deviates, from Our command, which We commanded of obeying Solomon, We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze, in the Hereafter. Some of them said: in this world, and that is because God Almighty assigned to them an angel with a whip of fire in his hand. And whoever among them deviates from the command of Solomon, He will strike him with a blow that will burn him.
34:13: 13- They build for him whatever he wants of sanctuaries, meaning mosques, and tall buildings. Among the things they built for him was the Temple of Jerusalem, which David began and raised to the height of a man. Then God revealed to him, “I did not complete that at your hands, but I will have a son of yours whom I will rule after you, whose name is Solomon. I will complete it at his hands.” When God took him, he appointed Solomon as his successor, and he wanted to complete the construction of the Temple of Jerusalem. He gathered the jinn and devils and divided the work among them, assigning each group of them a task that he would extract for him. He sent the jinn and devils to obtain marble and white gypsum from its mines. He ordered the city to be built with marble and stone, and made it into twelve suburbs. He assigned a tribe to each suburb, and they were twelve tribes. When he finished building the city, he began building the mosque, so he sent the devils, groups by groups, to extract gold, silver, and rubies from their mines and pure pearls from the sea, and groups to extract jewels and stones from their places. And groups would bring him musk, amber, and all other perfumes from their places. So he brought from that something that only God Almighty could count. Then he brought craftsmen and ordered them to carve those high stones and make them into panels, and to repair those jewels and pierce the remaining pearls. So he built the mosque with white, yellow, and green marble, and its pillars with pure gypsum columns, and its roof with panels of precious jewels, and its ceilings and walls were decorated with pearls, rubies, and all other jewels. He spread its floor with panels of turquoise. At that time, there was no house on earth more splendid or more luminous than that mosque. It shone in the darkness like the moon on a full moon night. When he finished it, he gathered the rabbis of the Children of Israel to him and informed them that God Almighty had built it, and that everything in it was purely for God. He took that day on which he finished it as a festival. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When Solomon finished building the Temple in Jerusalem, he asked his Lord for three things, and He gave him two. I hope that He gave him the third. He asked for a rule that would be in accordance with His rule, and He gave it to him. He asked for a kingdom that no one after him would have, and He gave it to him. He asked that no one should come to this House and pray two rak’ahs in it except that he would emerge from his sins as on the day his mother bore him. I hope that He gave him that.” They said: Jerusalem remained as Solomon had built it until Tukhtanasr invaded it, destroyed the city, demolished it, and demolished the mosque. He took the gold, silver, pearls, rubies, and other jewels that were in its ceilings and walls and carried them to his kingdom in the land of Iraq. The devils built for Solomon in Yemen many amazing fortresses made of rock. God the Almighty said: And statues, meaning: They used to make statues for Him, meaning: images from copper, brass, alum, glass, and marble. It was also said: They used to make images of wild animals and birds. It was also said: They used to place images of angels, prophets, and righteous people in mosques so that people would see them and increase their worship. Perhaps this was permitted in their religion, just as Jesus used to make images from clay, then breathe life into them and they would become birds by God’s permission. And bowls, meaning bowls, the singular of which is jafna, “like a jug,” like basins in which water is collected, the singular of which is jabiyya, it is said: a thousand men would gather around a single jug to eat from it. And fixed pots, fixed with legs that could not be moved from their places due to their size, and they could not fall or become stuck, and one could climb them by ladders, and they were in Yemen. Work, O family of David, in gratitude, meaning: And We said, Work, O family of David, in gratitude. Its meaning is: Work, O family of David, in obedience to God in gratitude to Him for His blessings. And few of My servants are grateful, meaning: those who obey Me in gratitude for My blessings. It was said: What is meant by the family of David is David himself. It was also said: David, Solomon, and his family. Jaafar bin Sulaiman said: I heard Thabit say: The Prophet David, peace be upon him, divided the hours of the night and day among his family, and not a single hour of the night or day would pass without a person from the family of David standing and praying.
34:14: 14- So when We decreed death for him, meaning: for Solomon. Scholars said: Solomon, peace be upon him, used to seclude himself in the Holy House for a year or two years, a month or two months, or less than that, and more, and he would put his food and drink in it. He put it in the place he died. The beginning of that was that he would not wake up a day without a tree growing in the sanctuary of the Holy House. He would ask it: What is your name? It would say: My name is such and such. He would say: What are you for? It would say: For such and such. He would order it to be cut down. If it grew for planting, he would plant it, and if it was for medicine, he would write it down, until the carob tree grew. He said to it: What are you? It said: The carob tree. He said: What did it grow for? It said: For the destruction of your mosque. Solomon said: God would not destroy it while I am alive. You are the one upon whose face is my destruction and the destruction of the Holy House! So he took it down and planted it in his wall, then he said: O God, conceal my death from the jinn so that mankind may know that the jinn do not know the unseen. The jinn used to tell mankind that they knew things of the unseen and what was in the future. Then he entered the prayer niche and stood up to pray, leaning on his staff, and he died standing. The prayer niche had windows in front of him and behind him. The jinn used to do the hard work they had done during his lifetime, and they would look at him, thinking that he was alive. They did not deny that he had been prevented from going out to the people because of the length of his prayer before that. They continued to visit him after his death for a full year until the termites ate away at Solomon’s staff, and he fell dead, so they knew of his death. Ibn Abbas said: “The jinn thanked the earth, for they bring it water and mud inside the wood. This is why He said: ‘Nothing informed them of his death except a creature of the earth,’ which is the earth, ‘eating his staff,’ meaning his stick. The people of Medina and Abu Amr read: ‘his staff,’ without a hamza, while the rest read it with a hamza. These are two dialects. Ibn Amir pronounces the hamza quiescent. Its origin is from ‘nas’at al-ghanam,’ meaning ‘I drove the sheep to drink and watered them.’ From this comes ‘God delayed his term,’ meaning He postponed it.” When he fell down, that is, he fell to the ground, the jinn realized, that is, the jinn knew and were certain, that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment, that is, in the fatigue and misery, subjected to Solomon while he was dead, thinking he was alive. By this, God wanted the jinn to know that they did not know the unseen, because they thought they knew the unseen, due to the prevalence of ignorance. Al-Azhari mentioned that the meaning of the jinn became clear is: the jinn appeared and were revealed to mankind, that is, it became clear that they did not know the unseen, because they had made that seem to mankind. In the reading of Ibn Mas’ud and Ibn Abbas: It became clear to mankind that if the jinn knew the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment, that is, mankind knew and were certain of that. And Jacob read: It was revealed with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ya’, meaning: I informed the jinn and mankind. It was mentioned in the form of an unspecified agent, and tabayyin is intransitive and transitive. Historians have mentioned that Solomon was fifty-three years old, and that his reign lasted for forty years. He became king when he was thirteen years old, and he began building the Temple of Jerusalem four years into his reign.
34:15: God Almighty said: 15- Indeed, Saba’ had a place of habitation. Abu Sabrah Al-Nakha’i narrated on the authority of Furwah bin Masik Al-Atifi, who said: “A man said: O Messenger of God, tell me about Saba’, was it a man, a woman, or a land? He said: He was a man from the Arabs and he had ten children, six of whom were on the right path and four on the wrong path. As for those who were on the right path, they were Kindah, the Ash’ariyyun, Azd, Madhhij, Anmar, and Himyar. A man said: Who are Anmar? He said: Those among them were Khatham and Bajila. As for those who were on the wrong path, they were Amala, Judham, Lakhm, and Ghassan. Saba’ is the son of Yashjub bin Ya’rub bin Qahtan.” In their dwelling place, Hamzah and Hafs read: their dwelling place with a fat-ha on the kaf, for the singular, and Al-Kisa’i read it with a kasra on the kaf, and the others read: their dwelling place in the plural, and their dwelling place was in Ma’rib in Yemen, a sign, indicating our oneness and our power, then he explained the sign and said: two gardens, meaning: they are two gardens, on the right and on the left, meaning: on the right and left of the valley. It was said: To the right and left of those who came to them, and they had a valley. It was said that the two gardens surrounded that valley. Eat, meaning: and it was said to them: Eat, from the provision of your Lord, meaning: from the fruits of the two gardens. Al-Suddi and Muqatil said: A woman would carry her basket on her head and pass by the two gardens, and her basket would be filled with various types of fruits without her touching anything with her hand. And be grateful to Him, meaning: for the blessings He has provided you with. The meaning is: Work in obedience to Him. A good land, meaning: the land of Sheba, a good land, not a salt marsh. Ibn Zayd said: Not a mosquito, fly, flea, scorpion, or snake was seen in their land. A man would pass by their land and there would be lice on his clothes, and all the lice would die from the good air. This is what God Almighty said: A good land, meaning: good air. And a Forgiving Lord, Muqatil said: And your Lord, if you are grateful for what He has provided you, is a Forgiving Lord of sins.
34:16: 16- So they turned away. Wahb said: So God sent thirteen prophets to Sheba, and they called them to God and reminded them of His blessings upon them and warned them of His punishment, but they denied them and said: We do not know of any blessing from God Almighty upon us, so say to your Lord to withhold these blessings from us if He is able. This is what God Almighty said: So they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam. The dam is the plural of dam, which is the dam that holds back water. Ibn Al-A'rabi said: Al-Aram is an unbearable flood. It was also said that it was red water that God sent upon them from wherever He wished. It was also said that Al-Aram is a valley, and its origin is from Al-Aramah, which means severity and strength. Ibn Abbas, Wahb, and others said: That dam was built by Bilqis, because they used to fight over the water of their valley. So she ordered their valley to be blocked with Al-Aram, which is Al-Misnat in the Himyarite dialect. She blocked it between the two mountains with rocks and tar, and made three gates for it, one above the other. She built a huge pool behind it and made twelve outlets in it for their rivers. They opened them when they needed water, and when they were rich, they blocked them. When the rain came, the water of the valleys of Yemen gathered to it, and the torrent was held back behind the dam. So she ordered the upper gate to be opened and its water flowed into the pool. They would drink from the upper gate, then from the second, then from the third, the lower gate, and the water would not run out until the water returned the following year. She used to divide it among them accordingly, and they remained like that for a period after that. Then, when they rebelled and disbelieved, God sent against them a rat called Al-Khald, which pierced the dam from below, and the water flooded their gardens and destroyed their land. Wahb said: “Among the things they claimed and found in their knowledge and divination was that a mouse would destroy their dam. So they did not leave a gap between two rocks without tying a cat to it. When the time came and God Almighty wanted them to drown, as they say, a large red mouse approached one of those cats and argued with it until the cat was delayed. It entered the gap it was near and penetrated the dam, burrowing and digging until it weakened it for the flood. They were unaware of that. When the flood came, it found a hole and entered it until it broke the dam and flooded their property, drowning it and burying their houses in the sand. They were scattered and dispersed until they became a proverb among the Arabs. They say: The sons of so-and-so became the hands of Saba’ and the hands of Saba’, meaning: they were scattered and dispersed. This is what God Almighty said: ‘So We sent upon them the flood of the dam.’” And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter fruit. The general public read it with the tanween, while the people of Basra read it as khamt with the addition. Food means fruit, and bitter fruit means the arak tree, and its fruit is called barir. This is the opinion of most of the commentators. Al-Mubarrad and Al-Zajjaj said: Any plant that has a bitter taste to the point that it cannot be eaten is called khmat. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Al-Khamt is the fruit of a tree called Faswat al-Dab', which is similar to poppy seeds and is rubbed but not used. Whoever makes Al-Khamt a name for something eaten, then the tanween in eat is good. Whoever makes it the root and eats the fruit, then the addition is clear, and the tanween is acceptable. The Arabs say: In the garden of so-and-so are grapes of vineyards, translating grapes as vineyards because they come from it. And tamarisk and some little lote trees. Tamarisk is the tamarisk, and it was said that it is a tree similar to the tamarisk except that it is larger than it. The lote tree is a well-known tree, and it is the nabq tree, whose leaves are used for washing the head and are planted in gardens. This was not of that nature, rather it was a wild lote tree that is not used and whose leaves are not good for anything. Qatada said: The tree of the people was one of the best trees, but God made it one of the worst trees because of their actions.
34:17: 17- That is how We rewarded them for their disbelief, meaning: that which We did to them, We rewarded them for their disbelief. And do We reward anyone but the ungrateful? Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Hafs, and Ya’qub read: And do We reward anyone but the ungrateful? with a noon and a kasra on the zay. The ungrateful is in the accusative case because of His statement: That is how We rewarded them. The others read it with a ya’ and a fatha on the zay. The ungrateful is in the nominative case, meaning: And does anyone reward anyone but the ungrateful with such a punishment? Mujahed said: He punishes means he punishes. It is said of punishment: He punishes and of reward: He rewards. Muqatil said: Is anyone rewarded for his bad deeds except the ungrateful to God for His blessings? Al-Farra’ said: The believer is rewarded but not recompensed, meaning: He is rewarded for his deeds and is not recompensed for his bad deeds.
34:18: 18- And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed with water and trees, which are the towns of Ash-Sham, towns visible, connected, the second one visible from the first because of its proximity to it. Their trade was from Yemen to Ash-Sham, so they would spend the night in one town and come to another, and they did not need to carry provisions from Sheba to Ash-Sham. It was said: Their villages were four thousand seven hundred connected villages from Saba to the Levant. And We measured the journey therein, meaning: We measured their journey between these villages, and their journey in the morning and evening was about half a day’s journey. So if they had traveled for half a day, they would have reached a village with water and trees. Qatada said: A woman would go out with her spindle and her basket on her head, and she would work with her spindle and not return home until her basket was full of fruits. This was the case between Yemen and Syria. Travel therein, meaning: We said to them, Travel therein. It was said that it is a command with the meaning of a statement, meaning: We enabled them to travel, so they traveled therein, for nights and days, meaning: by nights and days, at any time they wished, in security, not fearing an enemy, hunger, or thirst. So they became arrogant and transgressed and could not bear the hardship, and they said: If our gardens were further away than they are, it would be more appropriate for us to desire it.
34:19: 19- "They said, 'Our Lord, extend our journeys.' So place between us and Syria deserts and areas of separation so that we may ride our camels and stock up on provisions. So God answered them. Mujahid said, 'They became arrogant with the blessing and grew tired of comfort.'" Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read: ba’d with emphasis from ta’beed. The others read: ba’ed with an alif, and each is in the form of a supplication and a question. Ya’qub read: Our Lord with the ba’ raised, ba’ed with the fatha over the ‘ayn and the dal as report, as if they had distanced their short journeys and were arrogant and wicked. And they wronged themselves, through arrogance and tyranny. So We made them stories, a lesson for those who came after them to talk about their situation and their affairs, and We tore them apart, We scattered them in every direction in the country. Al-Sha’bi said: When their villages were submerged, they dispersed throughout the country. As for the Ghassanids, they went to the Levant, and the Azd went to Oman, and the Khuza’a to Tihama, and the Khuzaymah family went to Iraq, and the Aws and Khazraj to Yathrib. The one who came from them to Medina was Amr ibn Amir, and he is the grandfather of the Aws and Khazraj. Indeed in that are signs, lessons and indications, for everyone who is patient, in avoiding the sins of God, grateful, for His blessings. Muqatil said: It means the believer of this nation is patient in the face of adversity and grateful for blessings. Mutraf said: It is the believer who is grateful when given something, and patient when afflicted.
34:20: God the Almighty said: 20- "And Satan proved true his assumption about them." The people of Kufa read: "Sadaq" with emphasis, meaning: he had an assumption about them when he said: "Then by Your might, I will surely mislead them all Sad 82, And You will not find most of them grateful" Al-A'raf 17. So he proved his assumption true and made it happen by doing that to them and making them follow him. The others read it with emphasis, meaning: he proved true in his assumption about them, meaning: the people of Sheba. Mujahid said: about all people except those who obeyed God, "and they followed him, except for a party of the believers." Al-Suddi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means all the believers because the believers did not follow him in the fundamentals of the religion, and God the Almighty said: "Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority" Al-Hijr 42, meaning: the believers. It was said: It is specific to the believers who obey God and do not disobey Him. Ibn Qutaybah said: When Satan asked for respite and God granted him respite, he said, I will mislead them and lead them astray. He was not certain at the time of this statement that what he said about them would come true, but rather he said it based on conjecture. They rarely followed him and obeyed him, and what he thought about them came true. Al-Hasan said: He did not draw a sword against them nor did he strike them with a whip, but he made promises to them and gave them false hope, so they were deceived.
34:21: God Almighty said: 21- And he had no authority over them, meaning: We did not give him authority over them, except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from him who is in doubt about it, meaning: except that We might know, see and distinguish the believer from the disbeliever, and He meant the knowledge of occurrence and appearance, and it was known to Him in the unseen, and your Lord is Guardian over all things, Watchful.
34:22: 22- Say, O Muhammad, to the infidels of Mecca, Call upon those you claim, that they are gods, besides God, and in the verse there is an ellipsis, meaning: Call upon them to remove the harm that has befallen you in the years of famine. Then he described it and said: They do not possess an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth, of good and evil, benefit and harm, and they have no, meaning: the gods, in them, in the heavens and the earth, any association, partnership, and God has no, meaning: nor God, among them any supporter, helper.
34:23: 23- And no intercession will benefit with Him except for him whom He permits. God regarding intercession, said this to refute them when they said: These are our intercessors with God. It is possible that the meaning is except for him whom God permits to intercede for. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read: permitted with a damma on the hamza. Until when fear is removed from their hearts, Ibn Amir and Yaqub read it with a fat-ha on the fa and the zay, and the others read it with a damma on the fa and a kasra on the zay, meaning: He removed the fear and took it out from their hearts. So, tafzee’ means removing fear, like tamreed and tafrid. They differed about those described with this attribute. Some people said: They are the angels. Then they differed about the reason for that. Some of them said: It is only because of the faintness that befalls their hearts that they hear the words of God, the Almighty. We narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word, as if it were a chain beating a rock. Then when fear is removed from their hearts, they say: What did your Lord say? They say: The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.” Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, he said: Muhammad bin Al-Fadl bin Muhammad told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Khuzaymah told us, Zakariya bin Yahya bin Aban Al-Masry told us, Na’im bin Hammad told us, Abu Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jabir, on the authority of Abu Zakariya, on the authority of Raja’ bin Haywah, on the authority of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God wants to reveal something, He speaks the revelation, and the heavens are seized by it with a tremor, or he said: a severe trembling, out of fear of God the Most High. When the people of the heavens hear that, they swoon and fall down in prostration to God. The first to raise his head is Gabriel, and God speaks to him from His revelation what He wanted. Then Gabriel passes by the angels, and whenever he passes by a heaven, its angels ask him, ‘What did our Lord say, O Gabriel?’ Gabriel says: ‘The Truth said, and He is the Most High, the Grand.’ They all say the same as Gabriel said, and Gabriel ends with the revelation where He commanded him.” God". Some of them said that they are only afraid of the Day of Resurrection. Muqatil, Al-Kalbi and Al-Suddi said: The period between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, was five hundred and fifty years, and some say six hundred years, during which the angels did not hear any revelation. When God sent Muhammad, peace be upon him, with the message, when the angels heard it, they thought it was the Hour. When Gabriel descended, he began to pass by the inhabitants of each heaven, uncovering what they saw, and they would raise their heads and say to one another: What did your Lord say? They said: He said the truth, meaning the revelation, and He is the Most High, the Grand. A group said: Those described as such are the polytheists. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: When the fear was removed from the hearts of the polytheists at the time of their death, as proof was established against them, the angels said to them, What did your Lord say in this world? They said, The truth. So they acknowledged it when acknowledgment was of no use to them.
34:24: God Almighty says: 24- “Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?” So, the provision from the heavens is the rain, and from the earth is the plants. “Say: God,” meaning: If they do not say: God provides for us, then say: God is your provider. And either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. This is not by way of doubt, but rather by way of fairness in argument, as one says to another: One of us is a liar, while he knows that he is truthful and his companion is a liar. Meaning: We and you are not on the same path, but rather one of the two groups is guided and the other is astray. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who followed him are on the right path, and those who disagreed with him are astray. So he denied them without explicitly declaring the denial. Some of them said: Or it means the letter waw, and the alif in it is a connection, as if he said: And we and you are upon guidance or in clear misguidance, meaning: We are upon guidance and you are in misguidance.
34:25: 25- Say, ‘You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you do.’
34:26: 26- “Say: Our Lord will gather us together,” meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, then He will judge, decide, “between us in truth. And He is the Judge, the Knowing.”
34:27: 27- “Say: Show me those whom you have associated with Him as partners.” That is, inform me of those whom you have associated with Him, that is, with God, as partners in worship with Him. Do they create and do they provide for themselves? No, they do not create and do not provide for themselves. Rather, He is God, the Exalted in Might, the Supreme in His affair, the Wise in His management of His creation. So how could He have a partner in His kingdom?
34:28: God Almighty said: 28- And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to mankind, meaning: to all mankind, both red and black, as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, meaning: a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of the people do not know. We narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A prophet was sent to his people specifically, but I was sent to all of mankind. It was said: All meaning: Sufficient that will prevent them from their disbelief, and the ha is for emphasis.
34:29: 29- And they say, ‘When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?’ Meaning the Resurrection.
34:30: 30- Say to you, ‘There is an appointment for you on a Day from which you will not be delayed an hour, nor will you be brought forward.’ That is, you will not be advanced, meaning the Day of Resurrection. Ad-Dahhak said: The Day of Death from which you will not be delayed or advanced, by your lifespan being increased or decreased.
34:31: 31- And those who disbelieve say, ‘We will not believe in this Qur’an or in that before it,’ meaning: the Torah and the Gospel. And if you could but see, O Muhammad, when the wrongdoers are stopped, imprisoned, before their Lord, referring to each other in word, referring to each other in argument. Those who were oppressed will say, those who were despised, and they are the followers, to those who were arrogant, and they are the leaders and nobles, If it were not for you, we would have been believers, meaning: you prevented us from believing in God and His Messenger.
34:32: 32- Those who were arrogant said, those who were followed in disbelief answered them, to those who were oppressed, ‘Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals,’ by abandoning faith.
34:33: 33- And those who were oppressed said to those who were arrogant, ‘Rather, it is your plotting by night and by day.’ That is, your plotting against us by night and by day. The Arabs add the verb to night and day to expand the speech, as the poet said: I slept, but the mounts were not asleep at night It was said: The deceit of night and day is the length of safety and the length of hope in them, as God Almighty said: So the period was prolonged for them, and their hearts hardened (al-Hadid 57:16). When you ordered us to disbelieve in God and attribute to Him equals, and they concealed their regret when they saw the punishment, and We placed shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved, in the Fire, both the followers and the followed. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do? of disbelief and sins in this world?
34:34: 34- And We did not send to any city a warner but its affluent people said, its leaders and rich people, Indeed, we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers.
34:35: 35- And they said, meaning: the wealthy said to the poor who believed: We have more wealth and children, and if God had not been pleased with our religion and deeds, He would not have granted us wealth and children, and we will not be punished, meaning: God has been kind to us in this world with wealth and children, so He will not punish us.
34:36: 36- Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it.’ That is, God expands provision and restricts it as a test and trial. Expansion does not indicate God’s pleasure with him, nor restriction indicates His displeasure. But most people do not know, that it is so.
34:37: 37- And it is not your wealth and your children that bring you near to Us, meaning: nearness. Al-Akhfash said: Nearness is a verbal noun, as if he said: by that which brings you near to Us, except for he who believes, meaning: but he who believes, and does righteousness, Ibn Abbas said: He means his faith and his deeds that bring him closer to Me, For those will be a double reward for what they did, meaning: God will double their good deeds for them, so He will reward for one good deed ten to seven hundred. Ya’qub read: Reward in the accusative case, with the double being raised, meaning: For those will be a double reward. The general public read it with the addition, and they will be in the chambers, secure. Hamza read: in the chamber as one, and the others read it in the plural, because of His saying: We will surely assign them chambers in Paradise Al-Ankabut 58.
34:38: 38- And those who strive, who work, against Our signs, to invalidate Our argument, to be unable, who are stubborn and think that they can defeat Us and elude Us, those will be brought to the punishment.
34:39: 39- “Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for whomever He wills. And whatever you spend, He will replace it.’” That is, He will give what is replaced. Saeed bin Jubair said: Whatever was neither extravagance nor miserliness, He will replace it. Al-Kalbi said: Whatever you give in charity or spend in good, He will replace it for the one who spent it, either by giving it to him in this world or by saving it for him in the hereafter. "And He is the best of providers," the best of those who give and provide. We narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty said: Spend and I will spend on you.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ismail told us, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Sulayman - he is Ibn Bilal - on the authority of Muawiyah bin Abi Mazrad - on the authority of Abu Al-Habhab - on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no day in which the servants arise except that two angels descend and one of them says: ‘O God, give to the one who spends in charity a replacement,’ and the other says: ‘O God, give to the one who withholds destruction.’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ibn Abi Uwais told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Charity does not decrease wealth, and God does not increase a servant’s forgiveness except in honor, and no one humbles himself before God except that God raises him up. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam'ani told us, Abu Ja'far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abu Al-Rabi' told us, Abdul Hamid bin Al-Hasan Al-Hilali told us, Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir told us, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Every good deed is a charity, and everything a man spends on himself and his family is recorded as charity for him, and whatever a man uses to protect his honor is recorded as charity for him.' I said: 'What does it mean when a man protects his honor?' He said: 'What a poet or a man of eloquence gives to the pious, and whatever a believer spends, God is responsible for replacing it, except for what is spent on building or in disobeying God, the Almighty and Majestic.'" He said: I said what does Abdul Hamid mean to say to Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir? Mujahid said: If one of you has something in his hand, let him be moderate and not misinterpret this verse: And whatever you spend - He will replace it. For sustenance is apportioned, and perhaps his sustenance is little, and he spends on the expenses of one who is well-off. The meaning of the verse is: And whatever is left behind is from him.
34:40: God Almighty says: 40- And the Day He will gather them together, Ya’qub and Hafs read: He will gather them together, and the others read with a nun, all together, meaning: these infidels, Then He will say to the angels, ‘Was it these you who used to worship?’ in the world. Qatada said: This is a question of confirmation, like God Almighty’s saying to Jesus: Did you tell the people to take me and my mother as gods besides God? Maryam 116, so the angels will disavow them.
34:41: 41- They said, ‘Glory be to You,’ glorifying You, ‘You are our protector rather than them,’ meaning: We are your protector and not their protector. Rather, they used to worship the jinn, meaning: the devils. If it is said to them, They used to worship the angels, then what is the meaning of His statement, They used to worship the jinn, it is said: He meant the devils who made the worship of the angels attractive to them, so they used to obey the devils in worshipping the angels. So His statement, They used to worship, means: they obey the jinn, Most of them are believers in them, meaning: they believe in the devils.
34:42: Then God says: 42- So today you will not possess for one another any benefit, by intercession, nor any harm, by punishment. He means that they are powerless, they will not have any benefit or harm, and We will say to those who did wrong, ‘Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.’
34:43: 43- “And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, ‘This is nothing but a man who wants to avert you from what your fathers used to worship.’ And they say, ‘This is nothing but a fabricated lie.’” They mean the Qur’an. And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, ‘This is nothing but obvious magic.’ That is, it is clear.
34:44: 44- And We did not give them, meaning: these polytheists, any books to study, to read, nor did We send to them before you any warner, meaning: no prophet came to the Arabs before you, nor was a book sent down to them.
34:45: 45- And those before them denied, of the nations, Our messengers, and they are: Aad, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the people of Lot, and others, and they did not attain, meaning: these polytheists, a tenth, meaning: a tenth, of what We gave them, meaning: We gave the nations that lacked strength, grace, and long life, “so they denied My messengers. So how was My denial,” meaning: My denial and change of them, warning the disbelievers of this nation of the punishment of the past nations.
34:46: 46- “Say, ‘I only admonish you of one thing,’ I command you and advise you of one thing, that is, one characteristic, then He explained that characteristic and said: “That you stand up for God,” for the sake of God, in pairs, that is, two by two, and individually, that is, one by one, then reflect, all together, that is, you gather and look and converse with one another and be alone, so you reflect on the state of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you learn, There is no madness in your companion, madness. What is meant by standing up is not the standing that is the opposite of sitting, but rather it is standing up for the matter that is in seeking the truth, like His saying: And that you stand up for orphans with justice An-Nisa’ 127. It is, what it is, only a warner to you before a severe punishment. Muqatil said: The speech ended when he said: Then you will reflect, meaning: on the creation of the heavens and the earth, and learn that their Creator is One, with no partner. Then he began by saying: Your companion is not possessed.
34:47: 47- “Say: I do not ask you for any reward for conveying the message, lest you accuse me.” He said: Say: I do not ask you for any reward for conveying the message, lest you accuse me. The meaning of his saying: It is for you is: I did not ask you for anything, like someone saying: I have nothing to do with this, for I have given it to you, meaning I have nothing to do with it. My reward, what is my recompense, is only from God, and He is Witness over all things.
34:48: 48- Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord casts the truth.’ Casting is throwing an arrow, pebbles, or speech. Its meaning is: He brings the truth and the revelation that He sends down from the sky and casts it to the prophets. Knower of the unseen. It is raised by the predicate of that, meaning: He is the Knower of the unseen.
34:49: 49- “Say, ‘The truth has come,’ meaning: the Qur’an and Islam, ‘and falsehood can neither originate nor restore.’” That is, falsehood has gone and been swept away, and nothing remains of it that can originate or restore anything, as God Almighty said: Rather, We hurl the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it. (Al-Anbiya’: 48). Qatada said: Falsehood is Satan, and this is the opinion of Muqatil and Al-Kalbi. It has also been said that falsehood is idols.
34:50: 50- “Say: If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment.” That is because the infidels of Mecca were saying to him: You have gone astray when you abandoned the religion of your fathers. So God Almighty said: “Say: If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment,” meaning: The sin of my going astray is upon me. And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me, of the Qur’an and wisdom. He is All-Hearing, All-Near.
34:51: 51- And if you could but see when they are terrified, Qatada said about the resurrection when they emerge from their graves, there is no escape, meaning: they will not escape Me, as He said: and there is no time for escape Sad-3. It was also said: When they are terrified, there will be no escape or salvation. And they are seized from a place nearby, Al-Kalbi said: from beneath their feet. It was also said: they were seized from the depths of the earth to its surface, and wherever they are, they are close to God, they will not escape Him. It was also said: from a place nearby, meaning the torment of this world. Ad-Dahhak said: on the day of Badr. Ibn Abzi said: it was swallowed up in the desert. There is an omission in the verse, the meaning of which is: And if you could see when they are terrified, you would see a matter that you would consider.
34:52: 52- And they said, ‘We believe in it,’ when they witnessed the torment. It was said: at the time of despair. And it was said: at the time of resurrection. And how, from where, can they grasp it? Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr read: grasping it with a long vowel and a hamza. The others read it with a clear waw without a long vowel or a hamza. Its meaning is to grasp, i.e., how can they grasp what is far from them, which is faith and repentance, when it was close in this world and they wasted it? And whoever uses a hamza, it was said that its meaning is this as well. It is said that tanawash with a hamza comes from nabsh, which is a movement in slowness. It is said: He came nabsh, meaning: slowly, late. The meaning is: how can they move in what they have no power over? And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: They ask to be returned to the world, so it is said: how can they be returned to the world? "From a far place", that is, from the afterlife to this world.
34:53: 53- And they had disbelieved in it before, meaning: the Qur’an, and it was said: in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, before they witnessed the punishment and the horrors of the Day of Resurrection, and they cast aspersions upon the unseen from a distant place, Mujahid said: They cast aspersions upon Muhammad based on conjecture, not on certainty, and this is what they say about a magician, poet, or soothsayer. The meaning of the unseen is conjecture because its knowledge was hidden from them, and the distant place is their distance from the knowledge of what they are saying, and the meaning is they cast aspersions upon Muhammad with what they do not know from where they do not know. Qatada said: They cast aspersions based on conjecture, saying there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Hellfire.
34:54: 54- And they will be prevented from what they desire, meaning: faith, repentance, and returning to this world.
