It was also said: the pleasures and luxuries of this world, as He did with their followers, meaning: their peers and those who were in the same state as them from the disbelievers, before, meaning: faith and repentance were not accepted from them at the time of despair, indeed, they were in doubt, about the resurrection and the punishment descending upon them, disturbing, causing suspicion and accusation for them.
35:1: 1- Praise be to God, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, their Creator and Initiator without any previous example, who has made the angels messengers with wings, with wings two, three, or four. Qatada and Muqatil said: Some of them have two wings, some of them have three wings, and some of them have four wings, and He adds to them what He wills, and this is His saying, He adds to creation what He wills. Ibn Masoud said about the Almighty’s words: He has certainly seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord (al-Najm 53:18). He said that he saw Gabriel in his form with six hundred wings. Ibn Shihab said about his statement: He increases in creation what He wills, he said: A beautiful voice. On the authority of Qatada, he said: It is the beauty in the eyes. It was also said: It is the mind and discrimination. God is capable of everything.
35:2: 2- Whatever mercy God opens to mankind, it was said: of rain and provisions, no one can withhold it, no one can stop it, “and whatever He withholds, no one can release it after Him. And He is the Exalted in Might,” in what He withheld, the Wise. In what He sent. Imam Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abdullah ibn Asbat told us, my father told us, Abd al-Malik ibn Umair told us, on the authority of Warad, on the authority of al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say after every prescribed prayer: ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner for Him. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. O God, there is no one who can withhold what You have given, nor give what You have withheld, and wealth does not benefit one who is wealthy from You.’”
35:3: 3- “O mankind, remember the favor of God upon you. Is there a creator other than God?” Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with the genitive case of the ra’, while the others read it with the genitive case, meaning, Is there a creator other than God? because min is an addition. This is a question on the path of confirmation, as if he said: There is no creator other than God. He provides for you from the sky and the earth, meaning: from the sky is rain and from the earth is vegetation. There is no god except Him, so how are you deluded?
35:4: 4- And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], [other] messengers before you were denied, he consoled his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to God all matters are returned.
35:5: 5- O mankind, indeed the promise of God is true, meaning the promise of the Day of Resurrection, so let not the worldly life deceive you, and let not the Deceiver deceive you about God, which is Satan.
35:6: 6- Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy, meaning: be hostile to him by obeying God and do not obey him. He only invites his party, meaning: his followers and supporters, to be among the companions of the Blaze, meaning: to be in the Blaze.
35:7: Then he explained the situation of those who agreed with him and those who disagreed with him, saying: 7- Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, but those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.
35:8: God Almighty said: 8- Then is he to whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive? Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl and the polytheists of Mecca. Saeed bin Jubair said: It was revealed about the people of whims and innovations. Qatada said: Among them are the Khawarij who consider the blood and money of Muslims permissible. As for the people of major sins, they are not among them, because they do not consider major sins permissible. Is he who has made his evil deed seem good to him? That is, his ugly deed, so he sees it as good, Satan has made it seem good to him through whispering. In the verse, its metaphor is omitted: Is he who has had his evil deeds made attractive to him so he sees falsehood as truth like he whom God has guided so he sees truth as truth and falsehood as falsehood? For God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills? It was said: Its answer is under his saying: So do not let yourself waste away in regret over them, so its meaning is: Is it he for whom the evil of his deeds has been made pleasing to God, and God has led him astray, that your soul will waste away in regret over him? That is, you will feel regret over him, so do not let yourself waste away in regret over them. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: It contains an inversion of the meaning of: “Then is he to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive so he regards it as good? So let not yourself perish over them in regret. Indeed, God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills.” Regret is intense sadness over what has passed of the matter, and the meaning of the verse: Do not be distressed by their disbelief and destruction if they do not believe. Abu Jaafar read: So do not go with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ha’, Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what they do.
35:9: 9- “And it is God who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and revive the earth thereby after its lifelessness. Thus is the resurrection,” from the graves.
35:11: God Almighty said: 11- And God created you from dust, meaning Adam, then from a sperm-drop, meaning his offspring, then He made you pairs, males and females, “and no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no long-lived person is granted a long life,” not by the length of his life, nor does his lifespan decrease, meaning by the lifespan of another, as it is said to someone, I have a dirham and a half of it, meaning another half dirham, except in a book. It was said that His statement, nor does his lifespan decrease refers to the first. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is written in the Mother of the Book, The lifespan of so-and-so is such-and-such years, then it is written below that, A day has passed, two days have passed, three days have passed, until his lifespan comes to an end. Ka'b al-Ahbar said when Umar may God be pleased with him was about to die: By God, if Umar had asked his Lord to delay his death, He would have delayed it. It was said to him that God, the Almighty, says: And when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it (al-A’raf 7:34). He said: This is when the term comes. As for before that, it is permissible for it to be increased or decreased. He recited this verse: Indeed, that, for God, is easy, meaning: writing down the terms and deeds is easy for God.
35:12: God Almighty says: 12- "And the two seas are not alike," meaning: the fresh and the salty. Then He mentioned them and said: "This is fresh and sweet, good, and its drink is palatable," meaning: it passes through the throat and is pleasant, "and this is salty and bitter," very salty. Ad-Dahhak said: it is bitter. "And from each you eat tender meat," meaning: whales, from both the fresh and salty seas, "and you extract ornaments," meaning: from the salty sea but not the fresh sea, "which you wear," meaning pearls. It was said that pearls were attributed to them because in the salty sea there are fresh springs that mix with the salt, and the pearl is from between that. "And you see the ships therein steaming, sailing ships coming and going with a single wind, that you may seek of His bounty, through trade, and perhaps you will be grateful, God for His blessings.
35:13: 13- “He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. That is God, your Lord. To Him belongs dominion. And those you invoke besides Him do not possess so much as a speck of dust,” meaning the idols, they do not possess even the smallest particle of dust, which is the wrapping of the seed, which is the thin shell that is on the seed.
35:14: 14- If you call upon them, meaning: if you call upon the idols, “they do not hear your call. And even if they heard, they would not respond to you,” they would not answer you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association, they will disavow you and your worship of them, saying: You did not worship us. “And no one informs you like the All-Knowing,” meaning Himself, meaning: no one informs you like Me, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware of things.
35:15: 15- O mankind, you are those in need of God, in need of God’s grace and the poor, and God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy, the One who is rich in need of His creation and is praised for His kindness to them.
35:16: 16- If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.
35:17: 17- And that is not difficult for God, severe.
35:18: 18- “And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if you call upon another one laden with sins,” meaning: a soul burdened with its sins, to bear it, meaning: to bear what he has of sins, nothing of it will be borne by him, even if he were a relative, meaning: even if the one called upon was a relative of his, his son, his father, his mother, or his brother. Ibn Abbas said: The father and mother will meet their son and say: O my son, bear some of my sins, and he will say: I am unable; what I have is sufficient for me. You only warn those who fear their Lord unseen, who have not seen Him. Al-Akhfash said: Its interpretation is: Your warning only benefits those who fear their Lord unseen, “and establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself,” is righteous and does good, purifies himself only for [the benefit of] his own soul, which will reward him, and to God is the final destination.
35:19: 19- The blind and the seeing are not alike, meaning: the ignorant and the knowledgeable. It was also said: the blind to guidance and the one who sees guidance, meaning: the believer and the polytheist.
35:20: 20- Nor darkness nor light, meaning: disbelief and faith.
35:21: 21- Nor shade nor heat, meaning: Paradise and Hell. Ibn Abbas said: Heat is the hot wind at night, and the poisonous winds during the day. It was also said that heat occurs during the day with the sun.
35:22: 22- The living are not equal to the dead, meaning: the believers and the disbelievers. It was also said: the scholars and the ignorant. God hears whom He wills, so that he may learn a lesson and respond. But you cannot make hear those in the graves, meaning: the disbelievers. He likened them to the dead in the graves when they did not respond.
35:23: 23- You are only a warner. You are only a warner who frightens them with the Fire.
35:24: 24- “Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there was no nation,” no nation in the past but that there passed among them a warner, a warning prophet.
35:25: 25- “And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], those before them denied. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs and scriptures and the enlightening Book.” It is clear that the Book was repeated after mentioning the scriptures as a way of emphasis.
35:26: 26- Then I seized those who disbelieved, and how terrible was My reproach.
35:27: 27- Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors? And from the mountains are streaks. Paths and lines, the singular of which is jadda, like: madda and madad. White and red of varying colors, and black raven, meaning: black raven, in order of precedence and delay. It is said: black gharib, meaning: very black, in resemblance to the color of the raven, meaning: black paths.
35:28: 28- And among people, beasts, and livestock are those whose colors vary. The metaphor was mentioned for the sake of of. It was said that the metaphor was returned to what was implied. Its meaning is: And among people, beasts, and livestock are those whose colors vary. Likewise, meaning just as the colors of fruits and mountains vary. The speech ended here, then he began and said: Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear God. Ibn Abbas said: He means that only those who created Me fear Me because of My power, might, and authority. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Umar bin Hafs told us, Al-A’mash told us, Muslim told us, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did something and permitted it, but some people refrained from it. report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he delivered a sermon, praised God, and then said: What is the matter with people who refrain from something that I do? By God, I am the most knowledgeable of them about God and the most fearful of Him.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much. Masruq said: Fearing God is sufficient knowledge, and being deceived by God is sufficient ignorance. A man said to Al-Sha’bi: Give me a fatwa, O scholar. Al-Sha’bi said: The scholar is he who fears God, the Almighty and Majestic. “God is Almighty and Forgiving,” meaning: Almighty in His kingdom and Forgiving of the sins of His servants.
35:29: God Almighty says: 29- Indeed, those who recite the Book of God, meaning: read the Qur’an, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, hope for a commerce that will never fail, that will never be corrupted or destroyed. What is meant by commerce is the reward that God has promised. Al-Farra’ said: His saying: They return is an answer to his saying: Those who recite the Book of God.
35:30: 30- To give them their rewards in full, the reward for their deeds, and to give them more from His bounty, Ibn Abbas said: meaning, in addition to the reward of what no eye has seen and no ear has heard, For He is Forgiving and Appreciative, Ibn Abbas said: He forgives the great of their sins and is appreciative of the small of their deeds.
35:31: 31- And that which We have revealed to you of the Book, meaning: the Qur’an, is the truth confirming what was before it, of the books. Indeed, God is Knowing and Seeing of His servants.
35:32: 32- Then We caused the Book to be inherited, meaning: the Book that We sent down to you, which was mentioned in the first verse, which is the Qur’an. We made it end with, those We chose from among Our servants. It is possible that then has the meaning of and, meaning: and We gave him an inheritance, like His statement: Then he was among those who believed (al-Balad 90:17), meaning: and he was among those who believed. The meaning of We gave him an inheritance is We gave, because inheritance is a gift, as Mujahid said. It was said: We gave you inheritance, meaning, We delayed it. And from this comes the word inheritance, because it was delayed from the dead. Its meaning is: We delayed the Qur’an from previous nations and gave it to you, and destroyed you for it. Those whom We have chosen from among Our servants, Ibn Abbas said: He means the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He divided them and arranged them, saying: Among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds. It was narrated on the authority of Usama bin Zaid regarding the words of God Almighty: Among them is he who wrongs himself verse, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All of them are from this nation. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Fanjuwayh told us, Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Qadi told us, Bakr bin Muhammad Al-Marzouqi told us, Abu Qilabah told us, Amr bin Al-Hussain told us, on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Umaira, on the authority of Maimun Al-Kurdi, on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, who said: I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab reciting on the pulpit: Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants, the verse, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Our forerunner is a forerunner, our moderate is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven. Abu Qilabah said: So I told it to Yahya bin Ma’in, and he began to marvel at it. The commentators differed on the meaning of the oppressor, the moderate, and the forerunner. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Isa al-Sayrafi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Barti told us, Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Thabit that a man entered the mosque and said: O God, have mercy on my loneliness, and comfort my solitude, and bring me a righteous companion. Abu al-Darda’ said: If you are truthful, then I am happier with you than you. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite this verse: “Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds.” He said: As for the one who is foremost in good deeds, he will enter Paradise without being brought to account. As for the moderate, he will be brought to a light account. As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be detained in the place until he is overcome by worry, then he will enter Paradise. Then he recited this verse: “And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.’” Uqbah ibn Sahban said: I asked Aisha about the words of God the Almighty: Then We caused to inherit the Book those We chose of Our servants Al-Baqarah 2:17, so she said: O my son, all of them are in Paradise. As for the one who is foremost in good deeds, he is the one who lived during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, testified that he would be in Paradise. As for the moderate one, he is the one who followed in his footsteps from his companions until he joined him. As for the one who wrongs himself, he is like me and you. So she placed herself with us. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Qatada said: Among them are those who are unjust to themselves, and they are the people of the left, and among them are those who are moderate, and they are the people of the right, and among them are those who are foremost in good deeds, by God’s permission, and they are the foremost who are close to all people. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The forerunner is the sincere believer, the moderate is the hypocrite, and the oppressor is the disbeliever in God’s blessings and not the ungrateful for them, because He decreed that the three would enter Paradise, saying: Gardens of Eden which they will enter. Some of them said: This is mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The foremost is the one whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds, the moderate is the one whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, and the unjust is the one whose bad deeds outweigh his good deeds. It was said: The oppressor is the one whose outward appearance is better than his inward appearance, the moderate is the one whose outward appearance and inward appearance are equal, and the forerunner is the one whose inward appearance is better than his outward appearance. It was said: The unjust person is the one who declares the oneness of God with his tongue, but his actions do not match his words. The moderate person is the one who declares the oneness of God with his tongue and obeys Him with his limbs. The forerunner is the one who declares the oneness of God with his tongue, obeys Him with his limbs, and dedicates his actions to Him. It was said: The oppressor is the one who recites the Qur’an, the moderate one who recites it and knows it, and the foremost one who recites it and knows it and acts according to what is in it. It was said: The oppressor is the one who commits major sins, the moderate is the one who commits minor sins, and the forerunner is the one who has not committed a major or minor sin. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: The forerunner is the scholar, the moderate is the learner, and the unjust is the ignorant. Ja'far al-Sadiq said: He began with the oppressors, informing them that one can only draw near to Him through His generosity, and that oppression does not affect one's selection. Then he followed with the moderate ones because they are between fear and hope. Then he concluded with the forerunners so that no one would be safe from His deceit, and all of them will be in Paradise. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: He arranged them in this order according to the ranks of people, because the states of the servant are three: disobedience, heedlessness, then repentance, then devotion. So if he disobeys, he enters the ranks of the oppressors, and if he repents, he enters the ranks of the moderate, and if the repentance is sincere and the worship and struggle are abundant, he enters the ranks of the foremost. Some of them said: What is meant by the oppressor is the infidel. This was mentioned by Al-Kalbi. It was said that what is meant by it is the hypocrite. Based on this, the oppressor is not included in His statement, Gardens of Eden which they shall enter. This speaker interpreted the selection as referring to the selection in creation, the sending of the Messenger to them, and the revelation of the Book. The first and most well-known view is that what is meant by all of them are the believers, and this is the view of most scholars. His saying: And among them are those who are foremost in good deeds, meaning: those who are foremost in Paradise, or in God’s mercy, with good deeds, meaning: with righteous actions, by God’s permission, meaning: God’s command and will, that is the great bounty, meaning: their inheritance of the Book.
35:33: Then he told of their reward, saying: 33- Gardens of Eden which they will enter, meaning: the three categories. Abu Amr read they will enter it with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the ha’, and the others read it with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the kha’, They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing there will be silk.
35:34: 34- And they will say, meaning: and they will say when they enter Paradise: Praise be to God, Who has taken away from us sorrow. Sorrow is the same as miserliness and stinginess. Ibn Abbas said: The sorrow of Hellfire. Qatadah said: The sorrow of death. Muqatil said: They were sad because they did not know what God would do with them. Ikrimah said: The sorrow of sins and bad deeds and the fear of the rejection of good deeds. Al-Qasim said: The sorrow of the loss of blessings and the turning of the heart, and the fear of the consequences. It was also said: The sorrow of the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. Al-Kalbi said: What saddened them in this world about the matter of the Day of Resurrection. Saeed bin Jubair said: They are the bread in this world. It was also said: They are the livelihood. Al-Zajjaj said: God will take away from the people of Paradise all sorrows, whether for livelihood or the afterlife. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Dahhak al-Khatib told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Isfarayni told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ismaili told us, Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Turabi told us, Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no loneliness for the people of ‘There is no god but God’ in their graves or in their place of resurrection. It is as if I see the people of ‘There is no god but God’ shaking the dust off their heads and saying: ‘Praise be to God who has removed sorrow from us.’” God Almighty says: Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.
35:35: 35- He who has settled us has sent us down, in the abode of permanence, meaning: residence, “out of His bounty. No fatigue will touch us therein”, meaning: no hardship or difficulty will befall us therein, nor will we be touched therein by weariness, exhaustion from fatigue.
35:36: God Almighty says: 36- “And those who disbelieve will have the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed for them so that they die,” meaning: they will not perish so that they can find rest, as God Almighty says: So Moses struck him and decreed for him (Ash-Shu’ara’: 15), meaning: he killed him. It was also said: death will not be decreed for them so that they die, as God Almighty says: And they will cry out, ‘O Malik, let your Lord decree for us’ (al-Zukhruf 43:77), meaning: let death be decreed for us so that we can find rest, nor will its punishment be lightened for them, of the punishment of the Fire, Thus do We recompense every ungrateful person, disbeliever. Abu Amr read: yajza with the ya’ and its damma and the fatha on the zay, all nominative without naming the agent. The others read it with the noon and its fatha and the kasra on the zay, all accusative.
35:37: 37- And they cry out, they seek help and shout, in it, which is: they make a derivation from screaming, which is shouting, they say: Our Lord, bring us out, from it, from the fire, that we may do righteousness other than what we used to do, in this world of polytheism and evil deeds, so God says to them in rebuke: Have We not given you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember? It was said that it refers to puberty. Ata’, Qatadah, and Al-Kalbi said: Eighteen years. Al-Hasan said: Forty years. Ibn Abbas said: Sixty years. This was narrated on the authority of Ali, and it is the age at which God the Almighty excuses the son of Adam. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdul Salam bin Mutahhar told us, Umar bin Ali told us, on the authority of Ma’n bin Muhammad Al-Ghafari, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Muqtabari, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God Almighty excuses a man whose lifespan is delayed until he reaches the age of sixty. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Fanjuwayh told us, Ahmad bin Ja’far bin Hamdan told us, Ibrahim bin Sahawayh told us, Al-Hasan bin Arfa told us, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The lifespans of my nation are between sixty and seventy, and few of them exceed that. "And the warner has come to you," meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the opinion of most commentators. It was also said: It means the Qur’an. Ikrimah, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and Waki’ said: It is gray hair. Meaning: Did We not give you life until you became gray hair? It is also said: Gray hair is a harbinger of death. In the hadith: There is no hair that turns white but it says to its sister: Prepare yourself, for death is near. "So taste [the punishment], for there is no helper for the wrongdoers.
35:38: 38- “Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.”
35:39: 39- It is He who has made you successors upon the earth, meaning: you succeed one another. It was also said: He made you a nation that succeeded those before it. And it saw in those before it what it should learn from. So whoever disbelieves - upon him will be his disbelief, meaning: upon him will be the consequences of his disbelief. And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers in the sight of their Lord except hatred, anger. And their disbelief does not increase the disbelievers except in loss.
35:40: 40- “Say: Have you seen your partners whom you invoke besides God?” That is, you have made them My partners, according to your claim, meaning: the idols. Show me what they have created on earth, or do they have a share in the heavens, or have We given them a book? Muqatil said: Did We give the infidels of Mecca a book, so they have clear evidence from it? Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamzah, and Hafs read: clear evidence of monotheism, and the others read: clear evidence from it in the plural, meaning clear proofs from it from what is in that book of various types of explanation. Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion. Deception is what deceives a person for something that has no basis. Muqatil said: Meaning, what Satan promises the unbelievers of the children of Adam regarding the intercession of the gods for them in the afterlife is delusion and falsehood.
35:41: God Almighty says: 41- Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist, meaning: lest they cease to exist. And if they should cease, no one could hold them back after Him, meaning: no one could hold them back after Him, meaning: no one other than Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving. If it is said: What is the meaning of mentioning forbearance here? It is said: Because the heavens and the earth were about to do what they were about to do, which was to punish the disbelievers, so God Almighty held them back from disappearing by His forbearance and forgiveness, lest He hasten the punishment upon them.
35:42: 42- And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths, meaning: When the infidels of Mecca heard that the People of the Book had denied their messengers, they said: “May God curse the Jews and the Christians. Messengers came to them but they denied them. They swore by God and said: If a messenger came to us, we would be more guided in religion than them.” This was before the mission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then, when Muhammad was sent, they denied him. Then God Almighty revealed: And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that if a warner came to them, a messenger, they would be more guided than any of the nations, meaning: the Jews and Christians. But when a warner came to them, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, it only increased them in aversion, meaning: his coming only increased their distancing from guidance.
35:43: 43- Arrogance in the land, arrogance is in the accusative case as a substitute for aversion, and evil plotting, meaning: ugly action, plotting is added to its description, Al-Kalbi said: It is their gathering to polytheism and kill the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and Hamza read: evil plotting with a sukoon on the hamza for ease, and it is the reading of Al-A’mash, and evil plotting does not encompass, meaning: evil plotting does not happen and does not encompass, except its people, so they were killed on the day of Badr, and Ibn Abbas said: The consequences of polytheism do not happen except to those who associate partners with God. The meaning is: the consequences of their plotting will return to them, So do they await, wait, except for the way of the former peoples, except that the punishment will befall them as it befell those who came before from the disbelievers, You will not find any change in the way of God, and you will not find any alteration in the way of God.
35:44: 44- “Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them who were greater than them in power? And nothing in the heavens or on the earth is beyond God’s power. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.”
35:45: 45- And if God were to punish people for what they have earned, of crimes, He would not leave upon its surface, meaning: upon the surface of the earth, a metaphor for something not mentioned, of a living creature, as was the case in the time of Noah. God destroyed everything on the surface of the earth except those who were in Noah’s ship, “but He defers them for a specified term. So when their term comes, then indeed, God is ever, of His servants, Seeing.” Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He means the people who obey Him and the people who disobey Him.
36:1: Makki 1. Ya Seen and Nun were recited with the nun hidden in them: Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr. Qaloon conceals the nun in Ya Seen and pronounces it in Nun, and the rest pronounce it in them. They differed in the interpretation of Ya Seen according to their differences in the letters of the spelling. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It is an oath. It is narrated from him that its meaning is: O human being, in the language of Tayy, meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the saying of Al-Hasan, Saeed bin Jubair, and a group. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Oh man. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: O master of mankind.
36:3: 3. Indeed, you are among the messengers. He swears by the Qur’an that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is among the messengers. This is a response to the infidels who said: You are not a messenger (al-Ra’d 13:43).
36:4: 4. On a straight path, which is a piece of report after a piece of report, meaning: that he is one of the messengers and that he is on a straight path. It was said: It means that you are one of the messengers who are on the straight path.
36:5: 5. A revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read: A revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful, with the lam in the accusative case, as if he said: It was sent down in a revelation. The others read it with the nominative case, meaning: It is a revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
36:6: 6. To warn a people whose fathers were not warned. It was said: What is for negation, meaning: Their fathers were not warned, because no prophet came to the Quraysh before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And it was said: What means who, meaning: To warn a people with that which their fathers were warned, so they are heedless, of faith and guidance.
36:7: 7. The word has come true “the punishment is inevitable” upon most of them, so they do not believe. This is like His saying: But the word of punishment has come true upon the disbelievers (al-Zumar 39:71).
36:8: 8. Indeed, We have placed shackles around their necks. This was revealed about Abu Jahl and his two Makhzumi companions. Abu Jahl had sworn that if he saw Muhammad praying, he would crush his head. So, he came to him while he was praying, holding a stone to crush him. When he raised it, his hand stayed on his neck and the stone stuck to his hand. When he returned to his companions and told them what he had seen, the stone fell. A man from the Makhzum tribe said, I will kill him with this stone. So, he came to him while he was praying to throw the stone at him, but God blinded his sight, so he could hear its voice but not see it. So, he returned to his companions but could not see them until they called him and said, What did you do? He said, "I did not see him. I heard his voice, but something like a stallion moving its tail stood between me and him. If I approached it, it would eat me." So God revealed, Indeed, We have placed shackles around their necks. The scholars of semantics said: This is a metaphor, and there was no rancor. He meant: We prevented them from believing with obstacles, so he made the chains an example of that. Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is that we prevented them from spending in the way of God, as God the Almighty said: And do not make your hand chained to your neck (al-Isra’ 17:29). Its meaning is: Do not withhold it from spending. It reaches the chins. (It) is a metaphor for the hands - even though it is not mentioned - because the shackles join the hand to the neck. Its meaning is: We have put shackles on their hands and necks, so they reach the chins. They are oppressed. And oppression is the one who raises his head and lowers his gaze. It is said: A camel is oppressed if it drinks from the water, so it raises its head and lowers its gaze. Al-Azhari said: He meant that when their hands were shackled to their necks, the shackles raised their chins and heads, so their heads are raised by the shackles being raised.
36:9: 9. And We placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read: (a barrier) with a fat-ha on the seen, and the others read it with a damma on it, so We covered them, so We blinded them, from taghshiyyah, which means covering, so they do not see, the path of guidance.
36:10: 10. And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.
36:11: 11. You can only warn those who follow the message, meaning: Your warning will only benefit those who follow the message, meaning: the Qur’an, and act upon what is in it, and fear the Most Merciful unseen, so give him good tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward, which is good, which is Paradise.
36:12: 12. Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, at the resurrection, and record what they have put forth, of good and evil deeds, and their traces, meaning: what good or bad practices they have established. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam that is followed after him will have a reward for it and a reward like that of those who follow it after him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. And whoever establishes a bad practice in Islam will bear its burden and the burden of those who follow it after him, without that detracting from their burden in the slightest.” Some people said: His statement, And We record what they have put forth and their traces, means their steps to the mosque. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that he said: Banu Salamah complained about how far their homes were from the mosque, so God the Almighty revealed: And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind. Ahmad ibn Abdullah Al-Salihi informed us, Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Isa Al-Sayrafi informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm informed us, Muhammad ibn Hisham ibn Malas Al-Namari informed us, Marwan Al-Fazzari informed us, Hamid informed us, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, who said: “Banu Salamah wanted to move closer to the mosque, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not want Madinah to be laid bare, so he said: O Banu Salamah, will you not take account of your traces?” So they stayed.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Al-Ala told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Abu Musa, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The people who will have the greatest reward for prayer are those who walk the furthest, and the one who waits for the prayer until he prays it with the imam will have a greater reward than the one who prays and then sleeps.” God Almighty says: And all things We have enumerated We have preserved, counted, and explained, in a clear register, which is the Preserved Tablet.
36:13: 13. The Almighty said: And present to them an example of the companions of the city, meaning: Mention to them a similarity like their situation in the story of the companions of the city, which is Antioch, when there came to it the messengers, meaning, the messengers of Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him. The scholars of the stories of the prophets said: Jesus sent two messengers from the disciples to the people of the city of Antioch. When they approached the city, they saw an old man tending his sheep. He was Habib the carpenter, the companion of Jesus. They greeted him and the old man said to them: Who are you? They said: Messengers of Jesus. We call you from the worship of idols to the worship of the Most Gracious. He said: Do you have a sign? They said: Yes, we heal the sick and cure the blind and the leper, by God’s permission. The old man said: I have a son who has been sick for years. They said: Let us go and see his condition. He brought them to his house and they anointed his son, and he rose in time, by God’s permission, in good health. The report spread in the city and God healed many sick people by their hands. They had a king - Wahb said his name was Antiochus - and he was one of the kings of Rome who worshipped idols. They said: The report reached him and he called them and said: Who are you? They said: Messengers of Jesus. He said: Why have you come? They said: We call you from the worship of that which neither hears nor sees to the worship of He who hears and sees. He said: Do you have a god other than our gods? They said: Yes, who created you and your gods? He said: Go away so that I may look into your matter. The people followed them, seized them, and beat them in the marketplace. Wahb said: Jesus sent these two men to Antioch. They came but did not reach its king. Their stay was long. One day the king went out and they glorified God and mentioned Him. The king became angry and ordered them imprisoned and flogged each one of them a hundred lashes. They said: When the two messengers lied and were beaten, Jesus sent Simon Peter, the head of the apostles, after them to support them. Simon entered the city in disguise and began to associate with the king’s entourage until they became accustomed to him. They reported this to the king, who summoned him. The king was pleased with their association, became accustomed to him and treated him with respect. Then one day he said to him: O king, I have heard that you imprisoned two men and flogged them when they called you to a religion other than yours. Have you spoken to them and listened to their words? The king said: Anger came between me and that. He said: If the king sees fit, he will summon them so that we may find out what they have to say. So the king summoned them. Simon said to them: Who sent you here? They said: God is He who created everything and has no partner. Simeon said to them: [Describe him and be brief. They said: He does what He wills and rules what He wants. Simeon said:] What is your sign? They said: Whatever you wish for. So the king ordered until they brought a boy with blind eyes and the place of his eyes was like a forehead. They did not cease to call upon their Lord until the place of his sight split. Then they took two clay nuts and placed them in his pupils and they became eyeballs with which he could see. The king was amazed. Simeon said to the king: If you ask your god to do something like this, then honor will be for you and for your god. The king said: I have no secret from you. Our god whom we worship neither hears nor sees, nor harms nor benefits. Whenever Simeon entered the king’s presence upon the idol, he would enter as he did and pray a lot, supplicating until they thought he was of their faith. The king said to the two messengers: If the god whom you worship is able to revive a dead person, we will believe in him and in you. They said: Our god is capable of everything. The king said: There is a dead person here who died seven days ago, the son of a peasant, and I delayed him and did not bury him until his father returned, and he was absent. So they brought the dead person, changed and smelling good, and they began to call upon their Lord openly, while Simeon began to call upon his Lord secretly. The dead person stood up and said: I came seven days ago as a polytheist and was thrown into seven valleys of Hell. I warn you of the stench in me, so believe in God. Then he said: The gates of heaven were opened for me, and I looked and saw a young man with a handsome face interceding for these three. The king said: Who are the three? He said: Simon and these two, and he pointed to his two companions. The king was amazed. When Simon realized that his words had affected the king, he told him about the situation and called him. The king believed, and some people believed, while others disbelieved. It was said that the king's daughter had died and been buried, so Simeon said to the king: Ask these two men to revive your daughter. The king asked them to do that, so they got up and prayed and supplicated, and Simeon was with them in secret. Then God revived the woman and the grave split open for her, and she came out and said: Convert to Islam, for they are truthful. She said: I do not think you will convert to Islam. Then she asked the two messengers to return her to her place, so they sprinkled dirt on her head and she returned to her grave as she was. Ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Ka’b and Wahb: Rather, the king disbelieved, and he and his people agreed to kill the messengers. This reached Habib, who was at the gate of the farthest city, so he came running to them, reminding them and calling them to obey the messengers. This is what God Almighty said:
36:14: 14. When We sent to them two, Wahb said: Their names were John and Paul, but they denied them, so We strengthened them, meaning: We strengthened them, with a third, with a third messenger, who was Simon. Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim: (So We strengthened us) with a light pronunciation, and it has the meaning of the first, like your saying: We strengthened and we strengthened, with a light pronunciation and a heavy pronunciation. It was said: We defeated them, from their saying: whoever is strengthened, he is stronger. Kaab said: The two messengers were Sadiq and Saduq, and the third was Shalom. God attributed the mission to him because Jesus, peace be upon him, sent them by His command, and they said all of them to the people of Antioch, Indeed, we are messengers to you.
36:15: 15. "They said, 'You are only human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not sent down anything. You are only lying.'" You are nothing but liars in what you claim.
36:16: 16. They said, 'Our Lord knows that we have been messengers to you.'
36:17: 17. And our duty is only to convey the clear message.
36:18: 18. They said, ‘Indeed, we consider you an ill omen,’ meaning, we had a bad omen because the rain had been withheld from them. They said, “This has befallen us because of your bad luck. ‘If you do not desist, we will surely stone you,’” meaning, we will kill you. Qatada said, “with stones. And a painful punishment from Us will surely touch you.”
36:19: 19. "They said, 'Your bad omen is with you,' meaning: your bad omen is with you because of your disbelief and denial, meaning: bad luck befell you before you. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: Your portion of good and evil, 'If you remember,' meaning: and glorify God. This is a question with an omitted answer, meaning: If you remember and admonish God, you will take us as bad omens. Abu Ja`far read: (that) with a fat-ha on the softened hamza, (you have remembered) with a lightened hamza, Rather, you are a transgressing people, polytheists who have transgressed the limits.
36:20: 20. The Almighty said: And there came from the farthest part of the city a man, running. He was Jubayb the carpenter. Al-Suddi said: He was a launderer. Wahb said: He was a silk worker, and he was ill and leprosy had spread rapidly to him. His house was at the farthest gate of the city. He was a believer who gave charity. He would gather his earnings in the evening and divide them in half, feeding half to his family and giving the other half in charity. When he heard that his people intended to kill the messengers, he came to them, “He said: O my people, follow the messengers.”
36:21: 21. Follow those who do not ask of you a reward, and they are [rightly] guided. Qatada said: Habib was in a cave worshipping his Lord. When he heard the report of the messengers, he came to them and declared his religion. When Habib reached the messengers, he said to them: Do you ask for a reward for this? They said: No. So he turned to his people and said: “O my people, follow the messengers. Follow those who do not ask of you a reward, and they are [rightly] guided.” When he said that, they said to him: And you are opposing our religion and following the religion of these messengers and believing in their God? He said:
36:22: 22. And why should I not worship He who created me and to whom you will be returned? Hamza and Yaqub read: (Mali) with a sukoon on the ya’, and the others with a fatha on it. It was said that he attributed the innate disposition to himself and the return to them, because the innate disposition is the effect of a blessing, and it was more evident to him, and in the return there is a meaning of deterrence and it was more appropriate for them. It was said that when he said: Follow the messengers, they took him and brought him to the king. The king said to him: Are you going to follow them? He said: (Why should I not worship He who created me), and what do I have if I do not worship the Creator? And to Him you will be returned You will be returned at the resurrection and He will reward you for your deeds.
36:23: 23. Shall I take other gods besides Him? This is a question that means denial, meaning: I will not take other gods besides Him. If the Most Gracious intends me harm, meaning evil and misfortune, their intercession will not avail me at all, will not ward off anything from me. Nor will they save from that misfortune. It was said: They will not save from the punishment if God punishes me if I do that.
36:24: 24. Then I would be in clear error, a clear error.
36:25: 25. I have believed in your Lord, so listen, meaning: Listen to me. When he said that, the people jumped on him as one man and killed him. Ibn Masoud said: They trampled on him with their feet until his ribs came out of his anus. Al-Saddī said: They were throwing stones at him while he was saying: O God, guide my people, until they cut him up and killed him. Al-Hasan said: They made a hole in his throat and hung him from one of the city walls. His grave is in Antioch, and God brought him into Paradise, and he is alive and well there.
36:26: 26. This is what God Almighty said: It was said, ‘Enter Paradise.’ So when he reached Paradise, He said, ‘If only my people knew.’
36:27: 27. Because my Lord has forgiven me, meaning: because my Lord has forgiven me, and made me among the honored, he wished that his people would know that God had forgiven him and honored him, so that they would desire the religion of the Messengers. When Habib was killed, God became angry with him and hastened their punishment. He ordered Gabriel, peace be upon him, to shout at them once, and they all died.
36:28: 28. This is what God Almighty said: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, meaning: the angels, nor were We sending them down, and we were not doing this, rather the matter of destroying them was easier than they thought. It was said: Its meaning is (And We did not send down upon his people after him) meaning: upon the people of Habib al-Najjar after he was killed, from an army, and We would not send them down upon the nations if We destroyed them, such as the flood, thunderbolt, and wind.
36:29: 29. Then He explained their punishment, saying, It will be only a single blast, (Abu Ja`far read: a single blast), in the nominative case, making being mean occurring. The commentators said: Gabriel took hold of the doorposts of the city, then shouted at them once, and behold, they were dead.
36:30: 30. Oh, what a pity for the servants, Ikrimah said: meaning, oh, what a pity for themselves. Pity is intense remorse, and there are two opinions on this: One of them: God Almighty says, Oh, what regret, remorse, and sadness for the servants on the Day of Resurrection when they did not believe in the saffron. The other: It is from the words of the lost. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: When they witnessed the punishment, they said: Oh, what regret! Meaning: Remorse for the servants, meaning: for the three messengers, since they did not believe in them, and so they wished for faith when it did not benefit them. Al-Azhari said: Regret is not called upon, and its call is to alert the addressee. It was said: The Arabs say: Oh my regret! and Oh wonder! as an exaggeration, and the call to them means to alert, so it is as if he is saying: Oh wonder, is this your time? And Oh regret, is this your time? The true meaning: This is a time of regret and amazement. Then He explained the reason for the regret and remorse, saying: There came not to them a messenger but they used to ridicule him.
36:31: 31. Have they not seen, have they not been informed, meaning: the people of Mecca, how many generations before them We destroyed, and a generation is the people of every era, they were called that because they are linked in existence, that to them they will not return, meaning: they will not return to the world, so they should not be considered.
36:32: 32. "And indeed every one of them is all", Asim and Hamza read: (when) here and in Az-Zukhruf and At-Tariq, and Ibn Amir agreed with him except in Az-Zukhruf, and Abu Ja`far agreed with him in At-Tariq, and the others read it with a light pronunciation. So whoever stressed it made (in) mean denial, and (when) mean except, meaning: and every one is all, and whoever lightened it made (in) for emphasis and (what) a relative clause, meaning: and every one of them, are present with us.
36:33: 33. “And a sign for them is the dead land. We have given it life” with rain, and brought forth from it grain, meaning wheat, barley, and the like, and from it they eat, meaning grain.
36:34: 34. And We placed therein gardens, orchards, of palm trees and grapevines, and caused springs to gush forth therein, into the earth.
36:35: 35. That they may eat of its fruit, meaning: of the fruit produced by water, and what you have made, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr read: (I have made) without the ha’, and the others read (I have made it) with the ha’, meaning: they eat of what their hands have made, of planting and cultivation, so the ha’ refers back to (what) which means which. It was said: (what) is for negation in His statement (what you have made) meaning: they found it made and their hands did not make it, nor did they have any role in it, and this is the meaning of the statement of Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil. It was said: He meant the springs and rivers that were not made by the hand of creation, such as the Tigris, Euphrates, Nile, and the like. Will they not then be grateful? God's blessing.
36:36: 36. Glory be to Him who created in pairs all things, meaning: the kinds, of what the earth grows, of fruits and grains, and of themselves, meaning: males and females, and of what they do not know, of what He created of things from the land and sea animals.
36:37: 37. And a sign for them, which indicates Our power, is the night We strip, that is, We remove and scrape, from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness, entering into darkness. Its meaning is: We go with the day and bring the night, and that is because the origin is darkness, and the day enters into it, so when the sun sets, the day strips the night, and darkness appears.
36:38: 38. And the sun runs to its resting place, meaning: to its resting place, meaning: to the end of its course when the world ends and the Hour comes. It was said: It travels until it reaches the farthest point of the west, then it returns, and that is its destination because it does not go beyond it. It was said: Its final destination is the end of its ascent in the sky in the summer, and the end of its descent in the winter. It was authentically reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Its final destination is under the Throne. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Wakee told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the words of God Almighty: ‘And the sun runs to its resting place,’ he said: Its resting place is under the Throne.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Wakee’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Dharr when the sun set: Do you know where it goes? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It goes until it prostrates beneath the Throne, then it asks permission and permission is given to it. It is about to prostrate but it is not accepted from it, and it asks permission but it is not given permission. It is told: Go back from whence you came, then it rises from its place of setting. This is what God, the Most High, said: ‘And the sun runs to its resting place. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.’” Amr bin Dinar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the sun runs, with no resting place for it. This is the reading of Ibn Masoud, meaning: it has no resting place or stopping, so it runs forever. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
36:39: 39. And the moon - We have determined for it phases. That is, We have determined for it phases. Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, and the people of Basra read the moon with the ra’ raised, because of His statement, And a sign for them is the night from which We strip the day. The others read it with the nasb, because of His statement, We have determined for it, that is, We have determined for the moon, phases. We have already mentioned the names of the phases in Surat Yunus. So when the moon reaches the last phase, it becomes thin, and that is what His statement means, until it returns like an old cluster of date stalks. The cluster of date stalks is the stalk of the clusters on which the branches are placed. So when it becomes old and mature, it dries up, curves, and turns yellow. So the moon is likened to it in its thinness and yellowness at the last phase.
36:40: 40. Nor shall the sun overtake the moon, meaning: the day shall not enter upon the night before its end, nor shall the night enter upon the day before its end. This is the saying of God Almighty: Nor shall the night outstrip the day, meaning: they follow one another according to a known calculation, neither of them coming before its time. It was said: Neither of them is subject to the authority of the other. The sun does not rise at night, nor does the moon rise during the day, and it has light. So when they meet and each one of them overtakes the other, the Day of Resurrection will come. It was said: The sun cannot overtake the moon, meaning: it cannot meet with it in one orbit, nor can the night outstrip the day, meaning: one night cannot be connected to the other without there being a day separating them. And each in an orbit is swimming, they run.
36:41: 41. And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring, the people of Medina, Ash-Sham, and Jacob read: (their offspring) in the plural, and the others read: (their offspring) in the singular, so whoever pluralized it broke the ta’, and whoever did not pluralized it put it in the accusative, and what is meant by offspring are the fathers and grandfathers, and the name offspring applies to fathers as it applies to children, in the laden ark, meaning: filled, and he meant the ship of Noah, peace be upon him, and these are from the offspring of those who were carried with Noah, and they were in their loins.
36:42: 42. And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride. It was said that he meant by this the small ships that were built after Noah’s ship in its form. It was said: He meant by it the ships that sail in rivers, so they are in rivers like large ships in the seas, and this is the saying of Qatada, Al-Dahhak and others. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: (And We created for them from the like thereof that on which they ride), meaning: camels, so camels on land are like ships on the sea.
36:43: And if We will, We can drown them, but no one will help them, nor will they be saved, meaning: no one will rescue them, nor will they be saved, from drowning. Ibn Abbas said: No one can save them from my punishment.
36:44: 44. Except for mercy from Us and enjoyment for a time, until their appointed times come to an end, meaning: except that He has mercy on them and provides them with enjoyment until their appointed times.
36:45: 45. And when it is said to them, ‘Fear what is before you and what is behind you,’ Ibn Abbas said: What is before you means the Hereafter, so work for it, and what is behind you means this world, so beware of it and do not be deceived by it. It was said: What is before you is the events of God with the nations who came before you, and what is behind you is the torment of the Hereafter, and this is the saying of Qatada and Muqatil. Perhaps you will receive mercy. The answer is omitted, meaning: If this is said to them, they will turn away from it. The evidence for this is what follows:
36:46: 46. And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord, meaning: evidence of the truthfulness of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they turn away from it.
36:47: 47. “And when it is said to them, ‘Spend from what God has provided you,’ ‘God has given you,’ those who disbelieve say to those who believe, ‘Shall we feed,’ ‘Shall we provide for someone whom God could feed if He willed?’” That is because the believers said to the disbelievers of Mecca, “Spend on the poor from what you claim of your wealth is for God,’ which is what they set aside for God from their crops and livestock. They said, “Shall we feed, shall we provide for someone whom God could provide if He willed, but then did not provide for him despite His ability to do so?” So we comply with the will of God and do not feed someone whom God did not feed. This is one of the things that the misers cling to, saying, We do not give to someone whom God has deprived. What they claim is false, because God has enriched some of His creation and made others poor as a test. He has prevented the world from the poor, not out of miserliness, and He has commanded the rich to spend, not out of need for his money, but to test the rich with the poor in what He has prescribed for him from the rich man’s money. No one can object to God’s will and His judgment of His creation. You are in clear error. The disbelievers say to the believers: You are in clear error in following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and abandoning what we are upon.
36:48: 48. And they say, ‘When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?’ That is, the Resurrection and the Resurrection, if you should be truthful.
36:49: 49. God Almighty said: They are not waiting for anything but a single blast, meaning: they are not waiting for anything, but a single blast, Ibn Abbas said: He means the first blast, that will seize them while they are disputing, meaning: they are disputing over worldly matters such as buying and selling, and speaking in the marketplace. Hamzah read it: (يْنْشمفونن) with a sukoon on the kha and a soft sad, meaning: they overcome each other in argument. The others read it with a shaddah on the sad, meaning: they argue. The ta’ was assimilated into the sad, then Ibn Kathir, Ya’qub, and Warsh open the kha’ by transferring the vowel of the assimilated ta’ to it. Abu Ja’far and Qaloon make it jazm. Abu Amr intends to open the kha’, and the rest read it with a kasra on the kha’. We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will come when two men have spread out their garments, but they will neither trade nor fold them. The Hour will come when a man has raised his food to his mouth, but he will not eat it.”
36:50: 50. The Almighty said: They are not able to make a will, meaning: they are not able to make a will. Muqatil said: They hastened to make a will and died, nor will they return to their families, meaning they will not be returned, and the meaning is that the Hour will not give them respite for anything.
36:51: 51. And the Trumpet will be blown, which is the last blast, the blast of resurrection, and between the two blasts there will be forty years, and at once they will be from the graves, meaning: the graves, the singular of which is: jadath, to their Lord they will hasten, they will emerge from the graves alive, and from this the child is called nasl because he emerges from his mother’s womb.
36:52: 52. They will say, ‘Woe to us! Who has raised us from our beds?’ Abi bin Ka’b, Ibn Abbas, and Qatada said: They only say this because God Almighty lifts the punishment from them between the two blasts, so they sleep. Then, when they are raised after the final blast and witness the Resurrection, they will cry out in woe. The scholars of semantics said: When the disbelievers see Hell and its various types of torment, the torment of the grave will be like sleep in its side. They will say: Woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleep? Then they will say: This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth. [They acknowledged it when acknowledgment did not benefit them.] It was said: The angels said to them: This is what the Most Gracious promised, and the messengers spoke the truth. Mujahed said: The infidels will say: Who has raised us from our beds? The believers will say: This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth.
36:53: 53. It will be but a single blast, meaning the last blast, and then they will all be brought before Us.
36:54: 54. "So today no soul will be wronged at all, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
36:55: 55. Indeed, the companions of Paradise will be busy that Day. Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, and Abu Amr read in busyness with a sukoon on the ghain, while the rest read it with a damma. They are two dialects, like saht and saht. They differed on the meaning of occupation. Ibn Abbas said: In defloration of virgins. Waki’ bin Al-Jarrah said: In listening. Al-Kalbi said: They are busy with the people of Hell and with what they are in, they do not care about them and do not remember them. Al-Hasan said: They were busy with the bliss in Paradise, rather than the torment in Hell. Ibn Kaysan said: Visiting each other. It was also said: As guests of God Almighty. Fakihun, Abu Jaafar read: (Fakihun) wherever it was, and Hafs agreed with him in Al-Mutaffifin, and they are two dialects like Al-Hadhir and Al-Hadhar, meaning: comfortable. Mujahid and Al-Dahhak said: Admiring what they are in. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Happy.
36:56: 56. They and their spouses, meaning their wives, are in the shade. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it as shade with a damma on the dhal without an alif, the plural of shadow. The common people read it as in the shade with an alif and a kasra on the dhal, the plural of shadow. “On couches,” meaning the beds in the chambers, the singular of which is arīqah. Tha’lab said: There is no couch unless there is a chamber on it. Reclining, meaning those who recline.
36:57: 57. Therein they will have fruits and whatever they request, they wish and desire.
36:58: 58. “Peace be upon you, a word from a Merciful Lord,” meaning: God greets them with a word, meaning: God says a word to them. Abu Saeed Ahmad ibn Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abd Al-Khaliq ibn Ali ibn Abd Al-Khaliq Al-Mu’adhdhin told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa Al-Malhami Al-Isfahani told us, Al-Hasan ibn Abi Ali Al-Za’farani told us, Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, Abu Asim Al-Abadani told us, Al-Fadl Al-Raqashi told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “While the people of Paradise are enjoying their bliss, a light shines for them, so they raise their heads and behold, the Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, has looked down upon them from above and said: ‘Peace be upon you, O people of Paradise.’ That is His saying: ‘Peace, a word from a Merciful Lord.’ He looks at them and they look at Him, but they do not turn to any of the bliss as long as they are looking at Him until He is hidden from them and His light and blessings remain upon them in their homes.” It was said: The angels greeted them from their Lord. Muqatil said: The angels enter upon the people of Paradise from every gate, saying: Peace be upon you, O people of Paradise, from your Lord, the Most Merciful. It was said: He gives them safety, he says: Surrender eternal safety.
36:59: 59. And separate yourselves today, you criminals, Muqatil said: Stop yourselves today from the righteous. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: See the difference. Al-Suddi said: Be separate. Al-Zajjaj said: Separate yourself from the believers. Al-Dahhak said: “For every unbeliever in Hellfire there is a house. He enters that house and fills its door with fire, and he will be there forever and ever, neither seeing nor being seen.”
36:60: 60. Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, did I not command you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan, that is, do not obey Satan in disobeying God, for indeed, he is to you a clear enemy, apparent enmity.
36:61: 61. And worship Me, obey Me and believe in Me alone, this is a straight path.
36:62: 62. And indeed, He has led astray from among you a great many, the people of Medina and Asim read: (a mountain) with a kasra on the jim and ba’ and a shaddah on the lam. Ya’qub read: (a mountain) with a damma on the jim and ba’ and a shaddah on the lam. Ibn ‘Amir and Abu ‘Amr read it with a damma on the jim and a sukoon on the ba’, light. The others read it with a damma on the jim and a light ba’. All of these are dialects, and their meaning is: creation and group, i.e. a great many, Did you not understand, what came to you of the destruction of the past nations through obeying Satan, and it is said to them when they come close to the fire:
36:63: 63. This is the Hell which you were promised, in this world,
36:64: 64. Enter it, enter it, this day because you used to disbelieve.
36:65: 65. This Day We will seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify about what they used to earn. This is when the disbelievers deny their disbelief and denial of the Messengers, so their mouths will be sealed and their limbs will testify against them. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Amr bin Hafsawayh Al-Sarakhsi told us, in the year 335 AH, Abu Yazid Hatim bin Mahbub told us, Abdul Jabbar bin Al-Ala told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? He said: Do you have any difficulty in seeing the sun at noon when it is not cloudy? They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: Do you have any difficulty in seeing the moon when it is full when it is not cloudy? They said: No. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will not have any difficulty in seeing your Lord, just as you do not have any difficulty in seeing either of them. He said: Then the servant will meet Him and say: O My servant, did I not honor you? Did I not make you a black man? Did I not marry you? Did I not subject the horses and camels to you and let you rule and sit on your throne? He said: Yes, O my Lord. He said: Did you think that you would meet Me? He said: No. He said: Today I will forget you as you forgot Me. He said: Then he will meet the second one and say: Did I not honor you, did I not make you a black man, did I not marry you, did I not make horses and camels subservient to you and let you rule and sit on the throne? - Another one said on the authority of Sufyan: He ruled and sat on the throne in both places - he said: Then he will say: Yes, O Lord. Then he will say: Did I not think that you would meet Me? Then he will say: No, O Lord. He will say: Today I will forget you as you forgot me. Then he will meet the third one and say: Who are you? Then he will say: I am Your servant. I believed in You, in Your Prophet, and in Your Book. I prayed, fasted, gave charity, and praised You as much as I could. Then it will be said to him: Did We not send against you a witness? Then he will think to himself about who will testify against me. Then his mouth will be sealed and his thigh will be told: Speak. Then his thigh, flesh, and bones will speak about what he used to do. That is the hypocrite. That is so that he can excuse himself, and that is the one with whom God is angry. Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abu Sahl Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzaz told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Dabry told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Bahz bin Hakim bin Muawiyah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “You will be called and something will be brought to your mouths, and the first thing that will be asked about any one of you will be his thigh and his hand.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Nadr told us, Hashim bin Al-Qasim told me, Abdullah Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Ubaid Al-Maktab, on the authority of Fadil, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he laughed. He said: ‘Do you know why I laugh?’ We said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘Because of a servant addressing his Lord, saying: ‘O Lord, did you not protect me from injustice?’ He said: ‘Then He says: ‘I will not protect myself except as a witness from myself.’ He said: ‘Then He says: ‘Sufficient for yourself today as a witness against you, and the noble scribes are witnesses.’ He said: ‘Then his mouth is sealed and it is said to his limbs: ‘Speak.’ He said: ‘And they speak of his deeds.’ He said: ‘Then he is left alone to speak. Far be it from you and away from you! I used to struggle.’”
36:66: 66. The Almighty’s statement: And if We willed, We could have blinded their eyes, [i.e., We could have taken away their] visible eyes so that no eyelid or slit would be visible. This is the meaning of blind, as the Almighty said: And if God had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. (al-Baqarah 2:20) He says: Just as We blinded their hearts, if We willed, We could have blinded their visible sight. So they raced to the path, so they hastened to the road. How can they see? How can they see when We have blinded their eyes? Meaning: If We willed, We could have led them astray from guidance and left them blind, wandering about. How can they see] the paths then? This is what Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said. Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Muqatil, and Ata’ said: Its meaning is, if We willed, We could have gouged out the eyes of their misguidance, blinded them to their error, and turned their sight from misguidance to guidance, so they would have seen their right path. How can they see? Why did I not do that to them?
36:67: 67. And if We willed, We could have transformed them in their places, meaning: their place. He means: If We willed, We could have made them apes and pigs in their homes. It was also said: If We willed, We could have made them stones, sitting in their homes, with no souls. So they were unable to go on nor to return, to what they were in. It was also said: They were unable to go or return.
36:68: 68. And whomsoever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation. Asim and Hamza read: We reverse him with emphasis, and the others read it with a fatha on the first noon and a damma on the kaf, lightened, meaning: We return him to the worst of life, like a boy at the beginning of creation. It was said: (We reverse him in creation) meaning: We weaken his limbs after they were strong and return them to their deficiency after they were increased. Do they not then reason? So they will consider and know that the One who has the power to direct the affairs of man is also able to resurrect him after death.
36:69: 69. The Almighty said: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. Al-Kalbi said: The infidels of Mecca said: Muhammad is a poet, and what he says is poetry. So God revealed, to refute them: And We have not taught him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. That is, it was not easy for him, and no verse of poetry was balanced for him, until when he recited a verse of poetry, it flowed from his tongue in a broken manner. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Thaqafi told me, Ahmad bin Ja’far bin Hamdan told us, Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Mahan told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite this verse: Islam and gray hair are enough to deter a person Abu Bakr said, O Messenger of God, the poet said: Gray hair and Islam are enough to prevent a person The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Islam and gray hair are sufficient as a deterrent for a man. Abu Bakr and Umar said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. God Almighty says: And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul Rahman bin Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Ja’d told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Miqdam bin Shuraih, on the authority of my father, who said: I said to Aisha: Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite any poetry? She said: He used to recite poetry from the poetry of Abdullah bin Rawahah. She said: And perhaps he said: And he brings you report from someone you did not provide. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada: It reached me that Aisha was asked: Did the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite any poetry? She said: Poetry was the most hated speech to him. She said: He did not recite any poetry except the verse of the brother of Banu Qais, Tarafa: Days will show you what you were ignorant of, and report will come to you from someone you did not know.
