Al-Kalbi said: They will be struck with whips until they throw themselves into the Fire, out of fear of those whips. The leaders will say: No welcome to them, meaning the followers, They have entered the Fire, meaning: They will enter it as we have entered it.
38:60: 60. They said, so the followers said to the leaders: Rather, you are not welcome, and welcome and spaciousness means spaciousness. The Arabs say: Welcome and welcome, meaning: you have come with spaciousness and ease, and they say: No welcome to you, meaning: the earth is not welcoming to you. You brought it upon us, so the followers say to the leaders: You started with disbelief before us, and you legislated and imposed it upon us. And it was said: You brought this punishment upon us, by calling us to disbelief, so evil is the settlement, meaning: so evil is the abode of settlement, Hell.
38:61: 61. They said, meaning the followers, Our Lord, who presented this to us? meaning, legislated it and prescribed it for us, then increase for him a double punishment in the Fire. Meaning, double the punishment for him in the Fire. Ibn Masoud said: He meant snakes and vipers.
38:62: 62. And they said, meaning the leaders of Quraysh who were in Hell, Why do we not see men whom we used to count, in this world, among the wicked, meaning the poor believers: Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal, and Salman, may God be pleased with them. Then they mentioned that they used to mock these people,
38:63: 63. They said: We took them in mockery. The people of Basra, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read: (From the evil ones We took them), connecting and breaking the alifs at the beginning, and the others read them by cutting the alifs and opening them for questioning. English: The scholars of semantics said: The first reading is better, because they knew that they had taken them in mockery, so the question is not correct. In this reading, (Umm) has the meaning of (Rather), and whoever opens the alif said: It is according to the wording, not according to the meaning, to be equivalent to (Umm) in His statement, Or have the eyes turned away from them? Al-Farra’ said: This is from the question whose meaning is rebuke and astonishment. (Umm zaaghat) means: the eyes turned away from them. The metaphor of the verse is: Why do we not see that these whom we took in mockery did not enter the Fire with us? Or did they enter it, so Our eyes turned away from them, so We did not see them when they entered it? It was said: They are in Hell, but they are hidden from our sight? Ibn Kaysan said: Or were they better than us, but we do not know, so our sight was lost on them in this world, so we did not consider them anything?
38:64: 64. That, which I mentioned, is true, then he explained and said: The people of Hell will quarrel, meaning: the people of Hell will quarrel in Hell, which is true.
38:65: 65. “Say,” O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Mecca, I am only a warner, a frightener, and there is no god but God, the One, the Prevailing.
38:66: 66. Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.
38:67: 67. Say, O Muhammad, it is, meaning the Qur’an, a great report, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada said. It was also said that it means the Resurrection, as in His statement: About what are they asking one another? * About the great report An-Naba’ 1:2.
38:68: 68. You are turning away from it.
38:69: 69. I had no knowledge of the highest assembly, meaning: the angels, when they disputed, meaning: about Adam, peace be upon him, when God Almighty said: “Indeed, I will place upon the earth a successive authority. They said, ‘Will You place upon it one who will cause corruption therein?’” (al-Baqarah 2:30).
38:70: 70. It has not been revealed to me except that I am a clear warner. Al-Farra’ said: If you wish, you can put anma in the nominative case, meaning: What has been revealed to me is only a warning. If you wish, you can make the meaning: What has been revealed to me is that I am a clear warner. Abu Jaafar read: Innama with a kasra on the alif, because revelation is a statement. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Sadaqah bin Khalid told us, Abdul Rahman bin Yazid bin Jabir told us, he said: Khalid bin Al-Lajlaj passed by us, and Makhul called him and said: O Ibrahim, tell us the hadith of Abdul Rahman bin A’ish: He said: I heard Abdul Rahman bin A’ish Al-Hadrami say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, in the most beautiful form, and he said: ‘O Muhammad, about what do the highest assembly dispute?’ I said: ‘O Lord, you know best,’ twice. He said: ‘Then he placed his hand between my shoulders and I felt its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what was in the heaven and the earth.’ He said: Then he recited this verse: ‘And thus did We show Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth that he might be among the certain [in faith]’ (al-An’am 6:75). Then he said: ‘O Muhammad, about what do the highest assembly dispute?’ I said: ‘About expiations?’ He said: ‘And what are they?’ I said: ‘Walking to the congregations and sitting in…’” The mosques are after the prayers, and performing ablution in its proper place even in times of difficulty. He said: Whoever does that will live well and die well, and will be free from his sins as on the day his mother bore him. Among the degrees are feeding the poor, offering peace, and performing the night prayer while people are asleep. He said: Say: O God, I ask You for good things, and to leave evil things, and to love the poor, and to forgive me, and have mercy on me, and accept my repentance, and if You want to bring trial upon a people, then cause me to die before they are tried. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Learn them, for by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, they are the truth.
38:71: 71. The Almighty said: When your Lord said to the angels, ‘Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay,’ meaning: Adam, peace be upon him.
38:72: 72. And when I have proportioned him, I have completed his creation, and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration.
38:73: 73. Then the angels prostrated, all of them together.
38:74: 74. Except Iblis, he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers.
38:75: 75. He said, 'O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? You were arrogant.' An interrogative alif that came before the alif of connection. Or were you among the exalted? An arrogant question, a question of rebuke and denial. He says: Did you feel arrogant to the point that you refused to prostrate? Or were you among the people who are arrogant, so you were too arrogant to prostrate because you were among them?
38:76: 76. He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
38:77: 77. "He said, 'Then get out of it,' meaning: from Paradise, and it was said: from the heavens. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: meaning from the creation in which you are. Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said: This is a correct interpretation because Iblis acted arrogantly and took pride in his creation, so God changed his creation, so he became black and ugly after having been beautiful, "for indeed, you are expelled, banished.
38:78: 78. And upon you is my curse until the Day of Judgment.
38:79: 79. He said, My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.
38:80: 80. He said, 'Then you are among those given respite.'
38:81: 81. Until the appointed time, which is the first blast.
38:82: 82. He said, By Your might, I will surely mislead them all.
38:83: 83. Except for Your chosen servants among them.
38:84: 84. He said, 'Then the truth, and the truth I say.' Asim, Hamza, and Ya'qub read: The truth, raising the qaf as the subject, and its predicate is omitted, meaning: the truth is from me, and the second is in the accusative case, meaning: and I say the truth. This was said by Mujahid. The others read them both in the accusative case, and they differed as to their interpretation. It was said: The first is in the accusative case to encourage, as if he said: adhere to the truth, and the second is to impose the statement upon it, meaning: I say the truth. It was also said: the first is an oath, meaning, 'By the truth, which is God, the Almighty,' so it was in the accusative case by removing the preposition, which is the letter of description, and the second is in the accusative case by imposing the statement upon it. It was also said: the second is a repetition of the oath, God swore by Himself.
38:85: 85. I will fill Hell with you and those who follow you, all together.
38:86: 86. “Say: I do not ask you for it,” for conveying the message, of reward, making, and I am not of those who fabricate, making up the Qur’an on my own, and everyone who says something on his own is fabricating it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: We entered upon Abdullah bin Masoud, and he said: O people, whoever knows something should say it, and whoever does not know should say: God knows best, for it is part of knowledge to say about what one does not know: God knows best. God Almighty said to His Prophet: “Say: I do not ask of you for it any reward, nor am I of the pretenders.”
38:87: 87. His saying, It is, what it is, meaning the Qur’an, only a reminder, an admonition, for the worlds, for all of creation.
38:88: 88. And you will surely know, you infidels of Mecca, his report, the report of his truthfulness, after a while, Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: after death. Ikrimah said: meaning the Day of Resurrection. Al-Kalbi said: whoever remains will know that when his matter becomes apparent and prominent, and whoever dies will know it after his death. Al-Hasan said: Son of Adam, at death the certain report will come to you.
39:1: Meccan, except for the verse: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves,’ 1. The revelation of the Book is from God, [i.e., this is the revelation of the Book from God. It was also said: The revelation of the Book] is the subject and its predicate is: from God, the Almighty, the Wise, i.e., the revelation of the Book is from God and not from anyone else.
39:2: 2. Indeed, We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, Muqatil said: We did not send it down in falsehood for no reason, so worship God, devoting your religion to Him sincerely, obedience.
39:3: 3. Surely, the pure religion is for God, Qatada said: The testimony that there is no god but God. It was also said: [No one deserves the pure religion except God. It was also said: The religion that is pure and free from polytheism is for God.] And those who have taken for themselves protectors besides Him, meaning idols, we do not worship them, meaning they said: we do not worship them, “except that they may bring us nearer to God,” and this is how Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas read it. Qatada said: “That is because when it is said to them: ‘Who is your Lord, and who created you, and who created the heavens and the earth?’ they say: ‘God.’ It is said to them: ‘What is the meaning of your worship of idols?’ They say: ‘To bring us closer to God,’ meaning: ‘Nearness,’ and it is a noun that is used in the place of a source, as if he said: ‘Except that they bring us closer to God and intercede for us with God. Indeed, God will judge between them’ on the Day of Resurrection ‘in that over which they differ,’ in the matter of religion. ‘Indeed, God does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever.’ He does not guide to His religion one who lies, so he said: ‘The gods intercede.’ And taking gods besides Him is sufficient as a lie [and disbelief].
39:4: 4. If God had willed to take a son, He would have chosen, “from what He creates whatever He wills,” meaning: the angels, as He said: If We had wanted to take a diversion, We would have taken it from Ourself (Al-Anbiya’: 17), then He exonerated Himself and said: Glory be to Him, exonerating Him from that, and from what is not befitting of His purity, He is God, the One, the Prevailing.
39:5: 5. “He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night.” Qatada said: This overwhelms the other, just as He said: He causes the night to overwhelm the day (al-A’raf 7:54). It was also said: One enters over the other, just as He said: He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night (al-Hajj 22:61). Al-Hasan and Al-Kalbi said: The night decreases and the day increases, and the day decreases and the night increases. So whatever is decreased from the night enters the day, and whatever is decreased from the day enters the night. The maximum decrease is nine hours, and the maximum increase is fifteen hours. The origin of the word takwir is wrapping and gathering, and from it: the word takwir is used. “And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving.”
39:6: 6. He created you from one soul, meaning Adam, then He created from it its mate, meaning Eve, and sent down for you from the livestock, the meaning of sending down here is: creating and establishing, like the Almighty’s saying: We sent down upon you clothing to conceal your private parts (al-A’raf 7:26). It was said: He sent down the water that is the cause of the cotton plant from which clothing is made, and the cause of the plant that sustains livestock. It was said: And He has sent down for you from the livestock He made them a resting place and provision for you. Eight pairs, types, their interpretation is in Surat Al-An’am He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, a sperm-drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, as God Almighty said: And He has created you in stages (Nuh: 14), in three layers of darkness, Ibn Abbas said: the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta, That is God, who created these things, “Your Lord has dominion. There is no god except Him, so how are you turned away?”, from the path of truth after this explanation.
39:7: 7. If you disbelieve, then indeed, God is free from need of you, and He does not approve of disbelief for His servants. Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi said: He does not approve of disbelief for His believing servants, and they are the ones about whom God the Most High said: Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority (al-Hijr 15:42). So it is general in wording but specific in meaning, like His the Most High’s saying: A spring from which the servants of God will drink (al-Insan 76:6). He means some of the servants, and some people made it general and said: He does not approve of disbelief for any of His servants. The meaning of the verse: He is not pleased for His servants to disbelieve in Him. This was narrated on the authority of Qatada, and it is the opinion of the early Muslims. They said: The disbelief of the disbeliever is not pleasing to God, the Almighty, even if it is by His will. And if you are grateful, that is, believe in your Lord and obey Him, He will be pleased with you, and will reward you for it. Abu Amr read it as He will be pleased with you with a silent ha’, and the people of Medina, Asim, and Hamzah pronounce it with a sukoon, while the rest pronounce it with a sukoon. “And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.”
39:8: 8. And when harm befalls man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him returning to Him, seeking His aid, then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself gives him a favor from Himself, he forgets abandons that which he used to call upon Him for before meaning: he forgets the harm that he used to call upon God to relieve, and he sets up rivals to God meaning: idols, to mislead [him] from His way meaning to deviate from the religion of God. Say, to this disbeliever: Enjoy your disbelief for a little while, in this world until your appointed time. Indeed, you are among the companions of the Fire. It was said that it was revealed regarding Utbah ibn Rabi’ah. Muqatil said that it was revealed regarding Abu Hudhayfah ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi. It was also said that it is general for every disbeliever.
39:9: 9. Amman huwa qanitan Ibn Kathir, Nafi’ and Hamza read: (Aman) with a light m, while the others read it with a shaddah. Whoever reads it with a shaddah has two options: One of them: that the meem in (am) is a connective, so the meaning of the statement is a question and its answer is omitted, its metaphor is: Is one who is obedient like one who is not obedient? Like his saying: Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam? (al-Zumar 39:22), meaning like one whose breast He has not expanded. The other aspect: It is in apposition to the question, and its metaphor is: He who makes rivals to God is better than he who is obedient? And whoever reads it with a light pronunciation, then it is an interrogative alif that came before who, meaning: Is this like he who makes rivals to God? It was said: The alif in (Aman) has the meaning of a letter of address, meaning: O you who are devout, and the Arabs address with the alif as they address with the ya, so they say: My son so-and-so and O sons of so-and-so, so the meaning of the verse is: Say, enjoy your disbelief for a little while, for you are among the companions of the Fire, O you who are devout at all hours of the night, for you are among the people of Paradise, said Ibn Abbas. In Ata’s narration: It was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq. Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them. On the authority of Ibn Omar, it was revealed about Uthman. On the authority of Al-Kalbi, it was revealed about Ibn Masoud, Ammar, and Salman. Al-Qanit: the one who persists in obedience. Ibn Umar said: Qunut is the recitation of the Qur’an and prolonged standing, and during the hours of al-Layl 92:its hours, prostrating and standing means: in prayer, beware of the Hereafter means: fearing the Hereafter, and hoping for the mercy of his Lord means: like someone who does not do any of that, “Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?” It was said: Those who know means: Ammar, and those who do not know means: Abu Hudhayfah Al-Makhzumi, Only those with understanding will remember.
39:10: 10. Say, ‘O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord,’ by obeying Him and avoiding disobeying Him. For those who do good in this world, meaning: believed and did good deeds, is good, meaning: Paradise, said Muqatil. Al-Suddi said: In this world is good, meaning: health and well-being. And the earth of God is spacious, Ibn Abbas said: meaning: depart from Mecca. This urging includes emigrating from a country where sins are prevalent. It was said: It was revealed about the immigrants to Abyssinia. Saeed bin Jubair said: “Whoever is ordered to commit sins should flee. “Only those who are patient will be given their reward without account,” those who were patient in their religion and did not abandon it to harm. It was said: It was revealed about Jaafar bin Abi Talib and his companions, as they did not abandon their religion when the affliction became severe upon them, but they were patient and emigrated. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Every obedient person will be measured and weighed, except for the patient, for they will be given heaps of it. It is narrated: Those who are afflicted will be brought, and no scales will be set up for them, and no register will be spread out for them, and reward will be poured out upon them without account. God Almighty said: Only those who are patient will be given their reward in full, without account. So much so that those who are healthy in this world will wish that their bodies were cut with scissors because of the virtue that those afflicted lose.
39:11: 11. Say, ‘Indeed, I have been commanded to worship God, devoting my religion to Him sincerely, and not associating anything with Him.’
39:12: 12. And I was commanded to be the first of the Muslims, from this nation.
39:13: 13. Say, ‘Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord,’ and worship other than Him, ‘the punishment of a terrible Day.’ This was when he was called to the religion of his fathers.
39:14: 14. Say, 'I worship God, devoting my religion to Him sincerely.'
39:15: 15. So worship whatever you will besides Him, is a command of rebuke and threat, like His statement: Do whatever you will Fussilat 40, Say, ‘Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families, their spouses and servants, on the Day of Resurrection, Ibn Abbas said: This is because God has made for every person a home and a family in Paradise, so whoever acts in obedience to God, that home and family will be his, and whoever acts in disobedience to God will enter Hell, and that home and family will be for someone else who acted in obedience to God. It was said: The loss of the soul is by entering Hell, and the loss of the family is by being separated from his family, Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss.
39:16: 16. Above them are canopies of fire, canopies of fire and its smoke, and beneath them are canopies, beds and mattresses of fire until it reaches the bottom. The bottom is called canopies because it is canopies for those beneath them, similar to the words of God Almighty: For them are beds of Hellfire and above them are coverings (al-A’raf 7:41). This is how God frightens His servants. O My servants, then fear Me.
39:17: 17. And those who avoid the Taghut, the idols, from worshipping them and turn to God, return to worshipping God, for them is good tidings, in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter, So give good tidings to My servants.
39:18: 18. Those who listen to the word, the Qur’an, and follow the best of it, Al-Suddi said: The best of what they are commanded to do. It was also said that God the Most High mentioned in the Qur’an taking revenge on the oppressor and mentioned forgiveness, and forgiveness is the better of two matters. It was also said that He mentioned the obligatory and dispensable things, so they follow the better, which is the obligatory things. It was also said that they listen to the Qur’an and other things, so they follow the Qur’an. Ata' said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Abu Bakr believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so Uthman, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Talhah, al-Zubayr, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Sa'id ibn Zayd came to him and asked him. He informed them of his faith, so they believed. Then this verse was revealed about them: "So give good tidings to My servants * Who listen to speech and follow the best of it" - and all of it is good. "Those are the ones whom God has guided, and those are the ones of understanding." Ibn Zayd said: And those who avoid Taghut and the two verses were revealed about three men who used to say, There is no god but God in the pre-Islamic era: Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, and Salman al-Farsi. The best is to say, There is no god but God.
39:19: 19. Is he upon whom the word of punishment has come into effect? Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: He whom God knew beforehand would be among the people of Hellfire. It was also said: The word of punishment [His statement: I will surely fill Hellfire, and it was also said:] His statement: (These are in Hellfire and I do not care). Then will you save him who is in the Fire? meaning: You will not be able to do anything to him. Ibn Abbas said: He means Abu Lahab and his son.
39:20: 20. But those who feared their Lord will have mansions above mansions built, meaning: lofty mansions in Paradise, and above them mansions even loftier than them, “beneath which rivers flow. This is the promise of God. God does not fail in His promise,” meaning: God promised them those mansions and mansions with a promise that He will not fail to fulfill. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah told me, Malik told me, on the authority of Safwan bin Salim, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The people of Paradise will see the people of the chambers above them as you see a shining star setting in the horizon from the east to the west, because of the difference between them. They said: O Messenger of God, are those the dwellings of the prophets and none but them will reach them? He said: Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they are men who believed in God and believed the messengers.
39:21: 21. The Almighty said: Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky and causes it to flow meaning He causes that water to enter springs, springs and wells, into the earth - Al-Sha’bi said: Every remote part of the earth descends from the sky. Then He brings forth with it - that is, with the water - vegetation of varying colors - red, yellow, and green. Then it withers - dries up. And you see it - after its greenness and freshness - “yellow. Then He makes it debris” - broken, crumbled pieces. Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding.
39:22: 22. The Almighty’s saying: Is he whose breast God has expanded to Islam, meaning he has the capacity to accept the truth, so he is upon a light from his Lord, not like he whose heart God has hardened. Abu Saeed Ahmad ibn Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shaiba told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan ibn Yazid Al-Mawsili told us in Baghdad, Abu Farwah, whose name was Yazid ibn Muhammad, told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, Zaid ibn Abi Anisa told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘Is he whose breast God has expanded to [accept] Islam then he is upon a light from his Lord?’ We said: ‘O Messenger of God, how is his breast expanded?’ He said: ‘When the light enters the heart, it expands and becomes spacious.’ We said: ‘O Messenger of God, what is the sign of that?’ He said: ‘Repentance to the eternal home, turning away from the home of delusion, and preparing for death before death descends.’” The Almighty said: “So woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of God. Those are in clear error.” Malik ibn Dinar said: No servant has been struck with a punishment greater than hardening of the heart, and God the Almighty has not become angry with a people except that He has taken away mercy from them.
39:23: 23. The Almighty said: "God has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book," parts of which resemble one another in beauty, and confirm one another, with no contradiction or discrepancy. Repeated, in which promises and threats, commands and prohibitions, report and rulings are mentioned twice. Shudders, agitates and is disgusted, at it the skins of those who fear their Lord, and shudders are a change in a person's skin when feeling awe and fear. It was said that what is meant by skins are the hearts, that is, the hearts of those who fear their Lord. Then their skins and their hearts soften at the remembrance of God, that is, at the remembrance of God. That is, when the verses of punishment are mentioned, the skins of those who fear God shudder, and when the verses of mercy are mentioned, their hearts soften and calm down, as God the Almighty said: Unquestionably, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest. (Ar-Ra'd: 28) The true meaning is that their hearts tremble when they are afraid, and soften when they are hopeful. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad told me, Musa bin Muhammad bin Ali told us, Muhammad bin Abdus bin Kamil told us, Yahya bin Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Haad, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Taimi, on the authority of Umm Kulthum bint Al-Abbas, on the authority of Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the skin of the servant shivers from fear of God, his sins fall off him just as the leaves of a dry tree fall off its leaves. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad told us, Ahmad bin Ja’far bin Hamdan told us, Musa bin Ishaq Al-Ansari told us, Muhammad bin Mu’awiyah told us, Al-Layth bin Sa’d told us, Yazid bin Abdullah bin Al-Haad told us with this chain of transmission, and he said: When the skin of the servant shivers from fear of God for the Fire. Qatada said: This is a description of the saints, describing them as having shivers on their skin and hearts at peace with the remembrance of God. He did not describe them as having lost their minds and fainted. Rather, that is the case with the people of innovation, and it is from Satan. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Fanjuwayh told us, Ibn Shaiba told us, Hamdan bin Dawud told us, Salamah bin Shaiba told us, Khalaf bin Salamah told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisain, on the authority of Abdullah bin Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, who said: I said to my grandmother Asma’ bint Abi Bakr: How did the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) act when the Qur’an was recited to them? She said: They were as God Almighty described them; their eyes would shed tears and their skin would shudder. I said to her: There are people today who, when the Qur’an is recited to them, fall unconscious. She said: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. And on his authority, on the authority of [Sulayman ibn] Salamah, Yahya ibn Yahya told us, Saeed ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Jumahi told us that Ibn Umar passed by a man from Iraq who was collapsed, so he said: What is wrong with this man? They said: When the Qur’an is recited to him or he hears the remembrance of God, he collapses. Ibn Umar said: We fear God and we do not collapse! Ibn Omar said: The devil enters the stomach of one of them. This was not the action of the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Sirin: Those who fall down when the Qur’an is recited to them? [He said: The difference between us and them is that one of them sits on the roof of a house with his legs stretched out and then the Qur’an is recited to him] from beginning to end. If he throws himself down, then he is telling the truth. That means: the best speech, "is the guidance of God by which He guides whom He wills. And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide."
39:24: 24. Is he who will be protected with his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection? Mujahid said: He will be dragged on his face into the Fire. Ata’ said: He will be thrown into the Fire upside down, and the first part of him to be touched by the Fire will be his face. Muqatil said: It means that the disbeliever will be thrown into the Fire with his hands chained to his neck, and around his neck will be a rock like a huge mountain of sulfur, and the fire will ignite the rock while it is hanging around his neck, so he will fall and its blazing flames will be on his face, and he will not be able to push it away from his face because of the shackles on his neck and hands. The metaphor of the verse: Is he who protects himself from the evil of the punishment like he who is safe from the punishment? And it was said, meaning: the guards will say to the wrongdoers, Taste what you used to earn, meaning: its consequences.
39:25: 25. Those before them denied, meaning the disbelievers of Mecca denied the messengers, so the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive, meaning: while they were safe and unaware of the punishment.
39:26: 26. So God made them taste disgrace, torment and humiliation, “in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.”
39:27: 27. And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an from every [kind of] example that perhaps they will remember.
39:28: 28. An Arabic Qur’an, in the accusative case, without any crookedness. Ibn Abbas said: Without any disagreement. Mujahid said: Without any ambiguity. Al-Suddi said: Without any creation. This is narrated on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, and it was reported on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah on the authority of seventy of the Tabi’un that the Qur’an is neither created nor created. Perhaps they will fear God, disbelief and denial of it.
39:29: 29. “God sets forth a parable: a man,” Al-Kisa’i said: He put man in the accusative case because it is an explanation of the parable, in whom are partners who are quarreling, disputing and differing, and of bad character. It is said: a man who is quarrelsome and fierce, if he is of bad character, opposes people, and is not satisfied with fairness. “And a man who is at peace with a man,” The people of Mecca and Basra read: “peaceful” with an alif, meaning: purely for Him, with no partner or rival in it. [Others read: “peaceful” with a fatha on the lam without an alif, meaning that which is not disputed] from their saying: He is yours at peace, meaning: He is safe and you have no rival in it. Are they equal in comparison? This is a parable that God the Almighty set forth for the disbeliever who worships various gods, and the believer who worships only the One God. This is a question of denial, meaning: they are not equal. Then He said: Praise be to God, meaning: all praise is due to God, without any other worshipped ones. But most of them do not know, what they will become. What is meant by most is all of them.
39:30: 30. You will die, meaning you will die, and they will die, meaning they will die. Al-Farra’ and Al-Kisa’i said: The dead with emphasis is the one who has not died and will die. The dead with a light emphasis is the one from whom the soul has departed, and that is why it was not lightened here.”
39:31: 31. Then on the Day of Resurrection you will dispute before your Lord. Ibn Abbas said: He means: the one who is right and the one who is wrong, the oppressor and the oppressed. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told us, Ibn Malik told us, Ibn Hanbal told us, my father told us, Ibn Numayr told us, Muhammad - meaning Ibn Amr - told us, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Amr, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Hatib, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Az-Zubayr Ibn Al-Awwam, who said: When the verse, Then on the Day of Resurrection you will surely dispute before your Lord, was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Az-Zubayr said: O Messenger of God, will He repeat to us what happened between us in this world, along with our special sins? He said: Yes, He will repeat it to you until every person with a right is given his right. Az-Zubayr said: By God, the matter is very difficult. Ibn Omar said: We lived for a period of time and we thought that this verse was revealed about us and the People of the Two Books: Then on the Day of Resurrection you will surely dispute before your Lord. We said: How can we dispute while our religion and our Book are one? Until I saw some of us striking each other in the face with the sword, and I knew that it was revealed about us. On the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri regarding this verse, he said: We used to say, Our Lord is one and our religion is one, so what is this dispute? Then, when the day of Siffin came and some of us attacked one another with swords, we said, Yes, this is it. On the authority of Ibrahim, he said: When the verse, Then on the Day of Resurrection you will surely dispute before your Lord, was revealed, they said: How can we dispute when we are brothers? Then when Uthman was killed, they said: Is this our dispute? Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Ibn Abi Dhi’b told us, on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever has wronged his brother with regard to his honor or wealth, let him seek his forgiveness today before a day when there will be neither dinar nor dirham taken from him. If he has any good deeds, they will be taken from him in proportion to his wrongdoing, and if he has none, some of his bad deeds will be taken and placed on him.” Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know who is bankrupt? They said: The bankrupt among us is the one who has neither dirhams nor property. He said: “The bankrupt among my nation is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayers, fasting, and zakat, but he had insulted this one, slandered that one, consumed the wealth of this one, shed the blood of this one, and struck this one. So this one will be credited with some of his good deeds and that one with some of his good deeds.” He said: If his good deeds run out before he has paid off what he owes, some of their sins will be taken and placed upon him, then he will be thrown into the Fire.
39:32: 32. The Almighty said: Who is more unjust than he who lies about God, claiming that He has a son and a partner, and denies the truth, the Qur’an, when it came to him, ‘Is there not in Hell an abode,’ a home and a place, for the disbelievers? This is a question with the meaning of confirmation.
39:33: 33. And he who brought the truth and believed in it, Ibn Abbas said: And he who brought the truth means the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who came with There is no god but God, “and he who believed in it” means the Messenger also conveyed it to the creation. Al-Suddi said: And he who brought the truth means Gabriel, who brought the Qur’an, and he who believed in it means Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who accepted it. Al-Kalbi and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: And he who brought the truth means the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he who believed in it means Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. Qatada and Muqatil said: And he who brought the truth is the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and believed in it are the believers, because God, the Almighty, says: Those are the righteous. Ata’ said: And he who brought the truth are the prophets, and believed in it are the followers. In this case, who means those, like God, the Almighty, says: Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire Al-Baqarah 2:17, then He says: God has taken away their light Al-Baqarah 2:17. Al-Hasan said: They are the believers who believed in it in this world and brought it in the Hereafter. Abdullah ibn Mas’ud read: And those who brought the truth and believed in it. “Those are the righteous.”
39:34: 34. “They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.”
39:35: 35. That God may remove from them the worst of what they did, that is, cover it for them with forgiveness, and reward them according to the best of what they used to do, Muqatil said: He will reward them according to the good deeds they did and not according to the bad ones.
39:36: 36. The Almighty’s saying: Is not God sufficient for His servant? Meaning: Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Abu Ja`far, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read: His servants in the plural, meaning: the prophets, peace be upon them. Their people intended to harm them, as He said: And every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him (Ghafir 40:5). May God suffice them from the evil of those who oppose them. And they frighten you with those besides Him, that is, they frightened the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, with the shame of idols. They said: You must refrain from cursing our gods, or madness or insanity will befall you because of them. And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide.
39:37: 37. “And whomsoever God guides, there is for him no misguider. Is not God Exalted in Might, Lord of Retribution?” Impregnable in His kingdom, taking revenge on His enemies.
39:38: 38. “And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ Say, ‘Then have you considered what you invoke besides God? If God intended me harm,’ meaning severe hardship and affliction, “can they remove His harm or intend me mercy?” meaning grace and blessing? can they withhold His mercy? The people of Basra read: kashifat and mumskat with the tanween, darah and rahmathu with the accusative of the ra’ and the ta’, and the others read it without the tanween and with the genitive of the ra’ and the ta’ as an addition. Muqatil said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them about that and they remained silent. Then God, the Most High, said to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, ‘God is sufficient for me,’ meaning my trust in Him and my reliance on Him. “On Him do the trustful rely,” meaning the trustworthy rely on Him.
39:39: 39. "Say, 'O my people, work according to your position. Indeed, I am working, and you are going to know.'"
39:40: 40. Whoever is afflicted with a humiliating punishment and upon whom a lasting punishment descends, meaning: a permanent punishment descends upon him.
39:41: 41. “Indeed, We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book, for mankind in truth. So whoever is guided does so for [the benefit of] himself, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment,” and the consequences of his going astray are upon him. And you are not a guardian over them, a keeper and a watcher. You are not entrusted with them, nor will you be held accountable for them.
39:42: 42. The Almighty says: God takes the souls meaning the spirits at the time of their death so He takes them when their food is finished and their appointed time has come to an end. at the time of their death meaning the death of their bodies. And those that do not die meaning He takes the souls that do not die, during their sleep and the one that is taken during sleep is the soul that has reason and discernment. Every human being has two souls: one during life, which leaves him at death and with its loss the soul is gone, and the other is the soul of discernment, which leaves him when he sleeps, and after sleeping he breathes. Then He keeps that for which He has decreed death so He does not return it to the body. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read: Qadhi with a damma on the qaf, a kasra on the dad, and a fatha on the ya’. Death is nominative for what its agent is not named. The others read it with a fatha on the qaf and the dad. Death is accusative because God Almighty said: God takes the souls. “And He sends the other,” and He returns the other, which is the one that death has not decreed, to the body, for a specified term, until the time of his death comes. It is said: A person has a soul and a spirit. When sleeping, the soul leaves and the spirit remains. Ali said: The soul leaves when sleeping, but its ray remains in the body. Thus, a person sees a vision. When he wakes up from sleep, the spirit returns to his body in less than a moment. It is said: The souls of the living and the dead meet in dreams and get to know each other as God wills. When they want to return to their bodies, God holds the souls of the dead with Him and sends the souls of the living back to their bodies until the end of their life span. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmad bin Yunus told us, Zuhair told us, Abdullah bin Umar told us, Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Maqburi told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you goes to bed, let him shake out his bed with the inside of his garment, for he does not know what has come upon it afterward. Then he should say: ‘In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side and with You I raise it. If You should hold my soul, then have mercy upon it, and if You should release it, then protect it as You protect Your righteous servants.’” Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought, as evidence of His power, as He did not make mistakes in holding back what He holds back of the souls, and sending what He sends out of them. Muqatil said: These are signs for people who contemplate the matter of resurrection. He means that if the soul of a sleeper dies and is sent back after death, this is evidence of resurrection.
39:43: 43. Or have they taken intercessors besides God? Say, O Muhammad, ‘Or even if they—and if they mean the gods—do not possess anything of intercession, nor do they understand—that you worship them. The answer to this is omitted, and its meaning is: Even if you take them with this quality.
39:44: 44. “Say: ‘To God belongs all intercession.’” Mujahid said: No one can intercede except with His permission. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and then to Him you will be returned.
39:45: 45. And when God alone is mentioned, they are disgusted, they are repelled. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Muqatil said: they are withdrawn from monotheism. Qatada said: they are arrogant. The root of disgust is aversion and arrogance, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter. “And when those besides Him are mentioned,” meaning the idols, at once they rejoice, they rejoice. Mujahid and Muqatil said: That was when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surat An-Najm, and Satan put into his wish: Those are the exalted cranes, so the disbelievers rejoiced at him.
39:46: 46. "Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ." Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us, Abu Nu'aym al-Isfarayini informed us, Abu 'Awana informed us, al-Salami informed us, al-Nadr ibn Muhammad informed us, 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar informed us, Yahya ibn Abi Katheer informed us, Abu Salamah informed us: I asked Aisha may God be pleased with her how the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would begin his night prayers. She said: He would say: "O God, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. Guide me to the truth regarding that over which they differ, by Your permission. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path."
39:47: 47. The Almighty said: “And if those who did wrong had all that is in the earth and the like thereof with it, they would offer it as ransom from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from God that which they had never reckoned with.” Muqatil said: When they were resurrected, there appeared to them that which they had never reckoned with in this world would befall them in the Hereafter. Al-Suddi said: They thought they were good deeds, but they appeared to them as bad deeds. The meaning is that they were seeking to draw closer to God by worshipping idols, and when they were punished for them, there appeared from God that which they had never reckoned with. It was narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir was distressed at the time of death, and he was asked about that, so he said: I fear that there will appear to me that which I had never reckoned with.
39:48: 48. And the evils of what they had earned will become apparent to them, meaning: the evils of their actions of polytheism and injustice toward God’s friends. And that which they used to ridicule will overtake them.
39:49: 49. But when harm touches man, meaning hardship, he calls upon Us; then when We grant him, meaning We give him a favor from Us, he says, ‘I was only given it because of knowledge,’ meaning, because of the knowledge from God that I am worthy of it. Muqatil said: Because of good that God knows best with me. He mentioned the metaphor because what is meant by a blessing is a bestowal. Rather, it is a trial, [meaning, that blessing is a trial] to lure him in, test him, and affliction from God the Most High. It was also said: Rather, His word that he uttered was a trial. But most of them do not know, meaning, that it is a lure and a test.
39:50: 50. Those before them had said it, Muqatil said: meaning Qarun, for he said: It was only given to me because of knowledge I have Al-Qasas 78, so what they were earning did not avail them at all, so disbelief did not avail them at all in terms of punishment.
39:51: 51. So the evil consequences of what they had earned will befall them, meaning: their punishment. Then He threatened the unbelievers of Mecca, saying: And those who did wrong among these will be afflicted with the evil consequences of what they had earned, and they will not be able to escape, meaning they will be annihilated because their return is to God Almighty.
39:52: 52. Do they not know that God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it? That is, He expands provision for whom He wills, and restricts it. That is, He restricts it for whom He wills. There are certainly signs in that for a people who believe.
39:53: 53. The Almighty said: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ Ata ibn Abi Rabah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent word to Wahshi inviting him to Islam. Wahshi sent word to him: How can you invite me to your religion while you claim that whoever kills, associates others with God, or commits adultery will incur sins and his punishment will be doubled, while I have done all of that? Then God, the Almighty, revealed: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds Maryam 19:60. Wahshi said: This is a very strict condition that I may not be able to fulfill. Is there anything else? Then God, the Almighty, revealed: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills An-Nisa’ 4:48-116. Wahshi said: I still find myself in doubt, and I do not know whether He will forgive me or not. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God.’ Wahshi said: Yes, this is it. So he came and converted to Islam. The Muslims said: Is this specific to him or to Muslims in general? He said: Rather, it is for Muslims in general. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: These verses were revealed about Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, Al-Walid ibn Al-Walid and a group of Muslims who had converted to Islam and were then persecuted and tortured. They were persecuted and we used to say: God will never accept any ransom or justice from these people. They are people who converted to Islam and then abandoned their religion because of the torture they were tortured with. So God Almighty revealed these verses, and Umar ibn Al-Khattab wrote them with his own hand and then sent them to Ayyash ibn Rabi’ah, Al-Walid ibn Al-Walid and to those people. They converted to Islam and emigrated. Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: We, the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), used to see or say: There is nothing of our good deeds that is not accepted until the verse: Obey God and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds (Muhammad 47:33) was revealed. When this verse was revealed, we said: What is it that invalidates our deeds? We said: Major sins and immoralities. He said: “So if we saw someone committing one of these, we would say he is doomed. Then this verse was revealed, and we refrained from speaking about it. So if we saw someone committing one of these, we would fear for him, but if he did not commit any of them, we would hope for him.” By extravagance, he meant committing major sins. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he entered the mosque and found a storyteller talking about Hellfire and chains. He stood over his head and said: O storyteller, why do you make people despair? Then he recited: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of God. Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Haytham Al-Turabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abd bin Ahmad Al-Hamawi told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Khazim Al-Shashi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid told us, Hayyan bin Hilal, Sulayman bin Harb, and Hajjaj bin Munhal told us: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Asma bint Yazid, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins, and He does not mind.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Al-Siddiq Al-Naji, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There was a man among the Children of Israel who killed ninety-nine people, then he went out asking and came to a monk and asked him, ‘Is there any repentance for me?’ He said, ‘No.’ So he killed him and thus completed one hundred. Then a man said to him, ‘Go to such-and-such a village.’ Death overtook him and he turned his chest toward it, and the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. God Almighty revealed to this one to come near and revealed to this one to move away. He said, ‘Measure the distance between them.’ He found him to be closer to this one by a handspan, so He forgave him.” Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Anbari on the authority of Muadh ibn Hisham on the authority of his father on the authority of Qatada with this chain of transmission. He said: “He was directed to a monk who came to him and said: ‘He killed ninety-nine people, so is there any chance for him to repent?’ He said to him: ‘I killed one hundred people, so is there any chance for me to repent?’ He said: ‘Yes, and who will stand between him and his repentance? Go to such-and-such a land, for there are people there who worship God, so worship God with them and do not return to your land, for it is a land of evil.’ So he went until he was halfway there, death came to him. The angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him, and an angel came to them in the form of a human being, and they placed him between them. He said: ‘Measure the distance between the two lands, and whichever of them is closer to it is his.’ They measured it and found it to be closer to the land he wanted, so the angels of mercy took him.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A`raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man - who had never done any good - said to his family, ‘When he dies, burn him and scatter half of him on land and half of him in the sea. By God, if God has power over him, He will punish him with a punishment by which He has not punished anyone in the world.’ So when he died, they did as He commanded them. God commanded the sea to gather what was in it and commanded the land to gather what was in it. Then He said to him, ‘Why did you do this?’ He said, ‘Out of fear of You, O Lord, and You know best.’ So He forgave him.” Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ikrimah ibn Ammar, on the authority of Damdam ibn Jaws, who said: I entered the mosque of Madinah and an old man called me and said: O Yemeni, come here. I did not know him. He said: Do not say to a man: By God, God will never forgive you, and God will never admit you to Paradise. I said: Who are you, may God have mercy on you? He said: Abu Hurairah said: I said: This is a word that one of us says to one of his family members when he is angry, or to his wife or his servant. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There were two men among the Children of Israel who loved each other. One of them was striving in worship, and the other was speaking as if he were sinning. He kept saying: ‘Stop, stop what you are doing.’ He said: ‘Leave me to my Lord.’ He said: Until one day he found him committing a sin which he considered very great, so he said: ‘Stop.’ He said: ‘Leave me to my Lord. Have you sent a watcher over me?’ He said: ‘By God, God will never forgive you, and will never admit you to Paradise.’ He said: So God sent an angel to them who took their souls and they met before him. He said to the sinner: ‘Enter Paradise by My mercy.’ He said to the other: ‘Can you prevent My mercy from my servant?’ He said: ‘No, O Lord.’ He said: ‘Take him to the Fire.’” God the Almighty said: “Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.” Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Qaffal informed us, Abu Mas`ud Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Khatib informed us, Muhammad ibn Ya`qub al-Asamm informed us, Abu Qilabah informed us, Abu `Asim informed us, Zakariya ibn Ishaq informed us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of `Ata`, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: except for the deletion An-Najm:32, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a lot, and which servant of yours is there without pain?
39:54: 54. The Almighty said: And turn to your Lord in repentance, that is, come and return to Him in obedience, and submit to Him, that is, devote your monotheism to Him, before the punishment comes upon you and then you will not be aided.
39:55: 55. And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord, meaning: the Qur’an, and the entire Qur’an is good, and the meaning of the verse is what Al-Hasan said: Commit to obeying Him and avoiding disobeying Him, for the Qur’an mentioned the ugly for you to avoid it, and mentioned the lesser so that you would not desire it, and mentioned the best for you to prefer it. Al-Suddi said: The best is what God has commanded in the Book, before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive.
39:56: 56. That a soul might say, meaning: lest a soul might say, like His statement: And He has placed firmly set mountains in the earth, lest it should shake with you (al-Nahl 16:15), meaning: lest it shake with you. Al-Mubarrad said: meaning, hasten and beware lest a soul might say. Al-Zajjaj said: fearing that you might end up in a state where you say this statement, Oh, my regret, “Oh, my remorse,” and regret is grief over what has passed. He meant: Oh, my regret, with the addition, but the Arabs change the pronoun ya to an alif when seeking help, so they say: Oh, my regret and Oh, my remorse, and sometimes they add a ya after the alif to indicate addition. Abu Ja`far read this in the same way Oh, my regret. It was said that the meaning of His statement: Oh, my regret, is Oh, you regret, this is your time, “for what you neglected in the side of God.” Al-Hasan said: you fell short in obeying God. Mujahid said: in the command of God. Saeed bin Jubair said: In the right of God. It was also said: You were wasted in the sake of God. It was also said: It means you fell short in the aspect that leads to God’s pleasure. The Arabs call a side a side. And if you were among the mockers, those who mock the religion of God, His Book, His Messenger, and the believers. Qatada said: It was not enough for him that he wasted the obedience to God, so he began to mock the people of his obedience.
39:57: 57. Or you say, If only God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.
39:58: 58. Or you will say when you see the punishment, clearly, If only I had another chance, a return to the world, so I could be among the doers of good, the monotheists.
39:59: 59. Then it will be said to this one who says it: Yes, My signs have come to you, meaning the Qur’an, but you denied them, and said that they were not from God, and you were arrogant, and you were too arrogant to believe in them, and you were among the disbelievers.
39:60: 60. And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, claiming that He had a son and a partner, “their faces will be blackened. Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?” about faith.
39:62: 62. God is the Creator of all things and He is the Disposer of all things, meaning: all things are entrusted to Him and He is the One who preserves them.
39:63: 63. To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth, the keys to the treasuries of the heavens and the earth. The singular form is miqallad, like miftah, and muqallad is like mandil and mana’id. Qatada and Muqatil said: The keys to the heavens and the earth are provision and mercy. Al-Kalbi said: The treasuries of rain and the treasuries of plants. And those who disbelieve in the signs of God - it is they who are the losers.
39:64: 64. The Almighty said: Say, ‘Is it other than God that you command me to worship, O ignorant ones?’ Muqatil said: That is because the infidels of Quraysh called him to the religion of his forefathers. The people of Ash-Sham read ta’amru’unni with two light nuns as per the original, while the people of Madinah read it with one light nun as per deletion, and the others read it with one double nun as per assimilation.
39:65: 65. And it has already been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and to those before you, that if you should associate [anything] with God, [your] work will surely become worthless, that is, what you did before associating partners with God. This is addressed to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, but what is meant by it is others. It has also been said that this is a lesson from God Almighty to His Prophet and a threat to others, because God Almighty protected him from associating partners with God. And you will surely be among the losers.
39:66: 66. Rather, worship God and be among the grateful, for His blessings upon you.
39:67: 67. The Almighty said: And they did not estimate God with His true estimate, they did not glorify Him with His true greatness when they associated others with Him. Then He informed of His greatness, saying: “And the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: A rabbi from the rabbis came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “O Muhammad, we find that God places the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees on one finger, the water and the soil on one finger, and the leaders of creation on one finger, and then says: I am the King. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed until his molars were visible in confirmation of what the rabbi had said. Then he recited: ‘But they have not appraised God with true appraisal, and the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection.’” Narrated by Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj on the authority of Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Yunus on the authority of Fadil bin Ayyad on the authority of Mansour, who said: “And the mountains and trees are on a finger, and he said: Then he shakes them and says, ‘I am the King, I am God.’” Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, al-Husayn ibn Fanjuwayh told me, ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of ‘Umar ibn Hamza, on the authority of Salim ibn ‘Abdullah, who told me that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “God will fold up the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, then take them with His right hand, then say: ‘I am the King; where are the tyrants, where are the arrogant?’ Then He will fold up the earths, then take them with His left...” This is an authentic hadith narrated by Muslim on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba al-Kashmihani told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Zuhri, Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab told me, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God will seize the earth on the Day of Resurrection and fold up the heavens with His right hand, then He will say: I am the King. Where are the kings of the earth?”
39:68: 68. The Almighty said: And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and the earth will fall unconscious, they will die from fear, and it is the first blast, except whom God wills, they differed regarding those whom God the Almighty excepted, and we mentioned them in Surat An-Naml. Al-Hasan said: Except whom God wills, meaning God alone, Then He will blow into it, meaning: into the Trumpet, another time, meaning: another time, and at once they will be standing, looking, [from their graves] awaiting God’s command concerning them. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Between the two blasts there will be forty.’ They said: ‘Forty days?’ He said: ‘I refuse.’ They said: ‘Forty months?’ He said: ‘I refuse.’ They said: ‘Forty years?’ He said: ‘I refuse.’ He said: ‘Then God sends down water from the sky and they grow as plants grow. There is nothing in man that will not decay except one bone, which is the coccyx, and from it creation will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection.”
39:69: 69. The Almighty said: And the earth will shine, illuminated, with the light of its Lord, with the light of its Creator, and that will be when the Lord appears to decide the judgment among His creation. They will not be harmed by His light, just as they are not harmed by the sun on a clear day. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: With the justice of their Lord, and by the earth he meant the places of resurrection. And the record will be placed, meaning the book of deeds. And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, Ibn Abbas said: He means those who testify for the messengers that they conveyed the message, and they are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ata’ said: He means the guardians, indicated by the Almighty’s saying: And every soul will come with a driver and a witness (Qaf: 21), And it will be judged between them in truth, meaning with justice, and they will not be wronged, meaning their bad deeds will not be increased nor their good deeds decreased.
39:70: 70. And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has done, meaning: the reward for what it has done, and He is most knowing of what they do, Ata’ said: He means that I am all-knowing of their actions and do not need a scribe or a witness.
39:71: 71. And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, violently, in droves, one after the other, each nation separately. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: Groups means separate groups, the singular of which is group. “Until, when they reach it, its gates are opened,” the seven, and they had been closed before that. The people of Kufa read faṭahāt opened and faṭahāt opened with a light emphasis, while the others read it with a heavy emphasis, And its keepers said to them, rebuking and reprimanding them, Did there not come to you messengers from among you, from among yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours? They said, Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect, it has become necessary, for the disbelievers, which is the Almighty’s saying: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together Hud 119.
39:72: 72. “It will be said, ‘Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant.’”
39:73: 73. And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it, its gates are opened. The Kufians said: This waw is redundant so that it is an answer to his statement: until, when they reach it, as in the market of the unbelievers. This is like what God Almighty said: And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light Al-Anbiya’ 48, (meaning: light), and the waw is redundant. It was said: The waw is the waw of state, and its meaning is: Its doors were opened. The waw was inserted to clarify that they were open before their arrival, and it was deleted in the first verse to clarify that they were closed before their arrival. If you do not make the waw redundant in his saying: (And it was opened), they differed in the answer to his saying: And its keepers said to them, and the waw in it is omitted, meaning: until they came to it and its doors were opened, and its keepers said to them. Al-Zajjaj said: I think the answer is omitted, and its meaning is: “Until when they came to it and its gates were opened, and its keepers said to them, ‘Peace be upon you, you have become good, so enter it to abide eternally.’” They entered it, because the speech indicates this. And its keepers said to them, “Peace be upon you, you are well.” He means that the keepers of Paradise greet them and say, You are well. Ibn Abbas said: May your stay be pleasant. Qatada said: When they cross the Fire, they will be stopped on a bridge between Paradise and Hell, and some of them will take revenge on others until they are refined and purified and enter Paradise. Then Ridwan and his companions said to them: “Peace be upon you. You have been pure, so enter it to abide therein.” It was narrated on the authority of Ali, peace be upon him, who said: They will be led to Paradise, and when they reach it, they will find at its gate a tree from under whose trunk two springs will emerge. The believer will wash from one of them, purifying his exterior, and drink from the other, purifying his interior. The angels will meet them at the gates of Paradise, saying: “Peace be upon you. You have done well, so enter it to abide therein.”
39:74: 74. And they said, ‘Praise be to God, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth,’ meaning the land of Paradise. This is what God Almighty said: And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, ‘The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.’ (Al-Anbiya’: 105). We will settle we will descend in Paradise wherever we wish God Almighty said: So excellent is the reward of the workers the reward of the obedient.
39:75: 75. And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, meaning: engulfing and encircling the Throne, circling its edges, meaning: its sides, glorifying with praise of their Lord, it was said: This is glorification of enjoyment, not glorification of worship, because the obligation [will disappear] on that day, and it will be judged between them with truth, meaning: it will be judged between the people of Paradise and Hell with justice, “and it will be said: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds,” the people of Paradise will say: Thanks to God, when God’s promise to them was fulfilled. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ubaid God bin Musa told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The example of the Qur’an is like that of a man who went out to look for a place for his family, and he passed by the trail of rain. While he was walking through it and marveling at it, it descended upon soft meadows. He said: I was amazed at the first rain, so this is more amazing than it and more amazing. So it was said to him: The example of the first rain is like the greatness of the Qur’an, and these soft meadows are like the letter Ha-Mim in the Qur’an. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Rumi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Sarraj told us, Qutaybah told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, that Al-Jarrah bin Abi Al-Jarrah told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Everything has a core, and the core of the Qur’an is the Ha-Mim verses. Ibn Mas’ud said: When you encounter Al-Ha-Mim, you encounter delicate gardens. Do you adorn yourself in them? Sa’d bin Ibrahim said: They - Al-Ha-Mim - were called brides.
40:1: 1. Meccan: The words of God Almighty: "Ha Meem." We have already discussed the letters of the spelling. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "Ha Meem is the greatest name of God." Ikrimah narrated on his authority that he said: "Alif, Lam, Meem, and Noon are the letters of (Ar-Rahman) in separate letters." Saeed bin Jubayr and Ata' Al-Khurasani said: The Ha' is the opening letter of His names: Wise, Praiseworthy, Living, Forbearing, Compassionate. And the Meem is the opening letter of His names: Owner, Majestic, Generous. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kisa'i said: Its meaning is He has decreed what is to come to be, as if they indicated that its meaning is: Ha Meem, with a damma on the Ha' and a shaddah on the Meem. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr read: Ha Meem with a kasra on the Ha', and the rest with a fatha on it.
40:2: 2. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
40:3: 3. Forgiver of sin, Concealer of sin, Accepter of repentance, meaning repentance, the source of the verb taba to repent is taaba to repent. It is also said that tawbah repentance is the plural of tawbah to repent like dumah home and dum home and hawmah home and hawm home. Ibn Abbas said: Forgiver of sin for he who says there is no god but God, [and Accepter of repentance for he who says there is no god but God. Severe in penalty, for he who does not say there is no god but God, Possessor of bounty, the One who is independent of he who does not say there is no god but God. Mujahed said: The One with the length means the One with the spaciousness and wealth. Al-Hasan said: The One with the bounty. Qatada said: The One with the blessings. It was said: The One with power. The origin of the word length is the blessing that lasts a long time for its owner. There is no god but He, to Him is the final destination.
40:4: 4. None disputes about the verses of God, in refuting the verses of God by denying and rejecting them, except those who disbelieve. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Two verses are more difficult for those who dispute about the Qur’an: None disputes about the verses of God except those who disbelieve, “Indeed, those who differ over the Scripture are in extreme dissension.” Al-Baqarah 2:176. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad told us, Muhammad bin Khalid told us, Dawud bin Sulaiman told us, Abdullah bin Hamid told us, Al-Hussein bin Ali Al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Sa’d bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Disputing about the Qur’an is disbelief. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard some people disputing about the Qur’an, so he said: ‘Those who came before you were destroyed because of this. They struck some parts of the Book of God, the Almighty, with others. The Book of God was revealed to confirm some parts of it, so do not contradict some parts of it with others. Whatever you know of it, say it, and whatever you do not know of it, leave it to its scholar.’” The Almighty says: So let not their movement throughout the land deceive you, meaning their movement throughout the land for trade and their safety in it despite their disbelief, for the consequence of their affair is torment. Similar to the Almighty’s saying: Let not the movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you Al Imran 3:196.
40:5: 5. The people of Noah denied before them, and the parties after them, they are the disbelievers who formed parties against their prophets after the people of Noah, and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, Ibn Abbas said: to kill him and destroy him. It was also said: to take him prisoner. The Arabs call a prisoner a captive, and they argued with falsehood to refute, to invalidate, therewith the truth, which the messengers brought, and their arguments are like their saying: You are only human beings like us (Ibrahim 14:10), Why were angels not sent down to us? (al-Furqan 25:21), and the like, So I seized them; how terrible was My punishment?
40:6: 6.
