And thus the word of your Lord has come true, meaning: just as the word of punishment came true upon the nations that denied, it came true, upon those who disbelieved, from your people, that they are the companions of the Fire, Al-Akhfash said: because they or because they are the companions of the Fire.
40:7: 7. The Almighty said: Those who bear the Throne and those around it, the bearers of the Throne and those who circle around it are the Cherubim, and they are the masters of the angels. Ibn Abbas said: The bearers of the Throne, the distance between the heel of one of them and the bottom of his feet is a journey of five hundred years. It is narrated that their feet are at the borders of the earths, and the earths and the heavens are within their boundaries, and they say: Glory be to the Possessor of Might and Majesty, Glory be to the Possessor of Sovereignty and Dominion, Glory be to the Ever-Living Who does not die, Glory be to the Lord of the angels and the Spirit. Maysarah ibn Arooba said: Their feet are on the lowest earth, and their heads have pierced the Throne. They are in humility, not raising their eyes. They are more fearful than the people of the seventh heaven, and the people of the seventh heaven are more fearful than the people of the heaven below it, and the heaven below it is more fearful than the one below it. Mujahid said: Between the angels and the Throne are seventy veils of light. Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir narrated on the authority of Jabir that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given permission to speak about an angel of God who bears the Throne. The distance between his earlobes and his shoulders is a journey of seven hundred years.” Jaafar bin Muhammad narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that he said: [What is] between the pillars of the throne is clothed every day with seventy thousand colors of light, and no creation of God can look at it, and all things are in a state of trembling like a ring in a desert. Mujahed said: Between the seventh heaven and the throne there are seventy thousand veils of light, a veil of darkness, a veil of light, and a veil of darkness. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: “Around the Throne are seventy thousand rows of angels, one row behind the other, circling the Throne. These come before one another and those turn away. When they face one another, these glorify God and those say ‘God is Great.’ Behind them are seventy thousand rows standing, their hands on their necks, placing them on their shoulders. When they hear the glorification and praise of those, they raise their voices and say: ‘Glory be to You and praise be to You. How great and majestic You are! You are God, there is no god but You. You are the Greatest. All creation will return to You.’” And behind them are one hundred thousand rows of angels, placed right on left, and there is not one of them who does not glorify God with praise that no other glorifies Him with. The distance between the wings of one of them is a journey of three hundred years, and the distance between his earlobe and his shoulder is four hundred years. And God is veiled from the angels who surround the Throne by seventy veils of fire, seventy veils of darkness, seventy veils of light, seventy veils of white pearls, seventy veils of red rubies, [and seventy veils of yellow sapphires], seventy veils of green emerald, seventy veils of snow, seventy veils of water, seventy veils of hail, and that which none knows except God Almighty. He said: Each of the bearers of the Throne and those around it has four faces: the face of a bull, the face of a lion, the face of an eagle, and the face of a human. Each of them has four wings. Two of them are on his face, lest he look at the Throne and be struck dead. The other two are wings with which he flies. They do not speak except glorification, praise, magnification, and exaltation. God Almighty says: They glorify the praises of their Lord and believe in Him, they believe that He is One and has no partner. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Umar bin Abdullah Al-Raqashi told us, Ja’far bin Sulayman told us, Harun bin Rabab told us, Shahr bin Hawshab told us: The bearers of the Throne are eight, four of them say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. Praise be to You for Your forbearance after Your knowledge. And four of them say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. Praise be to You for Your forgiveness after Your power. He said: It is as if they are looking at the sins of the children of Adam. God the Almighty said: And they ask forgiveness for those who have believed, ‘Our Lord,’ meaning they say, Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge. It was said: It is in the accusative case for explanation, and it was said: It is in the transference, meaning: Your mercy and knowledge encompass all things. So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way, Your religion. And protect them from the punishment of Hellfire. [Mutarraf] said: The most sincere of God’s servants to the believers are the angels, and the most deceitful of creation to the believers are the devils.
40:8: 8. “Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them and to whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” Saeed bin Jubair said: The believer will enter Paradise and say: Where is my father? Where is my mother? Where are my children? Where is my husband? It will be said: They did not know anything like what you did. He will say: I used to work for myself and for them. It will be said: Admit them to Paradise.
40:9: 9. And protect them from evil deeds, the punishments, and whoever You protect from evil deeds, meaning: and whoever You protect from evil deeds, meaning the punishments, and it was said: the recompense for evil deeds, on that Day You have had mercy on him, and that is what is the great attainment.
40:10: 10. The Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out, on the Day of Resurrection while they are in the Fire, having hated themselves when their sins were presented to them and they witnessed the punishment. It will be said to them: The hatred of God was greater than your hatred of yourselves when you were called to faith and you disbelieved, meaning that God’s hatred of you in this world when you were called to faith and you disbelieved was greater than your hatred of yourselves today when the punishment descends upon you.
40:12: 12. God the Almighty said: That is because when God alone is invoked, you disbelieve. There is a metaphor in it that is not needed because of the apparent meaning of it. Its meaning is: So respond that there is no way to that, and this torment and eternity in the Fire is because when God alone is invoked, you disbelieve. When it is said, There is no god but God, [you disbelieve], and you say, Shall I make the gods one god? (Sad: 5). But if someone associates with Him, other than Him, you believe, you believe in that association. Then the judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Great. There is no higher or greater than Him.
40:13: 13. It is He who shows you His signs and sends down to you provision from the sky, meaning: the rain that is the cause of provisions. But none will remember, and none will take heed from these signs, except he who turns back, who turns to God Almighty in all his affairs.
40:14: 14. So call upon God, devoting your religion to Him sincerely, obedience and worship. Even though the disbelievers dislike it.
40:15: 15. Exalted in degrees, the Exalter of the degrees of the prophets and saints in Paradise, Possessor of the Throne, its Creator and Owner, Casts down the Spirit, sends down the revelation. He called it the Spirit because hearts are enlivened by it as bodies are enlivened by spirits, by His command, Ibn Abbas said: by His decree. It was also said: by His word. Muqatil said: by His command. Upon whom He wills of His servants, that he may warn, meaning: to warn the Prophet with revelation, of the Day of Meeting, and Yaqub read it with a ta’, meaning: that you, O Muhammad, may warn on the Day of Meeting, the day on which the people of the heavens and the people of the earth will meet. Qatada and Muqatil said: on that day the creation and the Creator will meet. Ibn Zayd said: The servants meet. Maymun ibn Mihran said: The oppressor, the oppressed, and the adversaries meet. It was also said: The worshippers and the worshipped meet. It was also said: A person and his deeds meet there.
40:16: 16. The Day they will appear, emerging from their graves, visible, nothing concealing them. Nothing of them, of their deeds and conditions, will be hidden from God. God the Most High will say on that day after the creation has perished: To whom belongs the kingdom today? No one will answer Him, so He will answer Himself and say: To God, the One, the Prevailing, who subdued creation with death.
40:17: 17. This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it has earned. The doer of good will be recompensed for his good deeds, and the doer of evil will be recompensed for his evil deeds. “There will be no injustice this Day. Indeed, God is swift in account.”
40:18: 18. And warn them of the approaching Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection. It is called this because it is near, as everything that is coming is near. Similar to the words of God Almighty: The approaching Day has drawn near (al-Najm 53:57), meaning the Resurrection is near. When the hearts will be at the throats, meaning that they will move from their places out of fear until they reach the throats. They will not return to their places, nor will they leave their mouths so that they may die and find rest. Suppressing [their expressions], distressed and filled with fear and grief. Suppressing [their expressions] is the repetition of anger, fear, and grief in the heart until it becomes constricted. The wrongdoers will have no close friend, someone close to benefit them, nor an intercessor who will be obeyed, who will intercede for them.
40:19: 19. He knows the treachery of the eyes, meaning: its treachery, which is stealing glances at what is not permissible. Mujahid said: It is the eyes looking at what God has forbidden. And what the hearts conceal.
40:20: 20. And God judges with truth, and those they invoke besides Him, [meaning the idols], do not judge at all, because they do not know anything and are not able to do anything. Nafi’ [and Ibn ‘Amir] read: (you invoke), with a ta’, and the others read it with a ya’. Indeed, God is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
40:21: 21. Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength. Ibn Amir read: of you with a kaf, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an, and traces on the earth, but that did not benefit them. So God seized them for their sins, and there was for them against God no protector, to ward off the punishment from them.
40:22: 22. That, meaning: that punishment that befell them, “was because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved. So God seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and Severe in penalty.”
40:23: 23. The Almighty said: And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority.
40:24: 24. To Pharaoh, Haman, and Korah, and they said, A lying magician.
40:25: 25. But when he brought them the truth from Us, they said, meaning Pharaoh and his people, Kill the sons of those who believed with him. Qatada said: This is different from the first killing, because Pharaoh had refrained from killing children, but when Moses, peace be upon him, was sent, he killed them again. The meaning is that they killed them again, and kept their women alive, to prevent them from following Moses and supporting him. And the plot of the disbelievers, meaning the plot and deceit of Pharaoh and his people, is only in error, meaning: their plot goes to waste, and what God Almighty wants will befall them.
40:26: 26. And Pharaoh said, to his people, Let me kill Moses. He only said this because there were those among Pharaoh’s elite who prevented him from killing him for fear of destruction. And let him call upon his Lord, that is, let Moses call upon his Lord who he claims sent him to us and who will prevent him from us. I fear that he will change, that is, alter, your religion, which you are following, or that corruption will appear in the land. Ya’qub and the people of Kufa read or that it will appear. The people of Medina, Basra, and Hafs read it will appear with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the ha’ for transitivity. Corruption is in the accusative case because of his saying that he will change your religion, so that the two verbs would be on the same level. The others read it with a fatha on the ya’ and the ha’ for necessity. Corruption is in the nominative case, and he meant by corruption changing the religion and worshipping something other than it.
40:27: 27. And Moses said, when Pharaoh threatened to kill him, Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.
40:28: 28. And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said. They differed about this believer: Muqatil and Al-Suddi said: He was a Copt, a cousin of Pharaoh, and he is the one about whom God spoke, saying: And there came a man from the farthest part of the city, running (al-Qasas 28:20). Some people said: He was an Israelite. The metaphor of the verse: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said. His name was Hazael according to Ibn Abbas and most scholars. Ibn Ishaq said: His name was [Jibran]. It was said: The name of the man from the family of Pharaoh who believed was Habib. Would you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God,’ while he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord, meaning: with what indicates his truthfulness. And if he is a liar, then upon him is his lie, that will not harm you. And if he is truthful, and you denied him, some of what he promises you will befall you, Abu Ubaid said: What is meant by some is all, meaning: If you kill him while he is telling the truth, then what he threatens you with of punishment will befall you. Al-Layth said: some is a conjunction, meaning: what he promises you will befall you. The scholars of meaning said: This is based on what appears in Al-Hajjaj, as if he said: The least of his truthfulness is that some of what he promises you will befall you, and some of that will be your destruction. So he mentioned some to require all of it, Indeed, God does not guide to His religion, whoever is a transgressor, [a polytheist], a liar, against God. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Al-Awza’i told me, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told me, Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Taimi told me, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me: I said to Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-As: Tell me the worst thing that the polytheists did to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying in the courtyard of the Kaaba, Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt came and seized the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by the shoulder and twisted his garment around his neck, choking him violently. Abu Bakr came and seized him by the shoulder and pushed him away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Do you kill a man because he says, ‘My Lord is God,’ when he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord?
40:29: 29. O my people, yours is the kingdom this day, dominant in the land, victorious in the land of Egypt, but who will protect us from the wrath of God, who will prevent us from the punishment of God, if it comes to us, meaning, yours is the kingdom today, so do not expose yourselves to the punishment of God by denying and killing the Prophet, for there is nothing to prevent the punishment of God if it befalls you. Pharaoh said, ‘I do not show you,’ of opinion and advice, “except what I see, of myself. Ad-Dahhak said, I teach you only what I know, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct, I call you only to the path of guidance.
40:30: 30. And he who believed said, O my people, indeed I fear for you a day like that of the Confederates.
40:31: 31. Like the habit of the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and those after them, meaning: like their habit of persisting in denial until the punishment came to them, and God does not intend injustice for His servants, meaning: He does not destroy them before the proof is established against them.
40:32: 32. "And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling," the Day of Resurrection, every people will be called by their leader and they will call out to one another. Then the people of Paradise will call out to the people of the Fire, and the people of the Fire will call out to the people of Paradise. Then the people of the A'raf will be called out, and happiness and misery will be called out: Behold, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, has attained happiness after which he will never be miserable, and so-and-so, son of so-and-so, has attained misery after which he will never be happy. And it will be called out when death is slaughtered: O people of Paradise, eternity but no death. O people of the Fire, eternity but no death. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak read: The Day of Calling with emphasis on the letter dal, meaning: the Day of Discord. This is because they fled and scattered on the earth as camels scattered when they stray from their owners. Ad-Dahhak said: Likewise, when they hear the roar of the Fire, they call out in flight, and they do not come to any region except that they find the angels in rows, so they return to the place where they were. This is what God Almighty says: And the angels are over its corners (al-Haqqah 69:17), and His saying: O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass (al-Rahman 55:33).
40:33: 33. The Day you turn back in flight / turning away from the place of reckoning to the Fire. Mujahid said: Fleeing but not escaping. You will have no protector from God to protect you from His punishment. And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide.
40:34: 34. And indeed, Joseph had already come to you before, meaning Joseph, son of Jacob, before. That is, before Moses, with clear proofs, meaning his statement: Are separate lords better or God, the One, the Prevailing? (Yusuf 12:39), But you did not cease to be in doubt about that with which he brought you, Ibn Abbas said: of worshipping God alone, with no partner, until, when he perished, that is, he died, you said, ‘God will never send after him a messenger,’ that is, you persisted in your disbelief and thought that God would not renew the proof against you, Thus does God send astray he who is a transgressor, a polytheist, doubter, a doubter.
40:35: 35. Those who dispute about the verses of God, Al-Zajjaj said: This is an explanation of the extravagant doubter, meaning they are those who dispute about the verses of God, i.e., in invalidating them by denying them, without authority, an argument, that has come to them, [from God], is most hateful, i.e., that argument is most hateful, “in the sight of God and in the sight of those who believe. Thus does God set a seal upon the heart of every arrogant, tyrant.” Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read heart with the tanween, and the others read it with the addition, and its proof is the reading of Abdullah Ibn Masoud upon the heart of every arrogant, tyrant.
40:36: 36. And Pharaoh said, to his minister, O Haman, build me a tower. A tower is an apparent structure that is not hidden from the observer, even if it is far away. Its origin is from tasreeh, which means to make clear, that I may reach the causes.
40:37: 37. The causes of the heavens, meaning: their paths and doors from one heaven to another, so he looked up to the God of Moses, the general reading is with the raising of the ‘ayn in accordance with his saying: (the most effective causes), and Hafs read from Asim with the lowering of the ‘ayn, which is the reading of Hamid al-A’raj, in response to (perhaps) with the fa’, and I think him, meaning Moses, a liar, in what he says that he has a lord other than me, and thus the evil of his work was made seem good to Pharaoh and he was averted from the path, the people of Kufa and Jacob read: (and averted) with the damma of the sad in accordance with his saying: (made seem good to Pharaoh) Ibn Abbas said: God averted him from the path of guidance. The others read it with the fatha, meaning: Pharaoh averted the people from the path. And the plot of Pharaoh was only in ruin, meaning: And his plot to nullify the signs of Moses was only in loss and destruction
40:38: 38. And he who believed said, 'O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the path of right conduct.' The path of guidance.
40:39: 39. O my people, this worldly life is only a temporary enjoyment, an enjoyment that you benefit from for a period of time, then it ends. And indeed, the Hereafter is the home of settlement, that does not cease.
40:40: 40. “Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except with the like thereof. And whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those will enter Paradise and will be provided for therein without account.” Muqatil said: They will not be held accountable for what they are given in Paradise of goodness.
40:41: 41. O my people, why do I call you to salvation? meaning: What is wrong with you, as you say: Why do I see you sad? That is: What is wrong with you? He says: Tell me about you? How is this situation? I call you to salvation from the Fire by believing in God, and you call me to the Fire? To polytheism that necessitates the Fire. Then he explained and said:
40:42: 42. You call me to disbelieve in God and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, and I call you to the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving, in His revenge on those who disbelieved, the Forgiver of the sins of the people of monotheism.
40:43: 43. There is no doubt, truly, that what you invite me to, meaning, to the idol, has no invitation to it in this world or in the Hereafter. Al-Suddi said: It does not respond to anyone in this world or in the Hereafter, meaning it has no invitation to be answered. It was also said: It has no invitation to its worship in this world because idols do not claim divinity, nor do they call to their worship, and in the Hereafter they disavow their worshippers. And that our return is to God, our return is to God, and He will reward each one according to what he deserves, and that the transgressors, meaning the polytheists, are the companions of the Fire.
40:44: 44. You will remember what I say to you, if you witness the punishment when remembrance will not benefit you, and I entrust my affair to God, that is because they threatened him for disobeying their religion, Indeed, God is Seeing of His servants, He knows who is right from who is wrong. Then the believer came out from among them, and they sought him but were unable to find him.
40:45: 45. And that is the saying of the Almighty: So God saved him from the evil of their plot, [the evil they intended for him], Qatada said: He escaped with Moses and he was a Copt, and the evil of the punishment befell the family of Pharaoh, drowning in this world and the Fire in the Hereafter.
40:47: 47. And when they dispute in the Fire, meaning: O Muhammad, mention to your people when they dispute, meaning the people of Hell in the Fire, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, ‘Indeed, we were your followers,’ in this world, so can you relieve us of a portion of the Fire? The word follower can be singular or plural according to the people of Basra, and its singular is tabi’, while the people of Kufa said: It is a plural that has no singular, and its plural is ibta’a.
40:48: 48. Those who were arrogant said, ‘We are all in it.’ Indeed, God has judged between the servants.
40:49: 49. And those in the Fire will say, when the torment intensified upon them, to the keepers of Hell, ‘Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the torment.’
40:50: 50. They said, meaning the keepers of Hell, Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs? They said, Yes. They said, Then call upon your Lord, meaning you are your Lord. We will not call upon Him for you, because they knew that He would not lighten their punishment. God Almighty said, And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error, meaning: it is invalid and leads astray and does not benefit them.
40:51: 51. The Almighty said: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world. Ibn Abbas said: By force and subjugation. Ad-Dahhak said: By argument, and in the Hereafter by excuse. It was also said: By taking revenge on the enemies in this world and the Hereafter. All of that was for the prophets and the believers, so they are victorious by the argument against those who opposed them. God granted them victory by subjugating those who opposed them and destroying their enemies, and He granted them victory after they were killed by taking revenge on their enemies, just as He granted victory to John, son of Zechariah, when he was killed, killing seventy thousand people. They are victorious in one of these ways. And on the Day when the witnesses will stand, meaning: On the Day of Resurrection, the guardian angels will stand and testify for the messengers that they conveyed the message and against the disbelievers that they denied it.
40:52: 52. The Day when the excuses of the wrongdoers will not benefit them, meaning if they apologize for their disbelief, it will not be accepted from them, and if they repent, it will not benefit them. And for them is the curse, meaning distance from mercy, and for them is the worst home, meaning Hell.
40:53: 53. And We gave Moses the guidance, Muqatil said: Guidance from misguidance, meaning the Torah, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture, [the Torah].
40:54: 54. A guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.
40:55: 55. So be patient, O Muhammad, in their harm. Indeed, the promise of God, to make your religion prevail and destroy your enemies, is true. Al-Kalbi said: The verse on fighting abrogated the verse on patience. And ask forgiveness for your sin, this is an act of worship from God to raise you in degree and to make it a tradition for those who come after you. And exalt [God] with praise of your Lord, may God bless him and grant him peace, thanking your Lord, in the evening and in the morning. Al-Hasan said: He meant the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer. Ibn Abbas said: The five daily prayers.
40:56: 56. Indeed, those who dispute concerning the verses of God without any authority that has come to them - there is in their breasts - what is in their hearts, and the breast is the location of the heart, so it was used as a metaphor for the heart because of the close proximity - nothing but arrogance. Ibn Abbas said: What drives them to deny you is nothing but arrogance and pride in their breasts. They will not attain it. Mujahid said: They will not attain the requirements of that arrogance, because God, the Almighty, will humiliate them. Ibn Qutaybah said: There is nothing in their hearts except arrogance towards Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a desire to defeat him, but they will not achieve that. The commentators said: It was revealed about the Jews, because they said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Our companion, the Messiah, son of David - meaning the Antichrist - will emerge at the end of time, and his authority will spread over land and sea, and he will return the kingdom to us. God Almighty said: So seek refuge in God from the trial of the Antichrist, For He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
40:57: 57. The creation of the heavens and the earth, despite their greatness, is greater, greater in people’s hearts, than the creation of mankind, meaning their resurrection after death, but most of mankind, meaning the disbelievers, do not know, since they do not use this as evidence of the Oneness of their Creator. Some people said: Greater [meaning greater] than the creation of the Antichrist, but most of mankind do not know, meaning the Jews who dispute over the matter of the Antichrist. It was narrated on the authority of Hisham bin Amir that he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Between the creation of Adam and the Day of Resurrection, there is no creation greater than the creation of the Antichrist. Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzar told us, [Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Dabry told us, Abdul Razzaq told us], Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Asma bint Yazid Al-Ansariyyah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in my house and he mentioned the Antichrist, and he said: ‘There are three years before him: one year the sky will withhold a third of its rain and the earth a third of its vegetation; the second year the sky will withhold two-thirds of its rain and the earth two-thirds of its vegetation; the second year the sky will withhold all of its rain and the earth all of its vegetation, so that not a single hoofed or molar animal will remain but will perish. And among his most severe trials is that he will come to a Bedouin and say: ‘If I revive your camels for you, will you not know that I am your Lord?’ He will say: ‘Yes.’ Then he will appear to him like his camels, with the best udders and the largest humps.’ He said: ‘And a man will come whose brother and father have died.’” He said: Tell me, if I bring your father and your brother back to life, do you not know that I am your Lord? He said: Yes. Then the devils appeared to him in the form of his father and his brother. She said: “Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to relieve himself, then he returned and the people were worried and saddened by what he had told them. She said: “He took hold of the flesh of the door and said: ‘Who is Asma?’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, you have dislocated our hearts by mentioning The Antichrist said: If he appears while I am alive, then I will be his opponent. Otherwise, my Lord is my successor over every believer. Asma said: I said: O Messenger of God, by God, we knead dough and do not bake it until we are hungry, so what will happen to the believers on that Day? He said: He will reward them with what rewards the inhabitants of the heavens of glorification and sanctification. And with this chain of transmission he said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of Ibn Khathim, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Asma’ bint Yazid, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Antichrist will remain on earth for forty years. A year will be like a month, a month will be like a week, a week will be like a day, and a day will be like the burning of a palm branch in the fire.” Abu Saeed At-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abd Al-Samad bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Bazzar told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq Al-Dabry told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood among the people and praised God as He deserved, then he mentioned the Antichrist and said: ‘I warn you about him, and there is no prophet but that he warned his people. Noah warned his people, but I will say to you something about him that no prophet said to his people. You know that he is one-eyed, and God is not one-eyed.’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Juwayriyah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Antichrist was mentioned on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “God is not hidden from you. God is not one-eyed,” and he pointed with his hand to his eyes. The Antichrist is one-eyed in his right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir Al-Jurjani told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad Al-Farsi told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Shuaib bin Safwan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umair, on the authority of Rib’i bin Harash, on the authority of Uqba bin Amr bin Mas’ud Al-Ansari, who said: I went with him to Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman. Uqba said to him: Tell me what you heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the Antichrist. He said: ((The Antichrist will emerge and with him will be water and fire. As for what the people see as water, it will be a burning fire. As for what the people see as fire, it will be cool, sweet water. So whoever witnesses that, let him enter that which he sees as fire, for it will be sweet, sweet water.)) Uqba said: I heard it as confirmation of Hudhayfah. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir told me, Al-Walid told us, Ibn Amr - who is Al-Awza’i - told us, Ishaq told us, Anas bin Malik told me, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no city that the Antichrist will not tread upon except Mecca and Medina. There is no pass of it but the angels will be standing in rows guarding it. Then Medina will shake with its people three times, and every disbeliever and hypocrite will come out to him.” Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Messiah will come from the east, and his aim will be Medina, until he descends behind Uhud. Then the angels will turn his face toward Syria, and there he will perish.” Abu Saeed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abd Al-Samad Al-Bazzar told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq Al-Dabry told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Harun Al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Antichrist will be followed by seventy thousand of my nation, wearing shields. Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, narrated it on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: With the Antichrist on that day will be seventy thousand Jews, each of them wearing a crown and an adorned sword.
40:58: 58. The Almighty said: “The blind and the seeing are not alike, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds, nor the evildoer. Little do you remember.” The people of Kufa read you remember with a ta’, while the others read it with a ya’, because the beginning and end of the verses are report about a people.
40:59: 59. The Hour, meaning the Resurrection, is coming, there is no doubt about it, but most people do not believe.
40:61: 61. “It is God who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day to see. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, but most of the people are not grateful.”
40:62: 62. “That is God, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no god except Him. So how are you deluded?”
40:63: 63. Likewise, meaning just as you have been led astray from the truth despite the evidence, those who used to deny the signs of God are deluded.
40:64: 64. It is God who made the earth a resting place for you, a bed, and the sky a canopy, a ceiling like a dome, and shaped you and perfected your shapes, Muqatil said: He created you and perfected your creation. Ibn Abbas said: He created the son of Adam standing upright, eating and taking with his hand, while others take with their mouths. And provided for you from the good things, it was said: other than the provision of the animals. That is God, your Lord, so blessed be God, Lord of the worlds.
40:65: 65. “He is the Ever-Living, there is no god but Him, so call upon Him, devoting your religion to Him alone. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.” Al-Farra’ said: It is a piece of report, and it contains an implied command. Its meaning is: so call upon Him and praise Him. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever says, There is no god but God, should then say, Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. This is what God Almighty said: “So call upon Him, devoting your religion to Him alone. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.”
40:66: 66. Say, ‘Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides God when clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.’ That was when he was called to disbelief.
40:67: 67. “It is He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot. Then He brings you forth as a child,” that is, as children, “then that you may reach your full strength and then that you may become old men. And among you is he who dies before,” that is, before he becomes an old man, and that you may reach, all of you, a specified term, a known, limited time that you do not exceed, meaning the term of life is until death, and that you may understand, that is, so that you may understand the Oneness of your Lord and His power.
40:68: 68. “It is He who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.”
40:69: 69. Have you not seen those who dispute about the verses of God? meaning: the Qur’an, saying: It is not from God. “How are they turned away?” how are they turned away from the true religion? It was said: they are the polytheists. And on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin and a group: that it was revealed about the Qadarites.
40:70: 70. Those who deny the Scripture and that with which We sent Our messengers - they are going to know.
40:71: 71. When the shackles are around their necks and the chains are dragging them. [They are dragging].
40:72: 72. In scalding water, then in the Fire they will be blazing. Muqatil said: The Fire will be lit with them. Mujahid said: They will become fuel for the Fire.
40:73: 73. Then it will be said to them, 'Where were those you used to associate with God?'
40:74: 74. “Other than God”? Meaning the idols. “They said, ‘They have gone astray from us,’ meaning we have lost them so we do not see them. “Rather, we did not call upon anything before.” It was said: They denied it. It was also said: It means, Rather, we did not call upon anything before that could benefit or harm. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: That is, we did not do anything before. That is, our worship of them was lost, just as someone whose work has been lost says: I did not do anything. God the Almighty said: Thus, meaning, just as He led these astray, God leads astray the disbelievers.
40:75: 75. That is the punishment that has befallen you, because you used to rejoice in your arrogance and boasting, on the earth without right and because you used to exult in your arrogance and boasting.
40:76: 76. "Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant."
40:77: 77. “So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is true. Then either We will show you some of what We promise them during your lifetime, or We will take you in death before that happens to them, and to Us they will be returned.”
40:78: 78. And We had certainly sent messengers before you, among them were those We have told you about, their story is in the Qur’an, “and among them were those We have not told you about. And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of God,” by the command and will of God, and when the command of God comes, His judgment between the prophets and the nations, it will be judged with truth, and there the falsifiers will lose.
40:79: 79. It is God who made for you the livestock that you may ride some of them, some of them, and some of them you may eat.
40:80: 80. And you have benefits in them, in their wool, fur, hair, and milk. And that you may accomplish through them a need in your hearts, they carry your burdens from one land to another, and that you may accomplish through them your needs. And upon them and upon the ships you are carried, meaning, on camels on land and on ships at sea. Similar to this is the saying of God Almighty: And We carried them on land and sea (al-Isra’ 17:70).
40:81: 81. And He shows you His signs, the evidence of His power, so which of the signs of God do you deny?
40:82: 82. Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and stronger in power and in traces upon the land. Meaning: their factories and palaces. But what they used to earn did not avail them. It was said that it is in the sense of a question, and its meaning is: What availed them from their earnings?
40:83: 83. So when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced, they were satisfied, with what they had of knowledge. Mujahid said: It is their saying, “We know best. We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished.” This is called knowledge based on what they claim and allege, but in reality it is ignorance. And that which they used to ridicule overtook them.
40:84: 84. So when they saw Our might, they said, ‘We believe in God alone and disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him.’ That is, we disavow what we used to equate with God.
40:85: 85. So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment, Our torment, the way of God. It was said: It is in the accusative case by removing the preposition, meaning: like the way of God. It was also said: it is on the source. It was also said: it is on the temptation, meaning: beware of the way of God, which has already occurred among His servants, and that way is that when they witness the torment of God they believe, and their faith does not benefit them when they witness the torment. And there the disbelievers will lose, by going to both abodes. Al-Zajjaj said: The disbeliever is a loser at all times, but their loss will become clear to them when they see the punishment.
41:2: 2. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Al-Akhfash said: A revelation is the subject, and its predicate is the Almighty’s saying:
41:3: 3. A Book whose verses have been detailed, its verses have been made clear, an Arabic Qur’an for a people who know, the Arabic language. If it had been in a language other than theirs, they would not have known it. And the Qur’an was made accusative by the statement falling upon it, meaning: We explained it as a Qur’an.
41:4: 4. A bearer of good tidings and a warner, two descriptions of the Qur’an, meaning: a bearer of good tidings for the friends of God, and a warner for His enemies. But most of them turned away, and they do not hear, they do not listen to it out of arrogance.
41:5: 5. And they said, meaning the polytheists of Mecca, Our hearts are coverings, in coverings, from that to which you invite us, so we do not understand what you say, and in our ears is deafness, deafness so we do not hear what you say. The meaning is: In our refusal to accept you, we are like someone who does not understand or hear, and between us and you is a veil, a disagreement in religion and a barrier in faith, so we do not agree with what you say. So act, you are on your religion, for we are acting, on our religion.
41:6: 6. “Say, ‘I am only a human being like you,’ meaning like one of you, and were it not for the revelation I would not have called you. This is His statement: “It has been revealed to me that your God is one God.” Al-Hasan said: God taught him humility. So be upright toward Him, direct yourselves toward Him in obedience and do not deviate from His path. And seek His forgiveness, for your sins. And woe to the polytheists.
41:7: 7. "Those who do not give zakat," Ibn Abbas said: Those who do not say there is no god but God, which is the zakat of the souls, and the meaning is: They do not purify themselves from polytheism through monotheism. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: They do not acknowledge zakat, and they do not consider giving it an obligation. It was said: Zakat is the bridge to Islam, so whoever cuts it off will be saved and whoever neglects it will perish. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: They do not spend in obedience nor give charity. Mujahid said: They do not purify their deeds, "and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter."
41:8: 8. Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have a reward uninterrupted. Ibn Abbas said: Uncut. Muqatil said: Undiminished. And from this comes al-manun because it diminishes a person’s reward and strength. And it was said: Undiminished. Mujahed said: It is not counted. Al-Suddi said: This verse was revealed regarding the sick, the elderly, and the decrepit. If they are unable to obey, they will be given a reward equivalent to the best of what they used to do. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Khaythamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If a servant is on a good path of worship, then falls ill, the angel assigned to him is told: Write down for him the same as his deeds when he was free, until I release him or take him to Me.”
41:9: 9. The Almighty said: “Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days,” Sunday and Monday, and attribute to Him rivals? That is the Lord of the worlds.
41:10: 10. And He placed therein, that is, in the earth, firm mountains, “above it,” from above the earth, and blessed it, that is, in the earth, with what He created in it of seas, rivers, trees, and fruits, and determined therein its sustenance, Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: He distributed on the earth the provisions of the servants and the animals. Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: He determined in each land what He did not establish in another, so that some of them might live off one another by trading from one land to another. Al-Kalbi said: He determined bread for the people of one country, corn for the people of another, and fish for the people of another, and so were their sustenance. In four days, meaning He created what is on the earth, and He measured the provisions in two days: Tuesday and Wednesday, so they, along with Sunday and Monday, make up four days. The latter is a response to the former in mention, just as you say: Yesterday I married a woman and today I married two, and one of them is the one I married yesterday. Equal for those who ask, Abu Ja`far read equal in the nominative case, meaning: it is equal. [And Ya`qub read it in the genitive case as a description of his statement: (in four days), and the others read equal] in the accusative case as a source, meaning: it was made equal, meaning: it was made equal, and its meaning is equal for those who ask about that. Qatada and al-Suddi said: Whoever asks about it, then this is the matter, equal, neither more nor less, in answer to whoever asks: In how much time was the earth and provisions created?
41:11: 11. Then He directed Himself to the heaven, meaning: He proceeded to create the heaven, while it was smoke, and that smoke was water vapor, and He said to it and to the earth, ‘Come, willingly or by compulsion,’ meaning: Come to what I command you, meaning: do it, just as one says: Come to what is best, meaning: do it. Tawus said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Bring means give, meaning bring out the benefits that I created in you for the benefit of the servants. [Ibn Abbas said]: God Almighty said: As for you, O sky, raise your sun, moon, and stars, and as for you, O earth, split your rivers and bring forth your fruits and plants. And He said to them: Do what I command you willingly, or I will force you to do it [until you do it unwillingly]. So they answered willingly, and they said, ‘We have come willingly,’ [and He did not say willingly,] because He referred to the heavens and the earth and those in them. Its meaning is: Bring what is in us willingly. So when He described them with the word, He treated them in the plural as those who have reason.
41:12: 12. And He completed them as seven heavens in two days, meaning: He completed them and finished creating them, and revealed in each heaven its command, Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He created in each heaven what He created of angels and what is in it of seas and mountains of hail and what no one knows except God. Qatada and Al-Suddi said: It means that He created in it its sun, moon, and stars. Muqatil said: He revealed to each heaven what he wanted of commands and prohibitions, and that was on Thursday and Friday. And We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps, planets, and as protection, for it. The word protection is in the accusative case as a source, meaning: We preserved it with the planets as protection from the devils who eavesdrop. That, the One Who made it, is mentioned, is the decree of the Almighty, in His kingdom, the All-Knowing, with His protection.
41:13: 13. The Almighty’s saying: But if they turn away, meaning: these polytheists from faith after this explanation, “then say: I have warned you,” meaning I have frightened you, of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ‘Aad and Thamud, meaning: a destruction like their destruction, and the thunderbolt is destructive to everything.
41:14: 14. When there came to them, meaning: ‘Aad and Thamud, the messengers from before them and from behind them, he meant by his saying: from before them the messengers who were sent to their fathers before them, and from behind them, meaning: and after the messengers who were sent to their fathers to whom they were sent, Hud and Salih. So the metaphor in his saying from before them refers to [‘Aad and Thamud] and in his saying: [and from behind them refers to the messengers] that you do not, that you do not, worship except God. They said, If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down, instead of these messengers, angels, meaning: If our Lord had willed to call [the creation], He would have sent down angels, then we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha'labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid Al-Isfahani told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Ubaidi told us, Ahmad bin Majda bin Al-Aryan told us, Al-Hammani told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Al-Dhayyal bin Harmalah, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The notables of the Quraysh and Abu Jahl said: The matter of Muhammad has become confusing to us, so if you were to seek out a man knowledgeable in poetry, divination and magic, he would go to him and speak to him, then he would come to us with an explanation of his matter. Utbah bin Rabi'ah said: By God, I have heard poetry, divination and magic, and I have learned some knowledge of that, and it is not hidden from me whether it is like yours or not. So he went to him, and when he came out to him, he said: O Muhammad, are you better or Hashim? Are you better or Abdul Muttalib? Are you better or Abdullah? Why do you insult our gods and lead our forefathers astray? If you want leadership, we will raise our banners for you, and you will be a leader as long as you live. If you have the means, we will marry you to ten women, from whom you may choose from any of the daughters of Quraysh. If you have the wealth, we will gather for you what will make you and your descendants independent of you after you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent and did not speak. When he finished, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. “Ha Meem. * A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. * A Book whose verses are detailed.” until His saying: But if they turn away, then say, ‘I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ‘Aad and Thamud.’ Utbah held his mouth and implored him by the ties of kinship to return to his family, and did not go out to the Quraysh, so he was detained from them. Abu Jahl said, “O people of Quraysh, by God, we see that Utbah has converted to the religion of Muhammad and has liked his food. This is only because of a need that has befallen him, so let us go to him.” Abu Jahl said, By God, O Utbah, what has kept you from us is that you have converted to the religion of Muhammad and have liked his food. He said, If you have a need, we will gather for you from our wealth what will suffice you without Muhammad’s food. Utbah became angry and swore that he would never speak to Muhammad again, and said, “By God, you know that I am one of the richest people in Quraysh, but I came to him and related the story to him, and he answered me with something. By God, it is neither poetry nor soothsaying nor magic.” He recited the surah until the verse: “But if they turn away, then say, ‘I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ‘Aad and Thamud. ’” Then I held his mouth and implored him by the ties of kinship to desist. You know that when Muhammad says something, he does not lie, so I feared that punishment would descend upon you. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: “I was told that Utbah ibn Rabi’ah was a forbearing master. One day, while he was sitting in the gathering of the Quraysh and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting alone in the mosque, he said: ‘O people of the Quraysh, should I not go to Muhammad and speak to him and present to him matters, perhaps he will accept some of them from us, so we can give him and he will refrain from us?’ That was when Hamzah had converted to Islam and they saw the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, increasing in number and number. They said: ‘Yes, O Abu al-Walid, so go to him and speak to him.’ So Utbah stood up and sat next to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O my nephew, you are one of us, as you know, with your extended clan and position in lineage. You have brought a great matter to your people. You have divided their unity, belittled their wisdom, denigrated their gods, and disbelieved in those of their forefathers who have passed away. So listen to me as I present to you matters for you to consider.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Speak, O Abu al-Walid.’ He said: ‘O my nephew, if you only want wealth with what you have brought, we will gather for you from our wealth until you are the wealthiest of us.’” If you want honor, we will make you our leader. If what you have is something you see and cannot ward off, we will seek medicine for you. Perhaps this is a feeling that has stirred in your chest, for by my life, you, the sons of Abdul Muttalib, are able to do that in a way that no one else is able to do. Then, when he finished, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Have you finished, O Abu al-Walid? He said: Yes. He said: Then listen to me. He said: I will. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. “Ha Meem. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are explained in detail - an Arabic Qur’an.” Then he continued reciting. When Utbah heard it, he listened attentively to him and put his hands behind his back, leaning on them, listening to him until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) reached the prostration. He prostrated, then he said: You have heard, O Abu al-Walid, so it is you and that. Utbah stood up to his companions and some of them said to each other: We swear by God that Abu al-Walid has come to you with a face other than the one with which he left. When he sat down with them, they said: What is behind you, O Abu al-Walid? He said: I have heard a saying, and by God I have never heard anything like it before. It is neither poetry, nor magic, nor divination. O people of Quraysh, obey me. Leave this man alone and stay away from him, for by God, what I heard will be true. If the Arabs defeat him, you will have been spared from him by others, and if he prevails over the Arabs, then his kingdom will be your kingdom and his glory will be your glory, and you will be the luckiest people with him. They said: By God, O Abu al-Walid, he has bewitched you with his tongue. He said: This is my opinion for you, so do as you see fit.
41:15: 15. The Almighty said: As for ‘Aad, they were arrogant upon the land without right and said, ‘Who is stronger than us in strength?’ This is because Hud, peace be upon him, threatened them with punishment, but they said, Who is stronger than us in strength? We are able to ward off the punishment from us by virtue of our strength. They were tall, so God, the Almighty, said in response to them, Did they not see that God, who created them, was stronger than them in strength? And yet they used to deny Our signs.
41:16: 16. So We sent upon them a furious wind, a very loud storm, which is the shout. It was said: It is the cold wind from sarr which is cold, in unlucky days, Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, Abu Amr and Ya’qub read (nahsat) with a sukoon on the ha’, while the others read it with a kasra, meaning: misfortunes and ill-omened misfortunes. Ad-Dahhak said: God withheld rain from them for three years, and the winds continued upon them without rain, that We may make them taste the punishment of disgrace, meaning: the punishment of humiliation and degradation, “in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful,” more severe humiliation, and they will not be aided.
41:17: 17. As for Thamud, We guided them, We called them, said Mujahid, and Ibn Abbas said: We showed them the path of guidance. It was said: We showed them good and evil, like His statement: We showed him the way Al-Insan 3, But they preferred blindness to guidance, so they chose disbelief over faith, so the thunderbolt of punishment seized them, [i.e., the destruction of punishment], humiliation, i.e., of humiliation, i.e., disgrace, which is what humiliates and disgraces them, for what they used to earn.
41:18: 18. And We saved those who believed and were righteous.
41:19: 19. And the Day when the enemies of God will be gathered to the Fire, Nafi’ and Ya’qub read: (We will be gathered) with a noon, (enemies) in the accusative case, and the others read it with a ya’ and raising it and opening the sheen (enemies) in the nominative case, meaning: they will be gathered to the Fire, so they will be distributed, they will be driven and pushed to the Fire, and Qatada and al-Suddi said: The first of them will be held back from the last of them so that they may catch up with each other.
41:20: 20. Until, when they come to it, they come to the Fire, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them, that is, their skins, as to what they used to do. Al-Suddi and a group said: What is meant by skins is the private parts. Muqatil said: Their limbs will speak of what their tongues concealed of their deeds.
41:21: 21. And they will say, meaning the disbelievers who will be herded into the Fire, to their skins, ‘Why did you bear witness against us?’ They will say, ‘God has made us speak, He who makes all things speak.’ The discussion is complete here. And God Almighty said, And He created you the first time, and this is not a response to the skins, and to Him you will be returned.
41:22: 22. And you were not concealing, meaning: concealing [according to most scholars]. Mujahid said: You were fearing God. Qatada said: You thought. that your hearing, your sight, and your skins would testify against you, but you thought that God did not know much of what you do. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hamidi told us, Sufyan told us, Mansur told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Ma’mar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: Two Thaqafis and one Qurayshite, or two Qurayshites and one Thaqafi with much fat in their bellies but little understanding in their hearts, gathered at the Kaaba. One of them said: Do you think that God hears what we say? The other said: He hears if we speak loudly, but He does not hear if we speak quietly. The third said: If He hears when we speak loudly, then He hears if we speak quietly. Then God revealed: “And you were not covering yourself lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins should testify against you. But you thought that God did not know much of what you do.” It was said that the Thaqafi was Abd Yalil, and the two Quraysh men circumcised him: Rabi’ah and Safwan bin Umayya.
41:23: 23. The Almighty said: And that is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord that has ruined you, that is, your assumption that God does not know much of what you do has ruined you. Ibn Abbas said: He has thrown you into the Fire, and you have become among the losers, then He informed us about their state, saying:
41:24: 24. But if they are patient, the Fire will be their abode, a dwelling place for them. But if they seek repentance, they seek to be appeased and ask for forgiveness, they will not be among those who are appeased, satisfied. The one who is appeased is the one whose rebuke is accepted and whose request is answered. It is said: So-and-so appeased me, meaning: he satisfied me after he made me angry. I asked him to appease me: I asked him to appease me, meaning: be satisfied.
41:25: 25. And We have ordained for them, that is, We sent and appointed. Muqatil said: We prepared. Al-Zajjaj said: We caused them to be companions, peers from among the devils until they led them astray. And they made attractive to them what was before them, of the worldly affairs until they preferred it over the Hereafter, and what was behind them, of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and reject the Resurrection. And the word has come into effect against them among nations, [with nations], “that had passed on before them of the jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.”
41:26: 26. And those who disbelieved said, from the polytheists of Quraysh, Do not listen to this Qur’an and speak noisily during it. Ibn Abbas said: He meant, Listen to it noisily. Some of them would advise one another, If you see Muhammad reciting, then oppose him with rajaz poetry and idle talk. Mujahid said: And speak noisily during it with bleating and whistling. Ad-Dahhak said: Speak excessively so that he will confuse what he is saying. As-Suddi said: Shout in his face. “Perhaps you will overcome,” Muhammad in his recitation.
41:27: 27. “Then We will surely make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do in this world, which is associating partners with God.
41:28: 28. That, which I mentioned of the severe punishment, is the recompense of the enemies of God. Then He explained that recompense and said: The Fire, meaning: it is the Fire, for them therein, meaning: in the Fire, is the eternal home, the home of residence from which there is no moving, as recompense for what they used to deny Our signs.
41:29: 29. And those who disbelieved will say, meaning, in the Fire, Our Lord, show us those who led us astray among the jinn and mankind, meaning Iblis and Cain, the sons of Adam who killed his brother because they committed the sin, that we may place them under our feet, in the Fire, that they may be among the lowest, meaning that they may be in the lowest level of the Fire. Ibn Abbas said: So that they may be more severely punished than us.
41:30: 30. The Almighty said: Indeed, those who have said, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remained steadfast, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him was asked about steadfastness, and he said: That you do not associate anything with God. Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said: Righteousness means to adhere to the commands and prohibitions, and not to evade them like a fox. Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him said: Purpose your actions sincerely for the sake of God. Ali may God be pleased with him said: Perform the obligatory duties. Ibn Abbas said: Remain steadfast in performing the obligatory duties. Al-Hassan said: They adhered to the command of God Almighty, so they acted in obedience to Him and avoided disobeying Him. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: They remained steadfast in their testimony that there is no god but God until they met God. Muqatil said: They remained steadfast in knowledge and did not turn back. Qatada said: When Al-Hasan recited this verse, he would say: O God, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness. God the Almighty says: {The angels descend upon them}. Ibn Abbas said: At death. Qatada and Muqatil said: When they rise from their graves. Wakee’ ibn al-Jarrah said: Good tidings are given in three situations: At death, in the grave, and at the resurrection. That you do not fear - of death. Mujahid said: Do not fear for what you will do in the Hereafter. And do not grieve - for what you left behind of family and children, for We will replace you in all of that. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said: Do not fear and do not grieve over your sins, for I will forgive them. And receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised.
41:31: 31. We are your allies, the angels who descend upon them with good tidings say to them: We are your allies, your supporters, and your beloved ones, in this world and in the Hereafter, [meaning: in this world and the Hereafter. Al-Suddi said: The angels say: We are the guardians who were with you in this world, and we are your allies in the Hereafter], they say: We will not leave you until you enter Paradise. And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, of honor and pleasures, and for you therein, in Paradise, is whatever you call for, that is, what you wish for.
41:32: 32. A lodging, a provision, from the Forgiving, the Merciful.
41:33: 33. The Almighty said: And who is better in speech than one who invites to God, to His obedience, and does righteousness and says, ‘Indeed, I am of the Muslims.’ Ibn Sirin Abu al-Suddi and Ibn Abbas said: He is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who invited people to testify that there is no god but God. Al-Hasan said: He is the believer who responded to God’s call, invited people to what He responded to, did righteousness in response to his call, and said, Indeed, I am of the Muslims. Aisha said: I think this verse was revealed about the muezzins. Akrima said: He is the muezzin Abu Umamah al-Bahili. And he did righteous deeds: he prayed two rak’ahs between the call to prayer and the iqamah. Qais bin Abi Hazim said: It is the prayer between the call to prayer and the iqamah. Abu Saeed bin Muhammad bin Al-Abbas Al-Hamidi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Al-Hasan bin Ayoub Al-Tusi told us, Abu Yahya bin Abi Maysarah told us, Abdullah bin Zaid Al-Maqri told us, Kahams bin Al-Hasan told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Buraidah bin Abdullah bin Mughaffal, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Between every two calls to prayer there is a prayer, three times. Then he said on the third time: For whoever wishes. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Zaid Al-Ami, on the authority of Abu Iyas Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah, on the authority of Anas bin Malik. Sufyan said: I do not know of it except that he traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A supplication between the call to prayer and the call to prayer is not rejected.
41:34: 34. The Almighty said: And not equal are the good deed and the bad, Al-Farra’ said: No here is a connective, meaning: Not equal are the good deed and the bad, meaning patience and anger, forbearance and ignorance, forgiveness and harm. Repel evil with that which is better, Ibn Abbas said: He commanded patience when angry, forbearance when ignorant, and forgiveness when harming others. Then he between whom and you there was enmity, meaning: If you do that, your enemy will submit to you, and the one between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend, like a friend and a close relative. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This was revealed about Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, because he relented toward the Muslims after his intense enmity due to the marriage that occurred between him and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then he converted to Islam and became a friend through Islam and a devoted relative.
41:35: 35. And none shall receive it, this quality of repelling evil with good, except those who are patient, in suppressing anger and enduring hardship, and none shall receive it except one of great portion, in goodness and reward. Qatada said: Great portion means Paradise, meaning none shall receive it except one for whom Paradise is obligatory.
41:36: 36. “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing,” of your seeking refuge and your words, the Knowing, of your actions and your conditions.
41:37: 37. The Almighty said: “And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to God, who created them.” He only said: created them in the feminine because he made it in the form of a broken plural, and did not make it in the form of the masculine preponderance over the feminine, if it is Him that you worship.
41:38: 38. But if they are arrogant, about prostrating, then those who are with your Lord, meaning the angels, glorify Him night and day, and they never get tired, they never get tired or slacken.
41:39: 39. And among His signs, evidence of His power, is that you see the earth barren, dry and dusty with no vegetation in it, “but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells. Indeed, He who gives life to it is the Giver of Life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.”
41:40: 40. Indeed, those who blaspheme Our verses, deviate from the truth of Our evidence. Mujahid said: They blaspheme Our verses by whistling, clapping, idle talk, and chattering. Qatada said: They lie about Our verses. Al-Suddi said: They are stubborn and disobedient. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl. “They are not hidden from Us. So is he who is thrown into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?” It was said that it was Hamza, or it was said that it was Uthman. It was also said that it was Ammar ibn Yasir. Do whatever you will, a command of threat and warning. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do, knowing that He will reward you for it.
41:41: 41. Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message, in the Qur’an, when it came to them, then he began to describe the message and left out the answer to Indeed, those who disbelieved, on the assumption that those who disbelieved in the message will be recompensed for their disbelief. It was said that its predicate is His statement afterward: Those will be called from a distant place. “And indeed, it is a noble Book,” Al-Kalbi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: Noble to God. Qatadah said: God Almighty honored it with such honor that falsehood will not find a way to it.
41:42: 42. And it is His statement: Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it. Qatada and Al-Suddi said: Falsehood is Satan, who cannot change it, add to it, or subtract from it. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that it is protected from being diminished, so that falsehood comes to it from before it, or from being increased, so that falsehood comes to it from behind it. Based on this, the meaning of falsehood is: increase and decrease. Muqatil said: No denial will come to it from the books that came before it, and no book will come after it to invalidate it. A revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy. Then he consoled his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for their denial.
68:48: 43. He said: What is said to you, of harm, is only what was said to the messengers before you, meaning: It was said to the prophets and messengers before you: A magician, as it is said to you, and they lied just as you lied. Indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness, for whoever repents and believes in you, and the possessor of painful punishment, for whoever persists in denying. 48- So be patient over the decision of your Lord, be patient with their harm for the sake of your Lord’s judgment, and do not be, in impatience and haste, like the companion of the fish, that is, Jonah, son of Matta, when he called, to his Lord in the belly of the fish, while he was distressed, filled with grief.
41:44: 44. And if We had made it, meaning: We had made this book that he recited to the people, a foreign Qur’an, in a language other than the Arabic language, they would have said, ‘Why are its verses not explained in detail?’ Why were its verses not explained in Arabic so that we could understand them? A foreign language and an Arab? Meaning: A foreign book and an Arab messenger? This is a question of denial, meaning: they would have said: The one to whom it was revealed was Arabic and the one to whom it was revealed was foreign. Muqatil said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to visit Yasar, the servant of Amir ibn al-Hadrami, who was a foreign Jew and was called Abu Fakiha. The polytheists said: Yasar is teaching him. His master hit him and said: You are teaching Muhammad. Yasar said: He is teaching me. Then God Almighty revealed this verse: Say, O Muhammad, It - meaning the Qur’an - is for those who believe a guide and a cure, guidance from misguidance and a cure for what is in the hearts. It was also said: a cure for pain. And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness upon them. Qatada said: They are blind to the Qur’an and deaf to it, so they do not benefit from it. Those are being called from a distant place, meaning: they do not hear or understand, just as someone who is called from a distant place neither hears nor understands. This is an example of how little they benefit from what they are admonished with, as if they are being called from a place where they cannot hear.
41:45: 45. And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but they differed concerning it, some believing and some denying, just as your people differed in Surah Fussilat, your Book. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, delaying the punishment for those who denied the Qur’an, it would have been judged between them, He would have completed their punishment and hastened their destruction. And indeed, they are in doubt about it, about your truthfulness, disturbing, causing them to have doubts.
41:46: 46. “Whoever does righteousness does so for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever does evil does so against it. And your Lord is not unjust to [His] servants.”
41:47: 47. To Him is returned the knowledge of the Hour, meaning: its knowledge, if asked about it, will be returned to Him, and no one else knows it. And no fruits emerge from their coverings, the people of Medina, Syria, and Hafs read it as fruits, in the plural, while the others read it as fruit in the singular, from their coverings, their vessels, the singular of which is kam. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It means the unbeliever before she splits open. And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge, [except with His permission], meaning: the knowledge of the Hour is returned to Him just as the knowledge of fruits and offspring is returned to Him. And the Day He will call to them, God will call to the polytheists, Where are My partners, those whom you claimed were gods, They will say, meaning the polytheists, We have informed you, “We have informed you,” There is not one of us who will bear witness, meaning: no one who will testify that You have a partner. When they witness the punishment, they will disavow the idols.
41:48: 48. And what they used to call upon worship, before in this world, has vanished from them, and they thought became certain, that for them there is no escape escape.
41:49: 49. Man does not grow weary, the unbeliever does not grow weary, of supplication for good, meaning: he continues to ask his Lord for good, meaning money, wealth, and health, but if evil touches him, meaning hardship and poverty, he despairs, of God’s mercy, despairs, of His mercy.
41:50: 50. And if We let him taste mercy from Us, meaning We give him goodness, well-being, and wealth, after a hardship has befallen him, after a hardship and calamity that has befallen him, he will surely say, ‘This is for me,’ meaning, because of my deeds, and I have every right to do this. “And I do not think the Hour will ever occur. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will have with Him the best,” meaning, this disbeliever says: I am not certain of the Resurrection. If the matter is like that, and I am returned to my Lord, I will have with Him the best, meaning, Paradise. Meaning, as He gave me in this world, He will give me in the Hereafter. Then We will surely inform those who disbelieve of what they did, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: We will make them stand up for the evils of their deeds, and We will make them taste a severe punishment.
41:51: 51. And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and withdraws; but if evil touches him, he is one of abundant supplication. Abundant. The Arabs use length and breadth to mean abundance, so it is said: So-and-so prolonged his speech and supplication and turned away, meaning: he increased.
41:52: 52. Say, ‘Have you considered, if this Qur’an is from God and you disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?’ opposing the truth and far from it, meaning: no one is more astray than you.
