41:53: 53. We will show them Our signs in the horizons, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: meaning the dwellings of the past nations. And within themselves, through affliction and disease. Qatada said: In the horizons, meaning: God’s events among the nations, and among themselves on the day of Badr. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Al-Suddi said: In the horizons means the cities that will be conquered by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims. And in themselves means the conquest of Mecca. Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth, meaning the religion of Islam. It was said: The Qur’an is clear to them that it is from God. It was also said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is clear to them that he is supported by God Almighty. Ata and Ibn Zayd said: In the horizons means: the regions of the sky and the earth, from the sun, moon, stars, plants, trees, and rivers, and in themselves from the subtlety of creation and the wonder of wisdom, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord is, over all things, a Witness? Muqatil said: Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord is a witness that the Qur’an is from God Almighty? Al-Zajjaj said: “The meaning of sufficiency here is that God Almighty has provided evidence that is sufficient for you. Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord is a Witness over all things, a Witness from whom nothing is hidden?”
41:54: 54. Indeed, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord, in doubt about the resurrection, Indeed, He encompasses all things, encompassing all things in knowledge.
42:2: 2. "'Ain Qaf", Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl was asked: Why is "Ha Mim 'Ain Qaf not separated and Kah Ya Ain Sad" not separated? He said: Because it is a surah that begins with "Ha Mim, so it is like its counterparts, so Ha Mim is the subject and 'Ain Qaf is its predicate, and because they are two verses, and its sisters such as Kah Ya Ain Sad, Al-Muslim and Al-Ra" are counted as one verse. It was said: Because the people of interpretation did not differ regarding Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad and its sisters, that they are letters of spelling and nothing else, and they differed regarding Ha Meem, so some of them excluded it from the scope of letters and made it a verb, and said: Its meaning is Ha Meem, meaning: He decreed what is to happen. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: H is His forbearance, M is His glory, A is His knowledge, S is His splendor, Q is His power. God swears by them. Shahr bin Hawshab and Ata bin Abi Rabah said: H is a war in which the weak will be honored and the powerful among the Quraysh will be humiliated. M is a kingdom that moves from one people to another. A is an enemy of the Quraysh who targets them. S is evil and will be among them. Q is the power of God that penetrates His creation. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: There is no prophet with a book except that Ha Meem * Ain Sin Qaf was revealed to him. Therefore, he said:
42:3: 3. Thus does He inspire you, Ibn Kathir read is inspired with a fat-ha on the ha’ and his proof is his statement: And it has already been inspired to you and to those before you (al-Zumar 39:65), so according to this reading his statement, God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, [the subject is clear as if it was said: Who inspires? So it was said: God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise]. Others read it as Yuhi with a kasra on the ha, to you and to those before you, God is the Almighty, the Wise. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: He means report of the unseen.
42:4: 4. “To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He is the Most High, the Most Great.”
42:5: 5. The heavens almost burst from above them, meaning: each one bursts above the one below it, due to the polytheists’ saying: (God has taken a son) similar to it in Surah Maryam 19:“And they say, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son.’ You have certainly done a thing outrageous. The heavens almost burst from it.” Maryam 88-90. And the angels exalt [God] with praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on the earth, of the believers, Unquestionably, it is God who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
42:6: 6. And those who take protectors besides Him - God is a Guardian over them, He records their deeds and records them for them in order to reward them for them, and you are not a guardian over them, God did not entrust you with them so that you would be held accountable for them.
42:7: 7. And likewise, as we mentioned, We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur’an that you may warn the Mother of Towns, Mecca, meaning: its people, and those around it, meaning all the villages of the earth, and warn of the Day of Assembly, meaning: warn them of the Day of Assembly, which is the Day of Resurrection when God will gather the first and the last, the people of the heavens and the people of the earths, there is no doubt about it, there is no doubt that the assembly will take place, and then after the assembly they will disperse. A party will be in Paradise and a party will be in the Blaze. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Khasmadi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Abu Uthman Saeed bin Uthman Al-Tanukhi told us, Bishr bin Bakr told us, Saeed bin Uthman told me on the authority of Abu Al-Zaher, Jarir bin Kurayb told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-As. Al-Tha’labi said: Abu Abdullah bin Fanjuwayh Al-Daynuri told us, Abu Bakr bin Malik Al-Qati’i told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Laith told us, Abu Qabil Al-Ma’afari told me on the authority of Shafi Al-Asbahi on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us one day, holding his hands and with him two books, and he said: Do you know what these two books are? We said: No, O Messenger of God. He said to the one in his right hand: This is a book from the Lord of the Worlds in which are the names of the people of Paradise and the names of their fathers and their clans and their number before they settle as sperm in the loins, and before…” They settle as sperm in the wombs while they are in the clay, intertwined, so there is nothing more in them or less in them. This is a summary from God for them until the Day of Resurrection. [Then he said to the one on his left: This is a book from the Lord of the Worlds in which are the names of the people of Hell and the names of the people of Hell and the names of their fathers and their clans and their number before they settle as sperm in the loins, and before they settle as sperm in the wombs while they are in the clay, intertwined, so there is nothing more in them or less in them. This is a summary from God for them until the Day of Resurrection.] Abdullah ibn Amr said: Then what is the point of working, O Messenger of God? He said: Work, strive hard, and draw near, for the inhabitant of Paradise will be sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, no matter what deeds he does. And the inhabitant of Hell will be sealed with the deeds of the people of Hell, no matter what deeds he does. Then he said: A group in Paradise is a bounty from God, and a group in the Blaze is justice from God, the Almighty.
42:8: 8. The Almighty said: And if God had willed, He could have made you one nation. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: On one religion. Muqatil said: On the religion of Islam, as the Almighty said: And if God had willed, He could have gathered them together upon guidance (Al-An`am: 35), But He admits whom He wills into His mercy, into the religion of Islam, and the wrongdoers, the disbelievers, will have no protector, to ward off the punishment from them, nor helper, to prevent them from the Fire.
42:9: 9. Or have they taken, [rather, they have taken, i.e., the disbelievers], besides Him, [i.e., besides God], protectors? But God is the Protector, [Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said]. Your protector, O Muhammad, and the protector of those who follow you, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
42:10: 10. And whatever you differ over, of religious matters, its judgment is with God, He will decide and rule on the Day of Resurrection with the decisive decision that removes doubt. That is God, He is the One who will judge between the differing ones. My Lord, in Him I have relied, and to Him I turn.
42:11: 11. "The Creator of the heavens and the earth has made for you mates from among yourselves," like your creation, wives. It was said that He only said (from among yourselves) because He created Eve from Adam's rib. "And of the grazing livestock, mates," different kinds, males and females. "He multiplies you, creates you, in it," meaning in the womb. It was also said that it was in the stomach. It was also said that it was in this manner of creation. Mujahid said: generation after generation of people and grazing livestock. It was also said that (in) has the meaning of the preposition "with," meaning that He multiplies you thereby. It was also said that it means that He multiplies you through marriage. "There is nothing like Him, (like) is a relative clause, meaning that He is not like anything, so the word like was introduced for emphasis, like His statement, If they believe in the like of that which you believe in" Al-Baqarah 2:137. It was also said that the preposition "kaf" is a relative clause, meaning that there is nothing like Him. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said that it has no equivalent. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
42:12: 12. To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth, the keys to sustenance in the heavens and the earth. Al-Kalbi said: rain and plants. He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it, because the keys to sustenance are in His hand, Indeed, He is Knowing of all things.
42:13: 13. The Almighty said: He has ordained for you of religion, He explained and prescribed for you, what He enjoined upon Noah, who was the first of the prophets of the Sharia. Mujahid said: We have enjoined upon you and him, O Muhammad, one religion. And that which We have revealed to you, of the Qur’an and the laws of Islam, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus, and they differed regarding the interpretation of the verse: Qatada said: The permissibility of what is permissible and the prohibition of what is prohibited. Al-Hakam said: The prohibition of mothers, daughters, and sisters. Mujahid said: God did not send a prophet without commanding him to establish prayer, pay zakat, and acknowledge God by obeying Him. This is His religion that He legislated for them. It was said: It is monotheism and disavowal of polytheism. It was also said: It is what was mentioned after, which is His statement: Establish the religion and do not be divided therein. God sent all the prophets to establish the religion, harmony and unity, and to abandon division and opposition. The polytheists find hard what you call them to, of monotheism and rejection of idols. Then He said: God chooses for Himself whomever He wills, selects for Himself from among His servants whomever He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back, who accepts His obedience.
42:14: 14. And they did not become divided, meaning the people of different religions. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: It means the People of the Book as mentioned in Surat Al-Munfikin. Except after knowledge had come to them, that division is misguidance, but they did that, out of envy among themselves, that is, out of envy. Ata' said: It means envy among themselves against Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, delaying the punishment for them, until a specified term, which is the Day of Resurrection, it would have been judged between them, between those who believed and those who disbelieved, meaning the punishment would have been brought down on the deniers in this world. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture, meaning the Jews and Christians, after them, after their prophets. It was also said: after the nations that had passed away. Qatadah said: It means before them, meaning before the polytheists of Mecca. There is disquieting doubt about it, meaning about Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him).
42:15: 15. So call to that, that is, to that, as one says, I called to so-and-so and so-and-so, and this is a reference to what the prophets recommended regarding monotheism, and stand firm as you have been commanded, that is, adhere to the religion that you have been commanded to follow, and do not follow their inclinations and say, ‘I have believed in what God has revealed of the Book,’ that is, I have believed in all of God’s books, and I have been commanded to be just between you, [to be just between you]. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, said: I have been commanded not to be unjust to you with more than what God has enjoined upon you of rulings. It was said: To be just between you in all circumstances and things, “God is our Lord and your Lord. To us are our deeds, and to you are your deeds,” meaning: Our God is one, even if our deeds differ, so everyone will be rewarded according to his deeds, there is no argument, no dispute, between us and you, abrogated by the verse on fighting. So if he was not commanded to fight and was commanded to call to Islam, there would be no dispute between him and those who do not respond, God will gather us together, in the afterlife to separate the judgment, and to Him is the final destination.
42:16: 16. And those who dispute about God, they dispute about the religion of God Almighty and His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Qatada said: They are the Jews who said: Our book came before your book, and our prophet came before your prophet, so we are better than you. This is their dispute. After people responded to him, [i.e., responded to him] and converted to Islam and entered his religion because of the appearance of his miracle, their argument is invalid, their dispute is false, with their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment, in the Hereafter.
42:17: 17. God is He who sent down the Book in truth and the Balance. Qatada, Mujahid, and Muqatil said: Justice is called a Balance because the Balance is an instrument of fairness and equality. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: God the Almighty commanded us to fulfill our obligations and forbade us from cheating. And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. He did not say near because its feminine form is not real, and its metaphor is: time. Al-Kisa’i said: Its coming is near. Muqatil said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned the Hour while some polytheists were with him. They said, in denial: When will the Hour be?
42:18: 18. So God revealed this verse: Those who do not believe in it urge it on, thinking that it will not come. But those who believe are fearful, that is, afraid, of it and know that it is the truth, that it will come without a doubt. Unquestionably, those who dispute, that is, quarrel, and it was said that doubt and suspicion enter them, about the Hour are in extreme error.
42:19: 19. The Almighty said: God is Kind to His servants. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: He is merciful to them. Ikrimah said: He is good to them. As-Suddi said: He is gentle. Muqatil said: He is kind to the righteous and the wicked as He does not destroy them with hunger because of their sins. This is indicated by His statement: He provides for whom He wills Al-Baqarah 2:212. Everyone whom God provides for, whether a believer, a disbeliever, or someone with a soul, is among those whom God wills to provide for. Ja'far as-Sadiq said: Kindness in provision is from two aspects: The first is that He made your provision from good things, and the second is that He did not give it to you all at once. And He is the Strong, the Exalted in Might.
42:20: 20. Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, harvest in the language means earning, meaning: whoever desires the Hereafter through his work, We will increase for him his harvest, by multiplying it by ten to whatever increase God wills. And whoever desires the harvest of this world, meaning through his work this world, We will give him thereof, Qatada said: meaning: We will give him according to what God has allotted for him, as He said: We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend Al-Isra’ 17:18. And he will have no share in the Hereafter, because he did not work for the Hereafter. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Bilal told us, Abu al-Azhar Ahmad ibn Mani’ al-Abdi told us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Faryabi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Abu al-Aliya, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Give this nation good tidings of glory, elevation, victory, and empowerment on earth. Whoever among them works for the Hereafter for the sake of this world will have no share in the Hereafter.”
42:21: 21. The Almighty said: Or have they partners who have prescribed for them a religion which God has not permitted? Meaning the infidels of Mecca. He said: Or have they gods who have prescribed for them a religion which God has not permitted? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: They prescribed for them a religion other than the religion of Islam. And had it not been for the decisive word, had it not been for God’s ruling in the decisive word between creation to delay the punishment for them until the Day of Resurrection, where He said: Rather, the Hour is their appointed time (al-Qamar 54:46), it would have been decided between them, would have ended the punishment of those who deny you in this world, and indeed, the wrongdoers, the polytheists, will have a painful punishment, in the Hereafter.
42:22: 22. You will see the wrongdoers - the polytheists - on the Day of Resurrection, fearful and fearful, of what they have earned and it will befall them - the recompense for what they have earned will befall them. “And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise, having whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.”
42:23: 23. That is what, I mentioned of the delights of Paradise, God gives good tidings to His servants who have believed and done righteous deeds, for they are its people. Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for my relatives.’ Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Maisarah, who said: I heard Tawus on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he was asked about His statement: Except for the love of kinship, Saeed bin Jubair said: The kinship of the family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: You are hasty. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not have a clan of Quraysh except that there was kinship among them. So he said: Except that you maintain the kinship between me and you. Likewise, Al-Sha'bi and Tawus narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Except for the love of kinship, meaning: that you should preserve my kinship, show me affection, and maintain the ties of kinship. This is the view held by Mujahid, Qatadah, Ikrimah, Muqatil, Al-Suddi, and Ad-Dahhak, may God be pleased with them. Ikrimah said: I do not ask you for any reward for what I call you to, except that you protect my kinship between me and you, and it is not as the liars say. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the meaning of the verse: Except that you love God and draw near to Him by obeying Him. This is the statement of Al-Hasan, who said: It is drawing near to God, meaning: Except drawing near to God and drawing near to Him by obedience and righteous deeds. Some of them said: Its meaning is unless you love my relatives and my family and protect me among them, and this is the saying of Saeed bin Jubair and Amr bin Shuaib. They differed about his kinship. It was said: They are Fatima, Ali, and their children, and it was revealed about them: God only desires to remove from you the impurity, O people of the House (al-Ahzab 33:33). It was narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Hayyan, on the authority of Zaid ibn Arqam, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of God and my family. I remind you of God regarding my family.” It was said to Zaid ibn Arqam: Who are the people of his family? He said: They are the family of Ali, the family of Aqeel, the family of Ja’far, and the family of Abbas. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Abdul Wahhab told us, Khalid told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Waqid, who said: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of Abu Bakr, who said: Watch Muhammad in his family. It was said: They are those from among his relatives who are forbidden from receiving charity and the fifth is divided among them, and they are Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, who did not disperse in the pre-Islamic period or in Islam. Some people said: This verse is abrogated and was revealed in Mecca, and the polytheists were harming the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so God revealed this verse and commanded them to love the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and maintain kinship ties. When he migrated to Medina and the Ansar sheltered him and supported him, God Almighty wanted to join him with his brothers among the prophets (peace be upon them), as they said: “And I do not ask you for any reward for it. My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.” (Ash-Shu’ara’: 109). So God, the Most High, revealed: “Say: ‘No reward do I ask of you for it. It is only from God.’” So it was abrogated by this verse and by His statement: “Say: ‘I do not ask you for it any reward, and I am not of the pretenders.’” (al-Zumar 39:86), and other verses. This is the view of Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim and Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl. This is an unacceptable statement, because loving the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, refraining from harming him, loving his relatives, drawing closer to God through obedience, and doing good deeds are among the obligations of religion. These are the statements of the early Muslims regarding the meaning of the verse, so it is not permissible to resort to abrogating any of these things. His saying: (Except for the love of kinship) is not an exception connected to the beginning so that it would be a reward in return for carrying out the message, rather it is discontinuous, and its meaning is: But I remind you of the love of kinship and I remind you of my kinship to you, as we narrated in the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam: (I remind you of God in my family). The Almighty said: And whoever does a good deed - We will increase for him good therein, meaning: whoever increases his obedience, We will increase for him good therein by doubling it. Indeed, God is Forgiving, of sins, Appreciative, of even a little, until He multiplies it.
42:24: 24. Or do they say, or rather they say, meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, “He has fabricated a lie against God. If God wills, He will seal your heart.” Mujahid said: He will bind your heart with patience so that you will not be burdened by their harm, and their saying that he is a fabricator, Qatadah said: He will seal your heart so that you will forget the Qur’an and what He has given you. So he informed them that if he had fabricated a lie against God, He would have done to him what He informed about in this verse. Then he began by saying: And God erases falsehood. Al-Kisa’i said: There is an inversion of the meaning: And God erases falsehood. It is in the nominative case, but the waw was deleted from it in the Qur’an according to the wording, just as it was deleted from His statement: And man will call Al-Isra’ 11 and We will call the guards Al-Alaq 18. He informed that what they say is falsehood, and that God will erase it, and establish the truth with His words, meaning Islam, through what He revealed in His Book. God did that, so He erased their falsehood and elevated the word of Islam, He is Knowing of that within the breasts. Ibn Abbas said: When the verse: Say, ‘I do not ask of you any reward for it except love for the relatives’ was revealed, something of it occurred in the hearts of some people, and they said that he wants to urge us against his relatives after him. Then Gabriel came down and informed him that they had accused him, and he revealed this verse. The people said: O Messenger of God, we testify that you are truthful. So he revealed:
42:25: 25. And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: He means His friends and those who obey Him. It was said that repentance is abandoning sins in intention and action, and turning to obedience in intention and action. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Repentance is moving from reprehensible states to praiseworthy actions. And He pardons misdeeds, if they repent. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Yahya bin Hammad told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara bin Umair, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Suwaid, who said: I entered upon Abdullah to visit him, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than a man – I think he said: [in a] deadly wilderness with his mount, on which is his food and drink. He got off and slept, then woke up and found his mount lost, so he walked around on it until he was overcome by thirst, then he said: I will return to where my mount was so I can die on it. So he went back and dozed off, then woke up and found it next to him, on which was his food and drink.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Al-Sabah and Zuhair bin Harb told us: Umar bin Yunus told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Ishaq bin Abi Talhah told us, Anas bin Malik, his uncle, told me: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God is more pleased with the repentance of His servant when he repents to Him than one of you who was on his mount in a desert and it slipped away from him with his food and drink on it. He despaired of finding it and went to a tree and lay down in its shade, having despaired of finding his mount. While he was like that, it was standing next to him. He took hold of its reins and said out of intense joy: ‘O God, You are my servant and I am your Lord.’ He made a mistake out of intense joy.” And He pardons misdeeds He erases them if they repent. And He knows what you do. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read ta-fa’alun with a ta’, and they said: It is addressed to the polytheists. The others read it with a ya’ because it is between two reports about a people, so He said: Before it about His servants, and after it, and He increases them from His bounty.
42:26: 26. And He responds to those who believe [i.e., He answers those who believe], and does righteous deeds, when they call upon Him. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “And He rewards those who believe. “And increases them from His bounty,” in addition to the reward for their deeds, as a favor from Him. Abu Salih said on his authority: He allows them to intercede for their brothers, and increases them from His bounty. He said: In the brothers of their brothers. “And for the disbelievers is a severe punishment.”
42:27: 27. And if God were to expand the provision for His servants, Khabbab bin Al-Arat said: This verse was revealed about us, and that is because we looked at the wealth of Banu Qurayzah, Banu Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa’ and desired it, so God, the Almighty, revealed this verse: And if God were to expand the provision God expanded the provision for His servants, “they would transgress,” they would transgress and act insolently, in the land. Ibn Abbas said: Their transgression is their seeking of one position after another, one mount after another, and one garment after another. But He sends down, their provisions, in measure as He wills, as He wills with regard to His servants, for He is, of His servants, Knowing and Seeing. Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Salihi told us, Abu Omar Bakr bin Muhammad Al-Muzni told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Abdullah, the grandson of Al-Abbas bin Hamza, told us, Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl Al-Bajali told us, Abu Hafs Omar bin Saeed Al-Dimashqi told us, Sadaqah told us, on the authority of Abdullah, Hisham Al-Kinani told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Gabriel, on the authority of God Almighty, who said: ((God Almighty says: Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine has declared war on Me. I become angry on behalf of My friends as a fierce lion becomes angry. My believing servant does not draw near to Me by doing what I have made obligatory upon him. My believing servant continues to draw near to Me by performing voluntary acts until I love him. When I love him, I become his hearing, sight, tongue, hand, and supporter. If he calls upon Me, I answer him, and if he asks Me, I give him. I do not hesitate about anything I do as I hesitate in taking the soul of My believing servant. He hates death, and I hate to offend him, but he cannot do without it. And among My believing servants is he who asks Me for a door of worship, so I restrain him from it until “No self-admiration will enter him and spoil it. And among My believing servants is he whose faith is not sound except by wealth, and if I were to impoverish him, that would spoil him. And among My believing servants is he whose faith is not sound except by poverty, and if I were to enrich him, that would spoil him. And among My believing servants is he whose faith is not sound except by health, and if I were to make him sick, that would spoil him. And among My believing servants is he whose faith is not sound except by sickness, and if I were to make him healthy, that would spoil him. Indeed, I manage the affairs of My servants with My knowledge of their hearts. Indeed, I am Knowing and Acquainted.”
42:28: 28. The Almighty’s statement: And it is He who sends down the rain, meaning the rain, after they have despaired, meaning: after people have lost hope in it, and that is more likely to make them feel grateful. Muqatil said: God withheld rain from the people of Mecca for seven years until they despaired, then God sent down the rain and reminded them of His blessings, and spreads His mercy, extends His rain, as He said: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy. (al-A’raf 7:75) And He is the Protector, for those who obey Him, the Praiseworthy, with His creation.
42:29: 29. “And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed throughout them of creatures. And He is able to gather them together when He wills.” Meaning: the Day of Resurrection.
42:30: 30. And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read bi ma kasabtu without the fa, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an. Whoever deletes the fa makes the ma at the beginning of the verse mean what struck you because of what your hands have earned. And He pardons much. Al-Hasan said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, no stick scratches you, no foot stumbles, and no vein twitches except for a sin. And what God pardons is more.” Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi narrated to us, Abu Abdullah bin Fanjuwayh told me, Abu Bakr bin Malik Al-Qat’i told us, Bishr bin Musa Al-Asadi told us, Khalaf bin Al-Walid told us, Marwan bin Mu’awiyah told us, Al-Azhar bin Rashid Al-Bahili told me, on the authority of Al-Khidr bin Al-Qawwas Al-Bajali, on the authority of Abu Sakhila, who said: Ali bin Abi Talib said: Shall I not tell you of the best verse in the Book of God, the Almighty, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us? “And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned. But He pardons much.” He said: I will explain it to you, Ali: “Whatever strikes you of illness, punishment, or affliction in this world is for what your hands have earned. God is too Generous to repeat the punishment for them in the Hereafter. And whatever He pardons you in this world - God is too Forbearing to return after His pardon.” Ikrimah said: There is no calamity that befalls a servant except for a sin that God would not have forgiven him except for it, or a degree that God would not have reached except for it. 7- So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it.
42:31: 31. And you will not cause failure, that is, you will not be able to tempt, on earth, that is, you will not cause failure to Me wherever you are, nor will you outrun Me, and you will have besides God no protector or helper.
42:32: 32. 31. The Almighty said: And among His signs are the ships, meaning: the ships, the singular of which is jāriyyah, which is moving, in the sea like mountains, meaning: the mountains, [Mujahid said: palaces, and the most beautiful of them is a flag], and Al-Khalil bin Ahmad said: Everything that is high is a flag among the Arabs.
42:33: 33. If He wills, He can still the wind, which it blows, so they will remain, meaning: the ships, still, fixed, on its back, meaning on the back of the sea that does not flow, Indeed in that are signs for every patient, grateful person, meaning: for every believer, because the characteristic of the believer is patience in hardship and gratitude in prosperity.
42:34: 34. Or He destroys them, that is, He ruins them and drowns them, for what they have earned, that is, for what its riders have earned of sins, and pardons many, of their sins [so He does not punish them for them].
42:35: 35. And He knows. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read: And He knows with the mim raised as a new sentence, like the Almighty’s statement in Surat Bara’ah: And God turns in mercy to whom He wills. (al-Tawbah 9:15). The others read it with the nasb as a declension, and the jussive mood when something conjoined is diverted from it is the accusative mood, and it is like the Almighty’s statement: And He knows the patient. (Al Imran 3:142). He diverted the jussive mood to the accusative mood, belittling and disliking the succession of the jussive moods. Those who dispute about Our verses will have no escape. That is, those who deny the Qur’an will know when they turn to God after the resurrection that they will have no escape from God’s punishment.
42:36: 36. Whatever you have been given of anything, [of the worldly luxuries], is but the enjoyment of worldly life, not the provisions of the Hereafter, and what is with God, [of the reward], is better and more lasting for those who have believed and put their trust in their Lord, in which it is clear that the believer and the disbeliever are equal in that this world is but a brief enjoyment for them to enjoy, but when they reach the Hereafter, what is with God is better for the believer.
42:37: 37. And those who avoid the major sins, Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read: (major sin) in the singular form here and in Surat An-Najm. The others read: (major sins) in the plural form. We have already mentioned the meaning of major sins in Surat An-Nisa. And immoralities, As-Suddi said: It means adultery. Mujahid and Muqatil said: What warrants the prescribed punishment. And when they become angry, they forgive, they are patient, suppress their anger, and overlook.
42:38: 38. And those who responded to their Lord, responded to what He called them to of obedience, and established prayer and their affair is [determined by] consultation among themselves, they consult about what seems best to them and do not rush, and spend from what We have provided them.
42:39: 39. And those who, when they are wronged, injustice and aggression, take revenge, they take revenge on their oppressors without transgressing. Ibn Zayd said: God divided the believers into two categories: One category pardons their oppressors, so He began by mentioning them, which is His statement: (And when they become angry, they forgive), and one category takes revenge on their oppressors, and they are the ones mentioned in this verse. Ibrahim said in this verse: They hated to be humiliated, but when they were able, they pardoned. Ata’ said: They are the believers whom the infidels expelled from Mecca and oppressed them, then God empowered them on earth until they were victorious over those who oppressed them. Then God mentioned the victory and said:
42:40: 40. And the recompense for an evil act is an evil act like it: [The recompense is called an evil act] even if it is not evil because they are similar in form. Muqatil said: It means retaliation for wounds and blood. Mujahed and Al-Suddi said: It is the response to the ugly person. If he says: May God disgrace you, you say: May God disgrace you. And if he insults you, insult him in the same way without transgressing. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: I asked Sufyan al-Thawri, “What is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: ‘The recompense for an evil act is an evil act like it’?” He said: That a man insults you and you insult him, or that he does something to you and you do something to him. But I did not find anything in his statement, so I asked Hisham ibn Hujairah about this verse. He said: If someone injures you, retaliation is due from him, but it does not mean that he insults you and you insult him. Then he mentioned forgiveness, saying: But whoever pardons, the one who wronged him, “and makes peace,” by forgiving between himself and his wrongdoer, his reward is due from God. Al-Hasan said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: Whoever has a reward from God, let him stand. No one will stand except the one who pardoned. Then he recited this verse: Indeed, He does not like the wrongdoers. Ibn Abbas said: Those who initiate wrongdoing.
42:41: 41. And whoever retaliates after being wronged, meaning after the wrongdoer has wronged him, they, meaning the victorious ones, will have no blame upon them, with regard to punishment or accountability.
42:42: 42. The path is only against those who wrong people - they begin with injustice, and transgress upon the earth without right - they commit sins therein. For them is a painful punishment.
42:43: 43. But whoever is patient and forgives, but does not retaliate, that, patience and forgiveness, is for him who is determined in matters, their right and firmness. Muqatil said: It is among the matters that God has commanded. Al-Zajjaj said: The patient will be rewarded for his patience, so the desire for reward is more complete in determination.
42:44: 44. And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no protector after Him, meaning he has no one to guide him after God has sent him astray and protect him from God’s punishment. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, on the Day of Resurrection, saying, ‘Is there any way back?’ They ask to return to this world.
42:45: 45. And you will see them exposed to it, meaning, the Fire, humbled, humbled, from humiliation, looking from a hidden corner, hidden because of the humiliation upon them. They steal glances at the Fire out of fear of it and humiliation in themselves. It was said that from means with, meaning with a hidden, weak corner out of humiliation. It was also said that He said from a hidden corner because he does not open his eye, but rather looks with part of it. It was also said that its meaning is that they look at the Fire with their hearts because they will be gathered blind, and looking with the heart is hidden. And those who believed will say, ‘Indeed, the losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection,’ It was said that they lost themselves by going to the Fire, and their families by going to someone else in Paradise. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers will be in an enduring punishment.
42:46: 46. “And they had no protectors to help them other than God. And he whom God sends astray has no way.” A path to the truth and to attaining the truth in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. The path to goodness has been closed to them.
42:47: 47. Respond to your Lord, respond to the caller of God, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before there comes a Day from God that no one can repel, which no one will be able to repel, and that is the Day of Resurrection. You will have no refuge, to which you can resort, that Day, and you will have no denier, from anyone who can denounce you.
42:48: 48. But if they turn away, from answering, “then We have not sent you over them as a guardian. Upon you,” upon you is nothing but the notification. And indeed, when We let a person taste mercy from Us, Ibn Abbas said: meaning wealth and health, “he rejoices in it. But if evil befalls them,” meaning drought, for what their hands have put forth, then indeed, man is ungrateful, meaning: when God bestows upon him a blessing, he forgets and denies all the blessings that came before him at the first hardship.
42:49: 49. To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and He has the right to dispose of them as He wills. “He creates what He wills. He gives to whom He wills female [children],” so He will not have a male child. It has been said that it is a woman’s good fortune to have a female child first before a male child, because God Almighty began with female children. And He gives to whom He wills males, so He will not have a female child.
42:50: 50. Or He pairs them, males and females, that is, He brings them together so that both males and females are born to him, And He makes whom He wills barren, so that he does not give birth and no children are born to him. It was said: This is about the prophets, peace be upon them. He gives to whom He wills females, meaning: Lot did not give birth to a male, but rather two daughters were born to him. And He gives to whom He wills males, meaning: Abraham, peace be upon him, did not give birth to a female. Or He pairs them, males and females, meaning: Muhammad, peace be upon him, had sons and daughters born to him. And He makes whom He wills barren, meaning: John and Jesus, peace be upon them, did not give birth to children. This is by way of example, and the verse is general and applies to all people. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.
42:51: 51. The Almighty said: And it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation, that is, the Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Will you not speak to God and look at Him, if you are a prophet, as Moses spoke to him and looked at Him? He said: Moses did not look at God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God, may God bless him and grant him peace, revealed: And it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation, revealed to him in a dream or by inspiration, or from behind a veil, so that he hears His words but does not see them, as Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to him, or that He sends a messenger, either Gabriel or another of the angels, who reveals, by His permission, whatever He wills, meaning that the messenger reveals to the one to whom he is sent, by God’s permission, whatever he wills. Nafi` read: or sends with the lam raised as a starting point, and reveals with the ya’ silent. The others read it with the lam and the ya’ in the accusative case in apposition to the place of revelation because its meaning is: It is not for a human being that God should speak to him except that He reveals to him or sends a messenger. He is Exalted and Wise.
42:52: 52. And thus, that is, as We revealed to all of Our Messengers, We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command, Ibn Abbas said: Prophethood. Al-Hasan said: Mercy. Al-Suddi and Muqatil said: Revelation. Al-Kalbi said: A Book. Al-Rabi’ said: Gabriel. Malik ibn Dinar said: meaning the Qur’an. You did not know, before the revelation, what the Book was and what faith was, meaning the laws and landmarks of faith. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah said: Faith in this context means prayer, and its evidence is the Almighty’s statement: And God would never let your faith go to waste Al-Baqarah 2:143. The scholars of the principles of jurisprudence agree that the prophets, peace be upon them, were believers before the revelation, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, worshipped God before the revelation according to the religion of Abraham, and the laws of his religion were not made clear to him. But We made it a light, Ibn Abbas said: meaning faith. Al-Suddi said: meaning the Qur’an. We guide with it means We direct with it, whoever We will of Our servants, and indeed, you guide meaning you call, to a straight path, meaning Islam. 38- The Day the Spirit will stand, meaning on that day, and the angels will stand in rows, and they differed about this Spirit. Al-Sha’bi and Al-Dahhak said: It is Gabriel. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Spirit is an angel among the angels. God has not created a creature greater than him. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will stand alone in a row, and all the angels will stand in a single row, so the greatness of his creation will be like theirs. On the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: The Spirit is an angel greater than the heavens, the mountains, and the angels. He is in the fourth heaven. He glorifies God twelve thousand times every day. From each glorification, an angel is created who will come on the Day of Resurrection in a row alone. Mujahid, Qatada, and Abu Saleh said: The spirit was created in the image of the children of Adam. They are not people who stand in a row while the angels stand in a row. These are an army and those are an army. Mujahid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They were created in the image of the sons of Adam, and no angel descends from the sky except that one of them is with him. Al-Hasan said: They are the children of Adam. Qatada narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he said: This is one of the things that Ibn Abbas kept secret. And the angels in rows. Al-Sha’bi said: They are the two rows of the Lord of the Worlds. On the Day when He will stand, there will be a row of the spirit and a row of angels. They do not speak except he whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is right, in this world, meaning truly. It was also said: He said: There is no god but God.
42:53: 53. “The path of God to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to God do all matters return,” meaning: the affairs of all creation in the Hereafter.
43:2: 2. And the clear Book, I swear by the Book that clarifies the path of guidance from the path of misguidance, and clarifies what the nation needs of the Sharia.
43:3: 3. Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur’an that you might understand. His statement, We made it, means: We made the recitation of this book Arabic. It was also said: We explained it. It was also said: We named it. It was also said: We described it. It is said: So-and-so made Zayd the most knowledgeable of people, meaning he described him. This is like the statement of God the Most High: And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females (al-Zukhruf 43:19) and His statement: They have divided the Qur’an into parts (Az-Hijr: 91), and He said: Have you made the giving of drink to the pilgrims? (al-Tawbah 9:19), all of which have the meaning of description and naming.
43:4: 4. And indeed, it, meaning the Qur’an, is in the Mother of the Book, in the Preserved Tablet. Qatada said: The Mother of the Book is the origin of the Book, and the mother of everything is its root. Ibn Abbas said: The first thing that God created was the pen, and He commanded it to write what He wanted to create, so the book is with it. Then he recited: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, so the Qur’an is confirmed with God in the Preserved Tablet, as He said: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, in a Preserved Tablet (al-Buruj 85:21). High and Wise, Qatada said: It is informing of its status and honor, meaning: If you deny the Qur’an, O people of Mecca, then it is with us, high, noble, and secure from falsehood.
43:5: 5. Shall We turn away from you the Reminder? It is said: I turned away from it or I turned away from it if you left it and refrained from it. Pardon is the source of their saying I turned away from it if you turned away from it, and that is by turning your face [and neck] to it. What is meant by reminder is the Qur'an. Its meaning is: Shall We leave the revelation from you and refrain from sending down the Qur'an, neither commanding you [nor forbidding you] because you have gone too far in your disbelief and abandoned faith? It is a question that means denial, meaning: We will not do that. This is the opinion of Qatada and the group. Qatada said: By God, if this Qur’an had been lifted when the first of this nation rejected it, they would have perished. But God returned to them with His reward and mercy, and repeated it to them for twenty years, or as long as God willed. It was said: Its meaning is: Should we turn away from you by reminding you of it, turning away and averting it? Al-Kisa’i said: Shall We then fold up the remembrance from you, so that you are not called upon nor are we admonished? Al-Kalbi said: Shall We then leave you in vain, neither commanding you nor forbidding you? Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: Shall We then turn away from you and leave you and not punish you for your disbelief? “If you are a transgressing people.” The people of Medina, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read in kuntum with a kasra on the hamza. If you are a people who are transgressing. The people of Medina, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read: If you are with a kasra over the hamza, meaning: if you were, like His statement: And you will be the highest if you are believers Al Imran 3:139. The others read it with a fatha, meaning: because you were a people who were transgressing [polytheists].
43:6: 6. And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples.
43:7: 7. And there never came to them, meaning, no prophet came to them but they used to mock him, as your people mock you, consoling their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
43:8: 8. So We destroyed those who were more severe than them in force, meaning stronger than your people, meaning the first ones who were destroyed for denying the messengers, and the example of the former ones has passed, meaning their description, their way, and their punishment, so the outcome of these people is the same in destruction.
43:9: 9. And if you ask them, that is, if you ask your people, who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, ‘The Exalted in Might, the Knowing created them.’ They will affirm that God is their Creator, and they will acknowledge His might and knowledge, then they will worship other than Him and deny His ability to resurrect due to their extreme ignorance. Up to this point, the information about them has been completed, then He began to indicate Himself through His creation, saying:
43:10: 10. "He who made the earth a cradle for you and made therein ways for you that you may be guided. To your destinations in your travels.
43:11: 11. And He who sent down water from the sky in due measure, meaning, according to your need for it, not as He sent down on the people of Noah without due measure until He destroyed them. Then We revived thereby a dead land, meaning, just as We revived this [dead] land with rain, you will emerge, from your graves alive.
43:12: 12. And He who created pairs, meaning all species, “and made for you ships and grazing livestock on which you ride,” on land and sea.
43:13: 13. That you may mount on their backs, he mentioned the metaphor because he referred it back to (what). Then remember the favor of your Lord when you are mounted on them, by making the ships subservient on land and sea, and say, ‘Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us,’ he made this subservient to us, and we could not have subdued it, “able to do so,” and it was said: able to control it.
43:14: 14. And indeed, to our Lord we will return, meaning we will return in the afterlife. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, Ali ibn Rabia told me that he witnessed Ali, may God be pleased with him, when he mounted. When he put his foot in the stirrup, he said: In the name of God. When he was level, he said: Praise be to God. Then he said: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it. And indeed, to our Lord we will return. Then he praised God three times and glorified God three times. Then he said: There is no god but God, I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You. Then he laughed. He said: What makes you laugh, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do what I did, and say the same as I said, then he laughed. So we said: What makes you laugh, O Prophet of God? He said: The servant, or he said: I am amazed at the servant when he says: There is no god but God, I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You. He knows that no one forgives sins except You. Sins except Him.
43:15: 15. The Almighty’s statement: And they have assigned to Him a portion of His servants, meaning a share and a portion, which is their saying: The angels are the daughters of God. The meaning of making here is judging and saying something, as you say: I made Zayd the best of people, meaning I described him and judged by him. Indeed, man, meaning the disbeliever, is ungrateful, ungrateful for God’s blessings, clear, apparent ingratitude.
43:16: 16. Or has He taken for Himself daughters from among those He creates? This is a question of rebuke and denial. He says: Has your Lord taken for Himself daughters, and has chosen you for sons? Like His saying: Then has your Lord chosen you for sons? (al-Isra’ 17:40).
43:17: 17. And when one of them is given the good report of that which is set forth for the Most Merciful as an example, meaning that he made a likeness for God, that is, that every child born resembles him, meaning if one of them is given the good report of girls as mentioned in Surat al-Nahl 16:And when one of them is given the good report of a female, his face darkens, and he is filled with inward grief (al-Nahl 16:58) from grief and anger.
43:18: 18. Or he who grows up, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read: (yansha’) with a damma on the ya’, a fatha on the noon, and a shaddah on the sheen, meaning he is raised. The others read it with a fatha on the ya’, a sukoon on the noon, and a soft sheen, meaning he grows up. in adornment, in ornamentation, meaning women. and in dispute he is not clear, in dispute he is not clear about the argument because of their weakness and foolishness. Qatada said about this verse: So when a woman speaks and wants to speak with her argument, she speaks with the argument against herself. There are three aspects to the position of from: nominative as a subject, accusative as an implied word, its meaning: or from those who create in ornamentation, they make them daughters of God, and the genitive is a response to his saying: from what He creates and his saying: with what He struck.
43:19: 19. And they made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females. The people of Kufa and Abu Amr read: (servants of the Most Merciful) with the ba’ and the alif after it and raising the dal like the Almighty’s saying: Rather, they are honored servants Al-Anbiya’ 26. The others read: (with the Most Merciful) with the nun and the dal is in the accusative case, and its confirmation is the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who are with your Lord Al-A’raf 206 the verse, witnessed their creation. The people of Medina read it as if its agent was not named, and the second hamza was softened after the question hamza, meaning: they brought their creation. The others read it with the fatha on the sheen, meaning they brought their creation when they were created. This is like His saying: Or did We create the angels females while they were witnesses? Al-Saffat 150. Their testimony will be recorded, on the angels that they are the daughters of God, and they will be questioned, about it. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: When they said this, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them: How do you know that they are females? They said: We heard it from our fathers and we testify that they did not lie. Then God Almighty said: Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned about it in the Hereafter.
43:20: 20. And they say, ‘If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them,’ meaning the angels, as stated by Qatada, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi. Mujahid said: It means the idols, and He did not hasten our punishment for our worship of them because He was pleased with us worshipping them. God the Most High said: They have no knowledge of that, in what they say. They only guess. They are lying when they say that God the Most High was pleased with us regarding their custom. It was also said that they are only guessing when they say that the angels are female and that they are the daughters of God.
43:21: 21. Or did We give them a scripture before it, meaning before the Qur’an, that they should worship other than God, to which they cling.
43:22: 22. Rather, they said, ‘Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion,’ meaning, a religion and a way of life. Mujahid said: following an imam. “And we are guided by their footsteps,” meaning, they made themselves guided by following their fathers.
43:23: 23. And likewise, We did not send before you a warner to any city except that its affluent people said, ‘Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and we will follow in their footsteps.’
43:24: 24. Say, Ibn Amir and Hafs read: (said) as a statement, and the others read (say) as a command, Or if I came to you, Abu Ja`far read: (We came to you) as a plural, and the others read (I came to you) as a singular, with better guidance, a more correct religion, than what you found your fathers doing, Al-Zajjaj said: Say to them [O Muhammad]: Will you follow what you found your fathers doing even if I came to you with better guidance than it? So they refused to accept, and They said, ‘Indeed, we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers.’
43:25: 25. "So We took retribution from them. Then see what was the end of those who denied."
43:26: 26. The Almighty said: And when Abraham said to his father and his people, ‘Indeed, I am innocent,’ meaning innocent. Innocent is neither dual, plural, nor feminine because it is a verbal noun in the place of an adjective. of what you worship.
43:27: 27. Except He who created me, for He will guide me, direct me to His religion.
43:28: 28. And made it, meaning this word, a word that will remain among his descendants. Mujahid and Qatada said: It means the word of monotheism, which is There is no god but God, a word that will remain among his descendants and progeny. Qatada said: There will always be among his progeny those who worship God and declare His Oneness. Al-Qurazi said: It means: And He made the will of Abraham that he enjoined upon his sons to remain among his progeny and descendants, and this is the saying of God Almighty: And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons Al-Baqarah 2:132. Ibn Zayd said: He meant his saying: I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds Al-Baqarah 2:131, and he read: He has named you Muslims Al-Hajj 2:78. Perhaps they will return, meaning perhaps the people of Mecca will follow this religion and return from their current path to the religion of Abraham. Al-Suddi said: Perhaps they will repent and return to obeying God Almighty.
43:29: 29. Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers, meaning: the polytheists in this world, and I did not punish them for their disbelief, until the truth came to them, meaning the Qur’an. Ad-Dahhak said: Islam. And a clear Messenger, explaining the rulings to them, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was right for this blessing to be given to them, or for them to obey him, but they did not, and they disobeyed.
43:30: 30. And it is the Almighty’s saying: And when the truth came to them, meaning the Qur’an, they said, ‘This is magic, and indeed, we disbelieve in it.’
43:31: 31. And they said, ‘Why was this Qur’an not sent down to some great man from the two cities?’ They meant Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah from Mecca and Urwah ibn Mas`ud Al-Thaqafi in Taif, as stated by Qatada. Mujahid said: Utbah ibn Rabi’ah is from Mecca, and Ibn Abd Yalil al-Thaqafi is from Taif. It was said: Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira is from Mecca, and from Taif: Habib ibn Amr ibn Amr ibn Umair Al-Thaqafi. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both.
43:32: 32. God Almighty said: Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? meaning the prophethood. Muqatil said, “He is saying: In their hands are the keys to the message, so they place them wherever they wish?” Then he said: We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, making one rich and another poor, one a king and one a slave. Just as We have preferred some over others in provision as We willed, so We have chosen with the message whomever We willed. And We have raised some of them above others in degrees, by means of wealth and money, that some of them may make use of others in service, by employing some of them. The rich may make use of their wealth for the poor workers in work, so that some of them may be a source of livelihood for others, this one with his wealth, and this one with his deeds, so that the foundation of the world’s affairs may be harmonized. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: Some of them own others with their wealth through servitude and ownership. And the mercy of your Lord, [meaning Paradise], is better, for the believers, than what they accumulate, by means of what the disbelievers accumulate of wealth.
43:33: 33. And had it not been that mankind would be one community, that is, had it not been that they would all become disbelievers and unite in disbelief, We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful roofs of silver, Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja`far, and Abu `Amr read saqfan with a fatha on the seen and a sukoon on the qaf, singular, and its meaning is plural, like the statement of God Almighty: So the roof fell upon them from above them (al-Nahl 16:26). The rest read it with a damma on the seen and the qaf, plural, and it is the plural of saqf like rahn and rahn. Abu `Ubaidah said: There is no third for them. It was said: It is the plural of saqif. It was said: The plural of suquf is the plural of plural. “And ascents,” elevators and stairs of silver, upon which they ascend, they ascend and climb. It is said: you appeared on the roof if you climbed it.
43:34: 34. And for their houses are doors of silver, and thrones meaning: We made for them thrones of silver, on which they recline.
43:35: 35. And adornments, meaning, We made for them adornments, which is gold, similar to: Or you have a house of adornment Al-Isra’ 93, And indeed, all of that is but the enjoyment of worldly life, Hamza and Asim read: (Lama) with emphasis to mean: And all of that is but the enjoyment of worldly life, so (Lama) means except, and the others made it light to mean: And all of that is the enjoyment of worldly life, so (In) is for the beginning, and (Ma) is a connection, meaning: Indeed, all of this is the enjoyment of worldly life that will vanish and go away, And the Hereafter is with your Lord for the righteous, specifically meaning Paradise. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu al-Abbas Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Taysifuni told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Turabi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Bastam told us, Ahmad ibn Sayyar al-Qurashi told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Yunus Abu Muslim told us, Abu Bakr ibn Manzur told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the world weighed in the sight of God the equivalent of a mosquito’s wing, He would not have given a disbeliever a single drop of water to drink from it. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah told us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Mujalid ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Qais ibn Abi Hazim, on the authority of al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, the brother of Banu Fihr, who said: “I was among the group that stopped with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) at the dead sheep. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Do you think this was insignificant to its people when they threw it away?’ They said: ‘Because of its insignificance, they threw it away.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘The world is more insignificant to God than this is to its people.’”
43:36: 36. The Almighty said: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious, meaning, turns away from the remembrance of the Most Gracious, not fearing His punishment, nor hoping for His reward. It is said: I went to the Fire, I went to Hell, meaning, I went to Hell, guided by it. And I went to Hell from it: I turned away from it, just as one says: I turned to so-and-so, I turned away from him, I inclined towards him, and I turned away from him. Al-Qurazi said: He turns his back on the remembrance of the Most Gracious, which is the Qur’an. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: He is wronged by turning his gaze away from it. Al-Khalil bin Ahmad said: The origin of blindness is looking with weak eyesight. Ibn Abbas read: And whoever lives with a fat-ha on the sheen, meaning he goes blind. It is said: He went blind, he goes blind, so he is a blind woman. The opposite of him is a devil, Ya’qub read: “We assign to him a devil, join him to him, and set him in charge of him. He is his companion, he never leaves him, he makes blindness seem attractive to him and makes him think that he is on the right path.
43:37: 37. And indeed they, meaning the devils, avert them from the path, that is, to prevent them from guidance. The plural is a metaphor because his statement, And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, is in the plural form, even though the wording is singular, and they think that they are guided, and the disbelieving children of Adam think that they are on the right path.
43:38: 38. Until when he came to Us, the people of Iraq, other than Abu Bakr, read: came to Us in the singular form, meaning the disbeliever. The others read: came to Us, in the dual form, meaning the disbeliever and his companion, and they were put in one chain. He said, the disbeliever to his companion, the devil: Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts, meaning the distance between the east and the west, so the name of one of them prevailed over the other, just as the sun and the moon are called the two moons, and Abu Bakr and Umar are called the two lifespans. It was said that by the two easts he meant the east of summer and the east of winter, and the first is more correct. Then what an evil companion, Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri said: When the disbeliever is resurrected, he is paired with his companion from the devils, and he does not leave him until he goes to the Fire.
43:39: 39. And it will not benefit you today, in the Hereafter, since you have wronged, that is, you have associated partners in this world, that you are partners in the punishment, meaning that sharing in the punishment will not benefit you, nor will sharing in it lighten any of the punishment for you, because each of the disbelievers and devils has the greater share of the punishment. Muqatil said: Apologies and regret will not benefit you today, for you and your peers today are partners in the punishment, just as you were partners in this world [in disbelief].
43:40: 40. Can you then make the deaf hear or guide the blind and those who are in clear error? meaning the disbelievers upon whom the word of punishment has been decreed will not believe.
43:41: 41. Then if We take you away, that is, by causing you to die before We punish them, then We will take vengeance upon them, by killing them after you.
43:42: 42. Or We show you, in your lifetime, that which We have promised them, of the punishment, for indeed, We are over them in power, capable, whenever We will We punish them. He meant by this the polytheists of Mecca from whom He took revenge on the Day of Badr. This is the opinion of most of the commentators. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He meant by it the people of Islam from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. After the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was a severe punishment upon his nation, so God honored His Prophet and took him away and did not show him in his nation except that which would please him, and He left the punishment after him. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was shown what would befall his nation after him, and he was never seen smiling or cheerful until God took him.
43:43: 43. "So hold fast to what has been revealed to you. Indeed, you are on a straight path."
43:44: 44. And indeed it, meaning the Qur’an, is a reminder for you, an honor for you, and for your people, from Quraysh, similar to: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance (al-Anbiya 21:10), meaning your honor, and you will be asked, about its right and the performance of its thanks. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked, For whom does this belong? he would say, For Quraysh. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Ja’d told us, Asim bin Muhammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This matter will remain with the Quraysh as long as two people remain. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: Muhammad bin Jubair bin Mut’im used to narrate on the authority of Mu’awiyah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “This matter is with the Quraysh. No one will oppose them except that God will throw him down on his face as long as they uphold the religion.” Mujahid said: The people are the Arabs, so the Qur’an has an honor for them because it was revealed in their language, and then that honor is given to the most special of the Arabs, until it is [most for the Quraysh and the Banu Hashim. It was said: (Remembrance of God) is an honor for you with the wisdom He has given you, (and for your people) the believers with what God has guided them with, (and you will be asked) about the Qur’an and what you are required to do in fulfilling its right.
43:45: 45. The Almighty said: “And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?” They differed regarding these people who were asked: Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, God sent to him Adam and his son from the Messengers. Gabriel called the adhan and then called the iqama, and said: ‘O Muhammad, come forward and lead them in prayer.’ When he finished the prayer, Gabriel said to him: ‘Ask, O Muhammad, about those of Our Messengers whom We sent before you,’ and the verse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I will not ask, for I have had enough.’” This is the statement of Al-Zuhri, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Zayd. They said: God gathered the Messengers for him on the night of his Night Journey and commanded him to ask them, but he did not doubt or ask. Most of the commentators said: Ask the believing People of the Book to whom the prophets were sent, did the messengers come to them except with monotheism? This is the saying of Ibn Abbas in all the narrations, as well as Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, Al-Hasan and Al-Muqatileen. This is indicated by the reading of Abdullah and Ubayy: (And ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you), and the meaning of the command to ask is to confirm to the polytheists of Quraysh that no messenger or book came to them with the worship of anyone other than God Almighty.
43:46: 46. The Almighty said: “And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs. He said, ‘Indeed, I am the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds.’”
43:47: 47. So when he brought them Our signs, at once they laughed at them, mockingly.
43:48: 48. And We did not show them any sign except that it was greater than its sister, its companion and partner that came before it, and We seized them with punishment, with years, floods, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, and obliteration. These were signs for Moses and punishment for them, and each one was greater than the one before it, that they might return, from their disbelief.
43:49: 49. And they said, to Moses when they witnessed the punishment, O magician, O perfect and skilled scholar. They only said this out of respect and reverence for him, because magic, according to them, was a science and a praiseworthy attribute. It was said that its meaning was O you who overcame us with your magic. Al-Zajjaj said: They addressed him with this because of the title of magician they had previously given him. Call upon your Lord for us according to what He has promised you, meaning according to what you have told us of His promise to you: if we believe, He will remove the punishment from us. So ask Him to remove the punishment from us. Indeed, we are [rightly] guided, believers. So Moses called upon Him, and He removed it from them, but they did not believe. This is what God Almighty said:
43:50: 50. So when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their covenant, they broke their covenant and persisted in their disbelief.
43:51: 51. And Pharaoh called out to his people, saying, ‘O my people, is not mine the kingdom of Egypt, and these rivers flow beneath me,’ meaning the Nile rivers, from beneath my palaces. Qatada said: They flow before me in my gardens and orchards. Al-Hasan said: By my command. “Do you not see?” meaning My greatness and the strength of My kingdom.
43:52: 52. Or am I better? Rather, I am better. Or means rather, and it is not a conjunction according to the majority of commentators. Al-Farra’ said: The pause is at his statement: Or, and there is an omission in it, its meaning is: Do you not see, or do you not see? Then he began and said: I am better, than this one who is humiliated, weak and contemptible, meaning Moses. His statement: and he can hardly make himself clear makes his speech clear due to the lisp in his tongue.
43:53: 53. Why was not a bracelet of gold bestowed upon him, if he was truthful, Hafs and Ya’qub read aswarah as the plural of sawwar, while the others read asawwarah as the plural of usurah, which is the plural of plural. Mujahid said: When they blackened a man, they would put a bracelet around him and encircle him with a necklace of gold, as a sign of his mastery. So Pharaoh said: Why did not the Lord of Moses bestow upon him bracelets of gold, if he was a master whose obedience is obligatory upon us? Or did the angels come with him in succession, one after the other, following one another, testifying to his truthfulness and assisting him in his affairs.
43:54: 54. God the Almighty said: So he belittled his people, meaning that Pharaoh belittled his Coptic people, meaning that he found them ignorant. It was also said: he led them to be ignorant and light. It is said: he belittled him for his opinion, if he led him to ignorance and led him astray from the truth, so they obeyed him, in denying Moses, Indeed, they were a wicked people.
43:55: 55. So when they angered Us, they angered Us, We took revenge on them and drowned them all.
43:56: 56. So We made them predecessors. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read salfa with a damma on the seen and the lam. Al-Farra’ said: It is the plural of salif from salaf with a damma on the lam, yaslaf, meaning to advance. The others read it with a fatha on the seen and the lam, as a plural of salif, like haris and hars, khadam and khuddam, and rasid and rasd, and they are all the past and advanced nations. It is said: salaaf yaslaf, if he advanced, and the salaf are from the advancement of the fathers, so We made them predecessors so that others would take a lesson from them. And an example for others, a warning and admonition for those who come after them. It was also said: a predecessor for the disbelievers of this nation to the Fire and an example for those who come after them.
43:57: 57. And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, Ibn Abbas and most of the commentators said: The verse was revealed regarding the argument between Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayri and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, concerning Jesus, peace be upon him, when the words of God Almighty were revealed: Indeed, you and what you worship other than God are fuel for Hell (Al-Anbiya’: 98), which we have already mentioned in Surat Al-Anbiya’, peace be upon them.
