When your people turn away from it, the people of Medina, Ash-Sham, and Al-Kisa’i read: (يصدون) with a damma on the sad, meaning they turn away, similar to the words of God Almighty: They turn away from you with aversion (An-Nisa’: 61), while the others read it with a kasra on the sad. They differed about its meaning. Al-Kisa’i said: They are two dialects, like ya’rashūn and ya’rashūn. Shaddād ‘alaih yasḍud and yasḍud, and nama bi-l-ḥadīth yanmaḍand yanma. Ibn Abbas said: It means they make a commotion. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: They shout. Ad-Dahhak said: They make a commotion. Qatadah said: They are impatient. Al-Qurazi said: They are impatient. And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, If your people turn away from him, they say, ‘Muhammad wants nothing from us except that we worship him and take him as a god, just as the Christians worshipped Jesus.’
43:58: 58. And they said, ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’ Qatada said: Or is he? They mean Muhammad, so we worship him and obey him and abandon our gods. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: Or is he? meaning Jesus. They said: Muhammad claims that everything worshipped besides God will be in Hell, so we are satisfied that our gods will be with Jesus, Ezra, and the angels in Hell. God Almighty said: They did not compare it to you, meaning this example, except to argue, arguing with falsehood. They knew that what was meant by His statement: And what you worship besides God is fuel for Hell (Al-Anbiya’: 98) is these idols. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Bakr Abd Al-Rahman bin Abdullah Al-Hamshawi told us, Ahmad bin Ja’far bin Hamdan Al-Qat’i told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Hajjaj bin Dinar Al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No people went astray after they were guided except that they were given disputation. Then he recited: “They do not present it to you except to argue. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people.”
43:59: 59. Then he mentioned Jesus and said: He is, he is not, meaning Jesus, peace be upon him, except a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, with prophethood, and We made him an example, a sign and a lesson, for the Children of Israel, by which they would know the power of God Almighty to do whatever He wills, since He created him without a father.
43:60: 60. And if We willed, We could have made angels from among you, meaning, if We willed, We could have destroyed them and replaced you with angels, on the earth to succeed you, who would be successors from among you, populating the earth, worshipping Me, and obeying Me. It was also said: They would succeed one another.
43:61: 61. And indeed, meaning Jesus, peace be upon him, is a sign of the Hour, meaning his descent is one of the signs of the Hour by which he knows of its nearness. Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, and Qatada read: It is a sign of the Hour, with the lam and the ‘ayn open, meaning a sign and a mark. We narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Soon the son of Mary will descend among you as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the pigs, and abolish the jizya. In his time, all religions will perish except Islam.” It is narrated: ((He will descend on a pass in the Holy Land, wearing two Egyptian garments, and his hair will be oiled, and in his hand will be a spear with which he will kill the Antichrist. He will come to Jerusalem while the people are praying the afternoon prayer, and the imam will be delayed, and Jesus will put him forward and pray behind him according to the law of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he will kill the pigs, break the cross, destroy the churches and the synagogues, and kill the Christians except for those who believe in him. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ibn Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Nafi’, the freed slave of Abu Qatada Al-Ansari, that Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How will you be when the son of Mary descends among you and your Imam is from among you? Al-Hasan and a group said: And it means that the Qur’an is knowledge of the Hour, teaching you about its occurrence and informing you of its conditions and horrors. So have no doubt about it, so do not doubt it. Ibn Abbas said: Do not deny it. And follow, on monotheism, this, which I am on, a straight path.
43:62: 62. “And let not Satan turn you away from the religion of God. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.”
43:63: 63. And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, ‘I have come to you with wisdom,’ with prophecy, ‘and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ,’ of the rulings of the Torah. Qatada said: He meant the differences among the groups who formed parties over the matter of Jesus. Al-Zajjaj said: What Jesus brought in the Gospel is only part of what they disagreed about, and he explained to them in places other than the Gospel what they needed. So fear God and obey me.
43:64: 64. "Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path."
43:65: 65. "Then the parties differed among themselves. So woe to those who did wrong from the punishment of a painful Day."
43:66: 66. Do they await anything but the Hour? meaning that it will inevitably come to them, as if they are waiting for it, that it will come to them suddenly, “while they do not perceive.”
43:67: 67. Friends, in disobedience in this world, on that Day, on the Day of Resurrection, will be enemies to one another, except for the righteous, except for those who love one another for the sake of God Almighty, in obedience to God Almighty. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shuraihi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, Aqil ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad told me, that Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi al-Qadi told them, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jiri, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ishaq that ‘Ali said regarding this verse: Two believing friends and two disbelieving friends. Then one of the believers died and said: “O Lord, so-and-so used to command me to obey You and obey Your Messenger, and command me to do good and forbid me from evil, and inform me that I would meet You. O Lord, do not lead him astray after me, and guide him as You have guided me, and honor him as You have honored me.” Then when his believing friend died, He brought them together and said: Let one of you praise the other, and he would say: What an excellent brother, what an excellent friend, and what an excellent companion. Then one of the disbelievers died and said: O Lord, so-and-so used to forbid me from obeying You and obeying Your Messenger, and command me to do evil and forbid me from good. He tells me that I will not meet you, and says, What a bad brother, what a bad friend, what a bad companion.
43:68: 68. O My servants, meaning it will be said to them: O My servants, there is no fear concerning you today, nor shall you grieve. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman on the authority of his father who said: I heard that when the people are resurrected, there is not one among them who is not terrified, so a caller will call out: O My servants, there is no fear concerning you today, nor shall you grieve, and all the people will hope for it and follow it.
43:69: 69. Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims, so the non-Muslims despair of it and it is said to them:
43:70: 70. Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing, happy and enjoying yourself.
43:71: 71. “Plates and cups will be served to them,” the plural of sahfah, which is a wide bowl, of gold and cups, the plural of kub, which is a round vessel with a rounded top and no handles. And in it, meaning in Paradise, is whatever the souls desire. The people of Medina, Syria, and Hafs read: tashtahhu, and this is also in their copies of the Qur’an. The others read it without the ha’. And the eyes will be delighted, and you will abide therein eternally. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, who said: “A man said: ‘O Messenger of God, are there horses in Paradise? I love horses.’ He said: ‘If God admits you to Paradise, you will not wish to ride a horse made of red rubies and fly wherever you wish in Paradise, but you will do so.’ A Bedouin said: ‘O Messenger of God, are there camels in Paradise?’ He said: ‘O Bedouin, if God admits you to Paradise, you will obtain therein whatever your soul desires and your eyes delight in.’”
43:72: 72. And that is Paradise which you have inherited for what you used to do.
43:73: 73. Therein you will find many fruits, some of which you will eat. And in the hadith: No man will remove a fruit from Paradise except that something twice as much will grow in its place.
43:74: 74. The criminals, the polytheists, will abide in the punishment of Hell forever.
43:75: 75. He will not cease from them while they are therein in despair.
43:76: 76. And We did not wrong them, but it was they who were the wrongdoers.
43:77: 77. “And they will call, ‘O Malik,’ calling the keeper of Hellfire, ‘Let your Lord put an end to us,’ ‘Let your Lord put us to death so that we may rest.’ Malik will answer them after a thousand years, ‘He will say, ‘Indeed, you will remain,’ residing in the torment. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, on the authority of Qatadah, who mentioned it on the authority of Abu Ayyub, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-‘As, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The people of Hell will call upon Malik, but he will not answer them for forty years. Then he will reply to them, ‘You will remain.’ He said: ‘By God, their call to Malik and to the Lord of Malik has become insignificant. Then they will call upon their Lord and say, ‘Our Lord, our misery has overcome us, and we were a people astray. Our Lord, bring us out of it, for if we return, then we will be wrongdoers.’ He said: ‘He will be silent about them twice for the length of this world. Then he will reply to them, ‘Get out of it, disgraced, and do not speak to me.’ He said: ‘By God, the people will not utter a word after that, and there will be nothing but sighing and breathing in the fire of Hell.’ So he likened their voices to the voices of donkeys, the beginning of which is a sigh and the end of which is a breathing.’”
43:78: 78. We have certainly brought you the truth, meaning, We have sent to you, O people of Quraysh, our Messenger with the truth, but most of you are averse to the truth.
43:79: 79. Or have they decided, or have they determined, a matter, in plotting against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then We will decide, or have determined, a matter in their punishment. Mujahid said: If they plotted evil, I will plot the same against them.
43:80: 80. Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? What they whisper to others and whisper among themselves? Yes, we hear that and know. And Our messengers, also from the angels, meaning the guardian angels, are with them writing it down.
43:81: 81. “Say: If the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first of his worshippers,” meaning if the Most Gracious had a son, as you say and as you claim, then I would be the first to worship Him, for He is One, without partner or son. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If meaning the Most Gracious did not have a son, then I would be the first of his worshippers who testify to that, making if mean denial. Al-Suddi said: Its meaning is that if the Most Gracious had a son, then I would be the first to worship Him with that, but He has no son. It was said: Al-Abidin means the first to deny and reject what you said. It is said: It means: I am the first to be angry for the sake of the Most Merciful that he be called a son. It is said: Abd ya'bud if he is disgusted and angry. Some people said: It is said that he is a slave, so he is a worshipper. Rather, it is said that he is a slave.
43:82: 82. Then He purified Himself and said: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe from what they say of lies.
43:83: 83. So leave them to indulge in falsehood and play in their worldly affairs until they meet the Day they are promised, meaning the Day of Resurrection. 84. And He is God in the heaven and God on the earth, [Qatada said: He is worshipped in the heaven and on the earth. There is no god but Him], and He is the Wise, in managing His creation, the Knowing, of their interests.
43:85: 85. And blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and with Him is knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned. Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read (yirja’un) with a ya’, and the others with a ta’.
43:86: 86. And those they invoke besides Him do not possess intercession, except for one who bears witness to the truth, and they are Jesus, Ezra, and the angels, for they were worshipped instead of God, and they have intercession. Based on this, min is in the nominative case. It was said that min is in the genitive case, and what is meant by those they invoke are Jesus, Ezra, and the angels, meaning that they do not possess intercession except for one who bears witness to the truth, and the first is more correct. What is meant by bearing witness to the truth is the saying there is no god but God, the word of monotheism, and they know, in their hearts what they have testified to with their tongues.
43:87: 87. And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ So how are they deluded? They are turned away from worshipping Him.
43:88: 88. And his saying, O Lord, meaning the saying of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, complaining to his Lord: O Lord, these are a people who do not believe. Asim and Hamza read and his saying with the genitive of the lam and the ha’, based on: And with Him is knowledge of the Hour and knowledge of his saying, O Lord. The others read it with the accusative, and it has two meanings: One of them means: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations and their saying, O Lord? And the second: And his saying.
43:89: 89. So pardon them, turn away from them, “and say, ‘Peace,’” meaning: leave them alone, as God Almighty says: “Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant” (al-Qasas 28:55), and they will know, the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read it with a ta’, and the rest with a ya’. Muqatil said: It was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
44:3: 3. Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: It is the Night of Decree. God sent down the Qur’an on the Night of Decree from the Mother of the Book to the lowest heaven, then Gabriel brought it down from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in stages over twenty years. Others said: It is the night of the middle of Sha’ban. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Al-Asbagh bin Al-Faraj told us, Ibn Wahb told me, Amr bin Al-Harith told me that Abdul Malik bin Abdul Malik told him that Ibn Abi Dhi’b, whose name was Mus’ab, told him on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, or his uncle, or his grandfather, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God, may His praise be exalted, descends on the night of the middle of Sha’ban to the lowest heaven and forgives every soul except for a person in whose heart is rancor or one who associates partners with God.” Indeed, We were to warn.
44:4: 4. In it, meaning in the blessed night, every matter of wisdom is distinguished, is detailed, is established. Ibn Abbas said: “It is written from the Mother of the Book on the Night of Decree what will happen in the year of good and evil, provisions and life spans, even the pilgrims. It is said: So-and-so performs the Hajj [and so-and-so performs the Hajj].” Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatada said: Every life span, deed, creation, and provision are decreed in the Night of Decree in the month of Ramadan, and what will happen in that year. Ikrimah said: It is the night of the middle of Sha’ban, in which the matter of the year is decided, and the living are replaced by the dead, so no one is added to them and no one is subtracted from them. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam'ani told us, Abu Ja'far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Al-Layth told me, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Uthman bin Muhammad bin Al-Mughirah bin Al-Akhns told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Deaths are cut off from Sha'ban to Sha'ban, to the point that a man marries and has a child, and his name is even brought out among the dead. Abu Al-Dhaha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: God decrees matters on the night of the middle of Sha’ban, and hands them over to their owners on the Night of Decree.
44:5: 5. A command, meaning We sent down a command, from Us. Al-Farra’ said: It is in the accusative case, meaning: in it is every command, division and command, meaning We command that it be explained as a command. Indeed, We were messengers, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the prophets before him.
44:6: 6. A mercy from your Lord, Ibn Abbas said: It is My compassion for My creation and My blessings upon them by sending them messengers. Al-Zajjaj said: “We revealed it on a blessed night of mercy. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
44:7: 7. Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. The people of Kufa read: (Lord) in the accusative case, in response to his statement: (Who is your Lord), and others raised it in response to his statement: He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. It was said: in the nominative case, if you are certain, that God is Lord of the heavens and the earth.
44:8: 8. "There is no god but He. He gives life and causes death. He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old."
44:9: 9. Rather, they are in doubt, about this Qur’an, playing, mocking it, heedless of it.
44:10: 10. Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. They differed about this smoke: Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Katheer told us, on the authority of Sufyan, Mansur and Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: “While a man was speaking in Kindah, he said: Smoke will come on the Day of Resurrection and will seize the hearing and sight of the hypocrites, and it will seize the believer [like a] cold. We were startled, so I came to Ibn Mas’ud, who was reclining, and he became angry and sat up. He said: Whoever knows, let him speak, and whoever does not know, let him say: God knows best. For it is part of knowledge to say when one does not know: I do not know. For God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it, and I am not of the pretenders’ (p. 86). And the Quraysh were slow to convert to Islam, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplicated against them, saying: O God, help me against them with seven like the seven of Joseph. So a year overtook them until they perished in it and ate dead meat and bones, and a man would see what was between the sky and the earth like smoke. Then it came…” Abu Sufyan said: O Muhammad, you have come to command us to maintain kinship ties, and your people have perished, so pray to God for them. Then he recited: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke to His saying: Indeed, you will return. Will the punishment of the Hereafter be removed from them when it comes? Then they returned to their disbelief, so that is His saying: The Day We will strike with the greatest strike, the day of Badr, and inevitably the day of Badr. “Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated” to They will be defeated ar-Rum 30:3, and the Romans have already passed.
44:11: 11. This is a painful torment that will overwhelm the people.
44:12: 12. And it was narrated by Muhammad bin Ismail on the authority of Yahya on the authority of Wakee’ on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: They said: Our Lord, remove the punishment from us, for we are believers. So it was said to him: If We remove the punishment from them, they will return to their disbelief. So he called upon his Lord, and He removed it from them, and they returned, and God took revenge on them on the Day of Badr. That is what He said: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, until His saying: Indeed, We will take revenge. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Five have passed: Al-Lazam, the Romans, Al-Batsha, the Moon, and Al-Dukhan. Some people said: It is smoke that will come before the Hour of Resurrection and has not yet come, so it will enter the ears of the infidels and hypocrites until it becomes like a roasted head, and the believer will be afflicted by it like a cold, and the whole earth will be like a house in which a fire has been lit. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, and Al-Hasan. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Aqil bin Muhammad Al-Jurjani told us, Abu Al-Faraj Al-Mu’afa bin Zakariya Al-Baghdadi told us, Muhammad bin Jarir Al-Tabari told us, Issam bin Rawad bin Al-Jarrah told us, my father told us, Abu Sufyan bin Saeed told us, Mansur bin Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of Rib’i bin Kharash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first of the signs will be the smoke, the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden, Abyan, driving the people to the place of assembly, taking a rest with them when they say. Hudhayfah said: O Messenger of God, what is the smoke? He recited this verse: The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, which will fill the space between the east and the west and will remain for forty days and nights. As for the believer, it will affect him like a cold, but as for the disbeliever, it will be like that of a drunkard, coming out of his nostrils, ears, and anus.
44:13: 13. How can they be reminded? How can they be reminded and admonished? He says: How can they remember and be admonished? And there has come to them a clear Messenger, apparently truthful, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
44:14: 14. Then they turned away from him, they turned away from him, and said, ‘A teacher,’ meaning a human being is teaching him, a madman.
44:15: 15. God Almighty said: Indeed, We will remove the punishment, meaning the punishment of hunger, for a little, meaning a short time. Muqatil said: until the day of Badr. Indeed, you will return, to your disbelief.
44:16: 16. The day when We will strike with the greatest strike, which is the day of Badr, We will take revenge. This is the opinion of Ibn Masoud and most scholars. Al-Hasan said: The Day of Resurrection. Ikrimah narrated this on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
44:17: 17. And We had certainly tried, We tested, before them, before these, the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble Messenger, from God, and he was Moses, son of Imran.
44:18: 18. Bring to me the servants of God, meaning the Children of Israel, “set them free and do not torture them. I am to you a trustworthy messenger,” according to the revelation.
44:19: 19. And do not exalt yourselves over God, do not act arrogantly towards Him by abandoning His obedience, Indeed, I bring you clear authority, with clear proof of the truth of my words. So when he said that, they threatened to kill him, so he said:
44:20: 20. And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord lest you stone me, meaning, kill me. Ibn Abbas said: You curse me and say he is a magician. Qatada said: Stone me.
44:21: 21. And if you do not believe me, then leave me alone, so leave me neither with me nor against me. Ibn Abbas said: So avoid harming me with your hand and tongue, but they did not believe.
44:22: 22. So he called upon his Lord, ‘Indeed, these are a criminal people,’ polytheists. So God answered him and commanded him to go, and he said:
44:23: 23. So travel by night with My servants, meaning Israel, for you will be pursued, Pharaoh and his people will pursue you.
44:24: 24. And leave the sea, if you and your companions cross it, still, in its state and condition, after you have struck it and entered it. Its meaning is: Do not order it to return, leave it until the people of Pharaoh enter it. The root of rahu is stillness. Muqatil said: Its meaning is: Leave the sea calm [raḥīn], i.e. still, so it was named after the verbal noun, i.e. calm. Ka’b said: Leave it as a path. Qatadah said: A dry path. Qatadah said: When Moses crossed the sea, he turned to strike it with his staff so that it would heal, and he was afraid that Pharaoh [and his soldiers] would follow him, so he was told: Leave the sea calm as it is, Indeed, they are a drowned army. Moses was informed that he would drown them so that his heart would be reassured that he had left the sea as he had crossed it, then he mentioned what they had left behind in Egypt.
44:25: 25. He said: How many gardens and springs did they leave behind, [meaning after the drowning], of gardens and springs?
44:26: 26. And crops and a noble position, a noble gathering. Qatada said: the noble and the beautiful.
44:27: 27. And comfort, and enjoyment and a soft life, they were in it enjoying themselves, soft and joyful: arrogant and haughty.
44:28: 28. Likewise, Al-Kalbi said: Likewise I will do to those who disobey me, “and We caused another people to inherit it,” meaning the Children of Israel.
44:29: 29. So neither the heavens nor the earth wept for them, meaning that when a believer dies, peace and the earth weep for him for forty mornings. However, no deeds of theirs ascended for the heavens to weep over his loss, nor did they perform any righteous deeds on earth for the earth to weep over him. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah Al-Fanjawi told us, Abu Ali Al-Maqri told us, Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili told us, Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Basri told us, Makki bin Ibrahim told us, Musa bin Ubaidah Al-Rabdhi told us, Yazid Al-Raqashi told me, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “There is no servant but that he has two doors in the heaven, one from which his provision comes out, and one into which his deeds enter. So when he dies, they miss him and weep over him.” And he recited: And neither the heaven nor the earth wept over them. Ata' said: The sky's crying is the redness of its edges. Al-Suddi said: When Al-Hussein bin Ali was killed, the sky wept for him, and its weeping turned red. And they were not given respite, they were not given respite when the punishment seized them for repentance or anything else.
44:30: 30. And We saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment, the killing of children, the enslavement of women, and the exhaustion of work.
44:31: 31. "From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty and among the transgressors."
44:32: 32. And We chose them, meaning the believers among the Children of Israel, with knowledge, of them, over the worlds, over the worlds of their time.
44:33: 33. And We gave them of the signs that which was a clear trial. Qatada said: A clear blessing such as the splitting of the sea, the shading of the clouds, the sending down of manna and quails, and the blessings that He bestowed upon them. Ibn Zayd said: He tested them with ease and hardship, and he recited: And We test you with evil and with good as trial (Al-Anbiya’: 35).
44:34: 34. These, meaning the polytheists of Mecca, say
44:35: 35. It is only our first death, meaning there is no death other than this one we die in this world, and there is no resurrection after it. This is His statement: And we will not be resurrected, meaning we will not be resurrected after our death.
44:36: 36. Bring our fathers, [who died], if you are truthful, that we will be resurrected after death, then their fear is like the torment of the past nations, so he said:
44:37: 37. Are they better or the people of Tubba'? That is, they are not better than them, meaning stronger, more powerful, and more numerous than the people of Tubba'. Qatada said: He is Tubba' al-Himyari, and he marched with armies until he bewildered al-Hirah, and built Samarkand. He was one of the kings of Yemen. He was called Tubba' because of the large number of his followers, and each one of them was called (Tubba') because he followed his companion. This one worshipped fire, so he converted to Islam and called his people, who were Himyar, to Islam, but they denied him. What happened about him was what Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others mentioned. Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they said: The other Tubba, who was As`ad Abu Karb bin Malik, came with Karb when he came from the east and made his way to Madinah. When he passed through it, he left among them a son of his who was killed by treachery. He arrived there, intending to destroy it and exterminate its people. When they heard about his plan, this tribe of the Ansar gathered against him and went out to fight him. The Ansar fought him during the day and supported him at night. This pleased him and he said: These are indeed noble people. When two scholars, named Ka`b and Asad, from the rabbis of Banu Qurayzah, came to him, and they were scholars and they were cousins. When they heard about his plan, they said to him: O king, do not do it, for if you insist on what you want, a barrier will separate you from it, and we are not safe from immediate punishment for you. For this is the place where a prophet will emigrate and emerge from this tribe of Quraysh, whose name is Muhammad. He was born in Makkah, and this is the place of his emigration. The place where you are now will witness a great deal of killing and wounding among his companions and their enemy. Tubba' said: Who will fight him, since he is a prophet? They said: His people will march against him and be killed here. He listened to what they had said about what he wanted in Medina. Then they invited him to their religion, so he accepted their invitation and followed them in their religion, treated them honorably, and left Medina. He set out with them and a group of Jews, heading for Yemen. On the way, some people from Hudhayl came to him and said: We will guide you to a house in which there is a treasure of pearls, emeralds, and silver. He said: Which house? They said: A house in Mecca, and the Hudhayl only wanted to destroy it because they knew that no one had ever harmed it except that he perished. So he mentioned that to the rabbis, and they said: We do not know of any house of God on earth other than this house, so make it a mosque and perform rituals there, and slaughter and shave your head. The people only wanted your destruction because no one had ever opposed them except that he perished, so honor him and do for him what his people do. So when they said that to him, he took the group of Hudhayl and cut off their hands and feet and put out their eyes and then crucified them. When he arrived in Mecca, he settled in the valley of the marshes and covered the house with wasail, and he was the first to cover the house. He slaughtered six thousand camels in the valley, and stayed in it for six days and circumambulated it and shaved and left. When he approached Yemen to enter it, the Himyar prevented him from doing so. They said: Do not enter upon us, for you have abandoned our religion. So he called them to his religion and said that it is a religion better than your religion. They said: Then judge us before the fire. And there was a fire in Yemen at the bottom of a mountain to which they judged regarding their differences, and it would consume the oppressor. And do not harm the oppressed. Tubba’ said: You have been just. So the people went out with their idols and what they used to offer in their religion. The two rabbis went out with their copies of the Qur’an around their necks until they sat for the fire at the exit from which it came out. Then the fire came out and approached until it covered them, and it consumed the idols and what they offered with them, and whoever of the men of Himyar carried that. The two rabbis went out with their copies of the Qur’an around their necks, reciting the Torah, their foreheads sweating, and it did not harm them. The fire receded until it returned to the exit from which it came out. At that time, Himyar clapped its hands on their religion. And from there came the origin of Judaism in Yemen. Abu Hatim reported on the authority of Al-Raqashi, who said: Abu Karb As`ad Al-Himyari was from the Tubba`a tribe. He believed in the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, seven hundred years before he was sent as a prophet. He told us that Kaab used to say: God blamed his people, but did not blame him. Aisha used to say: Do not insult Tubba’, for he was a righteous man. Saeed bin Jubair said: He is the one who covered the Kaaba. Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah bin Fanjuwayh Al-Daynuri told us, Abu Bakr bin Malik Al-Qat’i told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Abu Zur’ah bin Amr bin Jarir told us on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Do not revile Tubba’, for he had become a Muslim. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told me, Ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Salim Al-Hamdani told us, Abu Al-Azhar Ahmad ibn Al-Azhar Al-Naysaburi told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not know whether Tubba was a prophet or not a prophet. “And those before them,” of the disbelieving nations, “We destroyed them. Indeed, they were criminals.”
44:38: 38. And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.
44:39: 39. We did not create them except with truth. It was said: It means with truth, which is the reward for obedience and the punishment for disobedience. But most of them do not know.
44:40: 40. The Day of Judgment, the day on which the Most Gracious judges between His servants, is their appointed time all together, on which the first and the last will meet.
44:41: 41. On the Day when no protector will avail another protector at all, that is, no relative will benefit his relative or ward off anything from him, nor will they be aided, that is, they will not be protected from God’s punishment.
44:42: 42. Except for those upon whom God has mercy, meaning the believers, for they intercede for one another. He is the Exalted in Might, in taking revenge on His enemies, the Most Merciful, to the believers.
44:44: 44. The food of the sinner [i.e. the one who commits sin], which is Abu Jahl.
44:45: 45. Like the dregs of black oil, “boiling in the bellies,” Ibn Kathir and Hafs read boiling with a ya, making the verb for boiling, and the others read it with a ta to feminize the tree, in the bellies, meaning the bellies of the infidels.
44:46: 46. Like boiling hot water, like hot water when it boils intensely. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Bakr Al-Abdusi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Hamdun bin Khalid bin Yazid told us, Sulayman bin Yusuf told us, Wahb bin Jarir told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O people, fear God as He should be feared. If a drop of Zaqqum were to fall on the earth, it would make the livelihood of the people of this world miserable. So how about someone whose food is from it but who has no other food?”
44:47: 47. The Almighty’s saying: Take him meaning it will be said to the guards: Take him, meaning the sinner, and ride him, the people of Kufa, Abu Ja`far, and Abu `Amr read it with a kasra on the ta’, and the rest read it with a damma, and they are two dialects, meaning push him and drive him, it is said: `atala ya`talahu `atlan, if he drives him violently, pushing, and pulling, to the middle of Hell, its center.
44:48: 48. Then they poured over his head the torment of scalding water. Muqatil said, The keeper of Hellfire strikes him on the head, piercing his head to reveal his brain, then pours over him scalding water whose heat has reached the utmost.
44:49: 49. Then it will be said to him: Taste, this torment, for you, Al-Kisa’i read, for you with a fat-ha on the alif, meaning because you were saying: I am the Mighty, and the others read it with a kasra on it as an introductory word, for you are the Mighty, the Generous, according to your people, as you claim. That is because Abu Jahl used to say: I am the most honored and generous of the people of the valley, so the keepers of Hell would say to him, as a way of contempt and rebuke.
44:50: 50. This is what you were doubting, you were doubting it and not believing it. Then he mentioned the abode of the righteous, saying:
44:51: 51. Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure position. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read: (in a position) with a damma on the meem as a source, meaning in a residence. The others read it with a fatha on the meem, meaning in a secure assembly, in which they are safe from others, meaning from death and from leaving it.
44:53: 53. They will wear fine silk and heavy brocade, facing each other.
44:54: 54. Likewise, We married them to beautiful women, that is, just as We honored them with what We described of gardens, springs, and clothing, likewise We honored them by marrying them to hoor al-‘ayn, that is, We coupled them with them. The marriage is not valid, because it is not said: He married him to a woman. Abu Ubaidah said: We made them husbands to them as a husband marries a husband, that is, We made them two by two. Hawwar means pure white women. Mujahed said: The eye is dazzled by their whiteness and purity of color. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Houri is the one with intense white eyes and intense blackness. The singular is ahwar, and a woman is hawra’, and al-‘ayn is the plural of al-‘ayna’, which means large eyes.
44:55: 55. They will call therein for every fruit they desire, safe from its exhaustion and harm. Qatada said: Safe from death, ailments, and devils.
44:56: 56. They will not taste death therein except the first death, meaning other than the death they tasted in this world. After that, He placed except in place of except and after. This is like the saying of God Almighty: And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred. (An-Nisa’: 22), meaning other than what has already occurred, and after what has already occurred. It was said that He excluded the first death, which is in this world, from death in Paradise because when the happy ones die, they are transferred, by God’s grace, to the causes of Paradise. They encounter the spirit and basil and see their homes in Paradise. So their death in this world is as if they are in Paradise due to their connection to its causes and their witnessing of it. And He will protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.
44:57: 57. A favor from your Lord, meaning that He did this to them as a favor from Him. That is the great attainment.
44:58: 58. We have only made it easy, meaning We made the Qur’an easy, a metaphor for something not mentioned, with your tongue, meaning on your tongue, that they may remember, that is, take heed.
44:59: 59. Then wait, so wait for victory from your Lord. And it was said: Then wait for their punishment. They are waiting, so they claim, waiting for your defeat. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Fanjuwayh told me, Yahya bin Muhammad bin Yahya told us, Abu Isa Musa bin Ali Al-Khatli told us, Abu Hashim Al-Rafa’i told us, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Umar bin Abdullah bin Abi Khatham told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Ha-Mim Ad-Dukhan at night, seventy thousand angels will ask forgiveness for him in the morning.
45:2: 2. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
45:3: 3. Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.
45:4: 4. And in your creation and what He disperses of moving creatures are signs, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read: (signs) (and the direction of the winds are signs) with a kasra on the ta’ in both of them in response to his saying: (signs) which is in the accusative case, and the others read them with a nominative case as a resumption, based on the fact that the Arabs say: I have money on you and your brother has money, they place the second in the accusative case and raise it, for a people who are certain, that there is no god but Him.
45:5: 5. And the alternation of night and day and what God sends down from the sky of provision, meaning the rain that is the reason for the servants’ provisions, and thereby He revives the earth after its lifelessness and the directing of the winds are signs for a people who reason.
45:6: 6. These are the verses of God which We recite to you in truth, meaning that what We have related to you of the verses of God, We relate them to you in truth, Then in what statement after God, after the Book of God, and His verses will they believe? Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Abu Bakr, and Ya’qub read: (you believe) with a ta’, meaning say to them, O Muhammad: Then in what statement will you believe? The others read it with a ya’.
45:7: 7. Woe to every slanderer and sinner, a liar and sinner, meaning: Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith.
45:8: 8. "He hears the verses of God recited to him, then he persists in arrogance as if he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.
45:9: 9. And if he learns of Our verses, Muqatil said: of the Qur’an, “he takes it in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment.” He mentioned the plural form in response to all in his statement: for every slanderer and sinner.
45:10: 10. Behind them, in front of them, is Hell, meaning that in this world they will enjoy their wealth, and in the Hereafter they will enter the Fire. And what they have earned will not avail them at all, nor will what they have taken as protectors besides God, nor what they have worshipped besides God of gods. And for them is a great punishment.
45:11: 11. This, meaning this Qur’an, is guidance, a statement against misguidance, and those who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord will have a painful punishment.
45:12: 12. It is God who has subjected the sea to you that ships may sail therein by His command and that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
45:13: 13. And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and the meaning of subjugating is that He created them for their own benefits. It is subject to us so that we may benefit from it, all from Him, so do not make rivals to God. Ibn Abbas said: all from Him, all of that is mercy from Him. Al-Zajjaj said: All of that is favor and kindness from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
45:15: 15. “Whoever does righteousness does so for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever does evil does so against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.”
45:16: 16. And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture, the Torah, and wisdom and prophethood, and provided for them of the good things, the lawful things, meaning manna and quails, and preferred them over the worlds, meaning the worldly people of their time. Ibn Abbas said: No one among the worlds in their time was more honored by God or more beloved to Him than them.
45:17: 17. And We gave them clear proofs of the matter, meaning knowledge of the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what was explained to them about his matter, “but they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of jealous animosity between themselves. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.”
45:18: 18. Then We made you, [O Muhammad], upon a law, a way and a method after Moses, of the matter, of the religion, so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know, meaning the intention of the disbelievers, and that is because they were saying to him: Return to the religion of your fathers, for they were better than you, so the Most High said:
45:19: 19. They will never protect you from God at all, [they will never protect you from God’s punishment at all] if you follow their desires, and indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, and God is the ally of the righteous.
45:20: 20. This, meaning the Qur’an, is insight for the people, [signposts for the people] regarding the limits and rulings by which they may see, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain.
45:21: 21. Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We should treat them like those who believe and do righteous deeds? This verse was revealed about a group of polytheists from Mecca who said to the believers: If what you say is true, We will surely excel you in the Hereafter just as We excelled you in this world. Their life is the same. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Hafs, and Ya'qub read it as the same in the accusative case, meaning: We will make them the same. That is, do you think that the life and death of the disbelievers are like the life and death of the believers? No. The others read it in the nominative case as the subject and predicate, meaning their life and death are the same. The pronoun in both refers to the believers and the disbelievers alike. Its meaning is: The believer is a believer in his life and death, that is, in this world and the hereafter, and the disbeliever is a disbeliever in this world and the hereafter. Evil is what they judge. Evil is what they decide. Masruq said: A man from the people of Mecca said to me: This is the position of your brother Tamim Ad-Dari. I saw him one night, until morning, or almost morning, reciting a verse from the Book of God, bowing and prostrating with it, and weeping. Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds?
45:22: 22. And God created the heavens and the earth in truth so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
45:23: 23. Have you seen he who has taken his desire as his god? Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Qatada said: This is the disbeliever who has taken as his religion what he desires, so he does not desire anything except that he does it because he does not believe in God, nor fear Him, nor forbid what God has forbidden. Others said: Its meaning is that he has taken his desire as his god, so he worships what his soul desires. Saeed bin Jubair said: The Arabs used to worship stones, gold and silver. If they found something better than the first, they would throw it away or break it and worship the other. Al-Shaabi said: It is called desire because it causes its owner to fall into the fire. And God sent him astray with knowledge, from Him, of the consequences of his action. It was said that it was based on what preceded in His knowledge that he was astray before He created him. And He sealed He stamped his hearing, so he did not hear the guidance, and his heart, so he did not understand the guidance. And He placed over his vision a veil, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read it with a fatha on the ghain and a sukoon on the sheen. The rest read it with a veil, meaning darkness, so he does not see the guidance. So who will guide him after God? [i.e., who will guide him] after God sent him astray. So will you not remember?
45:24: 24. And they said, meaning those who denied the resurrection, It is not but our worldly life, meaning what is life but our worldly life. We die and we live, meaning the fathers die and the sons live. Al-Zajjaj said: It means we die and we live, so the waw is for gathering. And nothing destroys us except time, meaning nothing destroys us except the passage of time, the length of life, and the alternation of night and day. And they have no knowledge of that, what they said, that they did not say it based on knowledge [that they knew], “they are only guessing. Abu Ali Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abdul-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty said: ‘The son of Adam should not say, ‘Oh, what a disappointment this time is!’ For I am Time. I send the night and the day, and if I wish, I take them away.’” Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzaz told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Dabry told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let none of you curse time, for God is time, and let no one say of grapes ‘vineyard’, for the vineyard is the Muslim man. The meaning of the hadith is that it was the custom of the Arabs to criticize time and curse it when calamities afflicted them, because they would attribute to it the misfortunes and hardships that befell them, and they would say: The calamities of time befell them, and time destroyed them, as God Almighty said about them: And nothing destroys us except time. So if they attributed to time the hardships that befell them, they would curse the one who caused them, so their cursing would be attributed to God Almighty, since He is the one who actually causes the things that they attribute to time, [so they were forbidden from cursing time].
45:25: 25. And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is that they say, 'Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful.'
45:26: 26. Say, ‘God gives you life, then causes you to die, then He will assemble you for the Day of Resurrection.’ There is no doubt about it, but most people do not know.
45:27: 27. “To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And on the Day the Hour comes - that Day the falsifiers will lose,” meaning the unbelievers who are the people of falsehoods. On that Day their loss will become apparent when they go to the Fire.
45:28: 28. And you will see every nation kneeling, kneeling on its knees, which is the position of a litigant before a judge awaiting judgment. Salman Al-Farsi said: There is an hour on the Day of Resurrection that will last for ten years, in which people will fall on their knees, even Abraham, peace be upon him, will call out to his Lord: I ask You for nothing but myself. Every nation will be called to its book, which contains its deeds. Jacob read every nation in the accusative case, and they will be told: This day you will be recompensed for what you used to do.
45:29: 29. This is Our Book, meaning the register of the guardian angels, that speaks against you with the truth, testifying against you with clear evidence, as if it were speaking. It was said that what is meant by the Book is the Preserved Tablet. Indeed, We were transcribing what you used to do, meaning We commanded the angels to transcribe your deeds, that is, to write them down and record them for you. It was said: We copy, meaning we take a copy of it. This is because the two angels raise the deeds of the person, and God confirms from it what he had a reward or punishment for, and removes from it the idle talk such as their saying: Come and go. It was said: Copying from the Preserved Tablet. The angels copy every year the deeds of the sons of Adam, and copying only occurs from an original, so a book is copied from a book. Ad-Dahhak said: We copy, meaning we record. As-Suddi said: We write. Al-Hasan said: We memorize.
45:30: 30. “As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear triumph.” [The Victory] is apparent.
45:31: 31. As for those who disbelieved, it will be said to them, Were not My verses recited to you, and you were arrogant and were a criminal people? Arrogant and disbelieving.
45:32: 32. And when it is said, ‘The promise of God is true, and there is no doubt about the Hour,’ Hamza read: and the Hour, in the accusative case, in apposition to the promise. The others read it in the nominative case as the subject. “You say, ‘We do not know what the Hour is. We only think,’” meaning, “We do not know that except by intuition and imagination. “And we are not certain,” that it will happen.
45:33: 33. And the evils of what they did will appear to them, [in the Hereafter], and what they used to ridicule will overtake them.
45:34: 34. And it will be said, ‘Today We will forget you,’ meaning, We will leave you in the Fire, just as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours,’ meaning, you abandoned faith and action to meet this Day, and your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers.
45:35: 35. That is because you took the verses of God in jest, and the worldly life deceived you, until you said: There is no resurrection and no reckoning. So today they will not come out of it, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read it with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the ra’, and the others read it with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the ra’. Nor will they be asked to repent, they will not be asked to return to the obedience of God, because on that day He will not accept any excuse or repentance.
45:36: 36. So praise be to God, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.
45:37: 37. And to Him belongs pride, the greatness, “in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Sayyid Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Alawi told us, Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Sharqi told us, Ahmad ibn Hafs, Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Farra’ and Qatan ibn Ibrahim told us, they said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Abdullah, Ibrahim ibn Tahman told me, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of al-Agharr Abu Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty says: Pride is My cloak, and greatness is My garment. Whoever disputes with Me over one of them, I will cast him into Hellfire.”
46:2: 2. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
46:3: 3. We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term, meaning the Day of Resurrection, which is the term at which the heavens and the earth will come to an end, and it is a reference to their annihilation. And those who disbelieve - from that of which they were warned, with which they were warned in the Qur’an of the resurrection and the reckoning, are turning away.
46:4: 4. Say, 'Have you considered what you invoke besides God? Show me what they have created on the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Bring me a book before this,' meaning, a book that came to you from God before the Qur'an, which explains what you say, or a trace of knowledge, Al-Kalbi said: meaning, a remnant of knowledge transmitted from the first peoples, meaning, it is attributed to them. Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Muqatil said: narration from the prophets. Qatada said: specifically from knowledge. The root of the word is from athar, which means narration. It is said: I transmitted the hadith, athar, and athara, and from this, the report is called athar. If you should be truthful.
46:5: 5. And who is more astray than he who calls upon those besides God who do not respond to him, meaning the idols do not respond to their worshippers regarding anything they ask of them, until the Day of Resurrection, forever as long as the world exists, and they are unaware of their call, because they are inanimate and do not hear or understand.
46:6: 6. And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship, denying it. This is explained by His statement: We disavow to You that they used to worship us Al-Qasas 63.
46:7: 7. And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, ‘This is obvious magic.’ They call the Qur’an magic.
46:8: 8. Or do they say, 'He invented it,' Muhammad himself, then God Almighty said: Say, 'If I have invented it, then you will not possess for me anything against God,' you will not be able to avert His punishment from me if He punishes me for my fabrication, so how can I invent a fabrication against God for your sake? He is most knowing of what you indulge in,' you indulge in by denying the Qur'an and saying that it is magic. It is sufficient as a witness between me and you, that the Qur’an came from Him, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, in delaying the punishment for you. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a call for them to repent, meaning: God Almighty is Forgiving and Merciful to whoever among you repents.
46:9: 9. Say, ‘I am not an innovation among the messengers,’ meaning, I am not an innovation among the messengers, like: half and half, and the plural of innovations is innovations. “I am not the first messenger, many prophets were sent before me, so how can you deny my prophethood?” And I do not know what will be done with me or with you, scholars differed regarding the meaning of this verse: Some of them said: It means I do not know what will be done to me or to you on the Day of Resurrection. When this verse was revealed, the polytheists rejoiced and said: By Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, our command and the command of Muhammad are but one in the sight of God, and he has no superiority or favor over us. Had he not innovated what he said of his own accord, the One Who sent him would have informed him of what would be done to him. So God revealed: {That God may forgive you your sins, past and future} (al-Fath 48:2). The Companions said: Congratulations, O Prophet of God! We know what will be done to you, so what will be done to us? So God revealed: {That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens} (al-Fath 48:5), and He also revealed: {And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from God great bounty} (al-Ahzab 33:47). So God explained what will be done to him and to them. This is the saying of Anas, Qatadah, Al-Hasan and Ikrimah. They said: He only said this before he was informed that his sin would be forgiven [and he only informed that his sin would be forgiven] in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, so that was abrogated. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Kharijah ibn Zayd, who said: Umm al-Ala’ al-Ansariyya used to say: “When the Muhajirun came to Medina, the Ansar drew lots for their dwellings. She said: ‘Uthman ibn Maz’un was given a place to live, and he became ill, so we nursed him. Then he died. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered, so I said: ‘May God have mercy on you, Abu al-Sa’ib, for my testimony is that God has honored you.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And how do you know that God has honored him?’ I said: ‘No, by God, I do not know.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘As for him, certainty has come to him from his Lord, and I hope for good for him. By God, I do not know, and I am the Messenger of God, what will be done to me or to you.’ She said: ‘By God, I will never vouch for anyone after him.’ She said: ‘Then I saw a flowing spring for Uthman in a dream, so I told the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. ’” And he said: That is his work. A group said: His statement, And I do not know what will be done with me or with you in this world. As for the Hereafter, he knows that he is in Paradise, and that whoever denies him is in Hell. Then they differed about it: Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: When the affliction intensified for the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw in a dream while he was in Mecca a land with salt marshes and palm trees being shown to him, so he could migrate to it. His companions said to him, When will you migrate to the land you have shown me? He remained silent. Then God, the Most High, revealed this verse: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you. Should I stay where I am or should I go out with you to the land that has been shown to me? Some of them said: I do not know what will be done to me or to you. What will become of my affair and your affair in this world? Either I will go out as the prophets before me were brought out, or I will be killed as the prophets before me were killed. And you, the believers, I do not know whether you will go out with me or be left alone, or what will be done to you, [and you], the disbelievers. Will stones be thrown from the sky or will the earth swallow you up? Or what will be done to you, as was done to the nations of disbelievers? Then God Almighty informed us that He would make His religion prevail over all religions, saying: It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions (al-Saff 61:9). And He said about his nation: And God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would He punish them while they seek forgiveness (al-Anfal 8:33). So God informed us of what He would do to him and his nation. This is what As-Suddi said. I only follow what is revealed to me, meaning I only follow the Qur’an, and I do not innovate anything of my own, and I am only a clear warner.
46:10: 10. “Say, ‘Have you considered,’ meaning: Tell me what you would say, ‘if it,’ meaning the Qur’an, ‘is from God and you disbelieved in it,’ O polytheists, ‘and a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it,’ ‘like’ is a relative clause, meaning: upon it, that is, that it is from God, ‘and he believed,’ meaning the witness, ‘and you were arrogant,’ about believing in it. The answer to His statement, ‘if it is from God,’ is omitted, based on the estimation: Have you not wronged? This omission is indicated by His statement, ‘Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people,’ and Al-Hasan said: Its answer is, who is more astray than you, as He said in Surat As-Sajdah. They differed about this witness. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: He is Abdullah bin Salam. He bore witness to the prophethood of the Chosen One, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believed in him, but the Jews were arrogant and did not believe. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Munir told us, he heard Abdullah bin Bakir, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: “Abdullah bin Salam heard of the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in a land collecting dung beetles, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘I will ask you about three things that only a prophet knows: What is the first sign of the Hour? What is the first food of the people of Paradise? And what makes a child follow his father or his mother?’ He said: ‘Gabriel told me about them just now.’ He said: ‘Gabriel?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘That is the enemy of the Jews from the angels.’ Then he recited this verse: ‘Say, “Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - for indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by God’s permission.” Al-Baqarah 2:97. As for the first sign of the Hour, it is a fire that will gather people from the east to the west. As for the first food that the people of Paradise will eat, it is the extra liver of a fish. If a woman’s semen precedes, the child is taken, and if a woman’s semen precedes, the child is taken.’ He said: ‘I bear witness that there is no god but God.’” Except God and that you are Muhammad the Messenger of God. [O Messenger of God], the Jews are a people of slander, and if they know that I have become Muslim before you ask them, they will slander me. So the Jews came and he said: What kind of man is Abdullah among you? They said: The best of us and the son of the best of us, our master and the son of our master. He said: What do you think if Abdullah ibn Salam becomes Muslim? They said: May God protect him from that. So Abdullah came out and said: I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. They said: The worst of us and the son of the worst of us, and they belittled him. He said: This is what I feared, O Messenger of God. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Abdullah bin Yusuf informed us: I heard Malik narrating on the authority of Abu Al-Nadr, the freed slave of Umar bin Ubaidullah, on the authority of Amir bin Saad bin Abi Waqqas, on the authority of his father, who said: I never heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say about anyone walking on the earth that he was from the people of Hannah except Abdullah bin Salam, and this verse was revealed about him: And a witness from among the Children of Israel testified to the like of it. He said: I do not know whether Malik said the verse or the hadith. Others said the witness is Moses, son of Imran. Al-Sha’bi said: Masruq said about this verse: By God, it was not revealed about Abdullah bin Salam, because Ha Mim was revealed in Mecca. Rather, Abdullah bin Salam converted to Islam in Medina. This verse was revealed regarding an argument that took place between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his people. The Qur’an is like the Torah, so Moses testified to the Torah and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, testified to the Criterion, and each one confirms the other. It was said: He is a prophet from the Children of Israel, so he believed, but you were arrogant and did not believe. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
46:11: 11. And those who disbelieved, from among the Jews, said to those who believed, ‘If it had been any good, they would not have preceded us in it,’ meaning Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions. Qatada said: It was revealed about the polytheists of Mecca. They said: If what Muhammad was calling us to was good, so-and-so and so-and-so would not have preceded us to it. Al-Kalbi said: Those who disbelieved were Asad and Ghatafan. They said to those who believed, meaning Juhayna and Muzayna: If what Muhammad brought was good, the shepherds of the camels would not have preceded us to it. God Almighty said: And when they are not guided by it, meaning by the Qur’an as the people of faith were guided by it, they will say, ‘This is an ancient falsehood,’ just as they said the legends of the ancients.
46:12: 12. And before it meaning before the Qur’an, the Book of Moses meaning the Torah, as an imam to be followed, and a mercy from God for whoever believes in it. The word and is in the accusative case according to Al-Kisa’i. Abu Ubaidah said: There is an omission in it, meaning We made it an imam and a mercy, and there is something omitted in the statement, the meaning of which is: And the Book of Moses preceded it as an imam, and they were not guided by it, as He said in the first verse: And when they were not guided by it. “And this is a confirming Book,” meaning the Qur’an confirms the books that came before it, in the Arabic tongue, in the accusative case as a state, and it was said that it was in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who did wrong, meaning the polytheists of Mecca. The people of Hijaz, Syria, and Jacob read: to warn with a ta’ as addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The others read it with a ya’, meaning the Book, and good tidings for the doers of good, “and good tidings” in the nominative case, meaning this is a confirming Book and good tidings.
46:13: 13. Indeed, those who have said, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remained on a right course - no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
46:14: 14. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein eternally as reward for what they used to do.
46:15: 15. The Almighty said: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. The people of Kufa read: (ihsanan) [like the Almighty's saying: And to parents, good treatment Al-Baqarah 2:83] His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, meaning the severity of the labor pains. The people of Hijaz and Abu Amr read (kharaan) with a fatha on the kaf in both, while the others read it with a damma. And his pregnancy and his weaning, meaning his weaning. Ya'qub read: (and his weaning) without an alif, thirty months, meaning the minimum period of pregnancy, which is six months, and the maximum period of breastfeeding is twenty-four months. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: If a woman is pregnant for nine months, she breastfeeds for twenty-one months, and if she is pregnant for six months, she breastfeeds for twenty-four months: until he reaches his full strength, the peak of his strength, the height of his youth and maturity, which is between eighteen and forty years. This is what His saying: and reaches forty years. Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed about Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, and the story has already been mentioned. Others said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, his father Abu Quhafa Uthman bin Amr, and his mother Umm Al-Khair bint Sakhr bin Amr. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: The verse was revealed about Abu Bakr. Both of his parents converted to Islam, and no one among the emigrants had both parents except him. God commanded him to take care of them, and this remained the case after him. Abu Bakr accompanied the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) when he was eighteen years old, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was twenty years old, on a trade trip to Syria. When he reached forty years of age and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was a prophet, he believed in him and supplicated to his Lord, saying, My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, with guidance and faith, and to do righteousness of which You approve. Ibn Abbas said, “God answered him, so he freed nine believers who were being tortured for the sake of God, and he did not desire any good without God helping him in it. He also supplicated, saying, “And make righteous for me my offspring,” and God answered him, and he had no children who did not all believe. Thus, the Islam of his parents and all his children was united for him. Abu Quhafah lived to see the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and his son Abu Bakr, his son Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, and Abdur-Rahman Abu Atiq all lived to see the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and this did not happen to any of the Companions. He said, Indeed, I repent to You, and I am of the Muslims.
46:16: 16. Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did, meaning their righteous deeds that they did in this world, all of which are good. The best means good, so He rewards them for them. And overlook their misdeeds, so We do not punish them for them. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read We accept and We overlook with a nun, “the best” in the accusative case. The others read it with a ya, with a damma, “the best” in the nominative case. Among the companions of Paradise, with the companions of Paradise, the promise of truth which they were promised, which is the saying of God Almighty: God has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow (al-Tawbah 9:72).
46:17: 17. And he who said to his parents, when they called him to believe in God and to acknowledge the resurrection, Fie upon you both, which is a word of hatred, Do you promise me that I will come forth, from my grave alive, while generations before me have passed away, and none of them were resurrected, while they both cried out to God, crying out for help and calling upon God against him, and saying to him, “Woe to you! Believe. Indeed, the promise of God is true.” He said, What is this, what is this that you are calling me to, except legends of the ancients? Ibn Abbas, Al-Suddi, and Mujahid said: It was revealed about Abdullah. It was said: Regarding Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr before his conversion to Islam, his parents were calling him to Islam, but he refused and said: Bring back for me Abd God ibn Jud’an, Amir ibn Ka’b, and the elders of Quraysh so that I may ask them about what you say. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, denied that this was the case with Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr. The correct view is that it was revealed about an unbeliever who was disobedient to his parents, as stated by Al-Hasan and Qatada. Al-Zajjaj said: The statement of those who said that it was revealed about Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr before his conversion to Islam is invalidated by his statement:
46:18: 18. Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect, the verse. God Almighty knows that the word of punishment has come into effect upon them, and Abd al-Rahman is a believer among the best of Muslims, so he is not among those upon whom the word of punishment has come into effect. The meaning of (those upon whom the word has come into effect) is that the punishment is due upon them, among nations, [with nations], “that have passed away before them of the jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.”
46:19: 19. And for all are degrees according to what they have done. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He means those who were the first to embrace Islam, for they are better than those who stayed behind, even if only by an hour. Muqatil said: And for all are virtues, and God will fully reward them for their deeds. It was said: And for each: meaning, for each of the two groups, the believers and the unbelievers, there are degrees: stations and ranks with God on the Day of Resurrection based on their deeds, and He will reward them for them. Ibn Zayd said about this verse: The steps of the people of Hell go downwards, and the steps of the people of Paradise go upwards. And that He may fully reward them for their deeds, and they will not be wronged. Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra, and Asim read it with the letter ya, while the rest read it with the letter nun.
46:20: 20. And the Day those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire, it will be said to them, Did you consume your good things in your worldly life? Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Ja`far, and Ya`qub read it as did you consume? as a question. Ibn Amir pronounces it twice with a hamza, while the others do not pronounce it without a question, as a statement. Both are eloquent, because the Arabs inquire with a rebuke and leave out the question, so they say, Did you consume and do such-and-such? and Did you consume and do such-and-such? “And did you enjoy them?” He says, Did you consume your good things, meaning the pleasures, and enjoy them? “So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation,” meaning the punishment that includes humiliation and disgrace, because you were arrogant, [you were arrogant], on earth without right and because you were wicked. So when God rebuked the disbelievers for enjoying the good things in this world, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his companions, and the righteous preferred to avoid pleasures in this world in the hope of reward in the Hereafter. We narrated on the authority of Omar who said: “I entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was lying on a sandy mat with sand marks on his side. I said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to grant your nation plenty, for the Persians and the Romans have been granted plenty, and they do not worship God. He said: Those are people who hastened their good things in the life of this world.” Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juwzjani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, Abu Saeed Al-Haytham bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna and Muhammad bin Bashar told us, they said: Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: I heard Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid narrating, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Yazid, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: A family did not eat their fill of barley bread for two consecutive days until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away.
