Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran told us, Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: A month would come upon us in which we would not light a fire, and there would be nothing but water and dates, except that God rewarded some women of the Ansar with goodness, and they would sometimes give us some milk as a gift. Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juwzjani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Khuza’i told us, Al-Haitham bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Abdullah bin Mu’awiyah Al-Jumahi told us, Thabit bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Khabab, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would spend consecutive nights hungry, and his family would not find dinner, and most of their bread was barley bread. Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juwzjani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Khuza’i told us, Al-Haitham bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa told us, Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman told us, Rawh bin Aslam told us, Abu Hatim Al-Basri told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was afraid for God’s sake, and no one would be afraid. I was harmed for God’s sake, and no one would be harmed. Thirty days and nights passed me by, and Bilal and I had no food that a man would eat, except for something that Bilal hid under his armpit.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, [Muhammad bin Ismail told us] Yusuf bin Isa told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I saw seventy of the people of the Suffah, and none of them had a cloak, either an izar or a cloak, and they had tied it around their necks, some of which reached halfway up the shins, and some of which reached the ankles, and he gathered it with his hand, not wanting his private parts to be seen. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba al-Kashmihani told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn al-Harith told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Shu’bah ibn al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Ibrahim, [on the authority of his father Ibrahim] that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf was brought food while he was fasting, so he said: Mus’ab ibn Umair was killed, and he was better than me, so he was shrouded in a cloak; if his head was covered with it, his feet would show, and if his feet were covered with it, his head would show. He said: And I think he said: Hamza was killed, and he was better than me, so nothing was found to shroud him in except a cloak. Then he spread out for us from the world what he spread out, or he said we were given from the world what we were given, and we feared that our good deeds had been hastened for us. Then he began to cry until he left the food. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: Omar ibn al-Khattab saw some meat hanging from my hand, so he said: What is this, Jabir? I said: I craved meat so I bought it. Omar said: Or do you buy it whenever you crave something, Jabir? Aren’t you afraid of this verse: You have spent your good things in your worldly life.
46:21: 21. The Almighty said: And remember the brother of Aad, meaning Hud, peace be upon him, when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf, Ibn Abbas said: Al-Ahqaf is a valley between Oman and Mahra. Muqatil said: The homes of Ad were in Yemen, in Hadhramaut, in a place called Mahra, to which the Mahri camels are attributed. They were people of pillars that moved in the spring, and when the weather was hot, they returned to their homes. They were from the tribe of Iram. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Aad tribe lived in Yemen, and they were people of sand overlooking the sea in a land called Ash-Shihr. “Al-Ahqaf” is the plural of Haqf, which is the curved, rectangular sand. Ibn Zayd said: It is the elongated sand like a mountain, but it did not reach the level of being a mountain. Al-Kisa’i said: It is the rounded sand. And the warnings have passed away, the messengers have passed away, before him, that is, before Hud, and behind him, to his people, “that you should not worship except God. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible Day.”
46:22: 22. “They said, ‘Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?’ [To divert us], ‘Then bring us what you promise us,’ [of punishment], ‘if you should be of the truthful,’ that the punishment is coming upon us.”
46:23: 23. He said, Hud, knowledge is only with God, and He knows when the punishment will come to you. And I convey to you that with which I have been sent, of revelation, but I see that you are a people behaving ignorantly.
46:24: 24. So when they saw it, meaning the punishment they were promised, as a cloud, a cloud that appears in one part of the sky and then covers the sky, facing their valleys, a black cloud came out upon them from a valley of theirs called Al-Mughith, and the rain had been withheld from them. When they saw it, they were filled with good tidings, They said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain,’ God Almighty says: Rather, it is that for which you were hastening, a wind within which is a painful punishment, so the wind carried the tent and the woman traveling with it until they looked like locusts.
46:25: 25. Destroy everything, the men of Ad and their wealth passed through, [by the command of their Lord]. The first thing they knew that it was a punishment was that they saw what was coming out of their homes of men and livestock being blown away by the wind between the sky and the earth. So they entered their homes and closed their doors, and the wind came and tore their doors apart and they were thrown down. Then God commanded the wind, and it blew the sands upon them, and they were under the sand for seven nights and eight days, groaning. Then God commanded the wind, and it removed the sands from them, and they were carried away, and the sea threw them into it. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us, Abu Nu`aym `Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Asfarayni informed us, Abu `Awanah Ya`qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz informed us, Yunus informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, `Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, al-Nadr informed us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, on the authority of `Aishah, that she said: “I never saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughing so much that I could see the whiteness of his uvula. Whenever he saw a cloud or a wind, you could tell by it on his face. So I said: ‘O Messenger of God, when people see a cloud, they rejoice, hoping that it will rain, but when you see it, you can tell by your face that you are displeased.’ He said: ‘O `Aishah, what reassures me that it will not be a punishment? Some people were punished by wind, and some people saw a punishment and said: “This is a cloud bringing us rain” the verse. So nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Asim, Hamza, and Ya’qub read it as yaree with a damma on the ya’, masakinumi with a damma on the noon, meaning: nothing could be seen except their dwellings. The others read it with a ta’ and a fatha on it, masakinumi in the accusative case, meaning you, O Muhammad, could see nothing except their dwellings, because the inhabitants and livestock were destroyed by the wind, and nothing remained except Hud and those who believed with him. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
46:26: 26. And We have empowered them in that in which We have not empowered you, meaning in that in which We have not empowered you, such as physical strength, long life, and abundant wealth. Al-Mubarrad said: What in his statement in what is like which, and if is like what, and its meaning is: And We empowered them in that in which We did not empower them. And We gave them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing and sight and hearts availed them not at all when they denied the signs of God, and that which they used to ridicule encompassed them.
46:27: 27. And We destroyed what was around you, O people of Mecca, of towns, such as the rock of Thamud and the land of Sodom and the like, and We diversified the signs, the arguments and clear proofs, that perhaps they would return, from their disbelief. But they did not return, so We destroyed them, frightening the polytheists of Mecca.
46:28: 28. Why then, why then did not those who took other than God as offerings support them, meaning idols, they took them as gods by which they draw near to God Almighty, (offering): everything by which one draws near to God Almighty, and its plural is (offerings), like monks and monks. Rather, they have gone astray from them, Muqatil said: Rather, the gods have gone astray from them and did not benefit them when the punishment descended upon them. And that is their lie, meaning their lie that they used to say would bring them closer to God Almighty and intercede for them. And what they used to invent, they used to lie that they were gods.
46:29: 29. The Almighty said: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an (al-Baqarah 2:17). The commentators said: When Abu Talib died, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out alone to Taif, seeking support and protection from Thaqeef from his people. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Taif, he met a group of Thaqeef, who were at that time the leaders and nobles of Thaqeef, and they were three brothers: Abd Yalil, Mas’ud, and Habib, sons of Amr ibn Umair. One of them had a woman from the Quraysh from Banu Jumah, so he sat with them and called them to God and spoke to them about what had come to him of his support for Islam and standing with him against those of his people who opposed him. One of them said to him: He is tearing the cloths of the Kaaba, if God has sent you. Another said: God did not find anyone to send but you. The third said: By God, I will never say a word to you. If you are a messenger from God, as you say, then you are too dangerous for me to respond to you. If you are lying about God, then it is not appropriate for me to speak to you. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rose from them, having despaired of any good from Thaqif, and said to them: Since you have done what you have done, then conceal my secret from me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reluctant for his people to hear of it and that would make him do more harm, but they did not do so. They incited their fools and slaves against him, cursing him and shouting at him until the people gathered around him and forced him to take refuge in a garden belonging to Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi’ah, while they were in it. The fools of Thaqif and those who had followed him turned away from him, so he went to the shade of a grapevine and sat in it, while the two sons of Rabi’ah looked at him and saw what he had suffered from the fools of Thaqif. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had met that woman from Banu Jumah and said to her: What have we suffered from your in-laws? When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) felt reassured, he said: O God, I complain to You of my weakness, my lack of resources, and my insignificance among people. You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. You are the Lord of the weak, and You are my Lord. To whom will You entrust me? To a distant one who gathers me, or to an enemy to whom You have given control over my affairs? If You are not angry with me, then I do not care, but Your well-being is more expansive for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your face by which the darkness is illuminated, and by which the affairs of this world and the hereafter are set right, lest Your anger descend upon me or Your wrath befall me. To You is the reproach until You are pleased, and there is no power or strength except with You. When the two sons of Rabi’ah saw what had happened to him, their kinship was stirred, so they called for their Christian slave, whose name was Addas, and said to him, Take a bunch of grapes and put them on that plate, then go with them to that man and tell him to eat from it. Addas did so, then he brought them and placed them in front of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) placed his hand there, he said, In the name of God, and then ate. Addas looked at his face and said, By God, these are not the words of the people of this town. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, From which country are you, Addas? And what is your religion? He said, I am a Christian, and I am a man from Nineveh. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Are you from the town of the righteous man Yunus ibn Matta? He said, How do you know who Yunus ibn Matta was? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “That was my brother. He was a prophet, and I am a prophet.” Addas leaned over the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and kissed his head, hands, and feet. He said: The two sons of Rabi'ah said, one of them to his companion: As for your slave, he has corrupted him for you. So when Addas came to them, they said to him: Woe to you, Addas! Why do you kiss this man's head, hands and feet? He said: My master, there is no one on earth better than this man. He told me something that only a prophet would know. They said: Woe to you, Addas! Do not let him turn you away from your religion, for your religion is better than his. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, departed from Taif, returning to Mecca, when he had despaired of any good from Thaqeef. When he was at Nakhl, he rose in the middle of the night to pray. A group of jinn from Nasibin, Yemen, passed by him and listened to him. When he finished his prayer, they returned to their people as warners. They had believed and responded to what they had heard. God related their story to him, saying: And when We turned to you a group of the jinn. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musaddad told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with a group of his companions, intending to go to the market of ‘Ukaz. The devils were prevented from receiving report from heaven, so shooting stars were sent down upon them. The devils returned to their people and said: What is the matter with you? They said: We were prevented from receiving report from heaven, and shooting stars were sent down upon us. They said: Nothing has prevented you from receiving report from heaven except something that has happened. So travel to the east and west of the earth and see what is it that has prevented you from receiving report from heaven. So those who had headed towards Tihamah returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Nakhlah, intending to go to the market of ‘Ukaz, and he was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. When they heard the Qur’an, they listened attentively to it and said: This, by God, is what has prevented you from receiving report from heaven. So they returned to their people and said: O our people.” Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur’an. It guides to the right path, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate with our Lord anyone. (al-Jinn 72:2). Then God revealed to His Prophet: Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened.’ (al-Jinn 72:1). What was revealed to him was the words of the jinn. It was narrated that when they were stoned with meteors, Satan sent his troops to find out the report. The first of his troops was a group of people from Nasibin, who were the nobles and leaders of the jinn. He sent them to Tihamah. Abu Hamza [al-Thamali] said: We were informed that they were from the Shayban tribe, and they were the most numerous of the jinn, and they were the majority of Satan’s soldiers. When they returned, they said: We have heard an amazing Qur’an. A group said: Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to warn the jinn and call them to God Almighty and recite the Qur’an to them. So he sent a group of jinn from Nineveh to him, and gathered them together for him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been commanded to recite to the jinn tonight, so which of you will follow me? Then he asked them to follow him and they also followed him. Then he asked them to follow him a third time and they also continued to follow him. Abdullah ibn Mas`ud said: No one was with him except me, so we set off until we reached Mecca. The Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered a valley called the Valley of Al-Hujun. He drew a line for me and ordered me to sit in it and said: Do not leave it until I return to you. Then he set off until he stood up and began to recite the Qur’an. I began to see things like eagles descending and I heard a great uproar until I feared for the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Many black lions covered him and came between me and him until I could not hear his voice. Then they began to disperse like pieces of clouds, going away. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finished at dawn and came to me and said: Are you asleep? I said: No, by God, O Messenger of God. I thought many times to call for help from the people until I heard you hitting them with your staff, saying: Sit. He said: If you went out, I would not be safe from being snatched away by some of them. Then he said: Did you see anything? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God, I saw black men wearing white clothes. He said: Those are the jinn of Nasibin who asked me for provisions - and provisions are provisions - so I gave them every decayed bone, dung, and excrement. He said: They said: O Messenger of God, people find it disgusting. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade cleaning oneself with bones and dung. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, what good will that do them? He said: They do not find a bone without finding its flesh on it on the day it was eaten, nor a dung without finding its seeds in it on the day it was eaten. I said: O Messenger of God, I heard a great uproar. He said: The jinn argued about a murdered person among themselves, so they brought their case to me, and I judged between them justly. He said: Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) defecate and then came to me and said: Do you have any water with you? I said: O Messenger of God, I have a water skin in which is some date wine. He called for it and I poured it over his hand, so he performed ablution and said: Good dates and pure water. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that when Ibn Masoud came to Kufa, he saw some old men from the Zutt tribe, and they startled him when he saw them. He said: Come out! It was said to him: These are a group of Zutt tribe. He said: How similar they are to the group who were sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning the jinn. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul A’la told us, Dawud, who is Ibn Abi Hind, told us, on the authority of Aamer, who said: “I asked Alqamah, ‘Did Ibn Mas’ud witness the Night of the Jinn with the Messenger of God? ’ Alqamah said: ‘I asked Ibn Mas’ud, ‘Did any of you witness the Night of the Jinn with the Messenger of God? ’ He said: ‘No, but we were with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, one night, and we missed him, so we looked for him in the valleys and ravines, and we said: He was taken away or assassinated. ’ He said: ‘So we spent the worst night ever spent by a people. ’ When we woke up, he came from the direction of Hira. ’ We said: ‘O Messenger of God, we missed you and looked for you but did not find you. ’ We spent the worst night ever spent by a people. ’ He said: ‘A caller from the jinn came to me, so I went with him and recited the Qur’an to them. ’” He said: He set out with us and showed us their traces and the traces of their fires. He said: They asked him for provisions, and he said: Every bone on which the name of God has been mentioned that falls into your hands will have the most meat, and every dung will be fodder for your animals. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not use them for cleaning yourself, for they are the food of your brothers among the jinn. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Ali bin Hajar, who told us on the authority of Ismail bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Dawud, with this chain of transmission up to his saying: (and traces of their fires). Al-Sha’bi said: They asked him for provisions, and they were from the jinn of the peninsula, to the end of the hadith from Al-Sha’bi’s words, detailed from the hadith of Abdullah. God the Almighty said: And when We directed to you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an. They differed about the number of that group. Some say they were seven from the jinn of Nasibin, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made them messengers to their people. Others said they were nine. Asim narrated on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish: Zuba’ah was one of the nine who listened to the Qur’an. And when they attended it, they said, ‘Listen.’ They said, Shh. It was narrated in the hadith: “The jinn are of three types: a type that has wings with which they fly in the air, a type that is made up of snakes and dogs, and a type that is cunning and travels.” When they attended to him, some of them said to one another: Be quiet and listen to his recitation. Let nothing come between us and listening. So they listened and listened to the Qur’an until some of them almost fell on each other because of their eagerness. So when it was concluded, he finished reciting it, they turned back to their people, they turned to them, warning, frightening and calling out by the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
46:30: 30. They said, ‘O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it and guiding to the truth and to a straight path.’ Ata’ said: Their religion was Judaism, so they said: We have heard a Book revealed after Moses.
46:31: 31. O our people, respond to the caller of God, meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and believe in him, He will forgive you your sins, “of” is a relative pronoun, meaning your sins, and protect you from a painful punishment. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: About seventy men from among their people responded to them, so they returned to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and met him in al-Batha’. He recited the Qur’an to them and commanded and forbade them. This is evidence that he, peace and blessings be upon him, was sent to both jinn and mankind. Muqatil said: No prophet was sent before him to all of mankind and jinn. Scholars differed regarding the ruling on believing jinn. Some said: They have no reward except their salvation from the Fire. They interpreted the words: He will forgive you your sins and save you from a painful punishment. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, held this view. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Layth who said: The reward of the jinn is that they are saved from the Fire, then it is said to them: Become dust, and this is like the animals. On the authority of Abu Al-Zinad, he said: When judgment is passed between people, it will be said to the believing jinn: Return to dust. Then the unbeliever will say: Oh, I wish I were dust! An-Naba’ 40. Others said: They will be rewarded for their good deeds, just as they will be punished for their bad deeds, just like humans. This is what Malik and Ibn Abi Layla agreed with. Jarir said on the authority of Al-Dahhak: The jinn enter Paradise and eat and drink. Al-Naqqash mentioned in his Tafsir the hadith that they will enter Paradise. It was said: Will they enjoy any of its delights? He said: God inspires them to glorify and remember Him, and they enjoy any of its pleasures as the children of Adam enjoy any of the delights of Paradise. Artah bin Al-Mundhir said: I asked Damrah bin Habib: Do the jinn have a reward? He said: Yes, and he recited: No man or jinn has touched them before them (al-Rahman 55:74). He said: So the human women are for the humans and the jinn women are for the jinn. Omar bin Abdul Aziz said: The believing jinn are around Paradise, in suburbs and areas, but they are not in it.
46:32: 32. And whoever does not respond to the caller of God will not escape Him on earth, God will not be unable to escape Him, and he will have no protectors besides Him, supporters who will protect him from God, those are in manifest error.
46:33: 33. Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not weary of their creation, is not unable to create them, is able, this is how the general reading is. They differed about the reason for the inclusion of the letter ba in it. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Akhfash said: The letter ba is an additional letter for emphasis, like his saying: (It grows with oil). Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said: The Arabs add the letter ba to questions with denial, so they say: I do not think you are standing. Yaqub read: (yaqdir) with a ya’ as a verb, and Abu Ubaidah chose the reading of the general public because it is in the reading of Abdullah Qadir without a ba’. "On the condition that He brings the dead to life. Yes, He is over all things competent."
46:34: 34. And on the Day those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire, it will be said to them, Is this not the truth? They will say, Yes, and our Lord said, meaning, it will be said to them, Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.
46:35: 35. So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will. Ibn Abbas said: Those of resolve. Ad-Dahhak said: Those of seriousness and patience. They differed about them. Ibn Zayd said: All the messengers were people of determination. God did not send a prophet except that he was one of determination, resolve, opinion, and perfect reason. The word min was introduced for the purpose of alliteration, not for the purpose of partiality, as one says: I bought garments of silk and robes of fine linen. Some of them said: All the prophets were people of resolve except for Jonah, son of Matta, because of his haste. Don’t you see that it was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not be like the companion of the fish? Some people said: They are the noble messengers mentioned in Surat Al-An’am, and they are eighteen, because God Almighty said after mentioning them: Those are the ones whom God has guided, so follow their guidance (al-An’am 6:90). Al-Kalbi said: They are those who ordered jihad and showed openness with the enemies of religion. It was said: They are six: Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, Shuaib, and Moses, peace be upon them, and they are the ones mentioned in the same order in Surat Al-A’raf and Surat Ash-Shu’ara. Muqatil said: They are six: Noah, who was patient with the harm of his people; Abraham, who was patient with the fire; Isaac, who was patient with the slaughter; Jacob, who was patient with the loss of his son and the loss of his sight; Joseph, who was patient with the well and the prison; and Job, who was patient with the hardship. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: They are Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the people of the laws. They are five with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: God mentioned them specifically in His statement: And when We took a covenant from the prophets, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary (al-Ahzab 33:7), and in His statement: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah (al-Shura 42:13). Abu Tahir al-Mutahhar ibn Ali ibn Ubayd God al-Farsi told us, Abu Dharr Muhammad ibn Ibrahim Sabt al-Salihani told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn Hayyan, known as Abu al-Shaykh al-Hafiz told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim told us, Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj told us, al-Sari ibn Hayyan told us, Ibad ibn Ibad told us, Mujalid ibn Sa’id told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Aisha said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “O Aisha, the world is not suitable for Muhammad or the family of Muhammad. O Aisha, God is not pleased with those of strong will except with patience in its hardships and patience in its difficulties. He is not pleased with anything except that He charged me with what He charged them with, and He said: ‘So be patient as were patient the messengers of strong will.’ By God, I must obey Him, and by God, I will be patient as they were patient and strive as they strived. There is no power except with God.” The Almighty says: And do not hasten them, meaning do not hasten the punishment for them, for it will inevitably befall them. It is as if He was somewhat impatient and wanted to bring down the punishment on those of them who refused, so He commanded patience and not to hasten it. Then He informed us about the nearness of the torment, saying: It will be as if, on the Day they see what they are promised, of the torment in the Hereafter, they had not remained [in this world] except for an hour of a day, meaning that when they see the torment, the length of their stay in this world and the intermediate realm will be as if it were an hour of a day, because what has passed, even if it was long, is as if it had never happened. Then he said: A message, meaning this Qur’an and the explanation it contains are a message from God to you, and a message means conveying. Then will anyone perish, by the punishment when it is sent down, except the wicked people, those who go against God’s command. Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is: None will perish with the mercy and grace of God except the wicked people. For this reason, some people said: There is no verse stronger than this verse about the hope for God’s mercy.
47:1: 1. Medinan, Those who disbelieved and averted from the way of God - He rendered worthless their deeds, He invalidated it and did not accept it [and by deeds he meant what they did of feeding people and maintaining family ties]. Ad-Dahhak said: He invalidated their plot and deceit against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and turned the tables on them.
47:2: 2. And those who have believed and done righteous deeds and believed in what was revealed to Muhammad, Sufyan al-Thawri said: meaning they did not disobey him in anything, and it is the truth from their Lord, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: Those who disbelieved and averted: the polytheists of Mecca, and those who have believed and done righteous deeds: the Ansar. He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition, their state, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: He protected them during their lives, meaning that this amendment goes back to amending their deeds so that they would not disobey.
47:3: 3. That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, meaning Satan, and those who believed followed the truth from their Lord, meaning the Qur’an. Thus does God set forth for the people their examples, meaning their forms. Al-Zajjaj said: Thus does God explain examples of the good deeds of the believers and the misguidance of the deeds of the disbelievers.
47:4: 4. So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike their necks, is in the accusative case of enticement, meaning strike their necks, meaning their necks. Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, means you have killed them excessively and subdued them, then secure their bonds, meaning in captivity so that they do not escape from you. Captivity comes after exaggeration in killing, as He said: It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted slaughter upon the land (al-Anfal 8:67), Then either by favor or by ransom, meaning: after you have captured them, then either show them favor by releasing them without compensation, or ransom them. Scholars differed regarding the ruling on this verse. Some people said: It was abrogated by His statement: But if you overtake them in war, disperse with them those behind them (al-Anfal 8:57), and by His statement: Kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). Qatada, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Jurayj agreed with this statement, and it is the statement of Al-Awza’i and the people of opinion. They said: It is not permissible to show mercy to those infidels who have been captured, nor to ransom them. Others said that the verse is decisive, and the imam has the choice regarding sane infidel men who are taken captive, between killing them, enslaving them, or showing them favors, releasing them without compensation, or ransoming them with money or Muslim prisoners. Ibn Umar held this view, and al-Hasan, Ata’, and most of the Companions and scholars said the same. It is the view of al-Thawri, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. Ibn Abbas said: When the Muslims increased in number and their power grew, God Almighty revealed about the prisoners: Then either a favor afterwards or ransom. This is the most correct and preferred opinion, because it was practiced by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the caliphs after him: Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, [Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Yusuf told us] Al-Layth told us, Saeed bin Abi Saeed told us, he heard Abu Hurairah say: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent cavalry towards Najd, and they brought back a man from Banu Hanifa called Thamamah bin Aththal, and they tied him to a pillar [of the mosque]. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to him and said: What do you have, Thamamah? He said: I have good, O Muhammad. If you kill, you will kill a man of blood, and if you are generous, you will be generous to a grateful person, and if you want money, ask for whatever you want from it. Until the next day, he said to him: What do you have, Thamamah? He said: I have what I told you. If you kill, you will be generous to a grateful person. [If you are generous, you will be generous to a grateful person.] So he left him until the day after, and he said to him: What do you have, Thamamah? He said: I have what I told you. He said: Let Thamamah go, and he went to a nearby palm grove.” From the mosque, he washed himself, then he entered the mosque and said: I bear witness that there is no god but God and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Muhammad, by God, there was no face on the face of the earth more hateful to me than your face, but now your face has become the most beloved of faces to me. By God, there was no religion more hateful to me than your religion, but now your religion has become the most beloved of religions to me. By God, there was no country more hateful to me than your religion, but now your religion has become the most beloved of religions to me. To me from your country, and your country has become the most beloved of countries to me, and your horses have taken me away while I was intending to perform Umrah, so what do you think? So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him good report and ordered him to perform Umrah. When he arrived in Mecca, someone said to him: Have you converted to Islam? He said: No, but I have become Muslim with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. No, by God, not a single grain of wheat will come to you from Yamamah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, will permit. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al-Khalal told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Asamm told us, Al-Rabi’ told us, Al-Shafi’i told us, Abdul Wahhab bin Abdul Majeed Al-Thaqafi told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Al-Muhallab, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, who said: “The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a man from Banu Uqayl prisoner and bound him. Thaqif had taken two men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prisoner, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ransomed him in exchange for the two men that Thaqif had taken prisoner.” The Almighty says: Until the war lays down its burdens, meaning its burdens and loads, meaning until the people of war lay down their weapons and refrain from war. The root of wazr is: what a person can bear, so weapons are called wazr because they can be carried. It was said: The war is the warriors, such as drinking and riding. It was said: The burdens are the sins, and its meaning is until the warriors put down their sins, by repenting from their disbelief and believing in God and His Messenger. It was said: Until your war and fighting put away the burdens of the polytheists and their ugly deeds so that they submit. The meaning of the verse: Inflict heavy casualties on the polytheists with killing and captivity until all the people of religions enter Islam, and the religion is entirely for God, and after that there will be no jihad or fighting. This will be when Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon them, descends. It was mentioned in the hadith on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Jihad has been ongoing since God sent me until the last of my nation fights the Antichrist. Al-Kalbi said: Until they surrender or make peace. Al-Farra’ said: Until there is no one left except a Muslim or a peaceful person. That, which you mentioned and explained of the ruling on the disbelievers, and if God had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them, so He destroyed them and sufficed you with their affair without fighting, but, He commanded you to fight, that He may test some of you by means of others, so that whoever of the believers is killed will be rewarded and whoever of the disbelievers is killed will be punished, and those who are killed in the way of God, the people of Basra and Hafs read: (qātalu) with a ḍammah on the qaf and a light kasra on the ta’, meaning the martyrs, and the others read: (qātalu) with an alif from the word māqātila, and they are the mujahidin, will not let their deeds go to waste, Qatadah said: It was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed on the day of Uhud, and wounds and killing had spread among the Muslims.
47:5: 5. He will guide them during their life in this world to the most righteous matters, and in the Hereafter to the highest levels, and will set right their condition, satisfy their opponents and accept their deeds.
47:6: 6. And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them, meaning He will show them their homes in Paradise so that they may be guided to their dwellings without making mistakes or asking anyone to guide them to them, as if they had been its inhabitants since their creation. Thus, the believer will be better guided to his degree, his wife, and his servants than to his home and family in this world. This is the opinion of most of the commentators. Ata’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He made it fragrant for them, meaning he made it pleasant for them, from arf, which is a pleasant smell, and maref food means: fragrant.
47:7: 7. O you who have believed, if you support God, that is, His religion and His Messenger, He will support you, against your enemy, and plant firmly your feet, in battle.
47:8: 8. And those who disbelieve - for them is woe, Ibn Abbas said: Far from them. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Downfall for them. Ad-Dahhak said: Disappointment for them. Ibn Zayd said: Misery for them. Al-Farraa' said: It is an accusative of a source, by way of supplication. It was said: In this world, it is a stumble, and in the hereafter, it is falling into the Fire. And it is said about the stumbler: woe if they did not want him to get up, and its opposite is la'an if they wanted him to get up, and He rendered worthless their deeds, because they were in obedience to Satan.
47:9: 9. That, misery and misguidance, is because they hated what God revealed, so He rendered worthless their deeds.
47:10: 10. Then He frightened the unbelievers and said: Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? God destroyed them, meaning He destroyed them, and for the unbelievers is the like thereof, if they do not believe, threatening the polytheists of Mecca.
47:11: 11. That, which you mentioned, is because God is the Protector and Helper of those who believe, their Guardian and Supporter, and that the disbelievers have no Protector, no Helper. Then he mentioned the outcome of the two groups, saying:
47:12: 12. “Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But those who disbelieve will enjoy themselves” in this world, and eat as livestock eat, they have no concern except their stomachs and their private parts, and they are distracted and heedless of what will happen tomorrow. It has been said: The believer provisions himself in this world, the hypocrite adorns himself, and the disbeliever enjoys himself, and the Fire will be their abode.
47:13: 13. And how many a town was mightier than your town which expelled you, meaning its people expelled you. Ibn Abbas said: How many men are mightier than the people of Mecca? This is indicated by his statement: We destroyed them, and he did not say: We destroyed it, and they have no helper. Ibn Abbas said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left Mecca for the cave, he turned to Mecca and said: “You are the most beloved of God’s lands to God and the most beloved of God’s lands to me. Had the polytheists not expelled me, I would not have left you.” Then God revealed this verse.
47:14: 14. Is he who has clear evidence from his Lord, certainty of his religion, Muhammad and the believers, like he to whom his evil deeds have been made attractive and who has followed his own desires, meaning the worship of idols, and they are Abu Jahl and the polytheists.
47:15: 15. The description of Paradise, which is promised to the righteous, that is, its description, in it are rivers of water untainted, stagnant, old, putrid, Ibn Kathir’s reading is (asna) with the short vowel, akhtarna with the long vowel, and they are two languages and secret: asana al-ma’ means to become stagnant, and ajanna means to become stagnant, aswanan and ajunan, if it changes, and rivers of milk of delicious taste and rivers of deliciousness, [delicious], for the drinkers, not defiled by the feet and not defiled by the title, and rivers of purified honey. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Abu Usamah, Abdullah bin Numayr, and Ali bin Masahr told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Umar, on the authority of Khabib bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Hafs bin Asim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A Christian, a woman, the Nile, and the Euphrates are all rivers of Paradise. Kaab al-Ahbar said: The Tigris River is the river of the people of Paradise, the Euphrates River is the river of their milk, the River of Egypt is the river of their ancient wine, the River of Sayhan is the river of their honey, and three rivers flow from the River of Kauthar. And for them therein are all kinds of fruits and forgiveness from their Lord, as if they were to abide eternally in the Fire. That is, whoever is in this bliss is as if he were to abide eternally in the Fire. And they will be given to drink at gates. Hell will be blazing hot for them since it was created. If anyone approaches them, it will burn their faces and they will drink from it. Only their intestines, so it comes out from their backsides. The intestines are all the contents in the stomach, and the singular is me.
47:16: 16. And among them, meaning from these infidels, is he who listens to you, and they are the hypocrites, they listen and speak but do not understand or comprehend it, out of negligence and neglect, until when they leave you, meaning they leave you, the leaders of those who have been given knowledge, from the Companions: What did he say, Muhammad, about now? Meaning now, it is from the coalition and it is said: I began the matter, meaning I started it and the beginning of something is about to begin. Muqatil said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering a sermon and criticizing the hypocrites. They were released from the mosque and asked Abdullah bin Masoud mockingly: What did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say? Ibn Abbas said: I was asked about whom I was asked about. Those whose hearts God has sealed, so they did not believe, and followed their desires, in disbelief and hypocrisy. 16- And among them is he who listens to you until, when they leave you because the hypocrites used to come to the assembly of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and listen to his speech, they would leave. Sayings of those who were given knowledge meaning the scholars, the Companions, may God be pleased with them. What did he say just now? What he said just now, mockingly or to inquire if they did not listen to him out of disdain for him. Anfan from their saying Anfan for all of what came before it is borrowed from the limb, and from it is attended and begun, and it is a circumstance meaning a begun time, or a state of the pronoun in said. Ibn Kathir read Anfan "Those are the ones whose hearts God has sealed and who follow their desires" so for that reason they mocked and began to take his speech lightly.
47:17: 17. And those who are guided, meaning the believers, He increases them, as the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, in guidance and gives them their piety, enabling them to do what He commanded them to do, which is piety. Saeed bin Jubair said: And He gives them the reward for their piety.
47:18: ".ًََْةََُْْن َأًَاََاََِوف َََخْمون18. " َخَََا ََو اَحَن،اَْاوْيْاََحمن َن َورة محمَََْخَََا ََو اَحَن حْثَا،حْثَا ََو َِحاق اَُاْمي،َن موَى َن اَصلتَْن محمَْحم َمن َمع،َْْن راََخَََا معم،حْثَا اَن اَمَارك،اَحََن َن اَحَن ما: " ْقاْاَمَََي َحْث َن ََي َََُة َن اَََي صلى ا َلَه وَل َو َُماة،َو اْفَاة مفَْاة،َو فََاة مَََاة،غَىة مَُْاةَِمن اَََْاَْْْحْْعل ًََو اََا،ََََُغائبَْ ْفاََْاَْو اََْا،مَُزةة".َو موْاة،مفَْاة.ََي ". ََُْى وَمًَواََا ،َُْ:واحْة مَُا،َي َماراُْا وُا،َاء ََْاُُاََْ: ََْز وْوقا.ًَاََاُمن ََْاْوْان اَََي صلى ا َلَه وَل َْخَََا محم،ا اََعَميَََْنَْخَََا َحم،اَملَحيْاَواحَََْخَََا ْحْثَا فض، َْن اَمَْاْحْثَا َحم، َََْن َِماْحْثَا محم،َن َوَف رََت اَََي صلى: ْقاَْن َعَُْحْثَا، ْحْثَا ََو حاز،َن َلَمان َعثت ََا: ْاَوَُي واََي ْلي الَُا،َأصَعَه َُْاْقاْا َلَه وَل.ُْاَْنًَواََا َنْحْثَا محم،ا اََعَميَََْنَْخَََا َحم،اَملَحيْاَواحَََْخَََا حَََا،اَْامليَحْثَا حفص َن َم،َََْن َِماْحْثَا محم،َوَف ا صلىَْحَْث َمعَه من رَوَْْْح: َْن ََس قا،َن قَاْة،ُْْا ا صلى ا َلَهَْمع رَو،غََيَْه َحَْْحْثَ ْا َلَه وَل َوَْث،ََُْاَوَْث،َْن ََفع اَعلًَاََاُِن من ََْا: ََْوْوَل حَى َْون َخمََن،اَََاءَوَْثْاَََاََْو،ََْب اَخمَوَْث،اَزَا.امََة قَمةا واحْة ،َن َُاء َن ََار،َن َليْحْثَا ُل،حْثَا فلَح،َن ََانْحْثَا محم فيَََْما اَََي صلى ا َلَه وَل: " َْن ََي َََُة رضي ا ََه قا اْمَى اََاًَ؟ فمضى رَو: َْاء َََاَي فَاَِ ْمَلس َحْث اََو: ْفَْه ما قاَْمع ما قا: َْعض اََوْفَا،َحْثْصلى ا َلَه وَل ََن َن اََاًَ؟: ْقا،ََمع َك حَى َِا قضى حَْثهَْ َْ:َُاك: ْوقا اََاًَ؟َََُفاًََِا ضَعت الما: ْقا،اُْا ََا َا رَو: ْقا ُواََعاََََْاَُْفمن ََن،"ََُْْ َُِْا ََحملَُْفاَى: "ََْز وْوقا َِْْن الََان وََى َه اَحاَْو: "ََِا اْصلوا َُْ؟ فحََئًَواََو -23.ََاَف
47:19: 19. The Almighty’s statement: So know that there is no god but God. It was said that the address is to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and what is meant by it is someone else. It was also said that its meaning is, So adhere to it. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: So increase your knowledge upon your knowledge. Abu al-Aaliyah and Ibn Uyaynah said: It is connected to what preceded it, meaning: If the Hour comes upon them, then know that there is no refuge or one who can turn back when it comes except to God. It was also said: Know that there is no god but God, that kingdoms will cease to exist when it comes, and there will be no kingdom or rule for anyone except God. And ask forgiveness for your sin, He commanded us to ask forgiveness even though it had been forgiven so that his nation would follow his example. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Al-Aghar Al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is a veil over my heart, and I seek forgiveness from God one hundred times every day. The Almighty said: And for the believing men and believing women, this is an honor from God the Almighty to this nation as He commanded their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to seek forgiveness for their sins, for He is the intercessor whose supplications are answered for them. And God knows your [moving and resting place], Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: Your [moving and resting place] is your disposition and dispersal in your deeds in this world, and your resting place is your destination in the Hereafter, to Paradise or to Hell. Muqatil and Ibn Jarir said: Your turning around is your turning away from your work during the day, and your resting place is your place of rest in your beds at night. Ikrimah said: Your transition is from the loins of fathers to the wombs of mothers. And your resting place is your place on earth. Ibn Kaysan said: Your turning over is from your back to your stomach, and your abode is your place in the graves. Meaning: He knows all your conditions, and nothing is hidden from Him.
47:20: 20. And those who believe say, out of great concern for jihad: Why was a surah not sent down? commanding us to jihad, but when a decisive surah is sent down in which fighting is mentioned, Qatada said: Every surah in which jihad is mentioned is decisive, and it is the most severe of the Qur’an against the hypocrites. You will see those in whose hearts is disease, meaning the hypocrites, looking at you, with a squint, with intense stare, out of hatred for jihad and avoidance of meeting the enemy, the look of one fainting from death, as one stares blankly at death, so it is more fitting for them, a warning and a threat. The meaning of their statement in the threat: It is more fitting for you is: your friend and your closest friend is what you dislike.
47:21: 21. Then he said: Obedience and good speech. This is a beginning with an omitted predicate, the meaning of which is: obedience and good speech is better, meaning if they obeyed and said good speech it would be better and more excellent. It was said: Its metaphor is: These hypocrites say before the revelation of the decisive surah: Obedience, nominative case as a narration, meaning our command is obedience or from us is obedience, (and a well-known saying): good. (for them) means the preposition baa, it is a metaphor. It was said: It is connected to what preceded it, and the lam in his saying: It is more appropriate for them to obey God and His Messenger, and a saying known for the answer, meaning if they obeyed, obedience and answer would be more appropriate for them, and this is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Abbas in the narration of Ata’. So when the matter is decided, that is, the matter becomes serious and the obligation of fighting becomes obligatory and the matter becomes decided, if they were true to God, in showing faith and obedience, it would be better for them. It was said that the answer to if is omitted, meaning that when the matter is decided, they will fail and lie about what they promised. And if they were true to God, it would be better for them.
47:22: 22. And sever your ties of kinship, Yaqub read: and sever your ties of kinship, with a fat-ha on the ta’, while others read it with a shaddah. And sever your ties of kinship, from the root word taqatāwu, meaning, to sever your ties of kinship, Qatadah said: How did you see the people when they turned away from the Book of God? Did they not shed unlawful blood, sever their ties of kinship, and disobey the Most Merciful? Some of them said: It is from al-Wilāyah. Al-Musayyab bin Sharik and Al-Farra’ said: He says: If you are given authority over people, will you spread corruption on earth through injustice? It was revealed about the Umayyads and the Hashimites. This is indicated by the reading of Ali bin Abi Talib tawallitum with a damma on the ta’ and the waw and a kasra on the lam. He says: If you are given authority over unjust rulers, you will go out with them in the strife and assist them.
47:23: 23. Those are the ones whom God has cursed, so He has made them deaf and blinded their sight, about the truth.
47:24: 24. Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an, or are there locks upon their hearts? So the Qur’an’s admonitions and rulings are not understood, and Am means Rather. Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Aqil bin Muhammad told us, Al-Mu’afa bin Zakariya told us, Muhammad bin Jarir told us, Bishr told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Hisham bin Urwah told us on the authority of my father who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an, or are there locks upon their hearts? A young man from Yemen said: Rather, there are locks upon their hearts until God opens them or relieves them. So the young man remained in the same mood as Umar until he assumed power and sought his help.
47:25: 25. Indeed, those who turned back, they returned as disbelievers, after guidance had become clear to them, Qatada said: They are the disbelieving People of the Book who disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after they had come to know him and found his description in their book. Ibn Abbas, Al-Dahhak, and Al-Suddi said: They are the hypocrites. Satan tempted them, made ugly things seem attractive to them, and prolonged their hope. The people of Basra read it with a damma on the alif, a kasra on the lam, and a fatha on the yaa, referring to something whose agent is not named. Mujahid read it with a sukoon on the yaa as a statement from God Almighty about Himself that He does that. This reading is narrated on the authority of Yaqub. The others read: (and prolonged their hope) with a fatha on the alif, meaning: Satan prolonged their hope for them, he extended their hope.
47:26: 26. That is because they - meaning the hypocrites or the Jews - said to those who hated what God revealed - meaning the polytheists, We will obey you in some of the matter - cooperating in their enmity towards Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and sitting back from jihad. They were saying it secretly, so God Almighty informed us about them, And God knows their secrets. The people of Kufa, other than Abu Bakr, read it with a kasra over the hamza, as a source, while the rest read it with a fatha over it as a plural of secret.
47:27: 27. How will it be when the angels take their souls, striking their faces and their backs?
47:28: 28. That, the verse, is because they followed what angered God, Ibn Abbas said: because they concealed from the Torah and disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and hated His pleasure, they hated what pleases God, which is obedience and faith. So He rendered their deeds worthless.
47:29: 29. Or do those in whose hearts is disease think, meaning the hypocrites, that God will not bring to light their hatred, that is, He will not reveal their hatred toward the believers and expose it until they know their hypocrisy. The singular form of ghar is ghar envy. Ibn Abbas said: their envy.
47:30: 30. And if We willed, We could have shown them to you, meaning, We could have informed you and made them known to you, and you would have known them by their mark, meaning, by their signs. Al-Zajjaj said: If We willed, We could have made a mark on the hypocrites by which you would know them. Anas said: Nothing about the hypocrites was hidden from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the revelation of this verse. He knew them by their appearance. And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech, in its meaning and purpose. (And the melody): There are two faces, right and wrong. The correct verb is: to melody, to melody, to melody, so he is a melody if he is aware of something. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Perhaps some of you may be more eloquent in his argument than others. The verb is to make a mistake by tuning, which means to make a mistake. The root of this verb is to remove speech from its proper direction. Meaning: You know them by what they offer of ridiculing you and the Muslims and mocking them. After this, no hypocrite would speak in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except that he would recognize him by his words and use the meaning of his words to prove the corruption of his inner self. And God knows your deeds.
47:31: 31. And We will surely test you, and We will treat you as a tester by ordering you to fight and struggle, until We make evident those among you who strive [for the cause of God] and the patient, meaning: the knowledge of existence. He means: until the one who strives and is patient in his religion is distinguished from others, and We will make evident your report, meaning We will reveal it and expose it through the stubbornness of one who refuses to fight and does not have patience in jihad. Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim: (And We will test you until He knows), and yablu with a ya in them, because of the Almighty’s saying: [And God knows your deeds, and the others read with a nun in them, because the Almighty said] (And if We willed, We could show you them), and Ya’qub read: (And We will test you) with a silent waw, in response to his saying: And We will test you, and the others read with a fatha in response to his saying: until We know.
47:32: 32. Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them - never will they harm God at all, they only harm themselves, and He will render their deeds worthless, so they will not see any reward for them in the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: They are the ones who were fed on the Day of Badr. Similar to this is the statement of God, the Almighty: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God (al-Anfal 8:36).
47:33: 33. O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds. Ata’ said: With doubt and hypocrisy. Al-Kalbi said: With showing off and seeking fame. Al-Hasan said: With sins and major sins. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, believed that no sin can harm one if one is sincere, just as no action can benefit one if one is polytheistic. So this verse was revealed, and they feared that major sins would nullify their deeds after it. Muqatil said: Do not attribute favors to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lest you invalidate your deeds. It was revealed about Banu Asad, and we will mention it in Surat Al-Hujurat, God willing.
47:34: 34. Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God and then died while they were disbelievers - never will God forgive them. It was said: They are the people of the well. Its ruling is general.
47:35: 35. So do not weaken, do not become weak, "and call for peace", that is, do not call for peace initially. God forbade the Muslims from calling the infidels to peace, and ordered them to fight them until they submit, and you will be the superior, the victorious. Al-Kalbi said: The final decision is yours even if they defeat you at times, and God is with you, with aid and victory, and He will never deprive you of your deeds, He will not decrease your reward for your deeds. It is said: Witra yatrahu wawtra wawtra, if his right is decreased. Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Muqatil and Ad-Dahhak said: He will not wrong you for your righteous deeds, but rather He will give you their reward. Then He urged seeking the hereafter, saying:
47:36: 36. The life of this world is only play and amusement, falsehood and delusion, and if you believe and fear God, immoralities, He will give you your reward, the recompense for your deeds in the Hereafter, and He does not ask you, your Lord, your wealth, to give the reward, but rather He commands you to believe and obey in order to reward you for it with Paradise. His statement: I do not want from them any provision (al-Dhariyat 51:57), and it was said: Muhammad does not ask you for your wealth, similar to: “Say: I do not ask you for it any reward” (al-Furqan 25:57). It was said that the meaning of the verse is: God and His Messenger do not ask you for all of your wealth in charity. Rather, they ask you for a drop from the abundance, a quarter of a tenth, so be content with it. Ibn Uyaynah adopted this view, and the context of the verse indicates it:
47:37: 37. If they ask you about it, he will force you, meaning he will exhaust you and insist on asking you all of them. It is said: So-and-so exhausted so-and-so if he exhausted him and insisted on asking him all of them. "Be stingy" with it, so do not give it to her. And He brings forth your grudges, your hatred and enmity. Qatada said: God knows that the issue of money brings forth grudges.
47:38: 38. Here you are, being called upon to spend in the cause of God, meaning to give what God has enjoined upon you. But among you is he who is niggardly, with what has been joined upon him of zakat. “And whoever is niggardly is niggardly only from himself. And God is Free of need,” with regard to your charity and obedience, and you are the needy, with regard to Him and to what good He has. And if you turn away, He will replace you with other people; Then they will not be the likes of you, but rather they will be better than you and more obedient to God than you. Al-Kalbi said: They are Kind and Naha. Al-Hasan said: They are the Persians. Ikrimah said: They are the Persians and the Romans. Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Abi Nasr al-Kufanī informed us, Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Umar informed us, Ishaq al-Najībi al-Misrī, known as Ibn al-Nahhās, informed us, Abu al-Tayyib al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Riyāsh informed us, Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Muslim ibn Khalid informed us, on the authority of al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; Then they will not be the likes of you.' They said: 'O Messenger of God, who are these people who, if we turn away, will be in your place; Then they will not be the likes of us?' He struck the thigh of Salman al-Persi and said: 'This one and his people.' Even if the religion were at the Pleiades, men from among the Persians would attain it.”
48:1: Madinah, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi informed us, Abu Mus`ab informed us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, “That `Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was traveling with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on one of his journeys. `Umar asked him about something and he did not answer him. Then he asked him and he did not answer him. Then he asked him and he did not answer him. `Umar said: May your mother be bereaved of you, `Umar, you have called upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, three times, and each time he did not answer you. `Umar said: So I moved my camel and went ahead of the people, and I was afraid that something would be revealed about the Qur’an. It was not long before I heard a voice calling out to me, so I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him. He said: A surah has been revealed to me tonight, and it is more beloved to me than anything upon which the sun rises. Then he recited: ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest * That God may forgive you what Come forward from your sin and do not delay it. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Omar Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Muzni told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah, the grandson of al-Abbas ibn Hakza told us, al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Bajali told us, Affan told us, Hammam told us, Qatada told us, Anas told us: “The verse, ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest,’ to the end of the verse, was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was returning from al-Hudaybiyyah and his companions were overcome by sadness and depression. He said: A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the entire world. When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, a man from among the people said: Congratulations and well-seen! God has made clear to you what He will do with you, so what will He do with us? So God revealed the verse that came after it: ‘That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow,’ until the end of the verse.” 1. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. They differed regarding this conquest: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Razi, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas: that it was the conquest of Mecca. Mujahid said: the conquest of Khaybar. Most of them agree that it is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The meaning of conquest is to unlock what was closed. The peace treaty with the polytheists at Hudaybiyyah was impossible until God, the Almighty, granted it. Shu'bah narrated from Qatadah from Anas: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, meaning Hudaybiyyah. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’, who said: You consider the conquest to be the conquest of Mecca, but the conquest of Mecca was a conquest, and we consider the conquest to be the Pledge of Ridwan. On the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, we were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fourteen hundred men, and Al-Hudaybiyyah was a well, so we drained it and did not leave a drop in it. report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he came to it and sat on its edge, then called for a vessel of water, performed ablution, rinsed his mouth and supplicated, then poured it into it, and we left it not far away. Then it sent forth whatever we and our passengers wished. Al-Sha’bi said about his statement: (Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest), he said: The conquest of Al-Hudaybiyyah, his past and future sins were forgiven, they were fed from the palm trees of Khaybar, the sacrificial animals reached their destination, and the Romans were victorious over the Persians, so the believers rejoiced at the victory of the People of the Book over the Magians. Al-Zuhri said: There was no greater conquest than the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. This was because the polytheists mingled with the Muslims and listened to their words, so Islam took root in their hearts. In three years, many people converted to Islam, and the majority of Muslims increased because of them. The Almighty said: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, meaning, We have decreed for you a clear decree. Ad-Dahhak said: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest without fighting, and peace is part of the conquest.
48:2: 2. It was said: The lam in His statement: (li-yaghfir) is the lam of ki, meaning: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest so that the complete blessing of the conquest may be combined for you with forgiveness. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: It is attributed to His saying: And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women (Muhammad 47:19) That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come and That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens (Surat Muhammad 47:19). Muhammad bin Jarir said: It refers to His saying: When there comes the help of God and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of God in multitudes, then exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness (al-Nasr 110:1-3) so that God may forgive you for your past sins in the pre-Islamic period before the message, and for those that came after until the time of the revelation of this surah. It was said: What is delayed is what will happen, and this is in accordance with the method of those who permit minor sins for the prophets. Sufyan al-Thawri said: What came before of what you did in the pre-Islamic period, and what came after: everything you did not do. Such a thing is mentioned in order to emphasize, just as it is said: He gave to one who saw him and to one who did not see him, and he struck one who met him and one who did not meet him. Ata Al-Khurasani said: Whatever of your sins has passed means the sin of your parents Adam and Eve, through your blessing, and whatever will come means the sins of your nation, through your call. And He completes His favor upon you, with prophecy and wisdom, and guides you to a straight path, meaning He makes you steadfast on it. The meaning is that He will combine for you, along with the conquest, the completion of His favor through forgiveness and guidance to the straight path, which is Islam. It was also said: And He guides you, meaning He guides through you.
48:3: 3. And God will grant you a mighty victory. Mostly. And it was said: With honor.
48:4: 4. It is He who sent down tranquility, reassurance and dignity, into the hearts of the believers, so that their souls would not be disturbed by what befalls them. Ibn Abbas said: Every tranquility in the Qur’an is reassurance except for the one in Surat Al-Baqarah, that they may increase in faith along with their [present] faith. Ibn Abbas said: God sent His Messenger with the testimony that there is no god but God. When they believed him, He increased their prayer, then zakat, then fasting, then pilgrimage, then jihad, until He perfected their religion for them. So whenever they were commanded to do something and believed in it, their belief increased upon their belief. Ad-Dahhak said: Certainly with their certainty. Al-Kalbi said: This is about the matter of Al-Hudaybiyyah when God confirmed the vision of His Messenger with truth. To God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is God Knowing and Wise.
48:5: 5. “That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and He may remove from them their misdeeds. And that is, in the sight of God, a great attainment.” We have mentioned on the authority of Anas that the Companions said when So that God may forgive you was revealed: Congratulations, what will He do to us? Then the verse That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens was revealed.
48:6: 6. And He will punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women, the hypocrites in Medina and the polytheists in Mecca, who think evil of God, that He will not support Muhammad and the believers, upon them is a cycle of evil, of torment and destruction, and God has become angry with them and has cursed them and has prepared Hell for them, and evil it is as a destination.
48:7: 7. To God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and ever is God Exalted in Might and Wise.
48:8: 8. Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
48:9: 9. That you may believe in God and His Messenger and support him, that is, help him and aid him, and honor him, that is, magnify and glorify him. These metaphors refer back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and here he stopped, and glorify Him, that is, glorify God, meaning pray to Him, morning and evening, in the morning and evening. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read: (and that you may believe, and honor him, and honor him, and glorify Him) with the letter ya in them, because of His saying: (in the hearts of the believers), and the others read them with the letter ta in them.
48:10: 10. Those who pledge allegiance to you, O Muhammad, at Al-Hudaibiyah, not to flee, are only pledging allegiance to God, because they have sold themselves to God for Paradise. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Hatim bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ubaid, who said: I said to Salamah bin Al-Akwa’: On what did you pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah? He said: On death. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj, Yahya bin Yahya told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abdullah bin Al-A’raj, on the authority of Ma’qil bin Yasar, who said: I saw myself on the Day of the Tree while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pledging allegiance to the people, and I was raising one of its branches above his head, and we were fourteen hundred. He said: We did not pledge allegiance to him to die, but we pledged allegiance to him not to flee. Abu Isa said: The meaning of the two hadiths is correct. A group pledged allegiance to him to die, meaning we will continue to fight in your presence as long as we are not killed. Others pledged allegiance to him and said: We will not flee. The hand of God is above their hands. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The hand of God is above their hands in fulfilling the good He promised them. Al-Suddi said: They would take the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and pledge allegiance to him, and the hand of God was above their hands in the pledge of allegiance. Al-Kalbi said: Is the blessing of God upon them in guidance greater than what they did in the pledge of allegiance? But whoever breaks his oath, breaks the pledge, breaks it only to the detriment of himself, upon him and his family. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God, remains steadfast in his pledge, He will give him, the people of Iraq read (fasiyu’tihi) with a ya’, and the others read it with a noon, a great reward, which is Paradise.
48:11: 11. The bedouins who stayed behind will say to you, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: meaning the bedouins of Ghifar, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ashja' and Aslam. This is because when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) wanted to go to Mecca in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah to perform Umrah, he mobilized the bedouins and the people of the desert around Medina to go out with him, fearing that the Quraysh would attack him or prevent him from entering the House. So he entered the state of Ihram for Umrah and brought the sacrificial animals with him to show the people that he did not want to wage war. But many of the bedouins were reluctant to go with him and stayed behind, claiming that they were busy. So God, the Most High, revealed about them: The bedouins who stayed behind will say to you, meaning those whom God, the Most High, left behind from your company, when you return to them and rebuke them for staying behind. Our wealth and our families have distracted us, meaning the women and children, meaning we had no one to take care of them. So ask forgiveness for us, meaning we stayed behind from you. So God Almighty denied their excuse, saying: They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, regarding the matter of asking forgiveness, for they do not care whether the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked forgiveness for them or not. Say, ‘Who can control anything for you against God if He intended to harm you or intended to benefit you?’ Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a damma on the letter dad, while the others read it with a fatha because He contrasted it with benefit, and benefit is the opposite of harm. This is because they thought that their failure to follow the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would ward off harm from them and would hasten their benefit by ensuring safety for themselves and their wealth. So he informed them that if He intended to do something to them, no one would be able to ward it off. Rather, God is All-Aware of what you do.
48:12: 12. Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, meaning, you thought that the enemy would uproot them and they would never return. And that was made attractive to your hearts, Satan made that assumption attractive to your hearts. And you thought an evil assumption, meaning that they said: Muhammad and his companions are head-eaters and will never return, so where will you go with him? Wait for what will happen to them. And you were a people who were ruined, doomed and not fit for any good.
48:13: 13. And whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze.
48:14: 14. “To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful.”
48:15: 15.
