Those who stayed behind will say, meaning those who stayed behind from Hudaybiyyah, when you set out, meaning you marched and went [O believers], to spoils that you may take, meaning the spoils of Khaybar, Leave us to follow you, to Khaybar so that we may witness with you the fighting of its people. This is because when they returned from Hudaybiyyah, God promised them the conquest of Khaybar and made its spoils specifically for those who witnessed Hudaybiyyah in place of the spoils of the people of Mecca if they returned from them in a peace treaty and did not take anything from them. God Almighty said: They want to change the word of God. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: the word of God without an alif, plural of word. The others read: the word of God. They want to change the promises of God Almighty to the people of Al-Hudaybiyyah, specifically regarding the spoils of Khaybar. Muqatil said: It means that God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that none of them should go. Ibn Zayd said: It is the saying of God Almighty: And they asked your permission to go out, and said, ‘You will never go out with me’ (al-Tawbah 9:83). The first is more correct, and most of the people of interpretation agree with it. “Say, ‘You will not follow us,’ to Khaybar. ‘Thus said God before,’ that is, before our return to you, that the spoils of Khaybar belonged to those who witnessed Hudaybiyyah, and no one else had a share in them. ’ Then they will say, ‘Rather, you envy us,’ that is, envy prevents you from sharing the spoils with you. ’ Rather, they do not understand,’ that is, they do not know what God has for them and what is against them of the debt, ‘except a few of them,’ and this is from the truth of God and the Messenger.
48:16: 16. “Say to those of the Bedouins who stayed behind: You will be called to fight a people of great strength.” Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ata’ said: They are the people of Persia. Ka’b said: They are the Romans. Al-Hasan said: The Persians and the Romans. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Hawazin and Thaqif. Qatada said: Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn. Al-Zuhri, Muqatil, and a group said: They are the Banu Hanifa of Yamamah, the companions of Musaylimah the Liar. Rafi’ ibn Khadij said: We used to read this verse and we did not know who they were until Abu Bakr called for fighting the Banu Hanifa, and then we knew that it was them. Ibn Jurayj said: Omar, may God be pleased with him, called them to fight the Persians. Abu Hurairah said: This verse has not yet come. “Fight them or they submit. If you obey, God will give you a good reward,” meaning Paradise. But if you turn away, [expose yourself], as you turned away before, the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, He will punish you with a painful punishment, meaning Hell. So when this verse was revealed, the people of the time said: What will happen to us, O Messenger of God?
48:17: 17. Then God the Almighty revealed: There is no blame upon the blind, [meaning in staying away from jihad], “nor blame upon the lame or upon the ill. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. And whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment.” The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read nadkhalhu and na’dhubuhu with the letter nun in both, while the others read it with the letter ya because of His saying: and whoever obeys God.
48:18: 18. God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, at Al-Hudaibiyah, to fight the Quraysh and not flee, under the tree, which was a tamarisk tree. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: My father told me that he was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, under the tree. He said: When we left the following year, we forgot it and could not find it. It was narrated that Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, passed by that place after the tree had disappeared, and he said: Where was it? Some of them said: Here, and some of them said: Here. When their disagreement increased, he said: Go on, the tree is gone. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, Amr said: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah: You are the best people on earth, and we were one thousand four hundred, and if I could see today, I would have shown you the place of the tree. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj, Muhammad bin Hatim told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Abu Al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir being asked: How many were there on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah? He said: We were fourteen hundred, so we pledged allegiance to him, and Umar was holding his hand under the tree, which was a samura tree, so we pledged allegiance to him except for Jadd bin Qais Al-Ansari, who hid under the belly of his camel. Salim narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: We were fifteen hundred. Abdullah bin Abi Awfa said: The people of the tree were one thousand and three hundred, and Aslam was one-eighth of the immigrants. The reason for this pledge of allegiance - according to what Muhammad ibn Ishaq reported from the scholars - was that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Khurash ibn Abi Umayyah al-Khuza’i when he had descended, and sent him to the Quraysh in Mecca and carried him on his camel, called al-Thalab, to inform their nobles of what he had come for. They hamstrung the Messenger of God’s camel, may God bless him and grant him peace, and wanted to kill him, but the Abyssinians prevented him, so they let him go until he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Mecca. He said: O Messenger of God, I fear for myself from the Quraysh, and there is no one from the Banu ‘Adi ibn Ka’b in Mecca to protect me. The Quraysh know of my enmity towards them and my harshness towards them, but I will guide you to a man who is more honored there than I: Uthman ibn Affan. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Uthman and sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of the Quraysh to inform them that he had not come to fight, but rather had come to visit this House, respecting its sanctity. Uthman went out to Mecca, and Abaan ibn Sa’id met him. When Uthman ibn al-`As entered Mecca, or before he entered it, he got off his mount and carried him in front of him, then he rode behind him and protected him until he delivered the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The leaders of Quraysh said to Uthman when he had finished delivering the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you want to circumambulate the House, then circumambulate it. He said: I would not do that until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulates it. Quraysh considered it a reward for them. The report of Uthman’s death reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We will not leave until we fight the people, and he called the people to the pledge of allegiance, so the Pledge of Ridwan took place under the tree. The people used to say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged allegiance to them on death. Bakr ibn al-Ashja said: They pledged allegiance to him on death. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, on what you are able to. Jabir ibn Abdullah and Muqal ibn Yasar said: We did not pledge allegiance to him to die, but we pledged allegiance to him not to flee. The first of the Banu Asad to pledge allegiance to Ridwan was called Abu Sinan ibn Wahb, and none of the Muslims who attended stayed away from him except Jad ibn Qays, the brother of Banu Salamah. Jabir said: It was as if I could see him clinging to the armpit of his camel, hiding behind it from the people. Then he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said that what he had mentioned about the matter of Uthman was false. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Fanjuwayh told us, Ali bin Ahmad bin Nadruwayh told us, Abu Imran Musa bin Sahl bin Abdul Hamid Al-Joni told us, Muhammad bin Ramh told us, Al-Layth bin Saad told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter Hellfire. God Almighty said: He knew what was in their hearts, of truthfulness and loyalty, so He sent down tranquility, reassurance and contentment, upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest, meaning the conquest of Khaybar.
48:19: 19. And they will take many spoils, from the money of the Jews of Khaybar. Khaybar had real estate and money, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among them. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.
48:20: 20. God has promised you many spoils which you will seize, meaning the conquests that will be opened for them until the Day of Resurrection. So He has hastened this for you, meaning Khaybar, and restrained the hands of the people from you, because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, intended to go to Khaybar and besiege its people, tribes from Asad and Ghatafan intended to attack the Muslim families and children in Madinah, but God restrained their hands by instilling terror in their hearts. It was said: He restrained the hands of the people from you, meaning the people of Makkah, through the peace treaty. And that it may be, their restraint and your safety, a sign for the believers, confirming your truthfulness and so that they may know that God is the One who protects and guards them when they are present and when they are absent, and guide you to a straight path, making you steadfast in Islam and increasing your insight and certainty with the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the conquest of Khaybar. This is because when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Hudaybiyyah, he stayed in Madinah for the rest of Dhul-Hijjah and some of Muharram, then he left for Khaybar in the rest of Muharram in the year seven. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Humaid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, “When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) led us on a raid against a people, he would not attack us until morning and then he would wait. If he heard the call to prayer, he would hold back, and if he did not hear the call to prayer, he would attack them. He said: So we went out to Khaybar and reached them at night. When morning came and he had not heard the call to prayer, he mounted and I mounted behind Abu Talha, and my feet were touching the feet of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: So they came out to us with their shovels and their shovels, and when they saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), they said: Muhammad - by God - Muhammad and Khamis. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw them, he said: God is Great, God is Great. Khaybar has been destroyed. When we encamp in the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning for those who are warned.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Darimi told us, Abu Ali Al-Hanafi Ubaidullah bin Abdul Majeed told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Iyas bin Salamah told us, my father told me:... We went out to Khaybar with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said, my uncle Amir began to recite a Rajaz poem to the people: By God, if it weren't for God, we would not have been guided, given charity, or prayed. We are not independent of your grace, so be firm when we meet it. And send down tranquility upon us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who is this? He said: I am Aamer, may your Lord forgive you. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not ask forgiveness for anyone except that he was martyred. He said: Then Umar ibn al-Khattab called out while he was on his camel: O Prophet of God, why did you not give us enjoyment with Aamer? He said: When we arrived at Khaybar, their king Marhab came out strutting with his sword saying: Khaybar knew that I am a warrior, a skilled and experienced hero. If wars come and ignite He said: My uncle Amer came out to him and said: Khaybar has learned that I am a prosperous, armed, and heroic warrior. He said: They exchanged two blows, and Marhab’s sword struck Aamer’s shield, and Aamer went to carry it, but his sword came back on him and cut his ankle, and his life was lost. Salamah said: I went out and there were a group of the Prophet’s companions saying: ‘Aamer’s deed was in vain; he killed himself.’ He said: So I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and I was crying, and I said: ‘O Messenger of God, Aamer’s deed was in vain; he killed himself.’ The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘Who said that?’ I said: ‘Some of your companions.’ He said: ‘Whoever said that is lying; rather, he will have a double reward.’ Then he sent me to Ali, may God be pleased with him, who had sore eyes, and said: ‘I will give the banner to a man who loves God and His Messenger and whom God and His Messenger love.’ He said: So I went to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and led him, and he had sore eyes, until I brought him to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he spat in his eyes and he was cured and gave him the banner. Marhab went out and said: Khaybar has learned that I am a warrior, a skilled and experienced hero. If wars come and ignite Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: I am the one my mother named Haider, the lion of the jungles [hideous-looking] I will give them a measure of sandalwood He said: He struck Marhab’s head and killed him, and then victory was achieved at his hands. The hadith of Khaybar was narrated by a group: Sahl ibn Sa`d, Anas, and Abu Hurayrah, some adding and some subtracting. It says: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been struck by a migraine and did not go out to the people. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, took the banner of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then rose and fought fiercely. Then he returned and Umar, may God be pleased with him, took it and fought fiercely, more fiercely than the first fight. Then he returned and informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves God and His Messenger and whom God and His Messenger love, and God will grant you victory at his hands. So he called Ali ibn Abi Talib and gave it to him and said: Walk and do not look back until God grants you victory. So he came to the city of Khaybar, and Marhab, the owner of the fortress, came out wearing a helmet and a stone with a hole in it like an egg on his head, and he was chanting poetry. Ali came out to him and struck him, losing the stone and helmet and splitting his head until the sword was in his molars. Then after Marhab, his brother Yasir came out chanting poetry, and Az-Zubayr ibn Al-`Awwam came out to him. His mother, Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib, said: Will my son be killed, O Messenger of God? He said: Rather, your son will kill him, God willing. Then they met and Al-Zubayr killed him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to conquer fortresses, kill fighters, take children captive, and seize wealth. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The first of their fortresses to be conquered was the fortress of Na’im, and there Mahmud ibn Salamah was killed. The Jews threw a stone at him and killed him. Then he conquered Al-Ammus, the fortress of Ibn Abi Al-Haqiq, and captured captives from it, including Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. Bilal brought her and another woman with her, and passed by them among the dead Jews. When the one with Safiyyah saw them, she cried out and slapped her face and threw dirt on her head. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw her, he said: Get this devil away from me. He ordered Safiyyah to be placed behind him, and he threw his cloak over her. The Muslims knew that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had chosen her for himself. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Bilal, when he saw what he saw from that Jewess: Mercy has been taken away from you, Bilal, when you pass by two women who have killed their men. Safiyyah had seen in a dream, while she was a bride with Kinanah ibn Al-Rabi’ ibn Abi Al-Haqiq, that a moon had fallen into her lap. She showed her dream to her husband, and he said: This is nothing but that you… She wished for the King of Hejaz, Muhammad, so he slapped her face a slap that made her eyes turn green. Then she was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she had a mark on her. He asked her what it was. She told him this story. Then her husband, Kinanah ibn al-Rabi’, was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had the treasure of Banu al-Nadir with him. So he asked him, but he denied knowing its location. Then a Jewish man was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have seen Kinanah in this ruin every morning. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Kinanah: Tell me, if we find it with you, should we kill you? He said: Yes. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the ruin to be dug up, and some of their treasure was taken out of it. Then he asked him what remained, but he refused to give it. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam, saying: Torture him until you extract what he has. Al-Zubayr kept striking his chest with a flint until he was on the verge of death. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, handed him over to Muhammad ibn Maslama, who struck off his head with his brother, Mahmud ibn Maslama. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Abdul Aziz bin Suhaib told us, on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, invaded Khaybar, and we prayed the dawn prayer there at dawn. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode on, and Abu Talha rode on, and I was riding behind Abu Talha. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ran through the alley of Khaybar, and my knee was touching the thigh of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he lifted his garment from his thigh until I could see the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he entered the village, he said: God is Great, Khaybar is ruined. When we descend into the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned. He said it three times, and the people went out to their work. They said: Muhammad. Abdul Aziz said, and some of our companions said: And Al-Khamis means the army. He said: So we seized it by force, and the captives were gathered and came. Dihya said: O Prophet of God, give me a slave girl from the captives. He said: Go and take a slave girl. So he took Safiyyah bint Huyayy. Then a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, Dihya has been given Safiyyah bint Huyayy, the lady of Qurayzah and Nadir. She is not suitable for anyone but you. He said: Call her to him. So he brought her. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at her, he said: Take another slave girl from the captives. He said: So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) freed her and married her. Thabit said to him: O Abu Hamza, what is her dowry? He said: Herself. Free her and marry her. When they were on the road, Umm Sulaym prepared her for him and presented her to him that night. The morning came when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was a bride. He said: Whoever has something, let him bring it. He spread out a cloth and one man would bring dates and another would bring ghee. I think he mentioned gruel. They made a hais and it was the feast of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Abdul Wahid Al-Shaibani told us: “I heard Ibn Abi Awfa say: ‘We were afflicted with famine during the nights of Khaybar. On the day of Khaybar, we came upon the domestic donkeys and slaughtered them. When the pots boiled, the crier of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out: ‘Turn the pots down and do not eat any of the donkeys’ meat.’ Abdullah said: ‘We said: The Prophet only forbade it because it was not subject to the fifth.’ Others said: ‘He absolutely forbade it.’ I asked Saeed bin Jubair and he said: ‘He absolutely forbade it.’” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Yahya bin Habib Al-Harithi told us, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Zaid, on the authority of Anas, “That a Jewish woman came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with a poisoned sheep, and he ate from it. She was brought to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he asked her about it. She said: ‘I wanted to kill you.’ He said: ‘What would have given you the power to do that?’ or he said: ‘Ali.’ They said: ‘Should we not kill her?’ He said: ‘No.’ I could still see it in the uvula of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” Muhammad bin Ismail said: Yunus said, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Urwa said: Aisha said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say during his illness in which he died: O Aisha, I am still feeling the pain of the food I ate in Khaybar, and now I feel my aorta being severed from that poison.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Harmi told us, Shu’bah told us, he said, ‘Amara told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Aishah, she said: When Khaybar was conquered, we said: Now we will be satisfied with dates. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmad bin Al-Muqaddam told us, Fadil bin Sulaiman told us, Musa bin Uqba told us, Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Ibn Umar that Umar bin Al-Khattab expelled the Jews and Christians from the land of Al-Hijaz. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) defeated the people of Khaybar, he wanted to expel the Jews from it. When he defeated the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the land belonged to God, His Messenger, and the Muslims. The Jews asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to leave them alone on the condition that they refrain from work and that they would be given half of the dates. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, We will leave you in that state for as long as we wish. So they remained in that state until Umar expelled them during his reign to Tayma and Jericho. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When the people of Fadak heard what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had done in Khaybar, they sent to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asking him to send them out, spare their bloodshed, and release their wealth to him. He did so. Then the people of Khaybar asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to deal with them on a 50/50 basis. He did so on the condition that if we wish, we will expel you. The people of Fadak made a similar agreement with him, so Khaybar belonged to the Muslims and Fadak belonged exclusively to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), because they had not brought any horses or camels against it. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was about to leave, Zainab bint Al-Harith, the wife of Salam ibn Mishkam, presented him with a roasted sheep. She asked him which part of the sheep the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) liked best. She was told: The forearm. So she poisoned it a lot and the rest of the sheep. Then she brought it to him. When she placed it in front of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he took the forearm and chewed a morsel of it but could not swallow it. Bishr ibn Al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur was with him, and he took some of it as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had taken. Bishr swallowed it, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spat it out. Then he said: This bone tells me that it is poisoned. Then he called for her and she confessed. He said: What made you do that? She said: I have done to my people what was not hidden from you, so I said: If he is a king, I will be rid of him, and if he is a prophet, he will inform. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forgave her, and Bishr ibn Al-Bara’ died from what he had eaten. He said: Umm Bishr bin Al-Baraa entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to visit him during his illness in which he died, and he said: O Umm Bishr, the food of Khaybar that I ate with your son keeps coming back to me, and now is the time for my aorta to rupture. The Muslims believed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died a martyr despite the honor God had bestowed upon him of prophethood.
48:21: 21. The Almighty’s saying, And another which you have not been able to conquer, meaning that God promised you the conquest of another city which you have not been able to conquer, which God has encompassed, until He opens it for you, as if He has preserved it for you and prevented it from others until you take it. Ibn Abbas said: God knew that He would open it for you. They differed about it. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Muqatil said that it was Persia and Rome, and the Arabs were not able to fight Persia and Rome, but were subservient to them until they were able to defeat them with Islam. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: It is Khaybar. God promised it to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he visited it, and they did not expect it. Qatada said: It is Mecca. Ikrimah said: Hunayn. Mujahid said: They have not been conquered until today. And God is over all things competent.
48:22: 22. And if those who disbelieve fight you, meaning: Asad, Ghatafan, and the people of Khaybar, they will turn their backs, [be routed], and then they will find neither protector nor helper.
48:23: 23. The way of God that has already been in effect, meaning like God’s way of giving victory to His friends and defeating His enemies, and you will not find any change in the way of God.
48:24: 24. The Almighty said: “And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them. And ever is God, of what you do, Seeing.” Abu Amr read it with the letter Ya, and the others read it with the letter Ta, and they differed regarding these: Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Amr bin Muhammad Al-Naqid told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with them: Eighty men from the people of Mecca descended upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mount At-Tan’im, armed, intending to betray the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. He took them peacefully and spared them, so God Almighty revealed this verse: And it is He who restrained their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them. Abdullah bin Mughaffal Al-Muzani said: “We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-Hudaibiyah at the base of the tree about which God Almighty mentioned in the Qur’an. On his back was a branch of that tree, so I lifted it off his back, and Ali bin Abi Talib was in front of him writing the peace treaty. Thirty young men wearing weapons came out to us and attacked us. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, invoked God against them, and God took away their sight. We rose up against them and seized them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: ‘Have you come with a covenant? Or has anyone given you security?’ They said: ‘No, by God.’ So he let them go, [and God Almighty revealed this verse].”
48:25: 25. The Almighty said: They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque, the verse. Al-Zuhri narrated from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out from Medina in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah with some ten hundred of his companions, intending to visit the House, but he did not intend to fight. He led with him seventy sacrificial animals, and the people were seven hundred men, and each sacrificial animal was for ten people. When he reached Dhul-Hulayfah, he garlanded the sacrificial animals, marked them, and entered ihram for Umrah. He sent a spy from Khuza'ah to inform him about Quraysh. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) traveled until he was at Ghadir al-Ashtat, near Usfan. His spy from Khuza'ah came to him and said: The Quraysh have gathered forces against you, and they have gathered the Abyssinians against you. They will fight you and prevent you from the House. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Advise me, O people. Do you think that I should attack the offspring of those who helped them and take their share? If they stay, they will stay in resentment, and if they escape, it will be a neck that God has cut off. Or do you think that we should go to the House and whoever prevents us from it, we will fight him? Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, I only went out to this house with the intention of fighting or waging war. So head towards it, and whoever prevents us from it, we will fight him. He said: Go in the name of God. So they set out. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Khalid bin Al-Walid is at Al-Ghamim with the cavalry of the Quraysh in the vanguard, so take the right. By God, Khalid did not notice them until they were at the rear of the army. He set off running as a warning to the Quraysh. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued until he reached the pass from which they descended upon them. His mount knelt. The people said: He has come, he has come. She persisted, and they said: Al-Qaswa has become weak. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Al-Qaswa has not become weak, and that is not her nature, but the One who held back the elephant has held her back. Then he said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if the Quraysh invite me today to a plan in which they honor the sacred things of God and maintain kinship ties, I will give it to them. Then he rebuked it and it jumped up. He said: So he turned away from them until he reached the furthest part of Al-Hudaibiyah, near a small place of water which the people were drinking from, but it was not long before the people had drawn water from it. The people complained to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of thirst, so he took an arrow from his quiver and gave it to a man from his companions called Najiyah ibn Umair, who was the driver of the Prophet’s camels (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He descended into the well and stuck it in its throat. By God, he did not stop with their army at the watering place until they left it. While they were like that, Badil ibn Warqa’ Al-Khuza’i came to him with a group of his people. Khuza’ah were a tribe that had advised the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from the people of Tihamah. He said: I left Ka’b ibn Lu’ayy and they have settled near the waters of Al-Hudaibiyah with them, the Awadh Al-Matafil, and they are your fighters and they have prevented you from the House. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We did not come to fight anyone, but we came to perform Umrah. The Quraysh have been exhausted and harmed by war. If they wish, I will extend their stay for a while and leave me alone with the people. If I prevail, then if they wish to enter into what the people have entered into, they will do so. Otherwise, they have gathered together. But if they refuse, then by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will fight them over this matter of mine until my forelock is separated, or God carries out His command. Then Badil said: I will tell them what you say. So he set off until he came to the Quraysh. He said: We have come to you from this man, and we heard him say something. If you want us to present it to you, we will. Their fools said: We have no need for you to tell us anything about him. And the one with an opinion among them said: Tell us what you heard him say. He said: I heard him say such and such, what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said. Then Urwah ibn Mas`ud ath-Thaqafi stood up and said: O people, are you not the father? They said: Yes. He said: Are you not the son? They said: Yes. He said: Do you accuse me? They said: No. He said: Do you not know that I mobilized the people of `Ukaz, and when they became angry, I came to you with my family, my children, and those who obeyed me? They said: Yes. He said: This man has offered you a plan of guidance, so accept it and let me go to him. They said: Go to him. So he went to him and began speaking to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said something similar to what he said to Badil. At that, `Urwah said: O Muhammad, tell me, if I exterminate your people, have you ever heard of anyone among the Arabs who wiped out his roots before you? If it is the other way around, by God, I see faces and young men among the people who would flee and leave you. Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said to him: Suck the clitoris of Al-Lat. Should we flee from him and leave him? He said: Who is that? They said: Abu Bakr. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, were it not for the favor you did me that I did not reward you for, I would have answered you. He said: And he began to speak to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and whenever he spoke to him, he would grab his beard, and Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah was standing over the head of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with a sword and a helmet. Whenever Urwah reached for the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) beard, he would hit his hand with the scabbard of the sword and say, “Take your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” So Urwah shook his head and said, Who is this? They said, This is Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah. He said, What treachery? Did I not participate in your treachery? Al-Mughira was a companion of some people in the pre-Islamic era, so he killed them and took their money. Then he came and converted to Islam. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for Islam, I accept it, but as for the money, I have no share in it. Then Urwah began to watch the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: By God, whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who would rub it on his face and skin. When he gave them an order, they would rush to do what he ordered. When he performed ablution, they would almost fight over his ablution water. When he spoke, they would lower their voices in his presence, but they would not stare at him out of respect for him. Urwah returned to his companions and said: O people, by God, I have visited kings, Caesar, Chosroes, and the Negus. By God, I have never seen a king whose companions respect him as much as the companions of Muhammad respect Muhammad. By God, whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spat, it fell into the hand of one of them, who would rub it on his face and skin. When he gave them an order, they would rush to do what he ordered. When he performed ablution, they would almost fight over his ablution water. When he spoke, they would lower their voices in his presence, but they would not stare at him out of respect for him. He has offered you a plan of guidance, so accept it. A man from Banu Kinanah said: Let me go to him. They said: Go to him. When he looked down upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who venerate sacrificial animals, so send them to him. So they sent them to him and people met him, chanting the Talbiyah. When he saw that, he said: Glory be to God! It is not appropriate for these people to be prevented from the House. When he returned to his companions, he said: I saw that the sacrificial animals had been girdled and branded, so I do not think they will be prevented from entering the House. Then they sent to him Al-Hulays ibn Alqamah, who was at that time the chief of the Abyssinians. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: This man is from a people who are deified, so send the sacrificial animals in his direction so that he may see him. When he saw the sacrificial animals flowing towards him from the width of the valley in their necklaces, their fur eaten away by being held back for a long time, he returned to the Quraysh and did not reach the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of respect for what he had seen. He said: O people of Quraysh, I have seen something that is not permissible: the stopping of sacrificial animals in their necklaces, and their fur has been eaten away by being held back for a long time from their place. They said to him: Sit down, you are only a Bedouin man with no knowledge. Al-Hulays became angry at that and said: O people of Quraysh, by God, we did not make an oath to you for this, nor did we make a contract with you for this, that you should turn away from the House of God whoever came to it honoring it. By the One in whose hand is the soul of Al-Hulays, you must leave Muhammad alone with what he came for, or I will send the Abyssinians away as one man would. They said: Stop, Al-Hulays, stay away from us until we take for ourselves what pleases us. To him. Then a man from among them called Makraz bin Hafs stood up and said: Let me go to him. They said: Go to him. When he came to them, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is Makraz, and he is a wicked man. So he began to speak to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. While he was speaking to him, Suhayl bin Amr came. Ikrimah said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: Your matter has been made easy for you. Al-Zuhri said in his hadith: Then Suhayl ibn Amr came and said: Come, let us write a document between us and you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and said to him: Write in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Suhayl said: As for the Most Gracious, by God I do not know what it is, but write in your name, O God, as you used to write. The Muslims said: By God, we will not write it except in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: Write in your name, O God. Then he said: Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has decided. Suhayl said: By God, if we had known that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have prevented you from the House or fought you. But write: Muhammad ibn Abdullah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, I am the Messenger of God, even if you call me a liar. Write, O Ali Muhammad ibn Abdullah. Al-Zuhri said: This is because he said: They will not ask for a plan in which they will honor the sacred things of God except that I will give it to them. So he wrote: This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah and Suhayl ibn Amr agreed upon, and they agreed to stop fighting the people for ten years, during which people will be safe and will refrain from attacking one another. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: And that you leave us alone with the House, so that we may circumambulate it. So Suhayl said: By God, the Arabs will not say that we took it by force, but that will be from next year. So he wrote, and Suhayl said: And that no man from us will come to you - even if he is of your religion - except that you return him to us. So the Muslims said: Glory be to God, how can he be returned to the polytheists when he came as a Muslim? Abu Ishaq narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ the story of the peace treaty in which they said: If we knew that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have prevented you from anything, but you are Muhammad ibn Abdullah. He said: I am the Messenger of God and I am Muhammad ibn Abdullah. Then he said to Ali, may God be pleased with him: Erase the Messenger of God. He said: No, by God, I will never erase you. He said: Show it to me. So he showed it to him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, erased it with his hand. In his narration: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the letter, and he was not good at writing, so he wrote: This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah has agreed to. Al-Bara’ said: He made peace on three things: that whoever came to him from the polytheists, he would return him to them, and whoever came to them from the Muslims, they would not return him, and that he would enter it the next year and stay there for three days, and he would not enter it except with a weapon, a sword, a bow, or the like. Thabit narrated on the authority of Anas that the Quraysh made peace with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and stipulated that whoever of you comes to us, we will not return him to you, and whoever of us comes to you, you will return him to us. They said: O Messenger of God, have you married this one? He said: Yes, whoever of us goes to them, God will distance him, but whoever of them comes to us, God will provide relief and a way out. We return to the hadith of Az-Zuhri. He said: While they were like that, Abu Jabal bin Suhayl bin Amr came, swaying in his chains. He had escaped and gone out from the lower part of Mecca, until he threw himself among the Muslims. Suhayl said: O Muhammad, this is the first person I will sue you for, that you return him to me. The Prophet said: We have not yet fulfilled the contract. He said: Then by God, I will never make peace with you on anything. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Then grant him asylum... I will not grant him asylum to you. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes, do it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Then Suhayl began to drag him to return him to the Quraysh. Abu Jandal said: O group of Muslims, should I return him to the polytheists when I came as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered? He had been severely tortured for the sake of God. In the hadith: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Jandal, be patient, for God will make a way out and relief for you and for those who are weak with you. We have made a treaty and a peace agreement between us and the people, and we will not betray. Then Umar jumped up and walked beside Abu Jandal, saying: Be patient, for they are only polytheists, and the blood of one of them is like the blood of a dog. He brought the hilt of the sword close to him. Umar said: I hoped that he would take the sword and strike his father with it, but the man was jealous of his father. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left without doubting the victory, because of a vision that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had seen. When they saw that, the people were seized with a terrible situation until they were on the verge of perishing, and the matter of Abu Jandal increased their evil to what they were already suffering. Omar said: [By God] I have never doubted since I converted to Islam except on that day. Al-Zuhri said in his hadith on the authority of Urwah on the authority of [Marwan] and Al-Miswar, and Abu Wa’il narrated it on the authority of Sahl bin Hunaif that Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: So I came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: Are you not truly the Prophet of God? He said: Yes. I said: Are we not on the truth and our enemy is on falsehood? He said: Yes. I said: Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in Hell? He said: Yes. I said: Then why do we give up our religion? He said: I am the Messenger of God and I do not disobey Him and He is my supporter. I said: Did you not tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it? He said: Yes. Did I not tell you that we would come to it this year? I said: No. He said: Then I will come to it and circumambulate it. I came to Abu Bakr and said: O Abu Bakr, is this not truly the Prophet of God? He said: Yes. I said: Are we not on the truth and our enemy is on falsehood? He said: Yes. I said: Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in Hell? He said: Yes. I said: Then why would we give up our religion? He said: O man, he is the Messenger of God, he does not disobey his Lord and He is his supporter, so hold fast to his roots, for by God, he is on the truth. I said: Didn't he tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it? He said: Yes. Did he tell you that you would come to it this year? I said: No. He said: Then I will come to it and circumambulate it. Al-Zuhri said: Omar said: So I did some work for that. He said: When he had finished writing the book, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to his companions: Get up and slaughter, then shave your head. By God, not a single one of them got up until he had said that three times. When none of them got up, he got up and went to Umm Salamah and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah said: O Prophet of God, do you like that? Go out and do not say a word to any of them until you have slaughtered your sacrifice and called your barber to shave your head. So he went out and did not speak to any of them until he had done that. He slaughtered his sacrifice and called his barber to shave his head. When they saw that, they got up and slaughtered, and some of them shaved each other until some of them were about to kill each other out of grief. Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas said: On the Day of Hudaybiyyah, some men shaved their heads while others shortened them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: May God have mercy on those who shave their heads. They said: And those who shorten their heads? He...And those who shorten their heads.” They said: O Messenger of God, why did you express your sympathy for those who shaved their heads but not for those who shortened their heads? He said: Because they did not complain. Ibn Umar said: That was because some people were waiting and said, ‘Perhaps we will circumambulate the House.’ Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave Abu Jahl, in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah, among his gifts, a camel with a silver ring on its head, to enrage the polytheists with that. Al-Zuhri said in his hadith: Then believing women came to him, so God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, until he reached: By the protection of the disbelieving women (al-Mumtahanah 60:10). On that day, Umar, may God be pleased with him, divorced two of his wives who were polytheists, and he married one of them to Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the other to Safwan ibn Umayya. He said: He forbade them from returning the women and ordered the return of the dowry. He said: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to Medina, and Abu Basir, Utbah ibn Asid, a man from Quraysh who was a Muslim, came to him. He was one of those who had been imprisoned in Mecca. Azhar ibn Abd Auf and Al-Akhns ibn Shuraiq Al-Thaqafi wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about him and sent a man from Banu Amir ibn Lu’ayy in search of him, with one of their freedmen. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: The covenant that you made to us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Basir, we have given these people what you know, and treachery is not permissible in our religion. God will make for you and for those who are weak with you a way out and a way out. Then he gave him to the two men and they went out with him until they reached Dhu’l-Hulayfah. They stopped and ate some of their dates. Abu Basir said to one of the two men: By God, I see that your sword is good. The other drew it and said: Yes, by God, it is good. I have tried it and tried it again. Abu Basir said: Show me, so I can see it. So they took him and he attacked him with it and beat him until he was cold. He fled. The other one came to the city and ran into the mosque. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he saw him, This man has seen fear. When he reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said, Woe to you, what is wrong with you? He said: By God, my companion was killed and I am to be killed. By God, he did not leave until Abu Basir came out, girded with a sword, and stood before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, God has fulfilled your covenant. You returned me to them, then God saved me from them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to his mother, the instigator of war, if only someone had been with him. When he heard that, he knew that he would return him to them, so he went out until he reached the sword of the sea. The Muslims who had been imprisoned in Mecca heard the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Abu Basir: Woe to his mother, the instigator of war, if only someone had been with him. So a group of them went out to him, and Abu Jandal bin Suhayl escaped and joined Abu Basir, until nearly seventy men had gathered around him. By God, they did not hear a camel that had gone out to the Quraysh to Syria, that is, they intercepted it and killed them and took their money. The Quraysh sent to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, imploring him by God and kinship to send to them. Whoever comes to him is safe. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to them, and they came to him in Medina. Then God Almighty revealed: And it is He who restrained their hands. From you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca after He had given you victory over them. And God is Seeing of what you do. Until he reached the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance. Their fanaticism was that they did not acknowledge that he was the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they did not acknowledge In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and they stood between him and the House. God the Almighty said: They are the ones who disbelieved, meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, and prevented you from al-Masjid al-Haram, from performing Tawaf around it, and the sacrificial animals, meaning: they prevented the sacrificial animals, which were seventy sacrificial animals that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) drove, withheld, confined. It is said: I confined it, and withholding is for the intransitive form, just as it is said: he returned, returning, and returning. that it should reach its place, meaning its place of slaughter and where its slaughtering is permitted, meaning the Sacred Sanctuary. And had it not been for believing men and believing women, meaning the oppressed in Mecca, whom you did not know, “lest you trample them,” by killing and falling upon them, and there should befall you on their part a disgrace without your knowledge, Ibn Zayd said: A disgrace of sin. Ibn Ishaq said: The blood money. It was said: The expiation is because God Almighty has made it obligatory for the killer of a believer in the land of war if his faith is not known to be expiated without blood money, as He said: But if he is from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave An-Nisa’ 92. It was said: It is that the Muslims criticize you and say, People of their religion. The known meaning is: hardship. He says: If it were not for the fact that you have tread upon believing men and believing women whom you do not know, then you would be obligated to pay expiation for them or be disgraced. The answer to if it were not is omitted, and its meaning is: He would have given you permission to enter it, but he stood between you and that. That God may admit into His mercy whom He wills. The lam in li-dikhul is connected to an omitted word indicated by the meaning of the statement, meaning: He prevented you from that so that God may admit into His mercy in the religion of Islam whomever He wills of the people of Mecca after the peace treaty before you entered it. If you had separated, if you had distinguished yourself, meaning the believers from the disbelievers, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment, by captivity and killing at your hands. Some scholars said: We would have punished is an answer to two statements: Had it not been for men and Had they been separated. Then he said: So that God may admit into His mercy whomever He wills, meaning the believing men and women. And His statement: In His mercy, meaning His Paradise. Qatada said about this verse: God defends the believers from the unbelievers just as He defended the weak believers from the polytheists of Mecca.
48:26: 26. When those who disbelieved put into their hearts arrogance, when they prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from the House, and did not recite In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, and denied Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Arrogance means pride. It is said: So-and-so is arrogant if he is angry and proud. Muqatil said: The people of Mecca said: They killed our sons and brothers, and then they came upon us, [and the Arabs said that they came upon us] in spite of us, and Al-Lat and Al-Uzza would not come upon us. This is the pre-Islamic fanaticism that entered their hearts. So God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, so that they were not overcome by the zeal that had overwhelmed them, so that they would disobey God in their fighting, and He made them adhere to the word of piety. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ikrimah, As-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and most of the commentators said: The word of piety is There is no god but God. It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Mu’ab, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ali and Ibn Omar said: The word of piety is ‘There is no god but God and God is greatest.’ Ata bin Abi Rabah said: There is no power except from God alone, with no partner for Him. His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent. Ata Al-Khurasani said: It is There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Al-Zuhri said: It is in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And they were more deserving of it than the infidels of Mecca, and its people, meaning they were its people in God’s knowledge, because God Almighty chose for His religion and the companionship of His Prophet the people of goodness, and God is Knowing of all things.
48:27: 27. "God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger. You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in safety." This is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was shown in a dream in Medina before he set out for Hudaybiyyah that he and his companions were entering the Sacred Mosque in safety, shaving their heads and cutting their hair short. He told his companions about this, and they were happy and thought that they had entered Mecca that year. But when they returned and had not entered, they were distressed, so God revealed this verse. It was narrated on the authority of Majma’ bin Jariyah Al-Ansari: “He said: We witnessed Al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When we turned away from it, the people were shaking their camels. Some of them said: What is the matter with the people? They said: Revelation has been sent down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So we went out, hurrying, and found the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing on his mount at Kura’ Al-Ghamim. When the people gathered around him, he recited: ‘Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest.’ Umar said: ‘Is it a conquest, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul.’” It is evidence that what was meant by the conquest was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and the fulfillment of the vision was in the following year. So the Almighty said: God has truly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger. He informed us that the vision that He showed him on his way to Hudaybiyyah, that he and his companions would enter the Sacred Mosque, was true and correct. His statement: You will surely enter means, and he said: You will surely enter. Ibn Kaysan said: You will surely enter is from the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to his companions, narrating his dream. So God informed us on the authority of His Messenger that he said that, and he only made an exception despite his knowledge of her entering by God Almighty’s information, out of respect for the manners of God, where He said to him: And do not say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow,’ except [when adding], ‘If God wills’ (al-Kahf 18:23). Abu Ubaidah said: If means when. Its meaning is: If God wills, like His saying: If you are believers. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: It is possible that the exception is from entering, because there is a year between the vision and its confirmation, and people died in that year, so the meaning of the verse is: You will all enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing. It was said that the exception applies to security, not to entry, because there was no doubt about entry, like the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when entering the cemetery: And we, God willing, will join you. So the exception refers to joining, not to death. Shaving your heads, all of it, and cutting short, by taking some of its hair, “do not fear. So He knows what you did not know,” that the reconciliation was in the peace and delaying the entry, and this is the saying of God Almighty: And had it not been for believing men and believing women (al-Fath 48:25). Then He made before that, meaning before you entered the Sacred Mosque, an imminent conquest, which is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah according to the majority, and it was said: the conquest of Khaybar.
48:28: 28. “It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religions. And sufficient is God as Witness,” that you are a truthful prophet in what you say.
48:29: 29. Muhammad is the Messenger of God, the speech was completed here, Ibn Abbas said, testifying to his prophethood, then he said, starting: And those with him, so the waw in it is for resumption, meaning: and those with him from the believers, harsh against the disbelievers, harsh with them as a lion against its prey, not feeling compassion for them, compassionate among themselves, sympathetic and loving to one another, like a son to his father, as he said: humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers 5:54. You will see them bowing and prostrating, he informed about the abundance of their prayers and their persistence in them, seek[ing] bounty from God, that He should admit them into Paradise, and approval, that He should be pleased with them, their mark, meaning their sign, is on their faces from the traces of prostration, they differed about this mark. Some people said: They are light and whiteness on their faces on the Day of Resurrection by which they will be known that they prostrated in the world, and this is the narration of Atiyah al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. Ataa bin Abi Rabah and al-Rabi’ said: Ibn Anas: Their faces were illuminated from the amount of prayer they performed. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: The places of prostration on their faces were like the moon on a full moon night. Others said: It is a good appearance, humility and modesty. This is the narration of Al-Walabi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is not what you see, but it is the mark of Islam, its nature, characteristic and humility. This is the saying of Mujahid, and the meaning is: Prostration gave them humility and a good appearance by which they are known. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the yellowness of the face due to staying up late. Al-Hassan said: If you saw them, you would think they were sick, but they were not sick. Ikrimah and Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the trace of dust on the forehead. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They prostrate on the dirt, not on clothes. Ata Al-Khurasani said: This verse includes everyone who maintains the five daily prayers. That, which I mentioned, their likeness, their description in the Torah, here the speech is complete, then he mentioned their description in the Gospel, so he said: And their likeness, their description, in the Gospel is like a seed which sends forth its shoot, Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read: (its shoot) with the opening of the taa, and the others read it with the sukoon, and they are two languages like the river and the river, and he meant its shoots, it is said: the seed shot forth, so it is shot forth, if it shoots forth, Muqatil said: It is a single plant, and if it comes out after it, then it is its shoot. Al-Saddī said: It is that the other energy comes out with it. His saying: So he supported him. Ibn Amir read: So he supported him in the shortened form, and the rest read it in the extended form, meaning: He strengthened him, aided him, and strengthened his back. So he became thick, that is, the crop became thick. So he became straight, that is, its plants were complete and grew together and stood up. On its stem, that is, its roots. It amazes the farmers, that amazes its farmers. This is a parable that God Almighty gave to the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Gospel [that they will be few, then they will increase and multiply. Qatada said: The example of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Gospel: It is written that a people will emerge who will produce crops, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. It was said: The crop is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the shore is his companions and the believers. It was narrated on the authority of Mubarak bin Fadala on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: Muhammad is the Messenger of God and those with him: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. Harsh against the disbelievers: Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. Compassionate among themselves: Uthman, may God be pleased with him. You will see them bowing and prostrating: Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Seeking bounty from God: the rest of the ten who were given good tidings of Paradise. It was said: Like a seed that was brought forth Muhammad, its shoot was brought forth Abu Bakr, then Umar supported it and it became thick” Uthman, for Islam then it stood firm on its stalk Ali bin Abi Talib, Islam was made straight by his sword, (the farmers are amazed) He said: They are the believers. To enrage the infidels with them, Omar’s words to the people of Mecca after he converted to Islam: Do not worship God secretly from today on. Abu Hamid bin Muhammad al-Shuja’i al-Sarakhsi narrated to us by dictation, Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Ahmad al-Qaffal informed us, Abu Ahmad Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Fadl al-Samarqandi informed us, my sheikh Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin al-Fadl al-Balkhi informed us, Abu Raja’ Qutaybah bin Sa’id informed us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad al-Dawwardi informed us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Hamid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Awf: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Abu Bakr is in Paradise, Umar is in Paradise, Uthman is in Paradise, Ali is in Paradise, Talhah is in Paradise, al-Zubayr is in Paradise, Abdul Rahman bin Awf is in Paradise, Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas is in Paradise, Sa’id bin Zaid is in Paradise, and Abu Ubaidah bin al-Jarrah is in Paradise.” Abu Al-Muzaffar Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Tamimi narrated to us, Abu Abd Al-Rahman bin Uthman bin Qasim informed us, Khaithama bin Sulayman bin Haidar Al-Atrabulsi informed us, Ahmad bin Hashim Al-Antaki informed us, Qutba bin Al-Ala’ informed us, Sufyan Al-Thawri informed us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The most merciful of my nation is Abu Bakr, the strictest of them in the matter of God is Umar, the most truthful of them in modesty is Uthman, the most knowledgeable of them in the science of jurisprudence is Zaid, the most knowledgeable of them in the Qur’an is Abu, and the most knowledgeable of them in what is lawful and what is unlawful is Muadh bin Jabal. Every nation has a trustee, and the trustee of this nation is Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah.” It was narrated by Muammar on the authority of Qatada, without a chain of transmission, and it says: And the most just of them is Ali. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ma’la bin Asad told us, Abdul Aziz Al-Mukhtar told us, Khalid Al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Abu Uthman, who said: Amr bin Al-Aas told me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him in charge of the army of Dhat Al-Salasil. He said: So I went to him and said: Who is the most beloved person to you? He said: Aisha. I said: Of men. He said: Her father. I said: Then who? He said: Umar bin Al-Khattab. He counted some men, but he remained silent for fear that he would put me at the end of them. Abu Mansur Abdul Malik and Abu Al-Fath Nasr, sons of Ali bin Ahmad bin Mansur and Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Shadhuyi Al-Tusi, told us: Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Ya’qub told us: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Kaysan Al-Nahwi told us: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Sharik Al-Asadi told us: Ibrahim bin Ismail - he is Ibn Yahya bin Salamah bin Kuhayl - told us: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Abu Al-Zu’za’, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Follow the example of those who come after me from my companions: Abu Bakr and Umar, and be guided by the guidance of Ammar, and hold fast to the covenant of Abdullah bin Mas’ud.” Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bishran told us, Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, that someone trembled while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, and Uthman were on him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Be steadfast, for there is no one upon you except a prophet, a truthful person, or a martyr. Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Saeed al-Ashja told us, Waki’ told us, al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Adi ibn Thabit, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded me that none loves you except a believer, and none hates you except a hypocrite. Abu Al-Muzaffar Al-Tamimi told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Uthman told us, Khaithamah bin Sulaiman told us, Muhammad bin Isa bin Hayyan Al-Madani told us, Muhammad bin Al-Fadl bin Atiyah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Kaslam, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever dies from among my companions in a land, he will be their light and their leader on the Day of Resurrection. The Almighty said: To enrage the disbelievers with them, meaning that He increased their numbers and made them strong so that they would be an enrage to the disbelievers. Malik ibn Anas said: Whoever wakes up with resentment towards the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been afflicted by this verse. Abu al-Tayyib Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ala’ al-Baghawi told us, Abu Muammar al-Mufaddal ibn Ismail ibn Ibrahim al-Ismaili told us, my grandfather Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ismaili told us, al-Haytham ibn Khalaf al-Duri told me, al-Mufaddal ibn Ghassan ibn al-Mufaddal al-Ala’i told us, Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa’d told us, Ubaydah ibn Abi Rabita told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, God, regarding my companions, God, God, regarding my companions, God, God, regarding my companions. Do not take them as a target after me. Whoever loves them loves them out of my love, and whoever hates them hates them out of my hatred. Whoever harms them has harmed me, and whoever harms me has harmed God, and whoever harms God is likely to be seized by Him.” Abu Al-Muzaffar bin Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Hamid Al-Tamimi narrated to us, Abu Muhammad Abd Al-Rahman bin Uthman bin Al-Qasim narrated to us, Abu Al-Hasan Khaithama bin Sulaiman narrated to us, Ibrahim bin Abdullah Al-Absi Al-Qassar narrated to us in Kufa, Wakee’ bin Al-Jarrah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not revile my companions, for by the One in Whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend gold equivalent to Mount Uhud, he would not reach the level of one of them, or even half of it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Za’farani told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Urwa told us, Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Ishkab told us, Shababah bin Suwar told us, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Abu Khabab, on the authority of Abu Salim Al-Hamadhani, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If you are pleased to be among the people of Paradise, then there will be people who will claim to love you, they will recite the Qur’an, but it will not go beyond their collarbones, and they will be called the Rafidah. If you find them, then fight them, for they are polytheists.” The chain of transmission of this hadith is questionable. God Almighty says: God has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward, Ibn Jarir said: meaning from the sapling that the crops produced, and they are those who enter Islam after the crops until the Day of Resurrection. The ha and the mim were returned to the meaning of the sapling, not to its wording, and for this reason He did not say: (from it), forgiveness and a great reward, meaning Paradise.
49:1: 1. Medinan, O you who have believed, do not precede God and His Messenger, Yaqub read: (Do not precede) with a fat-ha on the ta' and the dal, from taqaddum, meaning do not precede, and the others read it with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the dal, from taqaddum, which is intransitive and means to advance, [Abu Ubaidah said] the Arabs say: Do not precede the imam and the father, meaning do not rush to command or prohibit without him, and the meaning is: between the two imams. And the qadam: meaning do not precede their commands and prohibitions. They differed over its meaning: Al-Sha'bi narrated on the authority of Jabir that it is regarding slaughtering on the day of Eid al-Adha, and it is the saying of Al-Hasan, meaning do not slaughter before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) slaughters, and that is because some people slaughtered before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed, so he ordered them to repeat the slaughter. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Sulayman bin Rahab told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Zayd, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Al-Ba’, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us on the Day of Sacrifice, and said: “The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is to pray, then we return and slaughter. Whoever does that has followed our Sunnah, and whoever slaughters before we pray, then it is only the meat of a calf for his family and has nothing to do with the ritual.” Masruq narrated on the authority of Aisha that it was forbidden to fast on the day of doubt, meaning do not fast before your Prophet fasts. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us that Ibn Jurayj told them on the authority of Ibn Malikah, that Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told them that a group of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr said: The matter of Al-Qa’qa’ is Ma’bad bin Zararah. Umar said: Rather, the matter of Al-Aqra’ bin Habis. Abu Bakr said: You only wanted to contradict me. Umar said: You did not want to contradict you. So they argued until their voices rose, and the following was revealed concerning that: O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger until it ended. Nafi` narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, who said: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet until His saying: a great reward. He added: Ibn al-Zubayr said: So Umar did not hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after this verse until he asked him about it, and he did not mention it on the authority of his father, meaning Abu Bakr. Qatada said: The verse was revealed about people who used to say: If only it had been revealed about such and such, or if it had been done about such and such, then God disliked that. Mujahid said: Do not say anything to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until God decrees it through his tongue. Ad-Dahhak said: It means in fighting and religious laws, do not decide a matter without God and His Messenger. And fear God in wasting His right and disobeying His command. God is All-Hearing of your words and All-Knowing of your actions.
49:2: 2. O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or be loud to him in speech as you loudly speak to one another, He commanded them to revere and honor him and not to raise their voices in his presence, and not to call him as they call one another, lest your deeds become worthless, lest your good deeds be rendered worthless. It was also said: for fear that your good deeds might be rendered worthless, while you perceive not. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit Al-Bunani, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet…’ the verse, Thabit bin Qais sat in his house and said: ‘I am one of the people of Hellfire,’ and he was kept away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Saad bin Muadh, saying: ‘O Abu Amr, what is the matter with Thabit that he is complaining?’ Saad said: ‘He is my neighbor and I do not know of any complaint from him.’ Saad came to him and mentioned to him the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
