Thabit said: ‘This verse was revealed, and you know that I am one of you who raises my voice to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I am one of the people of Hellfire.’ Saad mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Rather, he is one of the people of Paradise.’” " It was narrated that “When this verse was revealed, Thabit sat in the road crying. Asim bin Adi passed by him and said: What makes you cry, Thabit? He said: I fear that this verse was revealed about me, and I have a loud voice. I fear that my deeds will be in vain and that I will be among the people of Hellfire. Asim went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Thabit was overcome by tears. He went to his wife, Jamila bint Abdullah bin Abi Salul, and said to her: When you enter my horse’s house, fasten the latch on me with a nail. He said: I will not leave until God takes my soul or the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is pleased with me. Asim went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what had happened. He said to him: Go and call him. Asim came to the place where he had seen him but did not find him. He came to his family and found him in the horse’s house. He said to him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is calling you. He said: Break the latch. So he broke it. They went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What makes you cry, Thabit? He said: I am loud and I fear.” That this verse was revealed about him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you not satisfied to live a praiseworthy life, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise? He said: I am satisfied with the good report of God and His Messenger, and I will never raise my voice against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God revealed:
49:3: 3. Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God the verse. Anas said: We were watching a man from the people of Paradise walking in front of us. When the day of Yamamah came in the war against Musaylimah the Liar, Thabit saw some defeat among the Muslims and a group of them were defeated, so he said: Fie on these people! Then Thabit said to Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah: “We never fought the enemies of God with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) like this.” Then they stood firm and fought until they were killed, and Thabit was martyred wearing a shield. After his death, a man from the Companions saw him in a dream and he said to him: “Know that so-and-so, a man from the Muslims, took off my shield and went with it. It is in a corner of the camp near a horse that is about the same height as him. He has placed a basket over my shield. Go to Khalid ibn al-Walid and tell him so that he can retrieve my shield. Go to Abu Bakr, the successor to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and tell him: I have a debt that must be paid, and so-and-so is one of my slaves who is freed.” The man informed Khalid and found his shield and the horse as he had described it to him, so he retrieved the shield. Khalid told Abu Bakr about that dream and Abu Bakr approved his will. Malik ibn Anas said: I do not know of a will that was approved after the death of its owner except this one. Abu Hurairah and Ibn Abbas said: When this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr would not speak to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except as a confidant. Ibn al-Zubayr said: When this verse was revealed, Umar did not speak to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after that, so that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would hear his words until he asked him why he was lowering his voice. Then God the Most High revealed: Indeed, those who lower their voices lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God out of reverence for him, those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety He tested them and purified them as gold is tested by fire and its purest is brought out, for them is forgiveness and a great reward.
49:4: 4. Indeed, those who call you from behind the chambers, the general public read it with a damma on the jim, and Abu Jaafar read it with a fatha on the jim. They are two languages, and it is the plural of stone, and stone is the plural of room, so it is the plural of plural. Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a detachment to Banu al-Anbar and appointed Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari as their leader. When they knew that he was heading towards them, they fled and left their families behind. Uyaynah ibn Hisn took them captive and brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. After that, their men came to ransom their children. They arrived at noon and agreed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, speaking about his family. When the children saw them, they cried out to their fathers, crying. Each of the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a room, so they hastened for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come out to them. They began to call out: O Muhammad, come out to us, until they woke him up from his sleep. He came out to them and they said: O Muhammad, ransom our children for us. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down and said: God commands you to place a man between you and them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Would you be satisfied that there should be between me and you Subrah ibn Amr, and he is of your religion? They said: Yes. So Sabra said: I will not judge between them unless my uncle, the one-eyed Ibn Bashamah, is a witness. They agreed to him. The one-eyed man said: I think you should ransom half of them and free the other half. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am satisfied. So he ransomed half of them and freed the other half. Then God revealed: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason, describing them as ignorant and lacking in reason.
49:5: 5. And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. Muqatil said: It would have been better for them because you would have set them all free and released them without ransom. And God is Forgiving and Merciful. Qatada said: It was revealed about some Bedouins from Banu Tamim who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and called out at the door. It is narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: Banu Tamim came and called out at the door: Come out to us, O Muhammad, for praising us is an adornment and criticizing us is a disgrace. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out saying: It is God whom praising is an adornment and criticizing is a disgrace. They said: We are people from Banu Tamim. We have brought our poets and orators to recite poetry to you and boast to you. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was not sent for poetry nor commanded to boast, but bring them. A young man from among them stood up and mentioned his own merit and the merit of his people. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, who was the orator of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Stand up and answer him. So he answered him. Their poet stood up and recited some verses. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Hassan ibn Thabit: Answer him. So he answered him. Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis stood up and said: Muhammad has been given the task, and by God, I do not know this matter. Our orator spoke, and their orator spoke better. Our poet spoke, and their poet spoke better. Then he approached. From the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What happened before this does not harm you. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him the same as he gave them, and some of them disparaged him. Voices rose and the noise increased in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the following verse was revealed about them: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices the four verses until His saying: Forgiving, Most Merciful. Zayd ibn Arqam said: Some Arabs came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of them said to one another: Let us go to this man. If he is a prophet, we will be the luckiest people with him, and if he is a king, we will live in his chambers. So they came and began to call out to him, O Muhammad, O Muhammad. Then God revealed: “Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason. And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.”
49:6: 6. God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, verify it. This verse was revealed about Al-Walid bin Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Banu Al-Mustaliq after the battle as a tax collector. There was enmity between him and them in the pre-Islamic period. When the people heard about him, they welcomed him out of respect for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Satan told him that they wanted to kill him, but he was afraid of them and returned by the road to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Banu Al-Mustaliq have withheld their tax and want to kill me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry and wanted to attack them. The people heard of his return, so they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we heard about your messenger, so we went out to meet him, honor him, and fulfill what we accepted from God the Almighty’s right. Then he decided to return, and we feared that he had only returned by the road because of a letter that came to him from you out of anger with us, and we seek refuge in God from His anger and the anger of His Messenger. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accused them. And he sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to them secretly with an army and ordered him to conceal his arrival from them, and he said to him: Look, if you see from them something that indicates their faith, then take from them the zakat of their wealth, and if you do not see that, then do with them what is done with the infidels. So Khalid did that, and he met them and heard from them the call to prayer for the sunset and evening prayers, so he took their zakat from them, and he did not see from them anything but obedience and goodness, so he returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him the report, so God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a wicked person meaning al-Walid ibn Uqbah, with information “then investigate, lest you strike” so that you do not strike through killing and fighting, a people innocent out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful of your striking by mistake.
49:7: 7. And know that among you is the Messenger of God, so fear God lest you say falsehood or deny him, for God informs him and knows your circumstances and you will be disgraced. If he were to obey you, meaning the Messenger, in much of the matter, that you inform him of and he rules according to your opinion, you would be cursed, you would sin and perish. But God has endeared faith to you, making it the most beloved of religions to you, and has beautified it, made it beautiful, in your hearts, so that you have chosen it and obeyed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And He has made disbelief and wickedness hateful to you, Ibn Abbas said: He means lying, and disobedience, all of the disobedience of God. Then he returned from the address to the report, and said: Those are the rightly guided, the guided ones.
49:8: 8. By grace, meaning this was a grace, from God and a blessing, and God is Knowing and Wise.
49:9: 9. The Almighty said: “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them” verse. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musaddad told us, Mu’tamir told us, he said: I heard my father say: Anas said: It was said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Why don’t you go to Abdullah bin Ubayy? So the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, went to him and rode a donkey and the Muslims went walking with him, and it is marshy land. When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to him, he said: Go away from me, by God, the stench of your donkey has bothered me. A man from among the Ansar said: By God, the donkey of the Messenger of God smells better than you. So a man from his people became angry on Abdullah’s behalf and they quarreled, and each of them had his companions angry, and there was a fight between them with palm branches, hands and sandals. It reached us that the following verse was revealed: “And if two parties among the believers should quarrel, then make peace between them.” It is narrated that when it was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, read it, and they reconciled with each other. Qatada said: It was revealed about two men from the Ansar who were disputing over a right between them. One of them said to the other: I will take my right from you by force, because of the large number of his tribe. The other called him to bring him to trial before the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he refused to follow him. The matter remained between them until they pushed each other and attacked each other with their hands and sandals, and there was no fighting with swords. Sufyan said on the authority of al-Suddi: There was a woman from the Ansar called Umm Zayd who was married to a man, and there was something between her and her husband, so he took her to an upper room and imprisoned her. report of that reached her people, so they came, and his people came and fought with their hands and sandals, so God Almighty revealed: “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them” by calling for the rule of God’s Book and being satisfied with what is in it for and against them. But if one of them transgresses against the other and refuses to respond to the rule of God’s Book, then fight against the one that transgresses until it returns returns to the command of God in His Book. And if it returns returns to the truth, “then make peace between them with justice” by encouraging them to be fair and satisfied with God’s rule. And act justly be just, for God loves those who act justly.
49:10: 10. The believers are but brothers, in religion and guardianship, “so make peace between your two brothers,” if they disagree and fight. Jacob read between your brothers with a ta’ for the plural, and fear God, so do not disobey Him or go against His command, that you may receive mercy. [Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us], his father Muhammad Al-Hussein bin Ahmad Al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Al-Sarraj told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqil, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A Muslim is a brother of a Muslim. He does not wrong him or insult him. Whoever attends to the need of his brother, God will attend to his need. Whoever relieves a Muslim of a hardship, God will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever conceals a Muslim, God will conceal him on the Day of Resurrection.” These two verses are evidence that transgression does not remove the name of faith, because God the Almighty called them brothers believers even though they were transgressors. This is indicated by what was narrated on the authority of Al-Harith Al-A’war that Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him - who was the role model - was asked about the people of the Camel and Siffin in fighting the transgressors: Are they polytheists? He said: No, they fled from polytheism. It was said: Are they hypocrites? He said: No, the hypocrites do not remember God except a little. It was said: What is their condition? He said: Our brothers have transgressed against us. In Islamic law, the aggressor is the one who rebels against a just ruler. If a group of people with strength and power gathers and refuses to obey the just ruler based on an interpretation that may be interpreted, and appoints an ruler, the ruling regarding them is that the ruler should send an imam to them and call them to obey him. If they reveal a grievance, he should remove it from them. If they do not mention a grievance and persist in their transgression, the ruler should fight them until they return to his obedience. Then the ruling regarding fighting them is that their fleeing ones should not be pursued, their prisoners should not be killed, and their wounded should not be killed. On the day of Siffin, a crier called out to Ali may God be pleased with him regarding a prisoner, and he said to him: I will not kill you patiently, for I fear God, Lord of the worlds. And if one of the two groups destroys the other in the course of fighting, whether life or property, then there is no liability on him. Ibn Shihab said: During that strife, there was bloodshed, in some cases the killer and the killed were known, and a great deal of money was destroyed. Then the people settled down until the war between them subsided, and judgment was passed on them. I do not know of anyone who took retribution from anyone or fined anyone for the money he had destroyed. As for those who do not meet these three conditions, such as if they were a small group with no protection, or they did not have an interpretation, or they did not appoint an imam, then they should not be attacked if they do not set up a fight and do not attack Muslims. If they do, then they are like highway robbers. It was narrated that Ali, may God be pleased with him, heard a man saying in a corner of the mosque: There is no rule except for God Almighty. Ali said: A word of truth intended to be a cure. You have three obligations towards us: We will not prevent you from the mosques of God so that you may mention God’s name in them, we will not prevent you from the spoils of war as long as your hands are with ours, and we will not initiate fighting with you.
49:11: 11. And the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [the verse]. Ibn Abbas said that it was revealed about Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas, because he had a deafness in his ears, so whenever he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had preceded him in a gathering, they would make room for him so that he could sit next to him, so that he could hear what he said. One day he came and had missed [a rak’ah of the dawn prayer]. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished praying, his companions took their seats, and each man was miserly with his seat, and hardly anyone would make room for anyone else. So if a man came and did not find a seat to sit in, he would stand as he was. When Thabit finished praying, he approached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there was a man between him and him, and he said to him: Make room. The man said: I have found a seat, so sit down. Thabit sat behind him angrily. When the darkness cleared, Thabit nudged the man and said: Who is this? He said: I am so-and-so. Thabit said: The son of so-and-so, and he mentioned his mother who he used to insult in the pre-Islamic era. The man lowered his head and felt ashamed, so God Almighty revealed this verse. Ad-Dahhak said: “It was revealed about the delegation of Banu Tamim that we mentioned. They used to mock the poor companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), such as Ammar, Khabbab, Bilal, Suhaib, Salman, and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, when they saw their poor condition. So God, the Most High, revealed about those who believed among them: ‘O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people’, meaning men of men. ‘People’ is a noun that includes both men and women, and it may be specific to men, ‘perhaps they may be better than them, nor women of women; perhaps they may be better than them.’” It was narrated on the authority of Anas that it was revealed about the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they insulted Umm Salamah for being short. On the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. The women said to her: A Jewish woman, the daughter of two Jewish men. “And do not insult one another,” meaning do not criticize one another, and do not backbite one another. And do not call one another by nicknames, insulting means interacting with the word nabaz, which means a nickname, and it means that a person is called by a name other than what he was called. Ikrimah said: It is when a man says to another man: You are a sinner, you are a hypocrite, you are an infidel. Al-Hasan said: A Jew or a Christian would convert to Islam, and after his conversion, he would be told, O Jew, O Christian. So they were forbidden from doing that. Ata' said: It is to say to your brother: You dog, you donkey, you pig. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Blame-calling means that a man has committed bad deeds and then repented from them, so he is forbidden to be mocked for his past deeds. What a bad name is immorality after faith, meaning what a bad name it is to say, O Jew, or O immoral person, after one has believed and repented. It was said that its meaning is: whoever does what is forbidden of mockery, backbiting, and insults is an immoral person, and what a bad name is immorality after faith, so do not do that, lest you deserve the name of immorality. And whoever does not repent, from that, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
49:12: 12. O you who have believed, avoid much suspicion. It was said: “The verse was revealed about two men who backbite their companions. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went on a military expedition or traveled, he would bring a needy man with two wealthy men to serve them, and go to their homes and prepare for them what they needed of food and drink. So Salman the Persian was brought with two men on one of his journeys. Salman went to the home and his eyes overcame him and he fell asleep, so he did not prepare anything for them. When they returned, they said to him: ‘What did you do?’ He said: ‘No, my eyes overcame me.’ They said to him: ‘Go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and ask him for food for us.’ So Salman came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him for food, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: ‘Go to Usamah ibn Zayd and tell him: If he has any leftover food or condiments, let him give them to you.’ Usamah was the treasurer of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and was in charge of his luggage. So he came to him and said: ‘I have nothing.’ So Salman returned to them and told them. They said: ‘He had Usama had food but was stingy, so they sent Salman to a group of the Companions, but he did not find anything with them. When he returned, they said: If we send you to the well of Samiha, its water will boil away. Then they set out to spy to see if Usama had what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had ordered them to have. When they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, And he said to them: Why do I see the greenness of the meat in your mouths? They said: By God, O Messenger of God, we have not eaten meat today. He said: Rather, you have been eating the meat of Salman and Usama. Then God Almighty revealed: “O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption.” He meant: to think ill of the good people. Indeed, some assumption is sin. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Assumption is of two types: one of them is sinful, which is that you assume and speak about it, and the other is not sinful, which is that you assume and do not speak. And do not spy. Spying is searching for people’s faults. God Almighty forbade searching for people’s hidden affairs and following their faults so that what God has concealed of them is not revealed. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A`raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not spy, do not compete with one another, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be, O servants of God, brothers.” Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Isfarayini told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma’ili told us, Abdullah ibn Najiyah told us, Yahya ibn Aktham told us, al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Waqid, on the authority of Awfa ibn Dahlam, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, may God be pleased with them, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O group of people who have believed with their tongues but faith has not yet entered their hearts, do not backbite the Muslims and do not pursue their faults, for whoever pursues the faults of the Muslims, God will pursue his faults, and whoever God pursues his faults, He will disgrace him even if he is in the interior of his home.” He said: Ibn Omar looked one day at the Kaaba and said: How great you are and how great is your sanctity, and the believer is more sanctified in the sight of God than you. Zayd ibn Wahb said: It was said to Ibn Masoud: Do you think that Al-Walid ibn Uqbah has wine dripping from his beard? He said: We have been forbidden from spying, so if something comes to us, we will take it from him. And do not backbite one another, meaning, do not accuse one another in secret of something that upsets him about what he is doing. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Do you know what backbiting is?’ They said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘It is mentioning your brother in a way that he dislikes.’ It was said: ‘What if what I say is true of my brother?’ He said: ‘If what you say is true of him, then you have backbitten him, and if what you say is not true of him, then you have slandered him.’” Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu al-Tahir al-Harithi told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that they mentioned a man to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: He does not eat until he has eaten, and he does not travel until he has traveled. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have backbitten him. They said: He only told us what is wrong with him. He said: It is enough for you to mention what is wrong with your brother. The Almighty said: Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it. Mujahid said: When it was said to them, Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? they said, No. It was said, You would hate it. That is, just as you hate this, avoid mentioning him in a bad way when he is absent. Al-Zajjaj said: Its interpretation is: If someone who is not present mentions you in a bad way, it is like eating the flesh of your brother, who is dead and does not feel that. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told us, Ibn Shaiba told us, al-Faryabi told us, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us, Abu al-Mughira Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj told us, Sufyan ibn Amr told us, Rashid ibn Sa’d and Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr told us, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When I was taken up to heaven, I passed by people who had nails of copper with which they scratched their faces and flesh. I said: ‘Who are these, O Gabriel?’ He said: ‘These are the ones who eat the flesh of people and slander them.’” Maimun ibn Siyah said: “While I was sleeping, I came across the corpse of a Negro and someone was saying: ‘Eat!’ I said: ‘O servant of God, why did I eat?’ He said: ‘Why did you backbite so-and-so’s servant?’ I said: ‘By God, I did not mention anything good or bad about him.’ He said: ‘But you listened to him and were pleased with him.’ Maimun never backbited anyone, nor would he allow anyone to backbite anyone in his presence.” And fear God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
49:13: 13. O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female [verse]. Ibn Abbas said: "It was revealed about Thabit ibn Qays, and his saying to the man who did not make room for him: 'The son of so-and-so,' taunting him about his mother. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Who is mentioning so-and-so?' Thabit said: 'I did, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'Look at the faces of the people.' He looked and said: 'What did you see, Thabit?' He said: 'I saw white, red, and black.' He said: 'You are not superior to them except in religion and piety.' So this verse was revealed about Thabit, and about the one who did not make room: 'O you who have believed, when you are told to make room in assemblies, then make room.'" (al-Mujadilah 58:11) Muqatil said: When the day of the conquest of Mecca came, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered Bilal to ascend the roof of the Kaaba and call the adhan. Atab bin Asid bin Abi Al-Ays said: Praise be to God who took my father before he saw this day. Al-Harith bin Hisham said: Did Muhammad not find anyone other than this black crow to call the adhan? Suhayl bin Amr said: If God desires something, He reproaches it. Abu Sufyan said: I will not say anything for fear that the Lord of the heavens will inform me about it. Gabriel came and informed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of what they had said. He called them and asked them about what they had said and they admitted it. Then God revealed this verse and warned them against boasting about their lineage, increasing their wealth and spending money on the poor. He said: O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female meaning Adam and Eve, meaning that you are equal in lineage. And We made you peoples, the plural of shab with a fatha on the sheen, and they are the heads of the tribes like Rabi’ah, Mudar, Aws, and Khazraj. They were called peoples because of their dispersion and gathering, like the branches of a tree. A people is one of the opposites. It is said: shab a group, and shab a faction. And tribes, which are below the peoples, their singular is qabeelah a tribe, like Bakr from Rabi’ah and Tamim from Mudar. Below the tribes are the ama’ir clan, their singular is amarah clan, with a fatha on the ayn, and they are like Shaiban from Bakr and Darim from Tamim. Below the ama’ir are the batun clans, their singular is batn clans, like Bani Ghalib and Lu’ay from Quraysh. Below the batun are the afkhud thighs, their singular is fakhd clans, like Bani Hashim and Umayya from Bani Lu’ay. Then there are the fasail factions, and the ashira clan, their singular is fasila clan, and ashira clan, after the ashira clan so that it can be described by it. It was said: The peoples are from the Persians, the tribes are from the Arabs, and the tribes are from the children of Israel. Abu Ruq said: The peoples are those who do not claim to belong to anyone, but rather belong to cities and villages, and the tribes are the Arabs who claim to belong to their fathers. So that you may know one another, so that you may know one another in terms of close or distant kinship, not to boast. Then He informed that the one with the highest status before God is the most righteous of them, saying: “The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.” Qatada said about this verse: The most honorable of honor is righteousness, and the most despicable of baseness is immorality. Abu Bakr bin Abi Al-Haitham Al-Turabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hamuyah told us, Ibrahim bin Khazim Al-Shashi told us, Abd bin Hamid told us, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Salam bin Abi Mut’i told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Noble lineage is wealth, and generosity is piety. Ibn Abbas said: The nobility of this world is wealth, and the nobility of the hereafter is piety. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Al-Haitham told us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamuyah told us, Ibrahim ibn Khuzaym told us, Abd ibn Hamid told us, Ad-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated on the day of the conquest on his mount, touching the corners with his staff. When he came out, he did not find a place to rest, so he dismounted at the hands of the men. Then he stood up and addressed them, praising God and thanking Him, and saying: ‘Praise be to God, who has removed from you the arrogance of the Age of Ignorance and its pride in [its fathers]. People are of two types: the pious and God-fearing, honored by God, and the wicked and wretched, insignificant to God.’ Then he recited: ‘O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female. ’ Then he said: ‘I say this and I ask God for forgiveness for myself and for you.’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Salam told us, Abda told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: ‘Who is the most honorable of people?’ He said: ‘The most honorable of them in the sight of God is the most righteous of them.’ They said: ‘We are not asking you about this.’ He said: ‘The most honorable of people is Joseph, the Prophet of God, the son of the Prophet of God, the son of the Friend of God.’ They said: ‘We are not asking you about this.’ He said: ‘And do you ask me about the origins of the Arabs?’ They said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘The best of you in the pre-Islamic period will be the best of you in Islam if they attain understanding.’” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Amr Al-Naqid told us, Kathir bin Hisham told us, Jafar bin Burqan told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Asam, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God does not look at your appearance and your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
49:14: 14. The Almighty said: The Bedouins said, ‘We have believed.’ The verse was revealed about a group of Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during a year of drought. They outwardly declared Islam, but they were not secret believers. They ruined the roads of Madinah with their waste and raised prices. They would come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: The Arabs have come to you on the backs of their mounts, and we have come to you with our heavy loads, our families, and our children. We did not fight you as Banu so-and-so and Banu so-and-so fought you. They were doing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a favor and wanted charity, and they said: Give us. So God revealed this verse about them. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about the Bedouins whom God mentioned in Surat Al-Fath, and they are the Bedouins of Juhayna, Muzayna, Aslam, Ashja’ and Ghifar. They used to say: We believe so that they would feel safe about themselves and their wealth. But when they were called to Al-Hudaybiyyah, they stayed behind, so God Almighty revealed: “The Bedouins said: We believe” meaning we have spoken the truth. Say, ‘You have not believed, but say, “We have submitted, for fear of being killed and taken captive, and faith has not yet entered your hearts, so He informed us that the reality of faith is belief in the heart, and that acknowledgment with the tongue and manifestation of His laws with the body cannot be faith without belief in the heart and sincerity. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Ghurair Al-Zuhri told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Salih, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Amir bin Saad told me, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave something to a group of people while I was sitting among them. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left a man among them and did not give him anything, and he was the one I liked best. So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spoke to him in secret, and I said: What do you think of so-and-so? By God, I see him as a believer. He said: Or a Muslim. He was silent for a while, then what I knew of him got the better of me, and I said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of so-and-so? I see him as a believer. He said: Or a Muslim. He said: I give to a man, but I prefer someone else to him, for fear that he might fall on his face into the Fire. Islam is entering into peace, submission and obedience. It is said: A man has submitted if he has entered into peace, just as it is said: A man has become an astray if he has entered into winter, or asafa if he has entered into summer, or four if he has entered into spring. There is Islam that is obedience in truth with the tongue, body and soul, like the saying of the Almighty to Abraham, peace be upon him: He submitted, saying, ‘I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds’ (Al-Baqarah 2:131). There is also submission with the tongue without the heart, like His saying: But say, ‘We have submitted,’ for faith has not yet entered your hearts. “And if you obey God and His Messenger,” outwardly and inwardly, secretly and publicly. Ibn Abbas said: Purify faith, It will not diminish you, Abu Omar read (ya yaltum) with an alif because of the Almighty’s saying: And We did not diminish them (al-Tur 52:21), and the others without an alif, and they are two dialects, their meaning is: It will not diminish you in any way, it is said: alta ya’alta alatan or wa laitatan if it diminishes, of your deeds in any way, meaning it will not diminish the reward of your deeds in any way, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Then he explained the reality of faith, saying:
49:15: 15. The believers are only those who have believed in God and His Messenger and then have not doubted, did not doubt their religion, “and have striven with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God. Those are the truthful” in their faith. When these two verses were revealed, the Bedouins came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, swearing by God that they were true believers. God knew otherwise from them, so God Almighty revealed:
49:16: 16. “Say: Do you inform God of your religion?” And information here means information. Therefore, He said: of your religion and inserted the ba into it, saying: Do you inform God of the religion that you are following? And God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and God is Knowing of all things. He does not need to inform you.
49:17: 17. “They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. Say, ‘Do not do me a favor by your Islam,’” meaning by your Islam, rather, God does you a favor by guiding you to faith, and in Abdullah’s copy of the Qur’an ((when He guided you to faith)) if you should be truthful, meaning you are believers.
49:18: 18. Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and God is Seeing of what you do. Ibn Kathir read they do with a ya, while others read it with a ta.
50:1: 1. Meccan Qaf [Ibn Abbas said: It is an oath, and it was said:] It is the name of the surah, and it was said: It is one of the names of the Qur’an. Al-Qurazi said: It is a key whose name is Al-Qadir, “Al-Qadir,” Al-Qahir, “Al-Qarib,” and Al-Qabeed. Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: It is a mountain surrounding the earth of green emerald, from which the green sky is formed, and the sky is domed over it, and its shoulders are over it. It is said that it is behind the veil from which the sun disappears at a distance of a year’s journey. It was said: Its meaning is that the matter was decided, or what is to happen was decided, as they said in Ha Mim. "And the Glorious Qur’an", the noble and generous to God, full of goodness.
50:2: 2. They differed regarding the answer to the oath. The people of Kufa said: Its answer is: Rather, they were amazed. It was also said: Its answer is omitted, and its metaphor is: By the Glorious Qur'an, you will surely be resurrected. It was also said: Its answer is His statement: (Whatever word he utters). It was said: (We have known), and the answers to the oath are seven: (Indeed) the strong (Indeed) like His saying: (By the dawn) - (Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful) (al-Fajr 89:14), and (Ma) the negation like His saying: (By the forenoon * And by the night when it covers * Your Lord has not forsaken you) (al-Duha 93:1-3), and the open (Lam) like His saying: (By your Lord, We will surely question them all) (al-Hijr 15:92), and the light (Indeed) like His saying: (Indeed, we were in clear error) (Ash-Shu`ara: 38), and (La) like His saying: (And they swore by God their most solemn oaths that God would not raise up anyone who dies) (al-Nahl 16:38), and (Qad) like His saying: (By the sun and its brightness) - (He has succeeded who purifies it) (Ash-Shams: 1-9), and (By) like His saying: (By the Glorious Qur’an) - (Rather, they were amazed). If a warner comes to them, frightening, from among them, they know his lineage, truthfulness, and trustworthiness, then the disbelievers will say, ‘This is an amazing thing,’ strange.
50:3: 3. When we die and become dust, will we be resurrected? He omitted mentioning resurrection because the speech indicates it. That is a return, meaning a return to life. Far from it, and does not happen. That is, it is far-fetched that we will be resurrected after death.
50:4: 4. God the Almighty said: We know what the earth takes of them, meaning it consumes their flesh, blood, and bones; nothing escapes His knowledge. Al-Suddi said: It refers to death. He says: We know who among them will die and who will live. And with Us is a Preserving Record, [preserved from the devils and from being erased or altered. It is the Preserved Tablet. It was also said: Preserving] meaning: It preserves their numbers and names.
50:5: 5. Rather, they denied the truth, the Qur’an, when it came to them, so they are in a confused state. Mixed. Saeed bin Jubayr and Mujahid said: Confused. Qatada said about this verse: Whoever abandons the truth, his affairs will be confused and his religion will be obscure. Al-Hasan said: A people who abandon the truth will have their affairs confused. Al-Zajjaj mentioned the meaning of their confusion, saying: “It is that they say about the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ‘Sometimes he is a poet,’ and about him, ‘He is a teacher.’ And they say about the Qur’an, ‘It is magic,’ ‘It is a filth,’ and ‘It is a fabrication.’ So their affairs will be confused and ambiguous for them.” Then he showed them the reason for His power, saying:
50:6: 6. Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We constructed it without pillars, and adorned it with planets, and there are no rifts in it cracks, fissures, and fissures, the singular of which is farj.
50:7: 7. And the earth We have spread out, that is, extended it over the surface of the water, and placed therein firm mountains, that is, fixed mountains, and caused to grow therein of every beautiful kind, that is, beautiful and generous, which delights, that is, pleases.
50:8: 8. As insight, [i.e., We made that insight], and a reminder, i.e., insight and a reminder, for every servant who turns back, i.e., so that he may see and be reminded of it.
50:9: 9. And We sent down from the sky blessed water, abundant in goodness and in which everything lives, and it is rain, and We caused to grow thereby gardens and grain for harvest, meaning wheat, barley, and all other grains that are harvested. So He added grain to harvest, although they are one and the same because of the difference in the two words, just as one says: the mosque of the congregation and Rabi’ al-Awwal. And it was said: (and the grain for harvest) meaning: and the Prophet’s grain [the harvest].
50:10: 10. And tall palm trees, Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Qatada said: Tall, the palm tree became tall. Saeed bin Jubair said: Levels. It has spadix fruit and fruit, it is called that because it appears, and the spadix is the first thing to appear before it splits, nadeed, overlapping, piled up, arranged one on top of the other in its sleeves, but when it comes out of its sleeves, it is not nadeed.
50:11: 11. A provision for the servants, meaning We made it a provision for the servants, and We revived with it, meaning with the rain, a dead land, causing grass to grow in it, thus is the emergence, from the graves.
50:12: 12. The Almighty said: Before them, the people of Noah, the companions of Ar-Rass, and Thamud denied.
50:13: 13. And Aad, Pharaoh, and the brothers of Lot.
50:14: 14. And the companions of the thicket and the people of Tubba’ He is Tubba’ al-Himyari, and his name is As’ad Abu Karb. Qatada said: God Almighty condemned the people of Tubba’ but did not condemn him. We mentioned his story in Surat Ad-Dukhan. Every one of the messengers denied it, meaning: every one of those mentioned denied the messengers, so My threat is justified, and My punishment is due to them. Then He revealed the answer to their saying, That is an impossible return:
50:15: 15. Did We tire with the first creation? meaning: Were We unable to create them when We first created them, so that they would be unable to repeat it? This is a statement to them because they acknowledged the first creation and denied the resurrection. It is said to anyone who is unable to do something: He is tired of it. Rather, they are in confusion, meaning: in doubt, about a new creation, which is the resurrection.
50:16: 16. And We have certainly created man and We know what his soul whispers to him, what his heart whispers to him and his secrets and consciences are not hidden from Us, and We are nearer to him, more knowledgeable about him, than his jugular vein, because his parts and segments block one another, and nothing blocks the knowledge of God. The jugular vein is the neck vein, which is a vein between the throat and the two ribs, and it spreads throughout the body. The rope is the vein, so it was added to itself because of the difference in the two words.
50:17: 17. When the two receivers receive, that is, the two angels receive and take the actions and speech of the person, memorizing and writing them down, on the right and on the left, that is, one of them on his right and the other on his left. The one on the right writes down the good deeds, and the one on the left writes down the bad deeds. Seated, that is, sitting. He did not say two sitting ones, because he meant on the right one sitting, so he was satisfied with one of them instead of the other. This is the saying of the people of Basra. The people of Kufa said: He meant sitting, like the messenger, so he made it for two and the plural, as God the Most High said about the two: Then say, ‘Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds.’ (Ash-Shu’ara’: 16). It was said: He meant by seated one the one who is constant and does not move, not the one who is seated who is the opposite of the one who stands. Mujahid said: The seated one is the balance.
50:18: 18. No word he utters, no speech he speaks, except that there is by him an observer, a guardian, ready, present wherever he is. Al-Hasan said: The angels avoid a person in two states: when he defecates and when he has sexual intercourse. Mujahid said: They write down for him even his groans during his illness. Ikrimah said: They write down only what he will be rewarded for or punished for. Ad-Dahhak said: Their sitting place is under the molar on the palate, and the same was reported by Al-Hasan, and Al-Hasan liked to clean his molar. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Dinawari told us, Ahmad bin Ja’far bin Hamdan told us, Al-Fadl bin Al-Abbas bin Mihran told us, Talut told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ja’far bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The scribe of good deeds is on a man’s right hand, and the scribe of bad deeds is on a man’s left. The scribe of good deeds is the commander over the scribe of bad deeds. So if he does a good deed, the one on the right writes it down as ten, and if he does a bad deed, the one on the right says to the one on the left: Leave him for seven hours, so that he may glorify God or seek forgiveness.”
50:19: 19. And the stupor of death has come, it overwhelmed him and its severity that overwhelms a person and overcomes his mind, in truth, that is, in the reality of death. It was said: in truth of the matter of the Hereafter so that a person can see it clearly and with his own eyes. It was said: in what a person's matter will lead to of happiness and misery. And it is said to someone who is overcome by the stupor of death: That is what you were avoiding, you were inclined. Al-Hasan said: you were running away from. Ibn Abbas said: you were hating. The root of deviance is inclination. It is said: I deviated from something, deviating and avoiding it: if you turned away from it.
50:20: 20. And the Trumpet will be blown, meaning the blast of resurrection, that is the Day of Threat, meaning: that is the Day of Threat that God promised to the disbelievers that He would punish them on it. Muqatil said: By threat, he means torment, meaning: the day on which the threat will occur.
50:21: 21. And there will come, that Day, every soul will have with it a driver, who will drive it to the place of assembly, and a witness, who will testify over it as to what it did. Ad-Dahhak said: The driver is from the angels, and the witness from themselves is their hands and feet, and this is the narration of Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. The others said: They are an entire group of angels, and God will say:
50:22: 22. You were certainly heedless of this, today in this world, so We have removed from you your covering, which was in this world over your heart, hearing, and sight, so your sight today is sharp, penetrating, perceiving what you used to deny in this world. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: It means your sight at the tongue of your scale when your good and bad deeds are weighed.
50:23: 23. And his companion said, meaning the angel assigned to him, This is what I have ready, prepared and ready. It was said that what means of, Mujahid said: He says, “This that you have assigned to me from the son of Adam is present with me. I have brought it and brought the record of his deeds,” so God Almighty says to his companion:
50:24: 24. "Throw them into Hell" is an address to one person in the dual form as is the custom of the Arabs. You say: Woe to you, woe to you, saddle her and drive her away, take her and set her free. Al-Farra' said: The origin of this is that the minimum number of helpers of a man in his camels, sheep and travel is two, so the speech of one person is directed to his two companions, and from this is their saying in poetry to one person: My friend. Al-Zajjaj said: This is an order to the driver and the martyr, and it was said: to the recipients. Every stubborn disbeliever, a rebel who turns away from the truth. Ikrimah and Mujahid said: One who deviates from the truth and is obstinate towards God.
50:25: 25. Preventing goodness, meaning the obligatory zakat and every right due from his wealth, aggressor, unjust and does not acknowledge the Oneness of God, doubtful, doubting the Oneness of God, meaning: falling into doubt.
50:26: 26. He who has set up with God another god - then cast him into the severe punishment, which is the Fire.
50:27: 27. His companion said, meaning the devil who was appointed for this disbeliever, Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, meaning I did not mislead him nor did I lead him astray, but he was in extreme error, from the truth. So his devil disavowed him. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, and Muqatil said: His companion said, meaning the angel, Our Lord, I did not make him transgress, meaning I did not add anything to him and I only wrote down what he said and did, but he was in extreme, long error from which he did not return to the truth.
50:28: 28. "He said, then God says, Do not dispute before me, for I have already presented to you the threat," in the Qur’an, and I have warned you and cautioned you on the tongue of the Messenger, and I have decreed upon you what I am about to decree.
50:29: 29. My word cannot be changed, meaning My word cannot be changed. This is His statement: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together. (al-Sajdah 32:13). Some people said: The meaning of His statement, My word cannot be changed is: He does not lie with Me, and My word cannot be changed from its intended meaning, because I know the unseen. This is the statement of Al-Kalbi, and the preferred opinion of Al-Farra’, because he said: My word cannot be changed, and he did not say My word cannot be changed. I am not unjust to the servants, so I punish them without a crime.
50:30: 30. The Day We will say to Hell, Nafi’ and Abu Bakr read He says with a ya, meaning: God says, based on His statement: He said, ‘Do not dispute.’ The others read it with a nun, “Has it been filled?” This is because of His previous promise to it that He would fill it with jinn and people. This question is from God Almighty to confirm His report and fulfill His promise. And it will say, Hell, Is there any more? It was said that its meaning is that it has been filled and there is no place left that has not been filled, so it is a question of denial. This is the statement of Ata’, Mujahid, and Muqatil bin Sulayman. It was said: This is an interrogative with the meaning of asking for support, and it is the saying of Ibn Abbas in the narration of Abu Saleh. Based on this, the question is with his saying: (Has it been filled), before all of its people enter it. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: That God Almighty said beforehand: I will fill Hell with jinn and people all together (al-Sajdah 32:13). So when the enemies of God are driven to it, no group will be found in it except that it will go into it and nothing will fill it. So it will say: Did you not swear to fill me? Then he places his foot on it, then says: Are you filled? It will say: Enough, enough, it is filled, so there is no more. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Abbas Al-Hamidi [Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hafiz] told us: Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Al-Hasan bin Ayoub Al-Tusi told us: Abu Hatim Muhammad bin Idris Al-Razi told us: Adam bin Abi Iyas Al-Asqalani told us: Shaiban bin Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Hell will continue to say, ‘Is there more?’ until the Lord of Glory places His foot in it. Then it will say, ‘Enough, enough, by Your glory.’ And some parts will be drawn closer to others. And there will continue to be excess in Paradise until God creates a creation and inhabits it with the excess of Paradise.”
50:31: 31. And Paradise will be brought near, brought near and brought near, for the righteous, polytheism, not far, they will look at it before they enter it.
50:32: 32. This is what you are promised. Ibn Kathir read it with a ya and others with a ta. It is said to them: This that you see is what you are promised on the tongues of the prophets, peace be upon them. For every one who frequently turns back to God, returning to obedience from disobedience. Saeed ibn al-Musayyab said: He is the one who sins then repents, then sins again, then repents. Al-Sha'bi and Mujahid said: He is the one who remembers his sins in solitude and seeks forgiveness for them. Ad-Dahhak said: He is the one who accepts repentance. Ibn Abbas and Ata' said: He is the one who glorifies God, from His statement: O mountains, echo with him Saba' 34:10. Qatada said: He is the one who prays. Hafeez Guardian, Ibn Abbas said: He is the one who preserves the command of God. It was also narrated from him: He is the one who preserves his sins until he turns from them and seeks forgiveness for them. Qatada said: He is the one who guards what God has entrusted to him of His rights. Ad-Dahhak said: He is the one who protects himself and takes care of it. Al-Sha'bi said: He is the one who watches over. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: The one who maintains obedience and commands.
50:33: 33. Whoever fears the Most Merciful in secret, the subject of whom is a genitive noun describing the one who frequently turns back to God. The meaning of the verse is: Whoever fears the Most Merciful and obeys Him in secret without seeing Him. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: It means in seclusion where no one can see him. Al-Hasan said: If he lowers the curtain and closes the door. And comes with a heart turned in repentance, sincere and turning to obeying God.

50:39: َالمَْوَُا ق،َْاَماَُْاَُْمن قو،فاَاَْلى ما ََوََفاص39. " ُلوعَْق" ،حمْاة لْصلى ا َلَه وَل:َي،"رَكْوََح َحم،ََََُْا. َصلة اَعص:َعَي،"اََمعَات اََْوب" ،صلة اَصَح:َعَي،"اَْمس.َواَعص) ََُُاََْوب اَْق: (ْوروي َن اَن ََاس قا
50:40: 40. And during part of the night, glorify Him, meaning the Maghrib and Isha prayers. Mujahid said: And during part of the night, meaning the night prayer, i.e., the time he prayed. And the ends of prostration, the people of Hijaz and Hamzah read: And the ends of prostration, with a kasra on the hamzah, the source of adbara idbaran, and the others read it with a fatha on it, plural of dabar. Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, and al-Awza'i said: "The ends of prostration" are the two rak'ahs after the Maghrib prayer, and the ends of the prostrations are the two rak'ahs before the Fajr prayer. This is the narration of al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was also narrated on his authority with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is the opinion of most of the commentators. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abu Ayyub Al-Dimashqi told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not more committed to any of the voluntary prayers than to the two rak’ahs before the dawn prayer. Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Salih bin Abdullah told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Zarara bin Abi Awfa, on the authority of Saeed bin Hisham, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Two rak’ahs of Fajr prayer are better than the world and everything in it. Abu Uthman al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi told us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Badal ibn al-Muhber told us, Abd al-Malik ibn Ma’dan told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Mahdalah, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, that he said: I cannot count how many times I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite in the two rak’ahs after the Maghrib prayer and in the two rak’ahs before [the Fajr prayer]: Say, O you disbelievers and Say, He is God, the One. Mujahid said: And the end of prostration is the glorification with the tongue at the end of the obligatory prayers. Abu al-Husayn Tahir ibn al-Husayn al-Ruqi al-Tusi told us about it, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ya`qub told us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, Muhammad ibn Ayyub told us, Musaddad told us, Khalid told us - he is ibn `Abdullah - Suhayl told us, on the authority of Abu `Ubayd, on the authority of `Ata` ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever glorifies God thirty-three times after every prayer, and declares God’s greatness thirty-three times, and praises God thirty-three times, that is ninety-nine, and then says to complete the hundred: There is no god but God alone, with no partner, His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things omnipotent,’ his sins will be forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ishaq told us, Yazid told us, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Sami, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “They said: O Messenger of God, the wealthy have taken the highest ranks and eternal bliss. He said: How is that? They said: Pray as we prayed, strive as we strive, and spend from the excess of their wealth, for we have no wealth. He said: Shall I not tell you of something by which you will catch up with those who came before you and surpass those who come after you, and no one will come with what you have come with except someone who comes with something like it: You glorify God ten times after every prayer, praise God ten times, and magnify God ten times.”
50:41: 41. The Almighty said: And listen on the Day when the Caller will call from a place nearby, meaning: Listen, O Muhammad, to the shout of Resurrection and Resurrection on the Day when the Caller will call. Muqatil said: He means Israfil calling for the gathering: O you decayed bones, severed limbs, torn flesh, and scattered hair, God commands you to gather for the passing of judgment “from a place nearby, from the rock of Jerusalem, which is in the middle of the earth. Al-Kalbi said: It is the closest land to the sky by eighteen miles.
50:42: 42. The Day they hear the Shout in truth, which is the final Shout, that is the Day of Resurrection, from the graves.
50:43: 43. "Indeed, it is We who bring to life and cause to die, and to Us is the final destination."
50:44: 44. The Day the earth will split open and they will come out quickly, plural of quickly, meaning: they will come out quickly. That will be a gathering for Us, plural of for Us, “easy.”
50:45: 45. We know best what they say, meaning: the infidels of Mecca in their denial of you, and you are not a compeller over them, meaning someone who can force them to accept Islam. You were only sent as a reminder, so remind with the Qur’an whoever fears My threat, meaning: what I have threatened those who disobey Me with of punishment. Ibn Abbas said: They said: O Messenger of God, if you had frightened us, then this verse was revealed: And remind by the Qur’an whoever fears My threat.
51:1: 1. Meccan, And the winds that scatter the dust, meaning: the winds that scatter the dust, it is said: the wind scatter the dust and scattered it.
51:2: 2. And those who carry burdens, meaning: the camels carry a heavy load of water.
51:3: 3. And those that sail easily are the ships that sail easily in the water.
51:4: 4. And those who divide matters, are the angels who divide matters among creation according to what they were commanded to do. He swore by these things because they indicate His creation and power.
51:5: 5. Then he mentioned the object of the oath, saying: You are only promised, of reward and punishment, that which is true.
51:6: 6. And indeed, the religion [the reckoning and recompense] will certainly happen, will occur. Then he began another section and said:
51:7: 7. And the sky of interwoven fabrics, Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Ikrimah said: of fine, even creation. It is said to a weaver when he weaves a garment and does it well: How beautifully he interwoven it! Saeed ibn Jubayr said: of adornment. Al-Hasan said: interwoven with stars. Mujahid said: it is the well-built. Muqatil, Al-Kalbi, and Al-Dahhak said: of paths like the interweaving of water when the wind strikes it, and the interweaving of sand and curly hair, but it is not seen because of its distance from people. It is the plural of habbak and habika. The answer to the oath is His statement:
51:8: 8. You, meaning, O people of Mecca, are in a different statement, regarding the Qur’an and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. You say regarding the Qur’an: magic, divination, and the legends of the ancients, and regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: a magician, a poet, and a madman. It was also said: in a different statement, meaning, some believe and some deny.
51:9: 9. "Whoever turns away from him will be turned away from believing in him until he denies him, meaning: whoever God has forbidden from believing in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and in the Qur’an. It was said that from means: for the sake of, meaning whoever turns away from believing because of this different statement or because of it will be turned away from believing. This is because they would meet a man if he wanted to believe and say: He is a magician, a soothsayer, or a madman, so they would turn him away from believing, and this is the meaning of what Mujahid said.
51:10: 10. "The liars were killed," meaning the liars were cursed. It is said: "He lied about someone falsely." They are the dividers who divided up the punishment in Mecca and divided up the sayings about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in order to turn people away from the religion of Islam. Mujahid said: They are the soothsayers.
51:11: 11. Those who are in a state of heedlessness, heedlessness, blindness, and ignorance, negligent, heedless and neglectful of the matter of the Hereafter. Negligence is heedlessness of something, which is the heart’s departure from it.
51:12: 12. “They ask, ‘When is the Day of Judgment?’ They say, ‘O Muhammad, when is the Day of Judgment?’ meaning, the Day of Resurrection, as a denial and mockery.
51:13: 13. God the Almighty said: On the Day they will be tested, meaning this will be the punishment on the Day they will be tested, on the Fire, meaning they will be tortured and burned in it as gold is tested by fire. It was said that on means with, meaning by fire. The keepers of the Fire will say to them:
51:14: 14. Taste your trial, your punishment, this is what you were hastening for, in this world, denying it.
51:15: 15. Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs.
51:16: 16. Taking what their Lord has given them, that is, given them, of goodness and honor, “for they were before that,” before entering Paradise, doers of good, in this world.
51:17: 17. They used to sleep but little of the night, and sleeping is sleeping at night rather than during the day, (and what) is a connection, and the meaning is: they used to sleep but little of the night, meaning they used to pray most of the night. It was said: Its meaning is that the night in which they slept was all short, and this is the meaning of the statement of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, meaning: Hardly a night would pass by them without them praying something, either at the beginning or in the middle. Anas bin Malik said: They would pray between sunset and night prayer. Muhammad bin Ali said: They would not sleep until they prayed the night prayer. Mutraf bin Abdullah bin Ash-Shakheer said: Hardly a night would pass by them in which they slept all of it. Mujahid said: They would not sleep the entire night. Some of them stopped at his saying: (a few) meaning: they were few of the people, then he began: (of the night they do not sleep), and he made it a denial meaning: they do not sleep at night at all, rather they get up for prayer and worship, and this is the saying of Al-Dahhak and Muqatil. 18. And in the hours of the pre-dawn hours they seek forgiveness. Al-Hasan said: They only sleep a little of the night, and sometimes they become active and stay up until the early hours of the morning, then they seek forgiveness in the early hours of the morning. Al-Kalbi, Mujahid, and Muqatil said: They pray in the hours of the pre-dawn hours, and that is because their prayer in the hours of the pre-dawn hours is to seek forgiveness.God Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan bin Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Sarraj told us, Qutaybah told us, Yaqub bin Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sahl bin Abi Saleh, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God descends to the lowest heaven every night when a third of the night remains and says: I am the King, I am the King. Who calls upon Me that I may answer him? Who asks Me that I may give him? Who seeks My forgiveness that I may forgive him?” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, Sulayman bin Abi Muslim told us, on the authority of Tawus, he heard Ibn Abbas say: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would rise at night to pray, he would say: “O God, to You is all praise. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. To You is all praise. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. To You is all praise. You are the Truth, Your promise is the Truth, and meeting You is the Truth, and Your word is the Truth. Paradise is the Truth, and Hellfire is the Truth. The Prophets are the Truth, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the Truth, and the Hour is the Truth. O God, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, in You I have relied, to You I have turned, with You I have disputed, and to You I have turned for judgment. So forgive me for what I have done in the past and what I will do in the future, what I have kept secret and what I have declared. You are the First and the Last. There is no god but You, and there is no god but You.” Sufyan said: Abdul Karim Abu Umayya added: And there is no power or strength except with God. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Sadaqah told us, Al-Walid told us on the authority of Al-Awza’i, Umair bin Hani’ told me, Junada bin Abi Umayya told me, Ubadah told me on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever wakes up at night and says: ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner for Him. His is the kingdom and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is greatest. There is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty.’ Then he says: ‘O God, forgive me,’ or makes supplication, his prayer will be answered. If he performs ablution and prays, his prayer will be accepted.”
51:19: 19. The Almighty said: And in their wealth is a right for the beggar and the deprived. The beggar is the one who asks people, and the deprived is the one who does not have a share in the spoils, and nothing from the spoils is given to him. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: [The deprived is the one] who does not have a share in Islam, and its meaning in the language is: the one who was prevented from goodness and giving.God Qatada and Al-Zuhri said: The deprived one is the one who is too chaste to ask. Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is the one whose fruit, crops, or livestock are affected. This is the opinion of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: The deprived one is the one who is noisy due to the plague. Then he recited: “Indeed, we are losers. Rather, we are deprived.” (Al-Waqi'ah: 66-67)
51:20: 20. And on the earth are signs, he said, for those of certainty, if they traveled in it, of mountains, seas, trees, fruits, and various types of plants.God
51:21: 21. And in yourselves, verses, when it was a drop of semen, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then a bone, until the soul was breathed into it.God Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means the difference in languages, images, colors, and natures. Ibn Al-Zubayr said: He means the path of defecation and urine. He eats and drinks from one entrance and exits from two paths. Do you not see? [Muqatil said]: Do you not see how He created you and know His power to resurrect?
51:22: 22. And in the sky is your provision, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Muqatil said: meaning rain, which is the cause of provisions, and what you are promised, Ata’ said: of reward and punishment. Mujahid said: of good and evil. Ad-Dahhak said: and what you are promised of Paradise and Hellfire, then He swore by Himself and said:
51:23: 23. By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth, meaning: what you mentioned about the matter of provision is the truth. Like, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Abu Bakr, and Asim read: (like) with the lam in the nominative case instead of (the truth), and the others read it with the accusative case, meaning like the example of, you do not speak, so you say: There is no god but God. And it was said: The realization of what He informed about is like the realization of human speech, as you say: it is the truth just as you are here, and it is the truth just as you speak, and the meaning is: it is in its truthfulness and existence like that which you know by necessity. Some of the wise men said: meaning: just as every person speaks with his own tongue and is unable to speak with the tongue of someone else, so too every person eats his own provision that was allotted to him, and is unable to eat the provision of someone else.
51:24: 24. The Almighty said: Has there come to you the story of the guests of Abraham? We mentioned their number in Surat Hud, the honored ones, [it was said: He called them honored] because they were angels who were honored by God, and God Almighty said in describing them: Rather, they are honored servants (Al-Anbiya’: 26), and it was said: because they were the guests of Abraham and Abraham was the most honored of creation, and the guests of the honored ones are honored. It was said: Because Abraham, peace be upon him, honored them by hastening their visit, and by taking care of them with a cheerful face. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: He served them himself. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He called them honored because they came uninvited. We also narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his guest.
51:25: 25. “When they entered upon him and said, ‘Peace,’ he said, ‘Peace be upon you, strangers. We do not know you.’ Ibn Abbas said: He said to himself, ‘These are people we do not know.’ It was also said that he only disapproved of their behavior because they entered upon him without asking permission. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: He disapproved of their greeting at that time and in that land.
51:26: 26. "He was free, so he turned and leaned, to his family and brought a fat, roasted calf.
51:27: 27. So he brought it near to them, so that they might eat, but they did not eat. He said, ‘Will you not eat?’
51:28: 28. "So he felt fear of them. They said, "Do not fear, and give him good tidings of a learned boy.
51:29: 29. So his wife came with a shriek, meaning: shouting. It was said: This was not an approach from one place to another, but rather it is like the saying of someone: He came to insult me, meaning he began to insult me, meaning she began to wail, as He said: She said, ‘Woe is me!’ (Hud 11:72). So she slapped her face, Ibn Abbas said: She slapped her face. Others said: She gathered her fingers and struck her forehead in amazement, as is the custom of women when they deny something. The root of sakk is to hit something with something wide. And a barren old woman said, meaning: Will a barren old woman give birth? Sarah had not given birth before that.
51:30: 30. They said, ‘Thus says your Lord,’ meaning, just as we told you, your Lord said, ‘You will give birth to a boy.’ Indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing.
51:31: 31. He said [meaning Abraham], What is the matter with you, O messengers?
51:32: 32. They said, ‘We have been sent to a people of criminals,’ meaning: the people of Lot.
51:33: 33. Let us send upon them stones of clay.
51:34: 34. Marked, marked, with your Lord for the transgressors, Ibn Abbas said: for the polytheists, and polytheism is the most transgressive and greatest of sins.
