51:35: 35. So We brought out whoever was in it, meaning: in the villages of Lot’s people, of the believers, and that is His saying: So set out with your family during a part of the night Hud 81.
51:36: 36. And We found therein nothing but a house, meaning nothing but a household, of Muslims, meaning Lot and his two daughters. God Almighty described them all as having faith and Islam, because there is no believer who is not a Muslim.
51:37: 37. And We left therein, meaning in the city of Lot’s people, a sign, a lesson, for those who fear the painful punishment, meaning: a sign for those who fear that God Almighty has destroyed them, so they fear a punishment similar to theirs.
51:38: 38. And in Moses, meaning: And We left in the sending of Moses a sign and a lesson. It was said: It is connected to His statement: And on the earth are signs for those of certain faith, [in Moses], when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority, with a clear argument.
51:39: 39. So he turned away, meaning he turned away and turned away from the faith, with his pillar, meaning with his army and soldiers who strengthened him, like the pillar that strengthens a building. Similar to: Or he took refuge in a strong pillar (Hud 11:80), And a magician or a madman said, Abu Ubaidah said: Or means and.
51:40: 40. So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea, that is, We drowned them in it, and he was blameworthy, that is, he did what he was blameworthy for, claiming divinity and denying the Messenger.
51:41: 41. And in ‘Aad, meaning: in the destruction of ‘Aad also, there is a verse, when We sent upon them the barren wind, which is one in which there is no good or blessing and which does not pollinate trees or bring rain.
51:42: 42. It leaves nothing it has come upon, of themselves, their livestock, and their wealth, except that it makes it like chaff, like something that has perished and decayed, which is the plant of the earth when it dries up and is trampled down. Mujahid said: Like dry straw. Qatada said: Like the decayed remains of trees. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Like crushed dirt. It was also said: Its origin is from decayed bones.
51:43: 43. And in Thamud, when it was said to them, ‘Enjoy yourselves for a time,’ meaning the time when their appointed time would come to an end. That is because when they hamstrung the she-camel, it was said to them, Enjoy yourselves for three days.
51:44: 44. So they rebelled against the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them, after the three days had passed, which is death according to Ibn Abbas. Muqatil said: It means torment, and thunderbolt is every destructive torment. Al-Kisa’i read: thunderbolt, which is the sound of a thunderbolt, while they were looking on, seeing it with their own eyes.
51:45: 45. And they were not able to stand, meaning they did not stand after the punishment descended upon them, nor were they able to rise up. Qatada said: They did not rise from that blow, nor were they victorious, protecting themselves from Us. Qatada said: They did not have the strength to protect themselves from God.
51:46: 46. And the people of Noah, Abu Amr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read: and the people with the mim in the genitive case, meaning: and among the people of Noah. The others read it with the mim in the accusative case, based on the meaning, which is that his statement: So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea, means: We drowned them and drowned the people of Noah. Before, meaning: before these, and they are Aad, Thamud, and the people of Pharaoh. Indeed, they were a wicked people.
51:47: 47. And the heaven We constructed with power, meaning with strength and might, and indeed, We are expanding it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Able. And also from him: We are expanding the provision for Our creation. And it was said: Possessor of abundance. Ad-Dahhak said: Rich. Evidence for this is the saying of God Almighty: Upon the one who is provided with abundance is his measure. Al-Baqarah 2:236. Al-Hasan said: Capable.
51:48: 48. And the earth We have spread out, We have spread it out and smoothed it for you. How excellent are the spreaders, We are the spreaders. Ibn Abbas said: What I have spread out for My servants is excellent.
51:49: 49. And of everything We have created pairs, two different types and kinds, such as the sky and the earth, the sun and the moon, night and day, land and sea, plains and mountains, winter and summer, jinn and mankind, male and female, light and darkness, faith and disbelief, happiness and misery, truth and falsehood, sweet and bitter. Perhaps you will remember, so you will know that the Creator of pairs is One.
51:50: 50. So flee to God, so flee from God’s punishment to His reward, through faith and obedience. Ibn Abbas said: Flee from Him to Him and work to obey Him. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Flee from everything other than God to God, Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.
51:51: 51. "And do not make with God another god. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner."
51:52: 52. Likewise, meaning: just as your people denied you and said, He is a magician or a madman, so too, those before them, before the infidels of Mecca, had no messenger come to them except that they said, ‘He is a magician or a madman.’
51:53: 53. God the Almighty said: Do they enjoin it upon one another? That is, did the first of them enjoin upon the last of them and some of them to deny it and did they conspire against it? The alif in it is for rebuke, Rather, they are a transgressing people. Ibn Abbas said: Their transgression in what You have given them and provided for them has led them to deny You.
51:54: 54. So turn away from them, so turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed, there is no blame upon you, for you have conveyed the message and have not fallen short in what you were commanded to do. The commentators said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saddened and his companions were distressed. They thought that revelation had stopped and that the punishment had come, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ordered to leave them. Then God Almighty revealed:
51:55: 55. And remind, for indeed, the reminder benefits the believers, so their souls were at peace. Muqatil said: Its meaning is: Preach with the Qur’an to the unbelievers of Mecca, for the reminder benefits those among them who were previously known by God to believe. Al-Kalbi said: Preach with the Qur’an to those among your people who have believed, for the reminder benefits them.
51:56: 56. And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. Al-Kalbi, Ad-Dahhak, and Sufyan said: This is specific to the people of His obedience from both groups, as indicated by the reading of Ibn Abbas: And I did not create the jinn and mankind - from the believers - except to worship Me. Then he said in another verse: And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. (al-A’raf 7:79). Some of them said: I created the happy ones among the jinn and mankind only for my worship and the miserable ones among them only for my disobedience. This is the meaning of what Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is according to what they were created with of misery and happiness. Ali bin Abi Talib said: Except to worship Me, meaning, Except to command them to worship Me and call them to worship Me. This is supported by the Almighty’s saying: And they were commanded only to worship one God (al-Tawbah 9:31). Mujahid said: Except that they may know Me. This is better because if He had not created them, His existence and Oneness would not have been known. The evidence for this is the Almighty’s statement: And if you ask them, ‘Who created them?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ (al-Zukhruf 43:87) It was said: Its meaning is except that they submit to me and humble themselves. The meaning of worship in the language is: humility and submission. Every creature from the jinn and mankind is subject to God’s decree, humbled to His will. No one has the power to deviate from what he was created to be. It was said: (Except that they worship Me) except that they make Me One. As for the believer, he makes Him One in times of hardship and ease, and as for the disbeliever, he makes Him One in times of hardship and affliction, but not in times of blessing and ease. This is explained by the Almighty’s saying: And when they embark on a ship, they supplicate God, devoting their religion to Him sincerely. (al-Ankabut 29:65).
51:57: 57. I do not want from them any provision, meaning: that they provide for anyone of My creation, nor for themselves, nor do I want them to feed, meaning: that they feed anyone of My creation. He attributed the feeding to Himself, because creation is the dependents of God, and whoever feeds the dependents of someone has fed him. As it came in the hadith, God the Most High said: (I asked you for food, but you did not feed Me), meaning: you did not feed My servant. Then He explained that He is the Provider and no one else, saying:
51:58: 58. Indeed, God is the Provider, meaning: for all of His creation, the Possessor of strength, the Sturdy, and He is the Strong, the Powerful, the Exalted in strength and power.
51:59: 59. For those who did wrong, those who disbelieved from among the people of Mecca, will have sins, a share of the punishment, like the sins of their companions, like the share of their companions who perished from the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud. The root of sins in the language is: a large bucket filled with water, then it was used to mean luck and portion. So let them not hasten, the punishment, meaning that they will be delayed until the Day of Resurrection.
51:60: 60. This is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: So woe to those who disbelieve from the Day they are promised, meaning: the Day of Resurrection, and it was said: the Day of Badr.
52:1: 1. Meccan, By the Mount, meaning the mountain on which God Almighty spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, about the Holy Land. God Almighty swore by it.
52:3: 3. On spread parchment. Parchment is what is written on, and it is the skin of newspapers. Spread out is what is spread out. They differed concerning this book. Al-Kalbi said: It is what God wrote with His hand for Moses from the Torah, and Moses heard the scratching of the pen. It was said: It is the Preserved Tablet. It was also said: The records of the guardian angels will be brought out to them on the Day of Resurrection spread out, so I will take hold of his right hand and I will take hold of his left. The evidence for this is the Almighty’s saying: And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find spread out (al-Isra’ 17:13).
52:4: 4. And the Frequented House, with its many inhabitants and its many people. It is a house in the heavens next to the Throne opposite the Kaaba. It is called Ad-Dhirah. Its sanctity in the heavens is like the sanctity of the Kaaba on earth. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, circumambulate it, pray in it, and then never return to it again.
52:5: 5. And the raised ceiling, meaning the sky, is similar to the Almighty’s saying: And We made the sky a protected ceiling (Al-Anbiya’: 32).
52:6: 6. And the sea is set ablaze. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi and al-Dahhak said: It means the heated stove, like a set ablaze oven. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas. This is what was narrated that God Almighty will make all the seas fire on the Day of Resurrection, and thus the fire of Hell will be increased by them, as God Almighty said: And when the seas are set ablaze (al-Takwir 81:6). It was narrated in the hadith on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No man should embark on a sea except as a warrior, a pilgrim, or a pilgrims, for beneath the sea is a fire and beneath the fire is a sea. Mujahid and Al-Kalbi said: Al-Masjur means: filled. It is said: I filled the vessel if you fill it. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is the dry land whose water has gone and dried up. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: It is a mixture of fresh and salty water. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of An-Nazzal ibn Sabra on the authority of Ali that he said about the Sea of Fire: It is a sea beneath the Throne, covering it as if it were between the seven heavens and the seven earths. In it is a thick water called the Sea of Life. It rains on the servants for forty mornings after the first blast, and they grow in their graves. This is what Muqatil said: God swears by these things.
52:7: 7. The punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass.
52:8: 8. There is none to avert it, meaning something that prevents it. Jubayr ibn Mut'im said: I came to Madinah to speak to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the prisoners of Badr. I passed by him while he was praying Maghrib with his companions, and his voice was coming out of the mosque. I heard him recite By the Mount until His saying, "Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. There is none to avert it." It was as if my heart was torn apart when I heard him, and he had not yet converted to Islam that day. He said: So I converted to Islam out of fear of the punishment descending, and I did not think that I would get up from my place until the punishment befell me.
52:9: 9. Then he explained when it will happen, saying: The Day the sky will sway violently, meaning: it will swirl like a millstone and will overturn its inhabitants like a ship overturns. Qatada said: it will move. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: its parts will change with one another. It was also said: it will be disturbed. Al-Murr encompasses these meanings, as in the language it means: going, coming, hesitating, revolving, and turbulent.
52:10: 10. And the mountains will move, so they will move from their places and become scattered dust.
52:11: 11. So woe, severe torment, on that Day to the deniers.
52:12: 12. Those who are engaged in idle talk, they are engaged in idle talk, playing around, heedless and distracted.
52:13: 13. On the Day they are called, they are pushed, to the Fire of Hell, a violent and harsh push, that is, the keepers of Hell will chain their hands to their necks, and gather their forelocks to their feet, then they will be pushed into the Fire, pushed on their faces, and thrust up their backs until they reach the Fire. When they come near it, its keepers will say to them:
52:14: 14. This is the fire which you used to deny, in this world.
52:15: 15. Is this magic? This is because they used to attribute to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, magic, and that he blinded the eyes with magic, so they were rebuked for it, and it was said to them: Is this magic, or do you not see?
52:16: 16. They endured its severity, they endured its severity, whether you are patient or not patient, it is the same for you, patience and impatience, you will only be recompensed for what you used to do.
52:17: 17. Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and pleasure.
52:18: 18. Enjoying and delighted with that, with what their Lord has given them and their Lord has protected them from the punishment of Hellfire. And it will be said to them:
52:19: 19. Eat and drink at ease, safe from overeating and illness, for what you used to do.
52:20: 20. Reclining on thrones lined up, placed side by side, and We will marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes.
52:21: 21. And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith, Abu Amr read: And We followed them, with the alif cut off for emphasis, their offspring, with the alif and the ta’ broken in both of them, because of His saying: We joined them and We did not deprive them, so that the speech would be in a single order. Others read: And I followed them by connecting the alif, doubling the ta’ after it, and sukoon on the final ta’. Then they differed about (their offspring): The people of Medina read the first without an alif and with a damma on the ta’, and the second with an alif and a kasra on the ta’, and the people of Ash-Sham and Ya’qub both read it with an alif and a kasra on the ta’ in the second, and the others read it without an alif in both of them and with a nominative ta’ in the first and a nasb in the second. They differed on the meaning of the verse. Some people said: Its meaning is and those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith, meaning: their young and old children. The old are judged by their own faith, and the young are by the faith of their fathers. A young child is judged by his Islam following one of his parents. We will join with them their offspring, the believers [in Paradise according to their degrees, even if they do not reach the degrees of their fathers through their deeds] as an honor to their fathers so that their eyes may be comforted by that. This is the narration of Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them. Others said: Its meaning is, And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their young offspring who have not yet reached faith, through the faith of their fathers. This is the saying of Ad-Dahhak, and the narration of Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both. God, the Almighty, informed us that He will gather the offspring of His believing servant in Paradise, just as He loved for them to be gathered to Him in this world. He will admit them into Paradise through His grace and will join them to His degree through the deeds of their fathers, without diminishing anything from their deeds. This is His statement, And We did not deprive them - Ibn Kathir read it with a kasra on the lam, and the rest read it with a fatha, meaning We did not diminish them, meaning the fathers, from their deeds in the least. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hadith told me, Saeed bin Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Sayrafi told us, Muhammad bin Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Jabara bin Al-Maghlis told us, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, Amr bin Murrah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God raises the offspring of the believer in his degree, even if they are lower than him in deeds, so that his eyes may be comforted by them. Then he recited: And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring, to the end of the verse. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Abdullah bin Fanjuwayh Al-Daynuri told us, Abu Bakr bin Malik Al-Qati’i told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Uthman, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: “Khadijah, may God be pleased with her, asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about two of her sons who died during the pre-Islamic era. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘They are in Hell.’ When he saw the dislike on her face, he said: ‘If you saw where they were, you would hate them.’ She said: ‘O Messenger of God, what about my sons from you?’ He said: ‘In Paradise.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The believers and their children are in Paradise, and the polytheists and their children are in Hell.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring.’” Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned. Muqatil said: Every unbeliever is held in pledge in the Fire for what he has done of polytheism, but the believer is not held in pledge, because God Almighty said: Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right hand. Then he mentioned what will increase their goodness and blessings, saying:
52:22: 22. And We provided them with fruits, in addition to what they had, and meat of whatever they desired, from the types of meat.
52:23: 23. They will quarrel therein, they will engage in and take, a cup therein in which there is no idle talk, which is falsehood. This was narrated on the authority of Qatadah. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: There is no idle talk therein. Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab said: There is no obscene talk therein. Ibn Zayd said: There is no cursing or quarreling therein. Al-Qutaybi said: Their minds will not be lost, so they will not engage in idle talk or obscene speech. Nor will they commit sin, meaning they will not commit any sin. Al-Zajjaj said: Nothing idle or sinful will occur between them, as happens in this world when drinking wine. It was also said: They will not commit a sin by drinking it.
52:24: 24. And there will circulate among them, serving them, boys of theirs who are as if they were, in beauty, whiteness, and purity, hidden pearls, a safe, protected storehouse that no hands have touched. Saeed bin Jubair said: He means in shells. Abdullah bin Omar said: There is no one among the people of Paradise except that a thousand slaves strive to support him, and each slave is doing the same work as his companion. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that when he recited this verse, he said: They said, O Messenger of God, the servant is like a hidden pearl, so what about the one who is served? On the authority of Qatada also, he said: It was mentioned to us that a man said: O Prophet of God, this is the servant, but what about the master? He said: The superiority of the master over the servant is like the superiority of the moon on the night of the full moon over all the other planets.
52:25: 25. And some of them will turn to others, asking questions, asking each other in Paradise. Ibn Abbas said: They will remember the fatigue and fear they experienced in this world.
52:26: 26. “They said, ‘Indeed, we were before among our families,’ in this world, ‘in fear,’ fearing the punishment.
52:27: 27. So God bestowed His favor upon us, with forgiveness, and saved us from the torment of the poisonous wind. Al-Kalbi said: The torment of Hellfire. Al-Hasan said: The poisonous wind is one of the names of Hell.
52:28: 28. Indeed, we were before, in this world, calling upon Him, devoting our worship to Him alone, He, the people of Medina [and Al-Kisa’i] read: (that He) with a fat-ha on the alif, meaning: because or because, and the others read it with a kasra as a new beginning, He is the Righteous, Ibn Abbas said: the Kind. And Ad-Dahhak said: the Truthful in what He promised, the Most Merciful.
52:29: 29. So remind, O Muhammad, of the Qur’an to the people of Mecca, for you are not, by the grace of your Lord, by His mercy and protection, a soothsayer, inventing words and reporting what will happen without revelation, nor a madman, revealed about those who divided up the punishment of Mecca, accusing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of soothsaying, magic, madness, and poetry.
52:30: 30. Or do they say, rather they say, meaning: these false apportioners, He is a poet, meaning: he is a poet, We are waiting for him to be struck by the vicissitudes of fate, the accidents and vicissitudes of time, so he dies and perishes as the poets who came before him perished, and his companions disperse, and his father died young, and we hope that his death will be like his father’s death. Death can mean time, and it can mean death. They were called that because they cut short the appointed time.
52:31: 31. “Say, ‘Wait,’ wait for me to die, ‘for I am with you among those who wait,’ [among those who await] until God’s command comes to pass concerning you. So they were punished on the day of Badr with the sword.
52:32: 32. Or do their dreams, their minds, command them to do this, because the leaders of Quraysh were described as having dreams and minds, so God disgraced their minds when they were unable to distinguish between truth and falsehood, Or are they, rather they are, a transgressing people.
52:33: 33. Or do they say, ‘You create it,’ meaning, the Qur’an creates itself. “Taqawl” means to force a statement, and is only used to denote a lie. The matter is not as they claimed. Rather, they do not believe, in the Qur’an out of arrogance. Then he obliged them with the argument and said:
52:34: 34. Then let them produce a statement like it, meaning: like the Qur’an, with its structure and beautiful exposition, if they are truthful, that Muhammad says it himself.
52:35: 35. Or were they created by nothing? Ibn Abbas said: Without a Lord. Its meaning is: Were they created by nothing that created them, so they existed without a Creator? This is something that is not permissible, because the connection of creation to the Creator is a necessity of the name. If they denied the Creator, it would not be permissible for them to exist without a Creator. Or are they the creators of themselves? This is even more false, because how can something that does not exist be created? If both views are invalidated, then the proof is established against them that they have a Creator, so let them believe in Him. This meaning was mentioned by Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi. Al-Zajjaj said: It means: Were they created in vain and are not held accountable or commanded? Ibn Kaysan said: Were they created in vain and left aimlessly and are not commanded or forbidden? It is like someone saying: I did such and such for no reason, meaning: for no reason. Or are they the creators of themselves and are not obligated to command God?
52:36: 36. Or did they create the heavens and the earth? So they are the creators. This is not the case. Rather, they are not certain.
52:37: 37. Or do they have the treasures of your Lord? Ikrimah said: He means prophethood. Muqatil said: Do they have the keys to your Lord’s message, so that they can place them wherever they wish? Al-Kalbi said: The treasures of rain and sustenance. Or are they the ones in control? The powerful and tyrannical. Ata’ said: They are the overpowering lords, so they are not subject to command or prohibition, they do whatever they wish. It is permissible to use both the seen and the sad. Ibn ‘Amir read it with the seen here, and Qaleh said: bi-musaytir. Hamzah read it with the shin on the zay in both. Ibn Kathir read it with the seen here, and bi-musaytir with the sad. The others read it with the sad in both.
52:38: 38. Or do they have a ladder, an ascent and climb to heaven, by which they listen, that is, they listen to the revelation on it, as He says: And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees (Ta-Ha: 71), meaning: on it, meaning: Do they have a ladder by which they ascend to heaven, so they listen to the revelation and know that what they are doing is true through the revelation, and so they cling to it in the same way? Then let their listener bring, if they claim that, a clear authority, a clear argument.
52:39: 39. Or does He have daughters and you have sons? This is a denial of them when they attributed to God what they disliked, as He said: “Then ask them: Is it your Lord who has daughters and you have sons?” (al-Saffat 37:149).
52:40: 40. Or do you ask them for a reward? for what you have brought them and what you have called them to of the religion, so they are burdened with a heavy debt. The debt that you are asking them has burdened them, preventing them from Islam.
52:41: 41. Or do they have knowledge of the unseen? That is, knowledge of what was hidden from them, so that they knew that what the Messenger was telling them about the Day of Resurrection and the Resurrection was false. Qatada said: This is an answer to their saying: (We are waiting for him to be struck by a calamity of fate), meaning: Do they have knowledge of the unseen such that they know that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will die before them? They write means they judge, and writing means judgment. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the two men who had brought their dispute before him: I will judge between you according to the Book of God meaning according to God’s judgment. Ibn Abbas said: It means, do they have the Preserved Tablet, so they write what is in it and inform the people of it?
52:42: 42. Or do they intend a plot, a scheme against you to destroy you? Then those who disbelieve are the ones who will be plotted against, meaning: they are the ones who will be rewarded for their plot. He means that the harm of that will come back to them, and that their plot will surround them, and that is because they plotted against him in the House of Assembly and killed him at Badr.
52:43: 43. Or do they have a god other than God, who provides for them and gives them victory? Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him. Al-Khalil said: The mention of or in this surah is all interrogative and not a conjunction.
52:44: 44. And if they see a fragment a piece from the sky falling, this is an answer to their saying: (Then let down upon us a fragment from the sky), meaning: If We punished them by having some of the sky fall upon them, they would not cease their disbelief. They would say - out of their obstinacy - This is a heaped-up cloud, some of it on top of others, giving us rain.
52:45: 45. So leave them until they meet, that is, witness, their Day on which they will be struck dead, that is, die, until they witness death. Ibn Amir and Asim read they will be struck dead with a damma on the ya’, that is, they will perish.
52:46: 46. On the Day when their plotting will not avail them at all, nor will they be aided, meaning: their plotting will not benefit them on the Day of Death, and nothing will prevent them from the punishment.
52:47: 47. And indeed, for those who do wrong, [disbelieve], is a punishment less than that, meaning: a punishment in this world before the punishment of the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas said: It means being killed on the day of Badr. Ad-Dahhak said: It means hunger and famine for seven years. Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib said: The punishment of the grave. But most of them do not know, that the punishment will descend upon them.
52:48: 48. And be patient over the decision of your Lord, until the punishment that We have decreed for them befalls them, for indeed, you are before Our eyes, meaning, within Our sight. Ibn Abbas said: We see what is done to you. Al-Zajjaj said: You are where We see you and protect you, so they will not be able to harm you. And exalt the praises of your Lord when you rise, Saeed bin Jubayr and Ata’ said: That is, say when you rise from your seat: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. If the seat was good, then you will have increased in goodness, and if it was not, then it will be an expiation for it. Abu Abdullah Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Ahmad Al-Qaffal told us, Abu Mansur Ahmad bin Al-Fadl Al-Burjunjirdi told us, Abu Ahmad Bakr bin Muhammad Al-Sayrafi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Qurashi told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Saleh, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever sits in a gathering and engages in much idle talk, and says before he gets up: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You, then it will be expiation for what happened between them.” Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Its meaning is to pray to God when you rise from your seat. Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ said: When you stand up to pray, say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, and blessed be Your name, and exalted be Your majesty, and there is no god but You. Abu Uthman Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Al-Hasan bin Arfa and Yahya bin Musa told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Haritha bin Abi Al-Rijal, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, she said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began the prayer, he would say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, and blessed be Your name, and exalted be Your majesty, and there is no god but You. Al-Kalbi said: It is the remembrance of God with the tongue when you get out of bed until you enter into prayer. Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani told us, Abu Umar al-Qasim ibn Ja`far ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Hashemi told us, Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lu`lu`i told us, Abu Dawud ibn Sulayman al-Ash`ath told us, Muhammad ibn Nafi` told us, Zayd ibn Hubab told us, Mu`awiyah ibn Salih told us, Azhar ibn Sa`id al-Hazari told us, on the authority of `Asim ibn Humayd, who said: I asked `Aishah, may God be pleased with her, how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began his night prayers. She said: When he stood up, he would say, Allahu Akbar ten times, Al-Hamdulillah ten times, Al-Hamdulillah ten times, Subhan God ten times, La ilaha illa God ten times, Isti`a Allahu Akbar ten times, and Astagfir ten times. He would also say, O God, forgive me, guide me, provide for me, and grant me well-being, and he would seek refuge from the narrowness of the situation on the Day of Resurrection.
52:49: 49. And during part of the night, glorify Him, meaning, pray for Him. Muqatil said: It means the Maghrib and Isha prayers. And at the setting of the stars, meaning the two rak’ahs before the Fajr prayer, when the stars set, meaning they disappear with the light of dawn. This is the opinion of most commentators. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the obligatory Fajr prayer. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jarir ibn Mut`im, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite Surat al-Tur in the Maghrib prayer.
53:1: 1. Meccan, And the star when it goes down, Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Al-Walabi and Al-Awfi: It means the Pleiades when they fall and disappear, and its disappearance is its setting, and the Arabs call the Pleiades a star. It was reported in the hadith on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet said: No star has ever risen while there was any defect on Earth except that it was raised. By the star he meant the Pleiades. Mujahed said: They are all the stars in the sky when they set. Its wording is one but its meaning is plural. A planet is called a star because of its rising, and every rising star is a star. It is said: the star of the tooth, the horn, and the plant: when it rises. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is the stars, meaning what the devils throw when they eavesdrop. Abu Hamza Al-Thumali said: They are the stars when they are scattered on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that what is meant by the star is the Qur’an. It was called a star because it was revealed in separate stars over twenty years. The separation is called tanjeeman, and the one who separates is called munjeeman. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas in the narration of Ata’, and it is also the opinion of Al-Kalbi. Al-Hawa: to descend from high to low. Al-Akhfash said: An-Najm is a plant that has no stem, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And the star and the tree prostrate Ar-Rahman 55:6. Its descent is its falling to the ground. Ja’far Al-Sadiq said: It means Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, when he descended from the sky on the night of the Ascension. And Al-Hawa is the descent. It is said: he descended, he descends, like he went down, he goes down.
53:2: 2. The answer to the oath: His saying: Your companion has not gone astray, meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, has not gone astray from the path of guidance, nor has he gone astray.
53:3: 3. Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination, meaning: from [his own] inclination, meaning he does not speak falsehood, and that is because they said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, recites the Qur’an on his own.
53:4: 4. It is - what he said in religion, and it was said: the Qur’an except a revelation revealed, meaning: a revelation from God revealed to him.
53:5: 5. He was taught by one of great strength, that is Gabriel, and strength is the plural of power.
53:6: 6. Of great strength and power in his creation, meaning Gabriel. Ibn Abbas said: Of great strength means: of good appearance. Muqatil said: of tall, good character. And He rose up, meaning Gabriel.
53:7: 7. And he means Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Most of the speech of the Arabs when they want to connect in such a case is to show the pronoun of the connected thing, so they say: He and so-and-so were made equal. Similar to this is his statement: Shall we, when we and our fathers were dust? (al-Naml 27:67). The fathers are connected to the pronoun in we were without showing we. The meaning of the verse is: Gabriel and Muhammad, peace be upon them, were made equal on the night of the Ascension, at the highest horizon, which is the farthest part of the world where the sun rises. It was said: He was made equal means Gabriel, and it is also a pronoun for Gabriel, meaning: he rose in the form in which God created him, and he is at the highest horizon. This is because Gabriel used to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the form of humans, just as he used to come to the prophets. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him to show him himself in the form in which he was created, so he showed him himself twice: once on earth and once in heaven. As for on earth, he is at the highest horizon, and what is meant by the highest is the eastern side, because Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Hira’, so Gabriel rose to him from the east. The horizon was blocked to the west, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell unconscious. Then Gabriel descended in the form of a human being, hugged him to himself, and began wiping the dust from his face, as he said: Then he drew near and descended. As for the heaven, he was at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and none of the prophets saw him in that form except our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
53:8: 8. The Almighty said: Then he approached and came closer.
53:9: 9. "And he was two bow lengths away or nearer." They differed on its meaning: Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad bin Yusuf informed us, Muhammad bin Ismail informed us, Abu Usamah informed us, Zakariya bin Abi Zaida informed us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Ashwa', on the authority of Al-Sha'bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I said to Aisha, "So where is his statement: (Then he approached and descended, and was two bow lengths away or nearer?) She said: (That was Gabriel, who used to come to him in the form of a man, but this time he came to him in his true form, and he blocked the horizon.) Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Talq bin Ghannam told us, Zaidah Al-Shaibani told us: I asked Zara about his statement: (Then he was two bow lengths away or nearer), he said: Abdullah - meaning Ibn Masoud - told us that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel who had six hundred wings. The meaning of the verse is: Then Gabriel approached after he was at the highest horizon of the earth, and he came down and descended to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and was from him two bow lengths or nearer, or even nearer. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Qatada said the same. It was said: There is an inversion in the speech, meaning: Then he came down and approached, because coming down is the cause of coming near. Others said: Then the Lord Almighty approached Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and descended, so He came close to him until He was two bow lengths away or nearer. We narrated in the story of the Ascension on the authority of Sharik ibn Abdullah on the authority of Anas: The Almighty, the Lord of Majesty, approached and descended until He was two bow lengths away from him or nearer. This is the narration of Ibn Salamah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Drawing close means descending to something until one is close to it. Mujahid said: Gabriel approached his Lord. Ad-Dahhak said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, approached his Lord, so he leaned forward and bowed down in prostration, and he was two bow lengths away from Him or even nearer. The meaning of his saying: (the distance of two bow lengths) is the length of two bow lengths. (Al-Qab), (Al-Qayb), (Al-Qad) and (Al-Qayd) are all expressions of measure. (Al-Qaws) is what is shot with, according to Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid, Ikrimah and Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. So he reported that there was between Gabriel and Muhammad, peace be upon them, the distance of two bow lengths. Mujahid said: Its meaning is where the string is on the bow, and this is an indication to emphasize the closeness. Its origin is that when two allies from the Arabs wanted to make a covenant and a treaty, they would go out with their bows and stick them together, meaning that they were supporting each other, each one defending the other. Abdullah bin Masoud said: The distance of two bow lengths means: the length of two cubits. This is the opinion of Saeed bin Jubair and Shaqiq bin Salamah. The bow means the cubit by which everything is measured. Or nearer means: rather, closer.
53:10: 10. Then He revealed, meaning: God revealed, to His servant, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, what He revealed. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Ata’, Al-Kalbi, Al-Hasan, Al-Rabi’, and Ibn Zayd: Its meaning is: Gabriel revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, revealed to him. Saeed bin Jubair said: It was revealed to him: Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? (al-Duha 93:6) until the Almighty’s saying: And We have raised your fame (Ash-Sharh: 4). It was said: It was revealed to him: Paradise is forbidden to the prophets until you enter it, and to the nations until your nation enters it.
53:11: 11. The heart did not lie about what it saw. Abu Ja`far read (the heart did not lie) with a shaddah on the dhal, meaning: the heart of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not lie about what he saw with his eyes that night, rather it believed it and confirmed it. The others read it with a shaddah, meaning: the heart of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not lie about what he saw. They differed about what he saw, so some people said: He saw Gabriel, and this is the opinion of Ibn Mas`ud and Aisha. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Hafs - he is Ibn Ghiyath - told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: (The heart did not lie about what it saw) He said: He saw Gabriel with six hundred wings. Others said: It is God Almighty. Then they differed about the meaning of the vision. Some of them said: He placed his sight in his heart and saw Him with his heart, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Wakee told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ziyad bin Al-Hussain, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The heart did not lie about what it saw. “And he had already seen it on another occasion.” He said: He saw it with his heart twice. A group of people said that he saw him with his own eyes, which is the opinion of Anas, Al-Hasan, and Ikrimah. They said: Muhammad saw his Lord. Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God chose Abraham with friendship, chose Moses with speech, and chose Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with vision. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, used to say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not see his Lord, and the verse refers to his seeing Gabriel, peace be upon him: Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I said to Aisha, “O mother, did Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, see his Lord?” She said, “My hair stands on end because of what you have said. Where are you with regard to three things? Whoever tells them to you has lied.” Whoever told you that Muhammad saw his Lord has lied. Then you read: “No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.” (al-An’am 6:103), It is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil. (al-Shura 42:51). Whoever told you that he knows what will happen tomorrow has lied. Then you read: And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow. (Luqman 31:34). Whoever told you that he concealed something has lied. Then you read: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. (al-Ma’idah 5:67), but he saw Gabriel in his true form twice. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin [Shaqiq], on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Have you seen your Lord?’ He said: ‘Light, how can I see Him?’”
53:12: 12. Do you then argue with him about what he sees? Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read: Aftamuruhu with a fat-ha on the ta’ [and a sukoon on the meem] without an alif, meaning: Do you then deny him? The Arabs say: I showed a man his right if you denied him. The others read: Aftamuruhu with an alif and a damma on the ta’, meaning: Do you then argue with him about what he sees? This is because they argued with him when he was taken on the Night Journey, and they said: Describe Jerusalem to us, and Inform us about our caravan on the road, and other things that they argued with him about. The meaning is: Do you then argue with him with an argument that you want to push him away from what he saw and knew.
53:13: 13. And he saw him on another descent, meaning: He saw Gabriel in the form in which he was created descending from the heavens on another descent. That is because he saw him in his form twice, once on earth and once in the heavens.
53:14: 14. At the Lote Tree of the Limit. According to Ibn Abbas, the meaning of another descent is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had ascensions that night regarding the issue of reducing the number of prayers, so each ascension would have a descent, so he saw his Lord in some of them. We have narrated from him: He saw his Lord twice with his heart. And from him: He saw with his eyes. His statement: At the Lote Tree of the Limit. We have narrated from Abdullah ibn Masoud, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is in the heaven. Whatever ascends from the earth ends at it and is taken from it, and whatever descends from above it ends at it and is taken from it. God the Almighty said: Near it is the Garden of Refuge, when that which covers the Lote Tree covers it. He said: A bed of gold. We narrated in the hadith of the Ascension: “Then he ascended with me to the seventh heaven, and there I saw Abraham, peace be upon him, so I greeted him. Then the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised for me, and its fruit was like the jars of Hajar, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants.” (And the lote tree) is the Nabq tree. It is also called the Lote Tree of the Limit because it is to it that the knowledge of creation ends. Hilal ibn [Yasaaf] said: Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b about the Lote Tree of the Limit while I was present. Ka’b said: It is a lote tree at the base of the Throne over the heads of those who bear the Throne, and to it the knowledge of creation ends. What is behind it is unseen and no one knows it except God. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told me, Ibn Shaiba told us, Al-Masuhi told us, Ubaid bin Ya’ish told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Ibad bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandmother Asma bint Abi Bakr, who said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention the Lote Tree of the Limit. He said: A rider can travel in the shade of its branches for a hundred years, and one hundred thousand riders can seek shade in its branches. In it are beds of gold, and its fruit is like jugs.” Muqatil said: It is a tree that bears ornaments, garments, and fruits of all colors. If a leaf of it were placed in the ground, it would illuminate the people of the earth. It is the Tuba that God Almighty mentioned in Surat Ar-Ra’d.
53:15: 15. There is the Paradise of refuge, Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A Paradise to which Gabriel and the angels take refuge. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: The souls of the martyrs take refuge in it.
53:16: 16. When that which covers the lote tree covers it, Ibn Masoud said: A bed of gold. We narrated in the hadith of the Ascension on the authority of Anas on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Then he took me to the lote tree of the farthest boundary, and behold, its leaves were like the ears of elephants, and behold, its fruit was like jugs. Then, when the command of God overcame it, it changed, and no one among God’s creation could describe its beauty. And He revealed to me what He revealed, and He imposed on me fifty prayers every day and night.” Muqatil said: Angels like crows cover it. Al-Suddi said: From the birds. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, or someone else, who said: The light of creation covers it, and the angels cover it from the love of God like crows, when they perch on the tree. He said: Then he spoke to him, and he said to him: Ask. And on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The light of the Lord of Glory covers it, so it is illuminated. It is narrated in the hadith: (I saw on every leaf of it an angel standing, glorifying God Almighty).
53:17: 17. His sight did not swerve, nor did it go astray. That is, the sight of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not deviate to the right or to the left, nor did it go astray. That is, it did not go beyond what he saw. It was also said: it did not go beyond what he was commanded to do. This is a description of his good manners in that situation, as the two sides did not meet.
53:18: 18. He has certainly seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord, meaning: the great signs. It has also been said that he meant what he saw that night during his journey and return, as evidenced by His statement: That We might show him some of Our signs (al-Isra’ 17:1). It has also been said that its meaning is that he has certainly seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Ubaidullah bin Muadh Al-Anbari told us, my father told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Shaibani, he heard Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: He saw one of the greatest signs of his Lord. He said: He saw Gabriel in his form with six hundred wings. And Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Hafs bin Amr told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah [on the authority of Abdullah]: (He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord)? He said: He saw a green leaf that filled the horizon of the sky.
53:19: 19. The Almighty said: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? These are names of idols that they took as deities that they worshipped. They derived names for them from the names of God, so they said: Al-Lat from God, and Al-Uzza from Al-Aziz. It was also said: Al-Uzza is the feminine of Al-A’zz. As for Al-Lat, Qatada said: It was in Al-Taif. Ibn Zayd said: It was a house in Nakhal that the Quraysh used to worship. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Abu Saleh read: Al-Lat with emphasis on the ta, and they said: He used to mix gruel for the pilgrims, and when he died, they devoted themselves to his grave to worship him. Mujahed said, “He had a mountaintop where he had spoils from which he would extract ghee and take curd, and he would gather its messengers and then make a hais from it and feed the pilgrims with it. He was in Batn Nakhal, and when he died, they worshipped him, and he was Al-Lat.” Al-Kalbi said: There was a man from Thaqif called Sarmah bin Ghanm. He used to remove the ghee and place it on a rock. Then the Arabs would come to him and he would tie their markets with it. When the man died, Thaqif turned it into their homes and worshipped it, like the sidrah of Taif on the site of Al-Lat. As for Al-Uzza, Mujahid said: It is a tree in Ghatafan that they used to worship. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to cut it down. Khalid ibn al-Walid began to strike it with an axe and say: Oh glory to your ingratitude, no glory to you, I saw that God has humiliated you Then a female demon came out of it, spreading her hair, calling for her woe, and placing her hand on her head. It is said: “Khalid returned to the Prophet and said: I have uprooted it. He said: What did you see? He said: I did not see anything. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What did you uproot? He went back and came back with a pickaxe and uprooted it and pulled out its roots. A naked woman came out of it. He killed her and then returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him about that. He said: That was Al-Uzza and she will never be worshipped again.” Ad-Dahhak said: It is an idol of Ghatafan, placed for them by Sa`d ibn Dhalim al-Ghatafani. He came to Mecca and saw Safa and Marwa, and saw the people of Mecca circumambulating between them. He returned to Batn Nakhal and said to his al-Nas 114:“The people of Mecca belong to Safa and Marwa, but they are not yours. They have a god whom they worship, but you do not.” They said: What do you command us to do? He said: I will do the same for you. So he took a stone from Safa and a stone from Marwa and carried them to Nakhal. He placed the one he had taken from Safa and said: This is Safa. Then he placed the one he had taken from Marwa and said: This is Marwa. Then he took three stones and leaned them against a tree and said: This is your Lord. So they began to circumambulate between the two stones and worship the stones, until the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) conquered Mecca. He ordered the stones to be removed and sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to al-`Uzza, who cut them down. Ibn Zayd said: It is a house in Taif that Thaqif used to worship.
53:20: 20. And Manat, Ibn Kathir read it with a long vowel and a hamza, while the general public read it with a short vowel without a hamza, because the Arabs named Zayd Manat and Abd Manat, and the long vowel was not heard in it. Qatada said: It belongs to Khuza'ah and was located in Qudayd. Aisha may God be pleased with her said about the Ansar: They used to perform Ihram for Manat, and it was located near Qudayd. Ibn Zayd said: It is a house in Al-Mushallal that was worshipped by Banu Ka'b. Ad-Dahhak said: Manat is an idol of Huza'ah and Khuza'ah that the people of Mecca worship. Some of them said: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat are stone idols that were inside the Kaaba and they used to worship them. The reciters differed regarding stopping at al-Lat and Manat. Some of them stopped at them with a ha’, and some with a ta’. Some of them said: What is written in the Qur’an with a ta’ should be stopped at with a ta’, and what is written with a ha’ should be stopped at with a ha’. As for his saying: The third other, [the third] is an attribute of Manat, meaning: the third for the two idols mentioned. As for the other, the Arabs do not say the third other, rather the other here is an attribute of the second. Al-Khalil said: The ya’ is to agree with the beginnings of the verses, like his saying: Other desires (Ta-Ha 20:18) and he did not say: another. It was said: In the verse there is an inversion, meaning: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza the other and Manat the third. The meaning of the verse: Have you considered?: Tell us, O you who claim that Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat are daughters of God. Al-Kalbi said: The polytheists of Mecca used to say: The idols and angels are daughters of God, and if a man among them was given the good report of having a female child, he would hate that. So God Almighty said, denouncing them:
53:21: 21. Do you have males and He has females?
53:22: 22. That then is an unfair division. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: That is, a permissible division, since you have given to your Lord what you dislike for yourselves. Mujahid and Muqatil said: A crooked division. Al-Hasan said: Not balanced. Ibn Kathir read: (ِذِذزي) with a hamza, and the others read it without a hamza. Al-Kisa’i said: It is said from it yadhiz dayzan, and dazz yadhuz dawz, and dazz yadhaaz dazzan if he wronged and diminished, and the meaning of dhayzi from speech is fa’la with a damma on the fa’, because it is an adjective and adjectives are only on fa’la with a damma on the fa’, like hubla pregnant, aththa female and bishra good report, or fa’la with a fatha on the fa’, like ghadabi angry, sakra sick and ’asha thirsty. There is no fa’la with a kasra on the fa’ in adjectives in Arabic, it is only in nouns, like dhikra remembrance and shi’ra story. The Ḍad is broken here so that the ya’ does not turn into a waw and it is from the daughters of ya’ as they said in the plural of abyadبيضbiydh whites. The origin is bawdh whites like hamra red and safar yesfar. As for the one who said dazz yadhuz, the noun from it is dawza dowzi like shura courtship.
53:23: 23. They - what are these idols - are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which God has sent down no authority, an argument for what you say that they are gods. Then He returned to the statement after the address and said: They follow nothing but conjecture, in their saying that they are gods, and what their souls desire, and what Satan has made attractive to them, and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance, the clarification by the Book and the Messenger that they are not gods, for worship is only appropriate for God, the One, the Compeller.
53:24: 24. Or will man have what he desires? Does the unbeliever think that he will have what he desires and craves from the intercession of idols?
53:25: 25. To God belongs the Hereafter and the first life, not as the unbeliever thought and wished, but to God belongs the Hereafter and the first life, and no one owns anything in them except with His permission.
53:26: 26. And how many an angel is there in the heavens, of those whom these disbelievers worship and whose intercession they hope to have with God, their intercession will not avail at all except after God has given permission, in intercession, for whomever He wills and is pleased with, meaning: of the people of monotheism. Ibn Abbas said: He means that the angels do not intercede except for whom God is pleased with. The plural of metaphor in His statement: (their intercession) and the angel is one, because what is meant by His statement: (and how many an angel) is multitude, so it is like His statement: There is not one of you who can prevent Him (al-Haqqah 69:47).
53:27: 27. Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with female names, meaning: with female names when they say: They are the daughters of God.
53:28: 28. And they have no knowledge of it, Muqatil said: [Its meaning is] they are not certain that they are [the daughters of God] They follow nothing but assumption, and assumption is of no avail against the truth at all, (and the truth) means knowledge, i.e. assumption does not take the place of knowledge. It was said: (the truth) means torment, [i.e. I think that nothing will save them from the torment].
53:29: 29. So turn away from whoever turns away from Our remembrance, meaning the Qur’an. It was also said: faith, and desires only the life of this world.
53:30: 30. Then he belittled their opinion and said: That is the extent of their knowledge, meaning: That is the limit of their knowledge and the extent of their minds, that they preferred this world over the Hereafter. It was said: They did not attain any knowledge except their belief that the angels are daughters of God, and that they intercede for them, so they relied on that and turned away from the Qur’an. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided. That is, He is all-knowing of both groups, so He will reward them.
53:31: 31. To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. This is an objection between the first verse and His statement, That He may recompense those who do evil for what they have done. The lam in His statement, To recompense is connected to the meaning of the first verse, because if He were more knowledgeable about them, He would recompense each one for what he deserves, those who did evil and associated others with God: for what they did of associating others with God. And He will recompense those who do good with goodness, they believed in the Oneness of their Lord: with goodness with Paradise. He is only able to recompense the doer of good and the doer of evil if he has great dominion, and for that reason He said, To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
53:32: 32. Then he described them, saying: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor ones. They differed regarding the meaning of the verse. Some people said: This is a valid exception, and minor ones are among the major sins and immoralities. The meaning of the verse is: unless he commits an immoral act once and then repents, and the act occurs and then stops. This is the opinion of Abu Hurairah [and Mujahid and Al-Hasan], and the narration of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas said: A minor sin is less than polytheism. Al-Suddi said: Abu Saleh said: I was asked about the statement of God Almighty: (except for a few,)) and I said: It is a man who commits a sin and does not repeat it. I mentioned that to Ibn Abbas and he said: A generous angel has helped you. And we narrated on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: (except for a few, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive a great deal, and which of your servants does not commit a sin? The root of al-lamm and al-ilma is: what a person does from time to time, and it is not repeated or permanent. Others said: This is an isolated exception, meaning: but the slightest thing, and they did not consider the slightest thing to be among the major sins and indecencies. Then they differed over its meaning, and some of them said: It is what happened in the pre-Islamic period, so God will not hold them accountable for it. That is because the polytheists said to the Muslims: Did they work with us yesterday? So God revealed this verse. This is the opinion of Zayd ibn Thabit and Zayd ibn Aslam. Some of them said: It is minor sins such as a glance, a wink, a kiss, and anything less than adultery. This is the opinion of Ibn Masoud, Abu Hurairah, Masruq, and Al-Sha’bi, and the narration of Tawus on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail, Mahmud bin Ghailan told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I have not seen anything more like the licking than what Abu Hurairah said, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God has decreed for the son of Adam his share of adultery, which he will inevitably attain. The adultery of the eye is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speaking, the soul desires and longs, and the private parts confirm that and deny it.” It was narrated by Suhayl ibn Abi Salih on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he added: “The fornication of the eyes is looking, the fornication of the ears is listening, the fornication of the tongue is speaking, the fornication of the hand is touching, and the fornication of the foot is walking.” Al-Kalbi said: Al-Lamlam has two meanings: Every sin for which God has not mentioned a punishment in this world or a punishment in the hereafter, that is what prayers will expiate, as long as it does not reach the level of major sins and indecencies. The other meaning is: The great sin that a Muslim commits time after time and then repents from it. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It is what does not cause any danger to the heart. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: “A glance that is not intentional is forgiven. If he looks again, then it is not a glance, but a sin.” Indeed, your Lord is Vast in forgiveness, Ibn Abbas said: For whoever does that and repents, the speech is complete here. Then he said: He is most knowing of you when He created you from the earth, meaning He created your father Adam from dust, and when you were fetuses, the plural of fetus, called a fetus because it was formed in the womb, “in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves,” Ibn Abbas said: Do not praise it. Al-Hasan said: God knows about every soul what it is doing and what it is going to become, so do not claim purity for yourselves, do not absolve it of sins, and do not praise it for its good deeds. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: People used to do good deeds and then say: Our prayers, our fasting, and our Hajj. So God Almighty revealed this verse: He knows best who fears God, meaning: He was righteous, obeyed, and sincere in his work for God Almighty.
53:33: 33. The Almighty’s saying: Have you seen him who has turned away? This was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah. He had followed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his religion, but some of the polytheists reviled him and said to him: Have you abandoned the religion of the elders and led them astray? He said: I feared the punishment of God. So the one who rebuked him guaranteed that if he agreed with him and gave him such-and-such of his wealth and returned to his polytheism, he would bear the punishment of God on his behalf. So Al-Walid returned to polytheism and gave the one who rebuked him some of the money that he had guaranteed and prevented him from taking it all. So God Almighty revealed: Have you seen him who has turned away? He turned away from faith.
53:34: 34. He gave, his companion said, a little and was stingy with the rest. Muqatil said: He gave, meaning Al-Walid, a little of goodness with his tongue, then he stopped, meaning he stopped it and did not continue with the gift. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Al-Aas bin Wael Al-Sahmi, because he agreed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in some matters. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl, because he said: By God, Muhammad only commands us to have good morals. That is why his statement: (And he gave a little and was unjust) means he did not believe in him. The meaning of (was unjust) is to cut off, and its origin is from the word kadda, which is a stone that appears in a well and prevents digging. The Arabs say: The hafir became unjust and mountainous, if he reached the kadda or mountain in digging.
53:35: 35. Does he have knowledge of the unseen so that he sees? What is hidden from him and he knows that its owner will bear its punishment on his behalf.
53:36: 36. Or has he not been informed, that is, not told, of what is in the scriptures of Moses, meaning: the books of the Torah.
53:37: 37. And Abraham, in the Qur’an of Abraham, peace be upon him, who fulfilled, completed and perfected what he was commanded to do. Al-Hasan, Saeed bin Jubair, and Qatada said: He did what he was commanded to do and conveyed the messages of his Lord to His creation. Mujahid said: He fulfilled what was imposed on him. Al-Rabi said: In his dream, he slaughtered his son. Ata Al-Khurasani said: He completed the obedience. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: And in the arrows of Islam. They are His saying: And when his Lord tested Abraham with commands, and he fulfilled them Al-Baqarah 2:124. And fulfillment means completion. Ad-Dahhak said: And in the covenant of rituals. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim al-Shaibani told us, Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Zuhri told us, Ismail ibn Mansur told us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Ibrahim is the one who fulfilled [the obligation of] praying four rak`ahs at the beginning of the day. Abu Uthman Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Abu Jaafar Al-Samnani told us, Abu Mashair told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Buhair bin Saad, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ and Abu Dharr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of God Almighty, that He said: O son of Adam, bow down to Me four rak’ahs at the beginning of the day and I will suffice you at the end of it.
53:38: 38. Then he explained what was in their pages, saying: No soul shall bear the burden of another, meaning: no soul shall bear the burden of another, and its meaning is: no soul shall be taken for the sin of another. And in refuting the statement of those who guaranteed to Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira that he would bear the sin on his behalf. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Before Abraham, peace be upon him, they used to punish a man for the sin of another. A man would be killed for killing his father, son, brother, wife, or slave, until Abraham, peace be upon him, forbade them from doing that and conveyed to them from God: No soul shall bear the burden of another.
53:39: 39. And that man can have nothing but what he strives for, meaning: what he does, as in His statement: Indeed, your striving is diverse (al-Layl 92:4). This is also in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Ibn Abbas said: This is the abrogated ruling in this Sharia, in His saying: We joined their offspring to them (al-Tur 52:21), so the children entered Paradise due to the righteousness of the fathers. Ikrimah said: This was for the people of Abraham and Moses, but as for this nation, they will have what they strived for and what others strived for them, based on what was narrated that a woman lifted up her boy and said: O Messenger of God, is there a Hajj for him? He said: (Yes, and you will have a reward.) A man said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: My mother took her own life. Will she receive a reward if I give charity on her behalf? He said: Yes. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: And that man will have nothing but what he strives for, meaning the disbeliever. As for the believer, he will have what he strives for and what he strives for. It was said: The unbeliever has no good except what he does, for which he is rewarded in this world until there is no good left for him in the Hereafter. It is narrated that Abdullah bin Ubayy gave Al-Abbas a shirt to wear, and when he died, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent his shirt to be shrouded in it, so he had no good deeds left for him in the afterlife for which he could repent.
53:40: 40. And that his effort will be seen, in his scale on the Day of Resurrection, [taken] from: I showed him the thing.
53:41: 41. Then He will reward him with the fullest reward, the most complete and perfect, meaning: the person will be rewarded for his efforts. It is said: I rewarded so-and-so for his efforts and his efforts. The poet said: If Alqamah bin Saad rewarded his efforts, I would not reward him with a single day’s affliction. He combined the two languages.
53:42: 42. And to your Lord is the final destination, meaning: the ultimate destination of creation and their return to Him, and He will reward them for their deeds. It was said: From Him is the beginning of the blessing and to Him is the final hope. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Shaibani told me, Muhammad bin Sulayman bin Al-Fath Al-Hanbali told us, Ali bin Muhammad Al-Masry told us, Abu Ishaq bin Mansur Al-Sa’di told us, Al-Abbas bin Zafar told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far Al-Razi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: (And to your Lord is the final destination), he said: (There is no thought about the Lord), and this is similar to what was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: (Ponder over creation, but do not ponder over the Creator), for thought cannot encompass Him.
53:43: 43. And that it is He who makes people laugh and cry, this indicates that everything a person does is by His decree and creation, even laughter and crying. Mujahid and Al-Kalbi said: He makes the people of Paradise laugh in Paradise, and He makes the people of Hell cry in Hell. Ad-Dahhak said: He makes the earth laugh with plants, and He makes the sky cry with rain. Ata bin Abi Muslim said: It means I rejoice and I grieve, because joy brings laughter, and sadness brings crying. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malhi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Ja’d told us, Qais - he is Ibn Al-Rabi’ Al-Asadi - told us, Samak bin Harb told us: I said to Jabir bin Samurah: Did you sit with the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him? He said: Yes, and his companions used to sit and recite poetry and mention things from the days of ignorance, and they would laugh and he would smile with them when they laughed - meaning the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Muammar said on the authority of Qatada: Ibn Umar was asked, “Did the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laugh?” He said, Yes, and the faith in their hearts was greater than a mountain.
53:44: 44. And that it is He who causes death and brings to life, meaning: He causes death in this world and brings to life through resurrection. It has also been said: He causes the fathers to die and the sons to live. It has also been said: He causes the unbeliever to die with the indefinite noun and the believer to live with the definite noun.
53:45: 45. And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, from every animal.
53:46: 46. From a drop of semen when it is desired, meaning: it is poured into the womb. It is said: a man ejaculated and he desired. This was said by Ad-Dahhak and Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah. Others said: it is estimated. It is said: he desired something if he estimated it.
53:47: 47. And that upon Him is the other creation, meaning: the second creation for the resurrection on the Day of Resurrection.
53:48: 48. And that He is the Richest and Most Satisfied, Abu Saleh said: He is the Richest and Most Satisfied of people in terms of money, meaning: He gave the means and the origins of the money and what they save after they are satisfied. Ad-Dahhak said: He became rich with gold, silver, and various kinds of money, and he was satisfied with camels, cows, and sheep. Qatada and Al-Hasan said: Aqna means to serve. Ibn Abbas said: He enriched and satisfied means he gave and satisfied. Mujahed and Muqatil said: Aqna means to be satisfied with what he was given and content. Ibn Zayd said: Aghna means more and aqna means less. He recited: He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it Al-Isra’ 17:30. Al-Akhfash said: Aqna means become poor. Ibn Kaysan said: give birth.
53:49: 49. And that He is the Lord of Sirius, which is a planet behind Gemini. There are two Sirius stars, one of which is called Al-Abour and the other Al-Ghamisa’a. It was called that because it is more hidden than the other, and the galaxy is between them. Here he meant Sirius Al-Abour, which the Khuza’a tribe used to worship. The first one to establish that for them was a man from their nobles called Abu Kabsha. He worshipped it and said: Because the stars cross the sky in width and Sirius in length, it is different from them. So the Khuza’a tribe worshipped it. When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) went against the Arabs in religion, they named him Ibn Abi Kabsha because of his difference from them, like the difference between Abu Kabsha and the worship of Sirius.
53:50: 50. And that He destroyed the former 'Aad, the people of Medina and Basra read it with a double lam after the dal, and Qaloon hamzas the waw on the authority of Nafi', and the Arabs do that and say: qom lan 'anna, meaning: stand up now, and the pause is at ('Aad), and the beginning is (awla), with one open hamza followed by a lam with a dammah, [and it is permissible to begin: lawla] by deleting the open hamza. Others read: The first ‘Aad, and they were the people of Hud who were destroyed by a furious wind. They had offspring, and they became the second ‘Aad.
