53:51: 51. And Thamud, who were the people of Salih, whom God destroyed with the blast, and He did not leave a single one of them.
53:52: 52. And the people of Noah before, meaning: the people of Noah were destroyed before, Aad and Thamud, indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious, because of Noah’s long call to them and their rebellion against God through disobedience and denial.
53:53: 53. And the overturned, the villages of Lot’s people, he brought down, he brought them down, that is, Gabriel brought them down after he had raised them to the sky.
53:54: 54. He covered it, God clothed it with what covered it, meaning: the arranged, marked stones.
53:55: 55. Then which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute? Yes, your Lord, O man. It was said that Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira meant, do you dispute? Doubt and argue. Ibn Abbas said: Lie.
53:56: 56. This is a warner, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the first warners, meaning: a messenger from among the messengers sent to you as they were sent to their people. Qatada said: He says: Muhammad was warned as the messengers before him were warned.
53:57: 57. "The Hour has drawn near, the Day of Resurrection has drawn near and the Hour is approaching.
53:58: 58. There is none to uncover it besides God, meaning: one who makes it manifest and establishes it, as God the Almighty says: None can reveal it at its time except Him (al-A’raf 7:187). The ha in it is for emphasis or to assume: a uncovering soul. It is possible that kashifa is a verbal noun like khafiyya and al-afiya, and the meaning is: there is none to uncover it besides God, meaning none can uncover it or make it manifest except Him. It was said: Its meaning is: There is no repeller for it, meaning: If its horrors and hardships overwhelm creation, no one can remove them or repel them from them. This is the saying of Ata’, Qatada, and Ad-Dahhak.
53:59: 59. Do you wonder at this statement, meaning the Qur’an,?
53:60: 60. And you laugh, meaning: mockingly, and you do not cry, because of the threat it contains.
53:61: 61. "And you are heedless," heedless and negligent. "Sammud" means heedlessness of something and amusement. It is said: Leave your Samud, meaning your amusement. This is the narration of Al-Walabi and Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ikrimah said on his authority: It is singing in the language of the people of Yemen. When they heard the Qur’an, they would sing and play. Ad-Dahhak said: Ashroon is praising. Mujahid said: Angry and ignorant. So he was asked: What is Bartama? He said: Turning away.
53:62: 62. So prostrate to God and worship Him, meaning: worship Him. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musaddad told us, Abdul Warith told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated at the star, and the Muslims, the polytheists, the jinn, and mankind prostrated with him. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Nasr bin Ali told us, Abu Ahmad told me, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The first Surah in which a prostration was revealed was Al-Najm. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated, and those behind him prostrated, except for a man whom I saw take a handful of dirt and prostrate on it. I saw him after that killed as an unbeliever, and he was Umayya bin Khalaf. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam bin Abi Iyas told us, Ibn Abi Dhi’b told us, Yazid bin Abdullah bin Qusayt told us on the authority of Ata bin Yasar on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, who said: I recited to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, By the star, and he did not prostrate in it. I said: This is evidence that prostration of recitation is not obligatory. Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said: God did not prescribe it for us unless we wished. This is the opinion of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Some people said that prostration of recitation is obligatory for both the reader and the listener, which is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion.
54:1: 1. Meccan, The Hour has drawn near, “The Day of Resurrection has drawn near,” and the moon has split. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Abdul Wahhab told us, Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Saeed bin Abi Aruba told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, “The people of Mecca asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon in two halves until they saw Hira between them.” Shaiban said on the authority of Qatada: He showed them the splitting of the moon twice. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musaddad told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Shu’bah and Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The moon split into two parts during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one part above the mountain and one part below it. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Bear witness.’” Abu Al-Dhaha said on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Abdullah who said: The moon split in Mecca. Muqatil said: The moon split and then reconstituted after that. Abu Al-Dhaha narrated on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Abdullah who said: [The moon split during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace], and the Quraysh said: Ibn Abi Kabsha has bewitched you, so ask Al-Safa’u. So they asked them, and they said: Yes, we have seen it. Then God Almighty revealed: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split.
54:2: 2. And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, ‘Persistent magic,’ meaning: it is going and will go away and be nullified, from their saying: The thing passed or continued if it went away, like their saying: It fled and settled. This is the saying of Mujahid and Qatadah. Abu Al-Aaliyah [and Al-Dahhak] said: Continuous means: strong and intense, it overcomes all magic, from their saying: The rope passed if it became stiff and strong, and I made it pass if you twisted it tightly, and The thing continued if it became strong and firm.
54:3: 3. And they denied and followed their desires, meaning: they denied the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and what they witnessed of God's power, and they followed the falsehood that Satan made attractive to them. And every matter is settled, Al-Kalbi said: Every matter has a reality. Whatever of it is in this world will be made apparent, and whatever of it is in the Hereafter will be known. Qatada said: Every matter is settled, so good is settled with the people of good, [and evil is settled with the people of evil]. It was said: Every matter, good or evil, has a fixed destination. Goodness is settled with its people in Paradise, and evil is settled with its people in Hell. It was said: The statement of the believers and the disbelievers will be settled until they know its truth through reward. Muqatil said: Every hadith has an end. It was also said: Everything that is destined will inevitably happen. Abu Jaafar read mustaqar with a kasra on the ra’, but there is no basis for this.
54:4: 4. And there has certainly come to them, meaning: the people of Mecca, of report, of the report of the nations who denied the Qur’an, that in which there was a deterrent, [mutanahi], a verbal noun meaning deterrence, i.e., a prohibition and a sermon. It is said: I deterred him and I admonished him if you forbade him from evil, and its root is: muztajar, the ta’ was changed to a dal.
54:5: 5. A perfect wisdom, meaning: The Qur’an is a perfect wisdom that has reached its ultimate goal. So what use are warnings? It is possible that what is a negation, meaning: So warnings are of no use, or it is possible that it is a question, meaning: So what use are warnings if they disobey them and deny them? Like His statement: And what use are signs and warners for a people who do not believe? (Yunus 10:101). And the warnings is the plural of warner.
54:6: 6. Turn away from them, turn away from them, abrogated by the verse on fighting. It was said: Here is a complete stop. And it was said: Turn away from them on the Day the Caller calls, meaning: until the Day of the Caller. Muqatil said: He is Israfil blowing while standing on the rock of the Holy House, to something monstrous, [monstrous] terrible, they had never seen the like of it, so they would reject it out of awe. Ibn Kathir read: (nakar) with a sukoon on the kaf, and the others with a damma on it.
54:7: 7. Khashan absarhim, Abu Amr, Yaqub, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read: (Khashan) in the singular form, while the others read: (Khashan) - with a damma on the kha and a shaddah on the sheen - in the plural form. It is permissible for active participles to be singular or plural, masculine or feminine if they precede the plural. You say: I passed by men with handsome faces, handsome faces, and handsome faces. The poet said: And the men of good character are from Iyad bin Nizar bin Ma'ad In Abdullah’s reading: Their eyes will be humbled, meaning: submissive and submissive when they see the torment. They emerge from the graves, from the tombs, as if they were locusts scattered, scattered and confused. He mentioned the scattered in the word locusts, similar to it, as scattered moths, Al-Qari’ah 4. He meant that they emerge terrified, with no direction for any of them to go to, like locusts that have no direction, mixed together.
54:8: 8. Rushing, hurrying towards, to the caller, to the voice of Israfil, the disbelievers will say, ‘This is a difficult day’, a very difficult day.
54:9: 9. The Almighty said: Before them, the people of Noah denied, meaning before the people of Mecca, and they denied Our servant, Noah, and they said, ‘He is mad,’ and he was warned, meaning they warned him against his call and his statement with insults and threats, and they said: If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned Ash-Shu’ara’ 116. Mujahid said that the meaning of he was warned is: he was driven mad.
54:10: 10. “So Noah called upon his Lord and said, ‘I am overcome,’ ‘subdued,’ ‘so help,’ and take revenge on them for me.
54:11: 11. Then We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water, pouring down in a heavy flow that did not stop for forty days. Yaman said: It filled the space between heaven and earth.
54:12: 12. And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth, and the waters met, meaning the water of the sky and the water of the earth. Rather, He said: (and the waters met), and meeting does not occur from one person, but rather between two or more, because water can be plural and singular. Asim Al-Jahdary read: and the two full ones met. “according to a matter already decreed,” meaning: it was decreed for them in the matter of the Book. Muqatil said: God decreed that the two full ones would be equal, so they were as He decreed.
54:13: 13. And We carried him, meaning Noah, on planks and nails, meaning a ship with planks. He mentioned the adjective and left out the noun. He meant by planks the wide wood of the ship. And nails, meaning the nails that fasten the planks. The singular is dasar and dasir. It is said: you fastened the ship with nails. Al-Hasan said: The dasar is the front of the ship, so named because it pushes water with its bow, meaning it pushes. Mujahid said: They are the beams of the ship. It was also said: Its ribs. Ad-Dahhak said: The planks are its sides, and the dasar is its base and its two ends.
54:14: 14. "It runs under Our eyes," meaning: in Our sight. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "Under Our protection," and from this is their saying to someone bidding farewell: "The eye of God is upon you." Sufyan said: "By Our command. A recompense for he who disbelieved," [Muqatil ibn Hayyan said] meaning: We did to him and them by saving Noah and drowning his people as a reward for he who disbelieved in him and rejected his command, and he is Noah, peace be upon him. It was said: "From means what," meaning: a recompense for his disbelief from the favors and blessings of God upon those whom He drowned, or a recompense for what he did to Noah and his companions. Mujahid read: "A recompense for he who disbelieved, with the kaf and the fa' open, meaning the drowning was a recompense for he who disbelieved in God and denied His Messenger.
54:15: 15. And We have left it, meaning: [the deed that] We did, as a sign, to be considered. It was also said: He meant the ship. Qatada said: God kept it [in Baqir Di] from the land of the Arabian Peninsula. As a lesson and a sign until the first of this nation looked to it. So is there any who will remember? meaning: someone who will remember, admonish, consider, and fear the punishment like theirs. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Naim told us, Zuhair told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq that he heard a man ask Al-Aswad about His statement: (Is there anyone who will remember?) or a reminder? He said: I heard Abdullah recite it (Is there anyone who will remember?), and he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite it (Is there anyone who will remember?) with a dal.
54:16: 16. How was my punishment and my warning? That is, my warning. Al-Farra' said: Warning and warning are two sources. The Arabs say: I warned with warning and vow, like their saying: I spent spending and spending, and I was certain of certainty and certainty. The noun was used in place of the source.
54:17: 17. And We have certainly made easy, made easy, the Qur’an for remembrance, so that one may remember and consider it. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: We made it easy for memorization and recitation, and none of the Books of God can be read in their entirety outwardly except the Qur’an. So is there any who will remember? taking heed from its admonitions.
54:18: 18. The people of 'Aad denied, so how was My punishment and My warnings?
54:19: 19. Indeed, We sent upon them a furious wind, a violent blow, on a day of continuous misfortune, a severe and permanent omen, which continued upon them for about a year, and did not leave a single one of them without destroying him. It was said: It was on Wednesday at the end of the month.
54:20: 20. It pulls people out, it uproots them and then throws them on their heads, breaking their necks. It was narrated that it pulled people out of their graves, as if they were palm trunks. Ibn Abbas said: its roots. Ad-Dahhak said: palm trunks. Hollowed out, [cut off] from its place, fallen to the ground. The singular of ajaz is ajaz, like udhud and adhdad. Rather, he said: ajaz nukhil which are the roots whose branches were cut off, because the wind separated their heads from their bodies, so their bodies were left without heads.
54:21: 21. How then was my punishment and my warnings?
54:22: 22. And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
54:23: 23. Thamud denied the warning, the warning that Salih brought them.
54:24: 24. They said, ‘Shall we follow a human being from among us, one of us?’ We are a large group and he is one. Then we would be in error, error and straying from the right path, and a Blaze. Ibn Abbas said: Torment. Al-Hasan said: Severe torment. Qatada said: Trouble, they say: Then we are in trouble and torment because of what is required of us in obeying Him. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: It is the plural of ‘air. Al-Farra’ said: Madness, it is said of a camel that is mad if it is light-headed and wanders aimlessly. Wahb said: Sa’ar means: far from the truth.
54:25: 25. Shall I cast the Reminder upon him? Shall I send down the Reminder as revelation, “from among us? Rather, he is a liar, an arrogant haughty man who wants to show off to us by claiming prophethood. (And evil) means: hilariousness and haughtiness. “They will know.” Ibn Amir and Hamza read: You will know, with a ta’, meaning that Salih said to them. The others read it with a ya’.
54:26: 26. God the Almighty says: They will know tomorrow, when the punishment descends upon them. Al-Kalbi said: It means the Day of Resurrection. The mention of tomorrow is for the sake of clarity, as people usually say: With today comes tomorrow, "from the most evil liar.
54:27: 27. Indeed, We will send the she-camel, meaning: We will send her out and take her out from the plateau for which they had asked. This was because they were stubborn with Salih, so they asked him to bring out for them from a rock a red, pregnant she-camel. So God Almighty said: Indeed, We will send the she-camel as a trial for them, as a trial and test for them. So watch them, so wait for what they will do, and be patient, and be patient in watching them, and it was said: in whatever harm befalls you.
54:28: 28. And inform them that the water is to be divided between them, and between the she-camel, one day for her and one day for them. Their prophet only said this because when the Arabs spoke about the prophet Adam and the animals, they used son of Adam over the animals. Every drink, a share of the water, is present, attended by whoever’s turn it is. So if it is her day, she attends her drink, and if it is their day, they attend their drink. Attend and attend have the same meaning. Mujahid said: It means they attend the water when the she-camel is absent, and when the she-camel comes, they attend the milk.
54:29: 29. They called their companion, who was Qadar bin Salaf, so he took up, so he grabbed the camel with his sword and hamstrung it, that is, he hamstrung it.
54:30: 30. How was My punishment and My warnings? Then He explained their punishment and said:
54:31: 31. Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast, Ata’ said: He meant the blast of Gabriel, peace be upon him, and they were like dry stubble, Ibn Abbas said: It is a man who makes a pen for his sheep from trees and thorns to keep them away from wild beasts, so whatever falls from that and the sheep trample it is the dry stubble. Ibn Zayd said: It is the old tree that has been shattered and scattered by the wind. The meaning is that they have become dry trees when they are shattered. The Arabs call everything that was moist and then dried up: hasheem. Qatada said: Like rotten, burnt bones. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the dust that scatters from a wall.
54:32: 32. And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?
54:33: 33. "The people of Lot denied the warning.
54:34: 34. “Indeed, We sent upon them a hurricane,” a wind that pelted them with pebbles, which are gravel. Ad-Dahhak said: It means small pebbles. It was also said: Hisba is a stone that is less than the size of a palm, and Hasib may also be the one who throws stones. In this case, the meaning is: We sent upon them a punishment that pelted them with stones, that is, it pelted them with stones. Then He made an exception and said: Except for the family of Lot, meaning Lot and his two daughters. We saved them, from the punishment, by magic.
54:35: 35. A blessing from Us, meaning: We made it a blessing from Us upon them when We saved them. Likewise, just as We bestowed blessings upon the family of Lot, We reward those who are grateful. Muqatil said: Whoever believes in the Oneness of God, We will not punish him along with the polytheists.
54:36: 36. And indeed, We warned them, Lot, of Our punishment, that is, We seized them with punishment, but they disputed about the warning, they doubted the warning and denied it and did not believe it.
54:37: 37. And indeed they tried to seduce him from his guest, they asked him to hand over his guests to them, so We blinded their eyes, that is, when they went to Lot’s house and knocked on the door to enter, the messengers said [to Lot]: Leave them alone and do not enter, for we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you. So they entered the house, and Gabriel slapped them with his wing by God’s permission, leaving them blind, wandering around in confusion, unable to find their way to the door. So Lot brought them out blind and unable to see. His statement: So We blinded their eyes means: We made them like the rest of the face, so that no slit could be seen in them. This is the statement of most of the commentators. Ad-Dahhak said: God blinded their eyes, so they did not see the messengers. They said: We saw them when we saw them when they entered the house, so where did they go? But they did not see them, so they returned. So taste My punishment and My warning, that is: [what Lot warned you of] of the punishment.
54:38: 38. And indeed, a lasting torment overtook them early in the morning, meaning, it came to them at dawn, a lasting torment, lasting and settled upon them until it led them to the torment of the Hereafter. It was also said: a true torment.
54:39: 39. So taste my torment and my warning.
54:40: 40. "And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?"
54:41: 41. And indeed, the warnings came to the people of Pharaoh, meaning Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them. It was said that they were the signs with which Moses warned them.
54:42: 42. They denied all Our signs, meaning the nine signs, so We seized them, with punishment, the seizure of the Mighty, the Victorious in His vengeance, the Powerful, the Able to destroy them, nothing is beyond His power. Then He frightened the people of Mecca and said:
54:43: 43. Are your disbelievers better than those? “Stronger and stronger than those upon whom I brought My vengeance from the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, the people of Lot, and the people of Pharaoh?” This is a question with the meaning of denial, i.e., they are not stronger than them. Or do you have immunity from the punishment in the scriptures that what happened to the previous nations will not happen to you.
54:44: 44. Or do they say, meaning the infidels of Mecca, We are all victorious, Al-Kalbi said: We are all victorious over our enemies, meaning: We are one hand against those who oppose us, victorious over those who oppose us, and he did not say victorious because the beginnings of the verses agree.
54:45: 45. God the Almighty said: The multitude will be routed. Jacob read: We will be routed with a nun. “The multitude” is accusative, while others read it with a ya and added a damma. The multitude is nominative without naming the subject, meaning: the infidels of Mecca. And they will turn their backs, meaning: their backs, so it was singularized for the sake of the beginnings of the verses, just as He said: We struck their heads if the singular conveys the meaning of the plural. God informed us that they would turn their backs in defeat, so God fulfilled His promise and defeated them on the Day of Badr. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Khalid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was in his tent on the day of Badr: O God, I ask You by Your covenant and Your promise. O God, if You will, You will not be worshipped after today. Abu Bakr took his hand and said: That is enough, O Messenger of God, for you have insisted upon your Lord - and he was in his armor. So he went out saying: The army will be defeated and they will turn their backs.”
54:46: 46. Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more grievous and bitter. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: I heard Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: When the verse, The hosts will be routed and they will turn their backs, was revealed, I did not know which hosts would be routed. Then, on the day of Badr, I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, jumping up in his armor and saying: “The hosts will be routed and they will turn their backs. Rather, the Hour is their appointed time,” all together, and the Hour is more grievous and bitter. A greater disaster and more bitter than the capture and killing on the day of Badr.
54:47: 47. Indeed, the criminals, i.e., polytheists, are in error and a Blaze. It was said: in error means far from the truth. Ad-Dahhak said: and a Blaze means a fire that is blazing upon them. It was also said: Misguidance means going astray from the path to Paradise in the Hereafter, and a Blaze means a blazing Fire. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Indeed, the criminals are in error in this world and in a Fire in the Hereafter. Qatada said: In hardship and torment.
54:48: 48. Then He explained their punishment, saying: The Day they will be dragged—they will be dragged—into the Fire on their faces, and it will be said to them: Taste the touch of Hellfire.
54:49: 49. Indeed, all things We have created with a measure, meaning: whatever We have created is predestined and written in the Preserved Tablet. Al-Hasan said: God has determined for each thing of His creation the measure that is appropriate for it. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Qurashi told us, Abu Muslim Ghalib ibn Ali al-Razi told us, Abu [Mashar] Ya’qub ibn Abd al-Jalil ibn Ya’qub told us, Abu Yazid Hatim ibn Mahbub told us, Ahmad ibn Nasr al-Naysaburi told us, Abdullah ibn al-Walid al-Adani told us, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Isma’il al-Sahmi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn ‘Ibad al-Makhzumi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to dispute with him about predestination, so this verse was revealed: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness until His saying: Indeed, We have created all things with predestination. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni told us, Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sharik al-Shafi’i al-Dukhdashi told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jurabadhi told us, Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la al-Sadfi told us, Abdullah ibn Wahb told us, Abu Hani’ al-Khawlani told me on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman [al-Habli] on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God wrote down the destinies of creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. He said: And His Throne was over the water.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Sa`d, on the authority of `Amr ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tawus al-Yamani, who said: I knew some people from among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Everything is by the decree of God. He said: I heard `Abdullah ibn `Umar, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Everything is by the decree, even impotence and intelligence, or intelligence and impotence. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim al-Shaybani told us, Ahmad ibn Hazim ibn Abi Gharzah told us, Ya`la ibn Ubayd told us, [and Ubaydullah] ibn Musa and Abu Nu`aym told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rib`i ibn Harash, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A servant does not truly believe until he believes in four things: he bears witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God, who was sent with the truth, he believes in resurrection after death, and he believes in predestination. [Ubaydullah] increased his good and his evil.” It was narrated by Abu Dawud on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Mansur, and he said: on the authority of Rub’i on the authority of Ali, and he did not say: on the authority of a man, and this is more authentic.
54:50: 50. And Our command is only one, like the blink of an eye. His saying, one, refers to the meaning, not the wording, that is: And Our command is only one time. It was said: Its meaning is: And Our command for a thing when We want to create it is only one word: Be, and it is, without questioning it, like the blink of an eye. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means that My judgment regarding My creation is faster than the blink of an eye. Al-Kalbi said on his authority: And Our command for the coming of the Hour is not quick except like the blink of an eye.
54:51: 51. And We have certainly destroyed your followers, those who were similar to you and your counterparts in disbelief among the previous nations. Is there anyone who will remember?, who will take heed and know that this is true, so he will fear and take heed.
54:52: 52. And everything they did, meaning what the followers did, good and evil, is in the scriptures, in the book of the guardians, and it was said: in the Preserved Tablet.
54:53: 53. “And every small and great thing,” of creation, their deeds, and their lives, is written down, is written: it is said: I wrote down, I wrote down, I wrote down, and I wrote down.
54:54: 54. Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens, orchards, and rivers, meaning rivers. It is singular for the sake of the beginnings of the verses, and he meant the rivers of Paradise of water, wine, milk, and honey. Ad-Dahhak said: meaning in light and spaciousness, and from this comes the word day. Al-A’raj read it as and river, with two dhammahs, the plural of day, meaning: a day with no night for them.
54:55: 55. In a seat of truth, in a council of truth in which there is no idle talk or sin, with a powerful King, a powerful King who is not incapable of anything. [Ja’far] al-Sadiq said: God praised the place for truthfulness, so only the people of truth sit in it.
55:1: 1. Meccan, The Most Gracious. It was said that it was revealed when they said: Who is the Most Gracious? And it was also said that it is an answer to the people of Mecca when they said: Only a human being knows Him.
55:2: 2. He taught the Qur’an. Al-Kalbi said: He taught Muhammad the Qur’an. It was also said: He taught the Qur’an made it easy to remember.
55:3: 3. He created man, meaning Adam, peace be upon him. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said, He taught him eloquence, the names of everything. It was also said that He taught him all languages, and Adam spoke seven hundred [thousand] languages, the best of which was Arabic. Others said: Human is a generic name, and he meant all people.
55:4: 4. He taught him eloquence means speaking, writing, understanding, and making others understand, until he knew what to say and what was said to him. This is the opinion of Abu Al-Aliyah, Ibn Zayd, and Al-Hasan. Al-Saddī said: He taught every people their own language. Ibn Kaysan said: He created man meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He taught him eloquence meaning: eloquence of what was and what will be, because he was eloquent [about] the first and the last and about the Day of Judgment.
55:5: 5. The sun and the moon move by precise calculation, Mujahid said: Like the calculation of a millstone. Someone else said: That is, they move according to calculation and stations that they do not exceed, as said by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. Ibn Zayd and Ibn Kaysan said: He means that times and fates are calculated by them. Were it not for the night and the day and the sun and the moon, no one would know how to calculate anything. Ad-Dahhak said: They move according to measured calculation, and calculation is the source of hasabat hisaban and hisban, like al-ghufaran and al-kufr, and al-rajhan and al-nisaa’. It can also be the plural of hasab like as-shahaban and al-rukban.
55:6: 6. And the star and the tree prostrate themselves. A star is a plant that does not have a stem, and a tree is a plant that has a stem that remains in the winter. Their prostration is a prostration of their injustice, as He said: They spread their shadows to the right and the left, prostrating to God. (al-Nahl 16:48) Mujahid said: A star is a planet, and its prostration is its rising.
55:7: 7. And the heaven He raised, above the earth, and placed the balance, Mujahid said: By the balance He meant justice. The meaning is: He commanded justice, as indicated by the Almighty’s statement:
55:8: 8. That you do not transgress in the balance, meaning: do not exceed justice. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ad-Dahhak said: He meant by it that which is weighed to achieve fairness and equity. The origin of the word weight is to estimate that you do not transgress, meaning lest you tilt, wrong, or exceed the truth in the balance.
55:9: 9. And establish weight in justice, in fairness. Abu Darda and Ata’ said: It means establish the tongue of the scale in justice. Ibn Uyaynah said: Establishing is with the hand and justice is with the heart. And do not defraud, and do not reduce the balance, and do not cheat in measuring and weight.
55:10: 10. And the earth He laid out for all creatures, for the creation He spread out in it.
55:11: 11. In it is fruit, meaning: all kinds of fruits. Ibn Kaysan said: It means: what they enjoy of the countless blessings. And palm trees with sheaths, the vessels in which the fruit is because the fruit of the palm tree is in a sheath as long as it has not split open. The singular is kam, and everything that we wrap around something is a kam and kammah, and from this comes the sleeve of the shirt. The skullcap is also called kammah. Ad-Dahhak said: With sheaths means with sheaths. Al-Hasan said: Its sheaths: its wrappings. [Ibn Zayd said: It is the date palm before it splits open.]
55:12: 12. And the grain with husks, by grain he meant all the grains that are plowed in the earth. Mujahid said: It is the leaves of the crop. Ibn Kaysan said: (The husk) is the leaves of everything from which the grain emerges. It first appears as leaves, which are the husks, then it becomes stalks, then God creates sleeves in it, then He creates the grain in the sleeves. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Al-Walibi: It is straw. This is the saying of Ad-Dahhak and Qatada. Atiyyah said about it: It is the green leaves of the crop when its heads are cut off and it dries up. Similar to: like eaten-up straw (al-Fil 105:5). And basil means provision, according to the majority of scholars. Ibn Abbas said: Every basil mentioned in the Qur’an is provision. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: It is your fragrant basil. Ad-Dahhak said: The straw is hay. And basil is its fruit. The general reading is: (and the grain with husks and basil), all of them are nominative in response to the fruit. Ibn Amir read (and the grain with husks and basil) with the accusative of the ba and the nun and dha with the alif meaning: He created man and created these things. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read (the basil) with the genitive in apposition to the husks, so he mentioned the sustenance of people and livestock, then he addressed the jinn and humans and said:
55:13: 13. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? O two heavy burdens, he means by these things that are mentioned. And He repeated this verse in this surah to confirm the blessing and emphasize the reminder of it, according to the Arabs' custom of conveying and satisfying. He enumerates the blessings of God to the creation, and separates between each two blessings with what alerts them to them, like the saying of a man who did good to him and continued to do him favors while he denies and is ungrateful: Weren't you poor and I made you rich, so would you deny this? Weren't you naked and I clothed you, so would you deny this? Weren't you idle and I gave you honor, so would you deny this? Repetition like this is common in the speech of the Arabs and is a good confirmation. It was said: He addressed someone in the dual form, as is the custom of the Arabs to address one person in the dual form, as in the Almighty’s saying: Throw them both into Hell Qaf 50:24. It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surah al-Rahman to us until he finished it, then he said: Why do I see you remaining silent to the jinn? They were better at responding than you. I never recited this verse to them, ‘Which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?’ except that they said: ‘Nor do we deny any of Your favors, our Lord. To You be praise.’”
55:14: 14. He created man from clay like pottery.
55:15: 15. And He created the jinn, meaning the father of the jinn. Ad-Dahhak said: He is Iblis. From a smokeless flame, meaning the pure flame of fire that has no smoke in it. Mujahid said: It is the red, yellow, and green flames that mix together and rise above the fire when it is lit, from their saying: The matter of the people has mixed, meaning it has become mixed.
55:16: 16. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:17: 17. Lord of the two Easts, the East of summer and the East of winter. And Lord of the two Wests, the West of summer and the West of winter.
55:18: 18. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:19: 19. He merged the two seas, the fresh and the salty. He sent them and made them meet together.
55:20: 20. Between them is a barrier, a barrier from the power of God Almighty, they do not transgress, they do not mix or change, and neither of them transgresses against the other. Qatada said: They do not oppress people by drowning. Al-Hasan said: (The two seas meet) the Roman Sea and the Indian Ocean, and you are the barrier between them. Qatada also said: The Persian Gulf and the Roman Sea are between them is a barrier, meaning the islands. Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: The sea of the sky and the sea of the earth meet every year.
55:21: 21. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:22: 22. It emerges from them. The people of Medina and Basra read it as (يخرج)) with a damma on the yaa and a fatha on the raa. Others read it with a fatha on the yaa and a damma on the raa, pearls and coral. It only emerges from salty waters, not fresh water. This is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, to mention two things and then specify one of them with a verb, as God Almighty said: {O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?} Al-An`am 6:130. The messengers were from mankind, not the jinn. Some of them said it emerges from sky water and sea water. Ibn Jurayj said: When it rains, the sky opens its mouths, and wherever a drop falls, there is a pearl. Pearl is the largest pearl, and coral is its small ones. Muqatil and Mujahid said the opposite of this. It was said: (marjan) is the red beads. Ata’ Al-Khurasani said: It is ease.
55:23: 23. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:24: 24. And to Him belong the ships, the large ships, the installations, Hamza and Abu Bakr read: (the installations) with a kasra on the sheen, meaning: the installations for traveling [meaning those who initiated and established the travel]. The others read it with a fatha on the sheen, meaning the raised ones, and they are the ones whose wood is raised one on top of the other. It was said: they are the ships whose sail is raised, but as for what does not raise its sail, it is not from the installations. It was said: the creatures that are subservient, in the sea like flags, like mountains, the plural of flag, which is a tall mountain. He likened the ships in the sea to the mountains on land.
55:25: 25. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:26: 26. Everything on it, meaning on the earth, of animals will perish.
55:27: 27. And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty, Owner of Greatness and Pride, and Honor, Honoring His prophets and saints with His kindness along with His Majesty and Greatness.
55:28: 28. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:29: 29. Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him, from angels, humans, and jinn. Qatada said, The people of the heavens and the earth cannot do without Him. Ibn Abbas said, The people of the heavens ask Him for forgiveness, and the people of the earth ask Him for mercy [and provision, repentance, and forgiveness]. Muqatil said, The people of the earth ask Him for provision and forgiveness, and the angels also ask Him for provision and forgiveness for them. “Every day He has a matter to do.” Muqatil said: It was revealed about the Jews when they said that God does not decree anything on the Sabbath. The commentators said: It is His nature to give life and death, to provide sustenance, to honor some people and humiliate others, to heal the sick, to free the suffering and relieve the distressed, to answer the supplicant, to give to the beggar, to forgive sins, and to countless other actions and to bring about in His creation whatever He wills. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdus Al-Muzaki told us - by dictation - Abu Hamid Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Bazzar told us, Yahya bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Makki told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Abu Hamza Al-Thamali told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Among what God, the Almighty, created is a tablet of white pearl, its two covers are red rubies, its pen is light and its writing is light. God, the Almighty, looks at it three hundred and sixty times every day, creating and providing, giving life and causing death, honoring and humiliating, and God does what He wills. This is what He says: Every day He is concerned with a matter. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: All of time with God is two days, one of which is the duration of the days of this world and the other is the Day of Resurrection. The affair that He is in on the day, which is the duration of this world, is informing of commands and prohibitions, giving life and death, giving and withholding. The affair of the Day of Resurrection is recompense and accounting, reward and punishment. It was said: His affair, may He be glorified, is that three armies emerge every day and night: an army from the loins of the fathers to the wombs of the mothers, an army from the wombs to the world, and an army from the world to the graves. Then they all travel to God Almighty. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: It is the transfer of destinies to their appointed times. Abu Sulayman al-Darani said about this verse: Every day is a new day for the slaves.
55:30: 30. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:31: 31. We will devote ourselves to you, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: We will devote ourselves to you, with a ya because of His saying: He is asked by whoever is in the heavens and the earth, “And the Face of your Lord will remain,” And to Him belongs the neighborhood, so he followed the report. Others read it with the letter nun, and what is meant by it is not freeing oneself from one occupation, because God Almighty is not distracted by one matter from another, but rather it is a threat from God Almighty [to creation] of accountability, like the saying of the one who says, I will devote myself to you, and I have no occupation. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas and Al-Dahhak, and this freeing up is good because the matter was mentioned previously. Others said: Its meaning is: We will approach you after leaving and delaying and we will take action on your matter, like someone saying to someone who has nothing to do: You are free for me. Some of them said: God promised the people of piety and threatened piety and threatened the people of immorality, then He said: We will complete for you what We promised you and informed you of, so we will hold you to account and reward you and fulfill for you what We promised you, so that is completed and completed, and this is what Al-Hasan and Muqatil held. O you two heavy things, meaning the jinn and mankind, they are called two heavy things because they are a burden on the earth, both the living and the dead. God Almighty said: And the earth will cast forth its burdens, Al-Zalzalah 2. Some of the scholars of semantics said: Everything that has a value and weight in which it competes is a burden. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am leaving among you two heavy things: the Book of God and my family,” so he made them two heavy things out of respect for their value. Jaafar bin Muhammad Al-Sadiq said: The jinn and mankind were called Thaqalayn because they are burdened with sins.
55:32: 32. "Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:33: 33. O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass through, that is, cross and exit, from the regions of the heavens and the earth, that is, from their sides and edges, then pass through, meaning if you are able to escape from death by exiting from the regions of the heavens and the earth, then flee and exit from them. [The meaning]: Wherever you are, death will overtake you, as the Most High said: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you An-Nisa’ 4:78. It was also said: It will be said to them on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:If you are able to pass through the regions of the heavens and the earth and defeat your Lord so that He is not able to overpower you, then pass through, for dominion, power, and argument are all authority, meaning wherever you go, you will be in My dominion and authority. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Its meaning is: If you are able to know what is in the heavens and the earth, then know, for you will not know it except with authority, that is, with clear proof from God, the Almighty. It was said that his saying: (except with authority) means to an authority, like his saying: He has treated me well (Yusuf 12:100), meaning to me.
55:34: 34. "Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" And in the hadith: The creation will be surrounded by angels and a tongue of fire, then they will call out: "O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass through," the verse. So that is what the Almighty said:
55:35: 35. He will send down upon you a flame of fire. Ibn Kathir read it as Shawaaz with a kasra over the seen and others read it with a damma. They are two dialects, like Sawar from cows and Sawar. It is the flame that has no smoke. This is the opinion of most of the commentators. Mujahid said: It is the green flame that comes out of the fire. And copper. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read and copper with a genitive seen in apposition to fire. The rest read it with a damma over both of them in apposition to shawaaz. Saeed bin Jabero Al-Kalbi said: An-Nahhas means smoke. This is the narration of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The meaning of the nominative is that He sends upon you flames and sends copper, that is, He sends this one time and this one another, and it is permissible to send it together without one of them mixing with the other, and whoever breaks it with the conjunction to the fire is weak because it is not flames of copper, so it is permissible for it to be estimated as: flames of fire and something of copper, on the basis that it has been narrated that flames are only from fire and smoke together. Mujahid and Qatada said: Copper is molten brass poured over their heads. This is the narration of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abdullah ibn Masoud said: Copper is molten brass. "Do not be victorious, meaning do not resist God and do not have anyone to help you with Him.
55:36: 36. "Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:37: 37. Then when the heaven is split open, [opened], and becomes doors for the angels to descend, “and it will be rose-colored like oil, meaning like the color of a rose-colored horse, which is white that tends toward red and yellow. Qatada said: Today it is green, and it will have another color that is reddish. It was said: On that day, it will change colors like the color of a rose horse, which will be yellow in spring and red in winter, and when winter becomes intense, it will be dusty. So the sky was likened in its color when it splits to this horse in its color. Kaldahan, plural of dahan. He likened the color of the sky to the color of the rose among horses, and he likened the rose in its different colors to oil and its different colors, which is the opinion of Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ar-Rabi'. Muqatil said: Like pure rose oil. Ibn Jurayj said: The sky will become like melting oil when the heat of Hell hits it. Al-Kalbi said: Like paint, meaning like red leather. The plural is adhan and dahn.
55:38: 38. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:39: 39. On that Day, no human being or jinn will be asked about his sin. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: They will not be asked about their sins so that they will be known from their side, because God Almighty knew them from them, and the angels wrote them down for them. This is the narration of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was also narrated from him that the angels do not question the criminals because they know them by their marks. The evidence for this is what follows, and this is the statement of Mujahid. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the reconciliation between this verse and His statement: By your Lord, We will surely question them all (al-Hijr 15:92), he said: He will not ask them, Did you do such and such? because He knows more about that than they do, but He will ask them, Why did you do such and such? And on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: These are situations in which He will ask about some of them and not ask about others. On the authority of Ibn Abbas also: They do not ask a question of compassion and mercy, but rather they ask a question of rebuke and reprimand. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Only the criminal is asked about the sin of the criminal.
55:40: 40. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:41: 41. The criminals will be known by their mark, which is the blackness of their faces and the blueness of their eyes, as the Almighty said: On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black (Al Imran 3:106). Then they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet, the feet will be brought together to the forelocks from behind and they will be thrown into the Fire.
55:42: 42. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:43: 43. Then it will be said to them: This is Hell, which the criminals deny, the polytheists.
55:44: 44. They will circulate between it and scalding water, which is boiling hot. Al-Zajjaj said: Whenever it comes, it is boiling hot. The meaning is that they will walk between Hell and scalding water, but when they seek help from the heat of the Fire, their torment will be made into scalding water that has become like molten brass. This is His statement: And if they seek help, they will be relieved with water like molten brass. (al-Kahf 18:29) Ka’b Al-Ahbar said: ‘Aan’ is a valley from the valleys of Hell in which the pus of the people of Hell will collect, and they will be thrown into that valley until their joints are dislocated. Then they will emerge from it and God, the Most High, will have created a new creation for them, and they will be thrown into the Fire. This is His statement: They will circulate between it and scalding water, which is boiling hot.
55:45: 45. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? Everything that God Almighty mentioned from His saying: Everything on it will perish until here is admonition, warning, and intimidation. All of that is a blessing from God Almighty, because it deters from sins. That is why He concluded every verse with His saying: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? Then He mentioned what He has prepared for whoever fears Him and is wary of Him, saying:
55:46: 46. And for him who fears the position of his Lord, meaning: his position before his Lord for the reckoning, so he abandons sin and desire. It was also said: his Lord’s standing over him, as explained in His statement: Is he who stands over every soul for what it has earned? (al-Ra’d 13:33). Ibrahim and Mujahid said: He is the one who intends to commit a sin, then remembers God and abandons it out of fear of God. Two Gardens, Muqatil said: The Garden of Eden and the Garden of Delight. Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi said: A Garden for his fear of his Lord and a Garden for his abandoning his desires. Ad-Dahhak said: This is for the one who observes God in secret and in public, with knowledge of what is forbidden to him and what he abandons out of fear of God, and what good he does and brings it to God, and he does not like anyone to know about it. Qatada said: The believers feared that situation, so they worked for God and persevered day and night. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Qurashi told us, Abu Muslim Ghalib ibn Ali al-Razi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Yunus told us, Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Musa ibn `Isa al-Halwani told us, and Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Hamadhani told us, Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Abu `Aqil, who is al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Yazid ibn Sinan, I heard Bakir ibn Fayruz say, I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Whoever fears should set out early, and whoever sets out early will reach his destination. Beware, God’s merchandise is expensive. Beware, God’s merchandise is Paradise.” Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jafar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Harmalah, the client of Huwaytib bin Abdul-Uzza, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, “That he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating from the pulpit, saying: ‘For he who fears standing before his Lord are two Paradises.’ I said: ‘Even if he commits adultery and steals, O Messenger of God?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And for he who fears standing before his Lord are two Paradises.’ I said the second time: ‘Even if he commits adultery and steals, O Messenger of God?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Thirdly, ‘For he who fears standing before his Lord are two Paradises.’ I said the third time: ‘Even if he commits adultery and steals, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘Even if he commits adultery and steals,’ in spite of Abu Al-Darda’s disdain.”
55:47: 47. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny? Then he described the two gardens and said:
55:48: 48. With branches, twigs, the singular of which is fann, which is a straight branch in length. This is the opinion of Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Al-Kalbi. Ikrimah said: The shade of the branches on the walls. Al-Hasan said: With shadows. Ibn Abbas said: Colors. Saeed bin Jubayr and Ad-Dahhak said: Colors of fruit, the singular of which is fann from their saying afnan so-and-so in his hadith if he took on various kinds and types of it. Ata’ combined the two opinions and said: On every branch there are various kinds of fruit. Qatada said: With excess and spaciousness over everything else.
55:49: 49. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:50: 50. In them are two flowing springs, Ibn Abbas said: with honor and extra for the people of Paradise. Al-Hasan said: They flow with clear water, one of them is Al-Tasnim and the other is Al-Salsabil. Atiyah said: One of them is of fresh water and the other is of wine, a delight for those who drink it.
55:51: 51. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:52: 52. In them are pairs of every kind of fruit, two kinds and two types. It was said that its meaning is that in them are two kinds of everything that is enjoyed, fresh and dry. Ibn Abbas said: There is no sweet or bitter fruit in this world that is not in Paradise, not even the colocynth, except that it is sweet.
55:53: 53. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:54: 54. Reclining on mattresses, plural of mattress, its linings, plural of batana, which is under the outer layer. Al-Zajjaj said: It is what is closest to the ground. Of brocade, which is thick brocade. Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah said: These are the linings, so what do you think of the outer layers? It was said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: The linings are of brocade, so what are the outer layers? He said: This is from what God the Almighty said: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes (al-Sajdah 32:17), and it was also narrated from him: Their linings are of brocade, so their outer layers are of solid light. Ibn Abbas said: He described the linings and left out the outer layers because there is no one on earth who knows what the outer layers are. And the fruits of the two gardens are within reach. The harvest is what is gathered from the fruits. He means: its fruit is within reach and can be reached by those standing, sitting, and sleeping. Ibn Abbas said: The tree will come near so that a friend of God can gather it, whether standing or sitting. Qatada said: He will not turn their hands away from it after that, nor will he have thorns.
55:55: 55. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:56: 56. In them are those who lower their gaze, lowering their eyes, they lower their gaze to their husbands, they do not look at anyone but them and they do not desire anyone but them. Ibn Zayd said: She says to her husband: By the glory of my Lord, I do not see anything in Paradise more beautiful than you, so praise be to God who made you my husband and made me your wife. He did not have sexual intercourse with them, he did not have sexual intercourse with them or [have sexual intercourse with them]. Its root is from tamat, which means blood, and from it the menstruating woman is called taamith, as if he said: she did not have sexual intercourse with them, No human being before them or jinn, Al-Zajjaj said: This is evidence that the jinn overpowers the same way humans overpower. Mujahid said: If a man has sexual intercourse and does not say Bismillah, the jinn will wrap themselves around his urethra and have sexual intercourse with him. Muqatil said regarding his statement: No human or jinn has touched them before them, because they were created in Paradise. So based on his statement: These are from the houris of Paradise. Al-Sha’bi said: They are women of this world who have not been touched since they were created. This is what Al-Kalbi said, meaning: They have not been touched, so in this creation in which they were created there is neither a human nor a jinn. Talha bin Masraf read: He did not touch them with a dammah on the meem in both of them. Al-Kisa’i read one of them with a dammah, and if he pronounced the first with a kasrah, he pronounced the second with a dammah, and if he pronounced the first with a dammah, he pronounced the second with a kasrah, because of what Ishaq al-Sabi’i narrated, saying: I used to pray behind the companions of Ali, may God be pleased with him, and I would hear them recite: lam yatmuthunna, with the nominative case. I used to pray behind the companions of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud and I would hear them recite with a kasrah on the meem. Al-Kisa’i would pronounce one of them with a dammah and the other with a kasrah, so as not to deviate from these two traditions.
55:57: 57. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:58: 58. As if they were rubies and coral. Qatada said: The purity of the ruby is in the whiteness of the coral. We narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed in describing the people of Paradise, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Every man among them will have two wives, and each wife will have seventy garments of clothing. He will see the marrow of their shins, but not their flesh, blood, or skin.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, Abu Al-Zinad Al-Araj told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first group to enter Paradise will be like the moon on a full moon night, and those who follow them will be like the brightest shining star. Their hearts will be like the heart of one man. There will be no disagreement or hatred between them. Every man among them will have two wives, each of whom the marrow of her shin will be seen through her flesh because of her beauty. They glorify God morning and evening. They do not get sick, nor do they urinate or defecate, nor do they spit or blow their noses. Their utensils are gold and silver, their combs are gold, the fuel for their incense burners is Aloe vera, and their sweat is musk.” Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Harun bin Muhammad bin Harun told us, Hazim bin Yahya Al-Halwani told us, Suhayl bin Uthman Al-Askari told us, Ubaidah bin Hamid told us, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The whiteness of a woman from the people of Paradise can be seen from behind seventy garments of silk, and her marrow. God Almighty says: ‘As if they were rubies and coral.’ As for the ruby, it is a stone. If you were to insert a wire into it and then purify it, you would see it from behind it.” Amr bin Maimun said: A woman from the Houris will wear seventy garments, and the marrow of her leg will be seen from behind her, just as a red drink can be seen from a white bottle.
55:59: 59. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:60: 60. Is the reward for good [anything] but good? That is, what is the reward for someone who does good in this world except that he will be treated well in the Hereafter. Ibn Abbas said: Is the reward for someone who says, There is no god but God and acts in accordance with what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought anything but Paradise? Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told us, [Ibn Shaybah] told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Bahram told us, Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf Al-Maktab told us, Bishr bin Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Adi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Is the reward for good [anything] but good? Then he said: Do you know what your Lord has said? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “He says: Is the reward of one upon whom You have bestowed favor by making him a monotheist [believer] but Paradise?”
55:61: 61. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:62: 62. And below them are two gardens, meaning below the first two gardens are two other gardens. Ibn Abbas said: Below them in rank. Ibn Zayd said: Below them in excellence. Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari said: Two gardens of gold for the foremost and two gardens of silver for the followers. Ibn Jurayj said: They are four gardens for the close ones, the foremost, in them are two pairs of every kind of fruit, and two gardens for the companions of the right hand and the followers. In them are fruits and palm trees and pomegranates. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ali bin Abdullah told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdul Samad told us, on the authority of Abu Imran, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Qais, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Two gardens of silver, their vessels and what is in them, and two gardens of gold, their vessels and what is in them. And nothing stands between the people and their seeing their Lord except the cloak of majesty over His face in the Garden of Eden.” Al-Kisa’i said: And below them are two gardens, meaning in front of them and before them. This is indicated by the words of Al-Dahhak: The first two gardens are of gold and silver, and the last two are of rubies.
55:63: 63. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:64: 64. Mudahamtan, two soft black ones from their Lord and the intensity of their greenness, because when the greenness is intense it turns to black. It is said: the crop is idham if blackness covers it with watering it, then it is mudham.
55:65: 65. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:66: 66. In them are two gushing springs, gushing with water that never stops. (And the gushing): the gushing of water from the spring. Ibn Abbas said: They gush with goodness and blessings for the people of Paradise. Ibn Masoud said: They gush with musk and camphor for the friends of God. Anas ibn Malik said: They gush with musk and ambergris in the homes of the people of Paradise like the pouring of rain.
55:67: 67. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:68: 68. In them are fruits, date palms, and pomegranates. Some of them said: Date palms and pomegranates are not among the fruits, and the general public agrees that they are among the fruits. Rather, the mention of date palms and pomegranates was repeated, and they are among the fruits, for the sake of specificity and detail, as God Almighty said: Whoever is an enemy to God and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael Al-Baqarah 2:98. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba informed us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith informed us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i informed us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud informed us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal informed us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The palm trees of Paradise have trunks of green emerald, their leaves are red gold, and their fronds are clothing for the people of Paradise, containing their provisions and their garments. Their fruit is like jugs or buckets, whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and softer than butter, without pits.
55:69: 69. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:70: 70. In them, meaning in the four gardens, are good and beautiful things. Al-Hasan narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: I said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell me about his saying: good and beautiful things. He said: Good morals and beautiful faces.
55:71: 71. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:72: 72. Houris who are confined and veiled, confined and covered in veils. It is said of a woman who is confined and short if she is secluded and covered and does not go out. Mujahid said: It means they restrain their gaze and themselves to their husbands and do not seek any replacement for them. We narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If a woman from the women of Paradise looked down upon the people of the earth, she would illuminate what is between the heavens and the earth and fill what is between them with fragrance. The veil of her hair on her head is better than the world and everything in it.” In the tents, plural of tent. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdul Samad told us, Imran Al-Joni told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Qais, on the authority of his father that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The believer will have a tent in Paradise made of a single hollow pearl, sixty miles wide, in each corner of which there will be people who do not see the others, and the believer will go around them."
55:73: 73. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:74: 74. No human or jinn has touched them before them.
55:75: 75. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:76: 76. Reclining on green cushions. Saeed bin Jubair said: Rafraf means the gardens of Paradise. Khadr means dyed. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, its singular is rafrafa. He said: Rafarif is the plural of plural. And say: Rafraf means carpets, and this is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Muqatil, and Al-Qurazi. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Rafraf means the excess seating and carpets. He said to Dahhak and Qatada: They are green seating areas above the mattresses. Ibn Kaysan said: They are the elbows. Ibn Uyaynah said: Carpets. Another said: Every wide garment among the Arabs is called Rafraf. Abqari Hassan refers to the thick carpets and rugs. It is a plural, the singular of which is abqariyya. Qatada said: (Abqari) is the old carpets. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is the velvet rugs that are very thin. Al-Qutaibi said: Every embroidered garment among the Arabs is abqari. Abu Ubaidah said: It is named after a land where embroidery is done. Al-Khalil said: Every noble, generous, and distinguished person among men and others is considered by the Arabs to be a genius. From this comes the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Omar, may God be pleased with him: I have never seen a genius who is more generous than him.
55:77: 77. Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:78: 78. Blessed be the name of your Lord, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor. The people of Ash-Sham read Possessor of Majesty with a waw, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an, based on the name. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni told us, Abu Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sharik al-Shafi’i told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, Abu Bakr al-Jurbudhi told us, Ahmad ibn Harb told us, Abu Mu’awiyah al-Dharee’ told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Aisha, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished the prayer, he would not hold his head longer than it took to say: “O God, You are peace and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honor.”
56:1: 1- When the Event occurs, when the Day of Resurrection takes place. It was also said: When the Cry of Resurrection descends, which is the final Trumpet blast.
56:2: 2- Its occurrence is not false, its coming, false, a lie, like His saying: You will not hear therein any idle talk (al-Ghashiyah 88:11), meaning: idle talk, meaning that it will happen truthfully and rightly. And false is a noun like health and calamity.
56:3: 3- Abasing and Raising, it lowers some people to Hell and raises others to Paradise. Ata' said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It lowers some people who were elevated in this world and raises some people who were weak in this world.
56:4: 4- When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking, it moves and quakes violently. Al-Kalbi said: When God inspires it, it trembles with fear. The commentators said: It shakes like a baby shakes in its cradle until every building collapses and everything on it, from mountains and other things, is broken. The root of shaking in the language is: movement. It is said: I shook it and it shook.
56:5: 5- And the mountains will be washed away, Ata', Muqatil and Mujahid said: They were crushed until they became like kneaded flour, which is wet. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Suddi said: They were broken completely. Al-Kalbi said: They were moved on the face of the earth. Al-Hasan said: They were uprooted and gone. Similar to this is: Then say, 'My Lord will blow it away with a blast' (Ta-Ha: 105). Ibn Kaysan said: It was made into a heap of sand after it had been tall and lofty.
56:6: 6- And it was scattered dust, scattered dust like that which is seen in a ray of sunshine when it enters a window, which is the dust.
56:7: 7- And you were pairs, types, three.
56:8: Then he explained it and said: 8- Then the companions of the right hand are those who will be taken to the right hand to Paradise. Ibn Abbas said: They are those who were on Adam’s right hand when the offspring were taken from his loins, and God said to them: These are in Paradise, and I do not care. Ad-Dahhak said: They are those who will be given their books in their right hands. Al-Hasan and Ar-Rabi’ said: They are those who were on the right hand and were blessed for themselves, and their lives were spent in obedience to God, and they are the followers in righteousness. Then his Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was amazed and said: Who are the companions of the right hand? This is like saying: Zaid, what Zaid! Meaning Zaid is strong.
56:9: 9- And the people of the left hand, what are the people of the left hand? meaning the people of the north, and the Arabs call the left hand the unlucky one, and from it the Levant and Yemen are called, because Yemen is to the right of the Kaaba and the Levant is to its north, and they are the ones who will be taken to the left to the Fire. Ibn Abbas said: They are the ones who were on Adam’s left when the offspring were brought out, and God said to them: These are in the fire, and I do not care. Ad-Dahhak said: They are those who are given their books in their left hands. Al-Hasan said: They are those who are ill-omened and spend their lives in sin.
56:10: 10- And the first foremost, the first. Ibn Abbas said: The first to emigrate are the first to be in the Hereafter. Ikrimah said: The first to embrace Islam. Ibn Sirin said: They are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs. His evidence is His statement: And the first foremost among the Muhajireen and the Ansar (al-Tawbah 9:100). Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: Those who are the first to respond to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this world are the first to enter Paradise in the Hereafter. Muqatil said: To the prophets’ response with faith. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: To the five daily prayers. Ad-Dahhak said: To jihad. Saeed bin Jubair said: They are those who hasten to repent and perform righteous deeds. God Almighty said: Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord (al-Hadid 57:21), And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord (Al Imran 3:133). Then he praised them and said: Those are the ones who hasten to do good deeds and are the first to do them. Ibn Kaysan said: And the first to do everything to which God has called. It was narrated on the authority of Ka'b that he said: They are the people of the Qur'an who will be crowned on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: They are the first to go to the mosque and the first to go out for the sake of God. Al-Qurazi said: To every good.
56:11: 11- Those are the ones brought near to God.
56:13: 13- A group of the ancients, meaning of the past nations from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, to the time of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. A group is an unlimited number of people.
56:14: 14- And a few of the others, meaning from this nation. Al-Zajjaj said: Those who saw all the prophets from Adam, peace be upon him, and believed them, are more than those who saw the Prophet, peace be upon him.
56:15: 15- On woven couches, woven like the rings of a shield are woven into one another. The commentators said: They are connected and woven with gold and jewels. Ad-Dahhak said: They are woven and arranged in rows.
56:16: 16- Reclining on them, facing each other, not looking at each other’s backs.
56:17: 17- They are served by two boys, young men, immortal, who do not die, grow old or change. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say about someone who has grown old and has not yet grown old: he is immortal. Ibn Kaysan said: It means children who do not change from one state to another. Saeed bin Jubair said: Maqrtun, it is said: he immortalized his slave girl if he adorned her with immortality, which is an earring. Al-Hasan said: They are the children of the people of this world. They have no good deeds for which they will be rewarded, nor bad deeds for which they will be punished, because there is no birth in Paradise, so they are the servants of the people of Paradise.
56:18: 18- With cups and pitchers. Cups are the plural of cup, and they are round-mouthed goblets with no spouts or handles. Pitchers are those with spouts, and they are called pitchers because of the luster of their clear color. And a cup from a flowing spring, running wine.
56:19: 19- They will not have a headache from it, their heads will not have a headache from drinking it, nor will they get a bloodbath, meaning they will not get drunk. This is if it is read with a fatha on the zay, and if it is a kasra, then its meaning is that their drink will not run out.
56:20: 20- And fruits of whatever they choose, they choose what they desire. It is said that you chose something if you took its best.
56:21: 21- And the meat of birds of whatever they desire. Ibn Abbas said that the meat of birds comes to his mind and becomes represented before him as he desires. It is said that it falls on the man’s plate and he eats from it what he desires and then it flies away.
56:22: 22- And wide-eyed houris, Abu Ja`far, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read it with a kasra on the ra’ and the noon, meaning: And wide-eyed houris, followed by His saying: with cups and pitchers, “and fruit of whatever they choose * and the flesh of birds” in the parsing, even though they differ in meaning, because the wide-eyed houris are not to be walked around, like the poet’s saying: If the prostitutes appear one day and raise their eyebrows and eyes The eye is not glazed, but it is lined with kohl, and there are many examples. It was said that its meaning is that they will be honored with fruits, the meat of birds, and beautiful, wide-eyed maidens. The rest read it in the nominative case, meaning: And there will circulate among them fair women. Al-Akhfash said: It is in the nominative case, meaning they will have fair women, and in his interpretation it says: Fair women with white, large eyes.
56:23: 23- Like hidden pearls, stored in shells that have not been touched by hands. It is narrated that a light shines in Paradise. They said: What is this? They said: The light of the lips of a houri who smiled in her husband’s face. It is narrated that when Al-Hawra’ walks, the glorification of the anklets on her legs and the praise of the bracelets on her arms can be heard. If she wears a ruby necklace, her throat laughs. On her feet are golden sandals with pearl straps that ring with glorification.
56:24: 24- "As a reward for what they used to do.
56:25: 25- They will hear therein no idle talk or sinful speech.
