56:26: 26- Except a little, meaning a word: "Peace, peace", they are in the accusative case following his saying a little meaning they hear peace, peace. Ata' said: They greet each other with peace.
56:27: Then he mentioned the companions of the right and was amazed at their condition, so He, the Most High, said: 27- And the companions of the right hand - what are the companions of the right hand?
56:28: 28- In thornless lote trees, free of thorns, as if its thorns had been pruned, i.e., cut and removed. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah. Al-Hasan said: It does not harm hands. Ibn Kaysan said: It is that which has no harm in it. He said: None of the fruits of Paradise are uncircumcised as are the fava beans and other fruits in this world. Rather, all of them are eaten, drunk, smelled, and looked at. Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid said: It is the one that is laden with fruit. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: Its fruits are larger than jugs. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Ad-Dahhak said: The Muslims looked at Wajj - which is a fertile valley in Taif - and were amazed by its lote trees, and they said: Would that we had something like this. Then God revealed this verse.
56:29: 29- And Talh, meaning banana, its singular is Talha, according to most commentators. Al-Hasan said: It is not a banana, but rather a tree that provides cool, pleasant shade. Al-Farra' and Abu Ubaidah said: Talh, among the Arabs, is a large tree with thorns. Mujalid narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saad that he said: A man read in the presence of Ali, may God be pleased with him, from him: And bananas in layers. He said: What is the matter with bananas? It is: A layered banana. Then he read: Its ripe fruit. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, it is in the scriptures with a ha. Why don’t you change it? He said: The Qur’an is neither disputed nor changed today. The piled-up, stacked fruit that has been loaded from beginning to end has no prominent stem. Masruq said: The trees of Paradise, from their roots to their branches, are all fruitful.
56:30: 30- And an extended shadow, eternal and unbroken by the sun. The Arabs say of something that is never interrupted: extended. Abu Ali Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Taher Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah told us, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: and an extended shade, he said: A tree in Paradise on a trunk to which the people of Paradise go out and talk about its base, and some of them desire the pleasures of this world, so God Almighty sends upon it a wind from Paradise, and that tree stirs with every pleasure in this world.
56:31: 31- And poured water is poured out and always flows in a groove that does not stop.
56:33: 33- Neither cut off nor forbidden. Ibn Abbas said: It is not cut off once it has been harvested, nor is it forbidden to anyone who wants to take it. Some of them said: It is neither cut off by time nor forbidden by prices, just as most of the fruits of this world are cut off when winter comes, and they can only be reached by a price. Al-Qatibi said: It means that it is not forbidden to them as the orchards of this world are forbidden. It was stated in the hadith: No fruit of Paradise is cut except that God replaces it with a double one.
56:34: 34- And raised mattresses. Ali said: And raised mattresses on beds. A group of commentators said: Some of them are above others, so they are raised high. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told me, Ibn Hubaysh told us, Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Nasa’i told us, Abu Kurayb told us, Rashdin Ibn Sa’d told us, on the authority of Amr Ibn Al-Harith, on the authority of Diraj Abu Al-Samh, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the words of God Almighty: And raised couches, he said: Their height is like that of the two of you between the heaven and the earth, and the distance between the heaven and the earth is a journey of five hundred years. It was said: He meant women by bedding, and the Arabs call women bedding and clothing as a metaphor. Raised means they are raised in beauty and superiority over the women of this world.
56:35: The evidence for this interpretation is his statement after it: 35- Indeed, We created them a new creation. We created them a new creation. Ibn Abbas said: He means the old, decrepit human women. He says, We created them after old age a new creation.
56:36: 36- So We made them virgins, virgins. Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juwzjani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, on the authority of Al-Haytham bin Kulayb Al-Shashi, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Abdul bin Hamid told us, Mus’ab bin Al-Muqaddam told us, Al-Mubarak bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: “An old woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to let me enter Paradise. He said: O mother of so-and-so, no old woman will enter Paradise. She turned away crying. He said: Tell her that she will not enter it even though she is an old woman, for God Almighty says: ‘Indeed, We created them of a special creation * And made them virgins.’” Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Khatib told us, Abu Saeed Amr bin Muhammad bin Mansour told us, Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Sulayman bin Al-Harith Al-Wasiti told us in Baghdad, Khallad bin Yahya bin Safwan Al-Sulami told us, Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abaan, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: Indeed, We created them a special creation, he said: Old women who were blind and lame in this world. Then He made them virgins. Al-Musayyab bin Sharik said: They are the old women of this world. God Almighty created them anew. Whenever their husbands came to them, they found them virgins. Al-Musayyab mentioned on the authority of others: They were preferred over the houris because of their prayers in this world. Muqatil and others said: They are the houris created by God. They did not give birth, so We made them virgins, and there is no pain there.
56:37: 37- Araban, Hamza and Ismail read on the authority of Nafi' and Abu Bakr: Araban with a silent ra, the rest read it with a damma, and it is the plural of Aroob meaning: lovers who are beloved by their husbands. This was said by Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Saeed bin Jubayr, and it is the narration of Al-Walabi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Akrima said about him: Malqa. Akrima said: Ghanjah. Usama bin Zaid said about his father: Arabs are beautiful in speech. Atraban, levels in age at the same age. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told me, Ibn Shaybah told us, Al-Faryabi told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Shaybah, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The people of Paradise will enter Paradise hairless, with a white complexion, curly hair, and kohl-rimmed eyes, thirty-three years old, in the creation of Adam, with a height of sixty cubits by seven cubits.” Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Rashdin ibn Sa’d, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Diraj Abu al-Samh, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The lowest of the people of Paradise is the one who has eighty thousand servants and seventy-two wives, and for him a dome will be erected of pearls, emeralds, and rubies, the distance between Jabiyah and Sana’a.” With this chain of transmission, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “He looks at his face in her cheek, clearer than a mirror, and the smallest pearl on her illuminates what is between the east and the west. And she will be wearing seventy garments, and his sight will penetrate them until he sees the marrow of her leg through them.” With this chain of transmission, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever dies from the people of Paradise, whether young or old, will be returned to Paradise as thirty-year-olds, never to exceed that age. The same applies to the people of Hell.” With this chain of transmission, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: They will wear crowns, and the smallest pearl among them will illuminate the space between the east and the west. Muhammad ibn Abdullah Abu Tuba told us, Abu Tahir al-Harithi told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salim, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Atab al-Abdi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ma’bad al-Rummani, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The lowest of the people of Paradise in status - and there is no lowly one among them - will be the one who has ten thousand servants who come and go, each of whom has a novelty that his companion does not have.”
56:38: God Almighty says 38- For the companions of the right hand, meaning that We created them for the companions of the right hand.
56:39: 39- A group of the first ones, of the believers who were before this nation.
56:40: 40- And a group of others, from the believers of this nation, this is what Ata’ and Muqatil said. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Adl told me, Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Daqqaq told us, Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz told us, Isa bin Al-Masawir told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Isa bin Musa told us, on the authority of Urwah bin Ruwaim, who said: “When God revealed to His Messenger, ‘A company from the former peoples * And a few from the latter ones,’ ‘Umar, may God be pleased with him, wept and said: O Prophet of God, we have believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we have confirmed him, but who among us will be saved, even a few?’ So God, the Almighty, revealed, ‘A company from the former peoples * And a company from the latter ones,’ so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Umar and said: God, the Almighty, has revealed what you said. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: We are pleased with our Lord and the confirmation of our Prophet. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: From Adam to us is a company, and from me until the Day of Resurrection is a company, and it will not be completed except by the black camel herders who say, ‘There is no god but God.’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Husayn bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Husayn bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us one day and said: “The nations were shown to me, and a prophet would pass by with one man, and a prophet with two men, and a prophet with a group of people, and a prophet with no one with him. I saw a great multitude filling the horizon, so I hoped that they would be my nation. Then it was said to me: This is Moses among his people. Then it was said to me: Look. I saw a great multitude filling the horizon. Then it was said to me: Look like this and like this. I saw a great multitude filling the horizon. Then it was said: These are your nation, and with these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. The people dispersed and it was not made clear to them, so the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, discussed matters and said: As for us, we were born into polytheism, but we believed in God and His Messenger, but these are our children. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed and he said: They are those who do not take omens or seek ruqyah or…” They were cauterized and put their trust in their Lord. Then, Ukasha ibn Muhsin stood up and said: Am I one of them, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes. Then another stood up and said: Am I one of them? He, peace be upon him, said: Ukasha has already done it to you. Narrated by Abdullah ibn Masoud on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The prophets were shown to me last night with their followers until Moses, peace be upon him, came to me in the midst of the Children of Israel. When I saw them, I was amazed, so I said: ‘O Lord, what are these?’ It was said: ‘This is your brother Moses and those with him from the Children of Israel.’ I said: ‘O Lord, where are my nation?’ It was said: ‘Look to your right, and the gates of Mecca have been blocked with the faces of men.’ It was said: ‘Are these your nation, are you satisfied?’ I said: ‘O Lord, I am satisfied, O Lord, I am satisfied.’ It was said: ‘Look to your left, and the horizon has been blocked with the faces of men.’ It was said: ‘Are these your nation, are you satisfied?’ I said: ‘O Lord, I am satisfied.’ It was said: ‘With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being held to account.’ The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If you are able to be among the seventy, then be. If you are unable and fall short, then be among the people of the gates. If you are unable, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen there people quarreling a lot.’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Ghundar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a tent, and he said: ‘Would you be satisfied to be a quarter of the people of Paradise?’ We said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Would you be satisfied to be a third of the people of Paradise?’ We said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise, for none will enter Paradise except a Muslim soul, and you are not from the polytheists except like a white hair on the hide of a black bull or like a black hair on the hide of a red bull.” A group of people said that both thirds are from this nation, which is the opinion of Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, and Al-Dahhak. They said: A group from the first from the predecessors of this nation, and a group from the last from the last of this nation at the end of time. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad Al-Dinawari told me, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Sani told us, Abu Khalifa Al-Fadl bin Al-Habbab told us, Muhammad bin Kathir told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abaan bin Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: A group from the first and a group from the last, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are both from my nation.
56:41: God Almighty said: 41- And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left?
56:42: 42- "In poisons, a hot wind, and and scalding, hot water.
56:43: 43- And a shade of black smoke, very black smoke. The Arabs say: Aswad Yahmood if it is very black. Ad-Dahhak said: The Fire is black and its people are black, and everything in it is black. Ibn Kaysan said: Yahmum is one of the names of Hell.
56:44: 44- Neither cool nor generous. Qatada said: Neither cool of a home nor generous of a view. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Neither generous nor handsome. Similar to of every generous pair. (Ash-Shu’ara’: 7) Muqatil said: Good.
56:45: 45- Before that, meaning in this world, they were in luxury, enjoying themselves.
56:46: 46- And they persisted, persisted in the great perjury, in the major sin, which is polytheism. Al-Sha’bi said: The great perjury is the false oath. The meaning of this is that they swore that they would not be resurrected, and they lied about that.
56:47: 47- And they used to say, ‘When we die and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?’ Abu Ja`far, Nafi`, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya`qub read when as a question, when without it, and the others read it as a question in both of them.
56:49: 49- Say, ‘Indeed, the first and the last.’
56:50: 50- They will be gathered together at a appointed time on a known day.
56:52: 52- They will eat from the tree of Zaqqum.
56:53: 53- And they will fill their bellies with it.
56:54: 54- And they will drink boiling water over it.
56:55: 55- Fa Sharboon Sharb Al-Haym, the people of Madinah, Asim and Hamza read it as Sharb with a damma on the sheen. The rest read it with a fatha and they are two languages. The fatha is for the source, and the damma is a noun meaning the source like weakness and weakness. Al-Haym is the thirsty camels. Ikrimah and Qatadah said: Al-Haym is a disease that afflicts camels and they do not quench their thirst, and they do not stop drinking until they die. It is said: a camel Aheem, a she-camel Haymaa, and camels Haym. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Uyaynah said: Al-Haym is the flat land with sand.
56:56: 56- This is their lodging, meaning what was mentioned about Zaqqum and boiling water, meaning their sustenance and food and what was prepared for them, on the Day of Judgment, the day when they will be rewarded for their deeds.
56:57: Then he argued with them about the resurrection by saying: 57- We created you. Muqatil said: We created you and you were nothing and you know that. Why then, why do you not believe in the resurrection?
56:58: 58- Have you seen what you desire? What you pour into the wombs of sperm.
56:59: 59- Do you create it? meaning, do you create what you wish for as human beings, or are We the creators?
56:60: 60- We have decreed, Ibn Kathir read it with a soft dal, while the rest read it with a shaddah, and they are two dialects. Death is among you, Muqatil said: Some of you will reach old age, and some of you will die as children or young men. Ad-Dahhak said: Its meaning is that He made the people of the heavens and the people of the earth equal in it. Based on this, the meaning of We have decreed is: We have decided. And We will not be outdone, defeated and unable to destroy you and subdue you with your likes.
56:61: This is what God Almighty said: 61- That We may replace your likes, meaning: We will bring a creation like you in your place, and create you, make you soar in that which you do not know, of forms. Mujahid said: In whatever creation We wish. Al-Hasan said: That is, We will change your attributes and make you into apes and pigs, as We did to those who were before you, meaning: If We had wanted to do that, We would not have missed it. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: In that which you do not know, meaning: In the crops of black birds, which are in Barhout like swallows, and Barhout is a valley in Yemen.
56:62: 62- And you have certainly known the first creation, the first creation, when you were nothing. So why do you not remember, that I am able to restore you just as I was able to create you?
56:63: 63- Have you seen what you till? Meaning: what you till from the earth and what you throw into it of seeds.
56:64: 64- Do you plant it?, make it grow, “or are We the planters?”, the growers.
56:65: 65- If We willed, We could have made it debris. Ata' said: Straw with no wheat in it. It was also said: Dry stubble that is not useful for food or nourishment. Fadaltum you remained unintentionally. Its original form is fadhallatum you remained unintentionally. One of the two lams was deleted for ease. Tafakahunu you are amazed at what has befallen you in your crops. This is the opinion of Ata', al-Kalbi, and Muqatil. It was also said that you regret your expenditures. This is the opinion of Yaman. Similar to this is: So he began wringing his hands over what he had spent on it. (al-Kahf 18:42). Al-Hasan said: You regret what you have done in the past that necessitated that punishment. Ikrimah said: You blame one another. Ibn Kaysan said: You grieve. Al-Kisa'i said: It is yearning for what has passed, and it is one of the opposites. The Arabs say: tafakkahutu I enjoyed myself meaning: you enjoyed it, and tafakkahutu I was sad meaning: you grieved.
56:66: 66- Indeed, we are in debt. Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim A’ana with two hamzas, and the others read it as a report. The metaphor of the verse is: So you kept joking and saying, ‘Indeed, we are in debt.’ Mujahid and Ikrimah said: He is in debt to us. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: Tormented, and grave is torment. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Kaysan said: We lost our money and what we spent became a loss for us, and the one who is in debt is the one whose money was lost without compensation.
56:67: And his saying: 67- Rather, we are deprived, limited and prohibited, meaning: we were deprived of what we were seeking from the income from the crops.
56:68: 68- Have you seen the water that you drink?
56:69: 69- Did you bring it down from the clouds? The clouds, singular: muznah, “or are We the One who sends it down?”
56:70: 70- If We willed, We could have made it bitter. Ibn Abbas said: Very salty. Al-Hasan said: Bitter. Then why are you not grateful?
56:71: 71- Have you seen the fire that you kindle? You kindle and extract from your flint.
56:72: 72- Did you create its tree, from which fire is kindled, which is the date palm and the black palm tree, or are We the creator?
56:73: 73- We have made it a reminder, meaning the fire of this world, a reminder of the greater fire. If the dreamer sees it, he will remember Hell. This was said by Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Muqatil. Ata’ said: It is an admonition from which the believer will learn. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi told us, Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A`raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The fire of the children of Adam that they kindle is one part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell. They said: O Messenger of God, is that enough? He said: It is sixty-nine parts more than it. And provision, in language and benefit, for the travelers, and the one who stays in the land is the one who stays and the one who stays... Mujahid and Ikrimah said: For those who strengthen means for all people who enjoy it, travelers and residents alike, who use it for light in the dark, to warm themselves from the cold, and to benefit from it in cooking and baking. Al-Hasan said: It is a language for travelers, which they use to travel on their journeys, and they carry it in rags and sacks. Ibn Zayd said: For the hungry, the Arabs say: I have not eaten anything since such and such, meaning: I have not eaten anything. Qatrib said: “Muqawi is one of the opposites. A poor person is called ‘muqawi’ because he has no money. A rich person is called ‘muqawi’ because he has the strength to do whatever he wants. It is said, ‘A man is strong’ if his animals are strong, his wealth increases and he reaches a state of strength. The meaning is that it contains provisions for both the rich and the poor, and no one can do without it.”
56:74: 74- So glorify the name of your Lord, the Great.
56:75: God Almighty said: 75- "So I swear by the positions of the stars." Most of the commentators said: It means: I swear, and "no" is a connective. Isa bin Omar used to read: "So I swear," in the correct form. It was said: His saying "So" is a response to what the infidels said about the Quran that it was magic, poetry, and divination. Its meaning is: It is not as they say. Then he resumed the oath, saying: "I swear by the positions of the stars." Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read: "by positions" as a singular. The others read "by positions" as a plural. Ibn Abbas said: He meant the stars of the Quran, because they were revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, scattered as stars. A group of commentators said: He meant the setting and falling of the stars. Ata' bin Abi Rabah said: He meant their stations. Al-Hasan said: He meant their decline and scattering on the Day of Resurrection.
56:76: 76- And indeed, it is a great oath, if you but knew.
56:77: 77- "It", meaning this book, which is the subject of the oath. "It is a noble Qur'an", honored and respected, because it is the word of God. Some scholars of meaning said: The noble is that which is capable of giving abundant good.
56:78: 78- In a protected book, preserved with God in the Preserved Tablet, protected from the devils.
56:79: 79- None shall touch it, that is, that hidden Book, except the purified, meaning the angels described as pure. This was narrated on the authority of Anas, and it is the opinion of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Abu Aliyah, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd: that they are the angels. Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated on his authority that it is only read by monotheists. Ikrimah said: Ibn Abbas used to forbid Jews and Christians from being able to read the Qur’an. Al-Farra’ said: Only those who believe in it will find its taste and benefit. Some people said: Its meaning is that only those who are pure from ritual impurity and major ritual impurity may touch it. The apparent meaning of the verse is negation, but its meaning is prohibition. They said: It is not permissible for one who is ritually impure, a menstruating woman, or one in a state of minor ritual impurity to carry or touch the Qur’an. This is the opinion of Ata’, Tawus, Salim, Al-Qasim, and most of the scholars. Malik and Al-Shafi’i also said the same. Al-Hakam, Hammad, and Abu Hanifa said: It is permissible for someone who is in a state of ritual impurity or ritual impurity to hold and touch the Qur’an. The first is the opinion of most jurists. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn `Amr ibn Hazm, that in the letter that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to `Amr ibn Hazm, it was stated that no one should touch the Qur’an except one who is pure. What is meant by the Qur’an is the Mushaf. He called it the Qur’an because of its proximity and breadth. It was also narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade traveling with the Qur’an to enemy territory. He meant the Mushaf.
56:80: 80- A revelation from the Lord of the Worlds, meaning the Qur’an is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds. The word revealed is called revealed in the broadest sense of the word, just as something that is destined is called destined, and something that is created is called created.
56:81: 81- “Is it this statement,” meaning the Qur’an, that you, O people of Mecca, are believable? Ibn Abbas said: Liars. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Disbelievers. Similar to this is: They wish that you would compromise so they would compromise. (al-Qalam 68:9). The believer and the flatterer are the liar and the hypocrite. It is from idhan, which means acting inwardly contrary to what is apparent. This is its origin. Then the liar was called mudahan, even if he explicitly states his denial and disbelief.
56:82: 82- And you make your provision, your portion and share of the Qur’an, that you deny. Al-Hasan said about this verse: A servant has lost out whose only portion of the Book of God is denying it. A group of commentators said: It means that you make your gratitude that you lie. Al-Haytham bin Adi said: “From the language of Azd Shanu’ah is: ‘Ma razaq so-and-so is not thankful’, meaning ‘Ma razaq’ he was not thankful. This is when asking for rain by the stars. This is because they used to say when they were rained upon: ‘We were rained upon by such-and-such a star’, and they did not consider this to be from the grace of God Almighty. So it was said to them: ‘Do you consider your provision,’ meaning your gratitude for what you have been provided, meaning gratitude for your provision, to be denial?’ So the noun was deleted and the noun to which it was added was used in its place.” Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Salih ibn Kaysan, on the authority of `Ubayd God ibn `Abd God ibn `Utbah ibn Mas`ud, on the authority of Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the dawn prayer at al-Hudaibiyah following a rain that had fallen during the night. When he finished, he turned to the people and said: ‘Do you know what your Lord has said?’ They said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘He said: Some of My servants have become believers in Me and some have disbelieved. As for he who says: ‘We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of God,’ he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the stars. As for he who says: ‘We have been given rain by the influence of such-and-such a star,’ he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the stars.” It was narrated by Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he added: Then this verse was revealed: So I swear by the positions of the stars until His saying: And you make your provision that you deny (al-Waqi’ah 56:82). Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Saifan told us, Muslim bin Hajjaj told us, Muhammad bin Salamah Al-Muradi told us, Abdullah bin Wahb told us, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, Abu Yunus told us, he told him, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “God does not send down a blessing from the sky except that a group of people become disbelievers in it. God, the Most High, sends down rain and they say: ‘We have been rained upon by such-and-such a star.’”
56:83: God Almighty says: 83- Why then, “when it reaches the throat,” meaning the soul reaches the throat at death.
56:84: 84- And you will then be watching, meaning that you, the family of the deceased, will be watching him when his soul departs. It has been said that the meaning of his statement you will be watching is at My command and authority, and you will not be able to prevent it and you will not own anything.
56:85: 85- And We are nearer to him than you, in knowledge, power, and vision. It was also said: And Our messengers who take his soul are nearer to him than you, but you do not see, those who were present with him.
56:86: 86- If you were not indebted, owned, and most of them said: accountable and rewarded.
56:87: 87- And you will return it, if you should be truthful, meaning, you will return the soul of this dead person to his body after it has reached the throat. So He answered his statement, Then why, when it reaches the throat, and his statement, Then why, if you are not to be condemned, with one answer. Similar to this is the statement of the Almighty: But if there comes to you guidance from Me - whoever follows My guidance will have no fear (al-Baqarah 2:38). They were both answered with one answer, meaning: If the matter is as you say - that there is no resurrection, no reckoning, and no God to reward - then why do you not return the soul of someone dear to you when it has reached the throat? And if you are not able to do that, then know that the matter is up to someone other than you, and that is God, the Almighty, so believe in Him.
56:88: Then he mentioned the classes of creation at death and explained their degrees, saying: 88- But if he was among those brought near, and they are the foremost.
56:89: 89- Farooh, Yaqub read Farooh with a damma on the ra’, and the rest read it with a fatha. Whoever reads it with a damma, Al-Hasan said that it means: His soul comes out in the basil. Qatada said: The soul is mercy, meaning mercy is for him. It was said that its meaning is that there is life and permanence for them. And whoever reads it with the fat-ha, it means: he has a spirit, which is comfort, and this is the opinion of Mujahid. Saeed bin Jubair said: joy. Ad-Dahhak said: forgiveness and mercy. And basil, a rest. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said: It means provision. Muqatil said: It means provision in the Himyarite language. It is said: I went out seeking the basil of God, meaning God's provision. Others said: It is the fragrant basil. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: None of those brought near to God departs from this world until he is brought a branch of the basil of Paradise and smells it, then his soul is taken. A paradise of bliss, Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: The soul is salvation from the fire, and basil is entering the eternal abode.
56:90: 90- And if he, the deceased, was among the companions of the right hand.
56:91: 91- “So peace be upon you from the companions of the right,” meaning safety for you, O Muhammad, from them, so do not worry about them, for they have been saved from God’s punishment, or you see in them what you would like of safety. Muqatil said: It is that God Almighty overlooks their bad deeds and accepts their good deeds. Al-Farra’ and others said: It is agreed upon that they are among the people of the right hand, or it is said to the person of the right hand: It is agreed upon that you are among the people of the right hand, and you have found men like him saying, I will travel soon, and he says to him, You are believed, a traveler who will travel soon, and it is said, “So peace be upon you,” upon you from the people of the right hand.
56:92: 92- And if he is among those who deny the resurrection, those who have gone astray from guidance, and they are the people of the left.
56:93: 93- Then there will come down scalding water, so the one who prepares for them the scalding water of Hell.
56:94: 94- And the burning of Hell, and entering a great fire.
56:95: 95- This, meaning what was mentioned of the story of the dying, is the certain truth, meaning the certain truth, he added it to himself.
56:96: 96- So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great. It was said: He separated the mention of your Lord and His command. It was also said: The letter ba means, so glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjuwayh told us, Ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Hamza Muhammad al-Katib told us, Na’im ibn Hammad told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi, on the authority of his uncle, who was Iyas ibn Amir, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: “When the verse ‘So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great’ was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Make it part of your bowing. And when the verse ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Make it part of your prostration.” Abu Uthman Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Mahmud bin Ghailan told us, Abu Dawud told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said: I heard Sa’d bin Ubaydah narrating on the authority of Al-Mustawrid, on the authority of Silah bin Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah, “that he prayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would say in his bowing: Glory be to my Lord, the Almighty, and in his al-Sajdah 32:Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. And he would not come to a verse of mercy except that he would stop and seek refuge.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, Amara bin Al-Qaqa’ told us, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two phrases are light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to God and His praise, glory be to God the Almighty.” Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Jilfari told us, Abu al-Qasim Tamam ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Razi told me in Damascus, Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Bazzaz, Ahmad ibn Sulayman ibn Hudlam and Ibn Rashid told us: Bakkar ibn Qutaybah told us, Rawh ibn Ubadah told us, Hajjaj al-Sawaaf told us on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever says ‘Glory be to God the Almighty and with His praise,’ a palm tree will be planted for him in Paradise. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, he said: Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Al-Sari bin Yahya told me that Shuja’ told him on the authority of Abu Taybah on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever recites Surat Al-Waqi’ah every night will never be afflicted with poverty. And Abu Taybah never abandoned it.
57:1: Civil and its verses are twenty-nine 1- “Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
57:2: 2- “To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent.”
57:3: 3- He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Hidden, meaning He is the First before everything, without beginning. He was and nothing existed. He is the Last after everything perishes, without end. Everything perishes and He remains. The Evident is the Prevailing, the Supreme over everything, and the Hidden is the All-Knowing. This is the meaning of Ibn Abbas’s statement. Yaman said: He is the First, the Eternal, the Last, the Merciful, the Manifest, the Forbearing, and the Hidden, the All-Knowing. Al-Suddi said: He is the first, by His righteousness, when He made you know His Oneness. The second, by His generosity, when He made you know repentance for what you have done. The external, by His guidance, when He guided you to prostrate to Him. The internal, by His concealment, when you disobeyed Him, so He concealed you. Al-Junayd said: The first is to open hearts, the last is to forgive sins, the apparent is to discover distress, and the hidden is to know the unseen. Omar - may God be pleased with him - asked Kaab about this verse, and he said: Its meaning is that his knowledge of the first is like his knowledge of the last, and his knowledge of the apparent is like his knowledge of the hidden. And He is All-Knowing of everything. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir informed us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad informed us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi informed us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan informed us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj informed us, Zuhair bin Harb informed us, Jarir informed us on the authority of Suhayl, who said: “Abu Salih used to command us, when one of us wanted to sleep, to lie on his right side and then say: ‘O God, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and the Lord of all things, Cleaver of the seed and the date stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur’an, I seek refuge in You from the evil of every evil being whom You hold by the forelock. You are the First, so there is nothing before You, and You are the Last, so there is nothing after You, and You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You, and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing beneath You. Pay off my debt and enrich me from poverty.’” This was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
57:4: 4- “It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself on the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein. And He is with you wherever you are. And God is Seeing of what you do.”
57:5: 5- To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to God all matters are returned.
57:6: 6- “He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night. And He is Knowing of that within the breasts.”
57:7: 7- Believe in God and His Messenger, addressing the infidels of Mecca, and spend from that over which He has made you successors, possessing it: meaning: the money that was in the hands of others, which He destroyed and gave to the Quraysh, so they were successors in that money for those who had passed away. And those among you who have believed and spent will have a great reward.
57:8: 8- And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in God while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord and He has already taken your covenant, Abu Amr read: He took with a damma on the hamza and a kasra on the kha, your covenant with a nominative qaf for what the agent is not named. The others read it with a fatha on the hamza, kha, and qaf, meaning: God took your covenant when He brought you forth from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, that God is your Lord and you have no god but Him, said Mujahid. It was said: He took your covenant to establish the arguments and evidence that call for following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. If you are believers one day, then now is the most appropriate time for you to believe, as the proofs and information about the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the revelation of the Qur’an have been established.
57:9: 9- It is He who sends down to His servant, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, clear verses, meaning the Qur’an, that He may bring you out, God through the Qur’an, from darkness into the light, and it was said: that the Messenger may bring you out with the call from darkness into the light, meaning from the darkness of polytheism to the light of faith, and indeed, God is to you Kind and Merciful.
57:10: 10- And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the cause of God while to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? He says: What is it to you that you do not spend in that which brings you closer to God while you are dying leaving your wealth? Then He explained the virtue of those who were the first to spend in the cause of God and in jihad, saying: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest, meaning the conquest of Mecca according to most of the commentators. Al-Sha'bi said: It is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. And fought, He says: Not equal in virtue are those who spent their wealth and fought the enemy with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before the conquest of Mecca with those who spent and fought after it. Those are greater in degree than those who spent afterwards and fought. Muhammad ibn Fadil narrated from Al-Kalbi that this verse was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him, as he was the first to convert to Islam and the first to spend his wealth in the cause of God. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: The first to declare his Islam with his sword were the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Bakr. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad told us, Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Ayyub told us, Muhammad ibn Yunus told us, al-Ala’ ibn Amr al-Shaibani told us, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari told us, Sufyan ibn Sa’id told us, on the authority of Adam ibn Ali, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, was with him, and he was wearing a cloak that he had sewn around his chest with holes. Gabriel came down to him and said: ‘Why do I see Abu Bakr wearing a cloak that he had sewn around his chest with holes?’ He said: ‘He spent his wealth on me before the conquest.’ He said: ‘God, the Almighty, says: ‘Convey my greetings to him and say to him: Are you pleased with Me in this poverty of yours or are you displeased?’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O Abu Bakr, God, the Almighty, sends you His greetings and says to you: Are you pleased with Me in this poverty of yours or are you displeased?’ Abu Bakr said: ‘Am I displeased with my Lord? Indeed, I am pleased with my Lord. Indeed, I am pleased with my Lord.’” And to both, God has promised goodness, meaning that God has promised Paradise to both groups. Ata' said: The degrees of Paradise vary, and those who spent before the conquest will be in the best of them. Ibn 'Amir read: And to both in the nominative case, And God is All-Knowing of what you do.
57:11: 11- Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him and he will have a noble reward?
57:12: 12- The Day you see the believing men and believing women, their light proceeding, meaning on the Bridge, before them and on their right, meaning on their right. Some of them said: He meant all of them, so he used some to refer to all of them, and that is their guide to Paradise. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the believers are those whose light shines from Medina to Aden, Abyan, Sana’a, and beyond that, to the point that among the believers are those whose light shines only as far as the place where his feet lie.” Abdullah ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with them both, said: They will be given their light according to their deeds. Some of them will be given their light like a palm tree, and some of them will be given their light like a standing man, and the light nearest to them is the top of their thumb, so it is extinguished sometimes and lit up sometimes. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: Their light runs before them and on their right are their books. He means that their books that they were given are on their right hands and their light is before them, and the angels say to them: “Good tidings to you today are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein you will abide eternally. That is the great attainment.”
57:13: 13- The Day the hypocrites, men and women, will say to those who have believed, ‘Wait for us.’ Al-A’mash and Hamzah read: Wait for us, with a fat-ha on the hamzah and a kasra on the dhaal, meaning, Give us time. It was also said: Wait for us. The others read it by deleting the alif in the connection and adding a damma to it at the beginning and adding a damma to the dhaal. The Arabs say: Wait for me, wait for me. “We quote from your light,” we are illuminated by your light, and that is because God Almighty gives the believers a light according to their deeds with which they walk on the path, and He also gives the hypocrites a light to deceive them, and that is what God Almighty says: And it is He who deceives them (An-Nisa’: 141), so while they were walking, God sent upon them a wind and darkness that extinguished the light of the hypocrites, and that is what He says: The Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him - their light will proceed before them and on their right, saying, ‘Our Lord, perfect for us our light’ (al-Tahrim 66:8), for fear that their light will be taken away as the light of the hypocrites was taken away. Al-Kalbi said: Rather, the hypocrites are illuminated by the light of the believers, but they are not given the light. So when the believers precede them and remain in darkness, they say to the believers: Wait for us so that we may borrow from your light. “It will be said: Go back behind you.” Ibn Abbas said: The believers say to them. Qatadah said: The angels say to them: Go back behind you from where you came, and seek light. So seek light there for yourselves, for there is no way for you to borrow from our light. So they go back in search of light but do not find anything, so they turn back to them to meet them and distinguish between them and the believers. This is His statement: Then a wall will be set up between them, meaning a wall. The ba is a connective, meaning between the believers and the hypocrites, and it is a wall between Paradise and Hell. For it, meaning for that wall, a door, inside of which is mercy, meaning inside of that wall is mercy, which is Paradise. And outside of it, meaning outside of that wall, before it, meaning before that outside, is the torment, which is Hell.
57:14: 14- They call to them. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that he said: The wall that God Almighty mentioned in the Qur’an, And He placed between them a wall with a gate, is the eastern wall of Jerusalem. Its interior contains mercy, and its exterior, on the front, contains torment, the Valley of Hell. Shuraih said: Ka'b used to say about the gate called the Gate of Mercy in Jerusalem: It is the gate of which God Almighty said: And a wall will be placed between them, having a gate verse. Calling to them means: The hypocrites will call to the believers from behind the wall when the wall will separate them and they will remain in the darkness: Were we not with you, in this world, praying and fasting? They said, ‘Yes, but you tempted yourselves,’ you destroyed yourselves with hypocrisy and disbelief and used them in sins and desires, all of which is a temptation, and you waited, with faith and repentance. Muqatil said: And you waited for death for Muhammad and you said he was about to die so we could be rid of him, “and you doubted, you cast doubt on his prophethood and what he promised you, and wishful thinking deceived you, the falsehoods and what you had hoped for from the misfortunes that befell the believers, until the command of God came, meaning death, and the Deceiver deceived you about God, meaning Satan. Qatadah said: They continued to be deceived by Satan until God threw them into the Fire.
57:15: 15- So today no ransom will be taken from you, Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Amir, and Ya`qub read it with the letter ta`, while the others read it with the letter ya`, ransom, as a substitute and compensation for ransoming yourselves from the punishment, nor from those who disbelieved, meaning the polytheists, “your refuge is the Fire. It is your protector,” your companion and more deserving of you, for what you have done of sins, and wretched is the destination.
57:16: God Almighty said: 16- Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed about the hypocrites one year after the migration. They asked Salman the Persian one day and said: Tell us about the Torah, for it contains wonders. So this verse was revealed: We narrate to you the best of stories (Yusuf 12:3). He informed them that the Qur’an contains better stories than other verses, so they stopped asking Salman for as long as God willed. Then they returned and asked Salman about something similar, so this verse was revealed: God has sent down the best statement - a consistent Book (al-Zumar 39:23). So they stopped asking him for as long as God willed. Then they returned and said: Tell us about the Torah, for it contains wonders. So this verse was revealed. According to this interpretation, his statement, Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? means in public and with the tongue. Others said it was revealed about the believers. Abdullah ibn Masoud said: There were only four years between our conversion to Islam and when God rebuked us with this verse: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? Ibn Abbas said: God felt the hearts of the believers were slow to respond, so He rebuked them thirteen years after the revelation of the Qur’an, saying: Has the time not come? Has the time not come for those who have believed to humble themselves: to soften and soften and for their hearts to submit to the remembrance of God, and that which has been revealed – Nafi’ and Hafs from Asim read it with a light zay, while the others read it with a shaddah – of the truth – which is the Qur’an, and not be like those who were given the Scripture before – meaning the Jews and Christians, and a long period passed over them – the time between them and their prophets, and their hearts hardened – Ibn Abbas said: They inclined toward this world and turned away from God’s admonitions. The meaning is that God, the Almighty, forbids the believers from being in the company of the Qur’an like the Jews and Christians whose hearts hardened when time passed over them. It was narrated that Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari sent for the reciters of the people of Basra, and three hundred men who had recited the Qur'an entered upon him. He said to them: You are the best of the people of Basra and their reciters, so recite it and do not let time be too long for you, lest your hearts harden as the hearts of those who came before you hardened. And many of them are wicked, meaning those who abandoned belief in Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon them.
57:17: And the Almighty said: 17- “Know that God gives life to the earth after its death. We have made clear to you the signs that you may understand.”
57:18: 17- Indeed, the men and women who give charity, Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim read it with a soft sad in both of them from tasdiq, meaning: the believing men and women. The others read it with a heavy sad, meaning the men and women who give charity. The ta was assimilated into the sad, “and loan God a goodly loan,” by giving charity and spending in the way of God, the Almighty, it will be multiplied for them, that loan, and for them is a noble reward, a good reward, which is Paradise.
57:19: 19- And those who believe in God and His Messengers - those are the truthful ones. A truthful one is someone who is very truthful. Mujahid said: Everyone who believes in God and His Messenger is a truthful one, and he recited this verse. Ad-Dahhak said: They are eight people from this nation who preceded the people of the earth in Islam in their time: Abu Bakr, Ali, Zaid, Uthman, Talha, Az-Zubayr, Saad, Hamza, and the ninth of them is Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God Almighty be pleased with them all. God included him with them because of the sincerity of his intentions. And the martyrs are with their Lord. Scholars differed regarding the syntax of this verse. Some said it is connected to what precedes it, and the waw is a conjunction. They meant by martyrs the sincere believers. Ad-Dahhak said: They are the ones we have named. Mujahid said: Every believing friend is a martyr, and he recited this verse. Some people said: The speech ended with His statement: They are the truthful ones, then He began by saying: And the martyrs are with their Lord, and the waw is a waw of resumption, and this is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Masruq, and a group. Then they differed concerning them, and some people said: They are the prophets who will bear witness against nations on the Day of Resurrection. This is narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it is the opinion of Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Muqatil bin Sulayman said: They are those who were martyred in the way of God. For them is their reward, for the righteous deeds they did, and their light, on the path, and those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire.
57:20: God Almighty says: 20- Know that the life of this world, meaning that the life of this world and what is related to it, meaning that life in this world, meaning that life in this world, is play, meaning that it is futile and fruitless, and amusement, meaning that life in this world, and diversion, meaning that it ends, and adornment, meaning that you adorn yourself with, and boasting to one another, meaning that you boast about the abundance of wealth and children, then He gave an example of it and said: Like the example of rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers, meaning the farmers, then it withers, dries up, and you see it yellow, after its greenness and freshness, then it becomes debris, meaning that it shatters and breaks after it dries up and perishes, and in the Hereafter is a severe punishment, Muqatil said: for the enemies of God, and forgiveness from God and approval, for His friends and those who obey Him. The life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion. Saeed bin Jubair said: The enjoyment of delusion is for those who do not occupy themselves with seeking the Hereafter. But whoever is occupied with seeking it will have the enjoyment of transport to something better than it.
57:21: 21- Race one another, hasten, to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, if some of them were connected to each other, “prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers. That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.” So He made it clear that no one enters Paradise except by the grace of God.
57:22: God Almighty says: 22- No disaster strikes upon the earth, meaning: drought, scarcity of vegetation, or lack of fruits, or within yourselves, meaning: diseases and loss of children, except that it is in a register, meaning: the Preserved Tablet, before We bring it into being, before We create the earth and the souls. Ibn Abbas said: before We bring the disaster into being. Abu Al-Aliyah said: meaning the soul, that, for God, is easy, meaning that proving that, despite its abundance, is easy for God Almighty.
57:23: 23- So that you will not despair, be sad, over what has escaped you, of this world, nor rejoice over what He has given you, Abu Amr read it with a shortened alif, because he said has escaped you so he made the verb belong to it, and the others read He has given you with a long alif, meaning: He gave you. Ikrimah said: There is no one who does not rejoice and grieve, but make joy gratitude and sadness patience, and God does not like any arrogant boaster, one who is proud of what he has been given of this world, proud who boasts about it to people. Jaafar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said: O son of Adam, why do you regret what you have lost that death cannot restore to you, and why do you rejoice in what you have that death cannot leave in your hand?
57:24: 24- Those who are stingy, it was said: It is in the accusative case as a description of the arrogant. It was also said: It is in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is what follows. “And they enjoin miserliness on people. And whoever turns away,” that is: turns away from faith, then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read: then indeed, God is the Free of need, omitting he, and that is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an.
57:25: God Almighty says: 25- Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, with verses and arguments, and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance, meaning: justice. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: It is what is weighed with, meaning: We placed the balance as He said: And the heaven He raised and placed the balance (al-Rahman 55:7) that people may maintain justice, so that they may deal with one another in justice. And We sent down iron. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God sent down four blessings from the sky to the earth: iron, fire, water, and salt. The scholars of semantics said that the meaning of His statement, We sent down iron, is that He created and brought about, meaning that He brought out iron for them from the minerals and taught them how to make it through His revelation. Qatrib said: This is from the word nazl, just as one says: The prince granted someone a good accommodation. The meaning of the verse is that he made that a place of accommodation for them. Similar to this is His statement: And He has sent down for you from the grazing livestock eight mates (al-Zumar 39:6). Therein is great might, great power, meaning: weapons for war. Mujahid said: There is a paradise and weapons in it, meaning tools for pushing and striking, and benefits for the people, from what they benefit from in their interests, such as knives, axes, needles, and the like, since it is a tool for every craft, and that God may know, meaning: We sent Our messengers and sent down with them these things so that people would deal with truth and justice, and that God may know and see, who supports Him, meaning: His religion, and His messengers in secret, meaning: who supported the religion and did not see God or the Hereafter, and only he who obeys God in secret is praised and rewarded, Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might, strong in His command, mighty in His kingdom.
57:26: 26- “And We had certainly sent Noah and Abraham and placed among their descendants prophethood and the Scripture. But among them were those who were guided, and many of them were wicked.”
57:27: 27- Then We followed up their footsteps with Our messengers, and followed up with Jesus, the son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel and placed in the hearts of those who followed him, in his religion, kindness, which is the most intense tenderness, and mercy, they were affectionate to one another, as God Almighty said in describing the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Merciful among themselves (al-Fath 48:29), and monasticism which they innovated, of their own volition. This is not in apposition to what preceded it, and its being in the accusative case is an implied verb, as if he said: and they innovated monasticism, meaning they brought it on their own volition. We did not prescribe it, meaning We did not impose it, upon them except seeking the pleasure of God, meaning: but they sought the pleasure of God through that monasticism, and that monasticism is the hardships they burdened themselves with in abstaining from food, drink, clothing, marriage, and worship in the mountains, but they did not observe it with its right observance, meaning they did not observe monasticism with its right Rather, they neglected it and disbelieved in the religion of Jesus, so they became Jews and Christians, and entered the religion of their kings, and abandoned monasticism. Some of them remained in the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him, until they reached Muhammad, peace be upon him, and believed in him. This is what God Almighty said: So We gave those among them who believed their reward, and they are those who remained steadfast in it and they are the people of compassion and mercy, and many of them are wicked, and they are those who abandoned monasticism and disbelieved in the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Muzani told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Sulaiman told us, Shaiban bin Farukh told us, Al-Sa’aq bin Hazn told us, on the authority of Aqil Al-Ja’di, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Suwaid bin Ghafla, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: I entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “O Ibn Mas’ud, those who came before you differed into seventy-two sects, three of which survived and the rest perished. One sect rebelled against the kings and fought them over the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him, so they captured them and killed them. Another sect did not have the strength to compete with the kings or to stay among them, calling them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him, so they roamed the lands and became monastics. They are the ones about whom God Almighty said: ‘And monasticism, which they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever believes in me, confirms me, and follows me has observed it properly.’” Take care of her, and whoever does not believe in me, it is they who will perish.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: I was riding behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a donkey, and he said to me: O son of Umm `Abd, do you know from where the Children of Israel adopted monasticism? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “The tyrants appeared among them after Jesus, peace be upon him, and they committed sins. The people of faith became angry and fought them. The people of faith were defeated three times, and only a few of them remained. They said: ‘If we prevail over these people, they will annihilate us, and no one will remain to call people to the religion.’ They said: ‘Come, let us disperse throughout the land until God sends the Prophet whom Jesus, peace be upon him, promised us,’ meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they dispersed among the mountains and introduced monasticism. Some of them adhered to their religion, and some disbelieved.” Then he recited this verse: And monasticism which they invented (al-Baqarah 2:17). Then We gave those among them who believed, meaning those who remained steadfast in it, their reward. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O son of Umm `Abd, do you know what the monasticism of my nation is? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Migration. Jihad, prayer, fasting, Hajj, Umrah, and Takbir on the hills. It was narrated on the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every nation has monasticism, and the monasticism of this nation is jihad in the way of God. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: There were kings after Jesus, peace be upon him, who changed the Torah and the Gospel, and among them were believers who read the Torah and the Gospel and called them to the religion of God. So it was said to their kings: If you gather these people who have caused trouble for you, kill them or they enter into what we are doing. So their king gathered them and offered them to be killed or to abandon the reading of the Torah and the Gospel except for what they changed from them. They said: We will suffice you with ourselves. So a group said: Build us a pillar, then raise us to it, then give us something to raise our food and drink with, and we will not return to you. And a group said: Let us wander in the land and wander and drink as wild animals drink. If you gain control over a land, then kill us. And a group said: Build us houses in the deserts so that we can dig wells and cultivate vegetables, so that we will not return to you or pass by you. So they did that to them. So those people followed the path of Jesus, peace be upon him, and a people came after them who changed the Book. So a man would say: We will be in In the place of so-and-so, we worship as so-and-so worships, and we travel as so-and-so travels, and we take houses as so-and-so did. They are in their polytheism, and they have no knowledge of the faith of those who follow them. This is what God Almighty says: And monasticism, which they innovated, meaning these righteous people innovated it, but they did not observe it with its right observance, meaning the others who came after them, so We gave those among them who believed their reward, meaning those who innovated it seeking God’s pleasure, and many of them are wicked, meaning those who came after them.
57:28: He said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, and only a few of them remained, a man descended from his monastery, and a traveler came from his travels, and the owner of a monastery came from his monastery, and they believed in him, so God Almighty said: 28- O you who have believed, fear God, the address is to the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. He says: O you who have believed in Moses and Jesus, fear God in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and believe in His Messenger, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and He will give you two portions, two shares, of His mercy, meaning He will give you two rewards for your belief in Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Gospel, and in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Qur’an. Some people said: The speech stopped at His saying and mercy and then He began: and monasticism which they innovated, and that is because they abandoned the truth and ate pork and drank alcohol and abandoned ablution and ritual washing after sexual impurity and circumcision, so they did not observe it, meaning: obedience and religion with the right observance of it as a metaphor for something not mentioned, so We gave those who believed among them their reward and they are the people of compassion and mercy, and many of them are wicked, and they are the ones who innovated monasticism, and Mujahid went with this. The meaning of his saying: Except seeking the pleasure of God according to this interpretation is: We did not command them or prescribe anything for them except seeking the pleasure of God, and we did not command them to become monks. God Almighty says: O you who have believed, in Moses and Jesus, fear God and believe in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He will give you a double portion of His mercy. We narrated on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “There are three who will be given their reward twice: a man who had a female slave and disciplined her well, then freed her and married her; a man from the People of the Book who believed in His Book and believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace; and a servant who worshipped God well and advised his master well.” And He will make for you a light by which you will walk. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: It means on the path, just as He said: Their light will proceed before them (al-Tahrim 66:8). It is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him that the light is the Qur'an. Mujahid said: It is guidance and clarification, meaning He will make for you a clear path in religion by which you will be guided. And He will forgive you, for God is Forgiving and Merciful. It was said that when those of the People of the Book who did not believe heard the words of God the Almighty: Those will be given their reward twice over (al-Qasas 28:54), they said to the Muslims: As for those of us who believe in your Book, they will have a reward twice over them for believing in your Book and our Book. As for those of us who do not believe, they will have a reward like your rewards. So what is your superiority over us? Then God the Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy. So He gave them two rewards if they believed in His Messenger Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him), and He increased them in light and forgiveness.
57:29: Then he said: 29- So that the People of the Scripture may not know. Qatada said: Those of the People of the Scripture who did not believe envied the believers among them, so God Almighty revealed: So that the People of the Scripture may not know. Mujahid said: The Jews said, A prophet will soon emerge from among us who will cut off hands and feet. When he emerged from among the Arabs, they disbelieved in him. Then God, the Most High, revealed: So that the People of the Scripture will not know meaning, so that they will know, and there is no connection, that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God meaning, so that those who did not believe will know that they have no reward or share in the bounty of God, “and that bounty is in the hand of God. He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.” Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu’aimi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Ismail informed us, Qutaybah ibn Sa’id informed us, al-Layth informed us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, “Your lifespan in comparison to the lifespan of those who came before among the nations is like the time between the ‘Asr prayer and sunset. Your example and that of the Jews and Christians is like a man who hired workers and said, ‘Who will work for me until noon for one qirat, one qirat?’ So the Jews worked until noon for one qirat, one qirat. Then he said, ‘Who will work for me from noon until the ‘Asr prayer for one qirat, one qirat?’ So I worked.” Christians from noon until the afternoon prayer for one qirat each. Then he said: Who will work for me from the afternoon prayer until sunset for two qirats each? You are the ones who work from the afternoon prayer until sunset. Will you not have a double reward? The Jews and Christians became angry and said: We work more and are paid less. God the Almighty said: Have I wronged you in any of your rights? They said: No. He said: It is My bounty that I give to whomever I wish. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Al-Ala told me, Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The example of the Muslims, Jews, and Christians is like that of a man who hired people to do work for him until the night for a known wage. They worked until midday, then they said: ‘We have no need of the wage you stipulated for us, and what we did is invalid.’ He said to them: ‘Do not do that. Complete the rest of your work and take your full wage.’ But they refused and left. Then he hired other people after them and said: ‘Complete the rest of this day and you will have the wage you stipulated for them.’ So they worked until the time of the ‘Asr prayer came and they said: ‘What we did was invalid and you will have the wage you promised us for it.’ He said: ‘Complete the rest of your work, for only a little of the day remains.’ But they refused. So he hired people to work for him for the rest of their day, and they worked for the rest of their day until the sun set, and they completed the wage for both groups. That is…” Like them and like what they accepted from this light.
58:1: 1- "God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband," the verse. It was revealed about Khawlah bint Tha'labah, who was married to Aws ibn al-Samit. She was beautiful in body, but he had a defect, so he wanted her, but she refused. So he said to her: You are to me like the back of my mother, then he regretted what he said. Zihar and Ila' were among the divorce practices of the people of the Jahiliyyah. So he said to her: I think you have become forbidden to me. She said: By God, that is not a divorce. She came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) - and Aisha may God be pleased with her was washing the side of his head - and said: O Messenger of God, my husband Aws ibn al-Samit married me when I was a young, wealthy woman with a family. Then he consumed my wealth, wasted my youth, dispersed my family, and I became old, and he regretted it. Is there anything that can bring us together and revive me? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am forbidden to him. She said: O Messenger of God, by Him who sent down the Book to you, I did not mention divorce, and he is the father of my children and the dearest of people to me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am forbidden to him. She said: I complain to God of my poverty and my loneliness, for my companionship has been prolonged and my stomach is full of him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I see that you have been forbidden to him, and I have not been commanded to do anything about you. So she began to argue with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to her: You have been forbidden to him, she cried out and said: I complain to God of my poverty and the hardship of my situation, and that I have young children. If I take them with him, they will be lost, and if I take them with me, they will starve. She began to raise her head to the sky and say: O God, I complain to You. O God, send down a revelation through the tongue of Your Prophet. This was the first zihar in Islam. Aisha got up to wash the other side of his head and said: Look into my situation, may God make me your ransom, O Prophet of God. Aisha said: Stop talking and arguing. Do you not see the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? When the revelation was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), it would overtake him like a deep sleep. When the revelation was over, he said to her: Call your husband. So she called him, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited to him: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you [verses]. Aisha said: Blessed be He whose hearing encompasses all sounds. A woman was conversing with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was in a corner of the house, hearing some of her words, while some of them were hidden from me, when God revealed: God has heard and the verses. The meaning of his saying: The statement of the one who argues with you is that she quarrels with you, argues with you, and argues with you about her husband, and complains to God, and God hears your argument, your arguments, Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing, He hears what you whisper to Him and implore Him, and He sees whomever complains to Him.
