58:2: Then he condemned Zihar, saying: 2- Those of you who swear off their wives, Asim read: they swear off with a damma on the ya’, a soft dhaal, an alif after it, and a kasra on the ha’. Ibn Amir, Abu Ja’far, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read: with a fatha on the ya’ and the ha’, a shaddah on the dhaal, and an alif after it. The others read it with a fatha on the ya’, a shaddah on the dhaal, and the ha’ without an alif. They are not their mothers, meaning, those whom they make from their wives like mothers to their mothers. The ta in their mothers is in the accusative case as in the saying: This is not a human being (Yusuf 12:31). The meaning is: They are not their mothers. Their mothers meaning, they are not their mothers, “except those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they say something reprehensible,” not known in Islamic law, and falsehood, lying. And indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving, He pardoned them and forgave them by imposing expiation upon them. The form of zihar is when a man says to his wife: You are to me like my mother’s back, or you are from me or with me or to me like my mother’s back. Likewise, if he says: You are to me like my mother’s stomach or like my mother’s head or my mother’s liver, or he says your stomach or your head or your hand is to me like my mother’s back, or he compares one of her parts to another part of his mother’s parts, then it is zihar. According to Abu Hanifa - may God be pleased with him - if he likens it to the mother’s stomach, vagina, or thigh, then it is considered zihar, but if he likens it to another organ, then it is not zihar. If he said, You are to me like my mother or like the spirit of my mother, and he meant by that honor and dignity, then it is not considered zihar until he intended that. If he compared her to his grandmother and said, You are to me like the back of my grandmother, then it is considered zihar. Likewise, if he compared her to a woman forbidden to him by blood relationship by saying, You are to me like the back of my sister, my aunt, or my maternal aunt, or he compared her to a woman forbidden to him by breastfeeding, then it is considered zihar - according to the most correct of the opinions.
58:3: 3- And those who swear an oath of divorce against their wives and then go back on what they said - then the freeing of a slave is required. Then the ruling on zihar is that it is forbidden for the husband to have intercourse with her after zihar unless he makes expiation, and expiation is required if he returns to zihar. According to the Almighty’s saying: And then they go back on what they said - then the freeing of a slave is required. Scholars differed regarding repetition. The scholars of the Zahiri school said: It is repeating the word of Zihar, which is the opinion of Abu Al-Aaliyah, based on the Almighty’s statement: Then they return to what they said, meaning to what they said [i.e. they repeated it again]. If he does not repeat the word, then there is no expiation upon him. Some people say that expiation is required for the zihar itself, and what is meant by return is: returning to what they were doing in the pre-Islamic period of zihar itself, which is the opinion of Mujahid and al-Thawri. Some people said: What is meant by recidivism is intercourse, which is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Qatada, Tawus, and Al-Zuhri. They said: There is no expiation for him as long as he does not have intercourse with her. Some people said: It is the intention to have intercourse, and this is the opinion of Malik and the people of opinion. Al-Shafi’i said that the recurrence is when he keeps her after the zihar for a period of time during which he can separate from her, but he does not do so. If he divorces her immediately after the zihar, or one of them dies at that time, then there is no expiation upon him, because the recurrence of the statement is the violation. Ibn Abbas interpreted the return as regret, saying: They regret and return to friendship, and this is its meaning. Al-Farra’ said: It is said: So-and-so returned to what he said, meaning in what he said, and in reversing what he said, meaning: he went back on what he said. This explains what Al-Shafi’i said, that his intention by zihar is to prohibit divorce. If he keeps her for the sake of marriage, then he has contradicted his statement and gone back on what he said, so he must make expiation. He even said: If he makes zihar about his revocable wife, his zihar is valid and he does not have to make expiation until he takes her back. If he takes her back, then he has returned and expiation is required of him. His saying: Then freeing a slave before they touch each other. What is meant by touching is intercourse. It is not permissible for the one who has sworn to divorce to have intercourse with his wife from whom he has sworn to divorce unless he makes expiation, whether he intends to make expiation by freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding. According to Malik, if he intends to make expiation by feeding, it is permissible for him to have intercourse before that, because God Almighty restricted freeing and fasting to before touching each other. He said regarding feeding: But whoever is unable, then the feeding of sixty poor persons. He did not say: before they touch each other. And for others: the generality of food is carried over to the restriction of manumission and fasting. They differed regarding the prohibition of any direct sexual intercourse other than intercourse before expiation, such as kissing and pleasure. Most of them held that nothing is prohibited except intercourse, which is the opinion of Al-Hasan and Sufyan Al-Thawri, and the more correct of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, just as menstruation prohibits intercourse, but not all other forms of pleasure. Some of them are of the view that it is forbidden, because the term seeking includes all forms of sexual intercourse. If a person has sexual intercourse with the apparent partners before making expiation, he has disobeyed God, the Most High, and the expiation is his responsibility. He is not permitted to do so again unless he makes expiation, and no further expiation is required for sexual intercourse. Some scholars said: If he has intercourse with her before making expiation, he must make two expiations. The expiation for Zihar is in order. He must free a believing slave. If he cannot find one, he must fast for two consecutive months. If he breaks the fast deliberately one day or forgets the intention, he must start the two months again. If he is unable to fast, he must feed sixty poor people. We mentioned in Surat Al-Ma’idah the amount to be fed to each poor person. This is what you are admonished to do, you are commanded to do, and God is All-Aware of what you do.
58:4: 4- And whoever does not find, meaning a slave, shall fast for two consecutive months before they touch each other. If he has a slave but needs her service, or has the price of a slave but needs it for his own expenses and the expenses of his dependents, then he may switch to fasting. Malik and Al-Awza'i said: He is obligated to free a slave if he has a slave or her price even if he needs it. Abu Hanifa said: If he has a slave himself, he must free her, even if he needs her. However, if he has the price of a slave and needs it, then he may fast. So if the person who pronounced shahada a divorce by zihar begins to fast for two months and then has intercourse during the month at night, he has disobeyed God by giving precedence to intercourse over the expiation. However, he does not have to start over for the two months. According to Abu Hanifa, he must start over for the two months. The Almighty said: But whoever is unable to do so, he must feed sixty poor people. This means that if the person who has committed slander is unable to fast due to illness, old age, or excessive desire that prevents him from having sexual intercourse, he must feed sixty poor people. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Fadl Al-Kharqi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Abdullah Al-Taysifuni told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad bin Ali Al-Kashmihani told us, Ali bin Hajar told us, Ismail bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Harmalah, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, “That Khawlah bint Tha’laba was married to Aws bin Al-Samit, and he divorced her and he had a problem. She came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Aws has divorced me, and she mentioned that he had a problem. She said: By Him who sent you with the truth, I have come to you only as a mercy for him, for there are benefits for him in it. So God revealed the Qur’an about them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Tell him to free a slave. She said: By Him who sent you with the truth, he does not have a slave or her price. He said: Tell him to fast for two consecutive months. She said: By Him who sent you with the truth, if you gave him a task for three days, he would not be able to do it. He said: Tell him to feed sixty poor people. She said: By Him who sent you with the truth, he is not able to do it. He said: Tell him to go to so-and-so, son of…” So-and-so told me that he has half a date as charity. Let him take it as charity on his behalf and give it to sixty poor people.” Sulayman ibn Yasar narrated on the authority of Salamah ibn Sakhr who said: I was a man who had intercourse with women in ways no one else had. When Ramadan came, I feared that I might have intercourse with my wife, so I declared my divorce until Ramadan was over. While she was talking to me one night, something of her uncovered itself to me. I did not wait long before I had intercourse with her. I went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and informed him. He said: You are in this situation. I said: I am in this situation - he said it three times - I said: I am in this situation and here I am, so carry out the judgment of God, for I am patient for that. He said: Then free a slave. I struck the side of my neck with my hand and said: No, by Him who sent you with the truth, I do not own anything else. He said: Then fast two consecutive months. I said: O Messenger of God, did what happened to me happen only because of fasting? He said: Then feed sixty poor people. I said: By Him Who sent you with the truth, we spent this night feeling lonely; we have no supper. He said: Go to the collector of the charity of Banu Zuraiq and tell him to give it to you. Feed sixty poor people from it a wasq on your behalf, then use the rest of it to help you and your family. He said: So I returned to my people and said: I found hardship and bad opinion among you, but I found plenty and blessing with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He has ordered your charity to be given to me, so give it to me. He said: So they gave it to him. That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger, so that you may believe in what the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought from God Almighty, and those are the limits set by God, meaning what was described as expiations for zihar, and for the disbelievers is a painful punishment, Ibn Abbas said: for those who deny it and lie about it.
58:5: 5- Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger, that is, who are hostile to God and His Messenger, and who oppose and disobey their command, will be humbled, humiliated, disgraced, and destroyed, “just as those before them were humbled. And We have already sent down clear signs. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.”
58:6: 6- “The Day God will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. God has recorded it.” God preserved their deeds, “and they forgot it. And God is Witness over all things.”
58:7: 7- Have you not seen that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, what will happen? / Abu Ja`far read with a ta’, to feminize the whispering, and the others read with a ya’ because of the barrier, of the whispering of three, meaning of the secrets of three, meaning of whispering, meaning: there is nothing that a man whispers to his two companions about, but He is their fourth, with knowledge. And it was said: its meaning is that there are no three whispering to each other, but He is their fourth with knowledge, He knows their whispering, and no five but He is their sixth, nor less than that nor more but He is with them wherever they are, Ya`qub read: more in the nominative case in the place of speech before entering "then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things."
58:8: 8- Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversations? This was revealed about the Jews and the hypocrites, because they used to whisper to each other without the believers, and they would look at the believers and wink at each other, giving the impression to the believers that they were whispering about something that would upset them, so they would be saddened by that and say, We only see them when they hear about our brothers who went out in the raids, whether they were killed, died, or defeated. This would take root in their hearts and make them sad. When this became prolonged and increased, they complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered them not to whisper to each other without the Muslims, but they did not stop that and returned to their secret conversations, so God revealed: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversations? meaning secret conversations, then they return to what they were forbidden from, meaning they return to the secret conversation that they were forbidden from, and they whisper. Al-A’mash and Hamza read: and they produce, with the weight of they influence, and the others read they whisper, because of their saying: If “You whispered to one another, so do not whisper about sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger. This is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had forbidden them from whispering, but they disobeyed him. And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you. This is because the Jews used to enter upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “and say: ‘Death be upon you.’” Death means death, and they made him think that they were saying: “Peace be upon you.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would respond to them by saying: Upon you. When they left, they said to themselves: Why does God not punish us for what we say? They meant: If he were a true prophet, God would punish us for what we say. God Almighty said: Sufficient for them is Hell; they will burn in it, and wretched is the destination. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Abu Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha: “The Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Death be upon you.’ He said: ‘And upon you.’ Aisha said: ‘Death be upon you and may God curse you and be angry with you.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Take it easy, Aisha. Be gentle and avoid harshness and obscenity.’ She said: ‘Did you not hear what they said?’ He said: ‘Did you not hear what I said? I responded to them, and my prayer regarding them will be answered, but their prayer regarding me will not be answered.’”
58:9: Then God Almighty forbade the believers from whispering among themselves as the hypocrites and the Jews did, saying: 9- O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger, that is, like the actions of the hypocrites and the Jews. Muqatil said that by his saying believe, he meant the hypocrites, that is, believe in their own words. Ata’ said: He means those who believed based on their claim. He said to them: Do not confer privately about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger, “but confer privately about righteousness and piety. And fear God, to whom you will be gathered.”
58:10: 10- The private conversation is only from Satan, that is, from Satan’s embellishment, to grieve those who believe, that is, he only makes that seem attractive to them to grieve the believers, and it does not harm them at all, and it was said: Satan does not harm them at all, “except by permission of God. And upon God let the believers put their trust.” Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Zahiri told us, my grandfather Abu Sahl Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzar told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Dabry told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If there are three of you, two should not whisper in private without the third except with his permission, for that will sadden him.
58:11: God Almighty said 11- O you who have believed, when you are told, ‘Make room in assemblies,’ then make room, the verse. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to honor the people of Badr from among the Muhajireen and Ansar. One day, some of them came to the assembly first, so they stood in front of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, but they did not make room for them. This upset the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said to those around him: Stand up, so-and-so, and you, so-and-so. So he stood up from the assembly as many as the people of Badr had stood up in front of him. This upset those who were stood up from their assembly, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the dislike on their faces, so God revealed this verse. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas, and we mentioned his story in Surat Al-Hujurat. Qatada said: They used to compete in the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) assembly, and if they saw someone approaching them, they would be reluctant to take their seat, so God commanded them to make room for one another. It was said: That was on Friday, so God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, when you are told to make room, meaning make room in the assembly. Al-Hasan and Asim read it: in the assemblies because everyone is sitting in an assembly, meaning: let each man make room in his assembly. The others read it: in the assembly in the singular, because what is meant by it is the assembly of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So make room means make room. It is said: fasa yafsahan, fasahan: if he makes room in the assembly. God will make room for you, God will make Paradise and the assemblies in it for you. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al Khallal told us, Abu Al Abbas Al Asam told us, Al Rabi’ told us, Al Shafi’i told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Umar, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: None of you should make a man get up from his seat and then replace him in it, but make room and spread out. Abdul Wahhab bin Al Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al Khalal told us, Abu Al Abbas Al Asam told us, Al Rabi’ told us, Al Shafi’i told us, Abdul Majeed told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Sulayman bin Musa said on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: None of you should make his brother stand on Friday, but let him say, ‘Make room.’ Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Qurazi and Al-Hasan said: This is in the battlefields and fighting positions. A man would come to the people in the row and say, Spread out, but they would refuse because of their eagerness to fight and desire for martyrdom. And when it is said, ‘Rise,’ then rise. The people of Medina, Ash-Sham and Asim read it with a damma on the sheen, while the others read it with a kasra. These are two dialects, meaning, Rise up. It was said, Rise from your positions until you make room for your brothers. Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: There were men who were reluctant to pray when the call to prayer was made, so God revealed this verse, meaning, When the call to prayer is made, then rise up for it. Mujahid and most of the commentators said: Its meaning is: If you are told to rise up for prayer, for jihad, and for the gatherings of every good and right, then rise up for them and do not fall short. God will raise those who have believed among you, by obeying His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, by standing up from their gatherings and making room for their brothers, and those who were given knowledge, among the believers by virtue of their knowledge and their precedence, by degrees. So God, the Almighty, informed us that His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, was correct in what he commanded and that those believers will be rewarded for what they commanded, and that the group of people from Badr deserved the honor they were treated with. And God is All-Aware of what you do. Al-Hasan said: Ibn Masoud read this verse and said: O people, understand this verse and we will make you desire knowledge, for God Almighty says: God will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. The knowledgeable believer is higher than the one who does not know, by degrees. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Imam Abu al-Tayyib Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman told us, Abu Ali Hamid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Harawi told us, Muhammad ibn Yunus al-Qurashi told us, Ubayd God ibn Dawud told us, Asim ibn Raja’ ibn Haywah told us, Dawud ibn Jamil ibn Kathir ibn Qays told me: I was sitting with Abu al-Darda’ in the mosque of Damascus when a man came and said: O Abu al-Darda’, I have come to you from the city of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) because of a hadith that I have heard that you narrate from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: Did you have no other need for it? He said: No. He said: Nor did you come for trade? He said: No. He said: And you did not come except out of a desire for it? He said: Yes. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever takes a path in search of knowledge, God will make easy for him a path to Paradise. The angels spread their wings in satisfaction with the seeker of knowledge, and the heavens, the earth, and the fish in the water pray for him. The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon on the night of the full moon over all the other planets. The scholars are the heirs of the prophets, and the prophets did not leave behind dinars or dirhams, but they left behind knowledge. So whoever takes it has taken a great portion.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Ali Al-Hussein bin Ahmed bin Ibrahim Al-Sarraj told us, Al-Hasan bin Yaqub Al-Adl told us, Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab Al-Farra’ told us, Ja’far bin Awn told us, Abdul Rahman bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “passed by two gatherings in his mosque, one of the gatherings was calling upon God and yearning for Him, and the other was learning jurisprudence and teaching it. He said: Both gatherings are good, and one of them is better than the other. As for these, they call upon God and yearn for Him, and as for those, they learn jurisprudence and teach the ignorant. These are better, and I was sent only as a teacher.” Then he sat among them.
58:12: God Almighty said 12- O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an act of charity, before your private conversation. Ibn Abbas said: This is because the people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they asked him a lot until they were making things difficult for him, so God wanted to make things easier for His Prophet and to discourage them and deter them from that, so He commanded them to present an act of charity before their private conversation with the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed about the rich, because they used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and frequently commune with him, and they would overpower the poor in their gatherings, until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked their prolonged sitting and communing with him. When they saw that, they stopped communing with him. As for the people of hardship, they did not find anything, and as for the people of ease, they were miserly, and that was difficult for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the concession was revealed. Mujahid said: They were forbidden from engaging in private conversation with God until they gave charity, and no one engaged in private conversation with God except Ali, may God be pleased with him. He gave charity with a dinar and engaged in private conversation with God. Then the permission was revealed, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to say: There is a verse in the Book of God that no one before me acted upon and no one after me will act upon, and it is the verse of private conversation. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me and said: Don’t you see a dinar? I said: They cannot afford it. He said: How much? I said: A grain or a barley grain. He said: You are indeed insignificant. Then this verse was revealed: Did you fear to offer alms before your private conversation? Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Through me, God has lightened the burden on this nation. That is better for you, meaning: giving charity before supplication, “and purer. But if you cannot find anything, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful,” meaning the poor who cannot find anything to give in charity are forgiven.
58:13: 13- Did you fear to advance? Ibn Abbas said: Did you act stingy? The meaning is: Did you fear poverty and need if you advanced, "Before your private conversations, there were charities. But if you did not do" what you were commanded, God has turned to you in mercy: He overlooked you and did not punish you for abandoning charity. It was said that the and is a conjunction, its metaphor, so if you did not do it, God will turn to you in mercy and abrogated the charities. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: That was for ten nights, then it was abrogated. Al-Kalbi said: It was only an hour of a day. So establish prayer, the obligatory one, and give zakat, the obligatory one, "and obey God and His Messenger. And God is Acquainted with what you do."
58:14: 14- Have you not considered those who take as allies a people with whom God has become angry? This verse was revealed about the hypocrites who took as allies the Jews, advised them, and confided in the secrets of the believers to them. By God has become angry with them, he meant the Jews. They are neither of you nor of them, meaning that the hypocrites are not believers in religion and loyalty, nor are they Jews or disbelievers, as he said: Wavering between that, neither with these nor with those An-Nisaa' 143. And they swear to a lie while they know it. Al-Suddi and Muqatil said: It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Nabtal, the hypocrite, who used to sit with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and then relay his speech to the Jews. “While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in one of his rooms, he said: ‘A man will now enter upon you whose heart is the heart of a tyrant and who looks with the eyes of a devil.’ Abdullah ibn Nabtal entered and he had blue eyes. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Why are you cursing me, you and your companions?’ He swore by God that he had not done so and brought his companions. They swore by God that they had not cursed him. Then God, the Almighty, revealed these verses, saying: ‘And they swear to a lie while they know’ / that they are liars.”
58:15: 15- "God has prepared for them a severe punishment. Evil indeed is what they have been doing."
58:16: 16- They took their false oaths as a shield, to protect themselves from being killed and to defend themselves and their property. So they hindered [people] from the path of God, they hindered the believers from their jihad by killing and taking their property. So they will have a humiliating punishment.
58:17: 17- “Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God on the Day of Resurrection. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.”
58:18: 18- The Day God will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him, lying that they were not polytheists, as they swear to you, in this world, and they think that they are on something, from their false oaths, unquestionably, they are the liars.
58:19: 19- Satan took over, overcame and seized control of them, “and made them forget the remembrance of God. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan - they are the losers.”
58:20: 20- Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger - those are among the most humiliated, the lowest, meaning: they are among those who will be humiliated in this world and the hereafter.
58:21: 21- God has decreed, God has decreed a firm decree, “I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might.” Similar to His statement: “And Our word has already gone forth for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they will be the victorious.” As-Saffat 71-72. Al-Zajjaj said: The victory of the messengers is of two types: whoever among them is sent to war is victorious through war, and whoever is not commanded to war is victorious through argument.
58:22: God Almighty says 22- “You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose God and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred,” the verse. He informed us that the faith of believers is corrupted by befriending disbelievers, and that whoever is a believer should not befriend a disbeliever, even if he is from his kindred. It was said: It was revealed about Khatib bin Abi Balta’ah when he wrote to the people of Mecca. It will come in Surat Al-Mumtahanah, God willing. And Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated on the authority of Marra al-Hamdani on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud regarding this verse, he said: Or their fathers, meaning Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, who killed his father Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah on the day of Uhud. Or their sons, meaning Abu Bakr called his son on the day of Badr to a duel and said: O Messenger of God, let me be on the first journey. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Give us your life, O Abu Bakr. Or their brothers, meaning Mus`ab ibn Umair, who killed his brother Ubaid ibn Umair on the day of Uhud. Or their clan, meaning Umar, who killed his maternal uncle al-`As ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughira on the day of Badr, and Ali, Hamza, and Ubaidah killed on the day of Badr Utbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabi`ah, and al-Walid ibn Ubbah. Those in whose hearts He has decreed faith, He has established belief in their hearts, so they are certain and sincere. It has also been said that He has decreed that they will have faith, so He mentioned the hearts because they are its location. And supported them with a spirit from Him, He strengthened them with victory from Him. Al-Hasan said: He called His victory for them a spirit because their affair lives by it. Al-Suddi said: He means by faith. Al-Rabi’ said: He means by the Qur’an and its proof, as He said: And thus We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], a spirit of Our command (al-Shura 42:52). It has also been said that it is by His mercy. It has also been said that He supported them with Gabriel, peace be upon him. “And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein. God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of God. Unquestionably, the party of God - they are the successful ones.”
59:1: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. The commentators said: This Surah was revealed about Banu Nadir, and that is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Medina and Banu Nadir made peace with him on the condition that they would not fight him or fight with him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted that from them. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought Badr and was victorious over the polytheists, Banu Nadir said: By God, he is the Prophet whose description we found in the Torah. No banner will be rejected from him. When he fought Uhud and the Muslims were defeated, they became suspicious and showed enmity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers. They broke the covenant that was between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf rode with forty Jewish riders to Mecca, and they came to the Quraysh and made an alliance with them and agreed with them that their word would be one against Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Sufyan entered the Sacred Mosque with forty, and Ka’b with forty Jews, and some of them took Some of the covenant between the curtains and the Kaaba, then Kaab and his companions returned to Medina, and Gabriel came down and informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what Kaab and Abu Sufyan had agreed upon, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the killing of Kaab bin al-Ashraf, so Muhammad bin Maslama killed him - we mentioned this in Surat Al Imran. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had discovered a treachery on their part when he came to them regarding the blood money for the Muslims killed by Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri on his way back from Bir Ma’una. They intended to throw a stone at him from the top of the fortress, but God protected him and informed him of that - we mentioned it in Surat al-Ma’idah. When Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf was killed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) woke up and ordered the people to march to Banu al-Nadir, who were in a village called Zahra. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) marched to them, he found them wailing for Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. They said, O Muhammad, one wailing woman after another, and one weeping after another? He said, Yes. They said, Leave us to weep and cry, then your matter will be decided. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Leave the city. They said, Death is closer to us than that. They called for war and announced the fighting. The hypocrites - Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions - tricked them into saying, "Do not leave the fortress. If they fight you, we will be with you and will not abandon you, and we will support you. If you leave, we will leave with you." They trained on the alleys and fortified them, then they decided to betray the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) so they sent to him: Go out with thirty of your companions, and let thirty of us go out until we meet at a place halfway between us and you, so that they may listen to you. If they believe you and have faith in you, then we will all believe. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out with thirty of his companions and thirty Jewish rabbis went out to him. When they were in a clearing of the land, some of the Jews said to one another: How will you get to him when he has with him thirty of his companions, all of whom would like to die before him? So they sent to him: How can we understand when we are sixty men? So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out with three of his companions, and three of the Jews went out, carrying daggers and wanting to kill the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). A sincere woman from Banu Nadir sent word to her brother, a Muslim man from the Ansar, and told him what Banu Nadir wanted to do to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Her brother came quickly until he reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he told him the report of them before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) reached them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned. The next day, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to them with battalions and besieged them for twenty-one nights. God cast terror into their hearts and they despaired of the victory of the hypocrites. They asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for peace, but he refused to do so unless they leave Madinah as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to do. They accepted that, and he made peace with them on the condition that they leave and that they would have The camels did not carry anything of their money except the ring, which is the weapon, and they were to leave their homes, property, and all their money to them. Ibn Abbas said: On the condition that each of the people of three houses carry on a camel as much of their belongings as they wish, and whatever remains will be for the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ad-Dahhak said: Every three people were given a camel and water carriers, so they did that and left Medina for the Levant, to Adhraat and Jericho, except for two families, including the family of Abu al-Haqiq and the family of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, who went to Khaybar, and a group of them went to al-Hirah.
59:2: This is what God Almighty said: 2- It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, meaning Banu Nadir, from their homes, which was in Yathrib. Ibn Ishaq said: The expulsion of Banu Nadir occurred after the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) return from Uhud and the conquest of Qurayzah upon his return from Al-Ahzab, and there were two years between them. For the first gathering, Al-Zuhri said: They were from a tribe that had not been expelled in the past, and God, the Almighty, had decreed expulsion for them, and had it not been for that, He would have punished them in this world. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever doubts that the place of gathering will be in Ash-Sham, let him read this verse. This was the first gathering to Ash-Sham. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Go out. They said: Where to? He said: To the place of gathering. Then the creation will be gathered to Ash-Sham on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Kalbi said: He said: For the first of the gathering because they were the first of the People of the Book to be expelled from the Arabian Peninsula, and then the last of them was expelled by Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hamdani once said: The first gathering was from Medina, and the second gathering was from Khaybar and all of the Arabian Peninsula to Adhraat and Jericho in the Levant during the days of Omar. Qatada said: This was the first gathering, and the second gathering is a fire that will gather them from the east to the west, spending the night with them wherever they spend the night and resting with them wherever they rest. You did not think, O believers, that they would leave, from the city because of their strength and power, as they were people of fortresses, estates, and many palm trees. And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God, that is, Banu Nadir thought that their fortresses would protect them from God’s authority. So God came to them, that is, God’s command and punishment, from where they did not expect, that is, He ordered His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight them and expel them, although they did not expect that, and He cast terror into their hearts, by killing their master Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf. They destroy, Abu Amr read it with emphasis, and the others with emphasis, and their meaning is the same, their homes are in their hands and the hands of the believers. Al-Zuhri said: This is because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with them on the condition that they would have what the camels carried, they would look at the wood in their homes and demolish them and remove from them what they liked and load them on their camels, and the believers would destroy the rest of it. Ibn Zayd said: They would uproot the pillars, demolish the ceilings, dig holes in the walls, and pull out the wood, even the pegs, destroying them so that the believers would not inhabit them, out of envy and hatred. Qatada said: The Muslims were destroying what was near them on the outside, and the Jews were destroying it from within. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Whenever the Muslims gained control of one of their houses, they demolished it to make room for their fighters. The enemies of God would dig holes in the backs of their houses and then go out to the Prophet, fortify themselves in them, destroy what was near them, and throw the ones from which they had come out at the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is what God Almighty said: They destroy their homes with their own hands and the hands of the believers, so take heed, so take heed and consider what has befallen them, O you who have vision, O you who have intellects and insight.
59:3: 3- And had God not decreed upon them exile, leaving their homeland, He would have punished them in this world, by killing and captivity as He did with Banu Qurayzah, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
59:4: 4- That, which befell them, “is because they opposed God and His Messenger. And whoever opposes God, then indeed, God is severe in penalty.”
59:5: 5- What you have cut down of the palm trees, the verse. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) descended upon Banu Nadir and they fortified themselves in their fortresses, he ordered their palm trees to be cut down and burned. The enemies of God were alarmed at that and said: O Muhammad, you claim that you want reform! Is it reform to uproot trees and cut down palm trees? Have you found in what you claim that was sent down to you corruption on earth? The Muslims felt upset about what they said and feared that it might be corruption and differed about it. Some of them said: Do not cut them down, for it is from what God has bestowed upon us. Some of them said: Rather, we enrage them by cutting them down. Then God revealed this verse to confirm those who forbade cutting them down and to absolve those who cut them down from sin. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burned the palm trees of Banu Al-Nadir and cut down the buwayrah, so this was revealed: Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by permission of God. God informs us in this verse that whatever they cut down or left standing was by permission of God, and to disgrace the wicked. They differed about the soft date. Some people said: All palm trees are soft except for the Ajwa date. This is the opinion of Ikrimah and Qatadah. It was narrated by Zadan on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to cut down their palm trees except for the Ajwa date.” The people of Medina call the dates other than the Ajwa date: the colors, the singular of which is color and soft. Al-Zuhri said: They are all types of palm trees except Ajwa and Barniya. Mujahid and Atiyyah said: It refers to all date palms without exception. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them: It is a type of date palm. Sufyan said: It refers to the most generous date palms. Muqatil said: It is a type of palm tree. Its fruit is called the color, which is intense yellow. Its stone can be seen from the outside, and the molars are hidden in it. It was the best of their dates and the most pleasing to them. The price of a single palm tree from it was the price of a young palm tree, and it was more beloved to them than a young palm tree. When they saw them cutting it down, it was difficult for them and they said to the believers: You hate corruption on earth, and you are corrupting. Leave this palm tree standing. It is for whoever has conquered it. God Almighty informed us that this was by His permission.
59:6: 6- And what God bestowed upon His Messenger, meaning what He returned to His Messenger. It is said: Afa yafi’u means he returned, and God fa’a “from them” meaning from the Jews of Banu Nadir, you did not urge you placed upon it neither horses nor riders, it is said: the horse and the camel jifa’u wajifan, meaning to walk quickly, and its owner urged it to walk, and what he meant by riders is the camels that carry the people. When Banu Nadir left their lands and farms, the Muslims asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to divide them among them, as he had done with the spoils of Khaybar. God the Most High explained in this verse that it was spoils for which the Muslims had not mounted or trodden horses, nor travelled far, nor suffered any hardship, nor encountered any war. But God gives power to His messengers over whom He wills, and God has power over all things. So he made the wealth of Banu Nadir specifically for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), to place it wherever he wished. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divided it among the Muhajireen, and did not give anything from it to the Ansar, except for three people who were in need, and they were Abu Dujana Samak ibn Kharsha, Sahl ibn Hunaif, and Al-Harith ibn As-Summah. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Malik bin Aws bin Al-Hadathan Al-Nadri told me that Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him called him when his chamberlain, Yarfa, came to him and said: Would you like to ask permission to have Uthman, Abd Al-Rahman, Al-Zubayr and Saad? He said: Yes. So he let them in. Yarfa stayed for a while and then came back and said: Would you like to have permission to have Abbas and Ali? He said: Yes. So when they had entered, Abbas said: O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this man. - and they were disputing about the spoils of war that God had bestowed upon His Messenger from Banu Al-Nadir. - The group said: O Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and spare one of them from the other. He said: “Take it easy. I ask you by God, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand, do you know that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “We do not inherit what we leave behind is charity.” He meant the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) himself. They said: He said that. So Omar turned to Ali and Abbas and said: I ask you by God, do you know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that? They said: Yes. He said: Then I will tell you about this matter. God had singled out the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with something in this booty that He had not given to anyone else. He said: And whatever God bestowed on His Messenger from them - you did not urge upon it any cavalry or camels, until His saying: Powerful. This was exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He did not keep it without you nor keep it for yourself. He gave it to you and spread it among you until this money remained. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would spend on his family their annual expenses from this money, then he would take what remained and make it the property of God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that throughout his life. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died. Abu Bakr said: I am the guardian of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, took it and did with it what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did with it. You were all together at that time. He turned to Ali and Abbas: You remember that Abu Bakr did with it as you say, and God knows that he was truthful, righteous, and a follower of the truth. Then God took Abu Bakr’s soul. I said: I The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Bakr were my successors, so I took control of it for two years of my leadership. I did in it what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Bakr did, and God knows that I am truthful, righteous, and a follower of the truth. Then you both came to me and I spoke to you as one, and ordered you both. I said to you: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: We do not inherit; what we leave is charity. When I decided to hand it over to you, I said: If you wish, I will hand it over to you on the condition that you pledge to God and His covenant that you will do in it what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Bakr did, and what I have done in it since I took over. Otherwise, do not speak to me about it. You both said: Hand it over to us for that reason. So I handed it over to you. Do you ask me to do something else? By God, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand, I will not do anything about it except this until the Hour comes. If you are unable to do it, then hand it over to me, and I will suffice you.
59:7: God Almighty said 7- Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, meaning from the wealth of the infidels of the towns. Ibn Abbas said: It is Qurayzah, An-Nadir, Fadak, Khaybar, and the towns of Uraynah. It is for God and for the Messenger and for near relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler. We have already mentioned in Surat Al-Anfal the ruling on spoils of war and the ruling on fay’. The wealth of fay’ belonged to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) during his lifetime, and he used to spend from it on his family for their annual expenses, and he used to make whatever remained the wealth of God. Scholars differed about the distribution of the spoils of war after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some said: It is for the imams after him. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions on this matter: One of them is for fighting, and the second is for the interests of Muslims. He begins with fighting, then the most important interests, then the most important. They differed over dividing the spoils of war. Some of them held that it should be divided into fifths, with one-fifth going to the people of the spoils of war and four-fifths going to the fighters and the public interest. The majority held that it should not be divided into fifths, but rather that all of it should be spent on the same expenditure, and that all Muslims have a right to it. Umar ibn al-Khattab recited: What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, until he reached: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties and And those who came after them. Then he said: This includes all Muslims, and he said: There is no Muslim on the face of the earth who does not have a right to this spoils of war, except for those whom your right hands possess. So that it will not be a state, the common people read it with a ya', state, meaning so that the spoils will not be a state. Abu Ja'far read it with a ta', state, in the nominative case, as the subject of kana, meaning so that the matter will not be a state. He made being to mean occurring, and then it has no predicate. State is the name for the thing that people circulate among themselves, among the rich among you, meaning among the leaders and the powerful, so that they overpower the poor and weak. This is because when the people of the Jahiliyyah seized booty, the leader would take a quarter of it for himself, which is the quarter, then he would choose from it whatever he wanted after the quarter. So God made it for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to distribute as he was commanded. Then he said: And whatever the Messenger has given you, he gave you, take it, of spoils and booty, and whatever he has forbidden you, of stolen goods and other things, refrain from it. This was revealed regarding spoils of war, and it is general in everything that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded and forbade. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yusuf, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: May God curse the tattooers and the tattooed, the pluckers, and the filers for the sake of beauty, changing the creation of God. report of that reached a woman from Banu Asad called Umm Ya’qub, so she came and said: I have heard that you cursed such and such. He said: “Why should I not curse those whom the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) cursed, and it is in the Book of God the Most High?” She said: I have read what is between the two covers and I did not find in it what you say. He said: “If you had read it, you would have found it. Haven’t you read the verse: ‘And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from.’” (al-Hashr 59:7)? She said: Yes. He said: He has forbidden it. And fear God. Indeed, God is severe in penalty.
59:8: 8- For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty provision from God and [His] approval, meaning they went to the abode of emigration seeking the pleasure of God, the Almighty, “and supporting God and His Messenger. Those are the truthful,” in their faith. Qatada said: These are the emigrants who left their homes, properties, and tribes and went out of love for God and His Messenger, and chose Islam over the hardship they were in, to the point that it was mentioned to us that a man would tie a stone around his stomach to support his back from hunger, and a man would make a hole in the winter with no other blanket. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Tahhan told us, Abu Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Quraysh ibn Sulayman told us, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Makki told us, Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Umayyah ibn Khalid ibn Abd God ibn Asid, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: That he used to open with the vagabonds of the emigrants. Abu Ubayd said: This is what Abd al-Rahman said, and in my opinion he is Umayyah ibn Abd God ibn Khalid ibn Asid. We narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “O group of vagrant immigrants, be glad with the perfect light on the Day of Resurrection. You will enter Paradise half a day before the rich people, and that is the equivalent of five hundred years.”
59:9: 9- And those who settled in the home and in faith, and they are the Ansar, settled in the home, meaning: Medina, they took it as the home of migration and faith, before them, meaning they converted to Islam in their homes and preferred faith and built mosques two years before the arrival of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The structure of the verse: And those who had settled in the home before them, meaning before the arrival of the immigrants upon them, and they believed because faith is not a place of settlement. They love those who have emigrated to them, but they find no need in their hearts, out of resentment, anger, and envy, for what they have been given, that is, what the emigrants were given without them of the spoils of war. This is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the wealth of Banu Nadir among the emigrants, but did not give anything to the Ansar, and the souls of the Ansar were pleased with this. And they give preference over themselves, that is, they give preference over their brothers among the emigrants with their wealth and homes over themselves, even though they are in privation, in need and want of what they give preference to, because they shared their homes and wealth with them. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musaddad told us, Abdullah bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Ghazwan, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him for hospitality. He sent word to his wives, ‘Do you have anything?’ They said, ‘Except water.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Who will take him in or host this one?’ A man from the Ansar said, ‘I will, O Messenger of God.’ So he went with him to his wife and said, ‘Honor the guest of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ She said, ‘We have nothing but food for the children.’ He said, ‘Prepare your food, light your lamp, and put your children to sleep if they want dinner.’ So she prepared her food, lit her lamp, and put her children to sleep. Then she got up as if she was fixing her lamp, but she put it out. They made him think they were eating, so they spent the night hungry. When morning came, he went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, ‘God laughed tonight or…’” I was amazed at your actions, so God Almighty revealed: “And they give others preference over themselves, even though they are in need. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ told us, Shu’aib told us, Abu Al-Zinad told us, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Ansar said: Divide the palm trees between us and our brothers. He said: No. They said: Spare us the expense and we will share the fruit with you. They said: We hear and obey. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Yahya bin Saad, who heard Anas bin Malik when he went out with him to Al-Walid, saying: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon the Ansar to give them Bahrain, and they said: No, unless you give a similar amount to our brothers from the Muhajireen. He said: Be patient until you meet me at the Cistern, for you will be afflicted with self-interest after me.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Ansar on the day of Nadir: If you wish, you can distribute to the Muhajireen some of your wealth and homes and share this booty with them. Or if you wish, your homes and wealth will be yours, and nothing of the booty will be distributed to you. The Ansar said: Rather, we will distribute to them some of our wealth and homes and give them preference in the booty and not share it with them. So God Almighty revealed: ‘And they give others preference over themselves, even though they are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.’” In Arabic, greed means stinginess and withholding of wealth. Scholars differentiated between greed and miserliness. It was narrated that a man said to Abdullah ibn Masoud: I fear that I may be ruined. He said: What is that? He said: I hear God say: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful, and I am a stingy man, and hardly anything comes out of my hands. Abdullah said: That is not the stinginess that God the Almighty mentioned in the Qur’an, but greed is to unjustly consume your brother’s wealth. But that is miserliness, and miserliness is an evil thing. Ibn Omar said: Stinginess is not that a man withholds his money, but rather stinginess is that a man aspires to what is not his. Saeed bin Jubair said: Greed is taking what is forbidden and withholding zakat. It was also said: Greed is extreme greed that leads to committing forbidden acts. Ibn Zayd said: He who does not take something that God has forbidden him from, and is not driven by greed to prevent something that God has commanded him to do, has been protected from his own greed. Imam Abu Ali Al-Hussein bin Muhammad Al-Qadi told us, Abu Saeed Khalaf bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Muhammad bin Abi Nizar told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Hazzaz Al-Qahandari told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Saadi told us, Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ramadi told us, Al-Qa’nabi told us, Dawud bin Qais Al-Farra’ told us, on the authority of Ubaid God bin Muqsim, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection. Beware of greed, for greed destroyed those who came before you, for it led them to shed each other’s blood and make their forbidden things permissible.” Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam told us, my father and Shuaib told us: al-Layth told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Haad, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of Safwan ibn Abi Yazid, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ - he is Ibn al-Lajlaj - on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The dust of fighting in the cause of God and the smoke of Hell will never come together in the belly of a servant, and miserliness and faith will never come together in the heart of a servant.
59:10: God Almighty said: 10- And those who came after them, meaning the followers, who are those who come after the Muhajireen and the Ansar until the Day of Resurrection. Then He mentioned that they pray for themselves and for those who preceded them in faith and forgiveness, so He said: They say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts any rancor,’ deceit, envy, and hatred, “for those who have believed. Our Lord, You are indeed Kind and Merciful.” So whoever has rancor in his heart toward any of the Companions and does not have mercy on all of them, then he is not among those whom God meant in this verse, because God Almighty arranged the believers into three ranks: the Muhajireen, the Ansar, and the followers described as God mentioned. So whoever is not from the followers with this description is outside the categories of believers. Ibn Abi Layla said: People are divided into three categories: the poor emigrants, those who have settled in the home and faith, and those who came after them. So strive not to be outside of these categories. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah bin Hamid told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah bin Sulaiman told us, Ibn Numayr told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “You were commanded to seek forgiveness for the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but you cursed them. I heard your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: This nation will not pass away until its last curses its first.” Malik bin Mughol said: Aamer bin Shurahbil Al-Shaabi said: O Malik, the Jews and Christians have a distinction over the Rafidah in one characteristic. The Jews were asked: Who are the best people of your religion? They said: The companions of Moses, peace be upon him. The Christians were asked: Who are the best people of your religion? They said: The disciples of Jesus, peace be upon him. The Rafidah were asked: Who are the worst people of your religion? They said: The companions of Muhammad, peace be upon him. They were ordered to seek forgiveness for them, but they reviled them. So the sword is drawn against them until the Day of Resurrection. They will not have a banner, will not stand firm, and will not unite in word. Whenever they ignite the fire of war, God will extinguish it by shedding their blood, dividing them, and refuting their argument. May God protect us and you from misguided desires. Malik ibn Anas said: Whoever hates any of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or has rancor in his heart towards them, has no right to the spoils of war of the Muslims. Then he recited: What God bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, until he came to this verse: For the poor emigrants… And those who were established in the home and in faith… And those who came after them until His saying: Kind and Merciful.
59:11: God Almighty says: 11- Have you not seen those who are hypocrites, that is, they showed something other than what they concealed: meaning: Abdullah bin Abi Salul and his companions, They say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, that is, the Jews from Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir, making the hypocrites their brothers in religion, because they were disbelievers like them. If you are expelled, from Medina, we will surely go out with you and not obey anyone concerning you, asking us about your abandonment and opposition, “ever. And if you are fought, we will surely aid you. And God bears witness that they,” meaning the hypocrites, are liars.
59:12: 12- If they are expelled, they will not go out with them, and if they are fought, they will not aid them. And the matter was thus, for they were expelled from their homes, but the hypocrites did not go out with them, and they were fought, but they did not aid them: God the Almighty says: And if they aid them, they will turn their backs. That is, if they were to be aided. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that if they intended to aid the Jews, they would turn their backs in defeat. Then they will not be aided. That is, Banu Nadir will not be aided if their aid is defeated.
59:13: 13- You, O group of Muslims, are more fearful of God in their hearts, meaning they fear you more than they fear God. That, meaning that fear of you, is because they are a people who do not understand, the greatness of God.
59:14: 14- "They will not fight you all together except within fortified villages," meaning they will not come out to fight you, but they will fight you fortified by villages and walls. This is His statement, "or from behind walls. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read wall as a singular form, while the others read walls" with a damma on the jim and the dal as a plural form. "Their violence among themselves is severe," meaning that some of them are rude to others, and their enmity toward one another is severe. It was also said that their violence among themselves from behind walls and fortresses is severe, so if they come out against you, they are the most cowardly of God's creation. "You would think they were united, but their hearts were diverse," scattered and different. Qatada said: The people of falsehood have different desires, different testimonies, and different actions, but they are united in their enmity toward the people of truth. Mujahid said: He meant that the religion of the hypocrites differs from the religion of the Jews. "That is because they are a people who do not reason.
59:15: 15- Like those before them, meaning: the example of these Jews is like those before them, soon, meaning the polytheists of Mecca, they tasted the evil consequences of their deed, meaning the killing at Badr, and that was before the Battle of Banu Nadir, as stated by Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: Like those before them, meaning Banu Qaynuqa. It was said: The example of Qurayza is like the example of Banu Nadir, and there were two years between them. And for them is a painful punishment.
59:16: Then he gave an example of the hypocrites and the Jews as a whole in their cowardice, saying: 16- Like Satan, meaning like the hypocrites of Banu Nadir in their arrogance and failure, like Satan, when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ And when he disbelieved, he said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you.’ This is what was narrated by Ata and others on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There was a monk during the period called Barsisa who worshipped in his monastery for seventy years, during which he did not disobey God for a moment. But Satan exhausted him with his tricks, so one day he gathered the rebellious devils and said: Can I not find anyone among you who can suffice me in Barsisa’s matter? Al-Abyadh – who was the companion of the prophets and who confronted the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and came to him in the form of Gabriel to whisper to him through revelation, but Gabriel drove him to the farthest reaches of India – said to Al-Abyadh, I will suffice you in his matter. So he went and adorned himself with the adornments of a monk, shaved the middle of his head, and came to Barsisa’s monastery. He called out to him, but he did not answer him. He would not stop his prayers except every ten days and would not break his fast except once every ten days. When Al-Abyad saw that he was not answering him, he turned to worship at the beginning of his cell. When Barsisa turned away, he looked out of his cell and saw Al-Abyad standing and praying in the handsome appearance of a monk. When he saw that, he regretted not answering him and said to him, You called me and I was busy, so what is your need? He said, "My need is that I wanted to be with you, so that I could learn from you and learn from your work and knowledge, and we could meet in worship, so that you could supplicate for me and I could supplicate for you." Barsisa said, I am busy and you are not interested, so if you are a believer, then God will give you a share in what I supplicate for the believers if He answers my call. Then he turned to his prayer and left Al-Abyad. Al-Abyad went to pray, but Barsisa did not pay any attention to him for forty days after that. When he turned away, he saw him standing and praying. When Barsisa saw the intensity of his effort, he said to him, What is your need? He said: My need is for you to give me permission so that I may ascend to you. So he gave him permission and he ascended to him in his monastery. He stayed with him for a year, worshipping God, not breaking his fast except every forty days and not departing from his prayer except once every forty days, and sometimes he extended it to eighty days. When Barsisa saw his diligence, his soul declined towards him and he was pleased with the state of the white man. When the year had passed, Al-Abyad said to Barsisa: I am leaving, for I have a companion other than you, and I thought that you were more diligent than I saw, and we were hearing about you other than what I saw. So, a very difficult thing entered Barsisa’s mind because of what he had seen because of the intensity of his diligence. So, when he bade him farewell, Al-Abyad said to him: I have supplications that I will teach you, so that you may supplicate with them, for they are better than what you are in. With them, God heals the sick and cures the afflicted and the insane. Barsisa said: I hate this position because I am busy with myself, and I fear that if people know about it, they will distract me from worship. So Al-Abyad kept on with him until he learned of it. Then he went until he came to Satan and said: By God, I have destroyed the man. He said: The white man went and confronted a man and strangled him. Then he came in the guise of a physician and said to his family, “Your friend has gone mad. Shall I treat him?” They said, Yes. He said to them, “I am not able to overcome his madness, but I will guide you to someone who will call upon God to cure him. Go to Barsisa, for he has the name by which if he calls upon it, it will be answered.” So they went to him and asked him about it. He prayed with those words and the devil left him. The white man did the same to the people and directed them to Barsisa, so they would pray and be cured. The white man went and confronted a slave girl from the daughters of the kings of the Children of Israel among three brothers. Their father was their king, but he died and left his brother in his place, and her uncle was the king of the Children of Israel. He tortured her and strangled her. Then he came to them in the guise of a physician and said, Do you want me to treat her? They said, Yes. He said, “The one who has afflicted her is an unbearable demon. But I will guide you to a man you trust. You can call upon him when her devil comes and he will pray for her until you know that she has been cured and you return her healthy.” They said, And who is he? Barsisa said, "They said, 'How can he respond to us in this matter when he is of greater importance than that?' He said, 'Then go and build a monastery next to his monastery so that you can overlook him. If he accepts it, then all is well. If not, put her in her monastery and tell him, 'It is a trust with you,' so he can be rewarded for it." He said: So they went to him and asked him, but he refused them. So they built a monastery as Al-Abyad had ordered them to do and put the slave girl in his monastery. They said: This is our sister, a trust, so be patient with her. Then they left. When Barsisa finished his prayer, he saw the slave girl and her beauty and loveliness, and she fell into his heart and a great thought entered his mind. Then he went back to his prayer and Satan came to her and strangled her. Barsisa called upon those prayers and Satan left her. Then he went back to his prayer and Satan came to her and strangled her. She used to uncover herself, so Satan came to him and said: Have intercourse with her, then she will repent and achieve what you want from the matter. So he did not stop until he had intercourse with her. He continued to do that until she became pregnant and her pregnancy became apparent. Then Satan said to him: Woe to you, Barsisa, you have been disgraced. Would you like to kill her and repent? If they ask you, say: Her devil took her, and I could not overpower him. So he entered and killed her, then went with her and buried her on the side of the mountain. The devil came while he was burying her at night and took hold of the edge of her garment, and one edge remained sticking out of the dirt. Then Barsisa returned to his cell and began to pray, when her brothers came to check on their sister. They used to come at the end of the days asking about her and recommending her to him. They said: O Barsisa, what has happened to our sister? He said: Her devil came and took her away, and I could not bear him. They believed him and left. When evening came and they were distressed, the devil came to the eldest of them in a dream and said: Woe to you, Barsisa did such and such to your sister and buried her in such and such a place. The brother said to himself: This is a dream and it is the work of the devil, and Barsisa is better than that. He said: Three nights followed one another and he did not care. So he went to the middle one with the same thing. The middle one said the same thing as the eldest, but he did not tell anyone. So he went to the youngest of them with the same thing. The youngest of them said to his two brothers, By God, I saw such and such. The middle one said, By God, I also saw the same. The eldest said, I also saw the same. So they went to Barsisa and said, O Barsisa, what has happened to our sister? He said, Did I not tell you about her condition? It is as if you accused me. They said, By God, we do not accuse you. They felt ashamed of him and left. Then Satan came to them and said, Woe to you! She is buried in such and such a place, and the end of her garment is sticking out of the dirt. So they went and saw their sister just as they had seen in their dream. They went with their masters and servants, with axes and shovels, and they demolished his cell and brought him down. Then they bound him and took him to the king. He confessed. Satan came to him and said, “You kill her and then act stubbornly. Two things will come together for you: murder and stubbornness.” He confessed. When he confessed, the king ordered him to be killed and crucified on a cross. When he was crucified, the white man came to him and said: O Barsisa, do you recognize me? He said: No. He said: “I am your companion who taught you the supplications and they answered you. Woe to you! You did not fear God in your trust! You betrayed its people and you claimed that you were the most worshipful of the Children of Israel. Are you not ashamed?” He kept taunting him, then he said at the end: Wasn’t what you did enough for you to admit it, disgrace yourself and disgrace your peers among the people? If you die in this state, none of your peers will succeed. He said: Then what should I do? He said: Obey me in one thing so that I may save you from what you are in, then I will seize them by their eyes and remove you from your place! He said: What is it? He said: Prostrate to me. He said: I cannot. He said: Do it. So he prostrated to him. The king said: “O Barsisa, this is what I wanted from you. The outcome of your matter was that you disbelieved in your Lord. I am innocent of you. “I fear God, Lord of the worlds.”
59:17: God the Most High says 17- So the outcome for them both, meaning Satan and that man, “was that they were both in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers.” Ibn Abbas said: God made this parable for the Jews of Banu Nadir and the hypocrites of Madinah. God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to expel Banu Nadir from Madinah, but the hypocrites infiltrated them and said: “Do not respond to Muhammad’s invitation to you and do not leave your homes.
