If he fights you, we will be with you, and if he expels you, we will leave with you.” So they responded to them and attacked their fortresses and fortified themselves in their homes, hoping for victory from the hypocrites, until the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to them and they waged war against him, hoping for victory from the hypocrites. But they let them down and disowned them, just as Satan disowned and abandoned Barsisa. So the outcome for both groups was the Fire. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: After that, the monks among the Children of Israel did not walk except with taqiyya and secrecy. The people of immorality and wickedness coveted the rabbis and accused them of slander and ugly things, until the matter of the monk Guraij came about. When God cleared him of what they accused him of, the monks expanded after him and appeared to the people. The story of Guraij was as follows: Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Zuhair bin Harb told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Jarir bin Hazim told us, Muhammad bin Sirin told us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “No one spoke in the cradle except three: Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and the companion of Jurayj. Jurayj was a devout man, so he built a monastery and stayed in it. His mother came to him while he was praying and said: ‘O Jurayj!’ He said: ‘O Lord, my mother and my prayer?’ So he went on praying, and she turned away. The next day she came to him while he was praying and said: ‘O Jurayj!’ He said: ‘O Lord, my mother and my prayer?’ So he went on praying, and she said: ‘O God, do not let him die until he sees the faces of prostitutes.’” The Children of Israel mentioned Gregory and his worship. There was a prostitute who used to imitate him with her beauty. She said, "If you wish, I will tempt him to tempt you." She approached him but he did not pay attention to her. So she went to a shepherd who was taking refuge in his cell and allowed him to have intercourse with her. He slept with her and she became pregnant. When she gave birth, she said, "This is from Gregory." So they went to him and forced him down from his cell, destroyed it and began beating him. He said, "What is the matter with you? They said, You committed adultery with this prostitute and she gave birth to you. He said, Where is the child?" So they brought him. He said, "Leave me until I pray." So he prayed and when he finished, he went to the child and stabbed him in the stomach. He said, "O boy, who is your father? He said, So-and-so the shepherd." They then turned to Gregory, kissing him and rubbing themselves against him. They said, "Shall we build you your cell of gold? He said, No, rebuild it of clay as it was." So they did. While a boy was breastfeeding from his mother, a man passed by riding on a luxurious and handsome mount. His mother said, O God, make my son like this one. He left the breast and turned to it. He looked at it and said, O God, do not make me like him. Then he turned to his breast and began to breastfeed. It was as if I could see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) narrating how he was breastfeeding with his index finger in his mouth and he began to suck it. He said: They passed by a slave girl and they were beating her and saying: I committed adultery and theft, and she was saying: God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. His mother said: O God, do not make my son like her. So he stopped breastfeeding and looked at her and said: O God, make me like her. Then they went back to the hadith and she said: A handsome man passed by and I said: O God, make my son like him. So I said: O God, do not make me like him. They passed by this slave girl and they were beating her and they were saying: I committed adultery and theft. So I said: O God, do not make my son like her. So I said: O God, make me like her. He said: That man was a tyrant, so I said: O God, do not make me like him. And this woman is being told: I committed adultery, but she did not commit adultery, and I stole, but she did not steal. So I said: O God, make me like her.
59:18: God Almighty says 18- O you who have believed, fear God and let a soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow, meaning for the Day of Resurrection, that is: let each one of you look to what he has put forth for himself, a good deed that will save him or a bad deed that will destroy him? “And fear God. Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do.”
59:19: 19- And do not be like those who forgot God, they abandoned God’s command, so He made them forget themselves, that is, their own fortunes until they did not do any good for themselves. Those are the wicked.
59:20: 20- “The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. It is the companions of Paradise who are the successful.”
59:21: God Almighty said: / If We had sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God. It was said: If a discernment were placed on the mountain and the Qur'an were sent down upon it, it would have humbled itself, split and cracked from fear of God, despite its solidity and solemnity, out of caution lest it not fulfill God Almighty's right in glorifying the Qur'an, and the disbeliever turns away from the lessons in it as if he did not hear them, describing him as having a hard heart, And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought.
59:22: 22- “He is God, other than whom there is no god. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.” The unseen means what is hidden from the servants, that they have not witnessed or known, and The witnessed means what they have witnessed and known. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
59:23: 23- He is God, other than whom there is no god, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Pure from every defect, the Exalted from what is not befitting of Him, “the Peace,” the One who is safe from deficiencies, the Believer, Ibn Abbas said: He is the One who made people feel safe from His oppression and made safe those who believe in Him from His punishment. It is from the sense of security which is the opposite of intimidation as He said: And He made them feel safe from fear (Quraysh 106:4). It was said: Its meaning is the One who confirms His messengers by showing miracles, and the One who confirms to the believers what He promised them of reward, and to the disbelievers what He threatened them of punishment. Al-Muhaymin The Dominant, the Witness over His servants for their deeds, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Muqatil. It is said: hayman yahaymin, fahuwa muhaymin, if he is a watcher over something. It is also said that in its original form it is mu'aymin, the hamza was changed to a ha, like their saying: raqat and haraqat, and its meaning is the believer. Al-Hasan said: the trustworthy. Al-Khalil said: he is the watchful preserver. Ibn Zayd said: the verifier. Sa'id ibn Al-Musayyab and Ad-Dahhak said: the judge. Ibn Kaysan said: it is one of the names of God in the Book, and God knows best its interpretation. The Mighty, the Compeller, Ibn Abbas said: The Compeller is the Great, and the compulsion of God is His greatness, and according to this saying it is an attribute of God. It was also said: It is from the word jabr which means to repair, it is said: you repaired the matter, and you repaired the bone if you fixed it after it was broken, so He enriches the poor and fixes the broken. Al-Suddi and Muqatil said: He is the one who subdues people and compels them to do what He wants. Some of them were asked about the meaning of Al-Jabbar, so he said: He is the Subduer who, when He wants something, does it, and nothing can prevent Him from doing it. The Arrogant, the one who is too arrogant to do anything bad. It has also been said: the one who is too proud to do anything that is not befitting of him. The root of arrogance and pride is abstention. It has also been said: the one with pride, which is the king. Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him.
59:24: 24- He is God, the Creator, the Determiner and the Transformer of things by planning into something else, as He said: He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation (al-Zumar 39:6) the Maker, the Originator of things from nothingness into existence the Fashioner, the Representative of created things by signs that distinguish some from others. It is said: This is the image of the matter, meaning its example: first it is creation, then creation, then fashioning. “To Him belong the best names. Whatever is in the heavens and earth glorifies Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjuwayh told me, Ibn Shaiba told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ahmad ibn Abi Shuraih and Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us, they said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, Khalid ibn Tahman told us, Nafi’ ibn Abi Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Muqal ibn Yasar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says in the morning - three times - ‘I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Satan the accursed,’ and recites the three verses from the end of Surat al-Hashr, God will assign seventy thousand angels to pray for him until the evening. If he dies on that day, he will die a martyr. And whoever says it in the evening will be in the same position.” It was narrated by Abu Isa on the authority of Mahmoud bin Ghailan on the authority of Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri with this chain of transmission, and he said: This is a strange hadith that we do not know except from this source.
60:1: 1- O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, the verse. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told me that he heard Abdullah bin Abi Rafi’ say: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me, Al-Zubayr, and Al-Miqdad and said: Go until you come to Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman there with a letter, so take it from her. So we set off, our horses racing with us until we came to the garden, and there we saw the woman. We said: Bring out the letter. She said: I do not have a letter. We said: Either bring out the letter or throw away the clothes. So she took it out from her tie and brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In it was a message from Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah to some of the polytheists in Mecca, informing them of some of the affairs of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: O Hatib, what is this? He said: O Messenger of God, do not rush me, for I was a man who was attached to the Quraysh.” -He says I was an ally and not one of them- and those with you from the emigrants had relatives with whom they could protect their families and their money, so I wanted - since I lacked that lineage among them - to take a hand with them so they could protect my relatives, and I did not do it out of apostasy from my religion nor acceptance of disbelief after Islam, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, he has told you the truth, so Omar said: O Messenger of God, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite, so he said: Indeed, he witnessed Badr, and how do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do what you will, for I have forgiven you, so God, the Most High, revealed this Surah: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection until His saying: the right way. The commentators said: The verse was revealed about Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah as it came in the hadith. Sarah, the freed slave of Abu Amr bin Saifi bin Hashim bin Abd Manaf, came to Medina from Mecca, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was preparing to conquer Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Have you come as a Muslim? She said: No. He said: Have you come as a emigrant? She said: No. He said: So what brought you? She said: You were the origin, the clan, and the clients, and my clients are gone, and I am in dire need, so I came to you so that you might give me some food, clothe me, and carry me. He said to her: Where are you compared to the young men of Mecca? She was a singer and a mourner, she said: Nothing was asked of me / after the Battle of Badr, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged the Banu Abd al-Muttalib and the Banu al-Muttalib, so they gave her provisions, clothed her and carried her. Then Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah, an ally of Banu Asad bin Abd al-Uzza, came to her and wrote with her to the people of Mecca, and gave her ten dinars, and clothed her in a cloak, on the condition that she deliver the letter to the people of Mecca, and he wrote in the letter: From Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah to the people of Mecca, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wants you, so be on your guard. Sarah went out, and Gabriel came down and informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what he had done. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali, Ammar, Az-Zubayr, Talhah, Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, and Abu Marthad as horsemen. He said to them: Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman there with a letter from Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah to the polytheists. Take it from her and let her go, and if she does not hand it over to you, then strike off her head. He said: So they went out until they caught up with her in the place that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had mentioned. They said to her: Where is the letter? She swore by God that she did not have a letter with her. They searched for her and her belongings but did not find any with her. They intended to go back, but Ali may God be pleased with him said: By God, we have not lied and neither has the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He drew his sword and said: Bring out the letter or I will strip you and cut off your head. When she saw the seriousness, she took it out from her forelock which she had hidden in her hair. They let her go and did not interfere with her or what she had with her. They returned with the letter to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent for Hatib, who came to him and said: Do you know the Book? He said: Yes. He said: What made you do what you did? He said: O Messenger of God, by God I have not disbelieved since I became a Muslim, nor have I deceived you since I advised you, nor have I loved them since I left them, but there was not one of the emigrants who did not have someone in Mecca to protect his clan, and I was a stranger among them, and my family was among them, so I feared for my family, so I wanted to take a hand with them, although I knew that God would bring down His punishment upon them, and that my Book would not avail them at all. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) believed him and excused him. Omar bin Al-Khattab stood up and said: O Messenger of God, let me strike off the head of this hypocrite. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How do you know, Omar? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said to them: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you. Then God, the Almighty, revealed concerning Hatib: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies. “You throw them affection,” it was said: meaning affection, and the ba is redundant, like His statement: And whoever intends therein to commit injustice or wrong (al-Hajj 22:25). Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that you throw to them the report of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his secret with the affection that is between you and them, and they have disbelieved, the waw is for the state, meaning: and their state is that they disbelieved, in what came to you of the truth, meaning the Qur’an, they expel the Messenger and you, from Mecca, because you believe, meaning because you believed, as if he said: They do that because of your belief, in God, your Lord, if you have gone out, this is a condition whose answer precedes, which is His statement: “Do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, throwing them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, they expel the Messenger and you because you believe in God, your Lord, if you have gone out,” fighting in My cause and seeking My pleasure, you throw them affection, Muqatil said: with advice, and I know what you conceal, of affection for the disbelievers, and what you declare, what you show with your tongues, “and from Whoever among you does that has strayed from the right path, and has lost the right path.
60:2: 2- If they find you, if they conquer you and see you, they will be enemies to you and will stretch out their hands against you, by beating and killing, and their tongues with evil, by cursing, and they would love that you would disbelieve, as they disbelieved. He says: Do not advise them, for they will not advise you and will not befriend you.
60:3: 3- Your wombs will not benefit you, meaning: your wombs, relatives, and children in Mecca will not call you or lead you to betray the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the believers, or to abandon advising them and to befriend their enemies. Your wombs, nor your children, for whose sake you disobeyed God, "will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between you", and those who obey Him will enter Paradise and those who disobey Him will enter Hell. Asim and Ya'qub read Yafsal with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the sad, with a lightened pronunciation. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the sad, with a shaddah. Ibn 'Amir read it with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the sad, with a shaddah. The others read it with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the sad, with a lightened pronunciation. And God is Seeing of what you do.
60:4: 4- There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, of the people of faith, when they said to their people, of the polytheists, Indeed, we are disassociated from you, the plural of disassociated, “and from that which you worship besides God. We have disbelieved in you,” we have denied and rejected your religion, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone, He orders Hatib and the believers to follow the example of Abraham, peace be upon him, and those believers with him in disassociating themselves from the polytheists, except for the saying of Abraham to his father, ‘I will surely ask forgiveness for you,’ meaning: You have an excellent example in Abraham and his affairs except in his asking forgiveness for his polytheist father, for Abraham, peace be upon him, had said to his father: I will surely ask forgiveness for you, then he disassociated himself from him—as we mentioned in Surat At-Tawbah—and I do not possess for you anything against God, Abraham, peace be upon him, says to his father: I cannot do anything for you, nor can I ward off…” God’s punishment will be removed from you if you disobey Him and associate others with Him. Our Lord, in You we have put our trust, said Abraham and the believers with him. And to You we have turned back, and to You is the final destination.
60:5: 5- Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve. Al-Zajjaj said: Do not make them prevail over us, lest they think that they are on the truth and be tempted. Mujahid said: Do not punish us by their hands or by a punishment from You, lest they say: If these people had been on the truth, this would not have happened to them. “And forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
60:6: 6- There has certainly been for you in them, meaning in Abraham and those with him, an excellent pattern for anyone whose hope is in God and the Last Day. This is instead of saying for you, and it is a clarification that this pattern is for anyone who fears God and fears the punishment of the Hereafter. But whoever turns away, turns away from faith and befriends the disbelievers, then indeed, God is the Free of need, of His creation, the Praiseworthy, of His friends and those who obey Him.
60:7: Muqatil said: When God commanded the believers to be hostile to the disbelievers, the believers became hostile to their polytheist relatives and showed them enmity and disavowal. God knows the intensity of the believers' distress at this, so He revealed: 7- Perhaps God will establish between you and those among them with whom you have been at enmity, meaning the infidels of Mecca, affection. So God did that, as many of them converted to Islam and became their allies and brothers, and they mingled with them and married them. And God is All-Powerful, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.
60:8: Then God Almighty permitted the connection of those who did not fight the believers and did not fight them, saying: 8- God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them, meaning God does not forbid you from being righteous toward those who do not fight you, and from being just toward them, be fair and kind to them, for God loves those who are just. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Khuza’ah, who had made a peace treaty with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the condition that they would not fight him or support anyone against him, so God permitted being righteous toward them. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr said: It was revealed about Asma bint Abi Bakr. Her mother, Qutaylah bint Abd Al-Uzza, came to her in Madinah with gifts of dates, dried yogurt, and butter, and she was a polytheist. Asma said: I will not accept any gift from you, and do not enter my house until I ask permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So she asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed this verse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded her to enter her house, accept her gift, honor her, and treat her well. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah told us, Hatim told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Asma bint Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “My mother came to me while she was a polytheist during the time of the Quraysh when they made a treaty with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their agreement with her father. So I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, my mother has come to me and she is in need. Should I maintain ties with her? He said: Maintain ties with her.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah that he said: God revealed about it: God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion.
60:9: Then he mentioned those whom he forbade from connecting with, saying: 9- God only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion, and they are the polytheists of Mecca, “from taking them as allies. And whoever takes them as allies - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.”
60:10: God Almighty says: 10- O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them, the verse. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me that he heard Marwan and Al-Miswar bin Makhramah narrating on the authority of the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said: “When Suhayl bin Amr wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day, among the conditions that Suhayl bin Amr stipulated to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was: that no one from us should come to you - even if he was of your religion - except that you return him to us and leave us alone with him. The believers disliked that and Suhayl refused to do anything else, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to him on that day, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned Abu Jandal to his father Suhayl bin Amr, and no man came to him except that he returned him during that period, even if he was a Muslim. The believing women came as emigrants, and Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt was among those who went out to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day as an emigrant, and she was a free woman. Her family came asking the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to return her to them, but he did not return her to them because God revealed about them: “When believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. God knows best about their faith” to nor are they lawful for them. Urwa said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to test them with this verse: O Prophet, when believing women come to you, until His saying: Forgiving, Most Merciful. Urwa said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: Whoever among them acknowledged this condition, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say to her, I have pledged allegiance to you, with words he spoke to her. By God, his hand never touched a woman’s hand in pledging allegiance. He only pledged allegiance to them with his words. Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to perform Umrah, and when he reached Al-Hudaybiyyah, the polytheists of Mecca made peace with him on the condition that whoever came to him from the people of Mecca would be returned to them, and whoever came to the people of Mecca from the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would not be returned to him. They wrote a letter to that effect and sealed it. Subay’ah bint Al-Harith Al-Aslamiyah came as a Muslim after the letter was finished. Her husband, a traveler from Banu Makhzum - Muqatil said: He was Saifi bin Al-Rahib - came looking for her, and he was a disbeliever. He said: O Muhammad, return my wife to me, for you stipulated that you would return to us whoever came to you from us. This fold of the letter had not yet dried. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants from the land of disbelief to the land of Islam, test them. Ibn Abbas said: Her test is that she swears that she did not go out of hatred for her husband, nor out of love for a Muslim man, nor out of desire for one land to another, nor because of an event she had started, nor to seek worldly gain. She only went out of a desire for Islam and love for God and His Messenger. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made her swear to do so, and she swore, but he did not reject her. He gave her husband her dowry and what he had spent on her. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, married her. He used to reject any men who came to him and detain any women who came to him after testing them, and he would give their husbands their dowries. God knows best about their faith, meaning this is a test for you, and God knows best about them. "And if you ascertain that they are believers, do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them," what God has made lawful for a believing woman to a disbeliever. And give them, meaning their disbelieving husbands, what they spent, on them, meaning the dowry that they paid to them. And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their due compensation, meaning their dowries. God has permitted them to be married to Muslims, even if they have husbands in the land of disbelief, because Islam has differentiated between them and their disbelieving husbands. And do not hold on, Abu Amr and Ya'qub read it with a shaddah, and the others read it with a light shaddah, from holding on, to the bonds of the disbelieving women. "Braces is the plural of bondage," which is what one holds on to through marriage and lineage. "Disbelieving women is the plural of disbelieving woman." God forbade believers from marrying polytheistic women. He said: If someone has a non-Muslim wife in Mecca, then she should not be counted, because the marital bond between them has been broken. Al-Zuhri said: When this verse was revealed, Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him divorced two polytheist wives he had in Mecca: Quraibah bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughira, who was married to Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan after him, while they were still polytheists in Mecca. The other was Umm Kulthum bint Amr ibn Jarwal al-Khuza'iyyah, the mother of his son Abdullah ibn Umar, who was married to Abu Jahm ibn Hudhafah ibn Ghanim, while they were still polytheists. Arwa bint Rabia ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib was married to Talha ibn Ubaydullah, but Talha migrated while she was in Mecca following the religion of her people, and Islam caused a separation between them. After Islam, Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As ibn Umayyah married her. Al-Sha’bi said: Zainab, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the wife of Abu al-‘As ibn al-Rabi’. She converted to Islam and joined the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu al-‘As stayed in Mecca as a polytheist, then came to Medina and converted to Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned her to him. And ask, O believers, what you have spent, meaning: If a woman from among you joins the polytheists as an apostate, then ask what you have spent of the dowry if they withhold it from the one from whom she marries them, and let them ask, meaning: the polytheists whose wives have joined you, what they have spent, of the dowry from the one from among you who marries her. That is the judgment of God; He judges between you, and God is Knowing and Wise. Al-Zuhri said: If it were not for the truce and treaty that was between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Quraysh on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, he would have kept the women and not returned the dowry, and this is what he did with the Muslim women who came to him before the treaty.
60:11: When this verse was revealed, the believers acknowledged the ruling of God Almighty and paid what they were commanded to do regarding the expenses of the polytheists on their women. The polytheists refused to acknowledge the ruling of God regarding what they were commanded to do regarding the expenses of the Muslims on their women, so God Almighty revealed: 11- And if any of your wives have passed you by to the disbelievers, so they joined them as apostates, then you punished them, the commentators said: its meaning is you took spoils, meaning you raided and took from the disbelievers a consequence, which is the spoils. It was also said: you were victorious and the consequence was yours. It was also said: you inflicted punishment on them in battle until you took spoils. Hamid Al-A’raj read Faqabtum with a shaddah. Az-Zuhri read: Faqabtum without an alif. Mujahid read Faqabahum, meaning you did to them as they did to you. All of these are languages with the same meaning. It is said: a’qab, a’qab, and a’qab, and a’qab, ta’taba’, and it’taqab: if you took spoils. It was also said: ta’qeeb means raid after raid. Then give those whose wives have gone, to the disbelievers among you, the equivalent of what they spent, on them from the spoils that came into your hands from the disbelievers’ money. It was also said: you punished the apostate by killing them. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: Six women from the believing women and emigrants joined the polytheists: Umm Al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who was married to Ayyad bin Shaddad Al-Fihri; Fatima bint Abi Umayya bin Al-Mughira, the sister of Umm Salamah, who was married to Umar bin Al-Khattab, but when Umar wanted to emigrate, she refused and apostatized; Baru’ bint Uqba, who was married to Shammas bin Uthman; ‘Uzza bin ‘Abd Al-‘Aziz bin Nadlah, whose husband was ‘Amr bin ‘Abd Wudd; Hind bint Abi Jahl bin Hisham, who was married to Hisham bin Al-‘As bin Wa’il; and Umm Kulthum bint Jarwal, who was married to ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab. All of them reverted from Islam, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave their husbands the dowries of their women from the spoils of war. And fear God, in whom you believe. There is a difference of opinion as to whether returning the dowry of women who convert to Islam to their husbands is obligatory or recommended. The origin of the truce was that it included the return of the women. There are two opinions: One of them is that it included the return of both men and women, based on what we have narrated: No one from us comes to you, even if he is of your religion, except that you return him to us. Then the ruling regarding the return of the women was abrogated by His statement: Then do not return them to the disbelievers. Based on this, returning the dowry was obligatory. The other opinion is that the peace treaty did not apply to returning the women, because it was narrated from Ali: No man from us comes to you, even if he is of your religion, except that you return him to us. This is because there is no fear for a man from the temptation of returning him as there is fear for a woman from being harmed by a polytheist, and there is no guarantee for her from apostasy if she is afraid and forced to do so due to the weakness of her heart and the lack of guidance to the way out of it by declaring the word of disbelief with dissimulation and concealing faith. There is no fear for the man due to his strength and guidance to taqiyya. So based on this, returning the dowry is recommended. They differed as to whether it must be applied today in returning money if it was stipulated in a contract with infidels? Some people said: It is not necessary, and they claimed that the verse was abrogated, which is the opinion of Ata’, Mujahid, and Qatadah. Some people said: It is not abrogated and they will be given back what they spent.
60:12: God Almighty said: 12- O Prophet, when the believing women come to you to pledge allegiance to you, the verse. That was on the day of the conquest of Mecca, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished pledging allegiance to the men, and he was on Safa and Omar ibn al-Khattab was below him, and he was pledging allegiance to the women on the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and conveying it to them, and Hind bint Utbah, the wife of Abu Sufyan, was veiled and disguised with the women for fear that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recognize her, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will pledge allegiance to you that you will not associate anything with God, so Hind raised her head and said: By God, you are demanding from us something that we have never seen you demand from men, and the men pledged allegiance at that time to Islam and jihad only, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And they shall not steal, so Hind said: Abu Sufyan is a stingy man, and I have taken small amounts of his money, so I do not know whether it is permissible for me or not? Abu Sufyan said: Whatever you have acquired in the past and in the future is lawful for you. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) laughed and recognized her. He said to her: And you belong to Hind bint Utbah? She said: Yes, so pardon what has passed, may God pardon you. He said: And they do not commit adultery. Hind said: Does a free woman commit adultery? He said: And they do not kill their children. Hind said: We raised them when they were young and killed them when they were adults, so you and he know best. Her son Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan had been killed on the day of Badr. Umar may God be pleased with him laughed until he lay down, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) smiled. He said: And they do not come with a slander they have invented between their hands and feet - meaning that she accuses her husband of having a child that is not his. Hind said: By God, slander is ugly, and you only command us to be guided and have good morals. He said: And they do not disobey you in what is right. Hind said: We have not sat here with the intention of disobeying you in anything. The women acknowledged what had been taken from them. The Almighty said: And let them not kill their children, meaning burying girls alive, which was practiced by the people of the pre-Islamic era. His statement, And let them not bring forth a slander which they have invented between their hands and feet: This does not mean that they are forbidden from committing adultery, because the prohibition of adultery has been mentioned previously. Rather, what is meant by it is that she should pick up a newborn and say to her husband, This is my child from you. This is a slander invented between their hands and feet, because when the mother gives birth to the child, he falls between her hands and feet. His statement, and not let them disobey you in what is right: meaning, in every matter that is in accordance with obedience to God. Bakr ibn Abdullah Al-Muzani said: In every matter in which there is guidance for them. Mujahid said: A woman should not be alone with men. Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, Al-Kalbi, and Abd Al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: It is the prohibition of wailing, calling for woe, tearing one’s garment, shaving or plucking one’s hair, and scratching one’s face. A woman should not speak to men except with a mahram, and she should not be alone with a man who is not a mahram, and she should not travel except with a mahram. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Muammar told us, Abdul Warith told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Hafsa bint Sirin, on the authority of Umm Atiyya, who said: “We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited to us ‘that they should not associate anything with God,’ and he forbade us from wailing. A woman withdrew her hand and said: So-and-so has made me happy, and I want to reward her. But the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say anything to her, so she went and came back and he pledged allegiance to her.” Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Daynuri told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili told us, Hadbah ibn Khalid told us, Abaan ibn Yazid told us, Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us, that Zaid told him, that Abu Salam told him, that Abu Malik al-Ash’ari told him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are four things in my nation from the practices of ignorance that they will not abandon: boasting about lineage, slandering genealogies, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing.” He also said: If a wailing woman does not repent before her death, she will rise on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment of tar and a coat of scabies. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Amr bin Hafs told us, my father told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He is not one of us who strikes his cheeks, tears his garments, and calls out with the call of the Age of Ignorance. His saying: Then pledge allegiance to them, meaning if they pledge allegiance to you, then pledge allegiance to them, and ask forgiveness for them from God, for God is Forgiving and Merciful. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Mahmud told me, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwa, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pledge allegiance to women by reciting this verse: ‘They shall not associate anything with God.’ She said: The hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never touched the hand of a woman except a woman he owned.” Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha’labi told us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hamdun told us, Makki ibn Abdun told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who heard Umaimah bint Ruqayqah say: “I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the company of some women. He said to us: ‘As much as you are able and capable of.’ I said: ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more merciful to us than we are to ourselves.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, pledge allegiance to us.’ Sufyan said: ‘He meant shake hands with us.’ He said: ‘I do not shake hands with women. My words to one woman are like my words to one hundred women.’”
60:13: God the Almighty said: 13- "O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry," meaning the Jews. This is because some poor Muslims used to inform the Jews of report about the Muslims, thus reaching them and obtaining some of their fruits. So God forbade them from doing so. "They have despaired, meaning these Jews, of the Hereafter, that they would have any reward or good in it, just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves," meaning: just as the disbelievers who died and were in the graves despaired of having any share or reward in the Hereafter. Mujahid said: When the disbelievers entered their graves, they despaired of God's mercy. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers who died and saw the Hereafter despaired. It was also said: just as the disbelievers despaired of the inhabitants of the graves ever returning to them.
61:1: 1- “Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God. He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
61:2: 2- O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? The commentators said: The believers said: If we knew the most beloved deeds to God Almighty, we would do them, and we would spend our money and our lives on them. Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks. So they were tested with that on the Day of Uhud, so they turned their backs, so God Almighty revealed: Why do you say that which you do not do? Muhammad bin Kaab said: When God Almighty informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the reward of the martyrs of Badr, the Companions said: If we encounter fighting after that, we will do our best in it. So they fled on the day of Uhud, and God reproached them with this verse. Qatada and Al-Dahhak said: It was revealed regarding fighting. A man would say: I fought and he did not fight, I stabbed and he did not stab, I struck and he did not strike. So this verse was revealed. Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed about the hypocrites who promised victory to the believers, but they were lying.
61:3: 3- It is most hateful to God that you should say, in the nominative case, so it is like saying, Your brother is a bad man. The meaning of the verse is: That is, it is most hateful and detestable to God, meaning: God hates with intense hatred that you say what you do not do, that you promise something of yourselves and then do not fulfill it.
61:4: 4- Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, meaning they line themselves up in ranks when fighting / and do not move from their places, as if they were a solid structure, some of which has been joined together [i.e. some of it has been stuck together] and made firm so that there is no gap or defect in it, and it has been said that it is like lead.
61:5: 5- And when Moses said to his people, from the Children of Israel: O my people, why do you harm me? That was when they threw stones at him, while you know that I am the Messenger of God to you, and the Messenger is glorified, honored, and respected. But when they deviated, they turned away from the truth, God made their hearts deviate, He turned them away from the truth, meaning that when they abandoned the truth by harming their prophet, God turned their hearts away from the truth. And God does not guide the wicked people, Al-Zajjaj said: meaning He does not guide those whom He knew beforehand were wicked.
61:6: 6- “And when Jesus, son of Mary, said, ‘O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a Messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad.’” The alif in it is for exaggeration of praise, and it has two aspects: One of them: It is an exaggeration of the subject, meaning that all the prophets praise God Almighty, and he praises God more than others. The second: It is an exaggeration of the object, meaning that all the prophets are praised for the praiseworthy qualities in them, and he is the most exaggerated of them and the most comprehensive of the virtues and good qualities for which he is praised. So when he brought them clear proofs, they said, 'This is obvious magic.'
61:7: 7- And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God while he is being invited to Islam? And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
61:8: 8- They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
61:9: 9- It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although they who associate others with God dislike it.
61:10: 10- O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? Ibn Amir read will save you with emphasis, and the others with emphasis, from a painful punishment. This was revealed when they said: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God Almighty, we would do them. He made that like a transaction because through it they gain God’s pleasure, attainment of His Paradise, and salvation from the Fire.
61:11: Then he explained that trade and said: 11- “You believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew.”
61:12: 12- “He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in the Gardens of Eden. That is the great attainment.”
61:13: 13- "And another which you love," meaning: You have another characteristic in this world along with the reward of the Hereafter that you love, and that characteristic is: "Victory from God and an imminent conquest." Al-Kalbi said: It is the victory over Quraysh and the conquest of Mecca. Ata' said: He means the conquest of Persia and Rome. "And give good tidings to the believers, O Muhammad, of victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter.
61:14: Then he urged them to support the religion and fight the opponents, saying: 14- O you who have believed, be supporters of God. The people of Hijaz and Abu Amr read: supporters, with the tanween for God with the lam of addition. The others read: supporters of God, added to his saying: We are supporters of God. "As Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples," meaning, support the religion of God as the disciples supported him when Jesus, peace be upon him, said to them: "Who will be my helpers for God?" Meaning: Who will support me with God? "The disciples said, 'We are the helpers of God.' So a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved." Ibn Abbas said: This means during the time of Jesus, peace be upon him. This is because when he was taken up, his people split into three groups: a group said, 'God was, so he was taken up.' A group said, 'He was the Son of God, so God raised him up to Him.' A group said, 'He was the servant and messenger of God, so He raised him up to Him.' They are the believers. Each group was followed by a group of people, and they fought, and the two disbelieving groups were victorious over the believers, until God sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the believing group was victorious over the disbelieving group. This is what God Almighty said: "So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant," superior and victorious. Mughira narrated on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: So the proof of those who believed in Jesus became apparent by Muhammad's belief that Jesus is the Word of God and His Spirit.
62:1: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
62:2: 2- It is He who has sent among the unlettered ones, meaning the Arabs were an illiterate nation that could neither read nor write, a Messenger from among themselves, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, whose lineage is their lineage and whose language is their language, so that he may be more effective in establishing proof against them, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom - although they were before in clear error, meaning that before the mission of the Messenger they were in clear error, worshipping idols.
62:3: 3- And others among them. In others, there are two ways of parsing: one is the accusative, referring back to the illiterate, meaning: and in others. The second is the accusative, referring back to the ha’ and the mim in His statement, And He teaches them, meaning He teaches others among them, meaning among the believers who follow their religion, because if they become Muslims, they become among them, for all Muslims are one nation. Scholars differed about them. Some people said: They are the Persians. This is the opinion of Ibn Omar and Saeed bin Jubair, and the narration of Laith on the authority of Mujahid. The evidence for this is: Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Mu`allim al-Tusi told us about it. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ya`qub told us. Abu al-Nasr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us. Al-Husayn ibn Sufyan, `Ali ibn Tayfur, and Abu al-`Abbas al-Thaqafi told us. They said: Qutaybah told us. `Abd al-`Aziz told us, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Abu al-Ghaith, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “We were sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when Surat al-Jumu`ah was revealed to him. When he recited: ‘And others among them who have not yet joined them,’ a man said: ‘Who are these, O Messenger of God?’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not respond to him until he had asked him two or three times. He said: ‘And among us is Salman al-Farsi.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed his hand on Salman and then said: ‘If faith were at the Pleiades, men from among these would attain it.’” Abu Saeed Abdullah bin Ahmed Al-Tahiri told us, my grandfather Abdul Samad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Bazzar told us, Muhammad bin Zakariya Al-Adhafri told us, Ishaq Al-Dabry told us, Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Jaafar Al-Jazari, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Asam, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If the religion were at the Pleiades, a man, or he said: men, from the sons of Persia would go to it and attain it.” Ikrimah and Muqatil said: They are the Followers. Ibn Zayd said: They are all those who entered Islam after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the Day of Resurrection. This is / the narration of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid. His statement, They have not yet reached them, means they have not yet reached them, but they will come after them. It was also said, They have not yet reached them, meaning in merit and precedence, because the followers will not reach the status of the Companions. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
62:4: 4- That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills, meaning Islam and guidance. And God is the possessor of great bounty.
62:5: God Almighty said: 5- The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah, meaning they were charged with carrying it out and acting according to what was in it, then did not take it up, they did not act according to what was in it and did not fulfill its right, is like that of a donkey carrying volumes, meaning books of knowledge, the singular of which is safar. Al-Farra’ said: They are the great books, meaning just as a donkey carries them and does not know what is in them and does not benefit from them, so too the Jews read the Torah but do not benefit from it because they disobeyed what was in it. “Evil is the example of the people who deny the signs of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people,” those who wronged themselves by denying the prophets, peace be upon them, meaning whoever knew in advance that he would not believe, He does not guide them.
62:6: 6- Say, ‘O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of the people,’ not Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, then wish for death, so call for death upon yourselves, if you should be truthful, that you are the children of God and His beloved, for death is what will lead you to Him.
62:7: 7- “And they will never desire it, because of what their hands have put forth. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.”
62:8: 8- “Say, ‘Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you about what you used to do.’”
62:9: God Almighty said: 9- O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday, meaning on Friday, as He said: Show me what they have created on the earth [meaning on the earth], and by this call He meant the call to prayer when the imam sits on the pulpit to deliver the sermon. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam told us, Ibn Abi Dhi’b told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Al-Sa’ib bin Yazid, who said: “The first call to prayer on Friday was when the imam sat on the pulpit during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, and Umar. Then, when Uthman came and the number of people increased, the second call to prayer was added to the pulpit.” Al-A’mash read: from the day of Friday with a sukoon on the meem, while the general public read it with a damma on it. They differed over the naming of this day, Friday. Some said: Because God Almighty gathered the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, on it. Another said: Because God Almighty finished creating things on it, and the creations gathered on it. Another said: Because groups gather on it. Another said: Because people gather on it for prayer. It was said: The first to call it Friday was Ka’b bin Lu’ay. Abu Salamah said: The first to say After was Ka’b bin Lu’ay, and he was the first to call Friday Friday, and it was called the Day of Arabism. On the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: The people of Madinah gathered before the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Madinah and before the revelation of the word Friday was made. They were the ones who named it Friday. They said: The Jews have a day on which they gather every seven days, and the Christians have a day on which they gather, so let us make a day on which we gather, remember God and pray. They said: Saturday is for the Jews and Sunday is for the Christians, so make it the Day of Arabism. So they gathered before As’ad ibn Zurarah, who led them in two rak’ahs of prayer and reminded them, so they named it Friday. Then God, the Exalted, revealed a verse about that later. It was narrated on the authority of Abdur-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, on the authority of his father Ka'b, that whenever he heard the call to prayer on Friday, he would pray for mercy for As'ad ibn Zurarah. I said to him, When you hear the call to prayer, do you pray for mercy for As'ad ibn Zurarah? He said, Because he was the first to gather us in Hazm al-Nabi' in Harrat Bani Bayadah, in a place called Baqi' al-Khadimat. I said to him, How many were you that day? He said, Forty. As for the first Friday prayer that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gathered his companions, as the biographers have mentioned, when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) arrived in Madinah as a migrant, he stayed in Quba' with Banu Amr ibn Awf. That was on a Monday, twelfth night of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, when the forenoon had spread. He stayed in Quba' on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, and established their mosque. Then he left their midst on Friday, heading for Madinah. The Friday prayer caught up with him in Banu Salim ibn Awf, in the middle of a valley belonging to them. Today, he had built a mosque in that place, so he gathered there and delivered the sermon." The Almighty said: So hasten to the remembrance of God, meaning: go to it and work for it. What is meant by striving is not hastening, but rather what is meant by it is work and action, as He said: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land (al-Baqarah 2:205), and He said: Indeed, your striving is diverse (al-Layl 92:4). Omar ibn al-Khattab used to recite: Then proceed to the remembrance of God, and Abdullah ibn Masoud used to recite the same. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is not about striving on foot, and they were forbidden to come to prayer except with tranquility and dignity, but with hearts, intention, and humility. Qatada said about this verse: So strive towards the remembrance of God. He said: Striving is to strive with your heart and your actions, which is walking towards it. He used to interpret his statement: And when he reached the age of striving with him (al-Saffat 37:102) as meaning when he walked with him. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Maqil al-Maydani told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the prayer is established, do not come running, but come walking, with tranquility and dignity. Pray whatever you catch up with, and complete whatever you miss.” His saying, to the remembrance of God, meaning to prayer. Saeed ibn al-Musayyab said, So hasten to the remembrance of God, meaning the imam’s sermon. And leave off trading, meaning buying and selling because the word trading includes both. Trading and buying are only prohibited at the second call to prayer. Al-Zuhri said, when the imam comes out. Ad-Dahhak said, When the sun has passed its zenith, trading and buying are prohibited. “That,” what I mentioned about attending Friday prayers and refraining from trading, is better for you, than trading, if you only knew, the interests of yourselves. Know that the Friday prayer is an individual obligation. It is obligatory for everyone who is sane, of age, free, male, and resident in the country, if they have no excuse. Whoever neglects it is subject to the threat. As for the boy and the insane, there is no Friday prayer for them, because they are not among those who are obligated to perform the obligatory prayers due to the deficiency of their bodies. There is no Friday prayer for women, by consensus: Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al Khallal told us, Abu Al Abbas Al Asam told us, Al Rabi’ told us, Al Shafi’i told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, Salamah bin Abdullah Al Khatmi told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b that he heard a man from Banu Wa’il say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Friday prayer is obligatory for every Muslim except a woman, a boy, or a slave. Most of them said that there is no Friday prayer for slaves. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Al-Awza’i said: The exits are obligatory for the slave, but they are not obligatory for the traveler, according to the majority. Al-Nakha’i and Al-Zuhri said: It is obligatory for the traveler if he hears the call to prayer. Anyone who has an excuse such as illness, caring for a sick person, or fear is permitted to miss Friday prayers. Likewise, he may miss them due to the excuse of rain or mud. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musaddad told us, Ismail told us, Abdul Hamid Sahib Al-Ziyadi told me, Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Omar told us, Muhammad bin Sirin told us that Ibn Abbas said to his muezzin on a rainy day: When you say: I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, do not say: Come to prayer. Say: Pray in your homes. The people seemed to find it strange, so he said: Someone better than me did it. Friday is an obligation, and I hated to take you out so you could walk in mud and sand. Anyone who is not required to attend Friday prayers, if he attends and prays with the imam on Friday, the obligation of noon prayer is waived for him, but he does not complete the number of Friday prayers except for someone who has an excuse, because if he attends, he completes the number. Imam Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamuyeh al-Sarakhsi told us in the year 381 AH, Isa ibn Umar ibn al-Abbas al-Samarqandi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi al-Samarqandi told us, Yahya ibn Hassan told us, Muawiyah ibn Salam told us, Zaid ibn Salam told me that he heard Abu Salam say, al-Hakam ibn Mina told me that Ibn Umar told him and Abu Hurayrah that they heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the steps of his pulpit: Let some people stop neglecting the Friday prayers, or God will seal their hearts and then they will be among the heedless. Abu Uthman Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Ali bin Khashram told us, Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Ubaidah bin Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Al-Ja`d, meaning Al-Damri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever misses the Friday prayer three times out of negligence, God will seal his heart. Scholars differed regarding the location of the Friday prayer, the number of people required to perform it, and the distance from which it must be performed: As for the location: Some people went to the view that every village in which forty men of perfect character gather, meaning that they are free, sane, adults, and residents who do not leave it in winter or summer except for a necessary departure, it is obligatory for them to hold the Friday prayer there. This is the view of Ubaydullah bin Abdullah and Umar bin Abdul Aziz, and it was also the view of Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. They said: The Friday prayer cannot be held with fewer than forty men in this manner. Umar bin Abdul Aziz stipulated that there should be a governor among them, along with the number of forty, but the governor is not a condition according to Al-Shafi’i. Ali said: There is no Friday prayer except in Egypt, and this is the opinion of the people of opinion. Then according to Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, it is valid with four, and the governor is a condition. Al-Awza’i and Abu Yusuf said: It is valid with three if there is a governor among them. Al-Hasan and Abu Thawr said: It is valid with two like all other prayers. Rabi’ah said: It is valid with twelve men. The evidence for the permissibility of holding it in villages is as follows: Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Amir Al-Aqdi told us, Ibrahim bin Tahman told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza Al-Dab’i, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The first Friday prayer that was held after the Friday prayer in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the mosque of Abdul Qais in Jawatha in Bahrain.” If a person resides in a village where Friday prayer is not held, or if he resides in the wilderness, some scholars hold that if the call to prayer reaches them from the location where Friday prayer is held, then they are obligated to attend Friday prayer. However, if the call to prayer does not reach them, then Friday prayer is not obligatory for them. This is the opinion of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. The condition is that the call of a muezzin with a loud voice reaches them, calling at a time when the sounds are quiet and the wind is still. The people of any village that is this close to the location where Friday prayer is held must attend Friday prayer. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It is obligatory for everyone who shelters him to spend the night. Al-Zuhri said: It is obligatory for those who are six miles away. Rabi'ah said: It is four miles away. Malik and al-Layth said: It is three miles away. Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him said: There is no Friday prayer for the people of Sawad, whether the village is close or far away. Anyone who is obligated to pray Friday prayer is not permitted to travel on Friday after noon before praying Friday prayer. The proponents of the opinion permit traveling after noon if he leaves the city before the time for the prayer expires. If he travels before noon after sunrise, then it is permissible. However, it is disliked unless his travel is a journey of obedience, such as Hajj or military campaign. Some of them said that if he becomes a resident on Friday, then he should not travel until he prays Friday prayer. The evidence for its permissibility is as follows: Abu Uthman al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa told us, Ahmad ibn Mani’ told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-Hajjaj, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abdullah ibn Rawahah on a military expedition, and it happened to be a Friday. He went with his companions in the morning and said: ‘Shall I stay behind and pray with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then catch up with them?’ When he had prayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he saw him and said: ‘What prevented you from going out with your companions?’ He said: ‘I wanted to pray with you and then catch up with them.’ He said: ‘Even if you spent all that is on the earth, you would not attain the reward of their going out.’” It was narrated that Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, heard a man who looked like a traveler saying: If today were not Friday, I would have left. Omar said: Go out, for Friday does not prevent one from traveling. There are reports on the Sunnahs of Friday and its virtues, including: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarkhasi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi informed us, Abu Mus`ab informed us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Haad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that he said: I went out to al-Tur and met Ka`b al-Ahbar, so I sat with him and he told me about the Torah, and I told him about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Among what I told him was that I said to him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best day the sun has risen upon is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was sent down, on it he was forgiven, on it he died and on it the Hour will come. There is no creature but it is attentive on Friday from the time it rises until the sun rises, fearing the Hour, except for the jinn and mankind. On it there is an hour when no Muslim servant encounters it while he is praying and asking God for something but that He will give it to him.” Ka`b said: That is every year on a day. I said: Rather, on every Friday. He said: So Ka`b recited the Torah and said: The Messenger of God spoke the truth. May God's prayers and peace be upon him. Abu Hurairah said: Then I met Abdullah ibn Salam and told him about my meeting with Ka'b al-Ahbar and what I told him about Friday. Abdullah ibn Salam said: I know which hour it is; it is the last hour of Friday. Abu Hurairah said: How can it be the last hour of Friday! The Messenger of God, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, said: No Muslim slave encounters it while he is praying. And that is an hour in which no prayer is performed? Abdullah ibn Salam said: Didn't the Messenger of God, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, say: Whoever sits in a gathering waiting for the prayer is in prayer until he prays it? Abu Hurairah said: Yes. He said: That is it. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you comes to the Friday prayer, let him take a bath. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam told us, Ibn Abi Dhi’b told us, on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, my father told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Wadi’ah, on the authority of Salman Al-Farsi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If a man bathes on Friday and purifies himself as much as he can, and anoints himself with his oil, or uses any perfume from his house, then goes out and does not separate two people, and then prays as much as has been written for him, and then listens when the imam speaks, then his sins between that Friday and the next will be forgiven.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ahmad bin Khalid told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman, and on the authority of Abu Umamah, meaning Sahl bin Hanif, they told him on the authority of Abu Sa’id and on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever performs ghusl on Friday, uses the miswak a turban and applies some perfume if he has any, and puts on his best clothes, then goes out until he comes to the mosque, not stepping over people’s necks, then bows as much as God wills him to bow, and listens silently when the imam comes out, it will be an expiation for what came between it and the previous Friday.” Abu Hurairah said: And an extra three days, because God, the Most High, says: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof (al-An’am 6:160). Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani told us, Abu al-Qasim ibn Ja`far al-Hashemi told us, Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lu`lu`i told us, Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash`ath al-Sijistani told us, Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Jarjara`i told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us on the authority of al-Awza`i, Hassan ibn `Atiyyah told me, Abu al-Ash`ath al-San`ani told me, Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi told me: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever performs ghusl on Friday and takes a bath, then sets out early and walks and does not ride, draws close to the imam and listens, and does not engage in idle talk, will have for every step the reward of a year’s fasting and standing in prayer.’” Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al Khallal told us, Abu Al Abbas Al Asam told us, Al Rabi’ told us, Al Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When it is Friday, there are angels at each door of the mosque, writing down the people according to their ranks, first and foremost. Then when the imam comes out, the scrolls are folded and they listen to the sermon. The one who goes to the prayer is like a Mahdi, a camel. Then the one who comes after him is like a Mahdi, a cow. Then the one who comes after him is like a Mahdi, a sheep. Then the one who comes after him is like a Mahdi, a ram.” Until he mentioned the chicken and the egg.
62:10: The Almighty said 10- So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land, meaning when the prayer is finished, disperse within the land for trade and to deal with your needs, and seek from the bounty of God, meaning provision. This is a matter of permission, like His saying: And when you have completed your ihram, hunt (al-Ma’idah 5:2). Ibn Abbas said: If you wish, then go out, and if you wish, then stay, and if you wish, then pray until the afternoon prayer. It was said: Disperse within the land, not to seek this world, but to visit a sick person, attend a funeral, and visit a brother in God. Al-Hasan, Saeed bin Jubair, and Makhul said: And seek from the bounty of God means seeking knowledge. Remember God often that you may succeed.
62:11: God Almighty said 11- And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing, the verse. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Hafs bin Omar told us, Khalid bin Abdullah told us, Hisin told us on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad and on the authority of Abu Sufyan on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: A caravan approached on Friday while we were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people rose up except for twelve men, so God revealed: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it. This hadith is used as evidence by those who believe that the Friday prayer should be performed with twelve men. However, it does not state that he performed the Friday prayer with them in order for it to be considered evidence, as this number is required. Ibn Abbas said, according to al-Kalbi's narration: Only eight men remained in the mosque. Al-Hasan and Abu Malik said: The people of Medina were afflicted with hunger and high prices. Dihya bin Khalifah Al-Kalbi came to trade oil from Ash-Sham while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the Friday sermon. When they saw him, they stood up to him in Al-Baqi’, fearing that they would be beaten to it. No one remained with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except a group of them, including Abu Bakr and Umar. Then this verse was revealed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you were to follow one another until not one of you remained, the valley would flow with you in fire. Muqatil said: While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was delivering the Friday sermon, Dihya ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi came from Ash-Sham for trade. Whenever he arrived, every person in Madinah would come to him. Whenever he arrived, he would bring with him everything he needed of flour, wool, and other things. He would stop at Ahjar al-Zayt, which was a place in the market place of Madinah, and beat the drum to announce his arrival to the people, so they would go out to him to buy from him. He arrived one Friday, and that was before he converted to Islam, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was standing on the pulpit delivering the sermon. The people came out to him, and there were only twelve men and women left in the mosque. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: How many are left in the mosque? They said: Twelve men and women. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Were it not for these people, stones would have been thrown down from the sky for them. Then God revealed this verse. By amusement, he meant the drum. It was said: When the caravan came to the city, they would welcome it with drums and clapping. His statement, They dispersed to it, refers to trade as a metaphor because it is more important. Alqamah said: Abdullah ibn Umar was asked: Did the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, deliver his sermon standing or sitting? He said: Do you not read, and they left you standing? Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al Khallal told us, Abu Al Abbas Al Asam told us, Al Rabi’ told us, Al Shafi’i told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would deliver two sermons on Friday while standing, separating them by sitting. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Jabir bin Samurah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would give two sermons, between which he would sit and recite the Qur’an and remind the people.” With this chain of transmission on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah, he said: “I used to pray with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prayer and sermon were moderate.” The sermon is obligatory in the Friday prayer.
