One must deliver two sermons while standing. The minimum that can be called a sermon is to praise God, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and advise people to fear God. These three are obligatory in both sermons. In the first sermon, one must recite a verse from the Qur’an and in the second, supplicate for the believers. If one omits one of these five, his Friday prayer is invalid according to Al-Shafi’i. Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him said that if he recites a tasbih, a tahmid, or a takbir, it is sufficient. This amount is not called a sermon, and he is commanded to give a sermon. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abdullah ibn Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Mamuyah told us, Abu Saeed Ahmad told us from Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Basri in Mecca, al-Hasan ibn al-Sabah al-Za’farani told us, Abdul-Wahhab ibn Abdul-Majid al-Thaqafi told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abi Rafi’ that Marwan appointed Abu Hurayrah as his deputy in Medina, so Abu Hurayrah led them in the Friday prayer and recited Surah al-Jumu’ah in the first rak’ah and in the second: When the hypocrites come to you (al-Munafiqun 63:1). Ubaydullah said: When we finished, I walked beside him and said to him: Did you recite two surahs that you heard Ali ibn Abi Talib recite in prayer? He said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recite them. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Damrah ibn Sa`id al-Mazini, on the authority of `Ubayd God ibn `Abdullah ibn `Utbah, that al-Dahhak ibn Qays asked al-Nu`man ibn Bashir: “What did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recite on Friday after Surat al-Jumu`ah?” He said: He used to recite ‘Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming’? Abu Uthman Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa told us, Qutaybah told us, Abu Awanah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Al-Muntashir, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Habib bin Salim, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recite on the two Eids and on Friday ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ and ‘Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming?’ Sometimes they would come together on one day and he would recite them both.” There are five conditions for the permissibility of Friday prayer: the time, which is the time of noon, between the sun’s zenith and the beginning of the time of afternoon prayer, the number of people, the imam, the sermon, and the place of residence. If one of these five conditions is missing, it must be performed as noon prayer. It is not permissible for the imam to begin the sermon before the number of people has gathered, which according to al-Shafi'i is forty. If they have gathered and he delivers the sermon, then they disperse before the start of the prayer, or one of the people is less than the number, it is not permissible for him to lead them in the Jumu'ah prayer; rather, he should pray the Dhuhr prayer. If he begins the prayer with them and they disperse, the most correct opinion of al-Shafi'i is that the continuation of the forty is a condition until the end of the prayer, just as the continuation of the time is a condition until the end of the prayer. If one of them is less than the number before the imam says the salutation, the rest must pray it as four rak'ahs. Another opinion is that if two people remain with him, he completes it as Jumu'ah. It was also said that if one person remains with him, he completes it as Jumu'ah. According to al-Muzani, if they are less than the number after the imam has prayed one rak'ah, he completes it as Jumu'ah. If he remains alone, and he is in the first rak'ah, he completes it as four, even if one person is less than the number. Abu Hanifah said the same regarding the number he stipulated, such as the one who joins the prayer late, if he catches up with the imam in one rak'ah of Jumu'ah, then when the imam says the salutation, he completes it as Jumu'ah. If he catches up with less than one rak'ah, he completes it as four. The Almighty says: Say, ‘What is with God is better than amusement and trade.’ That is, what is with God in terms of reward for prayer and steadfastness with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is better than amusement and trade. And God is the Best of providers, because He is the Provider of provisions, so ask Him and seek from Him.
63:1: 1- When the hypocrites come to you, meaning Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and his companions, they will say, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.’ And God knows that you are His Messenger, and God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars, because they concealed something other than what they revealed.
63:2: 2- They took their oaths as a shield, a veil, and they hindered people from the path of God, they prevented people from jihad and believing in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Evil is what they have done.
63:3: 3- That is because they believed, they acknowledged it with their tongues when they saw the believers, then they disbelieved, when they were alone with the polytheists, so their hearts were sealed, with disbelief, so they do not understand, / faith.
63:4: 4- And when you see them, their bodies impress you, meaning that they have bodies and appearances, and if they speak, you listen to their speech, so you think it is true. Abdullah ibn Abbas said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy was large, eloquent, and had a smooth tongue. When he spoke, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would listen to him. They are as if they were propped up pieces of wood, ghosts without souls and bodies without dreams. Abu Amr and Al-Kisa’i read: wood with a sukoon on the sheen, and the rest read it with a damma. Leaned, leaning against a wall, from their saying: I leaned something, if you leaned it, and the emphasis is for emphasis. He meant that they are not trees that bear fruit, but rather wood leaning against a wall. They think every shout is against them, meaning they do not hear a sound in the army, such as a crier calling out or an animal getting loose and announcing a lost item, except that they think - out of their cowardice and bad opinion - that they are meant for that, and they think that they have been attacked, because of the terror in their hearts. It was said: This is because they were afraid that God would send down something concerning them that would expose their secrets and permit the shedding of their blood. Then he said: They are the enemy. This is the beginning and its predicate, so beware of them, and do not trust them. May God fight them, may God curse them. How are they turned away from the truth?
63:5: 5- And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads away, meaning they turn away and turn their faces away, desiring to ask forgiveness. Nafi and Yaqub read lawwa with a light pronunciation, while the others read it with a heavy pronunciation, because they did it repeatedly. And you saw them turning away, turning away from what they were called to, while they were arrogant, arrogant about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking forgiveness for them.
63:6: 6- It is the same to them whether you ask forgiveness for them, O Muhammad, or do not ask forgiveness for them - God will not forgive them. Indeed, God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people." Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others reported on the authority of a group of biographers that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed that Banu al-Mustaliq were gathering to fight him, and their leader was al-Harith ibn Abi Dhirar Abu Juwayrah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about them, he went out to them until he met them at one of their watering places called al-Muraysiq, on the side of Qudayd towards the coast. The people clashed and fought, and God defeated Banu al-Mustaliq, and killed those of them who were killed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took their children, women, and wealth and gave them their spoils of war. While the people were at that watering place, a watering place arrived, and with Umar ibn al-Khattab was a servant of his from Banu Ghifar, called Jahjah ibn Sa`id al-Ghifari, leading his horse. Jahjah and Sinan ibn Wabra al-Juhani, an ally of Banu Auf ibn al-Khazraj, crowded together. That water and they fought, so Al-Juhani shouted: O group of Ansar! And Al-Ghifari shouted: O group of Muhajireen! And Juhajah Al-Ghifari was helped by a man from the Muhajireen called Ja'al, and he was poor. Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul became angry and with him were some of his people among whom was Zayd bin Arqam, a young boy. Ibn Ubayy said: Will they do it? They have outnumbered us and outnumbered us in our land. By God, our example and their example are as the saying goes: Fatten your dog and it will eat you. By God, if we return to Madinah, we will expel the more honorable from it the more lowly. By the more honorable, he meant himself and by the more lowly, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then he turned to those of his people who were present and said, "This is what you have done to yourselves. You have settled them in your land and shared your wealth with them. By God, if you had withheld the surplus food from Ja'al and his family, they would not have ridden on your necks and would have moved to a different country. Do not spend on them until they abandon Muhammad. Zayd ibn Arqam said, By God, you are the lowly, insignificant one who is hated by your people, while Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is honored by the Most Gracious and loved by the Muslims. Abdullah ibn Ubayy said, Be quiet. I was only joking." Zayd ibn Arqam went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after he had finished with the enemy and told him the report. Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him. Abdullah said, "Let me strike off his head, O Messenger of God. He said, How will it be, O Umar, when people say that Muhammad kills his companions?" But he gave permission to depart at a time when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was not in a position to depart, so the people departed." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent for Abdullah ibn Ubayy. He came to him and said, Are you the one who said these words that I heard? Abdullah said, “By Him who sent down the Book to you, I did not say anything of that. Zayd is a liar.” Abdullah was a noble and great man among his people. Those of his Ansar companions who were present said, O Messenger of God, perhaps the boy was mistaken in his speech and did not remember what he said. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) excused him, and the blame of Zayd spread among the Ansar, who accused him of lying. His uncle, who was with Zayd, said to him, “You only wanted the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to accuse you of lying while the people hated you.” Zayd used to go along with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), but after that he felt too shy to come near the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out and set out, Asid bin Hudhair met him and greeted him with the greeting of the Prophet and sent him peace. Then he said: O Messenger of God, you have set out at an unusual time when you do not usually set out. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: Have you not heard what your companion Abdullah ibn Ubayy said? He said: What did he say? He said: He claimed that if he returned to Medina, the more honorable would expel the more humiliated from it. Usaid said: By God, O Messenger of God, you can expel him if you wish. By God, he is the humiliated one and you are the honorable one. Then he said: O Messenger of God, be gentle with him, for by God, God has brought you while his people were stringing beads for him to crown him, and he thinks that you have usurped his kingdom. Abdullah ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayy heard about his father’s affair, so he went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: “O Messenger of God, I have heard that you intend to kill Abdullah ibn Ubayy because of what you have heard about him. If you are going to do it, then order me to do it, and I will bring you his head. By God, I know that there was no man among the Khazraj who was more dutiful to his parents than me, and I fear that you will order someone else to kill him. I will not let myself see the killer of Abdullah ibn Ubayy walking among the people and I kill him, thus killing a believer for an unbeliever and entering Hell.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, we will be gentle with him and treat him well as long as he remains with us. They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, traveled that day until evening, and the night until morning, and the beginning of their day until the sun hurt them. Then he descended with the people, and no sooner had they felt the touch of the ground than they fell asleep. He only did that to distract the people from the conversation he had had the day before, from the conversation of Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Then he went with the people until he stopped at a body of water in Hijaz above An-Naqi', which is called Naq'an. A violent wind blew, which harmed them and they were frightened by it, and the Prophet's (peace and blessings of God be upon him) camel went astray. That was at night, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Do not be afraid, for it only blew because of the death of a great disbeliever who died in Madinah. It was said, Who is that? He said, Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn At-Tabut. A hypocrite said, How can he claim to know the unseen but not the location of his camel? Will the One who brings him revelation not tell him? So Gabriel came to him and informed him of what the hypocrite had said and the location of the camel. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informed his companions of that and said, "I do not claim to know the unseen, nor do I know it. Rather, God has informed me of what the hypocrite has said and of the location of my camel. She is in a gorge, and her reins are caught in a tree." So they went out running towards the gorge and found that she was as he had said. They brought her and that hypocrite believed. When they arrived in Madinah, they found that Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut had died that day. He was one of the leading figures in the Jews and a refuge for the hypocrites. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) reached Madinah, Zayd ibn Arqam said: I sat at home because of my worry and shyness. Then God revealed Surah al-Munafiqun confirming Zayd's truthfulness and refuting Abdullah. When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took Zayd by the ear and said: O Zayd, God has spoken the truth in you and fulfilled your promise. Abdullah ibn Ubayy was near Madinah, and when he wanted to enter it, his son Abdullah ibn Abdullah came to him and stopped at the intersection of the roads of Madinah. When Abdullah ibn Ubayy came, he said: Behind you. He said: What is wrong with you, woe to you? He said: “No, by God, you will never enter it except with the permission of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Today you will know who is more honorable than who is more humiliated.” Abdullah complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about what his son had done, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent word to him that he should leave him alone until he entered. Abdullah said: “If the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, comes, then all is well.” So he entered and did not stay there except for a few days until he became ill and died. They said: When the verse was revealed and the lie of Abdullah bin Ubayy was exposed, it was said to him: O Abu Hubab, severe verses have been revealed about you, so go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that he may ask forgiveness for you. So he turned his head and said: You ordered me to believe, and I believed. You ordered me to give the zakat of my wealth, and I have given it. All that remains is for me to prostrate to Muhammad. Then God Almighty revealed: And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads Al-An’am 2:17.
63:7: And he came down: 7- “They are the ones who say, ‘Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse. ’ To God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth.” No one gives anyone anything except with His permission, nor does He prevent anyone except by His will. But the hypocrites do not understand. That when He wants something, He says to it, Be, and it is.
63:8: 8- They say, ‘If we return to Medina,’ from the Battle of Banu Mustaliq, “the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. But honor belongs to God, to His Messenger, and to the believers.” So, the honor of God means His subjugation of those besides Him, the honor of His Messenger means His making His religion prevail over all other religions, and the honor of the believers means God’s victory for them over their enemies. But the hypocrites do not know, that is, if they knew, they would not have said this statement.
63:9: God Almighty says: 9- O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God, the commentators said that it means the five daily prayers. Similar to His saying: Neither trade nor sale diverts them from the remembrance of God (al-Nur 24:37). And whoever does that, meaning whoever is distracted by his wealth and children from the remembrance of God, then it is those who are the losers.
63:10: 10- And spend from what We have provided for you, Ibn Abbas said: He means the zakat on wealth, before death comes to one of you, and he asks to be returned, and he says, ‘My Lord, if only You would delay me,’ Why did You delay me and give me respite? It was also said: There is no connection, so the statement would mean a wish, i.e., if You would delay me, for a near term so I could give charity, so I could give charity and purify my wealth, and be among the righteous, i.e., among the believers. Similar to the Almighty’s statement: And those among their fathers who were righteous (al-Ra’d 13:23) (Ghafir 40:8). This is the statement of Muqatil and a group. They said: The verse was revealed about the hypocrites. It was said: The verse was revealed about the believers. What is meant by righteousness here is Hajj. Ad-Dahhak and Atiyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: There is no one who dies and has wealth on which he did not pay zakat, and he was able to perform Hajj but did not perform it, except that he will ask to be returned to it at death. And he recited this verse. He said: And I will be among the righteous. Abu Amr read and I will be with the waw and the nun in the accusative case as an answer to the wish and in the wording so I will believe. He said: The waw was deleted from the Qur’an for brevity. Others read: "And I will be in the jussive mood, in apposition to his statement and I will believe if it did not contain the letter fa, because if it did not contain the letter fa" it would be in the jussive mood. Meaning: If you delay me, I will believe and I will be, and because it is written in the Qur’an without the letter "waw.
63:11: 11- “And God will not delay a soul when its term has come. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” Abu Bakr read: they do with a ya and the others read it with a ta.
64:1: Ata’ said: It is Meccan except for three verses from His saying: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children to the end of them. 1- “Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God. His is the kingdom and His is the praise. And He is over all things competent.”
64:2: 2- “It is He who created you, and among you are disbelievers and among you are believers. And God is Seeing of what you do.” Ibn Abbas said: God created the children of Adam as believers and disbelievers, then He will return them on the Day of Resurrection as He created them, believers and disbelievers. We narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The boy who was killed by Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, was born an unbeliever.” God Almighty said, And they give birth only to wicked, disbelieving children. (Nuh 71:27) Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abi Bakr bin Anas, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God has appointed an angel to be in charge of the womb, and he says: ‘O Lord, a sperm-drop, O Lord, a clot, O Lord, a lump of flesh.’ Then when God wants to complete its creation, he says: ‘O Lord, is it male or female, miserable or happy? What is the provision, what is the life span?’ And thus it is written in the womb of its mother.” A group said: The meaning of the verse is that God created the creation, then they disbelieved and then believed, because God the Most High mentioned the creation and then described them through their actions, saying: And among you are disbelievers and among you are believers, just as God the Most High said: And God created every living creature from water, and among them are those that walk (al-Nur 24:45), and God created them and walking is their action. Then they differed in its interpretation: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that he said: Among you is a disbeliever during his life but a believer in the afterlife, and among you is a believer during his life but a disbeliever in the afterlife. Ata bin Abi Rabah said: Some of you are disbelievers in God but believe in the stars, and some of you are believers in God but disbelievers in the stars. It was said: Some of you are disbelievers that God Almighty created him, which is the doctrine of the materialists, and some of you are believers that God created him. In short: God created the disbeliever, and his disbelief was an action and an earning for him. He created the believer, and his faith was an action and an earning for him. So each of the two groups has an earning and a choice, and his earning and choice are by God’s decree and will. So the believer, after God created him, chooses faith, because God wanted that from him, decreed it for him, and knew it from him. And the disbeliever, after God created him, chooses disbelief, because God wanted that from him, decreed it for him, and knew it from him. This is the path of Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah; whoever follows it will attain the truth and be safe from compulsion and predestination.
64:3: 3- He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and He formed you and perfected your forms, and to Him is the final destination.
64:4: 4- “He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you declare. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts.”
64:5: 5- Did there not come to you, addressing the infidels of Mecca, the report of those who disbelieved before, meaning: the nations of old, so they tasted the evil consequences of their deed, meaning the punishment that befell them in this world, and for them is a painful punishment, in the Hereafter.
64:6: 6- That, the punishment, is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they said, ‘Are human beings guiding us?’ He did not say, Guides us, because although the word humans is a singular noun, it is in the plural sense, and it is a generic noun that has no singular form, and its singular is human, and its meaning is: they deny and say, A human being like us guides us! “So they disbelieved and turned away, and God was free of need of their faith, and God is free of need of His creation, Praiseworthy in His actions.
64:7: Then He informed us about their denial of the resurrection, and He, the Most High, said: 7- “Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, O Muhammad, ‘Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did, and that, for God, is easy.’”
64:8: 8- So believe in God and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down, which is the Qur’an, and God is Acquainted with what you do.
64:9: 9- The Day He will gather you for the Day of Assembly, meaning the Day of Resurrection, on which He will gather the people of the heavens and the earth. That is the Day of Loss, which is a verb from ghban, meaning missing out on a share. The one who is lost is the one who is lost in his family and his homes in Paradise. On that day, the loss of every disbeliever will be made clear through his dislike of faith, and the loss of every believer through his shortcomings in doing good. And whoever believes in God and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read: "We... and admit him." In Surat At-Talaq, We will enter him, with a nun in them. The others read it with a ya, "abiding therein forever. That is the great attainment.
64:10: 10- And those who disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of the Fire, abiding eternally therein, and wretched is the destination.
64:11: 11- No disaster strikes except by permission of God, by His will and decree. And whoever believes in God, believing that no disaster strikes him except by permission of God, He guides his heart, grants him certainty so that he knows that what befell him could not have missed him, and what missed him could not have befallen him, so he submits to His decree. And God is Knowing of all things.
64:12: 12- “And obey God and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away - then upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification.”
64:13: 13- God, there is no god but He, and in God let the believers put their trust.
64:15: 15- Your wealth and your children are only a trial, a trial, a test, and a distraction from the Hereafter, because of which a person falls into great sins, prevents the truth, and consumes what is forbidden, but God has with Him a great reward. Some of them said: When God mentioned enmity, He included from for the sake of partiality, so He said: Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, because not all of them are enemies. He did not mention from in His statement: Your wealth and your children are only a trial, because it is not free of trial and distraction of the heart. Abdullah ibn Masoud used to say: “Let none of you say: ‘O God, I seek refuge in You from temptation,’ for none of you will return to his wealth, family, or children without being subjected to temptation. Rather, let him say: ‘O God, I seek refuge in You from the misleading temptations.’” Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Muzaffari told us, Abu Saeed Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Faqih told us, Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Faqih told us, Ahmad ibn Bakr ibn Yusuf told us, Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Buraydah, who said: I heard Abu Buraydah say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering a sermon to us, when al-Hasan and al-Husayn came, wearing two red shirts, walking and stumbling. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came down from the pulpit, carried them, and placed them in front of him. Then he said: God has spoken the truth: Your wealth and your children are but a trial. I looked at these two boys walking and stumbling, and I could not be patient until I stopped my speech and picked them up.”
64:16: 16- So fear God as much as you are able, if you are able, this verse abrogates the Almighty’s saying: Fear God as He should be feared (Al Imran 3:102) And listen and obey, God and His Messenger, and spend [in charity] that is better for yourselves, spend from your wealth that is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, so that he gives God’s right from his wealth, it is those who will be the successful.
64:17: 17- “If you lend God a good loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And God is Most Appreciative and Forbearing.”
64:18: 18- The Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
65:1: 1- O Prophet, when you divorce women, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out, then addressed his nation, because he is the foremost master, so everyone is addressed with him. It was said: Its meaning is: O Prophet, tell your nation, When you divorce women, if you want to divorce them, like the Almighty’s saying: So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge in God (al-Nahl 16:98), meaning: if you want to recite. Divorce them during their waiting period, meaning, to purify them with whatever they can count of their waiting period. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar used to recite: Divorce them during their waiting period. This verse was revealed about Abdullah ibn Umar, who had divorced his wife during her menstrual period. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Nafi`, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, “that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and he said: Order him to take her back, then to keep her until she is pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure, then if he wishes he may keep her after that, and if he wishes he may divorce her before he has touched her. That is the waiting period for which God has commanded women to be divorced.” Narrated by Salim on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: Tell him to take her back and then divorce her when she is pure or pregnant. It was narrated by Yunus bin Jubair and Anas bin Sirin on the authority of Ibn Umar, and they did not say: Then she menstruates and then becomes pure. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad al-Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad al-Khalal told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, al-Rabi’ told us, al-Shafi’i told us, Muslim and Sa’id bin Salim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Abdul Rahman bin Ayman, the freed slave of ‘Uzza, asking Abdullah bin ‘Umar - and Abu al-Zubayr was listening - saying: What do you think of a man who divorced his wife while she was menstruating? Ibn ‘Umar said: Abdullah bin ‘Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Order him to take her back, and when she is pure, let him divorce her or keep her. Ibn ‘Umar said: And God Almighty said: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them during their waiting period. Al-Shafi’i is uncertain. It was narrated by Hajjaj bin Muhammad on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Umar said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them during their waiting period. Know that divorce during menstruation or postpartum bleeding is an innovation, as is the case during the period of purity in which he had intercourse with her, based on the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If he wishes, he may divorce her before he touches her. Sunnah al-Talaq 65:Divorce a woman during a period of purity in which she has not had intercourse. This applies to a woman whose waiting period is based on menstrual periods. If he divorces a woman who has not been consummated with during her menstruation, or divorces a young girl who has never menstruated, or a woman who has reached menopause after having intercourse with her, or divorces a pregnant woman after having intercourse with her, or when he sees blood, then this is not an innovation. There is no Sunnah or innovation in divorcing these people, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Then let him divorce her when she is pure or pregnant. Divorce during menstruation or during a period of purity in which he had intercourse with her is not an innovation, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave Thabit ibn Qays permission to divorce his wife without knowing her condition. If it were not permissible in all circumstances, it would be more likely that he would know the condition. If he divorces his wife during her menstruation or during a period of purity in which he intentionally had intercourse with her, he is disobeying God Almighty. However, the divorce takes place because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Ibn Umar to take her back. Had the divorce not taken place, he would not have ordered her to take him back. If he takes her back during her menstruation, it is permissible for him to divorce her during the period of purity that follows that menstruation before intercourse, as narrated by Yunus ibn Jubayr and Anas on the authority of Sirin on the authority of Ibn Umar. What Nafi’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: Then he should keep her until she is pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure. So it is recommended. It is recommended to delay the divorce until the second period of purity so that his return to her is not for the sake of divorce, just as marriage for the sake of divorce is disliked. There is nothing heretical about combining the three divorces, according to some scholars. Even if a man divorces his wife three times during a period of purity, it is not considered heretical. This is the opinion of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Some scholars are of the view that it is a heretical opinion, which is the opinion of Malik and the scholars of opinion. God the Almighty says: And count the waiting period, meaning the number of her menstrual cycles. Memorize it. It was said that He ordered counting the waiting period to distribute the divorce among the menstrual cycles if he wanted to pronounce a third divorce. It was also said that it was to ensure that the period of time remaining for taking her back remains and to take into consideration the issue of maintenance and housing. “And fear God, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their houses.” He meant that if the residence in which he divorced her belongs to the husband, he is not permitted to turn her out of it. And they should not go out. It is not permissible for her to go out until her waiting period has ended. If she goes out without necessity or need, she has sinned. If necessity arises - even if she fears destruction or drowning - she is permitted to go out to another house. Likewise, if she has a need to sell yarn or buy cotton, it is permissible for her to go out during the day, but it is not permissible at night. Men were martyred at Uhud and their women said: We feel lonely in our homes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them permission to talk to one of them. When it is time to sleep, each woman goes to her own house. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave permission to Jabir’s aunt, whom her husband had divorced, to go out to cut her palm trees. If she is required to observe the waiting period while traveling, she must observe the waiting period going and coming, and the Bedouin woman must reside where her family resides during the waiting period, because moving for them is like residing for the resident. His saying: Unless they commit a clear indecency. Ibn Abbas said: A clear indecency is if she commits a sin against her husband’s family, in which case it is permissible to expel her. A group said: What he meant by immorality is that she commits adultery, is taken out to have the punishment carried out on her, then returns to her home. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud. Qatada said: Its meaning is unless he divorces her due to her disobedience, then she has the right to move from her husband’s house, and the immoral act is disobedience. Ibn Omar and Al-Suddi said: Her going out before the end of the waiting period is an obscenity. And these are the limits set by God, meaning: what was mentioned about the Sunnah of divorce and what follows it, “And whoever transgresses the limits of God has wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps God will bring about after that something new,” which makes the husband want to take her back after one or two divorces. This indicates that it is preferable to separate the divorces and not pronounce them three at once, so that if he regrets it, he can take her back.
65:2: 2- So when they have reached their term, that is, their waiting period is about to end, take them back, that is, take them back, on acceptable terms or part with them on acceptable terms, that is, leave them until their waiting period is over and then she is separated from you, and bring to witness two just men from among you, concerning the taking back and the separation. He ordered that witnesses be brought to the taking back and the divorce. And establish the testimony, you witnesses, for God. “This is an admonition to whoever believes in God and the Last Day. And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out.” Ikrimah, Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Dahhak said: And whoever fears God and follows the Sunnah - He will make for him a way out until the return. Most of the commentators said: It was revealed about Awf bin Malik Al-Ashja’i. The polytheists captured his son, Malik, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, the enemy has captured my son. He also complained to him about his poverty, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Fear God and be patient and say often: There is no power or strength except with God. So the man did that, and while he was in his house, his son came to him while the enemy had forgotten him. He captured some camels and brought them to his father. Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The enemy took him for granted, so he drove off their sheep and brought them to his father, which were four thousand sheep. Then the verse, And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out was revealed about his son.
65:3: 3- And He provides for him from where he does not expect, what he drove of sheep. Muqatil said: He acquired sheep and goods and then returned to his father. His father went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what had happened. He asked him: Is it permissible for him to eat what his son had brought him? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes. And God revealed this verse. Ibn Masoud said: And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out. This means that he should know that it is from God and that God is his provider. Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim said: He will make a way out for him from everything that is difficult for people. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: A way out from every hardship. Al-Hasan said: A way out from what he was forbidden from. And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him, he fears God in what befalls him, and He will suffice him in what concerns him. We narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you were to trust in God as He should be trusted, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds that go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening full. “God will accomplish His purpose.” Talha ibn Musarraf and Hafs on the authority of Asim read: He will accomplish His purpose with the addition. The others read it with the tanween, He will execute His purpose in the accusative case, meaning He will carry out His purpose and carry out His decree for His creation. God has already set a [decreed] extent for everything, meaning He has set an end to everything, whether hardship or ease. Masruq said: In this verse, Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose, whether one relies on Him or not, except that the one who relies on Him will have his sins forgiven and will receive a great reward.
65:4: God Almighty says: 4- And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are not expecting to menstruate, if you are in doubt, meaning if you are in doubt and do not know what their waiting period is, their waiting period is three months. Muqatil said: When the verse: Divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods Al-Baqarah 2:228 was revealed, Khallad ibn An-Nu’man ibn Qays Al-Ansari said: O Messenger of God, what is the waiting period of one who does not menstruate, one who has not yet menstruated, and one who is pregnant? So God revealed: And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation meaning those who have stopped menstruating if you are in doubt are unsure about the ruling on her, their waiting period is three months. “And those who have not menstruated,” meaning young girls who have not menstruated, their waiting period is also three months. As for the young woman who used to menstruate and her period stopped before she reached the age of menopause, most scholars are of the view that her waiting period does not end until her bleeding resumes, in which case she observes a waiting period of three menstrual periods, or until she reaches the age of menopause, in which case she observes a waiting period of three months. This is the view of Uthman, Ali, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Abdullah ibn Mas`ud. It was also the view of Ata`, and it was the view of al-Shafi`i and the scholars of opinion. It was narrated on the authority of Omar: She waits for nine months, and if she does not menstruate, she observes a waiting period of three months. This is the opinion of Malik. Al-Hasan said: She waits for one year, and if she does not menstruate, she waits for three months. All of this is in the waiting period for divorce. As for a woman whose husband has died, her waiting period is four months and ten days, whether she menstruates or not. As for the pregnant woman, her waiting period is until she gives birth, whether her husband divorces her or dies, based on the Almighty’s saying: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. Abdul Wahhab bin Muhammad Al Khatib told us, Abdul Aziz bin Ahmad Al Khallal told us, Abu Al Abbas Al Asam told us, Al Rabi told us, Al Shafi’i told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al Zuhri, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father: “Subai’ah bint Al Harith gave birth a few nights after the death of her husband. Abu Al Sanabil bin Ba’kak passed by her and said: ‘You have made yourself attractive to husbands. It is only four months and ten days.’ So Subai’ah mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘Abu Al Sanabil lied - or: It is not as Abu Al Sanabil said - you are now permissible, so marry.’” And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. He will make the matters of this world and the hereafter easy for him.
65:5: 5- That, meaning the rulings mentioned, “is the command of God which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears God - He will remove from him his misdeeds and make great for him his reward.”
65:6: Lodge them, meaning your divorced women, wherever you live. “From” is a relative clause, meaning: Lodge them where you live. From your means, meaning: your means and ability, meaning: if he is well-off, he should provide her with housing and support, and if he is poor, then according to his means. And do not harm them, do not hurt them, in order to constrict them, their homes so that they leave. And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth, so that they leave their waiting period. Know that a woman in her waiting period iddah is entitled to maintenance and housing from her husband as long as she is in her waiting period. By housing, we mean the expenses of living. If the house in which he divorced her was owned by the husband, the husband must vacate and leave the house to her for the duration of her waiting period. If it was rented, the husband is responsible for paying the rent. If it was a loan and the lender returns, he is responsible for renting a house for her to live in. As for the woman who has been divorced irrevocably by khul’, three divorces, or li’an, she is entitled to housing, whether she is pregnant or not, according to most scholars. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: She has no residence unless she is pregnant. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Ata’ and Al-Sha’bi. They differed regarding her maintenance. Some held that she is not entitled to maintenance unless she is pregnant. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Ata', and Al-Sha'bi. It was also the opinion of Al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Some of them made it obligatory in all cases. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and it is the opinion of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, and it was also said by al-Thawri and the people of opinion. The apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates that she is not entitled to anything unless she is pregnant, because God Almighty said: And if they are pregnant, then spend on them. The evidence for this from the Sunnah is: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Yazid, the client of al-Aswad ibn Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Fatimah bint Qays, that Abu `Amr ibn Hafs divorced her irrevocably while he was away in Syria. He sent his agent some barley to her, but she was displeased with it, so he said: By God, you have nothing against us. So she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him. He said to her: You are not entitled to maintenance from him, and he ordered her to observe her waiting period in the house of Umm Sharik. Then he said: That is a woman whom my companions visit, so observe your waiting period in the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is a blind man. Take off your clothes, and when you are released, inform me. She said: When I was released, I mentioned to him that Mu`awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan and Abu Jahm had proposed to me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for Abu Jahm, he does not remove his stick from his shoulder, and as for Mu`awiyah, he is a vagabond with no money. Marry Usamah ibn Zayd said: I hated him, then he said: Marry Usama, so I married him, and he made me feel good about him and I was happy with him. Those who did not grant her residence cited the hadith of Fatima bint Qais: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered her to observe her waiting period in the house of Amr ibn Umm Maktum.” There is no proof in this, as it was narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: Fatima was in a strange place, and she was afraid for her companion. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Fatima was transferred because of her long tongue, which was difficult for her in-laws, and she had a sharp tongue. As for the woman observing the waiting period after suspicious intercourse, or whose marriage was annulled due to a defect or the option of emancipation, she is not entitled to housing or maintenance, even if she is pregnant. A woman observing the waiting period following the death of her husband is not entitled to maintenance, whether she is pregnant or not, according to most scholars. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that she is entitled to maintenance, if she is pregnant, from the estate until she gives birth. This is the opinion of Shuraih, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i, and Al-Thawri. They differed regarding her residence. Al-Shafi'i may God be pleased with him had two opinions: One of them was that she should not reside in it, but rather she should observe her waiting period wherever she wishes. This was the opinion of Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Aisha. This was also the opinion of Ata' and Al-Hasan, and it was the opinion of Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him. The second: She has the right to reside in it, and this is the opinion of Omar, Othman, Abdullah bin Masoud, and Abdullah bin Omar, and it was also said by Malik, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ahmad, and Ishaq. Those who required her to reside in it argued that: Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Ishaq ibn Ka`b ibn `Ujrah, on the authority of his aunt Zaynab bint Ka`b: Al-Fari`ah bint Malik ibn Sinan, who was the sister of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, told her: “She came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him to let her return to her family in Banu Khudra, for her husband had gone out in search of his slaves whom they had left behind. When they were at the edge of al-Qudum, he caught up with them, and they killed him. So I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘May I return to my family, for my husband has not left me in a house that he owns or provided for me?’ She said, ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Yes.’ So I went back, and when she was in the room or in the mosque, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me or commanded me to be called to him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘What did you say?’ She said, ‘So I repeated to him the story that I had mentioned about my husband, and he said, ‘Stay in your house until the appointed time has come.’ She said, ‘So I observed my waiting period there for four months and ten days.’ She said: When Uthman came, he sent to me and asked me about that, so I told him, and he followed it and ruled accordingly. Whoever says this statement says: His permission for Faree’a to return to her family at first was abrogated by his statement at the end: “Stay in your house until the term of the contract is fulfilled.” And whoever does not require residence, he said: He ordered her to stay in her house last, as a recommendation, not an obligation. God the Almighty says: If they breastfeed for you, meaning breastfeed your children, then give them their payment, for breastfeeding them, and consult together in what is acceptable, so that some of you may accept from others if they command you to do what is acceptable. Al-Kisa’i said: Consult. Muqatil said: By the agreement of the father and mother for a specified payment. The address is to both spouses, commanding them to do what is acceptable and best, and not to intend harm. But if you disagree, over breastfeeding and payment, and the husband refuses to give the woman her consent and the mother refuses to breastfeed him, then he does not have the right to force her to breastfeed him, but he may hire a wet nurse for the boy other than his mother. This is stated in His saying: then another woman will breastfeed him.
65:7: 7- Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance, according to his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what God has given him, of money. God does not charge a soul, in spending, except according to what He has given it, He gave it of money, God will grant, after hardship, ease, after distress and hardship, wealth and abundance.
65:8: God Almighty says: 8- And how many a city was insolent, disobeyed and transgressed, against the command of its Lord and His messengers, that is, the command of His messengers, So We brought it to a severe account, by discussion and investigation. Muqatil said: He brought it to account for its deeds in this world and punished it with a torment, which is His statement: And We punished it with a terrible torment, a terrible torment, which is the torment of the Fire. Both of them are past tense but their meanings are future tense. It was said: There is an inversion in the verse, and its meaning is: So We punished her in this world with hunger, famine, the sword, and all other calamities, and We held her to a severe account in the Hereafter.
65:9: 9- So she tasted the evil consequences of her deed, the punishment for her deed, and it was said: the severity of the consequences of her disbelief, and the outcome of her deed was loss, loss in this world and the hereafter.
65:10: 10- “God has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear God, you of understanding who have believed. God has sent down to you a reminder,” meaning the Qur’an.
65:11: 11- A Messenger, instead of the male. It was also said: He sent down to you a Qur’an and sent a Messenger. It was also said: With the Messenger. It was also said: The male is the Messenger. It was said: Remembrance meaning honor. Then he explained what it is and said: “A Messenger who recites to you the clear verses of God that He may bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from darkness into the light. And whoever believes in God and does righteousness - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. God has certainly been good to him in provision,” meaning the Paradise whose pleasures never cease.
65:12: 12- God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them, in the verse, the command descends between them, by revelation from the seventh heaven to the lowest earth. The scholars of meaning said: It is the wondrous planning that He manages in them, so He sends down rain and brings forth plants, brings about night and day, summer and winter, creates animals in their various forms, and transfers them from one state to another. Qatada said: In every land of His land and every sky of His sky there is a creation of His creation, a command of His command, and a decree of His decree. So that you may know that God has power over all things and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge, so nothing is hidden from Him.
66:1: 1- "O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful." The reason for its revelation is what Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ubaidullah bin Ismail told us, Abu Usamah told us on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved sweets and loved honey. When he prayed the afternoon prayer, he would pass by his wives and approach them. He entered upon Hafsa and stayed with her longer than he usually stayed. I asked about that, and it was said to me: A woman from her people gave her a gift of a bowl of honey, so she gave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a drink from it. I said: By God, we will find a plan for him. I mentioned that to Sawda, and I said: When he enters upon you, he will approach you, so say to him: O Messenger of God, have you eaten?" Maghafir? He will say: No. So say to him: What is this smell? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was very upset when he smelled the smell, so he would say: Hafsah gave me a drink of honey. So say to him: The bees of the `Arfait have bitten it. I will say that and you say it, O Safiyyah. So when he entered upon Sawdah, Sawdah said: By God, there is no god but Him, I almost told him what you said to me while he was at the door, out of fear of you. So when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came near, I said: O Messenger of God, have you eaten Maghafir? He said: No. I said: What is this smell? He said: Hafsah gave me a drink of honey. She said: The bees of the `Arfait have bitten it. So when he entered upon me, I said to him the same thing, and he entered upon Safiyyah and she said the same thing to him. So when he entered upon Hafsah, she said to him: O Messenger of God, shall I not give you some to drink? He said: I have no need of it. Sawdah said: Glory be to God, we have forbidden it. She said: I told her to be quiet. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ibn Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad Ibn Yusuf told us, Muhammad Ibn Ismail told us, Al-Hasan Ibn Muhammad Al-Sabah told us, Al-Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: Ata’ claimed that he heard Ubaid Ibn Umair say, “I heard Aisha, may God be pleased with her, say that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to stay with Zaynab Bint Jahsh and drink honey at her place. Hafsa and I advised each other that whichever of us the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, enters upon should say, ‘I smell the odor of maghāfir on you.’ I ate maghāfir. So he entered upon one of them and she told him that, so he said, ‘There is nothing wrong with that. I drank honey at Zaynab Bint Jahsh’s place and I will not do it again.’ Then this verse was revealed: ‘O Prophet! Why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? ’ until His saying: ‘If you both repent to God’ for Aisha and Hafsa, ‘And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives, ’ for His saying: ‘Rather, I drank honey. ’” And with this chain of transmission he said: Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ with his chain of transmission and he said: He said: No, but I used to drink honey at Zainab bint Jahsh’s house and I will not do it again, and I have sworn not to tell anyone about that, seeking thereby to please his wives. The commentators said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to divide his time among his wives. When Hafsa's day came, she asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for permission to visit her father, and he gave her permission. When she left, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent for his slave girl, Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah, and brought her into Hafsa's house. He had intercourse with her. When Hafsa returned, she found the door closed, so she sat by the door. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out with sweat dripping from his face, and Hafsa was crying. He said: What makes you cry? She said: This is why you gave me permission. You brought your slave girl into my house, and then I had intercourse with her on my day and in my bed. Don't you see that I have a right and a sanctity? You would not do this to any of their women. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Isn't she my slave girl, whom God has made lawful for me? Be quiet, for she is forbidden to me. I seek your pleasure by doing that, so do not tell this to any of their women. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left, Hafsa knocked on the wall between her and Aisha and said: Shall I not give you good report that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has forbidden his slave girl, Maria, to him, and God has relieved us of her? She told Aisha what she had seen, and they were at peace with each other and were supporting each other against the rest of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Aisha became angry and kept on attacking the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until he swore that he would not come near her. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? meaning honey and Maria, seek[ing] the approval of your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful.
66:2: And he ordered him to atone for his oath and return to his nation, so he said: 2- God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths, meaning He has made clear and made it obligatory that you expiate them if you break them, which is what is mentioned in Surat Al-Ma’idah. And God is your Protector, your Guardian and Supporter, and He is the Knowing, the Wise. Scholars differed regarding the wording of the oath. Some said: It is not an oath. If he says to his wife: You are forbidden to me or I have forbidden you, if he intended it as a divorce, then it is a divorce. If he intended it as a zihar pronouncement of divorce, then it is a zihar pronouncement of divorce. If he intended to forbid her or made general statements, then he must pay the expiation for an oath using the same wording. If he says that to his female slave, if he intended to free her, then she is freed. If he intended to forbid her or made general statements, then he must pay the expiation for an oath. If he says about food: I have forbidden it to myself, then he does not have to do anything. This is the opinion of Ibn Mas’ud, and Al-Shafi’i agreed with it. A group of scholars held that it is an oath. If he said that to his wife or his female slave, then he is not required to make expiation unless he approaches her, just as if he swore not to have intercourse with her. If he forbade a food, then it is as if he swore not to eat it, so he is not required to make expiation unless he eats it. This was narrated from Abu Bakr and Aisha, and Al-Awza’i and Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with them said the same. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muadh bin Fadala told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Ibn Hakim, who is Ya’la bin Hakim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said regarding the forbidden: He disbelieves. And Ibn Abbas said: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern (al-Ahzab 33:21).
66:3: 3- And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, which was that he forbade his girl to himself, and his saying to Hafsa: Do not tell anyone about that. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The matter of the caliphate after him was kept secret and Hafsa was told about it. Al-Kalbi said: He confided in her that your father and Aisha’s father would be the caliphs over my nation after me. Maymun bin Mihran said: He confided in her that Abu Bakr would be my caliph after me. When she informed him of it, Hafsah informed Aishah of it, and God revealed it to him, meaning God informed His Prophet that she had informed him of it, he knew some of it, Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Kisa’i read it as: he knew some of the action that she had done in revealing his secret, meaning he became angry with her for it and punished her for it, like the saying of someone who has wronged him: I will surely make known to you what you did, meaning I will punish you for it, and he punished her for it by divorcing her. When this reached ‘Umar, he said: If there had been any good in the family of al-Khattab, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would not have divorced you. Then Gabriel came and ordered him to take her back, so the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) kept away from his wives for a month and sat in the drinking place of Maria, the mother of Ibrahim, until the verse of choice was revealed. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not divorce Hafsa. Rather, he intended to divorce her, but Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said: Do not divorce her, for she fasts and prays, and she is one of your wives in Paradise. But he did not divorce her. Others read Araf with emphasis, meaning: He knew Hafsa after that conversation, meaning he told her some of what she had said. "And he ignored some of it," meaning he did not tell her about it, nor did he inform her of it. Al-Hasan said: No noble person ever fully understood it. God Almighty said: "He acknowledged some of it and ignored some of it," because when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw the hatred on Hafsah's face, he wanted to appease her, so he confided two things in her: He prohibited the Ummah for himself, and he gave her the good report that the caliphate after him would be in Abu Bakr and her father, Umar may God be pleased with them. Hafsah informed Aisha of it, and God Almighty informed His Prophet of it. He informed Hafsah of some of it and informed her of some of what Aisha had informed him of, which was the prohibition of the Ummah, and he ignored some of it, meaning the mention of the caliphate. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not want that to spread among the people. "So when he informed her of it, meaning he informed Hafsah of what God had revealed to him, she said, Hafsah, Who told you this," meaning: Who told you that I had divulged the secret? "He said, The All-Knowing, All-Aware informed me.
66:4: 4- "If you both repent to God," meaning from cooperating against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by harming him. He is addressing Aisha and Hafsa, "Your hearts have indeed deviated," meaning they have strayed and turned away from the truth, and you both deserve repentance. Ibn Zayd said: Their hearts have deviated because they were pleased with what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked regarding her avoiding his slave girl. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Abi Thawr told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, who said: I was always keen to ask Umar bin Al-Khattab about the two women from the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to whom God Almighty said: If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed become inclined, until he performed Hajj and I performed Hajj with him. He was just and I was just with him with a water skin. He relieved himself and then came back, and I poured some water over his hands, and he performed ablution. I said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two women from the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to whom God Almighty said: If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed become inclined? He said: How strange you are, Ibn Abbas! They are Aisha and Hafsa. Then Omar received the hadith and said: I and a neighbor of mine from the Ansar were in Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, which is one of the upper reaches of Medina, and we used to take turns going down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He would go down one day and I would go down the next. When I went down, I would bring him what had happened of the report of that day, whether it was revelation or something else. When he went down, he would do the same. We, the Quraysh, used to dominate women. But when we came to the Ansar, we found that they were a people who were dominated by their women. Our women began to learn from the manners of the Ansar women. I shouted at my wife, who talked back to me, but I did not like her to talk back to me. She said, “Why do you not like me talking back to you? By God, the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would talk back to him, and one of them would ignore him all day long until nightfall.” This startled me and I said, Whoever among them does that is doomed. Then I gathered my clothes, went down and entered upon Hafsa. I said to her, “O Hafsa, does any of you get angry with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) today until nightfall?” She said, Yes. I said, “You are disappointed and you have lost. Do you feel secure that God will not be angered by the anger of His Messenger and you will be destroyed? Do not think it too much for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), do not argue with him about anything, do not abandon him, and ask me whatever you want, and do not be deceived by the fact that your neighbor is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) - meaning Aisha. Omar said: We were talking about Ghassan shod the horses to attack us. My Ansari companion came down on the day of his turn, then he came back to us in the evening and knocked on my door violently and said: Is he guilty? I was startled and went out to him. He said: “A great event has happened today.” I said: What is it, Ghassan? He said: “No, something greater and more terrifying. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has divorced his wives.” I said: “Hafsa has been disappointed and has lost out. I thought that this was about to happen.” So I gathered my clothes and prayed the dawn prayer with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered a drinking place and secluded himself there. Then I entered upon Hafsa and found her crying. I said: What makes you cry? Did I not warn you? Did the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, release you? She said: I do not know. Here he is, secluded in the window. So I went to the pulpit and found around him a group of people, some of whom were weeping. I sat with them for a while, then I was overcome by what I felt, so I went to the window where the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was and said to a black slave of his: Ask permission for Umar. He entered and spoke to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), then he came back and said: I spoke to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned you to him, but he was silent. So I went away and sat with the group who were by the pulpit, then I was overcome by what I felt, so I went to the slave and said: Ask permission. So he asked permission, then he came back to me and said: I mentioned you to him, but I was silent. So I went back and sat with the group who were by the pulpit, then I was overcome by what I felt, so I went to the slave and said: Ask permission for Umar. So he asked permission, then he came back to me and said: I mentioned you to him, but I was silent. When I turned away, he said, "The boy is calling me and saying, 'The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has given you permission.' So I entered upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and found him lying on the sand of a mat with no mattress between him and it. The sand had left traces on his side, and he was leaning on a leather pillow stuffed with palm fibres. I greeted him and then said while I was standing, 'O Messenger of God, have you divorced your wives?' He raised his eyes to me and said, 'No.' I said, 'God is Great.'" Then I said while I was standing, seeking comfort: O Messenger of God, if you had seen me. We, the Quraysh, used to dominate the women, but when we came to Madinah, we were a people whose women used to dominate them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled. Then I said: O Messenger of God, if you had seen me. I entered upon Hafsa and said to her: Do not be deceived by the fact that your neighbor is more beautiful than you and more beloved to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - meaning Aisha - so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled again. I sat down when I saw him smiling, so I raised my gaze in his house, and by God I did not see anything in it that would distract the eye except three characteristics. I said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to make your nation generous, for the Persians and the Romans have been generous and given from the world, but they do not worship God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat up and said, "Is this what you are doing, O Ibn Al-Khattab? Those are people who hastened their good things in this worldly life." I said: O Messenger of God, ask forgiveness for me. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew from his wives because of that hadith when Hafsa revealed it to Aisha for twenty-nine nights. He had said: I will not enter upon them for a month - out of the intensity of his resentment towards them when God Almighty rebuked him. When twenty-nine nights had passed, he entered upon Aisha may God be pleased with her and began with her. Aisha said to him: O Messenger of God, you swore that you would not enter upon us for a month, but now you have woken up after twenty-nine nights, and I am counting them! He said: The month is twenty-nine, and that month had twenty-nine nights. Aisha said: Then God revealed the choice, so He began with me, the first of his wives, and I chose him. Then He gave a choice to all of his wives, and they said the same as Aisha said. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman told me that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, told him that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, came to her when God commanded him to give his wives a choice. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, started with me and said: I am going to mention to you something, so do not rush until you consult your parents. He knows that my parents would not command me to leave him. She said: Then he said: God said: O Prophet, tell your wives to the end of the two verses. I said: Is it in this that I consult my parents? For I want God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Zuhair bin Harb told us, Umar bin Yunus Al-Hanafi told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, from Samak bin Zamil, Abdullah bin Abbas told us, Umar bin Al-Khattab told me, he said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew from his wives and mentioned the hadith, he said: I entered upon him and said: O Messenger of God, what is difficult for you regarding women? If you divorce them, then God is with you and His angels, Gabriel, Michael, myself, Abu Bakr, and the believers are with you. And I rarely spoke - and I praise God - except that I hoped that God would confirm what I said, and this verse was revealed: ‘Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you. ’ ‘But if they both back him up against him - then indeed, God is his Protector, and Gabriel and the righteous believers, and the angels after that are your helpers. ’” His statement: And if they both back up one another against him, meaning if they both back up and cooperate in harming the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The people of Kufa read it with a soft ḍāl, while the others read it with a heavy ḍāl. Then God is his Guardian, meaning his Guardian and Supporter. And Gabriel and the righteous believers, narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud and Ubayy ibn Ka’b. And the righteous believers, meaning Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them. Al-Kalbi said: They are the sincere ones who are not hypocrites. And the angels after that are a support, Muqatil said: After God and Gabriel. And the righteous believers and the angels after that are a support, meaning: helpers of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is from the singular that suffices for the plural, like His statement: And excellent are those as companions (An-Nisa’: 69).
66:5: 5- Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, meaning: it is obligatory from God if His Messenger divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you, submissive, submissive to God in obedience, believing, believing in the Oneness of God, obedient, obedient, and it was said: supplicants. And it was said: praying, repentant, worshipping, traveling, fasting. Zayd ibn Aslam said: emigrants. And it was said: they travel with him wherever he travels, married and virgins. This is in reporting the ability, not the existence, because He said: if he divorces you, and it is known that He will not divorce them. This is like His saying: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you. (Muhammad 47:38) This is in reporting the ability because there is no nation in existence better than the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
66:6: The Almighty said 6- O you who have believed, protect yourselves, Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning by refraining from what God Almighty has forbidden you from / and working to obey Him, and your families from a Fire, meaning: command them to do good and forbid them from evil, teach them and discipline them, thus protecting them from a Fire, whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, meaning the keepers of the Fire, harsh, harsh with the people of the Fire, strong, strong, one of them pushes seventy thousand into the Fire at once, and they are the guards, God did not create mercy in them, they do not disobey God in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.
66:7: 7- "O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses this Day. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do."
66:8: 8- O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance. Al-Hasan and Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim, read: sincerely with a damma on the nun, while the general public read it with a fatha, meaning: a sincere repentance that advises its owner to refrain from returning to what he repented from. They differed about its meaning. Omar, Abu, and Muadh said: Sincere repentance means that one repents and then does not return to the sin, just as milk does not return to the udder. Al-Hasan said: It is for the servant to regret what has passed and resolve not to return to it. Al-Kalbi said: To seek forgiveness with the tongue, regret in the heart, and restrain oneself with the body. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: A repentance that you advise yourselves with. Al-Qurazi said: It is combined with four things: seeking forgiveness with the tongue, desisting with the body, intending to refrain from returning to it in the heart, and abandoning bad friends. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him, that is, God will not punish them by sending them to Hell.
