Their light will proceed before them and on their right, on the path. They will say, when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished, “Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent.”
66:9: 9- “O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.”
66:10: Then God gave an example of the righteous men and women, saying, Glory be to Him: 10- “God sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah,” whose name was Wa’ilah, and the wife of Lot, whose name was Wa’ilah. Muqatil said: Wa’ilah and Wa’ilah. They were under two of Our righteous servants, namely Noah and Lot, peace be upon them, but they betrayed them. Ibn Abbas said: No prophet’s wife ever transgressed against him. Rather, their betrayal was that they were not of the same religion. Noah’s wife used to say to the al-Nas 114:He is crazy, and if someone believed in him, she would inform the tyrants. As for Lot’s wife, she would guide his people to his guests. If a guest visited him at night, she would light a fire, and if he visited during the day, she would smoke it so that his people would know that a guest had visited him. Al-Kalbi said: They concealed hypocrisy and showed faith. But they did not avail them at all against God, they did not protect them, despite their prophethood, from God’s punishment, and it was said, ‘Enter the Fire with those who enter,’ with this verse God cut off the hope of anyone who commits a sin that the righteousness of others will benefit him.
66:11: Then he informed that the disobedience of others does not harm him if he is obedient, so he said: 11- “And God presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh,” and she is Asiya bint Muzahim. The commentators said: When Moses defeated the magicians, Pharaoh's wife believed, and when her Islam became clear to Pharaoh, he pegged her hands and feet to four pegs and threw her into the sun. Salman said: Pharaoh's wife was tortured by the sun, but when they left her, the angels shaded her. “When she said, ‘My Lord, build for me, near You, a house in Paradise.’ So God revealed to her her house in Paradise so that she could see it. In the story: Pharaoh ordered a huge rock to be thrown on her. When they brought her the rock, she said: “My Lord, build for me a house in Paradise.” So she saw her house in Paradise made of white pearl, and her soul was taken away, so the rock was thrown on a body that had no soul, and she felt no pain. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: God raised Pharaoh’s wife to heaven, where she eats and drinks. And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, Muqatil said: And his deeds means polytheism. Abu Salih said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And his deeds, he said: All of them. “And save me from the wrongdoing people,” the disbelievers.
66:12: 12- And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it, meaning into the pocket of her garment, and that is why He mentioned the metaphor, of Our spirit and believed in the words of her Lord, meaning the laws that God legislated for the servants through His revealed words, and His books, the people of Basra and Hafs read and His books in the plural, and the others read and His book in the singular. What is also meant by it is the multitude. And He meant by His books that were revealed to Abraham, Moses, David, and Jesus, peace be upon them. And she was of the obedient, meaning of the obedient people who obeyed her Lord, and that is why He did not say of the obedient ones. Ata' said: Of the devout means of those who pray. It is possible that by devout he means her relatives and clan, for they were righteous people who obeyed God. We narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “It is sufficient for you among the women of the worlds: Mary, daughter of Imran, Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, and Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh.”
67:1: 1- Blessed be He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent.
67:2: 2- He who created death and life. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means death in this world and life in the hereafter. Qatada said: He meant the death of man and his life in this world. God made this world a place of life and death, and made the afterlife a place of reward and permanence. It was said: Death was mentioned first because it is closer to oppression. It was also said: It was mentioned first because things were initially considered to be death, such as semen, dust, and the like, then life intervened in them. Ibn Abbas said: He created death in the form of a white ram that does not pass by anything and whose scent is not smelled by anything except that it dies. He created life in the form of a mare that meets a female, and that is what Gabriel and the prophets used to ride. It does not pass by anything and whose scent is not smelled by anything except that it comes to life. It is what the Samaritan took a handful of its scent and threw at the calf, and it came to life. To test you, between life and death, which of you is best in deeds. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: best in deeds means best in mind, most pious in avoiding God’s prohibitions, and quickest to obey God. Fudayl ibn Iyad said, The best deed is the one that is most sincere and correct. He also said, A deed is not accepted unless it is sincere and correct. Sincere means if it is done for the sake of God, and correct means if it is in accordance with the Sunnah. Al-Hassan said: Who among you is the most ascetic in this world and leaves it? Al-Farra’ said: Balwa is not used as a predicate of ‘any’ except that there is an omission between them, as you say, ‘I have tested you so I can see which of you is most obedient.’ Similar to it is: Ask them which of them is responsible for that (al-Qalam 68:40), meaning: Ask them and see which of them, so ‘any’ is raised as a subject and its predicate is better, And He is the Exalted in Might, in His vengeance against those who disobey Him, the Forgiving, for those who repent to Him.
67:3: 3- Who created seven heavens in layers, layer upon layer, one above the other, You do not see in the creation of the Most Gracious any discrepancy, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it: min tafawwat with a shaddah on the waw without an alif, and the others read it with a light waw and an alif before it, and they are two languages like tahamul and tahamul, and tatahar and tatahar. Its meaning is: What you see, O son of Adam, in the creation of the Most Gracious of crookedness, difference, and contradiction, rather it is straight and level. Its origin is from fut, which means that some of it escapes others due to its lack of straightness, Return your sight, repeat the sight, meaning: Look then return, Do you see any futur, cracks and fissures.
67:4: 4- Then return your sight twice, Ibn Abbas said: once after another, it will turn, it will turn away and return, to you, your sight humbled, humbled, humiliated, and distant, not seeing what it desires, and it is weary, tired and interrupted, not having attained what it sought. It was narrated on the authority of Ka’b that he said: The lowest heaven is a suppressed wave, the second is white marble, the third is iron, the fourth is yellow, and he said: copper, the fifth is silver, the sixth is gold, and the seventh is a red ruby, between the seventh heaven and the seven veils are deserts of light.
67:5: 5- And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven, meaning the lowest part of the earth, which is the one that people see. with lamps, meaning the planets, the singular of which is misbah, which is a lamp. A planet is called a misbah because of its light. And We have made them missiles, aiming targets, for the devils, if they eavesdrop. And We have prepared for them, in the Hereafter, the punishment of the Blaze, the blazing fire.
67:6: 6- And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination.
67:7: 7- When they are thrown into it, they will hear its sobbing, which is the first braying of a donkey, and that is the ugliest of sounds, and it is seething, boiling inside them like a boiling cauldron. Mujahid said: It will seethe inside them like a lot of water boils with a little grain.
67:8: 8- It almost bursts into tears, “from rage,” from its rage against them. Ibn Qutaybah said: It almost bursts into tears from rage against the infidels. Whenever a group is thrown into it, a group of them, its keepers ask them, a question of rebuke, Did there not come to you a warner? A messenger warning you.
67:9: 9- They said, ‘Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied him and said,’ to the messengers, “God has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.”
67:10: 10- “And they said, ‘If only we had listened’ to what the messengers brought us, ‘or understood’ from them. Ibn Abbas said: If only we had heard the guidance or understood it and acted upon it, ‘we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.’” Al-Zajjaj said: If only we had heard the hearing of one who understands and thinks or understood the mind of one who discerns and sees, we would not have been among the people of the Fire.
67:11: 11- So they confessed their sin, so destruction, away, for the companions of the Blaze. Abu Ja`far and Al-Kisa`i read so destruction with a damma on the ha`, and the rest read it with a sukoon on it. They are two dialects like terror and terror and saht and saht.
67:12: 12- Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
67:13: 13- And whether you conceal your speech or declare it aloud, He is Knowing of that within the breasts. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about the polytheists who used to speak ill of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, would inform him of what they said. Some of them said to one another: Conceal your speech so that the God of Muhammad does not hear.
67:14: So God, the Most High, said: 14- Does He not know who created? Does He not know what is in the hearts of their creation? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted. His knowledge of the hearts is Subtle, the Acquainted with what is in them of good, evil, and whispers. And it was said that who refers to the creation, meaning does God not know His creation?
67:15: 15- It is He who made the earth subservient to you, easy and walkable, so walk in its paths, Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: in its mountains. Ad-Dahhak said: in its hills. Mujahid said: in its roads and paths. Al-Hasan said: in its paths. Al-Kalbi said: in its edges. Muqatil said: in its regions. Al-Farra’ said: in its sides. The root of the word is the side, from which comes the word man’s shoulder, “the wind’s wrath,” and the side of someone. “And eat of His provision,” from what He created as provision for you on the earth. And to Him is the resurrection, meaning: and to Him you will be resurrected from your graves.
67:16: Then he feared the infidels and said: 16- Do you feel secure from Him who is in the heaven? Ibn Abbas said: meaning: the punishment of Him who is in the heaven if you disobey Him, that He will cause the earth to swallow you up and then at once it will sway. Al-Hasan said: It moves with its people. It was also said: It will fall with them. The meaning is that God the Almighty will move the earth when He swallows them up until it throws them down, rises above them and passes over them. It is said: Mar Yamur means: it came and went.
67:17: 17- Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send upon you a storm of stones? A wind with stones as He did to the people of Lot. Then you will know, in the Hereafter and at death, how My warner is, meaning My warning when you witness the punishment.
67:18: 18- And those before them denied, meaning the disbelievers of past nations, so how was My denial, meaning My denial of them with the punishment.
67:19: 19- Have they not seen the birds above them spreading out their wings in the air, and folding them in? “What holds them back” in the state of folding and spreading them so that they do not fall, “except the Most Merciful. Indeed, He is Seeing of all things.”
67:20: 20- Is this he who will be your soldiers? is a rhetorical question. Ibn Abbas said: meaning a protection for you, who will support you other than the Most Gracious, protecting you from His punishment and repelling from you what He intends for you. The disbelievers are only in delusion, meaning in delusion from Satan who deceives them that the punishment will not descend upon them.
67:21: 21- Is this He who provides for you if He should withhold His provision? That is, who is the one who provides you with rain if God withholds it from you? Rather, they persist in insolence, persisting in misguidance, and aversion, distancing themselves from the truth. Mujahid said: ungrateful.
67:22: Then he gave an example and said: 22- Is he who walks prone on his face, bowing his head in misguidance and ignorance, blind in heart and eye, unable to see right or left, and he is the disbeliever. Qatada said: He committed sins in this world, so God will gather him on his face on the Day of Resurrection, more guided than he who walks upright, upright, seeing the way, on a straight path, and he is the believer. Qatada said: He will walk upright on the Day of Resurrection.
67:23: 23- “Say, ‘It is He who created you and made for you hearing and sight and hearts. Little do you give thanks.’” Muqatil said: This means that they do not give thanks to the Lord of these blessings.
67:24: 24- Say, ‘It is He who dispersed you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.’
67:25: 25- And they say, ‘When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?’
67:26: 26- Say, ‘Knowledge is only with God, and I am only a clear warner.’
67:27: 27- So when they saw it, meaning: the torment in the Hereafter - according to the majority of commentators - and Mujahid said: it means the torment at Badr, close, meaning close, and it is a noun that describes a verbal noun and is used for both masculine and feminine, singular, dual, and plural forms. The faces of those who disbelieved will be made ugly, blackened and covered with gloom. The meaning is that their faces will be made ugly with blackness. It is said: something is bad, it is bad if it is ugly, and bad, it is bad if it is ugly. And it will be said, to it, meaning the guards said, This, meaning this torment, that you used to call for, you make a supplication from the supplication, you call for it and wish that it will be hastened for you. Ya’qub read tad’un with a light tadhkirun and it is the reading of Qatada and their meaning is the same like tadhkirun and tadhkirun.
67:28: 28- Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Mecca who wish for your destruction, “Have you considered: if God destroys me and those with me,” of the believers, or has mercy on us, and keeps us alive but delays our appointed times, then who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment? For it will inevitably befall them. It was also said that its meaning is: Have you considered: if God destroys me and those with me, or has mercy on us and forgives us, then we—despite our faith—fear that He will destroy us for our sins, because His judgment is binding on us. So who can protect you and prevent you from His punishment while you are disbelievers? This is the meaning of what Ibn Abbas said.
67:29: 29- Say, ‘He is the Most Gracious,’ the one we worship. “We have believed in Him and in Him we have relied. You will soon know.” Al-Kisa’i read it with a ya’, while the others read it with a ta’. Who is in clear error, meaning, when you witness the punishment, you will know who among us is astray, us or you?
67:30: 30- Say, ‘Have you considered if your water were to become sunken in?’ Sunken into the ground, beyond the reach of hands and buckets. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It means the water of Zamzam. Then who will bring you flowing water? Apparent, visible to the eyes and accessible to hands and buckets. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Flowing means flowing. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Farsi told me, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid told us, Abu Yahya Al-Bazzar told us, Muhammad bin Yahya told us, Abu Dawud told us, Imran told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abbas Al-Jashmi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is a surah from the Book of God that is only thirty verses long. It will intercede for a man, bringing him out of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection and admit him into Paradise. It is Surah Al-Mulk.”
68:1: 1- N, they differed about it. Ibn Abbas said: It is the whale, on whose back is the land. This is the opinion of Mujahid, Muqatil, Al-Suddi, and Al-Kalbi. Abu Dhabiyan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing that God created was the pen, which recorded what would happen until the Day of Resurrection. Then He created the letter Nun and spread the earth on its back. The letter Nun moved, and the earth shook, and it was fixed with the mountains, and the mountains boast of the earth. Then Ibn Abbas recited: “Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.” They differed about his name. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: His name is Yahmut. Al-Waqidi said: Liutha. Kaab said: Luwaytha. Ali reported: His name is Balhuth. The narrators said: When God created the earth and split it, He sent an angel from under the throne, and he descended to the earth until he entered under the seven earths. He placed it on his shoulder, one of his hands in the east and the other in the west, extending and gripping the seven earths, until he controlled it. His feet had no place to rest. Then God Almighty sent down from Paradise a bull with forty thousand horns and forty thousand legs. He placed the king’s feet on its hump, but his feet could not rest. So he took a green ruby from the highest degree in Paradise, the thickness of which was a journey of five hundred years, and placed it between the bull’s hump and its ear, and his feet rested on it. The horns of that bull protrude from the ends of the earth, and its nostrils are in the sea, so it takes a breath every day. When it breathes, the sea ebbs, and when it breathes, the sea ebbs, and when it breathes, the sea ebbs, so the bull’s legs had no place to rest. Then God Almighty created a rock the thickness of seven heavens and seven earths, and the bull’s legs rested on it. It is the rock that Luqman said to his son, O my son, if it is the weight of a mustard seed, it will be in… Rock" (Luqman 31:16) And the rock had no resting place, so God created Nun, which is the great whale, and placed the rock on its back, and the rest of its body was empty, and the whale was on the sea, and the sea was on the wind, and the wind was on the power. It is said: The whole world and everything on it is two letters, and the Almighty said to it: Glory be to Him, be, and it was. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Iblis penetrated the whale that had the earth on its back and whispered to it, saying: Do you know what is on your back, O Luwaythah, of nations, beasts, trees and mountains? If you shake them off, you will throw them off your back. Luwaythah wanted to do that, but God sent a beast that entered its nostril and reached its brain. The whale cried out to God about it, so God gave it permission and it came out. Ka'b said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, he looks at it and it looks at him. If he thinks of doing any of that, it returns as it was. Some of them said: Nun is the last letter of Ar-Rahman, and this is the narration of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan, Qatada and Al-Dahhak said: The letter nun is the inkwell. It was said: It is an oath by which God swore. It was also said: It is the opening of the Surah. Ata’ said: The opening of his name is Noor and Nasir. Muhammad bin Kaab said: God swore by his victory for the believers. "And the Pen" is that with which God wrote the remembrance. It is a pen of light, its length extending from the heavens to the earth. It is said that the first thing God created was the Pen, and He looked at it and it split in two. Then He said: Record what will be until the Day of Resurrection. So it recorded that on the Preserved Tablet. "And what they inscribe means what the guardian angels write of the deeds of the children of Adam.
68:2: 2- You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman, is an answer to their saying, O you to whom the message has been sent down, indeed, you are mad." (al-Hijr 15:6). So God swore by the letter "nun and the pen and what it writes of deeds, saying, You are not, by the grace of your Lord, by the prophethood of your Lord, a madman," meaning: You cannot be mad, and God has blessed you with prophethood and wisdom. It was also said: by the infallibility of your Lord. It was also said: it is as it is said: you are not mad, and praise be to God. It was also said: its meaning is: you are not mad, and the grace is to your Lord, like their saying: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, meaning: and praise be to You.
68:3: 3- And you will have a reward that is not limited, meaning: it will be diminished and not cut off by your patience in the face of their slander against you.
68:4: 4- And indeed, you are of a great moral character. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: A great religion. I have no other religion more beloved to me or more pleasing to me than it, and that is the religion of Islam. Al-Hasan said: It is the etiquette of the Qur’an. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, was asked about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: His character was the Qur’an. Qatada said: It is what he obeyed of God’s commands and refrained from of God’s prohibitions, and the meaning is that you are of the character that God commanded you to have in the Qur’an. It was said: God called his creation great because he complied with God’s discipline of him by saying: Take what is easy Al-A’raf 7:198. We narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God sent me to perfect good morals and perfect good deeds. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ahmad bin Saeed Abu Abdullah told us, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara’ say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had the most handsome face of people and the best character. He was neither too tall nor too short.” Abdullah bin Abdul Samad Al-Juzajani told us, Abu Al-Qasim Ali bin Ahmad Al-Khuza’i told us, Abu Saeed Al-Haytham bin Kulayb Al-Shashi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Ja’far bin Sulayman Al-Dab’i told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: “I served the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for ten years. He never said to me ‘uff,’ nor did he say about anything I did, ‘Why did you do that?’ nor about anything I left off, ‘Why did you leave that?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one of the best of people in character. I never touched silk or brocade or anything softer than the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor did I smell musk or perfume that was more fragrant than the sweat of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Saffar told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Barni told us, Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was neither vulgar nor obscene, and he used to say: The best of you are those with the best character.” Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, Muhammad ibn Hisham ibn Malas told us, Marwan al-Fazari told us, Hamid al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Anas, “A woman came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on one of the roads of Medina and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I have a need of you.’ He said: ‘O mother of so-and-so, sit in whichever alley of Medina you wish and I will sit with you.’ So she did, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat with her until he had fulfilled her need.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us: Muhammad bin Isa told us, Hisham told us, Hamid Al-Tawil told us, Anas bin Malik told us: “If a female slave from the people of Medina took the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and went with him wherever she wanted.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Ja’d told us, Imran bin Zaid Al-Taghlabi told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Al-Ami, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shook hands with a man, he would not remove his hand from his hand until he was the one who removed his hand, and he would not turn his face away from his face until he was the one who turned his face away from his face, and he was never seen putting his knees forward in front of his companion.” Abdullah bin Abdul Samad told us, Abu Al-Qasim Al-Khuza’i told us, Al-Hathim bin Kulayb told us, Abu Isa told us, Harun bin Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us, Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never struck anything with his hand except when fighting in the cause of God, and he never struck a servant or a woman.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ismail bin Abdullah told us, Malik told me, on the authority of Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Anas, who said: “I was walking with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was wearing a Najrani cloak with a thick border. A Bedouin caught up with him and pulled his cloak violently until I saw the side of the Messenger of God’s shoulder, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the border of the cloak had left marks on it from the force of his pull. Then he said: ‘O Muhammad, give me some of God’s wealth that you have.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to him, laughed, and ordered that he be given something.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Ali bin Al-Madini told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ya’la bin Mamlak, on the authority of Umm Al-Darda’, who narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The heaviest thing that will be placed on the scale of the believer on the Day of Resurrection is good character, and God Almighty hates the obscene and vulgar person. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam'ani told us, Abu Ja'far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abu Na'im told us, Dawud bin Yazid Al-Awdi told us, I heard my father say, I heard Abu Hurairah say: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: Do you know what most often causes people to enter Hellfire? They said, 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said, 'The things that most often cause people to enter Hellfire are the two hollow parts: the private parts and the mouth. Do you know what most often causes people to enter Paradise?' They said, 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said, 'The things that most often cause people to enter Paradise are: fear of God and good character.'" Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm told us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam told us, my father and Shuaib told us, they said: Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Haad, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr, on the authority of al-Muttalib ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Aisha, she said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘The believer, through his good character, attains the status of one who stands in prayer at night and fasts during the day.’”
68:5: God Almighty says 5- Then you will see, and they will see. So you will see, O Muhammad, and they will see - meaning the people of Mecca - when the punishment descends upon them.
68:6: 6- Which of you is bewitched? It was said that it means: Which of you is insane? So bewitched is a passive participle in the sense of a verbal noun, just as one says: So-and-so is not flogged or sane, meaning he is flogged and sane. This is the meaning of Ad-Dahhak's statement and Al-Awfi's narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said that the letter ba means in, and its meaning is: You will see, and they will see, in which of the two groups is the madman in your group or in their group? It was said that the preposition ba means with, and the one being tempted is Satan. The meaning is: Which of you is Satan with, the believers or the disbelievers? This is the meaning of Mujahid’s statement. Others said: It is redundant, meaning: Which of you is the one who is bewitched? That is, the madman who is bewitched by madness. This is the opinion of Qatada.
68:7: 7- Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
68:8: 8- So do not obey the deniers, meaning the polytheists of Mecca, for they were calling him to the religion of his fathers, but he forbade him from obeying them.
68:9: 9- They wish that you would be lenient so that they would be lenient. Ad-Dahhak said: If you were to disbelieve so that they would disbelieve. Al-Kalbi said: If you were gentle with them so that they would be gentle with you. Al-Hasan said: If you were to be gentle with them in your religion so that they would be gentle with you in their religion. Zayd ibn Aslam said: If you were to be hypocritical and show off so that they would be hypocritical and show off. Ibn Qutaybah said: They wanted you to worship their gods for a while and they to worship God for a while.
68:10: 10- And do not obey every worthless oath-taker, one who swears falsely a lot. Muqatil said: He means Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira. It was also said: Al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth. Ata' said: Al-Akhns ibn Shuraiq, worthless, weak and contemptible. It was said: It is a verbal noun from humiliation, which means lack of opinion and discernment. Ibn Abbas said: A liar. It is close to the first, because a person only lies because he feels humiliated.
68:11: 11- Hammaz, a backbiter who eats people's flesh by slandering and gossiping. Al-Hasan said: He is the one who backbites his brother in a gathering, such as by saying: Hamzah, Musha'a Binamim, a gossiper who spreads gossip among people to cause discord between them.
68:12: 12- He who prevents good", is miserly with money. Ibn Abbas said: "He who prevents good", meaning Islam, prevents his children and clan from converting to Islam, saying: If one of you enters the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him at all. "Transgressor", is unjust and transgresses against the truth. "Sinful, is wicked.
68:13: 13- Atal, Atal means rough and coarse. Al-Hasan said: He is the one with a foul and bad character. Al-Farra' said: He is the one who is very argumentative about falsehood. Al-Kalbi said: He is the one who is very strong in his disbelief, and every strong person among the Arabs is Atal, and its origin is from Atal which means to push with violence. Ubaid bin Umair said: The Atal is the gluttonous, the drunkard, the strong, the very strong in his disbelief, he does not weigh an barley grain in the scales. The king will push seventy thousand of those people into the fire at once. After that, meaning with that, he means what we described him with, Zanim, which is the pretender who is attached to the people, but he is not one of them. Ata' said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means with this he is a pretender among the Quraysh but he is not one of them. Marra Al-Hamdani said: His father only claimed him after eighteen years. It was said: The Zanim is the one who has a hump like the hump of a sheep. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said about this verse: He was described but not recognized until it was said that he was a sinner, and he was recognized. He had a mark on his neck by which he was recognized. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He is known by evil just as a sheep is known by its hump. Ibn Qutaybah said: We do not know that God has described anyone or mentioned any of his faults as He mentioned the faults of Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, and thus inflicted upon him a disgrace that will not leave him in this world or the next. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an Al-Wa’iz told us, Abu Muhammad bin Zanjawayh bin Muhammad told us, Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Hilali told us, Abdullah bin Al-Walid Al-Adani told us, on the authority of Sufyan, Ma’bad bin Khalid Al-Qaysi told us, on the authority of Haritha bin Wahb Al-Khuza’i, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you about the people of Paradise? Every weak and oppressed person, if he were to swear an oath by God, He would fulfill it. Shall I not tell you about the people of Hell? Every stubborn, arrogant person.”
68:14: 14- If he was a man of wealth and sons, Abu Ja'far, Ibn Amir, Hamza, Abu Bakr, and Ya'qub read: A'an as an interrogative. Then Hamza and Abu Bakr soften the two hamzas without extending it, and Abu Ja'far, Ibn Amir, and Ya'qub extend the first hamza, and soften the second one. The others read it without an interrogative as a statement, so whoever reads it with an interrogative, its meaning is: If he was a man of wealth and sons?
68:15: 15- When Our verses are recited to him, he says, ‘Legends of the ancients.’ That is, he made the reward for the blessings He bestowed upon him of children and wealth and disbelief in Our verses. It was also said that its meaning is, If he had wealth and children, would you obey him? Whoever reads the hadith, its meaning is: Do not obey every lowly swearer, even if he has wealth and children, meaning: Do not obey him because of his wealth and children. When Our verses are recited to him, he says, ‘Legends of the ancients.’
68:16: Then he threatened him, saying: 16- We will brand him on the snout, and the snout means the nose. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Mujahid said: That is, we will blacken his face, and we will make a mark for him in the Hereafter by which he will be known, and that is the blackness of the face. Al-Farra’ said: He singled out Khartoum for the name, as it is in the doctrine of the face, because part of something is used to express the whole of it. Ibn Abbas said: We will strike him with the sword, and he did that on the day of Badr. Qatada said: We will attach something to him that will never leave him. Al-Qatibi said: The Arabs say about a man who insulted another man with an ugly insult: He branded him with an evil brand. He means: He stuck a disgrace on him that will not leave him, just as a brand cannot be erased and its trace cannot be forgotten. God has attached a disgrace to what he mentioned of his faults that will not leave him in this world or the next, like a brand on the nose. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kisa’i said: We will cauterize him on his face.
68:17: 17- Indeed, We tested them, meaning We tested the people of Mecca with famine and hunger, as We tested, We tested, the companions of Paradise. Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated, on the authority of al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Regarding the words of God Almighty: Indeed, We tested them as We tested the companions of Paradise, he said: There was a garden in Yemen called al-Darwan, two farsakhs from Sana'a, which was trampled by people on the road. It was planted by people who prayed, and it belonged to a man who died and his three sons inherited it. When they cut down their palm trees, everything that the sickle passed through and did not cut it, and when it was thrown from the top of the palm trees onto the carpet, everything that fell on the carpet was also for the poor. When they harvested their crops, everything that the sickle passed through was for the poor, and when they trampled it, everything that was scattered was also for them. When the father died and these brothers inherited it from their father, they said: By God, the money is little, and the children For many, and this matter was only done when the money was plentiful and the children were few, but if the money was little and the children were many, then we cannot do this, so they made an alliance among themselves one day to go out in the morning before the people left and to harvest their palm trees, and they did not make an exception, he says: They did not say God willing, so the people went out in the morning to their garden to harvest it before the poor people left, and they saw it black, and a tormentor had come upon it in the night and burned it, so it became like a harvest, so that is what the Almighty said: When they swore, they swore, to harvest it in the morning, to harvest it and cut its fruit when they woke up before the poor people knew.
68:18: 18- And they do not make an exception, nor do they say, God willing.
68:19: 19- And a torment from your Lord swept over them at night, a torment, at night, and the torment only occurs at night. That torment was a fire that descended from the sky and burned them, while they were asleep.
68:20: 20- So it became like a barren land, like a dark, black night. Al-Hasan said: meaning that the goodness was cut off from it, so there was nothing in it. Al-Akhfash said: Like the dawn of the night. The root of sareem is the severed, like qatil and maqtool. Everything that is severed is sareem, so the night is sareem and the dawn is sareem, because each one of them is cut off from the other. Ibn Abbas said: Like black ash in the language of Khuzaymah.
68:21: 21- And they called to each other in the morning, they called to each other when they woke up.
68:22: 22- Go to your tillage, meaning the fruits, crops, and grapes, if you are severe, cutting down the palm trees.
68:23: 23- So they set out, they walked towards her, while whispering, they whispered.
68:24: Some of them say to each other secretly: 24- No poor person shall enter it upon you today.
68:25: 25- And they went out in the morning with a heavy heart. In the language, hard means intent, prevention, and anger. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: with seriousness and effort. Al-Qurazi, Mujahid, and Ikrimah said, On an agreed-upon matter that they established among themselves. This means intent, because the one who intends something is serious and agreed upon the matter. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Qutaibi said: They went out with the intention of preventing the poor. It is said: The year has been hara’id if it has no rain, and the she-camel has been hara’id if it has no milk. Al-Shaabi and Sufyan said: Out of anger and rage towards the poor. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: With power, “capable,” in their view of their Paradise and its fruits, with no one standing between them and it.
68:26: 26- So when they saw it, they said, ‘Indeed, we are astray.’ That is, when they saw Paradise burning, they said, “Indeed, we are on the wrong path. We have lost our way to Paradise. This is not our Paradise.”
68:27: Some of them said: 27- Rather, we are deprived. We are deprived of its goodness and benefit by preventing the poor and leaving out the exception.
68:28: 28- “The most just, wisest, and best of them said: ‘Did I not tell you why you do not glorify God?’ Why don’t you make an exception? He criticized them for not making an exception in their saying: ‘They will surely harvest it in the morning.’ The exception is called glorification because it is a glorification of God and an acknowledgment that no one has power over anything except by His will. Abu Saleh said: Their exception was: Glory be to God. It was also said: Why don’t you glorify God and say: Glory be to God, and thank Him for what He has given you? And it was also said: Why don’t you ask His forgiveness for what you did?
68:29: 29- They said, ‘Glory be to our Lord,’ they declared Him free from being unjust in what He did, and they admitted to their own injustice, saying, Indeed, we were unjust, by preventing the poor.
68:30: 30- So some of them turned to others, blaming each other, blaming each other for depriving the poor of their rights.
68:31: And they called out woe to themselves: 31- They said, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors!’ in denying the rights of the poor. Ibn Kaysan said: We were transgressors because of God’s blessings, so we were not grateful for them and did not do what our fathers did before.
68:32: Then they came to their senses and said: 32- “Perhaps our Lord will replace it for us with something better. Indeed, we are desirous of our Lord.” Abdullah bin Masoud said: It has reached me that the people were sincere, and God knew their sincerity, so He replaced it for them with a garden called Al-Hayawan, in which there are grapes, and a mule can carry a single bunch of them.
68:33: God Almighty said: 33- Such is the punishment, meaning: as We did to them, We will do to those who transgressed Our limits and disobeyed Our command. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
68:34: Then he told what he has for the righteous, saying: 34- Indeed, for the righteous are with their Lord gardens of pleasure. The polytheists said: We will be given in the Hereafter something better than what you are given.
68:35: So God said, in refutation of them: 35- Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
68:36: 36- What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
68:37: 37- Or do you have a Book, revealed from God, in which, in this Book, you study, you read.
68:38: 38- Indeed, you will have in it, in that book, whatever you choose, you choose and desire.
68:39: 39- Or do you have oaths, covenants and pacts, upon Us that are conclusive, confirming that We have made a covenant with you, and you have taken it as a pledge from Us so that your covenant will not be broken, until the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, for you, in that covenant, is what you judge, for yourselves of good and honor with God. And the breaking of in in the two verses is due to the inclusion of the lam in their predicate.
68:40: Then he said to his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: 40- Ask them who is a leader in this, guaranteeing that they will have in the Hereafter what the Muslims have?
68:41: 41- Or do they have partners? That is, do they have partners with God, lords who do this? It was also said: witnesses who testify to the truth of what they claim. Then let them produce their partners, if they are truthful.
68:42: 42- The Day the shin will be bared. It was said: The Day is an adverbial phrase for His saying, Then let them bring their partners, meaning: let them bring them on that day so that they may benefit them and intercede for them. The Day the shin will be bared. It was said: about a terrible and severe matter. Ibn Abbas said: it is the most severe hour on the Day of Resurrection. Saeed bin Jubair said: The day the shin will be uncovered refers to the severity of the matter. Ibn Qutaybah said: The Arabs say to a man when he encounters a serious matter that requires seriousness and enduring hardship: He rolled up his sleeves. And it is said: when the matter becomes intense in war: The war has uncovered its sleeves. Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa Al-Jaludi told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Suwaid bin Saeed told me, Jaafar told me, Hafs bin Maysarah told me, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that some people during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Messenger of God, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes. Do you have any difficulty in seeing the sun at noon when it is clear and there are no clouds? And do you have any difficulty in seeing the moon on a full moon night when it is clear and there are no clouds? They said: No, O Messenger of God. He said: You will not have any difficulty in seeing God on the Day of Resurrection except as you have any difficulty in seeing one of the two. When the Day of Resurrection comes, a muezzin will announce that every nation will follow what it used to worship, and no one will remain who used to worship God, whether righteous or wicked or other than the People of the Book. The Jews will be summoned and it will be said to them: What did you worship? They will say: We used to worship Ezra, the son of God. It will be said: You have lied. God has not taken a wife or a son. So what do you seek? They will say, We are thirsty, O our Lord, so give us drink. Then it will be said to them, Will you not return? They will be herded into the Fire as if it were a mirage, parts of which crush one another, and they will fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be summoned and it will be said to them, What did you worship? They will say, “We worshipped Christ, the son of God. Then it will be said to them: God has not taken a wife or a son. Then it will be said to them: What do you seek? They will say: We are thirsty, O our Lord, so give us a drink. Then it will be said to them: Will you not return? Then they will be herded into Hell as if it were a mirage, parts crushing each other, and they will fall into the Fire, until there remains only those who worshipped God, of the righteous and the wicked, then the Lord of the Worlds will come to them in a form less than the one they saw Him in. He will say: What are you waiting for? For every nation to follow what it used to worship. They will say: O our Lord, we left the people in this world when we were most needy of them, and we did not keep company with them. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in God from you. We do not associate anything with God, two or three times, until some of them are about to turn over. He will say: Is there a sign between you and him by which you can recognize him? They will say: Yes. Then He will uncover his shin, and no one who used to prostrate to God of his own accord will remain except that God will give him permission to prostrate. No one who used to prostrate out of hypocrisy and showing off will remain except that God will make his back a single layer. Whenever he wants to prostrate, he will fall on his back. Then they will raise their heads and he has transformed into the image in which they saw him the first time and he will say: I am your Lord. They will say: You are our Lord. Then the bridge will be struck over Hell and intercession will be granted, and they will say: O God, save us, save us. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is the bridge? He said: A slippery slope in which there are hooks and pegs and thorns. It is in Najd and it has a thorn called Al-Sa’dan. It will pass The believers are like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like birds, like the best horses and riders. Some are saved as Muslims, some are scratched and sent away, and some are thrown into the fire of Hell. Then, when the believers are saved from the Fire, by Him in Whose hand is my soul, none of you will be more ardent in exacting justice for God than the believers on the Day of Resurrection for their brothers who are in the Fire. They will say, “Our Lord, they used to fast with us, pray, and perform Hajj.” It will be said to them, Bring out those you recognized. Their images will be forbidden to the Fire, and they will bring out many people whose bodies have been burned up to the middle of their shins and up to their knees. Then they will say, Our Lord, there is no one left in it of those whom You commanded us to be. He will say, Go back, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of a dinar of goodness, bring him out. So they will bring out many people. Then they will say, Our Lord, we have not left in it anyone of those whom You commanded us to be. Then He will say, “Go back, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of half... Then they will bring out many people. Then they will say, “Our Lord, we have not left in it anyone of those whom You commanded us to be.” Then He will say, Go back, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of half a dinar of goodness, bring him out. In his heart is an atom's weight of goodness, so bring him out. So they will bring out a great number of people, then they will say: Our Lord, we have not left within it anyone in whom there is goodness than that which You have commanded us to have. Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri used to say: If you do not believe me in this hadith, then read if you wish: "Indeed, God does not wrong by as much as an atom's weight. And if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from His presence a great reward." (An-Nisa': 40). So God will say: The angels have interceded, the prophets have interceded, the believers have interceded, and none remains except the Most Merciful of the merciful. Then He will take a handful of fire and bring out from it a people who never did any good and have turned into blackened corpses. Then He will cast them into a river at the mouths of Paradise called the River of Life. They will come out as a seed comes out of the silt of a torrent. Do you not see that it turns toward a rock or a tree? Some of it turns toward the sun, yellow and green, and some of it turns toward the shade, white. He said: “They will come out like pearls with rings around their necks. The people of Paradise will recognize them. These are those freed by God from the Fire, whom God has admitted into Paradise without any deed they had done or any good they had presented. Then He will say: ‘Enter Paradise, and whatever you have seen is yours.’ They will say: ‘Our Lord, You have given us what You have not given to anyone in the worlds.’ He will say: ‘You have with Me something better than this.’ They will say: ‘Our Lord, what can be better than this?’ He will say: ‘My pleasure, and I will never be angry with you after it.’” Muhammad ibn Ismail narrated this hadith on the authority of Yahya ibn Bakir, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Khalid ibn Yazid, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam, with this meaning. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah Al-Nuaimi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Ismail informed us, Adam informed us, Al-Layth informed us, on the authority of Khalid ibn Yazid, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. Whoever used to prostrate in this world for show and to be heard will remain, and he will go to prostrate, but his back will become a single flat surface. ’” The Almighty says: And they are called to prostrate, but they are unable, meaning: The backs of the infidels and hypocrites will become like the hooves of cows, and they will be unable to prostrate.
68:43: 43- Their eyes will be humbled, meaning that the believers will raise their heads from prostration and their faces will be whiter than snow, while the faces of the disbelievers and hypocrites will be black. Humiliation will overwhelm them, the humiliation of regret and sorrow will overwhelm them. Although they were called to prostration, Ibrahim al-Taymi said: meaning to the obligatory prayer with the call to prayer and the call to prayer. Saeed bin Jubayr said: They would hear Come to prosperity but would not respond. And they were sound, healthy but would not come to it. Ka’b al-Ahbar said: By God, this verse was only revealed about those who stayed away from the congregational prayers.
68:44: 44- So leave me and he who denies this statement, meaning leave me and those who deny the Qur’an, and leave me alone with them. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is do not occupy your heart with them, they are all in Me, for I will suffice you against them. He said: And similar to it is: Leave Me and he whom I created alone, its meaning in the language is: do not occupy your heart with him and entrust him to Me, for I will reward him. Similar to it is a man’s saying: Leave Me and him, not that he prevented him from it, but its interpretation is all of it, for I will suffice you against him. God Almighty says: We will seize them by degrees, We will seize them with punishment, from where they do not know, so they were punished on the day of Badr.
68:45: 45- "And grant them respite. Indeed, my plan is firm."
68:46: 46- Or do you ask them for a reward? So they are burdened by debt.
68:47: 47- Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write down?
68:49: 49- Had it not been that a blessing from his Lord overtook him, overtook him, he would have been cast out into the open, he would have been thrown into the open air from the belly of the whale, while he was blameworthy, blamed and censured for the sin he committed.
68:50: 50- So his Lord chose him, selected him, and made him among the righteous.
68:51: 51- And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes. This is because the disbelievers wanted to cast the evil eye on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some people from Quraysh looked at him and said: We have never seen anyone like him or his arguments. It was said: The eye was among the Banu Asad until a fat she-camel or cow would pass by one of them and he would examine it and then say: O girl, take the basket and the dirham and bring us some of its meat. So it would not leave until it fell to death and was slaughtered. Al-Kalbi said: There was an Arab man who would not eat for two or three days, then he would raise the side of his tent and the camels would pass by it and he would say: I have never seen camels or sheep better than these today. They would not go far before a group or several of them would fall. The disbelievers asked this man to cast the evil eye on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and do the same to him, but God protected His Prophet and revealed: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes, meaning almost. The lam was inserted in lizalqunak because of the place of in. The people of Medina read lizalqunak with a fat-ha on the ya’, while the others read it with a damma. They are two dialects. It is said: zalaquhu yazlquhu zaliqan and azalaquhu yazlquhu izlaqan. Ibn Abbas said: It means: They will carry you out. It is said: The arrow slipped, meaning it passed through. Al-Suddi said: They strike you with their eyes. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: They aid you. It was also said: They remove you. Al-Kalbi said: They defeat you. It was also said: They distract you from your mission of conveying the message. Ibn Qutaybah said: He does not mean that they will strike you with their eyes as the one who casts the evil eye strikes with his eye what pleases him, but rather he means that they will look at you when you recite the Qur’an with intense hostility and hatred, almost to the point of making you fall. Al-Zajjaj said: It means that due to the intensity of their hostility, they almost defeat you with their looks of hatred. This is used in the speech of the Arabs, as when a speaker says: He looked at me with a look that almost defeats me, or with a look that almost devoured me. Evidence of the correctness of this meaning is that he coupled this look with hearing the Qur’an, as in His statement: When they heard the message, and they hated that intensely, so they looked at him with hatred, and they said, ‘Indeed, he is mad,’ meaning they attributed madness to him when they heard him recite the Qur’an.
68:52: Then God Almighty said: 52- “And it,” meaning the Qur’an, is only a reminder to the worlds. Ibn Abbas said: An admonition to the believers. Al-Hasan said: The cure for the evil eye is for a person to recite this verse. Abu Ali Hassan bin Saeed Al-Munai’i told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Mahmash Al-Ziyadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qattan told us, Ahmad bin Yusuf Al-Salami told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, told us: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The evil eye is real, and he forbade tattooing.” Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Sayyid Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Dawud al-Alawi told us, Abu Nasr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamduyah ibn Sahl al-Marwazi told us, Mahmud ibn Adam al-Marwazi told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Urwah ibn Amir, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rafa’ah al-Zarqi, that Asma’ bint Umays said: O Messenger of God, the children of Ja’far are afflicted by the evil eye. Should I recite ruqyah for them? He said: Yes, for if anything could precede divine decree, it would be the evil eye.
69:1: 1- Al-Haqqah means the Day of Resurrection. It is called Al-Haqqah because it has come true and there is no lie in it. It was also said that it is because the true facts and realities of matters are in it, and because the reward for deeds is due in it, meaning it is obligatory. It is said: A thing has come true upon him if it is obligatory, it is obligatory, it is obligatory. God the Almighty said: But the word of punishment has come true upon the disbelievers (al-Zumar 39:71). Al-Kisa'i said: Al-Haqqah is the Day of Truth.
69:2: 2- What is the Inevitable Event? This is a question that means to magnify its importance, just as one says: Zayd, what Zayd, to magnify his importance.
69:3: 3- And what will make you know what the Inevitable is? That is, you will not know it because you have not witnessed it or seen the horrors it contains.
69:4: 4- Thamud and Aad denied the Calamity. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: The Resurrection was called the Calamity because it strikes fear into the hearts of the servants. It was also said: They denied the punishment that their Prophet had threatened them with until it descended upon them and struck their hearts.
69:5: 5- As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the transgression, meaning by their transgression and disbelief. It was said: It is a verbal noun, and it was said: It is an adjective, meaning by their transgression, and this is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid, as he said: Thamud denied it because of their transgression (Ash-Shams: 11). Qatada said: By the transgressing cry, which is the one that exceeded the limits of a cry and destroyed them. It was said: It overwhelmed the treasurers, so they had no way to control it, and they did not know how much of it came out, just as the water overwhelmed the people of Noah.
69:6: 6- As for ‘Aad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind. It attacked its treasurers, so they did not obey them and they had no power over it. It exceeded the limit, so they did not know how much came out of it.
69:7: 7- "He subjected it to them," meaning He sent it upon them. Muqatil said: He made it unleashed upon them, "seven nights and eight days." Wahb said: These are the days that the Arabs call the days of the old woman, with cold and strong winds. It was said: They were called old women because they were in the last stages of winter. It was also said: They were called that because an old woman from the tribe of Aad entered a flock and the wind followed her and killed her on the eighth day of the punishment and the punishment stopped. "Hasman," Mujahid and Qatadah said: Consecutive with no break. Based on this, it is from the word "hasam" cauterization, which is to continue to apply an iron to the site of the disease until it heals. Then everything that is continued is called "hasam hesam, and its plural is hasum hesoom, like shahid witness and shahoud" witnesses. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Permanent "hasman." An-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "I have cut them off and destroyed them. Hasm means cutting and preventing, and from it is hasam al-da'a." Al-Zajjaj said: What the verse requires is in the sense that it is "hasam" hesoom that annihilates and eliminates them. Attia said: It is decisive as if it has decided the goodness from its people, and you see the people in it, meaning in those nights and days, fallen dead, perished is the plural of fallen, “as if they were hollow palm trunks,” fallen, and it was said: empty of hollows.
69:8: 8- Do you see any remnant of them? That is, any remaining soul, meaning: not one of them remains.
69:9: 9- And Pharaoh came and those before him, the people of Basra and Al-Kisa’i read it with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba’, meaning and those with him from his soldiers and followers. The others read it with a fatha on the qaf and a sukoon on the ba’, meaning and those before him from the disbelieving nations, and the overturned, meaning: the cities of the people of Lot, meaning: the people of the overturned. It was said that he means the nations who were overturned by their sin, meaning they were destroyed by their transgressions, by the sinful, meaning by the sin and disobedience, which is polytheism.
69:10: 10- So they disobeyed the Messenger of their Lord, meaning Lot and Moses, so He seized them with a severe seizure, meaning a growing one. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: severe. It was also said: in addition to the punishment of the nations.
69:11: 11- When the water rose, that is, it became violent and exceeded its limits until it rose above everything and was elevated above it, meaning the time of Noah, peace be upon him, We carried you, that is, We carried your fathers while you were in their loins, in the moving ship, in the ship that moves in the water.
69:12: 12- That We may make it, that is, that We may make that action which We did, of drowning the people of Noah and saving those We carried with him, for you a reminder, a lesson and an admonition, and that you may remember it, Al-Qawwas read it on the authority of Ibn Kathir and Sulaym on the authority of Hamza, by stealing the ‘ayn, while the others read it by breaking it, meaning that you may memorize it, a listening ear, that is, a memorizer of what came from God. Qatada said: an ear that heard and understood what it heard. Al-Farra’ said: so that every ear may memorize it so that it may be a lesson and admonition for those who come after.
69:13: 13- Then when the trumpet is blown with a single blast, which is the first blast.
69:14: 14- And the earth and the mountains were borne away, lifted from their places, and were crushed, broken, crushed one by one, so they became scattered dust.
69:15: 15- On that day the event occurred, the Day of Resurrection took place.
69:16: 16- And the heaven will split, and on that Day it will be fragile. Weak. Al-Farra’ said: And it will split means it will crack.
69:17: 17- And the angels, meaning the angels, are on its edges, its sides and regions / as long as it has not yet split apart. The singular is rajā, shortened, and its dual is rajwān. Ad-Dahhak said: The angels will be on its edge until the Lord commands them to descend and surround the earth and everyone on it. And the Throne of your Lord will be borne above them, meaning above their heads, meaning the bearers. On that Day, the Day of Resurrection, eight, meaning eight angels. It was stated in the hadith: “Today they are four, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, God will support them with four more, so they will be eight in the form of mountain goats, and between their hooves and their knees is like the distance between one sky and another.” It was stated in the hadith: Each of them has the face of a man, the face of a lion, the face of a bull, and the face of an eagle. Abu Bakr ibn al-Haytham al-Turabi told us, Abu al-Fadl Muhammad Asad ibn al-Husayn al-Haddadi told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khalidi told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanthali told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Yahya ibn al-Ala’ told us, on the authority of his uncle Shu’ayb ibn Khalid, Samak ibn Harb told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umayrah, on the authority of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who said: “We were sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in al-Batha’ when a cloud passed by. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Do you know what this is?’ We said: ‘The clouds.’ He said: ‘And the rain clouds?’ We said: ‘And the rain clouds.’ He said: ‘And the reins?’ We remained silent. Then he said: ‘Do you know how far is the distance between the heaven and the earth?’ We said: ‘God and His Messenger know best.’ He said: ‘Between them is a journey of five hundred years, and between each heaven and the next is a journey of five hundred years. Likewise, the thickness of each heaven is five hundred years. Above the seventh heaven is a sea between its top and its bottom, as is the distance between the heaven and the earth. Then between that are eight mountain goats between their hooves and their knees, as is the distance between the heaven and the earth. Then above that is the Throne between Its bottom and its top are like the distance between the sky and the earth, and God Almighty is above that. Nothing of the deeds of the children of Adam is hidden from Him. This is narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Umaira, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf bin Qais, on the authority of Al-Abbas. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: “Above them on that Day will be eight,” meaning: eight rows of angels, and no one knows their number except God.
69:18: 18- On that Day you will be exposed to God, nothing will be hidden. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read: Nothing will be hidden from you, with a ya, while the others read it with a ta. “From you, hidden things,” meaning a hidden action. Al-Kalbi said: Nothing from you will be hidden from God. Abu Musa said: People will be exposed three times. As for the two exposures, they will be arguments and excuses, and as for the third exposure, then the scrolls will be scattered. Then I will take him with my right hand and I will take him with my left.
69:19: And that is what God Almighty said: 19- But as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, ‘Here, read my record.’ Come, read my record. The ha’ in my record is the ha’ of stopping.
69:20: 20- I thought, I knew and was certain, that I would meet my reckoning, meaning: I would be held accountable in the Hereafter.
69:21: 21- So he is in a life, a state of life, satisfied, pleasing, as in His saying: flowing water At-Tariq - 6, meaning: he is satisfied with it, by having received reward and been safe from punishment.
69:23: 23- Its fruits are within easy reach. Its fruits are close to those who eat them in all conditions. They can reach them standing, sitting, or lying down, cutting them however they want.
69:24: 24- Eat and drink at ease for what you have put forth, the righteous deeds you have put forth for your afterlife, in the days gone by, meaning the days of this world.
69:25: 25- But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, Ibn As-Sa’ib said: His left hand will be moved from his chest to behind his back, then he will be given his record. It was also said: His left hand will be taken from his chest to behind his back, then he will be given his record, and he will say, ‘Oh, I wish I had not been given my record,’ wishing that he had not been sent to account. Qatada said: He will wish for death, even though there is nothing in this world more hateful to him than death.
69:26: 26- And I did not know what my account was.
69:27: 27- Oh, would that it had been the final judgment, meaning: Oh, would that the death I died in this world had been the final judgment, void of everything after it, and the one that cut off life, so that I would not have lived after it. "The final judgment" means a death with no life after it. He wishes that he had never been resurrected for judgment. Qatada said: He wishes for death, even though there was nothing in this world more hateful to him than death.
69:28: 28- His wealth did not avail me anything, it did not protect me from the punishment of God.
69:29: 29- My authority was lost to me, my argument was lost to me, according to most commentators. Ibn Zayd said: My kingdom and my power were taken away from me. Muqatil said: It means when his limbs testified that he was polytheistic.
69:30: God says to the guards of your Hell: 30- Take him and bind him, tie his hands to his neck.
69:31: 31- Then throw him into Hell, meaning: throw him into Hell.
69:32: 32- Then by a chain seventy cubits long, lead him through it. So they put him through it. Ibn Abbas said: Seventy cubits by the king’s cubit, so it enters his anus and exits from his nostril. It was also said: It enters his mouth and exits from his anus. Nawf al-Bakali said: Seventy cubits, each cubit is seventy cubits, each cubit is further than what is between you and Mecca, and it was in the square of Kufa. Sufyan said: Each cubit is seventy cubits. Al-Hasan said: God knows best which cubit it is. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abu al-Samh, on the authority of Isa ibn Hilal al-Sadfi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-’As, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a piece of sand the size of this - and he pointed to the size of a skull - were sent from the sky to the earth, a distance of five hundred years, it would reach the earth before nightfall. And if it were sent from the top of the chain, it would reach the earth forty autumns, night and day, before it reaches its base or its bottom.” On the authority of Kaab, he said: If all the iron in the world were collected, it would not weigh a single ring.
69:33: 33- He did not believe in God Almighty.
69:34: 34- And he does not encourage the feeding of the poor, he does not feed the poor in this world nor does he order his family to do so.
69:35: He has no close friend here today, a relative who can benefit him and intercede for him.
69:36: 36- And no food except from the pus of the people of Hellfire, which is derived from the word ghusl, as if it were the washing machine for their wounds and ulcers. Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ said: It is a tree that the people of Hellfire eat.
69:37: 37- None shall eat it except the sinners, meaning: the unbelievers.
69:38: 38- I do not swear, there is no response to the polytheists’ words, as if he said: It is not as the polytheists say, I swear, by what you see.
69:39: 39- And what you do not see, meaning by what you see and by what you do not see. Qatada said: He swears by all things, so this includes all created things and existences. He also said: He swears by this world and the Hereafter. It was also said: What you see is what is on the face of the earth, and what you do not see is what is in its belly. It was also said: What you see is of bodies and what you do not see is of spirits. It was also said: What you see is mankind and what you do not see is the angels and the jinn. It was also said: apparent and hidden blessings. It was also said: What you see is what God revealed to the angels, the Tablet and the Pen, and what you do not see is what He has kept to Himself and not revealed to anyone.
69:40: 40- It, meaning the Qur’an, is the saying of a noble Messenger, meaning the recitation of a noble Messenger, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
69:41: 41- "It is not the word of a poet. Little do you believe.
69:42: 42- "Nor by the word of a soothsayer. Little do you remember." Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Ya'qub read: "they believe and they remember with the ya" in both. The others read it with the "ta, and by little" he meant to negate their belief altogether, like when you say to someone who does not visit you: "You rarely come to us." And you mean: "You do not come to us at all.
69:43: 43- "A revelation from the Lord of the Worlds."
69:44: 44- And if you say, he made up and invented, about us, Muhammad, some sayings, and he came up with something of his own.
69:45: 45- We would have seized him by the right hand. It was said that it is from a relative clause, meaning: We would have seized him and taken revenge on him by the right hand, meaning by right, like His statement: You used to come to us from the right (al-Saffat 37:28), meaning: by right. Ibn Abbas said: We would have seized him by force and power. Ash-Shamakh said about Arabah, the king of Yemen: If a banner is raised for glory, Araba will receive it with her right hand. That is, by force. He expressed force with the right hand, because the strength of everything is in its right hand. It was said: Its meaning is that we would take him by the right hand, and it is similar in meaning to: We would humiliate him and disgrace him, like the ruler who wants to belittle some of those he wants, he says to some of his aides: Take him by the hand and make him stand up.
69:46: 46- Then We would have severed his aorta. Ibn Abbas said: meaning the strings of the heart, and this is the opinion of most commentators. Mujahid said: it is the cord in the back. It was also said that it is a vein that runs in the back until it connects to the heart, and if it is severed, its owner dies.
69:47: 47- There is none of you who can prevent us from punishing him, preventing us from punishing him. The meaning is: Muhammad would not commit a lie for your sake, knowing that if he committed a lie, we would punish him, and no one would be able to avert our punishment from them. Rather, he said: preventing in the plural, which is a single verb, in response to its meaning, like his saying: We make no distinction between any of His messengers Al-Baqarah - 285.
69:48: 48- And it, meaning the Qur’an, is a reminder for the righteous, meaning an admonition for those who fear God’s punishment.
69:49: 49- And indeed, We know that among you are deniers.
69:50: 50- And it is a regret for the disbelievers. On the Day of Resurrection, they will regret abandoning faith in Him.
69:51: 51- And it is the certain truth, he added it to himself because of the difference in the two words.
69:52: 52- So glorify the name of your Lord, the Great.
70:1: 1- A questioner asked, the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read it as asal without a hamza, while others read it with a hamza. Whoever reads it with a hamza says that it is from asal, and whoever reads it without a hamza says that it is a dialect for asal, it is said: asal yassala like khafa yakhaf, meaning asal yassala, he lightened the hamza and made it an alif. It was said: It is from the torrent, and the torrent is a valley of the valleys of Hell. This was narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and the first is more correct. They differed regarding the preposition ba in His statement: with a punishment. It was said: It means about, like His statement: Then ask one who is well-informed about it (al-Furqan 25:59), meaning one who is well-informed about it. The meaning of the verse: A questioner asked about a punishment that is coming, that is destined to befall, upon whom it will descend and for whom that punishment will be.
70:2: So God said, explaining and answering that questioner: 2- For the disbelievers. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) frightened them with punishment, the people of Mecca said to one another: Who are the people of this punishment? And for whom is it? They asked Muhammad about it, so God revealed: A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall * the disbelievers. That is, it is for the disbelievers. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan and Qatadah. It was said that the ba is a connective and the meaning of the verse is: A supplicant prayed and a questioner asked for a punishment that will befall the disbelievers, that is, upon the disbelievers. The lam means upon, and he is Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith when he prayed against himself and asked for the punishment, so he said: O God, if this is the truth from You (al-Anfal 8:32). So what he asked for happened to him on the day of Badr, so he was killed patiently. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid: There is no repeller for him, that is, for the punishment, anyone who can prevent it.
70:3: 3- From God, the Possessor of the Ascending Stairways. Ibn Abbas said: That is, the Possessor of the heavens. He called them Ascending Stairways because the angels ascend through them. Saeed bin Jubair said: The Possessor of degrees. Qatada said: The Possessor of bounties and blessings, and Ascending Stairways means the angels.
70:4: 3- The angels ascend, Al-Kisa’i read it with a ya’, which is the reading of Ibn Mas’ud, and the others read it with a ta’, and the spirit, meaning Gabriel, peace be upon him, to him, meaning to God Almighty, in a day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, of the years of this world if someone other than the angel had ascended, and that is because it ascends from the end of God Almighty’s command from the bottom of the seventh earth to the end of God Almighty’s command from above the seventh heaven. Layth narrated on the authority of Mujahid that the duration of this is fifty thousand years. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: If the children of Adam were to walk from this world to the place of the throne, they would walk for fifty thousand years of the years of this world. Ikrimah and Qatadah said: It is the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan also said: It is the Day of Resurrection. He meant that they will stand for the reckoning until fifty thousand worldly years have separated people.
