He did not mean this length of time to the exclusion of others, because the Day of Resurrection has a beginning and no end, because it is an extended day. If it had an end, it would have been cut off. Ibn Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is the Day of Resurrection, which will be for the unbelievers for a period of fifty thousand years. Abu al-Faraj al-Muzaffar ibn Ismail al-Tamimi told us, Abu al-Qasim Hamza ibn Yusuf al-Sahmi told us, Abu Ahmad Abdullah ibn Adi al-Hafiz told us, Abdullah ibn Saeed told us, Asad ibn Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Darij Abu al-Samh, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, who said: “It was said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about a day the length of which was fifty thousand years: ‘How long is this day?’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul, it is made easy for the believer to the point that it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer that he prays in this world.’” It was said: Its meaning is that if someone other than God were in charge of holding the servants to account on that Day, it would not take fifty thousand years to complete it. This is the meaning of what Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Muqatil. Ata’ said: God would complete it in the space of half a day of the days of this world. Muhammad bin Al-Fadl narrated on the authority of Al-Kalbi, who said: He says: If I were to assign the angels, jinn, and humankind to account for that day and I were to entrust them with their accounting, they would not finish it until after fifty thousand years, and I will finish it in one hour of the day. Yaman said: It is the Day of Resurrection, in which there are fifty periods, each period lasting a thousand years. And there is an advancing and delaying in it, as if he said: There is nothing to prevent it from God, the Lord of the Ascending Paths, on a Day the length of which is fifty thousand years, the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him.
70:5: 5- So be patient with a beautiful patience, O Muhammad, regarding their denial, and this was before he was ordered to fight.
70:6: 6- They see it far away, meaning the torment.
70:7: 7- And we see it near, because what is coming is near.
70:8: 8- The Day the sky will be like molten copper, like cloudy oil. Al-Hasan said: Like silver when it is melted.
70:9: 9- And the mountains will be like wool," like dyed wool. "Own" is only used for dyed wool. Muqatil said: Like carded wool. Al-Hasan said: Like red wool, which is the weakest wool. The first thing the mountains change is that they become scattered sand, then carded wool, then scattered dust.
70:10: 22- And no intimate friend will ask a intimate friend. Al-Bazzi read on the authority of Ibn Kathir no intimate friend will ask about a intimate friend, meaning: no intimate friend will be asked about a intimate friend, meaning he will not be asked: Who is your intimate friend? The others read it with a fatha on the ya’, meaning: no relative will ask a relative because he is busy with his own affairs.
70:11: 12- They will see them, they will see them, and there will be no creature on the Day of Resurrection except that it will be in the sight of its companion from among the jinn and mankind. So a man will see his father, his brother, and his relatives, but he will not ask him, and he will see his intimate friend, but he will not speak to him because he is preoccupied with himself. Ibn Abbas said: They get to know each other for an hour of the day, then they do not get to know each other after that. It was said: They see them means they know them, meaning: the intimate knows his intimate friend until he knows him, and despite that he does not ask him about his affair because he is busy with himself. Al-Suddi said: They will recognize the believer by the whiteness of his face, and the disbeliever by the blackness of his face. The criminal will wish, the polytheist says, that he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his children.
70:12: 12- And his companion, his wife, and his brother.
70:13: 13- And his faction, his clan from which he was separated. Mujahid said: his tribe. Another said: his closest relatives, which shelters him, meaning that which embraces him and to which he takes refuge.
70:14: 14- And everyone on earth, then He will save him. That is the ransom from the punishment of your Lord.
70:15: 15- "No!" Nothing will save him from God's punishment. Then He began by saying, "Indeed, it is a blazing Fire." This is one of the names of Hell. It was said that it is the second level, and it was named thus because it is blazing, that is, it is in flames.
70:16: 16- Naz'a'tan li-shuwa, Hafs read on the authority of Asim Naz'a'tan in the accusative case as a state and separation, while the others read it in the nominative case, meaning it is Naz'aat li-shuwa, which refers to the extremities: the hands, the feet, and all other extremities. Mujahid said: for the skin of the head. Ibrahim bin Muhajir narrated on his authority: it removes the flesh but not the bones. Muqatil said: Fire strips away limbs, leaving neither flesh nor skin. Ad-Dahhak said: It removes the skin and meat from the bone. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The nerve and the heel. Al-Kalbi said: The mother of the head eats the whole brain, then it returns to how it was, then it returns to eating it again, and that is its habit. Qatada said: For the goodness of his character and his limbs. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: For the beauty of his face. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Shawa means the human limbs as long as they are not fatal. It is said: He shot and caused a wound if he hit the extremities but did not hit the fatal point.
70:17: 17- It calls, that is, the Fire to itself, whoever turns away from faith, and turns away from the truth, then it says, To me, O polytheist, to me, O hypocrite, to me. Ibn Abbas said: It calls the unbelievers and the hypocrites by their names in an eloquent tongue, then it picks them up as a bird picks up grain. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Khalil that he said: It calls, that is, it torments. He said: A Bedouin said to another: May God have called you, that is, may God torment you.
70:18: 18- And he collected, meaning: he collected the money, and stored it, he kept it in the container and did not fulfill God’s right from it.
70:19: 19- Indeed, mankind was created impatient. Al-Suddi narrated on the authority of Abi Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Al-Halu’ is the one who is greedy for what is not permissible for him. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Stingy. Ikrimah said: Impatient. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Hasan said: Stingy. Qatadah said: Impatient. Muqatil said: Narrow-hearted. “Hal’ is intense greed and lack of patience.” Atiyyah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Its interpretation is what follows.
70:20: And he said: 20- If evil touches him, he becomes impatient.
70:21: 21- And if good befalls him, withholding it, meaning: if poverty befalls him, he does not have patience, and if money befalls him, he does not spend it. Ibn Kaysan said: God created man to love what pleases him and flee from what he dislikes, then He made him worship Him by spending what he loves and being patient with what he dislikes.
70:22: Then he made an exception and said: 22- Except for those who pray. He made an exception for the plural from the singular because man is in the meaning of the plural, as in his saying: Indeed, man is in loss * Except for those who believe.
70:23: 23- Those who are constant in their prayers, they perform them at their appointed times, meaning the obligatory prayers. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tuba told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me that Abu al-Khair told him: We asked Uqbah ibn Amir about the statement of God, the Most High: Those who are constant in their prayers, are they those who pray forever? He said: No, but when he prays, he does not look to his right, his left, or behind him.
70:24: 24- And those in whose wealth there is a recognized right.
70:25: 25- For the needy and the deprived.
70:26: 26- And those who believe in the Day of Judgment.
70:27: 27- And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord.
70:28: 28- Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not safe.
70:29: 29- And those who guard their private parts.
70:30: 30- Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed.
70:31: 31- But whoever seeks beyond that - then it is those who are the transgressors.
70:32: 32- And those who are to their trusts and their covenants attentive.
70:33: 33- And those who uphold their testimonies, Hafs read on the authority of Asim and Yaqub: upholding their testimonies in the plural, and the others read upholding their testimony in the monotheism, meaning they uphold the truth in it or do not conceal it or change it.
70:34: 34- And those who maintain their prayers.
70:35: 35- Those will be in honored gardens.
70:36: 36- So what is the matter with those who disbelieved? That is: What is the matter with those who disbelieved, as in His saying: So why do they turn away from the reminder? Al-Muddaththir - 49, heading towards you in haste, rushing towards you, stretching out their necks and constantly looking at you, looking in your direction. It was revealed about a group of infidels who were gathering around the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, listening to his words, mocking him, and belying him. God Almighty said: What is the matter with them that they look at you and sit with you while they do not benefit from what they hear?
70:37: 37- On the right and on the left, in groups, in circles and in groups. Azin means groups in a group, the singular of which is Azza.
70:38: 38- Does every man among them aspire to enter the Garden of Delight? Ibn Abbas said: Its meaning is: Does every man among them aspire to enter My Garden as the Muslims enter it and enjoy it, while he has lied about My Prophet?
70:39: 39- “No,” they will not enter it. Then He began by saying: Indeed, We created them from that which they know, meaning: from a sperm-drop, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh. He alerted people to the fact that they were created from a single origin and that they differ in their qualities and deserve Paradise through faith and obedience. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjuwayh told us, Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali told us, Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Faryabi told us, Safwan ibn Salih told us, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, Jarir ibn Uthman al-Rahbi told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nafe’r, on the authority of Busr ibn Jahash al-Qurashi, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day, and he spat into his hand and placed his finger on it, and said: God Almighty says: Son of Adam, how can you be unable to help Me when I created you from something like this, until I proportioned you and made you equal, and you walked between two cold places, and the earth was slow to yield to you, so it gathered and withheld, until it reached the collarbones and I said, ‘I will give charity,’ but when is the time for charity?” It was said: Its meaning is that we created them for what they do, which is command and prohibition, reward and punishment. It was said: What means whom. Its meaning is: We created them from among those who know and reason, not like animals.
70:40: 40- So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests, meaning the East and West of every day of the year, Indeed, We are Able.
70:41: 41- That We may replace them with better ones, that We may create better ones than them and more obedient to God and His Messenger, and We will not be outdone.
70:42: 42- So leave them to plunge into their falsehood and play in their worldly life until they meet the Day they are promised. This was abrogated by the verse on fighting.
70:44: 44- Humbled, submissive and submissive, their eyes will be overwhelmed with humiliation, disgrace will overwhelm them, that is the Day they were promised, meaning the Day of Resurrection.
71:1: 1- Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], ‘Warn your people,’ meaning: warn your people, before a painful punishment comes to them. The meaning is: We sent him to warn them of the punishment if they did not believe.
71:2: 2- “He said, ‘O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner.’ I warn you and explain to you the message of God in a language you know.
71:3: 3- Worship God, fear Him, and obey Him.
71:4: 4- He will forgive you some of your sins. “Some” is a conjunction, meaning: He will forgive you your sins. It was also said that it means your past sins up until the time of belief, and that was some of their sins. And He will delay you for a specified term. That is, He will heal you until the end of your appointed terms, and He will not punish you. Indeed, when the term of God comes, it cannot be delayed, if you only knew. He says: Believe before death, and you will be saved from the punishment, for when the term of death comes, it cannot be delayed, and you will not be able to believe.
71:5: 5- He said, ‘My Lord, I have called my people night and day.’
71:6: 6- My supplication only increased their flight, their aversion and turning away from faith and truth.
71:7: 7- And whenever I called them to believe in You, that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears so that they would not hear My call, and covered their faces with their garments so that they would not see Me, and persisted in their disbelief, and were arrogant about believing in You, with arrogance.
71:8: 8- Then I called them aloud, declaring the supplication. Ibn Abbas said: In a loud voice.
71:9: 9- Then I declared to them, I repeated the supplication, declaring, and I whispered to them secretly, Ibn Abbas said: He means man after man, I spoke to him secretly between me and him, I called him to Your worship and to Your Oneness.
71:10: 10- "So I said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving.'"
71:11: 11- He will send down abundant rain upon you. This is because when the people of Noah denied him for a long time, God withheld rain from them and made the wombs of their women barren for forty years, so their wealth and livestock were destroyed. So Noah said to them: Seek forgiveness from your Lord for polytheism, meaning seek forgiveness through monotheism, and He will send down abundant rain upon you. Mutraf narrated on the authority of Al-Sha'bi that Umar, may God be pleased with him, went out to seek rain with the people, but he did not say anything more than I seek forgiveness until he returned. It was said to him: We did not hear you ask for rain. He said: I asked for rain with the angels of the sky by which rain is brought down. Then he recited: "Seek forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers."
71:12: 12- And He will provide you with wealth and children. Ata’ said: He will increase your wealth and children, and provide for you gardens and provide for you rivers.
71:13: 13- Why do you not have reverence for God? Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: You do not see God’s greatness. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Why do you not glorify God as He should be glorified? Al-Kalbi said: You do not fear God as He should be glorified. Raja means fear, and dignity means greatness, a noun from taqweer, which means glorification. Al-Hassan said: You do not know God’s right, nor do you thank Him for His blessings. Ibn Kaysan said: Why do you not hope that God will reward you for your reverence for Him with goodness in your worship?
71:14: 14- And He has created you in stages, sometimes, one state after another, a drop of semen, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, until creation is complete.
71:15: 15- Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers?
71:16: 16- And He made the moon a light therein. Al-Hasan said: He means in the lowest heaven, just as one says: I came to Banu Tamim, but I only came to some of them, and so-and-so is hidden in the homes of Banu so-and-so, but he is in one home. Abdullah ibn Amr said: The faces of the sun and the moon are toward the heavens, and the light of the sun and the light of the moon are within them, and their backs are toward the earth. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And He made the sun a lamp, a shining lamp.
71:17: 17- And God caused you to grow from the earth as a plant, meaning the beginning of Adam’s creation, He created him from the earth, and people are his offspring, and His saying: a plant is a noun that was placed in the place of the source, meaning a growth. Al-Khalil said: Its metaphor is: He caused you to grow, so you grew as a plant.
71:18: 18- Then He will return you to it, after death, and bring you out, from it on the Day of Resurrection, alive, bringing out.
71:19: 19- And God has made the earth a carpet for you, He spread it out and extended it for you.
71:20: 20- So that you may take therefrom wide paths, wide roads.
71:21: 21- Noah said, ‘My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me,’ they did not answer my call, ‘and followed one whose wealth and children only increase him in loss,’ meaning: the lowly and the poor followed the leaders and chiefs whose abundance of wealth and children only increased them in misguidance in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.
71:22: 22- “And they plotted a great plot,” meaning a great and immense one. It is said: great and great, with the first letter pronounced with a light emphasis, and great with the second letter pronounced with a heavy emphasis, all of which have the same meaning, just as it is said: a strange matter, “wonderful,” and wonderful, with the second letter pronounced with a heavy emphasis, which is more exaggerated. They differed over the meaning of their plot. Ibn Abbas said: They said a terrible thing. Ad-Dahhak said: They fabricated lies against God and belied His messengers. It was also said: The leaders prevented their followers from believing in Noah and incited them to kill him.
71:23: 23- And they said, to them: Do not abandon your gods, meaning do not stop worshipping them, and do not abandon Wadd, the people of Medina read it with a damma on the waw, and the rest read it with a fatha, nor Suwa’ nor Yaghuth nor Ya’uq nor Nasr, these are the names of their gods. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: These are the names of righteous people who were between Adam and Noah. When they died, they had followers who emulated them and took after them in worship. Then Satan came to them and said to them: If you made pictures of them, it would be more energizing for you and make you more eager to worship. So they did. Then a people arose after them and Satan said to them: Those who were before you worshipped them, so worship them. So the beginning of idol worship was from that. These pictures were given these names because they were made in the image of those Muslims. Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, and Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The idols that were worshipped by the people of Noah were worshipped by the Arabs after him. As for Wadd, it was for Kalb in Dumat Al-Jandal, and as for Suwa’, it was for Hudhayl, and as for Yaghuth, it was for Murad and then for Banu Ghatif in Al-Jurf near Saba’, and as for Ya’uq, it was for Himyar, for the family of Dhi Al-Kila’. He mentioned it in his interpretation. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Musa on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais, regarding the words of God Almighty: And do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa’, nor Yaghuth, nor Ya’uq, nor Nasr. He said: These were the names of righteous men from the people of Noah. When they perished, Satan inspired their people to erect idols in the places where they used to sit and name them after them. They did so, but they were not worshipped. Then, when those people perished and knowledge was abolished, they were worshipped. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Those idols were buried by the flood and covered with dirt, and they remained buried until Satan brought them out for the polytheists of the Arabs. The Arabs had other idols, so Al-Lat belonged to Thaqif, Al-Uzza belonged to Sulaym, Ghatafan and Jashm, Manat belonged to Qudayd, and Isaf, Na’ila and Hubal belonged to the people of Mecca.
71:24: 24- And they have led many astray, meaning: many people have been led astray because of idols, as God Almighty says: My Lord, indeed they have led many people astray (Ibrahim 14:36). Muqatil said: Their leaders have led many people astray, And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error, this is a supplication against them after God informed Noah that they would not believe, which is His saying: None of your people will believe except he who has already believed (Hud 11:36).
71:25: 25- Of their sins, meaning: of their sins, and what is the connection, and Abu Amr read: their sins and both are the plural of sin, they were drowned, by the flood, so they were put into a fire, Ad-Dahhak said: It is in one state in this world, they are drowned on one side and burned on the other side, and Muqatil said: so they were put into a fire in the hereafter, and they found for themselves not besides God supporters, they did not find anyone to prevent them from God’s punishment.
71:26: 26- And Noah said, ‘My Lord, do not leave upon the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers.’ Someone who wanders around the earth, going and coming, its origin is from the word ‘dawwar’. Ibn Qutaybah said: Its origin is from ‘dar’, meaning: someone who resides in a house.
71:27: 27- If you leave them, they will mislead Your servants. Ibn Abbas, Al-Kalbi, and Muqatil said: A man would go with his son to Noah and say: Beware of this one, for he is a liar. My father warned me about him. The older one would die and the younger one would grow up like him. And they will not give birth to anyone but wicked disbelievers. Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Muqatil, Al-Rabi', and others said: Noah only said this when God brought forth every believer from their loins and the wombs of their women, and made the wombs of their women barren and the loins of their men dry up forty years before the punishment. It was said seventy years, and God informed Noah that they would not believe and would not give birth to a believer. Then Noah prayed against them, and God answered his prayer and destroyed them all. There was no child among them at the time of the punishment, because God the Most High said: And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them. (al-Furqan 25:37). And there was no denial from children.
71:28: 28- My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and his father’s name was Lamech son of Methuselah, and his mother’s name was Simha bint Enosh, and they were believers. It was also said that her name was Hegel bint Lamech son of Methuselah, so she was his cousin. And whoever enters my house, my home, as a believer, and Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi said: My mosque. It was also said: My ship. And for the believing men and believing women, this is general for everyone who believed in God and believed the messengers. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction, destruction and devastation. So God answered his prayer and destroyed them.
72:1: 1- Say, ‘It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened,’ and they were nine jinn from Nasibin. It was also said that they were seven. They listened to the recitation of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. We mentioned their story in Surat Al-Ahqaf. And they said, when they returned to their people, Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur’an. Ibn Abbas said: Eloquent, meaning: an amazing Qur’an that is admired for its eloquence.
72:2: 2- Guides to the right path, calls to the correct path of monotheism and faith, So we have believed in it and will not associate anyone with our Lord.
72:3: 3- And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord. The people of Ash-Sham and Kufa, except for Abu Bakr, read on the authority of Asim: And that He, the Most High, with the opening of the hamza, and so is what follows it until His saying: And we are Muslims from among us. The others read it with the opening of them, and Abu Ja`far opened it with and that He, which is what was referred back to the revelation, and the breaking of what was a narration from the jinn. The choice is to break the whole because it is from the saying of the jinn to their people, so it is connected to his saying: And they said, ‘Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur’an,’ and they said: And that He, the Most High, is. And whoever opens his response to his saying: So we believed in him and we believed in all of that, then he opens that the belief occurred upon him. Our Lord is great, the majesty and greatness of our Lord, as stated by Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Qatadah. It is said that a man is great, meaning he is noble. This is based on the saying of Anas: When a man would recite Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat Al-Imran, he would be noble among us, meaning his status would be great. Al-Suddi said: Our Lord’s grandfather means our Lord’s command. Al-Hasan said: Our Lord’s wealth. From this, grandfather is called fortune, and a rich man. Ibn Abbas said: The power of our Lord. Ad-Dahhak said: His action. Al-Qurazi said: His blessings and favors upon His creation. Al-Akhfash said: “Our Lord’s kingdom is exalted. He has not taken a wife or a son.” It was said: He, glory and majesty be to Him, is too exalted to take a wife or a son.
72:4: 4- And that our foolish one used to say, our ignorant one, Mujahid and Qatadah said: he is Iblis, against God an outrage, lying and aggression, which is describing Him as a partner and a son.
72:5: 5- And we thought, it was enough for us, that mankind and the jinn would not say a lie against God, Jacob read say with the opening and emphasis on the waw, that God has a wife and a son, meaning: We thought they were truthful in their saying that God has a wife and a son until we heard the Qur’an.
72:6: God Almighty said 6- And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn. That is because when a man from the Arabs in the pre-Islamic era traveled and spent the evening in a deserted land, he would say: I seek refuge with the master of this valley from the evil of the fools of his people. So he would spend the night in safety and protection from them until morning. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjuwayh told us, Abdullah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik told us, Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Marwazi told us, Musa ibn Sa’id ibn al-Nu’man in Tarsus told us, Furwah ibn Abi al-Mughra’ al-Kindi told us, al-Qasim ibn Malik told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Kurdam ibn Abi Sa’ib al-Ansari, who said: I went out with my father to Medina on an errand, and that was the first time the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was mentioned in Mecca. The house sheltered us with a shepherd, and when it was midday, a wolf came and took a lamb from the sheep. The shepherd jumped up and said: O ‘Amir, the valley is your neighbor. Then a crier that we could not see called out, saying: O Sarhan, let him go. The lamb came running until it entered the sheep without any injury. Then God Almighty revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca: And there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn. So they increased their burden, meaning that the humans increased the burden on the jinn by seeking refuge with their leaders. Ibn Abbas said: Sin. Mujahid said: Transgression. Muqatil said: Deviation. Al-Hasan said: Evil. Ibrahim said: Greatness. This is because they would increase in their transgression with this seeking of refuge, saying: We have become the masters of the jinn and mankind. In Arabic, rahq means sin and committing incest.
72:7: 7- And that they thought, God Almighty says: The jinn thought, as you thought, O group of disbelieving humans, that God would not resurrect anyone, after his death.
72:8: 8- And we, the jinn say, touched the sky, Al-Kalbi said: the lowest sky, and found it filled with stern guards, of angels, and shooting stars, of stars.
72:9: 9- And we used to sit therein, from the sky, in seats to listen, meaning: we used to listen, so whoever listens now will find a shooting star lying in wait for him, lying in wait for him to be shot at. Ibn Qutaybah said: Stoning was practiced before the mission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but it was not as strict as it was after his mission in terms of the severity of the guarding. They would eavesdrop on people in some cases, but when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, they prohibited that altogether.
72:10: Then they said: 10- And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth, by throwing meteors, or whether their Lord intends for them a right course.
72:11: 11- And among us are the righteous and among us are less than that, less than the righteous, We were divided into different ways, meaning: scattered groups and different types. And quddah is a piece of something. It is said: the people became quddah if their conditions differed, and its origin is from qad which means to cut. Mujahid said: They mean: Muslims and disbelievers. It was said: They have different desires. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: The jinn are like you, and among them are the Qadariyyah, the Murji’ah, and the Rafidah. Ibn Kaysan said: Sects and factions, each faction has its own desires, like the desires of the people. Saeed bin Jubair said: Various colors. Abu Ubaidah said: Types.
72:12: 12- And we thought, we knew and were certain, that we would not be able to frustrate God on earth, meaning: we would not escape Him if He wanted something from us, and we would not be able to escape from Him, if we sought.
72:13: 13- And when we heard the guidance, the Qur’an and what Muhammad brought, “we believed in it. So whoever believes in his Lord will not fear loss,” a decrease in his work and reward, nor oppression, injustice. It was said: an unpleasant thing that befalls him.
72:14: 14- And among us are the Muslims, meaning those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among us are the Qāṣitūn, meaning those who are unjust and deviate from the truth. Ibn Abbas said: They are those who set up rivals for God. It is said: A man is ‘aqṣat’ if he is just, so he is ‘muqsit’, and ‘qaṣat’ if he is unjust, so he is ‘qaṣit’. And those who submit - those have sought the right path, meaning: they have sought the path of truth and strived for it.
72:15: 15- As for the unjust ones, who disbelieved, they will be fuel for Hellfire, they will be the fuel of Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection.
72:16: Then he returned to the infidels of Mecca and said: 16- And if they had remained steadfast upon the Way, they differed in its interpretation. Some people said: If they had remained steadfast upon the way of truth, faith, and guidance, and were believers and obedient, We would have given them abundant water, abundantly. Muqatil said: This was after the rain had been withheld from them for seven years. They said that its meaning was, If they had believed, We would have provided them with plenty in this world and given them abundant wealth and a comfortable life. Abundant water was used as an example because all goodness and provision are in the rain, as He said: And if only they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them (al-Ma’idah 5:66). He also said: And if only the people of the towns had believed and feared God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the sky (al-A’raf 7:96).
72:17: And the Almighty said: 17- That We may test them therein, meaning: To test their gratitude for what they were given. This is the opinion of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Muqatil, and al-Hasan. Others said: Its meaning is that if they had remained steadfast in the path of disbelief and misguidance, We would have given them abundant wealth and provided them with plenty to test them with it, as a punishment for them and a lure until they are tempted by it, so that We may punish them. This is the saying of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Kalbi, and Ibn Kaysan, as God said: But when they forgot that by which they had been reminded, We opened to them the gates of every [good] thing (al-An’am 6:44). And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord - He will cause him to plunge into a torment ascending. The people of Kufa and Ya’qub read yasliquhu with a ya’, while the others read it with a noon, meaning: We will cause him to enter. A severe punishment. Ibn Abbas said: Difficult. The meaning of ascending is: difficult. Qatada said: There is no rest in it. Muqatil said: There is no joy in it. Al-Hasan said: It only increases in severity. The basic principle is that climbing is difficult for people.
72:18: 18- And that the mosques are for God, meaning the places that were built for prayer and remembrance of God, so do not invoke anyone with God, Qatada said: When the Jews and Christians entered their churches and synagogues, they associated partners with God, so God commanded the believers to sincerely call to God when they entered the mosques, and he meant by that all the mosques. Al-Hasan said: He meant all of the places because the whole earth was made a mosque for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Saeed bin Jubair said: The jinn said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: How can we come to the mosque and witness the prayer with you when we are far away? Then this verse was revealed: And that the mosques belong to God. It was also narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that what is meant by places of prostration are the limbs on which a person prostrates, and they are seven: the forehead, the hands, the knees, and the feet. He said: These limbs on which prostration occurs were created by God, so do not prostrate on them to anyone other than Him. Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Abbas Al-Hamidi told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ya’qub told us, Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Hilali and Al-Sari bin Khuzaymah told us: Ya’la bin Asad told us, Wahib told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was commanded to prostrate on seven parts of the body: the forehead - and he pointed to it with his hand - the hands, the knees, and the tips of the feet, and not to cover my garment or my hair.” If you make mosques places for prayer, then the singular is masjid, with a kasra on the jim, and if you make them parts, then the singular is masjid, with a fatha on the jim.
72:19: 19- And when Abdullah stood up, Nafi’ and Abu Bakr read it with a kasra over the hamza, while the others read it with a fatha over it, when Abdullah stood up, meaning the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, called upon Him, meaning worshipped Him and recited the Qur’an, that was when he was praying in Batn Nakhl and reciting the Qur’an, they almost, meaning the jinn, were all about to crowd around him, meaning they were riding on top of each other, and they were crowding together out of eagerness to listen to the Qur’an. This is the statement of Ad-Dahhak and the narration of Atiyyah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Saeed bin Jubair said about him: This is from the words of the group of jinn who returned to their people and told them what they saw of the obedience of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their following his example in prayer. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd said: This means that when Abdullah began to call people to Islam, mankind and jinn gathered together and conspired against him to invalidate the truth that he had brought them and to extinguish the light of God. But God refused except to complete His light, accomplish this matter, and grant him victory over those who opposed him. Hisham read on the authority of Ibn Amir: labdan with a damma on the lam. The root of labd is groups of people, one on top of the other. From this, the word labd is named after what is spread out because of its accumulation. And hair becomes piled up.
72:20: 20- Say, ‘I only call upon my Lord,’ Abu Ja`far, Asim, and Hamza read: Say as a command, and the others read: He said, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I only call upon my Lord,’ Muqatil said: That is because the infidels of Mecca said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have come with a great matter, so turn back from it and we will protect you. He said to them: I only call upon my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with Him.
72:21: 21- Say, ‘I do not possess for you any harm,’ I am not able to ward off any harm from you, nor any guidance, meaning I do not bring you any guidance, meaning good, meaning that God possesses it.
72:22: 22- Say, ‘None can protect me from God,’ “None can protect me from anyone if I disobey Him, and I will not find besides Him any refuge, “any shelter to which I can turn.” The meaning of al-Multahid is: the inclined. Al-Suddi said: a protection. Al-Kalbi said: an entrance into the earth like a tunnel.
72:23: 23- "Except for conveying from God and His messages," for in it is protection, security, and salvation, as Al-Hasan said. Muqatil said: That is what protects me from the punishment of God, meaning conveying the message. Qatada said: Except for conveying from God, for that is what I possess with the help and guidance of God. And it was said: I do not possess for you harm or guidance, but I convey a message from God, for I am only a messenger and I possess nothing but what I possess. "And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger, and does not believe, then for him is the fire of Hell, wherein he will abide eternally.
72:24: 24- Until when they see what they are promised, meaning the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, they will know, when the punishment descends, who is weaker in helpers and fewer in number, whether they or the believers.
72:25: 25- “Say, ‘I do not know,’ meaning I do not know, ‘whether that which you are promised is near,’ meaning the punishment, and it has been said that it is the Resurrection, ‘or whether my Lord will set for it a term,’ meaning a long-term end, meaning that knowledge of the time of the punishment is unseen and only God knows it.
72:26: 26- The Knower of the Unseen, is raised as an attribute of His saying My Lord, and it was said: He is the Knower of the Unseen, so He does not reveal, He does not inform, about His Unseen to anyone.
72:27: 27- Except for a messenger whom He has chosen, except for the one He chooses for His message, and He reveals to him what He wills of the unseen, because his prophethood is proven by the miraculous sign of him informing about the unseen, for He will make a guard precede him and behind him, mentioning some directions indicates that all of them are guarded, meaning: He will make guardians from the angels precede him and behind him, who will protect him from the devils eavesdropping, and from the jinn listening to the revelation and then submitting to the priests. Muqatil and others said: Whenever God sent a messenger, Satan would come to him in the form of an angel to inform him. Then God would send angels in front of him and behind him to guard him and drive away the devils. When a devil came to him in the form of an angel, they would tell him that he was a devil, and when an angel came to him, they would say to him: This is the messenger of your Lord.
72:28: 28- So that He may know, Ya’qub read: So that He may know with a damma on the ya’, meaning so that people may know, that the messengers have conveyed, and the others read it with a fatha on the ya’, meaning: So that the Messenger may know that the angels have conveyed, the messages of their Lord and He encompasses what is with them, meaning: God knows what is with the messengers, so nothing is hidden from Him, and He has counted everything in number, Ibn Abbas said: He has counted what He created and known the number of what He created, so nothing has escaped His knowledge, not even the weight of an atom or a mustard seed. He put count in the accusative case as a state, or if you like, as a verbal noun, meaning He counted a count.
73:1: 1- O you who is wrapped in your garment, meaning the one wrapped in his garment. Its original form is al-mutazammil, the ta' was assimilated into the zay, and the same is true of al-mudathir, meaning the one wrapped in his garment, the ta' was assimilated into the dal. It is said: tazammal and tadathir bi-thawbih, meaning he covered himself with it. Al-Suddi said: He meant, O sleeper, get up and pray. Scholars said: This address was to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the beginning of the revelation before the message was delivered, and then he was addressed later as the Prophet and Messenger.
73:2: 2- Perform the night prayer, meaning for prayer, except for a little, and performing the night prayer was an obligation in the beginning.
73:3: And he explained his value and said: 3- Half of it or less than a little, up to a third.
73:4: 4- Or add to it, from half to two-thirds, he was given the choice between these stages, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions used to stand up according to these amounts, and a man would not know when it was one-third of the night, when it was half of the night, and when it was two-thirds, so a man would stand up until morning for fear that he would not memorize the required amount, and this was so severe for them that their feet would swell, so God Almighty had mercy on them and made it easier for them and abrogated it by saying: "So recite as much of the Qur'an as is easy for you. He knows that there will be among you ill" [the verse]. So there was a year between the beginning of the surah and its end. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Na’im Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Isfarayini told us, Abu ‘Awana Ya’qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz told us, al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn ‘Affan told us, Yahya ibn Bashir told us, Sa’id - meaning Ibn Abi ‘Aruba - told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Zurarah ibn Abi Awfa, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Hisham, who said: “I went to Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and said: O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: Do you not recite the Qur’an? I said: Yes. She said: The character of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the Qur’an. I said: And the standing of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, O Mother of the Believers? She said: Do you not recite ‘O you wrapped in a cloak’? I said: Yes. She said: God made standing obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions stood for a year until their feet swelled, and God held back its conclusion for twelve months in the heavens, then God revealed the alleviation at the end of this surah, so the night standing became voluntary.” After the obligatory prayer. Muqatil bin Kaysan said: This was in Mecca before the five daily prayers were made obligatory, then it was abrogated by the five daily prayers. And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation. Ibn Abbas said: Clearly recite it. Al-Hasan said: Recite it clearly. Mujahid said: Recite it slowly. Qatada said: Stand firm in it. Ibn Abbas also said: Recite it at your own pace, three verses, four, or five. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Amr bin Asim told us, Hammam told us on the authority of Qatada who said: “Anas was asked how the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite, so he said: It was extended, extended. Then he recited: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, extending ‘In the name of God’, extending ‘The Most Gracious’ and extending ‘The Most Merciful’.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, Amr bin Murrah told us: I heard Abu Wa’il say: “A man came to Ibn Mas’ud and said: I recited Al-Mufassal last night in one rak’ah. He said: Is this like this poetry? I know the pairs that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pair together. So he mentioned twenty surahs from Al-Mufassal, two surahs from Al Ha Mim in each rak’ah.” Abu Ja`far Ahmad ibn Abi Ahmad ibn Mathwaih told us, Ash-Sharif Abu Al-Qasim Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Husayn Al-Harrani told us in what he wrote to me, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn Al-Ajurri told us, Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Hamid Al-Wasiti told us, Zayd ibn Akhzam told us, Muhammad ibn Al-Fadl told us, Sa`id ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah - meaning Ibn Mas`ud - who said: Do not scatter it like scattering dates, nor recite it like poetry. Stop at its wonders and move hearts with it, and let none of you be concerned with the end of the surah. Abu Ja`far Ahmad ibn Abi Ahmad ibn Mathwaih told us, Ash-Sharif Abu al-Qasim `Ali ibn Muhammad ibn `Ali al-Husayn al-Harrani told us in what he wrote to me, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Ajurri told us, Abu Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa`id told us, al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazin told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, H, Abu Muhammad ibn Ya`qub al-Kisa`i told us, `Abdullah ibn Muhammad told us, Ibrahim ibn `Abdullah al-Khalal told us, `Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Musa ibn `Ubaydah, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Ubaydah, who was his brother, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d al-Sa`idi, who said: “While we were reciting, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out and said: ‘Praise be to God. The Book of God is one. Among you are the good, among you are the red and the black. Recite the Qur’an before there come a people who recite it, setting up its letters as an arrow is set up, but it does not go beyond their collarbones. They hasten its end and do not postpone it.” Abu Uthman al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad al-Jarrahi told us, Abu al-Abbas al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Nafi’ al-Basri told us, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Muslim al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up one night to recite a verse from the Qur’an.” Narrated by Abu Dharr, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up one night until morning reciting a verse from the Qur’an, and the verse is: If You punish them, they are Your servants; but if You forgive them, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise (al-Ma’idah 5:118).
73:5: 5- Indeed, We will cast upon you a weighty word. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Severe. Al-Hasan said: A man may recite the surah, but acting upon it is heavy. Qatada said: God’s obligations and limits are heavy. Muqatil said: It is heavy because of what it contains of commands, prohibitions, and limits. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It is heavy with promises and threats, and what is lawful and what is unlawful. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: It is heavy on the hypocrites. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: A word that is light on the tongue, but heavy on the scale. Al-Farra’ said: It is heavy, not light, because it is the speech of our Lord. Ibn Zayd said: By God, it is heavy and blessed. Just as it was heavy in this world, it will be heavy on the scales on the Day of Resurrection. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, how does the revelation come to you? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and that is the hardest for me, and then it leaves me while I have retained what it says. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says. Aisha said: I saw the revelation come down to him on an extremely cold winter day, and then it leaves him while his forehead is dripping with sweat.
73:6: God Almighty says: 6- The rising of the night, meaning: all of its hours, and every hour of it is rising. It is called that because it rises, meaning: appears, and from this: the cloud rises if it appears, so everything that happens at night and appears has arisen and is rising, and the plural is rising. Ibn Abi Maleka said: I asked Ibn Abbas and Ibn Al-Zubayr about it, and they said: The whole night is spent in prayer. Saeed bin Jubair and Ibn Zaid said: That is, the hour when he got up at night, he arose. In the Abyssinian dialect, it means standing. It is said: So-and-so arose, meaning he got up. Aisha said: The rising is after sleeping. Ibn Kaysan said: It is getting up at the end of the night. Akrima said: It is getting up from the beginning of the night. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn that he used to pray between the sunset and evening prayers, and he would say: This is the prayer of the night. Al-Hasan said: Every prayer after the last evening prayer is a prayer of the night. Al-Azhari said: Nash’at al-Layl means the night prayer. It is a verbal noun that comes in the form fa’ila like afiya meaning forgiveness. It is more severe in its impact. Ibn Amir and Abu Amr read: wata'a with a kasra on the waw and an extension, meaning agreement and consent. It is said: I agreed with someone if you agreed with him. This is because the agreement of the heart, hearing, sight, and tongue at night is greater than during the day. Others read: wa-ta’i’an with a fat-ha on the waw and a sukoon on the ta’, meaning: more difficult and burdensome for the worshipper than the daytime prayer, because the night is for sleeping and resting. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O God, make your punishment severe on Mudar. Ibn Abbas said: Their prayer at the beginning of the night was the most intense. He said: It is more likely that you will be able to count what God has enjoined upon you in terms of standing, because when a person sleeps, he does not know when he will wake up. Qatada said: Be steadfast in goodness and remember to read. Al-Farra' said: It is more steadfast in standing, meaning: it is easier for standing and more comfortable for the worshipper than during the daytime, because the day was created for the worshippers to do their work, and the night was created for seclusion, so worship is easier during it. It was also said: it is more energetic. Ibn Zayd said: He freed his heart for him during the day because he had no needs. Al-Hassan said: It is more effective in achieving good and more protective of Satan. And I stand up straight, and this is the most correct reading and most correct saying due to the calmness of the people and the stillness of the voices. Al-Kalbi said: I explain the statement / in the Qur’an. In short: Night worship is more active, more sincere, more blessed, and more rewarding than day worship.
73:7: 7- You have a long day, meaning: you can move around, change, advance and retreat in your needs and occupations. The root of swim is to go quickly, and from it comes swimming in water. It was said: a long day meaning: free time and space for you to sleep and deal with your needs, a part of the night. Yahya bin Ya'mar read sabkha with the combined kha, meaning: rest and relief for the body. This is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Aisha, when she had cursed a thief: Do not curse him with your curse against him, meaning: do not lighten up.
73:8: 8- And remember the name of your Lord, by monotheism and glorification, and devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion. Ibn Abbas and others said: Be sincere to Him. Al-Hasan said: Strive. Ibn Zayd said: Devote yourself to His worship. Sufyan said: Put your trust in Him with complete trust. It was also said: Be completely devoted to Him in worship, and this is the root of the word. It is said: I devoted myself to something, meaning: I cut it off. And charity is complete: meaning cut off from its owner, with no way to it. Devotion is the act of cutting off, from which it is said: I devoted myself to Him, so he said: Devotion. Zayd ibn Aslam said: Devotion is rejecting the world and everything in it, and seeking what is with God the Most High.
73:9: 9- Lord of the East and the West. The people of Hijaz, Abu Amr, and Hafs read: Lord with the Baa’ raised as the beginning, while the others read it with the Jarir as an attribute of the Lord in His statement: And remember the name of your Lord. “There is no god but He, so take Him as Disposer of affairs,” as a guardian over your affairs, so entrust them to Him.
73:10: 10- And be patient over what they say and leave them with gracious leave, as the verse on fighting has been abrogated.
73:11: 11- And leave Me to the deniers, those of wealth, and grant them respite for a little. This verse was revealed about the leaders of the Quraysh who mocked. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed about those who were fed at Badr, and they were only pleased until they were killed at Badr.
73:12: 12- Indeed, with Us, with Us in the Hereafter, are shackles, great chains that will never be broken. The singular is nakl. Al-Kalbi said: iron shackles, and Hellfire.
73:13: 13- And choking food, an unpalatable food that sticks to the throat and neither goes down nor out, which is Zaqqum and Adh-Dharee’. And a painful torment.
73:14: 14- The Day the earth and the mountains will shake, meaning: they will quake and move, and the mountains will become a heap of sand. Liquid sand. Al-Kalbi said: It is the sand that if you take a bit from it, what comes after it will follow you. It is said, I stirred the sand, meaning I stirred the bottom of it until it poured down from the top.
73:15: 15- Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent a Messenger to Pharaoh.
73:16: 16- So Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a terrible punishment, severe and heavy, meaning We punished him with a severe punishment to frighten the infidels of Mecca.
73:17: 17- Then how will you guard yourselves if you disbelieve? That is, how will you guard yourselves on the Day of Resurrection if you disbelieved in this world? Meaning, you will have no way to guard yourselves if you meet the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that its meaning is, how will you guard yourselves against the torment on the Day of Resurrection, and how will you protect yourself from it if you disbelieve? A Day that will turn children white-haired, from its horror and severity. That will be when it will be said to Adam, Arise and send forth from your descendants a deputation to the Fire.
73:18: Then he described the humiliation of the Day, saying: 18- The sky will be split by it, cracked by the descent of the angels by it, meaning: in that place. It was said: The ha’ refers back to the Lord, meaning: by His command and majesty, His promise will be fulfilled, coming to be.
73:19: 19- Indeed, these, meaning the verses of the Qur’an, are a reminder, a reminder and an admonition, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way, through faith and obedience.
73:20: 20- Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand nearly, less than, two-thirds of the night and half of it and a third of it. The people of Mecca and Kufa read: half of it and a third of it, with the fat-ha on the fa and tha’ and the sukoon on the ha’s, meaning: and you stand for half of it and a third of it. The others read it with the genitive on the fa and tha’ and the sukoon on the ha’s, in apposition to two-thirds. “And God measures the night and the day.” Ata’ said: He means that the knowledge of what you do does not escape Him, meaning that He knows the amounts of the night and the day, so He knows the amount of night that you stand for. He knows that you will not be able to count it. Al-Hasan said: They stood until their feet swelled, so the following was revealed: He knows that you will not be able to count it, “You will not be able to know that.” Muqatil said: A man would pray all night, fearing that he would not attain what he was commanded to do of standing, so He said: He knows that if you count it, you will not be able to know that. Then He pardoned you, so He returned to you with forgiveness and leniency. So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an, meaning in prayer. Al-Hasan said: meaning in the Maghrib and Isha prayers. Qais bin Abi Hazim said: I prayed behind Ibn Abbas in Basra. In the first rak’ah, he recited Surat Al-Hamd and the first verse of Surat Al-Baqarah. Then he stood up in the second rak’ah and recited Surat Al-Hamd and the second verse of Surat Al-Baqarah, then he bowed. When he finished, he turned to us and said: God Almighty says: So recite whatever is easy for you of it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam’ani told us, Abu Ja’far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Uthman bin Abi Saleh told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Hamid bin Mukhraq told me, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, “that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever recites fifty verses in a day or a night will not be recorded among the heedless. Whoever recites one hundred verses will be recorded among the devout. Whoever recites two hundred verses, the Qur’an will not dispute with him on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever recites five hundred verses, a qintar of reward will be recorded for him.” Ismail bin Abdul Qahir told us, Abdul Ghaffar bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Isa told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sufyan told us, Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Al-Qasim bin Zakariya told us, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Yahya bin Kathir, on the authority of Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman, the client of Banu Zuhrah, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Recite the Qur’an every month.’ I said: ‘I have the strength.’ He said: ‘Then recite it every twenty nights.’ I said: ‘I have the strength.’ He said: ‘Then recite it every seven nights, but do not do more than that.’” God Almighty says: He knows that among you there will be sick people and others traveling throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God, meaning travelers seeking God’s provisions, and others fighting in the cause of God, who cannot stand to perform the night prayer. Ibrahim narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: Any man who brings something to Madinah from the cities of the Muslims, patiently and seeking reward, and sells it at the price of that day, will be in the sight of God like a martyr. Then Abdullah recited: And others travel throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God meaning travelers for trade seeking God’s provision, and others fight in the cause of God. “So recite as much of it as is easy for you,” meaning whatever is easy for you from the Qur’an. The commentators said that this was in the early days of Islam, then it was abrogated by the five daily prayers. This is the verse in which God says interpretation of the meaning: And establish prayer and give zakah and loan God a goodly loan. Ibn Abbas said: He means everything other than zakah, such as maintaining kinship ties and hosting guests. “And whatever good you send forth for yourselves - you will find it with God. It is better,” you will find its reward in the Hereafter better than what you gave, and greater in reward, than what you have delayed and not sent forth. Better and greater is in the accusative case as the second object, because if existence means seeing, it takes two objects. This is a separation according to the Basrans, and a pillar according to the Kufians, and it has no syntactic position. Abu al-Qasim Yahya ibn Ali al-Kashmihani told us, Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Ali al-Bukhari told us in Kufa, Abu al-Qasim Nasr ibn Ahmad al-Faqih told us in Mosul, Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili told us, Abu Khaithama told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Suwayd, who said: Abdullah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you loves his own wealth more than the wealth of his heir? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none of us but loves his own wealth more than the wealth of his heir. He said: Know what you are saying. They said: We do not know anything except that, O Messenger of God. He said: There is none of you but loves the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth. They said: How so, O Messenger of God? He said: The wealth of each of you is what he has sent forward, and the wealth of his heir is what he has left behind. “And seek forgiveness from God” for your sins, for God is Forgiving and Merciful.
74:1: 1- "O you who are wrapped up," Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi told us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail told us, Yahya told us, Waki' told us, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, who said: "I asked Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman about the first thing revealed of the Qur'an? He said: 'O you who are wrapped up.' I said: They say: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' Al-Alaq - 1?" Abu Salamah said: I asked Jabir ibn Abdullah about that, and I said to him the same as you said, and Jabir said: I will not tell you except what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us. He said: I lived in Hira', and when I had finished living in Hira', I dismounted, and I was called, so I looked to my right and did not see anything, and I looked to my left and did not see anything, and I looked in front of me and did not see anything, and I looked behind me and did not see anything, so I raised my head and saw something, so I came to Khadija and said: They covered me and poured cold water on me. He said: So they covered me and poured cold water on me. He said: Then this verse was revealed: O you wrapped in your cloak, arise and warn, and glorify your Lord. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqil, Ibn Shihab said: I heard Abu Salamah say: Jabir bin Abdullah told me: He heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, talking about the period of revelation: While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my eyes towards the sky and saw the angel who had come to me in Hira sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was afraid until I fell to the ground. I went to my family and said: Cover me up, cover me up. So they covered me up. Then God Almighty revealed: O you wrapped in your cloak, arise and warn, until His saying: and abandon the abomination of idols. Abu Salamah said: Then the revelation became intense and continued.
74:2: God Almighty says: 2- O you wrapped in your cloak, arise and warn, meaning: warn the infidels of Mecca.
74:3: 3- And glorify your Lord, glorify Him above what idol worshippers say.
74:4: 4- And your garments purify, Qatada and Mujahid said: Purify yourself from sin, so he used the garment as a metaphor for the soul, and this is the opinion of Ibrahim, Ad-Dahhak, Ash-Sha’bi and Az-Zuhri. Ikrimah said: Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement: And your garments purify, so he said: Do not wear them for disobedience or for treachery, then he said: Haven’t you heard the words of Ghailan ibn Salamah Ath-Thaqafi: Praise be to God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I cover myself with treachery. The Arabs describe a man of honesty and loyalty as: He has clean clothes. They also say of one who is treacherous: He has dirty clothes. Ubayy ibn Ka’b said: “Do not wear it out of treachery, oppression, or sin. Wear it while you are pure, chaste, and generous.” Abu Ruq narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak that it means: And your work, so improve it. Al-Suddi said: If a man is righteous, it is said that he has clean clothes, and if he is wicked, it is said that he has dirty clothes. Saeed bin Jubair said: Purify your heart and intention. Al-Hasan and Al-Qurazi said: Make your character good. Ibn Sirin and Ibn Zayd said: He ordered the purification of clothes from impurities that prevent prayer, because the polytheists did not purify themselves or their clothes. Tawus said: And your clothes, shorten them because shortening clothes purifies them.
74:5: 5- And avoid the abomination, Abu Ja'far, Hafs on the authority of Asim and Ya'qub read and the abomination with a damma on the ra', while the others read it with a kasra. These are two dialects with the same meaning. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, Al-Zuhri, Ibn Zayd and Abu Salamah said: What is meant by the abomination are idols. He said: So avoid them and do not go near them. It was said: The letter zay in it is derived from the letter seen, and the Arabs alternate between the letters seen and the zay because of the closeness of their points of articulation. The evidence for this interpretation is his statement: So avoid the uncleanness of idols (al-Hajj 22:30). It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that its meaning is: Leave sins. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Rabi’ said: Al-Rajaz with a damma on the ra means an idol, and with a kasra means impurity and sin. Ad-Dahhak said: It means polytheism. Al-Kalbi said: It means torment. The metaphor of the verse: Abandon the deeds that will cause you punishment.
74:6: 6- And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return, meaning: do not give your wealth out of favor in order to receive more in return. This is the opinion of most of the commentators. Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid said: This was specific to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ad-Dahhak said: They are two types of usury: lawful and unlawful. The lawful is gifts, and the unlawful is interest. Qatadah said: Do not give something hoping for a worldly reward, meaning give to your Lord and repay it to God. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is: do not bestow a favor on God by your deeds, expecting more in return. Al-Rabi' said: Do not consider your deeds to be too much in your eyes, for it is little compared to what God has bestowed upon you. Khasif narrated from Mujahid: And do not be too weak to expect more in goodness, from their saying: a strong rope if it is weak. Its evidence is Ibn Mas'ud's reading: And do not bestow a favor, expecting more. Ibn Zayd said: Its meaning is: do not bestow prophethood on people, expecting a worldly wage or reward for it.
74:7: 7- And for the sake of your Lord be patient. It was said: Be patient in obeying Him, His commands, and His prohibitions for the sake of God's reward. Mujahid said: Be patient for the sake of God regarding what you have been harmed with. Ibn Zayd said: Its meaning is that you have undertaken a great matter, fighting the Arabs and the non-Arabs, so be patient with it for the sake of God the Almighty. It was also said: Be patient under the resources of fate for the sake of God.
74:8: 8- Then when the trumpet is blown, meaning the trumpet is blown, which is the horn that Israfil blows, meaning the second blast.
74:9: 9- That, meaning the blowing of the trumpet, is on that Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection, a difficult Day, severe.
74:10: 10- For the disbelievers, the matter is difficult for them, not easy, not simple.
74:11: God Almighty said: 11- Leave Me and he whom I created alone, meaning: I created him in his mother’s womb alone and unique, with no wealth or children. This was revealed about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi, who was called the only one among his people.
74:12: 12- And I have given him abundant wealth, meaning: a lot. It was said: It is what is sustained by growth such as crops, livestock, and trade. They differed on its amount. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A thousand dinars. Qatadah said: Four thousand dinars. Sufyan al-Thawri said: A thousand thousand dinars. Ibn Abbas said: Nine thousand mithqals of silver. Muqatil said: He had an orchard in Taif whose fruits never ceased in winter or summer. Ata' said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He had camels, horses, camels, and sheep between Makkah and Taif. He had many caravans, male and female slaves. It was said: An abundant wealth, the yield of each month.
74:13: 13- And sons as witnesses, residing in Mecca, never leaving it. They were ten, as stated by Mujahid and Qatadah. Muqatil said: They were seven, namely Al-Walid bin Al-Walid, Khalid, Amara, Hisham, Al-As, Qais, and Abd Shams. Three of them converted to Islam: Khalid, Hisham, and Amara.
74:14: 14- And I made it easy for him, meaning: I made life and life long for him. Al-Kalbi said: It means the money being piled up on top of each other, just as a bed is laid out.
74:15: 15- Then he hopes, he hopes, that I will increase, meaning that I will increase his wealth and children, and as a prelude.
74:16: 16- "No, I will not do it and I will not increase it." They said: After this verse was revealed, Al-Walid's wealth and children continued to decrease until he died. "Indeed, he was obstinate toward Our verses, stubborn.
74:17: 17- I will tire him out with the climb, I will burden him with a lot of suffering that will have no comfort for him. We narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The ascent is a mountain of fire, and the unbeliever ascends it for seventy autumns, then he falls. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told me, Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, Munjab ibn al-Harith told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Ammar al-Dahni, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: I will make him ascend it. He said: It is a mountain in the Fire made of fire that he is forced to climb. When he places his hand down, it melts, and when he raises it up, it returns. When he places his foot down, it melts, and when he raises it up, it returns. Al-Kalbi said: The ascent: is a smooth rock in the fire that he is required to climb, not allowing himself to breathe while he is climbing, and he is pulled by those in front of him with iron chains, and he is struck by those behind him with iron whips, so he climbs it in forty years, and when he reaches its peak he descends to its bottom, then he is required to climb it and he is pulled by those in front of him and struck by those behind him, and that is his habit forever and ever.
74:18: 18- It is thought and destiny, the verses, and that is because when God Almighty revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing,” to His saying: The final destination (Ghafir 40:1-3), the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood in the mosque and Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira was close to him listening to his recitation. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, realized that he was listening to him reciting the Qur’an, he repeated the verse. Al-Walid went until he came to the assembly of his people, Banu Makhzum, and said: By God, I heard from Muhammad just now words that are not from the speech of humans or the speech of jinn. It has sweetness and freshness. Its top is fruitful and its bottom is abundant. It rises and rises, and nothing rises. Then he returned to his home. The Quraysh said: Muhammad has bewitched him, by God, Al-Walid has bewitched him. By God, you will bewitch all of Quraysh. Al-Walid was called the flower of Quraysh. Abu Jahl said to them: I will suffice you against him. He went and sat next to Al-Walid, sad. Al-Walid said to him: Why do I see you sad? O my nephew? He said: What prevents me from being sad while the Quraysh are collecting money for you, supporting you in your old age, and claiming that you have embellished Muhammad’s words and you go to Ibn Abi Kabshah and Ibn Abi Quhafah, and you take from their surplus food? Al-Walid became angry and said: Did you not know that I am among the wealthiest and most numerous of them, and did Muhammad and his companions ever eat their fill, so that they would have surplus food? Then he stood up with Abu Jahl until he came to the assembly of his people and said to them: You claim that Muhammad is mad. Have you ever seen him choke? They said: By God, no. He said: You claim that he is a soothsayer. Have you ever seen him practice soothsaying? They said: By God, no. He said: You claim that he is a poet. Have you ever seen him recite poetry? They said: By God, no. He said: You claim that he is a liar. Have you ever experienced him lying? They said: No. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was called Al-Amin the Trustworthy before the Prophethood, because of his truthfulness. The Quraysh said to Al-Walid: What is that? He thought to himself, then looked, then frowned and said: He is nothing but a magician. Haven't you seen him separate a man from his family, his clients and his children? He is a magician and what he says is magic that has an effect. That is what God Almighty says: He thought, about Muhammad and the Qur’an, and he estimated, in himself, what he could say about Muhammad and the Qur’an.
74:19: 19- He killed, he cursed, and Al-Zuhri said: he tortured, how did He decide? in the manner of astonishment, denial, and rebuke.
74:20: 20- Then he killed, however he was able, he repeated it for emphasis. It was said that its meaning was that he was cursed in any way he was able to speak, just as one says, I will strike him, however he did it, meaning in any way he did it.
74:21: 21- Then he looked, seeking what the Qur’an would use to refute and reject it.
74:22: 22- Then he frowned and frowned, he frowned and looked with intense hatred, as if he were thinking about something.
74:23: 23- Then he turned away, from faith, and was arrogant, he was arrogant when he was called to it.
74:24: 24- He said, ‘This,’ what Muhammad is reading, ‘is nothing but magic that is being cast,’ narrated and told about magicians.
74:25: 25- This is nothing but the word of a human being, meaning Yasar and Jabr, as he narrates it from them. It was also said that he narrates it from Musaylimah, the ruler of Yamamah.
74:26: God Almighty said: 26- I will burn it in Hell, I will put it in, Saqar, and Saqar is one of the names of Hell.
74:27: 27- And what will make you know what Hellfire is?
74:28: 28- It leaves nothing behind and spares nothing, meaning it leaves nothing behind and spares nothing in it except that it consumes and destroys it. Mujahid said: It neither causes death nor brings to life means it leaves nothing alive in it and spares nothing dead in it; whenever they are burned, they are renewed. Al-Suddi said: It leaves them no flesh and leaves no bones. Ad-Dahhak said: If you take them, you will not leave anything of them, and if they are brought back, you will not leave them until you annihilate them. And for everything there is boredom and a period of rest except for Hell.
74:29: 29- A glare for mankind, changing the skin until it turns it black. It is said: illness and sadness glared at him if they changed him. Mujahid said: It scorches the skin until it leaves it blacker than night. Ibn Abbas and Zaid bin Aslam said: It burns the skin. Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: Hell glares at them until they see it with their own eyes. Similar to his statement: And Hellfire will be brought forth for the deviators (Ash-Shu'ara': 91). A glare is raised as an attribute of Saqar in his statement: And what can make you know what is Saqar? "Bashar is the plural of basharah and the plural of bashar is abshar".
74:30: 30- Nineteen over it, meaning: over the Fire are nineteen angels, and they are its guardians: Malik and eighteen with him. It was reported: Their eyes are like flashing lightning, and their fangs are like hawks. Flames of fire come forth from their mouths. The distance between the shoulders of one of them is a year’s journey. Mercy has been taken away from them. One of them raises seventy thousand and throws them wherever he wants in Hell. Amr ibn Dinar said: One of them will be pushed into Hell at once more than Rabi’ah and Mudar. Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Ad-Dahhak said: When this verse was revealed, Abu Jahl said to the Quraysh 106:May your mothers be bereaved of you! I heard Ibn Abi Kabsha saying that the keepers of Hellfire are nineteen and you are the bravest, so are ten of you unable to strike one of the keepers of Hellfire? Abu Al-Ashd Asid bin Kalada bin Khalaf Al-Jumahi said: I can suffice you against them seventeen, ten on my back and seven on my stomach, so you suffice me with two. It was narrated that he said: I will walk in front of you on the bridge, and I will push ten people with my right shoulder and nine people with my left shoulder into the fire, and we will go on and enter Paradise.
74:31: Then God Almighty revealed: 31- And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels, not human men, so who can overcome the angels?
