And We have not made their number, meaning their small number, except as a trial for those who disbelieve, meaning as a misguidance for them until they said what they said, that those who were given the Scripture will be certain, because it is written in the Torah and the Gospel that they are nineteen, and those who believe will increase in faith, meaning those who believe from among the People of the Scripture will increase in belief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, if they find what he said in agreement with what is in their books, and let not those who were given the Scripture and the believers doubt, about their number, and let those in whose hearts is a disease, doubt and hypocrisy, and the disbelievers, the polytheists of Mecca, say, ‘What did God intend by this as an example?’ What did He intend by this hadith? And by the example He intended the hadith itself. Likewise, that is, just as God led astray those who denied the number of the keepers and guided those who believed, “God leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him.” Muqatil said: This is Abu Jahl’s answer when he said: Does Muhammad have no helpers other than nineteen? Ata’ said: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him, meaning from the angels whom He created to torment the people of Hellfire. None knows their number except God. The meaning is that the nineteen are the keepers of Hellfire, and they have helpers and soldiers from the angels that none knows except God, the Almighty and Majestic. Then He returned to the mention of Saqar and said: And it, meaning Saqar, is only a reminder to mankind, except a reminder and an admonition to the people.
74:32: 32- No, by the moon, this is an oath, he says: Truly.
74:33: 33- And the night when it departs, Nafi`, Hamza, Hafs, and Ya`qub read idh without an alif, adbara with an alif, and the others read idha with an alif, dabbar without an alif, because it is more in agreement with what follows it, which is His statement, And the morning when it brightens, and because there is no oath in the Quran besides idh, but rather beside oaths idha, and dabbar and adbara are both languages. It is said: dabar al-layl and adbara if it turned away and went away. Abu `Amr said: dabbar is the language of Quraysh. Qatrib said: dabbar means approached. The Arabs say: So-and-so came behind me, meaning he came behind me, so the night comes after the day.
74:34: 34- And the morning when it dawns, it shines and becomes clear.
74:35: 35- It is one of the greatest things, meaning that Saqar is one of the greatest things, and the singular of greatest is greatest. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: What he meant by greatest is the levels of Hell, and they are seven: Hell, Laza, Al-Hutama, Al-Sa’ir, Saqar, Al-Jahannam, and Al-Hawiya.
74:36: 36- A warner to mankind, meaning the Fire as a warner to mankind. Al-Hasan said: By God, God has not warned of anything more terrible than it. It is in the accusative case as a definite noun from His statement: of one of the greatest because it is definite, and a warner is indefinite. Al-Khalil said: The warner is a verbal noun like nakir, and that is why it is used to describe the feminine. It was said: It is an attribute of God, the Most High, the Most Great. Its metaphor is: And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels as warners to mankind, meaning as a warning to them. Abu Razin said: He says, I am a warner to you from it, so fear it. It was said: It is an attribute of Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, meaning: O you wrapped in garments, arise as a warner to mankind, so warn. This is the meaning of Ibn Zayd's statement.
74:37: 37- For whoever among you wills, instead of saying for mankind, “to advance,” in goodness and obedience, or to lag behind, in evil and disobedience. The meaning is that the warning has been given to every one of those who believe or disbelieve.
74:38: 38- Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, pledged in the Fire for its earnings and held accountable for its deeds.
74:39: 39- Except the Companions of the Right Hand, for their sins will not be held in the Fire, but God will forgive them. Qatada said: All people will be held in the Fire except the Companions of the Right Hand. They differed concerning them: It was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him that they are the children of the Muslims. Abu Dhabiyan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are the angels. Muqatil said: They are the people of Paradise who were on Adam's right hand on the day of the covenant, when God said to them: These are in Paradise, and I do not care. And he also said: They are those who were given their books in their right hands. And he also said: They are those who were given a right hand regarding themselves. Al-Hasan said: They are the sincere Muslims. Al-Qasim said: Every soul is held accountable for what it has earned, whether good or evil, except for those who rely on bounty. Everyone who relies on earnings is held hostage by it, but whoever relies on bounty is not held accountable by it.
74:40: 40- In gardens, they will question each other.
74:42: 42- What brought you into Hellfire? They replied.
74:43: 43- They said, ‘We were not among those who prayed,’ to God.
74:44: 44- And we did not feed the poor.
74:45: 45- And we were engaging in falsehood with the engagers.
74:46: 46- And we used to deny the Day of Judgment.
74:47: 47- Until the certainty comes to us, which is death.
74:48: God Almighty said: 48- So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them. Ibn Masoud said: The angels, the prophets, the martyrs, the righteous, and all the believers will intercede, and only four will remain in the Fire. Then he recited: They will say, ‘We were not among those who prayed,’ until His saying: on the Day of Judgment. Imran bin Al-Hussain said: Intercession is beneficial for everyone, except for those whom you hear. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, described the people of Hell and how they would be punished. He said: A man from the people of Paradise will pass by them and a man from them will say, ‘O so-and-so.’ He will say, ‘What do you want?’ He will say, ‘Do you not remember a man who gave you a drink on such-and-such a day?’ He will say, ‘And are you he?’ He will say, ‘Yes.’ So he will intercede for him and his intercession will be accepted. He said: Then a man from the people of Paradise will pass by them and say, ‘O so-and-so.’ He will say, ‘What do you want?’ He will say, ‘Do you not remember a man who gave you ablution on such-and-such a day?’ He will say, ‘And you are he?’ He will say, ‘Yes.’ So he will intercede for him and his intercession will be accepted.”
74:49: 49- Why then do they turn away from the reminder? The sermons of the Qur’an turning away is in the accusative case as a state, and it was said that they became turning away.
74:50: 50- As if they were donkeys, plural of donkey, frightened, the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read it with a fatha on the fa', while the rest read it with a kasra. Whoever reads it with a fatha, its meaning is frightened and terrified, and whoever reads it with a kasra, its meaning is repellent. It is said: nafar frightened and istanfar frightened with one meaning, just as one says ajab wonder and istajab wonder.
74:51: 51- She fled from a qasoora. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak said: Qasoora means archers. It has no singular form based on the same word. This is the narration of Ata' on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Saeed bin Jubair said: They are the hunters. This is the narration of Ata' on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Zayd ibn Aslam said: They are strong men, and every big, strong man among the Arabs is called qasur and qasoora. Abu al-Mutawakkil said: It is the noise and voices of the people. Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It is the fishermen’s ropes. Abu Hurairah said: It is the lion, and this is the opinion of Ata’ and Al-Kalbi, because when wild donkeys see a lion, they run away. Likewise, when these polytheists hear the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting the Qur’an, they run away from him. Akrima said: It is the darkness of the night, and the blackness of the first part of the night is called Qasoora.
74:52: 52- Rather, every man among them desires to be given spread-out pages. The commentators said: The infidels of Quraysh said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: So that there will be at the head of every man among us a spread-out book from God that you are His Messenger, in which we are commanded to follow you. Al-Kalbi said: The polytheists said: O Muhammad, we have been informed that a man from the Children of Israel would wake up with his sin and expiation written on his head, so bring us something like that. The books are the plural of the newspaper, and mansharah means spread out.
74:53: Then God Almighty said: 53- No, they will not be given the scrolls. It was also said: Truly, and everything that has been reported to you from it is its face. Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter, meaning they do not fear the punishment of the Hereafter. The meaning is that if they feared the Fire, they would not have suggested these verses after the evidence had been established.
74:54: 54- No, really, it is, meaning the Qur’an, a reminder, an admonition.
74:55: 55- Whoever wishes to remember it, will be admonished by it.
74:56: 56- And they do not remember, Nafi’ and Ya’qub read tadhkaruna with a ta’ and the others with a ya’, except that God wills, Muqatil said: Except that God wills for them guidance. He is the One worthy of piety and the One worthy of forgiveness, meaning He is the One worthy of avoiding His prohibitions and the One worthy of forgiving those who fear Him. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told us, Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, Abdullah ibn al-Fadl told us, Hudbah ibn Khalid told us, Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding this verse: ‘He is worthy of piety and forgiveness.’ He said: Your Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, said: I am worthy of being feared and of associating no partner with Me, and I am worthy of forgiveness for whoever fears to associate partners with Me.” And Suhayl is the son of Abd al-Rahman al-Qat’i, the brother of Hazm al-Qat’i.
75:1: 1- I swear by the Day of Resurrection. Al-Qawwas read on the authority of Ibn Kathir: I swear by the first letter without an alif before the hamza.
75:2: 2- And I do not swear by the self-reproaching soul, with the alif, and Abd al-Rahman al-A’raj read it this way, meaning that he swore by the Day of Resurrection, and he did not swear by the self-reproaching soul. The correct thing is that he swore by both of them, and not is a connection in them, meaning he swore by the Day of Resurrection and by the self-reproaching soul. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash said: It is an emphasis on the oath, like saying: No, I swear to God. Al-Farra’ said: No is a response to the words of the polytheists who denied it. Then he began by saying: I swear by the Day of Resurrection and I swear by the self-reproaching soul. Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba said: They say: The Resurrection, and the Resurrection of one of them is his death. Alqamah attended a funeral, and when it was buried, he said: As for this one, his Resurrection has taken place. And I swear by the self-reproaching soul. Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah said: It blames itself for good and evil, and is not patient during prosperity and adversity. Qatada said: The blaming woman is the wicked one. Mujahed said: You regret what happened and say: If only I had done it or if I hadn’t done it. Al-Farra' said: There is no soul, righteous or wicked, except that it blames itself. If it has done good, it says: Why did I not do more? And if it has done evil, it says: I wish I had not done it. Al-Hasan said: It is the believing soul. He said: By God, you never see the believer except that he blames himself: What did I mean by my words? What did I mean by my food? And the wicked person continues on without holding himself accountable or reproaching himself. Muqatil said: It is the disbelieving soul that blames itself in the afterlife for what it neglected regarding God’s command in this world.
75:3: 3- Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? This verse was revealed about Adi bin Rabi'ah, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, the son-in-law of Al-Akhns bin Shuraik Al-Thaqafi. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to say: O God, protect me from my evil neighbor, meaning Adi and Al-Akhns. This is because Adi bin Rabi'ah came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: "O Muhammad, tell me about the al-Qiyamah 75:when will it be, and what its matter and condition will be?" The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, told him. He said: If I were to witness that day, I would not believe you or have faith in you, or will God assemble the bones? So God, the Almighty, revealed: Does man think - meaning the disbeliever - that We will not assemble his bones after their dispersion and decay and bring him to life. It was said that he mentioned the bones and meant his own soul because bones are the mold of the soul, and creation is not complete except through their being complete. It was also said that it is outside the saying of the denier, or God will assemble the bones, as in His saying: He will say, 'Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?' (Ya-Sin 36:78).
75:4: 4- Yes, we are able, meaning we are able. It is a future tense verb that is in the present tense. Al-Farra’ said, Able is in the accusative case as an exit from we gather, just as you say in speech: Do you think that we are not able to overcome you? Yes, we are able to do more than you, meaning: rather, we are able to do more than this. Metaphor of the verse: Yes, We are able to assemble his bones and do even greater things than that, namely, to put his fingertips together, making his fingers and toes into a single object like a camel’s hoof or a donkey’s hooves. Thus, he would not be able to use them for grasping, stretching, or delicate tasks like writing, sewing, etc. This is the view of most commentators. Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Qutaybah said: Its meaning is: The unbeliever thought that We would not be able to reunite his bones. Yes, We are able to restore the small joints, and bring them together until we level the fingers. So whoever is able to reunite the small bones is even more able to reunite the large ones.
75:5: 5- Rather, man wants to explode before him, meaning that the son of Adam is not ignorant that his Lord is able to gather his bones, but He wants to explode before him, meaning: he continues to disobey God as long as he lives, riding his head, not removing it or repenting. This is the saying of Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and Al-Suddi. Saeed bin Jubair said: He commits a sin before him: He commits the sin and delays repentance, saying: I will repent, I will work until death comes to him in the worst of his conditions and worst of his deeds. Ad-Dahhak said: It is hope. He says: I will live and obtain such and such from this world, without mentioning death. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: He denies what is before him of resurrection and judgment. The root of fujur is deviation, and the immoral and disbeliever is called fajir because of his deviation from the truth.
75:6: 6- He asks, ‘When will the Day of Resurrection be?’ That is, when will it be, as a denial of it.
75:7: God Almighty said: 7- Then when the sight dazzles. The people of Medina read dazzle with a fatha on the ra, while others read it with a kasra. These are two dialects. Qatada and Muqatil said: His eyesight will be fixed and he will not blink at the wonders he saw which he denied in this world. It was said: That will be at the time of death. Al-Kalbi said: When they see Hell, the eyes of the infidels will flash. Al-Farra and Al-Khalil said: Barq - with a kasra - means: he was frightened and bewildered by what he saw of wonders. Barq with a fatha means: he slit his eye and opened it, from al-Bariq, which means sparkle.
75:8: 8- And the moon was eclipsed It became dark and its light and brightness were lost.
75:9: 9- And He will gather the sun and the moon as two black, round objects, as if they were two barren bulls. It was said: He will gather them together when the light is gone. Ata’ ibn Yasar said: They will be gathered together on the Day of Resurrection, then thrown into the sea and will become the Great Fire of God.
75:10: 10- Man will say, meaning the disbelieving liar, On that Day, ‘Where is the escape?’ Meaning: the place of escape, which is the place of flight. It was also said that it is a source, meaning: Where is the escape?
75:11: God Almighty said: 11- No, no burden, no fortress, no protection, no refuge. Al-Suddi said: No mountain. And when they were frightened, they would take refuge in the mountain and fortify themselves there. So God Almighty said: No mountain that Day will protect them.
75:12: 12- To your Lord, that Day, is the final destination, meaning the final destination of creation. Abdullah bin Masoud said: The destination and the reference are similar to the Almighty’s saying: To your Lord is the return (al-Alaq 96:8) And to God is the destination (Al Imran 3:28) (al-Nur 24:42) (Fatir 35:18). Al-Suddi said: The end is similar to: And to your Lord is the destination (al-Najm 53:42).
75:13: 13- On that Day, man will be informed of what he sent forward and what he left behind. Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas said: What he sent forward before his death of good and bad deeds, and what he left behind after his death of good or bad practices that he would follow. Atiyah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: For what he has done of disobedience and what he has done of obedience. Qatada said: Because of what he has done in obedience to God, and what he has left behind in terms of the right of God, he has neglected it. Mujahed said: By the beginning and end of his deeds. Ata’ said: By what he sent forward at the beginning of his life and what he left behind at the end of his life. Zaid bin Aslam said: What he gave of his money to himself and what he left behind for the heirs.
75:14: 14- Rather, man is a witness against himself. Ikrimah, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: Its meaning is that man has observers over himself who watch him and bear witness against him by his actions, and they are his hearing, sight, and limbs. The ha was added to insight because what is meant by man here is his limbs. It is possible that its meaning is Rather, man is a witness against himself, meaning: for his limbs, so the preposition was deleted like His statement: And if you wish to have your children nursed Al-Baqarah 2:233, meaning for your children. It is also permissible for it to be an adjective for a feminine noun, meaning, Rather, man is a seeing eye against himself. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Ata' read: Rather, man is a witness against himself. This is the narration of Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas. The ha in basira is for emphasis, which is evidence of this interpretation. God Almighty says: Sufficient for you this Day is yourself as a reckoner against you. (al-Isra’ 17:14)
75:15: 15- Even if he were to present his excuses, meaning a witness would testify against him, even if he apologized and argued on his own behalf, it would not benefit him, as God the Almighty said: The Day when the wrongdoers’ excuses will not benefit them. (Ghafir 40:52). This is the opinion of Mujahid, Qatadah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Zayd, and Ata’. Al-Farra’ said: Even if he were to apologize, then there is someone on his own who would deny his excuse. The meaning of presenting is to say, as God the Almighty said: So throw down to them the word, ‘You are indeed liars.’ (al-Nahl 16:86). Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: Even if he were to present his excuses, meaning even if he lowered the curtain and closed the doors. The people of Yemen call a curtain an excuse, and the plural is excuses. According to this opinion, the meaning is: Even if he lowers the curtain to conceal what he does, then his own soul will bear witness against him.
75:16: God Almighty said 16- Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding the words of God Almighty: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it, he said: “When Gabriel came down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with revelation, he would sometimes move his tongue and lips, and it would be difficult for him, and he would know from that, so God Almighty revealed the verse in “I swear by the Day of Resurrection”: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it.
75:17: 17- It is for Us to collect it and recite it. He said, It is for Us to collect it in your chest and recite it.
75:18: 18- So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. So when We have revealed it, then listen.
75:19: 19- Then it is for Us to explain it, it is for Us to explain it with your tongue. He said: So whenever Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him, he lowered his head, and when he left, he recited it as God, the Almighty, had promised him. Muhammad ibn Ismail narrated it, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Musa, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha with this chain of transmission, and he said: “He used to move his lips when it was revealed to him, fearing that it might slip away from him, so it was said to him: ‘Do not move your tongue about it. ’ ‘It is for Us to collect it’” that We collect it in your chest and to recite it’ that you recite it.
75:20: 20- No, but you love the immediate.
75:21: 21- And you abandon the Hereafter. The people of Medina and Kufa read tahbun wa tadhdharun with a ta' in both, while others read it with a ya', meaning they choose this world over the Hereafter and work for it, meaning the infidels of Mecca. Whoever reads it with a ta' then it is based on the estimation: Say to them, O Muhammad: Rather, you love and abandon.
75:22: 22- Some faces that Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection, will be radiant. Ibn Abbas said: Beautiful. Mujahid said: Happy. Ibn Zayd said: Soft. Muqatil said: White with light on them. Al-Suddi said: Bright. Yaman said: Bright and radiant. Al-Farra’ said: Bright with bliss. It is said: May God make his face radiant, and May God make him radiant and make him radiant, and May God make his face radiant, and May He make his face radiant, with freshness and radiance. God Almighty said: You will recognize in their faces the radiance of pleasure. (al-Mutaffifin 83:24)
75:23: 23- Looking at her Lord. Ibn Abbas said: Most people look at their Lord clearly, without a veil. Al-Hasan said: She looks at the Creator, and it is right for her to look while she looks at the Creator. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Al-Haitham Al-Turabi told us, Abdullah ibn Ahmad Al-Hamawi told us, Ibrahim ibn Khazim Al-Shashi told us, Abd ibn Hamid told us, Shababah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Thawir, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The lowest in status of the people of Paradise is he who looks at his gardens, his wives, his blessings, his servants, and his couches for a distance of a thousand years, and the most honored of them in the sight of God is he who looks at His face morning and evening. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord.’”
75:24: 24- And faces that Day will be gloomy, gloomy, dusty, and black.
75:25: 25- She thinks that a terrible calamity will befall her, she is certain that a great punishment will befall her. A terrible calamity is a great disaster, and a severe matter that breaks the backbone. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: A backbreaker. Ibn Zayd said: It is entering the Fire. Al-Kalbi said: It is being prevented from seeing the Lord Almighty.
75:26: 26- No, when it reaches meaning the soul, a metaphor for something unmentioned, the collarbones, so he gasped at death, and the collarbones is the plural of the collarbone, which are the bones between the opening of the throat and the shoulder, and the soul reaching the collarbone is a metaphor for approaching death.
75:27: 27- And it was said, meaning someone who was dying said: Is there anyone who can recite incantations over him? Is there a doctor who can recite incantations over him and treat him, so that he can be cured by his incantation or medicine. Qatada said: They sought doctors for him, but they could not help him at all against God’s decree. Sulayman al-Taymi and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: This is from the words of the angels. Some of them say to each other: Who will ascend with his soul? So the angels of mercy or the angels of torment ascend with it.
75:28: 28- And he thought, the one whose soul had reached the collarbones, that it was separation from the world.
75:29: 29- And the leg shall be entwined with the leg. Qatada said: Severity with severity. Ata’ said: The severity of death with the severity of the Hereafter. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Hardships befell him one after the other. Al-Suddi said: No one gets out of a hardship except that something worse comes to him. Ibn Abbas said: The matter of this world is related to the matter of the Hereafter, so it was on the last day of this world and the first day of the days of the Hereafter. Mujahid said: Life and death met in him. Ad-Dahhak said: People prepare his body and the angels prepare his soul. Al-Hasan said: They are his legs when they are wrapped in the shroud. Al-Sha’bi said: They are his legs at death.
75:30: 30- To your Lord, that Day, is the return, meaning that the servants will return to God on that Day and be driven to Him.
75:31: 31- He neither believed nor prayed, meaning: Abu Jahl, he did not believe in the Qur’an nor pray to God.
75:32: 28- But he lied and turned away, about faith.
75:33: 33- Then he went to his family, he returned to them, stretching himself, swaggering and swaggering in his walk. It was said that its root is: stretching, meaning: extending, and stretching is extending.
75:34: 34- It is better for you, then better.
75:35: 35- Then it is more appropriate for you, then more appropriate. This is a threat upon a threat from God Almighty to Abu Jahl, and it is a word used to threaten and warn. Some scholars said: It means that you are more deserving of this punishment, more deserving of it, and more worthy of it. It is said to a man who has been afflicted with something bad that he deserves. It was said: It is a word that Arabs say to someone who has been harmed. Its origin is from loyalty, from the word mawla, which means closeness. God Almighty said: Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you (al-Tawbah 9:123). Qatada said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told us that when this verse was revealed, he took hold of the hem of Abu Jahl’s garment in al-Batha’ and said to him: ‘It is better for you, then better, then better for you, then better.’ Abu Jahl said: ‘Are you threatening me, O Muhammad? By God, neither you nor your Lord can do anything, and I am more powerful than anyone who walks between two mountains!’ Then, on the day of Badr, God struck him down in the worst way and killed him in the worst way. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: ‘Every nation has a Pharaoh, and the Pharaoh of this nation is Abu Jahl.’”
75:36: 36- Does man think that he will be left neglected? neglected, not commanded or forbidden. Al-Suddi said: It means neglected, and camels are neglected if they graze wherever they want without a shepherd.
75:37: 37- Was he not a drop of ejaculated semen? poured into the womb. Hafs read on the authority of Asim ejaculated with a ya, which is the reading of Al-Hasan. The others read it with a ta, for the sake of the drop.
75:38: 38- Then he was a clot, then He created and proportioned him, so He put the soul into him and proportioned his creation.
75:39: 39- And He made from it two mates, the male and the female, He created from its semen male and female children.
75:40: 40- Is not He, who did this, able to bring the dead to life? Abu Tahir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Qashani told us, Abu Amr al-Qasim ibn Ja`far al-Hashimi told us, Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar al-Lu`lu`i told us, Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn Ash`ath told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri told us, Sufyan told us, Ismail ibn Umayya told me: I heard a Bedouin say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever among you recites ‘By the Fig and the Olive’ and reaches the end of it: ‘Is not God the best of judges?’ (al-Tin 95:8), let him say: ‘Yes, and I am among the witnesses to that.’ And whoever recites: ‘I swear by the Day of Resurrection’ and reaches: ‘Is He not able to give life to the dead?’ let him say: ‘Yes.’ And whoever recites: ‘By the Messengers’ and reaches: ‘Then in what statement after it will they believe?’ let him say: ‘We believe in God.’” Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz told us, al-Qasim ibn Ja`far told us, Abu Ali al-Lu`lu`i told us, Abu Dawud told us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Abi `Aishah, who said: “A man used to pray on top of his house, and when he recited: ‘Is He not able to give life to the dead?’ he would say: ‘Glory be to You! Yes.’ So they asked him about that, and he said: ‘I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.’”
76:1: Ata' said: It is Meccan. Mujahid and Qatadah said: It is Medinan. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: It is Medinan except for one verse, which is: So be patient over the decision of your Lord and do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate. 1- Has there not been over man, meaning Adam, peace be upon him, a period of time? Forty years, lying in clay between Mecca and Taif before the spirit was breathed into him, when he was not a thing worth mentioning, he is not mentioned nor known / nor is it known what his name is or what is meant by it, meaning: he was a thing and was not mentioned, and that was from the time he was created from clay until the spirit was breathed into him. It was narrated that Omar heard a man reciting this verse: It was not a thing mentioned. Omar said: If only it had been completed. He meant: If only it had remained as it was. Ibn Abbas said: Then He created it after one hundred and twenty years.
76:2: 2- Indeed, We created man, meaning the son of Adam, from a sperm-drop, meaning: the man’s semen and the woman’s semen. Mixtures: mixtures, the singular of which is: mix and mixture, like cheek and cheeks. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Al-Rabi’ said: It means that the man’s semen and the woman’s semen mix in the womb and from them a child is born. The man’s semen is white and thick and the woman’s semen is yellow and thin. So whichever of the two is higher than the other, the resemblance is to him. Whatever is of nerves and bones is from the man’s sperm, and whatever is of flesh, blood and hair is from the woman’s semen. Ad-Dahhak said: What he meant by mixtures is the different colors of sperm. The sperm of a man is white, red, and yellow, while the sperm of a woman is green, red, and yellow. This is the narration of Al-Walabi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Kalbi said the same: He said: Mixtures are whiteness in redness and yellowness. Yaman said: Every two colors that mix are mixed. Ibn Masoud said: They are the veins that are in the sperm. Al-Hasan said: A sperm mixed with blood, which is menstrual blood. If she becomes pregnant, the menstruation stops. Qatada said: These are the stages of creation: sperm, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then a bone, then He covers it with flesh, then He creates it as another creation. We test him means we test him with commands and prohibitions. So We made him all-hearing and all-seeing. Some Arab scholars said: There is an inversion of the former, meaning: So We made him all-hearing and all-seeing to test him, because a test does not occur except after creation is complete.
76:3: 3- Indeed, We showed him the way, meaning, We showed him the path of truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, and showed him the path of good and evil. Either grateful or ungrateful, either a happy believer or a miserable disbeliever. It was said that the meaning of the statement is the reward, meaning: We showed him the path whether he was grateful or ungrateful.
76:4: Then he explained what is for the two groups, saying: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains, meaning: in Hell. The people of Madinah, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr from Asim read: salasilan wa qawarir, fa qawarir with an alif when stopping and with tanween when connected in both of them. Hamzah and Ya'qub read without an alif when stopping and without tanween when connected in both of them. Ibn Kathir read the first qawarir with an alif when stopping and with tanween when connected, and the second salasil wa qawarir without an alif or tanween. Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Hafs read the first salasilan wa qawarir with an alif when stopping, in the script, and without tanween when connected, and the second qawarir without an alif or tanween. His saying and shackles means: in their hands, chained to their necks, and a Blazing Fire, a severe fuel.
76:5: 5- Indeed, the righteous, meaning the true believers who are obedient to their Lord, the singular of whom is barr, like witness and witnesses, “supporter” and supporters, and barr also like nahr and nahr, “will drink,” in the Hereafter, from a cup, in which is a drink mixed with camphor, Qatada said: It will be mixed for them with camphor and sealed with musk. Ikrimah said: Its mixture is its taste. The interpreters of meanings said: He meant like camphor in its whiteness, pleasant scent, and coolness, because camphor is not drunk, and it is like His statement: Until, when He makes it fire (al-Kahf 18:96), meaning like fire. This is the meaning of the statement of Qatada and Mujahid: The scent of camphor will mix with it. Ibn Kaysan said: It will be perfumed with camphor, musk, and ginger. Ata’ and Al-Kalbi said: Camphor is the name of a spring of water in Paradise.
76:6: 6- Ainan, accusative following camphor. It was said: It is accusative of praise. It was said: I mean a spring. Al-Zajjaj said: The best is that the meaning is from Ainan, He drinks from it. It was said: He drinks it and the ba is a connection. It was said: By it meaning from it. Servants of God, Ibn Abbas said: The saints of God, They make it gush forth abundantly, meaning they lead it wherever they want from their homes and palaces, like someone who has a river that he makes gush forth here and there to wherever he wants.
76:7: 7- They fulfill their vows. This is one of their characteristics in this world, meaning that they were like that in this world. Qatada said: He meant that they should fulfill what God has imposed upon them of prayer, zakat, fasting, Hajj, Umrah, and other obligations. The meaning of vow is obligation. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: If they vow to obey God, they must fulfill it. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarkhasi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashemi told us, Abu Mus`ab told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Talhah ibn `Abd al-Malik al-Ayli, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of `Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever vows to obey God, let him obey Him, and whoever vows to disobey God, let him not disobey Him. “And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread,” spreading and extending. The dawn spreads, if it extends and spreads. Muqatil said: His evil was widespread in the heavens, so they split, the stars were scattered, the sun and moon were rolled up, and the angels were terrified. And on the earth: the mountains were blown away, the waters sank, and everything on the earth, from mountains to buildings, was broken.
76:8: 8- And they give food in spite of their love for it, meaning in spite of their love for food, its scarcity, their desire for it, and their need for it. It was also said: in spite of the love of God, the Almighty, the needy, the poor who has no money, and the orphan, the young who has no father, and the captive, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Ata' said: he is the imprisoned one from among the people of the Qiblah. Qatada said: God commanded that the captives be treated well, and that their captives at that time were to the polytheists. It was also said: the captive is the slave. It was also said: the woman, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Fear God regarding women, for they are captives to you, meaning captives. They differed about the reason for the revelation of this verse. Muqatil said: It was revealed about a man from the Ansar who fed a poor person, an orphan, and a prisoner in one day. Mujahid and Ata’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, because he had made some barley for a Jew. He took the barley and ground a third of it, and they made some of it to eat. When it was cooked, a poor man came and asked for it, so they brought him food. Then he made the second third, and when it was cooked, an orphan came and asked for it, and they fed him. Then he made the remaining third, and when it was cooked, a captive of the polytheists came and asked for it, and they fed him, and they spent the day there. This is the statement of Al-Hasan and Qatadah, that the captive was from the people of polytheism. It is evidence that feeding captives, even if they are from the people of polytheism, is good and one hopes for its reward.
76:9: 9- “We feed you only for the sake of God. We do not want from you any reward or thanks.” Thanks is a verbal noun like contracts, “entering,” and exiting. Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said: They did not speak about it, but God knew that in their hearts, so He praised them.
76:10: 10- Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day of stern distress, when faces will frown from its horror and severity. Sternness is attributed to the day, just as one says: a fasting day and a standing night. It was also said that the day was described as stern because of the severity it contains, Qamtarir, Qatada, Mujahid, and Muqatil said: Qamtarir is the one who frowns at faces and foreheads. Al-Kalbi said: A frown is that in which there is no expansion, and Qatmarir is: intense. Al-Akhfash said: Qamtarir is the most severe of days and the longest in affliction. It is said: a Qamtarir or Qamatar day, if it is severe and unpleasant, and the day rained rain so it is raining.
76:11: 11- So God saved them from the evil of that Day, which they feared, and He met them with radiance, beauty in their faces, and joy, in their hearts.
76:12: 12- And He rewarded them for their patience, in obeying God and avoiding His disobedience. Ad-Dahhak said: for poverty. Ata’ said: for hunger. Paradise and silk, Al-Hasan said: God admitted them to Paradise and clothed them in silk.
76:13: 13- Reclining, accusative case in state, in it in Paradise, on couches, the beds in the chambers, and there is no couch except when they are gathered together, they will see therein neither sun nor freezing cold, meaning summer nor winter. Muqatil said: He means a sun whose heat will harm them nor freezing cold whose cold will harm them, because both are harmful in this world. And freezing cold is intense cold.
76:14: 14- And its shades are drawn near to them, meaning the shades of its trees are close to them. The accusative of drawn near is in apposition to His statement: reclining, and it was said: in the place of His statement: They will not see therein sun or freezing cold and they will see drawn near, and it was said: in praise, and its fruits are made subservient, subjected and brought near, its harvests, its fruits, in submission, they eat from its fruits standing, sitting and lying down and they take them however they want in whatever condition they are in.
76:15: 15- And there will be passed around among them vessels of silver and cups of crystal.
76:16: 16- Vessels of silver. The commentators said: He meant the whiteness of the silver in the clarity of the vessels, for they are silver in the clarity of glass, and what is inside them can be seen from outside. Al-Kalbi said: God made the vessels of every people from the soil of their land, and the land of Paradise is made of silver, so He made from it vessels from which they would drink. They measured it out, they measured the cup according to the amount of their drink, neither more nor less, meaning the cupbearers and servants who go around to them measured it out for them, then they gave them to drink.
76:17: 17- And they will be given to drink there a cup whose mixture is of ginger, which makes one yearn and delight. Ginger is one of the things the Arabs enjoyed very much, so God promised them that they will be given to drink in Paradise a cup mixed with the ginger of Paradise. Muqatil said: It does not resemble the ginger of this world. Ibn Abbas said: Everything that God mentioned in the Qur’an of what is in Paradise and named has no equivalent in this world. It was said: It is a spring in Paradise from which one can taste the ginger. Qatada said: Those brought near will drink it pure, and it will be mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise.
76:18: 18- A spring therein called Salsabil. Qatada said: A chain led by them that they may direct as they wish. Mujahid said: A very strong flowing stream. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: It was called Salsabil because it flows for them in the roads and in their homes, springing from the base of the throne from the Garden of Eden to the people of Paradise. The drink of Paradise is the coolness of camphor, the taste of ginger, and the fragrance of musk. Al-Zajjaj said: It was called Salsabil because it is extremely smooth, flowing down the throat. The meaning of his statement: It is called is that it is described, because most scholars agree that Salsabil is an adjective, not a noun.
76:19: 19- “And there will circulate among them immortal youths. When you see them, you will think them to be scattered pearls.” Ata’ said: He means the whiteness and beauty of the pearls, and when pearls are scattered from a thread on a carpet, they are more beautiful than those strung together. The interpreters of meanings said: They were likened to scattered pearls because they are scattered in service, so if they were in a row, they would be like strung together.
76:20: 20- And when you see then, meaning if you see with your sight and look with it then, meaning in Paradise, you will see bliss, that is, and a great kingdom, meaning that the lowest of them in status will look at his kingdom from a thousand year’s journey, seeing its farthest point as he sees its lowest point. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: It is that the Messenger of God, the Lord of Glory, from the angels, does not enter upon him except with His permission. And it was said: A kingdom that will never cease.
76:21: 21- Upon them are garments of fine silk. The people of Medina and Hamza read: Upon them with a silent ya and a broken ha, so it is in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is: garments of fine silk. The others read it with the accusative of the ya and the damma of the ha as an adjective, meaning above them, and it is an accusative of circumstance. Green garments of fine silk and brocade. Nafi’ and Hafs read green and brocade in the nominative case in apposition to the garments. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read them in the genitive case. Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr read Khidr in the genitive case and Istabraq in the nominative case. Abu Ja’far and the people of Basra and Ash-Sham read it in its opposite, so the nominative case is an adjective to the garments and the genitive case is an adjective to the fine silk and Istabraq in the nominative case because it is in apposition to and garments of fine silk. So the nominative case was deleted and the nominative case was replaced by the nominative case, like his saying: And ask the village, meaning the people of the village. Similar to that is his saying: Khaz, meaning a garment of fine silk. As for the genitive case of istabraq, it is in apposition to sandas, which is genitive by adding clothes to it. They are two types of clothes to which clothes are added, just as you say: a garment of silk and linen, so you add it to the two types. And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink. It was said: pure from filth and dirt, not defiled by hands and feet like the wine of this world. Abu Qilabah and Ibrahim said: It does not become impure urine, but it becomes a secretion in their bodies, its smell like the smell of musk. This is because they are given food, and at the end of that, they are given pure drink, which they drink and purifies their stomachs, and what they have eaten becomes a secretion that comes out of their skins with a smell better than the most fragrant musk. Their stomachs shrink and their desire returns. Muqatil said: It is a spring of water at the gate of Paradise. Whoever drinks from it, God will remove from his heart any rancor, deceit, and envy.
76:22: 22- This was indeed your reward, and your effort was appreciated. That is, what was described of the bliss of Paradise was your reward for your deeds, and your effort, your work in this world in obedience to God, was appreciated. Ata’ said: You were thanked for it, so He rewarded you with the best reward.
76:23: God Almighty said: 23- Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur’an to you gradually. Ibn Abbas said: It was sent down, verse by verse, and it was not sent down all at once.
76:24: 24- So be patient over the decision of your Lord and do not obey from them, meaning from the polytheists of Mecca, a sinner or an ingrate, meaning an ingrate, and the alif is a connection. Qatada said: By the sinful ungrateful he meant Abu Jahl. This is because when prayer was made obligatory upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Jahl forbade him from it and said: If I see Muhammad praying, I will step on his neck. Muqatil said: By the sinner he meant Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, and by the ungrateful he meant Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughirah. They said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you did what you did for the sake of women and money, then reconsider this matter. Utbah said: Then I will marry my daughter to you and bring her to you without a dowry. Al-Walid said: I will give you money until you are satisfied, so reconsider this matter. Then God revealed this verse.
76:25: God Almighty says: 25- And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening.
76:26: 26- And during part of the night prostrate to Him, meaning the Maghrib and Isha prayers, and glorify Him for a long time during the night, meaning the voluntary prayers after the obligatory prayers.
76:27: 27- These, meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, love the immediate, meaning the immediate abode, which is this world. And they leave behind them, meaning before them, a heavy Day, which is a severe one, which is the Day of Resurrection. That is, they abandon it, so they do not believe in it or work for it.
76:28: 28- We created them and strengthened them, We strengthened and perfected their families. Mujahid, Qatadah, and Muqatil said: their families means: We created them. It is said: a man of good families, meaning: creation. Al-Hasan said: It means their connections to one another through veins and nerves. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid in his interpretation of Al-Usr that he said: The anus means the place where urine and feces drain. When the impurity comes out, they contract. And if We will, We can replace them with others like them, meaning: If We will, We can destroy them and bring others like them, making them their replacements.
76:29: 29- Indeed, this, meaning this Surah, is a reminder, a reminder and an admonition, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way, a means through obedience.
76:30: 30- And whatever you will, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Abu Amr read: they will with a ya, and the others read it with a ta, “except that God wills,” meaning you will not will except by the will of God Almighty, because the matter is up to Him, Indeed, God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
76:31: 31- He admits whom He wills into His mercy, but the wrongdoers, meaning the polytheists, He has prepared for them a painful punishment.
77:1: 1- And the winds sent forth in gusts, meaning the winds sent forth in succession like the mane of a horse. It was also said: in gusts means in abundance. The Arabs say: People are heading to so-and-so in one gust, if they head towards him in large numbers. This is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid and Qatadah. Muqatil said: It means the angels who are sent with what is good of God’s commands and prohibitions, and this is the narration of Masruq on the authority of Ibn Masoud.
77:3: 3- And the spreaders spreading, meaning the gentle winds. Al-Hasan said: They are the winds that God sends as good tidings before His mercy. It was also said: They are the winds that spread the clouds and bring rain. Muqatil said: They are the angels who spread the books.
77:4: 4- The distinguishing verses, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ad-Dahhak said: It means the angels who come with what distinguishes between truth and falsehood. Qatada and Al-Hasan said: They are the verses of the Qur’an that distinguish between what is lawful and what is unlawful. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: They are the winds that disperse the clouds and scatter them.
77:5: 5- And those who cast down the Reminder, meaning the angels who cast down the Reminder to the prophets, similar to: He casts down the Spirit by His command (Ghafir 40:15).
77:6: 6- Udhran or nadhran, meaning for excuse and warning. Al-Hasan read Udhran with a dhammah on the dhal, and there was a difference of opinion about it from Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim. The general reading is with a sukoon on it. Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read Udhran or nadhran with a sukoon on the dhal in both of them. The rest read it with a dhammah. Whoever read it with a sukoon said: because they are in the position of two sources meaning warning and excuse, and they are not plural, so they transfer it. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Ibn Amir, and Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim and Ya'qub, according to the narration of Rawis bin Hassan: Udhran with a sukoon on the dhal, and nadhran with a dhammah on the dhal. Ruh read with a dhammah in both of them, and it is the reading of Al-Hasan. The face in them is that the excuse and the vow with two dhammahs like the ear and the neck is the original, and it is permissible to lighten them as it is permissible to lighten them in the neck and the ear. It is said: Udhran and nadhran, and Udhran and nadhran, just as it is said: neck and neck, and ear and ear, and the excuse The vowel is two sources meaning excuse and warning, like nakir, ‘udheer, and nadheer. It is possible that they are the plurals of ‘udheer and nadheer, and it is possible that ‘udhre’ is the plural of ‘adheer, like sharif and sharaf. The meaning in terms of movement and stillness is the same, as we have explained here in sections.
77:7: He mentioned it based on his statement: 7- You are promised, of the matter of the Hour and the Resurrection, that will happen, that will be, then he mentioned when it will happen.
77:8: He said 8- Then when the stars are extinguished, their light is erased.
77:9: 9- And when the sky is split open, split.
77:10: 10- And when the mountains are blown away, uprooted from their places.
77:11: 11- And when the messengers are gathered together The people of Basra read waqtat with a waw, Abu Jaafar read it with a waw and a soft qaf, and the others read it with an alif and a double qaf, and these are two dialects. The Arabs alternate between the waw and the hamza, as in their saying: wa-kadda and wa-ak-da, and warakht and arakht, and their meanings are: they were gathered for the appointed time on a known day, which is the Day of Resurrection, to bear witness against the nations.
77:12: 12- For what day have you been postponed? That is, you have been brought out. The deadline was set for their gathering, so the servants were amazed at that day.
77:13: Then he explained and said: 13- On the Day of Judgment. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The day on which the Most Merciful, the Almighty, will judge between the creation.
77:14: 14- And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
77:15: 15- Woe, that Day, to the deniers.God
77:16: 16- Did We not destroy the former peoples? meaning the past nations with punishment in this world when they denied their messengers.God
77:17: 17- Then We will make others follow them, those who follow their paths of disbelief and denial, meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, who denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.God
77:18: 18- This is how We deal with the criminals.God
77:20: 20- Did We not create you from a despised water? meaning sperm.
77:21: 21- So We placed him in a secure lodging, meaning the womb.
77:22: 22- To a known time, which is the time of birth.
77:23: 23- Faqadrana", the people of Medina and Al-Kisa'i read: "Faqadrana with emphasis from the word taqdir, and the others read it with a light emphasis from the word qudrah", based on His saying: "Then the best of the able ones", and it was said: their meaning is the same, and His saying: "Then the best of the able ones means the able ones.
77:25: 25- Have We not made the earth a receptacle? A container. The meaning of kaft is to gather and collect. It is said: Kaft something means to gather and collect it. Al-Farra’ said: He means to gather them alive on its back in their homes and dwellings, and to gather them dead in its belly, meaning: to contain them.
77:27: 27- And We placed therein firm mountains, “high,” and We gave you to drink sweet water, fresh water.
77:28: 28- Woe, that Day, to the deniers. Muqatil said: All of this is more amazing than the resurrection.
77:29: Then he told them that it will be said to them on the Day of Resurrection: 29- Go to what you used to deny, in this world.
77:30: 30- Go to a shade with three branches, meaning the smoke of Hell, which when it rises, branches out and separates into three groups. It was also said: A neck will emerge from the fire and branch out into three branches. As for the light, it will stop on the heads of the believers, the smoke will stop on the heads of the hypocrites, and the pure flame will stop on the heads of the disbelievers.
77:31: Then He described that shade, saying, the Almighty and Majestic: 31- No shade that provides shade from the heat, nor does it protect against the flame. Al-Kalbi said: It does not ward off the flames of Hell from you, and the meaning is that if they seek shade from that shade, it will not ward off the heat of the flames from them.
77:32: 32- It, meaning Hell, throws sparks, which are what fly from the fire, the singular of which is spark. Like a palace, which is a huge building. Ibn Masoud said: It means fortresses. Abdul Rahman bin Ayyash said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the Almighty’s saying: It throws out sparks like castles. He said: They are large pieces of wood that have been cut into pieces. We used to take wood and cut it into pieces of three cubits or more or less than that and save it for the winter, so we used to call it castles. Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Dahhak said: They are the roots of palm trees and large trees, and the singular is Qasra, like Tamra and Tamr, Jamra and Jamr. Ali and Ibn Abbas read like the palace with the opening of the sad, meaning the necks of palm trees, and the qasra is the neck, and its plural is qasr and qasrat.
77:33: 33- As if he returned the metaphor to the word, jamala. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read: jamala for all camels, like stone and stones. Ya'qub read it with a damma on the jim without an alif, meaning: the large things gathered together. The others read: jamalat with an alif and a kasra on the jim as the plural of camels. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and Sa'id bin Jubayr said: they are the ropes of ships gathered together, until they are like the waists of men. Safar, the plural of yellow, means the color of fire. It was said that yellow means black, because it was mentioned in the hadith that the sparks of the fire of Hell are black like tar. The Arabs call the black camels yellow because their blackness is tinged with some yellow, just as the whites of gazelles are called adam because their whiteness is covered with a turbidity.
77:34: 34- Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:35: 35- This is a Day when they will not speak. On the Day of Resurrection there are situations. On some occasions they will dispute and speak, and on others their mouths will be sealed so they will not speak.
77:36: 36- And they will not be given permission to make excuses. The subject is in apposition to his statement: they will be given permission. Al-Junayd said: That is, there is no excuse for the one who turns away from his benefactor and is ungrateful for his favors and blessings.
77:37: 37- Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:38: 38- This is the Day of Judgment, between the people of Paradise and Hell, We have gathered you and the former peoples, meaning the deniers of this nation and the former peoples who denied their prophets.
77:39: 39- If you have a plan, then plan it. Muqatil said: If you have a plan, then plan it for yourselves.
77:40: 40- Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:41: 41- Indeed, the righteous will be in shades, plural of shade, meaning in the shade of trees, and springs, of water.
77:42: 42- And fruits of whatever they desire.
77:43: And it will be said to them: 43- Eat and drink in happiness for what you used to do, in this world by obeying Me.
77:44: 44- Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
77:45: 45- Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:46: Then he said to the infidels of Mecca: 46- Eat and enjoy yourselves a little, in this world, for you are criminals, associating partners with God Almighty and deserving of punishment.
77:47: 47- Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:48: 48- And when it is said to them, ‘Bow down,’ they do not bow down, they do not pray. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: This will only be said to them on the Day of Resurrection when they are called to prostrate but they are unable to.
77:49: 49- Woe, that Day, to the deniers.
77:50: 50- So in what statement after it after the Qur’an, will they believe, if they do not believe in it.
78:1: 1- "Amma", its root is: about what, so the letter "nun was assimilated into the letter mim and the letter alif of ma" was deleted, like in saying: "fi-ma, and bi-ma? Yatasa'aloon", meaning: about what are these polytheists asking? That is because when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called them to monotheism and informed them of the resurrection after death, and recited the Quran to them, they began to ask each other: What did Muhammad bring? Al-Zajjaj said: The word is an interrogative word and its meaning is glorification, as you say: What is Zayd's thing? If you magnify his matter and status.
78:2: Then he mentioned that their question was about what, so he said: 2- About the great report. Mujahid and the majority said: It is the Qur’an. His evidence is His statement: “Say: It is a great report” (p. 67). Qatada said: It is the resurrection.
78:3: 3- In which they differ, so there is a believer and a denier.
78:4: 4- No, they will know. “No” is a negation of their statement, they will know is a consequence when matters are revealed.
78:5: 5- Then both of them will know, a warning to them following a warning. Ad-Dahhak said: Then both of them will know means the disbelievers, Then both of them will know means the believers.
78:6: Then he mentioned his deeds so that they would know his oneness, so he said: 6- Have We not made the earth a bed?
78:7: 7- And the mountains as pegs, for the earth so that it does not shake.
78:8: 8- And We created you in pairs, males and females.
78:9: 9- And We have made your sleep a rest, meaning rest for your bodies. Al-Zajjaj said: Sleep means to be cut off from movement and spirit. It was also said that its meaning is that We have made your sleep an end to your deeds, because the root of the word sabt is to cut off.
78:10: 10- And We made the night a covering, a covering and a membrane that covers everything with its darkness.
78:11: 11- And We have made the day for livelihood. Livelihood means living, and everything that is lived in it is livelihood. That is, We made the day a means of livelihood and disposing of interests. Ibn Abbas said: He means: that you seek in it from the bounty of God, and what He has allotted you of His provisions.
78:12: 12- And We built above you seven strong heavens, meaning seven heavens.
78:13: 13- And We made a lamp, meaning the sun, brilliant, luminous and illuminating. Al-Zajjaj said: Bright means lighter. Muqatil said: He placed light and heat in it, and bright combines light and heat.
78:14: 14- And We sent down from the pressed clouds, Mujahid, Qatada, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: It means the winds that squeeze the clouds, and this is the narration of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Azhari said: They are hurricane winds. According to this interpretation, min has the meaning of ba, meaning with the hurricanes, because the wind brings rain. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi’ and Al-Dahhak said: The mu’asarat are the clouds, and this is the narration of Al-Walabi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Farra’ said: The mu’asarat are the clouds that are milked with rain but do not rain, like the mu’asarat woman who is close to her period but has not yet menstruated. Ibn Kaysan said: They are the ones who help, from his saying: In it people are helped and in it they press. Al-Hasan, Saeed bin Jubair, Zaid bin Aslam, and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: From the pressed waters means from the heavens. Pour-down water, meaning pouring down. Mujahid said: profusely. Qatada said: continuous, one part following the other. Ibn Zayd said: a lot.
78:15: 15- To bring forth with it, meaning with that water, grain, which is what people eat, and vegetation, which is what the earth grows that livestock eat.
78:16: 16- Gardens wrapped around surrounded by trees, the singular of which is laf and lafif, and it was said: it is the plural of the plural, it is said: a garden wrapped around, and its plural is laf, with a damma on the lam, and the plural of the plural is alif.
78:17: 17- The Day of Judgment, the Day of Judgment between creation, is a time appointed, for what God Almighty has promised of reward and punishment.
78:18: 18- The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come in droves, in groups, from every place, for the reckoning.
78:19: 19- And the heaven was opened. The people of Kufa read it as opened with a light pronunciation, while others read it with a heavy pronunciation, meaning it was split open for the angels to descend. And it became doors, meaning with doors. It was also said that it dissolved and scattered until it had doors and paths.
78:20: 20- And the mountains will move, from the face of the earth, and will become a mirage, that is, scattered dust to the eye of the observer like a mirage.
78:21: 21- Indeed, Hell is lying in wait, a path and a passage, so no one has a path except to Paradise until he crosses the Fire. It was said: It was an ambush, meaning: prepared for them. It is said: I prepared something for him if I prepared it for him. It was said: It is from the verb rasadat to watch something if you watch it. Marsad is the place where the observer watches the enemy. His statement: Indeed, Hell was an ambush, meaning it watches the disbelievers. Muqsam narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: There are seven prisons on the bridge of Hell. At the first, the servant will be asked about the testimony that there is no god but God. If he answers it completely, he will pass to the second. He will be asked about prayer. If he answers it completely, he will pass to the third. He will be asked about zakat. If he answers it completely, he will pass to the fourth. He will be asked about fasting. If he does it completely, he will pass to the fifth. He will be asked about Hajj. If he does it completely, he will pass to the sixth. He will be asked about Umrah. If he answers it completely, he will pass to the seventh. He will be asked about injustices. If he leaves them, well and good. Otherwise, it will be said: Look. If he has voluntary prayers, he will complete his deeds with them. When he finishes them, he will be taken to Paradise.
78:22: 22- For the transgressors, for the disbelievers, a place of return, a reference to which they will return.
78:23: 23- Labtheen, Hamza and Ya'qub read it: Labtheen without an alif, and the common people read it: Labtheen with an alif, and they are two dialects. In it, ahqaban, plural of haqb, and one haqb is eighty years, each year is twelve months, each month is thirty days, each day is a thousand years. This was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Mujahed said: The epochs are forty-three epochs, each epoch is seventy autumns, each autumn is seven hundred years, each year is three hundred and sixty days, each day is a thousand years. Al-Hasan said: God did not set a period for the people of Hellfire, but rather said: They will abide therein for ages. By God, when an age passes, another one enters, then another, forever. So the ages have no number except eternity. Al-Suddi narrated on the authority of Marra on the authority of Abdullah who said: If the people of Hell knew that they would remain in Hell the number of pebbles in this world, they would rejoice, and if the people of Paradise knew that they would remain in Paradise the number of pebbles in this world, they would be sad. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: One era is seventeen thousand years. He said: This verse has been abrogated. It was abrogated by We will not increase you except in torment, meaning that the number has increased and eternity has been achieved.
78:24: 24- They will not taste therein any coolness or drink. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the coolness is sleep. Al-Kisa’i said something similar, and Abu Ubaidah said, the Arabs say: The coolness prevented the coolness, meaning the coolness took away sleep. Al-Hasan and Ata’ said: They will not taste therein any coolness, meaning: a spirit and comfort. Muqatil said: They will not taste therein any coolness, that will benefit them from the heat, nor any drink, that will benefit them from thirst. 24- They will not taste therein any coolness or drink. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the coolness is sleep. Al-Kisa’i said something similar, and Abu Ubaidah said, the Arabs say: The coolness prevented the coolness, meaning the coolness took away sleep. Al-Hasan and Ata’ said: They will not taste therein any coolness, meaning: a spirit and comfort. Muqatil said: They will not taste therein any coolness, that will benefit them from the heat, nor any drink, that will benefit them from thirst.
78:25: 25- Except scalding water and pus. Ibn Abbas said: Pus is the freezing cold that burns them with its cold. It was also said: The pus of the people of Hellfire, and we have mentioned it in Surat Sad. 25- Except scalding water and pus. Ibn Abbas said: Pus is the freezing cold that burns them with its cold. It was also said: The pus of the people of Hellfire, and we have mentioned it in Surat Sad.
78:26: 26- A fitting recompense, meaning We rewarded them with a recompense that matched their deeds. Muqatil said: The punishment matched the sin, for there is no sin greater than polytheism, and no punishment greater than Hellfire.
78:27: 27- They did not expect an account, they did not fear being held accountable, meaning: they did not believe in resurrection or that they would be held accountable.
78:28: 28- And they denied Our signs, meaning what the prophets brought, falsely, denial. Al-Farra’ said: It is an eloquent Yemeni language. They say in the source of the verb fa’al “fa’al.” He said: An Arab among them said to me on Al-Marwah, asking me a fatwa: Is shaving your hair or cutting it short more preferable to you?
78:29: 29- And everything We have recorded in a book, meaning, and every action We have made clear in the Preserved Tablet, as He says: And everything We have recorded in a clear register (Ya-Sin 36:12).
78:30: 30- So taste, meaning it will be said to them: So taste, “for We will not increase you except in torment.”
78:31: God Almighty says: 31- Indeed, for the righteous is attainment, victory and salvation from the Fire. Ad-Dahhak said: a place of rest.
78:32: 32- Gardens and grapes, meaning the trees and fruits of Paradise.
78:33: 33- And young maidens, female slaves with round breasts, singular is ka’ib, of equal age, of the same age.
78:34: 34- And a full cup. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said: Overflowing and brimming. Saeed bin Jubair and Mujahid said: Continuous. Ikrimah said: Clear.
78:35: 35- They will not hear therein idle talk, meaning false speech, nor lying, meaning they will not lie to one another. Al-Kisa’i read liar with a light kadh-haban as a verbal noun from kadh-hab like mukadh-haba, and it was said that it means lying. And say that it has the same meaning as tak-hab, like mush-daddah.
78:36: 36- A reward from your Lord, a gift according to account. That is, He rewarded them and gave them a gift according to account. That is, sufficient and comprehensive. It is said: I considered so-and-so, meaning I gave him what was sufficient for him until he said, It is sufficient for me. Ibn Qutaybah said: A gift according to account means a lot. It was also said: It is a reward according to the extent of their deeds.
78:37: 37- Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Gracious. The people of Hijaz and Abu Amr read: Lord in the nominative case as a new sentence and the Most Gracious is its predicate. The others read it in the accusative case following the statement: From your Lord. Ibn Amir, Asim, and Ya'qub read: the Most Gracious in the accusative case following the statement: Lord of the heavens. The others read it in the nominative case. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read Lord in the genitive case because it is close to the statement: A reward from your Lord. They read the Most Gracious in the nominative case because it is far from it as a new sentence. The statement: They do not possess is in the nominative case as its predicate. Meaning: They do not possess any power to speak to Him. Muqatil said: Creation is not able to speak to God except with His permission. Al-Kalbi said: They do not possess any power to intercede except with His permission.
78:39: 39- That is the true Day, the real and actual Day of Resurrection, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way of return, a reference and a path through his obedience to Him, meaning: whoever wills may return to God through his obedience.
78:40: 40- Indeed, We have warned you of an imminent torment, meaning the torment in the Hereafter, and everything that is coming is imminent. On the Day when a man will see what his hands have put forth, meaning every person will see on that day the deeds he has done recorded in his record, and the disbeliever will say, ‘Oh, I wish I were dust.’ Abdullah ibn Amr said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be spread out like a hide, and the beasts, livestock, and wild animals will be gathered together. Then retribution will be decided among the animals until the hornless sheep takes retribution from the horned sheep that butted it. When the retribution is finished, it will be said to it: Become dust. At that time, the unbeliever will say: I wish I were dust. A similar narration was reported from Mujahid. Muqatil said: God will gather the wild beasts, vermin, and birds and judge between them until He takes revenge for the horned ones from the horned ones. Then He will say to them: I created you and made you subservient to the children of Adam, and you were obedient to them during the days of your lives, so return to what you were, and become dust. Then if the disbeliever looks at something that has become dust, he will wish and say: I wish I had been in the world in the form of a pig, and today I was dust. On the authority of Abu Al-Zinad Abdullah bin Dhakwan, who said: When God decides between Hell and the people of Paradise, He will send them to Paradise and the people of Hell to Hell, and it will be said to the rest of the nations and the believing jinn, Return to dust, and they will return to dust, then the unbeliever will say, Oh, I wish I were dust. Layth bin Abi Sulaym said the same: The believing jinn will return to dust. It was said: The disbeliever here is Satan, because he criticized Adam for being created from dust and boasted that he was created from fire. So when he sees on the Day of Resurrection what Adam and his believing sons had of reward and mercy, and what he will have of hardship and torment, he will say: I wish I were dust. Abu Hurairah said: Dust will say: No, and there is no honor for you. Who made you like me?
79:1: 1- And those who extract the souls by drowning, meaning the angels extract the souls of the unbelievers from their bodies, just as the one who extracts the bow drowns it, reaching the maximum extension after he has extracted it, until when it is about to come out, he returns it to his body. This is His action with the unbeliever, and drowning is a name that is used in place of immersion, i.e., and those who extract the souls by drowning, and what is meant by drowning is exaggeration in the extension. Ibn Masoud said: The Angel of Death and his helpers pull it out from under every hair, from the nails, and from the roots of the feet. They return it to his body after pulling it out, until it is about to come out. Then they return it to his body without pulling it out. This is his action with the infidels. Muqatil said: The Angel of Death and his helpers extract the souls of the infidels as a skewer with many threads extracts wet wool, and his soul emerges like a drowning person in water. Mujahed said: It is death that takes away the souls. Al-Suddi said: It is the soul when it sinks in the chest. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ibn Kaysan said: They are the stars that move from one horizon to another, rising and then setting. Ata’ and Ikrimah said: They are the bows. It was also said: They are the archers of the war.
79:2: 2- And the active ones actively, are the angels who activate the soul of the believer, that is, they loosen it gently and seize it, as the rope is loosened from the camel’s hand, that is, it is loosened gently. Al-Farra’ narrated this saying, then he said: What I heard from the Arabs is that they say: I loosened the rope, if you loosened it, and I tied it with a noose. And in the hadith: As if he was freed from a rope. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is the soul of the believer who is eager to go out at death, because of the honor he sees, as Paradise is offered to him before he dies. Ali bin Abi Talib said: They are the angels who stir the souls of the infidels from between the skin and nails until they expel them from their mouths with distress and grief. Nasht means pulling and pulling. It is said: I stirred the bucket nasht if I pulled it out. Al-Khalil said: Nasht and inshitāt are pushing something towards yourself until it dissolves. Mujahed said: It is death that invigorates the souls. Al-Suddi said: It is the soul that is invigorated from the feet, i.e., it is drawn. Qatada said: It is the stars that are active from horizon to horizon, i.e., it goes. It is said: He is active from country to country, if he goes out quickly. It is also said: An active donkey, that is, he is active from country to country. Ata’ and Ikrimah said: It is the shackles.
79:3: 3- And those who swim in the water, they are the angels who take the souls of the believers and gently ask them, then they call them to rest like someone who swims with something in the water and is gentle with it. Mujahid and Abu Saleh said: They are the angels who descend from the sky, hurrying like a fast horse. It is called sabih if it runs quickly. It was said: They are the horses of the invaders. Qatada said: They are the stars, the sun, and the moon. God Almighty said: Each one floats in an orbit (al-Anbiya 21:33). Ata' said: They are the ships.
79:4: 4- The ones who are the first to precede others in goodness and righteous deeds. Mujahid said: They are the angels who precede the son of Adam in goodness and righteous deeds. Muqatil said: They are the angels who precede the souls of the believers to Paradise. On the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: They are the souls of the believers who precede the angels who take them, longing to meet God and be honored by Him, and they have witnessed the joy. Qatada said: They are the stars that precede each other in the sky. Ata’ said: They are the horses.
79:5: 5- Those who manage affairs, Ibn Abbas said: They are the angels who were entrusted with matters that God Almighty made known to them how to work on. Abdul Rahman bin Sabit said: Four people manage the affairs of this world: Gabriel, Michael, the Angel of Death, and Israfil, peace be upon them. As for Gabriel, he is in charge of the wind and the soldiers. As for Michael, he is in charge of the rain and the plants. As for the Angel of Death, he is in charge of taking the souls. As for Israfil, he descends with the command to them. The answer to these sections is omitted, based on the estimation: You will be resurrected and held accountable. It was said: His answer is his saying: Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears. It was said: It contains an inversion, meaning: On the day the violent earthquake shakes, followed by the subsequent earthquake and the storms that pull out the winds, drowning.
79:6: God Almighty says: 6- The Day the Earth shakes with a mighty earthquake, meaning the first blast, when everything will shake and move, and all of creation will die.
79:7: 7- The second blast will follow it, which is the second blast that follows the first, and there will be forty years between them. Qatada said: They are two shouts. The first one kills everything, and the other one revives everything, by the permission of God Almighty. Mujahed said: The earthquake shakes and the earth and mountains quake, followed by the second earthquake when the sky splits and the earth and mountains are carried and crushed with a single crushing.
