Ata' said: "Al-Rajfah means the Resurrection and Al-Radfah" means the Resurrection. The root of "Rajfah" is sound and movement. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told me, Abdullah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik told us, Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami told us, al-Hasan ibn Arfa told us, Qubaysah ibn Uqbah told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Uqayl, on the authority of al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka’b, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, who said: “When a quarter of the night had passed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would get up and say: ‘O people, remember God, remember God. The first earthquake has come, followed by the second. Death has come with what it contains. Death has come with what it contains.’”
79:8: 8- The hearts that Day will be trembling, fearful, anxious, and agitated. It is called al-wajif in travel, due to its intense agitation. It is said: The heart became dry, and became filled with terror, and became filled with terror, and became filled with terror, and became filled with a sense of obligation. Mujahid said: Fearful. Al-Suddi said: Moving from their places, similar to When the hearts are at the throats (Ghafir 40:18).
79:9: 9- Their eyes will be humbled, submissive, as He says: Humbled by humiliation (al-Shura 42:45).
79:10: 10- They say, meaning those who deny the resurrection, when it is said to them that they will be resurrected after death: Shall we then be returned to the grave? That is, to the original state and beginning of the matter, so that we become alive after death as we were. The Arabs say: So-and-so returned to his grave, meaning he returned from where he came. The grave, to them, is a name for the beginning of something, and the first of something. Some of them said: Al-Hafrah is the surface of the earth in which their graves are dug. It is called Hafrah in the sense of the dug place, like his saying: A satisfied life, meaning a pleasing one. It was said: It was called Hafirah because it is the place where hooves rest, meaning, will we be returned to the earth and then resurrected as a new creation to walk on it? Ibn Zayd said: Al-Hafrah is the fire.
79:11: 11- "Shall we then be decayed bones?" Nafi', Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read: "Shall we then?" as a question, if by leaving it out, Abu Ja'far is the opposite, the rest with their question, and Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Amr read: decayed bones, and the others read "Nakhrah" and they are two dialects, like greed and greed and caution and caution, and their meaning is worn out, and some people differentiated between them, and said: Al-Nakhrah is worn out, and Al-Nakhrah is the hollow in which the wind passes and decays, meaning: it makes a sound.
79:12: 12- They said, meaning the deniers: That then is a losing return, a failed return, meaning that if we are returned after death, we will lose because of what will befall us after death.
79:13: God Almighty said: 13- It is only, meaning the last blast, a single blast, a shout, that they will hear.
79:14: 14- "And suddenly they are on the surface of the earth", meaning: the face of the earth, i.e. they are on the surface of the earth after having been in its interior. The Arabs call the desert and the surface of the earth: Sahira. Some linguists said: You will see them calling it Sahira because it is where animals sleep and they stay awake. Sufyan said: It is the land of Ash-Sham. Qatada said: It is Hell.
79:15: God Almighty says: 15- Has the story of Moses reached you? He says: O Muhammad, the story of Moses has reached you.
79:16: 16- When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
79:17: He said, O Moses: 17- Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. He was arrogant, haughty, and disbelieved in God.
79:18: 18- Say, ‘Would you like to be purified?’ The people of Hijaz and Jacob read it with emphasis on the zay: meaning purify yourself and cleanse yourself from polytheism. The others read it with emphasis, and its original form is tatzakka, so the second ta’ was assimilated into the zay in the first reading, and was deleted in the second. Its meaning is purify yourself from polytheism, meaning submit and reform. Ibn Abbas said: testify that there is no god but God.
79:19: 19- And I guide you to your Lord so that you may fear Him, meaning: I call you to worship your Lord and to believe in His Oneness so that you may fear His punishment.
79:20: 20 So he showed him the greatest sign, which was the staff and the white hand.
79:21: 21- He denied, that they were from God, and disobeyed.
79:22: 22- Then he turned away, he turned away and turned away from the faith, strives, he works corruption on earth.
79:23: 23- So he gathered, so he gathered his people and soldiers, and he called out, when they had gathered.
79:24: 24- He said, 'I am your highest lord.' There is no lord above me. It was said that he meant that the idols are lords and I am your lord and their lord.
79:25: 25- So God punished him with the punishment of the Hereafter and of this world. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: God punished him and made him the punishment of the Hereafter and of this world, meaning in this world by drowning and in the Hereafter by fire. Mujahid and a group of commentators said: By the last and the first, he meant the words of Pharaoh: I have not known for you any god other than me (al-Qasas 28:38), and his saying: I am your highest Lord, and there were forty years between them.
79:26: 26- Indeed in that, what was done to Pharaoh when he lied and disobeyed, is a lesson, a sermon, for whoever fears, God Almighty.
79:27: Then He addressed those who denied the resurrection, saying: 27- Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? Meaning: Is your creation after death more difficult in your opinion and estimation, or is the heaven? And they are one in the power of God, as He says: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind (Ghafir 40:57). Then He described the creation of the heaven, saying: He constructed it.
79:28: 28- He raised its thickness, its roof and leveled it, without any cracks, fissures or fractures.
79:29: 29- And He covered, made dark, its night, and covering and ghubbish are darkness, and brought forth its morning, made its day and light prominent and apparent, and He added them to the sky because both darkness and light descend from the sky.
79:30: 30- And the earth after that, after creating the heavens, He spread it out, extended it. Spreading out means spreading out. Ibn Abbas said: God created the earth with its sustenance without spreading it out before the heavens, then He turned to the heavens and made them seven heavens, then He spread out the earth after that. It was said: Its meaning is: And the earth was spread out in spite of that, as God Almighty said: And he became a tyrant after that (al-Qalam 68:13), meaning in spite of that.
79:31: 31- He brought forth from it its water and its pasture.
79:32: 32- And the mountains He has fixed firmly.
79:33: 33- For your enjoyment and for your livestock.
79:34: 34- Then when the Great Calamity comes, meaning the second blast in which the resurrection will take place and the Day of Resurrection will take place. The Day of Resurrection is called a calamity because it overwhelms every terrible matter, rising above it and submerging everything else. The Calamity among the Arabs means the catastrophe that cannot be controlled.
79:35: 35- The Day when man will remember what he strove for, what good and evil he did in this world.
79:36: 36- And Hell will be made visible to all who see, Muqatil said, Its cover will be removed so that people can see it.
79:37: 37- But as for he who transgressed, in his disbelief.
79:38: 38- And he preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter.
79:40: 40- But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from desire, from the forbidden things that it desires, Muqatil said: He is the man who intends to commit a sin, then he remembers his position for the reckoning and abandons it.
79:41: 41- For Paradise is the abode. 42- “They ask you about the Hour: when will it come?” When will it appear and be established?
79:43: 43- What do you have to do with her memory? You have nothing to do with her knowledge or her memory, meaning you do not know her.
79:44: 44- To your Lord is its destination, meaning the ultimate knowledge of it is with God.
79:45: 45- You are only a warner for those who fear it. Abu Ja`far read: warner with the tanween, meaning you are only a warner for those who fear its occurrence, meaning: your warning is only beneficial for those who fear it.
79:46: 46- As if they, meaning the infidels of Quraysh, on the Day they see it, witness the Day of Resurrection, had not remained, in this world, and it was said: in their graves, except for an evening or a morning thereof. Al-Farra’ said: There is no morning there for the evening, rather the morning thereof is for the beginning of the day, but this is apparent from the speech of the Arabs, that they say: I will come to you in the evening or the morning thereof, but its meaning is: the last day or the beginning of it, similar to his saying: As if they, on the Day they see what they are promised, had not remained except for an hour of a day Al-Ahqaf - 35.
80:1: 1- He frowned, he looked grimly, and turned away, he turned his face away.
80:2: 2- That the blind man came to him, meaning: because the blind man came to him, and he is Ibn Umm Maktum, and his name is Abdullah bin Shuraih bin Malik bin Rabi’ah Al-Fihri from Banu Amir bin Lu’ay, and that is because “he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was conversing with Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, Ubayy bin Khalaf, and his brother Umayyah, calling them to God, hoping for their conversion to Islam, so Ibn Umm Maktum said: O Messenger of God, recite to me and teach me from what God has taught you, so he kept calling him and repeating the call, not knowing that he was turning to someone else until hatred appeared on the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for interrupting his speech, and he said to himself: These leaders say: His followers are only the blind, the slaves, and the lowly, so his face frowned and he turned away from him, and turned to the people he was speaking to, so God revealed these verses, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after that used to honor him, and if he saw him He said: Welcome to the one about whom my Lord has rebuked me, and to whom He says: Do you have a need? And He appointed him as His deputy over Medina twice during two battles that he participated in. Anas bin Malik said: I saw him on the day of Al-Qadisiyyah wearing a suit of armor and holding a black banner.
80:3: 3- And what do you know? Perhaps he will be purified. He will be purified from sins through good deeds and what he learns from you. Ibn Zayd said: He will be safe.
80:4: 4- Or he remembers, he is admonished, so the remembrance benefits him, the admonition. Asim read: so it benefits him with the accusative of the 'ayn as an answer to perhaps with the letter fa, and the general reading is with the nominative in accordance with his saying: he remembers.
80:5: 5- As for he who is self-sufficient, Ibn Abbas said: from God and from faith, with his wealth.
80:6: 6- So you turn to him, you expose yourself to him, accept him, and listen to his words. The people of Hijaz read: Tasada with emphasis on the sad due to assimilation, meaning: you turn to him, and the others read it with a light sad due to deletion.
80:7: 7- And it is not your fault that he does not purify himself, that is, that he does not believe or find guidance. Your fault is only to convey the message.
80:8: 8- And as for he who comes to you running, walking means: Ibn Umm Kulthum.
80:10: 10- You are distracted from it, you are busy and turn away from it.
80:11: 11- "No, a warning, meaning do not do the same after that, it" means this sermon. Muqatil said: The verses of the Qur'an are "a reminder, a sermon and a reminder to mankind.
80:12: 12- Whoever wills, of God’s servants, may remember it, meaning, take heed of it. Muqatil said: Whoever God wills may remember it and understand it, and take heed of His will and His making it understood. The ha in may remember it refers to the Qur’an, the revelation, and the preaching.
80:13: Then He spoke about His majesty with Him, saying: 13- In honored scrolls, meaning the Preserved Tablet. It was also said: The books of the prophets, peace be upon them, as evidenced by the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, * The scriptures of Abraham and Moses (al-A’la 87:18-19).
80:14: 14- Exalted, of high status with God Almighty. It was also said that exalted means in the seventh heaven. Purified, of which only the purified ones, who are the angels, may touch it.
80:15: 15- In the hands of scribes, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: scribes, and they are the honorable recording angels, and one of them is a safir, it is said: safrat, meaning I wrote. And from this, the word scribe is safir, and the word katab is safir, and the plural is asfar. Others said: They are the messengers from the angels, and one of them is an ambassador, which is the messenger, and the ambassador of the people is the one who seeks to reconcile them, and you travel between the people if you reconcile between them.
80:16: Then he praised them and said: 16- Noble and pious, meaning: noble in the sight of God, pious/obedient, plural of righteous.
80:17: God Almighty said: 17- Killing a human being, meaning cursing the disbeliever. Muqatil said: How ungrateful he is was revealed about Utbah ibn Abi Lahab. How intensely he disbelieved in God despite the many favors and blessings He bestowed upon him, expressing amazement. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is: Be amazed at his disbelief. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: What is an interrogative, meaning: What made him disbelieve?
80:18: Then he explained his affair so that he should know that God is his Creator, saying: From what did He create him? Its wording is a question, but its meaning is a statement.
80:19: Then he explained it and said: 19- From a sperm-drop He created him and proportioned him, stages: sperm-drop, then clot, until the end of his creation. Al-Kalbi said: He proportioned his creation, his head, his eyes, his hands, and his feet.
80:20: 20- Then He made the way easy for him, meaning the way he came out of his mother’s womb. Al-Suddi, Muqatil, Al-Hasan, and Mujahid said: It means the path of truth and falsehood, and He made knowledge of it easy for him, as He said: Indeed, We showed him the way (al-Insan 76:3) And We showed him the two ways (al-Balad 90:10). It was also said: He made easy for everyone what He created for him and decreed for him.
80:21: 21- Then He caused him to die and buried him, He made a grave for him in which to be buried. Al-Farra’ said: He made him buried and did not make him one of those who are found like wild beasts and birds. It is said: I buried the dead if you bury him, and God made him a grave means He placed him in a place where he would be buried, and He made him have a grave, just as one says: I expelled so-and-so and God expelled him meaning He made him an outcast.
80:22: 22- Then if He wills, He will resurrect him, He will revive him after his death.
80:23: 23- No, in response to him, meaning: It is not as this infidel says and thinks. Al-Hasan said: Truly. He has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded to do, meaning he did not do what God commanded him to do and did not perform what was imposed upon him.
80:24: When He mentioned the creation of the son of Adam, He mentioned his provision so that he might consider. He said: 24- So let man consider his food, how his Lord has determined it for him and arranged it for him and made it a cause of his life. Mujahid said: its entrance and exit.
80:25: Then he explained and said: 25- I The people of Kufa read I with the fat-ha as a repetition of the preposition, meaning: So let him look at I. The others read it with the kasra as a new sentence. We poured down the water abundantly, meaning the rain.
80:26: 26- Then We split the earth open, with plants.
80:27: 27- Then We caused to grow therein grain, meaning the seeds that feed it.
80:28: 28- And grapes and reeds, which is fresh grass, and it is called this because it is cut every day. Al-Hasan said: Reeds are fodder for animals.
80:29: 29- And olives, which is what oil is pressed from, and palm trees, plural of palm tree.
80:30: 30- And thick gardens, thick trees, singular: aglab, and from this the thick-necked person is called aglab. Mujahid and Muqatil said: Ghalab is the intertwined trees, some of them intertwined with others. Ibn Abbas said: Tall.
80:31: 31- And fruit, meaning the various types of fruit, and pasture, meaning grass and pasture that people have not cultivated, which livestock and animals eat. Akrima said: Fruit is what people eat, and squash is what animals eat. Qatada said something similar: Fruit is for you, and squash is for your livestock. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: What the earth produces of what people and livestock eat. It was narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taimi that Abu Bakr was asked about his statement: And fruits and herbage, so he said: What sky will shade me and what land will bear me if I say about the Book of God what I do not know? Ibn Shihab narrated on the authority of Anas that he heard Umar ibn al-Khattab reciting this verse and then saying: We know all of this, but what is the father? Then he threw away a stick that was in his hand and said: By God, this is, by God, an effort. What is wrong with you, O son of Umm Umar, that you do not know what the father is? Then he said: Follow what is made clear to you from this Book, and leave what is not made clear.
80:32: 32- For your enjoyment, meaning fruit, and for your livestock, meaning grass.
80:33: Then he mentioned the Resurrection and said: 33- Then when the Deafening Blast comes, meaning the Blast of the Resurrection. It is called that because it deafens the ears, that is, it is so intense in the ears that it almost deafens them.
80:34: 34- The Day when a man will flee from his brother.
80:35: 35- And his mother and his father.
80:36: 36- And his wife and his children, he does not pay attention to any of them because they are busy with themselves. It was narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said regarding this verse, On the Day when a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his wife and his children, he said: Abel will flee from Cain, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will flee from his mother, Abraham, peace be upon him, will flee from his father, Lot, peace be upon him, from his wife, and Noah, peace be upon him, from his son.
80:37: 37- Every man among them, that Day, will have something to occupy him, which will distract him from the affairs of others. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah told me, Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz told us, Ibn Abi Uways told us, my father told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Sawdah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘People will be resurrected barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, with sweat bridling them and reaching the earlobes.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, how wretched is it that we will look at one another?’ He said: ‘People will be busy, and each one of them will have his own business that will occupy him.’”
80:38: 38- Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, bright and luminous.
80:39: 39- Laughing, with joy cheering, happy with what she has received of the honor of God Almighty.
80:40: 40- And faces that Day will be covered with dust, blackness and gloom of worry and sadness.
80:41: 41- A darkness will cover it, darkness and an eclipse will cover it and engulf it. Ibn Abbas said: humiliation will cover it. Ibn Zayd said: The difference between dust and qatra is that qatra is the dust that rises and reaches the sky, while dust is what is lower on the earth.
80:42: 42- Those, to whom this is done, are the unbelieving wicked ones, the plural of unbeliever and wicked one.
81:1: Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Tha’labi told us, Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Muhammad bin Sahl Al-Sarakhsi told us by dictation, Abu Al-Wafa Al-Mu’ammal bin Al-Hasan bin Isa Al-Masarjisi told us, Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ramadi told us, Ibrahim bin Khalid told us, Abdullah bin Buhair Al-Qadi told us, he said I heard Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid Al-San’ani say I heard Ibn Umar say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wants to see the conditions of the Day of Resurrection, let him read: ‘When the sun is wrapped up.’” God the Almighty said: 1- When the sun is wrapped up. Ali bin Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas: It became dark. Qatada, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: Its light is lost. Saeed bin Jubair said: It was hidden. Mujahid said: It disappeared. Al-Zajjaj said: It was wrapped up as a turban is wrapped up. It is said: I wrapped the turban around my head, I wrapped it up and I wrapped it up, if I rolled it up. The root of wrapping is to gather some things together, so its meaning is that the sun gathers some parts together then it is wrapped up, so if that is done to it, its light is lost. Ibn Abbas said: God will roll the sun, moon and stars into the sea on the Day of Resurrection, then He will send a violent wind upon them that will strike them and they will become fire. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musaddad told us, Abdul Aziz bin Al-Mukhtar told us, Abdullah Al-Danaaj told us, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman told me, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The sun and the moon will be rolled up on the Day of Resurrection.
81:2: 2- And when the stars are scattered, meaning they are scattered from the sky and fall to the ground. It is said: The bird is scattered, meaning it falls from its nest. Al-Kalbi and Ata’ said: On that day the sky will rain stars, and not a star will remain that does not fall.
81:3: 3- And when the mountains are set in motion, they are uprooted from the face of the earth and become scattered dust.
81:4: 4- And when the ten-month-old camels are neglected, which are the pregnant camels that have been pregnant for ten months, the singular of which is 'ashra', and that is their name until they give birth at the end of a year, and they are the most valuable property among the Arabs. Targeted: they are left neglected without a shepherd, neglected by their owners, and they were attached to their tails, and they had no property more pleasing to them than them, because of the horrors of the Day of Resurrection that came to them.
81:5: 5- And when the wild beasts, meaning the land animals, are gathered together, gathered after the resurrection so that some of them may exact retribution from others. Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: They will be gathered together means their death. He said: The gathering of everything will be death, except for the jinn and mankind, for they will both be stopped on the Day of Resurrection. Ubayy ibn Ka’b said: They will be mixed up.
81:6: 6- And when the seas are set ablaze. The people of Mecca and Basra read it with a light pronunciation, while the rest read it with a heavy pronunciation. Ibn Abbas said: It is lit and becomes a blazing fire. Mujahid and Muqatil said: It means that some of it bursts into others, the fresh and the salty, so all the seas become one sea. Al-Kalbi said: It is filled. This also means: And the set ablaze sea (al-Tur 52:6). Set ablaze means filled. It was also said: Its waters become one sea of scalding water for the people of Hell. Al-Hasan said: It dries up, and this is the opinion of Qatada. He said: Its water is gone and not a drop remains in it. Abu Al-Aaliyah narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, who said: Six signs will occur before the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:While the people are in their markets, the light of the sun disappears. While they are like that, the stars will scatter. While they are like that, the mountains will fall on the face of the earth, moving and shaking. The jinn will flee to the humans, and the humans will flee to the jinn. The animals, birds, and wild animals will mix and swarm among themselves. This is what He said: And when the wild beasts are gathered together, mixed. And when the ten thousand animals are neglected, and when the wild beasts are gathered together, and when the seas are set ablaze. He said: The jinn will say to the humans, We will bring you report. So they went to the sea, and it was a blazing fire. He said: While they were like that, the earth rose in a single crack to the seventh lowest earth, and the heaven split in a single crack, and to the seventh highest heaven. While they were like that, the wind came to them and killed them. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he also said: They are twelve characteristics, six in this world and six in the hereafter.
81:7: And it is what God Almighty mentioned in His saying: 7- And when souls are paired. Al-Nu'man ibn Bashir narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he was asked about this verse. He said: A righteous man will be paired with a righteous man in Paradise, and an evil man will be paired with an evil man in Hell. This is the meaning of what Ikrimah said. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: Each person is affiliated with his own group, the Jew with the Jew and the Christian with the Christian. Al-Rabi’ ibn Khathim said: A man will be resurrected with his employer. It was also said: Souls are married to their deeds. Ata and Muqatil said: The souls of the believers were paired with the houris, and the souls of the unbelievers were paired with the devils. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: When souls are paired, the spirits will be returned to the bodies.
81:8: 8- And when the buried alive girl is asked, which is the girl buried alive, she was called that because of the dirt that is thrown on her, which weighs her down until she dies. The Arabs used to bury their daughters alive for fear of shame and need. It is said: Awd This is not correct in terms of structure because the buried alive girl is from wad not from awd. It is said: wadda ya’id wadan, so he is wa’id, and the passive participle is maw’ud. Akrima narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When a woman became pregnant in the pre-Islamic era and the time came for her to give birth, she would dig a hole and urinate at the top of the hole. If she gave birth to a girl, she would throw her into the hole, and if she gave birth to a boy, she would keep him.
81:9: 9- For what sin were you killed? The general public reads them with the passive verb, while Abu Ja`far reads them with the shaddah, meaning that the buried girl is asked, For what sin were you killed? The meaning of her question is to rebuke her killer, because she is saying: I was killed without sin. It was narrated that Jabir bin Zaid used to recite: And when the girl buried alive is asked, for what sin was she killed, and Abu Al-Dhaha read something similar.
81:10: 10- And when the pages are spread out, the people of Medina, Ash-Sham, Asim, and Ya’qub read spread out with a light pronunciation, while the others read it with a heavy pronunciation, like His statement: He will be given spread out pages (al-Muddaththir 74:52), meaning the pages of deeds will be spread out for the reckoning.
81:11: 11- And when the sky is scraped away, Al-Farra’ said: It is removed and folded. Al-Zajjaj said: It is removed just as a roof is removed. Muqatil said: It is revealed from whoever is in it. The meaning of scraping is that you lift something from something that had covered it, just as skin is scraped off a hump.
81:12: 12- And when Hell is set ablaze, the people of Medina and Ash-Sham, and Hafs on the authority of Asim, read: set ablaze with emphasis, and the rest read it with emphasis, meaning: set ablaze for the enemies of God.
81:13: 13- And when Paradise is brought near, brought near to the friends of God.
81:14: 14- I knew, at that time, every soul, meaning: every soul, what it brought, of good or evil. This is an answer to his saying: When the sun is wrapped up and what follows it.
81:15: God Almighty said: 15- So I swear by the stars that retreat, “la” is an extra word, meaning: I swear by the stars that retreat.
81:16: 16- The stars that appear at night and disappear during the day, so they are hidden and not seen. Qatada said: They are the stars that appear at night and disappear during the day, so they are hidden and not seen. And on the authority of Ali also: The planets are hidden during the day and are not seen, and are swept away and return to their paths. Some people said: They are the five stars: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and Mercury. They retreat in their path, meaning they return behind them and sweep away: they hide at the time of their disappearance and setting, as gazelles sweep away in their dens. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning of Al-Khans is that it is delayed from its rising every year, a delay that it delays from hastening that rising, it is delayed from it. And Al-Kans means it is swept away during the day and is not seen. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, that it is the wild animal. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the gazelle. This is the narration of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The root of khunus is to go back, and kanoos is to go back to its nests, which are the places where wild animals go to hide.
81:17: 17- And the night when it covers, Al-Hasan said: It approaches with its darkness. Others said: It departs. The Arabs say: The night covers and covers, meaning when it departs and only a little of it remains.
81:18: 18- And the morning when it breathes, it comes and its beginning appears, and it is said: its light spreads and rises.
81:19: 19- It, meaning the Qur’an, is the word of a noble Messenger, meaning Gabriel, meaning: Gabriel brought it down from God Almighty.
81:20: 20- Of strength, and among His strength was that He plucked the villages of the people of Lot from the black water and carried them on His wing, then raised them to the sky and then turned them over, and that He saw Satan speaking to Jesus about some of the eagles of the Holy Land, so He blew him with His wing, a blast that threw him to the farthest mountain in India, and that He shouted a shout to Thamud and they became kneeling, and that He descends from the sky to the earth and ascends faster than a bird, with the Lord of the Throne, firmly established, in the station.
81:21: 21- Obeyed then, meaning in the heavens the angels obey him. Among the angels’ obedience to him is that they opened the gates of the heavens on the night of the Ascension with his words to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the keepers of Paradise opened its gates with his words, Amen, to God’s revelation and message to His prophets.
81:22: 22- And your companion is not mad, he says to the people of Mecca: And your companion, meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, is not mad. This is also a response to an oath. He swears that the Qur'an was revealed by Gabriel, and that Muhammad is not as the people of Mecca say, because they say that he is mad, and that what he says he says on his own.
81:23: 23- And he saw him, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, in his form, on the clear horizon, which is the highest horizon from the east, as stated by Mujahid and Qatadah. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjuwayh told me, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, al-Hasan ibn Aliwa told us, Ismail ibn Isa told us, Ishaq ibn Bishr told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ikrimah and Muqatil, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: ‘I would like to see you in the form you have in heaven.’ He said: ‘You will not be able to do that.’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Where do you want me to appear to you?’ He said: ‘In al-Abtah.’ He said: ‘It is not enough for me.’ He said: ‘Then here.’ He said: ‘It is not enough for me.’ He said: ‘Then in Arafat.’ He said: ‘That is more likely to be enough for me.’ So he made an appointment with him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out at that time and saw Gabriel approaching from the mountains of Arafat with a rustling and a clang, filling the space between the east and the west, his head in the sky and his feet on the earth. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: ‘Allahu Akbar’ and fell unconscious. Gabriel turned in…” He took his picture and hugged him to his chest and said: O Muhammad, do not be afraid. How would you be if you saw Israfil with his head under the Throne and his feet on the borders of the seventh earth, and that the Throne was on his shoulders, and that he sometimes became small out of fear of God Almighty until he became like a sparrow, meaning a bird, until nothing carried the Throne of your Lord except His greatness. 24- And he is not, meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, stingy with the unseen, meaning the revelation, and the report from heaven and what he learned of what was hidden from him of report and stories, stingy with, the people of Mecca, Basra, and Al-Kisa’i read it with the letter dhaad, meaning accused. It is said: So-and-so is suspected of money and weighs, meaning he accuses it. Suspicion is accusation. The others read it with the letter dhad, meaning he is stingy. He says that knowledge of the unseen comes to him, but he does not withhold it from you, but rather he teaches you and informs you of it, and he does not conceal it as a soothsayer conceals what he has until he takes a fee for it. The Arabs say: I was stingy with something, with the letter nun broken, I was stingy with it, meaning I was stingy with it, stingy and miserly, so I am stingy with it, meaning I am stingy with it.
81:25: 25- And it is not, meaning the Qur’an, the word of an accursed devil. Al-Kalbi said: He says that the Qur’an is neither poetry nor divination as the Quraysh said.
81:26: 26- So where do you go? That is, where do you turn away from this Qur'an, which contains healing and clarification? Al-Zajjaj said: What path do you take that is clearer than this path that has been made clear to you?
81:27: Then he explained and said: 27- It is, meaning the Qur’an, only a reminder to the worlds, an admonition to all of creation.
81:28: 28- For whoever among you wills to be upright, that is, to follow the truth and abide by it.
81:29: 29- And you do not will except that God, Lord of the worlds, wills, meaning, inform them that the will lies in granting success to Him and that they are not able to do that except by the will of God. It is an announcement that no one does good except by the success of God and no evil except by His abandonment.
82:1: 1- When the sky is split open, it is split.
82:2: 2- And when the stars are scattered, they fall.
82:3: 3- And when the seas burst forth, burst forth into one another, and the fresh water mixes with the salt, becoming one sea. Al-Rabi’ said: blow forth means overflow.
82:4: 4- And when the graves are scattered, they are searched and their soil is turned over and the dead in them are brought back to life. It is said: I scattered the basin and searched it, if I turned it over and made its bottom its top.
82:5: 5- A soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind. It was said: What it has put forward of good or bad deeds, and what it has left behind of a good or bad practice. It was also said: What it has put forward of charity and what it has left behind of inheritances, based on what we mentioned in His statement: On that Day man will be informed of what he put forward and left behind. (al-Qiyamah 75:13).
82:6: 6- O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? What has deceived you and made falsehood tempt you so that you have wasted what was required of you? The meaning is: What has protected you from His punishment? Ata’ said: It was revealed about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed about Al-Aswad ibn Shuraik who struck the Prophet, but God, the Almighty, did not punish him. So God, the Almighty, revealed this verse, saying: What deceived you concerning your Generous and Forgiving Lord, that He did not punish you immediately for your disbelief? Qatadah said: His enemy who had power over him, meaning Satan, deceived him. Muqatil said: God’s forgiveness deceived him when He did not punish him the first time. Al-Suddi said: God’s kindness to him deceived him. Ibn Masoud said: There is no one among you but that God will be alone with him on the Day of Resurrection. He will say: O son of Adam, what deceived you about Me? O son of Adam, what did you do with what you knew? O son of Adam, what did you answer the messengers? Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad was asked: If God were to raise you up on the Day of Resurrection and say: What deceived you concerning your Generous Lord? What would you say? He would say: I would say that your low curtain deceived me. Yahya bin Muadh said: If he made me stand before him and said: What deceived you about me? I would say: Your Lord deceived me about you, past and present. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: If someone asked me: What deceived you concerning your Generous Lord? I would have said: The Generosity of the Generous One deceived me. Some scholars of allusion said: He only said By your Generous Lord without the rest of His names and attributes, as if he had taught him the answer so that he would say: The generosity of the Generous One has deceived me.
82:7: 7- He who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you. The people of Kufa and Abu Ja`far read fa`dalak with a light stress on the letter, meaning He directed you and made you into whatever form He wanted, good or bad, tall or short. The others read it with a shaddah, meaning He made you well-proportioned in creation and limbs.
82:8: 8- In whatever form He willed, He created you. Mujahid, Al-Kalbi, and Muqatil said: In any resemblance to a father, mother, maternal uncle, or paternal uncle. It was mentioned in the hadith: When the sperm settles in the womb, every vein between it and Adam is brought together, then he recites, In whatever form He wills, He has cast you. Al-Farra’ mentioned another saying: He puts you in whatever form He wills. If He wills, He wills in the form of a human being, or if He wills, He wills in the form of an animal or another creature.
82:9: 9- No, but you are lying. Abu Ja`far read it with a ya’, and the others read it with a ta’, because of His saying: And over you are guardians “with the religion,” with recompense and accountability.
82:10: 10- And over you are guardians, angelic watchers who record your deeds.
82:11: 11- Honorable to God, writers, who write down your words and deeds.
82:12: 12- They know what you do, whether good or evil.
82:13: God Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss. The righteous are those who were righteous and sincere in their faith by performing the duties of God Almighty and avoiding His sins.
82:14: 14- And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. It was narrated that Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik said to Abu Hazim al-Madani: I wonder what we have with God? He said: Compare your deeds to the Book of God, for you will know what you have with God. He said: Then where do I find it in the Book of God? He said when God says: Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure * And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. Sulayman said: Then where is God's mercy? He said: Near the doers of good (al-A’raf 7:56).
82:15: God Almighty says: 15- They will enter it on the Day of Judgment, they will enter it on the Day of Resurrection.
82:16: 16- And they will not be absent from it.
82:17: Then he glorified that day and said: 17- And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
82:18: Then he repeated his astonishment at his situation and said: 18- Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?
82:19: 19- A day when you will not possess, the people of Kufa and Basra read: A day with the mim raised, in response to the first day, and the others read it with the mim lowered, meaning: on a day, meaning: these things on a day when a soul will not possess anything for another soul, Muqatil said: meaning for a disbelieving soul something of benefit, and the command on that day is for God, meaning that God will not possess anything on that day as He possessed them in the world.
83:1: 1- Woe to those who give short measure, meaning those who reduce the measure and weight and cheat people out of their rights. Al-Zajjaj said: The one who gives short measure and weight is called Mutaffif because he hardly steals anything from the measure or weight except a small and insignificant amount. Abu Bakr Yaqub bin Ahmad bin Muhammad Ali Al-Sayrafi told us, Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan bin Ahmad Al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Hamid Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Hafiz told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Bishr told us, Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, my father told me, Yazid Al-Nahwi told me that Ikrimah told him on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, they were the worst people in measuring, so God Almighty revealed: ‘Woe to those who give short measure’. So measure well.” Al-Suddi said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina and there was a man there called Abu Juhayna, who had two measures with him, measuring with one and giving with the other. So God revealed this verse.” So God Almighty decreed woe to those who give short measure.
83:2: Then he explained who the defrauders are, saying: 2- Those who, when they take by measure from people, take in full. He meant when they take by measure from people, meaning they take from them and from, and on alternate. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that if they measure from people, they take full measure and weight from them. He meant: those who, when they buy for themselves, take full measure and weight.
83:3: 3- And if they measure or weigh for them, they lose, meaning if they measure or weigh for them, meaning for the people, it is said: I weighed you your right and I fed you your food, meaning I weighed for you and fed you, just as it is said: I advised you and I advised you and I earned for you and I earned for you. Abu Ubaidah said: Eisa bin Omar used to make them two letters, stopping at ‘ka-lawa’ and ‘waz-waz-wa’, and starting with ‘humu yakhsiroon’. Abu Ubaidah said: “The first choice is correct, meaning that each one is one word, because they wrote them without an alif. If they were separate, ‘ka-lawa’ and ‘waz-wa’ would be with an alif like all other verbs like ‘ja’awu’ and ‘qalawa’. The copies of the Qur’an agreed to drop the alif, and because it is said in the language ‘ka-llaka’ and ‘waz-waz-taka’ just as it is said ‘ka-lla lak’ and ‘waz-nata lak’. ‘yakhsiroon’ means they reduce, Nafi’ said: Ibn Omar used to pass by a seller and say: ‘Fear God and give full measure and weight, for the defrauders will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection until the sweat will cover them up to the middle of their ears.’”
83:4: 4- Does he not think, be certain, that those, who do that, will be sent?
83:5: 5- For a great day, meaning the Day of Resurrection.
83:6: 6- The Day when people will rise from their graves for the Lord of the Worlds, that is, for His command, His reward, and His reckoning. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir told us, Ma’n told us, Malik told me, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: People will stand before the Lord of the Worlds until one of them disappears in his sweat up to the middle of his ears.” Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tobah al-Kashmihani told us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yaqub al-Kisa’i told us, Abdullah ibn Mahmud told us, Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khalal told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, who said: Salim ibn Amir told me, al-Miqdad, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘When the Day of Resurrection comes, the sun will be brought near to the servants until it is the distance of a mile or two - Salim said: I do not know whether the two miles means the distance of the earth or the mile used for applying kohl to the eyes?’ He said: ‘The sun will melt them and it will be in their sweat according to their deeds. Some of them will have it up to their heels, some up to their knees, some up to their waists, and some will have it bridled. I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pointing with his hand to his mouth and saying: Bridle it.’”
83:7: God Almighty said: 7- No, a deterrent, meaning the matter is not as they are, so let them be deterred. The end of the speech is here. Al-Hasan said: No is a beginning that connects to what follows it with the meaning of truly, Indeed, the book of the wicked, in which their deeds are written, is in Sijjin. Abdullah bin Omar, Qatadah, Mujahid, and Al-Dahhak said: Sijjin is the seventh lowest earth in which the souls of the disbelievers are. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Al-Hussein bin Muhammad bin Fanjuwayh told us, Musa bin Muhammad told us, Al-Hasan bin Alawiyyah told us, Ismail bin Isa told us, Al-Musayyab told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Al-Bara’, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The prison is below the seven earths, and ‘Aliyyun is in the seventh heaven under the Throne.’” Shammar ibn Atiyah said: Ibn Abbas came to Ka’b al-Ahbar and said: Tell me about the statement of God, the Almighty: Indeed, the book of the wicked is in Sijjin. He said: The soul of the wicked ascends to the heavens, but the heavens refuse to accept it. Then it descends to the earth, but the earth refuses to accept it, so it enters under seven earths until it reaches Sijjin, which is the place of the army of Satan. Then a piece of parchment is taken out for it from Sijjin, which is numbered and sealed, and it is placed under the army of Satan, for it knows its destruction by the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection. Sa’id ibn Jubayr agreed with this, saying: Sijjin is under the army of Satan. Ata Al-Khurasani said: It is the lower earth, and in it are Satan and his offspring. Al-Kalbi said: It is a rock under the seventh lowest earth, green, like the green of the heavens, from which the book of the wicked is placed in it. Ibn Abi Nujayh also narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Sijjin is a rock under the lowest earth, which is turned over and the book of the wicked is placed in it. Wahb said: It is the last resort of Satan’s power. It was stated in the hadith: Al-Falaq is a covered pit in Hell, and Sijjin is an open pit in Hell. Akrima said: In prison means: in loss and misguidance. Al-Akhfash said: It is a verbal noun from sijn, just as one says fasiq and sharīb, meaning: in confinement and severe constriction.
83:8: 8- And what will make you know what Sijjin is? Al-Zajjaj said: That is, it is not something you or your people knew.
83:9: 9- A Book Marked. This is not an interpretation of the prisoner, but rather it is a clarification of the book mentioned in His statement: Indeed, the Book of the wicked. That is, it is a Book Marked, that is, their deeds are written in it, recorded against them like a number on a garment. It is not forgotten or erased until they are recompensed for it. Qatada and Muqatil said: It is marked on him with his partners, as if he is aware of a mark by which he is known to be an unbeliever. It was also said: Sealed, in the language of Himyar.
83:11: 11- Those who deny the Day of Judgment.
83:12: 12- "And none denies it except every transgressor and sinner.
83:13: 13- "When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Legends of the ancients.'"
83:14: 14- No, Muqatil said: meaning they do not believe. Then he continued: Rather, the stain has covered their hearts because of what they were earning. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd al-Samad al-Turabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamuyah al-Sarakhsi told us, Ibrahim ibn Hazim al-Shashy told us, Abu Muhammad Abd ibn Hamid al-Kashi told us, Sufyan ibn Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qaqa’ ibn Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When a believer commits a sin, there is a black spot on his heart. If he repents, desists, and seeks forgiveness, his heart is cleansed of it. But if he increases it, it increases until it covers his heart. That is the rust that God mentioned in His Book: “No! Rather, what they were earning has rusted over their hearts.”’” The root of rain is to overcome. It is said: the wine covered his mind, you see rain and raywan, if it overcame him and he became drunk. The meaning of the verse is: sins overcame their hearts and surrounded them. Al-Hasan said: it is sin upon sin until the heart dies. Ibn Abbas said: Ran on their hearts means it was stamped on them.
83:15: 15- No indeed! Indeed, on that Day they will be veiled from their Lord. Ibn Abbas said: No means: they will not believe. Then he began by saying: Indeed, on that Day they will be veiled from their Lord. Some of them said: they will be prevented from His honor and mercy. Qatada said: it means that He will not look at them nor purify them. Most of the commentators said: from seeing Him. Al-Hasan said: If the ascetics and worshippers knew that they would not see their Lord in the afterlife, their souls would perish in this world. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: Just as He prevented them in this world from believing in His Oneness, He will prevent them in the Hereafter from seeing Him. Malik was asked about this verse and he said: When God concealed Him from His enemies so that they could not see Him, He revealed Himself to His friends so that they could see Him. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, said: In His statement: No indeed! They will be veiled from their Lord that Day: This indicates that God’s friends will see God.
83:16: Then he informed that the infidels, despite being veiled from God, will enter Hell, so he said: 16- Then they will surely enter Hellfire.
83:17: 17- Then it will be said, that is, the keepers will say to them, This, that is, this punishment, is what you used to deny.
83:18: 18- No, said Muqatil: He does not believe in the torment that they will suffer. Then he explained the location of the book of the righteous, saying: Indeed, the book of the righteous is in ‘Illiyyin. We narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him: Indeed, ‘Illiyyin is in the seventh heaven beneath the Throne. Ibn Abbas said: It is a tablet of green emerald hanging under the throne, and their deeds are written on it. Kaab and Qatada said: It is the right pillar of the throne. Ata' said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is Paradise. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the Lote Tree of the Limit. Some of the scholars of meaning said: Elevation after elevation and honor after honor, and that is why it was collected with the letter Ya and the letter Noon. Al-Farra’ said: It is a noun in the plural form, with no singular form, such as twenty and thirty.
83:19: 19- And what will make you know what is the highest position?
83:20: 20- A Book Inscribed is not an interpretation of ‘Illiyyin, meaning their deeds are written there, as we mentioned in the Book of the Wicked. It was said: What was prepared for them of honor was written there, and this is the meaning of what Muqatil said. And their saying: A number for them informs. The verse is interpreted as advancing and delaying, its metaphor is: The book of the righteous is an inscribed book in ‘Illiyyin, which is the place of the angels, and similarly the book of the Wicked is an inscribed book in Sijjin, which is the place of Satan and his soldiers.
83:21: 21- It will be witnessed by those brought near, meaning the angels who are in the highest heavens. They will witness and attend that writing or that book when it is taken up to the highest heavens.
83:22: 22- Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.
83:23: 23- On couches, they look, at what God has given them of dignity and grace. Muqatil said: They look at their enemy, how they are being tortured.
83:24: 24- You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss. If you see them, you will know that they are people of bliss because of what you see in their faces of light, beauty, and whiteness. Al-Hasan said: The radiance is in the face and the joy is in the heart. Abu Ja`far and Ya`qub read: You will recognize with a damma on the ta’ and a fatha on the ra’ without naming the agent. Nadhra is nominative. The rest read it with a fatha on the ta’ and a kasra on the ra’. Nadhra is accusative.
83:25: 25- They will be given to drink of pure wine, pure, good wine. Muqatil said: white wine. Sealed, sealed and prevented from being touched by anyone until the righteous break its seal. Mujahid said: Sealed means covered.
83:26: 26- Its conclusion, meaning its clay, is musk, as if he meant this. Ibn Zayd said: Its conclusion with God is musk, and the conclusion of the wine of this world is clay. Ibn Masoud said: Sealed means mixed. Its conclusion, meaning: its last taste and end is musk. So, the sealed is that which has a conclusion, meaning its end, and the conclusion of everything is its emptiness. Qatada said: It is mixed for them with camphor and sealed with musk. The general reading is khatamuh musk with the taa’ coming first. Al-Kisa’i read it as khatamuh, which is the reading of Ali and Alqamah, and their meanings are the same, as one says: so-and-so is of noble character and nature, and the seal and the seal, the last of everything. And for this let the competitors compete, so let those who desire to take the initiative to obey God Almighty. Mujahid said: Let the workers work, is similar to the words of God Almighty: For the like of this let the workers work (al-Saffat 37:61). Muqatil bin Sulayman said: Let the disputants dispute. Ata’ said: Let the racers compete, and its origin is from something precious that people’s souls crave, and each one wants it for himself and is stingy with it over others, meaning he is miserly with it.
83:27: 27- And its mixture is of Tasnim, a drink poured down upon them from high above in their rooms and homes. It was also said that it flows in the air, rising, and is poured into the vessels of the people of Paradise according to how full they are. When they are full, it is held back. This is the meaning of what Qatada said. The word is derived from the word elevation. A high thing is called sanam, and from this comes the word sanam al-ba'ir. Ad-Dahhak said: It is a drink called tasnim, and it is the most honorable drink. Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas said: It is pure for the faithful who are brought near to God, who will drink it pure, and it will be mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise. This is what He said: And its water is mixed with Tasnim, a spring from which the nearest ones will drink. Yusuf bin Mahran narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he was asked about his statement: From Tasnim. He said: This is among what God Almighty said: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes. (al-Sajdah 32:17)
83:28: 28- A spring is an accusative of state, he drinks from it means from it, and it was said: the close ones drink from it pure.
83:29: God Almighty says: 29- Indeed, those who committed crimes, who associated others with God, meaning the infidels of Quraysh 106:Abu Jahl, Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, Al-Aas ibn Wa’il, and their companions from the wealthy of Mecca, were among those who believed: Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal, and their companions from the poor believers. They laughed, and mocked them.
83:30: 30- And when they pass by them, meaning the poor believers among the infidels, they wink at each other, and winking is a gesture with the eyelid and eyebrow, meaning they point at them with their eyes in mockery.
83:31: 31- And when they return, meaning the infidels, to their families, they return in joy, admiring what they are in and enjoying their remembrance.
83:32: 32- And when they see them, they see the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they say, ‘Indeed, these are astray,’ they come to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, believing that they are on something.
83:33: 33- And they were not sent, meaning the polytheists, over them, meaning over the believers, as guardians, of their deeds, meaning they were not entrusted with the preservation of their deeds.
83:34: 34- So today, meaning in the Hereafter, those who believe will laugh at the disbelievers. Abu Salih said: This is because the gates of Hell will be opened for the disbelievers, and they will be told: Come out. When they see it open, they will approach it to come out, and the believers will look at them. When they reach its gates, it will be closed in their faces. This will be done to them repeatedly, and the believers will laugh. Ka'b said: There are windows between Paradise and Hell. So if a believer wants to look at an enemy of his who is in this world, he will look at him through those windows, as He said: So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hell (al-Saffat 37:55). So if they look from Paradise at their enemies while they are being tortured in Hell, they will laugh. This is what God Almighty said: So today those who believe laugh at the disbelievers.
83:35: 35- On couches, made of pearls and rubies, looking, at them in the fire.
83:36: God Almighty said: 36- Has the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?, meaning the reward for mocking the believers. The meaning of the question here is confirmation. Thawb, “Athib,” and Athaba all mean the same thing.
84:1: 1- When the sky is split, its splitting is one of the signs of the Day of Resurrection.
84:2: 2- And she listened to her Lord, meaning she heard her Lord’s command to split and obeyed Him, from the word adhan, which means listening. And she was entitled to it, meaning she was entitled to obey her Lord.
84:3: 3- And when the earth is stretched out, the stretching of the hide by Al-Akkadhi, and its width was increased. Muqatil said: It is leveled like the stretching of the hide, so that no building or mountain remains in it.
84:4: 4- And it threw out, it took out, what was in it, of the dead and treasures, and it emptied, it was emptied of them.
84:5: 5- And she gave permission to her Lord and fulfilled her duty. They differed regarding the answer to if. It was said: Its answer is omitted, and its meaning is: If these things are what a person sees as reward and punishment. It was said that his answer is: O man, indeed you are a toiler, and its metaphor is: If the sky is split open, every toiler will find what he did. It was said: The answer is: And I gave permission, and in that case the waw is redundant.
84:6: The meaning of his saying: 6- Strive towards your Lord with exertion, meaning strive towards Him in your work. Toiling is the work and effort of a person in a matter, whether good or evil, until it exerts itself in him, meaning it has an effect. Qatada and Al-Kalbi Ad-Dahhak said: Work for your Lord with an action, and meet Him, meaning meet the reward for your work, whether it be good or evil.
84:7: 7- But as for he who is given his record, the record of his deeds, in his right hand.
84:8: 8- Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Nafi' told us, on the authority of Ibn Umar, Ibn Abi Malekah told me that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would not hear anything that she did not know except that she would review it until she understood it. She said: "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever is brought to account will be punished." Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: I said: O Messenger of God, does not God Almighty say: Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning? She said: He said: That is only the presentation, but whoever is questioned about the reckoning will perish.
84:9: 9- And he will return to his family, meaning in Paradise, among the houris and human women, rejoicing /, with what he has been given of goodness and dignity.
84:10: 10- But as for he who is given his record behind his back, his right hand will be chained to his neck and his left hand will be placed behind his back, so his record will be given to him with his left hand from behind his back. Mujahid said: His left hand will be removed from behind his back.
84:11: 11- Then he will call for destruction, he calls for woe and destruction when he reads his book, saying: Woe to me, O destruction, as God Almighty says: There they will call for destruction Al-Furqan - 13.
84:12: 12- And he will be roasted in a Blazing Fire. Abu Ja`far, the people of Basra, Asim, and Hamza read: and he will be roasted with a light fatha on the yaa, like his saying: He will be roasted in the Great Fire Al-A`la - 12. The others read it with a damma on the yaa, a fatha on the sad, and a shaddah on the lam, like his saying: And roasting in Hellfire Al-Waqi`ah - 94, Then they will roast him in Hellfire Al-Haqqah - 31.
84:13: 13- He was happy with his family, meaning in this world, following his desires and indulgence in his lusts.
84:14: 14- “He thought that he would never be changed,” that he would never return to us and would never be resurrected.
84:15: Then he said: 15- Yes, meaning: It is not as he thought, but he will be transformed to us and resurrected, Indeed, his Lord was ever Seeing of him, from the day he created him until he resurrected him.
84:16: God Almighty said: 16- So I swear by the twilight. Mujahid said: It is the entire day. Ikrimah said: It is what remains of the day. Ibn Abbas and most of the commentators said: It is the redness that remains on the horizon after sunset. Some people said: It is the whiteness that follows that redness.
84:17: 17- And the night and what it gathers, meaning it gathers and joins. It is said: And I made him drink it, I gathered it, meaning I gathered it. And the camels gathered together: if they gathered and joined together. The meaning is: And the night and what it gathers and joins what was spread out during the day of the beasts, because when the night comes everything goes to its shelter. Mansour narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: What wrapped around it and became dark upon it. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It came from darkness or a star. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: And what was done in it.
84:18: 18- And the moon when it is full, when it is full and its light is complete, and it is in the white days. Qatada said: It has become round, and it is derived from the word wasq which means gathering.
84:19: 19- Latrakaban that you will ascend, the people of Mecca, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read it as Latrakaban with a fat-ha on the ba', meaning that you will ascend, O Muhammad, level after level. Al-Sha'bi and Mujahid said: Heaven after heaven. Al-Kalbi said: It means that you will ascend in it. It is also permissible for it to be degree after degree and rank after rank in closeness to God Almighty and elevation. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Saeed bin Al-Nadr told us, Hisham told us, Abu Al-Bashar told us on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: You will go from one level to another, one state after another. This is your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: What he meant by it is the sky changing color after color, so it becomes sometimes like paint and sometimes like molten metal, and it splits with clouds one time and is folded up another. Others read it with a damma on the ba’, because the meaning is more similar to people, because it was mentioned before: But as for he who is given his book in his right hand, and his left, and it was mentioned after that: Why should they not believe? And he meant: You will surely go through one state after another, and one matter after another in the place of resurrection, meaning: the conditions will be reversed for them, so they will be in the hereafter in a state other than the one they were in in this world. And from means after. Muqatil said: It means death, then life, then death, then life. Ata' said: Sometimes he is poor and sometimes he is rich. Amr ibn Dinar said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means the hardships and the horrors of death, then the resurrection, then the presentation. Ikrimah said: One state after another: a baby, then a weaned child, then a young man, then an old man. Abu Ubaidah said: You will follow the ways and conditions of those who came before you. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz told us, Abu Omar Al-San’ani from Yemen told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You will follow the ways of those who came before you, inch by inch and cubit by cubit, to the point that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would follow them. We said: O Messenger of God, do you mean the Jews and Christians? He said: Then who else?
84:20: God Almighty says: 20- Then why do they not believe? A question of denial.
84:21: 21- And when the Qur’an is recited to them, they do not prostrate. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: They do not pray. Abu Uthman Saeed bin Ismail Al-Dhabi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Jabbar bin Muhammad Al-Jarrahi told us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ahmad Al-Mahboubi told us, Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi told us, Qutaybah told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Musa, on the authority of Ata bin Mina, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “We prostrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during ‘Read in the name of your Lord’ and ‘When the heaven is split’.” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Nuaimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musaddad told us, Muammar told us: I heard my father say: Bakr told me, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, who said: “I prayed the Isha prayer with Abu Hurairah, and he recited ‘When the sky is split asunder’, and he prostrated. I said: What is this? He said: I prostrated in it behind Abu Al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I will continue to prostrate in it until I meet him.”
84:22: 22- Rather, those who disbelieve deny the Qur’an and the Resurrection.
84:23: 23- And God knows best what they conceal. In their hearts of denial. Mujahid said: They conceal.
84:24: 24- Then give them tidings of a painful punishment.
84:25: 25- Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is a reward uninterrupted, not cut off or diminished.
85:1: 1- And the sky with its constellations.
85:2: 2- And the Promised Day is the Day of Resurrection.
85:4: 4- He killed the people of the trench, meaning: he was cursed. The trench is the rectangular crack in the ground like a river. Its plural is: trenching. They differed about them: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi told us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Sa’dan al-Khatib told us, Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Quraysh ibn Nuh ibn Rustum told us, Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Bushanji told us, Hudbah ibn Khalid told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Thabit al-Banani told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, on the authority of Suhaib that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There was a king among those who came before you who had a magician. When he grew old, he said to the king: ‘I have grown old, so send me a boy to teach me magic.’ So he sent a boy to him. On his way, whenever a monk passed by him, he would sit with him and listen to his speech, and he liked it. When he came to the magician, he would pass by the monk and sit with him. When he came to the magician, he would strike him. When he returned from the magician, he would sit with the monk and listen to his speech. When he came to his family, they would strike him. So he complained about that to the monk, and he said: ‘When you go to the magician, say: My family has detained me. When you go to your family, say: I have been detained.’ The magician, while he was like that, came upon a huge beast that had held the people back, so he said: Today I will know whether the monk or the magician is better? So he took a stone and said: O God, if the monk's command is more beloved to You than the magician's command, then kill this beast so that the people may pass. So he threw it and killed it, and the people passed. Then he came to the monk and told him, and the monk said to him: O my son, today you are better than me. What I see has reached your situation, and you will be tested. If you are tested, be patient and do not inform others about me. So the boy cured the blind and the lepers and treated people of all diseases. A companion of the king who had gone blind heard of this, so he brought him many gifts and said: I will collect everything here for you if you heal me. He said: I do not heal anyone, only God heals. If you believe in God, I will supplicate to God for you, and He will heal you. So he believed in God, and God healed him. Then he came to the king and sat with him as he used to sit, and the king said to him: Who restored your sight? He said: My Lord, the Almighty. He said: Do you have a lord other than me? He said: My Lord and your Lord is God. So he seized him and continued torturing him until he showed him the boy. So the boy was brought and the king said to him: O my son, your magic has reached such a degree that you can heal the blind and the leper, and you do such and such. He said: I do not heal anyone; only God heals. So he seized him and continued torturing him until he showed him the monk. So the monk was brought and it was said: Abandon your religion. But he refused. So he called for a saw and placed it in the parting of his head and split it open until both sides fell. Then the king’s companion was brought and it was said to him: Abandon your religion. But he refused. So he placed the saw in the parting of his head and split it open until both sides fell. Then the boy was brought and it was said to him: Abandon your religion. But he refused. So he handed him over to a group of his companions and said: Take him to such and such a mountain and climb with him. When you reach its peak, if he renounces his religion, well and good, otherwise throw him down. So they took him and climbed the mountain. So he said: O God, suffice me against them however You wish. So it shook under them. Then he came walking to the king. The king said to him, “What happened to your companions?” He said, May God save me from them. So he handed him over to a group of his companions and said, “Take him and carry him in a boat to the depths of such-and-such a sea. If he renounces his religion, well and good, otherwise throw him into the sea.” So they took him and he said, O God, save me from them however You wish. So the ship capsized and they drowned. Then he came walking to the king. The king said to him, What happened to your companions? He said, May God save me from them. So he said to the king, You will not kill me until you do what I command you. The king said, What is that? He said, “Gather the people in one place and crucify me on a tree trunk. Then take an arrow from my quiver and place the arrow in the bow and say, ‘In the name of God, Lord of the boy.’ Then shoot me, for if you do that, you will kill me.” So he gathered the people in one plain, crucified him on a tree trunk, took an arrow from his quiver and placed it in the bow of his bow. Then he said: In the name of God, Lord of the boy. Then he shot him and the arrow hit his temple, and his hand hit his temple where the arrow had been, and he died. The people said: We believe in the Lord of the boy three times. Then the king was brought and it was said to him: Have you seen what you were afraid of? By God, your fear has come upon you. The people have believed. So he ordered that trenches be dug at the mouths of the alleys and fires be set in them. He said: Whoever does not renounce his religion, throw him into it, or it was said to him: Jump in. He said: So they did until a woman came with her child, and she hesitated to jump in. The boy said to her: O mother, be patient, for you are on the truth. This is an authentic hadith narrated by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj on the authority of Hudbah ibn Khalid on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah. Muhammad bin Ishaq reported on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih: A man who had remained in the religion of Jesus approached the people of Najran and called them, so they responded. Then Dhu Nuwas the Jew went to him with his soldiers from Himyar and gave them the choice between fire and Judaism, but they refused him, so he dug trenches and burned twelve thousand. Then when Aryat defeated Yemen, Dhu Nuwas fled and crossed the sea on his horse and drowned. Al-Kalbi said: Dhu Nuwas killed Abdullah bin Al-Tamir. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr: A ruin was dug up during the time of Omar bin Al-Khattab and they found Abdullah bin Al-Tamir placing his hand over a wound on his head. If his hand was removed from it, blood would spurt out, and if it was left alone, it would return to its place. On his hand was an iron ring on which was written: My Lord is God. report of that reached Omar, so he wrote: Repeat to him what you found him doing. Ata’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas - may God be pleased with them both - who said: There was in Najran a king from the kings of Himyar called Yusuf Dhu Nuwas bin Shurahbil bin Shurahbil in the period before the birth of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by seventy years. There was in his country a boy called Abdullah bin Tamir, and his father had handed him over to a teacher to teach him magic. The boy disliked that and saw no alternative but to obey his father, so he would go frequently to the teacher. On his way there was a monk who was a good reader and had a beautiful voice, and that pleased him. He mentioned something close to the meaning of the hadith of Suhaib until the boy said to the king: You will not be able to kill me unless you do what I tell you. He said: How can I kill you? He said: Gather the people of your kingdom while you are on your bed and shoot me with an arrow in the name of my God. So the king did that and killed him. The people said: There is no god but God, Abdullah bin Tamir, there is no religion but his religion. The king became angry and closed the city gate and took the mouths of the streets and dug a trench and filled it with fire. Then he paraded them man by man. Whoever recanted Islam, he would leave him, and whoever said: My religion is the religion of Abdullah bin Tamir, he would throw him in the trench and burn him. In his kingdom, there was a woman who converted to Islam among those who converted and she had three children, one of whom was a baby. The king said to her: Recant your religion or I will throw you and your children into the fire. She refused. So he took her eldest son and threw him into the fire. Then he said to her: Recant your religion. She refused. So he threw the second son into the fire. Then he said to her: Go back. She refused. So they took the boy from her to throw him into the fire. The woman wanted to recant, but the boy said: O mother, do not recant Islam, for you are on the truth and there is no harm to you. So the boy was thrown into the fire, and his mother was thrown after him. Saeed bin Jubair and Ibn Abi Zayd said: When the people of Isfandahar were defeated, Umar bin Al-Khattab said: What rulings apply to the Magians, for they are not people of the Book? Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: Yes, they had a Book, and wine was made lawful for them. One of their kings took it and it overcame his mind. He then grabbed his sister and had intercourse with her. When the intoxication subsided, he regretted it and said to her: Woe to you! What is this that you have done and what is the way out of it? She said: The way out is to address the people and say: God has permitted the marriage of sisters. When it becomes widespread among the people and they forget about it, address them and forbid it. Then he stood up and delivered a sermon and said: God has permitted you the marriage of sisters. The people all said: God forbid that we should believe in this or acknowledge it. No prophet came to us with it and no book was sent down to us concerning it. So he stretched out the whip among them, but they refused to acknowledge it, so he unsheathed the sword against them. But they refused to acknowledge it, so he dug a trench for them, lit a fire in it, and exposed them to it. Whoever refused and did not obey him, he threw him into the fire, and whoever complied, he let him go. Ad-Dahhak said: The People of the Trench were from the Children of Israel. They took men and women and dug a trench for themselves. They lit a fire in it and made the believers stand over it. They said: Are you disbelievers or should we throw you into the fire? They claim that it was Daniel and his companions. This is the narration of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Abu al-Tayyib said on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: The people of the prescribed punishments had an Abyssinian prophet. A prophet was sent from Abyssinia to his people. Then Ali, may God be pleased with him, recited: And We had certainly sent messengers before you, among them are those We have told you about, (Ghafir 40:78).
