He called them, and some people followed him, so he fought them, and killed his companions and took them, and bound those who had escaped from them. They dug a trench and filled it with fire. Whoever followed the Prophet was thrown into it, and whoever followed them was left alone. Then they brought a woman with a baby boy, and she was alarmed. The boy said: O mother, hurry up and do not act hypocritically. Akrima said: They were from the Nabataeans and were burned with fire. Muqatil said: The trench was three: one in Najran in Yemen, one in Syria, and one in Persia. They burned it with fire. The one in Syria was Abtamus the Roman, the one in Persia was Bukhtanasr, and the one in the land of the Arabs was Dhu Nuwas Yusuf. As for the one in Syria and Persia, God did not send down a Qur’an for them, but He sent down a Qur’an for the one in Najran. That was because a Muslim man who read the Bible hired himself out for work, and he began to read the Bible. The daughter of the hirer saw a light shining from reading the Bible, so she mentioned that to her father. He looked at him until he saw him, so he asked him, but he did not tell him. He kept on at him until he told him about the religion and Islam. He and eighty-seven people, men and women, followed him. This was after Jesus, peace be upon him, was raised to heaven. Dhu Nuwas Yusuf heard that, so he dug a hole for them in the ground and lit a fire in it, and exposed them to disbelief. Whoever refused to disbelieve, he threw him into the fire, and whoever turned away from the religion of Jesus, he did not throw him. A woman came with a small child who did not speak, so when she stood up on… The edge of the trench looked at her son and retreated from the fire. She struck until she advanced and did not stop doing that three times. When she was on the third try, she went back and her son said to her: O mother, I see before you a fire that will not be extinguished. When she heard that, they both threw themselves into the fire. God placed her and her son in Paradise. Seventy-seven people were thrown into the fire in one day. That is what God Almighty said: The companions of the trench were killed.
85:5: 5- The fire with fuel, instead of the trench. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God saved the believers who were thrown into the fire by taking their souls before the fire touched them, and the fire came out to the infidels on the edge of the trench and burned them.
85:6: 6- When they were sitting there, meaning: sitting by the fire to torture the believers. Mujahid said: They were sitting on chairs by the trench.
85:7: 7- And they, meaning the king and his companions who dug the trench, are witnesses to what they are doing to the believers, of exposing them to the fire and wanting them to return to their religion. They are present, Muqatil said: meaning they testify that the believers are in error when they abandoned the worship of the idol.
85:8: 8- And they did not resent them, Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: They did not dislike them, except that they believed in God, Muqatil said: They did not find fault with them. It was also said: They did not know of any fault in them. Al-Zajjaj said: They did not find fault with them for any sin except their belief in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
85:9: 9- To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is over all things Witness. Of their actions, God is Witness.
85:10: 10- Indeed, those who have put to trial, tortured and burned, the believing men and believing women, it is said: to have put to trial if you burn something, similar to The Day they will be tried by the Fire (al-Dhariyat 51:13), and then do not repent, for them is the punishment of Hell, for their disbelief, and for them is the punishment of the Burning Fire, for what they burned the believers. It was said: And for them is the punishment of the Burning Fire in this world, because God burned them with the fire with which they burned the believers, which rose up to them from the trench, said Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas and Al-Kalbi.
85:11: Then he mentioned what was prepared for the believers, saying: 11- “Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment.” They differed in the answer to the oath. Some of them said: The answer is: He killed the people of the trench, meaning he was killed. It was said: It contains an inversion, meaning: the killing of the people of the trench and the sky with its constellations.
85:12: Qatada said: His answer is: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe. Ibn Abbas said: His punishment of the oppressors is severe, like His saying: Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe (Hud 11:102).
85:13: 13- It is He who begins and repeats, meaning He creates them first in this world and then brings them back to life after death.
85:14: 14- And He is the Forgiving, of the sins of the believers, the Loving, the One who loves them. It was also said that it means the One who is loved, like the milked and the rider, meaning the one who is milked and ridden. It was also said that He forgives and loves to forgive. It was also said that it means the One who is affectionate toward His friends by forgiving them.
85:15: 15- The Possessor of the Glorious Throne. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read Al-Majid in the accusative case, describing the Throne, meaning the great throne. It was also said that he meant its beauty, so he described it with glory, just as he described it with generosity, so he said: Lord of the Noble Throne (al-Mu’minun 23:116). Its meaning is perfection, and the Throne is the best and most perfect of things. The others read it in the nominative case, describing the Possessor of the Throne.
85:16: 16- He is able to do whatever He wills. Nothing He wants is beyond His power, and nothing He asks for is impossible for Him.
85:17: God Almighty said: 17- Has there come to you the report of the armies? The report of the infidel crowds who gathered against the prophets has come to you.
85:18: Then he explained who they were and said: 18- Pharaoh and Thamud.
85:19: 19- Rather, those who disbelieved, from among your people, O Muhammad, are in denial, of you and the Qur’an, as was the custom of the people of Pharaoh before them, and they did not take heed from those who came before them from the disbelievers.
85:20: 20- And God is behind them, encompassing them, He knows them, nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, and He is able to bring down upon them what He brought down upon those who came before them.
85:21: 21- Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, generous, noble, and full of goodness. It is not, as the polytheists claimed, poetry and divination.
85:22: 22- In a Preserved Tablet. Nafi’ read: Preserved in the nominative case as an attribute of the Qur’an, for the Qur’an is preserved from alteration, change, and distortion. God Almighty said: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur’an and indeed, We will be its guardian. (al-Hijr 15:9). Others read it with the accusative case as a description of the tablet, which is known as the Preserved Tablet, which is the mother of the book, and from it are copies of books, preserved from the devils, and from additions and subtractions in it. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shuraihi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjuwayh told us, Mukhallad ibn Ja’far told us, al-Husayn ibn ‘Alawiya told us, Ismail ibn ‘Isa told us, Ishaq ibn Bishr told us, Muqatil and Ibn Jurayj told me, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: “At the beginning of the Tablet is: There is no god but God alone, His religion is Islam, and Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Whoever believes in God, the Mighty and Sublime, and believes in His promise and follows His Messengers, He will admit him into Paradise.” He said: “The Tablet is a tablet of white pearl, its length is the distance between the heaven and the earth, its width is the distance between the east and the west, its two edges are pearls and rubies, its edges are red rubies, its pen is light, its speech is bound to the Throne, and its root is in the stone of an angel.” Muqatil said: The Preserved Tablet is to the right of the Throne.
86:1: 1- By the sky and the nightcomer, Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about Abu Talib, because he "came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he gave him bread and milk as a gift. While he was sitting eating, a star fell and filled with water and then fire. Abu Talib was startled and said: What is this? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is a star that was thrown down, and it is a sign from the signs of God Almighty. Abu Talib was amazed, so God Almighty revealed: "By the sky and the nightcomer, and this is an oath, and the nightcomer is a star that appears at night, and whatever comes to you at night is a nightcomer.
86:2: 2- And what will make you know what the night visitor is?
86:3: Then he explained it and said: 3- The piercing star, meaning the shining, illuminating star. Mujahid said: The glowing one. Ibn Zayd said: He meant the Pleiades, and the Arabs call it the star. It was also said: It is Saturn, and it was named thus because of its height. The Arabs say to a bird that has reached the center of the sky high: It has pierced.
86:4: 4- Every soul has a guardian over it, the answer to the oath, that has a guardian over it. Abu Ja`far, Ibn `Amir, `Asim, and Hamza read: lama with emphasis, meaning: There is no soul but that it has a guardian over it. This is the language of Hudhayl, where they make lama mean except. They say: I adjure you by God, when you stand up, meaning when you stand up. Others read it with a light pronunciation, making ma a connection, meaning: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it from its Lord. The interpretation of the verse is: Every soul has a guardian over it from its Lord who records its deeds and counts for it what it earns of good and evil. Ibn Abbas said: They are the guardian angels. Al-Kalbi said: A guardian from God who protects her and her words and actions until He hands her over and hands her over to the decrees, then He releases her.
86:5: 4- So let man consider from what he was created, meaning from what his Lord created him, meaning let him consider with the gaze of a thinker.
86:6: Then he explained and said: 6- He was created from a gushing fluid. Gushing means poured into the womb, which is semen. The subject is the passive participle, like his saying: A pleasant life (al-Haqqah 69:21), meaning pleasing. Gushing means pouring. He meant the man’s fluid and the woman’s fluid, because the child is created from them, and he made it one due to their mixing.
86:7: 7- It comes out from between the backbone and the ribs, meaning the backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman. The ribs are the plural of tarabiyyah, which are the bones of the chest and throat. Ibn Abbas said: It is the place of the necklace on the chest. Al-Walibi narrated from him: Between the breasts of the woman. Qatada said: The throat. Ibn Zayd said: The chest.
86:8: 8- He is able to return it. Mujahid said: To return the sperm to the urethra. Ikrimah said: To return the water to the loins from which it came out. Ad-Dahhak said: He is able to return the human being to water as it was before. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: If He wills, He can return him from old age to youth, from youth to childhood, and from childhood to sperm. Ibn Zayd said: He is able to hold back that water so that it does not come out. Qatada said: God the Most High is able to resurrect and return the human being.
86:9: This is the first of the sayings for his saying: 9- The Day when secrets will be exposed. That is the Day of Resurrection. Secrets will be exposed and hidden things will be revealed. Qatada and Muqatil said: Actions will be tested. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said: Secrets are obligatory deeds, such as fasting, prayer, ablution, and ritual bathing after sexual impurity. They are secrets between God the Almighty and the servant. If the servant wanted, he could say: I fasted, but he did not fast, I prayed, but he did not pray, I performed ritual bathing, but he did not perform ritual bathing. So He will test those who fulfilled them and those who neglected them. Ibn Omar said: On the Day of Resurrection, every secret will be in the hand of God Almighty. It will be an adornment for some faces and a disgrace for others. Meaning: whoever fulfills it, his face will be radiant, and whoever neglects it, his face will be dusty.
86:10: 10- He has no power or helper, meaning that this person who denies the resurrection has no power to protect himself from God’s punishment, nor any helper to defend him from God.
86:11: Then he mentioned another section and said: 11- And the sky full of returns, meaning full of rain because it returns every year and is repeated. Ibn Abbas said: It is the clouds that return with rain.
86:12: 12- And the earth with its cracks, meaning it cracks and splits open, revealing plants, trees, and rivers.
86:13: The answer to the oath is his statement: 13- It, meaning the Qur’an, is a decisive statement, true and proven that distinguishes between truth and falsehood.
86:14: 14- It is not a joke, but a game and falsehood.
86:15: Then he told about the polytheists of Mecca, saying: 15- They are plotting a plot, fearing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and showing that they are contrary to him.
86:16: 16- And surely a plot, and God’s plot is to lure them in from where they do not know.
86:17: 17- So give the disbelievers respite. Ibn Abbas said: This is a warning from God Almighty to them, Give them respite a little, a little, and the meaning of give them respite and give them respite is: wait and do not rush, so God seized them on the day of Badr, and the respite was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
87:1: 1- Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, meaning: Say, Glory be to my Lord, the Most High. This is the view held by a group of the Companions and Followers. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Sharahi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, Abdullah ibn Hamid told us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah told us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah told us, Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Aban told us, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Muslim ibn al-Batin, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High,’ and said: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.” Some people said: It means, Glory be to your Lord, the Most High, above what the atheists describe Him with, and they made the name a connection. Those who consider the name and the named to be one and the same use this as evidence, because no one says, Glory be to the name of God and Glory be to the name of our Lord. Rather, they say, Glory be to God and Glory be to our Lord. So the meaning of Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High is, Glorify your Lord. Others said: glorify the name of your Lord, by mentioning Him while you are honoring Him, respecting His mention, and obeying His commands. They made the name mean naming. Ibn Abbas said: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, meaning: Pray by the command of your Lord, the Most High.
87:2: 2- Who created and proportioned. Al-Kalbi said: He created every living thing, then proportioned the hands, feet, and eyes. Al-Zajjaj said: He created man level, and the meaning of proportioned is: He made his height even.
87:3: 3- And He Who has decreed and guided, Al-Kisa’i read: has decreed with a light dāl, while others stressed it, and they have the same meaning. Mujahed said: Guidance of man to the path of good and evil, happiness and misery, and guidance of livestock to their pastures. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: He has destined for everything its path, so He guided it: He showed it to her how the male and female come. It was said: It is the measure of provisions and guidance for earning provisions and livelihood. It was said: He created benefits in things, and guided man to the way to extract them from them. Al-Saddī said: He estimated the duration of the fetus in the womb, then guided it to exit the womb. Al-Wasiti said: He decreed happiness and misery for them, then made it easy for each of the two groups to follow the path that He decreed.
87:4: 4- And He who brought forth the pasture, He caused the grass to grow and the livestock to graze on it, from green, yellow, red, and white.
87:5: 5- He made it, after the greenness, a stubble, like the stubble you see on top of a flood. Black, black after the greenness, because when grass dries up and becomes black.
87:6: 6- We will make you recite We will teach you by Gabriel’s recitation to you, so do not forget.
87:7: 7- Except what God wills that you forget, and what God has abrogated the recitation of from the Qur’an, as He said: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten Al-Baqarah - 106, and forgetting is a type of abrogation. Mujahid and Al-Kalbi said: When Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would not finish the last verse until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had spoken the first, for fear that he would forget it. Then God Almighty revealed: We will make you recite, and you will not forget, and after that he did not forget anything. He knows what is said and what is hidden, both of them. The meaning is: He knows what is secret and what is public.
87:8: 8- And We will make easy for you the path of ease. Muqatil said: We will make easy for you the deeds of the people of Paradise - and this is the meaning of Ibn Abbas’s statement - and We will make it easy for you to do good. And ease means doing good. It was said: We guide you to the easy Sharia, which is the tolerant Hanafi Sharia. It was said: It is connected to the first statement, meaning: He knows the loudness of what you recite to Gabriel when he finishes the recitation, and what is hidden: what you recite to yourself for fear of forgetting, then He promised him and said: And We will make the revelation easy for you meaning We will make the revelation easy for you so that you will memorize it and learn it.
87:9: 9- Then remind, admonish with the Qur'an, if the reminder benefits, admonition and reminder. The meaning is: whether it benefits or not, but he did not mention the second case, like his saying: garments to protect you from the heat, and he meant: both the heat and the cold.
87:10: 10- He will remember, he will take heed, whoever fears, God Almighty.
87:11: 11- And avoids it, meaning he avoids the remembrance and distances himself from it, the most wretched, the wretched in God’s knowledge.
87:12: 12- He who will burn in the Great Fire, the great and terrible one, because it is greater and hotter than the fire of this world.
87:13: 13- Then he will not die in it, so he will rest, nor will he live, a life that will benefit him.
87:14: 14- He has succeeded who purifies himself, purifies himself from polytheism and says: There is no god but God. This is the saying of Ata’ and Ikrimah, and the narration of Al-Walabi and Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan said: He whose deeds are pure. Others said: It is the Zakat al-Fitr. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri regarding his statement: He has succeeded who purifies himself, he said: He gave the Zakat al-Fitr.
87:15: 15- And he mentioned the name of his Lord and prayed. He said: He went out to the Eid prayer and prayed. Ibn Mas'ud used to say: May God have mercy on a man who gives charity, then prays, and then recites this verse. Nafi' narrated: When Ibn Umar prayed the morning prayer - meaning on the day of Eid - he would say: O Nafi', is charity forbidden? If you said: Yes, he would go to the prayer place. If you said: No, he would say: Then go out now. This is what this verse was revealed about: He has succeeded who purifies himself, * And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. This is the opinion of Abu Al-'Aliyah and Ibn Sirin. Some of them said: I do not know the basis of this interpretation, because this surah was revealed in Mecca, and there was no Eid or Zakat al-Fitr in Mecca. Sheikh Imam Muhyi Al-Sunnah, may God have mercy on him, said: It is possible that the revelation was before the ruling, as He said: And you are settled in this city. The Surah is Meccan, and the effect of the solution became apparent on the day of the conquest, so that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: It was made permissible for me for an hour of a day. Likewise, the verse was revealed in Mecca: The host will be routed and they will turn their backs. (al-Qamar 54:45). Omar bin Al-Khattab said: I did not know which host would be defeated, so when it was the day of Badr, I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, jumping up in his armor and saying: The host will be routed and they will turn their backs. “And he mentioned the name of his Lord and prayed.” That is, he mentioned his Lord and prayed. It was said: The remembrance is the takbirs of Eid, and the prayer is the Eid prayer. It was also said that the prayer here is supplication.
87:16: 16- Rather, you give preference, Abu Amr and Ya'qub read: you give preference with a ya', meaning: the most wretched ones who were mentioned, and the others read it with a ta', the evidence for this is: the reading of Abi bin Ka'b: Rather, you give preference to the life of this world and what is meant by the most wretched is the plural, even though it is in the singular form, because if the definite article enters something for the genus, it becomes all-encompassing, so it is as if he said: and the most wretched avoid it, then he said: Rather, you give preference to the life of this world.
87:17: 17- And the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Urfajah Al-Ashja'i said: We were with Ibn Mas'ud when he recited this verse and said to us: Do you know why we preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter? We said: No. He said: Because the world was brought to us, and its food, drink, women, pleasures and delights were hastened for us, and the Hereafter was described to us and then hidden from us, so we loved the immediate and abandoned the deferred.
87:18: 18- This, meaning what was mentioned in His statement: He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself, to the end of four verses, is in the former scriptures, meaning in the first books that were revealed before the Qur’an, in which the success of the one who purifies himself and prays is mentioned, and the people’s preference for this worldly life over the Hereafter, and that the Hereafter is better and more lasting.
87:19: Then he showed the pages and said: 19- The Scrolls of Abraham and Moses. Ikrimah and Al-Suddi said: This Surah is about the Scrolls of Abraham and Moses. Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi told us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hayri told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Maqil al-Maydani told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, Saeed ibn Kathir told us, Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Umrah bint Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recite in the two rak’ahs after which he performed witr: ‘Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High’ and ‘Say: O you disbelievers’, and in witr: ‘Say: He is God, the One’, ‘Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak’ and ‘Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind’.”
88:1: 1- Has there come to you the report of the Overwhelming Event? Meaning: The report of the Resurrection has come to you, covering everything with horrors.
88:2: 2- Some faces on that Day, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, will be humbled and submissive.
88:3: 3- A working, exhausting person. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It means those who worked and exhausted themselves in this world in a religion other than Islam, such as idol worshippers and infidels among the People of the Book, such as monks and others. God will not accept from them any striving in misguidance. They will enter Hell on the Day of Resurrection. This is the opinion of Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam. The meaning of exhaustion is: perseverance in working with fatigue. Ikrimah and Al-Suddi said: She commits sins in this world and will be thrown into Hell in the Hereafter. Some of them said: She is working in Hell and making it difficult for her. Al-Hasan said: She did not work for God in this world, so I make her work and make her difficult for her in Hell by treating her with chains and shackles. Qatada said the same, and it is the narration of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Masoud said: You will wade through the fire as camels wade through the mud. Al-Kalbi said: They will run on their faces in the fire. Ad-Dahhak said: They will be ordered to climb a mountain of iron into the fire. The statement was made in various ways, and what is meant by it are its owners.
88:4: 4- You will be burned with a fire. The people of Basra and Abu Bakr read: "You will be burned with a damma on the taa', taking into consideration his saying: "You will be given to drink from a boiling spring. The others read it with a fatha on the taa', A blazing fire." Ibn Abbas said: It has become hot and is blazing against the enemies of God.
88:5: 5- They will be given to drink from a boiling spring, extremely hot, upon which Hell has been lit since its creation. So they are driven to it thirsty and thirsty. The commentators said: If a drop from it were to fall on the mountains of the world, they would melt. This is their drink.
88:6: Then he mentioned their food and said: 6- They shall have no food except from Dharee’, said Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Qatadah: It is a thorny plant that grows on the ground. The Quraysh called it shabraq, but when it becomes dry they called it Dharee’. It is the most disgusting and odious food. This is the narration of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Kalbi said: No animal shall approach it when it is dry. Ibn Zayd said: As for this world, the dharī’ is the dry thorn whose leaves dry up, and in the afterlife it is a thorn of fire. It was mentioned in the hadith on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The dharī’ is something in the fire that is like a thorn, more bitter than aloes, more putrid than a carcass, and hotter than fire. Abu Darda and Al-Hasan said: God Almighty sends hunger upon the people of Hell until it equals the torment they are in. They seek help and are helped with bitter food. Then they seek help and are helped with food that chokes them. They remember that they used to endure choking in this world with water, so they ask for water and it makes them thirsty for a thousand years. Then they are given a drink from a spring that is neither pleasant nor satisfying. When they bring it close to their faces, it flays the skin of their faces and roasts them. When it reaches their stomachs, it cuts them apart. This is what God Almighty says: And they are given to drink scalding water, and it cuts their intestines apart. (Muhammad
88:7: The commentators said: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists said: Our camels grow fat on the dry thorn. They lied about that, because camels only graze it as long as it is fresh, and it is called shabraq. When it dries, nothing eats it. So God revealed: 7- It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger.
88:8: Then he described the people of Paradise and said: 8- On that Day, faces will be radiant. Muqatil said: In bliss and dignity.
88:9: 9- For her efforts, in this world, she is satisfied, in the hereafter when she is given Paradise for her work.
88:11: 11- La yasma'a fiha laghiyah, idle talk and falsehood. The people of Mecca and Basra read: la yasma'a with a ya' and a damma, laghiyah in the nominative case. Nafi' read La yasma'a with a ta' and a damma, laghiyah in the nominative case. The others read it with a ta' and a fatha, laghiyah in the accusative case, addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
88:13: 13- In it are raised thrones. Ibn Abbas said: Its panels are made of gold, crowned with emeralds, pearls, and rubies. They are raised as long as its people do not come. If he wants to sit on them, they will be humbled for him until he sits on them, then they will be raised to their places.
88:14: 14- And cups placed there, according to them, is the plural of cup, which is the jug that has no handle.
88:15: 15- Namariq, pillows and cushions, arranged, one next to the other, the singular is Namariqah with a damma on the nun.
88:16: 16- Zarabi means wide rugs. Ibn Abbas said: They are carpets with nap, the singular of which is zaribah. Mabthathah means spread out, and it was said that they are scattered in gatherings.
88:17: 17- Do they not look at the camels - how they are created? The commentators said: When God Almighty described in this surah what is in Paradise, the unbelievers were amazed by that and denied it, so God Almighty reminded them of His creation and said: Do they not look at the camels, from among all the animals, how they are created? Camels were part of the Arabs’ livelihood, and they had many benefits from them. So when He did that for them in this world, He did for the people of Paradise therein what He did. The wise men spoke about the reason for singling out camels from among all other animals. Muqatil said: Because they have never seen a beast larger than it, and only the rare ones among them have seen the elephant. Al-Kalbi said: Because it can bear its load while kneeling. Qatada said: God Almighty mentioned the height of the beds and furnishings of Paradise, so they said: How do we ascend them? So God Almighty revealed this verse. Al-Hasan was asked about this verse, and it was said to him: The elephant is the greatest wonder? He said: As for the elephant, the Arabs have had a long history with it. Moreover, it is of no use. One cannot ride its back, eat its meat, or milk its milk. Camels are the most precious and valuable property of the Arabs; they eat date pits and husks and produce milk. It was said: Despite its size, it is flexible to heavy loads and obeys a weak leader, so much so that a young boy takes its reins and leads it wherever he wants. Shuraih the judge used to say: Let us go to the stable’s rubbish bin so that we can see how the camels are created.
88:18: 18- And to the sky, how it was raised, from the earth so that nothing could reach it without support.
88:19: 19- And to the mountains, how they are fixed, an anchor on the face of the earth that does not move.
88:20: 20- And to the earth, how it was spread out, spread out. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Is anyone able to create something like camels, or raise something like the sky, or erect something like mountains, or spread something like the earth other than me?
88:21: 21- So remind meaning: preach, O Muhammad, you are only a reminder.
88:22: 22- You have no control over them, you have no power to kill them and force them to believe. This was abrogated by the verse on fighting.
88:23: 23- Except for he who turns away and disbelieves, an exception disconnected from what precedes it, meaning: but for he who turns away and disbelieves after the reminder.
88:24: 24- Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment, which is that He will put him in Hell. He only said the greatest because they were punished in this world with hunger, famine, killing, and captivity.
88:25: 25- To Us is their return, their return after death. It is said: He returned “returning” returning and Abu Ja`far read: Their return with a shaddah on the ya, which is anomalous and no one permitted it except Al-Zajjaj, who said: “It is said: He returned “returning” on the pattern: He did “returning” returning and returning.
88:26: 26- Then it is up to Us to bring them to account, meaning their punishment after they return to God Almighty.
89:1: Meccan 1- By the dawn God Almighty swears by the dawn. Abu Saleh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It is the break of dawn every day, and this is the opinion of Ikrimah. Atiyah said on his authority: The dawn prayer. Qatada said: It is the dawn of the first day of Muharram, from which the Sunnah begins. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the dawn of Dhul-Hijjah because the first ten nights are linked to it.
89:2: 2- And ten nights, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are the first ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah. This is the opinion of Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Al-Kalbi. Abu Ruq said on the authority of Al-Dahhak: It is the last ten days of Ramadan. Abu Dhabiyan narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is the first ten days of Ramadan. Yaman bin Rabab said: It is the first ten days of Muharram, the tenth of which is the day of Ashura.
89:3: 3- By the even and the odd, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read by the odd with a kasra on the waw, while others read it with a fatha, and they differed regarding the even and the odd. It was said that the even means creation, as God the Almighty said: And We created you in pairs and the odd means God the Almighty. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, and it is the opinion of Atiyah Al-Awfi. Mujahid and Masruq said: The even is all of creation, as God Almighty said: And of everything We have created pairs (al-Dhariyat 51:49), disbelief and faith, guidance and misguidance, happiness and misery, night and day, sky and earth, land and sea, sun and moon, jinn and mankind, and the odd is God Almighty, as God Almighty said: Say, ‘He is God, the One’ (al-Ikhla 112:1). Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: Shafa’ and Witr are all of creation, from it shafa’ and witr. Qatada narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It is a number, some of which are even and some of which are odd. Qatada said: They are the prayers, some of which are even and some of which are odd. This was narrated on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Atiyah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The even is the dawn prayer, and the odd is the sunset prayer. On the authority of Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, who said: Ash-Shafa’ is the first day of departure, and Ash-Witr is the last day of departure. It was narrated that a man asked him about Ash-Shafa’, Ash-Witr, and the ten nights. He said: As for Ash-Shafa’ and Ash-Witr, then God the Almighty said: But whoever hastens [to depart] in two days, there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him (al-Baqarah 2:203). They are Ash-Shafa’ and Ash-Witr. As for the ten nights, they are the eight, Arafah, and the Day of Sacrifice. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The even number is the days and nights, and the odd number is the day after which there is no night, which is the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hussein bin Al-Fadl said: The even number is the degrees of Paradise because they are eight, and the odd number is the levels of Hell because they are seven, as if he swore by Paradise and Hell. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq was asked about the even and the odd, and he said: The even is the contrast of the morals of the created beings, such as glory and humiliation, power and weakness, strength and weakness, knowledge and ignorance, sight and blindness. The odd is the uniqueness of the attributes of God, glory without humiliation, power without weakness, strength without weakness, knowledge without ignorance, and life without death.
89:4: 4- And the night when it departs, meaning when it moves and goes away, as God Almighty said, And the night when it departs (al-Muddaththir 74:33). Qatada said: When it comes and approaches, and he meant every night. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Al-Kalbi said: It is the night of Muzdalifah. The people of Hijaz and Basra read: yāsrī with a ya’ in the connected state. Ibn Kathir and Ya’qub also pause with a ya’, while the rest omit it in both cases. Whoever omitted it did so because it is in accordance with the beginnings of the verses, and whoever confirmed it did so because it is the lam of the verb, and the verb is not omitted from it when pausing, like in his statement: huwa qādī and ana aqdī. Al-Akhfash was asked about the reason for the omission of the ya’. He said: The night does not flow, but it flows in it, so it is declined. So when he declined it, he diminished its right to parsing, like in his statement: And your mother was not a prostitute. He did not say: bughīyah because it was declined from baghīyah.
89:5: 5- Is there in that, that is, in what you mentioned, an oath, that is, convincing and sufficient in the oath, for one with reason, for one with intelligence, called thus because it restrains its owner from what is not permissible and not appropriate, just as it is called reason because it restrains him from shameful deeds, and prohibition because it forbids what is not appropriate, and the root of restriction is prevention. And the answer to the oath is His statement: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful.
89:6: And the Almighty said between the oath and its answer: 6- Have you not seen? Al-Farra’ said: Have you not been informed? Al-Zajjaj said: Have you not known? Its meaning is astonishment. How did your Lord deal with the ‘Ad? He is frightening the people of Mecca, meaning: How did He destroy them, even though they lived longer and were stronger than these people.
89:7: 7- Iram and they differed about Iram of the Pillars. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Iram of the Pillars is Damascus, and Ikrimah said the same. Al-Qurazi said: It is Alexandria. Mujahid said: It is Ummah. It was also said: Its meaning is: ancient. Qatada and Muqatil said: They are a tribe from Ad. Muqatil said: The king was among them, and they were in Mahrah, and Ad was their father, so they were attributed to him, and he is Iram bin Ad bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: He is the grandfather of Ad, and he is Ad bin Aws bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah. Al-Kalbi said: Iram is the one to whom the lineage of Ad, Thamud, and the people of the Arabian Peninsula is united. It was said: Ad was Iram, and Thamud was Iram. Then God destroyed Ad, then Thamud, and the people of Sawad and the Arabian Peninsula remained. They were people of pillars, tents, and livestock that moved in the spring. When the weather was hot, they returned to their homes. They were people of gardens and crops, and their homes were in Wadi al-Qura.
89:8: And it is the one in which God says: 8- The like of which had not been created in the land. They were called Dhat al-Imad for this reason because they were people of moving pillars. This is the opinion of Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Kalbi, and the narration of Ata’ ibn Abbas. Some of them said: They were called Dhat al-Imad because of their tall stature. Ibn Abbas said: He means their height was like pillars. Muqatil said: The tallest of them was twelve cubits. His saying: No one like it has been created in the land, meaning no one like that tribe has been created in terms of height and strength, and they are the ones who said: Who is stronger than us? It was said: They named it Dhat al-Imdah because of a building that some of them built, so he erected its pillars and raised its structure. It is said: Shaddad bin Aad built it in a manner that had never been created like it in the world, and he marched towards it with his people. When he was a day and a night’s journey from it, God sent upon him and those with him a shout from the sky that destroyed them all.
89:9: 9- Thamud, meaning: and with Thamud, who cut the rock, they cut the rock, singular: rock, in the valley, meaning: Wadi al-Qura, they used to cut the mountains and build houses in them. Ibn Kathir and Ya'qub confirmed the ya' in the valley in connection and pause based on the original, and Warsh confirmed it in connection, and the others deleted it in both cases according to the headings of the verses.
89:10: 10- And Pharaoh of the stakes, he was called that because he used to torture people with stakes, and we mentioned him in Surah Sad. Abu Saeed Al-Sharahi told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Tha’labi told us, Ibn Fanjawayh told us, Mukhallad bin Ja’far told us, Al-Husayn bin Alawiyyah told us, Ismail bin Isa told us, Ishaq bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Ibn Sam’an, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Pharaoh was called Dhul-Awtad because there was a woman, the wife of Pharaoh’s treasurer, Hizbil, who was a believer but concealed his faith for a hundred years. His wife was the hairdresser of Pharaoh’s daughter. One day, while she was combing Pharaoh’s daughter’s hair, the comb fell from her hand. He said, Cursed is he who disbelieves in God. Pharaoh’s daughter said, Do you have a god other than my father? She said, My God and the God of your father and the God of the heavens and the earth is one, with no partner. She got up and went to her father crying. He said, What makes you cry? She said, “The hairdresser is the wife of your treasurer. She claims that your God and her God and the God of the heavens and the earth are one, with no partner.” So he sent for her and asked her about that, and she said, You have spoken the truth. He said to her, Woe to you! Disbelieve in your God and acknowledge that I am your God. She said, I will not. So he stretched her between four pegs, then sent snakes and scorpions upon her and said to her, Disbelieve in your God, or I will torment you with this torment for two months. She said, Even if you torment me for seventy months, I will not disbelieve in God. She had two daughters, so he brought her eldest daughter and slaughtered her near her. He said to her, Disbelieve in God, or I will slaughter the younger one, for your sake. She was an infant, so she said, Even if I were to slaughter everyone on the face of the earth for my sake, I would not have disbelieved in God Almighty. So he brought her youngest daughter, and when she lay on his chest and they wanted to slaughter her, the woman became terrified, but God loosened the tongue of her daughter and she spoke. She was one of the four who spoke as infants, and she said, O mother, do not worry, for God has built a house for you in Paradise. Be patient, for you will attain the mercy and honor of God. So she was slaughtered, and she soon died, and God made her dwell in Paradise. He said: He sent Hizbil in search of her husband, but they could not find him. Then it was said to Pharaoh: He has been seen in such and such a place on such and such a mountain. So he sent two men in search of him, and they came to him while he was praying, and behind him were rows of wild beasts praying. When they saw that, they turned away. Then Hizbil said: O God, You know that I concealed my faith for a hundred years, and no one revealed it to me. So whichever of these two men concealed it from me, guide him to Your religion and give him what he asks for in this world. And whichever of these two reveals it to me, hasten his punishment in this world and make his destination in the Hereafter the Fire. So the two men turned back to Pharaoh. As for one of them, he took heed and believed, and as for the other, he told Pharaoh the story in front of everyone. Pharaoh said to him: Was there anyone with you other than you? He said: Yes, so-and-so. Then he called for him and said: Is what he says true? He said: No, I did not see anything of what he said. So Pharaoh gave him generously, but as for the other, he killed him and then crucified him. He said: Pharaoh had married a woman from the women of the Children of Israel called Asiya bint Muzahim. She saw what Pharaoh had done to the hairdresser and said: How can I be patient with what Pharaoh does while I am a Muslim and he is an unbeliever? While she was thus contemplating this matter, Pharaoh entered and sat close to her. She said: O Pharaoh, you are the worst and most evil of creation. You went to the hairdresser and killed her. He said: Perhaps you are suffering from the madness that was in you? She said: I have no madness. My God and her God and your God / and the God of the heavens and the earth are one with no partner. So he tore her clothes and beat her and sent for her parents and said to them: Do you not see that the madness that was in the hairdresser has afflicted her? She said: I seek refuge in God from that. I bear witness that my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of the heavens and the earth is one with no partner. Her father said to her: O Asiya, who is the best of the women of the Amalekites, and your husband is the god of the Amalekites? She said, "I seek refuge in God from that. If what he says is true, then tell him to crown me with a crown in front of which the sun will be, the moon behind it, and the stars around it." Pharaoh said to them, Get out of here. So he stretched her out between four pegs to torture her. Then God opened for her a door to Paradise to make what Pharaoh would do to her easier for her. Then she said, My Lord, build for me, near You, a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people. (al-Tahrim 66:11) So God took her soul and settled her in Paradise.
89:11: 11- Those who transgressed in the land, meaning Aad, Thamud, and Pharaoh, committed sins and were tyrannical on earth.
89:13: 13- So your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment. Qatada said: It means a type of punishment that He poured down upon them. The scholars of semantics said: This is a metaphor, because a scourge, according to them, is the ultimate punishment. This applies to every type of punishment. Al-Zajjaj said: He made His scourge with which He struck them the punishment.
89:14: 14- Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. Ibn Abbas said: meaning that He sees, hears, and perceives. Al-Kalbi said: The path of the servants is on it, no one misses it. Muqatil said: The path of people is on it, and the watchtower, and the watchtower: the road. It was said: The reference of creation is to His rule and command, and to Him is their destiny. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: He monitors the deeds of the children of Adam. Meaning: He does not miss any of the deeds of His servants, just as He does not miss the one who is watching. Al-Saddī said: God set fire on their path until He destroyed them.
89:15: 15- But as for man, when his Lord tests him with a blessing, then honors him with money and blessings, he says, ‘My Lord has honored me,’ with what He has given me.
89:16: 16- And when He tests him, with poverty, and restricts his provision, Abu Ja`far and Ibn `Amir read and restricts with a shaddah on the dal, while others read it without a shaddah. These are two dialects, meaning He restricts his provision. It was also said that and restricts means and gives him enough to suffice him. “Then he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me,’” He has humiliated me with poverty. This refers to the unbeliever, for whom honor and humiliation are due to an abundance of money and fortune in this world or a scarcity thereof. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed about Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi, the infidel.
89:17: God responded to those who thought that abundant provision was an honor and that poverty was an insult, saying: 17- No! I did not afflict him with wealth for his dignity, nor did I afflict him with poverty for his humiliation. So He informed us that honor and humiliation do not revolve around money and abundant provision, but rather poverty and wealth are based on His decree. So He grants generosity to the disbeliever, not for his dignity, and He grants power to the believer, not for his humiliation. Rather, He honors a person through his obedience and humiliates him through his disobedience. The people of Hijaz and Basra read akramni and ahanani with the ya’ in the connected word. Ibn Kathir and Ya’qub also stop with the ya’, while others delete it in the connected word and in the stopped word. "Rather, you do not honor the orphan." The people of Basra read: "you honor, you prepare, you eat, and you love, with the letter ya. Others read it with the letter ta. You do not honor the orphan" means you do not treat him well. It was also said: you do not give him his rights. Muqatil said: Qudamah ibn Maz’un was an orphan in the care of Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and he used to deny him his rights.
89:18: 18- And do not urge one another to feed the poor, meaning do not order that he be fed. Abu Ja`far and the people of Kufa read: you urge one another with the ha’ open and an alif after it, meaning do not urge one another to do it.
89:19: 19- And you consume the inheritance, meaning the inheritance, consuming it completely, meaning that he consumes his share and the share of others, and that is because they did not give inheritance to women or children, and they consumed their share. Ibn Zayd said: The greedy eater is the one who eats everything he finds, without asking whether it is permissible or forbidden. He eats what is his and what is not. It is said: I ate what is on the table, if you go to what is on it and eat it.
89:20: 20- And you love money with a great love, that is, a lot, meaning: you love to collect money and are obsessed with it. It is said: the water in the basin is abundant, if it is plentiful and accumulates.
89:21: 21- No, this is not how things should be. Muqatil said: meaning they do not do what they were commanded to do with regard to the orphan and feeding the poor. Then he informed of their longing for what they had done in the past when it would no longer benefit them, so the Almighty said: If the earth is pounded to the ground, time after time, and everything on its surface is broken, from mountains, buildings, and trees, nothing remains on its surface.
89:22: 22- And your Lord has come, Al-Hasan said: His command and decree have come. Al-Kalbi said: He descends and the angels, rank upon rank, Ata' said: He means the ranks of angels, and the people of each heaven are a separate rank. Ad-Dahhak said: When the people of each heaven descend on the Day of Resurrection, they will be in a rank mixed with the earth and those in it, so there will be seven rank.
89:23: 23- And Hell will be brought forth on that Day. Abdullah ibn Mas’ud and Muqatil said regarding this verse: It will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein being led by seventy thousand angels, raging and roaring until it is erected on the left side of the Throne. On that Day, meaning the Day Hell will be brought forth, man will remember, he will be admonished and the disbeliever will repent. But how will he receive remembrance? Al-Zajjaj said: Repentance will be apparent, but how will he receive repentance?
89:24: 24- He says, ‘Oh, I wish I had prepared for my life,’ meaning I had prepared goodness and righteous deeds for my life in the Hereafter, meaning for my Hereafter in which there is no death.
89:25: 25- On that Day, no one will be punished as He punished him.
89:26: 26- And no one will be bound as he is bound. Al-Kisa’i and Ya’qub read no one will be punished. No one will be punished as he is bound on that day, with the opening of the dhal and the tha’, meaning no one will be punished in this world as God punishes on that day, and no one will be bound as he is bound on that day. It was said: He is a specific man, he is Umayyah ibn Khalaf, meaning that no one will be tortured like this infidel, and no one will be bound like he was bound. Others read it with a kasra on the dhal and the tha’, meaning: No one will be punished in this world as God punishes the disbeliever on that day, and no one will be bound as he is bound, meaning no one among creation will reach the level of God’s reach in punishment, and binding is captivity in chains and shackles.
89:27: God Almighty says: 27- O reassured soul, referring to what God Almighty has promised to the one who believes in what He has said. Mujahid said: The reassured soul is the one who is certain that God Almighty is her Lord and is patient and submits to His command and obedience. Al-Hasan said: The believing woman who is certain. Atiyah said: The one who is satisfied with the decree of God Almighty. Al-Kalbi said: The one who is safe from the punishment of God. It was said: The one who is reassured by the remembrance of God. Its al-Sharh 94:His saying, And their hearts are reassured by the remembrance of God.
89:28: They differed about the time of this statement. Some people said: It is said to her at death, and it is said to her: 28- Return to your Lord, to God, satisfied, with the reward, satisfied, with you. Al-Hassan said: If God wants to take her, she will be reassured by God, satisfied with God, and God will be satisfied with her. Abdullah ibn Amr said: When a believing servant dies, God the Almighty sends two angels to him and one to him with a gift from Paradise. It is told: Come out, O reassured soul, come out to a spirit and fragrance, and your Lord is pleased with you. So it comes out like the most fragrant musk scent anyone has ever found in his nose, and the angels are in the corners of the heavens saying: A good spirit and a good breeze have come from the earth. So it does not pass by a door except that it is opened for it, nor by an angel except that he prays for it, until it is brought to the Most Merciful and it prostrates. Then it is told to Michael: Take this and place it with the souls of the believers. Then he is commanded to make his grave wider for him, seventy cubits wide and seventy cubits long, and fragrance is sprinkled in it for him. If he has with him something from the Qur’an, its light will suffice him. And if he does not have a light like the sun in his grave, he will be like a bride, sleeping and none will wake him except the dearest of his family to him. And when the unbeliever dies, God sends two angels to him and sends a piece of filth, the most putrid of all filth and coarsest of all coarse, and it will be said: O wicked soul, come out to Hell and a painful punishment, and your Lord is angry with you. Abu Saleh said about His statement: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, he said: This is when she leaves this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: Enter among My servants and enter My Paradise. Others said: It will only be said to her at the time of al-Qiyamah 75:Return to your Lord, meaning to your Master and your body. Then God will command the souls to return to the bodies. This is the opinion of Ikrimah, Ata’, and Ad-Dahhak, and the narration of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is: Return to the reward and honor of your Lord, satisfied with God for what He has prepared for you, pleasing Him, and may your Lord be satisfied with you.
89:29: 29- So enter among My servants, meaning with My servants in My Paradise. It was also said: among My righteous, obedient, chosen servants, similar to: And admit me, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants.
89:30: 30- And enter My Paradise. Some scholars of allusion said: O soul content with the world, return to God by abandoning it. Returning to God is taking the path to the Hereafter. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, died in Taif, and I attended his funeral. A bird came, the likeness of which we had never seen before, and entered his coffin. We did not see it come out of it. When he was buried, this verse was recited on the edge of the grave, and we do not know who recited it: O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, and enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise.
90:1: 1- I do not swear, meaning I swear, by this country, meaning Mecca.
90:2: 2- And you are permissible, that is, lawful, in this country, doing in it what you want of killing and capturing, and you are not liable for the sins of the people there. God Almighty made Mecca lawful for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of the conquest, until he fought and killed and ordered the killing of Ibn Khatal, while he was clinging to the curtains of the Kaaba, and Muqays ibn Subaba and others. He made the blood of some people lawful and the blood of others unlawful, and said: Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe. Then he said: God made Mecca unlawful on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and it was not lawful for anyone before me and it will not be lawful for anyone after me. It was only made lawful for me for an hour of a day, so it is unlawful by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. Meaning: When God Almighty swore by Mecca, this indicated its great value and sanctity. So He promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He would make it permissible for him so that he could fight in it and conquer it at his hands. This is a promise from God Almighty that He would make it permissible for him. Shurahbil bin Saad said: The meaning of his statement, And you are a resident of this country, is: They forbid killing game there, but they consider it permissible to expel you and kill you?
90:3: 3- And the father and what he begot, meaning Adam, peace be upon him, and his descendants.
90:4: 4- Indeed, We created man into toil. Al-Walibi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In hardship. Al-Hasan said: He endures the calamities of this world and the hardships of the Hereafter. Qatada said: In hardship, and you will not find him except struggling with the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. Saeed bin Jubair said: In hardship. Ata’ said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: In hardship during his pregnancy, birth, breastfeeding, weaning, weaning, livelihood, life and death. Amr ibn Dinar said: When his teeth grow. Yaman said: God did not create a creation that struggles with the son of Adam, and yet he is the weakest of creation. The root of the word liver is: hardship. Mujahid, Atiyah, and Ad-Dahhak said: It means upright and of moderate height, and everything created walks in a prone position. This is the narration of Muqsam on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The root of the word liver is: straightness and uprightness. Ibn Kaysan said: His head is upright in his mother’s womb, and when God gives him permission to come out, his head turns to his mother’s feet. Muqatil said: In the liver, meaning in strength. It was revealed about Abu Al-Ashdayn, whose name was Asid bin Kalda Al-Jumahi. He was a strong and powerful man who would place a piece of Ukaz leather under his feet and say: Whoever removes me from him will get such and such. It was impossible for it to be removed from under his feet except by cutting it off, and the place where his feet were left would remain.
90:5: 5- Does he think, meaning Abu Al-Ashdayn, from his strength, that no one will be able to overcome him, meaning: He thinks from his strength that God Almighty will not be able to overcome him. It was said: He is Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah.
90:6: 6- He says I have wasted, meaning I have spent, a lot of money, meaning a lot of it on top of each other, from the lapping, in enmity towards Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Ja`far read labdan with a shaddah on the ba on the plural of labd, like rak` and rak`a, and the others read it with a light labdah on the plural of labdah, and it was said on the singular like qathm and hataam.
90:7: 7- Does he think that no one sees him? Saeed bin Jubair and Qatada said: Does he think that God does not see him, and does not ask him about his money, where he acquired it from, and where he spent it? Al-Kalbi said: He was lying when he said he spent such and such, and he did not spend all of what he said. He said: Does he think that God Almighty did not see that from him and thus know the amount of his spending?
90:8: Then he reminded him of his blessings so that he might consider them, and said: 8- Did We not give him two eyes?
90:9: 9- And a tongue and lips. Qatada said: The blessings of God are evident, and He confirms them to you so that you may be grateful. It was stated in the hadith: “God Almighty says: Son of Adam, if your tongue disputes with you regarding something that I have forbidden you, then I have helped you with it with two layers, so close your eyes. If your sight disputes with you regarding something that I have forbidden you, then I have helped you with it with two layers, so close your eyes. If your private parts dispute with you regarding something that I have forbidden you, then I have helped you with it with two layers, so close your eyes.”
90:10: 10- And We showed him the two ways, most of the commentators said: the path of good and evil, truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, like His statement: Indeed, We showed him the way, be he grateful or ungrateful. Muhammad bin Ka’b said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We showed him the two ways, he said: the two breasts, and this is the statement of Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab and Al-Dahhak, and the way is a path in a height.
90:11: 11- Why did he not take the difficult path? He says: Why did he not spend his money on what is permissible, such as freeing slaves and feeding the hungry, so that it would be better for him than spending it on enmity towards Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace? This is the statement of Ibn Zayd and a group. It was said: He did not storm the obstacle, meaning he did not storm it or go beyond it. Storming means entering into a difficult matter. The mention of the obstacle here is an example that God gave to struggle against the self, desires, and Satan in righteous deeds. He made him like the one who takes it upon himself to climb the obstacle. He says: He did not burden himself with the hardship of freeing a slave or feeding him. This is the meaning of what Qatada said. It was said: He likened the weight of sins on the one who commits them to an obstacle, so if he frees a slave and feeds people, it is as if he has stormed the obstacle and crossed it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar: This pass is a mountain in Hell. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: It is a steep obstacle in Hell before the bridge, so cross it in obedience to God Almighty. Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and Al-Kalbi said: It is a path that is struck across Hell like the edge of a sword, a journey of three thousand years, easy, ascending and descending. On its sides are hooks and snipes like the thorns of the Sa’dan tree. Some will escape as a Muslim, some will escape scratched, and some will be thrown upside down into the Fire. Some people will pass like a flash of lightning, some like a violent wind, some like a horseman, some like a running man, some like a walking man, some like a crawling man, some like a slipping one, some like a slipping one, and some like a falling one. Ibn Zayd said: He says, Why didn’t he take the path that leads to salvation?
90:12: Then he explained what they are, saying: 12- And what will make you know what the obstacle is? What is storming the obstacle? Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Everything that is said, And what will make you know, has been described, but whatever is said, And what will make you know, has not been described.
90:14: 14- Freeing a slave * or feeding, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Al-Kisa'i read: free with a fatha on the kaf, a slave in the accusative case, or feed with a fatha on the hamza and the mim in the past tense. The others read free with a dhammah on the kaf, a slave in the genitive case, or feeding with a kasrah on the hamza, so an alif comes after the 'ayn, and a dhammah on the mim with a tanween as a verbal noun. By freeing a slave, he meant to set it free and set it free. Whoever frees a slave, his ransom will be from the Fire. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Sam’an told us, Abu Ja’far bin Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Abdul Jabbar Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Al-Layth bin Sa’d told me, Ibn Al-Haad told me, on the authority of Umar bin Ali bin Hussein, on the authority of Saeed bin Marjana, who said: I heard him narrating on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever frees a believing slave, God will free a limb of his from the Fire for every limb of his, until He frees his private parts with his private parts.’” Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Abu Mansur Al-Sam'ani told us, Abu Ja'far Al-Rayyani told us, Hamid bin Zanjawayh told us, Muhammad bin Katheer Al-Abdi told us, Isa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Salami told us, on the authority of Talha bin Masraf Al-Yami, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Awsaja, on the authority of Al-Bara' bin Azib, who said: "A Bedouin came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, teach me a deed that will admit me to Paradise. He said: If I have shortened the sermon, then I have overlooked the question: Free a soul and set a slave free. I said: Isn't that one thing? He said: No. Freeing a soul means that you are alone in freeing it, and setting a slave free means that you help with its price, and a gift means being generous, and spend on an unjust relative. If you are not able to do that, then feed the hungry and give drink to the thirsty, and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. If you are not able to do that, then hold your tongue except for good." Akrima said: His statement: Freeing a slave means freeing a slave from sins through repentance. Or feeding on a day of famine means famine. It is said: Saghb yasghb saghban if he became hungry.
90:15: 15- An orphan who is close to you, meaning one who is related to you. He means an orphan who is related to you.
90:16: 16- Or a poor person covered in dust, who has been covered in dust due to his poverty and hardship. Mujahid said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He is the one who has been thrown in the dust, with nothing protecting him. Dusty is the source of dust, which means he becomes poor.
90:17: 17- Then he was among those who believed, indicating that this closeness only benefits with faith. It was said: Then has the meaning of and, “and they enjoin one another,” they enjoined one another, to be patient, in fulfilling God’s obligations and commandments, and they enjoin one another to compassion, to be compassionate toward people.
90:18: 18- Those are the companions of the right.
90:19: 19- And those who disbelieve in Our verses are the companions of the left.
90:20: 20- A closed fire will be upon them, with its doors closed around them. No soul will enter it and no sorrow will leave it. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Hafs read: with a hamza here, and with a hamza, while the others read it without a hamza. These are two dialects. It is said: Asadat al-bab and awsadatuhu if you close it and lock it. It was said: the meaning of the hamza is al-muftaqa and other than the hamza is al-muftaqa.
91:1: 1- And the sun and its brightness, Mujahid and Al-Kalbi said: its light, and the brightness is when the sun rises and its light becomes clear. Qatada said: it is the entire day. Muqatil said: its heat, like His statement in Ta-Ha and do not be exposed to the brightness, meaning do not let the heat harm you.
91:2: 2- And the moon when it follows it, follows it, and that is in the first half of the month. When the sun sets, the moon follows it in illumination and is behind it in radiance. Al-Zajjaj said: That is when it turns round, meaning its light is complete, following the sun in illumination, and that is in the white nights.
91:3: 3- And the day when it reveals it, meaning when it reveals the darkness, a metaphor for something that is not mentioned because it is known.
91:4: 4- And the night when it covers it, meaning when it covers the sun when it sets and the horizons become dark.
91:5: 5- And the heaven and He who built it, Al-Kalbi said: And He who built it and created it is like His saying: Then marry such women as seem good to you. An-Nisaa’ 3 meaning whomever seems good. Ata' said: And He who built it. Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: What means a source, meaning and its construction is like His statement: Because my Lord has forgiven me (Ya-Sin 36:27).
92:6: 6- And the earth and what He spread out, He spread it out. 6- And believe in the best, Abu Abd al-Rahman and al-Dahhak said: And believe in there is no god but God, and this is the narration of Atiyah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Mujahid said: In Paradise. His evidence is the Almighty’s saying: For those who do good is the best meaning Paradise. It was said, He believed in the best, meaning in the successor, meaning he was certain that God Almighty would replace him. This is the narration of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Qatada, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: By the promise of God Almighty who promised him that He would reward him.
92:7: 7- And the soul and He who proportioned it, He created it justly and proportioned its parts. Ata’ said: He means all that He created of the jinn and mankind. 7- We will make it easy for him, so We will prepare him in this world, for ease, meaning for the easy path, which is doing what pleases God Almighty.
92:8: 8- He inspired her with her wickedness and her righteousness. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Ali bin Abi Talha: / He showed her good and evil. And he said in the narration of Atiyah: He taught her obedience and disobedience. Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Saleh on his authority: He made her know what good she should do and what evil she should avoid. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He made her commit her sin and her piety. Ibn Zayd said: He made that in her, meaning by guiding her to piety and abandoning her to sin. Al-Zajjaj chose this and interpreted inspiration as meaning success and abandonment. This shows that God, the Almighty, created piety in the believer and sin in the disbeliever. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shuraihi told us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha’labi told us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abdullah told us, Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Urwah ibn Thabit al-Ansari told us, Yahya ibn Aqil told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ya’mar, on the authority of al-Aswad al-Dailami, who said: “Imran ibn Husayn said to me: ‘Have you seen what people do and strive for? Is it something that was decreed for them and that had already passed them by a predestination? Or is it something that their Prophet brought them and the proof was confirmed for them? ’ I said: ‘Rather, it is something that has already been decreed for them. ’ He said: ‘Would that be injustice? ’ I was terrified by it, and I said: ‘There is nothing but that He created it and possesses it. He is not questioned about what He does, but they are questioned. ’ He said to me: ‘May God guide you. I only asked you to test your mind. A man from Juhayna or Muzayna came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, have you seen what people do and strive for? ’ Is it something that was decreed for them and happened to them from a previous destiny? Or in what they will face from what their Prophet brought them and with which the proof was confirmed against them? He said: No, rather it is something that was decreed for them and happened to them. I said: Then what is the point of action? He said: Whoever God created for one of the two stations, God prepares him for it, and confirmation of that is in the Book of God Almighty: “And by the soul and He who proportioned it. And inspired it with [whatever] its wickedness and its righteousness.” Abdul Wahid bin Ahmad Al-Malihi told us, Abu Muhammad Abdul Rahman bin Abi Shuraih told us, Abu Al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz Al-Baghawi told us, Ali bin Al-Jaad told us, Zuhair bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “Suraqa bin Malik bin Ja’sham came and said: O Messenger of God, explain our religion to us as if we were created now. Do you think this Umrah of ours is for this year or forever? He said: Rather, forever. He said: O Messenger of God, explain our religion to us as if we were created now. What is the purpose of working today, in what the pens have dried and the destinies have run? Or in what will come? He said: No, rather, in what the pens have dried and the destinies have run. He said: Then what is the purpose of working? Zuhair said: Then he said a word that was not clear to me, so I asked my relative about it later, and he remembered that he heard it, and he said: Work, for everyone is facilitated for what he was created for.” 8- But as for he who is stingy, in spending on good, and considers himself independent, of God’s reward and does not desire it.
92:9: 9- He has succeeded who purifies it. This is the place for the oath, meaning that a soul that God has purified has succeeded and been happy, meaning that He has reformed it and cleansed it of sins and guided it to obedience. 9- And he denied the best.
92:10: 10- And he who has plotted it has failed, meaning that a soul that God has led astray and corrupted has failed and lost. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is that he has succeeded who purifies his soul, reforms it, and leads it to obey God Almighty. And he has failed who corrupts it, destroys it, leads it astray, and leads it to disobedience. So the action is attributed to the soul. The root of dasaha is dasaaha from taddisa which means to hide something, so the second s was replaced with a ya. The meaning here is: he concealed it and hid its location through disbelief and disobedience. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni told us, Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sharik al-Shafi’i told us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jurbidhi told us, Ahmad ibn Harb told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Uthman and Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: “I will not say to you anything except what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: ‘O God, I seek refuge in You from incapacity, laziness, miserliness, cowardice, worry, and the punishment of the grave. O God, grant my soul its piety and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and Master. O God, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that is of no benefit, from a soul that is not satisfied, from a heart that is not humble, and from a supplication that is not answered.’” 10- Then We will make it easy for him to do what is difficult, We will prepare him for evil by making it happen through his hands until he does what is not pleasing to God, and thus deserves Hellfire. Muqatil said: We will make it difficult for him to do good. We narrated on the authority of Ali, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is no soul but that God has written for it its place in Paradise or Hell. A man said: Shall we not rely on what has been written for us and abandon working? He said: “No, but work, for everyone is facilitated for what he was created for. As for the people of misery, they will be facilitated to do the work of the people of misery, and as for the people of happiness, they will be facilitated to do the work of the people of happiness.” Then he recited: “But as for him who gives and fears God * And believes in the best * We will ease him toward ease. But as for him who withholds and considers himself free of need * And denies the best * We will ease him toward difficulty.”” It was said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, who bought Bilal from Umayya bin Khalaf for a cloak and ten awq, and then freed him. Then God Almighty revealed: And by the night when it covers until His saying: Indeed, your efforts are diverse, meaning: the efforts of Abu Bakr and Umayya. Ali bin Hajar narrated on the authority of Ishaq on the authority of Abu Nujayh on the authority of Ata’ who said: “A man from the Ansar had a palm tree and his neighbor had some of its dates falling into his neighbor’s house, and his children would eat from it. He complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Sell it to me for a palm tree in Paradise.’ But he refused. So he went out and met Abu Ad-Dahdah, who said to him: ‘Would you like to sell it for the garden’, meaning his wall? So he said to him: ‘It is yours.’ So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Messenger of God, will you buy it from me for a palm tree in Paradise?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘It is yours.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Ansari neighbor and said: ‘Take it.’ Then God Almighty revealed: ‘By the night when it covers’ until His saying: ‘Indeed, your efforts are diverse.’ The efforts of Abu Ad-Dahdah and the Ansari, the owner of the palm tree.” But as for him who gives and fears God, meaning Abu Ad-Dahdah, and believes in the best reward, meaning the reward, We will ease him toward ease, meaning Paradise. But as for him who withholds and considers himself free of need, meaning the Ansari, and denies the best reward, meaning the reward, We will ease him toward difficulty, meaning the Fire.
92:11: God Almighty said: 11- Thamud denied it due to their transgression, due to their transgression and aggression, meaning transgression led them to deny it. 11- And his wealth will not avail him, which he was stingy with, if he falls down, Mujahid said: if he dies. Qatada and Abu Salih said: he falls into Hell.
92:12: 12- When the most wretched of them arose, meaning he stood up. Arise means to hasten to obey the sender, meaning they denied the punishment, and they denied Salih when the most wretched of them arose, and he was: Qidar bin Salaf, and he was blond with blue eyes, short, and he stood up to hamstring the camel. Abdul Wahid Al-Malihi told us, Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Naimi told us, Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Ismail told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Wahib told us, Hisham told us on the authority of his father that Abdullah bin Zama’a told him that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon and he mentioned the she-camel and the one who had hamstrung her. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the most wretched of them arose, a mighty, mighty man, powerful among his family, arose for her like Abu Zama’a. 12- Indeed, it is upon Us to guide, meaning to explain. Al-Zajjaj said: It is upon Us to explain the path of guidance from the path of misguidance. This is what Qatada said, who said: It is upon God to explain what He has permitted and what He has forbidden. Al-Farra’ said: It means whoever follows guidance, then God will follow his path, as God the Almighty says: And upon God is the direction of the path (al-Nahl 16:9). He says: Whoever desires God will follow the straight path. It was said that its meaning is: It is up to Us to guide and misguide, like His saying: In Your hand is all good (Al Imran 3:26). He restricted it to guidance because the speech indicates it, like His saying: Garments to protect you from the heat (al-Nahl 16:81). He restricted it to mentioning the heat and did not mention the cold because it indicates it.
114:6: 13- Then the Messenger of God, Salih, peace be upon him, said to them, The she-camel of God, meaning, beware of hamstringing the she-camel of God.
